title: Excellent firestick
text: So easy to install and works like a charm.  Plan to buy more for the entire household.

title: Light on, light off
text: Worked as described. Easy Peasey set-up

title: Firm seating, nice looking
text: It comes in 3 boxes and the boxes will be delivered to the room of your choice. You need to attach the backs and the cushions get zippered together and Velcro into place. The couch looks nice and is comfortable to sit on. Not sure how long it will last but for the price it meets our needs.

title: It works
text: I live in the mid South where tornadoes and severe storms are quite common in the Spring. A reliable weather radio is a must. Meteorologists have recommended this brand weather alert radio. I’ve had it for a couple of weeks and it has already alerted me to severe storms in my area. It’s very simple to set up and use. I recommend having the Midland brand weather alert radio.

title: Didn’t Work For Me
text: Sounded great when I ordered it, but it would not work on my desktop computer that runs Windows 7. I don’t know why. The computer would not recognize this external hard drive. Maybe tech support would have given me some answers, but I chose to return this item. My rating simply reflects what I’ve written here. This device might be just what someone else needs, and work great for them. So don’t take my one star rating as the norm for this device. Could be it doesn’t work on an older computer like mine.

title: Very Nice Replacements
text: The replacement ear pads for my Bose headset seemed to be about the same as the originals. My son in law installed them, no video instructions needed. The pads feel pretty good on my ears. Haven't had a chance to really use them yet--I did test them with a tune or two--but I can recommend them if you need replacements.

title: Works For My Son in law's GoPro--It Was A Gift
text: I bought this skin for my son in law's GoPro as a birthday gift and he is using it and seems to be very pleased with it.

title: Love It
text: I love this cover/case for my Kindle Paperwhite e-reader. Worth every penny. Works perfectly. No complaints.

title: What's Not To Like?
text: There is nothing I don't like about my Kindle Paperwhite e-reader. Worth every penny. Totally awesome. Took it to Florida a few weeks ago and read my books easily in the bright sunlight on the beach. Can't do this with an iPad or a Kindle Fire.

title: Perfect for the Flip Pal scanner
text: If you've got a Flip Pal scanner, you need this carry bag. Perfect fit, sturdy material, removable/adjustable strap, and a side pocket for storage.

title: Great deal, great cords
text: I highly recommend these cords, they're durable and great quality. Get them!

title: I recommend
text: These make it easier to handle the small Roku remotes. I will always use these.

title: Works great
text: I'm using this in a 1 gallon tank for my betta. I've had it for some time now, and it's working great. It's keeping the temp at 82° consistently. No issues thus far.

title: Good clock
text: It's easy to read and bright. And also has fun colors for the night light. You can set dual alarms, which I love, and you can choose between a regular alarm, or the radio.

title: Love love love
text: I've always had the kindle fire, and I'm so glad I picked this one. I love the screen size, picture and sound. Amazon hit it out of the park with the 2021 fire. So happy!

title: Durable and protective
text: Great cover for my kindle fire. The quality is great. Couldn't be happier.

title: Great colorful bands!
text: I am absolutely excited about these bands. I was a little hesitant about buying these, not knowing if the quality would be good. Let me reassure you..these bands are great! They are very flexible and almost the same quality of the original fitbit band, but with all the different fun colors. The only reason I'm giving it 4 stars is because the size is much smaller than the fitbit bands. I ordered a large and I have to fasten it on the last 2 holes, so it just fits. I'm okay with that, just know before ordering they size quite a bit smaller.

title: Pretty durable so far
text: We really like this case for the iPad. Part of the rubber did rip already which is annoying. But it has still kept the iPad safe and our two year old has done a number on it. The glass screen was perfect, easy to put on and has held up well. Love that it has a kick stand to prop it up for movies and stuff.

title: I love this case!
text: I love the case. It works very well. It is tight though, hard to get my mac in it with a hard cover on my mac. Also it would be nice if I could attach the little pouch on it somewhere but thats not a big deal.

title: It works well
text: I kept this on my computer for about a year with no issues. Its cute and it worked pretty well for a while but it did break on the underside after regular wear and tear. The keyboard cover really just wasn't for me but it stayed relatively well.

title: Love
text: We love these kits. We have gifted them for christmas, we used them for our guest book at our wedding and our child has fun with all the customizations he can make with his photos!

title: It Works with 1st gen Chromecast
text:
There is no information to tell why the adaptor may not be working.
improper setup?; bad adaptor?; bad ethernet cable?; not compatible?
The blue led will light steady when power is applied with no ethernet connection, and flash with an ethernet connection .
If the Chromecast has previously been setup there is no need to do it again, just connect the adaptor and power it up.
Your WiFi name will not appear on the screen when its on ethernet.
I was able to power the adaptor from the TV USB.

title: Easy setup, perfect for a family computer
text: I like the screen size. Easy to use.

title: Beautiful blue colors
text: Perfect for my iPad mini.

title: It's a no from me
text: It was easy to put together but after I filled it with movies it was about to fall over.

title: Three Stars
text: Your cases are nice but should be just a littl bit more heavy duty.

title: Don't Buy
text: This is hands down the worst HDMI cable I have ever used. Not only is it the worst HDMI cable I have ever used but arguably the worst purchase I have ever made and worst product I have ever used. The locking mechanism is faulty at best. Upon my first use of this product the cable got stuck in my HDMI input for my laptop. I had to completely break the product down to the connector to free it from my laptop. Terrible product. I would not recomend this to anyone who cares for any of their electronic devices. DO NOT BUY THIS PRODUCT.

title: Great lights for the price
text: These are awesome!

title: Good product
text: Good

title: Great sign. Durable, easy to see
text: Great quality

title: Awesome
text: Great price, son is going to lover the design, plus many more to choose from!

title: Great!
text: This is a really pretty and protective laptop carrying case. The zippers zip smoothly and the soft inside of the case makes me feel like my laptop is being cradeled in protection. It is extremely lightweight, I don't feel it added any bulk or weight. it is a little bigger than described so theres about an inch above and a half inch around of extra material. That doesn't bother me but it is good to know it isnt snug on a 15.6" laptop. overall I think this is an amazing case for the money and I'm happy with this purchase! I would 100% reccomend it!

title: Cute but you get what you pay for.
text: This keyboard cover is good for the price. The pink is beautiful in person and from far away but unfortunately not as nice up close. It looks like my cover was either painted/printed a tad bit off because many of the keys have a white line on the right side where it should still be pink. There's also some extra silicone kind of hanging off the edge of the 0, ., and enter keys on the number panel. Other than the minor issues it seems ok! I just recieved it a few minutes ago and put it on so I can't really speak for the adhesion or durability so I will update my review as time passes. I'd say for the price it's worth it!

title: Great little keyboard / case
text: Works well and looks nice - just what I was after.

title: Works well for graphic design use
text: I wanted a bigger second monitor at home since I do some graphic design work and find it much easier on the larger screen. I am not one of those people that cares much about buying the most advanced specs on monitors. Does it work well without glitches? Yes? Perfect. Does the display look good with no obvious color issues? Yes? Perfect. Am I able to sit at it for long periods and do my work successfully? Yes! And, it was a good deal, too, so I'm happy.

title: I didn't expect to love this.
text: I have had a Kindle Fire for years (I'm on my second one), but before I went on vacation to Hawaii (where I expected to be reading in direct sunlight - something the Fire is not good for), I ordered this Paperwhite. You absolutely can read in direct sunlight with this. The battery life is PHENOMENAL! And, my eyes do not get tired like they usually do when I read on the Fire or my laptop. Despite not *really* wanting to spend the money when I already had a perfectly functioning Fire, this has become my go-to device. I love it!

title: Great value monitor
text: I use this as a second screen with my Macbook Pro 15 and it works perfectly (and makes working from home a lot easier). I recommend it!

title: Looks more expensive than it is!
text: I was actually in the market for a to-quality leather laptop case, but everything I found either wouldn't fit my Macbook Pro 15", or was far too large and heavy. When I found this one at such as reasonable cost, I was dubious that I would like it. Surprise: I love it! It's well-made and the perfect size for my Macbook. My boss (who only buys luxury Italian brands) noticed it and liked it as well. For the money, you can't beat it.

title: Good Bag, Good Value
text: While it was slightly smaller than I expected, it was a fantastic deal for the money.  It's every bit as nice as the $100 bags from a well-known camera bag maker.

title: Measure headphones accurately before ordering.
text: Purchased to replace damaged pads on an older set of SteelSeries headphones that are no longer made.  These fit perfectly.  Slightly tricky to install but they do stretch slightly.  Once on, they are secure and comfortable.  They appear to be well made and are reasonably priced. Shipped quickly.  Time will tell.  Extremely pleased so far.

title: Good value tripod, but quite heavy
text: I selected this tripod to try out on my recent Alaska cruise, but ended up not using it during the trip due to the weight. It would have easily tipped my luggage weight over the 50 lbs limit. Otherwise it is really nice though for an amateur photographer like me. It's sturdy, holds my camera well, and I'm able to take some neat wildlife photos at home. It has a nice carry case. It works great for home photos & I'll probably take it on trips where we don't travel by air, but I'll look into budgeting a carbon fiber tripod for other trips.

title: Great sound quality & comfortable
text: I selected this headset for my daughter, and she really likes it. The sound quality is great, and it's very comfortable. The changing colors are also fun too. The only thing my daughter wishes is that she had the ability to go wireless, as she has to remove them every time she needs to get up from her desk. But otherwise, it's a great headset.

title: Good battery life and very comfortable
text: I like to play computer games, and when I'm playing I usually go on for quite a long session. So an ergonomic mouse is a must have for me. I selected this mouse to go with my laptop and it's working really well. It's comfortable, reactive (no delay or drag) and the battery life is quite good. It fits nicely in my laptop bag. I also tend to be kind of hard on my mouse, so I usually have to replace them every 2 years or so. With the price so reasonable, I don't mind having to replace this mouse.

title: Perfect for laptops
text: When I received my new laptop, I was initially dismayed to see how few USB ports it had. Not only do I like to use a mouse rather than the track pad, I also like to use a cooling tray when I'm playing games on the laptop. This USB hub is perfect for me. I'm able to plug in the bluetooth dongle for my mouse, and the cooling tray cord. It's nice and compact, fits easily in my laptop bag.

title: Great for travel!
text: I selected this rolling backpack to carry my laptop and paperwork while I travel. It has worked out really great, especially on my most recent trip. It fits quite a few items, I had my laptop and my accordion file folder inside along with some personal items and it was easy to move around. It has loads of pockets to place most of the items I need handy while I'm traveling. I'm also able to maneuver it quite well along with my suitcase. It fit in the overhead compartment of the airplane with ease, and rolls with no issues.

title: Awesome smartwatch for a great price
text:
This lovely smartwatch packs all the bells and whistles of a name brand, but not at name brand price. The watch and the app were easy to set up and use, I really like the feature where I can use a photo on my phone as the watchface. It does a great job with sleep tracking, steps, and exercise. I can also set it to notify me and show texts from my phone. The alarm feature is nice, it wakes me up without waking my spouse too.

Even though the O2 and blood pressure aren't really for medical purposes, just for informational, they do seem to be close to what my actual readings are. So they do seem fairly accurate. I also like how there are a variety of exercises to choose from. The app links to Google Fit too, which is really nice. Battery life is quite good, I'm able to go a week before I need to charge again, and the watch charges to full within an hour or so.

I've tried a few different non-name brand smartwatches and this one by far is my favorite. I would definitely recommend it to others.

title: Fun cooling pad for my gaming laptop
text: There are a lot of things I like about this cooling pad. It has fun led lights I can set to a variety of color patterns, keeps my laptop cool, and I can raise up the back so my hand position is more ergonomic. I also like how small it is, I can fold it flat and easily take with me when I travel. It's made well, I've had no issues with it so far. The fan is a little noisy, but it doesn't bother me that much.

title: Good bag for smaller laptops
text: I would not recommend this bag for laptops bigger than 14 inches. It's nicely constructed, but on the small side. It is what it says though, durable and water resistant. It fits my 14 inch Asus nicely, plus the power supply & the mouse. It also has some pockets that could fit other items like your phone, pens, etc.

title: My favorite budget smart watch
text:
I've tried a variety of budget smart watches, and this one by Dr.Viva has become my favorite. It's very comfortable, great flexible band, no issues with feeling like it's pressing into my wrist bones. The screen display is a good size without being too large, perfect for smaller wrists.

The Zeroner app has been fantastic, no problems. It accurately tracks my steps, sleep & oxygen. I like how it has a variety of exercises for me to document. The battery life is a big winner. I recharge the smart watch once a week, compared to twice a week with the other watches I've tried before. I was disappointed that I don't have the option to have my own picture as the screen display, but the app still has plenty of screens to choose from.

If you're like me and don't want to spend an exorbitant price on a smart watch, but would still like to enjoy the features of a smart watch this one would be a great option.

title: Good for emergencies
text: I selected this radio to keep with the rest of our emergency supply kit. If you'd like to do the same, I'd recommend you charge the radio first before putting it away. You'll be working the hand crank for hours if you don't, and that's no fun if the power is out. Sound works pretty well, the light works great too. You'll want to hang onto the instruction because the buttons for the radio are not intuitive. I like how it has a usb output if you need to recharge your phone, but I too wish there was a storage area for the charging cable. I don't get a lot of direct sun where I am, so I don't think the solar panel would be that helpful for me, especially if there's a storm that knocks out the power. For the price though, I think this radio would be a good addition to your emergency kit.

title: Great price for a smart watch with lots of features
text: This smart watch has quite a few of the features that the name brand watches do, but without the name brand price. It keeps track of your steps, although it's a little over-sensitive and will count steps if all you do is move your arms like folding clothes or such. The sleep tracker is accurate, and so is the oxygen meter. I like how it has a variety of exercise types to choose from. The customizable watch face feature is great to. I like being able to use my favorite vacation picture as my watch face. I'd recommend this watch to anyone who'd like to try out a smart watch without paying a high price.

title: Fabulous smart watch for the value
text: This smart watch packs in a lot of great features for a really inexpensive price. The Inxfit app is very user friendly, easy to set up and quickly pairs to the watch. I like how I'm able to set goals, keep track of my sleep and activity. Steps & sleep readings are accurate, no odd variations. I like how it has a variety of watch faces, and the ability to make my own from a favorite photo from my phone. The watch is comfortable to wear, even for sleeping. No need to buy the expensive brand name smart watches, this one has them beat!

title: 5.0 not 5.1, works ok, static at long distance
text: I selected this bluetooth adapter for my daughter's computer so that she could use her wireless headphones with it. Overall, it does mostly do what it claims, but there are some issues. It found her headphones right away, but uses 5.0 tech, not 5.1. The sound works great if she remains in her room, but will encounter static at distances much less than 65'. The price is too high for what the adapter can do, and the static is very annoying.

title: Nice smart watch with a lot of great features
text:
If you cringe at the $$$ price of the brand name smart watches, I think this one by Eurans is a pretty good value. It still have quite a few features that are really nice. It tracks fitness, sleep, heart rate & O2 monitoring like a champ. The step counter is good too, fairly accurate compared to the Fitbit I previously wore. Pairing the watch to the app was a breeze.

I like how there's a good variety of fitness options to choose from, both indoor and outdoor. That's great when like me you like to do different types of exercise through the week to keep from getting bored or losing motivation. I'm very happy with the Fitdock app. No weird translation issues like with other apps I've tried. It's easy to understand, and it works well. It's fun to be able to use a picture from my phone as the background screen on my watch. The silent alarm works well too, it wakes me without waking my spouse, a great feature when couples are on different work schedules.

A couple of features I wish the smart watch had- the ability to monitor blood pressure (though I know it's not really a medically approved method), and a reminder to drink water. But these don't really detract from how nice this watch is, so I didn't remove any stars for it. I think this smart watch would make a great gift for someone who is interested in smart watches, but concerned about paying the high price for the brand name models.

title: Lovely little smartwatch, would make a great gift
text:
There are a lot of things I like about this smartwatch. The face is smaller than other smartwatches I've looked at and tried, about 1.09" which is perfect for me. Bigger faces like many smartwatches out there are uncomfortable for me to wear, especially when I'm trying to sleep. The design of the watch is really pretty, and I like how the neutral color goes with many outfits. One thing I do wish is that the watchband was changeable so that I could change it if the band wore out or broke (or if I wanted a different style). Most of the smartwatches with changeable bands are those with the large face, a little disappointing. Battery power is good. I use the smartwatch quite often so I tend to hook it up to the battery charger twice a week. I like how I could choose from a variety of screen displays to fit what my preferences are.

The app this smartwatch uses is great, the Da Fit app. It's super easy to use, you don't have to use Bluetooth to find the watch, you just use the app to find it. I like how it has a variety of physical activity you can choose to monitor, jogging, biking, walking, etc. The sleep feature is pretty good, the biggest detractor is that it only follows typical sleeping hours. It won't work for anyone who sleeps different hours due to working night shift. Hopefully they'll update that in the app someday. The blood pressure feature seems to be pretty accurate to what the doctor tells me my blood pressure is.

Since I really don't want to put out the money for the brand name smartwatches, I am very pleased that I can still enjoy quite a few of the features for a more reasonable price. I'd recommend this watch and it would make a great gift.

Update- After a couple weeks of use, the on/off button on the side of the watch popped off and a spring came out. It's so tiny I'm unable to find it. I wasn't using it excessively, so I'm disappointed that something on the watch would break within weeks of use. It's a really nice watch, and they have great customer care so hopefully my issue is not a common problem.

title: Great smartwatch for a good price
text:
If sticker shock with the brand name smartwatches have kept you from buying one for yourself, this watch packs a lot of punch for a very decent price. It has many of the options that the brand name watches have, but easier on the budget. Sleep monitoring, activity tracking, silent alarms, the weather and many more. It's a great watch. Battery life is on par with other watches, lasting close to a week.

Two small detractors that keep me from making this watch my favorite. The watch face is huge, too big for my wrist. On the one hand, it's nice because I can easily see it. But after wearing it for a while it's a little uncomfortable due to the size and I'm contemplating getting a smartwatch with a smaller face. The second problem is the alarm setting. I have an alarm set for 6am Monday-Friday. But the alarm is going off 6am Tuesday-Saturday. I've confirmed that the date is correct on my watch & phone so I'm not sure what's going on. Maybe it's an issue with the DaFit app? That aside, I still really like the watch.

title: Works great!
text: I've been using this cable on my nightstand to keep my phone charged for a couple of years now, and I'm very happy with it. I don't have issues with the cable kinking near the connectors, and I prefer braided cables to plastic. I plug in my phone before bed, and it's fully charged by the time I get up in the morning.

title: Looks Great but Inconsistent & Frustrating
text: Sadly this mouse did not give me the quality that I was expecting from a Corsair product. Their keyboards are great, but this mouse just doesn't stand up to the use that I need. It's a gorgeous mouse, and a comfortable ergonomic style. But the battery life was abysmal & the responsiveness was iffy. I ended up getting frustrated and going back to my Logitech mouse.

title: A must for laptops
text: I have a nice new gaming laptop and one of the first things I wanted for it was a good cooling tray. This cooling pad by Aicheson does the trick and it's reasonably priced. It does a great job of keeping the temp down, the lights are fun & I like how it has tilt options. It fits nicely in my laptop bag too.

title: Nice headphones at a great price
text: I selected these headphones for my daughter, as her old Sony headphones were falling apart. She likes these a lot, they're similar in style to her old favorites, plus they have pink accents which she loves. The sound is good, they're comfortable, and they're priced reasonably.

title: Built to last!
text: I am very happy with this braided USB to micro-USB. I took it to work and connected it to my computer so I can keep my phone charged up. It's great. The braided cable is awesome, I want to upgrade all of my charging cables to the type with a braided cable. Especially for the great price of the AmazonBasics brand. I would definitely recommend this cable to others.

title: Easy install, looks nice
text: Installation was a breeze, I followed the suggestion of installing them in a humid bathroom. That little tip really does help to cut down or even eliminate the lint. The anti-glare & anti-fingerprint finish is great, looks really nice.

title: Sturdy laptop bag
text: This laptop bag by Solo is nicely designed and well made. I like all the pockets & compartments it has, plenty of room for my laptop, tablet & accessories. The additional pockets for holding documents or ID is a nice feature, I also like the back strap for securing the bag to my luggage handle. As for the RFID blocking pocket, I'm not sure how helpful it is or not, but it doesn't detract from the bag so I don't mind it. The messenger bag is a pretty decent bag for the price.

title: Great sound, so comfortable
text: I have been through many different types of in-ear headphones over the decades, and these by Audio-Technica are by far the best I have ever used. Not only is the sound amazing, they are so incredibly comfortable too. I really like the wrap around cables, they are a great feature. The headphones are so comfortable too. One of my biggest complaints with ear-bud style headphones is that they start to hurt when wearing them. I haven't had that issue with these headphones. With the sound & the comfort, I think they're definitely worth the price.

title: More cables should be made like this!
text:
There is so much to love about this USB cable. Not only does it have the braided cable, but each end connection has extra enforcement that helps to avoid breaking after period of use. It's well worth the price, after dealing with cheap USB cables that come with my devices that crack where the cable meets the connector. It's expensive, but so is replacing those cheap plastic USB cables multiple times over the life of a device.

One thing I wish OtterBox would do, is to offer these in various lengths. I'd like to use one to connect my phone to my computer, so a shorter cable would be nice for that.

title: Inexpensive, simple install, does the job
text: My web cam bit the dust when it slipped and fell off my monitor, so I needed to pick up a new one. I decided to stick with Logitech, because I've been happy with their products for the most part. Installation was simple, I plugged it in and it was ready in a few seconds. The only thing I don't care for is the clip design. It's the same style as my previous camera (the C310), and the loose design doesn't make for a secure fit on top of the monitor. That's the reason why I went for the cheaper version this time, but hopefully I won't have another problem with clumsiness. Otherwise, I think it's a great camera.

title: I love how much storage I have for photos
text: I'm using the micro SD card with the adapter in my Canon PowerShot Elph 360. I love how much storage I have for photos, and the quality of the photos are great. It's easy to use, reasonably priced, and it's a brand I trust. I've been a fan of SanDisk products for years, and would recommend this SD card.

title: Inexpensive, does the job
text: They are simple and inexpensive earbuds that work as designed. Sound is crisp and clear. I especially like the small clip to secure the headphone wire to my shirt collar. That clip is my favorite feature of these headphones, I wish my others had this clip as well, but I can switch it to my other headphones, a nice touch. This is a good set to have for backup, or for when you don't want to spend much.

title: Absolutely amazing!
text:
Set up was an absolute breeze. I unhooked my old Samsung 22" flat LED monitor, plugged in this beauty and it started right up. Settings were off at first, but after fiddling with them, I am very pleased with how great it looks. Colors look amazing, very sharp and crisp. I thought the curve in the screen might bug my eyes, but they adjusted to it within a couple of hours. It doesn't bother me at all now.

I've been messing around with all of usual things I do on the computer, and I am liking all of them on this new monitor. I played some of my favorite games, wow. I am seriously blown away. Watched a couple episodes of Game of Thrones, and it looks incredible on the screen. Web browsing is very nice as well. I've been checking out the "Eye Saver" mode too. It's a little different, the slight yellow tinge I see while using it might take some getting used to. But, if it will help with eye strain I will definitely continue to work with it.

I've been a Samsung fan for monitors for a while now, and the CF591 is no exception. This is a fantastic monitor.

title: Great for computer backup, digital photos & videos
text: I have two of the Seagate 1TB external hard drives (one for me, one for my husband). We've been extremely happy with them so I was eager to try out the 5TB. I stored copies of all the photos I have from over the last two decades, family videos, scanned copies of important documents & files. It's amazing how much the drive can store. It doesn't bother me that it has to be powered by an ac adapter because I have it connected to my desktop computer. File transfer is fast, and luckily I've had no issues with heat. However, I still make sure nothing falls on or covers any part of the drive, just in case.  I think it's a great drive for the price.

title: Favorite trackball
text: I love this trackball so much I've bought one for my husband. I also bought a new one for myself, after my previous Kensington trackball started to fail after 3-4 years of use. One of my favorite features of it is how it can be easily switched for those of us who are left handed. I also like the scroll ring. The ball is easily removed for cleaning, and the shape is very comfortable. I've tried other trackballs that make my wrists ache. If I get 3-4 years of use out of this one I think $30 is well worth the price.

title: Well made case for Kindle Fire HD
text:
We have two Kindle Fire users in the family, our teen daughters, so I was looking forward to trying out this case. I was so pleased that I hopped on Amazon and bought a 2nd in blue. It's sturdy, and fits the Kindle Fire HD perfectly. The cutouts on the back match exactly where the volume & on/off buttons are, and also for the speakers. My daughters like how they can easily have their Kindle in whatever direction they want, vertical to read a book, or propped horizontal to watch a video.

The price of the case is right in line with other similar cases. It's strong & sturdy, not flimsy. I would definitely recommend this case for your Kindle Fire HD.

title: Very Happy!
text: After a dismal experience with a Patriot brand micro SD card (card died after a few weeks) I was eager to try the Samsung brand. I am very pleased with the card. I use it to save books, PDF files, & photos on my tablet. I have a Samsung Galaxy 2.0, a nice tablet but with limited storage space. By using this micro SD card I'm able to utilize my tablet more and get what I feel is full use out of it. The price was reasonable for the amount of storage on it, installation was quite simple, and it works extremely well on my tablet. I plan on buying a couple more for our cell phones.

title: Simple setup, works great!
text:
we are using the extender in a 2000 sqft one story home. We have our router set up in our family room at one end of the house, because that is where the cable connection is. Prior to obtaining the extender, we had issues getting a good signal at the other end of the house. Our laptops & tablets would consistently lose the signal or lag.

The Netgear Wi-Fi Extender has ended those issues, and we now have consistent signal everywhere in the house. Setup was simple, we followed the steps on the handy "Getting Started" installation paperwork. The extender has been placed at the midpoint of the house in the living room, so that there will be good coverage everywhere. I am able to get a good, consistent signal even at the very edge of the house in the master bathroom. No more issues for the laptops or tablets, we are quite pleased.

title: Only worked for 2-3 months
text:
Luckily I had nothing important on the card, just some saved tv shows for my tablet. It worked fine for a few months, then just suddenly stopped working. I'm glad I didn't spend that much on the SD card, but still, I didn't expect it to quickly fail like this. Next time, I suppose I'll pay a little more for a better brand. I thought Patriot was a trusted brand but I guess not.

If you want a cheap card that you don't save anything important on, perhaps this card is ok. But definitely do not save any pictures on it or anything else that you'd be sad to lose at a moment's notice. To the trash it goes, and I won't be buying this brand again.

title: Good choice for a first tablet
text:
Although I've been mucking around on a computer for many years now, this was my first venture into the tablet venue. I wasn't really sure what to buy. Do I go all out, buy a larger one with all the bells & whistles for the price of a base model laptop? Or do I stick with something simple & inexpensive?

I decided to go with the Samsung Galaxy Tab 2. The price was a definite consideration, I liked that it was under $200. I preferred to stick with name brand, as I've had too many friends who went with an inexpensive brand that broke within a few months. The size seemed sufficient for me to play some of the fun apps & keep notes for school.

It's been around 6 months since I first bought the tablet, and I'm overall pleased with it. I do wish it had two things. More storage, because the OS takes up a great deal of space. In hindsight, I would have paid more to have 16GB rather than 8. Also, I wish the charging port was a micro USB instead of 30 pin data port. My husband's Samsung Note has the micro USB and so does my daughter's Nexus 7. It would be really nice to be able to use other charging cords like they do (my husband can use his phone charger) than having to make sure I don't EVER misplace this one.

But for a simple tablet from a trusted brand, I do think the Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 is a good choice.

title: Roomy & Functional
text:
I have been a big fan of Case Logic for many years, all the way back to when I bought their storage case for my music CDs in the 90's. I still have that case and it's going strong. This messenger bag is no exception. It's built extremely well, with lots of pockets & space for all my camera gear. Everything is well padded. I tend to use a simpler camera for now, I'm not into multiple lenses (yet!) so right now I have room for both my camera & it's simple gear, plus my wallet as well. So I'm able to condense my bags when we go to Disney, which is really nice. When I do decide to start trying out the various lenses, there is plenty of room for them.

So if you're looking for a good camera bag that won't break your budget, stick with Case Logic. I've been very pleased with all their products so far.

title: Functional, but poorly designed
text:
This Belkin 8-outlet surge protector for the most part serves us well for plugging in our TV & entertainment center. I would have liked to use it for my desktop but the design has some flaws. Namely, anything with a DC converter ends up taking extra outlet space so I cannot use it & have every thing for my desk properly plugged in.

Like other reviewers have mentioned, there seems to be issues with the USB charging ports. I don't have much experience charging via USB port other trying with my computer. Attempting to charge my tablet via the USB port on my computer and the Belkin surge protector were equally disappointing. Slow as molasses in the dead of Winter. Is this a common issue or am I just unlucky? I'm going to go back to just using my regular charging cord & the outlet and not bother to try again.

In any case, I'm rather disappointed in this surge protector. Slow charging, poorly designed outlet spacing, & a high price makes it one that I would not recommend.

title: Good value for the price
text:
I purchased this stereo headset so that I can talk to my family members on Skype. It's a good, simple headset and not expensive. Granted, that could mean it might break quicker than other headsets. I will update this review if/when it breaks. As of now. The sound is clear and easy to understand, no static. I've also used it to listen to music & recorded TV episodes & movies. My family says that they can clearly hear me on the microphone. I'd say it's a good headset for the price.

Edit- I just wanted to add an update. I've been using this headset for over a year now with no issues. It's been a good purchase for me, well worth the price.

title: Good value for the price
text: I am using this webcam to keep in touch with my family via Skype. For the most part, it is working really well. The picture is clear and the audio for the built-in microphone is good. Installation was a breeze, all I had to do was hook it up and my computer searched for the drivers online and set it up for me. My only complaint is the short cord. I have my computer tower on the bottom shelf of my desk, under my monitor & keyboard. The cord barely reaches it, which is a concern for me.

title: Solid receiver with good sound
text: My husband & I are very pleased with the Harman Kardon audio/visual receiver. We have paired it with a set of speakers purchased from Fry's and our Samsung flat screen TV. Installation was easy for my tech-minded husband and it sounds great.

title: Great SSD drive for the price
text: Rather than replace an existing hard drive, we have chosen to install the Seagate in an external hard drive enclosure and use it as a backup drive. Installation in the enclosure was easy, and we had no issues when testing hooking it up to both the laptop and then the desktop. It's working very well as a backup drive, it's fast and we've had no failure problems. The hard drive enclosure we're using is made by Sabrent, but we bought it elsewhere. My only concern is that the enclosure can get a little hot, so I might look around more for an enclosure with a fan.

title: Good for a small family room, great price.
text:
This home theater system is working pretty well in our smaller-sized family room with our 42" Samsung flat screen TV. Our family room is on the smaller size, approx. 11 x 12 and open to the kitchen area. Installation was relatively simple once you completely read the instructions and/or have technical experience like my husband. He looked at the lengths of the wires and stated that if/when we move to a home with a bigger family room, it will be relatively simple to increase wire length. All you do is splice it to the bare wire end.

It sounds great, we haven't a problem with it. It's a good system for what we need, watching the occasional movie and our favorite TV shows.

title: Still going strong at 1.5 years
text:
Our daughters' charter school uses Kindle readers for their textbooks so we bought them each one Sept. 2011. Both Kindles are still working really well, and we're pleased with their durability. Because of the daily use during the week, they need to charge them every couple of days. But that is a simple matter to take care of. Once they've finished their homework they plug them in, then in the morning unplug before we head off for school. I have noticed that due to the frequent use, the numbers & letters have worn off of most of the keys. That could be a bit of an issue but the girls have memorized which key is for which letter or number.

I like how there's little to no glare in the sun, the Kindle is easier to read than other readers or a tablet. Because of the ease in obtaining books, especially many of the Classics for free, the Kindle has increased our daughters' love of reading even more. My one small complaint with the charger is that the white plastic cover on the cord is splitting near the end pieces. I've considered contacting Amazon regarding that because it's obvious that it's due to a defect. If I do, I'll update here.

Overall, we're very happy with Kindle and plan at some point to buy more readers for the rest of the family.

title: Sturdy, great sound, worth the price
text: We recently bought this for my husband to use in his garage workshop. He previously had a portable Memorex CD player/stereo that fell apart and wanted a replacement. We tried to with the inexpensive portable stereos you can find at Walmart, an RCA unit, but it was broken right out of the box. The CD player wouldn't even play. Because of of all the sawdust, grime, debris that comes with my husband's projects, I encouraged him to spend more for something that will do what he wants while lasting through the messes. The Sony ZSH10CP Heavy Duty CD Radio Boombox fits the bill. It's rugged and well made. The CD player doesn't skip if the boombox is bumped. He likes the rubber operating buttons and the sturdy latch for the CD player. The sound is excellent. He's really happy with it and so am I.

title: Works well, installation fiddly like all other protectors
text: I installed the protector film on each of my daughters' Kindle Keyboards. They use their Kindles for the charter school they attend so protector film is a must have. The installation was no easier or more difficult than any previous protection film I've used before, make sure the screen is clean, use a lint free cloth, gently rub out the bubbles, etc. The film is similar to the type that I had on their Kindle screens, just with the nice addition of the anti-glare. My daughters like their Kindles so much that they read books on them all the time, not just their text books. So they're very happy with the anti-glare feature. Like other reviews mentioned before, there is a slight gap where the protector film does not cover the screen.

title: Works great, even on eyeglasses!
text: I have used the Audiovox Surface SURF200N on our two flat screen TVs, my computer monitor, our family's 3 laptop monitors, the display on my Samsung phone, and yes, even our eyeglasses. It works fantastic, cleans the dust, smudges, fingerprints, you name it. The cleaning cloth is plush and absorbent, but doesn't leave lint on the screen. My husband is so pleased with the product, everything we'd previously tried left smudges or didn't clean the screen well. I see that Audiovox does have a version specifically for eyeglasses, the 60N. Since I've been so happy with how well the 200N cleaned our glasses, I think I'll definitely pick up some of the 60N for future use.

title: Either I receive a dud or it doesn't work with Windows 7
text:
I picked this external hard drive due to the reasonable price and because it said in the description that it's compatible with Windows 7. What a disappointment. It worked for all of about 30 seconds. Then I got the "A drive is not formatted" error and it shut down completely. I've never been able to get it to do anything since, my computer doesn't even recognize it now. I tried our laptops too, and they don't "see" the it either. It's as if it died.

I don't know if I got a dud or not. The pamphlet in the box said it's compatible up to XP. So why say it's compatible up to Windows 7 in the description here? Seems a bit dishonest. I would have looked for another external drive if I'd known. In any case, I'm returning for a refund and looking for a better product. I'd proceed with extreme caution when considering purchasing this. It's a shame because TEAC is otherwise a brand I've had good experience with.

title: Functional and lovely to look at as well
text: I am extremely pleased with this cookware set. I've had Teflon-coated cookware in the past, and everything still stuck to it. So I was amazed with how everything I've cooked on these just slides off. Clean up is a breeze too, soapy water & a sponge takes it all off. I like the handles for the pots & the lids too. They stay cool and rubberized coating on the handles help to give a good, strong grip, even when your hands are wet. The bronze color is lovely too, and would look nice in most kitchens. We retired our old cookware after the first meal! My only minor complaint is that there should be a vent hole in the lids. But otherwise this set is well worth the money spent.

title: Works very well, but way overpriced
text: In regards to quality, I am quite pleased with this cooling pad. It does the job quite well, and is rather quiet too. But not for this price, they're asking too much in comparison to others on the market. There are plenty of similar cooling pads who work as nicely for much less. Drop the price by at least 25% and I'd definitely recommend it to others.

title: Perfect for my phone
text: My digital camera is quite large, so I actually use this for my cellphone. It's perfect for my phone, and keeps it safe in the large bag I tote around.

title: Amazing desktop replacement
text: Fully loaded.  Crystal clear huge 18.4 inch 1920 X 1080 HD LCD backed by NVIDIA's GForce 9600M GT card w/512 ram, Blue Ray DVD ROM, full size keyboard with numeric pad and 64 bit Vista Home Premium OS.  Quick to set up, not too much bloatware.  Runs graphic intensive programs quite well however a cooling tray such as NZXT's Cryo LX would be beneficial.  Not a laptop, somewhat heavy, not something to easily tote from place to place unless you have a rolling case for it.  Highly recommended for anyone looking for a desktop replacement with the advantage of being mobile.

title: My personal favorite
text: I have tried various mice & trackballs over the years and have found this one to be the best fit for me. Compared to other trackballs I have tried, this model where my thumb moves the ball gives my hand the least amount of strain. It feels more natural to have the ball under my thumb as opposed to under my other fingers. Other models cause my hand to ache. Also, with the limited space I have in the keyboard tray of my desk a trackball is a better choice for me than a mouse. I have also found that the Logitech model stands up to longer use. When the time comes that I need to purchase a new one, I will buy this model again.

title: Still going strong after four years
text:
My husband bought me this camera as a surprise Christmas present about four years ago and it quickly became my favorite camera. It has been my camera of choice for two trips to Disneyland, a trip to Disney World and a cruise. It's a fantastic camera, and very easy for someone not technologically skilled like me to understand how to use. Battery life is great, I'm able to go through about two days of consistent use on our trips before I need to recharge. Speaking of which, recharging is a cinch, I bring the little charger, plug it in at the hotel room in the evening and by the next morning I'm ready to go (usually takes less than that but I plug it in and go to bed).

My only problems have been with trying to use the camera in lower lighting situations, like at my children's school assemblies and performances. Perhaps I'm not using the settings correctly but those pictures are coming out too dark with the colors off.

This has been one of the best presents ever. We're headed for another trip next year and this camera will be on my "must pack" list.

title: Worked ok for 1 1/2 years, then died
text:
We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.

title: Great, Professional, and Excellent at Doing What it was Made to do.
text:
After doing some research, I read that these headphones are the best "bang for your buck" earbuds and so far, they aren't wrong. This product does some with six different silicon eartips, an small instruction booklet, and a small but durable pouch to put your eartips and buds in. It took me about five minutes find the perfect removable eartips for my ears. It would have been shorter but I was afraid of tearing the silicon tips (so far none have ripped). Everybody's ears are different but my ears prefer the smallest snowman shape ones for both my right and left ear (Pictures of the tips can be found in the 'Wired' only version of this product).

They are easy to clean and the remote is secure (meaning that the remote button or volume slider won't move or activate if it accidentally hits your clothes or something). I haven't used the microphone yet. These things are very secure once you install them in your ears. You can talk, yawn, chew gum, run, jump and drink water and these tips wouldn't budge (you can take them out easily though). The sound quality and noise blocking are great too for when I run. It also works well for people that wear glasses like me.

However I have two small issues with this product. One is that the wire is a little long for me but it usually doesn't get in your way (only once so far but this was my second time using them). You may experience burning in your ears. I did at first when I was trying to find the best way to wear them. For me (using the smallest snowman ones), You just put them before the ear canal so the silicon tips rest comfortably in your ears. Don't push/force them in your ears because that will cause your ears to burn.

In conclusion, if you're looking for the best sleek 'bang for your buck' earbuds that stay secure during rigorous activity who doesn't mind a little burning in your ear canals at first, then I would recommend this product and I'll probably buy it again when/if this product wears out.

Edit: Just after a month of use the the remote button is a little glitchy. Before it could be resting against by chest while running and it would work fine. Now while running, I have to pull it about 5 inches away from my body and point the the top of the headset (where it branches off into two) at about a 45 degree angle in order to pause/skip a song. It's kind of cumbersome and if it didn't do this then I'd definitely rate it higher.

Edit: The sellers were very prompt and understanding with my situation and I got a new pair for free (under warranty). I've been using them for a couple of months and I haven't noticed any problems with them.

title: Great Product! But even better customer service!
text:
I bought this EVGA CLC 280/280mm AIO a few months ago but I wanted to try it out for a while before I left a review to really get a chance to see how it performs over a longer period of time.

Firstly, I am running this AIO on an i7 8700K WITH an overclock of 5GHz on all cores. With this AIO my idle temperatures are in the mid to high 20C range and under full load it warms up to the low to mid 80s C. This is great performance for such a high overclock. With stock clock speeds this AIO should perform much better and shouldn’t go above 65C during full loads.

Secondly, I want to share my experience with EVGA’s superb customer service. When I installed this AIO I had a problem with the RGB not working. I tried reinstalling it, using different motherboard plugins for the cables, but nothing seemed to fix it. Finally I contacted EVGA by email. They mentioned that the USB cable could be defective. Here is what amazes me: EVGA sent me a brand new USB cable at no cost to myself and they didn’t even make me go through the hoops and hassle of sending my product back, paying for shipping, waiting for processing, etc., they just sent me a brand new cable and THEY paid to have it shipped. I got it 2 days later.

That is the kind of customer service I love and is the reason I try to buy EVGA products when possible. Most companies will not do that. They’ll put you through the hassle of many steps and lots of waiting around and processing which discourages a lot of customers, such as myself, from even bothering to contact them when something goes wrong.

All in all, a great product with even better customer service!

Thank you EVGA!

title: Great SSD for SMALL workloads.
text:
I’ve had this SSD for a few days and I also have a 1TB 970 Evo Plus and 1TB 860 Evo and all of them are great! But they do have their drawbacks too.

This drive does really well with SMALL (under 15Gb) workloads. The speeds are right up there (~500MB/s R/W) with my 860 Evo until it gets to about ~14GB at which point it slows down drastically. This is fine for things like boot, games, apps, and most programs.

However, if you do heavy workloads like video editing, file transfers, etc,. where you are regularly moving large (15GB+) files around this is NOT the drive for you. If you are a “heavy” user I highly recommend the 860 Pro. It can keep up those high R/W speeds without slowing down after ~15GB. It will maintain full speed throughout the duration of whatever you are doing.

With that said this is a great drive for light/moderate workloads (gaming, web browsing, small work files, etc.,) and it is at a price that gives you excellent value and quality for your money.

I also really love the Samsung Magician software. It’s basically the main reason why 3/5 of my drives are Samsung. Samsung is also known for making reliable, high quality products. Yes there is a premium compared to cheaper drives but you’re paying that little bit extra for quality & reliability.

I took off 1 Star on this review though because Samsung doesn’t include any of the cables or mounting screws which just doesn’t make sense to me. C’mon Samsung start adding that stuff! I would’ve happily paid a couple dollars more for it and it wouldn’t have cost Samsung that much so they could’ve made a little bit of extra profit by adding it.

I still recommend this drive though and would buy it or the 860 Evo again if I needed more storage.

title: Got this for my 1TB Samsung 860 Evo and it works great!
text: Not much to say about this product. It works great with my Samsung 860 Evo and that's all I wanted it to do. If you need a good SATA cable I would recommend this one. It's a fair price for what you get.

title: Great SSD for the price
text:
Update: I see a lot of people complaining about the drive capacity being “wrong” (465gb instead of 500gb or 960gb instead of 1TB) and to those people I highly recommend going to YouTube and searching “What is Overprovisioning?” and clicking on the link by TechQuickie.

Samsung is NOT falsely advertising. The drive DOES in fact come with the advertised space it’s just that in order for it to work properly and perform optimally it requires approximately 10% of the capacity to be overprovisioned free space.

This is a really great SATA SSD for the price. It's perfect for storing games that have long load times without paying a fortune for an NVMe SSD of equal capacity. I highly recommend it for people like me who need more space for games, projects, and other things like that who want them to load quickly. You can get an HDD like a WD Black for cheaper but the loading times will be much longer and for those who dont like to wait for long load screens this is a perfect choice.

Also don't forget to enable RAPID mode. It uses RAM to speed up the programs & applications that you have been using recently. My CrystalDisk benchmark shows how fast it is with RAPID mode enabled.

title: Great PSU that will last for years!
text:
Update: 8/15/2021
I’ve now had this PSU for nearly 2 years and it’s performed beautifully since the day I bought it. I haven’t had any problems whatsoever.

I just got this PSU a few days ago and I really like it. This is an upgrade from my Cooler Master 750W 80+ (non-bronze/gold etc.,) PSU and I’m glad I got it.

The all-black cables look really nice and don’t clash with other aesthetics like ketchup & mustard cables on a lot of other lower quality PSUs do.

This comes with plenty of cables and I’m not using most of them but it’s nice that they are there.

I also think the little bag of zip ties they throw in is a nice touch. I actually ordered a bag of zip ties with this because I didn’t know it came with them and I didn’t even use them because Corsair had me covered.

All in all this is a high quality PSU with 80+ Gold certification and 850W which is more than enough to handle almost any system build that a normal, everyday computer will need. It will definitely future proof your system as you won’t have to replace your PSU for a LONG time.

Corsair also has a very nice 10 year warranty on this PSU which just goes to show how much faith they have in the quality and durability of this product.

title: Everything fits, great price, not bad!
text:
UPDATE (4 -> 5 stars)/ 9/20/2013 - This thing is $28 now! You'd be nuts NOT to get this case! I'm pretty sure they're taking a loss selling it at that price, maybe they're overstocked and trying to get rid of them? If you're going to buy this case BUY IT NOW!

Firstly, I just want to say if you want to SEE my PC check out the last 3 customer uploaded images, they are of my newly built PC in this case. If you can't find customer images, go to the main product page for this case, and click "See all 5 customer images", it's right under the picture of the case.

My current specs:
CPU: AMD FX 8320 (3.5GHZ stock) Overclocked @ 4.22 GHZ
CPU Cooling: Corsair H80 High Performance Liquid Cooling System
Motherboard: Gigabyte FX 990 UD3 AM3+
Power Supply: Rosewill Capstone 750W 80+ Gold certified.
SSD: Sandisk 32GB (I just use it for my operating system for quick bootups, nothing else.)
HD: Seagate Barracuda 1TB 64MB cache 7200 RPM SATA III
Graphics: Geforce 760 GTX 4GB 256bit GDDR5 (When I was deciding whether or not to order this case, this was my biggest concern, "Will one of the new big geforce graphics cards fit?" - YES it will! I MIGHT be able to fit another one in, but I really don't need another one, the 760 is a beast!)
Ram: 16GB Gskill Sniper Series DDR3 2400

Whew, now having said all that, EVERYTHING fits in this case. Is it a little bit snug? See for yourself, I don't think so, but some might. I also got a non-modular power supply so that adds alot of unnecessary cables.

The fact is though, my computer does NOT overheat. I monitor temps whenever my computer is on (with CPUID, free program!) and as an example, under a full load my CPU temp stays ~20C and my GPU can get up to ~60C on a warm day. Keep in mind though for the CPU I'm using a $104 liquid cooling system (I just happened to get a GREAT deal on it).

The see-through case is pretty cool too, I like being able to see the components plus with a liquid cooling system if any liquid starts leaking I can immediately take care of it, although I highly doubt it will leak.

Anyway, I hope this review helps, keep in mind I put alot of stuff in here with the 4 ram modules, and the pretty large graphics card (the Geforce 760 GTX is about 11.5" long, it's pretty big), but it does all fit!

Keep in mind this is a ~$50 case. For $50 it is a good deal, if you want a "better" case, you're going to have to spend more money it's as simple as that. People nitpick things like a flimsy backplate, or not having the best cable management, well the more you expect from a product the more you're going to end up paying for it. So take it easy on a $50 case.

I can say for sure it's better than my old HP desktop PC computer case. It actually FEELS like a gamer's case.

So all-in-all, if you're on a budget and looking for a nice computer case for $50 I recommend this case. It's got everything I needed and it's got everything 90% of people will need or care about. I'd buy it again.

title: Working Thus Far
text:
My modem was 6 years old and wasn't working properly anymore. I did not want to pay the $150 for a new modem that Centurylink was offering. I found this product and decided to take a chance with it.

Set up was surprisingly not too much of a headache. I plugged in the power cable, the phone line cable, and then I plugged an Ethernet cable in from the modem in to my laptop. These three cables were included with the product. I did call the Centurylink technical support. She asked for the serial number on the modem to connect the modem to their network. After that, it was very simple, I entered in to the browser "connect.centurylink.com" and it gave step by step instructions. Once internet was connected, I set up a new SSID and WiFi password by entering in the modems IP address: 192.168.0.1. Everything is up and working as it should. I will update this review if I have problems in the future. I would like this modem to last at least a couple years.

The seller included a page of set up instructions/hints and it was complete garbage. It was broken English and misspelled words. It wasn't helpful in the slightest. Don't bother using it. Information was incorrect even. The IP address given is for an older model modem.

title: Gave me a seasick feeling
text: I was so excited to try these and wanted to love them. I’m a hardcore Tacx user and have used a Neo most weeks for 5-10 hours/week for the past several years. They were definitely easy to unbox and install, it took about 5 minutes to get it set up. But after several hour rides, I couldn’t get used to the feeling of rocking back and forth. It made me feel a little bit nauseous, similar to the feeling I get on boats. If I kept my power really low and smooth, I would sometimes forget the plates were there. But any time my power increased, I felt a little sick.  Any large surge from sprinting was especially bad, but even small surges in power from shifting were enough to make me feel seasick from the rocking. Also looking down at the ground and seeing the bike move back and forth wasn’t great either. I tried to get used to it, but after several rides decided it wasn’t worth it to try to get used to something that is so expensive when I was happy with the trainer before. Thankfully popping off the plates and returning it was an easy process, so I don’t regret trying them.

text: Within a minute of taking this out of the box, I had it paired with my iPad. It was seriously so easy to just pair and go, and I love how it can be paired with three different things (just push a little button on the bottom of the mouse to switch between computers/iPads). It feels okay in my hand - not the highest quality I’ve seen (plastic is very basic and it is pretty lightweight as well), but it doesn’t feel cheap. The color is so fun, which is the main reason I got it. Also it is very quiet and doesn’t have any loud clicking. The one thing to mention is that the circle button under the scrolling wheel doesn’t have any functionality with an iPad. Nothing was happening when I kept clicking it to try and use the emoji shortcut, so after heading over to Logitech’s website i saw “*Emojis and software are currently supported on Windows® and macOS only.” So maybe iPadOS will eventually support this capability, but as of now it is useless. Overall I still like the mouse a lot for it’s ease of use, quietness, and color.

title: Amazing sound, but its height may be a problem for some setups
text:
This is an excellent sound bar. The details in the music and movies I listened to were incredible. I had nothing to complain about with my old Visio sound bar, but this DALI blows that one away. (Which is to be expected since it is about 6 times more expensive). The range and clarity of the sound is far beyond what I’ve experienced before. Also, despite the Visio having a separate subwoofer, I cannot tell any difference with regards to bass performance.

Just be aware that this sound bar is tall. I cannot put it directly in front of my 47 in tv because it blocks the bottom portion of the screen. I think the size is worth the sound quality, and I will have to figure out how to arrange everything so they work well together.

If you can afford the steep price tag, I highly recommend this sound bar.

title: High quality and works great
text:
This is a very nice charging cord. The braided sheath looks good and has a solid feel. The connectors are also well made and feel heavy duty.

As an added bonus, the cord itself is 6 feet long, so the overall length is a little bit longer because of the connectors. I have another charging cord that was listed at 6 feet, but it is actually 4 inches short. I never would have noticed or measured it had I not tried this one. The other brand was cutting some corners, but that is not the case with this cord.

I highly recommend this charging cord.

title: Without question this is one of my new favorite things
text:
These earbuds combine incredible sound in a stylish and functional package. I would give these more than 5 stars if I could. I had high expectations before trying these, especially in view of the price, and these earbuds blew those away.

Bang & Olufsen's engineers magically crammed a high-end sound system into a lightweight, wireless earbud. You have to hear them to believe how amazing these sound - clean, clear music across an impressively wide range. I noticed details for the first time in songs that I have heard many times before.

Beyond the sound, the craftsmanship and overall product design are outstanding. I don't know about the electronics as only time will tell, but the earbuds and the case themselves look like they will hold up to regular use without any issues. The leather and brushed aluminum on the case adds an extra-premium feel to the product.

Also, at first I thought the charging capability of the case was a bit gimmicky, but I quickly realized my error. It is so convenient to know that the earbuds are fully charged whenever I want to use them. I don't have a Qi charger, so I haven't taken advantage of the full wireless capability. But for me, it is not a big deal to use the USB cord when I need to occasionally charge the case.

To give some context, this is not a product I would have considered purchasing on my own. I've always thought of earbuds as cheap, portable ways to listen to music while working out or on the go - situations where the background noise means that you can't appreciate high-quality sound. However, after jumping at the chance to try these, they have completely changed my perspective on what earbuds can do. Excellent sound quality is available in a highly portable, convenient product.

The only downside I have experienced is that the touch controls take some time to get used to. I had trouble figuring it out at first, but after a few days I can usually get them to do what I intend to do on the first try. I prefer the minimalistic design, so this learning curve is not a significant issue for me.

I also like the Bang & Olufsen music app that allows selection of different listening modes that vary between - "warm", "excited", "relaxed", or "bright" sound profiles. Switching between the modes really gives the sound a different character. My favorite feature on the app, however, is the ability to select "transparency" of the music. A higher level of transparency amplifies your surroundings so you can hear what is going on around you. This does not give you spy-gadget levels of hearing, but it noticeably amplifies background sounds. I've been using these headphones at work, and I can easily hear when my phone rings or when someone knocks on my office door.

Last, the excellent sound quality carries over to phone calls. I have no trouble hearing the other person on the line, which is not always the case with the built-in speaker on my iPhone. Also the people I have talked to have had heard me clearly. This was an unexpected bonus, and I actually prefer to use the earbuds for calls now.

TL;DR: If you can afford these, you won't regret it.

title: Knockoff brand works for *SOME* Sirius and XM 5 volt radios
text:
Buyer beware. The item that I rec'd is not a Sirius brand adapter as described in product name. The product # that I rec'd is model #SMPS5V2A-XM. There is no red light indicator as described.

This power adapter does NOT fit *ALL* Sirius and XM 5 volt satellite radios. This adapter does not fit an old Sirius radio "SV1" model which is a 5 volt model, the tip is too small for this model.

This adapter does fit an old XM radio "XM2go" model which is a 5 volt model, and works well.

But it is much cheaper than buying the Sirius brand adapter, and it works if the tip size is correct for the radio model. For that I give it 3 stars.

Side note on satellite radios: Sirius and XM satellite radios are not one and the same, and neither are the subscription channels...depends on what your radio receives. The Sirius & XM radios are made differently and the stations that they receive are different. On that note, be sure to check with SiriusXM.com for specific subscription costs before you buy a radio to help you choose whether you want a Sirius or XM radio.

I learned this the hard way. I hope this saves you some time and hassle.

title: Very thorough, lightweight software
text:
I have been running Internet Security for several months and have been very happy. I am sticking with this program in lieu of the more expensive and boggy "Total Protection" ... a so called upgraded version.

I prefer this basic lightweight version of McAfee Anti Virus/Malware protection, it doesn't bog down your system. The cache cleaner (QuickCleaner) is also very handy.

** Better yet/Best deal: buy the 2010 or 2011 subscription version and McAfee automatically downloads the 2013 updated files for 1 year.
[[ASIN:B003VUNYIG McAfee Internet Security 2011 - for up to 3-Users]]
McAfee Internet Security 2010 or 2011 - for 1 or up to 3-Users (currently selling for $1 - $7) Screaming deal!

Your subscription is good for 1 year from the time that you install.

Never renew through McAfee, too pricey. Just buy another old version and update the license code.

I tried the McAfee Total Protection version and hated it. Super Boggy software. After 1 week the software broke and would not update, created registry errors, and hosed up my pc. The File Lock "feature" kicked in with every attempt to update and I had to reboot to reconnect to the internet every hour or two while troubleshooting the problems myself. Pain in the behind. Don't do it!

Forget about "Technical Support" from McAfee. They claim 24/7 support, which will get you their super slow Chat "support". The Call Center doesn't work 24/7. Go figure. Both Chat and/or thier phone/remote assistance is a joke, plan on spending up to an hour while you wait for the connection, then wait longer while they muddle their way through an attempt at troubleshooting. Either way, you will eventually be connected to an unnamed Eastern country, and waste a whole lot of time and patience dealing with those numb nuts. I swear during the 3 contacts that I made to them, they must have been texting their buddies while I waited for responses which came at a snails pace (over 5 minutes for each response, no kidding!). I ended up uninstalling myself after 1 hour on my 3rd tech support call they wanted to uninstall it for me and reload. No I don't think so. I permanently uninstalled and went back to Intenet Security.

Travel light and go with the basic Internet Security version for AV & malware protection. It has all of the basics: firewall, AV scanner (email, realtime & scheduled scans), online backup addon, network protection, cache cleaner, email anti spam, and parental controls. That is all that I have needed, and have been happy with it. Hopefully I won't ever have to deal with their under qualified tech staff again.

Other options: Kaspersky is great software, but boggy and too many options to set up. I also used AVG in the past, but it didn't offer the best protection and I had undetected invasions. ESET has the best reputation, but I have never used it.

Steer clear of Norton for AV/Malware: generates a migraine magnitude headache. Nothing but problems. However, their Ghost program is good.

I hope that this review saves you some money, time, and frustration.

text: What an improvement over the package of junk I got from Best Buy!

title: As described and really looks nice
text: The majority of the cons I read before purchasing were about the slot for the apple pen being on the wrong side. I don’t use the apple pen so that isn’t an issue for me. This protects my iPad Air 2022 beautifully. I got the black version based on reviews saying that the lighter colors tend to get dirty. The black looks great and I haven’t had any issues. It also holds the iPad up really nicely. I highly recommend!

title: Love it!
text: Love the color and that it’s a matte finish. It’s plastic and doesn’t have any rubber or rubber like material. Does the job of protecting my 2015 MacBook Pro from scratched.

title: The absolute cutest!
text: I adore this wireless mouse! I bought it to liven up my workspace and get rid of my wired mouse. I am so happy with my purchase. I bought my mom the RJ one and she loves it too! It’s very comfortable to use and while I wouldn’t say it’s exactly silent, it is much quieter than a regular mouse. I also love that you can store the USB connector inside the mouse when traveling to avoid losing it. The only thing that could have made this mouse even better is if it scrolled right and left too, but it’s not so sever that it merits less stars. It utilizes a USB connector and is not a Bluetooth mouse. It is battery powered and comes with the battery out of the box.

title: Perfect gift for my mom!
text: So cute! Got it for my mom who recently became a fan. She loves it! So easy to install. I got the Koya one for myself.

title: Great for Macbook Pro Retina 15"
text: Really solid piece of equipment. It's packaged extremely well which only adds to the product experience. Fits and holds my Macbook Pro Retina 15" perfectly. Very sturdy. I was worried it would not bring my Macbook to eye level but it does, I would have maybe added an extra inch to the height but that's just my preference. The stand also adds a sleek finish to my workspace which is much better than the stack of books I was using before. I read some reviews that mentioned how perfect it was for Macbooks, as if Apple had made it themselves. It's true. It matches Apple's design perfectly down to the quality. All in all I am very pleased with my purchase.

title: Good but short life.
text:
I've had this for about two years and last year it was dead. It resides in a portable enclosure and the enclosure suddenly wouldn't read the SSD. Before contacting customer service, I tried different cables, machines, and ports. Finally, after contacting customer service, I was informed it needed to be replaced, which Crucial did without issue.

But when it works, it works great. It's fast and doesn't cause problems between devices.

title: Not bad.
text:
Was actually pleased by the caps when they arrived. I used to be particular about keycap quality, but in the last few years the quality and cost of keycaps have been awesome; I'm so thrilled about those new to the hobby (although it's still expensive). When GMK 9009 was originally announced, I thought it was the perfect modern edition of classic beige. Everyone should have a good classic beige set, and 9009 is it.

Right now, my workhorse keyboard is a polycarbonate 910 with Cherry MX Grays and third-party springs (I forget the weight). Typing on it is a dream every day, and the keycaps can enhance the experience. I prefer PBT on this keyboard because it has a more pleasant, thocky sound than ABS caps. There's also a bit of tactile pushback with ABS, at least from what I noticed. While I love 9009, I'm not thrilled about ABS. Sure, ABS is cool and develops a nice shine based on use, but I prefer the consistent feel of PBT; having some keycaps stripped of their coating from use while others still feel new can throw me off. All that to say that I'm glad I was able to get this 9009 set in PBT. I was very hesitant, though, because the price for this many dye-sublimated, PBT keycaps was too good to be true.

When the package arrived, I was disappointed to find that there was no shipping box. The keycaps arrived in their manufacturer box with a shipping label slapped on it. Not only can that increase the chances of theft, but the shipping label covers the rendering that shows all the keycaps included. So now I'll have to resort to the listing to see what all should be in the box. However, nothing appears damaged. The keycaps come in wonderfully secure, plastic trays, three stacked on each other. There are a lot of keycaps here, so most keyboards should be covered. Of course, not everything will be perfect; for my 910, the Home cap is taller than the rest of the row, and there is no 1u Tab cap, nor a R1-height Fn cap. There's only one 1u blank keycap, which doesn't sit flush with the rest of the caps in its row. Minor gripes because I know my layout is particular.

But, again, there still is a great amount of keycaps so I'm sure most boards will be covered.

Now, as for the keycaps themselves. As I mentioned, I was very hesitant when the package arrived, but overall I'm pleasantly surprised. The keycaps are slightly thinner than enjoyPBT and BSP caps, and the stem can be a bit snug, but not too tight so that they don't come off easily. The sublimation is very good; I haven't noticed any that appear sloppy. Some num pad legends seem a bit thinner than others, but overall the legends are consistent and have that Cherry-legend appearance.

I wish there were more color options here, but for the price I can't complain. Truly, at $40, this set is an amazing bang for the buck.

title: The box could use a different latching mechanism if regular access is needed.
text:
The boxes are fine and do their job fittingly. The lids have a pleasant wood grain printing, but if you look closer the printing's blurriness shows.

Two of the boxes are used to store a circuit breaker that is rarely accessed. The other, however, gets opened a lot for charging devices.
