title: Enterprise/LTE/4G version works with Verizon
text:
Do not buy this if you're looking for the fastest tablet. That's not what it is, though it's by no means slow. It will take a lot more abuse than the fastest tablets available for the same price. You can stand outside in the rain or snow and use the touchscreen when it's wet. You can drop it in the mud, pick it up, wipe it off, and keep using it. I wouldn't take it scuba diving though. I will take it off-roading. This one has enough storage to preload maps for off-road hiking/biking/riding/driving for when there's no signal at all.

I've seen several questions about whether this works with Verizon, and several people answer that it doesn't. Those people are wrong. The Enterprise/LTE/4G/WiFi version does work with Verizon. It should work with others. Find this model number (SM-T577UZKGN14) on the Samsung site to check. Samsung knows. Those other people don't.

This is the third tablet I've used my Verizon SIM card in. The first was a tablet I bought through Verizon. The second was a TabActive2, and now I'm using the same SIM card in this TabActive3. This does not apply to the WiFi-only version. Don't confuse the two.

I pulled the SIM card out of the TabActive2, inserted it in the TabActive3, restarted the device as requested, and a few minutes later the line was active on the new device. I ignored Verizon's emailed instructions, because they don't appear to apply to swapping a current SIM card into a new device. I even restored a Google backup from the 2 to the 3 and saved a lot of time installing apps.

So, why this tablet? It's rugged. It's Samsung. I really like having an 8" tablet. It works with Verizon.

Why 4G/LTE? It's not 5G. I drive a truck through at least 5 states on a regular basis, and in some areas the signal constantly switches between 4G and 5G and the data connection is interrupted. When I can't access online banking, credit cards, and apps relating to business with my 5G phone, I often can with a 4G tablet. I have unlimited data on a second plan for only $10/mth, since I already have a smartphone plan. No hotspot/WiFi needed.

Why upgrade? My TabActive2 only had 16GB of internal storage. The TabActive3 I bought has 128GB. The TabActive3 has DEX. The TabActive2 didn't. I didn't manage to hurt the 2, and the 3 is physically very similar. The 3 has a faster CPU, and a faster GPU.

From the beginning, everything about the TabActive2 as a usable tablet simply wasn't enough. It wasn't fast enough. It didn't have enough storage. But it was rugged. It still is. This is the first time I've upgraded when the old tablet still worked as well as it did when I bought it. It appears that the TabActive3 is just as rugged.

Con: The biggest downside to these is that there's no external charger that I can find for the replaceable battery. At least I can't find one. Maybe one exists. I have no evidence of that. It is possible to buy another compatible battery, but I can't find any way to charge said battery other than to charge it in the tablet, and it's a pain to get to, because of the lengths Samsung went to to seal the battery compartment. The battery life is substantial, partly due to the less-than-premium performance, but it would really be nice to be able to easily carry a fully-charged spare.

title: Usually cheap enough for off-line storage
text: The price of these is usually low enough to consider buying them new for off-line storage. Something most people don't consider using a hard drive for. 4TB has become small for my purposes, but as off-line storage I don't want to risk more than that on one drive. It's much simpler to archive data on a 4TB hard drive in a dock and keep it in a case than to burn 4TB to a stack of Blu-Ray disks every few months, and DVDs are completely out of the question. I'm archiving around 20TB of 4K video that I've captured with GoPros so far. Most of it is on "retired" drives, but I've run out of reliable older drives and I think I'll be upgrading to these in the future. They're unlikely to store data forever without some degradation, but rewriting the data once a year won't wear them out for decades. These will not work well in an NAS or even a RAID array in a PC, and shouldn't be used in a PC with more than one or two hard drives anyway. They're not designed to cope with vibration from several other drives, but as a single drive or for data backup they're fine. It's a capable drive for typical home use. For full-time use in an array, the Red Plus and Red Pro drives are what I get. If you need to store large amounts of data off-line, or if you just need a new drive in a home PC, this is a good choice.

title: 4 years and counting
text: I bought this in March of 2018 and it still works and looks great. It's now my 4th monitor in the array, and I only use it for performance monitoring apps now. The other three are 28" 4K monitors. I had previously used it with other PCs in other locations, but it's never been one of my primary monitors. So, it doesn't have the hours on it a monitor of this age would normally have. The price fluctuates considerably. $200 and below is somewhat reasonable. $300 and above is ridiculous. If it ever drops below $150 I'll buy another one, just to have one. I paid just over that in 2018.

title: No longer available
text: I bought one of these on Apr 15, 2020. I've had no issues with it. Another similar dock will not read all drives correctly. This one does. I've reformatted, repartitioned, used diskpart to clean drives up to 10 TB with it. Unfortunately, it's no longer available, because I need another one to replace the other dock I bought that claims it does everything this one does, but doesn't. Oh well.

title: Almost works
text: I've used this dock quite a bit over the past few months, but today I ran into an issue that renders it useless to me. An 8TB drive that was partitioned on another PC as a GPT partition, shows up when inserted into this dock as a GPT Protected Partition, meaning it's inaccessible. Another dock I have reads the disk with no issues when plugged in to the same USB port. Whatever the cause, it's a problem I can't work around, so this dock just became trash. Others may not run into this problem, but I can't recommend this dock.

title: I was impressed
text: I use mine to edit GoPro videos while on the road. It works much better than a cheap laptop. I've added a 1TB microSD card for storage, and I have a 5TB external drive for backup. I record from 6 to 12 hours of video (1080 and 4K) a day on each of five cameras. Keeping track of that and editing it was overwhelming before I bought this. Each file can be up to 3.72 GB. One camera will record from 10 to 100 video segments, depending on settings. Using internal storage, the videos load into the editor almost instantly, and using PIP I can include one 4k track and three 1080 tracks with no issues. I've produced videos up to 2 1/2 hours long. A laptop that would do all that would cost thousands. I wasn't expecting it to work this well. That's a lot of processing. I'm normally disappointed by the gadgets I buy, and was expecting this to work, but not as well as it does. I was impressed. It far exceeded my expectations. TexasHillsurfer

title: Limited output, but perfect for some applications
text:
Update: I'd recommend the 7800mAh batteries for the difference in price. They're not much bulkier, and they provide about 8-9 hours of charge at 1080/30 for a GoPro Hero 5 Black. I haven't tested them other than that so far but the 7 should be comparable.

Note: Both batteries require a compatible camera case and cable to be waterproof.

Previous review: I've been using these batteries for years to power GoPros, and they work great up to a point. If you're recording 1080/30 video using GoPro Hero Black 5-7 they're fine. They really don't provide enough amperage for 4K. They'll record, but you may lose the connection if you're using GoPro Quik. It seems the cameras shut down WiFi and Bluetooth if the voltage drops. I have no way of knowing if that's actually the case, but that seems to be the weak point. At 1080/30 with a GoPro Hero 5 Black, they'll record from 5 to 6 hours of continuous video. Using WiFi to view the captured image will shorten that considerably. I normally use a Bluetooth Remote GoPro app to start and stop recording. It uses far less power, and can sync several cameras.

title: Does what I need it to do.
text: I use this to mount a dive case and battery for GoPro cameras instead of mounting the camera to the battery. This makes changing batteries much quicker than having to remove the case from the battery, then the battery from the mount. The standard GoPro mounts fit tight, and the screw tightens well with no slippage in the 65 mph breeze outside the truck and for hours on rough roads. Texas Hillsurfer.

title: Yes, it is waterproof with some cameras and the right cables
text:
2022-01-29: Added photos showing waterproof connections and waterproof camera case for GoPro Hero 5 thru 7 black. Also, I don't attach the camera buckle to the battery, but use a dual mount to mount both camera and battery. It's easier to change batteries in my application with this setup. If your battery or case doesn't come with the correct cables, send a message to the seller and they'll send them to you. They've informed me that they'll be including that cable with both the case and battery.

Original: Before you buy this, you need to familiarize yourself with Suptig's waterproof cases, mainly for GoPro Hero Black cameras, and a few others. If you don't find a Suptig charge case that fits your camera, this isn't waterproof. I've used Suptig products for a few years to protect and power my GoPro cameras when mounted on the outside of whatever truck I'm driving ... Peterbilt, Freightliner, Kenworth etc. in all kinds of weather. There's isn't a case for GoPro Hero 8 Black that I can find. There are cases for the 3, 4, 5-7 Black, and the 9 and 10 Black. I believe there are cases for some other brands. Only a charge case specifically made to connect to this or the previous battery using a cable with waterproof connections will be waterproof. It's not rocket surgery, but it isn't explained well in the product description. Lastly, you may have to message the seller to get the right cables. They're really good about sending out the correct cables for the application.

title: Lasted about 21 months
text: ... then any PC I install it in won't even start. I have WD Reds that are 6 Years old and still going. Guess this wasn't intended for continuous use.

title: These work
text: All you really need is something to hold your sound bar. These do that. They were a bit large for the 17" monitor I used them with, but they're unseen from the front, and they hold the sound bar over the monitor perfectly. This came with both too much and possibly too little hardware for every possible installation, but it had what I needed for my purpose. There's no way to include every possible screw, spacer, and nut.

title: The best I've found.
text:
I have dozens of GoPro mount screws that have come with various accessories. These are the absolute best I've found. Others are too slick, the screw falls out of the "handle", they're too brittle, the screw is too soft, the "handle" is too short ... Even the "official" GoPro screws don't come close.

I mount several GoPros inside and outside the Kenworth I drive. The only screws better than these, and they're too large for most uses, come with a suction-base camera mount made by a company that I can't name here or Amazon will ban this review. Suffice to say those mounts pan in any direction and hold like a vise. You can take that as a hint.

title: Better than the ones I just bought
text: I bought this back in 2019, and I just bought another brand, and though it doesn't seem like one piece of plastic would be better than another, this piece is better. It actually doesn't hold the microSD cards as tightly, but it hold them well, and it's easier to get them out of these than the others. Who knew. Well, I saved almost a dollar.

title: First impressions and background
text:
Just got this and started playing with it, but first a little background.

I also have two 5 Blacks and a 7 Black. I drive a truck (truck, not peekup) and use these to record my trips and the traffic around me. I record several hours of video every day. With a minor amount of effort, these work much better than typical dashcams. I use them without batteries inside the cab, with USB-C cables powering them. They tend to overheat with the batteries installed when mounted inside the windshield. The 5s still overheat sometimes without the battery. The 7 seldom does. They're often in the sun for hours at a time, so this isn't really a fault. It's not what they're designed to do. The 7 stays connected to the app much better than the 5s do. It's just a much more capable camera all around.

The Hero 7 Black TimeWarp and stabilization are first rate. The first video I took using it on my Jeep, a friend thought I'd bought a gyro-stabilized mount. It's that good. I assume the 8 is at least as good. I expect it to be better.

I've also owned a cheaper "Action Camera". It actually handled the heat better, until the battery swelled up and destroyed the camera. If you're looking for a toy, those are fine. If you want something that lasts, GoPro, with all its faults, is just about all there is. Nothing else does what they do while taking a substantial amount of abuse.

There is a dive case with external battery available from Suptig (on Amazon) for the 5, 6, and 7, but not for the 8. I use this case for the 5s when I mount them outside the truck. I use a Panavise mount with tethers outside the truck. The Panavise mount is heavy enough to hold the heavy battery with the camera mounted on it. I've also used this setup on my Jeep, but not as much as I'd like. There are dive cases for the 8, but not with external batteries that I've found.

The main feature of the 8 that I was drawn to was the ability to switch from TimeWarp to Realtime and back while recording. Unfortunately, this control isn't available on the app, only on the camera screen. I'll just have to mount the 8 where I can tap the screen easily while driving. Not optimum, but not a deal killer.

The app could be a lot better, but GoPro insists on using it for marketing. The app is useful, but I've already bought four GoPros. The cameras sold themselves. The app lacks a lot of features I'd like to see on it, though it is much better now than when I was given my first GoPro 4. The 4 still works fine, by the way, and I still use it where I'm afraid I might lose the camera, such as under the Jeep.

The battery door and charge port on the Hero 8 Black are completely different from the Hero 5 Black and Hero 7 Black. If you plan to use the camera for long periods without the battery, you'll need to get a battery door designed to allow connecting USB while closed. I've ordered one. Just search for "Hero 8 battery door." The alternative is to leave the battery door open, or off. I really don't like that choice. Either way, the camera isn't waterproof without the original door in place and closed.

I can't recommend any of the GoPro 6 series, because for a bit more you can get a 7, and for a bit less, you can get a 5 Black. I bought the 8 instead of another 7 because the price dropped to within $40 of the 7, and there are several improvements. Before you buy any of them, do some research into what each can and cannot do. There are various video modes on each. The older models drop in price every time a new model comes out.

I'll edit this after I put this one to work for a while.

title: Needs more power
text: If you bought one of these to transfer files between sd cards or external drives and your phone,  and the drive disconnects during a transfer, it needs a bigger power supply. A phone charger isn't usually enough. I don't know exactly what wattage you need, but I know that my 65 watt laptop charger is enough. The order I plug things in matters also, but I'll leave that to your own experimentation. I use it with my S9 and various cards and drives with good results, as long as it has enough power to supply everything connected to it.

title: Keeps the rain out
text: ... and dust, mud, whatever.

title: First impressions
text: It seems a bit quicker than I expected. I assume that's mostly due to the 16GB of DDR4. I've found over the years that ample memory makes a big difference in Windows machines. I'm glad I spent $600 instead of $350. I only intend to use this to manage video files from 4 GoPros, and organize them on an external drive while I'm on the road. I could have done that with a $350 system, but not much else. I'm sure I'll find other uses for this over time. The only additional feature I'd like to see in a system in this price range is 4G/LTE or 5G. I'd be willing to pay a bit more for something exactly like this with a SIM slot, but alas, those are only found in much more expensive systems, or cheap tablets. Go figure.

title: Quality cable
text: I can't speak on the durability, because I haven't had these long, but they did solve a problem I was having with an OTG hub. It didn't work with other cables I had. Drives dropped out in the middle of file transfers from my Galaxy S9. Now, no such problem. The connectors seem to be well attached, and feel like a more precise fit in all of the USB-C sockets I've used them with. I liked them so much I bought spares.

title: It's not slow, but it's not magical
text: I'm currently transferring about 1 TB of video files from this drive to an internal drive. The speed is ranging from 50 MB/s to 105 MB/s using the USB 3.0 cable that came with the drive on a USB 3.0 hub which is plugged into a USB 3.0 port on my desktop running Windows 10 Pro. This is about the same speed I get transferring similar files from one internal 4 TB WD Red drive to another via SATA III. From what I've read from actual experts in the field, this is slightly above average for a typical external USB 3.0 drive. It's not an SSD, and there are no physical drives that come close to SSD speeds, or close to the theoretical maximum throughput of USB 3.0. Ignore anyone who says it's too slow. It's not the drive. It's them.

title: It's PanaVise
text: I've had no issues using any of my PanaVise mounts with my GoPro. I like the fact that the various components will work with other sets. I like that they actually hold. This one is no exception.

title: Cheap fun, Great as a dash cam
text:
Akaso Brave 4 (Updated) Review

Note: WiFi apps tested using a Google LG Nexus 5x without a sim card, which is a spare phone I use to control my GoPro Hero4. I haven't tested it with my Galaxy S9, because I don't plan to use them together. You may have different results with a different phone, and there may be a better app than the recommended one. LD Cam, for instance, almost works better, but not quite.

Note2: Manufacturer claims "Since 4K resolution is too big, APP does not support." Well, the GoPro app does. I think it's the software library used in many of the other apps that limit the size to 1080p. USB transfers work extremely well. It identifies as a USB drive on the PC and other devices.

Pros:
-Inexpensive compared to GoPro (less than a used Hero 4 Black)
-4K/24fps is higher frame rate than GoPro Hero 4
-Simple to use (other than the WiFi app)
-Plenty of useful settings and features
-Can be used with a PC as a webcam
-Windows 10 recognizes it and loads a driver for it
-Connects via USB-OTG to Galaxy S9 flawlessly for transferring files
-Doesn't overheat like both my GoPro Hero 4 and Hero 7 Black.
-Very lightweight.
-Works great when set up as a dash cam.
-Doesn't overheat and shut down like a GoPro.

Cons:
-Recommended WiFi apps don't support 4K (yet?)
-Recommended WiFi apps require mobile data be turned off (even without a sim card)
-Recommended WiFi apps don't stay connected with my Nexus 5x
-WiFi apps reset camera settings to arbitrary values
-WiFi has to be turned off and back on and app restarted if it disconnects
-Battery cover could be easier to remove
-Not a rugged camera (though not that heat sensitive)
-Klemme 1, an open tripod mount, doesn't hold the camera firmly so wouldn't work as an action mount (used a heat gun to tighten it up and it's tolerable now.

Other:
Though this looks like a GoPro Hero 4, and is very similar in size and layout, it's only similar. They're different enough to prevent using a Hero 4 case. Not much. Just a little. But enough. That's unfortunate, because the Suptig case I have works with an external battery that allows me to record for several hours (5+) with the Hero 4. I was hoping this would work with that case, but it won't. That's what happens when I have unreasonable expectations.

It abruptly adjusts to changing light conditions but lags slightly behind during rapidly changing conditions, particularly when using time-lapse, so that going from the darkness under a bridge to bright sunlight while driving often results in a total whiteout. I haven't notice the same effect with the GoPro Hero 4, and I suspect that it ramps a bit more slowly from darkness to light to avoid this effect.

If the recommended WiFi app, or the alternative worked better, I'd give it one more star (gave it that one more star after using it as a dash cam). Even with all the cons relating to WiFi, I actually like the camera, and think it's worth the ~$80 I paid for it.

title: Much shorter
text: I only listen to SiriusXM, and I don't use AM or FM, so I have no clue if it actually works as an antenna. Simple enough to install. Plugs the hole left behind when the stock antenna is removed. In hindsight, I should have gotten a shorter one, but it'll do. I carry the stock antenna with me on the off chance I actually need AM or FM.

title: Great GoPro Mount
text: This kit is well worth the price. It's the most solid mount I have, except for the older style Panavise mount that I got with a used GoPro Hero 4. That mount is still just as solid as this one, but not quite as versatile. There are extensions available for other Panavise mounts that should fit this perfectly. I haven't tried them, but they look to be part of the same system.

title: Bigger than I needed
text: I only needed about half of each of these, and cut what I needed with a Dremel cutoff wheel. They're solid. They're versatile. They're strong. Half of each of them worked perfectly. The other half was in the way. I'd buy these again for a larger monitor/TV, or even if I only needed half of each one.

title: Doesn't deal well with vibration
text: I have another mount that's very similar, and almost every part of this one is just as strong and well made as that one. But, the plastic base where the suction cup is on this one is flat, not curved, and that flat piece of plastic flexes easily. So, on a rough road the arm vibrates on this one with more than a bit of vigor. If it's important that it not do that; if you plan to use this in a rough-riding vehicle on a rough road, it won't work well. The other one I have, that I don't know the brand of or where it was purchased, holds rock steady on the roughest roads. The plate where the suction cup resides on it is curved. It doesn't flex. This one does.

title: No need to pay more
text: Digital signals are either perfect or there isn't a signal. You won't get better than on. This cable's construction seems to be of good quality. There's no reason to buy a "premium" optical cable, because it won't work any better than "it works". The only other option is, "it doesn't work." This works.

title: No buffer
text: I got used to having a buffer that allowed me to pause or "rewind", and this doesn't have that capability, because it doesn't have a buffer. Other than that, for the price, it does what it needs to do.

title: Solid mount for larger monitors
text: I'm sure there's something better out there that costs more. This holds my three 28" Samsung monitors, and many stands only accept up to 27". Right now it's much stronger than the table I have it clamped to. Honestly, I detest that anything less than 5 stars indicates to some people that there's something wrong. Nothing is perfect, and I would think 5 stars would be reserved for perfection. By that standard, I'd give this 4 stars, but by modern standards, it gets 5.

title: Very useful for GoPro stuff
text: Which is what I use it for. Can't beat the price. I like orange. I'm not sure about why it has latches and straps and a zipper and velcro on the top though. That could have been simpler, but the zipper keeps stuff in as the bag bounces around the truck, and the straps with buckles hold the top down when you pick it up with the carry straps. So, maybe it makes sense.

title: I like it, but ... then, after a few months ...
text:
2021-10-05 Update:
This is the second one I've had. I finally broke the first one a few months ago when it fell to the floor with my tablet in it. I got the replacement in June. This one has an issue. I can easily swing the "foot" out, but it's getting increasingly difficult to swing it back in. So difficult that it'll soon break the holder if it gets worse. We'll see. The first one lasted much longer. I'll probably try to take it apart, which is possible, to "fix" it. If I can't, I'll be getting something else.

Minus 1 star.

Previous:

... the tablet I use has buttons along about half of one side, and that means I have to clamp the holder on to one end. So, pay attention to where your buttons are. I'm seriously considering cutting part of the short side of the holder to let me place it closer to the center. Other than my own issues, it's a great device. It makes carrying the tablet around much easier, and I can stand the tablet up in more places (such as the truck steering wheel when parked), and have it at various different angles pretty easily.

Updates: Cut it with a Dremel cutoff wheel and was able to center it better. Didn't affect the clamp at all, but be careful where you cut. Did that about a month after I bought it.

Bought the first one in February of 2019 and finally managed to break it. Hunted through the other options on Amazon and couldn't find anything that would serve my purpose better, so I bought another one on 6/3/21. It took a drop of about 3 feet at exactly the right angle with the "leg" open and the tablet attached to break it.

title: Exactly what I needed
text: It solved the issue I have having connecting external drives to the S9, because the S9 didn't provide power for long enough to transfer large video files (2GB+). So far this connects the LG Nexus 5x I use for a dash cam to my Galaxy S9 so I can transfer files while charging both the Nexus and the S9. It also connects the S9 to a 512GB mSATA drive in an external case. I haven't been able to get a connection that actually works with my GoPro Hero4, but I haven't tried all my min-B cables yet. And, I haven't tried the HDMI yet.

title: Cheap
text: Not very well made, but for the price, I wasn't expecting it to be. Won't work for me though, because it won't work with a case, which my Galaxy Tab Active2 wouldn't be as "Active" without.

title: A bit cheap
text: Okay for the price. Clip, as most, is brittle. Suction cup sticks great to glass. Arm uses small screws. Standard GoPro accessories will work if the hole at the end of the am is enlarged. I'm looking elsewhere.

title: Best charge case
text: Great charging solution for Hero4, even without the external battery. Secures the charge cable. Great for windshield mounting.

title: Works great
text: Fits perfect. Works great. Looks good. Gives me a place to put an mSATA drive I had no other use for. Now if I could only remember where I put it.

title: Version 2 will be out soon
text: I don't fully know how it will compare, but rumors have it with twice the power of this one.

title: More or less correct
text:
My rating is my first impression of the entire package, without knowing how well the battery itself will hold up. The battery was a higher capacity than the original, and physically larger. There was space in the DEZL 770 for the larger battery, that had been filled by a plastic card the original battery was stuck to.

The original was an 1100 mAH single-cell Lithium, while the replacement was a 1500 mAH of the same voltage. The Torx driver included appears to be a T6, while the 770 required a T9, which I already had. The pry tool included is something I'll probably use again. It does the job and seems to be made of quality materials. The disc included was for a DEZL 760, which is very similar, and possibly explains the incorrect driver.

The Garmin powered up and is currently charging fine. The original battery would only last about 5 minutes, which wasn't critical, but the device was occasionally resetting while plugged in and tracking, which I'm hoping was due to the battery being at the end of its life. Considering the price of this battery, compared to buying a new GPS, this is really a bargain if it solves the issue. If not, it'll still be a good spare if I buy a new device, with a good battery.

I can't comment on the video disc included, because I didn't use it. Replacing the battery isn't difficult, but does require some care. For someone who's never done something like this before, it might be a good idea to get a 10-year-old to help. I've been taking things apart for at least 55 years, and most of the time can put them back together. My philosophy relies on the fact that if it's not working now, I can't either fix it, or screw it up bad enough that it'll need to be replaced.

title: Big enough for a large hand
text: I like this at least as much as the Performance MX, but it would have been nice if Logitech included support for its previous devices in the new software. Having software for my previous Logitech devices as well as the software for this seems unnecessary. They all use the same receiver.

title: Photo of correct card matters.
text: Item shown in photo is compantible with 1.5v and 3.3v slots. Card actually only has the key for 1.5v slot. Therefore, I can't use it at all.

title: Doesn't wash well.
text: Worked great until I washed and dried it. Still worked after that, but the USB-A end was loose and would disconnect internally. So, I'm buying another one. Maybe I won't wash this one soon.

title: It's one of these
text: It's a power cord. It's 10 feet long. It has a male end and a female end. It's black. I wasn't disappointed. It did exactly what I bought it for.

title: Simple remote for a simple setup.
text: Though advertised to work with up to 8 devices, this one is best for someone who has a cable box, TV, soundbar, maybe a Blu-Ray player, and nothing more. For more complex systems, get one with a screen. It's not hard to set up with a simple system. And it is simple to use, with a simple system. I bought this for a friend so she'd only have to keep track of one remote. I'm on my second 650. I wore the first one out and dropped it entirely too many times. It's also easy to set up, but with a little more effort, and a little imagination, it can be customized to a much greater extent than this one. All of the Harmony's require a PC to set them up. I haven't found an IR device they don't have in the database yet, and I've had more than a few uncommon black boxes and gadgets.

title: We like it.
text: Great set for the price. I'm sure there's something better out there, but better is a subjective thing. We like it. It's a perfect match for our XBox One X.

title: Works as advertised
text: The glow-in-the-dark version is an ugly color, but it makes it easier to find, and easier to grip than that slick plastic. I've seen a few complaints about making pushing the buttons harder, but I didn't have any problem. It takes a bit of tugging and pushing to get everything lined up, and replacing batteries requires removing it and doing it all over again. I can't see how it could be made better for the price though.

title: Does what it's supposed to.
text: Works as advertised. I'll give one 5 stars when someone makes one that supports USB 3.1 or above. Not really a fault. Just an incentive.

title: Can't beat it for the price.
text: So far I've bought 3 of these, because of the quality and price. The oldest still looks as good as the newest.

title: Often cheaper than older, slightly slower MicroSD cards
text: Best MicroSD at the moment for the price. Or wait and get the next generation whenever it's released.

title: Lightweight. Good enough sound.
text: Lightweight. Very comfortable. Good enough sound for me. After decades of working in noisy environments and a youth spent listening to loud '70s rock, I probably couldn't hear the difference between these and a pair costing 3 times as much. There are other brands of headset that might be cheaper, but it's hard to go wrong with LG. I got used to being able to connect 2 devices to a headset at the same time with Plantronics Voyager Legend, and this doesn't do that. So, I can either use it with my phone or my tablet, but it has to be paired to either device if I switch. I'll know to check if I ever upgrade. This may be typical of this style in this price range.

title: As good as one needs
text: I use AmazonBasics cables for almost everything. I haven't been disappointed yet.

title: Check the dimensions. Thicker than most.
text: I used this in a small-footprint desktop that really didn't have a good drive bay arrangement. It's a lot of storage in a small space, and it works perfect for my purpose, but one would be hard pressed to find a laptop that would take a drive this thick.

title: Good External drive for XBox One
text: Used as external drive for XBox One. As usual, I'm not disappointed by WD.

title: Wondering why so many bought this without knowing what it was.
text: No, I don't own one. What I'm trying to understand is why there are so many people who insist on buying things they know nothing about. This is exactly what it claims to be, a development kit. It's intended market is those people who want to learn to write software for, and experiment with, the NVIDIA CUDA line of GPUs. That some think it works well for the price with Linux is great, but that's not it's intended purpose. Anyone looking at the reviews needs to at least stick to the positive ones to find if it will work for them. It is what it is. Leaving a negative review is like complaining about a Collie because it turned out to be a dog.

title: Not just better than I expected for the price.
text: Does exactly what I needed. Much heavier that I expected it to be. And, there are more ways to mount it than listed in the instructions. The clamp portion could be removed from the base and the base bolted/screwed to a vertical surface also. I drilled a 1/2" hole through my hobby workbench (countertop) and used the included base to bolt it down. I have another one on the way. Now I have to find a place to store all the spare parts, just in case I want to mount it some other way. The only issue I had was one set of VESA mount screws was too long even with the spacers. The other set mounted the plate flush to the back just fine.

title: Very versatile with AMD processors
text:
Almost any good cooler will cool, but this one's just a bit cooler. Not only will it allow mounting in any of four positions on an Intel processor. It also allows mounting in any of four positions on an AMD processor. So, not only will it fit in the case, and clear the memory, and anything else that might be in the way. But, it can also provide airflow for the memory from directly above it. Many AMD-compatible coolers only allow mounting in one of two positions. This one allows mounting in all four using two different sets of brackets.

Check the measurements on Cooler Master's site to be sure it'll fit your case. If it will, it's probably the best you'll find for AMD.

title: Glitchy under certain conditions.
text: It seems to work fine for everything but games, and it seems that the sound processor may be the source of the audio and video glitches. Certain sounds seem to cause more problems than others, including dropped audio, glitchy video, and sometimes a blank screen. This happens with both XBox Ones and a PS3. I mainly play Forza 6 and Gran Turismo 6, and certain engine sounds seem to be associated with these problems more than others. Streaming video doesn't seem to cause any problems with any of the input devices or either TV. The normal solution is to cycle the power off and back on. Different cables or settings don't seem to make a difference. I'm not using the audio splitter at all. Personal opinion (from decades of experience with processors of all kinds), is that whatever processor is used simply cannot process some sounds correctly, even to pass the signal through. I may be wrong. I've been wrong before. This may be a quality control issue, or it may be an engineering issue. Either way, I'm looking for a better product, and most of the ones in this price range seem to be identical except for the name on the box. In fact, many more expensive devices seem to be exactly the same layout, and likely use the same circuitry. There's no way to tell from the name on the box, or the Amazon description.

It is, by far, the best GPS I have ever had. Big, bright, clear display; intuitive menus; useful information. So what's wrong. The Smart Link app that provides the unit with weather and other information. The connection is Bluetooth, but it often fails to relink after you re-approach the unit. There is also a feature that shows where you parked your car. I used it the other day, and it reported my car was 32 miles away. The weather is M-Powered. Problem is the M-Power iPhone app itself is not highly rated. One problem is that it will display a warning or watch area, but will sometimes fail to delete that map layer so that you can see the actual storms...which you can see with your eye and on the unit sometime later. Garmin needs to do some serious work on this feature.

If you are serious about what the Smart Link feature can do, do not buy this unit until Garmin gets serious about fixing it.

title: Love the GPS unit. Garmin: Not So Much...
text: I love this unit. It is my first GPS and I complemented my purchase with a good "how to" book and a 2nd book on how to make your own maps.  Most of the negatives you read about are true and are mainly complaints about Garmin and/or support. The Garmin software is rudimentary, Garmin is totally proprietary and the maps are ridiculously expensive and a royal pain to download and to load to SD or microSDs. And, God forbid you buy a second unit and try to connect with the same computer. First of all it is challenging to the point of hair pulling frustration and secondly Garmin does not reward you for buying a second unit since they will charge you full price to buy maps for the second unit after you have already paid for the same software for the 1st unit! Not even a discount for being a good customer! Very shortsighted but that is probably why their profits have dropped so dramatically this year. But, having said all that, I still think it is an excellent and affordable choice if you want to navigate in the car (safer w/ a co-pilot helping), in the field and in the water and this unit does it better than most GPS handhelds that try to do everything. My total investment so far is $350 for unit + 1 map purchase. I will likely spend the time to learn to make my own maps (another $100 for 3rd party software)and to use them for hiking/canoeing/cycling and forget about Garmin maps entirely. As for boating, I will probably bit the bullet and drop another $100-150 for the Bluecharts I will soon want just because I'll have my hands full making terrestrial maps and it will be easy to just buy an already loaded SD card from Garmin. So, I will be into this unit for about $500 total. As I intend to use this unit for a long time, I think that is not a bad deal overall. One more thing: the unit itself is really big. It does not bother me but others have mentioned it and it was shocking the first time I saw the unit out of the box.  You may consider the new Colorado series if this is a deal breaker for you. But do check out the screen size comparisons. This unit has one of the largest screen sizes in the handhelds.

title: My new best friend.
text:
I LOVE, LOVE, LOVE my Kindle Fire. I had resisted Kindles for many years mainly because I wanted to borrow free books from the library and I read in the dark with a back-lit unit. Once that hurdle was overcome, I started to seriously look at the Kindle Fire. Not one to jump on the band wagon, I waited a few months and started comparing - online and in stores. My final test was between the Fire and the Samsung Galaxy Tab 7.0. The Fire was faster! The start up time is faster on the Fire than the new iPad...that is not from reboot.

Ever security conscious, the first thing I did was to download Dr. Web anti-virus and created a password. I bought the Fintie cover [[ASIN:B006GLEZ8U FINTIE ® Dark Purple PU Leather Folio Case Cover Value Package with Free Screen Protector/Stylus/USB cable for Amazon Kindle Fire 7" Tablet]] with the car charger and USB connector which came in handy as I needed to connect with my computer. These are such a good price that I can colour co-ordinate with the season.

I have had my Kindle Fire for two months now and am still in love. I am particularly enjoying the whole Amazon experience: the free app a day, the free books every day, the lending library with Prime and the free TV and movies with Prime, as well. I can not say enough good things about this system.

My husband was so taken with my enjoyment of the Fire that he just bought one himself. He is in love, too! Now I can loan him books. I was going to purchase the new iPad this summer, but now I think I will wait another year. :-)

title: Good, inexpensive alternative to an expensive camera
text: I ordered it with the mindset that it was worth a try.  I have more expensive cameras around the house but I wanted a less expensive camera so that I could check in on my dog when I'm not home.  It's worked well.  The picture quality and the night vision are adequate, the motion sensor works well, it can record and the set up and app are easy.  The features of being able to talk through it and being able to move the camera through the app are fantastic.  I especially love being able to move the camera remotely so that I can see different rooms  I wish my other cameras did that.  Overall, a good choice for a basic camera that you want to use for checking in on your pet.  It's also very discreet so it can be used as a nanny cam to monitor a babysitter or pet sitter.  I'm happy with it.

text:
This item exceeded our expectations. We were needing to be able to view our new puppy while we were away to see how he adjusts to us not being around. The problem is, we are at home with him ALOT, therefore we were concerned he would develope anxiety while we were away or hurt himself. This item allowed for us to keep an eye on him and monitor how long it takes for our little guy to stop crying while also helping put us at ease... Eventually we plan to get more to monitor the whole house and let our monster roam freely.

This camera has great coverage but excellent when mounted on a wall. Additionally, the night mode is impressive. Everything was still crystal clear and being able to adjust the sensitivity of the motion tracker /recorder was super helpful... otherwise we would have a lot of alerts for glare from other cars driving by.

My only complaint would be the sound... when i monitor my pup at work I have to turn off the sound because the app will bypass my headphones or blue tooth and go straight to speaker on my phone. First time this happened everyone in the office got to hear my puppies amplified screeches.. i was asked if someone was skinning him alive... i’ve emailed tech about the problem and went through the settings but no solution or response yet. We still love this item regardless of the one issue.

title: If you live in a valley surrounded by mountains where at best you have a fuzzy cell phone use
text:
We bought two of these in December 2015. Hooked each camera up. Downloaded the online app. Put in a memory card. Turned on our iPads, Phones, and Apples. Presto we could see every point inside our home should our exterior camera system connected to the home security device ever fail.

We travel 140 miles West to our 2nd home and watch inside our home, while driving whoever is not at the wheel will pull up the home-cam so we can see what is happening on our cell phones. We went to Vegas, a few months ago and hired a dog sitter to stay with our beloved pet at our home. We were able to check-in & from our hotel room, Freemont Street or the Strip and check on our home without any problems.

Unless you are still operating in the AOL age or have so many firewalls up the smoke detectors keep going off inside your home; I can't see why the product would not work for a person needing a quick install. The type of one they control that is portable enough to move from room to room, (even a window seal).

If you live in a valley surrounded by mountains where at best you have a fuzzy cell phone use, you may want to get the kind of cams able to be through DSL if possible. Personally, if you are using the most current technologies, keep you system updates performed and no longer have to type www after the dial tone stops screeching, can read and follow directions; then you should be able to follow the instructions and if necessary work with a customer service technician associated with this item.

By the way, it is not just your computer that needs updates if you no longer use brick phones. If you have advanced enough to be no longer paying for minutes, but rather have plans permitting you unlimited use of services through "unlimited data" plans (this includes calls too,) within the lower 48 and depending how fast you can drive into and out of Mexico, you will have excellent service.

title: Good deal for the money
text:
I'm pretty picky about how good speakers perform. I'm not a hard nose audiophile, but I know good speakers when I hear them. I have used the same song for decades to truly test the quality of the bass. That song is Alan Parson's "The Raven" and the bass test is the very last note in the song. Most speaker systems cannot handle this deep bass guitar note at any volume. This set did. So as far as the bass, this speaker set passed the toughest test I could throw at it.

The high end was strong and clean, the midrange was the only level I saw a little lacking. This was playing music of the classic rock genre. I play my music pretty exclusively through Windows Media Player which offers a built-in equalizer. Just a little adjusting on the equalizer and I had all levels well balanced, sound was very good.

Some reviewers had mentioned hearing a hum or the like from the right speaker (the one which contains the power and volume controls). When I first hooked everything up out of the box I heard it too. It was noticeable and given time I could see it becoming irritating. I know what causes this hum and how to fix the problem. The problem is caused by poor shielding on the speaker wiring. I added 3 ft. extensions that were double shielded and lo and behold...no more hum, dead silence. I have since put 10 ft. double shielded extensions on both speakers and they are working flawlessly with zero degradation in performance. If you check the answered questions you will find the exact extensions you need. Be careful, not any VGA extension will work for the right speaker! Keep the original speaker wires away from any power cords or power sources and you should get the same result in the end.

I haven't had these speakers for very long so I can't comment on longevity yet. If they unexpectedly have problems I will definitely update this review. But in my honest opinion they seem like a good deal for the money.

It's range is awesome.  I've gotten beautiful perfectly focused pictures of snowflakes (macro) to planets (full zoom) and everything in between.  You definitely should have a good tripod especially when using the extended zoom.  The camera is rugged construction and comfortable to hold and steady and the response to actually clicking the picture after autofocus is very quick.  Videos were very good quality and the stereo sound was well done.  I would honestly expect to pay hundreds more for a camera of this quality and though it is not Wi-Fi compatible, transference from camera to computer was not difficult at all.  Battery life was very reasonable and it operated admirably using the standard Amazon AA rechargeable batteries.

title: Lanyards are useless.
text:
The goods news is that the lens caps seem to fit my 58mm Canon lens.

The bad news is that the little lanyards for them is a joke. It came with a little key--which is good since I doubt the suggest ballpoint pen would fit in that tiny little hole--but the string is still too large for the hole. I worked at it for at least 15 minutes before the point of the key broke off inside the hole, where it is now jammed. Since it's jammed in there the string is also stuck in there. So technically I have the lanyard attached but I certainly wouldn't trust that! I'll likely end up cutting the string and tossing that lanyard.

Since the lanyards are at least half the reason for ordering these caps, I'm giving them 3 stars and I consider that generous.

title: Doesn't focus on what you want
text:
I have a hard time with this camera. Maybe I'm just not camera savvy enough, but I seriously just wanted a simple point and shoot that would produce good quality photos. This camera comes with a ridiculous amount of fancy settings which I'm sure a lot of people enjoy.

A big reason we got it was to replace our DSLR which I never really learned how to use and I wanted something simpler. I try to take photos of birds in the back yard and this camera is completely hopeless with that. It will not focus on anything you want it to focus on, especially if there's any movement. It'll focus right next to the bird or behind the bird or under the bird or wherever. So you have to try to zoom in to the bird so the camera focuses on it, then zoom out again and hope that it stays focused on your bird (or whatever).

If you're looking to take photos of wildlife or anything of that sort, I'd find something else. We've switched back to the DSLR for wildlife photos so this camera will sit around to be used once a year with family or something. Hopefully it takes good landscape photos but I haven't seen a setting for that yet.

title: Doesn't last long
text:
I've had this for a year and a half and only used it a handful of times to burn mixed music cds. Half the time when I plug it into my laptop it doesn't even recognize the device. When I can finally get it to show up, when I try to burn a playlist iTunes says "cd player or software not recognized" or something like that even if the cd player shows up in My Computer. Maybe it's an iTunes problem, I don't know (but I think not).
When I finally, FINALLY get the playlist to burn, it pops it out halfway through and says it couldn't do it. So I pop it back in to try again, and iTunes tells me that all the songs are on there. Oooook.....so I go test it out in the car which is where I'll actually be using the cd, and it only burned a few songs. When I try to reuse the same cd--even after formatting it or emptying it, whatever--it refuses to burn onto the same cd. I can't do anything with it. I've had to trash two cds this way which is my limit for waste. This is going in the trash.

The strap in the cover to help hold it is a little small and tight, so if you have big hands it might not work for you. I don't really use it much. The strap clipped to the corner to carry it isn't bad though, if you need that sort of thing.
I use the kickstand all the time though. I was always looking for things to lean my old kindle against to read while eating lunch, and now I can do it easily. Love it.
And I love the yellow--it's nice and bright! Not quite eye-watering, not quite mustard. A wonderful shade.

title: PROBLEMS
text:
I've only had this laptop for a year and a half. It's given me problems before, but recently I had to take it in to get professionally fixed. Apparently windows had a bad update or something, and I spent $125 fixing it. A week later the same problems I was having previously showed back up again. Now my trackpad isn't working. In fact, when I go into devices and drivers, it doesn't say there's a trackpad at all. There's nothing for me to try to update. Why would my laptop get rid of my trackpad? All I did was put it to sleep overnight! The only way to use it now is to plug in a mouse. I tried downloading the trackpad drivers-- no luck. I tried a system restore and it won't do the restore. So now I'll have to take it in to get fixed again for another couple hundred dollars. I spent almost $1000 on this piece of junk and I do NOTHING that would cause problems on a basic laptop. I use Word, upload photos, and surf the internet and social media. I do not game and I do not go on porn sites or anything sketchy. I don't download random files from the internet. I have virus protection and malware. Never again, HP!
Update: When I updated the BIOS driver, I would get my trackpad mouse back. This happened multiple times--and every time nothing worked except updating that already updated BIOS driver. Even the guys at the repair shop didn't know that something like that would "fix" it.
Update 6/5/2019: It's been less than two years since I bought this laptop. I have never mistreated it--never slammed the lid, never dropped it, nothing. But last weekend when I opened the lid I heard a "pop" and found a shard of plastic on my desk. One of the hinges became misaligned somehow, and then I could neither close it nor open it further without the outside backing of the lid forcefully separating from the screen. I shut it down real quick, and then was able to maneuver the lid and the hinge enough to get it closed. I was on a work trip when this happened, and luckily I was able to get by without using my laptop again until I came home. I was able to carefully open again and it seems to be working, but I will not attempt to close it again. I'll do an extra backup and I will probably use it (if it lasts) until August when my MS Office and Bitdefender subscriptions run out, then I'll have to shell out for a new laptop. You can bet it won't be another HP!

I don't know how it "chooses" whatever station it does, but by the time you scroll through to reach that station on your radio it is no longer the "clearest"--when really none of them are clear at all anyway.

I had a transmitter before this one (which eventually broke) that was $10 cheaper and it only came with an option for 4 channels, and it sucked but still worked better than this thing. I'm very unhappy that I paid $25 for this piece of junk. I thought transmitters would be one of those things that "you get what you pay for," but apparently not. If he picks it up. In 60 years I've owned 3 tvs, all of them lasted 10 to 20 years before i had to do any work on them except this one. Right now, ready to through over the hill and cancel the cable. What kind of crap is this that you pay well over 1000. For something and it works a year. Don't pay a big price for any of TV's regardless of brand. Terrible product. Don't waste your money. They all know these tv's suck and they don't care, all they want is your money.

Update: I changed the main board and t con myself, neither fixed the tv. The next part to change is the panel and that part is 1600. I'm furious that all these manufacturers are making tv's that last under two years. Look at all the reviews, all the LED tv's are junk, all Have a design flaw, especially the bigger ones. My tv repairman said all LED tv's will have to be worked on about every 3 or 4 years and most times the repair parts are more than the tv. So right now I'm looking for a dump or recycling place that will take electronics and someone with a truck to carry it off. i will never pay more than 200. On any LED tv again. BUYER BEWARE!

title: Good quality, not likely to use often
text:
I read a few reviews before purchasing this mouse (the Logitech Lift Vertical Ergonomic Mouse, Wireless). The reviews seemed to suggest this mouse made a big difference for people who were having aches/pains with using a traditional mouse.
I wanted to try this mouse for everyday use, and maybe even for gaming.
Unfortunately, the novelty of the vertical grip wears off quickly and what you are left with is learning how to use a new mouse efficiently all over again.
If you have wrist/arm/grip issues, this mouse might be a great solution for you. If you are just looking for a more efficient and accurate mouse, I would not recommend this product.
I used the mouse for a few weeks and found that every time I would switch back to my regular mouse it was like a handicap had been lifted.
To be clear, the mouse is very well made. The buttons are nearly silent, the wheel seems to track well, the surface that contacts your desk or mousepad seems to be smooth enough. I would even estimate the batteries are probably good for quite some time.
Logitech makes quality products, and I will be keeping this mouse just in case I ever have the need to switch it up a bit.
Overall, this might be a great solution for people with pain associated with traditional mouse posture, but not likely to be much fun for the average person who is just looking for a new or modern mouse.

title: Fantastic, great for tall people
text: These computer monitor risers were perfect for my office job.  I'm a grown man and stand almost 6 foot tall, so most desk setups have me looking down at the monitors all day.  These truly make a huge difference in neck and eye strain.  They were easy to setup and feel strong.  It would be even better if they were taller, but I suppose most people will do fine with them.  It's important to have your elbows bent at a 90 degree angle while typing, and you can't do that if your chair has to be super low to compensate for your height.  These stands help bridge the gap and make the workday more comfortable.

title: Very similar to Apple earbuds, these work well.
text: I think the price is great on these little earbuds.  The quality is pretty good, but they are manufactured in China, so you may notice they aren't quite as durable or heavy as an American made product would be.  The battery life seems okay for their size, and they charge via a convenient USB cable.  The only complaint I have is that the little "switch" or volume buttons (which are on the right side of the headphone wire) seems to pull the earbud wire to the right a lot.  This might not be noticeable to some people, but if the wire keeps going all to the right side, when you turn your head you can pull an earbud out pretty easily.  Otherwise, this is a great deal for blue tooth earbuds.

title: weak product, terrible support
text:
I have had problems with this mouse almost from the beginning. Primarily, every time the computer was restarted, I have to reprogram all the keys from scratch. I asked repeatedly for software that would work independent of the Internet, and simply store the program in my computer. Several promises were made to me but never kept.

Finally the program stopped working altogether, and I spoke to someone at customer service for the 10th time, and I was given case number 351267. She promised that a high level technical support person would get in touch within a few days.

It has been about two months with no reply, so I called into today. I was told that my case had been escalated to second tier support, and that there was nothing they could do but wait for a reply. This is shockingly bad customer service!

I no longer have faith that they can solve my problem. The concept is great, but it's very glitchy, and their tech people are nice but grossly ineffective.

title: Beware
text:
It synced and played music perfectly, but phone reception was terrible. The other people could hear me fine, but the sound i received was intermittent, distorted, and had a brrrrrrr ringing echo to every sound, even the ringing when i made a call.
I could not make out what the other people were saying at all.

I looked in trouble shooting, and it says the unit can get "interference from a wireless LAN, other 2.4 GHz wireless device, or microwave oven." Shocking! Where someone can go these days where none of these other devices are operating? i went 30 feet outside my house and it was just as bad.

Or maybe the one i got is just a lemon. I don't know.

I called SONY and they said to try the reset, but i'd already done that, so they offered to let me send it to them so a techie could look at it. I'm returning it in stead.

title: bad machine design
text:
1. the remote is very small and the buttons you need most often are just 1 inch from the bottom, so if you hold the remote in your palm normally, your thumb cannot twist back down to them. you have to cradle the end of the remote in your index and and middle finger, which slips easily. And at the easy-to-reach top are the number buttons, which i've NEVER used on any dvd or bluray remote in my life. (TIVO has the best remote design, i think)

2. much worse, (and I'll just quote from the manual):
Playback does NOT start from the resume
point where you last stopped playing...when
- you open the disc tray.
- you disconnect the USB device.
- you play other content.
- you turn off the player.
That means you have to start from scratch and get thruough ALL the warnings and previews EVERY time you can't finish a movie in one sitting. and the button placement makes it very easy to do so accidentally.

3. there are four buttons of different colors on the remote, and the manual identifies them as special function keys, but gives no instructions. I actually had to call a "product specialist" to explain. What?! I now question sony's sanity.

So I'm not buying sony products anymore.

PS. The machine is not malfunctioning (still very new), just badly designed, so one might say that it deserves more stars, but i always read the "1-star reviews" before buying anything, and i want to warn people.

title: A neat way to share digital photos with a loved one.
text:
This is a great gift for an older parent or really anyone who doesn't get around to printing out your photos. This is a wifi enabled digital frame, meaning you need wifi to use it's main attraction- adding photos remotely. This allows different faily members to add photos to the "cloud" where the albums are and they will show up on the photo frame. (You can load photos to a flash/thumb drive and still use it but that defeats the purpose of having a wifi enabled frame.)
Set up was easy and so was adding photos. I couldn't get the settings to work on the website but they are easily adjusted on the frame itself- Shuffle, how long photos display, transitions between photos etc.
It has a sleep mode, motion detector and timer. I haven't been able to fix the time. I set it to the correct time zone for us, but the time was off by 4 hours. I suppose with a little more looking into, I could've fixed this, but for now it is at my elderly moms house and she is happy with it.

title: Love this!
text:
I initially ordered this product because I wanted to be able to see what my dogs were doing, particularly our new puppy, when we weren't home. We have quickly grown to love this camera/treat dispenser/laser pointer. And the dogs love it too.

The pros: you can take pictures or short videos of your dogs, dispense treats, talk to them AND hear them, and use a laser pointer to entertain them. No monthly fees.

The cons: the treat dispenser only holds eight small treats, so if you have more than one animal or are going to be gone for a longer period of time, you may run out of treats before you return. Also, the laser sometimes gets stuck.

However, the customer service on this product is excellent. Outstanding, even. When our laser got stuck about three weeks after we purchased this product, we contacted the company and they attempted to walk us through a troubleshooting process to unstick the laser. When that didn't work, they sent us a brand new product no questions asked, no hassle, no fuss. We are extremely pleased with their customer service.

Also, unlike some other similar products on the market, this product does not require you to pay a monthly service for storage of photos or videos. You use an app on your mobile phone or tablet and can store photos and videos on your device or on your own cloud. I would highly recommend this product.

title: Works well, if you don't want to pan
text:
This is a great deal on outdoor cameras. They are easy to set up and work well with the software you can download. They are sturdy and compact. I got them to replace some cameras that are around our barn so we can see the horses, and the only surprise was that they didn't pan. The other cameras were able to move up and down, right and left so that I could see where the horses are.
I was going to give them 4 stars, but then I realized it was my issue. The description never said they would pan and I just missed that.
So, if you want remote cameras and don't mind that they are stationary, this is a great deal. You get three cameras for $160. However, if you look at the current description, one camera is $49.99, so you can buy three individual cameras for slightly less than the 3 pack. Goofy, but that's sometimes the case.
UPDATE: I also noticed that the speaker on the camera, so I can talk to whoever is there, has such a low volume it cannot be heard over 1 foot away. Not very helpful for a remore camera. I sent in a request to their support team asking if there is a volume control on the camera or the mobile app. They responded with a request for the model number, which is fine, and then didn't reply to my response for over a month. Their next reply was to ask a bunch of questions about firmware and app permissions, which was not helpful. This indicates to me there is a problem with support and also possibly a problem with the deveopment group. Any retail product should have a features list somewhere, maybe not available to the public, but certainly available to the support team. That feature list should indicate if there is a way to control the volume. Rather than taking a month to ask additional, irrelevant questions, the support people should have either looked at the feature list or asked the developers if there is a way to increase the volume.
That did not happen, and so I'm reducing the rating to 3 stars. All products can have problems and the test of a good product is having a support group that can quickly and accurately respond to the problem (or question), and that is not the case with Merkury.
Since I planed to install this about 6 feet off the ground, the camera is of limited value. It doesn't pan, which was my issue, and no one can hear what is said through the app, which is their issue. Support is not helpful so I don't know if this is a problem with the camera or a feature they left our or a feature they intend to include later. I can no longer recommend this product, unless you are going to install it very close to whoever you are wanting to speak with.

title: Nice USB-C hub
text:
I got this because my laptop has only 3 USB C ports and no standard USB ports. One of them is for power, and I've got a wireless mouse and keyboard, which leaves one port for everything else.
Needless to say, I need a few more ports and also an ethernet connection (RJ45).
The unit comes nicely boxed and for some reason has a bunch of stickers for the flags of various countries. Not sure why, but it's an interesting approach.
It has a lot of ports, an HDMI, RJ45,SD Card and micro SD, 1 USB C, 1 PD, which looks like a USB C, but is a power port, 2 USB 2.0 and 2 USB 3.0.
There is a warning label that says it might get hot (up to 130" F) and thatdevices with power higher than 7.5W are not supported, so check on the things you will be plugging into the hub before you buy it. It also says the PD adapter is under 40W and may not be able to charge all devices through the hub.
So, if you are going to use this to power a bunch of USB devices or charge your phones, it might not work. But if you are just plugging things in like cameras, microphones or drives then it will work fine.
For having all those ports, it's not as large as some others I've used and all in all is a nice hub. If you need more ports, then this is definitely worth considering.

title: Good cables
text:

These work great. I like the three lengths, (6.6, 3.3 and 1 foot), and alsolike the color, which makes them easy to find in the car..
So far, they have worked great in the car and are also good to use to charge the phone and tablets that use USB-C. They are also reasonably priced, and are less than some packages that have only 2 cables. If you need USB-C cables then give thesea try.

title: Nice hub that allows you to have multiple monitors
text:
I recently got a 15" portable monitor to use with my laptop when I'm traveling and because I don't have a lot of USB C ports on my laptop, I was looking for a hub. This one seemed to be just what I needed and it had the ability to plug in 2 HDMI monitors and also card readers for SD cards.
When I first tried it, I was disappointed in how it worked. It didn't light up the two additional monitors and the ethernet connection seemed slow. I took it off and went back to my old hub. Then a couple of days later I decided to try it again, and this time it worked great. I guess the monitors need some time to figure out what they are doing and I did a speed test with this ethernet connection and my old one and the speed was the same.
So, now instead of just having a portable monitor, I have three monitors and it works great. One thing I don't like about it is that you have to use the HDMI ports to make it recognize multiple monitors. That's fine for my desktop monitor, but the portable one has the ability to do USB-C to USB-C connection of the monitor. When I'm traveling, I can just use that connection and the cables are much easier to deal with. So that's one downside but it may be just my personal preference so I'm giving it 5 stars because it works and does what it's supposed to do. If you are looking to set up multiple monitors for a laptop, this is the hub you want to get.

title: Great watch, much better than my old "smart" watch
text:
I got Moto 360 several years ago when smart watches first came out and it was nice, but annoying. It was tied into everything and kept giving me alerts and so eventually I got tired of it. My wife also had a first generation Samsung Gear watch and that was about the same as the Moto.
Well, fast forward a few years and now my wife, daughter, son and daughter-in-law all have newer smart watches (Apple Watches and Fitbit) and they all love them. It was time to get a new phone, so I got a Samsung S20 FE and then decided to get the Samsung watch. I saw on the reviews that it really works well with Samsung phones and so I decided to get the Watch 3. I was looking at the Watch 2, which had a few less features and then I found the Watch 3 in the 41mm size and then found a refurbished one so I ended up paying about the same for the Watch 3 as I would have for the Watch 2.
I'm very impressed with the watch and really love it. I didn't get the one with a cell phone, it just connects to my phone with bluetooth and/or wifi, but it's really amazing. I get my messages, and can turn off the ones that I don't want and then I also get all the health apps. So, now it tells me to get off my chair and walk around and does EKG and stress tesing and Oxygen levels..
I was concerned that the 41 mm might be too small, but it is a great size for me as you can see from the pic. I have had a Citizen Echo Drive for more than 10 years and it is a little larger, but I like the size of the Watch 3 better.
If you are thinking about getting a watch, this one is a good deal right now and I believe it does work best if you use it with a Samsung phone.

title: Great webcam at a reasonable price
text:
When the lockdown started last year, I decided to look for an external webcam for my laptop. I talked with a couple of friends who recomended the Logitech 920, so Iooked on Amazon and was shocked at the cost. It normally went for about $60, but when I looked it was $200. I wasn't going to pay that high a price, so I tried a couple of low cost alternatives, both of which I had to return.
Then I found out about the Emeet webcam from a friend of mine. He said it worked great and so at $27, I decided to give it a try. I'm glad I did because it's a great little webcam. The camera iteslf is high quality and auto focus. It has a wider field of view than my laptop camera and also has a decent microphone. I'm very happy with the purchase and now use it most of the time on Zoom calls. If you are looking for an alternative to the 920, this is definitely it. The only issue is that I wish it had a privacy screen, but the 920 doesn't have one either so it's a fair comparison.
If you are looking for a good webcam grab this one, it's a great deal.

title: Great little USB Dongle Gadget
text:
My laptop, like a lot of them these days, doesn't have an ethernet port for plugging directly into the network. When I got the laptop it came with a dongle that allowed me to connect the the ethernet cable through my USB port. It worked great but took away one of the USB ports and also made it difficult to plug anything else into the port next to it.
I had been looking for something different and when I did a search I must have looked at 10-15 of them. This one caught my eye because it had three USB 3.0 ports, and it got a lot of great reviews so I gave it a try. I've had it now for about a month and it works great.
It allows me to connect to my network with an ethernet cable which gives me a lot better speeds than WiFi, and it gives me three USB 3.0 ports that I can use for anything I need to plug into the computer. The ports are spread out on the device so that I can actually plug three things in, which is an added bonus. The problem I had in the past was that I needed to use a device to read several types of SD cards, and the device is so large it can't really be plugged into my laptop USB ports. With the uni dongle I have no problems and it works great.
So, if you are looking for an ethernet to USB dongle, this one is highly recommended.

They normally have a setting that if you have a USB mouse plugged in you can de-activate the touchpad, but they don't recognize Bluetooth mice in the same way.
Nevertheless I really like it, and it turns itself off when not in use so the battery lasts a long time. Great buy.

title: Haven't used it, hope I never will
text: I always have to think about these accidental protection plans, but I decided to get it for my camera because it was about $1,000 and I mostly got it so that I don't have to worry about dropping it. title: Good size for my camera.
text: I love these cards for my camera.  The 32 GB are just the right size for me to use in my Nikon D5300 . title: Good product
text: I got this to put on my Newer flash attachment, but it was for a different model. I tried to put it on several different ways and finally gave up. Aside from that, it's a great product and wish it did work with my flash, but then I discovered that my flash has a built in diffuser so I don't really need it. Just make sure it fits the model you have and you will be fine.

title: Works fine
text: I got an Op/Tech strap for my camera and love it.  I got these to attach a wrist strap that I already have to my camera.  I have one of these on my camera to attach to the strap and now I just put the corresponding one on my wrist strap and it's a breeze to change over.

title: Nice case, does what it is supposed to do
text:
I got this to keep my memory cards in order and it fills the bill. I don't have a lot of them yet, but even having two or three can be a challenge to keep them from disappearing inside a camera bag. It is small, and will only fit 2 cards with cases, but since this acts as a case you don't really need any more room for cases.
I attached the strap more to be able to pull it out of the bag than for any other reason. I guess you could attach it to your strap, but I don't see the need for that.

title: Great little addition
text: I got this to hold an extra battery for my D5300 and it works great.  I attached it to my Op/Tech sling and it just sits there waiting to be used.  The battery is a snug fit which is great, and attaching it to the sling is easy.  You do need to have the ability to thread part of your sling or strap through this holder. but that keeps it more secure in my opinion.

title: Great product... get two
text: This is a great addition to any photographer's kit.  I already have a set, but figured that since it is all plastic, it will eventually break so I ordered this set as a backup.  At the price point, it's an easy decision.  These things really do reduce the glare from the built-in flash, so if you are wondering about getting it, just go ahead.  I've recommended this to several of my friends and they all really like them.

title: Great Monopod
text:
This is a great little monopod. It is lightweight and very sturdy. I like the wrist strap and the cap that goes on the screw. I added a ball head and the cap fits on that as well, so it makes a nice package.
I've used it now several times and it's definitely not a tripod, but will do in a pinch, and also is a great walking staff. Highly recommended.

title: and is very easy to use
text:
I wanted something to reduce the glare from my built in flash on my Nikon D5300. This does just that, and is very easy to use. When I got it, I took a picture of two oranges and there was a lot of glare. I put on the white diffuser and the next picture was remarkably better. I've posted the pictures so you can see the differences.
The thing is relatively light and will at some point break, but the price point is such that you can get a couple of them and keep one as a spare. If you are thinking about this just go ahead and order it. You will not be disappointed.

title: Heavy but good quality
text: I purchased this to go on top of my monopod but when it came I was surprised at how heavy it was.  I liked how it worked, and it is a quality product but it was about twice as heavy as the monopod so I ordered a simpler ball head.  I kept this one because it is a good quality product but if you are looking at this product, just know it is heavy.

title: This is a great product. I purchased it to use with my ...
text: This is a great product.  I purchased it to use with my Nikon D5300 and it works well on the camera and as a bonus it can be used as a slave flash to the built in flash on the camera without any wires.  I wasn't sure how this was going to work, but it is really simple and works well. title: this is the one to get
text:
