If g you are looking for a replacement for the official Nikon HB-32, this is definitely the one to get. It went on quickly and even went over the filter I had on the lens. I've got the Nikon 18mm- 10 mm lens and it fits perfectly. Great product.

title: Not a good fit
text: I bought this for my Nikon 18mm- 10 mm lens. The are a bunch of these replacement hoods out there and this one seemed reasonable.  I received it today and put it on the lens. There were a couple of dark spots sheer you can see the hood at 18mm up to about 24mm.  I tried talking off the filter and it was even worse,  then I tried to screw it in even tighter, but nothing worked.  The lens cap holder and brush are nice,  but the hood is useless.

title: Didn't work for me, but Seller is Great
text:
A friend of mine recommended this product and so I got it before taking a trip out west. The installation went well and it seemed to work at first, but after about 5-15 minutes things started going wrong. The music would just go out for no reason while I was riding. If I clicked the buttons it might come back on and it might not. I didn't want to fiddle with it since I was on my bike, but when I stopped I could get it to work and then it might work for half an hour. In some cases, it didn't even last as long as one song until it went out. After the first day I thought I had it working, and the second day was not too bad, but the third day it was a total bust. I couldn't get it to work at all.
That's the bad news, and from some of the reviews I've read it is a crap shoot whether you get a good one or not. And by the way, the price of this was $69 when I bought it and now it's almost double.
The good news is that I got in touch with IBD Electronics and they were great. They gave me the options of replacing it (but it was back ordered), refunding my money or getting another product. I had a couple of questions and acutally ended up calling them. The people there were fantastic. I eventually decided to get an LG Tone and they sent it out and credited me with the difference in the same day. Great customer service.
By the way, the Tone is great. I have not tried to use it to make or receive calls, but really don't want to do that while riding my motorcycle, so playing the music and listening to the GPS is all I need it for. When I'm not on my bike, the thing works great at not only the music, but also at making and receiving calls. The parrot device may be good for when you are on the bike,but that's it. The Tone is great for sitting at your desk and listening to music. Give it a look, and it's only about $40.

title: Amazing Value
text:
I looked at a lot of cases on Amazon and this one was not only reasonably priced, but also got great reviews. There is no reason a case for a Kindle or iPad has to cost $50, and the MiniSuit case is proof positive. The Kindle fits very snug in the case, and there is no chance it will fall out. The quality is reasonable and I really like the fact that you can have two angles for the stand.
The reason I did not give it five stars is that it doesn't have the ability to be a stand for the portrait orientation. Landscape works great, but it really should have a way to stand up the Kindle in Portrait. Otherwise, it is a great product and you should not hesitate to purchase it if you want a quality case at a reasonable price. Great job MiniSuit.

title: Player is great, software is garbage
text:
I had an iPod 2GB Nano and wanted to get something with larger capacity. I did some research and finally bought the Walkman. I was around for the very first Sony Walkman casette tape player, so the idea of getting a Sony MP3 player was appealing.
After using it for over a month, I find it a great little device. The battery life is amazing. I charged it over two weeks ago and have used it on multiple three hour car rides. I also had it hooked up to a speaker in my office and left it on for several hours and it stil has battery life.
It took me some time to get used to the navigation, but now I am fine with the difference between the Walkman and the iPod. The sound quality is good and although the volume could be better, it is acceptable for my use.
The major problem I have with the unit is the software. Sony included one of those mini disc's which loaded a couple of software programs on my computer. The main program is one which allows you to drag and drop files from your computer to the player; however, it doesn't work. I dragged a few tunes to see how it worked and then started dragging all the music. The software kept accepting the tunes, but after it "loaded" for about 2 hours, I discovered it had only loaded the first set of tunes. The rest, and the two hour wait, was for nothing. The software also has a "delete" function, which also doesn't work. It tells you that it delets items from the player, but they are still there.
So, I junked that software and decided to use the Windows Media Player. This is ok, except that the Media Player has a very odd way to create playlists. There are some round about ways to create the play list and I have finaly learned how to do it, but it took way too long compared to iTunes. The other odd thing is that when you create a play list it has to be from tunes on your computer, not on the device. Then when you sync the device to load the playlist, it may or may not put duplicate versions of the music on the device. Sometimes it finds the songs on the device and sometimes it does not. So, I ended up with multiple copies of some songs. The device software is also pathetic. It doesn't allow you to create playlists on the device, and as others have noted, there is no way to delete items from the device without using the software.
I finally just had the computer recognize the device as an external drive and was able to load songs and delete them with no probme.
Despite the isues, I still like the device better than my Nano. For one thing it has an FM receiver, which works great. Now that I have come to terms with the crappy software, it works great. So, if you are looking for an alternative to the iPod, this is a good option. Just stay away from the software provided by Sony and you will be fine.

title: Fantastic functionality; limited lifespan
text:
I should start by saying that purchasing this iPad case dramatically changed how and how much I use my iPad. How wonderful to have the laptop - style hinge, but one that rotates 360°. In any position, at a desk, sitting up in bed, lying on my side, or in my lap, it is incredibly easy to set the screen at the perfect angle. The Bluetooth connection is great, and the size of the keyboard is exactly right for my medium sized hands.

So why only four stars? The sad fact is that after six months of daily hard use, the plastic surrounding one of the hinges began to crack, with the crack growing progressively bigger. Finally, before the unit was seven months old, the two halves of the clam case began to separate completely, and the keyboard was no longer operational. That was very disappointing, obviously.

So why rate it so highly? Because I have tried a significant number of other cases, and none even came close to the functionality of this clam case. Given my heavy use, I would actually rather replace a clam case every six months than struggle with the fixed angle and other limitations of every other model I have used. My upshot: if you have the money to spend, you will love this item. Just don't expect the hinges, or the plastic surrounding them, to last for more than six months of heavy daily use.

Third time is the charm. Unlike the other two I tried before this one… The installation supplies worked flawlessly. The instructions were clear and easy to follow. The anti fingerprint works very nicely as well. Add in that this option costs less than the first two I tried.

Im so disappointed in this product. It will be getting returned.

The most significant is the fact that reading the Kindle 8.9 in bright sunlight is just not possible. The touch screen has a shiny surface that reflects causing reading, watching films or playing games virtually an impossibility. On the otherhand, reading in a dark room has been corrected with its own lighted background. Another issue is that many of the android apps that are available on other devices are just not available here (not a major problem but a disappointment). Using the Web has its limitations as well since it loads extremely slow and if opening something from an email closing the site will not take you back to the original email (again not a major problem). Recommend the optional quick charge plug since this Kindle requires a charge quite frequently (daily typically) and this provides a charge very quickly. Overall, I have really enjoyed my Kindle 8.9 and use it daily.

Edit (8/25/13). Additional comments. Certain videos require Flash Drive which is not available with the Kindle which is disappointing. While not the fault of Kindle potentially Amazon does not partner with Directv for their Directv Everywhere function or certain programing like ESPN 360 although HBO GO, Showtime Anywhere, Starz and Encore movies and programing are available if subscribed though Directv or a recognized provider.

update 1/12/17 .. tried ssd cache and really found no speed improvement, so ditched and added a 5th HDD and also switched to RAID 6 .. which is more reliable .. Still working great getting 110 reads/writes now

update 10/18/17 .. still working great. Had some reboot issues but switched memory and where I had plugged in and seems to have stabilized for now. Great buy when stable.

update 2/8/18 .. I off and on was having issues with this unit (dropping drives randomly)
Tech support right away said I needed to send in for RMA (which I finally did)
I had upgraded RAM, but luckily saved original otherwise they would not repair.
They will only repair original setup. 2 weeks later got my unit back and now it's been stable (20 days no issues) Looks like they replaced a faulty mobo.
Tech support for me was great, they have been very helpful.
I still really like this unit for the price, but my Synology seemed like a better built product. Hopefully, after this repair it remains stable (so far so good)

4/15/2019 - The Unit has now dropped drives again, and is out of Warranty so will not RMA
Basically 2 years of service with an RMA after 1 year, and dead after the second year.
Will not buy QNAP again

title: So far, so good
text: Imagine my happiness when I took my Ryobi string trimmer out of storage this spring only to find the battery (which was working fine when I put it away last fall) refused to take a charge. This, for a string trimmer which - with the original battery and charger - only cost $10 more than that. But I digress. THIS battery is the functional equivalent of the Ryobi branded device but about 40% less expensive. Still overpriced, but what choice do we - the Ryobi indentured - have? It fits, charges, works and lasts as long as the Ryobi device did when new. Have no worries about whether it will work - it will.

title: Minor complaints, but generally a decent buy
text: I’m not a DIY kind of guy, so I went with the cheapest, simplest mount I could find. It’s okay, but be prepared for some minor adjustments. The Pros: price. It’s much less expensive than most of the others. It’s also quite minimalist - no thick bezels. It’s made of a flexible silicone material - that’s both a pro and a con - the pro - it’s soft on your tablet - no scratches. It’s also somewhat flexible - I installed mine vertically in a tight space and there’s no room to slide the tablet in from the side. Instead, I have to seat it in the bottom mount and sort of snap it into place in the top. Given the flexibility of the material, this works fine. The cons: included with the mount are 6 each screws and wall anchors - no spares and no washers. The anchors don’t have any lip on the end so a couple of mine dropped into the wall cavity, making it necessary to go buy some spares. Also, the screw heads easily pull through the holes in the mounts when tightened. I fixed that with a handful of small washers which should be included with the mount kit. Also, my tablet (an old iPad Air 2) Is quite slim and doesn’t fit snugly in the mount so I put a short strip of thin silicone insulation behind it to better hold it in place. There is a slot in the center of one mount to allow access For a charging cable. Thoughtfully, it appears to be even wide enough for the old style wide Apple connector. Included is also a paper template for various size devices and a stick on cable retainer. Aside from the minor complaints about washers and wall mounts, I’m satisfied with the kit.

title: An alternative to Apple’s silicone tips
text: I have trouble with the OEM silicone tips keeping a good seal. If I do something wild and crazy (like turning my head /sarcasm) the seal breaks and noise cancellation is diminished. I’m used to using memory foam earplugs and decided to try these memory foam AirPod tips. Not as good as I had hoped, but not a complete waste either. They fit more snugly and hold a seal better than Apple’s silicone tips, so that’s a plus. However, they aren’t as comfortable for long listening sessions. I tried the smaller size, thinking maybe the issue was size... nope. I’d also suggest being very careful when removing them as well - the Apple tips are surprisingly resilient (seemingly indestructible, despite the impression that the silicone is easily tearable. It isn’t.) but I destroyed one of the memory foam tips in the process of unsnapping it from the AirPod.

title: Powers up my old iPad 1 👍
text: I was hoping for a braided cable, or something a little thicker than the cheap ones that Apple includes with their devices. Nope - same thickness, but at least this one has strain relief on both ends. Plus, it’s a fraction of the cost of the official Apple cable and twice the length, so that’s worth a couple of stars.

title: Treble! Hooray, I can understand Alexa now!
text: I have Echo devices of one kind or another in every room and have had others that I’ve decided to let go (original Echo and Echo Auto). They’ve all performed their smarthome duties acceptably well. My biggest complaint across the board is sound quality. Alexa always sounds like she’s talking to you from underneath a pile of pillows. Bass? Sure, on the Echo Show, at least. Treble? Nada. Sure, you can use the app’s “equalizer”... but it’d take an oscilloscope to detect the minuscule difference that makes in the sound quality. I’d given up on getting any more devices... until I saw a review of the Flex on Paul Hibbert’s YouTube channel... he liked it, but said (I think) that it sounded ‘trebly’. Trebly?! That’s a magic word to my ears. I ordered one up and found that it indeed sounds ‘trebly’ (call it tinny of you like) but who cares? Who seriously listens to music on these tiny little devices anyway?! I can understand what Alexa says now - all the plosives are there. I still wonder why Amazon can’t tune the rest of the Alexa enabled devices for better higher frequency clarity.

title: A good value
text: I bought these to use with Brain.fm. I would have preferred wireless but Bluetooth enabled models don’t seem to be able to run all night (8 hours) on a charge. These are actually better than I expected in a couple ways - first, they sound surprisingly good for the price. The bass response is acceptable and the sound is well balanced across the audible spectrum. Second, the cable is a very flexible and durable mesh fabric. It doesn’t kink and tangle as easily as plastic and is reinforced at the plug end. The headband is a light fleece type material - it tends to be warm, but that would be a plus outdoors in cold weather. The transducers are relatively easy to reposition by sticking your finger into the slots made for that purpose. That’s really my only complaint - there’s nothing to really keep them firmly positioned. They tend to shift around easily when putting on or removing the headband. (This tugs on the cable where it enters the back of the headband.) It might be helpful to put a couple of stitches on either side of them to hold them in place. Initially, the headband was a little tight on me but I was able to stretch it out a bit for better comfort - still snug enough to stay in position, but not enough to be uncomfortable.

title: I’m a satisfied customer
text: After reading the many critical of Blink’s customer service I wanted to add my two cents. I don’t have a LOT of experience with support, but did just have one of my cameras (indoor) fail on me after several months of trouble-free use. I tried an assortment of things before emailing Blink (reset, replace batteries, uninstall/reinstall) and had pretty much determined it was a hardware issue. Blink support had me go through the same troubleshooting steps and came to the same conclusion. The entire process from my initial contact to their resolution took less than a day. They had a replacement camera and an RMA label in my hands in about a week, and the replacement is working fine (along with my other cameras - both indoor and XT outdoor). I’m satisfied with my system and Blink’s support. My only criticism is minor - the iOS app doesn’t support iPad in native landscape mode and I live on my iPad. Battery life has been great - I’ve had most of my cameras for almost a year and haven’t had any batteries die yet. Blink’s servers have been down (maybe?) three times since I’ve been using their gear (that I’ve noticed) and one of those times was a widespread outage which couldn’t be blamed on them. Acceptable service, especially considering it’s provided at no cost. I’m sure you can buy better security cameras, but I don’t know of anything better, easier to setup or more flexible for the price.

And gods forbid you should hit the delete key to get rid of some of the repeating characters because the delete key will repeat and delete what you've just typed. The rubber pads on both sides of the keyboard mysteriously started peeling off not too long ago. They don't seem to be absolutely necessary, so I stopped trying to stick them back on and instead, peeled them off and cleaned the glue residue they left behind. Battery life is waning - I have to charge the case almost nightly or the orange light starts flashing and it loses connectivity or shuts down. Other than those issues, it still works. It looks good and fits well. I haven't had any magnet issues and the backlight is a godsend.

** update ** It's only fair to also point out that Belkin must monitor Amazon for comments about their products. I didn't contact them - they proactively contacted me and arranged a replacement for my QODE case/keyboard. The unit is two years old, and given my experience with most other manufacturers, I wasn't expecting anything, so this is a nice surprise. Kudos to Belkin customer support for what I consider to be service above and beyond. I've received the replacement and have been using it for a couple of weeks - no sign of the connectivity or repeating key issues and (of course) the rubber bumpers are intact.

title: meh
text: Keep in mind: this is a $40 device. If you're looking for reliable home surveillance, probably best to skip this one, and maybe D-Link altogether. That having been said, I found it fairly easy to setup. Video streaming to mydlink.com is at best undependable, however, so I wasn't sure at the time if setup was working or not. After messing with it for about an hour I had to leave and wasn't able to access the video stream. I checked in later and it had magically started working on its own. Go figure. You can access the camera directly via IP address or via their freebie app locally, but remote is a crapshoot. Resolution is low quality (320x240). Night mode is okay close up. I'm unable to access mydlink.com on my Mac - apparently there's no support for the current MacOS (Sierra). I emailed D-Link support with questions but received a generic "this is how to reinstall the camera" response, so I don't know if they eventually plan to support Sierra. It seems possible that this device has been orphaned in favor of newer models. The camera is small and light and the base is quite adjustable to allow easy positioning. (note: indoor use only) I bought it to enable watching for animal activity in my wooded back yard - I haven't managed to get it set up to email me activity alerts yet but it's (barely) adequate for that purpose.

title: the ear of the beholder
text: Everybody has an opinion and they're all different. I finally settled on a pair of MDR-EX51LP buds for my iPod. The buds that come with the iPod are poor sounding and uncomfortable, no matter how trendy it may be to have a white wires dangling from your ears. I tried several different types and brands and settled on these. They have a more balanced sound than the other headphones in the sub $50 bracket that I tested - good bass, clean highs and mids. Do they compare with premium studio cans? No, but neither do the price tag, size or weight. They block office noise at a reasonable SPL and allow me to concentrate on my work without distraction. I can still hear some outside sound if I keep the music volume low enough - as has been mentioned before, that can be a good thing. They're very comfortable - I wear them for hours at a time on a daily basis. I don't get the uneven cord length, but it really isn't a big deal. Headphones are like operating systems - there is no such thing as one size fits all. Get the ones that work for you (and your audio device!) and don't start a holy war with someone who prefers something different.

title: Just OK for the Keyboard
text:
I try real hard to be honest in every review. Some vendors take offense to honesty and products that are not a 5-star rating. But, we on Amazon, truly depend on each other and honesty for products that we want to purchase. We are all different but for me this is my honest assessment. The tablet case does secure the LG G f8 (8inch) tablet well. But, I have had a similar case in the past for my Kindle Fire and never had any issues. It is very strong and durable. My issue is with the keyboard and how it secures with the tablet case. The keyboard is a sturdy construction and not a silicone keypad. BUT, there is not tiny mouse pad within its design. That means to make my LG G tablet truly functional for writing documents, emails and the such I need to have an additional item - a wireless mouse; otherwise why need a keyboard. So, I had to order a mini mouse as well which doesn't exactly fit anyplace but in my pocket or carry bag. The other issue is the way the tablet, case and keyboard are designed to be closed. The case elastic strap is actually the same as the one on my kindle Fire and slips around the secured tablet and does it well. However, add a keyboard, which was NOT a design to this tablet holder and you have to decide if you want the keyboard face against your tablet, tight, as that elastic strap secures them both. that means the keyboard is actually not secure by the case but ONLY by the outer elastic strap. Or, you flip the keyboard so that the back of that keypad rests against your tablet screen and it is still only secured by the outer elastic strap. Both methods require that you ensure you keep this tablet case upright so that the keyboard does not slip out of this elastic band as time and use deteriorate the elastic and its tension. So, in essence, this is a case that has been around and works well for Kindle Fire and probably this tablet. but, this case was NOT designed to include a keyboard. this was a vendor added item with an existing product. When you pay $200 for a tablet you want to ensure you do not scratch the screen or damage the tablet. And if you like the use of a keyboard, note that a mouse will also be required and that it may be best to look for alternative cases to accommodate your needs in one neat package
Update: July 2016: well after very limited use the key board is no loner functioning. It's not the charge it is a dead key board. I am a senior and disabled Vietnam veteran appreciate each dollar of my disability pay and do not have that luxury of repeat purchases. So, even though I am only one customer I would consider other products that have a higher reliability and that are not tied to a protective case purchase.

title: Maybe it was my fault for not understanding how it worked but very disappointed
text: I thought that a wireless SDHC card was genious, i can upload my pictures automatically as long as I am in range of my wireless connection! Brillant, that means they'll automatically transfer whenever I come home, i don't even have to take my camera out of my purse.  NOPE, that's not how it works.  First of all your camera has to be ON in order to transfer, so you have to physically get your camera and turn it on near your computer.  That's about as much work as taking the memory card out.  Secondly, you have to leave this giantic bulky USB connected plugged into your computer which is annoying and not at all convenient.  By the time you've done those two steps it would have been easier to take out the memory card and stick it in the computer. Then i realize my computer has an SDHC slot in it making this whole thing even more stupid.  I'm going to try and send it back if I can.  I don't really see the appeal unless you are a professional that wants to be able to display pictures on a screen as he's taking them, then that's cool but if you just want an easier time transfering them to your home computer this isn't a benefit.  Considering how much more expensive they are than regular SDHC cards it's a total waste.

title: the device I didn't know I needed
text:
I've been a cynic of wearables for a long time by debating the need to charge a watch daily, and the slew of available features that I swore I'd never use such as calling, and texting from my watch...

I was wrong. I find myself relying more on the watch than my phone for setting alarms or timers. I use the phone feature to have brief calls, or send a quick reply to a text message.

The features for tracking my daily sleep, steps, and heart rate, help make me more conscious of my life style.

Before purchasing this watch I was looking at cheaper alternatives, but I am glad that I purchased the iwatch because it works well with my other devices and is a welcome member of my slowly growing gadget family.

There are a few annoyances by saying "hey siri" i summon the total of 3 siri's fighting over which device will answer my command.

I am a big guy and was worried the watch band would'nt fit but I am happy to report that it comes with 2 band sizes and the large band fit my beefy wrist.

title: Happy with my purchase it's a good basic trackpad
text:
The touchpad is exactly as advertised. Very basic features, and plug & play. The gestures work fine; however, I only use double finger up and down for scrolling and single tap for click.

The left and right buttons have a nice clicky snap to them that gives it nice feedback whenever you interact with them. And the surface area your fingers interact with to move the cursor has a slight texture but nothing significant. It's not smooth like glass but not rough like sand paper.

For the price it meets my expectations. My hands are quite bad and I can't use a traditional mouse. I prefer this over a trackball style setup and would recommend it to anyone in my situation.

I'll admit the one thing I forgot is that there's no middle mouse button, but that seems common among all trackpads and just highlights my oversight during pre-purchase.

title: 70 LBS Down and counting!
text: I credit Fitbit with my loss of 70 lbs over a period of approximately 9 months, a loss I've kept off for going on a year.  Using it regularly made me realize how little exercise I was getting, and made me focus on increasing my efforts.  I'm not one for group exercise, but competing daily against myself--my previous Fitbit results-- stirred my competitive juices, and I tried to better my numbers every day.  Now I'm at the point where I feel restless if I haven't walked my five miles a day, and I try to shake up my routine a bit by finding new and different forms of exercise--like skydiving!  When I think of all the money I wasted over the years on exercise equipment, weight loss plans and so forth, I'm grateful for the simplicity and effectiveness of Fitbit.  Not to say that it would work for everyone--motivation is key--but at this price, it's well worth a try.

title: A very poor tablet
text:
This tablet computer lacks several features that were present on my older Galaxy Tab A 10.1:

1. The new tablet lacks a hard Home button. This is inconvenient because I use the tablet for running Garmin Pilot software. Having a hard Home button is easier to use while flying that the soft button.

2. On my old tablet I was able to move apps from internal storage to an SD card, thus saving internal storage space. The new tablet does not allow for moving apps to an SD card. Very disappointed.

Had I known about these problems before I bought the new tablet, I would not have purchased it.

I tried using the tablet today while flying. I use the Garmin Pilot app for navigation and flight information. The display did not show all of the information provided by the app. For example, it failed to display the "Direct To" icon. This makes the tablet almost useless when used for running the Pilot app.

This afternoon, I contacted Amazon and asked for a refund. I returned the tablet computer to a local Amazon site.

Regrettably, the tablet proved almost worthless in light of the use for which it was purchased.

title: Poor picture quality
text: I have used this camera for a month.  I have used it in a variety of settings: low light, indoors, super zoom, outdoors bright light, twilight/dusk shots, sports shots.  I have to say in every case I have been extremely disappointed at its performance.  The shots are not sharp.  If I take 5 identical shots in a row - the lighting looks different in each of them - which means.  Shot one the light may fine but kid isn't smiling.  Reshoot and kid looks great but lighting is off.  Take another shot - kid is fine but flash too bright.  Frustrating!!!  My biggest complaint is that the IA setting (the intelligent auto) is SOOOOOOO slow.  Most of my shots are of my kids and I keep missing shots.  I have used a compact digital point and shoot before - I am used to a delay but they delay on the Panasonic is painstakingly slow.  I read countless reviews and felt so confident purchasing this camera.  What a letdown!!!  I tried to return it to Amazon but I was 1 DAY past 30 day return window.  Darn!!!!  Keep shopping around if you want a handy decent pocket camera - this isn't the one.

title: Protects pets from electric shock and protects oxygen tubing.
text: If you have pets that might want to chew wires, or chew something such as oxygen tubing, then this wonderful product is exactly what you need.  It will fit neatly and securely over whatever wires or tubing you need to protect.  But be sure to order the correct diameter and the length you need!  That is very important!  Little critters can electrocute themselves by chewing wires, and supplemental oxygen users can suddenly realize they aren't getting any air because their tubing has been punctured.  With the Alex Tech Wire Protector Tubing that won't happen because the critters actually leave it alone.  A great product!  It will give you peace of mind as it protects from harm.

title: 5-disc DVD player, perfect for Couch Potatoes!
text: So glad to have found a DVD player with a 5-disc changer.  They were almost impossible to find a few years back, but this time, I was able to find a few choices.  I know everyone is streaming now, and I like to stream movies, too.  But I also have certain favorites on DVD.  If you want to watch a bunch of episodes of your favorite TV series, or just have some kind of movie marathon - it's great to be able to put in a bunch of DVDs and then just click the remote to change discs.  Especially when I'm curled up on the couch, surrounded by dogs and the occasional cat, and don't want to get up and disturb everyone. This Sony has worked perfectly so far.  It came with a remote, of course, and also included audio/video cables, the ones that have the red, yellow and white ends.  Unfortunately, being an older model, it does not support HDMI input.  But the picture is still very good even without that.  I was really happy to find this unit, since my old one recently gave up the ghost!  If you like to watch a lot of movies or TV without getting up, this DVD player is for you!!

title: Great Wi-Fi router has great range for large 2-story house
text: I have a 3100 sq ft home, 2-story.  We were having trouble getting the Wi-Fi signal upstairs.  We moved our original Linksys router into the dining room, right near the foot of the stairs, with a long CABLE running down the hall to the office where the line comes in.  Kind of defeats the whole idea of Wi-Fi!  I called a cabler and was ready to run a cable upstairs, when he recommended just purchasing a better router.  I don't know why I didn't think of that - I guess I assumed all routers were basically the same.  (They are NOT!)  This ASUS router did the trick.  I have it in my office downstairs, and the signal reaches all the way to the other end of the house as well as upstairs to all bedrooms up there.  I was able to remove the embarrassing cable running down the hall, and it's been working very well now for over 2 months.  Just fyi, I also asked the cabler about signal boosters/extenders, but he told me they do not work as well as purchasing a quality router to begin with.

text: I very seldom review products I purchase on Amazon but felt this one merited a few minutes of my time. I received this bag the day after I placed the order- faster than the shipping speed I paid for. It is a beautiful, beautiful bag. The look is just what I was going for- vintage, without actually being old. The material and craftsman ship is superb. It looks lux, without the lux price tag. It is sturdy and lightweight and the front buckles keep things secure. The strap is adjustable which is great, since I typically like to wear my bags/purses cross body. The inside is padded and also adjustable. It has three "compartments". I have a Cannon Rebel T3i and when unassembled, the camera body fits in one compartment and the lens fits in the second compartment. These compartments can be adjusted so I can combine two of them into one large compartment and store the camera assembled...which is great if you don't want to constantly be removing and adding the lens. Either way, that still leaves a third compartment to hold other things, as well as a back pocket for additional storage. Overall it's just a fantastic bag and a price that can't be beat. It doesn't look like a camera bag so really could be used for all sorts of things.  I am excited to take this with me on my next trip!

The resolution is pretty good for the price you pay, the sound quality isn't bad, and the video display is good as well. The remote is great, as are its quick press buttons for "photos", "photos and music", and "video"....it's great for the less technically inclined. I gave this as a gift to my grandmother for Christmas and she LOVES it, and it's SO easy for her to use. It doesn't have all the bells and whistles that pricier models have, but if you're looking for a simple, easy to use digital frame to display your pictures, you can't beat this price!!

I've already had to send his brand new iPad back to Apple to replace the port (they just replaced the entire product) because he had messed it up propping it on the charging cable jutting out of the port). And because he has uncontrolled seizures, he has to have a kid proof thick foam case. When these popped up as a Suggestion... I know these apps listen but I swear I'm starting to think they read minds lol... I figured I'd give them a try. They fit!! Even with his thick, foam case. It's a little tricky to get it in, but going slowly it fits and stays in the port.

title: Trees are my issue... I live in the middle of a forest, literally
text:
My barn is downhill from my house, about 250' I suppose, and it should be connecting to my Xfinity Prepaid (I get ZERO cellular-data service because of the metal roof and the barn being in a valley, so a second PrePaid service wasn't feasible for the rare occasions I needed to look something up while I was at the barn). This took my signal of around .9 mbps to upwards of 15mbps. I'm not streaming or gaming, but I could absolutely stream on my one device easily at that speed. My son is able to play games on his tablet while I work, which was the main reason - really - that I 'needed' service down there.

It is possible I haven't set this up correctly, so my speeds might could actually be better, but it's been too too HOT in Georgia for me to stress about that yet. Lol

title: Popped in easy... wondering if it was TOO easy (**updated since initial review).
text:
UPDATE: I finally had to remove the 'FirePad' from the case. I can confirm it DOES NOT just pop out as easily as it pops in... which is a relief. Upgraded review to 4.5 stars as what keeps this allegedly kid-proof from being 5 is it's a little too hard plasticy (it needs a layer of firm foam around it) and the screen isn't recessed from the edge of the hard plastic. Believe me, an extra layer of foam which would automatically make the screen of the tablet recessed back about 3 mm would make a HUGE difference with a kid... or a 'dropper' adult (🙋🏼‍♀️). I have a review for an iPad mini 6 'kid case' in purple... that case is ideal. If only...

I feel like if butter knives and ripped-to-the-quick fingernails aren't involved in putting a tablet in a kid-friendly case, maybe it's not gonna stand up to 🌪MY🌀 kid. This went in so effortlessly, so easily, I wonder if it would pop out, if dropped, as easily as it popped in... I should be thankful it was THAT easy, no cuss-no fuss-no tears-no blood, but I'm so used to the NIGHTMARE of putting iPads in cases (any brand, any price point, any any any) that this legit has me nervous. title: UPDATED REVIEW!
text:
Update 2/9/23: My (cognitively) young son, who has that very expensive iPad mini I mentioned below in the original review, now pushes his iPad to the side at least 50% of the time and 'steals' my FirePad. There are apps and games on the FirePad that aren't on Apple's AppStore - granted, they're usually pretty basic, or else I imagine they'd be available across multiple OS platforms - but he's very young, cognitively, and he doesn't care. I am 100% certain that whenever this iPad he's got needs replacing (because Apple does that way more than is right, IMO) we will be going the 'FirePad' route.

Our family has had so many iPads, iPad Airs, iPad minis... and I can say that - when bought brand spanking new, at the time of release, we were in love. Honeymoons don't last forever, unfortunately, and neither do the tablets. NOT ONCE did we break them beyond being fixable; every single time they've 'updated out' and none of the apps worked. They're not even good for internet after awhile, because even Safari and Chrome have to be updated for use... and the updates will not work with the outdated IOS. Yknow, because $600+ for 2-4 years is acceptable. NOT. But dumb sheeple me, kept on buying them. 🤦🏼‍♀️

I bought my son a 6th Gen iPad mini last November. It was newish and on backorder til about early-mid December. I gave it to him as a gift IN A CHILDPROOF CASE. So it has been protected since I got it. Since before he got it. And two weeks ago it quit charging. Now, he uses his iPad for everything: Communication. Education. Entertainment. Besides the $600 I paid, and even with the $3.49/month AppleCare, it's just totally unacceptable. After taking it to two localish Apple Premium partners, neither of which wanted to fix it and both of which wanted to just sell me a new one, and because all our other iPads (4 that I haven't tossed yet) won't allow him to access his communication apps anymore, I cried and then ordered the Fire Mini on my 23% interest credit card because he needs accessS to something he can communicate on.

I'm, erm, a girl of a certain age. Getting more and more stubborn about learning new technology stuff. So getting used to this has been a mite frustrating for me. My son, 25 with the cognitivity and resilience of a 2 year old, hasn't skipped a beat. It's early days - and I did buy the 2 year Amazon Protection with the 'FirePad' as we call it - but for $200 plus tax, tag & title 😉 this little Fire Tablet is at least the quality equivalent of the $600 iPad Mini.

The only cons... the display IS just as good as the iPad, though the colors aren't quite as vibrant/vivid and the brightness isn't as bright. Is that worth $400 more... not for anyone I know. It just takes a little getting used to (I'm talking maybe 2 days with minimal usage by a stubborn adult) and then it's not an issue anymore. The biggest con, though, is that Google won't hop in bed with Amazon - apparently - as willingly as they do Apple. No Google app, no Chrome app, no YouTube app. I just use the Silk browser (Bing... YUCK!) type in Google for Google searches or YouTube to watch videos. Maybe 3 seconds of frustration but it does remember my YT log in after the first time, so there's that to help lessen the annoyance for when I use it. (My son watches YouTube on his TV anyway.)

CLIFF NOTES: 🔩🍎. 💸🔥
(Screw Apple. Buy Fire.)

title: BEST. THING. EVER.
text:
My 'kid' is 24 (cognitively he's about 2) and takes his iPad with him to bed. Doesn't use it, just that's where he puts it when he goes to sleep. Between his pillow and the wall. And every night the iPad was sliding off the bed (even though it is in a silicone case) and I was having to dig it out in the mornings for him. Not once have I had to do this.

I had contemplated a few Pinterest 'hacks' that suggested (for example) using Command Hooks attached to the wall and then sitting the iPad down into those (the big 5# ones) hooks. Problem for us is my kid has seizures that are not well controlled by meds, so all I could 'see' in my mind's eye was him seizing and in the convulsing or 'rooting' he does with most of his seizures (or unconsciously standing up then falling back down) one of those seemingly harmless plastic Command hooks gouging his eyeball out or ripping a nostril open. (If you knew all the off the wall sh** that can and does go wrong with seizures, you'd get why all the one-in-a-billions go through my head!)

Anyway, this was the best $ I've spent in a long time. It holds the iPad without any sliding or moving (the device or the pillow) and it came in his favorite color. He loved it. I love it.

title: It's pretty good -
text:
3.5 STARS. I rounded up because it is more good then bad:
Bought as a Christmas gift for the boyfriend. We are long distance and we FaceTime a lot. Well, actually, I FaceTime with the underside of his kitchen cabinets, the blanket on his bed, the ceilings in all his rooms, or the top of his nightstand. He talks away, oblivious until I say something. It's funny mostly but sometimes in a relationship you need all the connection you can get, even if it's their face on your device while they smile or laugh or talk you through a bad moment. So, I got him this for Christmas so that he could hands-free me and I could still see his pretty face. He finally put it together and started using it the other day... with an asterisk. *THE INCLUDED SCREW/BOLT IS GARBAGE. It was machined badly. Really badly. So it only screws maybe halfway into the arm/neck or whatever it is called, which sits in the weighted base. Thankfully he really doesn't need the screw/bolt because the arm/neck (like a metal dowel, I suppose, that inserts into the base maybe half an inch. The screw/bolt is inserted from under the base and - if it fits correctly) recesses into the base when it's tightened. As this one had threads that weren't smooth about halfway down on the screw/bolt, it left the screw/bolt jutted out. The base won't sit on the nightstand or other flat surface with this issue unless he just doesn't use the screw/bolt. I'd post a photo for clarification but the stand isn't available and getting him to send photos isn't always something I remember when we do talk.

The screw/bolt is I'm sure metric and it does use an Allen wrench (included) to screw in; the threading is very tight, so finding a true replacement screw/bolt is probably gonna require going to a specialty nuts/bolts/hardware store. That's annoying enough to take off 1.5 stars for me.

title: For my Dad...

title: This camera has given me a semblance of freedom!!
text: Mother/legal guardian/sole caregiver of an epileptic, mentally handicapped, Autistic adult son. After a hospitalization for a brain bleed, in which the hospital policy would not allow me to spend the night in his room and the night nurses were IMHO 25% the quality of the day shift nurses, he has become SUPER CLINGY. He naps every day and I’ve been afraid he’d wake up, alone, while I was in the yard and become more traumatized (I suspect he was waking at night and finding himself alone, as I was with him every minute from 6am to Midnight unless his Dad was with him or a nurse in the daytime.). I was super excited when I found this camera...last time I’d checked they were $150 each or more. The setup was super easy, the picture quality is INCREDIBLE. High-def 1080p. The sound is great. The app works phenomenally, just take a bit to learn the controls (mute, moving the camera, zooming, etc). I have been able to get out and get a brisk walk around my little acre, do some yard work, or just sit and enjoy the sounds of a lovely summer night. I am so thankful for this camera!!

title: Im ordering a replacement. Will stick with Momentum
text:
Ive had a momentum camera for 4years and have really liked everything about it. I am not tech savvy, but the picture quality-day and night is great, notifications, use on app easy, sd card, everything has been great. I have even reviewed footage to see where I set something down lol.
I have been looking for a few days to see if theres anything better or cheaper since I dropped my camera last week.
I am floored and appalled by what is out there.
Yes some cameras say they have clearer video. But no night vision. And some record only when motion detected, but only 6-12 seconds, what use is that? And many have a privacy policy that you absolutely have to agree to, or camera doesnt work. And those policies state that the company can access your personal information, files and data. As in social media, contacts, pictures, passwords, etc. and is authorized to use any of that and video clips to use how they want.
Some cameras dont turn off no matter what, and people found out they were being recorded without permission.
I don't like the idea of a surveillance camera in my home, but, I have been robbed too many times. So I would rather do passwords, get dressed etc in a different room.
And I have ordered another momentum camera. I did have trouble setting up the 1st camera, but I thought it was me. After reading a few reviews, I hope the 2nd one is as good as my other one has been for years.
I will do an update if anything changes.

title: Kindle Fire Broke Twice - Refused to Replace/Repair 2nd Time
text:
My mother is having the same issue. My family all pitched in and bought her a kindle for her birthday last year and I cannot express how angry I am at the customer service and quality of this product. My mother does not have much confidence when it comes to the latest technology and was hesitant about using a tablet in the first place. However, after my family kept telling her how great it was and how much she would love it, she finally agreed to give it a try. A few months after we purchased her first kindle, it broke and Amazon sent her another one, but that kindle also broke and Amazon is refusing to replace it.

Not only has Amazon ruined her experience/impression on using tablets, but the refusal to repair the charging component so many other customers have experienced problems with is unacceptable. I am a frequent shopper of Amazon, but after hearing that my mother's second kindle is not working and Amazon has refused to replace or repair it has made me reconsider my shopping preferences. My mother no longer wants to even use the kindle, she told me not to "worry about getting it fixed" because it's been such a hassle; which is disappointing considering how much my family lobbied for the product promising her that she would love how much it would improve her life.

title: Great Cable Modem - BUT...
text:
I have nothing but high praise for this Netgear CMD31T Cable Modem. The instructions were clear and no-nonsense; the physical installation took less than two minutes.

I would however, like to give NEGATIVE 5 stars to Comcast's ridiculous telephone service. I called the toll-free number that is provided on my bill and with the modem's paperwork. After wading through endless automated prompts, I was told that my waiting time would be 39-50 minutes. I sat and waited... After about 15 minutes, my call was disconnected. I went through the same ordeal again. After a total of close to an hour, I finally got to talk to someone - just to be told that they couldn't help me there; I needed to call a different number.

I called the new number. When I finally talked to someone there, she told me that she couldn't help me; I needed to call a different number. She read the "different" number to me - yes, the same number that I just called her on! I finally talked her into transferring me.

The person that I was transferred to didn't speak English very well. After repeating the Serial Number and the Mac ID many, many times to him, he finally got it. But it ends up that he couldn't actually help me either - he said that he would put me on hold to contact the correct person to do the switch over. When he put me on hold, he disconnected me...

I called again. 'Got someone else that barely spoke English. He said that my new modem was now in their system and that he would send a test signal. The signal did not make it to my modem for some reason. He asked me to unplug the modem from the power strip that it's on and plug it directly into the wall. I told him that I wasn't going to do that; it was obviously getting power. He then asked me to hold, so he could transfer me to tech support. When he put me on hold, I was disconnected again.

I decided that if the modem was showing up in their system now, maybe I could getting it working myself. I unplugged and replugged the power, and waited about 10 minutes. Then I unplugged and replugged my router's power. Success! It's working fine now.

title: It works, but not so well...
text:
I'm keeping this unit only because it fits the space that I wanted it in very well - I'm not at all happy with the performance of it.

I purchased this TV to mount on a very large desk that I have. The mounting is pretty straight-forward (they supply a cardboard drilling template and a few different spacer options). One thing to keep in mind on the mounting - make sure to allow for extra space for the speakers when drilling your mounting holes (the template does not have this space added).

Electronically, this is just a very average to below-average unit. I'm using cable as my video source. The TV that was in this location previously had an excellent picture. This unit has a snowy picture, and very poor color balance (I have tried adjusting it many times - it never does get a "good" picture).

The sound is awful. You have to create a balance between two different volume sources - one on the front of the main unit, the other on the TV itself (controlled by buttons on the TV, or by the remote). Between the two, if you turn it up to the point of what I would consider normal volume, you hear a faint but noticeable high-pitched whine (my Jack Russell Terrier hears it too...). The quality of the sound is pretty bad too - very thin and tinny. They should have added an Audio Out Jack, so that you could hook up a decent set of amplified speakers to it.

The Power button on the front of the unit is a cheap, spring-loaded design; I can tell that it will create problems in the long run (it has already stuck a few times).

The clock display is a bit annoying also - most digital displays will display the single-digit time without a zero in front nowadays - 3:00, for example. This clock displays it as 03:00.

The remote must use very unique frequencies - I was not able to program my regular Tivo remote to it (not even when cycling through the hundreds of preset codes that the Tivo remote has). I then purchased a "learning" Tivo remote - even that remote wouldn't accept the "power" or "volume down" functions ("volume up" was the only button that would accept the programming).

title: It's ok...
text:
I did not purchase this keyboard for gaming, I purchased it to use mostly as a higher-end computer keyboard. I'm using it in conjunction with [[ASIN:B003BIFI6E the Razer DeathAdder Left-handed Gaming Mouse]].

I like the feel of the keys on this keyboard - the rubbery surface is nice; the bumps on the F, J and 5 keys are easy to feel. The lighted keys look very cool in the dark, and have a good, solid feel when I press them.

What I don't like:

~ The lights in the keys are too dim. You can barely see them in a lit room. There should be a way to adjust the brightness of these lights.

~ The Num Lock, Cap Lock, etc. lights are too bright. There should be a way to adjust these also.

~ The Keyboard sits at too low an angle for my taste - the back feet of the keyboard should be raised higher.

~ The smooth finish of the area around the keys shows fingerprints horribly. This surface should be matte.

All in all, I like the keyboard (and will keep it), I just wish that a few things about it were designed differently...

title: 'Just one problem, but it's a VERY annoying one...
text:
I do like the angled keys - I thought that it might take a while to get used to them, but it did not. Even after getting used to these keys, I don't find it difficult to go back to the "regular" keyboard on my other computers. The keys are a little taller on this keyboard than I'm used to, but that's a quick adjustment also.

The one thing that I don't like is that the \ key is located on the right-side of the right "Shift" key. Every other keyboard that I've ever used has a Shift key that extends to where that key is located. When I'm using the other keys (the numeric pad, arrow keys, "Home", "End", etc.), quite often I'll reach for that Shift key, and hit the \ instead - 'very annoying...

If that one key wasn't there, this keyboard would get five stars from me. For those of you that will reply that this one problem doesn't warrant a one-star review, I disagree - it is VERY frustrating to have to stop working to delete the \, when they could have simply put that key where it is on most other keyboards...

text:

Fast forward to October 2014. The lens now has lost the ability to focus in either manual mode or AF. Until now, it had never shown any indication of any kind of problem.

Its warranty was for one year, so I'm now checking with Canon and other repair shops to get an estimate for fixing this problem.

I am very disappointed that a Canon lens had such a short useful life. The lens was used moderately, and stored properly. There's no discernible reason why it had a lens failure. title: Had to return it due to connectivity issues
text:
I got this internet radio and tried it for a few weeks. At first I was happy with it - the sound quality is quite good, it seemed pretty easy to set up, and I was able to find my favorite NPR station streams as well as connect to my Pandora stations. But after the first two weeks or so, I started having problems with connectivity.

- I'd come home from work and the thing would be on, not playing, with "error connecting to network" or some similar message flashing on the screen. The best way to solve this seemed to be to turn it off, then turn it back on, and then it would work (for a while).

- While listening, it frequently stops playing in the middle of a song. Then the display says either "Buffering" for a few minutes, or more frequently, will actually say "Connecting" for up to five minutes at a time! This happens, on average, every 4-6 minutes. The thing is, I have a wireless router upstairs on the same floor as the radio (Apple Time Capsule) and the wireless signal is quite strong. The other devices that connect to this router never have a problem with connectivity - devices that include a Roku box, a Chumby, my iPhone, my HP netbook, my Macbook, etc.

The problem with losing connectivity started infrequently but got worse and worse over the past two weeks or so, to the point where I can't really listen to music on it at all anymore. So I'm returning it. Too bad, because in terms of looks, sound, and basic functionality, it had everything I wanted.

title: An upgrade from my previous Nuvi!
text:
I previously owned a Garmin Nuvi 360 which I loved. I specifically need a GPS that includes Bluetooth, since I use it both for directions and for hands-free phone use (which is rare, but important when I need it). I loved my 360 and used it daily until just a few months ago, when the Bluetooth suddenly stopped working. After troubleshooting with Garmin's tech support, it was determined the unit would need to be sent in for service, and since it was out of warranty, the flat charge for service was $79, which didn't include insured shipping costs.

Well, do the math. Obviously, one can acquire a brand-new GPS for not much more than $79, so I started shopping. That's how I ended up with my new Garmin Nuvi 265T. And I LOVE IT! I'm almost glad that my old unit went on the fritz, because it gave me an excuse to upgrade to this newer, fantastic unit.

The 360 was great for accurate directions, easy to see and read display, and consistent Bluetooth (until it broke). Here's how the 265T is even better:

- Smaller, lighter, and thinner, but with a slightly wider screen.
- No "antenna" on the back to flip up and fiddle with - it just works.
- Uses my existing mount (from ProClips), so no change to that was necessary.
- Includes FREE traffic notifications, which so far seem to work pretty well.
- When you power it on, it seems to bypass the warning screen that you need to "Agree" to quicker, and then shows a simple display: Where To, and View Map. On the 360, if you didn't do anything else, it would sit on the menu indefinitely, but the 265T automatically switches to map display after a few minutes if you don't select anything else. Basically, you can start your car and just forget about it, until you need it!

The traffic feature is ad-supported, so occasionally very small banner-type ads appear on the display, usually offering coupons for local restaurants etc. They are quite small and not intrusive in any way, so I don't mind them. I guess there's also an option to upgrade to a paid traffic service that would not include ads, but I don't see a need for that for my own use.

In general I am thrilled with Garmin products, and this Nuvi 265T is no exception. What a great deal, and a nice early Christmas present for myself!

title: I May Not Know Much, But I Know I Love These!
text:
I'm not an audio expert by any means, but I know what I like and I have owned many, many pairs of headphones in the past. Noise-cancelling, non-noise-cancelling, earbuds, headphones, in-ear, out-of-ear, surround-ear, you name it. It seems like headphones and headsets are kind of an obsession of mine.

I use larger headhpones such as these Sennheisers primarily for playing video games on my computer after my toddler has gone to bed, and occasionally for listening to music (also on one of my computers). (When it comes to my iPod, I generally use something smaller and more portable, such as earbuds.)

When I took the HD201 headphones out of the box, I was first amazed at light they are. They seem to weigh almost nothing, though they don't feel flimsy by any means. I tried them on, and they were immediately very comfortable. They surrounded my ears comfortably, and the adjustable length on each side allowed for a perfect fit. I also noticed that the cord on these is nice and long, which is a plus. So far, so good. So I plugged them in for the real test.

WOW.

These sound GREAT! It's really kind of amazing to me that Amazon can offer these for under $20. I read the other reviews and paid attention when some reviewers said that they weren't loud enough, or sounded funny on "s" sounds. I did not find that to be the case for me. They sound just fine on all types of sounds and music, at various levels, and the volume is not a problem.

Pros: light-weight, comfortable, great sound, amazing price
Cons: too big for my taste to travel with, since they don't fold

I kind of wish they had an attached microphone, because then I'd never need another headset for gaming! However, for listening only, these are top-notch and I was very pleasantly surprised by the terrific quality at such a low price.

title: Cable too short!
text:
These are really, really high quality earbuds, especially for the price. The sound quality is actually pretty amazing. I had a middling-quality pair of those "Inked" earbuds attached to my laptop at work. The sound quality was always disappointing, but I had sort of assumed that it was probably due to the laptop sound card, etc. Then today I attached my new Sony Fontopias and wow...what a difference! Yes, they have bass boost, but not so much that it overwhelms the music.

These headphones are also surprisingly comfortable. They aren't the typical in-ear shape that gets jammed all the way into your ear, but there's a little more to them than the default "sort of hang in the outer part of your ear" that you get with the default iPod earbuds, for example. I like the hybrid, in-between quality and they fit me pretty well. They're not noise-cancelling, but the sound is so good that I really don't notice other office sounds (not even my disgusting cubicle neighbor who eats cookies like the Cookie Monster and sounds completely disgusting - now you know why I need to listen to music at work!). I'm so happy with the sound quality and comfort of these headphones, I'm willing to give then four stars in spite of one very major drawback:

THE CORD IS RIDICULOUSLY SHORT.

I have NEVER seen such a short cord on any pair of headphones, earbuds, headset, etc. that I have owned. I measured the cord from the jack to the point where the "Y" that goes to each individual bud starts, and it is barely 2 feet. TWO FEET! People, that is SHORT. So I'm going to go to Radio Shack at lunch today and buy an extension cord/adapter. So unless you're going to sit right next to the source you are connecting the headphones to, whether it's a computer or MP3 player or stereo, you'll need to add the cost of an extension cable to the price. Trust me - it's way too short as sold, like it wouldn't even stretch from my iPod in a backpack to my ears if I was walking around.

Otherwise, awesome headphones.

title: Portable, Quality Means for Listening to Music
text:
I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone.

What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use.

The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired.

There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged.

Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.

title: Connects With Ease
text:
I have several flat screen televisions in my household. With the improved technology, it’s usually simple enough to access the controls and bring most anything from the internet onto the big screen. But for those times when I need to connect a laptop or something else to the flat screen, an HDMI cable is needed and a very good choice for the task is this HDMI from Talk Works.

Six feet in length, this cable is designed for relatively short distance connections. Both ends of this HDMI are the same, so it doesn’t matter which end you use on which device. What matter is that you connect to the correct in/out plug, based on which one is the receiving end.

Once connected, this HDMI connects electronics with precision and clarity. It features a gold plated design that helps keep it from wearing out and apparently improves the connection, or so it seems. I don’t have any issues with it. If you want to improve the life even longer, be sure to save the plastic caps and place them back on the ends of the cord after use.

Connecting electronics is often necessary. This HDMI from Talk Works performs its intended task, with a snug connection that won’t come loose and a good deal of clarity from one device to another. It’s an excellent means to keep your electronics connected.

title: Secure Connection and Made to Last
text:
In the information age in which we live, electronics are part of our daily routine. Sometimes, it is necessary to connect electronics and a HDMI cable like this one from SIREG is ready to help.

Heavy duty in construction, this cable is designed to connect devices like laptops, monitors, projectors, etc. You simply plug in one end to the device you’re sending data from, and the other end to the device you want to send to. Be sure you are connecting the in and out the right way, and you should be set to go. The connection is secure and the cords don’t pop out easily, so you shouldn’t have any trouble in that regard.

The cord that comes with this is reasonably long- about 1.5 meters. This should be enough for most needs. You can’t connect at a great distance, however, so be sure to have your electronics devices close to each other. One other important thing to remember, before you make the purchase, is to check your devices to make sure they are compatible with the plugs on the ends of this cord. One end is HDMI, the other end is DP interface. Be sure your devices will match this, otherwise this cord will not work.

We often need to connect electronic devices. I often connect my laptop with my television and this HDMI cord from SIREG is a useful tool for the task. It securely connects and the images look sharp and clear. It’s a little more expensive than others, but the quality makes it worth it.

title: No Cords, no Noise
text:
A mouse is a must for most people. Unless you use a laptop or some other computer that already has a built- in mouse, you need a way to navigate and if you want to eliminate messy cords, a good option is this wireless mouse from BreSii store.

I’ve used other wireless mouses, but this one is better. It’s wireless by way of Bluetooth, which makes connection about as simple as it can be. You just plug it into the usb on the laptop or desktop pc and your ready to use. The mouse fits comfortably in your hands and is easy to use and control. There are no lights on this mouse or sounds made, but it does what you need it to do.

On the subject of sound, this brings me to what I consider this device’s greatest attribute: It’s quiet! You can’t hear the clicking sound, like you can with most others. This is great for those who get irritated listening to someone in another room, constantly clicking away on their mouse. With the silence of the clicks, there is no distraction. This is something I wish more manufacturers offered.

A computer mouse is a must- have item. If you want a better mouse that functions intuitively and keeps quiet while you work, then this wireless mouse from BreSii is the tool for you. It hooks up to most any computer or laptop and will navigate your way without cords or sounds.

title: No Batteries Needed and Cool Lights
text:
Navigating on a pc screen requires a mouse of some sort. They have come a long way over the years, with more features and more comfort. One that is great for those who like to add a little color to their navigation is this wireless mouse from PEIOUS.

Shaped for your hands, this mouse is comfortable to hold and click. It’s easy enough to use and you can’t feel any strain on your hands, so it earns good marks there. But the feature that is most appealing is the lights. You can change the lights to different modes and even shut them off completely, if you prefer. I like that the lights are soft- you notice them, but they are not so bright that they distract from what you are doing.

The bluetooth works okay on this mouse and one of the more unusual features is that you have to plug it in to charge. With most others I have used, you need to supply batteries, but this one charges by plugging it into a usb outlet. It’s nice not to have to buy batteries, but it also means you need to have a usb nearby for charging purposes. I consider this feature a plus, as I hate having to search for batteries when the need arises.

To conserve power with this mouse, there is a switch to shut it off. Plus, it will automatically shut off, to preserve power, if there is no movement for several minutes. This is good because, with regular use, you will need to recharge this more than you realize and saving power makes a difference.

Computers need a means for navigation and that requires a mouse of one type or another. You could go for the boring, ordinary mouse with buttons to click and nothing more, or you could have a little fun and get this wireless mouse from PEIOUS. I vote for the latter. It might only be a mouse, but the lights and the elimination of batteries make this a standout mouse and one I recommend.

title: It Works, but There are Some Issues

title: Quite Good for the Price
text:
My sound system on my work pc isn’t the best. Internal speakers are often not the best quality- you need an external speaker set if you want the enjoy better overall sound. This need convinced me to add Creative Pebble 2.0 USB-Powered Desktop Speakers to my office.

title: Improves Picture Quality
text:
With the current emphasis on streaming, there is less and less need to have a physical machine like a Blu-ray player in your home. But however small it may be, the need for this type of electronic hasn’t gone away and since I needed to upgrade mine, I went ahead and got this Sony Blu-ray Player.

Testing this unit with 4D Blu- ray disks shows that it lives up to its advanced claims. The picture and sound are both quite good and it can be used with regular DVD also. The colors are vivid- much more so than when played on ordinary electronic devices. If you would rather stream, you can do that as well. We are hooked on Netflix in my household, so it was nice to discover that this unit is ready for Netflix streaming.

This Sony Blu-ray player is compact in size and fits in most any space. It’s certainly a well- engineered electronic device and it’s great for anyone who wants to enhance the improve on their television screen. I can’t really find anything to criticize, so it earns an easy 5 stars from me.

title: Speeds up Connections
text:
Like most households, we have wifi. But depending on what we are trying to do, it is important to speed up the connection whenever possible. A good tool for the job is this ethernet cable from GLCON

Fifty feet in length, this cable has enough reach to accommodate most needs. I have a large house, but I can still reach my router with this lengthy cable. The main reason I got it is so that one of my kids can obtain a faster connection when she does streaming, gaming, and other things. This connects snugly on each end and it does make things move along faster.

I like that this cable is flat- it makes it easier to keep it out of your way. It also comes complete with 20 small fasteners. With these, you can clip it to the wall and run it, say, around the edges of a doorway, keeping it safely removed from the floor area where someone might trip over it.

Ethernet connections can speed up processes and this ethernet from GLCON is an excellent one overall. It performs as promised, is easy to use, and is designed to last.

title: High Quality Connections
text:
With a household overflowing with electronics, HDMI cords are essential. If you don’t need one now, you will need one eventually and a good choice is this UltraPro 8K HDMI Cable.

Three feet in length, this HDMI cord is durable, with metal connections that hold snugly in place and a thick cord that is made to last. The gold- plated metal connectors look cool, too. From a constructive standpoint, this cord seems like it is made to last an exceptionally long time, easily outliving the electronics it connects.

I got this HTML cord for gaming devices, but it can be used for much more. It is useful to connect laptops, high-definition televisions, and anything else that calls for this type of connection. The ends easily hold in place and the transfer of data is spot- on. It does exactly what I would expect an HDMI cable to do, and I don’t see needing to replace it for a long time.

HDMI cables are important to have around. We have several and use them for linking up many of our devices. This HDMI Cable from UltraPro is excellent overall and is all but certain to meet or exceed your needs.

title: Give Your Monitors the Raise They Deserve
text:
Modern- day monitors are a vast improvement over the bulky monitors of the past. Today, monitors are thin and flat, making them easy to fit into small spaces. However, monitors are often too low to the surface and require leaning down to look at them. A riser stand solves the problem and a good choice for the purpose is the Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Black Steel Laptop Stand.

Unpackaging these monitor stands reveals that a small amount of assembly is needed. But small is the word, as it takes no tools and almost no effort to screw the four legs into place. The black color makes this stand neutral and makes it match most any office space or décor.

What I like best about this stand is the adjustable legs. You can twist the knobs on the bottom of each leg to elevate the stands a little more. The stand can be adjusted from 2.5 to 3.25 inches in height and, if you’re like me, you will probably want to maximize the height, for the greatest level of viewing comfort.

Flat screen monitors are great, but they often need a little boost in height and Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Black Steel Laptop Stand gets the job done. They are strong enough to hold a small flat screen television, too. I purchased a pair and I like the results so far. It’s a sturdy stand that helps take the strain out of monitor viewing.

title: Sturdy and Love the Natural Wood Look
text:
More often than not, computer monitor screens are a little too low. They are too close to the table or desk on which they stand, and they require that you lean down to view. A simple elevation makes things much better and an excellent choice for the purpose is Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Bamboo Laptop Stand.

I got this pair of stands for my workplace monitors. I have two monitors and I selected this product first for the color. I like the natural wood and I knew it would help add some much-needed contrast to my workspace, which is comprised of black, white, and dark brown. If you like, you could apply stain and change the color to the shade of your choosing.

Taken from the box, all you need to do is screw the four legs into place and you’re ready to go. An added bonus with this stand is that the legs are adjustable- you can loosen and turn the knobs on the bottom and make the stand slightly taller. The brushed stainless steel legs look cool and the stands even have a wide slot on top, perfect for placing an iPad or something similar.

There is a small amount of space underneath these stands, so you can store other office items, thereby conserving desktop space. They are sturdy and can easily support my two large monitors. All things considered, Husky Mounts Monitor Riser Bamboo Laptop Stand is a winner in my book and I’m glad to have a pair of these stands in my workplace office.

title: Give Your Monitor a Lift
text:
Computer monitors are often to low and closer to a desktop surface than they should be. They often need a boost to bring them closer to eye level. There are lots of stands made for this purpose and the one I selected and generally like is this iPEGTOP Wood Monitor Stand Riser.

This riser comes unassembled in a box. You will need a screwdriver to put it together. There are only a few pieces and just six steps. It can be put together in a jiffy and once built and ready to go, all you need to do is place your monitor on top. Other office- related items can be placed on the shelf or the space underneath, which is open to your desktop.

I like the overall look and functionality of this riser. The black color goes well with my office décor and I like the added shelf because it is great for organizing and keeping my desk looking tidy. My one issue is that my keyboard doesn’t fit in the bottom space. It is just slightly too wide to fit. If your keyboard is more than 15.5 inches in width, you will have the same issue. I do have another, smaller keyboard that will fit so I may need to swap it out so that I can keep my keyboard stored, under the riser, when not in use.

Most of us spend a good deal of time at our computers so it makes sense to make the experience as comfortable as possible. My computer needed a lift and iPEGTOP Wood Monitor Stand Riser did the trick. It’s a sturdy stand and my desktop looks much neater and cleaner now. Other than the issue with my keyboard not fitting, I am happy with this product.

title: Lots of Variety and Lots of Fun
text:
