Okay it's supposed to be primarily used in a small enclosed indoor space but it also says it's great for camping, hiking and general outdoors stuff (please, don't blast music when you're hiking, wear headphones, show some respect and restraint). I've never seen a non-novelty speaker that was less than 5 watts. It feels light and cheap and thin. The suction cups; they send two likely expecting one to fail. Neither worked. The best I could get with the cup wet with soapy water, alone, no speaker, stuck to a mirror for maybe five minutes. I can't get these suction cups to stick to my desk. No worries, my shower has a shelf. I turned off my oontz Angle 3 and connected this to my phone using Samsung Music as a player to take advantage of the Dolby Atmos and excellent sound (only PowerAmp sounded better of the half dozen players I tested and PowerAmp is a paid app only) quality it offers. I guess if you wanted noise in the shower this would work. Sound quality was about as bad as you'd expect. Distorted bass, harsh highs, muddy midrange. No EQ settings I tried made this sound good. It's just not worth it. You can for just a little more money get far better sounding water resistant speakers. You should enjoy the music in your shower or bath not suffer with it.

title: Good Quality Memory Card
text: Always liked SanDisk products. Have used them for years and never had an issue. This worked great with my mom's new 8" Fire tablet once it was formatted by the device.  Got this on a Christmas sale so even happier with the bargain. Would recommend.

title: Secures Your Camera Nicely
text: I had no issues getting the backing material off. I used a pair of precision needle nose tweezers to peel the backing and to place the cover. Even with my shaky and arthritic hands I was able to get the cover 99% where I wanted it and just about perfectly level. I checked camera functionality and this cover doesn't seem to interfere in any way. Adhesion seems fine. I didn't touch the sticky material and I got it in place on the first try. If I'd needed to reposition or if I'd fumbled and gotten my fingers all over the adhesive I'd have discarded the cover and tried again. That's the good thing about having a multi-pack. Operation is okay. The cover slides open and closed with reasonable ease. It stays open or closed, wherever you put it. It doesn't interfere at all with the closing of my HP Pavilion gaming laptop. I'm going to put one on each of our tablets as well. I'm glad I finally got a cover. Have wanted one for peace of mind for a while now.

title: Nice Backdrop
text: Hung this up at a Halloween party as a decoration and everyone started using it as a photo background. I've used the reverse side to moderate success as a dark backdrop for photography. The size is great, covers a lot of area. Considered using it as a tablecloth as the product description suggested but just couldn't take the risk of stains or damage. Getting the wrinkles out was a bit of a pain. I don't have one and had to ask five friends before I found one with an iron I could borrow! Great for parties or just as a decoration.

title: More Fun Than  a Wooden Container of Densely Packed Primates
text: Have followed Nathan on Facebook and Instagram for a while. Facebook even says I'm a top fan (I whirl in joy!) and his art has brought a smile to my face almost every day. I didn't get the chance to pre order (sorry!) but I just had to support the artist who makes me smile. As Spider Robinson said, "Shared pain is lessened; shared joy, increased — thus do we refute entropy." Strange Planet is the epitome of that quote.

title: Useful But Flimsy
text: Years ago I had a similar stand in aluminum that was too small for the tablet I had at the time. These are pale copies of that device. They work and my mother is delighted to be able to stand her Kindle PaperWhite up in it. It works with the case on but even pulling the silicone tray liner out you have to leave the cover of the case off to the side. Not really that big of a deal. The aluminum stand I had locked in position. You pressed the button that was the end of the hinge set the stand how you like it and it locked in place. These stands have some mild detents inside the hinge mechanism that hold the place you set. . . more or less. It's okay with a Kindle and gently tapping the screen to change pages but I didn't like how my 10" tablet felt in landscape mode and I decided not to even try portrait. So, good for light use and light devices. Somewhat flimsy plastic. Not sure how long they'll last but we'll see.

title: Loving My New Phone
text:
I had a Galaxy S4 for several years. It was suitable and did the job. . . mostly. I was having some battery issues and my phone wouldn't update past Android 4.4. I was running into apps that needed a newer version of Android. I could have bought something cheap but I decided to treat myself and found the blue Galaxy S9 on sale for a decent price. I have to say I'm loving this phone.
The 5.8" Quad HD+ Super AMOLED screen is GLORIOUS! I run this is high performance mode with the brightness cranked up. Games, movies, even YouTube and TikTok videos look amazing. The curved edge I worried might be distracting but honestly I only notice in a couple games.
Sound is really good for a cell phone it has stereo speakers. Volume is more than enough.
Performance from the Octa-Core processor and 4GB of ram have not struggled to run anything I've thrown at it.
The camera is great. Maybe struggling a little in very bright light with a light colored subject. Otherwise, night mode gives great low light results. Video shooting is very nice with great slow motion results and a nearly unique super slow-motion recording mode at a mind boggling 960 frames per second is a lot of fun to mess around with.
Battery life is good, I got most of a day is high performance mode and could easily extend it by cutting things back to save battery.
The fingerprint sensor is quick to unlock and easy to use. A trick I found online to improve performance of the fingerprint sensor is to register the same finger more than once. It really works like a charm.
The look is sleek and sophisticated though I'm protecting that glass body with a nice Otterbox Symmetry case. The only real minor negative to the whole thing is this weighs more and is larger than my S4, a little hard on my hands and pocket but really, it's worth it.
I can't express how happy I am with this phone. I'm even buying props and things to use in creative videos and photo shoots.

title: Handy Case, Somewhat Fragile
text:
This is something I've needed that I never knew I needed and, until I was offered it to review, I didn't know such a thing existed. I spent a few hours coming through my house gathering up adapters, SD cards, micro SD cards all in old clamshell cases, sitting loose in a drawer or in devices I forgot I had and had forgotten I had cards in them!
Everything friction fits in this case, you just press things into place and they stay. In a couple spots I had to stop and compress the case itself because fitment was tight enough to flex a couple of my micro SD adapter cards.
There's plenty of space for full size cards, micro SD cards but not any spots for mini-SD adapters. Granted I only have one and I've never had a device that called for it but they exist and I hate not having all my cards and adapters in one place.
The case is quite sturdy except for the latches. Hard plastic in a stiff mount are a recipe for breakage. They should have been designed better.
So, while it really is useful there are enough flaws to drop the rating a couple stars. Use caution when first inserting cards to ensure things aren't too tight and be wary of the latches they unfortunately feel fragile. And hope I never need my mini-SD adapter, I have no idea where I left it!

title: Okay Cable
text: Decent quality cable, very stiff and material is rough against the skin (worse between the toes, ask me how I know). Connectors on either end are solid for now with little to no wiggle. I get high speed charging using my Samsung wall wart. Will update as time goes by if necessary.

title: Nice Fast Card For My Galaxy S9
text: Class 10, U3 nice and speedy for burst mode, slow motion and even Samsung's amazing 960 frames per second on my Galaxy S9. Have had no issues whatsoever. Affordable, good storage to double my phone's capacity.

title: Expected Better Quality Sound
text: The OontZ Angle 3 PLUS speaker has incredible battery life, pretty good bass, somewhat muddy mid range and okay highs (if you use the right app with a good equalizer). I found playing straight from the phone's built in apps wasn't so great but I downloaded another app with powerful settings and controls that bring out the best of this speaker. The OontZ Angle 3 PLUS has two speakers and 10 watts of power. There's a passive bass radiator. I never really thought those added much. All in all it's a decent speaker that kicks up my shower and shaving time. I got this on a Lightning Deal for a nice discount. I would not pay the full asking price.

title: Mediocre Quality
text:
I have two desks in my den. One has my 3D printer and other electronics. I have a similar (though more expensive) power tower on that desk. My other desk is for my laptop and random crafting. I had been using an old extension cord that lacked three prong plugs. When this tower became available I was happy to be able to replace the old extension cord and be able to charge my numerous USB devices. Then it arrived. . .
It's lightweight. Too light, cords drag it across the desk, you have to watch how you plug things in or it topples over. Overall the plastic feels like a toy not a serious device. A weighted base would seriously improve the unit.
There are no instructions. You have to figure out which set of outlets are controlled by which top switch. The switches feel cheap and engage/disengage roughly. There is no separate power button for the USB plugs (my other tower has one) and the red system power light is blindingly bright. I'm going to see if I have any black electrical tape to partially cover it. It's truly annoying.
The plugs don't want to hold two prong cords, grounded cords hold a little better (not much) but my devices that use just two prong cords barely stay plugged in! Tap it, move something that brushes the cord, the slightest pressure and the plug pops out.
It works and the ten foot cord is nice. I was able to plug this in half way across the room and get it onto my desk but. . . I don't like it. Thin cheap plastic. Klunky switches. Tips over too easily. It doesn't instill confidence in the product. I like the idea of a desktop power tower and have one I rely on. I don't recommend this one.

title: Just Junk, Avoid
text: There, of course, no way to adjust brightness on this and to see what you've written or drawn you nearly need a flood lamp to see what's on the board. Drawing is easy enough, erasure is okay but the whole concept is ruined by being nearly impossible to read. Very disappointing.

title: Good, But Far From Premium
text: I have a 'premium' battery charger. It can deep cycle your batteries, test, discharge and recharge to refresh your batteries. It can slow charge for extended life or fast charge if you need things quick. It has a multi line display that lets you see all sorts of information about the battery. This Duracell charger is a very basic but serviceable charger. I'm also not a fan of chargers that hang off the wall or need you to supply an extension cord. It works, it's better than most of the giveaway chargers that devices come with but it's not premium by any stretch of the imagination.

title: Inexpensive Cable is Inexpensive
text:
The price was right and you got two for the price of the higher end cable. I've had these for a month or so, the 1st one is in continuous use so the end plugged into my tablet is starting to develop wear and fray but no cable lasts forever in the setting I use them in so we'll see how long they last (about 9-10 months is the longest any cable has lasted) and see how much of a value they represent.I
Update: Just a quick update, just two months to the day that I ordered (not took delivery) these the first of the two pack has completely failed. It's used in my bedroom to keep my tablet charged and occasionally charge my Kindle. Far from rough use. The company did see my review and sent a replacement pack. That was nice. Then they emailed me numerous times asking me to change my review. That was not nice. I stand by my review. Even moreso now with the 1st cable in the trash.

title: A Good Budget Tablet
text: Had a Fire 8" tablet for a while. It had some issues after a lot of use a a few falls while I was in the hospital. Saw the 10" Fire was on sale and decided an upgrade was in order. So far so good. Size is nice except I can't 'palm' the tablet to pick it up. Haven't had much of an issue with the increased weight. Screen is sharp, colors vibrant. The extra RAM the 10" has over the 8" makes things a little bit snappier. More storage is nice. All around at under a hundred bucks you can't go wrong with this tablet.

title: What's Not to Like?
text: Fits the 10" Fire tablet just fine. Power on/off works 99% of the time. The texture of the cover gives a solid grip that doesn't slip. Expensive for what it is but I always seem to have bad luck with 3rd party cases.

title: One Size Fits. . . Or Not
text: The ear pieces are not replaceable there are no different size tips for these so they fit or they don't. If they do they sound pretty good. Fit, for me, wasn't uncomfortable though I have worn earbuds that were much more comfortable. There's some good bass and the high ends are reasonably sharp. The mid-range isn't muddy though it's a little. . . in the back. I've used these for hours at a time even fallen asleep while wearing them. They're okay walking around the house, no idea how well they hold while running or exercising.

title: Kinda Disappointing
text: I really wanted to like this video camera. I had planned on cobbling together a 3D printing channel on YouTube but some of the functionality of this is so disappointing. The zoom especially is the worst. It's stepped. There's no smooth zooming in and out, something every still camera I have with video capability can do. How ridiculous is that? You set up a shot and then go to zoom in on the piece you're printing and it zooms, then stops, then zooms, then stops, and does exactly the same zooming out. Video quality is mediocre. Menus are hard to navigate even with the touch screen. The 'night vision' capability is cute and works for a short distance but the quality is horrible. Still images are no better and possibly worse than the video. The wide angle/macro lens is seriously heavy. It does work but there's few elements and the glass is cheap. Macro shots are unimpressive. . , the same description covers just about everything. The external microphone doesn't sound much better than the onboard mic. This might be okay for a kid. Someone just starting out to see if they want to make videos. I'm not really sure who could or would want a camera that's mediocre on all fronts. Nothing stands out as impressive.

title: Middle of the Road Headphones
text: They're okay. Do you have a kid who's going through two pair of headphones a month? Do you want a pair you can take camping, hiking, skating, and where you knock around and might be rough on your stuff? Then these are good for you. They're not super sturdy. The plastic is thin and feels fragile. These are the very definition of Basics in AmazonBasics. They're a little small so if you have a big head they might be a bit uncomfortable. The padding on the ear cups is okay the stuff on the frame less so. Sound quality is. . . Basic, highs are flat, bass is muddy. These headphones aren't premium equipment and they don't pretend to be. They work and you won't cry if you break or lose them.

title: Nice Dash Camera
text:
I like the size. It's small enough that I was able to put it on the far side of the mirror and I really have to crane my neck to see the body. That being said I didn't pull the trim and conceal the cable so that runs down almost in the center of the car. But after a few weeks I completely stopped noticing it. The screen shuts down to be less of a distraction and the status indicator lights aren't bright enough to be annoying, even at night. Installation was fairly easy. Hardest part for me was getting the static disc that goes on the windshield and is what the mount glues to (this is done so you're not putting super strong glue directly on the glass) off its backing paper. I ended up needing an Xacto knife to get it free. Clean the glass then the clear plastic disk applies to the glass with static cling. The mount sticks to this and the camera easily attaches to the ball socket and can be swiveled into optimal position before being tightened down.
There are many settings you can use to configure your camera, I suggest going over them carefully and making the changes you want before mounting the camera. It's small and the buttons are fiddly. Some options include recording audio or not (I've got a foul mouth and tend to sing horribly off key so I turned my audio off), video resolution I set it to highest for best possible details, clip recording length; the camera will film for X number of minutes before saving a clip and starting the next (once the memory card is full the oldest video is deleted to make room for new video) I have mine set to 3 minute intervals. There's a G force sensitivity setting that once triggered (by impact or even extreme braking) it locks the current recording so it can't be deleted, recommended is medium to avoid over sensitivity. Night recording can be set to color or black and white. It does a good job with color in most situations. There's a ton of other options so make sure you explore and see what there is you may want to change. I'm quite happy with this unit and feel safer knowing it has my back. . . by watching out the front.

title: Very Useful Power Source
text: I've been using this on the desk where I have my CR-10s 3D printer. I use both sides, one for the printer alone and the other side hosts two lamps and a small wireless webcam for monitoring prints. I also use the USB ports to have two charging cables available whenever they're needed for my phone, speakers, etc. It's worked fine since the day I got it. I have it on the back of my desk with a couple large pieces of Fun-Tak holding it down so I can plug/unplug items without the unit moving around. I like that you can turn off half the plugs at will as well as the four USB ports can be active or off.

title: Works. . .
text:
I ran several speed tests on this card, the best speeds I got were:
Writing speed: 22.0 MByte/s
Reading speed: 78.6 MByte/s
It works in 16mp APS-C mirrorless camera including capturing 1080 video at 60fps. Right now it's in the HD dash cam in my Hyundai Accent recording 5 minute videos on a cycle. I've pulled the card and checked the videos, the 8-10 I looked at were fine, no stuttering, artifacts or other issues. so far, so good. I'm going o leave it in the dash cam for now and see how it's doing in a month or so. Card seems to be decent quality and at the time I'm writing this review reasonably affordable.

title: Fun Light, Good Speaker
text:
Okay, yeah, it's got a 128 LED lights and that's more and better than the ones that have only 60. . . or 96 lights. I already had one nearly, no exactly identical light/speaker to this with 96 lights. Now maybe there's a visible difference between 128 LEDs and 60, there pretty much has to be. But I have my 96 light speaker in the same shower nook as the new, 128 light speaker and Other than the large 1 I wrote on the bottom of the original speaker (96 lights) I can't tell them apart. That being long windedly said they're beautiful however many lights they have. As mentioned I have them both in the same wall nook in my shower and when I take a shower at night I use only the simulated fire from the two lights and it is awesome. The two speakers will sync into a stereo configuration very easily. Just sync once each and then turn them on. The speakers have decent sound as long as you remember they're small drivers running 5 watts each. More than enough for a shower, bedroom or out on a deck or patio for a small party.
About the only thing I don't like about these units are the white rim ring light and button lights for vilume, power, changing songs stay on the whole time and they're quite bright. I understand that you'll need to find the control buttons but the bright white lights detract slightly from the fire effect. They should either be orange/red to to match the fire effect LEDs or turn off after a short period of time. Besides that I really enjoy having these around. They hold a charge for weeks. Granted I only use them a few times a week for showers but I've never run them out of charge I end up thinking I should charge them because it's been a month or more since the last time they were charged.
Fun, entertaining light with a decent speaker, can be paired into stereo configuration. Good stuff.

title: Handy. . . But
text: These are handy, since you can reused them they're going to last for a long time. The only issue I've encountered is it's sometimes hard to pull the strap tight around cords and cabled, it tends to just slide around following your hand. It takes two hands to pull them very tight. but once you work around that they're great. Thin so they don't add bulk or weight. Durable as all get out they're not unbreakable but they're the next best thing. I had trouble cutting one with my knife they're that durable.

title: Works Good
text: I was leery of these devices as the first one I bought failed to work but on the recommendation of a friend online I gave this brand a try. My 3D printer has a little trouble holding onto the adapter. It can be pulled out without using the eject function. But carefully inserted and covered with a plate I downloaded and printed now everything is fine.

title: Didn't Work, Returned
text: I wanted this to use with my 3D printer. I tried this with my new printer and the printer couldn't see the card. I have three different adapter cards and I tried all three. I was using the micro SD card that came with both printers and made sure the machines could read the cards without the adapter. I have no idea what the problem was. I returned this for a refund and replaced it with another brand that worked first try.

title: Well Made
text: These are great for turning a single outlet into a multi-plug surge protected plug. The short plug reaches the floor and doesn't require bundling the cord or zip tying to shorten thing. My only dislike, and it's not a big deal is the plugs are arranged vertically meaning any device with an adapter is going to take two, possibly three outlets. Still, they're handy and give some sense of security against power surges.

title: So Far So Good 👍
text: Well, it has been running six plus hours a day 4 - 5 nights a week for a while now and although I know other buyers have had issues this TV has been great. Out of the box it was four screws to put on the two reasonably sturdy feet. Connectors for power and HDMI were easily accessible. Setup was confusing at first. This is supposed to primarily be a Roku/streaming TV although it can work just fine with you cable or satellite provider's set top box. Included instructions didn't have a bypass the online setup section but TCL support quickly walked me through getting the TV connected to the cable box. Image quality is stunning. I was honestly amazed at how bright, vibrant and saturated the picture is. Sound quality is good, nothing spectacular but it does go loud which was a necessity as my mother, the primary user, is going deaf and at full volume couldn't hear her previous TV. She hears this set perfectly and there's plenty of volume left if her hearing issues worsen. I would recommend this set to anyone looking for an affordable TV.

title: Perfect MicroSD Card for My 3D Printer
text: My 3D printer came with a lousy 256meg (yes, meg!) micro SD card. I wasn't able to keep a library of the useful items I print frequently let alone all the things I had sliced and planned on someday printing. With this 2gb card I have optimal compatibility and storage space for hundreds of models, far more than I actually want to keep on a card at once. I also have my slicing software and custom profiles for my printers saved in a separate directory. Handy! It doesn't come with an adapter but I have three or four laying around so it didn't matter. These small capacity, non SDHC U1/? cards are hard to find and often more expensive than much larger cards.

title: Durable, Quality Cable
text: I keep a tablet in the pocket on the bed rail on my bed, now only does it have a severe bend just below the micro connector it gets plugged/unplugged repeatedly every day as it gets moved around the house and back. I've had a horrible time getting cables to last. Some have died in a week most a month, maybe a little more. I received a PowerLine+ cable as a replacement with one of their cheaper cables failed on me. That cable lasted four months. That's more than twice the life of any other cable and not much more expensive than the other Anker cable I had. I broke that one myself, dropping the tablet on the connection and damaging the wire to the point it wouldn't charge. I bought this red one in the hopes I get a couple months out of it. If I do it's money well spent.

title: Didn't Work for My 3D Printer Project
text: I wanted to use this in lieu of binder clips on a glass bed mod for my 3D printer who's aluminum bed had warped. It just wasn't sticky enough to hold. . . let me change that to, it just wasn't sticky, at all. It might hold itself on my laptop's monitor below and near vertical but go past 90° and the pads would fall off in seconds under nothing but its own weight. They worked as spacers. I started with five 20x20 pads then cut those in half when they failed to adhere the glass bed to the printer. As spacers they worked well but the height of the glass and the spacers really stressed the binder clips and I worried about cracking the expensive borosilicate plate so I removed the silicone pads and stuck them in a drawer in case some friend might need them for something. I can't return them because I cut them up. At least they weren't expensive.

title: A Strong Entry Level Router
text:
This is a review of the Archer AC900:
It's a good router. In many ways it's a very good router. Might not be the choice for a large family with a lot of bandwidth consumption but it does do a good job for our small family usage. I've had multiple devices online at the same time the living room T.V. was streaming an HD movie. That and good coverage is all I really need. With our previous router the Echo Dot at literally the other end of the house had problems maintaining a streaming signal. Since installing the AC900 it's streamed music all night, every night for the two plus weeks it's been up and running. Signal strength was dramatically increased everywhere in the house. Speeds are a little better but not by too much. I had more of a consistency issue than a speed problem with the old router. The router sits low and doesn't seem to have great cooling so I have it sitting on a brace that I made so it's now couple inches off the shelf it's on. Better and more efficient cooling and less chance for dust build up.
I was happy to see that using a web browser you weren't required to install any software to get into the router's management although there is an Android app to manage the router. I've found the web browser access have be as easy if not easier to use though rarely I have to reload the main page a time or two but I think that's my choice of browser and not a problem with the device itself.
The router is great, for the novice, intermediate or even expert user. Unpack it follow the easy set up guide (pick a decent password) then connect your devices and you're done if you want to be or you can dig deeper and have fine control over the router's many features. It may not be the perfect choice for every installation but if you don't need a lot there's no reason to spend a lot.
In the end the AC900 delivers a lot of bang for the buck.

title: A Good Phone Cord
text: It's a phone extension cord, 50 feet was a little long but less expensive than the 35' cord available at the time I needed a new phone cord to wrap around my bedroom. There's a big somewhat tangled ball of excess cord behind a speaker but hey, I saved a couple bucks buying the longer cord and the sound quality of VOIP calls is just fine. Good product, good value.

title: Item DOA: Sold as New, Have Doubts
text: Description doesn't SAY the 2gb SD card is a return/refurbished BUT; Condition listed as: New. Card description says: "This product has been extensively tested, is certified to be 100% functional, and ready for use". This sounds like a refurbished item being passed off as new to me. Took a risk, card can't be written to, tried reformatting numerous times, nothing worked. Wasted my time. At least I'll get my money back.

title: Good Cover for New Oasis
text: This is my third case for 7" Kindle Oasis. I started with the absolutely horrible Amazon denim cover then I bought a faux leather MoKo cover which was by far better but still not right. Finally I found this CaseBot denim cover. I hope it's the last. The denim has a nice texture and makes the cover easy to hold and the burgundy is quite attractive. The inside of the cover and the lip that completely surrounds the device (there are cutouts for the power button and USB connection) is coated in a soft rubber like neoprene that gives excellent one handed reading control. This lip, which securely holds the device in place, is smooth and comfortable which was nice. I had had to sand the cutout openings on the MoKo case because they were rough. My only minor gripe with this cover is the fabric on the face which is lightly padded is a little loose and might get snagged on something and be torn. But I'm always careful with my items so I'm not too worried. All in all this is a rather nice cover. Recommended.

title: So Far So Good
text:
I've only had the cable for a couple of days but I've run several print jobs with no problems. The Amazon Basics cable is supposed to have gold plated ends I'll take their word on if. The cable itself is nice and sturdy much thicker than many othed USB cables I've received over the years. The connectors fit quite snugly. I even had to really work to get the printer end in. The standard USB end had a good but no where near as tight a fit but it stays in place.
The ten foot length is great! Previously I only had a 5-6' cable which gave me little choice where things would go but now I can run the cable out of the way and put my laptop in a comfortable position on the desk. Now I just have to see how the cable holds up over time. I'll update this review should I have to but for right now I'm quite pleased with the product and price.

title: A Not So Good Anker Product (Updated: 01/23/2018)(Updated: 02/08/2018)
text:
I have a six foot PowerLine cable that's just about a year old. That's twice as long as any other cable, braided, cloth, heavy duty, whatever, has lasted. Where I keep my tablet in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed puts a fairly sharp bend in cables. I've had them cracking and splitting at the plug as soon as a week and never more than two or three months. I'm replacing the six foot cable for two reasons. The six foot cable just isn't long enough, it's really close and the ten foot cable is going to be more than I need but I think it's better to have the extra length. The cable has developed a permanent bend at the small end but still shows no signs of cracking or splitting. The other reason is the connector has loosened up a little which I've noticed in both my tablet and Kindle but it still works so it's a good backup cable to have around. The new cable end are very tight fitting which I'm happy with, the old one was getting a little too easy to pop loose but it got a LOT of usage so I really can't complain seeing as how much longer the six foot cable lasted. If this ten footer lasts that long I'll be quite happy.

Update 01/23/2018 - I bought this 10' cable based on the longevity of the company's 6' cable of the same style. My 6' cable lasted nearly a year of numerous daily times plugging and unplugging my tablet. With no discernable change in usage or handling the 10' cable is now disconnecting from the tablet at the lightest touch after less than three months. Very disappointed.

Update: 02/08/2018 - I contacted Anker about warranty support for this cable. They were very quick to respond, friendly, concerned and quickly sent me a braided upgrade cable to make up for this cable failing. Communications were never delayed, response times were generally 12 - 24 hours apart. If you get a dud Anker will stand behind their product.

title: Another Great Kindle
text:
I've been a Kindle fan since I pre-ordered the K3. I have owned that, the PaperWhite (IMO for the money the best Kindle available), the Voyage and now, celebrating ten years of quitting smoking I scrimped and saved enough to buy the new 7", 8gb, Oasis.
The extra inch of screen greatly increases the reading pleasure the twelve LEDs create a perfectly even lighting environment even with the light set low to eleven or twelve. Contrary to some claims I've seen the screen is not square, it appears that way because of the different size bezels. I miss my page turn buttons from the K3 and now I have something similar, on a wider bezel my finger doesn't slip off of and hit the screen.
The edges are a little rough, I'll agree with that. In ways it feels like the device was rushed into production. That being said this is by far the most comfortable Kindle to read for long periods of time on. The fact that you can flip it over and switch hands with all the settings remaining intact was a great idea. I HIGHLY recommend reversing the page Forward/Back buttons so the lower button is the page forward and closer to where you'd grip the device to read.
I bought the 8gb version which leaves just over 6gb for the user, I have over 200 books on my Oasis and Windows still shows over 5.5gb free, I can't see needing any more storage than that, ever. My one real complaint, I'll mention here but deal with in another review is the cover (I chose the Blue cloth cover). If it's dark or late or I'm tired I find the magnetic only cover rather easy to come off with a little torque. I in the past put a finger between back and front cover of my PaperWhite and Voyage for easier one handed holding. That's not a good idea with this new configuration. I did hold the Oasis in it's cover over a pillow and had a friend ready just in case and the device DID stay securely in place during some fairly violent shaking it's just a twisting action that easily pops the magnetic connection loose. I'm hoping a 3rd party or Amazon for that matter does something to resolve the issue and hold the device securely in the cover like the PaperWhite and Voyage covers do.
I've only had it just short of two week but I'm very happy with the purchase and am truly enjoying reading on this new device.

title: My Favorite Kindle Yet!
text:
Some people have claimed the screen is square, it's not. Like all previous Kindles this is measured diagonally. It only appears square because the one side of the bezel with the buttons (also not loud as has been claimed and the touch screen works fine if the nearly inaudible click might keep a partner awake).
I really like the seven inch screen and design of this new Kindle it's much closer to a regular paperback page now. I do wish the boldness option was allowed to be applied to any book and not just those purchased from Amazon. I get plenty of books from other sites such as Baen and Project Gutenberg but they're not given the full functionality Amazon's books are. I don't think it's fair.
The weight and balance. In or out of the cover is almost perfect. I find I can comfortably read for hours and if either hand gets tired a quick flip and you're reading with the other. I've reversed the page turn buttons like on the old K3/Kindle keyboard the page forward button is more natural feeling if it's at the bottom I have no idea why Amazon has the default reversed. Holding it you're more apt to go forward than bsck plus if you need to go back you can just slide your finger towards the screen and use the touch screen to go back, then it's right back to the lower button to continue reading. I rather like this device. It's noy light years ahead of the Voyage or PaperWhite but it is certainly a few large steps ahead. I haven't and have no plans to test the waterproof claims. I like the idea because I'm disabled and on a walker my previous Kindles have gotten damp. Now i don't have to worry. I did pour a few drops of water on the cover. All but one rolled off. The one soaked in. Caveat emptor. Im happy with the purchase so far. It was a gift to myself for having quit smoking for 10 full years. I deserved it.

title: As Basic As It Gets
text:
AmazonBasics at its very basic. . .
Where to start? This does not have magnetic closure or magnetic auto on/off. There's an elastic strap you pull around that holds the cover closed. There's also four elastic straps inside with foam & faux leather pads that I found very hard to get in place that hold the Fire tablet in place. That's not a bad thing. It does provide a secure hold on the device. Unless these stretch out easily they appear to be a good system for a low cost cast to hold the device in place. The cover itself provides some protection against drops and strikes it would be good if you wanted to toss the tablet in a backpack or purse.
Complaints, I have a couple. They show this being used as a standing cover. The front folds back and fits into a slot built into the back. Good luck with that! Maybe if you broke it in for a few weeks but right out of the box all it does, no matter how I try, is tip over. The stand is useless. Next, which actually should have been first. No matter how you twist, push, pull or move the tablet one of the elastic straps meant to hold the device in place partially covers the charging port. I was able to use the plug to push the band out of the way and plug in the device. My 86 year old mother struggled for fifteen minutes and gave up passing the job to me. It'll work, that's about the best I can say for it. There's no frills, unless you count a stylus loop as a frill. It's as basic a basic cover can get. The blue which we received is much darker than the blue of the Fire tablet we own. It's not ugly but a better color match would been nice.
Personally I prefer the covers with the plastic bezel that the device snaps into place with and the magnetic closure that secures the cover and automatically turns it on and off.

title: Good Sounding, Poor Fitting (on me)
text:
I debated between three and four stars these do sound quite good; fairly good highs and the bass isn't bad with a large 50mm driver. My problem is the fit. the headband is somewhat narrow which makes the bottom of the ear cups (these are on not over the ear) feel looser at the bottom as if they're rocking from a point just above the top of your ear. You can adjust the length of both ear cups but not the width of the of the band. They're a bit narrow for my head. At first I thought these hadn't come with the cable mentioned on the box but eventually I did. These come with a somewhat short 4.2 foot braided nylon cable that's not supposed to tangle. There's a one button controller that sits on me at about the top of the shoulder, the controls supposedly only operate with the iOS operating system (Apple iPhones) and not with Android or Windows operating systems.
So in the end, they sound good but fit poorly on me. I do have a fairly large head so there's a majority of people whom these would fit just fine.

title: Attractive But Cheaply Made
text:
Cheaply made feels like it will easily break. I do like the grey and blue color. Cable is proprietary, would using a micro-USB plug to charge instead of an old style round plug-jack add that much to the cost? With a universal cable for power I could use my 10' cable and put the fan nearly anywhere without worrying about wasting batteries. I'd only use batteries during a power outage. I can still use one of my large battery packs but I honestly find it ridiculous not to use a standardized cable.
The fan had two speeds, I guess we didn't need the option of three. On low it moves a fair amount of air and is nearly silent. On high, with no batteries inside, it tends to creep across the desk. Use care or it will end up on the floor. It's somewhat noisier on high but surprisingly more quiet than similar portable desk fans. It moves quite a bit of air on high.
Pros: USB powerable. Quiet. Can be run off battery packs. Moves air well.
Cons: Cheap, thin plastic, proprietary cord. 'Walks' across desk on high.
I honestly don't have much faith in the hinge for adjusting air direction. The high/low/off switch. Or the very thin power cable lasting a year but we're heading into hurricane season so an extra battery powered fan isn't a bad thing to have around. I'll update the review should durability become an issue.

title: Perfect Replacement For Previous PaperWhite Version
text: We have two PaperWhites with the lower resolution screen. Viewing just text there honestly isn't a LOT of difference until you look closely at the edges. I replaced my PaperWhite with a Voyage (an almost regretful purchase) back in October and while there is a huge difference the added sharpness of an extra 88 PPI and the two extra LEDs make a difference. Since I tend to read in dim light the sharpness mattered more than the number of lights. when my mother's refurbished PaperWhite started acting up (reboots, updates, nothing helped) jumping forward or backward two, five, a dozen pages at a single click and often when turned on would be on the wrong page we decided to upgrade her to the latest PaperWhite. She's used to using the touch screen for changing pages and the lighting in the PaperWhite was more than adequate. In fact if I was asked to choose, right now, which Kindle to buy as a replacement I'd stare lovingly at the Oasis, look closely at its price, and honestly buy the PaperWhite. Two extra LED and the page turn 'buttons' just aren't worth the extra cost of the Voyage. They lured me in last year but after having had them since October I realize I could easily make due with the PaperWhite and the price difference would buy quite a few books. Now that this has the same 300 PPI screen, the adaptive lighting I turned off the first day and never turned back on. The PaperWhite has all the features you truly need and often goes on sale for a great price. In fact we were discussing replacing my mother's somewhat malfunctioning refurbished model she said to buy one when it went on sale and I swear the very next day Amazon had the Kindles all on sale (except the Oasis, grr). He unit had done three years of hard labor, that lady can READ so I didn't feel bad about replacing it. She's quite happy with it since it looks and functions exactly like her old one though slightly sharper. It even fit her customized case. Quite happy with the purchase.

title: Decent Laptop Computer
text:
Bought from HP's site so I could customize the configuration. (full HD screen, non-touch, backlit keyboard, etc.)
Had a rough start. Had to use a restore point, that failed. Did a system restore with the option to leave my files. That failed. Had to do a full system restore. I ended up reinstalling my software and files three times. But third time's the charm and things seem to be running good now. I really like the lighted keyboard and full 1920x1080 HD screen. The six gigs of RAM and Core i5 processor are much nicer than my previous Celeron system, The Dragonfly Blue color I optioned is absolutely stunning but does pick up fingerprints very easily.
So the computer's pretty good, granted it's no hard core gaming rig but Photoshop CS2 runs fine as does WordPerfect and all the programs I need. Now that it's working I'm pleased with the computer.

title: So Far, So Good (**Updated 08/11/2017**)
text:
I've bought expensive USB cable. I've bought cheap USB cables. I've had braided nylon USB cables that felt like they were taking your skin off you hand when they rubbed against you. Other than the braided cable every single cable I use to keep my bedroom tablet plugged in with has split, torn or ripped at the point just above the micro-USB plug end where the cable meets the plug (no, I don't, as I've been accused in the past, yank on the cord. I always use a firm grip on the plug.) Some last a month or two. My old white Kindle charging cable started flaking apart the same day I put it in use. I'd probably still be using the braided cable which hasn't failed but won't stay plugged in.
They advertise that this cable lasts 10x longer and has a 5,000 bend lifespan. I've only had it a short while. There just under seventeen months left on the warranty. I'd honestly be ecstatic if it lasts that long. I'm tired of worrying about shorts or what might happen to the tablet if it goes from plugged to unplugged over and over. So, here's to hoping that this cable lasts as advertised.

Update May 2nd 2017 - Well, here we are a little over three months since I purchased this cable and although it has developed a permanent bend just past where it plugs into the tablet it show no cracking, no lightening of the covering which would show stressing. This has literally at just three months has doubled the average lifespan of my USB cables. This device which is plugged in 24/7 (unless I need to charge my eReader) gets used numerous times a day, it just doesn't sit there. I'm extremely happy with the durability of this cable.

Update August 10th 2017 - I am amazed. No other cable has ever lasted as long as this Anker. I've had cables fail the same day, the same week and as I've mentioned it has developed a distinct bend from the way it hangs from my tablet, kept in the pocket of the grab bar on my bed, the cable shows almost imperceptible whitening just above the connector from strain but no cracks, splits or crumbling. It also stays firmly plugged into my Fire tablet and on occasion it's fine with my PaperWhite as well. Will certainly buy this brand again. Very impressive quality.

title: Comfortable, Works Well (Update 12-19-2017)
text:
Bought this for the rare phone call to thr county or government where I'd need to keep my elbow painfully bdnt while being on hold or transferred from person to person endlessly. I figured on these rare occasions a headset would be just the thing to ease my elbow pain (arthritis). A bit cheap but works okay. Sill have to see about longevity.

Update - 12-19-2017: The pair I bought this spring got stepped on and the plug was bent beyond repair. I ordered another set and they arrived promptly. In less than a year it feels like they changed the design for the worse and sadly raised the price. I wish I'd saved the old set to compare because these feel far more fragile and fit my head poorly. They still work for those rare times when I need to be on the phone for a long period of time and I want to spare my elbow the arthritis pain. I'm less impressed with this pair than the last but I guess they'll do for the little I need them I really didn't want to spend big bucks on a better set for the infrequent use they get. Hope these last.

title: Bought For Mom, She Loves It
text: Another rare five-star review. I have the full size Echo which I got when they were offered fot $99 to Prime members only. I have preached the virtues and benefits of an Echo since the day I received it. I was finally able to talk my mom into a Dot the other day. Normally she's got her television blasting to help her sleep and I worried about the Dot's smaller speaker not being loud enough. It's been a week and though there's been some learning curve she hasn't once had the TV on and she's sleeping better. Extremely glad I was able to talk her into a Dot. It's loud enough for her, she's only had to skip a few songs that were too soft. I'm glad she got it and she loves it.

title: Affordable Coverage for Your Dot
text:
Here we have another case of purchasing an extended warranty being asked to provide a review but never having made use of (and hoping never to have to) the purchased coverage. The price was right but lower on SquareTrade's site (I'm signed up for the specials and such mailings so I should have been made aware of. But it's only a few dollars so its no big loss).

The plan covers up to three replacements of the covered item or the term of the warranty you purchased (two years in this case). After trying to troubleshoot your device over the phone they will make the decision to either repair or replace your item. If they decided to replace the item it's wholly their choice to either provide a new or newest model of your device or provide a refurbished model of what you have. They promise quick turn-around and cover shipping in both directions. If you do not return the defective model within in a certain time frame (I believe it's 30 days) of receiving your replacement your credit card (which you MUST have on file to file a claim) will be charged the full cost of the device when new.

I've heard nothing but good things about SquareTrade for years and almost all of the low-star reviews seem to be user's not understanding the plan or not making sure they would be covered for their purchases rather than anything to do with SquareTrade itself. While I hope I never need to use the plan it was affordable enough to make up for Amazon's fairly deplorable ninety day warranty (our refurbished PaperWhite came with a full year's coverage. A brand new Dot, like their seven and eight inch tablets (unlike their six or ten inch tablets, the Echo or Tap and their entire eReader line which all have one-year warranties) only has ninety days I don't know why. I've always trusted Amazon's electronics, I wonder at their apparent lack of faith.

But anyway. I've rambled on enough. The two years of coverage is comforting and was quite affordable. I'm happy with the purchase and honestly hope I never need to use it.

title: Good But Not Great
text: Fits the 8" Amazon tablet well and securely. Leaves plenty of access to buttons and ports and even gives good access to the speakers. I had no real plans to use the different stand capabilities of the case and I'm not truly that impressed with them. Maybe it takes some breaking in. All I really wanted was to protect the screen where I store my tablet in a pocket on the grab bar of my bed and it does that job well. The automatic on/off function is a bit quirky. I've picked up the tablet with the cover closed only to see through the crack that it was already awake. 4 stars for fit and protection. 3 stars for the standing features not being that great and occasional it coming on before the cover is actually opened.

title: A Decent and Affordable Tablet
text: So far so good. A little different from a standard Android system like my older Samsung. Had to download a 3rd party file manager to see the music, books and other files I'd preloaded the 32 gig SD card with. The Amazon store does lack some apps, some I've paid good money for, so I'm debating installing the Google Play Store on this tablet (Amazon, you should offer us the option without all the bother it takes to install). But it is a lot faster than my old Samsung and the 8" size is perfect for use in my bedroom. A 7" Windows tablet that wasn't great was also a little too small. My 10" tablet was too big. This seems to be the perfect size and runs apps better and with less lag and choppiness. Right now I'm quite happy with the Amazon brand and the price at the time could not be beat. Text is sharp and clear. Video from both Amazon and the local cable company were crisp and vibrant at full screen. Games, music and books all open quickly. Quite happy with the purchase and the performance.

title: Hard to Review an Extended Warranty
text: How do you rate an emailed warranty? I had trouble with thr HTML since my email client logically only does plain text and leaves the web for the web. Other than that they have a record of my 2 year extended warranty and it's for the right device, the one I'm using right now. It was received on time and I've heard good things about the provider. Only time will tell. I'm not going to break my tablet just to see how well the warranty works.

title: Truly Couldn't Be Happier {Updated 04-04-2017}
text:
I knew, due to my disability, that I was going to need to find a professional installer to install this Boss Audio Systems B9351WRC head unit and wireless reverse camera along with two replacement door speakers I decided needed replacement (and wow, they really needed replacing). The installation took approximately three hours or so. The only problem which may not be a problem but I'm a worrier. The bracket for the wireless reverse camera somewhat, but not entirely, covers the plate expiration stickers somewhat. Other than that the head unit fit as good if not better than the stock radio fit. in the dashboard.
This radio plays AM/FM stations though there's very few decent radio stations around here. The unit also plays from USB thumb drives which plugs into a port under a panel under the volume/pause/power button. I put 600+ songs on a USB 2.0 16 GB driver and it played everything as far as I could tell. There might be a couple VBR or odd format MP3 files it may not play but I haven't gotten to them yes. Nothing's refused to play and even a couple that had imbedded album artwork actually showed up but so small it was almost impossible to see and I had no idea how to make it better. The instructions in the manual were basically "Play with things and see what happens!" more than specific directions how different functions work.
What I went with, is a 32 gig micro-SD card that had the same 600+ songs the thumb drive has. But with the micro-SD card you can close the hatch under the volume and control knob which you couldn't with the thumb drive. There's also an AUX input jack for old style MP3 players and phones.
The six inch screen is sharp and crisp. The backup camera, even with a streetlight thirty feet away had more than enough light to back out of my garage. I even backed down the street a ways in almost complete darkness and could see just fine with just the reverse lights on the car. Now as long as no cops have a problem with it I'm golden.
I tried home burned CDs and while it took a few seconds longer to recognize it played them fine. I tried store bought CDs and they played right off the bat. OH! and it plays DVD discs jut fine in case my passenger wants to watch a movie as we drive. I promise I'm no dumb enough to watch a movie while I drive.
According to the installer I can leave the micro SD card in the unit all the time. So, 600+ songs anytime I want which I can shuffle or randomly pick and play songs anytime I want. I couldn't be happier. With the stock deck I'd sometimes get to my destination just as the deck decided to recognize the CD so this deck is a godsend when I really needed a new one. Now with as many songs as I can cram into a 32 gig drive. Right now I've got 687 songs and tons of free space. I may have to start buying more music and ripping some more albums from my collection to add to my micro-SD card.
So I can play hundreds, thousands of MP3 songs on a micro-SD card. I can play CDs both homemade and store bought. I can watch DVDs on a pretty sharp (all settings can be changed in the system) the dimmer is a bit bright until it goes off completely but it's not too bad or too bright. There's a user setting EQ option as well as several other preset settings to choose from. There are options to add sound effects such as large hall, church, cavern, etc. I avoided them entirely and set my own EQ settings with the loudness off. The new speakers sound great for high end and midrange. The stock back speakers add some needed bass.
All in all? This is an affordable head unit with all the features and functions one could ask for. It comes with a remote that I'm not sure I'm even going to keep anywhere in the car. Anything you need to do can be done on the deck and no one's sitting in the back seat of a '07 Hyundai Accent, seriously. So the remote is useless but amusing.
I love this unit, the backup cam is awesome, The many ways to play music. The fit and finish, it's close to perfect.
This a little long and meandering review but I really like this radio and I'm glad I replaced the door speakers and went with a professional installer who's basically given me a lifetime warranty on his labor. I couldn't be happier.

Update 04-04-2017: It's been nearly six months since I had this head unit and backup camera installed. Radio reception is still bad, I still despise listening to radio so that's no big deal. Have kept a micro SD card loaded with hundreds of songs installed. Turn the unit on it automatically defaults to that. Everything is still working fine. Professional installation was worth the money.

title: So Far So Good. Decent Tablet For the Money.
text:
This tablet was purchased to replace my 85 year old mother's Big Lots special that she used for years and which was starting to have more problems than it was worth. The biggest problem my mother had was adjusting to the wide-screen 16:9 format of the Fire tablet compared to the old fashioned 4:3 format of her old tablet. This also had a faster processor with two more cores and four more megs of ram augmented by an 8gb memory card to expand storage. The blue color is quite attractive. The tablet so far runs everything she wants and I've even taught her to use the appstore to download her favorite games. The colors are sharp and clear. Video is smooth and while we watched only one half hour show so far there was no pausing or buffering.
I think the only thing I honestly dislike and it's my fault for not seeing it when this was a Prime Day special. I can forgive the tablet going out of stock and not being alerted to that fact when we placed the order. What I find somewhat insulting is this is the ONLY Fire tabled that comes with a limited 90 day warranty while every other Fire tablet has a minimum of one year warranty. I think there's something wrong with that. I probably would have bought this anyhow. My mom can't stand the weight of my 10" tablet (an ounce heavier than the 10" Fire) and the 8" was (and still is) available in one configuration (color, memory, special offers, etc.) which wasn't attractive and appeared to be fairly heavy.
So far so good. The tablet is functioning properly with a couple glitches here and there but every touch screen tablet and computer has similar issues. Other than what should have been a year warranty like every other Fire, Kindle, TV stick/device and Echo/tap has. That's just wrong and unfair to people buying a specific size of tablet.

title: Quite a Nice Micro-SDHC Card
text: I was quite pleased with the performance of this card. Using the included adapter copying large multi-meg files of course went much quicker than copying thousands of small files on my computer. But the job got done and it didn't feel slow but I can easily blame the built in USB card reader on my laptop. I also tried this card with my Fujifilm X-E2. It easily shot at 7FPS and emptied the 18 photo buffer amazingly fast. At 3FPS the camera would shoot until the card was full. Just for testing I held the camera and ran off over 250 images without a pause, slow-down or hitch. I also shot video at 60FPS in full 1920x1080 HD and it was flawlessly beautiful even shooting in the low light as sunset approached. I'll let other tech-centric users post data rate test result images. I go by what feels good and this card? It really feels good and works fine with my camera and computer. I couldn't be happier.

title: Speedy, Lightweight SSD External Drive
text:
I like tech. I've had a computer since the commodore Vic-20 came out. That being said I'm not into competing with or against other computers and computer users. I don't run testing or speed diagnostics on my hardware. If it works and feels or seems to be working as advertised and expected I'm completely happy. I just don't care to sit here are see how many micro-seconds faster my new drive is than my older ones.
All that being said I use external drives exclusively for maintaining backups of my personal files, photos, documents, music, eBooks, Etc. Everything else I can simply reinstall in a couple hours. I don't have that many things installed. My computing needs are simple. But I have lost files due to a drive crash so I meticulously make weekly backups of my important files. Currently I've been using two USB 3.0 Seagate Backup Plus drives to make my backups every Monday.
This new Samsung solid state drive is remarkably faster at copying files to than my mechanical drives and easily a quarter the size and weight of the Seagate drives. I had a couple hiccups when I first formatted the drive to NTFS (I had no need of proprietary encryption) and started copying my files over to the drive but after one or two false starts I got tens of thousands of files copied over with no more problems and have for several weeks just copied new files to the existing collections in their directories and once again this SSD drive flies through the process much faster than the Seagate drives. Now I have three complete backups of my files and feel that much safer and secure with three copies of my files and I love that there's no moving parts. The cable's long enough, about eighteen inches, to work fine with my laptop though someone with a desktop may want to invest in a longer cable.
I'm knocking one star off for a device this expensive not coming with even a cheap hard shell case or even a rubber plug to protect the USB port from dust. It's the one point of possible entry of foreign matter into the drive and causing damage or failure. For the price they're currently charging it wouldn't have been any real hardship to include a case or plug to protect this device.

title: Exactly The Length Cable I Needed
text: I have a small folding table that I use for my laptop. There's just enough room on the table to put my Kindle, external battery packs and other chargeable devices next to the computer. This one foot cable is just the right length to connect something to the computer and not have extra cable hanging all over the place. I also use this with several other varying length cables and a multiple port charger on another table where I can plug in several devices at once. The cable feels sturdy and well made though I don't see any real speed differences between this and any of my other USB cables but it works well for my needs and the length is great.

title: Incredibly Tall & Useful USB Light
text:
I love this light, absolutely love it. I purchased a laptop without backlit keys thinking I wouldn't be using it all that often but a disability has led me to require the touch-pad on the laptop as using a mouse on my desktop had become a near impossibility. I had come across another flexible USB lighting system that was less than half the height of this light and also lacked the on/off function as well as the dimmer capability which I find extremely useful.
When plugged into my rear most USB port this light reaches just above the top of the screen on my 15.6" laptop and with the light dimmed somewhat it doesn't glare even where it's just an inch or so from the screen itself but sheds enough light that I can see the entire keyboard easily.
The neck is strong enough to hold its position while standing there as well as once it's unplugged and put on the table when the laptop is not in use. It does wiggle a bit at the USB port but I think all USB ports seem to have a little wiggle room built into them.
Control couldn't be easier though controls would have, to me, been more convenient. You quickly press/tap the end of the USB light bar very, very lightly to turn or off the light. Dimming the light requires holding the end as the light dims or releasing it and holding it again as the light brightens. Personally I think separate switches would be more convenient but the single switch works well enough.
I love this light. It's absolutely perfect for my needs and puts so much more light on the keyboard than the smaller light I previously used (shown in one of the photos I'll attach) plus the fact that I can turn it on and off as well as dim or brighten the light just adds to the usefulness of the light. This also works great with a USB power pack.
I received this light in exchange for my review.

title: Add Three Usable USB 3.0 Ports to Almost Any Computer
text:
This is a decent multi-port 3.0 adapter. My laptop, like many other older models had just one USB 3.0 port and I have several USB 3.0 devices. At first I had a little problem getting the computer to recognize the devices were plugged in but a little wiggling of the cable that came with the adapter and things started working just fine. When plugged in both of the the ends and the port slots glow a rather attractive royal blue. I was able to connect both of my USB 3.0 portable hard drives and there didn't seem to be any speed problems or differences than when I had a single drive connected to the USB 3 port on the laptop.
I have one quandary about this device and one slight problem. On the back of the unit next to USB plug is what appears to be a power connector of some type. The only reference I could find was in the product description where it says "configurable with power switch; and USB LED indicator(Without power included)" so I'm guessing maybe you can use this with a power connector as a stand alone USB 3 port. As to my slight problem this unit could be a little heavier. With two drives plugged in as well as the unit plugged into the computer the unit tends to easily slid around on the desktop. A little more weight would help keep the device more stable and in one position. Other than that though this is a cool looking adapter that takes up little desk space but adds three more usable USB 3.0 ports to your computer. This is a very handy and attractive device.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Two Laptop Cooling Pad Reviews *Updated*
text:
I have been considering a laptop cooling station for quite a while now. I had really hoped to review the smaller N5 mode which appears much lower than the N3 I was asked to review.
The first thing I noticed is the unit expects your laptop to have a USB port on the left hand side. Okay, the cable IS long enough to reach one of the two USB ports on the left side of my laptop but just barely. The on/off button and the extra USB port that's part of the base which is powered by the laptop's port that powers the cooling pad are rather out of the way and hard to reach. The port is also USB-2 only so if your machine is like mine make sure you leave the USB-3 open for things that require USB-3 connectivity.
The single fan is very quiet, I wouldn't call it 100% silent but it doesn't make that much noise. When it runs it gives an attractive blue glow. . . which you really don't get to see because the laptop's on top of the cooling pad. There are two removable clips on the base end which can be used if you want to use any of the five higher positions to stand the laptop at and they'll hold your laptop safely in place.
I was a bit disappointed in the height of this unit. My laptop is ¾ of an inch from front to back to front sitting on the table. With the addition of this N3 laptop cooling pad the height increases to two inches at the wrist rest and two and three quarters of an inch at the monitor end. That makes using the laptop somewhat uncomfortable. In the instructions it mentions that if you want to use this stand you should consider using an external keyboard and mouse. . . Sorry, but if I wanted to use an external keyboard and mouse I'd have bought a desktop computer. I have a desktop computer I was just hoping for a small lift to the laptop and a bit of extra cooling.
This unit left me disappointed. It's too high, too hard to reach the additional USB port and on/off button. The adjustability is quite impressive you can raise the screen quite high, eye level or even higher, but I just don't want to buy and use an external keyboard and mouse. To me, that defeats the purpose of having a laptop in the first place. Being disabled I bought a laptop because I have such a hard time using a mouse and the touchpad on the laptop was a blessing. Some users may find this useful or handy but I honestly did not enjoy using this at all.
I received this in exchange for my review.

*Update*
I also received the N5 cooler to review (all items listed on the same product page share the same review pool) the N5 does not light up like the larger N3 reviewed above. The N5 has its power switch and USB ports far more conveniently located on the center of the back of the Unit. The N5 does not have the ability to adjust the height or angle of your laptop. It raises the front one and a half to one and a quarter inches in height in the front depending on how you position the laptop. In the back the laptop is raised between two and two and a quarter inches. My fifteen inch Asus laptop overhangs each side by about a half inch but that doesn't seem to affect cooling. Although the N5 lacks the light up fans and height adjustability I think it's a superior cooling unit that could even comfortably fit in your lap. The N5 is a solid four-star item while the N3 remains subpar.
I received this unit in exchange for my review as well.

title: Decent quality Samsung Cable
text: Well, this is my third extra length charging/synch cable for my Samsung Galaxy Tab2 10.1 tablet. I've had two other six foot cable each last about a year before they stopped working entirely. Luckily I still have the short stock cable that came with the tablet and it's helped keep the tablet charged while I find a new long cable to use with the tablet. The price was right and this cable has decent enough reviews (4.2 out of 5 stars) that I decided to take a chance on it. Here's to hoping I get more than a year's use out of this before it gives up the ghost.

title: Ten Feet of Quality HDMI Cable
text:
This review is of the ten (10) foot IBRA® HDMI Cable. The cable annoyingly came packaged in a very hard to open clamshell package. This cable, unlike two others I received from the company used twist-ties to keep the cable coiled in shipment. Much easier to remove these than zip-ties used on other cables. Build quality is quite nice and the ten foot cord lets you put your devices where you want. The cable is a bit pricy but the quality seems worth it.
I received this cable in exchange for my review.

title: Well Made Cable
text:
This review is for the six (6) foot blue HDMI cable. This cable is actually woven of plastic not cloth. Caps are provided to keep dust and debris from the cable connectors. The cable I received came in a plain grey Mylar bag with an identifying label. One thing I honestly cannot understand was the use of zip-ties to keep the cable coiled in transit. Twist-ties would make much better sense. Now I have to get in close to the cable with a knife or scissors and risk damaging the cable itself removing the ties. I had no functionality issues with the cable but also saw no remarkable improvement compared to the cable we had been using. The build quality is quite nice and at the time of this review the price, under six dollars, is quite nice.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Pack It Along in Style
text:
I love this bag. The canvas, I chose the brown color, is very heavy duty and has a retro look and feel. There is a large zipper compartment with a soft nylon lining which is quite big enough for any 15" laptop. My Asus X533M fit with room to spare. Zipping the bag closed with my laptop which is no lightweight by any means was not a problem. I ,carefully of course, held and shook the bag by the carry handle, the shoulder straps and the even side pockets with my laptop onboard and all the seams held nicely.
Other pockets for accessories, gear, cables, etc. on the pack a small zipper pocket inside the main laptop compartment as well as another half compartment pocket in the laptop area. Under the large flap that covers the back of the pack and is held down by two magnetic snaps are two generous snap closured pockets. On the sides are two pockets suitable for water bottles or other beverages. These pockets are resizable with a strap and two snaps which are set a few inches apart.
The brown canvas is so very attractive with darker brown strapping and brown contrast edging on the shoulder straps. There are also dark leather pulls on the laptop compartment and a decorative leather patch with the slogan "Taste Emoton On One's Way" Really, I checked twice, I don't get it but it's enigmatic enough to be clever. I'm guessing they mean 'Emotion.'
One small note about the shoulder straps. The pack continues its retro styling on the pack using an old style double chrome ring strapping system to adjust the shoulder strap length. Make sure these are taunt when you use the shoulder straps. This isn't anything against the pack. I was actually pleased to see them stay with the retro styling all around.
I received this item in exchange for my review.

title: Terrific Little USB Lights
text:
This is a review of the 2 Pack Mini Book Light LED Task Desk Lamp. I received these lights in exchange for this review.

These things are great! They're impressively bright and easy to adjust. My chair's in a darker corner of the living room and my laptop doesn't have backlit keys. I plug one of these into a USB port on the laptop and after a little adjusting to keep the glare off the screen and out of my eyes there's plenty of light to type and see even the small print on the function keys.

On top of being a good task light on the laptop you can plug these into a portable battery charging pack and instant flashlight! I have a charging pack with dual USB ports plugging both in creates a blinding amount of light. At only 1.2w draw per lamp a good battery pack would last quite a while.

Another use these would be handy for is if the dome/interior lighting in your car was inoperable. You could plug one or both of these lamps into a car's USB charging port for quick and you've got quick and easy interior lighting.

Two features I would love to see added to these lights are a dimmer control the lights are very bright and sometimes you don't need the full output of the lamp. An on/off switch would be a useful if not entirely necessary feature. I wouldn't mind the option to leave the lamp plugged into the laptop when I didn't need light.

One thing of note is on the opposite side from the lights there is a metal heat sink that does get quite warm. I tested the sink for a bit over an hour and while it didn't cause any burns it was warm enough that I wanted to stop touching it so give it a few minutes to cool down before handling or throwing it in your bag or pocket.

title: Can't Trust This. . .
text:
When I saw this I thought it would be a great addition to my camera gear. The description says it's good for DSLRs and up to six pounds. After opening and inspecting this monopod system I reluctantly tried my ultra-compact Sony WX9 camera on this mounting system. My conclusion is I can't and won't trust this rig with my WX9 let alone my much heavier mirrorless Fuji gear.

The padded extendable main monopod shaft consists of three sections that are secured with a twist. It's easy to not torque the sections hard enough for them to unexpectedly collapse while you're trying to take a picture.

The ball-head mounts, this system comes with two, are fairly smooth metal on metal construction. Alarmingly these have no secure locking system. You simply use your thumb to engage a friction locking system. All it takes is a tap to cause the ball-head to be completely free moving. I would never trust a camera I liked on these mounts.

There are two feet that come with this set. A rubber edged magnetic mount and a suction cup -
The magnet is too small for a secure mount. With the monopod vertical and not extended it was reasonably stable. Horizontally it felt unsafe set up in any configuration. Extending the monopod drastically increases the ease with which this tips over. The magnet is just not wide enough to be stable.
The suction cup mount was surprisingly strong but like every other securing point in this rig the slide to release the mount does not lock in place. It's just too easy to hit the release while trying to set things up. I had thought I could mount this low on the car to get some interesting video but after trying this out I'd be worried road vibration would cause this to release and drop the camera.

In conclusion: While the materials are of decent quality this system lacks security. I won't risk my cameras on it.

title: Brown Now Red on the Town {ReEdited 06/17/16}
text:
First and foremost let's get to the issue of PU leather, check Google or Wikipedia, it's not leather. It looks like leather. It feels somewhat like leather and it's supposed to be easier to clean than real leather. To me there's not really a lot of difference. The brown cover is handsome and reminds me quite a lot of old leather bound novels. The color is just awesome. The fit is as good, maybe better, than my Amazon PaperWhite specific cover. I usually put my name, phone and email contacts under my Kindles. I couldn't get this OFF of my Kindle! I have bruises on several finger tips from trying. I may have to use a screw driver to carefully pry this off or I may need to cut this off if I decide to go back to my custom air-brushed Amazon cover. I'm going to leave it on for now. I've had black Kindle covers for years. This does everything the Amazon case does. There's decent protection for the Kindle. It has a magnetic clasp that automatically turns the Kindle on and off. It certainly holds the Kindle well enough. The cover folds back all the way for easy one handed reading. I'd have given it five stars but for one thing, the company thought it was a good idea to emboss their company name on the front cover. I just don't care for that. It's small so no one's going to see it. The only person who will see the embossed name is me and I've already got the product. I don't need to be constantly reminded who made it.

{Edit - 06/13/16}
Just slightly more than a year since I obtained this case. I've left it on all this time because I really do like the brown color and the lack of the metal plate the Amazon case comes with. Fit's been perfect only had a couple issues where opening didn't turn the Paperwhite on but even the Amazon brand has that issue from time to time. My biggest problem is all the brown on the edges and corners either is or has already fallen off. The bulge where the magnet sits is beginning to split open.
