I've used it with my [[ASIN:B002FQJT3Q Kindle 3G Wireless Reading Device, Free 3G + Wi-Fi, 6" Display, Graphite, 3G Works Globally - Latest Generation]] without any problems. Data speeds were fine and I encountered no errors or problems. The plug ends fit snugly and securely with very little noticeable wiggle room. Well worth purchasing. I would recommend this product to anyone in need of a micro USB cable.

title: More Than Just a Television
text:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV is also a multimedia device supporting multiple image, video and audio formats. Audio through the unit's single speaker is a bit tinny and slightly underpowered. At full or nearly full volume it's not all that loud. The unit does have a headphone jack and the addition of a set of decent buds or headphones will improve audio quality quite a bit although there are no bass or treble controls. It comes with a clear plastic screen protector and be warned, if you remove it getting it to lay perfectly flat again is nearly impossible.

Along with the headphone connector the TV also has a single Micro-SD memory card slot. I purchased a 2-GIG card to test this device with. I do not know, and the manual does not say, if the TV supports the newer, larger SDHC style cards. The device has NO user accessible internal memory.

All input and control are accomplished via two buttons on the face and a four way directional button set. The buttons are stiff and I found, with my thick fingers, that manipulating the directional arrow buttons was a bit hard to do with accuracy.

My unit, which is white as opposed to the stated black, arrived with a USB cable (which I have not used) an AC adapter/charger, an external antenna and a peg/tab stand on a lanyard. I found attaching the lanyard to the unit (you'll likely lose the stand otherwise) to be a complete pain and required a bent pin to accomplish.

Television Reception:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV has a built in rod antenna which feels very fragile and easy to bend. The antenna also has a swivel base so care must be exercised when pushing it back into the unit. The included external antenna has a nicely long cord so it can be positioned easily for optimal reception. For the sake of reference I live approximately 80 miles South East of Orlando Florida on the coast. Using the built-in antenna, indoors, upon initial setup the channel scan was unable to find any stations. Plugging the external antenna in resulted in around a dozen channels being found during the setup scan. The 320x240 LCD screen images are crisp and sharp. Colors are vibrant and clear and I was pleasantly surprised at the adjustability of the picture including brightness, contrast, tint and color mode. Moving the television while watching TV should be avoided as the picture will often freeze and breakup. I was quite happy to find that one of the stations I do get is a 24/7 local area weather channel. During Florida's frequent power outages due to severe weather and hurricanes this will be invaluable.

Video Playback:
I loaded over a GIG of video files onto my Micro-SD card to test the Tivax's ability to playback video files. I chose a mixed batch of AVI, MPG, WMV and MOV file formats. WMV files are not supported at all (oddly the unit DOES support WMA audio files, go figure) and the support for the other formats was hit or miss. Approximately 60% of the fifty or so video clips I've tried to play were supported, but the rest just returned an error. Those that did play did so quite well. Picture quality was good (dependant, of course, on the quality of the videos) as was the audio playback. Perhaps they'll release a firmware update for the unit to add further CODEC support.

Audio Playback:
As I previously mentioned, the system's speaker is quite tinny. Don't expect great quality sound from it. It's not horrible but it could be better. I tested several dozen MP3 files on my Tivax including low (80 kbps) and very high (320 kbps) bit rate files as well as variable-bit rate encoded files and it played all of them without a problem.

Image Playback/Slide show:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV supports JPEG, PNG, GIF and BMP image formats. Images display crisp and clean with bright and true colors. Landscape oriented images display best and while you can rotate images that are portrait oriented there is a distinct quality loss during rotation. Images can be zoomed in on with multiple levels of zoom.
The slide show feature is nicely configurable. The delay between images can be set or turned off for manual page turning. The transition effect done while changing images also has many options. The Tivax will also play any MP3 files in the same location as the images as background music during the slide show. I actually couldn't find a way NOT to have this happen if the audio and video files were mixed together on the memory card although the volume can be set to zero this will surely use more battery power even with the volume down.
One feature which I liked, but was not mentioned in the manual, is the ability to set one of your own images as the startup `logo'.

Power:
The Tivax 3.5-Inch Digital TV comes with a built in Lithium Ion battery which they state can be recharged approximately 500 times.
I found that their claimed charge durations were quite accurate. Watching Digital TV with the volume set to around 75% I was twice able to watch for a bit more than three hours before the unit turned off. I loaded several hundred large image files onto the memory card and set the unit to running them as a slide show (silent) and was able to achieve just over six hours of playback before the battery died. MP3 playback resulted in similar results of around five and a half hours of continuous play.
When charging there are NO indicator lights showing that the unit is charging nor any way, short of turning it on, to tell if it has fully charged. There is also no on screen low battery warning. When my battery was depleted the unit simply shut itself off.

Finally:
This is a nice unit and far more than just a digital TV set. A padded case would be a nice option. I'm going to try some of the smartphone cases to see if any fit. I really don't want to scratch or damage the screen. The external antenna while mildly magnetic really needs to be weighted and/or have a clip attached to it as it is rather light and hard to keep in place.

title: Lowepro SlingShot 202 AW
text:
The fit and finish of this bag are top notch. I've been camping and backpacking for decades and I have to say the quality of this bag and the workmanship are among the best I've seen. The nylon material is heavy duty and durable. The bag and shoulder strap are well padded for comfort and protection of your gear. The pack includes a built in micro-fiber cloth and two memory card slots in the main compartment. There's even a tuck-away all-weather cover in the bottom of the bag for inclement weather situations. The dividers in the main compartment are infinitely adjustable and all can be removed/repositioned. The pack includes a pull-out tripod holder/foot pocket and strapping system on the side of the bag. There's also a separate compartment at the top of the pack for personal items large enough for wallet, keys, an emergency poncho, etc. Also included are two smaller pockets on the back of the pack suitable for lens pens, notepad, pens, what have you.

This bag is huge. Easily as big as most hiking day-packs. There's room for everything and the kitchen sink. Currently I have my old Canon AE-1 with 80-200 mm lens attached. My 55 mm auxiliary lens. A half dozen assorted filters. Cable release. 1:1 reverse adapter AND my Kodak Z-650 point and shoot all in the main compartment.

Ease of use is incredible. The shoulder strap and waist belt are widely adjustable for people of almost all sizes. The zippers work flawlessly and fast never catching or hanging. The velcro throughout the pack is quite heavy duty and looks like it will hold up to years of abuse. All you need do is slide the pack from your back to the front of your body and the camera access section is right there. You never have to take the bag off to get at your rig.

Those are the pros.

Here are just a couple cons:
The micro-fiber cloth is not removable. I'm not sure what you could do if it became soiled or stained and needed cleaning. The strap for the tripod is not fixed to the pack and could easily be lost. The all-weather cover fits very tight to the bag (in and of itself this is a good thing, but...) it won't fit over any but the smallest mono-pod or tripod. My [[ASIN:B00005T3TI Ambico 54 Inch Tripod with Quick Release (V-0555)]] just barely fits on the pack.

I have no doubt this bag would last years for anyone from amateur to most demanding professional.

title: good mouse that doesn't quite fit my hand - yet
text:
howdy y'all,

i bought this mouse to replace my logitech mx1100 cordless mouse. that one finally had the left mouse button start doing the dreaded false double click. it lasted several years, so i was not seriously annoyed. [*grin*]

for those coming from an mx1100, here are differences i noticed ...
- the mx1100 had the hump in the center instead of towards the back, so the main mouse buttons were shorter
this makes the mouse seem really rather too long. i am unsure if that will bother me once i use the new one for a while.

- the mx1100 had less of a slant to the right so that my hand sat a bit closer to level
the new one is more comfy for my very right-handed self.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel projected a tad more
combined with the sharp slant, the new mouse wheel feels like it is tilted the wrong way. it isn't, but i keep finding my finger on the right edge of the wheel instead of directly on the wheel.

- the mx1100 mouse wheel had a more pronounced side-move feel
the new mouse is very subtle. i liked the distinct feel of the older one when it toggled the side-move "button" function of the mouse wheel. of course, i like clicky keyboards, too ... [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had the upper thumb buttons just below the upper left edge
the new mouse has them on a surface that slants very sharply down to the left from the left edge. it makes the reach to the forward/back buttons a tad less comfy. combine that with a taper on those two buttons and i have found myself looking to see where the darned buttons went. they are also a tad more to the front of the mouse.
these admittedly annoying things that will likely fade out of my attention with use.

- the mx1100 used two AA rechargeable batteries
the new mouse uses one. since i use a lot of battery powered devices, i have a battery charger and several spares on hand. that means i will likely not use the usb charging function very often. still, one AA is better than having to charge two! [*grin*]

- the mx1100 had a larger usb wireless adapter
the new one is quite tiny! it works well - i put it on the back of my system among the tangle of wires that connect to other things and have had no reception problems.

*****
the parts list says there otta be a driver cd included. _not_ so! [*sigh ...*] you are referred to their download site if you want to use any of the extended functions or buttons. the performance mx has a $100 recommended price and there is no excuse to cheap out like that. thankfully, win7x32 has basic mouse support for the standard buttons, the mouse wheel, and the back/forward buttons.

this is a /_serious_/ fubar and i almost subtracted a star from my rating because of it.
*****

i suspect that folks with short hands will have problems with this mouse, but i am getting used to it already. i'm 6'1" and my hand is 7.5" from base to middle finger tip. not a _large_ hand, but not short.

*****
rated a THREE since it does what i expected - no more and no less. still, i came very close to rating this a two for not including the cd.

take care,
lee

title: Great value
text: I hesitated ordering these because of the price. Yet, I knew Celestron with decades of experience with their telescopes. I was not disappointed. These binoculars are excellent.

text: Works great on my Panasonic FZ80 camera.

text: Works great for my Lumix FZ80.

title: Amazing
text: Incredible is the only word I can use to describe the results I get when using this filter with my Panasonic FZ80 camera. It's as if a whole new universe opened up in front of my camera's lens. Wow!!!

text: Just enough room for my camera and the few extra accessories I want to carry. Not that big, either, since I hate carrying extra bulk. Only problem I had was that when I first opened it, the case reeked of an odor resembling stale beer. I had to hang it in the sun for a week to get rid of the scent. Other than that, the case is perfect for what I needed it for.

title: Works great
text: Charges perfectly both the included battery and the Panasonic battery that came with my FZ80. This unit's battery works perfectly with my camera. I haven't noticed any difference in performance. A good deal.

title: Exceptional product
text: I tried a Fire10 and a Lenovo Tab 4. They were frustrating in their speed and limitations. The Huawei, however, is incredible. Great speed, sound and the display is awesome. Yes, it costs more but the performance makes up for it. It truly is a frustration free tablet!!!

title: It works BUT...
text: ... it's cheaply made. Buttons don't quite match the middles and the volume control takes some getting used to. It can be frustrating.

title: Great product!
text: Really nice C cable. Use 1 as a recharge cable for my phone and tablet and the other one for my PC.

text: Works great for my Polaris 130. I keep my counterweight separate, though. Great deal.

title: Nice eyepiece
text: I wear glasses and this works well in my Meade Polaris 130. Worth the price. Well made. Granted, my eyes aren't what they were 40 years ago, but the whole field is crisp and clear.

title: So far so good
text:
Used 10 of these discs so far. Perfect.

Can't figure out why Amazon shipped these in a bubble bag. Spindle/case were shattered and the bag was filled with discs and plastic debris. No matter. These discs are working perfectly.

title: Excellent
text: These eyepieces and filters are excellent. Great job Meade!!!

title: Can't beat it for the cost
text: Wonderful product. Star fields are crisp and clear. I use it with my Meade Polaris 130. I also wear glasses and have no problems.

title: Great Li'l Gizmo
text:
Perfect for what I do with it, mainly rip my Blu-ray discs to MKV format and put them on a flash drive/cell phone. It's smaller than I thought and I keep wondering how Pioneer got all that greatness in that tiny drive. Great, super, exemplary product!!!

Bundled software isn't too bad, either. Everything works well with Windows 10. I'm very happy.

title: How?
text:
I'm an old fart and have had telescopes for a main portion of my life. I love the sky and stars. Astronomy has always been my major hobby. I just wanted something decent to look at the Moon, major planets and, since I live in a one bedroom apartment surrounded by severe light pollution, at least something to resolve the brighter binary stars without spending too much. I'd had Meade telescopes before and because of the name, I went with the Polaris 130.

Wow!!! Way WAY better than I expected. Excellent manufacturing and machining. The optics are superb. When I took it out on my first night, I figured it would take a while to collimate the glass. Surprise!!! Everything was dead on. Impressive since the telescope was made in China, shipped across the Pacific to California, then to me in Massachusetts.

The only drawback for telescopes such as this is the fact that they are bundled with cheap eyepieces. Uuugghhh! I knew that when I ordered this telescope and bought a decent set of Meade Plossles to go with it.

What I can't figure out is the price. Excellent materials, excellent manufacturing and machining, exemplary optics. Then all the shipping involved. How can you do it for the price?

title: Square Trade always came through
text: Haven't needed these folks for my TV, but they always delivered on the few times I've had to use them before.

title: Cheap
text: It lasted less than a day in my toolbox.

title: So far so good
text: Fit perfectly.

title: Junk
text: It looks good, but the buttons are abysmal and "mushy". Most often, you have to press multiple times to get a function to work. It takes about 10 presses just to get the TV on or off. Yes, my TCL Roku model is on the approved list and I tried 2 sets of fresh batteries. It's going back.

title: This is a bargain!!!
text:
Xfinity sent me a new "upgraded" cable modem and it was a nightmare. After mucho hours with tech support and diagnostics, I was told my speed/performance problems must be due to my Roku TV, my PC, my tablet and my cell phone and that I should contact their respective manufacturers. Funny that I didn't have any problems with the old, obsolete modem Xfinity replaced.
Well, maybe the frustration was a good thing. After researching, I decided to get my own modem and chose the Motorola. I'm glad I did.
After I unpacked it and set it up, I braced myself for what I thought would be installation purgatory. Nope. I turned on the modem and watched it go through it's power up sequence. Then I turned on my PC and went to the browser. There was Xfinity's activation screen. Here you must be patient. You'll go through a few screens where the PC seems to hang/freeze and gives you prompts to retry. The modem restarts a few times during activation. When the modem lights are normal, just hit retry and all will be well. The whole installation takes about 5 minutes. No human interaction required!!!
Don't forget to reset the modem's ID, password and network info.
Performance is great. I can have my Roku TV (I stream everything), other TV with a Roku stick, PC, tablet, cell phone and magicJack all working at the same time. Amazing. Plus, this modem will pay for itself in 10 months versus the $11 modem rental fee I would otherwise be paying ad infinitum.

title: One sexy, high quality case
text:
Beautiful case. Well manufactured, excellent stitching and made of high quality materials. The Tab 4 fits in it, pardon the cliche, like a bug in a rug.
Even if it's closed up just sitting on my desk, it seems to "ooze" an aura of class. This is one mighty fine product.

title: Doesn't work
text: I finally had to remove it. On the top horizontal half of the screen, I couldn't get 3 big bubbles to heal and the 2 top corners just wouldn't adhere properly. Yes, the screen was cleaned prior to installation and was immaculate. I've installed many protectors on other tablets and cell phones without any problem. This is my first lemon.

title: Look elsewhere
text: Not a great case. Poor spine that warps. Sending it back.

title: a ***HUGE*** disappointment
text:
I just set up a return for this item. It's a poor, slow, and inflexible product. The Amazon Store apps are limited and to get any really useful applications, you will have to go through 4 separate steps to load the required software so that you can get Google Play Store to work. Even then, after you install the apps you want from there, a lot of them won't work. I installed the required apps from Google to get into my bank accounts. The two most important to me just hang when I start them.
I ordered this because I'm getting old and my eyes aren't quite what they used to be. My cell phone runs every app I use perfectly but the screen size would become wearisome at times. I wanted a larger screen (and yes, Prime videos are great on this device) but the Fire seems fit to be more of an entertainment toy than a serious application and productivity tool.
Don't get me wrong. I love Amazon. Great service, no hassle returns, Prime, etc. I buy just about everything from them. My mailman must be sick by now of hauling my Amazon stuff (like 40 lb. boxes of cat litter). I really wish I even just "liked" this device and thus keep it. Alas, it's not to be.
I've handled and worked with similar devices that are around a $100 that do more. I'll get one of them (and bet I get it from Amazon).

title: Terrible, poorly designed phone
text:
I wound up returning this phone. I HATED it. In no way did it justify it's cost. The Huawei Mate SE is much, much better. Granted, the screen quality isn't quite as good, nor is the camera. However, the software is better thought out and implemented and, as such, much more user oriented and modifiable. I used the S9+ for about a week and went back to the Mate SE. I was much, much happier until (lo and behold) I received an S9+ as a gift. Now I use the S9+ just so I won't hurt someone's feelings. Karma better remember this.
BTW, who was the idiot that placed the fingerprint sensor right underneath the camera lenses? You always wind up smudging them when you scan your print.
The S9+ is one poorly designed phone.
UPDATE : The hell with karma. I went back to the Huawei Mate SE. I can be nice for only so long.

title: Look no further

title: Excellent
text:
I hated it at first. The user manual is abysmal. The bass was WAY to overpowering. Once I reset the unit by pressing the switch underneath, figured out the controls and then let the radio play for a few days, I fell in love with it.
Three things : 1) Get a better battery for the remote. I got an Energizer and now the remote is flawless. 2) The overpowered bass settled down after I let it play for a few days. Now the sound is incredible. 3) Reset the unit via the bottom switch after plugging it in before doing anything else.
Be patient and you'll fall in love, too!

title: How did I live without it?
text:
Tomorrow that ugly, bulky cable TV box goes back. I love the Roku! Within an hour of setting it up, I was in love. I even ordered an indoor HD antenna to make sure I could see my favorite local news channel in the morning and found that I get it on the Roku! Tons of free stuff. I love the multitude of free old movie, science fiction, horror and classic TV channels. Stuff I love to watch. I also have Netflix and Prime and was able to set them up without a problem. I was streaming them through my DVD player but the Roku is faster. Now I'm thinking of sending the antenna back to Amazon. Who needs cable TV?

Setting up the Roku account did require a credit or debit card, but there is no activation fee. The card is kept on file so that if you select a channel that requires one. Roku tells you this if you look at a channel's description before deciding if you want to add it. Plus, you need a PIN to activate that channel before your card gets charged.

Best $30 I ever spent!

title: You won't go wrong with these
text: I love these earbuds. Incredible sound.

title: Ok but not great
text: It's an "ok" but not great player. Sound isn't the best but not the worst either, irregardless the equalizer setting. Seems cheaply made. Buttons are "squishy". Directions aren't the best so getting around the menu presents learning that is trial and error. Once you figure it all out it's pretty easy.

title: Didn't work. Loses channels.
text: Doesn't work, even after moving the antenna to different places.

title: Get the TIVDIO V-111 instead
text:
Sad Sony product. The only thing good about it is the sound. Poor antenna design. Poor tuning, reception, drift and the tuning gauge isn't accurate.
For the same price, you can get the TIVDIO V-111 (it was the VITE VT-111) here on Amazon. It's digital display is accurate, size is about the same, auto-scan, nice antenna, clock, uses 2 AAs, reception is exceptional and doesn't just get AM & FM but LW and shortwave, too. Solidly built. Only drawback is the Sony's sound is a bit better.
For the $, get the TIVDIO V-111. Much better radio with more bells and whistles.

UPDATE : Added a star because of the sound. Once you work around the quirks it's not a bad little radio. Reception isn't the greatest, but for local stations it's adequate. Wish Sony would would look at the V-111 and upgrade to digital display, etc. I'd pay extra for it.

title: Love it!
text: Nice little case.

title: Better than nothing
text: Hard to work controls like tuning, volume etc. in the dark. Wish I had gotten something more elaborate. Sound is good, though.

title: Nice little unit!

text: Memory card that works well.

title: Works excellent

title: Nice little SW radio!
text:
When I was a kid 50 years ago, I asked for a SW radio for Christmas. We got our presents on Christmas Eve and when I took it up to my bedroom, I opened a storm window just enough to hang the extension wire out. I was able to listen to stations all over the world. Russia, England, Japan, India, etc. Didn't matter that I couldn't understand anything but English. These were voices from around the globe! I felt the world was in my hands. AM and FM, too. Big dial. Yes, the radio was big and bulky and forget any batteries. Power cord was it.

I bought this VITE just to see if SW would interest me still. I've only had it for a few hours, and it sure does. It's like my big, bulky radio was somehow shrunken down and forced into this tiny unit and with even more bells and whistles. Seems to be built very well and solid. Powered by 2 AAs. If you had a handheld transistor radio in the 60s, it's even smaller! Speaker is nothing to brag about, but so what? It's $20 bucks. Nice little SW. I might eventually look at something more powerful.

title: Definately worth the cost
text: Forget the Wi-fi. After plugging this cable into my PC and then my cable modem, online became an incredibly new experience.

title: Excellent protectors
text: Really nice power strips. Went through an all night thunderstorm with plenty of lightning. Not a flicker on my TV or DVD player, even when lights blinked on and off. Should I need to, will buy more.

title: You won't regret getting these!
text: Incredible sound. After my first Panasonic earphones went dead in the right earpiece, I tried several others and most wound up in the landfill. Sony, JVC, etc. One of biggest problems I had was even if a set of plugs sounded okay, I would get a splitting headache and I don't play my music loud. I should have stuck with what I knew. Got these and it was like the world opened up again. From bass to highs, Bach to Skynyrd, all encompassing and beautiful. Also, no headaches!

title: Terrible
text: Bought this after reading reviews. For benefit of the doubt, maybe mine are defective. Terrible sound, no matter which rubber eartips I used and I sealed them tight. Even when I adjusted the equalizer on my MP3 to what I thought was "acceptable", these gave me a headache after 5 minutes. Bought these to replace my Panasonic set which died after about a year but sounded great. I should've gotten another Panasonic set.

title: Impressed!
text: Surprised. Nice little speaker. Bass is nothing to brag about, but mids and highs are clear. Nicely packaged and it's great having the extension cable. I can put it and my MP3 player on mid volume and (I live in a small apartment) hear it my bedroom, bath and kitchen from my living room. Seems like the company cared and was fussy about it's product.

title: Excellent quality
text: High quality. Connectors fit like gloves.

title: Update
text:
Incredible. I've heard sounds I never heard before. Skynyd's "Free Bird" is now a totally new song for me.

UPDATE : They only lasted about three months.

title: You have to break these in. Takes a while but once you do, WOW!!!
text:
Have some patience with these. I needed a new pair of plugs since my five year old Altec Lansings started falling apart. I tried many others as replacements, but none were as good as the Lansings, most notably on the bass side. I read the reviews about these and figured what the heck.
When I first got them and fitted them to my ears, they were terrible. Why would Panasonic make this junk? 2 stars at best. Bass was horrible. But as time went by, I started to notice that not only the bass but the high end frequencies were getting better. Now I am more than satisfied!!! These even beat my old Lansings.
In short, have some patience. These need a break in period. You won't be sorry.

title: Nice little case for my Coolpix S3500
text: Nice little case with a loop to mount on your belt. There's even a little pocket on the inside back where you can store an extra battery and memory card. Also, the amount of Velcro to keep it closed is very generous. Other cases I've used had a simple little not-so-secure strip. My Coolpix S3500 fits in it perfectly.

title: Not for Coolpix S3500
text: Have to give it three stars because I honestly can't say how it is. I purchased a Nikon S3500 camera and below the item, the battery was included in the "Customers who bought this item also bought..." Since my camera was the S3500, I assumed it was the right battery because it said it worked in a Nikon 3500. Nope. Too big and the contacts are wrong. I gave three stars only because I've had Nikon products before and they were always good.

title: Wish I could give it ZERO stars
text:
A pure headache. A supreme instrument of utter junk. Out of a 6 drives, it finally worked on two (after a couple of hours of different configurations). There aren't any directions, so do I plug the power supply in first? Or the USB cable into the PC first? Do I power down, then attach everything and reboot? How about power up the drive, then plug the base unit into it? That worked on one of the drives. UUUUGGGHHH!!!! Also, when you do get the drive to power up, it gets hotter and hotter, and I mean hot. The only time it didn't was when the system actually recognized it. It was trial and error.

I gave up after drive 4. One year warranty? No phone #. Just a little tiny sticker on one corner of the box that says "Cybertech." Talk about generic packaging.

Don't be an idiot like me. Carefully read the reviews and get something with those that are positive. Yeah, it'll be more expensive, but it'll be worth the aggravation and temper tantrums.

title: Quick delivery, and what a difference!
text: I placed this order on July 11, and received it on July 15 with the weekend in between. Quick service from Amamax, the seller. Of course, I installed it as quick as I could.  Wow!!! What a difference just this 2GB made.  I have an HP All-in-One PC that came with 4GB and Windows 8, and it was like it went into turbo.  I really wanted to get 4GB but with me in "economy" mode, had to settle for 2GB, bringing my system to 6GB. For the price (plus free shipping from the seller to boot), I couldn't be happier.

title: WOW!!! Great keyboard!!!
text: I've only had it since yesterday, but this keyboard is wonderful.  The different colors are adaptive to different times of the day (and depending on the mood), and the large key characters are easy to see.  The keys themselves are responsive and have both a nice feel and "click" to them. Well built and it's plain to see that a lot of thought went into it. The box says Win 7 compatible but I'm using Win 8 with no problems. Well worth the money.

title: Great product. Bad shipping box.
text: I've never had a problem with Sony discs, and these are same. The packaging was terrible, otherwise this would be 5 stars. The box was WAY too big and the plastic wrap around the discs broke and the discs came off of the spindle. I had a box full of scattered disks. I was surprised that only 3 failed.

title: Great for the price.
text: Don't expect Bose sound quality. There's only one little speaker on the right end. For it's sound, however, the speaker is halfway decent for it's size. Decent reception. The buttons can be a pain at first, but once you've had it for ten days or so, you get used to them in the dark. I wish Sony had added another speaker on the other end to make it stereo. Then I'd give it five stars.

title: No Coasters Yet
text: Must have burned over 100 DVDs with it hooked up to my Acer Aspire One. So far so good. All the DVDs have been read by other devices without a problem. Great little inexpensive drive.

title: Great watch...when it works...battery/phantom messages
text: Galaxy Watch 4 Classic LTE. Bought 10 months ago as an adjunct for health and training goals. Watch features impressive, but some notable issues. Battery Life: is less than a day even with screen off and minimal use. Many software glitches with notifications, specifically phantom Voice Mail messages and incomplete messages from applications. Watch sent for repair once and now going in for second time. Not confident issues will be resolved. The other features, especially health and exercise work well, but the frustration level is terrible

title: Solid mount for Wahoo Bolt
text: Excellent mount for Wahoo cycling computers. Quality materials and construction.  Easily mounts to handlebars.

title: Refurb unit gives muffled audio
text: Purchased as a backup, which became my primary BT phone headset after my other unit flew out a car window at 70 MPH. Refurb unit functions well except the audio is muffled compared to  the identical unit this replaced. Good for price paid

title: Keys stopped working otherwise exceptional
text:
Purchased October 2017 for use with Android Phone. Design and footprint absolutely wonderful. Easy to carry, keys easy to use (yes, there is a placement issue for touch typists). The BK03 was a go to accessory whenever I traveled -- didn't need to bring a laptop for writing long E-mails or editing documents on the fly.

Suddenly in September 2018 some of the keys stopped working. Tried unpairing and re-pairing the device...tried pairing it to other phones and tablets...nada. Not much assistance from iClever. So the keyboard is kaput after about a year. As I purchased the keyboard on a discount, I'd say it was worth the price. Will I replace it? Probably not for the full retail Amazon price. It's a shame too, this is probably the best BT keyboard "ive used with my smart phone -- just not durable over time.

title: Be gentle, be kind
text: Bought 2 of these and one cracked inside my NEW mobile phone. Very dicey removal.

title: Five Stars
text: Useful and makes plugging in large power adapters a breeze

title: Wobbly view of maps -- great if you can shake in syncopation DO NOT BUY
text:
I had to purchase this in a hurry when my el-cheapo universal mount cracked just before traveling. The kit is constructed well and I've had no problems with the suction cup falling off the windshield -- YET. I'll reserve judgment until the summer months when windshield-mounted holders fly off heated surfaces.. Here's my issue: the bendable arm isn't rigid enough to prevent constant wobbling of anything in the mount. My lightweight mobile phone is unreadable even on smooth roads. My old cheap (under $10.00) model was far superior in keeping my device in view AND readable.

Update: 1/8/2015. After less than 2 months the mount connection to the gooseneck FAILED. flimsy plastic piece holding the tension spring flew off and now the mount cannot be attached to the gooseneck. TomTom doesn't want to know ....at nearly $25.00 this is a complete rip off.

title: Bus Basics -- save big money
text: I bought this 3-pack of HDMI cables for less than half the price the local stores were charging for ONE generic cable. Delivery was fast and easy

title: Great Product - One minor flaw
text: Purchased this to have remote control of my iPod Classic when playing through my home audio system. Remote works great and overall I am satisfied. The ONLY flaw is the audio quality when connected through the unit base. Audio is low and distorted when connected via the base...solution, plug audio into the iPod headphone jack. For the price, this product is an excellent choice.

title: Great little echo dot.  LOVE the clock and temp display, wish it came in more colors.
text: We have 3 echo's in our house and this is my favorite.  This has taken the place of a regular echo dot and alarm clock in my daughter's room.  We love the clock display and the fact that it dims when it is dark in the room so it is not crazy bright when she is trying to sleep.  We also love the fact that it displays the temp when asked.  What a neat little dot.  Wish it would have come in other colors as well, might have purchased them to replace the other 2 in the house.

title: Great procut, great price!
text: Great product, did just what I was hoping for. - Looks to be really nice quality. -

title: Product fits nice and looks good
text: Product fits nice and looks good.  Fun colors to choose from.

title: Great size and nicely built
text: Really nice size and well built.  Like the extra pockets for a pen and travel mouse and a few documents.  Perfect for a small bag to travel with.

title: Cute, but not very functional!
text: My daughter just had to have this, so I bought it for her for Christmas from Target.  The lid is very cheaply made and I don't think it will last long.  Also, the scroll button for the volume does not turn easily and when it does it takes a LOT of turning to change the volume up or down.  Returning this immediately - Hope I can find something both cute and functional!

title: Won't work with Rode Go Wireless to connect to GoPro
text: I am not sure if this product works for anything else, but it does not work as an adapter for connecting the Rode Go Wireless lavalier mic to a GoPro Hero 7, despite fitting the connector specs.  I thought I would try it since the price was <1/5 what GoPro charges for their adapter, but I knew that it was possible it may not work.  I plan to keep this adapter anyway since I may need it for something else in the future.  The build quality appears nice and the connections fit accordingly.

title: Got this after a tip from an online forum - best advice I ever took!
text:
This little filter was made with witchcraft. It is fantastic at bringing more clarity, color richness, and tone to my images. It basically lives on my 35mm prime lens. I plan to get other sizes for my other lenses.

title: Great inexpensive prime lens for crop sensor

title: Works
text: It works.  It is plastic.  I got this to try some extreme macro shots with some old lenses.  The threads fit well.  Good value for the price.

title: Guess I got a bad one...
text:
I ordered this lens about 2 years ago and right out of the box the AF motor sounded like it was 'too tight'...made a high-pitched, almost abrasive sound whenever it would focus. Being the first prime lens I got for my T2i, I didn't suspect anything at first. After about 3 months, the AF stopped working entirely. I sent it off to Canon to fix under a warranty claim and they had it back to me in about 3 weeks. From that point, it worked for about another 8 months before reverting back to the same state of disrepair. I resolved to just use MF on it, however, just having this lens attached to my camera nearly instantly drains even a full-battery....must be some kind of short in it.

Regardless of the failed mechanics and weird behavior, the glass was good and I really liked the way it handled indoor light....great colors and warm tone, nice FOV. Nonetheless, this lens is basically worthless to me now and just sits in the top of my closet. Because of this experience, I am very weary to invest in more Canon lenses and have since only purchased Sigma lenses, with mixed emotions there as well. One day....I'll get a good one...hopefully.

title: Not bad as a replacement kit lens, but don't expect too much
text: After reading some of the other reviews, I've concluded that I got one of the 'soft' lenses...meaning that the majority of the time, images don't turn out as clear as they do/did with the Canon kit lens.  But, honestly, what do you expect for $200 glass?  I'd say it's worth it for the price if that's your budget and you need a kit lens replacement. I've heard great stuff about Sigma and wanted to give them a shot with something small before getting their 10-22mm or other more expensive lenses...this, however, didn't fully convince me that they're on par with Canon, but I appreciate the potential they provide for competitive pricing.

title: Works, but Lens Cover sucks
text: This case does what it says as far as keeping your camera/lens dry, but the lens cover gets scratched way too easily and absolutely robs from the clarity of the image.  For $70, it's worth it to be able to bring my DSLR along in the kayak through rapids and so forth, but I didn't expect to sacrifice so much quality on my images.  Also, the finger slots for the lens gets in the way if you have to attach your lens to the body through the lens port, not to mention what an invitation it is to dust/debris in your camera from having to attach the lens from inside the case.

title: Not Bad, Not Great
text: For the price, it's ok.  If $50 is a big deal to you, I would advise not getting it as it's not really something of top quality.  I've had this for about six weeks now and have had a little fun with it, but the construction seems to be a little loose as there is already 'debris' underneath the glass....weird since I keep it in the provided pouch and inside my bag whenever I'm not using it....a disappointment indeed.  Nonetheless, you can have some fun with shooting a limited range of stills, although it takes a little bit of a learning curve to compensate for the focus lag when shooting fast moving subjects.

title: You Will Not Regret Buying This!
text: If you have a mid/high-end DSLR, or shoot lots of video....then this is the card for you.....it performs unbelievably better than my class 4 and 6 cards...seriously, if you think you get good quality with those classes and don't think it's worth spending a few more bucks on the big daddy class 10, you are a fool, yo!  And go with Sandisk, no one else....

title: Lacks Consistency...
text:
I bought this backpack for my gf last year and it was so awesome that I just bought one for myself. Side by side, mine is a tad bit smaller/tighter. I used hers for a few trips and was able to easily put my 19" HP laptop in it (despite other reviews regarding this), so I felt very comfortable ordering the same pack for my new 16" laptop, which barely fits in the new backpack.

My only guess for this is that NG has outsourced this bag to a different (Chinese) manufacturer, as the color is slightly off and the size is tighter/smaller. I'm sure, overall, NG is reliable, but who knows how well they're watching the tolerances in the manufacturing process. In my experience, Chinese manufacturers allow much more tolerance in their process than typical American manufacturers.

Nonetheless, it's a great pack, with lots of pockets, rugged integrity, and very comfortable.

title: Great Laptop for the Money!
text:
I ordered this laptop about a month ago and have been very impressed with both the performance and the look/feel of the notebook. This is my first ASUS after bailing off of the HP bandwagon for the last few years. The slim design and light weight package are very attractive. The keyboard gives a nice resistance when typing (almost as if it has some kind of magical 'type-assist'#....as well as plenty of space between the keys. The other comments regarding resolution are somewhat right, depending on what you're doing with it. The Video Magic software from ASUS allows for enhancement for videos, and I've been impressed with the output. The only disappointment would be if you do a lot of work in PS CS4...the resolution isn't the best for fine-tuning high-res photos. Not really a big deal.

The only other downside is that my webcam is upside down. Jeers to ASUS for not yet addressing this problem with this model on their website. I used a 3rd Party workaround and it seems to work now #in most cases#.

Otherwise, great speed....loaded CS4 in under 30 minutes and it boots Photoshop CS4 in under 10 seconds, twice as fast as my duo core HP.

Overall, for the price, this laptop is hands-down a GREAT value.

title: Carpal Tunnel Be Damned!
text:
I've been using these for years, and I honestly believe it's the only reason I don't have carpal tunnel problems. I use them at work and at home. There is virtually no repetitive wrist movement when using this mouse...but...after long-term heavy use, there is a lot of wear & tear on a person's thumb, which is used to click the primary mouse button. Sure, you can reverse the buttons, but imagine your hand over the top of this mouse. You'd use your index & middle finger together to roll the ball, probably, while your thumb clicks the primary button, and the secondary button is clicked with the ring finger or palm, not parts of the hand that have the most dexterity.

I'm left-handed, and have the buttons reversed, but some games & application don't recognize the reversed buttons, so the primary mouse button becomes the one I click with my ring finger or palm, and that's not good for gaming. Also, if this mouse has an alternative to a mouse wheel, I've never been able to find it, and, again, lots of games incorporate the wheel into the controls, so that's an issue for me. Eventually, the ball, which is normally smooth as silk to operate, loses its finish and begins to feel less accurate, harder to roll & rough...but that doesn't happen for years. In fact, I can't remember when I bought the one I'm here to replace. Despite the minor annoyances, which are few, this is a comfortable, sturdy mouse, and the best mouse I've found for my left hand. Plus, no carpal tunnel surgery. What's that worth?

title: Wow!  No more, "What'd they say?"
text:
Thank you to all you wonderful Amazon reviewers. I'd never purchased a Bose product before, with the exception of possibly headphones at some point in time. We know the Bose sound is legendary, but I never really needed a Bose radio or CD player. The Solo caught my eye because I love my flat screen TV, but the speakers are only so-so at best. Like many other reviewers, I have trouble understanding some dialogue on TV. It's fine as long as there is someone around to annoy endlessly by asking "what did they say," but watching TV alone, I miss big chunks of the story & plot. The doctor says it's just "one of the vestiges of old age." Oh. Another one of those. Thanks, doc.

So, I wondered if the Solo speaker might help, and thanks to all my hard-of-hearing contemporaries here (or should I say THANK YOU), I saw all the reviews promising that I wouldn't have to ask "what?" every 2 minutes any more. I could jump for joy after hooking up the speaker and giving it a listen, although my doctor would probably advise against it. On my TV, unlike some others mentioned here, the TV speakers work along with the Solo speaker, so it's easy to mute the Solo and hear the difference between it and the TV speakers. It's amazing. The sound is rich, and big, and crisp in a way that my surround-sound system isn't. Most importantly, in answer to my wildest hopes, I can understand every single word of dialogue, even Christian Bale mumbling behind his Batman mask. No kidding. The Bose speaker took 20 years off my age, and reduced my waist by four inches. Ok, I am kidding about that.

As if all that isn't reason enough to get one of these gems, it has to be the simplest piece of electronics to hook up, set up & operate. It's simply two cords, one to the power outlet, and the other to the TV. They include all the cables in the box: digital optical, HDMI & RCA. Plug, plug, power. That's all. The remote is four buttons: power, mute, up & down volume. It's hard to believe that such intricate, complex sound can come from such a simple device. Thank you, Mr. Bose, wherever you are. Not only would I highly recommend this to my friends, I think everyone with a flat-screen TV owes it to themselves to get one. Seriously. This is the audio-visual experience I thought I was already having with 5.1 surround system.

title: Perfectly Fine Keyboard, but Be Aware of What You're Getting
text: I don't really feel the need to criticize the keyboard since it is, and does, everything the manufacturers say, but I'm back to Amazon today to buy a different lighted keyboard and I'll keep this one for emergencies.  First, the positives.  The keyboard is sleek and visually appealing.  I love the blue back-lighting.  It would probably be a good keyboard to take along for use with a laptop, and that may have been the intent because the condensed keyboard is laid out like a laptop keyboard.  That, unfortunately, is also part of the problem.  The layout of the keys makes it difficult for me to use, with keys like the backspace, which I use a lot, surrounded by other small keys such as Home & End, which sends your cursor all over the page when you hit them by mistake.  It's probably not the best keyboard for people who do a lot of typing.  In fact, I plugged in my old keyboard to write this review.  For the price, I am not displeased, and it will be a good standby in case I need it, but for long-term use, a different keyboard is probably a better choice.

title: Use it all the time...
text: The last time I tried a device like this, I couldn't get it to work.  I didn't have much faith in products that transmit an FM signal to my radio, but this product works like a charm.  I use it with an iPod Touch, along with an app that tells me the best empty FM frequencies in my area by zip code.  Once I found the right frequency, the device works amazingly well.  It does drop out of sync for a few seconds sometimes, but that's a minor occurrence that doesn't present a problem for me.  Much will depend on the location of your cigarette lighter or power source, since it may block some controls on your dash, but, again, it's a minor problem considering the great music I can now hear while driving.  You can't beat the price.

title: Perfect in every way but one.
text:
Have had this TV for about 3 years now, and it was one of the best deals I've ever found. I did a lot of research, and this model had everything I needed (at the time) at an unbelievable price compared to other brands with the same specs. The picture quality if wonderful, especially the HD channels on my cable. Every time I'm in a store with HDTVs on display, none of them seem to compare to the great picture I get on my Soyo.

However, I've just purchased a PS3, mainly for the Blu-ray player, and realized I wasn't getting full resolution because the TV resolution goes to 1080i only, but full Blu-ray needs 1080p. I had bookmarked a review from 2006 saying there was really no reason to buy 1080p at that time, and I took that advise. That's no longer the case.

If you don't care about Blu-ray (the TV does an amazing job with regular DVDs), then this is probably still a great deal.

As another reviewer mentioned, this model had an update somewhere along the way. Mine is the older model with just one HDMI input, so perhaps they've updated to provide 1080p resolution.

title: Great Little Camera...
text:
I was concerned about some of the complaints regarding short battery life, noisy zoom lens and an overall cheap plastic feel of this camera, but it was a great value & I decided to give it a try.

Luckily, I havn't had any of those problems with the camera, and after several months, am perfectly happy with it. Yes, the camera has a plastic body, but it's been very durable while travelling and seems no flimsier than any other electronic device made today. The plastic body is one reason why the camera is so easy to take everywhere. It's light, compact & not a chore to haul around, which is nice.

Rather than a short battery life, I have been suprised at the long life of the battery that came in the camera. I bought an extra battery because I expected it to run out quickly, but I've never used it. I've never needed to. During a 4-day weekend in the mountains, I plugged the camera in at night, and was able to record any time and every time I wanted all day long each day.

The noisy zoom lens? I don't know. My model doesn't have a noisy zoom lens. I can barely hear it when I use it, and have never noticed the sound of the zoom during playback. Maybe it happens with some of them.

Granted, the built-in microphone doesn't produce the best sound, but it's been good enough for my casual use of video. The video has been clear, sharp & colorful. Would I use it to record a wedding? Probably not. To record my mother's belly-dancing recital? You bet!

title: They work in all areas of my house
text:
This is my second and third purchase. Bought these to get channels the cable companies want to charge you $10 a month for. I fooled them. This worked in my bedroom great so I bought two for the living room and guest room. They work great in all rooms with a bit of adjusting placement. I have to say that those who complain they don't work must live in areas where there are obstacles. I get 50 or 60 channels clearly and with Roku TV I get another couple hundred channels through streaming using this antenna.

Please note that the 200 miles range claim isn't possible because of the curvature of the earth. 80 miles is about the limit on any antenna, so you won't be picking up signals from cities 100 miles away.

Just to take another step towards cutting the cable, I ditched Comcast internet last week in favor of $50 a month T-Mobile Home Internet (which also works great at high speeds) recently available in my area, so these antennas are still paying dividends. I'm a streamer and this digital HD Antenna is a screamer!

title: Great except one nagging thing
text:
So far. after a few months this cooling pad works great. Quiet fan. Enough motion to cool my laptop. Thick enough not to bend when I pick it up with computer by one hand. My Cooler Master was two thin and eventually squashed fan to the point of not working.

Pretty lights are hidden though, but I didn't buy it for that.

My only gripe is the way the configured the extra USB connector. Not on the pad. One side plugs in to the laptop and it has a universal connector opposite the plug in on the same wire. Kind of funky and it always has me guessing which one to plug in to my laptop. Hint. It is a tad smaller, which I have to look at both and size them up every time. I'm thinking of putting a dot o nail polish on the insert end so I can more easily tell at a glance. It is a constant nagging chore. I only took one star off but maybe I should have taken 2 stars off for the inconvenience.,

If you don't need the fan or your eyesight is better than mine, then no problem. Otherwise be forewarned. This is a constant pain.

I went back and took another star off after writing this.

I'd just as soon not have the replacement USB port.

title: UPDATE: Seller made good and replaced old earbuds after Windows 11 made them outdated.
text:
UPDATE: Nrw ones work fine after old ones couldn’t handle Windows 11.

Really good earbuds only half good now after Windows 11 update. They connect but no sound. They still work on my iPhone but not on W11. Contacted Tozo and they say its up to Windows to come up with a fix. Don't think this is going to happen since this has a been a problem since June.

So if you ever plan to update to Windows 11, skip this product. I bought a second pair in case I lost my current pair (I've been known to do that) and now they are pretty much useless too.

----
Earlier Review:
Bought the T6 because it was on sale for the same price as the T10 with more features and it is the new model, plus I like the case better. You can put it on a wireless charger and this is the reason I chose them. Really? $25 bucks and it goes on a wireless charger? My old Apple Airpods don't do that.

The sound is impressive, much better than I expected. Also better than Apple airpods. I can only assume Apple's Pro model has also improved. On the T-6, I have to turn the damn things down sometimes. You can hear the symphony bass and treble and its full and rich.

The controls are touch and work well once you learn them. Tap once to pause, again to play. Hold down for volume. Tap Twice for Forward on right bud and twice on left earbud for Reverse Also hold down for 10 count to activate pairing.

The only thing I don't like about the Tozo 6 is how hard the magnetic airpods are to retrieve from the case. There is no easy way to find a grip to lift them. It takes several tries to get one, then the other out. Apple airpods can be difficult at times, but the magnet is stronger in the Tozo 6 and there is no logical spot to dislodge them with a finger. Still, I'm not taking off any stars for that. I think this is an excellent product.

I bought these because I kept misplacing my airpods, I found them in the crevice of my recliner, but guess which ones I use now. That's right, the T6 Tozo. They really are impressive and well built. Can't believe they sell as cheap as they do--although I see price increases on the horizon. Thinking of buying another pair in case I lose these.

title: Great Battery life
text:
The battery fit my Pavilion cc1xx laptop. It had the same model number as the OEM I removed. Battery is easy to install once the cover is off, but to have to remove the bottom cover shows lack of empathy from the engineer that designed it

So far I don't know exactly how long the battery lasts. It hit four hours the first time before I recharged it with 20 percent remaining but I had it on sleep mode for an hour. I do have my battery balance set to left of middle toward best performance because my old battery died after 20 minutes not plugged in. My guess is at least three hours, maybe four if you don't do a lot of heavy usage.

I've had this computer going on maybe 4 years and if I still have it when this batter finally dies I'll buy another and replace it again. Price is great and this is an original Manufacturer battery.

You can find helpful videos on You Tube for some specific models the merchant hasn't posted.

title: Went with a cheaper Brand to see if it worked and It does
text:
I decided to go cheap after seeing some online YouTube reviews because one of them compared a $3.99 antenna with a range of price point antennas and said it pulled in most of the stations with a few fuzzy channels. Couldn't see spending $50 on a Leaf or other models cause I tend to be cheap. If it didn't work I could always buy another.

I read that the limit for reception is 80 miles because of the curvature of the earth and Amazon features a lot of Antennas that claim 100-200 miles, which is impossible. Also impossible, 4-K. Free view stretches the 80 mile limit too., claiming 130 miles. New ATSC technology is supposed to be coming out that can extend ranges, etc., , but you can bet it won't be in the $50 and under price range.

I hung the Freeview near a window in our bedroom and it pulled in all the channels in our area including UHF, and most of them were crystal clear. The Freeview comes with an amplifier, which I think helps.

I don't like draping the cords along the wall, but I draped it above the bedrooms patio door and to a window.
It is sensitive to location and I found it didn't pull in behind the TV, when I wanted to see if I could hide it. .
Depending on where you need to put the antenna, you may have better or worse results than me, but what the heck. For $16 bucks you can't go too wrong.

My only suggestion: Offer it in white, please. All of these antennas seem to come in black. I don't want a black antenna hanging on a white or beige wall.

title: Changing my Review From 3 stars to none
text:
UPDATE 4/14/21: I'm giving up on this watch. It's always something. The sleep mode is mostly better now but won't register some nights. Now the weather fails to sync so I have ghost clouds instead of weather forecasts for the week. When I try to sync it manually it just cycles and cycles for several minutes and still no weather. I've updated location to allow the watch full access and still nothing.
DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME WITH THIS WATCH. IT HAS MULTIPLE ISSUES DEPENDING ON THE LAST UPDATE. Now the battery has gone from 14 days to 3 1/2 days after one year.

PREVIOUS UPDATE: After switching to an iPhone this works better even though a previous update killed it on my Android phone. The Thing that irks me now after another update is that the sleep app is way off. Lately I am told I've been awake for 3-5 hours a night which earns me a 30 to 50 rating. Never got better than a 80 rating so far. They did include the REM sleep to the graph which is nice. Since they changed the app name to Zepp it hasn't really been the same. The few other things I use it for, steps and watch faces and time of day and compass work okay. Battery life is the best feature.

The price has gone down $40 from when I bought it; maybe because of the Zepp app you have to use on your mobile phone. It's not the best.

I bought this watch to use in counting laps while swimming, but the Covid has put the stops on that this year. It was the only watch in this price range--since reduced-- that offered a swim mode although it is GPS distance (miles) rather than laps counted.

The battery lasts 10-14 days. My wife's Fitbit Versa 2 needs charging every couple of days. I don't leave the face always on. If you leave it always on, you'll probably have to charge it in 3 days. In the econ mode you have to tilt it to your face or click on the stem to make the face visible. A good trade off for not having to charge your watch all the time.

My main gripe about this watch is that when someone sends me a text message, it repeats 3-4 times on my watch. This seems to be a problem with several of the Amazfit watches according to some of the forums I have visited to remedy the situation without success. It's annoying and difficult to see texts from others in the long line of repeat sms messages. UPDATE: Buying an iPhone to pair with this watch seems to have solved this problem for me.

I tried the music mode and it works if you already have music playing on your phone. It will display the song playing, the Album or CD Title, volume control, pause and play, next and previous song controls. However if you are on economy mode, the music face disappears and you have to search for the music control again.

I used the Find Phone and Found it easily, but your phone must have power obviously. It will ring or force volume higher if playing music, lol. UPDATE: This find phone function no longer works. Beware updates. It's like Microsoft. Everytime they update to make it better it causes glitches.

If they could fix the multiple repeat sms messages and tweak the sleep mode with more info this would be a pretty good watch. Right now its only good. Would I buy it again? Maybe, if the swim mode is good. I'll have to wait to find out.

title: A really good laptop cooler, but . . .
text:
Update 10/21/21: The thinness I talked about below finally did this cooler in. I was thinking about how long I'd had it without it breaking and . . . you guessed it. I picked up the laptop and cooling pad together with one hand as I'm want to do and the fan struck plastic when i squeezed laptop and cooler. The fan went non-stop while making a scraping sound. I slapped it lightly and the fan stopped.
----
My wife got me this for Christmas after I searched a ton of coolers. It's better than the Targus I had before which was too small and the cord short-circuited so laptop had to be situated a certain way for fan to work.

The Cooler Master put the cord on the side of a small thumbdrive-like device which I hope will protect the cord connections. The fan is quiet enough and keeps my laptop cool, but it's probably the screened top and multiple larger vents on the bottom that let it air circulate better.

Unfortunately the pad is made of plastic, is thin, and when you set it down on an uneven surface--like my leather couch-- it hums louder hitting the plastic. Likewise, when I pick it up with one hand I squeeze the cooler pad into the ban and get the buzz saw effect. Don't worry, its fine on your lap. I just have to unplug it when I set it on the leather sofa.

Other than that minor flaw, I do like this cooling pad. It's lightweight and fits my 15 1/2" laptop perfectly. If you have a 17-inch laptop it may overhand an inch or so on each side.

title: Shady tactics on keycap sizes, and marketing
text: Like another reviewer has mentioned, if any of the keys in your ALT FN CTRL row differ in size from a standard keyboard, you have to buy two whole sets of keys to complete your keeb. What a surprise that they don't include 1U sized CTRL ALT keys even though it would only cost pennies and by now the 68, 71, 75 key variants of the 65% keyboard are extremely popular. Shady tactics to force the purchase of multiple keysets which they've already artificially created a hyped demand via controlling supply. I'm pretty certain China isn't out of pbt or abs plastic that is super cheap to make. These keyboard and keycap manufactures have given you the illusion of exclusivity and use Reddit to market and drive up demand. Now they want you to buy two sets instead because of one. *thock thock thock

title: Great for my smart mirror project
text: This is being used in a smart mirror project with a Raspberry Pi 3B. Unfortunately I didn't have any spare monitors sitting around so this ended up being the most expensive component but was worth it as it fits perfectly if the width or length of your mirror is 24 inches like mine (24x18). I just removed the from bottom portion of the bezel so the screen can lay flat, no need to remove the back. Nice and bright too. Awesome.

title: Reliable source of variable temp lighting
text: Nice led panels that feel pretty solid! These little guys provide fairly even and diffused lighting with selectable lighting temp. I was actually surprised they felt as substantial as they did given the price point. I've paired them with generic NP-F750s and get about 2.5 hours at 100% brightness using these mostly for ecommerce and macro work. The only negative I have is that the stand these come with is absolutely flimsy and if you plan on using a battery bigger than the NP-F550, I'd suggest spending 10-20 bucks on some new base stands for these. I found some cheap table top tripods made of aluminum and work perfectly since the panels have 1/4 inch threads. Great lights and it sure helps that they are affordable.

title: Holy smokes the bass is amazing.....
text: I wont bore you with similes about the response, or speak to clarity, soundstages, v shaped tuning, etc. Go to headfi for that sound snob stuff. I'll tell you what I like about these: the bass response. Holy smokes these rattle my head. I know it is my imagination  but I was just listening to liquid drum and bass, I honestly thought I felt the bass compression in my chest. Just like you might get when standing next to a row of large bass bins at a club. I had no clue you could get this low with ear buds. The caveat for me was I had to ditch the provided tips and got some large spiral dots. The new tips made all the difference. If you listen to any sort of EDM, you really should try these with proper fitting tips.

title: Bought because it is plastic, not despite of.

So that board has to commute to work with me everyday and as such I need it to be light weight. I have seen some complain about it being plastic but I think this is a feature not a cost saving measure. What are people doing to their keyboards that a hard plastic case doesn't give the durability you need? I mean this stuff lasts for thousands of years in a landfill so I am sure it can handle your office environment just as well as those heavier fire hardened/tempered steel or aluminum whatevers can. Excellent board that goes almost everywhere with me.
