Searched more than a dozen stores for a good looking portfolio for my husband's iPad.

He wanted leather or faux leather, zipper closure, separate/removable jacket for iPad, wake/sleep capability, no silly exterior logo (for professional/work use), heavy duty construction, stand option, and I was hoping for less than $100 price tag. This item had all that and more. The logo is impressed into material on the front and hardly noticeable. Plenty of room inside for business cards, a pad, a stylus (holder is in the spine), zipper is sturdy, etc. Amazon had the best value (in store and online) including Best Buy, Walmart, Sams Club, etc. We could hardly believe the quality when it arrived. For less than $40. All comparables were $75-175 before shipping. Great value. We plan to order another for my iPad3. Nice item and very inexpensive.

title: Very efficient ...
text: I had an outdated charging cord for my phone hooked up in the car, and bought this as a replacement. It works a treat! Much faster, so it's the cord, since it's the same car.

title: Good value ...
text: I keep losing the cord for my Kindle Fire ... hope this is the last one I’ll buy although I guess that’s up to me! Very fast and a great length for bedside charging. A good choice.

title: Just as expected...
text: Nice little USB hub with a slightly longer than average cord; the on/off switches are very useful.

title: The little speaker that could ...
text: It's small but has very good sound quality, great available volume, nice & compact. I bought it for my desk top although it's designed for a laptop because it's USB powered and my cats have a tendency to gnaw cords that are too long & tempting (this one is shorter). It sits comfortably below my computer screen and let's me listen to music or dialog from movies that comes through loud & clear.

title: Finally! Earbuds that fit my weird ears.
text: I have always had trouble finding in-ear headsets that don't hurt and/or don't fit. These have three sizes of buds, which stay in & are very comfortable. Great find.

title: Will not fit 2023 Forester!
text: Like other reviewers have said this will not fit on a 2023 Subaru Forrester. The screen is slightly curved and this will peel up at the edges and look absolutely awful. This is super cheap so it’s not a big deal but even if it was free, I still would put in on my screen. Absolutely do not buy this product.

title: Impossible to fold out
text: These legs lay so flush to the bottom of my laptop when they aren’t in use that they are impossible to pull out again without some sort of knife to slide in and pry them out. Maybe if you have a super long fingernails you can deploy the legs but otherwise they are more of a nuisance. And good luck if you don’t stick them on perfectly the first time because they’re impossible to get off and you’ll be stuck with a wobbly laptop.

title: Perfect for video meetings
text: No more setting my laptop on a stack of books! Puts it at a perfect height and allows you to utilize the space underneath. I’ve looked at a few products to elevate my laptop and they all seem so involved and over engineered. This is simple and sturdy. I have a MacBook Air and it fits perfect.

title: The bottom will fit
text: I purchased this before and the bottom did not fit.  It wasn't a huge deal as the top fit and thats what I really was interested in protecting.  I figured I just got a bad one.  I ordered this again in green and the bottom didn't snap on just like the first one I got.  Apparently its not a case of getting a defective one but rather they are not designed to fit.  If you get this product for your MacBook Air know that you will only be able to protect the top of your computer.

title: Bottom does NOT fit 2020 MacBook Air 13”.
text: This product is extremely poorly made. The bottom would not snap into my computer. I have the new 2020 MacBook Air 13 inch. It seems like it was either made for a different laptop or it’s of such low quality that it’s a crapshoot whether it fits or not. The one that fits on top is fine. The bottom is the problem. If you snap in one side the other side pops out and vice versa. Also, if both pieces are on, opening the laptop will pop off the bottom piece. Look for something better.

title: This will not add any height to a large TV
text: I bought this because I wanted my TV to be a little bit higher than it is now. They claimed this can be used on a 65 inch television. My television is 60 inches and it did not work at all. First of all, the back of your TV needs to be completely flat. If there is any bulge or anything like that (like mine) this stand will not work. It needs to be flush. The description implies that it will add height but it will not. If anything it would’ve made my television lower than using the current pedestal that it’s on. I would suggest that this product would work for something the size of a computer monitor or any TV that is 30 inches or less. If you are looking to replace the stand on your current TV and you don’t care about it having any extra height this product might work for you. For reference the back of my TV is 400 mm x 400 mm and this product says it can fit on 400 x 800. If I was able to attach it it would’ve been basically flush with the table that it’s on.

title: Cheap knock off but decent.
text: I bought this to replace one that was similar that I purchased in a store for about $40. This one is definitely made cheaper but seems like it’s pretty good. I don’t really tap on the screen while it’s sitting on a table or anything, I just use it to protect my iPad when I set it down and things like that. The only thing that I don’t like is that the case doesn’t cover the entire edge of the iPad. The shorter sides are completely exposed and could be prone to chipping. I suggest you go with a more rugged case if you travel with your iPad. The only place I really use mine is while I’m sitting on the couch.

title: Why am I just finding out about this thing now!
text: I eat lunch in my car just about every weekday because I drive for work. I’ve been doing this for over a decade and just found out about this thing. I wish I had one since day one.

title: Great!
text: Inexpensive comparatively and started working (charging) immediately. Super easy to change out the old and put in the new. I was concerned my computer was going out just as I am about to graduate nursing school and sick about losing all my info from school but turns out it just needed a new battery :)

title: Five Stars
text: The adapter worked just fine in Ireland. Delivery was prompt.

title: Wish it had lasted longer, but nice
text: Nice, as long as it lasted, which was almost two years.

title: Excellent Product!
text: Does just what it's supposed to do and is of a perfect traveling size!

title: What's Not To Love!
text: What's not to love about such a product that fills a need!

title: Works Well
text: Form to function; works well.

title: When you need a corded mouse
text: ... this is a great and inexpensive choice. I am a researcher, and my solitary foray into the realm of cordless mice taught me rather quickly that batteries don't last long when paired with long workdays. If your need is for a sturdy, apparently well-made computer mouse, choose this one!

title: New to webcams, but this is a great experience!
text: I have been intimidated with the thought of actually entering the 21st century & getting a webcam, but this little gem is perfect! Easy to set up and operate, and delivers a good picture and sound! Two thumbs up from someone who just wanted to be able to communicate with friends at a distance, and this is a fine product!

title: Great Surprise!
text: Logitech, THANK YOU for this great product! Having always had poor speakers for my PC -- until now -- I never realized what great sound could be delivered! All I can say is Wow! I am very impressed by the facts that these speakers are inexpensive, but clearly well-made, and the sound is pure and powerful. Two thumbs up!

title: Good product
text: It seems that wired computer mice are going the way of the dinosaur, so I bought two of these, and have only used one so far, but it's doing a great job! I'm thankful to have located these; my work as a researcher means that any wireless mouse would be in constant need of recharge. I made that mistake only once! If you need a good wired computer mouse, this one does the job!

title: Only slightly less than Perfect!
text: My decision to purchase this keyboard was based on a glowing review by someone that had been using his keyboard for a few months. I was seeking a keyboard that was quiet and ergonomic (fatigue-diminishing and user-friendly). My old H-P keyboard, after 4+ years of daily use, had become so "clattery" that it was a nuisance; plus, I'd worn the lettering off several keys! This new keyboard, though not 'whisper-quiet,' is definitely quieter. It took 2 or 3 days to get used to the different hand positioning and smaller "Enter" key, but was a breeze to adjust to. I'm hoping now to find a quieter Mouse! Would recommend this to anyone using a keyboard for several hours each day and in need of the relief provided by a soft-touch keyboard and quieter keystrokes.

title: Works
text: Works it’s a little difficult to get the hang but is ample magnification for cannabis trichromes

title: Works
text: Works

title: Protects my surge
text: It works

title: Appears brand new
text: Saving money

title: Inexpensive security
text: Price,ease of installation and very good views day or night

title: Super cute
text:
Super cute and easy to apply. It's a little too small though doesn't cover all edges.

Update: it doesnt hold very well, I have to constantly press it back down because it'll start peeling up on its own.

title: Jammed first time I used it
text:
I inserted a floppy after connecting the drive to teh computer, and it promptly jammed. The computer does not recognize the floppy as being inserted, and the eject button is impossible to depress. It looks like I may need to open the drive to get the floppy out.

Overall, a failure.

title: Impossible to install
text:
The information for these states that the pads can be used with Sennheiser HD4.50BT headphones. They in fact cannot be because the flap on the back that is supposed to go into the groove does not fit. Additional problems include lack of instructions and collapse of the headphones while trying to put the pads on. And I am assuming that the orange "pick" was to help push the material into the way too small groove, but I have no proof of this as I never got that far.

I should have been suspicious when they had to take the headphones off camera during the "instructional" video.

Totally turned off on the brand now because the pars failed much sooner than they should (a year), the cost of replacements was high (>10% of my purchase price) and the basic inability to use them. I now have some great sounding paper wights.

title: Bought refiurbished, did not work, tech support worthless
text:
I bought two of these refurnished expecting them to be reset to factory settings. They were not. As a result, I could not get into them. Called tech support, and they were never able to give me any useful suggestions. In the end, they turned into landfill because my time to return them expired.

Never buying refurbished gear from this company again.

title: Very good cables
text: These cables seem to be above average in quality and construction.  The wire appears to be reinforced well an should last for a long time.  Value for the money is good.

title: Great for laptops and otehr mobile devices
text: I damaged my audio jacks and needed a replacement for my laptop.  Rather than spend $1,000+ for a new laptop, I bought this.  It works fine and produces good sound quality.  It should work with other devices with a suitable USB port.

title: Excellent audio quality and small footprint
text:
I placed this under my 55" HDTV. It is a narrower but is a good width for getting stereo sound. I used a stand for the TV, and the speaker sets on the foot with about 2" to spare. The subwoofer was hidden behind my computer desk. Connection is by Bluetooth, so there is no wire out the back. The speakers and subwoofer both provide plenty of volume. If anything the subwoofer is overwhelming, but you can adjust its volume independently. The visual feedback through some blue LEDs hidden behind the speaker mesh works well. There are multiple preset buttons for music, conversation/voice, etc. They shape the response of the system and tend to work okay but are not exceptional. Overall sound quality is very good across the entire audible spectrum.

My biggest complaint is that the speaker will go to standby way too often and revert to the ARC input while I use the AUX input. Ut results in a lot of pushes of buttons to get the speaker system awake and on the right channel again. Small things like this prevented me from giving it 5 stars, but the speaker system is very good and a good value.

title: Mixed thoughts
text: These are good, solid Velcro fasteners, but the way that the end goes through the buckle and back has proven to not work well for me in a couple of cases.

title: Great fill lights
text: I used AI bought these for fill lights.  They can provide the equivalent of a 20 W incandescent light, which is plenty of light with modern DSLRs.  One or two can fill int he shadows when shooting in low light or backlit situations.  battery life is excellent with no problems getting over 90 minutes of life at full power and much longer with even a small decrease in output.  If I had any ideas for improvement, it would be to have presets for common light sources (daylight, tungsten, etc.) to better match the primary light source.  The value of the unit is great, and I highly recommend it.

title: Revived my dead laptop
text: The battery was hard to get into the laptop and lacks the foot to raise up the back of the laptop that I have on my old battery.  Once the difficulty with getting the battery in was solved with some sharp blows with the heel of my hand, it charged right up and is doing a fine job of powering my old Dell.

title: No box, no manual, bit so far no problems
text: This is as basic as it gets.  It was shipped in a non-ESD plastic bag with little protection.  It has no privacy cover.  You can get access to the manual on-line, but a print copy would have been nice.  I found out there that you can tilt the camera rather than needing to hang it cocked downward.  It has sufficient range of motion to work on a 55-inch monitor.  Picture quality is acceptable to good.  I have some issues with backgrounds being blown out that I need to address.

title: Some issues
text: The unit is particularly sensitive to even minor line fluctuations.  It was constantly making noises until I went to the Web sote and found the cause.  Decreasing the sensitivity seems to have cured the problem.

title: Works as advertised
text: Pops into the printer easily, does not jam, is easy to remove the backing and adheres well.  What more do you want?

title: Gemnerally works well but some issues noted
text:
I like these panels. They provide an even diffuse light. They have multiple filters, if you want to add colors or adjust white balance. They have a range of heights. The on/off and power setting buttons work well to control the lights.

My negatives are stability and power. The tripod legs are a trade-off of space for stability. They work, but the lights are prone to being easy to knock over. This is a common issue and hardly unique to these lights. The panels do not provide as much light as I was expecting, though it is generally adequate. The need to supply your own USB power block was a "hidden cost" that needs to be considered. If you have plenty of high current extras laying around, it is not an issue. If you have to order some, add the cost to your buying decision.

UPDATE: I dropped the rating to stars because the ON/OFF membrane switch on one of the lights died and the ilght is dead after much less than 100 uses. They need better switches.

title: Not as good as I was hoping it would be
text: I live in a major metropolitan area with several TV stations.  Most work fine, but at least two that should have a very strong signal are giving consistent problems, and a third can be problematic.  The other stations work fine.  If you are on the fringe of the broadcast area of a TV station you want, I would look at a different antenna.  If you want something for casual or occasional use and have good signal strength, the value for the price is okay, but you are never going to get the weak signal station with it.

title: Will not work unless you create a Roku account!
text:
All I want is a TV for the (None of your business) room. I was forced to create a Roku account to even get started. THIS IS NOT RIGHT! The TV tuner is all I want or need. If I want streaming, I will get an Amazon Fire Stick. The sole reason that this is not heading back is that I did not have to setup payment for Roku. If they demand payment, it will be! The questions required to srtup the account were intrusive and unneeded.

Value your privacy or just do not want an unwanted service that will probably track your viewing> DO NOT BUY THIS TV!!!

As for the TV itself, it fir where it needed to go and works well. Picture quality is good for a 1080p 32"-class screen. Sound is acceptable, but I will be routing it to a stereo as soon as I figure out how to connect the two. Without the Roku issue, this would have been a solid 4 Star unit.

title: Does what I need it to do
text:
Shooting miniatures and figures in a tabletop studio can result in some color shift due to reflected colors from the background or even the item being photographed. This card gives me white balance and color checks. I cannot speak to its absolute accuracy, but visually it is consistent with the advertised values. Once I get the images into Photoshop, I use the values to give consistent color rendition. (See the Web for hundreds of tutorials on how to do this.) It is quick , easy and gives superior results. It ir even a simple white card can really increase your photography game in these situations.

The second card can be taken on the road for when you are dealing with a lighting situation where you have LED, fluorescent and tungsten lights and need help deciding what to use for the white balance. (That was me at the IX Center during a prior Cleveland Auto Show.) You still might not be able to reach perfection, but you can examine the trades.

title: Solid case with easy access
text: The case is very stirdy with an anodized aluminum shell that should protect the cards inside against all but the heaviest of loads.  The molded foam interior holds the cards securely and will nto allow them to fall out when you open the case.  You can store micro-SD cards underneath full-sized cards or adapters.  The case is still slim enough to go into my camera bag easily.  My only small complaint is that the design of the slots does not allow me to flip the cards over to indicate that they have been used and are full.  I bought a second case for that.  The multiple colors made it easy to used blue for ready to use and red for ready to download iamges.

title: Great for VOIP and virtual meetings
text: These work very well for taking calls int he computer or doing a virtual meeting.  They are faily comfortable though they could use more and better padding.  Sound quality is good, and the microphone works well.

title: Solid batteries, good price
text: Sometimes unexciting is good.  These are good batteries at a low price that come with a charger that can be used virtually anywhere that has power.

title: Good stand with a couple of small issues
text:
The stand went together easily and works exactly as advertised. I have a 55" monitor weighing 50 pounds on it, and it is rock solid. I can rotate the screen side to side with no concerns. It also gives no indication of tipping over when pushed or pulled.

I really liked the compartmentalization of tools, fasteners, screws and spacers. If there is a screw needed to attach the monitor that is not included, I would be very surprised. Hanging the monitor on the stand can be done alone, but get someone to help if you can.

The one thing that loses this stand a star is the base. I was unable to get all four screws installed because the hole locatins were too far off. The sheet metal is also thin and will easily depress if you put something onto it or lean on it.

Overall, this is a very good choice for a stand.

title: Extremely small large storage option
text: These are so small that I can put the into my laptop USB ports and leave them there for tons of extra storage for my photos and other files.  They are also great for sharing.  The only downside is that they are so small that they can be easily misplaced or lost.  I suggest a storage container for them when they are not in the computer.

title: Did not work for me
text: I had two spots on my sensor.  I went through the cleaning process, and I still have two spots on my sensor.  There was no noticeable change in the spots after cleaning.  My conclusion is that I put my sensor at risk for no gain.

title: Impressive lens that is a bot difficult to focus well at first
text:
Toss out everything and start from scratch with this lens. First, on an Olympus OM-D EM-1 camera, the distance markings are worthless. Ignore them and use the screen to focus. Be absolutely certain to use electronic magnification while adjusting the focus, or you are going to miss more than hit. I find working in Manual Mode with Manual Focus is the best. An aperture around f/ 8 is my preference for bright subjects, but I have worked all the way down to wide open and gotten good shots. If you develop a mental checklist and go through it /every time/, you can get great results with this lens.

For my EM-1 and all other micro-4/3 cameras, the top and bottom of the circle are cut off some. I estimate that I still get over 80% of the circle area in my photo, and I am very happy with it.

Some subjects that seem to work well with this lens include landscapes, wind farms, museum falleries and cars.

Example photos are from The Early Ford V-8 Museum in Auburn, IN USA.

title: Screwed during registration if you do not have perfect eyesight
text:
Who was the moron who came up the the color scheme and font for registering the tablet? It is virtually unreadable even with a 5X magnifier unless you have 20/10 vision. It is very low contrast combined with extremely thin characters. And black on orange was a low level safety color combination to prevent photocopying game codes in my day.

And in case some of those on the design team missed it, SOME OF US need more than the absolute minimum illumination that is quick to go down and VERY slow to go up. Overall, I give teh Fire registration and initial startup a -1 on s scale of 0 to 10.

Also, I do not have a T1 or better connection, so my speed might nbot be up to Amazon's standards, but do you have to keep popping up "Slow network connection. Do you want to continue?" every ten seconds?

Horrible experience!

title: Great for small primes
text: I bought a couple of these for short primes (12 mm, 17 mm and 25 mm).  They hold the lenses well and protect them from damage.  They are easy to open, even one-handed.  The cases are well made and should prove very durable.

title: Good, but a bit small
text: The holder is well made and works well with one exception.  If you have larger card cases like ones for micro-SD and a regular SD carrier, the pockets are small and difficult to get the cases in and out.  If you need to be able to change cards quickly regularly, you need to use cases with just a regular SD card, use no case or get a different holder.

title: Easy to use
text: The unit does what it is supposed to do easily and quickly.  It provides a cheap "Go/No-Go" check on old batteries and rechargeable batteries that are questionable.  My only complaint is that D cells barely fit into the unit.  Even 2 mm more jaw depth would have helped.

title: Good prime lens
text: I recently used this to shoot a parade.  The large aperture made focusing extremely fast and accurate.  Out of 200+ photos I lost only 1 due to lack of good focus.  The pictures were crisp, even out to the edge using about f/ 4 for my shots.  The depth of field worked well with my subject in crisp focus with the background slightly blurred to isolate my subjects.  The build quality feels a little cheap, but I think it will hold up to regular use.  I would be careful using it where it might get bounced around or splashed.

title: Eats batteries
text: Overall, this radio delivers on what it promises, but it goes through batteries quickly.  I also found the manual charging to be less-than-great with a lot of work producing little time.  Great for burning calories but not what I want in an emergency.  I also wish that the storm / emergency on would turn the unit off after 5 minutes to prevent battery drain when no one is home and the unit was left in standby mode.

title: Nice moderate wide-angle prime
text: I like this prime for low-light situations.  I also find that the large aperture helps focus quicker and more accurately in good light.  It works well for night street shooting, the reason I bought it.  It is also lightweight and comfortable to use.  Build quality is, as usual for Zuiko lenses, excellent.

title: Good value and good batteries
text: The batteries work great and the charger being able to do two at once is a boon when you shoot as many photos as I do.  However, you need to bring your own power cube or USB port to the game.  I drop them one star for not including a 120 V-to-USB converter.

title: Great Macro
text: This is a really nice macro and a good compliment to my 50 mm macro.  It has a wider field of view and better depth of field.  This makes it great for photographing moderate size items.  If you do macro photography or sell items on-line, this lens should work well for you.

title: Fried my electronics
text:
I setup the unit as the directions indicated, plugged the low voltage side into my USB hub and then plugged the power supply into the outlet strip.

POP!

(Smell of burning electronics)

(Hurried rush to disconnect things in case a real fire started, like it smelled it would)

So much for the $50 USB hub!

I am not a happy customer. It is not worth the postage to return it, so I am just going to toss everything and buy a new hub.

title: Comfortable system neck strap
text: I like the system.  I bought the strap, extnesions and securing straps.  They work well together and allow me to have a very comfortable, secure neck strap for my DSLR, even when I have a grip, flash and large lens attached.

title: Great value unit with a couple of useful features
text:
This is your basic AM/FM clock radio. It has the nice additions of a port for charging your USB-charged device (no cable included). I originally did not think much of the projected time, but it has really grown on me. It makes it easy to see the time without having to turn around to see the clock, It also flips so that you have have the time at the foot or head of the bed.

Overall, this is a great value.

title: Well built
text: The head is well built and appears to function well.  I would have liked a detent at the 0 degree position, though.

title: Good protection
text: I bought this for a 30 mm macro lens that i do nto use every day and wanted to protect while it was on the shelf.  The case fits the lens well and provides excellent padding.

title: Comfrotable and solid
text: This is a solid, comfortable camera strap that delivered good value and performance.  It is a great replacement for a thin strap like the Nikon DSLR I inherited had.

title: Great camera strap upgrade
text: This is a very nice camera strap and a huge step up from what comes with most cameras.  the extra padding distributes the weight of heavier lenses whiel the padding makes it far more comfrotable.  I used the extension straps to give me a longer strap to make it easier to sling over a shoulder when I am walking and not taking photos.  They even offer Velcro straps to ensure taht the straps do not come undone.  Having nearly lost a camera from that, I really appreciate it.

title: Very good quality grip with plenty of features
text:
I like that it extends the bottom about an inch. My pinky hurts a lot less after a long shoot with this grip. The extra shooting button is great for vertical orientation shots. It also has dials, just like on the camera body. The ability to lock out the controls to prevent accidental changes and shots. The price is also hard to beat.

I wish that it had a way to put both batteries in the grip for easy access. You have to take the grip off to replace the internal battery.

title: Solid performance and large capacity
text: The card is fast and well built.  It is noticeably better than a similar card I got to share a micro SD card with another person.

title: Not a very good tripod
text:
The ball head does not lock well, and after I took the head off to see what thread I needed to replace the head, I cannot get it to screw down tight again. Overall build quality was also only good, at best.

Overall, very disappointing.

title: Five-year-old monitor design with issues
text:
(How old is this monitor? Both boxes were covered with dust!)

Considering that the monitor came out 5 YEARS AGO, it does well. The picture is pretty good, and the design is reasonable for having two monitors positioned side-by-side. Whites are nice and white, and color saturation and blacks look good.

The first major negative is the dang buttons. They are hidden on the stand, hard to reach, not mechanical so you get no positive feedback and do not always work. The second is the lack of a VESA mount, though there is apparently an adapter (another $60+) of questionable mechanical design. Overall, you can probably get a better monitor that is more up-to-date for a lower price, especially if you want/need a VESA mount.

title: Bad drive, worse customer care
text:
I give this drive a single star for two reasons.

First, the drive constantly stops responding. The drives go into some sort of constant seek cycle, and the drive becomes quite hot. I have to turn off the drive to get it to respond agian, and the problem repeats after any length of inactivity. Most likely, the behavior will greatly shorten the life of the drive.

The second reason is the total lack of support from Western Digital when I sought help with the problem or to return the drive for a warranty repair/replacement. My request for help was ignored. Given the cost of this drive, I think that I deserve a response at least.

title: Provides good ausio wirelessly
text: I wanted a high quality wireless solution for my presentations so that i could minimize some of the cabling I use.  This proved a good solution.  It synched easily and provided very good audio.  i found it very useful for presentations.

title: Did not work with WIN 8.1
text: It turned out that there were no drivers for WINDOWS 8, and I had problems accessing the Web site to find updated versions.  in the end, I used another option.

title: Works well
text: Let's be honest.  This is a diffuser.  It either works or it does not work.  I found that the diffuser worked and provided even illumination over a wide area with an acceptable loss in flash power.

title: Good cover
text: I was looking for a utilitarian cover for my Fire, and this fits the bill well.  It has enough padding to be protective without a lot of weight or bulk.

title: A great disappointment from Olympus
text:
This was a waste om money, IMO. The manual consists of six pictographs and a couple of sentences, the only one relevant to actually using the sight being "Keep the dot on the subject.".

I found a video on-line for the new Olympus camera with a built-in dot sight. What they expect you to do is hold the camera well away from your body and use the screen on the back of the camera. The dot is supposed to be used as a general guide, not a precision alignment device.

I regularly shoot wildlife and animals using a 300 mm lens. The last thing I want to do it hold the camera at arms' length. That is how you get shaking and other problems.

It would have been far preferable to have had a second mark or guide. Adjust the dot so that the camera lens, subject and sight are are aligned, and then you can hold the camera in close and use just the dot sight to follow the action.aligned

If you use dot sights like this and have no qualms about holding your camera a couple o feet from your body, it might be worth something to you. Otherwise, my siggestion is to not buy this sight,

title: Solid performer as a conitnuous ight source
text: I like this unit,  I shoot almost entirely witht eh light on rather than using the flash.  the flash has problems with getting the exposure correct, but the continuous light is dead on every time.  Lighting is uniform.  the color is slightly cool with a notable bluish tint.  Battery life for me has been very good.

title: Okay, but minimal to no benefit from warming filter
text: To be honest, I really do not see much if any difference when I use this polarizer versus my normal polarizer.  It works well, but the warming effect really does not show up strongly enough to really affect the images.

title: Worth the money to protect your Kindle

title: Good way to bridge the Four Thirds to Micro Four Thirds gap
text:
Converters have a bad history. Normally they slow down focusing, cut light to the camera, and otherwise degrade the camera and image. The MMF-3 seems to have overcome those problems when used with the OM-D EM-1.

The secondary benefit is that, if you invested in a series of good lenses for your Four Thirds system, you do not ahve to invest a few thousand dollars into new lenses.

title: Excellent Camera
text:
I have been shooting Olympus cameras since 1978. I have always loved the lenses. With over 2,000,000 shots on my Olympus E-500 camera, I decided it was time to invest in a new camera.

I was reluctant at first to try the EM-1 for three reasons:
- The format is Micro-Four Thirds, not Four Thirds. I take 99% of my photos in the telephoto range, and that is what Four Thirds was optimized to use. Micro-Four Thirds is geared more towards wide angle lenses.
- The camera is mirrorless and uses an electronic Viewfinder (EVF).
- I have to use a converter to mount my existing Four Thirds lenses, and converters have a very bad history.

Out of the box:
The first thing that you notice when you pull the body out is that it is SOLID. The thing feels like it is built like a tank. I have not tried the "splashproof" and other claims, but just holding this body I can believe them. The camera fits well in my hand. My hands are a little large, and my pinky occasionally slides off the bottom. I may buy the grip/extra battery holder later if this proves to be a problem. YMMV.

Using Four Thirds lenses:
I have no Micro Four Thirds lenses and a lot invested in Four Thirds lenses, so using them was a key issue. Olympus has 1/17 or 1 MP of the sensor dedicated to phase detection auto focus, the only type of auto focus that will work with these lenses. I find that the system works very well. Focusing is fast and accurate.

Mounting the converter is easy, as expected. Once mounted, you use a button on the side to release the lens. This is a learning issue since I still normally hit the lens release button on the camera body. I anticipate little real problems with this since as soon as I try to put the cover on the back of the lens I realize my error.

Balance with the 12-60 mm Four Thirds lens is excellent. Holding the lens by the zoom collar, the weight is only slightly behind my left hand. I only have to support the body lightly with my right hand. I personally like that balance. Longer lenses like the 70-300 are also well balanced.

EVF:
I have used a mirrored SLR since 1978 and a rangefinder 35 mm camera and 126 film P&S cameras before that. As you might guess, I favor a direct view to see what I am shooting. EVF have issues with resolution and lag when moving to a different point of interest or following a subject, especially in low light.

The EVF has turned out to be great. I really like Olympus' implementation. There is some lag, but it is generally minimal. The "What You See Is What You Get" is a big plus in my book. Adjust the exposure compensation or manual exposure settings, and the view in the EVF changes to reflect what the image will look like. It is not perfect, but it gets 95%+ of what you will actually get. The display of settings is bright, clear, crisp, large, and surprisingly unobtrusive.

The EVF also allows a lot of changes in camera settings to be done without removing the camera from your eye. Use the two dials, and you can see where the focus points that you are using are. Hit the OK button on the back, and you can use the dials to adjust just about every setting while watching the selections you are making in the EVF. Ditto with the other buttons like HDR and auto exposure mode.

HDR:
I had the opportunity to use in-camera HDR while on a recent trip. The day was cloudy, and there was a lot of shadow against bright grey clouds. The in-camera HDR used a series of shots at different exposures and combined them in the camera. The results were better than HDR Pro in Photoshop CS5.5 IMO. I was much, much happier with the dynamic range and overall look of the images. the 10 fps shooting mode was also great for minimizing camera movement, ghosts and other problems associated with HDR.

Image stabilization:
The EM-1 has a five axis image stabilization system for the sensor. That means any lens becomes can be used. The fourth and fifth axes are for rotations. One compensates for the slight turn of the camera that often occurs when you press the shutter button. I had good success using IS in low light with my 70-300 mm lens set at 300 mm.

Scenes:
the EM-1 has many useful scene modes. I used landscape and panorama with great success. The artistic filters and story modes may also interest you. I prefer to do those types of things in post-processing.

ISO:
The camera has an almost insane 25600 maximum ISO. Yes, you get image quality degradation and noise at that ISO, but the in-camera JPEG processor can actually give you some relief from the problems at higher ISOs. I so far have found shooting up to ISO 1600 produces no discerned degradation. I tried ISO 6400 and found minimal issues.

For those who started with film and were in love with the "high ISO" 1000 film for low light shooting, this is a major and welcome advancement. For those newer to photography that have been using higher ISO cameras for a while, the speed may not be much of a gain, but the image quality should be.

The low end ISO is 200, which is the new normal. I do not find it to be a problem. I would rather shoot at a faster shutter speed than have an ISO 100 setting in most cases. There is an ISO LOW setting, but I do not plan to use it. If you regularly shoot in bright light and want lower f-stops, invest in a neutral density filter.

Back display:
The back display is slightly disappointing. It can only tilt up and down, not rotate so that you can see your composition when you are getting into the shot. It works well for shooting over crowds or getting a low angle shot.

On the plus side, the display is clear, bright and a touchscreen that can be used to select a point of interest for focusing and can be used to take the shot in live view mode. You can also use it to select settings to change. The next generation should be even better, and hopefully it will have a screen that rotates.

SD card:
One change from the E-500 that I do not like is the use of SD rather than CF cards. CF cards are nearly indestructible, and a good Sansdisk Extreme card works virtually anywhere, anytime and is virtually impossible to physically break. The xD card slot disappearing is no loss, but not having a second card slot is somewhat surprising given the high-end prosumer/professional positioning of this camera.

Controls and customization:
The controls are pretty well placed for me with the exception of the auto exposure lock button. That is right beside the viewfinder and too far to the left for my liking. You can do a lot of customization with the control buttons and dials, but there are limits. I have not made any changes yet because I am still learning the camera. Overall the defaults seem logical and useful.

This camera has two dials, one on the front and one on the back. The E-500 only had a back dial, so I am learning to use the two dial system. They work well for adjusting and selecting options. I think the second dial was a good addition. Both are conveniently located for my fingers.

Image quality:
All of this is meaningless if the image you get out is bad. The EM-1 does not disappoint. I know that there are people who insist that they need 48 MP or some other ridiculously large number. The reality is that 16 MP is a great size for printing full-size 300 dpi images on your printer or using a commercial photo printing service. If all you do is screen displays, it is about eight times more pixels than you need for a typical 2 MP monitor.

The quality of the EM-1 pixels is very high, and you get excellent out-of-the-camera RAW and JPEG images. I have no problems seeing fine detail at 100% and higher magnifications.

Summary:
This camera is a winner, and it works with my existing Four Thirds lenses so I do not have to invest another $3000+ in lenses to use it. I have a lot to learn, and it will take some time to get the most out of the camera, but out-of-the-box, using my E-500 techniques, it is already doing great work.

title: Works relatively well
text:
The camcorder was bought to record some interviews and later to be used for general videos. It worked very well for the interviews with excellent image quality and color balance. The audio was good but not great with the built-in microphone, something that I expected.

I have tried to use it for other general videos with a fair number of action shots of animals, planes and other moving targets. I find the screen to be difficult to see in direct sunlight, one of the main reasons I strongly prefer an optical viewfinder over a screen. The audio is okay, and the video quality is very good in bright and moderate light. In very low light, it starts to suffer as most camcorders in this price range do until it eventually becomes almost unusable.

I am not enamored with the controls. I find that they do not fall where I need them. The still camera is only okay, though it does give a 12 MP image. Get a DSLR or quality P&S if you are serious about still images.

If you want a very good, moderate cost camcorder for moderate to bright lighting and can live with the controls, this is a good choice.

title: Good concept, not so good device
text:
I bought and installed the Pogoplug on my LAN for the purpose of sharing photos over the Internet.

Right out of the box I had misgivings. There is no documentation or technical specifications. That immediately raised serious questions in my mind about it being vulnerable to hacking or opening access to my computer and personal information. You have to attach it to your modem/router and allow it to go out on the Internet without knowing what it is doing. I decided to take it on faith that the company was legitimate and not going to install a backdoor into my system.

I attached a Seagate USB external hard drive as my main memory device. I have also used USB memory sticks for temporary storage. All are USB 2.0.

Initially I had issues with people accessing my files. The Web access used by outsiders does not show any indication of activity. If you have a couple of hundred photos like me, it can take a couple of minutes for anything to appear. I have also had people report 404 and other errors fairly frequently. My workaround was to create more folders to compartmentalize everything. They load quickly enough for people to see something happening and know that they are connected.

Once you get inside the folders, people see a filmstrip and a large image like they would see in Windows. It is a serviceable but not glamorous interface. It is also not customizable.

Once I established that people could access my photos over the Internet, the next step was to fill up the hard drive. To do so, my plan was to push the files over my 10/100 MBps LAN. The Pogoplug shows up as a drive, so all I have to do is drag-and-drop. The problem is that it is incredibly slow. I normally get about 30 kBps. That is dial-up modem slow.

This exposed the second big problem. Remember the total lack of documentation? I had no FAQ, troubleshooting guide, technical specifications or other information to go on. I had to contact technical support via the Pogoplug web site. The Web site is slow and not always working, but I did get to someone, and they gave me the obvious suggestions like turning everything off and back on, dismounting and remounting the drive, trying a different drive, etc. After several iterations, I still had a slow connection that was now unreliable, a bunch of tech talk gibberish on ports and processes to open and close, and a closed out support ticket.

Doing more research, this appears to be a known and frequent problem. It is a deal breaker for me. I am going to be looking for a replacement. As an interim solution, I will attach the USB HD directly and transfer my files on an as-needed basis. However, I am looking for an alternative now.

So, to summarize, the concept is great, the implementation is okay, but the tech support and the LAN connection are not good. If you are serious about file sharing, this is not the device for you.

title: Good sound not so good connectivity
text:
I got this wireless buds cause I lost my previous pair of tws buds. It comes in a cheap box with minimal packaging. As soon as you take it out of the box you question the quality of the product. It feels light and made of cheap plastic. But as long as it performs it's good right?

Well let's start with the positives. The sound quality is excellent. Not too bass-y which is what I like. It is clear and the sound separation is quite nice. I noticed instruments in some songs which I haven't heard in my previous wireless earbuds. All in all this is a great sounding earbuds. You can also use it mono or one at a time.

But that is where the qualities end. The ANC is bare minimum. There's no app support. And whenever you try to switch the noise cancelling mode it goes to ambient sound first then you have to change it again. Sometimes the taps doesn't register properly.

The mics on it are ok. It picks up a lot of noise but in a quieter environment the calls are good. But I dont know if it's my product or in general, the mic only seems to work properly on the right earbud. The left earbud barely picks up my voice.

The main issue I had with this earbud is the Bluetooth connectivity. It would disconnect randomly in the middle of calls. One time it kept disconnecting and reconnecting a few times in the same call. When listening to something the track sometimes skip randomly. And there is no clear indication or it doesn't let you know that it's low on battery. It just dies when the buds run out of juice.

The battery life is average. Not bad but not outstanding either. Around 5 hrs on the earbuds itself and with the case it lasts me around 2.5days I'd say. (On average I use the buds 3.5-4 hrs daily)

title: Great discreet bodycam…Kind of
text: [[VIDEOID:bc06b38f85cb90428ede7cda6c1d5f8f]] I picked this up as a “discreet” way to document my daily commute. Where I live I either commute by bike or transit. As of late our transit system hasn’t been the safest way to get around the city. I opted to try out getting a body cam in thre event anything unfortunately occurred I’d at least have some way of documenting the event while keeping my hands free. I picked this up and while it took me a bit to figure out how to navigate the menu once I did the cam was amazing. I can articulate the lens to point forward straight up or back towards me (vlogger style). It’s small enough that it’s relatively noticeable. The screen while small allows for playback on the device itself which it’s a welcome addition. The ONLY strike against this cam is the gold screw point on the clip. It sticks out against the black body of the cam and draws peoples eyes to the cam. Now to be clear I’m not recording people for nefarious purposes however I would prefer that part be blacked out so as to allow more discreet carrying options. Other than that this cam is great decent photo/video/night vision. And the sound on playback is surprisingly loud for such a small cam. All in all definitely worth a buy if you can get over the gold screw point.

title: You don’t need to be a cop to use body cams!
text: [[VIDEOID:ee99d8a345601f7d7ea29edf87624595]] I got myself a bodycam because I believe it’s a useful too for Civilians as well as LEO’s. This particular body cam is GREAT quality has good sound and some extra little features such as password locks and badge # (LEO’s specific but you can assign yourself a number through the menus). Now this cam is a FULL-SIZE body cam meaning it’s about the same size as LEO’s wear. If you’ve seen LE wearing a body cam they’re VERY Obvious. So if you’re looking for a discreet cam this isn’t it. Now with that said the options allow you to use a “stealth” mode where there’s no sound from menus, key entry or power on/off. It has incredible night vision mode as well as a flashlight and emergency mode. At this point I suppose you’re wonder what the hell does a Civilian need with those functions. Well…I can’t speak for everyone but what I can speak to is life happens car accidents , random drunks etc. having a way to document these things could be a life safer because memory isn’t the greatest when something wild occurs. I’ve used this for a hiking trip to help remember which path I’ve taken. As a dash cam (there’s a mode for that also). And as an additional part to my plate carrier. Bottom life it’s an amazing cam and I will likely order a few more for other purposes.

As for the device, it has a quick retrieval time when accessing your queue. The remote is small and uses radio waves, not infrared. This means you do not need to point the remote at the device, like most TV remotes, and the box can be hidden with the rest of your entertainment center wires.
All of this, and a free app called Twonky, which allows you to beam videos from your tablet/smartphone to your Roku, makes this device a must have for your entertainment needs.

title: Don’t buy it from this site
text:
I liked the watch however Amazon dropped the price $42 less than 5 days after I got it from them. Amazon refused to refund the price difference so I returned it.

Battery life was awful even when I removed numerous apps from it and turned off numerous notifications.

The watch itself? I also decided I didn’t need that big of an electronic nanny measuring how long I washed my hands, when I needed to take deep breaths, etc so I decided to not buy it at all.

Simply not for me.

title: Big, functional and serious
text:
This is a BIG & heavy watch which is what I was looking for. After owning Fitbit and Samsung smart watches I wanted something more functional and practical.

This was it... The Fenix 5X sapphire model. I don't care about touchscreens so this model lacking one was fine. The battery normally lasts 4+ days - not too bad coming from Samsung and Fitbit but still a tad low for a watch without a touch screen. All of the typical notifications are present along with a pulse oxygen measuring system. There are apps for rowing, biking, golfing, etc. It is hefty - you will notice it on your wrist but not a problem for me.

title: Description of pulse oxygen measuring isn't complete
text:
Not what I expected... From the description I thought I would get all day pulse oxygen measuring however it will only measure during sleep or for altitude acclimation. Battery life is very good, the monochrome screen is OK.

I prefer a color screen and all day pulse oxygen measuring.

Decent but not for me.

title: Poor battery life, feature rich
text:
If only the battery life was better... I have the GPS turned off and I only measure my blood oxygen level when I'm asleep yet it is nearly impossible for the watch to last a little more than 24 hours.

My next Garmin will be the one with a solar powered assist.

That being said for the negatives this watch has the features I wanted at a good price:

- Sleep quality/quantity
- Blood oxygen level
- Steps counter
- Flight of stairs counting
- Water intake recording ) manual input)
- Multiple activities recording (it can detect when I'm running, bike riding, etc.)

It has been durable and the screen is still scratch free.

If poor battery life isn't a deal breaker buy it.

title: Not durable... Design flaw
text:

I initially thought the angled connection would be a plus however that turned out to be a minus. The angled connection will now not seat securely inside the devices.

title: iPad Pro 11... Fantastic tablet!
text:
I’ve been a huge anti-Apple products person for a long time... I don’t like the iPhones and stayed away from their tablets.

I was promoted recently and was issued an iPhone XR. I’m impressed with the ease of using apps on it but think it is rather pedestrian when compared to my OnePlus 7 Pro. However when it came to buying a premium tablet I had been nothing but disappointed with Android tablets (I have Google and Samsung versions at home).

Neither seemed user friendly and were always terrible on battery life and speed.

After much research I bought an iPad Pro 11... this is a great piece of technical engineering! From the outstanding battery life, beautiful screen, app integration, picture quality, LTE connectivity and speedy performance I have never used any Android tablet that comes close to how great this iPad is!

From the small footprint of iOS on the hard drive to its graceful line this is a well thought out workhorse that is equally at ease for fun! My only quibble is the lack of a scrolling screen however everything I’ve thrown set it so far it has handled with ease!

I’m installing Office 365 on it today- Apple, I may not like your phones yet I love your iPad Pro 11!

title: Simple is good.
text:
I am not the target demographic for this device: middle-aged empty nester who loves to watch sci-fi, thrillers, and horror. I have a number of these brilliantly simple, highly configurable lights. They are perfect in the bedroom where, depending on our intended mood, a variety of different colors or modes might be appropriate. I have two in the living room, hiding behind tropical plants at a 3' height, on either side of the big screen, about 5 feet away on each side. I have a routine set up to turn off all the lights in the room and engage campfire mode in both lights at 45% brightness with a single keyword. Voila--instant torchlight in the jungle (or romantic candlelight - take your pick). I am a colossal LOST fan, and this lighting is perfect for watching LOST, or anything scary or dark. And if I need a different effect, that's only a few words away.

The simplicity with which these set up and configure themselves is so good it makes Apple products jealous. If you have an Alexa on your Wi-Fi network, simply plug the Glow in to a power source, open the Alexa app on your phone, and the light will auto-connect to your network and add itself to Alexa. It will then prompt you to configure it with a name and add it to any groups, etc. Utterly simple. If the setup fails, it might ask you to scan the barcode on the back of the booklet it came with to get it going, but this has not been my experience - they have all self-configured and join the network seamlessly.

For those of you complaining this does not have a mic and speaker - folks, it works WITH an Echo device. It is a light - that's it. If Amazon built Alexa mics and speakers into this it would cost double--and I am positive they are developing just such a light ...for which you will pay $60+.

Normally, these are $30/ea, but they were 45% off on Prime Day, so I added a few more. There are indeed cheaper (and much more expensive) smart mood lights on the market, but if you run Alexa at home, this is hands down the best way to do it. Seamless.

It baffles me that Amazon does not have a whole range of lighting products which work exactly like this. They easily could. Give me one of these on a larger scale (12-15") and make it weatherproof for outside on the patio, please.

title: Decent dashcam for the price, a pain to configure, not the image quality I expected
text:
For the price this is hard to beat. It has lots of great features, including a Wifi app, but resolution/quality even on the highest settings are slightly disappointing. I have everything configured to provide the sharpest possible image (highest resolution and bit rate, etc.), and if a car is more than 30' away, zooming in on a screenshot of a license plate is iffy at best, even if the footage was taken in bright daylight (screencaps taken in VLC). Something seems off to me. Yes, I removed the protective films, and yes, my window is reasonably clean (normal conditions). I have attached two photos: one of the unit in a fantastic little case I found for it (see below), and a screencap showing the problem I described. The van in front of me is semi-readable, and was about 25 feet away. The car 15-20 feet further away on the left is unreadable, as is the plate close to me on the left. And yes, I have the CPL filter installed on the lens.

Configuring this was a bit of a hassle. The Wi-Fi app is not intuitive, and some quick googling led me to discover you have to temporarily disable your cellular data the first time you use it to get the camera to connect. Once configured, the camera itself acts as the network your phone connects to. This means your phone cannot be connected to any other Wi-Fi network while you are connected to the camera. I have no idea why they don't just allow you to use Bluetooth for this--it would be simpler to set up, that's for sure. Honestly, having integrated security video will be a factor in the next car I purchase. This is all way too much work.

Many PCs will not play the default file format this records in as they lack the correct video codec (H.265) or enough processing power. I think there must be a way to change the format it records in, but I was unable to find the configuration setting to change in either the app or the camera itself. To get this to play files on your PC, I suggest using VLC Player. It is free, and if you are running the latest version (check for updates in the application), it will run them just fine if your PC has the juice for HD at this level. If you experience dropped frames or choppy video when playing back on your computer, this is probably because your computer is not equipped with a GPU to support this high resolution of video (many aren't; if you don't have a dedicated video card in your PC, you may experience this). My office desktop does not have a dedicated video card and the video is a bit choppy if other things are running--expected.

If you are interested, the case is the "Mchoi Hard EVA Travel Case for Garmin inReach Mini GPS", (ASIN: B08F9QV1BQ), which is very sturdy and cost me $13.49 in Feb 2021. I looked for EVER for a case for this, and this was the best fit I found.

title: A great value, love the SFF chassis, needs better packaging
text:
*UPDATED*

Update after living with this PC for half a year: Zero problems, fast, and works perfectly for my application (business use). And excellent value. VERY pleased with this purchase.
---

The PC itself seems to be a great value, and is working fine thus far. The system is plenty fast. The HDD is a bit busy/noisy, and spins a bit more than it should, as though the system is caching to disk constantly. I'm not doing anything demanding with it at all--just light MS Office use and surfing. That's it. No gaming, no video editing, nothing heavy. Note this system is intended for business use, and could not handle much in the way of gaming or video editing, as it has no video card. The on-board graphics use the system's RAM, so anything asking a lot from the system's limited graphics capabilities will slow the entire system down immensely. Luckily, I outgrew DOOM years ago.

The SFF case is heavy, but oddly a bit flimsy, with more flex than I had expected for the weight--especially the back panel--mine was oddly bent outward. I pushed it back in/straightened it (I had to in order to plug things in--the plugs were deeply recessed due to the bent real panel--very odd). The chassis itself is a joy to work with though, as the case pops open on hinges without turning a single screw--not even a thumbscrew, and everything is very accessible. The HDD's working vibrations and sounds are amplified by the plastic subframe the drive is mounted in, which acts like an amplifier for the vibrations. I worry a bit that the system's small case will have cooling issues. There just isn't much room in there, and there is only one small 3" system ventilation fan (+ the power supply's fan, and a fan over the CPU). There are vents on the front and rear of the system, but I would like a lot more ventilation--I would have appreciated a perforated lid. Heat is the enemy of all electronics, and my other systems all have more ventilation than this box. Of course, this is an off-lease corporate desktop workstation, and is not designed to have the long life of other systems. The components in the box are the cheapest possible variants thereof, and I do not expect this system to last more than 3-4 years at the most. That said, $269 for a branded Lenovo PC with a 3.2GHz Intel Core i5, 12GB of RAM and a 2TB HDD is a fantastic value. If it dies in 3 years, I will have gotten my money's worth.

Important note about the packaging: it simply was not enough protection. I guarantee the system took some hard knocks on its way to me. The UPS driver actually dropped it at my feet from a height of 1'--not kidding! The system is not packaged in an inner box within the shipping carton--the carton IS the box. The small Styrofoam corner blocks used to float the system inside the box are unusually rigid, so much so that they provide little in the way of cushioning, and one of them had cracked in half--meaning the PC wobbled around in the box during shipping. Also, the carton was sealed with "Microsoft Certified Refurbisher" packing tape, making it clear to all it contained a PC. They need to change the packaging--a desktop system simply needs more/better protection than this. I half expected it to be DOA due to the abuse it took on the way here from Arizona.
