title: Serious (and odd) design flaw makes it uncomfortable to hold in your hand - not a good case for reading
text:
I looked at a lot of cases before selecting this one, and I am sad to say I am very disappointed in this purchase. I have an Omoton case for my Kindle PaperWhite. I really like the design of the shell--the way Kindle fits into on it, so I was trying to find something similar, where the entire unit is enclosed all the way around. This was the only case I found which appeared to fit this way, so I ordered it. Build quality is fine, and the Kindle does fit snugly in the case, providing the fit I was looking for. Unfortunately, there is a serious (and odd) design flaw in this case: a small lip that protrudes outwards and runs all the way around the edge of the unit.

This lip serves no purpose, and I do not understand why it was built into the design. I don't know why the lip did not register as a potential problem when I was making the decision to buy the unit--I suppose I thought it would be too small to matter. I was wrong. It matters. It is not an issue when you are not holding it: for example, using the tablet to watch movies and it is supported by the folded case on a flat surface (although this feels somewhat precarious/barely balanced). The issue is when you are holding the case in your hand and trying to read with your Kindle: the lip digs into your palm or fingers and after a few minutes becomes uncomfortable. You end up shifting the kindle to your other hand every couple of minutes. This is uncool, and makes what would otherwise be a great case almost unusable as a hand-held device. I thought about returning it, but given the hassle involved, I decided not to bother for a $12 unit.

I cannot recommend this case. If you plan on reading with this case (i,.e. holding it in your hand for any length of time), it will be uncomfortable (sure is for me anyway).

title: *UPDATED REVIEW* Will not automatically pair, on-board microphone disables the mics in my phone, and charges phone VERY slowly
text:
*UPDATED REVIEW*

A seller replaced a different defective FM transmitter unit with this one for me (mine has the Kollea brand name on it, but this is the identical unit, private-labeled). This is a better product than what it replaced, but is not without it's flaws. I have three (*UPDATE: now four, and the fourth one is a deal-breaker--see below) complaints with this unit:

1) It will not automatically reconnect to my phone about 75% of the time. I have to manually shut Bluetooth off and turn it back on on the phone, sometimes a few times before it pairs successfully. This is a hassle--a PITA. Every time I get in the car, I have to go through this process--every time power is cut from the transmitter, actually, so if your passenger knocks it and it pops out of the 12V socket, it will have to be re-paired, which is supposed to happen automatically, but does not, and you then have to go through the process. Frustrating.

2) Charge output is only 1.0A. this is why I returned the first one--phone gives a "slow charging" warning when charging from this unit, regardless of what USB cable I use (I tried four different cables, all of which I know for certain can carry 2.1A).

3) Callers have occasionally complained they cannot hear me well when using this unit, and I occasionally (but not often) encounter FM interference. I believe Bluetooth itself is part of the problem, and anyone who has used a few Bluetooth headsets or units like this knows audio quality is terrible. Period. We just deal with it. Add to that the burden of having to transmit your signal via FM to a car stereo and the user-side audio (what you will hear in your car) is always going to be craptastic.

4) (*UPDATE) When paired, voice recognition on my phone, which is usually quite good, becomes severely impaired. This is also likely the culprit for complaint #3, above. I suspect this is because when paired, it tries to use the built-in microphone for voice recognition instead of the microphones on my phone (of which there are 4). It is disabling the extremely good microphones in my phone (Nokia lumia Icon which is well known for having incredible audio input) and using the unit's crappy microphone instead. This microphone is located in the unit, which is attached to the center console of my car near the shifter, and thus picks up all the vibrations and related road and engine noise transmitted through the structure of the car as I drive. This approach is terrible. I have stopped using the unit for anything requiring voice input, including telephone calls. In other words, this is just a big awkward charger now, and one that charges painfully slowly (see complaint #2). If it were possible to disable the onboard mic, and use the mics in my phone instead for calls and voice recognition, this would be a much more serviceable unit As it is now, it is just a piece of junk.

Cannot recommend this item. There are definitely worse products out there. I have not tried them all, but of those I have used, this is the best one so far. I will likely keep using it until the lack of automatic pairing pushes me over the edge with it one day and I get something else. (*UPDATE: this thing just does not work well, and I am now looking for something else.)

title: If you are looking for a good AM radio, keep looking. Not well-made and performed poorly. Expected better from Sangean.
text:
I returned this radio--it simply was not very good at the job I bought it to do (picking up AM radio) and was poorly made. I bought it to listen to Los Angeles Dodgers ballgames on AM570. Simply put, this radio could not hold the station. AM570 is strong and clear on most other devices, but the Sangean, despite the other reviews, seemed to have terrible reception in my apartment, even near a window (I live in an interior unit in an apartment building--windows on the courtyard). It could not hold the station well, and there was a lot of interference no matter what I tried. At no time was I able to tune into AM570 with a clear signal--far too much noise. This is the only reason I bought the radio and it's inability to pick up AM570 rendered it useless. I replaced it with the [[ASIN:B012F0DGYE Sony ICFP26 Portable AM/FM Radio (Black)]], which performs a lot better and costs about $3 more. The Sony picks up and holds AM570 in my apartment perfectly, with no noise/hiss. The Sony is clearly the better product. It also looks much nicer--the Sangean SR-35 looks and feels like a cheap piece of crap. The Sony is actually a far more appealing, sleeker-looking device (I wish it were a bit smaller).

The second flaw was that the battery door would not stay closed. the little tab that clicks to hold it closed seemed too small or something (it was not bent). It just did not stay closed. Even if it had worked well (which it did not), this would have beeen enough to return it. it would literally have required a rubber band to stay closed. I was really disappointed with this radio--I had expected better, given Sangean's reputation. I cannot recommend this radio for AM use--get the Sony instead and save yourself the headache of returning it. (*I would like to thank Amazon for making the returns process so painless though!)

title: Better reception than the Sangean SR-35 for the same price
text: Got this little guy to replace the Sangean SR-35, which I returned because it got terrible reception. This is a much better piece of hardware. I live in a large building and my interior unit faces into the courtyard on the ground floor. This means reception can be an issue with some devices. I bought the Sangean (and replaced it with this) to listen to Dodger's radio (because you cannot listen to games online at all--terrible! Thanks for nothing iHeart Radio, and to the Dodgers for selling out--again). An AM radio was literally the only solution. Unlike the Sangean, the Sony is able to provide consistently good reception of AM570 without a fuss. The Sangean simply couldn't--there was too much interference and the reception seemed poorer. One can only conclude the radio itself on the board is superior in the Sony. Bonus: The Sony is a much better-looking unit (but neither looks like it would survive much of a fall). would be 5 stars if it were slightly smaller and a bit more durable.

title: Fantastic--best eReader I have tried (I've tried a lot). Text-to-speech capability from previous Kindles notably missing (why?).
text: OK, so the Kindle Paperwhite is pretty much the greatest thing ever. Seriously. Now I can sit outside in the dark on my patio at night and read without a big bright light which also attract insects. I wish the bezel surrounding the screen were a couple millimeters wider (I keep turning pages by accident), but otherwise this is an absolutely brilliant piece of gadgetry. I own three kindles, and this is my favorite by far. HOWEVER, there is one feature sorely missing from it, which is why I am hanging on to my Kindle Keyboard and Kindle DX: it will not do the text-to-speech trick. Why not?? This seems like the simplest thing ever to integrate, and if adding the speakers is too expensive, just give us a headphones port. Anyhow, I love this thing and I wish I had bought one ages ago. Oh--and I purchased it used (like new) from a seller on Amazon for $50, which makes it an excellent value.

title: Did my homework - decided on this one - great decision so far
text: Did a lot of homework before selecting this case for my Paperwhite. The professional reviews out there placed the OMOTION case firmly at the head of the class in terms of build, features, and functionality. I bought it and have been extremely happy with the purchase. If this changes, I will update this review, but for now, I'm happy.

title: Love these--great sound and value, but what's with the flimsy cord?
text: I got these on sale for under $30. Love them. but I admit I hesitate to expect a long, healthy life for them. They sound genuinely excellent (unbelievably good for the price!) and are actually very comfortable (love the fabric for the ear pieces), but the cord is super-thin and flimsy-feeling. Unless it is a lot stronger then it looks & feels, I fully expect to accidentally get up one day with it plugged into my PC and accidentally rip it out of the headphones (at this price point you do not get removeable cords). This cord is only about 1.5mm in diameter and does not inspire confidence. Cord length is fine for most uses, despite other reviews stating the contrary--it's shortish, but at about 5' it's fine for me--I use it either sitting stationary, or connected to a device I am holding or carrying in my pocket. If these headphones had a tougher/removable cord, I would be perfectly happy. Note: Sennheiser really does conquer all--these were $26 (I think) and sound better than anything else I have tried lately (including Beats--terrible), including many sets costing much, much more.

title: Perfect
text: Bought this to protect my MS Surface RT. Love the feel of it, and it does a wonderful job. Lots of padding and is very soft. Interesting note: there was a water leak from the apartment above mine and this was laying on the counter with the Surface in it. The counter was flooded. The case absorbed water, leaving the Surface inside it only slightly damp. After leaving the Surface out with the kickstand open for two days, just to make sure it was dry, it booted up and worked fine with no indication of damage. The case took three days to dry and is now fine too. If the Surface had not been in the case, I am sure it would have been soaked and may not have survived. Also, I have another one of these cases I use for an Android tablet, and it works beautifully.

title: Love this case - exactly what I wanted.
text:
This case is exactly what I wanted: extremely durable shock-absorbing (read: drop-proof) protection without screen protection. Let me qualify that statement: I did *not* want screen protection. I love the pearl eink display on my graphite Kindle Keyboard, and it now has a big brother. I do not want a screen cover, as this would greatly reduce the screen's otherwise remarkable clarity, adding unwanted elements such as bubbles, surface scratches, and glare to the mix--no thank you. There is a reason I disliked reading on the iPad so much I gave it back (very reflective!). In fact, this OtterBox defender case came with a stick-on screen protector--no way. It would ruin that big, glorious pearl eink display.

A screen cover serves no purpose once you remove the device from your backpack/messenger/tote/briefcase for use. Assuming you transport your Kindle device safely in an appropriate sleeve (you put your other expensive electronic equipment--your laptop/tablet in one; your Kindle deserves the same amount of respect), the screen protector is completely unnecessary--the sleeve protects the screen during travel. THAT is when the screen needs protecting--when you are not using it, from the other goodies in your messenger bag/backpack (keys, pens, earbuds, and anything else rattling around in there). Yes, that's right--I'm talking about a Kindle in an Otterbox Inside a sleeve inside your briefcase. ...Inception-level protection. You got it. Better safe than sorry, right? What if they once again stop producing our beloved Kindle DX and something happens to yours? I do not want to have to replace my DX--especially if it has to be with a Fire device (5% the battery life, reflective, heavy, expensive--no thanks!). When you are holding your Kindle in your hand, reading, a screen cover only detracts from the experience.

What you see in my pictures is exactly what you get: a beefy, black rubber (not silicone--too easily torn; rubber is much stronger) form-fitting sleeve with an equally form-fitting outer plastic shell. Science geeks like me understand how this works, and just in case you are not one, here is the idea: if you drop your device onto the floor, the outer shell absorbs some of the impact energy generated by the device hitting the floor. It then disburses the remaining energy of the impact broadly into the rubber inner lining. The rubber lining then in turn disburses the now greatly-reduced impact energy into the device. In other words, by the time the force of the impact is filtered through two layers of protection, the second of which is very absorbent and resilient (rubber) the device inside absorbs little if anything of the original impact.

I feel very good about having my Kindle DX in an Otterbox Commuter. If I ever had one of those incredibly poorly-designed (read: seriously fragile) apple devices, such as an iPad or iPhone (which I do not, and am not ever likely to), it too would live in an OtterBox Commuter case. OtterBox = the best protection a device can get. I paid $18 including shipping for this. A great price, and worth much more in terms of peace of mind.

title: Returned immediately - should have read the reviews first
text:
I have gotten in the habit of checking the low-star reviews of items and because Amazon makes this product for use with their own Kindle DX device, I (lazily) did not bother. I foolishly assumed it would work just fine. So ...while I was waiting for my order to be delivered, curiosity got the best of me, and I checked out the 1 & 2-star reviews. *Whoops.* Turns out that this cover, which hooks directly into the Kindle DX on the left side with little metal hooks, puts a lot of strain on the front plastic shell of the Kindle DX, especially if you mistakenly open it up from the wrong side, which I am sure everyone does from time to time. Lots of users have reported the stress caused by the way this cover connects to the Kindle DX actually causing the Kindle DX shell to crack. No thank you. Not even willing to risk it. Returned, unopened. Bought another case.

(*Note/alternative suggestion: if you are lucky you might still be able to get one of the few remaining Otterbox Commuter cases for it here on Amazon. Otterbox no longer makes them, but if you hunt, you can find them around in small quantities. I got one for $12 + $5 shipping.)

title: This has an odd design flaw
text: Looks and feels very nice in the hand. Seems of decent quality, but the Kindle is held in with elastic which will eventually lose elasticity. The flaw I mention is the clasp: when there is no Kindle in it, an invisible magnetic clasp (as in embedded inside the product) holds it closed, making the front "stick" to the back. However, when the Kindle is in it, this clasp does nothing, and the unit does not stay closed. Not sure how wise it is to have a magnet in such close proximity to the Kindle either, but that is another story. Glad I got this for 50% off on a promo. Was a gift. So far so good.

title: Great strap, wish it were a little longer
text: I really like this strap a lot. Use it with my Panasonic Lumix DMC-LX7. I just wish it were a little longer (possibly adjustable?). The little pockets are exactly the right size to hold spare batteries! This is a super-tough strap, and may be overkill for my little compact-system camera, but I love it. The back is rubberized (three strips), and it holds the strap in place. If everything else in the world were made this well, I would be a happy camper. Worth every penny.

title: Much too large
text: This dust cover is much too large for the Brother HL-2270DW Laser Printer, with several inches of room on each side and in extra height as well. It fits like a an XL sweater on a medium-sized kid: baggy, wrinkly, and just sloppy everywhere. It is made for something considerably larger. (Note: the printer in the picture above is not a Brother HL-2270 series--it is larger and taller.) It also smelled quite repulsive when it arrived, so I aired it out outdoors for a couple days--helped. Then, of course, when I tried to use it on the printer it did not fit. Returned. May make my own.

title: Exactly what I expected--maybe a little better, even.
text:
I spent a long time hmmming and hawing over this purchase. I really wanted the OEM Panasonic case for my LX7, but at $65 here on Amazon, it was just too expensive. I compared the aftermarket cases for this camera and examined photographs closely. This was the winner for apparent quality and design. And it lived up to expectations.

I was worried that it would block some of the screen or controls in the back, but this is not an issue at all. This case fits almost perfectly (screw mount is slightly out of alignment with the hole on the bottom of the camera--but it works), and is of as high-quality materials as one can imagine, given that this is *not* a leather case. The prospective purchaser should be aware that the vast majority of the cases on Amazon for the LX7 are not real leather. You can tell a case is real leather on here if it costs a fortune. The real leather cases on Amazon are all >$50, and some are $100+.

For $15, this case represents an excellent value, as it fits pretty well, is well-made (sturdier than I expected!), and looks very nice. (I have the white LX7 and I bought the light brown case--the color of a well-worn baseball glove). One thing: as expected, the strap is made of vinyl, and looks it. I will likely be upgrading to a proper, padded camera strap though, so this is of little import, at least to me.

If you are on the fence, take my advice and go for it. This is a good value, and a decent case--especially for this price. I did, and I have no regrets.

Note: you will have to remove the case to access the battery/SD card compartment and the ports, as is the norm with all cases of this type for this camera (I was unable to find one that did not require this).

---

UPDATE: After several months of hard use, this case has held up remarkably well. No evidence of wear. I get compliments on it, as well. Note: Do not attach the camera to a tripod with the bottom of the case on. The knob on the case is threaded to allow you to do this, but getting it off the tripod mount afterwards is a nightmare. Just take it out of the case--trust me.

title: Excellent value laptop
text:
So , a while back (<1 yr) I did a whole bunch of research for a friend who needed a new laptop. Everything I read pointed to Asus, so we went that route. Everything worked out just fine, so when it came time for me to upgrade, I followed suit. I got this box, with a slightly faster processor and a 500GB HDD for $299 on sale elsewhere two weeks ago. Happy with it thus far. The keyboard layout is a little unusual, and definitely takes some getting used to. Battery life is excellent, and even at the dimmest setting, the screen is totally fine indoors. I wish it had another USB port, and the lack of Bluetooth seems silly (I miss it though). Built-in cameras is not great, but for Skype, its just fine. Love how quiet this thing is. Yet to feel any heat from it. Happy camper.

---
UPDATE: After using this for a while now, I can safely say it is a great laptop except for one, glaring fault: the keyboard is terrible. Worst layout I have ever had on a laptop. Makes me want to replace the laptop. If only this was not a problem... *sigh*

title: My world is forever changed; or how I learned to relax and love the box.
text:
This is ridiculous. Never before have I ever gotten so much joy from an electronic gadget (and I'm a gadget NUT). After renting from Netflix for YEARS, I finally got a Roku box for Xmakkah from my girlfriend, who shall henceforth be worshiped as a god. I LOVE it (and yes, her too!). I have only two complaints, neither of which has anything to do with the Roku box itself, but rather the service I receive from Netflix.

1) Netflix desperately needs to step up the selection of available streaming content. The vast majority of the 20K titles currently available are old, unloved, and largely undesirable. Sure there is some decent content, but nowhere near enough of it. A good example of this is TV: I can Watch Dexter, LOST, and Heroes, but not Survivor, X-Files, or The Sopranos. I can watch the Old Battlestar Galactica, but not the new one. I can watch Masters of Horror, but not The Twilight Zone. You get the idea.

2) Video quality degrades when other devices are used that eat up bandwidth. I use my broadband cable connection for everything except my microwave oven. Seriously: telephony (Vonage), Internet access, online backup, and Roku. If I am watching something on the Roku box and I answer the phone, the resolution on the screen drops dramatically and the audio quality on the call is terrible. You get the picture (pun intended)...

Oh, and I have one more issue, although this is not really an issue--more of a request: Roku needs to greatly expand the channel store!!! YES PLEASE!!

Setup was a breeze and I was watching a movie in less then 10 minutes (and 9 of those minutes were the Roku box connecting to Roku itself and registering/updating firmware). :o)

Get one of these.
Trust me.
Best thing I got for Christmas by a mile.

title: Buyer beware--lens mechanism problems
text:
This camera was highly recommended from a very trusted source, and the reviews were mostly positive. I expected a lot from it, and for a brief period, (maybe 4 months) it worked well. Then the problems began. Lens errors. Yes, despite Canon's insistence that this sort of thing "never" happens, the mechanical lens error you will read about in other people's reviews (known issue with this camera) of this camera happened to me. I bought it hoping they wouldn't, but alas, I am apparently a sucker. Next time, I shall heed the warnings of my fellow Amazonites. No more Canon products for me....

As time wore on, the lens error became more and more of a problem. After another three months, I called Canon. The (arrogant) tech support guy just said, "Oh, this happens when the batteries are weak."

"Oh really?" I said, unwrapping a new set of Energizer AA's. "Let me just stick these puppies in here and see what happens... Huh. Well, would you look at that. So much for your battery theory pal."

After embarrassing him thusly, his only "solution" was to send the camera in for Canon to look at it (at my expense). This would take a minimum of six weeks, after which there was no guarantee I would not continue to have the same problem with the camera. I mean, come on--a design defect is a design defect, after all. I was certainly not the first person to have this problem with this camera. Not only that, but no camera for SIX WEEKS?? I would not have survived.

Sadly, before I could pack the thing up and send it in, I dropped it from the staggering height of three feet. You guessed it, end of camera. Canon makes cheap crap with poor durability and cheap lens mechanisms.

So guess what I did? Yup, I bought myself a Nikon. I've had three of them with ZERO problems over the years. This is number four. My replacement is working beautifully, and is smaller to boot. Excellent image quality too. I will not buy a Canon again. Fool me once, it's your fault. Fool me twice, it's mine.

Buyer beware.

title: If it sounds to good to be true...
text:
...it probably is. I would be well served to remember that before buying stuff next time. This thing was just so tiny I had to have it. And for the first 2 weeks it worked ok. Not great, just OK. Then the talk time began slipping... then the static began... then people started telling me they couldn't understand me. Then it stopped working completely. Less than 3 weeks old and already headed to the trash. What a waste.

I've made up my mind: with bluetooth headphones, you get what you pay for. I'm going for a Jawbone 2, spending the extra cash on it, and I have no doubt in my mind it will be everything the reviews say it is. Enough Samsung garbage. Should have known. There are no other Samsung products in my home, and nor will there ever be.

Matt

title: Quick & dirty
text:
This is going to be quick--I only have a minute. However, as an avid point & shoot hobbyist, I wanted to contribute my $0.02 worth in on this magnificent little gem. Small, simple, and almost goof-proof, this is an ideal inexpensive camera for anyone just getting started. No optical viewfinder, managable file sizes, and the typical unbeatable Nikon lens mean you get serious bang for your buck with this camera. Full auto works well, and easy access to simple manual control over the basic parameters of the capture process mean it is easy for anyone to make minor adjustments. Also, there are (I think) 16 or 20 custom auto modes, including fireworks, black & white, etc.

HUGE plus: this camera runs on AA batteries. Spend about $25 once on a charger and two sets of high-capacity rechargables (2600miAh), and you will be all set. Regular Energizers are good for 100+ shots with the flash. The rechargables I bought are good for easily 250+ on a charge. MOney VERY well spent.

For your dollar, this is a hard camera to beat--and what makes it great is that it's a Nikon--these people know lenses... and TRUST ME, it's all about the optics. Nikon simply rules in that dept, IMHO.

title: Nice but very fragile
text:
I got one of these for the holidays last year (12/06) and I was totally stoked. This was my first iPod--what a shame that it turned out to be such a fragile, poorly engineered device. I mean, this thing got dropped once from about 2.5 feet (it was only 2 months old) and it was TOAST (and it was in a plastic hardshell case!). I have had Laptops that survived worse. Come to think of it, I've had a lot of (far cheaper) devices that are better able to take abuse than this $400 item--including TV remotes, cell phones, Nintendo Game Boys (designed to be nearly indestructible), OTHER MP3 PLAYERS, etc. It seems that a physically appealing design does not necessarily equate to superior engineering--quite the opposite in this case. I do like it, and the replacement I got from Apple works very well. It's great looking and it does the job well. Too bad I'm so terrified of dropping it that I had to buy a big, bulky silicone case to improve its chances of survival. Let me tell ya, in its crash-test-dummy outfit, it no longer looks even the slightest bit sleek.

Have you ever dropped your keys when getting out of the car? Your cell phone? If you answered yes to either of the above, then you can probably expect to drop your iPod one day. I hope you have a (thickly) carpeted garage--or that it lands on your foot. Bottom line: If I were thinking of getting an MP3 player, iPod or another brand, it would have zero moving parts; on other words, I would buy a flash-based device instead of one with a hard drive.

I also cannot help but wonder why Nintendo does not take what they have learned about building child-proof, nearly indestructible portable gaming devices and apply this to a worthy competitor to the iPod. I would be the first in line...

I gave this product 3 stars because it does a good job of what it is touted to do: play MP3s & video/images. In fact, the user interface, including the GUI and the click wheel is one of the nicest, most intuitive designs I have ever seen on a piece of consumer electronics equipment. Too bad it's put together so cheaply. Grossly overpriced? Most definitely. I hope the iPhone turns out to be a higher quality piece.

---

UPDATE: 8/2013: still working fine... :)

title: My 4x4 iPod
text:
This thing is genuinely neat. I got the black one for my black 80GB video iPod. I had to laugh when I (finally) got my iPod into this thing (no easy feat, let me tell you!): it looks like an iPod wearing a piece of an offroad 4x4 tire--which is just fine with me. It also makes me think of something you might see in Doom3 or Halo... totally rugged and "futuristic". This is a sci-fi fan's iPod case. I have not dropped it (yet), so I cannot attest to any protective qualities it may have, but the silicone is very thick and (reassuringly) strong. Do not try this at home, but I am reasonably sure it would bounce around if I dropped it. I removed the beltclip anchor as I would never use it (I cannot imagine myslf hanging a $[...] piece of hardware on my hip attached by a flimsy piece of plastic that reportedly breaks anyway. Nope, my ipod's travel plans will consist strictly of into and out of the briefcase (or jeans pocket).

Incidentally, you may be interested to know that I bought this case to replace one of those clear acrylic hinged ones that did nothing for my last iPod when I dropped it (may it rest in pieces). No kidding--my friends, you do NOT want to drop an unprotected iPod, and the form-fitting clear case I had for my last iPod may have protected it from scratches, but it offered zero crash protection. I learned my lesson, and this one should do a nice job of both.

title: Nicest USB Hub I've found
text: This is exactly what I needed to tame the mess of USB cables surrounding my PC. What I like best about it is the fact that it is WEIGHTED. This means is does not slide around all over the place on your desk like other (lightweight) hubs do. It's small (about the size of 1/2 a large Florida orange or a small grapefruit) and it offers all the features I wanted: weight, lots of ports (7) and LED port-in-use indicators for each port. the top-mounted port is nice too; great for plugging in and removing things frequently such as flash drives. This is one of the best PC gadgets I have bought in some time. Oh--and the free light that comes with it is a neato bonus. Highly recommended.

title: The Lexus of wheeled backpacks
text:
My son went through 4 decent backpacks last year (grade 4), including a tough-looking Samsonite (lasted 2 months). This rugged contraption (and a little extra care) is the solution. This is the first and only wheeled backpack that has stood up to the abuse he gives it. Also, this unit seems bottomless: it holds far more than you might expect. This is a very well engineered backpack and therefore highly recommended. Go ahead and by cheaper ones ...you'll eventually end up with a JanSport like we did. Just wait for a decent sale price...

---

Update: My son did manage to destroy this in less than one school year.

title: Solid
text: Much better than a wifi adapter for gaming and watching live streams, BUT, for whatever reason Youtube is almost unusable. Constant buffering and can barely watch videos at 1080p. This may be because my router is in the basement (1st floor), and I am on the third floor so it has to travel. but if that was the case wouldn't live steams lag more? anyways its perfect for gaming and and streaming, and for now I switch back to my wifi adapter when using youtube, and back to the powerline ethernet when playing games.

title: No more surprise knockd
text: Love these.  I now know if someone is coming to my door before they are standing at the door.  I have one set to say “front door” and the other “drive way”. No longer wondering if a delivery has been made and if so which door did they leave it at.  Highly recommend.

title: I highly recommend.
text: I love this tote.  My husband always puts his stuff in my purse when we are going anywhere together. He’ a diabetic so he always has his blood glucose monitor and candy incase of low blood sugars.  He also has a notebook with his medical info in that he takes when going to appts so I can put all of that plus my stuff in it.  I’ve been using it now a a couple of months and it holding up really well.

title: Holds great.
text: Love these clips for keeping small cords/cables in place and out of the way.

title: Great product
text: Installed the RV TV Wall Mount in my camper.  It was easy to install and the range of motion is great for our camper bedroom.  It locks easily when the TV is pushed back against the wall.  It is also easy to unlock  when you want to move the TV for viewing.  We have not traveled in the camper since installing the wall mount so hopefully it will holdup to expectations.  Will update if there are problems it after traveling.

title: Great product, awesome warranty!
text: I love Anker cables. I have about a half a dozen of these in our house, and until two weeks ago not one failed.  One of them eventually had a contact worn down and my iPhone wouldn't charge.  I contacted support through their website, and they quickly processed my replacement.  After getting burned on many other cables on Amazon, I will only buy Anker from now on since they honor their warranty!

title: Five Stars
text: Seems to work fine with my new MacBook Pro and CF cards.

title: Works
text: Works perfectly with Time Warner, and cheaper than renting a modem from them.  Not sure why more people don't buy their own.

title: Great antenna
text: Free HDTV, can't beat it.  We are picking up channels from 55 miles away and they all come in crystal clear.  It's easy to assemble.

title: As advertised
text: Coax cable came as advertised, not much else to say. I would purchase again if I needed another cable in the future.

title: Disappointed...better adapters out there
text: If you are looking for an inexpensive adapter for American to European these may work for you.  They will not work if your American plug has one "fat" prong and one thin one (for polarity).  If your American plugs have two thin prongs then it will work.  Also, I put one of these in the standard European 3 plug strip and it got stuck.  They work ok when plugging straight into the wall, but aren't well suited for the plug strips.  I no longer use these and have transitioned to the more expensive grounded adapters (~$5ea) [[...]] that work for all types of American plugs (2 and 3 prongs, as well as the 2 prongs with one thick one).

title: Great clips
text: I am currently renting, and don't want to limit how many holes I put in the walls, so I bought these cord clips to run a cable around a doorway. title: Easy plug and play.  Excellent audio quality
text:
I have had the Topping D10s DAC for about 3 weeks. It has proven to be a high quality DAC .
This is my current configuration:
PC -> DAC via usb
DAC -> headphone amp or AV receiver via RCA cable, or to second DAC via Digital COAX or Optical Toslink

The resulting audio is far superior using this DAC, compared with plugging my PC audio out directly into either my headphone amplifier or AV amplifier.
When using a DAC, the audio is much cleaner and there seems to be better channel separation. The DAC does not enhance the audio signal at all. There is no high, mid, or low end over amplification. The audio out is the same as the audio in, and that's the way it should be.

I have used other DACs and the Topping D10s is a good as the others

I highly recommend this product.

title: Excellent headphones for those who know what they're looking for
text:
It's "almost" (see my edit below) impossible to find a negative review of the Audio-Technica ATH-M50x Closed Back Headphones. And I have to agree. Probably the best headphones I've ever owned. They've been available now for 10 or so years. You can't get this high end quality audio anywhere else for this price point. I got an excellent deal. The headphone purchase also included 3 high quality extra items for just about the same price as the headphones alone. My package included an extra cable, a solid hard plastic carrying case, and a FiiO A1 headphone amplifier.
The headphones live up to all the positive reviews, and the extras included made for a very good total price.
I would definitely recommend this product.
Updated 2/4/2021, 4 months later.
I still love these headphones. I have to laugh when I occasionally check the customer reviews and find that most of the criticisms are based on how these headphones were purposely engineered. Let me be more specific. Some of the negative comments include:
-others around you can hear what you're listening to. Oh well. Too bad. They should probably put on their own noise cancelling headphones. Which brings me to my next point:
-they're not noise cancelling. Yup, that's right. When I did my search for headphones, I specifically did NOT want noise cancelling OR Bluetooth. Much prefer putting the money saved when not buying these options and putting it toward better cans.
-there is no microphone on the cables. Correct again. These headphones were not necessarily intended for those who want a set of cans primarily to support their cell phone addiction.
-they must be used with the company's proprietary cables to attach to the headphones. I'll take that and love it. Why? Because they twist and lock into the bottom of the can. How many times, with other headphones, have I moved too far, or stood up or whatever, and the cord would be ripped out of the cans!!
-too much bass, not enough base. Midrange too pronounced, or not enough. And they go on and on and on.
-the "best" (tongue in cheek) criticism stated that none of the included cables, nor the included adapters fit his computer. I don't know what kind of a computer this person has, but, if Bill Cosby appears in TV commercials for your computer, headphones should not be your #1 focus right now
-and finally, and I quote, "I needed to add an EQ to make them sound like I wanted them to". Precisely! These cans were designed and manufactured specifically for those who are looking for an accurate, unadulterated representation of the original recording. The way the musicians and the recording engineers intended it to sound. If one doesn't find that acceptable, and that's fine, include an EQ somewhere in the mix. As a matter of fact, I have more than my share of sound shaping hardware and software all over my system in order to tailor the music to my liking.
You need to like the sound quality reproduced through headphones and speaker systems alike. And this is very subjective. One person's likes are another person's hates, especially when it comes from those who love to sound like they "might" know what they are talking about.. I bought and returned a number of headphones because I didn't care for how they sounded. I kept these.
I do agree with one common complaint. The earpads do get uncomfortable after a while. I checked for aftermarket replacements, but many included their own negative reviews that they changed the sound quality from the originals. That's the last thing I want.

All in all, sizing is fine. They key placement and distance between keys works fine. I do run into issues at times where my fingers get lost on the right side of the keyboard. Getting used to that will come in time though. The key response is quick. They are mechanical switches but they do manage to deaden the sound a bit which is nice. The RGB features are basic at best. You have a few settings you can select from and all of it is done directly on the keyboard itself. It has your normal basic modes. It illuminates well though and you can increase/decrease the brightness. The build quality is nice. For being a 75% keyboard, it has some weight to it. I like the fact the keys are labeled for both Mac and PC. I primarily use it on my PC though. The place where it seems to shine is in the connectivity department. I can connect it by bluetooth to numerous devices or I can have it wired. I generally run wired to my main PC and if I need to use it on my MacBook or other devices, I just unplug it from the PC and connect by BT to the other device. It works out nicely.

From a gaming standpoint (which I do a lot of), I'm not certain that I like it as much yet. Emphasis on the "yet". I know it takes some time to become accustomed to a new keyboard. The response and feel. I'm going to continue gaming on it for a while to see if I become more adapted to it. It just feels different than what I'm used to. It most likely has to do with the key spacing more so than anything else.

This is definitely a nice keyboard and I recommend it. I will most likely continue to use it as my daily keyboard for a while longer to see how it holds up over time.

title: Nice band but could be better
text:
I've always leaned more towards this style band and this one is decent. It's definitely worth the price point, however there are some minor issues compared to other bands of this style that I have. The cuts in the metal, particularly on the sides, are not rounded off or smoothed. On my wrist, this makes it feel a little rough at times. It's not something I pay much mind to, but I do notice it occasionally. Other bands of this style, that I have, seem a little more rounded or smoothed out. They feel a bit more comfortable in that regard. The band does fit the watch face perfectly. Installation was a breeze. I did not have to adjust the length of my band so I can't speak to how easy/hard that is. The locking clasp works fine. Again, you can see/feel the difference between this clasp and pricier versions of these bands, but it gets the job done.

All in all, this is a decent band that's well worth what it costs. I'd definitely recommend it to someone looking for a replacement band for this watch if they were trying to stay more budget conscious.

title: Works but not for what I was hoping...
text:
This product is very easy to use. Setup is simple and in most cases I'm sure it works great. Particularly with remotely playing videos and whatnot. Or using it as a means of a screen share. My intent was a little more involved and I wanted to use it for gaming on my TV from my laptop. Everything was going smooth until I actually attempted to play a game. That's when you notice the deficiency in the product. I had attempted a few different games and the results were the same for all. The video lag was atrocious. The motion blur made games impossible to play effectively. The delay between actions and response on the screen was pretty long.

If you're looking for a means to cut out the HDMI wires to a display, and you have no intent of doing anything graphically intense, such as gaming, this product works great. If your intent is to use it for gaming purposes, you may want to stick to wired.

title: Works just as good as more expensive brands
text: I was a little leery about these SD cards because they have competitors beat in price by a fair amount.  The phrase, "you get what you pay for" kept crossing my mind.  I decided to make the purchase because I needed a couple cards for some of my cameras and I have to admit, I'm impressed.  No issues to report and they just work.  I'll definitely use this brand moving forward providing the cards stay stable and fast.  If you're worried about them not working because they cost so much less than the counterparts, don't worry.  I've yet to have an issue.

title: Great for the price, but...
text: These earbuds are great for their price, however I don't know that they deserve so many accolades that they're receiving through reviews here or on other sites.  There is nothing spectacular about them.  Sound quality is average.  Nothing like you'd find in much higher end (and higher priced) IEMs.  Comfort can be subjective.  What is comfortable to one person may not be comfortable to the next.  I personally prefer foam inserts but with that being said, these are relatively comfortable.  If you're looking for a cheap pair of earbuds, these will fit the bill.  If you're looking for something with higher end sound quality, you may want to move on.

title: Less filter choices does not always mean less quality
text: So I have a few ND filter sets for my mini 3 from various vendors, some great, some not so great.  I've not been disappointed with this set of filters.  There are less steps provided than some other offerings out there but that doesn't mean the quality is less.  They are staggered nicely and give you filters for every situation.  Why pay more for filters you'd never use.  The case they come in is nicely built and I'm confident the filters are protected while in it.  Image quality is fine.  I see no adorations or degradation to the image when using these.  If you're looking for more advanced filming techniques and blurring your motion, these filters will do the job for you.

title: Does what I need it to with no issue
text:
So I'll first start by saying I've yet to actually plug this into my PC. So I can't review it based on it's connectivity there. I've used other USB hubs and generally they're "okay" at best because you're obviously sharing the full speed of one USB port across multiple ports. The more ports the hub has and devices you have plugged into those ports, the more degradation you're going to see. I prefer USB hubs that also have their own power supply. This one does not. It has a neat little feature where you can turn on/off each port by a switch next to the port. Not entirely sure how useful that would be since typically if you have something plugged in, you'd most likely want it on, but maybe in the case of a webcam or something you may want that ability to just turn it on/off vs unplugging it.

I personally use this USB hub more as charging hub. I basically have it plugged into a wall outlet with an adapter just charge multiple devices off of it. Saves me from having multiple wall adapters and power strips. For that purpose I love this hub.

title: Great little watch...but...
text:
I love this watch but I do have some issues which usually sway me from wearing it all the time. When I first got it and saw the band style, I knew right off the bat I was probably going to have a couple issues. I was right. These bands (silicone maybe) typically cause my skin to get a rash. Not every watch band like this will but when things cost less, I find it typically does. I like that it continually reads your body metrics so I don't want to take it off. I'll wear it all the time, including in the shower, until the rash starts. Then I have to take it off for a few days. The bands do look replaceable but they don't say what other bands they're compatible with.

The other gripe I have with it is the accelerometer (I assume) being used to determine when you raise the watch to look at it. It's spotty at best. Often times I'll raise my wrist to look at the screen and it will not turn on. I will have to turn it on by the button. Other times it will be overly sensitive and turn on whenever it feels like it. Maybe it's just my device but I was really hoping that feature would work better. I like the idea of raising my wrist and the watch face turning on.

The app connectivity is nice and the tracking of all your stats is nice. The ability to customize what shows on the main screen as well as changing your watch faces is great as well. It really is a nice watch. If I can find a band that is better, I would wear this thing all the time but I get so irritated by the rash that develops. If you don't have that issue with silicone bands, then by all means, this is a great little watch.

title: A lot better than buying cans of air

Using it in the workshop when I need to blow sawdust off of a project.  It's been great.  If I had to complain about something I'd say it's awkward in shape and weight but other than that I've yet to have a problem with it.  It does make me wish it operated off rechargeable batteries though.

title: Wish it worked better
text: I've had nothing but problems with this extender.  I'll first start off by saying I do work in an IT field, so it's not lack of expertise in the area.  The device just fails to deliver.  I've mainly used it as a repeater in attempts to give a better signal to an outdoor camera but all too often the camera will lose connection to the device.  I've tried numerous devices through it and the connection / speeds have always been spotty.  Granted I could try running an ethernet cable to the device in attempts to create a better environment for it to succeed in but that was not the intent of it's use from the beginning.  All of these devices, including the outdoor camera, maintain better signals and connections to my WiFi router without the extender in the mix.  I, personally, would steer clear of this device unless I'm just unlucky and have a poor performing unit.

title: No issues to report and use regularly

So far so good and if you're looking for an adapter of this style, this one will fit the bill just fine.

title: Definitely not worth the price in my opinion...
text:
Maybe it's just the set I received, but on a few levels I can advise against these. For starters, the price.
I do not feel these are worth what they're charging. Although the filters look nice with the colorful trim, etc, that's about as far as I'd go with them. The case is okay. It's plastic and has a snap style latch to keep it closed. However, the filters just sit in foam. When I received mine and pulled them out of the box, all of the filters were out of their foam slots and just floating around in the case. After pushing them back into their foam spots, they seemed to hold in place. There's a lot more case than needed for the 6 filters so if you're trying to consolidate space, you may want to put them in something else.

The huge issue I have with all of them is how loose they fit the Mini 3 camera. Each one of mine can practically fall off. I'd understand if maybe one of them was super loose, but for all of them to behave the same it seems like a design flaw to me. I've used other brand filters that hold in place equal to that of the stock attachment but I'm afraid these are going to fall off too easily. Maybe not necessarily in flight since it's on a gimbal that accounts for turbulent air but I almost guarantee they'll fall off when fiddling around with the drone in your hands. A suggestion to the manufacturer would be to create a little more tension where they lock onto the camera like DJI and other brand filters do to prevent them from spinning back the very slight distance it takes for them to come off.

title: I am impressed but I feel for what you're getting the price could be cheaper
text:
I'll preface by saying I feel all companies that sell things like this charge more than they should. They're mini drone ND filters. We're not talking about a set of ND filters for a full scale DSLR here. Regardless with that being said, I do think you're getting a good product. They work as they're supposed to. Snap on to the drone securely and easily. The case they come in is nice. It's magnetically sealed which is awesome. Feels sturdy enough to know the filters will be protected in my bag or case.

If I were to give one complaint (and it's not really a complaint), I wish the company would have made the case a little taller. The filters are secured in place by the foam they sit on so it's not as if the lid is what's holding them in place. So if they were to make the lid a little taller, we could stick the stock DJI attachment in the case while the ND filter was on the drone. My biggest concern is losing the DJI attachment. It's just a suggestion. Certainly not a deal breaker on whether or not these are good filters.

title: It's fine...
text:
I'll preface by saying I do prefer the hand style straps where the padding goes around the back of your hand and if you let go it can hang from your wrist. I was just in need of a wrist strap and figured I would give this one a shot.

This wrist strap is fine. I can't really rave about it or complain about it. The price point is not terrible. I'd probably have valued it a little lower but I'd have said the same of any strap like this of similar quality. I already know by looking at it, in time the leather will undoubtedly separate like I've seen with similar wrist straps. I'm not entirely sure the purpose of the plastic clip. It's just as easy to remove the whole thing from the camera as it would be to unbuckle it. I also view that as potential point of failure where my camera could end up on the ground if the buckle wasn't secured properly, unbuckled, or something else went wrong.

Like I said, "it's fine". If it's the style you're after and you don't to spend a crazy amount of money on something as simple as a wrist strap, you'll be content.

title: Works just fine for my E422VA Visio TV
text:
The keyboard on the back of this remote makes searching on Amazon, Netflix and Hulu so much easier - no more having to navigate that onscreen "keyboard".

I was hesitant to purchase this item since it was not clear from the product description or from the Vizio website that this remote would even work with my model TV, which came with the VR17 remote. But I decided I would take a chance, and return if it it did not work.

The front of the remote contains three quick-access buttons for Amazon, Netflix and Vudu, and then all of the same keys found on the VR17 in the same positions, with one minor exception. The XRV1TV 3D is designed for use with a 3D TV, which mine is not. Where the VR17 remote has the "WIDE" key in the lower left corner position, this remote has a "3D" key. But that is not an issue for me, since I rarely use that function, and it is available through an on-screen menu anyway.

The one thing that keeps me from giving this remote a 5-star rating is that I find the remote a little awkward to hold and use without accidentally pressing a key on the reverse side. It takes some getting used to having to hold this carefully to prevent that happening.

For what it does, the Fire is a great little gadget at $139.00, but for my purposes, my Kindle 3 combined with my laptop is still a better option.

title: Center button is Power
text:
I want to kick this review off with a key point, as the title states, the center button on the front of the speaker is the power button. I didn’t read the directions to see if this was mentioned, I just charged it and struggled to power it on when it was charged.

Outside of that the sound quality and overall volume on this is great. When it first powered on, the automated voice had me concerned as it doesn’t sound clean, but it seems to be just how it was recorded.

I turned on a song and naturally had to crank up the volume to see what it could do. I was pleasantly surprised and it didn’t have issues with quality (sometimes speakers get louder in volume and it sounds like someone just singing closer and closer to a microphone).

This does include a short Aux cord (2 ft) and the charging cable (but no plug). The charging cable is USB C that goes into the speaker (but still plugs into a standard usb plug).

I am very pleased here!

title: Better than I thought
text:
I am really enjoying the sound quality from these as I needed to switch from a corded headset to something wireless. This is Bluetooth but the Bluetooth chip works well and doesn’t seem to have issue where it disconnects from my laptop and connects to my phone (I’ve had this with a few speakers).

The mic works great as I do user testing and the sound quality is important for good feedback as a tester.

I was pleasantly surprised to find out that the chip isn’t needed unless Bluetooth isn’t available on the device. There was no issue with connectivity either as my laptop recognizes the USB Bluetooth chip and automatically paired with the headset. A plus for me since my laptop tends to lag.

The headset has a good/decent look to it. The earpieces are squishy and comfortable. The headset adjusts easily. The plastic seems to be of decent quality so putting them on and taking off repeatedly should not be an issue. Very pleased overall.

title: Fantastic
text:
I bought this adapter because the other one I have always caused static and I’d have to turn my stereo up quite a bit to get the volume at a decent level.
I have had far less issues with static when this is plugged in while listening to the radio (weaker channels are always going to be an issue either way).
I am also able to turn the volume up about 25% less than with the other (knob was at 22 with other adapter and this one works well on 16 or 17).
Thoroughly pleased with this one and I got it because we are slowly moving toward the USB c style charging cables (as newer items seem to also be doing the same).

title: Great camera, cloud isn’t
text:
I liked the camera so much I bought the outdoor one as well.

This camera has motion detection that will follow the motion. It actually made my son nervous and thought someone was controlling it. I explained that it detects motion and follows that which is ideal should someone get inside the house.

The camera does have two way Audio that works well and only has a slight lag but is fairly clear.

I am able to monitor the cameras from the app but this is where the problem starts. The app is adjustable to some degree, the problem that I’ve explained to the manufacturer is they require each camera to have separate cloud storage at a separate fee per month. The cloud storage should be based on the account and total account cloud usage. This helps with better networking as well as retaining cloud activity in one central location. If the motion detection were capturing someone who did eventually make it inside, that sequence from camera to camera would be great if it all linked in one cloud account. The problem is that LongPlus has not done this and you pay separate fees per camera.

Not pleased but it is the only company I’ve seen that has an indoor camera and an outdoor camera (where the outdoor camera is battery powered).

title: Poor camera, poor cloud
text:
Update: arrived 4/16, installed after charging on 4/17. Died today on 5/3. Roughly 2.5 weeks of battery life.

I really enjoy the camera overall. It was easy to install the app using the QR code in the manual. Then following the manual to register the camera and have it read the QR code to register the camera to the account.

I wanted a camera brand that had both Indoor and Outdoor cameras but needed the outdoor camera to have a battery and found that in LongPlus.

There is a slight lag in the camera but the quality is solid.
The motion detection can be adjusted which is nice as it is fairly sensitive.

The big downside is regarding the future of the online world which is their cloud service. There is only a 7 day free trial, not 30 days (and nowhere to add a code to get the 30 days that is promised in the description). Outside of that, rather than having one cloud service payment per month, you pay for each camera. The cost saved appears to be made up with their cloud services costing money if you want a full network of cameras. Very disappointed by something so simple. There is no easy customer service portal for questions in the app, only app feedback (which I submitted but there should be an easy line of communication).

There are also many misspelled words within the app itself adding to the confusion and overall trust. I rarely have one star for my reviews but this is just really a simple fix on the LongPlus side.

title: So far so great
text:
We picked up this camera because we were getting a new puppy and needed to keep an eye on him during the day.

The clarity is pretty solid overall given the cost and can be seen in the photo above (which includes our little pup).

The camera can take snapshots which I am not able to save to my phone (or haven’t quite figured out how to save to my iPhone but they do save in the app).

I don’t really need this for motion detection but have tested that feature out as a just in case measure if we used in the future. The sensitivity can be adjusted but overall a very nice feature.

The camera does have a micro sd slot that would allow storage of footage (like movements) but we use the live footage as our means of checking the feed.

The connection to the device was fairly smooth but we did have to refresh our router when completing the process. It could’ve been a bandwidth issue given we have more Smart items than ever.

The app is fairly user friendly and my wife and I can both view the live feed at the same time. The feed itself is about .5 -1 second slow which we haven’t found as a problem.

The audio in/out is also quite clear which was fantastic. We try not to talk to our pup too much but it definitely was a nice feature for the first 2-3 days of him being in the crate (and being able to hear him as well as talk to him if he got frustrated).

Highly recommend this one!

title: Weak Signal
text:
I was setting this extended up to help boost the wifi at my parents house.

Getting connected to the device was fairly difficult and I had to get into the router settings to provide special permissions for it to be visible on the network. I had to reboot the router a few times for it to finally take hold and connect. From there I moved it to the location (router in attic) this would be on first floor of a two story house, almost directly below the router (two-ish floors down). I wanted a better signal in the attached garage as in some corners in got weak. Unfortunately this did nothing to increase the signal of the Wi-Fi.

I ended up going with a different model that worked successfully and allowed it to go from 1 bar to 4 (of 5 bars) for signal strength.

title: Weak
text:
The fan power is quite weak and doesn’t serve the purpose. I was using as a replacement for an outdoor Christmas decoration fan where the other fan died after a few years. This was the same specs as the fan it was replacing and. The air generated made it look like a dying Christmas tree.
That was my purpose, maybe it would work in other applications but again the specs lined up with the other fan it was replacing.

title: Don't last long
text:
These cords are quite thick and I was hoping that would help with quality, however these seem to have worn out the fastest. It isn't like the ends have the tradition wear marks where the cord connects into the phone, it's just that they stop connecting to the phone (incompatible notice) then when that is no longer displaying they just stop working.

I did find that manipulating the cord itself (not the end connected to the phone) helps make it connect so it's possible a wire just isn't fully connected inside the cord and is causing the failure. All in all these have lasted the shortest length of all the chargers I've purchased (which it's usually just the part plugged into the phone that normally wears and then won't connect).

title: Great headset
text:
This is actually my second headset of this type because I let my son use the last one and he decided to stretch it until it broke.
I really like that it has a clean sound quality as I do usertesting and that requires clear sound quality. They are also very comfortable and I enjoy they go on the ear versus in the ear which tends to irritate my ears.
The cable is also of solid quality which seems like it plays a role in producing clear audio.
Great buy!

title: Perfect!
text:
I am very pleased with this purchase and I wanted to write a review on things start to finish.
Packaging
-Fantastic overall look and also care in terms of making sure the watch face was protected and sitting in its' own section of the box. The bands were not attached but were easy to slip on (there's a small little nub on the band end that attaches to the watch, color side will face down). There is also a screen protector to peel off the watch face. The charger is magnetic and the charging process may have taken an hour (I just plugged into my computer).

Directions
-These were really fantastic. They lay things out in detail but also keep it brief for the many different options available. Turn on the bluetooth mode on your phone. I found the app "Da Fit App" from the product description, though the directions only show a QR code. From there it was opening the app and doing a quick profile setup (Sex, Height, Weight, Birth Year). It automatically scanned for the phone and the letters displayed on the screen and it was the only one shown so that was quick. I do wish it would pop up a notification that the pairing was successful but there is a watch icon in the app at the bottom. If you click that it displays "Connected" right at the top and shows your exact watch. It also let's you customize the "face" of the watch from within the app. I like Dial 3.

The App
-Very well laid out and some details were provided earlier but you can adjust the notifications you receive and it all pairs through Bluetooth so as long as they are on (and you accept push notifications on the phone) you'll receive the notifications on the phone. You can make a lot of the adjustments you want through the watch, but the app can allow for a faster level to set all at once.

The Modes
Phone calls, sleep (need to leave on during sleep), heart rate test, steps, training (stopwatch), blood pressure, SpO2 Test, Weather, Reminders, Shutter (photos/video), start/stop songs, Alarms, Timer, Stopwatch, Theater Mode (turns off vibrating and brightness), Move reminders, Drink reminders (stay healthy), Health reminders (menstrual, pregnancy, gender health).

The watch will sync to your timezone once the app is set and you can also get weather notifications which I set inside the app.

I am really thrilled to use the watch and was able to even deny a call earlier without having to grab my phone (unwanted caller). Excellent product and totally worth it!

title: Good sound, not good audo
text:
Here me out here in that the sound on these is solid (not a whole lot of bass) but the sound is clean. They also can go quite loud which is also nice given that sometimes bluetooth reception can be limited. These pair quickly with my phone too.

The issues I have are the popping these into and out of your ear, you are likely to hit one of the buttons to either pause music or adjust sound.

The other major issue is the audio quality for taking a call is terrible. I did test these out against airpods as that is the ultimate goal here (great deal and to not have to buy those, right?). Well, if you want to use these for taking calls, you will end up with a good deal of static (again with an even comparison in the same situation as airpods which I was able to borrow from a friend who helped with the test).

title: Cheap, but effective
text:
These mounts seem to be mostly set to as long as they fit your tv size, you've got endless options. The big key is price and this one fit the bill. It came in a fairly small, light box which is fine. The mount does not need to be massive. The materials these pieces are made from are steel but incredibly light weight.

The brackets that go on the backside of the TV are L shaped rather than the U shape or even Square shape I've had for other TV mounts I've purchased.

Outside of that, assembly was quick. The other small note is this did not come with a small level that is common to see on these mounts (but cheap versions of those can be less reliable also). It is a super bare bones item but has handled a 46" TV with ease and that's what we needed.

title: Get these!
text:
You NEED braided if you want these types of cords to last. I bought two standard style white cords and they were flimsy and ended up melting. These have worked exceptionally well and the long cord has been really nice as 3' is just slightly too short and pulls my headphones down. 6' is the way to go.
The sound quality is as expected. The audio plug that goes into your headphones is a little large but still ended up fitting in my headphones but I had to push a little bit. No loss of sound and I am incredibly pleased!

title: Great little mic
text:
The microphone easily attached to my camera. I did like that there was a replacement camera mount included (the red piece) as I’ve heard of people breaking those for similar looking mics. This one DID come attached to the red mount so there were no issues and I have a spare. The red piece is fairly flexible which has both pros and cons as the mic can move a little and not stress this piece, but the con being the mic can move.

As far as the mic audio, there was a good improvement when about 3 feet away and a major improvement when up closer. The audio is cleaner than the on mic camera which makes this a nice minor cost improvement.

There are different cables which allow you to attach the camera to a standard audio port or a TRRS port like on some iPhones.

The mic does not need batteries so there are no issues with needing the check the batteries before each use. This does seem to have a downside somewhat in that the mic doesn’t really have a power boost which would come from the batteries.

The mic comes with a pop filter screen as well as a wind screen filter which are nice additions for recording audio in any condition.

The mic can be sensitive with some light wind so if there is a breeze do not forget the wind screen filter.

I would definitely recommend this as a low cost alternative to the similar Rode mic.

title: Pleasantly surprised
text:
Unfortunately this item was far better than expected. I know that sounds odd but the item was well made, with a solid cord length. The cord itself was of thick material/casing which helps add durability.

I was pleasantly surprised by this item.

title: Holding up well
text:
The issue with most cords is the connection between the cable and head of the cord don't seem to hold up over time. This cord solves that issue with a flexible piece of rubber that allows it to have some additional stability for long term use.
They connect as expected and haven't worn down as some other cords have over time.
The cords also don't have the "device not compatible" issue which can occur with some cords.
Very satisfied with this purchase overall.

title: Not as described
text: The booster doesn’t seem to benefit this antenna. I figured they all had a similar design and this one was at the right deal. However, it just hasn’t really worked out well for me overall.

title: Not ready to go
text:
“Some assembly required”. Keep reading.

The disk wasn’t formatted properly to be used right away. Luckily I work with someone who is tech savvy and could get it formatted properly. The disk also needed a name, not in the sense that I have to name my devices but since it wasn’t recognized by my computer as a registered device, I had to give it a name which was interesting.

It does work but will require some tech knowledge to get it to actually store files. I would not deem this as a ready to go item.

title: Great replacement
text: Screen fit perfect and was well packaged. The screen itself also worked great once the unit powered back on. I’ve had some screens that did not quite light up like the original. This one was exactly like the original.

title: As expected
text: Packaged well and have not had an issue with it. It would be nice if there was a 1 year follow up on items like this to see how they’ve held up after a short period.

title: Don’t last long
text: This is the replacement I had to buy for the first one that died after 4 months.

title: Great buy
text:
I have not had issue with this product. It recognized it once attached to my iphone and I did not have to download an app to make that happen.
It either loaded the "Upload" feature once plugged in, or click photos and in the bottom tab you'll see the "Upload" tab next to the other common tabs.
Great buy and still use today (have had for over 1 year now)

title: Great buy
text:
Great product overall. The clips work well even though they are plastic. The metal connectors offer a nice level of comfort in attaching to the camera.
It is a little bit short, but that also makes it a little easier to brace the camera strap against your neck for stable video shooting.

title: Wall plug, laptop, car usb - does not work
text:
I purchased this unit because it appeared like it would work in my cars’ USB port. That didn’t work though the unit lit up its blue light. I tried a few different cables in each slot with no luck. I tested the port alone with a cable after and that worked fine.

I then tried it in my wall outlet. The units light lit up blue. I tried the same tests as above with no luck. I tested wall plug with single cable after and my wall plug worked fine.

Finally I tried my laptop’s usb and using the same testing sequence above it also didn’t work.

I am returning this unit.

title: Suits my needs
text: These are great and fit my needs for videography (youtube). It's fairly easy to change the style, however minus one star since it seems like the zipper may fail if I needed to use this on a daily basis (pro photographer). However if you ARE a pro photographer you likely know better than to buy something on the lower end in terms of price and expect it to be great.

title: Works great
text: Works great. Not much else to add.

title: Wouldn't recommend
text: Didn't work when connecting my camera to my laptop.

title: Great
text: Works well and hasn't fried any wires which has been common lately for all of the different adapters.

title: Great
text: We bought this to "cut cable" and setup our antenna. The quality is great and there seems to be limited bleed. We use a splitter and have one antenna and 2 tv's hooked to it from this main cable.

title: Great buy
text: Transfer speeds are great and it doesn't seem to have a bunch of garbage data consuming space.

title: Great flash
text: This is an awesome flash that has a great battery life and the flash is quite strong. I find that even in lower light, I'm on the 3rd setting (I believe there are 8 total intensities). This fits perfect into the shoe of my Canon EOS M.

title: Not very compatible
text: Doesn't work for Canon EOS M.

title: Great buy
text:
This is a great backpack that is comfortable and has quite a few compartments. I wish there were more Velcro dividers with this and that would make it five stars.
Otherwise it is very durable and works very well for me.

title: Ol
text: It is a decent product for the price. It is quite cheap but I needed an adapter very quick. If you are an audio "geek" look for something of higher quality.

title: Perfect
text: This little LED light is MUCH more powerful than one is led to believe. I wanted to use this for some night video shots and will most likely need a diffuser to bring down the light intensity a bit. Overall, incredibly satisfied with this little light.

title: Solid accessory for the videographer
text:
This mic came in a nice package that was foam packed so it had a very professional look.
The mic is solid plastic so it does seem like it would be easy to break (this review could be edited later should an incident occur).
The mic quality is much more improved over the mic on my EOS M (video difference is shown in my yt video, LiftingDad).
The +10db gain is a nice addition to the mic and really helps with improving the overall sound volume.
The shotgun aspect of the mic is decent but not the best from what I've truly seen from shotgun mic's (i.e. The sound picked up best is directly in front of the mic and dissipates from the sides to the back of the mic). It still pick up sounds fairly well from the sides and back. This is NOT ideal when shooting an interview or similar which is the common method for these mic's.
It does come at a nice price point and is a great piece for those on a budget (like myself).

title: You get what you pay for
text: Returned. A lot of feedback and poor audio quality.

title: A Bit Deceiving But The Right Price
text:
Why the 3 stars?
This package deal comes with items that seem to be drawn from an overstock bin of items in a similar category. So you DO get the items listed, just with different brands names.
The kit altogether is priced well and you "get what you pay for", however here you get what's given. It'd be better if they showed the varying brands given to customers.
Most of the cleaning kit was Polaroid which is great.
The lens protector kit is a brand I have not heard of but appears decent.
The bag (as others have mentioned) is not what's pictured. I need the tripod otherwise I'd return the package due to the seller knowingly sending items not accurately described.

Suggestion to the seller: Add accurate photos so people are more aware of what they may be getting versus what's expected from the provided pictures.

title: This is one solid unit which is great. The arms are their own pieces
text:
This is one solid unit which is great. The arms are their own pieces, but the mount is one solid structure. I have noticed some mounts are needed to be bolted together which isn't as structurally sound.

The only thing to be cautious of is to tighten the screws that allow it to tilt. Otherwise, you'll be in for a surprise when you attach the arms to the tv and set it on the mount.

title: Wouldn't re-purchase
text: I don't like reviewing products that I assumed wouldn't last all that long. This product took about 1 week before the cord ripped off of the earpiece. As previously stated, you get what you pay for with products.

title: You get what you pay for
text:
Awful product that breaks when you try to attach to the mounting unit. You definitely get what you pay for with this item. If you are trying to save a few dollars, don't.
It would be best if the tiny unit came assembled in one piece rather than two.

title: Four Stars
text: Not good quality. Plastic wiggled. Should be dollar store priced

title: Well designed fan.
text: I took a chance on this fan. Thought it was a bit much for a hand held fan but it was well worth the price. The fan is well designed. It folds down into a smaller size for carrying. It opens up to hold in hand. There's even a stand that the fan can go in and be propped up. I have it facing my computer sometimes to cool it down. There are three speeds. The highest speed is strong! It operates quietly and has a rechargeable battery that runs long and quickly recharges. So far I have used it at home, work, out in the hot sun and given it to a friend that was having a hot flash!

title: Great Fit!
text: Fits great and is beautiful!

title: Satisfied with Purchase
text: Totally cute!  Thanks!

title: AWESOME SURROUND SOUND QUALITY
