text: I am amazed at how good this is. I use it mostly for music and now I get the beautiful sound "everywhere" when paired with Alexa Echo bluetooth. The surround sound is exquisite .  This is the best gift to myself ever.

title: Worth every penny
text: Excellent tablet. I get everything I want with no trouble.

title: WORKS WHEN YOU REALLY NEED IT
text: It was so easy to set up. It does what it is supposed to do. Must have for emergencies. Wonderful battery backup.

title: It's classy and simplified working with a 10" Kindle Fire.
text: Wow!! What a wonderful surprise. Just elegant and so easy to hold. So glad I bought this. Love it.

title: It's like MAGIC WITH A VOICE!
text: Love everything about it. The sound for music is extremely clear. It makes phone calls without lifting a finger. I have a smart plug attached to my BOSE stereo system. Makes my life easier.

title: Great Product
text: They work so well. Easy to use and adds good light to my laundry area. Great Value.

title: Wonderful!
text: Once I found the insertion slot, it worked just fine. Great help from prior customers and Amazon email feedback. Happy!

title: Good Product
text: Case is very nice and easy to keep clean. Looks good too.

title: Good
text: Easier to use than gen 2. So far do good.

title: EXTREMELY POOR CUSTOMER SERVICE
text: I was very excited when I got my Kindle 1 1/2 years ago. All worked well until about 2 months ago. The wireless connection could not be maintained. My laptop is fine as is my smartphone. So I contacted customer service. What a disaster. I contacted their chat many, many times to no avail. Some said it was hardware and others said it was software. They do not have remote access capabilities nor a service repair center. Today it got to the point where I got such ridiculous highly technical instructions so I ended the chat. They are poorly qualified to provide technical support. Of course they will not send a new one . So unfortunately, I have no use for a dead kindle. So sad. I paid well over $250 1 1/2 years ago and now it's a throwaway.

title: Great Product!
text: Fast shipping! Cute looking compact radio combo. Worked perfectly as soon as I took it out of the box. Very glad I bought this .Great value.

title: Excellent for more than tripods
text:
I purchased the 25" model of the same bag from this brand in August 2021 and it has held up admirably. No tears; the zipper is solid and the outer material is tough.

My primary use is to use the bag for some drum hardware. I have a dedicated hardware bag for stands, etc., but for individual parts like floor tom legs, shell-mounted cymbal arms, and bass drum tom mounts I prefer this bag and found that the 25" model was larger than I normally need. The only bass drum tom mount that I use that will NOT fit in this bag is the Gretsch GS1THSL single tom mount that comes with modern Catalina and Renown kits. Obviously the double mount will also not fit. However, my other mounts do and this bag is the perfect way to transport drum kit-specific hardware and leave my general hardware bag separate.

My first one has lasted nearly a year and is still going strong. I expect many more years of use from that bag and see no reason why I won't have the same experience with this one.

title: Nicely constructed, but the product photos are deceptive
text:
The product page photos when I purchased this showed two bags. I assumed that was how many I would receive. After only one arrived I noticed that the photos were meant to depict the fact that the length was adjustable. I returned the order (no hassles by the way.)

I did take the time to carefully examine the bag before returning it and was impressed. The material was extremely sturdy, there was some padding and the zipper was first rate. Had it met my overall needs I would have kept it. Despite returning it I will not hesitate to highly recommend the bag or its value. Just bear in mind that you will be receiving a single bag, not two that the product photo [when I purchased mine) depicted.

title: Some minor issues, but a decent alternative to subscription cable
text:
I purchased this to upgrade an old Roku HD that I purchased in 2012. While the older Roku worked well for Netflix and YouTube, Amazon Prime discontinued support for it.

This has what I suppose user interface designers call a modern look, but I honestly preferred the older, less slick look of the HD model. However, that is not a show stopper for me.

My only complaint is I have to reboot this model every few weeks or it hangs. The ancient HD model was a solid performer that maybe needed to be rebooted two or three times a year. On the other hand, I can once again watch Prime video, and the price of this device is pretty inexpensive, so I am mostly a happy camper.

title: Exactly what it claims: simple and reliable
text:
I needed a spare mouse as a backup for one that is over fifteen years old and is starting to show its age. I purchased this based on price and reviews and am going to grab another one.

Plugged right into my aging Lenovo T400 running Windows 7. Even a utility called WizMouse recognized it and the settings (for a Logitech mouse) of that app worked perfectly as well. Plugged into a Windows 10 laptop, same result: immediately recognized and worked perfectly. Definitely plug and play in the Windows world, included a legacy, unsupported machine and laptop. I also tested it with a Chromebook ... works perfectly.

Durability? Haven't had it long enough to say one way or the other. The cord is about the same as the Logitech mouse, and every other aspect of construction appears to be close-to-identical.

title: Perfect for the way I use it
text: I subtracted a star because this battery does not last as long as an OEM one when you are not on external power. However, I am always plugged into external power when working, so I use it as a safeguard to give me time to shut down my laptop when we have a power outage. Those are sadly frequent where I live in central FL. For the price and the fact that it supports my ancient Thinkpad model I consider it a bargain. If you are looking for a replacement battery that will allow you to work untethered from external power you probably should invest in a genuine OEM battery from Lenovo. If you use it the way that I do, though, this is an ideal solution.

title: Perfect fit
text: This fits my Galaxy Tab S7 FE 2021 perfectly. It's a tad awkward, but only because of the size of the tablet itself. It had decent protection, precision cutouts, and is priced well below covers at the big box stores. I have zero complaints!

title: Not disappointed
text:
I am not going to cover every feature in detail since other reviews have some an excellent job of that. My points of comparison are a Galaxy Tab S6 Lite 10.4-inch Android Tablet 128GB that I purchased in June 2021, and my first large format Galaxy, the Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet that I purchased in June 2015.

This one is a major performance improvement over the most recent (June 2021) Galaxy, and better in all respects than the much older 12.2 Galaxy I purchased in June 2015.

I was totally pleased with the Tab S6, but missed the larger screen of the Tab Pro 12.2. This screen is significantly more vivid than the 12.2 Tab Pro, and the 256gb memory in this one pretty much assures that the performance is significantly better than either the 32GB Tab Pro or the 128GB Tab S6. But that is expected.

What I truly love about this tablet over the older large format one is the body is sturdy and not prone to bending. That is why my Tab Pro ultimately failed: the body was so thin that it flexed and at some point it started acting crazy. It would have cost more to repair it than to purchase the Tab S6. Prior to purchasing this one I made sure that that issue had been resolved. Yes, it's not as light, but it more than makes up for it in sheer speed, superior display, and even sound quality.

If you want or need a large format tablet that is reasonably priced and provides excellent battery life and performance this is worth considering.

title: Make sure you read the description
text: I ordered this and had to return it simply because of my own stupidity: I did not carefully read the product description. This is specifically for newer laptops and other devices that do not have VGA out, but have HDMI out. It is designed to allow you to connect your device to a legacy monitor or TV that has VGA in, It will NOT work in the other direction. For what it does and its intended market this is an inexpensive way to continue using a legacy, VGA equipped monitor or TV with newer devices that are HDMI only.

title: Allowed me to add a 2009 TV to a 2008 laptop via HDMI
text:
This device connects to the VGA port and from there connects to a monitor or TV HDMI port, It WILL NOT work in the other direction, and it requires a source of 5V 1A power (any standard phone charger will work.)

It comes with a USB charging cable and a 3.5mm cable for transmitting sound. Apparently it will not send sound interlaced with the HDMI signal through the HDMI cable (that you will need to supply.) For me this is not an issue because I am using it on a legacy laptop to send video only to a legacy TV, which I am using as extended video under Windows 7. Yes, it's using some ancient gear. But that is why I rated it five stars.

Limitations: even if your TV or monitor is capable of higher resolutions this is not going to provide more than 720p from an old laptop or PC to an old monitor or TV. I know the specs say that this will go higher, but I could not get it there. Yet, going straight VGA from my T400 to my Sanyo TV it went into higher resolution as an extended screen. I am OK with the limitation because I am only using the TV as a second screen with MS Office,

On an old Windows 7 system it's truly plug and play. I had it up and running without the scant instructions in mere minutes. For me it is a perfect solution.

title: After two years still working perfectly
text:
I own a Blu-Ray player, but have that attached to a different TV. This DVD player has been my main device since my DVD collection outnumbers my Blu-Ray discs about ten to one.

I've never had an issue with this player, and it has outperformed (and outlasted) the Sony players that I had been using. I purchased this two years ago (April 2019) and it was immediately apparent that this was solid from picture quality to the simplified controls on the remote.

The only complaint - and it's a small one - is the latency between pushing the open tray button on the remote and when the tray actually opens. Overall, this has proven to be reliable and considering that it's two years old and still going strong, a great value as well as solidly functional.

title: Perfect for a Samsung Tab S6 Lite
text:
Holds the Tab S6 Lite (a 10.4 inch tablet) firmly in both portrait and landscape positions. There is a cutout in the arm clamps the tablet in place to run your charging cable. I left my tablet in its third party folio style case, so connecting the charging cable to the tablet was a bit tricky. That is not the fault of this stand. Chalk it up to me being too lazy to remove the case.

Do note that it does not come with instructions. However, the instructional video on this product page is, in my opinion. a lot more effective than a piece of paper and showed how to assemble and fine adjust the stand for both phones and tablets. This stand is stable and infinitely superior to the built-in kickstand that came with the folio cover.

title: Use it more than I thought I would
text:
I purchased a pair of these in September 2020 - one for me, and one for my wife - and am surprised by how much I have become dependent upon it. It reads from my google calendar two hours from a scheduled event, so that is one useful feature. If I cannot remember a fact or quickly need to look up something, all I have to do is ask. I also use it as a clock.

Except for the visual display of time and date, I could have accomplished everything I mentioned with my old hockey puck, A.K.A. "Dot." However, for some reason I did not use that one as much, so, perhaps the visual display catches my eye and reminds me that I have a fairly useful appliance that will do things for me. At any rate I use this a LOT more than I did the Dot.

The real user in the house if my wife. She is constantly interacting with her Echo, but she was the household power user when she was using a Dot as well. While I feel as though I have gotten my money's worth from mine, the truth is my wife's daily (hourly?) use of hers makes the pair we have in our own home work spaces a bargain.

Bottom line: cool device that has numerous uses - many of which I don't personally use. For some reason the screen inspires me to use mine a lot more than the screenless Dot, and honestly I rarely use the Echo visually.

title: Nice workhorse tablet
text:
I finally upgraded my circa 2018 Galaxy Tab A to this. The Tab A and this one represent lower tier Galaxy tablets, meaning that they were not the flagship models. This one does everything I want. That said, my needs are relatively simple: mostly web browsing, and streaming movies from Netflix and Prime. Things that I absolutely love:

- the old Tab A had 16GB and this has 128, a major increase in storage.
- screen quality is amazing. Streaming videos is noticeably better from a visual standpoint.
- in the same price range as the old Tab A, so when I upgraded I felt as though I was getting a much better tablet for about the same price as I paid for the old one in 2018.

While the battery life on this new tablet is much better, it longer than I thought it would to charge it. And, yes, I am using the included fast charger and cable. When I was transferring my data and apps from the old tablet the power consumption of WiFi, CPU and whatnot resulted in the charging rate crawling to a snail pace. It was as though it was consuming power at close to the same rate as it was being charged. In normal use, the charging is faster, but still not as fast as I guessed it would be using a fast charger. Not a real issue, but I thought I would mention it to set expectations.

As for the S-Pen, I am not currently using it. I am using an old fashion stylus in lieu of fingers to navigate (old habits die hard), and have not found a use for the S-Pen that requires its power and capabilities. It is certainly more than just a stylus, and is designed to integrate with some specific apps. I did watch a Youtube video explaining and demonstrating it, and it is impressive. But that is for a later time when I feel like experimenting and exploring.

Overall I love this tablet and am not only pleased with its features and capabilities, but am very happy with its modest price tag.

title: Thick. Excellent protection
text:
I purchased this for my wife to house her new Galaxy Tab S6 Lite (purchased at the same time.) The tablet is pretty thin, but this adds some girth to it. Not complaining - I (and my wife) appreciate the protection that this case affords.

The case for her old tablet held the old one in place with straps, which were functional. This case has a synthetic material frame into which the Tab S6 snaps in. It is like having a bumper surrounding the edge of the the tablet, and it provides excellent protection. It is also why the S6 is no longer slim. Like I mentioned that is not an issue for her.

Five stars because the tablet is a perfect fit. There is room for the pen that comes with the S6 on the inside of the cover (and it attaches via magnet without interfering with opening or closing the cover). The outer material of the case provides a bit of added padding, further protecting the tablet.All of the buttons, the camera lens, and the other cutouts are precision cut and perfect placed.

Icing on the cake: the graphic gracing the cover is vivid and the coloration is both subtle and nuanced.

title: Reliable
text:
I've been using this constantly since October 2020 and it's totally reliable. I cannot speak to speed because it's housed in an old Levono T400 running Windows 7. I have a separate one of these that I purchased as an external drive that I use to move files between my Windows 10 and my Chromebook laptops and it, too, is totally reliable (and is used many times a week.)

If I find myself needing another external or internal SSD I will probably go with this particular brand because of my experiences thus far.

title: Works like a charm
text: In the nine months since purchasing this cable I have used it often to move large file systems from my work to personal computers (and even a Chromebook.) Never a problem, and the connections are as solid as the day it arrived. I have reached the point where I take it for granted that it will work every time I connect it to a different computer (usually with the same external drive attached.) Cannot ask for anything more than that.

title: Solid construction and performance
text: I've owned these since February 2021 and they have performed without a hitch. One of the cables is used in my vehicle and it is being constantly inserted into my phone. The C connector is just as good as the day I started using it nearly seven months ago, and the outer protector layer does its job. I use it with a Samsung A51 and my wife uses one of the cables from this pack with a Samsung A50 - both powered by a fast charger. I can say that these cables are one hundred percent compatible with our phones in particular, and fast charging in general. Plus the price is right.

title: Inexpensive replacement for an old dongle
text: My twelve year old bluetooth dongle gave up the ghost so I ordered this one based on price and reviews. The key feature was fast shipping via Prime. It worked out of the box (after I downloaded and installed drivers for my Windows 7 PC per the included instructions.) I can't make claims that this dongle is any faster or better than the dead one that it replaced, but it is just as fast and reliable. And easy to install. If I were not using an ancient version of Windows (by choice) it would literally be plug and play. Even with my need to add drivers it was a simple, quick job to get it up and running.

title: Amazing price (and performance)
text: I purchased this to replace a GLS Audio 20-Feet Ethercon CAT 6 cable that would not transmit phantom power because GLS stupidly cut one end of the shield for "ground lift".  I was attempting to use that cable to connect a pair of LyxPro 4 Channel 3 Pin Multi Network XLR Cable Breakout boxes. Since I needed phantom power I went searching and came across this cable. I was dubious since the price was so low (and half the price of the GLS cable), but the reviews were good so I took a chance. This is the perfect solution and a cost-effective one at that. Nicely made too.

title: Excellent quality as long as you do not need to transmit phantom power
text:
I am using this with a LyxPro 4-Channel pair of boxes connected via Ethercon. The quality of this cable is excellent, especially considering the lower price. It transmits noise-free too. And, finally, it is more flexible that I thought that it would be. If you are an old timer who remembers 10BASE2, this has about the same semi-flexible quality as that cable.

Unfortunately it will not transmit phantom power, and I suspect that is because one end of the ground is lifted. However, if you don't need phantom power this is a great value based on price, quietness and overall construction.

title: Heavy duty and perfect for my Canon T7i
text:
I stupidly broke my main tripod my accidentally placing a heavy crate on it. I wanted something sturdy and took a chance on this. It turned out to be even better than my more expensive tripod that it replaced, and the extra quick release plate is an added bonus. It allows me to quickly swap between my Canon and the also included cell phone mount for when my wife takes quick videos of my band's performances.

Initially I thought the bottom leg extensions were a bit flimsy, but while they have flex they are rock solid. The flex allows them and the movable feet to provide a stable platform on uneven ground.

The only thing that I don't care for is the center post that uses a crank to lift and retract. My gear is not that heavy, so a tension knob or ring would have worked better for me, but if you are using this for precision positioning (which I am not) you may find that feature to be to your advantage.

The bag that comes with it is more than adequate for my needs, but is pretty basic. If you venture into harsh environments you may want to order a more robust bag.

title: Heavy duty and large capacity for the price
text:
I purchased this as a drum kit hardware bag for a Tama Club Jam (small size) drum kit. It easily accommodates the center tom holder, the bass drum mounted cymbal holder, a Tama classic straight cymbal stand and a Tama HP30 bass drum pedal. I was also able to fit the floor tom legs. I could have managed the Tama classic hi-hat stand and classic snare drum stand, but that was pushing it and I was afraid that those last two components would have damaged the zipper. I am using a separate, small Tama hardware bag for those, plus a throne base and small stick bag.

The padding is superior to the Tama hardware bag, and the overall construction, including zipper is as good if not better. This bag actually holds more than the Tama one that was designed for drum hardware, and is about half the cost.

I also own a nice camera tripod that this case would easily protect and I will probably order another case for that. However, this case is a lot larger than the tripod, and I so rarely transport it, that the value proposition is nowhere as good as for my current use as a drum hardware bag. I am totally pleased with this bag!

title: Flimsy when fully extended, but good deal for casual use
text: I purchased this to mount a dB SPL meter. For that purpose this is an excellent deal and all the tripod one needs. For SLR cameras like my Canon T7i, this would be OK (and merely OK) as a table top tripod with the legs fully retracted. It wobble too much otherwise. For me this is all I need. Had I purchased for my camera it would have been returned. Bottom line: if you need to mount a stationary device or use it as a tabletop tripod you will love it and the price. Otherwise I recommend spending a few extra bucks and getting a tripod that is sturdier.

title: Fairly generic, but well made
text: Not too many years ago purchasing charging cables was hit-or-miss. No name brands like this one were usually shoddy and would not work will some phone brands. That has changed, so these days I shop strictly for price and have never been disappointed. I purchased these based solely on price and long length and am not disappointed. As an aside, I purchased this pack to power a device that required 5v via a micro USB cable. These cables do the job and are sturdy. For me it was a safe purchase.

title: Handy and sturdy
text: I've ordered these multiple times because they are reliable and come in lengths that are convenient for me. My only reason for reordering additional cables is they seem to walk off after I make one available to visitors or loan them. There is nothing fancy or particularity innovative about them - but I value reliability, price and convenience more than innovation. If you want cables that are easy to spot in a sea of black or white ones, and are dependable these are a safe purchase.

title: Cloning? This is probably not your best option
text:
I thought that I'd save a few bucks and grab this instead of the Crucial SSD in approximately the same size that was about ten bucks more. Unfortunately I did not read the full description and discovered that this does not come with cloning software or any software. The Crucial drive comes with cloning software that is easy to use and effective.

All is not lost, however. Although this is listed as an internal drive, the case is sturdy enough to use as an external drive without purchasing a separate enclosure. All you need is a SATA to USB cable and a spare USB port on your device, and you are good to go. I am using a StarTech cable that supports USB 3.0 and everything works like a charm.

For the price and the capacity this is a decent deal if you are looking for extra storage. If you are thinking about cloning, though, look elsewhere. Make sure that whichever brand that you get comes with bundled software. A number of other brands, including that one that I ultimately purchased for the cloned drive, come with OEM versions of an app called Acronis True Image. The bundled version will only work with the brand of SSD that it comes with, but for replicating a drive for safety, upgrading, etc. it works well.

title: Pretty solid and reliable.
text:
My initial purchase was in May 2020, and they had proven to be so reliable that I ordered more in August.

The cable is flexible, but well protected. The strain reliefs are solid. The reliefs are not flexible, but their rigidity ensures that the ends going into the connectors do have leeway to flex. The mating connectors fit snugly and stay inserted.

I am using one on a Chromebook, and the others on two Samsung A50 phones. The durability is why I purchased more, and I will purchase even more from this brand if I need more or additional spares.

title: OK for the price. Keyboard not that great, and the DVD player did not work.
text:
Not bad for the price, but there were some issues. The biggest is the Lenovo DVD app for playing DVDs kept crashing. I remedied that by downloading a free player that was stable. The keyboard is atrocious. I purchased this thinking that it had the same, superior, keyboard that my Lenovo T400 has. Sadly it does not. Yes, it's a step up from the "chicklet" style keys that Apple made in vogue, but not by much.

If you are looking for something inexpensive to browse the web and are not ready to commit to a Chromebook, this is probably a decent choice. I do recommend that you lower expectations (especially is a quality keyboard for touch typing is important to you.)

title: Vast improvement in performance and capacity over mechanical drive
text:
The company for which I work sent me this to upgrade my Levono T400. I was running out of space on the mechanical, 250GB SATA internal drive. Not to mention that the drive was starting to make alarming noises.

When this drive arrived I used a SATA to USB cable to connect it to one of my T400 USB ports, downloaded the free app that was recommended in instructions that came with the SSD drive, and cloned my mechanical internal drive to the new one. That process took about four hours since the old drive was getting very full.

While that was going on I went on Youtube and found a video that showed how to remove the original internal drive from the laptop. I was expecting a nightmare, but lucked out because the Lenovo T400's internal drive takes less than five minutes to swap out. Obviously your experience is going to be different depending on the computer that you are swapping the internal drive. If you are using this as an external, then you don't need the app, nor do you need to swap out anything. Just get a SATA to USB cable, connect it, format the new drive and you are done.

Some reviews complained about this drive being slow compared to other SSD drives. I cannot comment on that. I will say that compared to a mechanical drive this one is blazing fast. And since there are no moving parts, very quiet.

A few final notes: raw capacity of my drive was a little over 953GB, but formatted capacity is 887GB. Also, my install was on a computer running Windows 7 Professional and there were no issues.

title: Very sturdy and rack-friendly
text:
I purchased mine to use as a shelf for a small mixer. Although this shelf is overkill for the relatively lightweight mixer, it will hold a LOT more weight. I am guessing that it could easily accommodate twenty-plus pounds.

The reason I cited this as rack friendly is the mounting holes have enough play in them to work with 19" racks that are not precisely constructed. The extra slop allowed me to easily mount this in a rack that was a little off in exact dimensions.

Overall I am thoroughly pleased with the construction, finish and price.

title: Excellent value for 'vanilla' configurations
text:
I needed to extend a 15 foot HDMI cable from an HDMI switch box to an HDMI port on a smart TV. The switch box is carrying video from a camera, as well as a signal from a ChromeCast.

While the above application is relatively simple and just about any HDMI cable will handle my requirements, this cable's cost point and the fact that each end mated perfectly with the target connectors made it an ideal solution for my needs.

It has worked flawlessly since I received it and I expect a long service life.

title: Rock solid and holds my Canon T7i in any position
text:
I purchased this to mount an independent light source (a RALENO Led Video Light) but also tested it with my Canon T7i camera. The Led video light is light and is no real test. The camera is heavier, yet this small ball head held it steady at any angle with no need to overtighten.

The threads (male and female) mated perfectly with my tripods, camera and other adapters.

In my opinion this is a precision-machined ball head that is heavy-duty and reliable. I have yet to find any flaws or other issues with it after a month of frequent use.

title: Perfect for my application; battery life is less than advertised
text:
I use this to illuminate objects that I am photographing (mainly small items that I sell on various sites), but also to provide extra light for smaller rooms when I am making videos of my band at rehearsal and/or on gigs.

The battery life is touted to be 90-110 minutes under maximum illumination power, but I have gotten around 75 minutes. For me, this is still pretty good I especially like the fact that the battery is integrated, so there is no need to purchase extra batteries and chargers like the other lights that I investigated before purchasing this one. Moreover, this will work with the same external batteries that I use for my tablets and phones, as well as the wall chargers and cables for those devices.

Illumination is soft and can go from warm to cold, depending on your shooting environment. Since I am by no means a professional (or even an advanced) photographer, I found this light to be all that I need for easy to shoot videos and stills.

One thing that I am on the fence about is the mount. It is a little shaky in that it tends to not firmly hold the light steady when installed in my camera's hot shoe. I can live with it since I keep my rig stationary, but if you are on the move that mount is going to be the weak spot.

Despite my dislikes I intend to purchase one more of these as both a spare and as a second light source for some shots that will benefit from the added illumination.

title: Works perfectly with my Canon 800D
text:
No issues whatsoever with this battery in my Canon 800D (T7i.) There are a few things that I don't like. First, the battery life per charge is about 75% of my genuine Canon batteries. for someone on a budget these are an alternative to Canon batteries if you are willing to compromise.

Another issue is the charger is flimsy and not as travel-worthy as I would like. But you can use it in a vehicle or powered by an external battery pack. Just make sure that you have adequate protection for the charger if you are planning to use it in the field. Also, note that only one battery can be charged at a time.

Overall, I knew the main limitations when I purchased this set, so am pleased (especially by the fact that my camera accepts them!) If you are a casual photographer who wants some spares without spending a fortune these are a good deal. If you want the same performance as original Canon batteries, you will be better off getting those.

title: Thick and heavy, but fast and beautiful screen
text:
I upgraded from my old Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro 8.4-Inch, and the difference is like night and day. This is a fairly basic tablet, but much faster than the Tab Pro, and the screen is exponentially nicer.

Do know that this is not some slim, light and trendy tablet. It's surprisingly thick and heavy. However, it is not so thin that it will bend like yet another Samsung that I own - a Tab Pro 12.2.

The 10.1 inch screen has a lot more real estate than the 8.4 this table is replacing. The major reason why I rated this so highly is the price, combined with the obvious difference in both speed and display. It's not cutting edge, but is a workhorse.

title: Extra heavy duty
text:
I purchased both a 15 and a 25 foot cable to run from a splitter box to two monitors. The video and audio were perfect, especially since the splitter input was fed by a 10 HDMI cable (a different brand), making the total length for the longest run approximately 35 feet.

Be aware that these cables are stiff and not easy to work with right out of the box. Since my use was to have them permanently attached to the splitter and monitors there were no issues. On the other hand, if you are planning to run one of these from an adapter connected to a DSLR, I would recommend checking out lighter duty cables.

Overall, I am more than pleased with both the construction and the price. For my specific use they work perfectly and are a solid value.

title: Simple, easy to set up and works well
text:
I purchased this splitter to both simultaneously display video output from my Canon T7i camera, as well as stream video via a ChromeCast to two monitors in my rehearsal space. For less than twenty bucks I was able to accomplish that.

Set-up was as simple as plugging in the HDMI cables and power supply. I was a little confused about the tiny switch that has two modes: Copy and Auto. I selected Auto and everything worked. The instructions are not nearly as useful as the product description on this product page.

The unit is fairly small. I plan to glue some Velcro on the bottom of the case and affix it to one of my monitor stands.

Bottom line: I am pleased with both the price and ease of use and awarded it five solid stars accordingly.

title: Heavy-duty and all metal except for decorative parts
text:
This was actually overkill for me because I mounted a light, 24" monitor on it. However, I was able to assemble it without reading the instructions step-by-step. It only took a give minute glance through them to get all the information that I needed to assemble it. Note: it comes with two tools: a hex wrench and a stamped wrench. I needed to add in a screw driver, and found that using my socket wrench was a lot more effective than the stamped one that was provided.

With the exception of the end caps on the feet and a piece that fit over the center post where the pole connected to the foot assembly all of the parts were solid metal. That includes the wheels, which are very heavy duty (the actual wheel component is a high density synthetic material that is heavy duty.)

This stand has a fairly small footprint - at least when compared to the speaker stand and adapter that I had been using - and is easy to roll around.

Overall, this is a high quality stand that is not likely to tip over by accident due to both its weight and design.

title: Solid protection and vivid colors
text:
My Tab A fit perfectly. I was initially concerned that it did not feature the plastic snap-in holder like many covers, but the faux leather arrangement that holds the tablet in place offers good protection. One feature that I like is the thickness of the case, which is why I have confidence in its ability to safely house my tablet.

A plus that I did not notice when I purchased it is it comes with a stylus and has a loop to accommodate it. Since I use a stylus (and my other cases do not have that feature, nor a look for holding one), this quickly became my favorite case.

Unfortunately I use my tablet flat on a table, desk or across my lap, so I cannot vouch for the ergonomics of the stand feature. Also, do read the instructions. In my haste to insert my tablet into it I struggled with the faux leather part that houses the tablet without realizing that there is a velcro strip that needs to be separated to allow you to slide in the tablet. The fault is mine for not reading the instructions, which are clearly written and illustrated.

Overall, this is the perfect case - for me - and the price was right earning it five stars in my opinion.

title: Nicely constructed and a bargain for simple mounting without need for adjustable viewing angles
text:
Easy to install. Using the supplied anchors I was able to securely mount a [[ASIN:B00RPJOQQ8 ViewSonic VA2465SMH 24" 1080p LED Monitor]]. Granted, the ViewSonic is lightweight, but the built-in bubble level on this mount made the entire install process a breeze. Note that you do not have a lot of flexibility when it comes to adjusting viewing angle. My install took that into account since I wanted my monitor mounted like a picture frame.

This is well constructed and perfect for thin monitors like the one I installed. My main reason for the the high rating is price, followed by construction, and finally the integrated bubble level. This is a bargain if you are mounting a lightweight, thin monitor and are not concerned with viewing angle flexibility.

title: Keeps my iPad charged while controlling my Yamaha P-115 keyboard
text:
I purchased this to power my iPad Pro while using it as a controller for my [[ASIN:B00UHBGE7A Yamaha P115 88-Key Weighted Action Digital Piano]]. I had been using the [[ASIN:B014VGHG0U Apple MD821AM/A Lightning to USB Camera Adapter]], but while it worked as an interface to my piano, the iPad's battery would drain too quickly. This adapter solved that problem.

You can power from a wall charging unit or one of the many external battery packs on the market, while simultaneously controlling your Yamaha P-115. The iPad stays charged, and that makes this adapter a godsend to me.

Note: I have NOT tried connecting drives, or other USB devices to my iPad using this adapter, so cannot comment one way or the other about those scenarios.

title: Identical to Yamaha's OEM power supply at a fraction of the price
text: Identical to the OEM power supply in all respects. The cable length is the same eight feet, the strain relief is the same, and even the wire gauge is identical. The most important part is that it works, and does not heat up any more than the original Yamaha part. Plus the price, which is about half that of the original Yamaha power supply, makes it a bargain. I purchased mine as a spare to ensure that we do not cancel performances because of a lost or failed power supply.

title: Needs some improvement, but is truly useful (especially for the price)
text:
I ordered a three pack because I wanted one for my music room, living room and one for my girlfriend. Set up was super simple for the basics - connecting to a bluetooth speaker, your calendar (I use google's calendar), and a music source. For the latter I use Pandora and that, too, was simple.

The subtracted star is because while I own a few thousand dollars worth of MP3 albums that I purchased from Amazon, I cannot access them. Apparently you can only stream music from Amazon's cloud if you have Prime, and even then I am not sure that you can access any of your own music that resides in their cloud. To me that is a fail, and an indication that the business and requirements analysts who assisted in the development of this device do not fully understand customer requirements at a very basic level. Another nit is the iHeart Radio music source that is plain confusing to use.

Some other areas where this would be a LOT more useful is to have the ability to set up more than one route for traffic (currently I can only identify a single route, home-to-work or back, whereas I am frequently traveling from one place to the other and traffic conditions for those trips would be very helpful. The same for the calendar: you can get all events for a single day, but not for a week, or weekend so you still have to fire up a calendar app on your phone, tablet or computer if you want to get a sense of how busy you will be over a period longer than a day.

Still, for fifty bucks each - plus the discount for purchasing a three pack - this is a decent device that has proven to be surprisingly useful in my home. My girlfriend instantly took to hers too. In the week or so that I have been using it I find that I am growing increasingly dependent on mine for streaming music from Pandora, looking up quick information while I am reading or watching a documentary, and letting me know what is on my calendar for a specific day.

I have one of mine connected via bluetooth to a [[ASIN:B019PGACR0 LD Systems MAUI 5 Channel PA System]], and my girlfriend has hers connected to a [[ASIN:B00W8O6MJO Creative Sound Blaster Roar 2 Portable NFC Bluetooth Speaker]], both of which greatly out perform the larger Echo. However I also use my other Dot with just its integrated speaker and it is more than adequate, even for streaming music since I have it on an end table.

Overall, for the current fifty bucks this is a bargain (warts notwithstanding), and while I purchased mine more out of curiosity all three have proven to be useful and practical.

title: Runs a little warm, but works with Amazon Basics batteries
text:
Runs a little warm, but works as well as my three year old [[ASIN:B00MPWFO3O Knox 16-Bay Rapid Ni-MH AA/AAA Battery Charger]]. In fact, this and the Knox look similar (except for color and logo).

I charged a batch of [[ASIN:B007B9NV8Q AmazonBasics AA Rechargeable Batteries]] with no issues, so this charger and those batteries are compatible. I also charged four Knox AAA batteries after the Amazon ones finished. No issues other than the batteries from the AA batch were warm when I removed them.

This (like the Knox unit that I also own) comes with both a wall and a car charger. For me that is a major selling point because I use AA batteries in some wireless microphones my band uses for some gigs. I can keep standby batteries charging in my vehicle in case some need to be swapped out of the mics during intermissions.

Bottom line, I am not sure what the heat does to my battery life, but I do love the convenience of this charger.

title: Sturdy and electrically well constructed.
text:
I am totally impressed with the cable. The outer jacket appears to be tough, but the best thing is both ends are precise fits. I am using a pair of these to extend the distance between powered speakers and surge protector strips on stage.

These can take some abuse being dragged across less than smooth surfaces (although I am not sure about rough-finished concrete or brick). The key, though, is the 25 footers that I purchased do not get hot during prolonged use, and are rated at 125 VAC at 10 Amps. For me the safety factor is important, and I am one hundred percent confident that these are safe in indoors environments.

I am so impressed that I plan to order a pair of 10 and 15 foot cables for times when 25 feet is a bit much.

title: Easy to use in receiver mode - a little tricky in transmitter mode, but still solid
text:
I received mine as a free review sample. This is physically smaller than the photos lead you to believe (about 2.5x1 3/8 inches), but the switch and button, and charging port are easy to access and use. If I have a single wish it would be that the short 3.5mm cable were removable instead of fixed. That would allow you to not only use longer cables if you wanted, but also make it easy to replace that cable if it were to become damaged.

This is easy to use - there is a quick reference card in addition to an instruction sheet. I was able to have this up and running in receiver mode within minutes. Placing it in transmit mode took two tried, but that still took less than five minutes.

Mine will auto-reconnect as long as I do not connect to any other bluetooth receivers between uses with this one. Since I usually connect to a different receiver at home I need to manually reconnect to this one after using the other. However, if this is the last receiver to which I have connected, it will reconnect to my Note 4 phone when I power this on.

My main use is as a receiver going into the 3.5mm AUX port of a Fender Mustang Amp. In that capacity it works perfectly, especially when I stream a backing track into the amp via this receiver. I did test the transmitter mode to make sure it worked, but honestly do not use it.

Overall, this is as reliable as any of a half dozen bluetooth receivers that I own. It does not drop out or flutter even if I am separated by a wall, although it is sensitive to distances further than twenty meters AND a wall. The nice bonus is it can be placed in transmitter mode for enabling remote speakers, but for me it's the receiver mode that is going to be the primary use. In that respect it's rock solid.

title: Excellent construction and will allow plugging into AUX ports of devices encased in OtterBox Defender cases
text:
I received these as a free review sample. I also own various other high-end cable brands and this is the equal of most of them (I do have a few that are world class, but they are also a lot more expensive.) In that respect I consider these to be a great value.

My main use is to connect this cable to dual RCA tape out on my mixing board using an adapter. I then run the angled end into an AUX in on a small speaker array that I sometimes use as a monitor. Note that I have not used this for studio applications, so cannot comment on how noise-free this cable truly in. For live performances, though, it's solid and as noise-free as I need.

While testing this out I discovered that either end will fit the AUX jack on my Note 4 phone, even while it's encased in an [[ASIN:B00NF4SXSO OtterBox Samsung Galaxy Note 4 Case Defender Series]] if you own and use a Defender series case you already know that many cables will not work with it.

Overall, the construction is first rate, and for live applications (or plugging phones into a device protected by a Defender series case), this cable is a bargain and is super reliable.

title: Inexpensive solution for upgrading some older vehicles
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Since Vince McLaren's exceptionally helpful review of August 21, 2016 covers what I also discovered, take the time to read his (and mark it helpful because he did an excellent job.)

It took me a few weeks to get around to writing this review because I needed to order an adapter for the 1998 Ford Explorer it was destined for, and also to have it professionally installed. The adapter I purchased is [[ASIN:B01ES32D7C Fits Ford Explorer 1998-2001 Double DIN Stereo Harness Radio Install Dash Kit]]. There are other kits by different brands for most vehicles. One of those will allow you to install (or have professionally installed) in older vehicles where this system will add some modern touches.

The reasons why I subtracted a star are the touchscreen is not as sensitive as I had hoped (not unusable, but frustrating sometimes), and the instructions are not that great. A professional will have no problem installing this unit, and there is a comprehensive wiring diagram in the product photos on this page. If you are planning to do the install yourself, refer to that photo to get an idea of the complexity of the job.

For me, the bluetooth capability and radio make this is great bargain in my opinion. I have a back-up camera that attaches to a license plate holder that adds that feature (you will need to provide your own camera, but they are inexpensive.) While this will display videos, you will need to load them via the TF card slot because this has no DVD (or CD) slot for that kind of media. Frankly, streaming music via bluetooth obviates the need for a CD (in my opinion), and I do not foresee myself ever needing to use any video player in the driver/front passenger compartment of a vehicle. If those are important to you, this is not the in-dash solution for you.

My overall impression is this is a good - and very inexpensive - solution for upgrading in-dash entertainment and hands free solutions in older vehicles. Before you plunk down your money, though, make sure that this will fit your vehicle, and that there is an adapter kit available for installing it in your vehicle's make, model and year.

title: Excellent use of storage space, great construction and innovative features (but one shortcoming)
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I docked it a star is the active tablet window needs improvement (and that could have been one of the stand-out features if properly designed.) Here is the problem: it's the perfect size for an iPad Air 2, but could not accommodate my Tab 2 10.1 inch tablet. It did hold my Samsung Tab Pro 8.4 (even in an Otterbox Defender case). The vinyl window wrinkles and also reduces sensitivity when you interact with your tablet.

If the active tablet window is unimportant to you, then the rest of this backpack is a winner. Pairing my phone to the bluetooth speakers was as simple as flipping a switch and scanning for it on my phone's settings. And the speakers are loud with better than expected sound quality. I was pleased with that - some thought went into the speakers.

The padding is more than ample for protecting electronics, and there are sufficient pockets for the geekiest geek. What I like, though, is the storage areas are not overly complex. I own a Booq bag that is a storage dream come true, but almost requires a photographic memory to remember were all of the pockets are. This one is designed much simpler, but still efficient and effective.

Construction (except for the active tablet window) is first rate. The tablet window is marred by a difficult zipper, whereas all of the other zippers on this bag are sturdier and smooth. The outer fabric seems tough (I have not had it long enough to make any claims beyond that), and all of the seams are reinforced, straight and tight.

It's very comfortable and can be adjusted to evenly distribute the weight of a fully loaded pack. Considering that the bag itself is somewhat heavy this is a major plus for me.

I do want to note one thing about the backup battery: it is rated at (and stores) the full 4000mAh. However, like all batteries using this one's technology it's only 70% efficient, so expect about 2800mAh of usable capacity. That is not a flaw in this bag, but a reality that I wanted to point out so your expectations are properly set.

Overall, this is a well made bag with some innovative features (battery back-up and bluetooth speakers). If the active tablet window is not an important feature it's definitely worth considering. This one will be replacing my Booq because the storage is there without the complexity.

title: Beautifully made from quality materials (and NO split leather or other shortcuts)
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Frankly, this is probably the best crafted bag I have owned in the past twenty years (and I have one from Booq.) The reason for the high rating is the leather parts are the real thing. Too often these days you get split leather, which is a thin veneer of leather over polyurethane. Not the case here - the leather is not only the real thing, but is generously cut.

The construction is excellent in every respect. The canvas is high quality, all of the stitching and seams are straight and tight, and reinforcement points are heavy-duty. Moreover, the zippers are as heavy-duty as the other parts.

Unlike many bags (even high end ones) that have a chemical odor when you unpack them for the first time, this one does not. The lining is synthetic, which resists water (but I would not claim this to be waterproof.) The snaps, reinforcing rivets and other metal are designed to look like brass, but are probably steel since a magnet will stick to them.

The pockets and compartments make this an excellent work bag that can accommodate smaller laptops. I use mine for my [[ASIN:B00HWMPTI2 Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro SM-T9000ZWAXAR 12.2-Inch Tablet]], which is an easy fit. That leaves me room to spare for other odds and ends, as well as music charts. The main interior pocket is about 13 7/8 inches wide by 10 inches tall. If you are purchasing this for a laptop use those dimensions to determine if this bag will work for you.

Overall, I am not only pleased, but surprised by how well this is made and the quality of the materials. I want to emphasize that this may not fit many of the larger laptops on the market, but is still a great bag for books, tablets and assorted other gear. I hate gushing, but in this case I think the bag warrants it.

title: As good as an OEM Samsung cable at a greatly reduced price point.
text:
I received these as free review samples. Since there are other reviews extolling the virtues of these cables I will keep my comments short and to the point.

The biggest plus is these cables both synch and charge my Note 4 phone. Nearly all cables will charge it, but not all will synch. Also, when using an OEM Samsung charger that is QC certified, the cables in this two-pack will fully support the QC specification. Using other than Samsung cables I commonly get a message telling me that my charging is slow because of the cable. Not so with the cables in this pack.

While the braided metal jacket on these is sturdy, I am not sure one way or the other that is a plus. I did wonder if it would pick up electromagnetic radiation interference, but the one I am using in my vehicle has not as far as I know. I do know that the pair of cables in the pack I received cost less than a single Samsung OEM cable and the performance is identical. For me that warrants the five star rating I awarded.

title: Inexpensive DAC that is easy to install and performs nicely
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I actually had a need for one of these because I wanted to run an audio signal out of my Yamaha receiver to an older analog reel-to-reel recorder. The receiver had a toslink out, and the recorder had RCA in. This box was the perfect DAC.

My signals were noise free, but understand that I was not running the analog cable more than a meter. So in that respect I did not have an adequate test of noise characteristics for longer cable runs. Moreover, I did not really use the volume feature. I set it mid way and used controls on the recorder for volume level. However, for my needs this worked perfectly.

The instructions are a little weak, but anyone who knows what a DAC is should be able to connect and use this without them. The power supply is a standard 5V DC at 1 Amp with a center positive connector. I ran it for an extended length of time and it did not overheat (I have learned from experience to test power supplies because of occasional failures and issues.)

Overall, this is a reasonably priced DAC that I found to be easy to use. The performance was what I had hoped, so am pleased with it.

title: A little noisy and not exactly a micro-sized projector, but versatile and a cheap way to get a big screen
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because in small quarters the fan can get irritating, and also the picture area is a little skewed. The latter is not enough to ruin a video, but combined with the fan noise I felt that this falls into the four star category. To be fair, this is about on par with other portable projectors in this price range and sharing the general form factor.

On the plus side, this is an inexpensive way to get a large screen TV (assuming that your wall is the screen), that does a credible job of projecting movies, TV and presentations. I tested it using a Chromecast and streaming video from YouTube to my phone, then casting from my phone to the Chromecast dongle connected to one of the HDMI ports in the rear. No issues and it was actually a treat. I also tested it with an old Roku in an HDMI port streaming a movie from Netflix. To be sure, neither experience compares to my HD TV screen and surround sound system, but this does not come close to the price tags of those. Bang for the buck this is excellent if you are in a budget.

Frankly, I did not test the other ports, but do want to point out that the 'SD' card port is really USB A that will take a flash drive or an SD card using an adapter. Actually, I think that is a plus as well because flash drives are cheap and a 32GB one can hold a respectable amount of movies, home videos or presentations.

Sound quality is not spectacular, but is definitely adequate. Overall, this is as good as any projector among the four that I have either owned or tested, and is better than some. It would easily be a five star projector if it had a quieter fan. If you can live with that you will probably love it.

title: Especially useful if you use 18650 batteries; fast charging and auto-detect works very well
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because it does not center AA batteries very well in the left slot for some reason, and I got a spark at the plug the first time I plugged this into an outlet. That did not recur after a few more tests, but once was enough to give me pause.

Up front, note that this WILL NOT work with alkaline rechargeable batteries and the instructions clearly state that. It definitely works with the batteries listed, and I am thrilled to have this charger for the growing pile of 18650 batteries that I have accumulated.

My testing was confined to Ni-MH AA and AAA, 18650, and a few battery backups I use for phones and tablets. I let this device auto-detect instead of attempting to manually set voltage and current, and it was spot on in every case. It is relatively fast charging (especially for the Ni-MH AA and AAA batteries), and aside from the spark mentioned above has proven to be reliable. My only direct comparison for recharging speed is for the AA and AAA batteries that charged up 25% faster with this unit than with the Knox charger I had been using for those. I have no baseline for the 18650 and backup batteries that I tested.

I did not test the protection features cited in the specs other than polarity because I did not have depleted or non-rechargeable batteries. I also did not receive the optional car charger adapter, so cannot discuss that. I will say that for the batteries that I did test this performed flawlessly.

A final note: the display is a bit confusing, and the instructions will put you to sleep. However, I highly recommend that you carefully go through the instructions because there are some important caveats and safety precautions of which you need to be aware. Overall, I am pleased with this charging solution and highly recommend it if you use any if the IMR type batteries and especially the 18650 size.

title: Surprisingly good phones at an entry level price - not  optimum for all styles of music though
text:
I received these as a free review sample. They are one of three different models of Spider phone that I have tested, and these are the loudest and deepest from a low frequency perspective (to my ears) among the three.

Like another reviewer, I noticed that the right and left channels are inverted, but that is not a problem for me. The sound quality is very good across the high, medium and low frequency bands. These are compressed at the high end, with a definite bias in the mid and low frequency ranges. The mids are very realistic, while the low end is a bit on the processed side if you are listening to acoustic jazz, or similar styles of music. For modern music they are perfect. Factor that into your purchase decision.

I do need to mention that these can get a little on the loud side, especially if you are listening from a device that automatically attenuates SPL levels on phones and you opt to override that setting. For example, my Note 4 phone will attenuate direct AUX connections, but I can override that and listen full volume. These phones can actually damage hearing if you do that and listen at max for prolonged periods of time. For me the attenuated setting is still plenty loud.

Overall sound quality and level is perfect for modern music, especially genres that are bass and drum centric. For acoustic music (jazz, Americana, older country and the such), these are a little too processed. For those styles I recommend that you consider the [[ASIN:B01BY0262O Spider USA SPEB112-BK Jade Series Metal Earbuds]].

title: Decent, but not the best - there are some caveats
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the grabbing arms are not spring loaded. Indeed, they are a friction, pinion design that makes it a little more difficult to insert and remove your phone while the assembly is attached to your windshield or dash.

Also, before you make a final decision, make sure your phone will fit. The maximum width is 3.5 inches, and that measurement is absolute. My Note 4 would fit when I removed it from its case, but with two of the cases that I swap it between, it would not fit. Take that into account.

This will definitely stay where you attach it! It even adhered to the pebble grain covering on my vehicle's dash, but it was a but too awkward there for me. It is perfect on the windshield, though and that is its final resting place for me.

It's also rock steady, so if you are on bumpy roads the display is not apt to jiggle, which is a nice thing of you are glancing at your phone's GPS map (something I do often.) Basically, this is a decent mount, but not the best (in my opinion.) On the other hand, it's definitely not the worst either!

title: Entry level price; upper intermediate level performance - worth checking out
text:
I received these as a free review sample. Note: these are NOT bluetooth. They are wired ear buds that should fit any device with a 3.5mm output jack.

My rating is based on both sound quality and price. The list on these are in the twenty buck range, but the sound quality, in a blindfold test, would fool you into thinking that these are a tier above other buds in this price range.

The mid range and lower end of the frequency spectrum seem to be emphasized, with highs a bit compressed. These are perfect for casual (and even some critical) listening. An audiophile would probably not like the bias and compression, but most other folks will appreciate it. I mentioned the 'lower' end of the frequency spectrum. At the lowest end it is deep, but not thumping (although it will reproduce 20Hz, which you can feel if not hear.) For anyone listening to acoustic or lightly amplified music, and especially music that uses a big chunk of the audio frequency spectrum (for consumer phones), these are surprisingly good.

There is a disparity between the product description's claim that there have flat, tangle-free cable and the actual cable, which is tangle-free, but round. I want to point that out because one of the things I check when reviewing is any differences between product specs and claims, and what you actually receive.

Basically, these are priced at the upper end of entry level phones, but are good enough to pass for high end intermediate level phones.

title: Convenient and perfect for up to 60 Watt devices
text:
I purchased one of these from a different source to power a 12V portable fridge that was designed to operate from a lighter socket. This converter puts out a full five Amps, which is 60 Watts (5 Amps x 12 volts.)

In addition, this will easily charge tablets and phones if you use a multi-port USB vehicle charger with it. In fact, any 12V DC device like an air pump, etc., that is designed to operate from a vehicle lighter socket is fair game as long as it does not require more than 5 Amps or is rated at 60 Watts or less (and to be on the safe side I would probably lower that to 50 Watts.)

This runs fairly cool as long as you are not operating it at the edge of its capacity or for sustained periods, and mine has never gotten so hot that it alarmed me.

title: Light duty, and good for hanging banners indoors - not for outside use
text:
I purchased this to hand a band banner behind us on stage. In that respect this is perfect because the dimensions are totally as described in the product description, the product photo is accurate, and I knew up front that this was going to be a lightweight support.

There are some limitations. The first is although you can extend the tripod legs to provide decent stability, this is not for environments where passers by can bump into it. Also, with a banner or backdrop clipped to it, it is not going to work well outdoors unless there is zero breeze. It would not take much to catch a light breeze in the 'sail' area of a backdrop or banner and topple this. However, for me this is a major plus because it's light and easy to carry. If you are a musician you already know the advantage.

The cross-member sections are about an inch in diameter, so you will need large clips. The bag was a surprise. I was expecting some cheap, vinyl bag that was an afterthought. While the bag is lightweight, it is designed specifically with pockets for the two stands and the four cross-member sections.

Assembly and disassembly are fast and easy. I marked the posts with small pieces of tape so I could quickly level it after I initially got it to the correct height and leveled it. I recommend that you do the same because the first time it takes patience and a bubble level (or tape measure) to get it set up correctly.

title: Truly useful and if you are a musician who uses pedal boards, this is very handy
text:
If you are a musician who deals with pedals and pedal boards, or has other gear that uses DC power within the range of this power supply, this can be a life saver. Since I own pedal boards that use both 9V DC (Boss and a few other guitar effects pedals), and 12V DC (TC Helicon), this is a spare that sits in my gig bag in case I misplace or damage one of the wall warts that powers those pedals.

Also, because this can put out up to 1.2 Amps, it can power three of my TC Helicon pedals off of a power cable chain. I usually employ a TC Helicon power supply for that, but since I use this one as a spare, it is always ready if needed. I have tested it with the pedals and verified that it will power all of the ones I use simultaneously.

If you do get this and find that the adapters that come with it are not the sizes you need, you may want to consider this add on set by another brand: [[ASIN:B00CMMO6AE Generic Universal 28 DC Power 5.5x2.1mm Jack to 28 Plug Power Adapter for Notebook]]. For my needs, though, this is all I require and I am very pleased with it.

title: Excellent cable at a bargain price, but read on if you are using it on a crowded pedal board
text:
I purchased this cable based on my very positive experience with some other cables that I ordered from this brand ([[ASIN:B003L18XKE Monoprice 104749 1.5-Feet Premier Series XLR Male to XLR Female 16AWG Cable]].)

Like the XLR cables, this one is slightly different in size that what is described. Overall length is 18.5 inches and the cable that is approximately 17 7/8 inches when measured from the housing of the connectors. For me that is not a real issue, but what may be an issue of you are planning to use these with pedals mounted on a pedal board, the length from the strain reliefs to the top of the connector housings is 2 inches. Also, the TRS end's tip to the top of the housing is 2.25 inches, with 5/8" of the housing protruding when the TRS end is fully inserted. Those numbers should help you to determine if this will work in your particular pedal board.

The cable is noise free in my application, which is interconnecting a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1G9O TC Helicon VoiceTone Correct XT Vocal Effects Processor]] to a [[ASIN:B00HMQ1SHO TC Helicon VoiceTone H1 Vocal Effects Processor]]. I did notice that the housing ends are split, two piece design that are held together by the strain reliefs. Also, at the end of the strain relief, the bend radius of the 16AWG cable is very tight, which was a pleasant surprise.

Bottom line: the only potential issue I see with this cable the it may not work well on a pedal board with tightly spaced pedals. In all other respects it has proven to be mechanically and electrically sound, and I intend to order more.

title: One of the easiest-to-use and install dashcams I have come across
text:
I received this as a free review sample. M.Erb's extremely detailed and helpful video review of May 14, 2016 covers this in a great deal of depth. I'll add my thoughts and reasons why I also rated this five solid stars.

First, I have tested and used at least a dozen dashcams, many of which were excellent in their own right. However, the shortfall in each was the screen and a complicated array of controls. With this one your screen is your smartphone or tablet, and your controls are those that are provided with the app you need to download (for free) to control the camera and settings. There is a separate remote control, which is really just a clicker that does one thing: triggers a short video and a snapshot.

Another thing I personally love is the mounting kit. This one, properly used, will run your power cable in an unobtrisive manner (well, as unobtrusive as possible), and the cable is sufficiently long to run the cable from close to my rear view mirror to my dashboard lighter socket in my 2016 Outlander. Other dashcams either forced you to put up with dangling cable or - in one case - have the power and video feed cables professionally installed. Plus this uses a standard USB cable with USB A on one end and micro USB on the other. Some dashcams require a proprietary cable with a barrel connector that makes it difficult to replace if necessary.

Video quality is not award winning (indeed, the camera lens is a fisheye), but is still more than sufficient to capture accidents and even scenic drives. You can also use this for other than a dashcam. I discovered that will fit in a standard microphone clip that fits a Shure SM58 (i.e., a very common size.)

You can use up to a 64GB micro SD card, which will store almost eleven hours of video. Most dashcams are limited to 32GB. The instruction manual is adequate, but not comprehensive, and it also does not cover the software and its capabilities. I hope the company rectifies that, which will make this dashcam even more user friendly, especially for novices. However, most folks do not want to wade through a manual anyway, and the one that comes with this will get you going.

Bottom line: as far as dashcams go, this one is probably the easiest one to use that I have come across. My FAVORITE feature is simplicity that allows my phone or tablet to be the screen and controls.

title: Decent construction and great for my Tab 3 10.1 tablet
text:
I received this as a free review sample. It nicely accommodates my Tab 3 10.1 tablet, but is just a bit too small for my Tab Pro 12.2.

Up front, there is a chemical odor that lingers for about a day, but it dissipates afterwards. You can hasten the removal of the odor by wrapping a teaspoon of baking soda in a washcloth, securing it with a rubber band and leaving it in the case (opened) for an hour.

This is somewhat spongy feeling, and affords a little protection against falls. Frankly, it is not going to protect a tablet against a waist high fall on an irregular, hard surface unless the tablet is in a ruggedized case. On the other hand, it was not designed for that, so I am not docking it any stars. It's as good as any other case that I own.

Other things I like are the sturdy, dual zippers, and the bottom reinforcement. I would have loved a handle, but this is a portfolio style case, so I am still very pleased.

title: Decent as an external USB storage device, but read critical reviews carefully if you plan to use it as a boot drive
text:
I received this as a free review sample. Since there are reviews that cite premature failures I waited a full month before writing a review. In the ensuing time I have been using this as backup storage on two laptops - one running Win7 and the other running XP. I have had zero failures, although this is not the speediest SSD I own (which accounts for the subtracted star).

Over the course of any given day this drive is used about thirty minutes to backup Outlook files and any new documents that I may have created or edited. When I first initialized it the usable storage was around 111GB, so be aware that there is some overhead if you are expecting the full 120GB. This is NOT uncommon so I did not ding it another star for that.

Mine is housed in a [[ASIN:B00K6I9NL8 Patriot Gauntlet 3 SATA III 6 Gb/s USB 3.0 Compatible Hard Disk Drive Enclosure]], which is suitable for my uses and not a bad enclosure if you are planning to use this drive the same way I am. If you are planning to make this a primary boot drive I recommend that you carefully read some of the critical reviews and take them into consideration because there are reported latency issues that make make it untenable in that role. For an external USB storage device, however, this one has been performing for me reliably and I would not hesitate to get another if I need more space.

title: Easy to use, but some caveats
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I'll get the reason for subtracting a star out of the way first: (1) once you place a drive in the case bed removing it is difficult. (2) It runs a little hot. I had the circuit board exposed while initializing a 120GB SATA drive and by the time it was done the printed circuit board was hot. Not enough to cause blistering, but still hot to the touch.

If you plan to install a drive permanently this is not a bad case. It easily slides together (after a little finagling to get the drive in and lined up), and the USB 3 connector is a big plus. The drive that I installed was not the fastest on the market, but this enclosure and associated electronics got good results when I transferred a 5 GB set of MP3 files from my laptop to the external drive it housed.

This comes complete with screws (too many, in fact and the only ones that work are the black ones), and a screw driver. The cover precisely lines up with the bed that houses the drive, and the USB 3 cable that is included is decent.

I've been using this for a month with no issues, and have to admit that despite my complaints above it is an easy way to transform a SATA drive into an external USB storage device.

title: Functional hands-free solution for vehicles with 3.5mm ports in their stereo, but some limitations
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason why I subtracted a star is the cables (both the one from the charger to the control module, and the 3.5mm connection) are hardwired. This means that if either cable becomes damaged it can cost more to repair than to replace, unless you have the skills to repair them. Had the charger been configured with a micro USB port and the control module with a 3.5mm port for separate cables that can be easily purchased just about anywhere (including pharmacies and supermarkets these days), a damaged cable would be an easy swap and the value and utility of this solution been a lot more.

Operationally, this kit functions as promised. The mic will pass through commands if your phone has voice recognition, and the overall quality of sound is more a function of your vehicle's stereo system than this unit. Since my vehicle is already bluetooth-enabled I used a small, powered speaker with a 3.5mm input to test this. Since the cable, as mentioned, is fixed I had to still perform the test in my vehicle. The sound quality was overall good, and making and receiving test calls were easy and the connections clear enough to be heard without 'can you hear me now?'

Surprisingly the extra USB port in the charger was relatively fast, and proved to be as good as any high-speed (but non QC) charger on both my Note 4 and a friend's iPhone 5S. In fact, that is why I only subtracted one star because while the cable issue does detract, the charging capability of the extra port is better than I expected.

Bottom line: this is an OK hand's free solution for older vehicles that have an AUX port, but no bluetooth (and you NEED an AUX port to make this work.) Since the control module is hardwired into a lighter-style charger you cannot use this with a home stereo that does not have bluetooth, but does have 3.5mm input. There are similar solutions that use basically the same design, but replaceable cables that do allow this, so this one is restricted to vehicle-only use. If that is all you need, this one does perform as claimed.

title: For folks with USB C devices. Reliable file system and decent performance
text:
I received this as a free review sample. The reason for five stars is the design, which is convenient for folks who own USB Type C devices.

My acid test is to overfill a drive. On a poorly made thumb drive once the file is at capacity the files will become corrupted and are impossible to remove. In essence, the drive is useless. This one passed that test with no problems. I did not test the transfer rate because the only port I had open on my Thinkpad T61 was an ancient USB 1.1. It was slow (as expected), but the transfer was steady and error-free.

If there is a flaw, it's the loop for attaching this to a key ring is too small for one. Not a show stopper for me since I normally do not keep a thumb drive on my key ring, but if you do, this is NOT going to fit (and that I know of.)

This is definitely for folks who are now using USB C. I would have loved it even more had it come with a piggy back adapter on the C side for a USB micro adapter as well. Perhaps the next version will, but since USB C seems to be the coming thing, perhaps my personal wish is not practical in the long term.

title: Good entry-level speaker - OK sound quality and very LOUD
text:
I received this as a free review sample. I subtracted a star because the sound quality of calls using the hands-free function is a little tinny, That is curious because when streaming music the sound quality if more than adequate.

What distinguishes this speaker - for me - are two things: (1) it's loud, and (2) the controls contain separate volume and skip buttons. Especially the latter because on speakers that combine those buttons I am forever skipping a track when I really wanted to increase or decrease volume. Not so on this speaker.

Some reviewers complained about hiss; I did not experience that at any volume level, even when the speaker was on, but not connected to my phone. Other complained about a loud announcement letting you know power on, pairing and the such. Yes, that is true. And you cannot change it or turn it off (that I know of). For me it is not a problem, but if stuff like that irritates you then you should be looking at different speakers instead of this one.

Sound quality is decent for a small speaker. The high frequency is stable and does not break up or get tinny at max volume. There may be a little compression, which most people like. I prefer truer reproduction. The mids are rich and I suspect that they are purposely biased to emphasize that frequency band. It definitely enhances casual listening, but if you are accustomed to true fidelity it may drive you nuts. The bass is not especially boomy. It's more than adequate if you listen to acoustic music and other genres, but for bass-centric music it's a little weak.
