As great as it is, you need to pay attention to details when unpacking it. Specifically, the cardboard insert in the retail packaging has a web site for the manual. That is important because this thing will make no sense to you without it, unless you have used one of these before. The manual you will want to download is for model KP-810-10.

Basically, the dongle is cleverly stored in the body of the keyboard, and the key is to find the small power switch, which is on the upper left side. After that you are literally up and running. While this makes a wonderful remote for a PC doing presentations, it's even handier connected to any android phone or device that recognizes an OTG connection. That is where this thing excels. However, for Windows PCs this is also optimum because it has Windows keys.

If you need a remote for a Windows PC, or want a convenient way to interact with your OTG-capable phone or tablet this may well become your best friend. I can actually get real work done using this and my Note 3 phone. That is why I gave it five solid stars.

title: Rock solid
text:
These are a precise fit for the Benro models listed and are well constructed of aluminum alloy. They can take the weight of heavier cameras, including film SLRs. The key to why I like them is they are precision made to mate with the Benro heads, and have the non-skid surface.

Of course, another reason why I love these is they can remain permanently attached to your cameras to allow for quick swapping on the tripod.

Finally, price is a factor for me and these are a convenient way to add plates to all your gear without going broke.

title: Worth it for the app alone
text:
Kimberly R. Norton's helpful August 3, 2014 review thoroughly covers most aspects of this card. Actually, after spending a lot of time with the review sample that I received, this is a solution more than a mere card.

First, a caveat. This card requires a reboot of a Windows XP system before it's recognized as a removable disk drive. In a real medical emergency this could be an issue. Granted, XP is obsolete, but Murphy's Law would probably go into effect if you were in a time-critical situation. Plus, this is strictly a Windows based solution.

Now for the reasons why I love this. Foremost is the app itself. It leads you through the creation of medical information that is needed if you were being treated while unconscious or unresponsive. The text files can be read by any system, as well as uploaded to your phone. I have labeled my data card to note that the information is also on my smart phone - just in case the card fails for some reason. The heart of this solution is the app that created the medical data and the files that it produces.

The card itself is clever in that an 8GB flash drive is contained in the form factor of a credit card. The USB 2.0 plug slides out of a protected channel that does not appreciably add to the thickness of the card, so it will easily fit in a wallet.

In addition to the medical data this solution provides a scanner guard that you can use to sandwich your credit cards between that and the Medic ID Guard card. What this part does is guard against RFID identity theft, which is a very real problem. It does not take much to thwart thieves - wrapping credit cards in aluminum foil will do the trick - but this solution is much cleaner and is actually a side benefit. Prior to getting this solution I had been using [[ASIN:B00GC4RTKC RFID Blocking Secure Sleeve]]s. This solution, however, is a lot more convenient.

Bottom line: there are some things that I do not like about this solution, but the benefits greatly outweigh them. As I mentioned, the app alone is worth the cost of this solution because it allowed me to create complete medical data in a structured way. I could have never done that on my own without additional hours of research to discover what information is actually relevant.

title: Perfect for the working photographer
text:
If you own any of the Vanguard tripod models listed as compatible and multiple cameras this set allows you to keep two of them configured for quick swap.

The construction is precise, although these are not magnesium alloy like Vanguard's shoes. That is not an issue for me because they have near the same feel and the same precise fit. I can say for certain that these will work with the [[ASIN:B003BQ71MA Vanguard SBH-250 Magnesium Ballhead with Sliding Quick Shoe]], with which I tested it. As for the other models I am going to take the word of the product description. They also come with a pair of allen wrenches, so in that respect these are a complete solution.

If you own a Vanguard tripod with a compatible head these are as good as the more expensive Vanguard counterparts in my opinion.

title: Incredibly loud with above average sound quality
text:
There are a few things that set the review sample I received apart from most other bluetooth speakers. At the top of the list is sound pressure level because this is the loudest bluetooth speaker I have ever tested. Literally, this can compete with waves on a beach, which can get pretty loud when the tide is changing. I tested it from three rooms away from my writing desk and it could easily be heard. In that respect it could provide background music for a flash mob, which is way beyond the power of most other speakers, which are designed for personal listening on a desk or night stand.

The sound quality is also a cut above. While I have tested speakers that are better, this one is still on the short list of my favorites. The speakers are large and powerful, and they do a remarkable job of handling the high, mid and low frequency bands. As advertized the bass is pretty intense compared to ninety percent of the bluetooth speakers I have owned or tested (about fifty!)

In addition to volume and sound, this is ruggedized. I mentioned that it could compete with wave noise at the beach. It can also withstand moist and sandy environments and being banged around. It's not waterproof, but is designed to resist it.

While the product description and specs are complete I do want to highlight a few features that I personally love. First is ease of connecting this to my phone. When you turn it on it immediately beacons its presence (and announces it in a human voice.) Do a scan from your device for other bluetooth devices and this pops up immediately. A simple touch pairs and connects it. If you have an NFC-enabled phone like my Galaxy Note 3 it's even simpler. Just touch the device to the NFC logo on the speaker and you'll get a message on your screen asking if you want to connect to the speaker.

Finally, time and distance claims are accurate. This actually will play longer than most speakers. The claim is twelve hours. I had it on and playing for ten and it probably would have lasted another two hours. So say at least ten hours to set expectations. It also claims to work from 25 meters, which is significantly more than the normal 10 for bluetooth. I tested mine at about 18 meters and it did not falter - the music streamed with no breakup or dropouts.

Basically, if you want to play your music loud and still get decent sound this is the speaker for you. It has a lot of features that I did not mention (but are listed in the product description), but the defining one is sound pressure level.

title: Excellent low end as claimed with a qualification
text:
The qualification I mentioned in the title is as long as this is used as a close, personal speaker the superior bass frequency response is there. Since M. Erb thoroughly covered most of the characteristics in his excellent July 24, 2014 review I am going to focus on the sound quality and a few observations.

As stated, this speaker provides high quality sound in the lower frequency spectrum as long as it's within one to three feet. Even at twenty feet the sound is excellent, but the effect of the bass diminishes. The woofer is in the bottom part of the casing and do emphasize that part of the frequency spectrum.

Although this is marketed as a 'bass machine' the high and mid range response is actually better than the bass (to my ears anyway), and the overall sound quality makes this one of the best personal speakers that I have tested. In fact, while I normally use Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00IS4187Y Kind Of Blue]] to test speakers because it does exercise the full spectrum, for this one I used two other albums. First was Scott Lafaro's [[ASIN:B007CSETZU The Complete Live At The Village Vanguard 1961]] because Scott LaFaro's bass is prominent. That is how I arrived at my assessment of the bass response that I described above. I also tested this with a Chico Hamilton Trio album titled [[ASIN:B0089PCUT2 Jazz Essentials]] that contained a fuller range of instruments, including cello and flute. The reproduction of frequencies across the full spectrum was so spectacular that I had to give this speaker five stars.

For features and characteristics read (and watch) M. Erb's review. If you are picky about sound quality, as far as I am concerned this should be on your short list of personal speakers. It will not fill a room with sound, but you'll be able to hear every nuance if you have it near by.

title: Exceptional sound
text:
Normally when I receive a review sample I can do a thorough evaluation and write a review within two days. This one took longer. The reason is that it took me a while to hear the differences in this model versus the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]], which also impressed me (and I also own).

After going through a pile of albums to try to understand what the product description meant by smoother bass I finally found an album that allowed me to hear it: [[ASIN:B00492ANTS Portrait In Jazz]]. When Scott LaFaro's bass came in on Autumn Leaves I started switching back and forth between this and the S1, and also hauled out some studio reference monitors. These phones are capable of going down in the 18Hz range for the low end, which is lower than most in ear monitors and phones that are usually in the 20Hz range at the low end. I am not sure my ears can discretely detect the differences between 18 and 20, but I was able to detect nuances that the lower end provided.

These also go up a little higher than more phones, which are usually in the 20 KHz range, Again, I am not sure I can truly hear sounds at 24KHz, but there is a discernible difference. I tested that end of the frequency spectrum with a few Ahmad Jamal albums since he tended towards the right side of his pianos.

One other thing that took me some getting accustomed to was the over-the-ear way of wearing these. I am use to in-ear or the old fashioned over-the-hear phones and I had to play around with these before I figured out how to place them in my ears perfectly. If you are use to over-the-ear you will probably not experience the learning curve that I did.

A few other features that I have come to expect from this brand are here: extra tips of different sizes, a hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) and a 1/4" adapter. I love the flat, tangle-free cable that is tougher than it feels. And it has an adjuster like a chin strap on a cowboy hat that aids in keeping these firmly in place with the over-the-ear way of wearing them.

This is definitely a five star set of phones (according to my way of grading, anyway), and one that I will not hesitate to recommend to fellow musicians. We tend to spend a great deal of time listening to music and these do an excellent job of reproducing it. My advice, though, is to take your time when you first get them because their true power is not immediately apparent. When you do start hearing the difference you will understand why I rated them so highly.

title: Truly are studio quality
text:
I received these phones as a review sample and wanted to test the claim that they are studio quality. In point of fact they are very close. What I mean by studio quality is they are neutral sounding - there is no bias towards any particular frequency band. These are fairly even on the highs, mids and lows.

Of course, if you are listening to modern music that emphasizes low frequency response with a lot of bass you may want to check out other phones that do a better job. I will say that while the frequencies are naturally divided, the separation is excellent so I am certain these phones have a crossover.

Since there are ample specs in the product description (and two video reviews at the time of this one) I will spare you a recitation of that information. I tested these using a few key albums, and also plugged the 1/4 inch connector directly into my Roland RD-300NX keyboard to hear that instrument's natural responses. Both tests confirmed that these are studio quality. However, audiophiles who want unbiased sound will also love them. I played some of my favorite test albums like Miles Davis' Kind of Blue, Ahmad Jamal's Live at the Pershing and some 20-bit mastered CDs. In all cases the frequency response in each band was perfect and the ability to hear nuances (including the natural reverb on Kind of Blue) was a treat. More importantly I heard the albums the way the engineers wanted me to hear them.

To be sure I do have other phones that are at this level of quality, but most are in a much higher price range. I did not expect to be impressed with I accepted a review sample, but not that I've had time to put these through their paces I am impressed. They are now in my practice room/music studio and there they will remain. Definitely recommended.

title: Perfect for headphones
text:
I received this pack as a review sample and quickly came to the conclusion that these are excellent for noise-free applications. The most critical test was when I used this cable to connect a pair of [[ASIN:B006MA9XXM Brainwavz HM5 Studio Monitor Headphones]] to my stereo. The sound was as neutral and noise free as when I used the high grade cable that came with the phones, so the claim of double shielding hold weight. I would not hesitate to recommend these to audiophiles or sound engineers.

In addition to the listening test I thoroughly inspected the physical characteristics. That revealed attention to detail like what appears to be copper cladding or gold plating on the tip, ring and sleeve portions of the connector. The barrel housing is also well constructed and is probably stainless steel. The strain reliefs on the ends are also well done and should protect the ends from internal breakdown even if you frequently handle the cable. The cable itself will stretch to a full twelve feet, but at rest is a little over a foot and a half.

What I did not test is the claim that this will fit most phones through their case. That's because the cases that I have on hand will accommodate regular cables. There is a chamfer on the barrel that houses the connector and it looks as though it will fit some of the more finicky iPhone 5 cases, but I cannot guarantee that it will for all cases.

These are top quality cables that should last a long time if properly handled and stored. If I do experience a premature failure I'll update this review to reflect that.

title: Excellent composite audio cable
text:
Note: at the time of this review this cable set is described as '3.5mm Male To 3 RCA Cable' when it's really a 3-RCA male to 3-RCA male for composite signals. My HDTV has legacy composite jacks to connect older DVD players and I am using the review sample that I received for that purpose.

I replaced it with a premium grade cable by Monster, which cost me significantly more than this one is priced at, and there is no discernible difference in video and audio quality.

The outer shield is slightly different in appearance form the standard 6 cut ones that most RCA connectors employ, but the fit of this set is as precise as others that I have used, and the integrated strain reliefs are some of the beefiest I have ever seen on any brand of RCA composite cable.

Among the reasons why I awarded this five stars is value (relatively low price with high quality construction). This set sports construction features that are not usually found in sub ten dollar cable sets (the price range at the time of this review). For example, the connectors are gold plated, and the copper wire is oxygen free. The overall cable is both flexible, but heavy duty and is not likely to fail if properly used.

My advice is if you are shopping for composite cable, consider this one before investing a lot more in a 'premium; brand that does not really outperform this one.

title: Superior quality
text:
This is one of my favorite patch cables, and I especially love the fact that they come in a variety of them to color-code by function. I received mine as a review sample and it is one of the best constructed patch cables that I have used.

Since I am using them is my music studio the best thing is they are low noise. Actually this is about noise-free as you can get. Part of the reason is the double shielding, but part is the overall construction.

I also love the precision fit. I use these to patch bluetooth receivers in some of my amps and PA mixers for backing tracks. Lesser cables that I have used had a sloppy fit, These have a firm feel inserting and removing.

Construction is top notch. Everything from the heavy duty strain reliefs to the plated tip, ring and sleeve are well made. I also love the flexibility of the cable itself.

If you are looking for high grade patch cable for 3.5mm male-to-male, this is it in my opinion.

title: Handy for small peripherals and charging
text:
Stephen M. Charme's incredibly helpful June 19, 2014 review covers this device in exhaustive detail. I'll attempt to not repeat him, so will confine my review to why I awarded my review sample five stars.

Foremost, I love the convenience of having an all-in-one power and charging station for my phone, tablet and a few smaller electronic items. It takes up one full two outlet wall connectors in my music studio where I am using it. One of the plugs is a dummy that does not draw electricity. This ensures that you do not overload a circuit as well as providing stability to the rather large unit.

At 15 Amps (1675 Watts) this is more than sufficient for the small amperage devices I am using (although I do have a 5 Watt RMS output tube amp plugged into it as well.) Where I live the power fluctuates too wildly to plug anything of value directly into a wall outlet, so this is essential.

It's also a convenience with respect to the swivel. Most of the devices I am powering with this use wall warts, and even with the swivel I can only plug four in at any given time. While that blocks two of the outlets, had it not swiveled I would have probably lost one more outlet.

I have found this so useful that I intend to order another to place in my gig bag for playing out. There is always a dearth of outlets on most of the small venue stages where I play, and the power in most of those places is usually abysmal. One of these for a small PA and keyboard will afford adequate protection as well as being conveniently small.

title: Inexpensive and reliable storage
text:
Capacity is more than adequate for my needs, and the price is right. But the real reason why I gave it five stars is this drive is absolutely reliable. I have tried other brands only to experience premature death of the drive, data loss and other frustrations. In fact, one would get so hot in large transfers that it was uncomfortable to touch. This one does not have those flaws.

I use a pair of these. One for backing up my documents on my ThinkPad T61 running Win XP, and the other as a portable music library. For the latter use I've plugged it into my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Samsung tablet via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]], as well as a number of PCs and laptops of fellow musicians.

Just about every operating system, from my Android phone to a friend's Win 8 laptop immediately recognized this as a drive as soon as it was inserted in the USB port.

I did not bother measuring the transfer speed because I mostly use this for streaming music via USB. I have never experienced a freeze or lag in playing, so, again, I am very pleased with it. The final reason why I am happy is the small form factor, which is about the size of a bluetooth dongle.

Bottom line is you can save a few bucks by purchasing a competing brand, but you will get what you pay for in my opinion. I've been using this brand for literally decades and have never had to worry about failure or other issues.

title: Great feel, easy to connect and decent battery life
text:
I received the universal model as a review sample and tested on a few devices. Those were a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone, a Samsung Tab 3 10.1 and iPad 2 tablets. It paired and connected to each effortlessly and without going through a bunch of technical steps like the earlier generation of bluetooth keyboards. I pressed the connect button on the keyboard, scanned for it in my devices and - viola! - they paired and connected at a touch of my finger. I love it when stuff is that simple.

The key feel has the tactile feedback that sets this apart from cheaper keyboards, In fact, I would say that the feel is equal to the one on my ThinkPad T61 laptop. It's about 9 3/8 inches wide, which gives a lot of typing space. A point of comparison is my laptop's keyboard is about two inches wider.

Because this has an aluminum casing it is not going to creep away while you are typing, and it also keeps the keyboard from flexing when you are handling it. Again, some other keyboards that I have used were flimsy and did not last very long. One final thing I love is the micro USB connector for the power cable is sturdy. I actually had a keyboard from another brand that failed because when I pulled out the charging cable the internals of the port came out with it.

I have been using my keyboard for over eight straight hours, untethered from a charging cable, and it's still going strong. In fact I am writing this review with it to test it. This is a five star product in my opinion because of construction, feel, and the fact that it does everything the specs claim for less than twenty bucks (at the time of this review.)

title: Refreshing and better than soda, but not a true coconut water
text:
I purchase this locally so am going to confine this review strictly to the product without factoring price or shipping.

This is not a true coconut water, but a drink that contains coconut water, nata de coco (a gel made from fermented coconut water), and flavoring among the ingredients. I love it because it's refreshing, especially on humid days, and uses real sugar instead of substitutes that I try to avoid.

Each eight ounce serving contains 70 calories with 18 grams of carbs (16 of which are from sugars). Contrast that with the same serving of Classic Coke, which comes in at 95 calories and 26.4 grams of carbs (all of which are from sugars) and this wins from a nutritional perspective. This drink is much lighter than most sodas and I have personally found it to be good for suppressing my appetite as well.

While it does quench thirst, it does not have the sodium content to be ideal for rehydration. Gatorade, for example, contains roughly 100mg of sodium for the same serving size, which is significantly more than the 15mg this drink contains. Moreover, this drink is missing potassium, which is also recommended for rehydration. I am mentioning this because there are coconut waters that are formulated for rehydration, but this one is more of a beverage.

The main ingredient is mineral water, followed by nata de coco, organic cane sugar, coconut water, calcium lactate, citric acid, sodium citrate, gellan gum and grapefruid seed extract.

Bottom line for me: I consume about sixteen ounces of this per day, and during exceptionally hot and humid days about twice that. Although this is no substitute for a rehydration drink, it does quench my thirst and the sugar gives me a boost without causing cramps in my fingers and toes like a soda does.

title: Perfect TV Box control
text:
There are some incredibly detailed and helpful reviews of this keyboard, so I will stick to how I am using the review sample that I received, and a few of my impressions.

First, this is not a bluetooth device (it was described as such to me when I was asked to review it.) The only weak point is the documentation, which is terse, but well illustrated. Had it contained specs and compatibility data it would have been significantly more useful. However, this is not a major flaw.

I first tested it with an ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It was immediately recognized and functional. My next test was to see if it would work with my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone running Android 4.4.2. I connected with wireless dongle via a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0 Adapter]] and it worked. To be honest, that arrangement is a bit on the clumsy side for me.

My final test and where this keyboard shines is when I connected it to my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 Smart TV BOX]] running Android 4.2. This keyboard made a lot of sense connected to that box because I rarely used it prior. I was using a corded keyboard and it was a trip hazard. Plus most of in interaction with it included few keystrokes, so this mini keyboard is perfect. In fact I find myself using the TV box a lot more frequently now that I have this keyboard. I think of it as a smart remote control - which it is - and have quickly grown to love it.

As for prolonged typing, this would not be my favorite solution. However, that is subjective. I hated my Blackerry when I was required to carry one back in my consulting days too. But for occasional use this is wonderful.

Bottom line: I would have never guessed that this would be the missing link between me and my TV box. Had I only tested this with phones and tablets I would have probably written a single word review: meh. Now, though, I see the wow factor.

title: Great for folks who love full size KBs
text:
There are some excellent reviews already, so I will attempt to provide my reasons for giving this five stars without repeating what others have said.

The biggest reason for my rating is this keyboard has a great feel. I normally hate chicklet style keys (it reminds me of my very first computer back in the 80s - a Commodore PET), but these are a breeze to type on. A few things I look for in a keyboard are tactile feedback and the elimination of key bounce. The tactile feedback is in the zone that I prefer, which surprised me because I initially thought that this was more of a gimmick than a serious keyboard. Key bounce - when you press a key and more than one of the character appears - is common on cheap keyboards and tha bane of my existence. This keyboard is rock solid and does not suffer from that effect.

I love the weight of the board too. It's not overly heavy, but is heavy enough to stay put on a desk while I am typing. Moreover, while the ability to change the lighted key colors is somewhat cool, I touch type and was happy to discover that I can turn the lights completely off.

One final reason why I awarded this five stars is that I plugged it into my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 Smart TV BOX]] and it worked immediately. I expected that level of plug-n-play from my Windows laptop, but was pleasantly surprised when it also worked seamlessly on the Android as soon as I plugged it in.

This may look like a glitzy keyboard laden with bling, but it's really a pro grade one that fast touch typers will love.

title: Incredibly easy to install and use
text:
When my review sample arrived I tested it on a few devices and it worked perfectly on each. The first device was my ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. I inserted the dongle (look in the battery compartment for it), and it was immediately recognized and activated. As soon as I turned on power to the keyboard I was able to navigate using the touchpad, bring up an editor and type.

The next tests were with my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 1080P 5G 2.4G HDMI Bluetooth 4.0 Smart TV BOX]], then using a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] I connected the dongle to my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Tab 3 10.1 tablet respectively and was texting and performing other functions. This is truly a plug-and-play keyboard/touchpad.

One final thing I love is the battery is a standard BT51 that can be purchased just about anywhere if you are such a power user that you need a spare.

It's set up for thumb style texting, so most folks will be immediately comfortable with it. I love the tactile feedback from the keys, which were a pleasure to type with, as well as the array of function keys and buttons. If you spend a lot of time on smaller devices this is a dream come true. At about thirteen bucks at the time of this review it's a bargain for folks who are heavy texters.

title: Excellent sound and interesting features
text:
First, I will disclose why I gave this speaker only four stars: when the review sample I received arrived it was not very intuitive and the instructions were little help. In fact, it took me ten minutes of fiddling to realize that this is not a bluetooth device and it would have probably taken longer had I not read Comdet's May 27, 2014 review. Mind you I am not subtracting a star because it's direct connect only, but because they instructions were obtuse at best. That is a minor fix on the manufacturer's part and one I hope they rectify.

The sound is absolutely incredible. Not for it's size, but incredible period. The full spectrum of sound frequencies blew me away. The bass is what impressed me the most. Since this is a direct connect only type of speaker you will be listening to it fairly close, so the volume is more than sufficient.

One of the interesting features is you can daisy chain up to three of these together. To be honest I do not see the point since it's designed as a personal speaker, but the technology is embedded in the device and it can be done. This would have been more impressive had this speaker been bluetooth-enabled.

Controls are simple to use and cleverly designed to take up as little space on the unit as possible while still providing an array of functions. I love the SD card slot, but do not much care for the hardwired 3.5MM connector that plugs into a phone port on your tablet, PC or phone. A port and separate cable would have been a better solution since it's one less failure point. As it is, if you break the 3.5MM pigtail you are out of luck unless you can repair cables.

Quibbles aside, this has the makings of a five star product and especially the speaker technology that this is based on. The sound quality is incredible.

title: Gorgeous design and sturdy cover
text:
The motif on the review sample I received is a beautiful example of Mexican folk art. In that respect it's strikingly beautiful and unique. The review sample that I received had a strong chemical odor that was briefly overpowering when I removed the protective cellophane wrapping. I was forewarned about that before the sample arrived. So expect it and do not be alarmed because it dissipates within hours.

Aside from the motif and its vivid colors I loved the texture of the outside of the case. It has a fine, pebble gain feel so it will not get slippery on a wet day or if you are sweaty. The plastic holder into which my iPad 2 snapped provides very good protection. It's thick enough to protect the edges of the iPad, but with enough give to cushion shock. Of course, the outer part of the case does an excellent job of cushioning and absorbing shock if you accidentally drop your iPad. On the inside of the front cover are three strips that augment the cushioning across the screen, which is a nice feature that also shows the attention to detail when this case was designed. They are also the slots that allow you to angle your iPad.

Other features that I love and which inspired me to give this case five stars are the 360 degree rotation, the three viewing angles that should suit most people, and the cutouts. All of the cutouts were precisely done and even the camera one ensured that nothing interfered with the lens or caused flashback that some cheaply made cases do.

I've tested and owned at least a dozen iPad cases and this one is as good as the most expensive ones, but has a design that truly stands out.

title: Best in class for sound, quality and comfort
text:
I have tested a number of in ear monitors (IEMs) from Brainwavz and other brands and the review sample that I received is the best in its price range that I have come across. In fact, it's best in sub one hundred dollar IEMs.

The best feature to me is comfort because I normally do not care for in ear style phones. I can wear these for hours without even noticing them, and they ship with an array of tips that fit just about any ear size.

However, sound ranks right up there with comfort because I listen to a lot of music from a critical perspective as well as enjoyment. Nothing interferes with the sound quality, including ambient noise from the cables or other physical factors, and they do a great job of isolation. Every album to which I listen comes across with no gaps in any of the frequency bands. You can hear any note (and sometimes flaws) that musicians and recording engineers made, which is extremely important to me.

What truly sets these IEMs apart from other phones in its class are is the attention to detail. The cord is tangle free and practically indestructible. I have yet to worry about breaking or wearing out the inner conductor like I do with some other brands I own (including some pretty expensive phones). The plug is gold plated for and at a ninety degree angle - nice touches - and the phones ship with a protective hard case ([[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]]) that is not only convenient, but functional.

If I had to recommend a sub one hundred dollar set of IEMs to a friend or fellow musician these would be it. The performance, comfort and price make them a bargain in my opinion.

title: Works, but for geeks only
text:
I had the same issues with the review sample that I received that rpv's May 10, 2014 described. The camera and accessories are first rate; the documentation is not.

What I like is this is a full solution with various mounts, a waterproof case and all of the cables you need. All you have to do is add an SD card, and you can insert one up to 32GB. To be honest, all you need is a 4GB card since the camera itself will operate for an hour fully charged. For the extreme sports type videos this was designed to capture, an hour is a long time, so the operating time is certainly not a limitation.

Video quality is respectable and after you spend some time experimenting to fill in the gaps in the documentation you will fall in love with the camera. I attempted to use mine mounted to a microphone stand to capture practice sessions with me and a pianist. It can be done, but the results were less than spectacular. However, strapping this to a handlebar or helmet and dirt biking, skydiving or similar activities would result in some priceless shots.

For the right audience this is a great camera. All you need is a 4GB SD card, some technical savvy, and the patience to experiment. If the documentation were better I would give this a solid five stars for what it is and does.

title: New life for my ancient router
text:
Since there are detailed specs in the product description I will not repeat them here. Instead I'll use my personal experience with this kit to explain why I rated it five stars.

I used the review sample I received to extend the range of my ancient [[ASIN:B000BTL0OA Linksys WRT54GL Wireless-G Broadband Router]] (which is still working as well as when I purchased it ten years ago!) I removed one antenna from the Linksys, used a [[ASIN:B005IKGTXY Bluecell SMA female to TNC male Coaxial Adapter/Converter]] to adapt the included cable to the antenna connector, plugged it into the power supply and checked my home dead spot.

My dead spot is the master bedroom and my phone is always complaining about 'unstable WiFi connections' when I am in the room. I used an app called [[ASIN:B004EBZX6W Wi-Fi Analyzer]] to perform the before and after tests.

Before I installed this booster kit I was getting a strong reading of -45 dBm near the router and an absymal -80 dBm in the dead room. After installing this kit the signal boosted to -55 dBm in the bedroom, so this booster kit works as advertised.

It's practically worth its weight in gold if you do have dead areas in your WiFi coverage. Based on my experience and how easy and fast this is to install I rate this as a five star product.

title: Outstanding control & great feel
text:
When my review sample arrived I had no problem connecting it to an old ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. It also connected without fuss to an Android TV box and functioned immediately. On the ThinkPad the settings out of the box took some getting accustomed to because the mouse was super sensitive to my every move.

After downloading the driver and manual - neither of which are included in the box - I was able to fine tune this mouse to my personal movements. In fact, I am not sure I can go back to a plain vanilla mouse again!

I am not going to repeat the very detailed specifications on this page, including actual dimensions, nor am I going to regurgitate the roduct description. I have included user supplied images of the manual and screen shot of the driver menu that will show the incredible array of settings and features. Here are a few of the reasons why I personally love this mouse and awarded it five stars.

First, every possible setting and button a gamer or power user could wish for are included. You can assign just about any function to any button, and set sensitivity levels at the inch-pebble level. Even the lights and display are configurable.

Second, this is a quality product from the braided, five foot cable that will probably outlast my sixty-five year old body, to the buttons, which feel solid and provide excellent tactile feedback.

Finally, while I had to downgrade mine to conform to my less than steady hands, I did use the maximum sensitivity on a few Visio drawings I quickly created. If only I had this mouse when I was a consultant who cranked out system and network diagrams like a demon possessed. As it is, the shape feels natural and ergonomic under my hand. And for good reason: the design provides for two controlling points (index and/or middle finger and thumb), and a pressure point where your palm rests and a support point at the heel of your hand.

I could babble on and on, but the images I uploaded show most of the settings and an overview of the mouse. As for the lack of documentation and drivers in the box. that is a smart move because you can download the freshest ones as soon as you log onto their site (URL is printed on the front of the box).

title: Buy it for the sound
text:
This speaker has some convenient features like hands-free calling and receiving calls, but it's the sound quality that makes it stand out.

Before I list the many things I love (and why I awarded this five stars) I want to toss out the one thing that is keeping this speaker from being totally perfect: the older generation bluetooth pairing and connecting process. The newer generation of bluetooth speakers automatically beacon their presence when you turn them on. This one requires you to hold down a multifunction button for six seconds before you initiate a scan on your phone or tablet. It's not a big issue or deal breaker, but this would be the perfect speaker otherwise.

It is all about the sound and the review sample I received from the manufacturer passed my usual tests with flying colors. Among the tests are playing a handful of favorite jazz albums. The main one I always use us Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B003GIK2LU Kind Of Blue]] because it exercises a speaker's ability to reproduce the full spectrum of frequencies in the low, mid and high ranges. A truly great speaker will also reproduce the nuances from the natural reverb effect of the 30th Street Studio in NYC where it was recorded. This speaker did!

As I listened through this speaker I wondered how it would sound with something a little more in your face than circa 1950s acoustic jazz. I grabbed some old rock albums, dusted them off and gave them a spin.

Since I am sixty-five my idea of rock is probably ancient music to many folks. However, back in the day the following albums did stretch the woofers in stereo systems: [[ASIN:B001NCT8X4 Fresh Cream]] (Jack Bruce's bass and Ginger Baker's double bass drum kit came through as though I were in a small club), and [[ASIN:B0011Z5IUK Led Zeppelin II]] (same for John Paul Jones' bass and John Bonham's drums, especially on The Lemon Song).

Part of the reason the sound is so full and rich is the 360 degree speaker coverage. Another factor is the design raises the main speaker cabinet about a quarter of an inch off the base of the unit. This allows the low end frequencies to reflect a bit and sound deeper. Do be aware, though, that this is not an exceptionally loud speaker. It's perfect for most listening up to five meters away. That's about fifteen feet, so you can crank it pretty loud relative to its size, but as you increase the volume beyond three quarters the fidelity drops if you are too close. At the three quarter mark and a distance of five meters you can hear every note and nuance in the older jazz recordings with which I tested this speaker, and pretty good fidelity with the older rock albums.

If you listen to music with a critical ear this speaker is one that you should consider if you are shipping for a bluetooth model. Obviously there are wired speakers that are better, but in the bluetooth domain this is one of the best that I have tried from a sound perspective.

title: Works with a Galaxy Note 3 battery
text:
When I first received a review sample I was dismayed because the specs claimed that it would only fit batteries that are between 42 and 71 millimeters in length. In inches that works out to be 1.65 to 2.79 inches.

In actual fact, that dimension should have read width instead of length because my long Samsung Galaxy Note 3 battery (which is in excess of three inches long) not only fit, but charged perfectly. I also tested this on an HTC Driod Incredible and it worked perfectly on that phone's battery as well. There is a spring-loaded arm that opens to accept batteries with widths within the range I cited above, and they hold the battery firmly in place during the charging cycle.

What I love is the ability to charge a spare battery while simultaneously charging a phone with a battery installed. That feature makes this perfect as a travel charger (the folding prongs add to the function for that use. It is also ideal as an office charger for folks who frequently spend most of their work day in the field.

Do heed the two prominent notices in the specs (1) it is ONLY for phone batteries, and (2) it will only work with batteries that have contact points on the end (not the front of back). Indeed, the contacts on your battery (the metal strips that mate with your phone) cannot be closer than 3/8 inch from the edge of the battery, nor more than 5/8 inch away. If they fall outside of that range then this charger will not work for you.

For batteries that do fit this charger will automatically detect the type and capacity and charge it properly. So there is some intelligence built into the circuitry.

These are great for those of us who have spare batteries for our phones and want to keep them charged and ready to go. It worked perfectly on the phones with which I tested it. Measure and examine your battery before ordering to save disappointment.

title: Great idea well executed
text:
For bicycle enthusiasts this is an excellent speaker/radio combination that has decent sound and a lot of convenient touches. I received mine as a review sample from the manufacturer.

I'll cover the sound quality first. In a word, it's adequate. Not overly spectacular, but sufficiently loud to be heard over road noise while trekking through streets and paths. I do not view the quality as a problem because in most biking environments the sound level is more important than fidelity. Plus, the safety factor of having a hands-free solution is the major reason for getting one of these.

What impressed me is when I turned this on all I had to do is scan for bluetooth devices from my phone and it popped right up. I did not have to press a multifunction button and chant, hoping the device would show up like other bluetooth speakers - it was immediately there.

Another thing I love is the buttons are on the top of the case and when the speaker is turned on they light up blue. I have stationary speakers which have buttons that blend into the case so well I cannot readily find them, so this feature removes one major distraction when you are on the road. In the dark the lights are soft enough to not affect your night vision. The only improvement that I can think of is to use red lights instead of blue because those would actually promote night vision. Perhaps the designers will do that in the next generation.

Some of the other nice touches are the ample inside space for a phone and other incidentals, plus a ring clip on the outside for your keys. I also love the three point attachment to your handle bar and steering post. It is easy to attach and remove. In fact, that takes mere seconds.

Having a removable battery is yet another design factor that makes this a value. Most bluetooth speakers on the market have a fixed, internal battery that will eventually wear out. When the battery in this one inevitably dies you can quickly replace it with a new [[ASIN:B0006HP7NC BL-5C Extended Li-Ion Battery]] and you are good to go another 500 or so charging cycles.

Finally, the semi-hard case, heavy duty zipper and construction are all first rate and clearly designed by someone who understands the rigors of biking when it comes to gear. This entire unit is built to withstand the outdoors in most weather conditions.

title: When you need one - you NEED one!
text:
This is a great way to use HDMI devices on TVs that have no spare HDMI ports or are not equipped with one. I tested the review sample that I received on a 2008 Sanyo TV that came equipped with two HDMI ports that I quickly occupied with a Roku and a Chromecast, and with a 2011 model Samsung. Both displayed the transformed signal from this box beautifully.

It has come excellent features like the array of color encoding schemes and outputting either the most common PAL and NTSC ones with the flip of a switch. I also love that this is powered via USB, which one of my TVs as, so it's one less wall wart.

Do be aware that this only converts in one direction: HDMI in (from Blu-Ray players, etc) to composite out via RCA jacks on a TV or monitor. I tested this going the other direction - RCA to HDMI - and it did not work. Of course it was not advertised as such, but I felt compelled to try anyway. I would love it if I could flip a switch and change directions of the signal transformation because I could then connect my old VHS player to an HDMI port on my TV.

Regardless of my personal wishes, this does exactly what it claims with no problems or issues, and that merits five stars according to how I rate.

title: Excellent entry level IEM
text:
The review sample that I received proved to be a nice, low-to-mid range In Ear Monitor (IEM). It can compete with much more expensive IEMs from both Brainwavz and competing brands. To keep my evaluation in this brand I am going to compare the review sample of this model to two other Brainwavz IEMs: [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]] and the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]]. To provide some context please bear in mind that I listen primarily to acoustic jazz, so my listening needs may be vastly different from yours.

The first thing I do with I test phones or speakers is to play Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] to get a feel for how well the various frequencies are reproduced. That album has instruments in the low, mid and high bands, and these phones seemed to have more bass than the R1 or the S1. The mids and highs on those models, though, had more clarity. I tried a few other albums that had heavier bass and these definitely did a better job of reproducing those frequencies. When I switched to some tracks with female vocalists the R1 and S1 were better phones, and both of the other phones were clearer with higher register instruments.

From a comfort perspective these phones were a little lighter than the other two IEMs against which I compared them, although I would consider it a tie among them for overall comfort. These phones and the R1 had a value-added bonus in that a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] is included.

These are obviously designed for lower end audio gear like MP3 players, phones and tablets. For higher end audio in the audiophile range I would probably use the S1 model because to my ears that one sounds better. However, you cannot go wrong with this one for everyday use when you want to listen to your music without disturbing others.

title: These won me over
text:
Prior to receiving this review sample I was happy with in-ear type phones, but always grabbed headphones when I wanted to listen to music without disturbing others, These phones changed that. For one thing they are super comfortable. For another the sound is incredible. In fact I have been testing various phones - mainly from this brand, but also some Sennheiser models - and this is head and shoulders above the pack.

I'll be honest and disclose that comfort edges out sound when phones sound good enough. I will normally not quibble over a few hundred Hz one way or the other as long as I can wear the phones without noticing them. These are not only unobtrusive, but downright comfortable, which is a major reason why these have now replaced my trusty [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]].

Soundwise the specs do not begin to describe the richness, especially bass. In fact, when I read the 20 Hz to 20 MHz range I thought that the sound would be somewhat generic for phones in this range. I own a pair of IEMs (in-ear monitors) that go as low as 18 Hz at the same 95dB at 1mW sensitivity, yet these sound much deeper than those. I love the balance of sound across the frequency spectrum as though it's on a smooth continuum. Every one of my test albums I played through these phones sounded so good that I decided that it's time to hang up the headphones and go with these.

Part of the reason why I love these from a comfort perspective is the over the ear memory wire. I prefer that style, but not everyone does. They are definitely stiff and take on a shape that will be uniquely yours over time (and a very short time at that!) Also, while this ships with a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] the phones will not fit after you have contoured them to your ear. The case is useful for carrying around the array of adapters and tips that are included. In fact, the final reason I love these phones is the included triple-flange style silicon tips, which block out the rest of the world and allow me to focus solely on music.

If you love music and want to hear every note faithfully reproduced in their natural frequencies these phones are it. I can honestly say that I have not used a better set of phones from any brand in this price range, including some Sennheiser models that have a street price of fifty to seventy-five dollars more than these, so the value is definitely there.

title: Perfect for casual listening
text:
I own a number of Brainwavz models, all of which compare favorably to more expensive in ear monitors (IEMs). I am going to compare the review sample of this model to two other Brainwavz IEMs: [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]] and the [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]]. What I will try to avoid is repeating the other reviews - many of which are excellent - and the product specs on this page. Here are my impressions of these phones. Bear in mind that I listen primarily to acoustic jazz, so my listening needs may be vastly different from yours.

The first thing I do with I test phones or speakers is to play Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]] to get a feel for how well the various frequencies are reproduced. That album has instruments in the low, mid and high bands, and these phones seemed to have more bass than the R1 or the S1. The mids and highs on those models, though, had more clarity. I tried a few other albums that had heavier bass and these definitely did a better job of reproducing those frequencies. When I switched to some tracks with female vocalists the R1 and S1 were better phones, and both of the other phones were clearer with higher register instruments.

From a comfort perspective these phones were a little lighter than the other two IEMs against which I compared them, although I would consider it a tie among them for overall comfort. These phones and the R1 had a value-added bonus in that a [[ASIN:B00HPPL1M4 Brainwavz Hard Earphone Case]] is included.

My conclusion is these are nice low-to-mid range IEMs that can compete with much more expensive IEMs from both Brainwavz and competing brands. I am impressed with the quality, completeness of the solution and the way these sound on lower end audio gear like MP3 players, phones and tablets. For higher end audio I would probaby use the S1 model because to my ears that one sounds better. However, you cannot go wrong with this one for everyday use when you want to listen to your music without disturbing others.

title: Convenient if you use your phones a lot
text:
Shortly after I received this as a review sample it quickly became a permanent part of my home studio. Right now my [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]] are mounted for immediate use, and I tested this with some smaller phones I also use like the [[ASIN:B0002F74E8 Sony MDR7502 Professional Stereo Headphone]] and they fit perfectly as well.

This is a tall, thin stand that measures ten inches tall with a relatively short five inch base. Despite the proportions this sits stably and is not apt to tip if you accidentally bump into it. I love the contoured top over which the phones rest. That holds the phones in a natural shape. For expensive phones that is not especially a problem because the over the head mechanisms on those devices are usually very well made.

The material (I am guessing plexi-glass) is 8mm thick (about a third of an inch), and is flexible. Complaints about the large logo are valid if you want a cleaner look, but since I am currently using Brainwavz headphones - and this is in my music studio - the aesthetics are a non-issue for me. I care more about function and convenient storage and this stand provides both of those.

For me the convenience of having my phones readily available is important because I use them often. This stand is an inexpensive way of accomplishing that.

title: Not just for Brainwavz products
text:
This case came bundled with my [[ASIN:B009UNZ5WQ Brainwavz R1 In Ear Noise Isolating Earphones]] and I was struck by how nicely made and perfect it is. I will not parrot the other excellent reviews on this page with regard to physical characteristics, but will confirm that they are spot on.

Although these are bundled with a Brainwavz product do not let that deter you if you have invested in another brand because these will work with most of them. I tested the fit with the following phones and they are a perfect match:

[[ASIN:B001EZYMF4 Sennheiser CX 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass Earbuds]]
[[ASIN:B004PO10E2 Shure SE215-CL Sound Isolating Earphones]]
[[ASIN:B000XPG2QI Etymotic Research HF5 Portable In-Ear Earphones]]

Of course I also tested them with the [[ASIN:B00G4UQ6U8 Brainwavz S1 In Ear Headphones]] which I expected to fit and they did. Although many of the phones with which I tested these come with their own case, none of them are are as sturdy or as protective as this one. For low-end phones this will probably outlast the phones themselves, and will be ready their their replacement. For the higher end phones this is an investment - and an inexpensive one at they - for protecting the instrument from damage.

title: A real contender
text:
I had the opportunity to directly compare my review sample to the [[ASIN:B001EZYMF4 Sennheiser CX 300 II Precision Enhanced Bass Earbuds]], which is a highly regarded IEM (in ear monitor) in the same price range. This one actually sounded better to my ears although both were nearly identical in specifications.

This is my third Brainwavz phone model, and I have quickly come to regard this brand as a real contender in the market. I will not lie - I much prefer the [[ASIN:B00ENZRS76 Brainwavz HM9 Hi-Fi Noise Isolating Headphones]] model because I love over-the-hear style phones. However, this set of phones, at about a third of the cost, is also close in sound quality as the HM9. In fact, the bass in this one is much better than the HM9 (or the Sennheiser CX 300 II to which I am directly comparing these.)

For me comfort is everything because I listen to music much of my time. These are perfect for both pleasure listening where I sit back and enjoy the music for its own sake. These are also good enough for me to hear every nuance when I am transcribing or studying a track to learn. In that respect these phones are good enough for professional musicians, but I will admit that they would not be my first choice for plugging into a high-end sound system.

Since I spend more time listening to MP3 tracks than off vinyl these do the job since MP3 files lose some fidelity by their very nature. I will say, though, that these phones passed my basic test suite, which includes Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B00136JQMI Kind Of Blue]]. That is my reference model for sound because it contains high, mid and low frequency instruments that exercise any sound system. I listened to that album both from CD and from an MP3 file. Reproduction was superb.

Not only do these phones have respectable sound and comfort, the package is complete. They come with a zippered hard shell case, which protects the phones. However, they come with more extras that add to the value and provide versatility: a 1/4 adapter for plugging directly into standard headphone jacks, and an airplane adapter.

If you are in the market for mid-range IEMs give these serious consideration. In my opinion they are easily the equal of better known brands like the Sennheiser I mentioned and can be a better value if you need the extras that this set includes.

title: As good as the OEM cable that shipped with my Note 3
text:
I wanted a spare charging cable for my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and took a chance on this one. By that I mean that that other USB 3.0 cables that I have tried with the phone would charge it, but would not support full speed data transfers and synching. This one performed without issues and identically to my OEM Samsung cable that came with my phone.

The blue outer jacket is much thicker than the Samsung cable. Although it is slightly stiffer it's also pliable and easy to bend and coil. Part of the reason for the extra thickness is probably from the the foil and braid shielding. In fact, the shielding is one factor in this cable's ability to transmit data at such high speeds without error. Another factor is the gold plated connectors.

The bottom line is this cable seems to be the equal of the more expensive Samsung OEM cable. In my experience anyway. I have owned it for three months and it has been problem free in every respect.

title: Love the size and performance
text:
My desk gets crowded with the bulky 10-port USB hub I had been using so when this review sample arrived I was immediately pleased with the size. It is the perfect complement to my ThinkPad T61 which comes with three USB ports to begin with.

I will not repeat the exceptionally helpful review that Daisy S posted on February 11, 2014 - she thoroughly tested the specs and gave some pointers for also using this via the OTG interface on tablets. This also works on any OTG-capable phone using her approach because I tested it on my Galaxy Note 3.

A big plus is this not only works with USB 3.0 interfaces, but is backward compatible to earlier versions of the USB spec, including 1.0. That means that I can use this on my legacy devices around the house, as well as my newer 'toys'.

The final thing that I like about this hub is the construction. The manufacturer did not cut corners on cable gauge and the small details like strain relief, precision made connectors and other areas that cheaper brands do. The quality is there and this does work as advertised.

title: Excellent (and affordable) basic protection
text:
What I love about this case is the value. Most of the ones I checked out in the usual brick and mortar stores were priced at two to three times the cost of this one, and none of those seemed to be any more substantial than this one when it came to aesthetics, function and protection.

This case has all three. Although it's synthetic leather it looks like the real thing. So much so in fact that it goes perfectly with the [[ASIN:B00ESAGVLK Bear Motion for Galaxy Note 3 100% Genuine Lambskin Folio Case]] that I purchased for my Galaxy Note 3 phone.

Functionally it is a snug fit that provides me access to all buttons, ports and features of my Tab 3 except the SD card slot, which is covered. I view this as a plus, though, because I do not have to worry about the slot cover popping open and losing the SD card. I love how thin this case is - it's like a book. I also love the way a magnet holds the cover closed when the tablet is not in use.

The protection is basic and perfect for in home or office use. It is not for use in harsher environments, so factor that into your purchase decision. For what I do, it's perfect.

Bottom line: for the price this cover is hard to beat. There are no major flaws or problems that I can find after extensively using this with my Tab 3. If you are looking for basic protection with no frills this is worth checking out.

title: Perfect for primary and temp storage
text:
I have tested this card in both a Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and a [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 (10.1-Inch]] and it was immediately recognized by both devices. As I write this review the card has been running in my Tab 3 and constantly used for over a week.

Other reviews have dissected the specs of this card, so I'll share how I use it and why I prefer these over the 64GB cards (which I also own and use). The price point on these 32GB cards have dramatically fallen and as of the date of this review they are priced as commodities. I use a few pairs of these to rotate backups on my laptop, so I always have a daily snapshot of my documents. For that purpose alone these cards are well worth it.

For my tablet I have divided my extensive music library into genres and have them backed up to these cards. A 32GB card will hold about 150 CDs, so the space savings along over the physical media is significant. In fact one of these cards cost about the same as a rack for 150 CDs.

These are also excellent for saving practice sessions that I sometimes record using my phone or tablet. I pop my primary SD card out of the device and swap one of these in to video record. Since this card will hold about six hours of video it's perfect for that use.

Overall, these are reliable cards that have worked in a number of devices I own. I can assure anyone wanting to use them in a newer Samsung Note 2 or 3 phone or Tab 3 tablet that this card will work, and it is also excellent for HD video recording. At the price point it's an absolute bargain.

title: Excellent sound for some types of music and very comfortable
text:
I tested these on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone and my Tab 3 tablet and was impressed with the sound. Note: I always test using a Miles Davis album titled Kind of Blue because the instrumentation covers the high, mid and low frequency bands. However, the acoustic bass in jazz is different than electric bass in modern music so factor that into my comments when making a purchase decision. I did try a few tracks on an album with with electric bass that were not as deep sounding. Bottom line: for jazz these are superb, and especially for acoustic jazz that was recorded in the 1950s, but I am not sure about other genres of music.

What I love is the comfort of the ear buds. Normally I avoid them, but I received these as a review sample so decided to wear them and listen for a few hours straight. I found that the small ear tips that shipped with these fir me the best, although the medium ones were comfortable too. The large pair were definitely 'large', so there is a tip size for everyone. I did not care for the foam tips, preferring the silicon ones, but that is my personal preference and not an opinion of which is better. I was able to wear these for hours without the chaffing or discomfort that other bud-style phones cause me. One note: once in-ear the tips eliminated a lot of ambient noise, which allowed me to listen critically to the music itself. That is a big plus for in home (or in studio) use, but I would not recommend wearing these while driving because it cuts down on outside noise to the point that you may be unaware of traffic situations.

Another thing I love is the relatively long cable, which is slightly over four feet long. In my home studio it allows me to practice to backing tracks on my tablet what is usually on a nearby music stand. I also appreciate the fact that the connectors are gold plated, which ensures a good, clean signal to the phones.

Bottom line: these are relatively inexpensive phones with performance that can compete with phones costing two to three times as much. The sound is superior for the types of music I enjoy, but the bass may be too light for some modern, bass and drum heavy music.

title: Wow! But be careful if there are children around
text:
UPDATE August 18, 2014. I just received a newer model without the USB ports (the [[ASIN:B00KBO619E Arctic Breeze USA]]. Aside from the patriotic USA motif, this model has some improvements. First, the fan blades have a more efficient pitch and size, so it throws a nice breeze. I have mine running next to the earlier model and the difference between the two are significant.

A second feature is this newer model is safer. I can put my finger into the spinning blade and it will stop without as much as a nick. The earlier model that I reviewed below was a safety hazard around small children. This one has corrected that issue. In all other respects the two models are very close in specs. [END OF UPDATE]

About six months ago I tested and reviewed the smaller version of this fan: [[ASIN:B003XN24GY ARCTIC Breeze Mobile]]. When I was provided with this one as a review sample I was able to compare the two side-by-side. This one is hands down a more sophisticated and functional cooling solution.

I love this one because it is serious competition to my [[ASIN:B0000DJ27I Lasko #2500 12" Oscillating Table Fan]], and this one takes far less power to operate and the breeze can be focused. On warm days this is a godsend, but it also works to keep my hot running laptop cool. It's also so quiet that I cannot hear it three feet away.

A key difference between this model and the earlier one is this has a variable speed knob that allows me to go from a light 800 RPM to a very brisk 1800 RPM. One caveat is at the higher speeds this fan cannot be stopped with your fingers like the earlier model and there is no fan guard. This is a safety hazard if small children are around and is not a solution I recommend if that's the case where this will be used.

Another thing I love is the earlier model was a gooseneck that plugged directly into a USB port. This one has a cable that is just a little short of six feet and can be placed a lot more conveniently. The base is very heavy, so there is little chance of knocking it over, and the base also contains four USB ports. Note that these are 2.0 only.

You can plug this directly into your PC or laptop, but I also found that the Samsung wall charger that came with my Galaxy Note 3 will power this fan as well.

Bottom line is this is a great cooling solution for child-free work areas, and it will definitely cause rapid cooling at the full 1800 RPM setting.

title: Works perfectly on some devices, not so well with others
text:
Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy.

Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear.

I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars.

Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store.

Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.

title: Great price and excellent performance
text:
Because of the low price I almost passed on this card because it was suspiciously low. I am glad I didn't because this not only works perfectly in my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] tablet, but I also tested it in my Galaxy Note 3 phone with the same results.

I have not exhaustively tested the read and write specs and probably will not. I have put this card through its paces by first doing an over the air transfer from my music library on my phone to this card on my tablet. I transferred over 30GB of files that literally took hours. Cards that I have used in the past would have hiccuped with transmission errors or overheating. For this one I experienced no lags, I/O errors or overheating. That is the true test for me.

During my tests this card easily kept up with the more expensive [[ASIN:B00AK31M3G Samsung micro SDXC UHS-1 Card PRO 64GB Class 10]] model in my Note 3 phone. That is all the evidence that I personally need that this is a quality SD card.

At the time of this review his card is priced forty percent less than the Samsung card I have in my phone and the performance is roughly the same for my purposes. That, to me, is the definition of value and the reason why I rated this at five stars.

title: Works perfectly for my uses
text:
This is not the best adapter in the world, but I knew that going in. I use mine to transform a 3.5mm jack in a [[ASIN:B004VQDAQK Powerwerks PW50 Portable PA System]] into a third channel and this adapter works perfectly for that.

Note that I am not expecting stereo signals and have not tested this adapter to ensure that it supports that function.

Reading over other reviews complaining about flimsy construction and myriad other problems leads me to conclude that the adapter I received is a new and improved version. It's not particularly flimsy and both sides mate with their respective plugs with no tolerance issues.

Since I am using this to reclaim a channel on a relatively inexpensive powered mixer I cannot comment on signal quality. It's not especially noisy, but on the other hand if I were using this to enjoy music through headphones I would have probably purchased a higher quality adapter.

Bottom line: I am pleased with this adapter, but note that you do get what you pay for. If you want a quick fix like for what I am using mine for it's a bargain. If you want an adapter for high end stereo gear you may want to consider a higher end adapter like the [[ASIN:B0002E51CQ Planet Waves 1/8 Inch Female Stereo to 1/4 Inch Male Stereo Adapter]].

title: Surprisingly great feel
text:
I received a review sample and tested this on an ancient Acer One netbook running Windows XP. The netbook immediately recognized the wireless dongle that is included with this keyboard and I had the keyboard operational in minutes after inserting the included rechargeable batteries and charging them up.

Frankly, I thought I would hate the keys because they resembled the 'chicklet' style of a circa 1977 Commodore Pet's keys. These, though, have beautiful tactile feedback and are exceptionally responsive. You can touch type at at least 120 words per minute (my max) with no problems.

Although this key board comes with a retractable USB cable, that is for charging the two batteries that power the unit. This is strictly a wireless device, so you will need a spare USB port for the required dongle, and access to one or a wall charger that accepts USB cables to recharge the batteries when they run down. You can go two months between charges as long as you remember to switch the keyboard off between uses. There is an on/off switch on the underside of the board.

One final feature I love is this keyboard has some heft to it. It is not going to slide across your desk like some cheap, flimsy ones that I have tried in the past. The bottom line is of all of the portable keyboards that I have tested (well over two dozen), this one is the best of the bunch for me. The size and feel earn it five solid stars.

title: Precise, but has a learning curve
text:
I received a review sample and after I got this up and running there was a slight learning curve before it felt natural. After I did become accustomed to it, going back to a regular mouse was a slight letdown.

While the instructions are a bit terse I am still giving this four stars because it's easy to set up. The subtracted star is for lack of clear explanations in the quick start guide for how to precharge the unit or even for explaining that the retractable USB cable that ships with it is only for charging and will not connect the mouse interface to the host system.

This mouse operates wirelessly via an included dongle. My old ThinkPad running Windows XP immediately recognized the dongle when I plugged it in, and the mouse as soon as I inserted the included battery and charged it up.

Once I became comfortable with the mouse I found that it was a lot more precise for graphics applications and games than a regular mouse. Note that the base is fixed to the pen-style handle. You move it as though it's a pen affixed to a sled. After you become accustomed to the buttons and the wheel placement you will be using this like a pro.

There is a LED on the top of the unit that shows the charging state. Once that light turns green you can disconnect the USB charging cable. I initially did not like this feature, but have grown to love it because the battery is rechargeable. Other wireless mice I have used in the past seemed to have a voracious appetite for batteries, so plus one for the rechargeable feature.

Bottom line: this is an excellent mouse that is less stressful than using a normal one. Set-up is a bit confusing, but if you have issues leave questions in a comment to this review and I will answer them to the best of my ability. If the company redesigns the documentation to make it clear to complete novices this would be a five star product.

title: Superior construction and extra long cable
text:
I received a review sample of this cord and charger combination and have been testing it thoroughly. The most striking feature is the three meter cable, which is the longest I have seen for any iPhone (or Android phone for that matter.)

My first inclination was to test the cable for failures because the length seemed excessive. It performed every data transfer and synching operation flawlessly. It also fast-charges like an Apple OEM cable. I was a bit surprised that this and the charger were not MFi certified (Made for iPhone/iPod/iPad). Other cables and chargers that I have received from the manufacturer were, but this is indistinguishable from the MFi and Apple OEM cables that I have tested - both visually and from a performance perspective.

The contacts on both the USB and Lightning connector ends are precision made and mate perfectly to the ports to which they were designed to connect. The outer jacket is thick, but not too stiff to make handling it a problem. There are strain reliefs on both ends to ensure a long service life.

This set includes a bonus wall charger with folding prongs. This has the same well made construction, and also puts out a steady 2.1A for fast charging. This charger is perfect for iPads too because of the output rating. If I had one wish it would have a second 1.0A port for those of us who want to simultaneously charge a phone and tablet - perhaps the next generation of this product will have that feature.

Bottom line: when size (in the form of cable length) matters this is one of the very few on the market that is a full three meters long. Add in the fact that this one is made to perform like an Apple OEM cable and the value should be apparent.

title: Great product that is being marketed to the wrong demographic
text:
When I accepted a review sample of this holder I had visions of using it to entice my constant companion to sit in the back and play with her iPad. Indeed, this hooked right onto the two posts of the front seat headrest that would allow a backseat passenger to watch movies and do whatever else they use the iPad for. My companion did not take the bait, so I was left with a review sample that, frankly, I could not give away.

Necessity is the mother of invention and the best use for this mount was in my music room. This hooks into my [[ASIN:B000CDUDQG Belmonte Orchestra Stand Deluxe Black]] to mount an iPad and still have room left for sheet music and a [[ASIN:0961470143 The New Real Book - Volume 1]].
