title: Perfect... for my needs
text:
I have had the latest gen Kindle DX since October 2010. I am a singer in a choir and use it to display my sheet music. It is well suited to my needs. The display is clear and crisp and is the size of a standard music hymnal. The catch is getting the music onto the device. Most publishers are starting to provide PDF versions of at least melody with accompaniment. However, being an alto in a choir, that isn't sufficient. I need the 3 or 4 part choral version. Also, it is formatted for an 8.5 x 11 inch page with headers, footers, and page numbers. I only need the music staff and lyrics. So I do it the hard way. I scan my (purchased & owned) hymnal or sheet music, crop it down to what I need, then convert it to a PDF. Lots of work, but the payoff is worth it. I no longer carry around 100+ lbs of sheet music and hymnals twice a week! Keep in mind this isn't for everyone. It requires a lot of time and patience, but once the music has been prepped and imported, it's done and ready when you need it. I assume after a year I'll have perhaps 80% of my library scanned. Then I'll only need 5-10 minutes each week to add the relevant music to a collection for quick access.

I also use the Kindle not so much for reading, but for listening. I love the text-to-speech feature. I use it for casual reading as well as my Cisco tech books. Funky digital voice and some unusual phrasing and pronunciation, but you can't beat having it read to you while your hands and eyes are otherwise engaged in other things such as driving or crocheting :D

I have used the web feature while camping. Nothing great, but you can check email, news, Facebook and other text or mobile supported sites. I've also used it when traveling to get directions or check Yelp while on the go. Since I don't have a smart phone this is actually a huge plus! One thing to keep in mind is that image intensive sites may crash the Kindle (due to lack of memory) and you will have to reload it to clear the issue.

The music player is lacking, but for an e-reader, I guess that's expected. You can load music and it will play in the order you loaded it. You can pause and skip, but that's about it. No actual controls or playlist features.

One major feature that is currently lacking is hands free page turning. Since there is no USB driver or bluetooth support, I don't foresee this ever being available, but it is definitely something to keep in mind. I also play flute and am unable to use the Kindle to display my flute music unless it is a single page.

So, for my needs, it's great. However, if you're looking for more media support or better web access, you should look elsewhere.

title: Contender for best mouse I've owned
text:
Contender for best mouse I've owned, going up against the Logitech g900. They are very different mice, for different people though.

PROS:
-excellent feel. the ergonomics are on point, and it's honestly a pleasure to hold. slides nicely on any surface, weight is perfect, and fatigue is zero.
-separate buttons. so tired of the trend of mice that have one piece of plastic on top, rather than individual cut out buttons. (e.g. razer deathadder) it looks nice, but feels like crap.
-the auto switch scroll mechanism. I miss it on all other mice now. my G900 has a mechanical button to switch modes, and while that is nice, it's not as incredibly satisfying and intuitive as the MX master
-beautiful. my office mates are jealous
-LONG battery life. I forget it needs to be charged after 3 weeks to a month, which is about when it starts blinking at me. (I use it 4-8 hours a day at work), and when it does charge, the charge port is in a perfect place to not impede your work.
-excellent bluetooth. I leave it on my desk at night, and when sit down with my laptop it wakes right up and immediately works. I've had some input lag issues with it, but those are few and far between, and can be fixed by flipping the switch.

Neutral:
-the side scroll wheel. It's a nice feature, but doesn't respond all that well in GIMP or chrome. it's always either too sensitive or not enough. that said, it's the best side wheel i've ever used. they must be hard to do right or something.

CONS:
-mine came with a bump in the scroll wheel, due to bad molding. normally this wouldn't be a complaint, but for a $100 mouse (at time of purchase) it better be absolutely perfect.
-back and forward buttons are tiny. you get used to them for sure, but a more conventional layout would be a lot better, and more efficient.
-the gesture control button. might as well have just omitted it. It has its uses, but it's so awkward to press (the actual button is on the seam of the plastic and the metal) that it is 99% of the time easier to just do the thing the gesture was replacing. now, if the button had been under where your thumb rests naturally, this might have been in the pros category.
-the omission of side clicks on the scroll wheel. I can see why they wouldn't on a non-gaming mouse, but I would like them just to assign controls to.

title: Great case for my first serious build (i bought it ...
text:
Great case for my first serious build (i bought it a while ago). It's still in use, and I would really recommend it for a first timer or a pro

Pros:
-active cooling is awesome. watching the fins come up when i open a game is pretty sweet.
-great looking in a room. It's kind of a monster, so this is subjective, but it definitely lets people know there is serious power inside.
-SO MUCH STORAGE. seriously I ran out of SATA ports before i ran out of drive space.
-excellent cooling. my roommate has a similar build as mine in a phanteks case that gets uncomfortably warm.
-lots of room for modding or decoration. for the DIY inclined i would strongly recommend it
-the GPU holder is a great addition

CONS:
-didn't fit my motherboard. did not have the correct standoff holes for an MSI 970-A KRAIT edition, which i believe is a standard ATX motherboard. The right side of the motherboard is to this day completely unsupported. this makes changing RAM a pretty scary endeavor.
-a PSU basement would be nice
-the front dust filter sucks. it is removable, but i would much rather see something more like the PSU filter than the flimsy grate thing that sits behind the door.
-the fins on the top don't line up too well. again, at this price point I don't expect the mercedes of cases, but I would gladly pay more to see satisfyingly perfect alignment in the plastic bits.
-it looks great from far away, but once you start building in it, you notice that a lot of the parts are a bit cheap

Inexpensive - especially when it's on sale. You can upgrade a couple of times over the course of a couple of years and still pay less than you would pay for an IPAD, for example, so if you don't need any specific high end functions that the IPad has, then this is probably a better deal
Customer service - I had a technical issue with one of the first ones I ever owned and it happened over a year after I bought. Cumulatively, they spent a couple of hours on the phone with me and never once said they couldn't help me because it was out of warranty.

title: May or may not last
text: It's lightweight and works the way it's supposed to, for now, but I just got it and it seems kind of flimsy. I got a paper cut from the edges, if that tells you anything. Something tells me it's not going to have a long life but we'll see. It's Nov, 2018, I'll update if it falls apart.

title: 2 cards lost
text: had in wallet and have lost 2 cards worth $30+ dollars. Cards slip out easily. Spend a few dollars more for something more secure

title: Stable desktop unit
text: Better than power strips for me because I can keep it on my desk without having to worry about it slipping, or needing to mount it to do stabilize it. There's also plenty of space for plugs. One of these has easily accomplished what it took two to do before that left cords strewn about. The chargers seem to work fine. It would be nice to have usb ports on more than one side,though

title: Easy setup
text: It's only been a week, so take it for what it's worth. First, it was extremely easy to setup. The instructions are simple. I had the router and five devices up and running in minutes with no hiccups whatsoever. Secondly, my speed increased dramatically. I've only had to reboot once.

title: Just what I was looking for.
text:
I give it 5 stars with 2 caveats. First, it's not stated in the description that it recognizes fewer formats when in BT mode and the instructions seem to be lacking in detail, so it took a while to figure out how to access all of the functions. Hint: You can only access playback functions while in BT because BT, itself, is a sub-folder, so you have to back out of BT to do other things.

Ultimately, I gave it 5 stars because a) i had just a few songs in the missing formats and b) once I got past the navigation issues, it works quite well and the company was very helpful when I needed them.

Update: Turns out as I loaded more music I found a lot more music that wasn't found while in BT, including some albums where some of the songs appeared and some didn't. Al in all, it's kind of clumsy to navigate in BT and BT was the feature I wanted most.

However, it sounds good with the earbuds that they provide and it's size makes it convenient. The 8gb are plenty if you don't have a lot of music. I do, so I added a 32gb sd mini-card which is as large as it will take.

title: Use trifold as hand grip and speakers covered
text:
It fits snugly and has a nice grip. The trifold works well as a grip when folded and you're sitting upright. Particularly helpful if you have average or small hands.
However, there seem to be two kinds of covers: ones that have slots for the speakers and ones that don't. This one is the latter. Not a problem if you use headphones but if you plan on relying on these speakers ( which i don't) then you'll have to turn up the volume and itll still be a muffled.

title: Worth the price
text: It works great. I had an issue that is turned out to be something I had done wrong and the vendor quickly solved my problem. It's compact, making it very portable.

title: a terrific device.
text:
The 10" is great for movies and reading things that begin with small type and need to be enlarged. One issue I've always had with 6" Fires and Kindles is that when I need to increase the font, it can become a little cumbersome because the screen is too small. The larger screen solves that problem. The picture is clear and the it sounds better with the 2 speakers. Overall, I find it to be complementary to my 6" Fire and regular tv/ Fire stick.
You can't beat the price for it's use as an entertainment device, when comparing to another tablet brand. It works better and is more reliable than an HP laptop I have that is only a couple of years old (not to mention much better customer service). I only wish I could use WordPerfect on it.

title: one design flaw
text: It's comfortable and durable. Fits snugly, so I'm not worried about it slipping out. I would give it 5 stars if it weren't for a peculiar design flaw. You would think that there would be an opening in the front cover that corresponds with the rear facing camera. Using it is very difficult, as a result.

title: Worth the price.
text: Good sound for one-year plugs. The plugs fit well, so they're comfortable. I'm using the ones that were already attached.

title: Great tech support and very good product
text: It sounds about how I expected, maybe a little less bass than I was hoping for. There's one odd thing about it, though. There's no way to adjust the bass on the unit, itself, just on the remote. The first remote that came with it did not work but I received a response from tech support within about an hour of sending me an email and they sent a replacement immediately. That service is what got them the 5th star.

title: a good buy.
text: this is really great! It's very easy to use, lots to watch and do and there are no issues with the quality of streaming. A nice compliment to my cable.

title: As advertised
text: reliable and fits anywhere. A basic router that stands up to any similar router. It doesn't take up any space

title: Works well
text: This hub was the perfect solution for me. A must-have for anyone with a desktop and the price is minimal.

title: Nice camera
text: I'm not a camera buff, so this one works great for me. Relatively inexpensive and easy to use. The companion program is also easy to navigate.

title: Fantastic!
text: Sound quality is better than expected, although a little too much bass. I would give it a 5, if it weren't for that. It's a great looking piece, as well. Looks very elegant sitting on my wooden bookcase. I bought it mostly because I love Pandora but find it a pain in the butt to listen to it on my computer. Having the remote makes an even better experience. I don't have to run to the computer to rate/skip a song. I can keep doing whatever I was doing.

title: Font and brightness
text: The colors are vibrant and overall I love it.  My only issue is I cannot figure out how to increase the font in the books I am reading, and the brightness keeps going back down to dull.

title: Pleasantly surprised with this Kindle case!
text:
I can’t believe I’ve had my Kindle Paperwhite (6th generation) for ten years.

I am usually very careful with my things and this Kindle has held up well. I read every day mostly at home and just take it with me on a few trips. It basically sits on my nightstand when I’m not reading.

I originally bought a Kindle Smart Cover (ten years ago) and it also held up extremely well…except the other day the magnet flap on the edge started to come off. I decided to look into buying another cover and was concerned the quality wouldn’t be as good since this is a different brand.

I did, however, really like the color so decided to go ahead and purchase it.

My case just arrived and I couldn’t be happier. I would call the color more of a teal than “blue” which totally suits me. I find it easier to find when it’s sitting on my bed or other surfaces, since the case is lighter in color than black or gray.

The material is very soft (they say waterproof) and the edges are not so “sharp” against my skin as the first cover I purchased. (It took some time to get those edges smoothed down during its original use.)

The wake/sleep function on this new case works perfectly and my Kindle fit into the case snuggly. The cover folds back on itself so I can easily hold it in one hand…the inside of the cover is a nice soft gray material.

I think this “ultra thin” case might even be a bit lighter in weight than my original cover, so that’s a plus for me.

I think the value is quite good…assuming it lasts a good long while like my first cover.

I am very happy and would purchase again.

title: My all-time favorite mouse for work
text:
I work full-time from home and have been using this same Logitech mouse for years. When it’s time for a replacement, I do look to see what other options are out there…but I just keep coming back to this one.

It’s comfortable in my hand and responds well to my touch. The only reason I need to replace it is because I often eat at my desk and sometimes that’s hard on a mouse. Also, when you consider how much time we spend using a mouse, the surface is just bound to wear down.

I like the size…I have tried the mini versions but that size isn’t practical for me working all day at a computer.

I probably don’t use all the features…just the wheel and left/right clicks. It rolls nicely and the battery life lasts quite a while. I like the little green light on the top to tell me it still has a charge.

I use a basic mouse pad with a built-in wrist rest and my hand and arm do not feel any strain. The rubberized grip really helps me hold onto it comfortably.

I have seen this mouse in other patterns but I stick with this dark gray version. I have a black desk and I would just prefer to keep everything monochromatic, since my office is in my home.

Definitely plug and play once you put in the USB receiver.

I think this is a quality item for the price and I will continue to purchase, as needed. I highly recommend its reliability.

title: Best TV in the house
text:
I bought this TV a while back and absolutely love it. I wanted something for my bedroom…proportional for me watching while sitting on my bed…and I find myself wanting to watch from here more often than the newer TV we have in the living room.

The colors are vibrant and the sound great. Many times google just does its screenshot mode and flips on gorgeous photos. I keep my TV most of the time just to have this background. It’s like having an ever-changing 55-inch picture frame.

This particular screen is perfect in size for my standard master bedroom. The remote is easy to use and balances well in my hand. I can find the typical buttons pretty well just by feel.

I feel that the value is certainly there for the quality and would buy Samsung again.

title: Many uses for this sturdy industrial-looking stand
text:
I work full-time from home and originally bought this stand to raise my monitor. Then I bought another stand to raise my laser printer on one side of my desk.

Since I recently bought a new larger monitor (and don’t need to use a stand to lift it up), I now use that first stand for my color printer on the other side of my desk. I love how it is now so much easier for me to grab my printed documents. Such a simple solution to just raise everything up.

I put rubber feet on my monitors to avoid any slipping that might occur on the metal stands…so no problem there.

The stand allows me to put papers or folders underneath, so any extra storage is always helpful.

The vents are quite functional to keep electronics cooled down, and the stand has an industrial look to it that appeals to me. Each stand comes with its own rubber bumpers which helps keep it stable.

There are probably many uses one could find around the house or office for these stands. They are sturdy metal and I’ve never seen a scratch on them.

The quality and value are there and I highly recommend… I would certainly buy again.

title: This monitor is great for my multi-window work
text:
I work full-time from home and, over the years, have increased the size of my monitor because…why not, right?

I’m online all day long and currently working with so many windows, it just made sense for me to upgrade again recently and go with this 34-inch monitor.

I have always been drawn to the curved screens and decided I would just treat myself. It’s almost comforting to have that curve kind of wrap around you visually. I think it actually helps me stay better focused.

I set up a pleasant and not too busy (for me) background that frames whatever I’m working on. Sometimes I just center everything in the middle and other times I spread many of my windows out so I can drag and drop, reference something, etc. I honestly think this speeds up my work and makes me more productive.

I’m still learning what works best for me but look forward to turning this screen on every day.

I’m not yet into gaming but perhaps someday I will make that leap. I can see this wider monitor immersing the player in the game. The colors are rich and there are all sorts of ways to customize your preferences. I’m sure most gamers know what to look for, so check out the specs to see if this is the monitor for you.

I’m reviewing from a working aspect and am very happy with my purchase.

I’m glad I went with the height-adjustable model. I had my last 23-inch monitor on a separate monitor stand and that took up some valuable room on my desk. This LG monitor has the curved base (I’m sure to better have it balanced) and I work around that quite nicely. My keyboard can sit on the base comfortably, if I have to move it for paperwork I need to review.

I feel this is a good value and I trust LG products. I do recommend and would purchase again if needed.

title: A great option for behind my night stand
text:
Recently I found a need for me to have multiple devices hooked up at my nightstand. (Remember the days when it used to be just a lamp and a clock?)

With this unit I have the choice of three USB ports and four sockets. I wanted something with the USB ports on the top so I could easily reach them, as well as keep the cord length closer to me. This power “strip” has met that need and has certainly come in handy.

Instead of attaching it permanently to the wall or nightstand with screws, I used Command tape for a more temporary solution. Two Command strips have held it up with no problem. It has never fallen off, even when I plug items in and out.

I have my google home hub plugged into one of the sockets. I also have my Bose sleep bud charging case and iPhone charging stand plugged in. All things I want close to me when I’m in or on the bed.

Recently my eye doctor said I should be using warm compresses on my eyes, so I bought an eye mask with a USB cable. I leave the USB cord plugged in and just attach the other end to my eye mask when I’m using it. So convenient and really speeds up the process. When I’m done, I disconnect the cord from the mask and tuck the cord back behind my night stand. So easy to pull out and tuck back away.

Sometimes I need to plug in a heating pad and this is the only convenient place to plug it in while I use it from the bed. Since I don’t use the heating pad all the time, it’s easy enough to just plug it in when I need it.

I like that it’s low-profile enough to allow my nightstand to stay somewhat close to the wall. You wouldn’t even know it’s back there without leaning over and looking down.

I found this to be a good value and I would purchase again.

title: I feel like I have a new phone!
text:
I am so pleasantly surprised by this Caseology phone case. I bought my iPhone 6S plus phone over two years ago and ended up with the rose pink. At that time I could not find a transparent case online so ended up buying one at the Apple store for almost $50! It was a Tech21 case and I really liked it at first, but about a year later the transparent plastic started to discolor. Now it just looks dirty and embarrassing. It’s definitely the plastic turning a dirty looking brown.

When I recently found this Caseology case online I thought I'd give it a try since it had so many good reviews and was very reasonably priced. I am so happy! Someone mentioned it being slippery, but I find the sides have a nice grip to them. Better than my original case. My phone fits in it nicely and I see no gaps. All the ports show up nicely and the buttons all work. Plus I can once again see the pretty color of my phone. This case color also matches the rose gold phone nicely.

Five stars!

title: Love it!!! So much better than the older versions.
text:
I had the old models of this and used them daily, I've been using this model now since April and its better in EVERY WAY than the previous versions!

1) The retractable earbuds are FANTASTIC! No more dangling wires. I retract them constantly - when I walk into a store and don't want to seem weird, press the button. Boom, I'm a normal guy without a weird wire hanging on my shoulder.

2) The bluetooth is infinitely better. With the old ones, I would lose signal with my phone NEXT TO THEM! This one, I legitimately have 30 feet of range or more. It's so much better.

3) The buttons are better, smarter, and easy to use.

4) The little rubber piece at the middle of the hoop is perfect. Just enough to let you bend it around your neck.

In short, I'm in love again. These are awesome.

title: Are we beta testing a terrible product?  NOT READY YET!
text:
NOT Ready Yet. Sigh. So many issues, it's a joke at this point. Sorry, developers/owners of Ring.com but your product is not ready for release yet.

1) Android support is abominable. If the app isn't OPEN (and I mean you looking at the app) it's completely unreliable. Do anything else on your phone and it's a 50/50 gamble whether you'll get an alert. Even if you're standing inside the door. So this means that as a doorbell, it COMPLETELY FAILS. I can't have a doorbell that works 10% of the time, or 50% of the time, or 75% of the time. I need virtually flawless execution on the DOORBELL FEATURE OF THE DOORBELL. Until you have that, STOP SELLING DOORBELLS.

2) The default (and only) chime you get is super annoying. This is 2015 - I can't choose between chimes or upload my own?

3) The button is really hard to press - and the worst part is visitors won't know they're SUPPOSED to push harder to activate it. So they'll use normal pressure, nothing will happen, and nobody will know the difference.

4) You have a webcam connected to your wifi - and will be charged to store the content in the cloud - but you can't access the camera from the app. What a waste of a feature.

So - it's completely unreliable. It's feature set is terrible. And it's expensive. PASS. This is getting returned immediately. What a disappointment.

title: Great medium sized bag for 2 lenses.

I love the top snap closure - you can zip it up for more protection but the snap works great for quick retrieval.

The perfect medium sized bag. I tried them all at the store and got this one. I'm glad I did.

title: Amazing flexibility, serious value.
text:
I've got some experience with soundbars having been an early adopter in them along with the first generation plasma televisions. The thought then was to hide the wires and hang everything on the wall as if it were art - the modus operandi hasn't changed, it's just improved and become much more affordable.

First, the flexibility of this system makes it great for anyone. You can connect the speakers and create a large soundbar you can place on a shelf or hang up on the wall. This is ingenious - it looks great as one piece and you don't have to worry about multiple speakers. Or, you can keep the speakers separate and still either place them on a table or shelf or whatever, or hang them on the wall. So if you prefer the speakers vertical to the left and right of your TV, or if you prefer them horizontal under the TV, you have the freedom to do either with this system.

Next are the features. I found the Dialog settings to be superb. With my previous speaker setup I was always adjusting the volume between quiet monologue scenes and action scenes to hear what was being said. This system adjust everything on the fly automatically so you can hear the dialog without making any other changes.

I connected it right up to my cable box with HDMI and it was done. No complicated wires to hook up, one and done.
The subwoofer included is WIRELESS! That is terrific. I put it behind my seating and it was just perfect.

I tested the Bluetooth feature from my phone - I turned on Pandora and beautiful clear music came instantly through the speakers. Nothing to really setup, it was playing tunes in seconds.

All in all I'm really happy with this system. With the flexible speaker setup, the great features, and the price so low you can't even buy a subwoofer for that kind of money, it's a no brainer.

title: Excellent Tivo Killer!
text:
With features like built-in ethernet networking (no more relying on a phone line!), the ability to send shows to your friends (and receieve shows too! Missed Friends last week? Someone out there will send it to ya!), the fastest processor found in a DVR, sleek attractive design, a great remote, and Commercial Advance (No more commercials, ever!), don't even CONSIDER getting a Tivo.
No monthly 'subscription' fees to pay for a failing company to try and stay in business a few more weeks (Tivo), no more phone line hassles (Tivo), no more cartoony nonsense that looks like something your 5 year old should play with (Tivo) and no more need to HACK the unit to get the features you want (Tivo).
So much more than a VCR, it offers you a completely new way to watch television. Forums abound for the ReplayTV, so tips, tricks, and advice are just a moment away.
Buy more than one, and watch the shows from either at either location! The beauty of the ethernet port.
I know this sounds like an advertisement, but anyone reading this review is asking my personal opinion. ReplayTV is the best, high end piece of equipment in your stereo / home theater system.
Did I mention it has a VGA output, for your projector or progressive input TV?
Everyone who owns it loves it! Don't get stuck with a brick when Tivo goes out of business. ReplayTV is owned by a huge company (SonicBlue, who also owns GoVideo, Rio, and Diamond Multimedia, makers of video cards, sound cards, etc).

title: Home Made Might Be Better
text:
So it’s 2014 and I finally entered the world of touch screen computing and like a good sucker, I dished out $28 for the Kensington Virtuoso Pro Pen 39526 WW (Stylus and Pen combo). It arrived before the computer, but I decided to examine it nonetheless to see what makes a stylus a stylus. First of all, I didn’t like the feel and weight of this item and the pen leaked on my finger. The pen’s tip is a heavy weight metal, which makes it good for writing, but when it’s flipped for screen use, the heaviness is on the top of the stylus (where the pen is) instead of at the bottom. I don’t like that type of imbalance for drawing. I discovered that this item is an overpriced do-hickey that anyone can make at home from practically anything that you have lying around the house. For the how-to video instructions on how to make your own stylus to suit your personal taste and/or needs you can check out the websites that I’ve listed below and/or read the summary that follows.
Our smartphone, computer, or tablet’s touch screen senses touch because our fingers produce electrons, hence sending an electrical message to the screen that allows us to write or draw. Therefore to make a stylus, we need something that will behave as a conductor between our finger and the screen. Metal is a conductor. Inexpensive good metal conductors include aluminum, a metal rod (such as an antenna barrel or metal pen), a paper clip, a naked copper wire, or the metal spring that’s inside an old pen. A wet sponge or Q-Tip can also conduct electricity and neither of them scratches the screen.

To design a scratch-free stylus, insert a strip of sponge or Q-Tip into a metal casing (such as an old pen or a slender antenna tube that you’ve cut to size). Each should fit tightly into the barrel in order to make a good contact and connection with your finger and the metal casing. Wet the tip of that sponge or Q-Tip and use it on your touch screen.

If you don’t have a metal barrel available, you can use a cheap plastic pen. Drill two holes, one on either side of the plastic barrel. If you don’t have a small drill handy, you can burn the holes through the pen using a heated ice pick or paper clip. Insert the sponge (make sure it protrudes through the pen’s tip and that it also makes contact with the holes that you drilled). The final step is to insert a paper clip or a stripped copper wire through the holes and the sponge that you packed into the pen’s barrel. Next, wrap the wire tightly around the pen’s barrel. When you write, make sure your finger(s) touch the wire, which will transmit your electronic touch to the sponge and your tablet’s screen. title: Watch the Edges
text:
I ordered this USB coupler from Tiny Deal (China) through Amazon on January 20th and it arrvied February 20th. I should have paid careful attention to the edges that are clearly visible in the photo. Evidently a poor design, the edges are raised, appearing like metal burrs. In my opinion that design was unnecessary and potentially dangerous as the edges could have been rolled or not folded at all. Although the reliefs aren't razor sharp, they can still pose a hazard for young hands or for anyone who has pronounced arthritis.

When I inserted the male USB cable, it doesn't go all the way into the coupler, but it does appear to make a connection with the electrodes that are inside the unit. However, at this point, I haven't given it a trial run for continuity, since I have purchased numerous cables and connectors to keep in stock rather than for immediate use. In time, I suspect that I'll eventually find a coupler without burrs that will be less hazardous to connect and disconnect.

title: Great Educational Item
text: I believe this microscope may be for teens and older students, but I ordered two of these microscopes as gifts for families with young children, three are age seven, in Puerto Rico and Florida.  Last year, I decided to spend my money on true educational "toys" instead of computer games or other ridiculously expensive gadgets for kids.  The two scopes went to my siblings, grandparents who spend a lot of time with their grandkids and who would hopefully put them to good use.  I also sent them a lab manual and several Golden Book nature books.  The microscopes have proven to be such a hit with most of the family, namely three generations who have been collecting leaves and all manner of specimens to view with the children, photograph, and upload to the computers.  One seven-year-old is using it to do his school's science presentation.  I'm so delighted with their enthusiasm that I'm ordering a third scope for a family in Virginia that home schools there four children who range in age from two to ten.  Spring will soon be here and it's the perfect time to enjoy and learn about their environment.  By the way, if I had more time, I would love this science tool for myself.

title: A Major Disappointment
text: This product was designed for portability - it's small and takes up little space in a traveler's bag.  The compactness is what also contributes to its uselessness.  Most devices come with cube shaped plugs or three prong plugs that will overlap the neighboring socket, so instead of having three sockets, you're lucky if you get two.  The holes are also so small and tight that it's difficult to insert and remove a plug, especially if you have arthritis as I do.  Pulling at a plug on this device will loosen the surge suppressor from the host socket and I fear that I might accidentally electrocute myself.  Final analysis: Poorly designed unit that's unfriendly to large or broad adapter plugs.

title: Good for the Price
text:
UPDATE (03.20.14): The original review (Nov. 20,2012) is below. A couple of times, I tried to use the radio with the so called back up battery that had been more than charged, but the radio doesn't operate with it. I therefore dropped the rating from 5 stars to 3 because what's the use of having a back-up battery if it isn't going to work? The radio works fine with the AC/DC adapter that costs extra. I haven't tried the crank and have told myself that I will resort to such labor only in an emergency, which I haven't yet had. Also: You get static on the radio if your cordless phone activation is too close to the radio, but any microwave or radio wave (including flourescent lights) affect all radios, not just this one (that's the nature of transmission).

ORIGINAL REVIEW: Yes, you do have to buy the AC/DC adapter separately, but if you have a Radio Shack universal adapter, you can use that. I paid $10 for the Kaito one, which is a fair price.

I bought six of these little radios for myself, a relative, and friends. We get a good signal in both NYC and Alexandria, VA. I bought the green model from Amazon, which is fine for me because I'm not fashion conscious about most things. After purchasing them, I discovered that Acorn sells them in different colors: red, yellow, etc.

I prefer analog to digital because digital electronics has to be reset every time the power drops to zero, so the analog tuner on this radio is perfect for me. I wish the little front knobs were a little larger, but the fact that they are not totally round compensates for the lack of size, especially for people like me, who have arthritis. If you have vision problems though, you might need a magnifying glass or good glasses to read the markings along those front buttons. In summation, I like this radio and all the little connections that come with it for the cellphone or computer tablet.

title: It's a chore to communicate with manufacturer
text:
Keyboard keys stuck or did not respond, and manufacturer suggested that I download their new keyboard driver. Because I wasn't familiar with Windows 7, its operating system, Bing took me to its own website, instead of the Asus URL that I had entered. So, I selected an Asus driver site from the Bing list, and unfortunately ended up at an alleged Norton phisher site and downloaded the alleged driver, which in turn disabled the computer. So, if you need to download a keyboard driver, make absolutely sure that you are at the official, true, non-bogus Asus website. I called Asus and they reconfigured the computer to the factory setting.

The upper cover is rubbery on the outside - perhaps designed as a shock absorber, but it attracts a lot of dust that doesn't wipe off easily. Bottom line, I didn't like this laptop, so I gave it to my brother. Let him deal with downloading a new driver while I stick to my old 2002 Toshiba.

title: Belkin Easy Transfer Does Not Transfer Programs
text:
If you're looking for a cable that will transfer your programs as well as your files, this isn't it. I didn't expect it to do that when I bought it, but I hoped that it would. Shame on me, because I bought it without doing the research first. There are two products on the market that will migrate your programs as well as your files: one is Zinstall, which offers two versions, and the better of the two (XP7) is presently on sale - you can view a nice video on their website; the other is LapLink, which has received lukewarm or not so warm reviews.

If you have all your old programs on CD's as well as their product keys on hand, however, you might be able to install the programs manually and still use the Belkin Transfer Cable to transfer your files from the old computer. When I tried to manually install my MS Office 2007, which was an upgrade that I could use on up to two computers and for which I had the product key, the Windows 7 on the new computer would not accept it because it couldn't detect a previous copy on the new computer. The new computer came with an incomplete version of MS OFfice 2010, which isn't a PREVIOUS copy, but a more advanced copy, so it appeared that I was out of luck. I solved the problem with Zinstall XP7, which cost me $89 and allowed me to transfer files, settngs, and programs without needing any special cables. With Zinstall, you can use any type of computer cable- DSL, USB, whatever you have available. When the files are transfered, you're actually placing fresh copies of them onto the new computer; the original files remain on the old computer. So, if you plan to toss that old computer or donate it, and don't want anyone to inherit your personal business, you still need to delete those files from the old machine.

The Belkin Easy Transfer Cable for Windows 7 allows you to transfer the files from an XP, Vista, or 7 computer to a Windows 7. It comes with a CD that, similar to Znstall, you have to install onto the old computer and the target computer. You then follow very easy steps before you connect the cable. After you're instructed to connect the cable, you do just that and follow a few more steps. Because I used Zinstall, the Belkin software and cable were of no use to me.

UPDATE: On Windows Vista, I recently noticed an entry for transferring files and settings in the Control Panel. I haven't tried it, but I mention it in case readers are interested in following that link.

title: Medical Practice Applications
text:
This is an Asus Eee Slate EP 121-1A010 update; we've changed the rating from "Like it" to "Love it" and we're adding a couple more to the office. I chose it for a gastroenterologist friend who needed it for her medical practice. Now that patient records need to be digitized, she uses this tablet to keep track of all her business's management needs, which include patient vitals, records, and billing. In the doctor's own words:

"I log into Athena, which is our electronic medical record and practice management, and then all the info regarding a patient gets put in. So, the girls will use the tablet to populate BP, pulse, etc, past medical history, chief complaint, etc. Some of it is clicking onto specific fields and it will auto-populate with a touch. I think the ASUS Eee Slate is the perfect size screen by the way. I really like that one. The Acer (an alternate tablet which we tested) is good but, screen is small so it's difficult to maneuver over fields."

The doctor had been advised to get a Windows tablet and the ASUS fits the bill. She tried it and an Acer tablet so that she and her staff could get the feel of two different products. The Acer is considerably less expensive, has less memory, and lacks a few features that the Asus has. We had hoped to get tablets with the anticipated Windows 8 that MS announced around March 2011, but by August 8th, the anticipated release date was 2012. Failure to comply with new federal laws for digitized medical records means incurring penalties, so she wanted to have everything by September, hence these two touch tablets seemed to be the best choice as of August 2011. After nearly three months of use, it became clear that the Acer couldn't meet her needs, but the ASUS has been wonderful. The doctor and her staff can download medical templates and macros directly from her provider, Athena Health, onto a main computer or the tablet.

While her medical staff handles the initial patient consultations, the info can be transfered to or from a tablet into the office's mainframe computer, athenahealth.com, and to the doctor's own tablet via e-file or e-mail. They no longer need to transcribe handwritten information into the office's computer; it can now be done on the spot, saving time. The tablets can also be used to read Kindle books.

The ASUS has the added advantage of a wireless Bluetooth keyboard and a digital pen, which I believe can be an asset for anything that requires a signature, e.g. a prescription or an MS Office Word business letter. It also interfaces well with a wireless printer, but it does have USB ports. The ASUS also comes with a mediocre MS Office program that can be upgraded for a better version.

My initial favorites were the Apple iPad2 or a Toshiba tablet. However, neither of them comes with a Windows operating system (OS). Toshiba uses Google's Android (aka Droid) and Apple uses its own system. While you can change Toshiba's OS to a Windows OS, I wouldn't recommend it if you're not technically savvy.

text:
After about 24 hours of apparently normal use, it started freaking out. It uninstalls our clock faces and the ECG app. When we re-install them, they work fine for about two minutes, then disappear. In the Fitbit app, it gives us the option to re-install them, but only after showing a screen saying that there is no internet access (this house has almost a dozen other wireless devices that do not suffer this problem).

We will be returning this cursed thing at the earliest opportunity.

0/5, would not recommend.

title: Received used item instead. Stopped working in three weeks. Replacement Stopped Working.
text:
Took a coffee break and left the computer idle. When I returned fifteen minutes later, the monitor no longer worked. It's been in use for about three weeks, and now reports that it has no signal. Windows can see when the monitor is plugged in, but the monitor still reports no signal. Plugging in other monitors which continue to work proves that the problem is not the graphics card or ports.

To say I'm disappointed is a massive understatement.

I'll be asking for a refund as soon as I finish posting this review :-(

[Edited to add] I've received a replacement for the broken monitor, and it was immediately obvious that the monitor they sent me the first time had been used and returned. The tape on this box was new, the interior packaging was different, and there were items in the replacement such as decals and the like that were not present in the first one.

Shame on you for selling me used equipment as new :-(

[SECOND EDIT] The replacement stopped working three months to the day after I started using it. It would appear that the problem wasn't one bad used device, as I'm fairly confident the replacement was new. It seems like this line of monitors is just garbage unfortunately, and that malfunctions are common.

I'm so extremely disappointed.

title: Wheel Tilt functionality is too sensitive, only works for about 8 months before breaking.
text:
This trackball is a bit small for my hands, and it is difficult to use the "middle mouse click" functionality, but other than that I quite like this trackball.

Clicking the scroll wheel is a quite common user action these days, so I'm quite surprised that it's so difficult to do with this mouse without unwanted scrolling in the process ("Wheel tilt" is too sensitive). I regularly use programs like 3DS Max where the middle mouse button is an absolutely integral part of the functionality. Even in the web browser, where clicking the scroll wheel will open a link in a new tab, or clicking the scroll wheel on a tab will close that tab, I'm constantly being faced with this irritating limitation.

{EDIT] This trackball started acting wonky about six months in, and become almost unusable by eight months. It finally became completely unusable at almost exactly eleven months after purchase.

title: Didn't even last nine months
text: After approximately nine months of light usage (it mostly just sits on my desk until I need it to test software, which takes ten minutes then it goes back on the desk) it simply refuses to turn back on. There are all kinds of complaints that I have about this device, but none are more indicative of the quality of this piece of garbage than the fact that it broke after nine months of very light usage.

title: Works great on PC, completely useless on Surface RT
text:
This sweet little USB Ethernet adapter gets five stars for working like a champ on my PC, even though my PC already has a built-in Ethernet adapter.

If you are looking at this item because of the many articles out there suggesting that it works on the Surface RT, however, save your money. It's completely useless on the Surface RT, and will not work. There are no "official" drivers available for it, and even the ones that several sites have made available for download will not work because they are not MS-certified and therefore Microsoft won't allow them to run on the Surface RT.

I wish I had known this before spending money on it, since I have absolutely no other use for it. Can't knock the product though, it appears to work quite well for any other purpose.

title: Possibly the worst tablet ever made
text:
I've been a professional software developer for more than twenty years, and in that time I've used a very large variety of computing devices for both personal and professional use. I don't think I've ever hated a computing device more than I hate this abomination. Actually, I can't remember actually hating any device prior to this. The touch-screen is terrible and inconsistent, and I frequently need to tap things multiple times in order to get a response.

Windows 8 might be okay if it weren't so completely locked down on the Surface RT. For instance, you cannot install any other browser; you're stuck with Internet Explorer, the worst browser available on any device, and cannot even install plugins to block spam ads and malware. The web browsing experience is truly terrible, and the design of the browser is sufficiently different from *every other browser* to make it as counter-intuitive as possible.

There is almost no software that will run on the device except what can be obtained through Microsoft's online store, which is a fresh hell that deserves it's own product review. At least with my Android devices I have broad compatibility and a wide variety of software available for just about every purpose.

The on-screen touch keyboard is clunky and poorly designed, and is at times incredibly difficult to use. For instance, trying to compile an email in GMail is pathologically difficult, since the keyboard takes up literally 75% of the screen, leaving almost no space to see what you're typing and making it incredibly difficult to scroll down to the "Send" button to actually send the email. There appears to be no support for swapping the built-in touch-screen keyboard with a better version like Swype, which is incredibly disappointing.

Attempting to connect USB devices is extremely hit or miss, and many I've tried simply do not work due to lack of "official" driver support. For instance, I purchased a "Belkin F4U047-RS USB 2.0 Ethernet Adapter" on the advice of several websites saying that they'd been able to use that specific adapter to add an Ethernet adapter to the Surface RT. Unfortunately, Microsoft has asked those websites to no longer distribute the drivers that made the device work, and have disabled the use of such drivers on the Surface RT since they are not Microsoft certified drivers, leaving me with no Ethernet and twenty dollars wasted.

I could go on for several more paragraphs, but I've wasted enough of my life on this piece of offal. If I didn't require this device to be physically present to test software builds on, I would have sent it back almost immediately.

title: Great when it works, doesn't work for long
text: Pretty unreliable. I've ordered three of these, and I think the longest I've had one last so far is about eight months. The last one I ordered only lasted three months. It's really a shame that nobody makes reliable trackball devices anymore.

title: Complete crap
text:
Arrived with factory damage: one of the pre-installed screws was apparently the wrong length and had been screwed all the way through to the opposite side of the larger tray, creating a rather large and unsightly raised and broken section on the top surface. I am honestly quite surprised that the manufacturer's Quality Control process missed this rather large and visible defect, which is bad enough to make the product unusable for its intended purpose. I can only assume that they quite literally did not look at it once the few pre-assembled parts were screwed on.

The stand does not sit level, there's about a 10 degree slant along the wrong axis that makes it very annoying when attempting to use the computer, as the computer screen appears rotated clockwise in relation to the viewer. Additionally, two of the four wheels do not roll well at all, which makes the entire cart unstable and prone to falling over when attempting to roll it around.

Overall, one of the most disappointing purchases I've ever made on Amazon.

title: Horribly grainy photos, takes decent videos though

Battery life is pretty poor as well, in my experience, but that can be mitigated somewhat by always having rechargeable batteries charged and ready to go.

Overall, a very disappointing purchase.

title: Critical review, I use a lot of batteries.
text:
I use these batteries in a remote control, the annoying toilet flusher, a portable radio, my owl alerts, flashlights, and many other battery powered gadgets that normally discharge batteries. So far they work really well in these gadgets and the charger surprisingly charges them faster than I thought. Definitely worth the money because they last much longer than the non rechargeable disposable batteries and better for the environment. As for fit they seem to fit fine in everything so far without any problems which is really nice especially on expensive devices. I can tell you that they get a little warmer in the charger than I am comfortable with which concerns me. Because from personal experience fast charging getting batteries hot is not good for any rechargeable batteries it runis them plus its not safe I wish they had a slow or low charging setting. I can honestly say these easily out perform the Rayovac, Energizer, and Duracell rechargable batteries that discarge quickly saving you money and headaches. For just normal homeowners use for remote controls and around the household these should work perfectly fine. I have bought other batteries from EBL off Amazon and absolutely love them. I will have to keep taking notes on discharge, charging, and start measuring voltage on these to see how consistent they are and update this review. Stay tuned.

Truthfully the only reason why I bought these is they do not offer the red EBL 1.5v AA Li-Ion rechargeable 3000mWh batteries in any quantity greater than four with a charger on Amazon which is why for value for my money I only rate the "value for the money" partpurchase at 3 stars. EBL needs to make those available here just like these batteries why they do not is a mystery to me. If you need an honest to goodness AA 1.5v battery for something sensitive to voltage read my review on those batteries they sell.

title: Vast improvement over previous model
text:
I am impressed with the improvements in this newer model.
The headband is softer, more bendable and comfortable.
They now include a sizing band that holds it against your head (like a ring sizer).
Slightly better battery life too.
And they have added a little padding where the vibrators hit near your ears.
The controls are still really user-friendly even while wearing it.
As always, it is easy to load/change music.

What hasn't improved?
Well it still digs in a little at the sides.
And the battery life is still not as great as the competition.
I miss the bright yellow color of my old one. Hard to see/find in my bag.
The carrying case is not useful for watersport equipment. It shouldn't get wet. Which is dumb for a swimming headset.
It is just as heavy as before.

title: Love these more than I expected to!
text:
Pros:
It is hard to find a really good swimming headset. This is it. (I have tried many other types, and this is the winner for me.)
SO easy to charge. So easy to load music. Allows for folders (my other headphones don't).
Weighs NOTHING. You don't know you have it on! Doesn't press to hard or hurt anywhere. A lot of bone conduction headsets are uncomfortable but this one is not.
Has a huge battery life. Also it TELLS you every time you turn it on how much battery is left. (If you want to check after you are done, turn it off and on again and it will tell you.)
Controls make sense. Mostly. A few features require long push and hold to activate, but the stuff you use daily is intuitive.
Volume is good. Not super loud, but also you can adjust the placement around your ear to be louder/softer.

Cons:
The band is longer than I need. So there is a gap at the back of my head. I wish it were a little smaller.
The buttons are a little fidgety. They are so small and all feel alike so it takes a while to feel your way around and figure out which button is which. I wish they would put the power and mode buttons on one side and the Plus/minus buttons on the other ear. Or put the plus minus on the outside rather than under edge.
That said, I put my 400 songs on it and just let it play while I workout.
This one is petty but there are 2 modes - water and regular. It changes the EQ to supposedly sound better underwater vs. on land. But I find the on land mode sounds better in water. BUT I don't use earplugs. So maybe that is why.

title: Fits fantastically. Only get the clear version though if you have a light-up Mac keyboard
text:
I prefer these keyboard covers to others because they really fit better and are easy to type on. They hug the sides of the keys and don't slide. They also don't get all oily underneath like the cheap ones.

However I ONLY get the clear version for keyboards where the letters light up. (like my macbook) The colorful ones not only don't let the light through properly, but they are hard to read. (see Photos 1 and 2) The light only shines through the letters and the only clear part of the color covers is the letters - so unless they line up perfectly, it doesn't work.
With the clear ones it is no problem! Now fair warning - the clear ones are not crystal clear. The keys will not look shiny black. They will look matte and slightly greyed. (See Photo 3) But they are perfectly easy to read. And you can see how much dust and dirt is already on mine after 2 days - it is totally worth it to protect your laptop!!!

title: Gorgeous color. Works well. Sturdy. Great venting. Feet can't fall off. LASTS.
text:
I have had mine nearly a year. I love it. Best case I have ever had.
(EDIT: going on 2 years now and I STILL love it. I am really pretty rough with my laptop and it gets abused regularly. But the case is going strong)

Pros:
Gorgeous teal color (not plain blue). Works well. Provides ample corner protection, which I need. (see Photo 1) Once you get it on properly, it stays put. The 4 feet can't fall off because they aren't separate pieces stuck on like most cases. The venting is fantastic. In addition to the bottom vents, the way top and bottom meet in the back allows for full venting open or closed. This is rare. But it still manages to protect the back corners well. It's a fairly clever design. (see photo 2). I like the way the kickstands gently lock in place when open. Also the case is not heavy or bulky but is very protective.

Cons:
The biggest problem is that in order to take it off you pretty much have to break it. If you have a reason to need to take the case off and on again this is not for you. If you want it to never come off, this is great. It is also very (physically) hard to get on. The last clip just wouldn't clip (and I have a lot of experience with laptop covers). So I had to take it off and start over (doing the problem clip first). Even partially on, the thing did NOT want to come off! It was quite a challenge. Plus the instruction sheet is translated into such poor English it makes no sense. The two clips on either side of the trackpad might scrape your wrists a little, depending on your angle. (see Photo 3) Luckily the angle of my wrists misses the tabs and I have never had a problem. Most people wouldn't have an issue.

As to how it holds up:
I don't use the little tabs underneath that tilt the keyboard up. But they haven't broken off. I needlessly worried about the little bits that protect the back corners on the bottom cover. (See photo 4). They also remain unbroken. (EDIT: STILL unbroken after 2 years including dropping it)
A tiny portion on one of the many tabs holding the case did break off. (EDIT: 2 years in and I am now missing 3 of the tabs. STILL doesn't change the effectiveness at all) There is one tiny crack in the case near the bottom right of the keyboard. I think it actually happened putting it on in the first place. (Or rather when I had to pry it off to start over.) However it is very small and in a place where there are two layers. And the bottom layer has no crack. Therefore it can't really spread or get worse. And again, it doesn't affect anything. (EDIT: 2 years in and the crack has not worsened and case is still secure) I may need to buy a replacement because it's a work laptop and we have to turn it in once a year for maintenance. They will destroy the cover when they remove it. (EDIT: they didn't take the case off so yay! That is how I am on my 2nd year. If I ever need to buy a new one I am getting the same case. I love this case)

title: Not perfect. Love them anyway.
text:
I have had these for a year now and use them daily for watching TV, so I can say I have given them an exhaustive workout.
I love them, and can't imagine how I lived without them. BUT they do have their issues.

Pros:
They recharge easily and hold the charge for many hours. I have used them for 8+ hours straight without having to recharge.
They are comfortable and cushioned, and adjust for my son's Charlie Brown-like huge head and my small one.
They are comfortable when worn over just one ear (If I have to keep the other ear free to hear sound in the room)
They are in range even outside the house, so I can use while gardening, going to the laundry room, cleaning the garage...
The sound is clear.
The recharge station is compact and effortless.
Easily cleanable

Cons:
They slip off your head if you lean forward.
If they don't receive audio signal for a few minutes, such as when a show is paused, they play painfully loud static
If the volume is loud, others around you can hear.
When there is only a low sound signal, such as a very quiet moment in a film, or when you pause, you can hear a pulsing sort of hissing noise.
Like any wireless system, you need to be 5 feet away from the base for it to work properly. Anyone needing to be closer can use wired headphones anyway.
When you turn them on, they take a couple seconds to connect. So you don't get sound instantly.
It isn't easy to have multiple pairs so people can share. Charge station can only charge one. You either have to set up 2 separate units or take turns charging multiple headsets. I wish there were a way to daisy chain the sound output or there were more room on the charging rack.

I cleaned as much as I could without pulling out the stove which is beyond what this elderly handicapped woman can do. And this product fits nice and looks just fine for my purposes. I have previously had a hard white plastic strip which melted and then I had white (vinyl maybe?) strips I lost in a move. They didn't melt but they did get yellowish. I think these are an improvement on both. Would definitely buy again.

title: OK on a Toshiba Satellite P755d with a few fixes
text:
This is a decently made caddy, aluminum not all plastic like one I had purchased for an older Dell (never worked but too cheap to send back).

Two issues for my particular hardware, the Satellite and a OCZ Agility. First there is a small bracket in my laptop that secures the optical housing to the machine with one screw underneath the memory bay. There are two screws from the laptop of adequate length to reach the original equipment optical housing though this bracket. These screws cannot reach down to the thread portion located deeper inside this caddy. Although I have probably hundreds of screws, none were both long enough and thin enough to get through the holes in the Satellite's hold down bracket to the caddy. I ended up using electrical tape to secure the bracket to the caddy. I think it will be fine.

Second, the Agility did not appear in the bios or in windows when laptop was booted. After much messing around with other drives in the caddy I finally realized that the Agility was not shoving up tight enough to the connectors. I had to push it from behind with a thick screwdriver. Success. A Vertex was not a problem nor was the mechanical drive. Just the Agility. I believe it is just a problem with this drive, probably connector board a little off but not noticeable when regular SATA and power cables are applied to it.

Last is I guess a non-issue from function but not from form. The bezel or lack thereof. Yes, it will look a little funny without a bezel. I had quite the time removing the Satellite's bezel from the optical drive but did manage it in the end. And I can still pop the optical in when needed (like when I was troubleshooting) and run it without its bezel in a pinch. YMMV

Overall OK certainly for the price. They might want to look into how deep those threads are where a hold down bracket is applied. My mfr screws certainly were not long enough. Would be nice if they could supply two in addition to the HD screws they already do. And the lack of even some sort of generic-ish bezel were the only reasons for the one star off.

title: Works.. but not Great with my somewhat Older TV..
text:
I recently purchased this item (an BLK HDMI Composite​ Adapter by Audiovox) hoping that I could use it to connect my new Nintendo Switch Video Gaming Console (using the Switch's Dock) up to an somewhat older composite TV.

The television set in question does not have any HDMI inputs on it at all.

The adapter worked.. but not very well.

The picture displayed on the TV ended up being in black and white. And it was in fairly low resolution (of course I expected the resolution to be low).

Although I do think poor image quality probably results probably has more to do with the fact that the television itself is a bit older technology wise.. and less to do with the adapter.

So.. In the end, I will probably end up just getting myself a newer HDMI display/television of some sort to use with my Nintendo Switch. Because the results that I got using this adapter are not very suitable.

Something that I was a bit worried about.. going into this anyway.

Again, the poor results probably have more to do with the TV set is simply older technology.. and less to do with the adapter itself.

So I am only giving this product two stars.

EDIT: But again I am stressing that I believe my poor results where do to my TV being too old. I think this adapter probably works just fine.. and the TV in question just was too old and wouldn't work very well with any adapter.. due to it being older technology.

title: Not for photographers with small hands, but has some easy touches
text:
This is a sturdy tripod head, ideal for serious photographers shooting HDR images, panoramas and sporting events.

Pros:
1. Holds DSLR cameras and lenses firmly
2. The shoe slides into place easily and is secured by a knob lock and safety stops.
3. Simple system to rotate and adjust, with two spirit levels for portrait and landscape shots.
4. 360 degree rotation for very smooth and easy panning

Cons:
1. "Quick" shoe isn't that quick as you have to find a coin or screwdriver to attach it to your camera.
2. It's not easy to use if you have small hands - it isn't physically possible for me to use the Grip Position Release System with one hand.
3. The trigger action is very stiff and makes my hands tired very quickly
4. Adds significantly to the weight of the tripod

I use this mostly for motor sports events and panoramas because of the smooth panning action, where I don't need to move around much or pull the trigger very often. This would probably work a lot better in the hands of a stronger person with bigger hands.

Amanda Richards, October 17, 2013

title: Strong enough for a man, but doesn't understand women.
text:
Pros:

1. The 102 is small enough for everyday toting - great size for everyday working folk who always keep their camera close at hand.
2. Enough space in the main compartment for a DSLR with medium telephoto/standard zoom lens attached, plus an off camera flash and one more lens.
3. Easy zippers allow quick access to the camera, and support straps keep it secure.
4. Comes with an all weather cover neatly tucked away in a pocket and a built in microfiber cloth.
5. Two external compartments and a pocket for small accessories. Handy memory card pockets in main compartment.
6. Includes a tripod holder and strap
7. Nicely padded with customizable dividers

Cons:

1. The 102 is a lot smaller than it looks on-line. A Nikon SB900 flash can't stand upright as illustrated, but has to be pivoted over the DSLR compartment.
2. The upper compartment can't hold a change of clothes, or anything other than small accessories, keys, a wallet and a couple of calling cards. It can hold filters, a small lens or a point and shoot camera.
3. Can only hold compact tripods or monopods, and even then, it becomes unwieldy.
4. If you sling the strap over one shoulder, the bag isn't balanced and keeps slipping off your shoulder, especially if you're doing anything with your other hand.
5. If you sling it over your head and across your back as illustrated, it's stable, but not comfortable for the female anatomy, and certainly not aesthetically pleasing for frontal views.
6. If you use the additional support strap, it doesn't fit around your waist as it should, but across your chest, hence even more problems for female photographers with curves.
7. No place for water bottle, no cell phone pouch on strap

I bought this to use for everyday toting of my DSLR. Size wise it works for this purpose, but is not comfortable to walk around with. It's not big enough for travel or comfortable enough for nature shoots, or weddings, or suitable for anywhere you'll need extra gear, water or clothes. Definitely not for a theme park or hiking expedition.
I would recommend this to male urban or street photographers (or non-zaftig female photographers).

Amanda Richards
July 22, 2013

title: For those times when you need a little something to steady yourself
text:
First and foremost, this is a monopod, and should not be expected to perform the duties of a tripod. The two are not on the same playing field, especially if said field is not level, and the monopod's job is simply to hold the fort when a tripod can't go into battle.

Pros:
1. This monopod comes with its own little stand, and is perfectly capable of standing on its own three feet.
2. It can easily support a DSLR with a medium telephoto lens.
3. Set up is simple, requiring only unscrewing the bottom section, opening the legs and screwing the base back on securely.
4. Extends over six feet tall with two adjustable sections
5. Perfect for concert and theatre events in low or changing light, when a tripod either isn't allowed or is impractical.
6. Great for weddings and museum visits
7. You can sit with the monopod braced against your chair and your feet anchoring the legs for extra stability. (I also use a cable release)
8. Padded grip
9. Handy against attacks by stray animals in the wild.

Cons:
1. At the shortest it's still more than two feet long, and doesn't fit well in the external tripod section of smaller camera bags.
2. It's very heavy for all-day trekking around theme parks, museums, big city tours and the like.
3. No carrying case (but has a strap to fasten it on to stuff)
4. Little legs make a lot of noise when concealed (but see below)
5. A bit tricky on uneven ground if you want to use the legs

Things you can fix:
1. Needs a Quick Release head (albeit adding extra weight and cost)
2. Rattling feet can be muffled with a rubber band

Overall, I'm happy with this monopod, except perhaps for the length and weight. It does a great job when you're rushing around in crowded places where tripods fear to tread.

Amanda Richards, June 19, 2013

title: Great for walkabouts
text:
Point of View: Hobby/Amateur
Cameras: Nikon D7000/D600

I would not have purchased this lens if it hadn't come with the D600 as a kit lens, but I am SO glad that Nikon knows best. As a medium telephoto zoom lens, I use it on the D600 most of the time for capturing landscapes and street photography.

At 24mm it's wide enough to capture everything from foreground elements to distant landmarks, and at f/3.5 it's fast enough to get the wedding party in a church (if the lights aren't too dim) without using a flash.

When it comes to festivals and carnivals, I use this on the D600 for the big picture, and a 50mm f/1.8 on the D7000 for street portraits. It is light and unobtrusive enough to take into crowded places for extended periods, something I would never do with a 70-200mm f/2.8.

What it's not good at is wildlife photography and sports photography, but there are other lenses for those purposes. The only thing I don't like is the lens hood, which when inverted over the lens completely blocks the zoom ring. It also gets in the way when you're trying to remove the lens from the camera. If I don't need to use the hood, it's easier to take it off completely than keep it on-camera.

Overall, a compact, convenient and affordable lens for general purpose and vacation photography.

Note: Uses a 72mm screw-on filter

Amanda Richards, February 3, 2013

title: A cinch for a strap
text:
Pros:

1. Easy to set up - no tools required. Just attach the stainless steel/aluminum mount to the tripod socket at the bottom of the camera and tighten the thumbscrew. (And recheck ever so often that it's tightened)

2. Fits a lot more comfortably than a regular neck strap. All DSLRs should come with this type of strap. No neck burn or awkward carrying positions.

3. Can be tightened against the body by pulling on the pivot ring and camera (in opposite directions) for when you need to go hands free across some difficult terrain (or when your hands are otherwise occupied)

4. Can be worn on either shoulder or even behind your back as needed.

5. There's a locking mechanism to hold the strap in place when you're not shooting.

6. Strap adjusts itself and extends when you raise the camera to take a shot (when the locking mechanism is disengaged of course)

7. This strap is built for a man, (the women's strap has a small curve for the zaftig photographer) but it's still comfortable (and strong enough) regardless.

Cons:

1. Dangling an expensive camera and even more expensive lens
upside down,
from ONE screw,
in ONE spot,
on the bottom of the camera,
is a bit nerve-wracking. (But regular straps can malfunction also)

2. Strap could have been improved with a bit more padding.

3. Strap takes up quite a bit of space in a camera bag (but you can't have everything) For smaller bags you can detach the strap and reattach when needed in a couple of seconds.

4. Obviously you have to detach the strap when you want to use a tripod

5. No fault of the strap, but the models in the video on the product page need some instruction on how to hold a DSLR properly (LOL)

Overall, this has solved a big problem for me, as this is a much more comfortable way to carry around a heavy camera and lens for hours at a time.

Amanda Richards, January 8, 2013

Note: I recently bought the women's version of this strap. The only difference is that the strap is a little bit narrower at the top, and has a clever little bend for negotiating feminine curves.

title: Best bokeh for your buck
text:
I bought this because when you can't afford Nikon glass, you choose Sigma.

One of three (arguably) most recommended wedding lenses, the others being a 50mm f/1.4 or f/1.8 prime and a 24-70 f/2.8, my experience with this is creamy dreamy soft backgrounds with perfectly focused subjects. Please note that this is an amateur point of view, and I shoot weddings when the bride or groom asks whether I'm going to walk with my camera, because the camera takes really good pictures.

I love it for details like the decorations, cake and candles, for far off shots of the ceremony without getting in the way, and for those cool shots where the bride/groom is in focus and the groom/bride beside her/him is out of focus (but very recognizable)

What I don't like is the weight (but I can suck that up) and that you can't work the group shots without changing the lens (until I get a second camera) unless you're standing way back, which isn't always possible.

I also love it for portraits, especially of toddlers, and will be trying it next at a field hockey game, as I understand it to be aces at sports. I bought the [[ASIN:B000CDA7Y4 Sigma APO Teleconverter 2x EX DG for Nikon Mount Lenses]] which works fine with this lens, and plan to go stalking hummingbirds as soon as they discover my [[ASIN:B0019Y0YCA Aspects 153 Mini Hummzinger Hummingbird Feeder]].

If you need to shoot in low light, and prefer ambience instead of the brightness of flash, this fast lens and some ISO pumping can really do the job. (Note: I'm currently using a Nikon D7000 and hope to upgrade to a full frame in the near future)

Amanda Richards, January 2, 2013

title: Sound boost for your computer
text:
Pros:

1. It's a Bose
2. Relatively easy to set up even for a non-technical person
3. As would be expected, great sound
4. I didn't expect the ear buds to be comfortable with that funny looking rubbery plastic thingy that fits into your outer ear, but I was wrong (using the smallest size - it comes with three sizes) Plus, they don't fall out of your ears if you make sudden movements.
5. Control for volume and the audio jack are on the same speaker, so easily kept within reach
6. Sleek modern look
7. Not designed for noise reduction, so you can still be aware of what's going on around you.

Cons:

1. No "off" position - the volume can only be turned down, but not off
2. Speakers are a little on the large side if you're limited for space on your desk - just over 7" tall, 3" wide and just about 6" deep
3. Ear bud case is nice, padded and zippered, with Bose logo, but is too big to fit in your pocket. My iPhone actually fits comfortably inside the case.
4. Ear bud packaging requires a chainsaw and jaws of life to open

Overall, a good acquisition for me as my computer speakers went kaput some time ago, and this is way better.

Amanda Richards, January 1, 2013

title: A lot of bag to like
text:
Pros:

1. Light
2. Durable
3. Well thought out and constructed, aesthetically pleasing
4. Back mesh prevents overheating against your body
5. Adjustable straps around the chest and waist for extra support and portability
6. Can hold a DSLR with a 70-200 lens attached, plus 3 or 4 more lenses in the bottom compartment.
7. Three way access to the bottom compartment, plus customizable padding makes it easily adaptable
8. Padded lap top sleeve holds a 15" laptop
9. Top compartment and side pockets hold tons of extra gear such as memory cards, spare batteries, filters, remotes, lens cloths et al, plus a change of clothes and other personal stuff
10. Comes with a rain hood that covers the bag and your gear in inclement weather
11. Can fit on airplanes for travel
12. Bright orange interior makes it easy to find gear in a hurry

Cons:

1. Holds so much stuff that you tend to overpack, and THAT's when it weighs a ton
2. 9.6 x 8.1 x 16.5 inches sounds much smaller than it actually is. This bag is pretty big, but then of course it holds lots of stuff. Too big for everyday toting, but fine for photo shoots.
3. No compartment on strap for cell phone - not essential, but really handy
4. One external strap can possibly hold a tripod, but not very securely.
5. No water bottle pocket, but I guess you can attach one with a carabiner
6. Nice canvas zipper pulls, but I can see the pull tab breaking off from the slider, as that part is pretty thin. I wouldn't recommend grabbing the bag by the zipper pulls (if that's all you can reach without getting up.)

This is now the biggest camera bag of the three that I own, and probably the one I will be using for travel in the future.

Amanda Richards, January 1, 2013

title: Unsafe text
text:
The look of this is very cool
Retro-chic and so old-school
Great for teacher/boss misleading
"Wow! She made notes - and she's reading!!"

The problem with the Verso Trends

Because it's mostly pliant plastic
With corner straps made of elastic

Your Kindle may just go kaput
