We have 4 sections of 4 foot tall dog fence panels that attach to the underside of the rv via zip ties. These are as strong and supple as the ones we normally purchase. They lock correctly and stay put like they should.

title: Working well  for tablet to tv connections
text: Well made cables in the 15 feet length. I am using these to connect my tablet to a tv several feet away in the RV. In locations where our cellular service is very weak and even the booster can't get us online, I stream movies from my tablet to the television. These cables let me do that easily and keep my tablet by my side for easy access.

title: Temperature monitor warning is an hour delayed
text:
My original Echo, purchased when the first invitations were sent out, was much beloved for years. She finally began to have performance problems last month. Stuttering, failing to perform tasks and simply not hearing her name anymore. Definitely time for an upgrade.

I like this Echo Plus, but I'm not thrilled with the short, fat, squatty shape over the tall, slender original Echo. This one doesn't fit in the same spot and just looks like any generic, knockoff speaker rather than Alexa. However, the sound quality of music and Audible books is superior and can be clearly heard at lower volumes than my old Echo.

I will say the coordination/communication between the physical Plus and the Alexa app is spotty and slow. In particular when using the Plus's built in temperature monitor. I had hoped specifically to use this to monitor our RV temperature when traveling for the safety of our dogs. Alexa does tell me the temperature has reached the preset warning level - an HOUR later!!! That's useless. I ended up spending more money to but a dedicated Wifi temperature/humidity monitor that alerts my phone via text and email literally within 90 seconds of the preset parameters. I love Alexa in general and we have 3 Dots, the Auto and this Plus, so we're fully integrated in the ecosystem, but this Plus isn't as good as the original, 1st generation Echo.

title: Connected Alexa Auto to a 14 year old car
text: I wanted Alexa Auto in my 2006 Sequoia, but it is not equipped with bluetooth or the new tech. Fortunately, Alexa Auto comes with an AUX cable connection. This cable let me connect her to the car radio and my phone via Bluetooth to the Alexa app. Problem solved in one step.

title: Fits exactly and buttons all work
text: My husband finally upgraded his 4 year old tablet to a Tab 5SE - that 10" screen is a huge improvement over his old 8 inch tablet. But of course,  a new gadget requires a new case. This one is really working well for us. It fits exactly and all the buttons are accessible. The charging port is equally easy to use. I love that this case has built in rails to prop up the tablet so you can watch Netflix etc.

title: Works  like it should,  no interference with the touch screen sensitivity
text: I sincerely doubt there's any screen protector that goes on without a couple of bubbles.  This one has two air bubbles on the far edge, but they don't interfere with the visibility of the screen at all - we only see them when tablet is turned off actually. The shield is clear and is not noticeable when typing.  There is zero lag in screen response. We've used this brand on other tablets and it definitely saved one from damage.

title: Super handy, clever design
text:
We have another one of these tall cube style surge protectors with multi outlets and we love it. This one works exactly the same way and has a much longer cord. It does a good job.

You can plug several things in at once or divide the cube into two pieces and plug the top directly into an outlet. I like that option best. It gives us a place for a lamp and two phone chargers by the bed. Plus the second half can be used elsewhere.

title: Unreliable and  difficult to use
text: Skip this and buy the real deal instead. After trying multiple times over two weeks, we cannot get it to work correctly or consistently. We don't have Apple products and this is preset for Apple - you have to manually remove it from the tv to change it to Android every time.  It doesn't remember your previous setting choice. Additionally, it rarely actually works for mirror casting which was sort of the entire point. Instead,  we're just using the Google Chrome Cast thing. That works correctly every single time without the need for some random company's app.

title: Working well with phone and tablet chargers
text:
It seems like there are never enough power strips in the house. Between the TV's, phone chargers, tablet and laptop chargers, sound bars, air purifiers, fans, lamps etc etc, we're always short on outlets.

This power strip fits nicely the bedroom and the cord is a nice length for reaching the beside table. It handles two phone chargers, a table lamp and the tablet charger without any problems.

title: Bluetooth is a nice upgrade
text: I decided against installing this radio myself for reasons. We hired a local shop to do it. It seems to be done correctly and everything is working as it should.  The 6.8" screen is big enough to see and make the choices I want driving. It's working with my LG phone via bluetooth and that was the primary reason I wanted a new stereo in the older Sequoia. We'll see how it fares as time goes by.

title: Working great 90 days in
text:
This is the second bluetooth adapter I've tried and it's the best one. It stays plugged in despite bumpy roads and that's definitely a plus. I paired it with my LG V40 phone and for 3 months it hasn't forgotten my phone and connects automatically every time I get in the car.

The sound quality is fine for music and audio books on the go. The volume can be adjusted three ways- on my phone, on the car's radio control or on this unit directly. It also fast charges my phone and an LG Stylo 4 which is always welcome. My only complaint is the sound quality of hands free calls. On my end, they are fine. But on the other end, there is a noticeable buzz or tunnel type sound. Not a deal breaker though since I only use it for music and audio books 95% of the time.

title: Nice sound with classical music and audio books
text:
As a rule, I prefer over the ear headphone style for comfort. But there are circumstances when ear buds are safer and more practical - like riding horses. These buds are better than expected and suit my needs pretty well.

The case is the actual charger and you can charge the buds without the case being plugged in as long as it has residual power. You do need to put the buds into the case at the precise angle or they don't charge. These do come with small, medium and large ear pieces so you can get the correct fit for your ears. I do wish the right and left markers were more obvious and easier to see.

I listen mostly to audio books and country, 80s or classical music. I don't use or care about heavy bass in earbuds at all, so I cannot speak to that performance quality. The do fine with the 80s pop and hard rock and behave nicely with classical music as well. There is an option for noise cancellation - called Through Sound. It actually works and there is a very noticeable difference when it's on. I'm pretty impressed by that. I do not like having to put yet another app on my phone to set these up and get full functionality out of the ear buds.

title: Fine for casual use like audiobooks
text:
I love my wireless earbuds in specific circumstances, but there are times when I don't want to worry about batteries or bluetooth etc. I'm using these corded earbuds for basic stuff like listening to audio books and some music while walking dogs mostly. I've been using them with my LG V40 phone and an older Samsung tablet with no problems.

The sound is clean and clear and I have not noticed any buzzy feedback. The buds come with additional ear piece covers do you can the fit you need. I'm not expecting fine musical depth or clarity....seriously, these are just no name cheap ear buds. They are fine for that. The claims of noise cancellation are weak at best. They do not actively cancel outside noise, just soften it a bit as you listen to your book.

title: Works fine with several items
text: My old power strip finally quit and I replaced it with this one for a TV, sound bar, streaming box and a small dehumidifier. I like the cable on this one. It's very well made and doesn't look like it will fray from bending. Using it with the TV, sound bar and streaming box for a few hours consecutively  is fine - nothing gets hot and everything works fine.

title: Worked great for tablet to TV slide show
text: We have two dumb TVs and like it that way. The Rokus work perfectly with them and all's well.  However, I wanted to do a slide show of photos on the big screen from my tablet and that required a work around. This adapter fixed the problem. The USB type C works with both our Samsung tablets and the HDMI end fit properly on the TV. I was able to do my photos on the big screen and everyone could see them comfortably.

title: Never worked, won't stay on and app cannot connect
text: This is nonfunctional garbage. It charges until the light goes green. Turn it on and the light comes on and then press record... Nothing. All lights turn off and it's dead. The app gives you about 5 seconds to connect via Wi-Fi and then it fails. Multiple times... I deleted it entirely and gave up.  This is an interesting idea, but very poorly executed. Additionally,  one of the clips for the cap brim cracked putting it on the first time. Just avoid.

title: Easy to install and so far it works just as it should
text:
I keep a sensor at the point where the driveway opens to the barn area so I know if someone is arriving while I am doing horse stuff. Our old one lasted several years, so I hope this one lives up to that standard.

This one just went on the same fence post hook as the old one. The sensor is about 38 feet away just inside the barn door overhang - so it's a very short distance. (I can't speak the 500 foot claims)This system allows you to choose from several different alert sounds and that's nice... Our old one had a single shrill shriek that got old fast. So far this is working correctly and doing the job without problems.

title: Fits exactly right, screen is clear and clean
text: I love my Primetime tablet and have used it daily for two years. My old screen protector cracked after a dog knocked it off the sofa. So this one is the replacement. It was easy to install and fits exactly as it should. There's no clarity or touch sensitivity loss with the protector on the screen. I only see on bubble and it's hidden by the edge of the case, so I'm happy.

title: Brought in three out of five local stations
text:
We cut the cord in 2016 and haven't looked back once. We stream Prime, Hulu, and DirecTV Now for a quarter of the old cable bill. My only issue is the inability to get our four local channels - ABC, FOX, CBS, and NBC. I tried a very expensive antenna and it brought in only Telemundo...we have zero interest in that.

This one is very thin and doesn't require an electric connection. Just connect it to the tv and scan for channels. After trying four different locations and rescanning each time, this antenna is better than the other one. We now get the Telemundo AND CBS and Fox. Still no NBC or ABC, but an improvement. The signal is clear even on a rainy day.

title: Nice sound for classical music, more comfortable than other earbuds I've tried
text:
As a rule, I don't particularly care for in ear earbuds, I usually choose the traditional headphones instead. These come with different size ear pieces so I was able to get the most comfortable fit I could. They aren't bad and I've been able to wear them for an hour at a time with no real discomfort.

I had no trouble connecting these to my phone and using them working around the barn and horses. The sound quality is good for my needs. I mostly listen to audio books and a mix of country and classical music. Bass isn't a thing really for me. The clarity of sound is decent for Beethoven and current composers like Hans Zimmer.

I've gotten a couple of hours at a time without needing to recharge, but I haven't tried to run them down fully. The charging storage box is very handy. The earbuds can be stored and kept clean and charge at the same time - clever. box

title: Good size for traveling and charging more than one item at a time
text: My husband travels with his job often and into a variety of countries and we have all sorts of adapters lying around. This one packs nicely. This one is a nice size and provides multiple outlets so you can charge more than one thing. The system seems to work well - he's only used it once so far with his phone and tablet. Both charged correctly and nothing overheated. Keep in mind though, that these sorts of adapters are never meant to be used with stuff like a hair dryer etc.

title: Small bag meant for light duty
text:
This is a cute, little bag meant to carry just a few, small items. Both sides open with solid zippers and there's a bit more room inside than it appears. The leather feels real and appears to be nice quality. All the stitching is solid on my bag and nothing is loose.

I used it today at the Farmer's Market and running errands. It held my phone, a small wallet, an EpiPen and the car keys comfortably. I can see using this when we travel.

title: Restored WiFi connectivity to an older laptop
text: The wifi connection thingy in our older laptop failed recently, essentially rendering the entire computer useless. In a hail Mary effort, I thought we would try this gizmo to salvage the laptop. It worked. The computer is seeing our WiFi network again and working well.

title: Working well with a high use printer
text: I recently set up a new printer and it needed a direct Ethernet connection to the router. The cable worked fine and the 15 foot length allowed me to set it up across the room - about 8 feet away.

title: Works great with three different phones and two tablets
text: This is a very good charger that seems to work on everything we have. It's small enough to fit in a purse pocket or a carry on bag when you're traveling. We've used this in a hotel room and at home with three different phones and two different tablets. It charged the LG V40, LG Stylo 4 and a Samsung Note without overheating. The ten inch Samsung tablet and an 8" older Samsung tablet both charged normally, but the phones were faster.

title: Keeps a thick extension cord safely contained
text: I am remodeling a weekend cabin and have power tools and a portable air conditioning unit using extension cords. This cover is exactly what I needed. My cord fits inside and is contained safely. I am not tripping on it or having to move it every time I try to work.

title: Helpful with an low end projector
text:
We have a awesome Bose 500 soundbar for our living room TV that connects via digital optical cable only. And we have a low end projector that only has the RCA cable connections which means it can't talk to our soundbar. So we rarely use the projector because it's tiny speaker is essentially useless.

I managed to get this converter set up and working between the soundbar and the projector. It's not perfect or as clear as the tv to soundbar connection, but it works. We can watch a summer movie outside on the closed garage door and hear it now....that is a win. The nieces were here and we watched The Black Stallion outside to their utter delight.

title: Light and easy to use
text: I don't need a headset like this often, typically just a couple of times a week to do a video call with my Mother. The headphones help me block distractions and hear her more clearly. This is a very light weight set and the plastic feels a bit flimsy. I don't expect this to last more than a year with my light use, but in the meantime they do work for my needs.

title: App is useless. Antenna barely brings in two local stations
text:
Well, I don't hate this antenna, but I sure don't like it either. It's bigger than other indoor antennas, but but not enormous - it's definitely uglier than others. The app for this is pretty useless and I just deleted it. It shows the towers nearest your location, but then freezes repeatedly.

Supposedly we have three towers with a total of 14 stations in two towns within 45 miles of us. I have a clean line of sight for two of them within 15 miles and should get at least 8 stations. After messing around with this antenna for four days and moving it eight times, we never pulled in more than two stations. One is the local ABC affiliate and the other is some Spanish only channel.

In comparison, I borrowed a different indoor antenna from our next door neighbor and within minutes of attaching it, we had 8 different stations without a bunch of position drama. It's also smaller and less intrusive visually than this one. I think I will just buy one like my neighbor has instead and put this one away as a last resort backup.

title: Fits the Ubiquiti Rocket M9 Wireless Access Point and works great
text: We installed the Ubiquiti Rocket M9 Wireless Access Point to create a separate WiFi network in a second building on the property. I don't know all the technical details on how that whole system gets created etc - it is complicated and required a legit pro to set up. However, the Rocket M9 didn't come with external antennas and I didn't care to spend a bunch of additional money for their brand. Instead, we got this antenna. It works perfectly and fit immediately for about a third of the cost. The signal in the building is strong and unwavering and I'm able to stream Netflix etc on the tv when I'm working in there.

title: Ok picture, tinny sound and only one HDMI port
text:
We've never had a projector before and this is a reasonable beginner/introductory projector. It helped us realize that we're not really projector people for a couple of reasons. It works best in a completely dark room or outside with no residual daylight or street lights. We found the best picture came from using the the included screen out on the patio around 9pm. The picture wasn't bad, but it certainly wasn't really 1080p using the Roku stick. Going outside in the summer here for a movie is a cute idea, but this is Texas and it's just too humid and miserable for that.

The projector has speakers built in, but they are small and the sound is tinny. You can connect a sound bar if yours uses the RCA type cables - niether of my bars do. They only use HDMI or Digital optical line and the projector only has one HDMI port and no optical audio line. So we're just stuck with the built in speakers. I'm not unhappy with this unit, but I don't see us using it often at all.

title: Very handy way to get all the tv equipment plugged in
text: This is a neat gadget. It breaks apart so you can use it in multiple ways. I just need the original tower for the living room TV set up with the streaming sticks, tv, sound bar and router equipment. So far it is working just fine.

title: Beautiful bag, well stitched and roomy
text: My husband and I both love quality leather bags and he immediately claimed this one. It's gorgeous in a deep cognac dye. The stitching is thick and solid throughout the bag. There's room inside for his laptop, tablet and daily receipts and paperwork. It tucks away in a cubby in his truck when not needed and stats out of the way. He said a client already complimented him on the briefcase. Hopefully, it will last a couple of years at the least.

title: Gorgeous, astonishing battery life. Crisp, clean sound for music and books
text:
I have a pair of the Masters & Dynamic Leica edition and I absolutely love them even after almost a year. Lately though, my husband has been skulking about wearing them so trying these out was a no brainer. I've used these MW50s for three weeks now and I actually like them better.

First, the rich saddle color leather is really beautiful and there's no mistaking these headphones for some random pair. Second, they connected via Bluetooth to my LG V40 phone, my old Sony Xperia phone and two different Samsung tablets easily and quickly. Third is the excellent battery life on these. I've literally listened to music and my Audible audiobooks for three hours at a time for four days in row before recharging them. That includes getting a couple of calls. The fit is the main reason I prefer the MW50 phones over the Leica edition. These can go on or over the ears and since I have small ears, the on ear option is very comfortable for me for hours. No cauliflower ear and the heat build up is slower.

The sound quality is excellent and clear without distortion or fuzziness. I listen to a little of everything - country, classical, old rock etc. I can clearly discern the French horns in classical music as well as the background banjo in some old country music. I don't know about the quality of heavy bass with these simply because I don't listen to heavy bass music. Audiobooks with full production recordings, are clear and crisp - I can detect background sound effects comfortably without any fuzziness or distortion. Bottom line is these are worth that eye opening price if you use them every day and appreciate style as well as function.

title: Works well with small appliances. Pay attention to the power draw
text:
My husband has two of these that he rotates in the semi truck. This one powers his little lunch box oven when he's on the road - it draws far less than 300 watts so it's safe to use for the two hours it takes to cook his food while he's driving. After two weeks, he says he likes the inverter and it doesn't get overly hot.

You need to use caution with this sort of thing though. Attempting to use it with an appliance that draws the full rating of 300 watts will blow your fuses. You need a direct connection or larger, professionally installed inverter.

title: Handles basic video streaming very easily
text: I'm probably not using this router to its full capacity - we set it up in a cabin I'm restoring so I can access how-to videos as I work. The router is working well and providing a strong signal from about 75 feet away from it and through walls. I haven't experienced any excessive buffering watching YouTube on my tablet or phone. I've also put an Alexa Dot out in the cabin to stream music and my Audible books. For my current needs, this router is working perfectly - I'll move it into the cabin full time when the restoration is complete.

title: SD card slot isn't finished - card disappears inside the camera body. Non-functional
text:
Sigh. Yet more garbage from a random, no name brand. This is very small and flimsy to begin with. The charging cable is an old funky shaped connection rather than the universal "c" style. You can't charge it with any other cable. Little bit out of date with current tech.

It does not come with a SD memory card so you need to buy one or recycle one from another gadget. And that's where the real trouble starts. The slot for the card isn't closed inside the camera and the card just vanishes inside. You can't get it out without breaking the camera body open. Just don't buy this thing. Get a dash cam from a known company.

title: Portable and nice at the horse show
text:
We don't have a projector for home use, but after horse shows we like to watch the videos and learn from our mistakes or celebrate a win. One of my students brings her little projector and connects to her phone or mine. We've been using the literal side of a barn to watch the video - almost life size.

This screen folds and can travel with very little drama. We've used it twice so far and it just lives in the tack trunk between uses. It does what we need nicely, but I can't speak to the quality of an actual movie or images from tv. Our videos and still shots are a bit grainy, but that's amateurs recording moving animals in a group or over jumps. I don't think it's a problem with the screen...just us.

title: Working fine without signal distortion
text: I have the 25 foot length so we could connect a tv directly to the router. The tv was losing WiFi signal since it's several rooms away from the router - we only stream and don't have cable, so a clean, clear internet connection is a must.  This cable was easy to use and run through a hallway wall with little drama. It's flat and that makes a difference. I haven't noticed any distortion of signal or buffering and it fixed the lost signal problem.

title: Easy to use one handed. Good for wide open vistas, not great for details
text:
I haven't bothered with a video camera in many years - using an excellent cell phone camera is just so much easier and convienent. That is still the case when I decide between using this camera vs my LG V40 phone for quick video of the dogs and horses. However, I did take the video camera with me to Big Bend National Park last week and tried it out there.

There are two rechargeable batteries and they offer far more use time than I expected. Swapping them out is pretty simple once you figure out where they go. The instructions are skimpy, but things are reasonably logical. The little carrying case is padded and the entire camera and case fits perfectly in a side pocket of a small hiking pack.

Actual use is straightforward. The camera fits in your palm and the record, photo and zoom buttons are designed to be pressed with just a thumb. I do like the view screen - it rotates and lets you really see what you're filming. For wide, expansive vistas like West Texas offers, this camera is fine and captures the vast distance of the landscape. However, close up details are fuzzy - I sincerely doubt this is true 1080p quality simply because the video shot from my phone is sharper and prettier. This is essentially a fine, basic little video camera that won't break a budget if it's lost or stolen.

title: Nice option for showing photos on a television screen from a tablet or Chromebook
text: I have used this cable to throw photos from my Chromebook to a Sceptre television so we could see them more easily. It worked fine and we weren't having to hover over one ting screen. I have not been able to get it to work consistently with a Fire tablet though. The Samsung tablets are fine though.

title: Comfortable, noise cancellation actually works well.
text:
I have a very good pair of Bluetooth Sony earphones with pretty good noise cancellation, but I wanted a second set that could be used with a regular 3mm plug with my phone. Traveling brings enough aggravation without worrying about battery life on one more gadget.

These are very comfortable on the ears for an hour or two while listening to an audio book and my ears don't get hot. These are light enough not to cause cauliflower ear either. I tested the noise cancellation feature both at home with the tv and in a semi truck idling. Those trucks are pretty quiet inside compared to standing next to one outside, but the noise is still there and it impedes sleep if you're not used to it. I'm pretty pleased with how well these block external noise - it's an absolute difference and a little better than my Sonys.

Music is a pleasure with these also. There are adjustments to increase bass etc if you're so inclined. My primary use though is audio books. The full production Audible Originals with a full cast and sound effects are especially nice with these headphones - you can hear the background noises and details clearly and not the dog barking next door. I find myself reaching for these almost every day lately.

title: Syncs all Google stuff correctly, long battery, weighs nothing
text:
These Chromebooks are a weird hybrid of tablet and real laptop. They don't do everything can full laptop does, but they do more than a simple tablet. Oddly enough, there is a place for these. This is the second one we've had in the last few years.

This one is very light and easy to grab and use in the armchair or while on the road in the passenger seat. The screen is vibrant and the colors are true when watching a movie or looking at your photos. The beauty of a Chromebook is having super easy access to everything stored in your existing Google cloud account - photos, books, passwords, contacts, email, etc. This syncs exactly like your phone and tablets do so you can switch between machines and still keep current.

I've been pleased with the battery life on the Acer. It can go with light use and sleep mode a couple of days before needing to be charged. It has no trouble connecting to and staying connected to our WiFi even outside on the patio. I've connected my Bluetooth headphones and watched a movie with it and it works fine. I like this and find I'm grabbing it more often than I thought I would.

title: Nice choice for audiobooks
text:
Sometimes, I like to listen to my audio book in bed while my husband watches TV. In order to avoid disturbing him, I use a fancy pair of noise cancellation earphones that vost several pretty pennies. They work well, but can feel heavy after an hour or two.

This set is a decent substitute that I won't feel bad about breaking/dropping etc. They are extremely light and don't have noise cancellation, but that's fine. The fit is decent and the ear covers are soft and don't feel hot. The sound quality is better than expected - audiobooks are clear and clean. I listened to a bit of country and classical music with these and the music sounds right, but not quite as pure as with my Bose headphones - of course, that's not a fair comparison. Still, these are a good option for basic stuff.

title: Just pass on this. WiFi is non functional and cords are exposed after installing
text:
I'm not impressed at all with this camera. That's my own fault for choosing a camera from a random company I've never heard of - generic soap is fine, but not for electronics. This is difficult to install and just badly designed. There are cords left dangling unless you create a space in the wall to hide them. A thief could easily cut these and kill the camera....sort of defeats the entire purpose of having it.

The biggest problem here is the so called wifi connection. It simply doesn't work once the camera is outside of the house. I tested a Canary unit camera outside and it had no problems connecting and staying connected to our WiFi, but this one was essentially dead. Inside and connected via Ethernet cable directly, it works fine - again essentially useless for the purpose of protecting our home.

title: UPDATE REDUCED TO 2 STARS Beautiful sound, amazing with the 500 as a group.
text:
UPDATED REVIEW REDUCED TO TWO STARS JUNE 2019

We've had trouble with the remote for three months now. It works sporadically at best and has finally died entirely. This is a major problem because you cannot do important stuff with the sound bar without the original remote control. Such as.... rebooting it. If you change your WiFi network like.... getting a new router, then you cannot simply go to the app and update the connection. You must reboot the entire sound bar via the remote control only. WHICH DOES NOT WORK AT ALL. This design flaw has rendered the entire sound bar none functional because it cannot connect to the new Wi-Fi - going back to our old router isn't an option because it died. So now I have a sound bar that technically is operational, yet cannot be used. Our Bose 500 sound bar was able to be reconfigured for the Wi-Fi swap because it's remote works like a champ - it's also significantly simpler in design than the 700 remote. (I'll end up spending fifty bucks for a new 700 remote and that really aggravates me)

******* Original review before the drama*******

We've had an older Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System in our living room for a couple of years and we've been pretty happy overall. I recently put the Bose 500 version of this sound bar in our master bedroom and was amazed at the difference, so getting this 700 for the living room was a no brainer. I mostly just expected them to connect as a group and have the same sound, but this 700 is better than the 500.

It's a long, narrow, sleek looking unit with glass finishes that makes it almost invisible in front of the Tv. Our Roku fits alongside without drama. The connections are via digital optical cable or the HDMI. Just turn off your TV speakers - not mute, off from the tv settings. You need to use the included wired headset to fully set the speakers for your room's accoustics. I'm using this bar with a 55", 3 years old, Sceptre dumb tv and a Room streaming stick - the connection was immediate and drama free.

You must use the Bose app to get full functionality out of the sound bar. The app let's you connect two or more Bose speakers with the tech and use them all simultaneously as a group to play music or audiobooks etc. The app also starts the set up for the Alexa link and the streaming services like Prime, Tune In, Bluetooth streaming and others. You can also set 6 favorites as one touch launch options.

Alexa works fine through the sound bar, but the response speed is noticably slower than through a regular Echo. I get a glitchy message saying "This unit is unable to perform routines" every time I say "Good morning". Good morning triggers a specific set of actions from Alexa to turn on our bedside lamps, the bathroom lights, turn off our porch lights, give me the weather and then our daily news brief. Despite that glitchy message, every morning, the Bose performs our routine flawlessly. It's weird, but not a big deal really.

The sound quality is excellent and immersive in multiple settings from music to a movie. The app let's you adjust the sound quality and balance with bass, treble and center. You can also set it for dialogue mode to enhance/clarify voices and reduce background noise - this is very handy for the news or a talk show. Take some time to adjust the settings for what your ear really likes and you'll be amazed at the fullness of sound and all the background details.

After two weeks, I'm incredibly pleased with the build quality, looks, sound and full functionality of both the 500 and 700 units. The 700 wins out by a nose over the 500 for us because the sound is bigger, but mostly because the remote control is better. The remote lights up when you lift it and you can find the buttons instantly. I programmed our TV to the Bose remote and it controls the sound bar, channels up and down and power for both the tv and the sound bar. Bottom line is that I am now looking at buying another 700 for the master bedroom and moving the 500 to our guest suite so we'll have the full set.

title: Beautiful music, crisp television, immersive movies. Some Alexa functions missing
text:
There's a lot to love here with the Bose 500. We have a Denon Soundbase w/ Bluetooth Streaming Audio in our master bedroom and a Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System in the living room - both are from 2015. I'm replacing the Denon unit with this Bose 500 for several reasons, but primarily for significantly better sound quality and Alexa integration.

This is connected to a 2014 Samsung smart TV via the HDMI port. I had no issues connecting the sound bar to the Bose Music app (be sure you get the correct app from Google Play). Next you find the sound bar with the Alexa app and link your Alexa account to this machine. All I had to do for tv sound was turn off the TV speakers through the tv settings and press the tv image button on the Bose remote. Be sure to have 2 AAA batteries on hand because they don't include them for the remote.

You plug in the included headband and use the app to fully calibrate the best sound in your room by sitting in five different locations and letting the headband and sound bar talk. This takes about 6 minutes and it's definitely a step worth doing. The sound from this Bose is amazing - playing Beethoven or Hand Zimmer's soundtrack from Hannibal is immersive and gorgeous. The television is equally good - you can use the app to set the tv sound to dialogue centric for a talk show or regular for movies. You can also adjust the settings for the sound to increase/decrease bass and treble and to move more to the center or sides of the projection speakers. Once you get it set up exactly to your preferences, it can feel like a movie theater without the volume blasting you away. I'm especially loving rewatching Firefly with the Bose 500. The app also let's you do 6 preset favorite music streaming stations from Tune In, Amazon, Spotify and another service.

As to the Alexa functionality... This is actually pretty good with two glaring faults. The sound bar is always listening for the wake word like the Echos do and there's a privacy button as well. I have noticed a tiny lag on a few requests, but it's not constant. I've been getting a weird message telling me that this unit is not compatible with my Alexa routines, then it performs the routine perfectly. (For example, I say good morning and Alexa turns on our bathroom lights, the bedside lamps and gives me the weather) It's a bizarre glitch, but as long as the routines are completed, I don't care.

The first real problem is this unit cannot link to your other Echo units in a music everywhere group - I'm not sure if that's a Bose issue or an Amazon proprietary issue because our Harmon Kardon Alexa speaker cannot be linked either. This is a shame, but not a deal breaker for me, but it's still an issue. The thing that does aggravate me is that this unit is unable to connect to and read my Audible audio books. I get a message that says it is not compatible with Audible at this time. The work around is simply to use Bluetooth and stream my book via my phone or tablet. That's ridiculous with Alexa integrated into the sound bar. This may not bother anyone else, but I listen to audiobooks more than I read now and having that full body, room filling crisp audio is a great thing.

Bottom line for us is that we love this sound bar for television viewing and music. It's sleek and modern and just does it's job. In some ways, the Alexa integration isn't complete, but the basics are there for most functions. It's definitely an improvement over the old Denon box we used to have and it's even better than the Bose Solo 15 in our living room.

title: Very small, faint light that barely reaches past the little fixture
text:
We have several different types of lights from Mr Beams in the garage and outside n several locations. All are battery powered and use motion to come on - the outside spotlights are really bright and dependable. I was expecting the same from these little lights and they aren't really fulfilling my expectations.

These are much smaller than the photos show - just under 2 inches wide actually. On the one hand that tiny size means you can install them just almost anywhere, but that also means there is almost no useable light from these. I wanted to use them in the halls just outside the guestroom doors to guide guests.

The light is very faint and barely lluminates the fixture, never mind where to step on the floor below. I moved them to the bathroom where the light can reflect in the big mirror and that's a definite improvement. I'm going to stick with the regular old plug in nightlights for inside the house and leave Mr Beams to do outdoor spotlights.

title: Ok for basic stuff, but low quality manufacturing
text:
We have several high end sets of binoculars and mostly use them out in West Texas to watch wildlife or the stars. I also use them at horse shows, but I wanted a lighter weight pair. These are compact in size and weigh very little - carrying the case is easy.

However, these are pretty cheaply made. Within minutes of getting them out of the package, a piece fell off and that easy turn focus wheel is sticking. For unimportant viewing like just looking at a bird in a tree or a pack of wild hogs in the pasture, these are fine. But anything else....get higher quality binoculars.

title: Work well in high humidity working outside - stay in place without pinching
text:
I normally avoid in ear earbuds and use wireless headphones or do without. My ears are small and most earbuds hurt within minutes, but I have one really inexpensive set that works ok, but if I'm outside working in the horse barn, they can get sweaty and slippery. These are far better than I expected.

They come with three different size ear bud attachments so you can get the right fit - the smallest set fits me well and they don't pinch or hurt even after an hour of wearing them. The over ear hook isn't hard and it's thin enough to fit over each ear love when with my glasses on. I work with horses and the associated barn chores so that means sweat and lots of movement which can be a problem with earbuds. These have impressed me. After daily use for a week, they haven't fallen off, slipped out of place or lost the connection to my phone despite sweating, shoveling, riding and high heat.

The sound quality is fine for my needs. I listen to mostly audiobooks and some classical music while out with the horses. I can clearly hear the violins vs a harp or French horn without distortion. The only real complaint is when I get a call. I can hear the caller clearly, but they say I sound like I'm in a tin can.

title: Better for watching wildlife than the heavens. Easy assembly and use
text:
I've never owned an actual telescope before, but my father had a couple of them and we used them often. One was really high end and fancy and the other was more like this one - a beginner's, casual scope with limited abilities.

We had this one unpacked and put together, ready to use in about 20 minutes total. The instructions are a little lax, but they do cover what you need to do. There are three different lenses with it and they are relatively easy to swap. The tripod is sturdier than I expected actually and it's quite stable on the cement patio and driveway.

We have had it out a couple of nights with clear skies and we're able to see Venus and the moon and an actual shooting star by sheer good luck. However, I was a bit disappointed with the difficulty of trying to track and focus on a specific night object. Where we've really enjoyed using this telescope is at the farm in daylight. It's a lot of fun watching the horses and deer at distance just doing their thing - my friend even spotted a fox strolling by our pond yesterday at dusk. For my family, this is better suited for wildlife observation that night sky exploration.

title: Features only with expensive monthly membership. Camera images are high quality, works with Alexa
text:
This is one of those products where I really like the gadget itself, but absolutely hate the company and policies behind it. Enough so that I would never actually do business with or trust the Canary company with my personal financial information.

The camera itself is sleek and easy to use and set up. It connected via Bluetooth and wifi in minutes and upgraded its own software immediately. You have to have the app going first to get the camera online and running. There are blue, yellow, white and red lights on the bottom that sort of tell you what the status is - it's actually a pretty solid copy cat of the way the Alexa Echo devices do things.

I've been impressed with the clarity and detail in the camera both live streaming and the short recordings. The night vision is remarkably good - that alone warrants a five star review if the policies didn't ruin everything else. Setting up the app and camera to determine Home, Away and Night modes is ok, but doesn't always work. Right now Canary is alerting me that a person has been detected - IT IS ME! I set it to home mode, but the camera just doesn't believe it. I was able to connect the Canary with Alexa in the Alexa App Skills and watch live streaming of our living room on the bedroom television via the Firestick - completely painless.

Here's my problem. The so called three month free trial of the Canary membership requires a full credit card input BEFORE you can use the free trial. Umm.....no. I don't know this company, there's zero information in the app about exactly how they secure our info and if after the trial is over, you want to cancel, there aren't clear directions and a single step CANCEL button. It's about as sketchy as can be. All the features you might buy this camera for are locked unless you pony up that membership fee. Honestly, I'm just sick to death of being nickled and dined every month. This camera should include a SD card slot and it doesn't. Bottom line is that I have no idea if the microphone works or the downloading of recordings because the free trial isn't actually available unless I give them credit card access - never going to happen.

title: Works fine for basic phone calls indoors and audiobook streaming. Battery lasts for hours
text:
I have the Jabra 35 headset also and this one is noticably different with regard to the quality of phone calls, but that's really the only material difference I can find in my day to day use. The other unit does offer some noise cancellation effects that this one doesn't have and people you call can definitely tell the difference. My husband said that he could hear background noise much more clearly when I called him from this 15 than with the 35.

As far as battery life, this thing is really solid. I've used for three hours on two different days without recharging between days. I primarily use it to listen to audiobooks while I'm doing my barn chores and checking fence lines. I have noticed that I'm pretty limited with the distance I can stray from my physical phone before this headset begins to stutter to lose signal - it seems to be about 20 feet with my Sony Xperia phone.

title: Can be uncomfortable for small ears, nice for audiobooks while doing chores
text:
I like the idea of a single ear microphone and little speaker for when I'm out at the horse barn or riding. This unit is significantly better than a really old one I had several years ago. It paired with my Sony Xperia phone in moments without any trouble.

I mostly use this for listening to audiobooks while I do barn chores and the occasional phone call. The sound is decent with calls, I haven't had trouble hearing anyone clearly. The audio books are clear and the volume is fine for my needs - if I were trying to use this in a moving car, it might be a bit too low. My husband says that he can hear me fine on the other end, but he does get more background noise compared to when I just call directly through my phone.

I do think my big Bluetooth headphones have better range than this unit away from my physical phone. I can set my phone on the gate post and ride in the big arena and never lose the signal with the headphones, but this one stutters a bit after I get 20 feet away. I'm not a huge fan of the ear hook - I have small ears and getting any sort of earbuds to fit comfortably can be tricky. This fits, but it takes some finagling to get it just right. In the end, I think my husband will take possession of this for his daily use on the road - it definitely fits his physical ear better.

title: Fine craftsmanship, high quality materials. Really good sound quality and comfortable
text:
I'm not an audiophile by any means, but I do appreciate excellent quality recreation of certain types of music and full cast production audiobooks. I don't like earbuds for more than a few minutes at a time for a number of reasons so I try to always have a good set of wireless headphones around. My older Sonys are very good, but beginning to show their age after three years of regular, reasonably hard use. I think these will serve nicely as replacements.

The form factor here is just as nice as the actual function and that's not always the case with high dollar electronics. The materials are very nice and put together flawlessly - the entire unit is really gorgeous. These are actually quite heavy in the hand, yet balanced so perfectly that I don't notice the weight at all wearing them. The ear pieces are attached with magnets to the arch piece of you can remove them for cleaning or swaps in the future. The lambskin is very soft and doesn't cause excess heat build up for my ears.

Pairings with my Sony Xperia phone, my Samsung tablet and a Fire tablet were all easy and painless. I've used these headphones for streaming music via Amazon, Pandora and my own stuff from my cloud files plus Audible books for a couple of weeks now. I'm currently using them on vacation right now with the included travel case - they fold up a bit and the charging cable & 3mm direct connect cable fit in the case as well. Sound quality is excellent as well here for my types of music - primarily classical, country, and 80s pop. I can clearly hear the French horns, flute, or soft cellos in Hans Zimmer compositions or a Beethoven concerto. Aretha Franklin sounds great with these BTW. (I can't speak to thumping bass reproduction because I detest that style and don't listen to it.)

title: Standard Ottorbox protection that's above and beyond
text:
My husband travels constantly with his Samsung tablet and he's dropped it once in a different case with zero damage. However, I've met him and seen the havoc he can wreak on electronics, so the Ottorbox cases are a requirement here.

This one fits correctly and the buttons work. The case adds significant bulk to an otherwise thin tablet, but it's worth it for real protection. The corners are well buffered and bumping it on the car door or a piece of heavy equipment shouldn't damage your tablet at all. He's noticed a little loss of touch screen responsiveness with it on, but not enough to stop using the case.

title: Working great in my Sony Xperia XA2 phone - lots of photos daily
text: I recently got a new phone and it has less internal memory than my old phone (32Gb instead of 64GB). I needed to copy my old smaller SD card data to this one to complete the phone swap and keep going seamlessly. This card took all the data from my old Samsung card and has been working perfectly in my new Sony phone for a month now. It's holding photos, notes, PDF files and app backups without trouble.

title: My unit refuses to connect with WiFi.
text:
Well darn. I was actually excited to get this camera and use it to watch the front door to keep an eye on package deliveries. The unit is sized nicely and easy to handle, but not so big that it screams "camera here!" However, my unit will not connect to the WiFi.

I have tried everything and even took it next door to try their WiFi, thinking maybe something funky was happening with my set up. Nothing. I was able to set it up using a direct Ethernet connection, but that's not useful at all. Being tethered by the cable means I can't use the camera anywhere other than the corner of the living room where the modem/router sits.

title: Working as they should with a new Sony Xperia XA2 Ultra phone
text:
I recently upgraded my cell phone and of course the new phone had a newer USB C connection instead of the micro USB that all my existing cords use. The New phone only came with a single, three foot cord and that's essentially useless. I bought two of these so I can charge my phone by the bed and in the living room if needed and put the original cord on the car charger.

The six feet in length here is very handy. I have one plugged into the USB outlet on a power strip and the other through the regular outlet connection. Both work fine with my Sony Xperia XA2 Ultra phone. There's no heat and the cables fit my phone. It charges quickly enough for my needs - the phone has an enormous battery, so I typically only charge overnight or in the car.

title: Cut the cord now - working with HULU, DirectTV Now, HBO GO and more
text:
This is our second Fire Stick. Our first one is a first generation unit and we have it on the guest room tv now - it still works fine. We cut the cable cord completely six months ago and went totally to streaming. We added this new Fire Stick for the master bedroom and a Roku Express for the living room.

I love being able to link our Fire Sticks to Alexa. We have a Dot in the guest room and the original Echo in the master bedroom controlling both Fire Sticks. This one also works on verbal commands through the remote, but you have to think about what you ask for if you have several streaming services. We have Prime, Netflix, Hulu, HBO Go and DirectTV Now (still saving $165 a month over cable!) and Alexa can find a specific show, but perhaps not on the channel you wanted.

Comparing the Fire Stick and the Roku Express is pretty simple. The layout for the two is completely different and I actually think the Roku is easier to sort through and find stuff. It feels less cluttered actually. I do appreciate the full integration of the Fire Stick with my other devices through our Amazon account - I can pick up a show on Prime with my tablet, phone or tv exactly where I left off. Regardless of which streaming stick we use, we're still incredibly happy we dumped the cable.

title: Basic ear buds that simply work. Comfortable to wear while doing barn chores
text:
Sometimes you just need a super basic pair of ear buds that aren't fancy or expensive. I have a pair of high-end, very pricey Bluetooth over the ear headphones for use in the house. But I don't like wearing them working out at the farm or riding horses.

These are very light and work fine with my LG V10 phone for music and audio books. The buds have three different size ear pieces - my ears are a bit small and the small ones fit comfortably. Using these while shoveling horse stalls was nice and the thin cord just tucked away in my jacket pocket. I much prefer doing chores while listening to a book and these allow me not to worry if I drop them or they get damaged.

title: Easy to set up and sync with Android phones. Leak sensors work
text:
I have the Wi-Fi enabled leak detector not one of the outlet plugs. It's a pretty simple set up. Put in the batteries, download the app, sync to your WiFi and set it where you need it. I'm using an LG V-10 Android phone with this and have had no problems.

I have it behind a toilet which shares a wall with the big hot water heater - if we're going to have a leak, that seems like the most likely location. I tested the sensors with a small amount of water on a level countertop and it worked correctly. The sensors emit a very loud squeaker and my phone beeped an alert as well. I don't think you could hear the alarm if it's out in the garage though. So far I haven't had any problems with it.

title: Protection is a must, no degradation of images and bubble free
text: These fit my little Samsung Tab E tablet exactly right with no gaps or bare corners. If you thoroughly clean the screen and go slowly with the actual application of the screen saver, you should have no bubbles.i haven't noticed any degradation to the responsiveness of the touch screen and video images are clear and crisp.

title: Hefty, very loud volume, beautiful sound quality. Does not link to Echo, Dot or Fire TV
text:
As an avid fan of Alexa, I am delighted to have this Harman Kardon Alexa speaker. I've had my original Echo since the first week they released the initial invitation to buy and have since added a Dot and Alexa controlled thermostats, dining room lights, Fire TV sticks and plugs through out the house. This unit was meant to enhance the music sound quality from Alexa and expand our Alexa listening group and work with the living room television.

The speaker itself is considerably larger than my original Echo - wider and heavier. The lights on this are brighter as well - when playing music at night or listening to a book, you can leave the light on and it works as a night light. You can also turn the light off if you prefer. Setting this up takes a bit longer than my Echo or Dot - it's slower making the initial WiFi connection, but once you link to Amazon via the Alexa App, you're good to go. It connects via Bluetooth to both my LG V10 phone and my Samsung tablets without drama.

This unit is significantly louder at every volume setting than the original Echo and makes the Dot sound like she's whispering. I have this in our formal living room where we have 30 feet tall ceilings, grass cloth covered walls and an enormous open space - the room was designed for correct accoustics with my Grandmother's grand piano and music simply sounds beautiful in here. The Harman Kardon Alexa sits on a table where the piano used to be and the sound at volume 4 simply envelopes you no matter where you are in the room. Set the volume to 6 and I can hear my book or music two rooms away almost as if it's floating through the halls. The sound quality is excellent and playing Beethoven or opera or country music renders each instrument precisely from tiny flutes to cellos and twangy fiddles. I'm immensely pleased at the improvement from the Echo to this for just music.

The reason for the one star deduction is because I thought/expected the Harman Kardon to by fully, 100% integrated with Alexa. It is not. This unit cannot be linked to the Fire TV sticks, meaning that I cannot use it to verbally control the living room television. It cannot be linked to my Echo and Dot units. That means we can't include the Harman Kardon speaker in our multi room group so the same song/book can be heard throughout the house. We cannot do the Drop In skill where Alexa acts as an intercom system for multiple rooms. There are a couple of other skills this speaker isn't able to perform simply because it doesn't speak to the Amazon Alexa products. If they can correct this glaring deficiency, then this would be a five star product and one i would consider buying for the guest suite and master bedroom. As a stand alone Alexa unit, this is a top notch choice, but if you want to link to your existing Echo, you can't do so.

title: Very masculine design. Well made with thick padding for your laptop
text:
I was excited about this being convertible from a backpack to a tote style bag. However, the conversion is just pulling two handles out of pockets and not using the backpack straps. It still looks like a backpack which isn't quite what I had hoped for.

The bag itself is very well made and the stitching is solid throughout and the padding is thick. There's tons of storage pockets and areas stashed all around the bag so you can carry whatever you need - pens, keys, a drink, books etc. My 15" Toshiba laptop does fit inside and I can zip it closed, but...... It's an extremely tight fit and nothing else will go inside with the computer. However, as a quick grab bag for other stuff, this is quite useful. I fit three ten inch tablets, a small camera, a charger, a notebook and pens in it with room to spare. It's just too ugly for me to carry regularly, but my husband doesn't care and he's laid claim to it.

title: Loses connection within twenty feet indoors. Most helpful for things you lose in the house
text:
I have the grey TrackR Pixel and I am using it on our spare garage door opener. It's the opener we give to houseguests to use while they are here and on more than one occasion, it's gotten misplaced. Hopefully, this TrackR will cut down on aggravation of hunting down the opener n the future.

Once you load the TrackR app on your phone, it gives you pairing instructions via Bluetooth and you're ready to go. You have to allow the location permission in the app for this to work. There's a large button to press for location of the TrackR and you can make some small customization of the alert sound.

Actual use is a bit limited. My TrackR can't be found or alerted once I get more than roughly, twenty feet away from it. If you know your misplaced item is in a specific area this might not be a problem. However, if you have it on a key and dropped it without realizing it, you may be in trouble. The crowd source search option might work well in a large city, but in our small town, there aren't going to be many folks using these gadgets....much less within twenty feet of a dropped garage door opener out in the wild. For my needs this will work fine though.

title: Standard installation. Tablet is clear and still responsive
text: I'm loving my Primetime tablet and use it constantly. I take it everywhere and have a nice leather case for it. A screen protector is a must. This one is easy enough to install and comes with the screen cleaner wipe and a soft cloth for the screen as well. Once installed, the screen is just as responsive and perfectly clear even when watching streaming TV.

title: Fits both the big Fire and AT&T Primetime tablets. Not as useful as a folio style case
text:
I have a 10" AT&T Primetime tablet (this thing is actually a great tablet BTW). I usually keep a traditional folio style case on my tablets with the front cover to protect the screen. Those cases can get bulky and add weight, but the protection offered is worth it.

This skeleton holder does fit my tablet and none of the buttons, the charger slot or camera are blocked. The skeleton expands at the corners and tension keeps it in place. There's a pull out kickstand built in and a stylus holder. The center of the back has an elastic finger hold to grip. The corner pieces are slightly raised and should offer a bit of protection to the screen if you drop it. The back though isn't flat or smooth and can get uncomfortable too hold after a few minutes.

However, I just don't feel like this contraption is sufficient for my lifestyle. My tablets go everywhere with me and I use them in a variety of places.....the car, the horse barn, outside on the patio, and they travel in my hand bag, luggage and saddle bags. I need real protection and a flat back on the cases. For me, this skeleton thing just doesn't work as well as a regular folio case.

title: Big Echo is better for music. Controlling a TV, reading audio books etc is where the Dot shines
text:
I have had my main Echo since the first days after the initial invitation to buy was sent out. I absolutely love Alexa and use her for tons of things daily. - she lives in the hallway between the living room and kitchen where we spend the most time. I added the Dot a month ago to bring the Alexa functions into our master bedroom.

The Dot is as easy to use as the big Echo and now that the two can be connected, we have music throughout the house at the same time. I also like the intercom skill so we can talk to each other across the house quickly. My one dislike is the tinny sounding small speaker n the Dot. I've grown so accustomed to the balanced, clean sound from the big Echo that the Dot sound quality was a let down with music. However, reading me the news, ordering Starbucks, reading my audio books, working as an alarm clock or intercom is smooth and works just fine. I especially like being able to control our tv with Alexa voice commands - we cut the cable cord and stream via Prime, Netflix and Hulu Live and Alexa has made searching for a specific show much more simple.

title: Easy to install, much prettier picture than with cable. Cutting the cord is totally worth it
text:
After three price increases in two years from Suddenlink, we said Enough and cut the cord to streaming only. We had two Fire Sticks already, but needed something for the living room television. I picked up the Roku Express plus at a local store and in less than five minutes had it connected and working. So very easy.

I'm amazed at how much we've been missing by being tethered to cable! There's just a plethora of free tv and movies out there. The Roku essentially just gathers a ton of the options and puts them in one spot for you. You do have to activate most the big time channels through a paid service like DirectTV Now - TBS, NBC, Bravo, AMC, A&E etc. All require an activation and verification to watch vua the apps.

The remote is small, but feels sturdy and is simple to use. No getting lost in a jillion random buttons. My only complaint is the need for a second remote control for volume. We use sound bars for the 55 and 65" TV's and the Roku remote isn't set up for volume. Not a deal breaker by any means, just make sure you have another way to control volume. We're using the DirectTV Now cheapest option and the HULU LIVE beta for the first two months and then we'll keep the one that has been used most and drop the other. One thing I noticed immediately is with Roku (and the Fire Sticks) the 1080p picture on our big Samsung is much cleaner and prettier than when we had the cable service - we've used only the HDMI connection for years. I'm extremely pleased that we finally made the leap to streaming.

title: Small, easy to install. Re-established the wifi connection on a laptop
text:
My husband has a three year old laptop that was having difficulty holding it's wifi connection at inopportune times. The rest of the machine works fine and replacing the entire computer for this tiny issue didn't make sense.

This wifi adapter seems to have fixed the issue. I don't proclaim to understand this witchcraft, I just know that with five minutes of installation effort the laptop is staying connected. I loaded the included CD with the drivers, followed the set up instructions on the screen and entered out wifi password. Done. The physical unit slips into the USB outlet and is almost flush with the side of the computer. It's tiny and unobtrusive. Hopefully we won't have to think about the wifi connection problem again in the near future.

title: Sound is good, adjustable fit, but can be tricky to connect via Bluetooth
text:
I rarely use ear bud type earphones because they always hurt my ears. I prefer traditional over the ear, cushioned earphones as a rule. However, there are times when the extra bulk is a problem - like on horseback.

These have a couple of different size ear pieces and I have been able to get the fit adjusted enough to wear them comfortably for a couple of hours straight. The sound is good with classical music and country. I don't do the whole extra bass type of thing, so I cannot comment on that aspect. I can clearly hear the French horns, clarinets and background piano in several different pieces of music.

My issue here is that these don't connect by Bluetooth easily to every device. It took multiple tries to connect to my LG V10 phone, they never connected with my husband's Sony Xperia phone or my Android tablet, but they did connect to my Samsung tablet after two tries. These devices are all current and have updated software.

title: Pretty plum color, fits correctly and the sleep/wake function works smoothly
text:
I bought the Primetime tablet two weeks ago and I absolutely love it. It's far better than expected considering that it's an ATT branded tablet and I have found myself using it before picking up my other Samsung tablet or my three year old 10" Fire. So I needed a case for it immediately.

This one was the only one available right now that was affordable, but it's a good case. The sleep\wake function works perfectly and all the cut outs and charging port are located correctly. The tablet fits just as it should. Mine is the purple cover and it's a deep plum color that's not too bright. Definitely a good buy.

title: Pretty display, very responsive screen, works as a hotspot
text:
I have a first gen 8" Fire Tablet and a fourth gen 10" Fire that have both served me well for years and still work fine. Buuuutttt.... I wanted something I could travel with that wasn't reliant only on WiFi and I needed access to some specific, Google only apps.

I actually discovered this Tab E at the AT&T store and really liked it. It was also free since we were extending our contract anyway and I brought it home a month ago. It immediately updated to Android 6 and my Google account stuff populated within minutes - contacts, address book, etc. It's pretty snappy and the screen is very responsive. I was able to find a very inexpensive, but cute and functional case here on Amazon. Using this as a WiFi hotspot for other devices has been very smooth and it connects with Alexa as a speaker and Sony Bluetooth headphones are working great with this tablet.

My only complaints are the sheer amount of Samsung and AT&T bloatware that eats up the 16 gig internal memory. I've added an sd card of course. Additionally, I've found that I really miss the 10" screen from old Fire. I'm not happy with the tiny size of this tablet compared to what I had before. My final resolution was to order the new 10" Primetime tablet for less than thirty bucks from AT&T this week since I must have the LTE cellular connection as well as WiFi. This Samsung will become my husband's travel tablet since he actually prefers the 8 inch screen.

title: Fits perfectly. Purple is pretty and easy to spot
text:
I recently got a Samsung E tablet because I need the cellular data accessibility that my much loved Fire tablet doesn't offer. Of course I needed a good case so I can carry the Samsung with me as needed.

This one fits exactly as it should. The cut outs for the power buttons and charging slot are right. The camera is not covered or blocked at all. The case includes a stylus that works fine and can be stored on the side of the case. My issue is the closure flap gets in the way if you use the case as a horizontal stand to watch video etc. The flap doesn't lie flat or tuck under smoothly. But that's a small quibble and the case looks nice in purple and does it's job.

title: Works with Suddenlink perfectly. Increased signal stability and speeds
text:
We have Suddenlink cable, internet, and land line phone service and had been happy with our three year old router and their modem. Until we moved to a new house. The arris modem was dropping signal significantly every single day - we either had super slow or no connection for hours. I had the cable guys out here four times in 61 days to fix the problem. I was literally ready to just cancel Suddenlink and move to AT&T for internet, but decided to try this Nighthawk combo first.

It was spotted instantly by Suddenlink when I called to give them the new modem Mac address, so the connection was just a single phone call to start. No drama. I have 9 daily devices on WiFi and three TiVo receivers that connect via Ethernet or WiFi plus the land line phone. There's four Ethernet connections and two phone connections on the modem, plenty for our needs.

It's been almost three weeks and I've noticed an astonishing improvement in our initial connection and reliability. Rather than daily outages, we have had five total in three weeks and none lasted more than 15 to 20 minutes. Stability of the signal has improved and our speeds are double what they were with the arris modem - we're actually getting the high speed service we pay for. The router is also projecting the WiFi far enough that I no longer need to use a secondary extender to get WiFi by the pool and patio.

I like the Genie app with this. The ability to check channels, reboot the router if needed, and see which devices are online is very handy. I also like the clear, bright lights on the front. At a glance you know if there's a problem. Bottom line for me is that I haven't canceled our services from Suddenlink because this unit fixed 90% of our problem.

title: Charges my tablet, my phone and headphones  correctly
text:
I ha a pair of Bluetooth headphones that I love for audio books around the house, but now and then the battery will die just at a climatic point in my book. I have to stop and recharge them and switch to the Echo which means anyone else has to hear my book as well or... be tethered to the short cord and plug the in.

The ten foot length here makes being tethered a little more bearable. I can listen and fold laundry or paint my nails etc That's just not as easy with the typical 4 or 6 foot cords. This cable works very well at charging my Sony headphones, a regular phone and a tablet. Definitely handy to have an extra Micro USB cable in a super long length hanging around.

title: Slow as molasses, but works as emergency back up
text:
We were having drama with the Wi-Fi connection the first couple of weeks after moving into the new house. We got a new modem, all new Ethernet cables, and finally picked up this router thinking the problem was our original route. Turns out, the issue was a splitter on the cable company's end - whew.

This router is a good size and easy to use in almost any location. It sort of looks like the squatty third cousin to our Alexa. When we did have this unit connected it worked, but really struggled. Our usual router is a 2 channel set up and is just blazing fast. I knew this one wasn't on the same level before I bought it, but it is still considerably slower than expected. We have a thermostat, Alexa, two or three tablets, two smart phones, two TiVo minis and the laptops drawing from the WiFi at various times - a lot of stuff for this router to cope with. I've since gone back to our original router fortunately, but I am keeping this one as an emergency back up.

title: 25 feet provides lots of options for component location.
text:
I have the 25 foot cable because I wanted to relocate the TiVo box. Both the box and the tv were sharing a single shelf and the TiVo remote control sensor was a bit blocked

The extra length here gives me several options with regard to placement of the box. So far the connection is crisp and clear with no interference or stuttering with fast action shows.

title: Easy to connect and relocate. Allows us to have full Wi-Fi at the pool and backyard
text:
We have a good dual band router that is really great in the house, but Wi-Fi out on the patios or by the pool is sketchy at best. I've had this extender installed for about two weeks now and it's definitely improved things.

It took several tries to find the right location to push the Wi-Fi signal where I wanted it outside, but once that was figured out, we were set. Relocating this unit is pretty simple - once it's tied into your router, just plug it in and watch the lights until you see all green. I repeated this process four times before I had the exact spot I wanted. It never failed to connect after being unplugged and moved.

It actually throws the signal significantly farther than expected. I can use my tablet sitting on the bridge over the creek, about 250 feet from the extender's location in the house - in a straight line. I'm pretty pleased with the performance so far for my simple needs. It's really close to the speeds our direct router puts out, so we're not seeing any noticeable signal degradation on tablets, cell phones or a laptop outside.

title: Installed with no air bubbles on first try. Fits perfectly
text: I finally had to replace my last glass screen protector after a year of hard use. This one fits perfectly with no gaps or uncovered spots - the front camera lens and speaker cut outs are precise. I am really pleased with how easy this installed, I got this on my phone with zero air bubbles on the first try. The glass doesn't effect my touchscreen or the clarity of the screen at all.

title: A year of use and I'm still happy. Solid WiFi reception, strong battery, great for email
text:
I purchased my Fire 10" almost a year ago after having used my Fire 8" for 18 months previously. This tablet is surprisingly light considering the large size and it is thinner than my Fire Fire tablet.

I am really happy with the larger screen. Watching a movie or even just shopping and surfing websites is a nice experience. Better than lugging my laptop from room to room. My only real complaint is that the screen definition on my old Fire Hd was significantly better than this one.

I can use my tablet outside on the back deck because the WiFi reception on this tablet is stronger than my older Fire. I have also been really pleased with the battery life. I use this tablet daily throughout the day for email, surfing, games, record keeping for various projects, review writing, and of course, videos from time to time. I charge it over night and it rarely drops below 30%. I do have a memory card and back up my photos from both tablet and cell phone to the cloud with no problems. Bottom line is this is a nice tablet for basic use and it also travels well.

title: Only works with the remote! Nice, full, rich sound with 55" Vizio tv in very large room
text:
I bought my Bose Solo 15 at another online retailer during a one day sale for a price that made it irresistible and after a month, I am happy that I did it. We have two 55" televisions and the one in our master bedroom has the Denon sound base under it and that unit has simply been outstanding. I was actually looking to just buy a second Denon for the living room tv and chose this Bose unit due to the one time sale and the Bose reputation.

This unit sits directly under our 55" Vizio smart tv and connects with the digital audio optical cable - just like the Denon base. I turned off the tv's physical speakers and let the Bose take over. The sound is full and significantly improved over the thin tv speakers. The unit shines when watching movies that have lots of rich soundtrack music and when you use the Dialogue button to soften background sounds and highlight conversation type dialogue.

The Bluetooth connected with my LG V10 phone and my fourth generation Fiire tablet immediately, allowing me to play music and my audio book through the Bose. Very nice extra functionality - the Denon does this as well. The Bose includes a universal remote control that requires some effort to set up correctly and completely. However! Once the cursing and hair pulling was over, I got it done. The Bose remote now operates our television, the Bose base, and our TiVo/cable box exactly as the cable remote does.

My one star deduction is because the only way to use the Bose Solo is with their included remote control. There are no physical buttons on the machine and that strikes me as a real design flaw. If you break or lose this proprietary remote you cannot even turn the Bose on or off, much less actually use it for sound. At least the Denon sound base can be operated manually or trained to respond to other remote controls with three steps. For me this Bose Solo is worth the price I paid (under three hundred bucks) and it is equal to the Denon in sound quality. But for overall value and ease of use, the Denon is the five star product.

title: Never miss a soft flute or clarinet again! Comfortable, no cauliflower ear. Not noise canceling, great music
text:
Honestly, I have wanted a pair of good Sennheiser headphones for years, but I couldn't justify it to myself - I mean we have a Denon sound base that connects via Bluetooth and Alexa for music, so a personal pair of headphones seems like a selfish indulgence. OMG. Do it. Be selfish. I have been wearing these things for days now every chance that I get and falling in love with music all over again.

First thing, I must correct a misstatement in an earlier review - the HD 579 are NOT noise cancellation headphones. They do not have that technology and are not intended to, not marketed as such and I double checked with Sennheiser directly to be sure. It might be easy to mistake the beautiful sound quality and encapsulation of the sound for noise cancellation at first - simply because the headphones fit very well and at an upper volume, external noise doesn't readily intrude.

The fit is far more comfortable than I remember headphones being. The band is nicely padded and adjustable and the ear cups are very soft, thick and they fully cover your ear without any pinching. I have worn these for thirty minutes and up to three hours consecutively in vary increments, every day for five days now and never had cauliflower ear. Nor do my ears get hot.
