I'm using these with my Fire Tablet, my LG V10 phone and Sceptre 55" television playing music through our cable provider's music stations. The connection plug is tight and the cord has proven to be long enough for use in bed at night while reading, on the sofa reading & it rolls up to put in my pocket while wandering around cleaning house and doing barn chores.

As to the quality of the music.... simply outstanding. Far better than I really expected. One of my favorite soundtracks is from the movie Hannibal by Hans Zimmer. It has a mix of pure classical and opera. The HD 579 phones let me hear the French horns and the soft build of the clarinets as crisp and clearly as the big cellos and trumpets in other, louder movements. Simple acoustic vocal pieces from James Taylor, Tracy Chapman and Paul Simon are beautifully rendered and you can appreciate the realism of a live performance. These headphones are very nice and I wish I had bought something like them long ago, but now that I have these, I won't be far from them and I definitely will be grabbing them every time I want music, which is daily.

title: Great 25 foot length option, easy to grab ends. No signal degradation
text:
You can never have enough good coaxial cable around the house. Between multiple televisions, cable boxes, DVD players, streaming boxes, surround sound set ups etc something always needs to be connected.

I was trying to rearrange the guest room and pulled too hard on the cable from the wall causing a short or something where it connects to to cable box. The replacement offered locally was only 12 foot long....not helpful. This one is 25' long and I was able to get a friend to help me swap the bad one out in the wall with the new one without a call to the cable company. I'm very pleased with the quality of the Amazon Basics line - it works perfectly with no degradation of signal and was easy to twist into the box.

title: First one lasted three full years and I am buying a second one just like it
text: I bought this mouse the first time in 2013 and I am just now having to replace it - October of 2016. That's pretty darn good for a very inexpensive little wireless mouse. We use it primarily with a Chrome Book laptop and sometimes with a Windows 8 machine and it just works. There's nothing fancy going on here, it points, scrolls and clicks....just like it should with no drama.

title: No more slow charger message with my tablet! Extra length is very convenient
text: I'm a fan of the Amazon Basics line of chargers and cables in general. These are well made and the ten foot length is very handy. I am using this one with the wall plug that came with my Fire tablet. The extra length means that I can use the outlet under the bed that was previously out of reach. My tablet charges at the same speed as always and if I need to use it while it's charging, I don't get that "slow charger" message that shows up with some of the generic cords.

title: Sleep/wake function works, fits perfectly and the blue is very elegant
text:
I bought this case during the Prime Day sales when I upgraded my 3 year old Fire Tablet to the 10" version. The blue is really pretty and stands out (in a classy manner) when everyone else is carrying a plain old black or grey cased tablet around.

My Fire fits exactly right and is completely secure inside. None of the case edges interfere with the screen in anyway and the rear camera is clear as well. The inside of the front flap has three leather stops to use as viewing holds for the tablet which work well. Additionally, the front folds back completely flat to allow you to read, play a game or type comfortably. I've had no trouble with the sleep/wake function with the case either - close the cover and the Fire sleeps, open it and the Fire starts immediately. I'm really pleased.

title: Fits the 10" Fire tablet and works well
text: I got the 32gb card for use in my new 10" Fire Tablet. It fits the tablet correctly and was recognized immediately. I have been using strictly for photo and music storage and retrieval - everything is there and transferring back and forth properly.

title: 3 foot cord limits locations for use. Red & green lights show power & protection are functional
text: Huh....who knew Stanley was branching out from power tools and into power strips? I guess it makes sense though. I've been replacing a couple of my ancient surge protectors recently and this one has been designated for the laptop chargers. There are six outlets and I can fit three of those large, unwieldy plugs into this power strip comfortably. None of them are pressed against the others. It has a 3 foot cord, so it's just long enough to reach the top of the table we use, but the short cord means that this unit doesn't work for our televisions or printer setup. I do like that there are two lights on this - a red one showing it is powered and a green one that shows everything is protected.

title: This will do, but not as good as iCarez brand. Has bubbles after 2 tries & 2 days.
text:
I've had better tempered glass screen protectors from iCarez for my Fire tablets and my various cell phones. Unfortunately, iCarez doesn't have one available for the Fire 10" tablet right now. I chose this one simply because it looked like the same type and quality that I've been accustomed to in the past That's not quite the case.

This Omoton screen protector is harder to install and get on correctly. It catches and bubbles whereas the iCarez glass protectors on both my 8.9" Fire tablets and my Lg V10 phone went on in the first try without a single bubble or dust particle. But the Omoton took two tries and there is still a bubble on both ends of my tablet after 2 full days and nights. It's a small irritant, but one that shouldn't be there at all. I'm going to look for another brand that's closer to the iCarez quality and try again.

title: Compared to two other brands of cables, this is incredibly slow with two new cell phones in the car.
text:
Slower than the 5 year old name brand cables from my ancient Blackberry and slower than the Amazon basics cables from last year. This cable works and it does charge my cell phone in the car, but when used with the same car charger as the other two cables mentioned above, my phone charges much more slowly. I noticed the same problem when using this cable plugged directly into the USB outlet in my truck vs using the other two cables. I am charging a two month old LG V10 phone in the truck normally. This morning I switched things up and tried with a brand new (2 days) Sony Xperia X phone - exact same issue - very slow charging.

My LG typically gains a 10% bump in the truck in the time it takes me to drive from Starbucks to the horse barn every morning - this is while it plays my audio book via blue tooth at the same time. Yesterday with this StarTech cable my LG gained went from 83% on the battery to 86% under the exact same conditions. Bottom line for me is that this cable does work, but at a glacially slow pace and at best it's an emergency back up and nothing more.

title: Beautiful picture, tiny eye for the remote control to aim at, works with Denon sound bar & wifi
text:
I bought this television (I double checked the exact model number to be positive that t I am reviewing the correct one) used at an estate sale in January and it's been used daily in our master bedroom every since. The color and clarity of the picture is simply wonderful. In comparison to our brand new Sceptre 55" 1080p tv in the living room and the 3 year old Samsung in the guest room, this Vizio has the prettiest picture and best refresh rate. The Samsung has the best native sound though without a sound bar enhancement.

This Vizio is our only Smart Television and I have a Firestick on the living room tv. As of today, June 16, 2016, the Amazon app and others are all working just fine through the television's remote control with the direct access buttons. Connecting this tv to our wifi network did take several attempts and I had to update the firmware twice before it would connect and hold the connection for more than 48 hours. (To be honest, I have no idea if the former owner every actually used the internet connection so it may not have been updated before I got it) Since January, I have had no trouble with the connection or streaming. We do have a super fast internet service and a dual band router with this tv as the only thing typically streaming on one band.

My one star deduction is the tiny receiver area for the remote control. If you are using the actual remote rather than a universal one for the cable box, you have to aim directly at the very tiny eye in the far left bottom corner and it can take a couple of tries to hit it just right from across a big room. This drives me nuts when I'm streaming from Amazon Prime and need to pause the show quickly or try to flick through the selections. However, I would totally buy another Vizio tv again in the future if the new ones are as good as this two year old used one has been - I've definitely gotten my hundred fifty dollars worth out of this one.

title: Works as it should - great for multiple lamps and cleaning up multiple cord drama
text: I am using this surge protector for lamps in our living room and have this plugged in to the single outlet in the floor under the sofa. I have used three of the male to female 1 foot long AC extension cords with this surge protector to keep each of the lamp cords separated and flat. There's still space to plug in a phone charger and slip it on a side table. I'm pleased - the six foot cable allows me to keep everything hidden under the sofa with no stray cords to step on and my wall outlets are free for other things.

title: The regular plugs work great - the USB plugs work, but are slow
text: I picked this up locally after my 5 year old one started shutting off randomly. This one is in our master bedroom with the laptop, two tablet chargers and a cell phone on it a various times. It works fine and I really like the option of closing the plugs that aren't in use - keeps the dust or dog hair from getting in them. The USB outlets are a nice idea and they do work, but they are really slow for charging my Fire Tablet and my LG V10 phone.

title: Excellent battery life, very fast boot up, almost no bloatware. Good basic laptop
text:
In comparison to my Toshiba Satellite 15" with similar specs, this ASUS is about equal - there are definitely some things I like better about the ASUS for everyday use and a couple of small quibbles that bother me. First off the computer itself is about the same weight as my Toshiba so carrying it around is exactly the same and it fits in my existing laptop sleeves and bags. It does have a DVD tray so you can play movies & music and burn discs as needed (as does my Toshiba), but a lot of laptops don't offer this anymore, so this is a definite plus.

I do really like that the ASUS comes a lot cleaner out of the box than my Toshiba - almost no bloatware pre-installed. The basic Windows 10 and you can don't have to spend 30 minutes messing around with a bunch of garbage you don't want and won't use anyway. Additionally, the ASUS boots up about 20 seconds faster from off than my Toshiba and again from the sign in screen, the ASUS is still faster. The screen is very pretty and clear with a variety of images and video - keep in mind that it's NOT a touchscreen. I've been averaging about 6 hours of use with the battery before it hits the 30% mark - that is net surfing, watching some random videos, and mostly word processing. Leaving it on in sleep mode with no use - it went almost 4 full days before needing a charge. The wifi connects immediately and I've had zero issues with it dropping out either inside or out on the back deck.

I really like the keyboard and the overall shape of the frame on this particular laptop. My Toshiba has the keyboard just open and exposed and what happens is that the heels of my hands tend to slip upwards as I type or bump the space bar. Or my thumbs slide into the mousepad area and now my cursor has bounced someplace new & I'm typing in the wrong spot. The ASUS keyboard is slightly lowered and has a border around it - for me anyway, this design is MUCH easier to type with. (See the photo.) The shape of the overall frame is better on the ASUS than the Toshiba as well. The rounded corners and edges on the ASUS don't poke into your wrists after an hour of writing or research.

My quibbles seem small on the surface, but after almost three weeks of use, they are aggravating me. First - the ASUS doesn't keep time as well as the Toshiba. It's off by 2 full minutes. (See the photos) I've checked both a couple of times and set them manually at the same moment and within 24 hours, the ASUS has lost 2 minutes - it never loses more than that though. Second - The charger is smaller than every other one I have for the other two laptops and the Chromebook in this house. The other three are standard size, but the one on the ASUS is a tiny bit smaller and thus you can't use another charger for this laptop in an emergency. Third - the speakers on the ASUS don't sound quite as full as the ones on my Toshiba. Of course... no built in speakers on a laptop are really meant for full music enjoyment.

My bottom line is that at this price point, this is a nice machine and will do almost anything you can want with regard to basic internet surfing, movie watching, office work and the like. This is not a gamer's computer and it's not meant to be. But as a regular, go to every day laptop, it's a pretty good one. I want to give it 4 1/2 stars.

title: Very nice picture quality, easy to set up, poor sound quality requires a sound bar.
text:
I bought this television new from wally world on one day sale for under three hundred bucks and it has turned into an excellent purchase that I would have been happy with had I paid full price for it. We have the 50" unit and it was extremely easy to unpack, attach the included swivel stand, and place it on our entertainment center by myself. The entire tv weighs around 20lbs maybe - it's light enough for me to pick it up without strain. There are three HDMI outlets, a single USB outlet, the usual RCA plug-ins, the cable connection, and a digital audio connection for use with a sound bar.

The picture is clear and sharp and easy to adjust for our personal tastes with regard to color temperature, contrast, and brightest etc. There is no stuttering or shadowing watching sports or other fast moving live action. We have it connected to our cable box and a DVD player through the HDMI cables and the Amazon Fire Stick on the USB - all work correctly and are easy to swap between.

My one complaint is the native speakers are tinny and thin sounding, but that seems to simply be a fact of life with large flat screen televisions. I bought the Denon DHT-T110 TV Speaker Base with Bluetooth aptX Streaming and Dolby Digital Decoding to enhance the sound. The digital audio connection was a snap to connect and the box comes on as soon as the tv powers on. The two pieces operate as one and our living room has become the center of our evenings again....movies are a pleasure to watch and listen to. 45 days with this Sceptre tv and I am very pleased so far - it's every bit as good as our smaller Samsung for far less money.

title: Works perfectly, takes two AAA batteries, quick access buttons are correct & connect to Amazon & Netflix
text: I bought a Vizio smart tv at an estate auction last weekend for next to nothing and it works perfectly, but didn't come with the original remote control. The codes provided by the cable company allow the cable box remote to power on/off and control the volume, but nothing else. The only way to make use of the smart functionality or adjust the picture quality is with an actual Vizio remote. I ordered this one and it works perfectly (our tv model is the E500i.A0) The remote takes two AAA batteries and the quick buttons for Amazon, Netflix etc all work as long as your TV is connected to the internet.

title: Proven reliability for photos and daily data needs
text: My husband has finally decided to join me in 2016 and abandoned his 2006 Samsung flip phone. He converted to an international, dual SIM card BLU phone as his full time cell phone and that meant a memory card for photos and music and all the good stuff the rest of us have been doing/storing on our smart phones for the past ten years. I have a 4 year old Samsung card in my old Note phone and moved it to my camera recently and it is still working perfectly. Buying a second one for my husband's use was an automatic choice.... this is a brand that has been proven reliable over and over. This card is the micro size and does come with an adapter.

title: Incredibly easy to install. Impressive sound improvement for a big tv in a big room
text:
I bought this at another website thanks to a Christmas gift card, but I researched the different types of sound bars and enhancement systems on Amazon & various places first. I wanted a very simple to use, unobtrusive setup, a digital connection and something that could work with our very open and large room without requiring setting up ugly components everywhere and still sound clean. This Denon base ticks every box for me.

I literally had this unit out of the box, installed under our 50" television, connected and working in less than 20 minutes - that includes reading the directions and unpacking. The box looked huge at first just sitting there alone, but once the tv was on top of it, it sort of vanished. Another 5 minutes and I had the Denon machine trained to respond to the volume buttons on my cable remote control. Mine came with a remote control, the digital optical cable and the red & white style connection. It connected to my phone and tablet via Bluetooth on the first try and played music through both using the Amazon Prime streaming and music saved to my devices - the sound is excellent by the way.

The included remote is handy for switching between daytime and night modes - the overall sound is lower in night mode. And you can choose between the surround sound mode or regular with the remote as well. One thing I have noticed, is that it can take three to five seconds for those changes to register and to hear them. The box turns on automatically when it senses a signal - no need to fiddle with it. Just turn the tv on & go about your business like always. The most impressive thing here is the improvement in the quality of the sound - every single bit is better! The guy reporting the news, music channels, background sound effects in movies, conversations in dramas... it's all crisp and clear and full. I am really pleased.

title: Nearly invisible on some projects due to narrow width
text: These are more narrow in person than I realized from the description - that's ok. The four inch length is excellent for small indoor projects and the narrow width has actually turned out to be useful as well. I have several of these reinforcing a couple of decorative pieces on an enormous outdoor holiday wreath. You can't even see the zip ties. I also used a couple to repair the broken Velcro strap on a horse show championship neck drape so it can be displayed. No sewing required. Again - these ties are small enough to be nearly invisible.

title: Takes nice family & weekend getaway photos. Easy to use & lightweight.
text: I picked up this camera as an inexpensive travel camera. Sometimes you want something better than your cell phone and there are times when you just want a camera that is nothing else - just a camera. This one from does exactly what it should - takes pretty pictures in a simple manner. You can easily see them on the screen and delete them immediately and just move on. The 16MP allows for nice portraits and details of those tourist sites on the road. I installed a standard 16 gig SD card in this and have had no problems with it at all - another benefit to not using my phone, no tying up the memory there. The camera comes with a cord & software for downloading your photos to your computer. All things considered, this is a nice little quick use camera to keep in the car or your tote bag on a weekend jaunt.

title: Handy for a variety of things around the house - reusable & size is adjustable
text: These are more useful than I expected. At eight inches long, there is plenty of space to tie up thick cords or bundles without trouble. I'm using a couple of them with some of those great big outdoor extension cords to help keep them coiled and in place while stored on a garage shelf. Additionally, because I have one silly dog that is forever getting the tip of his tail caught in the strings on the blinds, I have used these to trap and tie up those strings out of tail reach. The fabric sort of acts like Velcro and is reusable again & again - this also makes the tie re-sizable to some degree.

title: Easy to use, exactly what I needed for a simple camera
text: I bought this for use with a simple point and shoot Kodak digital camera. It works just as it should and I haven't lost any of the photos - they are all there and transfer correctly to the computer when needed.

title: Exactly what I needed for music while riding horses - great for use in the arena,loud & clear
text:
I listen to music when I'm riding in the arena and I do some freestyle dressage to music which means my horses need to hear the music as well. I'm always hunting for a Bluetooth speaker that can be used inside and outside without breaking because of a little dust or sprinkle of water and that I can hear from 60 meters away. The actual quality of the music has sort of been pushed to the bottom of my wish list. This speaker has been a pleasure.

It has a carbiner snap and a loop on top so you can hang it up or hook it on a wall, but it's balanced perfectly and sits on a flat surface normally as well. For my purposes, suspended from a hook in the air is perfect. The speaker swings just a bit and the sound is projected outward rather than just up. Leaving my phone near it on a preset play list works very well when I ride - the speaker doesn't skip or stutter. When an email or text message comes in to my phone, the speaker just makes a pleasant boop noise and continues the song. No loud beep like some others.

The volume is sufficient for my outdoor needs while on horseback - I've used it with classical music, some country, some folk music and some 80s pop. I can't speak to the bass or thumping noise for hip hop or even heavy metal because that's not my listening preference. But the crispness of a violin, the breathiness of a fast flute and the deep resonance of a solo cello are well rendered and have no fuzziness or distortion. I have used this four times for an hour each time without recharging between uses, but I don't mess with it - I don't pause, skip etc. In all, this the best outdoor Bluetooth speaker I've used and indoors,it's pretty good too.

title: Works to call home from almost anywhere in the world. The companion app is equally excellent.
text:
My husband has been using a Magic Jack for three years when he's overseas working - we got it directly from their website and renew our service annually. He got a local number for our hometown and we were able to eliminate almost all of the international call expenses. He uses it with a cheap telephone we got on Amazon for less than ten dollars and his Chrome Book. The Magic Jack has worked just fine over the years making & receiving calls to the U.S. in Europe, Mexico, Afghanistan, Dubai, Canada, Thailand, and Britain. We had trouble with it in Cambodia, but the internet connections in our various hotels were weak. The key is the strength of your internet connection.

We just installed the companion app on an unlocked Blu phone and it worked like a charm using the free WiFi at Schipol Airport in Amsterdam this morning. The call home was clear with a tiny lag, but it was free! Magic indeed.

title: Very well made, room for the laptop and a tablet and the accessories
text: Having recently upgraded to a new laptop, I needed a better bag to carry it in and this one definitely solves that problem. My 15.6 Toshiba satellite fits perfectly in the center and the padded sides make me feel comfortable about transporting it safely. There are pockets inside for the charger and other assorted accoutrements we always have. I can also fit my Fire HDX 8.9" tablet  (in a case) in the bag with my laptop easily. The side pockets on the outside are handy for pens,  cards, and random miscellaneous small stuff - cough drops. I do like the thick padding on the handles and shoulder strap - all are well stitched and ought to withstand daily use for a long time. This seems like overkill, but I love that this case is compact and can fit inside my regular carry on luggage - extra protection and organization.

title: Steps lively for multi-tasking, responsive touchscreen, DVD RW drive, awesome battery ** APRIL 2016 UPDATE ***
text:
I've been using a 2009 17.9" Gateway Windows 7 laptop happily all these years until just recently when it began to cough and sputter and generally show signs of wanting to die. I nursed it for several months while shopping for a replacement and suddenly this Toshiba L55T-C/5388 appeared from Vine. Serendipity. I am writing my review from the Toshiba actually rather than my tablet which what I've had to resort to for the past few months - that's a nice change actually. My initial impressions after a week of daily use are pretty good overall with some niggling design complaints for the physical hardware.First - for the record ... I'm not a gamer - just a regular person using my laptop to write articles for the local newspaper now and then, do a lot of email, a lot of online shopping, some social media stuff, watch some videos now and then, sort and store serious quantities of photos and average net surfing. If I want to listen to music, I tend to use Alexa (the Echo) for that rather than my computer and we watch movies on the big television around here - though sometimes I'll use my laptop instead of my tablet for tv shows etc when I'm traveling.

This Toshiba has a very nice high definition screen and I haven't noticed any fuzziness or blurred screen edges etc. The HD video I downloaded from Amazon as a test sample looked as crisp and bright on the laptop as it did on our Samsung 1080p television. The sound clarity is very good for dialogue and background music - the full speaker running across the length of the front of the machine is really good and the volume is quite loud.
Additionally, the touchscreen is responsive, but not so sensitive that just brushing it will mess your page up or close an open tab. I did run into a couple of sessions where the screen would go to black as I was scrolling rapidly by touch - this seems to be a Windows 10 issue when using the new Edge browser and not a laptop physical issue. I haven't had a repeat of this in the Chrome Browser in a week. (It could also have been a fluke)

The battery life on this computer is freaking amazing! I've been using it for almost 3 hours now for a variety of things and it's currently sitting at 74% with an estimated 6 hours and 35 minutes run time left. By three hours of use, my Gateway would have already been at 10% and that's before it started having problems. Thus far, I have used this laptop for a five hour straight run - writing, with email refreshing in the background and music playing as a test at the same time and the battery barely hit 52% when I was finished working.

Uploading and transferring files from both the cloud and my old computer hasn't been as big a hassle as I expected. The USB 2.0 thumb drive I had handy worked just fine and everything came over intact. The cloud transfer was a bit stickier just because Windows 10 now wants to make unzipping files more complicated than before. (Thanks Microsoft) Additionally, the DVD RW drive works fine and I have had no problems at all uploading the software for my 3D printer and downloading files from the net for it. For those that are interested, unlike other reviewers, I had zero problems uploading and am now using Google Chrome as my browser etc. I've included a photo of my basic screen - the Chrome icon is right there. You just have download Chrome and then unzip it manually.

My one star deduction is for physical comfort. This is a light computer compared to my previous one and I appreciate that. However, the edges are not rounded off. They are sharp, square and pointy. This means that as you are typing - doesn't matter if it's on your lap or a desk - after awhile, these pointy bits will dig into your wrists or arms and this HURTS. My five hour marathon the other day left a little indention on my right wrist. That is just ridiculous. The second design flaw is the touch pad. It is very large and sits perfectly flush with the base of the laptop. This is pretty, but you tend to brush over it as you are actually typing and that can make the cursor jump - now you're typing in an entirely new location. These two issues are obnoxious enough that I am now looking for a way to create a little rubber bumper for the front edge of the computer and a wireless mouse.

In general, this is a nice replacement for my old workhorse Gateway - I've grown used to the smaller screen because Toshiba has made it very easy to enlarge the font and any image on this screen. The 8 gig of ram makes multi tasking and switching from things prompt and thus far, I haven't experienced any lagginess. There is some bloatware pre-installed (like with any computer), but it is easy to get rid of. WIndows 10 requires a learning curve of course, but that's not the laptop's fault. Four solid stars after almost ten days and if that changes, I'll update.

*********SIX MONTH UPDATE April 29, 2016 ********

After a little over six full months of regular, almost daily use, I have had no problems at all with this laptop. It just does its job with no drama. It streams movies, music and uploads photos and files to the cloud. It handles my word processing needs and email and all the regular stuff anyone does on a computer. It also handles my software for my 3-D printer with grace. I am still very pleased with the battery life and it has had no trouble connecting via blue tooth to my external speakers when needed. I still don't like the slightly sharp edges on the corners, but it's not the end of the world. All in all, this is a nice machine and I'm still using it and pleased with it in general.

title: Easily portable, works from my car's USB outlet
text:
After using this little light for a week, I'm pretty impressed with it's overall handiness. It weighs next to nothing, but is still stable when standing on a table or stack of books, mine doesn't wobble or tip over if you lightly bump it. The touch control is responsive and I haven't noticed any lag between touching it and the brightness changing. It cycles through all three levels and then off quickly and correctly. The LED light is a clean, bright white without that obnoxious yellow tint so it's a good reading light.

My one issue that I only get about two full hours of use out of a full charge and I can't see anyway to tell if it's completely charged or not. Two hours is actually plenty - the light is totally portable and I appreciate that it can be recharged via USB on a computer or even in the car if yours has a USB outlet. Mine does and I'll probably take this light along the next time we're on a road trip as part of the emergency kit. I received a free sample unit for testing and review.

title: Impulse purchase three years ago - still working perfectly.
text: We bought this late at night in a rush at Wally World when our old DVD player died while trying to watch a DVD marathon of True Blood. I had no time to do any research and I hate going into W-Mart to begin with, so I grabbed the first DVD player on the shelf with a recognizable brand name and got out of there. Three years later ~ it's still going strong. The lack of a HDMI outlet isn't a problem and the picture it sends out is clear and fine.

title: Keeps the cords from sliding behind stuff, velcro is easy to use, cut out holes are a smart idea
text: This is one of the better cable sleeves I've used. I like that it's really long - something like three feet which means it can actually gather up the whole cord from outlet to appliance. The cut out holes are pretty smart and let you adjust the sleeve and cables/plugs exactly where you need them without undoing the entire sleeve to pull different cords through. For example - I have my sleeve set up with the printer, a lamp and a shredder in the home office, but only two items can be plugged in at once. I swap the lamp and shredder as needed - the sleeve keeps all three cords raised off the floor and from sliding behind the desk when not plugged in. I received a sample sleeve from the seller for testing and review and I'm really glad I did - I think I'll buy one for the tv, dvr and streaming box now.

title: Fits my lamp, similar light quality to an old school soft white bulb in a decorative lamp, cool to the touch
text:
I received this light bulb as a sample for testing and review based on my use in my home and I think I am going to have to purchase a few of them now. I have been dreading making the switch to LED bulbs for many reasons - difference in light quality, the bizarre shape of some of the bulbs, laziness, but primarily the cost per bulb.

This particular Winnemucca 8 watt replaces a 50 watt incandescent soft white bulb in a decorative side table lamp, so I wasn't expecting much, just ambiance lighting in the formal living room. The bulb is wider than the original style, but it does fit my lamp and the light it puts out is just as good as the original incandescent bulb we were using. I do like that it doesn't get hot to the touch like the old bulbs. That alone makes me the happiest - if you forget to turn the lamp off at night, it's not sitting there baking the shade.

title: Tough, looks good, fits 4th gen Fire HDX 8.9 exactly
text: Fits the Kindle Fire HDX 8.9 4th generation tablet perfectly. The speakers are not distorted and music is clear with the case. The cameras both front and back, work as they should with no edges of the case appearing in the pictures. The case itself is padded and offers nice protection for the tablet in a handbag on the go and in actual use. It holds securely at each corner and even shaking it upside down over the bed, my tablet stays put. The grooves are just right for different viewing or typing angles and the bright white really stands out in the mix inside a carry on bag traveling. I love these Poetic cases - we have purchased several in different colors for two different 8.9 Fire tablets, one of the 7" Fire HDX tablets and my Fire Phone. For the money, I haven't found a better bargain or more functional case for any of these gadgets.

title: No degradation of screen clarity, obnoxious to install, fewer fingerprints
text: I waited almost a month to write my review because I wanted to see if the claims really were true. I received two screen protectors in the package and put one on both my husband's and mine 4th gen Fire HDX 8.9 tablets. The sheets fit exactly and the manufacturer claims of fewer fingerprints and less oil build-up on the screen surface seem to be true. The protector is clear and does offer more clarity when viewing photos & video than other brands I've used in the past.  My primary complaint is the sheer obnoxious difficulty of installing this screen protector compared to other brands out there...multiple steps and it took at least two tries to get it just right on both tablets. Oh our package came with a photo of the iPad on the front,not the the Fire, but the screen protectors inside were correct.

title: First tech gadget to drag my husband from 1997 into 2014! GREAT tablet!
text:
Wow! I got the Fire 8.9" tablet for my husband as an early Christmas present while he's recovering from major surgery. (I used a gift card for another store, so thanks Mom!) This is his first ever tablet - dragging the man into this century is like pulling an ox out of quicksand with a rubber band. I needed a tablet that would be: easy to use, back itself up, was big enough for his giant hands, light weight to use while in recovery, have access to all our photos in the cloud while he was in and out of the hospital and bed rest, and easy access to movies and the books already on his ancient Kindle Keyboard. As expected, the first hour with his new Fire HDX was full of complaining and cursing and shoutiness. (This also happened with our new car, the Kuerig coffee maker, yogurt, blue underwear, and every new toothbrush in the past 18 years. )

Two days on....The man is carrying his new Fire everywhere he goes. He's doing email on it, SKYPEing with a buddy, Twitter, reading the news, watching movies, shooting video and pictures of the dogs and throwing them to the TV via the mirroring with the Fire TV stick. (That is a neat trick). In short, my beloved Neanderthal has finally arrived in 2014 and I am delighted! To be honest, I love my 7" Fire HDX, but after seeing and using his new 8.9" in person, I am jealous and sort of want the bigger version myself now.

title: Covers dead spots, multi devices have no slowdown, installation w/directions was trouble-free UPDATE APRIL 2016
text:
I am not super "techie" like some of the other folks reviewing this router, just your average housewife who likes gadgets and tries not to drown in the constant wave of weekly tech improvements. As such, I wanted a new router to replace our two year old dual band Belkin with similar speed output, but only a single antenna. The Belkin had a number of dead spots despite using one of those extender things and I had had enough. Enter this TP-Link router.

I was wary of the installation after seeing some other reviews and the difficulties folks have been reporting. However, after reading the box and the instructions fully FIRST and then following the directions exactly, I had no problems. One thing I did notice immediately, is this router is meant to be used with a cable modem and that modem must be powered off before you connect it to this router. I used the website installation method and was up and going in a total of 20 minutes - that is from opening the box to having all our wireless stuff connected to the internet again. The website management page is very detailed and allows for a lot of customization of your network, honestly, more than I need or understand. But changing the router's password and setting our network name was simple and worked on the first try.

After three days of use I like it. The speed is decent and the dual antenna set up has improved the coverage problem we were having with the old Belkin router. I haven't experienced any slowdown or degradation of connectivity with multiple devices going at once thus far. A Fire Phone surfing the net, Fire tablet streaming music, laptop doing email, and a smart tv streaming video all at once in different rooms. So...a good router for every day family use in a pretty typical home.

*********** UPDATE FEBRUARY 2015 ***********
After 90 days this router is trouble free and really working like a champ. Our cable company upgraded our modem and increased our internet speeds recently, requiring a full shutdown and reconnect of my entire network. It was a snap and the router has had no problem with faster connection and the new modem. I relocated everything to the center of our house when everything was being swapped out and the router is now sending a five bar signal out to the back deck, which means I can sit out there with the dogs in nice weather to do email etc.

*****************UPDATE APRIL 2016 *************

I'm still using this router every single day for literally every single WiFi device in our house and it just does its job with zero drama every day. We now have two tablets, two smartphones, three DVR boxes on WiFi, two laptops, a printer, a Fire Stick for streaming movies, a smart tv connected the web now and then, and the Echo that's connected all the time. (yeah, I know...we watch a LOT of television in this house!)

Right this minute I am streaming music on the Echo, recording tv shows on two different DVR boxes, using my laptop to update this review, and uploading 42 photos from my phone to the cloud and pushing email to my tablet. Oh - and I am sitting outside on the patio enjoying the lovely spring day. This router is powerful and I have no dead spots inside or out in the backyard.

title: Very comfortable, good battery life, work with multiple devices & Fires
text:
So comfortable! I hate earbuds and finding actual earphones in Bluetooth that sound good has been a chore. These fit over your entire ear and have a full cushion, allowing for extended use in relative comfort. This has come in handy overnight at the hospital lately, trying to rest on the guest sofa next to a family member's bed. I found the battery life to be excellent for music and movies and games....several hours use at a time, turned off and then used again before recharging. I love being able to use the cable when the battery is dead or if you have a device without Bluetooth.

I have paired these via Bluetooth with my Fire HDX tablet, Fire Phone, and two new (2014) Galaxy phones - all worked perfectly. The NFC pairing was trickier, but did work on the Fire Phone and the Galaxy Note 4, after I figured it out. The sound is pretty good - way better than any of the other, less expensive, lower end headsets I've had in the past. The bass boost is definitely noticeable...I tried it on pop, rock, and even Beethoven. These are great if you listen to classical music, btw

title: Light weight, soft and sleek, not very secure for active users
text:
Very slim and sleek! The leather is soft and feels great in your hand which is big plus for a tablet case. There is an elastic strap that pops over the front of the case to keep it closed when not in use, but it's not really sturdy enough to double as a hand hold if you're using your Fire to read a book. The inside is nicely lined with a soft fabric that will keep your screen and the back of your tablet from being scratched up. The cutouts are correct - but one odd thing, the package does not specify which version Fire tablet this case is for, it just says "Fire". While my 7" HDX does fit in this case, the cut outs for the power & volume buttons don't line up, this case is meant for the other Fire tablet.

The reason for the single star deduction is because of the way the case holds your tablet. It slides in under a flip type tab on the top and the bottom two corners are held in place with elastic straps. This is fine if you only use your Fire sitting in bed or on the sofa and never really carry it around with you. I drag my Fires around everywhere - in the car, out to the horse barn, the doctor's office, the kitchen, airplanes, the garden, etc etc. (My current go to case has a hard plastic pop in style shell that is really difficult to remove.)I wouldn't trust this MarBlue slim tech case to hold the Fire super securely for my daily use and lifestyle. One snag of the bottom corner strap on a nail at the farm and disaster!

title: Light weight, well thought out, looks great
text:
Very light weight, sort of disappears in your hand. To be honest, I wasn't impressed when I pulled this case out of the box. It felt flimsy and I worried it might pull apart after a couple of days with my lifestyle. I am hard on my phone cases...in and out of my hand bags and pockets constantly, in the pocket on my saddle pads when I ride almost daily, and the covers get opened and closed hundreds of times a day. I even drop my phone now and then -GASP! The horror!

This one has a hard plastic shell that your Fire pops into and a face cover to shield the screen from scratches etc. The cutout on the back for the camera is excellent - a little oversized which I actually like, no chance of the edge of the case appearing in my pictures. The plastic shell carries over to cover the volume and Firefly buttons with a flexible push through so they are protected, but still fully functional. Again, I like this...no accidental photos in your pocket. Additionally, the face cover is cut back a bit so the folding hinge piece isn't coming into contact with your volume or Firefly buttons open or closed. The outside material feels like a cross between linen and leather...soft without being slippery and it doesn't catch dust or fingerprints on the front. The metal look on the back is eye catching and helps the phone stand out from the crowd a bit. Overall...a very good case and one I will pick up in another color.

title: Easy to install, works well, no blue tint, no air bubbles
text:
I tried the Anti Glare screen protector rather than the clear so I could use my Fire out at the barn and dressage arena in the sunlight more easily. It was super easy to install and took less than two minutes. I cleaned my screen with a lens wipe first to ensure it was free of lint, finger prints and oils. Followed the included instructions exactly and lined up the screen protector with the Fire's camera etc and laid it down. The package had a stiff cardboard piece that works better than a credit card to smooth the protector sheet as you go - I have no air bubbles at all on the first try. Once it's in place, you need to remove the blue top layer to reveal the actual clear screen cover you will be looking at and touching when you use your tablet. There should NOT be a blue tint of any kind on your screen.

The use of any screen cover is going to diminish the clarity of your high definition video, that's just a fact of life. This one is no exception. But...it does cut the glare in direct sunlight and it really helps prevent scratches to Fire's screen which means I can use my Fire in more places than before and in turn makes it more valuable to me. So this screen protector does what it says and does it well.

title: Work well with a tablet & cell phone for games & movies, no ear pain
text: I use these primarily to watch movies and for game play on my tablet rather than to listen to music on a regular basis. They work nicely with both my Kindle Fire HDX and my Kindle Fire phone and a laptop computer. The beauty of the 3mm plug in is that there isn't a blue tooth connection or battery issue to worry about, it just works as long as you have the headphones plugged in. The ear pieces are pretty well padded and do a decent job blocking out extraneous noises - the television for example can still be heard, but sort in the distance. I much prefer traditional over the ear headphones to ear buds, you can wear them longer with less pain and these Philips live up to that. They didn't pinch or bind even after watching a 90 minute movie. The sound is decent, full and complete and both sides seem correct, neither ear was missing out on dialog or background music. My one issue is there is a distinct static feedback when you connect them - I have to jiggle the cord or pull it out and try again more than once before it's clear with almost every device I connect them too. Not sure what that's about, but it's a relatively minor complaint.

title: Fits in your hand, works with Fire Phone, loud volume, can accept & make calls through phone
text:
I was very surprised at how powerful this little pod speaker actually is - it really does have a significant amount of volume and can be used in your car if you don't have a blue-tooth enabled system (for example my Mother's 10 year old Suburban out at the ranch) or at the barn when working horses in the round pen or dressage arena. It works via a standard blue-tooth connection or using the NFC option if your smart phone is equipped. There is also a microphone built in and the speaker does in fact, work very well with phone calls - we placed and received two calls using this as a speaker phone and the calls were a tad "tinny", but if you need to speak to someone hands free while cooking a meal or grooming a horse and you don't want a traditional headset, this is an excellent option.

I tested this speaker both inside and outside and it kept the signal from my Amazon Fire Phone almost 60 foot away outside in a direct line of sight with no degradation playing music. Inside the house, it managed to retain a strong signal through a closed door for about 30 feet before it lost the connection and that was far better performance than a no name blue tooth speaker we bought at Hastings in December. Sound quality is pretty good with both classical and country music. Pop can be a bit hollow at upper volume levels and hard rock has reasonable bass sound, but the vocals tend to become somewhat shrill to my ears. This is not a big deal in the least - just turn down the volume and know that at this price range you're buying the idea of portability rather than some super hi tech music snob gizmo.

Connecting this TechMatte Sound Pod to my Amazon Fire phone was super easy & took literally 10 seconds via NFC. It also connected just as easily to a Samsung Galaxy S2 and a Samsung Galaxy Note 1st Generation. My one complaint is that the on/off switch is directly over the charging outlet, so you have to disconnect the charging cable to turn it on or off and then reconnect the cord if you need it to charge or want to power it via the outlet while in use. A minor irritant that is at most worth a half star deduction. Overall, this is a very nice portable speaker that does exactly what it claims to do and fits in the palm of your hand. I did receive a sample speaker to test and review.

title: Adds some bulk, holds securely, easy to carry, buttons all work
text:
I got the gold case....think Gold Lame Barbie from 1985 to be more precise. Not ugly, but you definitely won't mistake this case for someone else's generic black folio Kindle HDX case. The case is actually a two piece set. The first part is a simple hard plastic pop out cover that goes over the back of the Fire and offers protection from scratches and bumps etc. It adds no bulk or weight at all. All the cut outs for the power & volume buttons and speakers are precisely placed and don't interfere with operations at all.

The second part is the zip around folio case. You snap the Fire with the first cover into the attachment on the folio. This is surprisingly secure and sturdy. Once it was snapped in, I jiggled and flapped the entire contraption every which way, trying to shake my Fire loose. It never budged or slipped. The folio case opens like a book would and can be folded back sort of like a paperback. There are pushable rubber buttons that reach inside the folio to actually touch your Fire's power & volume buttons, allowing the exterior of the case to remain solid with no holes except the speaker openings. This is a good thing since it's meant to be a travel case. The zipper is a bit stiff ~ something I don't mind, might keep it from coming open in a carry on bag dashing through the airport security etc. It does slide in and out of both my handbag and a carry on size suit case easily and packs well. There are pockets in the front cover for business cards and a loop to put a stylus as well. One thing I do like is the little handle/strap on the outside.

My reason for the one star deduction.... This case does add a bit of bulk to the normally svelte Fire HDX 7" and it doesn't allow for standing up to view videos and it can be hard to pop the Fire out of the folio part if you want to switch cases. Overall, it's not a bad choice and certainly a viable option when traveling ~ I'm writing this review on my Fire HDX sitting in this case at the end of a 4 day trip having used it.

title: Fits perfectly, hand strap is strong, looks nice
text: For five dollars, this was almost too good to be true. I love this case. It fits my new 7" Fire HDX perfectly - the tablet just pops into the four corner slots and stays put. The cutouts for the speakers, power & volume buttons and the charging slot are all easily accessed and functional. When the case is open & folded back, the hand strap is tight and sturdy, allowing you to securely hold the Fire while reading or playing a game - sort of reminds me of the feel of an old school paperback with the front cover folded back. The case adds no weight or real girth to the Fire, still fits into my handbag and the center console of the car easily. This case does put the Fire to sleep and wakes it up when completely closed, which is nice for battery savings if you use your Fire like I do - it's feeding music and audio books to my car's stereo system via the Bluetooth streaming, but there's no reason for the screen to be running or the XRay lyrics info etc while I'm driving. I can set the Fire to stream my audio content, shut the case and go on with my business. I don't understand why anyone would spend $40 or $50 on another case - this Poetic product is awesome & at these prices I can have more than one in different colors to match my handbags.

title: Very tight fit
text: My Gateway 17" laptop does fit in this sleeve, but it is a really tight fit. I can close the flap and the entire computer is covered, but the stitches on the band around the flap are visibly stretched. I will keep this sleeve - packing the computer in it inside a piece of luggage will offer some protection from bumps etc. As to the odor... it really smells bad when you first open the package. I soaked it in febreeze and let it sit to air out for 24 hours and that made a huge difference. (Apparently, there is nothing Febreeze can't fix)

title: Very sturdy, fits Kindle Keyboard nicely
text:
This a nice carrying case - feels very sturdy in the hand and the ballistic type material is tightly woven and I imagine it would withstand even a chewing puppy pretty well in a pinch. The inside is lined with a felt like soft fabric to protect the screen of your Kindle or Fire while in transit. This case held both my Kindle Keyboard and the husband's Fire - each one fit properly. My ONLY issue with this sleeve is that if you already have any type of skin or one of the Amazon lighted cases on your Kindle, it won't fit at all. You will have to remove your other covering in order to use the Timbuk2 ballistic sleeve. This is a pet peeve of mine - I want the lighted cover on my Kindle Keyboard for obvious reasons and if I want to add a dash of extra protection for traveling, then I'm out of luck. It's always a one or the other situation with all the electronics - smartphones, kindles, tablets....

Having noted that one issue, I think overall, this is a very good sleeve that will offer some real protection for your gadget.

title: Excellent value - good sound & long battery life
text:
I've been using these for a few days now and I'm pretty impressed. I use them mainly for listening to audio books & podcasts and some music while working out in the barn or cleaning house, that sort of thing. My normal usage pattern requires comfort when wearing for a couple of hours at a time in some serious heat & humidity outdoors. These Kinivo bluetooth headphones have just enough padding to be comfortable, but not enough to make it hard to hear oustide noises. The distance is pretty decent too - I know for a fact they are recieving & playing a clear signal at least 100 feet from my cell phone out at the barn. Now, that is in a relatively unobstructed line in any direction - just one or two half walls & gates. At home, they work throughout the entire house and only start to break up or lose the signal when I go outside to the yard and leave the phone inside. To my thinking, that's pretty darn good overall reception!

I have been VERY impressed with the battery life. Yesterday I was doing a hard clean in the barn and listened to 4 hours of an audio book non stop while I worked. Then got home and used them for another 2 hours straight while cleaning house and the battery was STILL strong. When I do charge these, I use the USB to wall plug adapter thing that came with my Kindle and it works just fine - you can also charge them via the USB on your laptop. I have only used these headphones with my Samsung Galaxy Note cell phone so I can't speak about how well they work with a laptop or other brands of phones. title: Amazing for those with vision trouble!
text:
I had decided I did not "need" a Kindle, having tons of other gadgets for all sorts of things. Then I began to lose the vision in one eye and realized over a period of weeks that I could not read normally (or at all some days). Magazines, books, the newspaper.... heck even email was difficult to impossible some days. All my friends have Kindles, so I borrowed one for a day and fell in love. We immediately ordered the Special Offers Wi-Fi Keyboard version. I've had it about 45 days now and my quality of life has seriously improved! I can enlarge the font and change the style of the font depending on my needs at that moment and on really bad days, when my eyes are tired or refusing to focus, the voice function is amazing. The very idea that it reads aloud to me is tremendous and once you adjust to the sometimes robotic pronounciation of some words, it works like a charm. So far, all the books I've purchased have allowed the voice option.

I signed up for Audible.com about two weeks after getting the Kindle and the quality of the audio books on my Kindle is excellent. No robotic voice here - you get the narration exactly as read by the real person - it's an MP3 file I think. Additionally, getting the local newspaper every morning on my Kindle has returned to me my morning tradition of the local editorials & coffee. I do love the number of free books available as well - some are garbage, but most are pretty decent and some have been excellent books. (Loads of Sc-Fi for free too, what's not to love?) I have used the sample option for a ton of books and it's helped me decide to spend the money purchasing a novel, or not. In case you are worried about the Special Offers... they are the screensavers while the Kindle is in sleep mode and NEVER show up in your actual books. I've used a couple of them already now that I think about it.

One last thing - the Kindle in a case, fits into almost all of my handbags and has saved my sanity sitting in doctor's office waiting rooms and at the car repair shop, and I can now sit out under a tree on a pretty day with my horses again while I read a great book. This version of the Kindle will also play my own music while I'm reading. Bottom line is that the Kindle has helped me get a valuable part of my life back and this in turn has allowed me to be more rational while facing possible permanent loss of vision in one eye. Very worthwhile purchase!

title: Works with 6 connections & quite fast once it was connected
text:
I am soooo not a techie with regard to setting up fancy networks and having the latest greatest of every gadget out there - let's just get that out in the open. I don't know or even understand most of the jargon for computer stuff, what I do know is from an average person's point of view. My interest in gadgets is centered on fast, easy to use, and reliable so I don't have to do this stuff over and over. I want frustration free or as close to it as possible and I do NOT want to have to contact "support" just to connect, install or use new software or electronic toys. This router came at just the right time, my 3 year old little cheap Belkin router was trying to die. I had been debating on what to replace it with now that we have more than two peripherial gadgets to connect to our wireless network. Priorities were speed, strength of signal accross the entire house, reliable and something that would install easily with minimal cursing & throwing of things.

I had the old router uninstalled and the new Netgear N600 powered up and connected to our high speed internet cable modem and the wired desktop within minutes. I was on the net with the desktop computer with zero trouble at all. Next I connected my Blackberry via the wifi on the phone and it was up and going within seconds - no trouble here either. Third item was the wireless Canon printer.... drama. I tried my laptop and my mother's laptop next....DRAMA. None of them could access the network. I shut the router down and started from scratch. The second time everything connected and the router was seeing each computer, the printer and the Blackberry. However now I had no internet access. (mild cursing had begun)

Third time.... by now almost an hour had gone by. I started from scratch AGAIN. I followed the instructions in the booklet exactly and this time when the router checked in and registered itself, there was a message bar saying there was a "firmware" update available. By now I figured nothing I did was going to make the problem any worse, so I installed the update. Lo and behold! This time the router saw all three computers and the printer and my Blackberry & my mother's Blackberry AND they were all able to access the internet. Now the final test was to reconnect the Wii system to the new router so we can use the Netflix streaming again. Worked like a charm.

Overall impressions of this router after a half day of use (and 90 minutes install time) - It's currently connecting a desktop, one printer, 2 laptops, the Wii and one Blackberry smart phone and all are working smoothly. The speed for downloading Netflix movies seems exactly the same as before, the speed on the laptops is a little faster, and the speed (loading webpages) via the Blackberry is MUCH faster than with our old router. The signal strength is very good - this is a 2600sqft house on a very large lot and I was able to send email from the back deck outside. Our old router could never do that on it's best day!

Final thoughts - this router is worth your time. Just make sure the new firmware update is installed before you add your computers etc to the network and save yourself some time. The speed and signal are very good, so I am willing to forgive the install bugs.

title: Returned it - no sound & box was hot to the touch
text:
Ok... I KNOW better than to purchase any electronic gizmo with less than a four star overall rating. I took a chance this time - I was looking for a cheap way to stream video on my television via the computer without having to buy a Roku etc. This converter thing SHOULD have worked fine. I guess, technically it works, but not the way I needed it to and honestly, it's just a HUGE hassle to use on a regular basis.

Pros..... it's small. It does send the video to the television (you do have to tell your computer to send the data to another monitor). It was inexpensive.

Cons.... Our 3 year old tv has all the connections for stuff - USB, S-cable, that 3 prong thing, 3 HDMI outlets and it connects easily & streams Netflix via the Wii game box. It works with the DVD player and I've played DVDs through the laptop in the past with the USB connection, so I KNOW they all work. The ONLY way it would work with this converter box was to use the S-cable and the yellow prong cable AND the USB all at the same time. The picture qualtiy was fine. I tried for 20 minutes to get the sound to transfer through to the television - never happened. Which meant I had to leave the laptop speakers on in order to listen to dialog. Not conducive to sitting several feet away from the screen. Meanwhile there was a huge tangle of all these cables on the tv stand, the laptop, low sound and no ability to pause etc without getting up and going to the computer to do it manually. By the end of a single episode of Frasier (23 minutes) the little converter box was very hot to the touch and the wood underneath it was hot as well. I imagine if you watched a full length movie you might end up scortching the finish on the tv stand or table!

End result.... I'm returning this converter first thing in the morning. I'll just cough up the money and buy the ROKU I guess.

title: Blazing fast, shorter range than expected, works fine though
text:
Ok I will be clear - I am NOT a super techie like some of the other folks who are reviewing this router, so I can't explain some of it's fancy gizmos and tricks. What I can do is tell my impressions of this unit from the point of view of your average person who knows a little bit about the techie things and can set up my own wireless network at home. The things that make this router different from the lower priced options out there seem pretty straight forward to me - it's fast and it's secure and you can use it for multiple wi-fi connections in your house. What more can your average family ask for? Well I'll tell you... SIMPLICITY of set up would be on the wish list. Here's what happened the day the new Netgear N750 router arrived.

Out of the box we noticed there was no instruction book. Just a single sheet with basic instructions. Ok, so it's a simple process, simple enough not to need a big book of directions. At first this was true, then things got complicated. It did hook up easily enough and had no drama talking to our cable provider's internet service and the Windows 7 desktop computer saw the router and they communicated very easily.

The Good.....As a test of the range, we used a Blackberry and walked throughout the house and the front & back porches searching for the wi-fi signal. This is a 4000sqft house with two stories on a normal size lot, so when the Blackberry saw the Netgear network and was able to connect to the internet even out in the yard we were delighted! Upstairs, downstairs, in the kitchen, at the opposite end of the house and in the garage we had a solid, strong signal from the router. We then tested the connection with a Roku box, a Wii game system, a netbook computer, a different smartphone scattered all over the house. Every piece of equipment found the network and connected to the internet like they were supposed to. And using the Wii, netbook and Blackberry all at once to load a photo heavy website was amazing - twice as fast as the old, cheap Cisco router and smooth as silk.

The Obnoxious...The next step of course, was to the name the network and do the security block so strangers can't piggyback on it. Especially since it was broadcasting out into the yard and off the porches. And that's where it got complicated and obnoxious. It took two hours to sort out the security settings. The first time we did everything as directed by the software. The end result was a loss of signal from the router everywhere except the room it was physically located in. Multiple subsequent adjustments rendered it useful in three rooms, but no longer were we able to pick it up or access the internet upstairs or on the back porch or even in the far bedroom where the Wii console is located. Not good. The end result was to wipe all the information, reboot the entire computer and router and start over using the lowest security settings. (Can you say frustration?) Once this was done we had a signal and were able to maintain the connection with the Roku, netbook, and smartphones throughout 80% of the house and a weak signal on the porch. The Wii however, cannot hold the signal at the far end of the house which means the router will have to be moved to a more central area of the house.

End result.... The weakened signal issue might not be a big deal or even worth taking a star away from my rating, but I keep coming back to this one thought. The el cheapo, 2 year old, VERY basic "off the shelf at a big box store" router we had been using put out a stronger signal for a third of the price of this Netgear N750. However, the Netgear router IS faster than the old one and there isn't a noticable reduction of speed even when multiple things are connected at the same time. If that's more important to you than overall range, then this is a darn good router for the average home.

text:
[[VIDEOID:5ccab2044675ebd47957448b1e0ac5e8]] I think this will actually be a useful item, as opposed to just being a cute gimmick.

The fan itself is good as well. It has a wide range of positions, so you can aim the air flow to your preference. There are three speeds; low, medium and high.

title: You can't have too many of these nylon ties
text:

As I have begun trying to prepare for various scenarios, as well as get more organized, I see the value of these ties. I've used them to control loose cords, seal up some kinds of packages and even reenforced a small, rolling metal shelf.

Overall, very happy with these. I know you can get them cheaper in a store, but my mobility is limited, so online works just fine for me.

title: You can't have too many of these

Our local store where I normally buy these has been out for nearly a year. While you pay a little bit more online, I'm still very glad I got them. No problems with these at all.

title: Very thin
text:
It is hard to have problems with zip ties, but I do have an issue with these. I had an entire bag of mystery cords that had entangled themselves like coat hangers do in dark closets. So, I sat myself down with the big bag, and a new plastic bin to bring some order to the chaos and bind up the cords. I had several sizes of zip ties with me to accomplish this task. The only black ties I had were these, so I know the issues I had were with these ties.

These are thinner than all the rest of my ties. Also, my others were made of nylon and were nice and strong. These black ties seemed to be more plastic than any nylon. They were a little harder to use, being a bit flimsy and much weaker than my other ties.

They did hold small cords together, but we're definitely cheaper and thinner. I would not buy these again.

title: Love the colors
text:
Well, these are certainly interesting!
I often lose my little Roku remote, with it sliding off the bed, then being hard to find under the bed, under cat stuff, etc.

These are silicone covers. If you or your child has ever bought a game controller cover, these are like this.

These are not super easy to get on to the remotes. There are so many button cutouts, it gets caught every step of the way. As a chubby woman, it brought back flashbacks of trying to put on pantyhose too soon after a shower, or on a humid summer day...good luck! 😄

But, I persisted and slowly got it on correctly. It has a textured back to help keep your grip. It does kind of cause the volume button to feel recessed a bit, but that is not a deal breaker. It also includes a wrist strap, but there is no designated punchout for it, so it seems useless to me. The strap is also too small to go over your wrist, so just a pointless addition.

I love the colors though, and it will definitely help me find it on the floor, or amid blankets. The silicone might even help stop my cat from ceremoniously shoving it off his spot by my pillow, but we'll see about thay one.

Overall, I'm pretty happy with these. The only negative side is having to peel it off again if a battery change is needed, but that isn't oftem enough to be a concern.

title: Works great, very helpful item

She has been able to plug other USB items into the adapter, with everything working as intended. Her mouse, a thumb drive and phone charger can all run off this hub.

title: Works just fine. Don't see any big difference from my 50-mile antenna
text:
I didn't want to review this until I'd had a chance to use it for a while.

We cut the cord on cable a few years ago, and went to antenna and a smart tv. The antenna I was using had a 50-mile radius. This one makes claims of 180 miles.

I placed it next to my other antenna. I have a very large tree fairly close to the bedroom window, so I do have some difficulty with reception here. We are near the STL broadcast area, so no mountains or forests in our way.

I first tried just switching the antenna connection without a new channel scan. Everything looked exactly the same as with my old antenna. No biggie. It has a nice, long cord, which helps for placement.

The next day, I ran a scan for new channels. I really expected to see some new channels pop up with the additional 130 mile radius. Nope. I have exactly the same channels.

Of course, your experience could vary greatly, depending on your location, topography, big buildings, etc. But I have to say that this 180-mike-radius antenna does nothing at all different from my 50-mile-radius antenna. So, not really better, and definitely not worse.

title: Works okay, horizontal footprint, very little memory, grunts a lot
text:
I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.

as I worked, seeing it out of my peripheral vision. However, it is mostly hidden by my hand anyway.

There are precious few directions included with the mouse, and what is included seems to be a loose translation from someone
who learned English on the internet. I have no idea how to set the side buttons or adjust the speed. My computer did recognize
it simply by plugging it in, but there were no driver updates or other information. I'd like to know how to adjust the DPI house settings, which are not an option in my control panel for mice.

The mouse is comfy for my hand - I like larger mice so my fingers don't cramp up - I am online for many hours a day.
This helps. I don't ever use the wheel, so won't comment on the wheel function.

Cons: This is something that definitely needs to be adjusted in the next "incarnation" of this mouse....

on the inside. However, as I mouse back and forth, these raised areas are not smooth, and they catch on my Belkin gel mouse pad.
I really don't like that at all. I am going to use it for a while longer before I decide whether to keep it or go back to my old mouse though.
