title: Nice Non-Focus Binoculars
text:
These do work as advertised. These are non-focus, not autofocus. In other words, the distance is pre-set and non-adjustable. You won't be able to see anything in focus within a short distance. But once you're past the minimum distance, you'll see things clearly. I prefer not having to focus binoculars.

These seem of nice quality.

title: Very Easy to Pair This Up with My Existing Mengshen Alarm
text: My Mengshen Alarm only came with one remote. I needed a second one. This was easy to pair up with my existing Mengshen Alarm, and both remotes can activate and deactivate the alarm.

title: Good Alarm
text:
This is a good alarm that's easy to use. The alarm feature is loud. The remote control seems to work at a nice distance. The infrared sensor kicks in immediately. Seems good quality. I am not using the door feature.

You have the option of using alkaline batteries in the main unit and infrared sensor, or to plug them into mini-usb situation for power. The USB cables and USB charger are not included.

title: Clicks Are Quiet, But the Scroll Wheel Is Not
text: The clicks are very quiet, which is great. Range and accuracy and battery life are great. The middle scroll wheel is not quiet.

title: Great Strap
text: Very comfortable. Easy to attach and detach. Good quality. I use this strap on various bags of various sizes. Works great. Durability has been good so far. The strap looks good, too.

title: Backpack Straps Not far Enough Apart
text:
The weakest part about this is the backpack feature. This is a narrow case, and the 2 straps to hold the backpack on your back are not far enough apart to easily get the backpack on your back. I am not an extra wide person at all. It's too much trouble and not smooth and comfy to squeeze my arms into the backpack straps.

As a case to carry with the neck strap or the handle, this is a good, small case. The zippers open and close easily. It will hold a laptop and tablets just fine.

title: Good Bag
text:
The color I chose does not necessarily look like just a woman's bag. It's fine if a guy wanted to do the cross strap thing and ride a bike with this.

I was able to put 12 pounds of groceries in this bag, and the bag survived. I would not put any more weight in it than that, however.

I put on a more comfortable shoulder strap than what was provided since I knew I would sometimes be carrying heavier items.

I like the bag. It seems to be of nice quality.

title: Nice Monitor
text:
There is a lot to like about this monitor. It's easily height adjustable, it can pivot, the angle can be tilted up and down, it has built-in speakers (I am using a Bose Solo 5 soundbar instead of the built-in speakers), the side and top bezels are not too wide, and the picture quality is very good, with a lot of picture configuration options. (I plugged a 3.5mm stereo patch cable from the back of the monitor into the soundbar.)

I watch TV broadcast and cable channels, movies, and TV shows via my computer, so I wanted a larger high quality-picture monitor with a higher DPI capability. I did not want to spend so much and buy one of the many monitors above $500, but I did not want one of the cheaper 32-inchers that had less DPI capability.

This LG has so far satisfied what I want. I have settled on the "HDR Effect" Picture Setting for most use, and it is quite nice. There is also a "Custom" picture setting that allows for a lot of configuration. (I could never have just settled for LG's factory default picture settings.)

The monitor is very heavy...much heavier in weight than I expected. Attaching the stand is really easy. Detaching the stand is also very easy. Build quality of this monitor seems good. Assuming this just-released monitor stays working perfectly for a long time, LG did an excellent job and I am glad I bought it.

title: Great to use in a bathroom outlet
text: This is perfect for using in a bathroom outlet that only has two plugs because the cord length won't take up much space.

title: Works as Expected
text: Good quality USB-C charger...and works as expected.

title: I am a Fan of MagSafe
text: I am using this in one of those table-top stands, and it is very nice to have my phone connected to the stand via MagSafe, which makes it very easy to put the phone on for charging.

title: Works Perfectly
text: I like that this has a USB-C port along with USB-A ports. The size is compact, perfect or my side table where I keep my iPhone Qi charger. I have two of them, and so far both are working well.

title: Works on my 2020 iPad Air
text:
I bought this for my 2020 iPad Air with USB-C port. (I have not tried it on any Apple USB-C laptops.) So far, it is working as advertised.

I'm not sure of its longevity, and while using it the quality of the components doesn't inspire huge confidence, but if it does indeed last in the long run, it's a convenient way to charge my iPad.

title: The Tripod Legs are Way Too Small
text:
The tripod legs are so small, too small. The slightest touch or shift in weight will cause the whole thing to topple.

If you are going to use this without ever using the tripod legs, it will be fine. If you need to use the tripod legs, do not buy this.

title: There's a lot to Like with this Orbi
text:
This Orbi replaced the Apple Airport Extreme for me. It is superior, and is providing much better WiFi coverage and speed. (I am using it at home, and not at a business.)

This Pro version of the Orbi does provide a way to disable automatic firmware updates, so you can choose when to do them manually.

I set it up using the Web-based configuration page. I did not use the smartphone Netgear Orbi app. While using the Web-based configuration is easier and faster, it is very disappointing and frustrating that Netgear has not fixed it where you don't first get an error that the page is not secure. There are people that might not know you can click "Advanced" and then click to proceed anyway.

I am also disappointed that Netgear does not turn on the settings to Enable Implicit BeamForming and MU-MIMO by default. (These settings are buried under Advanced>Advanced Setup>Wireless Settings.)

The Web-based Configuration page is easy to use, and informative. I recommend the Pro version over the Home version because you get extra features like the ability to create additional separate WiFi networks and you can turn off automatic firmware updates.

Netgear claims WiFi coverage of up to 2500 sq. ft., and you can add Orbi Pro satellites in the future, if needed.

title: The Cable Works
text: DisplayPort on my computer to the HDMI input of my TV ... picture and sound are as expected. The cable is working as it should.

title: Good Computer with a Loud Fan
text:
There is a lot to like with this computer: The small size is great. There are 2 USB-C ports instead of just 1 like with a lot of others. There is no bloatware. You can hook up your monitor to either the DisplayPort or USB-C connection. They include a USB-C to HDMI adapter. There are 4 USB 3.0 ports. Good speed for regular computer use with the I7 processor and SSD.

The biggest thing to dislike is the volume of the fan. You wouldn't think a computer this small would have such a loud fan, but it does. It's annoyingly loud. If you're going to be working on the computer a lot while in a silent room, I would recommend to not buy this computer because of the fan noise.

title: Quality Cable
text: The USB-C to USB-C cable is of very good quality. It works perfectly.

title: Not the Bose Clarity & Quality Sound You Expect
text:
When see you're buying Bose and the $200 price, you automatically think you're going to get a crystal clear, high quality sound from this soundbar. But you don't get that.

What I got was sound that was not all that noticeably better than the speakers built into my new-model big-screen Vizio TV. Yes, I am connecting the TV to the Bose Soundbar using the optical cable. So disappointing.

And, let's not forget that unnecessarily big remote control included. It's too big and uncomfortable to hold. I hate the remote control.

Oh, and remember, there are no buttons whatsoever on the Bose Soundbar itself. If the remote ever breaks, or if it is lost, your Soundbar is useless without it.

The build quality seems solid, but what good is that if the sound quality is so subpar? Considering the disappointing sound quality, this Bose Soundbar is way overpriced. Don't get me wrong, you can hear decent sound from the TV...it's just that since it isn't much better than what you can get from your newer HD TV, why bother? Now, if you have an older inferior TV with very low-watt speakers that produce tinny sound, the Bose Soundbar will make a bigger difference for sure.

title: The Purple People Eater
text:
We all know that when it comes to buying hard drives, we need to be one of the countless lucky ones who do not get defective units. And if ours is not defective, we will be very happy with the 10TB WD Purple Drive. It's a great drive for NVR camera surveillance systems.

The WD Purple Drives I have purchased seem like good quality, and they installed easily and are working perfectly so far.

title: Quality Ethernet Cable
text: This Ethernet cable is working as it should. Appears to be good quality. I am glad I bought it.

title: Works Well on a 39" Vizio TV
text:
My Vizio 39" TV came with legs that are installed very wide apart, which means you need a wide table. With this set of TV stand legs, the legs are installed very close to the middle of the TV, so you can basically put it on any narrow table you want.

Yes, the included instructions are quite disappointing, but installation can be figured out in spite of that.

The feet seem sturdy, and I recommend this for anyone that doesn't want to use Vizio's very far apart feet they provide.

title: Works for 32" Vizio
text:
My Vizio 32" TV came with legs that are installed very wide apart, which means you need a wide table. With this set of TV stand legs, the legs are installed very close to the middle of the TV, so you can basically put it on any narrow table you want.

Yes, the included instructions are quite disappointing, but installation can be figured out in spite of that.

The feet seem sturdy, and I recommend this for anyone that doesn't want to use Vizio's very far apart feet they provide.

title: It Works
text: It powers my Sony radio, and the price was good.

title: They Do the Job
text:
I put two of these into an NVR and they worked. WD says they're designed to be run 24/7, which is what I needed.

They are easy to install, as they're simply SATA drives. Plug in the power & data cables, and boot the device.

title: Works As Advertised
text: I like that this switch box is low profile and that it supports gigabit speed. The push buttons work well. The Ethernet connections are solid. There is no signal loss. I am glad I chose this Network Switch Box.

title: Works As Advertised
text:
I am using this between a Windows computer with HDMI and two separate screens. So far, it has worked as advertised and reliably.

The only negative for me personally is that if I have one screen on that is showing the signal from the computer, and then I turn on the 2nd screen, the signal to the first screen is completely cut off for a couple of seconds...after which the signal is shown on both screens. It's a tiny bit annoying. But perhaps they could not make this device where if you turn on a second monitor the HDMI splitter cannot split the signal instantly...it must cut off the first output before able to join both outputs together. (I have no idea.)

title: I'm A Little Blue That This Is Blue, But It Works Perfectly
text:
If it came in white, I'd wanna give it 6 stars. I have no idea why they made this in blue and not white.

I connected this cable to a powered indoor antenna and ran the 50 feet of thin coax from upstairs to downstairs and connected it to my TiVo Roamio OTA. The cable is delivering a perfect signal.

I really like the smaller size of this coaxial cable.

title: As Of This Posting There Are Too many Things The Voice Commands Cannot Do
text:
It was a struggle at first to get the VOX remote to pair with my Roamio OTA...but after multiple attempts it did eventually pair.

The voice feature needs to be improved by a lot. A lot of things I ask, it cannot do for me. One simple thing it should be able to do: I have channel 9.1 as an example. There are no sub channels on OTA channel 9. If I ask to go to channel 9, it won't do it. It should be smart enough to know that channel 9 is 9.1. Oh, and it doesn't work with " 9 dot 1." To voice change to channel 9, I have to say "9 dash 1." It's frustrating, to say the least.

Also, it won't switch back to the previous channel you were watching by voice command: "Go to last" or "Go to Previous"

Also, you cannot voice command for your TiVo to go into Standby Mode. You can voice command the TiVo to open up Settings, and then use the buttons on the remote to navigate to the section where you can press to go to standby.

title: I Would Not Recommend This Monitor For Purchase
text:
The first thing I noticed with this monitor is that it slants downward towards the right of the screen. The top is not level at all. I then saw online a review video where the reviewer also noted this issue.

The second thing I saw is that the picture sharpness regarding high definition is disappointing. It's slightly washed out. For this being as expensive as it is, I was shocked and upset. I hooked up my Apple TV 4 via the HDMI cable and fed multiple HD video, including live HD TV channels via the Channels app connected to an HDHomeRun.

There is no doubt that the design of the monitor looks great. But I'd rather it put out a spectacular 1080p HD picture than have the whole minimalist design.

Oh, and the screen has no height adjustment feature. Only tilt.

I am sorry I purchased this monitor.

title: I Am Glad I Bought This iPad
text:
The iPad is fast and does exactly what you'd expect. I am glad I bought it, and use it every day. It works exactly as advertised.

I deducted a star because it's still a bit heavy when holding after a while. Of course, at this time, if you want the bigger screen than what is offered on the iPad Mini, the extra weight has to be tolerated. I am looking forward to the day when they make the regular size iPad with the lower weight of the iPad Mini.

Bottom Line: I predict you'll enjoy using this iPad model as I do.

title: Works With Cox Gigablast Internet Service
text: I bought this to use with Cox's Gigablast Internet. I called Cox to have it provisioned, and so far it is working as it should. I deducted one star because I feel it is overpriced at this time.

title: It Works
text:
It is working fine on my Macbook Air, converting the USB 2.0 port to Ethernet. It was truly plug 'n play, worked right away.

It is perhaps overpriced now at this point, especially compared to other USB 2.0 to USB Ethernet adapters.

title: Good Picture/Poor Audio Quality
text:
I deducted 1 star because there is only 1 HDMI port on this TV, when there really should be 2, and because the audio output is of extremely poor quality. I think the use of an external speaker is a requirement when using this TV. I was really surprised at how bad the audio sounds on the TV. A prior reviewer called the audio sound "garbage." I would have to agree.

The TV is lightweight. The picture is pretty good for a $135 TV. I like that it has both RCA audio out jacks and a standard 3.5mm stereo out jack. If you want a small size TV, this is certainly one to consider.

title: Good Choice for a Small Size TV
text:
I deducted 1 star because there is only 1 HDMI port on this TV, when there really should be 2.

I deducted another star because they put a label right on the screen itself that left behind residue upon peeling it off. This is unacceptable on a television.

The TV is lightweight. The picture is pretty good for a $130 TV. I like that it has both RCA audio out jacks and a headphone jack. If you really want a small size TV, this is certainly one to consider.

title: Impressive Speed
text:
I am impressed with the speed of this drive. Connected via USB 3.0 to a Windows 10 computer with an i5 processor, I am transferring large files at about 310 MB/s.

I also like the small size of the drive.

As long as its longevity is good, I will be very happy I bought 2 of these drives.

title: I Like This Splitter
text: Great splitter. Exactly what I needed. Works perfectly.

title: I Had High Hopes, But the Darbee Disappointed Me
text:
I expected so much better of a quality picture per the claims made and because of the very high price.

I have an excellent computer with HDMI output directly connected to an excellent 2017 model 1080p LED HDTV. The computer is used to stream live HDTV channels and either 720p or 1080p downloaded movies and TV show episodes, etc. (The computer puts out a resolution of 1920 x 1080 at 60 Hz, of course.)

The Darbee default setting out of the box is HiDef 100. The picture was not good at all at 100. (And I just found a video review online where the reviewer said he also could not tolerate 100 and had to turn it down to close to where I did.) I turned down the number to 75 and that helped. But the overall difference between Darbee on and off is very small at the 75 setting, and hard to like when I think about the fact it costs $200. And in fact, often the Darbee turned on was worse in the sense it accentuated flaws in the picture, especially in low light scenes.

Yes, I experimented with all 3 modes, and multiple number settings.

I am sure there are specific uses and set-ups of the Darbee where the difference in picture quality is high. But again, in my case the Darbee failed to impress me, and I cannot recommend this if your set up is like mine: computer to TV.

The Darbee is a great concept, and it is very easy to set up and use. But at $200, the value just isn't there compared with the end result I got.

title: The Hum Is Gone
text:
It works. The annoying hum is gone. I can't believe that it works since other hum eliminators I bought failed.

I have a 2017 model High Def TV that has RCA audio output jacks. (The built-in speakers on the TV leave a lot to be desired, of course.)

I am going direct from the TV RCA jacks into the RCA input of an expensive speaker. The hum was bad.

I tried all the suggested tricks, including using shielded RCA cables, plugging the TV and external speaker electrical cords into the same outlet, or a different outlet, plugging the electrical cords into a line conditioner, and buying cheaper-than-this-product hum eliminators. Nothing worked.

I then spent $100 for this Sescom IL-STEREO-19...and I found success. The hum is gone. (The only reason I deducted a star is because it's expensive at $100. It's a passive box.)

title: A Good Choice for an HDMI Switch Box with Remote Control
text: Works exactly as advertised. Seems like a nice quality HDMI switch box. I like the remote control feature.

title: Overpriced & Underpowered
text:
For its very high price, I expected a lot more when it comes to speed and power. It takes 5 seconds to tune from channel to channel. The time to wake up from sleeping where the TiVo appears on the TV screen takes way too long.

I had technical issues right away, where the TiVo Mini would freeze up and only come back to life after being power cord unplugged. (I was very unhappy and frustrated with the TiVo Mini and returned it.)

title: The Best DVR for Antenna Users
text:
Yes, I had the initial difficulty getting it to set up after first booted. You know, where you get an error code and the advice that you should unplug and try again. You'd think after all of these years, the TiVo company would have perfected the set-up.

After a few tries, it did set up successfully.

If you are running off an antenna and want the very best DVR, and if the cost does not bother you, this Roamio OTA is the one to buy. It is so nice that cost of lifetime updates and guide is built into the price. The software is really easy to figure out and use. The TV Guide is the best there is. The tuners are high quality. If your signal is good, your picture will be great.

The TiVo is superior to other OTA DVRs like the Channel Master and the Tablo...as it should be since the cost is higher.

title: Horrible Reception in the Same Location Where Other Antennas Can Pick Up the Signals
text:
My high hopes for this antenna were quickly dashed.

I am 43 miles away from the broadcast towers. I currently use the Marathon antenna (I use it indoors). The Marathon picks up all the major network channels perfectly except occasionally 1, and all the independent stations perfectly except occasionally 1. (It will pick up those 2 stations, but there is sometimes annoying pixelation and signal drops.)

So, after I read how this brand new Mohu Leaf Glide 65 Mile Range antenna was supposed to be so wonderful, I bought it, hoping I could get all the stations in perfectly.

It's awful! Placed exactly where the Marathon was placed the Leaf Glide cannot even come close to picking up as many stations. And yes, I made sure the amplifier was plugged in. And it is getting power. (It also could not pick up stations that cheaper/inferior antennas could.)

I moved the Leaf Glide to different spots, but no matter where I placed it it could not pick up stations that it should have been able to pick up. It picked up some stations, so I know the amp was working. I unplugged the amp and those stations were gone, so I know it is not a defective amp.

I know that when it comes to antennas people's results will vary. But for this $89 (current price) supposedly "new technology" antenna to fail so badly is a huge disappointment.

There is no doubt that this antenna will work perfectly for many people, if they are lucky when it comes to distance, terrain, height, interference, etc.

You would think in today's world of big technology there would be a way to broadcast signals that everyone can receive successfully.

My guess is that this antenna would only pull in 65 miles away if one had it outdoors, high up, and with clear line to the towers.

(I am in no way affiliated with the company that makes the Marathon. I am just a cord cutter trying to get all the stations received perfectly. If the Leaf Glide had worked I would have been so happy, and would have gladly done away with the Marathon since it is quite big and not the most attractive. The Leaf Glide is paper thin and not anything that would be something you would not wanna look at.)

The Leaf Glide is very easy to place. I appreciate that they included two easy ways to hang it: Either with white or black push pins or with velcro sticky dots.

If you get all the stations with this antenna you will love it.

title: This Vacuum Is Laughably and Embarrassingly Bad -- Save Your $16 and Your Time
text:
The suction power is almost nonexistent. The blower power is just as awful.

I have to laugh when I see at the top of the Amazon page for this item that it was reduced from nearly $26 to nearly $16.

I am telling you that this vacuum truly is terrible. Do not waste your $16 or waste your time.

title: Exactly As Advertised
text:
This is exactly what I needed. It is worth the price. I am glad I bought it.

It is holding a heavy laptop just fine.

Easy to set up. Easy to use.

title: Good Quality Cat 5e Patch Cable
text: This Cat 5e cable is good quality. It does the job, as expected. I am glad I bought it.

title: I Will Make the Case for the Case
text:
I am giving this 5 stars for the plastic case, and 1 star for the cloths.

I do not understand why the what seems like countless companies who make microfiber cloths for eyeglasses cannot equal the superior quality and effectiveness of the genuine white Crizal cloths. (The Crizal cloths are not sold via Amazon, and are relatively expensive if you buy them from the Crizal company directly). I have tried Terrafiber and Magicfiber and many in between. (I would rate Terrafiber's cloths in second place out the many I have tried. I keep trying different cloths hoping I can find ones at Amazon that equal the Crizal cloths.)

I do not like these Spektrum cloths and do not recommend them. They do feel like they might scratch lenses, and they certainly are disappointing when it comes to cleaning.

What I do absolutely love, however, is the case Spektrum includes. I wish they sold they case separately. But since they don't, I will buy a second order of these just to have a second case to keep in my car. The case has a tiny magnetic closure. The case is perfect to hold microfiber cloths (or even pills, if you wanted.)

To the Spektrum Company: Have you considered selling the case separately?

So, again, if you want a great small case and do not mind spending $7.95 for it, I recommend this.

title: Returned It
text: If you're lucky to get one that works perfectly right out of the box, this seems like it would be a decent quality DAC for the reasonable cost. (Some have reported theirs did not last long, so of course I have no idea about longevity. Mine was not working right immediately out of the box. Returned it. I did not get another one since I lost confidence in it.)

title: Works For Me As Advertised
text:
I got lucky, as this works perfectly for the device I needed it.

So far, using it 24 hours a day to power the device, it has worked reliably.

I am glad I chose to buy this one.

title: It's Working Well So Far
text:
This does the job...and better than some similar units that can only do PCM audio.

Only negative: The box feels plastic-cheap for a $35 adapter. I just hope it can last a long time.

I am glad I bought this, so far.

It works as advertised.

For my use specifically: Optical audio sound goes in one end. Analog sound comes out the other end (I use the 3.5mm stereo jack).

title: The RAM Works Successfully
text:
It is always a great feeling when the RAM you buy via Amazon works. (And once you have bought RAM that doesn't work, like I have done in the past, you'll see what I mean.)

This RAM worked. No issues so far.

title: Has The Potential To Be Great But Not Great Yet
text:
A lot of things to love, and some things to dislike.

For the price they are charging for this pretty simple cheap-feeling box, their app for watching TV on Windows and Mac computers should be so much better. The guide position is at the right of the screen, and it's a bit awkward to use. Also, once you click on the channel, you can only see a few hours of what's on later, instead of an entire day or more.

If you have an Apple TV 4, there is a $25 app for the Apple TV 4 called Channels which has a much better TV guide (and it allows one to pause live TV), but I can see where people might be unhappy they have to spend any money at all to use their HDHomeRun on an Apple TV. (In other words, perhaps Silicon Dust should offer their own free app for the Apple TV 4 for folks who do not want or need to pausing of live TV capability.)

So, if SiliconDust eventually truly improves the Windows and Mac software that lets you watch your OTA TV signals from the HDHomeRun box, this product would be 5 Stars, in my opinion.

The Windows and Mac computers I watch the TV on from the HDHomeRun are Ethernet connected and not Wireless, and thus the picture quality is excellent.

title: The Cable Works
text: The cable works. It seems well built. I recommend it. I would buy this brand again.

title: Effective At Cleaning Eyeglasses
text:
Does a nice job on eyeglasses. They say it will not harm coated lenses. I am taking them at their word.

There are no ingredients listed on the bottle. (I think I do smell alcohol in the liquid. I know some say not to use alcohol on coated lenses, while others say it is perfectly safe, and that it cannot harm any expensive coatings.)

The only reason I deducted a star is because this doesn't come in a larger size as a second option. (And I also would like the ingredients on the bottle, of course.)

title: Wrong Directions on the Label. Spray Left Behind Streaks.
text:
First of all, on the spray bottle I received the directions are completely ludicrous. The directions say to "put a drop on a small wad of tissue." Well, this is a spray bottle that spritzes out a very fine mist. There are no drops.

I have no idea why the manufacturer would put the above directions on a spray mist bottle. Makes me lose some confidence right away.

But I proceeded to ignore the label directions (since there is no way to put a drop on tissue...and doing so defeats the whole purpose of buying a spray bottle version in the first place, of course) and spray this product on my eyeglasses. I noticed a strong smell of alcohol right away.

I used a brand new, high quality microfiber cloth designed for eyeglass cleaning. I was very dissatisfied with the result. I saw streaking, and not clarity. The company included a new cloth, and I tried that as well. Same disappointing results, on 2 separate pair of glasses.

I am sorry I bought the spray.

The Formula MC version that comes in a squeeze bottle is much better, in my opinion. (I bought the spray thinking it would be as effective, but that was not the case for me. So, in the trash the bottle goes, and I am out $12.51 total ($6.35 for the item and $6.16 for shipping).

title: I Love It For The Price
text:
If you keep this in context regarding the fact it costs just $11, you get your money's worth for sure.

But if you want a very loud alarm built in, you'll have to spend more money than this and find an alternative.

In my opinion, the volume of the built-in alarm is not loud enough. I was disappointed with the alarm volume immediately, as I was expecting it to be louder. The volume is not scare-inducing at all.

The tiny screw they chose to use for the battery compartment is ridiculous. How many people have a tiny screw driver handy that small? Yes, of course there are some people who will have one. But I didn't.

The item feels cheap, and thus does not inspire confidence the alarm part will last a long time. Maybe it will. Maybe it won't. All I know is that it doesn't inspire confidence. (I read a review at Amazon that said the alarm part broke after 3 uses, and that it is only being used as a silent door stop now.)

But the above notwithstanding, since I love the fact this will stop the door from opening (or closing), combined with the fact it is so inexpensive and that it does have an alarm, I feel the product deserves 5 stars. (Plus, the company is very responsive and stands behind their product.)

title: They Work
text:
Luckily, both cables are working as advertised. I am hoping for longevity, as we all know many 3.5mm patch cables can fail after a while.

The cables seem well constructed for their reasonable price.

I have one going from my TV's headphone jack into an expensive external speaker. The other cable is going from my iMac's headphone jack into another nice speaker. Sound quality is as expected and desired.

title: Spot On!
text:
I put my money into getting two Spot cameras via Indiegogo back in November, 2015, and I am very happy I did. Once I received the cameras I knew right away I made the right choice. I love the Spot cameras. They work exactly as described and are of great quality.

Set up was very easy. I have the app (which is easy to use and works well) installed on my iPhone and iPad. Picture and sound quality is very good.

With the cameras being so small and light, they are easy to move to a different location, if desired.

The Spot camera is perfect for my needs. I was so happy to get a product that really works as advertised. I have had my Spots turned on 24/7 for approx. 5 months now, and have not had any negative issues.

I recommend the Spot camera. It is a good camera from a good company.

title: Another Love-Hate Relationship
text:
Amazon 1 Star Rating equals to "I Hate It" ... and I do have hatred for aspects of the Bolt, even though I also have love for it.

(Please keep in mind I have owned many different DVR's, such as the Moxi, ReplayTV, and Channel Master DVR+.)

I Hate:

TiVo wants a fee of $600 for a lifetime license, after you pay $300 or $400 for your Bolt. This is insanity! I could understand if they were asking for $600 for the lifetime of the person, no matter what TiVo boxes they swap out in the future.

The design of the box is terrible, in my opinion. I really hate it. (And please do not say they did it only to allow air to escape, because air can escape just fine on their Roamios and on other DVR's such as the Moxi.)

Final thing I hate is the difficulty prying the box apart to swap out the hard drive after the screws are removed. TiVo knows one's hard drive will fail eventually after the warranty, and/or that people will wanna upgrade to a larger capacity drive. They could have easily designed this box with a removable cover just under the drive, instead of making it where you have to take the whole cover off in parts.

Love:

Hands down, the TiVo interface and extra features of the Bolt are superior to any other DVR out there as of this writing. Once you have the opportunity to use Commercial Skip, you'll fall in love. Also, the Quick Mode feature is very nice, and it works well. The speed of the Bolt interface is excellent.

The TiVo software is really easy to use. The Bolt is easy to get set up. I like that if you have to swap out your hard drive, the TiVo software will automatically install itself on the bare new drive.

I like the online and mobile interfaces which allow you to set recordings remotely.

There are countless people online who feel that TiVo's $15 per month (or $150 per year) fee is too expensive ... and of course if you are paying it, you will wish the fee was a more reasonable $10 per month/$100 per year.

I am hoping TiVo has heard the endless complaints of folks who hate the Bolt's box design and who want a flat box. It will be interesting to see if they do a redesign of their next DVR model. And I'm hoping they come out with a TiVo Bolt OTA for cable cutters where the lifetime license fee will be far more reasonably priced than the Bolt's astronomical $600.

title: Positives & Negatives
text:
I bought my pair of Bluez 2S directly from AfterShokz company, and not via Amazon. Just like with so many things there are aspects to like and aspects to not like.

I will start with the negatives. If you are in a noisy environment, such as working out in an exercise room, the volume just is not loud enough or satisfactory at all. You need earplugs in the ears to get the satisfactory volume. Yes, earplugs. Of course, that defeats the whole purpose of buying headphones that do not go inside or cover your ears.

You can test this out by simply putting a finger in each ear and then you'll hear the remarkable level of volume change.

Because of the lack of loudness one can achieve in a noisy environment, I cannot recommend these (unless you want to buy earplugs and wear them at the same time).

The only other negative for me personally is the lack of a way to go back to a previous song, or repeat the currently playing song. (You can skip forward to the next song, but you cannot go back.)

The positives: These are comfortable to wear and very lightweight. The Bluez 2S offers the ability for decent call quality when using them to make calls. Microphones seem good (I have only tried this indoors, and not outdoors, so I cannot comment further on this particular subject.)

The Bluez 2S are very easy to operate.

In a quiet environment, volume is fine, and music quality is acceptable for this price point. (Of course you will not get the level of music quality or bass you'd get with a more expensive name brand headphones that go directly over the ear.)

So, for specific purposes such as cell phone calls where you want to keep both ears free, these are quite good indeed, offering good voice quality for both parties. (Pairing with my iPhone 5 and 6S went flawlessly.)

title: This Works Exactly As Described
text:
It works exactly as advertised. I deducted one star because it only has 2 USB charging ports. There is certainly room in this thing for 4 USB charging ports.

If you are looking for this type of product, I recommend this one.

All of its features and benefits are already detailed in the positive reviews here at Amazon, so I figured I wouldn't repeat them...but simply say they are all accurate.

title: This Solved My Specific Problem
text:
I bought one of those very small ASUS VivoMini UN62-M037M computers. It has an HDMI out port to connect to either a monitor or your nice HD TV. (I have mine connected to my TV.) I am running Windows 8.1 on the computer.

Microsoft has acknowledged that there is a bug in Windows 8 and 8.1: When you turn off your TV but leave your computer on, the OS will always give you an Out of Memory error message. There is no software fix whatsoever. Many people are complaining of this issue on boards over at Intel and other places.

The only fix is to either never ever turn off your TV, or always turn off your computer when you turn off your TV, or fool the computer into thinking there is that HDMI monitor connected even when said monitor is powered off.

I bought this ConnectPRO for just this purpose...and it works.

Out of the box I did not get a green light, per the instructions. The light was orange, which implies it had a memorized EDID from the factory.

I reset the box and cloned the EDID from my TV.

I can now leave my computer on always if I desire and turn off my TV at any time, and no more problems.

Sad that Microsoft never offered their own software fix via an update, in spite of the fact they confirm the issue, which forced me to have to spend an extra $70.

title: Great SSD Drive At A Great Price
text: I installed this in a Mid-2010 iMac. So far, all is perfect, and as fast as expected. Price was great for the 250GB SSD. I would recommend.

title: I Bought 16 Gigabytes of this OWC Ram -- Success
text: I installed 4 sticks (4-gigs per stick) into a Mid-2010 iMac (3.06 GHz i3). All went perfectly. So far, all  is working perfectly. I did a MemTest after installation, and the RAM passed. I would say this is good quality RAM.

title: For My Specific Needs This Computer Is Perfect
text:
For specific circumstances, this Asus VivoMini UN62-M037M is perfect and wonderful. My specific circumstance: I wanted a computer to put next to my High-Def TV so I can play movies and TV shows, etc. My TV becomes the gorgeous computer monitor via the HDMI input. I have Ethernet right there, so I did not have to buy the additional WiFi adapter for the computer. I use a wireless keyboard and mouse.

This Asus has 4 USB 3.0 ports. I recommend this Asus model with the 4 ports instead of their model with only 2 ports.

I bought one 8-Gig RAM stick for $44 (Crucial CT102464BF160B via Amazon). I bought a 256GB mSATA drive for $103 (Crucial MX200 via Amazon). (I already had a wireless mouse [Logitech M525] and a wireless keyboard [Anker A7723].)

So, I spent about $435 total. (Luckily I already had a copy of Windows 8.1 I could use, plus a USB DVD drive. Of course, you can also install Windows via a USB Flash Drive.)

Opening up the bottom by removing the 4 screws is fast and easy. Installing the RAM and mSATA hard drive is also fast and easy.

I hooked up my HDMI cable direct from the computer to my TV and the rest went easy.

The Windows drivers are easily downloaded from Asus Website.

The computer is very quiet and small and nice. The i5 processor runs as expected. Boot times are fast. The Intel Video chip they provide is great at doing what I need it to: Provide a crystal clear picture to my TV, and allow me to stream high-def movies and TV shows from the computer.

For what I do and at the total price I paid, this Asus VivoMini is perfect. (With it seeming solidly built, I am hoping for longevity.)

title: This Universal Keyboard Is Perfect For Using On Your Sofa Or Recliner
text:
This keyboard is so nice and lightweight...perfect if you are typing with the keyboard on your lap while on a sofa or recliner, etc. I paired this keyboard to a Windows 8 computer just fine, no problem at all.

Works great on a desk, too, of course.

Very easy to operate. And the price is great.

The seller is also wonderful when it comes to communication, and replied fast when I had a question.

title: Good Quality Stereo Patch Cable
text: If you need a 15-foot 3.5mm male to 3.5mm male patch cable, this one is a great choice. It appears very well constructed. I like that the cable is thin. The ends seem solid. Sound is clear.

title: Disturbing Blindingly Bright Blue Indicator Lights On This Modem
text:
I am shaking my head wondering why Arris would think putting in blinding blue indicator lights on this modem was a good idea! The blue upstream and downstream indicator lights on the SB6121 and SB6141 are not nearly as blinding. Why?

I am not exaggerating at all. The blue lights are blindingly bright. Do not stare into them.

Of course, I could turn the modem around, but why should I have to do that on a $130 modem?

I could put tape over the lights...but that defeats the purpose of having the indicator lights in the first place.

If your shelf or cabinet setup is such where the modem is hidden from view, this modem is fine. But if you are in a situation where your room is small and the modem has to be in sight, by all means you should avoid this modem.

Do the people at Arris not actually look at the lights after designing?

This modem is listed as compatible with Cox Communications...and I was able to get it to work with Cox at full speed. However, due to the blindingly bight blue indicator lights, I either have to hunt down a different modem, or place something in front of it to block the lights. (Or tape a piece of paper or cloth on the front, which I'd have to lift up if I want to check the lights.) I paid $130 for this modem, and I have to do that? Mind-boggling.

title: Great Value For the Price. Great High Def Picture Via HDMI To Your HDTV.
text:
First I want to say that the first box I received did not work correctly immediately. The box kept failing to maintain recognition that my external drives were in fact present, no matter how many different types I used. There was surely something wrong with the ViewTV. (The ViewTV I received had software version installed from last month.)

I called the ViewTV company and they were really great. The nice tech support guy agreed I had to have something wrong with the unit...and he rushed me out a replacement. The replacement works much better...and interestingly its software version is dated 7 months ago.

I think the ViewTV at $50 is really a great value. (And I was impressed with the customer service the company provided.)

Running the antenna channel scan is relatively fast. The picture quality on my replacement box is stellar. Moving through all the settings menus is very easy and straightforward. Everything is easy to figure out.

When you think about the box's limitations, as pointed out by some very helpful reviews here, you must keep in mind the very reasonable price.

For $50 you get a good over the air box with a good tuner that sends a great picture via HDMI to your TV. You can time shift your viewing, if you plug in a drive to the USB port, and you can record programs to said drive.

For $50 you cannot expect multiple tuners or a great TV Guide. But at least you get to see the very basic guide info the broadcasters send down with their OTA signal. (My two HDTV's on their own do not show the OTA program info, which is very disappointing.)

For cable cutters out there on a budget, this box is definitely something you should consider. It delivers really well exactly what it promises.

title: Sadly, Not Nearly As Effective As Canned Air. This Has Weak Air Blowing Power In Comparison.
text:
I assure you, if you do a side by side comparison between this O2 Hurricane Special Edition and a typical canned air duster you will see a huge difference, and you will be disappointed like I was.

Dusting off a TV or computer screen or eyeglasses is a good test with this and the canned air side by side, of course, but you could simply just shoot the air on your hand and feel the inferior force from the O2 Hurricane Special Edition.

I was so hoping the O2 would be better than it is because like everyone I dislike the possible frostbite situation when using the canned air. Plus, the ability to use the O2 from any angle is really nice.

One day I do expect they will be able to make a canless air system in this kind of compact cordless size that has the air blowing power we need. But until that day, unfortunately, this one just isn't it.

title: Vizio Is Closer With This Model, But Still Far Away From Being Able To Satisfy Without The Need For A Separate Bass Speaker
text:
I got mine for $248 plus sales tax with the immediate $50 reduction in price if one has Amazon Prime. I think that is a fair price for this Soundbar.

There is a lot to like about this Soundbar. You will love its easy ability to program in your TV's remote control, or any IR remote, to control the volume and mute. Very convenient.

The volume on the Soundbar can get plenty loud. The sound is quite clear.

Vizio includes all possible cables you might need.

The Soundbar is heavy and appears solidly built.

Programming features via the Vizio remote are very nice and easy to understand and figure out.

The negative: I applaud Vizio for trying to include bass speakers into the Soundbar so you won't need a separate bass speaker, but sadly they have failed. I did lots of testing on various TV feeds, from Music Choice stations to movies to local newscasts to regular network TV shows. I did adjustments to the bass via the remote on all TV feeds. The bass level is not there yet to satisfy.

I plugged in an 8" Energy brand powered bass speaker (this is not a large bass speaker), and let me tell you the difference is remarkable with all the TV feeds.

I will strongly suggest that if you consider buying this Soundbar you accept that for the most satisfying sound you really need and should have an external bass speaker. You will not be sorry at all.

One day a company might be able to invent a Soundbar with built-in bass speakers that truly deliver. Vizio has not succeeded with this model. But again, excluding the bass aspect, the rest of the Soundbar does deliver the quality.

title: Nice Handle For The iPad Mini
text:
If you find yourself holding your iPad Mini for a long period of time, and if your hand gets tired, you are already thinking to yourself you wish the back had a handle. Well, at least that describes me.

I looked at all the possible iPad Mini handles and chose this one, even though the cost is higher than most of the others. I wanted one that would feel OK against my skin. This one does. I also like the soft feel of the back case the handle is attached.

This thing installs quite easily. Handle strap is easily adjusted for hand size (has velcro). Rotation of the handle is very smooth should you want to change from landscape to portrait.

title: Breaks down easily? I don't think so.
text:
What a disappointing and frustrating product this is. Something as easy as being able to break it down for packing up is almost an impossible task. Pulling so hard to remove the piece with the Numark name is ridiculous. Try it. I can't do it. Maybe a bodybuilder can.

This is a huge design flaw. Why not make it with a snap thingie you press in, and the piece would then pull out easily.

Sure, if you do not ever need to break it down for compact packing, the stand is solid and does exactly what it claims and what you'd expect.

But if you are going to need to break it down, forget about this product. Look for something else.

I was shocked. I cannot easily pull the thing apart. In fact, I cannot do it at all myself. And I cannot believe it is so difficult where it would take so much strength to get it done.

I read the two other reviews that state they find it easy to pull it apart. Did I get a defective one?

title: RAM Works -- And That Is What We Want
text: I have always had good luck with Kingston RAM, and I had good luck with this. Works perfectly. No issues at all.

title: Works Well. Solidly Built.
text: I am just using this as an audio switch box. And it seems well built. It works perfectly. I recommend this product if you need either an audio or video switch box.

title: Warning About The Warranty
text:
First, a warning for you about the warranty. This Speaker Tower is very, very heavy. Should it break during the one-year warranty, as expected you will have to pay to ship it to Pyle. (I am OK with this.) But along with the item you must include a $50 money order to pay Pyle Audio to send the item back to you.

Most companies work by you pay to ship the broken item to them, they pay to ship the fixed item back to you under the warranty period.

OK, now to the product review:

Overall, I am disappointed with the quality of the audio and I do not recommend this item to people who want the best audio quality and I would not ever purchase it again.

If anyone out there paid even close to the full retail list price of $433.99, you have my sympathy.

This tower does have some positives. The ability to play either FM radio, an iOS device, or other music source (you will need a 3.5mm to dual RCA male cable if wanting to play directly from the headphone jack of an MP3 player, etc.). It would have been nice if they had included a 3.5mm input jack as well, especially at this price.

Some songs sound pretty good, but others sound muffled or muddy. Not crystal clear like you would expect at this weight and price, and from Pyle Audio. If you compare your songs through this tower and then through the $300+ Dr. Dre Original Model Beatbox as one wild example, you will hear the difference in clarity and quality from the speakers immediately.

But again, some songs do sound quite decent, and with that I can see why some give this tower a great review. But if you are like me and you want and recognize the best quality sound, you might be disappointed with this tower.

The instruction manual is very disappointing, as well. I, and most can figure things out eventually, but there will be some folks who might need to ask for help.

The FM antenna is a small hard wired wire. You cannot add your own antenna.

I got the black matte model, and it does look nice in the room.

I think this deserves 3 stars because I think there are some people who will enjoy this tower and its features and its small footprint and its look for the $171 price.

title: They Are Great If The Cable Would Just Stop Failing
text:
I have ordered 4 of these things. Three have failed. And it is always the USB cable.

So frustrating.

title: I Like This Laptop Light
text:
This laptop light is perfect for mobile DJ's who use laptops. With its flexibility, I can easily bend the light to either illuminate my laptop keyboard or my mixer. And the light is just the right brightness for the job.

I have tested other laptop lights and I like this one the best. It truly is perfect for my specific needs and I am glad I bought it.

I like that it has an on/off switch, but I usually keep it on all the time.

title: I could hear no discernible difference in sound quality
text:
I use a $100 external sound card when DJ'ing because I want better sound than what the built-in laptop sound card offers. I notice a big difference.

I then was doing more research and read how the makers of these way more expensive USB cables claim they offer superior sound. So, I took the plunge and spent $50 for this Pangea Audio solid silver USB cable.

I seriously could not hear any difference between this USB cable and the $10 short USB cable I was using. For $50, I expected a perceptible difference, even if it was just a small difference.

I had others also judge...and they agreed with me.

From looking at and holding the cable, it does indeed come across as a quality cable. But again, I heard no difference in the sound...and I tested it with different genres of songs.

I would not recommend this cable. If you indeed have a great (and expensive) external sound card or a great DAC, my guess is you do not need to buy one of these $50 (or even more expensive) USB cables.

I give the cable 5 stars for build quality and 1 star for its inability to cause the sound from your laptop to either an external sound card or DAC to be noticeably improved. (So, I averaged it out to 3 stars.)

(I have not tested the much more expensive than this one USB cables, so maybe those do produce a perceptible difference?)

title: At a total cost of $116, worth every dollar...and I wish I could get more
text:
I got the 16 gigabyte HP Touchpad for $116 grand total and let me tell you it truly is a steal at that price. Do not believe anyone who says even at that low price they think the Touchpad is not worth it.

So, keep in mind that my review is for the $116 Touchpad and not the originally priced Touchpad.

My Touchpad is wonderful. The best part is the Web Browser that can access ALL of the Web. My biggest frustration with the iPad is that it cannot access ALL of the Web. And I visit lots of sites that use Flash programming in the site. I need Flash as long as those sites continue to utilize it.

Once the Touchpad arrived, I did the system updates and all is great.

The WiFi connects perfectly.

Touch response is nice.

I am very happy I got one at that price and will use it a lot. If anyone can get this Touchpad for that price, I feel it is a must-purchase for anyone who wants full-Web access.

title: Problems With Firmware Updates & Waking From Sleep
text:
(I bought two of these Vertex 3 SSD's...this one and the Max IOPS one).

I installed this SSD in a laptop. When the laptop goes to sleep (or if I put it to sleep), the drive will not wake up. I have to press and hold the power button to shut off the computer.

OCZ released a firmware update for the Vertex 3's that might fix this issue (among other issues) fairly quickly after the drive was released, but there is no way to upgrade the firmware on my drives.

OCZ blocks firmware upgrading if the Vertex 3 SSD is the Windows Boot Drive (which it is, of course, in my laptops).

OCZ also blocks upgrading the firmware if the SSD is connected to a USB to SATA adapter.

So, I have no way whatsoever to upgrade the firmware. I do not own a tower where I could connect the drive to a secondary SATA controller. (And honestly, I shouldn't have to do that in the first place.)

$300 and no way to update the firmware so I can fix the issues? In 2011? This is astounding, and a complete blunder on the part of OCZ, who could not care less.

Avoid these OCZ Vertex 3 drives!

title: It's All About The Price
text:
I own the Archos 70 Internet Tablet with Android 2.2 Froyo installed.

I am going to start by listing the three things I hate about this tablet.

1. It only has 256 megabytes of RAM. It really should have 512 megabytes of RAM. (And I would have paid a little more to get twice the RAM.)

2. It does not come with the Android Marketplace App or Google Apps pre-installed. (So, with each update, you have to rely on others to create the Google Apps .apk that you can hunt down and manually install. I did it, of course, but it is a little pain in the butt. And, not all the apps show up in the Marketplace.)

3. It is a fingerprint magnet like you wouldn't believe. The bezel around the screen absorbs oil from your skin like crazy. Keep a wiping cloth handy at all times.

OK, now to the good. I paid just over $250 for this tablet direct from Archos, and at that price, I am satisfied where I give the device 4 out of 5 stars. I like the size and weight (as I found the iPad to be too heavy when holding it for a long time). Battery life is good. The screen is excellent for Internet, email, and video.

Android 2.2 Froyo runs well on my tablet, and I am happy to have Adobe Flash (although not every single Flash Website works...and if you encounter a chat box that runs on Flash, like Chatango, the keyboard does not respond, you cannot chat).

Bottom line: If you want a very good and reasonably-priced 7" WiFi-only tablet right now, the Archos 70 is the one to get. (If you don't need one right now, it is expected there will be many more tablets offered in 2011...and they will have more RAM and a more powerful processor. And yes, I know, they will be more expensive.)

title: A Lot To Like With The Vizio
text:
First, let me say I own the 47" LG 47LE8500 for my living room with its stunning high def picture and extremely poor speakers. I was looking for a slightly smaller (and less expensive) TV for my bedroom and chose this 42" Vizio. Vizio has a similar 47" model under this newly released line. (So far, I am mostly happy with my purchase.)

Both the LG and Vizio have LED LCD with Local Dimming. I have to say that the high def picture on the Vizio is not as stunning as on the LG 47LE8500, but it is close, and still satisfying.

The black levels are better on the LG, but pretty close on the Vizio.

The Vizio arrived with one of the round rubber "feet" missing under the base. (Better quality control and inspection please?)

The WiFi on the Vizio is fabulous. The remote having a qwerty keyboard is fabulous.

First thing I had to do (for personal preference) is turn off the room light sensor. The picture was way too dark for me when the light sensor was on.

Also, the default screen brightness setting with the light sensor off is too bright, in my opinion. The brightness level is at 50 by default on the standard pic setting, and it looks brighter than the 50 setting on other sets. (But it is very easy to adjust, of course.)

The speakers on the Vizio are much better than on the LG.

I dislike that the Vizio does not have a swivel base.

Standard def is quite acceptable (and better than on the LG).

So, bottom line: If you want to save some money, this new Vizio line is a very good choice (and recommended). Once you customize the pic settings, I think you will be happy with the high def picture. If you have extra money to burn, the LG will give you a more stunning high def picture with better black levels, but you probably will dislike the LG's speakers, especially if you listen to a lot of music with the volume raised.

Adding to my review, August 28:

When the TV is off, the Vizio logo at the front is lit up in orange. I have found no way to turn this off. I hope that if enough people complain, perhaps Vizio will release a software update that will allow the turn off of this orange Vizio light.

I have encountered bad lip sync issues. But luckily, Vizio has included in the Audio settings a Lip Sync adjustment setting. I had to enable this setting, as the lip sync mismatch problem was really bad. The adjustment has helped.

You can also delete pre installed apps by holding your finger on the app until a sign comes up with an option to remove from the device.

title: The form fitting is perfect and while I do feel my phone is highly ...
text:
The form fitting is perfect and while I do feel my phone is highly protected, the case doesn't make the phone too large to handle or carry around (as you are aware the iPhone 6 + is already pretty big). While I like the idea of being able to change the back plate to different colors, I always stick with the black one. It's not a feature that I care much about personally, although it is neat. The case looks pretty mean overall and I love showing it off (as with most NewTrent products).

As always the screen protector is great and feels very similar to the actual glass screen and does not distort color or text. The buttons for sound are perfect, they depress smoothly and function the changing of the volume 100% of the time.

The covers for the charger, headphones and volume are difficult to open though. While I do appreciate the fact they are great to offer resistance to water and dust, etc. I do feel they could be a bit easier to open. They feel quite stiff and can be difficult to open (perhaps the tabs can be 'improved'). Another and more serious gripe I have is the inability to reach the vibrate/silent switch when it's cover is open. I have a very hard time reaching in there to toggle the switch because the cutout is too small.

The sound quality is good and I have no complaints there.

My phone has survived two nasty drops without a scratch.

If you want a case that offers top notch protection and looks great too - look no further!

title: AMAZING customer service
text:
UPDATE 22 August 2019:
The customer service team with GoScope contacted me soon after I left my original three star review (below) to explain to me that I had received a *newer* version of the customized case for Sony A6400 mirrorless camera. The newer version, they said, is engineered to not require the foam insert for the lid that I had been expecting. To demonstrate their concern and good faith, however, GoScope said they would send me a foam insert (with 3M adhesive) from the "old style" case, but ALSO a copy of the older case so I could use whichever one I prefer! Folks, you can't do customer service much better than that. In my original review I said that the case is well made and rugged. My problem with it has been fixed --in a friendly, helpful, and timely manner. So....Five Stars.
_____________________
When I first looked at this item I could have sworn that the photo illustrations showed a foam insert in the "lid" --the part that closes over the top of the camera. I looked at the Bergsma video on Youtube (see my screen capture from that video and another), and sure enough, there was a foam insert in those videos as well. The case that I received did not have one; I don't know if I got a used case or a dud from the factory. When I looked at the case on Amazon again just now, the photos look as if the foam insert has been blacked or blurred out. The case is well made, but no foam in the lid obviously reduces the drop or vibration security of my A6400. The $45 price tag seems steep if that's the new normal. The insides of the case are molded to cradle an A6400, of course, so the camera won't be rattling around, but now I think the Bergsma video might be misleading. As it is, I don't think I could drop my $900 camera body and $500 lens in this case and expect them to survive the fall. Anything to say about this, GoScope?

text:
UPDATE August 24, 2018: The Seller of this mouse contacted me almost immediately upon seeing my August 17th update with an offer to replace the defective mouse with a battery-powered version (2 - AAA batteries). I received the mouse yesterday and it has been performing very well. The scrolling wheel and pointer are working fine, as one would expect. But I am most impressed with the Seller's eagerness to make things right. Thank you!

UPDATE August 17, 2018: This mouse died this morning. The pointer just wouldn't appear on my desktop. CANNOT recommend this mouse; I like the design, but the scrolling wheel never worked properly, re-charges never lasted more than a few days, and now this. Don't waste your money.

UPDATE June 13, 2018: The scrolling wheel on this mouse has been balky since almost the beginning. I've tried several mouse settings in Windows 10 and haven't been able to remedy the problem. If you've ever driven a vehicle in which there was a lot of "play" in the steering wheel --meaning you turn it quite a bit before it begins to catch and actually steer the car-- you can get an idea of how scrolling wheel feels on this mouse. Computers are never fast enough for me, and wheeling away to scroll down a few lines can get really annoying. Might just be a defective unit.

My (much) larger ANKER vertical mouse died, so I had to replace it. 7Lucky mouse is smaller and fits my hand much better! I've been using it all day and haven't had a bit of wrist pain. I LOVE THIS MOUSE.

After a full day of trying to get it up and running --including a three-hour phone call to Linksys tech support, I got it working. Fifteen minutes later, it stopped working altogether. The system said I had wifi connected, but it would not load any content in any browser. Customer service was helpful and knowledgeable, but I don't have another 180 minutes to waste jumping through hoops and holding my mouth just right. It may just be that my PC and laptop are just too old (7 and 5 years, resp.); it was working fine with my Samsung tablet and smartphone. But I can't afford a new PC or laptop right now.

So, I took it all down, put it back in the packaging, and got my Tenda router up and running again in about three minutes. The Linksys AC2200 is going back for a refund.
