text: Very easy to apply and re-position.  I followed instructions, got the protector on slightly askew, but used the edge of an Exact-O knife to slowly, gently left it off the LCD screen surface to re-position correctly.  It "clung" to the surface better than the first time, no trouble with bubbles at all. Nobody hates those flimsy, easy-to-crease and/or ruin plastic screen protectors more than I do. The thin glass protectors are the answer.  Make sure you buy the right size!

title: Fits perfectly, feels solid, and looks classy!
text: Beautifully designed for easy access to all of the Tab S2 9.7's cameras, ports and jacks.  Fits perfectly, feels solid and luxurious, and looks classy.  This black ProCase is my third.  The moment I upgrade to a newer model of tablet, I purchase a ProCase for it.

title: My fourth OMOTON Glass screen protector
text:
I have used OMOTON glass screen protectors on my Galaxy S5 and Note 4 Smartphones, my Galaxy 8" ATT tablet and now this Galaxy S2 9.7" tablet for videos and Skype. So count me as a satisfied customer. Included in the sturdy shipping packaging are wet and dry cleaning fabric swatches, a dust cloth, clear directions --everything you need to apply the protector with maximum efficiency and minimum grief. I can't tell you how many film screen protectors I've wasted money on --only to have them show bubbles or rainbows or scratch really easily-- or inadvertently destroyed trying to apply them because of lousy engineering and/or materials quality.

OMOTON screens are easy to apply (with common sense preparations of a reasonably dust-free environment), look great, protect well, and ...wait for it... can be re-applied! In my book all that makes OMOTON worth the extra expense...and believe me, nobody paid me for this review.

title: Basic enough for a 1980s set up, but not webOS, 4K UHD or DirectTV...
text:
I have a 60" LG webOS 4K UHD TV, a Samsung soundbar, a Sony Blu ray player, and a DirectTV cable box. I'm not a gamer, but I use Netflix, Amazon Prime, Hulu, etc. a LOT.

I didn't find this Logitech Harmony remote to be even remotely (pardon the pun) sophisticated enough to handle the series of commands required to change inputs. (I never did find a way to add and name an HDMI 2 input based on the downloadable set up instructions.) Logitech's hardware setup interface is attractive enough, but I didn't find it particularly user-friendly or adequately interactive. Once I had the remote set up, I realized that one has to start from ALL COMPONENTS OFF (including the cable box) to move through the various commands to get to the activity intended ...and, as I said, even that won't take you all the way through without grabbing the old remote. No point for the universal remote then, is there? Returning this item for a refund. Keep trying Logitech.

title: Easy and Classy!!
text: I've used Omoton tempered glass screen protectors for two tablets and three of my most recent smartphones.  Trust me, the ease with which these excellent screen protectors are applied --without bubbles, and their capacity for being repeatedly remove and re-positioned perfectly FAR exceed those of flimsy film screens. Omoton screens are pricier, but you absolutely get what you pay for. Outstanding.  I recommend them.  Make sure you're getting exactly the right size, and order with confidence!

title: Worked adequately --for about 3 months...
text: Lasted for approximately three months, but never really worked as well as expected. I don't know why or how (and maybe I got a lemon), but it appeared to me that the M510 stopped working because the laser and opening thru which it "beamed" became mis-aligned.  Got to the point where the cursor wouldn't move at all. I also kept having to go into Control Panel and re-adjust the mouse settings.  I switched back to my Logitech M305 mouse and it worked perfectly under the exact same conditions.  VERY disappointed; first time I've ever regretted buying a Logitech product.

title: GREAT quality; could be a bit larger
text: Rugged, outstanding quality.  The main selling point for me was the inclusion of heavy duty velcro-fastened loops for carrying a collapsible tripod. For a "Large" it does turn out to be a bit smaller than I'd like, since serious digital photography these days requires enough room for batteries, filters, lenses, flash, etc. Very pleased overall.

title: Marketing promises KEPT!!
text:
I'm not a buyer of high-end ear buds. At my age my hearing isn't acute enough to hear much of the nuance of music through headphones, but I do like the sound to be much better than if I were holding a can and string up to my ears. That being said, these are the best earphones I've ever owned. When I first put them on, the bass response actually startled me and the middles and highs were present and clear --without any adjustment to my player. The "stays in your ears" feature actually works; you give them a twist in your ear and they stay put, as well as keeping out sweat. You can hear ambient noise just fine, but unless there's a high wind or other competing sound, you continue to hear the audio just fine.

I don't agree with other reviewers who report that the plastic earbuds fall off easily. I think those reviewers must be actually pulling the buds off to clean them and I don't believe that's the manufacturers' intentions. I clean mine with a mini-fiber cloth well moistened (but not soggy) with rubbing alcohol without removing them from the actual earpieces.

The reason I didn't give these earphone five stars is that there is no inline control --no mute off, or volume control. I like them VERY much, and would buy them again if I needed to replace.

title: After a pair of disappointments, I like it
text:
The specifications imply that this tablet is designed to accept a wireless sim card if the user decides to add an additional wireless telephone line. After spending half a day trying to register my purchase with Dell, I was told that, since Dell itself was not the seller, they are not bound to provide warranty coverage. So, Amazon Warehouse buyers might want to figure a Square Trade or other third-party warranty into the purchase price for this Dell. When I asked about the fact that a card slot for a wireless phone sim card is engineered into the Dell Venue, the Dell rep informed me that the Dell engineers originally designed a separate card slot for this purpose, but "in recent models it has been DISCONNECTED!" Which is just about the most nonsensical thing I've heard in a long time.

Several years ago, I worked as a technical telephone support person for Denon home theater systems, and realized at that time that audio and telecommunications engineers frequently make completely mystifying. unnecessarily complicated design decisions, so this was not news to me ....It WAS however, a disappointment that cost the Dell Venue 8 two stars on this review.

That said, the 2GHz processor and Jelly Bean OS are wicked fast for simple gaming, texting (with "My SMS" or other texting apps from Google Play, synched to your Android phone), etc. It can be synchronized via Wi-Fi, USB tether or Bluetooth. It's a nice size (although a little heavy), and makes a very good Kindle-type unit for reading news, books, online magazines, etc. I've decided I like the tablet very much, but would be a LOT happier with if I could get Dell updates and downloads or install a wireless phone card.

title: New competitor to Square Trade?!
text: The two-year protection policy for my Sony shelf stereo unit was only $8, and was easy enough to buy on Amazon along with the unit, so...why not?  As with many service insurance type policies, the proof will be in the repair pudding, when and if necessary.

title: Outstanding sound and value
text:
Although I don't use/have any iOs products, I am glad that this compact shelf stereo unit has a COVER for the iPhone/iPod connector to keep out dust. This is certainly not a mini-unit, but it is small enough to fit a deep shelf. It was easy to set up and program, mostly with the remote that works quite well at about a 40-degree angle to either side. I loaded a USB thumb drive with around 390 music files, all of which are playing flawlessly (mp3 and/or WMA), with a way to shuffle or random play from one artist or from all files.

The different EQ settings could be more varied in tone and effect; however, I'm 67 years old with some mid-range hearing loss, so that might be my fault. The bass response is fine even without the bass boost feature, and vocals, especially high male and women's voices, can seem a little harsh. Volume is fine without distortion, even at enough cranking for me --not sure how it would satisfy a head banger!

My only "like to haves" for this unit include a way to mute the radio or CD playbacks; however, the volume control is very responsive so that's not really a problem for the radio, and one can pause the CD and USB file playback. And of course, I can't imagine what Sony was thinking not including a regular headphone jack.

It's not the most elegant-looking set I've ever owned, but I'm quite satisfied, especially for the cost to value ratio I got on this unit. Very pleased!

title: Electronics can become TOO small...
text:
After a career in advertising, during which I've been around video cameras of all sizes, weights and shapes, this is my first camcorder for personal use. After one day of monkeying around with it, I'm delighted --with a couple of reservations. It appears to be of very good quality, feels lightweight and yet sturdy (with the exception of the rather stringy hand-strap/lanyard) and the user interfacing seems straightforward and intuitive, once you figure out where things are. I'll be back in a few weeks or months to describe my experiences with the software, data downloading and manipulation, etc.

The main criticism I have --more of an observation, really-- is that, for my somewhat arthritic hands, operating the controls are challenging because of their placement on the camera and because the thing is so darned small. (As in the length of a soft drink can --at only 2/3 of the diameter!) This may be simply because I'm unaccustomed to using camcorders, or indeed holding any camera as one does with the JVC GZ-HM550. Many reviewers have complained that this 2010 model still has scrolling and MENU, OK, and INFO buttons rather than Mac-style rolling touch screens. This doesn't bother me, although it takes a very delicate touch to get to the right menu selection on this camera, because they zip by so rapidly under a man's stubby fingers.

Low light results seem more than adequate, especially for daytime indoor shooting, and the shake reduction seems to me to be working very well. The zoom function is smooth and quiet, but --for me-- will be difficult getting used to because the toggle from wide to close-up is at the top rear, where it's difficult for me to reach with my admittedly somewhat inflexible fingers. As I said, I'm new to these mini-cameras, so they may be designed for two-handed use...??

All in all, I think it will be a very good mid-range camcorder with the advisory that people with large hands might find a somewhat physically larger brand/model easier to handle. GET A WARRANTY. (Square Trade offers a good policy against damage, etc.) This JVC model is small enough, the finish glossy enough, that I feel it would be fairly easy to drop it.

title: Works like a charm!
text:
Based on the reviews of these wireless phones, I was concerned that they might not be large enough for my head and neck, and if said head and neck were any larger/thicker, they would likely be too small. (I wear a size 7-1/8 hat and my neck is 16 inches in diameter.) However, they fit fine, and seem nicely comfortable and lightweight. The phones do seem rather delicate, so I'm not sure they'd do well at the bottom of a gym bag or left unprotected in direct sunlight on a hot car seat or dash.

I had no problem charging and pairing the headset with my Samsung Infuse 4G i997. The sound quality is not bad for the price point. I found I had to dial back on the bass settings using my Poweramp player, but the player seems to work well with the phones. I also bought a Kinovo Bluetooth USB adapter for my laptop, but haven't attempted that pairing yet. (Also haven't made or received any phone calls, but music quality and comfort are my primary focus.)

Overall, three hours after receiving the items I'm very happy with the "Kinovo Experience." Will re-post if my opinion changes.

title: Surprisingly good sound REVISED
text:
I just received this Sanjean RCR-10 and set it up. The good news is that the sound is wonderfully rich and balanced for a little radio. First bedside table clock radio I've ever had that sounds good enough to crank up loud to fill my whole apartment with music. I'm impressed, and I'm not easily impressed.

On the other hand, it seems that, the more sophisticated these digital electronics get, the more challenging and puzzling they are to set up. It could well be that these companies need to shell out a little more money for decent technical writers to produce more thorough step-by-step setup instructions. OR, they could simply design the units so they're easier to set up for those of us who are not geeks or electronics engineers. It's not all that terribly frustrating; just be ready for several minutes of trial and error ...and pray you don't have a power outage! (The unit also offers a back-up batteries feature, so I wouldn't forget to do that.)

The RCR-10 is solid, substantial (not flimsy or lightweight) and attractive. The display also includes basic metadata indicating station and artist. The only thing missing for me --since I use an Android phone as my personal music player-- would be a little close-able cover for the empty iPod docking slot. It's going to be a dust collector in my house.

UPDATE: I'm revising my five star review down to three stars, because after a couple of months' use, I've realized this thing is REALLY a pain in the butt to re-progam. Even turning the alarm pre-set volume down a notch requires that you go through a big long procedure, as if you were setting the alarm for the first time. The same thing is true if you think you'd like to awaken to some other type of music station. Hard to do anything on the fly; if you need to make a change, be prepared to sit down for twenty minutes with the OM open for reference to accomplish even the most simple adjustment. Sanjean needs to make these beautiful radios MORE USER FRIENDLY!

title: Fast, compact, dependable
text:
There's not much more to say about this little Patriot Xporter 16GB thumb drive, other than it fulfills all its marketing claims. I had been using an HP thumb drive to back up my work (graphic and text) and found it surprisingly slow, the plastic housing flimsy. This is the second of two Patriot drives I've now purchased, and find them blazingly fast, and very nicely designed. The quality is heartening when there are so many cheap, unnecessarily oversized thumb drives for sale both online and in office supply and big box media stores like Best Buy.

You won't be disappointed with a little Patriot Xporter Rage!

title: Streamlined and versatile
text: I use a small, older Toshiba laptop with a cooling lap desk. I wanted a device that would give me additional USB ports without the clutter of a long cord sticking out to get tangled or a loose-hanging dongle. This notebook hub plugs directly into one of my side USB ports and adds FOUR more, one of which can be adjusted to a different angle.  I added a Patriot XT Rage 16GB stick drive for auto backup of my work files.  Works GREAT for synching my Android phone, etc.  I looked for a long time for precisely this configuration, and I've been Very Pleased with it.

title: Excellent gift idea!
text: After purchasing a larger Logitech cooling pad (with speakers) for my laptop and being very pleased with it, I purchased this N200 as a Christmas gift for a dear friend.  She doesn't spend as much time on computer as I do, but she reports that she really likes how this lightweight, quiet pad "cools down" the computing she was experiencing while working with the notebook directly on her lap. So, I'd conclude from my happy camper's reports that the N200 is all it's cracked up to be!

title: Spent more time buffering than actually streaming music
text:
Everywhere I looked online, there were nothing but the highest words of praise for this radio. It's an attractive, compact unit, with reasonably good sound and lots of options for add ons, additional speakers, usb ports, etc. However, I had such a difficult time getting it to find my home network, I had to completely reconfigure my router (and two computers as a consequence) in order to get the radio to "find" my home network and accept my password key. The enclosed setup instructions are so inadequate that most of the information and procedures required to sign up for services like Pandora, I Heart Radio, Rhapsody, NPR, etc., were completely missing from the manual. The only indications of how to start appeared in the radio's display window, instructing me to go online to do the setup. After some perseverance, I finally figured out how to use the Reciva Internet Radio site to connect the radio with the services I've been using with my computers for years.

Once I finally got the thing to start streaming (about 4 frustrating hours after I began the set up) I realized that, even less than three feet from my router, the unit stayed in buffering mode more than it actually played music, no matter what bps settings I tried. I don't really know much about the technical end of audio streaming, but my MediaLink router works fine with my two portable computers, and streams video and music from services like Pandora and Rhapsody with no glitches whatever. I didn't see much point in listening to 10 seconds of a song, then waiting through 15 or 20 while the unit's memory silently buffered so it could continue.

Even if you're not a digital audio newbie, if you're looking for straightforward setup and easy operation, this AIN'T IT. I may look further into wireless digital radio --but I doubt it, at least not in the near future.

title: Nifty little mouse!!
text:
I purchased this USED-LIKE NEW from a seller who either didn't have or didn't bother to include installation instructions and other materials with the mouse. But I found that the Logitech website [ ] has all the necessary drivers, matched to your Operating System.

Very easy to download to my Windows XP laptop and install. The mini-USB receiver is small enough not to interfere with other USB devices on a row of closely-spaced ports. I like the compact size of the mouse, and I'm planning to buy another one to go with my desktop PC running Vista. Might be too small for the hands of some people with very large hands. Otherwise, what's not to like!

title: Be patient while setting up...
text:
I purchased this router to create a small two-computer network in my apartment. My PC is a refurbished and souped up Gateway running Windows Vista, and I bought an older Toshiba laptop, also refurbished and running Windows XP Home Edition. I wanted to be able to sit in my living room or on the patio while working once in awhile, rather than being chained to my home office PC. No gaming consoles, DVRs, or other components to connect.

The setup literature and accompanying CD shipped with the router are invaluable, easy to understand, even for a non-techie like me. However, don't expect your setup to proceed with no glitches! You may have to reset your cable modem two or three times, or restart the various components two or three times. Take your time, follow directions, keep your wits about you, and think about possible causes and likely solutions and you should have no trouble setting up this router.

The day after my order, I also received a lengthy, substantive email from Mediabridge Products, thanking me for my order and supplying me with all kinds of background, links, and telephone technical support information, so I felt confident that I had resources handy during the setup if necessary. So far the router is working like a charm. I recommend it, especially if you're interested in a fairly simple LAN setup!

title: Amazing value at this price!
text: I'm not a digital photography geek, and I've been working with lower-end Olympus and Canon A-Series Powershot cameras, primarily for static close-up work (for ebay postings). I never found those cameras to be easy to use or at all useful for on-the-fly, outdoor shooting.  With little or no absorption of the Panasonic DCM-FZ35 owner's manual, I've been able to shoot some really nice outdoor snapshots using both the LCD and the viewfinder. The various settings are almost fun to find and experiment with on the DCM-FZ35's display.  Overall, an exciting lower-to-mid range camera for amateurs who can't afford a DSLR!  I LIKE IT!!

title: TERRIBLE picture quality and mediocre design
text:
I purchased this player as a replacement because I clumsily killed my Toshiba SD-P1900 9" player. I figured, even with a half-inch loss of screen size, I'd still be in the game, right? Panasonic's a great brand name, right? WRONG.

This particular Panasonic model not only has lousy picture quality and no remote, but there are no fast forward or fast rewind functions other than skipping all the way ahead or all the way back to the beginnings of scenes. I'm a film buff, so I like to be able to back up two or three seconds to check out that explosion in fps detail, or to move forward or backward at 2X or 4X or 8X, etc. Plus, if you extend the adjustable screen forward as shown in most illustrations, you cannot see or reach the control buttons without moving it out of your way.

I'm no video product engineer, but I hope my impression of the VERY inadequate picture quality and overall poor design of this player makes you think twice. Go for the Toshiba instead!

title: Not intended to be a computer monitor.
text: I was hugely disappointed when the first one that arrived had a shattered screen. I didn't have my hopes up when I hit the replace button, but the second one came and the screen is fine. I now have it mounted on my wall next to my primary monitor. One strange quirk is that my universal remote turns both of my TVs on and off with one button. With this TV, I have an additional step of selecting what it's to be used for from the main menu before it's ready to go. Overall, it's lightweight and the design is fairly clean looking.

title: MUCH faster loading!
text: I have two of these drives in my computer now. One for the operating system and "work" type applications and the other for my games. Everything stored on these drives loads a great deal faster than any of the things stored on my SSD. If you can only get your hands on one of these, I recommend using it for your OS and the programs you'll spend the most time on.

title: Not an upgrade from M570 for me.
text: I was looking to upgrade my gaming mouse. I was excited to try this one, but when I got it plugged in, there were two things that immediately upset me. First, it didn't use the Logitech SetPoint software all my other Logitech devices have used for many, many years. Instead, I had to install a new software to customize the buttons. Second, the mouse acceleration I've become accustomed to was eliminated from this mouse in the software. In its place, they added a "precision mode" button that required me to take my thumb off the trackball to toggle between fast movement and slow movement. As a gamer, this is unacceptable. I loved everything else about this mouse, but it didn't work for me, since my primary use is gaming.

title: NOT for people with astigmatism!
text: I have astigmatism, so for me, it was impossible to "dial in" either lens for a good viewing experience, let alone both. I was really excited to try it and very sad it didn't work for me.

title: NOT for gaming.
text: The extra buttons (back and forward) are in an awkward place. For me, that meant I could either be using those or the ball. As a mouse for things like browsing the web, checking email, watching movies, etc. it wasn't bad. It just isn't laid out to make an effective gaming mouse.

title: NOT FOR GAMING!!!
text:
Initially, I liked the ergonomic design. It put much less pressure on my wrist than the Logitech trackball I've been using for many years. Unfortunately, when I started up World of Warcraft, I noticed the Kensington trackball button mapping software disabled the ability to use more than one button at once. I found the same detriment in Overwatch where multiple buttons often need to be pressed simultaneously. When I contacted the company, they sent me an email. The following is a direct quote from their email:
"Thank you for contacting Kensington Technical Support.

We would like to inform you that these trackballs are designed for basic office use and will not work on gaming applications.

We appreciate your time and patience."

To me, this came across as rather rude. This, coupled with the fact that this very mouse shows up in searches for gaming trackball mouse made me extremely disappointed and, in fact, somewhat angry. I feel Kensington needs to do any or all of the following. 1. Fix the software to make their hardware gaming inclusive. 2. Stop advertising their non-gaming devices as gaming devices (I feel this is blatant false advertising.) 3. Ask customers how they could fix issues rather than giving them a short, curt email to inform us that we, apparently, are idiots for expecting their devices to work as advertised.

text: Bought this extension cord for use while traveling. Last ship we were on had only 1 outlet in the stateroom and I recently started using a cPap machine. title: Finally getting rid of the ziploc bag

title: Very Protective
text: I bought this as the replacement for the original cover I bought when purchasing the iPad new 4+ years ago.  This is the exact cover as the first one because of how well it protected my iPad. Over the years, I have dropped the tablet a few times, and the cover has protected it completely. As a matter of fact, my tablet looks new coming our of the cover when placing in the new one.  The sleep function does not work for me, but it does not matter to me, so no problems.  I just us the button on the tablet. title: A good computer, after some tweaking

But because it's a model from 2016, it did require a Google search and a visit to the HP support website for a BIOS update for the computer to recognize the latest Windows 10 updates, and the computer also required an update there to fix a VCRUNTIME140.dll error. I also kept getting an error message requiring an update to HP 3D DriveGuard after the latest Windows 10 updates. In other words, expect to do some tinkering with your computer to get this refurb up and running properly. (One other little thing: When Amazon shipped the laptop, they overlooked removing from the box the original owner's receipt from a well-known national department store chain, which showed that buyer paid about $80 less for this laptop than I did as a refurb.)

To get it to work, I plugged into USB port with ethernet cable. Then to get the TV to stop using the Wi-Fi connection, I reset wireless network and left it blank in settings. title: Great tablet... TERRIBLE keyboard/case
text:
The tablet is quite good. A real improvement over previous models.

While the concept of a dex keyboard is nice, this execution is lacking if you want to use it as BOTH a tablet and laptop alternative. Moving around will cause the keyboard to attach and detach quickly, which will in turn cause the tablet to go to sleep. The placement of the pen holder makes is absolutely certain that thing will be gone within a day or so.

The price for what you get here is outrageous. It is a cheap case and cheap keyboard, stuck together.

If you are ONLY going to use this as a laptop and NEVER a tablet, this might work, but you can still find alternatives for 1/4 the price. If you plan to interchange use... don't buy this.

title: Protection and Functionality
text:
This cover is actually perfect in so many ways, to protect the tablet from the tough use my 6 yr old son gives it. He has had this tablet for nearly 2 years, and I think after the previous demise of several other tablets, he may have actually learned not to drop it, so I can't say how well this case would have fared in his 4 yr old hands, for protection of the tablet, but so far...so good, for now.

The grooves are deep enough to actually hold the tablet up, unlike other cases. The strap that closes it, for transporting is great, because it assures that the cover doesn't fall open and expose the tablet to a direct/unprotected fall. All the cut-outs are where they should be, but the negative, if there is one, is that the power cord has to be positioned just right to get the proper contact for charging, and the portion where you put the tablet isn't snug enough to keep it from obstructing camera, without constant adjustment, and it may even get worse with wear.

title: Doesn't Stay Plugged in Most Devices - Not Comfortable
text:
I purchased this for my son, to replace his previous headphones, because he had nibbled through the cord sheathing. I liked that this was cheaper, cute, and had one wire off one of the ear pieces, instead of the kind that look like a necklace that come from each ear and rest on your chest. I started using these headphones on his E-Reader and it just doesn't stay plugged in, because the L-shaped plug doesn't allow it to go in far enough, and it easily pulls/falls out. Now, I am going to go buy the slightly more expensive, but much better quality Kidz Gear headphones. I couldn't have known that this was really going to be an issue, until I got them, so I just wanted to help let others know.

My son, today, after using the headphones for the first time of more than 20 minutes, he declared, "These are hurting me." So, my four year old would like to add that to this review, as well. He was always really comfortable in the other headphones, even able to fall asleep with them on (even though they look bulky, they were even comfortable to me).

title: Kind of the gold standard on Earbuds when used with Apple Macs/iPhones/iPads
text: The Apple AirPods Pro are a definite step up from the regular AirPods, stay in your ears well (the Beats Fit Pro does slightly better here, but the microphone is not as good as on the AirPods Pro), have good noise cancellation (Bose and Sony might be a tad better, but these are very good), and excellent microphone pickup.  If you are going to be in a loot of phone calls, eMeetings (Zoom, Webex, Facetime, etc.) these are very much the ones to get.  About the only thing these are not good for would be high head movement activities (athletics), there the Beats Fit Pro does better, but these are on a par or better than the competitive Sony or Bose variants (which are larger, so easier to dislodge).  Also, once paired with Apple devices, you can just move them around to be used with whatever you happen to be doing, iPad or iPhone or MacBook, they autoswitch, don't have to be re-paired, and also handle Siri commands.

title: Decent Kindle Oasis case at a great price

The texture on the MoKo case makes it extremely easy to carry and hold onto, you are unlikely to have it slip and drop the e-reader.  Protection appears to be top notch.  The case has the further advantage of being able to fold and sit on a table or desk such that you can read easily.  I would have given this five stars, if the magnets had been just a little stronger.  They are adequate and work, in terms of the e-reader turning off and on, but you have to get the alignment just right in terms of the stand function.  Still, at the price, this case is hard to beat.  A great value.

title: One of the best cases for an iPad Air, particularly if you have apps that run in Portrait mode
text: The rooCASE Oragami Case seems to be currently at or near the top of the cases, the big advantage of this case being the number and variations of orientations, including both portrait and landscape, and at the price point, is hard to beat.  The oragami cover is ingenious, you can fold it up all sorts of ways, the iPad Air has a lot of applications that fairly beg for portrait orientation (reading a book, newspaper, etc.).  The conventional Apple case supports only landscape, as do a number of competitors (the CaseCrown Omni is one of the better conventional ones).  The Moshi and O!Case are also oragami cases, although the designs differ some.  The rooCASE has a more rubberized or grippy exterior, key because it's less likely to slip and get dropped.  Protection is generally pretty good, but the CaseCrown does a little better on edge protection, the openings on the rooCase tend to be U-shaped, the CaseCrown is more O-Shaped, but otherwise they are very similar.  The Moshi has one advantage, in that it has a back magnet, that lets it stay open better in book mode.  The rooCASE actually has magnets that keep it closed pretty well, but it lacks a back magnet.  The rooCase front cover of course folds up to support quite a number of variations or angles, which is a big advantage over conventional cases, and on a desk or table, is plenty stable.  The microfiber front interior is nice, it tends to help keep the screen clean, but it is worth noting that the orgami pattern tends to show up in the fingerprints and grease, so you do need to clean the screen from time to time.  rooCASE also shuts off the iPad Air screen when you close it, a very useful feature.  The end result is still pretty light and easy to carry, in keeping with the iPad Air design point.  Why not 5 stars?  rooCase is very close, but they could improve the edge coverage/protection, and add a back magnet (ala Moshi), and NuGuard KX probably has the better back protection (at the cost of some bulk), but at its price-point, front and back protection, oragami design that lets you pick multiple orientations and angles, the rooCASE is pretty much unbeatable, and worthy of consideration at any price.

title: Works with MacBook Pro Thunderbolt and DisplayPort Monitors
text: The Monoprice Mini DisplayPort Male is an adapter that has worked well for me, I keep it with the various adapters you need when traveling with an Apple MacBook Pro.  It's fairly simple in operation, one end plugs into a full size Displayport cable (for a Monitor or Projector), and you plug the smaller end then into the MacBook or other computer with a Thunderbolt or Mini DisplayPort port.  We have a fair number of projectors and older large displays around the place, and you run into them also when traveling to other companies, this lets you jack into them.  The Apple senses the connection, figures out the resolution of the external monitor, and you're off and running.  And the price is really quite good, nice little item for the laptop bag.

title: Good Soft Sided Camera case (for Canon IS800)
text: This is actually a pretty good little case, sized nicely for the Canon Powershot line.  Tamrac has always been one of the better names in the business, in terms of Camera bags.  This one seems to be no exception.  Everything seems pretty well protected, maybe the material could be a bit thicker/more protective on the side, but in general this seems much more protective then the standard Canon leather cases.  Construction is very good, no signs of sewing or other finish problems.  Inside of the case seems soft enough, maybe not quite as good there as the Lowepro's, but reasonable.  Flap closure is velcro, lots of it, so that's held securely.  I doubt very much a camera is going to fall out.  On the other hand, you'll never "sneak" this camera out for a camera shot, as it makes the standard velcro ripping sound.  If you use the wrist strap on the camera, that can just go out the side or be  left at the top of the case.  Belt loop on the back seems very secure, again lots of velcro, and oversized  (maybe 3.5 inch or so).  Doesn't seem to scratch the belt.  Room for a flash card, but probably not an extra battery, but that seems consistent with the small form-factor of the camera.  Overall, quite a nice little camera case.

title: They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can contro
text:
This review is for the Uniden BCD436HP I see reviews here for other radios, so not to be confused.
I used Amazon Prime Now to get the radio to me, in less than 1 hour (about 45 minutes) the delivery person was knocking on my door with my new receiver, wow, I was highly impressed and I will always check to see if Prime Now is available for all my deliveries from now on.....
So, the radio....
This receiver has a 4 gig SD card preloaded with every known frequency with text for the entire US and Canada. They have software called Sentinel you install on your PC and this is your gateway to all updates and firmware and it can control your radios SD card any way you like. Sentinel has an extensive database of all frequencies and let me say this again, all frequencies have text description included which is the most highly advanced scanner database system I have ever seen and I have owned scanner receivers most of my adult life, (long time)..
This is a digital receiver using the latest technology available. It can monitor any analog or digital TX (with some exceptions, like encrypted signals) and gives you extensive control over what you're listening to. There are FCC laws regarding what is legal and not legal to monitor and Uniden has got us right up to the maximum legally allowed to be monitored by civilians. If you are law enforcement persons you will have much more powerful receivers available to you capable of Cell phone conversation monitoring etc., things no civilian should even be interested in.
There is another version of this Uniden radio, the BCD536 which is a tabletop version. If you have large powerful outdoor weatherproof antennas the BCD536 is a good option and it is completely transferable to vehicle dash mount and back from your work desk to your vehicle.
I like this handheld BCD436 best personally for my purposes.
This is basically a plug and play receiver. It comes with 3 2300 milliamp rechargeable batteries, load those, charge them or just leave radio plugged in, enter your zip and you're in. Well theoretically that's how it works, in the real world? No.
When you first receive the radio I would suggest positioning yourself in front of your PC. Have the paper manual, the radio, you and your PC right there in front of you. Get ready to read and learn your radios keyboard layout and what these great, well thought out keys can do for you. You will learn, trust me, you will quickly come to love this radio.
Some cons:
No wall charger adopter included. You can charge from your PC's USB ports but you will need a wall charger with USB port. Most of us have several of these around the house from old cell phones etc. They work fine.
This unit should come with a nice wall charger adopter. That's really the only con, not to bad really.
Antennas:
Your ability to scan and receive signals on any scanner is proportionate to your antennas. The more robust and correct (correct meaning size, materials used etc).. You will need some nice antennas for this nice radio to increase your scanning powers. Amazon has some nice antennas, scannermaster.com has some also. Your local radio shop retailer will have some also. The included rubber ducky antenna is garbage, toss it from across the room to your garbage can, see if you can make a rim shot. Like I said, I have been playing with scanners for many years so I have many antennas to pick from.
Verdict:
This is without a doubt, the most powerful handheld scanning receiver available from any manufacturer. It is the luxury sedan of the scanning receiver world. It is easy and robust. It is backed up by Uniden's Sentinel software which will future proof your radio for many years to come.
I give Uniden 5 stars for this winner.
I give Amazon 5 stars for Prime Now 1 hour shipping, also a winner.

Edit:
Okay some people are wondering what the best accessories are for this receiver.
Go to scannermaster.com and look for the Austin Condor All-Band Portable BNC Antenna and the SpectrumForce Desk Mount for One Portable Scanner.
The Condor all band antenna is unsurpassed.
The desktop stand holds your handheld at the perfect viewing angle, you can listen and see all text clearly right beside your computer.
See my photos. The photos ended up sideways.... trying to fix this..... Amazon, can you turn my photos upright?

title: Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between ...
text:
I received this cooler today and installed it along with two new 140mm front panel case fans.
I have an AMD based system running stock cooling that came with the case and hardware components.
My system temps running stock cooling were way to high, idyling at temps around 45c to 50c and when running
demanding applications temps would shoot way up into the 80's and 90's sometimes causing shutdowns.
I kept remembering statements from AMD advising consumers to keep the down blowing fans installed but I decided
to try a liquid cooling solution out of desperation.

My case is a Corsair Spec 02.
My motherboard is a Asus Sabertooth 990FX R2.0.
The processor is a AMD FX-8320.
The graphics processor is a Sapphire Radeon R9 380.
That AMD FX 8320 runs hot, extremely hot also the NB and SB components on the Asus MB run very hot.
My system temps were way to high, I had to do something.

Installation of the Corsair H80i V2 wasn't easy in this smallish case but the radiator sandwiched between
the two 120mm fans does fit in this case. I followed the manufacturer recommendation and configured both
fans to push air inward into the case. This case has perforated holes in the roof for ventilation and this
allows used air to evacuate out of the case assuming the fans are configured to blow inward which will push
air out those top vents.
The two big 140mm red LED fans I installed in the front panel are configured to pull air inward and I set them
to run at 100% speed (1000 RPM), they are Cougar Red LED's, very high quality fans that move a lot of air
silently.

This Corsair H80i V2 has got to be the best liquid cooler available for smaller cases like mine, it has dropped
my system temps by 20 to 30 degrees C instantly. I am seeing system temps lower than I've ever seen them since
I built the system back in December 2015.

This fridge is rocking my system. Cool is good, the cooler the better when it comes to computer systems. I have
Core Temp 1.0 RC6 installed and it is showing my CPU temps idling at 13C - 15C... That is chill.

Chill is good.

Thanks Corsair, this liquid cooler system is awesome.
Thanks Amazon for the excellent service and thanks UPS for being the most dependable carrier on earth.
My system purrs away at 15C, OMG this is awesome.

title: Astounding powers........
text:
Install this on your compatible motherboard and you will think you have installed the heart of Superman in your computer.
I am in awe of this prodigy of modern computer technology.
Edit:
I've had this processor running in my new build for about a month now. I was being annoyed by the stock cooler fan buzzing at very high rpm whenever the heat rose to moderate levels like 52C. The fan was really buzzing like a little aircraft prop at full throttle for takeoff. It would crank up to 6600 rpm at the slightest provocation like CPU temp hitting 50C.
I decided to take everything apart down to the motherboard coming out and all components attached to it.
When I pulled the cooler off the CPU and looked at the thermal paste situation, OMG what a mess. The stock thermal paste was not covering the whole area, it was reduced to a gummy, sticky glue. I had to pull very hard to get the cooler off the CPU.
I cleaned the cooler base and the CPU thoroughly and applied a pea sized spot of Arctic Silver 5 then reassembled everything.
Instant cure. Instant quieter fan. Instant low CPU temps andQUIET!AMD needs to stop using whatever they're putting on the coolers and just include a syringe of a high quality thermal paste for customers to apply themselves because whatever they're using is junk.
The stock cooler and fan they include with the fx 8320 are very high quality but the pre applied thermal paste is garbage.
Just apply new first quality thermal paste, you don't need to spend big dollars on third party hardware and I suspect those of you who have installed new coolers and seen great results is because of the new thermal paste used during installation.
The fx 8320 is a very powerful processor don't smoke it because of 10 cents worth of cheap thermal paste, use the best for your investment and this hot CPU will give many years of great performance.

Check the specs, check your equipment, check your needs like the size of your space you plan to use this player in and check your expectations: maybe you need a more powerful device. For a modest user like myself, this is a very satisfying device. It rocks my equipment and my expectations.
Gus,
Portland, Oregon

title: Not great
text: I received my Fire on Dec 31st 2011 as a B-day gift.  I was thrilled! Sadly, my elation was short-lived. Less than five months later I had blown pixels in the display and had to have a replacement.  Before you assume I'm a careless person with my 'toys' - I'm not, just the opposite in fact. I received my replacement Fire, reloaded all the stuff I needed and went on my merry way, sure that I would use it until I wanted to upgrade - NOT SO!  About three months later, I was again on the phone with a service rep explaining that the charging port was loose and the unit no longer charged. So, I am on my THIRD Fire.  A few days into my third Fire, literally, I had to call and get a new charger, as the one they sent only charged for about 30 seconds at a time and that was it.  My complaint is that Amazon is selling poor quality electronics and I was nothing more than their guinea pig and I don't appreciate it at all!  I will NEVER buy another Kindle of any kind.  To be fair, Amazon's customer service, for the most part, throughout this ordeal has been acceptable to good, but my gift was not Amazon's customer service!  I have no reason to believe that Amazon's latest and greatest are better tested or higher quality than their last series.  Not happy!

text:
I bought this specifically to use with 2 new machines that have 8.1 on them. Unfortunately it stops moving data randomly for as much as 2 minutes.

I did my due diligence - swap computers (with Windows 7 and 8.1), drives (various usb 3.0 on the same 8.1 machines), cables, enclosures. The only thing that's consistent is that this specific enclosure hates Windows 8.1. All other combinations work fine.

I have to directly connect my keys vid and mouse for a few days, try it again, and it might start working. It's proven to be very unreliable.

title: Very happy with it
text: I bought this tv to use as the monitor on my gaming pc (and to watch movies and play games on a ps3). I sit about 44 inches from it, just far enough away to not see the pixels. I must say, even at that close it is absolutely amazing. Very bright, decent black levels. Great clarity even on text. I wouldn't say the picture is as good as my 50" plasma, but it's darn close. (and I wasn't about to use a plasma as a gaming monitor; too bright, too hot, and too hard on the plasma) I only see the bizarre backlighting pattern when the screen is all black. Also only got one stuck-red pixel, which could have been worse I suppose. TV is surprisingly light. Had no trouble lifting it up on the table and carrying it around the house by myself. Definitely a worthy purchase. I couldn't stop laffing like an evil lunatic when I fired up Crysis on it.

Moral of the story do not let non-IT professionals buy hardware for your organization.

title: Segate Green 2TB hard drive
text: This drive is working great as my new larger OS drive. This drive was packaged well and that is what makes the greatest difference in hard drive purchases. If the drive is sloshing around in an over sized box and getting rough treatment by the delivery service usually means that is is going to fail. The heads on the drive mechanism are not designed to treated harshly. Thanks Amazon for the great packing!

title: StarTech USB3 External Enclosure
text: I have been using this for three months now and this product is great. It was easy installing a hard drive and my Windows 7 system recognized the device as soon as I plugged it into the USB3 port on my machine. I actually bought another one because the first one worked so well.

title: USB Ports dis-functional
text: The USB3 chipset is seen by the system and the drivers were installed successfully but the two USB3 ports are dis-functional. Wast of money as far as I am concerned. Bought a USB3 external drive that works fine on my other system which has USB3 on the motherboard. Installed the card into my game system and neither USB port works on this card.

text: This replaces an older version of this mouse and I like the feel of the new one much better. It is a lot more responsive and it installed seamlessly. I really liked the very small USB wireless adapter.

title: Died within 3 months then ASUS STOLE MY BOX!
text:
Before this monitor was 3 months old it failed and I had to pay 55 dollars to send it in for repair. I double boxed it like the way it was from amazon, the factory box inside a larger amazon box. They kept both of them and returned it in much smaller generic box with no foam packing, no logos, nothing to affirm ownership of a quality product. I always keep the boxes for the larger, nice things I buy which is why I had this one to send the junk monitor back in. Then they kept it. Since I had to buy another monitor while this thing was being fixed I thought I'd sell this one when it got back. Doesn't seem to be worth as much without the original box.

Having used asus products before I was hesitant to give them another chance and unfortunately my doubts were right on. I fully expect this monitor to fail again before it becomes dated and I won't bother having it fixed again. Do yourself a favor and avoid asus like the plague. Everything they sell is below average and they are not an honest company.

text: Nothing special but at 4 bucks well worth it.  These are not 4 pin and are quite loud at full speed.  I doubt I will buy more, I do prefer the higher quality fans available.

title: Disappointed - Don't waste your money on this thing
text:
I've had this less than 3 months and the paint has already worn off some of the keys. Given the price I expected better. I won't be buying any more CM products.

Update: Now the cable is being flaky. Why would you want the main cable to plug into the keyboard instead of being hard wired? Every time I move the keyboard or bump the cable it shorts out, the keyboard resets and takes 30 seconds for the software to reconfigure.

There is no way this keyboard is worth the price. Buy something else.

Update 2: Now, just about 2 hours after my previous update the cable connection has become so bad the keyboard is unusable. What a waste of a money. CM should get into a different business and stop ripping people off. 100 bucks down the drain.

title: Love this card!
text: I almost always buy MSI video cards and motherboards but this is by far the nicest video card I've owned.  It immediately pushed my Win 7 graphics performance to 7.9 and runs my dual HD monitors at max settings on every game I've tried.  I do admit though I'm not big on first person shooter games so I haven't tried it a lot with those, but for the games I do play it's great.  I have one game which uses over 75% of the 2gb of video ram and it runs as smoothly as any other.  I also love that it overclocks by itself. I can watch the speed change as it needs to; much better than having the card overclocked all the time.  Now I'm saving up for a 2nd one!

title: I like it
text: For the price I think this is a fine lighted keyboard.  The key switches feel good to type on and the color lights up the letters well.  It obviously doesn't have fancy mechanical switches but I've used more expensive keyboards that did not feel as good.  The shiny piano black is really sharp and attractive.

title: Great features at a reasonable price
text:
I am very pleased with this monitor. As others have mentioned, the stand is great. Sometimes I sit up while using the computer, other times I lean back and this stand makes it very easy to get the perfect view no matter my position. I also like the onscreen menus which are controlled by buttons on the side. I find that much easier to use than the little pivot button some monitors have. And, unlike some monitors which are labeled 24 inch but are really only 23.6, this one is actually 24 diagonal inches.

I love it and based on this monitor, BenQ is now my brand of choice.

title: Shorter Than Expected

title: Very Nice
text:
This power supply came nicely packaged and looks great. It feels and looks solid and I rest easy knowing it is powering my computer. The only con I can think of is I don't care for the sata connector wires, they are flat and rather stiff cables instead of being pliable and wrapped.

Update: After just moving my drives around and installing a couple new ones I loath the sata power cables included with this. They are too stiff and the connectors are upside down for a bottom mounted power supply. Using extension/splitters was the only way to get power to all of my drives. At this point I very much regret buying this thing and certainly won't buy another. If you only have 1 or 2 hard drives it's no problem, but if you have a bunch of drives, it will be a nightmare. Find something with more pliable and correctly oriented sata leads.

title: Yes, it works with Windows 7
text:
It also works with Harmony remotes. It just doesn't do anything especially well. But for 7 bucks I don't see how anyone can complain. I took C. Watson's advice and set it up in my harmony software with the model he suggested and then did a little personal tweaking and it works fine, not perfect, but good enough. Having tried over the years numerous hand held mouse controllers I have found them all hard to use and unreliable. This one is probably the worst but then I don't use it to control the mouse pointer, just to control media player; pause, play, next, previous, full screen or not and mute. For these functions it is adequate and I don't regret buying it.

For those who need and want full mouse functionality from a remote control, this is sure to disappoint. But for those with needs similar to mine, this is a reasonable choice.

title: Mine had a problem, will be returning it
text:
This card is exactly what I wanted, small with low power requirements. I used it in a home theater computer and it played every HD movie I tested smoothly and cleanly. The problem is there is something funny with it's temperatures. At first it was fine, running 42 to 53 degrees but then on the 3rd day I turned it off to install a network card and burned myself on the video card's heat sink. When I had the computer back up and running I checked the video card's temperature and it was idling at 103 degrees, Celsius. I let it run for a few more minutes while I installed Evga's precision software to verify that temp and it agreed with hwmonitor. I shut it down. A couple hours later I brought it up again, this time it was idling at 63 degrees and didn't vary much from that temp for the next several hours. The next day it was up in the eighties and then again nineties. Today it stayed around 71.

I really don't have a good idea what is wrong with it and I'm not going to spend anymore time worrying about it for a brand new card. It's going back.

title: Impressive
text:
I have put together many, many computers using cases of all shapes, sizes and costs. Dollar for dollar this case is hands down the best value I've ever seen. As others have noted the materials are a bit flimsy but this is a computer case, not the frame for a tank. As long as it isn't abused it should last and give good service for years. And I like that is fairly light weight, many cases that are "sturdy" are also on the heavy side. By the time you have them loaded with a good power supply and several hard drives they begin to feel like a tank when you need to move them.

The cutouts and gaps to make routing cables easy are nice, they not only improve the appearance but also help air flow freely through the case. I was a little worried about sharp edges but have not found any, which is good because knowing me if there was even one I would have cut myself on it.

I read several reviews which mention the hard drive rails being difficult and backwards so I wasn't sure what to expect. At first I was a little confused about how the hard drives are meant to be installed but once I understood it, it makes perfect sense and is no problem to work with. If you have right angled power and data cable ends you can mount the drives facing left or right which might make things easier if you have several drives installed.

Another thing that both surprised and pleased me was when I was installing the power supply I noticed there were two extra holes which makes it possible to mount the ps either right side up or upside down. I am not a huge fan of bottom mount for power supplies and as others have said, it can cause problems if the leads for motherboard power are not long enough. Mine just barely reached to the cpu power connector after running it up the rear of the case, resting as it is on the motherboard and running under the video card. I have extensions on order though I'm sure I could get by for the life of the ps as it is now.

I like the long, thin blue light on the front for power on though the green light for hard drive activity is a bit hard to see. Most of all though, I love the paint. No more of that ugly, dingy looking gray metal with thoughts of how I want to paint it black. I am not an expert on such things but I believe the paint is baked on giving it a very nice texture and appearance.

This is a case I would not have been disappointed by if I had paid 60 dollars. Getting it from amazon for 36 with free prime shipping is one of the best deals I've ever found.

Three cheers to NZXT !!!

title: Very Pleased
text:
I bought this to sit on top of my i5-2500K and I couldn't be happier. I love the way it looks through the case's side window and it is so quiet and smooth. I don't believe in "burn-in" or "stress" testing but would expect core temps to near or pass 80c during such tests.

I also love that it is from Intel - who better than them to know what their processors need?

I would recommend this fan to all except possibly severe gamers who need every bit of cooling they can get.

title: Great Hard Drive
text:
I have 9 or 10 Hitachi 1 tb drives and am very pleased with them. They may not be the fastest or quietest drives in the world, though I never hear them and they seem plenty fast to me, but in two years the only one I've had fail had been improperly packaged by amazon and was beat to death in shipping. I am currently using a pair of these in my main computer in a raid array. Using raid 0 on the first array partition, to boot from, and raid 1 on the 2nd for mirroring.

Before I started using hitachi drives I was losing a wd or seagate roughly every other month. It was all I could do to keep up with the rma's and I completely lost track of how much data I'd lost. I should note I have approximately 20 hard drives spread over 5 computers. With the size of modern hard drives an effective backup method is very hard to achieve. Few people can afford tape drive backups for home, I certainly can't and dvdrw disk simply do not hold enough to be cost or time effective. After so many wd and seagate crashes I have begun using many drives simply for mirroring and I am pleased that with the hitachi drives I have not lost a single byte.

As long as they keep making them at the current quality level, I will keep buying them.

title: Nice earbuds but I decided swapped them out for Bose QuietComfort earbuds
text:
I went on the search for a set of ear buds that would stay in my ears better than my Airpod Pros but with the same level of Noise cancellation. It seemed like the Sony WF-1000XM4 and Bose Quietcomfort earbuds were the top picks in this space. After a lot of research i went with the Sony earbuds. Besides their sound and level of ANC. i liked the fact the Sony earbuds still had a lot of playback control available from the earbuds and you can use either earbud individually. I also felt like the fact that they sit in your ear canal rather than on the outside would contribute to the noise cancellation.

The earbuds felt and sound good and the accompanying app was nice but the case had a cheap, almost cardboard feel. My main issues were, although the earbuds never actually fell out of my ear, I think their top-heavy design made them feel like they were always about to fall out. The bigger issue i had, which won't apply to everyone, is how much effort went into getting them to sit correctly in my ear. Even with twisting, and pushing, I could never get the right earbud to fit securely in my ear like the left one did.

After a day of wearing the Sonys i decided to pick up a pair of Bose Quietcomfort ear buds as i already had a pair of Quietcomfort 35 over the ears that i loved, i figured I'd give Bose another shot. As soon as i opened the Bose, I immediately fell in love. Besides the unboxing and charging case feeling more premium, the earbuds went into my ear effortlessly and securely. I wore them the first day and they stayed in place all day and sounded great.

Although the Sony WF-1000XM4 is a great set of earbuds, The Bose earbuds have the same functionality, sound and ANC but are designed in a way to comfortably fit a wider array of ear shapes and at a cheaper price. The Sonys are going back and the Bose are going to be my new day-to-day earbuds.

title: Just WOW!!
text: Cut the cord with cable 2 days ago but wanted local channel access. Streaming services are nice but you are forever going from one platform to another to channel surf which I find super frustrating. Good old tv with antenna is so much easier. This antenna took less than 5 minutes to set up. I put it up in the window. Channel scanned and was watching 43 channels like that! All crystal clear pictures. I must say that most towers are about 40 miles away from my home ,all kinda clustered together. They sit southeast of me and where I have the antenna sitting is close to southeasterly. Kind of a no brainer but I would suggest looking up tower locations  in your area. The map will display channels broadcast by this tower... and try to configure your antenna in that general direction. Makes sense to me. Very pleased with this antenna and purchase. Cut the cord with cable. You won't be disappointed :) UPDATE: This is an indoor antenna and they work best in a window and pointed towards the transmission towers in your area. You will get max channels that way. That's been my experience but I opted to use the double stick tape provided and mount mine outside taped to a beam on my metal pergola. Channel availability jumped up immediately upon rescanning so outdoor antennas are the way to go...and yes this is not truly recommended for outdoor use.. I went from 36 channels inside to 55 mounted outside the same window..3 months and I have had no issues with outside use. It hasn't fallen once..the weather has been all over the map..from sunny, rainy, and even the current blizzard conditions we have experienced...that includes rain, freezing rain, and snow. Maybe it will crap out over time but I paid 15 bucks for over 50channels. If it lasts a year thats only $1.25 a month to watch tv which is hella lot cheaper than cable. I'm super satisfied!!

title: Acer gets 5 stars....Amazon gets a zillion.
text:
I did a little homework and this machine, especially at the price looked excellent. I noticed in reading Amazon reviews that a small percentage of buyers had received machines with faulty screens. So I went to BestBuy to see what they had, and found nothing appealing in any where near this price. So I ordered one. It arrived on Wednesday (days matter in this little story). Knowing there was a slight risk, I opened everything very carefully, saved everything in case I'd want to return it. Sure enough I got one with a faulty screen. However I'd also calculated the odds: very slim chance of getting two in a row. Thursday we started what I thought was likely to be a tricky, time consuming effort: filling forms, emails, getting to UPS, etc etc. It went like this: one click to get to the trade request on the Amazon order, five minutes to complete it ....Including a stunning question: did I want to drop the first one at UPS, or have them pick it up at my door? UPS would have the prepaid return label with them.
Then they shipped the replacement to me Thursday. SAME DAY! Monday the new one arrived, the man had the return label in his hand.He took one look at my shipping ready packaged box, slapped the label on, and left while I watched still in disbelief. This is way beyond 5 stars for Amazon.

And true to the odds, this machine I'm using for this is flawless. I love it. It's everything it is advertised to be, and more. The slowness some mentioned was easily remedied for my use by clearing the "Start Up", using Blackle as a homepage, and one click to change the "Next Window" screen. I don't play complex games, just puzzles, solitaire and the like so no need for speed there. Pictures, movies and TV are all beautiful, and quick to load.

The Windows 10 Home is surprisingly user friendly...and I'm 72. The machine runs cool, easy to upgrade, and most of all: affordable. So don't be afraid to take a chance if you're waffling. Thank you Amazon! Very much.

title: Locks up frequently
text: I've owned & used several  DVD and Blu-ray players over the last 20 years--some were Sony--but this X700 unit is the worst.  The picture is pretty good--when it works--but too often I cannot finish playing a 4K movie Blu-ray before it stutters and then stops. After that, the only way to get it going again is to unplug the player, wait a minute, then plug it back in... which is what Sony Help Line said to do, but is intolerable.  Unit also will not detect Dolby Vision discs; you must know the disc is so encoded, then manually activate that feature, THEN manually de-activate it after the movie is over!  I applied all online updates, yet none fixed these issues. Returned the player for refund, as it is a not something I want to struggle with for another minute--no matter how inexpensive it is or how good the picture is (when working).

title: Solves a problem
text: I can now charge my iPhone on any of my "old"(pre-Lifeproof case) chargers. It fits well in the case, and stays put--it doesn't come off until I take it off, so I don't have to worry about it falling off or leaving it behind when I undock. The only thing I find mildly in convenient is when I dock it on my alarm clock charger, my phone leans back and it feels as if it may fall--easily solved by making sure it's leaning against the wall behind it. I am so glad I no longer have to pop my lifecase off anytime I need to charge my phone or listen to the music. While this tool is wonderful, I don't understand why it must be purchased seperately, it should come with case, just like the headphone adapter.

text: This is the 2nd unit I've purchased. the first one I bought over a year ago has worked so well, I bought the 2nd one for the cabin. It has better AM & FM reception than 3 other radios I've tried there. The solar charger panel works well, as does the flashlight. I don't use the SW at all yet, and no wx channel reception where I am in the mountains in Alaska. Even so, it's a great unit for the price.

text: Upgraded from an older HD6. It's lighter, brighter and has a SD slot for more storage. I was very surprised to find out it has less battery life than the 4 year old kindle. I've tried to use every battery/power saving option possible, but it still drains after several hours of simple reading of books or pdf files. Will continue to attempt to improve the battery life and see if it will improve.

title: Excellent Security Camera
text: I owned several Arlo cameras before adding this refurbished Arlo Pro to my network of cameras. No problems with it at all so far after a month of use. Easy to set up and use, either from the web site or app. I would buy another refurbished one if i need to.

title: Failed often after first use
text: The adapters worked when used the first time. After the first use, they rarely worked. If the connecting plug was wiggled or moved just right, the adapter would work. Any type of plug that had any weight, when plugged into the adapter, would not work. Having to spend several minutes to get the adapter to work, and then it would fail again, was very frustrating. I would not buy this product again.

title: The most conveinient adapter out there.
text: I've gone through several different adapters over the years. Most are bulky, and some don't fit well after a year or 2 of use. These 2 adapters work in all the countries that are most common. I especially like the spring tension in the European model, they always fit tight. You don't have to carry a pack of 5 or 6 if you're going to many countries on a single trip. This is the 2nd set I've bought. Highly recommended.

title: Great Camera, easy to use
text: The system was easy to install and the arlo camera captures great, quality images. it's easy to control through the website. The latest site update makes it even easier to control. We use the system to monitor our house when we're gone and the camera's wide display captures all the entrances. I plan on purchasing another one to use outside soon.

title: Great headphones
text:
I love these. I normally have cheap headphones. I’m not much of a music person really but decided I needed something better than drug store check out lane earphones. I was ecstatic with these. Granted, my expectations were not DJ sound but I loved the sound on these. Very crisp. Very clear. Very comfortable. VERY happy customer.
Honestly, if I was designing them, I’m not sure how I could make them any better.

title: Great quality
text: Love this case. I recently bought some headphones that I spent more money on than I normally would (I’m not a music techie) and wanted a case to protect them. This one seemed perfect and it was. Exactly 100% what I wanted. Nice soft material and so far, seems a durable case. Very happy.

title: Right one will not charge
text: I got these because of the good reviews. They are useless. The right one does not charge and yes, I took off the protective film. What a waste. I have no idea why these have good reviews. Maybe I got a bad pair but getting to my local post office for a return is a huge hassle when you are mobility impaired so I guess I will just trash them. I am not a happy customer at all. I suppose I should have paid attention to where they were made or something. My advise is to stay away from these.

title: So-so
text: This are cute and the size stays in but the sound is very tinny. We will keep them but they are not the best, by a long shot.

title: Useless
text: I used one last night when a previous cord gave out. My iPad was on when I went to bed (I play music at night). It was 100% when I went to bed at about midnight. I woke up at 7, grabbed the iPad to shut off the alarm and though it showed it was charging, it was under 10% and in danger of dying. So, maybe they will work if you don’t run your iPad or iPhone at the same time, I don’t know. Maybe this one cord was a dud. However, I was seriously annoyed. This set my whole morning off as I need the iPad charged. I swear, why on earth does it seem an impossibility to find cords that work and work for a long time. I’m not hard on cords and yet they either don’t work or die very soon. Yes, the colors are great but I don’t care about that. I want cords that do their job. This one most certainly didn’t. I purchased due to the glowing reviews. I am sorry I cannot add my name to that list. My advise: look elsewhere if you need your iPad to charge while you use it.

title: Utter crap!!!!!
text:
I thought I would try them as the reviews were good. Something is very off with the reviews. Very (in my opinion)

I have tried each cord. Plugged my iPhone in and plugged the iPad into another. Both were plugged in while using. The phone drained to 91% (it was at 100% when I started). The iPad drained to 81% and was at 100% when I started. It took about an hour or an hour and a half for the iPhone to drain and about 3 hours for the iPad.
These are not really charging cords but more (will slow down you getting no charge left notifications” cords.

I will throw these away and no, I absolutely would not recommend these to anyone. I recommend you run the other way.

title: Awesome backpack!
text: I love this backpack. First day I got it, I spilled a thermos of lemonade in it. I turned it inside out, wiped it out, let it air dry and it was good as new. It’s a perfect size and very sturdy. I love the American flag print. So very happy with this purchase.

title: My brother loves it
text:
My brother works in a school and he has to walk into the building in the winter in ice, snow, slush, rain and mud. He also has some time to himself (very little) everyday. I thought it would keep his ears warm and let him listen to music into his walk into the building. He says he uses it to listen to music in his car so his ears stay warm, keeps it on into the school and puts it on to relax in a short break when he’s not working with nor seeing students.
He’s very pleased so I am too.

title: Threw it away
text:
I have put screen protectors on many things but this one was impossible. Didn’t stick. Could not get the bubbles out. I will never use this brand again. Total waste of money. I am ordering a replacement from another company and I guess I’ll just have to live with this crappy screen saver in the meantime. One of the top 10 worst things I have purchased on Amazon.

Very unhappy customer!

Now, I’m not hard on cables as I have been practically bed bound for months due to an accident p, so it’s not like the cord is being roughly treated. Yet, it fizzled very quickly. I’m very disappointed. When it worked, it did charge well as opposed to some cables I have had but it’s longevity gives it 1 star.

title: Hurts my ears

Try these. They are fantastic!

title: Protects player!
text: Love this case. I use my DVD player to watch multiple region DVD’s and have been in and out of hospitals in the last year. Finally, this case makes things easier. Awesome!

When I was using then, the speakers hurt my ears as I laid on them. I reluctantly used about once a week.....so about 9-10 times, then the battery fell apart. I’m just pitching them. Complete and utter useless waste of money.

title: Absolute waste of money!!!!!
text:
I have had these a bit over a month. All three have bitten the dust. Two would not charge my iPad if I was using it while charging. None charged quickly. The last one gave out last night. I used it to charge my phone. Tried numerous chargers, several devices.....nothing. It was the cord. They were all the cords. All in all, 3 cords useless within a little over 4 weeks, does not make me happy.
These cords are an absolute waste of money and I am now dubious of the reviews.

Be warned and don’t say I didn’t tell you.

title: Perfect for a therapy pool and survived total submersion!!!
text:
Got these today and used them in a therapy pool (rotator cuff issues) and it was so nice. I was in my own little world. I highly recommend these. Nice sound and survived a few splashes. Perfect!

UPDATE
Last week I was pushed into the swimming pool (friends just fooling around) and assumed my headphones would be toast. I went under water completely and the headphones were on at the time (that’s how my friends snuck up on me.....I was listening to music). I came up and they were still working. I was kind of shocked. I used them for the rest of my time at the pool. Figuring they would eventually die, I used them in the sauna (both wet and dry), as well as the shower. I thought they would probably not charge but they did. I have used them numerous times since then. They sound good and charge fully, every night.
I’m not saying you can swim in them but if they took a total submersion, high temps and hot mist...and came out working, I think they can take my normal splashes.
I’m even happier than I was before! Good buy!!!

title: Great for old dead iPods
text: Needed a cord to try to charge a couple of old original iPods and this did the trick. Both whirled back to life.

title: At last....a buckle!

title: Perfect for many little things I have and hanging some things on my backpack
text:
I have put everything for earphones to fidget spinners in the these things. I love the clips as I can hang them on my backpack, I'm very very happy with purchase. I may order more but I still have one left I have not used. I'm sure I will though.
So far, 2 fidget spinners, dice, extra keys, Bluetooth earphones, silicone ear protectors and extra cash have found homes in these. They are very handy to have. I frequently unzip one (hangs on my backpack) and get the fidget spinner to occupy my in various lines or get out my earphones and connect to my music on my iPad, if it's with me (those two hang on the straps of my backpack for a reason)
Highly recommended!

title: No sound at all and manual is useless
text:
I was excited to get this but it's not what I hoped for. I don't have any sound. I have tried to figure out why, watched you tube videos etc. It also does not record a smooth video. It stops and starts. Again, perhaps it's a setting but from what I can see, it's set correctly. The manual for this is worthless.
I don't know if it came defective (most likely) of I'm doing something wrong. As I have been trying to figure it out every way I can, I am guessing it came defective. It's probably too late to send it back and I have had it out of the box and attached to various mounts so it's probably not fair to send it back but it's a real annoyance. I guess you get what you pay for.
VERY UNHAPPY CUSTOMER. Buyer beware of this product.

I'm very happy with it.
It fits my Akaso EK7000 perfectly.

title: Very high quality!

This is a fantastic quality hat. I went out to the lake where all the ducks were out and about and got some good footage. The bill does not get in the way (which is great because my eyes are very sensitive to the sun) and it protects my eyes while getting good shots. I just need to remember to turn my head slowly.
It does take a little getting used to but it's well worth it!
