title: If you are on an extreme budget, go for it....otherwise, PASS
text:
I wasn't expecting diamonds but still......it's not great. It was cheap. It was just a tablet to have laying around as an extra. This would be great if it were not for a white line running down the side. It is part of the display. I cannot fix it and it is annoying but by the time I pay to send it back, pay to have another shipped etc....I might as well just keep this one. I notice others have had the same problems.

If you are on a tight budget and cannot afford a more well known product, this will be great. I have a tablet from another company and these don't even remotely compare but the price is hundreds of dollars difference.

It works for a crappy little tablet as a back up...that's about it.

title: Save your money!

Total waste of money. I got this for a heating pad that didn't even work when it came. Contacting them was pointless apparently.

Save your money.

title: Hurt my ear
text: These have ok sound but fit into my ear funny. I cant really use. Might just be the shape of my ear but they hurt. If they fit your ear, the sound is great.

title: Protects mine when my friend iPads in other cases still break!
text: These are great. They seem a bit bulky at first but I loved it. I have dropped mine and it never broke. Others of my friends did not have these cases and broke their screens or iPads in general. Not me. When I updated to an iPad Air the first thing I did was order another one (in red this time) and my iPad is still safe. This is the only case I will ever use!

title: Not bad
text:
I liked this but it was a bit hard to get used to. I thought I was going to pull the fan from the ceiling my first time using it. You do not have to pull hard on it, in fact, the dust comes off with gentle motions.

I like it but without knowing how much "pull" was needed on it, I could have damaged the fan or the ceiling (maybe I am just a moron but that was my experience.

title: Works great for some things
text:
I had one of these before and it not only did not help to charge, it ran things down. I was dubious about this one but willing to try it. It came and I was impressed. It adds length AND does what it is supposed to do......charge. I was so impressed I ordered 2 more.
I wish I had ordered this one a long time ago.

If you need a cable.....this is the one that works.

EDIT
Ok.....I ordered another one and let me say these work great for dome things. I have a USB aromatherapy diffuser and with this cord I can set it anywhere but if you want to charge your iPad, it would work if you were not using it. If you want to charge while using, don't bother.

title: Works Great!
text:
I have ordered chargers for this camera in the past and none worked. This one worked great. Charges the batteries fast and no longer have to worry about the batteries being charged. I have 4 batteries and I can charge them all within a few hours and I am ready for the next day. I have not used the car charger nor actually even tried it but I am betting it works. I never need a car charger, I just thought it would be nice to have.

If you need a charger or batteries for your camera, I highly recommend this one.

title: Northern Lights on My Ceiling
text:
I love these speakers. I plug them into my computer and they are always on, even if not playing music. At night, it appears as though the northern lights are cast on my ceiling. When I play music, the water dances and the ceiling lights up with the light show. I really enjoy these. They do best with fast rock and roll but will react to any music.

My only complaint is that sometimes one speaker does not work. All I have to do is unplug it and plug it back in and they both work but it's annoying to have to do. Worth it since these are so cool but still.....annoying. If it were not that, I would give them 5 stars easily.

Very unique and conversation pieces.

title: Had these for 2 months...they worked once
text:
I had these and tried them. They ere awful but I kept them because they were just a back up pair so I hung them on my desk. Went to use them yesterday.....after just a couple of months and only one use.....dead in the water. Nothing there.

Stay as far away from these things as you possibly can

title: Very nice
text:
I have been looking for a USB hub for a while and none were the "bang for the buck" I thought they should be. I read the reviews and thought I would try this one.

It is nice. It works well and I have quickly filled up each port.

The disadvantage of this unit is the length of the cord that runs from the hub to the computer. It is VERY short. I use a laptop and this would be really great if the cord was longer and I could then velcro it onto the lid and when using, the hub is out of the way. I can't do that with this unit. That is a big drawback for me and I do mean BIG however, the price was more than fair for four ports.

If it had a longer cord, it would be PERFECT

title: Works great.

title: Great buy!
text:

It seems a little thin and I figured it would not last that long when it came but thought if it got me through the vacation I would be happy. That was a while back and it still is going strong.

Best splitter I have ever had

(Hard to write a review for an "it's just ok" product)

text: I have used this when using the iPad (and obviously had it plugged in) and it still runs the battery down, just slower than it would have otherwise. It is ok but there have got to be others out there that will work better. I mean, Belkin makes some great products but this is not top of the list. I use it and its ok but I would really like to find a 10 foot iPad cord that actually works and not rely on thsi thing. When your computer is plugged in, it should not run down to 70% when being used. So, based on that...I consider this product kind of a failure and the only reason it gets 2 stars is that I actually do use it

title: Fantastic
text:
Ok, for some reason...and I blame my own stupidity, I thought I was just ordering the ear loops (it clearly says headphones with ear loops so I have no idea what I was thinking) and thought "the price is a bit steep" but I needed them and so coughed up the dough. I got the package and thought "It came with earphones?" (yeah...that stupidity was still hanging on apparently) and then I read the packing invoice and "poof" my idiocy (at least about this) vanished. I groaned, thinking "oh yeah, I need another pair of ear buds like a hole in the head" but I needed the loops. So...I attached the loops to another set of earphones and thought "Ok. They fit. This will work" and then I thought I should check and see if I wanted to keep the ear buds so I plugged them into my computer and turned on iTunes. WOW. Let me just say these are the best ear buds I have ever had (to think I thought "maybe I should just toss the ear buds as I don't need any more...ok so the stupidity was still clinging to me somewhat). They sound is sharp and crisp. They come with different heads for different size ear canals. They are...in short, just amazing. So as it turned out,the clips were the bonus. The clips work FANTASTIC and you can put them on other ear buds but these buds are truly amazing. As it is....for the price....this is a steal. I have had headphones that cost over $100 and these are better (I prefer buds to the over the ear headphones). I have also had ear buds that cost A LOT of money and these beat them, hands down.

I recommend these HIGHLY. The ear loops and earbuds are fantastic! You won't be sorry.

I have not tried to jog in them so I cannot answer to that but for me, these are worth double or triple what I paid for them

title: High quality angled Lightening Cord
text:
I paired this cord with an Apple brand lightening charger after reading MANY horror stories of sparks, overheating, charging failures, etc. and I’m really pleased with it. (And the Apple charger, which is never warm, doesn’t spark, & has caused me no paranoia I’m going to catch on fire.)

The cord itself feels substantial. Ten feet is perfect for where I use it. It flexes, but is still quite stiff. The little adapter is nice, but so far is living in a drawer.

My only complaint, which is minor and will not apply to many users, is that the actual lightening tip end is longer than I need it to be. I’m sure this is to accommodate cases that don’t have any cut-out design where the port is. Mine does, so there is a lot of tip before the barrel it’s mounted in. This requires some extra care that I don’t jar it when setting my phone down. Not a problem when I’m holding it.
I’m a big fan of this angled design, and the company has good reviews here and elsewhere. I especially recommend it to those that have heavy cases with minimal port access.

title: ... for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase
text:
I've been using this product for about 2 weeks now and I am very happy with the purchase! It provides a strong breeze of air to keep me dry despite the extreme Arizona temperatures. My only challenge is my daily driver is a 67 Mustang and this product will not mount on the dash too tall and too wide. I don't have the long center console in my car, so the only thing I can stick it to is the carpeted floor - and I would rather not do that. For the most part it stays put with nothing holding it, but if I hang a sharp right it goes sliding. Not the company's fault-but for anyone driving a 67 mustang, this won't sit on the dash. Other than the challenge with placement, i would definitely recommend this product. It's not a cure for the 110 degree heat but I have tinted windows to dim the sun and this to keep the air moving in the car. A huge help to get me through one more summer before I get an AC installed!
Edit: forgot to mention - it is not noisy! Obviously there is a little bit of a buzz but it's not annoying and nothing that can't be drowned out by your radio. Also, I like that the two fans can be adjusted up, down and side to side. So it can sit in the middle and one fan be pointed at the driver and the other at the passenger. It can tilt up or down depending if you have it sitting up high on the dash or low on the floor like I do. Anyway - great buy! Not sure why people have any issues with it dying on them but I will update if anything like that happens.

title: It absolutely works, but you can do a lot better.
text:
This cord is an identical replacement for the one that comes with the monitor. This is a pro and a con. My husband and I have used it every night after our son moved into his own room, and we absolutely love it. It’s so much nicer than the one we had 10 years ago when our daughter was born.

The only issue we’ve ever had with it is the cord that connects with the screen. It started fraying at the end near the plug after 2-3 months. We were able to tape it and continue using it for several months after that. Eventually you could see the copper wiring coming through and it only worked when positioned perfectly. A couple weeks later, it was done. I desperately tried to salvage it, but it wasn’t happening.

My Mom ordered us a replacement cord and all was well again. That didn’t last long though, because history tends to repeat itself. I learned my lesson and didn’t wait until it became useless before replacing it. This time I bought a universal adapter. It was actually cheaper than this cord and can be used for just about anything requiring an ac adapter.

Use your money wisely. Why pay the same price for a cord that will just fall apart? There are a ton of options when you search for a universal adapter, but they seem fairly similar. I bought one for less money than this cord, it came with about 10 adapters, and is much sturdier.

They said I should just return it, but it was a Christmas gift for our daughter and that wasn’t an option. Even though there were numerous chargers available to purchase (which is what they suggested I do) I was told they couldn’t simply send me one, I’d have to purchase it and they would not expedite shipping.

Eventually, I was given a $30 credit to my account.

The computer itself is great and I would definitely recommend it, but this whole experience left a sour taste in my mouth. I would not recommend buying refurbished. The hassle is not worth saving a few bucks!

title: Not bad, but ANNOYING pairing and audio interface
text:
I've had a number of Bluetooth headphones and the overwhelming majority of them have an "audio interface" that makes sense - some bare bones, some quite pleasant. This interface is in the form of sounds the relate to each of the functions - power on/off, paring, etc. These headphones have a TERRIBLE interface. When you power them on an annoyingly loud series of tones blares in your ear. The tones rise in pitch. When you continue to hold the power button, to access the paring mode, all you hear is an extremely brief, muffled tone. Apparently, the makers thought this was enough of a signal to indicate you're in paring mode. Believe me, it is NOT obvious at all. When you power off the headphones, you hear the same annoying loud series of tones. In this case, the tones do not decrease in pitch, which one might expect.

By comparison, the audio interface of my other Bluetooth headphones are a joy - unfortunately, they do not have volume controls or skip and rewind. When powering them on, a pleasant female voice says, "Hello", and when you enter pairing mode, the same voice says, "Ready to pair." When pairing is established, the voice says, You're connected", then tells me how much charge I have - either full, medium or low. These Cootree headphones do none of that. You'll be lucky if you're able to tell if they've been turned off properly.

In terms of sound quality, they're okay - nothing exceptional. In terms of fit, they're okay as well. Again, nothing exceptional. To my knowledge, they do not have an active noise cancelling function, other than what little noise they may happen to muffle by covering your ears. I mention this only because the rating form asks about it.

title: Make sure your device supports aptx
text:
I bought this to use with my LG TV and a couple of Anker Bluetooth speakers. Connecting the speakers to the transmitter was confusing because you have zero interface. Once I did get it connected, the latency was not good. The audio was not in sync at all - a god half to a full second behind the video. I'm returning this for a refund. If you're planning to use this with a TV and Bluetooth speakers, be sure they support the BT 5 aptx low latency codec.

EDIT

After returning the device, the manufacturer sent me a message. I almost deleted their email because it looked like spam, with emojis in the subject line. Anyway, they informed me that the problem I experienced was likely because the BT speakers (Upgraded, Anker Soundcore Boost) I used I paired with their device did not support the low latency aptx codec. This may have been the case, but I was unable to find specs for the speakers to confirm this.

I must say their customer support is extremely accommodating. In their email, they offered a number of options to make things right, including a gift card or a different BT transmitter. Unfortunately, I've already purchased wired speakers to replace the ones I had bought. Although I won't be taking advantage of their offers, I do give them high marks for service and have changed my rating from 2 stars to 4 stars.

title: Button functionality ruins this device. You get what you pay for.
text:
I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”

title: Inexpensive, but lousy UI
text:
For the price, this device is okay, but the user interface is pathetic. The touch interface is annoying because it only applies to half the screen. What's worse is when the device screen goes blank (to save battery life), you have to touch the screen - which performs one of the functions, like play or pause. It's quite annoying. The buttons of the touch screen are at the bottom and you can only navigate the interface by tapping up/down/left/right. So doing things on the device is a chore

I bought this for a friend and didn't spend much time with it - only to set it up. So I don't have an opinion of the sound quality or the build quality. However ... one comment on the latter. I've seen a number of reviews for this and similar products which reference the weight of the device and correlation it to the quality of the build. The 2 don't always to hand in hand. The Chinese have been known to add lead weights to devices to make them heavier so that people will believe it's better build quality or material than it really is. I don't know this to be the case with this device - just wanted to point out that weight may not be the telltale people think it is

BTW - the USB cable is SHORT. Probably only a foot at most. Also, it's micro USB, which is a pain in the butt.

The radio function required the use of headphones - as an antenna. Kind of a pain for Bluetooth headphone users. Also - if the headphones are plugged in, I presume you can't listen through the device's built in speaker (which is lackluster) or through an external Bluetooth speaker. I can't confirm this because, as I said, I only spent about an hour using the device.

FYI - the device has no internal storage. The 32GB is in the form of a micro SDXC card. This means if you opt to purchase a larger card to use with the device, you won't be adding to the 32GB, you'll be replacing it.

title: Didn't last long
text: Although I love the performance and features of this mouse, it doesn't last very long.  The small plastic feet on the bottom gradually slip loose which causes problems with the tracking - makes the device very irritating to use.  Logitech should sell replacements, but as far as I could find, they don't.  Also, the side button (the one below the forward/back buttons) seems to wear our faster than the other buttons.  I've owned at least 5 of these over the last 10 years and on 3 of them, the side button failed.  On one of them, I actually wore a hole in the plastic.  Not sure if this says more about the quality of the device materials or the force with which I click it.

title: Good price, functionality and features are as described
text:

The accompanying device directions could be clearer. The only other issue I have is I can't plug the device into my iPod Touch with the case I have - it's too thick for the connector to plug in. This means I have to remove the case in order to use the drive. I'm thinking about cutting out the bottom of the case to resolve this.

EDIT:
The drive doesn't function properly. I copied 400mb of mp3 music to it. None of the songs would play using the drive's internal player or a 3rd party player. Included in the music were 2 folders with additional mp3 files. The folders copied over, then after the transfer was complete, there was nothing in the folders.

The password protection is also incredibly easy to crack because it's not tied to the device, but to the app. Just delete the app, then reinstall it and you have access to everything on the drive.

You get what you pay for. Buyer beware.

title: It's cheap and works with Windows, but that's about it.
text:
I bought this because my laptop keyboard began to fail.

Pros
- Inexpensive - I paid $19, including tax
- Both the keyboard and mouse work with Windows with no problems - so far.
- Batteries were included - 1 AA for the mouse and 2 AAA for the keyboard.
- Includes all standard/function keys plus dedicated media buttons. Shortcut keys for email, web home page, power and calculator.
- All of the shortcut keys work with no config - except the email key - see cons below.

On the con side:
- There is no LED to indicate that the keyboard is on. If there is supposed to be, the LED on my keyboard doesn't work.
- If you use Gmail or another online service, the email shortcut key may not be usable. I use Gmail and when I pressed the email key, Windows Mail launched. If this can be configured to work with online email services, Logitech provides no instructions in the box.
- Unifying receiver is incompatible with newer Logitech software and devices.
- The mouse is bare bones - left and right click buttons and a scroll wheel with middle click function. No next/back buttons, no tilt scroll wheel. This mouse is best for emergencies or for temporary use until you get a new mouse with better features, etc.

Bottom line - you get what you pay for.

title: Okay for $25.  Still a little disappointed.
text:
Let me start by saying I don't use the cell phone features of these headphones, so this review is not all encompassing.

That said, I was a little disappointed in these headphones. Although the sound quality is good, the build quality and attention to detail in design could be better. The control buttons on the right ear are difficult to use as you can't easily feel with your finger where one starts and another begins, You just have to press in the general area, which is not very reassuring. The buttons themselves have no raised symbols or any physical element you can touch to let you know you're on a button, let alone the correct one.

The build quality is not the best. The control buttons fit together less tightly than other Bluetooth headphones I've used. The main play/pause/on/off/pairing button, located in the center of the right earphone in particular seems loose and misaligned.

The functions of the buttons work well enough. However, with some functions, there is no audio feedback. Having used other headsets that provide a short beep each time a button is pressed, I was a little confused when I first tried these - I'd press pause and the audio would just stop, with no beep. I suppose some users would find this preferable though. Some of the button functions, such as play/pause, are not instantaneous. There's a slight delay (about a second) between the time you press it and the time the audio actually plays or pauses. I've experienced this with other Bluetooth headsets and it seems to be a common annoyance.

Because the fit is somewhat tight, getting the earphones on requires a little manipulation. I often find I have to guide the tip of my ear into the space between the neckband (the part that holds the earpieces and wraps around your neck) and the earpiece.This is mainly due to the padding on the earpieces. Once the headphones are on though, they've not uncomfortable. However, a little more space between the neckband and the top of the earpieces would be an improvement. Wearing the headphones lying down or with your head against the back of a seat is not uncomfortable for the most part.

The charging port is has a rubber cover. Although it serves a purpose and some might find this helpful, I find it just gets in the way and will likely fall off. The charging cable is VERY short - about 3 feet, and it comes with no AC adapter, so you'll need to plug it into a USB port for charging - or acquire an adapter so you can use an electrical outlet. Due to the shortness of the cord, it will likely be inconvenient for use with some outlets.

Attaching the charging cord is somewhat difficult. This is to be expected, I guess, due to the micro-USB size of the plug that goes into the ear piece. The end of the cord that plugs into the ear piece is tapered on one side, so there's some visual indication of which way it should go in, but it's always a pain trying to insert these kinds of plugs, no matter what the device. I haven't used the headphones for any great length of time, so I can't comment on the battery life at this time.

The fact that these headphones can fold up to a fairly small size is nice and may be helpful to some when traveling. Typically, I wear them while walking or taking public transportation, so no real advantage for me.

I purchased 2 pair of these - 1 for myself and one as a gift. The ones I bought for myself were to replace a pair of Motorola Bluetooth headphones I thought were malfunctioning. Whenever I wore them, if I turned my heard too far to the right, the sound would cut out or it would seem to skip slightly. The first time I tried the Kinivo BTH240 headphones, they did the exact same thing. Is this something common to Bluetooth devices?

All in all, I suppose the negatives I've noted are minor and are likely more personal, but they still prevent me from rating these higher than 3 stars.

title: Would have been 5 stars but ...
text:
This is a nice little unit. I was surprised at how small it was - about the same size as one and a half packs of cigarettes. I gave the unit a full charge before testing it and the sound was pretty good - playing music from my iPod Touch via Bluetooth and via the included aux audio cable. BTW - that cable and the power cable are very cheap and I don't expect them to last long.

My biggest problem is with the sound quality when the product is connected to my laptop via the aux audio cable. The sound was horrible. There was a constant "white noise" type sound in the background. This sound was almost as loud as the music and it was very annoying. My laptop does not have Bluetooth, so that was not an option. I do plan on buying a USB Bluetooth adapter and testing that as well. Hopefully, I won't encounter the same poor audio.

One other thing I knew about prior to buying the product - it does not have a user replaceable battery. This means when the battery no longer holds a charge, you'll have to throw it away. My understanding is that these type of batteries will last a few years. However, throwing the product away is crazy, because it's bad for the environment - even if disposed of properly. It would be nice if the battery were user replaceable, so all that plastic and electronics didn't have to end up in a landfill.

So, as I mentioned, I like the product and would have rated it higher if not for the flaws I've noted.

title: Don't waste your money.
text:
OK, take 2. My original review of this product got hijacked somehow. After writing it, I checked back a couple hours later and my screen name and original title were there, but my review got replaced with what seemed like some guy's journal entry. It had absoluterly nothing to do with this or any other product. Strange.

Anyway - as mentioned in my original posting, this review is more a condemnation or earbud headphones in general than the Sennheiser CX300-B, which I decided to try after my "over ear" style Sony noise canceling headphones went on the fritz. My past experience with earbuds was not good, although I had only ever tried the type that come with the iPod and not the "ear plug" type that go in the ear canal, like the Sennheiser CX300-B. However, having owned a pair of Sennheiser over the ear headphones back in the 70's, my impression of the company and their products was good. So, I decided to take the plunge. What a mistake.

After opening the package (no easy feat - damn sound welded plastic clamshells!), I popped on the medium-sized bud covers (appropriate for my size ears) and inserted them into my ears. I turned on my mp3 player and listened for a few minutes. The sound was adequate - nothing spectacular. I did notice they had decent bass and did block some external noise. I kept listening as I stepped outside to go to the store. I couldn't believe what I heard. Every step I took was amplified in my head - like a booming bass drum. Even the gentle bumping of the cord against my chest was amplified - a constant thump, thump, thump that was impossible to ignore. As it turns out, the very feature that blocks a modicum of external noise, also amplifies any sound that travels through the body. Even breathing is amplified! As I walked, it sounded as though I was listening to someone breathe over a PA system! I had hoped to use these while running, but there's no way that's going to happen. In fact, the problem with amplified sound is so bad, I won't use them at all.

I am very disappointed in this product and will never buy any ear plug style headphones again. I don't understand why anyone would sell them, let alone use them. They may have great sound reproduction, but the listening experience is totally ruined by the sounds that get amplified through the body. It amazes me that people buy similar style products that sell for hundreds of dollars. The only way you can enjoy the sound they produce is to sit perfectly still. I'm glad I only paid about $16 for these things. I won't return them because it'll be too much of a hassle - probably cost more to ship them back than I paid.

BTW - The photo of the product is misleading. The cord looks thicker than it actually is and there's no way it can be coiled as is shown in the photo. It gives the impression the cord is more supple and flexible that it really is. Also, one end of the cord is longer than the other. Not sure why this is, but the thinness of the cord makes it prone to kinking and tangling. In fact, since one side of the cord is longer than the other, it makes it even more prone to tangling.

Bottom line - steer clear of the Sennheiser CX300-B and all ear plug style earbuds.

title: Works - poorly

I sometimes have to press the forward button 5-6-7 times to get the thing to advance to the next song. The volume control is also problematic - sometimes turning the volume all the way up or all the way down without stopping. The pause control works fine, except that once paused, it rarely is able to resume play. The range of the product is also a problem. I carry my iPod in my inside jacket pocket and carry the remote control in my outside jacket pocket - a distance of 12-15 inches. The iJet has trouble traversing this distance. If you're thinking of buying this product, don't bother. It's a waste of money. Thankfully, I didn't waste much.

I use my iPod while commuting on public transportation and thought these headphones would be a good replacement for another pair of Sony noise-canceling headphones I had been using for 3 years. I've resorted to turning the feature off and turning up the volume.  The only other complaint I have with this product is that they're not portable enough. So far, so great. Sound is clear, and seems that the mic works fine for calls, since no-one has asked me to repeat.
I'm hard on these devices, so we'll see if it's durable. For the price, I can replace it. I'm sending one to my son now.

title: Blue Dot ZIP-BLK-3.6x300-2-packages 12-Inch UV...
text: My husband says they work really well in the garden

title: Computer Part
text: This is the part that my son told me to order so he could fix my computer when it died...

title: Antenna more than satisfactory
text: We live in a rural area with no cable access.  Sattilite is too expensive for our budget.  We found the antenna works very well for our needs.

title: Horrible Motion Detection
text: So if you are buying this camera, test out motion detection.  I drove my truck by the camera, and no motion was triggered.  I think it has to do with the CloudEdge software that you are forced to download on your phone if you want to use it.  It only detects humanoid movements.  Make sure your phone is connected to the 2.4 Ghz WiFi router when trying to setup this camera.  Otherwise it won't work.  Doesn't seem to be a way to monitor the camera with a PC, it's mobile-app only.  So you are forced to view video on a tiny screen.  Setup was easy, everything seems to work within reason, except motion detection.  So test that throughly outside before you go through the trouble to  mount the camera outside.  Lousy motion detection was a deal breaker for me, I don't have time to monitor this thing 24x7.  I don't like external web cloud apps like CloudEdge, what happens when they go out of business?  Yep, you are stuck with useless hardware.

title: Windows installed it fine could see 2.4 and 5G, but speed was horrendus
text: Ran a speed test with this device after windows recognized it, and everything else I had was at least 10x faster than this adapter.

title: Not RP-SMA Connectors for Antenna, these are proprietary push-on-antennas
text: So I wanted to extend the range of this router by taking off some of the internal antenna's and screwing on another RP-SMA high gain antenna in a better location.  NOPE.  These are some kind of funky push on antenna's that are not threaded.  So good luck finding the right type of connectors to adapt to this box.  Don't advertise removable antennas like it's upgradable if it's really not.

title: Buggy, Lost Connection Often, Wonky Setup, unreliable
text: So setup was easy, but incomplete.  Asks you to change admin password, but not wifi password at the same time.  Once I got the wifi password setup, I could connect different devices to it, PC, Mac, Android, but it seemed to lose the connection.  After you make any router configurations, you will have to manually reboot the router and hope it comes back online.  I installed the latest firmware and it died, couldn't factory reset it either.  It's cute, but it's not worth the headaches at trying to make this thing work, it's a buggy product not ready for prime time that they are dumping out on the public wasting a lot of productive capacity.

title: Did nothing1
text: complete waste of money.

title: Ok, but these guys are clueless about security cameras
text: So the blinking led says fake.  usually the led will on blink if it detects motion.  Not metrodome on and off all night long.  The IR LEDS don't light up either.  It would be better if they put a motion detection circuit inside and then it might be more believable.

title: Couldn't get it to work over 200'
text: So I bought a used unit on Ebay.  The antennas are not UV stabilized, they were brittle.  I was testing, and it was Ok out to 200-250' feet, but asking anything out to 300 feet, forget about it.  Tech support told me to try channel 11, slight improvement but .... not what I was hoping for.  The wind blew it off  a 5 gallon bucket and broke all the antennas because they were sun damaged brittle..  I figured I would get some better, higher gain antennas for it.  It's very difficult to find N-Type antennas, so I got an N-Type Male to Male SMA connector and was able to buy some high 22dbi gain SMA antennas to try it out.  It performed worse.  My antenna was up about 25' off the ground, and I don't have trees higher than maybe 16'.  So this thing just won't cover the 5 acre property like I had hoped, so I think I am going to have to go with some sort of point to point type ubquity setup.

title: Seems to be a good value, but screen contrast doesn't work
text: So, if the sun is too bright, there is no way to adjust the contrast color.  The menu flashes up and then disappears rapidly.  Not sure if this is firmware upgradable.  I mounted this on my Bobcat T650 Loader so that when I am trenching I can see the spray paint line behind me as  I am dragging the trencher.  Problem is the contrast is terrible and no way to adjust it, so I couldn't see the fluorescent orange paint on the ground.  Everything else seems to work great.  Cabling was good.  Camera feels like a quality metal housing that will be able to stand up to the abuse /heat/dust on the back of the Bobcat.  Night vision is grainy, but it does work.  Not bad for the money.  The Bobcat solution was over 1k, this isn't bad for under $100.  Time will tell.

title: To hard to setup, junk software, not much range difference.
text: Put these on top of a 20' building, didn't see that much range difference.  Maybe 100' or so, but would not reach out to 300' for sure.  Not work the money.  Software instructions are not that clear, require passwords, email password reset doesn't work.  Real Sorry I bought these.  Requires a machine to stay on to run the Omada software, if you reboot your machine,  then the network no longer appears to work.  I think I am going to go with an Ethernet over Powerline type of adapter rather than trying to extend the signals through the airwaves.

title: A Maintenance Nightmare
text:
What should have been on the front of the BOX:

Warning, Charge this Device up Immediately before install. During it's use, you will have to unscrew it from the wall and disconnect the doorbell wiring and throw it on a charger for 5-10 hours from time to time to keep it working properly. The engineers who developed this product weren't smart enough to make it run off of power supplied by your doorbell alone, or trickle charge the battery fast enough during usage. From the factory, there wasn't enough charge on it to install it and test it's features completely out of the box. The hard-wiring will trickle charge a battery but if there's a lot of motion it will run it down and you will have to de-install and re-install the Ring device. The engineers didn't provide any sort of quick electrical connection disconnect mechanism either for the hard wiring XD!! The should have had some sort of automotive style quick-disconnect plug. Or even better yet, an external USB charging port that you could run an extension cord and charge up the doorbell in place or some sort of external solar charger. If the doorbell is on the side adjacent to the door, you will most likely need a 45 degree mount (separate purchase) in order to get a better view of the visitor. Very Very displeased with this company not being forthright with key installation and usage information.

I didn't buy this device here, I installed one purchased by a customer from Amazon.

The fish eye lens and picture are great, works great, but the battery/power situation was a big disappointment.

title: Delivered a Refurb Unit that Did Not work
text: Not sure if this was an Amazon Issue or a Supplier Issue.  I ordered this unit a while back and set it aside to when I could get back to my Hobbyist Project.  Opened box and screen had scratches on it.  Then pluged it in, and unit wouldn't connect to the Raspberry PI.  The green led came on saying there was power, and it would flash a rasbperry pi icon, but it wouldn't connect to video.  It's now an expensive paperweight.  There was a green card in the box for an email address to contact if there was any issues, and so I wrote them.  But I am posting here too, because I saw others that posted that had the same exact issue that I have.  So I decided to flag it and see what the company does to remedy this issue.

title: You'll hate the product when you need to change the battery.
text: Product does it's job, sometimes too well.  Rain will set it off, and so will rabbits and birds.  For this reason you may want to get a buried driveway probe otherwise you will get a lot of false alarms.  I have both this optical sensor and a probe and when I get dual notification, then I know something is out there.  Here's what needs to be improved:  #1  There are 4 Recessed screws to get to the battery, and when you flip it over so you can see where to put the battery they will fall into the dirt.  How Stupid of a design can you get!?!.  How about a simple battery compartment  access door or something that just snaps in place or a single screw.  #2  Who remembers obscure tones?  IF  you have multiple gates on your property, how are you going to remember which tone goes with what gate?  How about a voice over that says something like :  Area 1 or Area 2.  Or better yet, allow the user to upload or record their own tones or something:  "Someone at the Front Gate!"

title: Works like it should, quality product, 3 gripes
text:
So the range works, very few false alarms.

9v battery will take some time to replace in the receiver. At least the electronics inside are protected from the elements with a rubber gasket behind 4 screw plate.

Receiver unit doesn't have a rechargeable battery backup. This would have been nice to carry it to the gate for testing so that you can hear it go off when the sensor is tripped. Also if power goes out, you can still hear the chime. I have a plug in outlet in my truck as well as an inverter and a portable electric battery with 110v capability, just would have been nice for those without.
Programming the transmitter/receiver with dipswitches is a bit of headache especially getting the cover off the reciever. Should have just been exposed on the underside rather than have to pull apart the plastic housing. Maybe some sort of phillips head rotatable dipswitch settings. I do like the versitility of the current setup thought to prevent collisions with other systems.

Like the mounts, especially the swivel mount for gate post adjustments so that windy day swinging gates don't trip the sensor.

title: Doesn't come with 6 chargers, range is limited, support is outsourced joke, software is buggy
text: You aren't getting much of a break when you buy 6, they don't include usb chargers or enough outdoor mounting posts.  Can't use 3rd party chargers , need arlo chargers.  The magnetic ball in socket posts are really for indoor use.  I wouldn't trust them up 3 stories in a  strong wind.  Router is on 3rd floor, but seems like range is like 75' on the ground from the router.  Software is so so, buggy as hell and no updates.  Mobile App is always "Getting Status".  Website always "Request Timed Out" after 30 seconds of video feed, you can't really monitor cameras for more than 30 seconds through their sucky website.  Don't rely on this is an emergency situation.  No real forward thinking people involved in the design, they probably just paid a contractor to slap something together, now that he's gone and profits are gone, they don't give a rats ass about updating the software.

title: It's usefulness is determined by location of tripod mount.  Instructions were deplorable.

title: When Power Goes Off, Firmware gets Corrupted, and Router will not work
text:
When the router is working ,it's awesome. Range, speed, and setup are very easy. However, just like a bad musical performance, when things don't perform well, that's what people remember.

Here is why I cannot' give the product 5 stars.

There have been two situations where the router lost power and the firmware got corrupted and I had to reflash the router to make it work. I have NEVER had a device EVER get corrupted firmware. What a JOKE! Probably corrupted data issue as nothing will bring a system down like bad data.

Google: Router Power LED Blinks Slowly and Router No Longer Works

So rather than issue a RECALL on the defective merchandise, they do the next worst thing possible and give you some funky software called TFTP to download and fool around with to get the router re-flashed. Well, I thought the re-flash would correct the corrupted firmware. I got news for them, IT DIDN'T. I was moving my Router yesterday while the cable guy was here and then when we tried to hook everything back up, I got the blinking light of death again. I knew it was going to be a hassle to get the firmware downloaded and reflashed, so I switched back to an older working router for the time being.

In my opinion, NETGEAR should have done a 2 things amongst other things...

1) As an interim solution, Made special re-flash software that made upgrades a breeze. A one click solution to read the router's make/model MAC address and current firmware, and auto-magically download the new one and install it while PRESERVING all existing settings. It should also remember the OLD mac address and use it when you were migrating the settings to a router with a new MAC address. If their software engineering department can't do that, they need to be replaced starting with the Manager.

2) Recalled and Replaced the defective equipment for FREE, send out a new unit, and a postage paid return box for your old unit. Then use the above software to migrate the settings and old MAC address to the new unit so it works seamless with your existing cable model and service provider.

What do you call a router that does not work? An expensive paperweight? Can you say Regression Testing? Can you say Error Trapping Netgear? Words for the day for your Engineering Department. who worked on this product line.

title: So great that everyone you show them to will want a pair.
text: Good quality headphones, very nice case and choice of cords.  My nephew now has them.  He heard them while gaming at my place and didn't want to 'leave them behind' and his uncles, so we did a work trade and now he has them.  He said the kids at HS never have see anything like these, he grins from ear to ear whenever he has these on.  I bought the gold plates and it took a while to unscrew all the screws, but they looked nice. I would clean the gold plates every day but usually when I would get into work in the morning I noticed finger prints that were not mine on them.  So I know the workmates couldn't keep their hands off them when Ieft either!

title: Great for the money, dissapointing if you want wireless high-resolution.
text: Wireless does not work and I am upset they would advertise it as such.  Product is very stable, image quality about 640x480 grainy.  Audio works.  Good for the price, but if you want something with better resolution ... go with something higher-end.

title: Couldnt' get it working
text: ASUS Laptop incompatibility.  Couldn't get it working.  No diagnostics.  Company took it back and made good to return my money.  They were interested in fixing the problem and were sorry that it didn't work for me.  It could have been a bad unit or something.  Good price for what it will do (if it works).  YMMV.

title: Excellence in Engineering and Delivery
text: Money well spent for this device.  I had an ASUS laptop that had the HDMI port too close to the VGA Port.  Therefore, I couldn't only use one or the other.  I wanted 3 monitors. (Company provided laptop, I would have never bought the machine myself if I would have seen such a lame display arrangement in advance.).  I decided to give a competitor's cheaper USB3 to HDMI inline converter a try, but it failed horribly.  I paid a few more dollars for this unit from Anker after reading some of the positive reviews, and it worked perfectly.  I installed the CD ROM it came with, and it recognized my 2ndary Samsung monitor connected via HDMI instantaneously.  I pushed the limits and tried to use the HDMI and the DVI on the unit at the same time, but couldn't get it working, it's unclear whether they support that modality.  It could be a bad cable or something else I forgot, I didn't fiddle with it too long. USB 3.0 seems to deliver the 60Hz refresh rate, I don't see any lag or ghosting at 1080p, so I am well pleased with the performance.  I plugged my headphones in, and it immediately transferred the audio.  Looks nice, feels like great engineering.  It's been going strong for about 2 weeks now without a hiccup.  I recommended this product to 6 other co-workers.

title: Very Very Disappointed
text:
I see a lot of people stoked about this product, and at first I was. Until I tried to use it. Perhaps I just got a defective unit. Too many CONS to keep:

The biggest problem I had with the unit was inserting the MicroSD card, it just did not function properly. It was spring loaded and sometimes would shoot the micro sd card a few feet into the air. That can't be good for the card, and if it happens to go down a storm drain or get lost in a gravel bed, that's not good either. I would try to press it in, it wouldn't 'stick', do it again, and again, 15 minutes later I realized something wasn't quite right with the unit. Endless fumbling.

The unit should have an LED that when the card is inserted properly should glow green or something. (When the case was shut, it could stop the LED to save batteries or something.) The unit has cryptic LED blinks for diagnostics, doesn't help a lot when you don't have the manual handy and are missing the action you are supposed to be recording. It was a non-stop fumble trying to get the device to recognize the card. I bought good quaility SanDisk 32 gig chips, it seemed to recognize them after much fumbling, but only recorded 2gb out of the 32gigs before I had to change them. That's terrible. When you are on a backpacking trip, you don't exactly have access to a computer to see what's going on with the memory, you have to wait until you get home to find out you recorded nothing. If I put a new Memory stick in, it should perform a format/check sum to make sure the card is good and then let the user know it's been tested /accepted and the media is ready to be used. Not wait until your action moment has arrived, then just blink off.

The unit is durable, waterproof, and works sometimes....but not when I really wanted it to. The video looks grainy, it lacks much detail. I know my miniDV tape recorder 10 years ago was better. Forget about sound quality...it's terrible, unit needs external microphone.

PROS: Unit recorded in .MOV and was accessible by my Mac and PC via USB.
Unit is tough.
Unit seems to be waterproof, had it down about 8' in a stream under a waterfall. Although the unit said it was recording, it recorded nothing. I'm sooooo livid about that part.

Units going back. There are some other helmet cameras that are about 2x the money that I will gladly buy. Expensive is when the product is not worth the money. Caveat Emptor!

title: Nice deal
text: I purchased this as a gift and had it sent directly to my friend 1,500 miles away.  He was thrilled to receive it and said it worked great, so I'm giving it 4 stars just because I haven't seen it or used it myself.  Shipping was quick and it arrived a day earlier than expected, so that was a plus.  I like that the package included the HDMI cable so I didn't have to buy one to send separately to my friend.  Very happy with experience.

title: Just what I wanted AND made in the USA
text: This sling is perfect for use with a small Panasonic point and shoot camera.  I love the ease of having it as a sling, or around my neck.  The pad at the neck area is wonderful and comfortable.  The only little issue I had was threading the cording through my camera.  The cord is slightly thicker than the original wrist strap supplied with my camera.  I'm happy to have the stronger cord, but it was a tight squeeze getting it through the opening for my camera.  I finally got some dental floss to thread through the cord and used that to pull the cord through.  I'm very happy with this purchase.  It's a well made product and I'm happy to be supporting USA made goods.

title: I like it
text: I was looking for a simple sort of cd clock radio to keep on a nightstand.  It's amazing how difficult it was to find something like that that fit my needs, and I ended up with this unit although I really wasn't intrested in the iPhone/iPod connections.  I went to a local electronics store and first tried a litte Sony machine, was set to buy it, and then the salesman showed me this Phillips unit.  The sound was overwhelmingly better on the Phillips unit.  I admit I'm not an audiophile, but I just want something that sounds good when I played CDs at bedtime.  I quickly dismissed the little Sony and went for this unit.  Since having it about a week now, I really like the sound from the CD player.  I did try my iPhone 4 on it to see if it would connect, and it did and it played music like a champ.  Strong and clear.  I have a rubber bumper on my iPhone and had to remove it to make the phone fit properly but that's no big deal.  In fact what I'm thinking of doing is reprogramming my older iPhone (first generation) with nothing but music on it and leaving that plugged in the Phillips unit.  I keep my iPhone 4 in a different charger in a different room so it doesn't disrupt my sleep AND so I won't forget it when I'm leaving the house.  So far I'm a happy camper with this little Philips unit.  The only con is the brightness of the backlit display which is rather bright.  I placed the unit in a different part of the room where the remote still works but the brightness of the display doesn't affect my sleep.  I like a dark room!

title: Drops signal
text: Bought this 10 months ago. I have been generally less and less happy as time progresses. It was fine in the beginning. Installation wasn't cut and dry but I got it through. After a month or so I noticed the 5ghz kept dropping in and out. Now 5ghz just shuts off randomly. 2.4ghz strength will be erratic at times. I have moved the extender to several different locations. I have even moved it to the same room. Same thing happens. I have to unplug and plug every few days. Fortunately I have only used 2.4ghz lately since 5 continues to go out. So I don't notice when 5 goes out. Will probably get different one. Would not get this brand again.

title: Never buy again.
text: If you love your digital life and shopping controlled by Amazon then this is the tablet for you. There is so much Amazon bloatware on this tablet and the tablet will not let you disable or uninstall or force stop. Battery is horrible. Probably because of all the bloatware in the background. The setting menu is annoying. Can never find what setting I am looking for and no search capability. If you download an app that is not Amazon connected. The tablet basically puts a fence around it and makes you so aggravated that you end up deleting the program. Worst tablet. Would never purchase an Amazon tablet again.

title: Five Stars
text: No problem so far

title: Perfect but...
text: I bought this because I wanted something I didn't have to connect directly to the DC outlet and get the engine whine. No matter what I did on other products could not get rid of that. So I thought I would give this a try. Took awhile for it to be delivered. Mailed from the UK. I wasn't in a hurry so no problem for me. Charged it up making sure it had a full charge. I don't see a battery indicator on it. Very simple interface. Unplugged from charger and attached to phone. Got this hissing sound the whole time during silence and music. Not a sound like the usually FM transmitter that is not broadcasting strong enough and/or getting inference from another station. Just something else I thought "Damn another waste of money" I then plug back into the charger thinking maybe it needed longer to charge.Still not the case. So I plugged it into my phone with the charger plugged into in. WOW! Perfect! Crystal clear. No engine noise. No station interference noise. No weak signal noise. Awesome!. Unplugged it from the charger..hissing noise again. So it looks like the charge and unplug is not 100%. But if I plug it into DC charger runs perfect. Best one I have ever had. I give it only a 4 because it advertised the charge unplug and play thing and I don't see that happening at 100% Otherwise it's definitely a keeper

title: Excellent iPad screen cover (and at a great price)
text: This thin glass screen cover was even easier to install on my 9th generation iPad than I’d hoped. After I placed it initially, it started the process of smoothly covering, but I noticed I hadn’t gotten it over the small camera hole perfectly (I’d forgotten to use the idea of taping it, I impulsively just placed it on as I’d done a couple years ago for my iPhone). But, no problem!  I simply lifted it up, repositioned, and set it down again, and it just went through the process of smoothly covering by itself, and was almost perfect; then there was one area of a trapped bubble so I lifted that corner and allowed  the product to come down from the center toward that corner, and it was done! Super easy, and what a relief. The touchscreen surface feels amazing, as if there were no cover at all; and I’m not seeing any fingerprint smudging or having any issues. The touchscreen is working perfectly. I definitely recommend this product and I would buy it again.

title: Pass on this one--you can get better in this price range
text:
I bought into the hype and some early favorable 'professional' reviews on this product (and am now convinced the website that posted it was probably paid by Whistler to hype up the release) and purchased it back in late June. I could have easily gotten a similar quality product for much less...or better yet, spent more and got a better, more reliable unit. Convinced that it wasn't working as advertised, I purchased a V1, the 'King' of radar detectors, and compared them in my car side by side. First off, the 78SE gives TONS of false alarms. Often it would go off when the v1 wasn't making a peep. Sometimes, it would go crazy when I was out in the middle of a road surrounded by corn fields! Is this because it is more sensitive? I think not. I had tested them on some speed signs set up in my area, and the V1 would go off a 1/4 mile or more before the Whistler made a detection. A 1/4 mile in the world of radar is an eternity--the difference between getting a ticket and not. By the time the 78SE starting making weak little burps warning you to start being on the lookout, the V1 was already going off at full blast. The v1 would also detect the speed radar when it was up and over a hill--presumably from the minute signature bouncing off different objects alongside the road. Again, not a peep was heard from the 78SE.

I am not saying I expect the 78SE to be as good as a $400 V1. I do, however, expect the performance to be enough to serve its purpose, which is warning you of radar before the cop has your speed. This detector simply won't do that, which makes owning it more or less pointless IMO. The numerous false alerts make you on guard when you don't need to be, and eventually you will simply ignore all the warnings--even the legitimate ones. When the real threats arise, it is doubtful you will know before the cop has your speed--MAYBE it will provide a small benefit in the most optimal conditions (a flat road going perfectly straight)...but how often is that the case? Save your hard earned $$ for a detector that will work...or if your dead set on spending less than $200, do more research and see if you can find something better or at least cheaper!

title: Very Disappointed!!
text:
Very Disappointed!!
I replaced my 3.5 year old Dell XPS-8300 after several hardware failures, expecting this system to be much, much better since it has 2 times the faster DDS memory, a hybrid solid state drive, an 8 core faster processor over my 4 core i5, but in fact it's actually slower when working with Adobe applications like PhotoShop and InDesign. After 3 weeks of daily use, I have not experienced anything that seems like an improvement. I develop websites using Adobe Dreamweaver and MS Expression Web with lots a graphic content and have managed fine (OK) on my previous system except that it wore out. (I guess, hard drive failure, DVD drive failure, motherboard, one after another.) This system also comes with Windows 10, which I hate a lot. A joke! Maybe that's a contributing factor to my totally unimpressive more expensive, less capable new computer. Bottom line, the fastest processor and faster DDS RAM and solid state drives don't seem to add any power or performance so save your money and look for a Windows 7, Intel i5 if you can find one. Sometimes, you don't get what you pay for.. I wish I could have a 'do-over' but I have work to do with my so, so OK new computer.

title: this is an amazing little device
text:
For its size and price, this is an amazing little device. This thing is tiny and pretty easy to conceal. I only wish it came with some type of bracket to help mount in a vehicle. It has a very strange shape and some grooves on the side which appear like they were designed for some type of bracket to slide into. Ultimately, I will probably make something.

Video quality on the highest quality is amazingly good. It even does pretty well in low light conditions. Better than some similar devices I've tried. It has some default modes that will work without the widget, but you pretty much need to download and use it to take advantage of all its features. The widget seems pretty well designed and is fairly intuitive. I've had no problems using it. Audio could be better and in some situations it works pretty well, while other time its almost unintelligible. I believe this is just the nature of the little pinhole mike pick up. Results will vary based on the situation. I have found that sometimes the audio appears out of sync, but I'm not sure that doesn't have something to do with playback software. On the best quality, the files are pretty big and it will keep a processor busy watching the video.

Overall, it's a great little package that includes cables, power pack and just about everything you'll need except the mini SD card. Some of the earlier mini DVRs were poor quality and lacked features as well as cost a lot for the size convenience. This device takes the mini DVR to a whole new level that is light years beyond some of the earlier stuff. Having tried many other little minis, I can say that this just blows them all away and clearly has been developed to a much more advanced level.

Once you have played with it for awhile, you'll find endless uses. With a bit of creativity, concealment is pretty easy and battery life is quite good.
