title: Awesome pass thru modular crimper...
text: Excellent tool! Great heft to it at 10.3 oz. There are plenty of YT videos to learn how to use crimpers. If you are not a professional, the quality of this brand is good enough. A homeowner who occasionally needs to fix an ethernet cable, believe me, this will last you a lifetime. Search YT for "pass-thru modular crimper" and you'll get plenty of reviews and tutorials for this type of crimper. They may be different brands, different names, but just watch the videos that have the same appearance as this crimper, and you'll be good to go! 5-stars.

title: One solid power tower, the cubes do not separate...
text:
This is about 7 inches high in total from top to bottom of base. The round base has an approximate diameter of 5.5 inches, and the tower itself is about 3 inches wide. In case you're wondering, the divided lines between each outlet cube/row do not separate. There is a different power tower on Amazon where the cubes can separate and be used individually. You can check that product out here: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B089PRBZWM/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Even though the other one can separate, this one has an extra USB port and a built in flashlight. This item is also 5 stars in my book!

title: You will be getting the Triple AAA version, not Double AA.
text: Not sure if the seller is incorrectly naming his batteries because what you're getting are triple AAA batteries. Or, if in fact he is trying to sell double AA batteries and there is something wrong with the inventory. In any case, I can still find use for this AAA version. My remote controls are the things that eats up batteries the most, and they all take AAA batteries. I could have this adapter bedside, and use it for my TV remote. Your wireless keyboards most likely take AAA batteries too, so you can use it for that. Basically, anything that requires AAA batteries, but can somewhat be stationary.  I'm only subtracting 1 star because I can still use these, but I can see how someone can really be upset if they really needed the Double AA version.

title: Cool idea, but the app didn't work for me...
text:
Time stamp for this camera is incorrect, so I downloaded the OD Cam hoping to be able to set the time. After the camera has been powered up, you single click the power button to activate wi-fi. You will hear a voice say wi-fi on and you'll see a blue led light blink along next to the solid green light.

But it would never connect to the camera. The app is pretty quirky, half-baked. Once you turn on the app, it's immediately working, it will say "Connecting device..." But what is it doing? I haven't even selected their wi-fi SSID yet. Well, even after selecting the "EP7_XXXX" id, the password of 12345678 doesn't work. It keeps saying "check wi-fi and try again," then you'll hear the lady voice saying, "Wi-fi off." So it automatically turns off the wi-fi once you can't connect.

So I've been using this without the app, and without proper time stamp. There is a learning curve to understanding the camera angles when you're wearing it on your head. The camera can swivel, so you can record your funky toes, or point it up and record your water stained ceilings. LOL! Once you're happy with your recording, you can take it to your pc to view your files. There is no need to remove the micro sd card. When you plug it into your pc, the lady voice will prompt you to press the video button for removable storage mode, or the photo button for webcam mode.

Video quality is not that great, so I'm subtracting 1 star for that. I'm also subtracting another star for the half-baked app and connection process.

title: Nifty idea, but slower charging speeds...
text: [[VIDEOID:79526b07ccdde970c8fc7ce20ed2a28]] This is pretty nifty, but at the end of the day, I'm not sure how practical it is. I think we now live in a world where we have a gazillion cables in our home, so most likely you are still going to reach for whatever cable you need. Theoretically, these could be useful when you're in a bind. For whatever reason, lets say your lost your iphone cable, these will come in handy. But if you have a choice of the real cable or using this cable with the adapter, the choice will always be the real cable simply because they charge faster. You lose a bit of speed using these magnetic adapters. I know myself, I know my habits, and I'm 100% sure that I won't be able to find the box with all the adapter heads when I need it one day. LOL! These little heads looks like they can easily be lost. Very nifty, and I give it 5-stars for being something that is a reflection for the sign of the times.

title: Perfect dock for older thunderbolt Macbook...
text: Nice compact dock. Hooked up my brother's 2015 Macbook with no issues. Two usb ports, usb-c pd port, display port, hdmi, and a headphone port. Just for curiosity, we testing on windows laptop without thunderbolt, but we couldn't get the display to work on either HDMI or Display Port. The biggest con of this dock is the short and permanent thunderbolt cable. It is challenging to set up your desk exactly the way you want it when the cable is so short. Seems like they designed it with mobility in mind. 4 stars.

title: Of all the surveillance cameras I've used, this one has the best software...
text:
I've used cheap Wyze cameras as well as more expensive cameras like Arlo in my garage, but wi-fi is pretty iffy there. I wanted to see if the wi-fi receiver in this HomeHawk beats the Wyze or Arlo, but unfortunately, that's not the case. The HomeHawk struggled in my garage as much as the others did. As a matter of fact, I couldn't connect to it at all. So right off the bat, that is something to note... that paying more for a camera doesn't necessarily mean better wi-fi receivers are inside the camera. This isn't something I'm going to subtract a star for since no cameras on the market can help with my wi-fi situation, that's something that will have to be remedied by wi-fi extenders.

Now once I move this camera indoor, with better wi-fi reception, to monitor the backyard, it does the job wonderfully! The app is great and full of features. Be sure you select the proper MODE. By default, it was on BASIC and it did not do any recordings. I realize I had to change it to PROTECTION mode or 24/7 mode. Or, better yet, you can create your own mode! You can determine if it will record 24/7, or only when it detects motion. You can determine the duration of the clip. Now that is pretty cool! The default is 10 seconds, and for several weeks I thought I had to live with the default, until I discovered that I can actually change this by creating my own Mode. You can determine if it will notify you for every motion detected, or only for human detections. Lastly, you can name the mode anything you want, then select it and you're set! I've only used Wyze, Arlo and Homehawk cameras, and without a doubt, this Panasonic software is the best of the bunch. 5-stars!

title: Nice Cat 7 cables...
text: Ran these cables from garage to upstairs bedroom. No drop in speed. True shielded Cat-7. Not much to say, they get the job done.

title: Not as nice as their 8 inch frame...
text: This is our 2nd FeelCare picture frame. It works just as well as their 8 inch frame and the Frameo app is simple and awesome to use. However, my gripe bout this 10 inch version is that it doesn't look like a picture frame, it looks like a tablet. With a little effort, tablets can be turned into picture frames, so I think digital picture frames should separate themselves from tablets by actually looking like picture frames. Here is my review on the 8 inch version, you'll see that version actually looks like a picture frame. https://www.amazon.com/review/R2CMMW83H5X04G/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B08BKYZZ94 I'll give this 10 inch version 4 stars.

title: You can access motherboard from the top...
text: I do not have time yet to build out this case, but the #1 reason why I grabbed it was because you can access the motherboard I/O from the top. This is due to the vertical layout. This game changer potentially means, no more dragging out the pc and having to unplug things so that you can reach the back. Everything looks great! High quality metal or aluminum, consistent powder coating of the black color, and it isn't too heavy at 13 lbs 5 oz. I can't wait to build this out. 5-stars!

title: USB-C dock that works with my pixel slate chromebook as well as my old laptops!
text:
Hey Guys, this is it! A lot of USB-C docks do not play nice with older computers with no usb-c port. You would need to use a usb-c to usb-a male cable, or put a usb to usb-c port adapter on your laptop... but these are just solutions that are hit or miss. I tried these solutions with another dock and it was a 100% miss. Now even if you have a usb-c port, it still might not work if your device is a chromebook due to the Chrome OS. So a lot of these usb-c docks on the market were made specifically for windows pc with usb-c port. I do not own a new laptop with usb-c port. I only have older laptops with regular usb ports and the device which does have a usb-c port happens to be a chromebook. This pluggable worked for all my devices! My chromebook works perfectly with this! Not only that, using a usb-c to regular usb cable, my old dell inspiron worked with this dock as well. Instead of using a usb-c to regular usb cable, I even tested a usb to usb-c port adapter on the dell, then I plugged the usb-c cable from the pluggable into the usb-c adapter on the dell... and that worked too!!

This simply works! It is night and day compared to another dock product I was trying out that did not work for any of my devices. This is mindboggling to me actually. How could one dock not work with any of my devices, with any of my solutions and adapters, but another dock works with all my devices, all my solutions and adapters! Wow. Both docks were Vine items for me, so I have no rooting interest in either. This is 100% honest and ecstatic review! This is the one to get. Avoid this one... https://www.amazon.com/review/R32SN4BPM7SPAA/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8&ASIN=B088F7SY6S

title: High quality cables...
text: It's hard to get in depth about ethernet cables. LOL! What is there to say? I think most people just want to know do they work? Do you see a drop in speed? And to those questions, it's a Yes and No. Yes, they work as they should. No, I did not see a drop in speed. If you just need something that works, get it!

title: Perfect the curious elementary school kids...
text: We have two kids, so a great feature about this microscope is that the kids waiting for their turn can see what the person using the scope is seeing through an app.  That has helped tremendously! You don't know how useful the app is unless you have multiple kids. LOL! My son is into space and the universe, so the opposite world, the microscopic world is a great supplement to his curiosity. The scope is approximately 1 lb 8 oz without batteries. So it's not heavy duty, but the quality is adequate for the price and the age range of the users. The slides are pre-made and are interesting. We will definitely purchase blanks to do our own experiments. 5 stars!

title: Awesome cat 8 cables...
text: We wanted our NAS server to have the best cable connected to the router. This cable did the job. Checked our speed online and we're getting our advertised speeds. No complaints. 5 stars!

title: Doesn't play nice with my service and router...
text: This thing isn't big at all. You can see in the photo next to a soda can for reference. That's sort of the only positive thing I have to say about it. I have Frontier Fios and my Gateway is the ARRIS NVG468MQ. If you have this combination of service and equipment in your home, you should forget about the Dap-1955-US. I tried so hard, even went through several hrs with D-Link tech support, ultimately, we decided maybe it's defective and so I got a replacement, but to no avail. It will not connect on the replacement unit either. Not ready for prime time.

title: I'm getting top speed...
text: Needed to run ethernet from ONT in garage to adjacent bedroom. Got the job done. No speed slow down. We have fiber optics 500/500. Highly recommended.

title: Gets the job done...
text: Ran this cable from living room to garage. No issues whatsoever, getting my usual top speed via ethernet. Highly recommended!

title: No zoom, but best price in this class...
text:
In this $30-50 price range, I think you should stick with this one. We got another one listed at $40 and besides for the branding, it seems to be the same binocular with slight molding differences. The tech is the same. Don't bother spending a little more unless you really want to upgrade and get one with zoom function. All these economy versions do not have zoom. And if you're new to binoculars, there is a learning curve, but this is how you focus:

1. Set the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial to ZERO and set sight on a distant subject. I'm not sure what zero means since there are no numbers, but there are arrows, so I presume it's when the arrows line up.

2. Cover the RIGHT FRONT lens with your hand, and rotate the FOCUSING WHEEL (the middle wheel), until the image is sharp. Keep both eyes open while you make this adjustment.

3. Now cover the LEFT FRONT lens and rotate the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial until the image is sharp. So here, you're not touching the focusing wheel, you're adjusting the RIGHT EYEPIECE dial.

title: Beautiful picture frame...
text: Aesthetically, a digital picture frame should look like a picture frame, and this product knocks it out of the park. It is a beautiful looking picture frame. Everything about this item screams premium from the packaging to the frame itself. The app that this frame uses is called OUR PHOTO, and I've attached the picture to show what the user interface looks like on your phone. It is nice simplistic app. I've seen lazy products out there that want to sell as picture frames and they just look like tablets. This is what you want! 5 Stars!

title: Gets the job done...
text:
I needed another ethernet hub. I have multiple PCs at my desk, but only 1 ethernet line, so one of my PC is on wi-fi. This solved my problem.

My use case...

1. Ethernet goes into this adapter, then this adapter is plugged into a dock via the USB. The PC that uses that dock now has wired internet. Lets call this PC ONE.

2. PC TWO on the same desk can now get wired internet by connecting an Ethernet cable from PC TWO's ethernet port to one of the three remaining ethernet ports on the adapter.

Awesome product!

title: Super handy!
text: These ethernet couplings are super handy when your ethernet cord doesn't quite reach your destination. I have a mix bag of cables at home, cat 5, cat 6, cat 7, cat 8, you name it. I test them all and they all work! Not much to review here. They get the job done. 5 star.

title: High quality microphone, plug and play...
text: Plug and play, no issues. Very sensitive, so on a conference,  be sure to mute your mic if you wanna say something that's only meant for certain people in your room. For us, it's just a distance learning mic for our children. They love it because it also looks like a UFO. The weight, the material, everything about it is high quality. 5 stars.

title: Helpful if you're the tech guy in the family...
text: I don't have any long term need to share accessories with two computers. But I tinker a lot, and often times are asked to troubleshoot family and friend's computers. Instead of having to swap out cables, this makes setting up a new PC a breeze. Not just minor peripherals, you can connect docks to this and it will share it between your computers. Everything is connected to my dock.. the monitor, the mouse, keyboards, etc. So I take up only 1 port on this switcher, the usb that's coming from the dock. Highly recommend this product. 5 stars!

title: High quality multi-purpose stands...
text: Super nice set of stand/risers. They are made of metal and built to last. The legs have detents that will allow the pins to click into place. Use them in the kitchen or the office, very versatile. 5 stars.

title: High quality camera, but it runs very hot currently...
text:
Okay, you know the saying about first impressions? Presentation matters in a "premium" product. Anything north of $200, I expect good packaging. This Panacast is priced over $500 and has a retail of nearly a $1000. This is iPhone territory, yet the thin cardboard box with creases looks like packaging you'd find on any other white label gadget coming outta China. It was smushed a little cause it was shipped in an Amazon white padded envelope. If it weren't for the fact that this is a Vine item for me, I'd be so upset.

As for the camera itself, it is pretty nifty and the quality is what you'd expect for something over $500. It is small, but when you hold it in your hands, you feel the heft of the metal. It is definitely not one of those cheap lightweight plastic cameras. However, they got to do something about the heat. After a few minutes, you can fry eggs with it. It runs hot! I hope future firmware can do something about this.

There is nothing obvious in terms of picture or video quality that would separate this from the $100 stuff on the market. They all look the same to me. The 180 degree is the reason you're getting this. If you download their JabraDirect software, you'll have more control over the camera. For instance, you can lock in at a certain degree. I like to play around with the 180 degree, so initially I was annoyed that it kept automatically zooming in and out on me due to movement. The desktop software will allow you to lock in on any degree you want. I'm sure this will make a fine camera for business settings, but for us, it's simply for video calls with relatives overseas. Grandparents will often say, "what's my little boy doing over there?" Well, now they get to have a wider view.

The price, the underwhelming packaging, and the heat issue... I'm knocking 2 stars.

title: Soft quiet keyboard....
text: Some don't like the keyboard saying it's mushy, but to me, it's quiet, which is perfect if you're a night owl but your significant other isn't. LOL! Wrist pad perfect for average hands. The media controls work very well with youtube, netflix, etc. For some reason, I always struggle looking for the calculator app, so I like the calculator button in the far right that launches the app for you. Overall, a pretty nice user experience. The mouse is pretty standard, nothing to write home about. I do have a recommendation for the Logitech Unifying Receiver software... it would be nice if the software would tell you, "This mouse or keyboard has already been unified." I was trying to sync this keyboard, but I had forgotten that I had done it already. So when I was turning the on/off slider to sync, there was no reaction and I was puzzled for the longest time. It turns out nothing is wrong with the hardware, but something is wrong with my short term memory. LOL! So again, a pop-up notification saying the device is already paired would be nice.

title: Nice screen, but the buttons won't be kind to big hands/fingers...
text:
I don't know how these things are made, but I thought it was kinda strange that it's touch screen when you connect it to a computer, but the screen itself is not touch screen. So to mess around with the screen's settings you have to use these side buttons on the left. One of the button is designated as the back button, the other allows you to toggle by sliding the button up or down, then pushing in to select. I don't have the biggest hands or chubbiest fingers in the world, I'm relatively skinny, yet I found it difficult. If your fingers are muscular, you might not like these controls. If you're selling in the US market, it would be nice if the default language was set to English, but it is not, it was in Chinese, and it took me awhile to finally set it to English.

I'm not sure what's my use case scenario for this yet. I wanted to hook up a fire stick to see if this can be used for movies on the road, but there is only a mini HDMI port. I do have a USB-C to Female HDMI adapter, but it did not work. I was getting "NO SIGNAL" when I hooked up the fire stick to my adapter. As a PC monitor, it works very well. I also hooked up the Nintendo Switch and confirm it works, so that's something you can do, play the Switch on the road with a bigger screen. The stand is magnetic and very slim. I'll give this 4 stars.

title: Very versatile!
text: This tower strip is very versatile. I think the only thing that beats it in versatility are the power strips with pivoting outlets. You can use the lower base by itself, and you can plug the top base directly into a wall outlet too. The only thing they could have improved was perhaps more usb outlets because this thing is huge, and for it to only fit 2 usb outlets is puzzling. I put a coke can to show you how big it is. In any case, it needs to be big so power adapters don't get in each other's way. 5 star item!

title: A little more versatile than the standard strip...
text: My headline says "a little" because I tried several adapters that wouldn't fit next to each other. But as you can see in their stock photos, smaller profile adapters like apple may fit side by side. The most versatile power strips are the ones with the pivoting outlets. This donut strip gets the job done and even has 2 usb ports, but since it's an odd shape for a power strip, I thought there may have been a reason for it, but since it provides no advantage, it's just a different shape for the sake of being different. Nothing wrong with that. I'll go 4 stars.

title: Windows 10 Pro with energy efficient hardware...
text:
We've been grabbing a few of these mini pcs to test them out and see if they're good for Distance Learning. We have a lot of spare pc peripherals including old school 4:3 screens. But for many, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But if you do have these accessories laying around, and you're curious how this Minix works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great! I just reviewed a Beelink mini pc that is very capable too.

The 1080p camera, microphone, speakers and monitor connected with no issues. Windows did all the firmware work. The only software we had to fetch was Logitech's unifying receiver for the keyboard and mouse. In California, many k12 schools are using CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy.

It's mind-boggling that Windows 10 Pro is $200 alone. Of course if you're going to pay full price for Windows 10 pro, you wouldn't put it in a low end computer. Nevertheless, it is awesome that it's included here. I recently reviewed the Beelink T4 which has the Z8500 cpu. On paper, that's slightly a faster cpu, but interestingly, the Z8350 in the Minix is a newer cpu. They may have made the Z8350 more efficient or something. In any case, normal human beings won't be able to tell the difference. LOL! The MINIX Z83-4 Plus is a little bigger than the Beelink T4, but comes with a wifi antennae, and a built in micro SD reader.

Basic activities such as web browsing, watching Netlfix, Youtube, kids doing work on ClassLink, etc., this mini pc is very capable.

title: All plastic, no 1080P recording, and read my advice regarding micro sd card insertion...
text:
I used to have a cheaper one where you connect it to your smartphone, so when I saw this I grabbed it. I read two reviews where one said you cannot record 1080p, but the other said that you could. You know there are cheap cameras everywhere recording 1080p. For $90, I'm disappointed to confirm the reviewer who said this only records videos in VGA and snap pictures at 720p. 1080p is only for onscreen viewing. This won't be a big deal for me since I'm not in a profession that uses this daily. I figure it's nifty to have in the toolbox, and perhaps know my way around my walls. For example, last month I drilled a hole into my wall, thinking I can drop some cables down, but the cables hit a horizontal beam. I think in construction this is called a fire stop. Hopefully this will help me learn the paths I could take in my walls.

For a professional who will use this daily, who perhaps would like to bring back a picture or a video and blow it up on his monitor for a more detailed view, 1980's VGA quality is a big thumbs down! The build quality is also not substantial either. Everything is plastic. The whole unit is about 13.5 ounces.

I do like all the provided accessories, especially the hook. I can see how that will come in handy. To view something in the wall or pipe and to pry it out with the hook. The cable is stiff and bendable allowing you to position your lens just the way you want it.

IMPORTANT ADVICE REGARDING MICRO SD CARD!!!
------------------------------------------------------------
Be very careful when removing and inserting the sd card. You have to be sure to look at the slot, and be sure you slide the card in completely horizontal. If you slide it in at an angle, it will actually still go in, completely in! I made this mistake and the card was rattling around behind the LCD screen. LOL! Luckily, the screen was easy to take apart. Just 5 screws in the back and I was able to pry it in half and retrieve my card. When inserting the card, remember the orientation... with the LCD screen facing the ceiling, the card's gold contact side should also be facing the ceiling.

This is a 5 star product for hobbyist like me. I don't see myself recording much, if at all. For a professional, I think the shortcomings make it a 3 star product. So I'm rating this a 4.

title: Capable as a Distance Learning pc....
text:
We're using this for Distance Learning because we have a plethora of spare PC accessories at home. If you have the following items:

Monitor
speakers (if monitor doesn't have any)
Keyboard, Mouse
Camera
Microphone

So as you can see, an all in one chromebook or cheap laptop is still infinitely more convenient. But in case you do have these accessories and you're curious how it works for Distance Learning, I'm happy to report it's great!

Our 1080p camera was installed no issues. Logitech unifying software was installed for the keyboard and mouse, no issues. Microphone and speakers, no issues. Besides for the Logitech unifying receiver, everything was plug and play without needing to go to 3rd party sites for software. If you have kids, then you know about CLASSLINK and GOOGLE CLASS. I don't know about other states, but in California, that's what many schools are using. I went into my child's account, played around with all the apps. Opened and closed browsers, everything was pretty snappy. This will work! For basic needs, this will work. We do have a chromebook too, but I'd like for my kids to learn Windows as well. Best of all, Windows 10 is pre-installed, which is $130 on Amazon. Why not spend an extra $10 and get a mini PC too? LOL! This thing is so tiny, it could be used as a coaster for your Coke, but I wouldn't recommend that. It comes with hardware so you can hang it on the back of your monitor. In the last picture, you can see it's even smaller than a competitor mini pc, the MINIX Z83-4 Plus.

This is $140 folks! If you push it, you will be disappointed. If you use it for basic stuff like web surfing, or for your elementary child to do things on ClassLink.. you'll be happy.

title: Perhaps not compatible with older computers and Chromebooks...
text:
10/13/2020 UPDATE:
----------------------------
After trying another dock by Plugable, I stand by my original review 100%, the Anker dock is NOT ready for prime time. Or, it is, and you just need to have newer devices. Everything that did not work with the Anker, they all worked for me with the Plugable. Both the Anker and the Plugable are Vine products for me, so I have not rooting interest in either. This was my persona experience. This is the other dock that worked perfectly for me with all my devices... https://www.amazon.com/review/RB4NOJ0TLOOIA/ref=cm_cr_srp_d_rdp_perm?ie=UTF8

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
--------------------------
I tried and tried, but it just didn't work for me. Perhaps you truly need newer tech? I contacted Anker to get some info. They told me I absolutely have to use a USB-C to USB-C cable. Which basically means, only newer pcs and laptops. I was connecting the dock to my windows laptop with a USB-C to USB-A cable. Anker says this is not sufficient power, but my laptop has it's own power source and the Anker has its own power source, and the HDMI goes from the Anker to the monitor. Why can't this work?

So in any case, the only USB-C powered "laptop" I have is my Google Pixel Slate. Again, the Anker is connected with its own power source, and since my slate has two usb-c ports, I gave power to the Slate independently instead of having the Anker dock be the sole source. Then the other USB-C port is then connected from the Slate to the Dock. From here, HDMI out from Dock to monitor.... drum roll.... still no dice. I tried two dell monitors, so I figure lets try a normal tv, and unfortunately, no picture there either.

Perhaps I just don't have the proper USB-C laptop or tablet that's compatible with this dock. Perhaps it's not compatible with the Pixel Slate since it's running on Chrome. I dunno... Perhaps there is a firmware update that can fix this? I went to Anker's site. Went to SUPPORT. Clicked on UPDATE FIRMWARE. I was given three choices... Cables, Audio or Hubs and Docks! This is getting exciting! Perhaps there is a firmware update! So I clicked on Hubs and Docks and downloaded the software for Windows. But when I ran the software, it turns out to be an updater for their Speakers. :( Anker told me perhaps it's defective, so we did a replacement to no avail, it still doesn't display for me. All the other ports work fine, just no display.

My computer gear is top of the line from about 5 yrs ago. One of which is a Vaio Canvas Z, but neither have USB-C. My only USB-C laptop is the Pixel Slate, but it's a chromebook. Maybe you need a recent windows laptop with USB-C? I would appreciate any info in the comments section. Anybody who got theirs to work with a PC that doesn't have USB-C, please comment below. If you got it to work with a Chromebook, please comment below. Please let me know what you did. For me, it's not displaying anything, but all the usb ports, card reader, ethernet work fine. I will update and revise my rating if I can get it to display. Otherwise, it's a nice looking dock, sleek and compact.

title: Triangle face is not made of metal...
text:
About build and quality... Based on the pictures and based on the price tag, I was hoping for something of higher quality. I thought the camera looked compact and heavy duty in the stock photos. But the body is mainly black plastic, and the triangle face is actually chrome plated plastic. The clip is also light weight, but I think it could actually be aluminum or something. The entire thing weighs 4.8 oz with the attached cable. I tried taking off the cable from the scale, and it showed the camera to be 3 oz.

Does it work? Yes, on my windows 10, everything was automatic. I plugged it in and the computer did the rest. You don't need to go to any site for any drivers. Camera image quality is awesome, and easy to clip onto your monitor.
There are a plethora of cameras to choose, most of them have the same logitech black body type design. I decided on this one because it was unique. It looks like an alien robot head or something. If you like Transformers, I think this would go well with your decor. However, at this price, I'm just a little disappointed in the build quality. So I'm subtracting 1 star.

title: Perfect with OBS Studio...
text: I currently own an El Gato HD60S, a ClearClick 4k PC-less capture card, and this Unisheen capture card. Of the three cards, this Unisheen does not require a HDMI splitter to bypass HDCP for my smart devices. This a pleasant surprise! However, I did have audio issues to begin with. title: Complicated, but it got rid of HDCP for me...
text:
08/13/2020 UPDATE:
-------------------------
All right, so a quirk that some of you may encounter is that when you connect the splitter, your TV may turn on Action Smoothing automatically. I have a TCL and that's the term they use. Other TVs may go by a different term. But essentially, it is the "soap opera" effect. It is great for sports, but weird for movies. But when I turned it back to off, the "soap opera" effect was still there. So I thought the splitter overrides the TCL settings, which would make it unusable for me. But on a hunch, I decided to unplug the TCL tv, and when I replugged, the "soap opera" effect was gone. So if you're experiencing this, try unplugging your TV and replugging it. I was able to reproduce this quirk with a different HDMI splitter, so this is not an issue with the HDMI splitter, it is an issue with the TV being stuck on Action Smoothing... In my case, it's a TCL.

Original Review
------------------
I needed to disable HDCP for a PC-less capture card. This splitter is more advanced than any splitter I have ever used. I'm used to the splitters that just splits and has no settings. This splitter makes you use your brain, and sometimes I don't want to use my brain. After a lot of tinkering with the various combinations of the switches, I ended up leaving the EDID at COPY1 and the Scaler switches to OFF... which was actually the default settings they ship to you. LOL!

Also understand that for every setting you play around with, if you don't get a picture, it might not mean it doesn't work. Along with your settings, you need to try switching your tv inputs back and forth, turning off/on your sources, turning off/on your capture card, etc., to truly see if it works. This will be the most confusing and frustrating part of setting this up. Not to mention, do you have the proper HDMI cables? Manual says use HDMI 2.0 cables. A lot of my cables are 1.3 or 1.4, but it still worked. So maybe if I had some HDMI 2.0 cables, it would have saved me some headache?

Ultimately, I stumbled upon the fact that if I leave it at COPY1 and Scalers off, turn off my capture card, then turn it back on, as well as switch tv input, then switch it back. It works! And it's not something you always need to do every time you turn on your tv. It's a one time thing. Once the splitter and your devices are in sync, you're good to go. There is one more step you can take if this doesn't work. There is a pinhole on the splitter labeled "UPDATE." Right on the splitter itself, there are printed notes on what this pinhole is for. Basically after resetting switches, changing inputs, etc., and you still have video or audio issues such as garbled noises, you need to use a tiny pin key, like the ones supplied by your smartphones to remove your sim trays. Poke it inside and feel for a button. Press it until it flashes 3 times. I guess this does some sort of "update" telling the splitter.. "Hey, these are the new settings, get with the program!" It worked for me in fixing garbled audio.

I will acknowledge that user experience and expertise level in AV tech plays a role in how much "tinkering" is necessary. The less you know, the more you're going to tinker. Still, I think the manual could be better and more in depth, maybe provide a pin key for the pinhole? Regarding this pinhole, the instructions says to push the "button." There is no button, and I had to look around for my sim key. For most consumers, this won't be "plug and play" as the listing suggest. But it works, and I will go 4 stars for this.

title: You will need a HDMI splitter....
text:
THINGS YOU WILL NEED:
----------------------------
-HDMI Splitter that can bypass HDCP (For digital caputuring. What device isn't digital nowadays?)
-Flash drive or Hard Drive: Maximum flash drive space is 256gb. Maximum hard drive is 8tb.

As a kid, I used to love recording tv or cable to VHS. Then in the late 90's and early 2000's, I was into those Hard Drive recorders with built in dvd-r burners by Pioneer and Philips, remember those? But then Tivo and Cable DVR really took off and made recording to actual dvds a thing of the past. So what we have here with the ClearClick is simply a device that brings the "old way" of archiving to 2020, but instead of VHS and DVR-Rs, it will record as MP4 files into your flash drive. I also think the reason these devices are still relevant is due to the phenomenon of gamers who love to record all their game-play. Anyway, I'm happy to report it does exactly what it advertises brilliantly. However, unless you're only capturing analog signals (VHS transers), you will need a HDMI splitter that can bypass HDCP. In my use case scenario... I have a Caavo Universal Remote/HDMI Switcher. The Caavo has four HDMI inputs. I have my Tivo, a Fire TV, a Android TV box, and the Nintendo Switch hooked to it. Then it has one HDMI output. This output normally goes to the TV. So that's my set-up...

Now to hook up this ClearClick, I remove the HDMI that connects to the TV from the Caavo, and instead, I connect it to the Input of the special HDMI Splitter. Then HDMI OUT from this splitter to the input of the ClearClick. Finally, HDMI OUT from the ClearClick to an input on my TV. This way, I can capture from any device I want that's connected to my Caavo. Of course, you can just connect one source at a time too if you don't have a hub like I do. But remember, you need to connect your source to the HDMI splitter first. If you don't, you will just get a black screen that says "unsupported format." One more thing, the HDMI splitter obviously has 2 HDMI outs, one of which is going to the ClearClick. I also use the second HDMI out to connect directly to another input on my TV. The reason is to avoid having to turn on the ClearClick when I'm not recording.

The spliiter I use is called the ViewHD Model: VHD-1X2MN3D. You can find this on Amazon. However, I believe it is still YMMV (your mileage may vary.) I bought that years ago and it still works. But if you search in the reviews for that splliter, some do complain it didn't work for them. Sometimes a different batch has different chipsets, I dunno. So it may take trial and error before you get a splitter that works. I also have a 4tb Western Digital passport connected the ClearClick, and it works perfectly.

Lastly, inside the box, they give you a free license of Videopad software. This is so you can touch up your recordings, add effects, transitions, or even output to DVD. Before I registered my copy, I wanted to see how much this software cost, so I proceeded to purchase as if I didn't have a code. So currently, it's listed as $99, but it is on sale for $35 until August 15. We get it free!

title: Not just for displaying photos, I have some outside the box ideas...
text:
I've always thought photo frames are gimmicky, but FeelCare has changed my mind. The difference in using these versus turning a tablet into a photo frame is that it SIMPLY WORKS as it should. Getting a tablet to be a photo frame is quite involved and requires more maintenance. Also, this item actually looks like a picture frame! You can designate sleep hours for the frame so that it's not always on 24/7. I have mine asleep from 1 am to 8 am. Techies will turn old tablets into photo frames, but I think the main market here is for older people who are not techies. Here are some outside the box ideas...

A joke on your friends:
--------------------------

He'll be like, "What the... why do you have a picture of my mom?" LOL! -------------------

title: Easy peasy back up!
text:
I read some of the reviews and concerns. Many are saying you need the original power adapter. My testing says that is NOT true. I plugged this cube into two separate charging hubs, not apple brand, and both scenarios worked.

You need a micro SD card (not included). Some of the questions in the Q&A shows that shoppers don't realize this. There is no built in hard drive in this cube, you provide the storage.

Turning off auto-sleep/auto-lock may get you through thousands of pictures in one shot. This is what I mean... I'm no stranger to trying out different back-up programs. The current program we use is from Plex. When the iphone is backing up to my plex server, the iphone doesn't know that plex is working, so it goes to sleep after about 50 pictures. When it goes to sleep, plex stops backing up. So I always turn off auto-sleep prior to backing up. With the Qubii, the iphone KNEW that it was working, so it "almost" never went to sleep. I said almost because after 4000 files, for some reason, the phone went to sleep. Still, this is much, much, better than the plex app. When I started Qubii again, it picked up where it left off and backed the remaining 1000+ files. But I did the test one more time to make sure! I cleared the micro sd card, and I reset the Qubii count. This time I turned off auto-sleep/auto-sleep on the iphone, and it backed-up the entire camera roll of over 5000 photos and videos in one shot! More trials need to be done to conclusively say this thing can't get through 5000 files without the auto-sleep disabled.

After backing up everything, you should remove your SD card from the Qubii and transfer them to a larger permanent hard drive where you store your collection. The next time you charge your phone, the Qubii will remember the photos it already backed-up even if those photos are no longer on the SD card. So you can always clear your SD card. For whatever reason, if you need the Qubii to back-up the same photos again, like I did when I was testing things out, all you have to do is RESET the Qubii count, which you can do in the Back Up Settings in the app.

Below are the two pictures showing you the scenarios in which I tested this Qubii. Both scenarios used third party charging hubs, but I believe I had the original apple cable. As with all products dependent on apps.. one Apple update can ruin everything. LOL! So these types of app products depend on the company to stick around, so that if Apple breaks anything, they can fix it with a new firmware update. Qubii was on Kickstarter, but only time will tell. As is, this is an amazing product.

title: Subtle Wavy Diagonal Lines....

title: One word.... UNCOMFORTABLE.
text:
At $160, I said Nah. At $120, I said let me check this out, and my instincts were right, this is a no-go. Brydge seems to be a legit aspiring company, but I hope they go back to the drawing board and add upper cases to their keyboard design. So that you can put your tablet in a case, then the case connects to the keyboard, a perfect example of this design is an iPad keyboard made by Yoozon, I just reviewed it, it is awesome. There is absolutely no fear of damaging the screen with that type of design. But as for this Brydge keyboard, one word sums up my experience.. uncomfortable.

So there are 3 issues with this design:

1. There is no case, your tablet is exposed. This is not a deal-breaker, I knew it going in. But understand nobody makes any cases for pixel slate. Even Brydge makes a bunch of cases for various ipads complete with slots cut-out so that they can be slide right into their hinge keyboards. But there are no such products for the Slate, so you'll expose it to scatches.

2. Light bleeding in the corner caused by the hinges. I knew this going in as well, but I was thinking maybe it's paranoia. At $120, I wanted to check it out. And honestly, playing with it did not ease my concerns. You don't see any light bleeding at all, but you do see it when you close it like a laptop and the hinge is applying its pressure. I tried to reproduce this light bleed by applying pressure with my thumb, and I could not get it to bleed. So this tells me the hinge is applying a tremendous amount of pressure. Right now, the bleeding goes away the moment it's opened, but by opening and closing constantly and daily, I fear one day the bleeding will stay lit because I've seen this issue on normal laptops.

3. The hinge is a very thin sharp metal. The padding is what prevents it from scratching your tablet. But the padding for one hinge was no longer sticking flush with the metal. It would get caught at times when I'm sliding in the tablet. Good thing I was careful because if you carelessly trust the product, it can scratch your tablet if the rubber gets caught and pulled. Hard to articulate what I'm saying, so I've attached a photo to show you the separation of the rubber from the thin metal hinge. After a couple of uses, it was a chore for me to carefully slide the tablet in because that rubber kept getting caught. A little disappointed that just one day into this testing, I already have to resort to glue?

Like I said... uncomfortable. Brydge, please continue to focus on rigid hinge keyboards. You're on the right path. This is what we want. We want rigidness and lappability, but please design a detachable case so that the case takes the brunt of the hinge pressure, as well as protect the tablet from scratches exactly like the Yoozon design I mentioned above.

title: So much more than Harmony
text:
I was using the Harmony companion for the longest time, and before that, the Harmony 900. This Caavo is by far the best universal remote because it's so much more than that. Harmony is just a remote, it does not give you one unified user interface. If you've played around with a Smart TV's user interface, then you'll get the idea what this Caavo is all about. Except with Smart TV's, you still have to reach for your other devices' remotes, and if any device has voice search, it's only good for that specific device. The Caavo controls and searches all your devices! If I have a movie that's in my Tivo, that's in my plex, that is also available on Netflix.. all the choices are presented to me, so I can launch it from whichever device I choose. I have PLEX as my search priority, and it works beautifully. I was also a little nervous when hooking everything up because my TV is a Samsung from 2009, my Audio system is Sony from 2010. The Caavo has ZERO issues controlling everything.

My set-up.

Input 1: Tivo
Input 2. Fire TV
Input 3: Chromecast
Input 4: Currently Nothing
Optical OUT to my SONY AV system

My TIVO is set as the default. So when I push the power button on the remote. The Sony AV system comes on, tv comes on, and Tivo is what I'm watching! I was pleasantly surprised that it has all my Tivo controls because each button does double duty by short or long press. Let's say I want to watch a movie, I use the voice search to say BACK TO THE FUTURE, and since Plex is my priority, CAAVO gives me a list of choices with Plex highlighted. If it's in my tivo, netflix, prime, etc. it will give me all the options, but Plex will be highlighted since I set it as my priority. If I hit play, the Caavo switches input to my fire tv, launches Plex and auto-starts Back to the Future. And it happens fairly quickly. It's buttery smooth. If your preferred device to play Plex is on something else, say a Roku, you can set Roku as the default to launch Plex. If I fling something from my phone to the Chromecast, Caavo switches to my Chromecast input automatically. The voice search is perfect for youtube too because If you search something that doesn't sound like a movie, for example, How to Shop For a Miter Saw, the search results will show that there is no such movie, but included in the search results are youtube WEB searches, so you can easily play a youtube video on how to shop for a miter saw. LOL! Youtube is something I mainly do on my phone or pc because of the typing involved. But because of Caavo's voice search, we're watching it more on the big screen.

BTW, the voice recognition is terrific. It's pretty much on par with anything else out there. I've seen videos where some guy is complaining that he says Open Plex and it keeps giving him search results for DUPLEX. I don't know if Caavo has improved since his reviews, or if it just didn't like his voice, but I've never had an issue with Caavo not understanding what I said. Alexa, Google Assistant, etc. can also be integrated, but I don't see them as an efficient way to use Caavo, unless you lost the Caavo remote, then you can ask Alexa to turn on your tv I guess.

There is a slight learning curve, but it will be time well spent. And it will be easy to teach to your household members because it simply works. Lets face it, non-techies in the home will never touch your Harmony, right? I've used Harmony for 10 yrs, and nobody in my family touches it. They know how to use this Caavo!! This is a game changer!

July 17, 2019 UPDATE:
--------------------------
If you have Plex as your search default, I have a tip for you. The voice search will not understand funky spelling. For example the documentary "Comix: Beyond the Pages." The voice search will spell Comix correctly as COMICS, and so you will get zero results. But if you simply say "Beyond the Pages," the search engine will be able to find "Comix: Beyond the Pages" for you. Another quirk I ran into was "Mr. and Mrs. Smith." Even though the search engine spelled it exactly as my Plex has it, for some reason it didn't find this title. But if I just say, "Smith," it then pulls up the movie for me. So basically when you hit a snag, just use fewer words instead of saying the whole title. That's it! I really love this feature of the Caavo.

title: 4.5 blue ribbon Romance Junkies review
text:
At the tender age of fourteen, Davie Adams's life is ripped apart. His mother's loose ways leads to a series of events that leave him homeless after his she dies in his arms. Grief-stricken, Davie makes the decision to leave Blackburn and go in search of his father.

Davie could have returned to his grandfather's house but he can't imagine remaining in Blackburn and having to endure the pitying looks and talk about his mother. After his mother's collapse, Davie runs for help and finds Tom Makepeace. They get his mother situated in the back of his wagon and are getting ready to head to the infirmary but she passes away moments later. Immediately afterward Davie jumps from the wagon and runs into the woods. Everyone assumes he'll return. Tom even yells into the woods for Davie to come to his home when he's ready that he's welcome there. Davie has other plans though.

He does go to the Makepeace's home but it's only to spend the night in their barn. He hadn't expected anyone to see him but Judy, Tom's daughter and Davie's longtime friend spots him from her window. She goes out to see him and reassures him that his mother's body is taken care of and his grandfather will be just fine. Judy realizes that Davie has to do what he feels is right for him but she also knows that her feelings for him have gone beyond friendship.

Davie leaves the following morning with nothing more than the desire to leave his memories behind him. Life on his own isn't everything he thought it would be and his search for his father proves fruitless. For years Davie travels and holds many different jobs but through it all Judy and his life in Blackburn remain firmly at the forefront of his mind.

THE LONER is sure to pull at readers' heartstring. Spanning over an eight year time period, you get a lot of insight into the characters' personalities and backgrounds. I love that Josephine Cox doesn't focus solely on Davie and Judy's story, there are many other characters who possess stories of their own which add a feeling of realism to this storyline. Davie's journey of self discovery is the main theme and it's a story you won't want to miss. Josephine Cox is a gifted storyteller who knows how to keep readers engrossed page after page so that the doldrums of winter just disappear.

Chrissy Dionne (courtesy of Romance Junkies)
