title: Worst Tripod I've Ever (Tried)! Poor Engineering!
text:
I really wanted to use this. I absolutely hate this tripod. I own several. Upon extending the legs to set it up, it broke and I cannot fix it. There are these little thin, plastic tabs inside each piece of tubing that extends. The washer came off, the plastic tabs went flying, I placed them back, and the leg was stuck. I tried to retrieve them to try placing it again, and they were lost in the larger section of tubing. I carefully and methodically removed the larger washer to find the tabs, and they were so far up inside I couldn't retrieve them, so I replaced the plastic tabs from the larger piece, carefully placed it back... and low and behold those disappeared inside as well.

This is the worst engineered product I have ever encountered in my life. I cannot fathom paying anything for this. It's worthless garbage to me now. It cannot be used. I feel sorry for all the people that spent precious time of their life designing, manufacturing, selling and shipping this piece of trash. An entire tripod leg will no longer fix into place, because of these thin plastic tabs. Maybe this could have been saved by threading the adjustment washers differently, or even a piece of tape holding the plastic tabs. I cannot say for sure. What I can say is, this would be a waste of money. It's much too easy to unscrew the washers, then those tabs come out. They cannot be placed back. Once they are inside the tube, they are gone.

If I can somehow manage to fix this, I will update. Until then, don't waste your money. I would not even recommend this to someone I don't like.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you have found it helpful.

title: Great Microphone for Hobbyists, Gamers and Bloggers
text:
A warning to first time users, you may experience the microphone picking up background noise. It's very sensitive. Be prepared to set-up an area for recording if you are wanting to get clean audio. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came in a fairly plain box with a large hard foam protective insert. This microphone seems to be a great starting point for anyone interested in a higher quality microphone. I can whole heartedly recommend it.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone is a USB interface microphone that is a large step-up in quality to those used to the basic microphones that come with many web cameras. It provides a higher sensitivity to sounds; enabling both a greater ability to pick up lower volume noises and the ability to comprehend higher volume ones.

The lower volumes it was able to obtain included whispering, including the mouth noises associated with ASMR videos, and keystrokes from a non-mechanical keyboard roughly 6 feet away [With it's recording volume turned down to 50%]. On the higher end of volume it is able to accommodate singing, yelling, and screaming; by not topping out what it able to accommodate this allowed for wide arrays of vocals and would assist with those wanting to record instruments. I did many different experiments to test the range at home on different days.

The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone came with a short stand and pop filter that is attached to the stand by goose neck. The stand and metallic goose neck are both adjustable to assist with angling, but it is not vertically adjustable. The microphone, when pointing directly up, is about 26 cm / 10 in in height to the top of the microphone. It has a rubber ball footed desktop tripod for stability. The microphone can also detach from the included stand and be mounted to a standard size tripod or any other compatible stand, making the pop filter necessary depending on setup.

I had a great experience using VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone to audition for a voice acting role organized by fellow fans of an animated series. The VIMVIP USB Condenser Microphone certainly made me sound much better than my webcam microphone is able to do. I have been using this for cooperative game-play online as well. This is a great value, especially at the price point.

Thank you for reading my review. I hope you have found it informative and helpful.

title: I Wish I Had These Sooner!
text:
For my uses, these are great. They were very well packaged and secure for shipping. The box is very nice and sturdy, lined with foam. I need to hear the environment around me. This has been an issue with previous earbuds. Commercials between videos or songs can get so loud! That is the deal-breaker for me, as it's a safety issue. These do not get too loud, even on the loudest setting, so I am able to remain safe. I don't have an issue hearing the sounds coming from the buds, but I'm not in high-traffic outdoor areas regularly either. My ear canals are unusually small for an adult. I was afraid these may be too-big, but they are snug. Any bigger and it may have been an issue. I used the smaller of the plastic tips. Over the ear designs are the only ones that have ever worked for me. I did look at some other models in the past, but I found them a bit more expensive than I felt justified to spend unknowing how well they may work for me. However, knowing how well these work, I find them to be a really great value and would have purchased them before if I had known how well they worked. It was only by chance they were up for review and I had been seeking a replacement on my old pair that I've been using for the past few years.

The Bluetooth is nice. I have a simple cell phone. It only took asking my phone to connect to work. It was the easiest that I have ever had with connecting anything Bluetooth to my phone. I liked this as I'm not the most savvy at using Bluetooth electronics. If I can do it, anyone can.

I'm not great at using the buttons as they are really sensors on the flat-side of the body on the earbuds. I'm getting used to it but they are touch sensitive and there is a correct spot and amount of pressure that works best. I'm still getting a feel for it and there is a slight delay, so it's very easy to double-tap. The included booklet has been helpful to learn to use these straight out of the package.

Sometimes I get down on the floor at the gym to use the foam rollers and stretches, other times I'm using them in the car to take calls. I've tried them at work as well. Every scenario has worked well for me. I really do wish I've had these before. Sometimes while getting my breaks at work, I would want to listen to things from my phone, but didn't want to risk disturbing my co-workers with some of the news and hobby related videos I enjoy. I asked a few co-workers if they could hear my earbud noise, they could not.

The case is very easy to use as well and fits easily into my pockets. I'm a lady, so my pockets are not always very generously sized. It charges very quickly, and I've not found myself running out of charge. I cannot speak on the long-term durability for this as they are new. If/when I experience any issues with the charge, I will be sure to post an update.

In summary, these would be better for users that need to hear their surroundings for safety. For those that want extreme high volume, they may not be as happy. They stay on my ears securely and the case works very well. I'm pleasantly surprised how well I like these and hope that they are durable since they are working so well for me.

Thanks for reading my review. I hope you found it helpful.

title: Takes great pictures!
text:
This is a great little camera. It takes surprisingly good pictures. I guess I wasn't expecting much for a kids camera. It is pretty easy to operate. All the pictures in my review were taken on my recent visit to Colorado. As you can see, it handled a variety of shots with aplomb. The wildflowers was a closeup, the two landscapes were long shots with varying light conditions. The stained glass shot is the ceiling on the Broadmore Hotel in Colorado Springs. Everything came out clear and beautiful. I am not very steady when I hold a camera, so I was pleasantly surprised to find that most of my shots aren't fuzzy or blurred from my wobbly camera holding.

The only reason I didn't give this camera a top rating is because of the viewfinder. There isn't one, and the view screen is stationary. There is no way to rotate it or adjust it so that you can see what you are trying to shoot from any angle that you might hold it at. That made getting a good shot very challenging. The wildflower shot, for instance, was taken completely blind. I could not see the view screen at all. That would have meant crawling on the ground to see the screen. I can't get on the ground (mobility issues). I had to just gold the camera in front of the flowers and snap the picture, hoping for the best. The other issue is that, because you can't adjust the view screen, lighting conditions often make the screen unseeable, even if you are looking straight at it. The second landscape photo (the one on the right) was impossible to see what I was shooting at, even though I was looking directly at the screen. The lighting prevented me from being able to see the screen. Luckily, I got a good shot anyway, but I really don't like shooting blind.

So, overall, I recommend this camera. It is a good beginning camera. Very basic, takes good photos. It's just hard to use in some circumstances.

title: Nice little notebook
text:
I admit, I haven't been a fan of Chromebooks in the past, but I decided to give this one a try. I have been pleasantly surprised. I like this little notebook/pixelbook is really nice. I like how light it is. It is very portable and will fit in a backpack, large purse or tote.

One of the reasons I didn't like these before, was simply because I didn't like Chrome as a browser. Now though, you can load a different browser on it, so I put Firefox...my preferred browser. It doesn't work 100% the way I'm used to, but it is close enough, and I have all my bookmarks from my other devices that use Firefox.

Another thing that has been improved is the size. The last one I had was really small. The keyboard felt cramped and I couldn't type on it properly. I kept hitting the wrong keys, because the spacial arrangement of the keys was too small. This one is great...very functional. My hands rest comfortably on the keyboard, everything is spaced logically for maximum ease of use. My only issue is a small one. I am a touch typist and don't like to look at the keyboard, even when first placing my hands on the keyboard. Most keyboards have a tiny dot, or something on the letters "f" and "j" so that you can find your "home row" without looking. There is a tiny raised bar at the leading edge of those letters, but they are almost imperceptible. I keep having to look down to make sure my hands are placed correctly. It annoys me to no end. I think I will find a way to modify those keys just for my own sanity's sake.

This Chromebook comes with no instructions...at all. Granted, it is easy to set up, you just open it and go, but then you have to figure things out by asking Google play (oh yeah, you need to have a Google account to use this) or Googling it. An example is, how the screen is displayed when browsing. Every website I went to was reading my device as if it was a cell phone. I was getting a slender column of content that was too tiny to read and only filled one third of the page, down the middle. I couldn't enlarge it, and couldn't read it. I had to Google the solution. It was a setting that I had to change to "view as desktop". Now, everything is oriented correctly...except for Facebook. It is still showing up weird and I don't know how to change it. All that is to say that you may encounter issues, and if you do, you will have to know how to do Google searches to find the answers.

At any rate, I like this Chromebook and will continue to use it. I recommend it for people needing access to the internet in a portable manner, but who want a larger screen to view than a cell phone. It is very portable, the battery seems to last a long time, and it is easy to use.

But what if I bought this for my parents who don't have WiFi or a Google account?  I think TVs should work for their HDMI inputs without needing anything else if you choose.

title: Great Remote
text: If you have a lot of devices to control in one area, this is the device for you!  I have it controlling a Epson projector, Fire TV Cube, LG Blu-Ray Disc player, Bose BT speaker, and a few smaller gadgets.  It was easy to set up, but I am in IT, so YMMV.  The hub is my only complaint.  If the hub is lost, the remote does nothing.  With their old version, there was no hub.  That meant no control through cabinet doors if the device uses IR, but it also meant the remote worked no matter what.  My big complaint is that the hub went offline twice and both times I had to open things up and reset it before my remote would work.

title: Great Screen!
text:
There are no cases... How can you make a tablet without a case being available? Originally I figured I was going to give this 3 stars at best because of that one factor. But then I tried it out....

My one complaint about the tablet itself is that it is a little slow. I'm comparing it to ones that are twice the price though, because my daughter has a Samsung Tab S7 that was like $600. Other than that, this is a solid replacement and I would definitely buy it again if it had a good case available! The screen is frankly the best screen I've ever seen on a tablet. It rivals my Z Fold 4 in terms of video quality. The sound is decent, the responsiveness is great, and it has enough RAM to handle even my power user needs. So my plan is to use it as my travel tablet until it breaks from lack of a case (at which point I will be sad and have to buy a different brand next time since other brands offer cases).

I got this tablet at a reduced price for writing a review, and that fact did not influence my review at all. However, without a proper case, I wouldn't pay full price for this. It's an amazing tablet that is just waiting to be broken, which is a strange dichotomy. If the manufacturer is reading this, please e-mail me when you release a case for it!

Anyway, I'm still using the old remote for some things and I need to get around to fixing that, but for now I'm able to say that this is a good remote if you happen to be an IT expert who can figure anything out even when the company that made it cannot!

title: Great If You Travel With A Laptop
text: This is a great battery pack for people who travel with a laptop.  The different adapters mean that you don't have to convert DC to AC and then back again, so that saves battery.  And it has a long life!  The only problem is the size and the case.  The size is a problem I expected, it is heavier than most battery packs (definitely not a pocket unit), but for a traveler with a rolling bag, that's no big deal.  The case is disappointing, and that's why I took off the star.  The case only holds the battery pack (so there's no point in even having a case).  I wish the case had a pocket for a few cords and some of the adapters so I don't need to put them in a zip lock!

title: Great Camera, Great App!
text: This camera has a great interface and a great mobile app.  I can pull it up in seconds, move it about, talk two ways since it has both a mic and a speaker built-in, and generally do anything I'd like with a standalone camera.  But the best part comes if you have a Reolink NVR because the camera can be plugged straight in  or used over wifi to record to the NVR and to be controlled by it.  I just got my NVR, so I haven't tried that out yet, but I'm very excited to have these around my house!  The only downside is that it doesn't support PoE, so if you want a clean one-wire install, this is the wrong camera.

title: Didn't Work

I was hoping this would be a good upgrade, but apparently it doesn't recognize standard cameras!

This computer has the processing power you need to run a home VPN, or a file share (using an external drive), or a gaming PC for old games (think retro-pi operating system), or a home movie box (store all your discs on a hard drive attached, or over the network, and use VLC or XBMC to watch them on your projector). Add a wireless keyboard and mouse (be sure to get ones that are encrypted) and you're all set for movie night!

Overall, I love this computer at this price point. There are plenty of others out there that sound similar, and I haven't tried them all, but I can tell you that this one stands up to the test.

title: A Great Linux Laptop
text:
So my only complaint about Microsoft devices as a whole is their lack of compatibility with Linux. This one is better than the other 4 I have owned. It still isn't working well with CentOS, but Kubuntu works awesomely, and I also have Kali running. I've got a tripple boot (with Windows as well) set up, and the whole thing took about 5 hours to set up. If you're looking for a laptop to run Linux on, that is light and has a great battery, the choice is this one or the XPS. The XPS (my friend has one) doesn't run touchscreen, but it is lighter than this one and gets even better battery...

Overall, this laptop has a great battery, a great screen, and runs Linux with very little effort. The only downsides are the requirement to have power connected in order to detach the screen (yes, the button does work in Linux), the fact that all ports (USB, SD and charging included) are on the base (so in tablet mode it can't charge, can't read an SD card, and can't use a USB device), and the fact that it is so sealed that you can't upgrade or repair it yourself. Those are the reasons I dropped one star (personally, I'd drop 4 stars for all that, but I know most people wouldn't).

I like that they are compatible with my other walkie-talkie's even though they are not the same brand. The micro-USB charging cable is very convenient - not all of these have this. It can also be used with AA batteries, so I like the different options. It comes out clear. It is easy to use. It has a weather alert, which is also nice. I am very pleased with these.

title: My only complaint is that there is no web based ...
text: My only complaint is that there is no web based GUI or CLI that I can use to manage the switch.  Having to install their software is a bit of a pain.  But I didn't take off for that because it was a one time annoyance and now it's done, also because I just went by their instructions and I didn't search online so it's possible the instructions were incomplete.  I haven't upgraded my network to use POE cameras and APs yet, but that's coming soon and this is exactly what I need.  I can stack a few of these and run cables everywhere and the POE devices will all be powered!

title: Simple but effective
text:
This is a very good product. When you consider how much people spend for alarm systems, this really is a great deal. It works as a simple alarm. It started to go off and you have a small amount of time to put in the pass code to stop it. I think it will deter a lot of people... as soon as they hear the alarm they will turn around. They don't know whether it is monitored or not, after all. It can also work as a doorbell, too.

Installation was simple and easy. It works fine. The only thing is that it does require batteries so you will have to change those to keep up with it. Otherwise it really is a great idea for a home, business or something smaller like a shed.

title: This device provides great sound for my cheap computer speakers
text: This device provides great sound for my cheap computer speakers, but the quality was a little sub par when I hooked it up to a full stereo system.  Since the computer speakers are all I need, I'm happy with it overall.  My next task will be getting it to work in Linux, I tested it on my Windows system but I really want it for a Linux build I am working on.

title: I would recommend this adapter to anyone in the markeet for one
text: I had no trouble connecting this, Windows 10 recognized it without any problem.  I would  recommend this adapter to anyone in the markeet for one!

title: It works as advertised. I connected my USB-C output ...
text: It works as advertised.  I connected my USB-C output on my laptop to my VGA monitor with ease.  The screen looks as I would expect, no distortions due to the conversion!

title: Good value
text:
This is a good basic mouse. I thought it worked just fine. It is a very good value. We just needed something basic that would do the job and this does it. We've had tons of pieces from Belkin, and they usually work pretty well.

This mouse was very comfortable to use. It fit well in my hand. I like that it has a scroll wheel. It plugs in with the USB plug. It was simple to plug in and use on my computer. I wish the logo wasn't quite so big on the mouse.

Overall, a good mouse, especially for the price.

title: Awesome mouse
text:
I have had multiple Logitech mice, and let me tell you, I like this one. First, it looks cool. It definitely does not look like your average mouse it has a cool futuristic look I love. It is so responsive. I love how quick it is. This is important if you are in gaming, but even if not, it is fantastic to have a mouse that responds so well to you.

The scroll wheel is super fast. I have times have to scroll through a lot of documents, and I love this feature in it. Of course, it is also fantastic for gaming.

It is extremely comfortable in your hand. I love the design and feel like I can grip it very well. I have pretty small hands.

I love how flexible it is as far as programming. It has 11 buttons you can program, far more than most mice. This worked well, and was easy.

Everything about it worked well. I have a relatively new computer and had no issues with compatibility. It worked great.

This is a great mouse that can improve your gaming performance. Plus it just looks cool!

title: Nice watch
text: I am not a competitive runner, but I really enjoy jogging. I've done it for years and was looking for a way to track my progress and see how I am doing. I think this watched provided a wealth of information. I like that the GPS tracked how far I go and the pace. It worked quite a long while on the charge. Some phones and programs will provide some basic information, but this really went into depth. It worked well, and looked good. It was comfortable to wear. You do have to read the instructions and really learn how to use it the right way if you want to get the most out of it.

title: Great for kids
text: I don't care for earbuds for my kids so I really like these over the ear headphones. All my kids need these for school. I love that they limit the volume - it is definitely a concern that they will leave it on too loud and hurt their hearing with other headphones. It is bright and colorful - my son loves blue and green so it is perfect. I think the value is very good compared to other similar headphones. It is adjustable so it fit him fine and will grow with him. It worked just fine without a problem. I like that the plug lets you use it with many different devices. I was happy with everything about it.

title: Five Stars
text: Worked for a 150x200 VESA TV!

title: Nice subwoofer
text:
This is a great subwoofer. I love the digital control system. I can do it with my Android phone. It worked without a problem from my phone. It made it so much easier to set it up perfectly.

It is a larger piece of equipment. I thought it got a great sound. Sounds came out very deep and pure. It really made a difference.

title: Nice case
text:
This is a nice case. It will fit a lot of different tablet, even with the protective cover. We had no problem getting ours in there. The colors were pretty and vibrant. I liked that it has extra areas to store things like games.

The reason I took off a stay is that I thought it could have been a little thicker. It will provide some protection if dropped, but it is not so thick that it is fully protected. I thought it could have been a little thicker.

It felt well made. There is a card on the back where you can put your information, which is nice.

title: Lots of features
text:
For a little device this has a lot of nice features and options that make it suitable for school, work or personal use. I am using it for the latter application. First, it is easy to use. It doesn't take a long time to figure it out, and it worked well. The sound came out crisp and clear. I didn't hear a lot of background noise. I love that you can put in the simple mode if you just want basic features in an easy to use format. You can use the normal mode for everything.

I had no trouble with the functionality of the product. I like that it has a USB built into it and do not need a cable. This saves space and time. It has a little stand, which makes it easy to use. I like that it has 8 gb internal memory and a Micro SD card slot for more options. Overall, it was a good, versatile product that worked well. It is small and slim and easy to carry. I would recommend it.

title: This was easy to set up and integrate with my network
text: This was easy to set up and integrate with my network.  The whole process took about 30 minutes.  Now downloading a large file to my AC 0laptop is about 2 time faster than the N devices that I have.  Not quite a gig speed, but even my SSD can only write so fast!  When I have more AC devices I expect this to be more noticeable.

title: One Star

title: Works well
text: This is your standard USB micro cable and it did everything it was supposed to do. It worked well. Everything fit perfectly. It's your standard black to blend in. It felt durable and strong. We had no problems. I would recommend it.

title: These are great headphones. They really stop outside noise thanks to ...
text: These are great headphones.  They really stop outside noise thanks to the great padding, and they aren't tight enough to cause me pain.  One note:  the cord is hard to connect the first time, it needed to be pushed in at a particular angle and turned to lock in place.  I don't read instructions, and I almost sent these back as defective because only the right channel was working and it was going in and out as I moved.  My face is red, hopefully this review stops your face from being red too!

title: Nice versatile alarm clock
text: I like the options on this clock. You can set an alarm to the radio, a buzzer or audio from Bluetooth. It was very easy to set up, and the alarm can be set for different times on the weekday and weekend. It has a nice look to it that works well in the house or even in an office. The sound was pretty good for such a small device. You can use it as a Bluetooth speaker from your phone or other device. It has a battery backup, which is good if you lose power but want to make sure you still wake up in time. You can adjust the brightness of the clock display, which is very important for me so it doesn't keep me up at night. It's very easy to read. It also has USB charging for devices. This would also be something you can bring on business trips. I was very happy with this multi-function alarm clock.

title: Sped up our computer
text: This was a great hard drive to add a bit of speed to our older computer. As time went on, our computer was running slower and slower, and this really helped to get it back. I had no trouble putting it in, and it worked fine right away. I noticed a noticeable difference immediately.  It boots up and shuts down and just generally runs quicker. It's a lot cheaper than replacing the computer, which is where we were at. Quality and reliability are good. I'd recommend this!

title: Great to connect devices
text: The Netgear Powerline 1200 has been great to connect devices. I was very happy with how fast the speed is. It was very easy to do, and just took a few minutes. It's really just something you plug in and it works; you don't have to spend forever trying to put in software.  We had no problems getting it to work. This product is so versatile - you can use it for so many different devices and uses. It also has a lot of advantages like stopping interference with wifi. It can make your streaming quicker, too. It's a great product.

title: Overall pleased with the camera
text:
We use this camera for security and overall I am pleased. I like that it has a battery backup so that even when we lose power we still have it. I really like that I can see the streaming on my phone or tablet. It has a really good field of view, and the quality is pretty good. I feel like I can see what I need to see. The RapidRecap feature is neat, and I like that it connects to my Wifi.

We had no problem setting it up - it went quickly. So far everything has worked fine - no problems with any of the features or anything. I felt like provided a stable view of everything. Now you do have to give away some information to use the app, which could be an issue for some people, but I was okay with it. Overall, I'm happy with it.

title: Great product

I like the features. The setup time wasn't super quick but it wasn't terrible. It took several tries to pair it successfully, but then I got it working without a problem. It controls the phone well. I really like that it does that because many of the others do not. It even has a clock, which is a nice feature.

title: Great camera
text:
I was very pleased with this camera. Right off I was very pleased with how compact and light it is. This is a must for me, as it is for a lot of people. I like to keep it in my purse and it also makes it much easier for those who plan to mount it.

Set up was very easy - no problems there. Everything worked without a problem. I really liked the wifi feature.

I was happy with the picture. I felt that the quality was very good. I was also happy with the stabilization. This is obviously very important for those who are using it for action shots.

Overall, I'm happy with this camera and would recommend it.

title: I love this system
text: I love this system!  I have a few ideas for it, initially I just hooked it up to a light to show that it works.  The process was easy and the software is so intuitive.  I didn't even need the manual!  In future, I'm going to make it run a motor on my blinds cords to get motorized blinds for a fraction of the cost!

text: This is a decent case with a stand.  It doesn't stay closed well, and the protection is minimal, but it is lightweight and doesn't add bulk.

title: Great product
text: This is a good product that does what it's supposed to do. It was easy to install and we didn't have any bubbles. It provides some protection from scratches and the like. It fits the Kindle Fire HD 7 very well. It seems durable and well made. I'm happy with it and would recommend it to others.

title: Good screen protector
text: This screen protector does what it's supposed to do. It works well and was not difficult to put on.We were able to get it on without air bubbles and it stayed on well. I also liked that it reduced glare, which can be good if you are using it outside a lot. It's made for the Kindle Fire HDX 7" and might not fit something else. It felt durable and strong.

title: Decent privacy filter
text:
This privacy filter does what it's supposed to do. When you put it on, you can see okay from straight on, but as you go to the side it becomes darker and unreadable. This can be good if you are doing something sensitive and don't want someone to see. Of course someone behind you can still see it..

There are both pros and cons to this. It was easy to put on with the blue tape, although that might bother some people, but you can put it on a different way. One thing that's nice is it comes with a matte and a glossy side. you can also reduce glare, which can be an issue for some people. The other side is better for screen resolution. A con is that it does make the entire screen darker. This will bother people to different extents so you have to see if this bothers you.

Overall I was happy with this product. It made me feel a little more comfortable when using it in public.

It can really make things a lot faster than with the 2.0 technology (note: everything needs to have the 3.0 technology for it work - if the computer's port is only 2.0 then it will go down to 2.0). It was packaged well, and reasonably priced. It works well and no problems at all. I would definitely recommend it.

title: Did not work for me
text: We were not happy with this product. First, it seemed to provide little to no protection. It was thing and had a lot of holes by the sides, which would really do very little. Also, a big problem is that on the bottom there are all these grooves that made it uncomfortable for me to put on my lap. It doesn't matter how much protection it has, if I can't comfortably have it on my lap, then it doesn't work for me. I will not be using this product.

title: Good for organization, large
text:
Overall I am happy with this product. Right now we have all our tablets stacked on top of each other, which is not so convenient when it comes to taking them in and out. With this product, I can just put them side by side and it is easy to get to one. It comes with a decent surge protector under it. It's very easy to put together. I felt that it it looked very professional and would look good in an office or classroom. It'll help keep everything organized and looking good, and keep the cords neat and organized so they don't get tangles and you do not lose any. The slots were pretty good sized, and fit our tablets with the covers on them, which was good.

There were a few drawbacks to this product. First it seemed a big bigger than it needed to be for what it could do. There was a fairly big frame around the slots...they probably could've made that smaller so it would have a smaller footprint, which is important since it will be taking up valuable desk space. Even though it is big, they could've made it a little deeper and it could've accommodated bigger, standard laptops, which would've been nice. It didn't come with any of the charging wires, which would've been nice and helped for a professional, uniform look. I also felt like it was a little pricey for what you were getting.

Still for me the good outweighed the bad. It felt durable and sturdy. Four stars for a good organizational product for the home, office or school

title: peace of mind is priceless
text: With three kids, we have always had a motion activated baby alarm, and I cannot tell you the peace of mind it has given.  Although the risk of SIDS is small, it is still a risk, and this device can help prevent it by alerting you before it is too late.  I felt like I could sleep at night knowing that something was checking to see on it.  Yes, we've had false alarms and that will happen with any, but it is so worthwhile to know. title: What Happens When Things Go Wrong...
text:
When I first purchased my 3 TB MBL some time ago I was quite pleased. Network access, remote access, even an android app. In short, everything my DLink had plus the app and a nicer look on the shelf. I used it extensively for pulling up photos on my cell phone when I was bored as well as to store my most important files. I didn't back them up, a back-up drive is something I kept saying I would add later...

14 months later (note the 12 month warranty had just expired) the drive stopped being accessible over the network. I spent a week and at least 40 hours of my time going back and forth with tech support by e-mail and trying every option they could offer, and the result was that they deemed the unit broken. They said that the unit can not be opened because that would break the drive inside, and they said that they can't fix it. They "kindly" offered me a referral to one of several companies that give them a kick back for data recovery services. Incidentally, I asked two for pricing by e-mail and they didn't respond.

So I took the unit apart and bought a new unit and took that one apart and swapped the drives. Neither one worked. After talking to support again it turns out that WD didn't want these to be upgradable because if they were upgradable you could buy a cheap drive instead of a new unit so they code each board to the drive that will be in it. TO make matters worse, they encoded the drive in a Linux format that no known version of Linux can translate. Attaching it to my Linux system I couldn't mount it using any utility. Several Linux recovery programs couldn't do anything either.

Okay, having told you why I will never buy a WD NAS again, I should now tell you how to fix this if you have the same problem that I do: DiskInternals makes a program called Linux Reader. That's right, Linux can't read the drive but a program designed to read Linux drives from within Windows can! Recovering the data to a drive is time consuming though. I tried it all at once but that froze after a few days. Then I tried one major directory at a time and that worked better. But recovering nearly 3 TB of data has taken a very long time! I'm about 3 MONTHS into the recovery effort and I have about 400 GB remaining. After starting on my wife's computer because mine is a laptop and causing a few crashes and a lot of delays I finally had to pull out an older computer and set it up just to run this program.

If anyone has the same problem and can't get this solution to work, I'll do my best to help if you simply reply to this review and give me all the details. If anyone is considering buying a WD NAS, I want to encourage you to buy a DLink model 323 (I think the 325 is the current version but it is missing some features so I'd get an older one) instead. I've had that thing running for 5 years without a glitch!

title: excellent speakers
text: These are great speakers. I am very pleased with them. They sound great and provide a very rich sound, especially for speakers that are meant for the outdoors. I would highly recommend them.

title: Not A Stellar Case
text:
Okay, before I mention what is wrong with this case, I will mention two things that are right:

1. The leather feels so soft. For a mass produced case, they did a good job at this aspect.

2. The strap, which I am going to call a negative down below, does look cool if you are thinking of your KFHD as an ebook reader because it resembles the straps that are sometimes found in books.

Okay, done with the good. Now for the critique:

1. The spine likes to stay open. By that I mean when you open the device and then close it you have to use the strap to hold it shut because it will not do so naturally. Since the device turns on and off when you open and close it, this means that the device will waste power staying on because it thinks that the case is open. There are many ways to avoid this, but they manufacturer did not try to.

2. There are no pockets to put note cards or business cards.

3. There is no loop to hold a stylus or pen.

4. The case is open around all sides. This isn't a design flaw, but if I were the company I would offer a zippered version to protect the device from rain.

5. The strap SUCKS!!! I mean really, it takes effort to properly close this case! Why not design it not to need one like my Toshiba Thrive case, or design it with a magnetic clasp like my Kindle Touch case?

6. The rotating mechanism is pretty cool, I have seen similar for other devices, but it is pretty tight. Perhaps this will loosen up, but after 3 days I still report this to be difficult to turn.

7. The hand strap is useless. If you hold it open like that, the device is secured only to one side and can flap about. If you are going to put in a hand strap, this should provide secure and stable device placement.

8. And now for the most annoying factor: they get a point for designing a case that can sit at several angles, but then loose several million for designing it so that NONE of those angles are comfortable. They range from pointing slightly down to pointing slightly up, and all of them are best if the device is at or within 6" below eye level. If you sit it on your desk and not a long way off, it is not angled enough for a good view! Seriously? Didn't they test this before going into production?

My advice to the user is to find another case.

My advice to the manufacturer is to redesign. And while you're at it, please send me a free one of the new cases after the redesign so that I don't have to buy a new case!

One more word about the price. I know that this is a high end case with the rotating feature and all, but anything over $30 is just ridiculous! I got mine free in exchange for this review (sorry about that, but I am always fair and I have never been bribed in my reviews), but I wouldn't have paid for it if I had to do so!

title: Great Media Device...Terrible Tablet
text:
Okay, there are three types of devices which are this size. One is an ebook reader. If that's all you want, get a Paperwhite. Seriously, try reading on the Fire's screen for half an hour and it will be like reading on a computer screen (not so good for the eyes). Especially in low light!

The second is a tablet, if that's what you want then get a Galaxy Tab. I have a Toshiba Thrive, which is similar to the Tab (one step down in some respects, the same in others) and that blows this out of the water in terms of what it can do and how it does it. But it isn't the best at playing back movies. eBook capabilities are similar and screen is similar, so if you aren't going to watch movies on it then DO NOT BUY A FIRE HD!!!

The third type of device I call a portable media device. And here is where the Kindle Fire really shines. The screen is currently the best screen available on a 7" device. And the sound is great. Using the built in application, I can play movies ripped from DVDs with great sound and video. On my Thrive I have trouble with this, getting jittery video and low sound most of the time and no consistency. A free program will convert your videos over to Kindle Fire screen size and save them in a format that the Fire can open (search for them, there are many and lots of free options so don't pay for that).

The negatives are, however, many. The Kindle Fire HD sports the UGLIEST user interface I have ever seen. Some replacements are available, and I'm debating them just like I am debating rooting the device to get the Play store. Note that if you have an Android phone, without rooting you can not get your paid apps on the Fire. Also, you can access only a few thousand of the half a million apps that other Android devices offer. This is just because Amazon wants to reduce piracy by restricting apps that may get around protections, but it costs hundreds of thousands of legitimate apps. Also, Google apps are not present (except gmail), so you can't get Google Maps or Voice or the like without sideloading or rooting. I'm not sure why Amazon hates Google, since Google gave them the framework for this tablet! I got the $25 screen protector and I don't like the feel, but that isn't the tablet's fault.

If you have kids, Amazon's kidtime app is great. Other similar apps are available for other devices, and if you want any content this one costs $2.99/month for a one child license, but it is a good app and they did a great job of integrating it so there are no bugs which could cause your kid to find their way out accidentally (or on purpose for those smarter kids out there). If the service was free for Prime members, or if a limited version was free for Prime members, I would rate this app as 5 stars and perhaps raise the entire Kindle Fire HD up a star since that would add one great use which I currently am not taking advantage of.

Oh, and there is no SD slot, no USB slot for external drives, and no IR port so it can't be a remote control (all very disappointing).

Having said all of that, I am keeping mine for movie playback and occasional reading when on a plane or in a doctor's office. I have a 10" tablet which I love and wouldn't trade in for this Kindle if they paid me. But since I can have both (thanks mostly to putting several people together to buy me one present together), this is worth keeping.

title: An NAS, A Few Files, And Thy

title: Not Bad For Beginner Users, But Most Of Us Can Do This Anyway
text:
Pros: If you are a beginner to computer networking and you just want to host a cloud server at home for tablet and smartphone access to your music and video library, this is the device for you. Set-up is simple, anyone who can install a Linksys router can do it, and tech support is decent (for the purposes of this review, I called and asked them to help me with a non-existent issue so I could report that they do in fact help people, then I told the guy I was a mystery shopper and thanked him for his help).

Cons: If you have Carbonite back-up service, if you have a WD MyBookLive NAS, or if you know how to configure any of the several dozen software packages that do this for you, then you can already do this for free without buying this device. Yes, I do mean that there are free packages (at least for Android phones) which you can download and use to make your computer into this device without any fees whatsoever. So for anyone who is mid-level or above in computers, this is not a worthwhile purchase.

title: A Good Idea Poorly Implemented
text:
Let me start by saying that if you happen to be looking for a way to record music from one of the 41,000 radio stations that this company supports and then take it to your car without having to record it yourself and put it on an mp3 player, it does work.

That being said, the stations are not very inclusive. This isn't going to be XM radio we're talking about. most of the stations are non-US stations (which is a good thing for some people, but not what I was looking for). I wanted children's music for my kids to listen to. I love XM's Kids Place Live, and I wanted something like that. What I found was less than a dozen channels, only 4 in English, and at the time that I set this up all 4 were playing music that wasn't appropriate for my kids. So I decided to move on to pop and use it for myself. This was even harder. There were about 100 top 40 channels, mostly not in English again, and the ones that were were just random stations like 94.9 FM in Nashville, TN (I couldn't tell anything from the names and there is no way to get user reviews of the stations). So I picked one at random and decided to record it just to write the review and then I can add this to the pile of gadgets that I don't use anymore.

That wasn't easy either. You have to start it recording, let it go for the amount of time that you want (this isn't mp3 downloading where you can get a few hours in a few minutes), and make sure your computer doesn't go to sleep. Also, the station dropped out after about 20 minutes and when I came back 4 hours later I discovered that the software doesn't reconnect you automatically, so you really have to use this to listen to music at your computer and then replay the same music in the same order in your car.

The device is also missing features that I just assumed it would have like identifying when songs start and stop to separate tracks, identifying the music and labeling the tracks so I know what I am listening to, or the ability to mark a song at the unit while I am playing it back and later be reminded to go buy that song.

The device was very easy to set up, despite the fact that my 64 bit version of Windows doesn't support their 64 bit client and I had to run the 32 bit version (not a big deal just not sure why they bothered to include the 64 bit version if it doesn't work). I updated to the latest software quite easily as well.

This is a buyer beware situation. The device works as advertised, but has no bells and whistles that aren't mentioned in the product description (like auto-reconnect, which I would consider a standard part of this device's operation). And it is easy to use (if you don't mind baby sitting it). But you can access 100 times that many radio channels online and record them using free software that will do these other things and then download them to your mp3 player in minutes (assuming that you have one, if not check out the Samsung ones and remember to get one with speakers if you will ever want that capability, don't waste your money on a Zune or an IPod unless you have a good reason to).

For me, the product was a free test product, so I didn't waste anything. but I would be returning this if I had paid for it.

I didn't have to do any research, but I did go and listen to a few systems before buying, just in case.  The system didn't dissapoint.  And set-up was very easy.  Being a technician, I didn't need help setting the unit up; however, if I was less technically inclined, the color coded wires and easy quick set-up diagrams would have been very helpfull. title: Lots of Help if you are Adept at Computers
text:
This card is not for the faint of heart, it should only be used by someone who is familiar with building computers and repairing hardware. That is to say, if you don't know what a level 5 clean room is then you probably don't want to open your computer because you probably don't have the necessary skills to know how to keep your good components from getting fried.

That being said, this card is great. And if you like to see post codes, you can mount it permanently. I used it on my new system that I built and got code FF. Unfortunately, this is the most common error and it means a BIOS, motherboard, CPU or power supply issue. Since 2/5 of the possible problems were CPU related, I sent back my brand new CPU and that turned out to be the problem...

Do yourself a favor, if you know what you are doing, and get this card now so you have it when something goes wrong... Now if only it came with a bundled ATX power supply tester.

title: Perfect Headset, Perfect Operation
text:
EDIT: My original review is below, but here is some extra information: After two months of use, this device is still working well, but the silver paint is almost all gone and the case I bought for it is not rigid so the button keeps getting pressed in and the battery drains every day. I need to find a better way to carry it... The paint problem shows a definate lack of quality and if I could change my rating I would reduce this to a 3 star review.

I have had this headset for two days now, so this reviewer can't speak of the potential for battery problems or how durable it is. However, so far I am very impressed. The quality is beyond compare, I have carried on several conversations and then said "by the way, I am trying out my new headset, how does it sound?" and the response it always that they didn't know I was using one! I am so happy to have found this because I get nervous driving and dialing, plus I tend to drive fast and I like to have both hands on the wheel. I'll be buying the car kit next, but I still want a headset for use while walking around and while at events or fairs.

I have a Motorola V600 and it paired easily, though since this was my first bluetooth device and there is a pairing code to enter I had to read the quick start directions. From the time I opened the manuel to my first call it took 3 minutes.

Cons: It didn't come charged, which I get upset about because I am too impatient to wait. Also, when you plug it in it can take up to 5 minutes before registering the plug, which made me think that it was broken at first. Next, it doesn't come with a belt case and it is a strange size so buy the belt case (I am waiting for that to come so look for my review of it later on). And finally, the battery is not removable (I found out that this is typical of these headsets, but I still would have liked to be able to buy several and change them out).

Other than that, it is a perfect headset. Since those are minor problems and are typical of other headsets, I rated this model 5 stars.

As for me, this is my first bluetooth headset. But I know people who have problems with other headsets and this one outperforms all others that I have seen...

title: Great value for the amateur and semi-professional
text:
So you are looking for a good lens? You want something that will take great pictures, but you don't want to spend hundreds or thousands of dollars? Well this is the lens for you! I have used several 70-200, 70-255 and 70-300 mm lenses in stores which considering them and the answer is simple: You can't beat a Nikkor lens.

This lens has excellent clarity and optics. I am the director of the Nicholas Copernicus Observatory at the University of Miami and I have extensive expierence in optics. I can tell you, without a doubt, that you wont find a better lens than this for twice the price. I have only bought Nikon cameras and lenses, but I get plenty of chances to use other ones at the observatory as different people bring their equipment to learn how to use it better. No matter how many cameras I use, I still recommend Nikon above all else.

I presently use this lens with a Nikon D70s camera.

There is a more expensive version available, the Nikon 70-300mm f/4-5.6D AF Nikkor SLR Camera Lens, which has superior optics. I highly recomend that lens if you are a professional who needs perfect clarity on sunny days for nature photography at the 300mm length. If you are an amateur or even a semi-professional, if you use this in lower light, or if you are using the shorter length most of the time, save the $200 price difference and save it toward another lens!

title: Great system for your office or living room
text:
I needed a small system for my office. I wanted removable speakers, good sound at all volumes and a sleek look. This system filled that void. I searched for about a month to get it, and there is nothing less than fantastic about this system, even the price.

In terms of sound, I can understand music at all volume levels (many cheaper systems distort at low levels) and at high volumes it sounds great. I can't use it at high volumes now that I've taken it to work, but I am thinking about buying another for my living room at home (run the output of my family room stereo and I'll have a system that sounds good in both places for parties).

In terms of looks, this system is very cool. I tried to downplay it by placing it behind my desk, on the shelf where I keep my food, so that people wouldn't question it (because small stereos are allowed but not everyone likes us having them). Despite my attempts to blend it in, I've received several complements on the way that it looks. Silver casing and a sleek design are just the basics, this system features a blue backlit display that looks great!

I thought that the "DVD" option in the stereo meant that you could play MP3s on DVD (a great idea for someone who wants to never have to change CDs), but in fact it meant that the system is a DVD player, and it has a video output to connect to your tv. That's a nice plus. I haven't tried the MP3 idea yet, so it may or may not support them.

The stock antenna is terrible, but so are most stereo antennas. I'll buy a new one soon... The other downside is that you can't switch between presets without the remote (you can change the station, but not using presets). But with 30 FM presets, I'll never run out! The only thing that wasn't obvious about the set-up is that the disk buttons (disk 1, disk 2, etc) on the stereo are the eject buttons, not the select buttons like most other stereos. Overall, this is a great design for a great stereo. I used to work at a radio station as the engineer and now I wish I had this back then because I could blast music in my office and really utilize the system the way it was meant to...

title: A bit of Advice
text:
The other reviews and the description seem to properly describe this camera. I am writing this review to give you the perspective of someone who started out with film SLR cameras in school, then got a digital 5MP camera and have used that for years and am now finally getting into Digital SLR photography. This is a big step back into the professional circle for me, and I'm anxious to get out to the zoo or to some vacation spot in the mountains to do my professional photography once again. I purchased this camera almost a month ago and my opinion is that it is the best camera ever made under $2,000. This camera has everything you can need.

I want to warn you, get the full set with the lense. This lense sells for almost $400 and is about the best all around lense you can find. Don't go for the cheap models. I wrote a list about this camera that may appear on this page for you to look at, but be sure that you get the ML-L3 wireless remote (for $20, how can you go wrong) and a spare battery (2,000 pictures sounds like a lot, and I haven't needed to recharge in this month that I've had the camera, but remember that when you go on a trip you may forget to recharge and you don't want to get stuck). Also, get a tripod (try the Slik Tripods U9000, I wrote a review of it and I find it to be the best buy around for a light-weight tripod that acts like a much heavier one) and get a carrying case (the jury is still out, I haven't found one that I like, I want one that will hold two cameras, 4 lenses, a large flash and a bunch of accessories).

If you aren't sure if the D70s is worth the money over the D50 or the D70, it is. The improved autofocusing system is much better than the others and the larger LCD is worth all the tea in China! I leave the LCD protector that came with it on and have no problem seeing my pictures, even outside. Although this is a larger camera than the D50, it isn't much of a difference and you will regret going with the cheaper camera.

If your budget was lower, save up and buy this camera. I bought a CoolPix 5000 a few years back and always kicked myself for not going with the D100. Now I've gone with the best camera on the market and I'm perfectly happy. Plus, I have the satisfaction of knowing that none of my friends can show me a better camera (unless they spent $4,000 or more on a D2X or D2H, and none of my friends can afford to do that)!!!

title: A word of Warning for CoolPix owners
text: I bought this for use with my CoolPix 5000 camera because Nikon's tech support had recomended it.  They said it would improve my indoor shots (because the CP 5000 has a terrible flash built-in), but instead it overloads the shots and they come out mostly white.  I read the manual carefully and it looks like the reason is that this flash is built to automatically or manually focus the light for a 14mm to 70mm lense and the CP 5000 has a 7.2mm lense.  I subsequently purchased a Nikon D70s camera (1,000,000 times better camera) and this flash is great for extremely dark shots on that camera (though the built-in flash is perfect for fill so this is really only for night shots and shots in darkness where I want to get something far away).  If you own a CoolPix camera, consider buying a used flash that isn't as powerfull.  If you own a D70s and want superior night photography, this is the best flash in the world (good thing I ended up in the latter end of the spectrum).

title: Good product but takes some getting used to
text:
I got my Kindle Fire HD for Christmas and ordered this case because I wanted a keyboard and the price seemed right. There are some annoyances that I listed under Cons, but to me they're not dealbreakers. I am happy with this case and really like having a keyboard with the Kindle.

Pros:
The case securely holds the Kindle. I definitely feel better about letting my kids play games on the Kindle while it's in this case than when it's not protected.

I like the look of the case overall. The stitching is sturdy and the leather is nice. It's like a little dayplanner when it's folded up. (I kinda wish it came in a solid color though. All black or all white or all red would look better to me than highlighting the closure in a second color, but that's just my personal opinion.)

I love how light the keyboard is and how it can "clip" on and off magnetically.

It was super easy to set up even though the directions were written like they were translated into English from a foreign language.

I thought the little red flap at the base would get in the way of typing but it really doesn't. It can fold underneath or just be held down with my wrists without any discomfort.

Cons:
I am not sure how to tell when the keyboard needs to be charged other than to plug it in whenever I remember. A red light appears while it's charging then goes away, so I assume it's ready at that point. I haven't used it enough for it to wear out completely, but I wish there was a way to tell how much charge it has left since I use the keyboard here and there and don't want to charge it all the time, especially if it doesn't need it. (But I also don't want it running out on me.)

The keyboard is small and I haven't gotten used to it yet. One example is that the apostraphe is made by hitting Fn+L, and I keep forgetting that then hitting all kinds of wrong buttons trying to backspace and fix it. This is frustrating because I can type 108 wpm on a standard sized QWERTY keyboard without many mistakes. I think this will just take some getting used to due to its small buttons/size. The keyboard is in great shape though, and I haven't had any sticking or falling off keys like some other reviewers have mentioned.

The Kindle seems to take a while to recognize the keyboard each time. It gets a little annoying when I just wanted to type something quickly and be done. (I am still unclear if I am supposed to go into my Wireless/Bluetooth settings each time I turn on the keyboard or if it will in fact recognize the keyboard eventually if I just wait. I usually lose patience and open up the settings.)

In order to charge the Kindle, I have to either take it out all the way or lay the case flat and open the bottom velcro flap. So it can't really be used with the keyboard while it's charging.

The case doesn't really work vertically. If you fold it in half, the keyboard gets in the way and needs to be removed. And it doesn't stand up vertically on its own.
