title: A portable hub that's a perfect companion for my Surface Go 3
text:
Recently, I was looking for a tablet that is functional and portable. I settled on the Surface Go 3 for its capabilities to function as a laptop while being as portable as an iPad. I've been satisfied with my purchase and as with the purchase of any new device, a set of cases and accessories are necessary.

One such accessory is the iVANKY 7 in 1 USB C Docking Station. This neat little hub has everything I need for my new tablet. It has a microSD and SD card reader built in, which means that while on travel, I can use it to offload pictures from my mirrorless camera into my tablet to do some simple editing and to posting when I'm back at my hotel and the 3 USB-A ports allows me to have an extra copy of my photos on an external drive.

Back at home, I can use my tablet as a full desktop with the help of this hub. I have my keyboard and mouse receiver connected to the USB and an external monitor connected via the HDMI port. The video quality is great and the audio goes through the HDMI as well.

Now we can talk about the Type-C PD passthrough. The type-c PD port on this dock can take up to 100W of power and pass it through to the tablet, meaning that while I'm at home, a single USB-C connection takes care of my charging, video, audio, and keyboard/mouse. This product earns its name of a docking station.

This dock is great for travel and at home. It's simple and straightforward.

title: Audio drivers are hard to find, lack of support, and computer freezes randomly.
text:
I've purchased quite a few compact computers previously and all of them have little quirks that I have to deal with but in the end, I'm able to set them up with the necessary drivers and use them without issues. This Kamrui CK 10, though...

On paper, the specs of this computer is impressive. A 10th generation i7 processor with the integrated Intel graphics which I already knew wouldn't be winning any awards in the gaming department but that's expected. With 16 GB of ram and 512GB of nvme storage, this computer is a good starting point for anyone who needs a fairly powerful PC in a compact package.

Regarding the ram: I've disassembled this computer and found that the ram is soldered to the motherboard, as is the CPU. This means there is no way to upgrade the ram.

Regarding the storage: There is good news here. There are two M.2 slots supporting NVME so SSD storage is quite expandable. I installed another 512gb ssd in the secondary slot.

The operating system that was included was a vanilla Windows 11 Pro with absolutely no additional bloatware aside from what Microsoft has already included. This is good. All drivers were installed and the machine booted fine.

So in my case, it is customary for me to install Windows from scratch when I buy a new computer. It's just something I do. I don't trust that there are no hidden software in the preinstalled systems. As such, I needed to locate the necessary drivers for this computer.

As expected, Windows will successfully detect the graphics, wifi and bluetooth hardware. Also as expected, the Intel chipset drivers needed to be installed manually. All standard so far. With all of this done, there were three pieces of hardware that were unidentifiable. These were the sound drivers.

Scouring the search engines, I couldn't find the drivers for the CK 10. I finally located Kamrui's facebook page, which led to a linktree that then led me to their forums. In the forums, I searched and found a set of drivers for the CK 10. Unfortunately, that seems to be for the CK 10 with an i5 cpu. It did not contain the correct drivers for the sound card.

I resorted to searching for the drivers by device id. From there, I pieced together the necessary drivers to get sound working. I had to use drivers from three different driver sets from HP.

I did reach out to Kamrui's support email. They responded two days later but rather than read what I wrote, they responded with a canned form for me to list my product, serial, purchase date, etc.

So what else is wrong? Well, at least twice per day, this computer freezes without warning. It could be caused by the sound drivers that I had to piece together but how would I know? I don't can't actually get the right drivers for it.

title: Displaylink sets this dock apart.
text:
[[VIDEOID:8052bc9e6eb256b6a38698f645a9fee]] So you purchase a laptop or compact PC with one or more USB Type-C ports maybe not knowing much about the technology. In truth, the Type-C port is a huge mess. There are so many functions that the port is designed for that a normal consumer would have a hard time understanding all of them. In my case, the type-c port on my computer doesn't support HDMI video output. This port came in handy with its Displaylink technology.

As a dock, the iVANKY 15 in 1 Triple Display dock is a great product that, if your laptop has USB charging capabilities, can connect all of your external devices with just one USB plug. You can connect multiple external monitors, external USB drive, your keyboard/mouse, and gain the ability to read SD and MicroSD cards, all with a single plug. In terms of charging, the PD port outputs 18W of power which is good enough for fast charging your tablet and phone, and the computer port outputs 94w, powerful enough for many laptops running a CPU up to an Intel i5. All this is packaged in a modern, metal shell and it even has a 100w power adapter included.

Already, this is a great dock, but the DisplayLink feature sets this dock apart from the rest of the pack. DisplayLink allows a computer to output video to a computer monitor (up to 4K) through a standard USB 3.1 port. This means that if you have a type-c that doesn't support video output or if it only has Type-A ports, this dock can still give you the ability to add more monitors to your setup. Just install the included drivers (the dock shows up as a computer drive when you plug it in) and this dock will extend your desktop.

While it is a little pricey, this dock has the quality and functionality to justify it.

title: A solid enclosure with RGB goodness
text:
When I first got this M.2 NVMe and SATA SSD Enclosure, I was concerned about its build quality. The enclosure opens by squeezing the plastic at the top and sliding the drive mount out like a drawer. I felt that the plastic felt soft and didn't understand why it's not metal.

After plugging it into my computer, I understood. The drive tray is made of plastic because it is light with nice RGB lights. When plugged in, the lights will flash to different colors when data is being read and when the drive is idle, the lights pulse between different colors. It's pretty cool, actualy.

In terms of performance, it is on par with my many other enclosures. It is able to transfer at the maximum USB speed, although I don't have the diskmark app installed so I don't have any specific numbers. I just know that I'm happy with this purchase because the price is reasonable and the RGB was a nice surprise. Oh, and the enclosure comes with both type-c to type-c as well as type-c to type-A connectors cables. Other enclosures just come with a c-to-a cable.

title: Sometimes, just a simple hub will do.
text:
[[VIDEOID:676a9c562ee284b4873a8774f1caf9d6]] With modern computers cutting down on the number of ports, relying on the speed of USB 3.1 Type-c to handle all of the I/O load, consumers now have to provide their own docks or dongles. This means that we are dealing with more cables and what is termed "dongle hell". This is just the reality, unfortunately. It's both more convenient (a single cable to connect all of your accessories) and less convenient at the same time.

Well, this isn't the fault of the HENRETY USB C Hub, it's just here to help resolve the problem that you are facing... and it does a good job of it. The hub is sleek, with an aluminum shell and high-quality ports.

In my use, I already have a small dongle to connect my laptop to an external monitor but I ran out of ports for it. I needed more ports, but I didn't need another HDMI output. I opted to save some money and get a simple USB hub and it really does work very well. I have a backup external drive connected that I periodically backup my video editing projects to and I also have my Dualsense (PS5) controller connected to it. I haven't had a problem yet.

If you just need some ports without the fancy HDMI, ethernet, and audio outputs save some money and get the Henrety hub.

title: Works very well as an external drive for file backups and travel
text:
I have a few M.2 solid state drives in external enclosures for various purposes in my computer tool kit. I have one that I use to store files that come in handy while installing Windows. I have another to use as my storage drive, connected to my main PC so that my operating system drive is empty of documents and photos, making it easier when I need to reformat my computer.

For the NEMIX RAM Nemisis Series 1TB SSD M.2 2280 PCIe drive, my purpose for it is to use it as a backup drive for my video and photo editing projects. Being an external drive, the speed is actually limited by the USB 3.1 connection rather than the M.2 drive so my workflow is to have my current projects on an internal drive while some recent ones get placed on this 1TB drive. Older projects get stored on a larger 20TB drive.

In my work case, because I'm not working from the drive directly, its speed is plenty fast for copying to and from my internal drive. I'm quite satisfied with its performance. I have not had any issues with the drive so far.

title: Good features and powered by mains.
text:
While solar-powered cameras are convenient, I've found that they have too many compromises when it comes to functionality. In order to save on battery power, the software usually shuts down the camera when there is no activity. Usually, that means nothing gets recorded until the motion detector is set off. In addition, a couple of my solar cameras actually had firmware updates that made them almost unusable because the app can no longer wake the cameras up. This means that the only time I'm actually able to view the cameras are when there is actually motion to set it off.

This Reolink camera doesn't have those problems. It can be powered by a power adapter or power over ethernet. While this makes installing the camera more troublesome, it is worth it because I don't have problems like what I mentioned above.

In addition to solving this basic issue for me, I found that the Reolink camera is much more well-built than the solar cameras that I had previously. The camera mount is made of metal and the camera swivel mechanism is made of high-quality plastic.

The camera is pretty annoying during setup because it has a loud speaker that talks and talks until you finally pair it with your phone app but once done, the app runs like any other app that you might have used. It has controls for the pan, tilt, and zoom functions and it will show both of the built in cameras simultaneously.

Pop in a memory card and you have local recording capabilities with a nice timeline to control playback.

This is a high-quality camera that justifies its price.

title: These work.  High-speed charging and high-speed file transfers
text:
I love that Type-C plugs are reversible, it means that when you get a 90 degree adapter like this, it can be plugged in the direction that you need.

I had a couple of cheaper 90 degree adapters that I tried to use with my NReal Air video glasses but they didn't work because they were only good for charging and maybe USB 2.0 data transfers. I needed something better.

XAOSUN 90 Degree USB C Adapter will support high-speed file transfers as well as high-power charging (up to 240w), basically USB 4 specs. With these adapters, my video glasses work well and I haven't had any issues with lost connections or anything.

They simply work and you don't need to worry that a device won't run at full specs because of this adapter.

title: I'm not keen on the cover material
text:
While the Arae Electronic Organizer does what it says, its implementation isn't great.

The double layers of this product has one and a half flap of elastic bands to hold bundled up wires, that's 18 spots total. The rest are two large pockets and a small pocket. That's plenty of room to carry most charging accessories that you'd have with you if you were equipped with tablets and phones. For laptops and cameras, you'll need other solutions. Even action camera chargers may have a hard time fitting in this slim product.

It's not a problem that this thing is pretty much made out of nylon from the outside in but the material that makes up the exterior of this product makes it look cheap. It's a rough, synthetic material that just makes it a bit cheap looking. I think cloth or leather would have been a better choice.

In addition, the zipper sticks, making it hard to quickly open this up to retrieve your wires for charging.

title: Be aware, these are not active DisplayPort adapters
text:
I don't fully understand the difference between DisplayPorts but apparently, my computer's DisplayPort will not work with a simple HDMI adapter such as this. From my research, an "active" DisplayPort to HDMI adapter is sometimes necessary in order to successfully output a signal to an HDMI TV or monitor.

When plugging this adapter in, my computer doesn't even detect that a monitor is plugged in. I'm not sure why there is a need to label this adapter as supporting 4K if it doesn't do any sort of conversion...

title: Signal flickers
text:
plugging this DisplayPort to HDMI adapter to my computer, then to my HDMI switch, the signal flickers a lot and eventually, my monitor goes blank.

My computer has a single DisplayPort and an HDMI port. I purchased this adapter to enable multiple monitors but plugging this in to my HDMI switch (I use one of my monitors as a display for another device so I share the HDMI port). The signal coming out of this adapter initially looks very good, but less than a second later, static begins to flicker on the bottom half of the screen, then eventually, my monitor goes blank.

Plugging it directly into my monitor seems to be more stable, but it is not how I need this device to work.

title: Great cable that does exactly as it says.  High speed, high wattage.  A bit stiff
text:
This usb type-c to type-c cable is costs a little more than other cables you may see because it is not just a charging cable.

When it comes to the Type-C port, consumers now need to have a phd in electronics just to understand what works with what. There are just so many standards crammed into this reversible port that you need to really read the fine print to know whether it will work for your uses. What's worse is that once you throw these cables into a drawer, good luck finding the right one.

Type-C cables that come with your phone or phone charger will generally only be good for charging your phone, but not great for transferring data. This Type-C cable will carry up to 100w of power, meaning it will charge your phone or tablet at the highest speed it can support. When transferring data, this cable will allow you to copy files at the highest USB 3.1 speeds.

But more than that, this cable supports video signals so that it will be usable to connect your laptop or phone to a portable type-c monitor (assuming your devices support it).

Personally, I got this cable to work with a pair of NReal Air video glasses so that I have a backup to the cable included in the box. These cables work but are a little bit stiff.

title: Cheap build.  Didn't work for me.
text:
The Glorich DMW-DCC11 are made to plug into Panasonic Lumix cameras. They allow you to plug the camera into the wall so that you can use the camera for a longer period of time.

In terms of build quality, the product seems to be made from light-weight plastic and for me, I had problems fitting it into my camera and in the end, plugging it in didn't actually power on my camera. Yes, I did check the compatibility list for my camera and the GX85 is on the list. I may have received a defective item.

title: Great concept.  A compact surge protector with a lot of options
text:
The TROND Flat Plug Power Strip Surge Protector is a great concept. Everything about it shows that some thought has been given to its design. Unfortunately, their choice of materials weren't as well thought out.

Some design concepts that attracted me to this surge protector is that it gives you 8 power plugs in a surface area that's just under 4 x 4 inches. The four plugs at the top are grounded while the 4 on the side are two-prongs. In addition, the wall plug is flat, giving you a lot of options as to where you can plug this product in. Finally, there are three USB-A ports and one USB-C port.

However, as I've mentioned, some design choices are questionable. As with many surge protectors, the USB ports are under-powered. The Type-A ports are not too bad at 5V/2.4A, but there is no quick charge capability. The Type-C is not PD, so your charging options are no better than the Type-A ports. You're stuck with 5V/3A with a total wattage shared between them at 14W or 3.4A.

My second gripe is with the build material. Compared to many power strips, the plastic covering this product feels quite cheap. It has a smooth texture and just feels... thin to the touch. The same plastic also covers the wall plug. In addition, the power wire is thinner than other power strips that you'll find. They feel more like the two-prong extension cords, except that it has three wires.

Now, I don't have proof that their choice of materials will be an issue at all, but it does give me pause.

title: Could be a little taller and more firm.
text:
I converted a small room in my house into a useful room where the floor is covered in Japanese Tatami mats. These mats are used for everything. Sitting, lounging, and sleeping. It's a different concept from Western style rooms where the furniture is based around sitting on a sofa or chair. In a tatami room, everything is lower by a couple of feet.

In the room, we have floor chairs that are great for lounging on but what makes it even better is the ability to do some work in that room. This laptop desk was just the thing. With a tilting top surface, foldable legs for easy stowing, book and cell phone holders and even a small drawer, this desk seemed to be everything we wanted.

I do have to say that it really is something that I love using, but because of how often I need it, the shortcomings jump out at me every time. Firstly, the tilting function is fairly useless because it can only tilt at predetermined angles and nowhere in between. The tilt is just too much because of how low the table is. Tilt the table and it is touching your lap.

The second problem is as I said, the height. If this was a couple of inches higher, it would be perfect. As is, my lap barely fits under it.

The last problem is that the table is wobbly from side to side. It's just not very stable. I can't put a cup on it. I'm forced to use a either a closed bottle or a shelf on the side.

While this will work for now, I'll be keeping an eye out for a better table if one exists.

title: Multi device support with built-in mousepad.
text:
So how do 3's add up to a 4? If you want to talk about the typing experience for the HAMOPY Portable Tri-Folding Wireless Keyboard, it's a 3. When considering the track pad experience with this keyboard, it's also a 3. However, I'm giving this product a 4 overall because of what it can do, despite the experience being less than ideal.

Firstly, this keyboard/touchpad combo has quiet keys that are smaller than the keys on a laptop so your hands would have to squeeze in a little and if you have big hands, you're not gonna have a good time. Because of the folds, the keys are also somewhat compromised. The keys along the folds are squashed, especially the V key. With that said, between typing on a tablet screen or this keyboard, I'd choose the keyboard any day.

The touchpad can also feel a little bit cramped and somewhat insensitive when it comes to dragging, which is a tap and hold to start a drag. It does have the standard two-finger tap for right click and two-finger drag for scrolling (the scrolling direction is opposite of what I'm used to). While this touchpad will not be preferable over a tablet's touchscreen, it does work very well on machines that do not have a touch screen, namely a FireTV stick.

That is where this product shines. The two scenarios I listed were Typing with a tablet and typing/mouse with a FireTV. This product can do both with the press of a button. Able to be paired to three devices at once, I have a single, portable keyboard/touchpad that works with my three most-used devices. The trifold design makes this thing easy to pack into luggage or to simply stow away at the coffee table and easy to bring out when performing a search on the FireTV.

Great product whose versatility makes it worthwhile.

title: Volume seems to be a little low.
text:
I use an HDMI KVM to control multiple computers. This KVM has an optical output which extracts the audio channel from the HDMI port. I use this optical connection to connect to the 1Mii bluetooth transmitter.

The 1Mii Bluetooth 5.2 Transmitter for TV to 2 Wireless Headphones is a transmitter with an optical and a 3.5mm headphone jack inputs. On the output side, this device transmits through bluetooth 5.2 and supports various bluetooth audio standards such as APTX. You can connect up to 2 bluetooth devices to this transmitter and both will be able to hear the audio.

I picked up this transmitter to replace another transmitter because the 1mii has volume controls that is missing from the other transmitter and dedicated buttons to pair headset 1 and 2. After the replacement, I found that the audio coming from the 1mii was not as loud as my old transmitter. To address this, I actually had to install a volume plugin for Chrome which will boost youtube audio by over 200%. Unfortunately, I can't do the same for my other applications. This is a glaring problem that you will face every day when using this device.

To clarify this a little bit. I pair this device with an open ear bone conduction headset so that I can hear my surroundings while having the computer audio also in my ears. I can certainly put in an earplug to get better sound, it would defeat the purpose of using the open ear design when working at my computer.

title: Saved my headset
text:
These SOULWIT Cooling-Gel Ear Pads Cushions were not made for my headset, which is a USB gaming headset by [[ASIN: B01E8RS598 Sades]], which is no longer being sold.

Ear cups are pretty much the first thing to go on a headset and unless you have an expensive brand, it is hard to find a replacement cup for your specific headset. After two years of use, the cup of my gaming headset was falling apart and leaving little bits of plastic on my face after I use it. Rather than throwing away the headset, I wanted to try and find something that might work with it. I got lucky with this SOULWIT ear cup. It is attached via a stretchable flap, which is exactly how my old cups attached to the headset.

As you can see from my pictures, the shapes of the cups weren't the same as the originals had an odd angle to them but in the end, they fit and they are really comfortable.

The material is glossy on the sides, but where it touches your head, it is a soft cloth. I don't sweat a lot when I wear these so sweat being absorbed into the cup isn't an issue here, but I can see where someone who sweats will have problems with it. The gel is soft and comfortable.

I really love the new cups and the fact that I'll get more years of use out of my headset.

title: As advertised
text:
USB Type-C is just a super complicated situation all around. The ports themselves can be USB 2.0, 3.0, 3.1, 3.2, thunderbolt 3 or thunderbolt 4. I'm probably missing something there. That only covers data transfer speeds. For power, a Type-C port can be rated for multiple voltages and amperages. To protect the consumer from disaster (or they try anyway), each type-c product needs to be equipped with a chip that allows it to negotiate the speed and voltages. This includes the cables. The situation with cables is just as complicated. A cable may only be able to charge at 5v and not carry any data. They may carry only usb 2.0 data. Better ones may be rated for high speed data but not high wattage. Others have both high speeds and are rated for up to 100w. Good luck trying to find the right cable once all of them are dumped in a drawer somewhere.

This 240W USB C to USB C Cable 6.6ft is yet another odd one in the bunch. It is rated for high charging speeds but is only USB 2.0 for data. Why is it necessary though? I have a Dell Inspiron laptop that has a discreet NVidia RTX 3050 processor. This means that it has a high power demand.

This Dell was also designed to charge only from a USB type-c port and the input power must be 130w. So began my search for a charger that I can take with me when I'm away from my desk. I was able to find a macbook style charger that outputs 140w but I didn't own any cables that were rated for higher than 100w.

I came across this cable and connected everything up. During boot, the Dell's firmware still detected a low-powered charging device, but when I booted into Windows 11 and checked its power settings (after reconnecting the charger to the wall), Windows did not warn of an under powered charger as it normally would. I was then able to use this charging setup to play a graphics intensive game for over an hour with no sign of GPU or CPU throttling.

In the end, this cable allows me to have a portable solution for my laptop without having to lug around a standard laptop charger. It works.

title: Works well enough as a case and the laptop stand feature sets this product apart.
text:
In a world where seemingly all accessories are made for Apple products, it's necessary to accept that some things will just not fit right unless you've bought into the Apple ecosystem. I'm one of those holdouts that just don't find the value in Apple products but that's a personal preference.

With that in mind, I picked up this Gytumo Laptop Sleeve Case for a Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop. While that laptop is already quite thin, it wasn't quite thin enough for this case. As you can see from my pictures, the case is unable to close properly. Perhaps a stronger magnet would help to at least keep the flap closed. The design and material of this product doesn't lend itself to stretching in any way.

It's not so bad, though. It'll do when it comes to protection inside the backpack or handbag and it wasn't designed to handle a fall, no sleeve cases will.

I do like the fact that this case will act as a laptop stand to help it cool and to lift the keyboard to an ergonomic angle. It's why this product jumped out at me in the first place. The cover flap's corners fold in to create a triangular wedge that the laptop sits well on.

In the end, this case will do its job and I can deal with the fact that it won't fully close. It won't be a problem when it's inside the backpack anyway.

title: This did come with any plug converters because you shouldn't use them with this product.
text:
Traveling with electronics is inevitable and when traveling abroad, it's necessary to understand a few things about the places you will be traveling to. Language, currency, electrical standards, and cell phone bands being a few of them. Traveling to the UK or Europe, 220v is the electrical standards. To deal with this, you must understand the electronics that you will be bringing with you. Most modern electronics such as cell phone and laptop chargers will work fine at 220v with a plug adapter (make sure you check the power adapter regarding input voltage), but personal electric devices such as hair dryers and maybe electric shavers might not. There are two choices here. Look for hair dryers that have a switch to allow 220v or 110v. Otherwise, purchase a voltage converter.

The BESTEK 2000W Travel Voltage Converter power strip is one of the more powerful voltage converters that I've seen. Most voltage converters will not support hair dryers because they don't output enough amps for the devices to work. At 2000W, this voltage converter power strip is powerful enough to power most dryers out there (many work at 1800w). This device is well labeled to reduce any confusion. There are two output sockets. One rated at 200w for less intensive devices such as the electric toothbrush and my camera's battery charger. The other socket outputs the full 2000w. This is good for the hair dryer.

I was disappointed that this device doesn't work in the UK and since their standards are a little different from the EU, I didn't want to even try using a plug converter to try it. There's no guarantee as to what wattage the plug converter can handle so it's better to play it safe. Use this device only in the European countries and the others that are listed on this web page.

For me, I didn't take any chances with it. Since the USB ports are fairly standard at 2.4a output but no quick charge or type-c PD, I charged my phones using a different, more robust phone charger. I used this power strip only for the hair dryer with nothing else plugged in. Even then, I don't know that this thing can handle running the thing for too long.

In the end, I think the better strategy is to purchase devices that are rated for both 110v and 220v to save yourself some headache. I was able to find a third-party oral-b electric toothbrush charger rated for 220v and a travel hair dryer with the 220v switch. I'll still have this power strip with me for my camera until I can find a third-party charger for it.

title: Great for a beginner like me!
text:
I've been watching a bunch of electronics repair videos lately and thinking back at my past purchases and the electronics I threw away, I wondered how many devices I could have rescued. Determined not to let electronics repair scare me off from tacking them, I decided to start collecting the tools that I need to do my own repairs.

I started with an affordable, but well-reviewed soldering iron: the Pinecil. A good silicone mat (same one as StezStix Fix), and now a microscope.

The LLIMINK Digital Microscope 7'' LCD, Coin Microscope is a great product. In the box, you'll find all of the accessories you'll need to get started, including any cables that you might need. What I wasn't expecting of this device is that it is actually battery powered and that the battery is removeable (see my pictures) -- very much in line with the Right-To-Repair philosophy. The remote control was a nice addition as well (taking a picture seems to be only controllable from the remote so make sure you don't lose track of it).

The base of the microscope is aluminum with two built-in LED lamps that are separately powered from the microscope itself. They provide additional lighting from other directions if you need it. The microscope itself has bright leds that shine directly downward on the board.

If the microscope mounted LEDs are causing too much glare, there is a collar that can be fitted to the scope. It will block the LEDs and instead, reflect them so that the light is indirect. Kinda like the lamps the dentists use. You're not blinded by the bulb when you're looking up at those lights.

Moving on to the screen, it is a 7" screen with passable quality. The viewable angle isn't great but it gets the job done. Any issues with the screen quality is solved by connecting the included micro-hdmi cable to your monitor. I've included pictures of both the 7" screen and the ouptut from my monitor.

I've already done a couple of simple projects with the help of this device. I built a garage door opener and gate opener using microcontrollers that are connected to my home automation system. I'm building my confidence with electronics and soldering. Hopefully, I can keep more devices out of landfills by repairing them myself.

title: Create in concept, but might have build issues.
text:
I love the concept of this drive. In fact, I love the concept of drive enclosures with multiple functions (I had an enclosure that was also a portable router). This M.2 NVME Enclosure is a USB hub and memory card reader all-in-one without being any bigger than a standard NVME enclosure.

I love the tool-less design of this enclosure. A single button press allows you to slide the aluminum case open to insert the drive. To secure said drive, there are three cleverly designed clips (see my uploaded images). If your drive is shorter, you will use the first or second clip, but if your drive is the 2280 size, your drive will simply push down the first two clips and snap into the third.

Drive access speed is comparable to my other enclosures and the memory card reading feature works well.

Unfortunately, I had a couple of problems with my enclosure. Firstly, it did not work with my 1tb drive at all. It just wouldn't mount. It did work with my 512gb drive, but I found that the drive would disconnect after about 1 hour of being connected to my computer. Please check your product thoroughly while you're in your return period.

title: Good for IOT or guest WIFI networks, but wouldn't reconnect to my main router after a reboot.
text:
The Wavlink N300 Wi-Fi Range Extender is a quick and easy way to extend your 2.4gHz network to reach the remote corners of your house. It is easy to set up if you're familiar with normal router setup procedures (connect to its wifi or via ethernet cable, then access the router configuration through a browser). It will normally create a wifi SSID that's different from your original wifi, but you can just force it to use the same name.

For my phones and computers, I use my 5G wifi network but the older 2.4 Ghz is great for home automation products such as switches, doorbells, and cameras. Keeping those devices separate from your main network will keep your main network running smoothly and free up a lot of IP addresses on that network.

This device is very stable once it is set up. My IOT devices have been able to communicate at a good speed and have not lost connections yet.

Unfortunately, this extender did not automatically connect with my main router again when I rebooted it. In fact, I was forced to reset the device and set it up all over again in order for it to work. I can't say for sure that the problem is caused by this device or by my main router. It's just my personal experience. Perhaps test this functionality while you're still in your return period for the product.

title: Sleek and powerful with Type-C charging
text:
The Dell Inspiron 14 Plus 7420 Laptop, what a sleek little machine. It has a nice slate grey color with a matte finish. It is thin, it is powerful, and it just fits what my wife uses it for, which is some office work (word, excel, emails) and some media consumption (videos, social media, etc). Pretty much what everyone would need a laptop for.

Unfortunately, I'm unable to test this computer to its fullest with some games or video editing because I haven't been able to pry it away from my wife since she got it.

Looking simply at the specs of this machine, it is obvious that the i7 12th generation with the Intel Iris integrated graphics will be able to handle anything a casual user would be able to throw at it. The 16gb of ram will handle a LOT of browser windows and application being open at the same time. The 1tb ssd is actually great to have considering that many laptops only include half of this storage. Lastly, the 2.2K resolution is perfect for this small 14" screen. It's higher than full-hd 1080p and isn't too high to where the text and icons are barely legible.

The keyboard is the standard chiclet keys with good travel. It is quite and works well enough to not cause typos or missed key presses.

The screen is comfortable to look at and at 14" it allows this laptop to be a great portable workhorse.

Overall, I'm impressed with the stability, comfort, and just the build quality of this product. With the powerful CPU, I expect that this machine can last for quite a few years.

title: Great gimbal with strong motors
text:
Feiyutech is a brand that I've come to know for their camera accessories. Generally, their products have great build quality and is well-designed. I've had problems with their app working with LG phones but once I upgrade, that wouldn't be a problem anymore.

The FeiyuTech Official SCORP-C Camera Stabilizer is a 3-axis gimbal made for DSLR and mirrorless cameras. All of the axis arms are metal with high quality plastic in the body. The motors are quiet and there are plenty of buttons that control most aspects of the gimbal. There's even a video made by Feiyutech that explains the buttons very well. This SCORP-C model does not have an LCD screen.

The accompanying smartphone app is used to upgrade the gimbal firmware and for finer adjustments of the gimbal such as the follow speed and horizontal calibration. Control of the gimbal itself is also possible, but it is easier and faster to use the buttons on the device. It really is a good thing that the gimbal is designed to be operated without the need to fuss with a phone and app.

A few USB cables are included with this gimbal, which is designed to control the shutter of the camera that you own. Unfortunately, my Lumix GX8 is an odd model that just isn't well supported, even by Panasonic themselves. None of the included cables worked for me so this gimbal isn't able to control my camera. Not a big problem, though. If I really need wireless control of my camera, I can probably work out some sort of phone mount and use the Panasonic app. Just be aware that Feiyutech's list of compatible camera might be a little limited. They publish a compatiblity list. Just search for the term "Feiyu SCORP-C Lens Compatibility List"

With that said, the gimbal stabilization is great. Once your camera is balanced (search youtube for "Scorp-C Balancing" to see a video demonstrating this process), the motors are very, very quiet and the various follow modes help to create smooth motion in your videos.

Recently, I'm helping my daughter record videos and this gimbal has really come in handy. My camera doesn't support in-body stabilization for video and the lenses I have do not have in-lens stabilization. Gimbals are the best answers for my camera's limitations.

title: Good as an outdoor screen but not sure this is better than a painted wall when used indoors.
text:
Just as my title says, this 100 Inch Front and Rear Projector Screen is an acceptable projection screen for backyard movie nights but not great for indoor use.

It is a large piece of white, stretchy cloth that can be tricky to set up. Without a frame, you would need to figure out a way to stretch the screen taut without it sagging too much in the middle and you need to have these hooks set up well in advance of your event because it can take some time. Once you have a good setup for it, the screen is easy to hook up and stow away. It will fold nicely without leaving any creases the next time you need it again.

When used indoors, you will find that this screen leaks a lot of light through to the back wall because it is made to also be a rear projection screen and because of that you're probably losing a lot of the light that should be reflecting back to you. That's why I say that I don't think it works any better than a painted wall when used indoors.

The price of this screen is pretty low but just be sure you know what you're getting into with this screen or you'll just be disappointed.

title: A half-terrabyte for a good price
text:
I use the AIRDISK 500GB SSD in an external enclosure for portable storage. It has good read and write speeds through USB 3.1 and doesn't seem to get very hot while doing reading and writing.

It may not be the best choice for upgrading a gaming rig but it is perfect for quick storage, especially when used as a portable drive. I haven't had any problems with anything I wrote to it.

I'm unable to attest to the long-term stability of this drive, but if something goes wrong, I'll be sure to update this review.

title: Beefy, portable power that works with my Pinecil soldering iron
text:
This portable power bank is quite beefy and has some real heft. It weighs 2.5 pounds without the case but with this heft, you get some real power.

It sports two Type-A ports at 18w max, a type-c port at 45W max, and a 110V AC output at 120W max. The type-a ports are fairly standard and isn't anything out of the ordinary. The AC output should be enough to power most laptops but you would still need your laptop's power adapter.

The type-c port was why I wanted this device. It can be used to charge this power pack at 45w, which means you can fully charge this thing fairly quickly (sorry, I haven't timed it). The 45w output of the port allows me to run my pinecil soldering iron at full wattage, which means that my soldering iron can go to 300 degrees within 10 seconds.

Another use I had for this thing was that I had a skunk that was breaking into the crawl space under my house and I needed a camera to keep an eye on the movements of the skunk. Rather than purchasing a motion sensing camera, I was able to take one of my WIFI cameras and power it with this thing. The battery not only lasted the entire night, it only went down by one light (out of 4 lights total).

Two things I wish this power supply had: An adjustable DC output with a barrel connector. This would allow charging of laptops without having to plug in the laptop's adapter. I would also have liked the type-c port to support 100w because many laptops that charge by Type-C require at least 60w output. Those laptops will trickle charge from this power bank but will complain about it being under-powered.

title: Perfect for my Dell XPS 17 gaming laptop with RTX 3050
text:
Docking station or second power adapter? That's the question one would normally ask when considering a travel solution for their laptop. A docking station that sits on your desk with all of your accessories and monitor plugged in is a great solution that leaves the OEM power adapter available to be left in your travel bag. In the case of my Dell XPS 17, a docking station really isn't available for an affordable price.

The XPS 17 charges via the USB type-c port just like most laptops out there today, but it requires a 130 watt input through that type-c port. Most type-c docks or even power adapters only go up to 100w. If you wish to force the issue, the Dell thunderbolt dock will cost you over $200.

This 130w power adapter was the best solution for me. It truly delivers 130w as Windows does not give a warning regarding a low-powered power source when it is plugged in.

I had an extensive test of this device a few weeks back where I used it for three days straight. Initially, I thought it felt a little hot to the touch, but after rebooting my laptop, that no longer happened. I believe it was a problem with Windows power management.

This adapter comes with a nice, braided cable on the USB type-c side (normal two-pronged power cable on the other). The cable isn't overly stiff and feels like it has good build quality.

There really isn't much else that needed to be said about this adapter. It outputs the power as advertised and it worked great when I needed it. This will be the adapter I take with me on travel and my other adapter stays at my desk. Love it.

title: Fun little device
text:
The Frameo Digital Photo Frame 10.1 inch WiFi Digital Picture Frame is a fun little device that looks great on my family's piano. The matte black frame, while being plastic, doesn't look cheap and looks great on the satin-black finish of the piano.

This Frameo frame is basically a 10 inch android tablet without the built-in battery that tablets include. The OS is locked down by Frameo's customizations so only the frame's functionality is exposed. It would actually be nice if it can also display a webpage at the click of a button (to display weather or the dashboard for my home automation system) since it should have the capabilities to do that. The screen is 1280x800, which may seem low, but in practice, the pictures look clean and the backlight is really bright. I didn't feel like I was missing those extra pixels that higher resolution frames may have. That was pleasant surprise.

Setup for this device is quite simple. Set up the Wifi, download the app, and you're ready to send pictures from your phone to the picture frame. It's really great that you can share your pictures on this 10.1 in screen easily and quickly. Go out on a hike and took some great pictures? They can immediately go into the picture frame's slideshow rotation when you get home.

There is no account to sign up so anyone can download the app and input the sharing code generated by the frame to start sending pictures -- even over the Internet (which may or may not be a draw for you, depending on how security conscious you are).

With the ability to send over the Internet, I am planning on purchasing a second frame to gift to my parents. My brother and I can then send pictures of the kids to the frame every once in a while and my parents can have a nice frame to see their grandkids that is constantly updated.

title: This is a powerful vacuum/blower that works well for all sorts of functions
text:
The Xasla 15000mAh Electric Air Duster & Vacuum 2 in 1 is a great little device that works great for cleaning more than just a computer.

I wanted this thing for its blower functionality because it is always a good idea to clean out the vents in your computers once in a while to make sure they don't overheat. I have a laptop cooler that I use for my gaming laptop and that thing does get visibly clogged up with dust after about two months. It is great to have this thing around that I can just pick up and clean it whenever I want.

Obviously, this is intended as a replacement for canned air. Canned air can get into very narrow areas because they are equipped with a narrow straw to concentrate the airflow. Also because of how narrow the straw is, the air is very strong. The Xasla is not as powerful and the nozzle isn't as narrow as an air can's straw so it is not able to get into those deeper areas, but for the advantage of not having to worry about air running out in the middle of a cleaning and the convenience of having it available at all times, I think this is worth it.

The vacuum functionality is quite good as well. The first time I used this device as a desktop vaccum, I found that the suction was quite weak. Then I looked more closely at the device and found that there's a switch to change between blower and vacuum mode. After making the switch, the vacuum function worked much better. The difference between the two modes is that when the air exhaust is directed to the blower nozzle, there isn't a good amount of air flow to make a good vacuum. Moving the switch redirects the exhaust to a side vent that allows much greater flow.

This brings me to the only complaint about this device. The side vents was blowing on the desk while I was trying to vacuum up my desk. This is somewhat counter-productive, but in the end, it still got the job done.

One last thing about the Xasla 15000mAh Electric Air Duster & Vacuum 2 in 1. The battery handle is detachable and can be used as a battery pack for your phone. This is a nice bonus feature that can come in handy as well.

title: Some issues, but suits my needs
text:
[[VIDEOID:385afc8b9bb77a3a87ae44bd958be49a]] This double din aftermarket car radio has some great features, most important of which are the wireless Android Auto, wireless Carplay, and steering wheel controls. On paper it all sounds great, and it's really affordable to boot.

The implementation of the whole thing is just a little bit janky, but we'll get to that.

Installation:
I purchased a wiring harness for my Toyota Sienna 2009. My car is not the XL with surround speakers or dvd player so the wiring is really simple. Surprising to me was that the wiring harness colors matched up to the colors of this radio's wires exactly. Just match the colors and connect them together.

For steering wheel controls, it is necessary to patch into three additional wires: sw1, sw2, and sw gnd, which I located by searching google for "2009 Steering Wheel wiring diagram". I found a diagram of the back of my factory radio and using that, found the pins that the three wires ended in.

This radio didn't fit the generic mounting bracket for my van. It was almost as if the screw holes for this radio was drilled upside-down. If I were to mount the radio upside down, all of the holes would have lined up, but right-side up, they don't. Fortunately, the mounting bracket is plastic so I was able to drill the holes that I needed in order to successfully mount the radio.

Operating System:
This radio runs a rudimentary operating system with basic radio functions. It also seems to have the ability to play music from a USB drive.

The configuration options are limited. I found that I am unable to adjust the backlight of the radio at all and the screen is actually quite dim.

Android Auto:
Pairing of Android Auto is very easy. Simply connect the phone to the radio via a usb cable and choose the android auto function. Follow any on-screen prompts and you are connected. Disconnect the cable and the radio will try to connect to the phone wirelessly (make sure wireless AA is enabled on your phone).

The performance of AA can be a little laggy when compared to my other car, but it works well enough to bring my old car into the modern age.

Honestly, I'm actually okay with most of these issues because it is still much better than the original factory radio that lacked bluetooth and GPS. Being able to connect my phone to use its smart functions is all I really wanted out of this radio and that's what it delivers. Plus, I can still use my steering wheel controls. I'm satisfied with this purchase

title: The best low-priced led projector I've tried thus far.
text:
[[VIDEOID:6e49ad5f11d43ea1130e7014d1f00ce9]] I've always been interested in video projectors because I really wanted that theater experience at home. Previously, they have been out of reach because of the price of the devices as well as the price of the bulbs that required replacement.

In the last few years, LED projectors have really come down in price. When it became attainable for me, I started to try out various models and in the last two years, the prices have dropped to the $100-$200 range, even for native 1080p projectors.

As I've said, I have tried out various models and had problems with most of them, problems ranging from not being bright enough, 720p native, unable to fully focus the corners, or even that it needed to be very far from the screen to project a big picture.

The Vimgo Smart Projector is a stylish little projector that has a nice, vertical design that takes up less space than a normal projector. It has a good-sized speaker behind the cloth-covered side panels. The sound isn't high fidelity, but it can get pretty loud. Many other projectors barely comes with a 10w speaker or worse.

It is rated at 300 ANSI Lumen, which isn't going to work well in direct light but quite adequate when the lights are turned down. There are no dark corners and I find the picture to be evenly lit. The keystone functionality is great. You can adjust the "tilt" up and down as well as left and right. You can also zoom the picture out and if all else fails, each corner can be adjusted individually.

I really like that there is a motor that performs the focusing. With manual focus, I often get up and focus the projector, just to get back to my seat and figure out that the focus wasn't that great. With the focus controllable from the remote, I can sit close enough to really see if I got it just right.

The Android system works well for plex and jellyfin, which I have installed. Unfortunately, Netflix and Amazon Prime Video has DRM that prevents them from running on this projector, but that is easily remedied by projecting from your phone or with a FireTV connected to the HDMI (the USB port outputs enough amps to power the FireTV).

Here's a tip: Install the Android TV Launcher by downloading the APK file to a USB drive, then choose the USB app from the projector to install it. It is not only a better-looking launcher, it will also give you access to the full Android system settings. I wouldn't suggest setting it as the default launcher, though because I haven't found a way to launch the built-in launcher manually.

I also found that the Vimgo projector actually has a shorter throw distance than my previous projectors. I'm able to get a larger picture when set up at the same distance as my previous projectors. I actually had to zoom out to make the picture a little smaller to fit my projection screen.

So to conclude, the Vimgo projector does not have any of the problems that I found in my previous projectors. It is stylish and compact with a great picture and good-enough audio (for small gatherings, not for a home theater experience).

title: Works as advertised
text:
I got this ram to double the amount of ram that I currently have. While I'm a power user, I'm not a performance snob. I don't care about benchmarks and gaining just that tiny bit of performance. What I needed was more ram space in order to do video editing and gaming. There was definitely a performance improvement simply by the fact that there is less necessity to cache to SSD.

The SABRENT ram have not introduced any instability to my system. No blue screen of death due to poor quality ram and no hiccups during use.

With 32gb of ram, you'll have enough for every day use and still have plenty of overhead for memory hogging activities such as photo and video editing (as long as you're not working with super high resolution or with too many files at a time).

title: Survived the wash, but I wouldn't suggest that you try it yourself!
text:
These Omidyi True Wireless Sleep Earbuds are my second pair because I accidentally threw my previous pair in the wash. Surprisingly, my original pair survived and this pair is now my backup.

Here is my original review:
These earbuds aren't bad at all, if you use earbuds to fall asleep. The advantages these earbuds have over wired ones are, of course, the wires. I used to go through wired sleep earbuds fairly quickly because I tend to pull on them quite a bit when I sleep. There are no wires to tangle here.

What makes these earbuds "sleep" earbuds are that they are much smaller than normal wireless earbuds (see my picture). They sit flush in my ears and don't protrude. In general, depending on your ears, these may actually allow you to lay sideways and still be comfortable. In my case, I can lay against my right ear without it hurting me but I can't do the same with the left. I often end up using only the right bud.

In terms of sound quality, due to their size, these earbuds will not be loud nor will they have great sound depth. The battery life also lasts about 5 hours due to their size.

I still really like these buds because I do like them more than wired ones but I don't use them any other time.

title: Not bad for sleeping but won't replace other earbuds
text:
These Damipow True Wireless Sleep Earbuds aren't bad at all, if you use earbuds to fall asleep. The advantages these earbuds have over wired ones are, of course, the wires. I used to go through wired sleep earbuds fairly quickly because I tend to pull on them quite a bit when I sleep. There are no wires to tangle here.
