title: Good, basic machine with a discreet graphics card and plenty of ports
text:
This HP Pavilion desktop is a solid, but basic PC that, while it can be considered a gaming PC with its discreet Radeon RX 5500 card, that isn't going to raise too many eyebrows with its specs. What's out of the realm of this machine would be 4K gaming and VR, but it can run most modern games at medium settings at 1080p.

That's not why I needed this machine, though. As a Plex server, this serves well. It is quiet and can transcode videos using hardware transcoding. Unfortunately, it only has a single slot for an additional hdd. As a video editing machine, it can handle 1080p videos, but will struggle with 4K. As a photo editing machine, it can edit pretty much anything from the devices you have, but if you work in print, you'll find this machine lacking. For emulation, this machine will work quite well for all classic systems and even some more modern ones. Of course, for everyday web browsing and watching videos, this thing will be more than enough.

Overall, this is a fairly priced machine that is a step up from the basic computers that one may find and the discreet GPU will help to make this machine last longer than those with embedded graphics.

title: Simple pair of earbuds that work well for video conferencing
text:
These SUYUZREY 3.5mm Jack Wired Earbuds were for my daughter who needs it for her laptop when she is doing video conferencing during her group study sessions. This means that sound fidelity wasn't the primary purpose for their purchase.

These earbuds are comfortable for extended study sessions and with the included memory foam ear pieces, there's a good variety of sizes and comfort. Voices come through clearly and the microphone works well, but of course suffers the same problem as any other on-wire microphone: It can be a little far from the mouth and rubbing against the cloth can creating noise.

There isn't much else to say about a simple pair of earbuds like these.

title: Good headphones that leave your ears open so you're not cut off from the world.
text:
Bone conduction headphones have become quite popular and because of this, there are many to choose from. This specific model is quite minimalist. A thin metal frame with the vibration units and electronics hanging off it.

In terms of comfort, there is no adjustability to the metal frame so it may take some getting used to because the frame may feel like they are too big or too small depending on your head size. For me it felt a little bit loose but I came to realize that it actually stayed where you place it and it really wasn't a problem.

For sound quality, this bone conduction headphone will never match a nice pair of over-ear headphones but that really isn't what it's for. By leaving the ears open, one is still able to stay aware of the surroundings, making it great for cycling and jogging where hearing the traffic is essential for safety reasons.

A pair of earplugs are included with this product and with one or both in, one can really appreciate the difference between regular headphones and bone conduction. You can still hear the music (or in my case, audiobook) through the earplugs because of the bone vibration but all outside sound is cut off. This means that you'd be able to listen to music over the sound of a loud machine.

I have tried a few different pairs of bone conduction headphones and these are the ones that I have stuck with so far. The buttons maybe be somewhat limited (just two buttons that control volume and power), but they are easily reachable and not hard to press and the IPX6 means it's water resistant against rain and sweat.

title: Great mobile router with a T-Mobile restriction
text:
I love GL.iNet. They create routers based on OpenWRT, which has so many great features that you'd find in professional level routers that cost thousands of dollars. There is a fairly steep learning curve to it, though. Fortunately, GL.iNet understands this and makes things easier by creating their own customizations to the firmware to make OpenWRT easier to use and more custom to the routers themselves.

The GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) is their latest 4G LTE router. Pop in a sim card and the router will create a hotspot that routes to the LTE network. For additional protection, it is easy to set up the router to connect to a VPN provider. By connecting the router to VPN, all client computers connecting to it WIFI will be protected.

I used this router during my last trip and it was GREAT. I have a few devices that I bring with me. A laptop, tablet, and phone. I even bring a firetv with me sometimes. While in the car, I have the router connecting everyone's devices to the Internet via LTE and when I got to the hotel, I connected the router to the hotel's wifi and turned on VPN. The transition from LTE to hotel wifi was seamless. Not only did I not need to reconfigure everyone's devices to connect to the hotel WIFI, we were also secure behind the router's firewall and VPN connection.

The two restrictions that this product may present to potential buyers is first, the price. It is quite pricey and it can be hard to justify its purchase. Especially when you can get a travel router for around $40 with the ability to tether a phone via USB. The second issue is that this specific router is tied down to the T-Mobile network with no ability to unlock it for other networks (according to the seller's response in the questions section of for this product). If the convenience and the ability to fully control the TTL to bypass t-mobile's tethering throttling restrictions is important to you, it may justify the price you'd be paying.

title: Runs on old variant of Openwrt firmware.  Hope they address it soon.
text:
I love GL.iNet. All of their routers can run on either their own openwrt with added custom UI and ease-of-use packages or you can install their provided barebones openwrt. You can even download and install the firmware directly from Openwrt.org if available.

With that said, the GL-AX1800(Flint) WiFi 6 Router is a disappointing product. In the last year, Openwrt has made setting up a mesh network of routers using 802.11r and 802.11s but only if you're running version 19.07 or higher. I wanted this router in the hopes that I can upgrade to WIFI 6 for my custom mesh network but I was sad to find that the variant of the firmware is based off version 15.

While gl.iNet has backported all of the necessary security patches from the newer kernels, it won't help the many power users who have come to depend on the new Openwrt version.

Due to this, I didn't give this a thorough test to figure out its stability and wifi speed as both of these can be affected when/if the company finally updates the firmware to a more recent version. Meanwhile, this router will sit in my closet waiting for its day to shine.

title: Good if you want to use these for swimming, I guess.
text:
These bone conduction headphones are waterproof (IP68) and come with 16GB of storage so that they would work while swimming (bluetooth will not work well under water and really doesn't have the distance to cover a pool). They can be fairly loud and can be heard even with (especially with) earplugs.

The advantages of an open-ear, bone conduction headphone is that you can hear everything going on around you while still being able to listen to your music or audiobook. Put earplugs in your ear and you can retreat into a more private listening experience.

The disadvantage is that the sound quality is just not going to be as good as headphones that cover your ears. That is especially true for this pair of headphones.

The sound quality from these headphones is not good. The lows are barely audible most of the time and when you turn up the volume to try and hear more of the lower tones (including human voices), the higher tones are already too loud. This is alleviated by putting in earplugs. The plugs will block most of the higher tones as those come out of the speakers themselves while the low tones come in through the vibrations.

Another issue I have is that the buttons are horrible. They are made of a single piece of rubber on the outside and the buttons themselves are recessed pretty far in. This means that I have to push quite far before actually hitting the button and there is just no tactile response to know that I've actually pressed it. This makes everyday use of these headphones a chore.

The last problem I have with it is the custom charging cable. I really do not like devices that do this. Not only do you have to remember to bring the cable with you if you need to charge in your car or elsewhere, if it breaks, you're pretty much screwed.

For the price they are charging (more than Aftershokz Titanium), this really isn't worth it.

title: A basic projector with great brightness and full HD resolution
text:
The WEWATCH Video Projector with WiFi and Bluetooth is a basic projector that has all of the necessary features that one needs.

The description of this product may lead you to think otherwise, but this projector is not really a "smart" projector. It does not run on Android and the built-in user interface is quite basic. Yes, it will play videos and show photos from USB drives and it has WIFI... for whatever reason (I didn't really look into it because I simply plugged in a FireTV). The bluetooth, on the other hand, does have a function. I'll get into that in a bit.

So for video input, you have two full sized HDMI ports, a VGA (for those ancient laptops that your office may have lying around?) and a USB port which outputs enough amperage to run a fireTV, so no additional power adapter necessary.

There is no automatic keystone adjustment, but what is there works well. You can adjust the four corners up and down, although I found that it still seems to have some bloating in the middle no matter how I adjust it (could be a problem with my projection screen and projector positioning). A tip for doing the adjustment: If you aren't able to move the corners in the direction that you need, try adjusting the zoom first. By zooming out, it allows the corners to be pulled up or down more.

Audio is as expected in that it is not winning any awards. It can get pretty loud, but it still sounds empty. This is where bluetooth or the 3.5 mm headphone jack comes in. For wireless audio, you can either pair a bluetooth speaker/soundbar to the projector itself or you can pair the speakers directly to the FireTV or whatever dongle you're using. The advantage of pairing the speakers to the projector is that they will work for both HDMI inputs. If you really wanted to get full surround, you'll have to extract the audio out of the HDMI wire. Basically plug the HDMI into an audio receiver, then the audio receiver to the projector. The receiver can take care of decoding the surround depending on your setup.

For the brightness, the 1100LM beats out many other projectors of this price and resolution. You can really tell that the picture just pops. It will work well enough in a dimly lit room, but you can only truly appreciate it when the lights are completely off.

Overall, this is a low-priced projector that will work well for outdoor, temporary use, or even a permanent setup inside the home.

title: All-Metal.  That's good and bad...
text:
I listen to audiobooks to fall asleep at night so I wear "sleep" earbuds as to not disturb my wife. I usually buy the soft silicone type, which never have good audio quality, but does the job. They usually break withing a couple of months because I tend to tug on them a lot when I sleep so this time, I decided to try out these ceramic Wired Headphones with Microphone.

My initial impressions of these earbuds are that they have better sound quality than the other sleep earbuds that I've tried. They also have excellent build quality. There are silicone reinforcements at all of the wire connection points to protect them from failing due to tugging and the shape of the earbuds are as flat as possible.

When in my ears, these metal earbuds do not protrude at all, they lie flat. I tested by lying on my side to see if they would hurt but they seemed okay because nothing protrudes. Then after a couple of nights, I found that while direct downward pressure doesn't hurt, the earbuds do hurt when they are nudged from side to side, which happens when I'm shifting positions at night.

So overall, I'm still using these earbuds and have gotten used to them, but they do still hurt occasionally, depending on how much I move at night.

title: No keystone, 720p native, bright.
text:
The Salange 7500 LUX Mini Home Projector is a barebones projector that provides good brightness, good focus, full-sized HDMI input, but not much else. Connect a FireTV or AndroidTV device to this projector and you have all of the "smart" features that you'll need.

So the good of this projector is that it is somewhat compact, not as small as the pico projectors, but small enough... it's about the size of a bread box (as the saying goes). The focus ring is fairly tight, meaning that once you find your focus, it won't move. The USB outputs enough amps to power a FireTV and overall, it is very straightforward to use.

The bad is that there is no keystone adjustment, not even the analogue kind that tilts the lens. The resolution is only 720p and I found that projecting at a shorter range of around 9 feet, I'm able to see every pixel on the projected image. At a longer distance, the pixels may meld together better.

In summary, this is a low-priced projector that will project an image through an HDMI input. If that's all you're looking for, this will work, but if you're looking for something that you may set up more permanently, this isn't it.

title: Sturdy metal build, good read/write speeds and very versatile.
text:
This 5-in-1 card reader is exactly what I needed. It is fast, well-built, and connects to everything that I own.

Being USB type-c, this card reader will read and write to your microsd or SD card at the maximum speed that it is capable of. I found that the speed is in line with my previous reader as well as my laptop's built-in reader.

This reader has connectivity for Type-A, Micro-usb type-b, and USB type-c. It means that I can use this reader for my phones, including any older models that support USB host-mode and all of my PC's, including my Dell XPS that only has type-c ports.

Connected to the phone, I can back up my pixel phone, without having to upload all of the pictures to the cloud. Connected to my computer, I can quickly transfer files to and from my mirrorless camera.

This product does exactly what I need it to do and with its metal build and protective caps, this will be a product that I will carry in my tech bag.

title: These are NOT bone conduction headphones
text:
The only thing these headphones have going for it is a respectable battery life. Everything else is just a disappointment, unfortunately.

I've been trying to find a good but affordable pair bone conduction headphones because I keep a headphone on my head almost all day while I work and write my code but I end up shutting the rest of the family out and miss half of the conversations going on in the house. When I discovered open ear bone conduction, it seemed to be the perfect solution.

So far, I have not found a good one. The specific problems of this pair of headphones is that it is not bone conduction. It is a simple pair of speakers set next to your ear. There is no bone shaking going on. With bone conduction, you can put in earplugs and still hear the audio fairly clearly, with these, the sound is clearly muffled and hard to make out.

In addition, there is a half-second delay on these headphones meaning they are no good for watching videos. I have not experienced bluetooth delay in quite a few years so I wasn't expecting it. Further, there is no charging light, meaning there is no way to tell if they are charged or not.

Then there's the price they are charging for this thing. Everything is just NO.

title: Works well and is as I hoped.
text:
I'd seen these gel things being sold for cleaning keyboard and car interiors. I knew the concept but didn't know how well they worked. Now that I've tried it for myself, I really like it. When cleaning a car's center console, there are many corners that a towel just won't reach this gel can mold itself into those corners and its sticky nature will take out the little dust that is stuck there.

The texture of a gel is somewhat thicker than the slime that kids make with white glue and doesn't easily break apart. This is why it is great for cleaning keyboards. The gel can get in between the keys but it won't rip apart and leave pieces of itself under the keys.

There is an odd smell to the goop but that's expected of slime and other types of gels like this.

title: All the right ports, but doesn't work with Switch
text:
This Type-C dock really has everything one would need and on a Dell XPS, it truly is a must-have accessory. This dock doesn't waste useless space and circuitry with a VGA port like many others out there and provides a displayport instead. This means a total of three video outputs are possible, although I haven't tried it myself.

The power pass through on this dock only supports up to 100Watts, which means that the Dell XPS (which comes with a 135w power supply) would still warn that it is charging with a low-powered device and will throttle itself. So this dock will not the the one connection that will connected all of your devices. You'll still need to plug the power adapter in separately.

This dock will provide three usb 3.0 and two usb 2.0 type-a ports to your laptop while the SD and microSD card reader means you don't need to go searching for your card reader when you want to transfer some files. The gigabit ethernet will mean that you're running your games wired and the 3.5mm headphone jack is always good to have.

Overall, the dock worked well for me. The Ethernet did not drop connection like my previous dock, but I did find that the Dell XPS sometimes did not detect the HDMI monitor but that may be just because of my setup.

title: Good build quality and good picture quality.
text:
This Wireless WiFi Outdoor Security Camera Solar Battery Powered is a good camera. Taking it out of the box, I was able to tell that it is well-built and well thought out. The solar panel is of good quality and can be mounted on the camera or separately. The necessary USB extension cable and extra mounting arm is included in this camera kit if you decide to mount the panel separately from the camera. Mounting is easy. Just two screws into the eaves and you're done. No wires to pull and no batteries to change. Compare this with systems like Arlo where you would need to break out your ladder to switch out batteries every month or spend extra to purchase a solar panel for each camera.

This camera has all of the standard functions of live feed, motion detection, and night vision but of course it also has the pan and tilt function which helps to get a clearer picture of what you're trying to see. Local SD card storage means that a subscription service isn't necessary to review past events. It's all quite nice. I did find that there is a significant lag in the camera. It can take a full second for any pan and tilt commands to actually go through.

This camera works with the Tuya app (also works with Smart Life) so it's up to you to decide how much you can trust those apps, but otherwise the camera is a solid purchase.

title: Broken on first day.  Do NOT charge without first turning off the device
text:
I received my Tayogo Wireless Bone Conduction Open-Ear Headphones this morning and used it the entire day. While the sound quality isn't as good as a true on-ear headphone or earbuds, the advantage of a bone conduction headphone is the ability to keep your ears open to your surroundings. It was exactly what I needed.

It was a little bit odd to feel the bass vibrating my head at first, but I soon got used to it. I really did like this style of headphones.

At the end of the night, I plug the headphones in and I see the charging light come on. A couple of seconds later, it goes off and from then, I couldn't get any response from the headphone at all. No matter how long I try to hold the power button, it just won't turn on.

I realized that I forgot to first turn off the headphones before plugging it in. I believe that may be what caused the problem.

Quite disappointed to have a device work only for 1 day.

title: Acceptable for portable storage, will probably not cut it for PS5.
text:
The Centon Premium SSD at 1TB is priced higher than even the WD_Black while claiming faster speeds. Before I get into my conclusions, I need to say that I'm only testing this drive through a USB enclosure so the conditions aren't optimal, but my conclusion about this drive is in comparison to another drive that I test through the same enclosure, meaning all conditions are the same between the three drives.

I had two other drives that I was able to performance test against this Centon drive. The first is a [[ASIN:B09575SWX5 Pioneer NVMe]] drive at 256GB and the second is a [[ASIN:‎B08695D3VW Klevv NVMe]] drive at 512GB. All three drives were placed inside a USB drive enclosure and connected via a Type-C cable capable of video transfer (meaning it's made for data transfer, not just charging).

Because I'm only testing through USB 3.1, I'm not expecting to reach advertised speeds but using the relative performance between the three drives under the same conditions, I can make some conclusions. The Pioneer drive is advertised at speeds of up to 2,100/1,600 MB/s and in my setup, I was able to reach 1,041/937 MB/s which is quite impressive. On to the Klevv drive: it is advertised at speeds of up to 2,050/1,650 MB/s and my results for this drive was 915/922 MB/s. Both drives are quite affordable and for use as a fast, portable storage, they work well.

Now, the Centon makes big claims. It is advertised at 5,500/1,800 MB/s. That's faster than WD_Black's advertised speed of 3,600 MB/s read! This is obviously aimed at those who are looking to upgrade a PS5 with more storage, but my results can be see in the screenshot. Under the same conditions, it only meets the performance of the Klevv and is slower than the Pioneer. I don't have high confidence for this actually being great for a PS5.

In addition, just as a previous review stated: I received this drive in an electrostatic bag inside an Amazon Prime envelope. I was lucky that the drive was still functional when it got to me.

Not impressed.

title: easy to use, nice clamshell design, but a little bit too flexible.
text:
The Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is only 1/2" thick when folded, and of course, half that when undfolded. It is quite thin and portable. It caught my attention because it supports pairing with up to 3 bluetooth devices simultaneously and with many of us having multiple devices (phone and tablet is quite normal), these devices are great for someone like me.

The clamshell design means that the keys are protected when closed. It also holds itself closed magnetically, and powers on my simply opening it. Pairing is easy: hold the function key and press one of the Q,W, or E keys to select one of the three bluetooth slots, then press the big "connection" button on the left bezel of the keyboard. This all seems pretty slick to me but I did have one concern with this keyboard's design and that is the hinge system. When the keyboard is open, it is quite easy to twist it with just a little bit of pressure. It means that I'm always extra careful when I'm taking it out of my bag.

In terms of functionality, the keys are a the same size as the ones on my laptop and has the same amount of travel as well, although they are a little bit louder than my laptop's keys when typing. I'm using this keyboard to type this review right now. What I found is that the keys are a little bit unresponsive. I keep missing letters every few words I type. Just in this last sentence, I had to go back about 5 times to correct missing letters. This defeats the purpose of purchasing a keyboard to type more quickly on a mobile device. Perhaps if you are normally heavy-handed when you type on a keyboard, you wouldn't face this issue.

Something that I wish this keyboard had is a touch pad. If this device can be both a keyboard and mouse, it would be much more useful.

Overall, the Samsers Wireless Portable Folding Keyboard is a good device but ultimately, it has a couple of shortcomings that keep it from being great.

title: Fits my XP-Pen Artist 22 perfectly!
text:
I had a problem when I received my [[ASIN:B08X46P868 XP-Pen Artist 22]], a 21.5" monitor with a pressure-sensitive pen input for digital art. I'm not a full-time digital artist, so I couldn't lose a significant amount of my desk space to this monitor, nor do I have a justification to set up a separate station for digital art.

For the first week or two, I tried to use the original box for the item, but it was a hassle dealing with the styrofoam packaging trying to pull it in and out of the box when I needed to use the machine. I needed a protective case that will allow me to easily set up and stow the monitor.

The KISLANE Travel Carrying Case was the perfect solution. Advertised as a travel case for a 24" iMac, this case looked perfect for my uses. It was such a great relief when I first fit the monitor in the case and found it to have the exact dimensions that I needed. Really, it is like a glove fit, for the monitor!

In addition, there are plenty of pockets for the power adapter, pen case, USB cable, and an additional accessory that I use with the monitor.

I didn't know there was a need for such a product as this but I'm very happy that I'm able to benefit from it. I'm now able to keep my desk clean for normal work on the computer, but pull out the screen when I need to do some video editing or digital drawing.

title: Large 21" screen for better drawing experience
text:
I'm not a professional artist nor do I have a lot of experience with digital art, but that is one of the reasons that XP-Pen is a good choice for someone like me. Wacom rules the digital art world but for someone who is only a hobbyist when it comes to digital media, I have a hard time justifying paying the price that they charge. With that in mind, XP-Pen and Huion are the brands that I target for my budget.

Previously, I purchased a Huion Kamvas 13 and it was a great product but with my aging eyes, I needed a larger screen as even the 1080p resolution screen on that 13" screen was a little bit difficult for me to see without reading glasses. So when I had a chance to upgrade to a 21" XP-Pen, I took it.

This puts me in a situation where I am able to compare the two brands with each other. Both brands sport very similar pens and both screens have a matte surface to give the pens some friction for that "paper-like" feel. I'd say it's more like pen on paper feel, whereas I would've preferred to have more friction but it's something I think is worth training myself to get used to.

The XP-Pen drivers are on-par with the Huion drivers. Once the drivers are installed, it will show a preview of the screen layout that you have set up in Windows and it's quite easy to select the correct screen area that the pen should direct its touch to. From there, the pen buttons can be customized to macros that fit your needs and of course you can set up a different macro for each app that you use.

There are no additional macro assignable buttons on the XP-Pen screen, but there are standard OSD menu buttons at the top of the monitor, just like any other monitor you may own.

I'm happy to report that the XP-Pen drivers run alongside the Huion drivers without conflict. I have a Huion macro pad to make up for the buttons that are missing on the XP-Pen monitor.

So not being a professional artist, I do still try to spend as much time as I can to learn digital drawing and painting. In addition, I have interest in video and photo editing, so this pen tablet is great for selecting subjects using the rotoscope tool in video editor or smart select tools in image editors. Then there's 3D modeling. The pressure sensitive pen is great for sculpting in Blender and other 3D modeling programs. This is also something I'm trying to learn as well.

Despite the multitude of uses that I described above, I also don't have the desk space to devote to this 21" beast. It means that I needed a way to safely stow it. I didn't expect that I would find a carrying case for a large monitor, but to my surprise, that's exactly what I found! This [[ASIN:B099ZSDQ6V KISLANE travel carrying case]] fits the XP-Pen perfectly. It is big enough for the monitor, including its adjustable height stand and has plenty of pockets for the power adapter, pen, usb cables and my Huion macro pad. I didn't think there would be a market for people who thought "hey, it'd be great if I could bring my 24-inch iMac on my trip!", but thanks for that! Now I have a case for my 21" pen tablet.

One thing to note: I ran into an issue with inconsistent pressure with the XP-Pen drivers where I would run the pen across the scree and the darkness or width of the line would be very jittery. It was only alleviated by turning off the setting called Microsoft Ink. After my computer upgraded to Windows 11, I haven't seen this issue. So if it happens to you, try turning of that setting.

title: Attach my camera HOW?
text:
The premise with the ENSGO TC7 8” Teleprompter and others like it is to find a lens adapter that fits your camera and then screw it into your camera... then let your camera hang, by those threads, from the teleprompter. What??

First, the product: included in the box of the ENSGO TC7 8” Teleprompter is a set of lens adapters for common lens sizes going from 49mm to 82mm. There's also a bracket for a phone mount along with a couple of foam pieces to use with the phone adapter. Lastly, a bluetooth remote control for use with teleprompter apps.

If one follows the included directions or even use the product images as a guide, this would be the setup: Pick the correct adapter size and screws it to the lens of the camera. The adapter then slips into a slot in the main body of the product and from there, the tripod is mounted to the teleprompter or the camera. In either of these mounting scenarios, the thread holding the camera to the adapter is expected to hold the entire weight of the camera or the weight of the teleprompter + tablet. Please do NOT do this.

I use two tripods for this setup. One for the teleprompter and the other for the camera itself. I have yet figured out a secure bracket that would allow the camera to mount to the teleprompter without putting pressure on the screw threads.

title: Dell XPS is universally well reviewed, but still has its issues
text:
Super thin, huge 17" touch screen with colors that just POP, large touchpad mouse, and silent chiclet keyboard. These are just the initial impressions one would see at first blush when approaching this high-quality laptop. Look a little deeper and one would find that this Dell XPS 17 sports a powerful 11th generation I7-11800H cpu with a dedicated RTX 3050 graphics card with Nvidia's real-time ray tracing and 16gb of ram. A 512GB ssd rounds out the entire package.

The Dell XPS 17 is simply elegant and high-quality. I was able to upgrade this laptop to Windows 11 painlessly and the new UI just looks great on this screen. It runs silently during normal web browsing and video watching. When playing games, the fan kicks in and the cooling seems adequate, but I still have an external laptop cooler helping it along.

Speaking of games, this laptop will run the latest games, but being at the bottom of the RTX line of graphics cards, the screen's 3840x2400 resolution simply is too much for the 3050 to run at the highest quality. It means that one would either run at a lower resolution or lower quality. The resolution issue can be alleviated if one turns on DLSS for resolution scaling.

So that is one of the first problems I would point out with the specs that I have in this laptop. The RTX3050 paired with the super high resolution means one must compromise in some way. In addition, performance in VR is somewhat poor. Half Life: Alyx runs well at low quality settings but any higher and the screen stutters and can cause nausea -- this was tested through wired and wireless configurations.

The second complaint that I have for this laptop is that the only included ports are 4 usb Type-C ports, headphone jack and an SD card reader. It is great that the ports support up to Thunderbolt 3, but the fact that no Type-A ports are available, dongles will be a part of life. It's nice that Dell includes a dongle that sports an HDMI and a Type-A port, there is no ethernet or display port support out of the box.

A good 9-in-1 dongle will cost you at least $60 and even then, the quality could be questionable. I happened to have a 9-in-1 dongle, but the ethernet port seems to lose connection constantly. This means that either you take a chance with a $60 no-name dongle or you spend over $100 for a proven one.

This then brings me to the last problem that I want to point out. A gaming PC has very high power requirements. Currently, there is no Type-C product that will provide (or pass through) the 130W that the Dell XPS 17 will require. It means that the nifty dock that you bought to get the additional ports that you need? It won't be able to power the laptop. You can connect a 100W charger to the laptop, but you will get a warning from the operating system. So perhaps on travel, one can get away with trickle charging the laptop, but at home, you will always be stuck with taking up two ports, one for power and one for your monitor.

Overall, this is a GREAT laptop with high quality build, but at the current specs, some things just cause awkward situations that one needs to work around.

title: Touch works on Android, but requires a dock to work with Switch.
text:
What sets the INNOCN 15.6" portable monitor apart from other type-c portable monitors is the built in battery and the touch screen features. In the box, a soft silicone case is included with a cover that folds into a stand, making it feel like an oversized tablet.

Other portable monitors with built-in battery are usually a little bit thicker or have a bulge at back of the screen. The INNOCN doesn't have that. It is a thin slab that is around 3/8" thick. I actually use it as a secondary screen on a daily basis and while the monitor has an all aluminum casing, there is almost no heat generated by the screen during use.

The touch capability of this monitor brings touch support to any Windows PC without the need for drivers but even more, connect this to an Android phone such as my LG V40 and not only does the phone go into desktop mode, the touch screen works to turn the phone into a 15.6" tablet! The built-in battery will help to keep the phone topped off and allow fully wireless (no need to plug into the wall, but there will be a wire between phone and screen) tablet.

My previous monitor was a LePow 15.6" type-c portable Monitor. It is representative of many other portable monitors on the market. Compared to the INNOCN, the INNOCN is a lot brighter and the colors more vibrant. The LePow was instant on but the INNOCN can take about 2-3 seconds to turn on after receiving a signal. Both have speakers that are tinny and quite weak, but serviceable if you're on-the-go.

If you are purchasing this monitor to work with the Nintendo Switch, you will be disappointed. The Switch is very picky about the conditions that must be met before it goes into docked mode, mainly a 19v type-c PD. The power output from this monitor simply doesn't supply that, even when plugged in to an original Nintendo power adapter (the adapter will serve to charge the screen, but will not supply the 19v to the connected switch). It will only work with the switch through a dock, which really defeats the purpose of a portable monitor. On the other hand, the LePow does actually does work with the switch. Connected a power adapter or portable phone charger to the LePow and the monitor will supply the necessary 19v to the Switch.

So overall, a great monitor for most uses, especially the ability to turn a phone into a large touchscreen tablet, but if you want a portable large-screen solution for the Nintendo Switch, go for something like the LePow

title: Easily folds/unfolds and keeps its shape
text:
My first photo box was an 11x11x11 model by the same manufacturer. It was small and folded up quite easily. I was satisfied with it but its size limited its use to to photographing smaller items. Also due to its smaller size, it was necessary to post process the pictures because the sides of the box would always show up in the pictures.

Since then, I tried a cheaper 16x16x16 photo box with translucent vinyl walls that needed assembling to get set up and even after it was assembled, the walls were flimsy and tended to bow in on itself. Stay away from those if possible.

So when I came across this 16x16x16 photobox, I knew it would be better than the vinyl one. It comes with the same set of colored backdrop cardboards as the smaller box, but its light has adjustable brightness and warmth. Additionally, it addresses one of the problems that I have with the smaller box which is that the light ring is mounted on the inside of the box without any diffuser. This means that if the object in the box is reflective, the led will show up in the pictures. This larger box has a couple of velcro strips on its side walls where a cloth diffuser can be hung and the harsh led reflections will no longer show up.

This isn't the best solution, though. The diffuser takes away about 3 inches of height from the box and it is not possible to use it when taking a picture through the hole on the top of the box (where the reflection would most likely show up). This is why I didn't give the box 5 stars.

Overall, I am satisfied with this box. It is large enough for most of the products that I tend to take pictures of and it is easy to fold away for storage.

title: Super portable tripod with a tiny problem
text:
The MOMAX Compact Aluminum Tripod is super compact, moderately sturdy, and fairly light-weight and I really love it.

I have three kinds of tripods, all consumer grade, nothing professional. As seen in my pictures, I compare the size of all three types. Farthest to the right is the standard tripod that doesn't fold down all that much, the middle is the compact tripod with a ball head and quick release, and the MOMAX is the farthest left.

From the pictures, you can see how much more compact the MOMAX tripod is. What you can't see is that due to its compact size, the footprint when fully deployed is also much smaller. It expands to a height of 56 inches, which is about chin or head height, which is tall enough for most portraits.

The MOMAX tripod is super portable while not compromising on stability and sturdiness. Its folded size is only 10.3" long and 3" in diameter. Compare this to my previous solution, which was to use a monopod/selfie stick with a small tripod at the bottom, this tripod is so much better. Mounting my mirrorless camera on the MOMAX, I don't worry about the whole thing falling over.

The only tiny complaint I have about this tripod is its mounting head. It is a ball joint with a 1/4" thread at the top. It can't be removed easily to be replaced with a better solution and there is no quick-release option.

Each of my tripods serve a purpose but I foresee using the MOMAX most often because most of the time.

title: Be ready to reboot every day if using bluetooth.
text:
The only thing that separates this tablet from others in this price range is that it boasts LTE connectivity. Unfortunately, I do not have a sim to try with this tablet so I did not test it. Beyond this functionality, everything about this tablet is pretty much sub-par.

The screen resolution is barely HD. 1280x800 on a 10" screen means that the pixels are quite big and can be distracting. The audio quality is tinny and underpowered as one would expect and the cameras are nothing to write home about. The size and weight is fairly standard. It is about the thickness of an old cell phone such as an LG G5 and it is slightly heavier than a Samsung Tab A 10". I do need to say that the screen bezel isn't big.

The OS, on the other hand is pure Android with no extra bloat and to add to the good news, Netflix does run on this tablet (Neflix updated their app a while ago to stop running on "unknown" android devices). Most Android apps are expected to run on this tablet and for me, all apps that I wanted to use (comic book reader, plex, netflix, and youtube) run and I didn't feel any lag in using them.

The Achille's Heel of this device is its wireless drivers (which covers WIFI and Bluetooth). I use a bluetooth headset with this tablet and at least once per day, the drivers crash and is unrecoverable. An error is displayed every few minutes and only goes away with a reboot.

In the end, there are better choices out there.

title: Lexar has good quality, but also a timed expiration
text:
I've owned a few Lexar USB drives and Micro USB drives in the past and they have all had good quality and performance. I've attached the crystal diskmark performance below, but keep in mind that I am using the built-in microsd reader in my computer so speeds may vary as the reader has just as much to do with these benchmarks as the memory card itself.

I don't have any equipment that really stresses the microsd too much. The cameras that I have, while they can record up to 4K at 30fps, have generally had no problem writing to a U1 microsd. The Lexar, which I keep in my Osmo Pocket, is no exception, it has not had an issue recording video.

There is one key thing to point out about Lexar storage media that I've experienced in two of my past devices and that is the built-in expiration or time-bomb (if you don't agree with this philosophy). Lexar seems to have the philosophy that keeping your data intact is the most important when it comes to these products. Solid-state storage media has a theoretical limit to how many times they can be written to. Once that is hit, the media will be permanently damaged. Lexar has written into their firmware, a hard limit that once you write a certain number of times to their media, it will become read-only, keeping your data intact, but the storage unusable from that point on.

While I've experienced failed media in the past, I really only had this behavior with Lexar. I have to say, it did save my wife from losing the pictures on her phone if the card failed instead of becoming read-only.

title: The ball-joint is quite tight and the bubble level doesn't make sense.
text:
In the last few months, I collected a few tripods in various form factors and all of them supported the 1/4 inch quick release mechanism except for one. It was my main tripod, which had the traditional panning arm. It sported the square tripod mount.

I purchased the ZweiFuch Mini Ball Head to convert that tripod to the same quick release so that I can use my mirrorless with all of my tripods without changing plates.

What I found with the ZweiFuch was that it wasn't very convenient to use. The ball head is quite tight, which some may prefer, but I think it really should be able to be loosened more. The bubble level is placed to the side of the mount plate, facing vertically, meaning it is only useful for vertical pictures. There isn't a second bubble sitting flat on the face of the mount.

Of course, I expected this, but without a pan arm, it means that there is a small functionality loss to being able to quickly pan, then tighten it down again. It's just that added to the other problems I had with this ball head, I just don't think it's worth it.

title: A good product that's getting better
text:
I've been obsessed with fully wireless earbuds for years and have tried out at least a dozen different ones throughout.

I fully support some in the $30 range, I had a pair of old soundcores that worked great. I've also tried the more expensive Samsung Galaxy Buds (2018 version), which worked well enough. I've also tried some mid-range ear buds in the $70 range. Earbuds have gone through some growing pains with drop off issues between the left and right buds and battery life. In my experience, I believe the $30 buds are great value and >$100 buds are worth it only if they have good sound and good app support. For me every one of the $70 buds that I have purchased have broken down in less than three months, so I'd say stay away from those.

Now on to the review:
The Cleer Audio, Ally Plus II True Wireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds are in the >$100 range (although just barely) but in the last few weeks that I've used them, I truly believe they are worth their asking price. I will of course update this review if they break down in a few months.

There are so many wireless earbuds being produced these days, which most imitating the airbuds with their ugly stalks in one form or another, Cleer has gone with a tear-drop shape and capacitive controls that I appreciate. I purchased the tan-colored buds and they don't stand out like a pair of white or black buds would. There is only a single dim light on the earbuds to indicate charging status and they are the in-ear-canal style of earbuds.

Features:
- Light-weight.
- Charging/carrying case supports type-c connection as well as wireless charging. Interoperable with products designed for airbuds wireless charging.
- Long battery life. I listen to audiobooks and they have lasted for hours while I worked on chores around the house.
- Passthrough with good app support (more on it later)
- Active Noise cancellation
- Can be used as a single earbud without having to pair each separately
- Touch controls: Only tap, double tap, and triple tap are supported. Configurable through the app.

The App:
When I first received the Cleer earbuds, the app was unimpressive. There was a single slide bar that changed the balance between noise cancellation and passthrough, a equalizer with no presets (and no reset for that matter), and there was limited control over what the tap functions did.

Since then, the app has been updated and the earbuds had a firmware upgrade. While the app still has room for more improvement, they did separate the passthrough, normal, and noise cancellation modes into separate controls. Passthrough now has a slider to control the strength of the surrounding noise and the noise cancelling has a "smart noise cancel" mode. In addition, a new personalized audio feature was added. The app takes you through a hearing test and adjusts the sound to your hearing levels. Quite cool.

The limited controls over the touch function is still there and the barely passable equalizer is still there but I'm hoping that they will be improved in future updates.

title: Portable and easy to use.  Fairly limited.
text:
Taking it out of the box, you'd find that the LUXCEO light tube has good build quality. It is all-plastic, but that's much better than the fluorescent tubes of the past. The light is nicely sealed to be water proof and with a 1/4" screw hole on one end, it is easy to set up. A loop on the other end means this tube can be hung via a hook for additional mounting options.

In use, though, I realized that the Achilles heel of this product is in its lack of versatility. I agree with the other top reviews for this product that this light has limited functionality and the reason is because of its simplistic controls. While I normally prefer physical buttons that have specific uses rather than having to take out my phone to control something, the design of the remote control is such that there are only 8 colors to choose from (as seen from the picture). Without the ability to fine-tune the colors, you're really stuck. I think that unless you have a specific liking to the available colors, you'll end up using this as a white light for simply photography or video setups.

There is a single button on the light tube and its operation is as confusing as it is useless. Click on the button and it toggles on and off. Double clicking will cycle through various modes (R, G, B, white, yellow, flashing, etc). Hold the button and it will adjust the brightness.

To further confound the consumer, this light tube comes with a felt bag that fits the tube very well, but nothing else. Not even the remote control, meaning you'll need to find a solution for keeping the remote and tube together.

So in conclusion, this review is for the Luxceo P7RGB. Looking on Amazon, I see that there is Luxceo has a P7RGBPro that costs only $4 more which has a smartphone app to allow full control over the light's colors. It's fairly obvious which you should pick.

title: This is docking station for the RGB crowd, but what niche does it fill?
text:
The WD_Black 1TB D50 Game Dock has quality written all over it. Metal construction for heat dissipation, thunderbolt support, nice RGB lighting, and a fast NVMe drive. It is quite obviously geared toward the PC Gaming crowd, but which segment?

The build of this product screams high-quality gaming accessory. Its outer design is reminiscent of a cargo container and its collection of ports are impressive. Each USB port is well labeled with its speed (4x 10Gb/s Type-A and 2x 10Gb/s Type-C), two thunderbolt ports, one of which outputs 87 watts of power, one displayport, one network port (gigabit), and one 3.5mm headphone jack. Add to this, the 1TB high-performance NVMe drive. All in one sleek-looking, compact container (pun intended).

It is obvious that this dock is geared toward the Gaming Laptop crowd, whether its for gaming or for video/graphics production work, but I find that it really doesn't make sense for me. In my tests, this product does not work without the power adapter (it really should be able to power itself through the thunderbolt port). This means an additional outlet that's drawing power at all times. This would make sense if gaming laptops can actually be powered and charged from the 87w thunderbolt port but I have not seen a gaming pc with discreet graphics that actually accepts anything in that range.

So what other advantage would this product provide? External storage through a fast Thunderbolt connection. At $450, this product provides 1TB of additional storage. Which 2TB NVMe drives available for much less, I would opt to upgrade my internal storage to 2TB instead.

Then that leave the docking station. The ports are all of the high quality and your monitor, network, keyboard, mouse, headset, and speakers can be connected via a single thunderbolt connection. This is convenient, but I don't think this justifies the price as there are many docks out there that work just as well, albeit through a USB 3.1 connection instead.

WD has really done well to package a lot into this dock but is charging a premium for it. Personally, I think that there are just better ways of achieving equal or better results when it comes to upgrading a gaming laptop.

**update**
Coming back to think about it some more, I realized exactly what niche WD was going for: Macbooks. Some Macbooks have only two thunderbolt ports and all of them are not easily upgradeable so this product does indeed provide a value to those consumers. But then does it make sense to spend an additional 35% of the price of the laptop (Macbook Pro 13" is $1299) to address problems that Apple introduced into their laptops? I guess if you're already in their ecosystem, it's par for the course. That's not to say Apple is the only one. Microsoft has made their products impossible to upgrade as well, but none of these are actually gaming laptops.

title: Takes pixelated pictures but the printing part is fun
text:
No, I will not be reviewing camera specs, aperture, sensor size, etc. This is purely a toy camera that happens to print on thermal receipt paper.

As such, this camera does what it says. It takes pictures and can immediately print them out in black and white on receipt paper or stickers. For this purpose, the pixel count on this camera is enough. But what if you wanted to download the picture because it is actually worth keeping? That's when you'll discover that even pictures from the cheapest smartphone looks better.

Should one expect that the camera would be any good? No but you are expected to spend $100 for this device. The pictures really should be useable outside of printing on to receipt paper, right?

So the problem is with the price charged vs what you get. Camera technology has gotten much cheaper (the raspberry pi camera unit costs $20 and takes MUCH better pictures than this) and a thermal printer is not going to justify the price of this device.

With that said, if you can get over this aspect, this camera is a neat little toy that kids can have fun with around the house or with friends. As I said, just don't expect to be able to use the pictures for much else. What a shame it would be if the kid takes a very interesting picture but the resulting file is just unusable.

title: Simple camera with local storage.
text:
Yi is a brand that I know previously from their action cameras. They also dabbled in a mirrorless micro 4/3 camera as well so they know their camera tech.

The YIIOT 3MP HD Floodlight Camera is a lot like other wireless cameras that are on Amazon. The big difference here is that it is powered by the mains power, which I prefer. I replaced my regular floodlights with this camera. Just as with all other wifi cams, a separate app will be required. The setup is fairly straightforward. Go through the setup process and have the camera scan the barcode that was generated. From there, you're set.

This camera features high definition picture and local microsd storage. Notifications are customizable but mostly it is fairly standard.

There is ONE feature that sets this, and other Yi cameras apart, though. Install the Yiiot app through Alexa and you will be able to view the cameras if you have an Echo Show, FireTV, or Fire Tablet. Very nice.

title: Great companion to my Kamvas 13
text:
I'm no artist in any way but I do want to try getting into digital art. As a present to myself, I purchased the [[ASIN:B083W88L5H Huion Kamvas 13]] to get started. Huion is known for providing great quality in their products while keeping the prices affordable.

As anyone who has used a drawing tablet can attest, with the tablet taking up the main desk space, it's difficult to access the keyboard for all the shortcut keys that help to make the job easier. One option is to use an under-the-desk keyboard tray, but I really don't like doing that as I tend to kick the tray when I get in and out of my chair. Others purchase more expensive hotkey devices such as this one.

While the HUION Mini KeyDial KD100 does not have fancy led lights or e-ink display on the keys, it does have the basics of what one would need. The keys are laid out like the number pad on a full 101-key keyboard and the dial can be used to adjust anything that needs a kind of analog input (volume, zoom, brush size, etc). The keys are preconfigured for the most common shortcuts but each key can be customized.

The Mini KeyDial came in an oddly plain white box with the name Huion printed on top. It's almost like this is a rebranded white-box device but that really isn't a problem. It simply means that the unboxing experience isn't as satisfying as the drawing tablet itself. Once connected to the Huion drivers, the device feels fully integrated to Huion's ecosystem.

It is managed in the same driver/software that Huion uses for its tablets so that once you'll be able to get up and running customizing the buttons immediately.

Last thing to point out is that the dial on this device can support Microsoft's own RaDial drivers to emulate the dial that Microsoft introduced a few years ago for the Surface Studio, allowing it to interact natively with built-in Windows utilities.

title: All metal casing, tool-less construction
text:
Recently, I had two extra smaller-capacity nvme drives that I took out of my computers when I upgraded them. To turn them into portable drives that I can store my family pictures that I put in a safe, I purchased two different enclosures.

I found that the GMM M.2 NVMe SSD Enclosure Adapter was just a little bit faster of the two that I got. Both are all metal outside and both are tool-less assembly, but this one is just a little bit nicer. The drive attachment system is easy to use and easily secures the drive in place and the overall construction is just nicer.

This is the longer of the two enclosures that I got but the curved edges and grey color makes this enclosure stand out more.

title: Solid mesh router system with plenty of options in the firmware
text:
The NETGEAR Nighthawk Tri-Band Whole Home Mesh WiFi 6 System (MK83) is a great mesh router solution. It comes with three nodes (one base node and two satellites) that are paired with each other from the factory. At AX3600 speeds, this is the mid-range of the AX standard and is priced accordingly.

The mesh system supports ethernet backhaul (using an ethernet cable between the nodes), meaning that communications between the mesh nodes isn't taking place over wireless, slowing down overall performance.

As with any router, quality of the firmware is key. I found that all of the basic features are there: QOS, Dynamic DNS, UPNP, and various security settings like blocking internet access per device. Guest wifi network is also available.

I found that my wifi has been quite stable with this Nighthawk mesh system. I've not needed to reboot the router periodically as I'm sure many of us have experienced before. This means that when I have problems with a webpage or video stream, my immediate thought isn't to blame the router.

There is one feature with this router's firmware that is quite important to me. Under "Advanced Setup > Customize Wifi Network", IT IS POSSIBLE TO SEPARATE THE 2.4Ghz and 5Ghz WIFI NETWORKS with different names. This feature is sorely missing from all mesh systems that I have used. This is important because it gives you control over exactly which devices connect to the 5Ghz channel. While in the ideal world, devices would take care of connecting to the best possible network, that simply isn't how it really is. Too many devices have bad drivers that choose the first channel it sees and sometimes it chooses the 2.4Ghz. The worst offender is my Surface Pro 2, which ALWAYS chooses 2.4 over 5. With such an old device, good luck trying to get Microsoft to release a good driver for it.

title: A good drive with okay performance.
text:
While I posted a diskmark, it really is for consideration with the caveat that any benchmark really depends on many factors. I have this drive in a USB 3.1 enclosure and so the performance you see depends not only the drive itself but the enclosure as well. The speed of the PC's USB port and the drivers involved also play a role in these numbers.

What I can say is that I recently got a 256 Pioneer NVMe and with all other factors the same (same enclosure, same PC, same ports and drivers), the Pioneer did score a little bit better than this drive.

With all of that said, my opinion regarding this drive is that it may not be the centerpiece of a gaming rig build (which would probably call for a bigger capacity drive anyway), it is certainly a solid piece of kit that will perform better than a traditional drive.

At 512 gb, I'm using it to store some coding projects using the external enclosure so that all of it is portable. I also run a lot of portable apps from this drive and they all perform well. I have no complaints about this.

As with any other drive, spinning or otherwise, it is important to backup your projects to multiple locations so that any failure of the drive would not be catastrophic. I have no reason to suspect that this drive will fail on me any time soon, though. It doesn't run especially hot or anything.

title: Good quality and great-looking canvas backpack
text:
With school starting in-person instructions after the pandemic, it's time to start looking for school supplies again.

The Modoker Vintage Rucksack Backpack is a great-looking backpack with a drawstring top and flap cover that closes by magnet. The material is of good quality and is soft to the touch. There are plenty of pockets on the outside for all the school supplies and the inside has a laptop/tablet pocket with a fastening strap. The USB charging is just a bonus on top of a good backpack that should last.

title: Basic LED lights that are exactly what you'd expect.
text:
The Heorryn 180 LED Video Light Photography Studio LED Lighting Kit is a comparatively low-priced video lighting set is easy to set up with the included tripods. It has controls for brightness but no light temperature adjustment.

Unfortunately, I was in the same situation as others who have reviewed this product. In the box, I only received a white cloth diffuser and not the colored diffusers that the description described. The reason I still gave these lights 4-stars despite this is because I contacted the seller and they offered to send me a replacement unit to make it right. I put a lot of stock in sellers who are willing to correct any problems that buyers face.

With the diffuser on, the lighting is even and bright. I mostly use them to light the background rather than the subject. Combine this with a ring light and I have a very rudimentary lighting setup. I plan to purchase color transparency film in lieu of the missing colored cloths until the replacement unit arrives.

title: Easy solution to solve your airflow problems
text:
Easy solution for better air flow. I primarily purchase smaller nuc style computers around the house. They usually have a small fan with minimal air flow. When my computer started to throttle due to heat, I purchased these fans to help cool it down.

The fans are fairly quiet and have good flow. The rubber footing help to reduce vibration. No need to think about how to plug the fan into the motherboard and how to adjust it's speed. It's plug and power on. That's it

title: Works with Ring Doorbell 2!
text:
I hate to change the battery for the Ring Doorbell. It's one of the reasons that I didn't purchase those "stick up" cameras to put up around the house. I am not interested in having to change batteries every month. With that in mind, I set out to find a solar panel that works with my Ring Doorbell 2.

Looking at other listings, I saw that the ones that claim to work with Ring generate 5v, 3amps. I confirmed that this board also generates 5v, 3a (check my pictures) and took the chance to cut off the microusb connector that it came with.

What was exposed were two wires; red and black so there was no guess work necessary to figure out which wires would be positive and ground (usb usually has 4 wires). After stripping the wires, I screwed the wires to the back of the doorbell and crossed my fingers.

From my pictures, you'll see that the Ring app recognized the solar panel and also charged from 46% to 55% after one day in the sun.

Note: The wire is a little bit short so it may not reach your roof. I was able to get around this by soldering a longer wire from an old cell phone car charger.

title: Affordable SSD that works well as an OS drive
text:
What can a 256gb drive be used for? If one wishes to have storage space, we're talking in Terabytes, not Giga. For portable storage, a micro-sd card or usb pen drive has just as much storage for about the same price. So what niche does a 256gb, M.2 drive fit in?

There are two possibilities that I can think of:
1. A live-usb linux distro install. When combined with a USB 3.1 enclosure, this drive can be used to boot a PC into a linux operating system without affecting the internal drive of the computer. This can be useful for troubleshooting or simply testing out various distros. A drive like this would perform much better than a micro-sd or usb-pen drive.
2. Used as an internal OS drive for a computer. Even with Windows' requirements for space, a 256GB NVME drive will perform better than a traditional Sata drive, meaning faster boot up and faster app launching. It is always good practice to keep your data and OS separate, so for your pictures, videos, and other large files, put them on a separate drive, but use this drive to install your operating system on. This gives you the freedom to refresh your system without fear of losing data.

Specific to this Pioneer 256GB NVMe PCIe M.2 2280 Gen 3x4 Internal Solid State Drive, I currently have it in an external enclosure and am testing Windows 11 (which is only in Insider Preview at the time of this writing). I ran a crystal disk mark against it and posted the picture. I'm happy with this drive and how well Windows runs on it, even through USB.

title: A complete green screen setup for $40
text:
The Jebutu Green Blue Backdrop with Stand Kit 5 x 6.5 Ft is a complete kit to set up a green screen for game streaming or video special effects. Many other kits sell the scaffolding and the cloth separately or if they are sold together, are more expensive. With the Jebutu kit, one can set up a green/blue screen quickly and easily.

I was concerned about the single-tripod configuration of this setup but the stand works fairly well and is not flimsy. It will not be as stable as a full scaffolding but works well enough for my uses.

title: So this is WIFI 6
text:
The rise of home automation devices means that many of us have a lot more devices that connect to our wifi networks. While most of those devices use the 2.4Ghz frequency while devices like phones, tablets, and firetv use 5Ghz to stay out of each other's way, it still means that there are so many more devices to manage in a network and all of them are attempting to talk on the network. Not to mention interference from neighbors and their many devices.

This drives the need for beefy routers with faster CPUs to manage all of the chatter and radios that allow many more simultaneously connected devices.

The NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-band Mesh System (SXK80) attempts to address these needs. Sporting the latest wireless Wifi 6 technology, most of the basic features that a router needs (QoS, DDNS, VPN), and 60+ device support, the SKX80 holds a lot of promise.

Unlike one of the upvoted reviews, I don't have a different AX system to compare this to so for me, this mesh router performs admirably. It is fast and has good coverage. In my time so far, I haven't had any dropped connections. Videos stream well and web browsing works fine. I don't normally do voice or video calls while walking around the house, but watching videos while walking seem to work well. My device will jump from router to satellite correctly and there is no disruption to the video playback.

title: Good cooler with cool LED settings
text:
The AUTENS RGB Laptop Cooling Pad has all the bling of RGB lighting, digital readout, and six cooling fans. It is USB powered and has variable height adjustments for the legs.

It will serve well-enough as a cooler but there are many coolers out there so what might set it apart for a consumer? The honeycomb design and the RGB might be a big factor in one's decision. The buttons on the cooler control the LED light modes (I counted at least 8, plus hold the button to turn off). The power button will power on/off by holding it, but tapping the button while the cooler is on will toggle the number of fans that are turned on. The plus and minus buttons control fan speed. Unfortunately, there are only three speeds available but combine that with the ability to turn some fans off, one can achieve many levels of cooling. For me, it would be all on at full blast because I use my laptop for gaming or video editing.

Overall, great product that should help to keep the GPU temperature low for max performance.

title: This is not a gaming PC by any means but the Ryzen 5 APU packs a punch!
text:
The X300 Mini PC AMD Ryzen 5 3400GE would be the fourth Minisforum pc that I got over the past two years. They are a brand that I've really been keeping an eye on. Minisforum makes small form-factor pcs using the latest Intel and AMD mobile cpu's. Their computers are geared toward daily homework or office work use without taking up too much space. Most of them are VESA mountable.

The X300 is one of the bigger computers that I've seen from Minisforum. The entire chassis is metal and is well-ventilated. Whereas my previous compact PC's use laptop cooler fans, the X300 has a low-profile fan with 3-inch blades. During normal operation, the fan is very quiet.

I was surprised when I successfully booted up Biomutant, a 2021 game, and was able to play it at 1080p at a good framerate (sorry, I didn't turn on the FPS indicator...) at medium quality. Intel i5's would've had no hope of doing this without an additional graphics card (although, admittedly, I haven't had a chance to test the new Intel processors with their Xe graphics built in).

My son is learning to program games with Unity and Godot engines but had be previously unable to follow tutorials for 3D games due to the hardware limitations but with this PC, he will be able to expand into 3D.

title: 5amp total to share between 5 USB ports
text:
This is a fairly standard surge protector with 12 outlets with only two of those set apart for the larger adapters. The selling point that it attempts to sell consumers on is the usb ports, including one type-c so this review will concentrate mostly on those ports.

As far as the surge protector portion of this product, the face outward, which means that the longer style chargers that comes with some electronics will not plug in without taking up an extra socket. With only two set farther apart for power adapters, this power strip will not work well for a location with routers, modem, and NAS.

Now on to the USB ports. Five USB ports share a total of Five amps. It means that is the power strip is completely filled, it will only deliver one amp to each port. The type-c port is only useful if that is the only cable you can find because it does not support any fancy features such as quick charging or type-c pd, although it does support up to 3A so some phones may actually consider this "fast charging". Do not expect to replace a true 5-port usb charger with this power strip.

title: Still running an unstable OpenWRT release
text:
I needed a router that was confirmed to run Openwrt so I jumped on the opportunity to test the Cudy WiFi 6 Router AX1800 Smart WiFi Router.

At AX1800, this router really isn't much of an upgrade from the AC1750 Archer C7 that I had previously so in terms of WIFI performance, it wasn't much of an upgrade despite it being Wifi 6.

For me, the important factor here is the Openwrt firmware. The default firmware that is installed on the X6 router seems to be a custom skin for LUCI (verified by the URL of /cgi-bin/luci in the browser), but many features are missing in the UI, including the ability to enable ssh, so one of my first actions was to download the Openwrt Firmware from Cudy's website. The following is what I found:

Using the Archer C7 as my main router, I was able to put together a WIFI mesh with fast switching with Openwrt's 802.11r and 802.11s support. I was hoping that I can extend that mesh with the Cudy X6. What I discovered of the Openwrt firmware is that it is a custom compile of the 20.2 branch and therefore, not quite a stable release. After installing the wpad packages to allow 802.11s and WPA3, the wireless drivers didn't work correctly. Without going into too much detail, I believe that the drivers for the Wifi 6 adapter needs some work.

Hopefully, Cudy continues to work on the firmware and incorporate their changes into the official Openwrt repo. Once these problems are ironed out, it be a good replacement for the Archer C7 but even then, don't expect AX1800 to be a revolutionary step up from your current 802.11a wifi. This is the lowest Wifi 6 level that one can purchase.

title: Compact mic with included wind blocking fur cover
text:
The Mcoplus VM-M03 Metal Shotgun Video Microphone is the next step in my attempt to address sound quality issues in my videos. While a lavalier is good for a vlogging situation, it's not great for getting on location sounds.

I'm not a professional videographer or anything so I've included pictures of the frequency response charts from the microphone's instruction manual. In my specific case, the quality of this microphone vs the built-in mic of my phone or mirrorless camera is that it seems to pick up a little less of the unwanted ambient noise, but the biggest difference for me is of course, the wind noise reduction afforded by the fur cover.

This microphone is an affordable upgrade to the built-in mics of my equipment and fits my needs well. I can't say that my recommendation should be taken by anyone who actually does videography professionally.

title: A photo box that works...  I guess
text:
Photoboxes are simple things; It is usually just 5-sided box with some sort of backdrop and a strip of LED. The Heysliy Light Box Photography lightbox is just that and nothing more. Designed to be portable, the box can be folded flat and comes with a carrying bag that nicely stores everything in the kit.

Unfortunately, it's the execution of the thing that is to be desired. The box is cut from a sheet of translucent plastic then folded to form a box. The flaps are joined by a barely-tight-enough screw cap that can be easily lost because it is not actually part of the box. The plastic itself is stuff, but has an elastic memory, which means that it wants to fold back to its storage position, weakening the sides of the box unless the flaps are folded outward first. Overall, the structure is quite flimsy and can be tricky to set up.

The Heysliy lightbox comes with four backdrops made of that paper-like material that is used by some reuseable grocery bags. The colors are black, white, green, and red. The backdrop is hung by a hole cut into the material and a tab that's cut into the plastic box. Any hard tug will rip that backdrop so be careful.

So the conclusion is that the box is annoying to set up and with the LED's mounted on the inside of the box, reflections will be a big issue with this box as can be seen in my pictures (nintendo switch pictured for size reference).

title: Smart watch...  simplified to the essentials
text:
The Skagen Men's Hybrid HR Jorn Smartwatch is an elegant watch first and smart watch second. It is considered a hybrid because it is a watch first. Even with almost no battery life left, it still serves as a traditional watch with a stylish, all metal body and actual watch hands with glow-in-the-dark inserts for visibility without a front-light. In terms of thickness, unfortunately, this watch isn't any thinner than other Android Wear watches I've used.

For the "smart" portion of the watch, the Skagen is equipped with an e-ink display, which means that once the watch face is drawn, no more power is drawn from the battery to keep that display. This means that the watch will last much longer than a regular, oled-display smart watch. It is easy to tell that this e-ink display is of high quality because it does not have the yellow hue that older e-ink displays had. It is quite similar in quality to the paper-white kindle.

Beyond the screen is the software. The Skagen watch pares down the smart functionalities to only what a user may actually need on a watch. No games, no maps, no speakerphone functionality. Instead, the watch will track your workouts, show you notifications, and control your music player. It really is everything I normally do on my Android Wear watch. There are many watch faces, and multiple complications for customization. One can even use a photo as the background for the watch face. I did find that any watch faces with numbers tend to crowd out the UI and there is very little room for complications.

For all of this, Skagen priced this watch about $100 less than other smart watches so it really is a good option for those who just want a wearable that gives them the essentials.

title: This is a USB 2.0 cable.  Good for charging and wired android auto only.
text:
When it comes to usb type-c cables, the fine print is everything. The consumer must be aware of the USB version it is compatible with and even more importantly, one must be aware of the wattage that the wire can handle if charging through it.

The Kraft USB-C to USB-C High Speed Data & PD Charging Cable is advertised as a charging cable capable of 100W Type-C pd. The Nintendo Switch accepts it as a charging cable just fine and my Samsung tab A has no issues charging through it.

Look more closely its packaging and take note that this cable only supports up to 480Mbps speeds. This means it's a USB 2.0 data cable. It will not carry a video signal and when transferring files, don't expect USB 3.0 performance.

The cable itself is nicely braided and not too stiff. It is flexible enough to easy coil and tie together for storage. The USB connectors are a little bit long, though. The connectors stick out of the phone 2 inches before you get to the braided cable part.

I gave this cable 4 stars because they did not claim falsely advertise the capabilities of this cable. "High Speed USB" is actually what USB 2.0 speeds are labeled. For anyone who was expecting more, please look more carefully at the specs before purchasing.
