title: Much more than an airpods knockoff
text:
[[VIDEOID:ccc625498e24d19dfedabac29060c0d1]] At first blush, the Baseus S2 Wireless Earbuds looks like the countless number of Airpod knockoffs out there... and how dare they charge 70 bucks for it?

I'm happy to report that beyond the shape of the earbuds, the Baseus S2 is a high-quality pair of earbuds that can hold its own against even Samsung earbuds. Over the years, I've used many, many wired and wireless earbuds but I've always kept my budget sub-100 dollars. Of all of them, the S2 is definitely the best so far.

From the nice metallic blue color, to the discreet capacitive touch buttons, these earbuds look great and the mic stalk isn't so long as to look odd in the ear. The case is sleek and comfortable to hold and provides a button to initiate the pairing function. Oh, and NO FLASHING LED LIGHT on the buds themselves. Overall, great build quality.

In terms of functionality, these earbuds do not have the annoyingly accented "pairing", "connected", etc. voice prompts. Just beeps to indicate its current mode, which I'll go into in a bit. The earbuds can of course be used together or independently. On long trips with my family, I like to keep one earpiece in, listening to my audiobook while still being able to stay up with the conversation in the car, then switch the earbuds when the battery runs low.

A nice quality of life function that is also an homage to airpods is that the earbuds will pause the audio if removed from the ear and resume when inserted.

While I normally don't read instruction manual, I needed to reference it to figure out the capacitive buttons. So here's what I found out:
-- Single tap: Left earbud for previous track and Right earbud for next track.
-- Double tap: pause/play (or just remove the bud from the ear).
-- triple tap: Google Assistant
-- Long press: Active noise cancellation function
-- simple beep: ANC and passthrough mode off
-- a slow rise base sound: DNC (passthrough mode) on
-- a slow lowering base sound: ANC on.
(the slow base sounds are like the movie sound effects when a scene goes from normal speed to slomo and back)

One feature that I had to actually search carefully to discover on the product description was that the case actually has wireless charging capability. They really should advertise that more.

The sound quality has a rich full tone. I did not feel like I was missing the bass or treble parts of the spectrum, but then I'm not one for heavy bass in the first place. The clarity is also very good.

Please enjoy my mini unboxing video.

title: This is a little bit too small
text:
This Foldable Photo Box Portable Studio Kit comes with 6 pieces of cardboard that have various colors on the front and back, totaling twelve total backdrop colors to choose from. The LED Ring light is built in to the box and has many levels of brightness. The top of the box has a flap that allows photographing a product from the top with the light shining directly on to the product. There is no color temperature or RGB adjustment which I believe is the right choice. Accurate representation of a products colors is key. It has really elevated my product photography game.

One problem I faced was that when I received this product, I was surprised at how small it is. For reference, I pictured a FireTv remote in my pictures to hopefully give an impression of scale. You'll see that the length of the remote has almost reached to each end of the box. It means that the side walls of the box will always show up in the product pictures. It takes some creative cropping to remove the walls. Otherwise, it is necessary to break out the rubber stamp tool in photoshop or gimp to paint over the walls so that the backdrop fills the image. Either way, post-process is a must when using this box.

I'm happy to have this product in my photography kit as I no longer need to worry about dim images and ugly backdrops.

title: A good-enough camera for the price
text:
The NexHT 1080P Pan Digital Tilt / 8X Zoom Indoor Smart Camera has all of the features that one would want from a wifi camera. Panning, recording, remote viewing, infrared night vision and two-way audio. It is also very small. Designed to look like the Wyze cam, it is actually much smaller at 1.5" wide and 3" tall. While cloud storage services are available, there is a microsd port for local recording.

If one just needs a basic camera at a low price to monitor the home, this camera will serve well. To compare to products such as Wyze, this camera comes up a little bit short. The title of the product is carefully worded to show that the tilt function is "digital", which really means that the camera records with a wide-angled lens and when the phone is held in landscape mode, one can drag the image up and down. When held in portrait mode, the entire height of the image can be seen and there is actually no tilt function. Even so, in both modes, the camera image is squeezed together and not at the correct aspect ratio (I guess this depends on your phone's aspect ratio because the programmers chose not to maintain aspect ratio of the picture).

The recording function is fairly basic. It works like a dashcam in that the camera is always recording and will loop back over itself once the storage is filled.

As with any other wifi home automation product, a separate account needs to be created to log in to the app -- an app one must trust to not send any sensitive information back to the mothership. Personally, I plug this camera into a smart switch that I can turn on only when I'm out so that at least the camera isn't on when I'm at home.

So this camera will do what it advertises but it there really isn't anything that sets it apart from the large number of products out there. Wyze, while being a little bit bigger, costs only $30 and has actual tilt function.

title: I'm really liking the Ulanzi brand
text:
When I purchased the [[ASIN:B08RRV6S6W Ulanzi battery handle]] to go with my DJI pocket, I was impressed with the quality of the product. When gathering together my camera gear for my vacation, I realized that I actually purchased a couple of other Ulanzi products previously. Since then, this brand has jumped out at me when looking for camera accessories.

This ULANZI MT-33 Camera Tripod had a convenience feature that I didn't realize it had when I ordered it. It is well thought out and has good build quality (with one minor caveat). It is a flexible tripod that is strong enough to hold my mirrorless Lumix camera and is equipped with a cold shoe socket as well as a 1/4" screw hole. The cold shoe can hold a microphone or small LED video light which the 1/4" screw hole can either mount another cold shoe or other camera accessories.

The convenience feature that I didn't know about is that the mounting head of this tripod can open up to become a phone holder. It's not a separate accessory that screws on to the quarter inch screw. The spring-loaded phone holder is actually part of the mounting head's design. What this means is that one can switch from taking pictures with a camera to filming with a cell phone without fumbling around with phone brackets.

In my pictures, you will see a screw with its tightening wheel. The screw is supposed to be securely seated in the wheel but it wasn't seated properly in the product I received and it came apart. It wasn't a big problem. Simply reassemble the screw and wheel back and then mount a camera to the tripod. By tightening the screw to the camera and keep turning. The tightening action will seat the screw back into the wheel and should not come out anymore.

I'm not a video blogger but it seems like I'm slowly collecting many accessories that make me think perhaps it's a shame for me not to be? I have the necessary tools for it... not everyone is made to be in front of the camera, I guess.

title: Just didn't work.
text:
I understand that the Type-C standard is tricky sometimes. Type-C chargers need to agree with the device on the correct voltage to use and the amperage of the charger must be enough to drive the device for power to actually be delivered successfully.

With that said, I purchased the F1TP DMW-DCC8 USB-C Power Adapter DC Coupler Set for my Panasonic Lumix GX-8. I tried this adapter on every Type-C charger I have, a cell phone charger, a powerbank, and one that's rated for the Nintendo Switch (enough for the console to switch to TV mode). None of them got the slightest reaction from this adapter.

I really wanted the flexibility of the Type-C connection for my Lumix camera, especially if I wanted to use is as a webcam through an HDMI capture card, but this one just didn't work out.

title: High quality, tool-less enclosure
text:
Everything about the RSHTECH Aluminum M.2 NVME NGFF SSD Enclosure is exactly what I wanted from an NVME enclosure. A USB Type-C 3.1, tool-less assembly, and mostly-metal enclosure that was easy to use, very convenient, and good transfer speeds.

RSHTECH also didn't cheap out. Included in the box are two cables: a Type-A to Type-C cable and a Type-C to Type-C cable.

In terms of design, I really like that the circuit board doesn't add a lot of unnecessary bulk to drive itself, the metal casing has holes on the side for air flow and that there is no annoyingly bright LED. The button that you press to open the case is actually translucent plastic with the LED light under it. It's all quite nice.

title: poor build quality
text:
I own the original Osmo Pocket and it can be controlled by WIFI through an adapter. With this clip, the camera can be clipped to a backpack to record a "first person view" type of video. It can then be monitored from a smart phone. With the built in gimbal, the video will be very smooth except for the "gimbal bob" (up and down movement when walking normal) that's unavoidable with this device. It frees up your hands while still capturing the video.

It is unfortunate that this device has pretty bad build quality. The included GoPro style screw adapter wasn't able to reach the hex nut. In trying to force the screw in, I stripped part of it. I had other gopro adapters lying around so I was able to find a replacement. Even when screwed in, the fit isn't very tight. The joint is loose and will move when walking around. There just isn't enough friction between the parts to make it stay where you set it.

title: Slim is the word that comes to mind.
text:
The design philosophy is slim. The keys are almost flush with the board and the mouse is fairly flat. This gives a sleek look to this keyboard and mouse combo. There is a minimal bezel around the keys and the grey and black esthetic makes this a good choice for a clean, minimalist look on a nicely organized desk.

The keys are full-sized with enough travel to provide good tactile feedback while typing. This is a full keyboard that includes the number pad. The mouse response is good feels comfortable in the hand and has storage for the 2.4ghz radio dongle, which is standard in most mice these days.

This combo is rechargeable via USB so there is no need to keep a fresh set of AAA or AA batteries on standby, but one must remember to charge them every once in a while.

This combo won't be picked up by a hardcore gamer but it is great for anyone who simply needs a good looking keyboard and mouse combo for their computer.

title: Zoom like a boss!
text:
Over the last year, I've tried various hdmi capture devices and this one is the lowest priced and best of them. The most common problem with capture cards are their drivers. Custom drivers either introduce too much lag or are simply unsupported by various software.

The PACOXI HDMI capture bypasses ALL of those driver problems by showing up as a simple USB webcam. Without the need to install any drivers, the built-in Windows 10 camera app immediately recognizes the device and shows the signal. OBS, of course, fully supports this product and VLC can open capture device successfully . Turn off buffering in OBS or VLC and you get near real-time performance.

I've tested this capture device with FireTV and Nintendo Switch and both worked well.

I've even connected this to my phone through a USB-A to USB-C connector. On Android, it is necessary to download a "usb camera" app, but I can say that with the right software, this device will work.

In the last week, I've been using this for my Zoom calls. Plugging in the HDMI output from my mirrorless camera, I used a shallow focus lens and got a great image with beautiful bokeh (blurry background) without the weird cutout effect that you'd normally get when zoom tries to do it for you. At 1080p, the image in zoom is simply flawless.

At this low price, I'm thinking about getting more than one so that OBS can cut between multiple cameras or inputs.

title: affordable second charger
text:
Yes, I still have a Surface Pro 3 and it's still working well with the latest Windows 10 updates. The Surface Pro 3's i5 CPU is still going strong.

So when my daughter needed a computer to bring to school, this was the computer I let her use. To reduce the hassle, I needed a second charger for her to keep in her bag.

So far, this charger works perfectly and even has an LED to show that it's connected. Happy with this purchase.

title: Responsive camera that will not need charging
text:
Placing a camera around the house, one faces the problem of how to provide power to the device. Traditional systems used BNC coaxial connectors but as video resolutions increased, POE (Power-Over-Ethernet) systems became popular. Both types of systems required pulling wires around the house. POE is still the best solution because they are secure and won't hog up your wifi bandwidth due to being wired.

When only one or two cameras are needed, wifi cameras (preferably solar powered ones) provide a great solution to the problem. This wireless solar camera has many good qualities going for it. It is compact, and completely self-contained. While it can be charged via USB, the built-in solar panel will do a good job charging the internal battery throughout the day.

It has night vision, but no infrared LED's to help light the scene. Still, the nightvision does a good job all by itself. Motion sensor is built in and will send alerts to the app. One great feature is that there is no monthly subscription necessary to get recordings due to its built-in microsd card slot. The app allows one to highlight a section of the recording to save to the phone. Combine all of this with its relatively low price, this is a very attractive security camera!

So what are the drawbacks? The overall execution of the camera is somewhat disappointing. There is a huge problem consumers are facing when it comes to building a smart home. One either has to:
1. Pay an exorbitant amount of money for branded devices that connects back to a company that one hopes is trustworthy and still be required to purchase a monthly plan to get all the features.
2. Spend less money on unknown brands, but have to deal with each device requiring a different app to operate, but more disturbingly, trusting ones home security to an unknown entity outside of ones country.

This camera relies on the Tuya or Smart Life app to operate. This app has really become the defacto standard for all low-cost or unbranded smart home devices. The company behind the app is based in China so please make your own decision regarding whether this is safe for you. The devices live on your wifi network and connects back to its home server and the app lives in your phone with requirements to access your storage and GPS location, also requiring a login that connects back to its home server.

Security concerns aside, there are three issues with the recording functionality of the camera. Firstly, the microsd slot only accepts cards up to 32gb. At 1080p quality, this means perhaps 240min of video storage. This leads to a potential issue which is the second point: the recording function is similar to a dash cam in that it is always recording. Video is recorded in a loop and old footage is overwritten when the card is filled. The constant writes to a microsd, of course shortens its lifespan, but even more importanly, a better execution would have been to take advantage of the motion sensor and cache 60 seconds of video in memory and write to the card when motion is detected. The last point regarding the recording function is that if the camera is turned off while the SD card is in the slot, it will NOT be detected when the device is turned back on. One must eject the card and reinsert it (while the camera is on) for recording to start again. Combine this with the overpowered spring in the SD Card slot and you'll be guaranteed to lose your memory card because if you do not insert the card successfully on the first try, it will be ejected a few feet away and you will spend your time looking through your bushes trying to find it again.

title: This kit has more than I actually need to clean my mirrorless camera, and that's good.
text:
What I really wanted from this kit were all of the dry materials: The air bulb, the lens brush, and the various lens tissues and cloths. I'm a little unsure about using the liquid products on my lenses, and especially my sensor because I just don't know what kind of residue it might leave. So my review is for my experiences using the dry products.

I had a project where I was filming a video using my mirrorless and this kit came in handy.
The lens brush is retractable and has a good build quality. It helps to loosen dust from the lens and sensor. Follow that up with a few puffs from the bulb and most of the larger pieces of dust are cleared. These two are generally enough for the inner parts of the lens. The outside facing lenses can do with an additional rubbing from the microfiber cloth.

In case of fingerprint smudges, the lens tissue helps to really buff away the print and lift off most of the finger oils.

Overall, this kit is worth it because purchasing a brush, bulb and lens tissues would not have been as worth it as this kit.

title: This is a GREAT travel plug for international and domestic trips
text:
I had a chance to bring this World Travel Plug Adapter on a short vacation over the weekend and it was everything I would want in a travel adapter.

After the popularity of USB charging for almost every device, I found that the days of bringing separate power adapters for every device are finally behind us. The three USB type-a ports on this adapter are a little bit weak. They share 2.1A (total 10.5 watts) among them, but it is perfect to power my travel router and charge my smartwatch. The Type-C port is a PD (power delivery) port that outputs 18W. That is enough to kick of quick charging on phones like the Google Pixel phones.

In addition, there are two US-style power sockets that I can then plug my 6-port USB charger into which can charge my phones, tablets, etc.

I love the fact that the power connectors are modular and can either be clipped right into the adapter or made longer through the included power cord. With the power connector removed, the adapter itself is completely flat and very easily packed. That is quite important.

Please be careful, though. The power plugs on this adapter does NOT translate 220V to 110V, meaning that the 3 prong socket on the front of this adapter will output 220V if it is plugged into a 220V mains wall socket. Please make sure your device can accept 220V input!

title: works well but light is a little underpowered
text:
First, I want to say that I verified this to be a 2K camera. I had some confusion because there was a discrepancy between the title and the description.

Webcams are pretty much a requirement in these days of Zoom meetings and school classes. This camera has great image clarity and quality. The light has 3 levels of brightness but is fairly useless due to how small the light actually is. It simply isn't big enough to light up my face.

The camera also has a microphone so it is completely possible to do a hands-free setup by having a speaker plugged into the computer.

Overall, it does what I need it for, but the light takes away from the aesthetics of the camera. It wouldn't be a problem if the light actually worked as I hoped it would but as it is, it simply makes the camera look bulkier than it needs to be.

title: Thank you to the other reviewers for the warnings
text:
Please listen to the other reviewers for this product when they tell you that this device is a fire hazard. With their warnings in mind, I took the chance and plugged it into my computer. Within 10 seconds, the onboard chip became too hot to touch. I immediately removed it and won't risk trying to flash anything with it.

Please be careful.

title: Good, but not great
text:
Edit: just over one month in, the right earbud stopped working.

There are many, many true wireless earbuds out there. What attracted me to these were the features that they boasted: Wireless Charging, Active Noise-Cancelling, and bluetooth 5.1. So how does these earbuds compare to some of the cheaper offerings and does it justify being twice as expensive as some of them?

In terms of price, these earbuds can be considered cheap. Comparable to the mid-tier brands out there such as Anker and MPow, and much, much cheaper than Bose and Jabra brands. Still, there are many that cost half the price.

With the pricing in mind, let's look at the good of these earbuds:
+ Long battery life -- I'm on my fourth hour of listening to an audiobook and the battery is still showing 50% on my phone.
+ Battery status reporting to phone -- I'm sure most of the recent bluetooth headphones and earbuds do this now, but it is still nice.
+ Type-C port for charging -- The move to type-c as the standard charging port for all devices is happening and I'm glad NANNIO didn't cheap out and use a micro-usb. One less cable to worry about.
+ No app necessary -- The passthrough and ANC features can be turned on by tapping the touch controls twice.
+ Google Assistant Support -- Tap three times and Google Assistant launches.
+ No ugly microphone stick -- The tear-drop shape of these buds look much better than the ugly sticks that Apple's products have, in my opinion.
+ Smooth transition between left-only, right-only, and stereo -- These earbuds allow one to choose to use only one earbud while keeping the other in the charger without having to pair the other piece separately. It's something that I take advantage of on long drives. I keep one bud in the ear to listen to my audiobook and switch out when the battery runs out.

The bad:
- Not low profile -- The Anker SoundCores is pretty inconspicuous in the ear, but these NANNIOs, being white and sticking out more are anything but low profile.
- ANC not very effective -- The ANC levels are adjusted to be pretty minimal on these buds so while it is possible to hear the difference between the feature being on and off, it is also noticeable that only the lowest hums are cancelled out. Earbuds simply aren't good for ANC. Buds simply don't fit perfectly in the ear canal and when the jaw moves, the fit shifts. By this fact, there is always sound leaking through, reducing the efficiency of any ANC system. In earbuds, ANC is really just a gimmick.
- Passthrough needs to have wind noise reduction -- The reason for passthrough, in my mind, is to be able to hear surrounding sounds if wearing earbuds while running. It uses the microphone on the earbuds to pass external sounds through, but when running, there will always be wind noise. Without wind noise reduction, it makes this feature useless. I don't know of any earbuds that have addressed this issue.

So why did I still give these buds 5-stars? Because it is priced perfectly for what it is and what it promises. It has more features and quality that makes it better than the lower $30 dollar earbuds, but isn't a brand that can demand over $100. The features that are promised are delivered and any shortcomings are expected, as described above. With these buds, I get

title: Great price, great quality, but c'mon...  custom cable?
text:
First, I want to say that Huion's pen technology is probably as good as XP Pen and Wacom (from all of the reviews that I've seen) and it is well-build with quality all over the device. The matte screen protector helps to give the stylus more friction to replicate the feel of drawing on paper and the type-c interface means that one cable serves as the power, video, and digitizer (pen input) cable. The price is also great.

I do have a couple of gripes about it, though. First, this screen does not support touch input -- only pen. I understand that Wacom and XP Pen also don't have this feature, but it really should be included these days (perhaps next year's model?). With touch, it makes zooming, panning, and rotating the canvas second nature to users. Instead, it is necessary to customize these functions either in the buttons on the side or the pen... or to have one hand on the keyboard.

My second gripe is that the USB Type-C port on the screen is intentionally set deeply in an undersized hole so that you are forced to purchase a custom cable from them. It defies understanding. I know that not all cables work for video signals, but to use this method to stop users from using cables they know will work tells me that perhaps their circuitry doesn't have the protections against incompatible cables? I ended up buying a cheap cable that I was able to remove the outer rubber on and replace with a heat shrink wrapper instead of paying $30 for their custom one.

I'm otherwise happy with my purchase. Thanks for reading!

title: Well built stand that's very portable.
text:
Originally, I got this stand to lift up my work laptop for extra cooling and better ergonomics and it works pretty well for that. The Dell Inspiron is a 17" laptop and I was somewhat worried about whether the stand will be wide enough for the laptop to balance well. I was happy to find that it did.

I did find that because the front of the laptop has a rounded edge at the bottom-front, it slips a little bit because the front lip of the stand isn't very high.

I found an additional use for this stand that I didn't even know that I wanted. I have a Huion Kamvas 13 drawing tablet that comes with a fairly big stand. While I recently got a bag that fits that stand, the portability of this stand works even better for it.

title: A little oversized, but works well for my purposes
text:
I got the 15" - 15.5" size sleeve to safely store and carry my Huion Kamvas 13. It is a 13" screen, but I was concerned that a normal sleeve for a 13" laptop wouldn't work because the Kamvas 13 has a set of buttons on its side and a fairly thick bezel under the glass.

When I received the sleeve, I was happy to find that not only did it fit the Kamvas 13 well, the front pocket was also large enough to carry the stand that I purchased along with the drawing tablet along with its USB Type-C cable.

It was quite large so I compared it to my Dell Inspiron 17" laptop and it actually fit the laptop so I'd say that this bag might be a little oversized for a 15".

In terms of quality, I like the dark grey fabric and the plastic zippers, which feel fairly hefty. The padding isn't very thick but should be good to protect against scratches and bumps, but not enough for even short drops.

I'm giving this 5 stars because it is everything I wanted: Stylish, protective, and fits well.

title: Honestly, VGA?
text:
This usb type-c dock is very, very nice, but it isn't quite perfect.

First, a clarification for those who aren't versed on USB Type-C ports: There is a wide range of features that a Type-C port will support -- it's all up to the manufacturer. Just because you have a Type-C port, it doesn't mean you will be able to use all of the features that this dock provides. Unfortunately, you will need to dig into the online documentation or forums for your device to find out what you will actually get.

Windows PC -- Almost all Windows PC's will be able to use the SD/MicroSD reader, the Ethernet port, and the additional USB 3.0 and USB 2.0 ports. On my minisforum u700, this dock provides two HDMI ports and I didn't bother testing the VGA port. So on my PC and my laptop, I'm able to take full advantage of this hub.

LG V40 -- I'm on the T-Mobile service running their Android 10 rom. In this ROM, LG provided a little-know desktop mode similar to Samsung Dex that makes the phone work almost as well as a desktop PC. In this mode, the phone takes advantage of the SD/MicroSD card reader to transfer pictures and files, connect to your network through the ethernet port, and provide a large-screen experience through the HDMI port. Connect a mouse and keyboard and you have a great desktop experience. Plex and Netflix works extremely well in this mode.

Nintendo Switch support -- NO

My gripes about this dock: Being an 11-in-1 dock, this really should have a 3.5mm headphone jack, instead, they provided a VGA port. If your computer has a type-c port, would you really NOT have an HDMI monitor/tv to plug it in? Also, the lack of support for Switch means that I'd still need a separate Switch dock when travelling instead of having one dock that supports all of my devices.

title: This is such a good device for my kids but...
text:
The Huion H320M was exactly what I was looking for. When helping my kids with their Math homework, I found that we were wasting a lot of scrap paper so I began to look into purchasing the boogie board. I came across this Huion device that has a boogie board on one side and a pen digitizer on the other. Plus, the pen included is the 8192 level sensitivity pen that the higher-end huion devices come with.

For about a month, this worked great! My kids used it while doing their Math homework, my son used it during his class on during the pandemic, and I tried my hand at digital drawing.

After that first month, the boogie board began to show shadowing -- older scribbles in the bottom right corner were unable to be cleared. They would fade, but they wouldn't fully go away. The top left corner is still clearing fine. The pen digitzer side is still working well, though. In fact, the quality of the pen digitizer is great! The pen even has tilt sensitivity. Something that needs to be purchased separately on Wacom tablets (at least previously...)

I like Huion as a company as they are providing low-priced digital art tablets as compared to the prices of Wacom and even XP-Pen, but I was a little disappointed that 1/2 of my device's functionality is compromised. I had to take one star off for it.

title: Very nice.  Keep an eye on products from this company.
text:
[[VIDEOID:eca274f4b2284645b4d421ae2a0a300d]] Minis Forum has come out of nowhere to be one of my favorite PC manufacturers. When my kids needed computers for homework, I purchased the Minis Forum that ran on Intel Celeron for around $250 each. When I started looking for a more powerful machine to do some simple video editing and coding, I chose Minis Forum again.

Minis Forum has a line of small form-factor PCs that are well ventilated and comes fully loaded and ready to go.

In particular, this Core i5 pc includes an i5 cpu with an Intel Iris Graphics 6100. It comes with everything you need to get started. I chose the 256gb ssd with 8gb ram. There is an additional memory slot to upgrade the ram and the SSD can be upgraded as it is connected via the m.2 slot. There is also space to install a 2.5in laptop sata hdd or SSD.

Windows 10 pro is already installed and activated. This is very nice because they didn’t cheap out and provide the Windows 10 Home edition. The pro has more options for sharing folders on the network as well as the ability to be a remote desktop host. Good for running as a headless server.

The Intel graphics is powerful enough to perform multiple hardware transcoding streams, as shown in my video, so this mini pc can be easily set up as a capable plex server with some external USB drives attached through its USB 3.0 ports.

Overall, the computer has been stable and is very small. I’ll be keeping an eye on Minis Forum products in the future.

Please check out my pictures to see some internals for this computer.

title: A beautiful-looking travel tripod to replace my entry-level one.
text:
Years ago, not knowing what I was looking for, I purchased the [[ASIN:B017IS057O Albott 70 inch tripod]]. It was a good entry-level tripod that is quite traditional with it's pan-and-tilt head and quick release lock. As I started to build out my video and photo equipment (I'm still a total novice), I've found that I needed a tripod that was more compact and sturdy.

This K&F Concept TM2515M1 tripod is certainly not professional level, but it is a good travel tripod. With a ball joint, and a screw-lock plate, I found that it is more versatile than the Albott tripod. With the orange highlights, it is also much better looking.

I've included a few pictures comparing the two tripods. As you can see, with the K&F tripod, I do not compromise on any of the features of the other tripod while gaining a more compact and sturdy frame. The build quality of the K&F is great. All parts are metal and the tripod legs are tightly screwed, giving it a very secure feel.

From the pictures, you can see that compared to the traditional tripod, the head is smaller and easier to pack away, without that long handle to get in the way. The maximum height is comparable to my old tripod, but when packed away, the K&F is much smaller. The carrying case is also more rugged. It has a heavy-grade nylon and the zipper is nice and big. What I'm losing compared to the traditional tripod is the monopod height but I'm not a tall guy, so I would never use the mono fully extended anyway.

The K&F has the upside-down feature that is common among tripods of this kind. It allows one to shoot videos and pictures from a much lower angle without risking the safety of the camera. I can imagine a low-to-the-ground timelapse on the bank of a river looking at boats on the river.

Form really follows function on this one. The orange highlights accentuate all the joint locations and the all round design gives this tripod just a sleek look overall.

I'm quite satisfied with my purchase and the sub-100 dollar price that was exactly what I was looking for.

title: Very good value for Active Noise Cancelling headphones.
text:
I don't know how it happens but I somehow ended up buying over 20 pairs of bluetooth headphones over the course of my life. I'm also finding that I can't pass up a good pair of bluetooth headphones.

So of the over-head style bluetooth headphones, I've run across problems with short battery life (had one pair that lasts only 3 hours), too tight against the head, presses on the ear (supra-aural) and gets sweaty, active noise cancelling that can't turn on independently of the bluetooth function, and no carrying case.

This pair of RCA Active noise cancelling headphones don't have any of those problems. I sit at my desk all day with an air outlet behind me that is constantly blowing. I'm able to use them the entire day with music playing without the batteries running down. I don't keep the noise cancelling on the entire time but when I do, the fan noise is completely blocked out. Being circumaural headphones, the ear cups completely surround my ears and do not press on them. In addition, the spring isn't too tight to make me feel like my head is being squeezed in a vice.

As far as sound quality, because the speakers are not pressing against the ear, the sound seems to have a wider-room feel, making me feel even more like I don't have headphones on.

Overall, I'm quite satisfied with this purchase and don't feel the need to splurge and buy the much more expensive Sony and Bose products.

title: I really wanted this to work for me...
text:
While this dolly is useful for rotating the camera around an object, I also saw this product as an option for cases where I did not wish to bring the slider track with me. I'd be able to have the dolly on a ledge and get panning shots for b-rolls.

Unfortunately, a couple of things made it a bad fit for me:
-- Difficult to place object in the center. Being that the dolly is not on track, it was difficult to get the dolly to rotate around the subject. When I placed the dolly far enough away from the subject to fit it all in the frame, I found that the subject would eventually become off-center or go completely off frame because it wasn't perfectly in the center. I ended up having to tighten the turning radius and place the camera fairly close to the subject to shoot a complete 360 pan successfully. This would be the same complaint I'd have about any other dolly that's not on a track, I would imagine.

-- Lowest speed too slow for the timelapse I wanted. I have a plant whose leaves close at sun down and open again at dawn. I wanted to get a timelapse of this while the camera did a 360 pan. I estimated the leaves to close over a period of 3 hours so I set up my timelapse. The end result was that the dolly ran out of battery power at around 2 hours and 30 minutes and the resulting video was one where the plant moved slowly but the camera panned too quickly.

-- Tricky balance. Being three-wheeled, it was a little tricky to balance the dolly with my mirrorless camera. It actually tipped over while I was trying to set it up, dilocating part of the lens. Fortunately, I was able to pop the lens back together without any real damage.

title: I really wanted this to work for me...
text:
There are so many good things about GripGear's Movie Maker 2 Set that I just had to take the plunge and purchase it despite some of the problems identified by various youtube reviews. Unfortunately, I have to agree with many of their points and eventually, had to admit that some are showstoppers for me.

First, I want to state what is good about the Movie Maker 2 Set:
-- Low cost, comparatively. While there are other sliders that are in the same price range, those don't have the same versatility and portability. The motor can be used by itself to get 360 panorama shots and the track can be broken down and easily fit in a backpack. Additional lengths of track can also be purchased separately at a low cost. No other product on Amazon does all of this and would require separate purchases.
-- Remote control. While we expect remotes for almost everything electronics these days, I was surprised by the fact that many sliders/panorama motors do not come with one.
-- Versatility. Already mentioned previously, but I really want to emphasize that this is a unique feature of this product. In addition to the points already listed, the Movie Maker 2 set can also be used vertically

Negatives:
-- Top speed too slow: I'm in agreement with many youtube reviews that the highest speed is still not fast enough for some shots. This is why you will see many videos shot with this movie maker set sped up, making all of the videos look like timelapses.
-- Lowest speed too fast: When doing actual timelapse over two or three hours, the resulting video pans too fast. So while your timelapse subject is moving at the right speed, the camera movement is just too fast, making it uncomfortable to watch.

-- Weak 1/4" camera mount. The motor is made very specifically for the camera mount that was included with the set. Unfortunately, if your camera is not balanced or front heavy, it is difficult to get the tilt head to stay put without some grunt work turning the tightening screw.

I'm not a professional cinematographer so I thought my requirements would not be very strict, but not being able to get the shots I wanted due to the speed limitations makes me feel like this set is ALMOST what I wanted but it's just not there yet. I hope that the manufacturer can improve this product a little more and bring it across the finish line.

title: perhaps good for rear projection?
text:
I purchased this projection screen to improve the image quality for my portable projector over the bare wall that I was using currently. Unfortunately, I had to return it because it did not do what I needed.

This projection screen is made of a translucent, white fabric that is quite stretchy, which are both bad properties to have for a front-projection screen. Most people will be mounting their projection screen against a wall so being a translucent fabric, much of the projected light passes through the screen and hits the wall, then reflect back on to the screen. The net effect of this is that there is a fuzzy glow around everything in the image. Furthermore, being a stretchy fabric, you will end up with ugly curved edges in an effort to mount the screen tightly in order to remove any creases.

What you end up with on your wall is something that looks like you skinned a polar bear and a projected image that is akin to looking through a thick layer of fog.

I would not recommend this projection screen for anything other than a temporary screen that you might put up because there isn't a flat wall near by (camping?)

title: Surprisingly good.
text:
[[VIDEOID:2e7c0a6adbe4e28b15ec850150bf83ab]] Please check out the pictures that I provided for size and picture quality comparison between the TOUMEI Mini Projector and the [[ASIN:B008BUQ16S Vivitek Qumi Q5]].

**If you read through the entire review, I hope that I can provide some information that may help you get the most out of this projector.

THE REVIEW
I already owned a QUMI Q5, which was $500 when it came out and I really like the projector but I found that I did not take it with me very often when I travel because while the projector is small, it did not have built in battery and could not be powered by USB, requiring me to bring a power adapter. It also did not have Android so I had to bring a separate device such as a laptop or firetv. What this meant was that I ended up having to take up a lot of space in my bag for all the accessories necessary just to make the QUMI work.

The TOUMEI solves both problems for me. It has a built-in battery that should run for a couple of hours and can be charged using a USB charger (which I would bring with me anyway). Just remember that you need a charger with a high amperage (2.1A at least). With the built in Android, don't need to bring an additional media device. All I need to pack is the projector and its remote control. With the HDMI port, I still have the option to connect a laptop or FireTV to the projector (see caveats)

As you can see in my pictures and video, the TOUMEI looks just as good, if not better, than the QUMI when projecting a 30" picture. Fun fact: The TOUMEI was running on battery power when I was filming my comparison video. Projection brightness isn't lowered because it is running on battery power.

So for my use, the TOUMEI deserves its 5-Stars. I also want to give props to TOUMEI for updating the projector from Android 4 to Android 7.1.2. That's a 3-version jump! With that said, the projector is not perfect.

CAVEATS:
- Netflix not supported (See tips for workarounds)
- In HDMI mode, there are no keystone controls and auto-keystone doesn't work. This means you are forced to front-project and the projector must be level to the screen. I wrote an email to TOUMEI support and they were quite responsive. Unfortunately, they do not have a solution for this.
- Bluetooth mouse doesn't work very well. I've tried two bluetooth mice with the project but the pointer jumps around the screen, making it hard to use. Using a logitech usb mouse/keyboard worked well and mouse movement was smooth.

TIPS:
- Streaming apps: There is a builtin app called freeclick. From there, you can install a version of Amazon Videos and Youtube that works with remote control navigation. You can also install Netflix from there, but it is a very old version that was designed for touch/mouse input (see Netflix tip).
- Better UI: I was able to install "Leanback Launcher for Fire TV" (search google and click on the xda-developers link). Leanback is the codename for the launcher that is built in to Android TV. It is a more modern-looking launcher than what the projector came with. Also install "TV App Drawer" from the Play Store to show all apps that the Leanback Launcher hides.

- Better UI Alternative: I also tried out ATV Launcher from the Play Store and that is a launcher that looks just like the Leanback launcher but has more options but some are locked unless you purchase the PRO version.

NETFLIX:
The newer versions of the Netflix app no longer support any Android boxes that aren't on their "white list" so only version 4 or earlier work (Netflix is at version 7 as of this writing). So while the Netflix that is included with the projector works, it is old and you really need a mouse to use it. There are a few workarounds that you can try though:

- Miracast: While there is a builtin app for casting an android phone to the projector, it is buggy and doesn't retain the phone's aspect ratio, stretching the picture out. Instead, install AirScreen from the Play Store. The popup ads can be annoying unless you pay to remove them but AirScreen is the most stable Miracast receiver software I've used. It also supports Apple Airplay, Google Cast, and DLNA. With AirScreen, you can cast Netflix from your phone to the projector.

- FireTV: With the HDMI port, you can connect a FireTV to the projector and take advantage of all the great services that Amazon provides. Just remember that in this case, you cannot adjust the keystone in any way and ceiling mounting or rear-projection modes are not available.

- Kodi: As opposed to what you may have read, Kodi is not illegal. It is simply a great video player that supports addons. There are some addons that are bad, but Kodi itself is not illegal or malware in any way. So basically, only install Kodi either from their official website at kodi.tv or through the Play Store.

Kodi has a Netflix plugin (Search "Netflix Add-on [input-stream]") and click on the Kodi Community Forum link. Again, this plugin is not illegal and does not circumvent Netflix security in any way. You are still required to provide your Netflix login. I will not go into the installation instructions here because it will make this review even longer than it already is.

I hope that I was able to help some of you with my review and tips. Thanks for reading!

title: Cheap enclosure for my mSata drive
text:
It's a cliche to compare something to the size of a match box but this enclosure really is approximate the size of a match box.

This enclosure has a quality build and works well but it is not tool-less assembly. This means that once you screw the drive into the enclosure, you probably don't want to take it out again.

mSata really is a short-lived format and after I retired an old pc, I was only able to salvage the hdd. I purchased this ORICO enclosure with USB Type-C connector to make the best use of the old drive. I'm quite satisfied with its size and durability. It's performance is also quite good. It is recognized by the Windows PC without any hassle (unlike some WD Passports I had) and the drive shows up on the PC within a few seconds (again, unlike some WD Passports I had).

I use this drive to back up pictures and run some portable apps on (such as Eclipse IDE and portable chrome) and since it is an SSD with a USB 3.1 connection, the apps run fast. Faster than running these apps off an SD card.

title: Passthrough video quality bad, drivers bad, recording quality good
text:
I purchased this HDMI Capture USB device to record a Windows desktop session. What I noticed is that the passthrough video quality is very bad. What is clear text coming out of the computer becomes blurry by the time it gets to the TV. What this means is that you can't keep this device plugged in permanently to record when necessary. You'd have to settle for plugging it in only when recording. Perhaps for gaming devices that have larger text and buttons, it wouldn't be a big problem.

This device can also be used to live stream by plugging it in to the USB port on your PC. A few problems here:
-- This is only USB 2.0
-- The USB port is also used as the power supply for the device. This means that if your PC doesn't provide enough power through its USB port (especially if you have an external drive plugged in to the device), you won't be able to use this function. They did not include those two-headed dongles to provide additional power.
-- The drivers are bad. I was able to get OBS to preview the device only after a lot of changing inputs around. VLC will not work with it.

What I do like about it is that while the passthrough quality is pretty bad, the resulting recording isn't. You can certainly tell that it is a recording, probably due to the video compression but all of the text from the 1080p desktop is readable.

I also like the fact that you can record directly to a USB drive with scheduled recording capabilities. The UI of the built-in software is straight out of VHS days but it does the basics of what you need. The convenience of being able to press record on the remote to start your capture means you can set up your PC how you need it without having to also manage your desktop recording software.

title: Comparing 3 great flash drives
text:
In the last month, I purchase 3 different 128gb flash drives for $30 on separate sales that came up. So when the price is the same, it all comes down to speed when comparing these drives.

Drives:
-- [[ASIN:B00FE2N1WS PNY Turbo 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive]] (Newegg Deal)
-- [[ASIN:B00IVEI6CG HP x702w 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive]] (Fry’s Electronics Deal)
-- [[ASIN:B00S5V5PJC Lexar JumpDrive S75 128GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive]] (Costco Deal)

Useable Space (NTFS Formatted):
-- PNY - 119GB
-- HP - 116GB
-- Lexar - 119GB

Benchmarks (Crystal Disk Mark):
-- PNY:
Sequential Read (Q= 32,T= 1) : 87.825 MB/s
Sequential Write (Q= 32,T= 1) : 77.465 MB/s
Random Read 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 6.178 MB/s [ 1508.3 IOPS]
Random Write 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 0.829 MB/s [ 202.4 IOPS]
-- HP:
Sequential Read (Q= 32,T= 1) : 132.768 MB/s
Sequential Write (Q= 32,T= 1) : 57.274 MB/s
Random Read 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 7.834 MB/s [ 1912.6 IOPS]
Random Write 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 1.718 MB/s [ 419.4 IOPS]
-- Lexar:
Sequential Read (Q= 32,T= 1) : 97.070 MB/s
Sequential Write (Q= 32,T= 1) : 108.641 MB/s
Random Read 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 7.035 MB/s [ 1717.5 IOPS]
Random Write 4KiB (Q= 32,T= 1) : 0.938 MB/s [ 229.0 IOPS]

Conclusion:
PNY is the most popular on Amazon because it has the lowest price normally, but when you are able to find deals that equalize the price, it no longer looks that great. I ran Windows To Go on both the PNY and HP. The PNY had a lot of lag because of the low read speed. HP ran well because it has the best performance with 4kb files out of all 3.

The Lexar is a good drive with great write speeds. Good for uses where you are copying in more than you are reading out.

My preference is the Lexar for the size and the great write speeds. The HP is great for web developers to store their projects on because it performs well for reading and writing small files. The PNY is good because it stays at a low price for the most part.

title: Unique device for my unique needs.
text:
I purchase two WEme products in the last month and have been happy with both of my purchases. For my first purchase, I bought this enclosure.

For the last couple of years, I've been purchasing 8" Windows tablets (Acer W500 and Winbook TW801) for my primary use because of their portability and the fact that they are full Windows operating systems. The problem with these tablets are that they have only one USB port and very little disk space (64gb max). What I needed was the ability to connect a large drive to store my music and photos for which an SD card isn't enough. Using a USB hub is the obvious answer in this case, but the number of wires you'd be dealing with grows quickly.

This WEme Enclosure solves the problem of connecting an external HDD while providing access to additional USB ports while keeping the number of wires to 1. Just what I needed.

Features I like:
- Covered enclosure to store external 2.5" drive
- USB 3.0 hub
- Power switch to use switch off HDD to save power and use the enclosure as just a USB hub
- 5V 2A power supply included

Why 4 Stars:
I've had issues with many USB 3.0 cables that I purchased or received from products I purchased. The cable I got with this enclosure was very thick and hard to position in the port. Even when it was plugged in tightly, the enclosure would connect then disconnect after a minute or two. Switching out the cable, the enclosure worked well.

One additional feature would have brought this device 5 stars:
The power supply only seems to supply power to the connected USB devices but not to the computer.
In my case, my two 8" windows tablets had separate charging ports but many Android/Windows tablets and all Android phones out there have a combined port for USB and charging (such as the Toshiba, Dell, and Lenovo 8" windows tabs). A lot of people resort to hacking together connectors to be able to charge and host USB at the same time. I think this device would be perfect if the manufacturer can provide a solution for those users.

WEme seems to have a knack for filling unique needs that I seem to come up with so I hope they can modify their product to provide charging to the host computer if the user needs it.

title: Two Low Priced ANC Earbuds Compared
text:
This is a combined review of two of the lowest cost “Active Noise Cancelling” earbuds on Amazon:
[[ASIN:B004K09H32 Audio-Technica ATH-ANC23 QuietPoint Active Noise-Cancelling In-Ear Headphones]]
[[ASIN:B00SA5JCWO Egghead 1010 - Active Noise Cancelling Earbuds with Travel Pouch]]

PRICE
The price difference as of May, 2015 was $14 with Audio-Technica being the more expensive unit.

IN THE BOX
Both products contain:
--Earbuds
--Multiple silicone earbud cups
--Airline headset adapter
--Carrying Pouch

Audio-Technica contains in addition:
--Battery
--Pair of foam earbud cups. Not memory foam, just normal foam. I have not tried these.

Egghead:
--Mute button: In addition to the ANC on/off switch, Egghead has a nice mute button that turns off Noise Cancellation while it is pressed down.

SOUND QUALITY
I am not an audiophile so the sound from both headsets were good to me but the difference comes when you factor in the fit of the earbuds.

FIT
Both sets sit deeply in your ear and from pictures of both products, you will see that beyond the earbud, they have a circular piece before the actual connection to the wires.
--Egghead: The earbuds are attached straight to the circular piece so the fit is actually straight out away from your ears.
--Audio-Technica: The earbuds are angled forward so the circular piece actually serves as an anchor that sits nicely in your ear lobe and further cuts out outside noise. The additional foam earbud cup may make the difference for some people when it comes to a comfortable fit.
--Kids: I purchased these for a trip that the family will take. The kids usually have a hard time with normal earbuds not fitting in very well but they were able to keep the Audio-Technica earbuds in using the smallest earbud cups. The kids are 6 and 9.

NOISE REDUCTION
Here is the main event. I want to make a few points about Active Noise Cancelling: --Noise cancellation filters are designed to cancel out lower pitched, repeating noises like airplane engine rotors and car tires on a road, but it will not cancel out high or mid-range sounds like human voice. The same engine rotor and road noise also contain components of higher pitched sounds so NC filters will not cut out the noise completely.
--Using Noise Cancellation often feels like being underwater with your ears popping. It is a discomfort that you would have to get used to. The greater the cancellation effect, the greater the discomfort. Be prepared for this if you haven’t used NC before.
--ANC only works IF the inverted noise wave can overpower the noise coming in. If you are using a lawn mower and the noise it makes overpowers the “anti noise” because you’re standing right in back of the motor, you will not hear a big difference in the Noise Reduction effects.

Ok, so on with it. The Audio-Technica claims to reduce 90% of noise. I don’t have anything to confirm the claim but if we assume the Audio-Technica(AT) to be at 90%, my own assessment of the Egghead’s (Egg) noise reduction effects would be around 50-60%.

--Computer Fan Noise: Egg reduces the noise to slightly audible but you’d need to use toggle the mute button on it to really tell. AT completely removes the noise.
--Clothes Dryer: Egg takes the “edge” off the noise produced. You can still hear most of the noise standing about 3 feet away from the dryer. AT takes the bass tones completely out of the noise while leaving the higher pitched metal friction and buttons hitting the tumbler noise. In effect, with the AT, standing only 3 feet away, it sounds like you are actually 20 feet away.

So in conclusion, you have probably guessed that I think the additional cost of the Audio-Technicas are worth it. In addition to the benefits mentioned above, I have recently been able to get a great deal on a pair of [[ASIN:B00UETOW4C Harmon/Kardon SOHO II NC]] on ebay. The noise reduction effects of the Audio-Technicas equal or maybe even exceeds those of the Harmon/Kardons.

title: Love this enclosure
text:
I love how compact this case is. The rounded edges make the case seem even smaller.
I'm not going to section off the Good, Bad, Ugly features because I really haven't found any real problems with this enclosure.

Features I like:
- Fits 2.5" notebook HDD at the standard height (not necessary to buy a low profile SSD)
- Plug and Play. Some enclosures take almost a minute for the PC to recognize. The drive shows up instantly in My Computer once plugged in.
- Fast USB 3.0. I'll go into this in more detail.
- Aluminum case. Good for keeping the drive cool.
- Opens without a tool. A button (a little hard to press) releases the top and bottom covers allowing easy access to the drive inside.
- Led is not too bright. The LED is hidden behind black translucent plastic so it doesn't get too bright. Just enough for you to see that it is on and the drive is reading.

Speed:
I boot Windows 8.1 To Go from a standard 5400rpm drive plugged in to this enclosure. Windows To Go contains the entire windows OS and boots it from USB which allows a computer to dual boot to Windows 8.1 by simply plugging the drive in. From this drive, I've also installed and played games like Assassin's Creed Unity and Shadows of Mordor. While loading speed may be slower than an SSD plugged in to SATA, I still felt that the loading speed for the games were acceptable.

In conclusion, this is a nice looking case that feels good to hold, easy to slip in to a pocket and easily accessible (I switch out the drives sometimes). It is fully supported by Windows 8 and is sold at a great price.

title: Good cable.  No problems
text:
The DisplayPort to HDMI cable that I got was not as pictured. The HDMI side of the cable was much smaller than pictured which was a nice surprise.

The cable worked as expected. There were no compatibility issues. I connected the HDMI cable to my TV and the DisplayPort to my laptop and the TV was recognized as 1080p. No signal interference and good colors.

The price is also good at $8.

title: Affordable and adds very little bulk.
text:
This SmartShell case is not just a magnetic cover for the iPad Air. It has a hard shell that protects the back of the tablet. To me, this is preferable to the magnetic cover because of the extra protection. The disadvantage is that you will not be able to take the cover off easily like the magnetic cover. It adds about 1/8" to each dimension of the iPad which is a minimal as you can get and still have protection.

My kids dropped the tablet on its corner near the volume buttons from about 2 1/2 feet off the ground. The plastic around the volume buttons cracked (it's the weakest part of the entire case) but the tablet was fine. No dents or scratches. A little super-glue to seal the crack and the case was as good as new. Had it been the magnetic cover, the tablet would have had a pretty bad dent.

This case gives you the "tablet" stand capability of the magnetic cover while providing more protection.

title: It charges alkaline...  but mostly, it's an excellent Ni-MH charger.
text:
More than anyone, I really wanted alkaline charging to work like other rechargeable batteries but the sad reality is that they're just not made for it.

The reality of alkaline charging:
- Duracells seem to leak more than cheapo "Kirkland" brand from Costco.
- Energizers do not hold charge very well.
- All brands leak eventually.
- Takes a long time to charge.
- Unreliable even if successfully recharged -- usually, batteries are connected in series, which means that if one fails, the device will not work.
- Battery leak can happen while charging or while being used in the device, resulting in a very messy charger and messy device.

So after some dumpster diving (or at least, I raided the battery recycling bins at work), I came home with batteries of various brands. For a while, I really did use recharged alkaline batteries exclusively and kept my Ni-MH batteries in the drawer. What I found was that I needed to change the batteries a lot more often and I couldn't be sure that the battery would have a charge when I took it out of the drawer.

Leaking is a big problem. My charger now has one charging port that is stuck because the liquid got in to the spring mechanism and dried. I also have a couple of remotes and devices that had to be cleaned out because the batteries leaked.

In the end, I had to give up on the idea of recharging cheap alkaline batteries because of how long it takes to recharge and that it can leak at any time, potentially ruining your device (mostly, it's just oily and you need to clean it out with a tissue). I just couldn't trust those batteries.

So why did I still give this charger 5 stars? Although alkaline charging was a failed experiment for me, the charger is still a better-than-average Ni-MH battery charger. It has separate intelligent charging and LCD display for each battery and will trickle charge a battery even after the lights turn green. Other chargers that have the same features cost more -- and without the Alkaline charging capability. You really can't go wrong with this charger.

title: Clock that doesn't quite do what you need it to.
text:
I thought I wouldn’t be picky when it comes to buying a new alarm clock; I mean, I owned a Sony Dream Machine (yeah, you too?) for over 30 years and that had minimal features! At least, that’s what I thought until I actually started looking for a new one.

When you look at the possibilities out there you start to think that perhaps I need:
- Bluetooth? It would be nice to wake up to a playlist I set up in my phone.
- Good sound quality? If I’m gonna have bluetooth, the sound quality needs to be good.
- Projection? It would be nice to see the time on the ceiling with the press of a button.
- Atomic? It would be nice to NOT have to manually set the time for Daylight Savings.
- Temperature/Weather? It would be great to know the weather when I look at the time -- especially if it is projected on the ceiling!

The Soundbot tries to provide many of these features but fail to put them together into one cohesive unit. It tries to be an alarm clock and bluetooth speakers but fails at both.

The Good:
- Great looking design. The wood look and the size, color and placement of time and temperature all add to a great look for the Soundbot.
- Impressive sound. As I’m currently searching for a bluetooth portable speaker (and have already reviewed a few), I pay special attention to sound quality. It’s comparable to the Jambox Mini.
- Touch controls. No buttons to detract from the wood look of the clock. The snooze, volume, and phone buttons are all touch sensitive.
- Time is remembered even when unplugged.

The Bad:
- The clock does NOT play a bluetooth when the alarm goes off. The workaround is to use your phone as the alarm, but what’s the point?
- No Next/Prev track buttons. The +/- buttons only control volume.
- Only one level of dimming. You can choose full or half brightness with the snooze button but it is still a little bright for me. I have to turn the clock away while I sleep.
- Alarm only has one sound: an annoying beep.

Tip:
The alarm clock can be set to go off every day (the alarm LED is solid, not flashing). When the alarm goes off, PRESS and HOLD any touch-sensitive button to disable the alarm for today. It will then go off again tomorrow.

Conclusion:
With the inability to use the bluetooth as an alarm tone, and without an FM Radio as an alternative, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor alarm clock. You’re stuck with a simple beep. Without a next/prev track button, the Soundbot serves as a pretty poor wireless speaker. The good sound quality is the only thing it has going for it.

title: Good HDMI-CEC support; unimportant to most, important to me.
text:
I purchased this Panasonic Soundbar in June of 2013. At the time, my requirements were:
- Good sound (can't afford GREAT sound)
- Wireless Subwoofer
- HDMI input and good HDMI-CEC support
- Bluetooth support

In my search, I tested the [[ASIN:B00811NMMI Toshiba SBX4250]] and the [[ASIN:B00BLX9510 Samsung HW-F450]] from my local Costco. My final choice was the Panasonic.

Sound:
- Acceptable sound -- The front speakers are not a big improvement over the built-ins. With the subwoofer turned off, it is easy to mistake the Panasonic sound bar with the speakers from the Television.
- Good subwoofer -- The sub sounds good even at high volumes and fills out the overall sound from the sound bar.
- The Samsung has clearer mid and high ranges so the Panasonic seems slightly muffled in comparison.
- Overall sound better than the Toshiba.
- Wireless range for the subwoofer is short -- especially if placed behind the sofa (interference from people sitting in front of it). Range is about 15 feet with clear line of sight.

Decoders and Passthrough:
- AC3 and DTS Decoder (Toshiba lacks DTS)
- ARC (Audio Return Channel) -- If you use the Netflix app built in to your TV, audio is generated by your TV. Normally, an "optical out" cable from the TV back to the sound bar is necessary. ARC removes that need.

HDMI-CEC (also Aquos Link, Anynet+, Bravia LinkSync, Regza Link, etc):
This is where the Panasonic beats the Samsung. HDMI-CEC allows Televisions to control a connected device -- no matter the brand; The TV remote should be able to turn on a bluray player and send navigation (up/down/etc) and standard playback buttons without the need for a second remote control.

In the case of a sound bar, through HDMI-CEC:
1. The sound bar should turn on when the TV turns on -- Panasonic does this, Samsung does not.
2. The TV should play all sound through the sound bar and volume buttons on the TV remote should control volume on the sound bar -- Panasonic does this.
3. Turning on a bluray player, the sound bar should turn on and switch to the correct input automatically. The TV should also turn on and switch to the correct input -- Panasonic does this. It's then up to your TV do its part.

In conclusion, I chose the Panasonic because it gave me the ability to eliminate a remote control through HDMI-CEC (which Samsung didn't) and it had both AC3 and DTS decoders (which Toshiba didn't). With the added ability to play music from my phone through bluetooth, I'm still happy with my purchase one year later.

Tip: Unlike the Samsung and Toshiba, the Panasonic has a small "receiver" unit that adds another machine to your entertainment center. For me, I use some velcro strips and attach the "receiver" to the back of my TV. It is only 1 ¾" thick which was thinner than my wall mount.

title: Music that moves with you.
text:
Almost weightless with a great fit, and good battery life, the Avantree AS8Q Earbuds are great exercise headsets. The only factors keeping it from being perfect is the sound quality and clunky button controls.

For contrast, I also have the “Chicklets” style earbuds that have been rebranded by many companies (e.g. ECSEM Mini Lightweight...). If these “Chiclets” earbuds worked well for you, the Avantree will be a nice upgrade.

You should get the Avantree AS8Q if you are looking for:
-- lightweight and moves with you (after tightening the headband, there is nothing on these earbuds that flap, swing, tangle, or stick to your neck).
-- in ear, not over-the-ear (earbuds are angled slightly forward so they will fit deep into the ear).
-- separate earbuds (buds are not held together by a rigid band like the Motorola S10).
-- sweat proof.
-- good battery life (5 hours, while the “Chiclets” style earbuds have 2 hours).
-- no controls that dangle from the wires (like the Plantronics Backbeat)
-- great noise isolation (Deeply seated earbuds means you block out most of the noise. I’m able to hear the music and audiobook over the sound of a basketball bouncing off hardwood floors in an enclosed court without having to turn the volume up high).
-- good bluetooth range (I keep my phone on a chair near center of the basketball court, on the sidelines, and I’m able to go to both sides of the court without any drop outs. “Chiclet” style buds did not have this range).

And you don’t mind:
-- Fair sound quality. Compared to even the “Chicklets” style earbuds, upper and middle frequencies sound a little muddy, and the bass sounds blown out. Ever stand next to speakers on the dance floor? They sound horrible, but step away and they sound fine. The earbuds seat so deeply in your ear that you feel like the speakers are right next to your ear drums. Yes, the design advantage is also the design flaw. For all the other qualities that these earbuds have, I can overlook the sound quality issues (because let’s face it, you get used to it).
-- Clunky controls. The rubber that covers the control buttons are designed to keep sweat out, but they also make it hard to push the buttons. I often press the power button thinking I’ve got it pushed down, but after 10 seconds, I realize the earbuds aren’t turning on (or off). Same with trying to skip tracks. By contrast, controls on the “Chiclets” earbuds are easy to press while still being sweat proof.
-- Controls that seem backwards. Volume up is toward the back of your head and volume down is toward the front. Skip FORWARD is a long press of the volume DOWN button and the volume Up for skip back.

Wishlist for next revision:
-- Reduce the size of the housing.
-- Hard plastic buttons
-- Active noise cancellation. Noise isolation is nice, but you really can't hear anything when someone is talking to you.

In conclusion, I thoroughly enjoy my workouts with these earbuds.

title: Solid tablet mount for a good price.

title: Good enclosure with added benefits
text:
Video files are big and add up quickly to fill up your tablet. With a WIFI enabled hard drive, you can free up space but still have access to your movies and shows. With a USB 3.0 and Ethernet connection, the Macally enclosure not only solves these storage issues, it provides some side benefits as well. Unfortunately, with limited WIFI range and unstable firmware, there is plenty of room for improvement.

Macally has the following advantage over similar devices:
- Ethernet port AND USB 3.0: Other enclosures on the market either do not include ethernet or is not USB 3.0. This enclosure has both. With Ethernet, the enclosure functions as a portable router and NAS.

Good:
- Transfer speed: USB 3.0 means transferring large files is FAST. I get 60Mb/sec.
- Files On-The-Go: Files are shared via HTTP if you use the WifiStor app or SAMBA if you use a computer.
- Battery life: I get about 3 hours because I have a SATA drive, not SSD. Life can be extended using any cell phone charger pack.
- Functions while charging: Plug in to car charger and no worries about batteries during a long road trip.
- Portable router/Wifi Repeater: In a hotel room, share the ethernet connection with the rest of your devices or use the WIFI repeater function and log in to the hotel’s gateway page only once for all devices.
- Acts as a NAS: Plug this into your router using an Ethernet cable and you have a nice Network storage device.

Bad:
- WIFI range is short. Because of additional interference you’d get in a hotel room (other wifi hotspots), WIFI wouldn’t even work across the room.

- Desperate need of a firmware upgrade:
-- Need automatic switching between Ethernet or Wifi. If Ethernet is plugged in, use that as the Internet connection otherwise, use the last WIFI AP.
-- Need stability. When using WIFI as Internet connection, the unit crashes and requires a few reboots before becoming useable.
-- Need FTP Server.
-- Need UPNP/DLNA. While playing videos off SAMBA is possible, UPNP/DLNA is more widely supported on the IOS and TV’s.

Tips for iOS:
Don’t rely on the WifiStor app. Players like PlayerXtreme HD will stream videos directly from SAMBA shares. Share is \\10.10.10.254\WiFiDisk1_Volume1

Tips for Android:
Video is already supported because WifiStor will launch the correct player for each video, but my top choice is to use XBMC and connect directly via SAMBA.

title: It's a mouse, it works.
text:
When purchasing a bluetooth mouse, or any bluetooth device, an important factor is how well it connects and how well it STAYS connected. After all this time, the industry still can’t make up its mind about how bluetooth works:
- Microsoft with their mouse and Sony with their controller that pair without the need of a code (which Android’s bluetooth stack doesn’t support).
- Mice and keyboards that will not reconnect after it wakes from sleep mode.
- To this day, bluetooth devices still can’t wake a computer from suspend state.
So when I get a simple bluetooth mouse for a good price, and it actually works as expected, I was happy.

For my review, I’m comparing the Bornd mouse to the [[ASIN:B006428K7I Motorola 89519N Bluetooth Mouse]] which I got in a set that included the [[ASIN:B004L9MBH6 Motorola Wireless Keyboard for Motorola ATRIX and XOOM (Motorola Retail Packaging)]].

With the Motorola mouse, its frequency somehow conflicts with the Motorola keyboard, resulting in sticky keys, as in “I’m having a good daaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaay”. Conversely, the keyboard interferes with the mouse where the computer would actually lose connection with the mouse for a few seconds after typing, or lose connection completely.

What I liked about the Bornd:
- Pairing was simple using the button at the bottom of the mouse.
- Operating distance is about 5 feet, but this may be because of my computer’s bluetooth antenna
- Takes a single AA battery which lasts over a month of moderate use (2 hours per day)
- Mouse movement is good. No need to adjust mouse speed in the control panel.
- Accuracy is good. Editing images using Pixlr.com, I’m able to select precisely the parts of the image I need.

What gave me trouble with the Bornd:
- When you first put your hand on this mouse, you will not feel that it is very well built. The plastic is completely smooth and the mouse wheel seems to rattle when you shake it. I got used to it after a few minutes, though.
- The mouse reconnects with the computer most of the time, but sometimes it was necessary to turn the mouse off and on again after the computer reboots or if the computer was out of range for an extended period of time.
- Lately, I’ve been experiencing double-clicks when I click on the left mouse button once. I’m usually able to fix this by getting angry and slamming the mouse down a couple of times. This may indicate a build quality issue with this mouse.

In my specific case, the Bournd did not interfere with my Motorola keyboard at all and it seems the sticky key occurs only when the batteries on the keyboard runs low.

title: Great Portability, Okay Pictures, Poor Durability
text:
I bought this camera for my wife last summer when she was in China. She was looking for something with less shutter lag than our last generation of Nikon and Canon digital point-and-shoots, and something cute and portable. The Panasonic DMC-FX30 is both of these things.

Out of the box it overexposed and undercolored things, but this was easily fixable after fiddling with the settings menu. Even set up right, photos using the flash still look too shiny whit, and photos taken at high ISOs are pretty noisy. The lack of a real viewfinder also makes capturing action clunky, but this is obviously in part an artifact of my preferences. This camera takes fine outdoor pictures, and the wide angle zoom allows for some cool shots and works well in confined (well-lit) spaces.

The camera is a small, precision-made jewel of a camera, with controls and buttons designed for smaller hands than mine; they fit my wife fine. We both missed the lack of a real viewfinder; pocket cameras seem to making an unfortunate departure from this useful standard (bright sunlight washes the display out, and it's easier to take a picture from your eye, as that's what you're composing with in the first place). The camera performed fine in its role as a city camera in Beijing, and for snapping quick shots back home when lugging the SLR around was inconvenient.

Now, however, we are in rural China for a year doing field work, and I was using the Panasonic as a backup to my Nikon DSLR. It was nice having a wide-angle lens in a pouch in my pocket when I had my normal or telephoto primes on the SLR. The Panasonic worked great in this role for 3-weeks, and then the automatic lens cap froze shut and wouldn't open, despite my coaxing, cleaning, etc. I finally just pried it off so I can still use the camera (I keep a business card over the lens in the soft pocket pouch), but let's say that I am not impressed with the camera's durability, compared to any other camera I've had, film or digital. It never got wet, dusty, dropped, or sat on; it looks brand new, but the lens cap won't work, and failed in a way that renders the camera useless to someone unwilling to take pliers to a Leica lens (failing and staying open would be preferable).

Anyway, if you're looking for a field or reliable travel camera, pass this one up.

For anyone who hasn't done comparative research, Samsung SD (and micro-SD) cards have earned top ranks in terms of speed and reliability when compared with other brands - even name brands like Sandisk.  The green version is exactly the same as the red version of this card (same class and speed) except for color, and the green being slightly cheaper.  Amazon owns exclusive rights to the green version (so get the green and support Amazon!) but they are internally identical.  I've owned 2 other smaller versions of this card (a 32gb and 128gb) which have worked flawlessly for years, but are now too small for my storage needs.  I would recommend getting this largest version (although 1TB is not really a good value) of this card that you can afford.

title: Works exactly like the original charger, but cheaper
