My initial impression is that this charger is just like the original. The only very minor differences are that the rubber seems *slightly* firmer (who cares?) and the little charging indicator light on the end of the cord takes just a moment to turn on. So far, I'm giving it 5 stars since it works just like the original, including the extra usb charging slot on the transformer. Will update the review should it go kaput.

Update:. Still working strong but the connector has become a bit fiddly, whereas the original charger has not. I use both daily.

title: Mine does not work correctly, going to return this.
text: I would give this one star, except for the cheap price.  The number one problem with mine is that the heart rate monitor does not accurately measure heart rate, or even close.  After 15-20 minutes of running, the readings fluctuated wildly.  At first it was 120, then 131, then a few seconds later 85!  I tried looser and tighter band settings, and also tried rotating the watch to position the sensor on different areas of my wrist (to detect pulse better), and it still never worked correctly.  I'm not sure if mine is just defective, or this product is poorly designed.  There are also a few other minor issues, such as the dull screen (see photo - very hard to read when outdoors) and also my device has randomly shut off a few times.  Overall, I would not recommend this product for anyone.  It's too bad, though, because the design is nice (as is the price) and the bluetooth connectivity and software work well.

title: This keyboard is comfortable to use thanks to the fabric
text: This keyboard is comfortable to use thanks to the fabric, and doesn't feel cramped despite the 12" size.  Keys feel solid and type well, with medium-high resistance, and are somewhere in the middle between quiet and noisy.  The keyboard isn't as noisy as most mechanical keyboards (like a Cherry blue/green) but it's still noisy enough to bother my wife if I'm using it in bed when she wants to sleep.  The backlighting is well-balanced, enough to make keys clear and easy to read but not so much that it looks freaky at night.  The magnetic attachment to the surface pro works like a charm, and is so easy it's almost fool-proof.  It still feels expensive (compared to similarly priced mechanical gaming keyboards) but does its job well.

title: Flawless Set Up
text:
I took this laptop to use for running a Cameo cutting machine. The Silhouette folks suggest a gaming type platform for the machine so that there is enough memory and processing power.

This is my first time to have an HP computer. Set up was pretty straightforward once I found the power button. A little guidance on that would be nice from the manufacturer. It's on the top of the keyboard on the left. The unit runs quietly and does not get hot like some of the others I have. The keyboard is OK. The characters are backlit with a bright green light which doesn't do much for me and the alphabet is some sort of modern thing where the "A" doesn't look like an A. I'll adjust.
What I'm not impressed with is the construction of this. The top is very flimsy when you open and close it. Kind of bendy and thin. Not framed well like others I have had. It will be fine for me in my studio, but I don't think it would hold up to being carried around and banged about.
I also don't much care for the touchpad at all. It seems hypersensitive even set on medium touch and requires multiple fingers to scroll and capture. I never could figure out how to get it to grab something to copy and paste. I'm off to get a mouse as soon as I'm finished.
Processing time seems fast. The display is very clear and the colors are true. As an artist this is important for the work I do. Peripherals all connected and installed easily. All in all I am pleased to have this.

title: Nothing Special
text:
Let me preface this review with saying that I love the Spectrum Noir markers. Have had both generations and recommend them to everyone. They are easy to use and a good value. On the other hand, I am not so "gobsmacked" about the new line of pencils. I bought the complete set because I am an illustrator and I like to have full sets of the tools I use. First off I was put off by the fact that there are 5 tins to sort through to find a color. I'm sure they did this, so folks could buy a tin at a time, but it easy to keep flipping open lids and looking around for just the right color you want. The pencils also fit very snuggly in the boxes and it is difficult to get them out sometimes.
As for the "creaminess" of said pencils, I would say there are some inconsistencies in that as well. Some of the Floral colors are really soft and creamy, some of the browns and grays are hard and scratchy and then there are some that are just so waxy you can't lay down two colors on top of each other.
If you are a rubber stamper or crafter that plans to use them, you will probably be fine with these. They seem to be geared more to that kind of audience. The price is right for what you get. I had no trouble sharpening the few I used. No breakage like I have encountered with the Prismacolor set I've had for 10 years. The blending solution I suspect is just Gamsol which most stampers already have if they've been using pencils before. I was able to achieve the same results using the Prismacolor pencils I had over the markers.
I will say their customer service rocks because they are going to allow me to send these back. This is a great company to deal with, I just think they kind of missed the mark with these.

title: Excellent Ethernet Port Covers
text:
As all computer professionals can attest dust collection can be a major issue for computers internal components. As the internal fans work to pull air in to cool the computer it also will pull in dust through every open port. While the air vents typically have screens that help collect this the ports do not - this is where plugs are so important.

I utilize port plugs on all of my devices - computers, switches, cameras, TVs, any port not in use has a plug to prevent both dust and moisture intrusion.

These plugs click into place and perform exactly as they should protecting your equipment.

This is an excellent set that is well worth the investment.

title: Split the Signal without Losing Speed
text:
I have a super fast internet signal run into my home. With that I split it to 2 separate routers in order to keep my computer network and NAS completely separate from my IOT network. While the same can be accomplished by creating a virtual network I have found this solution more stable and it allows me to have far more devices connected without dropouts.

One of the keys to having this type of system work correctly is having a dependable, fast switch at the start where the signal originates - and that is where this switch has proven rock solid.

This 5 port switch is incredibly well built. Speeds are very comparable to business class switches I tested it next to yet it is far less expensive. In all of my testing the differences were so minor I would recommend this switch over the others every time.

This is an outstanding product you can depend on.

title: AWESOME ETHERNET SWITCH AND POWER SUPPLY!
text:
This powerful, silent, unmanaged Ethernet switch has 24 fast PoE ports (100 Mbps) that not only provide high speed internet (2 Gigabit Uplink) but automatically detects if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last several months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected (up to a total of 360 watts) but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide ample internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I used this switch within my security system setup and mounted it within my security closet. I love that it is easily wall mountable but it can also be mounted within a rack with no problem.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage utilizing this method as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

I have found this switch is rock solid and perfect for use as an unmanaged PoE switch for security cameras.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

title: Excellent Articulating Arm for Steady Base
text:
I built a custom computer desk last year and used another table top as my keyboard platform until now as I hadn’t found an articulating arm I thought was worth trying until I saw this.

I installed this earlier this week and have been so impressed. I was able to squeeze my full sized keyboard within the flexible fingers on each side with my wrist rest at the base. While tight, it is very secure which is exactly what I wanted.

The arm is highly adjustable to different usage scenarios which is very important. For those of us who are always thinking outside the box it is nice to know there are options with a product.

One of my concerns with using an articulating arm for my keyboard was whether it would bounce or jiggle as I typed. This has not been the case at all. It is easy to tighten the adjustments of certain bolts to hold those joints in place while still having other move which allows me to articulate the arm out of my way.

I have worked with several Mount-It! products and not only are the products themselves high quality but the customer service is amazing.

This is an outstanding product by a dependable customer focused manufacturer.

I definitely recommend this.

title: Amazing Smartly Designed Tower of Power
text:
I designed a cabinet space to house my farm of external hard drives that I use for backing up a variety of media and this ended up working absolutely perfectly to power everything.

My cabinet has a shelf and is open at the back and 2 drawers to the side. I was able to utilize the top drawer to house this tower shaped surge protector. This awesome surge protector provides plenty of power outlets for all of my external hard drives, my USB 3.1 hub and USB ports to power my cooling fans.

Due to this being an enclosed space I had to consider proper airflow and cooling. I placed laptop cooling fan units beneath each shelf of hard drives, in addition I am using three 120mm fans set up as 2 intake and 1 exhaust - all powered by the USB outlet ports.

I have been using this unit for nearly 4 months with no issue and could not be happier with its performance.

This is a well made, well thought out product that I certainly recommend.

title: Quality Micro SD Card

title: Decent Quality Clone at the Price - Budget Friendly Blue Iris Camera
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

As with all security systems my advice is never use cloud based recording - this opens your entire network to not only the company who you are giving blanket access too but also to hackers. The same is true for WiFi. Obviously WiFi is more convenient but if your privacy is a concern this really needs to be taken into account. Hackers have become quite adept at hacking into WiFi cameras and being able to not only watch your feed but control your cameras and access your entire network. If you choose to utilize WiFi cameras take the time to understand your router and employ proper VPN protocols.

Due to my security concerns with WiFi cameras my current security system is completely run through a dedicated computer utilizing the Blue Iris software. While this may seem intimidating to some, it is well worth learning and utilizing for the huge advantages in privacy and security.

I’ve noticed many people have asked if this camera works with a Blue Iris and it does without any issue. Just update to the latest firmware. The remainder of setup within Blue Iris is straightforward. This HITOSINO / VALUCAM 8MP IR IP CAMERA supports PoE 802.3af and will work with 48V active adapters which are more expensive, but you can also rely on a PoE switch, which in my opinion is a much easier, straightforward option.

The fixed lens size of 2.8mm provides decent field of view and the digital zoom is acceptable. The 1/2.7" CMOS image sensor is decent in low light, certainly not as good as 1/1.8” but I’ve found the low light capabilities average in comparison to other similar cameras. While low light capabilities will not blow you away they are reasonable. The LEDs must be illuminating objects to provide what is considered “colored night vision” which is misleading.

The camera has a built in microphone that allows for sound recording, though no speaker so two way communication will not be possible with this unit.

In terms of storage, the HITOSINO / VALUCAM 8MP IR IP CAMERA utilizes H.265 which is currently the best option for video compression. I have had this set up utilizing Blue Iris software which I definitely recommend. By fine tuning BI settings I have been able to find a balance between file size and image quality that works for my situation.

When all things are taken into account this is a solidly built camera, reasonably suited to outdoor environments - if at all exposed to elements rake the time to seal as an added layer of protection, decent daytime / nighttime resolution, easily mounted, and setup in Blue Iris was reasonably easy and straightforward.

While I would prefer to have pan and tilt capabilities at this price point that is unrealistic.

Overall I have been moderately impressed with this budget camera and would recommend it for many security situations.

title: Among the Best Wireless Doorbell Cameras I’ve Tested - but
text:

I have tested and reviewed many wireless doorbell systems. Typically I always advise to avoid any wireless cameras due to the inherent security vulnerabilities but this is often not possible with doorbell cameras. That being said there are key components I look for in wireless doorbell cameras: clear picture that provides a wide viewing angle, it either be hard wired or have excellent battery life, when chime button is pressed alert is sent and app can be opened and responsive in a quick time, 2 way audio communication is clear on both ends, motion sensitivity is adjustable and accurate.

I have thoroughly tested this product over the last 4 months and in comparison to the others on the market around this price point this product has proven to be clearly the best.

In terms of what is excellent - the internal battery is long lasting and dependable - I have found that it will last nearly 2 months on a single charge. The vast majority of wireless doorbells use proprietary batteries which forces users to purchase secondary batteries typically costing $30-$50. This factor is a huge bonus.

The camera is quite good. Images are clear and the wide angle provides a full view of the area in front of the doorbell. The AI Smart Human detection is without question the best I have found. This is a huge feature that helps prevent constant false alerts.

The base station holds up to a 128GB SD card for video storage. This is awesome for multiple reasons. If the camera was stolen the evidence will be saved on the base station within your home and all of your recordings are stored locally. This is an outstanding system.

Unfortunately, as with many similar products, while the hardware is good the software needs some work. As is typical, I can not find any way to force this doorbell to work with better software. It is obvious this was designed on the Tuya platform though I have not found any way of integrating it. I would much rather use the Tuya app where I have the bulk of my automation set but this will not migrate.

The lag from the time the doorbell button is pressed until you can see who is there is mediocre. The FASTEST I’ve been able to get this to work is 18 seconds - and I’m using an iPhone 13 Pro Max with 512GB on a super fast 1G mesh WiFi with a node located within feet of the doorbell inside the door.

The 2 way audio is spotty. It sounds like ordering through a drive through where every 3rd word is audible. Since I don’t use these to have in depth conversations it isn’t a huge deal but should be noted.

This is definitely among the best wireless doorbells I have tested for a while. It is not perfect, the sound leaves room for improvement as does response times but overall this is a quality unit.

While the vast majority of the doorbells I tested I advised to avoid all together this one is one worth using.

title: Awesome Concept - Poor Execution
text:
Being both an audiophile and a lover of all new tech when I first read about this technology coming out a few years ago I started looking forward to testing it.

So what are the potential advantages of bone conduction earphones? I’m glad you asked. When properly adjusted they allow the user to enjoy listening to whatever they choose while not blocking external noises, thus allowing the user to react to ambient noises. This should make them safe to use while driving or doing other activities that require hearing ambient noise in order to conduct safely.

As with other bone conduction headphones, these 9 Digital headphones allow for little fine adjustment. In order for this type of headphones to work properly and provide the highest sound quality they should rest flat, or almost flat against the skin between the front of the ear and the rear part of the cheek bone. When adjusting the speaker it will be clear when the speaker is properly adjusted. This set of headphones is designed to fall lower on the back of the head which for me pulled the speakers out of the ideal placement. While I have worked on adjusting this, it really is not possible. Due to this, sound quality is decent yet not optimal and surrounding people are able to hear what the listener is playing.

Just so it is understood, these headphones are rated IP53, meaning that they’re protected against dust, in so much as their inner workings won’t be compromised if dust were to get inside. They’re also protected against spraying water, with no pressure when tilted up to a 60-degree angle. This is a lower rating as compared to other headphones in this price range.

In terms of operation these headphones struggle to maintain a solid connection for anywhere close to the full 33 feet they are rated - typically Bluetooth 5.0 holds a connection with no problem though I have found that isn’t the case with these headphones. The batteries lasted approximately the amount of time listed. Sound quality is middle of the road especially due to not allowing for fine adjusting of the speakers.

This is a great technology with a lot of potential. I have tested and reviewed bone conduction headphones since they first were released a few years ago, due to how these fit and the connectivity issues this is not a set I would recommend.

This mount works, but I would really only recommend it for locations where the user does not intend to alter the tilt or direction of the TVs screen very often.

title: Quality Budget Friendly Blue Iris Camera
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

As with all security systems my advice is never use cloud based recording - this opens your entire network to not only the company who you are giving blanket access too but also to hackers. The same is true for WiFi. Obviously WiFi is more convenient but if your privacy is a concern this really needs to be taken into account. Hackers have become quite adept at hacking into WiFi cameras and being able to not only watch your feed but control your cameras and access your entire network. If you choose to utilize WiFi cameras take the time to understand your router and employ proper VPN protocols.

Due to my security concerns with WiFi cameras my current security system is completely run through a dedicated computer utilizing the Blue Iris software. While this may seem intimidating to some, it is well worth learning and utilizing for the huge advantages in privacy and security.

I’ve noticed many people have asked if this camera works with a Blue Iris and it does without any issue. Just update to the latest firmware. The remainder of setup within Blue Iris is straightforward. This IPC2387C supports PoE 802.3af and will work with 48V active adapters which are more expensive, but you can also rely on a PoE switch, which in my opinion is a much easier, straightforward option. Something to note, if you plan on powering via a DC cable this is not included.

The fixed lens size of 2.8mm provides decent field of view and the digital zoom is acceptable. The 1/2.8” CMOS 8MP image sensor is decent in low light, certainly not as good as 1/1.8” but I’ve found the low light capabilities average in comparison to other similar cameras. The LEDs must be illuminating objects to provide what is considered “colored night vision” which is misleading.

The camera has a built in microphone that allows for sound recording, though no speaker so two way communication will not be possible with this unit.

In terms of storage, the IPC2387C utilizes H.265 which is currently the best option for video compression. I have had this set up utilizing Blue Iris software which I definitely recommend.

When all things are taken into account this is a solidly build camera, suited to outdoor environments, decent daytime / nighttime resolution, fairly easily mounted, and setup in Blue Iris was reasonably easy and straightforward.

While I would prefer to have pan and tilt capabilities at this price point that is unrealistic. Overall I have been moderately impressed with this budget camera and would recommend it for many security situations.

title: Buyer Beware - This is NOT as it Seems
text:
When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.

title: Exactly the Cabinet Cooling Fan I Needed!
text:

This is where I have installed this fan as an exhaust at the top white 2 other fans pull cool air from the bottom. I always monitor the internal temperature of the cabinet and this fan has worked incredibly well.

This fan is easy to mount, it has a standard plug and the speed is adjusted by the attached knob. What is shocking is how much air this moves considering how quiet it is.

This has been an all around excellent product that I highly recommend.

title: ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE BLUETOOTH SPEAKER
text:
I have tested and reviewed literally hundreds of Bluetooth speakers and while I am not a fan of music that is particularly bass heavy I found this speaker produces rich, vibrant sounds from all wave lengths. It produces more than ample volume for most any setting and has several connection methods.

While I have tested and reviewed Bluetooth speakers costing far more than what this does, the sound quality from this speaker rivals them. In relation to the sound quality this speaker is simply incredible.

In regards to charging time and battery life, both are outstanding. In my tests charging takes about approximately 2 hours to charge the built in whopping 10,400 mAh battery and the speaker lasts a solid 6.5 hours at max volume - 10 hour with volume midway (of course this will vary a bit due to exact settings).

There are multiple ways to connect to this speaker including Bluetooth 5.0, which can reach much further than previous versions, through an AUX cable, a 3.5mm jack, TF/SD card and you can even connect via NFC (Near Field Communication).

I have taken this speaker with me to the pool for the last couple of months and have been thoroughly impressed with its performance. The battery, being 10,400 mAh, it’s much longer lasting than most allowing for all day listening and the sound quality has been outstanding. The battery is so awesome this can even be used as a power bank to charge your phone - most speakers can’t make that claim.

This speaker is rated IPX5 meaning it is tested and proven safe for splashes - technically, a device with a level 5 water resistance rating can survive small water jets projected by a 6.3mm nozzle at any angle. The testing lasts for 15 min and the volume of water is 12.5 l/min.

If you have 2 of these speakers they pair for true surround sound producing a full, rich, encompassing sound environment that is hard to believe can come from a pair of small Bluetooth speakers.

All of this battery and speaker comes with weight - 5.28 pounds to be exact. That is definitely the downside to this speaker.

This is an all around great Bluetooth speaker that I certainly recommend.

title: Decent Wall Mount for Large TVs
text:

We used this bracket to hang our new 75 inch Sony TV. The bracket itself has worked well. We did end up utilizing the extension bracket which gave us added mobility in locating the TV in the center of the wall. Due to our hanging the TV on an interior wall that had a narrow gap between the drywall and cinder block I had to get special wall anchors to support the weight of the TV.

This is definitely a stable TV mount - even for large TVs, it’s just not the easiest to connect accessories once the TV is hung.

There is limited tilt mobility but enough to adjust for viewing angle.

This is a decent TV mount for large TVs but could be better.

title: Simple Security Device - Batteries Drain - Too Much Hassle
text:
For many years I have researched, written about and reviewed all types of security equipment - from the most advanced to the most simple. This set falls into the later category.

I have tested and reviewed several similar sets. Each of these sensors work based on a simple magnetic principle which is why it is critical they be mounted on the same plains, directly next to to each other when the door or window is closed. When open the magnet is released and the switch triggers causing the alarm to sound. This technology has been used with great success for many years.

The alarms are very loud and work the way they should. If the batteries lasted as long as the listing claimed this would be a reasonable set though they do not. These sets will require battery changes every 2.5-3 months, each sensor requires 3 AG13 or LR44 button style batteries. If all 6 sensors are utilized you will need 18 batteries every 3 months or 72 batteries a year. Not only does this get expensive but it is a hassle staying on top of the batteries always dying.

For those interested in utilizing these sensors, I recommend the following batteries: Eunicell SR44W 303 357 Silver Oxide Button Cell 1.55V Battery Long Shelf Life 0% Mercury (https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07MMTG4ZF/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_7RB98F39642K4BXJ2Q2C) - while these are the same size and voltage they are made with better components and tend to last a bit longer and are far more consistent upon arrival.

After using these for 8 months I can say while these work and consistently sound when the sensors are separated there are far better options that use much more sophisticated, long lasting batteries. This is the type of product where you want a quality lithium ion battery that you can count on for many months or a year at a time - and ideally recharge it at that point.

After thoroughly testing this set I suggest looking into more sophisticated, sets that will cost slightly mor upfront but cost far less in the long run.

title: Incredible Budget Vari-Focal PoE Dome Camera!
text:
This review is for the Anpviz 5MP vari-focal 2.8~12mm PoE Dome Camera (IPC-D250G-4X).

I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

If you are new to home security camera systems, I recommend going with wired (non-WiFi), NVR or computer based recorders run with systems such as Blue Iris. This type of system is infinitely more secure and stable. While initial setup costs are a bit more the security it affords is worth every penny. It always pays to research the products, discuss them with those in the field, understand vulnerabilities and PLAN YOUR SYSTEM PRIOR TO PURCHASING ANYTHING. If you are at all tech savvy at all you can do it. While there is a bit of a learning curve it is not awful and in the end you will be thankful for the time you spent in the beginning as it will save you time, money and endless frustration.

I have set up, tested and reviewed more security systems and individual products than I can possibly remember. Without question my go to solution for home security solutions is a computer based, Blue Iris system with POE cameras run off of quality POE switches. This type of system is not only easy to operate but is highly secure.

As with any component there are a host of factors to consider. In terms of cameras more megapixels is not always better. For instance 2MP cameras often perform better in low light while 5MP will allow for more detail when lighting is good. One disadvantage of higher megapixel cameras is the recordings will take up more hard drive space. Depending on the number of cameras, this can become a larger concern.

When I saw this camera at this price point I knew it was something I needed to check out.

While the vast majority of cameras I test at this price point are disappointing I am pleased to say that was absolutely not the case with this gem of a camera.

First of all, let me point out this camera WILL NOT PAN NOR TILT. Where you position the lens is where it will remain. This means planning your installation location is very important. The ideal location for this camera is 8-12’ above ground. This will allow full use of the vari-focal lens (2.8~12mm vari-focal lens)
so you can capture both the wide angle and closeup images (4X zoom). When installing this type of camera I test different locations with it hooked up prior to install in order to decide on the optimal location.

I set this camera up on my Blue Iris system with no issues whatsoever and have had it in constant use for four months. I ran it via PoE router and everything has worked exactly as it should.

I use this as a secondary camera so after fully testing the capabilities I reduced the resolution to save on disc space and have found minimal image degradation. By using the H.265 high-efficiency coding you will save a lot of hard drive space while maintaining quality.

As with all dome style cameras night IR enhanced viewing can result in glare from the dome. I over come this by placing exterior light sources and not depending on the built in IR lighting which I have found produces far better image captures.

After four months of putting this camera through full testing, I can safely say this is an excellent camera at an amazing price. Without question I recommend buying it. This is dependable, easy to set up and use, made to last and an outstanding bargain.

While this camera is not natively a PoE camera I’m happy to share the 5 Pairs Passive PoE Injector and PoE Splitter Kit with 5.5x2.1 mm DC Connector RJ45 Power Over Ethernet by Exgoofit ( https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07F82YK6P/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 ) allow for this camera to operate almost identical to a PoE camera. The power adapter must be plugged in where the Ethernet cable is plugged in with the first pigtail adapter while the second adapter plugs onto the cameras power port and Ethernet jack. By utilizing this you can avoid the security concerns associated with WiFi cameras and still only have minimal wires run to the camera.

As with any component there are a host of factors to consider. In terms of cameras more megapixels is not always better. For instance 2MP cameras often perform better in low light while 5MP will allow for more detail when lighting is good. This camera is 2MP which is ideal for the vast majority of installation situations.

Highlights of this camera include:

Awesome Pan Tilt Zoom - Utilizing a 110° wide-angle varifocal lens and the head rotating 355° horizontally and 90° vertically, a 360° view is easily obtained. This makes this camera an outstanding choice to be placed on a corner of an eave where it can constantly monitor the largest possible area.

3.6mm Board lens - in my tests over the last couple of months I have been fairly impressed with the performance of this Fixed Focus 6mm lens coupled with the 1/2.8" Sony IMX307 CMOS with ICR image sensor. While this will not allow for near as clear zooming as a varifocal lens it is adequate in most circumstances.

Low Light Capability - this lens is decent in low light. Images are ok at low light, far better than the vast majority of similar cameras in this price range. IR lighting is dependable and nighttime / low light images are better than expected. My tests showed accurate images within 75’ of the IR lighting. By using both 4 IR lights and 4 bright LED lights this allows the camera to capture more details than many of the others on the market.

ONVIF Compatibility - critical for using with software such as Blue Iris. I have set it up with advanced features such as Patrol and Watchdog utilizing multiple detection zones.

2 Way Audio - I have had no issues utilizing the 2 way audio through Blue Iris - sound is accurate, clear and minimal lag.

Video Compression - This camera utilizes Smart 265/Smart 264/M-JPEG compression allowing for the smallest file sizes while maintaining the highest quality.

Great build quality - this camera is well built and will hold up outside in all conditions. That being said this is not a small camera in any way.

Over the course of my testing this product for the last several months I’ve been thoroughly impressed. It loads into Blue Iris without any issue and advanced features work without any trouble. By using the PoE splitter kit (referenced above) you can easily make this a secure camera by avoiding the use of WiFi. Build quality is excellent - this is made to last and hold up even in severe conditions.

This is a product I would definitely recommend. While this is the first ENSTER camera I have reviewed I look forward to seeing other cameras they create. All indications point to this being a manufacturer that builds high quality security cameras that are dependable and made to last.

title: Outstanding Extender for the Price
text:
I have tested and reviewed several WiFi extenders and this one works nearly as well as one that cost over six times as much and was far easier to set up.

I set this up simply using the WPS pairing method with the extender being plugged in next to my primary router. It paired perfectly in just over a minute and I was able to unplug it and move it to an outlet farther away where it would then repeat my signal for greater range into my shop in my back yard. This worked perfectly.

Here are a few tips for getting the most out of this or any similar device.

1. Understand this will only extend the coverage you already have. If you are not satisfied with your current speed when located close to your current router this type of device will not help. In this instance you will need to improve your internet service, modem or router.
2. An extender / repeater must be placed close enough to receive an optimal signal that it then repeats - if it is too far away, it can only transmit what it picks up - if this signal is weakened due to distance from your primary router the end result will be a reduced signal. It can only work with the signal it is receiving.
3. When placing any extender / repeater pay attention to what is between it and your primary router - keep in mind interior walls tend to not have insulation and are thus easier to penetrate than exterior walls, metal objects deflect signals more than other materials as do especially dense materials.
4. Optimally a primary router should be placed in a centralized location within a home and where the bulk of the time is spent. Extenders / repeaters can then be utilized between that and where you have found weak signal points.
5. In some instances, such as within Mesh WiFi networks extenders / repeaters can slow down the entire network and are thus not advised. A lot of this depends on advanced settings.

In all of my testing over the last 4 months I have found this to be an outstanding unit at frankly an unbeatable price.

This is definitely a product I recommend.

title: Outstanding PoE Injector for Long Runs
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

Like most people who understand security cameras and their vulnerabilities I completely avoid WiFi cameras on most installations. While they are much easier to set up they are also far more vulnerable to hacking and security breaches.

Most of the systems I build and setup utilize Blue Iris, PoE switches and cameras. While initially this may seem more complicated, in the end it really isn’t and the system is far more stable and customizable.

PoE injectors, such as this one by AD-Net, are the perfect solution for when a camera needs to be placed at a farther distance from your central hub.

I set this up a bit over 3 months ago to power a camera located approximately 750’ from where this box is plugged in. I make my own Ethernet cables for these types of runs using trueCABLE Cat6 Direct Burial ( https://www.amazon.com/dp/B07VPGDBKW/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_veE6FbZ3QK01F ) and pass through modular plugs ( https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0839DMK75/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_5yE6FbX7NDWNX ). I utilized the same wire to run between the master and slave and had excellent results. This is where primary loss will occur and thus is critical to use the highest quality wires if using this over a large distance.

Something that is important to understand when running PoE systems is “line loss” - this refers to the power lost along the run of cable. The longer the cable the more loss there will be. While this device is capable of delivering 16W it can not deliver that over a 800 meter (.49 mile) run. It is important to review the chart pictured in the listing to understand the drop in power and speed over distance.

I ran this to a fairly power hungry PTZ camera that constantly scans the area. As I mentioned I have tested this device for a bit over 3 months and it has performed without any issue. Even though this is powering a large PTZ varifocal camera, from well over 700’ away, that is constantly scanning I have never experienced any drop in power that caused it to pause or drag. While I wouldn’t describe this device as plug and play installation was not difficult. I have been thoroughly impressed by this PoE injector and highly recommended it.

Why do I wait a few months to write my review? I have found many products perform perfectly when first received, but within a couple of months they begin to glitch and have issues. Like most consumers, I find this incredibly frustrating as then it is typically beyond the return window and I’m left with another useless broken device. During my testing I really push the limits of each device, I have them run 24/7 and maximize their capabilities in order to discover if there are any inherent flaws. While this process is time consuming, I have found it is the best way to determine what products are utilizing inferior components and what products really are worth purchasing as they will hold up and perform as expected for the long term.

title: Excellent iPad Floor Stand but...
text:

I was looking for a floor stand that would support my iPad Pro where I could pull it to me when needed and then move it out of the way when I didn’t - based on the listing I thought this would be the perfect product.

While the design of this product is very good, clearly the manufacturer did not test it with the iPad Pro even though it is specifically marketed for it. The springs simply are not strong enough to support the weight of the Pro. It will work fine for iPhones or smaller tablets but if you intend on using this for an iPad Pro you will want to replace at least one of the manufacturer’s springs with a 7/16” x 1-1/2” extension spring. Here is what I used - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B008RFNRIW/ref=cm_sw_em_r_mt_dp_Pq.TFbC339YC7

If the correct springs were included this would be a solid 5 star item, as it is I give it a 3 and advise ordering the spring when purchasing the stand if you want to use this with your Pro.

title: Very Good Dummy Cameras with Excellent Motion Activated Floodlights
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential. When I’m discussing systems with people who are not familiar with the breadth of this technology, especially those on a tight budget, I always recommend making use of quality dummy cameras in addition to the real cameras.

To the casual observer, these dummy cameras look real - someone who is familiar with security cameras will easily pick it out as a dummy but for the vast majority of people this will not be the case.

What really makes these dummy cameras stand out from others is the solar powered nighttime red light and bright 800 lumen motion activated floodlights.

Any security camera configuration works best when each of the components works with the others to optimize performance. By setting these cameras as an initial trigger the lights will provide illumination for the real security camera so it doesn’t have to rely on infra red. By this product providing ample light the images the other security cameras in range capture will be far more crisp and clear.

These lights are easy to install and adjust so that the solar panel can absorb maximum sunlight. There are multiple adjustment points so the lights can be directed where most needed.

As with any solar powered product, there are some good tips to know:

* When placing each light make sure the panel is unobstructed from foliage so it can absorb the maximum energy from the daylight
* Every few months clean the solar panels with a moistened towel to remove any dirt or mildew - the panels tend to develop a film that diminishes their ability to absorb energy over time
* The rechargeable batteries that power these, and all solar lights, can typically be replaced without replacing the entire light. I have not opened this unit to see what batteries it uses as my set has worked flawlessly for the last couple of months. When the batteries no longer hold the solar charge I will attempt replacement.

So far I have loved these dummy cameras with motion activated floodlights. I highly recommend the set. It provides a deterrent both during the day and at night it will provide a bright light that can scare intruders away and provide better lighting for your other cameras. If performance changes I will update my review to reflect that.

title: Excellent Quality Camera at a GREAT Price
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

If you are new to home security camera systems, I recommend going with wired (non-WiFi), NVR or computer based recorders run with systems such as Blue Iris. This type of system is infinitely more secure and stable. While initial setup costs are a bit more the security it affords is worth every penny. It always pays to research the products, discuss them with those in the field, understand vulnerabilities and PLAN YOUR SYSTEM PRIOR TO PURCHASING ANYTHING. If you are at all tech savvy at all you can do it. While there is a bit of a learning curve it is not awful and in the end you will be thankful for the time you spent in the beginning as it will save you time, money and endless frustration.

I have set up, tested and reviewed more security systems and individual products than I can possibly remember. Without question my go to solution for home security solutions is a computer based, Blue Iris system with PoE cameras run off of quality PoE switches. This type of system is not only easy to operate but is highly secure.

While this camera is not natively a PoE camera I’m happy to share the 5 Pairs Passive PoE Injector and PoE Splitter Kit with 5.5x2.1 mm DC Connector RJ45 Power Over Ethernet by Exgoofit ( https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07F82YK6P/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o03_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1 ) allow for this camera to operate almost identical to a PoE camera. The power adapter must be plugged in where the Ethernet cable is plugged in with the first pigtail adapter while the second adapter plugs onto the cameras power port and Ethernet jack. By utilizing this you can avoid the security concerns associated with WiFi cameras and still only have minimal wires run to the camera.

As with any component there are a host of factors to consider. In terms of cameras more megapixels is not always better. For instance 2MP cameras often perform better in low light while 5MP will allow for more detail when lighting is good. One disadvantage of higher megapixel cameras is the recordings will take up more hard drive space. Depending on the number of cameras, this can become a larger concern.

Highlights of this camera include:

Awesome Pan Tilt Zoom - Utilizing a 110° wide-angle lens and the head rotating 330° horizontally and 90° vertically, a 360° view is easily obtained. This makes this camera an outstanding choice to be placed on a corner of an eave where it can constantly monitor the largest possible area.

Jide Tech lens 5MP - in my tests over the last couple of months I have been impressed with the performance of this lens coupled with the CMOS image sensor SONY IMX335 and the HiS3516 chipset. Obviously this will not allow for the zoom capabilities of a varifocal lens but in comparison to many other cameras in the marketplace the performance of this camera is very good.

Low Light Capability - Images are excellent at even low light, far better than most similar cameras in this price range. IR lighting is dependable and nighttime / low light images are better than expected. My tests showed accurate images within 25’ of the IR lighting.

ONVIF compatibility - critical for using with software such as Blue Iris. Interestingly, I noticed another reviewer mentioned this camera did not work with Blue Iris, that was absolutely not my experience. I have only used it with Blue Iris and it has worked flawlessly. I have set it up with advanced features such as Watchdog and utilized multiple detection zones.

2 Way Audio - I have had no issues utilizing the 2 way audio through Blue Iris - sound is accurate, clear and minimal lag.

Great build quality - this camera is well built and will hold up outside in all conditions

I’d like to thank Joanna who works support at YoLuke who did her best to always provide the highest level of customer service as I researched this camera and worked on this review. Knowing there is a quality customer service team behind the scenes of security camera products is always important and in my experience, I feel that has been the case.

Over the course of my testing this product for a couple of months I’ve been thoroughly impressed. It loads into Blue Iris without any issue and advanced features work without any problems. By using the PoE splitter kit I referenced above you can easily make this a secure camera by avoiding the use of WiFi. Build quality is excellent - this is made to last and hold up even in severe conditions.

This is a product I would definitely recommend. While this is the first YoLuke camera I have reviewed I look forward to seeing other cameras they create. All indications point to this being a manufacturer that makes high quality security cameras that are dependable and made to last.

title: VHS to Digital
text:
Finally I found a device that worked so I could plug my VHS tape player into my PC and use software to create digital files from our old tapes.

Even with this device I struggled and finally found the only way for audio to transfer was for me to toggle the switch on the side to 16:9 - theoretically this should have nothing to do with sound but in the 4:3 setting I have no sound transfer.

The single sheet of instructions are abysmal. Set up is relatively straightforward unless it doesn’t work. The first thing I would try is switching that toggle switch on the side.

If you are looking to transfer analog VHS tapes to digital using your PC, I recommend downloading OBS Studio (free software) via obsproject.

This device does get warm during use. Since I only used it for limited amounts of time for my specific purpose it wasn’t an issue. If this was to be used long term for connecting a game system to a TV I would question its longevity.

While this worked for my purposes it is a bit glitchy. I got it to work with time thankfully and was able to accomplish what I set out to do.

This is an ok product but not outstanding.

title: Disappointed - Completely Dead at 8 Weeks
text:
Initially when I received this HP MicroSD card I was impressed - speed was decent, price was great, it worked well. I formatted it in my computer, ran a few tests then installed it with a security camera.

For 3 weeks I had no issues, the card was written to and read from without issue. During week 4, I started noticing glitching. Initially I thought it could be the camera until I reviewed the recorded footage and it would freeze during playback - whether played through the camera or my computer. I reformatted and installed into the camera again.

Over the next several weeks the card became less and less reliable. It would record part of the time then freeze. Playback would freeze, play for 30 seconds then freeze again.

By week 8 this card completed froze and I could do nothing with it. It won’t format, read nor write. While the price is low on this product - you’ll get what you pay for here. Spend a little more and go with a reliable MicroSD card.

This is a perfect example of why I wait a few months of testing a product prior to writing my review. Most products will work right out of the package, but none of us like when products die immediately outside of the return window - and that’s exactly what you can expect from this card.

title: HARD NO on this CAMERA or ANYTHING by Evtevision!!!
text:
Security Warning: All devices from Xiongmai, a Chinese OEM who manufactures white-label video surveillance equipment, come with an always-on cloud feature called XMEye P2P cloud. This feature contains serious vulnerabilities that allow attacks on millions of devices, even ones that are behind firewalls.

Millions of security cameras, DVRs, and NVRs contain vulnerabilities that can allow a remote attacker to take over devices with little effort, security researchers have revealed recently.

All vulnerable devices have been manufactured by Hangzhou Xiongmai Technology Co., Ltd. (often referred to as Xiongmai), a Chinese company based in the city of Hangzhou.

End users won't be able to tell that they're using a hackable device because the company doesn't sell any products with its name on them, but ships all equipment as white label products on which other companies put their logo on top. Evtevision is one of said companies.

If the product description mentions anything about "XMEye," then despite the logo on the front of the device, the equipment was made by Xiongmai.

As you can see in the third bulleted point at the top of the listing:

“Easy view on Smartphone via Xmeye, PC tablet via CMS,and Web browser IE.”

This is, without question, a Xiongmai device. Installing it or any of its software would place the privacy and security of you and your family in serious jeopardy.

Most security companies have banned selling these types of cameras for the reasons I have explained.

As soon as I opened this camera and started examining it I recognized some telltale signs and therefore did not set this up on my network. I caution everyone to avoid these products completely.

title: Quality Budget Friendly Optical Zoom Blue Iris Camera
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential.

As with all security systems my advice is never use cloud based recording - this opens your entire network to not only the company who you are giving blanket access too but also to hackers. The same is true for WiFi. Obviously WiFi is more convenient but if your privacy is a concern this really needs to be taken into account. Hackers have become quite adept at hacking into WiFi cameras and being able to not only watch your feed but control your cameras and access your entire network. If you choose to utilize WiFi cameras take the time to understand your router and employ proper VPN protocols.

Due to my security concerns with WiFi cameras my current security system is completely run through a dedicated computer utilizing the Blue Iris software. While this may seem intimidating to some, it is well worth learning and utilizing for the huge advantages in privacy and security.

I’ve noticed many people have asked if this camera works with a Blue Iris and it does without any issue. Just update to the latest firmware. The remainder of setup within Blue Iris is straightforward. The RLC-522 supports PoE 802.3af and will work with 48V active adapters which are more expensive, but you can also rely on a PoE switch, which in my opinion is a much easier, straightforward option. Something to note, if you plan on powering via a DC cable this is not included.

The varifocal lens is a major feature that sets this camera apart from others. With an adjustable lens size of 2.8-8mm the optical zoom is excellent in comparison to digital zoom where pixels are simply enlarged. This will allow for this camera to be hung higher giving a better over view shot of an area while still being able to zoom in. The 1/2.7” CMOS image sensor is decent in low light, certainly not as good as 1/1.8” but I’ve found the low light capabilities strong in comparison to many similar cameras. The 18 IR LEDs do a decent job of illuminating objects in the fore and mid ground areas.

The camera has a built in microphone that allows for sound recording, though no speaker so two way communication will not be possible with this unit.

Unlike many similar cameras a mount is not required to be purchased separately. Mounting is fairly simple although care must be taken to mount so your lens is ultimately pointed in the direction you want as this camera does not pan nor tilt.

The varifocal zoom is not particularly fast so if you were trying to zoom in on action, such as a moving vehicle as it passed, you will likely miss it. Although if you have an area you want to focus on for a period of time it works fine.

In terms of storage, the RCL-522 utilizes H.264 rather than H.265 which will require more space to record the same data. Storage options include a MicroSD card slot with support up to 64GB - which I find lacking, cloud storage via FTP, the propriety Reolink NVR systems, or as I use set ups utilizing software such as Blue Iris.

When all things are taken into account this is a very solidly build varifocal camera, suited to outdoor environments, decent daytime / nighttime resolution, fairly easily mounted, and setup in Blue Iris was easy and straightforward. While I would prefer to have pan and tilt capabilities at this price point that is unrealistic. Overall I have been quite impressed with this camera and would recommend it for many security situations.

title: ABSURD PRIVACY AGREEMENT GIVES VICOO ALL RIGHTS TO YOUR RECORDINGS
text:

The app “Vicoo” has the most absurd privacy terms you will see on any security camera app. To be clear, I tested this with a phone I do not use on a network I temporarily set up for only testing this and after testing I completely wiped the phone and removed the network.

To summarize the privacy terms YOU MUST AGREE TOO (the fine print most people skip to the bottom of and hit Agree) you MUST give this company COMPLETE ACESS TO ALL OF YOUR VIDEO CONTENT.

“with respect to Content (including all related intellectual property rights) you submit or make available for the Vicoo Services, you grant Vicoo the following worldwide, royalty-free, nonexclusive, perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable and transferable license(s), as applicable: the license to use, distribute, reproduce, modify, adapt, make derivative works of, publicly perform and publicly display such Content on the Vicoo Services solely in connection with providing you the Vicoo Services, as permitted through the functionality of the Vicoo Services and under these Terms. If this doesn’t give you enough of a reason to not purchase this product or anything that uses this app read on...

If you want to use any of the primary features of the app, AI, alerts, etc YOU MUST SUBSCRIBE.

In my tests battery life was subpar with similar cameras although video quality was adequate. Due to the nature of the security issues with the app I was unwilling to leave it hooked up long enough to do my full battery of tests which require over a month of use.

title: Decent BUDGET Security System - with Absolutely Atrocious Software
text:
I have been working with security camera products for over 20 years - over that time I have installed systems for businesses, corporations and individuals - from enormous multimillion dollar systems to single camera nursery monitors. I’ve consulted on large projects and written about security vulnerabilities within networks for trade publications.

This is a field I know well. Over the years the technology has improved and become less and less expensive to produce. It is now practical to install security systems that would have only previously been used in commercial settings in residential. Unfortunately while the hardware has improved dramatically the software often has not - which is the case with this set.

The set I got did not come with a hard drive which wasn’t a big deal as I always have a few around. A suitable SATA Hard Drive can be purchased for $25-$400 depending on size and quality.

In terms of this system it should be clear based on the price - this is a budget system. That doesn’t mean it won’t work but these cameras are not going to pan, tilt or zoom (the lens is fixed).

If these are installed with this in mind they can still be very effective they just need to be positioned correctly.

For instance if these cameras were placed up high on a second floor overhang you would see an overview of the surrounding area but would not be able to zoom in to see facial characteristics. On the other hand, if placed on a porch a bit above head height you will have no issue making out the same. Placement is key.

In terms of wiring any POE (Power Over Ethernet) camera is excellent. The cameras are powered and transmit data over the same Ethernet cable. There are several advantages to these systems the most important is security as the cameras are not broadcasting wirelessly making them more difficult to hack.

The camera operation is excellent for the price. The images are clear and crisp and night vision operates without issue.

Where this set falls apart is on the software side - unfortunately this is often the case. The software is so non user friendly that it is almost unusable. I have used countless similar systems and this has to be among the all time worst software operating systems I have ever encountered.

There are countless glitches and bizarre, nonsensical methods for how it has to be initiated that it became comical as I worked through them all. I’ve actually used it as an example with colleagues as why a system must be actually set up prior to recommending it as on its face this appears to be an excellent value but the software unfortunately ruins what otherwise would be an excellent budget system. Unfortunately one depends on the other.

Due to the horrid software this set depends upon I would not recommend it. I can only hope the manufacturer would scrap the current software completely and rebuild with modern usability standards being their primary concern.

I have used and tested more Ethernet cables than I can remember and there is no question, all Ethernet cables are not created equally.

Typically any device requiring an Ethernet cable will come with one in the packaging - it will work (usually). A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without fail.

This Cat8 is designed to be thin, but don’t let that fool you into thinking that it lacks capacity - within the thin rubber coated shell, contains the needed shielding and wires for super fast transfer speeds. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

I used this 2 meter to run from my router to my computer - a primary connection where speed and a reliable relay is critical - and I’ve been nothing but impressed by this product.

You will not find a better Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love. This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

title: AWESOME ETHERNET SWITCH AND POWER SUPPLY!
text:
This small, silent, unmanaged 1000 Mbps Ethernet switch has 8 super fast ports that not only provide high speed internet but automatically detect if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last couple of months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in PSE Chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide super fast internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage doing it this way as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

title: Solid, Steady Connection but Not Great Speed
text:
In terms of convenience, this is an outstanding product. It literally is plug and play. Just plug the transmitter in near you router and plug the Ethernet cable into an open port. Plug the receiver where you need the signal press the button on each device and setup is about complete. I had zero issues in terms of connection.

The farther the distance you span and the more walls and obstacles between, the slower the resultant signal will be. I tested the unit in a multitude of locations and I always received a signal, although it dropped the farther away I moved.

The point of this device is to use in locations where it is not possible, or where it would be difficult to run an Ethernet cable. If you are in a position where you need to get a signal to a TV to stream programming this would be a great choice. I tested it with Hulu, Prime and Netflix and it worked great. Depending on distance spanned and the strength of your original signal it probably would be adequate for internet use. However I can not recommend this as a viable option for gaming.

This set will definitely fulfill many people’s needs. It is just important to consider your use in relation to the WiFi product you install. For my family this worked fairly well.

title: Decent Product for Appropriate Location
text:
I have had the opportunity to test and review several of these TV antenna sets over the last several years and I have been amazed by the advances in the technology.

While a few years ago the only way possible to receive decent signals in my particular location was to have a roof mounted antenna. Thankfully as technology has advanced that has become less necessary, but we are not yet to a point where topography is not an issue.

The 120 miles listed in the product listing on this item may be accurate but I can only assume that would be in a perfectly flat area with few obstructions. In my testing the area was around half that listed. Broadcasts beyond approximately 45 miles suffered loss in quality with those over 60 being severe.

This is a decent antenna system especially at this price point. For those living in relatively flat areas and where broadcasts are within a 60 mile radius this will be an outstanding product.

title: MINIMAL BULK allowing for INCREDIBLE PRODUCTIVITY with MAXIMUM PROTECTION!
text:
I have tested a few cases for my 10.5” iPad Pro and my iPro prior to that - I have found each case to have significant design flaws. Many are far too bulky which, while protecting the iPad, takes away from the inherent charm of it being a lightweight device to grab and go. Other cases I found would simply not stay attached, either the backing attached to the rear of the iPad or the keyboard cover would always be coming off. In testing this product by GreenLaw I have found that to absolutely not be the case - in fact, I have found after using the keyboard for a while it has functions that save me time far beyond just typing and protection!

As I stated, I’m using this with my A1709, 10.5” iPad Pro. It fits absolutely perfectly. While the set comes with foam feet that can be placed as bumpers if the case was a bit too loose in order to snug it tight, this was not necessary with my iPad.

I followed the directions and charged the case by plugging it in with the included micro USB cable for 4 hours prior to using it for the first time. Once it achieved charging its battery fully - the LED battery indication light changed from red to green, I unplugged the the case and moved on to pairing.

The pairing process could not have been easier. I just put my iPad in Bluetooth mode, turned the case on via the small switch on the right side of the keyboard and pressed function + delete (all instructions are well written in the manual) and it paired on the first attempt.

There are loads of helpful functions this keyboard can do once you start working on it. I tend to discover something new every few times using it even now. As is obvious by the listing, the keys can be backlit, although this will greatly diminish the battery life of the keyboard. It can be helpful in certain lighting but I typically leave it off. With the backlighting off this keyboard’s battery lasts a very long time.

Not only is the keyboard outstanding but this is an excellent case for the iPad! It doesn’t add a lot of bulk nor weight yet the hard plastic case and the rigidity of the keyboard laying over the glass of the iPad’s screen provide perfect security and protection keeping the iPad safe.

This is both an outstanding keyboard and an amazing case. I have thoroughly enjoyed mine and am sure you will as well.

title: Awesome Concept - Execution Needs Fine-Tuning
text:
Being both an audiophile and a lover of all new tech when I first read about this technology coming out a few years ago I started looking forward to testing it.

So what are the potential advantages of bone conduction earphones? I’m glad you asked. When properly adjusted they allow the user to enjoy listening to whatever they choose while not blocking external noises, thus allowing the user to react to ambient noises. This should make them safe to use while driving or doing other activities that require hearing ambient noise in order to conduct safely.

Unfortunately these R9 headphones allow for very little fine adjustment. In order for this type of headphones to work properly and provide the highest sound quality they should rest flat, or almost flat against the skin between the front of the ear and the rear part of the cheek bone. When adjusting the speaker it is clear when the speaker is properly adjusted. The adjustment that I was able to do came from working the rubber casing and sliding the speaker further onto the arm that wraps around the back of the head. By twisting the speaker inward I was able to get the speaker closer to the proper location but not exactly correct. Due to this, sound quality is not optimal and surrounding people are able to hear what the listener is playing.

In terms of design choices I find it odd that while it’s estimated between 70-95% of the population of any ethnicity is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the controls on the left side. This makes controlling them both awkward and difficult. While the buttons operate in a standard press and double press pattern it is awkward reaching across and doing it on the left side.

In terms of operation these headphones maintain a solid connection for the full 33 feet they are rated for and the batteries lasted approximately 6.25 hours on the first full charge cycle. Sound quality is middle of the road especially due to not allowing for fine adjusting of the speakers.

With a couple of minor changes these headphones would be a much better product. If the speakers are held in the correct positions it is much better - if an adjustment system were added these could potentially have much higher sound quality. In addition, obviously the controls should be placed on the right side for ease and regularity of access.

This is a great technology with a lot of potential. These headphones while not capable of fine adjustments would probably fit someone with an average sized head better. My head is a bit smaller than average which made these fit a bit too large for me.

title: MUCH GREATER CAPACITY THAN I  INITIALLY ANTICIPATED
text:
I have had the opportunity to review several products produced by WindTook and each of them have been well designed, manufactured from high grade materials with an excellent level of craftsmanship. This backpack fit that pattern in every regard.

While at first glance I didn’t think this backpack was going to be very large, once I began filling it in order to test I was amazed at all it could securely hold.

The outer shell of the backpack is constructed with 600D Polyester making it water resistant, very durable and easy to keep clean. There are dual mesh side pockets for holding a water bottle, umbrella or anything moist. Every pocket securely closes with zippers that are well made and have an 2” pull on each closure. All inner pockets are lined with a high quality polyester material. The bottom of the pack is protected by a polyvinyl covering. The right side has a built in charging USB charging port with a zippered pocket large enough to securely hold my largest power supply.

The back of the pack where the straps attach has as much padding as I’ve ever seen on similar bags - the padding measured it at approximately 1/2” thick. While this padding is thick it is designed to include ventilation so that is doesn’t cause a build up of heat while wearing. The center of the back area has an attached strap so the pack can be looped over the handle of a suitcase for ease of carrying when traveling.

The outer most pocket, on the front of the pack, measures 6” x 8”, is the perfect size for storing a wallet, keys, glasses or anything easy access is desired. The following pocket is designed for storing basic writing utensils - 3 locations for pens, a place for a calculator, a large sleeved area and a secured zippered area.

The 2 large zippered storage areas are what surprised me the most. The one at the center of the bag is padded on both sides, has dual sleeves for sliding a tablet or small computer down in either side, and the front side has a small 5” x 7” zippered pocket at the top to secure small items. This center area is deceptively large, I found I could fit far more than I anticipated as it expands allowing for additional space.

The rear most pocket is designed primarily for a laptop having additional padding on either side. I was able to slide my laptop in and out with no problem and it was secure while being carried.

I reviewed the 6351-Blue model this time. The blue material appears very similar to blue jean material in color while the inner teal provides a nice contrast. These colors are gender neutral, look nice together and should appeal to many.

This is a high quality backpack that will hold up well in use regardless of what you have in mind. It will be an excellent bag for school, overnights away or for traveling. This is a product I would recommend made by an excellent company.

title: HDMI - Highly Disappointing Misrepresented Item? You be the judge...
text:

title: Small, Unobtrusive, Motion Sensor
text:

title: EXCELLENT BUDGET PRICED ROUTER
text:

In an effort to not make this overly confusing and router will not replace the need for paying for internet service this only broadcasts the internet you pay for throughout your home so you can access it. Many people pay their ISP (internet service provider) for high speed internet and then have a router that can not utilize the speed they pay for each month - so it is wasted and they are left wondering why the internet speeds are so slow.

Depending on your internet usage characteristics and the size of your home this router may be a perfect option. After running full diagnostics on this unit I found that it performs well, especially at this price point. This is a great router for smaller homes with one primary user who does not utilize multiple SmartHome products.

I had no issues with setup and installation. I found the iOS app worked adequately. This router does not have many of the advanced features of other routers but at around a tenth the cost that’s to be expected.

For the appropriate homes and users this is a perfect solution for an economical router.
