text: This is a HEAVY DUTY wall mount. We are using it for our new 55" TV, so I didn't want to take any chances with a less hefty unit. The directions were clear and concise. We went directly into wall studs and from start to finish my husband had this "honey-do" checked off his list in about a half hour. The arm stretches out about 10" and you are able to swing TV left and right for optimum position!

title: What an ingenious invention. I love it!!!
text: Product was so simple to use. Right out of the box! I put the enclosed little sticky magnet on my phone and attached it to the enclosed base, which is also magnetic, all on my fridge. My phone is now elevated off counter. Everything looks neat and clean and I can access my phone at eye level now. No more, "oops that water spilled on my counter and got my phone soaked"  and no more counter clutter. Simple, clean design. Very easy to set up! Love it!

title: poor quality
text: Broke after my 8 year old wore them once.

title: The monitor looks great, sounds good, is portable  & can be powered by my laptop with 1 cable
text:
The monitor looks great & is very portable. I don't game so I'm not an expert on lag but I don't notice any in day to day use. I do travel for work & work from multiple locations & this has been wonderful for setting up a 2nd screen. It works best when plugged into the A/C power adapter but it can be powered from my laptop from a single USB-C cable that also provides the video source.

It is very thin with the stand/cover so it easily fits in my laptop backpack. The packaging it shipped in is nice & sturdy & has a lot of foam which made me question whether I should be unceremoniously chucking it in my backpack but it hasn't been damaged. The screen & case stand do weigh a little over 3lbs so the addition to my backpack is noticeable.

The case/stand was a little confusing to put on but it works great. The surface is grippy enough to tilt the monitor all the way to the edge. The speakers are about like laptop speakers in volume but lack low end.

title: Good picture if set up correctly & in a dim room. I couldn't get all of the inputs to work.
text:
The biggest difference between this projector & the much more expensive projectors in professional settings is the bulb. This one does a fine job in low light or with back light but will completely wash out with light around or over the screen. I ordered this primarily to do presentations & show videos at my club meetings. It performed well but we did have to fiddle a bit with the lights in the room & the position of the projector.

The usefulness of this projector is its portability & low cost. It is lightweight & compact & fairly easy to set up. I would have appreciated a padded carry case for the projector but the box it comes in works pretty well. It has foam that surrounds the projector, it holds all the cords, it has a handle & it is easily sturdy enough to set the projector on for more height.

It helps a lot with the focus & clarity if the projector is nearly horizontal. That means that if the projection screen is to be 4' over the ground then the projector also needs to be 4' off the ground which is generally going to be much higher than a table. The focus ring around the lens works very well to dial in the clarity. There is a foot that unscrews from the bottom front to angle the projector up. I tried propping something under the front to angle it higher but the image distorts & loses clarity the more it is tilted.

The biggest issue I have had with the projector is the image source. I can't get either of my laptop computers to recognize the projector as an external screen with the HDMI cable but the HDMI works on a DVD player. The IOS control works pretty well with my iPad. My Pixel phone doesn't support the built-in Miracast. The Bluetooth only recognizes my Samsung TV & none of my phones, computers or tablets sees the projector's Bluetooth signal. It has a YouTube app built into the device software but it is un-useable due to a cumbersome search process that doesn't return any results. I ended up using it with a USB thumb drive which works well & the menu is easy enough to navigate but takes some learning. I did not try the AV cable inputs or the SD memory slot.

title: Very strong magnets & all metal construction, much easier than using the plastic clips
text:
I like this magnetic mount a lot. Not only are the magnets very strong but the metal base plate is also heavy enough to put the camera at an angle without it tipping over even when it isn't on metal. I've been using it in my shop to record projects & it easily slaps on to my tool boxes, cars or motorcycle tanks & frames & holds well enough to adjust the camera. The metal plate has a very thin plastic coating on the bottom so it doesn't scratch paint.
The it comes with a nice, aluminum thumb tightener. The mount is all metal so it takes a bit of force to squeeze the metal plates to the plastic adapters. The kit also comes with a wrench to give some more leverage on the tightener but I haven't needed it.
The kit also comes with 4 metal plates & genuine 3m double sided tape so a magnetic surface can be added to a non-magnetic one. Using the metal plates & the magnet mount is so much easier than using the plastic clip mounts & installing or removing the camera doesn't stress the tape's adhesion. I added one to the dash of my truck so I can use my old GoPro as a dash cam & it's as simple as setting the camera on the plate.

title: Good options for securing airtags, the spring-gate rings are handy for swapping the tags
text:
The leatherette is very plastic feeling but I like the looks of them. They remind me of those '80s keychains with the car emblem attached. The clear, bubble type completely surround the tag & provide full protection from liquid or abrasion. Both styles hold the tag securely but the tag will get scratched up pretty quickly in the leatherette ones. The tags come with spring-gate rings which make them very easy to swap around.
We just got airtags & still aren't sure where to put them or to which devices to connect them for best results. This kit worked well having 2 different styles. My daughter used one leatherette holder on her keys & one of the plastic bubbles inside her backpack. I acted similarly & put & bubble holder inside my motorcycle & used the other leatherette holder on a key chain that has the one & only key for one of our vehicles.

title: Works well, has 3 outlets & 3 USB ports. I should have gotten a longer cord though
text: I ordered this power cord for my father in law's new assisted living room where the outlet is in the middle of the space where we put the couch. The cord provides 3 120V outlets & 3 USB ports to charge his computer,  phone & accessories without a bunch of cords. We didn't need the on/off switch at the power end but I like that it's a memory switch & not a rocker like most power strips. I thought that the 5' cord would be plenty to reach the window sill but it barely reaches so I am going to add some adhesives to make sure it stays put.

title: Works as advertised & setup was very easy, no app required
text:
I had this set up & working in a few minutes. Everything was through my phone's wifi & browser, I didn't have to download any apps or create a new account or password (except the password for the new wifi signal). My goal was to extend my wifi to a pool house that is about 100' from the nearest repeater. After installing this extender I was able to stream to a Fire Stick through 2 exterior walls & inside the pool house seamlessly
The extender has a light that is blue when the feed signal is strong & red when it is weak. I placed the extender a little over halfway to the pool house & even though the light is red, I had no trouble streaming. The extender also has a WPS setup that I didn't use.
The last wifi extender I had was a large tombstone style that had a wall adapter & cord & took up space. precious horizontal space This one is so compact & well laid out that it just hangs on the outlet & even leaves the other plug available.

title: Good sound, very good microphone, very good noise cancellation, always connect to each other
text:
These look different but they are comfortable & stay put, I guess earbud design is not a settled issue yet. I have been using these primarily for voice calls & listening to music on my computer in a very noisy warehouse where noise cancellation is paramount.
I have pretty much made these my 'computer' earbuds because the microphone is so good & the volume can be loud. The music sounds good but isn't especially dynamic. There is no volume control at the earbud but they will start/pause & answer calls with touch. They will also answer a call by double-touching the button.
I like the voice confirmation when turning on & off the noise cancellation. Instead of just different tones a voice says "active noise cancellation on/off" or "talk through mode" (it gets loud in the warehouse & I couldn't always be sure if the cancellation was on with my other earbuds). These default to no noise cancellation when they are turned off by putting them in the charge case which I do not like.
Pairing was easy & the two earbuds have never failed to connect to each other which is something I can't say about any other Bluetooth set I have used.

title: No computer required, very easy to use, captures sound & video from a player & saves directly to MP4
text:
[[VIDEOID:c19caf51ed5645772d7b1a0a5834b6d6]] The Soundbeast video capture device couldn't be easier to use. I have been wanting to make files from some old tapes & DVD's I recorded over the years but I dreaded using the computer. This device is so much easier to use & also doesn't tie up my computer. It simply plugs into a DVD player, VCR or even a camcorder with RCA type plugs & records to MP4 in real time. The device even has a tiny little screen & a tinny speaker so I don't even have to use a monitor to see & hear what is recording. It does have an HDMI output (not an input) to run a monitor directly from the device but I have just been hooking a TV to the DVD player while it plays.
The capture device records MP4s directly to either a USB drive or a micro SD card. I have only been using it with the USB stick. The little speaker sounds bad but the little screen has surprisingly good resolution. I have used it connected to the DVD player & a camcorder. It also converts purchased DVDs in my experience.

title: Comfortable, wireless mouse with some basic & some newer features.
text:
I ordered this mouse for my wife to use with her new Chromebook & she loves it. She likes the large, domed style with the thumb relief & hasn't been happy since her old Microsoft mouse died. It has more buttons than I know how to use (forward & back on the thumb side). I'm not sure if she even uses the thumbwheel but it is large, grippy & rolls smooth with light detents. We have been using it on a finished wood table & it moves smoothly & doesn't have any issues with the laser reading. The mouse requires the included USB, receiver dongle which stores in the bottom of the mouse & is easy to swap between computers.
I had to look up what the CPI adjustment button is but it is pretty handy in that the speed of the mouse can be adjusted from just the button on top. The mouse takes a single 'AA' battery. I prefer my rechargeable mouse but this is better for her.

title: Digital sound is great, the ends clip into ports well & hold tight, right angle end helps save space
text:
I'm getting very great sounding, digital, Dolby sound through this cable. The right angle connection reduces the depth of the cable behind my receiver but it still sticks out further than I expected. The connectors clip into the ports pretty well, I have moved the receiver around a bunch since adding the cable & it hasn't pulled out. I ordered the 10' cord & needed all of it for my ceiling mounted television installation.
I have never used optical sound cables before but the receiver I picked up used did not have HDMI. My inexperience with these was readily apparent when I couldn't get the plugs to stay in the sockets on the components. I finally discovered that there are tiny, protective caps over the optical input/output.
The right angle connector doesn't fit quite as close as I imagined but it does make a difference in getting the cable behind my receiver on the shelf. The cable blocks whatever connections are below it but that wasn't an issue for my setup. That said, I don't understand why these connections have to be indexed at all if it is just the light going through the center it shouldn't matter what angle it comes in.

title: Simple & versatile, use with or without dongle, rechargeable battery
text:
This very simple & versatile mouse is perfect for me. I like this low profile design both for how it fits my fingers & how it easily slips into pockets in my bag. The mouse has simple controls, left & right button, a grippy scroll wheel & a button that goes to the desktop which I love but haven't gotten used to using yet. There is another button on top that controls a light ring around the mouse that changes color but I prefer to not use the light. The top of the mouse has a slight texture like a smooth, grippy rubber coat. I'm not sure how to describe it.
The mouse comes with a dongle that can plug into any computer but it will also sync directly to a Bluetooth 3.0 device. There is a switch on the bottom to choose between the 2 so it could easily alternate between devices. There is a storage space in the bottom to store the dongle.
The mouse also has a rechargeable battery with a USB-C charge port. I'm not sure yet how long the battery lasts but I have been using it for 2 weeks now on it's original charge.

title: Low profile plug, compact, well thought out design
text: I mostly wanted a power splitter with a flat cord that exits toward the ground plug so that it would fit between my TV & fireplace mantle that has a recessed outlet. This outlet fit the bill perfectly but I also appreciate the external mounting lugs, the non-lighted power switch on the cord side, the included cord wrap & the well-spaced, opposite facing plugs. This only has 3 plugs & I'm using all of them to power the TV, satellite receiver & occasionally a Blu-ray player. I did have an adapter for my fire stick but I plugged that into one of the 3 USB ports & ditched the adapter. My wife hates seeing cords so I go through a lot of effort to getting everything tucked in & this splitter fits nicely.

title: Magnets are super handy for toolbox cable management
text:
I don't know how many people are going to find this as useful but for those few of us who work on a steel workbench this is perfect. Cable management is difficult for me especially when switching between devices. The magnets keep this table tight on my bench & it stays there when I unplug to move the ipad.
The magnets are plenty strong to keep the cable in place & even wrangle some other cables but they aren't so powerful that they wont slide or pull away with a little tug. I thought they might be good for keeping the cable coiled in a bag but they are lined up in such a way that the cable has to be stacked instead of coiling it flat.
I didn't have any issues with charging or data transfer. The cable is housed in a rubber sleeve & the magnets go between the sleeves. The only long-term concern I have is that the sleeve & magnet at the USB end are very close to the USB plug & it could cause strain on the internal wires if it is bent at too tight of an angle.

title: Good image quality & features with small size, portability & strong mount. No battery.
text:
[[VIDEOID:9b88dadfbf58bb503f1928922845b685]] I ordered this dash camera after stumbling across a dash-cam video on the internet & realized I could potentially save myself a lot of hassle either in an accident or even a police encounter. I had one a few years ago when I had a long commute but these days I do most of my driving in rental cars & in unfamiliar areas I wanted something small, portable & quick to install. This camera just takes a second to stick to the windshield with the suction mount & it takes a mini USB plug for power. It comes with a 12V port adapter with a very long cord but I mostly power it with a short USB cord & my own adapter.
I'm very pleased with the video quality & sound. I have tested it with 1080p30 1020x1080 & 720P60 1280x720. Given the long record time with the included 32gb memory I will probably keep it at 1080p. The microphone picks up the sound of the turn signal switch which is good & also my singing to the radio which is bad.
I don't know how well the video resolution will come across in the attached video but I'm impressed with the image I get on my computer, especially files made at night. In reviewing the videos taken at 1080p (& with my filthy windshields), I have to be right behind car to make out its license plate. I have since maxed out the resolution to 1440P because of this but I'm not sure it made that much difference. The wide angle also tends to make things look further away than they are, the car in the last clip was much closer to my car than it looks in the video.
The included 32gb memory card holds over 4 hours of video at 1080p30 1020x1080 resolution & that's day & night. The camera will over-write files that aren't saved & it has a "save" button that stores files where they won't be over-written. The software also has an adjustable feature that automatically saves files where an impact is detected. In the 2 cars I have used it, a big pothole or bump in the road will trigger an incident on the medium setting (see my video). The camera will also take still a still picture when the impact detection is triggered or the file is selected for saving.
The camera doesn't have it's own battery but so far it has managed to save the last file if the car shuts off the 12v port or usb when the key goes off. I have mine to record short, 5 minute clips as a precaution against this, The clip length is adjustable up to 10 minutes. Without the battery, won't record any activity when the car is parked even if the car is bumped if the cord is not plugged into an active port.

title: Gorgeous picture & fantastic Surround-Sound experience, intuitive Google home screen & 4 HDMI inputs
text:
This set has a gorgeous picture & great sound from the internal speakers. I didn't touch a single setting on the picture. I added 3 new sets to our new house this year & this is the only set that I didn't bother to disable the motion smoothing (soap opera effect) because I rarely notice it on this Sony set. Even up close or off to the sides the picture looks great & crisp though I have noticed occasional pixilated darks. I had this a few feet away from my 70" LED set when I was setting it up & everyone still ended up looking at this one.

Like I mentioned before the sound is fantastic for just using internal speakers that are not visible. It has an auto calibration to focus the sound to the seating position of the viewer. It just takes a second & is easy to get to in the menu so it's worth changing if the set or viewer position changes. My wife walked in while I had a movie on & she thought it had been connected to surround sound. It can sound weird if standing close & to the side (or especially behind) rather than in the calibrated area. I didn't try the TV with a wall mount. It would probably sound better with a close wall & ceiling to bounce the sound off.

Setup was very easy with the menu. I don't have the google home app on my phone so I logged into everything through the TV. Somehow it already knew my Netflix login & password. The remote has convenient "hot" buttons for YouTube, Netflix, Disney+ & prime video. There are a bunch of the usual privacy policies to work through, I think the only thing I opted out of was "marketing"

The set has 4 HDMI ports with one being eARC/ARC for sound out & two being 4K inputs. All of the inputs are on the left side, in a recessed area & everything plugs from the side. It's a small detail but it shows a well thought out design that allows for cable changes without having to move the TV which is especially helpful for wall mount situations & the cables don't have to bend awkwardly. It has a COAX input but no RCA type component connections.

The 2 provided USB ports are 500 & 900MA output respectively. Both of them have enough power to run my Fire Stick which is nice because my other TV's won't.

The base menu is Google TV, which is a first for me. It's a little unnerving how well the predictions & preferences are catered to me compared to other services that just show whatever is new or popular but it's also convenient. The home screen does a scary-good job of picking movies for me, seemingly based on my YouTube history. I wish I could opt out of channels to which I don't subscribe but I like that it shows prices on the screen for movies that aren't free.

The apps feature is weak. It has a dozens of apps but it won't search outside of that list. I tried to use the "Search for apps" but when I put in something that wasn't on the list it told me "I can't do that yet". The "Recommended for you" selection included apps like "UFC" & hockey so it certainly wasn't at all tuned to my interests unlike the movie guide on the home page. It also recommends apps from my other devices even a photo app that I don't think I even have on my current phone.

The remote is large & very similar to my other Sony but it works better. I like the more simplified remote that came with my Samsung TV & Fire stick but I was able to set this it up to control my Satellite TV receiver & now the size bothers me less. The number pad & superfluous play controls are now useful for selecting channels & controlling the DVR. The remote also controls my Fire stick somehow without any input or setup from me.

After much hand wringing I decided not to deduct an entire point for it because it seems harsh (& will hopefully be corrected) but the Netflix app crashes every 5-20 minutes. The app works just fine on my other SONY TV & on the Fire stick plugged into this one but the app on the TV consistently crashes. I had planned on my in-laws using this set because it is otherwise perfect for them but they use Netflix a lot & don't need the frustration.

title: Great mount for adjustments, lots of mounting options, very stable with the TV attached
text:
I just got finished mounting a 65" Sony television to my brick chimney with this kit. I love how much adjustment there is with this mount once it is up. It is easy to pull the set away from the wall & also turn it to the sides. The tilt angle is also adjustable but requires hand-loosening & then tightening a couple of fasteners. There are 2 height positions for the TV that are pretty easy to change &, at least with my Sony, more room for adjustments based on how the brackets attach to the TV.
The instructions for this mount are pretty good but there is a lot of measuring, math & test fitting involved in setting up the height which isn't addressed in the instructions. The kit comes with a variety of hardware options & even comes with a small, magnetic level to help position the mount, an HDMI cable & some cable organizers.
The only issue I had was concerning mounting to the brick chimney. There are a variety of holes laterally for different stud spacing but only two sets vertically. The vertical spacing was not to my liking because it pushed the mounting holes too close to the edge of the bricks. I was also a bit weary of the plastic inserts to mount to brick or concrete walls instead of the metal expanders but the screws bit hard and gave a good, tight feel when they were snugged.
Now I just need to sort out those wires.

title: Easy plug & play installation for Zoom calls, great resolution & microphone
text:
This camera was absolute plug & play. Within a couple of minutes it was recognized by my computer & discoverable by Zoom as a camera & microphone. The camera is better than the one on my computer & I was surprised how much more distinct it made my freckles. I tested the HD but didn't use it, mostly because of the freckles. The microphone seems to work well. I can't hear it of course but I haven't received any complaints during the many calls I have used it.
My work has been using ZOOM & other platforms for the past few months but there is a push to turn on the cameras to show that the attendees are engaged. So I shaved & started using the camera on my laptop but it always showed me looking up at my monitor behind the laptop. I clipped this onto the top of my monitor & all is well.
The camera has a clamp built in but it doesn't hold all that tight. It hooks on more than it clamps. It does have a 1/4" threaded insert so it can be mounted to a tripod. I didn't download the recommended software because I'll only use it for these calls & it is working perfectly.

title: Works well enough but it doesn't sound great
text:
This actually fits my needs pretty well, I just wanted a BT speaker for my daughter to use to practice her routines instead of turning the speakers all the way up on her iPhone. The sound is generated by a single-cone speaker, about 4" diameter & the enclosure doesn't do much to improve the sound. It probably won't sound as good as the device it's hooked to but it is louder & without distortion.
Bluetooth setup is easy but it will only link to one device at a time, I have to "forget" it from another device before linking to another. I haven't used it with USB, or micro SD (or even the audio jack) but since it doesn't have any kind of display I think it would be a pain to play anything but a pre-arranged set list or track albums. I have never run the battery all the way down so I don't know how long it lasts but it lasts a while.

title: Much easier to find remotes, improves grip, doesn't interfere with buttons though slightly recessed
text:
These were slightly tough to pull on but work exactly how I wanted to make them easy to find & tell apart. I have several of these Fire sticks now & the one in my workshop is perpetually missing. I took to putting white electrical tape on it so I can find it after I set it down. Now it is day-glo chartreuse & always easy to spot from across the room.
The rubberized coating adds a little thickness to the remote. The ring & some of the buttons still sit a little proud but most are flush or recessed. It is not a big deal & barely changes the function but it changes the feel. Speaking of, the remotes are easier to pick up & hang on to. It doesn't interfere with the buttons at all.
I was a little worried that the light green would pick up grease from my not-so-tidy workshop & hands but it hasn't stained yet. The green one glows a little in the dark. I'm not sure if the blue one is supposed to glow but if it does it is very faint.

title: Works flawlessly, solar power is holding up in tree shade & announces from a long way away.
text:
I have been working out of detached workshop behind my house & set this in front of my house to capture the circular drive. It's not excessively far but it's out of range for a bluetooth device reach. It rings if anything goes through the circle (where the Camaro is) or down the drive past the house. I have tested it by walking at the very edge of the drive & it hasn't failed to alert. I may adjust the settings down before I move the receiver inside because it picks up a lot of cat activity. I didn't realize how many neighborhood cats stroll through my drive early in the morning.
I wanted to check this out before I committed to a mounting place so I set it under that oak tree. I thought it might be too shady to maintain the solar power requirements but it's been there a week with no issues. It's so discrete I'll probably just keep it on the rocks & move it closer to the tree. The mounting hardware is pretty nice, though, with a ball-jointed mount that sets up easy since it comes apart & has a lot of adjustment.
The receiver has three or 4 chimes & none of them are subtle. It also has another 30 or so songs. Some are holiday themed which could be fun if you were expecting guests for a party. It has some public domain tunes from the Baroque & Renaissance period as well as some contemporary tunes like "Music Box Dancer". I currently have it on what sounds like a mariachi band playing "March of the Toreadors" from Carmen which is kind of hilarious but I can't imagine what maniac would want to be alerted by that in their house ever. Most of the rest of the songs are like that.

title: Sound great & comfortable but they quit pairing with each other
text:
These sound excellent though they aren't as dynamic as other earbuds I have tried & are a little light on bass. They are very comfortable, stay in the ear very well & I like that they grip the inner ear instead of going around the ear. Only having the inner ear clamps also makes the charger smaller. The earbuds charge in a small box that has a battery of it's own so they can recharge in a pocket.

When we first got these they set up easily & quickly. After about 2 weeks they quit pairing each other. Now, each earbud will connect individually with a phone but not with each other. I would drop a star but my daughter still uses them, one at a time & still likes them.

title: We're not mad, just disappointing. Excellent machine & support, app needs more work
text:
It's hard to hate on this drone when it is flying. Mechanically it performs very well in the air. The camera is great & the camera stabilization works very well. The app has been a frustrating experience that has kept me from fully exploring the capabilities of the drone.

After the last app & firmware update we have experienced freezing of the video feed, disconnects from the phone & disconnects from the radio. The good news is that, in the last case, the drone dutifully returned to its starting spot. I didn't have those issues before the update but I did have others.

I have put in a couple of tech requests & their support is very good. In some cases a confirmation email the same or next day & resolution in another day or so. In one case a very nice young man called me to talk me through a gyro calibration.

We have enjoyed using the camera to fly it around the neighborhood. The camera function is fantastic. The attitude adjustment for the camera is intuitive & handy. I'm still learning to fly by the screen so I like being able to "look" up & down to make sure I'm not about to hit something and figure out the location by looking at landmarks & streets.

On the drone platform, the camera can be set to track a person with just the camera & the drone stationary or have the drone follow the person while tracking. We used that to record my daughter's color guard practice. It also has a "point of interest" feature where it flies circles over a particular spot & the operator can start or stop recording while it it is circling. I'm thinking this will be cool for parties this Summer when we can finally have people over again. For now I have is top quality shots of the top of my camper & green pool.

It camera mode it performs very well as a stable, tracking camera. The camera gimble has a lot of range to track a person moving about & the tracking works well. If the person moves out of the frame it will not re-aquire them though in my experience. The camera can be mounted on a tripod or used as a hand-held "camcorder". On a tripod, it kind of hangs off to the side & down so it will interfere with some tripod setups. It is also a bit bulky to use as a camcorder but the stabilization is so good I forgive that. In either configuration a phone has to be used to stop & start recording or take pictures which I do not like & I hope they put out a bluetooth button for that.

The controller is small compared to the ones I used for model airplanes & it is easy to hold. There is no attachment point for a lanyard. The phone is held on a mount that extends out & up & puts the phone in a good place to see but puts a lot of weight up high. The gimbles have a rubber gasket around that makes them water resistant & doesn't interfere with their operation. The controller charges with a mini-usb (ugh) & connects to the phone with included USBC or Lightning cables. The cord going to the phone could be a little more tidy.

The case is nice, thick foam & will hold everything needed to fly except maybe a second battery. It's sturdy enough to put in checked luggage (with the batteries removed of course).

The beginner mode is seriously slow & a good way to get used to flying especially for someone who is learning nose-in hovering & other basics. It also makes a very stable camera platform.

A couple of observations:
I am not great at sorting out things on the app & would prefer robust instructions. I had no idea that the aforementioned gyro calibration was something I could perform myself or that I should have known where to look for it. It took me several tries to figure out how to turn on the tracking features (it has to be "started" after turning it on).

This is my first serious drone so I can't adequately compare it to other models. I used to fly model airplanes & helicopters decades ago & I tend to try to fly these quadrotors like an airplane in line of sight flight. This model seems to resist that more than others that I have flown & tries to force a flat plane rather than let me bank it & swoop around (I hope that makes sense).

I worked in a hobby shop for several years when I was younger (a long time ago). This is exactly what people who came in dreamed of buying; a small, aircraft that could fly in the backyard or far away that doesn't require a steep learning curve to fly or maintain. The camera adds to the fun & makes it useful.

title: A lot of features for the price, music sound is good, a little bulky but stay put
text:
These wireless headphones sound good but I wouldn't say great. They certainly have a lot of features for the price point. The charge case has a battery inside so they can charge while in a pocket & not plugged in. Both headphones have a button that can pause or answer calls but unfortunately there is no volume control on the headphones. These worked very good for phone calls, I am especially impressed with the microphone since it is at ear level & doesn't pick up ambient noise too much.

I mistook the "wireless charging case" for a case that could be set on a wireless charging pad & I was astounded that the headphones still had plenty of charge after 10+ hours of use without plugging in. Because of that I have only used them for about 4 hours a day without putting them in the case (where they got recharged without me realizing) so I haven't been able to test the 6 hour battery life yet. The case easily fits in a pocket or bag. The battery is only down about 20% after 3 days of re-charging the phones after 3-4 hours of use per day.

My set came in a fancy box with magnet enclosure. I may have gotten a pre-production version though because the contents don't exactly match the description & the instructions have some mistakes. These did come with several sets of memory phone & rubberized ear cushions. I tried a couple of different combinations & found that the foam cushions that were pre-installed were the best fit for me.

The headphones came installed with the "ear hooks" that go around the ears. The box also contains "ear fins" or "Freebit clips" which hook inside the ear. I tried both & prefer the inside ear option. They fit in the charger much more easily, don't interfere with my glasses & they stayed in place during my most rigorous activities. Both types of ear pieces slip over the headphones 360° & can be put on backwards or from the wrong side. It can take a lot of tinkering to get the fit just right.

Pairing was quick & straightforward. There are specific instructions for re-connecting the right earphone if it drops. I did have to do that once & it is several steps. I took a picture of the instructions so I could do it again but the set can also be "forgotten" & paired again to correct it.

These are pretty bulky. They don't feel all that big when wearing them so I was surprised when I saw myself in the mirror.

title: Big pack, holds equipment & change of clothes, sturdy but cumbersome
text:
This pack can hold a lot of luggage, at least a couple of days worth, as well as electronics & work gear. I had this pack for weeks while 2 trips got canceled & I thought it was too big for regular work. When I finally put it up against my regular pack, I was surprised that the profile was about the same. It is still pretty thick with space for clothing as well as office electronics & supplies. It fit easily under the seat of an Embraer 175 (picture) fully loaded & extra-stuffed with a jacket but it had to go in the overhead on an EMB-145.

The straps are comfortable but it is not something I wanted to wear as a backpack a lot while it was fully stuffed. The bag has a strap for hooking around the handle of a roller bag which worked well. It has compression straps & a compression zipper. Almost all of the zippers go behind the compression straps which makes accessing any of the sections a bit of a pain.

The center section has a large, expandable area where clothing can be packed. In the summer I could probably pack this bag for a 2 day trip & still carry my laptop, peripherals & supplies. I used this for a January trip to Milwaukee & needed the extra space to carry winter clothing. For this trip I was able to pack a change of clothes & toiletries (along with my work electronics & supplies) in the backpack & leave my roller bag in the car when I changed hotels

This is a great travel bag for gear & clothing but it could be more practical. It is thick even without clothing inside, I had to carry a smaller backpack for my laptop & supplies to take into accounts. It only has two outside zippers on the front which access internal pockets. There is no place on the outside for a water bottle or easy access to things a traveler would use to stash pocket items while going through security. I tried several different arrangements & I'll probably figure out better & more efficient ways to use it on future trips.

title: Compact & full of nice features
text:
This station is set up for all of the latest tech. It comes with two USB-C outputs which I hope become the standard connection soon. I used them to link my phone & also as headphone connections. The only video outputs are 4K which had me looking around for the for the weird cables that came with my monitors. It has two USB Gen 1 & one USB Gen 2. I appreciate that it has more connections than the Dell stations we get at work.

Everything was plug & play, my Dell Latitude 5300 immediately took to the new station. The computer & phone stayed at 100% all day while plugged in. I am surprised at the price premium of the dock is compared to the Dell docks even if it does have more features.

title: Good sound, excellent microphone & volume control.
text:
These earbuds sound good & don't have an exaggerated bass. The USB-C connection is flawless but it does stick out unlike a 3.5mm headphone with a right angle. The earbuds fit well but are bulky & the wires are heavy.

I love the volume and pause/play button section. It is large & easy to tell the controls by feel. The earbuds are also easy to tell the left from the right by feel because the left is convex & the right is concave. The microphone is better than any other set of earbuds I have had to date & I go through a lot.

When these earbuds are plugged into my LG phone calls & texts sound through the speaker when the earbuds are not being used.

title: Amazing sound, high quality & easy controls
text:
The 1st thing I noticed about these headphones when I received them (other than the amazing box they came in) are that they are noticeably heavier than my other headphones. I take that as an indication of higher quality speakers.

They do sound amazing. I listened to an album I have heard dozens of times before in the car & on earbuds & could hear elements I have never picked up on before. I actually thought I was listening to a different version of the song. I expected an exaggerated bass like I get with some earbuds but the sound is straightforward.

The noise cancelling seems about the same as my much cheaper headphone set but both are very good & make a world of difference on a plane or other noisy situations. Pairing is practically automatic on Apple devices but it is also easy for my Android phone. I think we have 3 or 4 devices currently paired to this set.

The headphones turn on as soon as they are unfolded. This is a cool feature but it means they are always on if they are worn around the neck. The battery lasts a long, long time. One charge played movies & noise cancelling for 7 hours of flying, probably another hour of music plus at least 4 more hours of just noise cancelling because someone forgot to close them until they were down to 2%

The volume & play /pause are easily controlled by tapping the right ear cuff. The charge port is the robust Apple lighting cable type which was a surprise to me until my daughter told me that Apple owns the Beats brand.

The carry case is much bigger than the folded headset. At first glance it doesn't look thick enough to provide good protection but pinching the material reveals that it has a thin, soft layer of foam or something inside. The zipper is the waterproof type which is a nice. The case comes with a hang tag & carabiner.

The headphones were too tight for my XL head. My ears were sore after long days on airplanes. I extended the cuffs all the way to reduce the tension which helped a little but made them harder to wear. The ear cuffs are a little smaller than another pair I have & I like the larger cuff because I can move them around a little on the ear for comfort while still getting a good 'seal' on my ear.

I ended up giving these to my daughter & she absolutely loves them. She is very is proud to have the Beats brand which isn't so important to me.

title: Easy installation & offers a clear picture
text:
I am using this HDMI to RCA adapter so that I am able to use my Fire stick on an older tube-style television in my workshop that has RCA connections. Installation is easy. It comes with a wall USB power adapter and a power cord & attached RCA plugs. The HDMI cable just plugs into the sides. It has an on/off button on the side of the box & a small indicator light.

The picture from the adapter is very clear. I have another of these adapters and there are almost always feint lines across the screen. This one doesn't have any artifacts on the screen.

The RCA connection wires are hard-wired into the unit with plugs on the end making it a little harder to hook into the TV & reduces options of where I can put the adapter. I'm not sure if I can leave this on all the time or whether I should turn it off when not in use. Turning it off & on requires access to the box which means I can't just stuff it behind the TV. The instructions say not to use the box in hot & humid locations. This is in my detached workshop & I live in the South so it will definitely see some of those conditions for the next couple of months. I'll update if there are any troubles.

title: Great sound, great battery life, noise cancelling is very effective
text:
I haven't had big, soft, over-the-ears headphones in decades. It is comforting how much this set blocks out outside sounds and immerses me in the music (or conference calls). The headphones sound great, the bass boost is actually pretty subtle compared to some of the earbud sets I have tried.

When I turn on the noise cancelling feature of these headphones I can just detect the "static" before background noises go away. I thought that I was the only person to have never tried noise cancelling headphones but when people asked about my new headset at work I handed them over they were all amazed at how the din of the rattling air conditioner and other office noises were silenced while they could still hear my voice. The noise cancelling switch can be turned on while media is playing or when using as a phone headset and does still work as a filter.

The battery seems to last forever. I charged this set once & have been using it off and on for over two weeks. I have fallen asleep with the noise cancelling on twice waking up hours later with it still running.

If I have a complaint about these it is the same complaint I have for nearly all of the headsets I have used; The buttons are hard to find. In this set the buttons are built into the right ear cuff and I have to carefully feel around to do anything. The start/pause/answer the phone button is completely flush and completely inconspicuous. The volume rocker is at the top & are flush except for a tiny dot on the volume up. The bass boost button also serves as the power button and is much more pronounced with a raised ridge across the center. The switch to turn on the noise cancelling is actually pretty easy to find & is a slider.

I have a large head (XL helmet) 7 3/4 hat, and these are kind of tight on my head. I hope they break in over time. They are especially 'pinchy' when I am wearing my reading glasses. I have these synced to my phone & tablet but this set also comes with a cord which is how I have to use them with my work computer. The cuffs turn 90º. I wasn't sure why until I packed them into a bag for a trip and realized that they would be a lot less likely to get broken with the cups folded down like that.

title: It's very long and works on finicky iPhones
text:
For some reason my wife's old 6s has begun to only charge on certain charge cords and this Anker was found to be one of them. Unfortunately I bought that 10ft cord to my daughter and had to take it from her so this replacement is the 2nd one of these cords I have purchased.

It is very long so my daughter can drag it across the room to look at her phone while partially listening to TV which is irritating to me.

title: If you ask me turn up the bass.
text:
I replaced all of the speakers in my wife's old 2001 Camaro this year and put these 6.5" subs in the sail panels. We are middle aged and it has been decades since I last messed with stereo stuff and had a 600 watt system in my ElCamino with 8 separates and 15" subs. I was a little worried that these subs would be too big to fit in the hole from which the paper speakers came but they slipped right in. After the install I stuck in an old copy of Bach Busters and I thought the whole thing sounded great. I was very impressed with the bass from these little subs as I ran through all the big bass tracks on the disk.

After my wife took the car to work I asked her about the speakers. She told me that there were some issues... She said that "Funky Town" came on the radio (did I mention that we are older?) and the subs were rattling the car and it embarrassed her. She isn't enjoying the music as much because she is self conscious about someone hearing the speaker rattling her car. I am going to replace these with some mid range speakers in her car and put these in my Jeep. One word of caution, these speakers absolutely need a box to be heard. When I was testing the wiring I thought I would be disappointed because I could barely hear them until I placed them in the enclosure. They might not work on say a trunk package shelf with too much air space.

title: I have to completely reset it from time to time
text: When this thing is working it works but I have to completely reset it from time to time since I got it three months ago.  I don't use many devices on this network but I use it as a repeater to a third router in a detached building which makes it extra painful to reset.  Talk about your first world problems.

title: This was a great gift, very pleased with the sound and the setup.
text: I bought this as a gift for my 20 year old nephew who usually gets a gift card from me.  He absolutely loved it.  He immediately set it up and began streaming music while we were opening presents.  I wish I had gotten a few more as gifts and I'll probably get one for myself.  It is very loud, very easy to set up and it even came charged enough to play for a couple of hours.  We only used it on Bluetooth from a phone so I can't speak to the other functionalities.

title: Very good sound quality
text: I purchased this DAC/amp a few months ago for myself and liked it so much I bought another as a Christmas present for my son. It provides excellent audio quality with my Focal and Sennheiser headphones.

title: Nice wall mount for a tv
text: This wall mount unit works great for my 50” flat screen tv. Easy to install if you have the correct tools. Range of motion makes it easy to adjust the tv for a wide range of viewing options. Price was good also.

title: Lots of tech in a small package
text: This small device packs a lot of technology in for barely over $20. Easy to pair via Bluetooth and transmit via the fm radio. Call reception is very good. I plugged in a USB thumb drive with flac files and the music playing on the radio sounds great. I also hooked up my Astell & Kern AK Jr via the aux input and again got very nice audio quality with the radio. Also charged my iPhone quickly. Highly recommend and lots less expensive than replacing the stereo in the car.

title: My granddaughter loves it
text: My granddaughter loves it. It was a her birthday present. Loaded with kid friendly apps and good parental control.

title: Nice little case
text: Very handy little case to store my digital audio player.

title: Sturdy and affordable
text: I did notice a slight improvement in sound quality over the Apple connector. Seems sturdy and well built. Good value at less than $20.

title: Sturdy, well made and good sound quality
text: I liked the original version of this iPhone headphone adapter so much,I purchased a second UGREEN iPhone lightning headphone adapter. I have several sets of quality headphones (Sennheiser HD598, HD599, Martin Logan Mikros 90) and want the best possible audio signal. Using these via the UGREEN adapter, I can stream HD quality music from Spotify and Amazon Music HD. If you have an iPhone and want the best audio signal for your headphones, I would highly recommend this item.

title: Nice speaker upgrade and a good value
text: I purchased these JBL speakers to replace the original speakers in my 2001 Dodge Dakota pickup. They provide better sound quality, especially at higher volume levels. These are a very good value also. Are there better speakers out there? sure, but I would have had to spend several times the price of these to do much better.

title: Easy to use and good sound quality
text: It is so nice to be able to use wired headphones with my iPhone XR. A wired connection with my Sennheiser HD598 headphones provides better sound quality that using bluethooth headphones. For me sound quality is far more important than bluethooth convenience. This seems more sturdy than the Apple version and enables a high resolution audio signal when using Amazon Music HD or Spotify. I liked it so much, I also purchased the updated version.

title: Affordable replacement remote control for TCL Roku tv
text: Works just like the original remote. I do hope it lasts longer than the original, which stopped working afer a couple of years.

title: Nice upgrade for Martin Logan Mikros 90 headphones
text: I was very pleasantly surprised what a difference these ear pads made to my Mikros 90 headphones. These are more comfortable and improve the sound quality of the headphones versus the original ear pads. They are a bit tedious to put on but are well worth the effort. If you own a set of Martin Logan Mikros 90 headphones, I would encourage you replace the ear pads with these Geekria pads even if the originals are not worn out. You will appreciate the improvement. Highly recommended.

title: Works well
text: The cable is a bit smaller and thinner than I expected, but it still works quite well streaming music from my iPhone through my stereo. It is compact enough to carry around for a travel cable. I would recommend it.

title: Affordable and works well
text: I have purchased several of these to store music for playback in my car. They work well and store lots of music with much better sound quality than most radio stations.

title: Excellent WiFi Router
text: This router is doing a great job in our 2000 square foot house. I can get a good signal anywhere in the house and a large portion of our yard even with multiple devices accessing the signal. Highly recommended.

title: Turns an older tv into a smart tv
text: This was on sale for $25, so I could not pass up this deal. It provides access to a wide range of apps and accessing programs via the Alexa enabled remote it quick and easy. I really like it!

title: Affordable, sturdy and attractive
text: We needed a larger entertainment cabinet when we purchased a larger tv. It easily accommodates a 50 inch tv and all my stereo components. Assembly was easy when directions were followed. It is very sturdy as well and looks nice in our living room.

title: Nice case
text: Nice case. It has a very smooth feel in the hand and provides some protection to the AK Jr. It is a bit pricey, which is why I deducted one star.

title: Nice Bluethooth Audio Adapter. Easy setup.
text: I purchased 2 of these for separate stereos in my house and both work perfectly. Setup was very easy using the included RCA to 3.5 stereo plug. You can also use a separate RCA to RCA patch cord (not included). Pairing a Bluethooth device was also easy. I chose this Logitech unit since it had both RCA plugs and 3.5 Stereo plug for extra flexibility. Audio quality is good when streaming music from Spotify or Pandora. I would buy this device again.

title: Very nice headphones
text: I already own a pair of Sennheiser HD 598 open back headphones, which are excellent!! I ordered the HD 598 Cs to use for travel and times when a closed back headphone would be needed. The 598 Cs was a very good choice.  They are easy to drive with portable audio devices, so no need for a separate headphone amp.  You also get an iPhone compatible mic that works well for phone calls.The sound quality is very nice, although a bit different from the open back 598. Closed back headphones are not as open and spacious in their sound presentation as open back headphones. The 598 Cs has a bit more bass emphasis, but not excessive like other brands of headphones. Vocals, acoustic guitar, strings and percussion are well presented on the 598 Cs. Comfort is excellent also. I can wear these for extended periods without fatigue. If you are looking for a comfortable set of headphones with very good audio quality, you will really enjoy the HD 598 Cs.

title: Nice case but too small to accommodate my Sennheiser HD598 headphones
text: I purchased this case for my Sennheiser HD598 headphones, but unfortunately, it is too small to accommodate them comfortably. In order to zip the case closed, it is necessary to rotate the ear piece 30-45 degrees, which I'm not comfortable with since the HD598 ear piece is fixed and not intended to rotate. For a smaller mid-sized set of headphones, the db case would work great since the case is well built. If you own a set of full size audiophile headphones, you should consider other options for a case.

title: Excellent replacement cable for Sennheiser headphones
text: Very good quality replacement cable for my Sennheiser HD558 headphones. It was a very easy plug into the the headphones. Audio quality is as good as the original cable and the 1.5m length is perfect for use with portable devices. Highly recommended.

title: What a nice turntable mat
text: Swiss Leather Turntable Mat works very well on my Pro-Ject Carbon turntable. I was concerned that it may be too thick, but my LPs sound great with it. I particularly like the fact that my records attract far less dust than they did with the felt mat that came with the turntable. Item shipped on time and arrived well packaged. This may be the most unusual packaging ever though!!! When I opened the box, it contained a 1957 Hi-Fi mono LP of the Robert Shaw Corale Christmas album wrapped in a plastic LP cover. My initial reaction was "oh no, they sent the wrong item". Then I noticed a small label on the LP cover stating Swiss Leather Turntable Mat. After opening the LP packaging, I discovered the leather mat inside the LP cover along with the 1957 LP. A nice bonus! The record was actually in very good shape. Thanks for a very creative and enjoyable shopping experience.

title: Nice CD player at a great price.
text:
I order this CD player to replace an old Denon CD player that I have been using for over a decade. The Denon has always been erratic about reading my CDs and skipping during playback. Amazon had a great sale price on the Onkyo, so I order one. The player has a nice weight to it, so I assume the components are good quality. The Onkyo reads my CDs quickly and plays everything I have tried on it, so all is good. I also noticed an improvement in sound quality with a tighter, more focused sound. Not major, but definitely a noticeable improvement. It is connected to Sony's entry level stereo receiver and out through an older pair of Boston Acoustics A70 speakers. It is perfect for my bedroom.
2/16/18 update. The CD player drawer has developed a problem in the past year. When I press the open button, the CD tray opens and immediately closes repeatedly. After multiple presses, it may work, but often not. Very frustrating. I now use my Oppo BluRay player as my primary CD player.

title: Good quality set of Audio Cables
text: I purchased a set of these cables along with a new Onkyo C-7030 CD player for my bedroom stereo and noticed a nice improvement in the sound quality of my system. The system is pretty basic. Entry level Sony stereo receiver and older Boston Acoustics speakers.  I'm not sure if it was the cables or CD player, but I could hear a tighter, more articulate sound of my CDs. I would certainly recommend these for an upgrade in sound quality. While my bedroom system is not high end, it still sounds very nice with these improvements.

title: Enhanced the definition and clarity of my turntable
text: I purchased a pair of these cables to connect my Pro-Ject Carbon Debut Turntable to my 20 year old Denon AV Receiver running out to Boston Acoustics M25 speakers and immediately noticed a significant improvement on overall sound quality of my LP records. Most noticeable was a significant increase is bass response with a tighter, more focused sound. Overall clarity of recordings improved as well. I'm going to order another set to connect my Oppo Blue Ray Player. I'm really enjoying the overall improvement in sound quality of my LPs now!!

title: Very nice record cleaner
text: Very nice record cleaner. These are getting hard to find in stores. If you listen to LPs, you definitely need one of these.

title: ... CD player into my receiver and and noticed a nice improvement in the tone quality
text: I purchased a pair of these cables to connect from my CD player into my receiver and and noticed a nice improvement in the tone quality. So, I ordered a couple more sets for my DVD player and my turntable. Not as much difference with these 2 pieces of equipment. As other reviewers have stated, there is some variance on the size of the input jack. They did not fit snugly into my turntable or DVD player. The build quality is good otherwise. The cables are nice and thick and the plugs ends appear to be well made. If you are looking for a good quality, and very affordable audio cable, these will work nicely for you.

title: The AKG K450 (& K451) are very nice headphones. They are the same in sound quality
text: The AKG K450 (& K451) are very nice headphones. They are the same in sound quality, but the K451 has an iphone compatible, in line mic with volume controls. These are very light wight and comfortable to wear. I could wear them comfortably for hours. The tone is clear and smooth. The bass response is nice, with warm mids and smooth highs. If you are looking for a heavy bass however, such as rap or hip hop, you should look elsewhere. For a very comfortable, nice sounding set of headphones, you can't go wrong with either the K450 or K451.

title: well controlled bass and excellent high end response
text: For $95, I could not pass up this deal. The sound on the Mikros 90 headphones is well worth the price. They deliver a very precise sound with tight, well controlled bass and excellent high end response. The are very well suited for jazz and vocals, and they can rock. Van Morrison's "Moondance" and Tony Bennett's duets CD "Playing With My Friends" sounds great. Tony's duet with Cheryl Crow sounds awesome. For some rock, I listened to Thin Lizzy's "Dedication" and guitar solos were clear and strong. These headphones deliver a very clear and accurate sound, so if you listen to a poorly recorded record, you will notice the marginal audio quality of the recording. As others have stated, they are quite snug on your head. The major issue I had with them initially was that they rotated too far forward, allowing the forward edge of the headphone under the ear pads to press into the side of my face just in front of the ears. This got to be uncomfortable after 15-20 minutes. I noticed that they did not rotate in the opposite direction, so I decided to listen with the ear pads on the opposite ear (left channel over the right ear and right channel on the left ear). In this position, the ear pads stay perfectly flat on my ears for a much more comfortable fit. I really enjoy the refined sound that these headphones produce.

title: I am amazed at the sound that these small speakers produce
text:
Looks like I have the privilege of being the first person to review the BA M25 speakers. I picked up a pair of these on Christmas Eve and have been playing them constantly over the past 2 weeks. My focus has been on 2 channel stereo recordings instead of movies. My set up is through an older Denon AVR 610 receiver that I have had for almost 20 years. I was initially impressed with the smooth, balanced feel of these speakers. Good mid range, nice high end, but not too bright, and a very strong bass response. The M25s defy their size in producing bass tones. Give them some break in time before making a final assessment. These speakers excel at producing music performed on real instruments. The do a great job on jazz, blues and acoustic folk styles of music. Vocals come across nicely as well.
Boz Scaggs "But Beautiful" CD of standards sounds great. Upright bass, piano and vocals make you feel like you are in a small jazz club. Diana Krall "Live in Paris" also plays very well. Nice piano, guitar & vocal reproduction. Jorma Kaukonen's "Blue Country Heart" CD showcases some great finger style acoustic guitar. Very natural acoustic guitar tones. Linda Ronstadt's "Winter Light" CD has some of the most powerful vocals you will ever hear and the M25s reproduce Linda's voice and backing instrumentation extremely well. The sound is never strained or harsh. Initially, I was a bit more apprehensive on some CDs with lots of bass. They sounded like they were trying to overcompensate on bass, but this has evened out over the past week. Eric Clapton's "Pilgrim" CD has come serious bottom end and the M25s produce very deep, tight bass response. Peter Gabriel "So" is a similar story. Deep, tight bass response that does not bottom out. Paul Rogers "Muddy Waters Blues" is a treat on the M25s. The opening track features some acoustic delta blues guitar, followed by a chorus of female backup singers and later some nice Strat blues guitar tones. It all sounds great on these speakers.
The look and finish on the speakers is impressive also. They are finished in a polished black exterior with a leatherette finish on the top, back & bottom. They look like a piece of fine furniture that would fit into a modern style of home décor. These speakers are very expensive though. I got a demo pair at less than half of the $399 per speaker list price. I don't think I would have bought them at full price. I have been listening to Boston Acoustics speakers for over 20 years. I still own a pair of A60s and a pair of A120s that have served me well over the years. The M25s have replaced the A120s as my primary speakers in my living room due to their sonic capabilities and their stylistic good looks.

Update 6/24/14 - After listening to these speakers for 6 months, I continue to be even more impressed by the Boston M25s. I bought these thinking they will do until I can find better. While there are better speakers out there, I have concluded, after many demo sessions, that I would need to spend at least $1500-$1800 or more to get some form of improvement over the M25s. Short of stepping up to KEF R300 @ $1800, B&W CM5 @ $1500 or Aperion Verus Towers, the M25s deliver the goods with very balanced & neutral sound, great detail in the upper register and sold bass. Highly recommended.

title: was easy to hook up
text: fire stick is fire, was super easy to hookup, install.

title: little computer
text: Love this little computer. Incredibly powerful, and plenty of storage. I don't game so can't say about that. But this one puts the other mini-pcs to shame.

title: easy enough for a child
text: Wonderfully easy for children to use. Picture is good, sound is just a little tinny, sturdy. Worth the money.

title: It took a while to figure out how to focus ...
text:
but the major problem is the whole in the eye piece that your phone camera lens looks through covers only part of the lens no matter how much you try to center it. title: So easy to use.
text: My radio in my car bit the dust so I ordered this to keep me awake on my trips to see my grandkids. Love the FM radio. The sound depends on your earbuds--good earbuds great sound, cheap earbuds good sound. It's not stereo, though.

title: perfect for connrcting to my TV
text: I Made my TV into a smart tv by connecting my laptop to it. This has fast streaming portals that work great with my TCL tv and my Acer laptop.

title: Extremely pleased except...

title: Super little tablet
text:
I like this little tablet. It isn't so heavy you get tired holding it for long time. It's fast, and it's a great value for the money. I haven't had it long enough to judge its sturdiness. One drawback is that it isn't compatible with the Kindle reader nor the Kindle software... so you can't read your Kindle purchases nor can you create your own Kindle books.

But for everything else, I normally use, it works quite well. Travels well and charges fairly fast.

title: This contraption is a bit complicated to install.
text: The instructions tell you yo get a qualified electrician to install so the thing complies with local building codes.I think it's worth hiring because you get so much protection from one tool. You can talk to whoever is at your door, watch whatever comes up on your porch or kids in pool. Motion triggered. Plenty of light. It's that extra protection that helps deter anyone from messing with your stuff.

title: Love this...
text: Would like a little more storage, but having the thumb drive is amazing. My computer doesn't have a CD drive or aSD card slot, so this is terrifically convenient to transfer videos and phoyos to my computer. Super!

title: small and flat
text:

title: Not as easy peasy as it sounds
text:
I thought this would be just plug and go. It's not. You have two ways to set up. WPS or using your cell phone with the Nighthawk app. If your wifi is 5g and your phone is 2g or 3g... it will set up the slower speed AND the faster speed, but it won't tell you that it is set up. You have to look at how it lights up on the unit itself. I didn't know this and struggled and struggled, finiggeled and finaggled trying to set up the 5g when all along it was set up. Just watch during set up and you'll know when the 5g is set up.

I haven't noticed that big a difference. If your internet is on cable (you may know this already), you share your internet with everyone on your block. When everyone logs on after work or on weekends, this slows down the speed of your internet. So I thought this would help during the slow times to boost the internet speed. Ummm, not really.

It boosts the signal, but not the speed as the box promises.

Just follow the instructions that come with the box. Watch the lights that will tell you what is set up and when. Then move your unit to half way between your modem/wifi hub and the "dead" spot in your house or whatever. It will help, just don't expect lightening speed if your internet is not lightening speed or if everyone on your block is using cabled internet just like you.

title: This is not worth the money
text:
This is too little and too slide-y.

When first turned on it kept up a jitter that kept me from clicking on the place I wanted to click. Found out that was because the touchpad was still on when this mouse was connected. Fixed that, but don't ever drop it or it will fall into plastic pieces. It does come with a AA battery, that's good. And getting to the USB connector is easy--just lift off the top of the mouse and grab the thing after putting in the battery.

Without a mouse pad, it slips and slides around so the cursor never stays in the same place.

Adult hands/fingers, people with shakey hands, and people who use their mouse constantly for drawing/painting/or other mechanical computer work, spend more money and get a better product. For all others and children, this is an okay product.

The thing is just too small for my hand which makes it really uncomfortable. I use my mouse constantly while digital painting. So I can't use it for work. It would probably be just right for a child, or for small hands.

title: Super product and Exceptional customer service!
text:
I did have a problem with the delivery of my Fire HD8 Tempered Glass Screen. However, the customer service is beyond satisfactory. I am deeply pleased. When it arrived broken, within 2 days I received a new one (I did send photos of the broken one). I did find out something tremendous, though. The broken screen held together safely. I was cracked and had fan-like cracks from edge to edge, but it didn't fall apart. It was smooth to the touch, so if for any reason your screen gets cracked on your device, don't worry about it scratching the screen. It won't.

The screen cleaner--both the wet one and the dry one--do a fabulous job of removing all those little dust particles. (On my phone screen, I wasted 3 of them trying to get a smooth adhering surface. Never did. But I did with the first try with this one. Just be careful to clean your screen really well under a bright light so you can see all the particles and spots. Lay the glass screen on the end, and push down (fairly hard) with the enclosed triangular plastic piece as you gently lower the glass screen onto your device's screen. If you do it slowly, you won't have any bubbles. If you see a piece of dirt that you missed, then lift the corner gently and dab the glass screen with the blue sticky paper enclosed. That keeps your fingerprints from the sticky side of the glass screen. Dab your device's screen with the blue sticky paper to be sure you removed all the dirt. Slide the triangular plastic piece over the indentation and it should give you a perfect seal over the device's screen.

It's beautiful.

title: She has always loved to read
text:
Not too heavy, very handy. I got this for my mom who is 87 years old. She has always loved to read, but macular degeneration took that away from her until I got her the first Kindle and enlarged the print to about 2 words per page. She's been devouring books ever since, but the old Kindles didn't have that white background. I got her this one so she could read more than 2 words per page (now it's almost a sentence per page) and the lighted screen makes the print much brighter for her to see. The 8" is a comfortable size for her.

The learning curve has been a challenge. The screen is so sensitive that when she barely touches it, it loses her place. We have not tried Alexa to get her back to her place in her book, but we might try that and see if it works.

The promo info said it would hold a charge for 12 hours. Nope. We're doing good if it lasts 6 hours. I try to check it to make sure no other apps except Kindle are running, but it seems like the Internet is draining the battery... or something is. We've gone to turning it off completely so she can read a few hours before having to recharge.

title: Customer service is 6 stars I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to ...
text:
Customer service is 6 stars

I certainly would love this product if we could have gotten it to work. I'm on a 5GB wifi network, and the StarTech is for a 2.4GB network. It won't work with my Internet speed. Or so both my techie, Brian, and I thought. Keep reading.

However... I couldn't connect the print server (that's the little white box) with my laptop. I had a problem and got online to get it fixed. The chat tech was very polite, patient and knowledgeable, but pointed me to the support page that gave me step by step how to set up my wifi print server. Went there. Followed the steps but I had no idea what the server IP address was. Gave up until I could call and get someone to walk me through it. A survey came up asking for my thoughts on my experience. I told them I was having a problem and just needed to know what my server IP address was so I could set up to print from my laptop. Got an email from a supervisor asking if I'd like a more experienced tech to call me. Yes! I would.

Got a call from Brian. He was very helpful, patient, and walked me through everything. Then I had to let him have remote control over the process because it got too complicated for me. That's when we discovered that the print server wouldn't work with my internet speed. So I told him how grateful I was for his patience and help even though I couldn't use the thing that was going to save me so much time. We hung up and while I was typing up this 6-star review of StarTech's great tech support, Brian called me back and said he was pretty sure he'd figured it out. I gave him remote control again, and 15 minutes later I've got my wonderful wifi printer!! I'm so elated! It works.

I have Windows 10 OS on my Dell Inspiron laptop, and an HP J4540 printer -- 2008. They are now friends and talking to each other wirelessly.

I do not recommend anyone that does not know what they are doing to install this device themselves. I know a lot about computers, but I know when I need an expert. Brian is an expert! Installing the thing is complicated. If your wifi is 2.4GB, then you can follow the instructions on the website most likely without a problem. If you have a higher speed Internet, then there's a lot more backdoor stuff that needs doing. I have a feeling they'll be updating the instructions on the website for this kind of problem. But if you have any problems, contact StarTech tech support. They are the greatest this side of the sun... no joke!

This is a really solid solution for adding DVD and CD support to a modern laptop, since it is so hard to find one included these days.
I love that not only does this support both USB A and C ports, the cable is actually embedded into the case so you can wrap it up for easy storage! I admit I don't need optical media often, but I do have some older software installation disks that I still occasionally need to use when I reformat a computer, and being able to rip content from old CDs and DVDs is great to have available. This worked for installing my old Adobe CS6 suite as well as Samplitude on my desktop (which also lacks an optical drive!). Great product!

title: Plenty of space and protection!
text:
I actually like this a lot better than the last backpack I tried from Amazon. I need something to bring my laptop and some gear along when setting up portable live stream studios, and the last backpack I tried offered a lot of storage space but not any padding- I felt like all my equipment could be felt through the fabric, and putting it down was going to scuff up the laptop.
Not with this one! This backpack feels like my stuff is safe inside. There's still plenty of space, but the padding and handles feel pretty rugged, I'm impressed. Really well made, solid handles, good material. Definitely would recommend this!

title: Case is ok, keyboard has a major fault out of the box
text:
[[VIDEOID:d9cb51d1c95a2bc172f8fec24c5f713b]] As you can see in the video, the keyboard is very cute, even though you need to sort of remove it and pull forward to get the tablet to stand. But the real problem is, even after I started getting used to the smaller keys, I noticed the equal key (=) started acting up. Sometimes it would get stuck on by itself, just pressing the key repeatedly. Other times it would refuse to fire at all. This is after using it for less than one day.
Considering that the keyboard in my case is used because I want to type in exact syntax commands (something an on screen keyboard is bad at), having functional number keys and an equal sign is important. I sadly can't recommend that keyboard for this reason.
Luckily, the keyboard can be removed and the case is still a good generic case for a 7-8" tablet. I'll still use it on my Galaxy Tab, but I'm disappointed by the keyboard.

title: Great concept, when it works.
text:
[[VIDEOID:3d513e57441130c25fa7c0b6059a91ae]] I really like this concept. It's tiny, and projects an image onto a surface that looks a lot better than I expected. I own some professional grade projectors that I use for work, so to be fair, you can't compare it to a real product like that. For starters, this needs an extremely dark room to work in. Don't even bother during daylight hours unless you have a room with no windows.
But, it comes with Android built in so you're actually able to stream content without plugging anything into it! You can install standard streaming apps, or load up an SD card with content to play, or use the ports behind the rubber gasket if necessary. This thing even does auto keystone if you tilt it, which really surprised and impressed me! And because the back is flat and doesn't block any vents, you can actually lie it down facing the ceiling!
But here's the fatal flaw: The battery isn't great, and when it dies it is very easy to get stuck in this sort of "limbo" state. I managed to twice already boot it without enough battery left to finish booting, and it gets stuck in this trying-to-turn-on mode in which it won't turn off but also won't turn on. Sometimes you can get the projector to show the boot logo if there's enough power for that, but then if it doesn't finish, it shuts off and gets stuck. You can see a little blue light inside, hear something making noise if you hold it to your ear, but it won't finish booting. It also won't TURN OFF. It's stuck like that, the power switch position doesn't matter once this happens. And charging it up won't help either. You need to wait for the battery to totally die (you can see the blue light inside finally turn off) and THEN charge it all the way up, and then it will boot and work correctly.
This is a pretty big flaw in my opinion. This thing really could have used a reset button or way to pull the battery in case this happens. The instructions are pretty terrible too, most of it I had to figure out on my own. But if they can manage to fix that flaw, this is an impressively cool device!
