I'm going to try and keep it charged and use it on our next camping trip, I really love that you can sit it on it's back and aim the projector at a ceiling! But part of me feels like it is pretty likely to get stuck in this state again.

title: Great aesthetics, decent sound
text:
The biggest pro of these speakers to me, is how uncluttered they are. One cable goes into a USB port, and that's it! They look GREAT on a tabletop, almost like desk ornaments, and they glow when in use, lighting up the wall behind it. I have an ancient pair of Altec-Lansing speakers that actually sound amazing, but take up WAY too much clutter on my desk. Traditional computer speakers have a cable going into the computer's 3.5mm output, a cable going to a comically oversized wall-wart AC adapter plug, and then another cable going to the other speaker. I try to keep my desktop neat and cable-managed, and honestly I usually go with headphones for that reason.

But these solve that problem by being a USB sound card, self powered and everything all wrapped into one connection, no more space on your power strip being used or still powered on after your computer has shut down. In fact, I can unplug them and put them away when I don't need them, if a client comes to sit and work with me, it is literally one plug to get external sound again.
There are cons, however:
The Right speaker has a shorter run than the Left one does. They clearly expect your desktop to be on the right side of your monitor. In my case, my L-shaped desk has my desktop housed on the right, with the monitors to the left of it. I'm trying to see if there's an easy way to have Windows flip the L+R sound so I can swap back when using headphones. The other thing, which is arguably more important, is that the sound quality is ok at low and mid volumes, but once you start to crank it up, it begins to peak. If you want loud high quality sound, this isn't the best option. If you just want aesthetic gaming speakers that won't clutter up your desktop, or just want occasional speakers like I do, they are perfect! They sound good enough for my uses and look pretty awesome- I'm a fan.

title: Quality name brand with subtle logo
text: I've had some mixed opinions on the new Brady branded gear, but this is a good one. I like the understated logo, the quality of the material is excellent too. It seems to magically repel sweat somehow, it's incredible! Looks great too, I'm a fan. Not just of Tom Brady, but this T as well!

title: Good value for a bunch of cards
text:
These aren't terribly fast or large capacity, but this set makes up for that in quantity. The idea here is to have a handful of smaller cards to spread around to different devices- a set of trail cams, security cams, small file handoffs, anything in which having a bunch of smaller instances is more valuable than one larger card for the same money.
I'm not familiar with this brand, and their advertising copy makes me feel a little hesitant to trust them with anything mission critical, however the packaging claims that it is somewhat weatherproof, and so far they seem to work well enough for the intended purpose.

title: It's good for packing, but lacks support
text:
I like how much you can fit into this bag, it's got a uniform box shape instead of the classic tapered backpack (narrow at the top and wider at the bottom). The advantage to this is that it can fit more things inside while still fitting into the guidelines for under-seat storage on a flight. The downside is that it doesn't look as nice when worn- this is a function over form design.
That's fine- the problem for me, however, is that this bag lacks the rigidity I was expecting to protect the contents inside. In fact, the bag actually ships folded over on itself, that's how flexible the material is. I'm used to there being more of a backing to protect, say, a laptop in the rear pocket. As it is now, the laptop is what holds the bag's shape. I actually think I'd rather stick to my older backpack which was more stylish and protective when I travel, but this will come in handy when I need to fit more things in carry on.

title: Sounds decent, but shoddy quality and no inline mic option
text:
EDIT:
They apologized for the units that were DOA, and sent a new set. Very happy with the customer support, if something is wrong they stand behind their product. Bumping up the rating to reflect this.

Original review: Some of these appear to be damaged as soon as we removed it from the packaging. Thankfully there are plenty more in the set in case some of them don't work, but keep that in mind when ordering- get more than you need in case you end up with some duds.
The ones that work seem fine. These do NOT have an inline mic so if using with a laptop for zoom, etc, you will need to rely on the built in microphone or whatever options you have available off this. These are great for things that are expecting just plain L+R+Ground (TRS tip) plugs, such as older headphone jacks, cameras, or seat backs on airplanes. They also don't have sound isolation ear cuffs, which can be a good thing if you don't want to block external sounds while listening. They sound pretty good as long as you get one that isn't broken.

title: Looks much better than Metra version.
text:
I had a Metra kit in my older Solara, and it worked alright but always felt a little cheap on the materials and paint quality, even the little cover in the middle didn't fit right. But after I lost it to an accident I decided to start over with a new kit, and I have to admit I'm glad I did. The quality of this one is much better!
It still doesn't fit my Atoto radio face exactly thanks to that being a full double din 7" display (instead of most double dins assuming a 6.8" hole). This will fit a standard 6.8" face radio with the plate just fine, but a 7" like my Atoto unit doesn't like the plate in the middle. That's not the fault of this kit, most double din kits won't fit a full 7" radio face. I was able to get around that by using a dremel to edge out some tabs and make it fit better, and now it looks better than the Metra ever did.

title: Solid ergonomics
text:
I have tried quite a few wireless keyboard and mouse combos, and it seems usually I have to compromise on either ergonomics, build quality, wireless capability, or budget.
This set really impressed me. It supports two Bluetooth connections as well as using the wireless dongle for a straight USB connection, and you can easily swap between them. I prefer the dongle because bluetooth won't wake up my computer when it goes to sleep (since BT also goes to sleep), and I can easily plug the dongle into something like a mini PC without having to get ANOTHER wired keyboard to pair it first.
Yet, it has a palm rest and split keys for ergonomic typing, plus the mouse is the taller bulb shape that fits in your hand better and feels like a substantial work tool. I'm used to only expensive wired ones feeling this good.
I have to admit, I'm out of practice typing ergonomically so I still sometimes try to hit the B key with my right hand, but that's on me. The B is on the left side here, which it should be, but I'm quickly getting used to it. This review is being typed out on it and so far I'm really liking it with my standing desk setup!

title: Good durable storage, albeit USB2.0 read speeds
text:
This is exactly what it claims to be. It says very clearly that this is USB2.0 speed, so keep your expectations realistic. It seems like some people rated this poorly because it wasn't as fast as other USB devices, and that's not really fair if comparing to modern USB3 or Thunderbolt speed device made for data transferring regularly. This is more like a write-once-read-many distribution device.
I'm attaching speed benchmarks here, and this honestly seems pretty average for a USB2 connected device. I have many old USB2 sticks that are slower. A USB3 SSD connected to my USB2 port faired a little bit better. To be clear and give this a sense of scale:
An old 4GB USB stick connected to my USB2 port clocked in at 15-20MB/s.
An ultra fast USB3.1 SSD connected to the same USB2 port: 42.24MB/s (so one shouldn't be expecting to a USB2 to be faster than this or even reach this maximum on an average setup).
This device, at 30.59MB/s, seems pretty on par.
Where you will feel the sting, however, is in the slow 5.87MB/s write speed. That's also not uncommon for sticks like these- they are designed for durability and fast read times, to read data off quickly and conveniently. This is great for distributing finished media for a client to play on a projector, or have your resume / photo portfolio on your keychain. Reading more often than writing. A friend of mine who does wedding video would use a stick like this to distribute the finished event production to the client. It's perfect that for what it claims to be and do, a solid 5 stars.

title: Great for video calls and music, or BT
text:
Wireless headphones are great, but I have a love/hate relationship with using Bluetooth on a PC. When using the mic with headset profile for calls, the audio gets routed totally differently than regular stereo sound (A2DP), which gets confusing if multitasking and playing sound while also using the mic. And then there's the delay/lag etc that usually comes along with Bluetooth from a Windows desktop. But that's why I love the USB dongle here!
Plug the little USB bit in, and it detects the headphones like an alternate sound card, full blown crystal clear stereo audio, even if using the mic! And the mic can be extended or retracted, something I love since I lost the removable mic on my old headphones.
But, if I want to use it with my phone or tablet, I can revert to standard Bluetooth and connect that way on my Android devices. The price is a little bit steep, but the quality is there, this is a well designed and well made product that works as intended so far. I'm impressed.

title: 3x HDMI and 2x Ethernet ports?!
text:
This is a VERY interesting Mini PC! I have to admit I'm not 100% sure what market this is trying to target, but I do find it a unique offering among the many Mini PCs I've had the pleasure to own and try over the years.
The biggest things to stand out?
-3x HDMI ports (that's right, TRIPLE display built right into the box!)
-2x Lan ports (dual LAN!)
-Small square sized footprint

So, having 3x displays is a cool touch, this could be great for digital signage or a job that requires a lot of data visible at once (day trading, etc). The dual lan is also cool for IT guys who want to monitor or bridge multiple networks, these are unique features to find on any PC, let alone one this tiny.
The N5095 isn't quite as fast as the N5101 chips I have in other Mini PCs, but it is still faster than most of the chips found in MiniPCs at this price. Impressive for the asking amount.
But the part that irks me so very much is the lack of USB-C.

Yes, you get 3x USB3 ports which is great, but not even a single USB-C, let alone thunderbolt?
Once again, the price must be considered here. You're getting something super capable and really unique with the hardware offered at the asking price. If they made a more expensive version with a higher end CPU and USB-C/Thunderbolt port, I'd recommend that in a heartbeat. This is a solid value if you have a need for the hardware, though. Very cool and different.

title: Great for fast charging or finicky devices
text:
As another reviewer pointed out, a cable tester actually will verify this as a 100W capable wire over PD. That means your PD-compatible laptop or device will charge at the fully rated speed it should when the charger and device support it.
I have an older Pixel phone that is also very picky about what cables it will accept to charge, and a validated cable like this seems to work better with it. So far I'm appreciating it very much, good build quality, seems durable. Would definitely recommend.

title: Its an OK camera, but I'd say teens is a stretch
text:
Sadly, the point-and-shoot camera market has been cannibalized by phones, so you can't really find simple cameras like this from big brands anymore. Real point and shoot cameras were great because unlike phones, you get a zoom lens and real camera controls. This isn't that.
Additionally, this is NOT going to compete with a modern cell phone camera. It's about on par with a low end entry level cell phone, the kind that you can usually get for free with a contract (maybe barely a mid range and DEFINITELY not a flagship). It does NOT zoom, there is a digital zoom only. The good news is that it comes with a decent sized memory card and two batteries, so you can have a spare one ready to go. I wish it came with a battery charger so you can keep one on tap (the only way to charge the battery is IN the camera, which means you can't charge one while using the other sadly), but the fact you get a backup is nice at least.
The pictures aren't great, but they're fun for a kid to run around with. I can see an elementary school aged kid having fun with this, my 5 and 10 year old like it well enough. The item suggests "4-15 year old" and to be honest, I can NOT see a 15 year old enjoying this AT ALL. My 12 year old has a similar camera that is waterproof so at least she can say it's fun to use in the pool (which she does), but this kind of underwhelmed me for the asking price.

title: It is an OK value for the price, but there are much better
text:
I'm going to be 100% honest here: This is not a great tablet. I'm awarding it 4 out of 5 stars because of the value for the money, but as a Tablet alone I'd only give it 3 out of 5.
With a 10" display, Android 12 and a kid friendly case, you'd be hard pressed to find anything better for the money- especially with the current promotional discount being offered. But understand that for a little bit more, you can get something more brand-name, like a Lenovo M10 or TCL tab, and the performance and build quality of those will be better in my experience.
Granted, you also get the kid-proof case here, which is great, but other kid-friendly offerings come with things like CLAP software suite, which my daughter was hoping this had (her old one broke, and we've had two previous no-name tablets before which both had that software installed with no subscription needed). Otherwise, it gets the job done, works with Google services, and is powerful enough to get through basic tasks.

title: Fast, maybe slightly slower than advertised.
text:
At the current price, one might argue that nearly $1 per Gb of storage isn't such a great value compared to other SD cards. However when paired with a proper UHSii reader, those extra pins on the back of the card make this really scream!
When working in a professional environment with large files that need to move FAST, this is actually a pretty tool. I wasn't able to hit the 300MB/s rated speed on the label, but I got well into the 200s, still a great deal faster than your average UHSi or Class 10 SD card. I feel like I've gotten closer to that 300MBs advertised speed with other UHSii cards, however.

title: Pretty inexpensive yet fast card
text:
This is a pretty excellent little powerhouse for storage. My speeds weren't quite the ones advertised, however that might be my reader and laptop port being maxed out, as I don't think I've ever seen anything clock faster! I had over 1,000 in both read and write speeds, attaching a screenshot from Crystal Disk Bench for reference.
So far, I'm impressed with the value for the money.

title: Awesome and so very necessary
text: These are great, at the current price asked they amount to about 20c per battery, which is a great deal. They are basic no-frill Alkalines, and last about as expected. I used them on a job for a wireless mic and they performed as expected. Great to have in my gear bag. With the holiday season upon us, these are a good value to have.

title: With compatible media this is plenty fast
text:
I haven't tried the CFExpress function yet, I intend to this coming week when my media arrives, but for now I tested this with a UHS-II card I have. If you're unfamiliar, UHS-ii has the extra pins on the back of the card that allow additional throughput for faster speeds. Well, it's easily 3x faster than the same card in my regular SD reader. So, I can vouch for that working as expected!
Hoping the CF Express speeds are as expected as well, but something tells me they will absolutely be.

title: Properly identifies TRS vs TRRS!
text:
Rather than the pigtail style adapters I've used in the past to bring my much lamented headphone jack back, this plugs in with a very sturdy connection and simply extends the phone in a way that I find much more aesthetically pleasing and easy to wear in a jacket
But what impressed me most: It can detect the extra ring for headphones with a mic vs not! This is something the last few 3.5mm adapters I tried could not do! In other words, if you plug in headphones with an in-line mic, it can be used for calls instead of the phone's mic (great for keeping your phone in your pocket on a call). I confirmed this by tapping on the headphone mic vs the phone during a test call. But if you have standard stereo TRS headphones (the kind with one less ring since it lacks a mic), it will automatically use your phone's mic instead. Just like a real headphone on a phone would do!
The one thing I'm disappointed about, since it says it in the description, is the lack of fast charge capability. This says it supports PD charging, but I tried it on my OnePlus with the OEM charger and it did not work. That's ok, I figured the "Warp Charge" VOOC that OnePlus uses isn't compatible, so I tried a standard PD charger. That didn't work either. Odd, because it specifically says it should. So removing one star for that, but I'm loving the TRS/TRRS detection! It's about time I found one that did that correctly!

title: Great deal on a decent Alkalines
text:
At the current asking price, these end up being about 22.5 cents per battery, which is a pretty good deal. We loaded up some of my kids toy walkie-talkies and they seem to be holding up so far to expected battery length for an alkaline.
I'm not expecting anything amazing out of them, just standard off-brand batteries. The box it comes it sort of falls apart easily so don't expect to store them in that, but this is fine- I have a battery drawer I emptied the box into anyway. So far so good!

title: Great value, full blown PC for price of a chromebook!
text: [[VIDEOID:82687f9e04155b23b9ed3f252bae7b12]] This is a really interesting product. It's a modern full blown Windows 11 laptop, complete with solid state storage and USB-C capabilities, yet it is running an older Intel chip (5th generation). Keep in mind this i3 CPU is no slouch, even to today's standards. It can blast through daily computing and browsing, even media and light gaming without hiccups. It's still faster than modern generation Celeron chips found in similar priced laptops, the only hangup is that it is limited to DDR3 speed ram. But again, if you're not doing heavy high detail gaming, 4K video rendering or software compiling, you won't feel like this is slow at all. And I LOVE that it comes with a real ports like ethernet and HDMI. The USB-C port even can be used to charge with a PD charger, so you don't need to worry about the awkward proprietary DC connector. That's a big plus, I don't think that was very common when the 5th generation Intel silicon was new! All in all, this seems like a really solid reliable and versatile machine for the money.

title: Surprisingly fast mini PC
text:
I've had the pleasure of using and reviewing a lot of different mini PCs, so I have a pretty good baseline of what they should be capable of. This is definitely upper level for the price.
Generally, you should expect these to be somewhere around a budget laptop in performance, but I'm happy to say that this one actually exceeded my expectations! The 11th Gen Celeron actually outperforms a lot of laptop level processors, and is faster than almost all of my other mini PCs I've tried! Combined with the 16GB of DDR4, Windows 11 feels like more a breeze than it has any right to be at this size and price point!

This thing will zip through most basic computing tasks, or stream video like a champ. Don't expect much GPU performance, but if retro gaming is your thing, this is more than enough- in fact, a great deal faster and more powerful than most of the stuff out there people use for that task (Raspberry Pi, etc). The only thing I'm disappointed about, is the lack of USB-C. I mean, to be fair a lot of the mini PCs on the market inexplicably omit it as well, but it just seems like once we're on 11th Gen CPUs and Windows 11, why on earth are we still skimping on the most versatile connection port in existence currently?
It is so close to being perfect, but if you want a small footprint HTPC or digital signage setup, or just a way to turn any existing TV into a more-than-capable PC, this is a hard value to beat!

title: Durable, tiny and faster than advertised!
text: When connected to my PC's USB3 port, I am getting consistently over 300MB/s according to CrystalDiskMark. That's more than the advertised read speed, which is unexpected for product marketing! I love the size and solid metal body of this, it feels really durable and I think will hold up well. So far I'm very impressed with it!

title: Classy and look/sound great!
text:
These actually produce some pretty respectably great sound. The volume can crank pretty high without any distortion, and you can feel the bass kick. The features are great, allowing inputs from a line source, bt, or even a microphone to mix. I admit the mic part wasn't actually something I thought we'd be interested in, but it turns out sometimes that's fun to have too.

I also LOVE the wood color, and they look great on my wooden colored book shelves. The only problem? They are about 20-30% bigger than the bookshelf speakers I wanted to replace! I used to have black shelf speakers from Sony, then traded those in for wooden panel ones that didn't sound as good, and now these are the best of both worlds, but they are bigger than any of the previous options! They actually could not clear one of the shelves I was using because it is too tall. I guess that's what you get for having better sound (larger speaker usually produces better response), but I have to rearrange my shelf heights to permanently place it.

title: Incredible, but kinda pricey
text:
I'm a HUGE Sony fan, I own Sony TVs, headphones, cameras, even my car stereo is a Sony aftermarket install. I was very, very excited to try this monitor.
And I have to say... it's an excellent upgrade from my old one (but to be fair, my old gaming monitor was 1440p). The 4K resolution at this size feels like a retina display- seems like you need a magnifying glass to see any pixels. I love the style of it as well- the design is very reminiscent of the modern Playstation and would fit right in as a monitor for someone with a PS5. I really like the way the monitor even has some clever cable hiding features in the base, it's not just aesthetic, it's got a function.
The only downsides are that:
1) The angle of the base means it can't sit flush against a wall. If you've got a small room with a gaming desk along a wall, the monitor is going to sit a few inches away from the wall because of the stand.
2) It's almost obscenely expensive for a 4k monitor. I mean, my Sony 4k TV was half the price and larger than this is. Granted, this has some pretty sweet features like higher FPS and GSync, but it still seems like a pretty high price tag.

If you can justify the price, it's a solid product.

title: Excellent value for the price!
text:
I have to admit, I've used some cheap tablets which were pretty much hot garbage. This is actually quite good for the money!
Is this the greatest tablet? No, it isn't perfect. But you'd be hard pressed to find a better one under 100. The display is large and clear- not full 1080HD, but it's enough and still technically HD. The IPS panel makes it look good in any angle, and the 3GB of RAM gives a noticeable boost in reliability over the 2GB options I played with just a year ago in this price range.
The included iWawa app library is a nice parent-control kid friendly portal that can be used to lock down the device and give controlled screen time, and the included case and screen protector mean this thing is ready for your kid out of the box. Or, you can remove the case and have a respectable cheap 10" tablet for adulting. Pretty solid experience for the price.

title: First one broke, but replacement has been good!
text:
UPDATE 11/30/22: I received a warranty replacement for the one that stopped working, and I'm much happier now.
I still don't understand what happened to the first one or why it stopped working after 2 days, but so far so good. I just used this on a 14 hour road trip for a weekend, and it broadcast wifi to the whole car without bogging down my phone. It's still working now everytime we drive. I might have just gotten a lemon the first time.

Original review follows:
I wanted to give this 5 stars because I love the functionality, and it worked pretty great at first! I put a T-mobile SIM card in, and it just worked out of the box like that. When plugged into a Windows PC, it detected it as a modem, and on some Android tablets I was able to select USB tethering and it would work like that as well! And if not, it broadcasts its own wifi hotspot so on devices like my car's Android head unit, I could just find a free USB port and I could connect over Wifi instead.
I even managed to get a Verizon sim (Visible wireless) working by manually entering the APN in the web interface. Sure, it didn't have all the bands so the speed was limited (max I got was 25Mbps down and 30 up), but it worked!
...Until it didn't. I noticed that sometimes the speed would suddenly crawl. It would be reduced to 0.5 or less mbps. I was experimenting with it today, my 2nd day of owning it, to try and figure out if some devices perhaps didn't give it enough power or something, or find some common reason it would sometimes drop. And then it happened... it stopped showing up on anything. No Wifi network broadcast, no USB device detected, the unit just suddenly up and stopped. The blue light still turns on (which it did when starting up), but it now never turns green (how you know the connection is live). I left it for an hour to make sure it wasn't just slow, and it just refuses to do anything beyond show me a blue light. No network to connect to, so I can't even log in and see what's going on. There is a reset button pin, I tried jabbing that with a sim tool to reset and that doesn't seem to have fixed it either.

I did love it while it was working, but it seems very unreliable unless I just got a dud.

title: Incredible- makes canon lenses act like native, even on video!!
text:
[[VIDEOID:cb18324350d1c28569f9f048e4b15338]] I'm impressed with this adapter, it enabled native features like video autofocus, even on a cdaf only camera like the og a7s.
I've used the Sigma mc11, metabones and other adapters before and none of them have managed to do that! This might be the best features adapter I've ever tried!

title: Best Smartwatch I've ever tried
text:
[[VIDEOID:66d0cfc068044b66d6e031e8655e16e8]] This is the most fully featured Amazefit watch yet. You get the goodness of the zepp os new features (respond to notifications, etc), plus this model has a speaker. That means calls, talking to Alexa, even playing music is possible right from the watch.
The latest zepp os update brings some new third party apps, INCLUDING GAMES! And yet this goes for weeks on a charge. Incredible! See video for more.

title: Perfect as a remote input device!
text: [[VIDEOID:f90aa667c2d990ae24336e50755fa4ed]] This is an excellent way to control a mouse or touchscreen from a distance, or just extend the function of a laptop. See video for demonstration of how I used this in my car!

title: Very cool for HTPC, and includes IR remote!
text:
I've been using a trackpad/keyboard remote for my home theater PC for a while, and I really love the ergonomics of that setup (it looks like a game controller). But this product improves on it with a very welcome feature:
A programmable IR system. In other words, you can control the TV as well the PC attached to it on the same remote!

When holding in the normal remote orientation (pointing towards the screen), buttons like power can be programmed and work as you'd expect an OEM remote would. If you want to move the mouse on the screen, press the mouse toggle button and the control works via accelerometers, sort of like swinging a wii remote. Move your wrist in the air, and the cursor mimics your hand waves. The only issue I have with this vs a trackpad, is that sometimes it feels like my movements aren't as precise... it's easy to overshoot your target, and you need to be careful to get the mouse exactly where you want before clicking. The act of clicking sometimes moves the cursor a little bit also, so it takes a little getting used to at first. The orientation also can shift depending on what direction you were in when toggling the mouse mode on- unlike a wii remote which has a sensor bar to know which way is forward, sometimes you may find that "forward" drifts to the right or left of the room. This doesn't take long to get oriented, but trackpads seem to have a smaller learning curve in my opinion. That's the only reason I'd remove a star.
Otherwise, I love the way it works. Turn the remote over and hold it sideways to input from the QWERTY keyboard, and there are toggles to turn on/off a backlight and the mouse (so you don't go moving a cursor around every time you put it down, lol). The batteries are not rechargeable, but that just makes it easier to replace and keep going when you finally used them up. Mine haven't needed replacing yet so I'm still loving this!

title: Good head unit, excellent customer support!
text:
[[VIDEOID:5f99a990ea71fc33e4d54b09c37038e2]] EDIT January 2023: I originally complained that Bluetooth used to only reconnect to the last phone used. This is an issue with all of their Android powered head units apparently, as the S8 did the same. However, I'm happy to say that customer support came though with a modified firmware that FIXED the problem! It will try to connect to the last device, but if not found will move on to connect to other previously-paired phones, as expected. I am now very happy with the unit for the asking price. Definitely would recommend!

Originally review follows:
Before I go into what I don't like, let me tell you what this product is:
This is a buttonless edition of their popular A6 PF head unit. I can't tell if it is identical to the button version internally, but if you like the look of a smooth bezel-less design, this is the head unit to try!
I have tried and owned a few of their devices and largely love what you can get for the money. That's not even counting that their customer support has been EXTREMELY responsive! However there is one major user experience problem I just can't get past which makes it hard to recommend this to my friends.
If you are the only driver of your car, you'll likely never know or care about this, but all of Atoto's Android powered units (S8 included) will only pair automatically with the last phone used. That means if you share the car with other family members, and they drove the car last, your phone won't auto-connect next time you drive. It will be stuck looking for THAT phone (the last one) in perpetuity. You had to manually go into the settings for BT1 and find the list of paired phones, then click on yours, and THEN it will connect. Only to repeat this process the next time someone else drives and wants their phone to connect. It's silly, honestly. Their F7 doesn't do this, but the S8 also did. Most name-brand head units will move on to the next device in their paired list if the last one isn't found, I don't see why this device can't do that. They claimed it has something to do with security and specifically with Android units (which would be why the F7, based on linux does not have this limitation?). It does not make any sense to me and is a complete user experience failure, to the point that my wife has told me she might want us to go back to our old OEM head unit- at least that one would auto-connect to whoever is driving the car, regardless of who drove it last!
See attached video for demonstration.

title: Good deal on name brand, no frills package
text:
This appears to be a legitimate Samsung branded SSD, offered at a lower than usual price because it comes in a no-frills plastic case. No documentation, no box, no additional hardware, just the drive. If I had to guess, I'd say these are packaged for bulk sales, and being sold at a discount directly to consumers.
The down side is that these are not formatted or partitioned to be recognized by a computer at first. Plugging it in as a secondary drive, Windows did not detect anything was there. You need to use Admin Tools or a utility like DiskGenius to find and partition the storage, then format it.
It also did not come with the infamously difficult to find M2 screw. If you don't already have a screw, these little oddly sized threaded metal bits are necessary to hold the drive in place. If you are replacing an older one, you already have one. If not, you better have one on the board or adapter you plan to put this on. The last M2 drive I bought came with one to use when mounting, I wish this came with one. But that's what you get in a no-frills package.
The performance of the drive is pretty great though, no complaints.

title: Not multi-user friendly, but pretty good
text:
[[VIDEOID:d7dac93a9ae5119758136812fcd18f71]] I'm very familiar with Atoto as a brand, I've used 3 of their aftermarket radios on different vehicles previously so I was excited to try this one.

I'll go into a full blown review in a moment, but first let me point out the problem no one seems to be talking about:
This is great and really easy to use (wireless Android Auto even automatically starts on power up) ...as long as you are the only driver of the car. You see, the Bluetooth system can pair with multiple phones, but it will only look for the last one you used when it boots up. Share the car with a family member? You'll have to go into the bluetooth menu and find the list of paired phones, click on yours and THEN it will connect and work properly, and it will continue to do so automatically whenever you get back into the car, as expected. But when that family member drives again? They'll have to do the same thing for their phone, taking the auto-connect away from yours! It's very very frustrating if you have multiple drivers on a family vehicle.
Atoto has similar functionality on their Android powered A6 and S8 units, however not their F7 (linux powered). They told me it has to do with the way Android security works, however this unit does not run Android natively so I assumed it would be like the F7. Sadly not. I can't recommend this unit to families or multiple users of a vehicle for that reason.

Otherwise, if you're the lone driver of your car, and you have an older car that lacks Android Auto (or even Bluetooth), this is DEFINITELY worth looking into. It offers Bluetooth for calls and music streaming as well as full blown Android Auto to mirror your apps to the display (both wired and wirelessly), yet requires no modification to your dash.

The concept is a good one, I know plenty of people who would love these features but don't want to replace their OEM radio. And for the most part, it works well- I like the way it is a single harness and one cable going down to the DC port, your aux/USB/etc all plugs down there. Similar units from other brands I've seen had all ports on the screen unit, so everything (USB port, aux, power, etc) was yet another wire going up to the dash top and looking like a spidery-mess. Hiding one wire is much more manageable. And you have the options of using aux out, FM out, or just using the unit's own loudspeaker.
I really hope Atoto will realize they need the bluetooth system to look for other paired phones when the last one used doesn't connect. OEM factory bluetooth systems work like that for a reason, and there is no security excuse here.

title: Excellent and convenient power delivery
text: This is a great power delivery system. It not only offers some outlets that are generously spaced apart (somewhat adapter friendly), but it also has USB ports with LED lights inside so that you can find them easily in the dark. Great for a dorm room or for travel, especially because the flat plug means you can hide it behind furniture and make an otherwise difficult to reach outlet more accessible.

title: Solid product, better than other meshes
text:
First of all, Wifi6 meshes are the way to go!
I'm coming from a TP-link Deco product as my Wifi 6 mesh, and I can honestly say this is much better as far as actual internet service goes. The TP-Link was very good, much MUCH better than a router + extender for coverage in my home, but certain devices seemed to drop connections when in between nodes. Most devices were fine, I just figured it was because they were too old to be fully WiFi 6 compatible, but now I'm seeing with this Dlink mesh that even devices I thought weren't so compatible can WORK FINE!
A few things I don't like:
- Set up and controls aren't as cool and refined as the TP-Link app. This is all web based like the traditional DLink routers of yesteryear. Don't get me wrong, no reason to fix what aint broke, but after using the TP-link Deco app, I think I'm spoiled by it. It would alert me whenever a new device hopped on to the network and give me real time stats and updates. And making changes was easy too. I wish this had that.
The Dlink setup here was a little slower and less intuitive, and you lose out on some of those live features.
- The units seem to take a long time to boot back up after disconnection. That means when there's a power outage or you just need to reboot in case of a problem, it could take a few minutes longer for everything to work again.

That being said, it works REALLY well once it is all up and running, which is really wonderful. There are enough ports for 3 hardwired ethernet connections as well as a dedicated yellow port for the modem (other devices like the TP link focus on wireless and make you use one of the 3 plugs for the modem). It's also a bit slimmer than other mesh systems and I like that the light in front turns off when it is set up and running which helps keep things looking tidy and unassuming (the TP-link nodes had a glowing light that was on all the time and was distracting when hiding on, say, a bookshelf or kitchen counter).

All in all, I'm really happy with the performance of this and I would highly recommend it.

title: Dirt cheap SSD
text:
I can't believe how inexpensive SSDs are now, I was very skeptical this could be a real product at this price tag but sure enough, there it is- giving me roughly 450MB/s read and 415 MB/s write. Granted these are no where near even the most basic NVMe speeds, but it is still easily 2-3x your average mechanical spinning drive and a fraction of the power consumption. So if you're looking to boot fast or upgrade an old spinning mechanical drive, this price is a no brainer.
I don't know how long it will last, as another reviewer said the actual chips used internally aren't bad- they are well known and mass produced. But there's no guarantees as this Fikwot brand hasn't been around long enough to have a reputation for longevity. I'm happily using it to revive an old laptop and turn it into a chromebook. It is plenty fast and a bargain for the price.

title: Another top notch product from Sony
text:
I'll admit, I'm a fan of Sony. I've owned all sorts of things from the brand, from the aftermarket stereo in my car to my professional camera equipment I use at work. They just make reliably good products. However I've mostly owned Samsung television sets just because it's what I had access to on a more regular basis.
I was therefore excited to try out this TV and see how it compared. To be honest, I really REALLY like Sony's color science. It's part of why I prefer their camera equipment, and it shows on this display. The contrast ratio and dynamic range are everything I wanted it to be and more. The skin tones as well, however the average consumer probably wouldn't notice or care about these things. Where the big differences lie in major TV brands these days is going to be features. The latest crop of Smart TVs have so many bells and whistles, you practically don't need anything other than an internet connection anymore. Unlike Samsung's UI which has embraces Amazon's Fire Stick style UI, Sony has gone the Google TV route. There are pros and cons to both approaches, although I think perhaps arguably there isn't as much free included content as Samsung (Samsung actually includes free live TV channels via "Samsung TV", which Sony does not have). But for all the content I actually WANT to see, Netflix, Prime, Disney+ etc, it works perfectly!

So why only 4 stars? This isn't the fault of Sony's TV, but I really wish they'd make it easier to spot and turn off... I really REALLY hate the default motion smoothing (aka "soap opera effect") that all the big brands use these days. As a content creator, I shoot videos in a particular frame rate on purpose. The motion blur or lack thereof helps tell the story in some kinds of scenes. But most TVs want to show off their high refresh rate and therefore use realtime smoothing algorithms to create fake overly-dramatic effects to pump out extra in between frames. The motion looks too smooth to the point it seems CGI (because it sort of is). It just looks off once you notice it, and Sony is no exception. You have to dig around and figure out what they call it on every TV just to make it look normal again, on this set it is called Motionflow and it can be confusing to turn it off. I wish manufacturers would make it a simple and easy to understand toggle switch... maybe even present it as an option to the viewer upon setting it up so they can understand what they are enabling and decide if they want it or not (I strongly recommend not!).
But again, that's true of all modern Television sets, on its own right this is a solid TV and I would recommend it.

title: So much potential, but some odd quirks hold it back
text:
I want to start off saying this thing has INCREDIBLE potential. For the same price as a mini PC, you can get a fully fledged tablet running a desktop version of Windows! Not only that, but the build quality seems pretty incredible for a cheap tablet, the back of it is actually a rubberized material that keeps it free of fingerprints and slipping out of your hands... it doesn't need a case, in other words. I haven't used a tablet that I felt didn't need a case in years!
It has limited storage, but that's expected of a cheap computing machine. It does have an expandable slot for additional storage, and the 4GB of ram is enough for most basic computing. You're not going to be using this for high end gaming, but you can plow through most desktop and office applications as well as browsing and streaming without a hiccup. The things that bothered me, however are:
a) It has USB-C, but does not allow itself to be charged with it. Unlike modern tablets and laptops that use PD chargers to juice up over the USBC, this actually uses a tiny proprietary plug that is almost certainly going to get lost eventually. It's not like it will be easy to find replacements or backups unlike major brands like HP and Lenovo, if I ever lose this plug I'm probably out of luck. I don't understand why it couldn't have used PD over the USB-c like every other modern device.
b) This one is a little bit more serious, but it complains that Windows is not activated. If you try to activate it, you are told that the server won't allow activation and to contact the vendor. I'm not entirely sure how to do that, and instead I'm left with a suspiciously inactivated version of Windows. Feels almost like for this price the software isn't licensed, which concerns me. I'm going to try and found out what it will take to activate, but it is definitely something you should know before plunking down money on a tablet that might not be using legitimate software.
Otherwise it is pretty useful for the price.

title: Small size of the GTS2 mini, but with advances features of the 3 series
text:
I love Amazefit watches. We've owned everything from Fitbit and Galaxy wear, and this is still my favorite. I even convinced my wife to give up her Google WearOS device for one of them! They are pretty accurate health monitors and can last long enough to be charged 1-2x per month, and this model is no exception. I'm a little bit confused by the naming system, since this came out before there is any other 4 series watch, the regular GTS and GTR are still on generation 3, and as far as I know there was never a "mini" series 3, so it seems the GTS mini jump a generation from 2 to 4.
However, it retains the form factor and square screen of the 2 and adds the new features of Zepp OS from the 3 series! If you are wondering what's new, that means you get the ability to now reply to messages (emojis or pre-defined lines of text only for now. The replies can be edited in the app), and there's actually a slowly growing APP STORE! Nothing fancy in it yet, but it is showing potential. There are some useful mini apps and even a couple of games now. Very cool if coming from the 2 series and a worthy upgrade. I love this brand so much, I'm surprised more people haven't heard of them!

title: A budget Teradek?!
text:
I've used wireless HD systems for productions before- whether to monitor a camera op from a distance, or send a wireless cameraman on stage as part of a live multi-camera gig. Usually we would rent Teradek equipment from someone like B&H since the gear can cost thousands. There are cheaper options I've seen before, but they usually have a noticeable lag of nearly 2 seconds, or require too much setup to be portable (designed to plugged into a source of power, etc).
This product blew me away. I'm not kidding. It is clearly designed for mountable use, with tripod style 1/4" - 20 threading as well as standard Sony NP-F battery mounts, you can easily mount this to a camera rig and go live. The delay is almost non-existent, and I'd say close enough to get away with on a live broadcast mixed with wired cameras. It gets a little bit warm when using, but not any worse than an Atmos Ninja recorder. For the price, this is almost too good to be true! I wasn't expecting to be as impressed as I am, it's really very VERY good at almost 1/10th the price of a Teradek!

title: Worked for a moment and then never again.
text:
I bought this to use in my minivan's A6 pf to send the video out to the rear seats. The plan was to be able to stream content throughout the car.
At first it did not seem to be doing anything, there is a glowing red LED so I know it's connected but nothing appeared on the external screen. At some point during testing I saw what appears to be a casting icon on the top of the display and the screen was mirroring, but I have been unable to get that to happen again. I tried resetting, changing USB ports, changing monitors to a portable RCA input screen I have... I even tried it on my other car which has an Atoto S8 ultra (gen 2). Both of these radios are listed as compatible yet nothing worked. I don't know if I just got a lemon but this has not at all been working. It comes with no instructions so there isn't even any troubleshooting guide to follow.

title: Good music player with streaming apps. Sort of Android, but not necessarily what you think
text:
Yes, the UI and apps are very clearly Android. No, it isn't a mini tablet.
Players like this are an interesting market that is hard to pin the audience down for. There are music players that are cheap on the market for those that would rather have a dedicated player (ie, not their phone). However the user interface tends to be wonky and slow, and newer generation features like bluetooth 5+ and streaming are often a mixed bag, if even available.
The idea behind players like this one, is that it is based on a supported operating system (Android, in this case) so it can play almost any format you throw at it, has plenty of support for popular streaming apps and features, as well as a familiar user interface that is already so polished, it seems silly to reinvent the wheel like the super cheap older media players.
Is it a mini tablet or phone without service? Not exactly. This is not a Google certified device, it does not have the play store or any Google apps on it. Unlike some other Android based players, I couldn't even get sideloaded apk files to install (it kept throwing errors at me). It seems like this device was purposely locked down to keep it an mp3 player. That's good in some ways, my kids aren't allowed unlimited screen time and their schools don't want them bringing smartphones around, so this is a strictly music-player oriented device (especially once you remove things like the browser for them, which it allows you to do). But I also know there are more capable players out there, some of which have quad DAC audio chips. Also, what happens when an app gets updated and goes out-of-date? Sometimes streaming services make changes and updated clients are required for it to work, however you are largely stuck with the version that this came with unless they issue a firmware update or something.
This is still cheaper than the higher end mp3 players that support high end DAC and app updates, but not by much. It seems to be a sort of in-between product. If you have a use for something like this, it could be a pretty good option. But if you're expecting a handheld tablet or alternative concept to an ipod touch, it is not exactly that.

title: Excellent for DIY repairs
text:
I can't scientifically test the 200lbs capacity claimed, but I can tell you this: These are great for attaching things to other things.
Heat shield falling off the bottom of my minivan? No problem, zip tie it back up! Attach the hose to the slip and slide and prevent it from leaking? Zip tie! These are LARGE so they can wrap around a large diameter and are very strong. So far they have worked extremely well. Highly recommended!

title: I don't understand what device this works with.
text:
I could not get this to to work.
I use AV equipment for a living, and sometimes I need to convert an HDMI signal to an analog RCA one. In the past I've had to use an adapter (box powered by 5v) to achieve that. I was hoping this was somehow a streamlined version of that which is self powered or something (I know HDMI ports have some residual power), but that doesn't seem to be the case.
I see on the description here that it "can't be directly transferred from PC, laptop, DVD, PS4, xbox and other devices with HDMI interface to TV." So then what DOES it work for?
I tried connecting several types of devices to the RCA input of a TV and nothing seems to work. I tried a Firestick, a camera, an Android box, Raspberry Pi, mini PC, etc. Nothing.

I'm scratching my head trying to understand what on earth this could be used for. I think I'd recommend a traditional HDMI digital to analog RCA converter box if you're trying to go from one to the other.

title: These work great!
text: Well I'm not running 8k, but it ran my 2.5k monitor just fine from my DP port of my Nvidia card to the HDMI in of my monitor. Replaced the old DP to HDMI adapter I used to run in order to plug a long HDMI cable in. This is so much cleaner and nicer, highly recommended.

title: Looks good, works great
text:
A solid adapter for bringing access to power in otherwise difficult to reach places. I love that I can fit this behind furniture like bookshelves or desks thanks to the flat plug, and then fasten it using the screw holes anywhere more convenient (shelves, desk, nightstand, etc).
The included USB ports are great as well. I use this behind our home electric Piano. The piano plugs into the AC part and a tablet with sheet music charges off the USB. The whole thing is installed on the side of the piano legs where it looks almost like it was designed to go! A very good looking product that serves a real useful purpose.

title: Great way to add volume knob to a setup (I used it to mod my custom radio)
text:
This is useful for so many things. If you want a big easy to use knob for your gaming setup or live audio production rig, this is a really great way to avoid having to hunt for buttons or click volume controls with your mouse. I like that the LED glows under the knob, but I sort of wish it stayed on all the time so I could find it quickly in the dark (it lights up during use, but then seems to turn off the light after a few seconds of non use).
Personally, I wanted to use this to add a volume knob to my aftermarket car radio. For some reason, new head units all rely on buttons and touch screens, but I want a good old fashioned volume knob. Thankfully this is compatible pretty universally as a USB input device (no drivers, so even Android can recognize it!) so I can pop off the knob and drill a hole in my double din adapter to mount the knob behind my dash. Plug it in, and it changes the volume as needed. Awesome! It isn't designed to work this way, you're supposed to just connect it to a desktop I think, but the fact that it worked the way I wanted means this makes it also a great modder/hacker/tinkerer's tool.

title: Let me adapt my 2nd monitor to the DP port of my GPU!
text: I have matching LG monitors which support only HDMI in, and I want to use them both on my desktop. My video card has 1x HDMI and 2x Displayport plugs, so I used to use a DP to HDMI cable. However over time, that cable seems to have started giving me trouble. I swapped it out with this and now use a high quality HDMI cable from this adapter to my 2nd monitor. It has been working PERFECTLY and I couldn't be happier with the product. Does exactly what I needed.

title: Does what it says, as long as you understand this is a USB2.0 cable
text:
This is not a fast cable. But it tells you that right away, so anyone expecting a USB 3.0 speed adapter should have read the description and gone elsewhere.
I wanted this for a multi-port charger I keep next to my bed which offers 4 USBC ports to charge devices. I have some older things that rely on standard USB-A charging cables, so I needed one of these to supplement the available ports. It works perfectly, and delivers the standard USB port power I needed. It can also plug into your phone or tablet to give you a standard USB host port, but just understand you will be limited to the older (but still very good) USB 2.0 standard. That's fine for most things, but if you're copying files from USB storage to your Macbook's thunderbolt port, you might want to get at least a USB3 speed adapter.

title: Excellent for the asking price!
text:
OnePlus already has standard buds which are more expensive than these. I've tried those and was fairly impressed with them for the price compared to other leading brands (*cough* airpods). I'll be honest, I wasn't sure what to expect here with these "Nord" brand ones. Nord is supposed to be OnePlus' value brand, and the price reflects that. I've tried out headphones that cost more than this which I didn't care for, so I was a little anxious.
However, I have to admit I'm fairly impressed. They sound better to me than other wireless earbuds at this price range. While they aren't as well made as the standard Oneplus buds, they aren't bad at all, especially for the money. Much like the Nord phones themselves, Oneplus seems to know how to make a value product that punches way above its price tag.
I know the brand has taken a hit lately with their Android 12 offerings (still holding out for OOS13 to fix this colorOS mess they are in), but I can say with confidence that their earbuds are pretty great and worth considering whether or not you are a fan of the brand.

title: Fast and reliable storage
text: As a photographer, I recognize Lexar as a trusted storage media brand, up there with Sandisk and other industry brand names. This product does not disappoint- in benchmarks, it appears to perform as advertised. And for the money, you get a very healthy amount of usable storage at U3 rated speeds! This is great in my DJI Mavic as well as GoPros and other recording equipment. Definitely recommended.

title: A level over over mini PCs
text:
I've owned quite a few Mini PCs, I love them for digital signage and use as HTPCs. Usually they are somewhat basic Celeron chips to keep power consumption low, and have pretty much bare-basic specs to stream video. In many, components are soldered onto the board and not user upgradeable.
But THIS one struck my eye for a few core differences:
1) The CPU, while still a Celeron, is much beefier than the J4125 CPUs I've used in the past. In fact, this one seems to rival a 10th gen i3 in performance benchmarks, if I'm reading these numbers correctly. I believe it- using this the system feels pretty snappy as long as you don't bog it down with intensive tasks like media encoding or compiling.
2) USB-C! Finally, I don't know why so many mini PCs skimp on this all-too-useful port. But this one has a USB3 standard A as well as a USB-C port. Thank you for this!
3) User upgradable RAM. Another major plus compared to some which have everything soldered onto a single board.

All in all, this is a solid offering. I'm not familiar with this brand, but I've seen similar specs on a device from Beelink, and can say the asking price seems pretty spot on for the specs. I'd say it is a good deal if you're in the market for a mini PC.

title: Surprisingly loud and portable
text: The speaker is small and portable enough to fit into a large pocket yet can produce some very respectable volume with its 14W power. My daughter found this is a great way to turn a fanny pack into a hip-mounted sound system (she's a counselor in a summer camp and using this speaker a lot). The sound is surprisingly immersive and the fact that it is waterproof enough to use around the pool or in the rain is a huge bonus. Great speaker!

title: Step up your cell phone content production!
text:
[[VIDEOID:b24da4d426cb291b56dc311a2d09dc8e]] If you've got a USB-C port and no 3.5mm input, THIS is the mic adapter you need! The phone receiver is so clean looking, it plugs directly into the port and is self powered by your phone, so no additional batteries or charging needed. It just sits there, like a chin bump. The transmitter needs 2 AAA batteries (4 if you want to use both transmitters).
Note: On some devices like the OnePlus phones, the built in camera app doesn't recognize external microphones, so you'll need to download something like Open Camera (excellent free app I recommend anyway for more camera control). Pixel and Samsung phones I tried this with did not require that.
ALSO- when this is plugged in, it registers itself as a "headset" to the phone, so it will not play back audio until you unplug it. I was able to monitor the audio via the headphone jack going in, but then I could not hear it recorded until I unplugged the receiver. This is simply how it works on Android and not the fault of the unit, however it would be nice if a future version could route outgoing sound over the included headphone jack (I was a bit disappointed it did not do this, however the product was so good I still want to give it 5 stars).

title: Great value, large space
text:
I had another pocket USB SSD from this brand that is larger (500gb) so I already knew what to expect, and I was NOT disappointed! These are excellent and fast when used with a USB 3.2 port. I was able to reach around the advertised speeds on the packaging with the right ports on my desktop.
The capacity is INSANE! This little guy is the same size as one of my laptop's internal SSDs, yet can be carried around on my keychain. I love that these exist and recommend them!

title: Phenomenal cosmic powers....
text:
I know the line "tiny yet powerful" gets thrown around alot, but I mean it for real here. The 500gb storage on this drive I'm trying matches my internal SSD in space, yet plugs into a USB and fits on my keychain! In other words, I can back up my entire drive C: and carry it around with me. That's awesome.
And the speed is super impressive over a USB3 connection, pretty close to the advertised speed (It is plugged into a hub for this test, so expect real world direct connection to be slightly higher). I can understand why some people might prefer a USB-C version of this for modern laptops, but the computers I'm using all offer USB3 in the full size A port, so no complaints here. I knew what I was getting and was NOT disappointed!

title: Best bang for your buck in tablets!
text:
[[VIDEOID:33b9e8cfecdf6f700ec0f6e6b36a3153]] I'll cut to the chase: Is this the best performing gaming tablet on the market? No.
But is it one of the best in the price range? Absolutely YES.

And when you consider that flagship Snapdragon 8 class options such as the Galaxy Tab S8 can cost 4-5x as much as this one, you have to consider that they aren't actually 4-5x BETTER for the money. The rest of the specs (storage, ram, sim slot, etc) are all pretty similar to this one, but for a price that makes this a no brainer to me.
I bought a Lenovo M10+ FHD last year for work related apps that require a lot of document reading, and it was almost the same price as this but with very VERY weak specs in comparison. I wish I had known about this back then instead!

title: Good softbox, upgrade your light
text:
If you've been using just umbrellas or cheap diffusers, you owe it to yourself to try a large softbox modifier like this. The light comes out so controlled and flattering, and the standard bowens mount means it works with strobes as well as constant video lights.
The construction is pretty good but it isn't so easy to assemble or fold if this is your first time using one. Practice with it before using it on a gig so you don't look silly trying to figure it out.

title: Works, but could be better.
text:
It does what it claims- it's bone conduction so the sound doesn't need to cover your ears to be audible. That's great if you want/need open ears so that you can hear those around you. However there are brand name versions of this that are much clearer. This is good, and it works, but the sound quality is going to be lacking some fidelity if you're looking for rich musical notes compared to earbuds in this price range. Everything has a sort of heavy treble tone to it.
The microphone is pretty good, as long as you don't mind it always sticking out. Even if you twist it away, it's always there, just pointing behind you. You can't really remove it. Callers can hear me, and much better than other headsets that have a mic up by your ears. I wish it could be removed to look a little less in-your-face when you don't need it. Also, I wish the unit had USB-C like all other new devices. This has the older micro-USB plug. I still have plenty of those in my wire bin, but most of my newer tech uses C and I prefer to have one set of cables for most things (my laptop, phone, over-hear phones, etc, all use USBC now). Just feels like they could have made this a little bit better. But it works.

title: It works, but no microphone. I still miss my phone's native jack. (not TRRS?)
text:
For the record: I hate this trend in mobile phones to push us away from a standard 3.5mm jack. I tried to hold onto a phone that had one for as long as I could, but when my Galaxy S10 had to go, I needed an adapter. I love using my high end studio IEMs for music instead of bluetooth or cheap USB-C headphones, and sometimes if my bluetooth earpiece isn't charged, I want to grab my laptop headphones with their in-line mic to do handsfree calls.
Well, I'm happy to say at least I can use this for music with my IEMs and other wired headphones. But I think the jack might be TRS and not TRRS. That means it is missing the extra pin to support the microphone if your headphones have one.
In a nutshell, this will turn a pair of regular stereo (no mic) headphones into a USBC compatible one, but it still isn't as good as a native 3.5mm jack. The real ones used to detect if there was a mic pin attached and give you the ability to use your headphone mic, or use the phone's mic if there wasn't the extra pin. This just defaults to no pin.

title: Not professional, but one of the better ones this price bracket
text:
[[VIDEOID:91ed971de75e2a1d366c0694560e3ad4]] Let's get this metric straight: Those who are saying a projector under $300 looks good, are probably comparing it to other cheap off-brand projectors. I've tried a few of these to use as throwaround backyard movie night things, when I don't want to get my expensive prosumer home theater ones dirty or burn out the bulb, and they all suffer from things like flat colors, lack of brightness (fudging the lumens numbers) and the worst: Inconsistent focus. Nothing makes me crazier than trying to nail the focus and finding the center focuses while the borders are out of focus, but adjusting for the edges makes the center out of focus. Usually this is because the lens is cheap and lacks proper rectilinear support, and it is MADDENING once you notice it. In short, sometimes you might find it looks better on a smaller TV than a bigger washed out and fuzzy projector.
But... usually, you should expect to pay somewhere towards DOUBLE this for a brand name projector that looks decent, so I'm trying to keep my expectations realistic for the price range. And I have to say, this is the first one that actually seems to have proper focus across the projected image! I mean, you do get some chromatic aberration in the corners (see image and video attached), but this is nothing compared to others in the sub-300 dollar range. I love that this also has built in features like miracast (which I tried and works great!) as well as an Office Suite so you can technically show a presentation without a laptop or casting device- just plug in a USB stick with your content and go!
These are not necessary in my opinion, I'd rather have better colors and sharpness than gimmicks, but honestly I think this might be the best of the lower end projectors I've tried yet! If you care about how your movies and presentations look, I'd still recommend a brand name like Viewsonic at the bare minimum. But this is fun for the kids, backyard movie nights, or impromptu presentations when a bigger and more expensive projector wouldn't be cost justifiable.

title: I want to give this more stars, I love it so much!
text:
This thing is AMAZING. It is tiny and discreet, and easily hides on or behind furniture without attracting attention to it. And it works as expected!
I have a Honeywell fan that we use to circulate air in a room with cathedral-style ceilings (gets very hot in the summer), but we're always forgetting where the remote went. With this product, I hid the IR Blaster on a shelf in line-of-sight of the fan, and programmed it using the app on my phone. It did not have the exact Honeywell codes for my fan in their library of known devices, but no problem- that's what the DIY learning mode is for! I dug up the original remote and pressed the buttons while aimed at the device in learning mode, and it was able to accurately repeat them towards the fan upon command after that.
The app does not have a schedule option, but it does connect with Alexa as a skill and that's exactly what I wanted since we use Alex routines for home automation. I set some on/off schedules and now we just let it run itself as needed, and manually override it with an Alexa voice command or the app on my phone when needed. So far, it has worked EXACTLY as expected and I couldn't be happier with it! Awesome!

title: A budget friendly Surface alternative
text:
[[VIDEOID:75569821202ef0194cf65687a61f63d]] This is a fully featured 11th Generation Intel laptop in a tablet form factor. I love Windows on a Tablet, I've been a fan ever since the original Lenovo Yoga convertibles and Microsoft Surface tablets went mainstream.
The only problem I've had with those Windows tablet concepts is that sometimes you encounter applications that were designed for a mouse and keyboard rather than a touch screen. And that's what makes Windows 11 so great: You can finally run Android Apps thanks to built in virtual machine support. This is the first time I'm trying a Windows 11 Tablet, and I have to admit there's some initial setting up to do to get Android app support working (you can't just download an APK like I was expecting to). But once you do, it's pretty awesome and works the way I imagined and expected!
I'm not familiar with the brand Alldocube, but I have to admit the iWorkGT is actually pretty solid, has good build quality and an excellent display for the money. Since you are running an actual X86 Intel CPU, you're going to get a powerful experience compared to an anemic ARM processor like a traditional tablet would have, but the trade off is it will need to cool itself off like a laptop sometimes. That means vents and fans, which you will feel in your hands.
And this leads me to the cons:
There is NO CASE included with this product in the box. And since it is not a major brand like the Microsoft Surface, finding third party cases are going to be difficult if not impossible. Alldocube does sell 2 keyboard style cases which are interesting, however they are sold separately and not cheap! Sure, this is a lot less than a Surface, but at least a surface has plenty of after market cases and holders for every style and budget. I can't help feeling like it should have come with at least some sort of basic protection case. Even the Surface at least gives you the kickstand to stand it up, with this you have a portable computer that can get warm in your hands and nothing to really hold it in or stand it up with. You NEED to purchase one of their cases here.
The other con is that I did notice some strange behavior at times- the tablet wouldn't charge the first time I used it until I turned it off and rebooted. Another time the sound didn't work, and also wouldn't come back until I rebooted. That second time could have been due to the Android virtual machine being set up (it was right after trying it for the first time) and hasn't come back since, but I feel like it is worth mentioning sometimes there are quirks. But overall my experience has been positive and I enjoy using it, I just really strongly recommend getting one of their keyboard cases.

title: Comes with EVERYTHING! But the average cell phone has better IQ
text:
Ok, to be fair I work with cameras for a living. I wasn't expecting this to compete with my cinema cameras or even popular DSLRs for video, but I was expecting it to at least hold up to the standards people are expecting from cell phone cameras these days. It doesn't. Aside from filling a 4K frame, there aren't a lot of positives to say about the video quality.
To be fair, this has a LOT of advantages over using a cell phone. Recording for long lengths of time onto an SD card is a big plus, not the mention the ability to mount it to a standard tripod and have accessories like a mic and light attached to the body (which are all included!). It comes with a wide angle lens (that is oddly called "macro", but no- it's not for macro shots, its for going wider) which screws on to the front, as well as a handle mounting bracket, an LED light and a microphone. It even comes with a 64GB card, a spare battery, and not one but TWO useful carrying cases (a large one for everything, and a smaller one for just the camera solo). But that's about all the positives I can say about it. If you are outside with a lot of light, you can get decent shots, but this isn't a zoom lens, the zoom is digital only. You can go wide with the external lens or just stay at a fixed medium without it. So no closeup shots for soccer moms. The dynamic range when using it indoors was pretty bad, worse than your average mid-range cell phone. Forget about low light. But that's ok, because the ergonomics of a camera make it better than a cell phone, right?
Well, sorta. Holding it with the strap and the flip out screen is nice. But the UI is confusing, it's hard to go back and watch clips you took because everything is kind of sluggish and not intuitive- once we went past the first page of recorded clips, it was really difficult to move to the next page without accidentally clicking and opening a clip for playback. It just feels really laggy to navigate. Then there's the mic input... it's actually a proprietary plug that goes into the charging/USB plug, and gives you a pigtail for USB on one side and a mic input jack on the other. Odd, considering it COMES with a mic, you'd think it would have an input directly on the body. But no, just this weird mess of wires. Everything about this feels like jumping through a hoop to make it do what you want, and at the end of the day you have to wonder if you couldn't just be better off getting a mic adapter for the cellphone you already own and putting it in one of those holster cages.
Speaking of cell phones, this does have an app which supposedly lets you remotely control and perhaps even copy files from it, but I didn't get that far. I tried to install the app but then gave up when I decided I didn't want to grant this all the permissions it wanted from my personal phone. And I didn't think the video quality was worth it either.
Oddly enough, I kind of like the accessories it comes with. The LED light is pretty nice, the mic isn't terrible either. But for the money, I feel like I would have rather skipped those accessories and just gotten a better camera for a little bit more. It feels almost like they realized this camera was a hard sell so they beefed it up with lots of a accessories for the price.
In conclusion, you DO get a lot of accessories for the money. It's not the worst camera I've ever used, and you can't really get a set with everything you need for any less so I'd say it's worth at least 3 stars for being a functional kit. But I can't really imagine a scenario that I would recommend it.

title: For when you need a LOT of ram (but not the fastest)!
text:
Since it doesn't say anywhere on the listing, the timings for this memory are 22-22-22-52 and running at the listed 3200mhz. This is with the standard JDEC spec, which was recognized by my MSI motherboard, and the XMP profile is not supported (so turn XMP off, it'll just confuse the bios at worst or be disabled at best).
I have a workstation that I use to render out video and animation, the process of which can often eat up oodles of RAM. I was previously using gaming memory that had relatively fast timings (16-18-18-36) @ 3200mhz, but limited to 32GB since that's all I could afford at the time. The JDEC spec on those was lower, and I'm actually wondering if I can clock these higher to more closely match the performance my gaming memory had, but I'm afraid of making my workstation unstable. The performance difference is actually quite small in real world use, and for those times that I actually need all the RAM this has, having more is preferable to faster but smaller with a swap file.
I ran memtest86 on the ram and everything passed 100% every time, and now my computer more-or-less doesn't need a swap file at all anymore (although I'm leaving a small 16GB one just to keep windows happy in case if ever decides to use it). Seems like excellent server-quality ram to me. No RGB glowing lights or XMP profiles here, just reliable and plentiful. I just wish the timings were a drop closer to what I had.

title: Big and fast
text:
EDIT: Got a chance to use a larger capacity one, loved the first one so much I had to get a larger one too!

Original review: This is an excellent memory card. Not only is the storage space huge, in my test it was pretty close to the advertised speed in a UHS-II reader. It's much faster than my regular UHS cards (the ones that lack the extra pins on the back).
I'm familiar with Sabrent for other PC accessories but this is my first memory card from them. It appears to be made in Taiwan, and feels like relatively high quality. Even the case it comes in seems top notch, a padded metal reusable box instead of the disposable plastic that my last few Sandisk Extreme Pro cards came in. I wish Sandisk would give a quality holder like this with their product! Very pleased.

title: Works great but not for headset with mic
text:
This does the job for those times I want to listen to my wired headphones but not lose my charging plug. Those who you who like to watch in bed know what I'm talking about! The problem however is if you wanted to use this for a headset with an inline mic for calls, this is NOT the adapter for you. The mic channel is not carried and it only uses the mic on the phone in my tests.
If that's not a requirement for you, it's great for just normal headphones.

title: Comparable to much more expensive watches.
text:
Wow, these inexpensive fitness tracker watches have really come a long way! I've used WearOS, Fitbit, Galaxy and Amazfit brand watches, and usually find the cheap ones are cute for my kids but not very accurate or full of mostly gimmicky features.
This one actually looks and acts a lot like a cheaper version of my current Amazfit GTS3 watch. The way the menu works, the way the app works... it's all very familiar. Granted, this watch does not have the high resolution OLED display that my Amazfit does, but the display is capable of vivid colors and looks great!

The accuracy is surprisingly spot on, I even tested my heart rate with this and other smartwatches I own since usually there's a lot of discrepancy, and it often lined up exactly. Steps were interesting- most smartwatches don't count steps unless you move for more than a few steps at a time (disregarding a step here or there as an error). This one goes a step further and actually refused to count steps I made unless I was WEARING THE WATCH! I'm not sure if this is a attempt to prevent cheaters from shaking their watch or something, but I noticed it would not count any of my steps when I held it in my fingers, but when I put it on my wrist, it counted! Perhaps there is a proximity sensor on the back of the watch, I'm not sure. This might be a problem for those who occasionally put the watch in a pocket or something to get steps if, for example, pushing a shopping cart (since your wrist doesn't move, pushing strollers and carts tend to not count anyway- one workaround is to put the watch in a pocket but that might not work now).

Another thing I wish it had is a better notification system. Certain apps which aren't in their list of known notifications won't work correctly (Google Voice, for example). But that's true of all cheap tracker watches. It also can't install apps or extend functionality like the more expensive ones. There is definitely a reason my regular watch costs 5-6x as much as this one, but for what it is on a budget, honestly, it's pretty amazing!

title: Big upgrade from my last Samsung TV, perfect for cord cutters!
text:
I have been using a previous generation 1080p LED Samsung TV mounted to my wall with a Firestick for entertainment, as well as some older game systems.
