title: Adds a super speedy nvme drive to my workstation! Can't figure out how to boot though
text:
I have an older HP workstation that predates M.2 SSD drives, and I REALLY wanted to add some high speed goodness to it for improving boot times. This adapter was super simple! Just assemble it using the screws and bracket (which are self explanatory if you've ever installed a card before), and then CAREFULLY mount the SSD to it. This actually took me a bit to figure out, I'm used to having a screw that holds down the SSD, this is more like a holding mount that it fits into which screws in on the back. But once I got it figured out, it installed fine and allowed me to initialize and format my SSD in Windows 10.
Speed was good, about what it should be on a MB mounted nvme, but the only issue I'm having is figuring out how to boot Windows from it. It doesn't show up as a recognized boot device in my Bios, which isn't really the fault of the device and more an issue with my computer in particular. I'm still hoping I can figure that part out to make this work the way I wanted, but to be fair, this adapter is just claiming to add an NVME drive to my computer, which it DOES do.

title: Seems fast and works as expected so far!
text:
I wanted to replace a slower mechanical hard drive in a gaming computer, so I'm trying this out. Using Crystal Diskmark to benchmark, it easily scored 10x higher than my original spinning hdd (2,000+ instead of struggling to hit 200), which is respectably awesome for the price, but about right for an nvme drive.
I find the lack of recognizable brand name somewhat suspicious for something I intend to use as my C: drive, so I wouldn't use this on my workstation or for anything mission-critical... I'd recommend a name brand storage device for reliability there. But to speed up this gaming computer, where everything can be easily replaced if lost, I'd say it's definitely worth a shot. It sped up our boot and load times noticeably, and seems quite cost effective for what you get.

title: Great for Aux inputs
text:
I tried with a couple of USB-C phones and the output was great on my car's aux input. I like that it's a single cable with a male on both ends, so no adapter to go from a headphone jack to an aux cord, this is all-in-one, nice and clean.
It's still not quite as nice as the Quad-DAC you'd get from something like LG's headphone jack, but these days you don't have much of a choice on a modern handset anymore.

title: Perfect for weird electronics around my home!
text:
I have an old Toshiba TV that I bought from a friend who moved, and never got the remote. I've also got some stereo equipment that is missing the remote. It's actually been really hard to find third party replacements that support these obscure products, so I've been using an old LG phone (V20) from back in the days of IR blasters to program them. It's annoying because the phone is getting old and clunky and the battery has to stay charged, but at least if I lose it I can use Google services to locate it.
This universal IR is the best, and replaced ALL of those features now! It actually pairs with my current phone via an app, and you're able to really easily program the different functions and devices, and thanks to the app's UI, it is easy to understand what you are doing. It works great with the audio equipment and Toshiba TV, and if I misplace the remote the app has a find feature! So cool! I'm very happy with this device and I recommend it. I'm going to go put my old LG V20 on ebay now because this was literally the only reason I kept it!

title: For "serious" use
text:
Ok, so I have to admit at first I was wondering why someone would spend this much on a Bluetooth headset that isn't a feature-rich entertainment one like those from Sony or a major fad brand like Beats, both of which I have some experience with. But this, no... this is actually something different. This is a serious tool for serious use with serious built quality and seriously useful features. Seriously.
For example, the telescoping mouthpiece means you'll get unparalleled mic quality compared to headsets that pick the mic up by your ears (looking at YOU, airpods!), both in clarity and isolation from background noise. You can also physically bend it out of the way, or use the button on the mic itself to mute. Try doing that with airpods. Then there's the button based features. Shortcuts and touch-sensitive buttons are cool on aesthetic devices, but the physical controls on this are an ergonomic user experience DREAM. Everything is easy to access and control, no apps or press-and-hold or counting LED blinks, etc. Sort of makes me miss the old days of phones with physical switches and buttons. When you want your equipment to get serious, this is the sort of user experience you expect. Then there's the charging rack. OMG I love that, I can store it on my desk and it's charging automagically. Pick it up and put it on, ready to go. Never needs to be charged because it's been charging in between uses. Finally, I'm really impressed with the USB dongle option. You see, the one thing I really dislike about wireless headphones is that you usually need to pair it with a device, then unpair it to switch to another device. For example, using my Sony headphones on my phone and tablet, if my wife wants to borrow them for a zoom meeting, I need to pair with her device but then also unpair with mine so that it doesn't keep trying to reconnect to it. Sometimes we just give up and use a wired headset to avoid that mess. Non-bluetooth wireless headsets have a dongle, which makes it easy to swap what you are connected to (no unpairing needed, just move the dongle) but then you can't connect to devices without a USB port like a phone. This is the best of both- you can pair it with your phone, but ALSO use the USB to quickly connect with your desktop or laptop without going through the process of pairing and unpairing. This is the kind of usability and professional quality I would expect from a brand like Plantronics, and all the while it works well as a stereo headset for music/gaming/etc as well. Very comfortable to wear for long hours, I'd highly recommend it for serious users.

title: Impressive value for the price! And add-on knob is possible!
text:
Yes, this is not a Kenwood or Alpine. And no, this is not an Android head unit. But honestly, it's actually really overwhelmingly been a positive experience, especially for the price.
Sure, it won't be the top-shelf quality audio, but you're not paying the price tag for that either. Thanks to my Toyota's built in JBL amp, I can honestly say the audio quality is at least on par with the factory radio that came with my car, so no complaints there. It isn't the cheapest head unit either, but honestly you won't get the features and customer support that this has with those. I'd say this is places at that perfect ratio of quality to price is an incredible value.
It is NOT an Android head unit, which is a good thing in my case. I've played with those, and didn't like them. Android is great and offers tons of customization, but for a daily driver it is ultimately an OS designed for a phone/tablet that was tweaked to be a car radio. The versions I tried, for example, took a long time to boot up, occasionally required updates like a phone, had background tasks that sometimes slowed the unit down, and things like switching to rear camera would mute the audio. This one, thankfully has NONE of that. This is a custom OS built from the ground up to be a car radio UI, and it works the way you expect (not like a phone/tablet pretending to be a car). The icons and fonts aren't just chosen at random like the bottom-barrel units, this actually is aesthetically pleasing to use. And when I WANT my phone UI on the screen, Android Auto is actually pretty great with my Pixel 3A.
Things that I found:
1) The style now is strictly buttons, knobs are outdated apparently, even with big brand names. I hate that, I miss my volume knob and hate fiddling with buttons to adjust the sound. Thankfully, I spoke to their support team who was super helpful at not only troubleshooting the steering wheel controls, but alerted me to the existence of an add-on remote part that connects to the IR port behind the radio, and gives some additional buttons you may not have on your steering wheel (it works in tandem with, not instead of). But the best part of that remote? IT HAS A VOLUME JOG DIAL around the outside! Since it magnetically sits in a holder, I was able to take it out, place an adhesive magnet on the faceplate around my radio, and BAM! I now have easy shortcut keys as well as a volume wheel! I'm thinking maybe I'll modify it to look more like a traditional knob (perhaps 3D print a knob part and hide the unit behind the plastic with a hole, I'm not sure yet), but the fact that this is supported as an extra customization is pretty great!
2) The rear camera requires a trigger wire, not just being turned on to activate. This isn't a bad thing, once I figured it out (thanks to their patient support team!). In fact, this adds the ability to turn on the rear camera while driving if desired, which is kind of useful if there's a lot of stuff in your car limiting rear visibility.
3) The mic quality for calls is only so-so. This is the only real con that I have with the device. It isn't the microphone, I tried using a pro-level Sennheiser lav mic to compare, and it just sounds a little more muffled than I'd like, as if there's an aggressive noise cancelling algorithm taking out too much fidelity from my voice. I can hear the other caller fine, but I tested calling an echo line as well as having someone call me, and using my phone in speakerphone had better mic quality than both the built in mic and the mic I mounted on the A-pillar. It's ok, and it works if I need it, but I wouldn't carry a long conversation on it, I think the other person would get annoyed trying to hear me after a while. But that's not really what I bought this for, I wanted to stream bluetooth audio and have Android Auto for maps, and for that it is perfect!

title: Great way to get dual-display on the go!
text:
This is a great concept- my office setup has dual monitors for work, and I find it difficult when I travel to go back to using a single monitor on my laptop. But with this, you can connect what looks like a 15" tablet (with it's own protective cover/stand) to the laptop, and get that oh-so-sweet dual display goodness!
On my 15" 10th gen i7 HP laptop, the display is almost exactly the same size and is close enough in color and brightness to feel like an extension of the desktop, which is nice.
However, the USB-C single connection did not work. That is, this device supports connecting in a couple of different ways- it can be powered by USB and connected to a video source over HDMI, or with a modern USB-C that supports dp, you can connect one cable for both. I liked that second idea and tried to do that since my HP laptop supports USB-C connections. Well, the screen powered on but then said no connection, and the laptop said it detected a USB device but threw errors about it being unknown. The only way I could make it work is by switching to the USB input for power only and using a HDMI cable from the laptop. This is fine, however it's a little cumbersome with two sets of cables required, and then along with the charger for the laptop to keep the battery from depleting (running another LCD takes battery power), it ends up kind of messy pretty fast. I really wish it at least had a rechargeable battery itself, or at the very least worked with the USB-C cable like it was supposed to. Oh well. Otherwise, it is still functional and useful, so 4 stars.

title: Did not work on my mp3 player
text:
I have an mp3 player that has only a USB-C port. It came with USB-C headphones as well as a 3.5mm adapter for regular headphones that we promptly lost.

I really wanted this to replace those, however I tried with several pairs of headphones and NONE of them had sound using this adapter. It detected that headphones were connected, but no sound came out. Very disappointed.

title: Pretty good product, not so great instructions
text:
I was convinced something was wrong with my camera at first because it wouldn't work on my car head unit. I tried hooking it up to my TV, and just got weird jumping lines. I left the white wire uncut like the instructions implied for older cvbs support, but after reaching out to customer support, it turns out the instructions were unclear and in fact the default is AHD you have to CUT the wire to put it into the correct mode for CVBS.
Customer support was actually super responsive and friendly, and asked me to send them a picture of the paperwork so they can fix it for the future. I have to admit that once they cleared that part out, the camera works really well and very clear. It's a shame I can't use the AHD mode, but I think my head unit just doesn't support it. It's a little pricier than other units, but if your head unit supports AHD having the extra resolution is pretty cool.

title: Not the fastest card, but an excellent storage value
text:
This card's R/W numbers aren't amazing, but I didn't really expect them to be. For the price, the fact that you get 2x cards with 64gb is impressive! I'm not familiar with this brand and I'm not sure if I'd trust it with mission-critical storage (flying a drone for work, for example) especially if it requires high speed data to read and write, but for something like a media player or dashcam/security camera recording, this would be a great option to throw in.

For now, I'm formatting one to use in a Raspberry Pi project and the other will probably go in my car's media player. Definitely a good deal for the storage space.

title: Great way to keep the wall neat!
text: We have a nightstand next to an outlet that used to have a plug for a bedside table, and then a multi-USB plug with cables going to 2 phone chargers and a smartwatch. Suffice to say, it was kind of messy looking. This power strip consolidated everything in a way that really looks great now! It's a single flat plug, which means it can easily hide behind furniture, and now there's only a single wire going to the back of the nightstand, where the lamp and USB ports can be plugged in neatly and without a mess of adapters/wires. Consolidated a lot of mess into a neat looking package, I'm VERY happy with this!

title: Works but hard to lock in
text: I found that these charge easily and hold their charge well enough to play for a long time... however they don't lock into the stock Xbox 360 controller that well. I found one of them did better than the other, but even then it didn't really feel "clicked in". I had to play with it before it clicked on finally and it seems to be working fine now. However it shouldn't be so difficult to get it working. Beats changing batteries with disposables, but still- I think you can find better ones that will lock in properly.

title: FAST storage!
text:
I'm very impressed with the read speeds of this on my standard USB3 port. Over 460+MB/s for a portable is pretty great! The write speeds are good too, at 230+ it is no slouch. My internal M.2 SSD is faster, but honestly this is one of the fastest (if not THE fastest) external storage I've tried on this PC. I'd say the speeds are good enough that I'd be comfortable editing 4k video directly off the storage media and not bother transferring to my computer first.
I also really like the size and lanyard strap, but as with all portable SSDs, I sometimes find myself wishing there was a direct plug like a USB stick instead of a cable. The cable makes it just a little messier to manage and keep track of versus a stick jutting out the side of your laptop / desktop. But, that's a minor nit-pick, it's otherwise a great product!

title: Works, but not the fastest for the price
text: It's a decent stick- great for storing content for local playback on a TV or handing files to a friend. It is fast enough to transfer a decent amount of data in a moderate amount of time, but make no mistake- this is NOT a high speed stick. In fact, if I have to find fault with it, it is that for the current asking price there are other options from reputable brands (PNY, Lexmark, etc) that have faster r/w speeds. Those are currently LESS than the asking price of this one, so I can't really recommend this product knowing those are available. But, for what it's worth, it DOES work and does what it says it should, so if you can find it for a good price, I say go for it.

title: Super useful
text:
I've tried a few neck fans before from Amazon and they were pretty cool (ha, see what I did there?) for humid days, going on hikes and the like. But this is the first one I've seen that also comes off and can double as two individual free-standing fans!
Each end has its own micro-usb charging port, which is cool when you want to separate them, but it also means you have to charge them both. Even when attached, there is no wire to transfer battery from one to the other, they are each powered by their own internal battery and need to be charged. So it is possible to accidentally only charge one or have one die before the other when on a hike. That's the trade off for such a cool and versatile product, so I'd still give it 5 stars for that. Why 4 stars then? Well, when attached as a neck fan, I found that the whole thing feels kind of long. I guess since each side needs it own battery and button and charging port, they are a little longer than the fan ends of a standard neck cooling fan. It's ok, and it still works, but doesn't quite look as cool, if I'm being honest.
Then again, you're not wearing this for style, you're wearing it to keep cool. And for that, it works!

title: Great combo
text:
This is a pretty decent mid-range wireless kb/mouse combo. If you mostly find yourself using a cramped laptop, it's wonderful to have the option for a full sized keyboard (with number pad) as well as a mouse for comfort instead of the trackpad most laptops give you. And I particularly like that the combo here allows you to use either the kb or mouse or both, and in all situations only uses a single USB port. The USB dongle can actually fit inside both the mouse AND the keyboard (they both have a space to store it) so you can keep it with whichever accessory you use most.
For gamers, this might not be the best option. No affordable wireless set is great for gaming response. This is definitely a level nicer than the keyboard on our cramped laptops however, so for long report typing and data entry, it is great to have around. And I'm not a fan of trackpads, so whenever I'm sitting for a while, having a mouse is very welcome for my laptop. For my desktop which I use for long day work hours (and even some light gaming) I'll stick with a wired option. This is not going to replace those. But for what it is and the price being asked, I'd say its a good option!

title: Does the job
text:
I needed this to replace an older mount that wasn't big enough for our new TV. It does the job- that is, it holds the TV in place securely. I did find that installation wasn't so simple, since the outlet is on the wall right behind it (to keep wires hidden) and this thing really HUGS the wall. I was kind of annoyed that after installing everything, I then realized I didn't have enough clearance to plug it in or reach any of the ports, so I had to take it down and use the largest bolts and spacers they had to give some space between the wall and TV to allow room for the cables.
One thing I noticed is that with ALL the spacers and longest sized bolts, the bolts were just a bit too long to screw all the way in securely. I ended up having to supplement my own using 2 metal washers in the middle of the array of spacers. They could have avoided this by just including a couple more of their thin spacers to make up for the extra length for people like me, but at least I got it working. I like that the TV easily comes off using the pull tabs, and I'm thankful that my 48" TV is large enough to hide the pull strings. I saw examples of other users mounting smaller TVs which show the strings hanging out the bottom. I wouldn't like that, and would probably tie them up or something to hide it. Not at issue at larger size screens I guess, but at least I like that it is easy to remove if I need to get to something behind it. Putting it back up on the wall is a 2-person job, not a big deal at all, but too hard to balance and click them on by myself.
For the money, it's a cost effective way to get your screen on the wall. I sorta wish I had gone for a slightly more expensive articulating arm one like my old one, since it makes getting to the back super easy without removing the screen, but those are more expensive and stick out further from the wall too. I'm happy with this one for now!.

title: Interesting light kit
text:
There's a lot to like about this kit, starting with the price. For the money, I've owned similar light kits to this before, but this one comes with batteries and chargers for wireless use as well as the AC plug adapters for constant power. Similar kits that I've owned required me to buy the Sony-style FP batteries separately. It also comes with a soft case, however I found the case very flimsy and not very protective (it comes folded up inside the box, there is no rigidity to it). BUT, I realized that the box it comes it is roughly a similar size to the case when unfolded, and sure enough it actually can fit inside the case perfectly! I'm not sure if this was on purpose, it was not obvious to me that this was the intention so maybe don't throw away that cardboard if you want to give your case some protective strength (see attached photo for carboard box inside carrying case).
As far as the lights themselves... they are pretty good. I was concerned about them being less densely populated than other LED panels I've used, however it appears that each diode puts out more light than I was expecting so overall it is a good amount of light for using with video for something like an interview setting.
Meanwhile, the colors and party mode are a bit different for me. I'm used to using light kits as a professional tool, and I think the multicolor part is a bit too gimmicky. It's cool to set a tone with a color like the way I'd gel a red light for a setting or something, but the party mode? I can't imagine a use for the strobe effect of it changing color constantly. I have DJ lights that can move to music and this has a mode for that as well, however it seems that the only option is to change color with each beat suddenly- no gradual fade or anything like that. The hard cut is kind of migraine-inducing distracting, so I'd honestly rather use a different light for party background style color changes. As a light kit, it's pretty good, but the selling point of using it as a sound-controlled DJ thing is iffy. Maybe a DJ at a bar mitzvah would find that option useful?

title: Cute and funcitonal
text:
I've used other wearable cooling fans before, but they never looked great- always more function over form. I really like that these look like headphones that you can wear around your neck. It almost makes me wonder if they should make a version that doubles as actual headphones too!
Only caveat I have is that they are actually kind of long and not really as adjustable as I'd like. Great for adults, but my daughter who wanted to use it found it sticks out a bit too far to wear comfortably without looking funny. Otherwise, exactly what I expected it to be.

title: Essentially a TRS splitter, but so much nicer
text:
For the type of run-and-gun projects I do, if I can get away with plugging a mic directly into the camera ( often a single stereo 3.5mm jack these days) I will always prefer to do that than a dual-sound setup that needs to by synced in post. However, sometimes you need more than one mic, so what's a one-man-crew to do? Well, traditionally I would use a TRS break out cable, which essentially looks like a headphone splitter Y-cable, but splits the Left and Right channel into separate plugs instead of doubling them. That's great because I can connect one mic to Left and the other to Right, then split them up and remix in post as needed.
But this is much more elegant solution- It is essentially the same idea, splitting the L + R into two sides, but not only is it less messy since you don't have Y cables dangling, it also serves as a point in which to mount 2 coldshoe receivers directly to single shoe mount, essentially making this an all-in-one solution to turn a single mic input setup into a dual one. No additional hardware necessary behind the second mic. I love this solution, it looks more professional, it is more reliable, and I would definitely recommend checking it out if you're in the same boat as me!

title: Most under-rated brand
text:
I'm a big fan of the Mi Band series of trackers, and this is the first device that finally got me to switch to something else. If you aren't familiar, Xiaomi and Huami aren't big brands in the US compared to other countries, but these are solid high quality products and not your standard fare Chinese junk. I've tried a LOT of different fitness trackers and smart watches- Everything from Google WearOS, Fitbit, Apple, and all the way down to the cheap trackers from Chinese throwaway brands with obscure apps. For a long time I've said I liked the features and quality of the expensive brands, but found they all had major flaws (battery life being a major one- I don't want another thing to charge as often as a phone!). The Mi band from Xiaomi was super affordable and high quality compared to others in that price range, and had a battery that only required being charged once a month.
This is basically the smarter older brother of that band. It is compatible with Mi Fit, so all my data transferred right over, but it is so much nicer than the band. For starters, the notification system is easier to read and keep up with messages, but the benefits go far beyond a larger screen. The music control is a nice touch, I like being able to pause and adjust the volume without taking my phone out of my pocket if playing on a BT speaker while I'm doing dishes, for example. The tracking is pretty accurate compared to other expensive brands, and while it doesn't support apps like Wear OS and Apple Watches, it has all the fitness functions you'd need built in already, including some fun widgets beyond the expected ones like a stopwatch, phone finder and even a compass! And unlike cheap brands, the UI is responsive and smooth. Not the smoothest out there for sure, but more than acceptably smooth considering how much a flagship smartwatch costs compared to this.
It has support for voice commands, but I honestly found that feature kind of gimmicky more than useful. The higher end version of this includes a speaker which might make the command function more useful as sort of a digital assistant, not to mention the ability to take phone calls from your wrist. But the model I got to try out lacks the speaker, which is a fine compromise for a cheaper price tag all things considered. The battery life at first was just OK, a few days on a charge if using lift-to-wake functions, but just as on my Mi Band tracker of old, I found if I turn off auto-wake and rely on using the button to wake the display, the battery life goes from counting in days to counting in weeks. That's the killer feature of this device- the ability to leave it on to track fitness and sleep habits without having to charge it so often. I'll have to charge it more than my old Mi Band's monthly top up for sure, probably at least 2x a month, but that's still very manageable.
So that's it, after years of loving my Mi Bands and considering it the standard by which all practical fitness trackers should be judged, I'm finally moving on to an Amazfit watch. This is a difficult value to beat.

title: Excellent big screen!
text:
Before this I had a smaller 70" pull down screen that we used with my projector. It was great for home use and easy to set up, but sometimes I need to present to a larger gathering and it wasn't quite large enough for that.
This is an EXCELLENT large screen! It comes in a few size options, but I opted to try out the largest one (120"). Now, to be clear, this thing is HUGE. With the feet on the stand, it is taller than most normal height ceilings. In this photo attached, I have it set up on a room off the side of my home with tall cathedral-style ceilings, there's no way this would fit downstairs or any room with normal height ceilings in our home! However considering how big and unwieldly this could be, I'm super impressed at how easily it snaps together and compacts back down to fit into that little carrying bag. I've set it up about 3x so far, and it definitely gets easier/faster the more often you do it. BUT, it's a heck of a lot easier to do with two people, especially putting it on the legs. It comes with the skirt to make it look more professional and with stakes and rope to hold it down against wind if using outside (it basically becomes a giant sail in the wind otherwise), but I haven't had much reason to use those. I love that they are included, though. As a screen, it is truly excellent. Highly recommended!

title: Perfect for modern setups
text:
Drives like this are so important to have around still. Sure, we don't use them enough that it makes sense to have it built in anymore, but there are still the occasional times we need to read or write optical media. An external like this is a perfect solution, because you can have it when you need it, but not have it permanently installed on all your devices for all the times we don't.
I recently built a new desktop for work, and of course I left out the optical drive because I can't remember the last time I used the one on my previous desktop. I instead used the empty bay for more HDD support (RAID anyone?), and skipped the CD/DVD entirely. Until suddenly I needed to install something legacy that I forgot about! Same with my laptop, I dig up my old Adobe CS6 discs and wanted to install it for my son, and without this drive that would have been very annoying!
We also have an Android based TV box, and plugging this into it enabled us to play DVDs through the Kodi media player as well. We don't always need/use it, but it's so great to have it available in a drawer for those times we do! It is a USB2 device, but that is perfectly fine since CD/DVD read and write speeds are well within the USB2 specifications. It also comes with a second USB port for supplying power in case the device you connect it to doesn't have enough amps to spin the motor (in most cases you won't need it). Very happy with this product!

title: Pefect for DC power!
text: This is an excellent kit to keep around for road warriors like us. I have both a Lenovo and HP laptop that have their own proprietary connectors, and this does a great job being able to be used with either in a pinch if we have the need! Even better, I have a power station for working on locations without access to outlets (about the size of a car battery) that offers 110v AC outlets as well as 12v DC port, and using the AC charger that comes with laptop is a waste of energy (converting the dc battery power to AC, then going into my laptop charger to convert to DC again just to go into the laptop). Using this off the 12v DC port means I get a more direct conversion of power and MUCH more life out of the power station. I couldn't be happier with this, I highly recommend it!

title: Affordable, good features
text:
[[VIDEOID:5a1bce8644783f1974b4478fd2851303]] The good: This device works! See the video attached using a Sony mirrorless camera going into the HDMI input as a webcam, recorded in the Windows 10 Camera app of my desktop. It has its own audio inputs as well as a headphone monitoring jack if your camera doesn't have its own, making this a really complete system. It also has an HDMI out if you want to pass through and send the signal on to a display or projector. I also really like that the box is large enough to dissipate its own heat, unlike other "industry standard" equipment in this category (I'm looking at you, overpriced Magewell!).
The bad: The build quality is a little bit suspect. Before I first set it all up, I actually found that the board inside was loose. Shaking the box, you can visually see the hdmi ports rattle around and not line up with the holes in box unless you tilt it the right way. It seems, however, that once everything is plugged in, it works properly. But that shouldn't happen.

Bottom line: This box is a fraction of the cost of some of the big players in this market (Magewell), yet seems to offer excellent features. And honestly, it just works. If you're looking for a setup like this on a budget, I say its worth checking this model out.

title: It works well enough
text:
This is an interesting product for gamers and content creators to capture and record live video feeds. So, for example, my son wants to record some of his gameplay to make a youtube video about it, he COULD just record using screencap software, but that would slow down the PC and use precious resources that are otherwise going into graphics and fps. This is great because it works EXTERNALLY of the computer, just sitting in between the PC and the monitor, and recording onto its own media without the computer even knowing. It even comes with its own sandisk USB card, which is a nice touch.
This can obviously be used for all kinds of things as well, including capturing content off a camera, video game console, or anything with an HDMI signal. While it did work on my desktop and game console, however, I found that my son had a had time getting it to work with his. I'm not sure if his monitor was trying to use a strange resolution or something, but whenever this was connected, his monitor wouldn't power on. I checked both cables, and even used an HDMI coupler to connect them directly and sure enough the monitor worked fine without this box in the middle. I have no idea why it doesn't work for him, and the instructions aren't very helpful. I may have to try swapping to a different monitor or gpu something because he really wants this work and it DOES work elsewhere in more standard setups, and it will record off his desktop, we just can't see it on his monitor when it's all plugged in.
The video quality recorded is decent. You can see there is compression on blocky text and fine detail, but it isn't any worse than standard youtube compression. It's a decent product if you want to play with a recorder like this.

title: Great for mounting options!
text:
As a guy who ends up with weird DIY camera rigs in the field, things like this are awesome! I can mount a monitor to my tripod leg, or a battery supply for my recording system, light panels, etc... But my favorite use, of course, is mounting a go-pro to the whole thing to capture a BTS view from any nearby stand or rig point.
It is pretty strong, but I wouldn't trust a full frame camera with a heavy lens on it. This is great for accessories or small cameras (like a Hero), and I love that it comes with standard mounting parts for both! Would recommend this if you want to get creative with your gear!

title: This saved me on a job!
text:
I was interested in this originally because I wanted to replace a faulty Dell charger and I couldn't remember which type of tip it used. I like that this has exchangeable tips included for almost every conceivable laptop brand out there, even the proprietary square Lenovo ones! But I had reservations about it actually working, since I didn't understand how the adapter is able to know what voltage to output. I thought, surely feeding 20v to a laptop that one uses 15v could cause a major malfunction, right? There is no control switch on the box to select an appropriate voltage.
But then I noticed the tips- each one has a fine embossed lettering that states what voltage it is designed to use, and I think THAT tells the adapter what to output appropriately. Very cool design! It turns out, this adapter saved me on a job. I needed an HP laptop to run a live stream station, and it uses these weird little blue tip ends that aren't a standard size for anything else. The original HP charger end got smashed and I was about to be stuck using only whatever remaining battery there was for the duration of the event, until I remembered this adapter! I found a matching blue tip, it said 19v on it (which is what my laptop says as well), and sure enough it worked perfectly! Charged up the device without any problem! I'm so grateful for this adapter!

title: Great and necessary on modern desks!
text: My new desk is lower than my old one, which means I really need to raise my two monitors for comfortable viewing angles. I had tried smaller risers before, but they were still just a bit too low. I like these because they are now only high enough to really help, they also have additional storage for under-monitor items like pens, flash drives, envelopes, etc. The quality seems good, they are nice and sturdy and they look great on my desk. I'm very happy with them!

title: Super useful!
text:
I love this little light! A colleague of mine uses a similar cube from a different brand to do interesting lighting with his photography at night, and I was always impressed with how much light you can get out of a little LED these days! This little cube has a rubber gasket for the charging port to make it dust/water resistant, and SO MANY different mounting points, the possibilities are endless!
I used it recently on a live production to light the crew so we could see our equipment around the dark stage. I think I'm going to need more of these, what a versatile tool!

title: Good product, on the small side
text:
I got this for my teenaged son to use on his gaming PC. He had actually broken his previous gaming headphones and this seemed like a no-frills decent replacement for him to try.
The sound quality is actually quite good. Both the ear pieces and the microphone are crisp and clear, so no complaints there. However my son found it a little uncomfortable to wear compared to his larger over-the-ear style headphones before. The actual ear parts on this are smaller, which means they don't fully envelop your ears the way other ones do. On the plus side, this means it doesn't block as much external noise, which I like for him in our household (no more calling his name when he can't us!), but others may want more noise isolation. Also, the smaller ear pieces aren't as comfortable when worn as the larger ones.
I also didn't like that it didn't come with an adapter to break out for mic and speakers like other headsets do. I thought it would come with that as an option, as I've never gotten a PC headset that didn't offer either a splitter or TRRS combo adapter so you can use it with both a laptop that has mic/headphone combos as well as separate mic and headphone jacks commonly found on a desktop.
Thankfully I had an extra one lying around for him to use, so that wasn't an issue. But something to take into consideration. Others, I've got to give it at least 4 stars for working well and doing what it should. But there might be other options for the price worth considering as well if you want larger earphones or a breakout cable included.

title: Actually impressive for the price
text:
Ok, as an owner of real "Brand name" home theater projectors (Viewsonic, Epson, etc), I'm usually not impressed with the budget no frills variations. They are often misleading with their specs, using different standards of measurement for lumens, or having much lower resolution than they claim ("supports 1080p" but really only shows 480 or 720, and downscales the 1080 input). This one actually seems better than the cheapos I've tried in the past. As far as I can tell, this might even be a real native 1920x1080 full HD resolution for a change! The picture quality is decent, although the colors might not be as vibrant or true as my Viewsonic, and it definitely lacks the contrast ratio and brightness of brand name projectors as well.
BUT, one thing that blew me away with this, was the on-board speaker. I've never used a projector's speaker for a presentation before, they are usually terrible hollow tin-sounding messes, like trying to crank up a laptop speaker to fill a room (which is pretty much what they usually are). This one actually has a half decent speaker that I could use for something non-audio critical. That is, I wouldn't use it to hear the cinematic score behind an epic movie, however for broadcasting a speech or presentation to a room of people, I might consider the speaker good enough to not bother plugging in any other sound to it.
One thing I really miss compared to real projectors, however, is the ability to adjust the throw in addition to the focus. My Viewsonic lets me adjust the picture size with one knob and the focus with the other, so I am able to make the thrown image be the correct target size within a small range of distances. With this, the only thing you can adjust is the keystone angle. Don't get me wrong, that's useful to have as well, but you are limited to having the projector sit an exact distance away to get a specific size throw. I'd rather have the throw adjustment.
The bottom line is, this still won't replace the quality and experience of using a brand name projector. Heck, even a 720p Viewsonic will look better than this even if it's full HD. But for what it is, I have to say it's a pretty good value!

title: Excellent Fluid Head Tripod
text:
This is an excellent tripod system for video shooters. The head is very similar to my Manfrotto 701 fluid head in performance, however the QR plate system seems to have a bit of a learning curve to me. I love how high this can unfold to, and the dual beam support legs gives me confidence that this can stand up and remain steady.
I love the carrying bag that is comes with as well as the little tools to tighten and maintain your tripod that come included in the bag. That's a nice touch!

title: A good mid-ranger
text: This is head-and-shoulders better than the cheapo webcams out there. Many webcams claim to be 1080p but actually either don't have the sensor or lens to actually resolve that much resolution, rather you get an up-sampled low resolution image in a 1080p frame. But not this one! This seems to have a properly sampled image which explains why it costs a little more than your average cheapo. The microphones are OK, they aren't great, but I always prefer using a headset or external mic anyway. I sit too far away from my screen to reply on camera mics. It won't compete with 4K brand name webcams, but in my opinion this can hold its own very well and does an admirable job for the money. It is definitely better than the built in cam on my old laptop, and adds a lot of value to my desktop for meetings. I recommend it for the price.

title: Useful, but just OK for my purposes
text: I have an HP laptop I want to use in the field for running an all-day event stream without needing to tether to a wall. I thought something like this would be a good move to keep it charged since the battery only lasts about 2.5 hours running the stream (it's CPU intensive). However, this laptop does not support USB-C PD charging unfortunately (I was hoping it did, there is a USB-C port, but sadly only output is supported), so I had to resort to using the AC part. Now, I know converting DC from a battery to AC requires quite a bit of power loss, but one recharge of my laptop from single digits to 80% practically wiped the power supply out. I definitely would not be able to charge the laptop more than once off of this, and I have my doubts it would even make it all the way to 100% without dying honestly. I was really hoping it would last longer. If you have a PD-compatible laptop, this might work better for you. I DO love that it has an AC outlet for emergencies, and I'll probably take this with us camping because it is pretty cool to have. But the product description implies this is a good option for charging a laptop, but for the price I've seen better options I think. At the very least, I wish this had a automotive-style 12v DC port so I could try getting that kind of charger for my laptop (less power lost since not inverting to AC), but alas. The only real laptop charging options are AC and USB-C/PD, and if your laptop doesn't use the latter, the first is a pretty inefficient option.

title: Perfect for my setup!
text: I used this to go from my PC's graphics card to my TV. The graphics card only offered display port, but the TV only accepts the more widely used HDMI as inputs. It's annoying that this is uni-directional, as you can't go from HDMI to a DP input if needed, but I think that's par for the course with these types of cables. For what I'm trying to do, it works splendidly.

title: I wish every USB cable I owned was like this one!
text:
This is the best! Between me and my wife, we have many headphones, phones, tablets, and battery banks that all use either USB-C or micro-USB ports. It has been extremely annoying to keep track of which needs which cable, swapping wires like musical chairs. But with this, I can swap the ends as needed and always have the correct cable for the device that needs it!
This has vastly simplified how I charge my things. I long for the day that standards stop changing so quickly so we can have one cable to rule them all, but even today you can still buy things with microUSB cable ports. So, until that day comes, I would love a bunch more dual-end cables like this one!

title: Pretty slow, even for USB2
text:
I wasn't expecting this to be a speed demon, it says right on the box USB2 so I knew I wasn't going to get the 150+MB/s level speeds I get with some of my thumb drives. But even for USB2, this is on the slow side. Plugging in a standard sandisk drive to my USB2 port, I'm able to pull over 40MB/s without breaking a sweat. This one? Even on a USB3 port, I'm only able to pull a bit over 18MB/s in read, and the writing is even more abysmal. That's less than half of what USB2 can pull.
For the money, this is a decent delivery platform for you to hand off large files to someone, or perhaps to play media on a USB TV or something like that. But for regular daily transfer of data, you might find this painfully slow. As you can see in the benchmark screenshot attached, it timed out for the last two write tests and never even finished.

title: Not impressed.
text:
I love the concept here, two stands with a bar in the middle to hang a backdrop or white projector screen material. I've wanted something like this for a portable screen and green chroma-key background option since my old portable projector screen has a broken leg. However, in reality, this is a lot smaller than they make it seem. Fully extended, the tallest point here is only up to my shoulders. That means the viewing screen is very low, too low for comfort (everyone will be looking down unless they are sitting on the floor). On my old screen, when set up in my living room or outside, I usually start it a few feet off the ground and end way up over my head so that everyone can see. This is just... a joke. It also isn't very stable when fully extended. Using material that needs to be stretched to avoid creasing bends the stands to the point it starts to warp and lean in different directions.
I'm very disappointed in this product. The only plus side I can say is that it DOES fold up nicely into the included carrying bag, but unless you're planning on sitting on the floor and have a very smooth screen that doesn't need to a lot of support on the stand to look right, you're better off looking elsewhere.

title: Good for wide storage under monitor!
text: I had 2 smaller risers I've been using with my monitors to make the viewing angle more ergonomic as well as free up space on my desk to store my KB and mouse. The problem has been that most standard risers aren't wide enough for my keyboard to fit underneath. This solves that problem by being quite a bit wider than your average riser, and plenty big enough for my full sized gaming keyboard with number pad to slide away when done.

title: Does exactly what I expected!
text: I have an LG display that accepts HDMI and wanted to use it as a second monitor for my desktop, but my Nvidia card only offers DP plugs. This adapter handles the DP to HDMI perfectly. I can't vouch for 4k@60hz, but I did try 1080p @ 75hz since my monitor supports that, and it works as expected perfectly. Very happy with the product.

title: A clean solution for power!
text:
We have an electric synth keyboard that my kids are learning to play piano with, and have an app on a tablet used for practice. Usually there's a mess of wires going to an outlet nearby to keep the piano powered and the tablet charged, but this unit really cleaned it up nicely!
Not only does this have the flat-style plug that makes it blend in behind furniture, The white color fits in with the wall paint making it look like part of the room decor. We mounted it to the wall behind the piano for a super clean look, and the 3 outlets means we can plug in the piano as well as other things without having to move furniture again to access the outlet on the actual wall. Then the USB ports means we can easily charge the tablet while also having ports available for phones or whatever else we want to charge without another USB wall adapter. The result is a much cleaner and more efficient looking setup. Very much enjoying it so far!

title: Clears up desk space and makes monitors more easy to read
text:
If you have a dual monitor setup, you owe it to yourself to get a matching set of risers like these. The height of many modern desks position the monitor slightly lower than optimal viewing angles for people who aren't shorter-than-average. This fixes that by raising it up a good few inches, which also frees up space underneath the monitors for papers or to store accessories like your mouse/keyboard when not in use.
Here's the thing, however- if you have a full sized keyboard like mine, you'll find these are just shy of wide enough to fit underneath. I'd recommend a wider riser for that, however for most people this is a really perfect size. The finish is nice, it was super easy to assemble, and it even has a slot and organizers for cable management to keep your desk nice and tidy. I really like how these look, they have transformed my desk into a more useful and aesthetic workspace.

title: Not really loving the concept
text:
I listen to lectures on headphones when doing chores around the house and often can't hear people trying to get my attention. I've seen neck speakers before, and I thought it would be a very cool option for me as my family gets kind of annoyed that I can't hear them and they can't tell if I'm currently listening to something.
But I'll be honest, after trying these, I'm not really loving them. I had a pair of sunglasses speakers that aimed sound towards my ears, but this sort of blasts sound out and around me. Like, not even towards my ears. Basically, it seems just as loud to someone else in the room with me as it does to me, which then begs the question of why not just use an external speaker at that point? The call quality was just OK as well. The one thing I can say is that the build quality seems quite good. It feels really durable and made with premium feeling materials. But I just can't shake the feeling that for the asking price, I'm missing the point of these. Shouldn't the speakers be facing upwards towards my ears instead of blasting at each other in front of my Adam's Apple? Seems like a weird design that might be missing the mark.

title: Good FOV with very little distortion
text:
A lot of these cheap webcams use very small sensors and rely on super wide optics to see the room. They also tend to overstate their resolving power, claiming to send a 1080 sized image that looks more like an upscaled 480. I'm happy to say this is a degree better than those!
The sensor is still small, as expected, but the optics aren't super wide to the point that edges distort. In fact, it seems pretty rectilinear (straight lines stay relatively straight in the background). The resolution seems decent as well. I'm not sure if it's actually resolved a full HD image like it claims, but it is definitely more resolution than a lot of the cheaper webcams I've tried. It looks pretty good and I'd argue that any live web call, skype, zoom, etc, will look perfectly fine with this camera and play at whatever resolution that protocol is capable of clearly.
The thing that sorta disappointed me, however, was the "ring light" built in. I mean, I have a REAL ring light so I get what that should do, but this sorta does... nothing. It doesn't create soft shadows or a circular catch light in my eyes- in fact, it's very hard to discern the difference between capture with the light on versus off. In a dark room, it can add a bit of illumination to the subject to make you a little easier to see, but it really isn't all that bright and under normal lighting conditions in my office, it makes zero difference at all. It also seems to get kind of warm as long as it is plugged in, even if not currently active, so I'm going to be in the habit of disconnecting it when not using, and only plugging it in when I need to make a video call at my desk.
For what it is, it is definitely a better webcam than most of the cheap ones, but it definitely is not perfect!

title: Ultimate power strip
text:
This is an excellent power strip for those who need many things plugged in. If you have a workstation with multiple monitors, external HDDs, speakers, and other accessories, THIS is the strip to get! With 10 outlets, you already are starting off with more than the usual 6-8, but add to that the fact that these face AWAY from the center on opposite sides, so wall wart adapters (such as those found on AC/DC plugs for external HDDs or speakers) have enough room to NOT take up the plug next to it! And then beyond that, you get built in USB ports, and even a type-C port, which means you can avoid additional adapters for all your USB-charging things.
And if that wasn't enough? This thing also has the flat the type of plug, so it can easily fit in the outlet behind your desk or other furniture, and not require a gap in the wall.
Essentially, other power strips should take note: THIS is what every single one needs to be like. They took everything that anyone could ever complain about on a traditional strip/surge protector, and went ahead and fixed it. A perfect product!

title: A great way to hide connections and adapters!
text:
I have a mess of wires by my TV- adapters and remote control receivers, etc. My Fire Stick has a USB breakout box for a remote keyboard as well as ethernet port, and then an HDMI extender for use with my projector as well as an HDMI to HDMI + audio to send the sound to my stereo system. It's a mess, and I used to keep it all inside of a shoebox. My wife wasn't a fan, it always looked kinda grungy. This plastic box is perfect however! All my adapters and cables can be wrapped up and contained in a neat little package that has holes made for this purpose, as well as being easy to open and rummage around if needed.
All that while having a wood colored top that matches the wood of much of our furniture. This is truly a great solution to a modern day problem!

title: Decent for the money, but not the absolute best
text:
This is a decent black backdrop for use in studio setups for photography or video. It can be held up using standard equipment like a rod and muslin clamps. I found, however, that the material has a touch of a sheen to it. It isn't a huge deal and honestly can be easily worked around, but it seems to reflect a little more light back at the camera than other backgrounds if you aren't careful. For example, a hair light that I've used before on other backgrounds spilled a bit onto this and it made a visible area of the frame brighter. I had to use some larger barn doors on the light to deflect it better, but the point is a more expensive and professional level material might not have needed that.
For the budget I'd say it is still good and worth using to get a black background on the cheap.

title: Simplified media setup!
text:
We have a firestick and 2 game consoles attached to the same TV, but the TV controls were always complicated to switch inputs between them. Even when I showed my kids how to switch to the Xbox input, they would forget how to turn it back to the Firestick when my wife wanted to watch something. This product solves that!
What I LOVE about this box, is that it accepts the feed in order. The firestick starts off on, and is active in Port1. Turn on a game console attached to inputs 2 or 3, and it automatically switches to that input and takes over the display. Turn them off, it goes back to input 1 (the fire stick). I basically just leave the TV accepting the one feed from this box, and everything else is automatic! It comes with a remote and a 5V power supply to control it, but honestly, I've found none of that is necessary. I don't need the remote if it works like this (which it does), and if you don't need the remote receiver, you can skip the power supply. It works and switches HDMI inputs just fine with a little LED self-powered off the HDMI itself. Very clean and perfect setup!

title: Perfect replacement or backup
text: I had lost the charger for my HP laptop in a recent move, and ordered this one hoping it would work. It's been excellent, and even though I eventually found my original, I'm still keeping this one as a backup. I highly recommend it if you need it.

title: Solid cable!
text: I have a DP plug on my GPU but my monitor only supports HDMI. Up until now I was using an adapter that goes from DP to HDMI, and then using an HDMI cable from there to the monitor. It worked well enough, but sometimes the cable would get kicked and the connection flicker. I'm never a fan of adapters if a straight cable is an option, and I'm glad it is. This cable made my connection much more reliable. I'm not running 4k resolution so I can't comment on that claim, however I AM using a 90hz refresh rate which uses more bandwidth than a standard monitor connection at 60. So, I can say this holds up a more-than-strong-enough connection for most people.

title: Perfect for my XBox Kinect!
text: I have a TV mounted to the wall in our play room over some kids toys. We have an Xbox connected to the TV, but the kids want to use the Kinect sensor, and there's no shelf or furniture to put it on in line-of-sight of the TV. Well, enter this perfect little stand! It mounts to the wall over the TV, and has a little hole to drop the wire down and hide behind it. A perfect solution to a first world problem! It is easy to install and exactly the right size for the base of the Kinect. I'm very happy with it!

title: Perfect!
text: I wanted my card reader for work on my desk instead of attached to my desktop tower by my feet, and this is EXACTLY what I needed! With this USB3 extension cable, I was able to reach the required length to put my reader where I want it, all while not losing USB3 transfer speeds. Does exactly what I wanted, couldn't be happier with it.

title: If you need one of these, they are perfect!
text: I work with video equipment and can never have too many connection options at my disposal. I love that this comes with both a straight patch and an elbow shaped one! I tried out both to attach an HDMI splitter to a display over 10 feet of wire away by combining two HDMI cables, and had no problems connecting at the highest resolution of both devices. They work!

title: Works great as a Wifi 6 card, BT needs USB header access
text:
I got this for my son's gaming desktop to make it WiFi 6 compliant, as his aging wifi adapter wasn't doing so well with our new router. It claims to also have bluetooth, which would have been a nice addition but it requires access to a USB header on the motherboard to do that.
We have USB access heads on the board, however we were unable to reach it with the length of cable provided unless I removed / shuffled around some other expansion cards (to be fair, he has dual GPUs and TV input card already, so there isn't a lot of space to navigate wires). I find this requirement kind of odd, because I have not seen other BT/WiFi cards that require a USB port. I was told the USB access is for Bluetooth, as it communicates over the USB channels, and wifi doesn't need it. But that still seems weird. I know that you can add USB ports via PCIe, so I don't understand why this card needs USB on the motherboard- can't it supply its own I/O for that?
Regardless, my son didn't care much about bluetooth, the point was to get an internet connection upgrade, and for that it worked splendidly. Without the USB wire, the WiFi portion of the card works just fine, plug and play. His connection is faster and with less lag. The Bluetooth portion is disabled for now as a result, but that's ok. Eventually we'll source a longer cable or maybe play musical chairs with the PCI cards in there currently to make it work.

title: A decent classroom/meeting webcam, but not perfect
text:
Really I think this product deserves 3 stars compared to other webcams, but the price is good enough that I think it deserves 4 for value.
The camera claims to be 1080p, however in my testing recording locally, there's no way this is resolving a FHD worth of pixels. I believe it is sending a 1080 sized feed to the computer, but the actual camera itself looks less sharp than 720 scaled up to 1080. I'd say it is better than those uber-cheap 480p cameras, but it is definitely NOT the resolution they claim. Secondly, this is a wide angle lens with a lot of distortion as you reach the borders of your frame. See included photo for examples of the fish-eye edge distortion. The microphone isn't all that great either, but that's to be expected when the mic is so far away from you. For good audio, I always recommend a desk mic instead of a webcam mic anyway. All in all, if you just need to show up for work meetings or classrooms on zoom, this will do the job just fine! But if you want to look professional, record a vlog or twitch stream, etc, you're going to want a webcam with better quality, resolution, and less lens distortion.

title: Excellent and versatile!
text: I wanted to add outlets to the inside of a shelf, and this was a PERFECT accessory to do it! The flat plug means that I can plug it in behind furniture and still have the shelf against that wall, and the screw mounting holes let me mount this strip inside behind the trim where it is out of sight. Now we can plug in lights, smart speakers, charge phones etc all without a mess of wires going to the inaccessible outlet in the wall. The built in USB is really welcome as well, since most of the things being plugged in are often just USB anyway. I'm very happy with this!

title: Excellent way to add monitors to your desktop
text: My video card has only a single HDMI port which is already being used, but I wanted to add a second identical monitor to my setup. Thankfully, my desktop's card has 2 display ports available, so all I needed was a cable to go from DP to HDMI for the second monitor. This performed PERFECTLY, the monitor response is exactly as expected and works exactly as it should! Just make sure you get the length right. I got a 3 foot cord and wish I had gotten one with a little more slack for freedom to place the monitor a bit farther.

title: Have a desktop? YOU NEED THIS!
text:
If you have a large desktop, editing workstation or gaming PC, you've probably dealt with the same struggle I have: finding enough places to plug everything in. A standard power / surge protection strip will give you about 6-8 plugs on average, so if you have, say, 2 monitors, a desktop power cable, speaker power, an external HDD and maybe a PD adapter or printer on the same strip, it should all fit, right? WRONG. They're usually all in a row so that an oversized wall wart adapter plug will overlap and block access to the plugs next to it.
My desktop has 2 LG monitors which have large AC/DC adapter plugs that are grounded- they easily take up almost an entire standard strip by themselves.
Enter this power strip to save the day! I LOVE this design, and I can't believe anyone still makes power strips in any other orientation than these! Each plug faces outward- AWAY from the center so that adapter plugs can have their wires trail away and not block the one next to it... not only that, but they alternate sides so that there is a nice amount of space in between each plug for those extra-chunky adapters. Every single one of my plugs is accessible, no matter what I put in the one next to it. And icing on the cake? 3 USB ports for direct charging of things like your phone or headset, amazon echo, or whatever else you'd like, all without using up one of the plug ports for a USB adapter!
BUT WAIT THERE'S MORE! I actually didn't notice this on the listing, but when I opened it up to try it out, I couldn't believe this also has the FLAT outlet plug that doesn't stick out of the wall, perfect for hiding behind furniture (like my desk?). I usually have a separate outlet adapter to my old power strip so that I can push my desk up against the wall with the outlet on it. This has it built in. I couldn't have asked for a better product, honestly. It's like they read my mind and finally made a product that does everything I wanted! I can't sing enough praises for this design, if you have a desktop you NEED this!

title: Forget soundbars- THIS is what you want!
text:
I was looking for something to give adequate cinematic audio to our projector movie nights that won't break the bank. In the past I've tried various sound bars but have never been all that pleased with the quality coming out of them once we turn it up to fill the room. This product, however, is astounding for the money. It has a real 2.1 speaker system, as there are two sets of woofer/tweeters for the left and right channels, as well as a decent subwoofer at the base of the tower. Sure, the sound is all coming from the same location so you won't really get the surround sound effect of having L+R on opposite sides of the room, but the clarity of the sound reproduction on this is better than my old 2-speaker setup and far better than any sound bar I've tried yet. It gets LOUD if you need it to, but unlike other speakers which can get loud, it doesn't seem to distort the audio or lose the treble in the deep bass. This is likely thanks to the dedicated subwoofer at the foot of the tower complimenting the smaller speakers above it. You may have to play with the EQ buttons to get the optimal setting for your listening experience, but I'm so surprisingly happy with this product that I'd consider that a minor issue.
The speaker supports bluetooth as well as aux inputs and other standard sources for a speaker of this classification. I tried the AUX input with the Quad-DAC feature of my LG phone to really push the speakers, and I was very impressed with what I heard. Then I connected it via bluetooth to our Firestick and put that in the projector, and a clean wireless projector movie night was had with excellent cinema quality sound. I do wish there was a way I could buy a second one and split the channels for L and R for a proper stereo experience, but honestly, I'm really just so pleased with the sound from this for the price that I can't say enough about that.

title: Great replacement for the orignal
text:
We got this to replace some broken Apple earbuds for someone in my family. You can tell they aren't Apple, but they also don't cost what Apple charges. The sound is actually super respectably good! And be careful, they're pretty good at isolating noise around you too! I lent them to a friend and had to chase them down the street before they could hear me calling their name!
They are pretty comfortable too, I'm comfortable recommending this product.

title: Excellent value!
text:
I've used Skullcandy products before and always found them to be on the mediocre side of a brand name, so I had what I'd think are pretty realistic expectations for this set. At first I just assumed this was their attempt to break into the now flooded market of inexpensive completely wireless earbud market. And you know what- it turns out that's not a bad thing at all.
These offer some impressive fidelity in sound, and unlike some other earbuds which crank up the bass to compensate for being tiny drivers, this actually delivers what I'd consider more realistic sound reproduction. It isn't too bass heavy, but the bass is still there. To be honest, that's something I'm used to hearing only on higher end speakers which don't have anything to prove other than just be good. I forgot how much I just wanted that in a headset. The battery life is pretty decent as well, not amazing but not terrible, slightly above average for what you'd expect for this style of headset. I was actually surprised to find the microphone was half decent as well, as I've never had a good experience with calls on earbuds before (the mic is just too far from your mouth to work well). These aren't going to be as clear separating your voice from the background as, say, a mic that is closer to your mouth (wired or protruding mic arm), or whatever magic Apple has in their airpods to pull off that directional sound, but honestly I was expecting worse and this surprised me. So, 5 stars for being an above average offering at an excellent price. I'd say that makes this a good value product!

title: Perfect for mounting things with cords!
text: This is great for mounting smart speakers or cameras to a wall. It is actually pretty ingenious the way it is designed to wrap the cable behind the base and then allow it down the back. I originally got mine to try mounting an Xbox Kinect sensor to the wall, but after seeing the heavy duty plastic I think I'm changing my mind and putting this in my bathroom to hold an electric toothbrush or shaver base and avoid unsightly cable mess. The base comes out easily which makes it easy to clean and fix the cable if necessary.

title: A little too bulky for a 10" tablet.
text:
I thought I'd want a bigger cover for my 10" Lenovo tab, but this was too much. It made the tablet feel heavy and bogged down, difficult to hold easily to read. That totally defeated the purpose for me, so I'm actually planning on returning it as soon as a simpler and thinner model arrives. The way the back is attached means it's basically double thickness, and the extra flap in the cover adds a cool aesthetic but also makes it double as thick. Compared to my Samsung Galaxy tablet with a foldable flip cover, this is like 3x the width, not to mention feels odd to hold open in my hands in comparison.
Some people might like this style, but it's not for me.

title: The good ol' 3.5mm jack!
text:
I'm a fan of Panasonic's electronics, and have been since I first used their GH camera line for work, and the DVX prosumer cameras before that. I was excited for a chance to replace my working headphones with ones from Panasonic, however I found it interesting that the plug type was NOT MENTIONED on this listing! The last pair of headphones + mic that I ordered came with a USB plug. It worked fine on my laptop, but not on my phone or tablet, obviously. I want a regular headphone jack, as in 1/8" or 3.5mm (whatever you want to call it!) to be compatible with all my things, and not rely on the limitations of bluetooth.
I was a little bit nervous about buying this one since it doesn't say anywhere that it is, in fact, a standard TRRS headphone-jack sized plug, but I'm happy to report that it IS! And the sound quality is what I expected from Panasonic, a good value for the price. One thing to note, however, is that this requires both sides have a wire going to the plug. This is a seriously old-school design that I almost forgot existed. Modern headphones have a single point of cable that splits to the other side in the band, however this is more like earbuds in that there's a wire going to each side.
It's not a deal breaker, it works fine and some people may actually prefer that look, but personally I'm worried about it being another point of contact that could get snagged/rip/break/go wrong, and actually prefer the more modern single-side cable style. But this is still a great pair of traditional tried-and-true headphones!

title: Dead simple to setup if you have a compatible router! But decide if you need this...
text:
I happen to use a D-Link DIR 1360 as my internet router at home, and while it does a decent job broadcasting signal around me, it is located at one corner of our home which means the opposite corner of the house has too many barriers for a fast signal. And if I want to take my laptop out to the porch? No reliability at all!
But with this placed a few rooms over from the router, it has greatly extended my network and the speed of things nearby it. It was super simple to set up, too! I'm not sure if that's just because I happen to have a D-Link router, but all I had to do was press the setup button on the router and extender while plugged in next to it, then once setup I could unplug and move it wherever I wanted to extend to. No app or IT knowledge required! Literally press the button, wait a few minutes for the lights to turn green, and good to go! The access point matches the original name of my router, so it is all completely invisible to the user. The device picks whichever device is closer / stronger and automatically connects to it without any user intervention, much like a cell phone. Now, this is only possible because my router supports this mesh-style setup. Otherwise you'll have to do one of those alternative SSID things where the device sees two networks and has to decide which one to connect to. The first was is preferable obviously, and just works better in addition to being cleaner.

With my laptop in my living room (on the other side of the house from my router), I used to get somewhere between 20-40mbps in my speed tests downloading. That's not terrible, but I'm paying for 300mbps service! But with this plugged in the middle of my home, that jumped to 80-90mbps reliably! Still not the 200+ speeds I get if only a room or two away from the router, but definitely an improvement by almost 2x... and spots outside on the porch that rarely had coverage before now do.

HOWEVER, like any extender, this WILL introduce some lag to your network. This is the part I was warning about in the headline, as most people think extenders will improve your performance across the board, which isn't true. While my download and upload speed improved, my Ping time degraded from 8ms to 14 (lower is better). That extra hop from the extender back to the router has a cost. Now, that difference shouldn't make a huge difference in most things, 14ms is still pretty respectable, however a larger ping lag can effect real-time performance like lag in multiplayer games and video call performance. Arguably, in those cases, a lower ping is more important than higher speeds. So if I'm having trouble with gaming lag or video call echo, I'd probably unplug this and go with the original weaker signal to the router directly. But if I'm going outside, or just streaming Netflix etc, than the download performance is more important than the ping. So, make your decisions wisely... I've seen too many people running multiple zoom devices over lockdown and think a wireless extender is going to solve their problems, but in fact just made everyone's zoom calls worse! But this isn't the fault of the device, that's inherent of how all extenders work. So, I'm still giving this 5 stars for being an excellent instance of what it should be: a way to boost transfer speeds and extend range that's dead simple to set up.

title: Excellent cable!
text: I got this to throw in my gear bag for live streaming jobs. The flat cable is ideal for taping down to the floors, and the length is enough to reach the closest ethernet jack in most of the rooms I've have to work in. Data throughput was reliable and solid, beats having to use WiFi in these scenarios! Very happy with this product!

title: This is FAST! If you have UHS-II cards, you NEED THIS!
text: If you don't know what UHS-II is, you probably don't understand what makes this reader special. But, if you've got one of these new UHS-II cards (you can tell by the extra set of pins, see photo), and you're using it in a regular SD card reader, you owe it yourself to get one of these! The price is right, as I've never seen a UHS-II reader this low, and the boost in speed is noticeable. I work in digital video, and coming back with tons of 4K content can sometimes take 6-10 minutes to load data for editing per card. With this reader and a compatible UHS-II card, I just managed the same task in 2 minutes. I performed a data speed benchmark (see attached screenshot), and you can see the read speeds are almost 2.5x what I get with my traditional standard SD reader! This thing reads faster than some internal HDDs! Super impressed, this will cut down on wait times dramatically.

title: Good heavy duty stand
text: This is a good alternative to my lightweight travel stands. My larger lights were always wobbly on those, but this stand gives me confidence that my lights are secure when setting up on location. It feels well made and has many mounting options thanks to the removeable mount pin on top. I would not recommend this if you're looking for a small and light stand to travel with- this is better suited for applications that require a heavier payload on top. I bring one of these now for my main key light (heaviest light), and then stick to the smaller lighter ones for my fill and backlight (generally using smaller LED panels). This is definitely a good value for a strong stand.

title: Better than expected!
text:
This is a perfect budget friendly way to add quality sound to a projector! We sometimes use our Firestick to watch movies on the wall with the projector, however the challenge has always been how to get epic sound to go along with the epic looking visuals (projector speakers are terrible). The Firestick lacks any audio out ports, however it DOES have bluetooth! I had tried smaller cheap soundbars before, but they were all the battery-powered variety that don't really get loud enough or deep enough to fill a room with rich sound.
I was expecting this to be another similar experience, but I have to admit I'm pleasantly surprised with how loud and clear this is! It looks, behaves and (most importantly) sounds like a much more expensive sound bar, and really fills the room with the cinematic sound I wanted. I actually like it better than our 2.1 stereo system's sound, so I might take down those and just use this!

title: PoE = only one power adapter needed! Almost perfect!
text:
First of all, the signal quality is great over my 300' of CAT5e cable going from my entertainment system in front of my room to my projector around the back (cable goes behind walls and snakes around furnishings to get where it needs to go). It is fast and responsive, and the lag seems minimal if any. I love that it can also be used as a pass through, and that it only requires power on ONE side!
