My old HDMI extender required a power adapter on both the tx and rx side, but this can actually send power over the network cable (PoE) so that the other side does not need its own adapter. Now THAT's awesome!
This is one of the primary reasons I was interested in this, as there are two times I use such an adapter: When I use my projector instead of my TV for movies, and when moving a camera around at an event that I want to send a live feed back to a screen or streaming box for. Currently I have to supply power at both ends of the network cable, but I imagined ONLY needing power on the receiver, and having THAT power the transmitter. For example, in the case of the camera, I could have the screen receiving the signal send power to the transmitter by the camera using PoE and be somewhat more free of tethered power on that side. Also, when using the projector, I could turn on the outlet controlling the projector via remote and have it power on the transmitter behind the TV as well. Less wires and outlet spaces where already difficult / congested is good! THE PROBLEM, however, is that this thing misses its potential by only sending power from the TRANSMITTER! In other words, I can send power from the tx with PoE to the rx side, but the RECEIVER can't power the transmitter! It only goes the same direction as the HDMI signal. This, to me, was disappointing as that's the side I wanted to save from having more wires to plug in. Not the receiving side. That side is never an issue to supply power.
So I was a little upset about that. But otherwise, it is a solid product that seems to do what it claims to, and so far seems more reliable than my previous setup. If it could send power using EITHER side, it would be perfect! So close this time!

title: Great budget device for streamers!
text:
This is a great little capture device for streaming and recording content from HDMI sources! I've been asked to stream a lot of live events (graduations, benefit concerts, etc) since Covid19 started. With this, I can take the feed out of my camera directly into the box, and stream or record using something like OBS software on my laptop. The input is considered like a USB webcam to the system, so really anything, including Zoom or Skype, can utilize the content coming from a camera or other HDMI source.
I have a Magewell HDMI to USB box that I was using before this one, and while the quality of the stream was professional (excellent color and stream clarity), it actually would often overheat and drop frames. I actually had to put a cooling fan on it to prevent that from happening on a long event outdoors. But so far, this adapter seems to be better at handling heat- likely because the overall box is bigger so the heat can dissipate. Crazy because the Magewell cost a lot more than this. Also this one has an HDMI pass through, which the magewell did not! That means you can split this with another ouput, for example run it out to a TV, a camera monitor, projector, or external recorder like a Atmos Ninja. The magewell couldn't do any of that without a separate splitter sitting before it to copy the signal to multiple outputs.
Yes, there are cheaper capture card adapters out there, but in my experience they are a mixed bag of mostly unreliable performance and subpar coloring, and lack the features this offers. The Magewell might still be the most pro version of this I've used as far as color and clarity, but it is more expensive and only offers a single input with no passthrough, not to mention overheats easily. I'd definitely recommend giving this one a try!

title: Does NOT live up to claims
text:
I'm glad I tested this card before using it on something in my camera. I don't know where they come off trying to call this "professional" in the title, but this is anything but. The speeds are atrocious, attaching a benchmark to show. This is no where near the claims of U3, or 1000x or 95mbs. As you can see, I'm barely getting 18 reading. And the test actually locked up for the last two items. I tried it again and played the settings and finally got it to complete the test, but the card seems super unreliable and too slow for 4K video caputre, possibly even too slow for decent 1080 codecs as well.
The capacity is also reported oddly- my Sandisk cards (which I tested right after this to make sure the equipment wasn't faulty), not only tested approximately to the speed printed on the card in benchmarks, but it reports a 64GB card is around 60 after formatting. This one says 62 after formatting, which makes me wonder if the capacity is fake and being incorrectly reported by the chip inside. This card seems too good to be true for a reason, I would not trust it.

title: Great pro light!
text: I've used Godox brand strobes before, so I was excited to try out this constant video light. I gotta say, LEDs have come a long way! This is a very bright light with standard mounts for light stands. It even looks like the strobes I've used before, except that this is a constant light for video. The color seems really accurate according to my camera's WB settings, and I like that it comes with sock diffusers of different colors to adjust it.  I wish it could adjust kelvin to match house lights like the way other LED panels can these days, however I understand that is difficult if not impossible in this form factor (it is not an array of lights that can be adjusted to make different colors, but rather a VERY LARGE diode in a reflector). Plenty of pro level lights are a single K value, so this is not really a con. It matches quite well with sunlight from a window, so I am able to light an interview subject using the sun as one of my lights. Super cool!

title: Very cool 4k recorder if you know what you're doing
text:
I've been doing a lot of live event streaming and usually have OBS software running to also record. Having this device however means I don't need to record in the software and/or use it as a backup, as this will offload the recording directly to my SSD drive I have plugged into it!
I have an Atmos Ninja recorder I sometimes use as well, however it is picky about the source (if there's a splitter or adapter in the middle, it doesn't like it), whereas this seems to accept almost anything I throw at it so far. I like that. Also, the fact that it can bump all the way to 4K is pretty sweet too, as I can even use the original Sony A7S (which only recorded 1080 internally) as a full 4K recorder now! Cons are that it doesn't really have a display to tell you what's going on so you need to rely on the little LED colors to figure it out. Plugging a field monitor into the HDMI out helps, as you can see the output as well as the "rec" label on-screen.
NOTE: DO NOT use the output of this box as your stream or other devices in a chain, as the output is NOT a clean copy of the original! Imagine that this box is using your monitor/TV/output as its own screen, with its own overlays and all. One other reviewer mentioned that it appeared cropped on the output versus what his camera showed. That is acceptable with using this with a field monitor to keep tabs on what it is doing, however, if you wanted to go straight from this box to an OBS stream or projector for a wall at an event, you're going to see the overlays. It does NOT support clean HDMI out.
I intend to use it with an HDMI splitter as a backup stream, or with my A7S mark i as a 4K recorder, and for that it is perfect.

title: Great for SSDs or USB adapters
text: I have a Magewell HDMI adapter for live streaming that tends to get pretty hot when used for an entire event. These seemed to be about the right size to stick on and get some heat dissipated. Just note, these don't have adhesive so you'll need to get some thermal paste. It comes in a pack of 4 which is nice. Does the trick.

title: Wonky UI, but very cool!
text:
My younger kids wanted a music player but they are too young for a phone so I looked into these dedicated touch-screen players. These are a big step up from the old mp3 players of my days. First of all, they have bluetooth so you can actually use modern wireless headphones which is awesome, in addition to regular 3.5mm headphones. The sound quality is excellent, and it even has a built in speaker for use without any headphones at all!
Granted, the speaker isn't very loud, but the fact that it HAS one is huge in my opinion! And my daughter thinks so too.
The user interface is a little bit difficult to figure out, things aren't very intuitive to find and sometimes it seems to respond with a bit of a lag, but kids seem to adapt to it pretty quickly. One thing I was not able to get working however, is the video function. The product details claim it can play video and indeed, there is a video function on the menu, however I could not get anything to play on it. It does not recognize any file extension other than avi, and none of the standard AVI codecs that I tried did anything. I have no idea what this thing can actually play so if you're getting it hoping to put little videos on it, you may be sorely disappointed!

title: Really PREMIUM sound!
text:
I've heard a lot of wonderful things about the Sony noise cancelling sets like these, and let me tell you: it isn't just hype. The sound quality is excellent, and the noise cancelling is eerily amazing. I put it on my wife and kids with the noise cancelling off and then turned it on to demonstrate, and you can see each them suddenly smile like "whoa". Like my Sony studio headphones I use professionally for work, the actual fidelity of the sound it reproduces is excellent, and the microphone for calls is excellent despite being up by my ears and so far from my mouth (other bluetooth headphones I've tried were good for music only, the mic being up by my ears wasn't good enough to isolate my voice from ambient sound, but this definitely does a great job).
The app gives a ton of control beyond what I expected to really customize the experience. For example, I have mine set to auto-pause if the headphones are removed, and to turn off noise cancelling when it detects me speaking to someone, and then resume playback when the headphones are removed/replaced. These features are all customizable, as well as many more. But you need the app. And this is where the cons come in:
1) You really need the app to get the most out of this. I was thinking about pairing this with my desktop and/or TV, but without the app you have far less control, and to be honest I couldn't even get it to pair with my phone using just Bluetooth alone. There seems to be a way according to the instructions, but I couldn't figure it out without using the app installed.
2) For a set that costs this much, I'm surprised at how scuffed up it got after one fall from about 3 feet next to my car. Including pictures. This happened the day I got it. I'm not sure if there's anything that can be done about that, pavement is hard to recover from if anything is dropped, but it's something to keep in mind if you're spending this much money on a gadget. My studio headphones have been roughed around for years and held up fine.

All in all, I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't so reliant on the app to get the features going and/or more resilient to being dropped. Feels like I should deduct one for that. But as far as features and sound quality go, this is a solid 5 out of 5.

title: FAST and tiny!
text: This little guy is closer in size to a USB stick than a traditional M.2 external SSD. Pictured here, you can see it next to a standard sized USB thumb drive on the left and a Sabrent M.2 SSD on the right. Remarkably tiny, yet mighty- I benchmarked over 450MBs (nearly half a gig per second!). Very impressed with this device!

title: The kind of thing that GoPro should have included in the box!
text:
When I first got my GoPro Hero, I actually found the included mounts kind of silly. I mean come on, not even a 1/4" 20 tripod screw?! At least give us something to hold it with?
This product is great because it you can open the legs and stand it up on a table or close them and use it like a handle / stick. For 90% of what I use my Hero7 for, this covers my bases. This is so useful, it makes the argument that it should have been included in the box with the Hero! At the very least, GoPro should have given us a tripod mount, but this is even better. I highly recommend it if you own a Hero camera.

title: Does what I need it to!
text: This is a decent sized stick, it performed similarly to an average HDD in read/write speeds. The capacity is generous and it makes a great tool for file sharing. I bring mine with me on jobs to transfer content from client's computers to my laptop for editing. Definitely something I recommend keeping around, and for the price it seems like a good value compared to big brand names that charge more.

title: Decent inexpensive player, but video is a myth?
text:
This may not be a high end DAC player like my expensive audio equipment or even my Quad-DAC LG phones, but it is an adorable little device that is more than capable of playing some high quality tunes on a budget. I have a 7 year old daughter who always wants to use my phone for music, so I figured this would be a good little player for her. It doesn't disappoint, we didn't even need to add a storage card since the internal 8GB is enough to load up plenty of songs from our library of mp3s.
I was actually hoping I could throw a couple of short videos on there for her too since it claims to also play that, however I have not been able to get that to work. It seems to only support AVI files, and I tried many different codecs and none are playable. The instructions are a joke, I wish it came with a demo file or something so I could at least inspect and see what codecs work. But otherwise, everything about this is pretty straight forward- connect via USB, drag and drop, use touch screen. Aside from the video, it really does just work as expected. I actually really like that it comes with a cool little watch band so she can wear it like a smartwatch and play music off it. I'm really pleased with the value of it.

title: Great features and sound quality! Some caveats
text:
I've been a fan of Panasonic's consumer electronics since their camcorder days, so I was excited to try these! I've owned many of the cheap Chinese wireless earbuds, and generally sound is good enough for music or listening to videos but I've never found one with a microphone decent enough for sound quality outside of the major brands (Apple, Samsung, etc).
Well, I'm happy to say these Panasonic 'buds don't skimp! They don't cost as much as the big players but the sound quality both for listening and microphone use is head and shoulders over the cheap knock offs. The noice cancelling feature is pretty amazing as well, and overall I'm very pleased with the feature set and quality of those features. But here's the caveat:
The ergonomics aren't great. Touch sensitive buds are difficult for me because I'm the kind of person who moves around a lot and needs to adjust my earbuds to keep them from falling out. But touch sensitivity means sometimes I'm accidentally activating things when I don't want to. I also didn't find some of the features intuitive and had to learn how to use them properly (changing noise cancelling modes for example). They also have rather bright blinking LEDs but you'll only notice that in a dark room. All in all, this is a good product that could be made better in a second edition. For the price, I think it fits squarely between the polished big name brands and the cheap knock offs. This is a good product, it works and doesn't exactly what it says. But it isn't perfect.

title: Painfully slow write speeds
text:
I knew this was a USB 2.0 drive, but this is slow even for that standard. I tried using it to copy the contents of a memory card over to another computer that didn't have a card reader, and it was frustrating. 32GB (half the capacity of the card) took about 2 hours to write! Playing it back was OK, but doing a benchmark speed test I can see that even the read speed is well below the USB 2.0 standard.
It works, so I'm giving it 3 stars, but I can't think of an opportunity that I would want to use this for the intended capacity. Can you imagine needing 4 hours to copy over the entire 64GB capacity of the card? No thank you!

title: AWESOME sound and so useful!
text:
I love this!
We often have spotty Wifi in our yard, so I was interested in both the WiFi repeater function as well as a good speaker system for our deck. First of all, the sound quality is AWESOME. Not that I expected less from Harmon/Kardon. They clearly know what they are doing in speakers. Having Alexa built it is super cool, however I did not like that it doesn't actually work like an Echo. Much like other "Alexa enabled" devices, this can't be added to groups for multi-room music, which was very disappointing. We own a Facebook Portal and Ecobee security camera, as well as some Kindles and phones with Alexa available, but none of those devices are considered actual Echos when it comes to music groups. Only our two Echo Dots and Fire TV Stick can be grouped for multi-room music. I was hoping since this was a speaker system first, maybe it would be an exception but alas, it is not.
However, I'm still giving this 5 stars on account of being an excellent sound system that also spreads Wifi out to our yard!

title: Adorable!
text: My 7 year old daughter LOVES these! They are cute and light up and fold to put away easily in a bag or backpack. She actually said the folding part of it made it feel less comfortable, but I'll admit I'm not sure what that means exactly. When I looked at them I couldn't find any part of it that would cause discomfort. Meanwhile, it comes with a spare battery for the light up part which is welcome, and sound quality is good enough for the intended use as a kid's listening device with some fun flair.

title: Really useful (even WITHOUT the subscription!)
text:
Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!

title: for SERIOUS sound!
text:
They're not kidding when they say this is a speaker made for outdoor use. Unlike smaller bluetooth speakers made for a desk or small room, this is a serious 15w device that can crank out some surprisingly loud levels of bass that can vibrate the floor (I put it on our living room floor to test it and you could FEEL it across the room thumping). I used it today out on our wooden deck, and it was actually TOO LOUD at full volume, we had to turn it down a little. That's impressive out of a battery powered unit!
I have to admit, at full volume (which we used just to test how high it can be cranked), the audio was exhibiting some distortion, but that's expected for a unit this size. Keeping it a few notches below top, it was plenty loud and clear quality to the music. It paired easily with our phones, however it took me a bit to figure out how to unpair and pair again with a different device (hold the play/pause button until it says "disconnect" followed by "pairing"). The audio cable is a nice option to have as well, and the build quality seems rugged enough to take on a camping trip and survive unscathed. It claims to be IPX5 waterproof, and the thick rubberized feel to it prevents scratches and scuffs. Very impressed with it!

title: A fantastic SSD
text:
I have an NVME drive already installed in my system but I'd like some additional storage for media editing that doesn't resort to the latency and slow r/w times of a spinning disk. These SATA drives are PERFECT for that! I haven't put it inside my case yet, but in just a USB3.0 enclosure it seems to do quite well (picture of speed benchmark shown). Not quite the 500+ speed advertised on the box, but a 10-15% discrepancy is reasonable especially when using an enclosure and not doing sequential reads and writes. I'm sure once I set this up internally it'll perform even better.
Great to add some storage to a modern system, and of course especially great if your mobo doesn't support NVME and you need something with an SATA interface. Quality product from a quality brand name, I recommend it.

title: Excellent desktop mic!
text: I work in video production and sometimes need to record narration for my work. I have an expensive Rode mic system that I use with my cameras, but I decided to see how a permanent mic setup like this would do. First of all, the amount of equipment you get for the money is insane. The pop guard and arm are pretty awesome, but it turns out my desk didn't have a good place to clamp an articulating arm like that. Thankfully, it also came with a little tripod base so you can have it sit on the desk instead. The USB sound system uses a standard RealTek Audio chip, so it's pretty universally compatible and offers excellent sound quality. In the past sometimes the PC's audio input 3.5mm jack produced extra noise on account of the PSU creating some sort of line humming. With a USB audio interface, that's a non-issue.  I'm impressed with the response of it, it managed to pick up my voice and not a lot of background noise (my computer fan can get loud sometimes!). The only hangup is that I spend some time trying to figure out how to get it accessible to my recording applications. For some reason it kept complaining that the sample rate of the mic didn't match. It did, but the computer kept complaining. I ended up going into Windows sound settings, changing the sample rate, then going back in and changing it back and THEN it worked. It's been good ever since. So, still an excellent mic with impressive quality for the price!

title: Decent value on the cheap
text:
This is a mid-range SSD drive for a pretty good price. Right now as I'm reviewing this, the 120GB model is about $20, which is practically nothing for a solid state drive. It's good for the price but there are also better options out there if you wanted to spend a little more on a brand name.
After formatting it, I tried it as a second drive with my desktop, and ran a benchmark using CrystalDiskMark. The results were OK- still faster than a spinning drive for sure, but a far cry from speed numbers written on the packaging, and definitely not as fast as other SSD drives I've owned (from brands like Sandisk). I was kind of annoyed that the packaging reported speeds being so much higher. Additionally, the rear of the packaging said 240GB capacity, however the front is correctly labelled 120GB for the one I got, which makes me wonder what else is a mistake (the data speed numbers perhaps?).
That being said, if you're looking for a cheap SSD to speed up an old laptop or maybe throw in an HDMI recorder or something, you could do worse than this one. I wanted to give it 3.5 stars but since that isn't an option, rounding up to 4.

title: Surprisingly awesome!
text:
I've owned many affordable bluetooth speakers, but never one this size! I love this, the sound quality is FAR BETTER than anything I've used in this price range. The woofers deliver solid bass, and the directions really help fill a space with sound. I love that it even has a carrying handle and a place to plop your phone onto (great for Karaoke!). I'm a little confused by the Mic input, I thought perhaps this could work as an alternative to the line in... for example, I can line in for music, but also sometimes I'd like a mic-level input for using with a microphone. But the mic input seems to only get used for some sort of recording to TF card function, which I couldn't get to work anyway. Doesn't matter, I wasn't so interested in that feature, I was more interested in using it as an amp and thought that might be an interesting alternative use.
Using the speaker for both bluetooth audio or wired aux in worked very well. The FM radio is nice too, but I didn't try it much. All in all, the battery life seems pretty solid and this thing is incredibly powerful for a battery operated speaker. We usually don't max out the volume because that's too loud!

title: Very cool accessory for Sony shooters
text:
Full disclosure- I own an A5100 because I sometimes want to video blog without using an external monitor to see myself. That camera has a flip up screen that can turn 180 degree and face the front like a selfie cam. But coming from my A7 series cameras, I really would rather use the more pro-features and full frame capabilities found there. Enter this genius little accessory... it's literally just a mirror that attaches to the hotshoe mount on the camera. If your camera has a display that can rotate at least 90 degrees (like the Sony A7 series can), it's a perfect fit to bounce that display back to the subject to see themselves. An extra perk? The original screen is still viewable by someone behind the camera, so you can actually allow the subject to see themselves AND a shooter monitor the display simultaneously, all without costly external monitors and batteries. The gadget still offers a cold shoe mount on top to attach more accessories if needed, so you don't necessarily lose the mount if using this (mic, light, etc).
I tried it on my A7S and it worked perfectly.

title: Great for action cameras!
text: I'm using this with my Go Pro Hero 7, and it works exactly as expected. The mount comes with the standard type that a GoPro camera uses on the factory case, so it was a breeze to connect it and tighten it up. The suction cup seems really solid- it uses a lever to increase suction and secure it to a smooth surface. I haven't tried it out the side of a moving vehicle like in the pictures above, but those pictures are pretty laughably fake anyway. Doesn't make this any less versatile, honestly, and I DID use it inside my car attached to the windshield to record a carpool Karaoke and that held on quite well (I actually had a hard time removing it!). So, it seems to work as expected!

title: Love a good wired pair.
text: Wireless headphones are all the rage right now, but sometimes I just want a good wired pair. When I'm using laptop especially, using Bluetooth headphones introduces lag and another thing that needs to be charged. These are excellent premium feeling wired 'phones that include an inline mic and controls if your device supports it. When used with my desktop that offers only a TRS plug (only two lines), it works as just a pair of headphones, with decent sound quality and bass response. On my LG phone or laptop which accept a TRRS plug (3 lines), the mic works as an input as well. My laptop didn't respond to the volume control buttons, but I think most phones will. Regardless, I'm impressed with the quality and presentation for the money this costs.

title: Great way to always have power ready!
text:
I have a Hero 7 Black, and I like to hyperlapse hiking trails with it. This set ensures that I'll always have a battery ready to go and a couple of spares I can even carry with me in case I to swap in the field. So far it seems to last about as long as the original Go Pro ones, and I regularly charge the OEM battery along with some spares in this charger. There's always at least one battery ready to go, which is much better than always charging like before!
One thing to note- this is USB powered to charge, and it does NOT like being plugged into a computer. I tried even on my desktop and it complained that a device is trying to draw too much power and cut it off. A standard USB power brick like for charging a phone is fine. But don't try using a computer, especially a laptop, to charge it.

title: Manual focus, but decent quality + surprise macro function!
text:
So, let me start off by saying, this isn't the best quality webcam on the market. But for the price, no one is expecting it to be. And it is FAR from the worst! During the Covid Pandemic, all the regular brand name webcams were sold out so I found myself trying out a bunch of these no-name brands from Amazon. The last one I tried actually had a much harsher fisheye effect in the corners, as well as over-saturated color. This one seems far less cartoony and more realistic in color reproduction, as well as being somewhat more rectilinear (photo speak for straight lines being straight, not as much curved distortion). There is a bit of fisheye curve on the edges, but it is very usable and didn't make my ceiling look concave like my last one I tried. See attached images for examples of the room's wall distortion. It's there if you are looking for it, but not terrible when you're looking at a subject. The microphone is just meh. I have a desktop mic and the sound out of that was MUCH better, especially because you can get it closer to your face than the camera. But the fact that this HAS a mic is a good option in a pinch. I would just strongly recommend an external mic if you want people to hear you clearly. Also something I didn't know before trying this:
It is MANUAL focus! That means it won't follow and focus on you automatically, you have to twist the lens until you're sharp in the view. It actually isn't that hard to nail focus, the depth of focus is pretty deep so once you've set it for your standard sitting distance, you likely won't have to change it ever again unless you walk away from the camera. A fun side effect, however is that the focus lens gear lets you push it to EXTREME MACRO distances! So you can do insane closeups of things if you want to, for example, put a webcam on an ant farm maybe? I tried it out on my desktop speaker, and in one picture you can see the relative size of it compared to my desk and then the closeup you can see the detail of the scratched plastic where it says Harmon / Kardon. Ha, if nothing else this shows me I should probably get new desktop speakers too! These are beat up when up close! A fun and versatile camera for a good price. If you need autofocus tracking, this might not be for you though.

title: A good workhorse (read for caveats)
text:
This is an excellent working laptop with pretty high end specs. To be fair, with these specs and price point I would have really liked a touch screen, but I supposed that's not the target market for this laptop. This is a workstation that you can fold up and take with you, not a gaming machine or touch friendly gimicky browser. This is for getting things done. 16GB of ram and the 10th generation i7 are pretty top mark for mobile specifications, and I love LOVE that this has an Ethernet jack. I actually have an older laptop that I use for live streaming setups attached to a pro camera, and I used to need a USB to ethernet adapter to get a solid internet connection (can't trust wifi for live streaming). This laptop will easily replace that, offering everything I need internally, and keep up better as well thanks to the more efficient CPU.
No, it doesn't have a GeForce GPU or anything like that, but the CPU is more than capable for things like video encoding and the gaming experience with the Intel Graphics is no slouch either! The webcam is just OK, it isn't as clear as modern phones or even higher end laptops, but it gets the job done. And that's the point of this laptop I think- getting the job done. This is a great option for a solid powerful computing machine.

title: Better than in-place adapters
text: I have a wireless mic that I want to use with my camera, however the receiver has a hardwired 1/4" jack and my camera uses a standard headphone sized 1/8" jack. I've been using one of those adapters to go from 1/4 to 1/8 that sits at the end of a cable, and those have always given me grief.  This is much more solid connection as the cable IS the adapter. It is much more reliable and has been great so far. I highly recommend it over an additional adapter on the cable.

title: Does what it is supposed to.
text: I needed these to connect an adapter to my Minivan's entertainment system. It's a slightly older minivan, and the system is based on analog RCA plugs, so I got an adapter to go from HDMI to RCA, and then use these bad boys to make the final jump to the car's inputs. It's just a straight cable, there's not really much else to comment on. It works as it should.

title: Decent performance for price
text: This is a pretty good value microSD card. I did some tests on my desktop to check speeds, they aren't the fastest ever but they are no slouch either. Pretty good for the money I'd say. I really like the painted graphic on the plastic, it is unique and fun, and probably a shame if you end up just leaving it in your switch all day! I used mine to record some drone footage today and it seems to be holding up great so far.  I got the 128GB version, of which 118GB is usable according to Windows (which sounds correct to me after format).

title: A good FHD webcam
text:
I really needed one of these for my desktop during this time of teleconferencing for work and school. I wouldn't say it's incredible quality, a selfie camera on a modern flagship phone will have better, but it is absolutely usable for zoom meetings, skype calls, and real time streaming, and allows me to use the comfort of my desk and dual-monitor PC setup.
As you can see in the image, the view is rather wide, which comes with a bit of barrel distortion (look at the wall curve where it hits the ceiling- I promise this is straight in real life!). It's not a fish eye distortion, but it's slight and noticeable on straight edges. It has an LED indicator that comes on to tell you it has power, and then another light that comes on to tell you when it is active. I like this, because you have a visual indicator that your camera is on so that you won't have to worry about covering it for hackers or things like that. There is a mic but personally I like using an external mic that is closer to my mouth. The mic is OK on this, and definitely useful if you don't have one already. All in all, it is very functional and a major upgrade over my XP-era VGA resolution webcam from forever ago. Just don't expect it to be amazing. It's a good value for the price.

title: Good for charging
text:
More and more phones and devices in my household are switching to USB-C for charging, so having more of these cables around are important! I like the build design of this one, in particular the way it is reinforced with rubbery plastic where the cable goes into the ends, which helps it slightly bend with less stress on the cable. I believe this design will make it more durable in the long run, as those ends are were cables eventually fray in my experience.
Yes, the spec is USB 2.0 as mentioned, so high speed data connections need not apply. But the item description title says "charging cable", which implies it is best suited for charging rather than data. For that usage, I can confidently say 5 stars.

title: Perfect for keeping USB C devices charged!
text:
We recently went from having 1 out of 4 phones in the house using USBC to all 4 using USBC. That means we're all fighting over the extra chargers in the house, so a multi-pack like this is GREAT to have on hand! The build quality is good, they don't feel like the bottom of the barrel flimsy cables. I can't tell how long they will actually last but they feel pretty good so far. I also like the color of them, the metallic blue makes it easy to spot in a multi-charger mess of wires.
I recommend it.

title: Better than other cheapos
text:
There are fortunately many wireless headphones in this price range these days. Usually they are pretty similar, but this is one of the better ones. The first thing I noticed is how SOFT the ear cups are. It feels like something that belongs on a more expensive set, almost luxurious. That makes these much more comfortable to wear for long periods versus many of the other inexpensive headphones. The build quality feels good, and the sound quality is pretty decent too. Speakers of this size are usually pretty good at their bass response, and these are no exception. They naturally have a bit of noise isolation due to the cup design, and you have the option to connect a 3.5mm cable to use them as traditional wired headphones as well.
The one thing I DON'T like, is the microphone. Don't buy these for phone calls. The mic is too far from your mouth to separate you from background noises. Yes, I know airpods also have their mic far from your math but Apple has some sort of magic voodoo to make that work somehow. I've never liked the mic on any of these headphones, so I'm used to that by now. But I feel like these are marketed more for people who want to listen to music, and for that they are great and comfortable! I honestly wish they would disable the handsfree profile so that my phone wouldn't keep trying to use it for phone calls. Otherwise, a solid buy for this price!

title: A cool concept, not quite what I expected- Read to understand
text:
Let's get one thing straight right away: THESE ARE NOT SUNGLASSES. They are blue-light blocking at best, or just mildly tinted most likely. I took them out of the box and thought "Oh cool! These are the kinds of glasses that get dark outside and transparent when you are inside!", but nope- I wore them for a full hour outside and they didn't get any darker or exhibit any sun blocking properties AT ALL. So that's false advertising right there. They aren't for use in the sun. They don't darken anything.
As far as audio quality... they are a cool concept, but again, falls short of expectations. The open ear design means the speakers have to work harder to be audible. That means they often make those tin-sounding rattles that tiny speakers make when cranked up too high. This is definitely NOT cool for music as most of the fidelity is lost right off the bat, and adding insult to injury is that they often don't get loud enough to use outside. I'm not saying using it in a crowded subway terminal (that you can just forget about completely), I'm talking about even just going for a stroll around my suburban block with some birds chirping and the wind blowing lightly, maybe a car driving in the distance. I tried listening to a recorded lecture (since music was a lost cause), and they couldn't get loud enough to hear clearly. The microphone for calls was OK in my test, so I guess they are cool as a way to take a phone call without wearing a headset, but that only works if you're wearing these anyway as sunglasses. They aren't sunglasses, so you wouldn't be wearing them anyway, and you wouldn't be wearing them for music, and you wouldn't be wearing them to make a phone call either because they rarely get loud enough unless you are home alone... in which case you can put your phone on speaker and avoid this whole mess.
In conclusion- its a good idea but executed poorly and does NOT live up to expectations. I'm surprised there are so many good reviews on this product. I can't think of a time I would use it.

title: Very comfortable
text:
I've owned many wireless headphones, so this isn't my first rodeo. I wanted something separate to leave paired with my work computer. Earbuds aren't comfortable for me to wear for long periods of time so over-the-ear style is important. I have to admit, I like these more than I expected to. The ear pads are soft and slow to reclaim their shape like memory foam- this makes them extremely comfortable to wear so I don't mind keeping them on for a good portion of my workday. It also has a rubberized cover for the charging port and 3.5mm jack, which is surprisingly nice to find on a headset in this price range!
The sound quality is about on par with what I expected for this price range- that is, it is very good. Not blow-your-mind-amazing like sets that sell for hundreds, but as good if not better than others in this price range. What I didn't like, however, is the microphone quality. Yes, it has a mic, but I'd like to pretend it doesn't. The mic is on the headset by my ears and doesn't seem to be directed towards my mouth. This makes my voice sound distant and muffled, with ambient background noise sometimes on the same level or louder than my voice is. For calls I'd rather use a different headset, but that's OK. This ends up being used paired with my computer rather than my phone. It is pretty decent at passive noise isolation as well, reducing sound around you naturally. The only things I wish were better are the mic and perhaps a physical on/off switch rather than a button, but honestly this is pretty normal for headphones in this price range so I essentially got exactly what I expected.
EDIT:
I loved these so much, I ended up getting another on in another color for a family member. A great value for wireless headphones.

title: Great and stylish Wear OS option!
text:
If you like fully featured smart watches, it is hard to find anything this watch can't do! It runs Google's Wear OS, which is their watch variation of Android, so Google users should feel right at home with it. It's got a Play Store for apps, a really fluid interface, and of course it integrates really well with an Android Smartphone. I've been told it doesn't play as nicely with iPhones, but a lot of the core features are standardized and cross platform so it can still function as a really nice watch and allow notifications and call support regardless of device.
My wife had a Fossil Wear OS watch previously, and the feature set is very similar except for one huge plus this has: A SPEAKER! Many of the third party entry level Wear OS watches have a microphone for digital assistant commands and voice-to-text typing, but lack a speaker for it to talk back. So you have to read your responses on the screen and you can't exactly take phone calls. But THIS ONE DOES! Thanks to the speaker, you can full on take calls like a modern day Dick Tracy. That's really useful and cool, especially if you put your phone down or have it in a pocket you don't want to pull it out of all the time.
But here's the big con:
BATTERY LIFE. While this is better than other wear OS watches I've tried, it seems like Wear OS is so feature-filled, they generally need to be charged as often as smartphones do. Battery obviously depends on usage, but average use seems to last about a day or two at a time. Heavy usage and you'll need to top it off every night at least. This isn't the fault of this watch, but rather Wear OS in general. Other smart watches such as the Samsungs and FitBits can go for days to nearly a week on a charge, which means you not only won't have to worry about charging it more than once or twice a week, but you also can do sleep tracking and just leave it on at night. That's something I'm trying to do in order to have healthier sleeping habits. Some devices such as the Mi Band and Amazefit can go for around 20 days on a charge! I was using a Mi Band 3 before trying this watch, and while it doesn't run apps or have a full color screen or take phone calls, I think I prefer having a watch that only needs to be charged about once a month, and can show me my sleeping data as well as pedometer and activity charts, all while alerting me to notifications. I feel like Wear OS has a ways to go before I'm ready to switch over full time. The good news is that devices ARE getting better, as this shows. If you love Wear OS and the smartest features available, this is a good option. But personally I think I'm going back to my "smartwatch lite" that has less bells and whistles but actually fits better functionally into my life.
I want to give this 3.5 stars, I feel like 3 is too low because it IS good for what it is, but I also don't like it enough to use it daily. So settling on 4.

title: Finally someone is mass producing this!
text:
I've been doing this for years with a DIY rig made out of an interchangeable-plate battery charger. I've even got a video on youtube with over 5k views demonstrating how it works on my A7S and a dummy battery. It is such a simple concept, since most of these smaller cameras have the same voltage requirements as the big NPF batteries, I couldn't believe the market hadn't embraced mass producing the concept.
I was so glad to see devices like this have hit the market, I had to try it! I'm happy to say, it not only works just as I expected it to (provided you have the right size dummy battery adapter), but they improved upon the design by adding USB ports and even USB charging! So now if I don't want to use my dummy battery on, say, my A7Rii, I can use this as a charger to top off the internal battery while recording speeches, AND top off my phone and/or power a recorder or monitor while I'm at it!
These guys thought of everything, even offering USB C or micro USB charging so that you can use whatever cables you happen to have around. So hats off to Power Junkie, for not only mass producing something we no longer have to DIY, but adding enough functionality on top of it to be so worth it.

title: Charged my Lenovo right up!
text:
I have a discarded 7th generation Intel Lenovo I was given from an office to scrub and give to someone who's working from home during the coronavirus shutdown here in NY. Problem is, they gave it to me without the charger and I can't go back to the office and get it until they reopen the doors. Thankfully, it uses a standard USB-C shaped plug to charge. I have plenty of phones and tablets that use that, but apparently laptops need the more robust Power Delivery standard, and not the lower power of USB phone chargers.
Amazon to the rescue, with this excellent replacement PD adapter. I love that modern computers and devices are starting to embrace a standard like this going forward- Macbooks and PC laptops both use this now, and it's even backwards compatible with USB devices like phones and tablets (the reverse isn't true- I couldn't use my phone charger on this laptop, but this laptop's PD charger can charge my phone).
This device worked great for getting that Lenovo back up and running, very appreciative for a future full of standards!

title: Great WIRED headset!
text:
It's so good to find more wired TRRS headsets hitting the market. For a while it seemed like only wireless ones were selling and the wired models were all low-end earbud styles or the kind that have the mic embedded by your ears instead of your mouth.
This is a good over-the-ear style set, with decent bass response and sound quality, as well as a mic on the wire. I really like the placement of a microphone on the wire, it is second only to the telescoping mic style you see receptionists and gamers using. It keeps the mic relatively close to your mouth (rather than headsets that put the mic by your ears) so you pick up your voice more than ambient noise in the room. Just keep in mind, it is a TRRS set which means it has the extra pin on the plug for a mic. It may not work properly in standard TRS headphone plugs (stereo only, designed for use with headsets without a mic), although some can work with both.
Most modern laptops support TRRS, as well as tablets and phones (if you're lucky enough to still have a 3.5mm headset jack!).

title: Decent budget batteries, slow and steady charger.
text:
The batteries are decent for budget brand rechargeable cells, they back a very usable amount of mAh for my kids RC toys and game controllers. The charger is interesting however... unlike my other battery chargers which feed from the AC wall outlet, this uses USB. It has both micro USB and USB-C, which is very useful because I use both for different kinds of devices and I readily have one or other available and can choose accordingly. Options are good. What isn't as good, however, is that most of my USB sources won't feed enough amps to charge 8 batteries at a time with any sort of "high speed". Even a 2.5Amp charger won't really feed enough juice to charge all 8 rapidly, and most of my chargers / laptops / etc are feeding more like 0.5amp anyway. Those are much slower.
That's not necessarily a bad thing- slow charging is actually well known to be better for battery life. I'd rather charge up 8 at a time slowly than 4 rapidly followed by another 4 in the same amount of time as 8 slowly. But it is kind of misleading to claim this is a fast charger.

title: A great travel mouse!
text:
This mouse is very comfortable to use and has some great features built in. It feels just as smooth and responsive as the one on my desktop at home, and since I work with graphics and video tools, I'm much more comfortable using my laptop on the go the same way I do at home rather than a trackpad or button mouse. I particularly like that it is rechargeable via USB so no more dealing with AA batteries like my old Logitech. It also comes with a pretty neat carrying bag.
The one thing I don't like so much is the way it shuts off after a while of no usage. I often step away from my computer and then come back and move the mouse to wake up the screen. If I leave the mouse for long enough, it goes into a "sleep mode" and will only wake up from pressing a button. My old Logitech one could be woken up by just moving the mouse. More than once while using this one I thought something was wrong because the mouse wasn't responding, then I remembered to press a button first and it came back to life. A minor inconvenience for an otherwise great product for an excellent price.

title: Works well, even on other Qi devices
text:
While the small size and slight curve of this is clearly made specifically for airpods, this is still a standard Qi charger and works with anything that supports wireless Qi charging. I tried it with my phone and some other devices in the house and they all light up and start charging just fine, although perhaps at a slightly slower speed due to not supporting the higher wattage of a larger Qi charger.
I actually like having a smaller base since I want to eventually embed this into a stand for other things and it's hard to find smaller Qi-enabled charging pads. So, 5 stars for it being exactly what I wanted it to be!

title: Official SONY UHS-II
text:
I currently own 3 Sony Alpha cameras, and regularly record in 4K for work. Having a high quality fast card is important if you rely on your footage. That's why I generally only trust my paying jobs to Sony and Sandisk media. This is a real UHS-II card, as you can see in the picture attached. You can tell by the extra pins on the card, which are used for the UHS-II standard to boost the read/write speeds.
Of course, you can still read/write with a regular SD card reader, but you'll only get the benefits of the speed boost with a proper SD card port that supports the extra pins for UHS-II. Unfortunately, my desktop does not support this so I was unable to run benchmarks on the card to show you (it runs as a regular UHS-I with average speeds), but the camera is where it will make the most real-world difference, and most modern Sony cameras will have the support for this standard. If you write a lot of high bitrate 4K, especially with a Sony camera, this is the card for you!

title: Big and FAST!
text: On my USB3 desktop, I'm clocking in 138MB/s read and 126MB/s write, which is surprisingly good for a cheap unbranded stick like this! I haven't tried filling the entire 128GB capacity yet, but it seems pretty legitimate so far. I have to admit I was a little nervous about a no name brand like this being fake (I've been duped before), but this seems like the real deal. The real test will be using it in my car's entertainment system to store and pull up media played off the stick for the kids on road trips.  Hopefully it will hold up, so far so good!

title: So much fun
text:
I got this for an event gathering and it turned out to be a real hit! Loading it up with different sounds really was a hoot, and it was plenty loud in a room together with other people. It doesn't get loud enough to use at an outdoor event in my opinion, or loud enough for a very noisy event event, but with a gathering of friends or in a classroom, it is plenty loud. Even the preloaded air horn sound effect is awesome.
My wife works in a school and can already see this being something she'll use in a classroom as well. A very versatile and fun product!

title: Excellent for drawing or scratch paper!
text:
This board is another knock off the classic Boogie Board, a great tool for drawing temporary things- a doodle, a scratch pad for math homework, a note on the fridge, etc. It is an analog touch-sensitive surface that "reveals" a more reflective back layer when the opaque top layer is pressed. Basically, think of it like a touch-sensitive etch-a-sketch. When done, you can erase the entire thing using the button.
It is NOT a digital tablet, it is very much analog, but it does have a battery used to zap the screen clear when done (resets the liquid crystal to opaque).
My kids love these. The original boogie board has a bit higher contrast, but this is a good value.

title: Fancy! And interesting for lectures/audiobooks
text:
I'm so happy to see they are still making new brands of wired headphones... lately all the new designs and features have been found in wireless only, and sometimes I just want a good pair of wired 'phones, especially for use with my Quad-DAC headphone jack.
They are passive noise cancelling, which basically just means they cushion sound out mechanically with nice big ear muff style rings, as opposed to any kind of digital reverse-sine-wave trickery (which are hit or miss on cheap brands usually), and it has a really interesting "focus" mode switch, which changes the EQ of the mix to promote the frequencies used in spoken words better. This is an amazing feature for those of us who listen to audiobooks or lectures, which I do frequently. To be honest, I didn't notice a big difference between having that mode on and off, but it was nice to know someone out there is trying to make products catered for people who want to do more than just listen to music over Bluetooth.
The sound quality is pretty good for the price, and the presentation is actually really impressive. The materials feel really premium and even the box it comes in feels super fancy, which might make this a nice gift. I don't expect much out of mics that are embedded in headphones, and this pair didn't change my mind about that. The mic isn't close enough to your mouth to be of much use, picking up more ambient noise around you than you. If they wanted to include that as a feature, they could have made a removable arm like a gaming headset, but they don't need to. This is a good pair of headphones for those of us who just want to listen, which is their ideal demographic IMO.

title: A great kit, cool LEDs and plenty fast
text:
These sticks are a hair faster than my previous DIMMs, which were also rated with a 3200mhz XMP profile. I actually really like the LEDs on them because I happen to have an MSI motherboard that recognized them instantly and let me control the lights via their Mystic Light setup. The glow adds a cool look to the case, and can also be used to keep an eye on CPU temp (you can have the colors change as the CPU temp rises). The ones I got were 16-18-18-36 timings, which actually were close enough to my G.Skill ram that I could combine them and get pretty good performance out of both kits together.
The only thing I didn't like, however, is how the height was difficult to work around my heat sync. I had to switch which DIMM slots I used because the one closest to my cooling system didn't have enough height clearance to fit. Thankfully my other RAM could slide in there and I now have these LED ones in the other 2 slots. So, just keep that in mind if you have a tight space and a large heat pipe system, you might need shorter DIMMs that forgo the LED.
I'm actually quite happy that I was able to make this work, there was a moment in which I was almost going to give up. If they'll fit in your setup, I'd say they are pretty cool looking and plenty fast for a modern Mobo.

title: Good utility storage, average speed, good value
text:
This is a useful card for what I want to do with it: specifically, store video and game files for a car entertainment system (a great way to keep kids entertained on long road trips!). Our old 32GB stick was running out of space, so I'm more than happy to test out this 64GB in it's place!
So far so good- it is able to store media and play it back without any hiccups. It definitely lives up to the USB3 speed in read- see the attached benchmark showing 111+MB/s, well over the USB2.0 average of ~40-60MB/s. However the write speed leaves much to be desired, averaging around 23MB/s even over USB3.
That's perfectly fine for use like ours- mainly, write once but read many times. If you want to use this to copy a lot of data over to it quickly, you might want to buy storage with faster write times. But for the price, this is a good value.

title: This is SOLID.
text:
I have a Crane 3 Lab that I tried this attachment on, and let me say this piece is impressively strong. I love that it has the groove teeth to lock it into place like an OEM attachment, it feels solid and won't move or budge an inch unless you loosen the teeth first. I guess I shouldn't be surprised with a brand name like Smallrig, I'm familiar with their other gear and they are reputable in this industry.
I see this is advertised to also attach to a Ronin S, which I also have but use less often. Honestly, it looks like it will attach and stay put as well, but it feels like it was really made for the Crane more than the Ronin. I love it, and intend to use it for mounting audio gear.

title: Great padded case for carrying your gear
text:
This is my second Condition 1 case that I've tried out for my photo/video gear. The last one was beige colored, but otherwise pretty much identical to this one. So my review of it should be the same- the foam cut outs are easy to tear and conform to things like cameras, lenses, microphones, and other goodies you want to keep safe. It is tough and rugged feeling, however I hope I never have to test the water proof part.
While this one came fine, the other Condition 1 case I got had a loose rubber lining that wasn't in the groove etched along the cover. I was able to push it back in and it's been fine there ever since, but I don't know how waterproof that really is if it ever gets dislodged again in the future. So, don't take these swimming with you, however I'd personally trust it to the elements like rain.
A good case otherwise. I'm going to check if they have a deeper one to accommodate my Phantom drone, as this is slightly too short for it.

title: This is a PRO light!
text:
I work in photo/video for a living, and I can tell you that good LEDs aren't cheap. I have worked with hot tungsten lamps for high output and smaller LEDs for lightweight smaller setups, but LED lights that can compete with the output of Tungstens are pricey.
That being said, this is a FANTASTIC light. It has high output yet has the pros of LED panels such as lower power consumption and heat, as well as being dimmable and color adjustable from the panel or remote control. I had the opportunity to use this for a job yesterday setting up an interview in an office setting. My tungsten bulbs would have been too bright and need gels to match the rest of the office. My other smaller LEDs would have cast smaller spots and we all know a larger light source casts a more pleasing glow. It seemed effortless to get the amount of light we needed in a short time.
HOWEVER, I did find that the mounting point was a little bit difficult to use. There are two bolts to secure it to the stand, and both need to be loosened to mount it properly. It took me a few attempts to get it on the stand, one side felt like I was screwing the bolt the wrong direction most of the time. Meanwhile, the light is large and kept wobbling during this overly complicated procedure. It didn't feel like a premium product during that, which I found odd considering the price point. I have lights that cost about half of this one that felt more premium during mounting. But, that being said, once the lights are up it works a treat!
So, a solid 4 stars from me. Almost 5 if the mounting were easier or the price lower to make up for that. But as a light, it does what it should do and well.

title: Useful for water-related photos
text:
I want to give this 3.5 stars- 3 is too low and 4 seems too high, but I'll round up for now. I have mixed things to say about this camera. It isn't going to take stellar photos. They are either going to have a lot of motion blur or if you raise the shutter speed (sports mode) you're going to get substantial noise. The videos side is even worse. A modern cell phone or point-and-shoot is going to snap better photos and videos. BUT... you can take this to a water park and not care what happens to it, which is exactly what we did.
I'm including three examples shots here that I wouldn't have gotten without this camera (excuse the smiley face for privacy). One are kids about to go down a water slide, where I as the photographer am being rained on by nearby sprinklers. Then there's a slightly more epic shot of the giant bucket atop the slides crashing water down on me. This shot froze the droplets of water right before thoroughly drenching the photographer (me) a split second later. The last is from some of our underwater pool shots. These are all cases in which I would NOT have been comfortable using my real cameras or even cell phones- as waterproof as they claim some flagship phones are now, I wouldn't trust them to this. In my experience, even waterproof phones have trouble operating under water (the touch screen doesn't work properly), and we have ruined the charging port of another at a pool previously. But this is totally sealed and has real buttons that work just as well under water as above. For all those reasons, I actually LIKE this camera. It takes photos I literally would NOT have gotten otherwise.
Also, as a bit of personal experience, after going down a water slide and trying to video it, I actually dropped the camera into the pool at the bottom. I was able to run in and chase and grab it, and the entire time I was thinking I'm SO GLAD this isn't my phone!
I'm actually printing some of the photos as I write this and although they appear grainy on my screen, on 4x6 photo paper they look perfectly acceptable.
So why 3.5 stars? Well, the user interface is terrible. More than once I had to turn it off and restart to get back to photo taking because I couldn't figure out how to get out of the mode I was in. Also, it claims to have a 21megapixel mode, but I'm pretty sure it is just upscaling a smaller resolution. The noise at 21mp seems soft, like it took a lower resolution image and then scaled it UP to 21 mp. The 12 megapixels mode seemed much more true-to-pixel size, so that seems like a bit of false advertising. Then there's the video mode- keep it at 720 if you want any kind of normal playable frame rates. It also looks like less-than-HD that has been scaled up to fit, but at least it works at all. At 1080 HD, it was doing a variable frame rate thing that often slowed to a slide show and wasn't playable on my phone or laptop. I'm only able to play it back from the camera, which I wish I had known before I chose it for some things I wanted to remember.
Outside of those caveats, it is good for the specific use as a camera you can afford to get wet.

title: Great way to store your gear
text:
I work in photo/video for a living, so cases like these to travel with are an absolute necessity. They feel relatively tough and rugged, however I hope that I never have to test the waterproof claim. When I first opened it, the rubber lining that I believe is used to keep it water tight was actually half detached and hanging. I had to feed it back into the groove it fits into, where it has stayed since. That's OK as I don't intend for this to suffer more than some light rain heading to/from a gig rather than survive a flood, but if the waterproof claim is what piqued your interest, perhaps a brand like Pelican would be a better wager.
Otherwise, this is a very decent and usable case for things I want to protect, such as lenses, batteries, microphones, etc.
NOTE: I was hoping my DJI Phantom 3 would fit in one of these, but it does not. I could have measured ahead of time and known that, but I got excited seeing the images here of others fitting their (smaller) drones in. The Phantom drones need a bigger case, unfortunately.

title: So handy to have around
text:
I know everything is cloud based these days, but a good USB stick is still indispensable in my opinion. For my job I find myself responsible for presentations in places that often have no reliable internet access, and being able to hand over the finished video on a stick like this is perfect. Just yesterday, I used one of these as a Windows installation media to fix a botched dual boot laptop without a CD/DVD drive. Now that I've fixed it, I might throw a live linux distro onto the stick for future use as a handy recovery system.
They aren't the fastest transfer speed available, but they are perfectly acceptable for daily use.

title: A great budget gaming card
text:
This is a good card if you're on a budget and want some CUDA acceleration for your desktop. Personally, I have some applications that require CUDA cores for proper operation (Photogrammetry and Adobe's Mercury Playback Engine), and it's not so much that I need the fastest performance out there as it is that I need some CUDA cores to merely EXIST at all for certain features to work!
This card is a great because much like the 1550 ti before it, it offers a decent entry-level gpu without costing significantly more than other components in your desktop. It is faster than the 1550ti, so that's nice, and does a decent job pumping out fps in light gaming if that's your thing.
One thing I didn't know beforehand and wish I did: This card does NOT support the Nevnc Turing engine. It only supports the (somewhat inferior) Volta one, which isn't as efficient in hardware accelerated video encoding. Since I bought this card primarily to compliment a home video editing setup, I wanted that feature. The new 1650 SUPER, which is a slightly more expensive card, DOES have the Turing engine, and when that showed up in a Google search I assumed this card had it as well.
Its a shame, I was looking forward to that but I'll have to wait until the next time I upgrade my GPU.

title: Added excellent WiFi to my new Desktop
text:
I recently built a new editing workstation based on an Intel Z390 chipset. My old WiFi PCI card barely supports 5ghz, and I had heard good things about the new CNVi wireless chips combined with a 9th gen Intel CPU.
I have to say, I'm thoroughly pleased by how well this performs. My connection is rock solid to my router, easily maintaining the max speed of my internet service. In fact, I'd have to say it seems to be on par with a wired connection to my router, which I'm thankful to NOT need to deal with (drilling holes and running cables, etc). I like that this came with the cables and external antenna all ready to go! The base of the antenna is magnetic and sticks nicely to my case for a good looking and extremely effective connection.
I also really REALLY like how this keeps my PC relatively uncluttered inside. This build has a glass window, so the lack of additional PCI cards combined with my NVMe hdd in the other M.2 slot of my motherboard makes a very clean looking install.

title: Works great!
text:
I don't have a 4k monitor to test, but I did set this up with my 2k monitor as a second screen in my video editing setup. I was previously using an adapter to HDMI since I didn't have a straight DP to DP cable handy, and generally a single cable with less adapter "breaks" in the chain means a stronger signal. That means I should be able to push higher hz and more pixels over the same connection with a straight cable like this one.
So far so good, connection is strong and it hasn't skipped a beat yet. Good solid quality cable, and a generous length too.

title: Ethernet is a no go on firestick
text:
This is basically a USB host cable that delivers power, and a mini USB hub with Ethernet built in. I wish I could review them separately because the USB host part works perfectly! I tried it on several devices (including my Moto G5 Plus smartphone) and it gives everything a USB port to plug a peripheral into. I wanted this for my Amazon FireStick 4k, which was successfully given a USB port which can be used for things like game controllers and wireless keyboard/mouse combos, etc.
The USB hub + Ethernet works alright- the USB ports, at least, work fine. I'm able to plug in a keyboard and wireless controller adapter dongle, and everything works fine and is recognized by the Firestick. You can even plug in a USB storage stick to play local content. But I REALLY wanted the Ethernet port to get a stronger connection by the TV for streaming. I know there are other USB host / ethernet combos that work with the FireStick, it is capable of working with the right hardware. I thought this would be one of them since it claims to be "for Streaming TV Stick" in the description, however the Ethernet port does NOT work. I'll have to try to source my own and see if I can use it with the USB host this offers. The Ethernet port did show up on my Windows desktop when I tried the hub there, so maybe it just isn't compatible with Android/non desktops? I don't know. If that's the feature you want, this might not work for you.

title: Incredible value on this Manfrotto knockoff
text:
Is it as good as a Manfrotto? No. Is it good enough for the price? TOTALLY.
This is an excellent lightweight alternative to the expensive video tripods out there, with one of the best fluid heads for the money. I've had video fluid heads alone that cost as much as this entire bundle, so the price is worth even just that! I've actually been using a Manfrotto 701 head on a slider and tripod, and for a shoot recently I decided to use this head on the slider so I could easily swap my camera between the two (thanks to the compatible QR plate). The tripod is pretty great too, although something about the weight makes me feel like I can't trust it as much as my carbon fiber Manfrottos. The truth is, once assembled, I found it really quite sturdy- I tried shaking it and it didn't seem to want to. So that might just be my own prejudice based on weight alone. I also really like the carrying bag it comes with, which is something my other high end tripods do not come with. In a nutshell, this is an incredible value for a video tool. If you're on a budget, you can't go wrong with it.

title: Just what I needed for my desk!
text: My deskop's built in SD card reader is slow (based on USB 2.0), and since I work with video for a living, I often need to transfer large files off the cards quickly. This is a great adapter because it connects over USB 3, so my cards actually transfer at their maximum speed (90-100MBs), and also gives me a hub to connect 3x more high speed USB devices, perfect for portable drives and USB sticks. Since the generous cord is long enough to reach around my the back of my desk to the PC, I can leave this on my desk where it is much easier to access than the tower underneath. I haven't used the micro SD card reader yet but that's gravy on top of an already excellent product!

title: I wanted to love it... Does not fit 12" Thinkpad
text:
Fist of all, this is a really well made case! The materials are top notch, the inside is so soft I wish I had a coat made out of it, and it looks pretty great too.
I have a 12" older Thinkpad tablet convertible that I use for sketching on the go thanks to the wacom pen built into the screen, however unlike my other laptops which fit in a protective case, the way the screen flips makes this impossible to get a skin/case for. So, I figured a sleeve such as this is exactly what I needed.
Turns out despite the laptop being only a 12-incher, it doesn't fit into this case at all. The battery and notch in the front and back protrude just enough that it can't slide in. I figured a case made for a 13.5" surface could certainly fit a 12" thinkpad, but sadly not. Meanwhile my Yoga S1 and family member's 13" Macbook fit, however those both already have skin cases and don't need this sleeve to protect it. Color me disappointed- but if you have one of the models it DOES fit, I'm sure you will love it. 4 stars because it has great potential, but minus one star because there are 13.5" cases that WILL fit this laptop. Just not this one.

title: GREAT for the price
text:
I'm not an ear bud fan. Neither are my kids, who often find them hard to keep in their ears at all. Sadly, its hard to find over-the-ear style headphones that aren't professional level expensive or Bluetooth these days. Sometimes you just want a standard set of 'phones for using on the plane or when connecting your set to different devices (don't get me started on pairing my bluetooth headphones with 4 different devices... it always just wants to pair with whatever I used last).
This is a fantastic budget friendly over-the-ear style set. They sound good, they are comfortable especially for younger ears, and they fold up to carry in a bag. The cable is also removable, which is nice. It comes with a cable that offers an inline mic with a TRRS plug on the end for use with a phone, but you can just as well swap that out for a standard 3.5mm end-to-end aux cable, making this truly a versatile pair of headphones for whatever you intend to use it with.
Giving it 4 stars because honestly, they aren't the most amazing sounding headphones and they don't have much noise isolation, but they sound decent enough to listen to music and movies and for the price it's hard to beat!

title: Breathed new life into our old AT&T cordless system!
text:
Our three handset DECT landline system all sort of died within weeks of each other. Which I suppose makes sense considering they are all the same age! We'd had them for a very long time and was about to start shopping around for a replacement set when I spotted these batteries for sale.
They fit perfectly, powered everything on and are happy running our home phones like new. My kids can now gab with their friends after school and leave my cell phone alone again!

title: LOVE this!
text:
If you want to connect two wireless headphones to the same source, this is what you need!
I actually have tried two larger versions of this on our TV so my wife and I could listen with two headphones and not wake the kids. The larger ones require a cable and a place to put it, so it usually goes behind the entertainment system.
This one fits in the palm of my hand! It plugs right into the headphone jack and supports itself like that, all while running self-powered with batteries! That makes it super convenient to use on laptops, while travelling, in hotel rooms, etc. I like it so much better, I actually might replace our home TV one with this because it is so much neater looking and easy to plug in/remove. The bigger one requires too many cables and sometimes would create a ground loop feedback hum if I didn't have it set up correctly. This one hasn't had that happen yet, thanks to the internal battery avoiding grounding issues!
The range might not as good as the larger ones (big one had large antennae which could work rooms away, whereas this one needs to be in the same room it seems), but this very much serves its purpose and I wish I knew it existed before getting the other ones!

title: So close!
text:
This has so much potential, but just barely falls short of what I want in a media center remote. I have a fire stick 4k attached to a TV, and while the stock IR remote it came with is close to everything I need (can do TV's volume and power thanks to pre-programmed IR), it lacks a keyboard and programmable buttons (my stereo system isn't in the Fire TV's list so it can't control it, and I use that for surround sound). I have a USB host adapter that allows me to use media keyboard combos like this one on the stick, so I could have my QWERTY but traditionally then I'd give up the Alexa mic and IR controls of the stock remote since they usually don't have that. Whats amazing about this is that on paper I should still have everything I love- a QWERTY on one side, nav pad and plenty of shortcut buttons on the flip side, programmable IR buttons (YES!), and even a voice assistant mic button!
Seems too good to be true, because it sort of it. The mic button doesn't seem to work on Fire stick or even on my old Chinese Android player box. In Windows it seems to launch Cortana but I don't use that. Maybe it does something on Apple TV like invoke Siri, but I don't have one to test. The button in my case, is useless. Also, the programmable IR buttons? I was able to train the buttons to my TV for power and vol + and -. but not the stereo system. Sometimes it would seem to work and remember one side (either volume up or down) but never both together. I'd clear the buttons to default and start over, and then the TV ones wouldn't work either (commence tearing out hair). After a few cycles attempted to learn my IR codes, I got the TV working again but never the entire stereo system. What stinks is that I can already do that on my stock Firestick remote, and at least there I also get working Alexa voice command via the same remote. This didn't do that properly. Also on the firestick, system android volume settings don't effect anything. So I really wanted to reprogram the vol up and down buttons to the IR codes, but I could only do that on one of the 4 programmable buttons.

The air mouse function is really useful, and having the full keyboard is cool and good to have, but sadly this isn't that much better than the cheaper standard USB or BT keyboards you could already hook up and lose the voice input and IR control. You still need both, and in my case also the remote for the surround sound.
