Already had some 500Watt tungsten bulbs in an Impact light fixture, so figured this with an umbrella holder would be good to soften the light, and it does a decent job. Not as fancy or controlled as a softbox, but for the price this is great place to get basic diffusion.

title: Great portable video lighting kit for interviews and and small spaces
text:
I have a larger hot tungsten kit that I use for big lighting jobs, but I found it tedious to use for talking head interviews and small spaces, not to mention needing outlets wherever I set up.
I decided to try these for a job in a warehouse (shooting video of people working), and the notion of it being battery operated was VERY appealing, since I did not want to run cables for power over hundreds of feet of warehouse. I was so impressed with these little lights that now I take them with me on other jobs too. They are so compact and fit so nicely into the included carrying case.
To be fair, they aren't a replacement for a tungsten kit if you're lighting a large area or want more bounce/fill/etc. LEDs simply aren't as bright (yet?), but these are far more convenient, and the light color rendition is very good. I do wish that they didn't require 2 batteries at a time to work (other LEDs I looked into only needed one at a time, these requires both for the correct voltage), and I also wish the case didn't have a big logo that reads "Great Video Maker" (kind of a cheesy name, isn't it? If it just said GVM that would be better IMO!). But these don't take away from how great the lights actually work, so 5 stars.

title: NOT suitable for Raspberry Pi
text:
I have a couple of Raspberry Pi zeros that use the mini HDMI sized plugs. I needed an adapter, so I searched Amazon for a 2 pack, and these even say compatible with Raspberry Pi in the title / description.
I can assure you THEY ARE NOT COMPATIBLE WITH THE RASPBERRY PI. As far as I know, the Pi Zero is the only board that uses this sort of HDMI plug (the others use full sized HDMI), and the angle of this adapter makes it IMPOSSIBLE to connect the DC power input at the same time. You can clearly see in the attached image, the HDMI cable blocks access to the input. If it was angled the other direction, it would work fine but in its current design, it DOES NOT work with any Pi board that I'm aware of.
It does work as an adapter for different hardware - my laptop for example has mini HDMI and my cameras use micro. So maybe I'll keep them around for that, but I'm only giving it 2 stars because I bought it based on the claim it would work for a specific product mentioned in the description, and it most certainly does not.

title: Great as an audio player AND headphones!
text:
I previously owned a black pair of these and liked it enough to get a second pair (in red) for my son. The important feature? TF card reader for self-contained music. My son isn't allowed to have a cell phone in school yet, and finding a good music player that isn't more-or-less a phone is hard these days- but THESE HEADPHONES ARE ALSO AN MP3 PLAYER! I took an old Micro SD card from a discarded phone (about 4GB in size) and filled it up with music files. The headphones have little controls for start/stop/ff/rr, and they can be used like that without being tethered, wirelessly or otherwise, to anything else.
Then, in school, he can use it with the supplied aux cable for use in the classroom during computer time, and then at home with our tablets wirelessly over bluetooth. Its amazing how many different roles it plays, and he couldn't be happier with it. The only caveat is that unlike some of my other headphones in this style, this feels a bit weak in build quality, with very shiny plastic that probably will break in my son's backpack eventually. So far so good so I'm still giving it 4 stars, but if the build quality gave me a tad more confidence, I'd give it a 5. For the price I still recommend it, the sound quality is great and it does isolate background noise quite well.

title: Excellent kit!
text: The CRI rating seems to be pretty spot on, the color rendition is awesome. It is actually quite bright (thanks to the 672 LEDs), and I find the diffusion panel included pretty interesting. I haven't tried using it with the included barndoors yet, but it seems to decently soften the light in a pleasing way. The diffuser does dim the light considerably, but I was still able to light a subject with a window in the room and match the ambient lighting color (love the variable color). I also like that it comes with a padded case to store everything in. I actually initially had a problem with the order, I specifically paid for the one that came with batteries and they shipped me one that was missing the batteries. But after reaching out to them and Amazon customer service, I was offered a refund of the price difference AND a shipment of batteries w/ chargers was sent out ASAP. They really came through in the customer service department and I'm very happy with the product. Will definitely buy more lights from them!

title: Incredible value- so much faster!
text:
It is incredible to me how much of a difference an SSD makes. I bought a new computer for my office with beefy specs (latest generation i7 chip, high end GPU, etc) and had already maxed out my budget before getting to hard drives, so I had to settle for a mechanical HDD. It was a decent speed 7200rpm one, but opening applications and just navigating the computer felt so much slower than my old computer with an SSD, despite that old computer being nearly a decade older. Thankfully, the prices for aftermarket SSDs like this one have dropped significantly. I don't know how Sandisk can offer these at the price they do, but it is fantastic for the price. I've actually bought about 3 of these to upgrade various old computers, even my ancient first generation i5 laptop feels like it is flying with this.
If you don't have an SSD yet, this is the single most cost effective way to make your computer feel faster.

title: Bought as a gift for my mom
text:
I actually own a set of Ailihen headphones for my laptop, and my daughter uses one for her phone, so we were already familiar with the brand. My mom saw ours and mentioned how she liked over-the-ear style more than earbuds, so I picked this up in black and gold for her.
She loves it, and it looks great! So, another satisfied Ailihen customer.

title: Great for outdoor movie night
text: I'm not a fan of the black border for indoor screen use, but it sure beats using a large white bedsheet outside when we do backyard movie night with the neighbors! That's what I bought it for, and its perfect for it! Just need to be careful when folding up not to accidentally get it dirty on the ground when mounting/taking it down.

title: I very much like that the default plug on this is a single ...
text: I very much like that the default plug on this is a single TRRS with mic and stereo. I had another headset before this with separate speaker and mic plugs, along with a USB port to power it (light up earphones and mute button controls). When I wanted to use it on my laptop or mobile device which offers a single TRRS plug, it came with an adapter to use... however, it was WAY too much wire and always looked messy. I like how clean this is, I can even use it as a headphone for phone calls in noisy environments because the ear sets are decent about isolating noise from outside. Also since the speakers are larger than your average earbud, the bass response is very respectable. They aren't audiophile quality sound, but I wasn't expecting that from these. These are for gaming, but I think I'll also find myself using them to watch a movie and make phone calls with as well. Good deal!

title: The low profile plug is amazing and the USB ports let us plug in an ...
text: Needed to plug in lights and speaker system behind bookshelf in our home. The low profile plug is amazing and the USB ports let us plug in an Amazon Echo on a shelf as well. All wires are hidden behind the shelf so everything looks really clean and nice now. Perfect!

title: A good cost effective over-the-head option
text: These seem to be a pretty great option for over-the-head style headphones that fold for storage and are still affordable. My son's back to school list required a pair of headphones for some computer lab work, and he hates the earbud style ones. This is comfortable for both kids and adults, has a decent amount of noise isolation, and even has the inline mic for TRRS plugs like a phone if used in that type of setup. Extra points because they actually look more expensive than they are. My son loves them!

title: A decent deal for what it is, however requires a bit of hack-fu to figure out!
text:
As other reviews have mentioned, this kit lacks instructions which makes it challenging. However, part of the fun in the RPi community is the DIY spirit to tinker and figure things out.
I'm still working on getting all the kinks worked out, but it is actually kind of fun figuring it out with my kids helping. A couple of things to note:
You'll need drivers found elsewhere- the seller has linked to a URL as an answer to a question. It would have been nice if that address could be included in a paper sheet or even in the product description, but the information is at least out there for you to find.
For assembly of the case, the pictures the seller has provided illustrates how it snaps together, however the included fan can't be used at the same time as the screen (physically only one or the other will fit together. Clearly the screen and case are two different items that the seller is bundling together for a good deal, they are not components that are made for each other as a single kit. Therefore you'll need to get creative in getting it all to fit together and working properly.

A fun summer project for me with my kids, good enough that I think it deserves 4 stars for the price. But be aware, this isn't necessarily an easy kit for beginners. For that, you should spend more on something else.

title: An interesting experience
text:
I have heard about "ergonomic" style computer mice before, so I decided to give this one a try. As someone in the visual graphic industry I've had wrist pain from prolonged computer use, especially on deadline projects. The idea is simply that rather than twist your forarm to hold onto a mouse palm-down, you let your arm grasp it a more natural sideways palm angle. The experience is weird at first- it doesn't feel right, but slowly you start to get comfortable with it. Today I had both mice plugging in (my old one and new one), and I found myself preferring this one for some reason.
I wasn't comfortable yet in graphic applications using it, but time will tell if I can get used to that or not. I'll update this review after giving it a few weeks to see if I managed to get used to it completely or not.

Some caveats- its quite a bit taller than a standard mouse, so it actually didn't fit on my sliding keyboard drawer. I had to use it on the desk's top instead. If you don't use a pull out drawer, this is a non ssue. Buttons at first would sometimes "stick", and accidentally double click something I meant to click once. Some hard clicking on the buttons to loosen them up seems to have worked. Also there is an LED that lights up and alternates color in a kind of cool way, but there's no way to turn it off. I'll update this review as I get to know my hardware better.

title: Impressed with Roku, wasn't expecting to be.
text:
Bought this to replace an old laptop being used as a netflix player on a family member's TV. It was on sale for a few dollars less than an Amazon Fire Stick, so I figured it was worth a shot.
Pleasantly surprised by how great it is- the way you can search multiple sources for content, use your phone as a remote or as an audio channel (so you can plug headphones into your phone and mute the TV- how cool!), and even its selection of free content, was more than I expected. I didn't buy it for myself, but now that I've helped set it up, I've got half a mind to replace my android-based TV box with one of these!

title: They are as cute as they look in the pictures, and the noise isolation is impressive.
text: My daughter loves this. Very cute, stylish looking headphones, and surprisingly comfortable to wear. My kids especially don't like earbuds, so the over-the-ear style like these are a welcome alternative. I was actually impressed at how much noise isolation they provide... it really blocks out the outside sound, you end up yelling when trying to talk without realizing, and that's not even when there is any music playing! Sound quality is OK- not as amazing as my brand name speakers, but good enough for what it is. A little echo-ey, but a worthwhile compromise for the over-the-head style and this level of noise isolation.

title: Breathed new life into an X201!
text:
UPDATE: After only a few months of use, the battery has severely degraded to about half of its original capacity. The worst part is, rather than deplete in a linear fashion, the battery seems to flatline at around 30%, sending my laptop into a sudden power off without warning.
Thankfully I haven't lost any data or anything due to this yet, but it is very frustrating and could be dangerous to my computer's hard drive (I'm using an SSD, but a sudden power loss during a write operation could corrupt the storage).
I'm going to reach out and see if there's anything we can do about this, and I will update my review accordingly.
This thing breathed new life into an old Lenovo X201 tablet someone gave me. I'm not sure if it was necessary or not, but I used the Lenovo tool to calibrate the new battery (it runs it down to nothing and then trickles back up to 100%), and now it runs like a champ.
Easily gets close to 5 hours of running time, and this laptop is a first generation i7 (not known for being energy efficient). I've only owned it about 10 days so far, so I can't speak for longevity down the road, but I'm hoping it will keep up, as my family is really enjoying using the tablet pen for drawing untethered.

title: The Gold Standard in memory!
text: My wife needed more storage for pictures on her phone. Of course, I went with a Sandisk. I work in photography for a living and have grown to trust this brand for all forms of storage. These guys are the gold standard- just make sure you get the ones sold by Amazon directly or at least a reputable seller FBA. I've found cheaper sellers that sold fakes. This one I can vouch is the real deal.

title: It had a deal pixel out of the box. ...
text: It had a deal pixel out of the box. I would have let that go, but there is also a sticker tab to remove the plastic shield that protects it in transit, and just trying to peel that off seems to have created enough pressure to break more pixels until a majority of the screen was damaged. Sent it back and tried a different product.

title: it worked great! It was actually a bit clearer than the ...
text:
I bought this to add a viewing screen for my passenger to watch what the kids are watching in the rear of our minivan. Upon initial testing, it worked great! It was actually a bit clearer than the RES screen in our 2010 Odyssey, despite being smaller. I was experimenting with wiring it up directly to difference sources of power when it suddenly died. It stopped turning on, and after poking around trying to get it to come back on, I smelled burning and saw smoke come out the back.
I contacted the seller and asked for help / suggestions. They were nice enough to refund my money, even though I admitted it might have been something I did to it since it WAS working out of the box initially. They told me to keep it at 12v input to avoid things like that from happening. So, I took away a couple of stars for it internally burning itself out when I was experimenting, but put back one for the amazing above and beyond seller response. I'm probably going to buy another one and try again... this time being more careful. :)

title: but it works fine. First one we got had some sort of ...
text: May not be as bright as the Boogie Board or other more expensive brand, but it works fine. First one we got had some sort of burn in problem (image from previous sketch would show up when surrounding area was given pressure), but seller replaced for free, and replacement hasn't had the issue. 5 stars for seller, 4 stars for product!

title: Gold Standard!
text: This thing is like the gold standard in simple flash modifiers. Came highly recommended by peers, and I'm so glad I tried it. Better than any softbox or other modifier I've ever used. In fact when discussing other modifiers with colleagues, most of the time the Rogue Flashbender is the standard by which all others are judged. A must have.

title: Works great on Odyssey, with caveats...
text:
I love that this gives an almost factory level integration with the car- no matter what mode the stereo is in (even off!), when a call comes in or is initiated, it will switch over and play over the speakers automatically. When installed using the XM port, it will even use the XM's ability to send text to the display, telling you that you are now in Bluetooth mode, which phone is connected, caller ID and track information, etc. It feels as if the car came this way from the factory!
Except for two annoying caveats:
1) THERE IS NO WAY TO INITIATE A CALL WITHOUT YOUR PHONE. Sure, you can use the stereo controls to answer, hang up, and change tracks if listening to music, but there's no button to wake up the Google Assistant/Siri/etc and speak commands like on a factory installed Bluetooth unit. This is the most annoying for me because I really want to be able to que up a song or place a call without taking my phone out of my pocket. I tried to find a way around this by using the always listening "Ok Google" function of my phone, but it eats up my battery to have it always listening for the command. There's also the possibility of using an additional device, like the iSimple ISBC01 Blueclik, which acts like a remote control that connects to the phone using the BT keyboard profile, so you can connect to it and the BT45-HON3 at the same time without conflict. The ISBC01 offers a mic button which SHOULD in theory wake up your phone and launch the voice assistant (it simulates a long-press home button), but while I've heard people say it works for Siri on an iPhone, all it did was wake up the screen on my Android phone. It didn't actually activate the voice command assistant. I found I could install a button remapper app and make it work, but it only seems to work when the device is already on. Additionally, the iSimple device goes to sleep after 10 min of inactivity. So, when first getting into the car, I have to press the mic button on the iSimple to wake it out of sleep and connect to the phone, press it again to wake up the phone, then a third time to actually open Google Assistant. This is obviously not ideal and makes me feel like I could have taken my phone out of my pocket and done all this manually by then. It really makes me wish there was a way to to initiate voice commands from the BT45-HON3 directly, either via a stereo button or with a hardwire remote. Their newer BT45-AUX device actually ships with a battery powered remote, but I'm told it is not compatible with the HON3 version (it is a newer product and didn't exist when the HON3 was made). This makes me hopeful for a future version of this unit, but saddens me that it does not currently offer the features I'm looking for.
2) If using in XM mode, you have to use the tuner up/down function to change tracks and answer calls. The steering wheel controls in my 2010 Odyssey don't have channel up down, but rather radio preset up down (because the understanding is that in normal XM operation, you don't want to go up and down incrementally through 100+ channels, but rather to the next preset at a time). Jumping to the next preset isn't a function the BT45 recognizes, so you need to use the buttons on the stereo to incrementally go up/down a station to interact with the Bluetooth control. On my Odyssey, this is a tuner knob. It seems kind of silly to need to twist the knob right to answer the call or left to reject it when there are perfectly good controls available to my thumb on the steering wheel, but this is a limitation of how the XM buttons are laid out on my car. If using CDC mode instead of XM (which can be set using the dip switches), the up/down on the steering wheel buttons would work since in CD mode they would advance next track / prev track (which is what the BT45 unit is looking for). However, in CDC mode, you lose out on the text display. I like the text display for many reasons- caller ID is nice, as is the artist/title of songs when streaming with Spotify, but most importantly, since I share the car with my wife, it is nice when it displays which phone is currently connected. In our other car, we have bluetooth with no display. When we drive together, sometimes we don't know whos phone is connected and sometimes have an awkward moment pulling away from the driveway when we realize the OTHER person's phone is connected. Having a text display makes it easier to know what is really going on, so I decided I'll just compromise the steering wheel controls and use the tuner knob in return for the text. Its just unfortunate that I have to choose between the two.

Otherwise, the unit is danged near perfect. Connects quickly and sounds really good.

A couple of notes regarding installation:
The instructions want you to install it in the rear where the XM radio is. On a car as long as the Odyssey, I don't want to do that. Its too far from the driver so the BT transmission will have more interference, not to mention how annoying it would be to wire up the mic so far.
I chose to unplug the XM radio from behind the head unit because A) I only have a 3 month trial and don't intend to pay for it, and B) Whatever stations there are, I have access to much much more and arguably better content with my phone and streaming internet station for free (unlimited data plan). Once I have Bluetooth music streaming, I additionally have the benefit of notifications and GPS commands coming in over the radio, so for all intents and purposes, XM is useless in this age of affordable mobile data. And hey, if you really like XM that much, you can always use the XM app with your subscription and do it over Bluetooth. Then you still get notification sounds and GPS commands over the music.
Either way, I recommend unplugging XM and using the included harness to plug it in behind the stereo. Then you can easily fish mic wire behind your dashboard trim, up the A-piller, and over the rear view mirror, where they recommend putting it. I was able to use the included clip to secure it to the headliner, and tuck the wire behind the trimming using a plastic pry tool. Easy peasy and looks nice.

One more thing I did is I decided to plug in a USB cable to the charging port on the unit and drilled a hole in the storage cubby under the climate controls to fish it into. Now, I can open the cubby door and plug in my phone to charge if needed, and not have to see a single wire hanging anywhere in the car. That's nice. :)

title: This was great, while I had it
text: This was great, while I had it. It was useful for breaking out an outlet behind furniture that prevented a plug to fit, but I used it literally once and then promptly lost it while reorganizing. Its a shame, I might have to just buy another one. Very useful!

title: No instructions, No power cord, No HDMI output. Frustrated buyer.
text:
I was trying to setup a studio for a multi-cam live Q&A web-broadcast, and this unit came highly recommended. Turns out this might not be the best choice, and the whole experience sort of leaves a bad taste in my mouth.
First the good:
The functionality of this device really impressed me! All I wanted was a live HDMI switch that would let me keep the audio separate (so it would be live regardless of camera active) and wouldn't blank the display when swapping inputs (which consumer hdmi switches do, as the connection re-negotiates). This unit goes far beyond that, using industry standard production controls for cuts and cross fades, title / graphic overlays, and even some basic Chroma Keying for doing live green screen (that was a surprise!). The little LCD is pretty neat too.
And now, THE BAD:
THERE IS NO HDMI OUTPUT. It only supports SDI, which no one mentioned to me when I said I wanted to toggle between HDMI sources. There is an HDMI preview which shows you multi-view (all the cameras in a grid), but no regular HDMI output. Only SDI, which is ridiculous to me. You have the HDMI port there, at least give us the option to choose whether it is multi-view or program out! Black Magic claims they didn't offer the HDMI out because the connection isn't reliable, so they want to push SDI as the output. But that isn't acceptable, the hardware is there, give us a choice! The result of this stream is going to an internet broadcaster which supports an HDMI input only! Now I'd need to purchase yet another accessory to convert the final product back into an HDMI signal so it can get where it needs to go.
Oh, and speaking of additional accessories that need to be purchased, THE BOX LACKS A POWER CORD. You have to source your own. That seems silly, its such an inexpensive thing that you expect to be there. Thankfully I have a cord from an old lighting accessory that I don't use anymore, but it seemed very odd that it was missing to me. Then, it did not come with a setup guide or instructions, only an SD card. That's fine, going green and all that, but I put it in my laptop and it came up blank. So now I have to find the software and manual myself. And at first, I found what I thought was the correct manual via Google only to realize it was for a different version of their ATEM products.
I know this is an inexpensive product for what it is, but let's be serious for a moment- it still costs nearly $1,000. For that amount of money, how much could it really cost to throw in a power cable and printed manual? $5? 10? Compared to the price of the unit, that's close to nothing. I also know that the buttons on front are because it is designed to be rack-mountable, but when you're setting this up on the fly and try to put on a tabletop, the controls are just awkward. It would have been a lot nicer ergonomically to have some controls on the top instead of the front side. But now that's just nitpicking. At the end of the day, I feel like this device is frustratingly close to what I was looking for, but the experience has been pretty crummy so far.

title: Short cables keep signal loss down when making multiple connections.
text: I bought an HDMI switch and adapter to send my home entertainment content to either a flat panel screen or our projector. But this meant that instead of having a single HDMI cable from my player to my TV, I now had one going into the switch, another going from the switch to the TV, and another going from the switch to a CAT5 adapter to run the signal to a projector on the other side of the room. Normal sized hdmi cables were cluttering up my AV shelf, which is where these come in. Perfect, short run multi-pack was exactly what I needed. Cables don't need to be tied up to make them shorter, don't get twisted or tangled with other equipment and the short run ensures less signal loss over the course of all the connections. Very happy with this!

title: Perfect for choosing your output device!
text: These are great because  you can go in either direction with them, unlike other multi-HDMI adapters which just support one direction, usually one input on a TV accepting multiple devices. With this, however, I can split an outgoing signal to choose between my Projector or smaller TV monitor. I originally had a different adapter which was a repeater- that is, it supported having two signals simultanously, so both projector and TV could be active - but I don't need that, and it was another box with another AC/DC wall wart plug that was clearly consuming some sort of power since it was warm to the touch. I'll save that for times I need to split a signal between two screens (event presentation, etc). For leaving on my home entertainment system, this is great- simple, effective, efficient. No additional power drawn, doesn't heat up (passive), just a solid solution to avoid physically unplugging and plugging an HDMI jack. Highly recommended!

title: Worked well for a job in which I had a ...
text: Worked well for a job in which I had a green subject (so the green chroma key background I usually use wouldn't work). Was a little wrinkly and had to be ironed out which seems par for the course every time I hang it. Would have been nicer if it were a thicker material that was a bit more immune to folds that create difficulty in pulling a key, but for the price this did the trick!

title: Great cheap remote trigger.
text:
I bought this to remotely trigger 3 very inexpensive speedlites I picked up (also Neewer brand). I figured one light can be fired via light trigger in slave mode, and I'd like at least 2 receivers. Works well as long as the batteries are good!
The first ones I tried were used from another gadget in my house, and although the little red LED would light up to tell me that it received the signal from the transmitter, the flash didn't fire. Fresh batteries fixed it, however. I guess it needed more voltage to fire the speedlight than my semi-used batteries had. So lesson here is: Keep fresh batteries in it, and you'll be great!

Used it on my Sony A7s and A7Rii.

title: Cheap, but great light!
text:
I have strobes in my office that I use for product photos and headshots, but wanted something I could walk around with and/or set up at home for personal projects.
I didn't want to spend a lot of money since I already have the expensive strobes, so I gave these a try. All I can say is WOW. I'm impressed at what you get for the money! The controls are kind of basic, and of course, its all manual, so no TTL or anything like that. But that's OK, I'm used to shooting manual with my strobes at work so I expected it. For the price, I picked up 3 of them and got some remote triggers elsewhere on Amazon to go with it. I love that these come with little feet as well so for under a hundred dollars, I had a 3 light setup that I could throw in a small camera bag. I just wish I had done this sooner!

title: Maxed out my Gateway PC!
text: I installed these in my Gateway i7 computer from a few years ago to max out the internal memory. Since the chips it came with are 1333Mhz, I didn't want to purchase 1600Mhz RAM (even though my motherboard supposedly supports it), in order to avoid any possible problems. I picked these because they are the same speed, voltage, etc, as the ones I currently have. Its been working very well so far, running memory intensive applications (media editing) are more responsive and a pleasure to use now. Highly recommended if you have a Gateway or similar box.

title: Great price for blower with addons!
text:
I bought this kit initially for the blower. As a mirrorless camera user, having a blower is a MUST. I picked this item because others were charging the same amount for the blower alone, and with this kit I also get a lens pen, cleaning cloths and whatever else you might need to keep your gear in top shape.
The quality of some components in the kit aren't necessarily the highest, but as freebies that come with a blower, they are pretty great and I'm glad I have them. Highly recommended if you own any sort of interchangeable lens camera system that frequently has lenses swapped. An absolute MUST if said camera is mirrorless, as they are practically dust magnets when the sensor is charged.

title: Instant on-the-spot prints... that are also STICKERS!
text:
I grew up loving my Polaroid instant prints. This modern version not only gives you the instant gratification of a print (that we all know and love), but it also peels off and actually doubles as a STICKER! How cool is that! Teenage-me would have loved having one of these instead of taping stuff to the wall.
To be fair, the picture quality isn't stellar... in fact, your cell phone might already take better pictures. But the instant gratification of a print is what you are buying here, and that is super cool. That and the fact that the camera itself is also super cool and retro- even the magnetic lens cap, as easy as it is to forget it is on, is very satisfying to "click" back into place. And unlike the Fujifilm instant print cameras, this will also save your pics to a microSD card for later reprints and/or safekeeping in this digital world.

If instant gratification is your thing or you just have a nostalgia for old Polaroid concepts, this camera is for you!

NOTE: Does not come with film/paper. You'll need that, and/or a Micro SD card. The camera can work with either or both, but not with none.

title: Incredible bang for buck and AMAZING parental controls!
text:
I bought this during a mother's day promotion for ten dollars less than normal. We had our iPad mini stolen almost a year ago, and figured it would be nice to have a small tablet around again.
I've seen the cheap tablets and wasn't expecting much for the price. They're usually laggy and have poor displays and cameras. Man, was I surprised to see how solid of a product this is! Don't get me wrong, it comes in basically minimalist packaging and doesn't look like much at first. But the UI is surprisingly smooth, screen has great viewing angles for both reading and landscape movie watching (more than I can say about other cheap tablets), and the Amazon software is pretty nifty.
Ok, the camera on this thing isn't very good, I must admit that- but I have a cell phone for pocket shooting and a DSLR for real shooting, so what do I really need a camera on a tablet for? Skype? Its good enough for video calls.

What really impressed me is the software for creating kid profiles. I love it that I can set up usernames for my kids that they can log into and are only allowed to access the things that I decide are appropriate for them- including movies and books from the marketplace! Also I can set up time restrictions to give them only specific amounts of time for play before locking them out. Another cool feature I haven't tried yet is one that seems to not let them play any games until they have spent a designated amount of time reading. I love that!

All in all, I was impressed enough with the parental controls and the price that I decided to buy 2 more to give my kids!

title: but it still works just fine.
text: Breathed new life into my Daughter's old Y430 laptop. Battery and charger were dead, but at least with this she can leave it on her desk plugged in. Note, this does not appear to be an OEM adapter, but it still works just fine.

title: Excellent value for the money!
text:
I bought this to use in an Atomos Ninja 2 video recorder for my camera after having a discussion with Atomos support to ensure compatibility. They actually told me this model should appear on their official "supported" list.
I already have an inexpensive larger HDD that I use for longer jobs (3+ hour concerts on a stationary camera, etc), but I wanted an SSD for jobs that I might require more shock-proofing if going off-tripod with the recorder. This is a perfect fit for that- performance is not the fastest on the market (Sandisk has other lines such as the extreme for that), but it is very respectable for an SSD in today's standards, and faster than my first-generation Intel SSD currently in my workstation. And if you're comparing to a mechanical HDD, we're not even in the same ballpark either way. These are FAST and solid. And I trust Sandisk a lot more than other brands out there.
In fact, I'm impressed enough with the quality-to-cost ratio that I might pick up another one to replace my workstation's older and smaller model. Great buy!

title: Cheaper than bare drive, and can open and reuse the enclosure!
text:
I bought this drive to replace an older 2GB internal backup that was nearly full. It is only a 5900rpm drive internally, but that's actually OK with me for my intended usage. I actually cracked the case open using a credit card and extracted the drive to put inside my tower (currently have 3 drives in there, and was replacing one).
You may be wondering why I chose this over an internal drive if that's all I wanted. Well, there are 2 reasons:
1) This is actually less expensive than a bare drive for some reason
2) You get a free external enclosure thrown in!

After removing the drive and cloning my old one to this one with Acronis software, I took the old drive and put it back inside of this enclosure. Great, now not only did I expand my internal 2GB to 4, but I now have a nifty 2GB external for backups and moving data physically. All for less money than an internal drive would have cost. Win win!

NOTE: This will almost definitely void the warranty, if that sort of thing is a concern to you.

title: I like that the cable is straight instead right-angled like some ...
text: I bought this for my Atomos Ninja to connect to a Sony A7S camera. Before this I had to use a miro-HDMI adapter and a normal HDMI cable. I like that the cable is straight instead right-angled like some other micro-to-standard HDMI cables, because it fits in my camera cage or a port protector and won't block other ports in the process. If you want to connect a micro device like a camera or tablet/phone to an external device or monitor, this is a great option. Very happy with the performance so far!

title: Great for adding more connection points to a QR plate, and also for attaching accessories to a cage!
text:
I have a camera cage that I used to mount directly to my Manfrotto QR plate, but would require tightening up frequently on a job (cage would start to have some play after an hour of use). I realized the cage has two mounting holes (originally designed for attachment to a rail system), so I put a second 1/4" screw in my QR plate, and now I have two points of security which not only prevents needing to tighten the screw, but the slight wobble is nearly non-existent now. I realized afterwards that these screws are not only useful for mounting UNDER the cage, but actually super useful for mounting TO the cage as well!
The cage is riddled with 1/4" holes, and in order to tighten an accessory like a microphone mount, the threading on the screw and cage and accessory need to be rotated usually. In other words, if the accessory is mounted in the wrong direction, turning it will also turn the screw, and tightening up the screw might once again move the accessory. These have clearance underneath the threaded part of the screw, so they can actually spin freely once inserted into the cage. That means I can hold an accessory in place while tightening the screw, and it will lock in tight the way I want it to face. Very versatile and useful part of any kit!

title: Fits Sony A7s battery door, and most any camera I've tried from Canon and Panasonic! Lots of mounting options!
text:
I got sick and tired of buying unique cages for each camera I use. This cage is great because it is the most universal design I've seen while still being solid and relatively compact, and most importantly: THE BATTERY DOOR CUTOUT FITS VIRTUALLY ANY CAMERA I'VE TRIED WITH IT! This was the biggest reason I wanted it. I happen to own many different types of cameras (Canon, Panasonic, Sony, etc) and all of them occasionally get used on jobs that require attached recorders, microphones, power supplies, etc. But until I found this, I needed specific cages that allowed access to the battery on each one, otherwise I'd have to remove the camera during a shoot to replace a dead battery, which is just unnecessarily complicated. I feel like this cage is a great addition to whatever I'm using now, and likely whatever I end up using in the near future.

As a few people pointed out, the rail system on the bottom has a knob that somewhat obstructs part of the battery door opening on some cameras (I noticed this on my A7s, other types of cameras may still get enough clearance). Someone on youtube showed that they were able to remove the knob to keep it accessible, but personally I just wanted the cage part. The cage itself has the same mounting holes as the bottom of the rail adapter, so you can just leave the rails off and attach a tripod QR plate directly to the bottom of the cage, which is what I usually do. I did one time try using the entire package decked out, with the rails, a matte box and follow focus attached... I got around the battery door problem by using a dummy battery with a DC wire that attached to an external power supply (I built my own adapter, I won't go into the details now but I'm pretty proud of it!). So I was able to swap batteries via an adapter mounted on the cage instead of under the camera. But this was a much more complicated setup than I usually work with. For normally daily use, I use the cage without the handle or rails, and with the camera attached it actually fits where my camera usually goes in my gearbag. I have the handle and rails handy if I ever need them, but the price is great for the cage alone!

title: Works on *ALL* E-mounts, not sure why they say only A7II, S and R2.
text:
I bought this initially for my A7S after seeing that they make a different version for the A7 and NEX cameras. The truth is, I also own other E-mount cameras like the A5100, and this mounts perfectly fine on either one so I don't know why they make the distinction! After all, all E-mount lenses can be mounted an all E-mount cameras, so why would this adapter be any different?
Works great, and I'm loving my Nikkor 35-70/2.8 on my A7S. Obviously as this is a mechanical adapter with no electronic contacts, you'll need to handle everything manually (aperture, focus). This also lacks an aperture wheel, so you'll probably want a lens that allows you to set that manually as well. All in all, works great on my old Nikkors and use it all the time on both my A7S and A5100!

title: Five Stars

title: Helped keep my Projector from overheating!
text:
This cooling pad is extremely silent, which is exactly why I wanted it. I bought one of these initially because I have a DLP projector that overheats on long presentations, and I wanted to help keep it cool. Obviously a model with loud fans and vibrations would be less than ideal, but this works well.
Only issue I have is that the USB power connection is short (so I need to bring an extension cord to reach a USB AC power adapter), but since it is designed for laptop use, that is expected.

title: But I'm glad I didn't see it
text: Solid adapter for my A7S. I actually did not notice that the listing stated "not for A7ii or A7s", its entirely possible that was added later as I bought this 6 months prior to this writing.  But I'm glad I didn't see it, because this is a solid, tight fit. There is absolutely no wiggle between the lens and body, and that's how it should be. I see Fotasy makes some "A7ii and A7s" versions of their adapters that are supposed to fit the grooves of the newer mounts better I guess... But I honestly don't understand why they make this distinction. This one fits wonderfully, if it were looser than this I'd probably call it cheap junk. No other inexpensive adapter makes this kind of distinction, so I'm not sure why Fotasy does.

title: Projector worked great for 1 month, unreliable now
text:
My previous model was an older model Viewsonic (don't recall the exact model, but it was an 800x600 one), and I had a very positive experience with it. I use this both for home entertainment and the occasional work-related presentation, so when my old one broke (fell off a table), I decided to go with another Viewsonic.

But I've got to admit, something seems to have went wrong with this model. I love using HDMI to my laptop to project vs VGA, however the first day I did this, when my laptop went to "sleep", the projector started going crazy. Waking up the laptop put it into some sort of loop, it would try to power on, the laptop would report there is no external monitor, the projector would shut off, the laptop would detect something is there just as it was powering down, projector would try to power up again, repeat. I unplugged the HDMI, the laptop went back to normal, but the projector would continue doing this until I pulled the power.

After that, I just made sure not to let the HDMI sleep when using the projector, and its been working OK. Wrote this off as a silly quirk, the picture quality is better than my old one so I'd just live with it. Until the day I was using it for a presentation at a fundraising dinner full of guests. The thing shut off every 10-15 minutes, apparently overheating. The little red light would come on and refuse to let me power it back on for a couple of minutes at a time. I had used my old Viewsonic in exactly the same situation and had NEVER had a problem like this before! After leaving it unplugged for a while, I was able to get it to come on long enough to make it through the presentation, but a couple of days later it did the same thing at another location, and I was forced to rent a backup projector.

Mind you, I'm in my third month of using the projector, I've clocked maybe 10-15 hours total on it. I brought it home, hooked it up to my entertainment center, and I was unable to recreate the problem. Worked just fine a couple of days ago. I just tried it again now, and it won't power up- keeps spinning the fan, then letting out a beep, stopping, and trying again. Like its stuck in that loop again, but there is nothing even attached to it yet! No lamp lighting up, no idea what's going on. If I leave it unplugged, it will probably start working again soon, but this has been totally unreliable for me! I'm hoping I got a lemon and perhaps Viewsonic will do something for me (Its too late to return to Amazon). I will update this review if so. Otherwise, I'm extremely disappointed in this model!

title: Great for expanding my car's audio, one caveat...
text:
This works great in my 2005 Mazda 3, stereo recognizes it and works as expected. With one exception; you can't switch between media and AUX without removing the media.

I wanted to mount this somewhere I wouldn't need to see it often (behind stereo, in glove box, etc) and fish the aux wire somewhere I could plug it in and use it. But if there is storage media attached, the Aux does not work! The aux only becomes active if no media is present, which means I have to dig in and remove it to switch modes. I was really hoping there would be a way to do this from the stereo!

I even tried making a blank 1-hour long MP3 to see if I could play the aux over it, but no luck- the AUX is actually disactivated, no matter what I do, as long as the storage media is present.

On the plus side, it seems to remember where I was up to when I put it back in. But I wish there was a way to do that remotely so I could hide this somewhere convenient. Its not necessarily a deal breaker, but I really wish I had known that before buying it- I would have shopped around more first!

text:
[[VIDEOID:c6eed282949ae4a0bf6692a543d107c8]] This FunFlix 1080 HD WiFi Projecter is very nice and the picture (once you get it up and running) is clear!

It did take some time to get it up and running as we tried to use a flash drive (which it says it accepts a flash drive into the USB port), however it didn’t identify it. We had to then shut it down and restart it and try again…. It still didn’t work. We then tried a USB adapter with a SD card, and no luck - Still not identifiable… Then finally we tried a USB adapter with a MICRO SD card and it worked! When I checked on my computer all of the data showed on the flash drive as well as the SD card, but for some reason the projector wouldn’t identify them. The instructions don’t say anything about a MICRO SD card, however I wanted to point this out as this is the only thing that worked for me.

The mirroring technique through your phone does work, however the further away your phone is from the projector, the quality fades and it starts to pixelate. Also, it will drain your phone quickly.

I plan to use this for Halloween and I am so excited! Only took off 1 star as it took some time to get this up and going. If the instructions were better, it would totally get 5 stars.

Second, the band is very comfortable. It is comfortable to even wear while sleeping. Speaking of sleeping, this watch monitors your sleeping habits: When you fall into a deep sleep (REM), light sleep, or if you have difficulties breathing while sleeping. It monitors your activities, steps, heart rate, and stress levels. It can even tell if you are in a relaxed mood or not. Impressive!

The app is so easy to use and you can control all of the features of the watch directly through the app. The watch even has an alarm clock if you want to use this instead of a traditional alarm clock or a phone. It will vibrate when it is time to wake up!

So far, this watch has been my wife’s best friend. Far less expensive than a Fit Bit and well worth the price. It’s fantastic!

title: Nice sport watch, but not sure about blood pressure accuracy.

The exercise monitor tracks running, cycling, jump roping, table tennis, badminton, tennis and swimming.  The watch is comfortable to wear and looks nice, it has five different watch faces you can choose as your display. I chose this watch because of the blood pressure (bp) monitor, I have high blood pressure and I take medication to keep it normal.  I own two electronic high blood pressure test cuffs and I tested my blood pressure with both of them and the watch and the two cuffs were +/- a point or two apart, but the watch was reading a lot higher than the other monitors.  Throughout the day I repeated the test and the watch was constantly reading that my blood pressure was high, even after I had taken my medication and I know the readings should have changed.  I will have to get with my doctor/nurse and have them do a manual test and see if the watch is showing the same results.  If the watch bp monitor is not accurate, I have not been able to find any way to recalibrate the watch to input the correct bp reading.  That is the only problem I have with this watch.  I like all the features the watch has along with the phone app too.  It doesn't take long to learn all the functions of the watch as well as the app.  If you have high blood pressure, I wouldn't rely on just the watch to monitor your blood pressure because I don't believe it is accurate enough. title: Nice Dash Camera
text:
The Hyperion auto dash camera is a decent dash cam for the money. It is easy to install and the suction cup holder is very secure. The recording modes/video files are, Crash detected, Loop-recording, Parking and Photo. You can plug your camera to you computer with the supplied cable to transfer the videos or you can pop out the memory card and put it in a card reader on your computer to transfer the videos. You can also update the camera the same way, if there is an update to the camera.

The camera has other functions as well, it has Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS), Front Collision Warning System, Front Vehicle Departure Warning. They seem to work, but I wouldn't rely on it. It just give beeping tones and sometimes it seems random whey they go off, also if you pass other drivers or vice versa it beeps as well. Installation is pretty simple, it comes with a long power cord that can be easily concealed under the trim. The only thing that might be a problem is you need to plug it into the cigarette lighter, so if you don't have another lighter plug outlet, you would have to unplug the camera to for example plug in a cellphone charger. The camera does have a rechargeable battery built in so it can run on battery power for a while, but you have to have the camera plugged in for a while to charge the battery first.

The ends of the wires are soldered, which keeps the wire from fraying and it makes them easy to plug in to the speakers and receiver ports. Another thing I like is that you can plug (HDMI) your cable box, video game console, DVD player, and Fire T!
V/Box etc... into the Onkyo receiver and you just have to run one HDMI cord from your Onkyo receiver to your TV to play any of them. You don't have to run a lot of individual wires to the back of your TV to hook up all your electronics. You might have to run one more cord from your receiver to the TV for sound, it depends on if your TV is an ARC enabled set. That means the TV has an ARC HDMI plug which receives sound and video through the HDMI cable, not just video. If not, you can run a sounds cable, it not hard to do. I also love that it has bluetooth capability, so I can connect to the receiver with my cellphone and play my music through the sound system. Set up is really quick and easy, I would recommend the Onkyo HT-S3910, it great for small rooms, dorm/bedroom, in a living room or in a home theater room. This isn't the top of the line theater systems, but it is very good quality surround theater system.

I emailed the manufacturer and he insisted that I must be using it improperly in some way, but that's not the case. Simply unacceptable that something that cost $20 with one single function would start doing the opposite of what it's designed to do after 6 months.

Here's my old review, for reference:

Pros:
- cleans my iPad screen as close to 100% quicker than anything else I’ve tried
- easy to throw in a bag and take with you

Cons:
- only takes off fresh fingerprints. You’ll need to use it regularly (at least once a day) and clean it well with a microfiber or something similar before first use. This is important.
- requires cleaning with soap and water probably about every 20 uses for me
- design is a bit crap as the cover will close itself while rolling sometimes.

As a result, when I took my action cam surfing for the first time, it unscrewed from the mount and thankfully was saved by the leash attached to my board. The Sony official surf mount has this pin that keeps the camera from rotating, and thus doesn't have this problem.

title: Not designed very well for Macs
text: When using these with a Mac, it's nearly impossible to align it such that it won't block the ambient light sensor (the thing that's responsible for automatically adjusting screen brightness and is to the left of the camera) without it partially blocking the camera's view.

title: Works well, looks cheap
text: The (computer rendered) product images make it look like this is metal & a perfect match for the iMac's aluminum frame, but instead it's made of cheap plastic and neither the color nor the texture match my iMac. It's not the end of the world, but disappointing that this was the most expensive option for this type of iMac USB hub and I thought it would look amazing.

title: No skip forward/back - annoying omission
text: Not bad for the price. Maximum volume is lower than I'd hoped, but I suppose I should've expected that from a small speaker like this. My biggest annoyance is that there isn't any way to skip forward/back using the controls on the speaker. I suppose you get what you pay for.

title: "Multi-function button" isn't so multi-function
text: This speaker is impressively loud for how small it is, however it's annoying that the "multi-function button" can only be used to answer/end calls, not play/pause music. How many people are taking calls in the shower versus listening to music? Come on, Amazon, I know it's "basics" but this is a pretty annoying omission.

title: White model works great with 27-28" monitors
text: Excellent mount for the price. Easy to mount, adjust & rotate monitors. I have a 2015 iMac 27" and a Dell P2815Q 28" 4K monitor and they both work great with this mount. I have them in a horizontal/vertical configuration, but I tried horizontal/horizontal and that worked fine as well. I considered a $250 mount before buying this an I'm amazed at the value for the money. It's mounted on my ErgoDepot Jarvis desk with bamboo top and seems very sturdy.

title: Great headphones but terrible phone headset
text:
The sound quality of these headphones is amazing for what they cost. I love the inline volume control and single control button that works with my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 to answer calls, play/pause audio, etc.

However, as far as taking calls on these goes, they produce a very obnoxious echo for the other party if the volume is turned up above a minimal level. My guess is that the mic pics up the output from the headphones and feeds it back to the other party. This is a bummer - they have a mic, but it's essentially useless. Ah well, I just got them to use as headphones anyway.

title: Surprisingly a great product
text:
I have to admit when I ordered this thing I expected it to be a complete piece of junk, but it works surprisingly well!

Pros:
+ Sound is surprisingly loud
+ Suction cup sticks really well, at least to my smooth tile
+ Battery lasts a LONG time! I've had this in my shower for almost a month and use it daily and I still haven't had to recharge it.
+ Controls work very well
+ You can actually take calls with it. I hadn't intended to, but I've gotten calls and ended up taking them in the shower (with the water off) and no one has complained about echo. Bizarre!

Cons:
- Looks pretty goofy

title: Great customer service, not that great of a product
text:
So I ended up going back to the 3M Ergonomic Mouse and asking Anker for a refund, which they promptly provided without even requiring me to send the mouse back. Great customer service from them! My review on my experience with the mouse below. My major issue with the mouse was that it was easy to lapse back into using it like a normal mouse - it didn't force me to stay on top of my ergonomics.

---------------------

I bought this to replace my 3M Ergo mouse (the joystick-looking one) that finally crapped out after years of use. I decided to try this because it's so cheap and because people always make "are you playing video games?" jokes around the office with the 3M. So, here I am after a day with it, and I have to say it's about what I expected. Here are quick pros/cons:

Pros:
+ It's inexpensive
+ It looks like a fairly normal mouse
+ It has 5 buttons

Cons:
- Button clicks require a lot of force and are the loudest I've ever experienced
- Back/Forward buttons don't work by default on Mac (but BetterTouchTool will allow you to program them)
- It's really easy to lapse into bad ergonomics and move this mouse with your wrist/fingers instead of keeping your wrist fixed. With the 3M you basically have to keep your wrist stationary since it keeps your arm at 90 degrees instead of 45.

title: Great bluetooth headphones, poor fit
text:
These headphones are great in every aspect except for comfort. They're the behind-the-head style that's oh-so-popular these days, but the fit is far worse than the comfortable (but breakage-prone) Logitech Wireless Headphones for iPod that I had before. These pair easily with my bluetooth-enabled Thinkpad, which is nice, and also with my phone (at the same time) so I can take calls and it will switch from the music, then switch back when my call is over. The built-in mic works surprisingly well, for a really hassle-free bluetooth experience.

Now for the bad: I feel like these headphones were designed for kids. They're so small (I was really shocked when I opened the packaging at how small they are) that they pinch my ears hard. The headband just simply isn't big enough for a normal-sized head. Another minor thing is that they have a mind of their own when you put them down. If you sit them down with the earpieces facing up (which you invariably will when you have to take your hourly break from the pain they cause), they "walk" themselves off of the desk if you put them down the wrong way.

title: Amazing sound quality, comfort and no breakage! (edit: Ok, they did finally break)
text:
I got these for a good deal after rebate, and was worried about the breakage problems I read about, but for the price I couldn't pass them up. I've had them for about 3 months now and I must say, I love them. I haven't seen any evidence of cracking, I believe that the problem has been fixed, or perhaps I got lucky. Either way, the quality seems great to me, both build and sound. I use them at work with my computer and it's great not to have to deal with tangled cords. The batteries easily last for a full 8-9 hour day and I definitely get a lot of questions about them from people around the office. Overall I'd have to say if you can get them for under $50 after rebate you really can't pass these up.

Edit: The headphones finally did break after about 8 months of daily use. Logitech sent me a replacement pair (which was really easy, no hassle, great customer service), which worked well for about 4 more months, and then the headband broke on those as well. When I called for another replacement pair, they told me that they were discontinued and instead they would just refund me what I paid for them. All in all, I'd say they were a great deal, but minus 1 star because they are pretty flimsy (I'd actually change the star rating if Amazon would let me, but I can't).

title: GREAT upgrade from tablet for my kids, first Chromebook
text:
I did a lot of research as to what to get for my kids to replace their aging and damaged Samsung Tab A's. We decided that it was time to go to a Chromebook so that they could get more repetition with a standard keyboard and GoogleOS. They are still able to download all the PlayStore apps that they had on their tablets, but now with better hardware and longer support.
This model has 64GB of storage (with SD card option), so thats a huge upgrade. The RAM is 4GB, which is more than most cheap tablets these days, and you can tell. Its a LOT snappier than the Galaxys.
The 2in1 flip with the screen is my kids favorite part! They can use it like a "real computer" and then flip it to make a huge tablet screen instead. Much bigger than the 8" screen they had before.
For an entry level chromebook, these are sturdy, snappy, and cheap! I dare you to find something better for preteens at this price point!
NOTE: some of the reviews here complain about the speaker quality/power. This was one of the only things I was weary about when I finally committed to this unit. Those reviews are DEAD WRONG. The speakers are GREAT on these Chromebooks. The quality is clear, and they are louder than both of my other laptops and tablets. Playing videos through YouTube at 1/2 volume is much louder than the max of my other units. Don't let the "terrible speaker" reviews sway you.

title: Great for a small desk setup
text:
If you are here for a trackball mouse, you are likely aware of the benefits. For me, the biggest benefit is that you don't need to physically move the mouse around. I have a very small amount of desk real estate, so no extra for a mouse pad and moving it around all the time. The trackball makes it easier for me to use the mouse for long periods of time without fatigue.
This mouse in particular was comfortable to use, and had all the options I wanted. You can use either Bluetooth or USB dongle connection. It has a rechargeable battery (that you can use while charging if needed). It works on all surfaces I have tried so far.
Great dependable workhorse mouse.

title: Everything I wanted in a mouse
text:
I have had to order several mice recently to replace the one I had that died. I use my mouse almost exclusively on the arm of my recliner, as I have my laptop on the table in the living room. Many of them, the laser will not recognize the surface, making them about worthless.
This mouse worked right out of the box for me, on all surfaces I could throw at it. Perfect!
It is comfortable in my hand, I have had no issues with extended use.
The scroll wheel is stiff and responsive, which is very nice. Sometimes they are very loose and spin too much.
The side back/forward buttons will take some getting used to, as I have accidently hit them a few times, but they are a nice option to have.
This mouse also has some LED lighting options, which I don't really care much about, but it is helpful incase your mouse falls behind something, which happens often for me.

title: Works great!
text: I ordered these for back to school and my kids have been using them for about three weeks with no problems. I would have to recommend  you try them since they have done a good job so far.

title: Small but powerful!
text:
My last desk fan lasted one full battery charge and then died, never to work again. This is the replacement.
This fan was smaller than I expected, but the output is plenty for a desk fan. I use this at my desk, and then take it with me to the treadmill. It is light and powerful. The battery so far has lasted for several days, with moderate use. When I need to charge, it uses USB-C, just like my phone, so nice and easy.
I have charged it and used it down to dead several times with no issues.
Hoping this is the one that sticks!

title: Not authentic

title: More security than I probably even need!
text:
I have had many Kingston drives and computer parts, and the quality continues to be excellent. I have never had to worry about them being cheaply made or breaking down. This drive continues that tradition.
It is ruggedly made, with a great looking case, as far as external drives go. The touchscreen that you use to access the drive is large and accurate to the touch. The USB acts as the power source, so you don't see anything on the screen until it is plugged in.
Setup was easy: Plug it in and let the drivers load, set a 6 digit PIN. You can setup additional passwords and security features, or emergency wipe protocol!
Security is 256bit, which is the limit you'd need to combat brute force attacks. I don't foresee having anything that someone is going to want to hack, but I am very glad that my documents and pictures are secure, just in case. I am sure there are more features on this device that I will never even use, but they are there if you have a need for even more security than I do.

title: Almost too many options!
text:
I wanted a Smart watch for the health tracking and monitoring, and this thing has so many options, I can't think of anything missing. 100+ sports modes, sleep/heart/stress tracking, and tons of features for the outdoorsy types (not me). I want it to track my steps/exercise, and monitor my body.
Figuring out how to get the info you want out of it can be a bit of a learning curve, I did have to watch a few videos to find everything I wanted it to do, but they work flawlessly.
The look is very clean and crisp, and I have enjoyed adding to my daily ensemble. I am sure there others using this watch to MUCH fuller potential, but it is doing the things I ask it to, and likely dozens more I am not even using.

title: Pricey, but the quality is unmatched
text:
4k Blu-ray the best home video and audio quality that you can get, and this device presents it the best I have seen. Panasonic has long been one of the top companies in the Blu-ray market, and I don't think you can find many better than this device.
The video quality is crisp and clean, and the HDR optimization is a feature that is very nice and not an option on a lot of models. This particular model is know for its audio features, and also doubles as the best CD player I have ever had. My speakers have never sounded better, obviously quality upgrade over streaming services.
The build quality is great, it very heavy and sturdy. The finish and styling is classy and will fit right in with your other high-end audio and video equipment.
If you can afford to add this to your setup, I do not think you would be disappointed!

title: GREAT for all purpose use! Nice touchscreen
text:
I have started using this laptop as my everyday device and I am loving the speed and versatility!
This is my first 2 in 1, and I am not sure how often I would use it as a tablet, as it is fairly bulky and kind of heavy for a tablet. Functionally, it is great. The touchscreen is very responsive and it flips back and forth between orientations quickly.
As a laptop, it has a 500GB SSD, which is very speedy and good capacity. Their is only 8GB of RAM, which I will likely upgrade soon, but I have not had any issues with it being limited by RAM so far.
For standard browsing and streaming, it has been very quick and I have had NO issues. The speakers aren't the best, but a huge upgrade from my last laptop.
It does not have a dedicated graphics card, but I have done some light gaming (World of Warcraft, Diablo 3/Immortal) and it has held up with no lag so far! I don't think it would handle new, graphics intensive games well, but that is to be expected from any integrated graphics card.
One note, if you have this in laptop mode and flush with your desk/lap it will get fairly warm. The main air flow in on the bottom and the back, so I would prop it up a bit for better cooling.
Overall, I would definitely recommend this as an everyday laptop, with touchscreen/tablet mode available as needed!

title: I'd probably pick something else honestly
text:
I have had several Netgear products in the past, and like those, this is functional and not bad, but not great.
Setting up was easy, fairly standard for anyone with some IT experience. The WiFi coverage and strength is great, it was a noticeable upgrade from my Google Home in that area. The hardware is quality
The issues are in the supporting software. Everything has to be setup through the Orbi app, which is clunky. As others have mentioned, there is no way to turn off the 5ghz range, and some devices need that option to connect. I did have issues connecting my smart thermostat and some of my older devices. I also had a couple instances where it would lose my connection to my devices and I basically had to start from scratch with setup again. Netgear's customer service is frustrating at best, completely unhelpful at worst.
I would likely stay away from this, and either get something cheaper that does the same things, or something better that doesn't give so many headaches.

Overall, the Pixoo has been quite a hit around here. Everyone uses it more than I expected. It was a fun find.

title: Very nice!
text:
I am genuinely impressed with this speaker. I would NOT consider myself a sound quality speaker snob, but my husband can be. He's listened to music on this speaker a few times over the past couple of weeks and he hasn't complained about the tinny-ness even once. And an imbalance between the treble and bass usually drives him nuts.
We both think the sound quality is excellent. Plus this speaker is incredibly loud for how small it is. It charges quickly and lasts at least the full 12 hours the manufacturer claims. Also, this Magnovox automatically connected itself via bluetooth to all of my devices with in a matter of seconds; so the set up has been a absolute breeze. I couldn't be happier with it and I use it nearly every day. This speaker was an excellent find.

Thank you for reading this review and I hope my opinion has helped you make your decision easier.

title: MORE than you need for working remotely
text:
For the most part I think webcams are pretty interchangeable for the needs of the majority of remote workers. Really all you need is a decent resolution and a microphone that isn't awful.
This webcam has 4K resolution the mic has intelligent noise reduction, so that's covered.
There are some extras that set this webcam apart from others I have used. The extra wide 120 degree view is very nice, especially when paired with the autoframing feature. This is the most easy, straight from the box device I have used for remote work.
Plug it in, and it interfaces seamlessly with Zoom/Teams/Webex/Skype, whatever you use. Everytime I used this I look and sound great, often far better than those on the other side!

title: Better alternative to headphones for gaming!
text:
I can't be the only one, but I do not like wearing headphones for an extended period of time. Ear buds are uncomfortable, and regular headphones are just too much after awhile. I VERY much enjoyed this speaker. You are able to have immersive, omni-directional surround-sound quality audio that is FAR more comfortable than any headphones.
It didn't take long at all for me to forget that I had this super light (12oz) speaker sitting around my neck. I was also very glad that the wired USB cable is almost 10ft long, because I have stood up to leave my desk, forgetting that I had the speaker on.
The best part is that you are able to hear your audio, but ALSO hear what is going on around you in your room. One of the things I hate the most about headphones is that you have no spatial awareness because your ears are covered.
The sound quality is great! The microphone was also crisp with actual noise cancelling. Easy to switch between audio modes for chat as well.

text:

However, for Roblox/Fortnite/World of Warcraft, etc, this is GREAT for my young gamer. The processor and SSD are nice and speedy, no lag or choppiness. 512GB is a pretty good size for a SSD these days too.

title: Absolutely fantastic!
text: I love our new label printer! It makes shipping from home a thousand times easier. Setting it up was incredibly easy. The quality of the dymo labels are exceptional. They stick very well to packages (cardboard or poly bags). I can't think of one bad thing to say about this label printer. Dymo's are truly fantastic.

title: Great midrange buds!
text:
I was looking for an upgrade from my standard bluetooth buds
- Sound quality is great! Full and rich, with deep bass. The noise cancelling works well, although not as effective as some higher end earbuds (AirPods, etc), but noticeable and effective.
- Earpieces are comfortable, and I like that the post that hangs out of your ear is shorter, not super long.

title: Worth every penny!!!
text:
This LG soundbar is simply fantastic. It was easy to hook up physically and the app works great. I don’t know how often we’ll actually use the app, but I like having it as a backup option (our kids manage to lose remotes all the time!). Once we had the soundbar and sub hooked up, the technical portion of setting the sound set up and configurations took a while for my partner to get right. I thought the sound was amazing and beautiful, practically right out of the box. But my picky husband fussed around with the settings for a better part of an hour getting it just right. I’m kinda glad he did though because the sound quality went from “now this is nice” to mind blowingly “excellent!!!” We watch a lot of Disney and nature shows, and now it sounded like we’re right there. As if we’re sitting in a real movie theater or in the middle of the rainforest! The sound really is that impressively good.

The only thing I didn’t love is the bar itself is a bit bigger than our old one (which is nearly 10 years old); so check the measurements if space is tight. I am sure I’ll get used to it in time. But the sub is quite small, so I can really hid this one! I think that is really nice. Overall, LG this set it looks modern and looks great in person. It works amazing well and we couldn’t be happier with it. I usually try not to comment on price, since what affordability is subjective. But I think this LG bar is worth it’s weight in gold.

title: Works great!
text: I've always purchased Dymo brand replacement labels in the past and now I feel silly. These non-name brand labels are working out great. I tested both and my Dymo recognized both rolls. And once I snip them off, I can't tell these labels apart from the name brand. Plus, they're sticking well so far too. I'm really happy with these. They were an excellent find.

title: Meh
text:
These are so close to perfect, but the connectivity issues drive my husband insane and eventually he stopped using these. The app is a pain and doesn't play nice with either of our new android phones.
The good is they fit amazingly well in both my husband's and my ears. I have a small head, and can wear a child size hats and glasses; my ears are smaller than most people's too. Also, the sound quality is impeccable and the battery life pretty good. He really wanted to love these. It appears to be a good company, and a year and a half in to covid, a lot of things that should work aren't going as planned... Hopefully they can get their issues resolved soon.

title: Not bad, pretty cheap feeling
text:
These are very similar to many of the other cheaper kids headphones.
They are comfortable on the ears, the sound quality is decent, and they look nice.
However, the build quality isn't the best. They feel cheap, and the inside foam from the ears came out after only 3 days. I don't think these will make it through the rest of the year.

title: Better quality than most kids headphones
text:
I have had to get several pairs of kids headphones for school recently, and I feel like these have been the best of the bunch. The materials they are made out of don't feel cheap, they are comfortable and have held up to my kids and their less-than-careful attitude with electronics. I think they will hold up for the rest of the school year and beyond.
Sound quality is pretty good

title: Decent school headphones for kids
text:
They are holding up so far through the first few months of school, better than the pair they had last year.
The sound quality is decent, not great. I was not able to notice any noise cancellation per se.
The ear pieces are spongey and comfortable for my kids.
Not bad as long as they hold up and don't come apart.

title: I like it a lot!
text:
I was an '80s child so we have tons and tons of real photographs. The photo albums they were all in have started to deteriorate and some of them even ruining the photos; so I needed a way to remove and preserve them. The space is great for storing it a variety of sizes. I love that I can organize and label the sections.
Hope this review was helpful.

title: Absolutely fantastic!
text:
I'm not sure how I lived without this photo booth for so long! Truly!!! My husband and I are obsessed with Legos. But we do not have unlimited space or money, so once we've completed a build, it usually goes up for auction. This photo setup is so quick and easy; and it truly gives us professional looking photos! It is made of out of sturdy, high quality materials too. Legos are heavy and have sharp edges so I was worried the vinyl would rip easily. But it's holding up beautifully. Plus storage is easy too. Once I'm done taking photos, it stores away nicely under my bed. I really am happy with it.

title: Great replacement cord for broken/misplaced originals
text:
Like most of you looking at this review, I needed a replacement for the USB C cable that came with my phone (or other device). I simply wanted something that "works".
I have had good luck with the Amazon Basics electronics, and this is also something that I can recommend.
It is 3 foot, so not the longest, but the cord quality is good and it is standing up to the abuse that my kids are putting it through.
It connects well and charges at max speed for my device.
If you need a replacement that does everything that your original does, this will work great for you.
