title: Great replacement cables! Right angle helps protect the port
text:
The dog got to my original cables for my Pixel, and I got these as a replacement/upgrade.
The braided nylon cord is more durable than the original plastic cords, I prefer this style.
One end of the cables are at a 90 degree angle, which I find REALLY helps with saving your charge port. It prevents a lot of the bending and abuse that your port gets when you use it while plugged in.
I would strongly suggest swapping to right angle chargers if you can't utilize wireless charging.
I hope this review was helpful!

title: Great compact projector!
text:
This is a great little unit offering lots of perks right out of the box.
The picture is true 1080p without upscaling, and its surprisingly bright. Other projectors in this price range i have tried had a decent picture, but were not very bright.
Adjusting the picture is easy, with the manual focus, and the "keystone" adjustment, which makes sure that the image is straight on the wall/screen. This feature was very easy to use, and made the picture look great!
The speakers werent the greatest, but there is an option to hook up with a 3.5mm connector for externals.
Very easy to hookup to your phone or gaming system, would recommend!

title: Perfect fit, great color (orange)

Orange color is great, helps me from getting it lost in the couch! Which has been an issue with these tiny controllers.
The only thing I didn't like as much is that it fits SO well, that the buttons are now flush with the sleeve, and its harder for my fingers to "find" the buttons. It will be fine once I get used to it.

title: Great for coin collectors!
text:

It is easy to take pictures with the included remote, and they save to internal memory, which you can then transfer to your computer if you want. I have been using it to accurately inventory my coin collection with MUCH more detailed shots than before.
Easy to setup and get right to it!

title: Easy to use

title: SSD is blazing! Very nice dock for Thunderbolt devices
text:
Great dock for my laptop. There are tons of USB ports on this, and other features I didn't find on other docks: Gigabit Ethernet, integrated 1TB SSD drive.
When testing data transfer, the write speeds on the SSD are faster than internal drive in my laptop! This has given my laptop some extra boost when docked.
Like others have mentioned, it does run hot, but I didn't notice it affecting the performance. My laptop runs hot too, so its not very noticeable for me.
Expensive, but if you want a USB-C dock with fast ports and a speedy SSD, this is very nice

title: Good starter telescope for kids

title: Great physical representation of digital currencies!
text:

They are all a good weight and feel professionally minted. Not those paper thin, super light "coins". You get 5 different of the major coins (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Litecoin, Ripple and Doge) and they all come with their own coin capsules to keep them scratch free.
Very nice and I would suggest for your cryptohead's keepsakes!

title: Really fun!

Highly recommend this drive!

title: So much fun!!!

I like the bright red color (it makes them easier to find) and I appreciate that it comes with different plug adapters, just in case. title: Nice selection of outlets, quality build

title: Our old Nexus survived a toddler, so we bought it again!
text:
This is our second Nexus. Absolutely just love it!!!!
After a ton of research, my tech hubby decided the newest version of the Nexus still meet our needs the best. We've only had this one 3 months, but so far so good.
Our old Nexus experience:
The first nexus we bought survived my sons' toddlerhood very well!. My husband bought it two and a half years ago for reading in bed. Our son had just turned two. And within days, the boy had claimed it as his own. In those 2.5 years, my son dropped the tablet upwards of a dozen times a day. Not exaggerating. And he's 'a rough' kid too and it only had a cheap case to protecting it. But eventually, the outdated software caused too many problems with the latest apps, frustrating both our son and me. So we decided it was time for a new one for our son, who was now 4 and a half years old. My husband wiped the old Nexus clean and it did help speed it up quite a bit... so it is now perfect for our 18month old daughter, since toddler apps don't require much space or the latest software. She can't really "play" any of the apps yet. All she really can do at this age is "color" on it.... but she's had the old one for three months and beats the ever loving cr*p out of it on a daily basis... and it's still going strong. There isn't a scratch on the screen. IDK, I'm just very impressed with Nexus, seeing as how every time one of my adult friends drop their iPhone, I see them ranting on facebook about how it shattered instantly.

title: Open these before starting!
text:
I strongly recommend that you open and inspect all the stickers BEFORE starting this project. Month 1 was fine. Took out month 2 today and it was completely mis-cut. I can't go back a month and start this project over with a different idea.... Nor do I feel like spending $15 and wait a week for it to show up in the mail. These were a shower gift, so I don't know where they were bought or even where they're sold locally to keep it close to her 2nd month b-day.

I'm mostly mad because in my opinion this was obvious mistake, but still packaged and sold intentionally. Shame on the manufacture for continuing to sell this defect knowing you won't notice until it's too late.

title: Stay far far far away from SONY!!!
text:
Ok, so we got this camera about 3 years ago and paid $150-ish. We take pictures once maybe twice a year (and NO more than a 100 total so far). Well I needed it for a school project tomorrow and guess what... it's dead! It will let me look at the pictures I took three months ago, but nothing else... it instantly shuts right back off.

Better yet, after an hour of internet research, apparently several people have had this problem... so I dug out my old SONY camera. It took two good pictures and then the picture/video card fried! It literally started trembling in my hand.

I'm done with Sony... last month our two year old Sony DVD player died too. This used to be the best quality company around, now they've obviously turned to crap.

title: Powerhouse Sony Moves into Corner with Its Own Future
text:
Unlike Coke Cola company, which continues to produce exceptional products, Sony has thrown in the towel when it comes to it WALKMAN market share, and loyal customers. While millions of hard working adults and millions of dillegent students have turned to Sony Walkman for their music while at the gym or out in the sports field, Sony has turned its back on them. This D-NF340 will be one of the last walkmans, as its quality has continuously diminished, and Sony has lost its willpower to make leading edge MUSIC.

First, the FM Tuner does a poor job in getting a good reception. I mostly get static on my machine. So, what happened SONY? Where is the quality?

Second, the CD Style is outdated, as so many are moving into SD cards, micro SD cards, and internal memory to play the music. Sony should have continued with their ATRAC-3 technology, and onto memory stick, rather than throw in the towel to just MP3. Yet, something could be said about going MP3, which makes sense. But, not providing a SPORTS walkman, now that is bad news. It is like Coke Cola saying to Pepsi, "ok, you win." Now, wait a minute. Both Coke Cola and Pepsi continue to make advancements, and both continue to make sales and keep business going. So, what happened Sony. Is this the end for Sony? The CD style is also very bulky. There is no need to carry such a bulky physical CD anymore. But, another version of the Walkman should have been created. Shame on you, Sony.

Third, the knobs and controls are good, yet they could be better served on a digital walkman. There is something nice by having knobs and buttons, controls and sliding switches. The controls of such nature blend well with humans who are sweating, running, exercising, stretching, pulling, pushing, bumping, etc. The digital up/down arrows, push etc. just are not controling enough for this person. Maybe it is the same with driving a car. Manual transmission, putting the hand on the stick shift knob, feeling the car going from first to second, from second to third, and so on. That feel is part of being human. Not sure why a sports version of a digital mp3 player by the GREATEST CREATOR of WALKMAN cannot put together such a product. Knobs, oh how they provide controlable pleasure.

Fourth, the sports thing. This CD player, along with its many many prior versions failed the drop test. Oh, so many start loosing a function, like the loss of one side audio, or loss of display, etc. after one drop on the ground. And, because they are heavy, what can you expect. Ahh Punka, Bash, Blop, Clunk!, Dah Pinga, Dah Dong, Blip, Ding, Dong, Crash, Kaput. Even the sports version was heavy. Eh. So, yeah SONY WALKMAN designers, make the MP3 version with digital memory, in the light weight version, please. Sweat resistant, slightly water resistant (for the rain,) unlike this one. Dah? Where have you been Sony? And, call it the Walkman, MAN!!

Now, for all the poor people who just do not want to hurt their eyes, make the display FONT size a good bit larger. Give your loyal customers a break. Large enough so it can be seen in various environments - lighted room, darken street, etc. Some of us JOG at night, and can use the larger font size.

Until then, this product is a "don't buy." It is not a sports version, It is not supported by Sony software, it is not MP3 and ATRAC3, it is not light weight, it is not water resistant, ... what it is ... OLD FASHION.

title: Low battery and camera shuts off with NO WARNING
text:
Problem #1: Camera eats up normal AAA Energizer batteries quickly. Maybe get 5 pictures and then it quits. Change to AAA Lithium Entergizer Batteries. Now, you are OK. The sensor on the camera trips just after a few underwater photos.

Size, and functionality seems comfortably nice. Not too technical to get started using this camera. Found this camera a great first step for beginners who want to document their scuba dives, take photos on surface, on the boat, on the shore, etc. But, hold on... when you want to go scuba diving:

Problem #2: Does not have an underwater setting for diffused lighting. Only Flowers and Landscapes. What dah? Is this not for underwater use? Hello! All of my underwater photos could have improved by 100 percent if there was a setting for underwater lighting. The sunny days at the shore, boat photos, trees and countryside photos, ok. These were nice, the detail in the landscape photos were good. You can even use the camera without its plastic shell. The protective casing makes this an excellent choice as a first step scuba camera. But, how are the photos underwater? This is a $100 camera, so please do not expect high quality photos from your squid, lobster, or grouper ... posing for you underwater, even at 25 feet. This makes a great first step camera, getting your feet wet with underwater photography.

Problem #3: strap holder is on right side only (for right hand use.) Better if there was a strap holder on both sides, for those who need on left hand side (underwater.) Why? My first hand experience is that you want to use this point and shoot camera using either your right hand or your left hand. Not both. This camera is a quick shot camera, not "oh, wait a minute, pose, look this way, now smile, ok, cheese ..." This camera sits on your right hand or left hand while diving. Now, if you see that nice fish, and want to take a picture, you try with one hand. If the strap is on the wrong side, it blocks your ability to use the left hand to hold the camera. So, this camera is ONLY FOR RIGHT HANDED folks. But, do not let go of the camera underwater, you may loose it. Right? Not really. Nice thing about this basic camera is that it float to surface (rather than sink into the bottom.) Wow, did that save me a few times. Dropped off my wrist. Then floated for a few feet, and I got it back. If it sunk down 300 Feet, I could have kissed this baby --- good bye.

I have taken about 50 surface images, and 50 underwater images, using this Intova. All 50 surface photos, with reasonable sunlight, were excellent considering this camera. Of the 50 photos underwater images, about 10 were acceptable, the other 40 were blurry and not acceptable. Yeah, I had to spend another 15 minutes per each of the 10 photos to convert the poor colors into something more exciting, adding RED, adding CONTRAST, adding BRIGHTNESS using a photo editor. But, I did get 10 acceptable underwater photos. And that was great. Really Great. These photos were generally above 25 feet.

Scuba divers need to know the difficulty of taking photos underwater while attempting to swim around reefs, wrecks, squid, lobster and other photographers. Buy this camera as a first step. Just correct that battery issue, take lots of pictures, and learn the responsibility of underwater photography is the PERSON BEHIND THE CAMERA. For $100, not bad, eh?

title: First Time MP3 User - Having Difficulty Here
text:
Because I am a First Time MP3 User, please ignore this review (if you are an expert.) I am having difficulty with this MP3 player because the manual does not have references in each paragraph as to "more readings." For example, Sandisk does not offer its own MP3 burner and/or Music Management Software. This would have been a great advantage, even if the software was at cost, say $10. It would mean the equipment would be integrated with mp3 music burning. I had difficulty transfering mp3 music to the sansa clip +8. First, it seems that the PROPERTIES data in each song was important. With 100 of songs having a song title as "track 1" and "track 2" the music had some chaos creating a playlist. So, a warning about this on the manual, for novice mp3 users would have been nice. (Do you agree?) Maybe I should have looked harder on the sandisk website. (Maybe?) At least a reference to help beginners in the manual would have been appropriate. Ok, second, the internal memory saves music more true to original names than the extended memory. Some of my files says "DN30000101 Journey - Love is Everything" where the DN330000101 tag was added by Sandisk. Not sure why, but this just adds to the chaos. (OK, stick a pencil in my ear.) I am a beginner, so music management means everything to me. Chaos with this Sandisk is life right now. If my collection was just two or three CDs, then I could say ok. (Life is beautiful.) But so many readers, I assume, have a collection of 100 CDs that have been existing on their library for a few years. So, the SANSA CLIP must meet integrating with old files in mid stream. (Old, old file systems, maybe?) It appears not enough testing my Sandisk has been done to make the product user friendly for first time MP3 users. If they did enough testing, they would have built their own music management software I am tired. I called Sandisk, and they suggest to change ALL of my ID3 tags on the PROPERTIES of each song. Well, there goes my summer vacation. If I can manually change 100 songs each weekend, in about 10 weekends I will have make sense out of chaos. Right now, I have so many songs saying "track 1." Yeah, etc, track 2, track 3.

Bottom line is that Sandisk is not creating a product like the iPOD which takes responsibility for all experiences the user has: managing albums, burning mp3, transfering data, creating playlist, and teaching novice people about the equipment. Instead, Sandisk just makes the equipment, and assumes "sink or swim" to the users. So, all the good reviews, I assume, come from experienced users, and not first time idiots, like me. Maybe I should go back to my old music player? (Tell me.)

I must be tired, because I am having a hard time with this Sansa Clip. Ok, give me about two years, and I'll catch up. So, I give it a 4-star.

title: Four different issues, One great CD player.
text: Before getting the DNF430, I owned the DNF420 version and was very happy with its performance.  But, there were four different issues with the SONY ATRAC CD player: 1) the player 2) the sonicstage software 3) headphones 4) recording in atrac.  The CD player was excellent - it displayed songs, allowed jump from song to song, or album to album.  Also, the FM tuning allowed reception inside gyms that broadcast tv shows on FM stations, like CNN and ESPN.  Every once in a while, I would watch a CNN breaking story on the gym TV monitor, and to hear the sound,  I just flip to the FM pre-set dial, and presto. But, the headphones needed to be replaced with Noise Reduction, over the ear headphones. At the beginning, I was not prepared for the headphone fuss. In the gym, with all the exercising and sweating, the standard headphones did not withstand the daily wear and tear, I am sorry to say. Yet, I was able to overcome this issue. I have dropped the CD player a number of times at the gym, on the treadmill, yet it continues to perform quite well. My critical issues was the sonicstage software. Unknown to me - until purchased and started to use stonicstage, this software was delicate and took a while to learn.  "RIPPING" a CD and "BURINING" a CD was relatively new to me. So, I was not prepared to "tolerate" with the learning curve issues surrounding the software. It took me time, and it was frustrating in the begining.  When all the tweaking was done, the learning understood - the software, the library, the burning, and the performance worked like a charm. I was able to store over 250 songs onto a single CD.  Yet at times, I was skeptical about reaching the quoted 400 songs SONY talks about.  Anyway, I also backed-up my music using the sonicstage software, and later restored it.  This worked like a charm, too.  I was very lucky to have this backup,  since my PC system crashes at least once a year.  My library and the selections were recovered nicely, thanks to Sony and the restore feature!  The ATRAC system featured a slightly different recording than MP3.  MP3 was transferable format, while ATRAC was not.  I don't thik the MP3 playback also had the descriptive and navigating features during playback mode. So, I stayed with the ATRAC recordings.  I am very happy with my CD player, because it performs well, has great sound, and can be stored in my gym bag, and left in my car overnight.  The CD player was able handle the COLD and HOT weather temperatures of Northeastern USA.  I use the CD player at least three times a week, at the gym, and so far - no problems.

title: Once this drive is format in NTFS, works great. 5-stars.
text:
I have used this product for 5 years, and it works fine. Just make sure you format for NTFS, else you may experience a nightmare below. Do not read below, unless you feel necessary NOT TO FORMAT ( and be stupid, like me. )

------------

I am editing the stars to 4 star - but cannot do it on amazon. After
you understand the pitfalls (you must format this drive NTFS first,) then all other aspects of it are very good. So, below -- just keep in mind that I was "upset".

If you do not format this external drive - be ready for some real problems. Forget the 2-page manual that says "preformatted." You need to format this one. Or else ...

The WD 250 boasts on being an external drive, but neglects to mention that it must be unplugged from the computer before power down. Well, clumbsy me, I made the same mistake twice with this product. The desktop and the laptop both recognized the MyBook drive "ok" and had no problem writing data files to it. So, I thought all is well. But, in both cases, once the PC was turned off - it became a nightmare. Since both my PCs run in XP Prof mode, with all service pack software updated, latest and greatest versions of everything, I would assume nothing should go wrong. Not so. In both cases, the Xp operating system was damaged to "the point of no return." Furthermore, all data on my PCs were lost. Now - why did I buy this external hard drive? Ok, this is not the first time some hardware has gone wrong on my PCs, but usually it does not take out the entire operating system - such that I cannot run a "restore," and get back to working. After calling WD on the phone, they suggested that I must unplug the MyBook each and everytime, before turning off the PCs.

I would have given this external drive a 4 star rating - if it was not for the bad experiences, and the loss of time, loss of data from my PC.

title: Great basic universal TV mount, easy to install even for a novice
text: Comes with an array of hardware to install on any TV, you won't need 3/4 of it but it's nice to know that this kit can accommodate most any TV.  The instructions are clear and the TV mount itself is very intuitive.  The mounting bracket has a built in level and there are multiple anchor points along the bracket to accommodate any spacing of studs wherever you need the TV to hang.  The dual hanger clip system that actually fastens to the rear of your TV can be attached anywhere along the wall mount.  They simply lift onto the top rail system and then click down to lock into place.  The TV can then be adjusted left to right sliding along the rails and adjusted to tilt up or down as well.  A very solid, easy to install universal TV mount that can accommodate a range of TV sizes.

title: Easily transfer audio from my computer to my speaker system
text: A quality, long length cable to transfer audio from 1/8th inch audio jack (3.5mm) to a left right analog speaker system.  Works perfectly for an iPod, computer or anything with a standard headphone jack.  Clean, clear audio out of both left/right speakers.

title: B.A.S.I.C.
text: Which is all I wanted.  It holds my camera and points it at what I want it to without any motion.  Perfect.  These version is cheap, light, and adjustable.  If you need a tripod and you're not a professional or just need to capture some home content, this does the job.

title: A direct fit for my 86' 4Runner, looks and operates great!
text: My truck stereo head was broken when I bought it so I needed a new one.  This fit perfectly in my center piece trim and install was smooth.  I had to hard wire it because there was no wiring harness in my truck but that was easy enough to figure out using the manual that came with the stereo head.  Connecting to my phone is a snap and I love that whenever I turn on my truck it automatically connects to my phone and begins playing the last track I was listening to.  AM/FM sound great, the user interface is easy to adjust the speaker fade front to back or left to right, bass boost or treble.  This isn't the most expensive stereo unit but I think it looks great, I love the scrolling blue light display and the removable face plate is a nice touch for security.  I've been running mine for 5 years and have never had an issue.  Plays and sounds great, looks great, super happy with it.

title: Good portable camera stand for self filming on the go
text: I used this for my GoPro Silver when I was backpacking by myself and wanted to record some travel moments.  This is really lightweight and can attach itself easily to the outside of my backpack for quick access.  My GoPro easily threaded onto the head and the flexible arms can twist and grip to sit on any uneven surface or even grab onto a vertical pole.  This made staging shots by myself super easy and quick to film without a lot of wasted time getting set up.  Cheap and easy to use, a great travel companion for a solo trip.

title: Easy to install in my 86' 4Runner, sound great!
text:
Needed to replace my crappy rear bed speakers and wanted to upgrade to something with a bit more power. These swapped in easily with plenty of mounting options to fit wherever I needed them to go. Direct swap on my existing wiring harness, took longer to take off the plastic quarter panels than to install these.

These aren't the most expensive speakers in the world but they can crank up pretty hard and still sound clean and clear without distortion. I mainly listen to talk radio or rock and both come through with great range and clarity. Super pleased with how these have held up for 5 years now without any issue and still sounding strong.

title: Perfect fit for my Nuvi Garmin, solid grip to the windshield
text: Cracked my old Garmin mount, this is an identical replacement that I think secures even better than the original.  I like to put a little spit on the back of the suction cup before I stick it to the windshield.  Maybe the fluid makes the seal tighter, maybe the evaporation pulls the gas out, I don't know?  But a little spit on the back of the cup makes for a strong, lasting hold that never falls off.

title: This and a youtube video saved me $300 and fixed my T.V.
text: I internet diagnosed my tv issue to a bad set of capacitors.  I watched a youtube video and after 30 minutes of careful disassembly and  amateur level soldering my tv worked perfectly once again!  This is a cheap solution to a possibly expensive problem, try it out yourself before you take it to the shop!  You can do it!

title: For a DIY home theater using a laptop these work great
text:
I use a projector attached to my laptop when we want to watch a movie. I have these speakers on the wall I'm projecting onto so when we're watching a movie I have the audio feed coming from my laptop, perfect for the 1/8" audio jack the transmitter uses.

These are not deluxe home audio equipment, these are glorified computer speakers. But they work great and for our needs are an adequate solution to watching a movie with clear audio projected towards us. The transmitter links quickly and without lag, the speakers are clear and don't distort unless theres a really heavy action scene turned up too loud. They're low profile and look fine dangling on the way when not in use.

For the price these are perfect for our application, but don't purchase these expecting 5.1 dolby audio sound, these are two decent computer speakers you can wirelessly connect audio to, and I recommend them.

title: An Ok outdoor speaker but they failed in less than a year
text:
These started out great. If you can find a way to protect and waterproof the outlet these need to plug into (yes, they're battery powered as well but it's useless) these worked really well at first. The wireless channel connected quickly and I could play my iPod through them clearly in my backyard and could even adjust their volume from my iPod alone. But after having these live in their new outdoor home their quality slowly degraded and then the right speaker starting disconnecting constantly and just buzzing loudly. Over time the speakers began sounding tinny and harsh until finally the right speaker stopped connecting entirely.

There are very similar style speakers to these on the market which work better. These are cheap and poorly made.

title: Super fast transfer speed, very portable and compact
text: My old external died so I decided to switch to a solid state hard drive that had enough storage to back up my computer and all of my music files.  This hard drive is lightning fast, I was able to back up my computer and all of my music (1.2 TB) overnight.  My old hard drive took 2 days.  It fits in the palm of your hand and being a solid state drive you don't have to worry about any moving parts failing after a drop or shuffling around in your bag.  Been using it regularly for over a year with no issues at all.  I definitely feel secure having this as my backup.

title: Pulls the audio from my PS4 HDMI to my speaker
text: I play my PS4 on a projector and since the standard version only has an HDMI out I needed someway to pull the audio off of it to my standard audio jack speaker system.  This does the trick.  Plug the HDMI into this then out the other end to my projector, it splits off the audio to L/R audio jacks that then I use a splitter to reverse back to a standard 1/8" audio jack.  There is no lag between the audio and the projector, the sound quality is great and it solves my issue perfectly.

title: 64 Gigs is so cheap these days!

title: A great beginners or even moderate users Stylus pad
text: A good introductory pad for drawing on the computer.  It took me a bit to learn how to draw without looking at my hand and to watch the screen instead but after I detangled my brain it went very smoothly.  The instructions which came with the pad weren't very clear but there were many fantastic instructional videos online which got me up and running quick.  Had the pad had better instructions I'd give it 5 stars, but overall I was impressed by its pressure sensitive features and how natural it felt in my hand after a day or two of use.  For a beginners first pad this did everything I wanted it to, the drawing area is plenty large enough and it came with extra nib tips to replace as they wear down from use.  I'm very happy with how responsive the quill is and the quick buttons make switching between features in my program super easy.

title: Bought it for my Mom and now she can see her Grandkids in real time
text: My siblings and I bought this for our Mom for Christmas and it is SUCH a hit!  We all downloaded the app and set it up before we gave it to her so all she had to do was plug it in and join her wifi at home.  Now we send her photos of what we and her grandkids are up to whenever we want it and it automatically uploads and populates them on her frame!  We set the frame to only randomize through the most current 200 photos so its always updating with the latest shares.  She loves that the photos are always changing (we put them on a minute timer) so whenever she passes through the room its new or even brand new!  This is social media I can get behind.  A great way to stay connected with family or friends!  We even showed her how to share her Frame ID with other friends and family so now they are sharing photos with her frame as well.  A wonderful and easy gift, we love it!

title: Boom for the buck
text:
I use this to play music while I'm riding my bike to work everyday so I have it turned up full blast the whole way. It takes full volume without distortion but I wish it could pump out a bit more bass (has a slight rattle when the speakers bottom out).

Still, for the price and against competing portable speakers it gets LOUD and pairs seamlessly with my phone. I get a week's worth of riding out of a charge, so that's roughly 12 hours of full volume playing without dying on me. Pretty good. I like this speaker, it sounds good, it plays loud and since I use it 12 hours a week I generally get a year or two out of it before it breaks. For the amount of use I put it through that's pretty good for the price, I'm sure it will last you far longer since I used mine so often.

title: Well made and comfortable, the best cheap earbud on the market
text:
I normally work with earbuds in all day and my ears would start to hurt from the added discomfort. Not since I bought these! They come with three different silicone ear tips to fit to your exact ear canal size. The tiny size fits easily into your ear and stays there or hours without notice. Works seamlessly with my iPhone for making calls or listening to podcasts, the pause button to start and stop whatever you're listening to is really nice. The microphone operates clearly.

For the price you can't do better, these aren't cheaply made and hold up to daily use. Considering the abuse my earbuds go through these hold up remarkably well and when once pair wears out after a year or so I simply buy a new one. I made my girlfriend into a convert, she loves and swears by her pair now too!

title: Decent battery for the price, power drops rather rapidly

For the price and that fact that my Macbook is plugged in most of the day this battery serves my needs.  After letting it cycle twice my computer now reads it's levels correctly and I'd say I get 2 hours of charge out of it on average.  Not amazing, but fine for my needs since I don't travel with my computer.  Still, if you need your laptop to be portable you should probably get a battery that holds a charge better since this one drains rather quickly and once you hit ~30% my computer shuts down.  An affordable battery but not great for portability.

title: So glad I bought it!
text:
I am not aiming this review at the technically advanced people. You people already know whether or not to buy this camera. This review is for the average person who is looking for a good deal on a good camera. If you are like me you want some value for your money...well this is it! I researched several cameras on various sites, read all the reviews & even went to a few stores to see the actual cameras. The Canon Powershot SD770IS is the one I ended up buying. I love it! I have no regrets buying it. It's very easy to use & the directions are not at all hard to follow. It's a snap to transfer pictures from the camera to the computer & it doesn't take long at all...even the first time.

I ended up buying a battery charger because it didn't show as coming w/the camera, but it does. So now I have a spare. I would also buy a bigger memory card, because the 32 byte one that comes w/it will fill up real fast. I bought one that came w/a free USB Reader.

I can't recommend this camera enough to those that are not really sure what they want. Again, very easy to use & learn to do some fun things w/it.

4/14/11
Over two years later & I still love this camera! I carry it with me daily & use it all the time. Even after all this time, it still takes pictures as great as it did on day one! No complaints. Not a one. Definitely glad I bought it. I've been thinking about getting the newer version...but I might wait it out & see how long this one lasts. Definitely going to buy Canon again. Great quality!

title: Works better than I thought
text: Our house is set quite far back from the road and is surrounded by trees. We have the motion zones set up so that as soon as a car reaches the cement portion of our driveway it alerts us. It has worked well for us and we don’t get many false alerts. The few we have had were from wasps hovering right in front of it or spiders crawling over it. The motion zones were easy to set up and we like that you can snooze alerts. We have the ring linked to Alexa so she also announces when someone approaches. The only problem with that is even if you have the motion alerts on snooze she will still announce them. This is annoying when someone is outside doing something. The only way to get her to stop announcing for that time is by going into the Alexa app and shutting off motion alerts. Then we have to remember to turn them back on again. It is very dark around our house at night because there are no streetlights and during the summer months we keep outdoor lights off. The night vision on the ring is excellent. We can see images very clearly. We’ve been so impressed with this doorbell that we’re going to buy a second one to put on our other door.

title: Poorly Sized - Tough Installation
text: I've installed a ton of these screen protectors over the years, and what I find is that the ones that are sized all the way out to the edge of the glass on the screen are very, very difficult to apply.  The protectors that are sized with a couple mm buffer around the edge of the glass are 100x more forgiving during application and also won't get pushed back by your case causing air bubbles around the borders.  I'm not sure why some companies haven't figure this out, but this is one of them.  Installation uses the "three sticker" method... which is ok as a basic guide, but the stickers always "give" a bit and if you don't have that buffer around the edge it's very hard to get it right the first time.  Anyway, this screen protector is not the smoothest installation, especially for a screen the size of the iPad.  I recommend looking for a different brand and read reviews regarding installation specifics.  Hope this helps.

Turned them on, and low and behold a bunch of crackle and pop comes out when you turn the bass knob. It's almost as if it was going to pop off the cone. Ok, no big deal, returned those for a replacement. The replacement comes, and it's a reverse twin of the first one - now the trebble is doing the pop and hiss. Sometimes, dust accumulates on the potentiometer, so you have to turn it a few times - I get that. After turning the knob about a 100 times, it still is producing a loud hiss and pop (which is coming from the left speaker). Changed the left speaker, and it's still there (so it's not the left speaker - it's the master unit).

Best for the dump. Sad that something that used to be of good quality is now trash.

text:
First, I want to say that I am an Amazon fanatic; I am an Amazon Prime member; I have over 4000 Kindle books that I started collecting with the very first Kindle tablet ever put out. I buy everything that I can from Amazon. This is my fourth Kindle tablet.

Let's start from the beginning. It is not thin and light. When you compare this to the Ipad, it does not even come close to being thin and light.

Second, even though I paid for no ads, I am constantly bombarded with ads. It tells me all of the things that I SHOULD LIKE TO BUY. If I wanted to buy the damned things, I would have bought them.

Third, it is incredibly slow. Much slower than the last generation Kindle. It is slow initially loading programs. It is slow going from one program to the next. IT IS JUST BORINGLY SLOW.

There is not enough memory associated with the processor. When I go from one program to the next, even though I can see the program by using the box at the bottom, it still needs to reload the program. When I switch loaded programs with either my Ipad or my Windows 8 HP tablet, it is instantaneous. I can not believe that is this way. Did no one test this?

I think the problem is with the new OS. It is horrible. If I could go back to the old OS. I would do it. If I could just use my old Kindle, dropped for the fourth time, I would.

This is the fourth kindle tablet that I have purchased. It is probably the last. I expect I will be buying Apple products in the future. In fact, I bought an Ipad this morning for my birthday.

I will continue to be an Amazon fanatic. I will never purchase another Kindle tablet.

title: Absolute Garbage
text:
Let me preface this review by explaining that I work in the IT industry and support a variety of businesses with enough thorough experience in networking to say with certainty - the router I received is absolute garbage.

Now, normally I'd say for this price that you should set you expectations quite low - being in the field I'm in, I understand that almost all consumer routers are not great options, and the ones that are somewhat viable are on the $300+ range. Not everybody has the money or cares enough to invest this much - I get that.

So, that leaves me and my old roommate pretty much one option; the TRENDnet Wireless AC1750. He doesn't need much and especially doesn't want to spend much, it was tough getting him to go high enough in price to even this router- the old router he had came with his cable subscription 3 years ago. It worked fine but was sometimes slow with downloading over WiFi, not surprising. From the research and reviews, and most importantly the price - we decided to try this Trendnet AC1750 router.

WOW what garbage - he no longer gets WiFi in his bathroom corner of the house - it is a VERY small 2 bedroom apartment. How in the world can this router not handle a signal from 20 feet away, with only 2 walls in between? A router of this caliber (even at this price) should EASILY be able to handle covering a 2 bedroom small apartment. Period.

On to the second problem - even if we're connected, the WiFi signal drops constantly, I have to now reset this router every single day by unplugging it and plugging it back in because it refuses to work longer than 16 hours before crapping out. I have tried updating firmware, all network resets I can. I've even tried using the old modem (we replaced both router + modem) to see if that was the root of our problems - nope, it's the router.

It has slowly been getting worse and worse, and when I am gone from this apartment my roommate will be forced to reset his router every day, sometimes twice a day, just to get internet - or purchase a new one.

I am extremely dissatisfied with this product, although not quite surprised or disappointed given its price. It just seems odd that a 3 year old Netgear N300 router performs much better than an AC1750 Dual Band router.

text:
Camera is a hardwire unit so installation takes a little longer over simple plug and play units. But installation outside took about 75 minutes and has performed great (one week so far). I am very impressed with the image quality and I can see two sides of my house (mounted on a shed 30 feet from the house). Connection to WiFi (Allo high speed) has been rock solid (even at 30 ft w/o a WiFi extender) with no issues. Outside durability is unknown, but in a week has withstood Nebraska winters. (I'll update if/when a weather issue occurs.) Use of the app has worked flawlessly.
Camera motion sensing is fairly sensitive so I get notices from large trucks that rumble by 25 yards away. Image quality at night is great. I have outdoor lights and so do not use night mode at all. With outside LED lights, image quality and colors at night are more than acceptable.
About the only complaint I have is that the alarm is not that loud but I hope to rarely use it. So impressed that I added two additional Geeni cameras (doorbell and second Sentry). I would highly recommend Geeni to anyone looking for easy to use cameras.

title: Rather powerful for its size and actually QUIET!
text:
I sit under a sunlight at work and while most of the time I love it, there is about an hour every day during the summer that the sun is directly above and I bake. Therefore, I've been looking for a small fan that I could pull out during that hour and power with my keyboard. However, I work with a few rather noise-sensitive people, so the fan had to be quiet. I tried a fan last summer that said it was quiet, but was definitely not. This one is actually virtually silent, like it claims! The typing on my keyboard and clicking of my mouse is definitely louder.

Today is not that warm of a day, so I am not 100% certain yet, but it actually seems to work pretty well, despite its small size.

I have two complaints though, which is why I only gave this product 4 stars instead of 5:
First, I wish the cord part were a little bit longer. It's hard to get it to sit where it will point at me, but the time I angle it out of my keyboard.
Second, and most important, I wish there were an on-off switch so I could angle the fan while it's plugged in, instead of having to guess first and plug in second.

title: What you need to know. Big files fast, little files slow.
text:
Pros;
1) It is a fast as they say, if you're using large files.
2) Price point is very good.

Mentions:
1) Unlike other reviewers I don't find it that large, I don't know it's not micro but it's not huge, smaller that my Lexar and Corsair Voyager .
2) No place to put the cap when in use.

Cons;

title: Easy install and strong, stable signal
text: The adapter installed without a problem in one of my Win10 machines and the utility software is versatile.  I’ve found the range and stability to be excellent and have a strong signal through two walls and one floor at the opposite end of the house.  I get nearly every bit of the 250 Mbps coming to my house from my ISP. The adapter’s high gain antenna -- which, at 15 cm, is longer than the picture in the product description at the time of my purchase -- is likely responsible for much of the observed performance.  I use this with an old laptop whose internal WiFi radio died, but the size of the antenna is not a problem for me since I don’t move the laptop very often. I would caution anyone thinking of using this with any device that is moved regularly. The only thing that concerns me is the loose fit of the adapter in the USB port.

Also if you have a lot of background noise like the windows are open (I live in a noisy city) or someone is doing dishes and the water is running or if the ac is on then you’ll have a hard time hearing unless you blast the the volume. However, this could be due to the distance of the tv from where you’re watching and the amount of empty space in your home. It’s kinda hard to determine causality. Overall though, good bargain!

title: Nice keyboard - but not for Mac OS
text:

My wife has used her beloved Logitech K811 keyboard for years with her iMacs - and that is the perfect keyboard but sadly is no longer made by Logitech.
Instead they sell this K380 keyboard which is a total disaster.
For a start, it uses batteries instead of being rechargeable and doesn't have the beautiful illuminated keys that light up the K811 at night, and it has user-unfriendly round keys.
The K380 doesn't even have a Caps Lock light to show that you are in that mode.
There is no 'repeat' function when you hold a key down - for multiple characters you have to keep clicking the key.
But the worst thing is that there is NO FORWARD DELETE function on this keyboard - just a backward delete. This is pathetic.
I wasted 2 hours going through Logitech's web site, downloaded drivers and software etc - there is NO mention of this missing and important feature in their technical or marketing bulletins.
I had to go on Amazon's K380 feedback to learn that other purchasers have this problem. There is NO FIX for this.
Fortunately the Vendor accepted the return of my K380 - so I am back to using Apple keyboards.
Very disappointing, frustrating and time wasting. Shame on Logitech!

text:
I have only used this drive a few times - to rip some CD's and burn ISO. I always suspected the speed was more USB 2 than USB 3. It is very, very SLOW.
The cable is definitely not a standard USB 3 cable, google the specs.
The distributors urged me to retract my first (rather) negative Amazon review - and I subsequently did, as I thought at least they believed in their product.
Tonight, I tried to eject a CD that I had in the drive and there was no response - when I looked at the 'USB 3 ' connector, I noticed it was just flopping around and not making contact.
It seems the connector on the drive is too weak to support the weight of the heavy USB cable.
Anyway it is being returned - but thankfully AMAZON will handle the defective return.
So ZERO stars for this 'Pawtec' drive, AKA 'Poor-Tech", and 5 stars for AMAZON!

title: Love this Moshi Magic Mouse cover
text:
OK, this is expensive - at $15 from Amazon with free Prime shipping, it is not cheap.
But it WORKS fantastically!
I had a lot of problems with erratic scrolling on the slippery magic mouse, especially for fine detail work - until I installed this cover.
Now the finger control with the slightly abrasive texture of the Moshi cover is PERFECT.
It has transformed the magic mouse from just being a great mouse to a fantastic mouse.
I think Apple should buy the Patent from Moshi and manufacture the magic mouse with this material!
And the bonus? The sleek silver looks so much better and more professional than the glossy white of the original magic mouse.
It is simple to install, just takes a couple of seconds, and stays in place - I can't figure out how some other reviewer couldn't work it out. Duh!
Try it - you will be delighted.

title: Corsair Memory doesn't work in Lenovo T500 Notebook
text:
I needed to upgrade my Lenovo T500 to 8gb & ordered the Lenovo recomended specification of memory and went with Corsair product CM3X8GSDKIT1066 XMS3 8 GB PC3-8500 1066Mhz, because Amazon could supply and ship fast.
This memory comes in two 4gb DIMMs. The memory did not boot up at all - I just got the dreaded startup 'beeps' from the BIOS. Turns out one DIMM was absolutely DEAD, the other 4gb DIMM booted up, but quickly failed memory diagnostics.
Thank goodness Amazon took this Corsair crap back!
I ended up buying Crucial memory directly from Crucial, and although slighly more expensive, it worked straight off the bat, passing all diagnostics and memory tests perfectly.

title: Stick it to Wacom, go Yiynova
text:
Let's cut to the chase, shall we?

This tablet is flawed. The drivers with the CD, as others have stated, are outdated. You have a choice of getting your PenPad drivers from either the Yiynova website, or alternatively there is a slightly newer version currently available from Waltop themselves. MAKE SURE YOU UNINSTALL ALL WACOM DRIVERS. I can't emphasize this enough - they can and will screw everything up and turn the hardest part (installing drivers) into a nightmare ordeal. Uninstall them, do a restart, and get the new drivers in there. Make sure you see Wacom's website for uninstall instructions, as there are additional files that you have to track down and delete to ensure they're fully gone.

After fiddling with the drivers, then comes the pen. The battery that came with mine showed up DOA, so I tried a fresh one. I can see the red 'on' light flash briefly when screwing the two components of the pen stylus together, but didn't find out until about an hour of frustration that you must screw the pen TIGHTLY together - do it with the pen on so you can see the red light come on and stay on when you've sufficiently tightened the barrel. Unfortunately, this also cascades into the rubber grip popping the side buttons slightly out of place when you're tightening it. A minor annoyance, easily corrected by shifting the rubber grip and gently pressing the buttons back into place, but still a bit of a design flaw that could be much improved upon.

I also noticed, with much confusion, that the on-screen tablet does not work outside of art programs like Paint Tool SAI and Adobe Illustrator. The cursor simply goes dead until you use a mouse to click back into one of those programs and then the on-screen tablet comes back to life. I'm not sure if this is how it's supposed to react or if there are still some issues regarding the drivers.

In spite of all this, you may notice that I still gave the tablet 4 stars. When the tablet works, it works very well. I've been spoiled by the pressure sensitivity of the Intuos4 for several years now, but the tradeoff of pressure for the ease and boost in productivity I've seen since working on the MSP19 is so worth it. It takes some getting used to if you've never worked with an on-screen tablet, but the learning curve is not steep at all. There is some discrepancy between where the tip of your pen is and where the cursor is on the screen, but you'll encounter this even with Cintiqs and I grew accustomed to it very quickly - just within an hour or two of initial use.

Weight-wise, the monitor has a bit of heft to it, but it's not unmanageable. The adjustable stand in the back is a very nice addition, and I've found that this tablet rests comfortably in my lap if I need to get up close. It's easy to pick up and move around as needed if you don't want to buy the adjustable stand add-on. My only lament is the lack of hotkey buttons, which I hope will be included in future models.

If you're like me and you're agonizing on whether to go with the 10" model or the 19", stop wondering and spring for the 19". It's a third of the price of the newest (and smallest) Cintiq models with highly comparable specs. You have more space to make wide, sweeping gestures, and you will save yourself a lot of pain and hand cramping since you have a ton of real estate to work with.

Despite its shortcomings, I am extremely happy with this tablet and hope to see the company take their success further into the future with better, sleeker, and more responsive models. Wacom could use some healthy competition.

title: Probably should have spent a little more
text:
There's nothing really wrong with this player, in fact there are more web-enabled features than I was expecting, but in hind-sight I wish I had paid a little more and gotten a player with better output options. For instance, this has a HDMI out, but not component out. I like HDMI, but with the stereo system I have now, component would have allowed me more flexibility.
Perhaps I haven't read enough in the options, but even though I'm hard-wired into a router, every time I use Pandora it checks my Internet connection and I have to select 'OK' once it's done checking. I'd rather it just check, then connect me once it determines the connection is good. I also wish there was a favorites area - I listen to Pandora a lot, so would like not to have to scroll over and down every time I want to use it. Also wish there was some indicator as to whether each service is free or not.
All in all, a good player at a good price

title: Not for use with most drives
text:
I purchased this when trying to prepare hard drives for recycling. Out of the 20 drives I had, only one worked with this cable. I assume this is because the power requirements of the drives is not supplied by the cable or the USB 3.1 Gen1 port. The one drive it worked with was the only SSD drive in the group. While this did not suit my needs, the product is cheap and useful in specific cases, hence the 3 stars. The quality is fair, with only minor use at this point. Based on the stiffness of the cable, I suspect it would not survive bends over time. I suggest paying more for a powered device that support more drive types.
Drive that worked: Intel SSD 320 Series 120GB
Dives models that did not work: Seagate Barracuda XT 2TB, Seagate Barracuda 7200.11 1500 GB, WD 1500HLFS Velociraptor.

It came the a shoulder strap and the print is beautiful and vibrant! Now the tough part is to pick one as I ordered 2 different prints. Highly recommend this product!!

title: Great compact book light!!
text: I wanted something compact but strong light output to read by and this one fits the bill perfectly. It folds in half so takes up minimal space and light switch is placed so it will not turn on accidently. Very pleased with this product!!

title: Love it!
text: Extremely well made, folds compact and I can use it for both my cell and 10" tablet.The holder tilts and still stays secure at any angle. The gripper material on the bottom keeps it anchored to the surface!

title: Great !!

text: I absolutely love the pattern and colors!! The cover fits my Fire 10 and offers good protection all around. Just tiny bit on the heavy feel with weight, and later I saw another one by the same company that is an accordian style like I had for my Ipad. Overall a great cover and would recommend it.

title: Five Stars

title: Excellent device for the price
text: Overall, this is an excellent device for the price. I'm no audiophile, but to me the sound is really very good.  It's perfect for the kitchen, where I have it. The one time I took it outside and cranked up the volume, it did great, but I would like to have had a bit more base.

title: Great headset, great price
text: I'm not a gamer and I did not want to spend $150 on a headset, but I did want something functional for zoom meetings, etc. This pair is exactly that. They work great, are lightweight and are very reasonably priced. A bought a second pair for at home and would happily buy another if needed and recommend them to others.

title: I trust Amazon... for now
text: It can be so time consuming to sort through a bunch of different brands of the same product to find one that seems like it's good quality, which reviewers are generally happy with.  I figure if Amazon is willing to stake it's reputation on a product, it will probably be pretty good.  So far, I haven't been disappointed by an Amazon Basics product.

title: I really like the Amazon Basics stuff
text:
Let's see... I plug my device into my tv using this cable, and it works. Ok, then 5 stars.

A little more seriously, I really like the Amazon Basics stuff. They seem to be producing good quality stuff at very reasonable prices.

title: I love it!
text: This is my first non-CRT TV, so I'm really impressed. Looks great, has built in apps and plays movies off my hard drive. The only complaint I have is that the sound quality does not match the video quality. I guess most people connect a sound bar or stereo.

title: Great Kit, Great Price
text: This is a great kit. It has all the parts you need to get started, and they were all of adequate quality. I've been using this kit for about 2 months and have had no problems with any of it. There are three parts in particular that make this kit a great value. 1) The wireless usb, 2) the USB to serial TTL cable and 3) the 2 Amp power supply. These are each about $10 on their own, and are very nice to have when working with the Pi.

title: Flair & function!
text: This is the best cooking pad I’ve purchased. The lights make it cool. No pun!

title: Great value & excellent quality
text: Excellent replacement!  Arrived earlier than expected. Packaged very well.  I recommend this bulb and the seller.  We have enjoyed outdoor movies with this working flawlessly.

text: Excellent case for the speakers.  Nicely made.  A gift for a teenage boy - holding up quite well after months of use.  Goes to the beach, parks, pool.
