text:
Well made - much better quality than the band that came with the camera.

Definately recommemd

title: To stream the impossible unreachable stream
text: Needed to stream high speed real time gaming data multiple interior and external walls composed of multiple materials that pervious extenders failed miserably at. Add to that multiple devices and operating systems. Excellently consistent performance.

title: Puffer - new and improved!!
text: Broke my first Puffer - this replacement is an even better design.  Love the fact that I an shoot inside, close up with the pop up flash.  I highly recommend.

title: Works Great
text: We got this remote after one of our dogs decided to eat our old one, and this one works exactly like the original so I am very happy with the purchase. I just looked up the number on the old remote and this matched so I got this one and it's perfect.

title: Love This
text:
Since I just got a new MacBook it made sense to get a package of items to help protect it. I really like the color of this, plus how easy it was to install. The only thing I ended up not using so far is the webcam cover, I haven't decided yet if I am going to.
First up the keyboard cover. I have been so unimpressed with items like this in the past, but my MacBook before this one had such a problem with dust and stuff getting under the keys so I decided it was time to try another cover. This one is fantastic. It stays on the keys even with a lot of typing. It doesn't move at all. I like the texture of the material, it kind of softens the sound of the keys while also being comfortable to type on.
The hard shell of is great, easy to install and very pretty. It has kind of a matte finish to it so it does sometimes get like oil from your fingers on it and making it have little smudge looking things on it, but it is easily cleaned.
I like the protective case, its small, fits the laptop perfectly and I think it gives it good protection as well. Now if if you are looking for a laptop sleeve with storage this is probably not the one for you, I can get a couple of cords in it but that's about it. So if you are looking for something you can slide charging cables, headphones, and the like all in one this isn't going to be that. But if you are looking for something more streamlined then this works great. I like to keep my laptop in the sleeve when I am not using it and it's just in my house because I have dogs and I want to keep it as protected as possible when not in use.
Overall I am really happy with this purchase and I would recommend.

title: Easy to Use
text: This is my third pencil type I have gotten for my iPad and this is probably a middle of the road one for me. It starts up just as easy as all the others, although I have to say I like the tap feature at the top of the pencil to turn it off and on easily as to not drain the battery. As for the writing elements, I would say that it is pretty accurate, and it writes smooth on the glass, but the actual implement is very slick, so it makes it harder for more precision writing or if you are using the iPad for anything art related, if you are using it for simply writing I would say this works great and it work it for the price.

title: Super Cute
text: I love these stickers, they are really adorable. I like that there is a wide variety of types of animals in this pack. There are a good amount of stickers for the price and they are of pretty good quality as well.

title: Needs Stronger Magnets
text: I like the brush on this to help with keeping my keyboard clean, and I also really like the pad used for wiping down the screen. My biggest issue with this is that the magnets that hold the detachable piece in place isn't exactly strong enough and it easily falls apart without any kind of effort. So if I am using it to wipe down the screen then I need to make sure I am physically holding the detachable part in place while I use it so it stays together, which is kind of annoying. Other than that it's great for maintenance cleaning, not so much for deep cleaning.

title: Love this Tablet
text: I love this tablet for reading book, I’ve been using earlier versions of this kindle for years and this is a great addition.

title: Love the keyboard
text: I like the design of the cover a lot. I also really like the keyboard, that it detaches from the case so I can place the keyboard wherever I want when I use it. It’s also very lightweight and I like the amount of pressure it takes for the keys. I feel like overall it does a good job protecting my iPad and I’m very happy with the purchase.

title: Love the Design
text: This is a super cute design and I really like how well it protects my kindle. I’m happy with the purchase.

title: Works
text: I don’t have a ton to say about this protector. Like most protectors it’s not the easiest to apply perfectly. I bought it to help with a screen that cracked until I got a replacement. It got the job done. I probably wouldn’t use if it hadn’t been for the crack.

title: I like it
text: I like most of things to be wireless, and I really like this mouse because I have yet to have an issue with the bluetooth connection. I will say that you do have to push a bit harder to click the mouse than I am normally used to, but it's negligible and ultimately didn't bother me. I like the lights on it, and the side of the mouse works great for me (although it's a bit small for someone with big hands). I would buy again.

title: Pleasantly Surprised
text: I have to say I’m always nervous about Bluetooth devices, I hate when things disconnect easily. So far I haven’t had that happen once. It was literally just plug and play. The next thing I was worried about was that it’s rechargeable through light, I have to admit I didn’t buy it. I couldn’t believe that this sucker would stay charged because I had the light on or had open blinds. But honestly so far I’ve never had a problem. So far I’m very pleasantly surprised. I also like the low profile keys, you don’t have to use a lot of force to push the keys and it feels really comfortable for both my fingers and my hands/wrists.

title: Super Easy to Use
text: My husband loses his keys more than any person I have ever met, so we got him an AirTag and it has solves all his issues with his keys thanks to this keychain. It was super easy to put together with the AirTag and it's very sturdy. It's also very easy to attach to a keychain, literally done in a matter of minutes. I really like these and would recommend.

title: I love it so much
text: I love this thing. I have been using the Fire TV since it first debuted, and I have always loved them. My biggest complaint has always been that  I still need more than one remote, and I am terrible at keeping my remotes in a place where I can find them. I love that this remote is able to sync up to my television and I can now control power and volume without needed the tv remote in addition to the fire remote. I also really like the buttons on the bottom making it easier to pull up certain apps. The device itself is a little smaller than my last model and I like it a lot, super easy to install. I'm very happy with this one, and plan on replacing my old fire TVs with these.

title: Works Well
text: I got this to primarily for my laptop and some of the accessories that come along with that. I like the added USB plugs, which charge decently fast. The cord length on the strip is really good, and I like the quality of the cord, its very strong and unlikely to be damaged or frayed. Happy with the purchase.

title: Easy to Install
text: Super easy to install. I wanted to hide an extension cord for a power strip and honestly the cord itself is almost bordering on too thick for this product. But it does get the job done. I'm happy with the look and how easy it was to install. My only complaint is that wheeled items, like chairs or rolly tables don't go over this product nearly as well as I was expecting. But it works so I'm happy with the purchase.

title: It works okay
text:
So this stuff works alright. It's not fantastic. If you have a really dirty keyboard or think you might have stuff under the key pads or even in the harder the reach crevices between keys you might want to try something else. If you are just looking to clean off an easy layer of dirt then this will get the job done.
I will say the smell is not my favorite and it kind of lingers, and i don't love the feeling it leaves on my hands so I highly recommend washing your hands afterwards.

title: In Love With This Thing
text: I love my iPad, but I have struggled with finding a good case for it. I had a keyboard case before, and really I didn't love it, it was too bulky and when using in the laptop position the iPad would often tip over. So I was looking for something I could really use in multiple positions but that was sturdy and wouldn't tip over. This works so amazing. It has never tipped over no matter the position it's in. I love the keyboard itself, it's nicely made, doesnt make a ton of noise and is just comfortable to use in general. I love the color as well.

title: Great for charging my phone with my laptop
text: This makes charging my phone while I am working on my laptop so much easier. It doesn't charge it quite as fast as it does when it is plugged into the wall, but almost. The length isn't to bad either, it's a nice middle ground.

title: Gets the Job Done
text: We use this for keeping our computers clean, particularly under the keys of our keyboards, and it definitely gets the jobs done.

title: Gets the Job Done
text: Gets the job done, was inexpensive, I have no complaints.

title: Probably my Favorite Alexa Device
text:
We own two of these in our house in addition to a lot of smaller dots. We put one in the kitchen which is great to use for cooking, she tells me about conversions in weight and cups and ounces, can read my recipes, set times, as well as listen to music. It makes cooking in my kitchen so much nicer and easier when I don't have to pick up my phone to google all the time.
My husband also really liked it so he got one for his room to use an alarm clock. It's loud enough to wake him up, and he likes that it can play video news briefs in the morning. Also because the screen is so large he can see the time at a distance. Plus this one machine replaced his old dot and alarm clock, so now he has one instead of two.

title: Well Priced Ram
text: The product was as listed and performed as was described within the description. I would recommend this to anyone who needs ram or replacement ram.

title: Best Headphones I have Ever Owned
text:
I love these headphones, they are easily my favorite. I always worry about these wireless headphones because I tend to be terrible at keeping them in one place, and these are quite pricey so losing one would really be unfortunate. They come with a really nice carrying case, it's a super durable case, thankfully, and I really like that it's easy to put the headphones in it (just drop it in and like a magnet kind of pulls them down). It's super easy to charge, and I really like that when I start using them a little voice comes on and tells me how much battery life is left. The battery life is also pretty impressive, I used them for hours upon hours without the battery running out, so I was pretty impressed by that.
The sound quality on these is amazing. I love how noise cancelling they are, I had my doubts with these being earbuds, that they wouldn't be that good at cancelling out noise, but these are great. I love how loud I can make it without affecting the sound quality.
I would highly recommend these to anyone, as I said these are hands down my favorite earbuds of all time.

title: Great for storing drawings
text: I have a lot of custom drawings in my house, but not all of them are hanging on walls. When they aren’t I wanted them to have a safe place they could be stored, and this works out perfectly. It’s easy to use, and it keeps everything nicely protected. I would buy again.

title: Great for lost keys
text: My husband loses his keys more than any person I know, and after many mornings of frantic searching for his keys leading to a very cranky attitude I bought these. We put one on his key ring and one in his wallet, and we have used it quite a bit since we set it up. It's loud enough to be found easily, and it seriously gets the job done. I really like this.

title: Cute Case
text: I have a padded case that I keep my iPad in, and I also have a snap on keyboard, but unless I'm using the keyboard, I don't have a case on it, and it always makes me nervous. I got this case so that the screen would be more protected from being scratched. Based on the thickness/design of the case I don't think it would be that great for impact protection, but it does a really good job at keeping the screen protected. I also like that you can use the case to keep the iPad upright when you are watching something. And I really like the color as well.

title: Pretty solid headphones
text:
This is my first pair of wireless ear buds, I have had wireless headphone before but never like this. I was a little concerned, and part of the reason I have not gotten a pair earlier, that it would be super easy for me to lose them. I like that these have a nice and easy carrying case, and that there is some sort of magnet thing that makes them kind of snap into position in the case, and that the charger is super easy to use.
As for function, its super easy to pair them with mobile phones and laptops, like a matter of seconds. The sound that comes out of them is pretty good, it's not like high end quality sound, but it is still pretty good. My ears are a little more sensitive than most, so it's not something I could use long term without my ears getting sore, but for an hour or two its perfectly fine. Overall, I'm really happy with these.

title: Best tv I’ve ever owned.
text:
This is easily the best tv I have ever owned. I really thought I owned quality TVs before, but the picture on this thing is just amazing. I don’t think I’ve ever seen picture this sharp in a home tv before (maybe I need to get out more). The tv itself is huge, I don’t know why I thought 65 was smaller than this, but there is almost no clearance in my entertainment center, it barely fit, so make sure you aren’t like me and measure first.
As for the sound quality, it’s really great. For the last few years getting speakers or a sound bar has been on my list of things I want, but with this tv I honestly feel no need.
I will say that it is taking me some time to get used to the app system on this tv, for several years now I have exclusively used amazon fire for everything (cable and apps), I’ve been trying out using the built in App Store that comes with this, but honestly I feel like I might be going back to my fire, but I’m going to give it more time.
Overall, I’m so happy with this television and I would recommend it to anyone.

title: Surprisingly Large backpack, great for my laptop
text: I was mostly just looking for a way to carry my new laptop around so that it would be protected from harm. This backpack without a doubt does that, but it is also shockingly large. It has a lot of different compartments, as well as spaces within the compartments to keep things organized. I really like how much stuff I can fit into this backpack comfortably. It's also very comfortable to wear and carry around. I would highly recommend this for students or anyone who needs to carry around a laptop as well as a lot of other material.

title: Decent
text:
When I got my iPad I wanted to try out a wide variety of stands and mounts. This was one of the ones I wanted to try.
It’s obviously super easy to set up, you just peel the backing of the magnet and stick it on the table and then peel the backing off the white mount piece and stick it on. The main piece is padded so it won’t hurt your tablet. The magnets themselves are pretty strong.
That being said I have a full sized iPad and the weight of the iPad with the magnet makes me nervous. I think it would be probably be fine, unless you were touching and pushing on the iPad while it was mounted, I think that could make it dislodge, I did some experimenting and the more you touch it the less stable the tablet was on the mount. That’s why ultimately I would rather use a stand versus this magnet mount.

title: Lightweight, good power, decent battery
text: My first impression was how light the laptop was compared to my laptop I had that was only a few years old. The speed at which it booted up was very quick, opening programs is very responsive. I have used it to play basic games (oxygen not included is the name of the game) and it ran very smoothly with no hiccups. Graphics work well and are solid for a laptop. I’m not sure how it would work with an MMO type gaming experience. The fingerprint reader never works for me. If this is something you are getting for work and school use I think this would be great, or even for midrange video games. I’m very happy with the laptop.

title: Great case and keyboard
text: I’ve been wanting an iPad for years, but didn’t want to spend the money, so when I got one for my birthday, I knew the first thing I needed was a good case to keep the iPad safe and sound, the keyboard was an added bonus for me. I liked how sturdy the case is, and the keyboard is great, although I have to say it took some time to get used to how small the keyboard actually is, but once I got used to the difference it was great to use. I like that the keyboard lights up, I love how easy it was to hook up to Bluetooth, and it’s super seamless when you open the case, and the battery on this keyboard is fantastic. Overall, I super love this case.

title: Gets the job done
text:
We got this camera so we could check on our dog while we are away from the house. The setup was pretty easy and quick. It comes with a cable to connect it to the Ethernet or you can use the WiFi. My biggest complaint about this camera is the app used for it. The app is what needs work. It’s clunky. Very clunky. Also the instructions on it aren’t great, and the app it seems like the text was written by a non native English speaker.
The two way communication function works, but’s it’s not great. It does cut out intermittently, so we use it primary only for the camera function. I don’t know if I would buy this camera for another room in my house, I would probably want to try another brand with a stronger app.

title: Definitely get the job done but very stiff
text: I wanted this stand for my iPad to use in the kitchen when I was cooking. The stand itself is very easy to assemble, and leaves you a lot of options. There is the stand for desktops/countertops and two pieces you could mount and use in other various places. My biggest issue with this stand is the piece that holds onto the tablet itself. It’s very stiff to try and pull the sides out to fit the tablet into it. It’s not the easiest to remove either. It makes me nervous when I’m trying to put it in or take it out that I’m going to drop the tablet. Overall, I think I would prefer a different stand that didn’t require the pulling stiff latch mechanism and instead maybe something with a ledge.

title: Perfect electronics protector
text:
I think the thing I was most nervous about with buying an iPad was breaking it. So the first thing I did was get a case for it. This one is pretty simple. But it definitely gets the job done. My iPad has another case with a Bluetooth keyboard attached and I was worried it would make it too bulky for it to fit into the sleeve, but it still fits, it’s more of a tight fit but it still works. The only downside is the zipper pocket where I would like to store the charger is pretty tiny and with the iPad in the case it’s basically impossible to get the charger that comes with the iPad to fit in there, if it’s just the cord it would work.
I also got a second one for my laptop and it’s works just as well for that. I always carry my laptop in a bag with cushions for it, but the added sleeve just makes me feel like there is a level of extra protection involved.

title: Good hard case
text:
I just spent a ton on a new MacBook Pro so of course I wanted to protect it as well. I picked this set because I had read a lot about how easy it is to get things under the keys so I wanted something with a keyboard protector. The hard case snaps right on, super easy, and I feel like it does it’s job no problem. The keyboard cover is literally just something you lay on top of the keyboard, I wish it was more secure, literally if I sign to hard the air from my mount will make the keyboard cover flap up. I’m going to be looking for a more secure keyboard option. But in the meantime it is doing its job of keeping things away from the keys.
I normally don’t use screen protectors, they are just such a pain to install and I always end up with a ton of bubbles, I did try with this one, it didn’t work out so I skipped it. Overall it was a good buy, worth the price, I would purchase again.

title: Great utility knife.
text: I have a couple of box cutters in my house and honestly they aren’t pretty flimsy. So I was looking for a knife that was a little more sturdy and I found it in this knife. I love that it folds up and away so I don’t have to worry about accidentally sliding the blade out of the casing like with my box cutters. We get a ton of packages at my house and my city requires cardboard be cut down before recycling so we do a lot of cardboard cut downs, since getting this knife it takes less time and way less effort. Would without a doubt buy this knife again.

title: Great job at cooling my MacBook Pro
text:
I bought this to replace my old cooling pad that broke. I was really happy with this one though, much more than with the old one. I like that this one has buttons and a digital display to control the speed of the fans (my old one had like a dial and no read out). It does a really good job at keeping my laptop cool, and it really isn't too loud, I think this one might be a little bit quieter than my old one.

I did knock off a star because when I took it out of the box the plastic piece with the buttons on it had fallen off, it was super easy to reattach, but I took off a star for that because I'm sure if it falls off that easily I may lose it in the future.

title: Perfect protection for the paperwhite
text: My husband got a paperwhite for Christmas and I knew immediately he was going to need some kind of case or cover. There are a lot of options out there but we picked this one because it looked well made, was the right color, and had a pocket in the front. The pocket easily fits the charge cable. The color is perfect, it looks nice and well made. The material is soft, but fully protective of the paperwhite. This is perfect for our new paperwhite.

title: Great for keeping my MacBookPro cool
text: A while back I bought a laptop desk for my MacBook Pro, and while I loved using it, my laptop would overheat so quickly. So I have been in the market for a cooling pad for a while now. I liked that this one has four fans, that you can control the speed the fans go at, and honestly ever since I have been using it (a few weeks now) my laptop hasn't overheated once. It does take up a USB port, but since I almost never use my USB ports this isn't a problem for me. I will point out that if you want to set it directly in your lap and the pad isn't completely level it does make a bit of a sound that is a bit disconcerting, so I put the pad on the laptop lap desk and then put the laptop on top of that, and it works perfectly. I would easily make this purchase again.

title: Great for TV's
text: My husband and I loved the price of this, and I was beyond excited to get my TV off of the dresser in our master bedroom, plus we planned on running all the wires behind the wall, and I have to say this worked out great. The instructions could be written a little bit more clearly, but in general this was a pretty easy install and it looks great in the bedroom. I do wish they would include a few extras of the hardware, we had an issue with one of the drywall anchors included, but thankfully we found some extras we had from another project.

title: Pretty Good Cleaner
text: I bought this for my laptop key board, and it worked pretty well. It's not a miracle goo by any means though, it doesn't get rid of everything. But in general it works pretty well especially at getting rid of the little stuff that gets stuck in between keys.

title: Great for people who love Apple
text: I bought this because my husband I both have a lot of apple products between the two of us and we are constantly fighting over chargers, this totally solves that problem.

title: Label Tape
text: I am a huge fan of my label maker, I could label everything if my husband would let me. I like this label tape because it's clean looking and the back is very easy to peel off while having great staying power.

title: Perfect for Military
text: We bought this so my husband could use it as a CAC card reader and could access his email at home as well as do the army correspondence classes from home. It was super easy to use and install, and now my husband can do what he needs to from home without having to stay late at work, a win win all around.

title: Audio very poor
text: It worked for only a week and then the following week, the audio started going in and out. Goes high and low. So its very disappointing.

title: Too much echo
text: Ugh too much echoe and I tried everything  to fix it. Waste of $

text: Unfortunately, it already took long to receive it but upon opening it, one of them had a cracked, like it was bent. VERY disappointed. UGH!!!

title: Not user friendly
text: It was too technical for my teen and just not what we expected when using it.

title: Looks cheap
text: When I got it, it definitely did not look like an authentic bag. It was really thin and not as thick as the other ones I bought from other sellers. Disappointed! Be careful everyone!

title: Handy little things
text: These clips word so well in running my cable along the wall nice and neat.

title: Great little dvd player

title: good functionality, sound is pretty good
text:
First of all, these work great for me. The design of the silicone flange is a little different from anything I've had before - they sit down into the ear canal, connect at a slightly deeper point. This seems to make a positive difference for me.

The sound is good enough. Not like OMG audiophile - I have the big Sony earmuffs that sound better than these, and some old corded AT's that sound better than the Sonys. And I've used some in a recording studio that had more detail and dimension than anything I've heard before or since. These are a long way off from that. But they are plenty good enough. There is nothing that catches my attention or causes fatigue or makes you want to apply corrective EQ to the source.

These are comfortable. The most comfortable earbuds I've ever had. I sleep in them.

Noise cancelling is like any ANC - good against some noise, less so with other things.

I've never run the batteries all the way down - IDK how long they last.

My one actual annoyance with these is the interface - I always touch the left bud by accident and switch into a mode I don't want. I would prefer it if there was a config utility or something to disable that touch gesture and leave it in ANC full time.

title: Amazing, instant improvement. So glad I got this as my first color management kit.
text:
Wow this made a huge difference. I use the Passport as intended, with the X-Rite plugin for Lightroom. So far I have only created one profile for each body/lens combo - I'm still fuzzy on whether more is needed.

I do like the variety of neutral squares on the Passport for white balance; OTOH I prefer to carry a WhiBal card in my wallet when I'm mobile - it's more portable. I wish the Passport was as small and portable and durable as the WhiBal card so I could carry it literally everywhere with no complication. I know the Passport is smallish - I try to ride a bicycle everywhere I can, and every bit of bulk and weight counts.

I didn't install any software from the included disk. I downloaded DisplayCal instead. I'm also a little shaky on the basics of that software; I simply downloaded and did the dummy/wizard calibration.

Between calibrating my display and profiling my cameras/lenses, I feel like a great amount of friction has been removed from my workflow. I used to spend too much time fixing color casts and toning images. Ironically, given the extra steps involved, now selection and editing goes much faster. To be fair, I updated my desktop box just a week before I got the X-Rite bundle, so LR/PS respond a lot snappier at the same time - that has to be part of my perceived change.

I would recommend this package for anyone. I wouldn't go any lower on the scale - the CMDisplay is the right one to get if you don't want to spend on the i1DPro (which I read has the same sensor?). You can get the CMDisplay and even a Passport used on eBay for *slightly* less money - not much. I was uncertain about how licensing works for this stuff so I just bought this bundle. If you consider what it costs to buy the CMDisplay on its own, the Passport is nicely discounted in this bundle.

IDK what is the difference between this and the newer version. It's hard to imagine getting significantly better results - at least at my current skill level and consort of gear.

title: most sensible tripod for me
text:
doesn't feel high end but doesn't feel cheap, either. comes with a head that is perfect size for the small sony cameras i'm using nowadays. the head is smooth enough. that's my overall feeling about this tripod: everything about it is plenty good enough.

i carry this on my bicycles and it transports well. first of all, it's almost the exact same weight as my schmancy carbon fiber tripod - which is bigger, but i was surprised by the reasonable weight of the Dolica.

mechanics are solid. all telescoping segments slide easily enough, twist locks function properly, head works well. the screw on the head is finely threaded to let you get the amount of resistance you want for adjusting the camera orientation. the legs are easy to lock pointing down. i've only ever used the notches for a narrow base, so i can't speak to using the other notches

there is a bubble level on the tripod, which i want to say is hard to see with my cameras on the tripod - can't remember because i don't use it. i used to use in-camera level and now i just use my eyes. anyway, it's there if you want it

for me this tripod represents the right kind of compromise. i do art as a part-time hobby. i like nice optics, and everything else really just needs to be good enough. this tripod does not radiate the aura of high-end engineering, manufacturing, and materials; it simply conveys good sense. this tripod is easy to use, easy to transport, and easy to throw in a dumpster if it got run over - i.e. i have no psychological attachment to it because of preciousness/expense like i do with nice lenses or overpriced/cutting edge cameras. this tripod is like a good pair of shoes that feel great and can go anywhere

title: best i've found so far, but misplaced keys really degrades it
text:
The comprehensive video review is spot-on. This is a GREAT keyboard. I shopped a lot for one and the others seems to have many obvious drawbacks, while this one just has two ergonomic flaws, both noted in that video. They are: right SHIFT is waaaay too small and misplaced, and the number row is misplaced.

So far I'm adapting, but I haven't gotten there yet. I''m about 40% on hitting the right shift. At present when I need the number row, all composition comes to a halt and my full attention goes into finding the key I want. Typing with this keyboard still has a ways to go before it feels transparent. That's a real bummer. I should take off two stars for that, but I'm trying to rate this keyboard against others, in which case it should almost be 5 stars.

If they fixed those two ergo problems I'd give it an enthusiastic five stars. If there is a new version with these problems fixed, I will buy it, which is very unusual for me - i generally make my decision and stick with it, trying to be a thrifty non-consumer. In this case I would do what I have to do to upgrade.

Overall the keyboard is perfectly sized and well built. I carry it with cash and a credit card inside a ziploc bag in my cycling jersey. Some things - especially consumer electronics - get quickly worn out in this environment, but the 1byone keyboard seems to take it, no problem.

title: very nice for what it is. a little off the mark for me personally
text:
displays power as a raw number, but doesn't record it to a FIT file. I/O is less than ideal. I'd say it would be fine for someone without a power meter who doesn't need a lot of inter-connectivity with the outside world. I could make a go of training myself or coaching someone with just this computer and a HRM, but by the time i got to this point i already had much more capable gear.

you can do as well with most fitness watches nowadays - especially garmin, which mostly have cycling modes. and all the watches have easy/effortless avenues for data to reach analytic services, e.g. garmin, trainingpeaks, strava, etc...

if pyle could write power data to the file and make it easier to move data to other services, it would be an easy five stars. as it is i don't know anybody for whom i would recommend this computer. i'm sure it works for some people, just nobody i know.

i looked at this for my wife but returned it when i saw how hard it was going to be to get her data out. i returned the pyle and gave her my old edge 520 and got the edge 820 for myself. that's overkill, but there's not much in between. i'm especially disappointed about how much i spent since my wife finally agreed to get a garmin watch with cycling mode, so she doesn't even need the head unit now.

i really wish there was more space filled in between the high end garmin stuff and the entry level. this computer is really close to being good enough for me, but it lacks key abilities. here's what it would need to work for me personally:
standard file format - e.g. FIT, gpx, whatever.
easy access to data - even just as files on a drive via USB - i can automate data transfer from there
write power data to file
option to display zones and percentages for all data

that's all i would need from a barebones head unit for my own training and riding

title: Picture quality is great, but causes an echo during videoconferences.
text:
I've had this camera a few months. The install went pretty well. I had to reboot a few times to pick the camera up, but once it was recognized, that has worked well. The camera does not clamp securely onto my external monitor. I fixed that problem by getting a separate flexible arm that clamps onto my desk and holds the camara. I love the physical lens cover so I can easily control when the camera is capturing an image. The picture quality is great. I love having an external camera instead of relying on the one on my laptop so my laptop can stay connected to the docking station and I don't have to try to get it moved over to the center of my desk every time I have a videoconference. Unfortnately there there are two remaining problems that are making me now decide to look for another camera:

1. Echos: When using this camera, is it causes an echo on videoconferencing that others can hear. I cannot hear it. It is so annoying to others that immediately people start talking about it and asking if the call can be done using some other audio. It definitely happens on Microsoft Teams calls as others have said in the Questions section for this product on Amazon. I can't remember if it happened on Webex videocalls also. Others have said switching the audio source solves that problem.

2. Wide View: This may be standard on these cameras. I'll find out when I shop for a new one, but the view is much wider than my native laptop camera. I can't find any way on the camera to "crop" it so that it shows only the person during videoconference and not a lot of what is to the right and left of the person. I solved that problem by installing OBS Studio and the OBS virtual camera. OBS allows me to crop the picture and then uses that video as the "camera" in Microsoft Teams. That works very well to get a good cropped video, however, the image quality went way down and it freezes up sometimes, so it is not a great solution because I end up not having smooth starts to videoconferences with all the troubleshooting I have to do to get OBS, the webcam, and the conferecing software to all work together.

I hope I can find a camera that works seemlessly so that the now much more frequent videoconferences, thanks to the pandemic, will go more smoothly.

title: Works great! We feel safer knowing who’s coming and going.
text:
FYI You don’t have to hardwire it. Ring sells a Plug-in Mount for Floodlight Cams which allows you to connect it to an outlet. Easy peasy.

We love having this. It provides peace of mind as the thieves seem to be getting more numerous and bolder & bolder. Recently, using the speaker function, I was able to question/chase away some Dude who was literally dumpster diving in our neighbor’s big trash bin. He wasn’t just picking up roadside discards. With identity theft so prevalent, I worried he was looking for personal information. I was able to challenge him while safe inside our house. I said I was calling the police and he quickly left. I wouldn’t have felt safe going outside to confront him.

I love that the notifications come on my Apple Watch. So easy & convenient since I don’t tend to carry my iPhone on me.

The floodlight camera is also great for knowing when/where packages have been delivered so one can retrieve them before the porch pirates grab them.

However, the greatest pleasure is seeing all the critters who come through at night. Before the floodlight camera, who knew? One night there was even a pair of coyotes! Cool!

I want to add one in the back but the price has gone up by $30! Guess I’ll see if the price comes back down. With the price of gas & everything else going up so much, the budget’s getting slammed. Sigh.

title: Disappointing product and customer service
text: I see from other reviews, that having this arrive in a plastic tube, compressed and totally out of shape, is par for the course.  Mine, after escaping the tube and sitting for 24 hours, was hardly recognizable as what I ordered.  I sent an email plus pictures to Ontel.  No response.  I went to the website and used the contact information to write my complaint - with pictures.  No response.  I got a message from Amazon asking if my communication with the manufacturer had resolved my problem.  I replied "no".  So, I called Ontel again, got help after a short wait, explained my problem (which she had probably heard many times before) and I was cut off.  Now, I'm getting a bit testy, but as I looked at the blue blob that arrived, totally unusable, I decided, one more try.  I got a very nice lady, who very quickly referred to "her manual", and said that the blob plus a damp towel on LOW in the dryer would bring out the shape in the pictures.  After three sessions of an hour or so each, I, at last have something that  looks like a very wrinkled version of what is pictured.  I give up.  It will hold a book and my IPad, and it's soft and very lightweight, so it will fill the bill.  If you are planning to purchase one, don't forget - damp towel and into the dryer on low for as many sessions as it will take to get a good shape.
