title: While it does most of what they advertise the BT connectivity is really poor unless you hold the phone in a stationary visible .
text:
I've recently purchased this BT headset and the first thing I did was install the latest firmware due to the reviews I've read. While it does most of what they advertise the BT connectivity is really poor unless you hold the phone in a stationary visible position from your phone or while it's stationary on a table. If you put it in your pocket or even in your hand with a normal hand swing the sound stutters and is not worth using. I've purchased a 60 dollar pair of similar BT ear buds without all the extra features but it sure does work reliably in a way you would expect any headset to work. I've written their technical support for assistance and this is what they told me after a few emails back and forth explaining my issue and running their tests. Here is their final reply, I didn't put in the agents name as to not hold the agent responsible directly for this issue.

(Bragi)
Apr 5, 10:26 CEST
Hello Derek

Thanks for getting back to us with the results of your test.

I understand The Black Dash has some issues when being connected to an external device via Bluetooth, specifically when using it outside. In certain cases we have had a few customers who experienced similar issues like you. As you performed the range test and got a positive result, we can confidently say that your unit's Bluetooth hardware is generally working correctly.

Nonetheless, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts. Bluetooth, in general is a technology that offers us the possibility to pair The Black Dash to many different devices, due to the technology's widespread usage. Never the less, it is also a technology that comes with disadvantages. One of those is the actual dependency of the surroundings as you discovered already. That actually means that Bluetooth works very well in closed surroundings where you have surfaces that reflect the Bluetooth signals. However, when being outside with no walls at all, the Bluetooth range very much varies. Having your external device in your right side pockets, your The Black Dash should work independently from the outside surroundings.

Again, this is not an excuse for your Bluetooth dropouts, but rather an explanation for this behavior. Furthermore, we are doing our best to regulate Bluetooth performance with our firmware settings, and every update should actually improve Bluetooth performance.
We hope you can understand that.

All the best,
(Agent name)& your Team Bragi​​​​​​

title: Defective product
text:
I bought the lighted leather cover with my Kindle in October 2010. That first cover was defective right out of the box, with the light flickering on and off. When it was working, the light would go out every time you turned a page. VERY disappointing for the price. The cover itself looks great and protects the Kindle, but the light is junk. I contacted Amazon and they sent a replacement with no arguments. The light on the replacement cover seemed to work ok for several uses so I thought I was good to go. The light was not used for a couple months. The next time I wanted to use it, it was completely dead and no amount of fiddling helped. I contacted Amazon and was told it was past the return period, but I could get a replacement under the one year warranty. After explaining that this was my SECOND cover and I felt that another replacement would produce the same results, they agreed to take it back and give me a full refund. I was pleasantly suprised that I didn't have to argue. Even though the cover is not worth a penny, Amazon (as always) is a class act when it comes to customer satisfaction!

Update: I was not given the full refund as promised by the Amazon rep. They charged me 15% on the return. grrrrrrrrr

title: Nice looking, but not so handy
text:
It looks like the designers wanted a very nice looking case, regardless its usefulness.

This carrying case looks really nice, the woven nylon has a catchy texture. It fits perfectly the MacBook Pro Unibody (even with a hard shell mounted, although it will become a little tight).

It has also a couple of pouches, but they are not so useful because they are too tight to allow the storage of something more than a few DVDs and a few memory sticks.

If you really need it, you can carry the AC adapter in it, but it's a very tight fit, not so easy to handle and not so nice to see (the puch will look a bit too "stretched" and you will have a problem to overlap the velcro bands). Without the hardshell munted on the Mac, everything would fit a little better, but the adapter is quite big for that pouch.

The removable shoulder strap looks stylish and it is very confortable. The shoulder pad is just a bit oversized IMHO, while the straps are a bit too long even adjusted at their minimum lenght.

Without the shoulder strap you will miss a simple handle to carry it, because its size is not so little to be handled easily without some sort of handle.

Overall it is very nice looking, well finished, quite sturdy and will give a good protection to your loved mac... with plenty of style. I would just like to find a thinner AC Adapter for my MBPu :-)

title: Get the MOST from LG C1 as PC monitor
text:
OLED has the best picture quality. For me, the best thing that happened to Video repro so far. Didnt go with QLED bc of the poor picture quality vs OLED. Black is truly black.

That being said, how to get the most out of OLED as a PC monitor?

Download the following apps:
1. Autohidedesktop icons (self explanatory)
2. Powertoys (allows you to take advantage of the massive screen by splitting up your windows into whatever sections you want. Then you can simply drag and snap each into place.
3. Autohidemousecursor (self explanatory)

In addition. Have a black background so when your mouse and icons disappear, your monitor essentially "turns off. " Also a minimal screen saver in case your on a program and it stays idle.

There are some additional options on the LG TV options such as screen shift. As a safety precaution run pixel cleaner once a week.

All these precautions should prevent any burn-in. 4 Months so far and no issues at all. These "hassles" are worth it. Your video and gaming experience will be markedly improved.

title: Switchers keep failing?
text:
All these hdmi switches are of similar quality. I have had to buy 3 or 4 of these types of products because there is no real practical alternative.

Why 3 or 4? Usually they broke down within a month if not sooner. Sometimes out of the box. Ive had this for about 4 months now and no major issues. The minor issue is sometimes it doesnt sync properly. Powering it off and on usually takes care of it. The problem may get worse as time goes on. But will see.

If you are wondering why they fail so frequently and quickly is because of the bad power supplies they are packaged with. Power supplies are critical. Yet they are the likely parts to get skimped bc they tend to be more expensive relative to other components.

So I replaced all of my power supplies with high quality power supplies the past year and havent had any issues or breakdown since doing so. You also get other great benefits that come along with it- increase in power efficiency, audio and video quality and best of all not going through the hassle of returning/trashing and rebuying these electronic accessories every month.

title: It works
text:
Like some people here when I first tried this, picture kept flickering in and out and would not lock in when changing games. I had to power cycle, etc... But its all resolved. now.

Here is what I did:

1) Yes you have to spend 10 bucks to buy an 8k Cable. That will make the signal stable and you wont get the full-on static on screen.

2) Update FW. Apparent to me was not up to date when I had to power cycle. Contact Club 3d. Dont know why they dont have the firmware readily available, but this is what you have to do. They are quite prompt- one business day. Turns out my device had o.g. fw.

TIP: if driver doesnt show up in device manager under USB, try switching USB port. That worked for me.

Is it worth it? Its a no brainer because OLED is worth it. OLED is the best thing to happen to AV for movies, videos and gaming. Upgrading at this time to 3080s or 90s not worth it for performance gains FAR exceeding reasonable price levels, especially if you already have a 2080ti like me. This will last me a long time. At least until the next set of graphics cards come out. I dont plan to go to 3080 anytime soon unless I happen to get a base level 3080 at retail price or lower. Even then Ill probably wait for next gen.

Should they have FW on their website? Probably. Could it be cheaper? Dont think so. This isnt a big market. Very niche market. A little troublesome to get it working but it is tech and Im very glad this exists.

title: Something to consider
text:
Not a criticism of the particular product but of the grounding mechanism.

Beware of grounding mats. Long term use may cause discomfort, pain and even damage. It should be okay to use briefly, but not for any extended period of time.

This is due to the way energy circulates through the body. Extended use causes the gathering and accumulation of energy in certain areas. This is rarely discussed and relatively unknown to most people.

Another thing to consider- you are plugging yourself into your house's electrical grounding system. You have to make sure your house is properly grounded. Youd be surprised that some may not be. If you are in a building its even worse. Also, all sorts of pollutants travel through the grounding path. It doesnt travel just one way.

Grounding is more complicated than it appears so be aware. There are other ways to do it but its not as easy as just plugging yourself in I suppose. Hence the allure of these mats

title: WD GET YOUR ACT TOGETHER
text:
I originally bought a WD 2tb NVME to use as my main OS, but it would not migrate/clone properly even with their own software. I downloaded a 3rd party migration/cloning software and that didnt work either. I tried nearly everything I could for 1.5 days! I even tried backing up/restoring manually and then repairing. Nothing worked. It was a complete waste of time. I didnt even learn anything in the process other than learning that I should go with a company that has a readily available comprehensive solution that doesn't needlessly waste your valuable time. 1.5 days down the drain.

So I ended up migrating my Samsung 1tb NVME to a new Samsung 2tb NVME and it couldnt have been any easier. < 15 minutes, very quick! I previously, migrated from a corsair SSD to Samsung 1tb NVME (when i couldnt get another SSD to migrate properly), and that was flawless as well. Why didnt I initially go with the Samsung 2tb instead of WD? Press had positive news about it. I am not a fanboy so I like to try different solutions. That was a mistake. What's apparent to me after this experience is that Samsung is better than all their competitors at providing a comprehensive package of the best hardware and software. The experience is FLAWLESS. I havent had any issues with any of their storage solutions to date.

Why did I bother writing this review? Because I wasted 1.5 days. Something has to come out of it. Maybe itll help someone or maybe WD will get their act together and work on their cloning/migration software because the hardware seems to be fantastic.

Disclosure, I bought and paid for everything myself and I still own HDs/SSDs/MicroSds by WD (only old HDs), Sandisk (microsds, ssds), Seagate (HD), Samsung (SSDs, Micro SDs and NVMEs).

title: Additional things to consider
text:
UPDATE 9/5/21 Still Five Stars. Operating flawlessly. No weird startup/freeze issues. I upgraded my cpu to i9 9900k and GPU to 3080 FTW3. Im likely bottlenecked at the CPU level, but ill take care of this later.

UPDATE 10/19/2021 4 to 5 stars after using for 2 years:

CPU had random starting issues for a long time. as I initially wrote.. I never updated my bios since there wasnt any major updates. Then one day it stopped working. F7 error. I was perplexed. So I updated my bios directly through the motherboard. A bit of a hassle, took about an hour or two to get it figured out and reset. Its has been working flawlessly for 2 months now. OS actually starts and loads a bit faster without any weird startup issues. In any case, really enjoy this motherboard. So definitely recommend getting it. Just update it and make sure you have backup BIOS on the other 2 slots since the working one can get corrupted for whatever reason.

Without adding to what others have said, I will say this is the great sounding motherboard. Assuming you dont use the internal DAC and just use the SPIDF output cable to an external DAC you will get very good results. Dont bother wasting money on external sound cards. That being said, the internal DAC is passable[for non-serious listening], but thats besides the point. This motherboard isnt made for audio. However, its apparent they use quality parts on the motherboard.

There are some negatives to this motherboard, and I dont know if its just because I bought mine from AMZN warehouse, which is supposed to be LIKE NEW, or because its how it is generally, but it gets a bit temperamental sometimes, and wont start right away. The bios boots, resets, multiples times before it gets to windows. Sometimes it doesnt boot right away. Ive checked against my other parts as well and they are fine. However, this only happens very rarely. Ive had this two months or so and maybe 4 times?

The other negative is the cheap I/O shield. They need to do something about this one. It may have something to do with the fact that it makes it easier to adjust to different cases. However, it is really cheap...

title: Pros and Cons
text:
Pros: Cheap price, handles 4 inputs (would love to see more). One of the [very few inexpensive options] to extract and output a pure digital audio signal (coaxial) rather than the lossier and worse standard- optical. Basically does what it is supposed to do, which is rare these days. Remote control functionality works fine.

Cons: Cheap. Input/output ports are made out of cheap stuff. Need to tweak a little to get the most out of it. Spacing is tight like a manhattan studio. The unit is lightweight and small so it shifts around when you have big cables. Sometimes it gets lost and doesn't do what it is supposed to do- switch. In which case you just have to restart, but it doesn't happen very often. Check video connection if there is an issue as well, which may prevent from switching.

Putting it together: All that being said, its great at this price doing what it is supposed to do, which is hard to say these days with all the ill manufactured things these days. There is nothing out there that will do what it does- 4 x switch PLUS outputting audio via digital coax. At this price point its great for people who dont really care about maximizing the quality of their output. For those who do, like me, not the best but its the only option at this point. Id be more than glad to pay a bit more for a unit with quality input/output ports with a more substantial case. Seems manufacturers these days think all people want are cheap products. There are enough people out there who would pay a bit more for a more quality product. They should consider a two tier product lineup- and not just for the functions. Since there is room for improvement, it gets 4 stars. Make some changes- Ill buy it, and assuming it works, it gets 5 stars.

UPDATE: down to 3 stars. Right at the 30 day mark, the one feature that differentiated this product from others- coax output, stopped working. I did get it replaced and it works. This is somewhat expected, given the quality of material used and the price paid for something like this. Another 30 days and this gets thrown out with the trash for good. At least Amazon has a great policy to protect against something like this. So its worth a shot if you need these features.

UPDATE 2: 2nd time it malfunctioned within a month. Video stopped outputting. When it works, its fine. They really need to use more quality parts in this to make it last. Raise the price a few bucks if necessary. The parts themselves dont cost much. Too much penny pinching. This is getting ridiculous.

UPDATE 3: really save yourself the hassle, frustration and money. Get a pro hdmi switcher. It costs more BUT the output quality and just as important, build quality, is much better. After switching over to a pro, I havent had a hardware issue in 3 months.

title: Great performance
text:
EVGA ftw3 version runs super quiet. Can barely hear it run. At highest settings @ 6880 x 1440 resolution, it never runs hotter than 65c. As to whether 2080ti is worth it in general:

Increase in FPS performance- Too many people judge the 2080ti's merit on raw FPS numbers, saying its only x amount of percent greater in performance than the 1080ti. so its not worth it. But what they completely miss is that its not just about the raw numbers. Its about how those numbers translate into the EXPERIENCE of adding/using that component. The performance of the 2080ti is so much smoother, more effortless and frustration free, than the previous generation, that it was worth it for me to make the change.

Alernative Sli option- I tried 1080ti sli for about a month, it didnt affect the quality of my experience in a meaningful way. The presentation is still jittery and stuttering , making for a distracting experience. Support for SLI is inconsistent and it demands more power and space, creates alot more heat and noise. You can clearly see the poor quality of performance in side by side comparisons on youtube. Judge for yourself. Again, its not all about the FPS. A perfect analogy would be to cars- most high end races cars have respectable 0-60 mph speeds, but the experience and qualty of performance arent the same.

Price argument: Just because its expensive and someone cant afford it doesnt mean its a 1 star product. Check the quality, time and effort the reviewer put into the review and judge for yourself. It takes money, time and expensive R&D to make products such as these. Im not going to argue that its not expensive. It is. But consider that it beats two 1080ti SLI in quality of performance, then you realize it isnt. If you are salty that you cant afford it, try skipping some meals and dropping some vices and prioritize things differently. Seems everyone wants free things these days. I wonder if they would work without compensation.

Conclusion: Sure its expensive, but if you can afford it and you want quality performance, not just eye popping FPS numbers, which can be meaningless, get the 2080ti. Some just cant see the difference and thats fine. But for those who can afford it and have more discerning eyes, the upgrade is a must. My only complaint? It cant make poorly coded, inefficient games like Kingdom Come run better at the highest settings on a 6880 x 1440 setup. (Runs nearly every other game at the highest setting flawlessly at these high resolutions) Might have to wait for the next generation for that. Because of that and the "high" price it doesn't get a top recommendation but a very high recommendation.

title: Effortless performance
text:
Just a phenomenal cpu. This is probably the best upgrade Ive done, coming from an i7 7700k. I had 30 days to use and figure out if I wanted to stay with this or go with the latest AMD cpu.

Work- I used to have trouble running programs that were either too complex or inefficiently coded that it led to stutters, hitches, delays or freezes. One program that always caused massive trouble for me over the years was the Think or Swim trading platform. I originally upgraded to the i7 7700k and it could not handle more than 2-3 chart at a time running the time and sales and L2. Run some side charts and you could forget about trading, especially at the open when calculations need to be run at an extremely rapid pace. I even added a total of 32gb ddr4 3400 ram and it still wouldnt run properly. Arguably, the program is encoded really inefficiently requiring much more from the CPU than necessary. Ive tried many different trading programs and this one caused the most trouble. After stepping up to the i9 9900k I can now run this inefficiently encoded program on my main chart screen, with two different tickers having 4 different time frames each with its own L2 and time and sales, PLUS 15 side charts without a hitch! Also im running my browser with at least 5 tabs open and video/audio running. Absolutely amazing. I never thought I could get it to work like this.

Gaming- even if the cpu doesnt run at 100 pct it affects the quality of the experience of the gameplay, especially for demanding games, or just poorly coded, inefficient ones. RPGs fall into these categories. I.e., Kingdom Come Deliverance. Video and streaming is flawless as well.

Vs AMD- Performance isnt always about raw numbers, if there are too many peaks and valleys, it affects the quality of the experience. I havent personally compared it directly to the newest AMD cpu, but having looked at the side by side comparisons, AMD cpu seems to put out better numbers for work-related applications, but clearly on the gaming side, intel is superior. From my observation, the quality of the experience with Intel was greater because the frame rate was consistent with much less, if any micro stuttering, which you can see with the AMD chips. As a result, Intel's presentation was more effortless and smooth. With the AMD setup, you can see some graying/discoloring/hazy effects in demanding scenes. It seems like AMD is an overcharged chip that experiences these dips because of that, causing a deterioration in the experience. AMD is perfectly fine for work I presume, but not for me when it comes to gaming. Intel performs like a more refined, polished product. This is just based on my personal observation of their performance in these two different areas.

Overclocking- its perfectly fine using it the way it is. No need to overclock, but of course you can overclock it. I run mine 16 hours a day without any problems. Top recommendation at the asking price these days.

title: Really nice tablet, with a bit of room for improvement. (Now QUITE a bit of room for improvement)
text:
I love this tablet and, if it weren't for the battery life and how long it takes to recharge, I would give it 5 stars. The tablet itself is beautiful, thin, lightweight and works beautifully. I have had mine since the beginning of September 2014, and I have only had to reboot it twice since then (due to errors, I mean). The display is beautiful. The sound is quite good, for a tablet. And now that Samsung has allowed it to upgrade to Lollipop, I can run most of my new apps from my 32 gb SD Card and this leaves me a lot less nervous about running out of memory. Though, I still find the 16 GB HD a bit on the tight side overall.

My previous tablet was a Toshiba Excite AT305T16. It was my first tablet, but I still could tell how slow it was. And it constantly needed to be rebooted. Everything kept getting bound up on it. Not so with this Samsung. It is quick, it stays fresh, and it just plain performs. Which is all we ask for, right? I will be buying more Samsung products in the future, I think. Those guys really know and deliver quality. Now, if they could just improve the battery and be a bit more generous with the on-board memory.

UPDATE: I have downgraded my review by one star. I have owned this tablet since August of 2014. And, although I still enjoy it, I am now running out of memory and, even though I have a 64gb sd card attached, I am finding it increasingly challenging and frustrating to manage the remaining space. While many of the apps can be moved to the SD card, most of them can't. And the apps themselves are becoming larger and larger overall. And, to make matters worse, suddenly, I can no longer update many of my apps residing on the SD card, unless I move them back to the internal storage first. This is too laborious and time consuming and I haven't found a fix for it yet. Also, suddenly I can no longer move PDF files onto the SD card either. Other types of files can be moved as before, but not the PDF files. Wondering if the tablet performed some sort of automatic system upgrade that may have triggered these issues. When I "upgraded" (and I use that term lightly, with tongue in cheek) from Kitkat to Lollipop, the tablet lost some very useful functions. So now I have to wonder why these problems are suddenly cropping up?

title: Bad on me.
text:
I can't believe I actually forked out $449.00 for this product. It lasted about a year before I began having problems with the battery. It would go into a mode where it looks like the battery was empty, but you could still charge it. But it would still indicate empty. So I had to guess when and how long to charge it to maintain power. Then, somehow, after a few weeks of being in this mode, suddenly it "got well" again and the battery would show its charge and charge correctly for a few months. Then it had another "breakdown" and started the false battery routine again. This time, when it was in this mode, it would power on immediately when the power button was depressed even slightly. No vibration at startup like it would do when it was working properly. It stayed in this mode for a few weeks again and then suddenly, for no conceivable reason, it powered on normally one day, with the vibration and the battery was showing healthy again. This battery game went on for another 2 arbitrary "cycles", until this last time which happened over 2 months ago now. It would add something extra to the decay each time. This last time, I now have a tablet that powers on at the least touch of the on/off button, IF the power cord is plugged in. It will not charge at all anymore. I even reset it to factory settings this time and no-go.

As another reviewer has stated: "How absolutely idiotic for Toshiba to have designed a tablet whereby the battery can't be replaced after it wears out" But, in all fairness, I have to add: How absolutely idiotic of me to have bought a tablet for close to $500.00 when the battery can't be replaced after it wears out. Kicking self and strongly advising others not to make the same mistake.

title: Sucking dust and grass particles into the optics!  New firmware not cool :(
text:
I originally bought this camera at the same time as the Canon G15, in order to try both out, compare them, and choose one to keep for my own use. As it turned out, I had not yet made my final decision, but was leaning towards the Canon because of its faster speeds and somewhat sharper pics and better overall performance, when my husband stepped in and commandeered the Nikon. I was a little nonplussed by his move because there were a couple of features on this camera that surpassed the Canon and I was still on the fence about it. I very much like the vari-angle LCD on the Nikon, as well as the much farther reach of the zoom.

However, after owning and using both cameras since the beginning of April, I have to say that I am much happier with the Canon. And not so much just because of the advantages described above, but more because we have also had the dubious "opportunity" to compare the warranty service levels available to both cameras. And also, in no small way, because our Nikon is now systematically sucking dust into its layers of lenses. Yes, I said "into".

Here is the whole story of what happened with both cameras: A few months ago, after having taken a total of about 11,000 pics with the Canon, it started jamming up. I called Canon, explained the symptoms and was immediately (within less than half an hour) emailed the documentation I needed to fill out and a prepaid UPS label and instructions on how and where to send the camera back and how long it would take to repair and return it. All this was done exactly as described, and I didn't have to pay a penny out of my pocket. The camera arrived back within the appointed timeframe, functioning perfectly. However, when I got it back, I noticed a very tiny nick in the paint on the removable neck ring around the base of the lens barrel. I called and asked Canon to replace it, letting them know that my camera had been returned to them in 'like new' condition, so it had obviously been nicked while in their care. The person I reported this to, asked me to hold while he asked a supervisor how to proceed with this. The supervisor came on the line and recommended I send the camera back so they could check it through again, to make sure that whatever had caused the nick had not further damaged the camera somehow - as in a drop or jar of the camera. I was pretty sure that was not the case, but agreed to send it back and let them look it over just the same. I told them I was a bit upset at having to be without my camera for several more days again. They told me they would expedite things for the second round, so I wouldn't have to wait as long this time. They made good on that promise by sending me a UPS Overnight label to pick up the camera. They kept it for just a few days, but sent it back via UPS Ground Service, which was a bit of a letdown.

In contrast, when Nikon was called about the dust and bits of grass in the lens problem the first time, a couple of months ago, it took them a couple of days to send over the paperwork to fill out. Neither the paperwork nor their email contained any information about how long the repairs might take, and we also had to ship the camera back to them at our own expense. Not a huge expense, admittedly, but still a contrast to Canon's better efforts to keep customers happy.

Now, less than two months after getting the camera back, there are dust particles in the lens again. We live in Vermont and my husband uses the camera for street photography here and in Montreal. These places are not exactly known for being dust bowls... So, in effect, the camera has not been subjected to any unusual conditions. Yet the seals are clearly not doing their job because the camera is sucking foreign particles into its lens system at several different levels of the optics.

We reported the problem to Nikon last Friday, early afternoon, and they sent a preliminary email acknowledging that they have received our communication. Once again though, here it is Monday and we are still waiting for the necessary paperwork to be sent, so we can return the camera (at our expense again, even though it's the same problem they were supposed to have fixed last time and the camera is still under warranty...) and hopefully get it back before Christmas. A hope that was communicated to the Nikon rep when we called in to report this reoccurrence of the problem last Friday.

I would have given this camera a 4 star rating, had it not been for the contrast in the service level with the Canon people and, of course, the unacceptable seals that allow dust to be sucked into the optics of our camera. I have not seen any other people complaining about this problem, so I am assuming it is unique to our own camera. Once this problem is corrected to our satisfaction, I will update my review and the star rating too.

UPDATE: Nikon took the camera and did pay for the shipping this time, when we asked (Canon does it without asking, every time). They did not get the camera back to us before Christmas. When they returned the camera to us the first time, the camera started having issues with accepting third party batteries. Since they returned it this time, it has not been accepting third party batteries at all. Clearly, they have upgraded to their new firmware, which locks out third party batteries for not only this camera, but all Nikon cameras that use the EN-EL14 batteries. There is more info about this on the web. I will include a link in the comments section about this.

Aside from our 4 back-up batteries now not working in our camera, it is also behaving extremely erratically. It has been on one photo shoot so far. Took over 300 pics. Had several strange things happen. The camera stopped taking pics at one point. LCD working fine, button depressing, but no pic. Tried again, display info disappeared, still no pic. LCD showing the scene, but display info gone, button depressing properly, but the camera is not recording the shots. Camera will not turn off. Had to remove the battery to turn it off. After that, it started working again. When the pics were downloaded, several overlapped, some vertically (kind of looked like a film camera's pics would if you didn't wind the film properly all the way to the next frame), some horizontally, creating a weird, half 'n half effect. One picture showed up with a severe white balance issue. It was in a deep blue hue. The camera was being used in AWB the whole time.

We have some more experimenting to do with the pictures. We will load them onto a different computer, with a different program and see what we find. We will also be scrolling through the images directly on the SD card. Will report back when we have more info.

title: Love/Hate relationship.
text:
I have had this camera about a week and absolutely love most things about it. Super fast focusing, great low light performance, awesome pictures, superb macros, stunning lcd display, great body, and the list goes on. You've seen it all in the other reviews. It's a wonderful camera that I can carry with me for strolls and spur-of-the-moment shots. I would love to have been able to use this for street photography, but because Canon saw fit to do away with the articulated tilt screen, this is not so very practicable now. It's so much easier to get great candid shots of people when you're not so obviously balancing a camera out in front of you at chin level or higher, trying to compose your shot. With a tilt screen or articulated screen you just casually hang your head to look down at the screen, and a quiet, incognito, stealth shot, with the camera hanging low in front at chest level, is so much easier to carry off discreetly and without bringing attention to yourself. With a fixed screen - not. Huge disappointment in that department. What was Canon thinking? Did someone at the design meeting say: "Gentlemen, perhaps we should step back a pace. This camera is so awesome that if we included the tilt screen, like we did for its last 3 predecessors, we'd leave the competition choking in our wake. That would not be fair. Gotta keep the competitors healthy and happy. Let's ditch the tilt screen." How logical was that???

So, now I'm faced with trying to decide between this camera and its close competitor the very cool, but somewhat slower-to-focus Nikon P7700. Also, the Nikon's flash is virtually unusable on macro photos because it casts the lens' shadow over your subject. Even though the Nikon also has a 20x zoom lens in its favor and many other awesome features, that slower focus is kind of off-putting... After all, usually you want to actually capture "that" moment, not the one that comes 2.5 seconds later. Also, I love macro photography and really resent that shadow. Who designed that flash anyway???

Hence, my dilemma. What to do...? What to do...?

title: Wow! Absolutely love, love, love it!!! (But buy the silver one)
text:
This is the most amazingly satisfying electronics product I have ever bought. The features are many and easy to learn. I especially enjoy some of the audio and video adjustment features: Audio: DRC setting helps bring up quieter sounds while controlling loud peaks. title: Canon SD950is Digital camera - Awesome battery at amazing price!
text:
I bought one of these about a year ago and have been using it in rotation with two other batteries, one of which is the original Canon battery that came with the camera. I recently dropped my original Canon battery so I thought I should be prepared in case it took offense to such thoughtless handling. So, I went back to my Amazon orders log, looked up my previous purchase and found the product still available, but from a different seller. I have to say that my jaw dropped when I saw the price. Unbelievable! Under $3.00, shipping and all! Wow! I quickly ordered 2 more. You can never have too many batteries...

These batteries are perfect! Not only do they last at least as long as the original Canon battery, they also charge a whole lot faster. I have marked an "L" on the Canon battery with a Sharpie pen to remind myself to put the timer on longer for that one. It takes at least 30 minutes longer to charge than the OEM ones. They take about 55 minutes each from empty.

What a great find! This is a great deal!

title: Wow! This is just great!!!
text:
What a great way to work on two PCs from a single set of Keyboard, Monitor, Mouse, Speakers and Microphone. This product is so easy to install and works perfectly! The length of the cords is pretty much perfect, so I can station my two towers well away from each other and thus avoid heat buildup, which could happen if they had to be positioned too close to one another.

I would suggest only one or two small improvements to make this setup work even better. I would label the switch itself with A/B tags, and I would also put two, different colored LED lights on each end of the switcher, which would each light up, depending on which computer one is working on. That way, the user can quickly visually identify which computer is currently in use, instead of trying to guess.

I have put A/B tags on my switcher and on my respective computers too. However, since the switch is not a toggle switch, I often still have to figure out which computer I am working from when I don't remember where I left off the time before.

Otherwise, this device seems to perform seamlessly. Just remember that when you are rebooting one of the computers, be sure to keep the peripherals connected until they are recognized. Otherwise, when you toggle back again, you may find a screen with very large graphics on it - like I did once. I just had to reboot and stay with that computer until I saw the Windows welcome screen. After that all went fine.

I have a Windows 7 computer and an XP connected to this. My peripherals are HP w2007 Monitor, Altec Lansing VS2521 2.1 Powered Speaker System, Microsoft Natural Ergonomic Keyboard 4000 v1.0 (USB) and a Logitech Cordless Trackman Wheel (USB). Have not yet tried my Logitech USB Desktop Microphone.

Great product at a very nice price. I recommend it highly!

title: Price came down. Have bought it. Awesome TV!
text:
This looks like a good little TV, but the price increased greatly since before Christmas. I would buy it at the pre-Christmas price of $250.00, but at this price I think I will consider a TCL with more feedback and a two year warranty. Pity. I would have preferred the lower price and then I could have gotten a 3 year Square Trade warranty to buffer my purchase. I will keep an eye on this for the next few days before I make my final decision. I am giving it 3 stars for the massive, sudden hike in price.

Update: Thanks to David Miller for the reminder, this review was due for an update. The price did come down, as it tends to when one makes an issue of it on Amazon - especially when there is an intention to purchase stated in the complaint. I have used this tactic several times now and it has paid off every time so far (3 times now, I think). And I am very glad I complained and then followed through on my intention to purchase this item. I bought it on Jan. 17th, 12 days after posting my initial complaint about the huge price hike.

This is a wonderful TV with great, easy to use features. The most important to me were that it has a truly great picture that is easily tweaked to my preferred specs. Also, it boasts 3 HDMI ports, one of which is conveniently located on the side, along with a USB port. It also has RCA inputs and component inputs, as well as an S-video input. All in all, I can hook just about anything up to this little gem of a TV! Overall, I am not as enamored of the sound quality from the unit as some of the other reviewers seem to be, but it really is better than what most other TVs give off, so that's just fine too.

The controls and functions are very user-friendly and it takes no time at all to be cruising along smoothly, switching from one input to another.

I have been shopping for a second TV for the upstairs bedroom and I have yet to find one that compares to this one for price, quality and features. I may very well be buying a second one very soon... as soon as the price comes down some more... ;)

UPDATE: January 25, 2017. Five years later. Still working perfectly. Very happy with this purchase.

title: Works great!
text: After reading the reviews, I decided to go for this hub and I am very glad I did. It is well designed. The connections are good and tight enough to hold well, and it generally does exactly what it's supposed to do and looks great too. I mounted it on the inside side panel of my desk, where it is out of the way yet near at hand. I have six items running off of it so far, including a printer and 3 backup hard drives. I also use it for my iPod and for downloading images from my camera. It has been operational for over a month without a glitch. If anything changes, I will update this review.

title: Too tight for me, but I would buy it for others if the price came back down.
text: I bought this in March 2010 for just over twenty dollars. It has a wonderful sound and is really nice quality overall, but it does not fit me. It is too tight for me and I can't wear it for longer than maybe ten minutes at a stretch before it becomes really uncomfortable. So I gave it away to a smaller-headed friend who is very happy with it. I would buy it as a gift again, but only at the lower price. If you have a small head, I recommend this product, even though it now costs about 50% more than what I paid for it less than a year ago. Good reviews seem to drive the prices up, eh? Pity.

title: Great case, but not all leather... if at all....
text:
This case is a wonderful fit for my iPod and very well engineered in almost every way. It looks great and feels great, is nice and tight around the iPod, while exposing all the connection and control points accurately. It is a great safety buffer for the occasional jarring tumble. I bought mine last June. My issue with the product is that the inside of the flap has a couple of habitual creases, from opening and closing, that have now worn through. At these creases one can clearly see that that particular portion of the case is definitely not leather. You can see how thin the material is and you can also see the fabric webbing that is the usual backdrop to vinyl. Now I have to wonder if the rest of the case is vinyl too, or if some of it is actually leather, as advertised. I would have to take a knife or scissors to it to find out for sure. I am not prepared to do that.... yet.

For the price ($25.67 with shipping), and if I had seen the quality beforehand, I probably would have purchased this product anyway. But I do prefer to be given fair options and know that I am buying the product as described. Hence, my lower rating.

title: Perfect! Sounds great, looks great.
text: Easy choice for me to go for this after reading all the great reviews. And, I have to concur: it's a great product. The length is just right to plug into my radio and rest the iPod securely on the passenger seat or under the radio. No more wire clutter like when I was using a 4 ft cord before. The sound is great, no distortion, the connection is solid and the two-tone ends look great. I am very pleased with my purchase. Thank you, Amazon. Thank you reviewers! What a great way to shop!

title: Toxic chemical smell.
text:
While this case is the right size for my needs and even has the extra compartments that I was looking for, it exudes such a strong, ghastly toxic chemical smell that it's difficult to focus on its good traits. Also, the color is a real disappointment as well. The Blue/Black model is not anywhere near the bright aqua shown in the picture. It's more like that color has been banged about in the back of a dirty pickup truck for a year or two and then dusted off. The color is even, but dirty looking. I have it sitting outside in the sun and wind right now, hoping those will clear that smell from it. The reason I am hoping still is because other than the smell and the color, the size is right and it looks and feels solid enough to be somewhat protective. However, if I can't clear out the smell, it's going back.
Update: I left it out, opened, on my front porch for over a week. It was exposed to sun most of the day. It did not rain at all during the time this was outside, but it was blisteringly hot and very humid as well. We also had quite a bit of wind for a couple of those days. When I finally brought it back in, it had no more smell whatsoever, I am happy to report. However, the color remains stationary.... Which could be a good thing, if it were a good color. But it's not.

title: What a great little workhorse!
text: I bought this little Sony almost a year ago for my elderly mother. She is not at all technologically savvy and she lives far away, so I photographed the player and the remote from all sides and gave her instructions over the phone on how to use it at first. Now she has pretty much mastered it and is very happy with it. She has been using it fairly consistently since she received it and has had no problems with it at all. This device is so small and lightweight that I am thinking of getting one for the guest bedroom. This is a very satisfactory little machine! Remember, it plays CDs and JPEG photos as well. If my mother can learn how to use it, anybody can.

title: Wow! Absolutely love, love, love it!!!
text:
This is the most amazingly satisfying electronics product I have ever bought. The features are many and easy to learn. I especially enjoy some of the audio and video adjustment features:
Audio: DRC setting helps bring up quieter sounds while controlling loud peaks. Great for taming those annoying audio surges in 'background' music or battle scenes, etc. The Dialog feature lets you adjust the dialog perception so that you can hear the voices better over the background sounds in the soundtracks.
Video: You can adjust the Sharpness, Brightness, Contrast, Gamma, Hue, Chroma Level and BNR (block noise reduction). Each one has several levels to choose from and you get to sample it as it adjusts, so you can skip back and forth and compare the difference before you decide what to settle on.
The USB mode has great, easy to navigate menus. You can also record to your thumb drive from a CD that you are playing. There is a choice of different bit rates to do this and you can record individual tracks or all tracks. Very user-friendly menus for all these choices.
This unit has too many features to list, especially for someone like me, who is not quite fluent in tech terminology. Suffice it to say that it performs all the functions beautifully, the manual is very user-friendly and not only tells you how to adjust/change the various settings, but also explains the technical terminology in real English, so you know what those settings actually do when activated.
I do love the region-free feature too. But for me, this is more ho-hum, since I already owned one - a far inferior quality Philips one.
About the only thing I can think of to improve the user-friendliness of this product would be to have an alphabetized index in the manual. But, since it's only a 61 page manual, it's not such a big issue overall.
Another suggestion I would have would be to allow it to record audio from DVDs also. So often, the audio track on a DVD sounds so much better than the soundtrack that is published on CD (i.e.: Brassed Off, Eyes Wide Shut), although I recognize there may be some copyright issues with that concept.
For the record: I am getting a second unit for my upstairs TV. Have I mentioned that I love it...? This is a really great product!!!

Overall lots of assembly buy good directions. Sturdier than I expected. Tools included although I got a flathead screwdriver (directions say Phillips included, wasn't. title: Bought it for my son
text:
but my daughter in law ended up with it since his job blocks cellular signal and he has no wifi access at work.

That said she absolutely loves it. Got the 42 mm but she says she would still prefer this size over the more delicate 38mm due to ease of use because of the larger face size.

It comes with a large and q medium band and the medium band fit her perfectly. Considering how small her wrists are the small band in the 38mm watch must be for children.

I'm sure the i5 or whatever is newest has a lot of extra nice features but this feels and looks modern and has plenty of great features.

Please make sure to get a case to protect the face. This younger generation is not used to wearing watches and without the Smiling iwatch case this watch would have bit the dust a half dozen times in the first day. They give you 2. One to get used to the watch I guess.

title: So disappointed
text:
1st the positives.
This is a beautiful case. The keyboard is responsive and the key height is better than the one that came included with a Samsung Galaxy Book that I bought a few years ago. The iPad fight perfectly into the case with no forcing or fighting. The magnet that hold the keyboard in place is secure. All of the buttons and ports on the iPad are easily accessible and line up perfectly. Smart looking set. Easy to follow set up for the Bluetooth connection. No connectivity issues. What could be wrong?

The negative.
This comes with a charger cord and no charger. This would not have been an issue if the cord was a USB C style cord. But it's not. The end that would go into a charger is standard USB and the end that goes into the keyboard is a USB mini. The old fashioned kind with the 2 prongs or teeth. My phone charger is USB C on both ends and so is my iPad charger. No adapter is supplied. What charger are they expecting you to use with this?

I can't tell you how disappointed I am to have to return this. I would have gladly used my Samsung or iPad charger if they had been compatible. Old technology accessory built for a new technology device is a deal breaker.

title: Never buy batteries again

title: Took me a few weeks to decide to buy
text:
And even though there's a small known issue that no one talks about, I absolutely love my drawing display. The screen is a tiny bit textured which is wonderful. I hated drawing on my 12 inch tablet's slick glass screen.

There is a bit of parallax but that's pretty common no matter the brand.

The 16 buttons come pre-programmed but are easily reprogrammed. So far I've only found 2 that I want to change. I did add small bits of masking tape over the buttons to remind me what features are where but they did a good job figuring out what made sense where so those will come off quickly.

The pen is comfortable, charges quickly, and you get 2. Although the charge stays for a long time so it's not like you're going to be swapping them out a lot.

So for the known issue. It took me about a half hour to set it up. About 10 minutes to unpack it and hook it up. 5 minutes to uninstall my wacom drivers. And 15 minutes to get my computer to recognize the 2nd monitor. 15 heart wrenching moments of signal not found, and omg what did I just flush $500 on... then i went to the install guidebook and saw... if the screen says no signal... yes. They know about this... so unplug, plug, turn off turn back on and reboot the computer. Voila!

Working just fine. And a pleasure to use. The screen size is mind bogglingly amazing.

Worth every penny.

title: Best Investment This Year
text:
I resisted the urge to throw it AGAINST THE WALL for the first few days, and I'm glad I did. I recommend using Internet Explorer to download the driver, register the product etc. Much frustration with Chrome and Firefox browser. Getting used to the pen (it is NOT a mouse) and figuring out what shortcuts are worth programming was a whole 'nuther trip. Disabling the Windows Pen and Touch long hold feature that turns into a right click was another adventure. THEN figuring out how to manipulate the brushes to get the effects for drawing... oye.

That said, after a little googling, watching some YouTube, and reaching out to some folks online who are familiar with the devices, I'm now having the time of my life. I'm an artist, and I use Photoshop, illustrator, indesign, and sketchbook pro. Moving from a basic stylus, and mouse to the pen has been a revelation. You CAN teach an old dog new tricks! But man o man, that's some frustrating learning curve. Deadman's curve!

title: Small and Useful
text: First off, this was so much smaller than I expected, which actually made me really happy.  I have a larger emergency backup charger/radio/light, but I have to keep it in the garage.  This device is small enough to keep in a drawer in my kitchen and I love the ability to charge using solar power.  I live in a high earthquake area, so having glitches in electricity is common when we have a minor rumble roll through.  As frightening as those can be, it's nice to be able to keep the phone charged so we can track the news and other information.  Overall, a nice emergency device!

title: Great for Travel
text: Pre-Covid, I was already an online teacher part-time, and now I've had to merge my full-time job and my part-time jobs and do a lot of teaching online.  Therefore, taking my computer with me wherever I go is a necessity.  I haven't done any air travel since the pandemic hit, but I know I'll have to once things start up again.  This case is perfect! I can hold a basic carry-on with this backpack/briefcase/bag.  I appreciate all the pockets for devices, cords, and mouse.  I also appreciate that it's waterproof, which is helpful for inclement weather.  Overall, a nice backpack!

title: Finally! A Compact but Efficient Storage Option
text: If you're like I am, I've had cords for every iteration of the iPhone hanging around, just in case! This works perfectly and everything is finally organized.  I highly recommend!

title: As Expected
text: I needed a cord that is a little longer with a bit more support.  These braided cords tend to hold up a bit better and don't fall apart. title: Perfect--Give Me Sleep Tracking, Which Apple Does Not
text:
For what I wanted, this watch is perfect. I love that it tracks my sleep, which is desperately needed. I have fibromyalgia, so I find that deep sleep is hard to find. While the watch can't make my sleep better, it does track it in a way that helps me work on my sleep times and relaxation so I can get better sleep.

Although, like most fitbits, it doesn't perfectly track all types of exercise, I love how it combines with the heart rate to calculate calorie burn. For instance, I box and swim. I can leave after an hour and only have 3,000 steps. On the flip side, I can go for a lazy little walk and get 5,000 steps. I've learned that not all exercise is the same, and with the heart rate capabilities and calorie calculation, that this fitbit seems to get it a little better. I don't worry about the steps quite so much, as long as I can keep working on my heart health and calorie burn.

Overall, I really like this watch. It does show text messages I get and alerts me of phone calls. I'm pretty okay not being able to call from my watch--I don't want to be available every second of my life, but I do like being alerted to things. For what it can do, this is a great watch!

title: Great monitor, with AMAZING customer support
text:
UPDATE: The vendor reached out immediately and apologized for the incorrectly posted weight. They had Amazon make the needed corrections. If you are looking for a product where the vendor stands behind it, look no further. The listed weight is now correct.

For starters – I really do like this monitor. The picture is nice, it seems to be well designed and well packaged, and the support email address was very responsive when I registered my warranty. I performed a very non-technical color comparison using colored bars in a spreadsheet (see photo), and the external monitor seems to be on par with the display on my primary personal laptop as well as my work laptop. I am pleased with the brightness, which seems to be the primary complaint for most USB-C monitors.

The only disappointment that I have pertains to the advertised weight of the monitor. Supposedly 1.43lbs.

I spent several days evaluating many products and narrowing down my selection, and I chose this model specifically because of the advertised 1.43lbs weight. By comparison, there are a number of similar monitors on Amazon with 300nit brightness and which sell for $40usd to $50usd less than this one. However, those monitors are all advertised as weighing more than this monitor, which is specifically why I chose this brand. Weight is extremely important to me for a portable setup and I was willing to pay extra for the lightest one I could find.

Advertised as 1.43lbs, in reality it is 1.6 lbs (see photo) – the same weight advertised by the other brands. But, when you add the cover (which is required to get this monitor to stand up without an extra stand), the weight is 2.6lbs. There are other monitors which have an integrated stand with a total advertised weight of 1.6lbs - 1.7lbs.

I did end up buying a separate stand which is very lightweight and larger than competing products. I am very satisfied with how well is support the monitor.

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B08K2W4X2V

So in the end, I really like the monitor, and the company is very responsive. But I would probably look at another option if I had to do it over again and was concerned about total weight. I probably could have saved some money and ended up with a lighter option that works as well.

So I drilled pilot holes and screwed in by hand.  The screws are made of a fairly soft metal, and several stripped out even after drilling a bigger pilot hole. It would be nice if they used some sort of mounting bracket that you could mount with a drill, then snap these into place.  As it is, they probably work OK for softer desks, but maybe not the best choice for a really dense wood.

title: Great Value for the Money
text:
I found it 'dark' and muffled at first. After putting an equalizer in front of it (I used the Windows 7 Equalizer APO 1.2.1, which has it's own graphic equalizer to play around with, and is free), I could tweak the response so that the speaker sounds very high fidelity and even across the frequency range. I am including a screengrab of the equalizer settings I use. As you can see it just needs a bit of tweaking to make it sound it's best. The volume is more than sufficient, but you need to put the speaker volume up high and adjust the volume from your computer or phone. Otherwise, there is a tendency to putting the volume up too high on the phone or computer and over driving the speaker, which will make it sound really distorted.

I spent half the day playing it at roughly 1/3 volume without it running out of power. I take it with me to work, and out on the porch. It's very versatile, but bigger and heavier than most bluetooth portable speakers. It's the price you pay for deep bass, and high quality drivers. If sound is most important to you, go with this. They can also be paired, which must sound very very good indeed.

title: Alert: Failures May be Primarily Power Supply Related
text:
I too had the EOL (End of Life) issue (red power led, no boot, etc.) I too ordered a replacement. However, while waiting for the replacement, I decided to check some things. First I checked the voltage of the power adapter: it read correctly - 5.1 volts. So I tried swapping it out for another 5 volt adapter i had lying around. Bingo! The thing works now. So, for 3-5 bucks on ebay or amazon, just get a power adapter. You may need to splice the old connector on (watch your polarity!). HTH.

Terry

title: Nice Deal but Firmware is Clunky
text:
This player is well worth the asking price, and I've not come accross any feature that doesn't work. Streaming, DVD, Network, USB all 'just work,' though I've not tested some features like 3D, Blu-Ray, and Wireless. The USB input sees my self-powered USB Pocketec hard drive as a media, and will play from it whatever formats the player supports. You just click your way to the directory on the drive that contains your media files. There is one issue: jpg thumbnails take 'forever' to load, much slower than a computer. If you have several hundred jpgs, it could take 5 or 10 minutes just for all the thumbnails to be displayed. There doesn't appear to be a cache either, so each time you load the directory anew, you have to wait.

The streaming video (I've only tested Netflix thus far) works pretty good. Also, DVD's play nicely and load quickly. However, the LG Apps are pretty lame - mostly stupid games you will not likely be using. :) Also, the interface is slow, so you have to wait a few seconds - 30 seconds for the main menu system to load when first turning on the device. However, the connection is pretty robust. I've only experienced very brief 'dropouts,' when the connection is lost, so far.

Overall I would say I am quite pleased with what I bought for the money. This was a replacement for my satellite service which I dropped for lack of use. Now for a nominal fee to netflix or Amazon (Pandora is, I think totally free), I have a wide assortment of home entertainment on demand. That is worth the 169.00 I paid for the unit. I recommend this model for anyone looking for a full-featured, internet ready, blu-ray/media player on a budget.

Terry

title: Old school knob with new school shortcuts!
text: Since starting to work at home for most of the year I’ve truly become obsessed with building my workstation. I’ve have become somewhat obsessed with working and interacting efficiently.  I’ve went through several mice, keyboards, and have a visited drawing tablets in search of something quick and interactive. I was looking for a trackpad & keyboard that would allow me to kickback with my feet on the desk or sit upright ergo style…something versatile and I ended up scratching my head and understanding that there is a huge gap in the marketplace for a trackpad/shortcut interactive device for Windows. Hence finding the Surface Dial. I only use normal Windows10 and still love the dial. I’ve been missing the old school knob like we used to have before touch everything…accept it’s customizable by application and it just works! Love the haptic feedback too! It makes Adobe so much better, as well as shortcuts like volume, zoom, and scrolling for other apps. I use it to the left of my keyboard and a Logitech MX 3 to the right of my keyboard. Lots of shortcuts while barely moving my hands. Once apple or Microsoft combines a keyboard with dial, trackpad , and shortcut keys it’s game over. I looked at purchasing the magic keyboard, trackpad, & the bridge but it’s still not cross functional/native without paying for a license or lots of hacks/downloads. No time for that. title: Quality product, but XP-Pen is better for the $$
text:
First off I am not an artist. I do a little of everything Adobe AI, photoshop, writing, drawing, signatures, annotating documents, basic coding, scripts, etc. I recently changed companies and went from Apple to Windows and have been missing some of the peripherals. I was originally looking for a keyboard/trackpad combo that would allow me to kickback(feet on desk), stand up, or be upright and take my interface with me, something different. I landed on drawing tablets and found many reviews of people who switched from a mouse and I was intrigued. I have a 34" monitor & 2 22" monitors(the basics.) The bigger the screen you have the bigger the tablet you need and they quickly get expensive. I ordered the XP-Pen Star05v2 & the Wacom Intuos Wireless Medium.

Unboxing:
The Wacom is much like opening an new iPhone. You get nice packaging, the device, and a charging cable. The texture and quality of the device is lovely. You find yourself liking it before you have even used it.
Setup:
Setup was super easy, I downloaded the software, and connected the device within a couple of minutes.
First impression:
At first it feels really weird at first…when you hover & move the pen over the tablet it moves the mouse. Tapping the tablet is like a mouse click. The pen/tablet is mapped 1:1 to your screen(s). If you go to the top right of the tablet the mouse goes directly to the top right of your screen. You can map the tablet to a specific screen so you have more space to draw on the tablet. You can also turn off the 1:1 mapping by putting the tablet in mouse mode. This is what I did to make the transition easier. However if you want to draw, sign documents, etc you really need to be in drawing/tablet mode. Otherwise your writing looks just like it would using a mouse. I setup some of the shortcuts in the software. I put the tablet back in tablet mode and tried Adobe AI and doing some of my work, diagrams, and did some drawings/writing.
Usability:
The tablet is superb for drawing, writing, design, & precision. I also liked that I could put it in my lap and scroll through web pages, applications, etc. However it just isn't quick enough for me. Perhaps one of the models with the dial and additional buttons would work.
Conclusion:
This unit is nice and if drawing & design were my primary function I would love it. I think I will try one of the other models with the dial. Probably the XP-Pen Pro as the Wacom Intuos Pro is just too expensive for my needs. I think a magic keyboard, magic trackpad, with the bridge would work perfectly for my needs, but I'm still using Windows primarily and not willing to pay for yearly software to make everything work.

title: Hearing loss and enjoy music? These are for you!
text:
I’m 40 and have high frequency hearing loss. I hear almost nothing from 1kHz & up in my right ear and 4kHz and up in my left ear. I only experience issues in loud environments(restaurants, etc) or when there is a lot of background noise, but I recently started experiencing low frequency tinnitus that was irritating so I started looking for solutions. I went to see an ENT doctor and went through the motions only for him to confirm that I have poor hearing for my age and it’s up to me if I want some expensive hearing aids. No way I’m dropping 5k... I began by just looking for something to relieve the tinnitus and ran across many people saying that noise canceling headphones helped. I then went to the Bose website and low and behold they had the Hearphones which also had noise canceling. I started reading reviews then first then I stopped by the store with my kids and tried them out. My son was across the store and I could hear him talking to his sister. I could also hear every word of the conversation of people not far away. I removed the Hearphones and could not hear my kids or the people talking. I did this a few times... tuning in on people, music, etc then removing the buds. Tried the noise canceling and the rumbling in my ears was almost gone. Needless to say, I was impressed. I discussed the warranty with the salesman...30 day return, 90 exchange for something else, & 1 year free replacement(btw the 1 yr starts replacement over every time you replace them). I was sold. I purchased them with the intention of using for 30 days and returning if I could do without them.

I have now had them for 1 month. Here is my experience... at first I hated the neckband and was considering returning, but I got used to it and now don’t notice it. I use them for 1 hour workouts every morning, driving in the car for phone calls, music, podcasts, noise canceling at work, so pretty much all day. The neckband twists a little while working out or running and you need to shift it back in place, but it’s not a big deal for me. I would prefer the Soundsport Frees for working out, but I can’t bring myself to spend another $200 for headphones when these are $500. The noise canceling is fantastic for the gym & office and allows me to listen to music at a much lower level, which saves what I have left of my hearing in the long run. I used the soundsport wireless for 1 year before getting these and the sound quality of the hearphones is better, plus the noise canceling, and it has the music boost/phone call boost. I gave my soundsports to my wife and now use these exclusively.

Hearing:
When there is a lot of noise I can put them on and hear every word of a conversation that I would normally not hear or tune all the noise out via the noise cancellation. I recently went to a concert and was shocked at how much I enjoyed the concert more while wearing them. I could hear the guitar strings, vocals, and so much more while having a conversation with my wife. Amazing! I even use them while listening to the stereo in my car because it sounds so much better. I am always surprised at the sounds that I miss while not wearing them.

Sound: Classic Bose sound. The best headphones I’ve owned and I’ve had a few nice sets including the Bose soundsports & Bowers & Wilkins. I enjoy music much more since having them.

Phone calls: Phone calls are so much better, I talk on the phone more now because I’m not struggling to hear the other person and I hear them in both ears.

Overall: They simply work great. One of the best features is the directivity. When you set it to front or focused it ignores the rear microphones. While at the same time merging the left & right sound together. You hear a little of the left in the right ear and vice verse which helps with conversations. If Bose can ever put this technology in earbuds like the Frees they probably could not keep them on the shelf. If you have hearing loss or tinnitus and love music buy the Hearphones. If you love music and have no hearing loss buy the QC30 or QC35 for the noise canceling feature.

There are other fun Easter eggs that I didn’t expect...Wearing these while listening to music creates a “karaoke” effect and you can adjust the world volume so that it increases your voice to blend with the music coming through the headphones. I also played my guitar and found that more enjoyable. I could hear the notes in more detail as well as hear my voice in more detail while playing. These are also great if you like to people watch. When you are in a mall or restaurant you can hear random people’s conversations from across the room in detail, while they think you are wearing headphones and not listening at all. If you have hearing loss and/or enjoy a premium set of headphones these are for you. I have not used any other hearing devices to compare, but there are plenty of other reviews that will provide that information.

My rating is 5 stars from my perspective, but here is the breakdown of positives and negatives as I see them:

Positives:
- The sound is amazing for music, podcasts, phone calls, everything. Probably the best sounding headphones next to the QC35
- Adjustable balance. I set the balance to about 20 toward my right ear and both ears feel equal again.
- The adjustable world volume is awesome. I constantly adjust when my surrounding are too loud or not loud enough.
- Treble/bass adjustment. I set the treble around 30 and my world comes to life.
- Noise canceling is superb. It has almost stopped my tinnitus altogether. Especially good in situations like moving the yard. Before the noise of the mower was exhausting , but now it does not bother me.
- Adjustable presets are nice
- The front, focus, & everywhere settings work great. I use the front 180 setting the most. The focus setting really boost voice in front of you which is very nice too.
- Hearing the outside world while listening to music is amazing. Especially when you want to hear music, but want to hear when someone talks to you.
- “Karaoke effect” is pretty cool and makes singing/playing more enjoyable.
Negatives:
- The neckband was annoying at first, but now I barely notice it.
- Sometimes the app does not connect right away, but it connects after a few seconds.
- You will get weird looks from people, but the look is them wandering if you are listening to them since you are wearing headphones. It disappears after you start taking to people.
- I worry about the durability of them sometimes, but with a free replacement of 1 year I feel better about that. Remember that if you swap them with the year the warranty starts over. I am considering the extended warranty they lasts 3 years.
- I don’t like the charge port, but the only thing to improve it would be wireless charging.
- You’ll get wind noise outside. Use the noise canceling.

Btw I bought these in the Bose store and wrote this review to help others with similar issues. The headphones have improved my life and I love using them for just about everything.

title: Five Stars

The cord is decently long and holds power well. sits almost flush with the counter top looks really nice.

text:
This solves one of the biggest problems with the arlo camera Systems. THE DEAD BATTERY. No more pulling out the latter to swap batteries.
At 26 feet it gives plenty of length to connect to the outlet and run up and around walls etc to connect to your camera. The wires are flat and thin and can easily fit between the gap of a closed door. With this it takes one more annoying thing off my list. Changing and charging the battery. Very happy with this product.

title: great price and stand up well
text: For the price you really can't go wrong. You get 4 in a pack for $10 and that is all we need and more in this house. Each family member gets to have one and they can place a tablet or phone on it of any kind and it holds it up with ease. I like placing my phone on it when I am getting ready in the morning and it holds it up so I can watch a show while I get ready. The holder does not slip and stays in place. text: Works perfect with my Arlo Cameras. It's a direct replacement for the existing battery. Battery life seemed a little better than the factory batteries.

title: I would highly recommend these to anyone who is getting tired of the wireless world.
text:
Long gone are the days of corded head phones, or so I thought... It seems as though everything is bluetooth in today's age, which has its benefits, but dead batteries and poor connections make me miss the old school plug and play.
That's partly why I loved these Belkin headphones that plugged right into my android device. The bass was deep and rich, the overall sound was crisp and clear.
They Fit snug in my ears, and were comfortable for over an hour of play time.
Like most wired headphones the cord is a bit short to my liking but it was sufficient.
I would highly recommend these to anyone who is getting tired of the wireless world.

title: Easy to set up and use. Great system!
text:
These are great wireless security cameras. They are a great upgrade from the arlo pro 2's, which we have had for about a year.

A few things I like about the arlo 3s.
-motion detection light
-wireless charging
-160 degree viewing angle is much better than the last cameras.
-Easy to set up and install

A few critic's
-The picture is good but not great. Seems to be a common theme with wireless cameras.
-The battery life is descent but depending on how often the camera is used, can be drained quickly. Another issue with wireless systems.

title: Solid headphones. Needs more Bass.
text:
These are awesome headphones. Some of the most comfortable headphones I've owned. The headphones are covered in a clothlike material that helps absorb and whick sweat during a workout.
The noise canceling is good but not great. The battery life has yet to leave me stranded and I've gone for a week without charging with fairly regular use.
The sound is clear and sounds crisp but I feel like it is lacking bass.

title: A few set up hiccups but overall works really well
text: Overall works well. I did run into a few hiccups with initial set up and had to contact Facebook portal chat team. With there instructions I had to do a factory reset and then was able to set it up with ease. Phone calls are made easily and I like how you can preset your favorites. Image quality is ok. I was hoping for a little better. The outside is made of a kind of cheap plastic which I don’t love. I do like that the camera follows you as you talk. Most of our video calling is done between my kids and their grandma so having a camera that follows them is nice. I also like that it is linked to my Facebook account so it shows pictures of mylife and kids. It’s like having a digital photo frame on the counter when I’m not using it. The sound quality on it is very nice. And it connected with Alexa easily.

title: Quality sound...but not sure if it’s worth the price for it
text: This sound bar does have excellent sound. I did have problems getting it to connect. You have to use the HDMI cord they provided. We tried using an extra long one we already had so we didn’t have to hang it under the TV but it would work with other HDMI cords. So you have to use their shorter one which is fine if you are setting it directly under the TV...we made it work (see picture). Volume control works with your TV control or the remote that comes with it once you have it set up correctly. This is our second sound bar we have had. The other one we had was far less expensive and the sound quality in this one is definitely better but I don’t think I would say it’s worth over 1,000 just for a little better sound quality.

title: I don't like the included ear buds but that was an easy replacement.
text: So far, so good.  This is my first experience with a bluetooth headset and the sound and connectivity are both great.  I did replace the ear buds with the style from the S7 phones, but with added wingtips, because the round silicone "ball" style ones that come with this don't stay in my ears no matter what size I try.  I've been able to do plenty of activities and not have any issues with slippage or loss of signal. title: Cheap and does it’s job
text:
I ordered mine today and received it 6 hours later. I bought it because I suspect the person that lives in the house upstairs is sneaking down into my basement apartment doing god knows what. I had a scare this morning. So I bought this as soon as I crawled out of bed at 5am after my cat got spooked and clawed up my face as he scattered off the bed to hide.
He only ever gets that scared when another person appears.
I was asleep so it took me a minute to deal with the pain and being shocked awake.
Then I heard the person walking on the floor above me and away from the door that connects the two levels.
Anyways, I’m starting to think something fishy is going on. I setup the camera pretty quickly to the app on my phone. I hid it in a box and covered the light with tape.
The only thing I don’t like is that the app can be slow. Like trying to load the live video feed can take forever sometimes. I believe that’s the fault of the app, not the camera. And my Wifi is really good.
But the motion detector certainly works because my cat keeps setting it off!
I hope to catch this bastard when I’m gone from the house or if he’s sneaking down while I’m sleeping.

Or maybe I have a ghost…I don’t know.

But if he is sneaking down here…I’ll be able to use it as evidence. Now I just need to buy another one so I can point it to the rest of the apartment.
