text: used this cord as an input from my AV power protection to my in wall power for my HDTV.  Works great....

title: Excellent organizers
text: These cable ties are great for fixing the rats nest of cables for your AV components.  They work like a charm. A 100 for less than 8 bucks too!!!

title: Can't Set It Up Properly
text:
Our last weather alert radio died and we were happy to see this appear. We have tornado watches and warnings from April to October. Husband loved the design. Then he tried to program it to get our local weather alert stations. He can't get them to come in. The closest station he could find was several counties away. Therefore it's useless.

If someone knows how to get this to tune in weather alerts for Cobb County GA, let us know.

title: Works Like a Charm
text: Since more and more gadgets come with USB charge cords and NO plugs, having one of these is a godsend. Of course there's no way for me to check if the international plugs work properly right now, but the plain old charger gives a nice quick charge, and that's the best thing.

title: CD AND Cassette Player!
text:
I've had an old CD player bought from a Name Drugstore years ago and also an old cassette/radio that I bought for work in the late 90s that both sit in the living room for playing of music and OTR (all of my OTR and filk music is on cassette). The CD player has been skipping for awhile, so I've been looking around for a new one. I'd found an interesting one with 4-star ratings and it also played cassettes (!!!), but in a review of it here on Amazon noted that there was a better unit from Sony. So I checked the Sony out; 4 1/2 stars, so I ordered it. We were listening to it yesterday--played my "Anne" cassette, a Celestial Winds album, and a Gaelic Storm album. The sound is good, nice FM reception, too. AM not so good, but I barely listen to the radio. I preset NPR and the Clark-Atlanta jazz station. Today I am playing MP3s of old radio series. Very nice fidelity. I hope this continues to perform so well!

It also comes with an aux in cord so you can plug a phone or MP3 player into it.

title: Great Tags for Your Home Theater System
text: I had half of our home theater plugs labeled with these neat Kableflags that I found on discount. I saved the rest, but they disappeared. So glad to find out they are still available. I modified the pre-printed ones by using paint markers to add details, or blot out words, but you can also get blank ones if you like. These are  heavy plastic and will take twisting and turning.

title: Good For Labeling Computer Cords
text: There are so many! I used one of each color to label printer, UPS cable, keyboard cable, etc. Used a Sharpie to write on them. The surface is not smooth but took the Sharpie ink okay, it doesn't run like it looks like it might, and the printing is readable.

title: Helps Eyes, But Touch Sluggish
text:
I actually have a 7" tablet to read on and didn't need this, but I have been noticing eye problems when I read; the glow of the tablet screen tires my eyes out and they hurt. I wanted an e-ink reader, so I got this when it was offered to me as a discount.

In general, it's okay. I do not read in the dark and try not to use the backlight, but without the backlight the text is pretty dark. I have to use a bold font to read properly. The touch screen is very uncooperative compared with the tablet. You have to poke and poke to get things to work, even turning the pages. I wish there was a volume control on this one which you could use to turn pages instead. It's also not very intuitive where everything is. For instance, once I finish a book and wish to go back to the front to collect information for a review--the copyright date, for instance, or the name of a character--I have to mess around trying to get back to the first page.

I gave it four stars because the battery life is incredible and it doesn't bother my eyes as much, but for the touch screen it might get closer to three stars.

title: Extra Bands for Versa 2
text: When you exercise or do heavy housework, it's inevitable you perspire, and that is death to watchbands. When I was wearing a regular watch I would have to change out bands every year. These will make sure I always have a band available, and if I like, I can change the color to match or perk up an outfit. The bands are nice and snug, buckle well, and I like the slimmer design that covers most of my wrist rather than the fatter band.

title: Fits My Kindle Paperwhite Perfectly
text: This is a perfect case for my new Kindle Paperwhite. It's nice and snug, and the Kindle doesn't wobble around inside. It comes with a small stylus which has a holder on the side of the case. The case cover is magnetic, and shuts off the Kindle when you close it.

title: Very Useful Multi Plug
text:
This is a great multi-plug! There are three sets of two grounded plugs on the three open sides of this plug, as well as four USB slots. The plug holes are VERY FIRM and there is no fear of any loose plugs in this unit. The USB slots charge a total of 5V/3.1A, so be aware the more USB connections you plug into it the slower the gadgets you attach will charge. Just plugging in will get you what Motorola calls a Turbocharge. I did not notice it in the description, but a light also shines through the USB ports, so this is also valuable as a nightlight.

In addition, the plug that goes into the wall rotates 180 degrees, so you can position it up and down, or canted to the right or to the left. Handy in limited-space situations!

title: First Smart Plug Experience a Happy One
text:
This is our first Amazon smart plug. Unfortunately the overhead light in our downstairs room, which we use as a library, doesn't work because there's the bottom half of a lightbulb stuck in it. (Yes, before you ask, we tried using a broomstick. We even tried getting it out with pliers. We're going to have to get someone in to replace the socket.) I plugged this smart plug in, fiddled with the Alexa app, scanned the included QR code, and voila, I had the plug working. Not using it for anything complicated yet, like routines; I just classified it as a light. Then took it downstairs, plugged the lamp into it, and said to the Echo Dot, "[name], turn on the lights." And there is light. "[name], turn off the lights" reverses it.

I need to figure out how to make the lights go on and off when I say "Lumos" and "Nox," but for now it's great. No Stygian darkness down there if I enter when the other lamp on its timer is off.

title: They're Okay
text:
I have a terrible time with my eyes when I'm at the computer for too long. The white background on most websites makes my eyes hurt. When I got new glasses I ordered a pair of blue light blocking computer glasses as well as regular progressives for my nearsighted eyes, but I rarely use the computer glasses when I use my laptop. So I thought this screen might help. There were two, so my husband could have one too.

Maybe it takes longer for some people, but I don't see any difference. I still get a headache when I use the laptop too long, so maybe it's not the blue light that bothers me.

Alas, I've never had any luck with these screen protectors anyway. With this one, I followed the directions to the letter to get all the dust off the screen and the bubbles from between the protector and the screen. The "squeegee" card to press the bubbles out worked really well, but there are still two bubbles in the middle of the screen that are there because there is a speck of dust there. When the screen is bright, the little speck of dust that was invisible when I was using the sticky thing to get all the dust off is now very visible. If you have better luck with putting on protective screens, you may like this one. It does not impede the touch screen function in any way.

title: Thought It Would Be Larger, But...
text:
...it still works for what I intended.

The moment I saw the product photo of the woman who had this laptop stand holding a laptop vertically, I knew it was what I wanted. I have one of those laptops that folds backward (Asus calls it a "Spin") so it can be used as a tablet. When I flip it around to use in that manner, it rests directly in the U-shaped hooks at the front so it can be kind of a television. If, God forbid, one of us had to go into the hospital and be god-forsaken alone because of the coronavirus, faced with the disgusting cable channels they have in hospitals that churn out endless horrible reality shows, we could at least have a laptop and the stand and could watch something decent on Acorn or Britbox.

The stand is very strong and very stiff--I can barely move the joints--which is terrific; no worries about the support suddenly letting go and dropping the laptop.

Again, it said it would fit a 14-inch laptop, so I thought it would be larger. It's 6 3/4 inches by 5 1/2 inches. But it holds the laptop fine.

title: Perfect for My Roku
text:
Our Roku came with a skinny, two-foot long HDMI cord. Seriously, who can use a two-foot long cord? I had to have the Roku stuck on the top of our flat-screen TV with electrical tape because there was no place else to put it.

This HDMI cable is a nice, thick, sturdy six feet long with the HDMI heads securely fastened at each end. It carries a flawless picture to the television. Amazon Prime and other services have never looked so good. Don't go to a big-box store and buy some "gold plated" cord that costs twice and three times the price--this will do.

title: Better Sound That Second Generation
text: Bought this on Black Friday due to the price to replace the one in our bedroom, on which we play the most music. The sound is much richer than the Second Generation Dot, especially when you go in the app and fiddle around with the sound balance and increase the bass a little and decrease the treble. I still wish for better voice recognition--if it is playing music, you practically have to bellow at it to get it to stop--and the ability to give it a novel name. C'mon, Amazon, Motorola did it with their phones several years ago. Surely you can get that to work!

title: The Best Replacement for What I Had
text: For years I used a cheap laptop stand I got at Fry's Electronics, but earlier this year it gave up the ghost. This one is much sturdier than the one I had, but it is also open at the bottom. I had to scramble to get it to hold the items I had tucked under the laptop stand (the DVD drive, a mouse pad, and a scanner pen). By tilting the DVD drive at the right angle, it does block the opening so I can keep the other things underneath. Unfortunately, the adjustable angle prop doesn't lock, so I have to be careful picking up the stand, but otherwise it works fine. Nothing else would do.

title: Nifty If You Don't Mind Sound Quality
text: Our laundry room is downstairs and often I cannot hear the bell go off when the washer or the dryer is finished. We had a cheap baby monitor in the laundry room and the receiver in the living room and monitored the laundry that way, but it was fifteen years old and static-y. Audio-only baby monitors in stores had terrible ratings and were about 30 dollars. For reasons too long to enumerate, we bought an Echo Show 5, so we moved the previously-used Echo Dot in the laundry room and used it for drop-ins; the sound was so much better. But I wanted the Dot for use in another room and using it just as a "baby monitor" seemed silly. Then I saw this little Flex on sale! Since I won't be playing music on it, there's no need for optimum sound out of the tiny speakers, and it's still useful for dropping in, asking the time or the temperature, etc. This is a great alternative to the Dot if you're not concerned with sound fidelity; talked to my husband on it via drop in and he says the sound coming via the Flex is pretty good!

title: Good Replacement for Fitbit Alta
text:
Apparently Fitbit doesn't make bands for their old Alta units anymore, so had to get these through a third party. I am quite pleased; in heaviness and thickness these are the same as the old Fitbit bands, and instead of having that annoying "button" closure, these bands have a proper buckle. In fact, they are a little difficult to get off because the little retainer strap that keeps the end of the notched part of the strap from sticking out has a little protrusion on it that clicks into the notches, so when taking the band on and off you have to figure out how to lift the little protrusion from the slot to get the band to come out of the retainer. However, this gives you a little measure of extra safety when the Fitbit is buckled on, so I feel it's a fair tradeoff.

These come in a variety of colors; you can go wild with metallics, or bright pinks and blues, or just do as I did and give your wrist a tiny fillip with purple or blue if you don't want to resort to sober black and grey.

title: I Have Been Waiting for This Since I Ordered It
text: My Blu-Ray player has been sitting on two rectangle blocks of wood for several years now, to keep it elevated enough so that the remote can send a signal to it. When I saw this monitor stand that could be adjusted high or short I knew this was exactly what I wanted! I chose to use the widest riser (I would have used both, but it wouldn't fit by one-eight of an inch) and now the Blu-Ray player sits up high, and my smaller region-free player is underneath on the blocks that were used to support the Blu-Ray previously. This makes good airflow around them to keep them cool. Really, really happy with this!

title: Upgraded Our Echo Dot...NOT an Improvement
text:
(I have upgraded my review again to take off another star. This gadget is IMPOSSIBLE. You have to BELLOW at it to make it do anything. I am sorry I bought it, and the second one that we sent to my mother-in-law so we could talk face to face. Unfortunately, no one where she lived knew how to set it up and she died before we could set it up for her. So I basically wasted $145 for two Echo Shows because the one we have at home is no prize.)

(I have upgraded my review to take off a star. Since we have not been able to do face-to-face calling on it--no one where my MIL lives knows how to set it up--it basically is useless for the purpose we got it. Yeah, I loaded some photos on it so now I can look up and see our previous dog or a pic of my mom. But really, the old 2nd Generation Echo Dot responded better and more quickly. THIS THING IS DEAF. I used to be able to call up the stairs before I took the dog out "Echo, what's the temperature outside?" and like THAT I'd get a response. You have to bellow at the Show two or three times. Sometimes I have to stand right next to it to make it listen. But it loves my husband's voice and always responds. The drop-ins were crisp and clear on the Dot. It was a real waste of money.)

We had a bright idea: buy one of these for us, and buy one for my husband's mother, so we could video call her at any time (she lives 2 hours drive away), and his sister who lives in with his mom. Well, due to circumstances, we still haven't gotten the second Echo Show down to Mom, but are using the first one. Right now we are not making much use of the screen, save for a clock and a thermometer, but we have branched out into routines that are rather fun. We have tried out its video capabilities and that is very good, although we have trouble with backlighting from where our Show is placed.

I have two complaints about the Show: I think the voice is more muffled, and it doesn't seem as voice responsive as the Dot. If anything is running in the background, like the television or music, it gets really hard of hearing. We have to shout.

title: A Happy Surprise!
text:
I didn't realize these cable clips would be so large! Previously I have only bought the small ones they sell at other stores in which you put one small cable in (I have them in my car to keep the power cord for my phone handy). But this is a happy surprise because, boy, do I have cables that need taming, the main one being the cable for the gaming keyboard I bought myself as a retirement gift. I don't game, but I wanted a clicky keyboard! But being a gaming keyboard, it comes with a big thick cable that has branches so you can plug headphones into it, and there it was dangling under my desk like a snake, in the way all the time.

Well, no more! The nice thing about these cable clips is that you have an assortment of them, the smallest being an inch in diameter. There are a couple that hold one cable, several that hold two cables, two that hold three, and two others that hold five. The keyboard cable no longer dangles in my way, but is tucked safely up and holding very firmly, and I look forward to taming several more cables that infest our bedroom where we charge our gadgets.

title: Good Player But Does Not Come Out-Of-the-Box Region Free
text:
*****New review again. I complained to the company and they sent me a new unit which works. For now.*****

*****November 14, 2020: I am changing my review on this again. After performing flawlessly since August, this unit suddenly quit working. Every time I put a disk into it it says "no disc." I can't even play CDs on it. I tried unplugging it and then plugging it in again, and it still doesn't work. Phooey--and I'd just gotten used to being able to see my Region 2 DVDs again!*****

This player came in the mail an hour ago and I rushed to set it up.

First, if you are buying this as an inexpensive DVD player for an extra player in a guest room, or for use with small kids who might break it. It does play well. I tested a full screen DVD (FLAMBARDS, unrestored), a widescreen (the hi-def version of ANNE OF GREEN GABLES), and something at 2.35:1 ratio (AIRPORT). Nice picture, nice sound. Nice little remote.

HOWEVER IT IS NOT AS ADVERTISED. While the listing says it comes with an RCA cable, the photos show it as HDMI, with an HDMI symbol in the visual, and an HDMI cord in the foreground. IT IS NOT HDMI. I could have let it go at that. I've run out of HDMI ports anyway.

IT IS ADVERTISED AS REGION FREE. It is not. I was looking forward to watching my British DVDs. So this is a complete fail as far as I am concerned.

(Later: The manufacturer has changed the visual so it indicates that it's not HDMI. However, it still says REGION FREE and it is not. )

(Even later: If you contact the manufacturer at the e-mail posted in "Questions & Answers" OR on the booklet that comes with the DVD player, they will send you a PDF of the instructions. For the record, here are the instructions to make it Region Free:

Connect RCA cables and turn on unit. Do not put a disc into it, or leave the unit open with no disc.
Type 5168. This brings up a menu that includes the choice "Region"
Go to "Region" and press Enter.
Choose "Test 0." Press enter.
Press setup button to exit, or get back to the left menu if enter has not already taken you there and go up or down to Exit Setup and then hit Enter.

This played all my British DVDs and my one Australian DVD, because Australia was the only company that released TNT's wonderful Alan Arkin film COOPERSTOWN on DVD.)

title: I'm Satisfied With It...
text: ...but actually wish I'd bought the cover my husband bought for his Galaxy Tab A. I like the color and fit of this one, but when I turn the cover back to read the tablet it twists slightly in my hand and is a bit uncomfortable. The grooves in the cover are perfect for propping up the tablet and watching it horizontally.

title: Pleased With This Little Shelf
text:
I had an Echo Dot taking up room on top of a bookcase and I needed this space. The Dot is plugged into an outlet that sits between the bookcase and a bureau. Having tested the Dot and sure it would respond to voice commands even in that lower position, I ordered this set of shelves. It's a doddle to install: unscrew the switch plate. Click the shelf portion together with the outlet surround so that it forms an L-shape, line up the surround, with the shelf on top, around the outlet, then screw the switch plate back on until it holds the wall outlet shelf firmly and doesn't wobble. Plug in the power cord, run the other end through the cord hole, plug into your gadget, then set your gadget (Echo Dot, phone, etc.--it should not be something heavy) on top. That's it.

Works great.

title: Sturdy Little Phone/Tablet Stands
text:
I considered buying a different model of folding cell phone stand from this manufacturer, until I took a good look at one and noticed they looked just a smaller version of one I had, which was flimsy and closed up with my phone on it at the least provocation. Instead, I ordered these and am very pleased. The half which holds the phone is a solid, but light plastic with a deep enough curve in it to hold my phone, and the other half which provides the balance for the stand is also a solid piece. Instead of an adjustable stand part that fits into visible notches on a base (which, on other stands, I find are unreliable), this adjustable piece has a very firm adjustable angle that is contained within the hinge. Both my phone and my 7-inch tablet fit into it horizontally AND vertically and still balance well. To my surprise, while I was repairing the case for my 10 inch tablet, I sat that tablet horizontally on this tablet holder and it held it beautifully. It does hold a 10 inch tablet vertically at most angles, but I would not trust it in any kind of active situation due to the majority of the body of a 10-inch tablet being above the center of gravity and unsupported in the vertical position.

Now, what seems to be the sticking point with most of the negative reviews: technically, this is not made for phones in cases. This is true, although my husband has been given two of the four of these and he manages to set his phone in a case on it very nicely, having had no problem with the stand tipping over or the phone falling out. If I put a case on my cell phone, I would still use this stand and it would still work. However, if you want a totally reliable stand for a cell phone or tablet with a case, you probably need to invest in something more expensive that has a wider lip to hold case and phone. However, for someone who doesn't use a case, this is totally perfect, even for a 7-inch tablet.

title: Great Card Reader to Tuck in a Pocket
text:
This neat little card reader is about the size of a BIC lighter and can be easily tucked in a pocket or pouch. One end is USB C and the other a standard USB and also a micro USB that has to be pulled out from the larger USB (this is a little tricky--follow the directions and be careful that you don't pull it too hard). The side slots take a micro SD card and a standard SD card, although I got a funny result: I plugged the micro SD card in the micro slot and it read the card perfectly. But when I put the micro SD card into an SD card adapter and put the SD card into the SD slot it told me the card needed formatting. So, not sure what happened there.

Note there are covers on either end of the stick, but, once taken off, there's no "leash" on them. It would be easy for the covers to get lost.

title: These Are Just What I Wanted
text:
Hard plastic, adjustable tilt, nice fairly deep curved holder for cell phone or small tablet. Hubby was given an Amazon Fire, I have a Samsung Galaxy Tab 7 inch, and they both sit in one of these holders quite nicely, and are not top-heavy like another "tablet holder" I bought several years back that keeps collapsing.

I have not tried an 8-inch tablet because I do not have one. Note: NOT for 10 inch-tablets. Also not for phones or tablets in thick cases.

I may have to get a few more. Love the way two of them nest together for a very small footprint. They can easily be slipped into a laptop case or a purse or a crossover bag to prop up your phone or tablet for reading when you are out (since if you're like me you never go anywhere without a book).

[Update: Surprise! I messed up the case for my 10.1 Samsung tablet. I put just the bare tablet on this stand horizontally and vertically and to my surprise it did NOT tip over like other stands I have had, even though it is so small. I did not have it at a super-acute angle. Very impressed that it did not fall over with a 10" tablet on it.]

title: Beautiful, Strong Messenger Bag With a Couple of Minor Problems
text:
Husband carries laptop back and forth to work so that he can telework one day a week and also if it rains (he can't take his power chair out in the rain), so I got this case for him. This is his review.

Likes: Looks great, very soft leather. The brown color is nice (although I would ordinarily choose black.) Enough center pockets that are well-padded. It will actually hold two laptops if you allow it, or a laptop and a large tablet, plus all their accessories (power cord and mouse). Nice strong shoulder carry strap that appears to be securely fastened to the messenger bag. Lots of small interior pockets for phone, pen, pad of paper, thumb drives.

Dislike: The coarse teeth of the zipper at the rear of the bag are hard on my hands. I have thin skin due to taking blood thinners and pulling out whatever is stored in the pocket is rather painful. Also, dislike the latch fasteners that hold the bag shut. I find these type of fasteners awkward to keep pressed down while opening the cover. I'm not sure what type of fastener I would prefer and would recommend, though, but not these. Perhaps the type with a metal toggle that fits through a slot when unfastened.

title: Nice Case, Unfortunately a Tiny Bit Too Small for What I Got It For
text:
Husband bought a refurbished Surface 3 for personal use and from the description I though he could use this to carry it. Alas, knowing it was still an expensive purchase he also bought a hard shell case for it. The Surface 3 and keyboard fit perfectly in the case, but not with the hard shell case on it. The zipper misses closing by about half an inch. However, if it is careful he can still carry the Surface 3 in it; with the case it is very snug and it would take a lot for it to slide out if upended.

This is a very nice case in a handsome grey, thick material with padding inside for a tablet, with a strap in the back for carry and also a shoulder strap. The outside pocket has a gusset so that a mouse and a power cord can be fit in without too much trouble. It should fit the iPads and other tablets it is designated for--unless they also have a hard case.

title: Lots of Room!
text: Bought this on Prime Day when it was even more value than usual. Finally got a new phone this year with double the storage, but I also wanted something to store radio shows I have accumulated during the year, and this phone takes a MicroSD card. I try to always get a brand name and SanDisk has served me well. The radio shows transferred to the phone with no trouble and play like a dream when I click on them in the file manager.

title: Good Kit
text: I bought this mainly for the lens filters, but also enjoy the cleaning kit and the flare cover. Not sure what to do with the long tube, but am slowly learning photography techniques.

title: Lightweight and Comfortable, Perfect for Work or Play
text:
I was hesitant to order these headphones because they had no boom mike. My husband's previous headphones, from Turtle Bay, had a plastic headband, and several weeks ago the plastic headband on the side of the phones that had the boom mike snapped in half. We had to tape the outside shell of the headband shut with electrical tape so that he could still use them to work with or play music on, so that the headphones sat cockeyed on his head. Luckily these Sony headphones turned up so we could try them out, but he was wary about the lack of external mike because their most important use was his taking phone calls when he teleworked. He needed to be understood by his callers.

All his fears have been unfounded. He uses them for his work, 10 hours a day. The people he speaks to over the phone can hear him perfectly, despite the lack of a boom mike, and he can hear them clearly as well. He charges it overnight and they last through the entire ten hours of his shift. Even better, these headphones do what his Turtle Bay phones did not: he can use them via bluetooth without the bluetooth shutting off when he doesn't use it. He was using the Turtle Bay headphones with a wired connection because if he didn't use them for over 20 minutes the bluetooth would shut itself off.

The noise cancellation function is excellent. When it is off, he can still hear external noises, but once on he can't hear much of anything. I shouted at him at one point and he did not hear me. If you were working, especially in a noisy office, these would be ideal, and they should be useful on a long airline flight as well. (Having no crying baby to test this with, he can't vouch for these covering a whiny child.)

As for the music, he said it sounded perfect right out of the box, without using the Extra Bass, better than his old Sony wired headphones. He listened to a favorite Moody Blues song and said he could hear when the riff changed channels from one guitar to the other, and the sound effects changing from ear to ear. Next he engaged the Extra Bass and listened to a Moody Blues selection with a heavy bass portion and loved the results.

At this moment we are totally satisfied with these headphones. Time will tell if they will stand up to weeks of work calls and listening to music. However, my husband says there is definitely one thing wrong with them: THE SIX INCH LONG CHARGE CORD. Really, who makes these things? Luckily we had a multipack of USB C charge cords we got here on Amazon.

title: When Your Second Pair is as Important as the First
text: I try to take a mile to mile-and-a-half walk each morning with our dog, to keep both our weights down, and since I walk the same route every day, after a while it gets a bit monotonous. Sure I can watch the weeds at the side of the road as they progress through the seasons--presently the privet and the honeysuckle are in sweet bloom, later on I want to see if the thistle plant blooms this year, in the fall the leaves make a carpet of color--but most of the time, dull, dull, dull. So I've taken to listening to a podcast while I walk, and was using the nice set of Jabra earphones I have, but they are too heavy to walk with; they work fine if I'm sitting still but if I move they fall out of my ear (I do mean my ear, because the traffic is so bad and I have to cross a busy street, I only keep one in). So I wanted a light pair to walk the dog in. These are great! The sound is nice and clear and very full even if I only have one in, and I love the fact that three sizes of earpads are included. I am using the largest ones and they are a nice tight fit. No having to push them back into my ear every three minutes. Very happy with these.

title: Small Footprint, Large Capacity
text:
I have to confess, I have bought these small backup drives for years and never used the pre-programmed software that came with it. I just want to back up my files. This time I was determined to use it to see how it worked.

First: this is physically about the size of my hand (with fingers; I have small hands) and heavier than the 1TB drives I have bought previously. Nice and solid. The connecting cord is short as usual. It was immediately plug-and-play, and I registered it. Then I started the backup software. This worked okay, except it took forever. I usually back up my hard drive once a month, and via USB it takes two hours. This one went on for hours, to the point I had to stop it by shutting off the computer at bedtime; it continued backing up for an hour. It did back up my files on my separate D: drive, and also my entire e-mail folder. But it also backed up my C: drive with my Windows setup on it--what's with that? Anyone knows that if your computer crashes, it is better to just reformat and reload. That way you get junk and possible malicious software off as well. So maybe that's why it took so long to back up, it was copying all those Windows files.

Not interested in using the other software, but a small 5TB backup for this price is good bang for your buck! I remember years ago (late 90s) when hubby and I bought a 300MB hard drive for $300 and we thought that was a bargain!

title: Long Reach and Fairly Stable
text: When I used to telework I bought a light similar to this to light up the front of my desk with my USB ports to the right of me on my tower. The head on this older light was so heavy that you could not extend the light its total length and have it stay up. This is much better; the head is smaller and lighter and throws off a good amount of illumination. When you bend it near the UBS port, you still have to fiddle with it to make it stay up, but it does do a good job of illuminating across the desk.

title: Worked Fine Until I Accidentally Tipped My Fitbit Into the Wastepaper Basket
text: I finally wore out the original strap and had to order this one, and it served me fine until the day I was so sick and having to gather the trash for garbage collection day. I carelessly swept my Fitbit, covered with paper from my day at work, into the trash can, and didn't realize it, due to how sick I was, until the next day. Alas, you could see its last voyage to the curb on the Fitbit's software.

title: Works Well
text: Husband had to have this because they gave him a brand-new laptop at work with only an HDMI port, but at his desk he has a monitor with only DVI and VGA connections and they never bothered to give him a cord to connect them. (A clear case of the cobbler's children having no shoes; he works for an IT company that has dreadful IT support.) He says the cable works perfectly.

title: Thank God for Quick Shipping!
text: Husband had similar size monitor he used for teleworking. When he was rolling his laptop cart out of the bedroom to start another workweek, the cart jerked and the monitor did a header. We got it to come back on, but the picture was full of lines and was erratic. Found the same monitor with good ratings on Amazon and promptly ordered another one; he had to go only one day without a monitor. The only thing we had to buy was a new cord because his new work laptop has only an HDMI out where the old one had VGA only. Husband is thrilled with this monitor. In his work he has to have many windows open and the type is teeny tiny. He can see it all clearly. The color is beautiful and vivid.

title: Well, It Works!
text: Husband occasionally teleworks and sadly needs an aux cable to lead from his headphones to his cell because the bluetooth in the headphones shuts itself off for no reason. He used this for several weeks with no problems, but the 4-foot length was too short. So I bought him another, longer aux cable and am using this one in my car to connect my phone to the radio. Still works fine. Noticed there were some complaints of it stopping working after awhile. We'll see.

title: Solid Memory Card
text: So far I have had no problems with this card. I ordered it to see if it was faster than the SanDisk Ultra that I had previously ordered for my Panasonic Lumix. They both appear to be about the same speed. The 3-second lag then is probably a function of the camera, not the memory card. Otherwise I am satisfied with the quality of the card.

title: Perfect for Our Needs
text: I bought two of these for my husband and myself to hold our phones. Just the right height and just the right size, and I like the hole to hold the phone cord. Very sturdy metal and the phone is at a good angle to use in the holder.

title: So Simple a Child Can Use It
text: There is not much to say about this great little USB disk drive. Sadly, the network card in my old laptop with the built-in DVD drive quit working and any new laptop with a DVD drive you could find cost an arm and a leg and next month's mortgage. This is a perfect solution: plug it in, put in a DVD or a CD and it responds immediately. You can also use it to burn DVDs and CDs, whether it's a data backup or a music disk. It's lightweight (the USB cord nearly weighs as much as it does) and can just be popped in a laptop case for media play.

title: Pleasing Set of Light Headphones
text:
Tried these out just recently. The first charge took something like six or seven hours, so yes, it will be showing red that long! Supposedly after charging you can get 13 hours of use out of them,but I don't think I'll ever have the chance to try them out that long; I just don't listen to music/other stuff for marathon sessions like that. While the fact that they're not Bluetooth and you have to find a place for the base station might put some folks off, on the other hand they work just fine once you plug everything in. Used them to listen to a tuba concert from Boston on YouTube and that sounded good, so expect even better things if I use them to listen to CDs or watch a DVD in privacy.

Please note that they are not noise-blocking, if that is important to you.

title: Helping Us Phase in USB C
text: So I have several portable chargers for our cell phones, from small ones that charge from a cable to larger ones that plug into a wall. But do I have USB C cords to charge them with? Nope, all my portable chargers come with USB Micro plugs. This is a great set to pair with the different chargers we have in the house. I've tried them and they work fine.

title: Sturdy and Practical, Just Not What I Needed
text:
This worked really well for my tablet, but it was very thick and heavy. Good if you constantly drop things!

However, I traded it in on a Nook cover so I could read vertically.

title: Compact, Attractive Extra Charge Cord
text: I wanted something small for weekend trips and this is just perfect! It's compact, but the cord is just long enough, and it's wrapped like the electrical cords I remember from my youth, except this is in an attractive green and white pattern that will stand out when we're packing to go home. Also, this will be a nice charge cord for visitors to use. I love the fact that it has surge suppression (although I don't want to test it).

title: For Those Silly Mistakes
text: I goofed and bought the wrong size filters for my camera. No worries. This adapter works fine.

title: When You Need a Longer Cable
text: I had an Epson scanner/printer with a 3-foot USB to B-Plug cable. That would be fine if I could scan from where the printer is located, but for me to scan I need to pull the unit out so I can raise and lower the flatbed cover. Couldn't do that with a 3-foot cable. This 6-foot cable works fine.

title: Nifty Small Speaker
text:
I've had this little speaker for two days and love it. I don't know what NFC is; all I know is that it paired beautifully via Bluetooth to my phone and is playing CDs that I ripped to MP3 with a nice fidelity, especially after I tweaked the equalizer app in my music player.

I actually wanted this for a special reason. I still have lots of records and cassette tapes, especially Christmas ones and old soundtracks, like my original STAR WARS LPs, and wanted to be able to play them in our living room. However, the only record player/cassette player we have is in another room, and it is not Bluetooth enabled (it's from the 1990s). I ran a line in cable and a power cord along a wall to another small speaker I have and have set it on a bookcase shelf at the entrance to the living room and this setup works wonderfully, but I wanted a better speaker. This one fills the bill admirably, and I will swap them out when I have a minute.

I'm not a big audiophile, so I can't give you decibel commentary or hifaluting audio reviews. However, it sounds nice and does what I wished it to do, and that's quite enough.

title: Finally Long Enough!
text: Do you know how short some charging cables are? I swear they think you are going to dangle your phone over the outlet. This cord is 48 inches long, which gives you a nice long lead if you have run your phone battery down and wish to surf or read while it's plugged in. It worked perfectly with my Pixel and commenced immediately to charging. A flick of the menu on the phone and it was now suitable for transferring files as well. Plus it is sturdy, with a nice thick protective covering over the wire. I expect this one to last a good long time. (Or until they change the port size on the phones again 😃 )

title: Works Fine, It's What I Connected It to That Doesn't
text: This worked fine for me, it's my phone that's the stinker. Google Pixels do not do OTG as readily as my old Motorola Droid Turbo. You still have to use an adapter.

title: Nifty Toy
text: I don't believe I have fully plumbed the depths of this gadget's usefulness. I've only loaded one skill so far. However, I have enjoyed what I've done on it. I can ask it the temperature outside when I get up, or before I go to walk the dog so I know what to wear outside. It has a good range, too; I can call from downstairs in the foyer and it will still respond. (Unless the TV's on too loud.) I've had it set timers while washing clothes or baking cookies. While I was decorating the Christmas tree I had it play Perry Como and Bing Crosby and the Ray Coniff Singers. It's not so good on "Wolfram-Alpha" type questions: for instance, I tried to ask it what date was 7 weeks from January 8 and it didn't get it. It WOULD, if I phrased it carefully enough, tell me what date was 7 weeks from the current day (which was January 3). I haven't played JEOPARDY on it or used it to order anything yet.

title: Pleased So Far, Save for One Thing...
text:
I will come back and do a further review when all the Christmas/New Year's hoopla is out of the way, but my husband got interested when he saw this gadget arrive in the mail and spent around an hour installing it (most of the hour spent trying to find somewhere to plug it in). He said installation is baby simple--plug it in the TV, plug in the power cord, then follow the instructions on the screen. You will need a computer, a tablet, or a smartphone to do the setup. However, I am automatically subtracting one point off the final rating because, although Roku states during the setup that there are many places you can access through its gadget for free, you are REQUIRED to give it a credit card number in order for your registration to complete "just in case" you want to order something that costs money in the future. This is like saying you can't surf Amazon and pick out a couple of books without registering first. I'd say you should allow your customers to "cross that bridge" when they come to it, not force them to supply a credit card, especially since Roku stresses in their advertising that there is no subscription cost!

Update: April 2017...I have taken this Roku stick off our guest room television and put it on the main TV because it gets Britbox, which I signed up for today. I am really happy with it, but must warn that the stick itself must be in plain view of the remote and you must aim the remote directly at it or it won't respond. Otherwise there is great reception and the remote is very easy to use. I found some interesting looking channels including one for the Great Courses.

title: Neat Gadget, But...
text: This is a great gadget but unfortunately I can't use it because Google Pixel phones do not properly support using a USB stick or adapter on your device (USB to Go). I wish I'd known this before I bought the stupid phone. I have already complained to Google, as if it will help. I can use the regular USB plug ONLY because I first used the USB stick in the official Pixel adapter, which I guess formatted it for Android.

title: Okay for Charging, But Can't Use for Data Transfer on Google Pixel Phone
text: These are okay for charging, and I did need a few more for that purpose. But they do not carry data to a Google Pixel phone from a USB drive with a micro USB plug. I bought two USB thumb drives with a dual micro plug/USB plug on Black Friday to use with my phone. Then we bought new phones with a USB C connection. I know there are USB thumb drives with USB C connections, but I don't want to spend any more money. (I just found out this is because Google Pixel phones do not support USB sticks, although Google Nexus phones DO. What kind of stupidity is this?)

title: Good for What It Is
text:
I wanted something I could take on a weekend trip or on vacation, or just someplace where I wanted both functions (laptop and tablet). I have owned one for nine months and I like it. I can tuck it under my arm in its included sleeve and take it just about anywhere. Can you play graphics intensive games, do complicated image manipulation, etc.? No. However, you can surf the internet, read Facebook, blog, write your novel, etc. Separate it from the keyboard and you can watch Netflix and read online magazine subscriptions, and Kindle and Nook books. On vacation I used it to blog as well as read my magazines on Nook and Zinio. (The Zinio app in Windows is a fat pain in the neck, but that's Microslop's fault, not this Nextbook.) Using a mini-SD card in my camera, I could transfer photographs I took during the day on my camera to my blog by using the mini-SD slot, which ordinarily holds a card for my files.

As others have mentioned, keeping the keyboard in contact with the tablet part is a bit aggravating. This is not a unit you can sit on your lap, but needs a stable surface. However, even a bed at a hotel will do as long as you don't jiggle it too much. I find it helps to uncouple the two parts, and then recouple it, FIRMLY, and if it connects, leave it alone! I bought a mini-mouse for it, plus a USB port multiplier (since it only has two USB ports and the mouse plug takes up one), and a stylus, and it's a light tool for keeping you connected.

title: Nifty Little Box
text:
Well, I just got this today as I have been hoping to be able to record on my DVD recorder a program that is on an over-the-air nostalgia channel. I hitched it up to my Leaf antenna, and soon it had tuned in every single channel I had hoped. Then I plugged it into the DVD recorder and it appears to be working fine. I have to watch the television through the DVD recorder rather than directly through the television, but that's no problem.

I also tried out recording on a USB flash drive and that appears to have worked out well, too. For a 30-minute program it created a 285MB file, and the picture looked great. I thought I would have to play it with VLC, but it will play fine on my computer using Windows Media Player.

Of course these gadgets are so cheaply made; hope it lasts long enough to record what I want with it. Right now I like it although the response to the remote is occasionally flaky.

title: Super Cell/GPS Holder for Your Car
text:
This is my second Bracketron purchase, the first having been from Radio Shack. I'm sorry to give poor Radio Shack even less business by not buying my replacement unit there, but really--$35 at Radio Shack, only $12 on Amazon? I'm saving for retirement here, guys, give me a break.

Anyway, I like this unit because it works on my air vent rather than having it dangling from or standing on a suction cup. I know through bitter experience how quickly these suction cups lose their suction; I'm not risking breaking a $200 smartphone. I plug my phone into the power cord, wire it for sound, and while I'm using the GPS listen to podcasts or music. With a little finagling, it's just on the correct angle to see with a quick glance while you're driving. Using voice commands I can make a phone call without having to take my hands off the steering wheel. Waze guides me through traffic. Rick Steves keeps me entertained. I love my Bracketron.

title: A Little Wonder
text:
This is an initial review of this nifty little flash drive. I have had it for five days and am totally satisfied with its performance. I first charged it up, using a USB-enabled electrical plug rather than attaching it to a computer. As I was charging the Wireless USB, I downloaded the app. I then tested it by transferring one music file to the USB drive via my computer. I pressed the button to turn the wifi on, then connected through the app, and successfully played the music file through the app. I then copied the remainder of my music files to the wireless USB. I also successfully renamed the unit. I have been using it extensively today to play music. At one point I had to leave my desk to deliver a file and did not shut the wireless off. I found I could receive the signal from the wireless USB drive from at least a distance of 52 feet, through several walls! Since my cell phone doesn't do anywhere near as well, I was impressed. :-)

The app is rather simple and a bit clunky (I wish the lettering on the files was smaller so I could see the longer names of some offerings), but it works.

title: What's Lower Than One Star?
text: I ordered this when it appeared on Vine to replace a recalcitrant Buffalo router that we had to buy in a hurry to replace our original router. However, right after we received this My Net AC1300 the Buffalo began working properly again. So the My Net has sat waiting for the day when we needed it. Last night was it. We unpacked the unit, plugged it in according to the drawings in the extremely limited "instruction" booklet, which is done all in images, and followed the steps. In the third step we were supposed to open Network and Sharing Center in Windows. Presumably, when we clicked "Connect to a Network," we were supposed to see a prompt which told us "this is a new router that has not been set up; click OK to start setup." We never received this prompt. The router just sat there with its blue power light flashing and we could never get any further in the setup. We tried all sorts of things, including resetting the router, unplugging it completely, etc., but we never received the prompt to set up that the booklet claimed we were supposed to receive. We tried manually typing the IP address it stated in the next step into a browser, but since we could not follow the previous step it did little good. We finally installed another router my husband had purchased right before this item appeared on Vine and had put away for an emergency.

title: A Really Nice Backpack With Electronics Perks
text:
First a caveat: I am not of the generation who grew up carrying backpacks to school and I do not have a lot of shoulder/upper arm strength; in addition I have arthritis in my neck, so to me any backpack seems a bit strange, stiff, and awkward. Frankly, I think if I'd had to carry around all the books I did in junior high school in a backpack (none of my classes were near my homeroom locker, so there was none of this dropping books off routine--we only had three minutes to get between classes), I'd have severe back problems right now, remembering the thick English, math, science, Italian, and history textbooks, plus a full size ring binder. Oy.

Now to our backpack: I like this. We have less expensive backpacks in our home, to use as a "bug out" bag in case of emergency. This is much nicer: padding, quality of material, and lots of nice pockets (I am a pockets-type person). I particularly like the "hidden pocket" that faces your back, which would be useful for money or any other valuables if you were backpacking or traveling. I have preliminarily tested this by putting my laptop and my 10-inch tablet in the space provided and walking around for a bit. My laptop is six years old and weighs a ton. However, the padded shoulder straps and the sternum strap were helpful in keeping this balanced well on my back. I went up and down stairs a few times and did not feel unbalanced or "top heavy." (I do now, however, understand why people like Airbooks.)

In addition to the laptop pocket with the inner sleeve for the tablet, this has a central compartment with two pockets, one zipped, and an outside compartment with all sorts of slots for pens, memory cards, CDs, whatever. A small pocket on the top of the back could hold a cell phone or perhaps your printout of a boarding pass, parking ticket receipt, whatever, and there are two small pockets, one on each side, one with an opening so you could put an .mp3 player in the pocket and have your earbuds come out through it. This is all in addition to the "hidden pocket." There is a strong handle at either end of the backpack as well as a handle.

My goal is to give this a better workout at Dragoncon, where I can carry lunch and snacks and juice boxes in the central compartment, carry my tablet in the laptop compartment, and also carry my camera, instead of slinging a lunchbox and my camera case over my shoulder. It seems like a much better option. I also see it being useful on the occasional weekend trip. If it works out for me, it's possible my husband might enjoy one as well.

[September: This was really, really good at Dragoncon; I will be using a backpack again next year. Much better than carrying the lunchbox and the camera separately and wearing a pouch. I put my tablet in the laptop pocket, my lunch things (juice boxes, sandwiches, snacks, fruit) in the middle pocket, and the camera in the outermost pocket. The little pocket at the top held my spare cell phone batteries, and my wallet was in the hidden pocket. This backpack needs a strap at the bottom, and, instead of an iPod holder, a water bottle holder. That's the only thing I can see wrong with it. Yeah, I could have put a water bottle inside with my lunch.]

[PS I liked this so much I bought my husband one for Christmas.]

title: Impressive Portable Speaker
text:
I received this item yesterday and immediately set it to charge; however, you can connect to Bluetooth and set everything up while it is charging, which is what I did.

Connection was ridiculously simple: turn on Bluetooth on your device (in my case a Galaxy Nexus), turn on the WAE-PTP05, which immediately shows up on your Bluetooth screen, you tell them to pair, and you're done. The next time you turn on device and speakers they pair immediately.

I am not an audiophile; I can't tell you about megahertz levels and give you minute techy details. What I can tell you is that the sound is excellent. I tested a range of input: soft instrumentals, lively Celtic tunes with vocals, a lush film score, and several different spoken word podcasts, most featuring men with baritone voices. All sounded super. One of the soundtrack items had little, soft bells in the background and they could be heard quite well. My husband, who was in the kitchen when I initially tested it, could still hear it clearly--he can't hear the television at the same distance--and was impressed.

The bass response, something I always check out in speakers, is excellent. In fact, the bass is so good that I've upset the dog. We have a fifteen-year-old dog whose hearing is not as acute as it used to be, but she does react with unease when we put the subwoofer on our home theatre system on. This unit made her act the same way as she does when we turn on the subwoofer; I didn't have it on very loud at all and I still had to turn it down so she would relax.

You can also download a free app which will give you a music interface and an equalizer for different music styles (rock, pop, etc.). Frankly, I find the interface too cluttered (YMMV), but it's easy to navigate after about five minutes and you can set a custom setting on the equalizer. I haven't yet tested battery life, but the sound, in short, is worth the price. I would wholeheartedly recommend these speakers.

title: Okay, I'm Convinced
text:
I confess, I'm not one for listening to things on earphones. I'm not attached to my iPod (I don't even have one). I don't listen to music on the bus or during lunch or anything like that. I have music on my smartphone, but I usually either plug it into the radio in my car via a cassette adapter and listen to it over the car speakers, or plug it into a speaker we got as a Christmas gift that is for use on music players/smartphones. So I all I had was a coupla dollar set of earphones from Micro Center when I absolutely had to use earphones. They were cheap and comfortable. Really, how much better can a high-priced couple of wires and earpieces be?

Mea culpa. I just did a head-for-head comparison of my cheap little blue earphones against these Jabra units. Wow. With my old earphones I could hear the fan and the television running in the background, and the sound was a bit smothered. When I changed to the Jabra VOX earphones I was awed. They were even more comfortable. The sound from the fan was completely inaudible and I could just, just tell that the television was on behind me, so I'm not saying they're noise canceling, but they do HELP reduce noise. The sound was excellent! The "smothered" sound was non-existent and the bass was especially good (I was listening to a podcast and the host has a nice deep voice). When I switched to music, the sound was much richer and I could hear a wider range of sound, and, again, the bass was excellent.

Plus the earphones come with a free app you can download that organizes your music. You can set playlists, view album covers, and it even has an equalizer.

If good sound is your goal while listening to your music device/smartphone, this is an excellent choice. My old blue earphones are going into the emergency bin as of now!

title: Oh, My, I Like This!
text:
This keyboard arrived today and I couldn't resist immediately pulling it from the box and setting it up. It comes with the required batteries, so you don't even have to hunt them up. The instructions are two tiny pages, which is how simple it is. I don't think it took me ten minutes, and I could have cut half that off had I remembered to immediately turn on the tablet's Bluetooth and go to the Bluetooth setup so I could pair the two. :-)

This has a "Chiclet" keyboard, but the keys are very responsive. It is the same size as the laptop-style keyboard that goes with my husband's Asus tablet; he has large hands and still feels he can type on it comfortably. The top of the keyboard has four function keys specially programmed to work with Windows 7 / 8, but the rest work as on a regular keyboard: "end," "home," etc. While the keyboard has an off/on switch that works with the function key, it also comes with a thick, rubber-coated (or "rubberlike," perhaps) cover which turns on the keyboard when you take it off and then turns it off when you put it back on. It fits snugly and completely covers the keyboard, protecting it. In addition, the cover bends in the middle so you can use it as a stand for your tablet.

I used it to write in Facebook and Blogger, and also tested it with a Word document in Documents to Go. Very comfortable to type with, although it suffers from the same problem with my tablet that my fold-up Freedom Pro keyboard does: when I use it in Blogger or Facebook, it types the first TWO letters of a sentence as a capital letter rather than one. I think this may be a problem unique to my Galaxy Tab 2 10.1. I did notice that the CTRL i combination for italics and the CTRL b combination for bold does not work with this keyboard, which I do find problematic and why I did not rate the keyboard as five stars. Otherwise I am very happy with it.

title: Very Nice Case/Stand for Galaxy Tab 2 10.1 Tablet
text:
After purchasing my tablet, I had found a case for it at Walmart, very sturdy, adequately padded, and with the ability to tilt the screen. However, the mechanism to tilt the screen was established with velcro, which after a while did not hold as well as it did in the beginning. In addition, at least one of the little elastic straps that held the tablet in the case pressed on the power button, sometimes with bizarre results. I therefore considered this Belkin case with interest.

Upon receiving, I immediately fitted the tablet into the case, and was delighted when it was held snugly and kept from slipping out by a flap which tucks under the tablet. All the buttons except the charging button were close to a cutout so that button could be accessed easily. In addition, the cover of the case has little grooves at intervals so that the tablet can be propped up to be viewed at various angles.

As other reviewers have mentioned, it's a very sturdy and thick case, which does increase the weight of the featherlight Galaxy Tab somewhat. And as I have been careful not to drop it, I do not know how well it protects and from various heights...and nor am I likely to test! But it appears very solid, and the elastic cord sewn into the case cover keeps it closed well.

Drawbacks: there's no hole for the charger, so you must charge with the case open. Nor can you charge when using the tablet propped up. And you can only prop horizontally, not vertically, although I doubt if that is much of an issue for most of the things you would want to do with the tablet propped up.

In short, it's not perfect because of the case having to be open to charge, and I also wish there was some way to keep my stylus inside; the case is so tight that I have to hang it outside, exposing the tip to dirt and damage. But otherwise it works well for me. Your mileage may vary!

title: Already Enjoying This!
text:
I thought long and hard about a tablet, knowing that for me it would basically be a toy. Plus I already had a Nook Color. When the iPad2 reduced in price, I thought about getting one of those, but decided against it for the following reasons: (1) no Flash--and yes, I know HTML5 is going to make that obsolete, but in the meantime many websites have a lot of money invested in Flash animation and even restaurants use the silly format to show you their menus (geez, just give us a LIST already--I don't need pretty pictures to find out if you serve something I can eat) and (2) I'm already invested in the Android market and would have to buy many iPad apps that I already have free from Android.

I have not even used it for a week yet, but this a preliminary review with some information I saw requested in other reviews (not necessarily here at Amazon).

UPS delivered this a little before 6:30 p.m. I immediately plugged it into the charger and left it alone. It was charged by 10 p.m. (it might have been earlier, but the unit was away from me and I heard no bleep or flash that might have have indicated the charge was finished). So it does not take six or eight or ten hours to charge as I have seen claimed on other sites. By midnight I was attached to wireless, had gotten into all my accounts and Android apps and was happily surfing and rearranging my home screen.

I used this over the weekend at a science fiction convention. I did not use it constantly, but turned the screen on and off all day for about a 12-hour period, reading Facebook and blogs, checking the news and weather, looking at the convention schedule online, playing short You Tube videos, etc. Nothing excessive, but sometimes did have it on for a half hour to 45-minutes at the time. I also do not have a lot of widgets going, like the Accu-Weather and news widgets that come pre-loaded on the home screen. (They delete easily.) In that 12-hour period it never got below 78% on the battery. It's very quick and fast and responds to a Targus stylus (rubber tipped) wonderfully, much better than my Nook color. The resolution of the screen is impressive. Maybe it's not the new iPad's "retinal display," but it's very, very sharp and bright, even though I keep my brightness turned down to save power. I downloaded the Nook app and the magazines I subscribe to look gorgeous and are simple to read; if not, a tap of the screen makes the text bigger. The unit also comes with Zinio preloaded, an app I plan to use to subscribe to non-US magazines. Kindle books look nice as well, but to me this is too large for marathon reading sessions. I prefer my Nook Color for that. Like my Android phone and my Nook Color, it connects to wireless like a dream, which is more than I can say for my laptop.

Things that might lead you to choose another tablet: (1) The camera is nothing special. It takes good close ups, but further away was problematic. However, I was in a low-light situation each time. Taking photos outside may be totally different. Why Samsung chose to remove the flash I have no idea. Silly, really. But who buys a tablet to take pictures with? (2) With a stylus I can tap to enlarge an image (like Google Maps), but not make it smaller and there is no plus or minus sign on the screen as on my Android phone. (3) Blogger doesn't work in the browser; you have to download the Blogger app, but that works well. iExit doesn't work on it, either. Rats. (4) As at least one other person mentioned, the screen cap button is right in a place where you can hit it easily. I thought of a good use for it this weekend (took a screen cap of the online schedule for the convention I was at, made a short-cut of it to the screen, then pulled up the screen cap for reference rather than going to the web page all the time). Very convenient! (5) Hate the pre-loaded websites in the browser, but I have seen this on other tablets. Apparently we the public are stupid (or lazy) and can't find our own favorite websites and bookmark them. [eyes roll], and (6) my Bluetooth keyboard won't work with it right now because there is as yet no driver for Android 4.0 (Ice Cream Sandwich).

I hope to check back with further comments.

[A few weeks later after I bought this, my husband found an Asus Transformer (TF300) at a good price. It appears to be just as good as this Samsung and the camera is better. It has a zoom and does take a better photo. So if you were looking for a tablet with a better camera the Asus Transformer may be for you. Note: It doesn't have a flash either.]

[Update July 31, 2012 to answer "How long does the battery last"?: I was sick and tired of not seeing any Olympic equestrian coverage except for a couple of hours in the wee hours of the morning, so downloaded the "Live Extra" Olympics app from the Android Market. This carries live streaming of events as well as archived events. This morning I watched about two hours of live streaming of the jumping finals. When that ended I watched six hours of cross-country eventing replay. Then about an hour and forty minutes of the replay of the jumping. I had my brightness at about 35%. This got me down to 10% of the battery from a full charge. Quite satisfactory.]

title: Used daily for 11 months - loved it until it broke
text:
TLDR; 5 stars for functionality and effectiveness. Gave it 3 stars because it died after 11 months of daily use.
Loved this cooling pad -- I used it under my gaming laptop on which I gamed and did data analysis/coding, and it kept my computer cool. Without it, my laptop would quickly reach over 82 C, with the cooling pad it was kept right around 70 C.
I bought it in January of 2021 and it lasted until December 2021, almost a year. I loved it so much I'm considering rebuying it, but I wish I knew why it crapped out on me. It's not expensive or anything, and I did use it for 8-10 hours a day (and a couple times I forgot to turn it off so it was on all night), but still... I wish it had lasted longer. I never used anything less than full-fan, and kept it tilted for air flow. There is a little bumper you can flip up to hold your laptop in place, but I found my laptop needed to be a bit more forward than the bumper allowed (to get the best air flow into the system) so I always kept it down and my laptop scooted forward -- still never slid off. One day I turn it on it the screen goes blue but the fans don't come on, no text is on the screen, and I can't get the lights to turn off unless it's unplugged. Not sure what happened, but there wasn't a power surge or anything.
Overall, I'd give it 5 stars if it just lasted a LEAST a year or so... But the thought of having to repurchase this yearly annoys me so it gets 3 stars.

title: I experienced connectivity and spacial issues.
text:
The Wireless Earbuds arrived as described nicely packaged. Once opened I inspected all items and found no physical defects. The ear buds came charged so I went right into testing.

Connecting to my iPhone was easy and took seconds. During the week of testing i worn around the house, yard, out driving and on runs. I experienced issues with connectivity were sound would drop out but come back immediately and spacial issues were the sound was not synced between the the left and right earbuds. Both issues were intermittent but frequent enough to be a problem and happen at random. One earbud use I only experienced the sound drop outs.

Sound quality is good, they are no AirPod pros or Bose but for the price I had no issues with sound quality.

The tap features I could not get to work but on occasion no matter what I tried. This was irritating.

The earbuds and case appear well made. I would say quality of both are average. Charging was simple and quick. The LED is a nice addition.

They were comfortable to wear and stayed in my ears well while running and doing other activities. There are three different sized ear cups to choose from.

Overall, I give the item 2 stars. This is due to the core features having issues and not functioning as designed.

title: Space and pockets galore, plus optimizable to specific needs.
text:
The JDITVYHANO Travel Backpack, Extra Large Laptop Backpack. Has space and then some. I travel frequently for work and this bag provides me the ability to take just one bag on short trip with everything I needs. Reminds me of my 3 day ruck when I was in the military. This is a multi-use bag for sure.

Some nice features included are the wet and dry sides, water proof pocket to include the zipper. Lunch bag, and USB hook-up. It will also accommodate a large laptop. The lunch bag is helpful when traveling for work. It tucks nicely into the compartment. You must be conscious not to crush your lunch though.

My only gripe are the two metal buckles on the front for the expandable pounce. Those two are metal, where all the others are plastic. They should have all been plastic but they work good.

The backpack material and components used for construction are a good quailing and appear durable. I did not see any quality issues with any of the components. All the zipper work well with no bidding. Pockets are strong sewn well and appear they will hold up under normal use and wear. All the measurements are accurate to within reason based on what is listed in the ad.

I have used the backpack traveling around my local area and plan on using for longer trips. My type of work requires me to carry test equipment and sometimes personnel items. Surprisingly, the amount of space in this bag allows me to carry both within reason, helping me to eliminating the need for traveling with two bags.

Based on price, size and quality the backpack is a good value. I’m satisfied with the quality and capabilities. This will definitely get used.

title: Met my expectations. Above average mechanical keyboard
text:
The keyboard took me a few days to get use to. The keys are not the typical shape. However, after a few days I adjusted and found the keyboard works well for me and is comfortable.

So, the keyboard came nicely package and upon taking it out of the box I found no cosmetic or functionality issues. All keys and volume knob clicked and twisted as it should.

Setup was easy, however, read the direction. You can switch between cord, usb and Bluetooth connections and this must be done manually using the function keys in orange. It’s not hard and will make since after you read the directions. There is downloadable software which supports all the features. It works well but I don’t intend on using much. It isn’t required to be downloaded in order to use the keyboard. The usb transmitter is small and can be stored in the keyboard if not being used.

I find comfortable to use. It did take a bit of time to get use to the key design but I expected this. The key are quiet but not whisper quiet.

I have used it over a week now for work and I have had no issues at all. All key work well and the battery has not needed to charged once. I use it up to 10 hours a day. It is easily charged via the USB cord and you can use while charging with no issues.

Based on other mechanical keyboards I have used, I consider this one above average and price reflects that. I have no issues with price or functionally. I’am happy with the keyboard and interfaces well with me and my work environment.

title: It will blow!
text:
[[VIDEOID:30666cfd882f55efa2655f2c2c614f95]] I hate buying canned air because I feel it’s a waste of money. How does this compare? In my opinion it is just as good if not better due to being rechargeable. My only complaint is the attachment tubes. Don’t get me wrong the two it comes with work great but there needs to be a tight space, high pressure tube like you would get with regular canned air…you know that little red tube. That would make this perfect. However, you could garage engineer yourself one which is what I will likely do.

The duster is simple to use and charges via a USB-A to USB-C cable…USB-C is the blower connect type. I connected it to an Apple charging block and charged according to the instructions. The tool has an on-off switch and a charging light with will stop “breathing” green when it is fully charged. It is blue during normal operations and red when dead.

The directions are clear enough…the English could be better. Terminology used is not typical to what you would expect.

The air duster is priced slightly high in my opinion but if you clean your computers, keyboard and really any countless number of things it pays for itself quickly. Works great in the car for your dash and center consoles. The brush attachment works great on keyboards for getting in between keys.

I’m happy with this product. My son thinks it cool so, he actually cleans his computer now and I don’t have to!

I gave it 4 stars due to slightly higher price and missing a tight space, high pressure attachment.

The plastic stayed in place, however, so I CAREFULLY continued to use the lamp - just making sure that the plastic piece did not fall out, resulting in me making direct contact with an electrical current.

However, after awhile, the lamp started to make strange popping noises. Then, there was a very loud popping noise, followed by some crackling sounds, and smoke started to emit from the lighting fixture.

Sure, I've had this lighting kit since 2015, but, honestly - it has been one problem after another with these fixtures. And electrical problems is a huge no-no! If you value your life, I recommend that you avoid this product at all costs. Just pay a bit more money and get something decent.

10/16/2015
Update. I contacted the company and told them about the faulty equipment. Literally, within 4 minutes of me verifying the purchase, they responded to me with the tracking information for my replacement. And they are sending it first class.

Things happen. Sometimes there are issues. But, with customer service like this, I couldn't help but come back in and upgrade my rating (from 4 to 5 stars) and leave additional feedback.

Thanks, Cowboy Studios.

title: Not really well suited for business travel
text:
This is truly a "you get what you pay for" type of situation. I travel a lot for work and bought this backpack to replace my old business travel backpack that I spent a decent bit of money in, but it finally started to fall apart after 3 years of use.

I realized quicky as soon as I started packing for my next trip that this purchase was a mistake. If you're looking for a bag to carry your laptop around, this bag will serve you just fine. But if you're looking for a bag specifically for business travel you should move up a few price brackets.

This bag is tight. And I don't mean that in the slang good way - you put a few things in it and it's almost busting at the seams, even after releasing the bag compression clips. The bottle pockets on the side have zero stretch to them and it's virtually impossible to fit a water bottle in them! I had to turn the bag on its side and wiggle it so the contents would shift enough for me to get my water bottle in the side pocket. Needless to say, this was not convenient.

As far as the rest of the bag, the zippers don't go all the way down (due to the useless water bottle pockets on the side) so it's pretty difficult to remove anything from the backpack that's more than a few inches down. The two compartments aren't adequately self-contained, so as soon as you put stuff in one side of the division it becomes almost impossible to put stuff in the other side. And even if you magically manage to get it all in perfectly, as soon as you remove one item - good luck getting it back in there because all the contents have now shifted and you'll never get that item back in the bag.

Oh and the lock on the top won't snap shut if you've got the bag full up to the top. You need a bit of empty space at the top of the bag or the lock is completely useless.

I'm going to return this bag because it didn't meet my travel needs. This bag will definitely serve you for simple tasks, but if you're a serious business traveler you should keep looking.

title: Cisco wants more money for VPN Client so they'll let it break after 1-2 years
text:
I've been a network engineer and architect for over 15 years, with most of the time configuring and installing Cisco gear.
I bought this for my home for two goals - VPN in and better firewall protection than what an ASUS router comes in with.

I prefer working on CLI, in the last few years with the push towards GUI, Cisco ASA's have become a lot less intuitive when configured from the CLI. GUI isn't so great either.

I've known Cisco to provide hardware and then charge extra for Licenses to enable features in the Enterprise space. So for home use I expected them to ask more money for Firepower etc. I didn't feel the need for firepower so I didn't bother with that.

I do care about ability to VPN in - which at the time when I purchased it was provided along with VPN client software for Windows and Mac (version 3.1). Now < 2 years later, after a routine OS upgrade on my MacBook, the VPN client stops working. I contact Cisco and jump through a few hoops just to get a ticket opened. And then I am told that I need to buy a contract/upgrade in order to download version 4.x. This to me is a new low for a company I once admired.

I refuse to do that because I've already paid for that functionality when I bought the ASA. I expected a company like Cisco to support the features I paid for until the End of life of the product. I'm not expecting configuration or installation assistance or any new features from them.

Simply a basic VPN client that was promised when I bought the Firewall. But their Supports unwillingness to do that leaves me with no choice but to stop supporting/recommending Cisco going forward.

If you are a home user or a small business owner then give other competitors a fair shake.
