(Since Unreal Engine won't play nice with Mac anymore, so the beautiful design of the ASUS eases the pain of going back to clunky Windows)

The first few days were a bit difficult though I must say. I needed to reinstall drivers because touchpad won't work which made me pretty nervous I had a paperweight to return after all the setup. I had to do a lot of installing, uninstalling and reinstalling of apps to get everything to work. I was also crestfallen that Windows obliterates the carefully curated desktops with every restart.

The ScreenPad is a delight and look forward to trying out Design / Drawing apps with it. The color is gorgeous and vivid and the machine is quite powerful - Unreal Engine will need that.

title: I love it. powerful amp in a small package.
text:
Pros:
- very compact, can be mounted almost anywhere.
- powerful for its size 400w 45rms output
- bluetooth with remote control
- usb charger port
- rca ports

Cons:
- no bass/equalizer controls (can easily be fixed by downloading a bass control/equalizer app)

I am loving this amp. I bought this to replace my old aftermarket car stereo that I used to connect my phone through a bluetooth radio tuner device. I decided to cut out all the other devices and install this amp so I can directly connect my mp3/pandora devices via bluetooth. This amp works incredible and I plan on intalling an old tablet in my car to connect to it. The sound comes out clear. I linked my phone but the sounds came out flat so I downloaded a bass booster app and now it rattles my windows. I did blow out the fuse in the car fuse box trying to turn the volume all the way up. The fuse in my car factory stereo wiring was rated at 7.5 amps but the fuse that is in the amp itself is rated to 15 amps. I might be able to get more speaker output if I installed new wires to handle 10-12 amps. I am enjoying the quality of this amp and all the applications that can be used for this amp.

title: Great Mount For More Then Half The Cost.
text: I love having this for my TV. Very easy to setup and my TV hangs great using it. I love that I only have to search for 1 stud in the wall to mount it especially with my walls were you never know were or how far apart the studs are in the wall. I had more issues trying to use a stud finder to find a stud to mount with then I did mounting my tv using this tv wall mount. I like that it swivels in just about any direction needed and can be tilted down pretty far as well as a bit upwards if needed. This all goes without saying that it does (like anything on the market) have some cons. It came with a very small bubble level that was a bit defective. If you tilted the level to the left and then level it, it would get stuck all the way left till you tilted it back to the right then level it. This for some could be an issue if that have the same problem cause if they are like me and don't have a real level to use they are stuck either going out to buy 1 or using the one that came with the tv wall mount. I managed fine with the included 1 considering the con. This thing came with a lot of bolts, washers and parts for just about any tv needing hung up. My tv manual states my tv is a Vesa 400x400 which this mount states you would have to use the arms included to for that type of tv. I think my tv manual was wrong about the vesa size cause I didn't use any of the arms for my tv at all but I did have to use 1 set of the included large washers cause the bolts to screw into the tv were either to short or to long without using them, no big deal it worked out great, it looks great and my tv is sitting pretty on the wall like it belongs there. I'm not going to take a star off for any of the cons I have cause this tv mount works just as good if not better then the way over priced ones at more then over half the cost.  I have this mounted to a Samsung KU6300-Series 40" 4k TV.

title: Fast Little Drive
text: Great drive, very small and fast. Gets really warm. It has a five-year warranty, but I was unable to register the product via the website at first, but a chat and a couple of pictures sent to support remedied the issue after a few days. In my experience, WD makes good reliable drives.

title: Great Earbuds
text:
I’m no audiophile. Usually I wouldn’t give over 25 bucks for a pair of earbuds, but I got these as a gift. That said, however, these are pretty dang impressive. First of all, they sound great. They have a really good tone once you adjust the equalizer in the software and I was surprised at how good the bass sounded. Second, the noise reduction really works. It doesn’t block out 100%, but I’d say it knocks out about 85% of room noise. It’s really appreciated in a houseful of rowdy kids and several multimedia devices running at the same time. Pass through sound works with a quick double tap. Thirdly, they fit well. They don’t fall out and are comfortable to my ears for the duration of the battery life. They include three sizes of inserts, so fitting was easy.

There is one thing I really dislike. Micro usb. It’s the reason I deducted a star from my rating. Why, oh why, does this device use micro usb for charging? Why force me to clutter up the floor with another cable? Stupid decision to forgo usb c for micro usb.

I can’t really speak for phone use or the Alexa functionality because I don’t use it. I disabled the microphones in the software. Don’t want amazon or anyone else intruding into my private life.

Over all, these are great buds; I use them everyday.

title: Great TV My Family Loves It
text:

Coming from a roku evironment of 5 years (no cable or satillite in my house), I thought Android TV would be a step down in content. I was pleasantly suprized to find it was not. While it's not quite as smooth and intuitive as the roku interface, I've found that I'm not lacking anything to watch. It has chromecast and bluetooth built in to boot.
As far as picture quality is concerned, it's the best I've ever owned. Thats not saying much as its also the most expensive one I've had too. If my opinion is not enough, please research reviews on the web. You'll probably find that most agree with me. Games look and play great too. Sound is average. Sill highly impressed.

title: Great Midrange Card
text:
Short form, quiet, and only requires one power connector. Paired with eight gigs of ram and a Phenom x4 965 it will run the majority of newer games at high settings and will run many at ultra settings. NVidia steady releases new drivers so this is a well supported card. It supports NVidia's PhysX technology, DX11, and comes with a very respectable 1GB of fast DDR5 VRAM. Only downfall is that these cards will not work in SLI mode. This is inherent to all 650gtx cards and not limited to this particular card.

Bottom line: PNY makes quality products and this one is no exception. Good choice for a budget build.

title: Works As Promised Even After Seven Months Of Near Daily Use
text:

The tip fits a little bit looser than the Acer, but after seven or so months of use it hasn't given me a hint of a problem.

Bottom line: Don't let the low cost fool you. This is a quality product that surpasses the original and has stood the test of time.

title: Impressive Budget Monitor
text:
Purchased this for a new build, retiring my seven year old system for a more modern and faster platform. This monitor was icing on the cake. Arrived packed securely without any dead pixels. Picture is clear and crisp with great color. Large display with full 1080p resolution and a very fast reaction time excellent for gaming or movie watching. It has a variety of ports including HDMI, DVI, and good old VGA. I cannot comment on the speakers as I own some high end Logitechs and have never bothered to hook up the built in audio. In a pinch, I suppose, it is nice to have it in case I ever need it.

Bottom line: I recommend this monitor to anyone looking for a quality product at a good price.

text:
These are definitely among the best-sounding earbuds I have ever used. The full-spectrum quality is incredible - like you will hear nuances in your music you may not have noticed before.
The noise canceling is also incredible. If you set it to 100%, you will hear NOTHING going on around you.
The buds are extremely well-made, and the charger/carrying case is also well-made, although the case is not quite on the same level - the lid is a bit wobbly, not incredibly solid when the case is closed.
Overall, these earbuds are worth the price. The battery lasts for over 6 hours and the case can charge the buds a few times over before needing to be charged itself. The buds are also holding up very well to daily use and some drops.

title: Good for the price and easy to use
text:
ARTECK HW086MW162 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse combo, still charging that's why there are cables. Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.

But dig it... this hand crank generator eliminates the need to have a stash batteries (which are not sustainable), or have radios that are hand cranked, or have to wait for sunny days (remember we're in San Francisco) for a mobile solar cell to power up. Now that we're addicted to our smart phones and tablets a device like this is a must have in areas where there are regularly occurring natural disasters.

title: I'm amazed that 32 gigs fit in a tiny bit of ...

text: My older sister said, "Why didn't you tell me that this Fire was on sale for Black Friday?" Well gosh I didn't know she was in the market for a Kindle Fire. Had I known I'd have told her. Had she logged on to Facebook the day I bought it she would have seen it posted on my Timeline. A bunch of my Facebook lady friends jumped on the deal. $35 for a Kindle Fire! I mean what a deal already. I like to watch movies with a tablet when I am in bed. Unfortunately my Samsung tablet could not display Amazon Prime movies. Also my old Kindle Touch was beginning to act up, giving me the nudge to get my replacement Kindle before the Touch kicked the bucket. Last but not least: VoiceView, aka Text to Speech. Instead of the robot voice of the Touch the Fire has a number of voices and accents to hear my eBooks. I haven't tested VoiceView on a webpage yet so I can't vouch for whether it works there. Anyway, Thanks Amazon for basically giving away this Kindle Fire for the 2015 Holidays. I'm in love with mine. title: Very Happy and it's "So Me!"
text: Everyone who has seen the Skin Sticker Art Decal on my new HP Laptop has said, "That's SO you!" I'm an astrologer and this laptop is dedicated to my astrology practice. It was important to me to have a decorative decal on the lid of the laptop because that's what the client is going to be looking at from across the table when I'm doing an astrology reading. I looked at dozens of "skins" and this one just jumped out at me. It is perfect for setting the mood of "Reading the Planets". As for the practical part of cutting it down to size I was happy to see the grid lines on the protective paper over the adhesive back. There were many sizes of laptop lid sizes drawn in different colors lines so one could just find the laptop size that fit their model and cut along the lines. As for applying it, if you've ever applied adhesive shelf paper or put up wall paper you know about avoiding air bubbles. With this decal when I trapped air bubbles it was easy enough to peel up the decal and reapply it. The adhesive is forgiving in a way that's surprising. But it stays put. The laptop has been moved about, in and out of the carrier bag, fussed with daily since the decal went on and it's still holding strong and not peeling up at the edge. The feel of it was more textured than I had anticipated and I'm glad of that. It gives the surface more traction. If it were smooth and slick I think the laptop would be in danger of slipping out of one's grasp if one's hands were sweaty. So I'm very happy.

title: Couldn't be more pleased
text: I looked all over for a laptop carrier that wasn't basic black, wasn't too "girlie", and was unique enough for me to express myself. This Newspaper Pattern Laptop carrier just tickled me to bits. It's like urban camouflage - put this in a shopping cart with a sweater and a bag of fresh produce, it does not look like it's something worth stealing. Not that I'd leave my laptop untended in a shopping cart, but it's the principle of the thing. The feel of the carry case is "spongy", very padded, and I feel that my laptop is secure and protected. There's a bunch of sections on the top side of the pockets for pens and "what not". The over sized flaps cover all that "what not" and is held in place with velcro. The pockets are large enough for me to carry the two part electrical cord. There's padding on the shoulder strap if you use that but it also has very comfortable handles should you want to carry it that way. I actually put it inside of a plain black back pack when I'm riding public transit and when I get to where I'm going, out at a lunch where I'm doing an astrology reading for a client, then I pull out the laptop carrier and it never fails to get a comment. It's fun and funky and fits my life style. I'm a happy grandma.

title: WOW - Update - Thank you one and all!
text:
As I was waiting for my Kindle3 to arrive I spent hours reading the reviews all of you kind people wrote. I want to thank you one and all for taking the time to write because your reviews and observations were more valuable than the User Guide.

That being said this is my experience.

First of all I want to kick the delivery person in the shins. Whoever delivered my Kindle just threw it on the floor by my apartment door, THUD, rang the bell and then ran to the elevator. Good thing I was home at the time. Yikes!

The Kindle is sturdier & the buttons on the side are stiffer to push than I had anticipated. All of which was a good thing. All the comments of it being like a fragile egg shell had me nervous because I've decorated egg shells and I was a bit concerned.

The first charge happened so fast. I had to double check the User Manual to make sure that the green light meant it was fully charged.

When setting up the WiFi I got myself confused with using my ISP password instead of my router password and got frustrated for a few moments. Once I figured out what the problem was I was able to download some of my archived books quickly. I don't see the sense in downloading everything. Makes the home page cluttered. It's in the "cloud" and isn't going anywhere any time soon.

Big Plus Benefits: Increasing the font for these old eyes & turning the view to "landscape". I'm looking forward to using the text to speech to listen to books while I'm doing crafts or cooking.

I heard tell that I can lend my Kindle books to another person with a Kindle (Not between Germany and Japan I read) but here in the States, yes? My DIL and I want to share digital books like we do our hard copies.

All in all, everything I hoped it would be and then some. I'm a happy grandma.
++++++++++++++++++++++
6-25-2012: Grandma is sad, the speakers died on my Kindle. I'm going to have to send it back for a replacement. I made a cover/carrier for my kindle to keep it out of harms way. I was very careful with it. I did use the earphone jack to listen to the books (text to speech) while I did crochet or other craft work. Now for the process of product replacement.
++++++++++++++++++++++++
6-27-2012: Would you believe I have the replacement Kindle charging up and downloading my books as I type? Talked to Jessica in Customer Service, she was wonderful, kind, & sympathetic. We went through the steps of setting it to factory settings, full 30 second shut off, everything. Nothing would make the sound return. It was odd, she said, because the earphones and speakers have nothing to do with each other hardware-wise. She send me an email with a link for printable return label. I repackaged the Kindle in the original packaging, which I kept just in case. Amazon shipped out the replacement before I got the broken Kindle to the UPS store on Tuesday. I received an email later that day from Amazon letting me know that they know the broken Kindle was on the way, so I would not be charged for the replacement. Wednesday before sun down my replacement Kindle arrived. WOOT! The UPS driver and I both like the Kindle 3G. He told me that the Kindle Fire that he got for his mother only plays audio books and does not have text-to-speech. He and I both love the text to speech function. My experience with Amazon exceeded my wildest expectations. Grandma is happy now.
\(*o*)/
____________________________________
Update: 8-13-13: Second Kindle 3G w/Keyboard sound problem. The jack for the earphones crapped out. The speakers worked but the earphones could not. I live with other people and one way we keep the peace is that we all have earphones with our electronic devices that make noise. I listen to Text to Speech all the time when doing chores at home and when I'm out and about running errands.

I purchased a 2 Year Extended Warranty when I bought the original Kindle 3G w/Keyboard. The first replacement was covered under the usual 1 year Warranty. This second replacement was covered under Year 2 of the Extended Warranty.

The Kindle 3G w/Keyboard was retired so I was offered a Kindle Touch, which has Text to Speech, as a replacement, for free. I jumped on that like white on rice, you bet I did! I'm a happy grandma now, all slick with touch screen and everything. So Bye Bye Kindle 3G w/Keyboard, it was a good run but it ran its course.

I highly recommend the calibration from the get go. I never bothered with the standard settings and just did the calibration from the start.

All in all this thing met all the requirements. I may get the Bose 700 surround as extra enhancement, but I still feel its not fully needed. The Bose 900 does it all in my case.

One other thing is that some content might not sound the same, which is normal for any set up, but adjusting the settings from the app couldnt be anymore easier and i dont feel its a complaint. I guess if taking a minute to adjust a movie bothers you, well then so be it

title: Good system for the price. Convenient
text: I found set up of this system (3 outdoor, 2 indoor cameras) very easy. Total of two hours for install of all components, initialization, customizing settings, signing up for Blink service, and adding local storage. I used double stick heavy duty tape to mount the cameras. This allows me to relocate until I find the best locations. I carried a camera close around our home to check for any signal weak spots. No issues outside or inside our 1 story ranch. Basement was even good. As an ultimate test I put the a camera about 70' from the Sync Module. It worked fine. Although I haven't checked out sensitivity distance of video capture from this camera. Video quality is satisfactory. Audio is ok, but not intending on using it. Jury is still out on the video capture sensitivity from there The activity zone feature is great. Basic is good for most cameras. Advanced is good for cameras that have flags, trees and or shrubbery that are easily wind active. One disadvantage is that the cameras are either all armed or all disarmed. (The reason for the 4 star rating) It would be nice to be able to arm/disarm on an individual camera basis. Also camera by camera scheduling would be great. BATTERIES!!! PLEASE NOTE BATTERIES!!!!: the instructions and notes are specific that alkaline batteries are to be used. Don't plan un purchasing rechargeable NIMH batteries. If you read the comments on NIMH rechargeable batteries you will see that they do not work with Blink cameras. I think that changing batteries, even on an annual basis, is better than running power/communication cabling to other cameras systems. I can relocate cameras as needed to meet changing needs without hassling with wires. I do have one camera mounted where it it will be exposed to sun, wind, rain, snow, whatever mother nature has in store. I will update on how that survives. I signed up for the annual blink service. I'll see if it was worth it in a year. For now it was a simple setup solution to check video capture and storage.

title: An Average Keyboard With Some Issues
text:
This seems like a fairly average keyboard with nothing to make it stand out above the crowd. There are some issues involved with it though that you should be aware of before buying. The first issue is general one with all wireless keyboards, a matter of the trade-off involved in going wireless. The advantages of a wireless keyboard and mouse are that they reduces the clutter of wires on your desk and they are more portable than their wired kin. The main disadvantage is that they need either regular batteries or regular recharging, either of which is just extra maintenance that wired equipment doesn't need. Only you can decide if the trade-off is worth it or not to you.

There is a big issue specific to this keyboard though that you should be aware of. The keys on this board come in three colors - red, grey, and black. The lettering on the black keys is done in white which makes them easy to read. The lettering on the red and grey keys though is done in a grey tone that is hard to see. Even though the keyboard is done in a fairly standard layout, the difficulty in seeing the lettering really is a pain. So, all in all, this is not a terrible keyboard but it's not a great one either, and I have to give it an average 3 star rating.
