I had a keyboard die when I spilled liquid on it so I grabbed the first one I saw available without looking at the details. When I opened the box and found that this was a backlit keyboard with large print keys, I was intrigued. As an old, retired guy, I spend hours a day at the computer gaming, streaming videos, and staying in touch with a far-flung network of family and friends via social media. This keyboard is particularly nice for the gaming. The white backlight against the black keyboard, as well as the large print keys make it very easy for me to hit the right keys when my eyes are bouncing back and forth between the screen and the keyboard while my hands are handling the both the keyboard and the mouse. This keyboard makes my responses faster and more accurate, which I very much appreciate as an older gamer.

There are those irritating glitches though. One of the worse is that the backspace key constantly sticks. Thankfully, I don't use that key in my gaming, or this keyboard would be totally unusable for me. When typing things like this review though, or posts on social media, that sticky key is very frustrating. Every time I have to backspace to clear a mistake I have to hit that key repeatedly, like I had to do three times while typing this sentence. What makes it even worse is that there is no telling how many hits it takes to move back the necessary amount of spaces. So it is very easy to backspace too far, causing even more mistakes.

Another glitch is that the keys seem bigger than on my last keyboard. I don't notice that in gaming, but when typing more than a few sentences of text, my hands and fingers begin to feel some strain. There are some minor glitches too. The volume control on my speakers is in an awkward place to reach. My last keyboard had separate volume control keys, making it easy to adjust the volume from the keyboard. This one also has volume controls but they are on the function keys, requiring two buttons to be pressed to raise or lower the volume. That sounds like a small thing but every time I adjust the volume,it is a bit irritating to have to hit two keys instead of one. And finally, this keyboard bills itself as "quiet". Hah! It's probably the nosiest, clackity clack typing I've done in a long, long time.

All in all, this keyboard feels like a cheaper knockoff of a higher quality one. For now I'll use this one, because I need it. As soon as I find that higher quality keyboard though, this one is getting tossed out.

title: It's Decent For A Low End Monitor
text: The monitor feels a bit generic, but with the ease of its set-up, it all worked out fine. The only drawback is that the clarity of color and resolution of the monitor can only be seen with a direct, straight on view. Any other viewing angle gives a whitewashed view to the entire screen. That won't be a problem if this is your main screen. However, it might be an issue if you plan to use it as a secondary screen in a multi-monitor set up.  Also, the anchoring device to hold the monitor upright is at an extremely low angle. I had to prop up the two front metal feet up by about 3/4" to view it. So this is not a high end monitor by any means, but it is fine for a low end one.

title: A Nice, Basic Keyboard & Mouse With A Few Minor Issues
text:
As an old, retired guy who spends a lot of his time gaming, my set up includes 3 computers and monitors spread across two adjoining desks. As you can imagine, that makes for a lot of cords and wires sprawled across those desktops. This keyboard and mouse combo is for the desktop PC that is the most awkward to reach. Instead of needing to zoom my chair over there, now I can just grab the wireless keyboard or mouse when I need to use them. That is a small, but very welcome, quality of life change.

Unlike other wireless keyboards I've used, this set up didn't require any special drivers or additional software downloads. It really was plug and play and I've generally been happy with this product since I started using it. The issues are minor ones but I will go ahead and mention them. I had to pry open the battery compartment on both the mouse and the keyboard with a knife. Then it took me a little bit to figure out how to turn the keyboard on. In order to extend its battery life, the mouse turns itself off when not in use. So it needs to be double clicked to turn it back on again. Not a big deal but it does take a bit to get used to. Finally, the nice thing about wired keyboards and mice is that one doesn't need to worry about batteries for them. Though the clutter of cords and wires can get messy, as I can attest from personal experience. Only you can decide if you would rather have the clutter or the gear that needs batteries. Should you decide to go wireless, this product is a nice, basic, no frills set up.

title: This Tablet Does What I Need It To
text:
As an old, retired guy, I find technology still significantly impacting my daily life in two ways. The first is that I spend a lot of time every day online - either gaming in my favorite MMO or binge watching the various streaming services. The second way is that I keep in touch with my far-flung network of family and friends via social media. Now, my desktop pc handles the first of those two very nicely. The problem is that I can get immersed for hours in gaming or in a good streaming show. Social media notifications break that immersion, causing me to move away from whatever I was doing to see what the latest notice was about. If I don't, it could be quite a while before I get around to checking my social media and responding to the messages there.

This is where a tablet comes in. I figured it would be nice to have a tablet that quietly beeped new notifications and allowed me to just glance over at the latest notice to see if it needed a quick response or not. Little did I know how hard it would be to find a low end tablet capable of that simple task. This is the fourth tablet I've tried and the first one which could do that one simple thing for me. The other low end tablets quickly crashed and burned for a variety of reasons. This is the first that actually continued to work after the first few days, giving me the notifications I wanted and that I could check out at a glance.

There are some issues with this tablet that folks should be aware of. The sound is tinny enough that I wouldn't listen to music or audiobooks on this thing. The visual quality is sufficient for modern movies and tv shows but vintage ones do look a bit fuzzy. The charge doesn't last quite as long as I'd like it to. The tablet needs to be charged twice a day, even when it's just sitting there beeping when a text message or email comes in. Charging once a day would be nicer but it is what it is. Still, this is the first low end tablet of four I've tried that actually does the simple task I want it to do. So for that, I have to give it a solid 4 star rating.

title: Some Nice Accessories But I Had Trouble Getting It To Work Properly
text: This is the third tablet I've tried recently. On the plus side, it has some nice accessories that didn't come with the other two tablets. Those include a case, a stylus, and a screen protector. For the Fire and other Android tablets I tried, those all had to be bought separately. I did have some practical issues with this tablet though. The more serious one is that I have trouble keeping it charged up. Sometimes it seems to charge just fine. Other times I can't get it to turn on. A lesser but still irritating issue was with the stylus. When first setting up the tablet I had a lot of trouble entering the passcode for my wifi server. A dozen times I was unable to get the code loaded even though I was being careful to enter it correctly. It turned out that the stylus was, for some unknown reason, entering a symbol I had never seen before instead of an s. When I used my fingers, instead of the stylus, to enter the code, it worked perfectly and I was finally able to connect the tablet to the internet. I don't know if the stylus and the charging glitches are something I am doing wrong or some problem with this tablet, so I'm giving it a neutral three star rating. Check the other reviews. If I am the only one having these issues, then it's likely just me. If, on the other hand, others are reporting similar problems, you may want to hesitate about buying this product.

title: Our Techie Teen Is Happy With This Mini 'Puter
text: We have two techie teens in the family and one of them has been wanting an extra computer they can dedicate as a game emulator. This machine fits the bill perfectly, allowing our nerd girl to play her favorite retro games, while keeping her main machine freed up for more serious use. She notes that this mini  computer is ideal for students or for anyone needing to do light tasks at home. She adds that it has a good amount of storage with room for expansion and also has a very simple vesa mount for connecting it to a monitor. The one caveat our techie has is that as a mini-computer, this machine can handle light gaming and content creation fairly well. However, you may not want to use it for modern, cpu and graphic intensive games, nor for heavy duty processing like creating videos. For what it is and is intended for, the machine works very well. It does have its limits though, so keep that in mind.

title: Excellent For My Niche Use But Only Entry Level For General Use
text:
As an old, retired guy, tech factors into my daily life in two important ways. The first way is that I spend hours every day online, playing my favorite MMO. The second is that my extended family, spread across the United States, stays in touch via social media. The very specific niche I got this tablet to fill was for a way to get social media notifications that wouldn't disrupt my gaming. I first tried an Amazon 7" Fire Tablet. The audio notification on that tablet died after the first day or two. There was also no way I could find to turn off the sleep function. The tablet kept shutting down so I couldn't just look over to visually see if there any notifications.

This Android tablet works perfectly to fill that niche. It sits quietly next to my main computer screen and gives a soft audio notification when I get an email or a text message. A glance shows me the first lines of the text or email, letting me know if a quick response is needed or not. The notifications were easy to set up and the sleep function is set to Never. So this tablet does exactly what I want it too.

There are some issues with it that you should be aware of though. For one thing, it charges slowly but drains quickly. For another, turning it back on sometimes takes a bit of extra button pushing. It looks like it is coming on but then shuts off again. At times I've had to hit the power button 4-5 times before it turns all the way on. Videos are just on the edge of being grainy while the audio is distinctly tinny, without any depth. I sometimes listen to audiobooks while gaming but the sound is just too tinny and irritating to listen to them on this tablet.

Since this product does exactly what I want it to, I have to give it a 4 star rating. Other than my specific niche use though, this is a basic, entry level product, which is why I can't give it 5 stars. It just doesn't have the high end quality of far more expensive tablets.

title: A Low Level Tablet With Issues
text:
The tablet came charged, which was nice, but the problems started very quickly after first turning it on. After connecting my email and turning on a YouTube video, the tablet kicked me off in a few minutes. It then glitched when trying to turn it back on, taking something like 45 tries before it actually started working again. I'm watching another video right now and the image is grainy while the audio is tinny. Photos taken with the built in camera are also very grainy and poor quality. If you need a cheap tablet and have low expectations for it, this might work. If you need a quality product though, pass on this one.

EDIT: After a few days of usage, this tablet finally crashed and won't turn back on again. It is now worthless and I am dropping my rating to 1 star to reflect that sad reality.

title: A Major Disappointment For Me
text: As an old retired guy, there are a couple of techie things that are a big part of my life. One is that I spend hours every day gaming online in my favorite MMO. The other is that I use social media keep in touch with family members who live all around the U.S. I got this tablet to keep next to my desktop pc just so it could give me notifications when messages came in from family members. That way, the notifications wouldn't directly disrupt my gaming but they would let me know to check social media when I wasn't in the middle of some major boss fight or the like. This tablet failed miserably at that simple task. By the second day, the notifications stopped giving the audio signal. Then the tablet kept going to sleep so I couldn't even check the notifications visually. And no, I couldn't find a way to just turn off the sleep function. I finally gave up on this Amazon tablet and instead got an Android one. The new tablet works like a charm, giving me exactly what I wanted - timely, non-disruptive notifications that a family member had sent me something. The sleep function is turned off. The audio notification signal is working just fine. And now I can respond to my family fairly quickly.

title: A Quirky Product With Some Useful Applications
text: As we got this in a four pack, everyone in the family who had devices with screens immediately got one to put to use. Everyone agreed that this screen cleaner did an excellent job on small screens, like phones and tablets. I found that it wasn't as good on larger screens though. On 1920x1080 full size desktop screens, the cleaner was more awkward to use and  was more prone to streaking and such. One nice thing though is that the spray had no chemical smell. In fact, it didn't have any discernible odor at all. Our techie teen figured out how to get the bottle out so it can be refilled when necessary. I did have a little trouble figuring out how the stand work and I wondered why a screen cleaner needed an attached stand. As it turns out, I'm glad it has one. It works very nicely for my 10" tablet. The family consensus was to give this product a 4 star rating because it worked so well on small screens and because the stand actually turned out to be useful. The fact that it was less effective on larger screens and that it is a bit pricey are the reasons it didn't get a full 5 stars. Our family liked this screen cleaner. It just didn't quite make it to the top rating.

title: Not For This Casual Gamer
text:
As a casual gamer who is very much not a part of the hard core, "git gud" crowd that feels the need to squeeze every ounce of perfect performance out of themselves and their gear. I play for the chill fun of it. Still I would like to be as effective as possible so I took a look at this mouse. The major attraction of it for me was the 12 extra programmable buttons. I play a complex MMO that uses a lot of keybinding to make the game easier and quicker to play. Sadly, those 12 programmable buttons were the very thing that turned me off about this mouse. They are not, contrary to other gaming mice I've seen, new buttons. The first 9 buttons on the side of this mouse simply duplicate the number pad found on most keyboards. So I've already got important keybindings on all those numbers. Thus, the side of this mouse only offers me 3 new buttons to program and they are in the most awkward spot.

Even worse, this mouse was not at all ergonomic for me. The side buttons are placed where my thumb normally rests on other mice. Instinctively, my thumb curled up away from those buttons and/or tried to rest on them very gently. Within a few minutes of using this mouse, I could feel my thumb getting sore in ways that don't happen when I game for hours on a regular mouse.

I'm giving this product a neutral 3 star rating because these things may or may not be an issue for other folks. All I can suggest is that you read a variety of the reviews here to decide for yourself if you want to try this mouse or not.

title: Definitely A Five-Star Product
text:
The first thing I saw upon opening the box was how beautiful the bamboo looks. The second thing was how sturdy and durable the stand was. It has a solid heft to it which is a very good thing when putting expensive monitors on it.

The third thing I noticed was the instructions. Some Chinese products come with instructions so small that you almost need a magnifying glass to read them. Those tiny instructions are often in broken English too, sometimes almost indecipherable, even with a magnifying glass. That is generally an indicator that the product is so cheap and cheesy that the manufacturer did not even bother to actually get it ready for the U.S. market. Not this product though. The instructions were on a full size page, easily readable, and completely understandable. Moreover, putting together the stand was so easy and well-designed that the instruction page was almost superfluous, though it was good to have it on hand.

Another thing that needs to be mentioned is the flexibility of the monitor stand. It is easy to configure the stand for 1, 2, or 3 monitors. You can also put the monitors in a straight line or angle one or both ends to curve the side monitors towards you.

Who needs a stand like this? Why would anyone need more than one monitor? Well, it depends on what you do with your computer(s). As an old, retired guy, I spend hours a day in my favorite game - Guild Wars 2, which you can find here on Amazon. The game is deep, rich, and complex enough that I use three computers, each with its own screen, while playing it. The center screen is for the game itself. The screen to the right has browser tabs full of maps, guides, reference material, and the like. The screen to the left has Discord open, so I can react to text chats there, without having to switch back and forth from the game. At the moment I have some nice monitor stands for all three screens. However, they are different lengths and different sizes, spreading the monitors too far for easy reach. This unified stand will bring them all closer together, making my set up easier and more comfortable to use. Only you can decide if you need a product like this one but if you do, this particular monitor stand really is a five-star product in my book.

title: Decent Sound For The Price - A Couple Of Practical Issues Though
text:
First, let me say that I am not an audiophile and have no need for fancy, high-priced speakers and such. For an ordinary listener like me, these speakers had a nice, clear, stereo sound. Both music and special effects in movies or tv shows came through very well. Dialogue in movies sounded a bit flat to me but I wasn't sure if that was the speakers or my ears. When I had the family fifteen year old listen to them though, he thought the dialogue came through just fine. So the issue was my old guy ears, not anything to do with the speakers. All and all, they really do have a nice sound for the price.

To talk about the quality of the speakers' construction, let me make a distinction between cheap and inexpensive. Cheap implies something flimsy that will easily break and fall apart. That's not an issue with these speakers. The materials they are made of are not high-end fancy, but they are not flimsy either. So let's call their construction inexpensive but not cheap.

There were two practical issues though, one trivial, one possibly a bit more problematic. The trivial issue is that the cord which connects the usb plug and speaker jack to your device has a very short connecting wire between the plug and the jack. For a phone or a laptop that is probably a non-issue. With my desktop though, I had to rearrange the usb plugs to open up one close enough to the speaker jack.

The issue which may be more of a hassle is that the volume controls are on the back of the sub-woofer. People usually tuck a sub-woofer away from easy reaching distance. So adjusting the volume may be a nuisance. Personally, I don't know why the volume controls aren't on the speakers which are usually more accessible. This may not be a big deal though if you can control the volume from your device. Just be aware of the possible hassle. In any event, our fifteen year old uses this speaker set to listen to music and movies on his laptop and he is happy with it.

title: Mom, An Avid Audiobook Listener, Did Not Like These Earbuds
text: Mom loves to listen to audiobooks while working. These days, a smartphone paired with good earbuds make that very easy to do. Unfortunately, she does not think these ones are good. They are uncomfortable to wear for extended periods. They are so touch sensitive that even her hair can turn them off. The sound is tinny on some of the audiobooks. To top it all off, she feels the charging cord is ridiculously short. All in all, she gives these earbuds two stars and is being generous in giving them that many.

title: Our Fifteen Year Old Nerd Likes This Tablet A Lot
text:
He's been drawing on paper since he was little and has been doing digital art since he was old enough to work on a computer. So he took to this tablet like a duck to water and here's his verbatim report...

-8 customizable hot keys
-good size for drawing but does take up a lot of desk space
- comes with weighted pen stand and half glove, half glove feels cheap but does its job
- no noticeable lag from drawing on the tablet to the screen
- 4 1/2 stars
-(also the drawing program I was using it with was Fire Alpaca if that’s helpful)

Oh and there was a glitch with the buttons on the keys where the color on the drawing program pen would switch when I tried to switch from eraser to pen but that might just be me getting used to the controls.

title: Mom Loves Them But Now Has To Share
text:
When these became available I asked our 15 year old nerd if he wanted them and his response a shrug and a "whatever". Mom wanted to try them though. She uses earbuds when she's walking the dog and wanted to see if these had better sound. Well her response was a big yes, their sound is really good. So is the Bluetooth range. She can leave her phone in the front room and hear just fine all around the house, even in the upstairs bedroom. They paired easily with her iPhone 7 Plus and are lightweight enough to be good for extended use.

When our nerd saw the headphones, his "whatever" immediately switched to "I have to try those!" He loved them too, saying the sound was great. With his iPhone 6 though, he has to connect them to his phone with a cord. The more recent Bluetooth of the headphones won't pair up with his older phone. Nice as she is, mom agreed to share the headphones with him so our family happily gives the product a 5 star rating. :)

P.S. I'm thinking of buying our nerd his own set of these headphones for Christmas. Don't tell him I said that though. :)

title: A Very Useful Plug & Play Video Chat Option With A Few Minor Issues
text:
While I've never bothered with a webcam before, having one now, in the middle of the pandemic, seems like it will be useful. As an old guy with a number of health issues, I am staying at home all the time and haven't been venturing out at all. Rather than actually going to the doctor's office these days, the webcam will allow me to teleconference routine medical checkups. It's also good for keeping in touch with family and friends I can't see face to face. Just this evening I spent time in a Google video chat room talking with a dear friend who lives in another part of the country. Then I checked in on Facebook video chat with one of my sisters. Talking with someone in a video chat is much nicer than chatting by text or visiting over a landline phone. So if you don't already have the capacity for video chatting, you might want to think about getting a webcam.

On my Windows 10 desktop, this really is a plug and play piece of equipment. No software or other downloads needed. One of the minor issues has to do with setting this webcam up for the first time. The instructions are minimal and of no practical use. At first, I kept getting error messages when trying to use the webcam to make a video chat call, with no clear indication of what the error was. Some trial and error efforts showed it to be a simple problem. I needed to give the device both camera and mic access before it would work. Once I figured that out, I was easily able to make calls without any further error messages.

Another minor issue was that when I first tried to put the webcam on my desk, it kept flipping over on its side. So I had to make my first video call holding it in my hands. Later, after the tight coiling of it's cord eased up, it sat just fine with no tipping.

Then, if I held the device too close to the computer screen, sitting just over the speakers, the webcam would pick up enough of the other person's voice to set up a feedback echo. Moving the device away from the computer speakers easily solved that.

Finally, the video on my end was okay but not great. I looked green but that may have something to do with the lighting in my room. Still, I loved chatting with my friend and my sister. Both enjoyed the fact that I looked so green and neither seemed to have any problem hearing me. This is the first webcam I've used and I'm pleased enough with it to give the device a 4 star rating.

title: Useless For Me
text:
Sigh, this one was a disappointment from the git go. After charging the remote and plugging in the wifi dongle, the first thing I did was hit the power button on the remote, intending to turn it on to pair it with the dongle. Nope, the power button shut down my whole computer even as the dongle was starting to download the necessary driver. Once I got the computer, a Windows 10 desktop, restarted, I couldn't tell if the driver had been installed or not. The mouse did not seem to be working at all. The keyboard did produce some results but they seemed to be random. The keys did unexpected, sometimes inexplicable things.

The instructions did give a couple of buttons to push if the remote didn't seem to be paired up. Unfortunately, the print and images were so tiny that I could not decipher what one of the buttons actually was. I tried to find an online manual that might have larger print but couldn't even find the company's website. Randomly pushing buttons finally got the cursor to appear. However, the pointer kept jutting off at odd angles whenever I tried to move the mouse. I managed to decipher the instructions for adjusting the mouse speed but that did nothing to fix the odd angling of the cursor. Moreover, while trying to use the buttons on the mouse side, I again started getting random, unexpected results. The whole thing was a mess and I finally gave up on it all. This product is useless for me. If you are tech savvy enough, you might be able to get it working properly but I'm not going to fiddle around with it anymore myself.

title: Didn't Work For Me - It Might For You
text: The idea is a good one. Given that on my desk I have two computer towers, two monitors, two sets of speakers, and four external hard drives, the area behind my computers/monitors is an unsightly mess of tangled cords and such. So a way of organizing that clutter seemed like it would be helpful. Sadly, this product didn't work for me.  For one thing, my power strip has two rows of four sockets rather than one long strip. It's simply too wide for this box. For another thing, the bottom of the box was cracked. Looking at the other reviews, it seems several people had boxes that had issues of one kind or another. Given the size problem I didn't go to the bother of returning mine but those who did seem to have gotten a satisfactory response from the company. The idea itself is a good one. The box has an attractive appearance and the use of renewable materials is a plus. So I have to give this product a neutral 3 star rating. It didn't work for me but you may want to try it out yourself.

title: A Sturdy, Attractive Monitor Stand
text: Assembly was fairly quick and easy with everything you need provided, including an Allen wrench. The stand seems durable and sturdy. The bamboo has a light, attractive appearance. There is one thing I feel the need to point out though. Monitor stands, including this one, are often marketed as an ergonomic item that eases neck and back strain. Personally, I've not seen any noticeable difference in my back or neck when using this or any other monitor stand. Your mileage may vary of course but I don't register any ergonomic benefit to using such products. Where I do notice a difference is in turning a cluttered desktop into a much more organized, attractive space. This stand, with its two shelves gives me a convenient place to put the miscellaneous items that tend to end up on my desk. And the attractive appearance of this monitor stand enhances the look of my home office. So even though I don't get any ergonomic benefit from using this product, I still very much like it and give it a 5 star rating.

title: A Nice Idea But Pay Attention To The Details
text:
A couple of weeks ago I got a monitor stand to use on my desk. It had a large circular hole on the back of the monitor shelf along with a plastic cover for the hole. Apparently the idea was to give a discreet place to run the monitor's plug through. That seemed like a silly waste to me as you could just run the plug off the back of the stand with much less hassle. So the idea of this product, using that hole for a charger with some extra USB connections, seemed like a good idea to me. A real caveat though is that there are several essential details to pay attention to in using this item.

The first essential detail is to pay attention to the size of the hole you are going to use this on and the size of this product. Apparently those holes are not a standard size and some folks have had issues using this item because of that. Handyman types who have the tools to enlarge a grommet hole have an advantage here but it would behoove everyone to make sure this product will fit what they need.

The second detail to notice is that this device only works with USB 3.0 devices. The 2.0 ones won't work. My desktop computer has both 2.0 and 3.0 USB plugs. You can plug any device into any of those slots and it will work although the speed may vary. A 2.0 device plugged into a 3.0 slot will run but at 2.0 speeds. With this product, the 2.0 devices won't work at all.

The final detail to watch out for may be the most important one. Several people who have plugged the charger into their computer have reported difficulties it's created with their machines. So if you want to do that, pay very close attention the first time you try it to avoid any problems.

title: Exactly What Our Family Needed
text:
I live in a family compound which is an old house divided up into several apartments. What makes these walkie talkies useful on a daily basis is the water situation in the compound. All the apartments are connected to the cold water line and a couple of the apartments share a hot water line. That means if you are taking a shower and anyone anywhere in the house turns on a cold water tap, not only will your shower lose water pressure but the cold water flow will abruptly decrease, leaving the hot water hotter than ever. For the apartments that share a hot water line, the same kind of thing happens. Suddenly you are taking a cold shower in a a trickle of water. These walkie talkies have solved that problem. With the group call button you can let the whole house know you are going to take a shower so no one will use any water till you call in that you are done.

Nor is that their only use. Several times a year our town will get a tornado alert. Should a tornado actually appear in our area, the whole family will head down to the storm shelter behind the basement apartment. With the walkie talkies we can make sure everyone got the emergency alert and knows that they need to be ready to move fast if the sirens go off.

One our family members has been sick the last couple of days and these units were in an easy way to check in on her throughout the day to see if there was anything she needed. By assigning each apartment its own channel and having everyone on the same group channel, it is easy to call one apartment or to reach them all, whichever is appropriate for a given message.

The units are easy to use and even our least techie family member quickly got the hang of it. The sound is clear even when calling from apartment to apartment. There is a flashlight function that is fairly bright, one that will come in handy in case of emergency. All in all, our whole family is well satisfied with this product and it deserves a 5 star rating.

title: The Cord Is Too Short But Otherwise It Works Fine
text:
My desktop tower pc has 4 usb ports in front, all of which are in use. So I thought it would be nice to use this adapter to give me some extra usb connections. Sadly, that won't work too well on my computer. The usb ports are high enough that the adapter dangles in the air because its cord is so short. Our fourteen year old nerd has a laptop which would work much better with that short cord and so the adapter was passed on to him.

One odd thing of note - I have a headphone set up that uses a usb charger. When I plugged that set up into this adapter, the sound through the headphones was noticeably higher and shriller than it was without the adapter. That was strange enough that I listened to the same song with and without being plugged into the adapter and the difference was very real and very noticeable. Why that is, I have no idea. I also don't know if that would affect sound quality when used with a streaming tv stick or other audio devices. Keep an eye on the other reviews as they come in here to see if this is a general issue or not.

Other than the cord being too short and the odd effect on the headphones I use, this does seem like a good product. It really is plug and play and it does provide extra usb ports at a time when we are attaching more and more stuff to our various devices. If I could use this with my desktop pc I would but our fourteen year old should be able to put it to good use with his laptop.

title: Not A HIgh End Product But Very Good For The Price
text:
Some of the edges are a bit rough and the grain pattern on the shelf itself was not the most appealing. Touches like that make it clear that you are not dealing with a high quality, high cost item here. For its price though, this is an excellent buy. No assembly instructions come with the stand because none are needed. It's obvious how to put it together. Use the included Allen wrench to install the included screws and you have the whole thing put together in just a few minutes. When you have it assembled, the shelf feels very sturdy and solid. The screws are gold colored which goes nicely with the bamboo color. The black mat it comes with is nothing fancy but it is a useful addition. The mat creates a well defined space on your desk for the stand and that helps the whole desk look more organized.

Organizing my desk was an unexpected side benefit of this stand. With a computer monitor on it, there is still room on the stand for a couple of small knickknacks I've gotten as presents. The space under the stand is good for putting small items that otherwise float around my desk, cluttering it up. I've never used a stand like this before and I find that I really like my monitor being elevated just a bit. That puts it more on my eye level when I'm sitting there, meaning less strain on my neck from looking down at a monitor all the time. I'm very satisfied with this product and am glad to give it a full 5 star rating.

title: Pretty Lights, Nice Sound, No Effect On My Gameplay
text:
Somewhere there is an ancient marketing survey that identifies teen-age boys as a prime segment of the gaming market and that says they really like bright, flashing lights. So manufacturers who want to sell to the gaming market still think they have to add flashy lighting to all their products. Well, the gaming universe is much larger than teen boys these days and bright, flashing lights have nothing to do with playing a game. With that pet peeve off my chest let me add a couple of things to give this review some context. First, I do spend a lot of time online playing an MMO but I'm very much a casual player, not a hardcore competitive one. Second, I am not an audiophile. High end stereo gear is wasted on me as the music coming from most any clock radio is good enough for me.

To my non-audiophile ears, the sound from this speaker is fine. It provides a nice range without being too heavy on the bass end or too shrill on the high end. Whether gaming, streaming videos, or listening to music and audiobooks, this speaker holds its own nicely. Though, like the flashy lighting, the sound quality really doesn't make any significant difference while I'm playing in my MMO world. The ambient noise, NPC chatter, battle music and such, all come through nicely but that's a perk, not something that particularly improves my game play.

The under the monitor design of this speaker really doesn't save me any desk space. The mini speakers I was using before were much smaller and were out of the way on the side of the monitor. This space bar basically sits in front of my monitor and takes up more room than other speakers. One strong plus to me for this speaker is the fact that it really is plug and play. I had it up and running in just a few minutes. Other "gaming" gear I've tried with flashy lighting systems require software to control the lighting and sometimes getting that software to install and run properly can be a major, frustrating effort. So I really, really like that this product lives up to its "plug and play" claim.

There is one last negative point to mention. a minor one. The volume and other controls are flat buttons on the side of the soundbar. So to adjust the volume, change the lighting, etc, you need to move the soundbar to look at the side of it so you can see what you are doing. I call that a minor issue because my keyboard has mute and volume control buttons on it and I can just use those to adjust the sound as needed.

The bottom line of all this for me is that I wouldn't buy this speaker as a "gaming speaker" but simply as a nice mid-range speaker who's sound quality I like, one that is easy to set up and use. Oh, and lest I sound too much like a Grinch, the lights really are pretty, the way Christmas lights are. It's just that they have nothing to do with gaming. :)

title: Excellent Backpack For High School Students, For Weekend Trips And The Like
text: This bag is an excellent fit for our 14 year old who carries a laptop and a load of books back and forth to school every day. It will also do very nicely for sleepovers and weekend class trips. The backpack itself is well built with a rugged durability. There is a lot of space inside with a variety of compartments. The USB charging port is a nice touch as is the breathable shoe holder, perfect for gym shoes. The water repellent fabric should help protect essentials like textbooks and homework. All in all, our teen is very happy with this bag and so am I.

title: A Nice Idea That Was Poorly Implemented
text:
Like many single guys I have various pockets of dust scattered around my place. My desk, behind the computer towers and monitors where all the cords are piled up is one of the worst. So a handheld vacuum to clean all those nooks and crannies sounded like a good idea. Sadly, this is not the portable vacuum that I am looking for.

A few design flaws were obvious as soon as I took this out of the box and started charging it. There is no stand or holder for the vacuum so it has to sit directly on the brushes you've just been cleaning with. The light indicating when the vacuum is charging/fully charged is pinhole size, barely visible from any distance. So I had to go pick it up and squint at the light to see if it was charged up. The little brush for cleaning the inside of the vacuum is one more tiny thing to keep track of and is easily lost.

Even more flaws became obvious as soon as I tried to use the vacuum. With the nozzle on I tried to clean the back of my desk where all the computer wires are. The nozzle immediately jammed up on hair and dust balls. That area is still as dusty now as it was before I tried to vacuum it. Next I tried cleaning some flat surfaces. The brushes pushed the dust back and forth while barely vacuuming any of it up. I put my hand across the bottom of the brushes and could not feel any suction at all. When I put my finger right into the center hole that the dust was supposed to be scooped up into, I could barely feel a tiny amount of suction. I still very much like the idea of a handheld vacuum but I very much do not like this one and cannot recommend it to anyone.

title: Hits The Sweet Spot For The Average User
text:
First, let me put this review in context. As an old retired guy I'm playing around on the computer for hours a day - gaming, streaming videos, reading the news, and keeping in touch with folks via social media. Let me also add that I am too old and slow to be a hard core, competitive gamer. So even though I can spend long hours in an online MMORPG, I'm actually a casual gamer. And here's a bit more context - over the last few months I've tried a variety of keyboards from high end gaming gear with high end prices to low end cheap stuff so flimsy it feels like it could fall apart even as you take it out of the box. In that keyboard spectrum, this one is not too hot, not too cold, it's just right.

The most expensive gaming keyboard came with all kinds of bells and whistles, from programmable flashing lights to programmable keys for running macros. Unfortunately the software needed to run that keyboard locked up so badly after three days of use, that I couldn't get it unfrozen, making all those expensive extras totally useless. The cheapest low end keyboard stuttered with a noticeable lag bad enough to get any gamer killed in a boss fight. This keyboard is just right for my use. It has a solid, durable feel that does not at all feel cheap or flimsy. There is a muted sound when hitting the keys, enough to let you know that you really are typing but not enough to be distracting. It also stays in place while typing with no slipping or sliding. The cord is long enough that the keyboard doesn't feel tethered on a short leash. It really is plug and play, with no extra software needed to run the thing. And there is no stuttering or discernible lag at all.

The Amazon Basics brand seems to be developing a solid line of products, from clothing to computer gear, that is well made, durable, and affordably priced. This keyboard fits well in the Amazon Basics family and I very much give it 5 stars.

title: Okay For Light Computer Use But Not For Gaming, Extensive Typing Or Other Serious Work
text:
As an old, retired guy I spend a lot of time online gaming, streaming videos, and dabbling on social media. Over the last few months I've tried out a variety of keyboards and mice, some of them high end gaming gear. As soon as you take this keyboard and mouse out of the box it's clear that this is a low end rig. It just doesn't have the solid heft of more expensive equipment. That's not necessarily a bad thing though as I've used some excellent, inexpensive keyboards and mice. Sadly, this product is not of that caliber either.

The compact size makes the keyboard feel cramped when typing. Even as I'm writing this, my fingers are feeling strained from the cramped tightness. The manufacturer makes the 12 function/F key combos seem like a big deal. To me those combos just seem like an unnecessary complication. There are other, more standard ways of doing all those things without having to learn a whole new set of keys. The six "hot keys" seem to be just a set of video controls that duplicate functionality already available on any computer with a standard video player.

The mouse is particularly disappointing for anyone who does gaming. Now I'm just a casual gamer, by no means a hard core one, and even I find this mouse to be a handicap. In my main game you move your character forward by holding down both the left and right mouse buttons simultaneously. With other mice that is no big deal. With this mouse there is a perceptible hesitation or stutter before moving when holding down the buttons like that. That may not sound like a big deal to a non-gamer but that kind of stuttering can quickly get your character killed in a gaming battle. Also, it seems to take some effort to hold those buttons down. My fingers feel a strain in holding these mouse buttons down, a strain I haven't felt with other mice. And yes, I did try the suggested solutions for mouse problems offered in the "Manual" that came with this product (one tiny sheet printed on both sides). They didn't help.

So if you are mostly watching videos and reading Facebook on your computer, you will probably be okay with this gear. Any more serious use than that and you will want to pass on this stuff.

title: A Solid, Durable Cable That Does The Job
text: The headline says it all. This is one of those products that fills an essential niche and does it well. If you want fast recharging for  your iPhone using a reliable cord, this one is for you.

title: Too High Maintence For Me To Bother With
text:
The need for an uninterruptible power source is obvious to anyone with a computer or other expensive electronic equipment. The very day this product arrived, before I even opened the box, a severe thunderstorm knocked out power in my neighborhood. My two computers immediately went down and the screen on one kept flashing on and off even after all the power was dead. So yes, a UPS seems like an important piece of equipment these days. Sadly, this one is not for me. To be fair to the manufacturer though I need to give you a bit of context to help you evaluate if my reaction and this review would be applicable to you or not.

At age 70 I have a pretty low tolerance for muss and fuss. If it requires special handling, if it is a hassle to use, I don't want it. If it's not plug and play, I won't bother with it. For example, I do all my laundry in one load throwing everything in together without any sorting of any kind. It all gets washed and dried on the hot cycle. Anything that can't handle that gets tossed out. I treat everything like that. This UPS looks like an industrial strength product but acts like a delicate little snowflake. Coming out of the box it has 20 pages of instructions they want you to read before using. I didn't bother, just plugged it in, turned it on, and starting using the USB charger to juice up a battery run children's night light. A little while later I noticed a burnt plastic smell and saw the warping on the case that you can see in the attached photos. So this thing is not for me. More detail oriented and careful folks might have better luck with it. Thus I'm giving it a neutral 3 star rating and suggest you read through all the reviews here before deciding whether you want to try it yourself or not.

title: Not Your Local Walmart's Surge Protector
text:
Pay attention to the measurements of this thing. I didn't, and I was shocked by how long it is. Most of us think of a surge protector as a compact set of outlets that can easily fit behind a computer or home entertainment center. Not this one. It's more than four feet long with the outlets in a single line running down that entire length. It's what you might see in a store's electronics department where they have a line of television sets all turned on at the same time so you can readily compare their pictures.

The instructions specify that it is for home not commercial use though. I have trouble visualizing a home set up that would require a row of outlets set in a four foot straight line. Perhaps a home workshop with power equipment? Or a more elaborate computer set up, one with components on a rack of shelves? The surge protector can be wall mounted so it could work well with a rack of components.

Despite my own bafflement I am still giving this surge protector a 5 star rating for a reason. If you have a place where you can use something along these lines, this could be an excellent product for you. It is solidly built with a durable heft to it. The rating for 600 Joules of protection is significant. A quick google search about Joules turned up a site saying that most surge protectors bought for home usage are rated at 200-300 Joules and as such are essentially worthless. The minimum suggested was 400 Joules and this surge protector is comfortably above that. That won't help in case of a lightning strike but should be good for more normal occurrences. I'm looking forward to reading the other reviews of this item to see how people would use it in a home.

P.S. I dunno if they would actually have something like this in a Walmart as I've never shopped there, or anywhere else, for a four foot surge protector. :)

title: A Solid Reliable Hard Drive
text:
Over the years I've used several Seagate hard drives and never had complaints about any of them. In my experience they do manufacture reliable drives. For this particular drive there was little in the way of instructions but none are really needed. On a Windows 10 machine this really is a plug and play product. There is some auto-back up software on the drive if you want to set that up, but since I prefer to simply drag and drop anything I want to save, I can't tell you how that feature works. The small size of this drive is a plus for me. Right now I have three other drives attached to my computer and all are physically much larger. It's nice to have a little one that doesn't take up a lot of space.

Given those other three drives connected to my machine, there is something that should be noted about this drive. A few years ago, 4 terabytes was a massive amount of storage, more than most people would ever need. These days though, 4TB is really not that much. I do a lot of work with videos and photographs and will probably fill this one up in nine months or so. Before buying this drive, think about how much data storage you will reasonably need. If not that much, if you only need a little extra storage or someplace to back up your computer, this is an excellent buy. If you need to save large amounts of data though, you might look into the 8TB - 10TB drives which are also reasonably priced these days.

title: Sleek, Stylish, And Fun - With Only A Few Minor Flaws
text:
It's a rechargeable glow stick or light wand that looks like something out of 2001 A Space Odyssey. What's not to like about that? It comes with a little stand to make it a table light, a wrist holder to make it a jogging light, and a magnetic holder to make it a strip light wherever you might need some extra illumination. It's also fun to just wave about while dancing or goofing around outside at night. There's four different light modes - white, cool blue, warm, and flashing, which can be shifted by tapping one end of the wand. The brightness can also be adjusted from very bright to nightlight dim by holding down that same end. So this really is a versatile lighting tool that goes beyond the traditional flashlight.

There are a few flaws but they are fairly minor. The instructions are minimal and it took me a little bit to figure out that you turn it off by tapping through all four lighting modes. An on/off switch along with a dimmer knob would have been the more traditional approach but that would have clashed with the sleek styling. So I can live with the finger tapping method. I'm still not sure I have the wrist strap set correctly but since I don't jog it's not a big deal to me. The other minor flaw is that the usb recharging cord has a different plug in than the other rechargeable devices I have. That means one more cord to keep track of but again that's not a big deal. Just looking at this thing makes me smile. That and its versatility far outweigh the minor negatives mentioned here so I happily give it five stars.

title: The Speaker Itself Is Good But Bluetooth...
text:
Bottom Line - The speaker itself is excellent but Bluetooth can be an irritating technology.

The speaker is lightweight and even has an attached carrying strap. Unlike a lot of lightweight products though, it doesn't feel flimsy or fragile at all. Instead it has a nice, solid, durable feel to it. While I am not an audiophile, the speaker has a deep, rich sound that I really like. It does well with audiobooks, music, and videos.

The problems seem to be with Bluetooth. One major issue is that the sound stutters while using Bluetooth. It's very noticeable when playing music and very irritating when listening to audiobooks. That's happened with every Bluetooth speaker I've ever tried. A google search indicates that it's a common problem related to the amount of information the computer is trying to pump out to the speaker. There's a checklist of possible issues to go through to try to fix the problem but the stuttering seems all too common with this technology.

Another issue involves changing modes on a Bluetooth speaker. To sidestep the stuttering I plugged this speaker into my computer with a standard jack. It worked fine and the sound was good. When I unplugged it to bring the speaker into another room with me, I had to redo my audio settings. When I plugged it back in with the jack, an audiobook played just fine but there was no sound while playing videos. Again, I had to go into the audio settings and fiddle with them to be able to watch a movie. I've had similar issues with other Bluetooth speakers.

If you are a techie you may be able to resolve such things quickly and easily. The less tech adept you are, the more hassle they will be though. Myself, I'm just going to leave the speaker connected to my pc via a good old fashioned jack because I like its sound. Bluetooth? Bah, I haven't got time to bother with it.

title: A Slow, Clunky, Bug-Ridden Piece of Junk
text:
What I thought I was getting was a competent mid-level machine that could comfortably replace a four year computer that was barely limping along anymore. What I actually got was a useless piece of junk far worse than the decrepit computer it was meant to replace. From the day I took it out of the box there were problems. Opening files, moving or copying them are all painfully slow. Even deleting files takes a long, dragged out time. Programs freeze even if I'm only running one. Forget running multiple programs at once - the machine just locks up. Videos stutter and freeze. Music stops and starts. The list of slow, clunky issues goes on and on. Even worse is the bugginess. If I switch jacks between speakers and headphones, no sound comes out and the indicators tell me no audio output is plugged in even though one clearly is. It takes 2-3 reboots before the computer figures out that yes, the speakers really are plugged in. Then there's the internet - or the lack thereof. At first I kept getting constant disconnects. That deteriorated to the point where now I can't log in at all. The wifi indicator says I'm connected at full strength. The network troubleshooter says there are no problems. All drivers are up to date. The firewall rules are correctly set. Norton Security, Windows Defender and Malwarebytes all say there is nothing bad lurking in my system. All of that and the machine simply won't connect. The Chrome browser just keeps saying websites can't load, pages can't open, because there is no internet connection. (This review is being written on another computer logged into the same network, one that connects just fine. So the issue is not the router, the isp provider or anything like that.)

As a 69 year old with significant physical issues, the thought of reboxing this piece of junk up and hauling it to a shipper to return it feels overwhelming. (My mailman carried it in for me and helped me unbox it.) Originally I had intended to just keep plodding along with it until I could save enough on my limited social security check to replace it. Given the fact that I can't even get online with it anymore though, I am going to have to figure out how to return it. The saddest part is that I have had Acer equipment before that worked just fine. Maybe this one got dropped on its head in shipping or something. I dunno, but I do know it has got to go.

EDIT: And the return process through UPS was a horrific mess. I stopped at the UPS store a couple of days ahead of time to ask them if they could box the computer and monitor up for me if I brought in all the original boxes and packing material. The nice young man working that afternoon said of course though he would have to charge me a dollar for tape. Two days later when I brought everything to the store, a different staff member said they had to charge me $30 for boxes even though I had brought the boxes in. Not only that, but I had forwarded the shipping label to that UPS store via email. They couldn't open the label so I had to go home, print out a screenshot of the label and send them that. The kicker though was that I couldn't leave the computer and monitor at the store while I ran home, ten minutes away. The clerk insisted that I carry it all out to the car again and then carry it back into the store when I returned. For somebody of my age with my health issues, that is not a trivial thing. The last time I tried to return something through UPS they gave me such a run around that I ended up throwing the item away rather than return it to Amazon. The hassle was more than the product was worth. If I ever have to return anything again, I'll ask Amazon if I can do it through Fed Ex or the Post Office. UPS is too much hassle.

title: Some Glitches & Minor Issues But I Love It!
text:
What I wanted was something I could use to listen to tv/movies/music/audiobooks/NPR while doing other work on my desktop computer. The Fire Tablet fits the bill perfectly. The video is crisp and clear. The screen size works nicely for an old guy who's had cataract surgery and wears bifocals. Even the closed captioning I need these days is easily readable on this screen. The speakers are not master quality but are more than adequate for this non-audiophile. This is my first time using Alexa and I love how easy she makes it to get the news and weather before shifting back to Netflix. The whole thing integrates nicely with my Prime account. So far I've just begun to scratch the surface of the options available through Amazon. I wouldn't try to use this tablet to do any heavy computing. That's why I have a high-powered desktop. For the entertainment niche I wanted to fill though, this tablet fits perfectly.

There are some glitches. At times Alexa will freeze up for no discernible reason. Netflix can stutter at times too. This on a new tablet with only minimal apps, used one or two at a time so I shouldn't be overloading it's capabilities. For someone new to Fire Tablets and Alexa, there is a bit of a learning curve. It's not too onerous though. In a short time I expect to be using this tablet familiarly. Every computer I've ever used has had occasional glitches and there is always a learning curve on a new device. So far I haven't come across any deal-breakers and I can whole-heartedly say I love my new tablet.

title: It's Fine With Several Minor Flaws And One Potentially Major One
text:
For streaming Amazon and Netflix videos, playing Steam games, and general web browsing, the screen is beautiful and the computer has been working flawlessly since I got it four month ago. I have no complaints on those fronts. However, there are some other things to talk about.

One of the minor flaws is that the mouse turns off after several minutes of inactivity. You have to click it to turn it back on again before you can use it. That may sound like a trivial thing but it can become an ongoing irritant, especially if you work on several different computers and have to remember to click this particular mouse before usage.

Another minor flaw, one that became a major irritant for me, was that the screen would turn off after 5 minutes without any keyboard or mouse usage. It would even turn off while I was watching movies. In the Windows 10 Power & Sleep settings I would change the screen turn off time from 15 minutes to Never. That would fix the problem temporarily. However, every time I rebooted the computer, the screen turn off time would reset itself to 15 minutes. So I would have to go back into the settings to change it again.

Fiddling with the Windows power plan and scouring the net for solutions turned up nothing. Yes, the power plan was set the way I wanted it. No, the problem had nothing to do with a screensaver. No, there was nothing in the Bios that would trigger the reset. After four months of constant irritation, I finally stumbled across the solution by accident. It seems that ASUS has it's own power plan that overrides the Windows one. The default setting on the ASUS power plan was to turn the screen off after 15 minutes. Changing the ASUS setting to Never finally solved the problem. Why ASUS felt the need to put it's own power plan on their machine when Windows 10 already had a perfectly good one, I have no idea. I especially don't know why ASUS set their plan to override Window's.

That problem touches on the potentially major flaw with ASUS. In trying to find a solution to a minor problem on another ASUS machine, I found that their customer service sucks. When, after much effort, I finally got to talk with a live person, their accent was so thick that I literally could not understand what they were saying. When I asked for someone who spoke clearer English, the service rep got all huffy and I never did get to talk with anyone else and my questions never got answered.

This happened after I had already bought the ASUS Zen Z240-C1, otherwise I wouldn't have gotten a second ASUS machine. Now I've got my fingers crossed that nothing major happens to this one lest I get tangled up in their customer service mess again. So, this machine itself deserves a 4 star review for good performance with only minor flaws. However, ASUS customer service would get no stars from me at all and that will keep me from buying anything else from them.

title: It Didn't Work For Me & ORICO Customer Service Was No Help
text:
The hub didn't work for me. When I tried to access the hard drives plugged into the hub I kept getting I/O error messages and was unable to read any of the files on the hard drives. When I unplugged those hard drives from the hub and connected them directly to my computer, they worked just fine. I did this three times rebooting each time to be sure and got the same results each time. Hard drives plugged into the hub were inaccessible. The same drives plugged directly into my machine worked just fine.

EDIT: After originally posting this review ORICO contacted me by email. Their suggestions did not help at all. When they told me to return the hub to Amazon, repeated phone calls, emails and two visits to UPS were unable to resolve some shipping issues. Since the hub only cost me $10 it wasn't worth all the hassle to send it back. I was simply going to toss the hub into the trash and write it off. At that point, Amazon Customer Service stepped in, refunded the $10, and told me not to bother with shipping the hub back to them. All well and good except ORICO had the nerve to email me again, making the same irrelevant suggestions and asking me to upgrade this review. Sorry folks, your hub didn't work and your customer service didn't help at all. You still get only 1 star from me. Amazon on the other hand gave me 5 star service on this issue.

title: This drive works well for me.
text:
Seven months ago I saw the 5TB drive at a Prime Lightening Deal price that was too good to ignore. Some of the negative reviews did give me pause though. Given the high ratio of positive to negative reviews and that sale price, far lower than I have ever seen for a drive of this size, I finally decided to go for it. Now I'm very glad I did.

I'm an average user, not a techie of any kind so I can't give you any tech specs. However, I can say that the drive has been working just fine on a desktop tower computer running Windows 10 for some seven months now. No heating problems. No crashing. No connection problems. This is with moderately heavy daily usage moving large amounts of data in the 5 - 25GB range. Your mileage may vary but I'm glad I gave this product a try.

title: The Best Flash Drive I've Used
text: Most flash drives I've used have been made of plastic that usually feels flimsy and cheap. This one is solid metal though which is very nice. The capacity/price ratio was also excellent. I've seen a number of 32GB drives that have cost as much or more as this 128GB one. The only thing about this drive I questioned was why it's original format was FAT32 which won't take files larger than 4GB. Given the size of this drive and of the files I wanted to put on it, the NTFS format made much more sense. Luckily, reformatting a drive in Windows 10 is easy and fast. It took just a couple of minutes to format this the way I wanted it. If I need more flash drives, this is the one I'll be looking for.

title: Does not work with a 2018 coachman class C leprechaun?
text: This is just false advertising.  This light has a 4 pin camera connector that does not work with the Coachman factory 5 pin connector!!

title: Great Quality for great price
text: If your desktop didnt come with speakers, well let me tell you this is the product for you! The sound quality is great! It doesn't take up too much room to setup and it isn't complicated to setup. Once plugged in just make sure the computer knows those are the speakers and its done!!!!

title: Good value
text: Nice and heavy duty multiple electronic chargers. My only complaint is that the android charger on both are very sharp (the two metal teeth plug-in part is not smooth - am a bit worried it will break off in the device while inserting or removing).

title: Like portability
text: Good portability, folds and comes in a nice pouch for taking with you. But I don't think it's very sturdy - would rather it had some sort of tray to sit on. I have a rather heavy laptop, so maybe it's just me. The newer laptops are much lighter, but the one I take to clients is a heavier one.

title: Corrects some issues with DVD
text: Love the size. The best part is that the player corrects some of the freezing/stopping issues with some DVD's. I had purchased a retail DVD that kept freezing and then starting again a few minutes later (on other players). It got to a point in the movie that it froze and would not unfreeze on it's own - I had to skip quite a bit of the movie to free it (the FF wouldn't work on the big freeze). When playing on this machine, the DVD froze, but the player corrected it almost immediately and continued on without losing part of the film. When it got to the big freeze, it corrected it and continued playing it, again, not losing part of the film. I have had many DVD players throughout the decades, but never one that corrected flaws in the DVD itself. I am very, very happy with this, as sometimes you cannot get another copy of the DVD because the movie or TV show is no longer being manufactured. Also, the DVD doesn't make noise when it's being played. I have a very expensive player from a few years back and it has developed a noise from the rotation of the DVD being played and it drives me crazy. No noise on this one.

title: Stay put and perfect size
text: Perfect - they fit not only my laptop, but also my kindles. And they stay put. Although it states you can remove and re-use them, I don't remove them as I don't want the cameras on my devices. For me, they work exactly as I need them to.

title: Use for Outside
text:
Use for Outside
By IBSuzyQ on Feb 26, 2017 10:14:33 PM

I feed wild animals on my property, and now have feral cats who have joined the frey. I have many blind spots around my house, so these are perfect for watching who comes to visit, dine or sleep. Couldn't run wires to cameras, so love this is wireless. and so easy to put up. Picture is very clear and you can zoom in; also get notifications on my iPhone and emails to my computer when motion is detected on a camera. I have seven cameras with the hub. Love these!!

title: Works great for a mobile printer bag
text: I bought this for an HP OfficeJet 200 mobile printer. I do not take my printer on planes, but rather in my car as I travel to clients. I mention this because the cases sold specifically for mobile printers are very well padded or hard-sided. This is a laptop bag, but opens completely flat and has a strap that holds the printer. It also can hold both replacement BW & Color ink cartridges at once, plus power cord. There is a full pocket inside that holds the booklet and half a ream of paper without distorting paper. The specific mobile printer cases are at least $80 - this was under $20, and besides the heavier padding of the specific cases, there is not much difference. The printer itself is hard and folds completely, so unless you are worried about it getting crushed (like in a plane overhead bin), this works great. I figure if it is ok for a laptop, the printer should be no difference. The printer is 4'1/4" H, and this bag is about 3-1/2", but since it is not a hard-sided case, it fits well. I checked what it would be like if you used it for a laptop (it's intended use) just to see how it fit, and there is plenty of room for cords, accessories, and also an outside pocket for pens, etc. Very substantial bag for $20. Recommend.

title: Wonderful cover
text: I have a Paperwhite Kindle and bought this cover for that size. Loved it. When I bought the Kindle Fire HD 8.9", I bought a leather (like) cover with a keypad (the description said leather, but it clearly wasn't). I didn't like it, it didn't clasp well and kept moving the Kindle around inside. I thought, "I wish I could get a cover like on my regular Kindle." I looked and looked through Amazon and found it! It is a wonderful cover, the Kindle Fire doesn't move around at all - it is so perfectly snug inside and is very comfortable to hold. I also have dropped both with this cover and it protected the Kindles. It may seem pricy, but it is real leather and the difference is noticeable. I bought the purple, it is a deep, rich purple. I am very happy with this cover. By the way, I have had my Paperwhite cover for over two years and it still looks new - unlike "leather-like" covers that wear and tear easily. And it was a lighter color and there are no stains either.  I expect this cover to last many years.

title: Best Android Watch On The Planet
text: I am no one's fitness freak at my age, but I do have things that I need to monitor for my continued good health. I decided to go all Samsung with this device cycle and I'm glad I did. I went with the Bluetooth only version because I always keep my phone on or near my person, and spending the money on an LTE capability and line for the watch does not make sense for me. Even without the phone line, this watch does just about everything but sign my paycheck. It's easy to set up and use. It interfaces well with my S22 Ultra and my Galaxy Buds 2 Pro, providing useful control of both. The available apps, faces and features should satisfy the most demanding user. Battery life is outstanding. I'm getting more than 2 days of continuous use on each charge. Charging is wireless and quick. If you have run it all the way down, it will take a couple of hours to bring it back to full charge, but a half hour will give you useful service time. I have picked up a few things that make my use nice and easy. You can read my reviews on them if you want. I cannot recommend this watch highly enough. Samsung has a winner here.

title: Love this watch and monitor
text:
My wife got this for me for my 40th birthday. Clearly, a subtle signal that I needed to workout more and was already over the hill and needed a heart monitor. She also got it because I'm a bit "techy" and the other reviews stated that you could track an immense amount of information with the GPS and monitor.

I absolutely love my Garmin. I use it all the time when I run and bike and religiously upload the information. It is outstanding for heart zone workouts and maintaining pace and can really give you a sense of how you're tracking on your regular routes. The upload and sync is easy. Over the 18 months I've had this, I have transitioned from PC to Mac and both syncs work well. PC actually works better and the application has better rendering. This is actually the only knock I have. I would have expected the Mac version to be more polished. That said, all the data is there and can be easily reviewed.

The GPS tracks well. The initial satellite sync can take a while, but I've found that if I bypass it by hitting the mode button, it will still pick up satellites and track pace and location relatively quickly. The display can be easily customized to show the information that you care about and there's a lot of workouts that you can program to augment your training.

The heart monitor works well. I've run into two issues when cycling where if I have a layer, like a wick shirt for running or biking, on, it can cause a strange heartbeat spike. This is actually due to some initial static that gets generated with some of the workout shirts, but can be resolved by sweating, or (what I do) licking your hand and wiping a bit of spit on the underside of the sensor before working out. I'm like accurate stats and seeing a 197 heart rate is disconcerting to me. I have not had to replace any battery on the monitor yet and it's comfortable and sturdy.

I absolutely love this thing and to this day, my wife and I agree, that it is one of the best gifts ever.

title: Best earplugs I've owned
text:
I've gone through multiple earplugs in recent years, and these are by far, the tops for solid, rich sound at this price. The noise canceling is outstanding and I've even just used them as earplugs on flights for when I want to sleep. I recently forgot them on a trip and purchased a cheaper pair at the airport. The difference is enormous.

That said, I think there are two draw-backs in my opinion: (a) even though the fit is snug, when I run do other mobile activities, the earplugs fall out occasionally (b) this isn't the worst thing given that the noise canceling probably doesn't make them the safest to wear when running or biking.

title: Disapointed...Updated from 2 to 5 stars
text:
I bought this screen protector for my Kindle Touch earlier this year and love it. I just bought a Kindle Paperwhite and I had one left over from the first order. It fit perfectly, except the small gap ended up on the top and I did not realize that the line cut through the top of the menu until I turned it on to read. I'd rather have the gap at the bottom where it's not noticeable so I ordered another pack. I just got my order today and after two screens, I realized that they were too wide for the Paperwhite screen. I had to cut the last screen to get it to fit. I was bummed since it fit great before and I thought I'd get it perfect on the first try. I'm not completely happy with the final result but I don't want to pay for another pack not knowing which size I'm going to get. Also the edges used to be rounded and they aren't anymore so I can't get the edges to stick flat to the screen which makes the screen protector more noticeable, whereas on my Kindle Touch, I actually have to look carefully to see where the edges are. I just don't understand why these things changed. I don't know if I got a bad batch but if this is the size they are selling now, they shouldn't advertise that it fits the Paperwhite.
As far as applying, I give that four stars. I can normally get a bubble-free application. If anything goes wrong it's usually a speck of dust. I use compressed air and a credit card to get the best results. A credit card is more solid than the smoothing card it comes with so it works a lot better.

UPDATE 11/18/2012: The GreatShield company responded to my review and they sent me a replacement order right away. Awesome customer service from those guys. After getting my replacement, I can safely say that the order I had before was defective. The new order fit the screen perfectly and the edges are rounded. It is installed on my Kindle Paperwhite and I'm a happy customer. In light of this, I have changed my rating from 2 stars to 5 stars.

I would recommend this product to others.

title: Love, love, love it!
text: I wanted to make the jump to my first cordless mouse but I wasn't sure about their reliability.  I am a gamer and when talking to hardcore gamers they say they would never use a cordless when they play.  But the freedom of having less wires was too hard to ignore.  I had ordered and tried two other wireless mice (both also Logitech) and I wasn't impressed and returned them both.  The G7 was my last resort since it was the priciest.  I've had this mouse for about 2 months now and I LOVE it!  Prior to the G7 I was using the Logitech MX518 and I believe they are about the same size and shape so the feel is the same.  It moves much smoother than the MX518.  I was concerned about the batteries since I read a lot of complaints about them in prior reviews.  I find that it is a non-issue.  I normally have to switch the battery once a day and it literally takes me 10 seconds (maybe even less) to do it.  I experience no lag with this mouse at all.  It performs just like a wired mouse.  I really can't tell the difference.  The G7 is a bit more pricier but I am a firm believer of you get what you pay for.  This is the best mouse I have ever owned.  I would definitely recommend it.

title: Logitech USB Desktop Microphone
text: I just wanted a basic microphone to use with Ventrillo to be able to talk to my in-game buddies.  This is the first mic I have ever bought. My friends say my voice is crystal clear.  I also like that I don't have to be  really near the mic to be heard.  My only complaint is that sometimes I echo to my friends.  I'm sure that is because I'm not using headphones and it is picking up my speaker sounds.  It is not bothersome enough for me to switch to a headset which I didn't want to do.  I spend long hours on the game and cringe at the thought of wearing headphones for that long.  Great little starter mic to use with chat especially for the price.  I even bought a second one for my husband's desktop.  I've had it for a little over a year now and it is still going strong.  I've never had a problem with it.  Great buy.

The USB cord is the perfect length since I already have a jumble of wires behind my laptop so that was a plus.  Only thing I really would like is auto focus but once you focus it the first time, you don't really need to adjust it anymore.  Overall I am very pleased with this purchase.

title: Nearly Perfect
text:
