It does not take up a lot of room in whatever you chose to carry it in. The headphones fit inside the case nicely (face down), and there is a zippered pouch inside that holds the removable cord. The headphones themselves are sleek looking and attractive. They are black with just a splash of silver.
(2) Cool Feature: Making the cord removable was a great feature. Why? If you ever get a short in the cord, you have the option of simply ordering another cord without having to replace the entire unit. The length of the cord is fantastic....not too long, not too short. The only things that I would probably change about these headphones (although it doesn't affect my love of the product) is to include a volume control button and make the cord a little more decorative (maybe add a nice stripe of red..or something to add some bling). Ok that is just the girl in me.
(3) Fit: The ear muffs (or headphones) fit snuggly over the entire ear. They are nicely padded and comfortable. They do NOT cause irritation from prolonged use or press against the ear causing any discomfort.
(4) Sound quality: The sound quality of the KOSS is great or comparable, especially when I compare it to other sets that I have had in the past. They aren't bass heavy like Beats, but offer decent sound quality like Sennheiser, V-Moda or Sony. The balance and frequency response are good. No matter the type of music.. from Alternative, to Neo Soul, Jazz, Classical to Rock....I get great sound. I am very impressed by the quality.

And finally I will mention:
(5) Cost. This headset will cost you about $150, which is comparable to other headphones of this quality. I truly believe for the money, you are getting a pretty great buy. The sound quality and features make this a great set of headphones for those in the market to consider. You definitely get a lot of bang for your buck. 5 stars

title: Boom, Boom, Pow! 4 stars
text:
For some purchasing this pair of BOSE SoundTrue headphones would be quite the investment. The question then becomes "are these headphones worth the money?" Over the last two years or so, I have purchased several headphones as gifts. My sons (both teens) had been begging for headphones, specifically the Beats by Dre, for some time. So began my research on headphones on the market. I wanted a quality product for a reasonable price. So when Amazon offered a special on the V-Moda headsets, during the holidays two years ago, I couldn't pass up the deal. I purchased two pair and was pleased. Both of my sons loved them, especially when they compared them to their friends "Beats". The V-Modas were sturdy and not as bass heavy as the Beats. The bass of the V-Moda wasn't amplified and overwhelming. They didn't feel that they were sacrificing sound quality or style. During this same time period, my husband purchased two sets of Sennheiser (PX 100 and 250 series), one for himself and another as a Christmas gift. One set was around the ear and the other, over the ear. So, over a two year time span, I have had the opportunity to listen to music with all of these headphones and can offer an opinion. And while I am not an expert, I am an average wife and mother who intends to use these headphones for recreational purposes (i.e., when cleaning the house, walking in the neighborhood, etc) only.

These headphones are:

1. Extremely light weight. Light enough to put in a purse, book-bag or briefcase, etc. without weighing you down.
2. Comfortable. The ear-covers and headband are padded and extremely comfortable when worn. They block out most if not all of the outside noise. Your ears are completely covered and the sound is crystal clear. **While the ears of the set remain secure or in place, I did notice that the headphone would fall down occasionally. To correct this, I would suggest that you adjust the headphones tighter than you normally would, especially if you have thick hair and this seems to correct the problem.
3. Functional. There is a long cord that attaches from your device to the headset. The long cord gives you some flexibility and mobility. But caution, you may want to secure some of the cord if you are using an armband type holder for your device. Otherwise the cord might get stuck on stuff while you are using it. You can operate various functions (volume, etc) from the back of the microphone. It is located on the cord near your mouth. However, I do wish that the microphone with the function button was lower on the cord, or could be adjusted because while it is comfortable when using the microphone, it isn't when you adjust the sound. If it was further down, you could adjust the sound easier and see the buttons clearly.
4. Can be used with multiple devices. I use mine with my IPOD, IPAD, computer and Android phone (Nexus 4, Google Phone).
5. Enclosed in a convenient carrying case. It fits well in most bags or luggage. They are easy to pack up and travel with.
6. Sound quality. While not bass heavy at all, I think these are perfect for all kinds of music. My playlist includes music from artists like Mree, Daley, Jhene Aiko, The Weekend, Diana Krall, Young Summer and Cary Brothers...and the sound is great. These headphones have a nice, kind of surround sound quality. These definitely complement all music types. But if you want deep bass, I wouldn't recommend these. But if you want clear sound, these are the headphones for you.
7. Kind of Expensive. These headphones cost about $180. And while that price is comparable to others (i.e., The V-Modas are around $200 and the Beats can range from $200 to $300.) on the market, are you getting the same features for the price? Probably. However, if you are a DJ or money is no object, you may not blink at the price, hence viewing it as an investment. But for the average consumer, you have to consider the features and decide if they are worth the money. So if you aren't looking for bass heavy or exaggerated sound, and you like the fact that these completely cover the entire ear, these are the perfect headphones for you. I give them 4 stars.

title: A "sweet" little product and it is portable too! 4.5 stars
text:
I will give you the down and dirty in short bullet form. Hopefully this answers most questions.

PROS of this product
* Easy to set up and use.
* Quality of the sound is good and it isn't heavy on the bass. Music is clear. The one speaker (mono) gives off great sound.
*Item is portable and sturdy.
*Item has Bluetooth function or you can hook it straight to your device. (I used my son's cord from his VModa head-set to connect to my android. ) Otherwise I used the Bluetooth function on my IPAD, IPOD and Nexus 4 (android phone) with no problem. The range or reception is decent. I didn't have any breaks in the connection, but I really didn't try to go too far. I tend to stay in the same room or in the general area, while listening to music.
*You can control the sound from your device or from the speaker. AND you can still pause your music using your device.
*Easy to charge. I really liked the fact that it is compatible with any USB or android charger. Meaning if you have an Apple device (ex., IPOD or IPAD), etc you can use the charger to charge this speaker. Or at least use the base portion of the charger. If you have an android, you can use that cord as well. The charge life for the battery is reasonable, and it even comes with a lithium battery.
*You can attach it to a book-bag or backpack (as shown in the photo), but I just place it where I want it to be and put it down. It is small enough (about the size of the palm of my hand) to fit into any purse, or bag without making it too heavy. Basically you can use this anywhere (in the home, camping, on trips, at the beach) and at any time.
* It's cute (I have the black. It kind of looks like a smashed soda can). Again, it's small. There are controls and indicator lights on the bottom of the device. The charge area is located on the top.
*Price seems comparable with other products of this sort (wireless speakers) on the market.

THINGS I WOULD CHANGE (not really a CON) about this product:
*The USB cord could be a bit longer. It was a little short for my tastes. But at least it's versatile.

So, as you can see, I was pleased with this product. The PROS definitely outweigh the "things that I would change" category. It had everything that made this a winner. It was easy to set up, and has decent sound quality. I definitely would recommend it.

title: Does what it is suppose to do.
text: The Logitech Wireless Mouse for Windows 7/8 is great. My kids use it with their laptops, and my husband has used it with our desktop. It does exactly what it should do. The size and shape are perfect. I'm a girl (smile) and it fits and feels well in my hand. My sons and husband have used the mouse, so I know that it is comfortable for someone with larger hands too. It also doesn't matter if you are left or right handed (ambidextrous), both can use it. There is a tiny little device that fits securely into the USB port of your laptop or desktop computer. It allows you to connect the device to another with little or no effort.  There are several shortcut buttons to Windows (located on the top & thumb area) that I rarely use (my son does because he has a Windows 8 laptop), but I could see where they can be helpful. You even have a wheel (located on the top) that is helpful for navigating a page. I haven't had a problem with the battery (I use the sleep mode) which so far has conserved its battery life. Not to mention that there is a handy indicator light. And I also appreciated the fact that this mouse came (conveniently enough) with an AA battery already enclosed. I would highly recommend this device.

title: For the price, it can't be beat.
text: I found myself in the market to replace my Belkin IPOD armband (the Velcro began separating from armband). I knew that it would probably be cheaper to just buy another one, than to try and repair it. Afterall, it didn't have to be especially cute, but practical and functional. Since I am planning a family (beach) vacation for the summer, I PLAN to start working out (my motivation being a vision of me in a bathing suit). But I ALSO know that I need something else to motivate and inspire me....so listening to music or an audiobook will definitely do the trick. The Griffin Streamline appears to be perfect for my 3rd generation Nano. Believe it or not, I wasn't wrong or disappointed. The Streamline is reasonably priced, and definitely does the job. It even looks a lot like my first one (Belkin), with the exception that the portion that surrounds the face of the IPOD is framed by hard plastic. This is the only thing that I would warn the consumer about....over time, I could see the hard plastic that surrounds the face of the IPOD cracking. Anyway, I haven't had any trouble selecting or manipulating the IPOD. The only drawback is the fact that you have to turn the Nano upside down so that you can access the earbuds and charger. The Nano fits snuggly in the case and doesn't move. The armband is adjustable and comfortable. And because I don't really sweat, I don't think that I will have to worry about the condensation collecting, around or behind it. The pack is slightly padded and appears to offer just the right amount of protection. With the exception of having to flip the device upside down so that you can access the cords, for the price and for what I intend to do with this product, it is absolutely perfect.

title: The perfect Christmas gift for the beginner photographer.
text:
**Please note that this review was written by a novice photographer.
I have been asking my husband for a camera for years. You know how it is....the entire time he is taking pictures with his Nikon D80 (he fancies himself a fantastic photographer...and he is), I am constantly in his ear telling how what I see and envision would make a better picture. I also tell him how he should take a picture of something that I believe will make him the next Ansel Adams. And I complete the photo shoot with, "if only I had really good camera, I would"..... Well, I guess he was tired of hearing it, and decided to buy me this camera (for Christmas thru Amazon) if for no other reason than to shut me up. I guess it was his way of putting "his" money where "my" mouth is, and I was delighted.

Now what is there to like about this camera.
-This camera is user friendly and great for a beginner photographer or at least one that is ready to move from a camera like a Nikon CoolPix. It is perfect for still shots and video (HD). It is easy to select a setting (portrait, action, etc), point and shoot. It focuses automatically (press halfway) and can be manually adjusted (tight or far away photos). There is a menu that allows you to edit and even make images, black and white. **Please note that this is the one feature that no matter how much I read the manual, I can't quite get it to do what I would like. I can edit a picture, change it to black & white, and even use the zoom tool, but when I attempt to save it, it won't. That is a feature that I will have to continue to fool with. And if anyone can help me, I would appreciate it.
-You can manipulate the viewing screen...it flips out and turns (for use while recording video) so that you can view it. Or you can swivel, flip and turn the screen around and collapse it against the body of the camera. This allows you to see or view the pictures you are taking or have taken.
- This camera takes crisp/clear photos. They are amazingly clear.
-This camera has a continuously shoot feature/function. It is great for my son's wrestling matches.
-This camera has an automatic flash that is useful if you aren't sure about the lighting.
-This camera is light (weight wise) enough to carry around for a long period of time (your hand won't get tired), but it also comes with a comfortable and adjustable neck strap. There are also cords that come with the camera so that you can use with the computer or TV.
-The battery life is decent. I assume that it also depends on how many videos you do versus still shots. However, I have done both and found and didn't have a problem. This camera also comes with a convenient battery charger.
Overall, I love my new Canon Rebel T3i and look forward to (a) learning everything about it that I can and (2) taking tons of fantastic pictures for years to come.

title: I'm officially a hit with my sons! They love these headphones.
text:
I was looking for stocking stuffers for my two teenaged boys. Both had expressed an interest in the Beats by Dre. I don't know about you, but I was looking for a reasonable pair of headphones to accompany other high priced gifts (new Xbox, Laptop etc) they were getting for Christmas. BUT paying almost $200 for the Beats seemed unreasonable. So when these (V-Moda, Crossfade LP) were highlighted on Amazon on Black Friday, I seized the opportunity and purchased two pair (which was still cheaper than one pair of Beats), and hoped that I could rely on the reviews that I read. (Please note that I did read reviews for Beats, and found that the V-Moda pair received more positive reviews.) So with both sets of reviews under my belt, I begin to compare the features and was even more convinced that I had made a wise purchase. (Also note that later my sons were able to compare them with the Solo Beats by Dre and they still liked the Crossfades better.)

Features that my sons say make these a standout amongst most headsets:
* The overall sound quality is great and not too bass heavy.
*The over the ear covers (ear piece) have memory cushions. They are very comfortable and you can't hear outside noise (Of course I found this to be true when they could not hear me calling them. Of course, they may be ignoring me). I also can't hear the music that they are listening to.
* The volume or pause feature can be used from a control button on the cord. They even say that besides skipping songs, the rarely have to touch their devices when using these headphones.
* These earphones are versatile and can be used with multiple devices (i.e., the computer, Ipod, cell phones, etc). They are able to even use them in the car by connecting with the stereo.
* These headphones are stylish and attractive. I ordered one pair in Phantom Chrome and the other in Phantom Black.

And finally, what Mom likes about the headphones...well, the price. These headphones were reasonably priced and offered the same features as the Beats. And later when I compared them with the Beats, they appear to be better quality in terms of sound quality and workmanship (the Beats are plastic looking and don't seem to be as well constructed as the Crossfade, which seems sturdy).
Finally, overall for the money I think I got a top notch product. I highly recommend these to anyone on the market for some headphones and give this product five (5) stars.

title: A wonderful stocking stuffer.
text: This case is easy to attach to your device and offers state of the art protection for my son's Ipod touch. Arrived on time and in excellent condition.

title: A lot for your money.
text: When I ordered the Cyber Acoustics CA-3908 3 piece set, I thought it would be perfect for our home office. I thought it would enhance the music that I played from my computer, as well as hook up easily to other devices. What I received was better than I could have imagined. Instead of being something that I could only use in the home office, I found that this system is a great little item for just about anywhere in the house. My sons have used it to attach to a variety of other devices...the IPOD touch, the Xbox, cell phones (I have a G2), and our personal PC. The sound quality is great and carries well throughout the house.  No matter what kind of music you are listening to (bass heavy or not), the sound comes across with no vibration or distortion.  This speaker system is easy to setup with only two wires connecting the subwoofer. The system is compact and doesn't take up too much space. Come to think of it, this system would even be perfect for a dorm room or apartment.  The volume control, on/off switch, headphone jack are located on a circular dial.  Overall, I am extremely pleased with this item and believe that it is a small investment for a quality system. I give it 5 stars.

title: Just enough technology for me!
text:
When I selected the Philips AS140/Fidelio Docking System for the Android, I really did not have any expectations only the hope that it would be easy to set up and do what I wanted it to do....play music and maybe wake me up. I definitely did not want something too complicated or difficult to operate. And to be honest, the Philips has just the right amount of technology and features for me because there are times when I am technically challenged. Simply stated, the directions for electronics need to be easy to read and understand. And who could ask for more than easy to follow directions will illustrations (even in Spanish if you need them)? And while I probably have not untapped all of its possibilities, I think I have a decent understanding of its basic features.

Setting up the Philips was easy enough. You simply go to the Android Market and install Songbird on your phone and PC (this allows you to download music and access it). In general, I consider the Philips Docking Station to be a super tuner (I am sure that there is a better word for it...but again, I am a girl), which allows you to access local and internet radio stations as well as podcast). You even have an option for an alarm clock and timer. When you attach your android phone (I have the LG G2x and it fits perfectly with or without the case), you can use the blue tooth feature as sort of a remote control. The phone doesn't even have to be attached to the docking station for you to surf radio stations or podcast. I was even able to access "Pandora" (a station that I access on my telephone) and listen to my favorite music selections. And remember, you aren't limited to just the radio, or other programs, but you can download music (from Songbird) to your PC and access it from your phone.

The positive things about the product:
(1) Easy set up. Download program, and you are in business!
(2) Decent sound quality. The sound is clear. It seems a little heavy at times on the bass, but maybe that is simply because I need to play with the features a little more and learn how to address it.
(3) The time automatically syncs between your cell phone and the station so you don't have to really worry about it.
(4) Your phone charges while docked.
(5) The blue tooth technology allows you to use your phone as a remote...changing the stations easily.
(6) There is a timer and alarm feature/option.
(7) Downloading music is simple.
(8) It's cute and doesn't take up a whole lot of space on your nightstand or dresser. And if you don't want to necessarily use it as an alarm clock, you could even use it in your kitchen. It's probably better than one of those under the cabinet radios.

Overall, I like the Philips AS140/37, it has some pretty neat features that a girl who isn't necessarily technologically savvy can enjoy. It's easy to set up and use. I give this system a solid 4.

title: This product arrived and was not exactly what I thought it would be. .
text: This is one of those items that was difficult for me to review. Why?  Because there were good attributes and some bad ones, which made me vacillate between a 3 and a 4. The main reason.....well, the bag was not exactly what I thought it would be. For some reason I felt that I would be able to use this product in the manner it was advertised...as a portable desk or mobile work station. Unfortunately it wasn't nearly easy to use as I thought, my resolve even more sure as I lay in bed writing this review. Perhaps I should have played with various surfaces, like a table tray versus my lap, but it just didn't seem as comfortable as I expected. To me, the little ledge did not hold the IPAD as steadily as it appeared in the pictures. The side bands that offer support also don't seem to be as taunt as they should be. Now the positive things (which I think outweigh the other stuff). For me, I love the fact that this bag offers storage space for everything that you'd need for your IPAD if you were traveling or just jetting around town. Instead of the work station concept, I decided that I would use this bag primarily to protect my IPAD, as well as my accessories. In essence, this is the perfect all-in-one electronic travel case. This basic black bag has lots useful compartments that can be used to hold a keyboard (securely), adaptors, chargers, wires, pens, or virtually anything that you think you could use while working and traveling.  And the bag can be carried by its versital handles or comfortable shoulder strap. And to be honest, as a girlie-girl, I love the fact that the bag is small, useful and compact. You could even throw it into an ever bigger purse, or just add your identification and a few dollars and travel to Starbucks and enjoy.

title: The perfect thing to protect!
text: I was looking for the perfect shield to protect the face of my new Apple IPAD. I wanted something that was durable, that would protect the face, and basically look like nothing was there. Being a girl, I knew that I wouldn't be able to put it on (that's a little job for the old hubby), but I knew exactly what I wanted. And of course, my husband did a fine job adhering the cover to the IPAD, there are absolutely no bubbles. It isn't too thick (it slides smoothly in my new IPAD cover), looks smooth (not one wrinkle) and is really clear (crystal clear, absolutely no haze). I can't even tell that there is anything on the front of it AT ALL. And if you get a few stray fingerprints, you can wipe it off with one of those soft clothes that you use to wipe the lenses of your glasses or camera with. And it is as good as new. And to top it all off, they offer a lifetime warranty/guarantee that it won't mess up. Finally, I couldn't beat Amazon's price. The same item was slightly cheaper ordering this item from Amazon versus purchasing it at Target. So on top of everything, I feel like I got a great deal for a great item. Overall, great purchase. I wholeheartedly give the Zagg invisibleSHIELD a "5" and would recommend it to anyone.

title: Just as advertised!
text:
The Logitech Pad N120 is light weight, quiet and cute.....just as advertised! The "cooling" pad is extremely light weight, and can easily be held between two fingers. It is really slim (not bulky at all) and therefore doesn't take up much space when stored. It is the perfect size (at least for a DELL) and comfortable to use anywhere. There is a USB cord that once connected to your laptop, turns on the fan which keeps cool air circulating underneath. And when the USB is not being used, the cord can be hidden underneath the cooling pad, its cord slipping smoothly into the area where it is designed to go. The fan of the Logitech Pad is extremely quiet. I can barely hear it when it is on. And finally, this cooling pad seems to be well worth the money. While it might be more expensive than some I have seen, it seems worth the money, and definitely has those features that I think most people desire.

Quality and Style- 5
Price - Reasonable (considering the features)
Features - 5
Overall - 5

title: Eco-nique = Unique!
text:
For Christmas I received the Kindle and this cover. Trust me when I tell you that selecting just the right cover is as important as selecting the Kindle itself. Isn't it all about the "packaging" or the look of your kindle. Anyway, this cover is fabulous. The hemp-like material with the exotic design is "cool looking", and there is just enough faux leather to make the case look old worldly. I also don't think the cover, being a deep milk chocolate color, will ever look dirty. This case not only looks great, but is light weight, durable and extremely sturdy. The Kindle slips right into the appropriate space easily and is secured by a snap. I prefer this slide in style versus the one where the bands just cover the corners of the Kindle. If dropped, there doesn't appear to be the possibility of it slipping out of the enclosure, so you feel better knowing that it is safely secured. Inside, there is even a place to put a pen or stylus, if you want. I haven't tried that feature out or even evaluated if the cover still closes securely with a pen or stylus in place because there is a feature in the Kindle that allows you to create notes, so I haven't found the need to write anything down YET! And finally on the rear of the cover, there are vents which allow for sound so that option is still available.

Warning: My husband said that when he ordered this case, it took longer than expected to arrive. It was apparently from Britain and had to go thru customs before it arrived. He did mention that he feared it would not make it in time, but never fear it was here before Christmas and waiting under the tree. BUT even so, it would definitely be worth the wait. The only other thing that I will mention is that I kind of wished he had gotten this same cover with a light. The reason that I did not send it back was because it is the prettiest cover that I have seen that offered the features (slide entry and durable fabric) that I would have wanted. My husband really took his time selecting this gift and I was pleased, so I didn't even consider sending it back to get one with the light, I just added a light that I purchased from Target.

Durability - 5
Appearance - 5
Functionality - 5
Overall - 5++ (Can't say enough about how great it is.)

title: Easy to set up. Easy to use. Small and lightweight..

For someone who isn't particularly technically savvy, or who wants to do nothing more than type, surf and play around....this keyboard is more than enough. It's small and fits on my lap (my kids have even used it for the Xbox..how I don't know...they're technically savvy, not me); the keys are easy to locate (I know people have mentioned the numbers, but I didn't have a problem using the ones that are on the top of the keyboard). While I realize that some who may have ordered this keyboard are really using it for complicated or difficult tasks, I think it is perfect for amateurs like ME. Although I still wish there was a mouse (wishful thinking since it is a keyboard), there are easy to use arrow keys that allow you to move easily. And talking about a setup for DUMMIES.....it was just three EASY steps that anyone should be able to follow.....put in the batteries, the USB, and turn on (just two buttons) and you are done. How easy can it get? So, if you want a small, easy to use keyboard, this is the one for you and it's affordable to boot!

Other than that, the keyboard is very well made and there are no complaints. I answered a question to help someone with their case because they were having issues trying to take off the keyboard case. What I do to remove my keyboard to clean my iPad is that I press on the center of the apple on my iPad and push and then I am able to remove it. If you try it any other way, you will break fingernails because it fits very snug to the iPad. This keyboard is also very sturdy. I’ve had keyboards where they want to close on me but this keyboard stays open and doesn’t try to close on me as I type. Very well made and I highly recommend!

title: Anyone Who experienced "CONNECTED AS USB 2" or "unstable connection" problem LOOK HERE!!!!!!!
text:
Firstly, if you want to use a cable link, please remember to turn off the air link in the headset's setting.
I had tried many times and found that the cable was first recognized as a USB 3 cable when you connect it.
Then it will turn to USB 2 （if) after you click "allow device access file" on your headset.
That option actually means that you choose to use the line as a "file transfer" cable instead of a pure link cable.
To solve this problem, you need to close the "allow device access file option" in your headset's setting or choose "not to allow device access file"(I did not try this one).
So that your cable will be recognized as a normal USB 3 cable with (mine was 2.8 - 2.9 GBMS).'

Overall DONT USE, unless you want to spend literal HOURS stripping cables to install this into your server rack. If any board failures in rack happens you are going to spend hours de-tangleing wires. Most other brands just have direct plug-ins and are plug and play.

title: Cheaply made, blurry and grainy
text:
Horrible customer service btw. I contacted them twice, once because the tv keeps losing it's wi-fi connection and the other time because the flimsy lightweight stand it comes with broke after a month. Don't move the tv too much to clean or anything, the stand can't handle the weight of the monitor. Anyway, they sent me to some parts websites they found and the stand costs almost $90 to buy (they won't replace it).

Image quality is good for cartoons/animations but terrible for anything else. It's grainy and blurry.

Stand is too bendy for the weight of the tv, It seems to buckle a little when the tv is moved or turned. Mine broke after about a month while I was cleaning.

Amazon isn't connected yet. They advertise the icon, but pay attention to the description. They expect to connect with Amazon in the future.

Wi-fi connection shows as "strong" but frequently goes out (even though it says it's a strong connection, don't rely on that). We have to unplug and wait a minute and restart too often.

Netflix app is not reliable either. It works half the time, but the other half, it goes out. And I know it's not Netflix because I can connect on other devices with no problems. Again, unplug and restart to "reset" the connection to Netflix.

Customer service is rude and nobody I spoke with or chatted with online seems to care about the customer at all. In fact they blame the customer for anything that goes wrong. The people I dealt with spoke down to me and made me feel like I didn't deserve their help, blamed me for the wi-fi connection, the broken stand, and made me feel like I was wasting their time.

Other than that, the tv is ok. I'm not going to say I'm impressed based on the price. I work hard for my money and if the company advertises high quality, I expect high quality, no matter how much it costs. False advertising is a bad practice, and we're conditioned to expect less all the time. But my time and money is worth every penny, so $350 may be cheaper than other products, but I value my money and expect things to work as expected, as advertised, and nothing less.

title: Decent components, poor execution
text:
Slept two nights with these headphones in their stock configuration and decided I could create something far superior.
For several years I’ve owned and extensively used a pair of the original wired SleepPhones. They are extremely comfortable. The drivers are only 2-3mm thick and sandwiched between two layers of felt. The fleece headband stayed in place without feeling constrictive. It was also easy to wash - open the hook and loop closure on the back, pulled out the speakers and wires, wash, dry, re-install.
By contrast, MusiCozy uses thicker drivers (granted, the frequency response is better than the SleepPhone drivers) then adds a rubber cover, then covers that with a thin jersey fabric. The headband was painfully tight, and I don’t have a big head (22.5”). After the first night, I stretched the headband over a small throw pillow for a day and that helped a bit. But the second night, the thick drivers hurt my ears so bad I took the whole thing off. I mostly sleep on my side and stomach. It’s also tricky to charge because the port is only accessible if you line up the slit in the jersey fabric just right. Some simple product testing would have identified these issues. But for $20, I couldn’t be happier….. why?
SleepPhoness wants $100 for their bluetooth units. I’m sure they are top-notch but I didn’t want to spend that much. Here’s my solutions: The entire MuziCozy headband was disassembled….all two components. The bluetooth receiver / battery compartment and speakers come out easily enough. The fake ‘control panel’ on the front isn’t needed. The speakers have a rubber cover that is not needed. Once that is removed, the speakers are only 3-4mm thick, which is good. I disassembled the wired SleepPhones as well. The felt driver covers were re-used with the MuziCozy drivers, then the whole thing was re-installed into the SleepPhone headband.
This is the best setup - the headband is comfortable, I can still use it to cover my eyes, the sound quality is improved, and the MuziCozy charge port is easier to access thanks to the large velcro opening on the back of the headband.
My girlfriend, by contrast, likes absolute silence while sleeping so she uses the MuziCozy headband to make sure her earplugs don’t fall out and to cover her eyes.
So the entire unit has gone to good use, just not in the way it was delivered. I’m happy with the results but the original product need some redesign.

title: Good value for my intended purpose
text:
The primary purpose of this speaker is to have something louder than my phone in the shower, around the pool, or at the beach. For the price, it is a good solution.

Battery life and portability appear excellent. Very easy to connect and it can get fairly loud without significant distortion. In terms of tonal quality it’s not bad. Very mid-range heavy. I typically find myself using an in-app EQ to boost the highs to get more clarity. It’s a small speaker so don’t expect any bass. At the beach with constant ambient noise, this works.

Biggest drawback is poor Bluetooth reception. 10-15ft and it starts dropping out badly and it’s even worse if your body is in between the phone and the speaker. I don’t have a big pool but i can’t be on one side with my iPhone 11Pro and have a clear, consistent connection to the speaker. If Bluetooth reception were stronger, this would be 5-stars for value. But again, for having a little music while sitting with a friend at the beach, it works well enough.

For the price, I’d recommend it as a good value.

title: So Happy To Have My Bose Speakers
text: I purchased a new desktop computer and I had Bose speakers (basically these) that were over 14 years old and so I decided to pass them on figuring that the PC speaker would work fine with music based on the fact it is 2022.  No such luck - the sound was okay - but for someone who likes to hear all the nuances I decided to purchase a new pair.  Not so easy - I did not want bluetooth, as they do need to be recharged and honestly I just wanted to turn the suckers on and go - - - I decided on these, the price was double what I paid 14 years ago, however I also expected a better product and it is!  Easy to set up (yes the left side cord could be longer, but the sound is awesome!  I was worried they would vibrate on my table as the old ones did (I used a potholder underneath to prevent the noise) but these are a tad larger and much heavier and there is no vibration no matter how loud Imake the speaker.  I don't consider these breaking the bank and back in my high school - college days sound and receivers nearly took an entire wall in a room and were quite costly getting into the higher quality stuff - these smaller speakers can pack an awesome punch - using my Amazon Music set on Ultra High Definition I can't get over the lovely sound.  So for me these are a 10 plus and for someone that wants a nice sound, but not such a hefty price they are worth every penny.

title: Had a similar one years ago
text: Several years back I had a high end phone that had an excellent camera, and eventually I let my little Kodak go - then it used normal AA batteries.  That phone had a sealed battery, and I finally had to go get another because the battery was shot.  Took pics as usual and they were horrific!  I did choose a significantly cheaper phone because I am retired now - but had no idea it would change the quality so much!  So I went looking for a new camera, but I did not want to shoot the moon on bells and whistles because I only need a camera for my online Etsy shop.  Even after the negative reviews I went with what I knew and purchased this camera.  So - set up was very easy - I plugged the camera in and charged the battery overnight as it was noted it needed to be charged.  Then I set up the camera, placed the card in and took some photos.  I was a tad suprised that the colors were off, but that may be the lights I use, and work to adjust that.  As far as the comments on the battery draining quickly - I was given instruction from the older Kodak not to leave the batteries in the camera when not in use as being a digital camera, it basically runs all the time.  So I just would open the door to the battery area and leave it.  I do the same now with this lithium battery, taking away the ability to let it just run keeps it from draining so quickly.  I have been a week taking pictures as needed and still have plenty of battery life left.  Great camera for the price.

title: The best screen size!
text: We traded in our high end new car purchase (a thing now for dealers with no cars to sell), and purchased an older vehicle (20 years old, but a super high end model at the time) deciding to wait a few years while things shake out in the economy and e-vehicles become easier to purchase and use.  It is a wonderful vehicle, and aside from the laughing about a cassette player in the dash, of course there is no navigation screen.  I kept looking at the dash to see the navigation screen.  LOL  So I decided that we do have areas where we like to know where we are, and we like to know if there is traffic issues ahead so I went exploring on Amazon and came up choosing this.  I love it.  The reviews were daunting - to difficult to set up - no way to store information - no battery life, etc.  I found no issues - clearly going through the set up and checking out all the bells and whistles - this navigation has an app in it for truck drivers who need to keep hours and such, more than one driver can be tracked.  Well I don't need that for sure but who cares, I have everything else I need.  Day and night colors, sounds for certain driving functions, voice choices, car icon choices, a device so you can place it on the dashboard and an adapter to keep it running.  It clearly states in the instructions that the battery life is for emergency use only and has a limited use time.  You must keep it plugged into a power source.  I had to do the same thing for my TomTom, which was purchased in 2004 and can no longer be updated which is why I looked for a new one, and a less expensive one.  I have set the home function, and have entered quieries for road trips, which the device has set up and moved forward with NO issues.  I placed the dash clamp just where the 9" screen sits just over the dashboard, where a navigation system would normally sit on the console.  My husband who claims to have eagle eye vision along with being able to hear a cat walking 100 feet away absolutely LOVES this screen because he can "easily see it" and "clearly hear it" as well.  We shall see the next time I tell him to take an exit!  LOL  You cannot beat the price and I am a very happy purchaser!

title: Power and Volume buttons hard to find AND/OR press.
text:

The power, volume up/down buttons are labeled on the backside, which is great in case you need a reference, but the thick case makes it difficult to find and especially PRESS the buttons. Everyone knows the volume up is above and volume down is below, so instead of + and - labels, just make them textured so you can actually feel the correct location and boundaries of the buttons, to press them spot on.

It would be better if the material above the buttons was thinner so it was actually easier to push the buttons in without having to simultaneously brace the front of the tablet forcefully with my thumb while applying pressure to the button from the button on the slight-rear of the side of the tablet. It's frustrating enough that I'm trying to remember to just use the pull down software menu from the display.

Positives:
Well constructed and sturdy feel you'd expect if you've had a similar style case from Spigen. All cut-outs line up properly. The design looks hilariously sturdy for an iPad Mini; even the stand is sturdy. I don't have kids, but there are seemingly two separate sets of hand holds on the back, presumably designed for a set of very small hands in mind. The case seems tough enough for kids as long as they're not literally throwing it around. It should withstand many drops.

title: Can't believe how CLEAN it sounds
text:
Ordinarily I just buy AVR Receivers for about twice this price that seemingly have similar specs, but this one stood out because of its really high SNR (going from low 90s to 110 is apparently a /huge/ difference). I can't believe how quiet it is when its on and how crisp the sound is compared to much more expensive AVRs I've had. The only sound distortion I ever hear is from the cables themselves as I have them running through a crowded cable area. Its also quick to fully power up and even indicates when its still warming up with the light fading in and out for about 2 seconds until its on, so that you don't blast out your speakers trying to get sound to come out only to find out that the amplifier wasn't ready (some units really don't indicate well when they are actually ready, or they take so long that you're not sure).

The Sound is also very loud. I can only turn the volume (gain) knob in the back of the unit to about halfway with my [[ASIN:B0071MSYEE Polk Monitor 40]] (20-125W, 89db) speakers. The manual indicated that ordinarily, you would want the power amplifier to have its gain knob at full, but that just makes my PC's volume settings way too sensitive.

The downside is that the unit only has a volume knob in the back and its very small and only meant to be set once really. The volume is intended to be changed from the source (preamp), or in my case, a volume knob on my keyboard that turns up and down the volume in windows on my PC.

If you're on the edge, trust me this is great for the price. This whole experience just made me wish that I had bought discrete amplifiers for all my other setups instead of AVRs.

title: In one car, it would power over even the most powerful local stations and sound fantastic
text:

In one car, a 2010 F150, it worked so well that it didn't even matter what radio station frequency that I set the unit to, it would power over even the most powerful local stations and sound fantastic. In the other car a 2004 Ford Explorer, it was still able to get fantastic quality that sounded just as good as if it came over a cable (and i'm often picky about such things), but only if set to a mostly empty frequency and it was much more difficult to find one.

I should also note that this was the top choice for an FM-transmitter in a review from the wirecutter, a popular consumer electronics website with articles comparing different products.

Also most of the adjustments for the back part that holds the tablet up, do not sit flush with the back of the tablet. It's just kind of a flawed product design. My advice would be to get something else for a couple bucks more. There's an entire category for laptop stands on amazon and there are tablet stands within it. There are a lot of happy customers of this product so I may have just gotten one that slipped passed quality control. Good luck guys.

title: Comically large antenna. Much more bass than expected.

The stereo is also very heavy on the bass (especially for how small it is). Anyone that hears this unit will immediately be impressed by the volume and bass extension from such a small unit. In fact it's actually /too much/ bass for me some of the time because I like to listen to certain talk radio stations. I wouldn't recommend this for anyone wishing to listen primarily to talk radio. The sound quality is a tad bit sub par to a discerning ear if you're picky but I don't mind it because it looks great and I have other speakers for more pure listening. The sound quality still sounds great for the reported 85 db SNR.  The Bluetooth aspect works seamlessly. Once you set it up, it will auto-connect when in range. Just don't expect perfect sound quality. If you're not a critic and you love bass then this is what you want.

title: Flimsy, breaks easy, not the correct size screwdrivers
text:
So, all I wanted was a cheap set of tools to open up my mid grade Acer Nitro gaming laptop and install a few parts. I needed a pry tool and some precision screwdrivers mostly for this task.
Several of these tools broke within minutes of me starting to use them for the first time, with gentle use. Plastic tips broke, etc. None of the included screwdrivers would remove the 12 screws that held the laptop case on without stripping them. I had to dig out my other precision screwdrivers, cheap Walmart ones that were about $7 for a set - and they worked on the screws. In the end, the only thing I found useful in this kit were the pry tools, and one of them broke almost immediately - and I was very gentle with it.
I didn't expect perfection. I expected a cheap, barebones set for light laptop and cell phone work. I didn't expect it to stand up to years of abuse, but more than 3 minutes of light use. I also expected appropriately sized Phillip head precision screwdrivers, but they didn't fit standard laptop screws, just a tad too small and would strip the screws if you tried to make it work.
This product set is very poor quality, even for the low price tag. I would never buy this again. It's going into the trash.

title: Super easy, plug n play
text:
My old enclosure stopped working. It showed it was getting power, and the drive would show up, but I'd get errors trying to access it. Figured it was my enclosure or my drive....and the enclosure is much cheaper to replace (not to mention the lost data if it's the drive). I browsed amazon real fast and this one seemed solid, and the price was good, so I bit.

In fact, I like it much better than my old Rosewill enclosure. No tools required at all. Very simple. I didn't even need to look at any directions. It was put together and plugged into my computer in under a minute. Worked straight out of the box with Windows 10 - I needed nothing else. I plugged it in and the drive appeared. I can't speak to longevity because I've only had it a month, but the enclosure itself feels very solid and like it could take a beating (not that you'd want to, like, toss it out your 3rd floor window or anything). I feel like my drive is safe in it.

It works perfectly, feels very sturdy, couldn't be easier to assemble, works plug-n-play with no additional software in Windows 10 at least, and the price was very reasonable. I can't really think of anything negative to say about it. I am pleased with my purchase and would buy it again.

title: Tons of errors after 5 weeks, malfunctioning, causing BSOD
text:
EDIT: 10/30/16: Product has been malfunctioning for several weeks now. First it started randomly losing power, and I had to unplug and replug. Thought it was my USB port. Nope, changed ports, plugged keyboard into that one - no problems. Then I started getting Bad_Pool_Header crashes over and over. Opened the dump file and it appears this wireless dongle is the problem. I also constantly get errors from windows saying the USB device is malfunctioning. I am NOT pleased. It's too late to return it to amazon, now. I've only been using it 2 months. Sent an email to Panda Wireless via amazon. Depending on how they respond, may change my review score, but for now, I lowered it to 3. It worked great when it worked....which was for about 5 weeks

I'd always had really bad luck with wireless dongles/adapters dropping me, so I always used a wired connection, even if I had to run it all crazy through the whole dang house. I moved in with someone and the apartment layout was such that it would have been a really bad hazard to run a ethernet cable through the place. So I thought I'd try the wireless adapters again, and this time opted for one with an antenna for better reception.

I've used it for 2 1/2 months now and been quite pleased. I haven't noticed any drops while gaming. And I have it plugged into the back of my computer, under my desk, against a wall. Still, zero issues. On windows 10, it was 100% plug and play. No installs. I simply plugged it into my USB port, selected my network and put in the password, and bam. Connected. So for (so far anyway) flawless functioning and couldn't-be-easier install, I'm giving this 5 stars.

Pros:

Radio tuner (!!)

Nice settings - you can set a picture as your background. Also, it has country settings for the Radio Tuner, so it can work in other countries besides the USA.

Huge screen, GREAT picture

(For some of us, it's a pro that it is not an iPod)

Non-scratchable case

Feels very durable

Wifi is neat (but rarely useful.)

Cons:

Lower battery life (about 3-4hrs of video if wifi is off)

No wall charger included

Slow syncing for video

Software is a bit clunky (but so is apple's)

4/5 stars - It has some things I don't like, but overall, I'm happy with it. And, as much as I will be flamed for it, I just did not want anything apple-related. (Plus they were more expensive)

title: This keyboard is superb, but...
text:
I really wanted to love this keyboard. Having a wireless keyboard to type on a propped up laptop while studying was my solution to really bad back pains. And for the first 2 days I loved this keyboard. The keys don't jiggle when typing, everything about the look/design/feel is sleek and smooth. The integration with my macbook and my iphone was seamless. The keys fought off dust and crumbs for a week.

HOWEVER:

1) Please be wary of the fragility of some of the keys. I had only been using the keyboard for the first day or so when I noticed that my "-" (dash key) was loose. Upon further investigation with a magnifying glass, a small piece of plastic had been broken, which was why I couldn't snap the key back into place. I don't bang keys loudly or carelessly when I typed, and given that I hadn't had the keyboard for very long, I assumed it the product arrived with a defective key. After a few days, I looked at my F2 key (bluetooth key)- I touched this key maybe ONCE while connecting to my iPhone- and found it LOOSE! I can't snap it back into place because of the same broken plastic issue.

2) Logitech does not have/provide spare keys: When I called Logitech to inquire about spare board keys (rather than returning the entire keyboard to Amazon, because I did really love it besides this key popping problem), the customer service representative offered to replace the entire keyboard, which is great, but he also made mention of the fact they they DID NOT MAKE/PROVIDE spare keys for this model. This means that in the future, if just one key becomes problematic, the customer will have to go through the struggles of shipping out the entire keyboard, etc. I confirmed with the customer service representative that they did IN FACT not make spare keys (I was shocked), but perhaps I had spoken with a particularly new/tired/unversed representative.

All that being said, I am awaiting for a replacement from Amazon (I figured the shipping would be faster w/Amazon's superb customer service), and will see whether the new keyboard presents with problematic keys.
Hope the above two caveats help.

title: I Can Now Rest with Continuously Buying Earphones
text:
It's about time!! Apple Air pods ALWAYS caused me left ear pain and also would fall out! Heck!! Even one fell out during my video interview for a job and that was very embarrassing!!! Then the other air pod disconnected from my laptop. Made the interview complicated. Anyways.. My husband wanted me to go with the customized UE headphones as they are extremely comfortable and have the best sound quality ever. I tried his on to get a feel of the harden material inside my ears. So I ended up purchasing them from UE’s website. He has the most expensive ones and the sound quality is like listening to live music. So, UE was quick to ship the molding pieces for my ears. I went with the most expensive earphones, too (Over 1k). Well, after taking pics of my ears and doing the molding, it turned out my left ear, according to their techs, was outside the 95% range, and they suggested seeing an audiologist. Too much trouble, but they offered me a discount should I have gone. What I think may have been the problem was that I moved the left ear mold during molding process and that may have led to the final conclusion. However...

I can across these Fits, and though I was reluctant to try the molding method again, I purchased them knowing that Amazon has a superb return policy. Upon their arrival, I immediately prepared for the molding process. Now, I did run into technical errors. And this is just to share with you what happened to me and what I eventually did in case you should run into the same error.

After placing them into my ears, the UE Fits app popped up a message that the batteries were low and to charge for 5 mins for molding process. Now, I followed the directions, multiple times, as I kept getting the same error. And all while doing this I also had difficulties with pairing, repeatedly.

So frustrated with the app, and after 2 hours of charging and attempting to do the molding, I eventually reached out to the questions community on here. I received good responses but none of them helped. Even UE (Logitech) responded saying to contact their support line. I didn't. I figured it out myself. So if you run into the same error, you will need to delete the app and reinstall. Worked like a charm immediately. Pairing was difficult. Many attempts to pair, but one side would pair and then the other side would not connect. Eventually from Apple Iphone, I would get the message to forget device and re-pair. It's was a real pain but I eventually got them to work. So just keep trying should you run into the same issue.

So now the molding process. It is just like the customization earphones. You will hear music and then feel the earphones warming up. To some it may feel hot but just hang in there. Then the app tells you when it's complete. And then you are all set!!

I will say that these earphones are the best!! The material used to mold to your ears are soft and extremely comfortable!!! I can literally wear them for long periods of time without them causing left ear pain and they do NOT fall out!!! These Fits confirm that the customization ones I wanted I somehow managed to mess up. UE customized earphones do provide two sizes to try on, whereas these Fits only provide one size, but that worked for me!! I am excited that my search, and spending all that money on various earphones, has come to an end. They may not have the same sound quality as the customized ones I wanted, but these sound great being that they are moldable earphones!

I will have to update later regarding phone call clarity and such. I haven't had a chance to test them on calls.

In the meantime I hope this review helps!! I highly recommend these Fits if you do not want to spend thousands of dollars on earphones.

Enjoy!!!

text:
The case came in this morning. I was SOOOO EXCITED ABOUT IT!!! I decided to charge up the keyboard while I ran errands. I just came home and now that I have a chance to sit down and play with it. Minutes within inserting the IPad Air and pairing the case with the device, I noticed that some other natural habits kicked in. I admit that when I was looking at cases that it seemed really neat to have a blue toothed keyboard as the cover and back-lit at that!! Yes..the keyboard paired up nicely with the iPad air and it literally felt like a tiny laptop. It felt pretty neat. But then those natural habits I mentioned earlier kinda kicked in. It breaks my heart to say that I have to return it. I want to make it clear that there is ABSOLUTELY NOTHING WRONG THE PRODUCT. Just things I did not consider at all before buying it. :(

After inserting IPad air, again, it literally feels like a little laptop. So being that I was on the home page my thumb instinctively started looking for a mouse tracking pad to place the cursor into the URL for web browsing. Then the instinct to pick it up and use my fingers kicked in because there is no mouse track pad and that's when it hit me that this case isn't going to work for me. I loved the idea of the backlit keyboard as part of the cover but what it really boils down to is that you STILL need to use your fingers to navigate AND you have to pick up the entire case to do that especially in portrait mode. Trying to navigate using fingers and a case that doesn't fold all the way around just doesn't work for me. It was truly uncomfortable trying to use the iPad when the case feels like a book. These are just things to consider before buying. And it's only a 130 viewing angle so navigating at all is kinda uncomfortable. So like I've said, nothing wrong with this product at all!!! If your the type of person who uses the IPad mostly for web browsing, skype, or playing games - this case is NOT for you. Otherwise..Great product!!

Not gonna lie, it is very bulky and sorta wish Lifeproof came out with one as they seem slimmer, but in either case I am very confident that my Kindle HDX is quite safe in their Otterbox protective case. I never feel safe buying a phone or device without an Ottterbox case, or some sort of protection until one has been produced. I thought that would provide some protection as well but its obvious that I didn't read the description completely.  The entire backing of the Origami is like a huge magnet and clings to the back of the HDX. So when opening and closing the front part of it, that is where it feels flimsy in my hands. I will be returning the Origami back to Amazon and have already ordered the Otterbox for protection. I have always used Otterbox for my IPhones and have been very pleased with their products. My Origami arrived sooner then the HDX. After my HDX arrived and actually had the device in my hands, I felt that better protection is warranted especially for the price we paid. In my opinion, HDX feels so fragile compared to my Ipads and previous Kindles. When the Otterbox comes in I will be posting a review on that as well.

title: A little underwhelmed for the price
text:
These headphones look great and the sound quality is nice but I don't think they actually feel very nice. The headphones themselves are a little hard and stiff, not to mention they're rigid when it comes to adjusting the size. They don't move nearly as smoothly as headphones I've tried at much lower price points.

The bottom line is even though they look nice and sound decent, I'm going to reach for these less because they're just not as comfortable as other pairs I own (some of which cost less than this pair)

title: Decent usb-c amid a myriad of choices
text: The has plenty of ports that work, and they seem to be laid out in a logical order. Most of my opinion is about the design. It's a very close color match to mac space gray. I think the 6" cable is a little too long, and it has a 90 degree twist in the port, so the dock doesn't like to sit flat. It looks more comfortable hanging off the edge of a table, which is weird.  It would be nice if the 6"  cable could slide or clip into a spot for storage, but it does not.

title: Good fitting case, needs a handle
text:
The good:
The laptop pocket fits the 13" macbook air perfectly. It has plenty of soft padding and ensures your laptop will be reasonably safe in your backpack. The zippers are feel sturdy and the metal on the zipper sliders and the badging give the sleeve a premium feel. The exterior material is a very nice feeling nylon material that seems sturdy enough to be carried outside of another bag.
The less good:
This needs a handle. Otherwise this is just a sleeve with pockets, and needs to be placed in a backpack or some other bag. It feels awkward to just clutch and carry by itself. Also, the pockets are sized slightly awkwardly, and feel tight on things that should fit.. I wish they had fused the two smaller pockets together into one big pocket (possibly a kangaroo net inside or not, whatever).

title: A few issues...
text:
This is a very big kit that has a lot of extras. If you want all of the included things then it is a pretty good deal.

Keyboard - I personally could not stand using the included keyboard, and did not manage to get the trackpad on the keyboard to work (though I did not try for very long). You’re much better off getting a cheap wireless keyboard for $10 - $20.

Screen - It seems pretty cool and was very easy to install. I did have trouble getting the correct resolution to show up. It feels like there is overscan that I can’t disable. It is still useable, but it is a little annoying for it not to be perfect.

Pi enclosure - fits the pi and screen perfectly, but doesn’t really stand up that well by itself.

title: Picture kinda misleading
text: This only comes with the metal rig. I wouldn't have ordered this if I had known it was just the metal rig, doesn't really seem that great of a deal IMO.:/

title: Thin, sleek minimal case with matte rubberized finish
text:
This case is a bit of a lighter dustier pink than expected but it's still pretty. It's very minimal and ads almost no bulk to the phone at all. The buttons push easily and have had no issues.

Snaps in pretty easily although it is a little harder to get out.

I like the matte rubberized finish on this case because it provides more grip and feels more secure in hand.

Despite the light color, it's pretty easy to clean/ wipe down when smudges get on it.

I think this is a great minimal case that really shows off the phone nicely. It's definitely very very light protection, but I'd still recommend it based off it's look and feel!:)

**Update*** popsockets will not stick to this case because of the finish unfortunately:(

title: Decent pair of inexpensive headphones
text:
For the price I think these are pretty decent quality bluetooth headphones.

Upon opening I was a little disappointed by how cheap the plastic bits on this headset feel and look. My boyfriend didnt think they looked too bad but I definitely feel like these look like lower cost headphones. The carry bagit comes with also looks pretty inexpensive. They stick out on the sides a little more than I'd like as well.

If you like your music LOUD, these will be for you. In comparison to some beats headphones I have, these are about 2x as loud. Quality is decent but can definitely become distorted at the higher volumes.

I found these comfortable at the top of my head but the ear pieces did begin to make my ears sore after a while.

They come with a wire to make them regular headsets which I think is awesome for places or times you can't charge these.

Overall for the price, I think these headphones are pretty good, just don't expect a luxury item. Would probably work great as travel pair.

title: Nice set of USB C chargers!:)
text: My boyfriend and I both have Google pixels 3xls, we like having chargers around the house just to avoid having to look for one when we need it. This pack is great. Very affordable, sturdy quality, and the different lengths work well for different locations in the house. Can't complain!:)

title: Hurts my noggin
text:
I've used headphones for long periods of time before and have never had any issues. These headphones apply some pressure on your ears, but for me it seems to apply a lot of pressure on the top, where the headphones rest. After a half hour or so of wear, it makes the top of my head sore.

The sound quality is decent, but nothing better than products I've tried before. you can push up or down on the actual headphones to increase/decrease volume, as well as pausing songs. The headphones fold up into a decent size that makes it a little easier to carry around in your purse or backpack. However these do come with a soft case so you'll still need to be relatively careful with how you handle them. To be honest I think beats headphones are more about brand name than actual quality.

The color and design is cool but for the price and the comfort (discomfort) level, personally I don't think it's worth it.

title: The BEST portable speaker I've owned!!
text:
Quality with portable speakers can vary greatly but the sound on this one is awesome!!

And this comes from someone that only listens to their music loudly. Lol

The battery life is nice, I use it regularly and have had to charge it only a very few amount of times so far.

The lights it comes with are super fun too, I think it really helps set up a party atmosphere, even if that party is just me cleaning at home by myself! Haha

title: Great sound and noise cancelling
text:
Great sound quality, and the noise cancellation on these is awesome. Even when I don't have any music playing it knocks out any exterior noise. I also haven't experienced any nausea that I get from over the ear noise cancelling head phones which is pretty great.

Comfort level is okay, and I also do notice the tiniest bit of delay when I go to pause or play songs, but I think for the price these are still an awesome set of earbuds. Just make sure these are set in their charging positions correctly to ensure a good charge.

title: Looks better than tape!
text:
While these little tabs do look much better than tape, you have to make sure to put them on carefully if you plan to use your camera. The opening is pretty small so it has to be adhered just right.

Personally I don't use my webcam so I don't have a problems covering up the sensors or anything. Swiping it left or right is pretty easy too. I think of you're not rough with it, it should hold up.

title: The silver looks a bit cheap...
text: The silver on these headphones is plastic and looks quite cheap in person. For the price and sound quality, I think there are a lot of other options for a lower price.

title: Awesome commuter backpack!!
text:
I walk to school everyday, it's about a 30minute walk. That combined with all the time walking to different buildings once I'm at school, is a lot of time to get cozy with this backpack.

A little back story, I previously owned a unisex North face backpack, I got rid of it because it was too big and hurt my back. I downsized to a women's North face. It was better but it still didn't seem very comfortable and never felt very light even with few items in it.

Cut to this backpack, it's a women's backpack so it's made smaller. (Also I'm 5'7" 120lbs so I'm not terribly small bit still). This backpack feels lighter than others, I think it has to do with the frame, it's very comfortable on. I typically have 2 binders and two medium sized textbooks in my backpack, occasionally I'll bring my laptop. With everything in it, It doesn't irritate my lower back or shoulders after hours of wear.

The backpack also comes with 2 straps on the side that allows you to compress it in even further. When your stuff is closer to your back, and not hanging far out, it's a lot more comfortable. There are several pockets, a large padded pocket for your laptop, another for your books and such and 2 smaller but still very spacious pockets, as well as an interior pocket and nonzippered outer pocket.

The pockets do zip all the way around, but the straps will need to be unbuckled to do this. I'm not gonna lie, I'm very lazy and have not unbuckled the straps since getting this item, (it's been a month), and I've been able to get my books/laptop in and out without a problem.

The pockets for waterbottles are nice and deep so your water bottle won't fall out, and there's also a strap on either side to secure it even further.

The chest strap on this is awesome too. It doesn't compress your chest in an awkward or uncomfortable way which is something I always look for.

The shoulder straps and back are vented so it's been really great for me, a very sweaty person walking in the summer time. Haha

Overall I think this backpack is awesome! I've already recommended it to my school friends, looks like Osprey is my new go to backpack brand!:D

title: Details that make it seem inexpensive
text:
This duffel is one of those items that looks quite nice, but from a distance...

One of the things I noticed right away was that it's unlined/poorly lined. For the price of this item I would expect it to look more finished inside.
The zippers and hardware were all coated in a strange sticky residue, with a bit of plastic overtop.
The seams on this bag are also double stitched but in some areas look a little sloppy. The leather doesn't feel very soft and it reminds me of a duffel you might pick up at a second hand shop. (Of course that worn/vintage look might be what you're into!)

I took this on a week long road trip, and I will say it is a nice large size and the side pockets are very convenient for shoes or toiletries. The front pocket I didn't find very handy, it's pretty flat and doesn't expand much.

One other issue with this bag is that it's heavy. Even with nothing in it, it's got some weight to it. This, combined with the strap that is much too long for me (I'm 5'7" and it hits almost at my knee on the shortest setting), makes it uncomfortable for me to carry for very long. The strap also can't be removed which is a bit awkward to work with.

If you like the look of this bag and aren't deterred by what I think are issues, you may be very happy with this bag! It just didn't really work for me, and I don't think I'd be satisfied with it if I had paid for it.

title: Problems holding charge.
text:
These earbuds seem like a good idea, as an inexpensive alternative to airpods. They look nice, fit well and also come in a little case.

The sound quality is decent in them, and they're able to stay in pretty well during workouts.

However, these came with no instructions, so it did take a while to figure out how to use them. And I'm still not sure if I'm using them to their best abilities.

The other problem is that about 2-3weeks of use they're struggling to hold charge. I'm not sure if I received a faulty pair but they frequently show to only be at half charge/low charge even after charging overnight.

These were awesome while they worked for me, wish they were still fully functional.

title: Affordable and compact
text:

Great product!

title: Beautiful watch but lacking tech
text:
So first off, this is a beautiful watch. It's arguably the most attractive smart watch out right now. It looks like a classic stainless steel watch, with understated gems around the face that add extra flair. As soon as you open it, the weight feels expensive and overall it just looks great.

The bad news though, is that it's just not that great of a smart watch. The screen isn't the best. My boyfriend has the Samsung sport and you can tell the difference in screen/tech quality right away.

The screen isn't very crisp, and it's sensitivity often lags. When I first opened it, it was having a lot of screen problems and would often go black, freeze or exit out of screens for no reason. It occasionally still does this even now, a month later.

The interface is also not as friendly as I've seen with other watches. The preloaded apps aren't that useful. Doesn't include basic things you'd think like a calendar. You'd have to download more apps on there which might possible make the phone slower.

I mostly use this phone as a regular watch. I don't necessarily want to always have my phone on blue tooth and drain the battery, and texting by speaking into the watch or typing on a very small keyboard isn't super convenient for me.

I think if you're someone that's looking for a high quality smart watch, this one may end up frustrating you. Like I said, it looks great, but $350 is a steep price for a notsogood smartwatch. Better to go with a different brand, or stick to non smart watches if youre just wanting the style aspect of it.

title: Extremely durable and fast charging
text:
These are the USB C to Lightning Cables you’ve been dreaming of! I’ve bent these, folded them, crammed them into my computer bag over the past months and not one of them has failed to charge my iPad, iPhone 13, or iPods. Very well designed and manufactured for someone who’s always on the go and expects a lot from their technology. I’ve even given one of these cables to my boss when his failed during a meeting after he was bragging about how long he researched before buying his chargers and cables - he placed an order for these during the meeting because he knows I’m a road warrior!!
The charging time has remained consistently fast as well - no degradation over time which is key so the materials used are quality. I’ll be following this manufacturer and as I replace cables it will be with their products. I rate these as a strongly recommend and it’s rare for me to carry on about a product but this has save me so many headaches and time. Thank you for a solid product!

title: Great for returning to the office and cube sharing
text:
Now that we’re “getting” to return to the office after working productively at home throughout Covid, we’re “getting” to share cubes for rotating days every week….
This device is perfect for connecting your keyboard, mouse, headset, and any other USB A accessory to your workstation from your file cabinet or caddy in one easy movement. Works like a charm and gets me in and out in less than 10 seconds!

title: This is NOT hard to install and configure!
text:
Slow down and read the screens as you're installing the Blink camera - I also was clicking through the screens and encountered a problem. So I started over and actually read the App screens as I scanned the QR codes on the Sync Module 2 and the Camera the 2nd time and that's where the problem occurred on the first attempt!! Not reading the screens.
After actually paying attention, the camera was successfully connected to my WiFi and Sync Module 2 showing live video of my front porch. This is Day 2 and so far, so good. I'm not interested in paying for cloud storage so have attached a USB drive to the Sync Module 2 and can access my stored events.
The only reason I didn't give the system 5 stars - yet - is the video capture does lag as other reviewers have clearly stated by a few seconds. I'll need to see if this is possible to adjust. Night vision quality is decent for perhaps 15 feet away and then darkness. That's okay because it's how close someone would be to your door when you could see them on a home grade camera like this. All said and done, for $69 on a deal I'm pleased with what's provided except the lag in capturing video. Will update when I have researched more.

title: Great thumb drive for multiple purposes
text: Cloud drive this, that, and the other - BLAH BLAH BLAH. I've worked in IT and InfoSec long enough to tell you sometimes you just need to make a local backup with your computer disconnected from the network in the event you fear corruption from a virus, malware, or ransomware. I keep a rotating set of thumbdrives offline with a 2 month history and one of my 128GB drives acted a bit sketch so this is an excellent replacement. Tested and read and write speeds excellent. Would recommend.

title: On conference calls all day
text: I am on conference calls for at least 6 hours a day as a telecommuting IT manager so comfort and sound quality are of equal importance to me. I am seriously considering buying a couple spares of this product for whenever the product is no longer available - that is how pleased I am with the headset.

title: This is a quality backpack

(Planning actually paid off - my son took it to ComicCon with him this summer.) Holds electronics perfectly, zippers are smooth, straps adjustable and padding excellent. I'd recommend this either for the office, for college, trips, about anywhere you'd want to bring a backpack. title: Great value, excellent drive
