text: The idea is good, the execution is not great. I loved the idea of being able to carry my pencil with me protected inside the case. The problem is, the edges of the case stick up way too much from the surface of the iPad. If you’re used to using swiping gestures they get in the way. A lot. Also, when you fold it to stand the iPad up, the magnets don’t hold a lot of the time. I like the case other than those two things, but it might be enough to make me send it back.

title: Neat idea!!
text: I really thought this was a great idea. Some people don’t like screen protectors because they do degrade the picture slightly no matter how good they are. And paperfeel ones degrade it quite a bit. But they’re really good for sketching and drawing. This gives you the best of both worlds. You can have a super thin tempered glass screen protector and then just put this on top when you’re using the pencil. I think it’s fantastic.

title: Too rough and too thick Plus some other issues.
text: First of all, this is way too rough. It feels like I am drawing on sandpaper. I previously used a paperfeel screen protector from the Homagical store on my old iPad Pro, but I thought having the extra protection of glass might be good for my new iPad Air. Unfortunately, while the concept is good, the execution hair leaves a bit to be desired. The screen protector is extremely rough. It feels like sandpaper to me and is a lot more pronounced than my old paperfeel protector. Secondly, it’s so thick that I feel like it distorts the text and images on the screen. It feels noticeably dimmer and less sharp. The cloth that they give you to clean the screen was super linty. I had more specks and threads on my screen after I cleaned it than before I started. Like others, it wasn’t aligned properly even using the guide when I applied at the first time. Unlike others, when I tried to reposition it, I ended up with bubbles that won’t go away.  But the biggest issue is the roughness. It’s just too much.

title: They do the job when plastic just won’t work.
text: I used these to tie up some hydraulic jacks under my RV while I was waiting for parts to repair them. Plastic zip ties weren’t working because the rough edges of the rusted metal were causing them to break almost immediately.

title: Dimensions aren’t right and very cheap product.
text: First and worst, the dimensions are not right. It’s 6 x 10, not 7 x 8. Secondly, you get three screen protectors, but only one packet of application materials. Which consists of one wet wipe (which was dry as a bone), one dry wipe,, and a 2 in. microfiber cloth. The wipes were the tiniest ones I’ve ever seen. It was almost impossible to try to clean the screen without touching it with my fingers because the wipes were minuscule. And, like I said, the wet one was dry anyway. I had to supply my own alcohol. And they only supplied wipes for one screen protector. I guess you’re on your own for the other two. One of the protectors was damaged on arrival with a crease in it. This had to happen before shipping because there’s no way to crease one and not the other two. The quality of the screen protector seems very poor. It’s very frosted and seems to inhibit the touch sensitivity of the device. The only positive thing I have to say about it is that it was cheap. But it wasn’t even worth the low price.

title: Expensive for what it is.
text: This device looks good, and it’s an OK hotspot. But it’s not worth $170, especially when you factor in the incredibly expensive data that is the main selling point. i’m paying 50 bucks per month for 50 GB of prepaid data on T-Mobile. GlocalMe is $36 for 10gb and that’s US only. Usually when a company is trying to entice people to subscribe to expensive recurring service, they do so by providing a cheaper device. In this case, the device is pretty expensive and so is the service. Of course, I knew about all that in advance. What I didn’t know was that the battery life was going to be so poor. I hope they manage to get their data prices down to a more realistic level. They may be good for international travel. I haven’t explored that yet because my T-Mobile and Google Fi has worked well when I’ve traveled overseas so far.

title: Cheap and not as described
text: I thought this would be good because they say it has silica gel on the pad. That stuff is super sticky and I knew it would hold my phone quite well because I have a pad of it on my dashboard and my phone doesn’t go anywhere when I put it on that. Unfortunately, it doesn’t have silica gel. It has plain, small, rather cheap plastic suction cups all over the platform.  It’s a shame. It would be a really cool design if it actually was what they say it is.

title: Very handy.
text: This is a long cable and great for when you have a security camera that’s pretty far from your house. I’ve used the Blink battery operated cameras, but they really chew through batteries, and they definitely do not have anywhere near 100 foot range. So I still have a few wired cameras.

title: Doesn’t hold the binoculars securely
text: I love the idea of this, but the screw doesn’t tighten down enough to hold binoculars securely.

title: Not super impressed
text: The covers are OK but a little flimsy. The mounting brackets are awful. Thin plastic and extremely cheap mounting attachments. I don’t think they’ll last a month.

title: Works with my Sony RX10
text: This adapter powers my Sony RX10 camera perfectly. I’m hoping to try doing some long exposure stuff with the camera, and unfortunately it is a battery hog. So hopefully this will make it possible.

title: Keeps cords and hoses organized
text: Simple solution to keep hoses and extension cords and things like that off the garage floor.

title: Wi-Fi range is extremely poor.
text: I upgraded to this when my Netgear unite explore hotspot had a swollen battery, and I decided it was time to upgrade instead of paying for another battery. Unfortunately, it doesn’t really feel like an upgrade. First of all, you need to use an app to access most of the information and settings on the device. I miss being able to change those settings on the display like I could with the Explore. But the big problem is that the Wi-Fi range is not as good. I have an art studio shed that’s about 30 feet from the hotspot. With my old unite explore I had no trouble reaching that shed. With the M1, it’s almost unusable. I like the fact that it includes bands that were not available on my old hotspot, but I don’t like the fact that the range is so much lower.  And I don’t understand why when the device is so huge. That’s another issue. I could put the explorer in my pocket and take it with me, I’m going to need a suitcase for the M1. Edit: after a couple months, I really regret buying this hotspot. It performs so much more poorly than the Explore that it replaced.  And having to do everything through the clunky app which is not built for iPad, is a severe pain. WPS? Forget it. I have a GLI Puli hotspot for my T-Mobile account, and it wiped the floor with this M1 for less than half the price.

title: Really did nothing for my wifi
text: I tried to use this to extend my Wi-Fi into my outdoor art studio shed, and it really didn’t make any difference at all that I could tell. If anything, it made it worse.

title: Great router with a lot of cool features and the ability to customize to your hearts content.
text: This is a great little device. First of all, I’m using it with T-mobile, and I have not yet tested it with any other carrier. It worked right out of the box with my T-Mobile prepaid hotspot data Sim. Speeds are good, the battery isn’t as good as the one in my old Netgear hotspot but it does work in a pinch. If you’re not a tech nerd, you can pretty much just use this out of the box as is, or you can go into the portal and customize away. The range is really good. I’m using it to connect a TV in my art studio shed which is about 40 feet from the hotspot. And it’s working just fine. The signal is better than with my Netgear nighthawk M1 which has my AT&T Sim in it. I keep meaning to pull that Sim out and try it in this router and I just haven’t gotten around to it. I will update the review when I do.

title: Really gorgeous picture, and decent sound
text: I got this to replace a Toshiba fire TV that was showing it’s age. I didn’t like the fact that the Toshiba lacked some normal features that you would see on a normal TV like being able to adjust the aspect ratio. Crazy. It also came with extremely limited app storage and you couldn’t delete half the apps that were taking up the limited storage. So far the Google TV operating system seems faster and easier to use. The picture is gorgeous. I don’t have cable, so I rely on digital OTA channels or streaming channels. I had to tweak the color slightly for my taste, they had the oranges and reds boosted a little too much. But it’s really fantastic. The sound is really good too, although, I am not an audiophile, and I don’t rely on my TV as my primary music source like some people seem to do. It has a cool feature where the sound is customized to the acoustics of your room and your position in it. You run this calibration holding the remote at chest high and the TV plays some sounds that sounds like space invaders and the remote records them and adjusts the sound accordingly. Oh, yes, the remote has a microphone built-in do it so you can use voice search and other voice activated features. The TV was easy to set up, although the whole linking of the Google accounts and all the other things they want you to sign up for was a bit of a chore. I opted out of some and kept others. Your mileage may vary. The table top stand is the easiest to install that I’ve ever seen, you just plug it into the bottom and there it is. No dealing with screws or anything like that. There are a decent number of HDMI inputs and two USB ports, so that’s a plus. Finally, while it says you need to people, I didn’t have two people and it was not that difficult to handle the TV. You do need to be really careful not to press on the LCD, which is a given for any TV. But the TV only weighs less than 30 pounds so it was easy to carry. All in all, it’s a really nice TV. I think it’s a little pricey, but you’re paying for the Sony name. And it does appear to be excellent quality.

title: Works fine
text: So far it’s keeping the cables off the ground and that is what I got it for.

title: Too bulky
text: If you never plan to use the type cover, this may be an OK case for you. I do use the keyboard cover all the time and I found it the case was just too bulky. And it was difficult to remove. I got it because I wanted more protection for the tablet when it was in my backpack or a bag or whatever. But I have taken to just using a regular sleeve that I remove when I’m using it. Once again, if you’re not constantly using the type cover and you only use your surface as a tablet, this is probably a pretty good case.

title: A big step backward.
text: I was so disappointed to get these cameras. I was expecting some thing a lot better than the XT2 cameras that I had, and in fact these are actually worse cameras. The picture isn’t any better, the sound is a little better, the way that the back attaches is better. But the video still sucks, you can’t record on demand, you still can’t put an SD card in for storage, none of the improvements that I was hoping for. The Wi-Fi range is still very poor as well. I was hoping the new hub would do some thing about that, but I guess all they changed on that was the color.  What these new cameras are is slow. They are slow as molasses. My old XT two camera makes it to three or four Mississippi while I’m waiting for the live video to start, these new ones take to 12. It’s crazy. It’s a lot faster to walk outside when you get an alert then to try and pull it up and see what’s going on.  I think the Wyze V3 that is just out will be better than these and at 1/4 the price. The only thing is that they’re not battery operated. Anyway, I’m just really disappointed in these cameras. I believe they’re going back.

title: Perfect
text: Works like a charm with my Toshiba Fire TV. Highly recommended.

title: Great product, wish it came with great directions.
text: This is my second set of these sensors. I have three sensors and two receivers. They work great. Very few false alarms. However, it’s tricky to set up. You need to go to their YouTube channel and watch the video if you’re planning to do some thing like my set up where you’re adding sensors to various receivers. Once they go through the process it’s easy to see how it’s done, but it’s not intuitive.

title: These things are junk
text: This is the second time I have tried to use these nano stations. Both times ended in aggravation and returns. Both times I successfully set up the device to receive the Internet, and both times after anywhere from 2 to 12 hours they would lock up and require a reset. Over and over. Once is a bad device. Twice is a bad concept. Enough already. I’m going with the Alfa Camp Pro. Overpriced, but is it overpriced if it actually WORKS? We shall see.

title: Great shelves
text: I am using these for extra space on my glass drafting table I use for my art. I never actually tilt the table so I’m not worried about them sliding. They match the table like they’re made for it.

title: Strong and well-built
text: I actually ended up getting a double monitor mount, but it is very beefy and strong. The movement is smooth and it stays put.

title: Won’t stay up
text: So far I am 0 for 6 on these things. I’ve cleaned the surface, I wiped it with alcohol, and they still don’t stay up. The zip ties work, but this was a lot of money to pay for a bag of zip ties.

title: Working fine so far
text: These cords are working fine so far. I love the flat cords, they are just so much easier to work with.

title: Tired of waiting for playback functionality. Can’t fast forward.
text: I have like a dozen of these cameras and I have been a huge supporter of them. But I am finally tired of waiting for the simple ability to fast forward through the footage. It does no good to allow me to continuously record to SD card if I can’t fast forward through it to find what I’m looking for! No one wants to sit through four hours of realtime footage. So you’re forced to do the motion roulette of just randomly hitting different minutes of the video hoping that you’re actually going to see the guy steal the package off your porch. Because the motion detection didn’t catch it. For the money they’re cute cameras, but the functionality is at a standstill. They’ve been looking at providing a fast forward function for over two years now and have decided it’s just too hard. And I’m tired of waiting.

title: So far I’m impressed.
text: I was a little worried about false alarms since there is a drug dealers house across the street from me and there is more traffic in and out of that place than the mall at Christmas. So far though, I haven’t gotten any false alarms from the traffic driving by my driveway and I have set it off myself by walking on my own property. That’s exactly what I was looking for.

title: Great for modern laptops
text: It’s been along time since I got a laptop that had a built-in DVD drive. Unfortunately I still have a lot of DVDs that I paid a lot of money for. Yes, I know how to rip them onto hard drives and I’ve done some of that. But then you have to plug the hard drive into the laptop too. Sometimes it’s easier to just do the DVD.

title: Looks great!
text: I have a bunch of real cameras scattered around my property. Blink, Wyze, and  Arlo. But I’m all about deterrence and this big white obvious camera at the end of my driveway is the first line of deterrence.

title: Works perfectly but the batteries only last about half as long as the OEM batteries.
text: Well, they’re certainly much cheaper, but they only last half as long as the original batteries. This is only a huge issue if your camera isn’t easily accessible, but it’s a bit of a bummer.

title: Great light, especially for the price.
text: At the time I purchased this, it was just under eight bucks. Reading the older reviews almost scared me off, but I figured for the money it was worth a try. I’m glad I did. They must’ve refined the design over the years. I don’t think that the light is too bright, the neck is very flexible, and I love how it folds up and has the little cock to hold the clip so it stays folded up. Time will tell on the battery life, but for now I love this little light. I might order another one.

title: Love these WD drives
text: As a photographer and digital artist, I have a lot of hard drives. And most of them are WD. They seem to be reliable and not as finicky as Seagate.

title: Small and classy
text: I really like the professional and classy look of this usb drive. Seems to work great and looks good doing it.

title: Love this tiny hard drive!!!
text: It's amazing how small this unit is. It's fast, small and looks classy. And the box it came in makes a great watercolor palette box. Bonus!!

title: Love these devices
text: I love the concept of these. I really like the slim for my backpack. It's hard to see down in the lining in a black backpack, unlike the tag which a thief would toss immediately.

title: Heavy duty. Great for Waze.
text: I have a standalone Garmin GPS where you get some traffic info. But Waze is much better. But, I could not figure out a way to use my iPad to get it while driving. I have a vent mount for my phone, but my phone is too small. This  mount is sturdy enough that I’m willing to put my expensive iPad in it.  I was actually astonished at the weight of the box when it arrives. This is not a cheap plastic mount, it’s metal.

title: Arrived with a crack in the top.  But seems to work well.
text: I was a little aggravated when I first got this as it arrived with a starburst crack in the top of the case. However, after some pretty heavy rains none has gotten into the case through the crack. The base was getting too wet, but that was because I had it sitting on the table. Once I mounted it on a mount it works better. The Infrared lights reflecting off the inside of the case at night. However, if you have a motion sensing light mounted nearby and it illuminates, the camera works really well.  One thing that surprised me is that the sound still works pretty well. I haven’t tried using the speaker function, so I can’t comment on that. I’m leaving one star off for poor quality control that the cracked item got through.

title: Frame is too big. I definitely liked my old Fintie case better.
text: The fake leather frame around the screen is too big. It's difficult to swipe in or top tap. Worst of all, the cutout for the brightness sensor is too small. Since the frame is also fairly thick, it tends to throw a shadow on the sensor. This leads to annoying brightness shifts when you shift positions. The case it pretty but it's just a little too clunky overall.

title: Beautiful monitor.
text: This was a huge upgrade to my 20” monitor. Great colors and sharpness.

title: Made a noticeable difference.
text: I use a laptop for photo processing, and didn’t have high expectations for this device. It was a revelation how much better my photos look in Lightroom after calibrating. Very cool.

title: Works great in the rv
text: I wanted a small inverter for just the laptop and iPad that wouldn’t draw a bunch of extra current like the big inverters do. This does the job, and is lightweight and small.

title: Ok but the app drags it down
text: The app is awful. Honestly, at this price point there are better options. But it works as advertised.

title: Doesn't stay tight.
text: I bought 6 of these mounts. After less than 2 weeks three of the cameras have come loose and are now hanging upside down and swinging in the breeze and alerting every minute. I’m 4000 mi away so my choices are let the batteries run out, rendering the cameras useless, or disable motion detection, rendering the cameras useless.  I should have stuck with the regular blink mounts. This was an absolute waste of money.

title: Nice thing to toss in a suitcase.
text: I didn’t understand how this worked before I got it. But it does work The instructions are a little too minimalist but I figured it out. . As stated, it has to be an inward opening door. On one of the bedroom doors in my house I had to pull the silicone completely off the plug to get it to fit. It worked just fine. This will be handy for things like AirBNB where you just don’t really want the owner having the ability to easily burst in on you. It hasn’t happened to me but it’s something I do think about.

title: Great picture, clunky menu and transitions
text: The screen is nice and large. The picture quality is great. The menu and transitions are super clunky though. It’s like someone time warped a Y2K screensaver into the box. So the pic quality is a 5 and the interface is at best a 3 and maybe a 2. But mom likes it so that tips the scales back to a 4 star rating.

title: Can’t get it to pair or do anything.
text: Well, it paired for like 15 seconds then lost connection and I haven’t seen it since. Holding the reset button down does nothing.  According to support, my internet connection probably isn’t up to par.  Well, it’s good enough for Wyze and Arlo, not to mention Netflix so I call BS on that one. It looks like a nice camera. Probably not ready for prime time.

title: Flat cable is good for going under doors, etc.
text: I didn't want a permanent installation of an outdoor POE antenna so I tried this cable. Worked great and the front door still closed easily.

title: Great addition to security camera system.
text: You do need to do your research and make sure your system will accept audio input, not all do. It's a simple mic and the power splitter cable worked fine with my zosi bullet cams. Nice addition.

title: They're too big and look cheap.
text: I was disappointed. They're big and clunky and look cheap. I don't think they'd fool anyone. The blinking red led is big and bright and obnoxious. I would have preferred a camera that gave off a faint red glow at night. This might fool someone who has never seen a real one but that's about it.  I think they're going back.

title: Unreliable. 3 of 5 are dead in less than a month,
text: I don’t know if it’s the crappy reader they include or if it’s the cards themselves but I’m encountering frequent errors. Finally a few of them quit working altogether.  And that included card reader....please. I've gotten better stuff out of a crackerjack box. Finally, one of them is only a 2 GB card!!!  What's up with that???

title: Doesn't fit in the provided bag.Doesn't fit in
text: Doesn't fit in the provided bag. I'm also not very impressed with the sound quality.

title: Watch the weight
text: Seems to work ok, though I feel like it might not support as much weight as they claim. I'm using on a 29" TV and it sags over time.

title: Setup is a pain with requiring Ethernet. App is clunky and unintuitive.
text: I guess I’m spoiled by my Wyze Pan cams. The setup for this camera was a pain and if there’s a way to make it track moving objects like my Wyze Pan does, I haven’t figured out how. The hardware of the Dericam seems good, it is amazingly quiet, but the clunky app drags it down.

title: I think there are better options.
text: First of all, I'm using this on windows since my macbook died. I am not overjoyed with the reliability. I copied hundreds of gigabytes of files onto this drive in preparation to move them to a different computer. When I plugged the drive in, it was empty. I've had files go missing off this before but nothing like this. I have no faith in it now.

title: Classy bag/backpack
text: It's one of those deals where it's not a great backpack and it's not a great messenger bag, but it's a decent compromise. It looks much better than your standard laptop backpack, more classy without contrasting trim.  It definitely holds more than my Targus backpack.

title: Good replacement for Zone Defense cameras
text: The camera is solid and well-built. The connector is a 4 pin 'aviation' plug. You can find cables and rca adapters here on Amazon but it was a direct replacement for my Zone Defense camera.  I went back and forth on how many stars to give. On one hand, there's not even the tiniest scrap of paper in the box to tell you how to install it. On the other hand, it's a good camera for the money. Since I really needed a new camera and didn't want to pay the 150 for a Zone Defense cam, I ended up giving it 4 stars. But they really need to get some documentation in the box.

title: Unreliable. Should be called Blank XT
text: I tried to love these cameras but they've let me down several times now.  Their motion detection is erratic at the best of times and since there's no ability to continuously record to an sd card or anything else, if the the motion detector doesn't catch it, it's not recorded. It takes too long for the cameras to wake up so I get a lot of 'blank' clips, where whatever finally triggered the camera is over by the time it gets around to recording it. Worst of all, the whole system has a tendency to randomly go offline where it stops communicating with the cameras and nothing gets recorded. After the neighbors annoying free-roaming dogs set off my Wyze cam for the 20th time today it suddenly occurred to me to wonder why I wasn't getting Blink alerts. So I checked, and lo and behold, I wasn't able to connect to any of the cameras, and apparently hadn't been connected for at least 18 hrs based on the last stored clips. But there's no indication of any problem on the aggravatingly bright leds on the hub, they look like everything is peachy. I had to unplug the hub for a few minuted then reconnect. Not so convenient when you're not home, which is when you most definitely want your cameras to work. This is the second time this has happened and I'm done. Returning these.

title: Looks great
text: I love the rose gold color and the braided cover feels nice. Seems like a thick and substantial cable.

title: Handy thing to have
text: This is great to have in the bag for those times when you or a friend really need to charge something. It's not really for daily use in my opinion as the doubled connectors make it a bit awkward sticking out from the device. It could be a bit longer too. But all three connectors worked, and I got no nagging popups on my ipad so that was good.

title: Looks good and folds super flat.
text: This is a classy looking item and will match a macbook or silver ipad perfectly. I like the fact that it folds so thin. I have a padded one that takes up too much room to put in the backpack with the laptop. This one is much better in that regard and it cools better too.

title: Wow wow wow
text: It's unbelievable how heavy these little speakers are. And it's even more unbelievable how good they sound.  These are my first real high-end speakers and I'm just blown away.  I guess now I understand audiophiles a little better. Really amazing sound.

title: So far so good....
text: It seems fast, it looks good, and was plug-n-play.  Can't argue with that.

title: These little GLi routers are amazing.
text: I don't know how they pack all the features into these tiny boxes but they do. Almost two months after hurricane Michael we still have no cable, and hence no internet. I'm using an older cellular hotspot to provide internet for the whole house, but it only allows 5 connections and between the smart TV, Roku, Tivo, printer, 2 laptops and 3 cellphones all jockeying for connections, it was a giant pain. My little mango router took 5 minutes to set up in repeater mode and has been happily rebroadcasting the wifi under a different SSID and allowing a lot more connections. It has been doing so for over a month now without so much as a hiccup. Highly recommended.

title: Works great! The provided tool to tuck wiring away was a nice touch
text: The camera works well and I liked that there was a memory card included. That said, I immediately swapped it for a bigger and faster one. But it's nice that one was included. I also liked the plastic tool that they included to tuck the wires behind the trim. That's handy and I'll use it for other installs.

title: Wow, heavy.
text: This is a very heavy duty unit. It weighs twice what my current mount does and doesn’t flex a bit.

title: Working so far in my little mp3 player
text: I only use big name cards for important stuff like my cameras but sometimes you need cards for non critical stuff. So it’s nice to have options that are more affordable.

title: Seems pretty durable
text: The plastic case seems very durable and there's a cap to protect the usb plug.

title: Great tiny routers.
text: These tiny routers have amazing features and performance for the price and size. I now have two of them. They're fabulous for travel but work well in a home setting.The only issue is that they're SO light that they flop around every time you move a cable.  Command strips solve that problem at home. When traveling I'm just careful.

title: Surge protection didn't work.
text: First of all, this is my second one of these. The first one had the battery fail after 2 years. But I thought maybe that's the standard for these units. So I bought another one as I did like the LCD screen. Well, not even a month later Hurricane Michael hit. I had a bunch of sensitive electronics plugged into this and half of them did not survive the power surge when our power went out. My brand new 50" Fire TV, security system DVR and Arlo base unit were all casualties. It did nothing to protect my stuff. My insurance company has a limit on power surge damage and I'm pretty sure this is going to amount to more than that. Do not buy this unit. Utter junk.  I would give it zero stars if I could.

title: The person who invented Velcro should be a saint.
text: These are just so handy for so many things. I usually don't bother threading them through the slot, they work just fine anyway.  So much better than using zip ties.

title: Soooo much nicer than running electrical wires.
text: This is a sturdy, high quality unit. It works great with my Wyze cam.  I plan to pick up a few more.

title: Great for adding more ports to a small laptop.
text: I have no issues with this little hub. Everything works with my Asus laptop. I mostly use the USB ports, but the micro sd card reader is handy too. The edges of the metal on the ethernet port are a bit rough but it's a small quibble....

title: You had better already know how to install one of these....
text: The instructions that come with this unit are the worst I have ever seen. If you don't already know how to install this, you still won't after looking at the leaflet that comes with it. I wrote to customer service and they sent me a link to a YouTube video of a wireless system. :-(  Sadly I let the 30 day window elapse so am stuck with it now.

title: there are thousands of them out there working fine. But if you let your account lapse
text: Don’t buy this. You won’t be able to activate it. I paid  a lot of money for this and only got a few years of service before TiVo refused to reactivate it and told me to spend another $400 on their newest model. It’s not that these boxes don’t work anymore, there are thousands of them out there working fine. But if you let your account lapse, go overseas or something, you will not be able to restore your service on the working device that you paid hundreds of dollars for. All so they can force you to buy a new one. Absolutely awful customer service. I will never buy another TiVo device.

title: Read the description and you’ll know what is and isn’t in the box.
text: This is a great light if you already have Sony batteries. You can use it with a third party ac adapter but obviously that will only work for studio use. Some of these reviews crack me up where people gave it one star because they didn’t read the description. That’s like buying a Canon lens then complaining it doesn’t fit your Nikon. The light is bright and adjustable and doesn’t weigh a ton. Great.

title: Great for frequent travelers.
text: If you travel a lot you know airplanes and rental cars are like a box of chocolates......you never know what you’re going to get. Even if you reserve something specific there are no guarantees. But with this little gadget, as long as you have a headphone or aux jack somewhere you should be good to go. Read the instructions....it’s not quite plug and play, but not rocket science either. Great item.

title: Looks sharp and has tons of pockets.
text: This backpack looks sharp and has a ton of pockets to organize all your gear. I really like the rubberized bottom. Too many times I’ve set my bag down and later realized the floor/ground was wet. Plus it’s a bit more protection.

title: Unreliable system and no support.
text:
Update after 2 months:
After two months I have to say that if you care about your security you should look for a better option. One camera failed completely after less than 2 months, and now the DVR randomly decides to stop recording every now and then and doesn't give any indication of that fact. You only figure it out when you try to go to playback and get the message "No Data". And obviously you are attempting to look at the playback since something happened. But you're out of luck. When it worked I loved the system. Other than the lack of a remote. That got to be a pain after a while......except it wasn't as big of a pain when I wasn't having to check if it was still recording every 15 minutes like I am now. I got no reply from Zosi when I tried to contact them. It's a shame.
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Original review:
Man......I felt like I could have circled the earth with the amount of wires in this kit. It’s definitely a struggle to run all that wire but it is more reliable than trying to go wireless. The quality is good. The hard drive is noisier than I’d like. I haven’t yet gotten the remote viewing thing set up yet but that will be a great feature that I’m looking forward to having.

title: Super handy.
text: When you have an older home with too few outlets this is a lifesaver. Be aware that this takes up both wall outlets when you plug it in.

title: Nice basic headphones. Good volume.
text: No one is going to confuse these with Bose, but at this price point I think they are nice headphones. I do agree with other reviewers that it would be nice if the earcups swiveled but I didn’t find them uncomfortable. One pet peeve I’ve had with some other headphones is that I can’t turn them up loud enough. Yeah, I know everyone is worried about ear damage, but if I can’t hear what I’m trying to listen to in a noisy environment like on the train the headphones are no good to me. They paired easily, sound good and the buttons work as expected so what’s not to like.

title: Great sound! I listen to a lot of Native ...
text: Great sound! I listen to a lot of Native American Flute music and it just sounds awesome on this speaker. My old bt speaker would sound terrible on the high notes. This speaker is crystal clear on the highs and the bass of the drums is surprisingly rich as well. It's very cool that the app allows you to adjust the sound to your liking. I'm not too sure about the leather strap.....I have a feeling that's going in a drawer. I really love the sound though.

title: The setup was quick and easy..
text:
Update: I don’t know what happened but now it won’t work at all.. Not sure if it was the app update or the camera firmware update but it’s not recording. The app is abysmal. I think it’s a decent camera but it needs a better app. I can’t recommend this camera at this time.

First review......
It's basic but it does work. I'm not fully clear what happens at the end of the first year when the free cloud storage runs out, if it's going to be at all usable without buying a subscription. The setup was quick and easy...just follow the directions. I wish it was smaller, it's certainly not unobtrusive.

title: It's a cool watch with a lot of features
text: It's a cool watch with a lot of features. Despite all the pics of women wearing this I find it to be too big for my wrist. It's just a bit too heavy and wide.

title: I upgraded the hard drive in my ASUS ROG laptop ...
text: I upgraded the hard drive in my ASUS ROG laptop and it couldn't have been easier. The increase in performance has been spectacular. I wish I had done this sooner!

title: Great all-around lens
text: Great all-around lens. Lots of people like to pick at these superzooms but they do the job for 99.9% of the people 99.9% of the time. And for that other .1% you can rent the $2000 glass you need. I've had multiple calendar images and magazine covers from images I've shot on fishing boats in Alaska, where changing lenses can be undesirable due to the probability of getting water inside the camera. No one ever said, "Oh my god, I'm sure that image was taken with a superzoom. We can't possibly use it!!" Might be different for wedding or product photography, I wouldn't know. :-)

title: I like the features on this watch
text:
I like the features on this watch. It's lightweight, the pink color is not obnoxiously bright, and the buttons are easy to use. I had no issue setting the watch up without using the app and just the onboard buttons and menus. It works well and the step and distance counts seem accurate.

One thing I don't like is the clunky, proprietary charging clip. I remember the bad old days, when every device came with its own charging or power cord and one had drawers and drawers full of orphaned cords and chargers. Apparently this is common in the fitness tracker world. I hope they go back to standard USB chargers.

title: Wish these worked better with tablets/iPods.
text:
These earbuds are really cool. I *love* not having wires and being able to just wear one without having the other one dangling annoyingly. The sound is good. Not great, but good. I definitely felt like my Jaybird earbuds have better sound, but losing the wire more than makes up for it.
Now what I don't like. Number one, the lack of compatibility with ipads and ipods and any other tablet is really annoying. I get that the primary purpose is supposed to be exercise but for the price of these earbuds I want to be able to use them with everything I do. And my ipad is my primary music device as it has waaaay better battery life & storage capacity than my phone so I use it on the treadmill, on the boat, sitting out on the deck, even on the bike, etc. In fact, the only time I use the phone for music is walking/hiking. It does not seem like it would be that difficult to make it work with all devices so I hope they do. The earbuds will pair with the ipad and play music, but the only earbud function that works is play/pause. You have to change volume, skip forward and back, etc on the ipad. Not always possible and never very convenient.

title: This is a gorgeous speaker with great sound. Love the bamboo
text: This is a gorgeous speaker with great sound. Love the bamboo. The carrying bag is kinda lame, in my opinion. The fact that it leaves the face exposed makes no sense, if it's rattling around in a trunk or backseat it's bound to get scratched and filthy.I think they could have put a flap on it that velcroed into place and that would have been better. That said, this thing is pretty heavy. I can't imagine walking around with it slung over your shoulder all day.  But it's great to take out on the deck or boat.

title: Not working on Windows 10. Not even in compatibility mode.
text: Stupid me didn't try it out before the return window closed as I trusted the Celestron name. That was a big mistake. iCap software crashes immediately upon trying to open the software. I'm now in a semi remote area with not great bandwidth exacerbated by 100,000 fellow eclipse chasers so it's hard to research alternatives and download any. I would have done it beforehand but was socked in with cloudy skies for two weeks before I finally threw in the towel and relocated almost 500 miles to a better eclipse site. I knew I couldn't test the camera with my solar scope and it never dawned on me I'd never even be able to get the software to run. I'd give it zero stars if I could and will probably file a claim with my credit card company.

title: It doesn't seem to do anything. Unfortunately I allowed ...
text: It doesn't seem to do anything. Unfortunately I allowed the return window to expire before I figured out I wasn't saving any GPS info.

title: but I liked the small handheld format
text: It was expensive, but I liked the small handheld format. This isn't something I'll use often, so I didn't want a permanently mounted radio. Worked well with an external antenna.

title: Proprietary cables and prone to expensive failure.
text: The firmware update process is clunky and dangerous. If your wifi goes out you can brick the camera. But I guess I won't have that risk as it requires a proprietary cable, which I don't have. The shutter is fragile. I'm on my second one. I've spent more on fixing my two olympus bodies than I have on every other camera I've owned combined. I will not buy another Olympus camera.

title: I think adding an SD card slot and providing long enough cords to plug them in when you're going to be gone for long periods wou
text: My previous security camera system transmitted the video over the house wiring by plugging into an electrical outlet. I much prefer that. If you have a slightly wonky wifi network this is not the solution for you. And if the wifi is down there is no onboard storage of video so it's lost forever. My old system had micro SD cards in the cameras so there was always a backup. Changing/charging the batteries is a pain on the Arlo as well. And they're not going to last for your two week vacation. I think adding an SD card slot and providing long enough cords to plug them in when you're going to be gone for long periods would have added like a buck to the cost. It's a shame they didn't do that.  Oh, and tech support? Don't bother. Go close your hand in a drawer a few times.....you'll feel about the same and not waste a day or two on the project.

title: Connecting to crappy, distant hotel wifi
text: Worthless for me. The performance on this wifi adapter is significantly less than the built-in wifi on my ASUS ROG laptop running Win10. Connecting to crappy, distant hotel wifi, I got 2.23mps on the built-in wifi & 0.76 on the HIRO. I didn't think anything could be worse than the laptop wifi, guess I was wrong. Sadly, I waited too long to test it so cannot return it. Don't make the same mistake.

title: Not transparent at all
text: I bought this because the reviews said it was semi transparent and the backlight would show through, though at a reduced intensity. What I got is completely opaque over the keys.  I got an Asus ROG laptop and love everything about it except the dark red printing on the keyboard. So I thought this would be perfect. White lettering on the keys during the day, and reddish pink backlit keys at night. Well, the white lettering s helpful during the day, but the backlight is not coming through on the keys at all, only on the clear sections between the keys, which is not helpful at all. I'm probably returning it.

title: I can't get past this awful keyboard...also not very customizable.
text:
I knew the keyboard was red when I ordered it. I didn't know how bad that would suck, however. The keys are hard to read during the day. So you have no choice but to crank the backlight to max, wasting battery. Battery life is bad enough as it is. And the backlighting doesn't help much during the day. I just hate it.

Next issue is that it doesn't come with DVD playing software. Seriously? Why did I buy a computer with a DVD player in it? Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. My Toshiba windows 10 laptop came with DVD playing software and it doesn't even HAVE a dvd drive!

Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.

title: I don't know.....I'm having a hard time putting my trust in this.....
text: Well, the concept is great, but I have a hard time trusting my ipad pro to this when the front is entirely open. I know the gaskets are supposed to press tightly enough against the screen to keep water from getting in, but I'm just not comfortable with it, not to mention I don't like tossing it in my bag/purse with nothing covering the screen.  It did work fine on the plastic mock iPad they include in the box, no water got in when I tested it. It's super lightweight and very thin. However, I do not like not having screen protection, and they tell you you must remover any screen protector you have on to use this case. Mine did not include the cover/stand they show on this page. If it had that cover I'd feel better.

title: Great for travel photo backup
text: It does what it says it does.....accesses media files. Yeah, I also wish wish wish it was a true external drive where you could copy and access all sorts of files on your iDevice, but it is not. And that's Apple's fault, not the Gigastone.  However, I love this thing for travel so I can back my pics up when I'm away from my computer.  Only gripe is having to take the case off. If they had made both sides of the reader the same it would fit. But one side of the connector is slightly shorter than the other and it's just enough to keep it from seating. This seems like a prime example of form over function...it looks cool with that asymmetric look but it would have been better if it fit.

title: Great all around machine that draws low power.
text: I love this laptop. It's replacing an HP Envy that isn't even a year old yet. The ergonomic on this laptop are way better.I haven't accidentally bumped the touchpad while typing, and the keys are large with a nice feel. Performance.....well, I'm not gamer. It's doing ok on Photoshop, Lightroom and Chrome, and that's pretty much my big three. The backlit keyboard is something you'll never be able to live without once you've had it. The screen is gorgeous. It could, perhaps, be a touch brighter.  The sound from the speakers is ok. No one will confuse it with a surround sound system but it's good for a laptop.  The hard drive is quiet. The spinning of the one in the hP drove me mad. The USB ports are towards the back of the machine. I have not been a fan of the recent trend to move them up front as I'm forever bumping them. Great to see. Despite being larger than the HP, the power drain is MUCH lower. I live in a solar powered vehicle so this is important. Right now, with music playing and the screen at max, in high performance battery mode, I'm showing it using 17w. When I first plugged it and it wasn't fully charged yet, I saw a max draw of 29w. The HP drew almost 50w charging and 90 or better while running. I could not be happier with the Toshiba. The tablet mode thing......well, it's nice to be able to adjust the screen to any angle. Using it in tablet mode......I haven't found a lot of reasons to do that yet. It's pretty heavy and unwieldy to carry it around like an ipad at 5 pounds. But I guess it's nice to have the option. That brings me to another small quibble....it's kind of heavy for how thin it is. I was a little taken aback. I guess you can't have everything. Well, you can, but you'll pay two grand and up for it. For the $$ this is a great all around machine. I'm definitely not buying another Envy. Windows 10......boy, I was prepared to hate it. I don't. So far anyway. A lot of headaches can be avoided by setting your wifi connection to metered, then all those background updates don't happen as far as I can tell.  PS The stupid stickers they put all over these things came off with little effort and no residue. I hate those things. The Intel one put up a little fight but came off relatively easily.

title: Unreliable.
text: Not reliable. 2 years old and it is constantly crapping out. Worst of all, it looks like it's still there but when you click on the drive letter it appears empty, as if all the files were deleted. And therefore, they were promptly deleted from my online backup. Unplugging the drive and then plugging it back in makes all the files reappear.....and then you get to re-upload 4T of files to Backblaze/CrashPlan/whoever. Awesome. If the drive had had a fatal failure during that time I would have lost a ton of stuff.  I've tried different USB ports and different cables and it still happens, this drive is just a piece of crap. I am now transferring the files to a trio of WD drives that are at least 5 years old and still plugging along. I won't be buying another Seagate.

title: Your neighbors will hate you. But you'll love it.
text:
I love this thing. It's gigantic, it's heavy, and it's awkward to move in close quarters. But it kind of brings me back to my youth where big stereos were the norm. It brings joy to my heart. It's like my 80's boombox, with Bluetooth. The sound is great. Bluetooth pairing was effortless, inside of 30 seconds after unboxing it I was streaming Spotify. And it sounded great. Mom loves purple so in her honor I changed the light to purple. (I still think she's less than thrilled, however.) My stepfather got an electric guitar for Christmas so the fact that you can use it for an amp is a bonus. There are handles on the top so it's not too bad to lift.

I wish it was easier to roll, you have to tilt it kind of far back before the wheels touch. I guess they're afraid some drunken partygoer might nudge it and mow down the crowd. I also wish there was an option to run it on 12v or batteries. I know I can use an inverter but it seems like something like this would benefit from the option. The cord is a little short too. But all in all, if you love music, you'll enjoy this.

title: Love the long cable. Excellent for airports.
text: My Lightning cable for my iPad was on it's last legs and it was too short to comfortably read with it plugged in. So when I saw this one I knew it would be perfect. It's nice for airport use where they have those outlet stations which are too high to sit and use your device.  The cord is considerably thicker than the original, but it feels sturdier, and it doesn't tangle as easily.

title: Did not work with older IDE drives
text: It did not work for me at all. Maybe these older IDE drives don't work with anything like this. Unfortunately I didn't get a chance to try it before the return period was up. If you plan to use this with an older drive, be sure and try it before the 30 days is up.

title: Very cool little speaker with big sound.
text: Very cool little speaker with big sound. This is replacing a Canz speaker for use in my rv and while biking. I really like that this has buttons, unlike my Canz, which required me to go to the phone to do anything. I just started riding bikes again after many years and it's nice not to have to go digging in my pocket for the phone when I want to skip a song or something. The mounts could be a bit more robust, but I'm riding a beach cruiser on bike paths, not mountain biking the back 40.

title: Personally like my passport drives better
text: This seems way slower than my Passport drive. But more disconcertingly, it isn't always recognized when I plug it in. I don't really trust it.

title: Fun to play around with
text: I bought this for my full-spectrum infrared camera. When used on such a camera, it generates in-camera faux colors such as yellow leaves and blue skies. Fun to play around with.

title: The camera the D800 should have been. And great for event photogs who like a less obtrusive presence.
text:
I upgraded to the D810 from a D800e. My reaction to the first shot was, "Wow, it's quiet!!" The noise level of the shutter/mirror action is in my opinion less than the Quiet mode on the D800, and doesn't sound odd to my ears. And the Quiet mode is even quieter. What a great upgrade that I wasn't really expecting.

I bought the D810 primarily for the new s-Raw option. I loved having the huge resolution of the D800e, but didn't love the way I was burning through memory cards and portable hard drives with the giant file size of the raw images. I did a month and a half long trip to Alaska last summer and ended up having a new portable hard drive & a few memory cards Fedexed to me in Kodiak as I ran out of space too quickly. My choices were huge raw files or shooting jpgs with the compromises involved there. Or shooting in DX crop format and trying to remember to compose correctly. It was a headache, and when I got back I bought a D600. Unfortunately that camera is not really comparable, and I ended up selling it. When I saw the new D810 had the s-Raw option I jumped on it. It's great for the less critical shooting situations where I don't need the full resolution raw file, but I don't want to go.jpg. The s-Raw resolution is 3680x2456 12-bit uncompressed. I anticipate that my travel laptop will have an easier time handling these files in Lightroom as well, which will be nice.

The high ISO settings have considerably less noise, which is another welcome improvement. The AF seems more accurate as well. All in all, I'm very pleased I upgraded. Very, very happy with the improvements.

title: Blazingly fast and lightweight.
text: I bought an external enclosure for this as I didn't feel like my ultrabook was going to open up easily, plus I have several other computers to use this on.  It's fast.  It seems to drain the laptop battery a lot less too.  I use my portable drives for photo storage and graphics projects, and when I'd be working on a 400mb PSD file using my WD Passport drive it would spin and spin and chug along.  Every save I'd get up and go get a drink or something.  Not with this.  The first time I tried I thought I didn't hit the save button, it was that quick.  Definitely the wave of the future.

title: Great quality bag.  A few quibbles.
text: First thing I noticed out of the box was that the bag looked and felt like it was super high quality.  Really nicely put together.  I'm not 100% sure about the whole split design.  If I have to take the pack off to access my gear anyway, I think I prefer the more traditional style.  But the biggest deal-breaker for me was the lack of easily accessible side mesh pockets.  I like being able to carry a water bottle on one side & my phone or other items I'm constantly grabbing on the other one.  When I'm using this bag the phone has to go in my pocket & the water......well I'm either carrying it in my hand OR putting it in the top of the bag which is bad for two reasons.  One, I don't like to mix fluids & expensive electronics, and two, I have to stop and take the pack off to get to it, which means I don't drink enough.  Oh, and no laptop pocket is kind of a non-starter for me.  I think this might be a great pack for say, an urban shooter, who doesn't need to carry a ton of provisions and a laptop.  For someone like me who's out camping with it & doesn't want to leave the laptop in the campground, it's not the right bag.  Unfortunately, the right bag for me is a lot bulkier, which is why I was hoping this would replace it.  Still, if you don't need to carry a laptop & water bottle, this is a great quality bag for a good price.

title: Fun!  Great for camping/travel/etc.
text: I got this as a Christmas gift and I was a bit stymied as I'd never seen or heard of such a thing.  Rounded up some batteries and an empty box and was amazed at the volume of sound.  I just took it for a weeklong camping trip and it was nice.  You don't (or at least I don't) want very loud music when camping....it's rude to the other campers and scares of the wildlife and masks the sounds of the outdoors.  And why are you there if not to enjoy the outdoors?  So at the subdued volume I like it was fine.  Here's the deal, if you think this thing is gonna sound like Bose, you're dreaming.  If you think 2 AA batteries and a Starbucks cup is gonna provide you with a rock-the-house experience, you're dreaming.  If you're looking for a little conversation piece you can toss in a bag and forget it's there that will provide you with a little background music, your dreams may have just come true.  Really fun item.  On a side note, the current price is too much, the $10 or $15 folks got them on Groupon for is more reasonable.

title: FOr the price, this is great.
text: I love this little setup.  I got it on a Black Friday Harbor Freight deal for @60 bucks and you cannot argue with that price.  The little cameras are surprisingly well built with metal parts.  The tiny monitor weighs nothing in comparison and it's small.  I had no trouble seeing enough detail to be useful, I'm not trying to read the newspaper through the camera, just see if a person is approaching my door/vehicle.  It's plenty good enough for that.  I actually used this recently as a poor man's backup camera in a rental rv.  Attached the camera to the bumper with a Command strip so it would come off without damage & used a 12v power cord I had from something else to power it from the cigarette lighter.  It worked great.  I thought about turning it on one night when I heard coyotes outside but decided not to as I figured I was probably better off not knowing how many there really were.  :-)  Of course this was in AZ with no rain and only for a week.  I don't think these cameras are designed to get wet.  But for simple door cameras (sheltered) so you can see who's at your front or back door, it works great.  And as another reviewer mentioned. you can always hook it to a better monitor or a VCR...you can probably get someone to give you a combined tv/VCR these days or they're almost nothing at goodwill.  Bottom line, worth a try.

title: Doesn't take up much room in the bag.
text: This is a great item to just toss in your suitcase and leave there.  Some, but not all, of the hotels that charge for wifi still have a live ethernet connection that they don't charge for.  I personally don't stay in places without free wifi if I have the choice , but sometimes you don't.  It's so small and light that it's no great hardship to carry just in case.

title: Works as advertised, great for planes, trains, etc.
text:
The filter is pretty easy to apply and works well. I used it on a recent flight and I could tell it was driving my nosy neighbor batty. Though she was dying to see what I was doing, she couldn't. :-) I don't know why it was so intriguing, perhaps the fact that it looked like I was typing on a black screen.

Only negative, dust can and will get under it as it's raised up from the screen slightly. Time will tell how much of an issue this will be. I keep my mini in a microfiber sleeve when not in use.

title: Great for crappy hotel wifi.
text: This has been a godsend while traveling.  It seems like this trip I've hit one crappy hotel wifi after another.  Unbelievably, the only decent wifi where I didn't need to use this antenna was in a $35/nt Rt. 66 'classic' motel in Gallup, NM.  The rest have been either so painfully slow as to be unusable or just not even connectable.  Usually I'd just use my personal hot spot but T-Mobile service is bad here too.  But this adapter has me connected and uploading trip photos at acceptable speed.  It was money well spent.

title: Nicely designed, sturdy case/stand
text: Nice case.  I wanted it primarily to protect my Kindle Fire HDX in my backpack, and it fulfills that function admirably, especially since it has an elastic band on the inside front cover that you can slip over the back of the Kindle when it's close to ensure it doesn't open up in your bag.  Nice touch.  I agree with the other reviewer who stated it's less comfortable to hold vertically.  However, I got used to it quickly, and now kinda pinch it against the Kindle with my left hand, and the lower left corner rests in my palm.  I tend to hold it horizontally most of the time anyway.  The horizontal stand function is great.  There are 3 grooves @ 1/4" apart that hold a tab on the edge of the case, so it's a bit more secure than those that rely on friction alone.  It doesn't pop out of the case at the slightest pressure, it takes a little work, but it's not like my iPhone hard case which requires 10 minutes of cursing and praying every time I remove it.  I like it, and may look for a Belkin case for my iPad as well.

title: Lost mine, this worked on my D300s and also fit D600.
text: It fits my D300s.  It's slightly wider than the original but this is actually a good thing.  Certainly looks like factory for 1/4 the price.  It also fit the D600 and looks almost exactly the same as the original.

title: Great, smooth, reasonably sized ballhead.
text: I currently use an Induro BH2 which is just a bit too large and heavy for my casual usage.  I was hoping this would be a better fit for my carbon fiber travel tripod, and it is.  The movement is smooth as silk, and it holds my Nikon D800 with 28-300 lens with no issues.  It also accepts every Arca-style plate I have though it's a close call with the RRS L-bracket.  I have to open it to its absolute widest to get that in there, but it does fit, unlike my old Giottos ballhead.  The other plate I use all the time is my Cotton Carrier tripod adapter and that works fine also. Another review mentioned how every plate used required an adjustment...well that's an issue with every ballhead as every manufacturer makes their plates in slightly different sizes.  Vanguard helpfully provides you with a detailed picture showing the size of the included plate so you can tell if it will work for your application.  So far, I have no complaints with this ballhead..

title: Unusable at max density.
text: As other reviewers have noted, this filter is unusable at the max density level.  I get dark banding and hot spots.  Opening it a bit wider results in some areas still showing a blue cast.  At about the halfway mark it becomes usable. Unfortunately I missed the return window by one day.  I did post a few example images.  Maybe some are better than others but I got a bad one.  If you roll the dice on one of these filters be sure you test it in the return window.

title: Unreliable, disconnects constantly.
text:
The drive looks impressive, however looks are deceiving. The cable disconnects at the slightest movement, which is a decided flaw in a portable drive. I have had quite a few files get corrupted due to this and it is being relegated to that junk drawer of electronics that just didn't work out. I guess I'll give one shot at contacting the manufacturer as it's past Amazon's return window. If it wasn't, this would have been a return for sure.

Very disappointed in this purchase.

title: Buggy software, insufficient memory and poor mounting hardware.
text: These units seem to be terribly inconsistent. Setup was a giant pain.  First there were a lot of errors connecting to the server.  Then when I tried to input my lifetime maps code, I got the message that I had to update my software first.  Fine, I'll do that.  Click on the update and get the error that there's not enough space on the device.  Ok, I'd read about this problem.....backed the device up so I could delete all the voices except for one.  Backup takes a loooong time.  More server errors.  Finally get the software updated and the maps code in.  Download updated map.  Takes over an hour.  Try to join Map Share.  Service unavailable.  Finally, 4 hours after opening the box, I theoretically have an updated working GPS.  Next day I used it going to work.  The interface is quirky compared to my Garmin but the screen is beautiful and the maps/lane assist/etc are nice. The routing was weird, wanted to take me 5 miles out of my way, but this is common with a lot of gps units. Leave work and when it started recalculating the route, it froze.  Had to reboot it, but it just kept freezing at the TomTom logo.  Get home and reconnect to computer, reload everything, only took 3 hrs this time.  Awesome. The next day I did not even make it out of the subdivision before the unit rebooted itself and got stuck in the reboot loop again.  I hooked it up and restored to the initial software etc.  Tried to do the software update again and was out of memory.  At this point I threw in the towel and did the Amazon return.  I may have gotten a defective unit, but the lack of memory is inexcusable.  Having to delete voices just so you can update the software/maps is really unacceptable.  The mounting hardware is poor also, the unit pops out every time you try to adjust it.  I was really disappointed.

title: Nothing but trouble on my MacBook
text:
It looks great but is a CONSTANT struggle to use. It refuses to eject/unmount, and when I DO finally get it to do so, when I plug it back in it's not recognized. I am constantly having to use Disk Utility to get it to work. I'm going to get all this stuff backed up somehow then reformat as FAT32. Maybe that will work. Seriously, this is a huge disappointment, I have 4 other Passport drives but this is the only HFS one, and I've never had a bit of trouble with the others.

Maybe if I had gotten this free like many of the other reviewers I'd like it better but I doubt it. Because no drive should ever be this much of a headache to use.

title: Cheap, and they work.  Awesome!
text: I ordered three and they work perfectly.  I have a couple Sigma lenses which have finicky rear caps, and these have replaced them.  Much more pleasant to use.

title: Not as described or pictured, and not autofocus, auto anything.
text: I ordered this and couldn't believe my eyes when I opened the box.  First of all, it had obviously been returned at least once already as the box was dirty and torn, and half open.  That's not a deal-breaker as I don't buy stuff for the box, but it gives a poor first impression.  Upon opening it, I found a set of manual extension tubes that appear identical to the ten dollar Fotodix ones.  The sections screw together and obviously have no contacts to allow autofocus or metering.  There were no caps either.  Or any instructions or paperwork.  Totally different than described or pictured.  I might have written this off as an Amazon error, however I have now read some reviews on other Cowboystudio items that make me believe it is not.  I would stay away from this "brand" for now.

title: Simple and works well
text: This is a nice webcam that gives a high quality image.  It took two minutes to install on Win 7 and has worked flawlessly since.

title: Setup not as intimidating as it looks.
text:
This system is a little intimidating out of the box as there are a ton of little parts. It took me a while to get around to installing as it looked like quite the project. However, the directions are clear and easy to follow, and it took less than 30 minutes to set up a two camera system. The software is simple and seems to work well. The biggest advantage in my opinion is you can set the system up to alert you via email if movement is detected. There is also a web page where you can sign in and view your cameras when you're away from home. Best of all, there's an iphone app that also lets you check your cameras. Just viewing is free, if you want the deluxe versions that allow you to change camera setting remotely there is an additional fee. Just viewing is sufficient for my needs however.

One annoyance I've found so far is there are FOUR different colored very bright (some flash) LEDs on the power unit for the main camera. It's VERY annoying and attention grabbing, and screams "UNPLUG ME!" You can turn off the LEDs on the camera itself (I don't, love the deterrent) but there is no way to disable them on the power box. They could do double duty as christmas lights.

All in all, though it's a great system. I'm very happy with it.

title: Needs image stabilization
text:
I am not sure why these cameras are so popular. I'm not tossing it in the Goodwill box, but I would not buy another.

Biggest con, no stabilization. I found the video to be waaaaay too jumpy.

But even when I'm not trying to use it on a boat, I love the fact that you can use regular AA batteries when the battery goes dead. This pro, however, is somewhat canceled out by lack of removable storage. If I could swap out batteries and memory cards I wouldn't be tied to my laptop so much. I would like the ability to record in non-hd to maximize storage but if that's an option I can't find it.

And while the large lens looks great, the fact that it protrudes so much makes it a fingerprint magnet.

The included Flip-share software is pretty cool, I wish it had the capability to view and share video from other devices.

I used this with an iPhone 3Gs and it worked perfectly. No pop up about having to put the phone in airplane mode or any interference.

The speaker looks good, and comes with a neoprene case to protect it. The case isn't very pretty though. There is an odd, somewhat floppy, attached pouch for the a/c adapter that looks like a bit of an afterthought, but at least it's there.

The only reason I give this 4 stars is the stand. It is thin plastic and swivels out when you press on it. The attachment does not feel terribly robust, and I worry about its durability. Also, the battery cover is behind it and didn't close securely the first time I installed the batteries.

text:
I really wanted this product to replicate the multi-touch trackpad on my new Macbook. Once you've used those large trackpads with scrolling and panning, etc., you find it hard to settle for a normal windows trackpad. (It is really the only thing I like better about the Mac) I also have a great handwriting recognition software called ritepen that I got with a previous tablet, and it does a great job of reading my lousy handwriting. Unfortunately, at least on my Windows Vista laptop, the Bamboo Fun doesn't quite cut it. It took multiple attempts to install to get it working properly but after the third or fourth time it did install. It doesn't perform that great, however, it gets laggy at times and once twice went into full spaz mode with the cursor jumping everywhere.

I'm still rating it pretty highly as I loved the pressure sensitivity. It works a lot better than my previous tablet and I was having some serious fun in Paint Shop Pro. It was also really nice to have that large area to draw upon. On my 13.3 Macbook and my 14" Win laptop the tablet lays nicely atop the keyboard and has little rubber feet that are perfectly situated to keep it off the keyboard. I don't know if i would work on a bigger laptop. It matches my aluminum Macbook, for those who like aesthetics. :-) The inclusion of Nikon Efex 3.0 was a nice surprise. Those filters are useful, but way too pricey for me. I was pretty happy to get them in this bundle. I think that Wacom, who is known for decent support, will tweak the drivers and alleviate the problems I've had.

title: Unit good, XM and Audible Player not as good.
text:
Update after a month:(6-2-06) XM setup on this unit was a real pain. I have 2 other XM radios so tried to add this one to my account online. No go, you have to call to activate this. Which means they charge you a $14.99 activation fee. It is $5 less online and sometimes they don't even charge it. Calling XM is an exercise in frustrating voice response menus, which won't let you activate the traffic service anyway. So just cut to the chase and say "Operator" loudly several times at the outset and save yourself some time and aggravation. It took 2 days and 3 calls to get the radio activated and working.

Secondly, do yourself a favor and toss the card about the 3 "free" audible.com ebook downloads. First of all you have to give them your cc info. Then you don't get 3 ebooks. You only get one real ebook. You get one credit and many books are more than one credit! They also "give" you a 30 minute speech by some guy, whoopie doo. So you get 2 downloads. They also don't tell you you have to download their player even to download anything. I figured that out finally after 5 tries. The player has crashed twice, I've heard 5 minutes of audio. If you actually want to transfer the ebooks to the 2730, you need to hook the unit up to the PC, and make sure the pc's connected to the internet. It's all too spywareish for my tastes. I cancelled it immediately but I regret ever signing up for the service.

I am very pleased with the gps. The routing is good and screen is bright and has nice graphics. I did not think I'd like the 3d view but I do, very much. You can add your own points of interest which I have had to do a lot....this area is growing so rapidly that many things are missing from the database. The traffic function of the XM radio is fantastic, unfortunately the coverage is very limited. Only 2 roads in my county have any coverage and it is only a few miles of each.

I love the MP3 player, and the remote is extremely handy. The XM radio is not nearly as full-featured as my old unit. I am used to being able to punch in the channel number, you can't do that on this unit. The other thing I *really* miss is the "favorite song" feature on my old XM radio (where it alerts you if a favorite song is playing on another channel) and that is not available on this unit. The FM transmitter is a lot weaker than my old XM one also, I often have static problems. I do live in the DC area but I had no trouble with the old radio. I really wanted the MP3, traffic and weather features, I just didn't expect the XM radio to be so disappointing.

title: *Updated review - would not recommend.
text:
*UPDATE ON REVIEW AFTER A FEW DAYS OF USE.
After installing the unit and using it for a few days it now has pop up ads on screen and wants you to purchase subscription services for extra features that were not mentioned in the description of the item. The ads make the unit difficult and unsafe to use while driving. We would not recommend this product.

ORGINAL INSTALL REVIEW BEFORE THE POP-UP ADS.
Pros: As the headline says, everything you need to install is included in the box including a backup camera and GPS antenna. The wire harness adapter is pre-wired to plug the unit directly into your factory harness/plugs without splicing any wires. It mounts directly up to the stock radio location without the use of any installation adapters or cutting plastics. The stock plastic trim plate aligns perfectly over the unit once installed and keeps a clean factory look. Optional RCA plug wire harnesses and USB tether plugs are also included for compatibility with your own custom aftermarket external sound equipment if needed. It works with both Apple CarPlay and Android Auto enabled cell phones. It can be used as a mobile Wi-Fi internet hotspot for passengers when paired with your cellphone. System updates can be downloaded directly to the unit through home or cell Wi-Fi once installed. If you have steering wheel controls, they can be manually programed from a menu on the unit to do the functions intended.

Cons: Menus are a little confusing and hard to find "while doing the initial radio setup". The EQ setting screen is hard to find and the HiFi setting (which acts a volume/bass boost) should be turned off if are using stock factory Jeep speakers. HiFi is turned on by default and it makes the volume level far too loud on the stock speakers at its lowest possible volume knob setting. Once the EQ and HiFi 0n/0ff settings are set to your ideal preferences you won’t need to navigate to the EQ screen again. Last minor con is when/how you exit your installed Aps. You’ll need to swipe them completely off the screen to stop them from running in the background and slowing the unit down similar to a cellphone.

Overall: Lots of features. Easy downloadable state maps for NAVI. Easy to download updates. Sounds better than the stock Jeep CD player once the EQ setting have been adjusted. Has a microphone intergraded into the faceplate. Easy to customize the display brightness, colors, wallpaper, and sounds. All the buttons/knobs are backlit with your headlight activation. It will play movies and MP3s.

I will not replace it with this same brand as I do not do anything but move my laptop from my bedside table to my lap at night before bed.  There is ZERO reason for 'wear and tear' after 4 months.

title: S20 Ultra Owners!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
text: I bought THREE of the 45W Samsung Super chargers and it took them 1 hour 14min to fully charge my phone from the 51% mark.  This cord charged my phone from 49% to full charge in 57 minutes.  That is 30% faster than the $50 Samsung Super Chargers with their pathetic 3 FOOT cords!!!!  I sent all three of them back to Verizon with a 'note'.  These cords ROCK!  I have two of them them plugged into USB ports in a desktop multi charge station that has electrical outlets in the top of it as well on the back corner of my desk.  The cords I have at home (same kind) plug straight into my wall outlets and bang out the same results.  The one in my backpack plugs into a really good battery pack and chargers about the same pace as the Samsung plugged into the wall.  I have five of them... they are worth every dime! ! !

title: No Bueno!
text: I have the Bose Sound Ultra for Android and they sound amazing to me.  BUT, the cord keeps fraying at the junction of the plug that goes into my phone.  I just had to order my 9th pair through Best Buy (who is no longer going to carry them for Android...only IOS).  wanted was an economical pair to have in my backpack for "emergency".  I ordered three different ones to see what sounded good to use until I find a permanent WIRED earphone with a tough cord made to survive the life of New York City with delicious sound.  These things ... THESE THINGS.... they will be sent back tomorrow.  They are HORRIBLE.  I wasn't expecting to be wowed for the price.  But the reviews made me think I might get somewhat of a "wow".  Seriously, I cannot even believe I allowed myself to have hope.  I can only hope Robert Smith of The Cure will forgive me for using his music to test these made for a six year old. There you have it.  I wouldn't accept these things to listen to a voice read a book to me.
