title: I so desperately want this to be great that apparently I ordered one 2 years ago and ...
text:
I so desperately want this to be great that apparently I ordered one 2 years ago and blocked it out of my memory and just received another one. Here are the issues:

1) If you have a good ergonomic keyboard (I have Microsoft 4000), then the keys on this are no better.

2) You will never have enough keys on there. Where is Escape? Number Keys? Large space bar? WSAD keys? Sure you can assign most of them but it just won't work well enough.

3) If you are thinking about assigning the the top row to numbers, it doesn't work well. It was designed for the middle top key to be your W in your WSAD keys (Those 4 have a nice curved depression for you to feel them here).

4) Reassigning WSAD to a lower set of keys will make your fingers cramped and start aching in no time.

5) I use Steam, adding Steam games to this is a HUGE pain the... um, fingers. First, I see no documentation about it. Second this thing wants to know exactly where the games are. That's no easy task when you have a few hundred steam games, the icon on your desktop won't work.

6) It doesn't autodetect what's running on my Windows 8 64bit machine. I even ran it as administrator.

7) It's not natural. You constantly want your fingers go where they have for years if you are a veteran to keyboard usage.

8) You spend more time wondering and looking down which key you assigned what to, where your hand is on the keys, where you assigned 3, 4, or other numbers to than you should.

9) In the end, I keep going back to my keyboard.

Hopefully I'll remember that this is not as good as I imagine and want it to be and stop ordering it every couple of years.

title: FANTASTIC! Works great
text:
FANTASTIC! Works great!

Has a website to configure it, you reach the website by connecting to it using wifi, no need to plug into the wired Ethernet.

It has an Ethernet port in case you want to directly plug something in (or a switch).

Configuring and re-configuring took seconds!

Range is awesome!

title: Used this all of 3 times.  Possibly twice even, then it died.
text: I bought this in November, tested it, and then forgot about it.  Six month later I went to use it, and it's completely dead.  Total waste of money.

title: Fantastic tablet.  I had always wanted a huge tablet, heck I wanted a 20" one.  But you do get a huge tablet.
text:
This is a flawless tablet. Everything you'd expect. There are a few things that don't feel comfortable or might feel jarring, but then you are here because you want a huge tablet, so they should be expected.

The screen if gorgeous! And Samsung has done a great job of making the icons proportional to the screen. Because at this super high resolution, if you left the icons to the normal size, they would be TINY. That said, be prepared to see -huge- icons since they are proportionally bigger than, say, even a huge Note 3 phone. Still the ratio isn't one to one from a tiny tablet, there is room for a couple of more icons per row.

Weight: This is light and feels great... for a tablet its size. That said, be prepared to always have to put it or your hands on something if you are using it more than a couple of minutes. While it is solid & light enough to hold it in one hand by a corner and use, your hand will be cramping in no time.

Look and feel: Just awesome. I don't get professional reviewers issue with "faux leather", it looks and feels awesome! Even though it's bigger than all the rest, this is still a tablet, as I said above, you can brag and pick it up by a corner without feeling like you are putting too much force on a corner or anything of the nature. But its dimensions do mean you have to lean your arm on something or put it down for using more than reading a single email, even then...

The large dimensions also mean awkward reading in bed unless you are sitting up with your legs or a pillow under it. If you are laying on the ground or on your bed faxing down with it flat and reading websites or an online book with the tablet in portrait format (as one would tend to read long things), then the top is too far away and an angle, as would a tall magazine be.

This can easily be fixed with a little something to prop the end away from you up of course, but just making sure you realize that you will get what you are asking for, a gorgeous, great feeling tablet that is the largest on the market, but you are also getting something rather large, and all that comes with that, so expect it. I read all professional reviews saying pretty much that and I figured they were just complaining to have something to write about... nope, it really is a bit hard to wield.

title: It does what it says, but it does NOT work for Windows 2 Go
text: I've gotten non-certified drives to work as a Windows 2 Go USB, but I tried various solutions with this, and it simply will not boot.

title: It does what it looks like it would do.  See the body/text for the surprises.
text:
I expected the back to have two plugs, fitting into a two plug wall plate. Instead it only has a plastic prong for the second/bottom wall plate.

So basically you are plugging this into one plug, and having a plastic stick where the second/lower plug's ground prong would be going into that plug, making it more stable.

The screw you see in the middle is not keeping this thing together, it goes through the whole thing and replaces the screw on your wall's plate (so it will screw through the wall plate into the wall plate's brackets). You can of course remove it and not use it.

title: A bit more rigid than I had hoped, but it works great.
text: That is not to say it's too rigid, but I had hoped to use this in bed on a laptop with the cable falling to the bed while holding my laptop, but it makes a long arch in the air, not bending too well.

title: Junk, lasted maybe 5 uses
text:
The USB contacts stop contacting. I've tried it on 3 different PC's USB plugs.

I've had dozens of USB drivers, never seen one do this. Especially after just a couple of uses.

title: Could not create Windows 2 Go
text:
Sure this isn't certified for Windows 2 Go, only their 500GB is, but why shouldn't this work just because it's not certified?

It simply died, no reason. Acronis also dies when partitioning this drive. Running their own Test application right now... hmm, says it will take hours, will update later.

Hmm, well it seems to be dead. Hours after starting to use it. Reducing it to 1 star and sending it back.

Also WELL worth noting: If you have Windows 8 (does this on my Windows 7 too), it keeps "disconnecting/going to sleep" almost immediately. The reason is actually under Power Options in Control Panel. If you go to Change Options, then Advance Options, scroll down to USB, you'll have to disable whatever that sole USB option is.

EDIT: I've since picked up another from CostCo (Amazon was cheaper), but this one works. Furthermore, with Windows 8.1 (has to be Enterprise), I was able to get Windows To Go to work on this just fine. Changing my review from 1/5 to 3/5. One dead drive, one working fine, for now.

title: Have had these for years, they are fantastic
text: Though I don't use them continuously, I use them 2 or 3 times a day and have done so since pretty much they came out.  I sometimes forget to plug it in and leave it out for a couple of days and it has no problems with charges.  In fact with light use, it has never run out of battery.  Sounds is perfect.

title: Seems fine, but I thought it would collapse in on itself
text:
Maybe it's just me but this totally looks like it would collapse in on itself, making it the height of the yellow part. Guess I just presumed.

The only moving part (other than the top loop that lets you hang it, like any other hook) is a mirror on the back (you can see it on the picture with the two next to the Pepsi bottle, one has it moved up, the other does not). It basically reflect more like towards the front from the back.

There is no way to make it work like a normal flashlight either (the description "flash-light style" is just plain misleading). You basically either get a 360 degree lantern, or more of a 270 degree lantern.

title: There are NO keyboard shortcuts the switch recognizes!
text:
This switch works great as a manual switch, but it is misleading to say it works with keyboard shortcuts, "IT" (the switch) DOES NOT.

What it will do is have software that will control it and the software will detect keyboard shortcuts. So this works fine in the many "driving/controlling" PCs connected to one USB device, but not a driving/controlling USB device connected to many PCs.

So you'd be mistaken, if like me, were hoping to use it as an automated KVM (well, minus the V I guess) switch. You can have a USB hub attached to it and your mouse and keyboard attached to the hub, and connect it to multiple PCs and hope that you can go from machine to machine/screen to screen, but NOT by pressing some key combo. You have to press the buttons on the switch.

title: Bought two, neither worked in either my PSP 1000 or 3000.
text:
I had an older version of this, so when I bought my PSP 3000, I ordered this. It didn't work in either my old or new PSP. So I ordered a second one (third if you count the older version which looks different than this one). That too doesn't work.

I wasted money not returning the first that didn't work, this one I'm going to waste my time and return.

title: The description is purposefuly misleading
text:
The line "Since IR-Illumination can't be perceived or seen by the human eye it is perfect for covert applications or applications where you don't want visible lighting." is intentional mis-advertisement.

Sure true IR Illumination can't be seen by the human eye, but these 3 giant LEDs shine red. Sure the visible red glow isn't anywhere as much as if you had 3 giant red LEDs, but these are definitely visible, even in bright daylight.

title: This is my second one, first one lasted years
text:
This item is awesome... and I'd give it a 5 (thought I had already), but alas I left my first one in the old house and the new one died after a single day while the last set worked for many years.

Hopefully that's a fluke. Returning the dead one and ordered a new one.

title: Another fantastic KABOOJM box.  The new design is gorgeous!
text:
I have every Kaboom! box JVC has made and love the design of this last one best.

I give it a four because:
. It's not as powerful as the original, but then none of them have been since. WHY JVC???
. The iPhone interface was a bad idea. Not only iPhone 5 doesn't support it, the MAJORITY of the market is now Android, why lock it down to a slice of the market, huge as that slice might be?
. It's not as long as the original. The length gave it better look and feel.

title: Just bought my second one
text:
First one worked for 6 years, then I moved and I forgot to take it with me. This product works great!

If you need to narrow its field of vision (I, for example, didn't want cats to set it off), you can either point it upwards, or put a piece of electric tape over the area you don't want effect (I put one at the bottom of the sensor).

I used this as a front door alarm since I can't always hear the door. Glued an earth magnet to the bottom and now it easily sticks anywhere there is a screw or metal. Just perfect.

title: Love it, does exactly what it says it does
text:
Not the best setup, but it has a web page you can run things off and setup. I didn't expect a good setup program though, it seems companies hire any Tom Dick and Harry as programmer.

Beyond that though, it worked just fine with my router, but even better, it has a builtin micro flash bay that lets you directly record and take pictures to it.

You can setup the camera to upload pictures or video to your network drive, or to the flash card. Pictures are 2MP, so nothing great, but better than I expected. Video is just fine too.

I have it setup to start recording when there is motion and take pictures (both). I use it at parties and the infrared works perfect for that. I have two of the best camera and camcorders with Infrared (so nothing new, the old ones that had some power), and the infrared on this works just as well if not better.

The IR light is not invisible though, so no candid shots. It lights up red. The visible red spectrum however is dim, like a power led, so it won't interfere with your lighting.

title: Wasn't that great the first night, much better now.
text:
The first night I opened it, I was not at all impressed, I wish I had just kept my SD4000 IS PowerShot and asked for something else for Christmas. I took pictures side by side and it wasn't that impressed. Not sure what the problem was then (condensation? The box sat outside for hours before I brought it in and opened it) but it has gotten better.

1) There are lots of improvements over my older Canons but this is definitely bulkier and bigger
2) The wireless feature works great with my home wifi and my Android. Took no time at all to setup either.
3) Low light pictures do seem a lot more bright, as if there is a hidden flash, but are grainy.
4) Camera is solid, feels great in your hand
5) The "ring" isn't a smooth turning one, it "clicks" quite awkwardly between each setting, so you go clicking through options and not in a way you can run through them, one at a time, and not smooth at all, I find myself using the menu items instead.
6) The touchscreen is awesome!
7) Touchscreen picture taking is useless, you'd be taking pictures all the time, there is no way to hold the camera really without touching the screen

In the end, I was quite happy to get a new and fairly cheap camera, but it simply isn't THAT much better than my SD4000, except in low light, and then not super low light, just low light.

I have since ordered and received the Sony RX100. Which is why I waited to return this camera, wanted to compare them side by side. After a couple of days of "playing" (yes I'm clearly not a professional, but I'd guess nor are most consumers), here are my thoughts:

1) The picture quality of the RX100 is better, but not always, and not that much more, sure it has a lot more pixels, but over all, not a huge difference. For just pictures, for ordinary consumer, I'd say get the S110, for being almost half the price, the pictures aren't THAT much different.

2) The RX100's menus are awesome for those who aren't well versed in photography, it actually explains what each setting does and is for, even with a sample picture, and then within each has sub menus explaining what they do, with yet more pictures, and finally has a help button. FANTASTIC!

3) S110's wifi is great, RX100 has none. Sending pictures to your phone and then posting or emailing them on the fly is really great.

4) As great as the S110's low light "brightness" is, the RX100 is a good 10 times better on really low lights. When there is enough light for you to see fairly clearly, they seem close, but when it's dark enough where you can't make out too clearly what you are looking at, and you can no longer see the colors, the RX100 can still take pictures that look like a cheap camera WITH a flash took (with a flash of course they both look great), where as the S110 takes pictures similar to what your eyes see when it's that dark. The RX100 really shines with no flash in pretty darn dark settings.

5) There are lots of other things the RX100 does, but might not be of interest to you, but they are there, like take pictures while recording video (but only in interlaced video, when I put it on p it doesn't let me take pictures), but those pictures aren't as great as doing so without video recording in room conditions. The function ring is much better as well.

6) S110's touchscreen awesomeness is missing

7) You can still put an S110 in your back pocket, though it would be like a thick heavy wallet. The RX100 however is almost a centimeter thicker and most of that is the lens sticking out further so I wouldn't call it a pocket camera. The S110 feels better (grainy, square metal feel, but the Sony has a smooth more rounded metal finish) and looks better.

title: Used them to lower the sound escaping when having parties
text:
Oh and this is ONE 2.5 inch foam. I had forgotten that I had bought this before myself and ordered it again this week thinking I was getting 2 half inch foams. Bad description 2-1/2 instead of 2.5 is quite misleading.

I cut this to fit my windows and it stays in pretty well (as long as you but an inch or so too much so it's squished a bit).

Definitely helps with noise levels going through it. I have not however used it for echo and such.

title: Just got my second one
text:
I had a 28" Viewsonic for years, figuring this wasn't that much bigger or better. Boy was I wrong. This is NIGHT & DAY different.

My pair of old 28" screens simply couldn't handle dark or black parts. Playing WOW or any game where it was dark, it simply looked crappy, while things look beautiful on this monitor.

Then there is the extra 2". You'd think that's just a tiny bit larger, but it is quite noticeable.

The resolution of course beats all other monitors. It is super crisp and gorgeous! Though of course this does mean you have to have a high end card that supports the resolution and be prepared for a heck of a lot more horsepower (and heat, and watts/power) needed to run games at this resolution.

The bad: Sitting next to my 26" Dell Ultrasharp, this thing simply can't compete when it comes to colors, white balance, & and hue. No matter how much you mess with the colors, it simply won't compare. When sitting next to the older gorgeous 26", it almost looks like there is a layer of film on the 30". I was hoping it was just my older 30" (from early 2011), but nope, my new one that I got yesterday (build June 2012) has the same problem.

Finally, the reason I needed a replacement is because a vertical line appeared in my old one that would randomly appear and never go away. I tried different video cards, but it was the monitor. Glad I had gotten the extended warranty.

Oh and one other thing, on the new one, I can't use the "custom" settings to change colors & hues (though it has half a dozen builtin ones). The custom setting do NOT apply evenly to both sides of the screen!! The left and right get out of sink! This effect is surprisingly not at all noticeable on a document or a browser page, but no way to avoid seeing it on a picture or a movie. I simply went back to using one of the preset colors and all is well again.

title: Stopped working less than 10 minutes after installation
text:
First thing I noticed when I got it working (wasn't as easy as any other router I've ever had, and I've easily had ten so far), was that it had a bar saying it had a firmware update. Unlike older ones, this one was a one click, updating itself. Fancy, nice, except when it was done, the router is dead.

Searching the forums (with my old router) shows that the firmware must have "gotten corrupt".

Well, if you are going to have a method to have the router do it all itself, make damn sure it actually works before you sell it to the customer! Like VERIFY a complete/full download of firmware before it installs? Have a way to UNDO it? Hard concepts I know.

title: About 100 pictures per battery, 9/10 picture quality
text:
This is a heck of a camera for $149! It takes great pictures (not DSLR quality, but pretty great otherwise), fast, and has an incredible zoom.

Two sets of Duracell batteries took right about 200 pictures and 6 videos. So about 100 pictures and 3 videos each set before running out.

Considering you pay about $200 less for the same camera with rechargeable batteries (and then I always buy a second/backup battery, for another $60 or so), I am just fine buying batteries. This way I'll never run out, not like there are many places you can't find AA batteries.

The only thing to note is that unlike other Canons, the flash does NOT pop up. The camera's screen blinks with something saying you should pop the flash up if it thinks you need it. Not doing so, is your way of forcing the camera to adjust and take the picture with current lighting (equivalent of changing flash settings on other Canons to turn off flash).

ps. Video has 2 settings, 1280x720 is the high/max resolution. At this resolution it takes about 9 minutes of video then stops (all digital cameras seem to have a max video size which equates to # of minutes).

title: USB ports are way too weak to power most of my devices
text:
Half of my devices won't charge at all or at a trickle (all night results in a 40% charge) including my EVO View and Galaxy tablets.

Also the Galaxy sees it as something it can sync with instead of just a charger (using the original Galaxy USB cable), so it can only be charged while it is turned off and then at a horribly slow rate.

Forget using both USB plugs or using a multiplier to use even more devices when you have power hungry devices.

title: First time making an RJ jack, did not go smoothly
text:
While I finally got it to work, doing so was not remotely intuitive. But if you just bought one and wondering what you need to do, here is how this one works:

You have to use the little plastic or small flat screw driver to put each wire in the lid, not the metal prongs. And when I say put them in the lid, I mean ALL the way down, they each pass a certain point when you get a feed back as your are pushing down that they are now firmly in. When done, double make sure they are all as far flat against the lid as possible (otherwise they'll align with the wrong metal prong).

Now close the lid and use pliers or something to REALLY clamp it down. After I removed the cable's built in jack and added this, my speed dropped from 1gb to 100, but after I grabbed a small rubber band TIGHTLY wrapped it around the lid/body, the speed is back up to 1gb.

So definitely not the best product, but I have nothing to compare it to since this was the first time I had done this.

title: Everything I had hoped for.
text:
For a first series Honeycomb Android, it is FANTASTIC. Responsive, fast, smooth, nothing remotely lags.

Gorgeous bright screen, apps working as good or better than one would hope on wireless only, great design (was worried the sides/margins were too big, they aren't), multitasking, all in all, far superior to the iPad 2 which I just returned yesterday.

The weight and price could come down a bit, or halve, but I'm sure they'll do that as more Android tablets come out.

title: Great monitor, EXCELLENT deal, too small of a viewing angle
text:
This monitor is perfect in every way I can think of, and I am a power user and can think of a lot of things. I was really worried that blowing up 1900x1200 this much would pixelate or there would be notable space between pixels... none of that, picture is awesome. I was also worried about ghosting in fast action games and there is none.

The problem I have is that the monitor's viewing angle is pretty small. So, for example, when sitting behind me desk, the top of the monitor is dimmed a bit. If I stretch my neck or stand up, I can see that the picture is not dimmed and it is only the angle. Since the stand is not adjustable, I can't bring it down the last few inches for which there seems to be room, so specially when playing games, the top two inches look inversed and blacks look weird because my head, level with the monitor, is out of the view angle of the top couple of inches.

Finally, the colors while gaming aren't that great. I play WOW a lot and blacks and shades look not so great to pretty bad.

title: It is the best at everything except taking pictures
text:
This camera has an awesome 3" display, the menus are the easiest and most user-friendly than any other camera I've seen, the design and everything is awesome. I have been waiting to go from my big digital SLR to a small little camera and I had high hopes for this.

It takes STUNNING video, you can zoom through, if you go from a light area or a dark one and back it adjusts right away, and just all together you think you had a camcorder. Fine video mode is just excellent.

Close up pictures are also excellent. Outside, in the sun pictures are pretty good (nothing to write home about but usable).

Pictures taken inside, or in auto mode, or in any settings over 100 asa (what's the point of having up to 3200 sensitivity when it look worse than a cell phone picture?). There is insane color bleed around the edges of things (like a millimeter or two of it), there is no "edge" definition, if you have something thin like a power cord, it will just be an undefined black blur, and EVERYTHING is grainy. Hands down some of the worst pictures I've ever seen. My cell phone literally takes far better picture at 1.3 mega pixels.

I returned the camera, got a replacement, and it has the EXACT same issues.

title: Mixed
text:
Well setting this up took all of 2 minutes, the menus were exactly what you'd expect, same old Linksys setup, but with a ton more options.

Everything went smoothly, speed was great, and no issues.

Then I went to update the firmware (3 minutes after setting it up) as I have with my other Linksys routers many times. The browser got redirected to a page not found right after the upgrade started and would do the same every time. I rebooted the router to try again, and it no longer turns on.

So if you get it, either try to upgrade the firmware right away so you can return it if it dies, or don't touch the firmware.

Starting to lose faith in Linksys.

title: Not bad at all for the price
text:
For the price, this camera works pretty darn well. My router/office is at the end of the house furthest from the front on the first floor, and I wanted a camera on the second floor up front to view my front lawn for when people come and I don't hear the bell and for the damn annoying neighbors that mess with my things (watching to see who is going to mess with my garbage cans as I write this)... and it is working GREAT! The refresh rate at 640x480 is far bettern than I had expected.

The picture looks pretty good but while I can see individual leaves on trees, I can understand why one would have a hard time recognizing someone's face unless you knew them, not the clearest/sharpest picture, but certainly good enough to see what is going on.

It is also true that as soon as it starts to get dark, and I mean just starts to, the camera becomes useless. I have also not found any other way of viewing the camera's output than through the ActiveX component (but I haven't tried too hard yet either).

However configuring the camera was very easy. You connect it using the wired network port (you can connect this camera wired or wireless, which I think is something they fail to advertise enough), you go to the 192.something.something.x site of the camera, tell it to use DHCP, change it's IP address, set up your wireless setting and WAP, and you are set. You can unplug the camera from the network and power (it retains the settings) and you are set.

I have it hanging upside down from the ceiling of my window using a magnet. Pretty light.

So if you are looking to recognize people's faces from across the street, this isn't for you. If you just want to see that there are people across the street, then it is great. I got more than I expected. Well worth the money. Guess it is all in what you expect ;)

title: 1-5 second delay in response
text:
This is the worst mouse ever. While it feels great in your hand, and I wish more mice had rubber on their body, the functionality is horrid. When you move the mouse, it takes 1 to several seconds before the mouse/receive "wakes up". This happens EVERY time you stop moving the mouse not after a while of sitting.

I called their tech support, all they would do is tell me to use newer and different batteries. So I yelled at them and they sent me another set... and it did the exact same thing.

I want a mouse that moves when I move my hand!

What's worse? When the mouse actually does sit around for more than 30 seconds (maybe a minute? didn't time it but not long at all), then it really goes to sleep and you can't make it move at all unless you click one of the buttons... what sucks? It SENDS the "wakeup" button click through!!!

So if you left your mouse on "Buy Now" on a thousand shares of X to think about it and research it and decided not to buy it, you are screwed. You can't move the mouse off the button and clicking the button to wake mouse up will pass the click through and press on the button for you.

title: Two weeks later it's broken
text:
Junk - I've had it two weeks. TWO WEEKS and in the middle of a meeting it just stopped working.

Yeah, I'm sending it back.

title: wish i didn't toss out my old one!
text:
On my old d-link router I had excellent speed (wired desktop, wireless desktop and 5 laptops), but only one of the ports in the back worked - whenever I'd want to swap to xbox or bluray dvd (neither of which I had the wireless option for) I'd have to swap out the cables. This got annoying - time to upgrade.

Waste of money. Yes this was easy to set up, even the least technically inclined person wouldn't have an issue setting this thing up. But on my old router, everything ran at optimal speed, this thing doesn't even let me watch a movie without constant stopping, its finally stopped so long that I pulled up my laptop and started writing this review.

I think i'm going to have to return it.

title: Awesome quality - Netflix is perfect on here!
text:
I love this player!

Set-up is super easy, its been less then 20 minutes since I unboxed this and already i'm streaming from Netflix. I was worried that I'd encounter buffering issues, but nope. It took less then a minute to load the movie and its playing like a champ! I'm not using wireless though, so I can only attest to the quality of a wired connection. Just ran a test on my wireless computer and i'm at 2.07mps, so I imagine the wired connection is slightly faster then that.

Just a quick note on the Netflix side, for those of you who don't currently have accounts, NOT EVERYTHING IS AVAILABLE FOR LIVE PLAY.

UPDATE: I just upgraded(!) my router and now have nothing but issues with buffering. I'm about to uninstall and return this new, guaranteed faster speeds router and reinstall my old one. After half a year of flawless playback, this can only be the issue of the router. For anyone experiencing buffering issues, check your router and if you have the option of testing another router, do so - that will hopefully fix it. p.s. its been 10 minutes and I still haven't been able to get my movie to re-start. crazy.

title: A good fitting angle plug. Sturdy.
text: I’m really pleased with the sturdiness of this angle adapter. Plugs fit in with a real positive snap and no sloppiness.

title: Great cable with a great warrenty.

I contacted the company’s support and they replied the next day very kindly saying they had already made arrangements for a replacement! That is exceptional! Highly recommended.

title: Good adapter!

title: Great cable adapter.

title: Update. Not a good deal. Unreliable

Great deal. Well made.

title: Get the Megivez E20 instead of these.
text: The Megivez E20 is better than this T08 by far for about the same cost. I started out with these Megivez T08 model but the microphone did not perform well at all for phone calls. I contacted Megivez and told them I wanted to upgrade to the Megivez E20 based on reviews and that the volume can be controlled from the earbuds unlike the T08 and I must say they are a huge improvement in all areas. I am happy to report that Megivez is way on top when it comes to customer service and support. They quickly sent out the E20 model and it is much superior, in my opinion, as the microphone works and volume can be controlled from the earbuds themselves. The sound is quite good provided some adjustments are made. There is plenty of bass. In fact, too much as it can make the rest of the frequency spectrum sound muddy. However, using the built in EQ on my iPad and iPhone and selecting Bass Reducer mode brightens up the midrange and highs with still plenty of tight bass, as it should be, with a balanced sound. I feel that, like headphones or speakers, a short period of “break in” time is needed as the sound improves after a few days of use. The buds are very comfortable and unobtrusive. I often fall sleep with them in. The charging case is solidly constructed, more slim and compact than these T08, and fit comfortably in pocket or bag. I have seen the E20 buds offered with a $10, $15, even a $20 dollar coupon by Amazon making these TWS earbuds an amazing bargain. Highly recommended.

title: Outstanding truly wireless, in-ear buds
text:
I've sought a pair of wireless earbuds for a couple years now, both for general use, and for when running/working out. I originally purchased a pair of Blueant Pump earbuds a few years ago. They are completely waterproof, and have over-the-ear hooks designed to keep them firmly attached during vigorous activity. Those buds are very solid overall, but have a couple critical flaws that prompted me to keep searching. My ideal earbuds would have the following characteristics:

* truly wireless
* strong battery life
* in-ear "wings"/arc support, as opposed to employing over the ear hooks (I sometimes wear glasses and also hats which I didn't want competing for space with the ear buds)
* excellent audio (music and phone calls)
* hear through/ambient listening capable

The Blueant pumps lacked the ambient option, and also had a cable connecting the two buds, which prevented me from effectively performing weight lifting exercises while laying down, since the stiff cable would bump against the bench when I laid back, and knock loose the earbuds, breaking the seal in my ear canal.

After exhaustively researching my options, I decided to give the Powerbeats Pro a shot (in spite of the over the ear hooks), as well as these earbuds under review, the Sony WF-SP800N model. I decided against trying out the very popular Jabra Elite Active 75t, due to the shorter battery life relative to the Powerbeats and Sony options.

The Powerbeats Pro are indeed comfortable, and do a great job staying in place. What I learned is that they do not offer listen-through audio, (which I need for situational awareness when running/biking), and the audio when taking phone calls was incredibly scratchy. This was not a Bluetooth connectivity issue, because the phone played streaming Spotify audio just fine, and the cell phone was in my pocket the entire time, so distance was a non-factor. I found that I could manage to wear glasses at the same time as the Powerbeats buds, but it was slightly awkward. Additionally, I noticed some worrisome discussion on Reddit about the long term battery life of the Powerbeats Pro model, and so for those factors (and considering the high cost of this item), I decided against the Powerbeats Pro earbuds.

The Sony earbuds have performed fantastically. Initially I was disappointed because there was an unbelievable amount of wind noise on my first run using them. The fit felt sloppy and I was concerned about them dropping out of my ear. When I got home, I switched the earbud tips for the largest size. That made all the different in the world. The wind was largely sealed out (there is still some), and the music jumped to life. The fit was true, and I had no problem with the earbuds falling out, even when I went out of my way to shake them loose.

Battery life promises to eclipse even the mighty Powerbeats Pro, and the Sony model offers ambient listening. The water resistance looks to be at least the equal of the Powerbeats, and phone call clarity was excellent. All this at a price more than $100 less than the Powerbeats.

I will update this review if my opinion changes significantly as I get more time in with these Sony earbuds. Based on my initial experiences, I strongly recommend them, for both athletic and casual use. They are excellent.

title: Very good basic case, with excellent belt loop design. Fits camera 4.2 x 2.4 x 1.4 inches perfectly.
text:
This case cost just under $6 when purchased a few days back. As is my practice when purchasing or accessorizing an expensive item (in this case, the Sony HX20V camera), I did fairly exhaustive research prior to making the purchase. (Other cases on my shortlist were the LowePro Apex 20 and the Lowepro Rezo 30). My main interests were portability and protection. I wanted to be able to store one extra battery along with the camera, inside an efficient case that would allow for belt-carry and had a dual-zipper design to allow for the wrist strap to be used while the camera is inside the case. This case meets all those requirements. The fit is snug but not tight around the camera, and the zippers have protective flaps along the inside edge to protect against scratches on the camera. The front pouch, which has a velcro flap is pretty small, but will accommodate the extra battery. The dual zippers can be closed at the middle of the case with the wrist strap coming out between the heads of the zippers. This facilitates carrying the camera by the wrist strap if desired, while still benefiting from the case's protection in the event of bumps or falls. The padding sewn into the case is firm and seems like an adequate buffer against minor knocks. One feature I really like is how the belt loop works. The belt loop extends from the upper back edge of the case, and snaps in place at the bottom back edge. Instead of being a single piece of material that extends from the top to the bottom of the case, it is an actual loop. The upshot is that you can run your belt through this loop, and leave the bottom connection unsnapped, so the case essentially hangs about two inches below your belt line. I find this to be much more comfortable carrying method than having it flush against my belt, where it would be crumpled against a jacket waistline, or creating a bulge at the belt line. Originally I had planned to order a carabiner in order to achieve this same result, now that will not be necessary. If you are looking to travel light, you will be well served by this case. It is an outstanding value. Note, the approximate dimensions of the camera I have are 4.2 x 2.4 x 1.4 inches.

UPDATE, 2/20/2013: The case has proven its worth already. A couple days ago my wife sitting in the car and carrying the camera on her lap, in its case. When we arrived at our destination, she got up to exit the vehicle, forgetting that the camera was on her lap. The case tumbled to the ground just outside the car. After dropping from a height of about two and a half feet or so onto concrete, there were no ill effects noted.

title: Has Something No Picture Can Show: A Genuine Book Feel
text:
I was a little bit worried when I ordered this, because it is on the expensive side for a Kindle Paperwhite case, and because it is so very different from the case I bought for my old Kindle. However, since I wanted a case with a zipper, this really was my only option.

But I needn't have worried: I am extremely happy with this puchase. My new (as of March 2021) Kindle Paperwhite fits perfectly into this case. And the included stand makes it easy to set it on the table in front of me when my hands are full or busy.

Furthermore, the feel of this case in my hands really does feel like a genuine, well-loved hardcover book. The cover feels amazing, with a soft texture (similar to suede) but sturdy boards. The spine uses a different, harder leather, as you'd expect from a real book. There's just a little bit of filigree decoration embossed into each outside corner, and the stitching is uniform and well-placed. It can be zipped up from either side.

On top of that, it actually smells like a real book! That's one of the biggest things I miss when using an eReader, so it's nice to have it again.

Overall, it's clear that the designers put a lot of thought into what makes a case pleasant but inconspicuous for the reader, and I would recommend it to anyone looking for a case for their Kindle. Worth. Every. Penny.

title: Mishears What I Say a Lot
text:
She mishears what I say about 25% of the time. This is versus the full-size Echo, which only mishears what I say about 5% of the time.

The sound is also very tinny, particularly compared to the full-size Echo.

If you can afford it, I definitely recommend the full-size Echo over the dot. Particularly if you want to use it to play music or control smart home devices. Having to tell your "smart home" to turn off the lights two or three times before it understands you can get annoying fast.

That said, it's still nice to be able to just add something to your shopping list while you're running around with full hands, or to turn your lights on from the doorway (even if you have to say it twice).

title: Simply Works
text:
I have four of these now. They work really well, and consistently. As long as they are plugged into a power outlet, the clock continues to run, and the thing plugged into it goes on/off at the times you set. When I'm away, I use them on my lights. When I'm home, I use them on kitchen appliances to ensure that they are off during times I don't use them. You can also just set them to 'on' when you're home, or store them for the next time you need them.

It's a little counter-intuitive the first time you set it up, but, once you get the hang of it, it's very easy.

Unlike digital timers, you don't have to worry about small power outages. The only problem I can foresee is if there is a long outage, then the clock will be wrong and it will be going on/off at different times. However, compared to not working at all at the slightest outage, I feel that this is a very minor drawback.

It does handle power blocks better than the long strips and I’ve got it nice and handy next to my computer.

title: Good sound not the most comfortable
text: These have good sound and good noise cancellation. They also look good but after wearing them a while they become uncomfortable. Not a problem for short periods of time, but if I’m on a trip or need to wear them longer, I’ll pick something else.

title: Never enough plugs
text: With so many electronics and pretty much everything requires some type of power, there are never enough plugs. I like that there is surge suppression so I don’t overload it but there are also usb connections which is very helpful. 2 to 6 is a good expansion and really fits my needs. So far it’s working great and has really been useful.

title: New Monitor needs new cables
text: I needed new cables for my new monitors for my desktop computer. My new monitors are 4K and my video card has display port connectors. This does the job. It's long enough to go from my tower which is hidden away to my new shiny beautiful monitors and it provides a great connection.

title: New monitors, new cables
text: I needed new cables for my new monitors for my desktop computer. My new monitors are 4K and my video card has display port connectors. This does the job. It's long enough to go from my tower which is hidden away to my new shiny beautiful monitors and it provides a great connection.

title: Good sound
text: Good sound, good noise cancellation, decent battery life and NO wires. These do a good job and are fairly comfortable. I think headphone do a more comfortable job of noise cancellation than ear buds especially around the house and these are doing a good job.

title: Replacement cables.
text: I'm pretty sure there's a rule that says when you need a cable there isn't one that works around but I ordered replacement cables to be sure it doesn't happen to me. These all work (and I've ordered replacement cables that don't so now I always check). It's nice to know that I have a cable where I need it, when I need it. I travel a lot and my cables get a workout--they go into and out of bags and cases and wound around in unusual shapes to get to a plug. These have held up.

title: What time is it really?
text: I love the easy visibility of this clock but the fact that it won't sync to EST makes it frustrating. I tried several times to get it to work but eventually gave up and selected another. YMMV

title: Provide excellent lighting
text: I originally got these when I started doing more zoom meetings. The way my computer is set up was giving a ton of shadows. These help immensely so I started using these for overall lighting. Now I like to have the light so I use them more often. They were easy to set up, work well and have a small footprint, while being adjustable so I can get the light where I need it.

title: Comprehensive set
text: Both blue and green sides and everything you need for a backdrop. A bit awkward to set up the first time but once I figured it out, it was easy to use. Does the job.

title: Extender
text: Never enough outlets for everything that needs to be plugged in. I hate having to crawl around or to move things around to get to the outlet. This alleviates the problem by allowing me to plug a lot of things in, even if I’m not actually using them now.

title: Just what I wanted
text: This is great for turning my existing desk into a standing version. It took me a while to get used to the standing version of working but now that I am, I find it way more efficient (and I’m a lot less likely to feel chair-bound). I was considering switching to a dual desk, but this works fine and I probably won’t change at least for a while.

title: Power and surge suppression
text: I think there’s a conspiracy to never have enough outlets to use where I need them. This solves some problems for me. It’s a great size, all the plugs are useable and it does surge suppression as well which is an added plus.

title: Never enough cables
text: My cables get a workout and never last long between traveling and them getting lost/misplaced/borrowed it seems that I’m always buying more. These all work and the longer length works for me. So far they are holding up and connect well.

title: Fits my Lenovo
text: Fits my Lenovo laptop. I’ve been using a sleeve which just isn’t quite big enough to haul all my “must-haves”, ear buds, power supply, etc when I’m traveling. I’m trying to keep it as downsized as possible and this does the job. Holds what I need without being so big that I feel like I’m hauling another suitcase. Seems durable but I’ll update after a few more trips if there is a problem.

title: The kids can use them
text: We've recently moved out to the country and the little ones are having a great time running around. That being said, I prefer knowing where they are and can't always see them. We now allow them to run around as long as they stay on the property AND carry one of these so we can find them if we want them. They also have to check in regularly and tell us when they are going somewhere else. They find "obeying" is fun since they get to talk on these and we like knowing where they are when we can't see them. These are simple enough for the little ones to use and have enough distance and battery life that so far there haven't been any trouble staying in touch.

title: Using it to keep the kids entertained
text: My niece didn't realize her new car didn't have a disc player until she tried to put in a cd with kids stories on it during a trip. This takes care of the problem. She hasn't had any skipping while driving, it keeps the kids entertained. Small footprint, good sound.

title: No more crawling under my desk
text: I love this. I attached it to my desk so I can plug and unplug things without having to run an extension cord from across the room (what I've been doing) or trying to crawl under my desk to get to a power strip. All the outlet's work and although I'm not using them all at the moment, it's nice to know there are more. Right now, if I need to plug something in, I can reach it easily, plug it in and remove it when it's time. It took a minute to install and then to move it a bit so it was easier to get to but now it's working great. Wish I'd had it a long time ago.

title: Is it me?
text: I'm not sure if it's me or not but I always seem to be replacing cables. The ones I use at home seem to last a while but when I travel the putting in and pulling out really wears them out quickly. Nice set, they all work and are already starting to replace those that have given up/given out.

title: So far, so good.
text: This produces a great picture and moves so it's always on top of what's happening. We had a bit of trouble hooking it up and had to turn off notifications because they were so annoying but otherwise, it seems to be working great. We have a baby due any minute so we haven't put it to a real test yet but so far it's working well.

title: Took a while for them to feel comfortable.
text: These took a while for me to feel comfortable and secure with them but once I did, I was sold. Sound is good and they are very easy to wear and feel like they'll stay in place, now that I'm used to them. I really appreciate how good the sound is. A little annoying to try and store but worth the effort.

title: Great for traveling.
text: This works well when I travel. It was easy to setup and it's easy to use. I wish it was lighter but am willing to put up with the weight for the results and the convenience of being able to print as I go.

title: Decent starter
text: I got this for the kids to get them into their science classes while we home school. It's a decent enough telescope for beginners and it's working for us but if you are looking for a series telescope this may not be enough for you. For now, it's great and I'm glad to have it. The kids enjoy using it.

title: Very comprehensive
text: Nice - it has a night light and enough outlets for all my plugs as well as USB (and even a C) ports. Pretty much covers everything I can think of and it works well by just plugging it in. Never enough plugs and this solves THAT problem. I'll get more for other outlets.

title: USB to Lightning
text: Cables really do have limited life span, especially when you are constantly moving them and plugging and unplugging them. These are a necessary replacement for some that have gotten too worn to stay hooked up. They all work fine and allowed me to dump some that are falling apart and replace them with nice looking cables that do what they are supposed to.

title: Nice add on.
text: Works great and is very accurate. I love having it (although it took me a while to remember to use it). Now I wouldn't be without it. Really adds to the versatility of my ipad.

title: Ouch?
text: While sound quality is decent, these are so very uncomfortable that I can't use them. I realize that everyone's experience is different but I also had trouble connecting them. Not worth it to me.

title: Great sound
text: Sound is good but most importantly, they are comfortable and stay in for a long time without irritating my ears. Easy to wear. Easy to charge and battery life is good. And they do sound good.

title: Can’t have too many cables.
text: I’m hard on cables so it seems I’m regularly in the market for new ones. I thought I’d try these since the connectors are turned but while they work just fine, I don’t notice them being any easier to use than the regularly shaped cables. These do work fine and for me the plus is that they are pink so it’s easier for me to pick the cable I want when I can spot them by colors. These all work and while I don’t notice much improvement or change using the angled connectors, it does make it easier when I am putting my iPhone on a charging pad to keep the cable from getting in the way.

title: Works with my Roku tv
text: I'm not sure what happened to my original Roku remote but it could have been kids playing with it. I was getting frustrated when this showed up and solved all my problems. It works just like the original Roku remove (I have a roku tv) and seamlessly took the place of the broken on. I haven't had any trouble. It does require batteries but that was easy. Removing the aggravation factor -- that was important.

title: Does a good job.
text: I'm gradually switching over to rechargeable batteries. This does A, AA, and AAA all sizes that I use. USA charger that plugs right into one of my newer power strips that has USB charging ports. Keeps it out of the way. Only downside is the size but when I got it I wasn't very committed to rechargeables but now that I am, I've relegated this to my travel bag so I have it handy if necessary while on the road, which was an excellent decision because as soon as I put it in my bag and got away, I needed to recharge. Ha! Good planning or good luck, you decide.

title: Doesn't wrinkle
text: We live in a green screen age but I've tried several that just don't hold up well. They wrinkle (which does show) or are too slippery or too stiff to maneuver. I do have to put this up when I need it and take it down again, when it's not in use but I just fold it up, shake it out and it goes right back into place. I clip it over the top of my moving white board and it's just perfect. It hides everything and allows me to put in a nice background.

title: Useful
text: I love that there are so many adjustment options. Now that my phone camera is better than a regular camera, I thought a light ring would be helpful and it is. There are a lot of adjustments to light color and brightness and the remote allows me to set the phone and light up and then adjust from the distance I’ll be using. It’s height adjustable but for table height (not floor). Just what I needed.

title: Never enough cables.
text: I’m very hard on my cables and since it seems that everything in my life needs to be charged these days, these are a great item. They are long enough to actually reach, the connectors are firm and the cable is very durable. I like that it has a color so I can spot the one I’m looking for. USB to C I got them to use with my iPad but find that there are more c devices today than there were even 6 months ago, so they are getting more use than expected. Also, now that there are USB ports on extension cords, I can plug these in to an extension because this cable is long enough that I can still maneuver my device while it’s charging.

title: Didn’t even know I needed this but I do.
text: I didn’t even know I needed this but it makes my echo dots portable which is fabulous! Just plug it in and take it with you. Battery life is decent and it works perfectly although the limitation of the dot continue — sound is good but not great but for a portable dot, that isn’t a deal breaker. Be sure and check that your dot fits. (I have several different sizes and shapes of dots but one size does not fit all for a battery base.

title: An answer to never enough ports.
text: I have a bunch of USB 3 ports on the back of my computer but that is pretty much of a pain so I thought I'd give this a try and it's working perfectly. I hooked it up to the back and now I don't have to use long cables to hook up all my USB 3 devices. Since I use a bunch of portable drives this is a big deal for me! Plug and play and it's all in easy reach.

title: USB to C and long enough!
text: I'm hard on my cables and everything seems to need them these days so I'm always in search of. These are great. They are long enough to actually reach without me having to stretch. The connectors stay in place (I'm using them for my ipad) and the cable feels sturdy without being hard to handle. I also like that it's not a regular white or black cable so I can spot it when I'm looking for a C.

title: Bigger than I need.
text: I like the look and feel of this. Very good quality but it was/is bigger than I really need which means it’s just extra space. That being said, I’ve made it work and it does hold a lot. Great for traveling and it still looks good after being slung around. It does hold my 15” laptop and my iPad but the bag gets heavy with both and all the cables, power supplies etc. They all fit though so if you need to get everything into one case, this might be your answer.

title: Pretty nice little player
text: Self contained and easy to set up and use. Sound is good, the whole thing can be packed up, moved around and carried to another location with easy setup. Footprint is small. Sound is pretty good for what it is but when it’s hooked up to speakers, it’s way better. Great for the price.

title: Moving Time!
text: It’s moving time for me and these came at just right time as we start taking apart all the cables and connections (who knew there were so many). I love that that we can even color code. We have computer cables, AV cables and more extension cords than I expected. Nice to have them all neatly banded together for sorting at the other end. These are easy to use and they stick together well.

title: I needed these!
text: I’m not sure what happens to cables in my house and I know they don’t last forever but it’s amazing to me how many times I have to go looking for a cable and can’t find the one I want. Thank goodness for this 3 pack. Now I have one at home (hidden) as a spare and one on my desk. Hopefully I won’t have to try and find a cable the next time I need one. These are sturdy and the connections work fine. I like the longer length so I’m not having to reach or stretch to grab the cable I want.

title: I needed a longer cable
text: I needed a longer cable for some reach and this works. I’ve hooked it up to my pc so I can use my tv as a monitor and once I eliminated all the technical glitches, it works great. The cable was never the problem but sending the signal was a bit of a pain. Still it works now, I have the length I need in this cable and I can do what I was trying to do.

title: Works for me!
text: I have a number of webcams and this one finally does the job. It has a cover so I feel better when it’s off and the ring light really makes a difference in helping with shadows. Camera quality is decent and it works without any hookup problems. Sound is just okay but I can live with that for now - I’ll probably end up supplementing with an additional microphone but this does the job and it’s all in one so I’m not trying to organize a bunch of different things. It works when I first plugged it in and hasn’t stopped.

title: Easy to use and it works.
text: I just plug this into my laptop when I need more connections and it works fine. I do use it more than I expected to and I love that it’s lightweight and small but mighty. I never seem to have enough ports for everything when I travel so this little gadget has come in handy. I haven’t use all the ports, there are couple that I just don’t need, but the ones I do, I use frequently and they all work just fine.

title: Does anyone have enough cords?
text: I’m convinced someone comes in at night and steals my cords. No matter how many I get, I can never find one. This set gives me an extra. I do know none of these cords hold up to hard use and they do need regular replacements but these have reinforced connectors and hopefully will last longer than the basic models. I also like that they are color coded - it helps to spot them and grab the right one when I’m fishing for a cable.

title: Plug it in and use it
text: This just works. Easy to plug in and extends my connectors. Doesn’t take up any room, works without installing drivers or anything and is really easy to just stuff into my laptop bag and have around. I find it use it more than I expected which is great. Glad it works so well.

title: Works great - way more options
text: I’m not actually sure I’d travel with this (they asked if it was good for travel) but I have been using it and love that there are enough options. It was a bit weird at first but once I figured out the best layout for my cords (so they didn’t tangle) it’s working great. Small footprint and the cord is long enough that I can position it where I need it to maximize my range. No trouble with anything other than the initial setup.

title: Non-techie but I got it working
text: I’m sure I’m not the idea customer for this — there were a lot of settings that I didn’t even attempt to deal with. From my POV - it hooked up pretty easy and worked. I get a good signal, the box doesn’t have a lot of weird antennas and it seems to cover most of my house without having to use range extenders. I did have some flukey connection issues in the beginning but it may have been my less than stellar ISP because it seems to have resolved without doing anything else. Occasionally I seem to get some hiccups but for now, I’ll attribute them to my provider as well, since I had them before.

title: These work but comfort is a problem
text: It’s taken me a while to get this to where they are comfortable for long term use. I’m not sure I love noise cancelling because I feel like I’m cut off from the world. However, these did pair quickly and easily and the sound is good. Once I got them adjusted to my ears, they stay in and are fairly comfortable. I know I’m not maximizing the benefits by using just one most of the time but it balances my need to be aware of what’s going on around me (and I still get to listen to my tunes or an audiobook - my newest addiction).

title: This is a love hate for me.
text: This is a love/hate thing for me. I love that it’s backlit, makes my IPad into a laptop and is easy to setup and use. I hate that it’s so big (yes, I know a trade off but it’s bigger than the standard keypad) and I hate that it has to be recharged. I switch between using it or putting my iPad back into the standard keyboard case that doesn’t need recharging. You may love and/or hate it but if you are aware of the good and the bad, you’ll be able to make a better choice. Overall I’m glad I have it and it’s been handy to have.

title: No assembly but there is a learning curve
text: I was having issues with online presentations. Trying to use a webcam had some issues - I’d be looking at the screen instead of the camera. I’ve never used a teleprompter before but thought it might solve the problem.  I didn’t expect it to require so much practice. At first I knew it would be hard but then I found that I was depending and focusing on the prompter and reading rather than ‘talking’ to the camera. I’ve got it down now and it’s proven to be a blessing. For me it works better if I bullet point my materials rather than trying to read the whole talk (again I found I was reading rather than talking) but with the bullet points I can talk about my material, not miss any points and can do it directly into the camera. Now that it’s working for me, I’m not sure how I managed anything else. It’s easy to set up and now it’s easy to use.

title: Works for me.
text: Who knew I could find something so small that actually works but we’ve come a long way from the days when we needed rooms to hold less power than this has. I like the size and shape of it but you do have to connect everything to it and while it’s okay, it’s also an extra pain - of course you have to do that with any type of desktop computer so it’s not that hard but it does have to be done. What is a problem as far as I can see is that you really have to have some experience to be able to set this up to really work well. If you’ve ever built a computer, this baby will be easy. If you haven’t, read through the comments. There were some very helpful tips that I was glad to take advantage of.

title: Works but not as useful as I thought
text: While the quality of this is awesome, I haven’t found it as useful to have a dual headed microphone (thanks covid) as I anticipated. I did use it a couple of times and it works wonderfully but until we are more together, don’t expect to get a lot of use out of it. Too bad - quality was good and it was easy to use. I have been using it as a single and it works fine for that but feels like overkills. Hopefully soon we’ll be able to be in the same room with someone else and it will be handy to have.

title: Nice kit
text: This is a nice starter kit or is suitable for someone who is an active but not professional user. It’s not always easy to setup but it’s not that hard once you figure out what’s happening. It comes complete with everything you need and it’s all in one compact package. Great deal for what you get. Does a good job with video, audio is just okay but workable. Just having everything in one is a step in the right direction.

title: Poolside
text: So far these haven’t taken a dip in the pool but we are using them poolside and waterproof was a safety feature. The sound is good, pairing is painless and the battery life is good. Does what we need/want and I’m happy. Now I can have tunes when we are sitting around the pool.

title: Extra for the car
text: Never enough hookups for charging. This really helps when we are on a trip - now there are two more plugs. This works well and I’ll probably get another for the other outlet in the car. I remember (fondly) the days when no one NEEDED to charge something. Now everything requires a port and this helps. Cables seem to work fine and color coding is good - saves arguing.

title: I needed this
text: I have a ton of things that need to be plugged in and/or charged in my bathroom and there just aren’t enough plugs. This is perfect for what I need. It not only has light so I don’t have to fumble around when it’s dark but there are enough outlets to keep everything plugged in, instead of having to swap things in and out. It’s a life saver. I haven’t traveled with it because it has a home in my bathroom.

title: Yes, I needed this!
text: So, I never thought of anything like this but boy has it come in handy. I travel a lot and over the last few years have managed to have duplicates of everything so I don’t have to pack/unpack every time. I didn’t have anything like this but did have all my electronics stuff in one place. This cleans up my act, allows me to actually find something when I’m looking for it and gives me a nice grab and go bag for all things that require plugs, etc.

title: It was time for some replacements
text: Cables never seem to last as long as I want them to and so it seems I’m always buying replacement cables. These work great, I love that they are colored so I can tell what I’m reaching for before getting to the end. I also like that they are all the same length. Sometimes 6 ft is a bit long but at least I never have those too short cables that I have to try and use. These work. No problems whatever.

title: Great for small product pictures.
text: This makes small product and jewelry pictures so much easier it’s not even funny. If you don’t have one of these and you take small product pictures, you are missing out. It’s easy to use and eliminates shadows and improper shading. Light is evenly balanced and pictures come out clear and crisp. I’ve used it with both my camera and even my iPhone and had excellent results with both. I wish I’d know about this years ago. Well worth the investment.

title: Handy to have
text: These are small which is both good and bad but I did buy some power adapters that have c slots and then realized most of the USB cables need to be replaced or adapted. These don’t take up any room, attach nice and firmly with no wiggling or slipping and allow me more options when charging things.

title: Versatile
text: While I originally got this thinking I’d use it for my iPad, I’ve ended up using it for my camera and my iPhone. I love that there is a range of heights available which I consider as one of the best features and that it holds everything (I have a couple of cameras) and my iPhone. In a pinch, I can use my iPad but I find I’m using it for everything else. Nice to have options both for devices and in height. Very sturdy and lightweight. Easy to set up and adjust. A winner!

title: Great if you have room to leave it set up.
text: This is very sturdy, although taking it down and putting it up is a bit of a hassle (I'm short) but once I managed to get it to a place where I could just leave it, I'm much happier with it. It is too heavy/large to easily move around but for one and done, it does a great job. Once it's set up, it does what it's supposed to do. It's easy to position a bit if necessary. It does fold down and can be stored but then putting it back up again takes a taller person than I am.

title: A little touchy.
text: This does work. It cuts the glare and has the blue light filter. I'm still not sure there is proof that the blue light is a problem but my eye doctor says it is and it's not that big a deal so I'll go along. That being said, the only real negative is that this seems a little less sensitive. It's not horrible but there are times that I can't use my fingertip and actually have to press. Doesn't seem to be a deal breaker, at least not yet so far the benefits outweigh the costs. We'll see if that continues.

title: NO more canned air!
text: I've always felt a little silly buying canned air but this saves me. I thought it was a bit pricy but when I compare to how often I go through the cans, it really does pay for itself. It's easy to use and dusts everything from my computer and my keyboard to my mini-blinds. Handy to have, easy to use and I don't mind replacing all those cans!

title: Went right on and works fine
text: Definitely good sound and went on without any trouble at all. The price is right and if it fails, it's easy enough to replace but the sound for this is excellent and the size is small enough that it doesn't impact use at all. I'm pretty happy with it, we'll see how it does long term but for now it's great.

title: Never enough!
text: It seems that there are always more devices than plugs...Maybe it's just me? but this has come in handy in splitting my hdmi devices. I could probably put some of them in the back of the TV but since this is so much more accessible, it's easier to just plug them into this box. It works well and I've been happy with it. Plug and play, nothing tricky and does the job. I also don't notice any decrease in quality which was a concern in the beginning.

title: Decent starter for home schoolers
text: We've got several being home schooled (unintentionally--covid) and this has come in handy for basic science studies. It's easy enough to use and small hands can maneuver it without any trouble. I thought it would be going on to the shelf for later but I'm glad we had it when we needed it.

title: Great addition
text: I wish I'd discovered this before. I've been using a makeshift box and while that works okay this far exceeds the performance and makes it easy to set up and take down as needed. Works well.

title: Nice add on
text: This was easy to add on and works well. It does much better than a direct light and it saves having to set up lights when I just need a quick or on-the-go video. Battery life is okay but not great, but it's not a deal breaker, especially at this price. It does save the settings when you turn it off (yay) and it's easy to adjust.

title: Help improve the sound
text: I've got an "extra" computer that is a bit older but still gets some work done. This has helps with the marginal sound quality I was getting. It plugged/played without any trouble which is exactly what I needed it to do. I'm not sure I would find it useful if I didn't have that one device but for now it's coming in handy.

title: Handy when you have power blocks
text: I haven't traveled with this so I can't say but it's come in handy at work where I have all sorts of weird and unpleasant power blocks for things. All the plugs can be used because there is enough room and there are usb ports as well. It also has a power switch for each outlet which might be useful for some but I just found that to be an extra step I didn't need.

title: Conveniently small and easy to carry and use
text: This is the best power strip I've found so far for traveling. I usually have to take my laptop and my ipad and my iphone and my..... you get the idea. This gives me enough plugs to be able to connect everything that needs an actual plug, and there are additional USB ports for those things that can be cabled right in. It folds up small and doesn't take up much room, is light and works like a champ.

title: Works well but is a hassle to deal with
text: This does a great job of picking up sound but it's a bit awkward in size and shape and isn't the "perfect" solution I was looking for. It is way better than the internal microphone and the noise cancelling is helpful too. It does the job and if it was less awkward to deal with it would be a winner. For now, I'm still in search of....

title: Works well but the cord is a pain
text: This does a great job picking up the sound but the cord is an annoyance when I want to move. It's great for sitting in a zoom meeting and does a much better job of the sound but when I'm doing a presentation it's less than optimal. I did have a tech tell me that a wired microphone really helps with the sound/video lag that can sometimes happen with a live event but I'm not sure it's worth the hassle. I'm still using it and will keep on doing so when I'm in a meeting but doing presentation is going to require some rethinking.

title: Beefs up the quality of the picture I am getting on my monitor
text: My monitor is newer than my computer and after changing the video card to support the improved monitor I noticed some improvement but when I upgraded to this cable, I was totally wow'd! Easy fix to improve the signal. It is NOT bidirectional but I didn't need that so this works.

title: Much needed
text: Has anyone else started receiving an endless supply of items that need a micro usb for charging but come with a 1 foot cable? My ports are far enough away that I was tired of putting all this stuff on the floor next to a charger so I could charge all the little items. This longer cable really meets my needs. It allows me to charge from my desk or on a counter without having to crawl down to get to that little cord. This is pretty durable and is holding up well considering I use it ALL THE TIME! I need more of these!

title: Needed to get info off some old ide drives
text: I needed to recover some very old information. This does work. I just plugged in my old drive and hooked it up to my new computer. I moved the files, no muss, no fuss. It's a bit awkward to maneuver but it's easy enough to use. Idiot-proof connectors and just plug what you want to access in. I won't use this very often, but when I want something, it's nice to be able to retrieve it. I did set all my jumpers to master so never had a problem.

title: Lots of options
text: As I continue to wrestle with the best way to handle close up video in my small space, this has helped a lot. It's a softer light than some of the others I've tried. It does have a good sized footprint and my space is at a premium but the light it produces is way more flattering for close ups than anything else I've tried. It's a bit of overkill for what I need but until I find something better, this is the winner in my lighting wars.

title: Nice durable cable
text: All my earbuds require a micro USB and all the cables that come with them are short. This is long enough to be useful and does the job. Pretty durable - I’ll be getting a few more because everything is coming with micro usb now and those annoying short little cables that aren’t easy to work with.

title: Into my travel bag
text: This is great for when I travel. It seems that there are never enough ports and this gives me just a couple of more so I can use a mouse and separate keyboard for my laptop. It also allows me to connect a second monitor which makes the laptop a real business machine.

title: Does a great job, makes all the difference
text: Until I actually used a light ring with my iphone I didn't realize just what a difference it made. This holds the phone steady, provides variable light source that comes from all around. The only down size (and I marked off a star for it) is the tripod feels flimsy and I ended up getting a better tripod for this light.

title: Got this for a laptop but using it on my desktop
text: I got this to use with my laptop when I travel but find I'm using it on my desktop for some additional connections. It plugs right in and worked right away (no tricky anything) and gives me the extra connections I need. (I'll probably snag it and take it with me when I travel too but for now it's being used full-time.)

title: Great add on
text: I have a standing desk on wheels that I use where-ever I might need it. I’ve got this attached and it’s the perfect add on to the desk. It gives me outlets and USB ports so I can keep everything on the desk without a lot of handing cords. There is just one cord - and it stays with the desk. I love having this and was glad I saw it because I hadn’t though to use if for what I’m using it for.

title: This is the answer!
text: If anyone else has a million kitchen appliances (they wouldn’t make it if I didn’t need it, right?) this is the answer. It replaces the measly two outlets they give you so I can keep everything plugged in (no I don’t use everything at once but it’s nice to have everything already plugged in). The USB ports were an added plus since I’ve recently seen several kitchen items (a candle lighter, my stand for my iPhone and other things) that actually require a usb hookup. I’m getting these for all my outlets!

title: Easily clips on but I’m still in search of
text: Since I’m not quite sure exactly what I really need, I’m still looking. This does a great job and there’s nothing wrong with it but for me, I think I’d prefer to have an all-in-one device. My webcam is good but trying to get everything exactly right is a pain and I’d just as soon have an all-in-one that just plugs in and works. If you are more capable than I am (and have more patience) the light works well has both a clip (which I didn’t like) and a tripod which I did.

title: Great replacement for the internal webcam on my laptop
text: I have a new laptop but the video quality just isn’t as good as this - I’m not sure if its the resolution (the specs say they are the same) or the ring light but this just does a better job all the way around. Clips right on takes a bit more room in my laptop bag but worth every bit of it!

title: Tons of Options
text: I needed a smaller ring light for my desk - all the zoom meetings these days, sigh — and this fills the bill. It’s not so big that I can’t manage to move it around when necessary and it stands just behind my desk so it’s not in the way but does the job. Remote works fine and is a necessary item because of where I have it placed but it solves the problem. More than enough options to make anyone happy (and it’s fun to play with when things aren’t speeding along).

title: Great set of lights
text: This is a great set of lights and better than I expected. The app was the hardest part of using them but once I got the hang of it, they are performing way better than I hoped. They are sturdy and heavy enough to stay where they are put. The light options are extensive and the results is awesome. If you are doing photography in a studio type of setting, this may be just what you need for effects but also for true light that you control.

title: Yup - needed these
text: I'm not sure what happens to the "right" cables when I need them but it's aggravating and these alleviate that problem. I need a container with with a bunch of these but these work perfectly and save me a ton of trouble.

title: These work but don't want to stay on
