text: I like having these but they are less wonderful and staying on. I've got one on my laptop and it works perfectly but I do travel a lot and my laptop gets a workout. I do find that from time to time they disappear. Good thing there was more than one in the package. YMMV, especially if your device is stable.

title: Works Flawlessly!
text: I needed a display port to C connection and this does the job. Easy to plug it right in and use my big monitor to display from my ipad or laptop. Flawless operation, works perfectly.

title: Easy to use and pretty effective
text: This was easily enough to install and use. I've had infrequent lags but it may not be the device, it may be my service at the end. Just plug it in and play from your phone or your laptop on the big screen. I like it and find it pretty useful. It's great when I travel so I can use my paid subscriptions on the big TV.

title: Needed to hook up my portable drive to my ipad
text: Works great - I just added it to the cable that came with my portable drive and plugged it into my ipad giving me tons more storage space. Just what I was looking for. Easy to use, has been working flawlessly.

title: Very disappointing
text: I’ve tried all of these in several plugs and none of them work. I’ve got an iPhone 12 and haven’t had any trouble with cables in the past (other than not being able to find them when I need them). I was hoping to solve that problem with this set. I love that they are color coded so I don’t have to look at each cable end, if I known I need the blue one for the phone charge, I just grab it. Would have been nice if they worked. I am traveling so will try them in a couple weeks at another location so maybe. In the meantime, I’m not hauling them around since they don’t want to work. I did try all of them.

title: Perfect for traveling
text: There are never enough outlets to recharge all my “stuff” when I travel. I’ve tried a variety of plugs, cords, etc. etc. to charge everything with the one measly plug that is usually available and without all kinds of plugs and connections. This has enough power adapters for the things that need to be plugged in and enough ports for the things that need USB power. I had it almost full and everything charged quickly and without any hiccups. Also the cord was long enough to give me some reach so I didn’t have to stretch around to get my devices all lined up against a wall - I could put them on a table. Winner for me!

title: Never enough plugs
text: Everything needs a plug and there aren't enough anywhere. This is a good quality power strip with surge protection so hopefully it'll catch it when I plug too many things into too few plugs. The cord is long enough that I can plug it in behind something and position the outlets where I need them. There are also usb charging ports which I didn't think I'd use because of the position of the strip but I plugged in some rechargeable power packs and a few other things that I don't need right away but want to keep charged.

title: Improves sound quality - I've only used it for meetings
text: No complicated setup which is a winner in my book. Since I've been spending what seems like hours a day on zoom, I thought this might help with the audio quality since I still haven't found a good camera that has great sound too. This was definitely easy to start using and when I see a recording of a meeting or something it absolutely improves the quality of the sound.

title: Not great for recording but fine for regular use
text: The quality of the camera is good unless you are trying to record. I talked to friends first to be sure they could see and hear me (sound is iffy but I expected that--I use a separate microphone when I'll be doing a lot of talking) and got positive results. Then I tried to record a meeting and the quality of the recording left a lot to be desired. If you are just visiting or even working without trying to record anything this camera is fine. If you are doing a lot of recording, the quality isn't there - keep looking.

title: Easier to use than I expected
text: Plugged and played perfectly. It was also easier to use than I expected (I was dreading all kinds of horrible problems with installation so this was a super-pleasant surprise). It definitely improves the quality of my voice. I've been using it in meetings so far but plan to use it for webinars in the near future. Works great but mostly easy!

title: Plugged and Played
text: The video camera I had on my computer suddenly stopped working in the middle of a zoom call. I grabbed this, plugged it in and it worked perfectly without any adjustments and picked up right where it left off. I was very pleased, audio and video quality seem good and I like the privacy cover which just flips up and down.

title: This is a pretty good wifi adapter
text: I have a couple of older computers that have network connections but don't deal as well as they should with wifi so I ordered a couple of these dongle's and this has proven to be one of the best. The signal seems more steady than some of the others I used and it was easily installed.

title: Very Useful
text: I've found that this is way more useful than I expected when I ordered it. It's not full size so it's easily transported. I've used it when I connect my laptop or ipad to the TV and it's easy to carry around and handle. I love the backlight. It took a bit to get used to the size of the keyboard (used to a full size board) but once I got used to it, I love it. Nice feel to the keys and sticks into my bag when traveling.

title: You know you need these
text: I’ve gotten tired over the years of trying to move cables around and these have solved my problem. I’ve tried many other types of labeling but the size of these is great and I can put one at each end of the cable which speeds up moving things around when necessary. I use them on my computers and on my audio/video equipment. Very nice! Obviously a pain in the rear to set up the first time but they’ll pay for themselves many times over in lack of aggravation.

title: Makes changing out hard drives easier
text: I attached this to my desktop computer in order to swap out drives for more space and higher speeds. I put the new drive into this dock and cloned my existing drive to it, then swapped out the disks. Worked perfectly. Still have several to go but this will make the whole process MUCH easier.

title: Nice power strip
text: I never seem to have enough outlets no matter how I try and crawling around on the floor to find an empty plug just doesn’t appeal to me. I put this onto the corner of my desk and everything feeds right off of it. I like that it has USB ports as well as electrical but most important to me is that I don’t have to crawl under the desk anymore.

title: Nice length
text: I needed a longer HDMI cable to connect my computer to my big screen tv. Spending so much time on the computer these days - it’s nice to be able to sit back and with my wireless keyboard and mouse, I can sit in a nice chair and get away from the desk (and I also don’t have any trouble seeing what’s being shown. Got it for the length, it works well and appears to be a very sturdy cable.

title: Never enough ports
text: I recently added a new camera to my computer with a USB hookup. I also have my wireless keyboard and mouse and an external drive connected, leaving me with no easily accessible usb ports. I've got one of these for my laptop (travel) because it only has 2 ports but was pondering how to handle getting more ports when it occurred to me that this will work just as well on a computer as it does a laptop. Plugged it in and instantly (or as fast as windows recognized it) 4 more ports (that I can easily reach).

title: Add speakers to my laptop
text: My laptop (new) just doesn't have decent speakers. Since it does everything else right, I added an external speaker which generally works with bluetooth but it seems a bit louder with the aux cable so I added that. This works just fine, doesn't take up a lot of room and gives my external speaker full range. Does what it's supposed to.

title: Never enough cables.
text: If I gathered all the cables I'v gotten over the years, it would probably be one of those things that cross the world several times. No matter, there is always a need for new/more cables and these are good ones. They are c to c and now that I have power supplied with c connectors and so many devices that use the c connector, they've come in handy and I'm getting a lot of use out of them. They seem durable and the one I have connected to my ipad is getting a superworkout and it still holding strong. I think these are winners!

title: Great Camera, I'm using it to replace an older webcam
text: I'm in a cramped space and can't easily move around or add extra "stuff" to my computer area. This fits in just fine, does a way better picture than my original webcam and I like the various lighting options. I wish there was a camera cover for my own peace of mind but it's easy enough to turn to the wall. I've been told I sound just fine and I can see a truer picture of myself than I did with my old cam so it's easier to set up and align. Works great. Was easy to set up and easy to use.

title: And in Colors
text: I never have enough cables - I'm always looking for one or another. These work great USB A to C and I LOVE that they come in colors which makes them easier to spot. I've used them all while traveling and haven't had any trouble. They are short - but I use them to travel with so no extra cords all over the place.

title: My first ring light stand
text: This was easy to put together and it does work but I’ve traded up to a larger one. I got the new iPhone 12 Pro Max which is HUGE and I felt like I was getting shadows. If you have a smaller phone, this should work fine and I’ll be handing this off to a family member that can use it. Light is good, easy to use, does the job.

title: Decent quality and easy to install
text: Now that our whole lives are conducted on-line, I found that I needed to add webcams all over the place. Our laptops and iPads are already video ready but we’ve got desktops throughout the family that all needed upgrading. This was easy to install, plug and play and the quality is fine for what I need.

title: Thanks Covid for forcing me to put web cams on everything
text: With the advent of Covid, everything has gone on-line so I added the webcam to one of my desktop computers. I still prefer to do most things on my laptop or iPad but with everything on-line it’s a must. This works fine, it was plug and play and the quality is adequate for my needs.

title: C to C - fast charge
text: I really find that this is the one of the better cables for fast charging. I like that it’s braided so I can spot the color and also it feels more durable. I also carry a couple of adapters and this will pretty much charge anything/everything. Maybe one day I’ll get all organized and make my c cables one color, usb another, etc. but that hasn’t happened so I’m still using the search method but the colors do help spot them.

title: I got several sets of these - I LOVE them
text: I’ve got these scattered all over my life. They are easy to use and extremely handy to have. Since I travel a lot, I’ve got a set just for “on the road” and they really clean up my carry on bag that requires every kind of cable I might need for the rest of my life. I like these better than the ones that come with the cords — they are easier to handle and way easier to spot.

title: Must have accessory
text: Didn’t even know how much I needed these until they arrived. I’ve got them all over the place and they come in extremely handy for cord management (especially when traveling). They are easy to use (and reuse) and do the job. I’d get the variety pack because sometimes you just need a longer or shorter one but this is a great grouping. (I recommend you buy 2).

title: I’m a believer
text: I was skeptical of this and overwhelmed when I got my new iPad — it was SOOOO big and that in and of itself was an adjustment. I added this and was pleasantly surprised that it didn’t ruin my view, did improve my use of a stylus and actually does help cut down on the glare. It’s not noticeable but the effect is there - my iPad looks like new and it has been used. A great bargain. I did find it greatly improved my pinpoint accuracy when using the stylus which wasn’t my “normal” mode of working.

title: it works but didn’t wow me
text: While this does work if you plan carefully it’s not as easy as slap a sensor on and find your stuff. The remote is a bit annoying (what happens if I can’t find the remote) and there are easier systems to do this. This works best on larger items but i usually lose the small things. YMMV.

title: Once I got them in right...
text: These are pretty noise cancelling which I'm not sure I'm totally in love with. It took me several tries to get these babies into position and comfortable enough that I could actually work out with them. The sound is good. I'm not convinced I can work out without some feel for what's around me. It's my personal problem - buds work well, feel good and stay in.

title: Needed accessory
text: I've got device - old, new, different brands, etc. I've got a couple of these everywhere and I use them all the time. It's a simple adapter. Doesn't do anything except switch the plug - Just what I need it for.

title: No more lost keys
text: Just like your key fob for the car. This works just fine my only real problem with it is having to hang onto the remote. Not sure how to do a work around but sure would be nice if I could just ask Alexa where my keys are and be told (or hear a beep). I like this and it works but there are better ways to keep track of things.

title: Can't find your???
text: Easy to use - just put them on and sync them up and you won't lose anything again. I LOVE these - but I probably need way more if I'm going to keep track of all my things.

title: Finally a steady connection
text: This has been used to replace the cable company's Internet Cable. The one they have is frequently losing it's signal, not sure if it's a hiccup or a faulty cable but since I put this onto the modem, our service has improved (a lot). Good tight connectors and feels like it's going to last forever. In any event is way more sturdy than the cheap cable they gave us when they did the install.

title: Ok on comfort sound is good
text: This took me several attempts to sync up but once I got them working, they sound good and cancel noise perfectly. After wearing them for several hours, they became uncomfortable. I’m going to have to do some adjusting to get them to stay in comfortably but once I manage that, these are keepers - small size, good battery life and good sound.

title: Makes using my laptop MUCH Easier
text: My laptop sits FLAT and this adds an extra angle that allows me to work much longer using the laptop without carpal tunnel issues creeping up. Definitely improves my productivity.

title: Awesome help for laptop
text: I’ve got my laptop on this and its proven to be a real wonder. It give me enough lift and angle (which is adjustable) to stand at my desk and work. I needed one of these years ago, but I’m happy to have it now.

title: Still more cables.
text: It doesn't seem to matter how many cables you have, you always need more or different or longer or shorter or whatever. I got these because a lot of devices are coming with micro USB connections and they come with this dinky little short cord. I love these because they work and I Love that these come in colors so I know the blue is micro USB. I have grey for lightning to C and red for lightning to USB. I can grab the cable I want when I need it without having to drag them all out and look at the ends. Give me color coded any time. The three feet is long enough for me -- I"m able to plug one end into my power supply for charging and put the device out of the way instead of piling everything around the power supply.

title: Works well
text: This works well for expanding the very few available ports on my laptop to handle what I really need. I got this one because it handles all the cards but haven't really used it for that yet (I see it in my near future). What I really LOVE is the length of the cord -- I can push the attachments out of the way still use it as a "laptop".

title: Must have!
text: I’ve added this to the newest iPad. It pretty much allows me to use it as a laptop instead of limiting me to a tablet.  In fact, with this hub, my ipad is almost better than my laptop. It’s certainly smaller and lighter so for short trips, as long as I have this hub to allow me to add things on, I can make it work. It plugs in and works! I haven’t ever had any trouble with it, other than sometimes it’s in the way if I’m trying to carry the table around and forget to remove it.

title: A must have
text: There are NEVER enough ports for tablets, laptops or anything you travel with so this (or another model) is practically a must have. I like this one because I know it works. I’m not messing with micro SD cards or anything like that (I have another hub that deals with those) but this is perfect for traveling and fits into my laptop bag without a blip. Always works and allows me to turn my laptop into a working computer.

title: Handy to have
text: I have a ton of electronics and it's always a hassle to find the right plugs, connectors or power supplies. This is a handy little thing to have that works, and converts type c cables to usb so you can plug into any power supply. If you don't have a couple of these around, you are missing out. Just plug it in and it works.

title: Lightweight, fits and easy to carry and use.
text: Works perfectly for my 14 inch laptop (lenovo) and has a bit of extra room. It's lightweight, has enough pockets to store the things I need and keeps the laptop from banging around. I have put my laptop in it and then put the whole case and all accessories into my carry-on roller bag and it works fine. I don't have any trouble (unless they are gate checking carry-ons and then I just grab the case and carry just that. Works great.

title: Love this mouse.
text: This is smaller than my desktop mouse and I wasn't using it for a while because I'd tossed it into my laptop bag. After a recent trip I realized I actually love this mouse. The smaller form means it doesn't take up a ton of room in my bag but still functions just fine. It paired easily and works perfectly. I did have a bit of trouble in the beginning because I'm used to a taller (higher) mouse but it didn't take long and it's way better than the touch pad....

title: Winner!
text: Plugged it in to the usb port. Snapped it on to the top of the monitor and we have video. The technical part of getting the video working (software and users) was harder than getting this working. Delivers a nice picture and sound and was an easy add-on to an older computer now that everyone is zooming.

title: Way more options
text: I've always just used monitors that sit on the desk but after using these, I'm a convert. Both monitors can be moved or adjusted as needed and the extra desk space is fabulous. I didn't know what I was missing but now, I'm converting all the computers to these. Fabulous. If in doubt, give them a try, you'll never go back. I've got them support 32 inch 4K monitors and it's wonderful!

title: Handy addition
text: As my laptops get smaller I find that they have less "stuff" on them. I attached this to my window laptop and it worked just fine. I've also used it on my desktop computer for an additional drive and it too worked fine. If this is what you need, this is a good sturdy piece of equipment that works very easily. Just plug and play (no additional workarounds needed).

title: Add on for when it's necessary
text: I don't do a ton with numbers but occasionally something comes along and I "need" a number pad. My regular keyboards all have them but my laptop doesn't (I was trying to size down as much as possible). This is a great add-on. When I need it, I grab it out of the computer bag, plug it in and go to town. It's works fine every time and has proven very useful on a number of occasions.

title: Must for travelers
text: I've tried several of these and I love the concept but this one has proven to be more useful (more ports) for everything I need when I travel. It's nice to just pull out my lap top and be ready to go without having to hunt down hubs, or power strips or anything else. Everything is in one place and it's easy to plug and play and unplug and run.

title: Never enough
text: Thank goodness. I really needed this. There are never enough places to plug in everything that needs to be plugged in and this is fabulously useful. It's small enough to toss into my computer case without making it impossible to carry and it's small enough to be unobtrusive (and out of the way) when I'm using my laptop. If you travel and have more than one or two devices, this is the answer --

title: C to Lightning - hook up your iphone to your c adapater
text: So I purchased all these C adapters and realized I couldn't charge my iPhone unless I also have a Qi option. This is my solution. It plugs right into the C adapters and I can connect my phone without using additional chargers. Nice to have especially when traveling. It works perfectly and does fast charge.

title: Compact and easy to travel with
text: Very handy to have and works well with both of my laptops (both Lenovo's but different models). It plugged right in and started working without any trouble. I did have software for reading, writing and playing dvds on my computers so it worked right away but you'll have to install software to get it to work. So far it's played everything I've thrown at it. It's compact and easy to travel with. All in all a great drive.

title: Great deal - nice to have
text: These have all worked just fine and I like the longer length, especially when I'm traveling because my charger sometimes has to be rather farther away than I would like. They feel sturdy and are very useful. Seem durable and I haven't had any trouble with them and they've been twisted and turned and squeezed into my case and so on - still no trouble.

title: USB to C cable
text: So many of my newer devices (iphone, ipad and even my windows laptop) all have c ports now. All those "other" cables aren't working so I selected this one and it works just fine. My main gripe is that it's only usb-2 instead of 3 so charging isn't that speedy but it does work. I haven't had any trouble with it and will just use it at my desk so I have time and I'm not in a rush to get anything charged. For faster charging, I'll have to find another option.

title: Plugged it in and it worked.
text: I've got a windows 10 machine and just plugged and played. It was recognized instantly and I ran the usb 3 connector to 3 switch boxes and finally have enough 3 hookups for everything. I've got at least 3 or 4 devices connected right now and I don't notice any service degradation. 5 Stars.

title: C to Lightning work flawlessly.
text: I probably own more cables than many third world nations but they disappear or get lost or even stop working. These are great cables, they work just fine and they do fast charge my ipad and my iphone. They also allow me to connect my iphone to my windows pc and use the phone networking when I'm in the middle of nowhere. So far, they are flawless.

title: All in one for every connection
text: I've used this for a variety of connections - my ipad to my computer monitor, to my tv and from my laptop to the same things. Very versatile and has worked just fine with my Apple device as well as my Windows devices. Very handy. Was recognized right away and I haven't had any trouble at all. I carry it everywhere now.

title: Easy to use and fast to install.
text: Plugged it in and it worked perfectly with my win10 laptop. It was recognized right away and I was using the sd card within 2 minutes. Two thumbs up. Sometimes, these devices don't connect right away, but this one worked fine in my C port.

title: YES! Everything in one place and it's easy to use
text: This is the answer to what you've been looking for. It works with my new ipad and with my laptop to expand their capabilities. I think every connector is there but it turns your tablet into a work ready solution. It was easy to hook up (idiot-proof) and I haven't had a problem since I started using it.

title: Works just fine.
text: In my continuing search for enough chargers to keep everything running, this works just fine. It does fast charge my stuff which is a good thing and the prongs fold in so they don't get mangled when I travel.

title: Works with the 12.9 iPad with keyboard
text: I got the 12.9 inch iPad and I couldn't find a sleeve that was durable, lightweight and the right size. My iPad does fit in this with room to spare. It's decent looking and there is enough padding that I feel safe tossing it into my carryon with worrying the whole time. There are just enough pockets for a few items and maybe about 1-2 inches between my iPad (with keyboard) and the top end. Zips closed. Winner!

title: Long enough cables (finally)
text: This is 3 LONG lightning cable with a 90 bend in the adapter. This does make them easier to use while doing something and the length is the biggest selling point. Not totally crazy about the light (although it's nice to know it's working I guess) but I was sold on the length and the shape.

title: Decide where it works before trying to put it on
text: It took a big of maneuvering to get this in place where it would do what I need but not be in the way. In the end the side was better than the front or back. Slid right onto my desk and put all my plugs at the tips of my fingers - FINALLY I don't have to crawl around when I need to add something new (which seems to be all the time) and it works just fine. I haven't had any trouble at all with it and I've been putting it through it's paces. Stays in place which I was afraid it wouldn't and keeps me running

title: Easy to use - brighter colors, sharper picture
text: Whoa. I recently realized that some of my hdmi cables were very old (as in original) and decided to see if it was really worth while to upgrade. If you are wondering, YES! Makes a ton of difference. I noticed going from a regular HD to UHD was a big improvement and when I upgraded my dvd player, that made an improvement but I may be seeing things, I think that this new cable made even more difference. At last I'm seeing clear, bright, colors. Love it! Only bad thing, now that I know the difference, I'm going to have to upgrade all the remaining cables. Oh well!

title: Check your settings for the motion detection
text: We didn't use this for a baby, we had a very ill person staying with us for a couple of weeks and we used it to keep track of him. He was supposed to stay in bed but didn't want to so we set this up so we didn't have to go running every time we heard a sound (now we only ran when he was trying to get up). It made some long nights way more bearable. We hooked it up and set it up without the instructions and at first every little movement was pinging us.  Not quite when he was breathing but we got every twitch. We finally adjusted the setting so that normal movements were okay but "big" movements we were pinged. Once we got  that figured out it worked perfectly. Better than a standard baby monitor because we could hear but we could also see what was happening. Great night vision (it was dark but we could still see) and we had no trouble hooking it up to our wifi. The app went right onto our phones and we were notified when there were changes. If you are using this for a baby, you'll find that it works well and is very easy to use. Highly recommended.

title: Improved picture, easy install
text: This has good points and bad points. The main negative is that you can really see what's on the TV. I never used to notice when makeup was blotchy or cakey because you couldn't see it. Now every flaw shows up. The picture is amazing when you have 4K all the way but like I said, some of the older shows really look icky now. That being said, there's nothing better than a great picture and I love that this DVD player works for everything (so far).  It was an easy install, took about 5 minutes to swap out with my previous player and I was up and running without so much as a hiccup. Great picture - I'm off to watch TV!

title: Small, portable, works!
text: We all know that there are NEVER enough places to plug things in. There is always new gear or things that you can't live without. I got a new laptop recently and it was fine at first until I started trying to attach extra drives and a keyboard and mouse and monitor and so forth. This little baby is small, easy to use, works great and is portable. I'll be looking for something else to use at my desk when I want  to attach all that stuff, but it does fit in my laptop case and allows me to actually use more than one device at a time.

title: Simple, easy to use and works well
text: I received several of these and was very happy with them. Then they started disappearing after people saw them. They just click open and work as a stand for pretty much any device we have (mostly apple products). They are strictly low tech and just work. They fold down for easy carry and allow you to place your phone upright or on the side where you can charge it. Great for watching videos or anything of that type without having to hold onto your phone. If you get them, hide a spare for yourself--they are very handy to have.

title: Two pack at a good price - they worked the first time
text: I'm not actually sure how you can mess up a printer cable. They've been around a long time and should be perfect every time. That being said, these are a great length, the price is right and it's a two pack. The braided cable feels very durable and unlikely to tangle. I've plugged both in and they both work right out of the box. The connectors feel sturdy--these should last a long time.

title: Good sound, comfortable to wear.
text: Decent sound and fairly comfortable but I found them to be just a bit heavy and it didn’t feel like the earbuds would stay in with a lot of activity. That said, they are very comfortable, don’t wiggle around and don’t just fall out.  I thought the case was a bit oversized and the whole package was bigger than I like for wireless but as long as I’m not moving around a lot, they stay in, are very wearable and the sound is decent. I’ve got another pair that I wear frequently and compared to those these feel a bit “top heavy” so it may not be a problem for someone else.  I do want to comment that they come encased in a foam holder and it was VERY difficult to get the earbuds out of the foam.

title: Standard earbuds — wired
text: You’ll need to plug these into your phone with the audio jack. This is NOT a lightning connector  and it is NOT wireless but if you can still use earbuds that plug in these fit fine and the sound is decent. I don’t think they are stable enough for a lot of moving around but if you are more or less stable, these will do the trick. Earbuds have enough options and I found them to be very comfortable.

title: These might work for you but they didn’t for me
text:
Well they sound ok and it was easy enough to pair them but I had some real problems with these headphones that may or may not be of concern to you. My biggest gripe is the darn things are so uncomfortable and the ear pieces are awkward to get around my ears. I’ve used headphones with ear clips before and never had this much trouble. They just don’t fit me. The buds themselves also needed to be tweeked. I’ve been wearing a variety of ear buds for years but these feel too bulky outside so the don’t want to stay inside. The whole thing is uncorfotable. I was interested in these specifically since they claim to be waterproof but they won’t stay in well enough for me to really test them.

Since I was reviewing, I did want to put them through some action. While not nearly stable enough to run with, I thought they would work just listening to music or an audiobook. I got them paired with my iPhone and set up. The sound is decent (might be better if the earbuds fit better) but the control switch was another problem. Standard switch, but if I hadn’t been sitting down working at it, managing the controls was horrible. The three buttons are difficult to differentiate from each other and there aren’t any raised surfaces to feel around for what you want. Almost impossible without looking, I can’t imagine trying to adjust them while moving.

These just don’t do it for me, of course YMMV but they lack comfort, feel insecure and are difficult to operate. I never got as far as seeing how they held up while working out so can’t comment on whether they are waterproof or not.

title: Great sleek, slim keyboard
text: I have computers both at home and at work, and they all have the same keyboards. Once I get used to a keyboard, I never want to change because each board has its own idiosyncrasies and sometimes those include putting the keys at a slightly different angle or a slightly different spacing between keys. I've been using Logitech keyboards for a while, and have been happy but when this one showed up, I wondered how I was going to change. This keyboard is sleek and slim and wireless (which I have been using for a while) but this one isn't nearly as bulky as the former ones. There is a nice back light when necessary and it shuts itself off when not in use. I've been using it for a couple of weeks now and i LOVE It! I just packed away my old keyboard (in case I change my mind) but I think I'm going to be happy with this one. The keys are all in the "right" spaces and there is an additional number pad (which I find very useful). All in all - it's lightweight, wireless, easy to use and pretty much perfect so far.

title: It’s a little strange
text: I really wasn’t sure about this at first—it’s just the wrong shape and it was weird trying to use it. After a couple of days though, I’m really pleased with it. Once you adjust your frame of reference, you are using the exact same movements and you press the same buttons as you’ve always done, you just don’t have to turn your wrist. I can see a reduction in wrist pain and irritation with continued use. It did take about 2 days to get the hang of it, and I confess that occasionally I revert to trying to grab it the same way I’ve always grabbed a mouse, but once I’m working I hardly know the difference until I notice my wrist doesn’t ache and my hand doesn’t get numb.

title: VHS to DVD but it does take some work.
text: Okay this DOES work but it's not easy. It took me a while to find/hookup my old VHS player and then to figure out how to actually copy it to dvd. There is minor editing available but nothing fancy and I still haven't found out how to add menus or closed captioning. I plan to spend some time this winter working on it because I have BOXES of VHS tapes that I would like to keep. For now, it's adequate just remember you don't get any quality boost so if the original is grainy, the copy will be too. It does seem to be comparable - quality wise but I haven't tried anything complicated yet. Will update when/if I get it working. I am using Win7 and it does work. I don't know about any other systems.

title: Study Power Strip can go where you actually need it
text: Great idea. This power strip actually tightens right onto the desk so the plugs are in a convenient location. It's a bit heavy but it is heavy duty so you can plug anything you need into it. It also come with 3 USB ports and a long enough cord to actually put it on your desk and still plug it in. Works great, easy to hook up and it screws down tight so I don't expect it to fall/fly off. It's a bit on the bulky/heavy side, but the build is good enough that it all works just fine.

title: Fast Charging for 3.0 type device.
text: Finally fast charging for everything. This does NOT come with a cable so you'll need one to use it but I haven't found anything that usb charges that doesn't work. With 30W, you get fast charging if your device has that ability and the little blue light (very non-offensive) tells you that it's working. It is a 3.0 socket but everything I've purchased lately is 3.0 and I have a couple of adapters for the "older" devices that aren't 3.0. I LOVE that the prongs fold down so it's easy to carry and use without the plug catching on everything. Very handy to have and mine came in an amazon frustration-free package so I opened the box and used it.

title: Fast and Easy to use - a bit bulky
text: 4.5 rounded up to 5. Works great - and it's fast but it's a little bulky (as in short and stubby) and I'm afraid it might not connect as well in the future. However, for now it's fast, it's easy and it works great.

title: Great case if you’re traveling with a 17 inch laptop
text: Great case with lots of storage and capacity to hold my 17 inch laptop. This size case is usually cramped and poorly organized but this case solves all those problems. Plenty of pockets to separate your things and it’s TSA friendly so you don’t have to drag it out at the airport. Case feels balanced and laptop feels secure and safely stored. Looks great and is easy to carry. I can see where it might carry too much stuff and would be heavy, but if you’re carful, it’s a go everywhere case. (I voluntarily reviewed a free sample).

title: So Handy and Reliable!
text: I have half a dozen of these to accommodate all my electronics. (I admit to being an electronics junkie) but its so much easier to plug everything in and just one or two plugs to the router. I do stack them in groups of two or three giving me lots of inputs. I highly recommend color coding your cables to make it easier to trace a problem but these have proven to be super-reliable. I've had several for at least 5 or 6 years and never had a problem. Now I can plug EVERYTHING in! YAY! I have them at work, at home and at the vacation house. Have also made all my friends and relatives invest in them too (we're all happy)!

title: Not that great
text: My tiny phone speaker was louder.

title: Great for special needs
text: This product has been an excellent tool for my son who has muscular dystrophy and can’t reach a keyboard on a computer.

title: Good overall but not fantastic
text: Good product but at highway speeds it is difficult to hear. Possible issue with install but every now and then I can hear static. Overall great unit and very user friendly. Great battery life. Just needs to be a little louder.

title: Disappointing. Do Not Buy !!!
text: Not sturdy and did not prop up well. Cover slid all over the place and made it difficult to access the buttons.

title: Sturdy, inexpensive case for my new iPad Mini 2 (with retina display).
text:
Good cover, sturdy without being hard. MUCH better and a lot cheaper than the covers I found in stores like Best Buy, Radio Shack etc. The case protects my new iPad mini 2 (retina display) very nicely and the magnetic enclosure helps it snap shut. The cover is soft and supple, yet easy to grip when using the the ipad mini as a reader.

A few options that would have been a nice to have (but that don't bother me much) are
1) Ability to rotate the iPad to view both in portrait as well as landscape mode
2) The strap on the cover! A good idea, but instead of the strap being towards the edge of the cover, it should have been placed more towards the spine as it would be a lot easier to put one's the fingers through to grip the book.

I searched several stores in the neighborhood and found the cases over priced and ugly plastic looking. This case in Amazon is certainly a deal in both the price and looks department.

On the whole, extremely satisfied with my purchase.

title: Better than expected. Better than other, lighter competitors...
text: Assembly requires lining up threaded holes in the interior pipe with unthreaded holes in larger outer pipe and using the hex wrench to screw the pipes together. Typical but a bit fiddly for me 'ol hands. Also black-on-black hard to see. Better would be a slot in the outer pipe and ready-set bolts sticking out from the inner which slide into the slot and are tightened with a strong wingnut. No fiddly tool needed. Same for the upper connection which is slightly but not fatally out of align likely due to the crimping of the inner pipe which inevitable shortens it by a 1/16th inch or so. As the threaded holes were likely set in prior to crimping, this moves them down a tad versus the outer pipe holes which were punched with a certain alignment that is not there after crimping. Net: slight misalignment not fatal but do not expect the holes to be properly centered. Just push real hard on the top pipe to encourage alignment as best you can. Back speaker support bracket adjusts horizontally and vertically. High enough for my Polks and design permits wires from wire posts to pass through unobstructed. This is a very clever, unique, successful design. So we now have 2 very strong and satisfactory speaker posts. Well worth the money. Might spray white Rustoleum on them to blend with the wall and replace speaker fabric with white available right here on AMZN. Then we would have something truly superb. Net: these posts are very good. Buy them, say we.

title: Superb sound at a reasonable price. Polk has ruled, is ruling and, we may hope, shall rule.
text: Been buying Polk for decades. Never disappointed. Stay with what you know. Why go elsewhere? At this price point anyhow. Sounded good when I was younger and had better high-range hearing. Still sounds great 20 years on. Its the clarity, donch'a know. Running off my old legacy spare Sony STR-695 plus Sony legacy 5-CD carousel changer set up in the bedroom as an auxiliary music source.  Tried others. tried Bluetooth connection. Rejected. Just use wires and figure out a wire route. Under the rug at these low voltages is not gonna kill you. Or get a wire run. Or get an electrician to pull thought the walls. These Polks deserve a proper input. BTW: Classical (meaning Beethoven and the like - NOT movie music) is what I typically play and the Polks do well with this material. Might add a subwoffer if I go crazy but not really needed for classical - I think. We shall see...

title: Light weight barely adequate for Polk bookshelf speakers.
text: First step per instructions is to detach 10 felt pads, one at a time, from the paper backing and place them on the 10 legs (5 each) on the bottom of the 2 heavy metal base pieces. What a pain as these fiddly little felt pads don't detach easily from the backing. And are so small they are hard to position on the legs just right. Black on black. Hard to see. And why 5 when 3 bigger ones would do it? I have bought desktop computers and other items with the rubber feet already installed. Why not these? What would it cost the manufacturer? Peanuts. Aluminum pipes screw together fine but when the speakers are installed, with the base oriented as per instructions, whole thing pitches forward. Solution: orient the bases in the opposite direction and the balance is better. Better not perfect. To get a straight up balanced posture, the bases will have to be shimmed in front. Not the end of the world but still. Tip: during assembly, ignore instructions and attach speakers to the upper pipe alone and then insert the upper pipe into the lower pipe and tighten down the friction-fit as needed. Much easier than wrangling the whole assembly with heavy base attached. And I wonder if this system will hold the speakers solidly to permit the full bass sound to be projected. Won't these flimsy pipes allow the speaker to vibrate and so loose sound energy projection? Much better would be mounting the Polks on the wall (for resonance) but this was not an option.

title: Sounded worse than the Samsung big screen TV speakers. Maybe because no connection worked but
text:
audio out. HDMI is an old standard but no joy here. Bluetooth? Worked from my Dell laptop but not from the TV. So maybe the problem is our 4-year-old TV? Kinda doubt it. Impossible for me to repack for return shipping (and I'm pretty conscientious about such things) but as I kept all packing materials, including extras and the crazy l-shaped store box, the good people at the UPS store packed it up in a trice. I watched them. It is a 2 person job and they had 2 people. So back it goes and I say "Thank you Amazon for your return policy."
In the past Yamaha was a great brand but a soundbar is essentially an impossible idea: too small. No better than good TV speakers, so why bother?

title: Actually, it worked! Legacy Sony radio-amp no Bluetooth, but superb...
text: with a Sony 5 CD carousel - so I can listen to my huge CD collection. (Yes, later, will burn to disk but for now...), Just plugged it into the headphone out, with an extension to get to where the USB power hub was  (needs power, thought I) and this little gem paired to Bluetooth Headphones and now I have wireless headphones that the then SONY did not have. Next step is to buy shelf speakers because if the cans sound, so will the boxes. We are very pleased. Simple, cheap, effective - what more is there to say, I ask you?

title: Sound quality? Amazon wants me to rate sound quality? These do not have
text:
anything to do with the sound. That comes from the speakers...

But these did restore my old mPow cans to service. I was tired of the little black flecks from the old rotted out earpads getting all over the place. (Hey! Why does Amazon spellcheck red squiggly underline "earpads" here when the title says, well, earpads? I ask you..)

Fiddly to install but worth it to ban the annoying little black flecks...

Hey! Spellcheck does not like Bezos! Bozo is OK but not Bezos. Yikes, IT folks, this best not get to his level.

title: Sometimes you need strain relief. This is such..
text: Right angle turn is helpful when you need, well, a right angle turn. Rather than sticking straight out, if you know what I mean...

title: If you push the male end into your legacy HiFi headphone outlet and plug...
text:
the little tiny headphone plug into the other end, you'll most likely get sound.

What more is there to say?

title: SIngle wire that came with my SONY STR DE695 box worked better. This antenna clips.
text: Clipping (AKA crackle) can be heard in loud passages from local FM classical station. It is as if the signal strength is made too strong - but how could that be? Whereas the simple single wire antenna (which just turned up after our latest move) provided with the Sony box works fine. Could it be that the Bingfu antenna overdrives the 75 OHM FM antenna input?  But how could that be? Or perhaps the antenna itself has a weak internal connection that fails to carry the most strong signal? FM is Frequency Modulation, not Amplitude Modulation so the amplitude stays the same, right? So why clipping? OK. You get the idea. This Bingfu goes into the junk box for reuse as... what.

title: Bought in August 2022, failed in November, 2022.
text: Mid November, 2022 - loud crackling noise for a moment then gone. But video-to-audio sync failed thereafter. Meaning the actors' lips move and the sound of what they are saying is heard a second or 2 later. Swapped out to another (MPOW) headset and synced perfectly. Hence these BERIBES Bluetooth Headphones are most unsatisfactory.

title: These are actually quite useful for extending power line from USB wall transformer to...
text: to a USB-powered item whose cord is too short. A USB powered fan is a good example. So we use this not as a signal channel but merely as a power channel. Better than an extension cord with the USB power transformer hanging off the end, as you can well imagine.

title: Bit fiddley go get over the retaining rings but doable.
text: The retaining rings must be removed from the earpieces, these replacement pads slipped over and then the rings snapped back into place. As described in greater detail by other reviewers. Worth the effort.

title: Utterly useless impenetrable tap tap tap controls. Impossible to use.
text: Slide the left bud down to lower, right up to raise volume. So you're supposed to remember this arcana? And which is L and which R? Can't see any indication. OK. Enough rant about unfriendliness. Now on to pairing. Won't pair with my new Dell laptop. Pairs with my new iphone but one channel constantly cuts in and out. Yes, impenetrable new unfriendly modern technology requires that we learn it rather than it learn us. And I had such high hopes for these that now I think I'll drop them in the Cuisinart and watch (gloat) at the subsequent rubble. Revenge is mine!

title: Amazingly muddy and distant sound versus prior $50 pair
text: Prior $50 MPOW still in service but earpads crumbling with age. So did research and found Philips Audio Fidelio X2HR Over-Ear Open-Air Headphones as, I hoped, a replacement and upgrade. Put music CD on the old but very good Sony amp, listened to the old MPOW via headphone output jack. All good. Swapped out for the new Philips Audio Fidelio X2HR Over-Ear Open-Air Headphones and it was like listening through cotton batting. Dull bass. Shrill treble. Muddy mids.  Fidelio was Beethoven's only opera. That Philips expropriated the name is a huge overreach. Obliged to return. Hope the new Amazon does not whack me with a bunch of hidden return fees...

title: Set up today 2022-06-26. Caution! Factory installed speaker wires set too far in: no sound.
text: So last thing to check if no sound but VU meters moving and headphones sound OK. Yes, the factory installed speaker wires were pushed too far into the connectors so the insulation prevented metal-to-metal contact. Solution: back out the speaker wires an reinstall. Just trying to be helpful. 2 days later: noted clipping and crackle in the FM radio at peak signal. As pointed out elsewhere, this is a bad FM radio. Occasional click/pop on the CD.

title: Developed tremendous static noise after 2 weeks. Yes, as others have rightly said:
text: This is a piece of junk. Loud, intrusive static crackle after 2 weeks. Both on Radio and CD. So this is not the CD only. Plus the cover on the remote had to be held in place by a rubber band. Free UPS pickup returned - for which I say, in this case, "Thank you, Amazon!" as I just made the return window. In other cases I have been hit by unexpected costs or inconvenience. But not in this case, for some unfathomable reason. As I am old and somewhat frail, sincerely appreciate the drop-off and pickup - when it works.

title: Way to unstable.
text:
Cuts out at it's own volition! And then cuts back in. And, yes, the wireless here is otherwise fast and perfect.

Based on the startup time, when you go to look, the signal has to go all the way to the Chinese servers and back again. This is called latency.

Look elsewhere, please.

Do not be fooled by the advertising which is utter self-serving marketing fluff.

Best too all us fools on Amazon - which depends on fools to keep the business running.

Just buy locally where there might be someone to talk to...

title: Very light plastic. Thin. Click action is weak. No way by looking to see if it is on or off.
text:
Tina's New Stars Scale: 3 = as expected. 4 = better than expected. 5 = much better than expected. Conversely: 1 = much worse than expected. 2 = worse than expected. This New Stars Scale thus allows a negative rating as some have complained that they "Can't give negative 5 stars." Well now you can as 1 and 2 are in effect negative ratings, being lower than 3 which is essentially "OK. It works as expected, no better, no worse."

Well this mouse gets a New Stars Scale rating of only 2 because there is no way by glancing at it to tell if it is on or off. Rather one has to either 1) wiggle the mouse and see on the computer screen - if it is up and running - what the cursor does, or even if it is there or 2) pick up the mouse and look at the tiny black on/off switch on the bottom. Whether on or off, the tracking beam is invisible to the human eye.

Whereas my Amazon Basics mouse has a red jewel on top that lights up when it is on. Good idea! And it has a solid feel and better click. It is better then expected (or normal) so it gets a 4.

So I won't be buying the Logitech M170 mouse again.

title: Failed within a few uses. Dead as a doornail. China strikes again.
text: What dd I dislike, Amazon coyly asks? Me? Well the thing failed almost immediately. What's not to dislike, I ask you?

title: Status window did not light up then did then did not. Tested various batts and...
text: Tested. Put in new fully-charged enerloops and this charger was totally confused. Yes, I know the batts are fully charged. I just wanted to see what the charger did. Should have said AOK no need to do anything. But no! Brand new fully-charged enerloop shows 1 flashing bar on the screen. As if near dead. Also put in known near discharged batts and charger was totally confused. I do not think this is a very high-quality piece of equipment. As with so much from China nowadays, quality control is lax lax lax. So please be warned - but I suspect you already know this. Sad to say...

title: Outlets too close together. No room for transformers.
text: Kinda like going into a Costco parking lot and the spaces are just a bit too small. So 1 car takes 1.5 spaces. 2 cars take 3. But wait! 2 cars should take 2 spaces, no? So 1 is wasted. Hence you will not get the number of outlets advertised. Unless, of course, you buy those very short extension cords that are specifically designed to overcome this defect. Money. It is just a matter of money. Of which, I assume you have a lot extra, no? So this outlet strip might have simply been made with 1/2in bigger spacing between the outlets. Then you would get 6, as advertised. But in the real world, you only get 4. Crowded design doubtless to force the buyer to buy another strip. I feel cheated. How about you?

title: App inferior. Night color great! Randonly offline 20% of the time after 2wks. DO NOT BUY!
text:
Color at night. Not washed-out shades of grey. But if the camera is offline, what does color matter?

But as stated below from first review, the app is very poor: Waay too many alerts. Plus shape detection does not work. Plus where app supposedly allows a free-form monitoring window to be drawn by hand across the field of view, simply does nothing.

2021-05-03 went offline randomly and cannot be recovered remotely. For this reason, I will cancel my suggestion to our condo board to buy 10 and try to return the camera. Too unstable. Bad. Bad. Bad. Total waste of my time in evaluation. And, yes, I know how to setup a network. It is the camera. Instructions say to press reset button. I'm supposed to climb a ladder? This is an unstable camera. Please beware and be informed. Stay away.

Update: offline for 24hrs, suddenly came back online all by itself. Don't know what to make of this but cannot recommend this camera to our Condo Community. Too unstable.

When offline, camera stops recording creating huge random gaps in the history and, yes, recording set to internal card not cloud. So why did it stop? Must require online connection in the background. Is someone spying?

2021-06-30 Offline for NO REASON last 24 hours. The down time was from the camera itself, not the net. Surely in the 21st century we can do better than this! Unstable.

Update 2021-07-19: Last Wed went offline at 10PM then back online at 8AM Thurs! Exactly the hours we need monitoring! Had we not have reviewed the history, we would NOT HAVE KNOWN!

Further: Of course we have VLC. Latest. Sound OK but no video. So whomever suggested this as a solution clearly knows not of what he speaks. The amazon community is going downhill. Sad. Very sad.

Today 2021-07-19 after an internet hunt found a free media player that works. But we're not gonna share. HaHa!

title: Got it  2021-02-07. First impressions on Cons (Pro's stated prior correctly) but U need to know:
text: 1) No little feet on the back bottom. The keyboard cannot be tilted. Thus when flat, the key lights can be seen underneath the keys, creating a bright, distracting pattern of lines. These disappear if the keyboard is tilted so you can look at it straight, or nearly, on. But given my desk height versus chair height and consequent angle of vision, I am looking at the keyboard from approx a 45 degree sideways angle. Keyboard needs to be tilted to achieve an approx 35 degree angle of vision which would require about 1in feet on the back bottom of the keyboard. I'll have to use a book or something. And even when properly angled, the numeric keypad leaks light along the left edge of the keys. 2) When the F6 and F7 dim/bright keys are set to "Standard Function Keys" per the set up, then the dim/bright function is lost. I need standard F's. Possible solution: Provide dim/bright slider on the back next to the on/off switch. Doubtless the keyboard can be re-mapped as a fix but: How? More later... And now: 3) Waving hands over the keys and light will not turn on! So hit space bar or something and have to wait 1 Mississippi 2 Mississippi then the light grudgingly comes up to 100% bright. Which is not all that bright! All this when powered through USB port. Sigh. And it turns off on a whim. 4) But wait! I'm using this specialty item wrong: not for the desktop but for the lap - literally. When sitting well away from the PC and big monitor, sit back, relax and watch tube video but control with this wireless, lit keyboard which you look directly down upon - as it is in your lap. Problems solved. But not a serious desktop keyboard. I'll keep it for this one use - entertainment.

title: Worked perfectly
text:
The definition of PnP.

We have a splendid and expensive (back then) VGA screen but with no HDMI plug! New Dell: no VGA just HDMI.

What's so great about HDMI versus VGA anyhow? Looks good to me.

For a small fee, this transitional cable bridged the gap and restored our older screen to perfect view.

Thus do we small'uns defeat the big'uns relentless upgrade path! Hoorah!

title: Camera arm set-screw simply fell out and was lost! But such is life. Fixed it. See text:
text:
So the camera position lock fails and the camera flops around like a dead turkey neck. Please, ye assemblers, tighten down the set screw and use a dab of Locktite. Sloppy assembly is like a tire falling off your SUV: Clearly, someone forgot to torque it down. And now the set-screw is lost. And as we urgently needed the camera arm for a Zoom session, this equipment fail was most disappointing. Send me another set-screw in the mail and we shall be friends again (not likely). Or simply send me the specs on the set-screw and I will try to find a replacement - again, not likely.
2021-02-05 Edit: But thanks to the good people at ACE (yes, it is the place) a new set screw was obtained and with my new 2.5mm Wiha 96325 Precision Hex Metric Screwdriver, 2.5 x 60mm $7.45 on Amazon, it was, well, set. Securing the ball (of ball-and-socket) against the thumb screw which together lock the camera mount at the desired angle. So all is good. That I had to put in a bit of time and money for the fix is in the nature of life: What can go wrong will go wrong. So: No hard feelings.

title: Bent to the left (viewed from front). Poorly constructed. Regret buying this. Details below:
text: Not straight. Considered a fix using washers to offset the left-side bolts but that would look even more terrible than it does now. And it is painted solid black. Illustration looks like chrome or white to me; certainly not black. Ugly. Plus packed in a slightly too-small light cardboard box which was obviously stressed by the manufacturer's packing. title: Expecting Disaster But Installation Flawless with Great Instructions/Video!
text:
Let me be frank....I was honestly expecting to have a hard time with this. We all have "Screen Protector Installation Gone Wrong" stories by now, and I was totally resigned to another. With two films included in the pack, I figured that improved my odds of getting one on there half decent. I even had an adult beverage to steel my nerves for the ordeal, which is something I generally only do once a year on the Fourth of July. Yeah, I definitely had a few misgivings.

I started by pre-cleaning my screen with an alcohol square to remove any grease. I then watched the video from the link provided on the instructions twice. Then I simply followed their instructions. The installation was flawless--so flawless that I initially thought I had peeled off the entire film protector with the second tab and was back to bare screen. When I examined it with a magnifying glass, I was able to discern the cutouts around the "Home" button and camera. That's how perfect it went.

No sterile containment suit or CDC reverse vacuum seal room necessary. No special powers or ninja skills required. Just follow the instructions PERIOD. Believe me. If I can do this on my bed with a 110 pound pit bull and a cat beside me and get PERFECT results, anyone can! Thank you, amFilm.

I'd like to note that there was minor damage to one of the tabs on one of the films I received and I contacted Customer Support to let them know. They could not have been more helpful, courteous, or prompt with their reply. I would suspect they would be just as responsive if your installation attempts somehow malfunctioned. We all have bad days. I would absolutely be ready to give it another go; it's a good product from a good company that seems genuinely interested in keeping their customers satisfied. To me, that's all the hallmarks of a winner.

PS. Watch the video!

title: Instructions were lacking
text:
Small, solid and nice looking. But the instructions have zero help and had multiple spelling errors like "white corn, green corn" instead of cord.
As for the install, this is what I did on my 2011 Altima:
1. Removed the lining of the trunk lid. Removed the license plate shade where the lights sits. Drilled a hole where I was going to mount the camera. Drilled a second hole thru the trunk body to the interior of the trunk.
2. Ran the cord from the camera thru both holes and screwed the camera in place with the locking washer. I taped this cord to the other cords that ran thru to the trunk interior.
3. Unplugged the main wiring harness from the taillight. Used a multimeter to test each pin in the wiring harness. You can go to a shop like PepBoys and ask to test it, it only takes a minute. First I turned the car on and tested each pin while it was running, all lights off, and marked down the numbers. Then I pulled the emergency brake and put the car in reverse and tested each pin again to see which wire was the reverse relay wire as that is the wire I tapped for the red power wire. In my car the white cord was constant power, purple was the reverse relay. I used a simple quick splice to tap the red power wire into the reverse wire. The black wire I grounded to a nearby bolt.
4. Ran the longest cord under the trim pieces along the driver's side and up under the steering column to the stereo.
5. Connected the rca cords and the camera cord. Covered all with electrical tape. And put some silicone around the wire where it entered the trunk to keep it sealed.

Overall, it's a decent camera. I just found the instructions lacking and unhelpful. The diagram wasn't easy to follow either. So it goes Camera to short RCA cord. Red & black wire from that RCA need to tap to the reverse light and ground. Then the short yellow RCA into the long RCA then into the stereo system. The two really short red wires were unused. Hopefully that helps some people.

title: Wait for the next version.  An unexpected and serious disappointment.
text:
I found Bose's latest wireless headphones to be a fairly serious disappointment, which was surprising and frustrating after having bought 5 or 6 pairs of headphones over the years, along with speakers and a Wave Radio. I *like* Bose products.

Let me start with the positive, to be fair.

1. They sound great.
2. They stay in my ears. (A feature Apple did not think to include with their glorious AirPods.)
3. The Bose connect app on the iPhone is slick and useful.

The negatives.

1. They are very big and jut from my ears in a way that looks comical. I've seen other people compare them to the bolts on Frankenstein's neck, but for the ears. Actually, though, it's worse than that, because their weight makes them droop. So I'd describe the look as more Frankenstein Eeyore. If you have hair that covers your ears, you will probably be ok. But I am close to bald, so I can't really wear them in public. Since I bought them to wear during my workouts at LA Fitness and while coding at work, the fact that they make me look silly is a show stopper.

2. Given the look issues, I'd love to wear them when I listen to music on my computer at home, but they don't pair properly with Windows 10. They have a voice profile and a music profile. No matter how I fiddle with my PC, based on advice from the various threads on Bose's support forums, I cannot get the music profile to activate. The reason this is a problem is that the voice profile only plays music in one ear, and at far reduced quality. Like it's-being-piped-to-your-ear-through-Satan's-toilet quality. Bose's suppport forums have various threads about this, and it's clear that some part of Bose's software group either doesn't get it or is trying to avoid publicly stating that they can't fix the problem. They claim it is Windows or software differences on various PCs, but my Apple AirPods work fine as do Bose's SoundSport Wireless headphones (though they lack a mic, so the scenario is somewhat different).

3. I wish there was a way to hear audio in both ears while making calls. You can do this with the AirPods.

HEAVY

COOLING

POSITION

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great stand for having at a desk or table. It is good for a larger heavy laptop for gaming, or even my larger tablet works on there. Be prepared to use with USB or bluetooth keyboard.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is not quite as portable as I was thinking it would be, but I can get something else to take with me. For home use, this is great especially this summer when I need to do a lot of business work on my laptop.
