This machine is set up with the gamer in mind. It is very powerful and does play some of the highest demanding games on the market right now without any trouble. It is also set up with the console gamer in mind, specifically the Xbox crowd as it comes with a wireless Xbox 360 controller (which is already set up to work in Windows).

Many Playstation gamers as well as others are not fond of this controller. We did manage to set up a Playstation 3 controller using the Motion Joy and Pinnacle Profiler method that we downloaded from online. Motion joy is free, but Pinnacle Profiler is a one-time fee to download it (after a 20 day trial period).

CAN YOU PLAY OLDER PC GAMES ON THIS SYSTEM?
One of the concerns I had, which I am sure others out there might have is- "Can I play all of my older PC games on this unit as well as Steam games?" The answer is YES! All of our games (purchased through Gog.com previously) work beautifully on this system. That means you do not have to be connected to the internet to play them.

WHAT SHOULD YOU PLAN TO PURCHASE?
--Keyboard (I use Logtiech K400 wireless w/ touchpad on board I use for basic Windows stuff)
--Mouse (I use Marathon Mouse for games)
--DVD-ROM/CD-ROM USB drive (if you want to install anything using those)
--Wireless headphones if you want to use them for gaming

BLUETOOTH
I have a pair of Turtle Beach i30 wireless headphones that operate by bluetooth. I found conflicting information on their site as to whether this would work with Windows 8.1 or not, so I tried installing it.

Windows 8.1 has some idiosyncrasies with bluetooth and is notorious for causing problems in this area. When attempting to install my headphones with this system, the process somehow completely messed up the bluetooth operations in the system. It took me a couple of days to figure it all out, but with a lot of perseverance and some Free Ccleaner added for registry and system cleaning, I managed to get the bluetooth headphones to work beautifully.

This is not a console problem but a Windows 8.1 problem.

ARMA III
We ran this game with maxed out settings, this system ran 30fps smoothly and perfectly. (At the time of this review Arma III is a military simulator that has a very high graphics demand. It is one of the top most demanding games on the market at this time.)

Graphically it looks way better than anything from Modern Warfare.

IS THIS WORTH IT?
PROS
-completely functional PC in all aspects of Windows 8.1
-small physical footprint
-plays all levels of PC games very well
-comes with Xbox controller
-works with PS3 controller
-can get decent keyboard and mouse for very little extra money
-allows family gaming
-more convenient for limited space in living area
-will shut off with front switch like console
-everyone can have their own account
-can play old PC games on this (if updated as in GOG.com purchases)
-can upgrade memory and hard drive

CONS
-expensive(but very powerful for this price range)
-need to purchase keyboard and mouse for Windows operations
-Windows 8.1 can be a bit frustrating at times (Win 8.1 is not unique to this console, however)

THE BOTTOM LINE
When I first read about this console/PC unit, I thought it was way overpriced, but after using it, I REALLY like it so far. We have put this thing through constant use and pushing it since we got it. I have to say it is up to the task. My son who is an avid gamer and builds super computers is even impressed with it, which is saying a lot. In his opinion, it is a very powerful system for the price.

This is a PC designed for console gamers who might not really have discovered the world of PC gaming yet. It seems to be a solid machine that performs well. Working with Windows is not always an easy task, but in set up and basic gaming operations this system is really impressive to me.

WHO WOULD NOT WANT TO GET THIS SYSTEM
This is a high functioning computer that will run games on it and has a console experience attached with it. If you are just interested in using this for Steam, I would say that it is not worth the money. If you want to have a highly functioning Windows 8.1 system (capable of some great gaming) that allows you to have a console experience with Steam as an added bonus all on your TV, then this system is great.

UPDATE 6-2015
We are still crazy about this system. The more that we use it, the more fun it is to explore. The Alien Respawn takes a bit of messing with to get it to work right, but after the update, I finally got the system backed up.

The Steam console has been fun to use, although again, it is quirky when trying to use the Xbox 360 controller that we got with it. There is a glitch that causes some problems occasionally and has to be re-installed from time to time. I am not sure if it is a Windows 8.1 problem or a Steam problem. We are hoping to get the Steam controller when it comes out if it looks like a solid option.

We all have gotten and use Steam accounts and found it to work well so far. We are playing on Wi-Fi (not solid line in) and it still performs quite well.

All in all, this system is FANTASTIC and I can not recommend it highly enough. If I could give it TEN stars, I would.

And as silly as it seems, having the ability to change the colors on the alien head and the triangle shape thrills me to no end. Simple but fun.

Will update if we get the Steam controller to let you know how that works.

title: Excellent Little Speaker To Conference, Listen To Presentations, and Basic Music
text:
One of the things I like to do is listen to messages from conferences that I could not be a part of in person via my tablet. I have an Acer Iconia A1-830,and I like to tune into conferences, presentations, and speeches and listen to them either for the first time or in recap as I do work around the house or in a single room. It is very helpful to have a bluetooth speaker to carry with me as I move around and still be able to hear what it is that I am listening to.

I have a Outdoor Tech OT1800 Turtle Shell 2.0 Rugged Water-Resistant Wireless Bluetooth Hi-Fi Speaker that I bring with me by clipping on my bet and walking from room to room when I want to hear music or presentations. I was interested to know how this speaker compares. For presentations it is just as nice. For music, well, considering the price (which is far less than the Turtle Shell) I think this speaker is great.

WHAT IS THIS SPEAKER LIKE?
Recharging is easy with the enclosed USB charging cord, which I plug into an adapter in my wall outlet instead of computer. It only takes about 45 minutes to fully charge. This speaker is about the size of a few chocolate chip cookies stacked on top of each other in size. It has good controls and is easy to sit anywhere. The back of the speaker has a rubberized/silicone type pad on it to keep it from sliding around easily and to cushion it against buzzing or vibration from the speaker.

HOW DOES THIS SPEAKER PERFORM?
I have to say, I am impressed at how nicely this speaker performs. When it comes to presentations, I have to say that it is high quality. The sound is very 3D and has great range to it. I have played it at full volume on both the tablet and the speaker without a lot of sound distortion, unless music enters the presentation then it will distort a bit. I can hear it around the entire room.

We also tested this with a Samsung Galaxy 3.4 MP3 player. To play music, we tested this speaker by running it with a bluetooth connection as well as an auxiliary cable. The auxiliary cable had a stronger sound with less distortion and great depth to it. The bluetooth had a good sound but there was a slight deterioration in sound over the cable connection. You can not play this with both the MP3 player and speaker at full volume for music as there will be distortion. That is often true with speakers, so it is nothing out of the ordinary. You can play it close to full however, and get some pretty decent sound from it without buzzing, distortion, or vibration.

FINAL COMMENTS
For the price, this is a great little speaker. It comes with a basic carrying pouch which is nice to transport it but if you want to travel with it, you will need a padded pouch with a bit more protection. I am rating this five stars because for the price, I think it is great quality. If you are the type of person who is a music enthusiast and loves to listen to all kinds of music with attention to detailed depth and intensity, you might want to move up to a more expensive model. For the general casual listening person, however, this is a very nice speaker.

title: The ULTIMATE Business or School Computer Case
text:
Wow. That is the only word that came out of my mouth when I first saw this case.

I have several older electronic devices as well as smaller new ones and the problem I run into is that most cases are either way too big or way too small to accommodate more than one or two devices without crowding too much. This case, however is AMAZING!

Here is a list of what I can put in this case all at one time:
-Lenovo Thinkpad (large footprint)
-HP Elitebook
-Kindle 2
-cell phone
-Acer Iconia A830
-MP3 player
-notebook(spiral bound for notes)
-recharge plugs
-3 pens and pencils
-sticky note pad
-keys (fit on clip inside)
-3 workbooks
-kleenex
-lipstick, gloss, and small makeup mirror

AND THERE IS STILL ROOM FOR A FEW MORE THINGS

Granted, the case is heavy with all of that stuff, but it fits and if I need to take it somewhere, I can.

WHAT I LOVE
-roomy compartments- many zip shut
-outer fabric is tough canvas- not thin
-REAL leather on corners will make this last a lot longer than most cases
-screws hold handle on to case
-tons of padding
-lining is woven to avoid rips and is not too slick or too rough at all
-great color inside allows me to see what is in there but not prone to show dirt
-outer compartment allows me to slip in notebook etc if I need constant quick access
-padded shoulder strap is slip resistant- a BIG plus for me
-padded shoulder strap is VERY padded
-zippers are metal with easy grip and heavy duty
-inner velcro strap allows laptop and tablet to be protected while accessing other pockets and compartments
-key strap is bright red so it is easy to locate quickly

WHAT I DON'T LIKE (very few things)
-no outer pocket for easy access to cell phone to make it quick to answer when ringing while carrying case
-outer fabric does show dust and dirt easily but I can live with that
-magnetic closures barely attract at all (but weight of flap helps to stay closed anyway)

WHO MIGHT FIND THIS CASE USEFUL
-graphic artists (even room for graphic pads if necessary)
-business people who travel a lot
-women who want to combine purse and carry bag
-students, especially those who have to travel to different buildings and classes
-business owners who need all of their necessities and electronic devices in one place for easy access in stores or offices
-sales people and product reps
-marketing (allows for carrying brochures and cards to distribute)
-anyone going on vacation who want their devices and information in one place for easy access when needed

This case is one of the best I have EVER seen. It allows me to take with me every device I want to if I would like or I can take as few as I would like. There is room for most other materials I would want to bring (including lipstick and mirror) so that I could literally use this instead of a purse if I wanted to.

The pockets and compartments were well thought out. Some zip shut, some don't. The dividers for the laptop and tablet compartments are padded nicely. I also like that the fabric is not too slick so things slide around too easily. It is JUST right. And as silly as it seems, the bright red key strap with the hook on the end is BRILLIANT. So easy to locate when I need it quickly.

I can not recommend this bag highly enough. It is truly a masterpiece and SO well made!

title: I Like This, But Prefer Covers Designed for Specific Tablets
text:
I was very excited to get this case. I had originally got it with my Kindle 2 in mind which is an 8 inch tablet. However, when I got it installed in this case, to my disappointment, the corners that hold the table in, interfered completely with all of the buttons on the Kindle.

Okay, so I moved to my 7 inch tablet- Acer Iconia A1 830. It did fit, but honestly, it is not as nice as the 7in case I have made specifically for it. The back does bend down to take a photo, and it does stand up, but not quite as stable as I would like.

The texture of this case is rubbery and does make for a nice water resistant cover. The plastic corners do hold the tablet firmly in place and adjust well. The side has a slit so you can access any slots. The cover does extend past the edges of the tablets for good protection.

This case/cover is okay, but I just don't feel it is as good of a fit as I had hoped for my Acer Iconia or my Kindle 2. Perhaps other brands would work better.

title: The Most Frustrating Experience In A Long Time
text:
I originally got this unit so I could transmit video or presentations to a larger screen for more people to be able to view. Sounded simple enough, so I could not wait to get it.

The whole process has been a pain. At the time of the order, I saw no reference at all to the fact that I would have to buy an adapter for this unit. Okay, I really wanted it, so I consulted my fellow techie freak to see if we had one in the house, and unfortunately we didn't I had to buy it. I had to spend the $ and then had to wait for it to come in the mail.

I got the CNE70196 High Quality Black DisplayPort Male to HDMI Cable Male 6ft/2M as well as the micro port adapter so I could try it from my tablet as well. After all, I planned to use this so why not? Yeah, right.

Once the adapters arrived, I set out to test the unit. I tried to download the drivers from the online site. No dice. They didn't work at all. Then I got the disc that came with the unit and tried to put the driver on from there and software. Well, after all of this, I can say at this point of trying and trying to make this work, neither I or my fellow resident techie fanatic can get this to work on any laptop in the house. We also can not get it to work with a tablet as there is not software for it.

So, all in all, this was a rotten experience and I can not recommend it in any way in reference to what I went through to try to get it to work. I am disappointed as I was really looking forward to using this, but alas, it is not to be.

title: A Few Adjustments And This Would Be Five Stars
text:
Several of my family have been into taking photos for a long time. We have been through quite a few cameras, although not top of the line, still not inexpensive by any means. $500 is usually the price range of cameras we have purchased.

The Fujifilm FinePix S1 is a contradiction of sorts. You might say there is a love-hate relationship with it.

WHAT WE LIKE
Camera lightweight for what is in it
Easy grip- to hang on to and hold
Great neck strap
Macro and Supermacro capabilities are good
Durable
WiFi feature works great with tablet (android OS)
50X zoom works great (have to have very steady hand for that)
Great movies for what it is
Mini HDMI port works for TV or monitor
Photos with flash turn out well consistently
Left and right zoom buttons come in VERY handy
Takes decent self portraits, although a bit clumsy at times to hold
Timer worked well

WHAT WE DON'T LIKE
Navigation can be frustrating
Directional pad can be frustrating
Light sensor is unstable
Automatic settings very unstable and inconsistent
Photos look better on LCD pad than they actually are
Sometimes photos look flat and/or grainy (not 3D looking or clear)

THE BOTTOM LINE

THE LIGHT PROBLEM
We tested this camera extensively inside, outside, at night, in indirect light and with sunlight and found that the light sensor in this camera is way too inconsistent for satisfying picture taking. Sometimes the colors captured were exquisite and better than any other camera I have ever used. I didn't have to do any adjusting at all. Other times they were abyssmal.

For instance, in taking 10 pictures in a row, changing absolutely nothing, it was virtually impossible to have two pictures turn out alike. They were all vastly different. Sometimes they were dark, sometimes way too light, sometimes perfect. That is a lot of effort to capture the perfect picture.

On the flip side, one night in absolute frustration not being able to capture anything decent at all, I turned out all of the lights so that the room was pitch black. I held my camera up to my fish tanks and snapped a few pictures. Besides traumatizing my fish from the sudden light, I was shocked to see some of the most beautiful photos I had taken all evening. Perfect colors, clarity and definition consistently.

It appears that when you use the flash, that the color calibration kicks into high gear and you get pretty darned good photos.

You can not live your life taking flash photos unfortunately.

PHOTO QUALITY
I found that by using various settings and experimenting, I could get pretty nice photos- but I had to use a lot of effort. The menu is not easy to navigate, nor is it forgiving if you take too long to decipher it- it shuts off on you and you have to go through it again.

I did find that sometimes I was taking what I thought were fantastic photos (from the LCD screen) only to upload them to my photo editing program and seeing that they were grainy or blurry or just plain flat and un-dimensional. On the LCD screen they looked amazing. On the other hand, sometimes they turned out blah on my LCD screen, but great on the SD card.

Once in a while, I have problems with my Canon with color. I love bright colors and my photography focus is often color oriented. Canon often understates color way too much for me and I have to spend some time to get it to look accurate in photo editing. With the FinePix S1, however, once in a while, I could capture color that was so gorgeous and realistic that I would gasp and be very excited.

The problem is that it is not always predictable and that was frustrating. Like the proverbial carrot on the string in front of the horse, I find myself reaching for this camera when frustrated with my others to capture colors that don't seem to do well on any other camera. Once in a while the effort is worth it so I come back for more frustration.

FINAL COMMENTS
As I said at the beginning, I have a bit of a love hate relationship with this camera. On the one hand it is a lot of work to get decent photos, but on the other hand, when you do manage to get one, it is amazing. Rare, but amazing.

If Fujifilm would fix the issues with depth in photos, consistency in the light sensor, and quality issues on automatic settings, this camera would be a MUST buy. As it is now, however, I can only give it three stars because of the inconsistency in quality of photos and the effort I have to go through to get a good one. I gave it three stars because once in a while it does capture photos with brilliant colors that none of my other cameras will capture, despite the slightly lower quality at times. The videos are great- sound excellent and clarity nice. The flash is great. Out of the way when you don't want it- and nice photos. It has potential to be a fantastic camera.

As it is now, until they correct a few things, it is only average.

title: (SUPPORT  & COMPARE TO SAMSUNG)Excellent Tablet For the Money, But Don't Get Rid of Your Laptop
text:
(SEE END FOR UPDATED COMPARISON TO SAMSUNG GALAXY 4)
I have ready many reviews on tablets, and have found most of them to be why a certain tablet is better than another to the nth degree with all kinds of technical jargon which really just pits one expert against another. As a person who tutors people who are not technologically savvy, I am going to review this tablet from the point of view of someone who has not had one before and whether or not this is a good choice if you want to get one.

I have been told by several business people and those who claim to be very tech savvy that they have gotten rid of their laptops except for occasional spreadsheet work in their offices or at home. Can you get rid of your laptop by getting a tablet like this? Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS TABLET LIKE?
SIDE SWITCHES
This tablet is around the size of an ipad mini or a Kindle. The on off switch is on the upper right hand side (with screen facing you) and below it is a rocker switch just below the power switch. There is a space between the two buttons which will allow for elastic bands should you want to get a case for it that has them. That will make it so that the tablet will not be turned on and off by accident. The power button has to be pushed and held for a moment before the unit turns on.

SCREEN
The tablet screen is shiny which can be annoying, but that is the nature of the beast.
The touch sensitivity is excellent- I did not find any problems with response time or lag.
The orientation changing when you turn the screen around is also well set. It works nicely and is not overly sensitive.

INPUT
To input into the tablet, you have a choice to either type or speak what you want the tablet to do. I have to say that this tablet responds very well to either set of input. After working with several i-pads, my daughter constantly raves about how this Acer tablet is superior in the way it responds to input with the microphone than the i-pads are. I have not had any problem with typing into this tablet beyond what I normally do on any unit. The microphone occasionally mistypes a word, but it is not nearly as bad as I expected it to.

Response time of the tablet is excellent. I am quite impressed with how quickly it responds to input without lag or difficulty.

APPS
I have put a few apps on this unit which tend to be popular with tablet users. Sketchbook Pro is one of those apps. I really like it. The response time is good, and the app seems to work well on this tablet. I also love the radio app which allows you to listen to radio stations in the area or around the country. With a case that folds into a stand, it is a great panel to use in a room where you want to listen to the radio.

Quite a few apps that come in the tablet already are handy and easy to use. The screen is quite intuitive and easy to use.

INTERNET USAGE
This tablet is wi-fi accessible to the internet which means that you can not go out in no-man's land to use it like you can an android phone, but you have to be near a wi-fi station to use it.

The wi-fi response time is excellent- although it does occasionally lag when the signals get weak- something that all wi-fi units will do.

Android is a Google engine so everything you do will be monitored by Google or you will be using something they have designed to get where you want to go. You can find other ways to purchase apps if you don't like the Google store, however, such as Amazon.

This tablet comes with McAfee virus scan which is not a huge deal, but I am not sure how to replace that yet, should I desire to do so.

CAMERA
I am not a big advocate of phone and tablet cameras. This one has a decent camera to use on the back, and an adequate camera on the front of the camera to use for Skype which is pretty much all you need. If you want a really nice camera, buy one. For quick pictures to capture something you want to show someone, then this will be fine.

PROS
Easy to hold
Screen responsive
Speech recognition works well
Good fast performance
Boots up quickly
Clear screen makes reading books nice
Good colors for photos on the screen (better than laptops)
Power button hard to accidentally turn on or off
Learning is pretty intuitive for first time users

CONS
Wi-fi only
Not as easy to use as laptop for extensive typing
Can be a bit clumsy to use at times (the nature of tablets)
Start up literature is a bit underwhelming for first time users

THE BOTTOM LINE

CAN YOU GET RID OF YOUR LAPTOP?
Can you get rid of your laptop to substitute this tablet? My answer would be no.

Even if all you did was go on the internet to wander through web sites, using a tablet is a bit cumbersome if you want to do any kind of extensive writing. If you use the microphone, it will probably be pretty accurate, but you will still have to use the keyboard to correct what is used.

For occasional internet usage, watching videos, movies, and reading books, this tablet is fabulous. I think it works beautifully. I would say that it is just as nice as other more expensive tablets and you will invest a lot less money in it.

If you want a tablet and do not want to pay a fortune for it, this is the way to go. The Acer Iconia A1-830 is an excellent value and I use mine a lot. I just could not substitute it completely for my laptop. I prefer to have a choice in my browser, features, and fine tuning or replacement of parts should I desire to do so.

I do find that having the tablet helps a lot when I want to quickly do something on the internet and don't want to boot up my laptop. This tablet is pretty quick and I like it. If you are a tech fanatic and have to have the biggest and best, you might find fault with this tablet, however. It is worth a test run in any case.

UPDATE 3/4/2015 SAMSUNG GALAXY 4 (8 inch) vs ACER ICONIA A1-830
I have had quite a chance to get to know this tablet over time and also to use a Samsung Galaxy 4 8 inch tablet in comparison both on its own and with a keyboard. After working with both tablets, I have to say that I still prefer the Acer over the Samsung and here is why:

-Acer has slightly smaller screen area, but is easier to work on
-Acer has the return and menu buttons incorporated into the screen instead of on the side so it rotates with screen
-Acer surface is less shiny and has less glare
-Performance of Acer is the same as the Samsung in terms of speed
-Wifi of Acer is as good as the Samsung
-keyboard of Acer is much easier to use than Samsung (the one in the screen)
-set up of the Acer is much easier and user friendly
-voice commands on Acer works MUCH better than on the Samsung
-Samsung speaker is a bit nicer than Acer, but I use a bluetooth speaker for best sound anyway.
-Samsung battery does last a bit longer than the Acer, but the frustrations of the Samsung still make me prefer the Acer.

All in all, I have to say that I have tried to honestly look at both tablets and give them a fair comparison and I still like the Acer better. The price is better and the ease of use is better too. The microphone on the Acer seems much more responsive than the Samsung. The screen of the Samsung is a bit more dense in terms of pixels and color perhaps, but the glare is more annoying. I also get very irritated at the side buttons on the Samsung. They are static (stay put) and when the tablet is on its side, it is way too easy to hit a button that screws up what I am trying to do on the Samsung. This is especially true when I am trying to type something and is VERY frustrating.

There is one thing about the Samsung that I really wish the Acer had and that is longer battery time. The Samsung does run a little longer than the Acer without having to recharge. The speaker on the Samsung is a bit nicer, but with my portable bluetooth speaker as my main source of listening, I don't find that to be a problem for me.

So, after time and the chance to use the Acer and the Samsung so I could compare them, I still really like the Acer tablet better. Because I do a lot of graphics work and computer work, I still would not get rid of my laptop or desktop, but I do save a lot of time using this tablet when I want to look up quick information and cruise the internet.

UPDATE March 2016
I wanted to take a moment to update you concerning this device.

As time has gone on I have enjoyed using the Acer Iconia A1-830 very much. It is a nice tablet for an affordable price.

HAVE I HAD PROBLEMS?
A few.
-tablet went nuts as if a baby were in charge of it and had five Redbull drinks first. I rebooted and cleared out some programs and all was fine.

-I could not move my information from my device to my PC- this was solved, but it has taken a lot of research, effort and time. The support at the Acer site is rather pitiful to be honest. That is one thing that I will say about this, is compared to Samsung, Acer does not support their devices as well as they should, but then again, the price is a lot less too.

IS THIS STILL WORKING?
Yes., I use it daily and it still is working. I keep the HD less than 60% full as I do with most devices as they tend to work best that way. I find that it connects via wi-fi at times when other devices in the house do not. I also find that the battery wears down a lot less quickly if I turn off location and even wi-fi if I don't need it.

NO UPGRADE PAST KIT-KAT 4.4.2
There will be no upgrades to Lollipop or beyond, so if you want a more modern unit, then try for something new.

MY REVIEW STANDS
I now have a Samsung Galaxy Tab S2 that I am using and it of course passes the Acer by a mile, but then again, it is a much more expensive machine too.

title: REVIEW UPDATE-The Quality of This Speaker Continues to Amaze Us
text:
(REVIEW UPDATED 10-15-2014 see end)
When I first got this Turtle Shell, my electronically addicted children turned up their noses at it. They thought it was stupid and did not really do much for them. Then I turned it on with my Sansa MP3 player and they perked up and I got their attention. I plugged it in with the jack (included) and the sound from this little gem was amazing.

My son grabbed his Nokia C3 and plugged it in with the auxiliary cable and the sound was unreal! The family fought over who would use it next and tried every kind of music from classical to hip hop, rock, jazz, Christmas, and intense vocals. In every case the Turtle Shell performed really surprisingly well. I could not get anything bluetooth to hook up with it at the time of this review, but as I work with it, I will update this review.

The highs and lows are excellent and the sound produced is well rounded and quite intense. The dynamic range of sound is really good and it has fantastic mids with the perfect touch of lows so that the sound is balanced. The design is very easy to use, carry, set up, and use whether staying put, or carrying with you. The design of the Turtle Shell sends the sound in multiple directions that covers a wide range of area. You can either aim it on its side or have it sitting up to cover about 120 degree of sound direction.

The cover of the jack and recharge spots is a bit difficult to get into place sometimes, but it is doable. A small frustration with an otherwise fabulous speaker. If you don't use the blue tooth, it will shut the blinking light off so that it won't use battery power. It is light and is very solidly built. The volume buttons are a bit difficult to press and that is a bit frustrating. They seem a bit stiff and not easy to control. Maybe over time they will loosen up, I am not sure. I am still rating it five stars anyway because it is very impressive!

All of this insight is from the collaboration of my family who are all heavily into electronics and sound (my son who has a speaker collection like you would not believe).

EDITED- UPDATE
I wanted to take the time to update this review. Since the writing of this review, I have obtained an Acer Iconia A-830. This has taken my use of the Turtle to a whole new level.

When I want to sew, do different things around the house, or if I have to move in location a lot and can not be near a radio, computer, etc, I can set my radio or listen to presentations from my Acer Iconia and clip my Turtle to my belt loop and I can hear what I want to listen to almost anywhere in the house. Once in a great while, the speaker will go out of sync and lose signal if I go through too many walls but it reconnects pretty quickly when I am back in range again. If I know that I will be changing location, I just take the tablet with me and set it down and continue to work.

What I love is that the use of the Turtle does not drain the battery of either the speaker or the tablet and I an listen for a long time. The sound is fantastic. My kids still remark how they can not believe what a fantastic little speaker this is. There is no sound distortion and you can play it pretty loud without vibration or having it go way out of balance.

I use the Turtle constantly now and am thrilled to have it more than ever before

title: Great Tablet, A Few Idiosyncrasies But Still Like It
text:
I have been using Wacom tablets for so long, I can not begin to tell you. Perhaps it would make a difference to say that my first tablet I got was before Painter hit the market when it was developed by Fractal Design.

My most recent tablet was a workhorse- the ArtZII Tablet which was a pro version graphics tablet. I never had trouble with it and it worked with everything, including most games, believe it or not.

Unfortunately, the drivers began to malfunction so much with WinXP that I was forced to get a new tablet. If I could have gotten a serial to USB conversion adapter, I probably would still be using it if I had a driver to use with it.

The Intuos5 Touch Medium Pen Tablet is a wonderful tablet. Thanks to the previous reviewers, I did not even attempt to use it until I got the clear plastic cover for the pad to keep my pen from wearing down the nibs. I am SO glad I did. Now I feel like I am at home like I did with the ArtZII pad.

WHAT I USE THIS WITH

I like to use this pad with handwriting added to documents to sign things.
I use this for Corel Painter
I use this for Corel Graphics Suite X5.
I use this for general mouse uses when I don't need to use a lot of words on a keyboard.

WHAT I LIKE

The touch feature is helpful when I want to turn a page in Painter just like I would in real life
I like the responsiveness of the pen
I like that the screen can be made larger or smaller with my fingers.
I like that the light goes on in the screen to remind me that it is on.
Auto keyboard that pops out allows me to do minimal typing and not have to grab my keyboard

WHAT I DON'T LIKE

Silly, probably, but the round programming spots on the left side drive me nuts. They are not marked, and I just can not get into them yet.
I don't like that every time I grab the tablet near the round rubber area, it sends the screen coming in- but it does go away okay
The screen changing from one direction to another does not always work smoothly. Sometimes it gets stuck

A FEW MORE COMMENTS

I have not really tried programming this pad at this point as I have had not had the opportunity to do so as of yet. I usually am in such a hurry to do some photo work or graphics or sign something that I grab, do what I need and move on. I hope to study it more in depth in the future and use it even more than I do now.

The programming in Corel Painter X3 seems to work beautifully with this pad which I very much appreciate. The touch levels are fantastic and I feel the closest that I have ever been to using natural media on a computer than I have ever been in the years I have worked on computers with natural media programming- as I said, that is quite some time now.

The pen stand is kind of annoying, I am not sure why they set it up that way, but it is something I can live with. The pen itself is comfortable enough to work with and relatively easy to operate without too much thinking or reading of directions.

I will update this review as I learn more about this system and let you know how I like it. So far, I am quite happy with it, and have had no crashes or lockups while using it. The drivers load up well and I don't seem to have any difficulties.

I am using Windows 7 on a system I recently built so am just getting to know it better.

title: Great recharger, instructions could be a bit better
text:
Although I have had a few battery chargers over the years, I have never had anything quite this intricate before. This battery charger has a great layout. It has clearly marked buttons, and an easy to use adapter unit that plugs into it. You can also recharge USB items through this unit which is a great bonus.

Lately I have not had the time to really sit down and study directions as my life has been rather overbearing. This made it difficult to use this charging unit. The instructions are not set up very well, the printing is small, and although clearly marked, I have a hard time figuring out how it is supposed to work.

I managed to easily recharge the batteries my first time, and it only took about two hours tops, but as for the finer features of this charger, I just could not get a quick and easy understanding of how it worked.

So, as I continue to use this unit, I will update this review with information. I find most people I know have much less patience and understanding of items like this, so if I had a hard time figuring out the finer details of this charging unit, I know others will too.

If you have the time to really sit down and study the instructions, it will help get the full use out of this system. However, if you don't have time to do that at first, it is pretty easy to slap some batteries in and begin to recharge sufficiently at first until you can.

I am giving this four stars because of the small printing, and difficulty to figure out the system without having to spend a lot of time thinking and studying it at first. I do like that it is quick and small with a USB port in it so it is a four stars PLUS.

title: Great Sound- My Family Loves These

title: My Mouse Was Mouse-napped!
text:
When I first got the iHome Wireless Optical Network Mouse I was excited to have a mouse to use with my netbook that had storage in it for the little USB wireless receiver so that if I had to remove it, it won't get lost.

The tracking is accurate and the wheel works very well. I have seen precise operation and no more mousepad frustrations as my pointer gets all spastic around my screen. I have used this for a few months and the batteries worked very well.

I went to get my mouse one day and found out that it was mouse-napped! My son swiped it for his netbook and has held it captive ever since(batteries are still going strong)! He absolutely loves the mouse and he is a very fussy electronics person. He loves that it works on any surface and is precise. He has very large hands, and I have medium hands and both of us find this mouse comfortable and easy to use. It is a simple straightforward mouse without tons of bells and whistles, but it is solid.

I highly recommend this mouse!

title: Small But It Works!
text:
Compared to the Duracell Inverter we have, the quality of the battery hookups is a bit cheaper and thinner. However, this little inverter is adequate for the job of recharging ipods and cell phones. Although this unit says you have up to 175 watts, that is peak power. Consistent wattage is 130 so you want to be sure that what you have to use on this needs to be consistent with the 130 wattage instead. I would not go above that, as 175 is PEAK.

The unit is easy to use, you can plug it into the cigarette lighter in the car and it provides power to the USB port for easy recharging. There is a little fan on it and a light to indicates that it is working. I also tested out the battery usage, and it is great to use for campsites, or other areas where you might need to have a way to run simple 130 watt (or near it) electrical units or recharging of cell phones, etc.

The packaging was great- quick open and easy to get to. No struggling with plastic packages that are frustrating, etc.

This is a great simple inverter to have on hand for recharging of various USB friendly components. It worked quickly and efficiently.

title: Compact Yet Practical
text:
I have a variety of sizes of laptops from the larger Thinkpad to the smaller HP Elitebook. This backpack fits both of these beautifully- together or separately. I can also put my Kindle in its case in another pocket, my cell phone, glasses case, and a few books too.

There are places for pencils and even bottled water - a smaller bottle. I love the front pocket which makes it easy to access things I need to access quickly on days when I can not carry them in my pockets or coats. The straps are comfortable and don't hurt my shoulders like some of them do.

If you are carrying a huge load of books and supplies to class or other places, this might not be a bag for you. It is primarily for a smaller loads of books and supplies as well as the laptop, ipad or other tablets. This is not for the long day of carrying all of your books with you everywhere, like I have done in the past.

I have brought this with me on quite a few trips and found it really handy, but I only had a few books with me. I have also used it for other things like shopping trips at fiber festivals, and craft fairs too. It was helpful as I needed to have my laptop for later in the day so I could carry it with me, protected and separated from my other stuff.

This is not waterproof, but resistant, so if you have to walk a long way, you might want to put your electronic components and books in plastic bags inside the backpack, just to be extra careful.

All in all, I love this backpack because it is not over-sized and is perfect for those times when I want to carry my laptop and smaller other things, and don't need a large backpack for larger loads. It is handy and well divided for convenience. For larger all day loads- I suggest a larger backpack.

title: I like these, but my twelve year old not so much
text:
These headphones had a mixed reaction in my household. My daughter at twelve likes to spend some time with headphones on connected to her MP3 player. She has literal headphones. I showed her these headphones- or ear buds with loops on them- and asked if she would try them.

Her reaction was that she did not really like them because they had a suction and made it feel uncomfortable on her ears. They did stay in place very well and allowed her to do a lot of activities she could not do with her headphones on. She just couldn't see to get past the suction feeling.

I, on the other hand, like the tight fitting ear rubberized buds because they lock into the ears and close out interfering noise which I appreciate when working outside and trying to block out annoying noise like our next door drummer on days when I just don't want to hear it.

The earphones are comfortable and do stay in place well for activities like gardening and running. They are nice.

Some people might not be able to get past the suction feeling, but if you can, these are nice and will stay in place during active times.

title: Great for Some Situations
text:
We tried this internet adapter in quite a few ways in our home and came to the conclusion that it is a great lower cost alternative for large homes that want to have internet around but don't have the ability to have it around the house available for whatever reason.

This works well most of the time- performance is like that of our hardline and wi-fi connections. Download and upload times were the same and smoothness of operation was also good. The only problem we had was occasionally it would cease working for a minute.

It is hard to tell why this happened- it was erratic and not predictable. Heavy machinery in the house did not seem to affect it, nor did other fluctuations of power usage. However, that workability of the internet did get affected on a few occasions, but I am not sure why. It could have been our internet or it could have been the adapter.

All in all, it is a good less expensive alternative to running expensive wire around a large home to give access to the internet. It does take up an electrical outlet for each unit, however, which could be frustrating in some situations.

title: I Both Love and Hate This Thing Intensely- and it eats cards
text:
It is amazing how I could love and hate something so intensely as I feel for the Plantronics Discovery 925 Bluetooth Earpiece.

First of all, what I love
-The sound is fantastic- people hear me no matter where I am very well.
-Wind is dulled greatly
-Charges up quickly
-Comes with carrier case with enough power for one charge
-Fits my old Plantronics recharger
-Long talk time (about 4-5 hours min with full charge)
-Easy to carry
-Fits really well- for the first week, if I am lucky

Now what I hate
-The stupid case demagnetizes credit cards if it gets too close
-This ear piece only stays in my ear for the first few days of a new earpiece
-Once it is past a few days, this earpiece will NOT stay in my ear no matter WHAT I do

Yes, I know I am putting it on my ear correctly- the little U shaped tab goes down the ear canal and then I plug in the center silicone plug area into my ear canal. Like I said, the first few days of ownership and a new replacement pad, I can wear it for the entire day with no problems. Then after that, it gets worse so fast that I can not keep it in my ear.

I am so upset about this, because I really truly love this earpiece. The sound and clarity is fantastic, but when it pops out of my ear, I not only can not hear, it is dangerous if I am on the road when it happens too.

I have tried everything to get this to work in my ear. After a whole year of owning it, I am going to try elastic and then probably try another one eventually when I can swing it.

I can not believe how much I love and hate this thing at the same time!

title: I am NOT a Pro - so this is my review as such
text:
I am not a professional photographer. I can not go into great detail about all of the settings and fancy terminology that others can do so if that is what you are looking for, you won't find it in this review.

I AM an artist, however. I have spent the last 20 years taking accurate color specific photos which need to have accurate texture as much as possible for posting photos of my art in many different media.

When I was younger, I used to devour every inch of every tool that I had. I would learn it inside out and study it until it became like an extension of my hands. Unfortunately life has crowded out my time and ability to study things so I am forced to learn things off the cuff and fly by the seat of my pants.

This can be a problem, however, when it comes to having a very refined taste in photos with color and accurate texture, but only the time to run a quick set of photos.

When my Kodak camera broke, I was very upset. I had one of the nice Z series of Kodak cameras. Although low light photos were a nightmare, the color intensity and accuracy always delighted my senses- especially when taken outdoors.

The Canon G12 is both a huge step forward and a step back.

WHAT I LIKE

The step forward is that in low light, this camera is unbelievable! I can capture a photo in a pure dark room with a flash that I can not capture with most cameras in good artificial light.
There are a ton of settings with the G12. I can set them any way that I want to and that is really nice- except when I am in a hurry.

The auto setting is adequate, but not quite as colorful as I would have hoped.

The camera is solid and can stand on its own for self portraits and a timer.

The intense color setting does a great job in some instances

The camera is easy to hold and I have no problems adjusting to it

The back screen flipping around for self portraits is fabulous- I take a ton of those and this is a huge help.

The lens is FAST- retracts and goes out really quickly.

After not using the camera for a few moments, the lens does retract back again into the camera, but if you press the button lightly that takes photos, it comes out quickly again.

WHAT I DON'T LIKE
The camera can be a bit heavy and cumbersome when I am attempting to hold it with one hand out of necessity (when photographing my arm or hand).

The color capture of this camera is nice outside but in subdued light- photos look washed out. I am well acquainted with photo editing and do use it, but it is a bit more challenging with the G12.

The neck strap can sometimes get in the way when using one hand for photos- but it is a bit too heavy for a wrist strap- although I would like to have that security in case I drop it like I did my other camera.

The manual has to be printed out which annoys me to no end. For a camera this expensive, you would think they would include a manual. This makes it really hard to learn how to use this camera.

I know that some people feel you need to know photography rather than a manual, but I find that I would like to learn this tool, and am very frustrated without inclusion of a manual.

I have not used this camera at all near to its potential. As a point and shoot camera on auto- it is adequate and for most people would probably be just fine. For the other features, there is no manual at all, unless you print it out, which takes ink and paper.

I do love the camera so far, although the color saturation is not quite what I am used to, I will learn to work with it. The lovely low light capacity of this camera makes up for it, I guess.

I have given this four stars because of the lack of manual mostly and the auto mode not being quite as accurate as I would have hoped.

But the G12 is such a nice camera in other ways, it is still close to five stars despite my disappointments.

title: This stuff is weird, but it works- just be careful not to drop it
text:
This Splat stuff is really interesting. When I first got the jar, it was filled to the top with gooey shivery bright orange goo that is the same type of thing we used to get at the toy store and throw against the wall and watch it roll down.

This glob of goo, however, is supposed to be used to clean crevices in your car- speakers, dials, switches, vents, etc, that you can not easily clean otherwise. I did not use this goo right away, and almost a month later, I was surprised to see that the volume of the Splat goo went down by half. It had shrunk- and no one had taken any out either.

It is a bit weird to get used to using at first too, but it quickly becomes easy to manipulate into little places you want to clean.

When using it, it really does work. Little switches and indented areas that gather a lot of dirt and dust were cleaned well with no residue. The only problems I had were two:

---Don't drop it on the floor or it will grab every single stone, piece of dirt, or garbage it touches.

---Don't let it touch the windows or it will leave a smudge that you can only see at night when lights are coming at you and it can be very distracting. It does wash off relatively easily- but it takes a bit of work to get it back to the way it was.

All in all, however, I like Splat. As long as I don't drop it or let it touch any windows in the car, it does a good job. It is only useable for 50 uses and that is not a whole lot- but it is biodegradable. I have not used it up yet so I can not comment on the biodegradability of Splat.

title: Finally I can use my laptop without screaming!
text:
I love my laptop. It is so handy and easy to type on, but one thing has a tendency to drive me crazy- the touchpad. Although I like some of the features on the touchpad, it has a tendency to make so many mistakes or tracking errors that I often want to throw it out the window.

When I was given an opportunity to review and rate the Logitech Wireless Marathon Mouse 750, I was skeptical, but willing to try it.

I do not do well with most mice. They hurt my wrists and make me so frustrated that I prefer using my desktop keyboard touchpad which is perfect- has been for over 10 years.

I was so frustrated with my touchpad on my laptop, however, that I decided to give it a try anyway. What I discovered was so exciting that I actually LOVE using a mouse with my laptop.

WHAT DOES THIS MOUSE COME WITH?
Although the mouse comes with a CD with drivers and program on it, I downloaded it from the Logitech site finding it to be more current. There are two AA batteries that come with it and they are easy to put in the mouse. There is also a short instruction sheet, and a tiny little USB wireless antenna that plugs into the laptop USB.

HOW WELL DOES THIS MOUSE WORK?
I am very impressed with this mouse. I use my Kindle case to run the mouse on, but it will work with many surfaces. Tracking is very accurate and can be adjusted through the program. Plugging in was easy and the mouse worked instantly with no problems. The ergonomic mouse is the most comfortable mouse I have used. There is an ON OFF button and a side button for going forward and backward on web pages.

I can not comment on battery longevity as I have only had it for a month. This is supposed to last for three years. Only time will tell.

All in all, despite the fact that it is an extra piece to stuff in my laptop case, I really like this mouse. It is very comfortable, easy to use, and excellent in tracking performance. The buttons work well and the center wheel will magnify or reduce the size of the screen- internet pages are esp handy this way. You press once, and then a magnifier comes up. Clicking the wheel one direction will enlarge, and the other direction would decrease the size. Clicking again locks it into place.

The center wheel will also scroll the page down incrementally, or really fast if you spin it, making it much easier to control the page views. Two buttons on the left hand side will forward or reverse pages on the browser very easily using the thumb. There is a little button just below the center wheel which I have not figured out yet.

There is a press point right where the thumb rests which reduces windows allowing you to pick the application you want to use- you click on the window you want to change to.

You can completely change the settings on your mouse any way you want to, however so that you can have it the way you like it.

FINAL COMMENTS
I really love this mouse- and I can not stand most mice for computers- they really get to me. This one is so comfortable and easy to use, it has changed my opinion of mice- at least this one.
