title: I LOVE these buds!!
text:
I ordered the ‘1More True Wireless ANC in-Ear Headphones with Microphone’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

I have been looking for a true wireless earbud with true ANC which until recently have been pretty hard to find. I have a few different earbuds that claim “Noise Cancelling” but really they just “Isolate” the background noise. I have had these 1More earbuds for some time now. I have tried and tested several other brands both before and after receiving these and I have to say that these have become my Go-to earbuds for many reasons including their true ANC features. I will lay out my Pro’s and Con’s in no particular order.

Pro’s
* TRUE ANC - Yes these actually are true ANC earbuds with two different level settings. Is it the best ANC I have ever tried? No, but these 1More earbuds are the first True Wireless ANC “earbuds” I have tried and for me, I am impressed. The ANC does not work as well as some of the over-the-ear ANC headphones that I have, but that is to be expected. Again, for my use and in my opinion, the ANC functions beautifully for such small True Wireless earbuds.

* SOUND - These are the best sounding earbuds I own. The Bass is a bit on the heavy side but not to the point of becoming muddy which I appreciate. The Mids are well balanced and the Highs are crisp and clean.

* PRESENTATION - 1More did an incredible job on the presentation and unboxing experience with these.

* DESIGN - This may be my favorite thing about these earbuds. The case that both houses and charges the earbuds is a beautiful small metal matt black pill shaped case that not only looks great but feels nice and solid in the hands. The lid stays closed via a satisfying strong magnetic click which in my opinion is the best option and design. I have had others that use a flimsy plastic tab to click closed, and they tend to break after only a short time which then you need to use rubber bands to keep the lid closed so the buds charge and don’t fall out easily. Speaking of magnets, the buds snap satisfyingly into their respected right and left sockets and hold quite tight with no worries that they will fall out unless you take them out. The design of the buds themselves were not as impressive initially. They seemed to look a bit awkward compared to the other buds on the market which are more sleek. However after using them, I quickly changed my opinion. They poke out a bit from the ears and are not very “stealthy” so to speak, but I actually really like the look. Plus unlike other earbuds that are hard to figure out how they position into your ear, these 1More earbuds are as simple as popping the case open, pulling the bud out and putting it into your ear the same way it was positioned in the case.

* PAIRING - I had zero issues pairing these to my Android device. It was quick and easy and once paired, they will quickly and flawlessly connect every time I take them out of the case. I also love that everytime I take them out of the case, they pair back up using the same volume level that I used last when wearing them even if my media volume is turned all the way up or down before taking them out of the case.

* CHARGING - I love the fact that these not only charge via USB C but they will also charge wirelessly which really surprised me. While I am talking charging, these also retain a charge for several weeks which is most definitely a Pro. I have had other buds that will not hold a charge while stored after a week or so. With these 1More buds, I can give them a full charge and know that they are ready to go even after several weeks of no use.

* SINGLE BUD USE - I love that you can use just one bud at a time. It doesn’t matter which one you take out first and put in your ear - it will automatically pair and be ready for use as a single bud. I use this feature a lot as I will put just one in my ear while I lay on my side in bed.

* BLUETOOTH 5 - This is huge if you like to watch any streaming media. I have other earbuds that only offer Bluetooth 4.2 and there is an annoying sync issue with these. With the 1More earbuds I do notice a slight sync issue right at the beginning of the video for maybe a couple of seconds. After that, they sync up perfectly and continue to stay synced up throughout the video. If you happen to pause the video then unpause it again takes a few seconds to sync back up, but this really isn’t an issue considering that once synced, they stay that way during the rest of the playback.

Con’s

* FIT - Though they fit well and there are several bud tip and wing sizes included to choose from, I have not found the “perfect” combo to where they are totally secure in my ears. Don’t get me wrong here, they do fit well but after a while I find myself pushing them back into my ears. This is usually if I am, say just doing housework and bending over a lot. If I am just standing upright and walking, there are no issues.

* APP - there is a 1More APP for these and it works great for updating the firmware or changing the ANC or passthrough settings but other than that, there isn’t much to it.

* TOUCH CONTROL - Now I have had these for a while and I still struggle with the “conveniently located button” on each bud. Sometimes I can get them to work and other times I can’t. For me this is probably the biggest con although I did not take away a star rating for this because it very well may just be me. I love tech and usually am pretty good about figuring things out but the touch controls on these are a little tricky or perhaps just a little finicky.

To sum this lengthy review up, in my opinion the Pro’s far outweigh the Con’s. This is an amazing quality product and well worth the price. Are they better than some of the other Top brands out there? I really don’t know for sure, but so far in my experience, they are the best True Wireless ANC earbuds that I own! They look, feel solid and sound amazing! I hope that this was helpful.

title: Image quality is good but motion sensor is WAY to sensitive.
text:
I ordered the 'Geeni, Sentry Floodlight Security Camera with Motion Sensor, Intruder Alarm and Audio Video Recording' for review and would like to share my thoughts.

So I have had this camera for a while now and finally got it installed a couple of weeks ago and I am ready to share my thoughts and experience so far. This camera requires hard wiring which is why it took so long to get it installed. In my old home it was going to require me to get an extension cord, drill through my wall in the garage and plug it in, in the garage. This was much more work than I had anticipated. Now the new home already had normal motion sensor lights installed on switches, which made this more feasible for me to install. I took one of the motion sensor lights down and had to retrofit a new mount out of a piece of wood to cover the original hole left by removing the old light. This wasn't to hard to do and the Geeni light mounted with ease. Once installed and I turned the light switch on, it was ready to set up which took some time to do. I had to reset the device several times to get the App to set it up properly which was a quite pain however.

The camera itself is very good but so far I am not happy with all the notifications that I get which seem to be false alerts. It seems that everything seems to trigger this thing with absolutely no control as to how sensitive you would like the sensor to be. This is truly my main con with this device. I ended up turning notifications off on my mobile device which kind of defeats the purpose really.

Then there is the App which has thus far been pretty buggy. It has crashed many times and it is not so easy to find the "actual" activity that it seems to detect. Of all the motion activity that it detects, I would say that only 40% of it is relative. I do have the App set to just record everything (continuous) on the 128gb SD card which makes more sense seeing as there are so many false readings.

As for the good of this Geeni device, the image quality both during daytime and nighttime recording and playback is great. There is very little lag when accessing the footage which is surprising as I have other WiFi cameras that are painfully slow to connect and playback footage. This is probably my favorite feature (when the App doesn't crash).

Overall I do like this motion sensor and think that there is absolute value to it. I am however, really hoping for a firmware update which might help with some of the issues and allow you to adjust the sensitivity of the motion detection. Also it would be nice to have an easier way to track down and view "actual" activity rather than having to try and find that exact moment of capture. It seems to just tag a portion of footage, and you need to watch several minutes before you can find what it detected. You are also able to save the footage via the App, but doing so can take several days for it to show up on your mobile device which is another downside to this device.

I hope that this was helpful.

title: Ok camera for the price
text:
I ordered a ‘Digital Camera, 2.8 Inch HD Digital Camera Rechargeable Point and Shoot Camera, Students Cameras Kids Digital Camera Compact Cameras for Photography (Black)’ for review.
Pros:
• Inexpensive option for kids.
• Light and compact.

• Has an auto setting to make it easier to get started taking pictures
• It does have face detect.
• It has a multitude of settings to play with.

Overall, for under $40, it is an ok camera. It would make a good kid’s camera, that you would be able to replace without spending a fortune if they accidentally broke it. But, otherwise not one that we would use for other photo needs.

title: Amazing light!
text:
I ordered this 'D&O Lighting 180W Pro LED Panel Series V-Mount (120º Beam Angle)' for review.

Let me start off by making clear that I am not a professional photographer or videographer by any means. I am however aspiring to be both. My passion really is photography but I am learning more about video and someday I hope to turn my hobby into something where I can make money at it. With that said, I had the opportunity to order and review this incredible 180W LED light by D&O and I have to say that this is the best LED light I have ever used. I Truly never thought I would own such an incredible professional grade light. It's super bright and adjustable from 3200 - 5600K so you really have some good range of color there. The light comes with a nice padded case and also includes the AC power cord as well as a remote control which gives you all the functions that is available on the back of the light itself. The light is of incredible quality and everything packs nicely and is well protected in the included case. I had had zero issues with this kit but if I were to complain about anything it would be that it did not come with a C-Stand or anything to mount it to. I had to order a C-Stand just to be able use it, as it will not mount to a tripod. Another thing that I might mention is that the mounting adapter is made of plastic and does not mount very solid to the C-Stand Baby Pin. I worry that over time this plastic mount bracket may break. Since I have never owned anything like this before, I am not sure if this is how all lights of this type are, but I really would have thought that if this was made to mount onto a C-Stand with a "metal" Baby Pin, that the mounting bracket itself would also be metal and made to fit tight and secure to this pin. I have had several times where this light would spin while mounted and I was afraid it was going to break off as the light is pretty heavy. This may be my fault as I am still learning how it works and I have gotten better at getting it tight and secure. Plastic vs metal and metal is always going to win right? Overall however, I am super happy to own such an incredible light and I hope to take my photography to the next level. I do feel that for what you get, it's a bit pricey, but not being familiar with what other kits like this cost, I honestly don't know for sure. I just know for myself, I would have a hard time justifying the price until I was making more money from my "hobby". I hope that this was helpful.

title: This thing really packs a punch!
text:
I ordered the 'Divoom Pro Premium 40W 12Hour Playtime TWS Portable Bluetooth Speaker, Water Resistant for Indoor/Outdoor Use(Black)' for review.

I am a sucker for portable Bluetooth speakers and I had to give this one a go and I must say that I was not disappointed (well maybe just a little - continue reading .....). My first impression when opening the box was that this thing is heavy for how small it is. The speaker itself is a nice size with a beautiful basic design. The controls are really simple and feel very tactile. They are easy to feel which button you are pressing. The speaker comes with really nice braided type cables. One for charging and one Aux cable. Both are quite short however which really isn't a big deal. Especially for the fact that once you fully charge this beast, it'll give you a "claimed" 12 hour play time. I have not pushed this limit yet as I have only used it for a couple hours at a time but I have not recharged it yet. Although this speaker has a water resistant rating of IPX5, I have not tested this, but from how this is built, I would feel confident that I could take it outside and not worry about a little Oregon rain or being splashed on by the kids playing in the sprinklers. The really cool thing about this speaker is that you can charge your device while listening to it via the USB type A port.

There are only a couple of cons with this speaker in my opinion. First con - Where is the USB C charging? I always have to point this out with new products. This charges via Micro USB. USB C should be integrated and standard in all new products in my opinion. Second con is that when watching videos there are sync issues. So if you are planning to use this for watching anything video streaming, it gets pretty annoying. This is a new product, and I would think that both USB C and Bluetooth 5.0 should be a standard these days. With that said my overall impression with this Divoom speaker, is that for listening to music it's a beast. It pairs up easily with not much of a delay at all once it has been initially paired to your device. Turn the power on and it'll pair back up fast and ready to play. I also like the fact that if you have two of these (I wish I did) they can sync together to produce a much fuller stereo experience. Maybe down the road I will get a second one and update this review with how well that feature works. I hope that this was helpful!

title: Solid drive.
text:

text:

So far I have used it with the USB type A ports as well as the USB C ports on my machines and it seems to function quite well. I am really not sure of the increased speeds with the USB C but it does transfer files from both my SD and TF cards seemingly faster than my older card reader. There have been a couple times that this reader has not been recognized by my PC but I blame that on issues that I have had for some time with card readers and some of my USB ports. My Chromebook which is much newer has not had these issues at all however there are times that my Thunderbolt 3 compatible Laptop has not recognized this reader, but it does that sometimes with Thunderbolt 3 external drives sometimes. Overall I love the size and options this little guy has and think that it's a great value for the $$. I hope this helps.

title: Great gimbal with a few issues.
text:
[[VIDEOID:139d076ab53a69b4c9863743d4ea0df8]] I ordered the ‘MOZA AirCross 2 Stabilizer 3-Axis Handheld Lightweight Powerful Gimbal for Camera Up 7Lb Intuitive Control Panel Intelligent Features Advanced Shooting Modes 12h Battery Life Beyond Your Imagination’ for review and would like to share my thoughts.

First off I would like to let it be known that this is my very first camera gimbal. With that said, understand that I am not very savvy when it comes to gimbals. I am fairly new to filmmaking and videography. Now that you know that this will not necessarily be a super technical review, I will share some of what I have experienced thus far with this gimbal.

I ordered this originally to use with my Canon 60D DSLR. From the Moza website, I did find the 60D listed as a compatible camera, so I figured that this gimbal would work which it, it but not exactly how I had expected. The 60D is a DSLR camera which is a bit on the heavy side and I did find it a bit tricky at first to get the camera to balance correctly. Once balanced, the gimbal did work, though I could tell it struggled. I have since read and watched many reviews with even lighter cameras, and users have stated the same thing. The Moza AirCross 2 is rated for a max weight of 7lbs and my 60D comes in at 2.7lbs with the EF 17-40mm L lens, so there really shouldn’t be an issue. Yet when checking the gimbal it showed all axis at or near 100% which means that the gimbal is working hard to handle the camera weight even though it’s nowhere near the max weight advertised.

Since then, I have upgraded my camera to the Canon 90D (yes another DSLR). It’s slightly lighter but not by too much. I am still using the EF 17-40mm L lens which, in-of-itself is a fairly heavy lens. It’s probably the heaviest yet the best glass that I own. This has made little to no difference in the Moza AirCross2 working hard on all axis however it does seem to handle this set up a bit better. See attached video and note that I had added a small microphone to the camera which turned out not being set up right on the new camera. So the balance was slightly off for the recording yet the gimbal worked. There was some slight shaking in the footage but overall I was happy with the performance. Again, being an ameture at this I am just happy to have a working gimbal haha.

Now for some other issues. First I cannot get the 90D mounted and balanced to where the Roll axis bar won’t hit the Pan axis bar when trying to do a full Roll. This is a real bummer. I am not sure if it’s something that I am doing wrong or this is just the way it is with this particular camera. Second issue I have had is that the Moza AirCross2 comes with a plethora of cables to hook up to your various cameras. It was trial and error for me on both cameras to find which one I was “supposed” to use. Eventually it seems that both (60D and the 90D) seem to do better with the Micro USB cable yet again, I am not positive which I am “supposed” to be using. I could not find any documentation that stated what cable should go with what camera. Third, I thought that I would have more control over the camera with this gimbal. I understand not having all the options available for the 60D, but I figured there would be more options that I could control the camera with on the 90D. All I can seem to do via the gimbal on the 90D is control the video record button. For the 60D I was able to get the camera to autofocus and take a picture but that's about it. Even with the very nice App that you can download for the gimbal, there isn’t a whole lot that I can get to work to control either camera. Again I would have thought the 90D would have been more compatible seeing as it has both WiFi and Bluetooth capabilities. I do plan to do more research as there may be settings on the camera that I need to enable.

On the plus side of things, this is a nice quality gimbal. It is a bit heavy with my camera mounted but it feels solid. The App is nice although I have not used it to its full potential as of yet. The included foam hard case is very nice and keeps everything safe and tidy. Everything fits snug. Some parts more than others but nothing is going to be flopping around inside. The footage taken with this gimbal is so much smoother than if I were to try and take it all hand-held. Even running looks great (to my untrained eye). Again see attached video.

Overall, I am both disappointed and quite happy with this gimbal. Disappointed that it’s not all I had hoped for, yet very happy to actually have a working gimbal. It’s been a huge learning curve for me and I really want to give this gimbal a 5 star rating. However I feel that with the advertised max weight being an issue for me and others much more savvy, that takes one star away. Plus the fact that the Roll axis bar hits the Pan axis bar when the camera and gimbal are balanced is annoying. For that I won’t dock a star, as this may be user error. I would just say that if you own a mirrorless camera then this would be great for you. If you own a heavier DSLR, you may want to look at spending a little more for one better rated for the extra weight.

title: Great set of re-chargeable batteries with Charger
text:

title: Functionality not thought out well
text:

title: Small, bright but does get hot.
text:
I ordered the 'SOKANI X21 Pro X21Pro Bi-Color LED Video Light Portable Pocket-Sized 3200-6500K 122 LED Bulbs OLED Screen Build-in 3000mAh Battery for DSLR Sony, Nikon, Canon, iPhone Video Vlogging and Selfies' for review.

I have several LED lights similar to this one and this Sokani is the smallest and most compact of them all. With that said, it's not the brightest that I have, nor does it have RGB as some of the others I have which is sort of a con to me since I have experienced the others. However for what this light is, it is a great little LED light. The OLED screen is a great feature that not all LED lights offer. The OLED screen allows you to easily see and adjust the brightness level, color temp (3000k - 6500k), and see the battery level. The included padded soft carry case, cold shoe mount, USB type C (Yay!) charging cable, and plastic color filters all make this little LED even more valuable. The color filters are nice however they don't quite fit into the soft case without bending up the corners. This was a bit of a disappointment as they should have been sized small enough, and maybe with a little plastic case to keep them protected and together when stuffing them into the soft case. (see attached images) They attach to the LED light with the installed magnetic diffuser. This is another great feature however I have other lights that are RGB so there is no need for plastic color filters on those lights.
The only cons with this little light, besides the color filters not fitting very well into the soft case, is the fact that this thing gets pretty hot after being on for a while. I don't know if this could eventually cause issues if left on for the full advertised 1.8 hours of battery life, as I usually only run it for 20-30 min at a time. Overall this is a great little light and though I have other lights in my collection, I find myself using this one quite a bit. It really is a great value.

title: Great quality. Works with Canon 60D.
text:
[[VIDEOID:13857efa3820e6eb7b02a0a8943823dd]] I am reviewing the ‘AODELAN Camera Wirless Shutter Release Timer Intervalometer for Canon EOS 800D, 200D, 80D,750D, 650D, 600D,1300D, 1200D, 90D, M6 Mark II, 6D Mark II, 7D Mark II; Fujifilm X-T3; Olympus E-M1 Mark II‘

I have been looking for a wireless shutter release for my Canon 60D for quite some time now but haven’t been able to decide what kind to get. There are quite a few out there from basic to full featured like this one seems to be. Most of what I shoot is landscape or product photos but I would like to do more in the line of Time-Lapse, Wildlife and Night Photography. This Aodelan looks to have a bit of everything that I needed. So far I have only used it for product photography and I used it briefly with a Time-Lapse. During that little bit of testing I found that I could only set the remote to take a total of 199 images and set intervals. I set it for 199 shots at 10 second intervals but was cut short by rain hitting my gear and only ended up with 149 shots. (See attached video) There really should be a way to set it for much longer as 199 shots compiled into a Time-Lapse is only a few seconds long. I am still learning this device so hopefully I can figure out if 199 image is truly the limit. If so, this is very disappointing..

As for the Wireless Shutter remote, it functions perfectly for my needs. I am able to set the shot up and wirelessly trigger my shutter with the remote from quite a distance, which will be perfect for capturing the Hummingbirds that frequent my kitchen window feeder. I will be able to set up the shot outside and trigger the shutter from inside the house when the Hummingbirds are in position. Night photography will also be fun to try, as I can now remotely trigger the shutter using Bulb mode without causing any camera shake. You can also use this kit wired and only need to plug the Transmitter into the Remote port on the camera, but personally I will mainly be using this kit Wirelessly.

The quality and features of this kit are really nice. Both the Transmitter and Receiver are made of what seems to be a good quality plastic. Both devices take 2XAA batteries which were not included. Battery life seems to be good thus far and I would imagine that my newly installed batteries should last a good long time.

Though I am still learning this kit, I did notice that when trying to take continuous shots, it seems to limit the camera from shooting as fast as it is capable of. This isn’t a huge deal (because this isn’t what I plan to use this kit for) but I thought it worth mentioning.

Other than the 199 shot limit when shooting Time-Lapse I am very pleased with the overall performance and quality of this kit and think it is good value for the money.

*Update - I just found the setting that will allow unlimited shots during the "Timer" mode. This will allow you to take as many shots as desired for Time-Lapse photography. This is really nice though I do wish you could limit it to a higher number than 199. How about 999? lol

title: Very small and compact.
text:
[[VIDEOID:3ce16a8b55f3aad3783525af27494ea6]] I ordered the ‘Fotowelt AIR 36 Channels UHF Wireless Lavalier Microphone System Built in Battery Wireless Mics Compatible for Canon Nikon Sony Panasonic D/SLR Camera,XLR Camcorder & Smartphone (70m-229foot)’ for review.

I have been on a quest to find a good quality wireless Lav Mic because my built in camera mic just doesn’t cut it for audio when not right on top of the camera (Canon 60D). I do have a couple external mics that mount to the camera, but if I am shooting at a distance, these just don’t do as well as I would like to capture voice. This Fotowelt Air looked like it might be the answer I was looking for.
When I received this mic kit, I was blown away at how small these are. Both the receiver and transmitter, along with the cold shoe mount, Type C charging cable (Yay), Lav mic with attached cable, plus cables for both the camera and mobile phone come packed into this small hard shell case. This case fits easily into my camera bag which really impressed me. Both the transmitter and receiver charge via the included USB C cable and only take a couple hours (if that) to fully charge. I love USB C! The Lav mic cable is a nice length and the clip is very strong. So far in my use I have not needed to change the channels on the transmitter/receiver. I have only used channel 1 although there are 36 total channels to choose from if you run into any interference.
*I might have needed to change the channel during my test video that I attached, because I notice some strange audio fluctuation. However that may have just been the very high wind gusts*
The indoor testing was fine and I have not noticed any issues during indoor recording just using channel 1. So far this set has performed quite well without any drop outs, and the voice recordings sound pretty clear. Even in the high wind gust video, you can still hear my voice although you can also hear the wind quite a bit. I won’t hold that against this kit as even my good external mics do this in the high wind, even with a dead cat installed. Speaking of dead cats, this kit did not come with one unfortunately. The volume can be adjusted on both the transmitter and receiver which is nice and it can help to bing the volume levels to where they need to be. In most of my work so far I keep them both set to 13 which might be a bit much, but I can adjust if need be in the video editing software. In my attached video, I did not adjust the levels via the editing software. Overall I love this kit for the size/weight and the quality of the devices so far. The built in batteries can last for several hours and can take a pretty quick charge on the go with a portable power brick. I really feel that these are a pretty good value for what you get, although I have not tried many Lav kits to really compare.

title: Won't fit my very large 17" gaming laptop

title: You can charge 8 electronics all at the same time.
text:
I ordered this Oviitech Surge Protector Power Strip Tower 5 AC Outlets with 3 USB Charging Ports(3.1A Total), 4 Feet Cord Wire Extension, White and Gray, ETL Listed to review. Having multiple Power strips that lay flat, I was curious to see how this would measure up. My thoughts are below:
• This standing power strip is well made.
• It feels durable and the cord is thick and well protected in rubber.
• The cord works well on our crafting table, as it has 5 plug in outlets and 3 USB ports. We can have multiple items such as a sewing machine, heat press, die cut machine, magnifying lamp, etc all plugged in it at the same. Not to mention you can charge your phone also at the same time.

• The distance between the outlets is wide enough that you can actually fit three plugs on one side and two on the other. So many times, power strips are made with outlets that are too close together so you only get half use out of them.
• The base is sturdy, and it sits flat on the table/desk. Does not easily tip over.
• It has worked exactly as it is described.
• The quality is worth the price point. Probably exceeds it.
Overall, this is well made functional standing tower power strip. Well worth it’s cost. We will most likely be buying another for our den/office.

title: Nice sound and great value.
text:
I ordered the 'MIDOLA Wireless Earbuds Bluetooth 5.0 Stereo Headphones TWS in-Ear Headset with Charging Case Built-in Mic for Phone Pad Sport Black' for review and would like to share my thoughts with some pros and cons.

Pros:
1- Sound - For the price, these sound pretty amazing. Bass isn't real heavy, Mids sound great as do Highs.
2- Size - The size of the case is really nice.
3- Pairing - They pair up very easily and once paired to your mobile device you can put them back in the case and when your ready to use them again, take them out of the case and they immediately pair back up and start playing whichever media app you were playing last and start playing. No need to repair and choose an app then pick a song. I love this feature!
4- USB C charging!! This makes me very happy.
5- Looks - Yes they look similar to the "other" brand but I actually like this look much better.
6- Touch Controls - They just work for me. The touch controls take some getting used to but with this Midola brand, once you figure out how to work them, the touch controls work great.
7- Magnets - The headphones stay put in the case with magnets. Even though the case does not click shut (I think the lid also has magnets to help keep it closed too) if your case lid pops open, the buds stay put and don't easily fall out of the case.
8- Price - These are an incredible value for the price!!

Cons:
1- Sync Issues - Even though these use the Bluetooth 5.0 tech, which should have no issues with syncing, I have yet to have these work for any streaming video media. There is maybe 1/10th of a second delay. Now this isn't huge and it's a big difference from Bluetooth 4.2, but it gets annoying to try and watch a whole movie or TV show with that tiny delay.
2. Battery Life - Though it's not really huge as I normally don't listen to my headphones for more than an hour or so, 3.5-4 hours advertised battery time is not the greatest.
3- Bass - As I said in the pros, the Bass isn't the greatest and the only reason I list this as a con here is the fact that they claim in the description "deep bass". It's decent but I would not personally consider it 'deep bass".

Overall in my opinion the Pros far outweigh the Cons. With that said, I really think these are an incredible value for a pair of bargain Wireless Earbuds with decent sound quality, USB C charging and Bluetooth 5.0

title: Nice sound. Interesting design.
text:
I ordered the 'Nomodo U Wireless Wearable Bluetooth Speaker, Rechargeable and Portable' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts and experiences.
First off, out of the box this Bluetooth Wireless Speaker not only looks interesting but it is beautiful. I say interesting because I have never had a Wireless Speaker like this, and I wonder where would I use it and would it be practical. Well after some time with this device I must first report that it really does sound amazing. The sound is clean and immersive. It is hard to describe the incredible sound sensation while wearing it. It is almost as if you have speakers floating on either side of your head (pointing directly to your ears) and it is nothing like I have experienced before but it is pretty cool. I have been trying to think of how this Speaker would actually fit into my life. It's not like you are wearing headphones that only you can hear. While wearing this speaker, everyone else around you can hear it too but it's just not as immersive as it is to you. It's hard to describe, but what I will say is that it really is an incredible experience. If the volume is down low you can still hear your surroundings yet when you crank it up, surprisingly your surrounding sounds seem to disappear. Personally I have decided that this would be best worn while alone in your home while doing simple household chores. Like doing dishes or folding laundry. The Nomodo U speaker stays put pretty well for the most part due to the rubber neck pad, yet if you are constantly bending over or doing anything where you are moving around a lot and twisting your head and body, it tends to need re adjusted. Sitting in bed listening to Music or listening to an audio book works really well with this device as long as you wont be disturbing your partner. As for watching movies, for me this really doesn't work. I can't find anywhere where it says what version of Bluetooth this is using but I don't think it is Bluetooth 5.0 unfortunately. There are noticeable sync issues and this just gets annoying. Speaking of the Bluetooth, it connects/pairs effortlessly to all of my devices and that is a bonus. I am disappointed however that it uses Micro USB (the cable is included btw) for charging. With this being a new device it should have USB Type C. I always have to mention this with any new devices. Call quality is acceptable. Those on the other end can hear you just fine, as long as you are not in a loud environment. This is pretty typical with most wireless headphones. Overall I do love this device and think it is a great value for what it is.

title: Bluetooth 4.2 and no true ANC
text:
I am reviewing the ‘TruSound TruWireless Noise Cancelling Earbuds | True Wireless Earbuds with Charging Case for Buds and Phone | Comfortable, Secure Fit | Immersive Stereo Sound, Deep Bass | Easy Touch Control Operation’.
Based on my experience thus far I would like to share my thoughts.

Pros:
1- The sound is decent but compared to other Wireless Earbuds that I have tried, these are pretty average.
2- The case is rechargeable via the included 18650 battery. This allows you to have extra 18650 batteries on hand which is an interesting feature.
3- It comes with extra ear tips.
4- It comes with a mini USB cable and even a USB type A to Mini USB adapter.
5- Aesthetically the earbuds look nice, feel comfortable and don’t protrude much when wearing them.
6- They stay in place quite well and do not randomly fall out.
7- Earbuds are held in place magnetically when in the case charging.
8- They pair up real fast and very easy. I have had no issues at all with pairing.

Cons:
1- I ordered these based on the description stating “active noise reduction is also a standout feature of TruSound ear buds, ensuring a distraction-free audio experience”. I took this as they had ANC or Active Noise Control. This is not the case. These “isolate” the outside sounds via the ear tip inserted into the ear canal. If you get the right tip fit, they do “isolate” the outside sounds but just not as expected.
2- No USB type C. In my opinion all new devices should have USB C charging.
3- The case is a bit bulky due to the fact that it uses the 18650 battery.
4- The case is plastic and uses two plastic tabs to snap the lid closed. The design makes it really hard to open the case once it’s snapped shut. I am worried that I will break the plastic tabs at which point I would need to use a rubber band to keep the lid closed.
5- The Stand-By time is not the greatest. I fully charged the 18650 battery with my own charger when I first got the Earbuds. I used the Earbuds briefly while initially testing them and when I went back a couple of weeks later to try them again, the battery was already dead. I have other earbuds that have this same issue. I should be able to fully charge my earbuds, keep them in my backpack for a few weeks and have them ready to go when I want to use them.
6- No IPX rating? Pretty much all of the newer Earbuds these days have some kind of waterproof rating. It’s not advertised so I am not really sure if they are.
7- No Bluetooth 5.0? These have Bluetooth 4.2+EDR which isn’t bad, but there are sync issues when watching YouTube, Netflix ect. It’s not bad, but it’s noticeable and I could not use these to watch videos for too long.

Overall these TruSound Earbuds are average, and I feel that compared to the flooded market of True Wireless Earbuds these are a bit overpriced. With that said, I do like these but, I do feel there could be some improvements made that would ultimately increase the value.

title: Great little Docking Station.
text:
I ordered this 'LENTION USB C Docking Station with 100W Power Delivery, 4K HDMI, Gigabit Ethernet, USB 3.0, USB 2.0 and Aux Adapter for MacBook Pro (Thunderbolt 3), New Mac Air, Surface Go, More (Space Gray)' for review.
I originally ordered this for my wife to use with her new Surface Pro however her employer had already ordered her one in, so I was happy to put this one to good use. I have been using it now for several weeks, mainly on my Chromebook so that I can connect to my TV via the HDMI port. I have had zero issues with that and connecting to my PC for extra USB ports. Again, no issues. The only complaint I have is that it states that it's got a 100W Power Delivery so I would think it would do Fast Charging. However no matter what I have tried, it won't fast charge my mobile phone. The Lention Docking Station is very well built and looks great. The USB C to USB C cord that is included is really nice and it's a perfect length to use for my PC and plugging into the back of the case. Other docks similar to this one usually have very short cables that are more for Laptop use. The base mount is nice and heavy so that it doesn't get top heavy when plugging a few cables into it. It also has a nice rubber grip bottom so it doesn't slide around on my table. Overall I think this is a really good quality device that has great value. *On a side note, I have not tried the Gigabit Ethernet nor the 3.5mm Audio, so can't comment on how well those work.

title: Excellent value camera mic!
text:
[[VIDEOID:331807d8d8d087a6f9d617912336adb7]] I ordered this ‘Deity V-Mic D3 Pro High SNR Super-Cardioid Directional Shotgun Microphone with Rycote Shockmount for DSLRs, Camcorders, Smartphones, Tablets, Handy Recorders, Laptop，Bodypack Transmitters, Wind Shield’ for review.
Let me start by saying that I have never owned an external camera mic as I never really had much use for one until recently, so I don’t have anything to compare this one too other than the on board built-in mic from my Canon 60D. When I first received the D3 Pro I was totally blown away by what looked, and felt like a quality device. The included hard case is really nice (see attached images) as is the included Deadcat or Wind Muff, although it is a bit tricky to install as it fits so snug. The difference between the onboard built-in mic and the D3 Pro is like night and day (see attached sound check video). In the video I state that I have the “Volume” on the mic set to 4 and it’s actually called the “Gain” control which was actually set to 5. Even in the slightly breezy conditions during the outside test I did not use the LCF or Low-Cut Filter, which can reduce light wind noise. The Mic has LCF settings for 75Hz, 150Hz and Off. The D3 Pro also has a built in rechargeable battery via the USB C port on the side which is nice and much appreciated. I don’t want to carry around extra batteries and these days I much prefer USB C charging on newer devices. I can’t really report on the battery life as of yet, because I have only done a few short video sessions and have yet charged it since the initial full charge once I got it.
Overall I am really impressed with this D3 Pro and feel like this has absolute value for the price and I highly recommend it.

title: USB C port won't charge my phone.
text: I ordered this 'USB C Hub,MAOZUA 6 in 1 Adapter with 3 USB 3.0 Ports,SD/TF Card Reader, Portable Aluminum Hub with USB-C PD 3.0 for MacBook, iMac, and More Type C Devices' for review. So far before today, I have only used this device as a portable SD card reader for my PC and Chromebook. For that purpose it has worked flawlessly however today while writing this review I tested the charging capabilities of the USB C port. It is supposedly capable of quick charging yet it does not charge my phone at all. I have tried it with different cables on both PC and Chromebook but it still won't charge. I tested the the same cables on another card reader type device and it worked just fine. The USB Type A ports work fine for data and charging however the USB type A ports have weak charging according to my Note 8. I am disappointed to find this out just now but as I said before, I have only been using this as an SD card reader for the past few weeks. For that purpose it works fine and I will continue to use it as such. unfortunately if I need to charge, I will have to find another solution. Overall, I was pleased with the "reader" part of this device however I think I just got a dud regarding the charging capabilities of this device.

title: Nice and bright for size!
text: I ordered this 'ANDYCINE R1 Pocket Size RGB On Camera Video Light 360Colors,Dimmable 2500-7000k Range Led Video Light,7 Common Scenario Simulations with Premium Aluminum Alloy Shell,3600mAh Built in Battery' to review and use in my photography arsenal. I have been in need of some of these lights for a long time and this little guy is super bright for it's size. It's easily pocket-able and the battery holds up a long time. It will last at least a couple of lighting sessions before needing to be recharged. Speaking of recharging, I did notice that when plugged into a fast charger that I use for my phone and other lights of this kind, it didn't charge at all with no indication that anything was happening. It wasn't until I plugged it into my USB 3.0 port on my computer that it showed charging. At which point it charged up pretty quick. There must be an over volt protection build in so that is good news that I didn't fry the thing. It's got a great range of color temperatures and other modes that flash different colors (see attached video), however I mostly wanted, and use this for adding some light to my pictures - which it does well. It also includes a little cloth pouch to store it in, which I love to see included with these lights for a little extra protection when storing. Also included is a camera hot-shoe mount and short USB C cable for charging. Overall this light is a great value for what it is and especially for the size. This one is about half the size of some of the others like this that I now own.

title: Quality leather and snaps.
text: I ordered the 'Gydandir Leather Cable Straps Cable Ties Cable Organizers Cord Management for Organizing USB Cable Headphone Wires, 2 Sizes 5 Colors' for review. So far I am pretty impressed with the quality of materials used. The leather and snaps are a nice quality and the stitching is flawless. They do take a little time trying to get the cables wrapped just right so that straps fit correctly. Some have mentioned that the smaller strap is useless as it wouldn't fit anything, but if you wrap the smaller cords right, they fit just fine (see attached images). The nice thing is that if you can't get the smaller straps to fit, then just use two smaller straps (snapped together) to wrap your cord. Overall these are a nice way to clean up my cord drawer and they look really classy. I would say these are a great value if you want something nicer than a bunch of rubber bands holding your cords together haha.

title: Works well with my wife's Surface
text:
My wife has been using this Uiosmuph Wireless Bluetooth Mouse for about a week now. She has a Surface Pro. She is continually on her Surface when she is working, crafting, reading emails, etc. the mouse came charged and she still has not needed to charge it. It connects both wireless with a USB Bluetooth Dongle and through direct Bluetooth if your device is Bluetooth capable. My wife has tried both connections and has not felt that there were any significant issues with either. The mouse connected easily to her Surface. The Bluetooth capability without the dongle is a bonus when using it with the Surface, as her Surface Pro has only has one USB port.
The ergonomic design fits nicely in her hand. The lilac purple color is very pretty. It moves well over a mouse pad. The dongle snaps into the bottom of the mouse versus in the mouse battery area. It can at times, trip up the mouse if it is not in properly or comes loose. It does not snap as securely as she would like it to and anytime the mouse is dropped or even at times when she lifts the mouse from the mousepad the dongle will fall out. This may cause you to easily loose it. She has experienced a few skips when it is connected via Bluetooth, not sure if it is because of the dongle placement on the bottom of the mouse or the connectivity. The right and left buttons click smoothly and with a light touch. The mouse wheel has functioned well for her.
It will auto shut off when not using it for a period of time and you have to sometimes run your finger over the optics to get it to work again. For $15, it is not of exceptional quality, but the quality does meet its price point. Overall, this mouse functions well for my wife’s purposes.

title: Love that it covers both my Surface and Keyboard
text: I ordered this ACdream Microsoft Surface Pro 7 Case, Multiple Angle Viewing with Pocket Business Cover Case in Blue for review and use with my Surface Pro 7.  It took me a bit to figure out how to put my surface into it to allow it to stand up when working with it.  At first, I kept taking my Surface in and out of it to use it.  Directions do not come on the case.  It was in viewing the photo in the description, I realized the elastic bands on the bottom two corners slide over the stand on the back of the Surface and not over the screen.  Once I figured that out it, I no longer need to take it on or off to use my surface.  I like the aesthetic look of this case.  The Exterior has a soft vinyl feel and the texture does not look quite like it does in the photos, but it reminds me of a worn pair of jeans.  The inner fabric is very soft, it is not abrasive and does not scratch my Surface.  I really love that it fits over the keyboard as well and does not hinder it’s use.  It is not padded super well, it most likely would not protect the Surface from a drop or fall.  I just slide mine into a padded case before traveling with it.  Overall the quality and workmanship meet the price point and it functions very well for my purposes.

title: Solid product!
text: I ordered the 'BRAYDEN 66W USB-C Laptop Charger, GaN Tech PD 3.0 + USB-A Dual Ports Compact Foldable Plug Type-C Charging Adapter, Compatible for Laptops, MacBook, iPad Pro, iPhone, Galaxy, Pixel and More - Black' for review as I like to have extra charging bricks on hand, as my kids tend to lose them all to often. So far this one has done a fabulous job at quick charging anything we plug it in to such as mobile phones, battery packs, Nintendo Switch  and even my Chromebook. Pretty much anything that takes a USB C plug will charge with this guy. This one won't go to the kids for a very long time as I have replaced my favorite old brick with this one, and don't plan to let this one go for a long time. This one just performs and feels like a very premium brick and I think it is going to last longer than most. Overall I am vary happy with this one!!

title: Solid quality and construction.
text: I ordered the 'KAUKKO Vintage Casual Canvas and Leather Rucksack Backpack, 1Black' for review as I am always looking for an extra, durable and functional backpack for every day abuse. This one has held up quite well and feels of quality materials. The zippers are solid and function smoothly and just feel like they will hold up to many years of abuse. Though this backpack can hold a smaller laptop I would not consider this one to be optimal for doing so as it is not really padded as I would expect for laptop use. I would consider this one to be more for packing for a weekend trip or taking on a day hike. I have used it off and on now for several weeks and love that when not in use, it can easily be folded up and stashed on a shelf or even in a drawer, as when empty it really doesn't take up much space. I guess I would describe it like a backpack duffel bag with several pockets that are all quite functional. I do appreciate the strong magnet latches that keep the bag closed even when stuffed pretty full. The leather zipper pulls are a nice touch and all the leather feels to be of nice quality. Overall I am very pleased with the quality, durability and looks of this backpack and feel that it is a great value.

title: Really is a huge tote
text:
I ordered this ZoneFoker tote for Women, leather and nylon shoulder bag for review. My wife is a road warrior and needs something to carry-on that is bigger than a purse. The bag itself is made from a nylon material that has slight shine to it. The base and details are in a smooth brown leather. The workmanship on it is good. The handles seem well secured, which is good because this bag is quite big and I image one could really load it full of heavy books and files.

There are only two interior pockets both the full size of the bag. One with a velro enclosure that is has a padded feel to contain your laptop and one that is also nylon but not padded. My wife uses a surface, so this bag is a bit too big for her purpose. The Surface slides around in the bag since it is not a snug fit. This bag also needs more pockets. And some smaller pockets.

The overall look of the bag is nice, although it is pretty basic. The quality meets the price point. And it definitely is huge. I believe instead of my wife using this bag for travel, we will use it for my daughter to use when she has a sleepover. It would nicely fit her clothing, small blanket and toiletries. And she could slide her tablet in the protect for a little more protection.

title: Works for Tablet usage only,  Keyboard can not be attached with this case on
text:
I ordered this OtterBox Symmetry Folio Series Case for use as my wife has a Surface Pro 7. The Pros and Cons are listed below:

Pros:
* The case fits the surface tablet quite snugly
* The back is clear, which allows you to showcase the Surface Pro 7's sleek encasement
* It has a fold-able cover that can be manipulated into a stand for the Surface when using it like a tablet
* The case's sides are made of a thick rubber that would provide some protection for the corners of your Surface
* The case base would provide decent protection

Con's:
* You can not use the case with the attachable Surface Keyboard, so you are limited in using your Surface only as a
tablet.
* The clear back scratches and marks easily. giving it a worn and unclear view of the back of your surface.
* The fold-able cover is not very good protection for your screen, it is relatively thin
* Because the cover is relatively thin, it is not really a stable stand when folded and the tablet is on it

This case does not really live up to the OtterBox brand. It seems quite an inconvenience to not be able to use your Surface keyboard without taking the case off. You would be limited in only being able to use your Surface as a Tablet. For some this maybe acceptable. But for my wife who travels extensively and uses her Surface more than her desktop for work, that just is not feasible. Plus, having to buy additional protection for your screen is also a negative aspect. I just would not trust this cover alone to keep the screen safe from breakage.

Overall, my wife will not be using this case on her Surface.

title: Nontraditional but does have benefits.
text:
I ordered the 'Tripp Lite 3 Outlet Surge Protector with USB, Detachable Wall Outlet Surge Protector, 6 USB Ports, 6 ft. Cord, 540 Joules, Black, $50, 000 Insurance (TLP366CUBEUSBB)' for review and would like to share my thoughts.
First off this Surge Protector is very odd looking. Second there is only two actual plugs to use unless you take off the top piece which ads the 4 extra USB plugs. I ended up doing this to give me a total of three outlet plugs to clear out some of the more bulky plugs that were taking up space on my normal power strip. Using The Tripp Lite 3 Surge Protector gave me 6 extra outlets on my main power strip which was huge for me. The nice thing about not using the top piece attached to the actual surge protector, besides giving you that extra plug, is that the top piece can be plugged into a regular wall outlet to give you charging for up to 4 USB devices.
Overall, and even though the the thing is ugly and a bit nontraditional, it does have benefits. Big bulky plugs are not an issue at all with this one and the top portion works great for me as a travel USB plug. With all that said my only complaint and reason for the 4 star rating and not a full on 5 star is the retail price seems a bit steep to me. Quality and function are great but personally I feel it to be overpriced.

title: Solid build quality but with a few quirks.
text:
I ordered the ‘adidas RPT-01 Bluetooth Sport On-Ear Headphones - New’ for review as I am a sucker for wireless headphones. My initial thoughts right out of the box were that these are solidly built, lightweight and beautifully designed headphones. They look and feel "high end". I’ve now had these for nearly a month and feel that I am ready to share more.

First I would like to comment on the fact that these are touted as “Sport” headphones and my idea of “Sport” headphones are more of the "in-ear" earbuds, which fit much more securely and do better in the “head-shake” tests. I honestly don’t see these working for anything more extreme than jogging. Don’t get me wrong, they do fit well and are lightweight but just don’t quite pass the “head-shake” test haha. These are IPX4 Water Resistant which is a bonus, and the padded ear cups are removable and washable which is nice (though I have not been able to figure out how).

Pairing was super easy and they sound really good for “On-Ear” headphones which leads me to comfort of “On-Ear” headphones and wearing glasses. I wear glasses and I have issues with “On-Ear” comfort in general. These are no different. Though they are very light and comfortable at first, within only a few minutes of wear they get quite uncomfortable for me. With that said, my Son who does not wear glasses has zero issues with comfort and says that they are really comfortable to him. Also speaking of comfort, personally (after about 30min of wearing) my ears tend to feel like I am wearing Winter Earmuffs as my ears get quite warm. This isn’t a huge deal but I thought it worth mentioning.

Now on to my absolute favorite thing about these headphones. The single Toggle Button on the right earphone. This is so simple to use and can control pretty much everything. Long Press to turn the headphones On or Off. Toggle forward or back to go forward or back a track. Toggle up or down for Volume Up or Down. Short press to Answer and End calls. This innovation is absolutely incredible and makes this the easiest pair of wireless headphones I have ever used. The button on the Left Earphone has the ability to assign three different functions. For example a single click could activate your phones default assistant or double click to play your favorite Spotify playlist and three clicks could play a different Spotify playlist. So basically the left Earphone button can only be used to use your default assistant or play Spotify. My guess is that Adidas could eventually add other apps to this button (with a firmware update) but for now, you only have the two to work with. In my experience so far, this button is a little tricky. First off, the button does not protrude much and can be harder to get it to click, especially if you have large fingers. Once you figure out how to get it to click, the next issue is that you really need to click fast to get the triple click to work. I've gotten to where I can get the triple click to work nearly 80% of the time. It's not a big deal because there's really only two apps it can control. I did notice that if you use this button to start playing Spotify, the Spotify app does not actually open on your phone which kind of freaked me out. This means that the headphones will be all that you need to use to quickly start playing Spotify. If you need to access it for anything else (on Spotify) you'll need to actually launch it from your phone.

USB C charging! More companies need to get on board with USB C and I appreciate the fact that Adidas have included USB C charging which makes for super fast charging of the Adidas RPT-01 Headphones. I have not fully tested the advertised 40 hour runtime but I can say that I have used these a couple hours here and there over my time with them, and I have only had to fully charge them once.

The Adidas app is pretty basic but it does offer some nice eq presets with the option to customize your own. Personally I like to start with the Adidas preset which is "flat" by default. Then if you prefer, you can customize it. The sound is amazing but not quite comparable to some of the other higher end noise cancelling headphones which I won't name.

Overall, I do love the Adidas RPT-01 headphones and they definitely have a place in my collection. Really the only two complaints that I have is, the comfort issue while wearing glasses, and I feel that at this price point they should have come with a nice protective case.

title: Tripod is great but my DSLR with attached lens does not fit in the bag properly.
text:
ordered the ‘Vanguard VEO2GO235AB Aluminum Travel Tripod with VEO GO34M BK Shoulder Bag’ for review and would like to share my thoughts. I will list the Pros and Cons for each, the Shoulder Bag and Tripod.

Shoulder Bag
Pros:
It is of great quality with sufficient padding throughout.
It comes with a rain cover in the back zipper pocket that is attached to an elastic cord which can be removed.
The Tripod fits nicely into the bottom zipper compartment.

Cons:
I don’t really like the design.
Not many pockets nor compartments.
My DSLR won’t fit properly in the main compartment with a medium sized lens attached. (See images)
The Shoulder strap is not removable.

Tripod
Pros:
It’s very compact!
It’s seems to be of good quality and performs very well.
It’s pretty stable when fully extended.
Center post can be inverted to where the camera can mount hanging upside down for very low angle shots.
It has a hook on the bottom of the center post to hang some weight from for more stability under windy conditions.
The rubber leg adjustment knobs work well and make for easy leg extension and breaking down.
It comes with metal spikes which can be added to the bottom of the legs for a more secure footing. I installed these and slid the rubber boots over them so if I need the spikes, they are as easy as just pulling the boots off to use.
The included Ball Head is nice.

Cons:
It’s a bit on the heavy side.
I don’t like the camera to Ball Head attachment. There is a metal spring loaded pin that does not seem to work for the included camera attachment which makes it not so easy to remove the camera from the Ball Head mount. You have to nearly unscrew the bracket all the way to get the camera off and it is a bit annoying.

Overall I do think this kit of great value but if I were to buy this, I would not get it with the bag. Please see the attached images.

title: Good quality but the 90° angle may be an issue for some applications.
text: I ordered the 'AmazonBasics 10FT 90 degree angle High Speed 1.4b HDMI Cable' for review. So far my impressions are that the cable and connectors are of good quality. I ordered this cable with the intent of using it for my Xbox One but because of the 90 degree angle connector, it does not work unless the Xbox is pushed to the back end of the table (as the cable points down instead of up). I was able to at least test it for connection briefly and it works just fine, and as well as my original much shorter cable, but I'll need to find another use for it. Overall this cable is a great value but just keep in mind the 90° angle when considering your application.

title: Really impressed by this product however not so good for listening to videos.
text:
I ordered the 'Soundcore Wakey Bluetooth Speaker Powered by Anker with Alarm Clock, Stereo Sound, FM Radio, White Noise, QI Wireless Charger with 7.5W Charging for iPhone and 10W for Samsung' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts after a few weeks.

First off, this thing is actually pretty amazing. The build quality is nice and aesthetically it looks clean. The sound quality is nice but not phenomenal. However for how small it is, it does produce decent sound and for a bedside alarm clock it does quite well. The wireless charging works great for my Galaxy Note 8 (and does in fact Fast-Charge) however there have been a couple nights to where my phone was not charged the next morning. The fast charger also works with my wireless earbuds which I attached an image showing the charge light on the Wakey, and the wireless earbuds case indicating charging. However for the wireless earbud charging, it does take some precise positioning to get them to charge. I noticed in other review that others weren't happy with the bright display light with no way to adjust it any dimmer than the lowest setting, however they must have updated that with a firmware update (which was super easy to do) as I had no issues with the display being too bright at night. I use the auto adjust setting which seems to work quite well as far as I can tell. Also I love the sleep mode sounds that you can adjust several (or just one) sound volumes to create your own personalized preference. I do wish that there were more sound options but the ones they provide are acceptable. I also wish that you could download and install more alarm sounds. Bluetooth connectivity is super quick and have never once had an issue with pairing it up to my phone. Really the ONLY issue I have with the Wakey is that to get the sleep mode sounds going, you need to connect with the app, and via Bluetooth connect to the device. No big deal right? Well my concern is that you will need to keep it connected for this feature to work. This means you will be connected to the Wakey ALL night and this kind of bugs me. It's just kind of creepy that the Wakey is connected to your phone all night while you sleep. I wish there was a way to just play your favorite white noise sleep sound by pressing a button on the Wakey device without having to always connect and stay connected to the app and your phone. The other gripe is that the plug design is huge and makes it so that I have had to move my nightstand further way from the wall to use it. Other than those two gripes, and the only reason for docking one star, the Soundcore Wakey is a very good product and a really great value.
*On a side note - I just tested the Wakey while watching some Youtube videos and the latency is not so good. There is quite a bit of delay and the voices do not sync up at all so I wouldn't recommend using the Wakey for listening to videos.

title: Awesome value!
text: I ordered the 'Seagate One Touch SSD 500GB External Solid State Drive Portable - Black, USB 3.0 for PC Laptop and Mac, 1yr Mylio Create, 2 months Adobe CC Photography (STJE500400)' as I am always in need of more storage. This little One Touch with 500GB of storage will work perfectly for transferring files (Music, Video and pictures) between my PC, Laptop and Chromebook. So far I am really impressed with not only how small and light this thing is, but at how fast it is. It also seems durable enough to take a drop, but I really would like to have seen some rubber trim around the edges rather than plastic. I do like the looks and design of it, but it just seems like even some rubber on the corners would make for a much more durable case. Overall however this drive has performed flawlessly and seems to be a great value. Also the free One Year subscription to the Mylio software and free Two Month subscription to Adobe Creative Cloud make this a really nice added value.

title: Love EVERYTHING about these except the soft flimsy case.
text:
I ordered the 'New Sennheiser Momentum Wireless Noise Cancelling Headphones with Auto On/Off, Smart Pause Functionality and Smart Control App' to review. So far, and after almost a month of testing and playing with these amazing headphones, I am ready to share my thoughts.

First and foremost I must express that I am really disappointed in the case that Sennheiser has included with these "High End" Headphones. I mean come on Sennheiser. It seems pretty standard these days for higher end headphones to come with a nice clam-shell hard case. The case provided is a soft zipper pouch with little to no padding at all. I would not feel comfortable to stuff these into my backpack or even suitcase for that matter.

Now with that said, these headphones ARE solid. The stainless steel headband is sturdy and not fragile. The headphones themselves are of a very nice quality construction with real leather, both on the headband and ear pads. The physical buttons (which I tend to like much better than the new "touch" buttons on some of the others out there) are nice and solid and function perfectly.

The sound is absolutely AMAZING! I compared them to my wife's Bose QuietComfort 35 II headphones and honestly I love the sound signature on the Momentum's better. And as for the Noise Cancellation, I honestly can't tell much difference between the two. I do think the Bose do a slightly better job but for the sound quality you get out of the Momentum's, I'll stick with the Momentum's.

As for the weight and comfort compared to the Bose, the Bose are lighter but not necessarily more comfortable. The Momentum's just feel SOLID. The Bose feel nice but light and flimsy.

Other thoughts - Others complain about the "auto pause" feature on the Momentum's, but I personally love it. Others complain about the way you have to power these off by folding them up and personally, it doesn't bother me a bit. I would rather that then pressing a button and wondering if you pressed it correctly. This way, you KNOW they are off.

Battery life isn't the greatest compared to many others in this price range but for me it's just fine. I don't travel long distances and for the occasional 5-6 hour flights I rarely take, they will give me what I need. Plus with the much appreciated USB type C charging port, they will charge pretty fast.

Overall I LOVE everything about these, except for the soft flimsy case provided. Sound is fantastic! They are loud with rich thumping Bass, Nice clean Mids and wonderfully crisp Highs and for me the Sound Isolation works great.

title: Nice quality and value.
text: I ordered the 'Elimoons Phone Stand, 2 Pack Multi-Angle Cell Phone Stand Tablet Stand Universal Smartphones for Holder Tablets(6-11"), e-Reader, Compatible Phone XS/XR/8/8 Plus/7 Plus(Black/White)' for my daughter to use with both with her mobile phone and iPad mini. These work great for both and are really convenient and pretty durable. Overall these are a great value and work very well. I especially like how they are able to adjust at different angles and still hold your device quite well.

title: Good value but not perfect.
text: I ordered the 'iPhone Charger Lightning Cable 3Pack - (3ft, 6ft, 10ft Long) by TalkWorks | Strain Relief Metallic Heavy Duty MFI Certified Apple Charger iPhone Cord for iPhone XR, XS, X, 8, 7, 6, 5, SE, iPad - White' for review. title: Don't let the size fool you!
text:
I ordered the 'AmazonBasics 9-Watt Bluetooth Stereo Speaker with Water Resistant Design - Black' for review. When I first received it, I wasn't expecting it to be so small as you can see from the attached images. But don't let the size fool you. This little guy does a pretty good job at handling big sound. The Bass isn't that great, but the Mids and Highs are surprisingly clean. Bluetooth connects very fast and the range is pretty good as long as you are in the same room. Another noticeable thing is that for the size, it's got some weight to it and feels of great quality.
Overall, and considering the size, this little guy is well worth the price.

title: Great quality and design.
text: I ordered the 'AmazonBasics Rotating 9-Outlet Surge Protector Power Strip, 2160 Joules' to review and would like to share my thoughts. First off I am pretty impressed with the quality and design of this surge protector. It feels quite sturdy and I like the rotating plugs, which allow for more plug-in options. Overall this device seems to be a great value!

title: Must have for the absent minded ;)
text: I ordered the 'Tile Pro (2020) - 4 Pack' for our family to use. My wife has been using the Tile products since they first came out years ago and we always thought it silly that they didn't have replaceable batteries. This version was a must have for that exact reason. Not only can you replace the batteries but they are very solidly built and should last a good long time. One of these went to my daughter who continuously misplaces her phone. She always came to me to use the "find my phone" app to locate her phone. Now, she just keeps a Tile hanging on her door knob so she can find her phone on her own. It works GREAT. I ended up placing one in my laptop bag and we may put another in one of our vehicles. At any rate these are pretty much a must have for those loosing stuff all the time and I have even been thinking of a way to attach one to our TV remote as it's ALWAYS getting lost haha.
