title: Packs a punch!
text: I ordered the 'DOSS SoundBox Pro+ Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with 24W Impressive Sound, Booming Bass, Wireless Stereo Pairing, Mixed Colors Lights, IPX5 Waterproof, 15 Hrs Battery Life, 66 ft Bluetooth Range -Grey' for my oldest daughter as she keeps "borrowing" my wireless Bluetooth speaker and rarely gets it back to me. When I first received the device and opened it, I had my doubts that this one would compare to my device however I was pleasantly surprised. The sound quality for this little guy is amazing and at 24W gets fairly loud. The Bass boost button ads just a touch more Bass but not as much as I would expect but again, for how small this is, it packs a punch. The lighting inside the front grill is fun and ads to the "fun factor". At first my daughter was not so impressed with the speaker, but after using it now for a while, she stated that she loves the grey color, the light effects and the sound quality. Also a nice little surprise with this speaker is that you can ad music to your own SD card (up to 32GB) and install it directly into, and play it through the unit. Though I don't think my daughter will use this feature, it's nice that DOSS included the option. Overall this was a win for both myself and my daughter.

title: Great sound and easy to pair.
text:
I ordered the 'Jabra Evolve 65e UC & Link 370 Wireless Professional Earbuds' as I'm a sucker for trying out new wireless earbuds. I've tried various different types. Some that are "truly wireless", some like these that have the connected wire around the neck. These Jabra Evolve 65e earbuds are really pretty amazing for what they are. Sound is great but not booming with bass. They are crisp yet not loud. There is really no sound isolation as the buds don't fit snug in the ear, (even trying the included different size tips and wings) but that seems to be on purpose. As from I can tell from reading about these, is that they are meant to allow some outside sound, so that if you are say jogging, you should be able to hear to be safe right? Now with that said, I see the purpose and the market for these earbuds, and there is absolute value to these.
Pairing these to my Android mobile phone was an absolute breeze. Also, using the USB Bluetooth adapter on my Chromebook made pairing these super simple as well.
Call quality is on par with most wireless earbuds. It's good, but not the same as just using your phone obviously but better than some "cheap" buds I've tried. These are definitely built with the Jabra quality you would expect and I'm overall impressed.
They fit comfortably and secure and I've had no issue with them popping out, but then again I'm not a jogger. They are easy to fit into your ears, unlike others that I've had that take a bit of twisting to get the fit just right.
The app is nice and works well but as with most apps like this, it's gimmicky. I mean I've played with it a bit at first but any more, I just pop the buds in and go, and haven't used the app in quite a while.
So to summarize, these are great earbuds if you don't need "truly wireless" and you don't need sound isolation.

title: Perfect replacement for lost original remote.
text: I bought this replacement remote for my Daughters Roku TV and it works flawlessly, and just as well as the original that has been lost for some time now. The little mountable holder is a nice addition and should help her keep track of this one haha

title: I'm quite impressed!
text:
I ordered the Acer Chromebook 15, Intel Celeron N3350, 15.6" Full HD Touch, 4GB LPDDR4, 32GB Storage, Google Chrome, Pure Silver, CB515-1HT-C2AE, 15-15.99 inches so that I might have a lightweight portable travel laptop to enjoy and use for travel and at home. I have had some time with the new Chromebook and I would like to share a few thoughts and experiences with this particular model.

The first thing that I noticed with this Acer Chromebook was how thin and lightweight it was. It reminded me of a Macbook, though I have never owned one. I love the silver metal look and the keyboard is very enjoyable and comfortable to use. The speakers on either side of the keyboard are nice and sound amazing considering the size and the fact that they are housed in a very thin and compact space.

Initially I did experience some issues with the screen where it would not turn on despite the fact that there was power. It was very random but about 80% of the time the display would not turn on. I was able to contact Acer and they did resolve the issue within a reasonable amount of time. I had to send it back to Acer and they replaced the mainboard which I assume was the culprit. As I type up this review I am doing so on the repaired Chromebook and I have to say that though I had that initial experience, Acer made it right and I absolutely love this product! I’m not real savvy with the Chromebook OS but it really is simple and I appreciate the fact that this model comes with a Micro SD slot for my 128gb card which will come in handy to use for loading some movies and or music for on-the-go. Also it will come in handy for loading a few photos to edit with my favorite mobile photo editing app using the excellent touch screen which I quite enjoy.

Speaking of movies I have played a bit with Netflix, Google Movies and Hulu and the video quality is quite amazing with the 1080p screen resolution and, as I mentioned earlier, the sound is surprisingly loud and clear.

Battery life has been pretty impressive and lasts much better than I expected. As I stated before, this has been my first Chromebook experience so the only thing I have to compare battery life with is my much larger gaming laptop which I can't even get a few hours of use before I need to plug in.

Overall this Acer Chromebook 15 has been quite enjoyable, and because of Acer’s great support, I would highly recommend this Chromebook if you are looking for an inexpensive well rounded mobile “Laptop” experience.

title: Sound quality is better than most over-ear headphones!
text: I ordered these Razer Ifrit: Low Profile Design wired earbuds to use mostly for gaming on my Xbox One console and I am absolutely blown away by the amazing sound quality. Even the mic performance is better than expected. I've always loved Razer products as they tend to be well made and of higher quality, and I have to say that these are no exception. If I were to complain about anything it would be that the band that wraps around the back of your head (they fit a little big for me) tends to brush against my gaming chair, which gets picked up by the mic on the other end. This gets a bit annoying but after a bit you learn how to avoid this by keeping your head from bumping and brushing against the chair. No stars deducted for this however, only because of how incredible the sound and build quality is. I may be retiring my over ear headphones in favor of these ;)

title: Packs a punch for the size.
text:
I ordered the iHome Alexa Built-in Bluetooth Speaker Portable Wireless Waterproof Rechargeable Lights Up to Music, with Speakerphone, Passive Subwoofer, Carry Strap, Durable Shockproof Floatable Design (IBT158) to replace an old sub par portable speaker that I’ve had for years. The iHome is quite the upgrade with the built in Alexa, better sound and being waterproof. I’ve had this product now for several weeks and would like to share my thoughts.

I must say that the sound is pretty good and packs a punch in such a small size. It’s much better than the much smaller and several years old portable wireless speaker that I have been using. In fact there really is no comparison at all. Let’s just say that it is the best sounding portable wireless speaker that I personally have ever owned. My daughter who “borrowed” the older speaker some time ago (and she never gave it back) keeps asking to "borrow" the new iHome as she says, “it’s louder and sounds WAY better”. I absolutely agree with her. Plus the lights on this thing are a nice touch, and there are options (via a button on top) to cycle through and change the color options or turn them off.

Setting up the iHome for Bluetooth and Alexa was easy and very straight forward, and there has been no issues whatsoever. We are mainly an Android household however my oldest daughter uses an iPhone and everyone has had the same great experience. So far my only complaint is that the Bluetooth connectivity distance isn’t the greatest but with that said, none of my Bluetooth devices really have much range in our home so I am not going to knock points off for that. The sound out of this little guy makes up for the Bluetooth short comings and the bonus of Alexa being packed into this as well as the waterproof features make this a great value for the selling price.

One thing worth mentioning is that to use Alexa, you can’t just say “Alexa” to activate her. You do have to physically press a button on the iHome speaker to access her, which isn’t a huge deal breaker, but because of this, you can’t use other Alexa devices to make an announcement and have it broadcast to the iHome speaker. Being fairly new to the Alexa and smart home world, I am not going to hold this shortcoming against the iHome device. It actually makes sense that with this being portable, you wouldn’t want to have Alexa always listening and drain the battery while on the go. Speaking of Battery life, it's decent but not spectacular by any means. This is pretty subjective however as usually when I use the iHome, I'm listening to it at a pretty high volume ;)

Another observation is that this uses micro USB to charge, and I really would like to see more devices using the newer and better USB C charging capabilities.

As far as the “waterproof” capabilities go, I must report that I have yet to float the device in a pool or let the kids play with it outside while running through the sprinklers. I know that it says it’s waterproof and it absolutely looks like it would hold up to getting wet as it is very well built, rugged and quite solid, but I don't want to risk ruining this new toy that the whole family has been enjoying so much.

title: Nice sounding with soft and very lightweight cable.

On the other side, I appreciate that the cable doesn't weigh the buds down and I find that they stay in place even when trying to shake them out. title: Super easy set up for both Android and iOS.
text: I ordered these Bose Frames Audio Sunglasses, Rondo, Black - with Bluetooth Connectivity for my wife as she loves her Sunglasses and listening to music while on the go. Before I handed them off to her, I paired them up with my Android device and played around with them a bit (so that I could show her how they worked of course haha) My fist impressions were how amazing they sounded without having actual earbuds. The sound is crisp but definitely not loud and booming as the speakers don't fit into your ears however for what these are, and meant to used for, they perform quite well. Don't expect an "immersive" experience with these, but more of an "awareness" experience, to where you can enjoy your music on the go and still experience the world around you. Call quality was decent and others can hear you clearly unless you are in a noisy or windy environment but this is pretty normal for most Bluetooth headphones. I never experienced any issues with the sound "dropping out" in either speaker and neither has my wife. As for the construction of the sunglasses themselves, I felt that they were well made and on par with a mid price ranged pair of sunglasses. The magnetic charging cable works great and I love to see this in more products as the Micro USB cables and ports seem to be the first thing to break. The cable it'self could be a little longer in my opinion but on the plus side it's less to get tangled and much easier to tuck away into the included soft pouch (which by the way works great to clean the lenses). My Daughter played with them for a bit using her iPhone and she was able to set them up on her own without any difficulty at all. The built in sensor knows when you take the Sunglasses off and stops the music which is nice so you don't have to worry about remembering to turn them off. Once you put them back on you have to push the easy to find button (bottom right front temple) and you will hear a battery status prompt and "connected to" prompt. Press the button again and your back to you're music. Bose has really thought these out and I found that they are quite intuitive and very functional. My wife loves them and my Daughter wants her own pair.

title: Great buy if you can catch them on sale!
text:
Disclaimer - I've only had these for about a week so far and these are the very first Truly Wireless Earbuds that I have ever owned.

I purchased these earbuds on a great sale while waiting for another more expensive brand to get restocked, and honestly didn't expect to much from these. First impressions were that they were quite cheap however after using them for a little while now, I've come to appreciate them even more. Even though these are my very first Truly Wireless Earbuds, I feel that after tons of research and watching reviews, I know what to look for in sound and quality. There are so many budget wireless earbuds on the market right now with so many more on Indigogo (which from comments and reviews I've seen and read, I will NEVER buy from). This makes it quite hard to know what to buy. For me, I have been waiting for that perfect very small and discreet Truly Wireless Earbud with amazing sound. The Iyesku YK-T02 TWS Sport Earbuds didn't hit that mark for me but at the price I paid, I honestly can't complain.
Pros:
1. Bluetooth 5.0 - This was one of my main requirements when searching and the YK-T02 has it.
2. Easy to pair (I am using the Samsung Note 8) and pairing was very easy. Once the buds are initially paired, they connect super fast once you pull them out of the charging case.
3. No loss of connectivity to either earbud. I've seen a bunch of reviews where this is an issue with MANY other wireless earbuds on the market. Even some of the more spendy ones.
4. Fit is very comfortable and seem to be very secure though I have not put them through the test of running nor exercise. However I don't think this would be an issue at all.
5. Sound quality is decent. More about this in the Cons.
6. Tons of ear tip options. Most earbuds come with a few extra sizes but these come with a plethora, for that perfect custom fit.
7. Quite small and discreet.
8. Small pocketable charging case.

Cons:
1. Sound. As I stated in the Pros these sound "good" (for the money) but the Highs are quite loud (Mids and Bass are not) and almost hurt when the volume is turned all the way up. Mids are not to bad but the bass is nearly non existent which was a huge let down. HOWEVER let me say, once I played with the ear tips and found the right fit, Highs, Mids, and Bass are much better, but still not what I would have hoped for but again these aren't "High end" earbuds right?
2. Because the volume of these buds are quite low, Audio books are hard to hear when in a loud environment.
3. No satisfying magnet to hold the buds in the charging case like many others on the market. (The case does click shut to ensure the buds wont be falling out.)
4. Speaking of the case, my first impression was that the case felt very nice and lightweight, but it does feel cheap.

Final thoughts:
Like I said earlier in this review, if you can get these from Amazon on a lightning deal or with a coupon, I would say grab you a pair, but just don't expect these to compete with higher end buds. These would be great for the kids and anyone that just wants a good pair of Truly Wireless Earbuds that wont break the bank.

title: Absolutely the best Digital Frame and Service
text:
I've owned a PhotoSpring Frame for many years and upgraded to a newer one a few years ago. Also I have gifted many PhotoSpring Frames to family members over the years all of whom have loved them.
Abour seven days ago I discovered my frame had a strange message " PhotoSpring is updating your frame - this may take a few minutes so don't turn the frame off" Showed a line with %completed that indicated 0%. So I just left it and went to work - when I came home same message at 0% So I turned it off and waited a few hours - same message showing with the 0% completed. This went on for 2 days thus I contacted PhotoSpring helpline via email.
Dan Smythe replied the next day that it seemed they'd have to have me send the frame back so they could fix it and assured me that it was still under warranty. Well I didn't have an opportunity to send it back this past week then yesterday received a message from Dan that if I hadn't sent it back they may have figured out how to fix it all I had to do was turn it on which I did. Well this morning I glanced at the frame and there it was showing all of my pictures! I've no idea what magic they used but I am obviously thrilled. I've over 17,000 photos on it and everyone loves watching it when they visit.
So first Kudos to Dan and his team for quick responses and for figuring out the problem.
Second - if you are considering a digital frame this is the one to buy. It's so easy to send pictures from your phone to the frame and within minutes they appear. Again huge thanks to the best service team you could have.

I need something to protect it and so will just cut my losses with this one and buy something else. It’s a real shame because I truly wanted to love this case.

title: Wonderful Case, magnets can affect function of computer though
text: Love my case! It is beautiful and very stylish! I also feel like it is solidly protected, so long as it’s in the case. The only reason I’ve given it 4 stars instead of 5 is because the magnets, that hold the case closed, interfere for some reason with the capability to use the stylus on the area of the screen that coincides with where the magnets are located on the opposite side. I almost attributed it to my glass screen protector but when I slip off the case I am able to write no problem in those areas of the screen that my stylus would not seem to catch before. Other than that, the case is totally worth it!

title: Stunning watch!
text: Great watch, and packs a lot of features into this elegant gem. Bands are super tricky to switch off though and if not careful could end up breaking them off. Saw many how to vids on how to do this but regardless, was never an easy task for me. Aside from that, it is absolutely stunning on!

title: Terrible shape

title: Warm and soothing light to read/work by
text: I love the amber lighting and it helps me get sleepy earlier by using this and avoiding blue LED before bed. I use it to cross stitch and it works but I do have very good up close vision. If your vision isn't the best I would recommend getting a large magnifier in adddition to this light. title: Disappointed

I'm terified my laptop will fall out the bottom if the zipper unzips while I'm carrying it. The padding around the sides is non-existent. Personally I don't like the handle design either - its uncomfortable in my palm and I don't believe it will hold up over time. title: I love my new fire 8 tablet!
text: I was searching for a kindle, and then I noticed in the "other products" section that there were more affordable fire tablets.  It was a no-brainer but of course I upgraded from the basic model. I purchased the fire 8 instead of the fire 7 so it was larger, but still could be held in one hand. I added a scandisk card to upgrade the memory and added a cover from Moko. More bang for my buck and the cost was just about the same as a kindle, but now I can read my books, access the Amazon store, watch my favorite anime, TV subscriptions, search the web, read my college course homework, get on zoom calls, listen to Spotify, play games, and watch the Election and inauguration coverage on all my favorite news channels. I think it holds the charge for awhile, not sure it's 12 hours though, but I can watch media most of the day.  The fire tablet could charge faster. However, I didn't spend another $15 on the fast charger out of principle. It should come standard IMO.  I also think my fingers leave too many smudges so I may buy a screen protector too. Still, I recommend this product to everyone. I really love it!

title: I really love this case
text: I spent a long time, a few days, trying to decide on a case. I knew what I wanted -- a strap for sturdier holding, a card protective case in case I drop my kindle, cuteness. And this case, which I stumbled across has those things!. It doesn't have the hard silicon shock absorber edges, but my kindle is securely strapped in and the edges of the case extend beyond that and are hard and sturdy. It has a wide, comfortable strap that stretches without constricting my hand (I have a wider hand-span). And I like how I can prop it up to watch videos.. I love it! I bought the all black version.

title: This vendor (Selens) delivered what they promised -- a 59x78.7inches Pop Up Green/Blue Screen
text:
My order was delivered on time within 2 days. It is the correct material (thick woven material that I cannot see through, and slightly shiny), chromacolor green and blue color, and correct size. It was in its carrying case and the case was sealed in plastic. I knew other seller products were supposedly hard to fold back down and so I tried folding mine right away. It folded down for the most part easily (took me two tries to get the hang of it), but then it popped closed easily. It opens flat. There are a few small wrinkles that should shake themselves out if I hang up the screen, but I think they are fine to use the screen with anyway. And there are straps to hang the screen in portrait or landscape layout, which I like very much.

I really searched for a vendor I could trust. Some of the other sellers had customer reviews saying their screens were nylon and not muslin, had dark colors, wouldn't lay flat, and couldn't be closed. I didn't want to buy from any of those vendors and waited a long time for a seller who might deliver a product that matched their ad. I took a chance on this seller (Selens) even though they had no reviews mainly because they were so very accurate in listing the size of the screen as 59x78.7 inches. I thought that this was a seller who wanted to do a good job for their customer. Thank you for delivering what you promised, Selens.

One comment -- there is a small (oil?) stain/streak about 2 inches on the green side, but you can't see it when looking directly at the background so the manufacturer probably didn't see it. But if you look at the screen from a high angle it is noticeable. I'll have to shoot some video/photos to see if it is a problem. I don't think it will be. I didn't see it on the blue side which is darker, but I just glanced. I'll look to see if it is on both sides later. Again, I don't think there is a problem as on the green side you can't see it if looking directly at the screen. But otherwise I liked what was delivered so far. :-)

title: Be prepared for heavy...

Cons

title: So painful to wear
text: I don't have complaints about the sound. I thought the sound quality was pretty good. But, because I work in an open-space environment at work, I need earphones that I can wear for long periods of time—these are not comfortable. After about a half hour, my ears were in so much pain that I gave up and went back to my old pair that didn't have quite as good of sound to them. title: Great router and offers so much flexibility because of the touch screen.
text: We have blown through about 4 routers this year in hopes of finding one that we like.  This one definitely fit the bill.  It was very simple to set up and the speed is fantastic.  We used to have to put the router downstairs by all of the computers, but now with the touch screen, it gives us so much more flexibility.  Setup took me about 10 minutes and then about two or three minutes per wireless device to verify everything was working.  So, it was really easy.  I think because we were able to put it upstairs this time, it has an incredible range.  We have always had to use a range extender before, but not with this one.  I would highly recommend this product.

title: Can't go very loud before the sound gets distorted
text:
We have several small, portable speakers that have great sound for their size. Unfortunately, this is not one of them. This one is a bit of a disappointment. If it gets loud at all, the sounds is really distorted and almost static. It feels very cheaply made, lightweight, and although the case is aluminum it feels very plastic. Overall... here are the pros and cons as I see them...

Pros
- Very small size
- Book-like square body makes it easy to throw in a backpack or bag because it isn't an awkward shape
- Very easy to pair with a Bluetooth device

Cons
- Sound is distorted when volume is even slightly increased
- Feels cheap and very plastic

Overall, I would not recommend this speaker. We have other ones that have much better sound, quality with comparable price and size.

title: I love this little pen
text: I love this little pen.  It has been great for sketching on my 3rd generation iPad.  I love the fine point and it seems pretty accurate.  I think the one thing that I had to get used to was the angle when using it at different angles, it sometimes doesn't draw as expected.  Overall, I am happy with it, but it did take some getting used to.

title: Disappointed... we like our Roku boxes much better
text:
I normally like Amazon and their products, but this one fell really short for me. We own four Roku boxes and one Apple TV box. So, we thought we would give this one a shot. Installation of the box was simple. Getting Netflix to work on the box was a nightmare and ended up resulting in a call to their tech support department. The tech support department was very nice and was eventually able to solve the issue with an update of the firmware. With that said, I have been so disappointed in the interface. I probably should have expected it, but I didn't. The interface is so predominantly focused on Amazon streaming that it makes other apps/tv options difficult and cumbersome to find and use. Unlike the Roku boxes where all of your channels are at the top level, on the Amazon box, they are buried. It also forced me to re-enter my password constantly for Netflix. This is so annoying. Another thing that drives me absolutely crazy is on the new releases. It drives me nuts to have to select a new release and go to it's page to see if it is available for rent. So many of them are only available for purchase. Amazon needs to put these in a completely separate category so we can just avoid them instead of wasting time. My daughter has been begging to purchase the remote for games (which I have refused, because that's what our gaming systems are for), as most games are are finding can't be played with the remote, so there is another $40. I wish they would categorize the games more appropriately. I still haven't figured out a way to make the dolby stereo work even though our tv is capable of it.

Okay... now for the things I like. It does seem to stream a bit faster without issues. I like the voice search, although it really only works on Amazon. I like that they have separated prime viewing videos. I like that I no longer have to input my pin number to order video on demand rentals.

Overall, I wish I could recommend this box, but I really don't recommend it. I think the Roku is so much better, as it isn't focused on just Amazon content, but rather overall viewing content from many channel providers. So, while this may have a couple "nifty" things, they just aren't enough to outweigh the negatives on this box. So, back to Roku we go.

title: Great little router for the price.
text: For the price, this is a great little value.  It was very easy to setup if you are just wanting a basic wireless network setup.  The dual bands were both working well and the guest network seemed to work well.  I didn't notice a different in speed from my old wireless-n router... it seemed to be the same with all my devices and I suspect it's because my devices also need updating to gain a faster speed.  However, it did perform just as well and at about half the price I paid for my old router.  This was installed in my basement and it has a range that works well on both floors of our house.  It streams Netflix, Amazon and Apple TV just fine (using Roku, Amazon FireTV, and Apple TV boxes).  We didn't have any issues with the quality being throttled or losing a connection.  Overall, I would say this is a good buy for the price.

title: Built well... but it is much smaller than I expected.
text: This case has a great adjustable shoulder strap and has a solid velcro loop on the back so you can attach it to a belt or bag. This case is built really well, but it is much smaller than I anticipated.  First, let me qualify this review by saying if you own the professional line of lenses, then some lenses might not fit.  I shoot with a Canon 5D III and almost all my lenses I have are the L series.  Some did not fit at all.  For example, my Canon 85mm f/1.2L lens would not fit in the case at all, and my Canon 50mm f/1.2L was so snug at the top that it felt like it would have been forced in there.  The case narrows a lot at the bottom.  This is ideal for some lenses because it keeps your lenses more secure, but for most of my lenses, it was a tough fit.  It did fit my 135mm, 24-105mm f/4L, 17-40mm, and my 100mm Macro lenses in it perfectly. So, it will work for most lenses that are no more than 3 inches in diameter for the glass (about a 77mm thread) and I would say no taller than 4.5 to possibly 5 inches.  It's built really well and is a nice little case, so I would recommend on this condition to just pay close attention to the size and match it up with your gear.

title: Works like a charm...
text: This little Seagate portable hard drive is great.  We have been using it as a backup device for my husband's MacBook Pro and it works like a charm.  The speed is great and the size is great as well.  So far, so good.  I will follow up my review if we have any issues with this hard drive.

title: Great little product... a couple of drawbacks...
text: This little box is solid!  It comes with a nice carrying case and was easy to setup.  As for sound, I have other speaker devices that provide a bit better sound quality.  The bass isn't very good, but it does get pretty loud for it's size.  The setup was easy and pairing was easy.  Using it for calls was easy too.  I want to use it a bit more, then I will do a follow-up review.

title: Easiest setup ever! Great little speaker.
text: So, I own several of these types of small speakers and this one, for the most part, does not disappoint.  The setup was incredibly easy.  Of all of the Bluetooth connected speakers I have, this was by far the easiest setup out of all of them.  Now, I had to subtract a star because although this speaker jams, the bass wasn't quite there enough for me.  I like a little more bass in my speakers and adjustments from my iPod didn't seem to help too much. Would I recommend it to a friend... absolutely!  It seems like a great little speaker.  The size is perfect too.  We actually took it on vacation so the kids could have a better speaker once we got to the hotel room so they could all watch a video off of the iPad.  So, it's very portable.

title: Great bag and holds a lot for the size...
text:
I have a couple Lowepro bags and they are all great. This one is also a great bag. I like the backpack style because it is easier on my shoulders to carry. However, with that said, it is much harder to quickly grab your camera or switch lenses without putting the bag down. So, it's not necessarily ideal for some photo shoots. I like the compartment for the laptop. It fits my MacBook Pro in it nicely and securely. I am not quite sold on the layout yet. But that is a matter of preference. It's nice for both my DSLR and if I have my video camera on top, but mostly I don't use the top compartment and I am thinking I may prefer a better compartment for more protective lens storage. All-in-all, it is a really great bag and I would recommend it if the compartments provide the configuration you are looking for.

UPDATE 9/17/14
I have gotten so I really love this backpack. I started putting my longer Canon L lenses up top where the video equipment is meant to go. It will hold one of my large lenses at a time. It can hold my camera body and three additional lenses (one on the body) in the lower compartment. I find that I am using this backpack a lot more. I still struggle with the fact that I have to put it down and lay it flat on the ground to get my stuff out. I am used to grabbing it from my over-the-shoulder bag which was much more convenient. But, I have to admit that this has alleviated some of my shoulder and back pain because the weight is more evenly distributed across my back instead of over my shoulder. So, I am going to increase my rating from a four to a five star because I am really loving it.

title: Love this ball... but I have been unable to fully test it yet...
text:
So far, I love this ball, but I haven't been fully able to test it yet because the cable it comes with is not for high-end Canon DSLR cameras. I tried to find the cable locally at our camera stores and they did not have one in stock. So, I have ordered a Vanguard one (that wasn't as cheap as I thought it would be), but it is on a 1-2 month backorder. So, I will have to test that functionality once it comes. So far, I am thoroughly impressed with this ball. It is solid and it moves easily, but not so easily that your camera flops over out of your control. Even on the loose settings, it is still fairly tight. It has two levels on it which are great. So far, I have used it for panorama shots and it has done a fantastic job. Usually, I have so much overlap that it stitches the photos a bit weird in Photoshop and takes quite a bit of correcting. I noticed that using this ball allowed me to glide more smoothly while keeping the photos all at the same level. It was fantastic. The one thing that I really wanted to try... and the one thing I was so excited for was to be able to use this for night shots. I was thinking the pistol grip with the shutter trigger on it would give me the ability to use that to trigger my shutter and thus remove the camera shake without having to tote a separate remote around. Unfortunately, this is the one thing I can't try since they don't include a compatible cable for my Canon 5D III. So, I will have to update this review once I receive my cable and I am able to test it out.

Now... it is heavy... much heavier than toting a small ball around. So, I have noticed on some of my outdoor shots where I have to hike a ways in, I don't take it with me because it is just simply one too many heavy things in my bag and it is the one thing I can do without when deciding between pistol grip and lenses. Other than not including the high-end cable and the weight of the pistol grip, it is a fantastic piece of equipment and I look forward to continuing to use it. I will update my review once I get the cable.

title: Don't let size fool you... this little speaker packs a punch!
text:
I own a lot of little speaker sets and this one is by far the most portable, easiest to bluetooth pair, and sounds the best for its size. I had no trouble pairing it with my iPad. I did, however, have trouble pairing it to my iMac. It kept giving me errors and I finally gave up. I can't speak to whether or not it was easy to pair with another Jam Plus speaker, as Amazon did not send me two as first was noted. I would definitely recommend this speaker. We actually took it on vacation last weekend and had it by the pool. Everyone there commented on how loud it was and what great sound it had for its size. So... thumbs up on this one!

UPDATE 9/12/13 - I received an additional speaker and so I thought I would provide an update. I absolutely love these little speakers. They have an incredible sound and a great bass for their size. They really do jam. I thought one was great... two of them synced are exceptional. We love to travel and these are the perfect size for that. So, I would highly recommend these speakers.

title: WOW... I never cared for Netgear products, but this router is awesome!
text: Okay... I have had Netgear routers before and they never really seemed that great. I also had a Linksys router that was just okay too.  All seem to struggle to get from my basement, where I house my network equipment, up to the rest of the house.  By the time I get to my furthest back bedroom, I am lucky to get a single bar.  So, to my amazement, I bought this router, hooked it up, took my laptop to the furthest bedroom in my house and I had five bars.  FIVE BARS!!!!  WAHOO!!  This router is lightening fast, the range is amazing, and I liked the available configuration options.  The other thing that was very helpful is that it has multiple ethernet ports and two USB ports.  So, I was able to hook up one of my printers and a USB network drive directly to the router without having to put everything through my ethernet and print server boxes.  It was extremely easy to setup and so far I am thrilled with it.  I will update for longevity and reliability at a later date.

title: A bit disappointed...
text: I have two other Lowepro bags that are extremely well made.  I purchased them about three years ago.  I was shocked to see how much their quality has gone downhill.  The canvas used was thin and stiff.  The seams are not all double stitched and the cording they used to use around the seams doesn't exist any longer.  Also, the plastic clamps are much less heavy duty and don't appear they will stand up as well over time.  I have loved all of my old bags by Lowepro, but I purchased another camera and needed a larger case.  I am so disappointed and will be returning this bag and going to the local camera store to check out some other brands before I purchase my next bag.  As far as the size, there is no way this holds a DSLR and 4-5 lenses.  I have a Canon 5D Mark II with the Canon 24mm-105mm lens.  I also carry my 85mm lens.  With these two items in the bag, most space is taken up.  You would have to have extremely small lenses to have it hold 4 to 5 lenses.

title: WOW WOW AND WOW!
text:
I think this is now my favorite portrait lens. I just received this lens in the mail and already I can tell it is going to help me immensely. This lens makes me look like the most amazing photographer. Every shot seems to be perfect with minimal to no effort. I initially choked on the price when I purchased this lens, and was somewhat hoping it wasn't going to be that great so I could send it back and get my money back. Well, NO SUCH LUCK! This lens is awesome!

I am shooting with a Canon 40D and a Canon 5D Mark II. Both are great cameras and both have performed perfectly with this lens. No regrets here! I am thoroughly pleased. If you do any portrait or wedding photography at all, this is a must have lens.

title: Sound quality is lacking.
text:
This product is just OKAY. They are really onto a good concept, they just need to refine it a bit. I wouldn't say it is great or horrible... just average. I have a Phillips docking station that has incredible speaker sound for its size. I was very disappointed in the speakers on this unit. My favorite part is that it can rotate. This makes it nice if you are laying in bed and want to watch a movie while it is docked and charging. It allows you to lay it horizontally and still have louder volume output, though not very good stereo. The other thing I didn't really like is that it doesn't come with its own power supply. You have to use a USB cable and then use your Apply power supply for it to work. This is unlike the other docking stations I have. So, would I purchase it... only if I just had to have a horizontal docking station with slightly more audible sound. Now, if this system had good quality stereo output and its own power supply, I would definitely spend the money to get it.

Pros:
- Rotating into a horizontal position while in a docked mode
- Can pivot vertically forward and back just like a monitor
- Comes with a sync cable
- Provides a bit louder speaker output than the iPad does
- Very easy to use and didn't even need the instructions
- I like that it is elevated a bit like a computer monitor

Cons:
- Relies on the Apple power supply
- Speaker output is lacking and the stereo is terrible
- Unable to control the volume using the iPad. Once in the dock, you have to use the nob on the side of dock.

title: On the fence still...
text:
First, let me say I purchased the Powershot 510 and the Powershot 310. The 510 is a much more solid camera and a lot less plastic than the 310. I think my two largest complaints and frustration comes with the touch screen and the 12 power zoom. The touch screen drains the battery faster than my other Canon Powershot cameras and the zoom is incredibly difficult to get stable when at full 12 power and my pictures haven't turned out as well as I would like at that distance. Overall, I really didn't like the Canon Powershot 310, so I am on the fence as to whether or not I will keep this one. I have a few more days to think about it. For now... here is a more detailed list of pros and cons:

Pros:
- Takes incredibly good photos with regard to color.
- Easy to use.
- The vivid setting is great for flowers and fall colors.
- I love the fisheye effect without having to carry around my Canon DSLR camera and lenses. I also love having the wide angle.
- The miniature setting is kind of fun to use.
- Feels incredibly heavy and solid, unlike the new 310.
- Fits easily in my purse and pocket.

Cons:
- Can't stand having finger prints all over the screen when I go to take my picture.
- Touch screen drains the battery pretty quickly over the other Canon Powershot cameras.
- When zooming out, it is very difficult to keep it steady.

Not sure what to order if I send this one back. So, I am still on the fence, as I am partial to Canon cameras over Nikons. The red color is not as it is shown in the picture. It is more of a rust/burgandy color of red... it has a bit more brown to it, but I actually like it.

UPDATE: 12/12/2011 - I ended up sending this one back and kept the Canon 310. I am really glad I did. I get a great battery life and when I compared the photos on this camera vs. the 510, the photos had better color and looked a lot more crisp from the 310. I am happy with my decision.

title: Not quite sure about this camera yet...
text:
First, let me say this camera does take some great pictures and it is very easy to use. My complaint comes in by how plastic it feels. It just doesn't feel solid like all the other Canon cameras we have purchased in the past. I love my husband's Canon Powershot 300HS, but I wanted a bit higher zoom. So, I purchased this one. I also purchased the Powershot 510 as well to see which one I would like better. I must say, I am swaying towards returning both of them. This camera feels flimsy compared to the other Canon Powershot cameras. I prefer the non-touch screen of this one vs. the Powershot 510, but overall, the 510 just feels a lot more solid for only around $75 more. The touchscreen on the 510 drains the battery too fast, but this one just doesn't seem to be that durable. As for the zoom comparisons, on the 510 it zooms to 12x, but it is extremely difficult to keep it steady. On this one, the 8x seems about right. So, I am not quite sure which one to keep. I love the new settings for vivid, foliage, miniature, fireworks, fisheye, etc. If it weren't for all these new settings and a higher power zoom, I wouldn't even consider trading up from the 300HS for this one. So, I am torn as to what to do.

UPDATE 10/30/2011 - So, I decided to keep this one instead of the 510. It still feels kind of plastic to me compared to older models we have. However, I have been thoroughly impressed with the video, picture and color quality. The battery longevity helped to make this decision as well.

title: Great RTX Card
text:
(11/20/2018) I purchased the MSI RTX 2070 Gaming Z 8G. I took many factors and pricing based on what was available and compared to other cards. I was primarily looking for a card to replace my ASUS GTX 970 Turbo. With Battlefield 5 releasing and testing my setup (below) with the GTX 970, my settings could only handle 60 FPS with everything at medium. Battlefield 1, I was able to play at around 80 FPS with DX12 off, so it was definitely time to upgrade.

My Setup:
CPU: Intel Core i7 7700k at 4.2 GHz
RAM: 16 GB Vengance
Motherboard: ASUS Strix B250G Gaming
Monitor: ASUS MG278Q (2K res at 144 Hz)

Upon receiving the card, the card is definitely bigger than the GTX 970 and heavier. Make sure you have enough room in your case as this card extends the micro ATX board setup. The card come with plates and can customize the RGB LED's.

I chose this card as it was par with the RTX 2080 in cores and clock speeds, and even the GTX 1080. The downfall which many will know is that RAY tracing is not amazing with this card. I play all my games in 2k res at 144Hz and really only enjoy playing FPS at or above 60 FPS. Playing BF5 with ray tracing on (low) with everything at ultra had around 20 to 30 FPS average with sometimes reaching mid 50's. Once i reduced my graphics to high instead of ultra, FPS gains were up 10 to 20 FPS. With Ray tracing off and everything on ultra, I was getting anywhere between 80 to 130 FPS. Changing my res to 1080 with everything on ultra and even RAY tracing on ultra I had FPS above 60. The downfall to this was quality of the game graphics.

As of 12/13/2018, EA/Nvidia release patches that improved the FPS with RAY tracing, but only a gain of about 10 FPS. I still continue to play BF5 with RAY tracing off and everything on ultra. I did notice some hiccups where the game would freeze for a split of a millisecond, but it could be the game more than the card as BF5 is still buggy.

As of 4/4/2019 this card continues to perform perfectly with any game I throw at it. I currently have been playing anthem with above 50 FPS with the new ray tracing features and DLSS available in the game. There are some dips due to high fidelity and other high graphical areas within a battle area, which is why the lowest I have seen is 50 FPS. With Ray tracing turned off, i get above 70 FPS. While this card is big, I am hoping to replace the stock fan with a water loop system. On a micro ATX board, do not expect to utilize any of the PCI lanes besides the one for the GPU.

Overall, I am very happy with this upgrade for the price. The 1080 ti stock is basically depleted or costs over $1000. The 2080 cards are better than the stock 2070 cards, but this msi card is par or better than the 2080 stock cards. Only advantage to the 2080 cards was more CUDA cores. This is my first msi card as well, since i usually go with EVGA or ASUS. EVGA unfortunately did not have any in stock during the time of my purchase.

title: Best Video Doorbell
text:
Back in 2016, I was getting into the Video Doorbells for extra security for packages. After much review of Ring, Skybell, Nest, and August doorbells, I decided to purchase the Skybell. I instantly enjoyed being able to get notifications when there was motion and when the button would be pressed. The advantage with Skybell was that it came with free subscription. Well... after 2 years of using the Skybell, i ran into many issues where the motion would not notify me or even pickup, wireless trying to connect to my network at home, and many other headaches which you would think be fixed after many patches. I have my own server room and network system which I ran network throughout my house and even have a business hotspot near the Skybell, still had many issues with the Skybell doorbell.

Moving forward......

I reviewed my options again as I was fed up with Skybell and still only had the same options today as they were 2 years ago. After much consideration i decided to choose the Ring Doorbell 2. They do offer a free subscription now, which is great, but you cannot review any motion or button press history events. Of course this is just due to needing to purchase the basic plan for the cloud storage. Even for $30 annually, the basic plan is still cost effective. After using the doorbell in the trial version of the plus plan, I am planning on paying the $30 just because its cheap cost and I would rather have the events to review rather than just seeing the live view.

Setup was easy (easier than Skybell). The app loads quick and can edit motion detection's, alerts, and much more. I connected the doorbell via hardwired to an analog doorbell. The box comes with many customization options, tools, and took only 10 minutes to install.

Testing the Ring doorbell worked perfectly and better than Skybell. I installed my Ring doorbell with the provided wedges that came in the box. I have a 20 foot driveway and the detection works so great that cars driving by alert me. You can decrease the range of the motion in the app. When there is motion, I can open the app from my lock-screen and only takes about 2 to 3 seconds before i can see the event. The load times are very quick and faster than Skybell.

Overall, I am day 15 in my trial and I am glad I decided on Ring. The product is great, and far better than competitors. Cost is ideal for those that do not want to pay hundreds each year on cloud storage like nest. I would highly recommend Ring to others.

title: Great Surround Sound Wireless Headset
text:
I got this headset during the 50% off deal and I am really enjoying it with Battlefield 5. I decided to upgrade from my Logitech G430 headset. I was mainly looking for a wireless headset that had great battery life, great sound and did not cost too much. Even without the deal, the $200 price point is still reasonable compared to other wireless headsets. I was considering the Corsair and Astro's before purchasing this one. I am using this headset for my PC only, to game.

The Headset:
- Customizable buttons to change the Equalizer, play/pause, and many other options to choose from
- Convenient volume dial to change sound on the fly. This is great so you dont have to minimize the game and adjust the volume settings with the mouse
- Headset grips my head. I have an angled forehead which my old headset would easily slide off when moving around
- Comfy ear pieces that does not cram my ears and feel uncomfortable
- Comes with long braided charging cable, AUX cables, and RCA cables
- USB adapter to connect the wireless headset it plug and play. You just need to make sure you install the Logitech dashboard to customize the headset
- The Logitech logo and a line down each ear-cuff lights up. To me this is a pointless feature as I am wearing the headset and cannot see the lighting and only uses up battery life. I disabled the lights and my battery life increased by 3 hours.

Sound:
The sound i will say is significantly better than my G430. There are multiple equalizer profiles to choose from (FPS, Cinema, etc.). Once you turn on surround sound and 7.1, it makes a big difference of sounds. You can change the treble, bass, and customize the sound to your liking.

Battery:
I cannot say too much about the battery life, but after a full charge, and turning off the leds on the headset. It said I have 12 hours of battery left. After wearing the headset playing Battlefield 5 for 4 hours, I still had 93% battery life. Overtime with charges and draining, i would assume the life would degrade a bit and would get around 10 hours of battery. I did not check how long it takes to charge the headset from a full depletion.

The only cons I have are the pointless LED lights if you are not showing off your headset. I do feel the headband part of the headset is not as strong as I would have expected it to be, just do not twist headband much.

title: Great for lowering 10 degrees Celsius
text:
First off, i had a little bit of a problem installing the backplate for this setup. You do not have to remove the backplate at all when you put the corsair black backplate on. My setup is consisted of a push pull system for my radiator. I have it mounted on the top of my chassis hooked up to an LGA 1155 motherboard with a 2500 cpu intel core i7. I have it setup at 3.5 Ghz so far, and i plan to push it to 4.0 ghz. I have ran Real Temp GT version 3.7 for an hour and thirty minutes. My results so far as of idle and playing some battlefield 3 on ultra consist of the following

core 1-25C min, 53C max
core 2-24C min, 53C max
core 3-25C min, 51C max
core 4-25C min, 53C max

My idle temps consist of around 30C.

Based on air to the H60, you will only see 10 degrees C difference. Of course this is also based on the pre applied thermal paste that comes on the GPU cooler. I have not tried an aftermarket thermal paste, which would result in different temps. I have an adequate chassis supported with 2 fans in the front to intake air, 1 fan on top to intake air along with the radiator setup, and 1 fan for exhaust in the back to keep the flow of the air within the chassis continuous. I currently also have the GTX 670 gpu in my computer which will soon be applied with the H60 cooler as well with my modified setup. This could potentially see a difference in temps, but nothing too major.

Overall, this is a decent way to quiet the computer and keep your cpu cool. It did take some time to setup based on how you want the GPU cooler to be setup. I would recommend this to a friend if they want all of the above. If they want to push the boundaries more, i would suggest the h100.

title: Best Case for ventilation and room
text: This Termaltake full tower case is amazing in every way possible.  It ships with 2-240mm fans that are led lit, 2-150 mm fans that are not led lit, and 1-150mm fan that is led lit.  It would be nice if there was more room to store the cables, but i was still able to fit a ton a cables in the space provided.  It has 2 holes on near the bottom that are pre-punched for people who want to water cool there case. There is a lot of bays to store HDD and other hardware needed to run the computer.  It also has and extra 240 mm vent on the top of the case if you want to add another fan, on the otherhand there is already one on top.  The only downside to the setup of the fans is that the 2 intake fans on the front are below the cpu and GPU section.  It would be optimal to put them higher so that the exhaust fans blow the heat out while the intake fans blow cool air in on over the main motherboard.  All the air is being disipated through the top section while the intake fans blow the aird straight out the bottom.  Like i said, this setup does not make since.  So i modifyed my 2 intake fans and moved them up higher.  Overall this case is amazing, and would purchase it for another build in a heartbeat.  Love the multiple choice of colors i can choose for my fans also with the button on the front panel.

title: Recommend highly. Versatile, Durable, Value, & Sound Great.
text:
Let me start off by saying I gave the noise cancellation five stars, and these don't actually offer active noise cancellation so I don't think it's really fair to put that as a category to rate them by however another factor in my five stars was isolation these are in ear monitors in your buds combined therefore the isolation is good.
As far as quality goes they're absolutely five stars they're a Shure product, I absolutely love the case, the adapters fit tightly in there for a secure positive charging experience every time, also the case zips closed so they're very secure, there is a feature where you just simply push the button on the outside of the case when it's closed and it tells you how many charges you have left which I find to be very convenient and very helpful. These are very much the same quality as something that if you are a professional musician you can take on the road and they would endure the rigors of the road.
As far as sound quality goes I'm not a huge fan of the transducers that come with the adapters however I did make the decision to buy them with the transducers because they're not much cheaper without I also then elected to buy the Westone transducers which are compatible with these for a very very nice end result. These are most definitely my go-to pair of earbuds when I'm on the go. I believe that any person that gives these a bad review didn't get the fit right because musicians all over the world everyday use in-ear monitors such as these, with the exception of the Bluetooth feature. Therefore if you are reading a bad review or listening to a pair and you don't hear enough Bass or it's not loud enough, chances are you don't have the proper fit. (That is not factoring in hearing loss or fatigue)
Keep in mind if you ever read a piece of specifications for a piece of audio equipment there's so much erroneous information in there it's absolutely mind boggling and that is because hearing is something that is very subjective, just simply can't tell someone how they hear. So based on your expectations and your preferences these adapters paired with the right transducers for your desired sound I believe to be one of the best combinations there are on the market today and I also believe that because they are so versatile and you can add so many different types of transducers to them based on what you want or don't want it makes them even more desirable to sum it up they're a very good value for your money.

You can tighten the joints but it really needs to be tight and you use the smallest wrench to tighten it. It feels like it's going to break. Also, if you move it any, it has to be retightened. After a while I found that the screw that holds the arm on, loosens and finally come apart. It's done so several time and finally broke.

title: Great replacement laptop
text: I needed a replacement laptop for my wife and came upon this one. It's very lightweight, that helps. The touch screen is excellent, especially when you open it all the way up to use as a tablet. And speedy, absolutely. It is very quick. My wife loves it and she uses it a lot which really puts the battery to the test. Luckily, it holds up to the use. The battery lasts a long time.

title: Exactly what I needed
text: I needed light for my video blog and this was perfect for me. The brightness and temperature knobs are solid and the battery life is awesome. It gives soft light when I need it and bright white in a twist of a dial. a great buy.

title: Great for home user.
text: I work in IT and have made MANY RJ45 cables using many different connectors. These are, by far, the easiest to use. One of the biggest issues when making the cables is that you cut the wires too short so they don't crimp right, or you leave them too long and the cable stress relief doesn't exist. These allow you to run the wires straight though so everything is the right length. I haven't had to re-make a cable since using these.

title: Get more local channels
text: No cable company gives you all the local channels. I put this up and connected to to the TV and there they all are. I never realized how many local stations were in my area and all for free. Bye cable.

title: The best tablet stand
text: I've had many tablet stands and most were flimsy. This is very sturdy and fits all my devices. You also get a few hangers to use in multiple places. Absolutely fantastic.

title: Great for traveling
text: If you travel a lot, This is a great companion to have. It allows you to organize your electronic life. Chargers, batteries, external hard drives and cable will all fit in this bag. No more looking for that needed cable that got lost deep in your back pack. It's all organized and kept safe in your organizer bag.

title: Enlarged my footprint
text: I had a bit of a dead zone in my WIFI signal and needed to find an easy to use solution to this. In comes Netgear WIFI Range Extender. This is great. Just plug it in and connect it to the network and I can get great signal in what was once a dead zone. Highly recommend.

title: Great microphone
text: I was starting a podcast and needed a decent microphone. I saw this and decided to give it a try. It works great. Sound quality is good, it's easily adjustable and recordings are great. It comes with everything thing you needed to record great sound.

title: Just what I needed
text: We are adding things to our "smart house" and there are things we want to get that would require power run to them. Sometimes using AC is not possible in the areas we are looking at. Outdoor cameras are one example. That's where this switch comes in. POE (Power over ethernet) supplies the power needed and the switch also gives you a better connection to these units than WIFI. Most times these cameras are on the fringe of the WIFI footprint and causes the connection to be intermittent. This solves that issue as well. All in all, a great product. Everything works as desired.

title: Disappointed
text: I got this to use with my tablet. I thought it would be great to use while reading. First, there's no way to use it for a tablet without the gooseneck. Without the gooseneck, it's basically a tripod for a camera. Second, you can't use the gooseneck WITH a tablet or iPad because they are too heavy for the gooseneck to support. The only thing that I could use it for is my phone, which is a little overkill.  Lastly to use the gooseneck it becomes too high to use in most of the application I wanted it for.

title: Nice door lock
text: My daughter always forgets her keys. That's a real issue if we go away. This alleviates that. She picked a code that she can remember and now she can get in anytime. installation was straight forward and instructions were easy to follow. If not, there is a video you can watch to see how to install it. Set up was also a breeze. Just follow what it says and you'll be done with set up in about 5 minutes.

title: Does the job
text: I needed this because I wanted to use an external monitor on my laptop. The only issue was, the monitor I had didn't have a HDMI port and my laptop didn't have a VGA port. This allows me to hook them together and everything works great.

title: Great coupler
text: I have many shorter Cat6 cables and they are always too short for my needs. These couplers do the job to let me get the length I need with what I have on hand. They work like a champ and I see no degradation of signal.  Exactly what I needed.

title: Nice little speaker
text: I have a couple of meetings a seek and have been putting on a headset to attend them remotely. This is so much easier and allows me the ability to have multiple people listen when I'm in the office. The sound quality is good for a conference speaker. Music is ok, nothing to write home about, but that's not what this was made for. Controls are straight forward and easy to use. A very decent conference speaker.

title: Could have been just a little more portable.
text: This is small and unobtrusive. The video is good and the night vision is also pretty good. I did have a few issues when I first plugged it in. It appeared to be in a reset loop and there was nothing about that in the instruction's troubleshooting area. I decided to shut it off and let it sit for a while and that did the trick. Apparently, it needed to charge a bit. The instruction were a little sparse, so you are lift to search on your own. Once set up, it works like a champ. One caveat, I drive quite and bit and use multiple cars. This is set up to placed in one car and left there. The charging base for it needs to be able to be moved from one car to another.

title: How WOW!
text: Where has this been all my life? I have a home office and run everything off my laptop. I also use an external monitor as a second screen so I can see the details of the picture I'm editing. Until this, my laptop sat on my desk and was too far as I also use a wireless keyboard and mouse. With this, the laptop is off the desk and at the same level and closeness as the external monitor. This allows me to be more productive and not cause me so much eye strain.

title: Grand kids love it
text: My grand kids were very excited to get this. They love to read and this Kindle with the access to all those books keeps them busy. It was very easy to set up and start using and the battery last forever, which is good since it's almost never off. The kids can't put it down with all of the choices to read and we couldn't be happier. We may have to buy another so that they don't have to share.

title: Great replacement
text: I needed a replacement for my service provided router. Their router was not reaching parts of my home. This is a great replacement. Set up was easy and I saw a speed improvement immediately. I would sometimes get buffering while streaming a show. That doesn't happen anymore. I also found that my WIFI footprint is larger. I get a strong signal in my backyard. Something I didn't get with my old router. My property is relatively small, so I only needed one unit, but with this, you can form a mesh with remote units. Highly recommended.

title: What you need for your webcam
text: Very straight forward installation. Adhesion is very good. Nice and thin. It doesn't interfere with the closing of the laptop. Does exactly what it needs to do. Great product.

title: Great product but...
text: This is an amazing capture box for game play. A plus is that it captures in 4k. Setup: Basic set up of equipment in simple and well explained in the instructions through text and diagrams. You are provided with a link for the software and the installation of the software is straight forward. The only issue I had with the instructions is the lack of detailed guidance for mic set up, but I was able to figure it out in the end. The output is video capture is crystal clear as well as the sound recording. All in all, a great product but more instructions on mic set up would make this a 5.

title: Great sound in a smaller package.
text:
There was a bit of an issue when I first plugged it in and tried to pair it to my phone. The speaker, kind of, froze. After a little while, I thought a reset might help and it did. You are able to use the speaker while it's charging, which is a plus that some don't have. It also only comes with a charging cable, there is no adapter. This is an issue because the user manual, which is very sparse, recommends using an adapter with a higher amperage rating than come with most phones.

Now with all the bad out of the way, let's talk about performance. I was blown away by the amount of sound that comes out of this. It sounds great in a small room where I usually am, but wanted to see how it did with a large setting. I took it to work and went to the warehouse. This is where it shined. I turned it on and played Kansas. The sound traveled everywhere and was clear from at least 100 feet away. I then turned on the clear vocal and enhanced bass options. These aren't just hype, it brings more dimension to the sound. I could do without the party lights but they don't really bother me.

title: Nice headphones
text: There are nice headphone. They paired easily and stayed in the ear, even while doing rigorous exercise.  Other sets I had would turn themselves on and run down the battery which was a huge pain. So far these have not. It takes a little while to get used to the button functions. The there is no separate volume controls so it's a bit of a pain turning it up or down. Actually the hardest thing I find with these is getting them out of the case. :-) I did experience a connection loss when I went into the room next door that I didn't have with other headphones. The sound quality is excellent.

title: I was blown away
text: Very easy to set up. Everything was straight forward and I was up and listening in 5 minutes. In my room, it sounded great, so I decide to take it on tour. Took it out to the back yard and was very impressed. I could hear it everywhere on my property and didn't even turn it to 10. I took it to work with me because there were many different areas to test it in. In a large, open area with a lower ceiling, it filled the space with music. Next, I went to the warehouse and, again, music filled the room with no distortion in sound. The hardest place I took it to was the data center where the noise level is very high. This was the only place it struggled, but music could still be heard over the noise. This speaker, beyond a doubt, is the best portable speaker I've heard. I highly recommend this speaker.

title: Great...after you get used to it.

After so many years of using a regular mouse, I thought I'd give this one a try. It does take some real time getting used the the design, but after the initial time getting used to it, it becomes second nature and is actually a lot more comfortable to use than a regular mouse. It also seems to help with your wrist pain. I would recommend.

title: Great set of headphones
text: All I can say is WOW! The sound on these headphones are excellent and has plenty of bass. The noise canceling also works very well. When it's on, I can't hear my wife. ;-) It allows you to fully enjoy what you're listening to. As for comfort, I can't say you forget you're wearing the, but you won't mind having these on for an extended period of time. I didn't suffer  the discomfort I felt with other brands after a while. I was able to use them all day, which also says something about the battery life. I highly recommend these headphones.

title: Am I supposed to see the ring?
text:
I bought this and put it in and everything works fine, except, according to pictures I've seen, I don't think you're supposed to see the inside frame of the camera. Check out the pic I've included. I've called support and they are sending me a replacement. I'll update after I set that one up.

Update: Nothing actually changed. I installed the new Ring and the framing is still there. I'm guessing that this is the actual view you get. That said, beware, the actual view you get from the doorbell video is not what is shown on Amazon or on Ring.com, which shows you a full screen with no circular framing that takes up about a 1/3 of the screen. Also, this is supposed to be 720p. I doubt it. Even on the small screen of your phone the video is grainy. I've seen reviews of the more expensive models that say the same.

All in all, even though I was disappointed, I can live with that to get a little piece of mind. The price is worth if for this refurbished doorbell. I will upgrade the rating to 4 stars.

title: Overall great experience for this price range.
text:
For the money and considering I've only used these ear buds for 1 day they are an exceptional buy. I work mostly outdoors (Florida) in grounds keeping with noisy equipment and lots of sweat. They charged quickly and paired without issue. The range from transmitting device is basic at best with them occasionally losing signal when phone is in pocket and I bend over and have my ear muffs on. I can get about 30' away from phone if there isn't any obstructions. They hold their charge well. They are pretty comfortable to wear especially since I typically have ear muffs over them. As for noise canceling I don't notice any difference than any other in ear bud but my ear muffs fit over these just fine.

My only complaint really is the sound quality. Mids and highs are decent for this price range but there isn't really any lows. They are small devices so I'm not looking to thump but I'm not impressed compared to others I've worn.

I will update as I get more time on them.

title: It's not horrible but it's close.
text:
I've had this head unit installed for 2 weeks now. Great concept that was poorly executed especially for its price. Installation was easy enough despite the directions not being too helpful. YouTube videos saved the day once again. Device setup wasn't too bad since it's Android based. Bought all the peripherals - the steering wheel controls because the stereo interfaced with my factory controls flawlessly.
Radio was installed into a 2006 F-350.

After 2 weeks of daily use and several hundred miles here are my complaints: volume and sound quality are terrible compared to the stock system--only the head unit was removed. A good amp may correct this but I'm guessing it's the processor in the deck. Forget watching videos with the engine running. Can't hear it.

Like many other complaints, the unit does not like to pick up radio stations well. Only the strongest get through even though my 13 year old stock system had no problems before (the connection if fine).

The unit also doesn't like any internet connection I've tried. Slow as hell when it does work. Google play store crashes constantly making it extremely difficult download updates or new apps.

Frequently have to reboot system to get things to function again.

I'll probably add more later.

I'm regretting this purchase. Considering returning it.

After killing a 3 of them the Sales Team looked for a better solution. They got rid of all the covers and keept the new units naked. title: Greased Lightning
text: It's near impossible to find high end, quality RAM, but this fits the bill.  This works out of the box with the ASUS ROG Crosshair VIII Dark Hero motherboard.  I suggest always checking the compatibility list on the websites between the two products before buying.  There are very exact versions of this that both are and are not made for each other. title: Slick to Use
text: This little tool set is really quite impressive compared to several other cheap sets I have owned in the past.  The bits are all snug in the case.  The case design is deceptively functional.  I found myself turning it over to the side that has the handle and then quickly flipping it back over to the other side to get to the bits.  It is very compact compared to other sets I've owned.  I find this appealing because desk space is always scarce as is bag space.  Everything feels very well made and not like cheap junk.  The case clips together and the plastic is thick and durable.  The hinges on the case are also not flimsy.

title: Because, More Monitor
text: Putting together this beast was not a very difficult task.  I am using the 'Ergotron – HX Single Ultrawide Monitor Arm' with this monitor.  There was a little bit of an odd feeling when it took me hooking both hdmi and display port up to figure out how to deal with the monitor source correctly.  This overall though is the most amazing monitor I've ever sat in front of.  I use this for engineering work as I'm not a gamer.  The screen real estate is much larger than typical 4k 1440p monitors.  The jump from a 34" to 49" was not as drastic of an impression as I would have expected.  The curve softens the hit to the senses as it seems a little shorter than it actually is.  The curve takes a little getting used to but it's not near as aggressive as people claim.  This is my first curved monitor because I didn't know if I could get used to it or not.  After a few hours of working on it, I barely notice anymore.  The picture is very clean and crisp.  I'm using it in conjunction with a sapphire card.  There are plenty of reviews about the exact specs of this monitor, but really I wanted to note that it shines when it comes to just immersing someone into the screen.  I only would suggest this to people that have a very deep measuring desk because this does take up quite a lot of room over the desk even with an arm holding it up.  Works well with Ubuntu 22.04 + Gnome + Wayland using a Sapphire Radeon Pulse RX 5600 XT which does PCIE 4.0 and has for a long time now.  The card actually handles it very easily at 120hz on gnome for daily grinds, fans are not even moving at the moment.  The booklet instructions are confusing, so while waiting for the monitor to ship I would suggest watching some unboxing.

title: Fast but not as fast as advertised.
text: This drive is super fast but it's honestly not near as fast as claims make.  I have a brand new dark hero motherboard, 128gb gskill ram, motherboard is stock configuration but some changes, (nothing to drives or slots) and this performs out of the box on Ubuntu 22.04 as 5.1gbps reads and 3gbps writes without tweaking the disk on perf tests ran multiple times.  People complain about it not lasting long because of wear.  I would have done much more research if I had read more carefully in the reviews.  Many motherboards these days come with multiple nvme slots, so it's best to get two smaller drives and raid 0 them (striped) for much better performance.  Overall impressed with the drive but the numbers don't yet add up for me.  maybe someone did better tweaking.

title: Works well as expected

title: Works perfectly
text: This external enclosure worked perfectly when a family member's laptop crashed and I needed to get all the data off the drive.  It works with almost any operating system without any configuration.  Things work very fast and it's best to use it with the fastest USB connection of the machine you can utilize.  Works with Ubuntu 22.04 and Windows 10.  The top snaps open and closed to enclose the drive and the button to open it is well made and does not feel flimsy.  Overall the build quality is good and well put together.  Works well with a USB extension cable and conversion to type C cable.

title: Can I just say... Wow!
text: Can I just say, wow.  I'm a engineer and when I hooked this up at first I was a little skeptical.  I unboxed which was very simple.  Only a few pieces that were obvious in the box.  Then I plugged it all in and followed the instructions of the app.  Let me say, it was a little odd with the weird "waiting" on the app as things were happening and the instructions were not exactly totally obvious if someone was not already an IT person.  But overall it's very suggested that you update the firmware and even if things don't go through the first time, the second time the app connects, it figures out where you left off.  This helped me in one spot where I thought I might have to start over from scratch.  I was clever enough to rename the original 5g and 2.4g to the original names I had for the previous router, which fooled by ADT system into just popping back up as if nothing happened (without intervention.)  This does work with ADT which is freakin awesome.  This is the first time my husband actually said something like "that was seemless" which never happens.  I did have to change the 192.168.1.1 originally address of the gateway over to 192.168.0.1 along with the names.  Once that happened everything was so fast I almost didn't believe my eyes.  Recently we all got Galaxy 22 ultra phones and they picked things up right away, but the trick is to reboot your phone and then it comes up as 6E and the applications literally pop up twice as fast.  I couldn't believe my eyes.  This is the router to get.  I himed and hawed over the comparisons of other routers and I can't say how happy I am with this.  But the interface is kind of clunky.  Once you get it started you can enter the web interface via https but the interface looks like something out of 1995 which is ok but you'd think they'd put more into this given how far and easily things have advanced in 2022. Family can't be more impressed.  Overall a family pleaser.
