title: Beautiful jbl sound with noise canceling or ambient monitoring
text:
Very nice. I've always been a fan of jbl products. They make a very high quality speaker system (I currently have jbl's for my home theater as well as for my computer speakers). I also have Apple Pro ear buds as well as a pair of Samsungs. These jbl's are definitely on a par with both of those.

The Apples have a warmer tone. Clear and concise with solid bass performance.

The Samsungs have a "crisper" tone (possibly due to being a 2 way system). Their bass is solid and treble tones give heightened presence.

These jbl's fall somewhere in between. They do have the jbl signature sound with smooth solid lows and clear highs. The mids may be slightly attenuated and the overall sound is a bit thinner than either of the other two, but that being said, it's still clear and present.

Often, with ear buds, it comes down to fit - a better fit provides a "seal" that creates a fuller effect, and I think that's the case here. These are certainly comfortable and they come with various sizes of the rubber thing. Once you get them properly fitted and properly sealed, they are very comfortable and the sound fills out beautifully.

As for telephone functions, they work as they should with customizable functions for tapping actions. The app allows the use of noise reduction or ambient monitoring - both function effectively. Recommended.

text:
[[VIDEOID:a84ee2dce6fe9f0ce7f918516e7727fc]] This convertible from Lenovo is really nice. I've been using Lenovo products for years and have never been dissaponted. This convertible falls right in with the others- build quality, speed, functionality.

When you swing the keyboard back behind the monitor, it becomes a full featured tablet. At 14 inches, this is sized right for various uses, sketching, surfing, etc. The pen tracks nicely with the touch screen with only a very slight lag.

The machine comes with a 256 gig solid state drive, and with the AMD Ryzen processor, it loads quickly and has a very stable user interface. Even logging in is simplified and secure with a fingerprint sign in block.

The only concern about convertibles in general (all of them, not just this one), is that flipping the keyboard behind the monitor seems just a little clumsy, as the keyboard itself remains exposed. If you were to sit it down on a table, you'd be sitting it right on the keyboard.

All in all, if you want both a great laptop and a great tablet, this one is a clear winner. Definitely recommended.

title: Quick and responsive - premium grade laptop
text:
This Surface Laptop 4 model from Microsoft is an excellent premium grade laptop. My prior laptop is an older 17" Lenovo. This one is smaller (obviously), but much, much quicker.

The aluminum chassis is thin, lightweight and solid. The display is looks great- colors are detailed rich and vibrant, and the touchscreen is effective and appropriately responsive. I find myself simply reaching for the button on a given sites screen, rather than maneuvering the cursor and tapping. (Although, the TouchPad is certainly responsive, too). The keyboard is comfortable and responsive - the surface around the keys and track pad has a texture that makes it seem sort of "soft" (even though it's not). Sound is rich and full. Very nice!

Very few ports - only what you need and not much else. A USB Type-A and Type-C, a headphone jack, and the chargers connector. (Or you can charge using the USB Type-C port).

Set up is straightforward, I loaded in some software (Wordperfect suite) and everything just fell right in place and all worked as it should without issue)

5.) The keyboard is good. It’s not the best, a little spongier than the MacBook Pro 16’s, with a slower rebound, but still among the “good” keyboards on the market, - reasonably tactile. It has physical F-keys, something I wish I had on the MacBook Pro 16. I think the TouchBar is one of the worst things to happen to MacBooks (inadvertent touches are the worst!), so I hope Apple reverts to physical keys this coming year on their flagship system. Rumor has it they will.

6.) Ergonomics are decent, though it’s actually a bit tricky to open the laptop as there’s no indent where you’re meant to flip the screen up, - a peculiar oversight. Bezels are a little large for 2021, but far from offensive.

7.) Sound quality is not bad, but a far cry from the bass that the MacBook Pro 16 is able to generate. You could certainly listen to music here, but headphones would be preferred.

8.) Battery life and thermals are absolutely fantastic, decimating the MacBook Pro for general usage, which is just a portable toaster. The laptop just runs remarkably cool with this AMD setup. That said, when the fans kick in, they kick in with a WHOOSH, which can be a bit disconcerting. Battery life is superb, easily giving me 8-11 hours for general web usage, a good 40% longer than my MacBook Pro doing the exact same things at a comparable brightness.

  9.) The SSD is nothing too special. While yes, any SSD is faster than not-an-SSD, this is on the lower end of the spectrum in terms of NVMe performance.

Overall, I really enjoy the Surface Laptop 4, but it’s not hard to see where Microsoft could make some massive improvements and solidify the Surface line as THE Windows 10 systems to buy.

4 out of 5. A worthy alternative to high-end laptops, but not yet at the top of its game.

title: Pro grade optics with easy connectivity - nice!
text:
[[VIDEOID:f8be83e3530c313d3485906c32dd0520]] Typical web cams built-in on laptops and phones have gotten pretty good, but those of us that spent some time with old school video or SLRs know that that best zooms are optical (instead of digital) and the best lenses are large enough to allow a lot of light to pass through (making low light images more natural). This camera embodies those old school concepts with a 5.5x110 mm lens that's got aperture settings up to F1.6 (depending on zoom settings). These are impressive numbers by any measure. Where modern technology shines in this camera is in the electronics and interfaces, etc. Auto focus, remote zooming and panning - and multiple outputs as well. When you bring all of this together into a very usable camera like this one does, you've got a winner.

First, the obvious - the picture quality is excellent. Certainly suitable for conferencing or a video blog, and in fact, will look great in any type of performance videos. If you want to put your best face forward by emitting a professional grade video, you should use professional quality equipment like this.

Second is ease of use. I confess that when I first set this up, I simply plugged it into a monitor - that doesn't work. You need to plug it into a device with appropriate software. Once I plugged it into the USB drive of my older Lenovo laptop, I simply pulled up Skype and there it was. I was able to run it through some simple paces without any further action. And again, the picture looked great. I even dimmed the lights in the room to see how well it would handle it - beautifully! Just for fun, I zoomed out to show the room and then zoomed in to show my whiskers... all presented in GREAT detail (the autofucus struggled just a little to lock focus on my whiskers when zoomed all the way in, in a low light setting, but I switched to manual focus and was able to tweak it right in). And the real beauty of this system is that it's all controlled by remote.

Another nice feature that was immediately obvious - the gimbal that the camera's mounted on is, of course, motorized - but it runs in complete silence. Nobody's going to want to watch a video of they can hear the sounds of a camera being manipulated. This is yet another feature that separates the pro equipment from the rest.

The base is solid and usage is straightforward. My only nit would be that the manual is a bit sparse, giving technical specifications about various models of cameras rather than detailed info about usage - but so far, everything I've tried has been fairly straightforward, and I've managed without any further detailed instructions. Very nice!

title: Nice feel - easily integrated with my windows 10 system and software
text:
I had been looking at these types of drawing tablets and wanted to give this one a try. I'm not a professional, and I know that things like "lag" are sometimes a concern, but I personally didnt find excessive lag (not that I could notice, anyway). In fact, I found this to be very impressive in that regard for this price.

Installation was a breeze, simply download the apps and away you go. (I'm using a windows 10 system). I was able to immediately use the Penwalker thing on my main screen with nothing open (scribbling notes right across my screen, etc). Then I pulled open photos hoping and tried some simple scribbling- that's when I noticed that the touch sensitive nature of this system is really effective - pressure effects line weight, etc. The pens are lightweight, yet the pressure sensitivity gives them a certain "feel". I think I could get used to this.

Then I opened Clip Studio Paint Pro and just doodled for a moment. Alternating between brushes, fades, erasers, etc. Again, the "feel" is what impressed me most (in spite of the lightweight pens). There's function buttons identified right on the tablet, (everything appears to work as it should), and when you bring the pens tip within an inch or so of the tablets screen, you can use to pen like a mouse to position the cursor- then touch the screen to do your work. Same with the eraser end - turn the pen around and point the eraser end to the screen and position your cursor with it - then touch down to erase.

As an amateur, I've barely scratched the surface of this tablets capabilities, but I can already tell that it's going to be fun learning some new skills as I spend more time with this. For me, this one's a winner!

title: Responsive backlit keys - nice protection for the tablet - bluetooth
text:
This keyboard is impressive. I'm using it with my iPad air 3 and its a perfect fit. The plastic is a little stiffer than some of the softer cases available, so getting the tablet to pop in and out requires a little extra effort and care, but once in, its solidly held in place and the whole thing seems very sturdy. When closed, it seems to offer very good protection, although, with the stiffer plastic, I suppose the case itself could potentially crack if subject to overly rough treatment.

As for the keyboard, it operates independently of the tablet... that is to say, it has its own on-off switch and it must be charged separately (in addition to the tablet). Since it connects via Bluetooth, it really doesn't need to be physically attached to work, just within Bluetooth range. (You could leave your iPad on a stand while typing on the keyboard in your lap, for example).

The keys themselves feel good, with adequate travel and response to the touch - you can actually "type" on it... although it is slightly smaller than a standard keyboard (as you would expect), its still comfortable enough for regular use. Also, there's a backlight for the keys which I kinda like... my laptop also has that feature and it makes it usable anytime, anywhere (out on the deck after the sun goes down, for example).

The fact that it can be twisted around and folded back on itself for simple tablet use makes it that much more usable. It does add a little heft to an iPad air, including some weight and some thickness, so if the thin form factor and light weight were key reasons for choosing the Ipad Air in the first place, this will negate some of that.

Personally, I like this keyboard - I intend to use it when traveling instead of lugging along my oversized laptop. Recommended.

title: Attractive and functional protection for my iPad air - slot for pencil
text: Nice case for my iPad air. The marble like coloring is attractive and the fit is right forming a functional protective case. Theres even a slot for the apple pencil. Nice.

title: Attractive and functional protection - with slot for pencil
text: Nice case for my iPad air. The marble like coloring is attractive and the fit is right forming a functional protective case. Theres even a slot for the apple pencil. Nice.

title: Fast and flawless - absolutely silent operation
text: I installed this 240 G solid state drive in an external case to use between computers. You have to initialize the drive upon installation to get your pc to recognize it, but once complete, it's functioning flawlessly. As a solid state drive, its absolutely silent... its fast and trouble free (they say they're more durable, too, but I don't plan on testing that theory). Recommended.

title: Functional leather case - looks good and helps protect your Airpod Pro buds
text: Nice leather Keychain type case. Seems well made and should last. Theres a magnetic closure that seems to hold well, and a pin hole where the front led can be seen. On back is a "power" imprint that aligns with the power button on the apple case (you do have to press harder to push the button through the leather, but it does work. And an opening on the bottom for the recharge cable access. All in all, a functional leather case that looks good and should provide an additional level of protection for your expensive Airpod Pros buds.

title: Fast - quiet - powerful... everything you need in a basic desktop computer
text:
I've always had good luck with Lenovo computers. The desktop I bought back in 2007 is still going strong, and so is the laptop I bought a few years after that. This IdeaCentre 3 is a basic desktop, but it comes with everything you need for years of computing needs. As for inputs and outputs, it has 8 USB ports, along with an hdmi port, a dvd-rom drive and an SD card slot. Of course there's wifi and Bluetooth both supported.

As for performance... its fast. Much faster than you would expect at this price point. Setup was simple and straightforward... it wasn't overloaded with ads upon arrival, either... just trials for ms office and mccaffee protection. And with the 256 m solid state drive, this thing is dead quiet! Nice!

It comes with a keyboard and a wired mouse... no monitor. Definitely a winner!

title: Transfers exactly whats on your phone display - short USB cable
text: This is an interesting piece. Small enough to fit in a purse or pocket, it makes displaying what's on your phone easy to transmit to your TV. It does require wifi, but when i hooked into it, it showed exactly what was on my phone display. It even did the auto rotate this, switching from photo to landscape mode when i rotated my phone. If you have a service on your phone (Youtube, or whatever) it would allow you to transmit that to your TV. Of course, for sharing photos, or home videos, etc. It would be great. The one nit is that it gets its power from USB and the attached cable is relatively short, so you have to have a spare USB on your TV to power it. The only other option would be to buy a USB extension cord so you could reach a wall charger. Its a small issue, but important to note. Otherwise, it does a great job.

title: Gold plated contacts - sturdy construction
text: Sturdy construction, gold plated contacts for better electrical contact. Standard hdmi on both ends. The plastic covering is reasonably flexible and will prove generally useful.

title: Sturdy and useful cable to directly adapt type c to hdmi
text: Sturdy adapter type cable that allows direct connection between your USB type c device and your hi-def hdmi tv/monitor. In my case, that means I can use my phone to drive my tv... nice!

title: Useful adapter - sturdy construction
text:
This is a handy little adapter. It converts USB type c to hdmi and old style usb... and even includes a USB type c port in the extended array. This means you can hook your phone up to your TV with an hdmi or USB cable while maintainkng charge through the USB type c.

The construction is solid an aluminum housing with a sturdy cable... it should last for years.

title: Sturdy construction - sound quality is good.
text: I've got several sets of wired headphones that I like to use with my smartphone, so I was disappointed to find my new Samsung S20+ came without a headphone jack. Thats where this adapter comes into play. Construction is sturdy and the size is small. I like to leave them attached to my headphones and then I can plug those into my phone just like I used to. The sound quality is good, and the only downside is that you can't charge while listening... although that's the phone's fault, not this adapter. This adapter does exactly what its supposed to do.

title: Sturdy cables in different lengths
text: These are nice sturdy cables. There's a braided covering that feeds into sleeve, then metallic handle with USB on one end and USB type c on the other. The USB end has a nice bright USB signal indicating which end is up. Both ends fit snugly and positively. The package comes with 4 cables in 3 handy lengths. Recommended.

title: One digital signal in, three out - small footprint - just what I needed!
text:
This is a great addition to my studio... I've been swapping digital cables around on a regular basis for years, trying to get the studio output to a selection of other pics and audio devices. With this little box, I can set it up so my studio output feeds three different devices at once. All I have to do is turn on the device!

It's a small little box, with a small footprint. That's a big plus for a small studio owner. Its solidly constructed, too. I expect itll hold up very well over time. Recommended!

title: Limited ethernet ports - will serve as extensions to existing router
text: Overall, I've got mixed feelings about vfc this mesh system. I already had a decent router and was probably pushing the limits of my provider anyway, but I was hoping for increased coverage. The first challenge came when i realized there weren't enough ethernet ports for the extras in our home (a couple hubs for alexa enabled devises, etc.) So i bought an ethernet port expansion device to use with this system. I dont know if that somehow confused the system or what, but walking through the installation seemed to result in little glitches. I finally pulled the extension out of the setup to just get something working and in the end, the whole thing didnt really perform any better than my old router (and with fewer devices). So now I plan on using thg hem in bridge mode - using them for added coverage was my original intent and they seem to accomplish that just fine. Apparently my old modem was doing a better job than I was giving it credit for.

title: Nice sounding, versital studio mic - large and solidly constructed
text:
This is a USB based studio mic that's mounted on a desktop stand. The mic can be swiveled in the stand to tilt forward or back as needed. The mic itself is solidly constructed... it feels very well made. The stand is similarly constructed and should sit firmly in place. Theres a headphone volume control on the front of the body, along with a mute button, and similarly positioned on the rear of the body is a polar pattern selector switch and a gain control for adjusting the mic's recording output. The pickup patterns available are:stereo, omni, cardioid and figure 8.

I have some typical studio mice, but this is my first USB based mic, so I ran it through some typical trials to see how it fared. First of all, I found the sound to be accurate and with just the slightest "edge" - which seems to give it a slight touch of presence, especially in cardioid mode. Playing with tv he polar patterns, I could tell a bit of change in tone as I moved in close or away from the mic when in cardioid or figure 8 pattern - the effect is expected for these patterns and, though slight, were definitely there. Omni mode (picks up sound from all directions) did not show this effect (you would not expect it to). As for off axis rejection, I tried singing off to one side and then the other. Again, it performed as expected with no rejection whatsoever in omni mode. Rejection was minimal in cardiod and figure eight mode, though. (I would have preferred more). Also, in cardioid mode (signal is picked up directly in front of the mic only), I found the directional pattern a little wide. I like to use this mode specifically to isolate what's directly in front of the mic from the rest of the room. It works as it should, but I would have preferred it to be slightly more "directional". Finally, for stereo mode... this probably had the most impressive sound. It truly delivered a stereo sound... evenly balanced, with no dropout in the center. I even snapped my fingers on either side to see if it would pick up properly... it performed exactly as it should. As for sensitivity, it picked up the central heating unit fans in the background (just like a studio mic should), so some form of noise reduction would be called for (or turn off the hvac). Self noise did not appear to be evident - another specification that would have been nice for them to share (I dont even know if self noise is an issue with USB mics- this one didnt seem to have a problem with it).

Most people that I know would be interested in things like diaphragm size... that kind of detailed technical information is lacking from any of the paperwork that comes with this mic. It makes reference to a three capsule head, which makes me assume theres 3 diaphragms in there with the pickup pattern selector turning them on and off as needed, but no other info is provided.

All in all, I was impressed with this mic... it sounds good and has great versatility. It simply plugs into your computer's USB port and you're good to go (you may have to select the mic through your systems settings page). I think it would be ideal for any desk top application, podcasts, etc. It even has a screw in stand mount on the bottom. The only thing missing is some kind of a shock mount system, like a spider mount, or something), to shield it from noises that may vibrate through the desk to the mic. I suppose, sitting it on some foam would serve to isolate it.

title: Floppy lid
text: This is made of plastic, with a clear plastic flip top lid. The slots for the batteries are properly sized and everything is as advertised. The only problem is that the long flip top lid kind of flops into place. If you were to mount this somewhere, it would be less noticable, but the lid just seems clumsy and I suspect batteries could come topplin out if you weren't careful. I ended up buying a foam filled suitcase style case instead.

title: Easy set up - does what a smartphone can do
text:
My wife really likes this watch. This is the one with the glittery watchband... It comes with a magnetic charger that just attaches to the back - no fidgeting. And I was surprised at how quickly it charged.

The screen colors are great! Vibrant colors and clear graphics. The touchscreen itself can lag just a little, but overall responds very well. Neither one of us have ever had a smartwatch before and I was a little apprehensive about setting it up, but I downloaded the wear OS app to her phone and from there, it just walked us through the process. It paired on the first try and seems to be working just as it should.

She's now got it set up to check emails and can generally do anything on the internet that she would do with her phone. Then theres the added advantage of the fitness stuff... heart rate monitor, etc.

All in all, she loves it!

title: Well made power strip - individual outlets can be rotated 90 degrees from normal
text:
This is a handy power strip. It features 6 electrical outlet and 2 USB charging ports. It has surge protection for up to 1080 joules - not enough for a lightning strike or anything like that, but certainly good enough for more typical voltage spikes. It has a cable that's about 6 feet long.

The odd thing is that it also features individual outlets that can rotate in either direction. This is a nice feature to help organize cables - something that's always at issue where theres a power strip involved. These individual outlets rotate and click into place at 45 degrees and 90 degrees from normal, in either direction - but you cant plug into them at 45 degrees. The outlet holes are blocked. So why have them click into position at 45 degrees if you cant use them there?

This is a well made power strip with some nice features...

title: Excellent sound - excellent build- snug fit - bluetooth
text:
These are really nice headphones. The built quality is first rate and the sound is excellent. I would put them on par with my favorite (similarly priced) Sennheisers. Clean, clear highs - smooth solid lows, nicely balanced overall sound. The active noise reduction system is phenomenal. I had an air cleaner (with fan) sitting right beside me and it disappeared! The amazing thing is that the sound quality didnt change - it was excellent whether on or off
They paired easily with both my phone and my laptop... no issues there whatsoever. Powers up when unfolded, powers back down when folded.

They come with a USB charging cable, and a soft sided case. The controls are cleverly built in, with a pause/play in the center of the eight ear, volume up on upper portion, volume down on lower portion. Theres one button on the left ear... that turns the active noise reduction on and off.

The two things that I thought were negatives... one is that the overall size is suited for average sized heads. I have a rather large head (my hat size is xxl). These headphones fit, but they're snug. They do have really nice soft cushions which make them usable, but they could be just a smidge larger (my Sennheisers are bigger). The other thing that I consider a negative, there's no provision for "plugging in" to some of my older gear... its bluetooth or nothing.

title: Omnidirectional sound - clear and natural
text: This bluetooth speaker joins a long list of similar devices designed to bring big sound from a small device. It does this nicely. It boasts multiple speakers pointing in different directions (listed as "omnidirectional") including a passive radiator for extended bass frequencies. This wont give you the "thumping" bass tones that some people might enjoy, but rather a full range of clear and accurate, natural sound. Pairing was easy (as most bluetooth devices are these days) and it comes with it's own charger. Definitely recommended.

title: Fast and sturdy storage
text:
Its call a game drive and it's designed to be fast... it claims speeds up to 140 mb/sec. Well, I didnt get it for games, but simply to use for additional storage space... I transferred a large number of files into it (mostly jpeg and documents). I witnessed speeds of up to 68 mb/sec. I would imagine that would improve in a real time gaming application. So it's definitely fast!

A small form factor and sturdy case means this is ideal for what I'm looking for. In addition to storage, it allows me to easily transport and transfer among various machines. Nice!

title: Very functional... plenty of room for laptop, books, accesories, etc.
text:
I was looking for something to use as a casual overnight bag, of sorts. Something with enough room for my 17" laptop, a few personal items and a change of clothes. This backpacks fits that bill nicely.

It's softsided, so I dont know if sturdy is the right term, but it certainly appears durable. There's smaller pockets for various accesories and an open space for larger items. This would make a great carryall for a student running from one class to the next. Theres even provisions for a USB charger. The straps are adjustable and well padded for comfort. Very functional.

title: Storage and protection for 10 inch tablets.
text: This handy little sleeve is just the thing for my 10 inch Samsung tablet. There's no struggle to slide in the device, the fit is just right. Once inside, its secured by padding on both sides with minimal shifting within. Outside, theres 2 additional pockets, one zippered - and a sturdy handle. The perfect storage/protection for a tablet of this size.

title: Great monitor - sound's a little lacking
text:
This is a really nice monitor. Assembly was about as simple as it could be... you snap the arm into the back, then into the base. It took about a minute.

I ran an hdmi cable from my 17" laptop (see pictures) and turned it on. The image came right up, bright and clear... the only negative is that the speakers are a bit lacking. It probably deserves the loss of a half star due to that, but everything else about it is so good, I left it at 5 stars.

Great monitor!

title: Solid mounts, hold tablets firmly in place
text:
This adjustable tablet holder is fairly straightforward. With the clamps manually extended, then slid into position, the holding is reasonably easy to use. When clamped into place, it does seem to hold the tablet firmly. I was attempting to use it with my kindle (including its cover) and the extra thickness of the cover didnt seem to be a problem.

This has a 5/8 inch mount that will screw directly onto a mic stand, which is how I intend to use it. It also comes with a clamp to allow clamping it onto the shaft (allowing a mic to still be mounted at the top). So I wanted to try that... it turns out, even using that clamping system, the whole thing was held firmly in place! Impressive!

I'd definitely recommend this tablet mount... my plan is to use it in front of my elliptical machine for workouts.

title: Clumsy controls and charging port cover...
text:
These a are decent ear buds... not great, but decent. I didnt have and problem pairing them to my phone and the sound was clear, but they didnt seem to have as much low end as I would have liked. They sound just a little thin.

Today, I put them on for a routine on my elliptical. They did okay, but again, I felt they were lacking in the low end. When I started sweating, they started slipping and I struggled to keep them in my ear. They come with extra earpieces of different sizes, but the ones I had on felt comfortable before I started. Perhaps I need to experiment with those for awhile.

As for function, the charging port is a standard one like a typical phone and it charged reasonably quick. Near the end of my workout, it seemed as though I was losing volume. So the length of service was only moderate. The real concern for new, though, was the charging port's cover. It's a tiny rubber piece with an incredibly small "nib" that needs to be grasped to reveal the port. The only way is with your fingernails (my nails are not very long - this was not easy). Then there was the controls... 3 side by side buttons that are positioned on a piece that's out of view (when wearing them). So you have to feel for the buttons.

Also, a case would have been a nice addition.

title: Sound is clear... lacks a little on bass
text:
Nice bluetooth speaker. It's portable... charged quickly and seems to hold the charge well (still going strong after a couple hours.) Neither my phone, nor my echo unit had any problem pairing in bluetooth mode.

As for sound, I think the sound is good... maybe not great... but definitely good. Its sound is clear and reasonably accurate... In comparison to the echo dot (gen 3), the echo is definitely fuller sounding... with more low end. But then, the echo is less portable (requires ac power) so I guess that's the trade off. Since its physically bigger, I was thinking of using this as an alternate speaker for the echo, but I truly think the echo dot sounds better. So this'll get some use as a portable bluetooth speaker... but not as an echo speaker substitute.

It comes with a nice case and both "recharge" and "auxiliary in" cables. I posted a pic with an echo dot sitting on top of it for visual comparison. It's clearly bigger... but still a manageable size.

title: Nice laptop protection in a minimal package
text: Nice case for my wife's laptop. The Targus case is of sturdy construction and is exactly the right size for her Acer laptop (in fact, it's a little snug). Zippered from both sides and a pouch for accesories on the front. The rear has straps for attaching to your roll around carry on bag. The 2 strap style handles join from either side to form a sturdy grip. Padding is adequate and should provide proper protection. Otherwise, this is minimal, size wise... which is a good thing. No worries about the laptop flipping around inside and it takes up little space when traveling

title: Great mouse!
text:
I've been using an old wired mouse with my laptop for so long, the thing has been jumping and skipping around on my screen! I decided it was finally time to scrap that worn out thing.

Of course, there's a certain convenience that comes with a wireless mouse... especially with a laptop, but I've tried them before and my biggest problem has always been that I forget to turn them off... so they're never charged and ready to go when I am. After reading some reviews, I decided to give this Logitech a try...

I have to say, I'm REALLY happy with this mouse. First of all, setup couldn't have been easier. I plugged the little reciever thing in a usb port, put in the supplied AA battery and turned it on - voila! It's working!

It tracks just like my wired mouse used to (when it still worked properly) and is accurately responsive. Using it took absolutley no "getting used to" as the thing does (and goes) exactly where I want it to. But the big feature... it's "auto-off" works great! I've been using it for months and the battery's holding up just fine. I couldn't be happier.

title: Fits my 17" laptop nicely
text:
I bought a 17" laptop awhile back because I thought it would be great to have the nice large screen... etc... etc... I don't take it many places, but when I do, it's always a problem. I should have thought of that before, I suppose, but on vacations, I tend to just find a suitcase to squeeze it into. On a daytrip, it may end up in a random bag in the trunk - hardly a way to keep it safe. Well, I finally got myself a proper bag that seems to have been made for it!

The bag itself is not heavily padded. In fact, I would describe it as "adequately padded". That is, it has enough padding to protect the laptop, but not so much that I would get careless with how I handle the thing. As for fit? Perfect! The laptop goes right in without difficulty but still doesn't seem to flop around inside. It also has extra pockets both inside and out - on both sides of the computer compartment. The outside pockets are zippered - and there's a shoulder strap that comes with it as well. Plain black... it's understated, as it should be. I like it... I'd recommend it.

title: Good sound - good price
text:
I'm somewhat particular about my music and my headphones and have specific things I look for. I'll try to touch on those items in this review.

Sound Quality: obviously most important. I look for solid bass (not boomy or hyped). And clear trebles (not sizzling or hyped). These headphones performed okay on both counts although it did seem the bass was a little hyped. I have some expensive headphones that these did not compare favorably to. I also look for general clarity in vocals... here, they did good... nothing nasally or buried in the mix. The exception came when turning on the noise reduction circuit. More on that later.

Comfort: okay, I have a big head (size xxl hat). So comfort is important to me. These headphones are adequate in that regard. I had to extend them fully, but at full extension they fit me properly and comfortably, sealing off around the ear. They did not completely surround my ears as some studio monitors do, but they did cover my ears. The padding is decent and I was able to listen for a reasonable amount of time before they became uncomfortable pressing on the perimeter of my ear. If your head/ears are smaller, my guess is they'd be plenty comfortable.

Noise reduction: I'm not used to using this feature and wasn't sure how to test it, so I simply sat down next to an air cleaner I have in my home and tried turning noise reduction on and off to see what happened. There was definitely a reduction in the noise... mainly in the lower frequencies. It didnt completely eliminate the sound of the blowing air, but what was left was a thinned out version of the original noise. It was definitely an improvement in the level of noise. The only thing I didnt care for was that there seemed to be an impact on the sound of the music also. Again, the noise reduction thinned the music and left it a little nasally.

Controls: straight forward controls. Theres a slider to turn noise reduction on and off and an adjacent button to activate the phone function. Since the phone button was just below the slider, I kept accidentally turning on the phone when trying to activate the noise reduction. Better button placement would have helped.

Overall, I was reasonably impressed with these headphones. Especially considering the price, they seem to do well. They come with a nice, soft sided carry case and needed cables. I expect I'll get some good use from these.

title: Good sound at a good price
text:
I'm somewhat particular about my music and my headphones and have specific things I look for. I'll try to touch on those items in this review.

Sound Quality: obviously most important. I look for solid bass (not boomy or hyped). And clear trembles (not sizzling or hyped). These headphones performed admirably on both counts. I have some expensive headphones that these compare favorably to. I also look for general clarity in vocals... nothing nasally or buried in the mix. Vocals are natural and enjoyable.

Comfort: okay, I have a big head (size xxl hat). So comfort is important to me. These headphones are adequate in that regard. I had to extend them fully, but at full extension they fit me properly and comfortably, sealing off around the ear. These headphones are advertised as an over the ear design, but with my big ears, they did not completely surround my ears as some studio monitors do, but they did cover my ears. The padding is decent and I was able to listen for about an hour before they became uncomfortable pressing on the perimeter of my ear.

Noise reduction: I'm not used to using this feature and wasn't sure how to test it, so I simply sat down next to an air cleaner I have in my home and tried turning noise reduction on and off to see what happened. There was definitely a reduction in the noise... mainly in the lower frequencies. It didnt completely eliminate the sound of the blowing air, but what was left was a thinned out version of the original noise. It was definitely an improvement... and with very little impact on the sound of the music I was listening to.

Wireless: pairing was pretty straightforward (I guess that's typical these days) and the wireless aspect suffered no dropouts anywhere in the room. Going up to a different floor in the house did cause dropouts, though. So I guess that's about the limit.

Overall, I was impressed with these headphones. Especially considering the price, they seem to do well. They come with a carry bag and needed cables. I expect I'll get some good use from these.

title: Suits my needs perfectly...
text:
I know this considered an electronics bag, but i actually bought it for an alternate use. I needed a place to store some bonsai tools, cutters, trimmers, wires, etc. I also have a couple of light, ph and moisture meters. So it was the size and adjustable dividers that got my business.

This bag was exactly as described and suited my needs perfectly. Lightweight, flexable and good looking too... And all my bonsai tools are now stashed in one place.

title: Perfect fit replacement pads.
text: These are exact replacements for tge original Sennheiser headphone pads.  I really like my Sennhwisers and have been using them for years.  The pads had become stretched and sloppy, frequently falling off, etc.  When i decided to replace the pads, I almost went with an alternate dye to the hefty price on these genuine pads (They are, after all, just foam).  But in the end, I decided to go ahead and get the originals... now I'm glad I did.  They fit perfectly and seem to have turned my old used Senns into a new-like set!  I can find no fault with these pads.  I'll take away one star for the price... leaving a four star rating.

title: Nice quality floor lamps... great for grow lights.
text:
I bought 2 of these to use with grow lights in our living room. I wanted something that would be adjustable, allow a "straight in" insertion of an led grow light, and be fully adjustable.

These lamps assemble easily and seem nice and sturdy. They look nice too... fit and finish is good, especially considering the price. The head itself is plenty big enough for an led grow light. The 3 sections don't extend in and out individually, but they do adjust by rotating at the joint. Having 3 sections therefore allows a wide range of adjustment to position the lamp head where you need it.

title: Nice headphones... uncolored sound!
text: As a musician with a home studio, I needed some new headphones to track with. These came with good reviews, so I decided to give them a try. Good move on my part... they have a good uncolored sound, cover the ears completely and even come with 2 cables (1 coiled, 1 straight).  I do have a big head (size xxl hat) and proportional ears. I wouldn't say these are "roomy", but they do just cover my ears and seal around them nicely to minimize any sound leaking.

title: Great sounding wireless headphones...
text:
I'm a musician with a home studio. With several sets of headphones all getting old, I decided to invest in some new ones. I've had good luck with Sennheiser in the past so I wanted to check out what they were currently offering. After reading lots of reviews, I decided to give these rs175 rf's a try. I was a little leery of them being wireless but trusting in the Sennheiser name, bought them anyway. I wanted them for general recording and playback.

Pros: Excellent sound... flat, uncolored. Clear detailed, etc. All the qualities I've come to expect from Sennheiser. Wireless setup was virtually nothing... plug in the base where you'd plug in the headphones and you're done. Turn on the headphones and start listening. The stand serves as the charging station and placing the headphones on it is straightforward and secure... not clumsy at all. I have a fairly large head with proportional sized ears... (size xxl hat). The ear pads fit completely over my ears and completely seal very nicely around them. You won't be bothered by outside sounds, nor will your spouse be bothered by what you're listening to. A quick check of the range shows I can go anywhere in my average size home without losing the signal. (I didn't try going outside).

Cons: The only negative is that there is a bit of latency. If you use them for listening to music or even tv, you won't notice it... but if you turn on speakers at the same time and listen to both, you'll notice a very slight lag in the headphones.

Bottom line: these are excellent headphones, quality of build and quality of sound are both first rate. But if that latency is an issue, you probably shouldn't be looking at wireless anyway (I suspect this occurs on any wireless system).

title: Samsung 64 g memory card - I'm Happy With It
text: Well, not a lot to say... package arrived quickly, as I've come to expect from Amazon. Wrestled with the packaging a little to get the memory card out, plugged it into my Samsung Edge and I was good to go. Couldn't be easier to get more memory on the phone. I'm happy with it.

title: Inconsistent, may serve as a watch independently, better.
text: Losses Bluetooth connections often. Missed texts. No way to return texts. No calling or phone alerts. Camera shutter doesn't work. Unable to correct the calendar date. I thought I was in April when I was in January. Otherthan a cute watch. Not much cellular connectivity uses.

title: Cute little antennae
text: Works well. I currently have a 3’ non-retractable antennae. It makes going thru garages and car washes a problem. This short antennae pulls the same stations I listen to while being cute and compact. Only minus is the exposed base on my car’s antennae. The short antennae rests on a larger base. Not a precise fit. Wonder if that’ll damage the car when wet. Anyone please advise.

title: Works perfectly
text: Easy to use. Has extra ports for charging.

title: Still staticky in rural areas
text: Not a bad antennae. In rural areas, still have a little static. Unfortunately; compared with the slightly longer antennae; 5”; the quality is slightly less efficient.

title: Can only hold 7 songs max.
text: Device times out after a few seconds. Though the library held "24 songs". It only plays the same 7 songs on a loop. Only holds 2 hours of charge time after full charge. Disappointing.

title: Adhesive came off after 1 month.
text: Adhesive losses it’s grip after 1 month or so. All the stickiness is on the glass.

title: It works.
text: Huge to wrestle with when folding back. Came wrinkled. Imperfections are easily shown.

title: Huge!
text: Difficult to fold back and sometimes the background is still too narrow.

title: Failed.
text: Didn’t work.

title: Works well so far.
text: Have high hopes about this system. Only problem is the 5 sec delay for live transmission. By the time I can react, the perpetrator has already done the deed. Or vice versa, didn’t catch the perpetrator in the act bcuz the camera only records a few secs.

title: Not very versatile.
text: Needs plug in. Couldn’t get it to work cuz the plug and the QR code couldn’t connect.

title: Didn’t work.

It has connectios for two apple device, twoUSBC for the newer for Androids and 2 usb a for the older generation droid. I have personally used this to charge our 10 in Samsung tablet, Samsung Note 20 ultra, iPhone 12 , an older iphone (think it is an 8) as well as galaxy S20 and it works great with each of these. We can charge 5 at the same time no problem. No overheating. The cables are well made and durable. There are no signs of distress from being shoved in my purse or mangled by a 6 year old. We'll be buying more to use at my charging stations around the house. Great quality product for a great price!

text:
Update: December 2022 and still perfect condition. Never using "paper like" again. I've also referred a ton of people to this screen protector!

I'm an artist, so I'm drawing on my iPad for hours every day. I still haven't had to change my apple pencil tip since I got this screen protector. When I had the Paperlike, not only was it extremely expensive (like $40 for a couple), it has completely chewed up the apple tip within a couple weeks.
The screen protector doesn't look "dirty"... It's MATTE, BRO. It will pick up your sticky fingerprints, if you don't ever wash your hands and you're literally looking for imperfections.

Also, the Paperlike protector would constantly give me eye strain because of the weird diffusion of the light through the mat... This screen protector has never given me weird eye strain OR eye fatigue.
Highly recommend, 10/10

title: Tons of options to control these AND can lay down with them!!!
text:
So, a lot of people complained about the headphones pausing for voice etc.. there's an app you can download where you can turn off auto pausing, auto turn off, and you can even turn off the noise cancelling. I personally can't handle the noise cancelling aspect, as it hurts my ears and gives me weird head pressure.. so I'm super happy I can turn that off.

My headphones lasted about 3 days, listening about 4-6 hours per day. The headphones only take about 30 minutes to charge as well.
They are suuuuuper comfortable.

I am a smaller person, and a big issue I have with most headphones is they're way too big for my head, so I can't lean my head back onto the bed or couch with them on.
Not with these! I can lean my head back FINALLY, and I barely feel like I'm wearing them.

I had beats before this, and they hurt my ears and my head because they were so weirdly shaped and tight. Like my ears would literally fall asleep. I seriously don't even notice I'm wearing them. No tightness, no pressure, no ears falling asleep.

The case they come with is high quality, and it comes with an aux cord in case you want to listen that way!

The sound cancelling is... Amazing. Literally no sound got through. I thought my husband was messing with me and just mouthing words at me, but no.. he was speaking quite loudly.

Highly, highly recommend. Probably my favorite out of all the ones I've tried.. and I've tried about 7 just this past year.
Splurge and get them, you will not regret it.

title: Before you buy please keep in mind of few things
text:
Please keep in mind the service is friendly. They will take back item, but there is a 20% restocking fee. The price of sending it back and the fee does not make it worth it. You lose money either way if you wind up thinking that you will get a hard, clear, LCD screen protector and find out the only hard cover is the one that acts as a shade to the screen. Once you close that part, you don't see your LCD screen.

It's not so much the service afterwards. It's the service of not being more clear on the words and the picture before hand. I had 2 options. Either buy from another site that actually has a hard, clear, LCD screen or from this one which I've thought was that and then some. Instead the screen cover is just the flimsy sticker that everyone sells for a few bucks. Those don't stick on very well without bubbles showing up. The few tries didn't go as smoothly as one would like so it makes the screen look worse.

If you want to buy the black cover/hood, the flimsy sticker for the LCD screen and the lens cleaner all in one then this is the set for you. If you're wanting a clear, hard, LCD screen protector to protect your LCD screen and camera better, this is not the one.

The idea is to invest in something that would protect the camera better.

Yes, the items did come within estimated time. But I've found it odd that it had a sticker on there stating it's time sensitive. It took 9 days to be delivered from CA when it usually takes 4-7 days for things to get to my state.

4 stars for the courteous reply in trying to resolve the matter, but the restocking fee isn't good.
1 star in not being clear about wording and pictures that is misleading.
3 stars for the items being alright.

In no way that I'm saying this is a bad seller. Just wish some things were more clear. I want future buyers to know what they're getting unless they want to be disappointed. For those who want a clear, hard, LCD screen cover for the Sony HX200, go to that well known auction site. But it's not sold as an auction which is good.

title: 2ND PAIR THAT DIDN'T WORK!  POOR QUALITY & PERHAPS HIT OR MISS!
text:
These were meant to be a birthday gift for me in October, courtesy of my husband. We purchased the first set of these because the Jlab ones were hurting my ears (Jlab have always worked great for us, but I have small ear canals) and these Eddkie ones are advertised for small ears. Furthermore, reviews suggested they've worked well for others with small ear canals. I found them to be fantastically comfortable in my ears! So, I'm incredibly disappointed that two sets of them were both faulty!!

I didn't write a review when the first pair were bad. That can happen, afterall. My husband and I decided to request a replacement but were surpised to discover when we requested a return that wasn't an option. This, unfortunately, left us seeking our refund several times over approximately six weeks - very unusual for Amazon in our experience. So, you can imagine how disappointed we are to find out this second set is faulty too!! It would seem again to be a battery issue with not holding a charge. Are these made with poor batteries?

After being charged in their case, they worked fine the first night for two hours before being put back in their case. The second night, not yet recharged, they ran out of power after 5 minutes use. So, after reading the instructions that they hold power for 24 hours 'in their case', we thought maybe they only work for a couple of hours out of their case. So, we charged them again before use. This time, however, they worked for 5 seconds at most and died! When activated, the ear buds said 'power on' and 5 seconds later 'power off'. Now they won't come on again. They are completely dead! We tried pairing them with both a tablet and phone and tried charging them again. We've checked and tried all the instructions but nothing works!

One faulty pair we can accept, but two suggests these are poor quality and perhaps hit or miss!

title: The folks at Roxant have thought of everything!
text:
The folks at Roxant have thought of everything! I wanted a monocular because I only have sight in one eye. I wanted a lightweight scope I could hold and focus with the same hand. I love the focus wheel and the hand strap. When the strap is tight, I don’t even need to grip the scope, just lift it and hold it against my eye.

The size is very workable, and the weight is ideal. The overall quality is great. It feels very solidly built, the lens caps are sturdy and thick and I love that they attach to the scope so that I don’t have to worry about misplacing them.

I also love that it came with accessories that I would have had to buy aftermarket. The case is sized right, the phone attachment in particular is very solid. The tripod is a bit flimsy, but probably stable enough for light use. In any case, it doesn’t take any space in the case and doesn’t add any weight, so I pack it in with the scope. Sometimes I use it as a handle for the scope and it works well.

But here’s the best part: the optics are great! I have an Eagle Solo which just isn’t stable enough against my eye for me to enjoy, and is a pain to focus. The Roxant Falcon gives me just as good vision and magnification as the Eagle. At a fraction of the price, especially when considering the accessories!

I hesitated to order this, since I had a good quality monocular already, but it had so many features I wanted from a monocular (focus wheel, strap, accessories), for the price I figured I’d give it a try. It vastly exceeded my expectations. It will now be my go-to scope for everything.

Thanks Roxant!!!

text:
I've owned these cameras since March and would not buy them again. In addition to a large proportion of defective products, Yi offers no phone support and very bad tech support via email for customers who do not subscribe to their cloud plans. Furthermore, their recent (major) software update killed one of my cameras (I have six at the moment, minus the one that died).

Lastly, after the September 2021 software update, they started hijacking user data unless you buy their cloud plans. I save motion data (pictures and short videos) to my own, personal microSD card, and Yi/Kami no longer allows users to access past motion detection pictures and videos (their software now limits access to all but the past several hours of data) UNLESS you purchase one of their cloud plans.

Personally, I do not want pictures and videos inside my home uploaded to their cloud or anyone's cloud.
The lack of support and data hijacking is just pure greed. I spent almost $500 on my cameras (indoor and outdoor wireless).

Now that USB-C is becoming common, I needed some cables for those items too. Enter this cost-effective assortment of short -C cables.

title: Good picture (a bit dim), passable UI, lots of apps, software updates still coming 5 years on!
text:
This is a nice TV and a good value.

I give LG great credit for supporting this unit with software and app dates five years into ownership. Ours is a 2017 model.

We have no problems with it. Picture and sound quality are good, and as a smart TV it offers lots of apps that also are updated even today. The user interface is reasonably responsive. Its viewing angle is generous and there are no display artifacts. It works fine with our WiFi (which, in this site, is sort of entry-level, about 10Mbps).

Built into the unit is an IPTV app! This offers a wealth of live channels. All are legitimate, nothing pirated here. So cable-cutters aren't lacking for "broadcast" content.

A few small quibbles: The brightness could be a few notches brighter for daytime use. The Xfinity app no longer supports this 2017-vintage TV, but all the streaming apps work fine and are still updated: Amazon Prime, Netflix, Disney, AppleTV+, Hulu, Peacock, Pluto... Also, some apps and menus are easier to navigate (and get out of!) than others; some manus lack a clear "dismiss" button, for example.

I have noticed no ads-- one reviewer here complained about them. Perhaps it's a regional thing? (I'm in the U.S.) Or, maybe there's a setting somewhere that invites ads in. In any case, that annoyance has not emerged in our usage.

I'm sure there are better units out there, especially now--five years later--but this is entirely satisfactory, and I'd certainly consider LG for future purchases.

title: Didn’t adhere well for me

title: Very superior lightweight laptop / Made in China
text:
I'm coming to this machine as a Mac user who needed a light-but-powerful Windows machine for some specific business purposes.

Bottom line: I'm impressed.

First, the basics. This is a thin/lightweight model with a 4-core i7 CPU, a 14 inch screen, and Intel's latest integrated graphics. Its body is a black magnesium affair, good-looking and really lightweight. The black finish is satiny and looks a bit like plastic but is far more rigid.

This laptop is based on Intel’s new “Eco” i7 chipset that runs cooler and more efficiently than Intel’s recent offerings. I’ve hammered it pretty hard and it’s been stable, cool and quiet. My model's specs are quite good for a lightweight business laptop, with a proper 1TB NVMe SSD and 32GB RAM.

For comparison purposes, in terms of price and features it’s roughly comparable to a current-model M1-based MacBook Air. Now, an Air with 16GB RAM (which, given its ARM architecture, is functionally equivalent to about 32GB on a Wintel machine) and 1TB SSD lists for $1509 direct from Apple. The LG was about $1750 at the time of my purchase. It has no biometric login gizmo, which is okay because for some reason the Windows world has yet to implement one that works half as well as Apple’s TouchID. It has the expected webcam, microphone and speakers… all of decent quality and again comparable to the Air’s. It has two USB-C/Thunderbolt 4 ports and two USB-A 3.2 ports. There’s an SD card reader and of course some spiffy WiFi and Bluetooth. It has a 14” screen, slightly larger than the Air’s. Resolution is similar, and I have no complaints about color fidelity or brightness with either machine.

The differences are most obvious in the details.

Keyboard
Both machines have truly excellent keyboards. Both can keep up with my frenetic speed-typist pounding and have a good feel and throw. But the LG’s keyboard backlighting surrounds each key with an unwanted glow that looks a bit cheap. So, the keyboard scores maybe an 8 on the Apple scale of 1-10.

Trackpad
Similarly, the trackpad is the best I’ve used on a Windows machine but is still behind Apple’s in terms of the hardware’s fluidity and consistent behavior. Fortunately, on the software side, Windows has advanced mightily in terms of gestures and support of things like multiple virtual desktops, so this machine can replicate most of my Mac-centric workflow without too much getting-used-to, if you spend some time fiddling in the setup screens. Score: another 8.

Display
The screen is fine, glossy like the Air's but not as glasslike and flat. Intel's latest integrated GPU is more than adequate for my purposes, and I've noticed no stuttering or frame limitations. Another 8.

Construction
The magnesium chassis is stiff and solid while remaining commendably lightweight and thin. The bezels are very thin as well; the top bezel contains the tiny camera and two nearly invisible microphone apertures. It merits a 9 on the Air's jewel-like reference 10.

Power
Battery life is good, not up to MacBook M1 standards, but looks like I'll top 6 hours of pretty intensive multitasking use with the screen on full brightness. Charging is via USB-C. The LG charger is compact and comes with long AC and DC cables. Call this another 8, with the Air demerited to an 9 as battery-life leader Apple no longer provides a long AC cord.

Summary
So far so good. After two Dells that were unsatisfactory and poorly supported, two HPs that died young, and after watching Lenovo go downhill, this seemed a good choice.

I'd certainly recommend it if a Mac is not an option for your use. The Air remains my top choice and is a better value, and the Genius Bars are wonderful for support and getting questions answered.

So far there's been only one surprise: despite LG being a Korean company, this laptop is made in China... like the Air.

title: Works great with the "Chromecast with Google TV"
text:

Since the CCwGTV has minimal storage, I bought this to allow me to use a well-reviewed USB3 thumb-drive (https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B08MB9G2GM) to boost its storage by 128GB for recording with TiviMate and such.

It works great! To do the same, use your computer to format the drive in FAT32. The CCwGTV will recognize it and, in its storage settings pane, offer to reformat the drive to ext3 and treat it as internal storage. The process takes a couple of minutes and then you're good to go.

This particular hub is more energy-efficient than most, and it works well with the 7.5W power plug that comes with the CCwGTV. You can of course use a bigger supply if you want, but the point is you probably don't need to.

The gigabit Ethernet port just works, too.

text: My well-traveled original-issue Apple USB-C charging cable (for my 15" MacBook Pro) finally started acting up after more than a year.  This one looked good on Amazon, and it is.  It supports full-power charging for this machine, which many/most cables don't.  The 90-degree connector is wonderful.  I've had this cable for a few months now and no problems.

title: Impressive speeds, no thermal throttling, great value
text:
I bought the 1TB version of this NVMe SSD to do a Carbon Copy backup of my end-2018 MacBook Pro's internal 1TB SSD, which is about 80% full. Starting from scratch, after formatting in APFS (which is eye-blink fast to do), this drive did the full backup job in about 20 minutes! It showed no signs of thermal throttling.

If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this is a fantastic drive and an amazing value, based on my early experience. I'll update this review if anything changes, but so far, I'm delighted. It is a worthy companion to my beastly 6-core Mac, and that's the highest possible praise.

title: Extreme speed for Thunderbolt 3-equipped PCs
text:
If you have a Thunderbolt 3-equipped computer, this drive provides speeds approaching the highest-end built-in SSDs. Case in point: I have a 2018 MacBook Pro with top specs. Its internal SSD is a screamer. And, as you can see from my screen shots, the X5 is right in the same neighborhood. These tests were run on my computer while it was running a bunch of other things (Word, Excel, VMWare Fusion, Mail.app, Safari with about 15 tabs open), so it represents real-world use.

And, as you can see, the X5 is really fast. If you need speed and have Thunderbolt 3, this is a great drive.

Installation was easy. My Mac recognized the drive right away. I could've just used it, but Samsung provides a utility on the drive for enabling its onboard encryption and keeping its firmware up to data. Recommended.

(But do make sure your computer has Thunderbolt 3. You can't tell just by looking at the ports, as TB3 is implemented as a superset of USB-C. So, Thunderbolt 3 is USB-C but the converse is not true. Similarly, previous-rev Thunderbolt interfaces aren't forward-compatible to TB3 devices. Some of the one-star reviews of this drive are clearly from folks who didn't know these issues.)

title: Worked first time, no fuss no muss
text: The best thing I can say is that there's little to say.  Plugged it in; it worked.  Happy.

text: I travel way too much on business and always have this with me.  Its laptop compartment carries two 15" laptops (which I sometimes need to do); no problem. title: This is the real deal, Thunderbolt 3 speeds PLUS high-power charging
text:
"USB" has always been synonymous with confusion, and USB-C is no different. Add Thunderbolt capability as a superset of USB-C and it rapidly grows even more perplexing. That charging cable that comes with your amazing new MacBook Pro? It's good for USB-2 data throughput only, sorry. Need something faster? You can find it but it probably won't charge the computer. Or it'll be really short.

This cable has it all: Tidy USB-C connectors, full Thunderbolt 3 40Gbps capability (roughly 100 times faster than USB-2), 100W power-carrying capability, 6 foot/2 meter length.

Add the four-year Square Trade warranty available at checkout for something like a buck seventy more, just in case some wayward schnauzer chews it up.

title: Decent upgrade!  Some nitpicks though.
text:
I upgraded from a year-old, previous-generation Paperwhite, mostly to gain the new inverted white-on-black screen mode that Amazon insists requires new hardware and to have built-in Audible playback over Bluetooth.

This unit ticks most of boxes, and after some debate I've decided to give it five stars, but there are some imperfections worth knowing about. It's mostly good, though, and often great.

Battery life
No complaints. In several long international flights, I've yet to run it down more than about 30%, either in long reading sessions with the front-light or in lengthy Audible playback sessions over Bluetooth.

Audible content
The Audible player works brilliantly. Excellent sound, simple controls (including playback-speed adjustment). It does work best if you don't have a screen password enabled, though-- that will get in the way if you just want to rewind a few seconds to catch something you missed. Playback proceeds even if you have a case closed, which shuts off the front-light and saves battery charge.

There's no headphone jack-- this is for Bluetooth only. Fine with me. I have Bluetooth-enabled hearing aids (cochlear implants, actually) and it's a true joy to be able to listen to books on this device. Thanks, Amazon.

Screen
The screen is pretty much the same as my previous-generation Paperwhite's, meaning not bad but could use more contrast when reading in a dark room using the front-light. Outdoors or in well-lit areas, it's fantastic and mostly glare-free.

More seriously, the lack of contrast mars the new Paperwhite's valuable ability to invert text to white-on-black. This is a marvelous accessibility feature for those with "floaters", vitreous separation and other vision issues. Unfortunately, when used with the front-light in a darkened room, such as when reading at night or in a darkened airplane, the black background is more of a medium gray. So this new feature is less helpful than it could be. In fairness, poor contrast is characteristic of today's e-ink displays, which provide perhaps 8:1 contrast. If Amazon can significantly improve the contrast, I'd upgrade again in a flash.

The screen is plastic and will scratch. Keep it clean and use a case. Even with a case (I prefer one of the various "origami" cases available here, which allow the Kindle to prop itself upright) it will fit nicely into a pocket.

The touch-screen user interface is the same as the previous-gen Paperwhite's. I'm not a huge fan of it; too easy to touch it when you don't mean to, and end up on the wrong page. But, the earlier button-driven Kindles had sort of the same problem, so whatever. I recommend a simple fix, perhaps as a Settings option: require a double-tap rather than a single-tap. How about it, Amazon?

Connectivity
The 4G/LTE capability is a nice speed upgrade from the previous 3G connectivity. Downloading Audible content requires a WiFi connection as before.

Unfortunately I'm finding that global connectivity with the new 4G hardware is inferior to the previous-gen's 3G radio. For example, my year-old 3G Paperwhite connected without issue in Saigon, but the new one won't.

The user interface for turning Airplane Mode on and off could be improved. As it is, engaging Airplane Mode cuts all connectivity including Bluetooth. So if you're in the middle of listening to a book when the time comes to put your gizmos in Airplane Mode, it will cut your connection. Better to do what the latest iPhones do, and have the device learn if your usage prefers that Bluetooth remain active.

Browser
It's high time for Amazon to replace the minimally-functional "Experimental Browser" with something more useful. I get it that Kindles are all about battery life and browsers can be major energy hogs, but c'mon, it's 2019, and this browser feels like a relic from 1996. Probably is.

title: Nice case, works well, really nice red
text: At time time I upgraded to the 10th-gen/2018 Kindle Paperwhite, this was one of the few compatible origami cases available.  Previously, for my earlier-generation Paperwhite, I'd had a Fintie-branded origami case.  This one is lighter-weight and has the same functionality.  It protects the Kindle well.  It integrates magnets that turn the Kindle off and on when the case is closed and opened.  The "origami" vertical stand is not quite vertical but is stable and works well on airline tray-tables. title: An Apple-class clever engineering detail makes this a good choice
text:
So far, very impressive. The magnetic breakaway connector is tiny, and its 87W-capable cable is lightweight and flexible-- way more so than the Apple USB-C charging cable that came with my 15" MacBook Pro and its 87W charger. It looks good, fully Apple-class in design and construction. But what sets this apart is a clever technical detail:

It uses a six-pin design approach that splits the charging current between two pairs of pins at the corners of the pin array, cutting the current through each by half. That is clever and I think unique, and it should make life easier on the port and probably on the Mac by reducing arcing and generally providing a better, more robust connection.

The magnet is nice and strong, and the L-shaped cable configuration lowers the torque on the connector, reducing unwanted disconnects while ensuring it breaks away when you want it to.

As with most USB-C charging cables and magnetic-breakaway adaptors, this is for charging only-- no data will traverse it. If you want a MagSafe-like adaptor that will handle both 87W charging and high-speed data, check out the Snapnator, also available here on Amazon. I have one of those too, and it's excellent, but it sticks straight out from the Mac and is more prone to disconnects, partly because I use it with the Apple charging cable that is so puzzlingly heavy and stiff.

My only issue with the design of this cable is that its strain relief construction is identical to Apple's, meaning the cable will eventually wear at the edge of the strain-relief. That's a common issue with charging cables and something we've all come to live with but it's still regrettable. I do wish cable designers would pay better attention to it, but it's universal, even with Apple's premium-priced cables.

The cable came in a nice little zipper case made of some sort of rigid formed fabric covered with a rubbery coating. Unfortunately there was a paper bar-code sticker on the case, and when I peeled it off, off came the coating. Ah well.

I'll post any updates over time.

title: Five Stars
