text: Was too hard to remove the gopro to get to the mem card, almost broke the gopro getting it out. If you can, just take the connector door off and use a cable to download. Forget taking it in and out for battery change, just expect to have the down time to recharge from a cable with the gopro in this unit.

title: Works, good price
text: The spade connectors are different from the APC units wiring, but just smaller so it still works. Fits fine and has been working properly for a month now (the APC batt shows charged, but the unit would immediately shut down on a power-outtage)

title: Two-days old, loaded with backups, now can't access, no customer svc available...
text: I suppose it's what I get for trying Toshiba. Their security SW is total GARBAGE. Now the drive can't be seen, reports error: "cannot execute this software because the required service program has not been started," when you try to access the drive by opening the security program. When you try to start the security program on your main system, you get the SAME ERROR!!! So..., the drive is secure alright. So secure no one will ever be able to access ANYTHING on it again! Seagate??

title: Too big for most portable drives, drive just bangs around inside this
text:
This will NOT protect your drive in drops and bangs as there is way too much space inside, so the drive just bounces around inside it, allow it to accelerate a bit before hitting the inside of the case when dropped. If I wanted a case with enough room to carry a change of clothes along with my drive, I'd just buy luggage..., sheesh...

See pic, you'll notice over an inch of extra space, top to bottom, that's what I have a problem with.

title: Door is different color, missing the kept screw, but fits, sort-of - Brittle mat'l
text:
The rails are a harder rubber than the stock T-pad and the ones I got were a bit deformed, you can fudge them in, for sure, but overall, the kit is not very hear T-pad quality. For $10 it'll do if you need a tray or the cover, but the cover is a barely-fit kind of deal and is a graphite/grayish black, not the darker black of the Lenovo, so you can tell it's a replacement. Comes with a bag of screws, but no circlip to hold the HD cover screw in or on, just locktite it and don't remove it often I guess.

---------------

Update Aug 2019: Bought another set for yet another T430. This time the door I received was almost exactly the Thinkpad black color, still fits kind of wonky, but it fits. Still no kept screw for the door, so make sure you locktite the threads. Also, the rails I received this time were soft rubber, not the hard-as-rock rubber of the last order. So, YMMV on what you get, but hopefully, they corrected the issues with the last batch.

Update, Sept 2019: Door started rattling the other day, unscrewed and now see why. At some point, the material gave way and the boss for the screw broke out (see pics). This didn't happen when installing, it happened a few weeks after. From stress on the plastic I suppose. Just junk. I'd avoid this item, find another seller.

UPDATE Oct 2021: Boss around holding screw broke out and door fell off. Again, material is VERY thin and brittle. Not for long-term use.

title: WD Black drives are the best, these portables..., are not...
text: Have many decades experience with HD's, from 12" winchesters to huge 80meg drives to Maxtors, etc., you had to be careful with most. The WD Black drives have always been the most reliable and solid drives available. Now in this era of needing large-capacity, portable drives (film/editing) we need reliability even more as there is much more overall data that we can lose. Well..., I've depended on the Passport drives for on-the-road backups, but no more. I've had two of three fail on me over the last few years. Not sure what's up with WD, but these drives are NOT reliable. I have the latest gen (just as the pic in this ad) and one partition takes up to five-minutes to show up once drive is connected. I can still get to and see the data, but it's a slow process. When the drive was new (a year ago), it was fast, now it's a slug and acting like it's giving errors (light continuously blinks, locks up the OS, etc.), so I'm looking at other mfg's for external drives. Not willing to lose 4tb of film that can't be replicated. My advice; I'd shy from these and try Tosh or Samsung.

title: Bought as used, still under Canon warranty and UNOPENED
text: This is my new go-to body after destroying a 7D and finding the 6D Mark II complete rubbish. Seriously, this crop sensor body has more DR than a FF? Canon used the most sub-standard sensor (prob 5D rejects) they could in the 6D MkII..., avoid that POS at all costs. Anyway, this is about the 80D and it's a fine camera, not much more than the 70D, but a better processing engine and a few upgrades for those who don't have a 70D. If you have a 70D, this wouldn't be worth the "upgrade" to you, just subtle changes, nothing worth the cost of the "upgrade." If you want a do-it-all crop sensor camera, this is it.

title: A cheap cable that works 100%
text: Cable was cheap, but have been using it for a month now and all is fine.

title: Seems high quality, worked perfectly (so far...)
text: Fit perfectly, works fine, moves air.

title: MUCH taller than it appears, def won't cut it for "personal item" on airlines
text: Seemed OK quality, but was VERY tall. Would not qualify for "personal item" on most airlines.

title: Does what it's supposed to do. Fits properly.
text: Works. And much cheaper than the Canon equiv. Fits, works, no issues. Save some cash.

title: Not as the picture. Not mono, has two ear bud tubes, neither are coiled.
text: This is just an acoustic stereo headset. That is bulky.

title: Sharp as a tack. These feel heavy and sturdy, but they're not. Read review
text: The actual barrel that the mount base (stainless steel) mounts to is an engineering plastic. So even though it feels and looks all-metal, it's not. And an important piece is breakable plastic inside. The lens will separate from the mount if any hit is taken by the lens and that in-turn tears the flex cables, making a repair an expensive proposition. All in all though, it goes head to head with L-glass for sharpness, bokeh and light gathering. Wish it were a bit more of a range as 18-35 is pretty damn limiting at times.

title: Small and light, uses same charger as phone, so this is the one for travel
text: Seems fragile, but so far, no problems. Nice to not have the bulky stock one and this uses the same cable and charger as your Android (micro USB). For travel, this is the one to get. Light, small and so far, reliable.

title: Tested power output not close to advertised, but closer than clones!
text:
Had this and a Luiton UV-5RHP tested, both with 1w/4w/8w settings for power. Luiton: Low=700mw, High=1.5w
Baofung UV5R MK4 8w: Low=2w, High=5.8w
The genuine BF has markedly better power, but still doesn't match its output power claims. Doesn't have the cool screws on the front holding it together, feels a bit cheaper, but aftermarket batteries clip right on, unlike the clones where you have to play with and force them. So far, I'm impressed, just wish claims were something close to reality.

*Knocked one star for fragile plastic. Many cracks now and the belt clips (I've bought a few now) constantly break. S**ty plastic, very fragile.

title: Feels fairly well made, works fine, hard to seat, but stays put
text: Didn't have to mod this to get it to fit a Luiton LT-F9HP or a BF UV-5R. Works great with NiMH rechargeables. Seats firmly and never had a connection issue. Remember to use rechargeables or get a dummy battery, won't work with regular alkalines unless you use a dummy load for one. Worth every cent.

title: Like everyone says, has mold lines in middle of riding surface, still works fine
text: This works really well for what it is. Like others have said, the wheels have the parting line from injection molding right in the middle of the running surface, so if you have a light camera, it won't be smooth. Otherwise, it's well worth the price and made quite well.

title: Works like factory
text: Perfect hood and works just like a Canon.

title: Works like it should
text: Tried the cheapo cables with ZERO success, none would connect or even show the radio. This cable hooked right up and in five minutes I had my system downloaded, moded and uploaded. Just plain works, the cheap ones just don't and you'll find yourself playing musical drivers, plugging, unplugging both sides, restarting, etc.

title: High SWR, but solid build, a little better than stock
text:
These work almost as well as the 16" Nagoya's, but are actually usable and portable. Fits the Baofeng UV-5R, BF-F8HP and Luiton copies perfectly (mine had no gaps or threading issues).

Update: tested 3.4swr. 144.00/2m. Better than stock HT rubber duckie, but not much..., perhaps mine's a fake?

title: Fits like it was made for it (it was), with the correct radius on one corner
text: Fit and worked perfectly. The C100 Mk II has a radius on the upper left corner only, the other corners are square (ask Canon...). This protector has the proper radius and it matches flawlessly. As to longevity, time will tell. Will update review if it has issues.

title: Fan is an exact replacement (in detail) and is whisper quiet. So far, so good.
text: This came unbelievably fast from China. Saved about $50 by waiting about a week and a half, instead of the week turn-around the others claimed (at three-times the price!). Works flawlessly, totally quiet (but still moves a lot of air) and was CHEAP!! Will update this review if an issue arises, but it's identical to the stock, so I'm going to assume it's a stock fan that was overrun, or not bought and rebadged by Lenovo.

title: Drains batteries almost immediately.
text: Seems robust and well-built, but doesn't function properly. Sometimes you'll spend ten or fifteen minute re-seating and screwing, unscrewing this onto the camera body to get it to work. That's IF the thing hasn't completely drained the batteries just sitting, off. I'd pass on this one. You'll destroy your camera from frustration using this grip.

title: Drains batteries overnight, if everything off, intermittant connections
text:
Grip seems well-made and everything "worked" on it for a few weeks, but now it needs to be constantly reset into the camera to get it to power it and if left overnight with full batteries and every switch turned off (camera off, grip off), it will drain both batteries dead as hell. Seems well-built otherwise, but doesn't matter how well built something is if it doesn't work.

The 6D Mark II turned out to be a POS of a camera, worse EV than my crop sensor. Better off going for an 80D or selling one of your children to buy a 5D Mark 4. Or a Sony. Anything BUT the 6D Mark II (sent to Canon twice in the two months I've owned it, the camera is a step BACKWARDS from the original 6D!)

Sorry, went off on a tangent there. Bottom line is, this grip is a risk and the 6D II is an even worse risk.

title: Does what it says, will charge individually, or full-up. Light changes when each batt is charged.
text: This comes and feels so feather-light, you think they sent an empty plastic tray. But it works. And works well for charging one or eight batteries at a time. The lights for each individual battery are nice to have as you can pull a batt out to use as soon as it's charged. Overall, so far, works just as it claims and as intended. Well worth the investment.

title: Works "OK," but batts are hard to remove and you always have to reset to get cam to see
text: This grip, all in all, is a pretty well-made piece of equipment. Only a few issues, one is that you have to attach the little patch cable for the switches on the grip to operate the camera functions. Another is that the way the batteries install is a bit unique, doesn't use a tray like most, you open a trap-door and slide the batts in from the back. But the retention springs are a pain and you find yourself struggling to remove the glossy, smooth-sided batteries from the grip. The only other issue is that you occasionally find your cam body without power, even though you know the batts are good. This is your cue to unscrew the grip, slide it down, the slide it back up and screw it back in as tight as you can to "re-seat" the connections so it will work again. This always worked for me, but just re-tightening the thumb-screw didn't work at times. All in all, it's a decent grip, and for the price well-worth it. I just couldn't deal with bringing my camera up to shoot a fleeting moment and find myself fumbling around re-seating the grip so the camera has power. Then your shot's gone..., aggravating!

title: Batteries work, but ONLY charge with OAproda charger!
text: These batteries DO NOT charge with the Canon charger, they ONLY work with the OAproda charger they come with. Tried these this summer and seller said they were updating the batts to be compatible with the stock charger. Well..., they're not there yet. The good news, these batts do work, last about as long as the Canon battery and the charger is MUCH lighter and smaller than the stock Canon charger. Just a pain that they won't charge with the Canon charger when you need to charge three or more batts at once. Or if you don't have your USB cable for this charger and the Canon (with integral plug) is the only thing you have.

title: Weird battery loading from the rear, hard to remove batts
text: This works, for the most part. But there's no battery tray like many are used to, you load them through a trap-door at the back of the grip and there's so much friction on them, it's next to impossible to remove the batteries without a tool. I commend them for re-designing something new, a new way of loading batteries while reducing the amount of parts, but this was not a great integration.

title: Returned to Canon for repair for out-of-the-box sensor mis-calibration
text:
Tried to write a review of this on DP Review, but their over-the-top, religious zealots banned one post for using the word "gobsmacked" (when describing my experiences with the first 6D) and another post because of the word "pissed," (after calling Canon and finding out I would have to send it to them at my own cost) both banned claiming violation of their "rule 6," for "profanity." So..., I'll make sure my review is somewhere that people can or might see it and be able to use for their determination if this camera is right for them.

For the price, overall, it's NOT a good deal. Uses the same processor as the Rebels (ie; T7i) and the same articulating screen. Also, the focus points are all bunched-up in the center of the sensor, so a FF sensor is kind of meaningless for AF when you only cover 40% of sensor and it's all in the center? Also, the sensor is a step back from the older 6D. It claims more MP's, but really, if it doesn't have the DR of the original camera it's supposed to replace, then I say it's a step back. Yes, it has DPAF, but that's a function of the processor, not the sensor. So it's basically a weather sealed (maybe) FF T7i. Except without the flash...

Honestly, the T7i feels like a toy, but the few weeks I had and tested it, it was rained on, snowed on and I generally beat the camera up. It took the abuse with zero issues and the DPAF worked brilliantly. Photo's rivaled that of this 6D MII.

First day I had the 6D Mark II, something seemed wonky, but an update of the firmware to 1.0.4 fixed the weird switch issue. Nothing could fix the wildly un-calibrated ISO issue though. After talks with Canon repair center, they said to ship it to them. Since it was after the 30-days I have to return something at BB, I had no other choice.

So why did I send it in? The ISO calibration was WAY off from the get go. Orders of magnitude off. The orig 6D had me gobsmacked (oh my..., there's that profanity!) with it's low-noise at very high ISO. That was unbelievable. This camera though couldn't touch a 5D MII, a 70D or the T7i. Same lens, same coverage (making allowance for 1.6CF of the 70D/T7i), same shutter speed, same aperture, the three test subjects were 1200ISO, with the 6D MII, to get the same exposure, I was at 3200 and higher ISO. Kind of the opposite of what you'd expect, especially considering my opposite experiences with the original 6D. Esp from a $1600+ NEW camera/sensor. And sending back to Canon means YOU Pay the shipping to them. And insurance. So roll in $35 more into the price of the camera.

Some will say just a fluke and that these things happen. They do. But with all the issues combined in a camera that is sub-par to a $750 rebel in almost every aspect, well..., I say stay away until the price comes down to a point that it makes sense to buy a FF rebel with (alleged) weather sealing and no flash.

title: Good batt life, but very fragile
text: Little studs that hold the rubber band isolators break off easily, just from tension of the 0-rings. Two broken so far, not from rough handling, happened in storage. If more than two on one side break, then you're hosed. Or you could drill and tap for screws to hold the rings (then the plastic of the body would probably fail...)

title: Pretty much identical to Canon.
text: Quality and rigid, works like the Canon one, can't tell difference (aside from the price)

title: Not as advertised
text:
They claim "noise isolating," but nowhere in literature or packaging does it mention anything about noise cancelling or isolating. Trying to sell these riding on the "noise cancelling" wave of the active cancelling headphones. It probably just means because the buds go into your ear canal (like all buds).

Seem well made (of course made in China..., WTH isn't?)

For the price, they're probably worth it, but just seems kind of slimy to use words that sound like they mean something more than just, "ear plugs."

title: Does NOT fit SMH10. Somewhat fragile feeling.
text: Does NOT fit the SMH10-11. Seems kind of fragile too.

title: Rock-solid so far
text: 100% so far. Very solid and stable. No issues. Will update if any fails.

title: Onbelievably light weight and small
text:
Works 100% and I like that you can see the charging progress with a lighted LCD indicator. This is so light, you think it's an empty plastic shell. JUST what I wanted. Very small, compact and light for travel (when airlines charge for every flippin' ounce anymore, weight means a lot to me!). Works so far. Will update if I have issues, but so far, it's 100%. Would def buy again! Uses same charger and cable as my cell phone - no need for duplicate equipment.

Bonus: This saves even more travel weight for using the same mUSB cable/charger as the typical android phone, so you don't have to carry an extra charging cable.

title: Sharper than expected at most focal lengths, minimal CA.
text: The range is great and for the range, the focus was very sharp. Mine back-focused severely, but found it was an issue with my camera body, not so much the lens. Overall, this is an outstanding deal all-around, esp. with all the stuff Digital Goja ships it with. Can't say enough good about these people. Anyway, the lens is sharper than most Tamron's, surprisingly, and gives Sigma a run for the money.

title: Great mugs, stay warm/cold, but color off
text: Bought the "greyed jade" and it's neither of those colors as are most are commonly used to. This is very much green. Just plain green in every way. I know that's being picky, but was hoping more for grey or jade, not bright green. If that's the worse thing to piss and moan about, then overall, the mug's awesome. These hold their insulation well and seal (if you get the lid to screw on straight, because of the course threads, that can be a challenge!). Worth every penny

title: Quality part, seems well-made, fits perfectly
text: Works and fits like the Canon one. Seems good quality.

title: Batteries last, but will not charge with the Canon charger, you can only use the OAproda charger for these batts
text: They work, and damned if they don't seem to last LONGER than the stock Canon battery. But the Canon charger doesn't charge these batteries (or even SEE them), so buyer beware. You MUST use the charger base these came with. On the plus side of that, this charger is VERY small and light, so as long as it's reliable, it's a better option (over the canon) for travel.

title: Feels cheaply made, but works fine so far
text: Doesn't feel anywhere near the quality of the Canon or other past non-OEM grips I've bought for other camera's, but after an exhaustive comparison of the other's (Neewer, Vivitar, etc.), they're the same mfg, made the same, feels the same, just different name and price. For the $19, this is certainly the best deal I've found so far (for the T7i). Have taken to multiple all-day shoots. Rocked it just fine.

title: Junk, came apart third time I used
text: The ring that holds the lock tabs in snapped off the bottom of the hood and lost one of the locking tabs. No matter, it never locked onto the lens properly anyway. Keep looking, this one is pure junk.

title: Works, but not as full-charging as the canon.
text: Works, not as good as the canon one, but it works. Is smaller and lighter.

title: Seems high quality, way sturdier than the plastic ones that break their fingers off
text: Super well-made, very sturdy. My last few plastic ones broke one of the fingers off from vibration or over tightening. Time will tell, but this seems pretty high quality.

title: Not OEM, but works so far
text: So far, so good. You can tell it's not OEM, but works so far.

title: So far, so good, still well with proper prep.
text: Stick great (with proper prep: clean surface with alcohol just before applying, press firm for a minute), good deal on a large quantity of these. No problems so far. Will update review if something changes (they come un-stuck, break, etc.)

title: Bit of backfocus and not as sharp as I'd expect from Sigma
text: Not as sharp as I've come to expect from Sigma. Also, had a backfocusing issue that couldn't be resolved in-camera.

title: Didn't meet needs as a travel pack
text: Pretty much just a huge cavity inside and little padding anywhere. Returned it. Didn't meet my needs for a travel pack.

title: Not that sharp, a bit of backfocus
text: Copy I received backfocused a bit and was not sharp (at any range)? Maybe I'm picky, using L-series and Sigma Art Lenses, but sharpness is something I can't live without now...

title: Great idea and works as intended.
text: Brilliant idea and works superbly for finding back/front focus issues with different lenses. Love it.

title: Well-engineered, well-made, rugged, works flawlessly
text: Not into five-star reviews, but this is very well engineered (love how the battery door from the body mounts into this, brilliant mounting), rugged and works. What more to ask?

title: Worth every penny. Took some beatings, held up well. Like that it's tulip.
text: Like this better than the Canon hood. Worked perfectly, got banged around and held up well so far. I'd buy again.

title: Out of focus autofocus
text: Nicely made, but autofocuses OUT of focus. Pull out, put only lens on, autofucuses perfectly. Re-install this doubler, autofocuses out of focus.

title: Hole too big, but well-made part, excellent value
text: Very well made, excellent materials and finish, holds Gopro sturdy, unlike the plastic ones. Only problem is they ONLY make this for a 1-1/8" handlebar (31.8mm). NO ONE makes a tall aluminum mount for 1" or 7/8" handlebars.

title: Pincushioning at 16 and soft at 300. Not a great lens. Good warranty.
text: Soft (OOF) at the long end, distortions at the short. Wasn't good enough to keep, not for the almost $600 price. Love Tamron's warranty though. Kudo's to them for having more than anyone else.

title: Perfect Canon cap
text: Perfect. To replace a stock cap I had lost.

title: Thin red gel filter, about a nickel sized. Works, price too high for what it is.
text: Just a thin, round (nickel sized) cutout of gelatin in no. 25 red. Lost it immediately (just watch when opening case!)

title: Works, no leaks to 20m depth.
text:
Only did about 20meters down with this, but no leaks and OK, light. Wasn't as wide-angle or bright as I had hoped, but close-ups work well (just don't filter for it).

EDIT 03/19: So far, no leaks to 90ft (a number of dives to this) and love that they are a way to store your gopro batts too. Overall, great deal on a decent light.

title: Good item, but can fall off easily.
text: I like these a lot. Install them on all my camera bodies. They don't like to stay put though, so I use some black gaffers tape to hold them in.

title: Works, but screws are way too long, cut into you while wearing a pack with this mounted
text:
UPDATE: Seller contacted me about the screws and offered to send shorter ones, stating they would provide them now with any new purchases. The screws came very quickly (from China) and they are the perfect length now for about anything you'd use it on (BCD, backpack strap, etc.). Seller went above and beyond to correct the original problem, so I raised my rating up.
-----------------------
The screws are too long and punch into your BCD if you use it for diving, on my backpack, the threads dug into my chest. Figure out how long you need, mounted to your packs straps, and cut off the excess or you'll be sorry.

title: Strong and works
text: Worth the $'s. Strong and works well. Use it as a travel tripod.

title: Sharp, but terribly fragile build quality
text:
The good: First, lens is very sharp, even at full aperture. Used as a travel lens for paying photo work (don't tell anyone, please!) as it's light and covers the range I needed.

The not so good: lens is cheaply made, plastic abounds and is fragile. Lens creep is insane and the little switch that locks it back doesn't work half the time, the other half you're quickly struggling to find the tiny switch it to unlock your lens to shoot a fleeting shot of a genuine alien spacecraft flipping off tourists in Tahiti.

Broke the zoom (internally) two-days after landing in Phuket, Thailand (luckily it was for an underwater shoot with GoPros). Took eight-weeks for Thailand to get the parts and fix it at the genuine Canon service center. The knackered cheap plastic internal parts they replaced and were so gracious to give me the originals back, do NOT inspire confidence in reliability. If you don't use the lens and keep it stored in a box, it should last a long time for you. If you actually use it..., beware!

title: NOT German optics, but still a quality, slim filter
text: NOT "German Optics," but a quality, slim filter. The one I got was a K&F Concept filter. Still seems very high quality and slim, but not German Optics.

title: Outstanding quality and fits perfectly, very heavy though
text: Quality is outstanding, VERY high quality, excellent machining and parts. Awesome looks with camera in this. Only problem for me is that it weighed a LOT. More than the camera. And I'm weight restricted where I travel to. Just too heavy, but it is probably a stronger mount than anyone would ever, EVER need! Four stars for excellent made item, less one for the weight. Perfect fit on Hero4 Black. The weight might be beneficial for those who want to stabilize their camera on a tripod (tripod threads in the bottom and lots of mounting options).

title: Fit and function just fine.
text: Seem to fit and work just fine. We'll see how they last.

title: Works, kind of cheaply made
text: Kind of cheaply made, end caps don't line up no matter what you do, but it works.

title: Did NOT come as a 2.5ghz machine
text:
This just arrived and upon booting, in BIOS and in Control Panel, it shows as a 2.4ghz processor, NOT the 2.5ghz advertised (and yes, it DOES make a difference, esp. with video processing). Also, in the Amazon ad under "more information" it shows as a 2.66ghz processor. Sigh...

Just a caveat, check your machine thoroughly as soon as it comes, make sure all the peripheral HW is working and has drivers, etc.

title: Good system, excellent instructions, one clicker was dead from a leaking battery, auto re-arm is permanent...
text:
Easy install, I like that there's only a few buttons, a large "on" button and a smaller off, then siren-off.

Seems good quality, esp. for the price. Instruction book is very clear and professional (unlike most other Chinese alarms systems).

Issues: One clicker didn't work, take it apart to check battery and it's corroded to the spring terminal. Two-new batteries ordered (at the cost of the complete alarm system). Overall, I'd recommend.

*UPDATE (minus a few stars): One really bloody annoying thing is that it re-arms itself if you don't turn the ignition on within it's programmed time. You can double click the off to "temporarily" turn off the auto re-arm, but there's no way I can find to permanently turn off the auto re-arm (annoying as HELL when you're working on the bike in the garage!)

title: OK for price, but didn't fit and needed filing and mods to make it fit
text: Needed extensive mods to make work on a Chevy truck with factory 4" x 10" speakers. For the price, it's OK I guess.

title: Best (and loudest) of the rugged laptop platter drives
text: These are louder drives than you'd think, you can always hear them whirring, but they stand up to abuse in travel laptops. For platter drives, these are it, anything else, you'll eventually bump something and crash, loosing your data.

title: NOT SMOOTH. Ad says so, but these are dimpled just like every other factory-like touchpad sticker. Skip these...
text: Ordered these because they are advertised as SMOOTH. What came are dimpled/dotted stickers like the original. I'm trying to replace the crappy original with SMOOTH. These are NOT smooth, even though the ad says they are smooth.

title: This had intolerable CA, but like Tamron lenses in general
text: Had focus issues, but most lenses now do that, you just need to play musical-lens until you find one that matches your body. I overall like Tamron lenses and their warranty, this one also had unacceptable chromatic aberration (extreme purple fringing at long focal lengths and high contrast subjects). Was returned.

title: Perfect part, just as advertised
text: Just what was advertised, works flawlessly, good seller and fast shipping.

title: Doesn't work like a Glidecam or other gimbled stabilizer, impossible to keep stable. Small hands only!
text: Like everyone else, had a hard time stabilizing unless someone has micro-sized hands (and I have a steady cam and fly cam nano to practice with). Look to something else, this thing just doesn't work.

title: Junk. Can't tighten it enough to stay put, slips around and pops out of locking teeth. Get the stock GoPro or equiv.
text: Fits on various size bars, frames, etc., but won't stay tight no matter how much you cinch it down. Tighten it hard and it immediately slips past a tooth or two from the rubber pulling against the flimsy locking teeth. Just a bad design. I'd return if I could. Had to tape it to the handlebars to get it to stay put and not rotate around because it can never be tightened enough to stay put. Junk, really.

title: Just plain works, just like they claim
text: Like everyone else says, this one works while most of the other Vag-Com cables just don't. Follow instructions on Triumphrat explicitly. And a hint: Turn off automatic updating of drivers in windows BEFORE hooking it up.

title: Overall, a great housing, with a BIG caveat
text:
Overall, this was a good housing. Never leaked (and even has a leak-sensor that lights an LED in the housing if it senses water, not even advertised by MFG) and worked properly with ALL functions available. But..., trying to operate the round dial on the back of the G7x was a pain, would always hit something else for functions.

WARNING: I will probably not use this housing again and it will sit on a shelf. One glaring flaw. The made the WiFi switch a lever that is NOT momentary. So just bumping it while diving, stuffing it in your dry bag, carrying it around, the lever, sticking out the side like a sore-thumb, gets pushed down (out of the way), thereby operating the WiFi function (turns the WiFi on). So by the time you get to the dive site, the battery is dead. Or almost gone. It happened consistently. So much so I'd be checked every five minutes to see if the WiFi was on (turns the screen on too). Now..., I am not sure who's bright idea it was to make sure you have WiFi access while diving (OK, we all check FB way too often, but I could at least wait till the dive was over to "need" WiFi. Seriously? Do we even need to operate the WiFi in a dive housing? Maybe we want to transfer pics while the camera is in the housing, but most don't want to haul their laptop out deckside to do that and we could have had a button that was momentary that didn't hold the WiFi-On switch to constantly on. Stupid!!! Arrggghhh!!!

Bottom line, I'd take a dremel to the lever and cut it off, leaving a stub so it stays sealed. If you NEED WiFi while diving, you could turn it with your fingers, might take some effort, but I'd rather it take effort to turn-on, than turn on from a stiff breeze blowing on it...

Good housing other than the above, very much worth the cost. Remember to grease the seal. And wash with tap water after EVERY dive.

If I could get my $'s back for this I would probably return it because of the battery drain lever, but overall, I'd be happy with it if not for that.

title: Random freezing with two drives. Lost data each time. Doesn't test as fast as claims. Going back to Crucial or something else.
text: Have always had nothing but good to say about Samsung. Till now. These drives must be replicas, fakes, whatever, not only are they slow, but BOTH (bought a 1tb and a 250gb) randomly freeze. No input/output. Nothing you can do but reboot. Then it does the same a while later. NEVER had that problem with platter drives (WD blacks) or the Crucial M500 960gb I had in the laptop I put the 1tb Samsung in. Clone OS, update all drivers, all runs fine until, at some point, it just freezes. Like the drive shuts down and refuses to allow any data in/out. Nothing you can do to wake it up, tried it all. You'll just lose data and have to reboot. Going to try to return to Amazon since it's only been a few days. No more Samsung and cheap chips hidden in their housings masquerading under their old laurels of fast SSD's. I reserve the right to modify this review at any time, but right now I'm really f**king pissed!

title: Manfrotto, Made in Italy part
text: Real Manfrotto, really works. What else can I say. Some, or much, of their stuff is made in China now (hell..., what isn't?), this though, is made in Italy (perhaps FROM Chinese parts, again, what isn't?), but marked as Italy and seems fine quality. Something that used to cost $60 and up, now a third of that. Not sure how, but I needed a handle for a tripod and this did it.

title: A few grades up from genuine Manfrotto
text:
I have a new Manfrotto mount and just got this Neewer mount. Quality difference? Yes. The Chinese-made Neewer is substantially higher quality in fit and finish. If I mixed these up and asked 100 out of 100 fellow photog's, they'd pick the Neewer as the Manfrotto, seeing the quality of mfg. Seriously, I'm SO not impressed with Manfrotto these days. Wait..., uh..., it's ALSO made in China! Sigh...

Bottom line, the Neewer plate is a quality product, better fit, better finish all-around, looks quality and parts are solid and close-toleranced. From now on, I'll actually look for these instead of Manfrotto. If I had looked at these side by side, I wouldn't have looked at price at all, just chosen the Neewer and been done with it.

title: Works perfect, good deal.
text: Thought this cable was bad at first, turns out it was the cheapo lavalier mics. Three out of five bad. This cable is perfect, works flawlessly. Good deal for what it is.

title: What is not shown in the pic, is the ...
text: What is not shown in the pic, is the volume controls in each wire. They are large in comparison to the ends. Overall though, they work as stated. Wanted just a splitter as they show in their pic, but now I have two vol controls that I have to tape over.

title: Love these. Sound is SO much more than it was with Scoche and Pioneers
text: Unbelievable sound from just 4" speakers. Replaced a pair of cheap Wally World speakers (that cost me what these cost) and what a difference. If you're constrained to 4" speakers, these are the ones. You won't get much bass out of 4" speakers, but at least I HAVE bass now, unlike the "tinny" sounding dual-speaker Scoche's.

title: Great for new builds for trouble-free conn issues.
text: Just as advertised and just as show in pic, metal clips. Installed these in last build and no SATA conn issues since.

title: EDIT: New is MUCH better design!
text:
First design review: For the price, it seems like a great tripod, but..., it was falling apart in the new bags it came in, so expect to locktite all screws, including the one holding the QD head to the ball section. And speaking of, the ball was way too tight for anyone to move without tools and that's with the tightening knob totally unscrewed. Sigh..

It's not a Sirui (though it looks like one and is kind of a copy), but it's half the price. If you're picky about equipment and need a light, small travel tripod, best try a Cullman Nanomax or a Sirui and shy from this if you need dependable.

EDIT: So Ravelli customer care gladly returned the original one and sent me one of the latest designs. Night and day difference. And this one comes completely assembled (unlike the first one I reviewed). This design is VERY reminiscent of the Sirui in design and function. The ball on this is smooth and very effective. I was impressed, was like night and day compared to the first one (of the same model #, so not sure how to order and actually get one of the new designs). Just when I thought they finally had a hit, well, the padded bag has a zipper that comes pre-stripped to save you the years of wear in order to accomplish a popped-zipper. And the way this is sewn-in, there's not a good way to get it back together. So while the tripod (new design) is an exceptional design, the bag..., well..., this one's unusable now and I just took the thing out of the box for the first time to review it. Nice otherwise though, so it might be worth the $20 or so to have someone sew in a sturdy YKK zipper or something like that. Bottom line though, this new tripod (APGL5) is a hit (but I haven't used it yet, will edit again if issues come up) and a keeper for sure.

title: Connects and disconnects randomly, but overall good housing
text:
Accidentally ordered two of these, but since they're 3.0 at 6gbps, I'll change out the 2.0 housing I have another drive in currently.

Work and have cooling vents. Does seem to want to D/C and reconnect in windows a lot, like there's a problem with the cable or a connection, hence the 4x stars and not five.

title: The tactile feel is just right and these simply last.
text: These work. Just always. And they last. Not the latest bluetooth, jet-propelled, whiz-bang, but they always work. They last.

title: Solid and loud
text: Really well built compared to most of the cheapo alarm components out there. The horn inside is metal and the plastic is not flimsy, like supported ABS. Bottom line, I have no clue how they can sell this so cheap, but it's a $50 horn, easy. You can hook it up two ways inside, single continuous tone, or a warble. Both are loud. Ordering another one to attach in parallel...

title: 100% quality - no problems with many burns
text: So far, 100% burn success rate. No coasters yet. Impressed, esp for the price.

title: Solid, reliable, maintainable
text: I use these when I travel. Upgraded to another brand when my Thinkpad was destroyed in Israel. After many countries, then back to the US, I ended up with an old, used X201 again! They're that reliable and still fast/enough RAM. Only drawback is no SATA 3, but with an SSD HD, speeds are acceptable. Best part, you can swap out about any component and on the 9-cell batt, last an overseas flight before a charge is needed.

title: Love these eye cups
text: Love these eye cups. Install them on all my cams. Reminds me of the days of my Canon F1 and the Canon accessory cups for that.

title: Great deal, works perfect
text: Great deal, works perfect. Not worth the new price, but def worth it for a used item. All works flawlessly.

title: Fast ram that's never failed me. Kingston and Crucial ...
text: Fast ram that's never failed me. Kingston and Crucial are tops for builds (and I've built many systems over the years, starting with AT's and the likes). This is fast, meets spec and works, not much else to say there.

title: Use this exclusively now. Travel internationally 4-6-months of the ...
text: Use this exclusively now. Travel internationally 4-6-months of the year and have this around my shoulder more than most people carry their purses around. Just zip-tie through the quick releases or you'll be sorry!

title: Small, almost too small to actually use, but ...
text: Small, almost too small to actually use, but come in handy as you can actually carry them in a camera bag, as opposed to an 8x10 WB card. All in all, they've saved me a few times.

title: Amazing. I love this
text:
Small but not too small (I still suggest getting one of those cable keychains to put this on to make it harder to lose - it's really small!)

Fast data transfer, and LOTS of space. Amazing. I love this. It's my go-to flash drive for video file transfers, etc.

Kingston reliability so far. Don't expect any issues.

title: Awesome bag, not too big, but big enough...
text: Thought I'd written a review on this. Bag is great, not too big that it's heavy, but big enough to haul all your lenses and audio gear. VERY well built. The opposite-opening thing is weird, as others have pointed out, it opens away from your body, making total sense from a human-engineering point of view, you can open it out and have clear view and shot at everything inside, but since every other bag made since caveman days opens the other way, you just never really get used to this one? Matters not, overall a killer deal for a very well-made bag that's protective and one of the few I'll trust to expensive lenses.

title: Still works, had over a year.
text: Still works just fine and connections are solid, no shorts in cable where it bends like many of them do. For the price, very worth it.

title: Cheap and "OK"
text: These are kind of fragile, but work. Bass isn't good, not the greatest sound replication, but for the price there's no complaining. Except I also bought a pair off Amazon that cost a whopping $3 and they work the same. Same sound, same quality. Skullcandy is the one to beat, but I don't like using those where they might get wet or destroyed.

title: Works as it should.
text: Bought this to charge batteries for an LED light back that uses SONY camcorder batts. Works perfectly, no problems and no overheating or other issues.

title: Awesome item, esp for the price...
text:
But I never use it anymore. Pretty much do glide cam work now and never use this kind of thing. Was perfect for tripod work. Adjustable eye piece for glasses wearers, used stick-on wide velcro to put it over the flip-out LCD, works great and not permanent.

If I did more close up or tripod work, this wouldn't come off.

title: Awesome for the price!
text: These seem a bit fragile, but I've used and abused them now for a while and they've held up like champs. Sound is clear and nice, though lows are not too pronounced. For the price, get a few pair. Well worth it!

title: Heavier than the "non-slim," regular passport
text:
This is a metal case, and looks sleek, but weighs more than the standard 2-tb passport (plastic case).

Thought I'd find something smaller and save some weight while traveling. No dice. The plastic passport is rugged and is lighter, though a bit bulkier, so I'll just still with that. Overall I've had awesome luck with WD drives (stick with the black's) and the plastic passport is no exception to that. Had been dropped, yanked from it's cable, sat in a humid backpack in Egypt's heat (and Thailands, AND India's...), with no ill effects. Fast and reliable. I'd assume this one is the same, but won't be using it as much as the lighter one.

title: I do so miss the orig MS Natural board, this isn't quite there..
text:
The good is that the tactile response is close to the orig MS board, I like it. Works. Overall, the keyboard works fine.

Cons? Well, the ALT/Ctrl/Windows keys on the bottom are WAY too tall. The MS board had sloped keys there so you didn't accidentally hit them while typing. The keys on this board are squared and HIGH! I'm constantly hitting one of them by accident while typing. I'm getting used to holding my wrist up while I type, but then that defeats the purpose of an "ergonomic" keyboard in the first place, right?

The only other "con" is that bios sometimes doesn't recognize it. So if you need a keystroke in response to a boot issue (like to acknowledge booting from a CD or something), you can't, it just sits there until whatever timeout is reached. Once Windows loads, you can enter a password and all works as it should, but something about this USB keyboard isn't seen until Windows starts. Weird. I've loaded defaults in BIOS, set legacy USB's active, all USB ports, blah, blah, no change.

If you're like me and tear a board up whipping a book out, then get this. Just put a pad under your wrists so you don't hit the keys on the bottom. The feel is good and positive and they seem to last OK. The MS boards now are crap, so this is about your only choice for a natural.

------------------

EDIT: This has almost hit the wall a few times now. I like the tactile feel, but the annoyance of losing your writing or going to some place you didn't intend in an instant from hitting the Alt/Windoze, etc., keys that stick up at the bottom like trees is getting to be too much.

Find a NOS MS Natural or maybe wait for another mfg or this one to figure out that people don't want to hold their arms in the air to type to avoid hitting the keys at the bottom...

------------------

EDIT #2: A few months into using this board and it started to smell like burning electronic components. That unmistakable smell. No smoke, but the smell was strong and coming from the keyboard. Now my system randomly reboots. When I plug back in the very worn-out MS natural, no reboots. Plug THIS back in and a few minutes (5-20) later, system reboots. Like bad clockwork, but it's consistent. I'm not reducing my rating on it, but I will give a hazard warning for this board. Prob should find another option.

------------------

EDIT #3: Board has been fine for over six-months and a few renditions of the guy smashing his keyboard, then tossing the monitor out his cubie. Maybe not that far, but it's had (I'm not telling how many) "spirited" bangings and came through like an MMA fighter. It's almost abusing it whipped it's problems into shape or something. Been rock solid after some good poundings that would have sent a Logitech to the morgue. So I've actually upped my rating on this board. Still hate the ungodly high special keys at the bottom, but I've gotten used to them. And the tactile feel to the keys is lasting longer than I had expected.

title: Used one in India a few years ago, sold it, now back to the same thing
text:
The one I purchased was a different machine #, didn't have bluetooth, but was a faster processor and a few other upgrades. Needed BT so I installed a BT daughter card out of my old T61 that had a bad Invidia chip. Works like a charm and now can do skype meetings without being tethered to the system.

These are rugged, fast, work. I'd take an older one of these (I did) over a new something else any day (I did). Went from a Samsung Ultrabook (admittedly a great system too) back to a 3-year old one of these. Cheap, but still fast and has everything you need. No CD/DVD, but most don't have them anymore and using CD to USB is fine.

Case is magnesium alloy and breaks the fins for the cooling fan easily. That was a bad design. Otherwise, it's a perfect system that is more than a netbook, but not the weight and size of a lappy while still having a good size screen and almost full-size keyboard.

title: Bought a bunch for overseas travel..., like them
text: They're just small enough to put here and there and lose in your own luggage. But I like these. Hold just enough and weigh just right when full. I used different colors to tell which ones were charged and which ones were used (for rechargeables). Get a few, you'll be glad you did.

title: Sadly...
text: I never got to actually USE this. Re-sold it on Amazon, still new. Only time I got the opportunity, it was a deep-dive in Thailand that I needed a "real" housing for. This seemed a bit thin, but it's only rated to 3-meters and I'm sure it'd do that. Quality build though and I probably would have found a use for it (rafting, etc.)

title: Not sure why the low price, but it's VERY high quality and no complaints here.
text: These work very well. Use them for lighting, or putting a P&S on a mono-pod to raise above a crowd (or to avoid getting shot at when in a foreign country during a military overthrow..., don't ask how I learned that neat trick). Anyway, does a unique job and does it well. Is small and light and quality made. For the price, it's a steal.

title: Works, holds batts, but didn't think about how heavy that many batteries in a small space would be..
text: These hold a lot of batts, but I fear the whole thing will explode if you drop it, full, onto a hard surface. I try not to do that. It's a lot of batts in a small space and can get heavy, but great for packing batts in luggage and that kind of thing. Just pretend your carry-on is feather light, tossing it around like it's only feather pillows, cause if they weigh it, you're done for...

title: These and Wasabi Power are the best non-OEM (IMHO)
text: From experience, I don't even look at cheaper batts (these are about as economical as they get anyway), these and Wasabi Power are the non-OEM quality champs. Last, hold charges a long time, never let me down. Good deal and for just a few bucks more than the bottom-feeder non-OEM's, it's a no-brainer to buy these.

title: One of the best of the aftermarket batteries.
text: These and Wasabi Power are probably the best of the aftermarket battery packs. I use them both liberally. They both outlast the stock Canon, but not by much (even though they're rated at a much higher MaH rating. Worth having a few as spares at all times. Cheap enough and good enough.

title: Thin enough that it doesn't vignette, but thicker than I'd like
text: For what it is, and the price? 100% good deal. Thinner than most filters, does it's job (making sandwiches on the set) and no complaints. At least it doesn't interfere with wide-angle (at least on 17mm with 1.6 crop sensor).

title: Find myself using this a lot for accents or hairlights. VERY handy to use rechargeable cam batteries too!
text:
More often than not, I find myself reaching for this light and mounting it into a light stand to use for fill-in, hair-light or shadow depth reduction. Works really well, actually. And I use some of the filters that come with it too. Best part? It uses really cheap, older (that you can still get new for dirt cheap) camera batteries from Sony's or Panasonic's. Get a few extra batts and one of the cheap wall-chargers for them and you're set for a LONG shoot (the LED banks last a long time on a camera battery charge!)

If I did more shooting, I'd order more of these. And use them.

title: These hold up and keep data as safe as any platter can
text: After many crashes, traveling with laptops in 3rd-world countries, I landed with WD Black series drives. They can take a beating and have rarely had issues with them. They are def more rugged and faster than other mfg's options. If you can't do SSD, this is your next-best option.

title: These work as-advertised, but mount close to magnet
text: These work as other say, just mount them close to the magnet so it makes a clean and long break from the sensor. Have only had a few weeks, but so far, they're rock solid (as I'd hope, for an alarm, right?)

title: Won't fit an older X200 or a newer X201 std lappy. Latch is too short. Nice vendor though.
text: These are crap batteries. The latch is made too short to latch and lock into either an X200 or X201 (not tablet) that we have. Tried it in another travel X201, same thing. Ordered another brand from another vendor. What came was yet another CBD battery. Identical latch, identical problem. Battery falls out of chassis if held with battery toward ground (whenever you slide it into a laptop sleeve or your backpack/briefcase. Will damage chassis eventually. The vendor was sympathetic though, said they'd refund return shipping. Seemed like nice people at least.

title: It's OK, it works, but not very long lasting between charges...
text: Cheap and works, but doesn't last. Takes a LONG time to charge and used for an LED light, it lasts maybe an hour. About as long as the stock, 5-year old Sony battery. Can't complain too much, it was cheap, but have to constantly change them out and have chargers going all the time. I'd prob buy again, or maybe try another brand to see if something else lasts longer, but for the price...??

title: These are the best of the non-OEM batts
text: Have used the STK's (good), Opteka (OK) and a few others, but the Wasabi power batts last the longest and have zero issues with charging or anything else. Always work. When I go overseas with gear, I bring these knowing I can depend on them.

title: Works as it should, excellent longevity of charge
text: Bought this for my old, OLD Sony cybershot, but it also fits the LED light bank I have and lasts FOREVER in that. Literally will last more than a full day of run time with the LED light. Good battery, works perfectly.

title: They work
text: Mom said to invest in CD's. So I bought-in. $50,000 worth. Have no idea how these are supposed to earn interest, but I'm still waiting... (just kidding, these are what they are. Work fine for music, which is all I use them for since DVD's have all but taken over data storage..., at least till that little android b*stard finds his way out!)

title: Not really super slim as claimed, but works and doesn't have a lot of artifact or flare issues
text:
Fine filter for protecting expensive lenses (yes, I'm from the old-school that way). I can just leave this on and not worry about having a lens cap, just a blower or brush and I'm always ready to shoot (but make sure you have a lens hood on, or you'll have insane flare (as with any filter).

Not as thin as they claim, but it's adequate.

title: Seems to hold up longer than the stock battery
text:
Higher MAH rating than stock and does seem to hold up longer. I've had zero problems with it and have learned to trust it. Almost lasts forever, even with showing people slideshows of pics on the cam.

If I get back overseas again soon, I'll get another as a backup.

title: Said Genuine Canon/OEM, IS Canon/OEM
text: Just what it claims to be. Fits fine and was economical replacement to a lost one. If you need to sell a body and lost your cap, get this one and not a generic.

title: Not as big as I wanted or hoped to find
text: Quality was great, but still not big enough to fit all I need into it (I need something exactly TWICE as big as a standard camera bag, this was about the same size as most other bags)

title: Great batts and high quality charger
text:
These are the best of the aftermarket batteries. Last, work perfectly, no issues.

Charger looks like the cheap ones, just with a different name, but there are subtle differences and it charges fully when the cheap, generic one says it's done. Works perfect with the Canon battery too, so I use this when I travel.

title: As good as Canon brand
text: Re-glue the pad inside and this will last as long and be as tough as the Canon mount. Really, made well and works as it should. Great collar mount.

title: One of the sharpest Canon L-lenses
text: Have had this for over a year now, not a lick of trouble. Was in Cairo last summer during the demonstrations and used it there. Awesome, crisp lens, nice bokeh, fast AF. Can't say enough good about this lens. The IS was a lifesaver, BTW.

title: Use in a Thinkpad T400
text: Works just fine in a T400 T-pad. Windows 7, so I don't know about drivers for XP if someone is still running that, but it loads drivers and reads cards. What more do you want. And it's flush-mount. That was important to me.

title: Cheap, but light and works
text: Bought a Delkin solid case with solid rubber cutouts for cards, was heavy as hell and since I was to travel extensively, I opted for this case instead. Not water proof, but really, doesn't need to be for most situations anyway. This is light and works fine for what it is.

title: Carry a Canon 70-200L lens in this
text: Great for lighter protection when traveling. Went through half-dozen or more countries last year and used this for my long lens. Fine protection, but don't drop it, of course.

title: Works as advertised.
text: Not much to say, works as it is advertised and gives you extended drive space. Theoretically, you can have two terabytes of storage in your IBM (two 1-tb WD blue drives), but I ran a Scorpio black 750 as the main and a 1-tb Blue as this drive for storage.

title: Solid, reliable for 1.5 years now, no signs of any issues
text: Use these in my main desk system and for backups. Bullet proof (even with a drop of system that I though for sure would crash it) and as reliable as you will find. Moreso, actually, with Seagate now only giving one to two years, tells you what they think of their own reliability. You still lose your data of course, that's the cost, not replacing the HD, but a 5-year warranty tells me WD stands behind their drives and believes they might actually go that long. Just rotate a new drive in every three or four years and you'll not have an issue. Have had some crashes in the past (WD, Maxtor, Seagate, Hitachi -remember the "Deathstar" moniker? It was earned!), but overall, WD has been the most reliable for me, both desk and lappy drives (but get the black, Scorpio and Caviar, always!)

title: Great P&S camera that takes outstanding macro shots!
text: I LOVED this camera. Carried it all over the world with me last year. Looked to buy another one before this one's warranty ran out, but now they are more expensive than when I bought this one? Shot times are slow with flash, it takes a while to lock on or charge so forget trying to get quick, action shots with this one. At least not with flash. Otherwise it's acceptable. Awesome video too!!

title: Solid, stays locked, light and compact for travel
text: Carried this through France, Israel, Egypt, Thailand, Taiwan, Sri Lanka and India last year. Remains in my loadout for travel photo gear. Used it as a boom-pole for shotgun mic among other uses. Light, compact and worth every penny.

title: Awesome copy of Glidecam
text:
This is a knock-off of the Glidecam design, but at less than one-third the cost and works as well (tested side by side).

I actually like the weight system for this better than the Glide as I can travel with it and not have to take all the weight with me, just find large washers wherever I am to put into the weight cups (or fishing weights like I did in one country)

Overall, a great buy on a camera stabilizer that works.

Screws are kind of chintzy, flimsy plastic heads, unscrew themselves a lot, but what you put up with from Chinese-made anything.

------------------------

Edit, 1.5 years into using; pressed-in nut came out on me when I was using it overseas. Luckily I managed to find it and epoxy it in when I got to somewhere I could find epoxy. I still like the weight set up with this more than the glidecam. I can load the pockets up with fishing weights or whatever is heavy to balance this. If could link to a pic of the fallen out pem nut I would, but the only options I have are for video review...

title: Great and compact, one-piece unit, unlike the Canon
text: Canon factory charger has the charger, then a nice cord to lose somewhere. This one just has a flip-out plug and is a lot lighter than the Canon one. It works, charges well, lights green when charged. I take these traveling and leave the Canon at home.

title: Hella deal on this solid QR mount.
text: Mounted this to a Flycam Nano with two fender washers underneath. Works great. The mount has a hold for a flathead screw. Screwed through the base of the Flycam and ran a nut on. Simple, easy. People complaining it's not tapped need to look at the pics better. It's not for mounting directly onto a tripod. Or you can tap the hole out to 3/8-16 thread for a large thread tripod.

title: Meike is probably the best knock-off battery grip out there!
text:
This grip (genuine Meike, not the no-name ones!) is solid, works perfectly, doesn't drain batteries like the the cheaper knock-offs and fits superbly. They use metal where they should (baseplate, etc.) and they are rugged. Spent 4+ months kicking around India with one of these attached. When I got back, I sold it for what I paid for it and THAT one is still working!

Save your cash for expensive lenses and consider a Meike grip over the Canon. One thing with the Canon grip though, they are a little sturdier if you mount them to a tripod (I usually DC the battery grip when I mount the body on a tripod though).

title: The lens that came had obviously been mounted and was unpacked
text: So someone had already tried it on their body and sent it back. Didn't really matter since it might be perfect on my camera, but nope. It had a severe backfocus issue with my body and since the principle camera I was going to use it on is a T4i, no MFA. So I sent it back too. Also, at f/1.4 it was unacceptable. Not until f/2.8 did it sharpen up, but I have a 17-50 f/2.8 sigma that is razor sharp at f/2.8, so the advantage of an f/1.4 lens was out the window... Oh well, you try what you can. Aside from shelling out a few g's for a Zeiss that IS sharp at 1.4 or the canon 24 f/1.4, not sure what else there is out there?

title: Nice case, but VERY heavy!
text:
You wouldn't think a small case that holds eight SD cards would be something you could call "heavy," but the rubber that the cards fit into is VERY dense and bordering on lead-heavy. You could hurt someone throwing this at them. It works, but for travel? I left it home after all and went with a cheap zippered case that weighed one-tenth of this thing. If I were traveling in a way that I didn't need to haul all my gear and had slave-labor to depend on, sure, I'd use this. For the normal traveler though, forget it. Too many things that take precedence, weight-wise, over an SD card case made of lead (OK, rubberized-lead, but still...).

Upside is that it seems very durable and will probably outlast the next apocalypse. I won't so who cares?

title: Nice that it's variable, bad that it takes 5-batts and doesn't like rechargeables.
text:
I took this overseas for use as highlight/hairlight in a run/gun, one-man video production deal. It works, but you have to use alkaline batteries AND you have to have FIVE. Really? When most batteries are sold in packs of 2,4,8, etc., ever heard of even numbers guys?

Whatever. For the money, it was worth having and I really like the step-adjustable switch in back (it adjusts for various levels of light and has a dedicated on/off switch). Anyway, dropped it once and it shut off immediately. Thought it was gone. Turned off, then on again and "presto," worked.

Pros: lots of light for a small package, variable, tough.

Cons: doesn't like rechargeable (1.3v) batteries, takes five batteries to run, mounting is weird and a bit flimsy.

______________

UPDATE: about this fifth time this was used, we went to set up a shoot (closeup interview) and this just doesn't turn on. New Ray-O-Vac AA's. Buy fresh, 10-year Duracells, still nothing. Do everything we can think. Still nothing. Just dead. Sitting in a padded equip box for a year without batteries stored in it and it just stops. Dead. Nothing. So we got four uses out of this light that was totally picky about batteries. RUN AWAY from these lights! RIPOFF!!

title: Front feet VERY fragile
text: Bought this because it was a LOT cheaper than the Cam Caddie. The front feet both broke off within two weeks. Glued, broke again. Sheesh. The injection molded rears are solid, but the fronts are unsupported underneath, just the way it's designed. Works great as long as you don't have to pack it in luggage or camera bags. I like that it has a mic-mount on top that's adjustable.

title: Aftermarket, poor quality, worthless
text: These were bought to replace the hinges on a 4-year old T61. These are really, REALLY cheap knock-offs that look something like the stock hinges, but the casting flaws, flash in the holes and all the parting lines and looseness betray their fake origins. You are better off with the old, stock, loose hinges than these. Even the support bar that is supposed to be riveted to the zinc casting part was loose and fell out of the bosses that should have been staked-down to keep it on. Sheesh. Anyway, after about ten openings of the LCD, these hinges are looser than the 4-year old ones they replaced. If it wasn't so much work to get them out and replace them, I'd just put the old ones back in. I probably will just that soon though, when I get tired of these being even looser than the old ones. Don't waste your time OR money on these cheap copies. They aren't worth the (lead-plated butter) metal they're made with.

title: Skeptical about it's build, but upon inspection, WOW!
text:
I have been through 4-different "travel" tripods so far, ranging from Ravelli to Polaroid to Sunpak to Targus. Seemed like no one made a HIGH-END, high-quality travel tripod. But I just received this and am pretty impressed. All-aluminum means all important parts are aluminum. The snap-locks on the legs are plastic, but they almost look like glass-loaded plastic, not the shiny, cheap looking molded ones on the low-end tripods?

This thing is pretty short at full extension, but for its size and weight, it's unbelievably well-built. Like a little tank. The thinnest legs are a bit flimsy, but I don't see how they could be made larger without making this thing TOO big for a small, lightweight travel tripod. There are always going to be some compromises. Almost think they should have just left out the smallest legs, but you can opt to just raise it by the first two and leave the smallest ones inside.

Swivel is "OK," but for travel stuff, I don't go to places where I have the luxury of just buying another one somewhere, so strength and endurance are more an issue for me. I go through all my gear and tighten, locktite, lube, etc., everything that needs the respective attention.

The bag it came with is also worthy of a review. It's well-made and a really nice, soft, tough material that I'll actually use instead of doing the normal thing and make a ballistic nylon bag for.

It was a hard decision spending $60 on a tiny travel tripod (that's with leaving the $500 Bogen vid tripod/head at home - go figure), but after playing with this, I know I will be glad I did when I'm photog'ing in some jungle in the middle of nowhere.

10-year warranty, great build, light, VERY compact, reversing center column, outstanding stowage bag = great deal!

title: Great camera, but drains batteries when off
text: Great camera that gives the 7d a run for its money. It's not a sealed body like the 7d, but if you care for it as you should anyway, that shouldn't be an issue. The only problem, which for us is HUGE, is that it will drain batteries within a few days when sitting OFF in a camera bag or on the shelf. It seems to use a huge amount of power when off. Called Canon and they said, "yes, they can do that," like, "so? did you have any other stupid questions?" Our 7D and even the 60D never did that. The two Elph 300 camera's we use for quick shots of sets and what not will last MONTHS on a battery just sitting in an un-used state in the camera. This T3i will drain batteries if they are left in a camera body whether or not it's on, so we have to store batteries outside the camera. Which means it's no good for news or run and gun stuff. We're selling it and going to something else since we can't have a camera that drains a brand-new, fully charged Canon battery in three days while sitting on the shelf or that we have to find the battery to install it to take a quick shot. Low rating due to Canon's attitude when I've tried to deal with this issue.

title: Bought for T3i and works like a charm
text: Can't say enough good about this grip. The mount on the bottom is metal threads, the intervalometer works, all the switches that we need work for us and it's SO nice to have enough battery to last through a shoot without having to charge something. I'd buy this again any day.

title: Tube of the eyepiece sticks out too far from the cam, but OK
text: The tube of the eyepiece is round and restricts you from seeing the corners of the viewfinder because the tube is too long, but I'd buy this again if it were the only thing out there, or if something else cost more than twice what this did. Good deal for the price. Doesn't stay locked into the eyepiece rails, but a bit of gaffers tape cured that.

title: Cheap, but works great
text: Works as it should. We needed to extend our USB cable and this does it for us. We use it to join two USB extension cables together. Seems cheap, but it works as-advertised and is well worth the $'s.

title: Great stands, economical way to light your production
text: These are pretty cheap, but higher quality than I expected. They have worked perfectly for a while now and the only thing that might be an issue is the plastic tightener nuts, but those are easily replaced locally. For the price, you can't beat these.

title: Zykkor hoods rock for the price!
text: These are sturdy, tough and work perfectly. Better than most factory hoods. Threads work perfectly and the aluminum they are made of is really tough stuff. I've banged, scraped and done lots of nasty things to them on the end of long lenses and so far they have been an awesome hood. I'd buy again in a heartbeat.

title: Works like it should, nice quality for the price
text: We have a few of these cheapo adjustable ND filters and they have been a life-saver where we want shallow DOF, but already have too much light and don't want to raise shutter speed. Make sure yours won't come apart, I've heard they do that, but ours have worked fine for 6-months now and WELL worth the price!

title: All-metal and works perfectly
text: For the price, I just don't see how they can even make this item? Works just as it should and is all-metal and very well made. We use it to mount a small field recorder on our DSLR for video sync. Works like a charm. Really good deal on a well-made item.

title: Great sound and like that they're collapsible.
text: We use these in our audio bag since they collapse down nicely and have very good sound for their low price. Well worth it if you need some cheap headphones that stow away easily. Feel kind of cheaply made and like they'll break easily, but so far, no problem.

title: Great box for the price, PITA to assemble.
text: Really, for the money, I can't complain at all about this soft-box. It's a GREAT size to get into tight places and nicely diffuses light to soften shadows and give a warmer tint. Just leave it assembled after you get it together and it's fine. Since it's only 16", you can carry it to shoots as it is. Anything bigger and you would have to disassemble it. Anyway, quality is pretty darn good for what it cost and the value is high. I'd buy one again. Most stuff from Cowboy Studio has been excellent for the economy.

title: Awesome variable ND filter!
text: For the price, these just can't be beat. We have two of them on a few large aperture lenses (for cinematography) and they work SO nicely. Optics of the ones we got are clear and not an issue. If you need a low shutter speed and want shallow DOF from a 1.4 lens, then this is the only way to go. You could spend $250 on one, but these work great for feature-film quality reels. May have some quality issues, so make sure you test your model and spin it a bit to make sure it won't fall apart on you, other than that, a fantastic deal for the $'s.

title: Premium sockets are the only ones to get
text: We bought a few of the "non" premium sockets and they are cheap and "plasticky." One lasted less than one shoot. So we bought some of these and they are the ones to get. Just make sure you tighten the screws holding the ceramic socket in, or better, take the whole thing apart and put a lock washer or locktite on the threads. The thermal expansion loosens them in short-order and you'll lose the screws if you don't. Other than that, especially for the price, these are a very good socket at a great price.

title: Excellent hoods
text: We have a number of these and they are all rock-solid hoods, strong, take a beating, threads work great, do their job and WAY better than most factory hoods.

title: All these Zykkor hoods have been awesome
text: We have three types of cheap Zykkos hoods and they are all great hoods. Strong, threads work perfect, protect the lens banging on things and WELL worth the cost. Can't say enough good about them. For the price you can't go wrong.

title: Works like it should
text: Works just as designed, threads are "gritty," so "lube" them with wax or something, hand lotion, whatever, so you can get it apart from a filter (or they could seize). Well worth ordering, good price, good ring.

title: Kenko 52-77 step ring works just as it should
text: Ring works, but make sure you "lube" the threads with wax or chapstick or something, otherwise it'll grind and seize on other alum threads. Just how these kinds of things are. Can't believe they can make and sell these so cheap, but they work just as they should.

title: Ordered Tamron SP Di VC, got something else.
text:
EDITED: We ordered a Tamron AF 70-300mm f/4.0-5.6 SP Di VC USD XLD for Canon Digital SLR Cameras with 2nd day shipping to take to a shoot this weekend. What came, shipped by Amazon, was a NON VC lens, a $150 crap lens with a different part number and our camera wouldn't even notice that a lens was installed with this on it.

Edit: Had to pay full retail for one (Tamron SP Di VC) locally for a specialty shoot this weekend as we promptly (the day we received it) sent the wrong one back. Since we could test them in-store, we took the one that looked the best for sharpness at the time. After pixel-picking on a FS monitor, there was some CA where I wouldn't expect it and sharpness falls-off a bit at corners, but overall, and CERTAINLY for the price, this lens is well worth having. Except the size. It's very bulky. Not too heavy, just bulky. Big. Hard to store in bag. Otherwise, it's not a 70-200L, but it's nice glass.

title: Inner metal threads fall out
text: I like the way this articulates and mounts, but the thin metal threaded ring in the socket fell out. Bulbs won't thread in. This happened the first time I tried it, when I pulled it out of the box. YMMV, but I'm sending this back and will order another brand, hopefully not China and hopefully higher quality. Some of the products with the "Neewer" name on it have been pretty good, for a cheap Chinese mfg, but this one doesn't hold up to the name.

title: Works as expected and great for location shoots!
text: There is not much to this item, but the reflector works just as it should and really like having the gold side to warm the light a bit on a subject. Collapses easily (practice collapsing it to the size that fits back into the case) and very transportable. Was a great deal on something that every photographer should have!

title: Excellent product, honest sellers
text: This works as expected (read the manual, takes a bit to get used to its menu), and made us money on a project. Quality is very high for the price of this item. Am impressed with it's flexibility. Also use it as a remote shutter release. All in all, a great deal for the cost. Sellers were very communicative and honest. I would do business with this company anytime.

title: Solid system, but hinges SUCK!
text:
Great reliability, tough, fast, workhorse, but on my third set of NEW hinges (they last about 3-6 months max before they start to become wobbly - bad design, every one of these I've played with has the same crappy hinge problem).

I like being able to swap out the memory, hard drive, keyboard easily by yourself. Since Lenovo took these over from IBM, the quality has been going down, but this one is still nicely made (again, except the damn hinges!)

title: Agree with others, these just suck. I can scream louder!
text: These are "Poor Horns," not power horns. They might startle a sleeping baby with it's head butted up against it, otherwise, they're a joke. Also, after about six months and having never been actually triggered, only tested, they stopped working. Expensive, worthless white  boxes. Find something other than X10. Just not a real alarm. A toy at best.

title: Cheap, but works just as it should.
text: Light, very inexpensive and reads about anything (needed a spare CF card reader), works just as advertised, not much else to say.

title: Just like all the rest, only flimsier.
text:
Had one of these and it was light and loud (after decades on the range, my ears need more volume than most people), but it kept falling off and you never notice it's gone. The ear piece is too "rubbery" and flops all over, but that's why it's so comfortable.

Anyway, finally lost it for good, so I bought another off Amazon. This new one SUCKS! At full volume even people with sensitive ears can't hear it well enough to understand if there's any background noise. I guess like everything now, if it's made in China, it's hit or miss. One is great, one sucks. Going to yet another brand to see if someone else can get it right.

title: Works, but expect a little softer focus
text: Worked great, but the focus was always a little "soft," almost like a very light diffusion filter. Use care when installing, but it should mount perfectly. It did for us. Worth the cost for the ability to use the older, FAST FD lenses.

title: Very poor noise cancellation.
text: Purchased this as a gift. The recipient wanted the pricey and unattractive air pods, and I thought these would be great. However, during calls the person using these sounded muffled and they couldn't hear other people during calls. I could hear every noise and talking in their background better than I could hear them. I returned them for a refund. I thought this was a great purchase based on the reviews. :(

title: Not so Great Charging cable
text:
Great charging cable for Android phone. The length was the main reason for making this purchase. I purchased two 10ft cords from a different seller and they both lasted approximately 6-8 months. It seems to be difficult finding cables at a reasonable price that actually last. These cords have almost a cloth-like feeling to the cords, its not a hard, stiff wire feel like the previous brand. I will update this review if anything changes.
