This one specifies 5-900MHz, which is likely to cause problems with your HD channels. Most frequently, some channels won't come through, or you may see a lot of "digital noise". (I've seen the problems, and verified that the splitter is the culprit, by removing the splitter.)

You may want to get a splitter with a wider frequency range ...

title: very nice case
text:
I bought the case for a Canon SD8xx series camera, and it's just the right size for those. (I have another case that's very similar, same brand, just a bit softer.)

The case is well-cushioned, and I'd expect it to do a good job of protecting the camera in the kind of fall you might get in normal use. (Sorry, I'm not going to test it. But you can see "test" results in another review.) And the pocket inside is quite suitable for an extra memory chip or something like that, perhaps even a spare battery.

I'm very pleased with the product -- it's really very nice for the low price.

title: Excellent SDHC card, great price
text:
I have been using Panasonic SDHC Class 6 4GB cards, and have been pretty happy with them. I decided to get this one just because of the low price and high ratings, and am pleased to find that I agree with the many 5-star reviews.

Some information I didn't see in the other reviews, in case it's of interest: I ran a write test with a big file on my computer, and saw write speeds consistently above 6MB/s, as you ought to expect for a Class 6. (Among other things, that means of course that your camera can get ready for the next shot just that much faster because it's spending less time waiting for the recording to be completed.)

I didn't bother with a read test, since read speed is rarely an issue.

A comment on SD card readers/writers. As many have said, older SD devices, including older cameras, will not work with SDHC cards. My old card adapter (Sandisk 8-in-1) hung when I put this chip in. But my newer adapters (a built-in slot, and an Edge All-in-1) worked just fine. So if you're having trouble, this is possibly the first thing to check.

title: excellent camera, sd870 is the updated version (not sd850)
text:
This is (was) an excellent camera, if what you want is a pocket-able point-and-shoot camera. Very versatile, easy to use, excellent pictures every time.

Contrary to what Amazon says, the SD870 IS is the new model equivalent to this one. And it's available at a pretty good price right here. (I just got that one, but haven't used it enough to review yet. Check other websites for professional reviews, e.g., cnet.com.)

title: excellent blu-ray player, but dvd upconversion not so great
text:
As many other reviews (including professional ones) have described, this is one of the best blu-ray players available in this price range right now.

I don't have much to add to those reviews, but will make two quick points.

(1) If you have a Bravia tv, the player and the tv work together well (e.g., you can use the remotes to control both, can have the tv automatically turn on and switch to the BD player).

(2) If you play a regular dvd in this, you will get upconversion (electronic conversion of the 480p video to 1080p video), but I found that my Oppo 981 dvd player's upconversion was noticeably better (sharper & clearer picture).

So I'd definitely recommend this player for blu-ray, but you might want to hang on to your Oppo for playing your dvd collection.

title: flimsy, poorly made, broken out of the box (FAN-CLRC)
text:
NOTE: Amazon seems to have clustered reviews for several different cooling products under one set. I've edited this one to do a new review of the product "Sabrent Laptop/Notebook Cooler Pad with 230-Milimeter Fan (upto 17-Inch) (FAN-CLRC)". (I don't even remember which product the original review was for.)

The product I received looked ok, but as soon as I put it on the table, the housing of the fan came partly loose from the plastic base (on which the computer would sit). So now the unguarded fan is hanging down in a tilt, hitting the table, etc. Obviously quite unusable, so it's going right back in the box.

I can't recommend such an obviously shoddly product. I'm amazed that it's even on the market.

title: good cable, no need to pay for some brandname
text:
I use these cables for connecting MP3 devices and such, and also for connecting my Razr cellphone, using the Motorola Phone Tools software on my computer. (Note that for the latter purpose, you can actually use Bluetooth if you want to, and have the capability on your computer.)

Cable works perfectly, no problems or hassles. Construction quality is good. This is pretty basic technology after all.

title: excellent amp
text:
I replaced my old Yamaha receiver with this Onkyo amp, and also got the related tuner and single-disk cd player. I used them with my old speakers while my new ones (Aperion) were arriving, and my reaction was "Wow!" All of a sudden the sound was bigger, clearer, and brighter.

If you're looking for a stereo amp in the $5-900 price range, and care about sound, you won't regret buying this component. It's all it promises to be.

title: simple to set up, easy to use
text:
Just got this, so can't comment on reliability and longevity. However, it was easy to set up -- just plugged in an ethernet wire from my router, and it became visible on the network. It's quiet, and doesn't take up much room. Performance is decent with 100Mb network, I don't have Gigabit setup right now.

I didn't bother installing their software (you don't need to if you are familiar with networked servers & storage). I was able to log in (easily) through a browser on one of my machines, make configuration changes, and make it become a member of the workgroup. Seems to work fine with XP and Vista, so far completely trouble-free.

I haven't tried hanging usb drives off it yet, will do so and update this review. They also provided some backup software from Memeo that might be worth trying out.

I like it enough that I'm planning to get a second one to use as a mirrored backup.

title: excellent mouse at a great price
text:
This is an excellent mouse, works like a charm. It's precise and reliable (much better than the Microsoft mouse I threw away), does what a mouse is supposed to do.

I can't understand why some others have had problems with it, but I haven't had any problems with sleep mode or connection or whatever.

Ok, I can make one criticism: I don't like the little buttons on the top left, I find them less convenient than the bigger buttons on the sides that some other mice have. But I was looking for a nice travelling mouse, not a mouse with many buttons and features.

(I bought the V400 in Orange, if that matters.) Great price at Amazon, and a Logitech rebate of about half the price!

title: excellent dvd player
text:
Just to add my vote, this is an excellent DVD player. I use it with an older Sony LCD tv (XBR1, only goes to 1080i), and compared the picture, using a standard widescreen DVD, with my older Panasonic progressive scan Panasonic dvd player (480p output). The picture with this one is clearly superior.

As others have said, the whole thing reeks quality and attention to detail. A good quality HDMI cable is included, as well as standard video/audio cables in case you need them for troubleshooting. The packaging is a class above the industry.

If you want something for watching standard DVDs with a good HDTV, consider this one or the 981HD model.

title: excellent -- worth the money
text:
I concur with the other reviewers, this is an excellent TV (Sony KDL-40XBR4). The picture is gorgeous, especially with HD input (1080i or 1080p). Even looks good when watching VHS tape! The only problem is that some analog tv channels just look plain bad (grainy and fuzzy).

The controls are sensible, configuration and customization (e.g., input labels, picture/sound settings) are easy. The remote is a bit bigger (longer) than I'd prefer, but that's a minor quibble.

Yes, possibly you'll pay more for this one than some others. And sometimes a know-it-all salesperson will tell you that X or Y has much better reviews from "experts". For my money, I always find that the Sony in the store has the best picture.

On LCD vs. plasma, perhaps that's more a personal thing. But I don't find the "black level" argument in favor of plasmas particularly convincing. And I like watching 4:3 without stretching, so I'm not about to risk burn-in on a plasma. So I only considered LCDs.

BTW, the EagleGL shipping service used by Amazon for this was ok. They gave us a 4 hour window and were more than an hour late, but other than that no problems. (Mine was easy -- ground floor, 10 steps from the front door. So might not apply for every case.)

title: works fine, but uncomfortable
text:
I've had this headset for about a year now; I use it with a Razr. It's a fine headset from a technical perspective: the sound is fine, it's easy to pair and use, etc. I haven't run into any problems using it in a car, or out of doors.

However, it's really not very comfortable: the hook that goes over the ear is just a bit too stiff and edgy, I wouldn't want to wear it for a long call (more than 15-20min say).

For comfort and performance, consider the Plantronics Voyager 510 (around $50 at Amazon); I've had one of those (now used by my son), and it is excellent. If you're into new gadgets, check out the Jawbone sets -- I haven't used one, but a colleague swears by the one he's been using for a couple of months.

title: Works as advertised.
text:
If you care about speed (why wouldn't you?), then you'll probably be getting SDHC Class 6 chips. But even among those there appears to be some variation. This particular Panasonic chip, and the Extreme III line from Sandisk, appear to be the best ones.

Just make sure your device (camera or whatever) is fully compatible.

(Start with something like Wikipedia if you want more technical info about SD & SDHC.)

title: very unreliable
text:
Clearly the quality control on this product is terrible, since some people report a good experience with it. Mine worked fine for about 2 months, since then it's erratic, which of course means unusable in practice.

Also, I found that I heartily disliked the fussy design of the key storage -- if you don't get it in exactly right it doesn't turn off the switch.

title: it works, which is all I ask
text:
I was sceptical of a "non-impact" punchdown tool, but it was really quite easy to use, and it does the job. I only would use this rarely, since I don't do this for a living, so getting something at a reasonable price was a factor in the decision. Unless you need a professional tool that you're going to use frequently (in which case get a Paladin), this will do it for you.

It's 4 stars instead of 5 because the Paladin I had borrowed and used once before had a more satisfying motion and was clearly a superior tool.

title: excellent monitor, great value
text:
This is an excellent monitor, and at Amazon's price, an amazingly good value. I bought two of these for my kids, after doing a ton of research. I was a bit sceptical, until I hooked them up and checked them out (using normal stuff, plus games, photos, and dvd video) -- the visuals are bright and sharp, the response time is excellent, everything looks very good.

Just make sure you use the native resolution, of course, and use the DVI cable that comes in the box. (Check your video card to make sure you have DVI output.)

You will read in some online reviews that the screens are glossy, and that some people don't like that. I find I have neither any objection, nor any problem with reflections or whatever (the lights in the room are overhead). But make your own decision on this.

title: fantom drives are garbage
text:
I'd advise against anything from this manufacturer. My experience is that their products are shoddy, made with cheap components, and therefore don't last. First, you get increasing noise. Then you get intermittent cacophony. Then you get a failing disk.

If you want recommendations: I've been happy with Maxtor and Western Digital products.

title: very uncomfortable, poor volume
text:
I recommend AVOID. This item is poorly designed -- it's very uncomfortable (the ear-hook is odd and stiff, there is no soft cushion against the ear), the volume is poor and can't be adjusted much, and the cord for some odd reason comes out on the inside of the mike boom. (Whose brilliant idea was that?)

I can't explain all the great reviews, which induced me to buy this, so I won't even try.

Consider the M175 if you want a really nice headset at a reasonable price.

title: nice, but a bit too compact perhaps
text:
<<Targus CVR400 15 CityLite Notebook Case>>

This is very nice if what you want to carry with you is a 15in laptop, powercord, small mouse, plus some paperwork. There's no room for anything more, it's not really made for stuffing extra stuff. Even an extra paperback might be a bit too much.

I find it just a bit too small for my use -- I'd have liked it to be a little bit fatter, so I can carry some extra stuff like a book, pill bottles, and such.

One criticism: the strap is ok, but not as comfortable as you'd ideally want. I found it handy to take the strap off my old Lands End canvas briefcase and use that instead.

title: excellent case, well designed & made, will hold 17in laptop
text:
(Targus TCG417 17 CityGear Los Angeles Notebook Case)

As others have said, this is a well-designed and well-constructed case. It is great if you want to carry a 17in laptop, some cds & dvds, a few books & magazines, etc.

Go for it if it meets your specs.

title: it does extend range if used with a range-max router or wap -- but it's not spectacular
text:
Yes, it does "work". Meaning if you get the RangeMax router or wireless access point, the pair of them do give you better range than (for example) a Netgear WGT624 router with a WGT511 card (and other such combos that I've tried). It's a bit erratic -- the signal level fluctuates, which seems to me to be a software (algorithm) problem. I hope they can improve it further, but for now it's meeting my needs.

A bit more detail: I have a large house, and the networking stuff is all at one end (never mind why), so at the other end of the house the wireless signal would fade to nothing. With this RangeMax combo I can now get an adequate signal (2 bars) where I used to get nothing.

So don't expect too much, but also don't be daunted by the bad reviews, it's worth a try. As you know, every building is different, so as they say in another context, your results may vary.

title: excellent sound, works reliably and consistently
text:
Definitely a good buy, especially as the price keeps dropping! Excellent sound. I have it paired with a Razr, and it was fairly straightforward, after I carefully re-read and understood the instructions :-)

I wish they had made it easier to fold and put in a pocket (and also that it shut off easily like some of the Moto models). Also note that if you use the little foam tip for the mouthpiece, it can fall off way too easily.

title: good choice for a basic wireless optical mouse
text: Nothing fancy, but a great choice if what you want is a good solid optical mouse without a wire.  Good for younger hands (I bought it for a 7-year old boy).

title: nice sound, limited features
text:
Very nice sound, better than the Philips product of similar price. However, some deficiencies make it a bit disappointing: (1) no digital volume control, so you can't set volume level for an alarm, and there is no progressively louder alarm; (2) (as someone else noted) if you want 2 alarms at 2 different times (e.g., 5am & 6am), they need to be on different music sources (e.g., 5am radio, 6am CD).

I'd still recommend it if the features don't make a big difference to you, since the sound is good and everything works well.

title: works well while it lasts -- but don't count on long life
text:
I've had two Linksys products die on me shortly after a year (a 4-port router/switch, and now this 8-port switch). It works fine until it dies (but that's like saying a stapler staples correctly: it's supposed to).

Just to note: I run them in a very friendly environment -- no dust or heat or voltage spikes or any of that to blame for the problem. (Also, you can count me as an "expert user".)

I myself will never buy another Linksys product again -- I'll try out Netgear & DLink and other brands, but goodbye Cisco/Linksys. If you chooose to try their products, caveat emptor.

title: good while it lasts, but doesn't last long
text:
As others have reported, quality is disappointing. Thought it was a good router at a decent price, until it started breaking down, regularly (shows red diagnostic light).
Linksys website indicates that company knows about the problem, and will replace (only) if within warranty period. Technically within their rights, but seems unethical to me -- they sold a defective product and aren't taking the responsibility for it.
Recommend you avoid this, and be careful about other Linksys products.

title: Updated review:  broke after three months of use
text:
Edited to add: It stopped working after three months. We changed the batteries,
updated the driver, cleaned out the ball area, moved out to another PC and nothing had worked to make it work again. The return window closed 30 after purchase and the product support page leads nowhere. We won't be buying this again.

ORIGINAL: This was purchased as a means to alleviate shoulder and elbow pain from traditional mouse use at work. So far, it's helped dramatically. Like many new things, it takes getting used to this type of mouse/trackball device, but it's great if you're willing to adapt. You don't have to have your hand or elbow resting on the desk to use this and can stand or walk around with your arms relaxed.

title: Worked once and never again
text: We were able to get this cd player to work literally one time,  and then it wouldn't work at all. Wouldn't turn on after multiple battery changes. It's too expensive for so much of a hassle,  so we returned it.

title: Only one side works after two months
text: As title states. I bought these for my Samsung S9 phone, and have used them once every few days since purchasing them on Sep 7. Now only one side is functioning and the other is completely silent.

title: Shaped so that the earpiece can't actually fit into ear.
text: The material is too soft, and the earpiece collapses out of the ear. It's also shaped in such a way that the piece that goes into the ear canal actually doesn't. I can't use these at all.

title: So far so good, hopefully it won't fall on someone
text: We used this item to mount a PC to the wall, but the supplied straps were too short by about a foot for my case. I measured and it was within the dimensions mentioned, but it didn't work. We were able to get some other straps that were longer, and hopefully they hold up long term. I would have given a higher rating if it seemed more sturdy and less like a wall mounted death trap.

title: Failed randomly after three years of use
text: Expansion drive for my xbox one failed after three years. Started the click of death and nothing loads. I won't be buying another.

title: {Edited}There was a sticker inside the adapter
text:
I would have given these cables a higher rating, but I had to remove a sticker from inside the adapter before it could be used. Still don't know if it will work after pulling it out. See photos.
{Edited on 10/29/2018 to reflect customer service assistance. I received an entirely new package of hdmi cables at no extra cost to ensure my satisfaction with my previous order. It was an unexpected, but pleasant surprise. }

title: Bulb lasted almost exactly two years before burning out.
text: This bulb lasted almost exactly two years from purchase (April 2015-May 2017). I guess this is reasonable, but I'd rather have it work a bit longer given the expense. It was easy enough to install, but I don't think we're going to buy another one to replace it. At this point, I could buy a new tv that doesn't require a $90 part every two years.

title: Just buy the daggon thing already..
text: Ok, I'm hooked on alexa.. I use her for everything. If only she could love me back 😢

title: Efficient product, in line with description
text: Great product

title: Excellent HDMI HD Cable!!!
text: Bought this to connect my new Roku Ultra to my television. Great purchase! Excellent picture and sound quality!! Great Velcro cable holder, allowing one to keep cable neatly organized if entire length not needed.

title: Great protection for your iPad screen!
text: Be sure to watch the You Tube video on the manufacturer-provided link. If you follow the directions, this applies beautifully to your iPad and protects the screen well. No problem with bubbles and it went into place precisely. Buy with confidence!

title: Lovely listening for your ears!
text:
I have had all sorts of earbuds, but must admit for the price these are simply wonderful--and absolutely beautiful! I tend to listen while sitting or lying down, and these have wonderful sound for such use. I also love the simple beauty of the wood.

On the other hand, I am not so sure these would be the best choice if you are jogging or working out --- they might not stay put.

So bottom line, if you are not working out and relatively still I think you will love these! Superb sound and a great price!

title: Don't buy--Stops at 75 minutes
text: I had bought these successfully before but this time every disc stopped recording at about 75 minutes on SP. Could record 4 hours on EP but not 6. Kept thinking the next disc would be better but entire pack was defective.

title: Top Rate Replacement Cable for your Apple Device
text: What a delight!  The cord and fittings are first rate, thicker, and seemingly better engineered. My original cable from Apple, careful as I was, began to fray badly just from normal wear after 3 years.  I expect this Monoprice cable to last at least double and maybe triple the time of the original Apple cable. It is also twice as long, which has made it considerably more useful, especially when travelling.

title: Great TV and fantastic value -- Get one while you can!!!
text:
I bought this TV to replace a wonderful but very old Panasonic 32" CRT that finally gave up the ghost just before Christmas. It is a totally satisfactory replacement and I recommend it strongly.

I had admired the new LED screens, but as I began investigating refresh rates and looking at the displays in stores, I came to the conclusion I would prefer a plasma screen, but my space would not accommodate anything larger than a 42". Which made this model absolutely perfect. Sears had the best price, but they were sold out by the time I placed an order. However, Walmart had the next best price at $398, so I ordered one for pickup at a local store. As it turned out, they were out of stock locally, but were able to get one within 10 days. It was well worth the wait.

In comparison to similarly sized LED TV's, this model is slightly heavier ( just under 40 pounds out of the box). Of course, in comparison to the old CRT, it was much much lighter. The stand assembled easily and seems quite sturdy. 8 screws total and a ratchet and it was ready for cables to be attached.

This is an HDTV. I may eventually bite the bullet and get HD service from Comcast, but even with the normal, non-HD cable box, the image is wonderful and light years beyond my old CRT. And the sound is GREAT! Unlike many of the LED models I considered, the sound on this model is better than on my old CRT and no need to get a sound bar. Right now I have it hooked up to an older Panasonic VCR/DVD recorder/player (non Blu-ray), an Apple TV (for streaming Netflix and which uses one of the two HDMI connections) and my Comcast cable box. It was easy to set up and I am very satisfied with the image quality. Speaking of which, I used the settings provided by R. White in his review, although I changed the tint to a -3 rather than the 0 he uses, and strongly recommend you try them as a point of departure. I am now assessing universal remotes to replace the four I currently need to operate the various components and will probably settle on a Logitech Harmony model.

If you are looking for a good and serviceable TV and don't need a larger size than 42"' or more than two HDMI connections, or the other bells and whistles, this is a fantastic choice. I don't understand the relatively low marks it gets in its review by CNET; In my opinion, it is much better than the review indicates. The advantage with the plasma is you don't need to worry about the refresh rate and the picture is great no matter what angle you watch from. (Note that if the room in which you are will place this unit has a lot of natural light, you may prefer the LED.) Also, as other reviewers have said, for this size of TV, I really don't think the eye can distinguish between 720p and 1080, and the image quality is really quite satisfactory. With the addition of an Apple TV or Blue-ray player with WiFi, you have the equivalent of a smart TV without paying the premium for one. Even at $500, this TV is a very good buy and better than you will find most of the LED's of similar size. If you can find one for under $400, grab it! But you should move fast, because these are going quickly.

title: Made for small/narrow faces; otherwise fine
text:
I bought these on sale without, and I can't quite bring myself to return them because they are otherwise serviceable, but they feel quite tight on my head and there's no proper way to adjust them out, just longer or shorter. Because these are on ear headphones, that lack of adjustability means that my ears are smashed pretty tightly against my head and quickly become uncomfortable and warm. For reference, my head is between 21" and 22" around at the top of my ears... which appears to be average per Google.

TLDR: If you are an adult with an average size head, these may not be as comfortable a fit as you'd expect.

title: Much slower than the Fire TV Stick system I traded in
text:
We had the Fire TV Stick streaming media player with Alexa built in, includes Alexa Voice Remote, HD, easy set-up, released 2019, but occasionally the remote would become undetectable by the base and I saw that this one could control the soundbar and tv, so I traded it in for a coupon. The new system is very slow when we open up apps like YouTube and Twitch, so much so that my household has been using our old Google Chromecast for those tasks instead. Overall I really wish I had just kept the old system and cannot recommend this new one.

UPDATE: I am returning this fire stick because I just received and installed the 4K version; it works so much more quickly and easily! I would /not/ recommend the 3rd Gen fire stick with dedicated app buttons to anyone. Get the 4K even if you don't need the 4K definition!

I wish the analog clock showed the date - just the digital one does.
The watch seems to work well enough and the battery lasts about a day. The battery recharges quickly.

title: It's amazing what an extra 2" can do
text:
I guess I'm a little bit of a Fire-omaniac in that I own 3 different Fire tablets; an old 7" that I use primarily to play solitare; a 10" that I use with a keyboard as a small laptop and now this New 8" Fire HD. I traded in a Fire 6" for this . The 6" , I felt was just a little small. It's amazing what an extra 2" can do! This Fire fits perfectly in the murse that I bought in Italy last year.
So much for fashion, but how does it perform? Well, the screen definition is bright, sharp and clear. I LOVE the Blue Shade feature for night time reading in bed. I'm impressed with the audio quality of the two small speakers. As a professional musician, sound quality is important to me. The option of using an SD card for extra storage of music and photos is also a valuable asset.
The tablet responds very quickly, is easy to navigate and simple to use. I bought it for travel but find myself using it at home in place of my laptop.
The only slightly disappointing feature are the on-board cameras. The photos are a little grainy.
All in all, it's a great tablet. My wife likes it so much that she wants one as a substitute for her iPad.

Addendum: having written this review I was contacted by the sellers who understood my concerns. They offered and sent a newer version of the bag that is far superior to the the original. It is far, far roomier, even with a pocket that fits my 6 inch Fire Tablet in a case. There is a good handle for carrying and two compartments for storing "stuff". I like the extra slots for flash cards, Sims etc. All in all a far superior product and I'm impressed by the customer service of the seller.

title: these ear phones are comfortable to wear and I like the 'folding" feature.
text:
OK, these ear phones are comfortable to wear and I like the 'folding" feature. Now about the sound. I have been a professional musician all my life - acoustic, rock and country - so sound is important to me. I like a crisp and clear sound with a balanced sound. The sound is good.
Since writing this first review I have used them for travel - two plane rides to and from London, UK out of Miami FL USA.
As someone else noticed they are bulky and take up a lot of space in carry on luggage.I wore them for about five of the eight hour flight and they were comfortable. Even without the noise cancelling feature they greatly reduced the cabin noise. Listening to movie soundtracks the sound was very good indeed - not surprisingly, far superior to the video quality of the small screens. When I listened to the audio music feed provided on BA, the quality was good, still a bit bass heavy but not too bad. I realize that sound is very much a personal taste and some people prefer much more bass than I do and I've played bass professionally.
One of my problems with the sound was probably because I am used to wearing passive cans with no amplification in the set themselves. These obviously are amplified and the sound is boosted far more than in passive cans.
For the price, these are good head-phones.

title: Worthless external drive
text: I bought the first WD 2TB external drive, but I could not get it to work. The WD Utilities found that the drive was defective, so I asked for a replacement. The second drive passed all of the WD tests, but the WD Backup utility thought the drive was offline. Windows could see the drive and reported no problem, as well as the WD Utilities and Security programs. But, the WD Backup program still thought the drive was offline. I opened an incident with WD technical (worthless) support. All they send is boilerplate FAQ's. I did considerable research on this drive and I really liked the backup software and encryption. But, if it cannot backup my PC, all of those features are worthless. Just like WD technical support. I was in IT for 45 years, so I am comfortable trouble shooting hardware / software problems. But, WD technical support was of no help, what so ever. I recommend that no one buys this drive.

It has a gripper on both sides of the tablet to aid their use and to protect your investment.

Thanks for a great deal and for helping us to help our mother.

title: Terrible Technical Support
text:
I just purchased the router as an upgrade, and proceeded to install it yesterday. The installation CD did not work, tried multiple times and it kept erroring out with run time errors. So I called LinkSys Technical Support and their IMMEDIATE fall back was to do a manual install/configuration. [That tells me this is a fairly common occurance]. The woman I talked to spoke very poor English and had trouble understanding me. She asked to set up a remote session so that she could do the install for me. I said okay and that is where the real pain began. Think she was referencing some sort of a knowledge base to do the set up since it took minutes between key strokes. In any case it took 3 hours to complete the install and the only devices I had connected to the router were my laptop [which is wireless] and cable modem. She knew nothing about setting up netowrk printers, wireless or LAN, nor Vonage. So she said she would have level 2 support call me back to help with them. Ten minutes later they did, and to make a long story short he was clueless, and after 15 minutes gave me the "router is working, that is all I am responsible for, call the printer manufacturer. I said that was NOT acceptable, and HE HUNG UP ON ME. [can't wait to get the survey] In any case I pulled out the installation CD for my wireless printer, ran it and 10 minutes later it was working. Than I simply plugged the other network printer into the router along with the vonage router and both worked.

I truly hope that the router is reliable so that I never have to call for technical support. All I can say is shame on you John Chambers.

title: Very dissapointing
text:
It's so disappointing to pay extra for the "newer" version of something only to find out the old version was better. This is exactly what happened with the gen 3 airpods. If you love your current airpods just hang on to them. It's getting really annoying that apple only tells you about the "new" features and doesn't tell you what you lose when you upgrade.

First they changed the shape so it doesn't fit your ear as well as the prior version. I have to try to jam these in my ear and they constantly fall out. Be sure to try them on before you buy them.

Secondly, they got rid of the super useful tap controls and replaced them with the less useful 'force' control. Which means instead of just tapping your airpod to pause or accept a call you have to feel around your whole head to find the tiny little magic spot on the tiny little stem of the airpod (which is in your ear now since it's shorter than before) and gently pleasure it until it does what apple wants it to (NOT what you want it to- see below). Why anyone would think squeezing the thing would be better than just a simple tap is beyond me. you have to use at least 2 fingers to gently message the stem in just the right way, rather than just a one finger tap (while you are also holding your keys or wallet for example).

Last but not least if you are planning to customize the way you use them (the gestures), like you used to be able to do on the OLDER cheaper version you can forget it. That's gone. Can't customize the new ones. You just have to learn the 42 preset apple gestures of squeeze once for this, three times for that, now spin around and squeeze the other one for siri. It's maddening.

I wore these for an hour then spent 3 hours trying to figure out how to adjust the gestures before i gave up. I immediately went back to my old airpods (gen2) which are far superior to the new more expensive ones. i will probably re-gift these to someone for xmas and I will definitely be betting another gen 2 set.

title: Amazing headphones
text: First off, let me say that I am neither a music pro nor an audiophile.  That said, I have been alive and listening to music long enough that I can hear the difference in quality between crappy, highly compressed MP3s, lossless FLACs/actual CDs, and HD audio.  Anyway, I like headphones that have wide tonal range and have enough bass without sounding stupidly thumpa-thumpa (like Bose or Beats products), and these Sennheiser Momentums fit the bill perfectly!  I use this with my tablet (MP3s), phone (MP3 or streaming from Spotify), and computer (FLAC, CD, and high def audio through external DAC). Sounds absolutely wonderful all the time.  The fact that they look incredible, and are incredibly comfortable, are awesome bonuses.  At under $200, I think this hits the price/performance sweet spot. One thing though... people with big ears might not like to wear these for long periods, because the ear cup seems a bit smaller than other over-the-ear headphones.

title: Just do it
text: Set-up was a total no-brainer.  A quick phone call to Comcast and I was up and running in minutes.  The modem locked on to the signal right away, and now I'm getting about 90mbps downstream pretty consistently.  The status lights are a lot easier to interpret than those in my old Comcast-issued modem. Best part about the whole thing?  I no longer have to pay Comast the $10 a month modem rental fee.  Which means this modem pays for itself in ~9 months.  If you're thinking about buying your own cable modem, stop thinking.  Just do it.

title: I bought this adapter because I need a cheap way ...
text:
I bought this adapter because I need a cheap way to add a second external monitor to my Macbook Pro, which only has one Thunderbolt port. I'm very satisified with this product. Installation of the drivers was quick and painless. The adapter worked right away. When you plug your monitor in via this adapter, there's a momentary delay of probably half a second, then your external monitor comes to life. I connect my monitor's DVI port to this thing, and I get full screen resolution. I only have two quibbles, which together prevent me from giving this 5 stars:
1) I don't know why but my Mac seems to slow down slightly whenever I'm driving a second monitor via this adapter.
2) Unlike with an external monitor connected via Thunderbolt/mini-DisplayPort, which remembers all of the windows that "live" on that monitor's desktop, this one forgets all of the window placements. Every time you unplug this from the USB port of the laptop, all of the windows in snap back to the laptop screen and they do NOT move back to the external monitor automatically when you plug the adapter back in.

Other than those two annoyances, it works perfectly well. The price is definitely right.

title: Ok while it lasted, but it croaked with zero warning.
text:
How long are these supposed to last, anyway? I bought mine in late 2012, and subjected it to what I would consider average use. I used it to store movies, videos, and photos. Three days ago (it is now Feb 2015), it started making a weird noise, then stopped working completely. If I powercycle it, it will make the weird noise (like not-so-muffled clicking sounds) for a few seconds and then turn itself off. The computer doesn't recognize it anymore. I even tried plugging it in to a different computer, but it behaved exactly the same way. I KNOW hard drives eventually die, but every other hard drive I've ever had gave some sort of warning that it was dying. Weird noises would start happening, and I would have enough time to buy a new one and move all my data. This one had NO warning and just DIED. Thank goodness I have cloud backup for my photos. My movies are gone, though.

WHILE IT WAS WORKING, it was decent. Quiet and always functional. Not terribly fast on read / write, especially large file transfers inbound and outbound. It never gave me problems, which is why I'm so incredibly annoyed that one day it just decided to not work at all. I don't think I'll ever buy a consumer-grade Seagate product again.

The mic on both for calls were not impressive. Overall I don't think most people will be disappointed with this purchase.

title: Stable speeds--does not thermally throttle
text:
I am hungry for a high performance flash drive. I want an SSD on a small stick.

The number 1 defect in every flash drive that I have owned up till now is that you get their rated speeds for maybe10-30 seconds, and then, due to crap thermal designs, the controller detects over heating and throttles the speed down by 3-5X. Disaster when you want to do serious file transfers.

This drive, however, is the first that I have ever owned which seems to maintain its speed over long time periods. Writing a 20 GB file to it sees no diminishment in speed over the minute or so that that takes.

I also love how the width and depth of this drive are minimal.

My main complaint about this drive is that I do not like its flip cap. I would prefer a traditional cap. SSK: just make sure that you can put the cap on the non port end when you have the drive inserted, so that you do not lose the cap.

SSK: you also need to revise this product to have a USBC-C version that gets the speeds of the Kingston DataTraveler Max. I would have bought the Kingston, but a) it is way too wide (causes port crowding) and b) it thermally throttles.

text:
The included instruction manual is very defective.

First the manual is physically tiny, with microscopic font that almost requires a magnifying glass to read. There should be a law against too small of fonts like this.

Second, there are absolutely no instructions for how to install the thermal pads. My understanding is that it is critical for proper heat conduction that you use the right thickness pad and put it in the correct spot. I have no official idea how to do this with this card.

My guess is that you stick thermal pad(s) along the inside of the big metal heatsink, as indicated in one of the photos, and that you use a just thick enough pad (or multiple pads) so that when you remove everything you can see an impression from the SSD on the pad (so you know it made good contact). But I should not have to guess this, the manual should thoroughly discuss this and have multiple pictures with examples of different SSDs that required different solutions.

Especially galling is that I went to Sabrent's support website and downloaded their PDF file manual for this card. The PDF is once more microscopic at 100% size for no good reason. Sabrent: this is a digital file, you can make everything really big sized, and have tons of photos and discussion in there.

I also would appreciate if they used screws that were a bit bigger. Theirs are very small, hard to handle, and I wonder how durable they will be if I unscrew and rescrew them many times.

This defect turns out to be mentioned in several Amazon review that I I wish that I had noticed, and is discussed on TP-Link's forums.

title: That is utterly pathetic: I just benchmarked my 6+ year old Western ...
text:
Patriot: I am reaming your drive for one reason: it is supposed to be a premium drive, but it has utterly ABYSMAL small (e.g. 4K) random write speeds.

The benchmark below was done with CrystakDiskMark (all default settings) on your drive as shipped (bizarrely formatted as FAT32). Note the 4K write results of < 0.040 MB/s. Reformatting the drive as exFAT changed most of the results very little, except the sequential write dropped to 143 MB/s for some reason.

That is utterly pathetic: I just benchmarked my 6+ year old Western Digital SATA hard drive, and it gets ~1 MB/s for those same 4K random write speeds. Oh, and that hard drive is fully encrypted with TrueCrypt, which handicaps it even more...

Patriot: update this product NOW. Dump whatever craptastic flash controller you are using, and put in a real SSD controller. A premium drive needs uniform premium performance (as well as the best ECC).

And while you are at it, dump the el cheapo plastic housing and use a quality metal, like aluminum (both for the strength as well as the heat dissipation).

It saddens me to have to rate this drive so low, because it actually has a lot of potential. First, I like its size, which is small enough. Second, the slider mechanism actually seems robust. Normally I hate slider thumb drives because of bad experiences with Sandisk's awful sliders, which have broken multiple times on me. Third, the fact that this drive has OK sequential read and write performance means that you have solved half the performance problem.

I bought this drive on impulse late at night without spending sufficient time scouring reviews. I am adding this very negative review to ward off other potential buyers who also might need a drive that has decent 4K performance.

I so hope that someone comes out with a smallish enough thumb drive that consistently performs like a SSD. The closest drive that I know of is Visiontek's.

title: Real SSD controllers offer things like better reliability (e
text:
This drive meets most of my requirements for a flash drive. There are so few well made flash drives that I gotta rate it as 5 stars simply for filling this niche fairly well.

First and foremost, I need a flash drive with a real SSD controller, not the cheapo craptastic "flash controllers" used by almost every other flash drive. Real SSD controllers offer things like better reliability (e.g. error detection and correction, wear leveling), higher performance (especially for random reads and writes), and secure erase. A real SSD controller should also mean that you can treat the flash drive just like an internal SSD. For example, it should support partitioning, and have software that lets you specify the amount of over provisioning. Maybe it also ought to support the TRIM command and S.M.A.R.T. drive performance and health monitoring?

Second, I need a drive that is physically robust. I want a strong case, with zero moving parts, and ideally it meets some good dust and water resistance standard (e.g. IP68; see trustedreviews's article on "IP67 vs IP68: Waterproof IP ratings explained"). Since the drive must have no moving parts, its connector must be protected by a cap, and to help avoid losing the cap, the drive must let you put the cap on the non-connector end when it is in use.

I am not sure where I stand about encryption. In principle, I support it. In practice, manufacturers always seem to use proprietary solutions, which makes them intrinsically bad; when closely examined by real security professionals, they usually turn out to be rubbish (e.g. Western Digital's line of "My Passport" hard drives ~2015). Furthermore, depending on how it is implemented, you may have issues with the host operating system (e.g. if some custom driver is needed).

So, how does the VisionTek 900903 measure up?

First, it claims to use "a high-performance Silicon Motion controller". Off to a good start. Benchmarks below go into further details, but the conclusion is that it offers decent performance.

Second, this drive is an all metal rectangular case ("tough aircraft-grade aluminum housing" according to the manufacturer). Its case is solid: there are no moving parts except for the cap, and the cap can be put on the rear of the drive when you have it inserted. Good, tho the cap could fit a tad more snugly. There are ridges on the drive that allow an excellent grip, which is a nice touch. Sole defects are the 4 corners of the case which are slightly sharper than they ought to be, and the drive seems to meet no official dust and water resistance spec.

Contrast VisionTek's case with that of a Sandisk Extreme Pro USB 3.0 128 GB (model #: SDCZ88) that I also own. The Sandisk case is only partly metal. The metal came from a sheet that was stamped and then folded. Part of the metal near the connector end, where the slider is, is dangerously sharp--an idiotic design... The metal is way too smooth (is hard to pull the drive out in some situations). The slider mechanism is made of plastic and is weak (I have had 2 drives fail on me).

Concerning performance, attached are 5 CrystalDiskMark screenshots. The first 3 benchmark this VisionTek 900903 under 3 different disk formats (FAT32, exFAT, and NTFS); default format parameters (e.g. Allocation unit size) were consistently used (tweaking might improve performance). For reference, in the other 2 screenshots, I also benchmarked my Sandisk Extreme Pro (SDCZ88) as well as my internal SSD (a Samsung 840 EVO).

The disk format does not make too much of a difference; to my surprise, NTFS came out slightly ahead in most categories (I would have guessed exFAT would be). To be sure, the differences are small enough that maybe this was just measurement noise (did not have time to try multiple runs).

Comparing the VisionTek 900903 to the Samsung 840 EVO, the Samsung is clearly faster in every test, altho the VisionTek's Sequential Read and 4K random Write are respectable for a drive so small. (You should probably ignore the Q32 = queue depth 32 results, as they are not relevant for most desktop users, only servers.)

Comparing the VisionTek 900903 to the Sandisk Extreme Pro, the VisionTek is faster in 3 out of the 4 tests. The Visiontek is much better in Sequential Reads, and blows away the Sandisk in random 4k Writes. (Is that due to it having a real SSD controller?) It only loses moderately in Sequential Writes.

The sole performance disappointment with this drive is its 4k random Reads. That's a sore spot for the Samsung 840 EVO too, indeed, even Samsung's latest and greatest PCIe NVMe 960 Pro has awful 4K random read performance. It must be hard to achieve with current flash technology. The Sequential Write performance of the VisionTek 900903 could also be a bit higher.

All in all, I am pleased with this drive.

Altho I hate its past case designs, SanDisk has just announced at CES its new Extreme Pro USB 3.1 flash drive, which claims to offer "read speeds up to 420MB/s and write speeds up to 380MB/s" (when attached to a USB 3.1 port). Those are surely its Sequential specs; the fact that they do not mention its random specs makes me suspect that they are still bad.

Another case design I dislike is Corsair's way too fat Flash Voyager GTX, as it causes port crowding. A tragedy, since it otherwise is one of the few flash drives that claims to use a real SSD controller.

Speaking of CES, some other announcements for the small storage enthusiast to check out are Longsyss SATA Disk in Package (SDP) and Toshiba's BG Ultra Mobile SSD.

title: I just learned the hard way that I really need a longer drive to easily insert/remove it with this TV
text:
I bought 2 of these, they came today, and I and am returning them both tomorrow.

Chief reason: the drive is so small, that it is hard to plug into either USB port in the back of my new TV, a Sony XBR 850C. That TV has a somewhat constricted space where all of its ports are (USB, HDMI, etc). I just learned the hard way that I really need a longer drive to easily insert/remove it with this TV. Anyone else in a similar situation should likewise give this drive a serious rethink. I note that I had little problem with inserting/removing this drive from the front of my workstation, where I have unrestricted space.

Secondary reason: this drive has poor write speeds. My first transfer was of a single 2 GB movie file--a pure sequential write, which should be optimal--and yet I got an initial speed that started at ~50 MB/s and then it decay to maybe 40 MB/s. I should have paid more careful attention to the write benchmarks of this drive. I really want >= 100 MB/s write speeds.

It looks like my best bet is this drive's bigger brother, the Samsung 32GB USB 3.0 Flash Drive MUF-32BA/AM. Ordering 2 right now, stay tuned...

title: I am returning it solely because some highly intelligent designer at LG choose to put the support feet ...
text:
Went to Target on Thanksgiving evening to buy some groceries, and on an impulse walked out with this TV for $499.

Unfortunately, I am returning it solely because some highly intelligent designer at LG choose to put the support feet so far out that my 35.5 inch wide TV stand cannot safely support it. To be precise: the screw hole center-to-center distance for the support legs is 35 inches (the legs themselves obviously slightly straddle this dimension).

Why LG, why would you choose to eliminate about 50% of your potential customers with such a design decision?

I could have lived with all the other flaws on this unit (back connectors are awful if you want to wall mount, refresh rate is 60 not 120 Hz, etc).

Congratulations: you just made me buy a Samsung.

title: Company now does offer support
text:
UPDATE #2:

I am updating my review to 3 stars to reflect the satisfactory customer service that I finally got from Visiontek. My UPDATE #1 got the attention of the right person at Visiontek, Rick Givens. He reached out to me, and to make a long story short, has resolved my issues in a way satisfactory to me. If anyone reading this is having customer support issues with Visiontek, then make sure to contact Rick directly.

UPDATE #1:

I am changing my rating from 4 stars to 1 star. DO NOT BUY THIS DRIVE (or anything else from VisionTek).

Reason: several weeks ago, my drive simply stopped working at USB 3.0 speeds when plugged into USB 3.0 ports. I spent a couple of hours on the phone with Dell's professional support seeing if my Dell T1700 was the cause: no dice. Indeed, I eventually got my hands on another USB 3.0 device (an external hard drive), and verified that my USB 3.0 ports work at high speed. So the problem must be with this flash drive.

Even worse, after I emailed VisionTek, it took days before I got a response. They wanted to know how I was doing the benchmarking. This was stupid: my original email gave them enough details to know that the USB 2.0 speeds I was seeing could not be due to benchmarking flaws. Nevertheless, I gave them another detailed answer. I never heard back. I warned them 8 days ago that I was going to ream them on Amazon if they did not start offering me proper support. They never responded. Hence this review downgrade.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:

I ordered this drive a couple of months ago, and have been using it steady ever since.

I wanted a thumb drive that is really an SSD. In particular, that uses a proper controller, as opposed to the crap el cheapo controllers in almost all thumb drives. This VisionTek drive is one of the very few that fits the bill. I bought it instead of Corsair's because it is slightly physically smaller. The review that best informed my judgement was this one:
[...]

Overall, I am pleased with this drive.

It has been, and remains, reasonably fast for an SSD drive in this form factor. For example, using the freeware benchmarking program AS SSD just now, I measured:

sequential read speed = 156.91 MB/s
sequential writes as 101.43 MB/s
4k random read = 16.74 MB/s
4k random write= 63.26 MB/s
4k-64 thread random read = 16.76 MB/s
4k-64 thread random write= 72.84 MB/s
read access time = 0.155 ms
write access time = 0.347 ms

(The above was measured in the drive's first partition, which is a 8 GB FAT32 partition that I have strictly for backwards compatibility with certain software or operating systems that require it, such as GParted or Clonezilla live images. I do most of my storage in the second partition, which is all the remaining space formatted in NTFS with 4K block size.)

My device gets warm, but NOT HOT (where I define the start of hot as when it becomes uncomfortable to touch).

I love the fact that it has a cap, and that the cap can be put on the back when plugged in. My previous thumb drive was a Sandisk Extreme Pro slider which eventually broke; never want a slider again.

I have 3 moderate complaints that prevent me from rating it at 5 stars. First, it is bigger than I would like. Sure, it is still small enough that you can still carry it around in your pocket, and I do, all day long, but I would like it to be smaller if possible. Second, the case, while made of high quality metal, has some edges and corners that are sharper than they out to be. Third, the paint has started to chip in places (like those sharp points).

Overall, this is the best thumb drive currently shipping that I am aware of, but it could be improved. VisionTek: I hope that you are reading this review.

Because some idiotic engineer (or evil MBA swine?) at Panasonic decided that it would be a good idea to use a proprietary USB cable connector. Why oh why did you do this, Panasonic, when there is a perfectly capable industry standard micro USB cable connector format?

I got burned badly by this on a recent vacation, when I temporarily lost my camera box, and could not use my wife's Samsung Galaxy S3's USB cable to connect to my camera. That Samsung smart phone uses bog standard micro USB. If Sammy can use those, why can't you, Panny?

title: misleading on features
text:
I've ordered laptops through Amazon before, and haven't been disappointed until now. I specifically looked for what I wanted, which included RAM size, a certain processor, screen size, touchscreen, and a backlit keyboard. This laptop clearly states that it has a backlit keyboard in the title. I read the reviews and one of them noted that they had to turn on the lights, but one (and only one) that they didn't receive a backlit keyboard.
Well, the laptop arrived today (a day early), in a torn outer box. The inner box was fine, though, and so far the laptop seems all right (so no sending it back for a refund as a 'dead' purchase). However, as you can see, the F5 key is missing markings to indicate that it possesses a backlit keyboard. Checking the control panel, there's no option for brightness under the keyboard setting. As I do a lot of typing, a backlit keyboard is very important to me.
I'm rather upset since I could have gone w/ lots of other options if I hadn't specifically chosen a laptop with a backlit keyboard. If it's one of your requirements for a laptop, don't take a gamble on this one/this seller.
