Installation is easy, and it does a really good job of keeping people from seeing your monitor unless they're right in front of it.

title: good wireless mouse
text: This is a good wireless mouse which 'plugs' in quickly and you can take on the go. It comes with a battery, so you just have to connect it properly, put in the USB tab into your computer and it registers quickly. It's comfortable in the hand and it goes to 'sleep' if you don't use it after a set time, so you'll have to move it around if you leave your computer for a long break, but that helps to conserve the battery. All in all, this is really nice if you want to take it on the go or if you move your laptop around. You can also turn off the mouse and put the USB tab in it for safe keeping.

title: quality monitor
text: I purchased an Asus monitor since they're a brand known for quality, and so far I'm happy. It was easy to set up (came with a stand you screw onto the monitor) and an HDMI cable (which is my only complaint, really - the reviews said that it didn't, that it came with a VGA cable, which is what my work laptop supports, so I had to scramble to find one). Since I have headaches, I wanted a monitor which is easy on the eyes, and this fits the bill. The picture is clear and crisp, and not a problem to adjust to one's preference. Perfect monitor for work from home, not too big but better than a laptop screen.

title: works well
text: I'm using this screen protector for its anti-glare properties, but it does also provide some privacy as well - it helps to 'blur' what's on my monitor from a few feet away or if you're looking at it from another angle. I like that the kit provides two different ways for you to attach it to your monitor, the usual plastic tabs which you can use to slide the screen off and on (with four long ones and several smaller ones), and then sticky tabs where you can directly apply it to the screen (if you're not going to be removing it all the time).  Just be certain to measure your screen properly so you buy the right size.

title: keeps my HP at its current charge
text: Somehow, the power cord for my HP G3 vanished. Since I know IT can be a bit slow on ordering things, I got this power cord to hold me over until a new one arrived, based on the reviews. I will say that it works - there's no error messages from my laptop, no issues. However, it seems to say 'not charging' when it shows it being plugged in, and it holds the laptop at a steady charge while I'm using it. So it's not perfect, but as long as my pc is charged/has some charge when I use this cord and it doesn't cause any problems, I'm happy.

title: fast and portable
text: I feel bad that I can't write some of the impressive technical reviews like others here, but here's my take as someone who uses tech (laptops, tablets and smart phones) but isn't 'techie'. This Sabrent Rocket Nano 1TB external SSD is a step above the usual USB or external devices I use to backup or 'transport' data. It's small, just a bit bigger than other USB drives, has a nice aluminum casing and comes in an aluminum box which holds it and the two cables included to connect to your device (I've used it on phone, tablet and pc - not Mac). It's fast, really fast. I don't think it's reached the 1000MBs, but close and I'm not complaining (usually it depends on file size). I haven't noticed heat issues, but then I don't think I've had it plugged in more than an hour. Easy to use and tuck away in a bag.

title: gonna last a while
text: I received a three pack of these to cover the camera for devices, so they're gonna last a while. I mean, between personal and work devices (laptops and tablets), it's easy to go through them, and they are a lot better than using tape (can slide them open and close at will). These adhere well (just press and hold for a few seconds) and they stay closed, and don't affect the laptops closing.

title: perfect
text: Got this because got tired of trying to play music loud for others through my phone - an external speaker was needed. This is easy to carry around (especially with the case), easy to pair to my phone with the Bluetooth feature, has really good sound quality, and you can use the speaker itself for volume or pause/play/forward or your phone (I find it easier to adjust sound on my phone) or whatever device the speaker is paired to. Price was really good, too.

title: great for behind furniture
text: We needed an extension cord to reach a plug behind a bookcase, so this works out great - it is more 'flush' against the wall and allows multiple items to be plugged in, along with some electronic devices, and a little surge protection (not an awful lot, but a little). And it looks nice.

title: added functionality
text: This is really handy if you need extra USB ports (2) or card slots for your pc or tablet (Windows 7 or higher, various Macs), and a means to charge devices. Just plug in (there's a short cord or you can plug in directly) and good to go. We tried it with a couple of different devices and it worked well.

title: sturdy and quick
text: This is a braided USB type-C to type-A 3.1 cable, which means it charges nice and quick to type-C devices. It's a foot long, so it offers a little bit of length when I'm charging or connecting my phone to my laptop or tablet, enough to move it around but not lose track of it, or connect my phone to my car if I don't want to bluetooth it. The braided cable gives it more strength/durability than most cords, and Amazon Basic has proven to be a quality brand for the price.

title: all right bluetooth headphones for the price
text:
These are a decent set of 'noise cancelling' headphones for the price with bluetooth capabilities. The on-ear headphones are rather small (part of the lower rating) - my husband found them a little uncomfortable for that reason, and if you're moving around they jostle and shift, which means they're not a good fit. I'm smaller and noticed that they didn't give the best coverage, so yes, the size is a problem.

As for the 'noise cancelling' quality - there's a button/switch which produces a low, crackling 'white noise' which helps offset any sound. It's not the best. It does help cancel outside noise, but again, smaller headphones/not total muffling means you still hear some noise. I've other headphones that are larger and more insulating that do just as good a job of not better (but then they also cost more).

You can hook these up directly to a device with the cord or use the bluetooth option. Not too difficult to set up and the range is good. So is the battery life (well over half a day). I'd say these probably will work well for a kid or teen, maybe not too many adults but I could be wrong. You get what you pay for in the end.

title: helps to pick up the local channels
text:
We cut the cable habit when we moved to the new house - netflix and youtube was more than enough before then, so why not? But it's nice to be able to check the local channels for news and weather at times, so we decided to try one of these tv antennas.

The GE 40529 one works well, with one or two things given. It won't work on just anything, you do need a newer tv, one with HD/digital. It also took a while to figure out the right input to get this to work. Once we went through a good bit of trial and error on that part with our Sony digital tv and got the auto program to search for channels, we found about twenty. That honestly was what took the longest time - physical set-up wasn't too hard and we get a decent signal (we're not that far outside of the city proper). The signal lights are a nice blue that stand out to let you know the best place to put it.

title: lightweight and useful pc
text:
The laptop arrived in a cardboard box that was a bit mangled, but the LG box is designed to protect the laptop. There's also plastic covers on the brushed metal casing. Set-up is easy as you plug it in and power it on, and the MS assistant 'talks' you through things, allowing you to use voice or keyboard control. It's Windows 10 on the laptop, but no MicroSoft Suite (you have to pay extra for that).
With a SSD and 8 RAM memory, everything is very fast and responsive - I can have multiple tabs open on my internet browser, be playing music and have an app or Windows up and nothing is slow at all. It wakes up out of sleep mode quickly, too, and there's a fingerprint sensor for log-in or I can use a pin or 'drawing picture' function (there's lots of security options available).
Music/sound - the speakers are on the back/around the hinge, so if you're on a flat surface, the sound is good (it's not a high quality 'music/entertainment' laptop). But if it's on your lap, it may be muffled a little, fair warning.
Image/screen - it has good resolution and images are clear/crisp, but due to the fact that it's so lightweight, it's not a glass surface and has a little 'give'. When touching it, it leaves a faint 'trail' behind, but that does fade away quickly.
Keyboard - keyboard has some nice 'give' to it and I had to use Fn+F8 to make the backlight work. It didn't light up automatically, but you can turn it on/off and adjust the brightness.
There's three USB ports, an HDMI port, one for headphones and a micro SD card and others, split between both sides. That's a nice amount for a new laptop.
This is indeed a lightweight computer. It's lighter than my older generation Surface. The touchpad is responsive and the battery does have a good charge (at least for now), depending on what you're using (how many apps, backlight, etc.). All in all, this is a great laptop for work, writing, some entertainment and anything you would need to take on the go due to its light weight and thinness.

title: fancy earbuds
text: These are rather pricey for what they do, which is cord free earphones/buds. The case which holds and charges them (with a USB cord) is rather nice and handy, and lights up (red or green) to let you know when they're charged. They also charge relatively fast, which is good, and have various molds to help ensure a good fit. But yes, you'll be charging these a lot if you use these daily or often, be forewarned. Also, the controls are a little tricky to figure out and you might fumble with them a bit, considering you're pressing the things, basically, no nice cord with clear buttons. The sound quality is decent, not quite what I'd expect for the price, since part of the price is for the cordless nature of these things (that and the internal storage and the google speak and...). So yes, they've got a lot of nice options to them which make them more than just earbuds.

title: perfect for taking files on the go
text: This is a small (about the size of a palm), stable (SSD!), fast (relatively speaking), dependable portable hard drive/back-up for your devices (laptops, computers, tablets). It has two cables that should work with your Apple, Windows or Android devices, and you can lock it down with a password if so inclined. I love having portable back-up on hand because you can take it with you and access it wherever. With SSD there's less concern to carry these around (not saying to just drop kick the thing, but less moving parts) and it's easy to figure out how to use. Each year they're getting faster and faster, too. It doesn't take long to back up (though documents go faster than video files).

title: lightweight and decent sound quality
text: These are very nice looking earphones with denim and fabric accents (denim on the band, fabric wrapped cord), recycled aluminum and even some 'wood'. All in all, very nice. They are lightweight as well and they fit comfortably - then again, I'm on the small side. The sound is good, nothing spectacular but consider the price range. The music I'm playing comes in nice and clear so I'm happy. You have a microphone feature with them to take calls, but being able to pause music or adjust volume would be nice as well.

title: easy to set up, lot of features
text:
We replaced an older router with this one to take advantage of better speeds and slightly better coverage. This router has 3 antennas and the signal seems to be a little stronger in the furthest rooms than with our old router.

Physically the router is about 30% bigger than the average home routers we’ve owned, but it does have 3 antennas and a touch screen that's about the size of a smaller iPhone screen. It also has holes in the back for wall mounting.

We don’t use a lot of the advanced features that this router offers, such as mode-switching to a repeater, or the parental controls (it's not like the cats are going to surf the net... at least as far as we know), but it's there if you want it. The touch-screen did make it super-easy to setup. There's no need to connect a laptop to it, everything can be setup right on the screen which is nice.

Overall our usage of a router is pretty basic. Just set in and forget it, and so far it's been reliable considering the amount of gaming and streaming we do.

title: pretty good monitor for the price
text:
This review is one of those times I really wish we could leave a partial star review - the View Sonic MHD 22" monitor is not QUITE a five star, but it's pretty good. The quality is a slight bit lacking compared to the higher end HD monitors... but you're not paying the higher price so there's some give and take. The image is nice and crisp, but the color (at least on the one I received) is a little washed out. Also, the manual controls/buttons are on the back of the monitor which can make for some awkward adjusting depending on how you set up the monitor. Those are the reasons for the lack of a five star rating.
That said,you get a nice, light screen that comes very well packed, and with an HDMI cable included in the box (looked all over on the page and didn't see anything about cables included, and know that not all equipment comes with cables these days). Set up is easy, and it has selectable presets for games, movies, etc, that have predefined settings to optimize for those activities. It holds up well to gaming and is a step up from using the laptop screen.

title: really great tablet, just a minor design flaw
text:
Let me state that again, wish there were half stars because this is more like a 4.5 review than a four, but it's not quite a five. The Sony Z4 is a really nice tablet - it's very slim, has a sharp screen with great resolution, is mostly intuitive (could figure out most things with it pretty easily) and yes, it's great for playing videos and media. It IS an Android-based tablet, so when surfing the net (Chrome browser is supplied), some sites might not load as you'd like because they are loading based for Android and might lack some other OS features you're used to on other tablets or laptops. But you can have multiple tabs opened without much lag or issues. And again, it handles the videos really well, and takes decent pictures.
The issue I do have with this? The power button is not recessed but a nice shiny silver button that sticks out on the side so when you're holding this, you (if you're anything like me and the boyfriend) might tend to hit it accidentally SEVERAL times while using the tablet. Yes, it sticks out that much. Yes, it's that sensitive. Fortunately the tablet powers up very quickly, but again, to me it's a design flaw. Not sure if a cover will fix it or not.
BUT, the tablet did come with a free keyboard, which is really nice if you want to use it for any long-term typing (or hate typing on the screen). That was an unexpected bonus. As well is being able to expand the memory and a pretty good battery life.
Now, obviously I'm not going to try the water resistance aspect of this table (not unless offered a free one should it fail), but this is a very nice, sealed tablet so I think it should be good on the dust and water side. Don't quote me, but yes, it's thin and doesn't seem to have too many obvious cracks and such. It looks well made, acts well made and over all is really good. Just have to get used to that annoying power button sticking out on the side.

title: really nice laptop at a good price
text:
This is a great gaming laptop. The keyboard is very responsive, the visuals are great for the price (yes, some fuzz around the very edges) and over all it's fast. It starts up fast and is responsive once booted up. I don't have an issue with the track pad being a bit to the left because have dealt with another laptop set up the same way, have just gotten used to it, I guess, as well as over-responsive, twitchy track pads (and search out apps that help correct it, like TrackFreeze). Love that there are lots of ports for USB and the such, and that I can expand the memory since with 256 gig it is a little lacking, but it being solid state I won't complain (initially).
All in all, it's a nice laptop with just minor quirks at a decent price that you can easily customize. For a gamer, it's a great price.

title: would be a much better radio with bluetooth
text:
The thing about Bose products is you get great sound from them, and the Wave Radio IV is no exception. Stations come in crystal clear, and you have presets to program your favorite stations (six each for FM and AM - would be nice to be able to program 12 over all since not sure there are six AM stations I want to preset...). Most of the functionality is done through the remote, which is good because the radio itself does take up a lot of space for a nightstand. There's an alarm function to the radio as well, allowing you to set more than one wake-up time on the radio as well as a snooze. So you have a quality radio with excellent sound and an alarm clock all in one.
Why isn't this a five star review? Because there is no bluetooth capability with this radio - not without spending a good bit of money ([[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]]). I know you're paying in part for the Bose sound, but it's rather ridiculous to not have bluetooth capability included for this price.There is an auxiliary input for other mp3 devices so you're not stuck with just using the airwaves, but then you need to use the mp3 player, device or phone to control the music.

title: screen works well, tabs could be better
text:
The Belkin TrueClear Privacy Screen Protector for Touch-Screen is a decent privacy screen if you're concerned about people viewing what's on the screen of your laptop or pc. Considering that I travel sometimes with my laptop, this is a concern - I hate the feeling that people are looking at my 'business', let alone the risks involved with them seeing personal information.
The Belkin TrueClear Privacy Screen works much like other screens, in that once you apply it, it darkens your screen slightly and anyone looking at your screen from an angle can't see what is displayed (if they're directly behind you, they still can see it from some distance, however). It even works on touchscreens, which is an important feature these days.
However, I don't like the little tabs that they included with the kit to install (along with a folder for when you remove the screen, and a microfiber cloth to help clean your screen before install - which is a must). Previous privacy screens have installed with 'plastic tabs' that you attach onto the pc itself, allowing you to easily slide the screen off and on, which I must admit that I prefer to these tabs (seems to allow for easier - and constant - removal, sizing and a closer fit).
Very nice screen, just wish it had better tabs.

title: great wireless keyboard/mouse combo for on the go
text:
The Logitech Wireless Combo MK345 with Full-Size Keyboard and Right-Handed Mouse arrives with batteries included and is easy to set up - you just install the small USB tab in your PC or laptop and it's quick to set up.
There's some complaints about the size of the mouse - it's on the smaller size, but neither I nor my boyfriend had any issues with using it. It and the keyboard is was very responsive - the keys on the keyboard were solid and had a nice amount of pressure behind them, and they're quick and no lag with the laptop we used to test it. We even used the keyboard with an online game and it kept up with the commands. The keyboard itself is light, so perfect for carrying around and traveling. The description does note that it's just the KEYBOARD that's full size.

title: pretty good but expensive wireless headset
text:
The Klipsch KG-300 Pro Audio Wireless Gaming Headset is a very nice headset and easy to install - right out of the box you can plug in the base via USB (batteries included in the headset) and start using them. The audio is pretty good for a gaming headset, with the sounds of the game coming through clear, and people on the other end can easily hear what is being said. The headset is mostly comfortable - they're not the lightest and a bit bulky/padded, but they fit well.
Now, for the price of this headset, one thing that did surprise me is how much background noise DID come through. While it is true that they don't claim to be noise cancelling, considering the price and the padding, I didn't expect to be picking up so much background noise while wearing them. Definitely won't have to worry about anyone sneaking up on you while wearing these.

title: great anti-glare/screen protectors
text:
These are great screen protectors that also cut down on the glare. If you've ever used screen protectors in the past for phones or other tablets, you know the process already - clean the screen as much as possible, do it in an environment that's 'dust free' (well, don't do it in a place that's too windy), peel off the backing and don't touch the sticky surface, smooth it out as you press down and you're basically good to go. If you're new to the process, just take some time when putting them on and you'll be good.
These screens do make a lot of difference, they help in bright lights and to keep the fingerprints from dulling your screen. Definitely recommend to enhance your reading/viewing experience.

title: very basic cover, but decent
text:
This is a very basic cover for your Kindle Fire HD (4th generation) that will offer some protection if you're going to carry it about - the price isn't too bad, but there are better, more functional covers out there (of course, you'll pay more for them, so it's a give and take).
First, though I was offered a red cover, a black one arrived. That was a bit perplexing and made me double-check what I clicked on. Nope, order said red. All right. Second, when you slide the Kindle Fire into the cover, it's basically held into place by a tab/molded frame on one end and elastic tabs on the other. You don't slide it in completely like with some cases, or snap it all in with others so it's completely secure. Second, there's no 'sleep' mode with this case, so you have to make sure you power it off or on when you close the case or else you'll drain your battery (as I said, very basic). Also, it only has an easel/landscape viewing mode - you flip the case open and stand it up that way to read or view the Kindle, there's no tab or folding capabilities with the back flap, no stand other than the cover flipping back.
You close the Kindle and 'seal' it with an elastic band. That's not uncommon with a lot of covers. The case is nice and slim, which means that you can fit it easily in a purse or a bag, which is nice. The case has a 'leather' look to it, and has the necessary holes cut out so you can access power, sound, etc. It's not a bad case, it's just if you are going to be traveling a lot with your Kindle and do want to use it to for apps or movies, or to set it down to read, I'd spend a little more money for an origami case or something with a little more features.

title: Decent case, not much options
text:
This is a nice, average case for your Kindle Fire HDX 7" device. One of its advantages is it's lightweight and slim, so if you're looking for a case that won't add weight or bulk to your kindle, this is a good one to buy. It's also 'stiff', the bottom part being reinforced plastic, so it gives some support and protection (not much, but a little, it's not thick or too strong). You have holes for the sound and cut-outs for the power button and the sound buttons, and you snap the kindle into the case. The 'lid' folds over to protect the kindle in transport when it's closed, and an elastic keeps it in place (no magnets or anything, which would be an improvement or what I'd expect for the price, to be honest). You fold the cover back and bend it to put it in a horizontal position for viewing or use - it's a very thin crease to do this, so it's not the strongest 'catch' to hold it in position. Obviously it's not meant to stand in a vertical position.

So you have a very thin, lightweight case in a nice shade of blue (neutral color) that holds/supports the kindle well and makes it easy to transport it, it just doesn't give it much options to display it. Considering the price, you might want to look at other options....

title: Some issues, but not too bad of a cover
text:
I find it interesting that the title description says 'shock protection' yet the description says 'scratch protection'. I think this is more of the latter - what this provides is a thin layer of silicon that does stretch to cover my Asus 15.6" laptop computer (barely - it took a bit of tugging to get it to fit and it bubbles a little in the corners at the bottom and the inside top corners are peeling back a little). The last thing I'm going to do is test it by dropping or bumping it around, it's not THAT thick. But yes, it should provide adequate protection from scratches and, if it does drop off the coffee table or if it gets hit in passing, should help protect the corners from damage.

A couple of mild dislikes - the bottom right fold that holds the cover in place is over the light display that shows wifi, charging, lock, and other status symbols. Slight annoyance there. Also, the bottom part of the cover is very nubbly, probably for traction. Not the nicest sensation against a lap (if you don't have a chillpad or something). There are 'blocks' on the back of the cover and a couple on the very front of the sides so you can cut out (or so I assume) if you need access to USB ports or cables, which is not the case for my Asus, but can see how that would be an annoyance for some people.

If you need to protect your laptop from scratches, you might want to consider this. Just be aware you might have to work with the cover a bit to get a good fit.

title: Good every day ultrabook
text:
The Asus has a sleek look with its silver brushed metal lid and slightly rounded sides. Between this and it being JUST under 5 lbs, it makes for an easy transport if you want a laptop to carry around.

I noticed immediately the ultra-fast sleep mode. As soon as the lid is closed the laptop goes into immediate hibernation. After opening lid and clicking to un-hibernate, the laptop is back to active within 2-3 seconds.

The touchscreen has a sleek design with a black outline around the active screen that frames the look of the screen nicely. If you put pressure on the top of the laptop lid it does not affect the screen at all which tells of the durability of the laptop casing. The touchscreen has very nice vibrant display graphics that allows it to be seen easily from various angles without too much glare.

The visuals of the screen are great, which make for impressive video viewing. Picture is great and graphics are very crisp whether it is a Powerpoint still picture on display or a movie. The audio is great, too. While not a gaming pc, this is a nice one for video/audio usage.

It is a very thin and elegant design. The DVD multi recorder fits nicely along the side panels along with three USB ports, a microphone jack, SD slot, network slot and HDMI port.

The grooved out design around the touch pad is a small detail that has a nice impact on the overall look of the keyboard and touchpad (the touchpad is a bit of a different design with the 'clicks', but honestly, at this point with various keyboards for various devices, I'm used to things being different and just roll with it. But FYI to buyer). Keyboard is nicely laid out with light/'chiclet' touch keys and touchpad is sensitive without being too touchy. Considering that I also have a Asus Ultrabook S500-CA with a twitchy as heck touchpad OOB, this is a welcome relief.

Battery life appears to be great as well. I had the machine in hibernate for approx. 6 hours after machine was fully charged and the battery was not even down past ½ charge after all that time. And while in use, it does last about 6 hours. Considering the size and weight, that's pretty good.

Now for some negatives (or at least not so greats).
Fan vent is on the bottom which can be seen as a negative to anyone that works with the laptop sitting on their lap. I would imagine that the fan would be blocked in this instance and would not function properly and possibly allow machine to overheat? Gonna need a cooler for this one while using it for any length of time.

No SSD at all?

It barely comes in under 5lbs. As stated, I also have a ASUS Ultrabook S500CA, which is a 15" screen and weighs less. It also doesn't have a DVD drive, so.... You're definitely adding weight here for that and a few other options (and losing USB and other ports).

No full Microsoft Office Suite/software (you'll have to pay to get more than a trial version or use something else). Just making that clear. - edited as before I had stated 'Windows'. Sorry for any confusion.

All in all, this is a responsive laptop with impressive visual and audio that can be useful to an everyday user. It probably has some drawbacks to someone needing serious processing (no SSD), but for a lot of users, this one is good. I like ASUS, I find them to be reliable laptops, their designs tend to be good, and this ultrabook is no exception.

For everyday use, I'd give this 4.5 -5 stars. Anything else, take off a star or two.

title: Decent protection, okay application
text:
I didn't have that much of a problem applying the screen protector to my kindle HDX, but I'll admit that I've had previous (and recent) experience applying screens to my smart phones (and watching the videos that were suggested for one of those brands). That probably helps, having previous experience. If you're a newbie at the application process, you may be a bit frustrated at the 'IKEA' type of instructions included with these screens.

First, you want to be in as clean of an environment as possible to apply it. I've been told in the past it helps to be in the bathroom, but really, just wipe the area down around you, don't kick up any dust and hope for the best. Once you peel off the first protective layer of the screen, if dust is floating around, it'll stick to it. So be in a clean, dust-free environment, clean your hands, clean your screen (you may want to wipe it down and dry it), and have everything ready BEFORE you peel off the protective layer.

If you have any type of wrap or decal on your HDX, you're gonna have to remove it before putting on the screen. :-(

There will be bubbles when you put on the screen. I didn't have too much trouble repositioning the screen or smoothing them out after removing the second protective layer. So far, so good with the screen, but it doesn't seem the stickiest, so not sure that I'll be able to put a decal wrap back on the HDX w/out peeling the screen back off by any attempt to reposition it.

The nice thing is, there are two screens included in the kit - I know in the past it's taken me two tries to learn how to apply a screen. This kit wasn't too difficult to use and so far, don't impact the use of the kindle or muck up too quickly with fingerprints.

title: wonderful portable tablet
text:
Okay, I have officially bought into Amazon's kindle crack. This is not my first kindle (or second, or...). This tablet is definitely an improvement over the previous versions, it's more responsive, it handles video and web browsing so much better than the previous Fire generation, and I love the slimmed down version.

The overall design is an improvement. The video quality is great, and music does play with a decent quality. Love the feature where it can display lyrics while playing song (if the mp3 has the information), thanks to the whole X-Ray/Lyrics feature. There's a lot of new touches here that are fun. I really appreciate the volume and the power buttons being on the opposite sides of the kindle now (don't know how many times I've hit the wrong one on my Fire >.<).

Also, being able to have more than two browsers open on Silk now w/out it crashing all of the time is a great improvement.

Some minor quirks - not sure if it's me or the tablet, but still trying to figure out how to get pictures already taken from my phone onto the tablet and directly into the photo folder.

Have installed several apps without a problem, downloaded files and opened them, so far so good. The kindle goes everywhere with me (literally, it's the perfect size to fit in my purse). I wish there were more cover options for the 7", but it seems to be increasing the longer the kindle is out, and I think a cover/case is a must for one of these. This is the kindle that I do take everywhere, and on a recent trip, I used this more than my Surface as it has my most frequently used personal emails installed on it (easy to set up), I can access my social accounts, my music, and of course my books.

The battery is... eh, decent. I can keep it on and play music for a few hours, video less, and use it to read books for most of a day. It could use some improvement.

All in all, it's a great tablet that you can take with you.

title: Fancy cover, few drawbacks
text:
They seem to have put a lot of effort into this case to make it as 'fancy' as possible - it's not just a 'put the kindle in the elastic tabs and close the flap' type, that's certain. When I opened the package, I had to check the description a few times to assure myself that it was leather, as it's rather hard to the touch (I'm sure it makes it nice and durable, and it helps with both protection and standing up the kindle). What I like about the case is that it's rather slim, keeping your kindle protected without adding a lot of bulk to it (good while traveling), and that there are real buttons where the on/off and volumn buttons are on the kindle hd (so it offers some more protection there). Your kindle 'snaps' into the case and it's not too difficult to put it in and out.

As for the origami folding, it was pretty easy to get it to go into landscape mode. At first I thought that was ALL it could do. It wasn't easy to get it to stand portrait-style, and I'm not convinced that it's very stable this way, to be honest. I still have to play with my cover to get it to 'fold' right for portrait and it doesn't seem to fold as neatly, but maybe that's a personal issue. Also, this works best on flat, stable surfaces.

It tells you on the directions that you're going to have to slide the kindle hd out in order to take a picture. So if you're planning on using the camera a lot, that might get very annoying.

All in all, it's a sturdy cover with magnetic closure that will put your kindle hd into sleep mode but won't add too much bulk and seems to offer decent protection, and does offer some display capability (ymmv). Because it's not as thick, I don't have as much problem folding it back to hold it and read, but there is the odd texture because of the folds (so another thing to consider). I like this cover - it's not perfect, but I think it's pretty good. But there are some quirks that people should probably consider in light of its price.

title: Sturdy covers, good protection
text: Belkin does nice, 'book'-covers. They offer nice protection for Kindles, though the downside (and a possible loss of a star) is that this one really makes the Kindle viewable more in a landscape mode more than anything. It does secure the Kindle well thanks to the way it snaps in, and it's handy if you use it for typing or playing this way, and especially for viewing any video or online content.

title: It's good for a basic case
text:
I was torn between the three and four stars, I'll admit. This case DOES get the job done, which is to be a slim case that helps the Kindle Fire HDX 7" fit well in my purse so I can carry it around and use it at work, etc., protect it and prop it up. I love the color choices and that it doesn't add bulk. The magnetic cover is okay, could be a little stronger but it does manage to stay close. The fit COULD be better, I find that I have to keep sliding it back up to help align up the power button or to make sure the power cord is fully seated in the Kindle. And you better plan on just using the screen if you want to play with the sound setting.

You will have to set/stand the Kindle in landscape mode, there is no portrait stand with this case. For the most part, that's fine if you're listening to music, watching videos or typing/reading, but if you need a game or a screen that is only portrait mode, you're going to want another case fast. Hence the debate on three or four stars. However, for the price, the fact that this is lightweight/slim and that it does a decent job for its limitations, I think it's a decent case. Just don't go buying it thinking it'll do everything or that it'll free up all of the buttons.

title: slim case, doesn't slide out yet protects
text: There doesn't seem to be too many cases out there for the Kindle 7" HDX yet, and I mainly wanted something to keep it safe while carrying it back and forth. This sleeve definitely does just that - I was confused at first when I heard about the opening and didn't understand about how it didn't close, but after it arrived, I realized that you're supposed to slide the Kindle inside and that it doesn't slide out. The first time or two it was difficult to get the Kindle HDX inside, but it goes in a bit easier now and it doesn't slide out until I remove it. This case is slim and does a great job of protecting the Kindle while I carry it about in my purse without taking up too much space.

title: small, fast HD
text:
This is one of the smaller external HD's that I've received lately, and while the size and weight is nice for a portable HD, it does feel a little on the flimsy side (not as thick plastic) which would make me more concerned while carrying it around than with other HD's. That said, it looks nice, and more importantly, it works well. I'd just tuck it inside of something better than the little cloth bag they so kindly included with the drive. There's a small bluish/white light on the side that lets you know when it's linked, transferring and safe to disconnect.

It supports USB 3.0 connectivity, and is very fast in transferring files on my pc. There's very nice, detailed information on setting up the back-up functionality on the drive as well as any files you need (maybe too much - if you're just going to use the drive as a regular portable HD, then I'd delete the folders/programs to clear up space - or clean up after you get what you need off of it after setting up as a backup). I was a bit surprised to see that they send you to Dropbox for the cloud backup, considering that there's an associated cost for large file size storage (kickback much?).

So basically it's a small, lightweight drive that is very fast (if you've the right connection) and a decent price if you want to use it as a backup drive. It helps you back up to the cloud, but you'll be paying for your own storage.

title: pretty good laptop for the price, a few quirks
text:
I'm not the most tech-abled person out there, but I think I can manage to get by - I work with computers all day, I've owned several laptops over the years, bought into the Kindle crack (several different versions) and have a tablet. So I'm used to different types of tech and have been using Windows 8 for a couple of months (albeit on a Surface Pro). Seemed logical to give a touchscreen laptop a try, and Asus has a pretty good reputation.

The Asus Ultrabook S500-CA had some decent reviews, and the main draw (other than being pretty big for an ultrabook with not the greatest battery life) was that the touchpad is 'quirky'. Other people have commented on this, and yes, I HAVE to agree. I adore touchpads. I rarely use a mouse w/ a laptop because it's in my lap most of the time (yes, bad ergo). This pc might break me of the habit unless I get the touchpad reset properly. I can't tell you how many times my screen has zoomed out because of this touchpad. But it should be fixable (there's comments below on resetting). It's just annoying as all heck.

I also find that sometimes the touchscreen isn't very responsive. I don't know if it's the site I'm on, my browser (it seems to freeze up on the net most of the time) or what. Sometimes it won't let me close apps or is a pain to do it. Sometimes it doesn't let me scroll. I don't seem to have this problem w/ my Surface. But I'd say it works 95% of the time (I have to admit that I have a different web browser on the Surface).

Speaking of my apps, it's a pain how some of them pop up all the time when I don't want them to, and I have to spend a few minutes getting them to close (see screen).

These have been the most annoying issues w/ the laptop so far. Well, that and figuring out the keyboard. Having the number keys on the side causes the keys to be a little offset, and it took a few days to get used to it. But that's something that you can get used to (or I did). Other than that, it's figuring out where one of the two deletes are that's bugging me the most. Not the most intuitive changes there.

But the laptop is nice and light for its size. Screen graphics are pretty good (it's not the greatest for gaming, but for everyday use and video viewing, it's nice) as is sound. Speed has been decent. I'm still trying to figure out the why's of the HD partitioning, but maybe that's just me.

Quirks aside, it's a light, sleek pc that works well, is responsive (maybe too responsive) for the most part and is meeting my every day needs. The longer I use it and figure it out, the less quirks there are. I like the pc, I just wish it had a better OS on it. And a less sensitive touchpad.

title: great sound quality, works good for Apple products
text:
I've tried a couple of high quality headphones and earphones lately, and have to say that these are probably the best. The sound quality is exceptional, for pc, iPhone and mp3 player listening, providing clarity and definition of both bass and tremble. It was easy to pick up elements to the song that other - lesser quality - earphones left out, and the Munitio earphones were comfortable to use (in part thanks to the three different sizes of earbuds that they provide to ensure the best fit).

The microphone and the control buttons work well with any Apple products, which is nice (one day it'll be great to come across a universal product), and the design is appealing with the thick, flat cord (which isn't entirely tangle-free but less likely to knot up like some other earphones I've come across, especially those which are fabric wrapped) and the bronze accents. Munitio provides a nice, flat bag to carry your earphones in which can be easily tucked into a pocket or bag.

There are probably higher end earphones that provide just as good if not better listening quality, but for the price, I'd have to recommend these.

title: nice looking bag, lots of space
text:
I am in love with this laptop backpack! The nylon is perfect to deter spills of my morning coffee (which is inevitable) and I love the sleek look and design of the bag. Everything is finished and double-stitched so it appears very sturdy and durable from first glance.

The side dedicated panel that unzips and securely holds the laptop away from other items is perfect. It has thick padding to protect the contents and is ample size to fit my 16" laptop with room to spare.

The interior is a fully lined berry color that contrasts perfectly with the black of the bag. I like the brown criss-cross tabs that are on various parts of the bag - it adds a very stylish look to the design. There are smaller, secure pockets both on the inside and outside of the bag to keep other items such as keys, cables, extra batteries and drives. I was surprised - once I loaded it up with my laptop and accessories, it was very comfortable to carry. The straps are also fully adjustable so you can carry it as high or low on your back as you choose. It felt so light as compared to carrying all my things in a shoulder bag.

Would love it if they made it in patterns and other colors, not sure if this is available or not.

title: wonderful, useful tablet
text:
I've a tablet for entertainment purposes, but nothing really beats a laptop when it comes to some tasks (writing, creating spreadsheets, presentations, etc). So when given a chance to get a Surface Pro at a great deal, I took it - I'd heard that this was a tablet that *could* do the work of a pc, that actually belonged in the workplace. After getting it in my hands and activating the Microsoft Office 2013 package, I have to say that I wasn't mislead on this matter.

The Pro is a bit heavier and a bit thicker than most tablets (which doesn't make it THAT heavy, it's still lighter than most netbooks out there, if not all). That thickness/heft gives you the processing ability to run multiple programs and software as well as a USB port and expand memory (more memory than other tablets out there, a friend who owns an iPad was *very* envious). The touch screen is very responsive and it takes just a little bit to figure out the new system of jumping back and forth between screens/desktop, and I think the detachable keyboard is a MUST if you're going to do any serious work on the Pro (I'd recommend the Type as opposed to the Touch as it has a more tactile feel). Response time has been very good on the Pro with the programs and the system not too difficult to figure out.

All in all, it's basically a computer in a tablet, nice and (relatively) light. Perhaps it's not as thin as some other tablets, or have as many apps, but it can out-work the heck out of them, which is a lot more important to me. If you want a tablet for doing something more than playing app-based games and updating your online status, this is the one to get.

title: grown to love it
text:
I'll admit, I've bought into the Amazon/Kindle crack. I own three now, the old e-ink, the old Fire and now the Fire HD. I'm sure if there's a new version that comes out, I'll probably find an excuse to buy it at some point as I keep finding uses for the older ones. That said, it took me a while to warm up to the Fire HD. Perhaps because I expected so much from it, it being the first real tablet Kindle to come out, even though I'm not going to rave about Apple or the others.

At first I mainly stuck to the reading and video capabilities - of course it's easy to download, manage and read material on the Fire HD. Videos look great on the screen as well, and as someone who streams their Prime account as well as Hulu and Netflix all of the time, I haven't noticed any issues with the video quality or capability. Some days I watch more on my Fire HD than I do my tv.

Music streams and plays well, also (though have a complaint with the playlists on Kindles and how they can time out. Why no loop feature, Amazon?).

I'm not the biggest app person out there - I've been able to eventually track down what I need and notice that there's more out there all of the time, but again, it's not like I hit the app store that often. I've never had an issue with the apps I have downloaded.

It took me a while to get used to the Silk/internet feature. I'm not the biggest fan of this aspect of the Fire HD - if there was something to detract stars from,t his wold be it. Maybe because on a regular pc I'd have a couple of dozen tabs open and tons of bookmarks, and I don't think the bookmark nature of Silk is very intuitive and I have to remember to keep the tabs to a minimum for it to function well. Here's hoping to improvements in future upgrades.

All in all, the Fire HD is a great tablet/multi-media/entertainment device. It's something I use pretty much every day and can take anywhere, and it's easy to figure out and set up. It also comes with fantastic customer service.

title: Useful keyboard for Microsoft Pro
text:
If you're going to do any serious typing while using a Microsoft Pro, this definitely seems the type of keyboard that you'll need - the 'touch' style keyboard, while usable, doesn't seem as conducive to 'blind' typing as this one since it's flat and doesn't give any resistance when you type. I like actually feeling the keys when I type, and I don't have any problems with this board's layout (I will admit that I do have small hands/fingers, though). I've been able to attach the keyboard and type with it on my lap, but I must admit that it's taking some getting used to with the touch pad - I wish the right/left 'mouse' click buttons were separate or below the touch pad as with the 'touch' keyboard. If I'm having any problems with this keyboard, it's clicking on the right mouse button.

Still, it's great for typing, I don't notice that much of a 'lag' when I type and it attaches quickly and easily to the Pro and seems sturdy (which is not to say to use too much force while typing). Just wish there were more color options as with the 'touch' keyboard.

title: Offers some protection
text: The Marware Swurve kid proof case does offer some protection for your Kindle Fire HD 7" - it makes it easier to grip for small and big hands (always a good thing), pads the edges and is a nice foam cushion against falls. It sticks out a bit, too, which makes the Kindle a bit bigger, but it doesn't have a cover so there's not as much protection to the screen as some other cases can provide (that's why this doesn't get a 5 star review). This cover will work if you take a little care with the Kindle, but if you think it'll be in destructive (very young) hands, you might want to invest in a very good screen protector or a better case.

title: Very nice sound quality
text:
I'll admit that I usually get by on the earbuds and don't usually pay a lot for headphones - most of the time I just use what comes with whatever music player I've purchased. These were available for trial so I figured 'why not'? I must admit that they are doing a very good job of convincing me to turn in my earbuds....

These aren't noise canceling headphones, but they do a very good job of muffling out the sound around you, which is great because a lot of time I do listen to music while in a noisy environment (traveling, work, etc). The sound quality itself is definitely an improvement over other head/earphones I've used in the past - I'm picking up more musical instruments and definition in songs. These are also very nice looking headphones. I received the white/ivory ones and while plastic, they appear solid and have a nice heft to them, with good padding and a thick cord that is less prone to tangling.

The downside (and the reason they didn't get five stars)? Well, they are pricy, and they are a bit bulky (you're not going to fit them in your pocket), although they do come with a nice bag and collapse somewhat so you can throw them in a backpack or bag to protect them while traveling. I also wish that the toggle to adjust volume/tracks for iDevices was lower on the cord - it's about shoulder level on me and I'm not a big person (but it works great w/ my iPhone). The headphones also exert a bit of pressure against the ears to provide a snug fit and block out noise, so I find myself adjusting them from time to time for a bit of relief, especially since I listen to music for a few hours at a time while working. They take some getting used to on that front. But overall, I think they're worth it for the quality and listening experience.

title: great yet simple MP3 player
text: I think this is the third Sansa mp3 player I've bought - I tend to load various mp3's onto them and stash them into my car to play when the radio gets annoying. They're easy to transfer music onto (drag and drop), the screen is easy to read as well and to navigate, and it plays most music formats. You can expand the memory by adding a microSDHC card, and best of all, these players are cheap (so little worry about them being broken or stolen). Not that there's as much a worry about the latter as they don't stand out too much as some other mp3 players. Yes, they're simple, but if you're looking for a reliable mp3 player, these are it.

title: gorgeous cover
text:
This really is one very nice looking cover. It makes me feel as if I am holding a real book instead of a tablet/ereader, and it does look a lot like leather (which it isn't). I really like the 'sleep' feature that this cover has, putting my Kindle to sleep mode when I close the cover, something I haven't come across in the other covers I've bought in the past. It does have a handy stand feature that lets you prop it up, in the horizontal position only. The fasteners to hold the cover closed and to keep the Kindle in place inside are rubber, but they do a decent job of it (and can be positioned to prevent any important ports/buttons from being covered). Of course, with this type of cover (fake leather, going for the appearance of a real journal/book), the speakers are going to be covered, but it doesn't have too much impact on the sound when you're using it.

There's been comments made on the smell of this cover, and I've noticed that pretty much all of my fake leather covers come with some sort of odor when they arrive. It usually dissipates after a day or two (longest might have lasted a week) and this was no exception - if anything, this was one of the 'better' smelling faux leather covers I've received. None of them were so awful as to be off-putting, in my opinion, but I'm aware that it's a personal thing, how much it affects you.

All in all, this is an impressive looking cover that has a few nice features and enough heft to provide some decent protection for your Kindle Fire.

title: Provides an okay cover
text: I've a couple of different Kindles already (yes, buying into the Amazon crack), and this is probably my least favorite of the Kindle covers.  Which isn't to say that it doesn't do its job - the Kindle fits snugly into the cover, and it does protect it.  You've got the whole fake leather thing going on, which means you've got to put up with the pleather odor for a few days once it arrives, and there's nothing really atheistically pleasing that stands out about this cover (design-wise) that stands out.  I'll give it points for leaving all of the buttons/ports easily accessible for the Kindle Fire, but there's basically one display position for your Kindle with this cover (horizontal) and it could be more stable.  You also have the rubber band closure to keep the 'lid' closed.  So if you don't want anything too fancy, this will definitely do.

title: Nice, thin and lightweight cover
text: If you're looking for a thin, lightweight cover, this definitely fits the bill. Not sure if it's worth the money (especially since I received it through the Vine program), but this is the thinnest/lightweight cover I've seen, and I've purchased several different ones for my various versions of Kindles. It does have a horizontal display stand option, not the most stable I've seen, but the cover will fold back to allow that, and you 'snap' the Kindle Fire into place in the cover.  All in all, it seems like a decent cover if you want some protection (especially for your screen) while carrying it about without too much weight, but if you're accident prone, I'm not sure this will hold up to too much abuse (or that the cover fastens closed all that well).  Also, I've had other covers that provide much more stable display bases with more options as well.  But it does live it up to its name/advertising, I'll give it that much.

title: very impressed!
text:
As a person that appreciates style and appearance, as soon as I saw this UE Boombox I was impressed. It is a modern, sleek design that includes a long handle across the entire top of the boombox that adds to the portability of the speaker. It is shiny silver with a rubberized silver bottom and sides that assist in gripping it to whatever surface it is set on. The right side has a blue rubberized "quick hit" volume up and down panel and the left side houses the Bluetooth Pairing button, Power switch, battery indicator, and 3.5mm aux input (this cable is not included with the product).
According to the product specifications, two 0.5-inch tweeters, two 3-inch woofers, and four 2.6-inch passive radiators deliver the audio and it contains a rechargeable battery with a 6 hour life as estimated by Logitech. This battery is replaceable after it has reached the end of its lifetime. The battery charger is included with the product.
Pairing of my iPad and this UE Boombox was so easy I was actually really surprised. I removed it from the box, charged it for about two hours (which I later learned on Logitech's website was no necessary. It comes fully charged). After two hours, I followed the simple three step instructions to pair the UE Boombox which consisted of turning it on, waiting for the Bluetooth light to blink rapidly (took about 5 seconds) and then selecting the device under Bluetooth on my iPad. It worked just liked the instructions said it would! Sooooooooooo simple!
I played through many types of musical genres and again was very impressed. The bass is great on this UE Boombox. I do Zumba dancing and music like Pitbull and Flo Rida sounds fantastic on this (even blaringly loud). I also ran through Kidrock, Styx, Journey, and some Barry Manilow and the music sounded fantastic at all volumes. The bass is really deep and intense at loud volumes making this the perfect party boombox.
Overall, at $250, the Logitech UE Boombox offers a good-looking design and impressive output in this reviewer's opinion.

title: good sound, nice for Kindle Fire
text: This is a great idea for a Kindle Fire - the kit comes with two speakers that really does improve the sound quality of whatever you're listening to.  You can charge the speakers by USB - either through your computer or an adapter, and the stand/cradle will hold your Kindle and allow it to charge as well (through your own charging device, it's not included in the kit).  The stand doubles as a case for the speakers, which allows you to easily carry them around if you want to take them and your Kindle with you to the office or somewhere else.

title: works just as well as a name brand card
text: This would be a five star review except that the card didn't work on an early model digital camera (a Nikon), but it was accepted by a much newer one (a Lumix) and worked as well as a Sandisk, Kingston or any of the other SD cards out there.  It was quickly recognized by the newer camera, and the photos were easily retrieved and of good quality.  This card should hold over 9000 photos from the camera settings.  Not a bad bargain at all.

title: great tv
text:
I bought this tv when a local store had them on sale, after deciding to get an internet tv. I am by no means an expert, but I have been impressed by this tv. The visuals are very clear, even for non-HD channels, and the sound comes through just as good even without the aid of any additional speaker systems. Set-up was easy, the internet interface isn't difficult to figure out nor was it hard to set up new accounts to different sites or download new apps. The remote helps to navigate the web as well, with an actual keyboard. It's great to have everything on one television and not have to worry about having other devices if you do want to connect to your Netflix, Hulu, etc account.

The one complaint I do have isn't about the tv but the lack of instructions. You can go to the Sony site, but it would have been nice to have more info WITH the tv.

title: sold me on ebooks
text:
After running out of space for bookcases and space *on* those bookcases, it was suggested that I look into getting an ebook reader. I decided to give a Kindle a try, and it's made the transition from paper to e-ink a mostly painless transition. The Kindle Keyboard is lightweight - even with a cover it's light enough to hold for long periods of time and usually thinner than most books. It's a little bigger than most paperbacks but smaller than hardcovers, to I can fit it into a larger purse and take it with me if I'll have time to kill during any appointments. Of course, it makes traveling much, *much* easier as now I only need to pack the Kindle and one book to read during that 'power off all electrical devices' time.

The 3G version allows more connectivity but does drain the battery faster. If you want to conserve energy, you can turn it off unless you are downloading a book. The keyboard is small, but I haven't found it too tiny to use when unlocking it for use or searching. My only complaint is sometimes trying to remember when to use the 'Menu' button and the 'square' button for some features - it could be a bit more intuitive (like when to remove a book or sample from the device).

The Kindle Keyboard is only 4GB (actually a little less) and can't be expanded beyond that, but it does hold a lot of books. It's also easy to load books by USB cable and sending via email (to Kindle email account). It's definitely saved at least a bookcase or two! While I would hate to see all books go digital, if you do have an issue with space or you want to have a few books always on hand, a Kindle definitely helps in that regard.

title: Great wireless mouse
text: I've used several wireless mouse with my laptops over the years, and the Logitech M525 wireless mouse is definitely one of the better.  First, it helps that the USB link is small and unobtrusive - if you're going to carry your laptop around at all, either from room to room or (for various meetings or whatnot), it helps to not have to worry about removing it to avoid having it snag on things or risk being snapped off.  Second, there's a very nice 'feel' to this mouse in that it fits well in one's hand.  Third, the mouse moves very well over a surface (various flat surfaces, desk and mousepads) and flows easily on the screen.  The scroll ball and clicks are smooth as well, making it very easy to use and not jumpy on the screen.  I have no problem using this all day in a work environment - it's a definite upgrade from my older Logitech mouse!

title: It gets the job done
text: I purchased this to have next to my desk while working from home.  It is powerful enough between the three speeds.  It's a little cheap looking and depending on the angle, the head sometimes drops.  It is also a little noisy, especially in a small space.  I will say the clip on is sturdy and it is good enough for what I needed.

title: Great quality!
text: These earbuds are great for the price! They are pretty sleek and the charging box is very compact. Easy to throw in my purse and go. Easy to use. Clear instruction manual.

title: I recommend rolling/wrapping the cord and NOT just stuffing them somewhere ...
text: I use these as a "backup" pair of earbuds. I have had my pair for well over a year & they still work well. I recommend rolling/wrapping the cord and NOT just stuffing them somewhere in a drawer because the cord tends to "crease" up a little bit.

title: Durable, attractive, just the right size.
text: This is great, especially for CDs. So glad it also plays cassettes, serves as an AM/FM radio, etc. and can be used with headphones.

title: Five Stars
text: Great product at a good price.

title: liked it very much
text: Purchased the identical rack a few months ago, liked it very much, so this purchase is to accommodate more movies and CDs. The width and height of the rack suits my limited space perfectly.

title: Five Stars
text: Nice and sturdy, as described.

title: Very good product. Strong
text: Very good product. Strong, well-made, does everything I need, even holds my cell phone still attached to the charger and cord.

title: Five Stars
text: Great product. I bought two. Much better than any other charging cord. Highly recommend.

title: Excellent sound and very comfortable
text: Excellent sound and very comfortable. The only potential negative is that the smallest width may be too broad if you have a small head. I'm using these headphones to listen to music as well as to watch movies. Very good buy.

title: but otherwise it's a very good unit.
text: Exactly as described. Figuring out how to set the clock was tricky, and the remote is too tiny, but otherwise it's a very good unit.

title: Love it
text: Small, durable, efficient.

title: Best desk so far
text: I have tried so many desks before but none of them are comfortable to use.  This one is very good in quality and style in looks. It is made with weightless wood. It comes with a cup holder. Easy to adjust.

title: works as advertised
text: Plug it in, do backups, pull it out.  It works. Comes with a detachable cable and a carry / storage case. Come on guys, it's a hard drive.  How excited do you expect me to be?

title: Good stuff.
text: It's my second buying batteries and chargers from this BM company.  It's a good fit and I think we'll made.  It is also 25% of the original cost of a Sony OEM battery and charger.  I don't know about the longevity of these batteries, but I will find out on an upcoming trip to Central America.  I would recommend a buy from this BM (bowel moment?) company.

title: perfect
text: It worked perfectly.  Recharging went with a problem.  Sony OEM battery recharged to full.  It only quarter the price of a Sony OEM charger.  Great buy.

title: Good stuff!
text: Very useful especially if you have bunch of devises with bulky chargers.  They don't get into each other's way.

title: Well Made!
text: This is a good computer bag.  I was surprised of the quality.  Definitely would recommend it to anyone looking for a computer bag.

title: Above average
text: I like it, but they should make it a bit brighter display for the money that I paid.

title: No Good!

title: Bad Camera

title: Not Reliable Connection!
text: I usually buy Netgear and trusted them for many years.  Their wireless routers are the best on the market.  I was hoping for the same quality when I bought the Universal Dual Band Wireless Internet Adapter for my slingbox and TV at home.  This device is totally unreliable!  The problem with this product is that it cannot maintain a reliable connection 24/7.  It also cannot re-establish the connection to the wirless router once it's disconnected.  You have to physically go up to the device everyday (minimum) to disconnect the power and reconnect the power to re-establish the wifi connection to the wireless router.  Also, the problem is worst as you get farther from the wireless router.  It works best within a close proximity to the wireless router.  It's better to get the Netgear Universal Dual Band Wifi Extender with the Ethernet ports in the back.  It will automatically re-connect to the wireless router if the wifi gets interrupted.

title: I wake up gently and refreshed
text:
In the summer, I gradually wake as the sun filters into the bedroom. My consciousness slowly emerges, and by the time I am truly awake, I am alert and ready for the day. I usually even beat the alarm clock out of bed. In the winter, when the sun is a lazy-bum and sleeps in far too late, I get no advance notice of the impending alarm buzz. I am ripped unceremoniously from a deep and stuporous sleep, ejected from bed to wander the dark frigid halls, hitting my knees on unseen hazards, and bumbling through a groggy and grumpy morning.
In summary, waking up with the Philips Wake-up light in the winter just feels like summer - it's awesome.

I would change one thing: the time display cannot be dimmed all the way down (I'd prefer it to be completely dark).

title: Perfect for splitting signal from box to two TVs.
text:
Here are my findings for this device. I have FIOS. I have two TVs from one of my boxes. One is a 1080(Sony) and one is a 4K TV(Samsung). Both work perfectly. What I have found is that there is a short lag from the splitter. When you turn TVs on or off there is a lag of about 10-15 seconds while the switch waits to start the signal. It is not so long as to be annoying but it is not immediate. Also if you have one TV on and you turn the other TV on or off the signal is lost for that short lag period. Also positive for this device is that the splitter does not get warm. When the TVs are off it is room temp. I have found that the splitter works best with a higher quality cable.
For what it is worth I have used a 6FT cable and a 10FT.

CONS: USB-C DisplayPort 1.2 ONLY. NO backwards compatibility. NO adapters. NO options. This will work with most new(ish) phones & laptops, but this WILL NOT connect to your desktop unless it has a native USB-C port in either the Motherboard or GFX card. Some new high-end desktops may have this, but most do not.

I appreciate that USB-C is the best way to go for a device like this, but without any option or support for backwards compatibility, it is extremely disappointing. So I've bought this one having the L-shape plug, instead of the straight one that the original cord had and long power cord. Also it doesn't spark (has 3 prongs). It charges my laptop quickly and properly as my original charged did. I was happy at that time.
But on next day I've noticed that my 22" Dell monitor connected to my laptop is flickering when my laptop is charging. (All devices were connected to one surge protector).
I unplugged the charger from my laptop and my Dell monitor stopped flickering. I googled the issue and found out that users with the same problem use 2 different approaches to fix this problem. 1st one is to plug extended monitor to another outlet, 2nd one - to buy a charger with a shorter cord.
Ist one worked for me but it was very inconvenient to have a long extension cord across my home office.
I've tried my daughter's original Toshiba charger and it didn't cause any flickering to my extended display.
So, I am going to return the charger back.
------------------------
My update.
I sent this charger back to Amazon and bought another one - iTEKIRO 90W AC Adapter for Toshiba. It works perfectly without any flickering.

title: Great keyboard
text:
I must say, I love this keyboard. I am a medical student and I type a lot of my notes into my macbook from online lectures, text-books, review books, ect. Doing so on my lap is fine, but, for practical reasons I need to type on a table to keep all my books, ect in front of me. The macbook keyboard is not meant to be used on an elevated surface like a table for extended periods to time. After a while I noticed that my wrists were getting some carpal-tunnel like symptoms as well as tendonitis. I promptly bought this keyboard from Microsoft and have been very happy with the purchase and my wrists and hands have also thanked me.

Pros: The keyboard is beautiful. It is black, with some reflective black trim on the top. The keys are angled, to put less stress on the wrists and it is a full keyboard. It has the number pad, the directional buttons, function keys, page navigating buttons and some short-cut buttons. Not all the buttons work natively when I connect it to the macbook (for example the home and end keys don't always work in web browsers), the calculator short-cut key doesn't work. However, the most important keys for my purposes work. The function keys enable a mac user to use expose and panels, and the volume short-cut keys work as well. The keys have a good response, and I can definitely type much faster (and with less fatigue and typos) with the microsoft keyboard than my built-in macbook keyboard. Considering it is a full keyboard, it does feel pleasantly light and portable. I can't fit it in my satchel bag, but I do carry it around to the library / conference room to work, without any hassel. Another pro, the price is right.

Cons: It doesn't bother me, but the keys do make more noise than my laptop when typing. I feel badly sometimes when I start vigorously making notes and I know other people in the library hear the clackity-clackity of my key strokes. I don't think its worse than your typical desktop keyboard, but if there were one thing I could change about it, I would make it quieter. I've only been using the keyboard for a month or two, so I can't vouch for its durability, but at the price, I could easily buy another when it breaks.

title: Excellent for the price
text:
Ordered one from Amazon, $35. Like that camera can sit inside on window sill, flush to the glass of the window, and perfect video picture, night vision is spectacular (have read some ambient light outside is required). No need to worry about batteries or wiring, it plugs into the wall. You also do not need a subscription for just basic usage, but it will only film an event and notify you once every 5 minutes if you opt for no subscription. For $15/year, it is unlimited with no 5 minute pause between even detections. Has a micro SD slot (micro SD card not included), we just used one we had, but not necessary for camera operation. It can also be paired with other appliances through an IFTT app like a garage door.
The MAJOR ISSUE is that even though you may set your detection area, the detection is via a change in pixels (where Ring, Blink, etc. are infrared and detect a heat source) and we receive an EXCESSIVE DETECTION NOTIFICATIONS when the sun sets and shines through the leaves or at night when car headlights flash across the detection area. We have also read where people receive excessive detection notifications when it rains or bugs attracted to light, but we have not had an opportunity to put it to the test with these. The only solution to minimize these notifications for these non-events is to move the camera or to set up rules to silence events during certain times of the day. For the cost, we decided we can live with this. Our walk around for now, is to just have one family member's phone receive alerts. And the other family members must block the alerts for this specific app in the settings of their phone (not within the app, or it blocks everyone's notifications).
Only the initial person who sets up the camera on the app, can make a lot of the changes to the camera within the app. And other family members are just shared access to the camera and can set up their own rules. The initial person who did the set up will receive notifications a split second before the people it is shared with.
Ordered a 2nd one that was supposed to be new, but WAS OPENED and still had the UPS stickers on it with the customer's name and address who had returned it. So returning the 2nd camera and ordering a replacement, hopefully this one will be new.
Realize with any electronics that receive updates (like with cell phones, fitness trackers, etc), they do not have an infinite life due to technology restrictions so another reason to go for this budget friendly option. I believe Wyze retired support for their 1st model after 5 years.
Price on Wyze website was $29.99 ($57.98 for 2) plus $5.99 shipping, but decided buying it from amazon would make sure we had free returns with Prime. Wyze is a company started by former Amazon employees and it is based in Seattle.
Update: very sensitive to raindrops on the window, birds, neighbors' lights turning on and creates an event and notification.

title: Endured the elements for four wintry months, and my headphones survived intact!
text:
I wanted a simple hardshell case to attach a carabiner to and sling my noise-canceling headphones off my backpack. This did the job. It was fine, I was pleased.

Then I came back from a December trip to Helsinki and somewhere between baggage claim at DFW and my front door, the case - with my beloved headphones, a battery bank, and my Apple rapid charge block - vanished.

I was heartbroken. I filed reports. I checked with my Lyft driver. I went through my backpack and suitcase over and over and over again. I poked the bushes around my apartment building. Nothing.

Fast forward four months to today. I took the trash out and as I came back up the stairs, I saw something dark colored under the feral cat shelter on my patio. In all these months I’d never noticed it. But when I lifted the shelter, there it was. Filthy, scratched up, covered in pollen - my headphone case. I believe I knocked it under there while I was looking for my house keys.

In the last four months the DFW area has seen torrential downpours, freezing sleet, and even snowdrifts. My porch often catches the brunt of these storms. And yet when I zipped the case open, my headphones and battery bank and charging block were perfectly fine. Not so much as a dust mote on them. Everything was still fully charged and absolutely totally functional. As if they hadn’t just spent four months outdoors in Texas’ wacky winter weather under a cat hutch. Completely perfect.

And the case may be fine externally as well once I take some Clorox wipes to it.

Anyway. Good case, STUPENDOUS dang value for the cost.
