This is a great cable for hooking up a USB-C peripheral or extending a rear USB-C port on a computer to the front of it. It is weighty and feels quite durable. A little thick and a little stiff (on account of the length) for what I would call everyday use - I wouldn't typically use this sort of thing for my phone for example - but quite suitable for hooking up an external USB-C SSD for example.

Not a fan of the long-ish USB-C connectors, they create quite the lever to apply substantial forces to USB-C ports. That's not exclusive to this cable, though, but the USB-C standard itself.

title: Remarkably effective at what it does
text:
I only purchased a smartphone about a year ago, previously being in the flip-phone-for-life crowd, due to the requirements of a job I was on. Since then I have slowly been picking up the various accouterments of such devices, the latest being this magnetic mount. I bought it mostly so I can use Google Maps for navigation.

It is remarkably effective. I have a Motorola Moto X4, in a slim silicon case, and an 05 Subaru Outback. The kit comes with the magnetic mount, two metal plates with adhesive (a rectangular one and a little circular one), a clear adhesive interposer, and, as a nice surprise, an alternate, black bezel.

What you do is attach the metal plate to the outside of your case, the inside of your case, or your phone. If you choose the lattermost option, then you don't attach it directly to the phone, but to the clear adhesive interposer (just a clear plastic sheet with adhesive on both sides), likely to prevent surface damage and dampen shock/reduce possible strain. If you have one of those pop-socket devices, you attach the little metal circle to the center of that instead. Then, you fit the magnetic mount to one of the grilles of your car's vent system, wherever it is most convenient. Now you can mount your phone to it, the magnet clinging to the metal plate.

I attached the metal plate to the inside of my case. It is very thin - I would say 1mm or less - and even on my slim silicon case it leaves only a very slight rise, hardly visible from the outside. I also attached it about 2/5ths of the way up from the bottom of the phone, as recommended (the Moto X4 does not have wireless charging). The magnet adheres quite well to the phone - the silicon case actually slightly pulls away when detaching the phone from the mount - not nearly enough to dislodge the case, but enough to let you know that the magnet is really sticking. As the mount has a rubber pad, and my case has a rubber texture, the phone does not slide at all in any lateral direction, the shear resistance is quite high. I am not concerned about the phone just falling off during normal operation of the car.

The tines of the mount grip the vents quite well - I have only had the mount pull off the vents once when detaching the phone after parking. There are two sizes of gaps - narrow and wide - and the narrow gap seems to fit pretty well on the Subaru. I like how you can pivot the mount a little to the left or right, and use the vent's own hinge to pivot it up and down.

There are some basic shortcomings of design. Obviously you can only attach this to the vents of the car, which limits your choice of positioning. I tried putting it on the left vent, but that caught too many outside reflections. I tried the right vent, but my hand was mostly blocking the screen. I tried the left passenger-side vent, but found that this took my eyes too far off the road while checking the navigation. In the end, I went with the driver's side right vent, since it required the lease eye-movement to check navigation and it was actually helpful to have my had block the screen, so as to avoid distraction. The tines hold, but they are not as secure as a hard mount would be. Likewise, the magnet could, in theory, be bumped out of position by kids/pets/carelessness and fall down into the foot well.

However, I would generally recommend this, at least as someone's first mount, to get a feel for what they are looking for if nothing else.

title: Decent foam, but the OEM Pick N Pluck is better
text:
Like it says in the headline, this foam is of good quality - it has heft, it easy to cut, and feels quite supportive. It fits the case perfectly, of course. However, unless you have a laser cutter or considerable skill, the Pick n Pluck cubed foam is *much* easier to work with. Even with a good hour's work of work using an art knife, a razor, a straight-edge and a t-square, I could not get the same clean, perpendicular lines as I had with the cubed foam in about five minutes. The original foam is even less expensive right now, ~$26 vs the $29 for the Cobra foam I'm reviewing here.

Maybe if you are working with complex curves and have the skill to cut them, this solid foam makes sense. However, if it's all straight lines, I recommend the OEM foam (ASIN: B0018NG3LS) instead.

title: Great little charging cable for the desk
text:
I purchased this for two reasons; one, to use as a phone charging cable, and second, to control my phone through my computer via ADB. It works well in both regards. I have the phone connected to a USB hub and it will fast-charge and talk to my system without issue. The cable is strong and flexible, and the weave on it is tight.

I might like something completely in black, without the white logo, but that is just a matter of aesthetics. In terms of function, these are on point. Would recommend.

title: Great for dashcam use
text:
I bought a pair of these to use with my dashcam (a Viofo A119v3), and so far have not had any problems. No problem recording 2560x1600 video, and can store about a week of my commute before it needs to start overwriting it, good stuff. Obviously the endurance component will need to be tested over time, but even regular SD cards have lasted years for me, I don't imagine these will be failing any time soon.

Value is decent - the PRO Endurance versions are about 2x as expensive as the regular cards. For most uses I wouldn't care, but for dashcam use, I am more than willing to spend the extra money up front, especially since you can get so much space for so little these days. If it comes down to it, I would purchase a smaller-capacity PRO Endurance card than a larger-capacity standard micro-SD, at least for this use case.

I typically install one in the camera and keep a second with a USB-C SD card reader ( an uni Sturdy USB C to Micro SD adapter) in my car. This way, if I do witness an accident I can backup the video onto my phone, surrender the one SD-Card to the officer on duty, and install the backup one for my trip home. It also is useful as a fallback in case the one MicroSD fails, is lost (dropped in some inaccessible place in the car) or damaged in some way.

Anyway, would recommend thus far. Will leave an update if anything comes up.

title: Great for general networking use
text:
I grew tired of making new 10' Ethernet cables every time a user came by looking for one, or losing my lab cables to other techs, and I didn't feel like putting in an actual order, so I just ordered this 10-pack. Great choice - I basically outsourced part of my job to China and only had to pay a fraction of my hourly rate to save an hour of annoying work. I've had them hooked up and operational for a month and a half and have had no issues, quality seems good.

Like many Ethernet cables, these are tricky to remove on account of the shroud. Not the most difficult I've ever had, but not great either.

Other than that, I would recommend.

title: Excellent cable ties
text:
These are narrow, plastic-sheathed ties great for securing cables. 300 is about enough for any non-commercial purpose, I like to keep a set of them aside so I don't have to constantly salvage used ones from new products. While I prefer to use velcro ties for active cable management, since they are a bit broader and neater, but these are great for storage. Much better than the cheaper, thin plastic film sort of ties that are also sold on amazon.

Anyway, high quality, tough, would recommend.

title: Great for organizing and protecting your cells
text:
I purchased this to protect my lithium AAs. Since those cells remain stable for so long, I can drop a dozen into this caddy and put it into long-term storage. Much better than just throwing a handful of batteries into a ziploc bag, and better than storing the cells in the original packaging with some tape over the cardboard to keep them from falling out. This is compact, durable, and it is very easy to tell how many cells are left. It is designed in such a way that the batteries stay in the caddies and are wholly prevented from creating a circuit with each other's contacts.

I have Storacell caddies for AA, AAA, C, CR123A, 9v, and 18650 cells and will continue to purchase more as I need them. Whenever I give someone a gift that uses batteries, I will include an extra set in one of the caddies as a sort of added bonus, it adds a lot to the presentation.

Broadly speaking, unless you need your battery caddy to be sealed against moisture or dust, this is the way to go.

title: Great caddies as always
text:
I use these to keep batteries in order while in storage. It isn't much, just enough to keep the contacts from touching each other, something that can be a problem if you keep your cells in a bag or on a shelf. It also lets you know exactly how many batteries you have left, instead of wondering if you have rogue cells bouncing around the back of the shelf.

The plastic is hard and strong, and the design ensures that the batteries are not likely to come free without a dedicated effort. It will protect them from some compressive damage if you keeps these in a tool box or pack, though obviously the walls are open and so the cells can still be damaged by hard edges in the wrong circumstance.

Overall, throw the cells in the caddy and the caddy in a ziploc bag, and you should be good to go.

title: Solid fan extenders, but there are better options when it comes to aethetics
text: Not bad as fan cables go, great for extending the length so your cable management is on point. Functionally, they are completely satisfactory. Aesthetically, the sleeving does not run all the way into the connector, so it is a little disorderly. Not an issue for the 99.9% of all users, but if you want a completely clean appearance, I would recommend going with the Cablemod fan extenders instead, since those sleeves run right into the connector itself, no visible wires.

title: Nicely designed, but a little overpriced
text:
I purchased this as a "desk unit", by which I mean I want it to be visible with the rest of my workstation. As such, it was important to me that it look good. And it does! It looks quite nice with its aluminium body, much better than the plastic bodies typical of seven-port hubs. Works well too, high transfer speeds and everything. No general complaints about the product itself.

It is a little expensive for what you get. I would like more power delivery across all ports, or at least one that supports Fast Charge. I would appreciate it if the unit was a bit heavier, it sort of skids around a bit in its current state - I may add some weight to it myself for stabilization purposes.

I think it's worth about $30, rather than $50, so if you can get it for that price, I recommend you do so.

EDIT: Just like other users, I have started to experience the "frequent dropout" problem, where some or all devices connected to the USB hub occasionally just disconnect, almost constantly, regardless of the port I have it connected to. As I purchased this 11 months ago, I will contact the MFTR for warranty service.

EDIT2: I have purchased three of these, and all three have the issue. After checking my system logs, I can see the hub dropping connection every three or four minutes or so, constantly. I have also seen the same thing with units we purchased for my work, so it isn't just my system or me. Started at four stars, dropped to three with the initial issue, but seeing that this is a widespread problem, one star.

title: Great for cable management
text:
I use these exclusively for cable management - I pass the end of the strap through the slot so that the strap is permanently secured to the cable, then bundle the cord up. EZPZ. Great value for the money, I bought two bags to organize my cables and I should probably be set for the next twenty years or so. Much better than constantly scavenging velcro straps from new purchases. I prefer these to wire ties, as they can be secured to the cable, stick better, apply force over a broader area and look a far bit more orderly when properly installed.

The straps are of good quality, adhere very well, and are easy to remove when you want to. The length is suited for wrapping up, say, most of your average 10-15ft computer or AV cables, it hasn't been a problem yet.

Only annoying thing is that when the factory punched out the slots in the strap, it only did so partially, so the little central bit is still stuck to the velcro most of the time. Bothersome, but not excessive so, you just have to tear it off each time. Another nitpick would be that I prefer my straps to have a constant width, rather than tapering down near the end - again, looks neater IHMO.

Other than that, would recommend.

title: They're screws all right, but could be a bit lower profile
text:
Good screws for 3.5" HDDs. I had trouble using them in my QNAP NAS sleds, the stuck out a bit from the surface, and I had to file down the heads quite a bit. For anything that doesn't require extreme low profile, they should be okay.

Quality looked good, no malformations or filled-in slots that I could see.

So now I have 394 backups. Doubtful most people need 400 HDD screws, but as someone who has general IT related interests and activities, it is nice to have a vast surplus of the hardware I need without having to dig through the sack of a thousand leftover screws to find even one thing with just the right pitch and length for my purposes, let alone four like it. Buy them once, put them in a labeled container, and you've solved the 3.5" HDD screw problem for the rest of your life with a outlay of about $9. Worth it to me.

title: A vast improvement over standard Corsair PSU cables
text:
I purchased these for the RM650x in my new build. to clean up the appearance of my case, as the default Corsair cables are serviceable but neither flexible nor visually appealing. Do I have a fancy case? It's a Fractal Define Mini C, so, sorta. Do I have a side window? No. Will anyone ever see the interior of this case aside from me and randos and I'm flexing on? Certainly not.

Why get cables like these? Call it an eccentricity. I don't like chaos hiding right out of sight. Sure, the Mini C would have the outward appearance of a stocky monolith of unalloyed order, but inside there would be a twisting madness of PVC and copper, heaving silently against the surface. There would be no evidence of it, sure, but I would know.

I would know.

So anyway, I purchased these to extend the relentless teleology of the IC into the broader world, and to this end I was successful. The cables are much more flexible than the default ones and the paracord is an interesting contrast against the typical circuit boards and enameled aluminum panels. They are a bit pricey for what you get, that's definitely the case - you might be better served by getting a different brand or shorter extensions rather than the full PSU set. I just happened to have the money for the CableMods.

Caveats: if you are using velcro ties inside the case, then you have to be careful with the ModFlex, as the hook-side can pull threads from it. I presume ModMesh, being nylon, would not have that issue. to get around it, I used rubber/silicon bands, since unlike zipties they can be removed and adjusted relatively easily.

Would I recommend them? If you have a side-window or transparent case, they are a definitely aesthetically on point. ModFlex or ModMesh, either should be suitable. If not, unless you too are eccentric, it probably isn't worth it. The improvement in airflow and the reduction in strain on the components are minimal so long as you are implementing reasonable cable management techniques. I'm still happy I purchased them though, since I'm pretty sure I'll be able to use them in the next two-three builds and they did make it a bit easier to get everything where I wanted it.

title: Much improved look for fan cables
text:
I purchased these for my Noctua 120mm and 140mm chromax case fans, and am pretty happy with them. They are short, 30cm, which is all you need. The Noctua fans come with their own cable, but you can pop it off and replace it with these instead, so you don't end up with a bunch of extra cable hanging around. I particularly like how the sleeving runs right into the plug, rather than stopping short of it. The additional flexibility is also welcome - as you can guess, fans fit into tight places and it can be difficult to maneuver the cable around within them.

As always is the case with ModFlex sleeving, be careful around velcro, as the hook side will tend to grab threads from it and pull them free.

Definitely would recommend as replacement fan cables.

title: Quality finish and a good fit
text:
I ordered these for my Fractal Design Define Mini C case. I had replaced the case fans with Noctuas, so the entire case was black except for the PCI slot covers. These have a great finish and fit perfectly. I might like it if they had a slot/hole for the screw rather than a notch, but that hasn't been the standard for a while now and isn't a huge thing.

Only thing to note is that they were a little dusty when they arrived.

Would recommend for anyone looking to replace lost covers or who want to spruce up the appearance of the their case a bit.

title: So it buzzes
text:
Great littlle buzzer to use with your motherboard, in case it didn't come with one. The little wires are movable, if you take some basic care; all you do is gently lift the little plastic tab where the wire comes to and end inside the black plug. This was necessary for me because my buzzer leads were on pins 2 and 3, not 1 and 4. It is a delicate operation, though, so be careful.

Build quality is adequate. Not the prettiest thing, especially if you are going for an A E S T H E T I C case design, and one wire was loose when the buzzers arrived. Not terrible, not not great eitheir.

Anyway, it buzzes when it is supposed to buzz, so it gets a recommendation.

title: Great for stabilized keys, meh otherwise
text:
I am running a WASD CODE v2 with Cherry Clears. Those aren't very loud keys, but that keyboard has a bit of an echo to it, you can kind of hear the return action reverberate against the metal backplate. Not a big deal.

I purchased these as an experiment to see if they affected the sound at all. I found that they didn't do much for the noise and if anything made it more difficult for the key press to register. It also changed the way the keypress felt, making it blunter and a bit soft, I didn't care for it to be honest, though someone who doesn't drive the keys as hard down might not care.

What I did like - quite a bit - is dampening the spacebar, enter key, and backspace. That was worth it - these pads significantly dampened the sound of those larger keys, such that they sound almost exactly like the rest of the smaller keys now. Great in particular for the spacebar, but also helps if you are hammering the enter or backspace for some reason.

So, in short; worth it for stabilized keys, a little too thick for regular ones, at least when using a WASD CODE and Cherry clears.

title: Great storage solution for 9v batteries
text:
These are great solutions for 9v batteries. I like using them for my 9v lithiums, since they have a very long shelf-life and tend to hang around the storage closet for years at a time. I'm also an electrical technician and have many tools which make use of 9v cells, and there is little more annoying than getting out into the field to discover that the battery in one of your meters is dead, so I always keep a four-pack of 9vs in with the rest of my kit. the caddy keeps them in order and makes it obvious when you need to refill it, instead of wondering how many extra batteries you are carrying and if you have one bouncing around in the bottom of the bag somewhere

As for this specific caddy, it seems well-built and feels very sturdy in the hand. Batteries are easy to insert and remove again, but do not feel like they would fall out on their own. The shell would likely help protect the batteries so they aren't crushed by accidentally impacts. I purchased the orange caddy, so it is easy to locate when needed.

Would recommend.

title: Surprising impact on sound
text:
I've had my AKG K701 headphones for many years, so I didn't really notice the breakdown of the (original) pads until right after I washed them a month or two ago. Soon after, the headphones were increasingly uncomfortable to wear and I realized that my ears were resting directly on grill covering the drivers - that's how degraded the pads had become. I considered ordering new OEM pads, but honestly I've now replaced the driver on one side of these headphones, resoldered the connection, repaired the wire and chewed up the outer cups in the process so I supposed it didn't really make a difference. I just needed my headphones to be wearable again.

These fit the AKG K701 perfectly. The material itself is not as nice as the OEM - you'd probably have to pay ~$80 for a pair of similar pads - but it is sufficient. Cushioning is okay, a little firm at first, I'm guessing they'll break in over time. They are still fine for people with glasses, like myself.

The one thing I didn't expect is the boost in sound quality, which is truly remarkable. Improvements across all frequencies, everything is crisper and clearer with these new pads, enough that I feel like I'm wearing a new pair of headphones. I suppose people who know headphones well probably see this as obvious, but for me it was a very pleasant surprise.

Would recommend for basic replacement pads for the AKG K701 headphones.

title: Fantastic cable ties
text:
Very happy with these - I'm in a technical position and always need more of these to corral cables and secure things down. Normally I am stuck scavenging them from new equipment that comes in, but they're never quite the right size and already kinked and hard to come by besides.

These are great. Long, strong, completely covered with their soft-plastic coating, they look and feel high quality and with 200 of them there's plenty to spare. I just keep a small handful in my desk at work and the rest at home, and have never wanted for twist-ties again.

Definitely would recommend.

title: Stout, low profile
text:
I'm using these with as standard pair of headphones (no mic or buttons) and they work just fine. I bought them for the low profile - that is, they don't stick as far out from the player as typical jacks do, creating the opportunity for damage if it torques the wrong way in your pocket. In this, they are pretty good. No audio problems. The male side snaps nicely into my player. The female side is sufficiently snug, could probably be a little tighter, but there's no play/intermittency I haven't had any issue with the headphones coming out yet. They appear to be well made, lot of material in these.

I'd probably recommend them to a friend, if they were looking for this sort of thing.

EDIT: I found, later, that I had not inserted the headphones all the way into this adapter. In actuality, the jack is exceptionally snug, not loose at all. So I will repeat my recommendation for this, I think it is just great.

title: Good for keeping on a lanyard under your shirt
text: I purchased this to wear on a lanyard, after losing my last one while out and about despite the thing being tied to my neck (encrypt your data folks). It's about what you expect from a drive, but it is very small - small enough to wear on a cord and it doesn't make a noticeable bump under your shirt - and it has a cap that snaps pretty snugly over the USB connection. In the past I've had problems with the gold contacts wearing down over months on account of perspiration and dust getting into the connection, but this cap may help prevent it. No transfer errors yet. I like it as it is for now, will leave a review if it starts to act up.

title: Works, but is little bulky in design
text: I used it a couple times. It works, but the plastic body is a little wide and awkwardly formed. I don't think it would be a major issue in most cases, but in tight spaces - such as the back of a computer, for me - it doesn't quite work.

title: Great mid-range tablet for general mobile media activities
text:
I purchased this for my mother after her old TF101 finally fell behind the times in terms of hardware compatibility. I was looking for a mid-range tablet at or around $200 for web surfing, reading books, and playing cards, which would continue to perform for the next four or five years or so. I also wanted something with a larger screen, decent battery life, and that didn't weight too much. After some research, I chose this T580 Galaxy Tab A.

It came with a charger (white) and in a non-retail box, but the device itself looks brand new - indistinguishable from something right off the shelf. I checked it over, installed all her apps, and it has been working for about two months now without any trouble at all. Battery life for reading/browsing/cards sorts of activity is at least 4-5 hours and probably more. Movement is silky-smooth, load times are minimal, and the screen quality is great (full 1080p with good pixel density). I'd recommend picking up a case, and maybe a anti-glare screen protector to cut down on the reflections a bit, but it's a solid tablet. I've already recommended it to another family member who is looking for something similar.

I gave my mother the TF101 a couple years ago, and she taught herself to use tablets around the age of 60, with very little help needed from me, so I'm pretty proud of her. Now she even helps my grandmother use her own tablet - often over the phone, no less. If you have relatives in that range, they might enjoy something like this, it's pretty user friendly with the touch interface and a lot of older folks like playing cards or casino games on them, just like the previous generations used to watch TV or listen to the radio.

The only complaint she's issued is that the bezel is a little narrow, so that she sometimes will accidentally advance pages in her books or change other elements in whatever she's doing through incidental touch-screen contact. A case helps mitigate this, but it's still a minor problem. She said she'd take off a quarter star for this, so we'll just round up.

Otherwise, my mother's very happy with it, so I'm happy with it. I'll leave an update if it gives us any trouble, but for now I'd say it's a good buy.

EDIT: It has been about six months, and my mother reports that the tablet is still doing great, no problems at all. She uses it essentially every single day, mostly for reading, looking up recipes, and playing some card games. We're both still happy with it.

EDIT2: It has been about a year now. Tablet is going strong, no problems with the device. We did have to replace the charger, just recently. It was becoming intermittent for some reason, same thing happened with two separate cords. Not sure what the deal was there, may be a usage issue, but a new charger was all of $10 and the problem was resolved, so not too bad all and all. The rating stays.

EDIT3: Two years and no problems whatsoever with the tablet; it's running as well as ever. I just wanted to leave this last update for those worried that a refurbished tablet might not last - for us, at least, it's doing just fine.

title: The only thing worse than one of these things is two of them.
text:
This is cheap and yet still not worth the money. It did not work from the start - a temperamental connection even at the outset. It will make rebellion against you, dropping channels or insidiously attenuating them just enough that you're checking the balance on your receiver every week or so.

You are a good person; there are people who want to see you happy, and therefore wouldn't want you to buy something like this. You want 1/4" to 1/8" audio adapter? Try this [[ASIN:B001DK1ZVO Grado Mini Adaptor]]. It's well built; you can hear the connectors snap into place from two rooms away. Try something like that. You'll be alright.

title: A high-quality, secure adapter that is worth the price
text:
I have a setup where I have some AKG-K701s running to a 30ft audio cable which connects to my receiver. This allows me to wander around the room while still listening to music without trouble - or almost without trouble. The headphones have a 1/4" stereo plug and the cable a 3.5mm jack, and though I tried two separate brass adapters (one of which was ASIN B01GPQJ5DA ) they were woefully inadequate for the task - loose from the very start, then constantly cutting out and eventually degrading entirely in the course of weeks.

This Grado adapter is in a completely different class. It was a nice hard snap, not only when plugging in the 1/4" connector but the 3.5mm as well. The short wire puts some distance between the two connections which relieves the stress. This is one case where the product is absolutely worth the price, I would recommend this to anyone who needs this kind of adapter.

EDIT: Six months later of kicking and dragging the adapter around the workshop has had zero effect on its performance. I've even tripped over it a couple times without issue. Still happy, still would recommend.

title: Quite happy with performance
text:
Does exactly what it is supposed too. I had to disassemble my Deathadder to clean it out and lubricate some of the switches, but in doing so damaged the footpads. I ordered this five pack, and though I had to use two layers of feet in order to get the proper thickness, I'm very happy with the results, I've had absolutely no problems since. Even looking now, I can't even tell that there's two layers there, that's how well they adhere to the surface.

The five pack is nice, not only because it lets you use multiple layers, but also provides plenty of extras if you accidentally screw up when apply them, or need to replace a foot again.

Definitely would recommend.

I called back to try to talk to another rep--was told they couldln't transfer me. Then, when i said i was recording it, and told him i had been transferred last time, suddenly he now could transfer me. Back to initial rep who refused to let me talk to anyone else and refused to budge on sending a new camera, even though it was an option in the email. I wrote letters and emails to management. Got a response, said they'd send me a new camera after i said i had the whole thing on recording and was thinking of posting to youtube. but they wouldn't pay for me to ship the old one back.  Anyway this story goes on and on, including me mailing the camera back and being told it actually WAS a new one and they were shipping the same camera back to me.  Was a nightmare. I don't know if any of the other companies are better, but i've been a solid Canon customer for 20 years--as i told them--and I won't be anymore.  They need to take lessons from Amazon on customer service.  Hope this camera lasts awhile as I know now it won't get serviced properly without it being more trouble than it's worth.

title: Great Laptop for the Money
text:
Purchased this laptop about 1 1/2 year ago and haven't had any major problems with it. For about half the money of a similar laptop it has met and exceeded my family's needs. This laptop is fast and reliable. The only problem we're having now after all this time is that the battery is dying and a message appears "consider replacing your battery." I have to admit I've had laptops with batteries that lasted 2 - 3 years before dying off, but the battery for the laptop is only $45 so it's worth it in the end.
The laptop doesn't get hot on the bottom like most of the laptops I've had until now. The fan is built into the back so I don't claug it when sitting on to sofa and browsing. The wifi works great. Nice options like the 1-touch buttons for backup, wifi, touchpad, and program. Sleek design, and not very thick for its size.
Overall I rated this product a 4 star only because of it's battery life. But If given the choice again, I'd probably go with this laptop again.

title: short life
text: Got this battery at the same time I purchased my Nikon point & shoot camera. The camera came with an original Nikon battery, but I wanted to have a spare on vacations etc.. This battery has a very short battery life compared to the original battery; about 1/4 or less life. For example, I could use the original Nikon battery to shoot about half day (200 - 300 pictures). With this battery I could get in about 100 pictures with no flash, and 50 or less with flash. It's inexpensive, but not worth the hassle.

title: Affordable Quality
text: I bought this camera a little over a year ago to have on vacations and family get-togethers so I wouldn't have to cary my SLR camera with me all the time. The camera shoots with good clarity in daytime shooting, but in low light or at night it has a hard time focusing / taking clear pictures. The video is the best thing about this camera. Really love the clarity and sound of the videos. Overall, I rated the camera a 4 star because of the low light issues (but every camera will have this problem.. some more than others). I would recommend the camera to anyone looking for a low budget camera that does an nice job.

[[VIDEOID:95306b827bbe3fa5240ee04bfcd54967]] My friend just bought a house and I got him this security camera set along with a video doorbell.

This set has a lot of cameras so you can double up corners and doors. I explained that you don’t just want high up cameras because then anyone wearing a hat can hide their face. You want some below eye level a bit to catch someone’s face even when they’ve got a hat on.

Installation of these will be easy enough - mount the cameras and run the wires. I’ve recommended to my friend using his vinyl siding to hide the wire. I did that with other cameras and it worked well.

Overall it’s a comprehensive set - looks really good.

title: Great while it worked
text: Absolutely great when it worked. Best camera I’ve used.  But the usb burnt out or something and stopped working

title: Works for my wife’s small business
text:
My wife runs a small business sewing and selling children's clothing. I got her this to help take pictures and it’s worked very well.

It’s easy to assemble, less than a few minutes. It’s bright inside and takes away from busy backgrounds.

title: Super easy
text:
Really couldn’t be any easier to use this. It’s total plug and play.

One side connects to your iPhone and the other the hdmi cable. That’s it.

It’s got the same finish as any apple product (that glossy white) and feels like it’s good quality.

title: Great for a road trip
text:
We didn’t buy the entertainment package with my minivan - we decided to get a few portable DVD players instead, and I am glad we did !

They’re so easy to use and it’s really nice that each kid can pick whatever movie they want to watch, without fighting over the TV. They can have headphones and we’ve got a quiet trip to wherever we are going.

These DVD player is a great size, light weight and easy to use. Screen seems very nice.

title: Durable and great price
text:
[[VIDEOID:e1deb0e19227c09b3ee6dc2245cdf1ac]] Zip ties are great to have in bulk. Super handy to have for random things - I attached string lights to my gazebo using these very easily!

These are sturdy and easy to use - can’t complain at all

title: Really easy to use
text:
Couldn’t be easier to use! Just plug and play

The finish on this is very nice as well - matches the finish on my HP laptop and makes it look very nice.

title: Great sound
text:
I liked these a lot because they don’t go in your ear. When I walk my dogs at night, I don’t like too much noise cancellation because I want to be aware of my surroundings.

I got these because they don’t sit in your ear. Your music comes through crystal clear but the world around you can still be heard. It makes me feel much safer.

title: Nice monitor
text:
I got this for my outdoor space. I wanted to plug a fire stick into it and have a portable tv !

I was worried at first as this didn’t have a USB plug in but it comes with every adaptor too need. It has the hdmi to usb adaptor I think its called. Exactly what I needed.

The built in stand is nice too. I might have done it wrong (ha) but I got it to stand and hold itself up just fine.
Really happy with this !

title: App control makes this the best I’ve gotten
text:
I have tried probably 4 or 5 different alarm and wake up clocks for my kids. This is my favorite. Why? The app!

I picked this one because the others were nice but they were limited. Lack of control - the minimal user interface through the clock was rough. Hard to set schedules and times. This one solves that with the app!

I like how I can easily customize wake up times and sleep times for my kids. The app connected easily and changing colors was also very simple. Highly recommend this

title: Didn’t work for me
text: Tried using this to connect my phone to my label maker and it didn’t work

title: Adapts to different systems
text:
Very simple and straight forward plug in speaker. It’s easy to use and it has a nice finish to match a computer workstation.

I liked that it had multiple adapters. Some computers have (or don’t have) USB and this provided the adapters as needed. Very nice addition.

title: Works as described
text:
[[VIDEOID:baf3b8b7decc714b5fce3a50b323212f]] This is a great idea for stores or even for a house. If you want to ensure you can make a loud emergency noise, you definitely want a system like this !

It’s got the two call buttons, each control the siren. You shut the siren off with the same button you turned it on with. It’s a nice safety idea for the system.

title: Could use more support
text: Could use more support near where the phone connects.  That’s where you pull and it always comes loose over time

title: Not to great
text: Not too great.  Work ok I guess

title: Comfortable
text:
These fit in my ears very comfortably.

I like the light up case a lot. Makes it easier to see when they’re charged and ready to use.

The fit in my ear without and issue and I was able to move around without them falling out.

title: So cool!
text:
These are a great idea for any backyard.

I got these for my friends backyard - they have a small yard in Jersey City. These are really cool. Speaker quality is actually pretty good.

They aren’t going to replace flood lights but they offer a nice ambiance and the addition of a speaker is really cool to have in the light.

title: It’s comfortable
text:
I work from home and I’m on the phone about 5-7 hours a day probably. I need comfortable headsets.

This is nice. It’s got good padding for both ears with decent noise cancelation.

title: Love that it comes with a screen
text:
I love that this comes with a screen. Makes it so much easier to use than projecting on the side of my house !

It’s got multiple ports as well, so you can plug in a laptop or phone via hdmi, or probably a fire stick as well and just have all yours normal streaming apps that way.

The remote makes this very convenient as well - sit back and relax, control as needed.

The system itself is very easy to use. Adjusting the picture and focus is simple by just turning the dial.

title: Elegant finish
text:
This has a really nice and elegant design to it. Fits in really well with my house and decor.

Controls are very easy to use. They’re clearly displayed but blend well into the sound bar.

It’s got a wide variety of inputs which is nice as well, so you can pick different items to plug into.

title: Does what it should
text: I’ve got an older tv from 2009 that is still alive and doing well, and many newer TVs from 2020.  I’ve gotten a few adaptors like this now for it, so I can use the older devices in the new TV without an issue.  I still use a DVD player sometimes !

title: As easy as an Apple Watch
text:
Download the app and this works great. Very easy to use and control. Pretty much just like an Apple Watch.

The app lets you track different items on the watch and easily change settings or your background. The heart rate monitor seems accurate and worked well for me as well

title: Works as expected
text:
The touchscreen is great. It’s easy to type and very responsive. I was getting tired of having to always use my phone to navigate, especially now that my kids wants it from the backseat to play games.

This works great right out of the box and had no issues navigating to different spots.

title: Nice camera
text:
[[VIDEOID:ea58b5709af8b92df97ad853ac91f882]] Really nice dash cam I think. Got this for my friend who lives in Jersey City. It’s a good idea for safety purposes to have this to ensure you’ve got video evidence if you ever get into an accident or have any issues.

Installation seems easy and the instructions are very specific on what to do - make sure you read them carefully, especially about formatting memory cards

title: fit well in my ear
text:
This fit very well in my ear. It was comfortable and they didn’t fall out easily.

The packaging is very nice and looks great. I like the case they come in as well. Battery life of these seems really long too

title: Nice to have for road trips
text:
We have a minivan but I didn’t get the DVD player built it. Decided to save several thousand dollars and just get this.

Super easy to add a dvd for the kids and they can watch whatever they want!

It’s a great size and it’s light, so it’s very portable.

title: Awesome speaker
text:
I wish I could use this speaker outside if a car! It’s awesome.

I love the waterproof setting for it - I want to keep this outside all the time for my patio too! I wish there was a way to wire this to an outlet - I would use it everywhere.

Light and colors are great too. Really feels like a sturdy tank of a speaker.

title: Really nice camcorder
text:
This camcorder comes well packaged. It’s a great little camera.

Very easy to use and simple to work with.

It fits very well even in small hands. It’s super simple to use. Basically turn it on and it works! Very easy and great if you don’t want to rely on your phone camera to take videos!

title: Wish I had this years ago
text:
Wow I wish I had this years ago! Feel like a car you’d see in the original fast and the furious movies !

I recommend you have a professional install this if you aren’t sure how the harness hookup works (you’ll probably need a specific harness for your car). It comes with the needed stuff for its own hookup (even the molding and trim remover) but each car may need a separate harness.

Touchscreen is cool - and I love that I can mirror your screen. Great feature to have.

The remote is also nice - stuff I wish I had previously !

title: Colors !
text:
There are many Bluetooth speakers on Amazon - I picked this one for the size and colors. I wanted something small and portable, but lights up!

I’ve got big speakers (like 48” tall) but needed something small for around the house or the patio. This works great and I really like the colors lights up

title: Does what it says it does
text:
Overall this is very easy to use. It’s a switch! Plug stuff into both sides and you can swap!

Got one monitor but two video game consoles? Well plug each hdmi cable into this and switch as you need. Very simple tool.

title: Easy to assemble
text:
This is a great device if you want to have TV without paying for cable!

The idea with this is that you attach it to a TV and you get access to the TV channels that are broadcast (so it’s not a cable channel but the normal ones like fox or ABC).

I have a TV too far from a cable jack (and I don’t want to pay for cable, prefer to cut the cord!) so things like this are great for me

title: Great for older devices
text:
[[VIDEOID:8f2eb983cdb3c9a0fe3c7a3435908ee0]] So I got a really nice Pyle speaker that hooks up to Bluetooth. But my TV doesn’t have Bluetooth! So I got this device.

You plug this into an audio out jack like for headphones and it turns your TV or other device into a Bluetooth device. It’s awesome for older TVs like mine (it’s a LG from 2009!).

It’s light and feels solid.

title: Great short hdmi cable !
text: This is a great hdmi cable.  I couldn’t find a short cable for so long and I’m glad I got this.  Works perfect and the cable feels sturdy. Plugs arrived safely and protected.  Exactly what I wanted

title: Arrived safely
text:
Comes very well packaged and arrived safely.

My friend is a police officer and I wanted to get something for him. Camera quality and safety is important.

This comes with all the needed accessories you need - the proper connecting wires and USB hookups.

title: Keeps bumping into stuff
text: It’s super cool that the screen moves.  Speaker is nice.  But it keeps bumping into the wall!  I’ve set the boundaries and “taught” it how far to turn but it seems to forget

title: Looks really professional
text:
My friend works in music technology and recently got an new job. Wanted to get him a present and this was great.

He works with students in a high school as a teacher and is always recording them playing so they can listen - he needs high quality tools to do his job well, and this I think is great.

The microphone is a perfect size and the stand holds it nice and steady.

title: Nice headset
text:
I work from home and I am on the phone 5-7 hours a day. Need something comfortable.

This headset is comfortable. The microphone easily adjusts wherever you need it to be.

The ear piece fits on my ear well and the material is nice. Should work great

title: Nice quality
text:
Good quality sound bar. Very good value for the price.

The remote is simple and nice to use as well. It’ll easily hook up to most TVs without an issue I think.

title: Very nice looking tablet
text:
Very easy setup. This is similar to any other android tablet - turn it on and connect it to a wifi network.

Plug in your gmail credentials and you’re off. I like how simple and easy to use it is.

The internals are very nice. I’ve been using it for casual web browsing and Amazon shopping (ha!) and it works great for that.

title: Love charging and audio at the same time
text:
I was able to plug my kids tablet into this, allowing me to charge it, give them audio and charge another device !

This make it really convenient to charge and multitask at the same time. Color is nice that it stands out clearly too !

title: Fit great on my head
text:
Comes in a really nice case. I like the packaging.

The headphones fit nicely in my head and did not fall out. They felt very comfortable.

title: A lot of cool functions
text:
So I think the Apple Watch is too expensive for what it does. There are so many other cool watches available that have the same functions. Here is a great example.

It’s easy to hookup - download the app and just go from there.

The functions are cool. Not only did it tell me my blood pressure but my heart rate and O2 stats

It has easy to use swipe functionality and the screen even looks sort of like an Apple Watch. Just a way better price

title: Great case
text: This tablet has the same internal hardware as the one I just bought myself!  It’s for adults as much as kids.  But the great thing is the awesome case this has.  It’s got a lot of padding so it can survive lots of drops from little hands. The kick stand is nice too for watching tv or movies

title: Seem really nice
text:
These function really easily. They’re normal Walkie talkies - the charging base plugs in via usb and keeps them both charged for whenever you need.

The color is bright so you won’t lose them. My kids were able to handle them easily so they’re very lightweight.

title: Really nice and compact
text:
So I love that this has tons of ports.

I got this for warm summer nights when we want to sit in the pool and project a movie. I picked this one for a few reasons. It doesn’t have wifi, which makes if cheaper than the wifi models. And that’s ok because the plan is to use a fire stick. This has so many ports, you can easily plug one in and stream all your favorite content. The fire stick has wifi, so you’re covered and save a lot of money!

title: Solid feeling case
text:
[[VIDEOID:1b1f9d16a8aca805482371f852443e40]] This is a very solid feeling case.

Working it is easy, comes in two parts that you assemble together over the AirPods.

This feels very sturdy. I wouldn’t run a truck over it haha but if you drop the case, it’ll be just fine I think.

title: Feel very nice
text: These seem very high quality. The material feels nice and soft.  Stitching is very nice as well.  Really make the air tag look pretty

title: Worked great
text:
[[VIDEOID:cfb1653d1d150d6bd7e11bc5bf4e2ce3]] I took these on a road-trip to Disney. I had the opportunity to use them in the car, with a power bank, and plugged into a wall adaptor.

They worked great in all three situations. Charging worked perfect.

They also were sturdy and even with all the moving around , kept right on working.

title: Handheld
text:
I got this to turn my tv that is not Bluetooth into a Bluetooth for a speaker.

It’s very handheld and small - fits right in the palm of your hand.

It’s got lots of wires for easy hookup too.

title: Love these
text:
This is probably my third or fourth digital photo frame.

They’re awesome for friends and family - I send them pictures all the time and they just upload right to their frames. No need to keep sending hard copies of photos - this make it so easy for family to have the nicest and latest pictures of my kids

title: Super sturdy
text:
Love that you can use as many as you need and change sizes, and love that they send you zip ties to attach them with.

Overall seem sturdy and nice for parties

title: Nice clock
text:
Nice bright numbers that are easy to see.

The radio works well and I like that it and separate controls for alarm volume and radio volume.

Snooze button is a good size to hit quickly as well. Plugs in with a standard usb.

title: Super strong
text:
I tried this with my kids tablet (8” android tablet). This held it without issue. The arm is very stiff and strong - it locked the tablet in without issue.

The clamp is easy to adjust as well and worked without issue to hold it onto my countertop

title: Nice colors
text:
Colors are very nice and what attracted me to pick these chargers over the 10,000 others on Amazon.

The extra rubber around the connecting is nice as well for extra durability

title: Good value - need practice using
text:
Cool device overall. It can hookup to a phone, but was a bit challenging with a case on my phone (kept holding down the buttons). You will be able to figure it out though once you play with it a bit.

It fits well in your hand though and has good picture quality.

title: Case offers a lot of protection
text:
I’ve been collecting a few “kids” tablets lately because they’re basically the same internals as an adult tablet, but have a crazy case.

I’ve got a 2 and 5 year old who play silly games on them - they’re great for a few apps (especially kid apps). The case offers a lot of protection as well to ensure the tablet stays safe when the kids drop it (and they do!)

title: Worked well for my new laptop
text:
I got my friend a laptop for her office and she wanted a stand with it. This has been great.

It’s lightweight and works well. Holds the laptop without an issue and allows for much easier utilization.

title: Great value laptop
text:
Got this laptop for my friend who manages a gymnastics gym. She needed an office laptop for light administrative work, like email, Microsoft office and general web browsing.

Overall this laptop works great for her. It’s met all her needs. It’s better than the laptop she was using previously and offers more functionality for an office environment than a tablet does.

She liked the quick boot up time and responsive operating system. Internal hardware seems pretty well suited for this type of work.

title: Nice cable
text:
There are 10,000 hdmi cables out there on Amazon. I picked this one because of braided cable cord which makes maneuvering it (and hiding it) very easy.

I’ve ordered cables before from other places, and they’ve come damaged, but these arrived perfect - seller was smart enough to put a plastic cover over the connection pieces. Great idea for safe shipping

title: Held my phone great
text:
I got this for my workouts and a way to mount my phone to my bike.

Action mount is simple to put together. It's very versatile allowing me to mount my phone or action camera in portrait or landscape mode.

The magnet mount is strong and i was able to securely attach to surfaces.

title: Great for a Mac book
text:
This type c Ethernet adapter adds all the useful ports that my MacBook is missing.

I can plug in my Ethernet cable for faster internet and a USB port to plug in my extra keyboard and memory stick.

It’s small and lightweight making it easy to travel to and from the office with.

title: Nice speaker
text:
Turn this on and you’ll see immediately that is a solid speaker with some power. I’ve bought a few items from this brand and it’s been very good so far. They make good speakers at an affordable price.

This has a huge rubber guard to protect the charging ports from water. This makes me feel safe about it being in the shower. The suction cup screws onto the back easy enough but took some force to stick to the wall.

Lights are nice and bright. Nice effect. Has a band on the back too so you can hold it easy if you’re moving with it.

title: Great for kids or cosplayers!
text:
[[VIDEOID:311480c99286c6d19bddbe73d0595f11]] I got my five year old son a light saber a few weeks ago and he loves it. My 2yr old then of course wants one! I found this one and it was perfect. It’s shorter than a standard sword, so amazing for kids of toddler stature! It would also go great for a cosplayer who wants a “short sword” light saber to partner with a full length. Or you can combine two of these together for a staff (think about Darth Maul).

This is super easy to use. Just hit the power button and it turns on. Tap some more and it easily changes color. Really nice functionality.

Plastic feels sturdy. This won’t break easy. Don’t go crazy in a light saber battle but if you want to cosplay or make cool videos for YouTube, this is a really nice option for you!

title: Battery charging dock for two batteries
text:
This is the second camera of this style I bought for my friend. I love the 90s look of these - very retro feeling. He is a music technology and band teacher at a local high school. He used these cameras when he teaches to help make videos and cool projects with his students. He was very happy with the quality and battery life of this camera.

Also important to note is that docking station can charge two batteries. This is great to keep the camera working as long as possible.

title: Nice size speakers
text:
Really great size speakers. We’ve all got a lot on our desks, so these were nice to have so slim.

It easily plugged into my laptop. Usb and audio went right in and it powered right now. Looks great.

title: Very comfortable
text:
Overall these are very comfortable headphones. I like the idea of bone conduction. I didn’t know anything about it but they’re pretty cool. It doesn’t sit in your ear like a normal headphone but sits outside it.

I was able to pair Bluetooth without issue. It’s a very simple process. You can also load music directly it seems. When you first turn them on, it plays a nice song - this must be from the onboard memory. Hit the power button once again and it’ll switch the Bluetooth mode. I hooked up my phone and was listening to audible within seconds.

Quality is good. It’s nice nothing having anything in your ear but still does offer noise cancellation. They stayed in place well too.

title: Daughter loves it
text:
[[VIDEOID:ed232c9c5d414bb7bb99fd775f315ecc]] Seems like this is an adult tablet in a soft pink case, and that’s awesome!

The hardware here seems to be similar to what you’d get in an “adult” tablet, not a kids one - so this has some solid power and works pretty well with kids apps. There is very little lag or downtime.

The soft pink case is great. My daughter is 2 and of course drops everything. So it’s really nice to have this for protection. We also really like the kick stand in the back for added feature and function.

Screen quality seems very nice as well and it handles kids games without any issue.

title: Comfortable
text:
My friend drives her e-scooter from jersey city to Manhattan and back for work. I got this for her to help her stay safe.

It’s very comfortable and fits well. I liked the safety features that it provides such as the reflector in the back.

Comes with a lot of accessories and even a camera ! It also has the smart options like Bluetooth which are very important.

title: These have nice range
text:
I got these as a gift for my buddy so we could chat while at work and be ridiculous. Well happy to say that these work, and work well!

We tested a range of 1500 feet in a suburban neighborhood. From my friends house to a local ice cream shop - multiple blocks away, across houses, backyards and busy roads. They worked great.

We also checked around the property - top level of a house and down 5 floors into the basement. It worked again, and worked well.

Definitely think these are nice walkie talkies

title: Compact and quiet
text:
[[VIDEOID:a7131e4f64fc285608434af3dbec0ff2]] I like this keyboard a lot. I got it to replace my Logitech keyboard that I’ve loved for years but the “r” key stopped working !

I added some pictures so you can see the difference. This keyboard is much more compact and takes up less desk space, which is great (desk space is always at a premium!). It’s quiet and seems to work very well.

I’d say I’ve got medium to large sized hands and the mouse is comfortable. Fits very well.

title: Great for outside work
text:
Was wearing these when taking down Christmas decorations and listening to an audio book.

My neighbor thought it was ignoring him but I just didn’t hear him - these have good noise cancellation. Sound quality was great too.

title: Great for little kids
text:
A few things stand out for me about this tablet.

It comes pre-setup with a kids profile. That makes it easy and made me feel better about handing this to my 2 year old right out of the box.

Also, it charges fast. 50% in under an hour and is great because my kid isn’t happy when it’s not charged !

Downloading apps is easy, just like on a regular tablet.

Overall great for young kids. The case helps protect it from dropping too!

title: Easy install on my MacBook
text:
Wanted a simple camera for my MacBook. This clipped on and installed easy.

The integrated lens cover is a very nice touch. I like that a lot for the times I don’t want a camera but may have it on accidentally.

Picture quality seems good - works for general classroom and zoom meetings

title: Bass time with the mega bass mode
text:
This is loud right out of the box, which is awesome. Then try mega bass mode to really kick it up a notch.

Side lights are a nice touch as well and controls are easy to use

title: Small but mighty
text:
This is a modern take on an old school design. I thought it was going to be some massive camera like from the 90s but it was small! Fit right in my friends hand no problem.

Design looks the same - flip out screen, microphone on top - but way smaller and packed full of modern technology.

title: Powered like an adult tablet
text:
This tablet might have a nice kids case but don’t let that fool you. It’s powerful and fast!

Setup was very easy. Login with google and you’re done.

It’s very responsive and downloaded a bunch of games very quickly.

My son loves it - spent all morning playing games. Lots of storage too. We downloaded a ton of games and it was only at 25%

Very happy with it overall

title: Great set
text:
Got this set for a friend and he was immediately impressed with the quality of the cameras and the overall construction of them. He just bought a new house and this was a gift for him, as he expressed interest in wanting safety cameras around his property.

They feel strong and like they’ll survive outside. Wireless is a bug plus for me as I don’t want to deal with that when installing!

title: Wish I had this years ago !
text:
I used to have an old HP laptop that would always overheat. Your lap would be a furnace and the fans would get over worked and couldn’t keep the laptop cool. I wish I had this.

I just got a new laptop and immediately bought this stand as well. I want to keep the base cool when I am working at my desk. It fits the laptop perfectly and will allow for much more comfortable use.

title: I like this a lot
text:
Never had a 2 in 1 laptop before, so this is pretty cool. All the ease of use of a tablet but also the feel and power of a laptop.

I opened the box and the computer easily powered on. Hold the power button and it turns right on.

Pick your language and the setup begins. Cortana kicks on right away and helps guide you along the entire process.

The screen is nice and bring. Very good quality I think for general work use and internet browsing.

Connecting to the keypad is easy - it magnetically catches very easy. Kickstand in the back helps hold it like a laptop.

Overall this is very nice

title: Not sure length is accurate
text: Maybe I should put a tape measurer to this, but it doesn’t feel like 4ft. It felt short for what I wanted it to do (floor to a bit over counter height which is 3ft standard).

title: Make sure you find studs!
text:
Make sure you’ve got a good stud finder or know now to anchor. No one wants an expensive TV to fall and the mount only works if you install it correctly!

Now in terms of a mount, this is fine. It does the job when you install correctly. Got a new TV from black Friday ? Get this mount. It’s meant for two studs which I think makes it more safe. It’s got tilt functionality which I also like a lot. My living room has glare so the tilt functionality is very nice.

title: Works great
text:
Got a really nice wifi projector a few weeks ago and wanted a stand for it. Also thought I could use it for my laptop when working.

This was an easy to setup and assemble projector stand. Works like it says it will and seems sturdy. I like the pullout side tray as well - really nice addition for a mouse

title: Love that it has a stand
text:
I loved that this came with the stand cover. Makes it so much easier to use.

I want this for a portable tv basically. I want to plug in a fire stick to the USB adapter (which is great that they provide it ! ) and then watch tv on the go or in my outdoor kitchen.

This seems like it’ll be great. It’s lightweight and easy to love. Very simple and exactly what I think I need.

title: Strong base
text:
I just got a laptop for my dad and wanted to get him a stand too.

This one seems very sturdy and the stand has an Allen wrench you use to loosen and set it in place. I liked this feature as it made me feel more confident in the stand staying still and not falling (which would break the expensive laptop!)

title: Nice for grandparents
text:
After getting this for my mom, I also got wifi frame for my in laws. These things are great for grandparents who want the latest pictures of their grand kids!

It’s easy to download an app, hook it up and load the images to your frame. The free memory card was nice too. You load 9 photos at a time which is a little annoying but once they’re on, it works great. The frame is very fast and responsive to touch too. I was shocked at how easy this was !

title: Very easy to use
text:
I got this for my mother who is not a techie person. She needs something simple and easy.

This seemed to fit the bill. The instructions are very clear that you just need to download an app, connect it to the frame and you can add pictures. This is great because I can keep my moms frame updated easily now.

The packaging was nice but said merry Christmas. Wish it didn’t as this was a Hanukkah gift.

title: Very bright
text:
My friends run a very popular energy drink review show. They’ve made over 100 videos and wanted nice lighting for their studio. As a fan of the show, I bought these for them to help elevate their production level.

Upon assembling, we found the stands don’t collapse. That isn’t an issue for us but just a heads up. Immediately we noticed how bright they were though. And they’ve also got a lot of color changing options that make them really cool.

Also, the bendable arms are great and definitely a reason I picked these. Gives them a lot of flexibility.

title: Great decoration
text:

title: You must configure to use
text: You will have to configure a second keyboard option.  This is easy and instructions are all over the web telling you how you can switch on-the-fly between keyboards.  The instructions are OS based, so instructions will differ for say Win 10 and Win 7.  Note the keyboard delivered to me was Latin American specific, so I pick Panama, Latin American as my second keyboard.  I can click on a desktop icon to switch between it and my regular English keyboard.  There are no instructions, but let me explain how some of this works.  The key to the right of the letter "P" has the accent and the diaeresis  (double dots).  For an accent you hold left Alt key down while pressing that key.  It will do nothing until you next press another letter and it will add the accent to it, á.  For the diaeresis, hold Shift and then that key.  The next letter you type will have the double dots.  For keys with a third or alternate character, hold the "AltGR" key while pressing the key with the extra character (@^`¬). Some of the other characters are just regular keys, such as ñ, ¿,¡.  I hope this helps.  Please note that I was able to buy a Microsoft wireless Spanish keyboard... really nice one, for less money.

title: Really like it so far
text:
I haven't had this for very long yet, so I can't comment on longevity, but so far I like it. I take it for granted that there will be some sacrifices when using this type of mouse, I just don't expect to get the same flexibility and usability in terms of various buttons and their placements, so I can't really knock it for being a bit worse in that area than some regular, non-ergonomic options. It works very well and the buttons are easy to click and have a nice "click" to them (unlike cheaper ones). Of course, it takes some time to get used to an upright mouse if you haven't used one before, but after a while it becomes easy/natural.

Regarding the wrist angle, I had some wrist pain and in the past I'd used a cheaper upright ergonomic mouse to help. This is not carpal tunnel, I get joint inflammation on the top side of my wrist, so it may be a bit unusual.
When my old ergonomic mouse broke I decided to try a more expensive one in hopes it will last longer. I can't provide any definitive conclusions on whether this particular aspect of my "treatment" really does anything. My ultimate conclusion is that while treating with other things (e.g. braces, compression, cold or hot), using an alternate device sometimes to change the stress points probably doesn't hurt. Sometimes when going back to use my normal mouse, just putting my hand into position seems to cause some strain, so I think this upright position is helping some. But my experience is that if I use anything for too long, I'll find some joint and/or muscle getting stressed. I'm concerned that this upright mouse position may not be as good for my elbow. So my conclusion is mix it up to spread out the strain rather than hammering on a single weak area, and try to be more careful in the future to start treatment sooner, when I see the early warning signs of strain, before it gets bad.

title: Click Sensitivity Can Be a Probelm
text: The shape seems ok for relieving wrist pain.  I used this mouse for a while and then when my pain went away (the mouse may have helped but it took a while to heal and I was doing other treatments so I can't really say) I went back to a regular mouse.  I started using it again about a week ago when I started having some pain again, and now the primary buttons don't work at all. However, even back when I was using it the first time I recall that I had issues with clicks registering at times.  The main issue is with the primary left and right buttons which are the ones I mainly use.  I can't really comment on the other buttons.

title: About what you'd expect for the price
text:
When my much more expensive Bluetooth on-ear headphones broke I was a bit frustrated and decided to go back to something cheaper. As expected, this product is less comfortable and clearly uses cheaper materials and construction, but I can't really complain given the price. The sound quality is fine as far as I can tell. The battery life is decent but noticeably shorter than my previous headphones. Also, the low battery warning is a very annoying loud series of beeps that repeats periodically until you charge it. So if you just want to listen for 5 more minutes or get through the last couple of minutes of that video and then charge it, well too bad, because the beeps are going to annoy the **** out of you until you charge it. Also, the pictures in the instructions were not clear to me at all, and it took me a while to find the charging port (you have to tilt one of the earphones to reveal the port which is otherwise hidden behind the headband).

Also, unlike my previous headphones, this one does not work well with my tablet's media volume sync (when the headphones are turned on they always revert to a default volume, they don't remember the last volume used), so I had to turn sync off to avoid constantly having to recalibrate the volume of the headset relative to the tablet.

title: In terms of audio performance these seem good. They are a bit uncomfortable to wear for ...
text:
In terms of audio performance these seem good. They are a bit uncomfortable to wear for longer periods of time, e.g. more than say 45 minutes (rough approximation) and they start to hurt my ears a bit. I do have asymmetrical ears, one has a larger fold on the top than the other, this could be a factor in the comfort (along with possibly other head/ear size/shape differences among people). As a result of this discomfort alone it is hard for me to give them more than 3 stars. I found the best way for me to wear them when I am not on the move is in reverse, with the neck bar over my chin. There is enough tension to keep them on as long as I am basically just lying back or reclining, and in that configuration they don't hurt my ears.

Another con is the type-C USB connector. Yes it is mentioned down in the wall of text of the product page so perhaps it is my fault for not noticing. But to me there is no excuse for any product of this nature not to use a standard micro-USB connector. Now I have to make sure I keep track of this cable for this device which is the only one of this type that I have, since all the other use micro-USB. I can't just plug it in to all the other micro-USB cables I have lying around my apartment.

I'm also not getting any kind of audible low battery warning, which other similar headsets always had.

The other functions such as the equalizer and locator app are fine/nice, though honestly I don't really use them.

title: they are comfortable for the most part
text: They work well, battery charge seems to last for a decent amount of time even after more than a year of almost daily use, they are comfortable for the most part, range seems good.  The way they wrap around the back of the neck makes it difficult to wear them while lying down or reclining, e.g. head propped up on a pillow or couch arm, because the little arch/arm that connects the two earpieces will hit against whatever is behind you making it uncomfortable.  I've managed to solve that by wearing them upside down so the arch goes under my chin when lying down, though they don't fit as snug that way and it may not work for some people, it also rotates the buttons into a different place relative to normal, and I cannot really eat with the arch under my chin. I then added both a Diggz Xenon build (for RD & Trakt) and the Xanax build (via an apk). We each have RD (real debrid) and Trakt. You can find more info regarding them and how to add builds via the Internet. Both these builds are pretty good. Note:when you follow the directions to install them and they say "Force Close" in Kodi remember to go back to Settings>>Apps from main screen and Force Close Kodi there and clear Cache before reopening it. Much to my surprise,  this is a great sd card.  It works just as well as my other one,  but I saved a lot of money by going with the Amazon brand.

title: Great sound quality
text: I have a echo flex in my bathroom due to a lack of space.  It works just like my dot, but the sound quality is terrible because it is so small.  I bought this to use in my shower so I could hear my music clearly.  I am amazed by how good the sound is.  I can turn it up really loud if I want,  but I really just wanted to be able to hear it over the shower noise.  It is also super easy to install and connect to my echo.  The Alexa picked it up right away and it automatically connects each time I turn it on.  This is so much more convenient than my other Bluetooth devices that I have to reconnect each time with to my phone.  I was a little concerned about the clip, but it holds well,  too.

title: User friendly
text: [[VIDEOID:782255f0c5d8a3a165bc5cfe3121852e]] I bought this for my backyard. I'm a wheelchair user so I won't go to the door unless I know who it is so this is very handy for someone like me. It was very easy to operate and I was able to install it on my own. I really appreciate that it is plugs in so I don't have to worry about charging it.  The app is very user friendly,  too.

title: What a hoot!
text: I bought this for my sister who is a practicing Wiccan.  She worships Diana so owls are a big deal to her.  This is a work of art.  It looks beautiful and has some heft to it.  It seems durable and well made.  I was a little concerned that it would affect the sound quality of her echo,  but it sounds exactly like it did before.

title: Lots of outlets
text: I needed this for my many, many kitchen gadgets.  It has a whopping 12 outlets, plus 4 USB ports.  I even have outlets to spare now.  I really appreciate that it doesn't take up a lot of counterspace.  Another cool feature is that the outlets are a snug fit if you know what I mean.  You really need to push them in there with a bit of force, but this insures that I won't accidentally yank out one of the cords.

title: Great for ring lights
text: I bought this for my old ring light.  It came with a little clip, but it was too awkward to work with.  This is a much better option.  It screwed right into the top screw and feels very secure.  I clamped it to the side of my desk which is much safer than sticking it on my laptop.  The top part can be adjusted to any angle due to the ball joint.  You can also adjust the height to whatever you need.

title: Terrible
text:
I have used tiles several times and I love them. I decided to try this because it was cheaper, but it's awful.
It doesn't to connect to the wifi. The smart life app is user friendly and works well with my other devices so it is definitely a problem with this device rather than an issue with the app. It's not loud enough either. Even if it worked, it would be useless if you can't hear it.

text: [[VIDEOID:52278f09f20c0355edc6c212b0c5a941]] I was a little concerned that this wouldn't fit properly or would be too flimsy to actually protect my tablet,  but I decided to try it anyway. I really like that the cover can be folded into a stand to prop it up on.

title: Easy to use
text: [[VIDEOID:f3253f4f1268938cdb17b628a210bc70]] I bought these for a recent camping trip.  I wanted to do some bird watching while the family went on a hike so I needed some good binoculars.  These are a great option because they are good quality at a bargain price.  They are waterproof so you can use them near water.  They also have night vision so you can use them in low light as well.  They come with caps to protect the lenses and eye pieces.  They are easy to adjust to get the right fit.

title: Small, but powerful
text: [[VIDEOID:e42c650287548516d25d6a6606b7310e]] I like to sit outside and listen to music while the kids play.  I wanted something that was louder than my phone speaker, but still small enough to be portable.  This is very easy to use.  It connects to my Bluetooth quickly and the sound quality is great.  You can also insert a USB drive or a SD card to play downloaded music.  It's small enough to fit in my pocket and it has a handy strap for carrying.

title: Great for on the go shots
text: Obviously this isn't enough for a huge project,  but it's great for everyday use.  It's very lightweight so I can keep it my purse until I need it for on the go shots.  It's compact enough to put on top of a regular size camera without throwing it off balance or feeling awkward.  There are different color options, but my favorite is warm white.  You can also adjust the brightness.

title: So pretty
text: I bought this for my baby sister.  She loves anything pink and girly so this fits in great with her decor.  It's a nice medium sized mouse pad so it's good for a regular laptop.  It has a rubber backing so it doesn't slip and slide around.

title: Just as good as airpods
text: [[VIDEOID:50a509ca92ee072cbb2d2a4c48213b4d]] I love my wireless ear buds, but they are too expensive for me to share with my son.  When I saw these at such a good price,  I decided to buy him a pair.  I wasn't expecting much, but the sound quality and battery life is as good as my airpods.  I really appreciate the case.  I think it will protect them, but also keep them from getting lost.  I also like that you can charge them directly from the case.  It's very convenient that I can charge the earbuds several times before I need to recharge the case.

title: Powerful

He just plugs it into the cigarette lighter and it circulates cool air.  It feels really nice and it doesn't make any noise.  I really appreciate that it comes with mounting strips.

title: Easy to use
