title: Easy to use
text: I bought this for my son's school laptop.  He was using the regular overhead light, but it left a glare and a reflection on the screen.  This is a much better option.  It fits directly on the laptop like a booklight.  It lights up the screen without leaving a glare.  It works really well and I like that I can change the color from a cool to a warm white if I want.

title: Super easy to install
text:
[[VIDEOID:17027ba80b586ba4c6eb0ff2f587e618]] I am a bit of a helicopter mom so I am naturally worried about my son driving. This is a good way to monitor his driving habits so I know that he is being safe. I also think it serves as a reminder to follow the rules because mom is watching.

It was super easy to install and the camera itself is pretty self explanatory. The mounting portion works really well and it feels very secure. The best part is that it shows what is recording on the screen. This way you can adjust it as needed so you always get the perfect shot.

title: Great for gaming
text: I bought this for my husband who loves playing online games.  He recently started using 2 monitors by putting one on a riser, but this is much better.  You can move or tilt each one independently so you can get the exact angle you want.  It was very easy to set up and seems sturdy.  I'm not worried about the monitors falling off or being damaged.

title: Clean up those messy cords
text: I bought these for my lights under my kitchen cabinets.  They are a series of round lights connected by individual cords, but the cords look so messy hanging down.  This is the perfect solution because it allowed me to zip tie the cords neatly and stick them to the cabinets,  up and out of the way.  There are openings on each side so I can wrap the zip tie around horizontally or vertically.  The foam adhesive holds well,  but can be removed if needed.

title: Very user friendly
text: [[VIDEOID:6e72e181d122a7c468d1cdb80368edcc]] I bought this so I could take some nice pictures of the super moon. title: Good for ring lights
text: I bought this to hold my ring light.  I recently started teaching my cousin to crochet over zoom and I needed some extra light for her to see everything clearly.  This is a great way to mount it up and out of the way.  Because of the ball head, I can tilt it to get the angle I need.  It clamps onto my table easily,  but isn't so harsh that it could damage my table.  When I'm not using it,  I can remove it and put it away in under a minute.

title: Very simple to use
text: [[VIDEOID:46e1cb6a53fe991701460d40a1ba6c0f]] I bought this for my husband to use at work.  He is the kind of guy who will fiddle with something for half an hour trying to figure something out rather than just reading the directions.  Thankfully,  this was pretty self explanatory.  In the video you can see how it normally remains mostly quiet.  However,  once the mic is pointed at his phone,  it picks it up and reacts immediately.  The alarm sound isn't annoying or too loud, but it's unmistakable what it is.  There were no other bugs in the room when it was searched, but I have no doubt that it would have reacted if there had been.  I also appreciate that the mic has to be pointed directly at it to pick it up.  If it just reacted as soon as it was near something,  it would be hard to find out exactly where it is. title: Marginal at best
text:
I waited several weeks before I did this review, I really wanted to get familiar with these earbuds and do a fair review on these. I really wanted to love these, but I don’t. They’re very hard to turn up and down, in fact, I have not mastered this at all. I’ve read the instructions over and over and over again and still I’m not able to turn them up or down, only on a fluke. Noise cancellation works part time. It’s not supposed to be rocket science. I like the beige color it’s very nice. I like the fact that the case keeps the earbuds charged and the case has a nice feel to it and you can just toss it in your bag and not have to worry about them being ready.
The other problem I’ve had is thst my beats flex headphones don’t want to hook back up to my watch Apple Watch for some reason since I’ve had these even if the new earbuds are not connected to the device. I have not figured out what’s going on with that? If the case even gets opened a little bit it will instantaneously go right into earbud mode. It’ll interrupt your phone calls or whatever you have going on with whatever device your using or any device in range. It’s a tad bit frustrating. Because I can’t control the sound on these among other issues, they’re not getting a whole lot of use right now. I think I will contact the store seller and find out if they can send me another pair possibly there’s something wrong with this particular pair? I will update my review and let you know, but for now I do not recommend this item.

title: Nice, just not my style.
text:

It is a large bag. There is a center padded insert to carry your laptop. I also like that there are a ton of pockets. The zippers all worked great. Nice because it will go with anything and even with a more dressy look such as for the office just as well as for the gym on the way home. Easy to wipe clean. Multi pockets internally. title: replacement for original
text: Purchased as a replacement for original cord Samsung galaxy 8.9 tablet. Charges and fits just like the original cord, super long cord too. This is such an odd charger that I was glad to find a replacement.

title: Excellent protection
text:
My husband ordered this case. I love it also. He needed something to survive the work day and regular wear. The case is nice. It certainly offers excellent protection (generally we purchase otter but wanted something a bit different). This case adds to size and weight but doesn't create bulk. Creates excellent seals.

There is no built in screen protection. Purchase a Moshi matte protector. (these are washable and reusable)

The case uses hex, or allen, screws. While this is awesome, it will not make for quick removal. This case also creates an intense seal so once you take out the screws ( we had to get a different ipad) you will have to pry it off (carefully!).

Little things that are slightly annoying is that the hinge scratches very easy, the earphone jack is hard to get just right to keep in place.

title: No bubble, no glare, smoothe
text:
This protector is very nice, certainly worth the price. (note that if you purchase in a mobile store they run about $35.)

This is no glare but keeps a crisp screen, some matte protectors can dull colors, this one does not.

It is reusable. It is washable. It is the easiest ever to apply.

This protector goes on with NO bubbles, if you are off set a bit you can remove and reapply. I have never had a screen protector so fluid in application. I also like that the screen remains ultra sensitive and there is no interference.

What is also great is that this covers the entire front, not just the actual working screen, the black border blends perfect and I can not tell I even have anything on it.

This protector doesn't print either. Some printing is visible when screen is off but not once lit up. Easy to wipe clean and feels silky under fingertip.

Very happy with this product.Certainly worth the price, if you normally buy inexpensive 3 pack...don't! I used to do that but not anymore. Buy one and done! No bubbles, washable, reusable!

title: Unbelievablely strong clear reception
text:
After a bad experience with another flat amp antenna I purchased the leaf for just over $50 .
It picks up 19 stations in the "low country" around a lot of tall pine trees.(20 is the max number of stations in a 60 mile radius here with any antenna according to the TV manufacturer).

You can paint the ant/ cables to match the walls. Comes with push pins for walls and Velcro for wall or window if you want them.Also has a plug into TV for the amp or you can plug into the wall like I did so it isn't hampered by the surge protector.

I get ABC, CBS,NBC,FOX,THIS,3 PBS stations, 3 Christian channels,a Spanish channel, WE,GET,MY,BOUNCE,YOU TOO, one music video channel and one other. The reception on all (but 2) is exceptionally strong with no blips in power even if you cannot put it in a window. I have mine hanging behind my curtain and most channels get 90-100% station strength almost constantly when 35%, even 30% will give you the station clear enough to watch a program with very few "blips" in reception.

I am enjoying not adjusting the Rabbit ear antenna (when I watched certain channels) even though it worked *good* enough for the money.

If you had another antenna before that only picked up 5-13 channels (for exp.) and you switch to a more powerful one like this, remember to unplug your TV a good minute before re- auto programming ( I forgot at first myself) as some TVs seem to "remember" how many it gets and stops at that number.

No need for an ugly outside antenna with this one.

When I use my hair dryer or turn on another "power draw", it doesnt get the interference the previous amplified antenna had, so probably uses less electricity, yet pulls in more stations.
I'm very happy with it. I get more channels than my basic cable had that I enjoy watching also.

title: The band has a nice plushy cushion over the head
text:
The MHBT0545W is a simple blah, as much as you might expect, given the kind of reviews, number consumer responses, manufacture details-specs, and the retailers you would generally find these at. While trying to understand what market these are aimed towards, given the MSRP, you would think Memorex or the OEM would have given these more respect.

Packaging aside, what you find them here on Amazon, price wise is really what they are worth, or a bit less. So with that I am not that impressed. The shrink wrap is not every sophisticated and they very well might have been rewrapped. The sleeve cover slides off and reveals front flap to the headphones which sit in a velvety plastic tray. Under neath is a gold tipped red flat wire aux cable, which reminds me of the cable on the Sony MDR-V55 head phones. Also included is a micro USB charging cable. Although I had expected it, there was no carrying pouch. While doing my research I was under the impression a pouch was included. There is a 90 day warranty card, and a fold out instruction sheet, in both English and Spanish. The headphones seem to have been fully charged, as they powered up out of the box, and when I charged them they stopped charging very quickly.

They sound okay. A bit too bass for me and not clear at that. However because they have an adjustable equalizer, I prefer the treble boost setting, the most. They are not "over the ear" but more or less on the ear for me. They do well at isolating sound, the cups are soft, but the headphones keep my ears and the surrounding area warm or hot. The band has a nice plushy cushion over the head, and the cups are quite tight on my ears. I will have to see what I can do about that. The buttons are labeled well, but until I get used to them I have to take the phones off and look. So with that in mind, they are not intuitive. The lower cost model of Memorex headphones have touch controls in obvious locations on the outside ear cup - for comparisons sake, I am wondering what is up with that? These are $70 ear phones and more difficult to use.

I was able to pair them with my laptop and phone, and while connected at the same time, will switch to the source of the audio, automatically. They will not auto connect to your second device, only to the first one - which is the last device you used or paired, then you have to go to the second one and manually select connect. There is a slight gap in audio, as it detects and plays the source of sound, or start your source.

There are no voice prompts that I have noticed. The headphones have basic alert tones which do not seem very loud. Some customers will understand and appreciate what I am writing here. I will have to come back to this part and update as I get more use out of them.

Double clicking the play/pause/power button activates SIRI. However SIRI does not understand anything I say and when she speaks it's the worst quality I have ever heard. This is not particularly important, as SIRI is not an advertised feature. I will get back to this in a moment.

Conclusion, these headphones are using circuitry and a chipset, meant for $80+ headphones. Although not mentioned, they are using a CSR 8645 chipset which by specification, can multi-point connect to two phones or other combination of bluetooth audio sources. They do not advertise what codecs are supported but again by definition the chipset is meant to support Apt-X, Low Latency, and ACC, please see [...] for reference. I am led to believe, they use the chip for it's most basic features, Bluetooth 4.1, half of the available slots meant for equalizer settings, and nothing else. SIRI sounding as bad as she does, is a victim of this basic configuration, and I am surprised she actually does anything at all.

The phones look good, sound okay and worth the amount of money I paid for them. However I will be buying something else at some future date, as the bluetooth headphone market matures.

(I will be editing for grammar other mistakes)

title: Great memory - with a little advice on installation. Search YouTube!
text:
Fast delivery, and it gave my wife's netbook a much needed boost. I wish I could put more in, but 2GB is the max.

Okay, for some advice, the Acer keyboard has these tabs to hold it in. All the tabs can be slid off the keyboard, for it's removal. However the upper left tab, which no one talks about, does not move at all. It's physically apart of the plastic mold, therefore can not be moved. To get the keyboard off, you will have to masterfully maneuver past this last tab. The keyboard is very thin, and bendable. You risk damaging it. So please use some care in removing that last corner, and don't spend any time trying to press the tab in, because it can't be moved. A suggestion, is to press down on the top of the netbook, with your hand, where the battery should be, (but removed), and leverage that tab away from the keyboard. title: There is no such thing has burning in your headphones! Stop it. It either sounds right the first time or it doesn't at all.
text:
I was trying to choose. Sony MDR-V6 Sony MDR-7506, ATH-M30, ATH-M40... I looked at everything. I found a youtube channel, which plays direct from CD sample, then crossover in sync to various model headphones resampling the sound from the each headphone as it's placed over a foam head. - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sj69-mWHV3E - The point is, they are trying to reproduce what is heard. Also, I found another youtube channel of a guy who shows various headphones sampled through a graphic analyzer, showing the frequency response.

All headphones add something to the signal. So what you hear on one model isn't the same, with another. But of all the head phones, the ATH-M40x was identical in sound reproduction to the original music. You couldn't tell the difference. Why is this important? Two reasons, if you are an audio engineer, you will have a truer sound, what you hear, is what you will get. It goes both ways, what you listen to, will be what the sound engineer intended for you to hear.

For music with base, it has good presence, and you can hear details that sound muddy on other head phones. I have been listening to a lot of head phones. You do understand muddy and clarity, once you hear it.

With that said, and having spent some time, in store sampling, (note: I must say that the Sonys are really good too. I tried and liked the MDR-V55 as well. It's a DJ headset so it's a bit more base. I felt they were very clear and better than the MDR-X05 hands down.)

The ATH-M40x, has removable cables. They are field repairable. And you can choose between three different cables, although two come in the box.

They are son tested and approved. Now I have to keep them locked up, joking. They are well built. Some say the ATH-M50x is better. It's also said the M50x sound the same as last year's model, and the M40x sound as good as last year's M50 model too. Which is it? The M40x is specifically flat sounding for audio engineering. The M50x is targeted for the audiophile, with a V shape EQ. The M40x is in the sweet spot, unless you have money to burn.

They are a bit tight, but this may be alleviated by exchanging the ear pads with velour pads. This exchange compromises the sound profile a little bit, but makes them more comfortable. You be the judge. I am still waiting to do it myself.

title: Great Little Device of its Genre: Highly Recommended
text:
I have to say that I love this little guy almost as much as I loved my Withings Activite--which was a lot. But, my husband bought me a gold watch, and you can't wear two watches, so I switched to the GO on my coin pocket. It seems to accurately capture my steps and the e-ink screen is awesome: totally visible from any angle, which is really nice when you just want to glance down and see how you're doing (which, for me, is what I want most of the times I'm looking at it at all). I also vastly prefer Withing's "percent reached of your set goal" indicator (as also on the Withings Activite and their lesser watches) rather than a numerical display of steps, and I loathe numerical digital watch/clock displays, so the e-ink analog timeface is a wonderful touch. I've never actually looked at the thing to learn the time (cf. "I'm wearing a wristwatch," earlier) but it's classy--IMHO--that Withings has maintained the analog style and not just cheaped it with numbers.

The only thing it doesn't have that I might have added is a second indicator when you sweep your step goal twice (or more times) within the day. I'm very fond of how the central icon turns into a star after the first 100%; changing to a "2" or "3" or something other would have been nice for multiple sweeps.

Finally, the only constructive feedback I'll give is that the recent software update to the Activite made it sync almost imstantaneously with my iPhone SE, while the software in the GO (or, perhaps, the Bluetooth energy level in the GO) syncs as slowly as the Activite did before the recent update. My iPhone is set to auto-lock after 30 seconds; there's no good reason why the device can't sync with the phone app in that time, when the two (GO and iPhone) are sitting next to each other, with the GO near the iPhone's "silencing" switch for maximum pickup. Sync speed was always my only constructive feedback about the Activite (other than that it doesn't come in a 14k gold case option) and sync speed is the only thing I'd suggest that Nokia and Withings continue to perfect.

Enough complaints. I'll close by saying that Withings' customer support is among the fastest and best I've experienced. Can't go wrong.

text:
For less than half the cost of a typical DAC/ Headphone AMP stack, this item gives you both in one package, saving you money on cables and space on your desk. I highly recommend this product. Customer service and post-purchase support has been wonderful!

While this performs in the top tier of products with balanced connections per ASR, it isn't truly balanced internally. The balanced connections are provided for convenience. Since you can't hear a difference or measure a difference, it doesn't matter. The engineers at Aoshida / SMSL know how to optimize a product for a price point. If you receive more enjoyment from spec sheets than the extra money in your wallet SMSL has other more expensive products to purchase that are internally balanced with very similar performance.

Great features include:
* More than enough to drive 300 ohm headphones.
* Integrated power supply, so you don't have a brick or need to find an extra USB connection.
* Included useful remote.
* Quality feeling front button.
* BT is easy to pair and fine for convenient streaming when not engaged in critical listening.

Things to keep in mind:
* Included USB cable is a bit short. You may want to purchase a longer USB input cable.

Reasons to look elsewhere:
* You need to drive a high impedance headphone, such as something with 600 ohm impedance.
* You want a DAC/AMP that is internally balanced.
* You need something portable to with a built-in battery that fits in your pocket to use on the go.
* You need your DAC/AMP to have a sub out, for ease of connection to a sub. (If using with a sub, you can normally connect the C200 to your SUB. Then, you would connect the sub to your speakers.)

text:
Pros: Fast 185MB/sec transfer speed; Provides good power; Sits flush; Package is easy to open.
Cons: My driver disk was blank; Power Cable that connects to USB Port to provide power makes your laptop look funny; USB has lots of overhead.

The diver disk included with this product was a blank CD-R, this was probably a manufacturer oversight. Thus, no driver was included. Windows 7 could not find a driver for the product automatically. Product that was sent to me has an NEC (Renesas) Chipset.

Once I found a driver this product worked great. I was able to push 180-185 MB/sec with an SSD in a USB 3.0 enclosure. Around 180MB/sec is known to be close to the top speed of the USB 3.0 certified NEC chipset. The NEC chipset is used on many motherboards to provide built-in USB 3.0 support. The same drive connected internally over SATA revision 3 (aka SATA 6.0 Gb/sec) pushes about 250 MB/sec. If you want full speed connection to a fast SSD, you are probably better off with eSATA. Obviously there is some slowdown in the conversion from going from SATA to USB. 185MB/sec is fast enough for my needs, and super fast compared to the slowness of normal USB at about 40 MB/sec. This powered a 160 GB SSD and a 500 GB HDD in an external enclosure just fine with the extra power cable attached.

title: Get it if you can
text:
After researching and reading and thinking for far too long I thought I might get one of the routers recommended by CNet; but I didn't want to spend as much as the CNet rated ones cost and I wanted something more recent to the market. I kept eyeing this one, but Amazon never seemed to have it in stock. Finally I stumbled on its availablity on Thursday. I decided to go ahead and give it a shot. It arrived on Friday so when the kids finally got off my desktop I jumed on the chance to set it up.

This is my first router. I usually know enough to do more than just the basics, so I wasn't overly concerned with set-up. I followed the quick start instructions and then put the cd in the drive to configure it. The Windows hardware wizard did the basic stuff and I used the MSI website to check everything. My netbook recognized it right away, though it wasn't named anything that I would have expected; the signal strength and the fact that it was new to the area made it clear. I still haven't got my netbook configured exactly the way I want it but I expect that's because I didn't upgrade my Windows 7 starter system.

I took the netbook upstairs, which puts me about 12 feet over and 10 feet above the router. My signal strength is 4 - 5 bars consistently. I've had a few drops, usually when I stop to read something and the keyboard is inactive. I was able to watch a movie on my netbook via Netflix, while at the same time my kids were watching cartoons via Netflix on the desktop pc. Ahhh, bliss! Next step wil be to get a cable to stream video to the tv from the netbook.

So far, I am very happy with this router and impressed that I didn't have to spend twice as much to get it!

With a little sewing to alter the nose area & shorten the Velcro plus move the earpieces around to be near my ears, this mask could be made to work, not perfectly & certainly not noise cancelling but acceptable

title: WARNING of a PROBLEM if you are using a wired headset designed for Apple products
text: I love the Amazon Echo Dot products BUT there is a problem when using a wired headset plugged into the audio out when using Bose QuietComfort 25 Acoustic Noise Cancelling Headphones for Apple devices.  The audio only works if the plug is part way inserted. It's a rather hit-or-miss process.  The same problem exists for all Amazon tablets as well. I called Amazon tech support to see if there was an adaptor to assure a perfect fit for the audio out on Amazon devices &  iPhone specific wired headsets. The answer was NO.

title: AirPods are now wearable
text: I was afraid to wear my AirPods 2 because even with an added tip, they feel out. I wound up buying the AirPods Pro just before this tip became available. Now both stay in my ears. I had tried almost every other tip on the market because I wanted to use the "Live Listening" feature

title: Good product

title: Defective audio
text: I liked the style & fit of these glasses, but I noticed a tinny sound in one ear when the audio was made louder. I contacted the company & they offered to do an exchange. Instead I chose to order a second pair of glasses to compare the audio. Just as I suspected, the audio in second pair of glasses was just as bad. These glasses are advertised as "Youth" - I would hate to think that the company was just being sloppy with Quality control because kids would be as critical as adults.

title: Finally airpods covers that work
text: I have tried all the airpods covers on the market and none worked - until these. With the Softconnect tips the airpods stay in my ears for the first time. The fit is comfortable. If you've found airpods difficult or impossible to wear, these might work for you. I just purchased the newest airpod Pro's in London. The new design does stay in my ears and has a very similar design to the Softconnect covers. The memory foam ear piece has an even better fit than the new ear pieces on the airpod Pros. Perhaps the makers of the Softconnects with make a replacement tips for the new airpod Pros. My only complaint is that you have to remove the airpod covers before putting them in the charging case, but the Softconnects are easier & quicker to put on & take off than other covers.

title: First wireless headset which stay in my ear & is comfortable!
text: I’ve tried iPods, Bose SoundSport Free & many other wireless headset - these are the FIRST TO FIT PROPERLY & stay in my ears. I wanted a headset that would work with the iphones new widget  “Live Listening”, which only works with AirPods or the Powerbeat Pro

title: Didn't work as advertised
text: I was hoping that the dots would help to hold the airpods in my ear as was indicated in the product description. They were not at all helpful.  The airpods fell out of my ears.

text: I have used chrome books for years at school and home. Recently bought a PC with windows. Hated it and bought this gem to replace it. title: Works great

I owned the previous generation of Oontz Angle, and while I loved that one, this iteration is a lot better sounding! The bass really sounds great in this device! title: lots of storage
text: I bought this for my personal backup and to put machine embroidery designs on and I love it!  It is easy to use and I find I will have plenty of room for my dense designs for a long time to come.  I would buy this again.

title: Compact reader is delightfully portable
text: This is my 4th kindle device, I still use them all for different purposes. I love the small, thin lightweight size of this one and after using it for several weeks now, it's become a favorite because it takes up so little space in my bag. The only aspect I'm not in love with yet is the pale gray background which requires an external light source to read the darker gray text. The font style and size is adjustable, it holds a charge well and reaches full capacity quickly. This is affordable, compact and holds a huge library. Just be prepared that if you are outside reading and the sky becomes dark, you will likely need to move inside where there is a lamp.

title: Better in my car than its installed speakers
text: I have gone through many Bluetooth speakers and had yet to listen to one that had such depth of sound as this Bose SoundLink Revolve.  I know it's not the first Bose SoundLink Bluetooth speaker, but it's my first and it blows away all the others that gather dust around here.  Visually similar to my Amazon Echo, I had to let Alexa know that she has a competitor in my home but reassured her that she is still loved.  I can't talk to this Bose, but each time I turn it on, a generated female voice alerts me to the battery life remaining and what device it's pairing with.  Setup took only a minute, the manual is only a few words and diagrams, and after a full battery charge, it's still going after daily use for what seems like dozens of hours.  I'm serious, I have not plugged it back in yet because I want to see what happens when the battery nears death.  I did not want to wait to write this review because I'm so impressed with the audio that is generated from this little speaker that can also withstand being carried outside without harm.  Of course, I'm not willing to test it in the rain, but have to say that my neighbors could not believe the music was coming from this little black speaker.

title: Exterior zipper is a single pull, not double as pictured
text: Ignore the photo of the black backpack if you are concerned with the zippers.  It looks like the photo, but the zipper in the exterior pocket is a single zipper, not the dual zipper pull as pictured.  I hate this, especially since the zipper opens and closes from the end opposite of the gorilla which I wanted to slip inside the exterior pocket. Being that there is no dating on the bag or any of the tags, I can't say if this is an old or new model, but I can say that it does contain the guarantee card inside one of the pockets identifying it as a genuine Kipling product.  We still have a Kipling fanny pack from decades past and it looks perfect, but I was happy to see that this black fabric is not the crinkly style, rather is a heavier textile.  It's not as heavy as canvas, so it won't add weight if this is for a child.  Know what you are getting, this model has no bottle holders or bells and whistles, just the gorilla.  The lining is a bland beige and the laptop "sleeve" has satisfactory padding on all sides, including the base.  My 15 inch laptop fits with the flap sealed and there's still room for more height and width.  If the zipper was as pictured, I would like this backpack more, but it's not and that's too bad.  It was made in China.

title: I hear more distortion than I like from these headphones
text: Unlike the Sennheiser HD 598 headphones I often use, the HD 559 does not include a 3.5mm adapter plug, so if you need one, have it or you will be unhappy should you want to use these for a laptop or other small device.  To test these, I kept my adapter in the laptop and switched between the two headphones, listening to an assortment of various tracks so I could really compare the audio elements and physical feel of the headphones.  I prefer the HD 598 headphones over this newer model and see that they are both comparable prices now because a newer model is available of the 598's.  You may prefer the HD 559's if you prefer a tinner, bass accentuated audio, but I would rather hear the differentiation between the elements of audio which I hear more clearly with the HD 598's.  The separation is simply more refined and I guess I'm spoiled. The newer 559 is cheaper than the upgraded higher end model, and i find them to be a tighter fit which becomes uncomfortable and irritating when worn for hours at a time, something that I never experienced with the others.  I think this band is stiffer, too. These produce a much less elegant sound which some may prefer, but the more I listen to these, the more I wonder if there is something wrong with them due to the pounding sound which is replicated each time I switch to them.  To avoid prejudice, I had an assistant do the switching for me as I kept my eyes closed through several songs and an audio narration.  I worked in the film and video industry and always used Sennheiser earphones, so my experience with the brand spans decades. These just don't match up, and that may just be the cause of my disappointment. They are not bad headphones, they are not great for my desires in experiencing audio in either recording or playback modes.  Of note is that the detachable long cable is nowhere near as easy to remove or insert as my other headphones which is of concern.  This set was made in China and it comes in a no frills 2 part box with a simple document written in numerous languages.

title: Adjustable inside and out, the black bag is well designed and constructed
text: By far the coolest camera bag I own, the AmazonBasics camera sling bag offers a lot to like.  The black fabric is solid and softer than I'd expected, there are several types for each section.  It is stitched perfectly and the nylon zippers each work well with pretty flat zipper pulls.  Place it on its side to unzip the main compartment, unzip the lengthy curved zipper and you have easy access to your camera and lenses by adjusting the velcro attached modular spacers as you desire.  The bottom section has a waterproof fabric hidden away inside a velcro sealed pocket, so be sure you don't miss out on discovering this feature.  There is a small handle at the top for grabbing and hitting the road or wear it across your torso, with a couple of secure straps for security.  Both are nicely contained in a small elastic band which can be moved to open them up for use.  There are a lot of nooks and crannies in this bag, much more than I was expecting.  It is well padded and the design works for me.

title: Great computer for entertainment applications
text:
Being a Mac user for decades, it has been some time since I've had the opportunity to use a Windows based computer, so I was eager to try the Windows 10 operating system on this convertible notebook computer, also a first for me. The Acer Aspire R 14 R5-471T-79YN has far exceeded my expectations in form and function, despite the learning curve I'm experiencing. I won't get into the Windows 10 system, but will say that I can definitely see the influence of the Mac operating systems on its development and I am impressed. Perhaps I like it more than many users might simply because I can't even remember the last Windows system I used being that even my remote work situations tend to not use these computers now.

The Acer is not as lightweight as a tablet, of course, but it's also not the weightiest notebook of this size, and the brushed metal texture of the case is appealing. It looks sleek and feels good when the computer is used. I find the keyboard to be very comfortable, the touchpad is positioned well and the silver edging surrounding it is a nice contrast. I do not like the position of the power button which is directly beneath the power plug, as I find that if plugged in, I have to fiddle with it to turn on the computer. The USB ports, HDMI port, SD card reader and volume control are all easily accessible and have functioned well so far in every case I've used them this week. The speakers are a little odd, but that makes sense since the convertible form of this means that when used as a tablet ,the rear speakers will face the area between the folded computer. To my surprise, I find that the sound improves in tablet form, better than when used in laptop or tented configurations. I have mine set to ask if I want to switch to tablet layout because I found that it did not always respond appropriately when set to automatic conversion. The true HD makes this a very nice system on which to watch videos and with external headphones or speaker, either cabled or Bluetooth, it becomes a great system. I would actually consider this one to be best suited for entertainment, and would imagine that it is excellent for games although I have not used it for that purpose at all. The touch screen is very responsive, but it does take some time to get accustomed to the responsiveness. The computer is very fast, very quiet, very cool (temperature), and it starts quickly. I rather like the lack of an optical drive because that keeps it quieter and lighter, yet allows me to add a peripheral drive if I want or when it is needed. I rather enjoyed streaming a movie from my Amazon Prime directly to a non-smart TV. I've used this in the kitchen in both the tablet and tent configurations using the Kindle app and much appreciated having a larger screen than when using my Kindle Fire for recipe following.

For the price, I think this is a great convertible computer which comes with a single year warranty. I intend to give this Aspire a workout and hope that I never need to discover how the Acer warranty service performs.

title: Not sure about the mileage, but we are impressed
text: Not a fan of big and bright walkie talkies, I was attracted to the Motorola T260 because of its simple grayish color and no frills appearance.  It is powered by either 3 AA batteries in each which the consumer provides or the single rechargeable NiMH battery for each which is included.  The batteries do take a very long time to charge, so have AA's on hand if you need to use this immediately.  The operating manual is well written and when followed, seems to be accurate.  Some steps to prep the devices seem to take longer than they should, but since they do work, I won't complain.  The two-way radios can be married by any one of many channels, we had no difficulty getting one pretty quickly, and the volume is audible.  This model offers weather channels which come in loud and clear, and it also allows the user to activate the iVOX feature which allows hands free operation without accessories or with additional things you can purchase separately.  The only thing I didn't care for with this pair is the "Roger" tone which was very annoying to both of us, but fortunately, I finally discovered that it can be turned off.  It helps to read the manual even if you don't think you need details.

title: My favorite desktop holder of any shape or form
text: Every once in awhile, I find a gadget that I think is wonderful and this rotatable aluminum desktop holder is one of those things.  It is sleek, simple, and it works extremely well to hold a number of devices for me in a variety of situations.  My favorite of late is using this to hold my Kindle Fire even while it is in its case.  I can slip the case flap through the opening on the bottom of the holder, put the Fire into the holder while flipping the case front over the rear of the holder.  I then can use this in the kitchen to keep my recipes from Kindle cookbooks at hand and clean, elevated from the countertop.  The holder angle can be adjusted quickly and when it is tightened, remains in position.  I love this.  A sample was provided for evaluation.

title: Blue version has even more bling than the black
text: The wallet may be marketed as a phone holder, but it is a wallet first and foremost. It is attractive and the zipper functions well, with very shiny gold colored hardware and a nice wrist strap. Aside from some stitching that I am concerned might become loose because the stitch gauge is too long, it is very well made and very utilitarian. It holds quite a bit, including a phone, making it a good accessory to carry when I don't want to take a purse or backpack with me. Since it is closed by a single surrounding zipper, I don't hear the phone if it rings unless the volume is turned to the highest and the zipper is left with an open gap. All in all, I have grown to like this wallet more and more each day.  The leather is holding up beautifully and I can't tell you how often I am asked about where to get one.  It is a really good value, too.  Sample  was provided for review.

title: If you need a privacy screen protector, this is sturdy and reversible
text:
Before receiving the Belkin True Clear Privacy Screen Protector, I watched the online video to learn about it and see how to apply the screen to my computer/s. It clearly is very straightforward and I saw no need to even look at the diagram instructions which are enclosed with the protective plastic folder, adhesive pads and beautiful bright green microfiber cloth which also works for eyeglasses.

The screen has a shiny and matte side and you can switch it to your heart's content. Since I have a MacBook Pro and a Toshiba Chromebook which both can wear this screen protector, I'm especially appreciative, and it does indeed fit both screens perfectly. I have found that with the Chromebook, I don't need to apply the little black oval strips because the protector lays perfectly against the screen.

Protecting the screen from invading eyes works as long as the beholder is not directly facing the screen because they will see whatever I see. If they are off to the side, they see a black screen. I see a greyed screen that has a majority of the brightness dulled. For simple text, I have no problem with this and like it, however when doing anything with graphics, I'm not crazy about the alteration to the appearance of the images. I'm hoping that over time I will not find myself drawn to the faint horizontal lines which appear through the protector.

As I am typing this review, there is a news report on internet privacy and a reminder that anything we post about our children to Facebook or Twitter remains for the world to see. This made me think about my idea of privacy and I realized that if someone really wants to see what is on my screen, they will. On the other hand, if you are in an environment where it is important to keep whatever is on your screen from the person/s walking into your office or room, then this protector is likely a good choice. It does what it suggests and despite the high cost, it appears to be a product with a long life. As I learned in the video, when the adhesive strips lose their stick, simply wipe them with a little scotch tape and they will be good again. There are also four extras included and I've placed mine in the plastic folder so that I won't have to search for them.

title: I use this every day
text:
My first impression was that the [[ASIN:B00NFAGZRO iPad Stand - Portable Waterproof Travel Stand For Your iPad, Tablet, Kindle, Smartphone & iPhone (Red)]] is much less flexible than I'd anticipated. Nevertheless, I've fallen in love with this little stand which is in front of me each and every day. Produced in assorted lovely colors, it holds my Samsung Galaxy S5 while out of a case or in a leather folio case that I have folded back. Because the opening is fixed, it's important that your device is not too thick to fit in the holder. It is sturdy and attractive, easy to clean if it gets dirty. These are great gifts, too.

I was provided the product for review.

title: Pretty color but not much more to offer for protection or feel
text: The best this about this Kindle case is that the color is a pretty orchid.  Other than than, the [[ASIN:B00LNTO1E8 Standing Case for Fire HD 7 (4th Generation), Purple]] is nothing special.  It doesn't feel good in the hand, kind of rough compared to other cases I use.  The elastic is stretchy, so that's a good thing if it lasts.  The case reminds me of a vinyl covered cardboard.  Two holders contain the Kindle, one on top and one on bottom, both are also elastic.  I don't trust this to hold very well. It's not terrible, but I wouldn't look twice if I saw this in a line-up with other Kindle cases.

title: The future is now and here's a little gadget for robot lovers
text:
First of all, the marketers of this [[ASIN:B00JVUO0RO DE Chrome Robot Dual Headphone Splitter]] have a good sense of humor as is evidenced by the instructions on the package. Very cute.

I don't carry much on my keychain because I don't want additional weight in the car's ignition weighing it down. This robot is lightweight despite its size, therefore, I put it on a separate lanyard so I don't misplace it. When hung in a special place, I know where to find it quickly. The robot separates, revealing a mini plug with splitter eyes for using two electronic devices. I've had no problems so far and find the plugs fit smoothly, but it's really a novelty item and not my number one choice as a splitter. It's a handy little device to take on long trips with kids, so the driver can enjoy a quiet time with the kids enjoying a movie while wearing headphones, and if you keep it in the car, you're always ready. The quality is not great, it's just a cute novelty for a robot loving person.

I received the product for review.

title: Floral pattern is pretty but not centered like in the photo
text:
I've tried the [[ASIN:B00IU7CEV8 Incipio Journal Cover for Kindle Voyage, Green]] and this [[ASIN:B00IU7CG5W Incipio Journal Cover for Kindle Voyage, Floral]] and I really like them both. Whereas the first is a faux leather, this is a woven fabric. I find this one easier to bend backward when reading on the Kindle. With both, you slide the Kindle down into the hard plastic tabs which contain it and there are little magnets between the gray faux suede lining which keep it closed. This does not automatically switch on and off your Kindle, so if that is a function that's important to you, it will be disappointing. It's lightweight and adds about double the depth while adding protection for your Kindle. The interior pockets are fine but I haven't used mine in either model. I've also found that this is a good size for holding 4 x 6" cards if you tire of using it as a Kindle cover. I know that some people rely on index cards for studying and this might be a nice addition if the price didn't bother you. That's better than the rubber band my daughter had to use for hers.

Because of the asymmetrical floral pattern, be prepared to receive one that's not as perfectly balanced as the one in the photo. It's the type of product that I'd select in a store after going through them all to find the most centered. I like the front of mine better than the rear but it's not well balanced visually. I don't mind the INCIPIO logo in black raised letters but I wanted to mention it because it is a contrast to the purple patterned fabric.

title: As described, it is a simple folio design
text: The green of the [[ASIN:B00IU7CEV8 Incipio Journal Cover for Kindle Voyage, Green]] which I received is more of a darker kelly green as opposed to the blue green that shows up on all of my devices.  It's very pretty and the faux leather is thin and smooth.  The gray faux suede interior is also soft and the stitching throughout is really good.  Sliding the Kindle Voyage into the hard plastic sections of the cover's rear holds it securely and the depth of the device instantaneously is doubled while wearing this case.  Not much weight is added considering the protection it affords.  Very small magnets are encased between the face and the lining which hold the top to the back but there's nothing to activate the automatic on/off of the Kindle Voyage.  This doesn't bother me, but it might not meet your needs.  It has a one year guarantee and was made in China.  If you don't like it for your Kindle, you can always store 4 x 6" index cards in this if you don't shake it too much.

title: Instructions in languages galore and clear application procedure
text:
There's nothing like the relief I experience when receiving disposable items in minimal packaging and that's the case with the [[ASIN:B00MJKZH7K AmazonBasics Screen Protectors for Samsung Galaxy S5 (3-pack)]]. Actually, the heavy cardstock in which these 2 protectors will be reused after we go through all three of them because it's a good size and very rigid. There is a little cloth included in this package which I also like because I tend to misplace mine and this way I did not have to search for one. Another great thing about this package is the instruction sheet is very well written and illustrated in an assortment of languages which will help many individuals.

Not all instruction sheets for screen protectors specify to wash and dry your hands, but this is well noted and really should be step one. The steps are easy to understand and follow and the application was as simple as any others, particularly with a clean and dry Samsung Galaxy S5. I personally removed my case from the smartphone because I found that benefited the fit. The cut outs are perfect, the fit is superb and the responsiveness of the S5 is unhindered. These are very cheap and I think they are a great product, particularly for those who have more than one of the same models in the household like ours.

title: Watch the Kindle Fire while in landscape position
text: According to the synthetic leather Clarino website, CLARINO is three times stronger than real leather, requiring only a third of real leather's weight to achieve equal tear strength.  So, if you like the look and feel of leather but do not want an animal skin, you could consider the human-made [[ASIN:B00JP46IC6 BUFFALO Case for All New Kindle Fire HDX 8.9", BLACK (will only fit All New Kindle Fire HDX 8.9")]] instead of genuine leather.  It is indeed lightweight, fitting, and folds back to hold the Kindle Fire HDX 8.9" in landscape position.  This is good for using an external keyboard or watching a video.  I personally like the look of the Amazon Origami case, but this one works fine to hold the device.  I would not expect this to protect it, just to give it a home.  The device can be positioned in a single position.

title: I hate it because now I want one for our second camera
text: We have been using SanDisk products for years and tend to return to the brand when in need.  Unfortunately, I received a [[ASIN:B00M55C1I2 SanDisk 64GB Ultra Class 10 Micro SDXC up to 48MB/s with Adapter (SDSDQUAN-064G-G4A) [Newest Version]]] and now I am ruined because I must acquire another for our second camera.  Actually, truth be told, I can use two more.  The speed is quick, storage is enough for each individual device, and the packaging is even secure.  Addition of the adapter is appreciated, too.  Very nice to record in HD!

title: Great look and feel is contemporary
text: So many covers and cases for all our digital devices.  The [[ASIN:B00JGHVKPC Solo Active iPad Air (iPad 5) Slim Case and Viewing Stand(ACV231-4)]] is special because it not only looks good and feels even better, but it functions well. The simple package wastes little yet makes the same statement of style and even a bit of class.  The honeycomb texture feels good and I've found myself playing with it while holding it.  Functionally, it is indeed sleek and thin, lightweight yet sturdy.  Resting open in landscape position, as long as it is on a flat and solid structure like a table, it remains stable and there's nothing around the edges to draw the eye.  It's a great viewing stand.

title: Glossy variety is as good as anti-glare
text: We have numerous devices and each has a screen protector.  Basically, the process is the same for each type -- with clean and dry hands in as dust free an environment that you can find, first clean the screen with something like an alcohol wipe.  When it is completely dry, remove the backing from your new screen protector and gently apply  it to the screen.  Peel the backing off while continuing to apply the screen protector and then follow as necessary with something like a plastic gift card to press it firmly and remove air bubbles that seem to inevitably gather between the screen and protective sheet.  The [[ASIN:B00DQZSDPU Buffalo Clear Screen Protector Kit for All New Kindle Fire HD 7" (will only fit All New Kindle Fire HD 7"), 2 pack]] is reasonably priced, shaped as it should be, and if you prefer, you can get an anti-glare option.  It is fine and includes two screen protectors with a sheet of instructions and is packaged in the most minimalist way possible so there is virtually nothing except the backing, cellophane wrapper and the paper which can be recycled.  This was made in Japan and I like the way there is a 1 inch strip which is removed first which assists in the application process.  I have cut this down for a different Kindle Fire and it was easy to do if you have more than one Kindle and want to purchase a single pack of two.

title: Silicon underside is effective
text: We have numerous devices and each has a screen protector.  Basically, the process is the same for each type -- with clean and dry hands in as dust free an environment that you can find, first clean the screen with something like an alcohol wipe.  When it is completely dry,  remove the backing from your new screen protector and gently apply  it to the screen.  Peel the backing off while continuing to apply the screen protector and then follow as necessary with something like a plastic gift card to press it firmly and remove air bubbles that seem to inevitably gather between the screen and protective sheet.  The [[ASIN:B00DQZQ370 Buffalo Anti-Glare Screen Protector Kit for Kindle Fire HDX 7" (will only fit Kindle Fire HDX 7"), 2 pack]] is reasonably priced, shaped as it should be, and the anti-glare option does reduce the glare.  It is fine and includes two anti glare sheets and a sheet of instructions and is packaged in the most minimalist way possible so there is virtually nothing except the backing, cellophane wrapper and the paper which can be recycled.  This was made in Japan and I like the way there is a 1 inch strip which is removed first which assists in the application process.

title: Leaves no room for growth, so verify that it fits your device
text:
I have a love/hate relationship with Belkin products. Some are a major disappointment, but then there are those that are so well constructed and attractive that I forget about those others. The [[ASIN:B00D2CNXK2 Belkin 11-Inch Laptop /Chromebook Sleeve, Blue (B2B081-C01)]] is a beauty that I am very happy to have requested. Unfortunately, the dimensions are just as described and if your device is a hair over, there is no leeway because the outside gusset is not stretchy or flexible at all. You can't really tell from the images, but the opening of this sleeve is on one single end, that is the shorter side of the rectangle. Because the corners are all rounded, the zipper extends about an inch or two down the length, so you can wiggle your device in and out of the sleeve, provided it is not wider than 8 inches. Seriously. As I said, the black gusset is made of a woven heavy duty fabric, measuring about an inch in width, and there is piping sewn into both seams, front and back, for a finished appearance. A full sized pocket is sewn into the front of the sleeve and it contains a zipper as well. There is a small handle made of the same gusset fabric which is beautifully concealed when not being used. The neoprene is a lovely blue which is darker than the image online and I love it.

Because none of my devices can be squeezed into this sleeve, I am using it for other purposes. The price of this is perfect for a terrific sleeve.

title: Looks like it will handle my needs
text:
I have had good service from AmazonBasics cables and this [[ASIN:B00I83XD4Q AmazonBasics USB 3.0 A to B Cable - 3 Feet]] works as well as any others. It is sturdy, short and has gold plated connectors. This cable was made in China and is not of the flexible type, so needing only 3 feet works well because I do not have to wrap excess cable. Although longer cables are available for a minimal increase in cost, my thought is that a cable ought not be longer than physically needed. I personally like the logo which is applied to USB 3.0 A male end.

Be sure this is the cable you need or you will not be happy. It is covered by a 1 year warranty and is packaged exactly like the image provided online.

title: Can't even come up with a repurpose for this one
text:
The [[ASIN:B00CNMYP0E CoverTop Universal 15.6-Inch Laptop Shock Protection 100% Pure Silicone Cover (LCBLACK156)]] is so stinky that even if it did fit any of our three laptops, we would not use it until after airing it outside. The nubby texture in the rear is very unattractive and this is not a cover I would have purchased had I seen and touched it in advance. It is folded in half inside the cardboard package and when I removed it, was shocked at its heavy weight. To me, it looks like a tire, not a protective cover for a valuable laptop. Although the claim is that this is a universal product, it is very far from being a one size fits all. I'm wavering between a one and two star review, but giving it the benefit of the doubt in that it might fit something and work for them and the smell will disappear over time, it gets a two.

On the back of the box is a complex diagram and one blurb confuses me, ¨ATTENTION Prior to the installation of the covertop please remove any laptop exit as needed, in order to allow ventilation and proper connections of devices.¨ I don't know what a laptop exit is.

title: Works well with proper smartphone and television
text: The Belkin Miracast Video Adapter works well if the correct equipment is available, but doesn't work at all if you are using a noncompliant smartphone or television.  I first thought my two year old Vizio television would not work because it has no USB port, but after ordering a new set, realized that the USB could be utilized from an outside source.  After trying several times to ate my Razr to the Belkin, I realized that the connection was unobtainable because the phone is not operating on the correct system.  I then enlisted a friend with a compatible phone and we were able to make the connection very quickly, then watched gleefully on the Vizio.  For a smartphone with Miracast capability, this works well and should be considered.  Since technology changes rapidly, as do our phones, I would not hesitate to use this if it fits into your budget.  When I replace my smartphone in the next few months, I will certainly verify on the Belkin website that the new purchase is compatible because it is an outstanding option for viewing images and listening to audio on a big screen.  I have been satisfied with my other Belkin products and find them to be a reliable company.  If your set has an HDMI port which isn't easy to access, this device also includes an extender which has worked well for my set.  Otherwise, I would not have been able to plug in the USB cable because of its position.

title: Impressively sleek in appearance, fast, with long lasting battery
text:
I purchased a MacBook Pro a few months ago and love the laptop computer. I've been an Apple customer since the inception of Macintosh, owning only one PC in my lifetime. I have never purchased an iPad. The [[ASIN:B00HRO3IBA Toshiba Chromebook CB35-A3120 PLM01U-002005 13.3-Inch Cloud Computer]] is Toshiba's first entry into the Chromebook market, my first Chromebook and it did not disappoint this consumer.

It is about the same dimensions as my MacBook Pro, but thinner and substantially lighter in weight. With a solid state, no hard drive or DVD in this one, it is the one I'll take when traveling. Out of the box, I plugged in the Chromebook, then opened the lid. Immediately, the registration process began and since I'm already a Google customer, it was quick and simple. Setup was faster than fast and within a couple of minutes I was on the web, with access to all my Google contents, even those from my Android. Another few minutes and I was set up to print from my Epson printer which is in another room. Whereas I need to use an Epson app to print from the Android, this prints from the Google Cloud. The Google store offers a lot of apps, many of which are free, and a few which I found desirable and downloaded. With two USB ports, I'm able to carry a USB with me instead of relying on the cloud for everything. With the HDMI, I can hook up to a larger screen if I want. Chromebooks are designed for streaming and internet based operations, and there is no software to install. It's all out there for you to use without taking up space or requiring moving parts in your computer. Microsoft Office doesn't work, but documents can be put into Google Docs, then be converted to an Office document.

The appearance of this Chromebook is very sleek, with an attractive texture to the cover that feels good in the hand. For me, it's an easier, less slippery grip than others I've held onto. Start up is nearly instantaneous with the Chromebook as soon as the lid is lifted up -- I turn it off each time I'm done with it. The battery time is longer than I'd expected, fortunately because although the charge time is fast, the power supply I have gets uncomfortably hot. Because of this, I do not keep it plugged in while charging. My second criticism of this unit is that it makes a disturbing noise on the left side closest to me periodically while operating. At first, I thought the sound was coming from the power supply, but determined it is from the Chromebook after disconnecting the power supply. It's not constant, just annoying when it occurs because it takes over my focus. The keypad is very comfortable for me and I've not stumbled moving between my MacBook Pro and Toshiba Chromebook. The trackpad is a little jumpy, but not as bad as it could be, even after making adjustments through the Settings. The screen presents a terrific image and the speakers also are better than I'd expected at this price. All in all, I can't believe they are selling this Chromebook for 279. I can see why Chromebooks are all that in schools now. It's nice to have an option to lock your Chromebook if you're taking it to a place where it might "walk away" and requiring a sign-in to access the operating system is another plus. I like it and could love the Toshiba Chromebook in time.

UPDATE a few days later: Amazonian Consumer, another customer, provided comments on my review which I think are important. He/she noted things that are posted on the Toshiba website, so I'll address the components. I have used the Bluetooth with no problem at all. The RAM is limited to what's installed and the battery is not user-replaceable. There is a Skype limitation because Chrome OS uses Hangouts instead, and the camera does work fine. The SD card reader works, too, without a problem. I also didn't mention that I like the Velcro cable wrap attached to the power cord, so I don't have to add one. Mine power supply still gets hot, but when the charge is complete, it cools down. Ironically, my Chromebook has stopped making the noises it was initially making. Another observation I've made is that the trackpad seems to occasionally have a mind of its own and it sends things before I'm ready. It's more than being overly sensitive and I'm going to need to work on correcting this.

UPDATE 2/6/14: The audio now continuously goes in and out and the machine sound which I mentioned in my initial review is occurring again, usually when the audio goes out. I have a call in to Toshiba but they aren't trained yet to deal with the Chromebook, so someone will be calling me back "in a day or two." I'm also still experiencing the cursor arbitrarily moving up on the page when I have stopped typing, so I have to be especially careful to assure that what I'm typing is being entered where intended.

UPDATE 2/18/14: The audio problem is even worse and Toshiba never called me or net an email other than a survey on their customer service. It took several of my initiated attempts in phone calls and I'm finally awaiting a box and label which will take another two days to arrive for this Chromebook to be returned to Toshiba for repair. They offered me no option of simply sending a label and letting me return it in the original boxes. Dealing with them has been terrible and one rep had the gall to ask if I'd rate him a 10 on a scale of 1-10 for assistance in a survey.

I'm tempted to reduce my rating of four stars but will hold off until I receive my repaired lemon of a Chromebook which I still love despite its clicking sound, faulty speakers, sticky trackpad and terrible Toshiba telephone customer service.

UPDATE 3/11/14: Received my repaired Chromebook last night (FedEx signature required delivery was only option) and the speakers had been replaced. What a difference! No clicking sound, humming, anything other than the sound of lovely audio through the speakers. The trackpad still isn't the smoothest, but more importantly, it still selects things that I have no intention of selecting. For example, when selecting an email, one above or below opens instead of the one I select. I've also had pages close or disappear for no apparent reason.

title: Quite the bargain for a compact yet sturdy mini tripod
text:
I'm impressed. First of all, the [[ASIN:B00DRA4CW2 Mefoto A0320Q00B DayTrip Tripod Kit (Blue)]] lightweight aluminum mini tripod is lovely. It is housed in a nice black cardboard box that makes a good first impression. The tripod inside is protected by a black carrying case with orange piping trim. There's an attached lightweight adjustable carrying strap that functions without any padding. Inside of the case is a side zippered pocket that contains a hex tool and the owner's manual which is very well written in two languages. The English is easy to understand and without many grammatical or spelling errors. The two pages of diagrams are also well done and the publication is very basic. I'm happy that too much money didn't go into this part of the package and there weren't additional packing materials either!

The tripod I received is an appealing blue which reminds me of the Caribbean waters. It's definitely a color I would have selected in a B&M store. The entire tripod weighs less than 2 pounds and stands a maximum of about 24 inches tall. You can safely mount a camera of a maximum of 8.8 pounds. Each part of the tripod seems well constructed and very well designed. My favorite little treat is the bubble level which is recessed in the mounting platform, underneath the easily removable mounting plate. The ballhead allows for a relatively smooth head movement, better than I'd expected. I appreciate the retractable weight hook for situations where a bit of extra stability is required. Another feature is the reversible center column which I use quite often for shooting table top close ups. Having the tripod legs fold up greatly reduces the packing and carrying size of this tripod, and it can be folded and stored in the bag very quickly if necessary while on the go.

I must say that when I first read "Mefoto", I saw it as "Manfroto". They are not the same company or products, but for the cost of this great little tripod, I don't care what it's named. It's a bargain that securely allows you to better use a camera in situations where a full sized tripod is either inconvenient, overkill or simply too cumbersome. I'll likely purchase a couple as holiday gifts this year and will also check out their other products! This was a fine introduction for me.

title: It's small, functional and affordable
text: We've been using the [[ASIN:B00DR8LAE2 SanDisk Connect 64G Wireless Media Drive Streaming On the Go (SDWS1-064G-A57)]]successfully and have encountered no problems since first transferring pictures and sound files.  Its size is compact, about the same size as a Royal Castle hamburger and bun I used to order as a kid,  The battery lasts longer than any other portable media storage device I've used, making it a perfect traveling companion.  I think this would be a good little device for a gift and am considering one for a niece who has no television.

title: Groovy quilted case
text: The positioning grooves for standing your Kindle in the [[ASIN:B008X9Z9ZQ Belkin Quilted Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 7", Black (will only fit Kindle Fire HD 7")]] are perhaps the best of any of my Kindle cases.  The quilted cover is thicker than I thought I'd like, however, it is absolutely fantastic, with exquisite detail.  A Kindle Fire HD 7" snaps in securely and remains in the case until you decide to remove it.  The magnetic closure easily folds and adheres to the rear when the case is opened, and the interior will not scratch your device.  For the price, this is a definite winner and I'd be eager to see it's alternate colors.

title: In black and gray, it's more classy than glam
text: Suitable for the most discerning of individuals, the [[ASIN:B008X9ZBVI Belkin Glam Tab Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 7", Black (will only fit Kindle Fire HD 7")]] is well made, easy to use, beautifully designed and a secure home for your precious Kindle.  The magnetic closure is a snap to open and close and the case offers a variety of positions for standing the device.  This is one of my favorite Belkin cases and right now, the price is more reasonable than many others.

title: Learning curve is well worth the effort
text:
I intended to give the [[ASIN:B00AQRUW4Q Seagate Wireless Plus 1 TB Mobile Device Storage with Built-In Wi-Fi Streaming (STCK1000100)]] a rating of four stars, but have decided that it really is a five star product. The near deduction was because of the frustration I experienced in my attempting to get the device up and running with the limited information provided in the package and on the website. Once I successfully downloaded the software to my Droid, Kindle Fire and MacBook, I still encountered more trial and error than usual until I was able to figure out how the darn thing works. Fast forward to days and weeks of loving the device!

The Wireless Plus can be used as an extra drive for storage if you're not interested in using it for streaming, but if that's your true need, I'd likely recommend purchasing something else. With it's own Wi-Fi streaming, you don't need to use your home or hot network. Using it's Wi-Fi has been quick and has been glitch free for us thus far. We have used three devices at once and found it to be problem-free, with no freezes, crashes or difficulties. We had it up and running for four hours and still had battery power, then recharged. Although it can be charged via the USB on your computer, it is much faster by plugging it into an electrical outlet if one's available. Since we haven't drained the battery yet, I can't say how long it really lasts.

Music, movies, pictures, documents, audiobook, you can use whichever you want on any networked device as long as the device has the appropriate application installed. I watched the Seagate tutorials several times and found them to be difficult to follow, however once I spent some dedicated time just feeling my way through, I discovered that I do like the applications, too. Even if I'm not accessing the Wireless Plus on my Droid, I have been using the Seagate app.

This arrives with little documentation, but it is USB 3 capable if you need it. The housing is lightly rubberized and it has a matte metal plate in a charcoal gray color on the face side. The plug appears to be proprietary, the second reason I almost deducted a star from this review. It looks like a hybrid mini plug that's attached via a thin wire, not a cable, to a USB for either a device or the two prong electrical plug. No case is included, but I have a couple that work great. The size isn't so big that it feels cumbersome, but it is heavier than it appears to be upon first glance. I don't mind the weight because this little device holds 1 TB, much more than I have loaded on it as of today. I highly recommend this device and look forward to Seagate upgrading it as time passes. It's unique and not expensive for what it offers.

title: Watch your hairs
text: Since the [[ASIN:B009S4FMB6 Jabra SUPREME Driver's Edition Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black/Silver]] comes with a headband, I tend to use it with the headband.  Unfortunately, my hair is thinning because I lose some each time I remove the headset.  Regardless, this bluetooth is extremely easy to synch with my Droid and it's recognized each and every time I turn on the Bluetooth in the car.  I wear this only for driving and I don't care that passersby give me funny looks, it works great.  The earpiece is larger than most contemporary bluetooth devices, but it's cushiony and comfortable for long drives.  The microphone is sensitive and responsive.  I haven't had a complaint yet with any call.  Slipping the earphone onto the headband is a simple task, and I find that I'm wearing it 90% of the time, preferring that to the ear wire and no band.  My main criticism other than the hair pulling of this design is that it takes some getting used to to operate the touch controls as well as turn the device on and off.  When off of the band, it's an easy feat, but no so when it's attached and you can't bend the microphone down completely.  Since the battery is really long lasting, it hasn't run out of power yet in the middle of a call.  Because you have options for charging this set, you're a step ahead, and with an adjustable headband, it fits most head sizes.  It's a good set.

title: Most suitable for Apple products
text:
I've been using the [[ASIN:B00BFNYD90 Jabra VOX Corded Stereo Wired Headsets - Retail Packaging - Black]] for a couple weeks now and like them but don't love them, largely because they don't do all they can do on my Droid. I downloaded the Jabra app and was all set to improve their capabilities, but all I got was a really good app that allows me to import, organize and equalize my collection. I ended up listening to radio stations because I don't usually download music to my phone anyway. I tried the phones on my MacBook and iPod as well, and found them to produce satisfactory sound, albeit a little tinnier than my other headsets, either canned or budded.

The headset is attractive and lightweight. It appears to be well constructed and the sets of gels fit well onto the pair of appendages. They originally attached gels fit my ears without a problem but the left one tends to make a squishy sound when inserted. It's the actual earbud because it happens when I place it in either ear. I like the knobbed design of the buds because that angle lets me know in which ear to place the bud. I simply can't read the LEFT/RIGHT on the headset. These are comfortable for a very long time (hours) and I get only a little extraneous sound seeping through most of the time. On phone calls, this is outstanding for myself and the people to whom I've spoken. Five stars here. The standard microphone is another asset, and my voice commands on the Droid are smoothly recognized, too. It's not omnidirectional, but I don't really need that in this headset. The 3.5mm jack isn't as snug as others I've used and I have to be really careful about inserting it at the correct angle so that it's not jiggled while I move. Listening to Phillip Glass was at first awful, until I realized I'd moved the plug. Once it was inserted properly, the sound was beautiful and larger than what comes through many other earbud headsets. I appreciate the magnets on each wire because they allow me to wrap the cables uniformly and put into the little lightweight storage case. The pouch case has a nice opening that's comfortable to open and close with one hand and it stays closed well. I also am using the hard plastic shell in which this was packaged, but you could recycle it if you have no use for the "package."

I'd recommend that if you have no device which allows you to use the in wire control, you save some money and get something else. For my use, it just gets in the way and is frustrating. I was disappointed that I couldn't even answer a phone call as I was under the impression this would work on my smartphone. I can't blame my misinterpretation on the product, though, so no stars off here. It's tempting to use these earbuds while I drive, but I try to remove one so that I can hear what's going on outside of my own space. While walking the dog, these are great, again upping the star rating. The volume control only works on Apple devices and the pause/play music, answer/end call, reject call, redial last umber, or skip track forward/backward are phone dependent on the in wire control. None of these work on the Motorola Droid. If you're looking for realistic hifi sound from your device, try out this headset that weighs in at just over 1/2 of an ounce, but I'd suggest thinking about if you need or can use the mic and music control which adds to the price of this product. This is a five star design and it seems like the headset will surpass it's 2 year warranty. This was made in China.

title: Compact size offers little
text: The [[ASIN:B00BFYVXYM Case Logic CHC-101 Compact System Camera Day Holster (Black)]] will, "Transform any bag into a camera bag."  The case will accommodate the largest sized camera of 5.9 inches wide, 4.6 inches tall, and with lens attached, a maximum of 7.5 inches deep, that is a compact camera base.  It's designed to attach to your camera's shoulder strap, slipping it through the case's tether strap, and you can slip your lens cap into the interior pocket while you're snapping away.  Basically, you put your camera with it's lens down into the neoprene case and you can remove it quickly when taking a picture.  It is lightweight, so not much stress is put on the camera's strap if you're wearing it around your neck.  This holster can be put into any larger bag or case and it's somewhat protected by the unsealed, yet velcro closed top flap.  The exterior dimensions are 6.3 x 3.6 x 5.3" and the interior dimensions are 4.7 x 3.1 x 4.0".  We have a couple cameras that fit into this case, but it really seems like an unnecessary sleeve of sorts.  I believe this has a small audience and a big price.  Made in China.

title: Less bubbles than my previous screen protector
text:
First of all, I'm in favor of protecting the screen on my Kindles, but I just don't understand why they are so expensive. That being said, the [[ASIN:B00AHPSTBU Belkin Screen Protector for Kindle Fire - 4 Pack]] was easier to apply to both of our Kindle Fires without residual bubbles than the previous protectors. Since they tend to cost several dollars each, I wasn't eager to switch them out, but after doing so, I'm glad I did. This is not an anti-glare protector, but that doesn't bother me. I usually like Belkin products and have no complaints with this product other than what I consider to be a high cost.

As with any screen protector, it's really important to clean your screen and make sure it's dry prior to applying the sheet of plastic. Rigid or not, the little bubbles can appear between the protector and the screen and it's nearly impossible to get rid of them once the cover has been applied. I do find that the little applicator card helps, as does a clean work surface, a steady hand and no distractions. It's pretty quick and does protect your investment without affecting the sensitivity of the screen.

title: Lightweight cover has a closure
text: An advantage to the Belkin Classic Tab Case for Kindle Fire HD 7", Gravel for the Kindle Fire HD 7" is the magnetized tab.  Other than that,  it is a rather benign gray color with a black spine and it's very lightweight.  I personally don't find the materials to be up to par, however, and would look at other options offered by Belkin rather than this one.  The man-made materials are stitched together perfectly and the Kindle fits into the elasticized rounded corners.  Of note is that the elastic stretches on one side of each corner and the other is stable.  I like this technique for containing the device.  The interior has a more matted feel than the exterior.

title: Very bright case not exactly like duct tape
