text: I received the [[ASIN:B008ULPE70 Verso Trends OMG! Duct Tape Case for Kindle Fire HD 7", Neon Green (will only fit Kindle Fire HD 7")]] as well as the [[ASIN:B008MF3X9K Verso Trends OMG! Pink Duct Tape for Kindle Fire (Pink) (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)]], so I can actually compare the sizes.  The green is definitely wider because it's designed to fit the Fire HD 7", but the length is about the same.  Both have an interior pocket and the four elastic strips for containing each corner of your device.  Neither has a closure for the case.  Although this doesn't really look like duct tape, it's cute enough and it is really, really bright.  They aren't kidding when they call it neon green!  Verso Trends has many cases available right now and they're worthy of a look!  This particular style isn't the best for protection, but it's good enough if you aren't taking your Kindle on the road.

title: Not exactly like duct tape, but it's cute enough
text: I really was expecting a cover that resembled duct tape, but the [[ASIN:B008MF3X9K Verso Trends OMG! Pink Duct Tape for Kindle Fire (Pink) (does not fit Kindle Fire HD)]] looks more like a wrinkly sort of dull crinkled patent leather.  Nevertheless, it is very cute and fits the appropriate Kindle Fire for which it was made.  Verso Trends has produced a number of cases for various sizes of Kindles and other devices and each appears to be made well.  Some are more reasonably priced than others, so I'd recommend checking out all the cases they offer.  With only elastic straps to hold each of the four corners and no closure for the case, this one isn't the best for protection, but if you're not taking it out and about, it's fine.  The pink is lovely and is really bright.  I would imagine that a young person would really like this case because it's very simple and it does have an interior pocket.

title: Nicest case we have
text: We have several Kindle devices and several cases.  The [[ASIN:B008X9Z6O0 Belkin Genuine Leather Standing Case for Kindle Fire HD 7", Gravel (will only fit Kindle Fire HD 7")]] is one of the nicest for several reasons.  It is a true leather, has a soft black lining, allows for four viewing heights, is well made, and didn't come with extraneous packaging or literature.  The Kindle slips into elasticized corners of a plastic material and the elastic used to hold the closed case together is very soft.  I especially like the way the case actually slips into the slots when it is used as a stand.  My only criticism is that I tend to worry that the Kindle device will actually slip out of the corners if it is suddenly moved, but that has not happened.  The Gravel color is a very soothing medium gray.

title: Delicious sound and comfortable on my average sized ears
text: The [[ASIN:B009FHFFIG Sennheiser Momentum Over-Ear Headphone]] are circumaural  which means they cover the whole ear and they have a closed-back.  They are lightweight, gorgeous with soft brown leather cushioned earpieces, have two easily switchable cables, one for general use and the second for specified mac devices.  A MacBook is not one of the specified devices, but my iPod is.  With its swivel plug and embedded on the cable remote, I'm sure iPhone and iPad users will be as thrilled as I was when I tried it on a friend's devices.  Crisp, clear, complete, these need no amplifier, but they do need ears which are not larger than average or the whole ear coverage is lacking and therefore, so is the desired effect of a circumaural earpiece.  I've listened to music on a MacBook, an android phone, a Kindle Fire, and tested these on the aforementioned iPad and iPhone.  In each and every case, the sound was outstanding and my ears did not tire, nor did they feel uncomfortable or overheated.  Most sounds surrounding me were not heard and those nearby did not hear what I was listening to at any time.  Watching movies is enhanced every time and I'm finding that even when impulsively finding a video on the Web in my usual activities, I tend to grab these headphones to listen instead of simply hearing through the computer.  My favorite music in these earphones thus far today has been John Coltrane's [[ASIN:B000V698WE A Love Supreme]].  I tend to switch genres throughout a day, but thought this was worth mentioning.  Nothing like really hearing the instrumentals as they were intended to be heard!  Outstanding headphones.

title: Pretty and comfortable in the hands
text:
The [[ASIN:B008S2DC1Q Tribeca Genuine Leather Portfolio Case for Kindle Fire, Berry Metallic]] is very pretty and shiny, smells creepy because it's only been out of the box since last night, is comfortable to hold, fits the Kindle Fire snugly with four elastic corners, has a tab closure that can be folded back into a slot when the Kindle is being used in landscape mode on a flat surface with the case folded back, and is better than average, but not fabulous. It's lighter in weight than my previous cover and feels better, but I'm not 100% sold on it for several reasons. Any time an accessory arrives with a nasty smell, I'm not happy and I found it necessary to remove the Kindle for now and let the case air out. The packaging states, "Folio design converts into a stand with multiple viewing angles." I was able to view in a single angle with the stand folded properly. The tab closure is secure, but it's an extra step to slip it through the holder and the tab is a bit long. I imagine this will improve as time goes by when it's used frequently. The genuine leather exterior is a thin leather that's irregularly finished with the metallic look, but I don't think the "cushioned" lining will protect the device well if it's accidentally dropped. Tribeca claims, "You aren't boring, so why should your accessories be?" That's a catchy phrase and the accessory has a bit of cuteness to it. It is easy to locate because this one is bright, and it does make a statement of color. I think it's a nice product.

EDIT 3/27/13: I like this case, but the odd smell remains on its interior after three months. Otherwise, it's condition is great.

title: Simple to pair, easy to operate, this is a good headset
text: The compact [[ASIN:B006C248BC Motorola H19txt Universal Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging]] arrived in an attractive hard plastic box which I'm using for storage of some little bits which made me happier than having another package to recycle.  The headset is compact and different than my other bluetooth headsets because the boom is foldable.  The most difficult part of getting this up and running was removing the little plastic from the headset, so I'd give it tom marks for accessibility and function.  Easy to charge, this headset hasn't burned the charge any faster than my other headsets, another plus.  Pairing with a Motorola Razr was simple and required nothing other than turning on both units, yay for ease!  I'll admit that I was startled because a voice spoke to me as soon as I opened the box, but I wasn't too surprised since the light was already on in the headset.  I've had no problems with the fit in my ear or the reception, but I dpn't usually travel too far from my phone, so it hasn't been tested to the max.  The design reminds me of a Volvo, boxy, if you know what I mean.  I'm very impressed with this Motorola headset, but must admit that I prefer my Plantronic bluetooth headset which is in this price range.  I am not complaining about this one, I just really prefer the other because I like it's design better.

title: Oy
text: I'm not eager to award a product with a single star, but the [[ASIN:B007YYUUA0 BlueAnt T2-BK-USEN-US Endure Bluetooth Headset - Retail Packaging - Black]] has earned one measly star.  I've been using a [[ASIN:B00177YJFM Plantronics Discovery 925 Bluetooth Earpiece (Cerise) [Retail Packaging]]] for four years without complaint and would recommend that headset hands down over this one.  I'd definitely not recommend the BlueAnt because of it's poor design, lousy fit, flimsy construction, terrible pairing and most importantly, undesirable sound quality.  There are many other bluetooth headsets available with better characteristics at a much lower cost, so I'd investigate others and try them out if you can.

title: Hope it  will last a long time
text: I think 3M makes great products and found the [[ASIN:B007BY0MIS 3M Natural View Anti-Glare Screen Protector for the New iPad (3rd Generation) and the iPad 2 (NVAGiPad3RTL)]] to live up to 3M quality.  The packaging is simple, screen protector is easy to apply if you follow the directions and are patient, and it will hopefully last for a very long time.  I personally had no difficulty eliminating any bubbles and can attribute that experience to my good luck and not any particular expertise.  The matte finish reduces glare and I find no difference in either feel or responsiveness.  If you need an anti-glare screen protector, I think this one is a great choice.  I've given it four stars only because I think it warrants a cost of less than twenty dollars.

title: Only real wish is for longer battery life
text: Bought two of these in refurb condition and they both arrived as good as new.  After using them for a few weeks now, we both love our Kindle Fire devices and feel they are a great value for what they offer.  I still use my keyboard Kindle, loving the long battery life, and only wish the Fire could compare.  Unfortunately, even with the wi-fi turned off, this one needs a recharge much more often, but what this offers far outweighs the need to plug a cord between the device and an electrical supply.  It's easy to read, not too heavy, fits into the sleeves I'd purchased for the keyboard Kindle, and with wi-fi turned on, gives me a connection to the internet.  Love being able to use Gmail and more, don't miss having to pay more for wireless connection, do miss being to move with the device and remain connected, though.  Carousel feature is great, not having to go to archived items to identify what's in our growing library, and being able to download very easily from the icon is a time saver.  It's well worth the cost for the Kindle Fire and I recommend it to anyone who doesn't think it's a cheaper version of an iPad, expecting it to offer and provide more than its capabilities.  Two different products, each has its assets.

title: These Open Back Headphones Deliver
text:
If you're looking for closed headphones, the Sennheiser HD 598 Audiophile Headphones with High-Gloss Burl Wood Accents are NOT for you. On the other hand, the open back design of these headphones is perfect for my needs, providing clear and consistent sounds. With an open back headphone, you can hear outside sounds and what you're listening to can be heard by others around you. The sounds through these are clear and true, making them a great asset when listening to spoken word as for transcription purposes. Because they are so true, when hearing some older or poorly mixed tracks, the obvious difference in location recordings can often be jarring. I can get by that since these are wonderful when used in true stereo or hifi, well-mixed applications. They really do mimic a hifi speaker system in the small space of my head!

I'm not a fan of the burl-look in cars, and I'm also not crazy about the burl-look of these headphones or the beige band. Since I'm not looking at the headphones but rather listening through them, it's not an issue for me. The velour covered ear pads are thick, comfortable and have shown no signs wear since I've been using my set. I've spent many hours at a sitting listening through these and have yet to have a problem or complaint with the fit, feel, or sound. The band is rather easy to adjust, the pads tilt smoothly and once I've settled in, I've not needed to readjust unless I've removed the headphones.

I've used Sennheiser microphones in film and video production, both in the field and studio, having trusted them for providing great sound for a recording, but I've not used Sennheiser earphones until the HD598's in the Audiophile series. I wish my studio headphones were as comfortable as these, but then I'd need a closed set! With a long 10 foot cable, I'm able to move more than a couple steps and if I want to extend the distance, I can add on a longer cable. Coming with an attached gold plated phono (1/4") plug and a gold plated mini (1/8") adapter, I'm set for use on laptop, ipod, amplifier, television or professional equipment. I like them a lot and find that they improve every day!

title: Simple to install with no bells or whistles
text: The Philips SQM6415/17 Tilting LCD Wall Mount for 19-Inch to 31-Inch Screens mounts your 19 inch to 31 inch screen weighing less than 44 pounds onto the stud on a wall, attaching the mounted bracket to the VESA holes at the rear of a tv or monitor.  Prior to receiving this wall mount, I downloaded the manual from the Phillips website, and I recommend you do the same.  The manual is far from the best, mainly pictures, and like the one which arrives with the package.  If you have a small monitor, then it's possible to hang this on your own, but if you have a set approaching the 31 inch size, I'd definitely recommend having two people complete the installation.  Since the monitor is held to the wall on a vertical bracket, be sure you attach this to the stud and not drywall, and if you have no stud, then construct something very solid (perhaps horizontal boards attached to the studs above and below) from which to attach the bracket.  If you're unsure about using a stud finder, please do not guess or assume you've found the solid wood stud.  You'll need a drill and screwdriver for installation, and a pencil.  I used a level to make sure the tv was even because I have a cathedral ceiling and we couldn't agree on what was level to the eye.  Had the manual been better and the MSRP lower on this product, I would have rated it four rather than three stars, but all in all, I'd say it's an average wall mount.

title: Sturdy, smooth and intuitive for me
text:
Until I wrote this, there was only one review for The Manfrotto 498RC4 Ball Head with Quick Release posted on Amazon. Since it didn't evaluate the head but rather the author's experience with Ace Photo's poor customer service, I read Amazon reviews for the Manfrotto 488RC4, the previous model of this ball head.

This is an excellent ball head which I'm using attached to my Vanguard tripod legs for both still and video photography. Its weight capacity is listed as 17 pounds and I've witnessed nothing to contradict this capability. Although this adds about a pound and three quarters to my system which is heavier than many, for me it's not a problem since I'm not hauling the tripod system for great distances. I debated between this and the 498RC2 Ball Head, but I chose this for it's two notable differences. I wanted the broader 410PL plate because I prefer the locking switch on this mounting system, and I like the two onboard bubble spirit levels. The Amazon description says, " The locking lever securely locks the head both in the +90° -90° ball positioning and in the 360° pan movements." It doesn't tell you that there is a separate lock on the panoramic axis which allows for rotation adjustment or panning so that framing isn't messed up. The movements on this tripod are smooth and can be adjusted with a friction knob to get it just right for the individual user. The 360º markings on the base are also an asset. I also find the ratcheting locking levers to give me more freedom because I can quickly turn them to a suitable position if they are in the way. I'm really pleased with this purchase and was thrilled to see that with an online product registration with Manfrotto, the warranty is automatically extended.

title: Low price for low quality = value for cost
text: At less than six dollars, I'm happy with this purchase of 2.5" USB 2.0 SATA Hard Drive HDD Case Enclosure.  I was not looking for an incredibly durable case which will be transported much, if at all, so this works fine for me.  All parts were included and the quality is far from great, but it does work and that's what I needed.  My package included two little screwdrivers because perhaps they've found that one is too soft to use for two little bitty screws, but I used another screwdriver anyway.  The black faux whatever case fits snugly, so if you don't use screws on yours, the case can actually be held together.  The silver aluminum is not a heavy gauge, but then again, I don't need a heavy duty case.  Plugging my 80 gig drive (removed from a MacBook) into the end slot, being very careful to not dislodge or mess up anything since it's not real sturdy, careful to hold only the edges of the drive and use a flat table to hold the end cap.  When I first inserted the drive into the case, the opposite end popped out one of the little holes on that end.  I could not get it reattached with the drive inserted, so I removed the drive, placed the reinserted end cap (one without the drive) on the table and gently inserted the drive.  It was not a smooth operation, but took less than a minute.  I then lined up one hole and inserted the screw with only a turn or two.  Lined up the second hole and inserted the second screw, then tightened them both.  Next, I plugged the USB cable into the drive, then inserted the USB which was not an offshoot into the MacBook.  It took a couple attempts for the Mac to accept the drive because it had not properly been ejected when removed from the computer, but after removing it and restarting the computer, it was recognized and accessed right away.  It's been working fine and I'm pleased to have this additional drive now in case it's needed.

title: Quick set up, clear images, classy frame
text: The HP 7 inch Digital Picture Frame (model df730p1) was the quickest to set up of any digital frame I've used.  My first impression upon receiving the box was that it was packaged economically, a plus in my book with no extraneous styrofoam materials for protecting in the box.  I was then impressed by the actual frame which is described as, "Dark Espresso Front Concave, 1 Decorative Paper Mat, double color: White on Espresso."  It's lovely and the paper matte gives it a more finished appearance.  This frame can be rotated if desired, as can the photos.  I looked at the quick set up guide, read the very complete manual and then removed the frame from its package, plugged it in and turned it on.  The internal slideshow began in seconds and I was eager to replace the graphics and pictures with my own.  Seeing that this has a calendar, I switched from the default date in 2008 and set it to the current date and time.  Options exist to display the calendar with the photo in the upper corner or to have the time displayed in a small font, but I selected neither of those options and went for just the pictures to be run in a slideshow at 5 second intervals.  Being able to set a schedule for images is a great advantage, allowing for the slideshow to cease when it's not needed to run.  I set all these things with the intuitive little remote control which can be attached to the rear of the frame by the enclosed magnet.  Smart option.  The LCD screen is 480x234 and the image is very clean.  With a 5-in-one card reader, you can use SD, MMC, XD, MS, MSPro or MMC.  This model has an internal memory of 128 MB which supposedly can run up to 800 compressed images and there is also a mini USB port.  A little dial on the side enables you to adjust the brightness of the image.  Only JPEG files can be read and there is no speaker, so keep in mind that it's a visual frame.  Most menu options are very logical and easy to follow, and a majority can be accessed via the device itself, without using the remote.  Although the remote action does take a second or two to register, I've found that preferable.  All in all, I think this is a very nice frame in this price range and would not hesitate to recommend it.

title: Sturdy Tripod Legs are Superior to Most
text:
The Vanguard Auctus Plus 323CT Professional Tripod for Cameras and Camcorders is even better than I was anticipating and now I must purchase a new tripod head to get the most out of this high quality photographic instrument. To maintain a stable and secure foundation for a camera, this is outstanding -- attractive, easy to assemble, sturdy, and versatile. It arrives in a very nice cardboard box with a handle, so if you're inclined to store it in the box, you have that option. Also included is a black and orange carrying case with a shoulder strap and there is a little zippered compartment near the top of the bag for the hook, included hex key, car key, flash drive, roll of film or whatever you'd like to store. A hand crank raises and lowers the center column and it moves very smoothly, not too easy and not too hard. The tripod can simply be converted for macro shots with low camera placement. For low angle photography using very wide legs, the bottom half of the center column can very easily be removed by simply unscrewing the hook and turning the bottom ring. Very smart and pretty fast, too. Having the option to attach anti slip spiked rubber feet is a great advantage in snow or sand and adds to the stability of the tripod. When the tripod arrives, the large rubber feet are snugly attached and I doubt that they will be lost when removed to use the spikes or standard rubber feet. The three sectioned legs are extremely easy to extend with a slight turn of the amply sized twist locks and each leg has clearly marked segments for perfect measuring. They can be locked at the top, another stability and security advantage, at three angles (25, 50 and 80 degrees). If desired, a camera bag or weight can be hung from the hook on the center column. The rubber foam casing at the top of each leg makes for a very comfortable feel and aid in moving the legs and carrying tripod. Although there's a little bubble level, mine was dry, so customer service is sending me a replacement level. It's small and may be obstructed when a head and large plate or camera are attached, but it's a nice little bonus nevertheless. Changing the camera screw from 1/4" to 3/8" is another simple process that takes seconds. I'm not sure if the orange anti-shock ring really does much, but it can't hurt. This carbon tripod can hold 39 pounds and it weighs around 8 pounds. It has an ample extension and I'm very satisfied with it in all regards for use in the studio as well as in the field.

UPDATE: Vanguard CS is out of this world. When they promised to send a replacement bubble level, I was politely told it would be 2-3 months before they were expected from the manufacturer. Several weeks ago, I received a padded envelope containing a brand new perfect bubble level. It's rare that follow-up isn't necessary in a situation like this, but Vanguard clearly maintained the information to fulfill this promise. If I could award another star in my review, I would!

title: Good impression after first month of use
text:
The TOMTOM GO2535 TM WTE is quite attractive with a large screen and smooth appearance but because of its size, this is a heavier GPS than many others. A magnetic plug attaches the power supplies either to a computer with its USB plug or to a car with its accessory power plug. As with most GPS devices, no "home" DC power supply is included. I have found the car mount to be great, easy to attach and remove from the windshield with a simple turn. My only complaint with the mount is that it takes some work to direct the device to a visible position and I fear that it will not last as long as the GPS. The magnetic plug slips into a cutout in the mount, allowing it to remain in position so the GPS can quickly be inserted or removed for safekeeping.
As for the functionality of the GPS, it has some problems, thereby preventing me from giving this a 5 star review. I'll simply list the Pros and Cons.
Pros:
Start up time is quick and option to start from last destination can save time if the satellite connection is delayed.
Menu options are easily learned even if at first they seem to include extra steps.
Responds quickly to need for alternate route when a turn is missed.
Ease in moving through functions on screen.
POIs are expansive and easy to discover
Map identifies a location I frequent which is not identified by any other GPS I've used.
Identifies traffic light cameras adequately. Have yet to receive speed camera warning.
Voice commands are intuitive and a little printed card is included if you're in need of prompting.
Connectivity to my Mac is easy and the option to automatically check for updates can save time.

Cons:
Speed is not always accurate. Often has my car going at 10 mph less than actual speed.
When setting a new destination, I've been unable to change the state unless I do it using the voice command. This may be possible, but I haven't had the time to investigate. Since I'm in a metropolitan area and may venture through 2 states and the District of Columbia in less than an hour, it's important for me to access the individual states.
When using phone through the GPS, although I can hear the conversation with no problem, the person on the other end of my call can't hear me clearly. Every time I've used it with a phone, the call has been dropped. I've never had a call dropped otherwise with my phone or other Bluetooth capable device.
Does not recognize voice commands at times.
Voice prompts are very frequent and I'd love to be able to reduce them but not turn it off.
Seldom comes up with the routes I usually take, even with a second try after selecting the Change Route option.

All in all, this is a good GPS navigation device and the lifetime updates are a definite advantage. I haven't traveled the wold with it, but will update my review as necessary with observations internationally. I do know the maps are on the device because I saw them when I performed the update last week and couldn't figure out how to get back to the USA on the device. For some reason, TOMTOM put me in the UK even though I'm registered in the USA and confirmed that selection.

What's interesting is that I still prefer my 3-year-old Navigon for its ease of use, accuracy and lovely displays, with two exceptions. I do not care for their customer service or necessity to download map updates to the device's SD card instead of doing a direct update on a Mac. This TOMTOM excels there and it comes in a very definite second for any GPS I've used. When the time comes for my beloved Navigon to bite the dust, I feel confident that I'll still be happy with this TOMTOM.

title: Versatile Velcro has a multitude of uses
text: Velcro Reusable Self-Gripping Cable Ties, 0.5 Inches x 8 Inches Long, Black, 100 Ties per Pack (91140) are addictive!  I needed something to tidy up several cables and cords and bought this package of more than I thought I would need in my lifetime.  Because I'm discovering so many applications for the ties, I'm likely going to need to reorder these before the year is up.  They arrive wrapped into two spools of conjoined ties which utilize every millimeter except for the little plug which pops out for slipping the tie into it's hole prior to wrapping around your neatened cords.  Packaged in a simple re-sealable plastic bag, there's nothing else to be discarded or recycled as it's all used!  Lightweight yet sturdy, they wrap even the smallest cable and I find that by wrapping the tie around and around, without cutting it, I'm able to reuse them on larger cables if I dispose of the smaller one.  Because the bag contains around 100, I can afford to use them on everything and I sure do!  The pile on the Velcro is rather flat, but that aids in it's not attracting unnecessary objects they come across while I'm wrapping the cables.  I like these so much that I'm considering wearing one as a bracelet!  I can decorate it with the popped out plugs so that absolutely nothing is wasted.

title: It's music to my ears
text: Although I've used a Plantronics Bluetooth earpiece, I must admit that I've never been crazy about the idea of an earpiece.  The Jabra CRUISER2 Bluetooth In-Car Speakerphone is so much more comfortable for me to use while driving!  After I realized that it would take a couple hours to charge the unit, I plugged it into the car and it was ready for pairing by the time I arrived home from my day of errands.  The pairing was intuitive, the voice basically guided me through the process, and I was making my first hands free, earpiece free call in a minute!  The clarity is excellent and the battery is outstanding.  Because it's so cold outside now, I've charged it again, but the battery was still alive.  I love the option to charge the unit either in the car or via the usb option.  This is a lightweight unit, small in size and the clip is lightweight but sturdy.  It doesn't contain extraneous buttons or lights, just what it needs.  Listening to music through the FM worked, but I doubt that I'll use the function often.  All in all, I really like this speakerphone and see why my favorite warehouse club store offered it through their coupon booklet recently.

title: Great also for SLR film camera & lenses
text: The Case Logic DCB-307 SLR Shoulder Bag is structurally sound, pleasing to the eye and compact enough to not weigh you down with heavy construction or materials.  It's streamlined shape stands on its own without toppling over, yet when carried with the optional detachable shoulder strap, it doesn't bounce around on my hip like many other "boxy" camera cases.  Although I tend to prefer bluish reds, the orangish red is a lovely contrasting interior and it's extremely well put together.  Having a lighter weight fabric for the interior reduces the weight and increases the flexibility of the adjustable padded sections, also giving a smoother touch when against my delicate camera gear.  In some cases, I wrap lenses even with their caps attached for added protection, but with this one, I don't think that's necessary.  I would not worry about any surfaces as long as they are separated from adjacent components with the not too thick or wide included removable pads.  The zipper pulls are smooth and strong and the attention to detail with a little fabric cover under which the pull is stored is much appreciated.  If I were to only use a case with a shoulder strap, I would be bothered by the upright handle, but since I personally use the handle to carry the case on many occasions, it doesn't bother me.  Using the case for an SLR film camera, I would have liked a single pocket to be a bit deeper for film canisters, but I can compensate by putting a roll or two inside the case or attach them to the shoulder strap.  I also find the shoulder strap to be comfortable and not bulky, easy to carry the goods.  I tend to not carry too much extraneous stuff with me, so this size is perfect!  Since I dedicate camera and equipment only to the case, I don't need more space or other compartments, hooks, baubles, fobs and the like.  The top loading zippered case meets my needs better than most and I'm grateful to be using this Case Logic DCB product.  I will definitely investigate the smaller cases for other uses, too!

title: Would love it to be Mac compatible
text: If this was Mac compatible, I'd buy many as gifts.  It's easy to set up and operate and the quality is great for the price.  The Logitech HD Webcam C510 with 720p Video and Swivel Design gives you the capability of live video and audio communication at a cost that's likely less than your cell phone.  The size is compact and fits nicely in a laptop USB as well as a desktop computer.  It would be great to have a family bundled pack!

title: Tom Tom grows on me every day
text:
My first GPS was a hand me down Magellan that I could never get to work. My second was a Navigon 2100 max 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator with Text-to-Speech which I absolutely love. Next was the Nextar SNAP5 Super Slim 5-Inch Portable GPS Navigator which I seldom use. This TomTom XL 340M LIVE (Lifetime Maps Edition) 4.3-Inch Portable GPS Navigator is better than all, but I still love the Navigon for it's quick re-routing and ease of operation. That being said, I'll describe my experiences over the past few weeks of owning this GPS.

Out of the box, it's necessary to hook the GPS up to your computer to check on the maps and register the product. I did remove the extra voices to create some space as was recommended by other reviewers, saving them to my computer before removing them from the device. I wasted time trying to find Tom Tom Home and like another reviewer, was able to get it through an internet search. The website listed on the box (as I recall) was not accurate and it's not intuitive. Once I had the software downloaded and installed, I began confirming that I had the most recent map installed. This can be done only once. I reviewed the online manual because there was none included and that was no big deal for me. No papers to lose. Although I did not register for the Live option or provide any information (payment), I've used the live services to do a Google search for a POI and the gas prices has already been used 3 times with success. I'm not crazy about having the computerized female voice as the only option for "speaking" street names, and the names are not always pronounced correctly or even completely, but it does work. The Navigon is far superior in this regard. The Tom Tom accesses satellites very quickly for me and I don't find myself waiting ever for the device to start navigating. The POIs are far superior and easier to access on the Tom Tom. Rerouting options were not intuitive for me and a friend showed me the way to select specific options. The mount is lousy in my opinion and the GPS has popped out on too many occasions for me to be comfortable. It's the weakest link for me in the entire package. I did have the audio set to automatically change with the speed of the vehicle but that drove me crazy with a computerized female voice yelling at me as I was driving the Beltway, so that's been changed and she's set at about 70% consistently. I wish I'd had this GPS a week earlier because I received a $150 speeding ticket in the mail from DC through a Radar unit. Once I recover from the shock and guilt, I'll travel the route again within the speed limit and see if the GPS warns me of the radar unit. It does alert me of the red light camera installed (but not operational) which is permanently installed on my street corner. The first few times I heard the alert, I had no idea what was going on, until I read the online manual again. I now also set the speed alert to let me know when I'm exceeding a speed limit, but the limits have not always been current. One day, I will notify Tom Tom of several routing major screw ups I've discovered but that's going to have to wait until I have some time on my hands. The Navigon is superior in this regard of more direct routing and fewer errors. All in all, I like this and would recommend the product. Perhaps when my Navigon Fresh Maps subscription expires I'll remove the second GPS from my car, but for now I just can't give up Sarah (the Navigon text to speech voice).

title: Wired way to watch from afar
text: The Lorex LNE1001 Easy Connect Network IP Remote Surveillance Camera (White) was not too difficult for me to connect after reading the materials and checking the Lorexcctv website.  A lengthy brochure describes the step-by-step sequence for setup which must be followed in order, but to install on a Mac, I had to go to the website for instructions.  The camera is small in size and a short white ethernet cable was included.  Unfortunately, for our needs, we'll be getting a wireless surveillance camera, but this was an inexpensive way to get started.  We'll also be looking for a camera that enables us to record on a Mac which is not an option with this camera and the reason I've deducted a star from the review.

title: So happy and feeling safer now
text: I'm one of the folks who had a hard drive crash without having backed up for several months.  That was all it took for me to realize the importance of backing up my hard drive regularly and not simply putting current files on a flash drive.  I'd been using a Western Digital drive for the past three or four years, then was told that hard drives have a limited life span.  That made sense, so I decided to replace the external drive which is used to backup my MacBook.  I almost purchased the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex 500 GB USB 2.0 Ultra-Portable External Hard Drive STAA500100, then decided that I don't take the external drive with me and didn't need it to be portable.  Enter the Seagate FreeAgent GoFlex Desk 2 TB Desktop External Hard Drive STAC2000100, a shiny black drive that looks much sleeker and way more shiny than the dull Western Digital.  2 TB seemed like more than I need, but I went for it anyway.  Before the package arrived, I watched the videos available on the Seagate website, so I was prepared for this drive and felt comfortable using it as my new backup drive.  My only question was whether or not to format it for use with Mac and PC or just the Mac.  Decided on the Mac only and didn't install the other options onto my MacBook.  Since I use Time Machine, I immediately proceeded to backup the hard drive.  Not having purchased the optional Firewire, eSATA or USB 3.0, the transfer is not faster than on the other external drives I've used, but this one sure is quiet and it's much nicer to look at.  It also doesn't weigh as much as other desktop external drives.  Looks like the attractive Seagate sleek shape, just bigger.  There is no button to push, just plug in and connect, then go to Time Machine.  I cannot review the included Memeo backup because I've not installed it.  Can't imagine that it would be better than Time Machine.  This meets my needs and exceeds my expectations.  It also looks nicer when locked up in my fire retardant portable safe than any other drive.

title: I like it but my neighbors may not
text:
When the huge box arrived, I thought I'd made a mistake by ordering the Altec Lansing VS4621 Octane 7, 2.1 Computer Speaker. Fortunately, the shipping box was much larger than the item, so my blood pressure was quickly reduced. The speakers do have a small footprint and the taller contemporary shape is quite attractive. The subwoofer size is compact enough and unobtrusive in it's solid black boxy shape. I now have it placed on the bare wood floor, so my downstairs neighbors are likely not too happy with me right now. I will be placing a small carpet beneath it this afternoon.

Installation was intuitive and quite simple -- the most time consuming aspect was removing all the plastic. I didn't even notice the visual directions for set up are imprinted on the inside top flaps of the box. Because there is no bottom covering on the speakers by design, I'm especially careful when moving the speakers from one position to another. You'll get a different sound depending upon what surface you place the speakers. In the past hour, I've listened to Bob Dylan, The Grateful Dead, Johnny Cash, Radiohead, Sigur Ros, M.I.A., my Dad's dictation of his life story, Charles Mingus Lama Karta, The Black Lips, David Sedaris and Luka Bloom. The least pleasing on these speakers was a classical piece by Schubert which demonstrated the "muddy" nature of this sort of speaker system. Now this is a wide variety of music and sounds and my impression is that this is a really nice system which for the most part I would recommend. There's also an AUX input on the front of the speaker with controls so it can be hooked up to another electronic device of choice. Being able to adjust the volume, treble and bass gives me simple control options but by using the iTunes Equalizer, I can adjust to my preference with each cut. Throughout the years, I've purchased and used various speakers for my stereo, iPod, computer and entertainment systems, and I'm very impressed with these! Can't now wait to watch a movie and hear how these speakers reproduce the sound!

title: POI's are nice but it confused East and West
text: I've had this now for several weeks and have used this side by side with my Navigon.  Living in Northern Virginia, traffic can be a problem, and changing routes is very normal.  With the Nextar SNAP5, I can be miles down the road before it kicks in with another route.  More disconcerting is  driving East on I-66 in Falls Church, and having the voice tell me I am going West.  When signage tells me I'm going a direction, the compass tells me I'm going in that same direction and the GPS voice tells me differently, I panic and want to pull off the road but I know better.  This system is large in screen, but that screen displays many icons and a map that is eclipsed by the Navigon 4.3 smaller size in package.  Startup is much faster in the Navigon than the Nextar SNAP5 under the exact same conditions, as I turn them on at the same time in the same place and wait for the navigation to begin.  It has taken me in very complicated and inefficient routes which would make Euler roll in his grave.  The text to voice function is less clear than the Navigon and the voice often breaks in and out with delivery, making the words unrecognizable.  I do not like the coiled cable at all, but do like the placement of the connection better than the one on the Navigon.  The map representation on the screen is unappealing and difficult to read in either option available and it's extremely difficult to see during bright days.  I sometimes cannot identify the map at all, regardless of how I position and reposition the device.  I have not used the MP3 function and never will, so that's wasted on me.  The POI's are nicely organized and it's interesting to find spots from a database that is very outdated which haven't existed for years.  It's a great concept if it is current but otherwise is a waste of time and can cause problems if you head to a spot that doesn't exist.  I do not know if updates are available as they are (with subscription purchase) for the Navigon.  This also does not have a traffic update availability as does the Navigon.  Since I don't use it without power from the vehicle, I cannot comment upon the battery life.  A stylus is included, but I also haven't used that expect in a rare occasion.  The carrying case is nice if you want to carry it, but I have yet to use the case.  Very nice to have a power cord to charge it away from the car.  All in all, the price of less than a hundred and a half is reasonable if you want the MP3 function but for me, I much prefer the Navigon.

title: I'm sold on AmazonBasics cables!
text:
I wonder what makes HDMI cables so costly. Spending over fifty dollars seems ridiculous to me, so I've been waiting for a reasonably priced, high quality, flexible cable and I found exactly what I needed with the AmazonBasics Braided Ultra High Speed HDMI Cable at 6.5 feet! Costing substantially less than comparable cables I've researched and held in my hands, this stands heads and shoulders above the others and I'm thrilled to now have my new HDTV hooked up to Cox Cable via this HDMI cable rather than the standard cables provided by the company. Without an HDMI cable, I was not receiving the full options available but don't regret waiting to get this brand and model from Amazon; I would have spent far much more money to purchase another brand and it likely would not be as flexible and substantial as this. My television is providing much more entertainment today than it was yesterday and the HD channels are overwhelmingly wonderful now! Wish I'd utilized the HDMI capability sooner, but I'm happy to have this particular cable now and more money in the wallet for popcorn and beverages.

The images provided by Amazon cover just about everything included with the exception of a little black twisty tie. Nothing is wasted in this packaging, it can be reused or recycled and you do not need tools to access the cable from the packaging. There is no chemical scent and you'll receive no cuts on the fingers from hard plastic packaging.

If you're in the market for a longer braided cable, AmazonBasics also offers a 9.8 Feet model.

title: Average ear buds at an average price
text: For variety, the Altec Lansing UHP606 Backbeat Pro Reference Earphones are a fine change from my Ultimate Ears SuperFi 3 Studio Noise Isolating Earphones when my ears need an alternate bud phone.  If the lighterweight and more flexible cables are bent and wrapped around the back of the ear as they are with the Ultimate Ears, the length is just about equal.  These are simply the cables into the ear buds.Both have a mini plug w/ a right angle, but the Altec Lansing is about 1/2" further extended when inserted.  The cables are less rigid than the Ultimate Ears and are encased in clear plastic rather than the more usual black.  They look cute.  The sound, on the other hand is only average.  I like the zippered small case which is included and most ears likely will have a satisfactory fit from the included assortment of silicone tips.  External sounds are restricted with a nice tight fit, but the range of this audio could be improved.  The price is what I expect to pay for an average pair of ear buds which are better than many, but not the best available.

title: Groovy GPS when used with Fresh Maps update
text:
I first bought this GPS several months ago when Costco had it on sale but ended up returning it because I was not pleased with the time it took to recognize my location. More specifically, I would be on the Capital Beltway surrounding DC and the stern female voice would repeatedly tell me to make a U-turn. Impossible. I then used a friend's hand-me-down Magellan which would not hold a charge, not recognize the location and simply needed to be retired. Enter Amazon and their great price for the Navigon 2100 max. Since I'd read that the device was improved with the Fresh Maps update, I purchased Fresh Maps and I highly recommend you do the same if you're contemplating this beautifully sleek GPS.

If you have a PC, you are able to upgrade by connecting the GPS directly to your computer. If you have a Mac, then it's a little more complicated but so worth the effort. You need to remove the SD card from the GPS and transfer the downloaded software to the SD card with a card reader/writer and then reinsert the card into the GPS. I kept a backup of the original software on my hard drive just in case, but have had no need since the upgrade immediately worked. Now on to what I really like about this system.

The 4.3 inch screen is easier to view than the 3.5, particularly if you have many of the POI's selected for display. I first chose them all, then realized they obstructed my map because I'm in the DC metro area. Mine connects with a satellite in only a few seconds each time and reroutes immediately if I change my route. Previously, it would announce that it was rerouting, but it no longer does that, just does the work. Three choices for trip planning are fine enough for me, I tend to choose the Optimal Route. I love being able to select different destinations, too, if I'm going to different places. The address book is easy to access and locations are easier to save. Traffic support is a great asset and now comes free with this device -- I've been saved from many a jam and not have to be tuned into the radio for traffic reports on the 8's. I have the screen set to automatically change from day to night and have had no problem viewing the screen at any time. With the new software, you are able to turn off the GPS from the touchscreen in addition to the usual power button at the upper right hand edge. I love the 2D/3D view, especially when I'm approaching a multi-lane area and I'm unsure as to which lane I need to take. Two voice selections are fine for my needs, Dagmar is more pleasant, but the higher pitched Sarah gives the text to speech option (TTS), so that's the one I've selected. She's not very pushy, either, as some voices I've heard on GPS systems. In the pre-update version, her voice sounded more Germanic, I assume from its origin of Germany, but it's not as odd now. For me, this GPS is intuitive to use and I can make any adjustments from the touchscreen very quickly. I've yet to have a freeze of the system and it has always known where I was with one exception when I was off road on a gravel trail.

My only real criticism of this unit is the rigid cord which extends straight out of the bottom of the device, being so inflexible that I sometimes dislodge it when attaching the mount to the windshield. I'm not crazy about the mount either, but am trying to decide how to approach a new mounting system. I do not want the display obstructing my field of vision but am not ready yet to get a sandbag type dashboard mount. I'm thinking of constructing something myself using the little plastic disc which was included with this GPS system. Also included is the USB cord, but no AC power supply.

title: Perfect in a crowded airport or wifi spot
text: Yes, this mini surge protector/dual usb charger is perfect in a small bathroom, kitchen and hotel room, but I have found it to be even more perfect in a crowded airport where one outlet is surrounded by electronic device users hovering around until a flight takes off, thereby freeing up an outlet or two.  With this multiplier, you can enable three users to plug into one outlet and bring joy to two usb charging devices as their power is refreshed.  I must admit that I didn't even realize this had a swivel plug until it was pointed out to me after I'd used it in public a few times.  I'd purchased this in a combo pack with the Belkin swivel usb hub and didn't even take this out of the packaging until I headed out for an airplane trip a couple months ago.  Ironically, I've found this to be more useful than the hub which isn't as sturdy and doesn't swivel very well for me.  I now take this with me any time I head out with my laptop because I like the option of plugging in, particularly when I'm having a cup of coffee with dozens of others who also want to plug in and turn on.  If anything happens to this one, I'll replace it pronto.

title: No complaints
text: At the suggested retail price, I would never have made this purchase, but because it was a reasonable Gold Box offer, I leapt toward my first bluetooth earpiece.  The pink was not a selling point, but I preferred that to a more common black contraption, and I'm not at all disappointed.  It's more of a mauve than pink which was more pleasing to me.  It synched up immediately with my cell phone and I suspect it will do the same when this phone is replaced in 2009.  The manual was easy to read and understand and I had no difficulty placing the earpiece into the lovely leather carrying case/charger or removing it to use.  Although some have complained about short battery time, I have not experienced that and have not have the battery die at any time.  It is easy to check the battery level by depressing the two buttons on the device and observing the number of red flashes for remaining power.  The small size might be easy to lose for some, but I'm aware of that possibility and exercise caution when I put it in my bag or pocket.  Because of that small size, it takes only a second to plug the earpiece into the ear and I do not wear it unless I am on a call.  Realizing that it's lightweight, I am also cautious in more windy situations.  I had only one experience with a less than perfect call and was a bit disturbed until I realized the static was generated from the other end of the call.  In general, I like the fit, clarity, ease of use, and don't feel like I have a growth erupting from my ear.  I'd buy this again.

title: Lightweight which may not be a good thing for swiveling up and down
text: The first Belkin Swivel Hub I bought just wouldn't stay in the position I wanted, so I returned it which was a good thing because when I removed it from my MacBook, the hub literally fell apart in my hand.  I'd had it for less than a week so there was no problem.  The replacement also doesn't stay in position, but it really makes sense that it won't because the entire hub is lightweight and USB plugs and cables have a weight to them especially when you have 4 plugged into the device.  I've learned to live with this and am happy to be able to swivel it around and expose my second USB port rather than having it obstructed from usability.  The shape of this hub allows for a very comfortable fit in a briefcase or laptop carrier or even a file folder for that matter because it's less than an inch thick.  My computer has had no difficulty reading any device plugged into the hub whether it's a hard drive, iPod, camera or printer.  I was fortunate to purchase this bundled with the Belkin BZ103050vTVL Mini Surge Protector/Dual USB Charger which I also find to be a useful addition to computer peripherals.

title: Almost a 5-star keyboard
text:
This recent purchase is a backup keyboard and I'm not using it yet because the coffee I spilled did not affect the performance of the old keyboard. The keyboard in the picture has been in use since January of 2017. The fact that I purchased a 2nd one in case the original stops working tells you how much I like using it.

Pros: the ergonomic layout is better than most split keyboards; it is super quiet--I interview people on the telephone and type while they are speaking--with my former keyboard, people would ask what all the noise was and could I hear them okay--this keyboard eliminates that distraction completely; battery life is long.

Cons: several letters have disappeared (E, R, T, S, D, F, C and most of the G and N) so it is a good thing that I'm a "touch typist" and don't need to look at the keyboard much; I don't have small hands but it is a bit tough to reach the & key while pressing the shift key; the wrist rest shows a lot of wear after a short time.

Overall, I recommend the keyboard if you are looking for a quiet and ergonomic keyboard.

title: You can use it with or without the very easily magnetic attachable riser to raise the wrist rest
text:
I've been using this keyboard and mouse since it arrived on 12/27/16 and it fits my use perfectly. I work from a home office and got a treadmill desk for Christmas and needed a wireless keyboard so I can move it back and forth between the treadmill side and the keyboard tray on the other half of the desk for when I'm seated. I got so used to a split ergonomic keyboard and had difficulty finding this style in a wireless keyboard.

This is low profile enough to fit under the desk when I slide the keyboard tray out of the way. You can use it with or without the very easily magnetic attachable riser to raise the wrist rest; I use it without the riser when on the treadmill and with it when I'm seated so this is a great feature for me. I suppose it is somewhat equivalent to using the legs on traditional keyboards.

A large part of my day is spent on the phone with executives and I often type while talking with people (conducting telephone interviews). This keyboard is so much quieter than my old one! Now people don't even know that I'm typing while speaking with them. It did take me a day or two to get used to the keyboard layout since it is a bit different from my old wired ergonomic keyboard.

The mouse seemed too big initially but now I really like it.

I use the number keypad a lot and having it separate from the keyboard is sometimes not the most convenient. However, if it was attached to the keyboard, the set up would be too big for my keyboard tray and mouse so it is more of a positive than a negative with the new treadmill desk set up.

Overall, I am very happy with it and recommend it wholeheartedly. You will especially like it if you are used to using an ergonomic keyboard.

title: I love it!
text:
I love the ring doorbell. It looks nice at my front door, especially with the option of different colored faceplates, and it works well. The video and sound quality is good. The app is easy to use, and I like the ability to get notifications on my phone when there's motion at my front door. I dont live in a high crime area but it's always nice to have that extra set of eyes on my home. Plus it comes in handy for me because while I'm at work I'm able to see my son leaving and coming home from school every day.

The battery lasts a long time before needing to be charged. I've had it for over a month already and I'm still on my original charge. I ordered a spare battery so that when I need to charge it I can just switch them out and not have to worry about interruption in service. The battery charges with a regular phone charger so it's easy and convenient.

My only complaint with the ring doorbell is that in my situation the motion detection is almost too good. I live in a townhouse that is only about 15-20 ft from the street so anytime a car drives by or someone walks down the sidewalk, it triggers my camera. In the settings there is the ability to adjust the field of view slightly but it hasn't been enough to avoid the false alarms. I dont really fault the product for this. It's doing what it's meant to do. Just keep that in mind if you intend on using it in a high traffic area like I do. Other than that, I've been very happy with it and I'm glad I got it.

title: Pretty cool
text:
Over the last couple of years I've been slowly adding more and more of the alexa technology to our home. I have smart plugs, smart bulbs, echo dots in each room, etc. I recently purchased a ring doorbell and liked the idea of being able to view the camera from this echo show device. This has been working great. I also like seeing the weather report for the week when I ask alexa about the weather, seeing song lyrics while listening to amazon music, and so many other things that just make it easier to visually see instead on just hearing what alexa tells you. But I do have one complaint. The screen will go to sleep after a while of not being used. Now normally I dont mind that. It just goes to a black screen with a clock on it. But sometimes I'd like the option of keeping it awake. For example when I'm listening to music. It shows lyrics and song info for whatever you're listening to but after a few songs, the music continues but the screen blacks out. I have to wake alexa up or tap the screen to get it to come back on. Same goes for if I'm reading an article or recipe or something that I may have to revert back and forth to the screen, I dont want to have to wake it up to finish reading what I'm doing. I've tried searching through the settings and I've even searched on the internet for solutions but it doesn't look like there is one. Apparently I'm not the only person who thinks this should be a setting that we can choose to turn on or off.
So, overall, this is a cool device and I'm happy with it. It does everything I need it to do. But it's a little frustrating and disappointing when there should be a simple solution to an annoying problem.

title: Be sure to search for open source maps before you buy them from garmin.
text:
This unit is night and day above any car-based GPS I've ever used. Tons of functionality, great accuracy, and performance. The ability to load custom tracks, routes, and maps from the internet is fantastic as well. I like the form factor (no antenna sticking out), and the screen is very readable in pretty much any conditions. The interface is intuitive and easy to use unless you're trying to type in city or street names, in which case it's pretty time consuming. The battery life is fantastic as well, I've had mine on for over 24 hours and it's still at full charge.

The base map that this unit comes with is pretty much worthless. I would suggest searching online for free open source maps, as there are plenty of good ones available, including topo and routable ones.

I do have a couple issues with it (hence the 4 stars) -
* Smallish screen - LCD screens are so cheap these days, there is no reason why this thing couldn't have had a 1" bigger screen. It makes my iPhone feel like a big screen TV. The resolution is good, so it's still very usable, but it makes trying to navigate around the map on the unit itself slightly less enjoyable.
* The joystick button on the top - this should be on the bottom. Buttons go on the bottom, screen goes on the top, otherwise you hand covers the screen when you're doing things - Basic electronics design people!

title: First one was great; second one turned into a dud
text: I had purchased one of these over a year ago in order to be able to listen to my iPod in the car. It was also useful in that it doubled as a car charger for my phone (or the iPod, as the need arose on long trips). However, that initial iTrip was lost when someone broke into my vehicle this summer. Having had no problems with the first one (other than the occasional background static or need to switch frequencies, as mentioned by other reviewers), I immediately went out and bought another one to replace it. The only difference I could see between them was that the first one was black and the new one was silver and black. At any rate, it worked great for a while. But I have had it about four months now, and it doesn't work more often than it does. The USB port still charges devices with no problem, but the cable for channeling the iPod to the radio apparently is kaput. I will be in the middle of listening to a song or podcast when the power suddenly dies on the iTrip. The radio switches to loud static and the display on the iTrip goes blank. Occasionally I can get the connection to resume by unplugging and replugging the iTrip into the power port, wiggling the plug or the wires...and sometimes nothing works. Haven't pulled my receipt and warranty, but I suspect I have no recourse at this point. Very disappointing for something that costs $50+ (after tax). Not sure what else I can use to listen to my iPod in the car since I don't have an auxiliary jack, but I'll be looking for another alternative unless Griffin will replace this one.

Instead of pulling out the the foam chunks all the way, I sort of carved them out with a sharp pair of scissors to fit my guns. Then I put some Gorilla tape around the edge of the piece of foam, so I have sort of a "tray". Then I can lift it out, to where I have ammo stored underneath.

As you can see, I still have room left in the lower level. I'd love to fill it with a 22 revolver, but I guess we'll see if my numbers match someday, hahaha!

title: Sounds Amazing!  Better than the Angle 2 IMO
text:
I actually use this as my PC speaker (when I am not using it on adventures) as it fits neatly onto the base of my 27" BenQ monitor.

Does not have ANY annoying "features" like most other Bluetooth speakers do, such as beep prompts and creepy voices that tell you the status of your speaker, when you are trying to listen to music. Instead of that crap, it has an extremely useful auto-shutoff feature. As a result, I hardly ever have to charge this thing. It is smart enough to shut off when you are not using it, and stay on when you are!

I initially purchased the Angle 2, and while I did like it, my audio snobbery forced me to keep looking. I purchased the 3, and have not looked back. Sounds great with any type of music I have thrown at it. Ruggedly built, and aesthetically pleasing to boot!

title: Sounds Awesome with my KEF Eggs!
text:
I always wanted a Yamaha Aventage Receiver, but until now they all had features I didn't need, let alone wanted to pay for; Enter the RX-A550.

This receiver is designed for people like me who appreciated great sound quality, but could care less about features such as dual HDMI out, dual subs, 7 channel speaker capability, multi-room listening, or Sirius adaptability. In the past I have always been duped into paying for those features, because that was the only way I could get a nice quality WiFi AV Receiver with the functions I wanted.

Couldn't agree more with another reviewer that getting this receiver is really not worth it unless you have high end speakers. Movies and music sound rich and detailed when this unit is paired with my KEF Eggs. Really an enjoyable listening experience, which I would take over a mediocre 9.2 set-up any day of the week.

My favorite feature of these newer Yamaha receivers is the Virtual CINEMA FRONT option. Personally, I prefer all sound to be coming from the front of the room. I know the thought of this makes some die-hard type-A AV people cringe, but hey it's all about personal preference.

This unit is made in Malaysia, unlike my previous lower end Yamaha receiver, which was made in China. Malaysia has been churning out high quality electronics for some time now. One example of that is the "Boston Acoustics Recepter" (not the inferior HD version). I purchased my Malaysian Recepter new in the '90s and it still works as new. Recepters are still selling used for at least 1/3 of original sticker price, unlike just about any other piece of electronics from the '90's.

The Yamaha iOS App has decent look and feel, but the UI that you see on your TV screen has an archaic aura matched only by that of a Commodore 64. This however does not bother me in the least. I bought this receiver to listen too, not look at. Much of the time I am controlling the receiver with my iPhone listening to music, and the TV isn't even on. There other receivers that have prettier user interfaces, but few are as long lasting or rich sounding as the Yamaha Aventage line...

title: Tomato Compatible and Cheaper Alternative to ASUS RT-AC66U
text:
I picked this router up at another online retailer as soon as I spotted it was on sale. I had my eye on the Tenda 1800/1801 routers for a while before that though, as these seem to be the only decent Gigabit / AC routers that are directly compatible with Tomato right out of the box, that don't break the bank!

My router is essentially the same thing as the much more expensive ASUS RT-AC66U, but with less memory. Having less memory on a router is not really the same thing as less memory on a computer. In other words, most people (including myself) will not notice the difference.

Hardware Look and Feel:
This Tenda sports the basic router design, and includes wall mounting screw holes that are 6” apart, and 3 movable antennas that are easy to install. There is lots of good ventilation on the sides and bottom, and a glossy white top. Altogether, the router seems will made, and doesn't feel cheap at all. Glad to say that it doesn't have a gimmicky cylindrical shape, or a stupid upright design, with an even more stupid non-adjustable plastic stand. I don’t mind at all that I can't take selfies next to my neat looking stylish black router to post on Facebook; Boring routers are just plain under-rated!

Stock Firmware:
I spent about 5-minutes poking around in the stock firmware before flashing to Tomato. To me the stock firmware seemed like an unpolished version of Asus firmware. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but why settle for stock when there is a specific version of the very stable, configurable, and admired Tomato USB written just for routers just like this! Enter Shibby K26RT-AC...

Tomato Flashing Process:
No feverish searching the internet for firmware “that will work” with your router, simply go to the Shibby download page, find the latest version for your router, download the compressed file, and unzip it.
Then unplug your WAN cable, open your routers firmware page, go to tools, upgrade, navigate to the folder your just unzipped, select the .TRX file, click upgrade, and wait about 10 minutes. Once it is done, you might want to do a factory reset in Tomato to clear the RAM.

That’s it people, no messing around with cumbersome flash utilities, no 30/30/30 resets in restore mode while holding your nose and saying the alphabet backwards in Pig Latin while crossing your fingers that you won’t brick your router. This one is as simple as it gets!

title: Punchy, Tough, and Compact.  Not Boomy!
text:
My KEF C4 Sub came with one of the less popular speaker sets from KEF (white eggs). I thought I would review the sub separately for those who are shopping for just a sub.

The C4 is a small, unobtrusive 8" sub that is boasts an external volume control, along with an external crossover. It also has a removable power cord (standard PC power cord I believe), a phase switch, and a power switch. The sub itself sounds just awesome; Very punchy, and not boomy. I compared it against a 10" Polk, and a 12" Harman Kardon. Performance wise, the C4 defecated on both the Polk and the HK subs, despite being way smaller.

The sound from the C4 also blends well with my Kef eggs. I hate it when you can "hear" subs annoyingly reverbing and booming along with your music, and am glad to say this one does not seem to have that problem

I use the C4 mostly for music listening, but it also sounds superb with movies.

The sub is built solidly and tough. My Boxer (Carl) regularly puts his front paws up on the sub and stomps hard as he looks out the window barking menacingly at whatever kindly old man, or Christian mom with a stroller happens to be passing by. After a couple years of that, it still cleans up nicely in a few seconds with a little bit of mild cleaner. I use a highly diluted mixture of Sal Suds in water in a squirt bottle myself.

I have had this sub for some time now, and have no plans to replace it at all. This is unusual for me, as I tend to get tired of electronics very rapidly, and start shopping for the latest and greatest and shiniest whatever...

title: Bluetooth and Wi-Fi are Reliable!
text:
Since I am a fan of audio equipment, I usually replace my receiver every 2-3 years. I purchased the Onkyo TX-NR626 on WOOT a little over a year ago. This unit replaced a Yamaha RX-V671.  I will try to leave things out of this review that other reviews have already talked about.

Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
To my surprise, I have never had any issues with Wi-Fi or Bluetooth. My Wi-Fi network uses WPA2, and I use a variety of Android devices to Bluetooth to the receiver. This means that from a back room of the house, I can turn the receiver on via the Android App, and Bluetooth whatever I want to whoever is in the living room.  One time out of the blue I made thunder play loudly to an unsuspecting room full of people and animals. The pandemonium that was created as a result of that, was both memorable and delightful.

Remote
The remote on my RX-V671 never saw much use, due to how cumbersome it was to use  The remote on this Onkyo is so easy to use, that I now use it instead of my Logitech Harmony.  I use the Onkyo remote to control my receiver (of course), the TV set, the xBox, and the LG Blu-ray player.

Sound / Setup
It sounds as good as the RX-V671, but is easier to use.  I felt that the Yamaha had too many unnecessary settings, which actually made me want to play with it less.  What I don’t like about the Onkyo though, is that the labels for the buttons on the front of the receiver are hard to see.

The famous HDMI sound issue
This happened to me twice over the last year.  Each time I needed to unplug it, and plug it back in to resolve the issue.  I don’t think this is related to heat, at least in my case, as I have plenty of room on top for ventilation which is open on either end to enable a cross draft.

title: Exchanged HD 518 for these
text:
Why I chose the 439 over the rest

Clamping force and comfort
I have a large head, and have read comments from other large headed reviewers stating that some of the other big brands are not comfortable for long periods of time. I can tell you that these are comfortable for both my large head, and others with smaller heads that have tried them. Not sure how they would be for large ears though. I have regular sized ears, and they fit perfectly.

Replaceable Cord
These are the only headphones in the lower-mid-range closed back Sennheiser line that has a replaceable cord. You would think that the 449 does (since it is a higher number) but it does not. Yeah I am pretty good with a soldering iron, but that doesn't mean that I actually want to use it.

Why I exchanged the 518 for these

Sound isolation
The open back design of the 518 was more prohibitive to my lifestyle than I had originally anticipated, as they leak more sound than I thought. You could actually hear the sound leakage in the next room if the doors were open, and the house was fairly quiet.

I watch a lot of cartoons and strange independent dramas. I also listen to ancient heavy metal, along with a smattering of other unlikely musical genres. Few people want to hear that combination of things spewing from my headphones. Now I can enjoy watching things like the Rectify (Especially the Drip Drip episode) without having to explain later to others in the next room.

Roku and Smart Phone use.
The 518 has a 1/4 plug, and the 439 has 1/8. I like to use the headphones with my Roku 3 remote a lot, and having a 1/4 to 1/8 adapter in my pocket with the Roku remote adds a lot of bulk. On the other hand, whenever I want to use the 439 on my old school stereo, I just use the included 1/8 to 1/4 adapter, which isn't really a hassle at all.

title: Very good Gaming monitor
text:
Received my Dell D2719HGF and it is everything I hoped it would be. Bright, Good colors and contrast after getting it set up and tweaked to my liking.
Spent the day testing it out with my 2 gaming PCs, One with an AMD RX 480, And another with an NVIDIA RTX2080 and thought I'd share the results, since there have been a few questions about compatibility and setup.
This monitor supports Freesync from 40-144Hz over both HDMI and DP with a recent AMD Graphics card. The newer NVIDIA cards also work fine using adaptive sync, but only over DP.

For the people who can't get 144 Hz on their AMD Graphics card, try going to Windows 10's "Display Settings" page, open Advanced display settings. Open Display adapter properties for your connected Display. Click on "List All Modes" and,using the drop-down menu, set your resolution/Refresh rate to "1920 by 1080, True Color (32 bit), 144Hertz". After that, you should be running at 144 Hz. Enable freesync in your monitor's OSD, then you should be able to enable freesync through AMD Radion Settings.

If using an NVIDIA card, it's much simpler. Use NVIDIA Control Panel's Display settings to change the resolution to 1920 x 1080 (native) under the PC header, setting the Refresh Rate to 144Hz. Enable Freesync on the Monitor's OSD, Then you can set up adaptic sync using Nvidia Control Panel/Display/Set up G-Sync.

title: So far, so good!
text:
I ordered this to replace a dying ATI Wavy-On X850 Pro (heat issues, slightly wavy screen). It not only came earlier than indicated, but it was wrapped well and securely to survive its shipping (from China). In this box, with an "old" AMD Sempron Socket A Barton core, running at 3400+ speed (2.4 GHz), in an Asrock KT880 (VIA chipset) mobo, it performs barely faster than a BFG 6800 128-megger I scored off of Ebay for forty bucks. This is due to:

a) the Athlon's memory throughput is about half the Opteron's or the hi-end P4's

b) you lose some throughput in the AGP bridge chip, compared to a straight PCI Express connection, which the 7x00 series was designed for.

But this is not really a caveat...because:

It is safe to say that I can practically max out the aniso and AA without much of a slowdown: clearly the card is not really the worst bottleneck. I do not have to overclock it for increased performance (rather a waste in a box that won't keep up with it). Additionally, it runs cool enough so that CPU/video/case interior ambient temps ARE NOT AT ALL an issue. Older games such as Far Cry 1+2, Quake 4, etc. run with maximum eye candy and fluidity at 1280x1024, lowest framerates are WELL within playability. I can crank the AA and aniso higher without slowdown than with the stout little BFG 6800 with its massive copper heatpipe sink, which is living in a nearly identical box.

It works very well with Windows 2000, XP (no doubt later versions of Windows, though I won't touch any more Microsoft bloated spyware metadata-indexing, and internet bandwidth theft datamining crap with a barge-pole after my experiences with Vista and Windows 7---crApple is just as bad, and they do it with this graceless, insipid, effete, snobbish attitude common to Apple, as opposed to the in-your-face, "screw you" you get from Micro$othoth!), and Linux (which is what I use for real security and productivity)... I could likely get it to work with Windows 98/ME as well (the 6800 does), but why bother?

The card installed flawlessly after the S.O.P. of cleaning out all the orphaned registry driver nonsense ATI typically leaves behind on its departure. It has been working without issue since. What more can one ask for?

Nvidia's support for WIndows 2000 is head-and-shoulders better than ATI's. Ditto with Linux. Nothing new here, please move along, I'm not evangelizing, just speaking from experience. I haven't seen too many software problems with either red or green guys with XP and above.

If it dies anytime in the near future, which I seriously doubt will happen (lifts hat, knocks...), I'll review THAT too...

Thank you, Tangca, for not only shipping it promptly and packaging it properly, but for also making what appears to be a solid, quality video card to replace old AGP stuff! I am ordering a 256-megger version of this to upgrade someone else's box, and will likely happily review it as well!

If the next one is near as good as this one, I know who'll be on my top list for my recommendations/upgrades!

Thank you, again!

title: Returned, will get the official one
text:
This item is one version of the OSSC, and turns out it is not case-compatible with the official one, having several different components populated on the board, so it will not fit in the normal OSSC cases.

It is not at all confidence-inspiring that the manufacturer here deviated from the official board layout and component selection. The PSU is extremely cheap, and some things are just incorrect.

Some of the components I noticed were different are:

- the screen: The height of the screen is quite a bit lower than what's shown in pictures of the official OSSC, and on closer examination, it appears the screen was soldered to the wrong side of the board because of layout issues.
- the buttons: the buttons here have yellow nubs on top, but the official one has low profile tactile buttons. This is another point where 3D printed cases made for this (such as those sold by Laser Bear) will interfere with this OSSC, preventing the case from closing.
- The audio select switch: the switch is mounted to the bottom of the PCB instead of the top. There appear to be traces for the switch on the top of the PCB, but it's not clear why they were mounted to the bottom of the board. Again, this is an issue because cases will have allowance for this switch, and expect the switch to be located on the top of the PCB.

Given that these components were swapped or moved, I can't be certain about the rest of the component choices, and given how cheap the power supply is, I'm not confident at all that the manufacturers here prioritized quality over price in any way whatsoever.

* The friction knob is pretty much useless, as it has too little range of adjustment between being fully tight and completely loose and doesn't stay where it's set.
