* The bottom plate (where it joins with the tripod) does not have grooves like the other head does, so with enough torque (not even a lot), it can twist free. This is even after tightening the three immobilizing tension screws as much as I dare.
* The pan/pan lock is not as useful as I thought it might be, particularly because there is no built-in level, and I paid more for this feature over the 496RC2, but pretty much never use it.

Time Warner online activation communicated with the modem but then failed. This sent me to activation support where a polite lady in India wasted an hour of my time. Finally I got through to "level 3 tech support" and my modem was activated in less than 5 minutes. The issue was because the modem had been registered to a previous owner (refurbished -- duh!) and the activation needed a lvl 3 tech authorization to move it from one account to the next (kicker is that it was likely TWC who sold these refurbs in the first place!).
Please learn from my mistake, try the online activation if you like but if it fails after already recognizing your new modem (step 2), give up and call TWC "level 3 tech support." Make sure you have the MAC # which is on the bottom of the modem.
Or if you have any alternative to TWC then do yourself a solid and switch providers.

title: Great picture but deal breaking annoyances
text:
The picture quality of the HD26 is wonderful, very happy on that front. It's great for gaming and Far Cry 4 has been great fun using this projector. However, I have some major practical issues using the HD26 with my HTPC set-up. The projector is ceiling mounted in my living room and seems to kick into extra loud fan mode a lot. It's quiet in normal mode but it's like sitting under a jet engine when the fast fan kicks in. I've pored through every menu option on this thing and there's no setting to control this behavior. The projector also constantly auto-seeks (black screen and hourglass icon for 20-30 seconds) when it gets the slightest of signal changes over HDMI. This process is annoying and seems utterly unnecessary, again poring through the menus and playing with signal lock options etc. has no effect. I even locked the output on my Denon E400 but the projector still seeks constantly. I find this particularly annoying when using my HTPC, browse the web the projector has to reconfigure the signal, open media center another reconfig, play a digital movie yet another reconfig. Clearly these are firmware issues and maybe they'll get fixed, but in daily use I'm developing a real love-hate relationship with this projector. Another annoyance is the massive amount of light leak from this projector, it glows above my head in my living room like something out of Close Encounters. I brought it to replace an an HD66 which had none of these issues connected to the exact same set-up (of course that one did have the dreaded dodgy DMD chip which starts losing pixels the second the warranty is up). I'll keep the HD26 for now, but my takeaway is to never buy Optoma again.

Bulb lasted less than a year in daily use.

title: Well worth the money to get better performance
text:
I bought this camera to replace one of those cheap $20 cameras with the LEDs on the front. While the old cheap camera will prove if a car pulled out in front of you or if the light was green when you drove through the intersection, it couldn't give you more detail than that.

This DVR has crystal clear true 1080p video that puts the cheap camera to shame. This may have cost 3x what I paid for the cheap camera, but the image is 10x better. This camera has great low light image quality. Some will say that the image is noisy, but that is what you get with any digital camera that costs under $1,000. My cheap one was worthless in the dark. The 8GB micro SD card that was included was made by Samsung and so far holds about 1 1/2 hours before being written over. (Recording at 1080p, 3 minute files and using Wide Dynamic Range) The camera was ready to go right out of the box. All I had to do was change the date and time. The manual was well written and easy to understand. The suction mount holds tight and the ball head can be articulated to any position you need. The power cord was plenty long enough to hide it and run it in the overhead, down the passenger side and back to the 12v power supply in the middle console.

As with anything in life, you get what you pay for and you have to balance what you want with what you can afford. As I said before, a $20 camera will tell you if a blurry car pulled out in front of you during the day. But this camera will show you if they were on the phone.

Answers to common questions;

Q: Is this camera HD?
A: Yes the camera records in 1080p

Q: Does the camera turn itself on and off automatically?
A: Yes the camera turns on when the car starts and turns back off 10-15 seconds after the car shuts down. As long as you have it plugged into a 12v outlet that is only powered when the car is on. If the outlet is always on even when the car is off, the camera will not shut down unless you turn it off or remove the plug.

Q: How long can it record, what happens when it runs out of memory?
A: At 1080p, the highest setting the included 8GB card will hold between 1 1/2 hours worth of video. Once it reaches capacity, the oldest video file will be deleted to make room for the new file.

Q: How can I view/save files on my computer?
A: Remove the Micro SD card from the side of the camera and insert it into the included USB micro SD card adapter and insert it into your computer. Or if you want you can always take down the entire camera and plug it in to your computer using a mini USB cable.

Q: Can you read license plates?
A: Yes, but only until the cars reach about 20' away. Since the camera is a wide angle lens, it becomes hard to read. All Car DVRs suffer from this because they have wide angle lenses. I can read plates of cars that pass me too.

title: UPDATED: NOT COMPATIBLE W USB CONVERTERS and Check Your Outlet Setup vs 3-prong Plug
text:
UPDATE: I wanted to use another AC/USB converter in one of the AC outlets - it doesn't pass through power to be recognized by my iPad. (Yes - the USB converter works fine when plugged into several wall outlets).

They did not provide a photo with the plug extended, but when "right side up", the 3rd prong (grounding plug) is on the underside/bottom of the unit's plug. This means if your wall outlet has the 3rd/round opening at the top, you will be installing this upside down - and it will either block the "other" usable plug in the outlet, or be "upside down" and position the USB port on the bottom (hard to access), or both.

title: No Longer Deserving of "A Keeper"
text:
UPDATE: Just under one year later, unit was blown by power dip/restore. No longer can it accept Ethernet connections, so my Air Port is acting as the single port for me when I need two. Bummed.

This was modem number three to replace the rental with my Time Warner service. Finally. Following the ratings from intelligent and thoughtful people (who provided details of WHY other models weren't any good), I resigned myself to paying more to get something reliable.
I also subscribed to the "white models are genuine Arris, black models are junk". Arris bought Motorola, so I think Arris is superior.

This was the right one for me, if two days of heavy use counts for anything. I wanted built-in WiFi as a backup to my Apple AirPort, and wanted more than one internet connection. I wanted downward compatibility so I could connect my old Big Mac G4 through the internet port, and have it do basic internet functions. This modem is both IPv4 and IPv6 compatible through Time Warner. (Your ISP must have the capability to address the modem with the right code, which varies from maker to maker and sometimes between models.)

No hangs and 404 errors I was getting with TWC's own modem, and the installation with the TWC field tech was a quick matter (15 minutes), including connecting/testing hard wire Internet, renaming, changing passwords, and masking the Broadcast ID - which I recommend you do after you connect all your devices (so they have the correct Network ID stored, but others in the area don't see the modem to try to hack into it). Do yourself a favor if you call a tech: power up the modem upon receipt to make sure it works. (That was the problem the last time.)

If something lowers the 5-star rating, and I can figure out how to get into this review again, I'll update.
My Apple AirPort has had no problems over two years (using only Apple's internet connection cable), and now I feel I have a modem and backup router which will deliver more of the same reliability.

text:

It’s a fatal design flaw from a company that usually makes good products. How this passed their QC department is bewildering.

text: The lens construction is flimsy plastic and is not weather sealed. But the performance given the price range is great. It is the only affordable wide angle Auto Focus lens for the Sony full frame alpha series, which performs very well in both still and video application. The auto focus mechanism is very quiet. The built quality does not give me confidence this will be a long term workhorse, especially for outdoor use, but given the price range that's OK.

title: Significant quality issues. Very poor optical quality
text: On appearance alone looks like an excellent bargain. Alas the lens I received was  either defective of subpar quality in all aspects of optical performance. It’s a manual focus lens and when focus was set correctly there was ignificant chromatic aberration across the lens and very poor sharpness. I've included a comparison for the Canon crop sensor lens with similar focal length and the Rokinon 18mm AF lens. Both the Rokinon AF 18.2.8 FE and the Rokinon 16mm Cine DS were shot on a Sony A7IV with identical settings.

title: Innovative design and good quality material
text: For the price this provides an excellent product. An innovative design and good quality for the price. I wouldn’t consider this tripod for heavy video use and that’s not really what it’s designed for, but for DSLR still photography it provides a stable foundation. The build quality seems on par with other similarly priced tripods, but the flexible design is what sets it apart from similar priced tripods.

title: It’s a cheap slider and it shows
text:
This slider is the cheapest priced motorized slider I’ve come across. The slider construction is sturdy and lightweight. The remote is made of cheap plastic with software that is very poor making it somewhat difficult to set accurately.

More importantly, the battery that controls the motor quickly dies and the timer controls introduces considerable drift between camera shutter and the movement of the platform. This makes it impossible to use for any meaningful time-lapse photography. The build quality and poor remote and software just doesn’t inspire confidence that this unit can do anything but basic video work, let alone Timelapse. It could be useful for video b roll, but the motor and belt is quite noisy at all speeds so audio recording may be affected in a quite environment such as a studio.

title: Manual lens with great fisheye look
text: The build quality seems good. There are definitely some major focus issues depending on your setting. This is a manual lens so there's no autofocus to the rescue and the focus easily becomes blurred. When dialing in the right settings it does produce so great fish eye shots.

title: Suitable for basic daytime photography only
text:
The unit feels solid and provides a stable foundation. But this is a very simple basic timer unit that uses constant rotation while active, which makes it useless for holy grail, night or long exposure time lapses as the the long exposure time and rotation makes for blurry images.

Based on the solid, but simple construction and only rudimentary duration and rotation settings, this is good for basis daytime time-lapses and nothing else.

title: Good for video, useless for Timelapse photography
text:
This is steady for video work, but still to lightweight for heavier setups or having a smartphone attached on top of the main camera. What’s worse is it is completely useless for Timelapse photography regardless of how light the camera is. The unit is simply too unstable to produce any meaningful results.

I tested it both indoors and outdoors with no wind and a very heavy base setup used for Time-lapse. The time-lapse was set for 1 you with intervals of 6 secs. The results were shaky and uneven in the movements either due to the time-lapse software not working as expected or the unit having too big a tolerance in the joints and construction when panning.

title: Good for video, Useless for time-lapsephotography
text:
It's pretty good for lightweight setups. But any DSLR with a decent lens will not be a good fit, due to the wight limitations which is what the Ronin-S is for at over twice the price.

More importantly, the unit is advertised as being able to be used for time-lapse photography. It is decidedly NOT able to perform that task under any conditions. The arm is simply to light and introduces frequent shaking over the span of an hour when tested indoors. I can only imagine outdoors even with the slightest amount of wind. It rendered the footage unusable for time-lapse photography.

It may well be better and save $20 and get the wired only model. The provided USB chord is much longer compared to previous models in the same price range.

title: High quality, but changing springs is near impossible
text:
Pros:

- The vest and plate/arm materials are of high build quality.
- Vest seems to be able to adjust to a good fit.
- Good lumbar support from back pad.
- Arm seems to work very well and moves very smoothly
- Adjustment knobs are easy to adjust.

Cons:
- Near impossible to change springs. It cannot be done by 1 person and still takes at least 20-30 minutes. It's a major design flaw and should be improved, otherwise this unit is rendered useless unless you have someone to help you.
- 1 small plastic washer was missing, but does not seem to make any difference in performance
- The padding material is very rough and will leave your skin chafed around your neck unless you wear a collared shirt.

title: Bigger is not always better
text:
Bigger is not always better. In fact, when tested against cheaper shotgun mics this fares significantly worse. This is a surprise given the quality of audio technica microphones in general. The sensitivity is exceedingly poor, with lots of noise due to the low sensitivity. The frequency response is also very poor with no low end whatsoever which is very noticeable on Dialog or voice recording when shooting video. The pattern setting makes minimal difference.

The materials seem to be of good quality and there is attachments for both camera shoe and mic stand. But the appearance simply cannot make up for the exceedingly poor sound quality regardless of which setting used.

title: Cheap low quality Indian knockoff of the Flycam west
text:
Cons:
- The product was not shipped in what appeared to be a professional product. It had a strong unpleasant odor from the packing materials, which was shipped directly from India.
- The manual is very sparse and pretty much useless.
- A second spring for cameras 2-8lbs are included, but the built quality is so poor that replacing the spring took quite a bit of work and if not careful could have damaged the arm.
- There were no instructions with regards to replacing the spring.
- The vest doesn’t fit well.
- The arm is heavy and poorly designed.
- The tension adjustment can easily be damaged and cannot be adjusted easily.

The price is rock bottom and it shows in the product. If at all possible, I would recommend spending at little more on a dual spring from a reputable manufacturer such as Flycam, which is what it seems they’ve trying to imitate.

The signal strength is powerful even in an older building with thick walls, a kitchen, etc. the download speeds are identical to the wired Ethernet connections. When I travel, I carry a large laptop, sometimes two, power supply(s), a hub, notepad, kindle, iPad, and then a cable per device to charge and a USB power hub. I also like to take things that every other person might take on travel: snacks, light sweater/scarf. Believe it or not, this bag holds it all. I've been using it daily for work and love it. It did feel a little heavy out of the box when I received it, but it hasn't been a problem. The straps are really solid and the back is nicely padded (the laptop compartment). The removable crush-proof AC-Adapter garage makes a difference. I think this helps better distribute the weight because AC Adapters can be pretty hefty. I saw other reviews mentioning the bag's weight but decided to give it a try anyway and I'm glad I did. It's only 3lbs, 6 oz. I don't think you'll get a lighter bag with better construction. title: I think it works just pretty well.
text:
I slotted a Corsair MP510 2TB PCIE3.0x4 NVMe m.2 SSD into this adapter for my PC and shoved it into the 3rd PCIex16 slot on my motherboard. It works great in my O11-Dynamic case and has no issues clearing the bottom fans.

Other reviews regarding the heatsink bending the unit are absolutely correct...IF you attempt to tighten the screws all the way. Here's the fix: Just don't tighten them down all the way. Tighten both screws a little bit at a time evenly, swapping back and forth, until it's snug with just enough friction to stay tight. If you do it this way, the heatsink will stay on and neither the unit nor the m.2 drive will be bent.

title: Sounds great but Auto VA does NOT work for Bluetooth
text:
I CHOSE this model over another because of the supposed built-in Alexa compatibility. You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.

title: I've loved these little earbuds for four years! Still going strong.
text:
My Otium beats will be four years old in July. I've tried to upgrade earbuds (nothing too pricey) and have always been disappointed.

🏋🏼‍♀️ I wear them while I work out. They have a great sound and block outside noise pretty well. They help me get in my zone in my own little world, and I love them.

💦 I tried to swim in them, and while they're waterproof, they stop playing as soon as my head is underwater.

🎧 The plastic ear tips, which are super comfortable for my tiny ear holes, eventually broke down — as aging plastic will do. I replaced them with BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips, which are nearly identical to the originals [[ASIN:B07FF9DN5K BLLQ Replacement Ear Tips]].

💵 They're $20. BT 4.1. So not the newest Bluetooth, and I'm sure Bose sounds better. But at this price point, I love these little guys.

🏆 Actually, I got them on a lightning sale for $13, so even better! So I paid $20 for the earbuds AND replacement tips.

🌚 I still want something new because I just want something new, you know. But knowing the disappointment I always feel with my attempted replacements, I'll probably keep using these sweet little babies.

🔊 I don't know what the heck they're talking about with the "noise canceling" in the product title. There is no ACTIVE noise-canceling, but the earbuds do form slight seals, which have a passive noise-canceling effect. I think I actually bought them for noise-canceling, but whatever. It's overrated as a feature unless you are willing to pay hundreds of dollars.

In sum, these are great earbuds, especially if you're prone to losing things and hate to feel heartbroken about losing something expensive.

title: Not so much "new" as sitting on a shelf for several years
text:
The computer itself is fine. It was originally sold to a university in California, and half the warranty had been used while it sat on a shelf. I had to have the warranty put in my name, and that took several days, so I could get it repaired. Still out 1.5 years of warranty! What even! The box was slightly worn, and the cables were dirty even though the box was sealed. I made the mistake of thinking it had a screen protector on it and tried to pull it off. Y'all, it was part of the screen. The seller refunded me the difference in price between a new item and a like new item. Since this already had a registered owner in Dell's system and it was some trouble to transfer over, I'd say it was conceivably like new but not new. I used that difference in price to pay for the repair. [Note: they did initially not want to make up the difference until I provided pictures of dirty cords, etc, and offered to escalate it to Amazon's customer service. But they did eventually grant the refund in difference. But it took weeks to get the difference in price and then to have the warranty transferred to me. I was *this close* to going through Amazon to try to return the whole shebang because of being misled. But they finally came through with a compromise I found acceptable. And I am otherwise happy with the computer.]

Here are my thoughts on the machine itself--unrelated to the seller:

PROS
- Terrific resolution. Much easier to read screen text.
- Lots of variety in color configurations for different light environments.
- 32 GB of memory really makes a difference over my previous 4-8GB.
- SSD is likewise fast and the whole system is quiet.
- This list of pros is short, but they are the most important things to me. Everything else is small beans.

CONS
- It is unbelievable how hard it is to get to the USB ports, etc, on the back! I literally have to use needle-nose pliers to plug or unplug USB devices--and a flashlight and contortions. I've read it's because the speakers didn't leave a lot of options for where to put these, but it just ridiculous.
- The sound is not as good as I expected. My last Dell AIO had JBL speakers and I don't think I realized how good those were. To be fair, the sound is fine, I was just expecting to be blown away by the six speakers on the bottom.
- Poor webcam placement. It's on the bottom at a really weird angle. Will probably upgrade.
- Onboard mic is also worse than what was in the Inspiron 2320. Remedied by purchasing a separate mic. But on a system this expensive, the mic and webcam should be premium, not barely useable.
- The screen would buzz softly at anything less than 100% brightness. A workaround is to reduce brightness via Radeon Pro graphics board. SOLUTION: go through Dell community customer service boards to update the VBIOS.
- The color temperatures sometimes get really off after the monitor goes to sleep and wakes up. I put a shortcut to Dell Premier Color in the taskbar and just reapply the setting, and it's fine. Still shouldn't even be a thing that happens on a machine with this price tag.
- Not a fan of the included wired mouse and keyboard, so I swapped out my own. I'm guessing this was originally meant for a computer lab where you wouldn't want someone to walk away with the peripherals.

OVERALL VERDICT
It took a while to get everything sorted, some of which was my fault. But I did get it sorted. The lower price from the seller comes with the tradeoff of losing some of the warranty and it taking extra time to get the remaining warranty transferred to me. But it still cost thousands less via this route than it would have otherwise. So worth it, I guess, if you've got the time for shenanigans.

title: Defective product. Possibly the worst customer service experience of my life--and that's saying a lot.
text: I wanted this range extender so that I could stop using 2.4ghz because it has become too crowded in my neighborhood. The range extender only broadcasts 5G in the following conditions--straight out of the box when it isn't connected to the router, when you set up the extender to NOT connect to the 5G router signal, or when you select High Speed Option 1, which connects to the router by 2.4Ghz but broadcasts on 5G. So it's absolutely impossible to get it to connect to the router via 5G and broadcast 5G. I spent HOURS trying to set it up every which way. I repeatedly tried to set it up via WPS, via the internet, and after doing several factory restores. Every single time, the same poor effects. Having exhausted all possible ways of setting it up, I made the mistake of calling customer support. It was easily the worst customer service call I have ever experienced. I have lived and studied outside of the States and work with many, many colleagues who are from many different countries, and I rarely have trouble understanding someone who speaks competent English with an accent. However, the woman I spoke with was frequently unintelligible. I often had to ask her to repeat herself and could not answer her questions on the first try because it sounded like she was speaking gibberish. It was probably just the language difference, but she also had trouble understanding or remembering my responses, so I had to answer the same questions several times. Nonetheless, I reset the range extender with her over the phone several times. After forty-five minutes she told me that she'd have to have an engineer call me back tomorrow, at which point I said I'd just send it back and they can fix it on their own time. At one point she offered to email me updated firmware (the TP Link website only has firmware older than what came on range extender), but then at the end of the call when I reminded her of this, she said the firmware was universal and isn't even designed for this device. I asked her to send it to me. She asked me if I wanted her to send it to me. I said yes. She asked me again if I wanted her to send it to me. I again said yes. She asked AGAIN if I wanted her to send it to me, and I had enough and hung up. I hope this device is just defective as I've requested a replacement. If the second one works, I'll update my review accordingly. If not, I will promptly return it and be done with this fiasco.

title: AMAZING! with some flaws
text:
Aww man, there is so much about this mouse that I absolutely lurve. My wrists definitely feel better (and for sure use a long gel pad in front of your keyboard and mousing area). But there are a couple of design flaws that keep me from giving it the full five stars.

1) I like to left click and scroll. If you do that with the standard buttons, the left click button kind of snags on the center wheel. Uh: bad! I guess I could program one of the many other extra buttons as a duplicate left click to make click and scrolling easier. But why should I have to do that with a $100+ mouse? I mean really.

2) crud can develop on the bottom of the mouse causing it to move erratically. There are four little slick plastic pads that poke out from the bottom surface as glides. They get crud around them. Why can't the whole bottom be a single thing that's less likely to get the crud?

My second concern is really trivial, but the click and scroll thing is a big problem in something otherwise so well-designed.

Even so, I wouldn't trade this mouse for any other pointing device, and I've tried a lot: various mice, a so-called vertical mouse that was more at a diagonal, a trackpad, the thing with the ball (I'm too lazy to look it up), and let's not forget those ancient eraser buttons in the middle of old laptops. Thank god someone got rid of those!

title: Review Date 1/7/21 - Love this device!!! Why aren’t they available now???
text: Why are they not available now? It’s a great device!!! I’m not a ‘tech’ person at all! I’m a single female that’s 65 years old and have problems with almost all of these things EXCEPT for this one! This is a small, handy ‘plug’ with a mini speaker - great for a relatively unused room. I have mine in my 3rd spare bedroom that I use for my ironing board, drying rack, etc. I’m home alone just about every day and I have music playing from the time I get up in the morning till I fall asleep at night and with this I can now hear it while I’m doing my laundry chores. The sound quality isn’t great but acceptable for its purpose and Alexa responds quickly and very well with my voice commands, whether it’s music related or something else! I like that it’s both a small plug and has some of the capabilities of an Echo Dot, Show, and the other larger Smart devices. I can also use the USB port and normal, non ‘smart’ outlet. The cost was minimal and I’m really bummed that I can’t buy this anymore! I only started using ‘smart’ things several months ago and now I’m slowly adding more and more. Amazon, PLEASE make this again or an ‘identical’ item! Note: I gave this 3 stars because of the combination of the item (5*’s) and the fact that it’s no longer available (0*’s).

title: Great picture quality and price!
text: I am a single 60+ year old female so I can’t really go into much detail about all the features of this TV. What I can say is that the picture quality is great and I have no complaints about the sound being very low as one reviewer mentioned. This problem is likely due to the program channels and not the TV itself, at least it’s what I’ve noticed. This is my 5th TV and the largest one that I’ve ever had. I have one that is also a Samsung and a Sony, LG, and Insignia - each one a different size. This size (as are all TVs) is based on the diagonal measurement and not the width - so it should be able to fit into a space that’s not larger than the given length and height. The best part is the price and the ability to have it delivered to me at home. This spares having to go to a Best Buy or other store and being overwhelmed with the variety of brands, sizes and salespeople hovering over you and trying to make you buy the most expensive one. The delivery was mixed up and it took a few extra days to get it back to my town and it was delivered without any damage.

title: Fits a small camera perfectly!

Since I go away on a cruise for 1 month every year I have been trying to make things easier for packing, using, etc. This scarf strap is the 4th one that I’ve bought and tried - 3 of them were returned as they didn’t fit. This is the only one that did work on my camera! I have a compact Panasonic (that was quite expensive despite the size) and this scarf not only fit but was also comfortable around my neck. One reviewer said that it felt flimsy and thought it wouldn’t last very long - in my opinion this does not feel like it is! This will be the first year that I will be taking it with me for my month-long cruise and I have no regrets in buying it and I don’t hesitate to recommend it! This is a great price and I will probably buy another one in a different color. The reason why the other neck straps didn’t fit was because they didn’t have any ‘clips’ to attach the ends of the strap on the sides of the camera (even the more expensive ones than this, i.e. close to $30.00).

text: I'm very happy - this is my first LG purchase and I would recommend this TV for the picture quality and sound. I have had Samsung and Sony in the past and present, both of which are also good, but since Sony doesn't make them any longer I didn't want to be stuck with something that might not be able to be repaired if necessary. This left me a choice of LG or Samsung, and after comparing both of them I went with LG only because it has a center stand versus side stands (the Samsung). I bought this 32" set for my sunroom to replace a slightly smaller one which will fit better in another room. Being a technically challenged 60+ woman I had a male friend stop by and set it up for me which hardly took any time at all. I think the picture is very clear and the sound level is much lower than its Samsung predecessor (a good thing I would say). I'm not into playing games, DVD's, shopping on Amazon, etc. that so-called 'Smart' TVs can do (I have 3 of them and have never used these functions). For my use I only want to watch TV and have a sharp and clear picture with good sound quality and this is exactly what this LG TV can provide - I guess life is good with LG!

I have optimum/cablevision and the ones I wanted to replace have 2 males - one at each end - that twist onto a female but my male has a pin that protrudes from each end. This one doesn't have pins that extend I'm sorry to say because they are flexible and a little thinner than the existing ones and I would have liked to be able to use them. I would definitely recommend these IF they are the correct ones to fit whatever 'F-M' setup you have! title: ARRIVED DEFECTIVE
text:
MINE DOES NOT WORK. This thingy was a gift from my grown son, it arrived inoperable with a booklet with instructions printed WAY too small to read, and with diagrams on how to operate it that required a magnifying glass to see the details. The booklet had cutesy round pages but staples that had rusted and stained large patches of the instructions. The font is way too small for most people anyway [you know, paper is SO EXPENSIVE]. If they had used a square format instead of round pages, they could have tripled the font size and yet used no more paper. My advice: Give up the Cutesy format.

I polish metal specimens for aerospace testing so I know how to polish out scratches in plastics. This device might have accomplished that - if it had functioned. But the cheap construction plastic gears hidden inside did not seem to engage and so the disk did not turn. Also, the reversing switch did not work, in fact, it would just lock it if I tried to go counterclockwise. My kids even tried and agreed it was just broke when it arrived. (kids know these things, old guys not so much)

1- it didn't work and appeared to be non-repairable - a complete waste of $30.
2- the poorly written instructions and pictures were sized for ant-people to read.
3- They had spent way too much attention on [silly] appearance and not performance.
4- The product was ridiculously hard to extricate from the packaging which was wasteful with no apparent recycle symbols either.
5-IF I had gotten it to work, I would have needed more than a square inch of the buffing cloth they included. The blue non-woven cloth included had succumbed to degradation in the package and had holes and weak spots in it. Apparently it was degraded by the packaging plasticizes. And it was just way too small for a polishing or buffing job.
6- Apparently the marketers, designers or tech development team did not understand that keeping a wet polishing compound on the disc is the secret - so apparently they did not know they could have just made a tray on the disk holding the CD, to contain liquid and help users out. I feel like it was just designed to look like a gee whiz thing and get your money, not really concerned about whether or not it really worked. Save your money. Instead, buy polishing rags and buffing compound from outfits that do this sort of thing for a living. You will very likely be happy and for a much longer period of time.
Polishing plastic is not that hard, but it is NOT EASY either, because it takes a lot of patience and some properly applied buffing compound and elbow grease. IT TAKES A LITTLE TIME no matter how you do it. This device is trying to make you think it is physically and temporally easy. No magic machine exists that can polish without some work. We use polishing machines where I work, and it takes a LOT of time and effort, even when mechanized.

I think that maybe the product COULD have worked, but I doubt if the company leader-persons who oversaw the packaging and function decisions that dragged it's quality and capability down are accountable for their poor decisions. It definitely does not work as delivered. Look elsewhere when you need to restore and polish a scratched disk.

title: I'm with stupid...
text:
Update: The bud cover came off and stuck in my ear! Dangerous! Poorly designed and sending it back.

Great sound! But, a fatal flaw: the medium and small sized bud covering diaphrams are also smaller and therefore do not fit around the bud piece. The large coverings fit but are loose; mine came out and I just happened to notice it on the floor. Lowered to 3 stars. This may precipitate a return.

They had superior bass, great music sound, and I didn't have to open the box to see the charge status. Phone calls worked fine. Fit all good like my former K23's from a different brand. Case is larger and heavier than with those.

I got a low power message. Okay I left them to charge. There were no indicator lights. Oh well. The next morning they were not charged! I got a low power message again but checked and the case was to 98% full! Well I don't need technical difficulty, there was no wiggle room in the holder, I'm not putting up with this! and I ordered my old brand.

My old brand were mostly like I remembered them, not as good consistent bass but pretty good, not as good for loud music. When I opened the new (old) pair the sticker instructed me to remove the little strips of plastic that were across the metal charging points on the earbuds that make contact with the case points. The lights went on and I'm happily listening to my replacement pair at coffee.

Ohhhhh... Do you suppose? Could be?...

When I got home, just in case, I got out these new pair from the box again and opened the case and took out the bud and... I see. (sheepish smile) I removed the little stickers on the contact points and the new pair of these that sounded so good for music with lots of bass are now charging with indicator lights working. I cancelled my return.

Now I'll have to return the new old ones because I can't afford both and have no use for them. Just sharing this story with others who may not see so well such as I.

Tip: If you have prior buds that display K23 in your phone or device bluetooth list you have to delete that and repair these as new for them to work. They're great buds! :)

title: happily surprised
text:
I'm surprised at the build quality, overall functionality and sound of this unit (including bluetooth which I'm listening to as I write this).

The only caveat would be I wish they had tuned the speaker for a little more bass. The volume is definitely centered in the middange/treble zone; when a trumpet came on I had to turn it down. The bass is there somewhat just subdued. The volume knob goes to loud too fast. It'd be hard to adjust very low. I think the price is too high.

However it's instantly likable and as I got it exclusively to stream CBS Radio Mystery Theater next to my bed I'm unconcerned how it would reproduce modern music. Listening to my 20s/30s/40s playlist the bluetooth connection is solid, no hums or crackling, and volume is more than loud enough. Sounds great! Love the light, knobs, feel. Happy purchase!

I updated to 5 stars! This has a very clear, loud and upfront sound; not at all like ClearClick wooden radios which are crackly, introduce artifacts, skips, are muffled, and have a very low bluetooth volume and poor connection.

title: superior shortwave reception

text: After using it a year it's still my go-to favorite radio. Reception, durability, quality. And sounds great with or without high quality headphones.

title: looks and sounds great!
text:
Be aware there's no headphone jack, since shortwave tends to be a nighttime activity you may not be taking this outside unless you don't have neighbors. Or a spouse.

It's wood with a veneer-like finish so don't expect old wood. The markings is a decal.

With thai said, it gets great reception, is sturdy and heavy and the speaker sounds terrific on both radio and bluetooth; clear, loud, and bassy not tinny at all. I notice no great volume difference between functions; I did not test cards. The knobs are sturdy. It tends to be louder with soft bedside volume being more difficult to achieve. But really great sound/tone for both voice and music. As good as Tivoli or Sangean. I find the tuning button slightly difficult to work with I wish it was larger. Nothing's lit, there's little led specs for power and bluetooth. I like it a lot for an inside table radio and esp. bluetooth (nice to play vintage shows on it for its looks) and quality sound/build, definitely worth the $30 I paid for it.
***
Still great sound, a little hard to tune, but as others have noted the caveat is very short battery life like 3 hours after all night charging; you can listen to it while charging.

Okay, lowering to two stars because as a review mentioned the bluetooth function does not receive the full stereo signal and plays just one channel. This is an unacceptable failure in design. Also the battery only lasts 3 hours as I mentioned and you'd need to leave it plugged in all the time. Not worth the high price despite the good sound on talk radio.

title: Spend $50 more and get an Eton Field instead.
text:
If you're looking to buy this radio probably the radio you want is the Eton Field. Yes it's 50% more in price but more than 50% in value. The build quality is superior, it's heavier, the knobs are more substantial, the sound is better, and the reception is better.

This does have great sound, and the reception is decent, with some distortion on voice, nothing to write home about. It's lighter and the plastic is thinner than the Eton, and the knobs are cheaper.

The reception and sound quality of the Eton Field is why I'm sending this back. It sounds better on easy stations, and it gets a hard to get FM station at the very edge of the dial locally that the CCrane EP Pro can't hear at all. It's a rave station I like. Plus my usual oldies stations which can be hard to get are received better on the Eton. The Eton sound with high fidelity home stereo system Sennsheiser headphones is superb, free of interference artifacts and the Eton on battery easily powers them.

Because I already had the Eton Field I had something else to compare the C Crane EP Pro to. And there is no comparison.

title: Quality,  Superb
text:
I like this radio better than other bands and it'd be great for travel but I went with the Field because it's HUGE, hefty and just what I wanted despite some disparaging reviews. Can I afford to keep both?? Maybe if I send back all the others...

Together this Eton Elite Field and the Eton Elite Executive are the ultimate pair in my opinion. Despite the heavy promotion of newer brands which I don't believe are better.

Okay now I have to have the Eton Elite Mini Compact (currently $25) to complete the set. Didn't expect this result but tried lots of radios in several brands. Sold on Eton.

title: This is the one.
text:
This is the one that I'm keeping. I bought a lot of radios including vintage GE and watched many videos, and I liked the Eton Elite Executive a lot and the included folding protector/case, it's great size for travel; but this radio by modern standards is HUGE (Executive is dimension of Field speaker grill), bigger than the GE, sounds FANTASTIC. Really heavy, more than substantial, and comes with the vinyl brown case that does not have speaker or control holes.

I honestly didn't think they built radios like this anymore. Size, weight, construction of quality vintage, but reception, functionality and features of new. I absolutely love this radio. And it's cheaper than all the more expensive smaller ones that can't begin to sound like this.

Padded handle that doesn't quite leave enough room for fingers (I'll find out if it adjusts), and carrying strap with the satchel. I didn't pay more for the satchel so good deal. Reception superb. I saw lower reviews on this particular model so I'm really glad I took the chance and got it with the others, which are going back, because while they're great this is greater. Also some newer brands don't have better reception or circuitry despite some reviews.

Did I mention I really LOVE this radio?

Update: Still loving this radio, no regrets. Great for AM/MW (DSP) DX. Oklahoma, California, Texas. Something on EVERY frequency; I didn't have patience to wait and hear each call sign. So don't know about bad reviews on shortwave, but on AM this outperformed all the others esp. smaller expensive ones by a mile. You need DSP to filter digital interference these days. AM DXing is what I bought it for so very satisfied. Also Bluetooth works/ sounds great.

A Little Later: Okay, I got to try it more and used a clip-on antenna and headphones. Yeah, as others have noted this is totally deaf on shortwave. I got best SW results with a $16 Supersonic. Really. After trying quite a few. But for Shortwave this isn't it you'll have to look elsewhere. I still prefer this radio for its excellent AM DXing reception (and FM!), speaker sound, and build quality. And BT.

Incidentally to turn the annoying beep off turn radio off, press and hold ALARM and display will say beeping off. Done.

title: First Okay, then Appalled.
text:
The tablet itself is okay; that is, mediocre. It's a sub-hundred dollar Android tablet sans Google Play. Don't compare it to other devices (costing hundreds of dollars more). There was video pixelation as well as motion distortion on YouTube. This may be due to the Silk Browser as there is no native app. The sound did not have the hightop of my 2017 J7 $250 phone. Both the picture quality and sound frequency range is inferior to my 10+ year-old HD tv and my old mid-value phone. For this reason alone I'm returning it. Like I said it's okay.

Then I downloaded 5 Amazon appstore apps. 4 didn't work *at all*. The 5th seemed, again, okay but useless. I used to be a regular Fire user since 2011. I liked most of the tablets and Amazon's appstore through those years. I was APPALLED at the current status. What are the apps for if not Amazon tablets? I don't believe they make phones anymore. It's okay if all you do is watch Amazon video. But you can watch Amazon Prime, listen to Audibles, and read on Kindle on any tablet through their respective apps which work fine. And watch YouTube on a native Android. Why sacrifice?

Note: My Fire HD 10, 7th edition through it's Silk Browser doesn't have these picture and sound problems. Tested same videos on YouTube. Superior picture, no distortion or motion problems, and good sound.

title: pass

The bass is not only recessed and somewhat muddy, it sits in the middle while the treble is in outer space at the edges and the sound is neither clear, pleasant nor coordinated. title: Radio yes,  Bluetooth no.
text:
As a tip the coin battery goes in fancy side (also marked +) in first, behind the little black tab which is behind the trap door in the back. This is because the connections touch the center and edge separated by the dark ring on one side. The compartment could be to store the included antenna except the radio isn't portable so doesn't make a lot of sense. None of this was mentioned in the instructions which is a one-page get started sheet. If there's a larger instruction manual it was missing on mine. You have to wait 30 seconds for a station to be established before tuning up to the sub- channels (HD2, HD3) like all the modern HD portables. There is no AM, however I noticed some of the major talk AM stations (ClearChannel) are broadcast on the FM sub-channels. The sub-channels include news talk, sports, and music (often oldies). Push the Mode on top for settings, then the Volume selects from the menu and pushes in to enter selection, then you adjust selection parameter with Tuning, then push Volume again for previous menu or Mode to leave settings or just wait and it'll return to normal after a few seconds on its own. It's more simple than the instructions once you get the hang of it and the controls, being the Volume and Tuning knobs are consistent throughout the menus.

For an HD receiving and FM table radio, after turning the bass up all the way (to level 12), it sounds good and performs adequately. It does not receive all my local stations unless they're powerful.

Bluetooth is where it totally fails me. The sound is unacceptable even with volume up to 20 (radio is loud and clear at 6). It might be good enough for narration but not music. The volume difference, and quality, between radio and bluetooth is extreme. Again on FM and HD radio the sound is good and clear on volume 6 with the bass turned up. Odd the sound on bluetooth was so poor.

I started the return process just to see what would happen since it's shipped from a 3rd party and received the shipping label within a few hours without giving a reason. I decided to keep it because of the good radio sound and HD and quality build and space-saving form-factor. It's white in the front and wood around sides. Black plastic in back. You can choose the display text to be orange, blue, or white. It displays the time and date when off. It is AC powered only and does not run on battery.

If you merely want to listen to strong local FM stations and HD sub-channels I would say it's worth the price.

title: Finally a real radio! :)
text:

title: Great sound, poor design
text:
I hate to write this review, since these have the best sound I've heard comparing to Sony (wired) 7506s. The sound on these is excellent. It's everything else that fails, eventually causing me to return them after a couple days. I'm currently trying Cowin E7s.

The humorously deep ear pads aren't bad and that's where I think they get most if their bass response from, as the "extra" deep bass is non-existent as far as the electronics are concerned. To repeat, these are absolutely not for bassheads. Nothing like Anker. I'm not a basshead so this worked out for me. Panasonic repeatedly gets an almost Sony sound; bright highs and balanced mids.

However they did press against my temples a little too much and I can see them causing someone a headache after awhile. Again I'm not susceptible so it wasn't a problem for me. The bluetooth, unfortunately, has interrupts about every 20 minutes. Unlike others, I have never experienced this phenomena with any other bluetooth device or phone. My inexpensive Mpows don't do this. And, sigh, the stupid bass switch RATTLES. With loud volume and pop/rock bass you won't hear it. Listening to classical or jazz with these would be impossible. They creak. The plastic is super lightweight, cheaply built, and poorly designed. Trying to enjoy music in a rocking chair after awhile will get to you. Again none of my other headphones do this.

Bottom line, super balanced sound (NOT bassy despite their advertising) but poorly designed with cheap materials and subpar bluetooth which defeats enjoying the great sound. Really too bad.

Until Anker and Sony have a baby...

title: WAY TOO MUCH BASS!!!
text:
WAY TOO MUCH BASS!!! My less expensive Mpow 7s have plenty of bass but include the middles and high frequencies equally, sound really good and loud like Sony's. These simply don't have the hightop and even lose the middles in the bass, that's with the BassUp turned off.

On the positive side they were instantly the most comfortable headphones I ever put on, seem well constructed, and I liked the blue and beige design. Really, really comfortable; moreso than my Sony's.

But it's sound that counts. And these are going back.

title: Finally!
text: I've tried,  and sent back,  like 10 radios from Amazon.  I'm afraid they're going to delete my account.  The last one was an expensive (for me) pocket Eton. This Sangeon is what the Eton should have been.  And I bought a used one; looks and functions perfectly.  I haven't stopped listening to it since unboxing.

title: Great sound one tenth the price!
text:
I'm a Sony fan, don't enjoy bluetooth and normally use the MDR7506 which is the only headset I can stand. In the past I had a $35 Panasonic set that sounded surprisingly good. They are no longer available on Amazon. I hate 'V'- sound oriented phones. Panasonics are similar to Sony in that the response is even across the spectrum (with the bass enhanced). No middle tones recessed or dropping off the top. Good soundstage full and present upfront, no recessed or hidden instruments and wide stereo separation. Front and loud. Perfect clarity. For me this is "the Sony sound" and my comparison standard. Panasonic reproduces this standard closer than any brand I have tried including phones that cost up to $300 (I *really* hate the 'V' profile). I usually have to wait on the Sonys for Christmas.

This headphone set comes, again, amazingly close given its price range, which is about 1/10th of the cost! They're the only ones that can hold me over till Christmas and make a great backup pair. Comfortable, truly circumaural, very lightweight and can handle the wattage output and full volume of my home theater system. At this ridiculous price they're remarkably good. And better than other midrange brands I've tried.

title: brand & price fails
text:
This is the first and probably only time I could afford a Grundig related radio. I'm sorry to report all the other comments are true, especially the negative ones. My main problem is it's basically unusable because of the controls on every edge and side of the radio. It has two wheel knobs on one side for volume and manual tuning which is good because without autoprogramming or presets the button tuning process is hair-pulling frustration. You have to go to each station, one at a time, to get anywhere on the dial. And there's no direct entry. That leaves the side-wheel which of course changes the frequency every time you pick it up or put it in a pocket. Volume likewise. The band selector opposite edge is very stiff and you cannot switch to a specific shortwave or AM band with any accuracy. It also mutes sound while tuning so you won't know if there's a faint signal to be heard unless you wait a second on every frequency. The autoscan bypasses most AM stations including local moderately strong ones. If you do take the time the actual AM reception isn't bad, just tuning is tiring. Reception on shortwave is far better with my cheap handhelds. The stereo signal on FM has a problem and even strong local stations are usually monaural. Even when it's on the stereo field is almost absent.

I originally was going to say good design, poor execution but trying to use it it's just poor design. I would hold the brand and the price to a higher standard and it fails miserably. You're much better off with a cheaper product. I'm glad I paid half-price.

title: Great quality sound,  softer,  $11, yup
text:
I was surprised at the sound quality from these phones right out of the box. I'm a fan of the Sony sound and normally use MDR-7506 with my home equipment. These have balanced highs and lows, and a good stereo field. The only caveat they don't go really loud. They're adequate, probably as loud as my old ears should listen anyway. But i turn my phone up all the way which is unnecessary with my earbuds. For $11, definite buy.

Update: I got my 3.5mm to 1/4" adapters today and was able to try these with my home theater stereo in place of my 7506's. Looks like I already mentioned how good they sound. They weren't very loud on my Amazon tablet. They were better with a handheld radio. Softer on my phone. With my home stereo (Sony) they were amply loud and surprisingly good. I don't like "on-ear" phones. But the reproduction of this pair was excellent and lives up to the Sony standard, for the most part. Obviously you have to have a device that pushes enough watts to power them adequately. I had different volumes with different devices, from full volume to way too soft. The stereo field width and separation isn't quite the 7506's, so don't expect something 10x the price. But for $11 they're more than fine. If you're device can power them.

title: Finally a radio that stands up.
text:
I'm going to be the odd one out and give this handled portable my approval. I've tried nearly every handled radio on Amazon and sent them all back for various reasons, chiefly they would wobble or couldn't stand up by themselves. Some had controls making it impossible to tune.

Yes, this is feather-lightweight plastic, etc. However this radio is just slightly thicker than the others and stands by itself even as you adjust the all- frontal knobs if you're careful; it tunes well and sounds loud and well, more treble than bass. The handle is flimsy and flops back down by itself but I don't in danger carrying the light radio by it. Easy to take to beach, etc. and loud enough for outdoors. When I live within 1,000 miles of a beach I'll take it there.

I unboxed it and tried the knobs and to my surprise it came on lol. Then I opened the battery compartment hearing rattling and the empty 'C' or 'D' cell (?) compartment was empty but contained the power/charging usb cord as the radio was playing. The 'AAA' battery designation in description is wrong. The most important part is it has a good wide base and sits securely for its weight (one bird feather) without wobble. I also like that not only are the controls on the front and simple,
but the top and both sides are free of controls and the radio is large enough. Keeper.

Update: After trying an old radio with batteries that nearly blew up, I'm appreciating this even more. The lithium charging system works better than the old. Still playing out of the box with me not installing batteries, plugging it in, or anything. Great!

A year later now and happy with it still after several new and vintage radios couldn't get my local stations. This rocks. Sorry it's double price what I paid for it; I liked the silver better. It's got a brand stamped on it now.

title: don't like the brand
text: I got this on a lightning deal so didn't mind the $8 price.  However this is the second Retekess product that's failed me.  No bass or dynamic full sound,  stereo not great,  clarity of signals subpar. I don't recommend,  and I won't purchase this brand again.

title: Too lightweight,  can't tune, static,  don't bother.

title: Don't bother
text: Of all the radios I've tried on Amazon,  this was by far the worst.  Impossible to tune. I had to hold it down on my lap and use both hands and still couldn't get my station in well.  Too much static,  and AM didn't come in at all.  It's way too lightweight to handle without bracing it and controls stiff.  Sound subpar, even for static.  Don't bother.

title: Prettiest and Works and Sounds Perfect!
text: I've bought a lot of radios on Amazon; I've had to return most of them for very poor quality including impossible tuning.  This is one of the ones I kept.  All the features work and I'm currently listening to it while charging it with my phone micro usb cord.  I especially love the 2 color lights to function.  It sounds really good,  better than cheaper bigger radios I've tried,  and it's built more solidly than they were.  The tuning is feather light touch and much easier than the others with less static and a harder to get classical station I like comes in clearer.  You're not going to listen to it from your pocket because just handling it the tuning knob will change frequencies; you have to treat it like a table radio.  But it performs as one,  admirably.  Bluetooth connects easily,  sounds great and the whole radio is a joy.  I believe this brand also makes a larger size portable/ table radio with a handle I'll have to try as I've not found a good one yet.  But this is at the top of my keepers.

title: Insta-love!
text:
I got the "acceptable" unit for total $17 (sorry), one foot pad is missing, I'll innovate. Firstly, I had wanted the chrome front but couldn't afford it and didn't want to wait a week; when I saw this used for the price I just pushed the button.

From the pictures you would think the front is all matte black, it is not. It's actually a very dark brown and the controls are a dark bronze, in shiny metal; closer to chrome aesthetic and looks far better with more tones than the photos would suggest. I'm actually happy I bought the darker color now seeing it. I tried to capture this on my pic, but it's too dark and still doesn't capture the wonderful appearance.

Plugging it in and turning it on was instantly satisfying, easy to use controls, no stiffness, good quality, lights work, radio is a deep amber or orange. Nice wood, looks and operates easily and great.

Tuning to a somewhat hard to get classical station locally was surprisingly easy and the signal came in loud and clear, unlike the other radios I've tried from Amazon. It felt like an old stereo where you didn't have to give it thought and was instinctive in the first 30 seconds without the difficulty and poor reception and static and crackling of tuning and volume controls or pops of turning it on nearly all cheap modern radios have now.

Bluetooth connected and performed seamlessly, perhaps a little softer than the radio but not horribly so. And the sound... On both radio and bluetooth the sound quality is superb; *just* enough bass without being muddy and the treble is good and clear. Bass in the voices and high pitches in the music, and very loud without screech or static at still low volume on the knob, with room-filling sound on FM and bluetooth.

This is the most pleasing product I've purchased from Amazon in a long time, especially in the radio category.

Update: After trying several others, I bought a second one! Like New $21. The only thing I notice is neither sits perfectly evenly, there's a slight wobble, even with all four feet pads. No biggie. Love the radio, excellent big sound, bass, but not muddy. Best radio on Amazon, and a true "table radio".

title: Egregious lack of quality.
text: It sounds very good (don't expect bass), clear, loud bluetooth sound,  not softer than the radio sound and that's the last good thing I have to say about it.  It's very plasticky and looks it,  but wooden at all and the shape manages to appear smaller than the dimensions would suggest.  The am reception is non- existent; and the FM tuning is nearly impossible with poor control; it changed frequencies when I adjusted the volume the first time! I would designate this bluetooth only; for that it's clear,  loud,  and sounds good.  Easy to connect.  Forget the radio.  And the metal looking handle is of course very cheap, lightweight plastic.  If you're looking for a wooden cabinet and a sturdy handle with some weight and a good build,  this isn't it.  There are better bluetooth radios with more bass that are smaller and at this price point, I feel ripped off.  Also no headphone jack,  and who uses 'D' cells anymore?  Going back,  esp. at this price. I've tried a few radios,  and there are seriously better deals on Amazon.

title: My Favorite Radio
text:
Just get it. This is my new go-to radio. Blows the 910ET away at half the price. Superior sensitivity, selectivity, stereo signal reception, and sound quality which is both bassier and LOUDER; stereo FM way louder and better sound (more bass) over quality earphones with a much stronger and stable stereo signal and spatial field. AM and SW sensitivity also superior to the DSP digital tuning 310ET.

If you're older and grew up instinctively "DXing" on your clock radio in the 1970's, this is the experience you're looking for. So much more fun than letting an ATS or ETM circuit do it for you, and again it gets more stations on both FM and SW and that's without an added antenna. This one comes with a free clip-on antenna to boot. But natively with telescopic I'm getting more SW than 910ET with SW antenna plugged in. As mentioned this doesn't cut sound during tuning inbetween frequencies. Seriously, heed this tip and turn the analogue volume on the left all the way down to bottom before turning the unit on the first time; nearly broke my eardrums.
This is my favorite radio by far, and closer to being truly portable.

title: Surprised!
text:
I find the skill set/setup dubious and the Alexa app was slow and very glitchy. This review is strictly about the device as a streaming Wi/Fi/Bluetooth speaker and sound quality.

I am an Amazon Prime customer and all my music is on Amazon streaming. Both ease of use (on Amazon Music/Pandora, etc. only) and sound in one word, Superb! I'm completely surprised because I own the $200+ UEBoom (which has been sitting unused on a shelf, I had to go look for it) and assumed the sound on that would be much superior as reviews and it's reputation suggest. Not so! I just listened back to back.

Without intending to compare them, I got my UEBoom to play while I setup the marvelous SOAIY Aurora projector (upgraded version), and in the back of my mind notice the music, not played very loudly because it's nighttime, was rather muddy; I think it wows people for its volume and base. On a whim I switched to my new Amazon Tap received today (I hadn't much time to experiment with it) and... Wow! Fantastic sound quality! Much more enjoyable than the popular UEBoom.

Better flat frequency response like a pair of reference headphones (like the Sony Studio MV6 I prefer), more clear definition and detail, not muddy, better treble response (I don't mean tinny or lack of bass), and bass rivaling that of UEBoom. Oh, the main thing I noticed also, which confused me at first, is the wide stereo dispersion (?), um, I mean wide field effect and stereo separation. I literally looked at the cylinder puzzled as to what I was hearing and mentally verifying only this device was on and was the source of the sound I was hearing.

The UEBoom always sounded merely monaural from one sourcepoint; this sounded like surround sound effect applied to a two-speaker (not 5.1+) tv. I was amazed at what my senses were reporting to me. Okay, I'm going to say it, to my ears, and I have a class D amplifier and 5 pairs of quality headphones of different brands, the sound of this Amazon Tap is superior, right out of the box. I was amazed. And of course streaming directly sans device is certainly more convenient. It "just works". (After connecting to your Wi-Fi network.)

I learned to say "playlist rock", since I have a playlist named rock, or it will play all my Amazon music in the genre "rock". I did ask for the weather after entering my zip code through the Alexa app, which I dislike, and it responded with detailed information. Luckily music playback works directly without a need for app use. I will now mention this superior sound quality is half the price of it's aforementioned similar-sized competitor. I'm now really glad I bought it :)
***
Update: I returned it. It couldn't find a track in my music library, I checked title of track and found it instantly on my Fire, but the Tap still couldn't find it; everything I've tried to do with it either completely fails, or I resort to a different device because it's quicker and more convenient. It's mistaken "no" for "yes" and when asking for Julie Andrews started playing the soundtrack to Fifty Shades of Gray. It's been sitting on the kitchen counter unused. I could spend the money elsewhere better (I purchased two Fire HD 6" tablets which are excellent, speedy devices and fit into my front pocket). To each their own.

title: Do *not* buy a SIM card on Amazon; you'll need a new one from AT&T. GREAT HotSpot Device! :)
text:
I'll update if there's a problem once I receive my FREE SIM card with FREE Express Mail from AT&T. The unit comes charged, and everything worked perfectly, connected to my laptop, WiFi name & password printed on sticker. Very, very nice, compact, well-designed device. Easy connection, easy info once I learned to use the built-in electronic screen and "Info". The "ICCID" number is the SIM number, it's under "Info" with the IMEA number in the electronic screen (AT&T will need both numbers for activation). The IMEA is also listed beneath battery. Slide two little metal sliders on side to remove back cover to remove battery. But you don't have to, it's in the electronic screen "Info" :)

Persons much more mechanically inclined than I will see that the door to the SIM card is on the side edge, not in the back or under the battery. I would have ruined the device trying to dig out the back compartment if my husband hadn't stopped me. He needed tweezers to get out the SIM card regardless.

This is a great, mobile, easy HotSpot device that works just like any Wi-Fi on any device with a great connection. Mobile supposedly for 10 hours, less than hour recharge.

There's only one caveat: AT&T will tell you the pre-installed SIM card it comes with, sealed in new packaging, is INVALID. AT&T will give you a good one for FREE. You simply have to replace it, or if you're like me, get someone that can. :) That simple, and you're ready for set-up. *NOTE*: Both the pre-installed SIM card *AND* the SIM card being sold by a separate seller on Amazon that is suggested as being a good companion purchase with this device are INVALID. This according to AT&T themselves. They will send you a new, free one you can use; tell them what device you have and setup a data plan.

All you need then is to add a Data plan. This device, according to AT&T, *only* works with a postpaid plan ($50.00/month for 5 G's minimum), however there's no contract. There is a credit check. It will not work with prepaid, it will not work with a lesser plan, no matter what the packaging or Amazon description says. I just spent like 20 minutes on the phone with a very helpful, patient, and knowledgeable AT&T customer service representative who also consulted another department for verification.

The one exception is if you already have an AT&T cellphone plan (I do), you can "share" your data package you already have for only $20/month. So that's what I did. It still is postpaid, and there still is no contract on that part of the plan with your new HotSpot device. You'll be given a new number that's only for the HotSpot without a cellphone (Voice) plan component.

I'm really glad I bought this great device, I was a little apprehensive because I'm not techie and I've never tried a mobile HotSpot device before. To make it simple, get AT&T to install (instore) or send you a new SIM card that they say works with this device, and then you can set up the device (supposedly) online with ease. You have to add a data plan for it. I'll update if there's a problem, but the connection to my laptop worked seamlessly and looking through the device hardware and software on the electronic screen, it's designed beautifully and is a definite winner! :) :)

ps. Oh!, and it DOES receive 4G out of the box! :) Shows right in the screen corner like a Cellphone would with the bars.

title: I Fixed My Wi-Fi Problem
text:
I'm going to paste my comment from another earlier post I updated because I want to make sure everyone sees this, and hopefully it will help with your Wi-Fi problems too. Maybe Amazon won't be getting so many returns on these sweet Sony Ultrabooks.
_________

UPDATE: I know how to fix the Wi-Fi problem. It's easy and it's worked on two of my Sony Vaio Pro Ultrabooks. Get the latest driver directly from Intel's website. The name of the driver you need is: Wireless_16.10.0_e64

I did a full factory restore on both my Sony ultrabooks to insure a clean start. I set up my internet connection/password as if I was able to connect. I know it won't be able to. I'll then have to type in my name and computer password. When the process is complete and I'm on the start screen, I click on the desktop tile. I plug in my usb flash drive, click the folder icon on the task bar, and then click on the usb drive (E), whatever you've named it. I moved the new updated Intel driver from my usb flash drive to my desktop. Installed the update, ejected my usb flash drive, rebooted, and like magic I had a perfect internet connection. Sony's Intel Wireless Lan driver updates are not updated enough which is why so many people have been having problems and frustrations, blaming Sony, Microsoft, etc. But it's really an easy fix.

Remember to do all your Vaio Updates first thing, before updating Windows and upgrading to Windows 8.1. There are some critical updates that Sony states need to be done before upgrading to Windows 8.1.

I'm getting used the Windows 8.1 and I like it better than Windows 8. I have mine set to boot up to my desktop. I've had no problem adjusting to the right click on the left windows icon on the task bar to shut down/restart. Programs I use regularly I simply pin to my task bar.

Did I mention yet how much I love everything about this Ultrabook? :o)

title: Thankful for my Computer Savy Son

I'm in love with Windows 8 and this laptop! I would not be feeling the same if it weren't for my son's help. Everything went smoothly during setup, except I was having a frustrating time getting connected to the internet. Internet showed I was connected, all looked perfect, just could not get a good connection. I was feeling like I had the slowest laptop ever made, my Sony Vaio netbook was faster! I was not very happy. Disappointed, I even had another model laptop picked out after reading the reviews here.

Thankfully my son, who's been singing the praises of Windows 8 since his beta version, informed me that I probably needed my drivers updated. He told me to use my other laptop to access Sony's website to get to the software/drivers needed for this model. I simply downloaded the update for the Wireless LAN, moved the file to a usb flash drive so I could install it on this laptop. After the update was installed, I restarted just to be sure everything was set, and like magic I had speedy internet service.

My husband and daughter have different models of the S Series, only with Windows 7. I knew what to expect concerning the larger mouse pad, as it takes some getting used to, and can get in the way a little while typing. I like the lighted keyboard, and how thin this laptop is. I also chose this model because I'm not ready to give up my CD/DVD drive yet. This laptop has everything I wanted, except I plan to add more memory. I think it is at a reasonable price too.

Anyway, everything is working great. Now I have only to learn my way around Windows 8.

Wanted to add: Don't make the mistake I did an order 2x8 GB memory kit. My fault that I didn't notice that the 4 GB was fixed. I should have ordered just the one 8 GB of notebook memory to get the maximum 12 GB.

title: when i say 'turn off soundbar' t kinda blinks the green led on the Bose like its trying to do something but it doesn't in ...
text:
Its okay. it doesn't really work with my Bose Solo 15.
I'll say 'Alexa, turn on tv' and it doesnt turn on the Soundbar, i tried adjusting the delay settings but doesn't seem to work (no IR attachment should be needed as the soundbar is right under the TV).
If the soundbar/tv is already on, when i say 'turn off soundbar' t kinda blinks the green led on the Bose like its trying to do something but it doesn't in the end... Once I manually turn on the soundbar, if i say 'Alexa, raise/lower the volume' it does seem to work.

Also the Advanced setting to go straight to the tv/cable instead of the Fire Home doesn't work (I've tried changing it to the FireCube and swap back to TV/Cable but didnt work). Thats kinda important as my old parents dont want to see 'new things' and just want the old way the tv works working for them (with the added convenience of being able to use voice commands).
Cool product, but I'm going to return it if an update to resolve issues isn't out in next 30 days and maybe try out a Nvidia Shield with Google Assistant.

Also the wires are nice and loose on those other models ( https://www.amazon.com/JVC-HAFX101V-Headphones/dp/B007HIR3MG ), and not as rigid as these. The wire is a bit thicker on these, which maybe gives it some rigidity (which I don't like on these).

title: * The features are kinda cool (pressing the side of the headphone to stop/play/forward/backward playlists)
text:
I got a couple of these where Spotify offered them @ 50% off $50 sale...
I'd say Its somewhere between 2-3.5 stars.

Pluses:
* The Bluetooth works well.
* The features are kinda cool (pressing the side of the headphone to stop/play/forward/backward playlists).
* Above feature even works with Spotify on my Windows computer.
* The wire where you plug-in w/o using bluetooth is kinda cool so can use without using power.
* feature to share the bluetooth w/ a wire to a friend is cool. Me and sis watched a meteor shower and I played some tunes we could share w/o disturbing our quiet suburban neighborhood.

Minuses:
* I'm 5'3" with a small to regular-sized head, and it feels too tight and hurts ears after 30m-1hr. Almost a deal breaker.
* The headphones themselves feel tight, but also don't wrap around your ear like some headphones and dont stay on tightly. Like they are the size of your ear which I don't find very comfortable.
* The power button and USB charger port are right in the area where the headphone can rotate (and be half covered by the plastic).
Its annoying to access those buttons sometimes .
* sometimes accidentally activate the touch feature. Could be set to be less sensitive.

In fact it's so slow I thought mine must be defective, but after being on the phone with "tech support" for over 2 hours (just for them to hold my hand as I did a factory reset and analyzed some data) I was told it only has 1gb of RAM. I've got a tablet that's 5 years older with half that RAM that's, literally 2-3 times as fast.

You can't use any play store (and can't access most software) except for Amazon's garbage app shop.

Really, do not waste your money. Even attempting to watch prime is a nightmare of lag and frustration.
