title: Surprisingly good.  Picked up 40 channels.
text: This FlatWave Micro FL-2000 is surprisingly good.  It is small. Definitely smaller than my Mohu Leaf Metro that I have in another room, and it gets the same amount of channels. The cable attached is thinner than a regular cable wire which is nice, but it is also not that long.  I did not need to place the antenna too far from the TV, so for me it was fine.  But if you need to place it on a wall a few feet way, you will need to buy an extension cable.

title: Sturdy and easy to assemble.
text: I bought the TT104001GB for my 32" Samsung TV.  I wish the 2 bars that stabilize the square frame that you hang the TV on was movable.  Where the bars are, are exactly where the HDMI ports are on the back of my Samsung. So my tv has to sit off to the side instead of centered.  But I guess that's the fault of Samsung, but it would make the design better if you were given an option to adjust it to a different position.  The stand was very easy to assemble.  All the parts were lettered and numbered, and the instructions were very clearly pictured.  When I first opened the box, and saw all the screws an pieces needed, it thought it would be a daunting task, but with the numbering and the lettering system, it was fairly easy to assemble.  No extra tools needed, ever screwdriver and allen wrench is supplied in the kit. My advise is to only open the bags of screws as you go along following the instructions. That way everything is organized and not jumbled together.

title: I have range envy.
text: Range is OK, but my neighbor's is better.  This is a good router.  Much nicer than my old one.  The router is located upstairs in my office.  But when I went to connect my smart TV that is downstairs to my new router, I could see my neighbor's router had a stronger signal.  If you are looking for a good signal, my neighbors NETGEAR05 signal is stronger in the next house over than my ASUS router upstairs. I don't know, maybe he has a Repeater making his signal stronger.  But clearly mine doesn't cover the same range.  Other than range envy, I'm happy with it.  It was easy to set up, and I like that I can set up guest networks.

title: Excellent renewed phone that looks/acts brand new.
text:
Got this to replace spouses S6 that was on it's last legs. Didn't want to spend a fortune on a new phone, just needed a more updated phone that does basic functions. I've ordered open box/renewed items before, & never had an issue so was comfortable with this option also. You would never know it wasn't brand new, & it works great. It was wrapped really well in a plain box with a charger. While the S6 served us well, this one is nicer overall (bigger screen, more sleek). The best part is that it didn't come with any other phone carriers bloatware, & we use Mint Mobile & it set up perfectly. It came with Oreo, & within a day got a software update to Pie. You will need a new case, as the S6 one doesn't fit J7 & we have a new case/screen protector on the way. It has a regular headphone jack which we like, & uses micro USB for charging. It has a separate slot for an SD card, & dual SIM slot that accommodates one slot for nano (which is what we put in), & another that would fit micro SIM.

Very pleased with the renewed phone & hope it lasts as long as the other phone did.

title: Works perfectly.

title: Picked up a lot of signals
text: We're going to start cutting the cable cord, so before we do that, wanted to start in a room that has a cable box & test it out with with an antenna. This antenna was recommended in the reviews, & once I found the right spot, it picked up over 100 channels (without the amplifier), with plenty we like, including the main network ones. I tried to set it up without reading the instructions, figuring it can't be that hard, but dang, I definitely needed them.  The buttons are small & kinda hard to read what they are for , but have them memorized now them so no issues there.  Daylight savings hasn't happened yet, so will see how that feature works in Nov.  I have the brightness on the medium setting, & that is fine for me.  Unplugged it to see if the backup batteries work, & all ok there. I didn't want a fancy thing with USB charging, wave sounds etc, just a basic clock radio to ensure I wake up on time.  Honestly, if I'd searched Amazon to find a replacement, I probably wouldn't have chosen this, but overall I'm pretty happy with it, & have no plans to replace it unless it breaks.

It comes with many cables to hook it up, & I originally used the RCA ones, but wanted to use the optical cable, but couldn't since already was using that for something else, so I got a this optical splitter from amazon (http://www.amazon.com/MOTONG-Toslink-Digital-Splitter-Out-Black/dp/B00P8J0J0E/ref=sr_1_sc_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1457204231&sr=8-1-spell&keywords=matong+optical) & now I can use both items with an optical cable. I have to say I'm really bummed this didn't work out as I liked it a lot & for anyone with a normal wrist size, the refurbished one is a great deal.  With my tiny wrists I probably won't have a lot of options for any kind of fitness band, but would recommend this product otherwise.

text: I didn't order this from Amazon, as Wal-Mart had a deal that was a lot cheaper than the price here.  Had it delivered since a long heavy box that we didn't want to deal with. I had been looking for a really long time for something that called out to me that was worth replacing my beloved wall unit with, & fell in love with this immediately after seeing it in the store.  It's a beautiful piece of furniture for sure & we love it. Very sturdy. We used the included TV mount for our 55inch TV which works great & we do enjoy the swivel feature. The shelves have enough space for all our electronics that are stacked 2 high. The only 2 minor cons:  1) it's particle board, not wood & does scratch easily, so be careful. They do include a touch up pen, & we had to use it almost immediately  2) the styrofoam it's packed in is terrible & just crumbles, making a big mess!  I fear I will be cleaning up little white balls for years to come, & they are even stuck underneath the shelves, so who knows when they will drop off.  Apart from those 2 things, we don't regret buying this at all & are really happy with the purchase.

title: Really Good Antenna.
text:
I had no idea which antenna to buy, as read that really varies as to signal towers etc & my tower is approx 30-31 miles away so figured this would be fine. I just bought a new TV to replace a tiny TV for a small room that doesn't have cable & won't be getting it, but wanted to get just a few channels for guests. This antenna is great & works really well. I didn't want a really cheap one, but didn't want an expensive one either, & this one was right in the middle. It brought in a ton of digital channels, including most of the local stations & some others like KCET etc. The picture is very clear, which surprised me as was expecting it to break up like my old analog antenna, but it's actually almost perfect & I forget that it's not cable. I really love the 20ft cable length, as works perfectly for the room size. I have it behind the TV, nowhere near the window, so am not using the suction cups.

**update 11/7/15 - love this thing, I'm still blown away at the quality of the reception it brings in.

title: Better than most iPods
text:
I purchased this 4GB Sandisk MP3 Player from Best Buy and I paid $10.00 more. That does bother me but I found myself in need of an MP3 player right away or I would have gone mad so I guess the extra $10.00 was worth it. I was going to buy an iPod Touch, 8GB, 4th generation, on sale for $204.00 at Best Buy, but I'm glad I didn't. This Sandisk sounds better than previous iPods that I've had and it has a good equalizer too.

Dragging iTunes music directly into Sandisk folder (that appears once it's connected to the computer), didn't always work. Instead, create a folder on the desktop of your computer and drag the iTunes into that and then drag the contents of that folder into the Sandisk folder, it just seems to work better that way.

The one thing that was not included in the box was the AC Adapter and I was highly annoyed that I had to purchase a duel USB/AC adapter wall charger. Get one here from Amazon; Best Buy honestly has no bargains. To be fair I didn't HAVE to buy the adapter because the device comes with a USB cord to charge via the computer, but if you do not want to bring your computer with you it's nice to have an AC adapter that can be plugged into any wall outlet at any time. Other than that it's a very good purchase.

title: It doesn't work.
text:
Update on 12/29/14...This was the biggest waste of money ever. It crashes regularly, sometimes hourly, at least daily. There's no seeming correlation between activity and crash, and it often happens when I'm not even using it. Screw this; I am done with ASUS......

I'm on my second one of these, after the first was replaced. When it works, it's a great little device. Fast processor, better wi-fi reception than any of my other devices, brilliant screen, excellent battery life. However, this replacement has the same exact problem as the one I sent back: it frequently shuts down and restarts itself. It's not just going to sleep, but rather fully shutting off with a crack of the speaker and reload to the google screen. When it happens, all of the open/recent apps are cleared. This problem doesn't happen all the time, but when it does it will be a handful of times a day for a number of days...then it'll be fine for a couple weeks, then it starts all over again. It can be pretty infuriating, but i'm not using it for anything so critical that I'm willing to spend a couple hundred more for something else, or the same price for something that is inferior though more reliable.

title: It was a joy.... TO TAKE THEM OUT
text:
I can't believe I fell for buying these expensive as hell headphones, all of the positive reviewers must not have ever made a trip to Walmart to buy headphones with rubber fittings for like $15. These headphones suck for the following reasons:

*Fit - what they do is force themselves against the upper portion of the ear which after a few minutes becomes extremely painful. The cord is longer on one side on purpose, BY A LOT so you have that wire hanging in your mouth/face the whole time due to the cord been coiled. I prefer to have cord hanging straight down and out of my face.

*Sound - no base like you would get from headphones that fit into your ear, I did not realize how much it sounds better when the headphones go inside your ear instead of been outside.

*Cost - you are paying only for the looks and packaging.

Positives:

I will keep the clipper that came with them, it is a very nice clipper and I will use it on my $10 set of headphones I been using at the gym. Too bad this clipper cost me $50.

Lessons learned: never buy anything for 2x than what it should cost.

title: With great sound...comes not great build quality
text:
[Great Sound]

As noted in some of the other reviews this pair of headphones has great sound for its price range. Sound is quite neutral, without the bass emphasis of a lot of headphones at this range. Highs are also good and not muted. The cable is also very generous in length, which is great as my computer is far away from my chair. Finally, the headband adjustment is exceptional. I have a fairly large skull and most headphones I've purchased have not fit well. However, this one fits perfectly and even has more room to expand. The only comfort downside is that the pads have quite a stiff covering material. This is not so great for comfort for long use sessions, but not too big of an issue as you can replace them eventually if needed. The thicker pad material would make the headphones last longer...if it were not for the major issue I describe below with build quality.

[Disappointing Build Quality]

I've had my pair for about 1.5 years now, and today the headphone snapped at the joint between the top band and where the extension band slides out. See attached photo. You can see that there is a metal band in the headband to provide elasticity and resistance. But the extension band (the part that slides in and out) doesn't have a metal band inside of it. This concentrates stress at this transition point, causing the plastic to snap here eventually. I noticed that the plastic on the other cup has also started cracking. The plastic itself feels quite brittle and is about as thick as the metal strip in the headband. I think the fact that I have a large head and had to extend the headphones out only hastened their demise as this put more stress on the plastic-only part of the headbands.

[Conclusion]

This is a great sounding pair of headphones for their price, but alas I cannot recommend them anymore due to the snapping of the headband. To fail after about a year of use is a bit on the low end. My previous pair of similarly priced headphones lasted over 10 years without the headband failing (only cable had become worn). I think you *might* be OK if you have a smaller head and don't have to extend the headphone band too much, but if you have to expand it to near its maximum, it will probably snap off like mine did.

title: For all those who said that it doesn't fit the FZ28
text:
The camera has threads on the inside edge of the barrel to attach a filter. The Tiffen filter has 2 sets of threads on it. The first set faces outwards and screws into the lens barrel (not clearly visible in the picture). The other set is on the opposite side and faces inwards. It allows attachment of additional filters or other extensions. Only one side will attach to the camera, so make sure you are attaching it the right way.

As far as a review, the lens is not the best one out there for best image quality (you might see some flaring and glare), but is a good value for the price, good protection for your camera, and has a nice 10 yr warranty. I would still recommend it, since its much cheaper to replace this than your camera lens.

title: Great video quality!
text:
Purchased two of these Eufy 2K cams to test out and determine if they're good enough to replace the Wyze cams. These Eufy cams definitely capture higher resolution, more detailed videos compared to the Wyze cam v2. The pan and tilt feature is great when I want to remotely check different parts of an area and the pan/tilt action is very silent. You can set the cam to automatically track/follow motion when it's detected. The amount of time it takes to go to live view on a cam is within a couple of seconds and the alerts for motion is definitely faster than the Wyze cam v2. The time from me waving my hand in front of the cam and getting an alert on my phone is about 3 seconds or less.

I did experience issues with one Eufy cam where it would randomly start panning by itself and would do a 360 degree pan. The Eufy app works overall, but I did notice several times I had connection issues when trying to live view, but this issue also happens on Wyze cams, too.

You can set the Eufy cam to record only when motion or sound is detected or set the cam to continuous recording. If you choose continuous recording the video resolution will be reduced to 1080p resolution. For motion recording you can set up activity zones (specific areas you want to detect motion), adjust motion detection sensitivity, detect people, detect pets, and detect all other motion. Eufy's app is still missing the ability to view multiple live views of cams at the same time, which is a shame and hopefully they have a software update for that.

Overall, the Eufy 2k cam has great video quality, the pan/tilt motion is useful and silent, has a lot of features, and the price is competitive. They go on sale from time to time, so if you're not in a hurry then I'd wait for a sale.

title: Great 4k video quality, but has issues
text: The 4k video quality of the front dash cam is great compared to it's competitors. Previously I used a Blackvue DR-650s. Reviewing/sorting through video clips is not as easy compared to the Blackvue. Viofo app isn't great and sometimes the settings don't save, so you have to go back and try again. I also don't like that the dash cam has to stop recording before you can review saved video/ photos or change settings. I'm using a Blackvue external battery pack with this dash cam so it continues to record when the car is off, but it doesn't go into parking mode while plugged into the battery pack. I read online that I need to purchase some other set of wires to connect in between the dash cam and the Blackvue battery pack. I didn't have to do this with other dash cams I've tested. In terms of reliability of this dash cam I would rate it average at best. I noticed a couple of times it was frozen and had to unplug and plug the power cable to get the cam to work again. The previous Blackvue came did occasionally freeze also, but it restarts itself and continues to record afterwards. The last issue I noticed is that the cables for this dash cam system are very THICK compared to the Blackvue's cables. This makes it difficult to neatly tuck and hide the cables in the car. Overall, this is a dash cam with great 4K video quality, but issues mentioned above that make it an overall average device. I'll probably replace it when there's a better option. For now it's difficult to beat with the price tag compared to it's competitors for a 4K front + 1080p rear system.

title: Great TV! 59" Samsung PN59D6500
text:
I was hesitant in purchasing a large TV online without at least seeing the same model at a store first, but I saw this TV with a good blu-ray/3D glasses/Shrek combo that was difficult to pass on. My girlfriend was doing everything she could to convince me not to buy a huge, expensive TV. I was tired of my Samsung 32" LCD TV and wanted something bigger. I still can't believe I pressed the submit order button, but I'm glad I did. I spent 30 minutes weighing the pros and cons while the TV was in my shopping cart. I wasn't sure if it was my imagination or a sales tactic but the quantity shown was going down as I refreshed the description page for this TV as I was deciding. After submitting the order I went through the "there's still time for more research and cancel the order" phase and spent a couple more hours looking up reviews and trying to not look at my gf directly in the eye that night...I survived and a couple of days later two guys carried a giant Samsung box up to my place. The TV is HUGE compared to my old 32" LCD.

Physically this TV is beautiful, thin, it has a clear border, and has Samsung's smart tv WIFI access. The picture quality looks great with deep blacks and vivid colors. There are many options to adjust the picture and sound. My friends come by to play games sometimes and I found out that this TV even has a game mode. Another benefit of this model is the realistic 3D effects. You have to wear the 3D glasses to enjoy the 3D effects, which will add to the cost of the TV if you didn't get in on the combo deal.

I did find a dead pixel on the screen during my trial period and called Amazon to exchange the TV right away. I was amazed how easy it was to process the exchange and schedule the delivery of the TV. The delivery company Amazon used didn't provide very friendly or timely service but that's not Amazon's fault. The only thing I wasn't informed of until I was surveyed is that the TV delivery service includes setup and disposal of the box and packing material. Those lazy delivery men didn't even offer any of that service but even if they did I wouldn't let them touch my new baby. The second TV didn't have any dead pixels or other issues. I've been enjoying the TV so much it took me almost a year to write this review. I highly recommend this TV for value, it's features, and great picture quality. It has other cool features such as the ability to stream Netflix through WIFI and use your Android phone as a remote control. I was laughing the first time I downloaded the remote app on my Samsung Galaxy phone and tricked my gf into thinking the TV was changing channels by itself.

Pros:
- great picture quality
- lots of customizable settings
- gaming mode
- realistic 3D
- huge 59" screen
- loud speakers
- Samsung smart tv WIFI DLNA support
- use Android phone as TV remote as long as you have Samsung's remote app installed.
- stream netflix on the TV without extra equipment
- software update through WIFI
- connect your laptop to the tv via HDMI cable to use the TV as a computer monitor.

Cons:
- heavy TV
- slight buzz noise when TV is on but not really noticeable unless it's really quiet.
- you will be watching more TV than normal.
- your friends and family members will come over sometimes uninvited to watch TV or play video games.
- wish it had more ports

title: Had it forever, love it, and will keep using it forever.
text: I've had an UltraPod for about 30 years.  The same UltraPod. I can't count the number of times I've used it, and it does its intended job perfectly.  Don't expect to put a full-size DSLR with a telephoto lens on it; I think you'd have to crank the ball-and-socket joint dangerously tight.  But for a small camera, or a video camera -- fantastic.  One of my favorite uses is for taking indoor shots where a flash would be disallowed, inappropriate, or simply useless.  You can attach it to the camera, leave the legs closed, and simply hold it against a vertical surface (especially a wall corner) and keep the camera rock-steady during a long exposure.  Someone else said that the velcro strap was too short to wrap around most branches, and my reaction is, "Well, perhaps so.  If only velcro straps were readily available ..."  My only issue with the design is that you can easily loosen the clamp so that the head simply falls apart. Fortunately, it goes back together just as easily, and I still think that the design is ingenious. I highly recommend the UltraPod.

title: Worse than worthless to me
text:
Both the image and audio quality from this camera have always been disappointing. I didn't really know just how poor it was until I owned an iPhone 4S, which captures vastly superior video, and mono audio that sounds much better than the tinny stereo captured by the Picsio.

And then there's the problem with mysteriously aborted video recordings, which has happened twice to me. The first time I missed part of a dance performance, but that was mostly an annoyance at the time, since it was an ad-hoc recording and I simply switched to my phone. The second time, I missed a good chunk of a recital I'd been asked to video for a friend. The recording stopped unexpectedly and retained only 1 second of the segment. I had started the recording, watched a few seconds to confirm that it going, and sat down. 9 minutes later someone notified me that the display had gone black and it hadn't been blinking for the previous two songs. When I hit the power button and it woke up (!?!?), the display said something about "file" and "management" and "update", and after trying to get it to come on and start recording, it said "update complete" or "finished" and then it recorded the remainder of the performance. (Pardon me if I don't remember the exact on-screen messages.) I had an hour of capacity (in iFrame mode) left on the card, which was freshly formatted, and the camera was on DC power so that batteries wouldn't be an issue. There was no discernible reason for this to have happened.

Bottom line: I can't trust this camera, and I won't even try to resell it or give it to someone; I wouldn't want to do that to someone else. For more serious video, I dropped the coin on a Canon VIXIA (which is fantastic), and for casual video, I'll use my iPhone. Either way, I will never rely on this camera again.

title: Command for copying audiobook folders properly
text:
One tip for folks who want to fix the "playing out of order" bug when copying files in an audiobook folder over, on MacOS you can use the following command to ensure that a folder's contents are copied to the xtrainerz in alphabetical order:

rsync -rv --ignore-existing <source_dir> <xtrainer_dir>

Then, the files will play in the correct order on the device. This command will skip/ignore existing files if they already exist for whatever reason.

title: HORRIBLE CAMERA
text:
I got this camera from my kids for christmas. I was sooo excited. As I had wanted a camera for some time. They picked it up at Target during the sale, so they had not been able to get reviews in advance.
WELL. I took this on literally a once in a lifetime trip: The Great Wall in Beijing
I took it out of the box, got extra batteries, packed it and off I went-Carry on only.
Got to Beijing, took a few pictures around town, feeling pretty comfortable in how to use it given I didn't want to mess up when I was at the Great Wall.
No issues, although the initial batteries did not last more than 35 pictures, but alas, I had anticipated that and had more!
(actually I did have some times where the camera was irratic and would and would not take pictures as it said the battery was low) I put in new high use batteries.
Finally the tour bus gets us to the "wall". I get out all smiley and ready to walk the Great Wall.
Got ONE picture. I am not kidding. ONE. Even with the new batteries, it would turn on but have a blank screen-white and nothing else. Took batteries out, put them in again just in case I messed up. Nothing. Had my husband try. Had my 14 yr old son try. NOTHING.
I come home with ONE picture of the Great Wall on my camera, 5 on my husbands Iphone.
DO NOT BUY. HEARTACHE. HORRIBLE
Not only did I not get Great Wall pictures, but my kids were sad that they had gotten me a bum camera when they were so excited to have gotten me one. Too late to return of course, so I guess I have to add to the garbage sites and that does not make me happy either.

title: Easy to set up
text:
It works well once set up and the setup is easy. The application software is a little annoying in one respect: the camera views on my iPad are always rotated to portrait orientation, which makes the view itself sideways instead of vertical. I assume that it's some configuration issue, but I can't find it: it shouldn't be that obscure to find.

The basic functions (detection, control) are mostly fine. You will need to subscribe to the PLUS service from WYZE in order to have longer recordings made after motion detection, to control the rest period between recordings, and to detect anything other than motion. It's not expensive, but if you're on a tight budget, you should check the current subscription price, too. The battery charge lasts several weeks in our rural location, with only two or three callers a day (UPS and Post Office, mostly).

You'll also need to buy little memory cards for the camera(s) and the base station, if you want the videos quickly available for review and you don't have fast internet speeds. I bought mine directly from WYZE to assure they'd work, other reviewers have said that they've had problems with non-WYZE supplied cards. The cards don't fill up fast (good compression, I guess) and allow you to keep the videos for longer than WYZE will keep them for you.

Detection of motion is not as quick as I'd like, particularly at night. It misses our newspaper delivery which takes about 5 seconds for the carrier to drive into our driveway, drop the paper, then back out. There may be a sensitivity control to adjust in the application; if so, I've clearly missed it. It did detect a bobcat at night that jumped onto and walked along the top of our gate, so it's not clear to me what is going on with detection sensitivity -- see a bobcat, miss a car?

WYZE keeps making improvements to the software for the camera system; we've had about three updates from them since late 2020, when I bought and installed this. As one would hope, the camera system recovers from an electric blackout quite nicely. The cameras seem nicely weather resistant, too; we've had some heavy downpours and wind this winter.

title: Sony's reliability has gone to hell.
text:
Sony's quality has gone to hell. When I bought this, I wrote: There's nothing about this clock I don't like except that it takes a little while to familiarize oneself with the digital controls, but once over that slight hump, it's logical and easy to use in the dark, fumbling around by touch. The dimmest setting is dim enough not to be a bother to sleep. The reception is good, the tuning straightforward.

Now, July 14, 2018, I am extremely disappointed with this radio. Yesterday morning, it woke me at 4:00 am (I had not set either alarm), would not turn off normally, then began scanning through the FM frequencies. It would not stop, none of the buttons responded, and finally, I had to pull the plug on it to shut it off. Sony's website suggests removing the battery and letting the unit return to whatever its default state is. That did not fix it, nor have several attempts of the same method, once with the battery left out and powering up. This clock/radio has become completely unresponsive; it's bricked itself.

I have two older Sony cube clock/radios, one 30 years old, the other 20. Both are working fine, still, though the display is dimming on the 30 year old unit. I like the newest clock/radio, as shown by my initial review. But 2 years on and total failure, that's ridiculous. When will manufacturers with good reputations learn that their reputations will fall apart if they don't control the quality of their products? This kind of thing makes "Made in China" mean that it is of poor quality, poor workmanship, and poor design.

title: Take care, protect your purchase, or suffer from a delayed pig in a poke.
text:
Back in November 2015, I purchased this used AMD 1065T from M&D. I installed it a few days later (Nov. 7) and it had been working fine since that time until July 12, 2016. Then it failed suddenly, no BSOD, nothing. Hoping that it was my five year old power supply, I replaced that with a new one. No joy. Today, I replaced the 1065T from M&D with the 925 that I had replaced with the 1065T. My system started up with no problems, so it is definitely the case that the 1065T from M&D has failed.

I should say, given the nature of these devices, how they are used, etc. that I don't and didn't overclock this device. But given the sudden failure of this CPU, my bet is that a previous user did overclock it. My experience with AMD and Intel CPUs (all new) has been that properly installed and used, they don't fail. I did not expect that a used CPU would fail at 7 months of use.

I did not make use of Amazon's two year protection plan, more the fool I. M&D consider their posted policy of 30 days refund/return to be adequate customer service. You will not as I do not, when your used M&D CPU fails after a few months. Unfortunately, the used market is the only way you can get one of these CPUs, now. If you're not willing to kiss your money and effort goodbye in a few months, get Amazon's protection plan, because M&D will not help you at all after thirty days. Their response to my request for a replacement: "Are [sic] warranty is limited to 30 days." Genius!

title: Good quality at a good price
text:
This is a great PSU. I stick to brands I trust when it comes to the power supply as well as looking them up on the cybenetics site. If you don’t know what that is, look them up, they are a great resource. I do see what other people are saying, this unit is louder than my old one and that is confirmed by third party testing. I don’t think it’s the worst thing, but that could be because my case fans are a little loud in comparison to the fan in the PSU.

The cables are nice, they feel like corsair in their wrap and heat shrink, but that’s no surprise since most power supplies are made by a handful of suppliers. Just as a note, you should never mix cables from another brand though unless you are certain that they are the exact same pin out on the supply side. I have the Silent Base 802 and it fits fine in there. The case is well insulated so it’s not as loud in there as it was in my test build with the side panel off. The system definitely doesn’t need the 1000w of power currently since it’s only powering 4 HDDs, 2 SSDs, non-overclocked i7 10th gen and RX480 8GB GPU. The upgrade here was in preparation for a 4080 and overclocking the CPU.

Overall, I am impressed with the quality of it. The price is closer to that of a gold rated 1000w than it a platinum one. I will use it in my daily PC and see if it gives me any issues. I will update if anything goes wrong.

title: Works as expected
text: I have had the gimbal for a bit now and was looking for a way to protect it. It’s really good for car trips, but it would take up precious space on a carry-on bag. It is a tight fit for the main body of the gimbal. It’s not a bad fit, but with how close it is to the corner of the case, I worry that it could be problematic if it takes a fall right on that spot. All the accessories are held well, and the pocket is great for the cable and bag it came with. I do like it and would recommend it for any car trips or if you have a checked bag. If you need a compact solution though, you are going to want to save the soft bag it comes with.

title: Easy to install and good quality
text: These cable raceways are nice and really help organize wires behind my desk. They are wirdly rebranded from another name I’ve never hear of, but that doesn’t seem to be a bad thing. I have used everything in the kit, and they all work as expected. The adhesive that came with it is different than what I expected but works well so far. I was expecting the standard 3M Foam tape, but this is thick elastic clear tape that I have used in similar applications. The opening is wider than expected so when I was pushing cables through, they would occasionally fall out. It was not too bad to install though and overall, I’m happy with the how it is helping me organize my cables. I will update if the adhesive lets go on either the raceway or the cable clips

title: Causing my monitors power light to pulse
text: I usually don't have a problem with cables from this brand, but this one is a miss for sure. I can't even test the picture quality since it causes my monitor to power cycle. The led light just goes on and off and occasionally the logo will pop up for a second and then go back to power cycling. The locks are standard and hold well, but they do make removing it a little more annoying. This normally isn't a problem, but when the cable is causing such issues it's nice to be able to unplug it as fast as possible. Overall, I can't recommend this product.

title: Unique option with some great features
text:
I really like this NVME enclosure. It offers excellent features and power loss protection is nice to have when dealing with desktops that don’t have their own battery. I really like the data available right on the enclosure and it really is nice to see additional data you couldn’t see without it. I have included pictures of some of the available screens. It’s not as fast as I would have expected, but it’s possible my laptop is the restriction. I think something is restricting it since the file size seems to have insignificant effect on transfer speeds during my tests. I have provided pictures of my results with file size set to 256MB, 1GB and 4GB. These tests are very consistent, and I know the drive isn’t the limiting factor so it’s either my gaming laptop or the enclosure. It does get warm to the touch, but not dangerously hot. The screw that holds the drive down had manufacturing bur left on it so look closely before screwing yours down.

I still recommend the enclosure since it’s faster than my internal HDD and my SATA SSD. I noticed that it has the ability to update firmware, but at the time of writing this review, the firmware update page doesn’t mention this product. I will keep using this regularly and update if I have any issues with it.

title: Great for drones
text: Samsung makes some great flash storage and most of my micro SD cards are from them. After testing this one though I don' t know whether I need to get a new adapter or I just got a slower card than another reviewer. I’m using a ugreen usb 3.0 card reader with and without the SD adapter. The best I was able to get was ~96MB/s read and ~84MB/s write. I plan to get a new card reader and retest since I believe it to be that. I know from my experience with Samsung flash storage that the reliability is great. I am using this in my DJI drone and have no issues with it. If you are looking for a good card for action cams or drones, then this is a great option.

title: Good budget option, but not the best budget option
text:
Easier to set up than you might think, although not as intuitive as offerings from TP such as the m5. I have set up a few mech networks at this point and I do think having that knowledge was helpful when setting up this one. I don’t think it’s particularly hard, but you will need to take your time with it and follow the instructions to the letter. Start by adding just the first unit and let it update. Then add the second and update the firmware on that too. You just have to wait until the lights turn the appropriate colors, if you don’t it will cause issues.

If you’re not using this in as a replacement for the main wireless router select the new network option. If you are adding on use the extender option. There are a lot of ways to set this up if you are a network person, but for the average person just go with extending your current network.

The app isn’t the best, but I don’t think it deserves as much hate as it gets. I’m on Android 9 and it works fine for me. I prefer the web interface, but you can get most things accomplished in the app.

Overall, I do notice a drop in wireless speed when compared to being connected to the fios router, but it’s still fast enough for most. Just a note, when you use one of the further away nodes you get even less speed. I have included screen captures from node 1 and node 2 in the system and you can see the noticeable drop for yourself. They are a cheap option that works decently well, but if you’re a power user look elsewhere.

title: Easy to install. Great for reusability
text:
These connectors are a great option for users that have trouble with the crimp style, or just want to make temporary patch cables and want to reuse the connectors. The build quality is nice and with the strain reliefs and anti-snag design, it’s nicer to pull the cable back from a disconnected equipment. When installing I recommend putting the cable tie in place when installing the boot. I have done it both ways and pushing the cable tie through does work, it’s just not as easy as easy as putting it in place with the boot.

For those that have never used these connectors before, just remember “ToolLess” really means less tools. In this case it really is the same number of tools because you swap the crimper out for pliers. So, you will still need a wire cutter and pliers to install the connector.

Overall, these are a great option for reusability and great if you need a temporary or permanent end. They are bulky in comparison to their crimp on counterparts, but that is expected. If you have an area where space is limited, you might want to go with crimp on ones.

title: Great upgrade from my old card
text:
There isn’t much to say about this piece of network equipment, it works well even being used on a very old desktop from 2008.

I use a lot of TP-Link products and this one doesn’t disappoint. I put it into an old tower I use mainly as a NAS drive and remote PC in the basement. This works extremely well and has brought network speeds way up from the old PCI Wi-Fi card I was using. I have included a before and after picture and you can see the big improvement. I’m using the newer FiOS router (G3100) which supports 802.11ax so these speeds are from a computer from 2008 to that router. There’s a good chance it will be faster in a newer computer.

I recommend this if you need a new network card or just want one for your new build. The antennas are not small though so keep that in mind if there are a lot of wires behind your tower or space is tight.

title: Well made and feels durable
text:
This adapter has made my new work computer usable again. I recently switched to a 2019 MacBook Pro and the lack of anything USB-C was annoying. I wanted a simple adapter for one of my monitors and this fit the bill. I like the led status light, knowing that it is working does help rule it out when plugging it in to HDMI cables at the office. I have also tried it using my S8 and it works with DeX without issue.

I think it get a little hot considering it is not a power adapter, but it will not burn you. Another thing I noted against my old MacBook with an HDMI port built in, is that with an adapter the colors don’t seem as dark. It’s not only this adapter that I noticed this with, so I think it’s more of an issue with adapters in general.

Overall, I would recommend this to anyone who needs just an HDMI adapter for either a phone, computer that uses type C ports exclusively or you just need one for a third monitor.

title: Easy to use and quick to set up
text:
The projector screen is leaps and bounds better than my old one. I no longer get fiberglass splinters in my hands from setup and it’s much quicker too. I really like the tripod, but wish it was a little more robust. The telescoping action can slip a little with too much downward pressure. One thing to note is this is a thinner fabric, only one piece instead of two. At night I don’t notice a huge difference going from the double layer one to this. I wish it came with a little carrying case. It would make this a perfect set if it did. The poles are like tent poles, with bungie connecting them, which makes it easier to set up and take down.

Overall:
A good option for an easy to use projector screen. I would recommend it for anyone looking for something simple and easy to use.

title: Good fit, but noisy
text: So the fan comes in a very simple brown box, no marketing materials or anything. I needed to replace a PSU fan, and due to the annoying size of the fan this brand was one of only a few options. The fan is not extremely noisy when it's outside of the PSU case, but the added air pressure when installed gives the fan a quite loud hum. It's not a normal fan noise either. It is by far the loudest fan in the case now. Compared to the old one this is much louder. It does work and it's definitely pushing more air through then the last one so it's an acceptable annoyance. Overall if you need a new PSU fan this one isn't a bad choice if noise isn't a huge concern.

title: 1 Failure and the other very slow
text:
I was trying to replace a few older 2.0 SanDisk flash drives with something a little newer. These caught my eye and I decided to give them a try. After testing their speed using the standard software, I noticed something weird. They have a burst of speed at the start but die out quick. I tried another one and same result. I was trying to set one up as a Ubuntu usb but the speed of the drive made it unusable. It was at least 10x slower to get into th OS then the 5 year old SanDisk Cruzer I use. I reached out to the company amd they said to basically send them back to Amazon through the normal return channel. I'm always extremely pleased with the ease of returns through Amazon and that was the only high point of the whole purchase.

When I formatted the drives to send back, one threw itself into read only mode and caused a BSOD. I cant possibly recommend this product to anyone, and I would stick with the brands most people are familiar with.

title: Didn't work with my Seagate Drive
text: The product looks like it will work for some drives, but not all. I have a pretty standard Seagate drive that I was trying to use and the retaining pins wouldn't seat. I'm not sure if it was a defective product or not. If they had just put holes and provided screws that would have been a much better solution. I know it's probably cheaper to use plastic pins, but from a reliability standpoint screws win every time. Id look elsewhere for a drive cady, with so many options don't bother with ghis one.

title: Good but definetly cheap
text:
These were a cheap pair that in all honesty I got because it came with the mic/headphone y adapter. I needed a cheap pair for work from home and the computer required the adapter. I started to use the earbuds and was a bit underwhelmed, but understanding for how cheap they were.

Pros:
Usable and comfortable
Decent quality (For the Price)
The volume control is slider based and easy to use

Cons:
Sound is muffled
Audio quality is lower than earbuds only a little more expensive.

Not a pro or a con, just something to note:
The mic is at where the two headsets meet. Normally earbuds have it higher up and on the right or left side. It doesn't seem to effect audio quality of the mic, but I have heard it's a little quieter than my other earbuds that came with my phone.

Overall:
If you need everything from the headphones to the splitter, and don't expect incredible audio then the are a decent pair to buy. If you have a nice pair of earbuds and just need an adapter I would say just buy the adapter. If you don't need the adapter at all there are better earbuds for a little bit more. I will update this review if these break or I have other issues.

title: Nice earbuds with QI charging
text:
These are very well packed and overall nicely designed. I like that they went with a type C cable to charge them. Other earbuds I have used have gone with micro USB and that is definitely getting annoying to keep an extra cable on me. I really like the ability to charge these with the QI charger I have. That makes it convenient to charge at not android users houses. The sound quality is nice and honestly they are extremely easy to pair.

Using them as a pair or as just one is easy. After pairing with your phone you can simply put the one you aren't using in the case. When you want to switch back to two you take is out and you will hear powering on and the sound will sync. The one downside I have found with earbuds in this price range is they don't offer the ability to sense when it's removed from your ear. This means when you want the earbud to turn off you'll need to put it in the case. The manual does a good job of explaining what tapping the side will do and you can also power them on and off holding down the side of it.

Overall:
These are great set of earbuds and are being used as my daily pair at the moment. I will update this review if I have any issues.

title: A cheap price for a good replacement
text: After the factory antenna was stolen off my car I thought I'd have to get an oem one at around 50-70 dollars. Luckily I found this cheap option. title: Good and Improving
text:
These testers are made in China, but do show a good build quality. This review will include two of these units since the first units board is starting to loosen. They sent me a newer updated model that will soon be available here. They have addressed some, not all, of the problems found in the first generation.

First Unit:
Came in a white box with a pluggable sticker identifying it. It came slightly scratched on the screen already, but was not to bad. This was the first generation that suffered from an flipped display when plugged into devices such as a mac. The display is slightly dimmer than the new model and flipped between charge voltage and amperage to charge direction. This make it harder to review products when the screen suddenly changes and the camera taking the picture.

Second Unit:
This unit came in a proper retail box, and looks like something you would see in a store. The screen was also in better condition and clearer, which made reading the display easier. They have flipped the display to make it easier to read when plugged into certain ports, but a button to rotate the display would be optimal. They have also put all the information on one screen, so it isn't constantly switching between charge data and direction.

Overall:
The unit is improving, but still needs a few tweaks to make it great. First is the offset of the USB-C plug. It makes it difficult to use on thinner devices. Second would have to be the lack of total milliamps transferred (mah). I would say if you get the white box one, return it and wait for the newer one, it offers a few improvements and the company assures me "we did some display work and internally we upgraded to stronger USB-C connectors. The new unit should also read higher as there is less electrical loss through the new connectors". Their words not mine. But they have switched from the USB-C connectors with a joint, to ones that are solid.

So the product, like all in this price range, is made in china. The sound quality is okay for a 5 dollar set of earbuds, but definitely not a great everyday pair. It's more useful as a spare. title: Not a bad simple option
text:
This is definitely a good option for someone with not a lot of room, but still needs an alarm clock, but that being said it is outdated for modern times.

Cons:
The screen can be hard to read at certain angles.
The two charging ports only supply .5 amps and 1 amp ( useless for modern phones).
Feels a little cheap.

Pros:
Not that bad of sound quality.
Good reception for the radio.
An available auxiliary plug and cord.
Simple and easy to use.

The bottom line is if you are looking to charge your phone with your alarm clock than definitely look elsewhere, but if you need a small simple alarm clock for a spare bedroom than this is a great option for the occasional guest.

title: Doesn't live up to the Sennheiser name
text: As I try to start all my reviews with where it's made, this one falls into the Made in China category. It's not an extremely expensive hi-fi unit, eben thou it says it is hi-fi, but for the price the sound quality should a lot better. It's like listening to an am radio station that goes in and out of range. The tuning is not a simple selector switch, but instead it uses a scroll wheel located right by the volume scroll wheel. I'm not sure what genius thought that was a smart location for it, because on a few a occasions I've changed the tuning by mistake. if your TV is like mine with an aux cord out, and no sound system, than you might run into the issue where the TV won't play through its own speakers when the unit is plugged in and your using it. This may be an issue if you wanted to use it as a audio booster if you are hard of hearing and want a separate volume control from that of the TV's speakers. Overall it was just poor experience with the unit. I usually love Sennheiser products, and they used to be made very well, I believe there high end is still that way. but like every company these days they sacrifice a lot trying to cheapen themselves to a price point that everyone can afford.

title: My first drive failure
text: I bought this product back in 2014, and forgot to do an initial review purely because I didn't use it a lot until now. I have been using it for 2 semesters now, and it is primarily used to backup my sandisk flash drive. After unplugging it from the school computer it no longer works, I have lost all of my programs for school, because for this semester I decided to switch to this as my primary drive for my large programs. I am in the process of trying to recover the drive, but I'm not expecting it to be successful. I am going to try to get it replaced under warranty, but that still won't replace the data I lost. This was a tough lesson, but I guess I'll have to backup my backup from now on. This drive isn't bad, but it is my first one to fail, and I own quite a lot. The speed were comparable to my other 3.0 drives. I know drives fail, but with the small amount of use that this drive has on it, the failure was unexpected.

title: Good, But I'll Stick with another brand for my main computer
text: It is a great relatively cheap SSD Made in Taiwan. It functions as it should and I haven't had a problem with it yet. The product registration for this product, and all SP products, is sketchy to say the least. They don't ask for a serial number or anything just the product type. I was worried about what I was actually getting after I looked at some of the reviews, so when I got the product I did some lets call it "investigating". Mine came with a sandforce controller but not the 8 Channel SF-2281, but rather the 4 channel SF-2241, which will be slower. It also came with part number 29F16B08MCME2 nand similar to that found on the msata intel 525 64GB. I will be uploading a few picture along side of my review. As for now it works for what I intended it for (windows 10 preview/ Ubuntu). If I have any problems I will update my review.

title: Great universal charger
text:
As for all items made by Nitecore this charger is made in china. That being said I find their products to be high quality and well constructed. This charger is no exception. The charger is a great improvement from my Nitecore I4 as I can now select charging current when charging only one AAA or low mah battery. When I say selectable I mean from 300 ma to 750 ma. This is as far as the current adjustment goes, which is fine for most needs. The current does not stay fixed at those currents as the battery charges, but it will not apply more than the selected current during the charge cycle. It will not tell the capacity of the battery like many other chargers I have seen and owned. This charger purely charges and does not discharge so if your looking for one that does look elsewhere. La Crosse makes a nice one for NiMH and NiCad. The feature to turn the screen off during charging is nice, and was one of my biggest complaints with the I4. I use it to charge every thing from AAA to 26550 batteries. When charging the larger batteries an issue arises with how many can actually fit, and when I charge 26650 batteries that is only 2.
It is a great universal charger, and with the added Li-FePO4 charging cycle it makes it an easy choice for people that need a good solid charger that works for almost everything.
If you have any more questions feel free to ask in the comments, I will try to get back within the next few days.

title: Good Basic Speakers
text: For the price of the speaker these work well. They are made in china as expected, but still feel well made. These are simple only three wires power, 3.5mm , and the wire joining the two speakers. They are simple to operate with only a volume level control, and are great for the YouTube watcher or some moderate level music. You won't get the same bass out of these as you would with a 2.1 channel sound system, but that is expected. I like Logitech speakers because in my experience they tend to stand behind their product. I had another set of speakers from them that went bad, and after a few questions they sent me a new unit without requiring an RMA for the old ones. Overall if you need a set of basic speakers these are great and reasonably priced.

title: Tracking one small step...starts with knowing what you want.
text:
I bought my Fitbit One after a considerable amount of research among the various "life activity trackers" on the market. As I read, my focus shifted from the features of the products themselves to the personal goals I intended to accomplish once I started moving around. Ultimately, this helped me make my final purchase.

As you may have found, I discovered that despite the choices available to the consumer, I did not find a particular fitness tracker that measured all daily activities equally well. Design philosophies and marketing strategies seem to conspire to confuse the subject further and make it difficult to match a particular product to your needs. However, many excellent reviews have been published by Amazon-reviewers as well as by online product-review writers which were very helpful.

In any event, I was looking for a decent pedometer and sleep monitor. I can't run anymore due to arthritis, but I do enjoy walking and was pretty sure that I am not moving around enough. I also suspected that sleep apnea was starting creep up on me and hoped that the sleep tracking function could share some insight into my sleep patterns. I do some biking and other exercises, but I wasn't all that concerned about accurately tracking those activities through the Fitbit. Other electronic gizmos cover those areas.

The Fitbit appealed to me because it is tiny and can be carried discretely. Pedometers tend to work fine, but can be bulky and clunky-looking. The Bluetooth syncing was also a big selling point allowing data entry to be very simple, although for some the data analysis may be too simple. As of this writing, the Moto Droid just became Bluetooth 4.0 compatible with Fitbit products. According to the website more smartphones and tablets are being added on the Android platform. The package came with a small pocket clip, an armband for sleep tracking, and a charger.

Since I picked this product up, from RadioShack incidentally, I have been very happy with it. The pedometer function is very accurate and works equally well at measuring flights of stairs, which is a very nice feature. The small size is great for pocket carry, particularly in the change pocket of a pair of jeans, and can be clipped to pants or shirts depending on your preference. I compared the Fitbit's ability to monitor sleep patterns with a sleep monitoring app on my Droid. Gross measures of restlessness were comparable for each and it seems that I sleep better than I thought.

I've worn this unit during other activities, but the accuracy of movement that it measures is questionable. The Fitbit One, at least, is probably best suited for walking. Nonetheless, with consistent wearing, overall activity can probably be deduced, but will have to be inferred from data recorded as "steps".

In sum, the Fitbit One seems to be the closest match to an activity-meter that meets my personal needs. That means measuring natural everyday movement, such as steps, stairs, and sleep, in a tiny sleek wireless package. It helps raise my awareness of non-structured daily activity and is an important tool for overall health.

title: Big sound small package
text:
I needed a speaker for the kitchen because my wife insisted on playing music off of the laptop. While I am no audiophile, this drove me crazy. I also wanted some type of wireless system in order to optimize speaker placement without the hassle of running wires. I felt that bluetooth speakers would be more convenient than Airplay speakers, because finding IP addresses for speakers doesn't add to my listening enjoyment.

This speaker has a small footprint and is easy to pair with a bluetooth capable device. The sound is very good and fills the room. I tend to keep the speaker volume a bit short of maximum capacity because it will develop a "buzziness" if set too high. This solution is a far cry from laptop speakers and would probably sound spectacular if paired with multiple compatible speakers and a subwoofer. I have noticed we now play more music in general because of the ZiiSound.

Two caveats may be noted. First, pairing devices intially is easy, but I have found that when switching among devices, such as our iPhones, the speaker may have trouble picking up the second device. This happens more often after the speaker goes to "sleep" and sometimes necessitates restarting the bluetooth on the phone or hitting the power button on the speaker.

Second, I have found moving the speaker above arm's reach can be a hassle. Due to the somewhat regular need to hit the "connect" or power button on the unit I found that mounting the speaker lower is far more convenient. Mounting brackets are not an option for this unit, but a small shelf is more than adequate.

Despite these small concerns I am very happy with the sound and ease of use of the ZiiSound. The expandability of this system also suggests intriguing ways to enhance the sound of the room at a fairly reasonable cost.
