We recently purchased a new tablet and ordered protector.
This pack did not bring the usual stickers and cleaning wipes to help make installing a bit easier. I had to toss out the first one I tried to put on because it was just horrible lol
Other than that, it was good. I just enjoy the easy install kit it usually comes with.

title: Parent Approved
text: Our little one loves this case. Great for little hands! Love that the clips came with it.

title: Nice headphones
text: Great value.  5th grader loves them.

title: Works great!
text: Works great!  Needed to replace the screen to screen A/V cord on our portable car DVD player.  Saved me from buying a new DVD player.  Shipped fast.

title: Great quality, great value.
text: Perfect for connecting Kindle Fire HD 7" to big screen HD TV.  Not we can watch streaming easily in hotel rooms or anywhere where we want.  Kids can watch each other play video games on Kindle.

title: Basic and comfortable
text:
This is a very basic headset, I am using it as my backup for my fancier (more expensive headset) and so far, I think it works well.

The sound is good enough for conference calls, a bit tinny sounding with music.

It does a pretty good job with noise cancellation and it folds up small enough to fit into my overpacked carry-on bag.

title: So tough and sturdy
text:
We used this in our garage and I had to run the dolly over it with several heavy items, including a solid oak book shelf.

So far it is really holding up and I have no doubts that a motorcycle or tool chest would be fine as well.

It is a bit high profile than the rubberized kind I am used to at work and it does move around if you don't secure it to the ground.

title: Easy to use
text:
Zero setup and easy to use.

This USB charger is perfect and I know it will really come in handy on trips. Even with the cord it fits easily into my carry-on bag and so far it is working as intended.

If I had any complaints it is that I sorta wish it was more brightly colored, my carry-on bag is lined in black, practically all my computer equipment is black so this item tends to get lost.

title: Excellent Christmas Computer!
text:
This computer worked right away with no driver issues at all.

The set up came with a helpful physical note that let me know that I had to create a local account and finish setup before I could add my microsoft account.

Here are some other thoughts about this computer, in no particular order;

So far, there has been no overheating and zero noise. My old laptop sorta sounded like a distant plane getting ready for takeoff, so this is a novelty to me.

I am using it as my main computer, I mostly surf around online, look up recipes, check the weather every 20 mins (I need to stop) and watch a few youtubes to get the full benefit of paying for that adsfree youtube that my son deemed 'essential.'

I'm also using this to play minecraft in an infinite world. My old computer had so much lagginess that sometimes I had time to reheat a cup of coffee before it was finished filling out the landscape and adding in all the creatures. I didn't like it, but any minecraft is worth the wait, but this is now so so fast. No waiting, no screen juddering, it's perfect.

I am using chrome with a bunch of plugins and this is still totally fine.

This doesn't have a built in speaker or microphone.

The item itself is very lightweight and small, it fits on my tiny desk under my monitor without one of those monitor shelf tray thingies.

It comes with a VESA bracket so you could attach it to the back of a VESA monitor or TV.

Windows 11 pro was preinstalled and only took a couple of hours on my slow home internet connection to get up to date.

This boots up very fast, no lagging or delays in chrome or minecraft.

It arrives in a smart box that is a perfect cube for wrapping as a present or just putting a nice fancy bow on top.

All in all, I am super happy with this.

title: Works as intended
text:
I am not using this for tech work, just for a placeholder in gaming and so far, it works as intended and I was able to leave my computer for some necessary things I was working on across the room.

The set up is simple and honestly, if I can manage it, anyone can, I once spent an hour setting up a VCR (yep, I'm old and read old people manuals).

Anyways, I don't know that this will work for your needs, but it worked for me.

title: Easy Set Up
text:
This is your standard plug n' play setup, I don't have much more to say about this because it is as easy to use as a plug in pencil sharpener, once its on, you are good to go.

Seagate is a reliable brand and I have never gotten a dud from them and this backup is more of the same.

I get this kind of external drive every two years, each time with a little more storage space for work documents and product and every time they have been proven reliable, easy to use and worth the money.

title: Nice hub
text:
I am using this with an HP XPS 15 9510 with Windows 10 22H2 19045.2251
I am not using and have not tested all the ports. I am using and can verify is working well:
a) USB ports (mouse, keyboard, HD Pro WebCam c920)
b) the usb-c power-pass-through port (factory power supply)
c) the two HDMI ports
The device is sturdy and the connections through the ports are solid.

title: Too small for my  laptop and smallish keyboard
text:
It is so hard to find a good laptop bag that fits a laptop AND a keyboard.

This one, boring as hell looking, seemed like it would work and while I didn't relish the thought of carrying this lump of canvas around, I did like the thought of my precious electronics making it through trips safely.

But, alas, my search for a safe bag continues.

This bag does have a lot of pockets and zippers. All the zippers zip and all the pockets function as a pocket should.

The handles on top were securely sewed on and the bottom of the bag was likely to be water resistant, in case you set this down on a rain wet spot.

title: Works Great
text:
I am using this with an HP XPS 15 9510 with Windows 10 22H2 19045.2251
I am not using and have not tested all the ports. I am using and can verify this is working well:
a) USB ports (mouse, keyboard, HD Pro WebCam c920)
b) the usb-c power-pass-through port (factory power supply)
c) the two HDMI ports
The device is sturdy and the connections through the ports are solid.

title: A must for a home office
text:
I remember when home offices were a home computer balanced on an unused sewing table in a spare bedroom.

Now with video conferencing you have to reach a much higher level of office'ness. My office space was dark and hazy looking without this light. The area behind my desk is a window so I thought that meant my space would look lightfilled and cheery, I was so wrong.

Also, I often work at night and to keep my space from looking like a hostage video this lamp changes that.

Installation - was less than five minutes.

Remote Control _ As long as you directly press it it is fantastic.

Redness Control = I have a lot of facial flushing and this light can be set at different colors to counteract that.

Lightweigh, easily moveable endlessly changeable (there are a lot of different color combinations

This is a great light for a home office.

title: Easy to use and frees up space on my desk
text:
This clamp is so quick to install that I had it done before my coffee was done brewing, there was some kind of a grip strip adhesive that came with the mount, but I couldnt find it in the packaging and as it turned out, I didn't need it

The mount is very sturdy and doesn't move, at all, with a large laptop tray that would fit even bigger sized laptops with a little space leftover.

It is super easy to adjust and easy to swing out, you can clamp this mount on the edge or drill a hole through your desk or table top, I chose the clamp only option.

I was hoping this would save me some room on my workspace and it has.

The only downside is that I didn't use the monitor mount because none of my monitors were VESA so I couldn't use that yet, but just the laptop arm tray is enough to free up space for my two other monitors, keyboard, mouse pad, etc.

Also, and this is the last thing I have to say about this, is that it has five points of articulation, so you can position your laptop exactly where you want it.

title: Easy to adjust laptop stand
text:
Easy to use laptop stand. So easy I didn't even have to use the directions to put it together and immediately set it up on my kitchen counter.

This is not a lighweight stand, it is sturdy and a bit on the weighty side so if you planning on packing it with your laptop for a trip, might want to cut down on other items you are packing to make up for the extra weight.

So far, my laptop hasn't slid off of the seat nor has it overheated, there is a hole for heat to escape and the bottom foot part has stayed pretty steady during my vigorous stabby way of typing.

Nice stand and I wouldn't mind getting another for my ipad.

title: Excellent high powered router
text:
The manual was clear and easy to follow and I didn't use the advanced mesh features.

I moved to a much bigger house, so I needed a more powerful router to be able to have strong wifi signal throughout the house.

I connected it to my ISP and had internet immediately.

one nice feature are the status lights, .no more second guessing why I'm not getting a signal.

title: Basic laptop safe keeping
text:
This is a nice big sleeve that fits my 15 inch DELL XPS with room to spare, its a little on the big size.

Some other details you should know about this laptop cover;

good sturdy zipper

decent amount of firm foam to protect your computer

it feels safe having my laptop in this foam sleeve rather than having it in my bag alone.

title: Nice headphones
text:
Worked for my android phone which makes me happy. The sound quality is about the same as regular headhphones when I used a headphone jack.

Nice to not have to charge these headphones and the cord is long enough.

You don't need an adapter for these but you need to plug it into the USB C port.

Installation: Plug in and use.

Packaging could be smaller and more recyclable.

title: Very good laptop stand
text:
This is a pretty good stand and I really like adjustable it is.

Also, it matches with the modern decor of my desk and it is slightly larger than the laptop stand I used for the last couple of years which makes me feel that this stand is sturdier and less likely to tip over.

There is an included allan wrench and if you are clever you will tape it to the underside so that you don't need to spend time guessing which one of the many wrenches you've collected over the years is the correct one for adjusting this stand.

title: Wonderful in ear headphones
text:
First off, these are almost cat proof! My cat is the main reason I have been buying so many pairs of these in ear headphones, she loves the cords. Somehow, she alwasy manages to get to them no matter if I have placed them in a drawer or left them, for just a second, on the bathroom counter, she pounces on them and bites clear through the cord and then wanders off, her job done, the vile headphone critters are dead.

But she wasn't able to bite through these! Oh happy day! I did a dance of joy when I saw her try and fail.

Now on to other non-cat centric reasons that I love these headphones, in no particular order of importance;

Great sound. Some of my headphones have been a bit tinny, I listen to a lot of audiobooks and news so it was unhealthy to have to keep the sound so high in order to understand it.

The stiffness of cord doesn't lend itself to tangling. It has the tension of florist wire instead of floss and somehow I haven't had the great irritation of needing to untangle it once. I didn't realize what a normal part of owning corded headphones it was until I stopped needing to untangle them every five minutes. What'll I do with all this free time?

They aren't black. I keep getting black headphones and they disappear against the black lining of my bag, on the black speckled counter, on dark tables. My eyesight isn't great and I kept losing things, but these are light enough that I can find them easily.

Now, for my one complaint. The button for pausing is so so tiny and it doesn't have a lot of clickiness so its a little hard to know if you have engaged pause or not so I end up pushing pause twice and then it unpauses. But, I'll get used to it eventually.

title: Excellent adjustable-ness
text:
There is a lift button to adjust the height. This is in addition to clicking to adjust the angle from the base which is a bit better than the other laptop stand I have, because it doesn't require tools to make adjustments.

The support rod on this stand extends up or down with an easy squeeze button which is nice for a standing desk and it has a non skid surface on bottom of the laptop stand, so no unplanned movements.

This stand is so easy to adjust with the three buttons, button one is the support rod to adjust base angle, button two is the support rod to panel angle adjustment, button three is the support rod extension that raises and lowers the laptop. You can't set any of these three to an exact level like you can with the laptop stand that requires an allen wrench to make adjustments, but there are multiple set notches, enough to satisfy even the most discerning laptop user and so far, I haven't felt that it wasn't perfect as is.

Also, this is very light, yet sturdy.

The set up on it is very fast, would be perfect for travel as it could easily fold up for a laptop bag carryon thingie.

Other, cheaper models are more modifiable, so that once you have it set with your allen wrench you probably wouldn't want to move it as you'd mess up your settings. But for me this one is so easy and nice that I don't miss the other kind of stand.

This stand has a venting hole that lines up with the Dell XPS15 9510 vent so it wont overheat, however the lip at the front that holds the laptop from sliding off, is just thick enough for a laptop so I couldn't recommend using a cooling pad underneath.

title: Excellent, quality piece that has been super useful
text:
The unique low profile shape means it can plug into anything, even recessed USB ports.

It is sturdy and light and formatted exFAT.

It specifies that it is waterproof, I have no way of knowing because I don't want to risk it by dropping it in water.

There is no bloatware, it just came empty and clean formatted.

I used it for transferring files to a new computer for an OS install and network drivers.

title: Useful and colorful taptop bag
text:
This laptop bag turned out exactly as pictured online. I really love the blues and golds.

It is the perfect size for carrying a laptop. I had a bag like this before and the zipper was wonky, so this bag replaces that one. Someting else to know is that unlike the broken zipper bag I used to carry around, this zipper seems a lot more solid. The old bag's zipper seemed a bit rusty from day one.

So because of the rusty zipper situation I was only able to use it for a few months. I think this bag could last for a couple of years.

title: Great sound, easy set up
text:
This soundbar is great and a huge upgrade from the one we had before. It balances left and right audio unlike some bars where left or right is louder, it has a crisp clear sound, we can understand voices and music without distortion and we don't have to turn it up loud.

It looks really good on our entertainment console because it is so low and small and it fit perfectly in our tv cabinet shelf.

We live in an apartment and we wanted to be considerate of our neighbors but it needed to be clear enough that my husband who has hearing loss could understand everything that was said without blasting the volume.

Something I really love is that it has a remote that controlls everything. Our old soundbar made this extremely loud and annoying 'K'Bonnng!' sound everytime it turned itself off, which happened every time you stepped away. I'm sure our neighbors loved it.

This remote lets you choose between inputs and you can even enable and connect the bluetooth and then use the remote buttons like you would use bluetooth control buttons to play, pause, etc.

Last but not least, you know how sometimes you are watching something and it gets really, really loud because you had to turn the sound up to hear the talking bit before, this soundbar minimizes that effect.

title: The pictures make this look big
text:
In the pictures ofr this camera it gives the appearance of being the size of an outside security camera, but in actuality this is a snack sized snickers bar.

My last camera started to have darker and darker images. I had to get a light or risk having weird zoom meetings. This camera is bright and it doesn't matter how much natural light is available.

The startup is simple and it was easy to use a bit of double sided tape to affix this to the top edge of my monitor.

All in all a nice camera.

title: Very bright and easy to use
text:
My only complaitn is that there is no way to dim this light, it is either full headlights in your face or blackest night, there is no inbetween. But other than that, this light is great.

1. Easy to set up and easy to attach to the top of your monitor. It comes with a standard tripod mount but instead I used a small amount of double sided tape.

2. The light has it's own battery and a standard usb charging cable. It doesn't need to be plugged in to work and it arrived charged and I try to plug it in overnight, so far it hasn't run out of charge on me.

title: Wow, I just blasted myself with sound!
text:
I didn't realize how bad my old set of earbuds had gotten until I tried listening to an audiobook with this new pair and just about had a heart attack. So loud! So clear! Like a foghorn in my head!

Anyways, once I adjusted the sound down, they are perfection. I am listening to a book with a new (to me) narrator and her accent (very British) was difficult to decipher before. Probably because there was a tiny bit of background static with my old earbuds, but now I can hear and understand everything.

Some other things I like;

Sturdiness, the cords seem a little thicker and they seem less likely to tangle the way my old set was wont to do.

Magnets on the backs of the earbuds. These are super cool and I really like that they keep the earbuds from tangling and they are easier to find by touch when I am using them at night in bed with the lights out.

A pause button that is clearly delineated from the sound buttons. This is just all around a tiny bit bigger than my old set and it is super useful and easier to pause and restart.

Great set of earbuds, if I can keep my cat from chewing on the cord, I could easily end up using these for a long time.

title: Works great
text:
This cable is working great. Now we can play games on our big screen tv in the living room.

This has been so much more fun than playing seperately especially for games like Mass Effect, Little Nightmares and KOTOR.

So far, everything is working perfectly and the set up is faster than what we were trying the last time we decided to play, all together, from our comfy living room easy chairs.

The 6 feet of cable isn't as useful as I thought it would be because things are set up right there at the TV cabinet and there are no cables snaking across the floor to trip up the unwary.

All in all, a great cable.

title: No driver needed
text:
This doesn't need a driver it is USB powered and HDMI.

The Thinrelain portable monitor is fitted with a black, leather looking folio, the folio is easily removed. Once it is detached, four VESA mount points are visible on the back of the monitor. These mount points could be used to attach the portable monitor to a wall or a laptop extender/stand.

Video Quality - Average. This isn't a laptop and the screen was noticeably darker than my computer. Not enough to put a person off from using it.

Installation - Virtually none. All you need is to plug in the power and then use the cable to connect the Thinlerain to your laptop. The cable is about three feet long.

This device is perfect for zoom meetings, you can have an agenda or spreadsheet and talk at a meeting while referring to it. Very useful.

title: This is an excellent camera and it produces a clear image even in low light
text:
It had been several years since I bought a little ball shaped webcam and this new camera just blows that one away. I am in awe of how much progress webcams have made in the last few years.

Clearer pictures. Wider view. The background isn't blurry. My husband was able to get rid of cheapy (but super useful) greenscreen that we used when making video calls with friends and family.

The camera comes with all you need to affix it to the top of your computer and it stays put! I can't stress this bit enough, no more falling webcams so that all and sundry is made aware of your threadbare shorts and the cat in the lap.

Last but not least, this camera will not cost you a week's salary. It really is affordable and I wish I'd realized that a few years ago.

title: Sturdy and useful
text:
Its a good strong magnet and it wont fall off.

The adhesive metal circle is staying on the back of the phone and it looks so non descript, I hardly noticed it.

Very space age in that it doesn't actually attach to your computer, it is just the magnets

I just had it ion my lap not on a table and the phone stayed secure even when touching the screen. It came with a second phone plate and glue strip which I guess is for in case if the device was lost and you need more to use on your computer. So you have a spare, can't argue with that the convenience of that.

title: excellent device for a crowded electronics space
text:
First off, my husband and I share a home workspace and between us we have four computers, two phones and various other devices and this tower is really helping to organize the space and keeping our cat from crawling into the spaghettie'd mess of corns and cables.

But, there's more! It looks the Tardis, Dr. Who's time ship and that is an unexpected bonus that I didn't realize I really wanted.

There are so many open spots that we we aren't even using all of them, it is that space concious that we got rid of other two strips.

Excellent and a must have for today's modern at home office workers.

title: These are metal not plastic
text:
I don't know why I thought they were made of plastic. It's right there in the product description. Anyways, these are so sturdy I think I could use one as a stepstool and it would look pretty much the same afterwards.

They are super usefule for our home office space. We don't have a separate home office, just a space in our bedroom where we (my hubby and I) are sharing a kitchen table as a desk and trying to get some work done, it mostly works, but he has multiple screens and some other stuff and he needed some extra space, these monitor risers are just the thing!

Our workspace is so much better now, I love it! He has enough room for his computer, keyboard, phone stand, headphone hook and a pad of paper.

Our cat was super curious, she always is, but it is like these risers came coated in catnip, she wouldn't leave them alone, so if you have a cat, beware.

The color of the risers is so boring they just fade away, I kinda like that in a desk product. Anyway, these risers are just the right size and have really added to our shared work space.

title: Works Great
text:
I think we might have given our second remote away when I got rid of some things at the Goodwill. So we have been making do with just one remote. Last week we couldn't even find that (it was under the tv cabinet, covered in cat hairballs).

So it was clear that we needed a backup but these things are so changeable, they don't have universal remotes anymore (at least I don't think they do) and I was concerned that we would be getting the wrong one.

But this remote works fine. It is perfect and the set up was nothing. It take batteries that we already had and if it didn't have a VUDU button I wouldn't be able to tell the difference between it ad our new remote.

title: Great length charging cable.
text:
This USB charging cable worked well to charge my phone, headphone and my external battery. I was thinking 3.3 feet might be too long and sort of annoying to deal with, but I tuck the excess length into the top drawer of my nightstand so that my cat wont eat it (she LOVES charging cables).

Note: there is no data connection.

The cable arrived in a special box, that is a little bit gift-y, if you were thinking of gifting this eminently practical item.

It is quality construction and is a little thicker and stiffer than other charging cables, if that matters to you.

Nice cable.

title: These are really nice
text:
I've had a lot of pairs of earbuds over the years, I prefer them to headphones.

This pair is really nice. The cord seems less inclined to tange and the size of the rubber bug thingamajigs is just right for me.

My last pair of earbuds went through the washing machine, I forgot them in the pocket of my apron. They came out working, well, one side did the other was silent and I ended up wearing them for a few more weeks. So having sound on both sides of my head was wonderful and I'm trying to be objective but Lizzo sounds much better if you can hear her from both ears!

Anyways, these earbuds work, they wind up well and don't seem to tangle as easily as my old pair.

title: Easy to use, plug and play set up
text:
My son used this to stream himself playing video games online.

Before he would stream directly from his computer and his computer would slow down and get hot. It was nice because the streaming was done from a different computer than the computer he was playing on so it didn't slow down his playing the game, never got overheated and it looked pretty professional.

It was easy for him to setup, just plug and play, so I can't say anything about tech support, because it was so easy to use and we didn't need any help to get it started.

He hasn't streamed in awhile, but if he does it again he will use this hardware again.

title: Works great if you tighten it down
text:
Im using this for my kitchen ipad, it's an older model and I like to watch videos or look at recipes while I'm working.

Here are the best features of this tablet stand, in no particular order;

1. waterproof - since this is on the kitchen counter it is good that it doesn't hurt if a little water ends up on the feet.

2. Adjustable - I had my ipad in this and set up just like the picture but it seemed a bit wobbly and top heavy, I mean is still worked but I was worried that one slight nudge and my ipad AND the tablet stand would fall over, probably into a sink full of dirty dishes. So we flipped it, to create a standard 'S' shape, with the feet acting as a weighted counterbalance on the opposite side of the ipad. Now it is much more stable.

3. Not much set up, not sure what else to say, it's pretty easy to put it to use.

4. I had this flimsy little suede covered cardboard folding deal that I got for the ipad and it would always slide away and the faux suede started to separate from the darn cardboard within a month! This is much more durable. I could see this lasting for a few years.

5. Wall mounting. Well, I really really wanted to do this but it looks like I'd have to make a lot of holes and I rent and so I just couldn't do it, le sigh. But I think it would be extra double convenient if I could mount it on the wall and keep it off my small counter. Maybe someday I will own a home and can make as many holes in the walls as I want!

6. Height - this is adjustable, it has a way to tighten it down which minimizes wobblyness so you can have this set up with the tablet or ipad or whatever warms your heat is at a little closer to eye level without worrying that the entire production will crash.

Very useful and highly recommended.

title: I'd buy this again
text:
It worked to run my keyboard, mouse and monitor from my iIT closet to my office, which is on the other side of the building. The extender works just like I was in front of it working.

I was able to bounce the KVM and debug boot messages which is just as advetised and I would definitely buy it again.

The Set Up - - plug and play, no configuration required.
Negatives - - Itt would be nice if there was some sort of remote access feature but all of th e extenders with that feature that I've found have been crazy expensive remote products like RDP or VNC. This is affordable.

title: This is perfect for a tablet
text:
My husband was using an empty box with a small folding phone stand for his tablet and this is a great upgrade.

It has a flexible adjustable angle shelf thingamabobble so that you can tilt this as much or as little as you want.

In his case, he has it just barely angled backwards set up next to his computer and so far, it is working out even better than we'd hoped.

What I like;

Easy set up
Sturdy, you don't have to worry about your tablet or phone falling over
looks professional (much better than a pile of books or boxes)
Small, so it doesn't take up much space on a crowded desk

What I don't like:

Nothing, I love it!

title: Great upgrade for your life
text:
With the number of things these headphones can do, it almost seems like you could ask them to make you a sandwich and the response would be, 'do you want tomatoes, yes or no?'

They do not pinch my head nor do they slide off if I happen to be walking around while wearing them.  They aren't as hot and thus sweaty as my old wireless set.  

The noise cancellation is almost too good.  I didn't hear the bus arriving or a car honking at me when I was waiting to cross the street.  Even with the sound turned down low I could still hear it while standing next to a busy street.
It worked using the alexa voice commands and making a phone call was easy and worked just fine and the sound was good.  Even without a boom it had a good mic and people understood everything I said without distortion.
The only thing I didn't like is that they cup the ear and press on underside of my ear at the eustachean tube (not a doctor) and it was a bit irritating after a while.  

I wish they were a different color, brown is just the ugliest color and I don't know why everything this year is some vile shade of mud.

title: This is so modern!
text:
I need to take notes in meetings.
I used to take a laptop into meetings, but presenters would think I was ignoring them, or the clacking of my keyboard would distract people. Other people would ask to look things up or present from my laptop.
I tried a tablet with a pen but it felt unnatural and the inaccuracy impeded my speed or being able to coalesce the notes later on.
I then would use a regular notebook and paper, and then attempt to type out my notes when I got back to my desk, but would inevitably forget the notes or misplace them in my office before I would get a chance to transcribe.
Enter LiveScribe.
Everything I write down, goes into my LiveScribe app on my phone. That's it, nothing else I need to do.
I can write notes and draw diagrams and even make recordings and send them to other meeting participants.
I can see all my notes on my phone in the app or from anywhere in Google Drive.

LiveScribe is freaking amazing and I really hope this tech keeps innovating and doesn't get dropped, because I've grown used to the convenience of it and don't want to go back to what I did before.

title: Great, basic backpack with an antitheft feature
text:
This is a nice, roomy backpack.

there is plenty of space to carry a laptop or tablet, plus a load of schoolbooks.

Best of all it has very comfortable padded shoulder straps and the weight is nicely spread across the back without any of that pulling sensation that makes a backpack so irksome.

My only complaint is that the lining is so dark! If you lose a pen, you end up having to upend the entire bag to find it. Any light color would fix this, but it seems most backpacks are made this way.

All in all, pretty nice way to carry around some heavy books and computers.

title: Nice basic monitor
text:
Bright picture quality. This has vga and hdmi, but it comes with a vga cable only.

Sadly, the base doesn't tilt. If you are like me, with back pain and leg cramps that propel you from your seat every hour for an uncomfortable bout of standing computing, this monitor will be a trial to use.

But its at a pretty good angle and resolution is great.

This is a good standard monitor, nice specifications for gaming, for example it has a nice refresh, no ghosting. When I played minecraft on it there was no ghosting and when I used it for spreadsheets my numbers didn't blur and swim across the page.

But, like I said before, I wish it tilted or rotated. Nice price for a good basic monitor.

title: Delightful keyboard
text:
This keyboard really adds to the usability of my Google Pixel Slate.

Sure you can use the Slate without a keyboard, but it is really nice with the keyboard and makes it a lot more laptoplike.

I can't prove it, but having the keyboard seemed to add to the battery life of the Slate.

If it's your thing, this keyboard is really clicky, like an older style of keyboard.

title: Excellent Battery life, but usefullness is limited to Chrome
text:
For the positives;

There is a really great battery life to this device, so if you are using it to watch movies, it will last an incredibly long time.

If you are doing everything in Chrome, this is pretty great and super useful.

It works in a very cellphone like way, which is great, but I was hoping to use this to connect to work while traveling and it just wont work for that.

Now for the negatives;

There is a LINUX mode but it is not quite out of development.

The chrome operating system seems kind of abandoned, not updated or supported.

title: If I could give these sunglasses 10 stars I would
text:
Here are just a few of the things I really love about these audio sunglasses, in no particular order;

1. Super easy set up, like it took less then five minutes to get these ready to use.

2. Great sound quality, I worried this could be a redux of the wind up radio I got a few years ago, barely loud enough to understand, certainly not good enough to listen to news on.

3. Classy, understated look that would look good on anyone.

4. They hold a charge for longer than I expected

5. Easy to charge, no pronged ended charging cable, these just have to be pressed against the gold dots on the inside of the sunglass arm, little magnets take hold and voila! you are charging.

6. I can wear these when I have a migraine. I can't use earbugds when I feel that horrible. The pain seems to spike if I touch the inner parts of my ears and down my jawline to add to my agony. But these were great, no pain no nausea, no reason I can't pass the time with a fun book or listen to mosic.

7. The lenses are just dark enough that I can wear them even on the brightest summer day.

8. They came with a nice case that is big enough to hold the charging cable.

9. The bleed out sound when I am using these sunglasses is very minimal. I'm not botheirng anyone AND I can still hear what is going on around me. When I have the sound turned down low the music seems like I'm in a room where someone is playing the stereo, low and I can have a conversation with someone without shouting.

10. I can leave my phone on my desk and head to the kitchen for a snack and I can still hear my playlist.

title: This is a large projector and it creates a really big image
text:
I thought this would be like the smaller projector at work that is used in the conference room and at large presentations at the hotel ballroom, but this is gigantic, like what you would use in a smallish theater to see a movie.

The picture was nice and clear and with the new picture quality of tv and movies, I think this would be a really nice way to watch a movie.

It has a separate video box, so you don't have to run cables to the projector, which is pretty nice. It's a got a great refresh rate and I never saw any flicker.

The automatic lens cover worked flawlessly.

It could use a cover, something to protect it when not in use. It is large and heavy, you couldn't just hang this from ceiling tiles, it needs real supports.

title: My cat pic collection is saved
text:
I am using this for backups, my collection of cat pictures has really gotten away from me. So the only choice, other than deleting thousands of adorable fluffy pictures is to save them on this Seagate Backup plus.

I didn't use the included software, I don't think it is any better than the built in Windows software.

Easy to use and fast.

title: Clever
text:
Very minimalist style. Plus it works!

You can't tell from the image, but this is actually really solid and heavy. Like a paperweight, so you don't have to worry about your laptop falling out of it. But be careful of moving it with the laptop, it is a bit ungainly so be sure to move the items separately.

All in all this is super useful for watching tutorials.

title: Great Harddrive
text:
I put in the enclosure and it is the fastest usb drive I've ever had.

Installation; there was no real installation, it works like all other usb drives. Used it to transfer large files between two secure locations and it worked great. There was no delay in writing to or reading from it.

Significant improvement in speed over USB 3.0.

It's a harddrive and it is awesome.

title: Great headset
text:
These headphones are the most comfortable I have ever owned. The ear cups sit flat against the ear, which feels more natural than the usual headphone with ear cups that surround your ear with a hot and sweaty dome. I could only handle that style for a while and then my ears needed a cool off to dry out. If you are using these headphones somewhere loud, like a train stop, the environment noises will interfere a bit, same if you turn the volume up bystanders will hear it. But the lack of hot and sweaty ears is such a bonus so these other problems are easily avoided.

The headphones are instantly compatible with all smartphones with a headphone jack. I used it on a Google Pixel and on iPhone 5's the sound quality was crystal clear, much better than any bluetooth headset I've ever had, and I've had plenty.

The USB adapter with the call controls worked great for my business calls GoToMeeting, Skype for Business and Google Voice.

The cord is three feet long, perfect for me since I get tired of getting the cord tangled as I pace around during calls, but it might be a bit on the short side for some. For use with the computer the USB adds two feet between the USB port and the controlling buttons. The cord is round, and so far, has been resistant to kinks.

The volume and mute buttons are on the cord instead of the headset, I like this because I don't have to memorize the placement during a call and the indicator light for mute keeps me from forgetting that I have muted a call and no one can hear me because I muted to sneeze, cough or shush my cat.

The only drawback is that unlike with a bluetooth headset there are no volume or mute controls as part of the headset or cord when it is plugged into a smart phone.

title: Great Laptop
text:
You can rum pretty much any game on the ultra graphics and range settings, for example I wasn't able to play Overwatch on my old computer, no matter how low I set the graphics and everything else on it, it played terribly on my old computer.

Now I am playing Overwatch all the time. Same with Fallout 4, it plays beautifully, same with World of Warcraft and Skyrim.

It heats up, so be sure to buy a cooling pad or fan. This is what I have done to stop the overheating; I am using a cooling pad that plugs into the computer and it has a little fan. They cost about $25 so not a big expense.

The laptop has a basic keyboard and touchpad, so I have a better keyboard and a mouse hooked up for gameplay. But other than this, the laptop is ready to go and easy to use. The best laptop I've ever had.

title: Better than I'd hoped.
text:
Update 30 June 2018 - This computer is one year old and today it turned off. For no reason at all the screen went black and it just will not turn back on. I don't know if its the power supply or the computer. So bummed out!
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
I love this computer. I was a bit worried about the touchscreen aspect. Everyone has experience the peculiar frustration of an insensitive touchscreen and after a time, they all seem to dull a bit. But this is perfection from the very beginning.

The large size of the screen has made reading comics truly a delight.

Setting up was super fast and before lunch, I was computering away like mad.

The other concern I had, besides the touchscreen, was the balance of the machine, it rests on a smallish foot and I have been known to bump into my desk with my chair, to lose my balance and fall into my desk too. I am just a bit unsteady on my feet and I was picturing myself knocking this wonderful device onto my very hard tile floor.

So far, it has not wobbled a bit. The entire thing is a bit heavier than I thought it would be and it has been extraordinarily steady.

As for computing power, it has been a lot less buggy for playing minecraft and hearthstone. Same with some of the other games I like to play. I can't say it is as powerful as a real gaming computer, but I'm not trying to run Overwatch on this machine so it is working out fine for me.

All in all a superb computer.

title: Nice
text:
Where have you been all my life?

I simply love these tiny headphones. I was worried that the strap going around the neck would get sweaty or just feel super weird. But I hardly noticed it after a few minutes.

title: Very useful.
text:
We have bought several of these portable hardrives for work and they are always worth the money.

Installation: Not much, it's an external harddrive so its good to go right out of the box.

Usefulness: Do you like to save stuff? Great, then you will love this hard drive!

Size: It fits easily into a laptop bag and it doesn't weigh much so it's perfect to lug around

All in all this is a great product.

title: Nice monitor.
text:
We used it to replace an old crt television in our bedroom. We don't watch a lot of tv in our room. I just don't find the bed comfy for show watching.

So not only has it freed up a ton of room on top of my dresser, the picture is about a million times better.

I didn't realize how fuzzy it had gotten, then again, the tv was about nine years old.

Installation: It is plug and play, no installation needed.

Easy to use and the screen space is about the same as our old television.

title: Highly useful
text:
I am using this for the bluetooth headset with my Windows 10 Computer.

It gave me better reception than what I had with my old dongle. It works exactly as I thought it would, the driver was built into windows 10.

I was able to walk to another room in my house (same floor) and still had clear sound. I am using this for a work IP phone and so far it has been perfect.

I got out of range when I went outside to check the mail. Then I had to turn the headset off then on again to get it to re-pair.

I would buy this again and would recommend it for anyone.

title: Great, useful product.
text:
I'm using this to connect my computer to external hardrives.

So far it is working exactly as I'd hoped and the piece is solidly constructed. There is no setup for this item, it is just a plug and play device.

I can't think of any piece that is comparable except for my old usb adapter, obviously it didn't let me use the higher register speed, it did seem like when I was talking to multiple hardrives it would choke, but this Startech Hub keeps everything at the same speed, no interruptions at all.

I would definitely buy this item again if I needed another one.

title: Excellent
text:
First off, because it wasn't entirely clear in the product description, this is for a car audio system, not a computer office system. So if you were hoping to hook this up in your home, you are out of luck.

Second, I don't know a lot about car audio systems. Half the time I'm in the car, I don't listen to anything at all. My usual commute is through several construction zones and I like to have all my attention on the traffic. I'm a nervous driver.

But I do like a nice sound system to listen to audiobooks on. I don't know if there is a comparable brand. But I am super impressed with this product

title: This is great
text:
This is fast. Fast set up. High speed and super reliable, good coverage, no longer getting drowned out by the neighbors coverage.

With the amount of network traffic, we had to reset our old router about once a week. So far, we haven't had to reset even once. We've got screaming fast internet with no interruptions.

title: Worth the money
text:
Our internet comes into our bedroom which is several feet away from where we have our computers. With this Powerline Adapter, we have the router on my desk in the dining room, a lot more central and we didn't have to hook up a cable going halfway across the house to make this happen.

Best of all, it has eliminated some of the annoying deadspots in our house.

The installation took minutes and so far it is working great.

Lovely product

title: Not sure how to rate this.
text:
The drive plugged in and was recognized as a drive with my motherboard and Windows 10.

Unfortunately, I could not set up windows to boot from it, and when I ran Steam games from it, my computer would spontaneously shut down. I gave it to a friend that has a newer motherboard and he says it works great for him. I don't know what motherboard he has but I do know it was manufactured after 2014.

My Motherboard is MSI FM2-A55M-E33 FM2 AMD A55 (Hudson D2) HDMI Micro ATX AMD.

title: Nice product
text:
Good upgrade in visuals. This really will let you clearly see anyone who is lurking, even a cat or small dog.

The set up is simple and the system seems durable.

Good buy for a home or a small office setting.

title: Worth a second look.
text:
This is the nicest camcorder I've ever used. It's pretty lightweight considering all of the great features and it creates a great picture.

The zoom is so crisp I might finally get a video of the racoons fishing in my backyard that is watchable.

My son has been setting up a several lego stop video animations and so far, with this camera the movie is turning out crisper and better than we expected.

the new and upgraded anti shake feature is great for when you are trying to set up a longer shot. I haven't even touched on the more technical specs. For true artists this camcorder has manual control of the balance and white shift. You can manually adjust the zoom and shutter speed, something true professional find absolutely necessary. For us amateurs it offers a rare chance to experiment with home videos.

The sound on this was great and the auto wind correction was perfect because we were outside videoing and the wind didn't seem loud but I knew that another camera would have been overwhelmed by wind noises.

All in all a great camcorder.

title: Nice tassel!
text:
What a stylish and useful product.

The color is a bit more melon than pink, so if you are trying to coordinate this with a handbag, look for something a little less orange.

I've only used it once, but it worked and I got so many compliments, it was pretty strange how much people liked it.

title: Great
text: I use it for a 2010 Mac Mini. I have only used the HDMI port so I do not know if the VGA port works, but I’ve used StarTech.com products before and it appears to be the same high quality.

title: Nice Monitor
text:
This is such a nice screen. For some reason, I thought it would be just a tiny bit smaller than our other monitor, but it really is much bigger.

It makes the screen on my old laptop look positively microscopic.

In every way this monitor is perfect.

Right now, it's hooked up to a brand new Raspberry Pi and the whole family has been enjoying some vintage arcade games; Lode Runner, Super Mario War and Dr. Mario. I suck at all games, but it was pretty cool to see these old games on such a spiffy new screen.

The monitor seems a bit lighter than I'm used to, but other than that, everything seemed pretty standard.

title: Not compatible
text:
Does not work at all. It didn't work with my windows phone nor with my with my samsung galaxy tablet.

I think in the spec's it should clearly state what it would work with. So disappointing. I love the design and was really hoping this would work with my phone and tablet.

title: Usable in a narrow capacity
text:
The good and the bad.

The good is that these work. I plugged them in and walla!, sound.

The bad is the pause button is pretty sporadic. I use these kind of headphones with my ipod to listen to audio books. The pause button is absolutely essential (honestly, having a pause button saves the battery on your ipod, so I guess it's important that way too). But it just didn't work every time, sometimes, even with lifting it up and very deliberately pressing the button one time, it would stick and whatever you are listening to would advance. This isn't super bad if you are listening to music, you just might cut short you favorite jam. But if you are listening to an audio book it will advance to the next chapter of a book, before you have finished listening to it.

This has caused me supreme annoyance, trying to go back and find my spot in an audiobook means you will end up having to listen to something twice because it it is pretty impossible to find where you left off.

So, these were super duper cheap, I use them on my computer now because I don't have to worry about the pause button, I have a mouse and keyboard for that.

Guess you get what you pay for.

title: Small radio
text:
This radio is a lot smaller than I thought it would be. I guess I've watched too many movies, because I was expecting something much larger, more military, like in a movie where a group of soldiers doubletimes it to a an evac point and then uses their radio to call in a chopper.

This radio is tiny by comparison, it's smaller than the freebie Clinique bag I got from Nordstroms. The radio itself is very lightweight too, which I would have already known if I'd taken the time to read the product description.

Also, it's a bit quiet. My husband and I had to strain to hear it, but since it is so lightweight, it wouldn't be much of a problem to carry it close to your ear.

The screen is tiny, but easy to read and once you've turned the radio on, it doesn't crackle and shoosh roaming through stations to find a live one. You have to manually turn it to the station you wish to listen to. The reception was pretty good, we live in a flat area and get a lot of radio stations, but I'd imagine that if you took this hiking, you might have trouble receiving anything, the antenna is a bit short.

The crank seems a little flimsy, I imagine that repeated cranking would cause a stress fracture that would eventually break, rendering the radio mostly useless. We haven't tried charging this with solar power yet, it's been super overcast here, but as soon as we have a sunny, rain free day, I'll give it a go.

Pretty good radio, I don't have any other emergency radios to compare this to, so I don't know if its flimsier than it's competitors.

title: Wellmade and sturdy
text:
I dropped it twice and it didn't break.

I saw in the description for this product that it's ideal for schools and offices, I'm using it for home, we have two kindles, three phones and one table to charge on a pretty regular basis and this charge station is keeping us from having a spaghettied across the counter mess of cables and devices.

While the Charge station is pretty nifty, it comes fully assembled, it's not as lighweight as it looks, much sturdier and drop proof, but it's the industrial sized power source that made the shipping box so heavy. I almost feel ashamed using this fine piece of hardware on our crappy homemade wiring (we didn't do the wiring and I suspect an Electrician didn't either - hence our plethora of fire alarms and two fire extinguishers - never can be too prepared!).

All in all, a nice addition to our house.

title: Nice way to spy on your own house!
text:
Something to know about this is that this has a one way radio. I was a bit surprised that it had a radio at all. Our old camera didn't.

This also has a motion detection feature and because of the radio, it has a sound detection capability. This last bit turns out to be sorta annoying since we live off a busy road and every car or truck, every group of chatting people sets off the camera.

The picture is a lot clearer than we had before and I feel sure that if I set this up in a mouse traffic area (We had a terrifying mouse infestation last year) I'm sure this video is clear enough that we would be able to see the nasty rodents scurrying around on their horrible tiny little feet. Blergh!

All in all, this is a pretty nifty product.

title: I love my iPod
text:
Washing dishes is fun because I listened to the Battle of Hogwarts
I rode my bike up Grant that little bit faster because I was listening to the Hives while riding.
I didn't mind cleaning the toilet because I was just about to find out who was killing everyone in Gretchen McNeil's Ten.
Vacuuming the house went by faster because I created a Clean the House playlist with all my favorite kpop hits.
My root canal was still horrible, but at least I couldn't hear the high horrible drilling noise because I was busy listening to Jesse Eisenberg narrating White Cat.

Loading books is easy and there is enough memory for me to store several audiobooks that I downloaded to it.

Which means as long as I remember to bring it with me, and charge it overnight every once in a while, I will never be bored enough to read a pamphlet on gingivitis at the Dentist's office or waste time trying to remember the name of all of the dwarves in the Hobbit.

title: Everything is awesome!
text:
This standing cover seemed entirely too decadent a product, like buying pre-sliced hot dogs or easterbaskets that are pre-stocked and wrapped, they cost more and seem a little bit lazy to me.

But, then again, I only have one kid, maybe if I had to make up hot dogs and baskets for multiple kids my opinion would be different.

As to the laziness I thought this product represented, I meant that I've been using a rolled up towel to prop up my kindle when I want to read it hands free. I do this pretty often. A hot bowl of spicy chicken soup and a good book is about as close to heaven as I can imagine. My kindle's one touch page advancement feature just makes the reading while eating soup experience that much better.

But this standing cover is fantastic. In fact, I wish it came standard with kindles, most readers I know enjoy eating and reading as much as I do.

The cover is very lightweight and nicely folded when not in use, my son has used it a few times for his kindle, he has the regular kind not the paperwhite and it works for his device too.

There is one downside; I'm a little worried that the cover will be a dirt and grease magnet. My current kindle cover is pretty plain, a lightly textured faux black leather, plain and ugly, but functional since it is easily cleaned with a damp washrag.

title: It pays to read the product description
text:
Once again I was in such a hurry I didn't read the product description fully so I was a bit surprised when I received this in the mail.

Surprised because it was much smaller than I was expecting. Yeah, my bad. Anyways, this is a great product, easy to install, does exactly what it should and is, so far, reliable. I'll update this review in a year.

title: Not as versatile as I'd like, but works okay
text:
Most people are raving about this camera because they are using it with their iPhones.

But if you don't have an iPhone, keep looking, there are other kits that will be more to your liking. Because of my lack of an iPhone (oddly, I just got one two days ago, so I may give this another try and then update the review if I like the camera more) I had to use the included link to the executable Windows program. The program is outdated (like from the days of VCR's and answering machines) and has no documentation.

By documentation, I mean there are minimal instructions and no built in help files. I was able to get it to work by running the software with a lot of finagling and figuring it out by means of hunting around through my past experiences hooking up cameras.

All in all, a bit of a disappointment, I was hoping to catch the wankers who keep spraypainting my carport.

Update - Still using this with the PC, just a note, you have to leave the PC software running to report. This camera works through an extension cord but not a surge protector. Not sure of what the range is and at least in our house, it needed to be on the same circuit breaker as the base, but this could just be weird wiring in our house.

A nice feature of the camera is a motion detection feature, so you don't end up with hours of blank unmoving street view for example. For the recording, pretty much continuously, it takes about 2GB per night (this is with camera on from about 9pm to 8am). There is a way to look at the recorded footage in super fast motion, so it takes about five minutes to watch the entire night's events (use VLC);'oh, hello again, curious kitty who keeps hanging out on my porch.'

This is not an outdoor camera, but we are using it outdoors anyways (tried placing it near a window, but glare of light on the window blinded the camera). I don't have any need to record stuff indoors. Because of the camera we caught a strange creepy person coming up to our house while we were out yesterday, they also visited the houses of two of our neighbors. If not for the camera we wouldn't have known about this. There are a lot of strange characters in our neighborhood and there have been a few incidents; nothing major, a crazy woman tried to break in while we were eating dinner, a man with dementia was wandering around our bridge, kids stealing wood from our woodpile, you know, ordinary disturbances, so this person was exactly what we wanted to see while we weren't home.

The software allows for up to nine cameras to be in use, I can't even imagine that, but it might be cool to have another to watch our backyard, we might be able to catch the raccoons or the river otter who we've only gotten fleeting glimpses of.

title: Happy Update of my previous review!  It works like a dream now.
text:
Update - the kindly people at Snugg sent me a new case, frankly, I wasn't real enthused about it, I figured it would probably still have the design flaws that made it a worthless $20 investment, but I was wrong, wrong, wrong. That will show me to stop being such a pessimist. I couldn't be happier with this now, it is everything I was hoping for, it clips on to the strap of my apron when I'm getting my cooking on, it hooks onto my backpack when I'm out riding. All in all, it is wonderful.

The headphone/earbud thingies I use, pretty standard ones called Coby also the ones that came with my ipod are able to make contact with the bottom portal which is now clear of the protective rubber. The carabiner clip seems slightly more substantial, I'd have to weigh it or take it apart somehow to verify this part.

So here's my old review, use this for info, in case you end up with a flawed Snugg, I guess you should just return it then, or maybe the bugs have been worked out now and all new Snuggs are good. Anyways, here's the old review with a listing of the pertinent problems.

!OLD REVIEW!

The problems Other people have mentioned, mainly the difficulty inserting the nano into the clip case, wasn't really a problem for me. After watching my husband struggle with it for a few minutes I pulled it away from him and decided to do it myself. I was aided in this task by two things, 1) I have more fine motor skills than he does and a lot more experience with tiny detail work (painting, beading, etc) and 2) I have fingernails, real ones not acrylic (I think acrylic nails would be too thick).

I used the thin edge of my fingernail to seat the bottom of the nano in the case after sliding it top first under the rubber part at the top of the clip case.

Once it was in my iPod did appear to be very secure. The carabina clip is a bit of an exaggeration, it isn't nearly as sturdy as a carabiner, the like of which is used by climbers, this is more of a jewelry version and feels very lightweight, I'm not pleased with that.

I paid $8 more for the clip aspect of this case and the clip is there but isn't as functional and sturdy as I'd hoped.

The second fail for this case is that the rubber casing covers part of the headphone port.

I bought this case along with my new iPod, so once I'd unpacked both, I loaded a new audiobook onto my new iPod and slipped the case on and decided to take a listen. Nothing.

I couldn't hear anything at all. It was so disappointing. For a moment I thought that my new iPod was defective. Nope.

It turns out that there wasn't enough room for the headphone jack to make a complete connection unless you peeled back the case wall and held it in place while listening.

So annoying.

Anyways, I have a x-acto knife and have been debating whether or not to modify the bottom of the case myself (the clip isn't great and it kinda ticks me off that I have to act as seamstress for this failure of a product if I want to use it). But sending stuff back is tedious and time consuming (okay, it takes about five minutes to return stuff on Amazon, but still, I don't want to do it!).

title: Good quality sound without distortion
text:
These headphones are even better than I'd hoped. I tried them out for music, which is really the deciding factor when it comes to headphones, I allow a lot of leeway when it comes to sound for movies, audiobooks and tv shows.

But these were super nice. They are comfortable too. The cord is thick and is the right length to go from head to pocket with extra wiggle room and the sound adjuster is on the cord, tres convenient.

It was hard to see in the picture, but they are not totally white. there is a thin line of lime green that is on the out part, the color is bright enough that it almost seems to glow, like a LED light from the sides of the headphones, it looks pretty cool actually.

title: Kept my old laptop useful
text:
Like many. my laptop had the wireless module as part of the motherboard so when wireless went out I had no WiFi without an adapt0r. The first adaptor I got did not have enough range to reach the far side of the house where the wireless router was installed. This one gave me a good strong signal. It did not require any special drivers and they have a 24 hour technical support line, which would be good to have if you have any problems, I didn't, but it's a nice little feature.

The casing feels solid and sturdy but is nicely lightweight and portable, but it lost a star because it is bigger than I thought it would be and blocks the other USB port on the side of my laptop, that is until I found the included extension cord, this way the other USB port is free to use and the device can be mounted on the side of the screen with double sided tape so that it is like a TV antenna (a lame Mcguyver'ish solution to keep it out of the way of all the other stuff on my desk).

title: Works for Mac
text:
This is basically the same device as the IPEVO adapter. The difference is that this one doesn't have the audio out nor does it have its own power supply. Also the design is flawless, the IPEVO had a crooked HDMI IN.

The adapter is pretty basic and it delivers what it promises, a male HDMI to female VGA adapter compatible for use with Macs. Because of the adapter I've been able to avoid buying a new laptop or monitor for my son.

title: Good enough for VOIP phones
text:
The positives about these headphones outnumber the negatives.

In no particular order;

1. Easy set up. Like all bluetooth devices, these headphones were a quick set up by simply turning them on and my mac responded with 'Do You Want To Use This Device?' The total set up time, approximately sixty seconds!

2.Excellent for VOIP gmail phone.

3. You can charge the headset, while you are using it. So on marathon conference call days, I can plug them in, while using them for about twenty minutes and then they are charged enough to last through a long, boring, three hour conference call (more's the pity!).

4. They charge off the USB port and they come with a cable for doing this.

5. They are lightweight and comfortable to wear, so no headaches!

6. Adjustable volume which is perfect for the hard of hearing.

The negatives, in no particular order;

1. The sound quality is not so great. It is too grainy for music, there is a static sound in the background of everything you are listening to, not a big deal if you are using them for phone conversations, but a definite loser if you are trying to listen to music.

2. It gets more static background noise as the batteries wind down.

title: 3-D Minecraft!
text:
These glasses are the perfect gift for the minecrafters in your family. We've only been playing mine craft since the summer and already it's become a favorite. When my hubby and son figured out they could play a 3-D version, we pulled out the paper 3-D glasses that came in a box of cereal. Quickly it became evident that if we were going to use the 3-D function, we'd have to get better glasses.

First off, I didn't realize there were so many different kids of 3-D glasses, some are red and blue, like these, and some are red and green, which means there are two images, a red image for one eye and a blue image for the other eye. When Jaws 3-D came out there was an urban legend that if you didn't have the 3-D glasses, the movie would be invisible. Crazy and completely untrue.

But the newer kind of 3-D, like what you see if you watch a newer 3-D movie (like the upcoming Star Wars) uses a new system, called polarization (two projections of the movie are shown and your eyes are fed both images simultaneously, creating a 3-D effect), for a polarized movie you get those black glasses they give you when you buy a movie ticket.

Those black glasses will not work on an old style red/blue or red/green 3-D game or movie (we checked, just to make sure!).

My only complaint with these glass are the fit, they slide around a bit and on my son, they slide down a lot. But other than that, they are great.

title: Worked even after being run through the washing machine
text:
We tore the couch apart, lifted the area rug, moved the television, I even checked the refrigerator! But no luck, the tiny white wafer that controls what we watch, when we watch itand if we watch anything at all was gone.

I called my hubby to find out if there was any way I could watch my favorite shows without it, nothing but dreadful silence from his end of the phone. So we ordered replacements, an heir and a spare. Yahoo, television!

I like to watch my shows and fold laundry, so I went to remove the wet, freshly washed clothing from the washing machine to the dryer and heard something drop. Something hard and plastic-y sounding, IT WAS THE REMOTE!

In the one place we didn't look; the washing machine. Apparently the remote was in the pocket of my sweetie's robe, he spilled coffee on the robe and gave it to me to wash. So now we have a squeaky clean remote. Just for fun, I took it to the living room and pointed it at the television, hey, weirder things have happened! The remote worked! All except the UP button, for whatever reason, you can scroll down, sideways and the menu button will always flip you back a level, but there is no scrolling up.

Long story short, these are some resilient remotes. The clothing I washed wasn't on the gentle cycle and they went through the spin cycle. Amazing, right? Now if only I could find a blender this tough, life would be grand.

title: Best and most durable splitter I've bought
text:
This is the fifth headphone splitter I've bought. The others all suffered from the same, unusable defect, they were crapola and broke. Worse the sound quality was crackly and very 1985 (remember listening to tapes with a walkman, yeah, that's the sound quality I'm talking about).

I hook my cordless headphones in and then traipse around the house washing up, folding laundry, making beds (sometimes I do this) secure in the knowledge that the cord pluggy thing will not come undone from the techno starfish I've plugged it into. It has more ports (I think that's what they are called) than we really need, but it is still the most functional splitter.

I love this, I can listen to a book on tape while my hubby watches a movie and my kiddo listens to music, all of us lost to the world for a little while.

When this one wears out I'd order another lickity split!

title: I don't like this
text:
Somethings off in tech-y town. I guess I expected to be a lot more impressed by this little black lozenge of coolness.

It is portable.

It is shiny and black and it does look like something from Battlestar Galactica (though I can't remember if they had computers with mouses on BG).

It doesn't have a cord (now this was the part I did really enjoy).

But, it is mostly just a mouse with a small area of sensitivity for clicking. It took a while to get used to the limited area of click-y-ness, but compared to a regular mouse, I just couldn't see a reason (other than shininess) to spend three times as much to buy this.

title: Sweet little backup
text:
This is the third home external hard drive I've bought and so far, it's the smallest and easiest to install and use (possibly I'm just getting quicker and quicker at doing this - think of it like the pit crew at Nascar).

Anyway, I don't have a lot to say about this. It's a hard drive and it does exactly what a hard drive should, it stores stuff that I can't bear to lose if my computer suddenly made like the Titanic.

This isn't a super size hard drive, like something to store a complete collection of the last ten year's worth of home videos (if you have super short home videos like me, then you could give it a try).

All in all, a worthy and useful project that's sturdy and easily installed.

title: Underpowered Fan
text: The device is well made and has functions well as a stand, but the fan is underpowered, so I had to replace the unit two months after purchasing it.  I suggest the company made an upgraded unit with 3-5 fans instead of 1.  My new laptop stand isn't adjustable like this one, but since I keep it closed unless I'm on a conference call, it's not as important.  With a larger fan, the computer runs quieter and faster, so the net volume inclusive of the laptop/stand is about even.

title: Powerful
text: I have all six fans running on speed 3 of 5, and my laptop is noticeably cooler than the single fan (single speed) product I was using.  The fan noise is comparable to my old laptop stand, but the laptop itself is quieter because the internal, laptop fan doesn't have to work as hard.  The laptop also runs faster when I am running multiple programs, because it doesn't need to throttle down the processing speed to reduce the heat.  This was the most powerful laptop stand I could find on Amazon, and I believe I made the right choice.  My only criticism is the buttons on the front, which would be better off as dials to eliminate the need for the screen which can be distracting.

title: Broke after a few uses
text: The adapter broke after a handful of uses 3 months after purchase.  The audio has severe distortion/feedback.  It is not the headphones, which work fine on an old iPhone.  There is no recourse since it's outside the return window.

title: 150-200 Mbps Actual Speed
text: My internet connection is 600 Mbps, and I can achieve this on my work computer, which is rated to 1000 Mbps.  My personal computer's internal modem has a max speed of 100 Mbps for wired or wireless connection, and I typically received 95 Mbps download, and by adding this device, I consistently have download speeds of 150-200 Mbps.  There has been no impact to my upload speed, which is in the 20-30 Mbps range.  It also reduces the number of disconnections when streaming/gaming.  I can only connect to either the 2.4G or the 5.0G band, so you can't double dip here.

title: Excellent Product.
text:
Edit.

I left the review at 5 stars as I use it for my IPad 12.9 and IPad Air attached to a Magic Keyboard. Both fit well.

However, my wife informed me it doesn’t work for a laptop. Typing on such a raised keyboard, would be torture on the hands. With my IPad attached to my Magic Keyboard, it’s fine as it keeps my head straight, while I can alternate to the touch Ipad or the Magic Keyboard.

Definitely not recommended for a standard laptop.

Original review.

Solid product. Very stable.

My IPad Air 11 which is attached to my Magic Keyboard, and my IPad 12.9, in a Speck case, both fit fine. It is fixed so it can’t be adjusted. That may make it inconvenient for some. There are pads on the bottom, so the desk it’s placed on won’t be scratched. Highly recommended in case your current setup is causing neck or upper back issues. Not good for couch use. I didn’t consider the so called cable management system worth bothering with. It required peeling tape and sticking it on your desk, possibly permanently marking it.

I can definitely recommend it.

title: Very sturdy.  Bottom rungs are 2 3/4 inches apart.
text: This is a very sturdy item.  The bottom rungs measure  2 3/4 inches across.  That’s end to end. My wife’s IPhone 13 fits perfectly.  My Mini Ipad 6 fits fine, but could fall if not centered correctly.  I would not buy it for anything larger than a mini ipad.

title: This review is for the bluetooth model.
text:
Likes.

1. Simple to use.
2. My IPhone recognized the radio immediately, establishing a bluetooth connection. It never cut out.
3. The sound quality for both music and voice is very good. OTA radio less so, but that’s understood.

Dislikes.

I wish it was smaller. It’s much larger than I expected. Make sure you have enough room.

Overall.

The radio works flawlessly, both with four C batteries and by plugging it into an outlet. I tested the sound quality by playing some songs that I had downloaded from You Tube Premium, to my iPhone. The sound was very good. I then tested voice quality by playing an Audible book through it. It was Neil Gaiman’s voice, and the sound quality was very good. The volume was fine.

The bluetooth connection.
I set the radio to bluetooth, then went to bluetooth settings on my IPhone. The IPhone immediately recognized the radio, and paired. I played both songs and the Audible books, using this connection. I ordered the radio in order to listen to hours of Audible books at night. I usually fall asleep while listening, and it played throughout the night. That way, I wouldn’t be exhausting my IPhone battery constantly, as it uses a lot less battery life, when it doesn’t need to pump out volume. I have 2 Sonos systems and a bluetooth Bang and Olufsen sound bar. However, I wanted an easy to use radio right next to me in bed.

title: Very heavy. Too heavy for my comfort level.
text:
Likes
Good adjustment features.
Clarity 7/10 to 8/10.
Easy adjustment to match your face size.
Nice case.

Dislikes.
Too heavy for my comfort level.

I last used binoculars on a trip to Alaska. I had inexpensive compact binoculars, which had a more limited range than these, and with less clarity. I was using them to look straight up the mountains to watch the amazing white goats. They were very light and my arms never became tired. Those are the ones I would take if I went again. These binoculars are superior, with the major exception being they are just not comfortable to hold. I couldn’t watch those goats for more than a few minutes, with these binoculars.

These will probably work great on a tripod, for a very muscular person, and certainly for viewing an object for a few minutes. If you have a stationary object to rest it on, that would help. Though one reviewer mentioned using a tripod, I wasn’t able to locate a place to screw in the tripod.

The price of these seems to fluctuate quite a bit. These can be a good buy for the right person.

title: Stainless Steel vs Aluminum.
text:
This is my fourth Apple watch. I’ve purchased the series 0, series 1, 2, two series 4. One stainless, one aluminum. The 4 is such a great watch, I never felt the need to upgrade. I recently paid Apple $ 79 to replace my battery. They actually replaced the watch. I’ve never had a problem with any Apple watch. I purchased the 7, because of a great Amazon price.

Stainless steel vs aluminum. Both are great. I put one bad scratch on my aluminum crystal. It doesn’t affect function, and it only shows when the watch is dark. It happened when my watch hit the rough edge of our granite countertop. My SS has never scratched.

Why spend the extra money to get the stainless? If you want a GPS only model, the SS is $ 300 more than the aluminum. If you want cellular capability, the difference drops to $ 200. Due to health issues, my wife convinced me to get the cellular capability. In an emergency, these will call 911, even when your phone is not around, and even when you don’t subscribe for service. That’s important.

The series 7 has a blood oxygen measurement feature. During Covid, we purchased two different fingertip devices to measure blood oxygen. We were disappointed with both. The watch oxygen measurement works seamlessly. We consider it worth buying for that feature alone.

Summary.

If you want cellular capability, spend the extra $ 200 for SS. If you don’t, buy the aluminum model and save $ 300.
Both are great watches.

title: Square Trade , (Allstate Protection). Purchased policy for wood platform bed.
text:
I have had about 8 Square Trade protection policies. I had one claim, on a washing machine. They immediately shipped me the part they believed was defective, had an appliance repair person 2 days later, and it was fixed. Kudos.

This furniture policy unlike their appliance polices, does not extend any manufacturers’ warranty. It is an accident policy only. I took this policy when I purchased a platform bed with slats. I guess that means if the wood bed cracks due to a defect, the manufacturer must handle it. If children jump on it and it cracks, SQ covers it.

title: Perfect for my needs. Excellent build quality.
text:
Likes.
Good build quality.
The sound quality of the music is fine.
Quickly connected to my Iphones and Ipads.
Comfortable enough.

Dislikes.
No plug provided.

I am an audiophile of sorts. I have a Bang and Olufsen soundbar, a Sonos Playbar, and a Sonos Beam. Obviously, these headphones do not compare. The music quality is very acceptable for my purpose.

My wife has the main TV on 12 hours a day at a mid volume. I like to sit in the same room because the comfortable chairs are in that room. The TV dialogue was very annoying to me. These headphones do a great job of allowing me to enjoy my music, as they block out the TV sound very well.

The quiet mode works well. It is not a true noise cancellation headphone. That’s okay. There is no annoying air pressure, just 3 modes of what is best described as programmed white noise, such as rainfall. Excellent for blocking sound.

The phone quality is excellent. You do have to hit a button on the earphones, if a call come in, or to call out. The “active,” feature shown in the instructions controls a lot of the features.
