Although it was a snap pairing it with my iPhones and IPads I wasn’t able to pair it with my Samsung or LG OLED TV. I also wasn’t able to pair it with my Apple TV. I’ll keep trying.

I was considering buying the Airpod Max for my over the ear headphone. It’s been available for about $ 450. I figured I would upgrade every year. However, I checked the big yellow store and the trade in value was only $ 80, for the current model. WOW. Pay $ 450 today, get $ 80 tomorrow. No thanks.

My dislike was that a plug was not provided. It seems minor. However, I received a $ 90 pole lamp from Amazon and the plug was missing. I used a plug from another pole lamp and it blew out my new lamp. The wattage was too high. Who knew? The instructions say to use a 5W plug. Reading the microscopic lettering on the plugs has you guessing what the wattage is. I used a basic Amazon tablet plug and it worked.

Overall. The build quality is excellent and I believe it’s a very good value overall.

title: Easy to set up if you are Alexa fluent.
text: The round ball shape looks a lot nicer than the earlier models.  I’m pleased with it.

title: Great design. Very useable pockets.
text:
I placed my MacBook 12 in it. Though it’s a little smaller than a 13 inch MacAir, it is spacious inside and can easily handle the 13 inch size.

Likes.

The pockets exceeded my expectations. On the back, there are two back pockets, one with extra fabric which expands enough to handle a mouse, chargers, really any accessories most people carry. The pocket next to it doesn’t have the extra fabric, but still expands nicely. Easily holds a standard IPhone 13. The expandable pocket closes with a magnetic flap to keep valuables from slipping out.

The front pocket doesn’t look like it holds much, but it is very spacious and would hold a wallet and an iPhone easily. The best way to describe the spacious front pocket is to think of a hooded sweatshirt, with a large single pocket going across the entire midsection. To be precise, the outside of the case is 13.75 inches wide, and the front pocket gives you 10 inches of usable space for storage.

2. The design is top notch and it really has a great look. You will receive compliments on this case.

3. The center of the case holds the laptop, and also closes with a magnetic closure.

4. I also placed my 12.9 inch IPAD PRO in the case. The IPAD is in a Speck case. It fit in fine, though snug, with the Speck case, but the case added just enough height to keep the Magnetic flap from locking.

title: Works very well.  Location dependent.
text:
Likes.

Well made.
Long cord. The long cord is very important.

Setup.

I used the long cord to place it on the floor, next to my patio door.
I then set my TV to auto scan.
It gave me many more stations than my non amplified leaf antennae pulled in.
Every station was crystal clear.
However, that was not a convenient permanent location, so I then placed it behind the TV.
It was important to first place it in the best possible area, in my case against the patio door to identify all possible stations.

Issues.

After auto scan identified all possible stations, I moved the antenna to behind my entertainment center. I lost half the stations. But, the TV showed those station numbers, it just couldn't pull them in. I then placed it flat on top of the entertainment center. It improved the reception. I then slid it partially inside my TV wall mount hardware, flat against the wall. It gave me excellent reception on all identified stations.

My advice.

Take advantage of the long cord, move it next to a window even if it won't be left there. You can then place the antenna in more convenient locations, trying to get back to as many identified stations as possible.

title: Updated look to my 2015 12.9 Pro.
text: My Ottobox Defender finally fell apart after 6 years of use.  The Speck case gives it a much cleaner, updated look.  Glad I got it.

title: Fits perfect.  Transmits signal fine,
text: My Air-tag fit into the holder perfectly and works well.  I am submitting photos of this air tag holder, next to the Apple branded Air-tag holder.  I bought the 4 pack of air tags, and two Apple branded holders, which cost me about $ 35 each. The brown one is the Apple holder.  It is open on both sides as the photos show.  This holder is closed on one side. I was concerned that having one side closed would affect the transmission, but it instantly pinged very loudly.  This holder is a much better value.

title: Actually helps.
text: It seemed like a gimmick item but my glasses, with my mask on, stayed noticeable clearer.  The only issue I had was deciding which cloth was the cleaner, and which has the solution in it.  The instructions didn’t state that.  Going back to the product information site, gave me the answer.

title: Get the smaller band for wrist size 7 and under.
text:
I purchased one band from Apple and one from Amazon.

1. I purchased the smaller band from Apple, for a 40 mm watch.
2. I purchased the larger band from Amazon for a 44 mm watch.

My wrist size is 7 inches. The smaller band fits better and looks better.
The smaller band leaves 7 links uncovered.
The larger band leaves 2 links uncovered.

I thought the larger band must have more magnets and would hold better.
Both hold great. The smaller band is easier to get tight.

Because I reviewed the band purchased from Apple first, Amazon will not let me review the bands purchased from them separately. That’s why it doesn’t say verified purchased.

title: Ridges won’t hold the IPad up.  Good supplement to the Magic Keyboard.
text:
Plus. A major improvement over Apple’s older two separate piece magnetic covers. Those didn’t hold up. They were always falling off. This is one piece and the magnets really hold.
Negative. Bad ridge design. They don’t hold the IPad up. Prepare for a tired left hand.
I read that on some reviews but thought, that can’t be right.

I have the $ 300 magic keyboard. I love it, but some apps only show in vertical, and you have to remove the IPad to view those.
The magic keyboard is great on your desk or your lap, when watching TV, or just relaxing. Not great for bed.

My advice. Some major big box stores are selling the magic keyboard for $ 199. You will be much happier spending the extra money buying a magic keyboard.
This smart folio cover does cover both sides, looks nice, and provides some protection.
If you get a magic keyboard, this is the only folio type cover that makes sense. A quick snap in and out. Easy to swap around. You don’t want one that takes effort to put the IPad in, an take it out.

If you don’t plan on getting the magic keyboard, buy a different brand.

title: Easy install.  Good range.  No WPS button. Great with Amazon plugs and smart devices.
text:
I replaced an old Apple Express with this. I have ATT DSL, and it is connected to my ATT modem/router.
In the photo, it looked to be the same size as my Apple Express and I was surprised at how much larger is was.
It provides much greater range than my old Express.

Setup. Very easy to install. I’m not a techie.

Advice. Write down the exact name of your current router, as displayed in your wi fi settings. Also the passwords.
It will facilitate the install, as your other devices will recognize the router easier.
It does not have a WPS button, but my Canon printer recognized it with minimal effort.

I did plan on subscribing to Erro’s security features. However, it appears that since my Erro connection goes through my ATT combo, I can’t benefit from those services.

title: Important warranty information.
text:
I purchased my Magic Keyboard and IPAD Air one day apart.

I then learned that AppleCare on the IPAD Air also covers the keyboard and pencil, if purchased on the same receipt. There is a lot of misinformation on this subject. It is clearly stated in the Apple T&C. I called Apple and given the circumstances, they added it.

Other confusion.

The USB-C port on the keyboard charges the IPAD, when docked while charging. It does not charge the keyboard.
The keyboard has no battery.

Uses.

I use it while on my couch. It is compact and very comfortable to use.

title: Folds back completely.  As convenient as a naked Oasis, for reading.
text:
Purchased on Prime Day 2020, along with the new (2019), Kindle Oasis.
Feels good to the touch.
Folds back entirely, so you read your Oasis, as easily as you can without a cover. Very important.
5 stars all the way.

title: Read without glare.
text:
Flimsy shipping packaging. Scuff on top right of screen. Shipping package did not contain outside label required for lithium batteries. On my trade in, I had to print the lithium warning label in color, per Amazon directions.

I paired my Airpods easily. Overall, nice enough. Nice not to have eye fatigue caused by glare.

Negatives.

1 No real browser. I realize this is a reader, but here’s the issue. I subscribe to the Amazon owned Washington Post at a recurring bargain price of $ 30 per year. It was originally a Prime Day deal. The entire newspaper including all comics and ads. Even though it is linked to my Amazon account, as an Amazon subscription, with payments to Amazon, I cannot read it on my Kindle reader, just my Fire or IOS devices. To read it on my Kindle Oasis, I must take the monthly subscription for $ 19.95 a month. Same with all subscriptions. This is a major disappointment. For that reason, I can’t recommend it.

2. I got the 32 gb, because I also have Audible. I thought I could listen to Audible, as I read the book on the Oasis. You can’t. For example, I have the Audible, “ Sandman). I also have the Kindle reader version. It is a very graphic comic book, by graphic, I mean great illustrations. What I need to do as I go through Sandman, is listen on my IPhone, while following the comic pages on my Fire. That enhances the experience greatly. Since I need to use two devices simultaneously, I use the Fire, as it appears in color, vs the BW in the Oasis. If I knew I would need two devices, I would have saved $ 25 and purchased the 8 GB.

title: Arrived smashed.  Sharp shards of glass.
text: The packaging was intact and not damaged. The screen protector had a large section that was smashed.  I ran my index finger along it to make sure it was not a wrinkled piece of cellophane covering it.  My finger feels like it was penetrated by the shard of glass.  See photo.

title: Easy to install.
text:
This review is for the 5th generation IPad mini case.
It is easy to install, and appears to offer good protection. There is no protective screen.

The stand is okay and does allow both vertical and horizontal viewing.

One issue. I had great difficulty taking it apart in order to install my IPad. Why do they need to ship it fully assembled? I needed to watch a You Tube Video, in order to take it apart without damaging it.

title: It has a strong snap closure and a belt hook.
text:
Buying the right case is critical. My first AirPods Pro case did not have a snap. At the airport last week, I dropped the case onto the cement floor, while in a food line. The two ear pieces flew out of the charging case. One wound up 4 people ahead of me. The other flew under a large stationary condiment food cart. Fortunately, someone saw where it went. I had to lie down on the dirty floor and keep waving my arm until I snagged it. When I returned home, the first thing I did was look for a case with a snap.

This case has a strong snap. It is a very stiff case. I had trouble snapping it the first time. It should loosen up with wear. It works but the top part could have used a little more material. Every time I unsnap it, it pulls the top of the Apple charging case open. Pulling it all the way back frees it.

Overall, after my experience with the first case, I will give this case 5 stars. Whatever case you chose, get one with a strong snap closure.

title: Perfect fit.  Attractive look.  Not for other Airpods.
text:
Update. Though the case is nice and securely contains the charging case, there is a problem.

It does not have a snap. The case dropped on the hard concrete floor at the airport. The AirPods flew out of the charging case, which remained in this case. They flew in two different directions, in a crowded food line. One went under a food cart. I had to lie on the floor and sweep my arm until I got it. A snap would have prevented that.

I received this a week before my Airpods Pro arrived. I was disappointed on opening and was ready to return it. It looked cheap. It is a soft case, not rigid like my other Airpods case. That's why it looked so flimsy, when empty.

Once my Airpods Pro arrived, and filled the case, the fit was perfect and the case looked great.
The small pinhole in the front lets you check the charge status without opening the case.

Unlike my regular Airpods case, there is no snap button to secure it, and no hook to latch it to anything.
The fit is so perfect that the Airpods case will not slip out.

Do not order this for other Airpods. They will fall out.

title: Fantastic sound.  Better instructions needed.  App needs improvement.
text:
I am posting updates at the bottom.

This is a review of the new Beo Soundstage soundbar.

The instrumentals are amazing. Listening to the London Symphony, or Boston Pops, I can differentiate different string instruments.
Vocals are excellent.
I listened to podcasts and didn't find much difference in the speaking voices.
However, this replaced my Sonos Playbar which has fine audio.

This is an outstanding speaker with a poor app and virtually nonexistent instructions.
This would not be a problem if professional installation is used.
Because I have not used HDMI ARC previously, and I expect that most buyers will either use professional installation, or have experience with B&O or similar high end products, I did not deduct a star. My rating is based on the audio quality.

My current audio equipment includes a SONOS Playbar, a SONOS Beam, a SONOS one, and the Sony HT-X9000F.

I found this Beo Soundstage soundbar the most frustrating to set up.

Setup.

I did not get anywhere trying to get the unit set up using the app.
I have all Apple equipment, plus the Google mini, and the Google Home App.
I have a paid subscription to Google Play and You Tube Music.
Apparently, Beo and LG have a relationship, and the instructions for setting up the TV gave the setup instructions for the LG OLED TV. I have a Samsung TV.
The Beo app stated I could use the Google Home to set up the speaker. I have a Samsung TV. I followed the instructions in the app. That didn't help at all either. Not for WiFI, not for bluetooth.

I finally got bluetooth connected with no help from the app. My IPhone eventually connected to the Beo, via blue tooth. I never connected via WiFi. After connecting via blue tooth, and while listening to music via bluetooth, I again tried using the app to get WIFI. I received the message, error cannot connect to bluetooth. Sure, I was already using bluetooth.

I then moved the Beo to the room with the ethernet cable. I had never used an HDMI ARC connection. I made the connections.

I then turned my Samsung TV on, and the soundbar worked perfectly. My Direct TV remote worked perfectly without any pairing.
I then changed the source to my Apple TV. Everything worked perfectly. I used the Direct TV remote for that also. So, yes, your TV remote will control the sound.
I use bluetooth to play music from my IPhone.

Beo says the speaker can be wall mounted, or used on a tabletop.
My wife doesn't want it wall mounted.
My TV is wall mounted, and I wanted to place the Beo, vertical side up, on our entertainment center, directly under the TV. However, if used in the vertical or tall position without wall mounting, it will fall over. It is not balanced. I was very disappointed.
If used in the horizontal, or flat position, resting on a shelf, one of two soft pullout tabs must be removed. The power cord and HDMI cables can then go through the bottom of the speaker, to the back.

Beo needs to provide or sell, a small stand for table mounting. They do sell a large entertainment type piece of furniture, apparently adapted and with screws to hold the speaker in the vertical position. I'm not interested in another piece of furniture. A separate company sells three different accessories for the mounting. The one for tabletop mounting consists of a few pieces of soft feet. It sells for 100 pounds plus 20 pounds shipping from England. Probably weighs 5 ounces at most. I'll pass. Beo could have included that with the Soundstage. Probably costs under $ 1 to produce.

The speaker looks much more impressive in the vertical position, than it does laying flat on a table. For those that prefer a non intrusive look, the horizontal position would be fine. I tested it in both positions. In the vertical position, speakers aimed directly at my seating position sounded much better than in the horizontal position. However, when in another part of the room, as you may be when entertaining, the sound was better in the horizontal position. In the horizontal position, the speakers face my 12 foot ceilings

I did contact B&0 and asked if horizontal placement degraded performance. A simple question.
They e-mailed back. Contact a dealer and have an installation technician help me. More $$$$.

The speaker is just under 44 inches long, and weighs about 20 pounds.
There is no remote.
The wall mount is part of the speaker, and it just drops onto two small round holders put in the wall with screws. Screws are not provided.

The small box provided was missing the fabric puller, which would allow the speaker direction to be changed for tabletop placement.

Update.

I finally connected through the B&O app.
There are a number of optiuons.
One of features allows me to tell the speaker whether it is in a horizontal or vertical position.
On my failure to get a Wi Fi connection, I didn’t notice that the speaker has icons that can be pressed for pairing.
The icon, and others such as sound and the on/off icon are deliberately made hard to see in order to present a more streamlined appearance. In my initial setup, I set it up in the vertical position, propped up to keep it from falling over. I just didn’t see the icons.

There are 2 ways to hook up the TV to the speaker.
1. Plug the HDMI cable from the satellite or other type of receiver directly to the TV. Works great. An initial 20 second delay in sound when the TV is turned on.
2. Plug the HDMI cable from the receiver directly into the soundbar. This reduces your cable use by one. In both cases, the ARC connection remains the same. The sound was instant.

With option 2, on my Samsung TV, the "Anytime NET, " appears to cause compatibility problems.
The soundbar went on immediately, but after about 30 seconds, the video disappeared, and the message appeared, "check your connection." My Apple TV was not affected, neither was the OTA connection. The soundbar was working fine for both of those.

Troubleshooting.
On my Samsung TV, I went into menu. Nothing notable there.
I went into tools.
It showed the Anytime Net setting.
I clicked refresh, for the Samsung Genie, the Apple TV, and the B&O.
Each time I clicked refresh on the B&O, the video shut off, along with the sound.
I tried everything a number of times.
I went into every setting.,
I disconnected the Anytime Net. Nothing helped.
I have read that some older satellite receivers can cause problems with HDMI ARC.

I finally decided to go with my original connection, the receiver to the TV, and then the ARC connection for the robust sound. That did give me one extra cable, but is problem free.

Dec19th update.
Things coming together. I finally connected my google nest mini to my Soundbar. Went through the google home icon.
I selected my premium YouTube Music as my default service.
Now every time I want to listen to music on the Soundbar. I just say, Hey Google, Play Dean Martin in the family room. Works great.
I also noticed that when I request music, the Soundbar automatically turns my TV off.

I’m very pleased with the features. Just wish B&O had a 30 minute You Tube video walking buyers through the features.
Would have avoided a lot of frustration. I really love the features and the sound quality.

title: Super Comfortable.  Gets dirty.  Very difficult to clean.
text:
I just purchased two. Received next day. We already have 3, so I can contribute something.

Pros.
The bands are easy to put on, infinitely adjustable, and very comfortable.

Cons.
They get dirty and are very difficult, if not impossible to clean.
The first one purchased was Seashell. For my wife. Looked terrible after getting dirty. I tried it for a while. Great comfort. Threw it out. To me, that’s bad durability.

The second one was denim. My wife is a neat freak and takes care of everything.
At about the 4 month mark, it is getting dirty. Shows the dirt.

Still, we just ordered two more. Just super comfortable.
Mine is the indigo. Goes well with my Space Grey. Looks sharp. Hoping the dirt won’t show as quickly,.

A final point. Unlike the rubber band that through Series 4, came with all watches, these are very easy to install.
The rubber bands can stick and be difficult to install.

title: Perfect fit for Mac Book 12.  Attractive and well made.
text: Perfect fit.  Magnet closes case tightly.  Excellent for travel.

title: Easier set up  when used with Amazon products.
text:
Easier to set up with Amazon products, than the non Amazon brands.
Works great. Biggest problem I have is remembering what I have named each of the 3 plugs,
If you use the wrong name, the lamp in another room can go on and wake someone up.

title: Works perfectly.  Great price.
text:
Works perfectly. Includes batteries. Took me about 5 tries to have it work the TV and my Sonos Playbar.
Great price.

title: Works with I phone.  Very sharp look. No speakers.
text:
I am using this watch daily, and am continually providing reviews, as I learn things.

I previously commented that the watch disconnects occasionally. This was caused by my swiping/ clearing open apps. The wear os app must be left open.

I like this watch enough to wear it daily, and my Apple series 2 has been relagated to a stay at home nighttime watch,
Killer looks make this my watch of choice for outside use.

As I said earlier, no speakers mean no phone calls, and texts sent through the Apple IMessage system don’t come through.
Does everything else important to me.
Overall, a keeper.

Caution. There are many versions of this watch, so make sure the watch you order has the features you want.
This watch has no speakers, but has the heart rate, GPS and Google Pay functions.

In reading this review, please keep in mind that I am an I Phone user. I am very familiar with Apple smartwatches.
I believe an Android user, would not have the same problems I reported. Especially a user familiar with an Android smartwatch.

Correction to initial review.
I stated the watch does not receive texts. It does.
It does not receive texts sent through the Apple System IMessage.
All texts sent by banks, pharmacy, everything else is received.

Pros:
Connects to I Phone.
Very attractive black stainless watch.
Nice leather band.
Many customizable faces.
Functions most important to me, such as weather, heart rate, fitness and step measurement work well.
Google Pay.
Easy setup.
Gmails come right through.
Apple News, a news feature I like, also works fine.
The watch also has an always on function I use. When on, the screen turns a darker shade, but is easily readable.
A flip of the wrist brings it back up to my customized blue screen.

Cons.
No speakers.
Cannot talk on it.
I do get a vibration when a phone call comes in, and the screen shows the phone number calling.
This is helpful if I’m relaxing and I don’t want to answer that call.
Watch didn’t recognize my Apple AirPods

I have had I Phones since the early 3GS model. Have had Apple smartwatches from Gen 0 to my wife's series 4.
They work well but the aluminum models look cheap, and the upgrade to stainless is an extra $ 300. Was $ 200.
Apple is now forcing everyone to pay an extra $ 100 for the cellular capability, in order to get a stainless steel smartwatch. I resent that marketing ploy and am looking at smartwatches by other makers. That is why I selected this watch. It is a great looking watch.

There are a number of very nice customizable faces, appropriate for office wear, as well as several sport faces.

Setup.

Had an initial problem where my I Phone couldn't find the watch. Just hit factory reset on the watch. Problem solved.
Went smoothly after that.
The Google OS watch App., downloadable on the Apple App store, walked me through everything.
Current and resting heart rate, and the fitness app are the apps I use most on the Apple smartwatch, and these are comparable. Weather App is very good.

Downloaded Google Play Music, which I subscribe to, but I could not listen to it since I couldn't connect my Airpods.
The problem with the connection may be in the way the watch shows available devices. It identified my Apple TV, and my Samsung TV. Five other devices were identified only by meaningless codes. The first one I tried, turned out to be my Sony Soundbar. Worked fine on it. Trying another code turned out to be a time consuming process. Gave up after over an hour.

Overall. Works well enough for I Phone users, wanting a more attractive smartwatch than the Apple watch.
Probably would be 5 stars for an Android user.

title: Bluetooth equivalent plus WI FI.  Optical connection available. Excellent sound quality.  Big sound.
text:
I have three Sonos devices. I purchased both the Playbar and Sonos One, and received this Amazon Vine item. Sonos software is incredible, and is worth buying for entry into the Sonos world. My Playbar is connected to our main TV, and my Beam is connected to our bedroom TV.
I actually think the dialogue clarity is better on the Beam. Maybe it’s the smaller room.

I am using optical on the Beam. Several reasons. I had trouble getting the HDMI to work on my Samsung. My bedroom TV, a 50 inch Samsung, only has two HDMI ports. I need one for my satellite and one for my Roku. Sonos provides a connector that makes the optical connection seamless. I had an HDMI connection on my Sony 9000. It has an HDMI in and an out port. My satellite went through that to the TV. That left my Roku going straight to the TV and I lost the benefit of the speaker with Roku. To me optical is the most trouble free connection. The sound from any device goes through the speaker. Very happy with optical on both my Playbar and Beam.

For those not having a Sonos, and being apprehensive about not getting a remote, be thankful. Your phone, or your tablet is the best remote possible. It shows every music service available, and makes searching for any song, or radio station, or genre so easy, and so complete.

Sonos as a Wi FI device. Wi Fi is so much better for your soundbar than Bluetooth, including Airplay 2. I like music when I fall asleep. I select a radio station or loop songs, and shut my phone down. The music plays all night without diminishing my battery. Cannot do this with Bluetooth or Airplay. Songs don’t get interrupted. It does not make a difference on your TV.

Airplay 2 is Bluetooth equivalent. The Sonos website gives very simple directions. I started my google play song, swiped up on my IPhone, hit the same type of icon, right above the song, that shows on You Tube. For those that don’t know, there is an icon on top of the You Tube screen that allows to watch You Tube on your TV. I also used Airplay 2 to connect You Tube music to my TV. Works easily.

The Beam is compact, has big sound, great clarity, and you control volume, or pause, by just saying Alexa.
I do not have a Sonos sub or surround with either system.

I can’t imagine any competing systems in this price range, being comparable in value.
I think this leaves Bose as an afterthought.

title: Included Freetime makes the Kids Kindle a bargain purchase.
text: This is a lot of fun at a very low price for a toy.  It is a full featured kindle, but it will be used as a dedicated toy.  The Free Time included in the Kids Kindle really makes the kids kindle the one to buy.  A neighbor decided to save money by buying a regular Kindle, and a rubber case.  Big mistake.  Free time is what makes it worthwhile for my 3 year old grandson.  He instantly gravitated to Catman, and the Elmo coloring pages.  Yes, it’s a coloring book too.  You can set a pin to prevent youngsters from going outside Freetime.  My thought now is to replace the Kindle when free time expires, rather than pay a monthly charge.  When he outgrows it, he will have several regular kindles.  That will be handy if one is damaged after the warranty ends.

title: Easy setup.  Excellent sound.  Plug and Play subwoofer. Great vocals. Follow QuickStart guide.  It’s excellent.
text:
After a week's worth of usage, I am modifying my original review. I am also providing a comparison of this Sony Sound-bar, to the Sonos Playbar. I'm doing this as I think the price range of each is similar enough to interest potential buyers in each system.

I am rating the Sony Sound-bar as excellent.

1. My Direct TV remote, and my Samsung remote control the volume on the Sound-bar. They also turn it off. No pairing was needed.
2. Both of the above remotes also turn it on, but since you need the Sony remote for the HDMI link, you must use the Sony remote when turning the TV on. There are also easily accessible buttons on the Sound-bar, in case you lose the remote. Once the TV is on, you don't need the Sony remote unless you want to change the optional features such as voice for news, dialog, or music.
3. Bluetooth is a snap. You use the remote to activate the Bluetooth function.

Sonos Playbar vs Sony Sound-bar.

For TV only usage.

The Sonos cost $ 700, with no subwoofer. The subwoofer doubles the price.
The Sony has a wireless subwoofer. As a result, the Sony is better as a TV soundbar.
I purchased my Sonos as a standalone item, 6 months ago. If you plan on only buying the Sonos Player, it is not a good value. The value of the Sonos its for those that intend to have a multi-room Sonos system. Last month I added the Sonos One in a different room. The Sonos software is outstanding. I fully agree with a comment I read a year ago, that the Sonos Playbar is worth $ 350, and the Sonos software is worth $ 350. The software is a pleasure to use.

Both give clear dialog.

Winner for TV usage. Sony Sound-bar by a wide margin.

For music usage.

No clear winner as each is very different.

The Sonos Playbar is connected through your internet.
It does not have bluetooth. That is a big negative. However, it is always on, and not dependent on any other device. You use your phone, IPad, or other device, as your Sonos remote. Very simple, with their great app. You can shut off all your other devices and the Sonos will play all day and all night. You will only need your phone remote to select a new station.
It is very easy to change music services on the Sonos. Once music is on, I just tell Alexa to increase or decrease volume, or shut the music off. Alexa is incorporated in my Sonos One, and I have the Echo Dot next to my Sonos Playbar in another room. It is a wireless connection. You just tell either Alexa which room to play the music in.

The Sony Sound-bar has bluetooth. That is very convenient. It also has the subwoofer.
Excellent music quality.

The Sonos Playbar is not competitive with the Sony soundbar, as it doesn't come with a subwoofer. A full fledged Sonos system would cost over $ 2000, and would be awesome. That is beyond my budget.

Although I really like both my Sonos devices, on a value basis, I would buy the Sony Sound-bar. The included subwoofer makes the difference. The bluetooth is also more convenient, for playing a few songs.

A final note.

We prefer the styling of the Sony. Consider it a miniature Sonos Playbar.
It is longer than the Sonos Playbar, but definitely a miniature look.
The actual length is 37 inches. A template is provided for mounting on the wall, but no hardware is available.

Important comment.

Using the HDMI connection from the cable box, through the Soundbar to the TV and return. My streaming devices are only providing audio through the TV speaker. I guess I need to connect an optical cable to get audio through the soundbar on streaming devices. That should work.

Also. I’m thinking of going from Direct TV to Direct TV now when my promo ends. The latest Apple and Roku devices have HDMI so I would think after removing my cable box, I can connect the HDMI directly through the Soundbar. The streaming device simply replaces the cable box. That will leave OTA stations only providing audio through the TV speakers. Need the optical connected for that. Am I missing something?

title: Standard quality cloths at a very reasonable price.
text:
Work very well at a very reasonable price.

These are standard cloths not remarkable in any way, but at a very reasonable price.

title: Very impressive service on my Square Trade Claim.
text:
5 Stars based on prior Square Trade purchases. One large claim. Immediate service. Washing machine. Called Square Trade. Diagnosed over the phone. Part sent directly to my home. Repairman came next day. Fixed four days after initial failure. Very impressed.

On this item, Square Trade cancelled this warranty due to a mistake.

I purchased a Sonos Soundbar at the military exchange. I then purchased this warranty on Amazon as it is listed separate from the main item. I provided the receipts to Square Trade and they told me I was covered. A week later they contacted me. It turns out even though it is listed as a separately available purchase for my device, you must purchase the covered item from Amazon. They said they sell it at a very low price based on volume sales on Amazon. The Square Trade Direct price is much more expensive. It is a great bargain when purchased on a Amazon. Not only price, but a longer warranty.

title: Looks good.  Solid feel. Less chance of damage when used propped up.
text: My second case for this IPad.  The first, a different type had a tab in back to hold it up horrizontally.  That tab failed with minimal use.  That caused the IPad to fall backwards hard. This has ridges in front that seem to hold well.  Important.  When the tab is in back, a failed tab could cause the IPad to fall back hard, bad if you have a granite counter as we do.  With the front ridges, IPad  would slip forward slowly, and the IPad would not be damaged.

title: Looks like a professional job.
text:
Easy to install. Looks great. I did not have to cut it. After installing the piece with screw holes, I removed the cables off the TV, held them against the installed portion,at TV height, then placed the cover over it, and slid it down. I then reconnected the HDMI and optical cables.

The TV plug was at the opposite end of the TV, from my cables. I added a second set. The wall mount prevented me from sliding the cover down, and the floor stopped me from sliding it up. Cutting was an option. Instead, I placed the plug cord in the holder with screw holes, placed the cover over it, and then pressed the cover into the holder until it snapped in. The same way you snap a lid on a refrigerator bowl. Worked fine. Using a second set for just one plug may seem like overkill, but it really balances the setup, and looks great.

title: Easy setup.  Clarity of dialogue.  Direct TV remote controls TV functions.  Easy to program DTV.
text:
My first Sonos.

Tried to buy this through Amazon but the Thanksgiving day price went up substantially between the short time I placed it in my cart, and the time I checked out.

Would buy again. I use my IPhone and my Direct TV remote. Very easy setup. My first Sonos. Ethernet connection. Recommend you have a spare Ethernet cable and a long optical cable.

My Apple express has only one Ethernet port. Fortunately the Sonos has two. Removed the Ethernet cable from the express router, connected it to the Sonos. Then connected a second cable from the Sonos back to the express router. Very smooth.

Incredible improvement in clarity of TV dialogue. Stream music directly from Sirius XM, with the TV off. WI FI connection, not Bluetooth.

Alexa link.

Easy connection using the Alexa app.

I had one problem. Wording.

I asked Alexa to play the Carpenters on Sonos. Nope.
Finally, asked Alexa to play the Carpenters in Family Room. Worked beautifully.
Since I named my location Family Room, in Sonos setup, that’t what Alexa knows.

Wish I bought it sooner.

title: Very pleased. Looks more expensive. Good push in clip.  Perfect fit.
text:
Very pleased with this item. It looks like a classy piece of leather. The Airpods fit perfectly. They can be charged while in this case.
The push in clip looks solid, though I do keep these in my pocket. Smooth surface makes it very easy to take out.

Only caution. For those with small pockets, or that keep these in the same pocket as their keys, the smooth surface does increase the odds that they may inadvertently slip out. As a guy, my cell phone is my left front pocket, and my keys and this case is in my right front pocket.

title: Used properly, a very worthwhile device.  It works very well.
text:
Edited. The original review is below.
I just changed phones. I needed a new case. That's the end of the pixel on the phone. It can't be removed and attached to the new phone. Also, it made a mess of my leather Apple case when I removed it. Better the case than the phone. This edit in no way denigrates the pixel, but it is something to consider. Without a pixel on the phone, the pixel is not useful. Suggest you consider how long you will keep both the phone or case it is attached too. I like to change cases.

This product works well. We did not use the case. We have other cases on our phones. I placed one on my phone's case. That's mandatory. I placed another on a leather attachment to my keychain. They stick very well. It works by showing you the distance you are to your phone. If you go the wrong way, the distance increases. As you get close, the distance gets to zero. You may make a few circles getting oriented. I did. You must have the phone in your possession to use the Pixie. Therefore, you can't use it to find the phone. In reading the description page, I thought the phone somehow showed you a picture of the object you are looking for. Not so. Though the batteries are not replaceable, you can order replacement Pixies.

A good use would be to place one in your everyday handbag. Useful if your handbag disappears at a party.
Best for locating hard to find items.

title: Extremely useful and a fun toy. Updates makes this orig gen watch a great buy.
text:
I recently purchased two original gen watches. Did not buy them on Amazon as I was looking specific bands. This review is of the Watch, not the seller.

Awesome technology. After reading a Consumer Reports Oct 2016 online review of the first gen watch, I bought one for my wife and one for myself. We wanted the stainless case with sapphire lens. We previously purchased both a series 2 aluminum and series 1 aluminum and returned both. Really wanted the stainless sapphire combo without spending a lot. We considered these nice toys. We both have Rolexes and the sapphire lens is virtually indestructible. Our Rolexes went into the jewelry box as these Apple smart watches are both useful and enjoyable.

These are not toys. Extremely useful watches. Great features. Use Siri to make calls off your contact list. You don't have to type the number on a tiny screen. On the walking track, or while walking the dog, glance at your watch if a call or text comes in. Don't have to fumble with the phone while holding a leash. Have the music icon on the Watch face. It allows me to activate and change songs or albums without pulling my watch out. Have the calendar on my watch face. Quick glance each morning keeps me from forgetting about appointments. Weather icon also on my face. Tap it twice and it goes from current temp to 10 day forecast. Activity monitor on face lets me track my steps without having to pull my phone out.

All in all, an extremely useful item.

Disregard all early reviews. The updates make the original gen watch an extremely useful item. And a fun toy to boot.

title: Easy install, feels much lighter than Ottobox Defender on my Air 2, no screen protector.  That surprised me.
text:
This is my first Lifeproof.

Pros. Feels light compared to the Ottobox Defender on my Air 2. A very nice feel to it. Yes it makes it bulky, but not heavy. That was a big surprise. I didn't weigh the two, and the specs indicate the Defender and Lifeproof weigh about the same, but it just feels better in my hands than the Defender. The Defender does have a stand though.
Very easy to install and uninstall. Lifeproof provides a plastic key to open the case easily. Simple but wonderful.
Reasonable protection. I have the Apple Smartcover and Smartcase on my 12.9 IPad Pro. I like it. It's very light, has a stand, but does
not offer much in the way of protection. It's also very expensive, for what it is.

Cons. I was shocked that it does not have a screen protector. On the plus side, not having a screen protector maximizes enjoyment of the screen. Nothing to peel off either. If you add a screen protector, you increase the risk of leakage. If water isn't a concern, then add a screen protector. A stand feature would have been nice.

Other: The directions say to perform a water test before the first use, every 3 months, and before an expected water inflow, such as boating. A you tube video was very helpful. Otherwise, I would have thought I was missing a screen protector. There are some good amateur videos demonstrating an IPad Air installation. Same process.

title: Wonderful device if your speakers do not have wi fi built in.  Works with both Bose and non Bose speakers. Superb global app.
text:
I have a Logitech Z 625 in my mancave. Not wi fi capable. I connected this Bose accessory to the Z 625 and immediately very good sounding music wirelessly from my iPhone. At first I connected the standard line in cables, as I was using the optical input for the TV. Then I decided to go with the optical from the Bose to the speakers. The sound was decidedly richer. My IPhone connected immediately to the Bose, via Bluetooth. I was also pleased that my IPhone controlled the volume on the speakers. When using the optical from the TV to the speakers, I could not control the volume.

In response to another review, it does play my purchased Amazon music directly from my iPhone
All cables are supplied. The optical, as well as standard cables.

I had been using the Amazon Echo for my music play. I got the $3.99 monthly subscription for unlimited music streamed to my Echo only. I still love listening through my echo. However, with this device, I can now use my Logitech speakers and so I cancelled my $3.99 subscription and upgraded to the $7.99 subscription. This Bose adapter is a great device and does work with non Bose products.

After playing music from my Amazon library, I downloaded the Soundtouch app from Itunes. Though the reviews were poor, I went ahead and tried it. The app worked perfectly. Instructions on the app made the process simple. The app doesn't seem to have a search function. It does allow presetting stations. When I hit the Amazon icon, it doesn't give a search function, just a list. That means I simply go to the Amazon music icon on my phone, and easily search. This means I alternate between the Soundtouch app, and Amazon music app. The app gives me global internet radio. I want to emphasize this point. The Soundtouch app gives me superb global internet radio. Truly global and easy to use. I have some filipino friends who will love the stations they get in the Phillipines. Highly recommend the app.

Tremendous cost savings possible if you have expensive speakers that don't have a wireless function.

The Bluetooth on my IPhone connected immediately to the Bose adapter.

title: Excellent for the price. Thankfully more compact than my older Z2300.  No remote.  See edit.
text:
Latest edit after some frustrating months of use.

I ordered this as a TV speaker. That was in the description.
With no remote, and no way to raise or lower the sound without getting up, the item is useless to me. I like to watch TV in bed.
Who wants to keep getting up. As a computer speaker, it takes up a lot of space.very dissapointed.
I will donate it a church, where they will appreciate a loud speaker for youth groups.

Edit after 5 days use.

There is no remote. The volume is controlled by a dial. When using this connected to your TV, it's a major disadvantage getting up every time you need to change the volume. I have to downgrade from 5 stars to 4, because of this. They need to add to either a remote, or an app letting your phone control the volume. Not a problem when using this as a computer speaker, since the control is by your hand, not across the room. This is promoted as a TV speaker, not just a computer speaker, so it's a major fault.

Original review below.

I have been using the Logitech Z2300 that I purchased years ago. Connected to my computer and much appreciated when I listen to my apple subscription music. A real monster for a computer speaker. Thankfully, the Z 625 is decidedly smaller and fits on the bottom shelf of my 42 inch wood TV table with room to spare. There is also room left for my Amazon Echo and Braven wireless bluetooth speakers. The smaller size results in a much cleaner, more attractive package.

The dialog is much clearer than I expected. I have a ZVOX 450 on my main TV, so I do appreciate clear dialog.
I was disappointed that there is no bluetooth. The computer and Man Cave TV are on opposite sides of the same room, and having the Z2300 for music, and the Z625 for the TV is a bit too much. However, the problem was easily solved. On the Z625, I'm using the optical cable for the TV sound, and am using the enclosed jack to connect the speaker to my extra Iphone. As I type, I'm listening to Herman's Hermits through my Iphone to Z625 jack connection. The music is very soothing and suits my needs perfectly. No adjustments are needed when switching from the music through my smartphone via jack, or the TV sound through the optical cable. Automatic switching,

My TV test via optical was the opening of Game of Thrones. The subwoofer bass sounded great and added greatly to the enjoyment of watching the series. The galloping horses sounded thunderous.

Other considerations. I gave away my monstrous Polk system when we moved to our condo. Soundbars provide the cleanest look but really don't have any bass. My wife is picky. The soundbar is on the main TV for a cleaner appearance, while the Man Cave is a perfect home for this unit.

There was absolutely no documentation/instructions in the box, other than safety information. However hookup instructions were printed on the cardboard box. Don't destroy them opening it. Hooking up via optical was very intuitive and took minutes. I'd still like some instructions. For example, the power button is a push button. Does it shut off after inactivity? I'm doing it manually. Going by the Z2300, it probably won't make any difference. These are built to last.

title: My favorite streaming device.  Voice control is great.
text:
I already had the Amazon stick, the Roku 3, and the latest Apple TV. I now use this as my primary device.
The Apple TV does not have an Amazon app, so I can't use it for prime videos or music. Game over there.
The Fire Tv. It's very fast and versatile. I like the voice control. Makes it so easy to find movies and songs. I have an echo, and pressing the fire tv voice control lets me add items to my shopping list easily. The shopping list is my favorite use of the echo. List appears on my IPhone a few minutes later.

title: Bluetooth issues explained.  Fantastic sound worthy of 5 stars.
text:
Upgrade from 3 stars to 5.

I originally graded this 3 stars because of Bluetooth issues.
I'm upgrading to 5 stars.

This evening I paired the headphones to my Amazon Fire TV. Paired immediately. Now I get the full sound of Game of Thrones, without waking my early to bed wife. Very important to me.

These paired easily.
Amazon Fire TV.
iPads. Both Pro and Mini 2.

Not paired.
5 year old IMac.
iPhone 6.

I have had problems pairing this IPhone with other devices, even with wi fi. I'm going to give the headphones a pass on the IPhone and my 2011 IMac. It paired very easily with the other devices.

I have the Apple Music subscription, and used the full spectrum of music to test these speakers.

Fantastic quality of music. Quality feel and appearance.

No Bluetooth through IMac
No Bluetooth through IPhone 6S. The B&O shows in my phones bluetooth display, it just won't connect at all.
Perfect Bluetooth connection on IPad Pro.
Perfect Bluetooth connection on IPad mini 2.

I have the Bose Soundlink. Lesser quality, but no problem connecting all my devices to Bose Soundlink.
I also have the Zvox 450 wireless/Bluetooth speaker, a Panasonic Bluetooth speaker, and a Braven Bluetooth speaker.
All work perfectly from my IMac and IPhones.

Realistically, while I consider Bluetooth critical for light walking/exercising headphones, as well as stand alone speakers, it is less critical for these studio type headphones that are best for home use. I'm content using the cord to connect my iPhone, while I relax on the sofa. I'm thoroughly enjoying them as I type this review on my IPad Pro using Bluetooth. I can't go over 3 stars because of the Bluetooth issues.

title: No automatic shut off. 5 stars for value.
text:
Fits perfectly. Doesn't seem to shut my IPAD off. They shut off soon enough anyway.
I purchased this because of the color selection. A black/dark cover can easily be missed on a chair or sofa, and sat on. I've had a couple near misses with black covers. I have a mini cover in red and it's easily seen.

Only thing I don't like is that when placed in a standing position on a counter, the home button is on the left. Feels awkward. I always place it by my right hand.
Still 5 stars for quality/price.

title: Surprised and very pleased.
text: This is my second.  This one was refurbished.  First was new.  Both work perfectly in my first floor brick condo.  All of the transmitting stations are on the opposite side of the building. Surprised and very pleased.

title: Astounded how well it worked in our ground floor brick condo.
text: We have Uverse.  Need these for Uverse outages.  We live on the ground floor in a brick condo.  We face north, and all the stations are west and south.  Our rabbit ears have to be constantly turned to get different stations.  I pinned the antenna to an inside wall behind the TV.  Astounded that it picked up every station possible.  No longer have to turn rabbit ears to different stations.

title: OEM, Brand New.  Performs perfectly.  Great deal.
text:
This is identical to the remote that came with the pricey 60 inch Samsung 3D TV I purchased 6 years ago. SN is not the exact same, but the remote is.

A few years back, I purchased this replacement remote for a less expensive 50 inch Samsung TV. Paired instantly. Works perfectly. Gave me functions the cheaper OEM didn’t,

I just purchased a new 2020 Samsung TV Q model. I am not a fan of the Samsung One remote that comes with the newer Samsungs. This remote actually gives me easier to use adjustment functions than the Samsung One remote. Performed perfectly. Paired automatically. A steal at this price. When using this remote, on new Samsung TVs, the labeling doesn't match the functions, so a bit of trial and trial. It’s much more user friendly than the new Samsung One remote, in getting to adjustment functions, going fast forward/reverse, and volume controls. Wish Samsung stayed with this great remote.

Thank you seller for selling these very reasonably priced remotes.

title: Nice improvement.  Perfect fit.  Feeling of security.  See installation video before doing anything.
text:
This is our fifth OtterBox, dating back to my I phone 3GS. This version has a major improvement,

Pros.
1. The plastic screen finally looks good. There was always a gap between the screen and the I Phone glass. That gave it a cheap look. That gap is gone. The plastic screen goes flush against the I phone glass and looks much better.
2. We have never dropped our phones, but this case gives us a great feeling of security. At $ 800 or so per phone, it's really cheap insurance.

Cons.
1. Installation and removal. We don't install these often enough to remember how to do it. The case comes assembled, and must be disassembled before use. Couldn't remember how to disassemble it. I finally went to You Tube to watch a video. Search term: "installing an OtterBox case." A comment to the video jogged my mind. It's like changing a bicycle tire. I used a miniature screwdriver to separate the rubber from the case at the corner. Nothing sharp. The rest of the rubber came off easily. The plastic parts separated easily enough. Place the phone inside, after cleaning both screens. Click the plastic pieces together, then place the rubber on. Keep massaging the rubber until it fully envelopes the plastic tightly. Had a few gaps at first.

2. Takes away the looks of the I Phone. Steve Jobs must have hated OtterBox.

3. Apple has a neat stand up charger for about $ 35. I bought one. OtterBox was late to the party with the OtterBox 6 plus, so I purchased the Apple 6 Plus leather case. Not much protection, but looks sharp. Worked great with the Apple stand up charger. Looked sharp together. Unfortunately, neither the OtterBox, nor any case that recesses the apple phone insert will work with this charger. Only a very thin shell will work with the charger. Back to using the regular Apple cord. I also have the OtterBox Strada for my I Phone 6. I like it. Although much thinner than the Defender, it doesn't work with the stand up apple charger either. Looks great. Many compliments. For those that don't like to carry a wallet all the time, the Strada has a pocket that contains both my license and one credit card. Great for trips to the gym. My wife has the Defender.

title: Poor choice of colors.  Very good quality item.
text:
Excellent fit. Look of quality.

The price is fair. Not happy with the choice of colors. Wanted a deep red.

I want bright colors on my covers because black covers are more likely to be misplaced, left on airplanes, or sat on, especially in a dark room.

title: A nice bluetooth speaker system, that has a CD player, an FM radio, and a slim profile.  There are cons.
text:
It's an attractive unit and has good sound. Features work well. Four stars on that basis. I got this primarily for listening to music and ballgames through my I phone, via bluetooth. I Tunes App available for this product. Worked okay.

Things I didn't like.
1. Not stable on the shelf. While trying to understand the controls, it fell backwards with a light touch. No damage though. If it's not wall mounted, suggest you place support behind it. I Was fiddling with the controls trying to find the pair button, since I couldn't find it on the remote. Later, I found the pair button on the remote. Should have better support for shelf use.
2. Remote control is confusing. Must be paired each time you want to play via bluetooth, even when you don't shut the unit down. Instead of a pair button, the button says play menu. The small pamphlet does explain the functions on the remote. Not intuitive at all. Read the pamphlet.
3. Paired to my I phone easily enough, once I hit the pair button (on the radio, as well as the remote).
4. Although it paired easily to my I Phone, my I mac couldn't find the signal.
5. Weak FM. A few stations were fine, but I only picked up about 1/3 of the stations available. Not a real problem since I will stream via bluetooth.
6. No AM. I expected AM.

title: A good travel case. Not for everyday home use.
text: This is a good case.  I wish it was slightly larger.  The zipper come very close to the mouse.  Careful when you close the zipper. This will protect the mouse.  Good for traveling.

title: My 5th Ivisor.  Guess that tells it all.  Apple 6 plus.
text:
My 5th I visor. Just traded in my 20 month old original mini for the Mini Retina. Peeled the Ivisor off the trade in and applied it to the new Mini with retina. Old screen looked new, and the Ivisor after being washed looks new. On the Iphone 5, I
just sold, I couldn't get the Ivisor off.

Warning. Did not work with my Iphone 6 Plus Speck case, but did work on my Apple leather case. The Speck case was just too tight and knocked it off every time. Returned the Speck case which had other issues.

It does cause a grid imprint on your Apple screens. Not noticeable when the phone is turned on. Grid imprint is permanent, like plasma burn in. If this bothers you, don't buy it.

title: More functional than the Apple Smartcase.
text: Our 4th Bear in Motion Product.  We have been satisfied with every one.  I recently picked up 2 Apple Smartcases at a great sale price.  My wife wants me to remove the Apple smartcases and put the Bear in Motion case back on.  Not as classy, but a better stand when you use the Ipad to play games while sitting in an easy chair. The Apple stand tends to collapse.

title: Amazing for the price.
text:
Amazing for the price. I don't understand how such a nice product can be sold for such low prices.

It's not a cheap item at all. Looks good. Functions very well.

Very satisfied.

Edited 2/7/2015

Price is substantially higher than it was when I purchased it.

At $ 5, with free prime shipping, , it was amazing for the price. Still a good item though..

title: Recommended. A very nice soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and easy to use bluetooth function.  Easy pairing.
text:
Very satisfied with the S3821 unit.

I purchased this at Costco's online site as it was on special for $ 30 off. That's why it's not shown as an Amazon verified purchase.

Overall excellent. A few issues and one dislike.

The digital optical cable provided was flimsy and didn't work.
So- I decided to try the Coaxial cable provided. It fit the Vizio soundbar, but not the Vizio TV.
Next, I went with the RCA cable, analog connection. Disappointing sound, but still better than my TV. Subwoofer was nearly nonexistent.

The next morning, I found an old high quality optical cable I had in storage. Connected immediately with noticeably higher quality sound. Also, the subwoofer sounded a lot better after the optical cable replaced the RCA cable.

My dislike is the led light system that you must use to find the right input. Finding the right input by sound is certainly possible, but I kept missing the connection by not waiting enough between presses. Look at the instructions provided. For optical cable, it's the lights out preceding the 4 lights to the right. Wish they just had a few lights with marked inputs.

Every time you go to bluetooth, the input automatically changes to the correct input, but you need to manually reset it for your sound input. Easy enough after a few times, but confusing at first.

Likes. VG sound. I previously had a Polk 5.1 system, but retired and we moved to a small condo. Had to give it away. So I have invested in HQ sound systems. With optical, subwoofer sound is noticeable and adds to the system sound. Where my Polk subwoofer sound output faced the floor, and boomed off the hardwood floor, this subwoofer sound is front facing, and relies on bouncing off the walls. That's better if you have carpet, and not hardwood. Voices are much clearer than my Vizio TV speakers. Hated using closed caption so often. That's why I got a soundbar.

Likes. Excellent and easy bluetooth pairing. Paired immediately to my Iphone 5. I have Amazon Prime, with free music streaming for many of my favorite songs. Pulled up Amazon music on my Iphone, picked a song and wow - great sounding music. Soundbar is worth the cost for this feature alone.

Likes. Subwoofer paired easily.

Likes. My Vizio TV remote controls the soundbar with a few exceptions. Need the soundbar remote to switch to bluetooth. Important functions are on the soundbar itself, if the remote breaks or gets lost.

Likes. Have it in front of the TV. Low enough that it doesn't interfere with the TV remote. Some soundbars would have covered the the Remote to TV receiver.

My deduction is for the LED light feature.

title: Sharp looking when installed on mini.  Good for non typist.  Not too good for typist.
text:
Edited review. Upgraded from 3 stars to 4.

Originally rated 3 stars due to somewhat unconventional keyboard.
We recently received the Belkin keyboard case for the larger IPAD, and it has become our constant companion. It really makes the IPAD easier to use, even when playing games.
After getting used to the larger keyboard, I returned to this keyboard to change my e mail addresses, passwords, and other settings due to a change in providers. Made those many changes effortless.
I guess it became a case of getting used to using this type of keyboard. Now recommended.

Original review.
It's not a protective case, but it looks sharp when used in the cover position, as well as when in use. Really dresses up the IPAD.

I'm a hunt and peck typist, so the keyboard was okay for me. My wife is very proficient at typing, and took an instant dislike to the keyboard layout and stopped using it. Doesn't do as much as I thought it would. Thought it would get me into the small captions on USA Today. The kind where your finger often presses the wrong article. Not for that.

Good posture position at my kitchen bar.

Would not work until I unplugged the USB charging connection. Not a big issue. I thought I had a defective keyboard.

It's a plus for anyone that types anything long on it. A big plus if you like to work on a kitchen bar.

title: Lightweight.  Usual Logitech quality.
text: USB connection to computer.  Very clear sound.  You can hear someone in your vicinity call you, which is what I want.  I use it at home, and it's very good for that purpose.  If you want total silence, you don't want this headset.  Long cord is a big plus.  I have been a Logitech fan ever since I had a warranty claim on a large purchase.  It was handled promptly and correctly.  The replacement was ordered while I was still on the phone.

title: My 5th Ivisor.  Grid complaints commented on.
text:
Had one for my IPAD 3, my mini, my 2 Iphones, and now one for my IPAD Air. They are great. No bubbles.

When I sold my IPAD 3, I forget I had one one, until I was cleaning it and noticed a grid effect. For Ipads, I recommend the XT (clear). For Iphones, which are often used outside, the AG (anti glare) is a good choice. Every other protector out there has given me frustration with bubbles.

A number of one star reviews mention the grid effect. When I sold my IPAD 3, I cleaned it and did notice a grid effect when the IPAD was turned off/asleep.
It is not noticeable when the iPAD is on and you are using it. So really - who cares? A bubble free screen protector with a grid effect that is only noticeable when the device is off.
Or - would you rather have bubbles?

title: Had to downgrade from 5 stars to 3.
text:
Update. This does not have a latch that allows you to stand it up for using it comfortably on a breakfast counter. My wife will be ordering another product. Out $ 20.
If that doesn't matter, buy this product.

Original review.

Closing cover puts the IPAD Air to sleep, opening it wakes it.

I didn't hear a snap on one of the corners when I inserted the IPAD, but it seems to be in securely.

Too many negative reviews on the real Apple Smartcover. Glad I purchased this instead.

title: Downgrade from 5 stars to one star.
text:
Update. April 12, 2014. 4 months after purchase.

I have unplugged the TIVO, will pay the monthly fees for the next 8 months. At least I'll save the $ 3 month cable card fees.

I got another tuner. The tuner works. I have 2 TIVOs and the new tuner works in the old TIVO, but not the new Roamio. It is a Roamio problem.
I now only get 4 standard def stations with the Roamio.

TIVO offered to replace the Roamio for a flat $ 49, plus shipping. I figure the total cost will be $ 75. I'm sure I will get a refurbished TIVO.
Decided it wasn't worth spending $ 75 to get a refurbished TIVO, which may or may not work. Since my ROKU 3 gives me Time Warner Demand channels, it is much less compelling to have a TIVO.

I'll keep the TIVO Premiere connected as it has a lifetime and is trouble free, The Time Warner demand capability of the ROKU 3 is a major threat to TIVO's existence.

I did purchase the TIVO on Amazon with the AMEX credit card which doubles the warranty. I called AMEX. Was told it would not cover the cost of the replacement ($ 49). Only would cover the labor cost, since parts were still under the TIVO warranty (90 days labor, 1 year parts). Since labor isn't separately charged, I'm not covered. Think that stinks.

Update. 105 days later.

Well warranty is up by 15 days. TIVO doesn't recognize tuning adapter. My old premiere works perfectly.
Time Warner spent 2 hours at my home today, swapped out cable cards and tried 3 different tuning adapters. It's a TIVO issue.
I bypassed tuning adapter for a direct hookup. Gives me half the channels. When my one year committment is up, I'll scrap it.

Only saving grace. When I called to cancel my 13 month old Premier XL, they offered me a lifetime for $ 199. I took it.
Do not recommend it Roamio. I was one of the original TIVO users. A 45 hour standard definition TIVO. Very disappointed.

Original review.

Integrated Wi Fi. It's about time. This is my 4th TIVO. Currently paying for 2 monthly subscriptions. Have been satisfied with all my TIVOs. Getting rid of the $ 90 Wi Fi accessory is a big plus. Our other TIVO is a 2 tuner Premiere XL that holds 300 hours of HD. We've never had it over 25% , so 75 hours is enough for us. Our other TIVO has been moved to the bedroom. We really needed at least a 4 tuner set. Two tuners may seem enough, but the stations are now playing it cute by ending programs at 9:01 instead of 9. This causes a conflict and forces you to cancel a show, or not watch a live station at the same time. It effectively reduces the two tuner to a one tuner. Before your TIVO arrives, go to your cable source (if you use cable), and get the appropriate cable card for a 4 tuner set, and tuning adapter. TW charges me $ 2.80 each for the cards. One for each TV. You need to call your cable company to activate and pair your cable card. TW has a great system, and it took only minutes to do. You also need to have an HDMI cable on hand, and a USB to HDMI cable. The kind that connects from your wired printer to your computer.

I also pay monthly, not lifetime. On my original TIVO, an old 45 hour SD job, I took a $ 199 lifetime plan after 2 months. Three weeks later, a nearby lightning strike wiped out the modem on my TIVO, and my computer. Yes, I did have surge protectors, as well as a $ 300 whole house surge protector sold and installed by my electric company. End of my TIVO, end of my $ 199 lifetime plan. TIVO offered no sympathy. So TIVO yes. Lifetime plan NO.

You cannot stream to your mobile devices with the 4 tuner TIVO, without adding accessories.

Added. You also need a short coaxial cable. My prior TIVO packages included every possible cable you may need. No longer. The power supply, remote, remote batteries, and the TIVO were all that were included. An added explanation on the usb needed. The standard side of the USB connection connects to the TIVO. The printer type side connects to the tuning adapter. I went to my junk box, and pulled an old printer cable out. It's not the older type with the large ends. It is a very small odd sided type that plugs in. The cable company should be providing these. Ask them for one.

title: Comfortable.  Works on computer and at gym.  Good enough sound quality.
text: Good sound quality.  Plugs into my Apple IMAC and immediately silences the computer, without going into systems preferences, as a USB headphone requires.  Also works at my gym.  Comfortable, and a long enough line.  5 stars to me.

title: Simple, yet effective.
text:
Box did not include a surge protector, as some had suggested. Did not get the cable cords that should have been enclosed. No big deal.

A very simple, well thought out, cable clutter management box that really hides most of the cable clutter. My surge protector fit in it easily, as well as its thick cord. Also my TIVO cord, TIVO wi fi cords w thick adapter, Roku cords, and everything else except the cable itself.
Room finally looks free of cable clutter after years of disarray.

title: Disappointed.  Does not cover drywall opening. Not for  modern plugs.
text:
I changed most of my outlets to the modern decora type, Lowes Aspire.

Screw feature is worthless for these outlets.

I planned on using these on the old fashioned outlets that I left in. I figured they would cover the plate, and I wouldn't need to update those plugs. Wrong. The plug in feature is near the very top of the Belkin. That means they leave a prominent part of the upper part of the old ivory plate showing. Remove the plate, and you have unfinished drywall showing (the cutout). You wouldn't know that by looking at the given size specs for the Belkin. Why don't these cover the entire plate?

I opened one package, and will return the other three.

title: Works fine.  IMAC to printer.
text: Have a wireless printer with 5 devices connected via Wi FI.  Have been having trouble with my main computer via Wi Fi.  This solved that problem.

title: An excellent product.
text:
We have anti glare (the AG), on our iphones.

We have XT (clear), on our IPAD 2 and IPAD 3. That's because we use our IPADS indoors, while we use our cellphones indoors and outdoors.

The XT is completely clear and invisible.

These Moshi Ivisor's install in seconds (okay, really about 2 minutes), with no bubbles.

Magnetic edges make it easy to remove and reposition, if you didn't center it perfectly.

How does zagg shield stay in business?

title: Awesome product.
text:
We purchased a condo and had our vacant house for sale.
Close the blinds or shades, set the timer, and it really looks like a TV is on.
Our neighbors thought we were staying there at night.

This is really a wonderful product that works.

title: Third Bear motion case we have purchased.
text:
Wonderful value.
Very inexpensive.
Looks nice.
Very useful and protective.

Purchased for an IPAD 2, an IPAD 3, and a mini. Different model numbers of course.

title: From another Ottobox defector.  Buy the grip model.
text:
Ottobox is a nice case. If you need rugged, it's the one to get.

The Speck is not as rugged, but gives you a more attractive package, with a nice grip on the case. The grip extends under the phone, and keeps it from sliding.

Easy to put on, but was more difficult than the Ottobox to get off. I googled. Slide a credit card under the case lid, starting near the top corner. Just google for instructions.
That helped a lot.

Bottom line. Since I do pay for Applecare Plus insurance , which covers drops, I wanted the more attractive case.

The black shows scratches. The white scratches, but doesn't show them as easily. The gripper (this model), reduces scratches.

Definitely get the Grip model.

title: Excellent product.  Why is it priced so low?
text:
This is my third Bear in motion product. Purchased one for my IPAD 3rd gen. Then purchased one for my son. Now I"ve just added an IPAD Mini to my collection, and immediately ordered another Bear in Motion product.

Perfect fit. Attractive. Camera hole just right. Protects both sides of IPAD. Very easy to take in and out of the case. Can't believe the low price.

I also use Moshi Ivisor on all my products. No problem inserting IPADs in case, with Ivisor on.

title: Puts my Time Warner DVR to shame.  Highly recommend.
text:
Purchased Oct 2012, from TIVO.

Easy installation. Fantastic video quality. Very responsive. THX seems to make the difference. Great software.

I had one of the newer TW DVRs (high capacity). My TW DVR was slow to stop, go back. Very frustrating. Myriad of issues. Poor software. Was my third TW DVR this year. TW, SW Ohio. TW, SW OH does have great service.

The video quality on the TIVO far surpasses the TW DVR. I guess that may be the THX quality. It comes with a useful pair of glasses that you use, in conjunction with both your TV remote, and an 8 minute TIVO certification video, to get a near perfect video setup (tint, color, contrast, brightness). It's not a gimmick. Use it. Takes 20 minutes of your time. TW gave me the M cable card and a tuner (hardware box, about 1/3 the thickness of the TIVO. Charges me $ 2.95 per month. Early in the setup installation, you must call your cable company to activate the card. A screen pops up to let you know when it's time. 30 minutes on hold. TW rep was great, and walked me through it. Call from the same room the TIVO is in. I called from a different room, and had to run back and forth to give her the info. Activated perfectly. I don't fully understand why I need the tuner box. Works without it. I did have a problem inserting the M card. Seemed too big. I used TIVO chat and they said they never heard of that problem. I let my wife try. She got it the first time.

I received the N wireless adapter as part of my package. I needed it as I have no landline, and my Apple Airport express does not have any ethernet connection. Totally wireless.
I did skip the instructions, and after much frustration, read them carefully. You must connect the wireless adapter directly to your computer ethernet port, to be accepted into your router. Then once it is accepted, remove it from the computer, and attach it to the TIVO.

Overall, excellent ease of installation, except for my errors. Flawless performance.

Edit added 11/01.

I found I was missing a number of stations. After calling TW and being transferred to their TIVO support division (which turned out to be TIVO), it turned out I didn't have the USB cable connected. TW didn't give me one, so I didn't know I needed one. It's not a standard USB, but the kind with the older printer connection on one end, and a standard connection on the other. Re-did setup, works fine.

title: Ease of setup for all Apple network.
text:
Just purchased this last generation product from an authorized Apple dealer for 1/3 of list.

Took minutes to install a wireless network. Didn't need to use the software disc.

I do have an Apple computer. Just went to applications on my IMAC. Then utilities, then Airport Express. It asked me to create a password and my network was set up.

It then took just minutes to add my IPOD, IPAD, MacBook Pro, I phone, Roku, and my two Apple TVs. A few extra few minutes to add my wireless canon printer.

Returning my wireless rental to Time Warner this morning.

Because of the ease of installation, I will buy the new generation if I have some of the problems others have complained about.

This is the older generation. Don't pay over 50% of the new generation price.

title: Wanted this to control my Apple TV.  It does.
text:
This is my first Harmony. I read enough setup complaints that I was prepared for a hassle. My wife wanted it - so.
Installation took about 3 hours. It became more of a Trial and Error process, than anything else. Yes. I would buy it again.
I did not have to call Logitech support, but did use their website support.

I set it up to control my Vizio TV, my Direct TV DVR, and my Apple TV.

The Apple TV was the hard part.

After googling and learning from the misfortunes of others, I read that you need to click "computer," since there is no Apple TV heading.
Eventually, after much trial and error, I added my TVs input choices (TV, Component 1, 2, HDMI 1, 2, etc). Before I did that, it wouldn't recognize my HDMI input, used for my Apple TV. I then changed the title from computer to Apple TV, by typing in the words, Apple TV. Easier for my wife.
Thought I had it, everything was working, then found the remote was turning my Apple computer on/off, every time I worked the control. Had to "unpair," it.

I love my Apple TV, but hate the tiny remote with the limited button selections. Constantly hit the wrong button when typing in passwords. The Harmony works great on the Apple TV.

Everything seemed to be a trial and error process. I followed the instructions, made changes, and finally got there. Allow yourself enough time, and there is a feeling of accomplishment. Just don't try to set it up before the big game.

title: Good for domestic use.  Key benefit is for overseas use.
text:
This item has been used to charge my iphone 3 GS in my auto, and at home.

Works perfectly. Good use of interchangeable parts.

I have not used it overseas. The greatest benefit is for travel.

If you don't plan on any foreign travel, then it is an overkill.

This is a nice item if you travel overseas and rent an automobile.
If you don't rent autos overseas, the benefit is lessened.

Still, the item deserved a 5 star rating in that it works as advertised,
and appears to be well made. Consider alternatives, and get the one
that best fits your needs.

title: Works well over my glasses.  Real 3D effect.
text:
We ordered this item to use with the flight control game option on the Ipad.

The movie theatre ones didn't work.

These worked well. They fit over my progressive lens glasses.

They gave the planes a 3D effect in that the planes appeared to be in the air. Make this option a nice touch.

My grandson will love them.

For the price. Recommend.

title: Great idea.  A little longer would have been nice.
text:
My surge protectors and power outlets are jammed up with large plug ins that take over the entire outlet.

This allows me to use the entire outlet. Just wish they were a little longer.

title: Very good, when the connection holds.
text:
Used this to connect my Apple Mac Book Pro to my speakers.

Worked well much of the time, but the connection wasn't the best. Often got no sound. Had to fiddle quite a bit with the connection.

title: Disappointed.
text:
The case arrived in perfect condition, and went on easily. Easy to remove. Looks good.
Fits in my Griffin stand. Like the dock idea. Keeps moisture out.

The problem.

It's just too slippery. Can slide right off any sloping hard surface.

I replaced it with my original Speck rubbery pixel, which grips very well.
Other issue. It didn't fit in the vertically shaped Speck IPAD carrying case. The one with the handle.
It didn't say it would, but come-on. Speck should realize most people like cases to protect their IPAD. My Pixel skin wouldn't fit in the carrying case, so I ordered this one. Slippery as it is, still wouldn't fit.

Waste of money all around. The Speck Pixel Skin is great though.

Slippery on surfaces and wouldn't fit in the Speck case. Great design team.

title: Grips well.  Excellent protection.
text:
I have one on my IPOD so I tried this one. Works just as well. Perfect fit.

I love the way it grips. No way it will slip off of anything.

The only negative. It will not fit into any type of IPAD size sleeve or case. It's just too grippy.

title: Snug fit.  Cloth texture.  Does not grip.
text:
Would be a 5 star if it would accomodate an IPAD that had a Speck case covering. That's the problem with these snug items. Most people have cases on their IPAD already. These are designed for naked IPADs.

This is a good enough item for the right purpose. I have 2 Speck Pixel Skin rubberized cases that grip very well.
