text: I have seen salespeople use this device to get a better fit with clip on earrings.  I have never seen one for sale.  I should have known-Amazon has it.

title: Good buy
text: Great size.  I can keep one for Musicals, one for operas, etc.  And yes, many of us still have CDs but don't want the plastic cases.  The cases come in a variety of sizes  I tried forever to find these in brick and mortar stores.  Of course, they were on Amazon

title: Perfect for reading in bed or in a darkened room.
text: I love this.  I can make it as bright or as dim as I need.  i can still make all the adjustments I need to the print size.  I am buying the new one coming out at the end of September

title: Better than soft
text: My husband sat on my first Kindle.  Not good for it.  So I went with the hard cover.  At least the Kindle now has a fighting chance

title: Tough To Install on the Samsung S8 Ultra
text: These are made well, the cutouts look good. I've put protectors on other devices so I'm not new to this, but wow, it's a pain for a large screen. Smaller than the Ultra, you'll do fine. It said if you get a small air bubble lift the corner slightly... um no, that's a bad idea, my first screen I barely lifted in the corner and the glass cracked. Next, okay second screen, done. Rubbing alcohol helps and being ever so light with your touch. Now it's been on, durable, no issues with the pen, movement with your finger or cover.

title: Way Too Tight Screen
text: First, the case is slender, seems like it's a great fit for my A7 Lite, no issues with the cut outs, color nice and looks good. The problem is that the case itself is hard plastic and once you get it on you literally have to break the case to get it off! I think they designed it so the plastic has a little extra gripping power, but I have never not once ever came across a case you have to break to get off. You start on one corner and normally you work your way around, not so with this, you cannot get it to budge at all, it's insane. You think your tablet will break. Also if you have a black screen, the case is so tight, it has a little white ghosting on your screen around the edges, not sure if this is going to cause long term damage to my tablet screen, but certainly not worth it. The case color and look of it is nice, but seriously they need to adjust the tightness.

title: Magnets Placed In A Good Spot
text: I purchased this case for my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6, it fit perfectly, no issues. I've had some cases that when you fold them back the magnet somehow interferes with the S-pen when taking Samsung Notes, like a part of the screen you are writing on seems to have bad spots or something. This case does have a couple magnets but it's placed on the edge down a little from the side buttons. If you try to write using the Samsung Notes there isn't any interference with them, not even when you fold the cover back. The trifold has a couple of options for sitting up, it is a slender case so it could fall flat if your moving it too much, but actually sits quite well when placed on a table or desk. I am looking for a basic cover, not bulky, I don't need heavy protection, so this works great for me.

title: Using It For My Laptop
text: In my neck of the woods we have had some pretty hot summer days and I have a laptop that seems like it constantly was running the internal fan. After blowing out any dust, it needed some extra help. I hooked this up and set it over the vent to my laptop and have been running it all day and night no issues. It's amazingly quiet and it does have an off switch, or high and low. I have no complaints with this little fan at all. If I had a gaming computer or tower I would buy two or more for sure, but the one works great for my size. I have my laptop on a stand (using my laptop, it folds back like a tablet) and set the fan between the back and the lid for good air flow. I think it was a good buy.

title: Works for Samsung Tab S6 and the S6 Lite
text: Fit both pens with no problems, writes just fine, easy to pull the old one out and insert the new one. The only suggestion would be to make sure when you put in the new nib you don't force it down too far.

title: Almost Perfect Fit
text: I purchased this for my small Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 Lite and it came with two screens, wipes, stickers. It has a small area (I used my towards the bottom) where a little notch is cut out so you have a place pull it up when you might need to change it. The size is just a hair short in width/height, but so little, it's not an issue or noticeably annoying. Use the stickers to get it lined up good first, and it's fine. No bubbles or any problems, followed the directions, easy. The A7 tablets screen always seemed to have a slight drag I hated, now, with this protector, no more drag. Awesome.

title: Loses Bluetooth Connection
text: These connect okay, and sound is fine, depends on your device as usual. Feels comfortable in the ear, I have small ears, but I wouldn't work out with these, they don't feel snug enough. I connect to any Bluetooth device just fine, but it has a very small amount of distance. If I walk into another room to get something it starts cracking up. No problems with other headphones, just these. Fine for sitting at your desk, but there are better ones out there for the same price.

title: Horrible Rattle, Noisy and Cheap
text: Perfect size for my desk, uses a USB-C, not expecting a perfect fan, but as soon as you plug it in, it makes a horrible noise and rattles so bad no matter the direction! It's absolutely a loud defective rattle, and sounds like the fan is cheap plastic going around against other cheap plastic. The fact that I'm not the only one complaining, the manufacturer obviously could care less. This should not sound like this, and there is no way to fix it. The fan at first look doesn't look bad, cheap plastic, thin, but with the way it works, they should be embarrassed. It really is that bad.

title: Using For A Couple Months
text: I wanted to really get some time with this mouse before reviewing. I have about a 7", right hand. I have the medium white, Lift mouse. Simple, easy to set up. I've had trigger finger and carpal issues, so I had to find a mouse that works. This is really great. With carpal tunnel you want to keep your wrist straight, not bent, this works. I use the the roller and all the buttons and it doesn't bother my fingers. I do think you should get the right size for you hand measurement, that's very important. I purchased a larger ergo mouse and it was not working, I gave it to my husband who has large hands, great for him. Also, this mouse you can use with 3 different devices, and has an off switch. I use it on my white desktop with no mousepad and it works great. Adjusted the speed in my windows settings a little, but no problems. I would recommend this mouse, just measure your hand to get the right size.

title: Can't See Writing
text: Not even fun to doodle on, let alone bad for the fridge. The colors are so dark and really not easy to see, the battery is fine. It's just a bad board. If you barely touch it while writing it does leave some marks, but your writing is just hard to read. The lighting is so dark not like the picture. Dry erase board is better. I wouldn't even give this to the kids. Not good.

title: Looks Good, Construction Good
text: I have a few different tablets and have quite a number of tablet covers. This is a really nice cover. I purchased the black, and it looks good, sewn well, nothing strange on the construction. I bought this to fit the Samsung A7 Lite, and all the holes line up with no problems. It fold just fine and the magnetic flap stays shut. One of my new favorite covers.

title: Works Great
text: It works, nice tight fit, and works with any 3.5 headphones I have plugged into my OnePlus 8T or Samsung Tablet.

title: Works No Problem
text: I have different 3.5 headphones, plugged into my phone or Tablet and have no problems. Fits nice and tight and works.

title: Easy to Sleep, Not Good For Snoring Spouse
text: These are probably the smallest and most comfortable earbuds to sleep with. They are small and a little soft, and flimsy when trying to put them in, however, they do stay in okay, just small. I am a side sleeper and have sensitive ears so I don't want anything protruding out, and these don't. I am average female height, so if you have large ear canals or are large in size, these may be too small. They are not noise canceling, they do muffle my husbands snoring, but he sounds like he is sawing logs so... I am happy these have a long cord and I purchased a small adapter for my USB-C on my phone and it works just fine. For the price, it's fine, sound quality is okay, but use for sleeping not working out.

title: Light, Adjustable, and Incredible Battery Life
text: I have quite a few different styles of headphones and some others on the ear. I was really surprised how lightweight these are, which I'm happy with, I don't want something putting a bunch of weight for 2 hours or more. Inside they are easily marked for Right or Left. Connects great to an adapter I use for my audio player, connects no trouble to tablets or phones or PC. Sound is good, I have your medium average female ears I guess, so it fits fine over the ears and I have had trouble in the past with some headphones being too large, with these you can set the adjustment down and they fit really well. If you are a person with a large head, you might want to keep looking, but these do adjust quite a bit so it's worth a shot. I get really good sound no matter the device, and podcasts sound so good sometimes it's sounded like they were in the room. The sound you get can be excellent if you have a device with a good equalizer. I have been really shocked how good the battery has been. If it's fully charged, I could listen to music on my phone for a couple hours, and check the percentage and it's barely used any battery. I go to plug it in and it charges really fast. I've had really good luck with these. I don't expect them to be like Bose or something, but for an average user, these are good.

title: Really Good Quality and Durable
text: This is the fourth case I ordered for my Galaxy S6 Tablet from this Infiland brand. Every one has been well made, no problems with the look, the quality at all. I have ordered a few because I wanted some options of colors, and have tried ordering from other brands and there is no comparison. Infiland makes theirs really well and I did recommend them to a family member and they too said for the tablet they had they were really happy. It closes well, no problems with pen or stitching, and it flips so you can easily watch movies, folds back no problem, and it closes nicely to protect the pen when your not using it. Not getting paid for my review, if it's a good product (and I'm picky) then I will definitely give credit.

title: Can't Flip It Back
text: The cover is cute, not as vibrant colors as the picture, but okay. The sewing is fine and the tablet fits fine. The problem is when you close the cover, the home page on your tablet goes black, which is fine if you're not using it you don't have to click the screen on and off. BUT when you flip it back like your going to read your tablet in portrait mode, it causes your screen to also go black. If you flip the cover back to read, it goes black then it's useless unless you want to always hold it open like a book. If you only need to use this cover with your tablet in landscape mode, then your ok.

title: Holds My 10.5 and 8.0 Samsung Tablets
text: I wasn't confident in the stability, but after checking the directions it tells you to twist it into an 'S' shape pattern and it makes it more stable. It seriously does. Also when you put the tablet in, place it in portrait mode first, then turn to landscape mode. My smaller 8" tablet was easier than my 10.5 with two hands, but they are both completely stable in it. It has some small padding to protect the edge, must for me, and there is padding where you tighten and attach to the desk. The part that you attach to the desk is super simple, twist clockwise, very easy and I have arthritis. It is stiff (which is a good thing). It took me very little work to get it into the shape and height I needed. Once the tablet is in you can pull it down a little or tilt it up pretty easy. I use this mostly for viewing while it's in this. I tap here and there through videos, it seems a little springy in the movement, but feels secure and if you hold it while you need to flip or something, no big deal. If you need something where you are wanting to pull it towards you or push it away with use, get something with a different arm. I think over time this would possible get too loose with constantly pulling on it. For the way I need to use it, it's great. Gets it off my desk so I have more surface area.

title: Way Better Than Expected
text: I like having a pair of wired headphones in the house, nice to not worry about having to charge your headphones. I was purposely looking for headphones that are more flat on the outer part, so it makes it a little more comfortable to sleep with, and also use with multiple devices. Not expecting much in the way of sound, often the wired headphones have more treble and are usually good for audiobooks, or voice, more than music. I hooked these up with an adapter for a couple of different tablets, phone, and laptop. They sounded different on different devices, makes sense, so my phone, wow awesome bass, in a wired headphone? Okay, cool, and on my tablets with turning off my equalizer, the sound was crisp and clear and still had some bass, but great too for podcasts. I like how snug these fit in the ear, but I changed out the little plastic ear covers for some others I have, and I have to say, that snug fit makes them much better with more noise being filtered out. The longer cord is good too. So surprised how good these sound, and for the price, good deal.

title: Rotation Works, Quality Poor
text:
I am using the rotating case for my Galaxy Tab S6 and the cover rotates and works in landscape and in portrait view. The case isn't bad, I ordered the black. However I have a couple complaints; the frame you put the tablet into... it is a plastic frame, and the company decided it was a good idea to add a thin looking fabric (glue on) around the edge to make it look better. They should have left it off, one corner of the fabric was not glued properly and cut too short, and the fabric is not glued down. There is a gap or opening between the plastic and fabric an if I glue it, the fabric is still too short, and it's not going to look better or make it less vulnerable to tearing, very tacky looking, quality control anyone?
Second complaint is the elastic band. There is no cover over the S Pen on back, now if you close the case (pulling the elastic over the case) to not have if fall open in your bag, it covers just about 1/4th of the S Pen on back and so it's not keeping the pen from getting lost if it gets knocked around. Placement is bad.
Third, the lid has a permanent cup looking ring embedded into the cover, because obviously there was another rotating case (plastic ring part) with something heavy setting on it.
So, could've been better, rotation works, but quality is poor.

title: Have a Few Infiland Cases All Are Good
text: I ordered the white and black marble and for some reason received a marbled one, but the background is rose blush color (matches my rose Galaxy Tab S6) and darker rose spots. I must say even though it wasn't right, I love the color. I  didn't know they had this color, but pleasantly surprised. I have a few of the Infiland cases and every single one is sewn well, closes properly, works well with my S6 pen and is more durable than many other thin cases. I also recommended Infiland to a few and they are pleased with theirs too. Wish they had more color or design choices, but I seriously believe they make the best covers and the quality is always good. Cool.

title: Sloppy Quality Control
text: The case closes and it doesn't line up very well. Standing up is okay, but you have to tuck it into the back flap to hold properly. The border that holds the tablet came and looked a little deformed, and sure enough you put in the tablet and some areas were not tight or smooth on the tablet but like the border was stretched out in certain spots. I really was hoping it could be used regardless, but like others, forget it if you want to draw with the S Pen. This is not the first Fintie cover I have purchased and the others have had issues to. I will be staying away from this band, sorry Fintie.

title: Been Using For a Bit
text: The case is put together fine, fits my Samsung Tablet S6 no problems. Flips fine for using in landscape. Pen stays in well. The only gripe is that where the volume buttons are it is covered with plastic and it it is fairly flat leaving it a little hard to push the volume up or down or the power. Other than that, I have no complaints, would buy it again.

title: Good and Not So Good
text:
I had previously purchased a case like this almost completely identical, only by a different brand name. I wanted another case, I like the color choices from this company and they said they were made in the US so I thought it would be okay. The item 'denim' I ordered was a bit more grey not quite like the picture, but that's okay.
I purchased the one for Galaxy Tab S6.
The good things; it has the right cut outs, feels durable on the outside to protect the tablet, flips open with 3 lines on the inside cover to adjust using the tablet in landscape more. The materials used seems okay as well, sewed well, no loose ends.
The not so good; unlike the previous case (from the other company) this one has a little looser binding. When they cut the inner cardboard they cut it a little too short and that leaves a little extra fabric on the binding causing it to shift the tablet so it doesn't fold over tight like a book. It's usable but very annoying when you close it and it doesn't look straight. More like a torn binding on a book when you close it. The other issue is the camera opening. Yes it does have the right cut out, however, the height of material cuts off a corner in your camera shot, it looks like a cornered vignette on the photo. Having to remove the cover to take a picture is also annoying. It's not a bad case, just needs a few adjustments.

title: Clear Sound, Some Breakups During Calls
text:
The packaging, quality and sound I have no complaints. Charging was easy, no problems pairing with 4 devices. The bass was better obviously on a device that has a better sound system, but very clear. I have a variety of devices all with different sound profiles, and these sound good on all of them. It comes with a medium tip already on and the fit is comfortable and blocks out noise pretty well, probably because of the design. When you put the earbuds in it snaps (magnetic) to charge. You don't have to close the lid to charge. It has lights that tell you when it's connecting and charging. The charge box is good if you need to take it and charge your phone too. Controls are good and not too hard to learn, you just need to tap once on the right to increase volume and tap on the left bud once to volume down. I thought it might be super sensitive and even fell asleep with them on, but no problems with it accidentally changing volumes. I did try using them for phone calls and the person said that they can't hear me very clearly, and sometimes it breaks up even when no one is moving, not sure why since I can hear them clearly. I do own two of Soundpeats wireless headphones and have no complaints, that's why I thought I would try these. The clear sound I get from these are really great, and with the phone break up during calls could be the weather or my area but I am seriously glad I bought these and have already recommended them.

UPDATE: After playing around with these, my biggest complaint is when I went walking, one ear would cut in and out, like bad connections, so I disconnected, popped them back on the charger and reconnected and then good for a few minutes and no good, kept happening. Okay if you sit in one spot in the house, lousy when you are exercising outside. They are pretty testy when trying to stay connected too. I live in apartments and in an urban area, so these can't handle it. I don't have any problem with other wireless headphones, just these.

title: Comfortable and Design is Good
text: I have small to medium hands and it still works okay. If it was a little lower in height it would be perfect, because the palm of your hand has to sit up a little higher in order to reach the back and forward buttons on the thumb side. It's comfortable and easy to move around. The wheel scrolls well and the back and forward buttons are nice too. If you have not tried an ergonomic mouse this is a good one, and the price is a good deal too.

title: Ends Tight and Length Good
text: So the cord itself is clear with the visible braided cord inside. Durable, doesn't get twisted up and the end plugs in to devices nice and snug. We'll see how long it holds up, but so far I could use another one.

title: Lightweight, Little, But Works
text: I have an old VISIO and it fired right up, no problems. It's lightweight and feels kinda cheap but hey as long as it works.

title: Middle of The Road
text: Trying to write a review on these is a little tough because I there is some good and not so good. I think the quality of the materials is fine, the end pieces have magnets in them so if they are hanging around your neck they stay together so you won't lose them. Stays in your ears pretty good, but not really noise canceling at all. The on/off button, connecting and volumes are all good and easy to use. The range is not very good past 15-20ft or walls in an apartment if you move a lot. Fine if you keep your phone with you. The rectangular pieces (volume button/mic) that sits around your neck feels a little weighty and it's fine if you are just sitting at your desk, but not for working out. It pulls, and moves and you have to do a lot of readjusting. Sound quality is not terrible, but not great. 1 being the worst, 10 being the best; Sound 5, noise canceling, 4, comfort, 6, distance, 3, design, 4. These would be okay to have as a second pair if you are stationary, listening to audio books.

title: Simple and Works
text: I have mine hooked up to external speakers , TV (older model) and gaming system. It was actually easy to set up, HDMI and regular speaker wire capable. It is heavy duty, not cheap feeling. It has FM radio with ability to set favorite channels, and the system has sound options (Dolby, concert, etc..). My volume works with TV remote or use the one that comes with it, but it's not really necessary. It has a headphone jack on the front (I use a Bluetooth adapter and works with wireless headphones that way). That will then turn off the outer speakers, great for listening to a movie late at night. My only complaint, wish you could just use wireless headphones without an adapter. The ability to connect your phone up or tablet/laptop using Bluetooth to listen to your music through it is very cool. When switching inputs on your TV to your game console it automatically says gaming and remembers your sound style choice (Dolby, concert, etc..) and when you switch back to Media, TV  or whatever it does everything smoothly. Really can't complain, and I think the price was pretty good. I have a couple old box speakers hooked up and it make them sound good.

title: Loud and Lightweight
text: Easier than digging in your purse for mace, take all the help we can get with so many scary things going on in the world. You pull the top pin (like a grenade) and it sounds like a super loud emergency exit door just opened up. Put the pin in and it stops. The pen is not loose so it stays in good and it would definitely surprise an attacker. Or just set it off to attract attention. It's light so you could put it on your key chain or hook it to a zipper on a purse or backpack. I took one and gave the other two to family members.

title: Great
text: No complaints, works great

title: More Durable than Expected
text: Fit's perfect on my Samsung Galaxy Tab S, and I have been using it for a while. The cover still looks new and the magnetic clasp still going strong. I flip this over to read recipes while cooking, or watching movies, and it stays up great. Not thick and bulky it is more slender, but looks good and is durable. Not sure about other styles but very happy with this. I would have expected to pay more. And it can rotate which is great for a smaller tablet, not so much needed on this big tablet, but cool feature. A friend ordered a smaller one for the 7" and they are happy with the quality of theirs too. Husband complained they need more guy colors but he likes his too.

title: Nice!
text: Great quality, no feathering problems, and doesn't clog, very happy with Private Reserve inks. The Black Cherry is true, black cherry.

title: Great!
text: Works great, took a minute to set up, but having 5.0 and 2.4 options is great, works really well in my apartment surrounded by networks. Security is good and works well with my cable company (unfortunately Comcast).

title: Great
text: Great no problems

title: I Am Picky And Happy With This Monitor
text:
I rate it at 4 stars because I think the stand is not so hot. Okay, just kind of plastic and no movement.
When I read reviews about the stand I ordered a wall mount the same time I ordered the monitor, and glad I did. The mount I ordered works perfect and I got it here at Amazon. "Mount-It Single Arm Articulating Flat Panel Monitor Mount for 13-30 Inch" Sold by Value Max and Fulfilled by Amazon. Sturdy and easy to put up. Love the movement options on this arm!
The monitor is a little wider than my previous one and I understand we have to just get use to new things. I like it, and I am picky. I wanted a monitor that would work for photos, and art, I need good coloring. This has good options for color adjustments, but I also use my Video Drivers AMD Control Center and then I can tweak it as needed, but that's personal preference. I did have to turn the brightness down, but again everyone is different. I think everyone's color preferences are a little different, but your video card can make colors look different too.
The monitor looks good and not cheap like I was concerned about. Has a black glossy plastic frame, and the screen is very clear, matte finish which I prefer. Lightweight enough for mounting and I didn't want to spend a fortune. I was pleased it came with cables, but I use my own DVI cable and has HDMI for those want it.
I was concerned about ordering a monitor online and having it shipped, so I made sure I purchased this sold from Amazon, not anyone else. Glad I did, box was in good condition, packaged well, no weird pixels and monitor was in great condition.
I wondered if the price was too low and I would be better off buying a more expensive name brand, glad I didn't waste my money. I am really happy so far and would recommend this.

title: Great Movement!
text: This is not too heavy, good quality and moves easily. I use it for my 22" monitor. Goes up to 100mm. Works great, with two adjustment knobs I can swing my monitor screen flat centered on the wall, pull out straight, out to the right or left, and adjust the face of the monitor tilted upwards or downwards. Sturdy, mounted on the wall really easy.

title: Fast  shipping. Snug fit.

text: Much better quality than the original IBM PC camera available on the laptop.  Picks up especially well in areas which are dark.

title: Different than original keyboard.
text: Unlike the original keyboard. Fake red dot mouse inclusion. Overall good quality but unlike the original keyboard. Overall I’ll give it four out of five stars.

title: Excellent Product
text: Bought this for my wife.  Did not know what to expect.  Extremely easy set up.  Great camera with alerts when packages are delivered etc.  At times there is some connectivity issues with the app for iphone in areas that wi-fi is limited.  Other than that, great product.

title: Excellent value....Crisp video. Relatively easy to install.
text: I bought the 4 camera package from Cromroc on Black Friday.  Relatively easy to install.  The most difficult thing is learning how to place your cameras in that it can be run as a wireless system.  The trick I found is spacing your cameras relatively equal distance apart.  You have to also work with the sensitivity settings for each camera.  They are very sensitive.  If you dial it down to 20-30%, things such as insects and raindrops will not set off motion detection as much.  The app which work with the system works well- IPPro 3.  Push notifications are sent to your phone when there is motion detection as well as being able to see a live feed at any time.  I utilize a 3 TB SATA drive which provides plenty of space for continuous recording.  I am curious as to how they stand up over time.  They appear to be built very well for both outdoor and indoor use.

title: No Issues.  Great aftermarket replacement for my Apple Lap Top
text: No issues.  Works well with my old Apple laptop.  For an aftermarket product, good quality.

title: Four Stars

title: Great Improvement Over Previous Generation Fire Stick

Much more responsive than the previous generation FireStick- a great improvement.  You ask Alexa about the weather and not only get a voice narrative but a visual for your local weather or any city that you specify.

Later I was gifted a T3i that for all intents and purposes is basically the same camera. Images were a bit sharper... no, a lot sharper even, though they shouldn’t be. The same sensor and processor can be found in both cameras.

Finally I got around to trying this out one night when I couldn’t sleep. I started off on the T2i figuring “if I mess up, it’s just my backup camera” but let me tell you... the cleaning process was a breeze. I shot a few practice shots after, and it was sharper than my T3i, so I cleaned that one up too! Now both cameras are shooting nice and sharp, and I’m a happy man. If you’re looking for an affordable kit to maintain your aps-c camera, look no further, this it the one!

title: Great price, Better Storage.
text:
Do you have a MacBook Pro with a 12gb SSD in it? Of course you do, the 1tb or 2tb models are almost as expensive as a black market kidney. Why not expand your storage the most portable way possible? You can install apps directly to this drive, and only plug it in when you need to access them. It’s not the perfect solution, but until someone makes a memory dock to stick to the bottom of the MacBook, this is one of the better options out there. Plenty fast, and a decent amount of storage.

I have my entire 90+gb Logic Pro X installed to one, and I save all of my projects to it as well, which helps keep my 5gb MacBook Pro SSD nice and clear.

I miss the days when they let you install your own upgrades on Macs.

Anyway, what is there to know? It’s a flash drive. It works with USB-C or USB 3, it gets the job done, and the price is right. Buy a bunch of them.

title: $7 could save you hundreds.
text:
This tool set is almost perfect! I’ll start with a little background... I am tech savvy for the most part, and I refurbish my own electronics, as well as stuff for friends and family from time to time. My MacBook Pro was bogged down by a “feature” known as thermal throttling. When older thermal paste dries up, it fails to conduct heat as well, so performance takes a nose dive in favor of preservation.

I’m not entirely sure if Apple actually does this servicing upon request, or not, but I honestly wouldn’t think that they do. So, after figuring out what was going on with my laptop, I rolled up my sleeves, brought out the few electronics tools I had around, and proceeded to gut my MacBook. Bad idea. You ever hear that saying about not bringing a knife to a gunfight? It went about that well.

Long story short, I busted a clip off of the motherboard that would have held the keyboard ribbon cable in place, and you can’t really just replace the clip on a motherboard, you have to replace the entire board. If I had this tool set in time for that repair, I could have saved the cost of replacing the board.

That said, these arrived in time for me to do the motherboard swap, and before I did (managed to upgrade to the i7 processor from the i5, a mild boost in performance I’m sure.) I made sure to once again, remove the heat sync, and remove the old thermal paste, replacing it with fresh TG-7. My geekbench scores now come in above what is average for the i7 version of my MacBook Pro. Above average is virtually unheard of. It’s like a brand new machine.

But these tools, if you attempt to do a repair without them, you could end up costing yourself a few hundred extra dollars. Learn from my mistake!

My only negatives here are for the durability and sturdiness, because I feel like the plastic spudger thing is definitely going to break eventually at the sharp pointy side. I don’t trust the plastic much. Other than that, the kit is well worth it, and every Mac enthusiast who plans to repair their own machine should really have it.

title: Great tablet, Even better price.
text:
If you're looking for an excellent tablet and e-reader at a great price, look no further. While there are things that it lags with (like playing the Pokemon trading card game, which last I knew, needed to be sideloaded) it does a lot of other things really well. Great experience with watching videos, and reading comics or manga.

If you're into hacking your devices, this tablet (well, the 2015 version that I have) does a really good job of running a clean Nexus rom, which gives you a stock Android experience, and access to the Google play store. I have to say, that was probably the best thing I've done with it so far.

Expandable storage allows you to carry an entire library with you on the go to make sure that you will never run out of things to do. I keep a 128gb micro SD card in mine, but I wouldn't be surprised if you could slot in a larger card, even though it's only officially rated for up to 128gb.

What i'd like to see change for the 2018 version (assuming they do a revamp) would be full 1080p resolution, a snapdragon octacore processor clocked around 2ghz (my free ZTE Blade Zmax has one, and I can't imagine it would be too expensive for them to use it in the fire tablet as well, if even free phones have them now) and 2-3 gb of ram. If Amazon would just do these 3 little upgrades, this tablet would be unbeatable. I wouldn't even mind a mild price bump ($70-80 instead of $50) if these upgrades happened. I would also like to see a future version either running full stock Android OS, or released with the option to unlock the bootloader somehow, to facilitate diy development and cutom roms. But I know that's just asking too much.

If you're looking for a great tablet at an even better price, the Fire 7" is a great choice.

title: "It's not you, it's me... okay well, it's both."
text:
Let me be honest here. My post is very subjective, but I'm going to post it as honestly as possible for the benefit of those like-minded people.

The unit itself is really great. Ultimately I returned it because I was not working out for me. It's as simple as that.

The more complex nature of my unhappiness may come from the fact that I am a long-time Apple product user who really, really tried to go beyond the Apple brand. The Kindle Fire is a GREAT device - but when replacing an iPad it really didn't compare for me. Things sync'd seamlessly with my Apple products, but not the Kindle (I didn't expect it to, but I did miss that). I couldn't download some Apps that were unavailable for the Fire but available to other Droid interfaces. It took a bit of relearning how to navigate the Kindle, but that was fine (and very easy to do). The image was crisp, the response quick, the actual unit solid. It felt nice to hold in my hand, and the Origami case was a nice touch. But when push came to shove I ended up returning a perfectly good device because I just wasn't in love with it. I missed many of the features and uses that came naturally from my iPad. I may need to spend a bit more to get it, but if it is what truly works well for me without any sacrifice (other than about 200 dollars more)... then perhaps I should just save up and get the iPad.

It's embarrassing to admit all this, but it's true. I thought switching would be easy. The reviews are great - and the unit itself is truly great. But it just wasn't the right match for me and for my purposes. I'm heading back to the iPad.

title: Something I Missed in All the Reviews
text: OK, it's easy to use and works great!  Now, the rest of the story:  When you use it, it identifies itself as headphones.  Seems ok, but then you leave the house with your phone and you will miss every call and audible notation because it thinks it is still connected to headphones.  The solution is simple -- you must go into your phone settings and select bluetooth>Esinkin BT Adapter>Forget this Device.  That's right, every time you want to use it you have to pair it and then Forget it when done.  Simply "disconnecting" it only lasts a few seconds and your phone returns to headphone mode.  Now, if I am all wrong about this, please correct me and let everyone else know.  This would be great for a retired phone you use as your music box and stays connected to your sound system all the time.  But for an active phone, it's a PIA.

This viewer is the most awesome accessory I have added in recent history.  I have Nikon D750 bodies and if you also do make sure you order the correct Hoodman because it is critical it covers edge to edge. title: Worth it
text: OK, it's pricey.  OK, it's a fixed lens.  I shot about 200 pictures around a golf course and duplicated every shot with my Nikon P7100.  The P7100 is an awesome camera and the 28-120 effective zoom range is handy, but for this outing I set the Nikon to the same focal length of the Fuji, about 35 mm.  I shot landscapes with sky dominate, with land dominate, water scenes, close ups of flowers, I shot using both standard and vibrant settings, I used the flash fill for portraits of my wife in full sun, half shadowed face, and full shadow.  Result:  I like the Fuji color and details in the shadowy areas better.  I like the controls better on the Fuji.  I like the old time move-yourself-to-get-the-right-composition mode of the Fuji fixed lens rather than the just zoom in or out of the Nikon.  You can set it to aperture preferred, shutter preferred, or programmed -- nothing different than on the Nikon, EXCEPT if you go aperture preferred (my preference in order to control depth of field) you move the aperture ring on the lens mount and you set the shutter speed dial to "A" (for Automatic); or if you prefer shutter preferred you set the aperture ring to "A" and rotate the shutter speed dial. On the Nikon, if you go manual or semi manual, the control rings are in places that don't make sense -- in the traditional old style sense.  OK, I'm an old guy and have been doing landscape photography since the early 70's, originally with a hand held light meter.  Now my main landscape camera is a Nikon D700 and 11 lenses and all the "modern stuff."  Still, the Fuji is a neat camera and I felt "closer" to photography by using it.

title: Nice on a Budget but Quick Mount May Lack Long Term Toughness.
text:
NOTE: I am reviewing the BR268 which is no longer available and I believe thie BH0 is the replacement model. My concern is with the quick attachment/quick release mechanism which looks exactly the same. It's a great feature to just pop your camera into the quick mount and have it automatically lock in place and to remove, just squeeze the two levers together and turn them 90 degrees and the camera is free. Mine worked great for a while and then the spring loaded pin (which is pressed down by the base mount on the camera as you load the camera thus setting the locking levers) stopped springing back upon release of the camera. It is still usable but not at all quick or convenient.

During manufacturing the pin and spring are somehow stamped into a hole in the mount with no opportunity for future maintenence. I ended up drilling through the rear of the mount into the pin cylinder, freeing the pin from the backside, replacing the spring, and closing the hole with a stub bolt and now it works ok. I believe the pin was stuck because, as mentioned above, I frequently "popped" the camera into the quick mount and I have probably nicked the pin causing it to stick. If that is the case, the manufacture should make a baseplate and or pin that are tougher and virtually indistructable. I don't want to be mounting the camera on the tripod with the same semi-gentleness I mount my lens to the camera.

In addition to that, there is too much play in the quick mount itself unless you take extra effort and push the quick release lever firmly shut. Automatic locking alone doesn't do it. Once locked in place the base plate still has a little play in it.

Still, you pay for what you get. I only paid $38 for this ball head. I replaced it with the Manfrotto 496RC2, another "low end" ballhead but twice the cost of the BR268. The Manfrotto is very solid and the friction knob makes fine tuning of the camera position easy.

I'll end this on a good note: The Benro is very light when compared to the Manfrotto 496. If you are lugging your tripod into the outdoors you will appreciate the lighter weight of the Benro.

title: Great Value
text:
After retiring my well used and beat up Welt tripod after 35 years of field use and began looking for a new tripod I was shocked when I saw the prices of medium to light weight tripods for 35 mm camera use. $200-$300 -- are you kidding me? I like quality and long term durability (as was my Welt, but...no longer made) and am usually willing to pay for it. However, I decided to give this relatively inexpensive Benro a try and couldn't be happier. I've had it in the field 8 times already, setting it up in water, on muddy slopes, in freezing temperatures and it performs very well for me. The legs extend easily. It is firm. It is light, and with the attachment of a shoulder strap is comfortably carried. I also purchased the Benro BR268 Ball Head for it and it too is of high quality and excellent functionality. This is a great value.

----
Update March 2012. This may be moot, as Benro no longer makes this model. It has been updated to the A0580F as far as I can tell. Anyway, this inexpensive aluminum tripod has performed great in the field. I've done my best to beat it up everywhere from a hike to the bottom of the Grand Canyon to sloughing through the Everglades. It works fine. The Benro Ballhead BR268 is another story. The quick attachment/release spring loaded button/pin now longer works and the entire mechanism has too much play in it. I only paid $38 for it. So I upgraded to a Manfrotto 496RC2 which works wonderfully, smooth and tight. As I was researching ballheads I checked out tripods. Nothing comes close to the value, portability, and toughness of this cheap Benro. There isn't anything out there with the stability and light weight of this Benro. At 2.4 lbs it is lighter than all Carbon Fiber tripods of the same relative size costing $250 and up.

Note to reviewer who complained that Amazon.com should have better details on the size and weight. He is right, but I think most people do the research and find that information elsewhere, then come back to Amazon.com to buy. Benrousa.com is easy to find and has all the data you could want.

title: Exceeds Expectations
text:
This is a fantastic external drive that exceeds expectations! This is a massive amount of storage, in a quiet professional looking designed enclosure that with USB 3.0 connections makes for an incredible value to expand the capacities of an existing PC while adding backup capabilities for recovery purposes.
CrystalDiskMark test shows the drive's sequential read at 213 MB/s, sequential writes at 198 MB/s which is really fast for a platter based hard drive (even faster than some if my WD Black internal SATA drives). The random reads are also very quick at 27MB/s for 4Kib and random writes of 2.3 MB/s are beyond my expectations as these speeds are faster than some of my USB thumb drives. The drive can be placed flat, or on its side and the heat is passively vented from the rear of the unit. The blue LED blinks when data transfers are taking place and when PC is off the light is also off to not add additional lights to a room. The drive comes with backup software Backup Now EZ which is fairly intuitive allowing for scheduled backups of specific files and even an entire PC. I've not had to do a restore yet from this software's backup so it may be more useful to do a windows image to the drive and then restore from that. I would highly recommend this drive for anyone in the market for an external USB 3.0 drive with large capacity looking for fast drive speeds. Very satisfied with this product and I will be looking to Toshiba for future storage needs.

title: The Camera you didn't know you needed!
text: This thing is pretty cool. There have been a number of times where I have missed a photo opportunity because I didn't have my phone or was too slow to take it out. With the ZAGG Now Camera, you can have a lanyard around your neck just ready for those situations. Now there are some limitations to this camera, specifically as it relates to lower light situations. There isn't a flash on the device and as a result lower light photos might come out more blurry than a picture that is taken outside in bright sunlight. Now it takes fast photos and has 4gb of storage so that will allow you to quickly take as many pictures as you would like. With the Now Cam, it also doubles as a bluetooth portable speaker and microphone so you can have it paired and on standby to take calls by pressing the play button. The speaker is loud! Voice calls can be clearly overheard and depending on who you are talking to might be too loud. Not sure if there is a way to turn it down but with the lack of options on the physical device I'd say probably not. Playing music via bluetooth is also a nice feature and sounds really good for what it is, especially when compared to many speakers on phones. The camera creates it's own wifi connection to allow you to transfer photos to your phone so you can see what you have taken. I had some initial issues getting the app to connect on an android phone, but after those initial errors it somehow corrected itself and is now working. I've not transferred any videos yet, but the photo transfer was pretty quick. Overall I'm really impressed with this device.

title: Solid NAS for small business, less so for personal use.
text:
I feel like Buffalo has created a quality product with the TeraStation, but some of it's features get in the way of it being a really intuitive product. From a hardware perspective, the processor is quite capable and is really responsive. While small it is larger than comparable 2 drive NAS devices, but I can say that it is quiet and fairly unnoticeable in that regard. The drives included are WD Red 1 TB drives in RAID 0 for redundancy providing approximately 900GB of network storage (which would seem small by today's standards depending on the data / number of pc's backing up to the drives).

Accessing the configuration of the device is easy to do either from the desktop software itself or by accessing the NAS from a browser and typing in the IP address which is displayed on the LCD screen (a feature I really like). The login has given me some trouble in that after typing in the admin password or user password I am often met with user authentication failed, but if I refresh my browser I am able to access the settings and it indicates the correct user.

That being said, the user interface is pretty standard and is broken up into appropriate categories from File sharing to drive management, web services and backup. I've been able to add users and folders pretty easily, and have been able to set up time machine backups to the system as well.

Transfer speeds to the NAS were approximately 75 - 80 Mbps using gigabit network connections, copying over 5gb of files across the network.

There is the capability to run a web server off the device as well as a mysql server, which I have not had enough time to test out but seems fairly robust. There are built in DLNA capabilities to allow for sharing of media files across devices that support it, as well as the capability to create an iTunes server as well as a print server.

Overall with my limited experience with the Terastation I have been pleased but there have been hiccups. I would recommend this device for use in a small business / office setting, but for personal use something more like a Synology NAS or a WD Mycloud might be more appropriate. Additionally the 1 TB drives will have limited long term capabilities as storage requirements continue to rise, and would almost necessitate the need to purchase at minimum the 2 - 2 TB drive version of the device.

title: Great compact router unit for when traveling
text: When travelling, does a great job of creating a secure personal network behind either an Ethernet connection or as type of wireless repeater which can connect to a hotel wifi network and then create a private network off of that. The range on the unit is pretty good considering the lack of external antennas, but it's limited in the respect of what you will likely use it for which is a single large room without many walls. Once you start going through walls the unit's speed will begin to decline. Compared to packing a full fledged router, this is a convenient space saver that provides full fledge router capabilities with both 2.4 and 5 ghz wifi capabilities. I'd say that based on my testing, the unit provides 90 - 95 % of the rated speed that I was getting with a wired connection which isn't bad but certainly takes away from my overall review. The user interface for the firmware is intuitive and easy to use and configure. Would recommend this unit for anyone who travels frequently and wants a secure network to keep their data away from the rest of a public wifi.

title: Fast, Beautiful Screen, Highly Recommended! Love it!
text: What a piece of technology. When you are choosing from a modern tablet, you are looking for an amazing screen, fast hardware, and a quality operating system to give you access to your apps and media. This tablet does so with flying colors and oh is it fast! I love this tablet and would highly recommend it. You get a high res beautiful screen, a fast 8 core processor with 3 gb of ram and 32gb of internal storage with the ability to add capacity with an sd card. You get stereo sound (which for me is a first with a tablet) for great portable sound and or video watching. The AC wifi allows for blazing wifi speeds and I'm blown away with how quickly I'm able to load and watch 1080p Youtube video's with no buffering. The unit is so thin and light, compared to my older ipad 3rd generation it almost feels half the weight but same screen size and more power. The cost with that lighter weight has to come from somewhere and I'd say it's the battery, as I've had to charge the unit more frequently as a result. I believe it is rated at 6.5 hours which seems pretty accurate with consistent use. Another criticism I would have to add is the time it takes to charge. If you are needing to add power during the day be prepared for 3-4 hours for the unit to charge back to full. Plugging it in at night would be a good habit to get into. The camera's are quick and take great pictures comparable to modern smart phones on both the front and back camera. The fingerprint scanner has been hit or miss, I've reregistered my fingerprint a number of times but have had periods where it simply will not recognize my print. The Samsung software is fairly unobtrusive when I compare it to previous Samsung devices I've had in the past. The price for the 9.7 S2 is great for what you are getting and did I mention it is fast!

title: A quality performance portable storage solution
text:
The Lexar 32gb 3.0 USB Thumb Drive is likely the first usb 3.0 drive that I have had that has exceeded my expectations. It's not unusual to see speeds that disappoint when a drive claims high performance but this isn't the case with this drive. In addition to that, the sliding mechanism to protect the usb connector when not in use and the aluminum housing makes this feel like a premium product that will last.

When transferring large files from a pc via usb 3.0 from an SSD I saw maximum speeds of 140 mb/s and likely an overall average of 130. I was able to copy 13.6 gb folder of diablo 3 with a mixture of smaller files and larger data files in less than 2 minutes. That is outstanding write performance for a USB thumb drive. And read speeds are just as impressive as I was able to copy that same 13.6 gb's back to the same SSD drive with read speeds averaging 300 mb/s! I'm so used to usb drives letting me down when i was hoping for so much more.

The build quality has a very premium feel to it. It slides into your pocket without catching like some usb drives that have a rubber texture. The slide mechanism also feels consistent and doesn't feel like it will fail anytime, in fact i find myself fidgeting with it because it is so well done. It's not going to come out on accident and it does require you to "mean" to open it for it to slide out. It comes with a lanyard as well but I don't plan on putting this on my keychain anytime soon but was a nice to have feature.

Overall I am completely satisfied with this Lexar Drive and I would highly recommend it over some less expensive options.

title: Clean Realistic Sound for Movies and Music
text: The JBL Cinema 500 5.1 surround sound speaker system is a quality upgrade from a box setup home theatre system.  There is a significant improvement in sound clarity and the overall theatre experience.  Starting with the center channel speaker, voices are clearer when watching movies, providing a solid balance between music and ambient sound.  Often with surround speakers, they excel at volume for music and effects, but voices get washed out.  This is not the case with these speakers.  It is amazing how well one can hear even the slightest breath from a character on screen regardless of background sound.  The front surround speakers have excellent mid-range reproduction with no audible distortion at high volume levels.  There is an excellent sense of space with effects and soundtrack reproduction.  No sense of emptiness with the sound, the content comes through as the producers intended it to be heard.  The surround speakers, the satellites of this system are larger than some, about a foot from top to bottom, but have a very nice modern appearance.  They do have a keyhole type mounting for anchor mounting on a wall, perhaps different from some other speaker mounts.  The sub woofer has a large base on the floor, but the pyramid shape minimizes the shape near the top.  It completes the sound range and can have its output controlled from rear controls to increase volume as well as crossover to prevent higher frequencies.  The built in 500 watt amplifier does boost its volume significantly.  It has plenty of capacity for a large space, as we did not feel the need to crank it up in a smaller space.  When the bass hits in music, it has a very clean tone and compliments the surrounds nicely.  Testing a wide variety of music on these JBL speakers, it is easy to just get lost in the music.  Everything sounds amazing on these from pop and rock to classical.  Whatever the taste in music, it will sound superb.  This system is a great value and a terrific replacement to any standard home theatre in a box.  We are thrilled to have received this product to review, and do recommend it.

title: WORKS great and helps me keep an eye on our elderly mother.
text: My mother, who is 88, needs supervision.  My sister and I live close by but can't be running over to her home every hour to check on her.  These cameras are a perfect solution to our anxiety.  Pictures come in clear, will alert us when there is movement.  Just now, I got an alert and checked it to see Mom had gotten up, moved to the couch and turned off the light she usually keeps burning in the living room.  It immediately went into night vision.  She just wanted to lay on the couch instead of her bed (it is now 6:00 am Indianapolis, IN time.)  So she is safe.  I can also monitor the "laps" she is supposed to make throughout her house (3 laps 3 times a day.)  The only thing I would change is the volume.  I can talk to her but she is hard of hearing and doesn't always hear me, even with hearing aids.  Mom refuses to go to an assisted living place, even thought we looked at several that are very nice (and expensive.) The outside open pockets are big - 7"x8" deep.

That said, for me, since I will have no problem sewing in pockets today, this bag is worth it as I'm using it for an art bag and it easily carries a 9"x12" Strathmore Visual Journal water color paper, as well as a metal watercolor kit, brushs etc. I would not consider it for a laptop bag as it's on the smaller side, and I haven't tried it as one.

title: How to fix when power adapter goes bad, when pixilation, when problems loading photos
text:
The power connector came dead which means it can only start by USB.

When USB is running in power mode it can only do power, it can't be recognized by the computer to load pictures.

Okay, I had to buy a male to male USB on Amazon as the stores sell male to female. I could then plug the USB to the frame and to a USB phone charger wall connector, to power the device for now on.

Because the USB is being used for power it can't be used to transfer photos when plugged in between the computer and frame - it defaults to being used for powering the frame. This would not be a problem if I bought a power adapter specifically for this frame but since mine came bad I do not trust that company's power adapters so am not buying one.

I had to buy a scan disk mem card and it's adapter and load the pictures in jpg format from my computer and then insert into the frame for it to read them. First I had them in GIF format which didn't work. I verified BMP, JPEG and JPG work.

If you get a pixelated frame there is a power button on the frame - it's the first button, hold it down while starting the frame which should reset it to factory default and will most likely fix.

My frame works now. Moving from 1 star to 3. I am happy with it.

title: It worked - after I copied the dvd to my computers desktop and ran it there
text:
This worked after I copied the dvd (not large - in data size or physical size) to my desktop and installed it from there.

The program that captures audio is a pain. You have to read the manual to figure out simply how to record. After a few times I got it down though. It only saves in .wav file format. I had to save the wav file and bring it into to Audacity(free music editing program I got from internet) and then save it out as an mp3 file there. Fine as I was only using the Guitar Rig 2 program that came with the audio link cable to capture anyway. The Guitar Rig 2 program looks like it does a lot more so I'll be investigating that further.

I have now tried several things through this guitar link instead of just my guitar. If you have an instrument without a normal music jack, you can use an RCA mini stereo jack into what ever instrument you are using's headphone jack(which works as audio out) and it will record through the guitar link cable to the computer. Things I've tried even include the $13 dollar paper jamz drum kit and my Flanger(like a distortion pedal but fits right into the guitar's music jack), and my electric violins - one had a standard music jack and the other had the mini stero jack.

You should buy a cable that goes from mini stero to standard size music jack - to fit your head phones into the guitar link head phone slot. That head phone slot is for standard music cable, not mini stereo(the little head phone jack most head phones have.)

I've now tried it on Win 7 Starter and XP. I can use it on both.

title: SO MANY straps!
text:
I use a backpack like a briefcase. I carry the miscellenea of the day back and forth from home to office in it. On days I don't want to carry a handbag, it holds wallet, keys, phone and sunglasses too. I've tried the purse/camera bag option with Kelly Moore bags and it works, but I wanted a pack so I could carry a little more gear and a bit smaller purse. I picked the Tamrac based on price and reviews. I expected something a little bit larger for some reason, it's smaller than my basic Columbia daypack. It also has delusions of grandeur evidently, a daypack with a waist strap and chest straps is kind of overkill for my purposes and since I don't use them, they flap annoyingly all over the place when I do my usual "both straps over one shoulder" or carry by the hand grip at the top.

The padded camera bag section is compact but roomy enough for camera body mounted with a mid-sized lens along with space for additional lenses, charger, etc. The thing I really like about the camera bag section is that it feels very under control when you open it. I've got another pack that when I unzip it I am always terrified it's going to flop over and dump my gear out. The clip and the zip are easy to work and the top bag part flips back, leaving the camera section stably positioned.

The upper bag section is pretty small, you can't carry full sheets of paper or files without folding but a wallet, phone, sunglasses and small diary will fit, as well as a small tablet. You're not going to get a jacket in there unless it's very lightweight and you've got nothing else to carry.

In retrospect, I probably should have gone with the Adventure 9 but I was trying to save money and it looked much bulkier (but probably isn't since I thought the 7 was going to be bigger.)

title: Good tablet, recommended. These people stand by their product.
text:
I've never had such easy service and support for their product than Simbans support. They stand by their product and will go the extra mile to make things right. I highly recommend.

I've never dropped it, but still the touchscreen cracked. Support team was right there for me to fix the issue.

Two thumbs up and much gratitude to Simbans support for going the extra mile. I highly recommend their product.

DO NOT:
1) Play high end games for too long, this is a lower end tablet. If you'd purchased something with an octa core and paid about$400-600+, that's different.
But this is only a quad core.

2). Apply too much pressure on the touchscreen, it's too delicate, don't sit on it, put other heavy weighted objects on top of it, you'll crack the screen.

DO:
Give your tab a rest, about two hours or more per day. Give that quad core and RAM some downtime.

Protect your screen! It's a lot more delicate than you think. Don't put too much pressure on it. Make sure you get a warranty for such mishaps, you'll need it.

title: powerful fast charging cable, too weighty for my phablet
text: First off:  Let me say that this cable IS AN EXCELLENT, FAST CHARGING CABLE.  Please do not turn away from buying it just because my phablet is too darn thin to hold up under the weight of Anker's solid cable, so it pops out on it's own.  It's about time I found a USB mini cable that's worth its weight in gold x1000.  PACKAGING:  Niiice.  Anker took their time and boxed it up quite nicely.  The cable itself was wrapped with care, no knots, no sloppy packaging, a good Velcro strap tying it down.  Perfectly rolled up in what looks to be a leather carrying case.  Then I plugged it in, all well.  But the USB mini connector, due to the cable's weight, keeps popping out---not falling out, popping out.  But I find that if I bend it toward me when my device is upright (MY phablet mini USB port is on top not bottom), then sometimes it'll stay in.  I have to play with it to get it to stay in.  Once the cable's in, it's in that mini port tightly, I mean I just tried gently pulling it out and it would not budge.  If I leave it upright to charge, it'll stay in and charges fast.  But it's the only reason I gave less stars, cuz otherwise, I don't think you can get a USB charging cable any better than Anker.

I was paid a discount rate to give my honest opinion of this product.  So glad I bought it!  I highly recommend this product to anyone looking for a great water speaker with clear sound and vibrant lights and water action.

title: Great gaming laptop, fast
text:
I use this msi thin laptop to game on. Works great. Quality is great. Only thing i hate about it is that when i try to reset my msi, it wont let me. I have no idea why its not letting me reset it, like erase all info incase i want to resale it. I have googled online about the reset problem and it seems im not the only one. But for now im just kepping it. I have had it for almost 2 years now, its still working great like how i first got it. I mostly play world of warcraft on it like for long hours, plugged in. If you dont keep it plugged in while gaming anything, it most likely will lag and so keep it plugged in when youre gaming on mmorpgs or any fps online games. I can play on highest graphics settings but it will get very hot on the keyboard if doing so, and the fan will turn faster. I always game on lowest setting though. The fan is quiet, cant hear it when on low graphics settings, but on high, you will hear the fan in turbo mode blow. Overall this is a great gamer laptop. Its thin, lightweight for travel. It turns on fast. Its fast on web surfing, etc. I paid $2k for my msi thin. Yes id recommend this to gamers. It doesnt hold too many games on it, but it doesn't hold too less too. Again it depends on how big your game is. Keyboard typing sounds are quiet almost silent. Nice feel to type on. Thin keys. Mousepad tracking is nice, smooth, finger movements reads great. Love the keyboard lighting functions. Dim it down or brighten it up. Doesnt hurt the eyes. Even on lowest dim it doesnt hurt eyes, cause its really dim, yet i can still see the letters, i love it. Msi comes with dragon center to set up your personal keyboard light, choose which keys, for which color you want, and save it. Love that too. Great gaming laptop.

Edit: i just system reset my msi laptop but it didnt erase a few things that i had put on it and i even clicked the automatic option reset too. I didn't even click manual/personal option. And my old screensaver bg was still on it as the desktop bg even after i completed the factory reset. Hmm weird but the pictures were all deleted.

title: Awesome sound system!
text:
For the price, this thing is awesome! I must be honest and say that it's a bit larger than I thought it would be, but I'm OK with that.

The sound is nice, crisp and clear. It has a good amount of bass. I've listened to everything from the news to movies to music, and it does really well with everything. Bluetooth hookup is also a breeze, and it connects to my devices in a couple of seconds. The sound is also great for streaming. Something that I REALLY love about this is that there is an audible voice that tells you when it has successfully connected to your device(s).

Hookup was a breeze. It comes with an AUX cable that goes into the back of the system and into the headphone jack on the back of the TV. It took literally 2 seconds to hook it up. The directions in the manual weren't that great, but due to it being a simple hookup, it should be easy enough for those that aren't tech savvy to follow. Note: we purchased an optical cable separately, and I will update this review in regards to sound when we have received and used it.

The remote is simple - just the way I like it! It has only the basic buttons one needs to control the system (volume, input, sound, bass, treble, pause/playback, rewind, fast forward).

This isn't your normal "sound bar." It looks different. It sounds different. The subs are at the bottom, and I believe that gives off a better, fuller sound that seems almost as if it bounces off the mantel (or whatever it sits atop).

title: Great amp!
text:
Over the past several months, I've become a huge fan of Pyle products. Like the other products that I've acquired, I am very pleased with this amp.

We hooked it up to some speakers that came with our JVC stereo, and it worked perfectly. Unless you have a very complicated system that you're connecting to the amp, setup is a breeze. After connecting the speaker wires to the amp (which took a while because of the wires that we have and has nothing to do with the amp itself), connecting a device took no time. You can connect to the amp via several methods, and that is a major plus for me. We normally use the amp with an Echo, which we connect via Bluetooth, and it works flawlessly. It seems to be well built, sturdy and has a decent weight.

The amp is fairly small, and can be mounted virtually anywhere, or simply sat on top of any place of your choosing. It is mostly black with black dials, the "Pyle" logo in blue, numbers and lines around the three dials (volume, treble and bass) and in other places are white, and there are a few more small words/sentences on it in white. There are USB and SD slots on the front of the amp, above the LCD screen. It isn't an eyesore, and can sit in any room without being noticed or taking away from the decor. It blends very well with my living room and doesn't look out of place. The LCD screen isn't excessively bright. It is bright enough to clearly see what is on the screen, but not excessively bright to the point of being distracting at night or in the dark.

The sound is awesome. While I'm not extremely well versed in this kind of technology, I have enough knowledge to say that this is a very decent 2-channel amp. Our speakers aren't "top of the line," so alone, they don't put out the best sound in the world; but with the amp, though, one would never be able to tell that the speakers are on the fairly low-end of the price and quality spectrum. Are the speakers awful on their own? Absolutely not, but this amp does a lot for them. The sound is crisp, clear and loud.

The amp comes with a remote, which you can use to power the amp on/off, change the mode (input), decrease/increase/mute volume, pause, fast/skip forward, rewind/skip backwards, pause/play, scan (there are other things included on this button), randomize/repeat songs/tracks (at least I think that button does one of these things), access the equalizer and enter numbers. I honestly use the remote to control the amp a lot more than I use the controls on the amp itself.

As I use the amp with more devices/speakers, I will update my review as/if necessary.

Just a note: It doesn't come with cables, so you'll need your own or purchase them separately.

You can mirror all other types of apps, but not streaming content. For that you'll need a fire stick or something similar. Or hook up your laptop. But for general screen mirroring the connectivity was easy with ios at least. Android seems a bit more clunky. Fan noise is reasonable if you're watching movies at normal volume. Not a silent device by any means. But normal fan noise should be expected. Could be a little brighter, but for the money you can't really complain. Plenty bright under the right circumstances. title: The best bang for you buck - bar none
text:
Let me start off by saying that I have used many, many different earbuds and headphones over the years, and these are by FAR the best bang for my buck in terms of quality, durability, and comfort. I've always managed to land jobs where I'm able to listen to audio content throughout my workday, and have consequently spent most of my working hours with at least one earbud tucked into my ears.

I thread these down to my pocket where they are plugged into my iPod full time. No matter how much running, walking, lifting, jumping or moving around I do (and I work as a package delivery guy, which means hundreds of movements and ten miles of walking a day), these things take ages to wear out. Under normal use, I'm sure they'd never need replacing unless you managed to blow out the speaker somehow, or cause blatant damage to them. They don't cut in and out from wear on the jack end or on the headphone ends like some other earbuds, which will give way after being cranked around a bit.

Next, I have to address the comfort of the ergonomically shaped buds themselves. They are formed to fit into ear, with the speaker being offset from the center of the housing. On others, such as the classic white Apple earbuds, the round shape causes me some discomfort and soreness after hours of wear. But these are just fantastic. I wear them for up to 11 hours at a time with no discomfort whatsoever.

Finally, the sound quality. While an audiophile purist will say that they probably don't meet the highest standards in the land, they do a pretty good job. They stand up to much more expensive earbuds, and if you use the proper sized adapter for your ear (three sizes included), the speaker isolates sound very well, so you don't even need any noise-canceling feature. I wear them while driving a diesel truck with the doors open driving down the freeway, and I can hear every word of the audiobook I'm listening to. The treble is good. The bass is excellent for such an inexpensive earbud. And the overall sound quality is going to put other in-ear buds to shame.

For less than ten bucks, there is no better ear bud out there. I've owned three pairs over the last two years, and I would only have needed one if I didn't abuse them so much with daily use and extreme wear. If you want to try these, but would like to keep a microphone feature for hands-free calls, you can get some identical to these with in-line microphone in the Panasonic RPTCM125K model.

title: I guess it works
text:
My title for this review is not deliberately obtuse, it is just that I was desperate for an antenna and chose the one with the reviews that seemed to best meet my housing needs (apartment) as well as my budgetary needs (retired with small, fixed income).

You know, these small antenna types can only provide as well as they can, given their limited powers and whatever physical/geographic challenges are caused by one's limits on where the thing can be placed.

I do not live surrounded by mountains or trees or large buildings. I do not live in a valley or in the middle of nowhere. I DO live within forty miles of every transmission source in a nearby big city, so it might be considered reasonable to expect that an antenna that touts a sixty-mile range to be useful.

It is, but only partially because the fault is not in our stars, it is in a huge menu of influences (which may include the some sky/heavenly/ astronomical stuff, but that is another story).

My point, and the useful part, is that these simple and, more importantly, cheap antennas can only do what they can because geography, distance, obstacles you cannot see or image and even the stars (yep) conspire to modify their successful use, and even all that can be affected by other stuff we are unable to anticipate or influence.

If you want an antenna that has a potential for reasonable performance, simply spend the considerable dollars that will buy a reasonably and consistent performance.

Sellers, provide honest claims so that purchasers will know what they are getting. Customers, be discerning so that you can use your dollars to get the best you and your critical thinking can provide.

As for me, hope springs eternal that I will someday be able afford an antenna that allows me to watch our local PBS stations and in the meantime I will ignore the religious (not aligned with my personal spiritual practices) and selling-stuff channels.

It is the best I can afford, and a little late-night cartoons never hurt anyone.

The four-star rating is only because I finally hold a decent perspective on all this jazz.

text:
I bought this cover and the Zing Pro Zoom cover. I like the Op Tech D Pro Zoom better.
Pros:
It was easier to get on and off my camera then the Zing.
It fits my camera and accessories nicely.
Seems well made. I have many other Op Tech products that I purchased and they have all held up nicely.
Cons:
To securely close the cover, there is a flap that has 2 snaps. You wrap the cover around the back of the camera, and snap the flap closed with the 2 snaps. I'm not a fan of snaps. These were easy to snap closed, but Velcro would have been much easier.
There is a strap attached to the inside of the cover. It came with 2 ways of attaching the cover to your camera so you don't lose the cover:
1. a piece of leather that attaches to the camera by screwing it into the tripod mount. This piece attaches to the strap with a snap. I could see either end of the leather coming apart - the side with screw could detach or the snap could release.
2. A ring that can go around the lens. This ring attaches to the strap with a snap. I don't like having things attached to my lens and the snap could release.
I came up with my own method of securing the cover to my camera. The bottom of my battery grip has a connection point for a strap. I had an extra set of Op Tech Uni Loop connectors (https://www.amazon.com/OP-TECH-USA-1301062-Uni-Loop/dp/B0010HA6A6/ref=sr_1_1?ie=UTF8&qid=1485137755&sr=8-1&keywords=optech+uni+loop).
I attached one end to the bottom of the battery grip. I attached the other connector to the strap by looping the strap thru the connector loop and snapping the two snaps on the strap together. Using the uni loop connectors, I clicked the two pieces together. I think the weakest point is where the snaps are attached. I'm going to sew a few stitches next to the strap as a precaution in case the snaps come undone. You can use any type of strap to secure the cover to the camera. I also attached a photo using an extra camera strap from one of my point and shoot cameras. If I used this method, I would still sew a few stitches next to the snap. I like the uni loop method. If the cover gets in the way, I can just disconnect the uni loop clips.
I'm happy with this cover even though I'm using a different method of attaching the cover to my camera. I dropped the rating to a 4 because of the use of the snaps.
