title: Terrific price, great list of features, well built and good sound. A good buy for most people.
text:
I am an audiophile but I always take into account the nature of the product that I am looking at or listening to. One cannot possibly expect a $99 portable bluetooth speaker to have legitimate audiophile sound. In this case, we're talking about the Creative Sound Blaster Roar. And that assertion is not in any way a knock on this product. I bought one a few days ago and I like it and am quite happy with the purchase for a variety of reasons. The main reason I like it is because the sound it produces is GOOD. That sound is not great nor is it bad. Perhaps the worst credible thing you might say about the sound is simply that it is FINE. When I consider the size of the unit (and the size of the very small speakers it contains) and the cost, I judge the sound to be GOOD. You are not going to get Martin Logan or Definitive Technology sound out of the Roar, plain and simple. Nor will you get super sound out of any of the other competitive products such as the Bose or JBL, etc. I think they all produce generally good sound for the money. The best and smartest thing a buyer can do is perhaps go to
Best Buy or any of the other retailers who carry such units and give them all a listen and look at the features they offer and then buy the one that meets your needs in terms of both sound quality and features. Having said that, for me the Roar has more features than any of the
competing units. That is simply fact and not opinion. Most of the products that are in this category seem to be made well but in my opinion, the Roar seems to be made just a little sturdier. I haven't tested that notion by dropping my Roar on the floor but in my hands it simply feels
more robust. Back to the sound question.....since I seriously doubt that many users of portable bluetooth speakers plan on doing serious
listening that entails sitting in a quite room and doing nothing but listening intently to these little portable speakers, consider how they will actually be used. Most people are playing them as background music while they are doing other things such as sitting on the beach or
cooking on the grill or in the kitchen, etc. Critical listening ain't happening here. So let's not talk about sound imaging or speaker spatiality etc. That said, for me, I don't like speakers that have a bass response that overwhelms everything else. I want a more natural sound, One that is

more balanced to my ear. Because of that, I will gravitate towards something like the Roar. If you are one who wants more bass, then you will assuredly better like the sound of any Bose product as they have made a fortune producing bass heavy products for the last 50 years. Again, for me, the features are a big deal and the Roar excels inn that regard. I won't waste your time talking about them as you can look such things up just as easily. And price is a big deal to me. The Roar 1 can be had for $99 now.... so I bought one. The Bose is $299 the last time I checked,...three times the cost of the Roar. So simply put, I loved the price of the Roar, the feature list is unmatched, it feels like military grade construction and lastly, I thought the sound was GOOD. That's why I bought it.

title: Outstanding
text: I am an audiophile who is determined to get great sound without spending large amounts of money.  It is esy to get world class sound if you are willing to spend over $5,000.  I will never do that, however.  In the 1970's, I worked part time in two high end audio stores -- hence I know what good sound is and is not.  I was interested in the Motion 4's because they are Martin Logan speakers and Martin Logan has been a leader in producing remarkable speakers for decades.  And I was interested because of the technology employed in the Motion 4's. I got a pair of the Motion 4 speakers about one week ago after auditioning them three times at my local Best Buy. In the store, they sounded far superior to any other speaker even close to their price range.  Once I got them home, they sounded even better as I hooked them up to a Denon 3805 receiver.  I got the 3805 used for $200 after doing much research on receiver performance vis a vis 4 ohm speakers -- which the Motion 4's are.  This is a big deal -- matching you amp to your speakers -- since there are many amps that simply fall apart sonically under 4 ohm speaker loads.  Many receivers won't even rate their output into 4 ohm loads because of their embarassing performance. This particular Denon receiver, however is a throwback in terms of build quality and handles 4 ohm loads exceedingly well. The Motion 4's are not big speakers but they will fill an average sized listening room quite nicely. There is not much low end but that did not surprise me and it wasn't needed since I have a subwoofer. The midrange and the high end, however, are nothing short of glorious.  They are spacious and very open and incredibly detailed. I absolutely was hearing more and better sounds than I have heard in years. The folded tweeter -- a smaller version of the incredible Heil Air Motion transformer of 30 years ago -- clearly is amazing. Any high frequency -- cymbals, pianos, acoustic and electric guitars, etc -- simply come to life with a sense of immediacy and aural acceleration lacking in any other speaker near its price range and size.  The only possible reason anyone would find these speakers lacking is if you installed them in a very large room that they couldn't possibly fill OR if you hooked them up to an amp that could not handle 4 ohm loads -- and beware, there are a lot of amps out there that have this problem.  Otherwise, buy the Motion 4's with confidence.

title: cheap feeling, grey screen, flimsy tabs
text:
NOTE: This is for the 3m pf23.0W9, not sure why the review says it's for the 19.0W version although I doubt it makes a difference.

I just got this and I think that I'm going to return it. I moved to a new office and got a new computer with a shiny, gorgeous new monitor (the Dell Optiplex all in one 9000 model, 23 or 24" inches with a flat bezel - or maybe it's no bezel, but it's completely flat across, no indentation where the screen is). The florescent lights shine on my computer screen all the time, it's like having 3 large white shiny bars across my computer screen. So I decided to go with this anti-glare screen protector to reduce the glare.

First of all - you're paying $90 for a piece of flimsy plastic that you tape on your computer screen with the included sticky tabs. There are two sides to this screen, one side is shiny and does absolutely nothing to reduce the glare. The other side has a bit more of a matte finish and reduces glare by a small amount but not much. The screen is still shiny where the lights shine on the monitor.

Secondly - the tabs which are used to attach the film to the screen are flimsy pieces of hard tape. They fall off, aren't very adhesive, and look awful and cheap. If you touch the sticky part your finger print ends up on it.

Thirdly - the screen gets DARK. I have the screen on the highest brightness setting and it's grey.

Also - the screen is blurry - text isn't as crisp as it is. I can already feel my eyes starting to strain.

I'm gonna try it for another week - if I don't get used to it it's going back. I'm not pleased, especially given the price.

text:

The buds themselves are larger than on the iPod headphones. They have a rubber edge which makes them somewhat comfortable while wearing. Because they're so large, though, they often fall out because they don't fit right.

The cord is noticeably shorter than on the iPod headphones, I measured and it was about 6 inches shorter which makes a difference if you want to keep your device in your bag while wearing the headphones.

They're only $10 so it's not a huge loss but I wish I had spent a little more and gotten a better quality set of earbuds. Other earbuds in the $10-20 range (particularly those made by Sony) are of a much higher quality. Just because they say Philips doesn't mean that they're good!

Update 9/3/10: I've had these headphones for about a year and they still work! Granted, I don't use them daily, they are my backup headphones, but I'm really surprised that they have held up so well for a year! Not bad for 10 bucks!

The Pros of this little printer are: size (iPhone-sized), lightweight, quick printing, decent photo quality for a small, portable, Zink-paper printer, easy to set up, charges quickly

Cons: Comes with no instructions. You have to download the user guide from the app; the app is difficult to manage when you have to keep checking back to the user guide to adjust something on the app; once an item is in your printing queue, that baby isn’t coming off your queue until it’s printed. If you’ve accidentally uploaded multiple images of something, those items will print until you shut off the printer. Any new pics you add are loaded behind the old images, so if you think you’re going to quickly print a picture you’ve just taken, guess again. You’re getting the duplicate photo that might be days old. There is no way to delete these duplicates—and I’ve tried customer service MULTIPLE times. The “Virtual chat” with a Robo-tech tells you to cancel the print. This stops the printing of the image, but doesn’t delete it. The next time you flip your Sprocket on, guess which picture from your queue is headed your way? Exactly. This brings me to customer service, which is pretty shabby. You’re directed to chat with a virtual assistant, and, if you’re lucky and your question goes through (it often says “cannot send message”), you’ll get a generic answer that helps with bandaid fixes. HP has also added an “App Doctor” app that helps you do your own troubleshooting and performance tweaking on your sprocket. With the somewhat difficult maneuvering on the plain sprocket app, I’m praying for all I’m worth I never have to go to “the Doctor.”
Also somewhat annoying—there are different sizes of Zink paper for the Sprockets. Be sure you look carefully at which Sprocket model you have before ordering more paper, or you’ll end up doing the exchange dance. Just because the product headline says a package of paper is “For the HP Sprocket,” you’ll need to look much closer to see if it will fit in your model.

Boiling it down, I’d have to say the product is awesome in itself. It accomplishes exactly what a journaler on the go wants. But the app that drives this little printer? If I had ten thumbs, they’d all be down.

UPDATE: Everytime the app “adds improvements,” it decreases productivity. I now have to turn the printer off between prints, wait a few minutes, then turn it back on. Then I have to go to the printing queue and reactivate the process. The device freezes frequently when in use. I liked my original brand-new Sprocket Plus; the “improved by app” model less so.

title: Major Upgrade Especially if You Own a Vizio TV!
text: My wife and I decided to upgrade our entire living theatre setup this February. We purchased this soundbar for $798 and a Vizio P759-G1 TV for $1234. The best part of this setup is that the Vizio TV and soundbar support “common mode” transport of Dolby Atmos. This means that our Apple TV 4K can be plugged into any of the five HDMI ports and this soundbar will receive (compressed) Dolby Atmos. The majority of our movie watching happens on the Apple TV 4K with iTunes movies that have Atmos soundtracks. This form of Atmos is already compressed (Dolby Digital Plus) so we aren’t really losing any quality. We love our new setup in our smallish living room. The 10” subwoofer is also a huge improvement over the 8” woofer in the Vizio SB4551-D5 soundbar we had previously. The passive radiators inside the bar also help with its musicality. There’s actually a lot of detail in the mids versus other bars. Vizio has always made very “musical” soundbars, but this one is exceptional. We moved that system to our bedroom. Now we have full surround sound in two rooms (one with full Atmos!) and we couldn’t be happier.

title: Cute little camera that packs a punch
text:
So this is the cutest camera I’ve ever had. The video quality is great, and I love the motion tracking feature. It makes it the perfect camera to watch cover my dogs whenever I have to step out of the house.

The app could use improvement though. The tracking feature lags when you want to manually use it. There was one time I tried moving the camera down with the arrow, but it wouldn’t go. It was stuck in the level position, but would go in all of the other directions. I physically took the camera in my hand and moved the camera to point down with my finger. After that, it worked. It lagged, but it worked. The app also freezes sometimes, and I have to exit and close out of the app and go back in. I find that part annoying, especially when I’m going into the app because it detected motion and the buggy app makes me wait longer to see what’s going on.
Despite the buggy app, I think this camera is a great value for its price. It’s a motion tracking camera with 2k video quality. You don’t need to buy a service to use it, although they do offer a cloud based plan. But you can just purchase a micro sd card for it, and you’re set. It’s also really cute.

I should add that one of my dogs has noticed this camera because of its head. He barks at it whenever it moves to track him. Just something to note if you are worried about that.

text:

No subscription needed (if you install a micro and card). They do offer a cloud storage option, which is nice, and they offer an option to insert a micro and card to store locally- which is exactly what I was looking for. I just popped out my card out of my Nintendo switch to test it out.
This arrived packaged neat in the box shown. I was able to put this together in a rush, as I was in the middle of moving and I wanted to be able to watch my pups while I was go for an hour or so. I downloaded the app and connected the camera- all in less than 2-3 minutes. There were no hiccups. Just set up and go.
This little security camera began picking up motion and sound right away (fyi, you need to go into settings to switch on the alerts). On day 2 of having this installed, I caught one of my pups jumping over his pen. Thankfully, the app alerted me, and I was able to rush back and get him back in before he did any damage to himself. So, yeah I’m glad I got this small (but mighty) little security camera! I’m thinking of buying one for my back porch now, to see how well it holds up outside!

Cons: App lags a little. Could just be my internet speed, but the live stream doesn’t start right away when I go to view. When this happens, I close out of the app and open it again and it’s all good. Not really enough for me to knock a star off for. But it’s something I’d like to note.

title: Pretty good - ultra sensitive
text:
This is our first Ring purchase. It’s nice and small. Setup was easy. For a first ring purchase, all the software (creating ring account) and hooking up to WiFi and Alexa probably took about 20 mins.
We set it upside down in the window next to the front door.
The speaker isn’t that great and has a fair delay to it.
The resolution is decent, it has a very wide angle.
It is very sensitive to motion, almost too much. We’ll be moving it today I believe to a better location. Biggest problem we had was it pick up every reflection on the window if one of us or the dogs walked up the stairs, so it kept going off. We fixed it temporarily with a “shield” behind it. But it even goes off every time some one pulls their car out of their driveway up the street, up to 3 or 4 houses away.
I do like the Ring app, and tie into our echo devices. We could never hear the doorbell from most of the house or in the back yard.
And nowadays with all of the door dash bandits it’s a good peace of mind.

title: Works ok with sheetrock work but be careful. Wood is far easier.
text:
An excellent little enhancement to my setup. I would love to see a larger trim ring for this unit. I was concerned with my specific usage, that of recessing it into a sheetrock wall. It turns out it can be accomplished but be careful with tolerances. You could miscut and blow through your normal screw holes. I ended up needing to place a piece of wood behind the wall and secure it with a couple of sheetrock screws, then secure my unit to that wood. I expected as much so no harm on my end. A bit of paint, and all is well.

That said, most people using this in an entertainment center would never experience this. I am well pleased and another great product from the seller.

title: Leaps and bounds above the rest.
text:
Edit 11-20-2018

Mobile app iOS,

I noticed as some others have that I was unable to see a camera remotely yesterday. I had previously setup and tested the app with just 3 cameras. Nothing would bring the new cameras into view. Well almost nothing, I removed the app from the phone and reinstalled it, now all cameras are showing remotely.

Original :
I was a low voltage installer in years gone by and this brought back memories of why I no longer like crawling in attics at this age. Seriously though the unit is superb. Its not that bad of an install, its just me hating crawling in attics after having done it for so many years.

It came packaged really well. I was surprised at how well it was protected. We purchased the 16 channel NVR for future expandability. I put cameras all over the place. They are arranged to keep track of important areas as you would expect. The image is great. Better than I had hoped for.

The cables are not really internet ready, each cable only has 4 wires in it. I would rather have had a fully functional cable.
Upon taking the DVR out of the box, there was a small rattle inside, more of a piece of plastic moving around. Like a broken tab during assemble.

Installation activities.

The cables also a little short for larger homes, though they do sell longer versions. In most of my use cases the cables were fine. It's just 3 were all the way across the home in a far corner. I could have used another 10'.
So, I simple ran my own cable and terminated the ends. No big deal for me. However if you think you'll have enough and your getting close in your estimation, you better have one or two longer ones. The 60' cables seem to be a standard in the security camera kits.

The cable protector/environmental protection covers are a little large, not overly so. Just notating it here for others. You'll need to make sure you have extra room behind the camera. Most people will not see this issue. Make sure and use a drill bit big enough for the protector to pass though if it will be placed inside a wall, or overhang etc. You are not just drilling a hole for the cable. Look at the camera and you'll see the size you need to make it. I also ended up needing a longer HDMI cable, the one that came with this was about 6' I needed a 10' due to my particular situation. Not a mfg. fault, just my use case. So this one went into the spare bin and one in a 10/12' came out.

The first day, I needed to arrange things in my AV closet, and add a plugin. You may wish to have a licensed electrician preform this, if it's needed.

We started about 1 pm and finished about 7 putting in the NVR, 3 cameras, pulling 3 new wires, terminating those wires. The second day we started at 9 am and finished at 8 PM, with the remaining cameras. Though we had some extremely challenging placements this day. Your install time may or may not be this long, or it could possibly be longer.

Use :

As to the cameras they work really well, I was surprised at how well the picture looks and the microphone, well its as another user put it almost too good. You can go into settings and turn down the volume., Make sure you do that for cameras that are internal, aka in the house. If you using a monitor it may not be necessary that much. But ours is piped into the living room tv, and the kids or I, leave the volume up. You'll clearly know it when you switch over to the camera system and click on the camera.

Notes:

For anyone looking for answers here its also a good bet to look at the Swann forums. There are some good topics from other users there as well. Especially for users who may be asking more technical or unique issues. For anyone looking at this I would suggest also looking at some youtube videos there are a few that go over some of the options in the NVR settings. Like setting recording limits etc. Motion detection and so forth.

End results / Opinion:

I am more than pleased with my purchase, it far lives up to my desires. I wish I had bit the bullet and done this earlier on. Like years ago, but oh well its up now and I am more than happy. It's a little large purchase, money wise. But I personally think it was well worth the money at least for us.

This replaced a wireless competitor and its leaps and bounds above it.

title: Great watch, it has held up well.
text:
I am fortunate enough to be someone who has had the ability to purchase this version and this year get the newer version 4. I have used this one since it came out and its my daily driver, aka work watch. I am using the 4 for when exercising and evenings out (a rarity). I know a lot of folks will say how do you afford 2 etc. I don't have any vices so I buy a watch or a phone every other year. This year I forgo the new phones and went with a watch. It was cheaper too. :)

The 3 has lasted a year doing construction work, don't get me wrong, I use a screen protector, along with a larger whole watch protector and it has helped. I love it. I use it to track my daily activities including workouts and get an occasional call in those occasions I forget the phone in the car. Its came in handy twice now. About the only down side is the battery I wished it lasted a little longer. It usually lasts all day at this point, but must be charged every night.
Before I made some changes the watch only got about a work day, and no exercise etc. I turned off the raise to wake feature and reduced the time the screen stays on when waking it.
iOS 5 has really, helped the battery IMO.
I would certainly buy this again, and very likely will, if something happens to mine as its invaluable to me at work. Both as a time piece and easily getting the iMessages our office uses to communicate.

title: Great router, I purchased 2 of these and I ...
text:
Great router, I purchased 2 of these and I am using them with Asus AiMesh setup to cover my home in seamless wifi. I already owned the RT-AC5300 which is serving as the router and these 2 will serve as Nodes.
I live in a giant Faraday cage, a 60+ year old house with plaster walls and chicken wire mesh behind those walls which severely cuts down on wifi traveling through them. Add metal siding too, no much WiFi gets out or even through the walls.
The router is small, in size but seems to have a big attitude. I was able to get great speeds throughout the house. With one of them on each end and the 5300 in the middle.

I will likely be buying another one of these to extend the range from the house to my detached garage and the backyard. I was hesitant to spend the money but the better performance was well worth it. If I had purchased it here on Amazon I could have saved myself a lot of money. But that's the price you pay the you want something and don't necessarily want to wait for delivery.

I would recommend it to anyone and also suggest you look at setting up the AiMesh. I know I am a happy camper and can go all over the house with no dropped connections.

The only con I had was I was never able to get the router into rescue mode. Its pretty straight forward on the 5300, not so much on this one. Though that's something not everyone would need. I had to reset the router with e WPS button held until it reset. I was attempting to use the rescue mode to go from Merlin to stock firmware. Just a minor hiccup, I was able to refresh the firmware using a wireless connection vs a wired one. That goes against everything I have learned but it worked. So ???

title: I love the looks of it
text:

I have ordered an additional 3 for other drives.

The description says a 9.5mm drive will fit. It would not fit mine, the connector board is screwed to the case and there is not enough clearance to allow the drive to fit the connector. You can unscrew the board which allows movement and the drive to be connected but then you cannot get the closure closed.
I do really like this enclosure, but due to not being able to place a 9.5mm in it I removed 1 star.

Long story short. Good for 7mm, bad for 9.5mm this is my third purchase Ill just keep this and order another that will fit my 9.5mm 1tb drive

Edit. : ** Warning, this will void warranty ** If your really serious about putting a TB 9.5 MM drive in the case, it can be accomplished, however it requires unscrewing the board, and cutting some fo the rubber that the drive would sit on. Which removes some of the vibration dampening. I used the included screw driver to loosen the board and an ordinary pair of scissors to trim the rubber. While I personally would not mind such activities I think the average person would rather buy a closure better suited to simply insert and go.

Having said the above the drive works like a charm in the enclosure. No issues at all. None. You can see it attached in the picture near the bottom of the ethernet cords by a cable tie.

title: I absolutely love this box
text:
Edit :
Captive Portals:
Works well for getting your Xbox on the hotel wifi. You connect to this router thru your phone, when you first get to the hotel, and go through the captive portal process. That registers this routers Mac address with the hotel internet system. Then you plug in or connect wirelessly to the router from the xbox etc and your good to go. The next time you need to authenticate repeat.
All the hotel sees is 1 authenticated device the "router" anything behind it, like a laptop or xbox, etc they don't care about. It looks like all traffic is coming from the "router" in their eyes.

Original : I absolutely love this box, works great in WISP mode. Has 2 LAN connections, and a WAN port. It keeps a stable connection on the hotel wifi and keeps my devices all connected to my private net. Love the VPN function. It has a small form factor, at first I was unsure if I would like that. edit 5/25/2018

title: I am very easily able to maintain
text:
I own 2 of these 16 port switches housed in a wiring cabinet in a closet and another, a [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Switch (GS108)]] at my computer desk mounted to the wall, and an, [[ASIN:B00MPVR50A NETGEAR 8-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch (GS108)]] behind the LR TV, then another 3 separate bedroom TV's (kids and my br) have [[ASIN:B002NVOLGI Netgear GS605 5-Port Gigabit Ethernet Switch]] behind them for all the various game systems, video devices etc. I purchased them to upgrade my network from older legacy 10/100 switches a few years back. I have always trusted NETGEAR, mainly because it was used by an old employer of mine. I am very easily able to maintain, GB transfer levels, and all devices on my network are able to pull great speed tests.

I used the switches to segment my network into logical groups, the cabinet, holds the main switch's that run to things like the modem, router, alarm panel, other WiFi AP's, and they connect to my other switches.

One pro tip if you have young kids in the home, make sure and keep the network switches where they (young kids) cannot plug cords into it. At the time my 4 or 5 year old decided he would help dad by plugging the loose end of a cat5 cable into a spare port on the switch. You can guess it wreaked havoc on my system causing crashes etc.

These have held up well to years of use and show no signs of letting me down. I will certainly buy NETGEAR again.

title: It so far it has been a very good purchase. Its held up well to construction work ...
text:
Earlier this year I purchased this (880) at a truck stop. I use the radio occasionally, mainly for work communication between transport and chase vehicles.
It so far it has been a very good purchase. Its held up well to construction work (heavy equipment movement). I have had no issues with the radio at all.

I think the stock speaker has too low of a volume (well for fast approaching 50 it is). I purchased a remote speaker and mounted it in the rear window area of my truck (F150) I have no trouble hearing now, as I often have to turn it down. The remote speaker works well when you have the car radio lightly playing on the long trips. Then the iPhone giving NAV reports over the car stereo speakers too (CarPlay). That remote speaker still allows plenty of volume to properly hear your other vehicle.

Since my job varies and I don't always need this unit hooked up, or for quick changes. I elected for a slightly different approach. I used 3 magnetic car phone mounts and attached them to the front slide out cup holder assembly of the F150. The magnets will latch onto the radio allowing me to choose various angles of mounting it at. We always run ch 19 so really changing or seeing the display while driving is almost always not necessary for me. However it is easily accessible if needed. I find it helps cut down on the amount of light distractions with the unit side ways. Though the CB does have day/night mode if you want to use it.

I have not seen any issues with the CB and the magnetic mounts. The 3 mounts have held the radio in some bumpy construction, terrain and it hasn't fallen off yet.

I am not by any means a power user, I just need a good, well made, radio that will hold up over time. This unit fits the bill.

title: Super easy to change this tailgate latch out
text:
Super easy to change this tailgate latch out. All in all the swap out took maybe 15 minutes at most (just latch assembly). It was really easy to swap out the key tumbler from the old latch.

The only issue I had and it could be a manufacturing issue or an install issue. I don't think it was install issue as I have installed low voltage wiring for 20 years and know how to run it properly etc. The issue could come from the factory as I have had some new wiring (just out of the package) damage from the factory. It is also possible it could have come from the installation activities. Let me clarify the issue was the included RCA cord and not the camera assembly, the cable was simply bad.

As always test the system before installing it permanently. It was a super easy fix for me, throw away the old wire and grab another RCA cable which I had in my electrical spare parts bin. I did not ask for a replacement from Amazon as it was way to easy for me to grab a new cable. I had the spare parts and the spare cable was a little higher quality (braided shielding and thicker diameter). My experience over the years with how often bad wiring occurs tells me very few people would experience this issue. Since the issue could have been me, the manufacturing of the cable or a combination of all, I have not taken any stars away.

The Camera (image) looks good, well as good as I would want. I installed this into my 2012 F150 work truck The install took 4 1/2 hours total. That total was also including installing an [[ASIN:B000C19DNM Pop & Lock PL8250 Power Tailgate Lock for Ford (For tailgate with OEM lock)]]. Since the wiring for both had to be done to the same areas of the passenger compartment, I elected for the an all at once installation. I am a little more picky than some on running my wiring, again due to my experience over the years. I would estimate most folks could do this within a couple of hours if they are familiar with their vehicle and accustomed to wiring electronics, and have a good set of tools to work with.

Oh this also was a 45+ year old man crawling around on the ground running wiring and so forth. I did not have a lift to facilitate the process which would have greatly sped up the installation process. Plus saved me throwing out several Danny Glover, Lethal Weapon quotes. :P If you have to ask go watch the movie bonus points if your 45+ and can relate once you watch it.

The instruction are lacking if your a novice, regarding the change out of the latch assembly. Its really just 2 bolts and slide the old one out and the new one in. If the new unit seems awkward to get back in slightly pull the handle as if opening the latch when trying to reinstall it.

It took a few minutes of fiddling to get the camera where I wanted it set. (rotation within the latch assembly) and I followed the advise of the instructions to put some silicone on the back of the camera housing between it and the plastic assembly. This secures the camera in the desired rotation and also reinforces the retaining clips ensuring your camera doesn't fall out.

I did notate the handle was slightly harder to pull to release the tailgate. That however was after the electronic lock assembly was installed. In a test fitting prior to that, it performed just as the original did. So IMO this product works perfectly and the harder pull was that of the power locking assembly.

I would 100% buy this product again.

I am super pleased with my purchase and the product in general. I elected this as a more factory looking camera.

I have taken out competing products over the years, and replaced them with these. I always had predictable results and could count on these to work time and time again.

I always prefer the stubby over the standard length as they were always a better quality. I think the stubby allows you more room to put bennies behind the contact and have room to slide the collar into the hole.

I always used a collar with my installs. I would take a razor knife and on the 3 ribs of the stubby trim away about 1/8 to 1/4 of an inch worth of the spline near the tip. Start little and increase the size of you need to rather than ruining the contact by removing to much of the spline. This will allow the stubby to fully seat into the collar and if done precisely, the stubby will snap into the collar. I came up with this as I always had them pushing out of the collars.

If you drill that collar hole just a little too big or the bit wobbles and the collar will not stay in. Take your staple gun and shoot a staple into the wood just back from the edge of the hole you drilled. That staple will be going into the side of the 3/4 hole for the collar. Flatten that staple out with your pliers. When you push that collar into place you'll very likely have a very hard time getting it back. At least you will not have a customer calling saying hey I closed the door on the contact.

title: Installed in this professionals home.
text:
I once upon a time was a installation tech for several large name security companies. I would pull these units and replace them with what ever we were using. Nothing wrong with these panels mind you. Its just like other industries, you put the supplied equipment in.

I however learned a few things about these panels. All of it good. When I moved into my home. I installed this unit in my home. It has been a valuable piece of my home security for years now. I have installed 4 major brands excluding this one and by far I have had fewer issue's with this than any other.

Programming may be a little on the intimidating side if your not use to such things. But its easily done and I think the average user could do it as well. This unit has been almost touch free for me for 6 years now. The only thing I had to do was replace a bad backup battery which can be found here on Amazon or through local battery retailers. Which that life span for the battery is not bad in my experience. I went with an upgraded keypad with a full digital read out. Its not really necessary, I mean how often are you standing and staring at the keypad. Its out of the way and often forgotten. Having said that any systems I install will have just such a keypad as it making programming much easier in my experience.

You can't go wrong with this system.

As many others here have stated I purchased the M1XEP to automate security messages to my iOS device. The remote programming software or RP is the perfect way to program the system.

title: Good connector.
text:
I have used these for years and made countless patch cords and full run cables. I have two jacks in my home that the plug snaps into easily. It however is a pain to get out requiring some force. I have issues in that jack with factory patch cables as well. That means to me its a plugin issue and not one of these ends.
They work great and I cannot see me ever using another product. I think they are expensive, well slightly. I usually buy these from Lowes and usually wait till I absolutely run out. So its my own fault for not purchasing these from Amazon and saving a few buck and making my price point better.

But truth one told you get what you pay for. I have yet to have one of the ends simply break, even after years of use. So the money is worth it. I would recommend theses to anyone looking to make their own cables. Its easy and you can do it too. It you don't think so just youtube it.

Do understand that you will make some mis-wires when you start making your own cables. Its easy to do, even if you have doing it for years. The best way to get proficient at it is to make cables, and crimp ends. If you make a mistake its a learning experience. You will get better. Even if you think you wired the cable correctly its not a bad idea to buy a cable tester and verify the wiring from end to end.

title: The cameras are good, picture is decent and with free cloud recording
text:
Its been a bit since I purchased cameras. I took the plunge and decide to update/replace my system with Arlo Pro's. The cameras are good, picture is decent and with free cloud recording. Its a no brainer.
I do not like the fact that you have to use a specific charger cable. I have multiple chargers around but the Arlo uses a proprietary charging system. I took off one star due top this dumb decision. I am happy with the camera system but hate it when companies try to lock you into a specific ecosystem even if its just a charging cord. Having said that I am generally happy and will most likely purchase other units.

I found the battery life to be sporadic when using longer record times. I have mine set at 1 min. with acceptable results. I did make a small self reporting system for battery notifications. I use Apple mail to parse the incoming mails and if it matches the name and sending address. It catches the camera name and then sends me a pushover notification to all my iOS devices. Using the group messaging feature from pushover you can send it to multiple users and devices. Currently it reports to all my Macs and then his/hers iOS devices ensuring no matter who is home we can charge the batteries. Currently due to 3 active kids and always letting my cameras record. I average about 3/4 a week charge time. This is compounded due to our cameras watch our rear yard with 11 highly active Siberian huskies. ;) So you could see why my battery charge times would not be indicative of the normal user.

I also don't like the fact the system setup a second wifi network along side my own. I would rather it use my existing network as I have worked hard to ensure it covers my property with extenders hardwired to the main router.

All in all those cons are not that huge of a deal and considering I am more of an advanced user and the camera system is geared to set it up and forget it for a normal end user. I would say it is well worth the investment. I would like to see the Pro version represent more self customization but thats just me.

Still very much liking my purchase. Still rocking Merlin firmware. No issues with stability or performance.

Edit:

I have moved from the standard firmware to an open version, search for "ASUSWRT-Merlin" if interested. This has fixed my IP address issue as well as made several other improvements. The changes are too many to mention. That doesn't mean new features but bug fix's and so forth. However, if non stock firmware is not your cup of tea. ASUS rolls many of the fixs into its firmware from my understanding. So if you want to maintain more stock and less bleeding edge. Simply wait a bit longer and most of the changes will make it to you.

I am still very thrilled with my purchase.

The only thing I find meh is the antennas tend to be more floppy than I would like. However if you set it and don't get behind it monkeying around they stay just fine. I am sure many of us know the cord hell behind the entertainment center. This past go round I eliminated 90% of that and hopefully made it future proof. The only area still needing tweaking is behind my router. :(

Oh, I also turned off the smart connect feature. I was having issues with some of my iOS devices and its just easier for me to keep 3 separate SSID's and use them.
I maintain the following.
1 - 2.4 GHz for the IOT devices such as smart lights switches, older iOS devices of the kid's, etc.
1 - 5 GHz for all higher capable devices, media streaming devices so forth. Also configured as failover protection in devices that can support multiple configs and use ethernet first and wifi on failure of ethernet.
1 - 5 GHz for the wife's MacBook / iOS devices, my MacBook / iOS devices etc.

I am going to experiment using the smart connect more soon and see if the previous usage changes.

title: SOLID Camera for the Price!
text:
What I really like the most:
Cable is the integrated thin type with a snap together 4 conductor connector near your trunk end
Cable is very long, reached the back of a 2006 4Runner with about 4 feet left to go. I can't imagine many consumer grade vehicles that it wouldn't be long enough for
Camera body is solid cast zinc junk of some sort, very dense, still zinc, but a good choice
Cord goes thru the cast threaded stem, so you only drill one hole and put the flanged nut on the back side
There was a white version to color match my newly purchased 2006 4Runner
Small, trim product packaging
Configurable via the jumper wires
Camera has a wide view - see below

Dislikes:
The wire from the camera could have been a few feet longer so that I could make the connection near my rear tail light
The paint may chip off quick, leaving zinc exposed, which would quickly corode and cause the rest of the paint to come off from adhesion failure
Camera is very wide view, perhaps too much
NUMBER ONE --- The adjustment wedges are facing the wrong way for standard installation! You can't angle the camera up at all from a standard horizontal surface. On my truck this means I can't see the horizon, mounted on the chrome part of the rear lift gate. To make it worse, the Boss BVCP9685A I paired it with has a "CHECK SURROUNDINGS" message across the entire top of the video monitor, so I can't see cars oncoming at all.

Overall a solid purchase for the price, small, tidy, good enough, although horribly ENgrish instructions (read them 5 times before you start!).

title: Cheap screws
text:
I'm going to give this the same review as a similar product I reviewed.

As convenient as this product makes hooking up networking cables, the cheap screws that come with this wall plate make installation a nightmare.

Do yourself a favor, if you have an extra light switch plate laying around, use those screws instead. I've installed two of these ethernet wall plates into two different low voltage mounting brackets. There are no threads in these mounting brackets. You're essentially creating the threads as you go. This necessitates a greater amount of torque and the screw heads are shallow. If using hand tools, this will require immense amounts of force to prevent stripping the heads. Normally, only a small, flat blade screwdriver is all that is required. But this installation works best if you have a powered screwdriver that will provide the necessary torque.

If you can run the screws in and out prior to installation, it may prevent some headaches. I did something similar to the first low voltage mounting bracket I purchased too.

You'll also find that if you have some screws from an existing light switch plate, that they have a deeper slot and are half the length. The provided screws were much longer than necessary. I replaced the screws on the second wall plate I installed after backing out the originals with a set of pliers after the heads were damaged.

To put this into context, I have the right tools and do more DIY than most other people I know.

With that having been said. If it had come with the same screws I replaced the originals for, I would have given it a 5-star rating.

title: Not sure if this should be used as a solar generator??
text:
I've sent off an email to customer support with a couple of questions. Based on that support feedback, I will adjust my rating and provide further comment.

This is really not being touted as a Solar Generator but was part of the search results when I was looking at replacing a solar generator that I had recently returned.

Please be advised that the charging port is somewhat proprietary. The 8.0mm charging port isn't very common but is similar to some of the Goal Zero products that are increasingly becoming more difficult to find if you'r looking at connecting to an MC4 solar panel.

It’s interesting that the only place I could find the manual online was from a site called manualslib.com. I wasn’t sure of it’s legitimacy and didn’t read through it fully but it seems to be a match to what was provided with the product. If I had read it first, I may have held out and looked at another product.

My biggest concern after having read the instruction manual is section 12. Service life of lithium ion batteries. Do not continue to charge the battery after it has charged completely. It would seem to indicate that there no sort of smart charging technology or battery managment that limits charging at a cutoff voltage? There is also no mention that I could find in the manual for a solar charge controller. I may not be able to keep my panel connected or will have to purchase one separately??

Some LED lights can be annoying but I am surprised that there is no LED for the sole purpose of showing that the device is on. Nor is there any indication within the manual that a short press is necessary to turn on the device, while a long press is needed to power the device off.

The device came with a 44% charge according to the indicator. After a couple of hours charging via the provided AC charge cord, it was noticed that the converter brick was very hot - 142°F according to my infrared thermal device. I was able to dissipate some of that heat by turning the brick on it's side so that there was less surface area on the kitchen counter and more exposed to the air.

UPDATE: 05/18/18
Well it's been a complete work week with no reply from Polaroid at the email address provided within the listing at polaroidenergy@digitalsupportdesk.com

But I have increased my rating from 3 starts to 4 stars. This was basically because I was able to confirm that the Goal Zero 8mm barrel plug indeed fits this device. There was no availability for the Goal Zero MC4 to 8mm so I had to purchase an alternative cable and cut off the end and substitute with Male / Femail 2.1x5.5MM DC Power Jack Plug Adapter Connectors
https://smile.amazon.com/gp/product/B01J1WZENK/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

Once I was able to connect my 50W solar panel, the results were fantastic. Even for a cloudy day I was able to increase the charge by 20%.

Alternatively I still do not know if this has a charge controller and may have to purchase one separately.

UPDATE:05/19/18
FAQs from the manual would ask, "Can I charge the PS300 while supplying power at the same time?" The answer states that the PS300 power supply unit can be used to charge the devices during the charging process of the unit itself. This may be true of the 5V USB outputs but not out of the Auto cigarette lighter port. I cannot comment as to the DC output port or Type-C port for I do not own those cables.

title: Happy with the installation
text:
I've only just installed this and my ASUS RT-N66U Gigabit Router had been working seamlessly for nearly 5 years. However, my son is nearly 11 years old and is spending more and more time online. Can you say "YouTube".

So I've been researching these new mesh wifi routers. I opted for the Eero after reviewing positive endorsements on TWiT.tv and it received the Runner-up pick from thewirecutter.com. Factor in EERO PLUS, price, and Alexa integration; it became the clear winner for our family.

Prices are a little high for this device compared to normal wifi routers but I couldn't put a price tag on a kid safe network along with easy to use Parental Controls. Shop for the best prices. I'm a avid Amazon shopper but I did find this elsewhere. There's also something to be said for an easy installation. No computer necessary. It's completely installed from your smart phone. Just follow the instructions. It's that easy!

The new generation 2 eero systems comes with an eero and additional beacons. As to the number of beacons that are needed, they provide recommendations but this will depend on the structure and layout of your home. The other thing to consider is the entry point of your homes internet.

Our two-story home is pretty square, constructed of your basic framing materials and drywall. I had previously run our cable internet to a centralized broom closet on the main level of the home about a year ago. It was a great location for our previous router. Having said that, installation of the main eero gave me similar to slightly improved performance throughout the house. I'm not sure if I really needed any additional beacons but I had purchased the recommended 1 eero + 2 beacons for a home with 2-4 bedrooms. With the simple installation of 1 beacon I was able to improve the "fair" wifi connection of a computer in our bonus room to "excellent". Improving download speeds marginally from 25 Mbps to 30 Mbps. Similar speeds could be reached from the mailbox as determined with fast.com. The second beacon still remains in the box.

title: NOT Made in USA...don't expect to use the PowerAlert Software on your home Mac
text:
First off, this was purchased for a 27" iMac for home usage.

I changed my previous configuration where my modem, router, NAS and iMac were all located in or on my office desk. These were all connected to a CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD that's been working perfectly for almost 5 years. After moving the location of the modem, router and NAS to a more central location; I moved the CyberPower UPS along with them. This left me for a need for a small UPS for the iMac only.

I originally looked at the smaller Cyberpower UPSs but then looked at the competition. The two I had narrowed it down to were similar in price, but the Tripp Lite offered a larger battery capacity. I then looked at their listings and found the Origin listed under the Product Information. The Tripp LIte stated that it was Made in USA or Imported while the Cyberpower was listed with a China origin. A little more searching and Tripp Lite is based out of Chicago. This essentially sealed the deal and the INTERNET 550U was ordered from Amazon.

Much to my disappointment, there was a large label on the side of the box clearly stating MADE IN CHINA. -1 Star

From the Manufacturer section of the listing would have you believe that the PowerAlert Software will work on the Mac OSX. After trying to find the PowerAlert Software from the Trip Lite web site would state the following...

"If you are a home or small office user, PowerAlert Local is for you. It allows you to monitor and control a UPS system connected to your computer through a USB or serial cable. It also supports automatic file saves and unattended computer shutdown during power outages."

Looking below this statement and there is no download availability for Mac OSX. The only Mac OSX software availability is called PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent and it states the following...

"If you need to automate computer shutdown during an outage without a USB or serial connection to a UPS system, or if you can’t use Java, PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent is for you. When it detects a user-selected event (such as low battery) broadcast by a network-connected UPS system, it initiates shutdown or hibernation after a user-defined delay."

Not quite what I was looking for but I did find that the native software within Mac OSX seems to do what I need it to do without the need of installing additional software. -0 Stars

This UPS is considerably light compared to the larger CyberPower. For whatever reason, I was expecting something heavier. It gives the impression that it's cheap in feel. Not necessarily of any fault of the device but some perceived notion that I had. But when coupled with the horrible, plastic smell; it comes off as another characteristic of a cheap, Chinese product. -1 Star

In summary, we had a long power outage last weekend while I was at the computer. The UPS worked as it should, allowing me to shut down the computer.

title: Great $20 USB-C Hub ( using a iPad Pro 11' inch 2018 )
text:
[[VIDEOID:6f0dc76b357c6acd70c1666d3f7b0b85]] I was in the market for a USB-C hub for my iPad Pro that I just recently got second hand. I have the Logitech Combo Touch keyboard case so I can turn it into a laptop, but I felt like I was missing extra functionality that could make me further use my iPad Pro in a professional way for school or anything else that I need to do. I did some research and I came across this $20 hub and I knew that it fit the criteria that I wanted out of a hub, but unsure how compatible it would be with my iPad since there isn't many in-depth reviews with them. I was mainly an audio jack since using AirPods all the time can get quite annoying with charging. I was thinking about ethernet, but honestly it's not really necessary since this is an iPad so it's not that serious.

All I can say is that the hub really worked well in all aspects. It has a metal casing that is cold to the touch like a macbook, a braided cable and all the ports work as intended, but with some caveats.

1. You can't change the audio level when the hub is plugged in. This is whether or not you are connected to a monitor/tv/projector with speakers or even playing off the tablet. You must unplug the hub, change the volume, then plug it back in. Not a lot of work, but it could be annoying. (I show it in the video)

2. You can't use the SD card reader and the microsd card reader at the same time, only once. But you can use a hard drive plugged into one of the USB slots and an SD/Microsd card at the same time. And if you want to do more, you can probably have a USB SD card reader to plug into one of the ports and read them all at once if you wanted to. Haven't tried it, but honestly might work.

3. You can plug in a mouse & keyboard and have everything else functioning at the same time. Charging, audio, hdmi, sd card, the iPad Pro can handle it all for the most part.

4. You can't change the source of audio if you have the HDMI plugged in and headphones in the audio jack plugged in. The iPad will only play sound out of whatever the HDMI is connected to. So you are better off with using AirPods/Bluetooth headphones if you want to use a monitor and listen to something independently.

I currently have no complaints and if something goes wrong then I'll update my review, but I'm satisfied with my purchase. So if you're looking for a relatively inexpensive USB-C hub for your iPad Air (3rd gen+)/iPad Pro (2018+) with an audio jack and everything else you might need besides an ethernet port, I'd recommend this hub.

I couldn't schedule it with the link/code they gave me. I had to call support. 4 hours later I am talking to a supervisor that tells me her agents were wrong. I had been told for hours it was just delivered o them and it would take a couple days for it to be ready to schedule. OK??? whatever.... that didn't even sound right, so I got the supervisor. She told me it was actually unable to be scheduled because they don't deliver to my area..??? She went on to say they need to find a 4th party shipper to accept my package and only once they confirm receipt of my item, then I can schedule it for delivery with them... I told them what was oging on, I explained I didn't want a TV that had been bounced around to 5 different shipping facilities and vendors. that it was going ot be late if they even could deliver it and that I had purchased a different TV from walmart of the same size, better quality, and delivery through fedex the whole way, no issues or 3rd party shippers. I thought everything was fine. Of course my phone starts ringing at 7 am on Saturday morning the 17th, and it's some random lady in a shady looking cargo van from Boise, Id, dropping off my TV... Not scheduled, no warning, Order was cancelled... Multiple supervisors had been spoken with at all three companies... So now I'm out another 300 bucks from buying a TV at walmart, and this thing arrived, I can't return it and I won't deal with those delivery services again. so... WOW
Never ever purchase Best Buy products via amazon. I blame Amazon for this only 1% for allowing a competitor to sabotage their prime day deal. Avoid Best Buy and never let anyone deliver anything to you from pilot Freight services... I have nothing bad to say about the company from Boise except that they didn't schedule deliver, but given who they had to deal with at Pilot, I don't blame them... I can't stress how much hatred I harbor for Pilot freight.... title: Love these
text:
First thing's first, it is important to understand what you are getting. This isn't a VR headset - you aren't going to be bringing these on a trip to play some beat saber. These are simply a screen that you can strap to your head.

Now that we have that out of the way, lets go into the things I love about these. Plugging these into a device is (usually) a breeze and you can get to consuming your content on a virtual screen in no time. The included blackout shade is a great addition, giving you the choice between maintaining situational awareness of your surroundings, or closing yourself off to the world and immersing yourself in the content.

I particularly like using these on a plane. It is great to be able to shut out everything that is going on around you and just watching content without your seatmates peeking over to see what you are watching. I do recommend using in-ear headphones since on or over ear types of headphones can get uncomfortable when combined with the glasses.

If you wear glasses, I suggest purchasing prescription lens inserts - it will really make your experience just that much better.

I think it is really smart that these are powered by whatever device they are plugged into. This allows the device to be less bulky and lighter; hence more comfortable for long term wear. The downside being, your device will consume power quicker. This can be mitigated with a wireless charger (since your glasses are plugged into your device).

I am not a huge fan of the iphone adapter solution, but it does work, and I find the experience better on iphone than other devices I have tried (samsung phone, iPad pro, and laptop).

title: Bought used and highly recommend
text:
TLDR: Used or not, the newest base kindle is a great buy for anyone looking for a good e-book reader. The features of the higher end models are nice to have, but by no means need to have. The money you save on the device can be put toward more books to actually read, which, at the end of the day, is what we are all here for.

This is my second time buying a used kindle device (the last one was an Oasis). I have to say, it is my preferred way to buy Kindles. The Kindle I purchased this time was in Used-Acceptable condition (I believe that is the lowest condition amazon warehouse sells used products- the rest go to woot or get recycled).

When I unboxed it, I found that it had very minor scratches on the bezel and back- visible from only certain angles - all just superficial surface scratches, nothing gouged into the plastic. Even if it cost more (I paid less than $40 for it) I wouldn't be annoyed in the least to find the very faint, surface scratches on this device. I have zero regrets and would do it again. Not only that, but I was pleasantly surprised to see that special offers was turned off on the device despite the fact that it was sold as 'ad supported' (it is likely the previous owner had turned them off and amazon just never turned them back on before selling the device - I wouldn't expect all used device to have it turned off, but it was a nice bonus to see that I got lucky and saved the $20 removal price).

Device works just like new and I am very happy with it. This is my second Kindle (and 7th e-ink device). My last Kindle was the second version of the Oasis. I traded that in to get the discount on the new paperwhite, but I am still waiting on it to ship (looks like I will get it in Late November)- hence the purchase of a cheap device to have on hand. This version of the Kindle has most of the features of the second version of the Oasis minus:
-Dark mode - I liked this mostly because I found the automatic light settings to be too bright most of the time and I liked to read in bed.
-Auto-light settings - Often too bright and I would manually adjust it anyway (or my hand would cover the light sensor and the device would suddenly get bright).
-Page buttons - Nice to have, but definitely not a need to have. The way I hold my reading devices is usually from the bottom anyway, so the touch turn is the most ergonomic.
-Waterproof - I tried reading in the bath once. It wasn't for me. I don't really sit and read in places I am going to get wet.
-Resolution - 167ppi may sound low, but when compared to mass market paperbacks, printed on recycled paper, I would say the text looks about the same - perfectly legible. Plus, you can change the font type and size to suit your taste, so it is superior to most printed text.
-Option for cellular data - Looks like Amazon may be phasing this out since it isn't available on the newest paperwhite. I rarely used it, but it was nice to know that I would be able to buy a book on the go without having to connect to public wifi if I really wanted to.

The current Oasis and Paperwhite also have warm lights in addition to the normal lights (which is the main appeal of the paperwhite for me). Again, not a deal breaker for a device, but it is nice to have.

title: Even 12 years old, this thing is still in use
text:
I know this reader has been out of production for a long time, but I felt like I needed to send it a little love as I have been using it again and just realized it is over 10 years old.

Lets start off with what this device is missing:
-Comfort light
-Wifi
-Bluetooth
-Expandable memory
-Audio output for audio books

With all the features that you expect to see in a modern e-reader, you may be asking yourself why I would rate this device so highly. While this device only carries 512MB of internal, non-expandable memory, I find that I can easily carry a library of over 300 books. The contrast of the e-ink screen is great for books; though it should be noted that it only has 8 levels of gray. This device is definitely a text only device - no comic books, graphic novels, PDFs, or manga here. With all these draw backs I keep bringing up, who do I love this thing so much? It is reliable. I know it is always there when I need it. If I want to dump a book onto it, I just fire up Calibre (since the old sony software is obsolete and they recommend adobe editions - no thanks). I rarely find a book I can't put onto this device with Calibre.

I don't use this device as much as I use to, but there are times like when I want to trade in a kindle to upgrade to the newest model and I am waiting for the trade in and release of the newest model and I will be without my kindle for a month. It is times like that where I dust off the old PRS-300 and load it up with books for the time without a kindle and I am reminded of why I love this device. It is simple, straight forward, rugged, and pleasant to stare at for an extended amount of time. I don't even mind that I don't have the comfort lighting - I even kind of prefer not having a light on my device because it just looks more like paper. It isn't any kind of hardship to turn on a light to read by.

Bottom line, this device is a delight despite all the modern features this is missing.

I work in an IT office and we have displays that need to be restarted from time to time - having a receiver in that device makes it so much easier to login from my desk. I love the fact that I can remap the buttons on the mouse and find that I do use them more than I expected. Plus the scroll wheel settings are not just functional (the continued scroll and the ability to turn on and off clicking), but also satisfying. I would definitely recommend this mouse, especially if you can get it at a discount.

If I could fix one thing it would be bluetooth. I rarely use this (or my logitech keyboard) over bluetooth on my laptop. I find that it frequently needs to be reset leaving me scrambling to find a wired mouse and keyboard to log back in and reconnect the devices. I think this is an issue with my laptop or WIN10 more than an issue with the mouse since this happened with other brand devices as well. title: A good reading experience
text:
I am so happy I picked up the Oasis. I couldn't justify the full price of the high capacity model without ads, so I bought refurbished and think it was a pretty good deal at the same price as the base model of the Oasis! It feels good in the hand, with or without a case on it (although a little slippery if you are just holding the bare metal).

I have owned 3 Sony ereaders, and 3 version of the nook (2 were e-ink) - this is the best all around ereader I have owned.

Pros
-Super light weight
-Battery is good enough for at least a week, and holds its charge when left unused for weeks
-Holds a TON of books
-Easy to load books from other sources
-Easy to borrow books from Overdrive (public librarys)
-Lighting works fine
-Inverting colors makes for the best night reading when paired with the lighting
-Included mobile data makes books available almost anywhere (lets be honest, this isn't necessary for most people - most useful if you travel out of the country)
-Physical buttons for page turns reduces the changes of having annoying smudges on the screen
-Screen material fairly smudge proof

Cons
-The price
-Screen can be a little reflective under harsh, fluorescent lighting - this seems to be a common issue with readers with a touch screen. Not terribly bad, but notable enough that I thought I should mention it
-The metal is cold in the winter
-I don't like most of the case options - I didn't buy such a slim reader to buy a shell to bulk it up.

title: Keyboard is pretty good, I would pass on the mouse.
text:
Lets start by defining what this set is and is not: it is a set of devices that are designed to be aesthetically pleasing. It is designed to be minimalist. It is not designed to be ergonomic.

I liken the keyboard to the apple wireless keyboard; keys feel like a laptop and you can't adjust the angle of the keyboard unless you stack up stuff under the back of the keyboard.

I do like the design of these. They are good looking devices and have an interesting magnetic battery compartment. If sleek and minimalist is what you are going for in your work space, these fit the bill.

These devices are plastic. I don't find this to be a major drawback, but some might have issues with it.

I have already stated, this set is not ergonomic. The mouse is especially awkward to use (unless you like the generally flat styles mouses like the apple magic mouse). My everyday mouse is the Microsoft Arc mouse (the older hinged one, not the one that bends). If you like the programmable back button on your mouse, you will find that you miss it on the microsoft designer set.

Pairing is where most people seem to have the biggest problem with this set. I also had issues. I am running Win 7 64 bit and have bluetooth on the computer. I had the most current BT4.0 drivers, but still ended up having to check the manufacturer's driver site for an additional driver. Even after installing a new driver, I was only able to get the keyboard to work consistently. The keyboard seems to work well and even when I start up my computer. The mouse, on the other hand, was less forgiving. No matter what I did, I could only SOMETIMES get the mouse to correctly pair. The computer could see it, but it wouldn't save the device or even stay connected after the pairing was complete. I am sure with more noodling around, I could probably get it connected, but for me, it isn't really worth it (I like my old Arc Mouse better). I bought the set with the intent of using just the keyboard, so it was not really a huge issue for me.

It seems that this set is intended for devices that use with Windows 8 or above, so keep that in mind when purchasing. I am using 7 and it generally works, but it is going to be most dependent on the Bluetooth drivers you have installed.

Pro-Tip: Look for used sets. A lot of people buy this keyboard thinking it will be easy to set up, then return it when they realize that you need bluetooth on your computer or you will have to buy a dongle. Currently, there are sets that are like new at 30% the suggested retail (half what they are actually selling for). Buy from Warehouse deals and the purchase is guaranteed by amazon (just like any new item that is sold by amazon). I think the deals that can be had on this set make it worth while for someone who is looking to try out the set, but not sure if it will play nice or if they will even like it.

title: Great antenna at a great price
text:
I was a bit leery about the whole OTA situation where I live. I live out in the Temecula Valley/Lake Elsinore area of southern California. The major networks broadcast from just over 60 miles away and this is a mountainous area. FCC and TV Fool showed there was a good chance of picking up channels in my area provided I mount a big enough antenna high enough (recommended 30 feet above ground level).

I picked up this antenna as a warehouse deal, so it was likely a returned product. I was a little sad to see that some of the metal forks had some bends in them (probably due to a poor re-packing job), but I went ahead and flattened them out. I mounted the antenna on a mast on top of my patio cover (for about 16 feet of elevation) and pointed it towards Mt Wilson. Surprisingly, I picked up 76 channels! That is even more channels than FCC had projected. This is without any amplifiers or anything. I am very pleased with this antenna!

For the price this antenna is definitely work a try! Worst case, you end up returning it.
