I have even used it to mess with people at restaurants that have a lot of TVs (calm down, I only did it once to see if it would work and it did).

title: Bought them in a pinch and they have lasted more than 3 years
text:
I needed to pick up a pair of headphones while I was travelling when mine broke. The only place I had available to me was a place that only had these and JVC marshmallows for earbuds. I am not a fan of the JVCs (I have tried them and find their foam tips to be scratchy in my ear); so while I don't particularly care about the hype of Beats and definitely am not a fan of Lady Gaga, I went ahead and purchased these - they at least looked well made.

I have had these earbuds for nearly three years now and I am happy with how well these have held up. The design of these earbuds makes them distinctive, which is ok, I guess. The inline mic make them a great for taking calls in the car. There is no inline volume - just an answer button (that can also control music- play, pause, and next). The tips are comfortable and this set comes with a lot of options! The cable is tabgle free and shows no signs of weakness.

title: It was ok, but not without issue.
text:
This GPS tracker is a little on the heavy and bulky side, but considering that I used it with a system that uses a chest strap, it wasn't a huge inconvenience. The GPS tracker did connect to my FT60 without hassel. The AA battery lasted long enough for a couple weeks worth of workouts, but I wish it used rechargable instead.

My biggest complaint is that the GPS tracking would get points too slowly and would give me odd routes that would consistently cut corners by a lot more than I found acceptable. It was still better than nothing and probably the best on the market when I bought it back in 2011.

I no longer seriously train due to knee problems, so I don't use this product any more and have moved on to Fitbit trackers for a more casual workout routine!

title: but I can still say I am mostly happy with this remote
text:
I have had this remote for a couple years, but I can still say I am mostly happy with this remote! It is easy enough to program and use; you can program special functions (like when you want to play a blueray, it automatically turns on the TV, Blueray player, and surround sound with a single button.

There are a couple things that are a pain:
-Frequent requests for you to update the remote (I usually ignore them)
-The rechargeable battery life is just OK.

I do love that I can use my phone since the remote works through your home network though!

title: Pretty design, poor execution.
text:
Oh Samsung... I had such hope for you, but then you let me down. The screen on this is BEAUTIFUL - it is a curved OLED screen. As beautiful as it was, the face of this tracker was still too wide for my wrist. Wearing this correctly, it had big gaps between the edges of the face and my wrist. I hate that! Also, the wide screen was odd to use. The app left a lot to be desired too. This device is ultimately a let down - spend you money elsewhere!

I just got the Fitbit Surge last month and it was the tracker I have been waiting for.

title: A fantastic luxury device for digital arts!
text:
This tablet is great for photo and video editing. There is very little learning curve for this device - you can generally pick it up and intuitively use it. The express keys can take a bit of time to get used to, but you get the hang of them pretty quickly (as long as you don't keep changing them because you are indecisive)!

Is this a must have? Not by any means, but it is definitely a fantastic luxury.

The pen accuracy is fantastic and I love the pressure sensitivity, with so many levels of sensitivity.

title: Love this tablet
text:
I am a bit biased since I love my Note phone (despite the fact that I replaced it with the Galaxy SIII), but I absolutely love my Note 10.1. I am a crafty type and a technology type as well. The combination of being able to utilize technology and creativity makes this a winning product in my book.

The stylus technology of the Note family of products a real stand out for anyone who wants to be able to be creative with their devices! You won't find this level of accuracy in any other tablet currently on the market. If you are fed up with using the annoying rubber nub stylus, look no further. This device has a stylus that has a precision tip that doesn't feel like you are using a crayon to write on your screen!

Additionally, the processing power of this device won't leave you wishing for more. You will be scribbling and browsing and whatever else you do with your tablet with ease!

I highly recommend this device!

title: Better suited to those stepping up from point and shoot than a step down from DSLRs
text:
I tried this camera out for a couple days before ultimately returning it.

Pros-
Upgrade-ability of the glass
Quick focus
Lots of options

Cons-
Most of the features that you have at your fingertips on a DSLR are buried in menus
No hot-shoe (can't use a better flash)
Proprietary glass (if they stop supporting this you are screwed- if you upgrade to full DSLR, you need all new lenses

I believe those upgrading from a point and shoot will be satisfied but DSLR users may be underwhelmed if they are used to being able to control most of their settings easily.

This still makes a good camera for DSLR users that want something that is better than a point-and-shoot but smaller than their DSLR, as long as they are willing to give up the ease of adjusting settings (example, your dial has 4 settings- none are M, A, S, or P- get ready to dig through menus).

title: One of the most durable screen protectors out there
text:
I have been using Invisible Shield on my various electronics since 2006. This stuff is, by far, the best screen protector out there.

Pros:
-Stays on devices without peeling if applied correctly
-Takes a beating without scratching
-Free lifetime replacement

Neutral:
-A little bit of a process to apply it correctly, but when it is done right, it is worth it. If done wrong, it is replacable.

Cons:
If you don't use enough of the spray, you will get micto bubbles under the shield (I don't know about you, but they bother me)- USE SPRAY LIBERALLY!!!

The micro bubbles are bad enough to me for a loss on 1 star, but otherwise, I love this stuff, and I haven't found anything else out there that even comes close.

title: Great little tablet
text:
First and foremost- What every prospective tablet user needs to consider: What am I planning on doing with my tablet?
For most users, tablets are for entertainment and are considered a luxury item. They aren't good for working on school work, or anything that requires a lot of typing, so for most people, these devices are for consuming media (news, videos, social networks...).

Why pick the Wifi only:
When I was looking at Xooms at the local electronics establishment, I was confronted with the decision of getting the $599 Xoom Wifi or the $799 Xoom 3G/Wifi (upgradeable to 4G at a later date at no cost). For me, while 3G was tempting for convenience, it was still a pretty easy decision to buy the Wifi only device. With the 3G, you are tied into a service contract. If you go with Verizon's service (which is advertized with the device), you only pay $599 for the device, but you have to pay $20 a month for 24 months. On top of that, you can only use 1GB of data. For a device that is going to be used for the consumption of data (especially videos), I don't want to be limited to only 1GB. Another decision point was the fact that I knew my Xoom would be used mostly at home, where I have a Wifi network, or at local eatting establishments that provide free Wifi. The real nail in the coffin on this decision was that my 4G phone is capable of wireless teathering and my data plan is unlimited- taking that into consideration- there really is no need to pay for an additional data plan.

The Device- an out of the box look:
Out of the box, you find the approximately 1.5 lbs device, power cable, and a couple booklets. I would have been nice to have a sleeve for the Xoom, but Motorola doesn't provide any type of protection for the tablet. I made sure to pick up a [[ASIN:B004S748UY ZAGG invisibleSHIELD for Motorola Xoom (Screen) (MOTXOOMS)]] to make sure my screen stayed pristine. The device is a solid little tablet. The back id 4/5 aluminum and the top part of the back case is rubberized plastic.

The hardware feels solid. Additionally, the layout of the device generally makes sense. The power button was a little confusing, but once I found it on the back, the idea really grew on me. It will be a little wierd when it comes to accessories, but I have no complaint about the device itself. Next to the power button, there is the HD camera lense with LED flash. Having an HD camera is nice, even if shooting pictures on a tablet isn't really practicle. The back of the device also includes stero speakers that are surprisingly loud for a device of this size.

All of the connectors (power, usb, dock...) are all located on the bottom of the device, except the headphone jack. Not sure I am a fan of this oddity, but I have yet to use headphones, so it is not really an issue to date. Also, the volme buttons are located on the left side of the device and are sufficiently easy to reach and use.

On the face of the device, there is a forward facing camera- this is great for video chatting. While GTalk works, Skype currently does not support video chat on this device (app issue, not hardware). There is also a light senseor- I hate the light sensor- I sometimes find that the brightness of the screen changes abruptly by a huge amount because I accidently put my thumb over the sensor. The best fix for this is to just turn off the auto adjustment.

Orientation:
Deviating from the norm, the Xoom is built to be oriented in landscape mode rather than portrait mode. With the 10 inch screen, landscape works great. I find that I am able to thumb type on the on-screen keyboard without straining much to reach the keys in the middle. The size is really what makes landscape work well with this tablet. In portrait, I (like many others) find that the device is a little bit hard to balance- feeling a little top heavy. It isn't so bad that the device is difficult to use- it just takes a little getting used to.

Android:
The android 3.0, Honeycomb load on this device is great. Many who don't use android or are iPad users will probably find that the device will take a little bit of learning to get used to. I am an android user (though my phone has an older version of android), and found that I was able to fully use and understand the device in 30 minutes of playing with it. The learning period may take up to a day, but once you fiure it out, you will notice that the controls really make sense and are easy to find when you need them.

Overall, I love this little device. There are some minor little design dislikes, but nothing that impacts my 5 star rating of this device!

title: Excellent for getting wide angles on small cameras- not a fan of the magnet
text:
Overall, this little lens is perfectly sufficient for gaining view angle for your pictures.

The only thing I didn't like with this lens had nothing to do with the actual lens- the thing I don't particularly like is the little metal ring that you stick to your device so you can attack the lens magnetically. The little metal ring has a sharp corner on it that is annoying when you are handling your device. This may not be a big deal for devices you only use once in a while, but if you decide to stick one of the three rings that you get to your cell phone, you will notice it and your hands will drag over it frequently.

Other than that I like the lens and think it is a great non-permanent accessory for your camera!

title: Excellent value for what it is- a reader with an LCD
text:
First off, for those of you buying this product expecting the e-ink experience, you are wrong. This isn't an e-ink screen, if that is what you are looking for, go with (a) the original nook, (b) the kindle, or (c) any of the other e-ink dedicated e-readers on the market.

This iteration of the nook is marketed towards certain select categories of readers:
-The Magazine reader
-Students with text books that have graphics
-Childrens' books with lots of pictures
-Comic book readers

If you notice, these are categories of readers that benefit from the ability of the reader to handle color graphics, which is something e-ink can't yet do!

PRICE
For the price, you are getting an android tablet with limited functionality, though, with some technical knowledge, it is possible to unlock this device to be able to fully take advantage of the android market (though it may void your warranty, so do it at your own risk). Similarly sized android tablets go for prices starting at double the price of the nook color, but they come with full functionality. Another device this has been compared to is the iPad- which runs at about twice the price as well for the very base model. On the price point, you are definitely getting a decent deal, though, you are sacrificing some of the functionality for the the reduced cost.

Also note, you are not getting 3G access or any other cellular service to access the market- unlike the original nook, that came with the free mobile access to be able to make purchases from the nook market on the go. The likely reason for the lack of mobile access is due to the fact that this device runs a lot faster and features a full web browser- this increases the speed and easy of the user to access web content- which would be undesirable to any phone service that hosts access because it would reduce the service that their paying customers get. Instead of mobile data service, users have the option of accessing the BN market and the full internet through wireless. With today's cell phone technology, many phones are able to be set up as wireless hotspots that users can use to get access on the go- when they are away from their home network. Overall, this isn't a big deal to me, but I am sure some original nook users depend on that free mobile service to get access to the BN market, so this would be a draw back for you for sure.

WEIGHT
Honestly, this device does run a little on the heavy side, however, I do believe that it is slightly lighter than it's predecessor. Still, for the e-reader market, it is heavy. For the tablet market, it is a little more reasonable. The weight is a sacrifice, but as long as you aren't trying to read while laying on your back, you should be ok.

USER FRIENDLINESS AND EXTRA FEATURES
I find this device to be quite simple almost immediately. Every function that I have looked for has been where I expect it to be and everything has worked smoothly for me. The page controls while you read work great, and I love that they now give you the option to tap to turn the page rather than having to swipe like you did with the last version of the nook.

The full web is pretty easy to use once you get used to typing on a touch screen keyboard (which is always annoying).

This device also integrates with your facebook, twitter, and google accounts. This is great for the avid readers that want to be plugged into their social media.

Another feature that is nice to have on the reader is Pandora- it is a nice added bonus to have internet radio available on the reader.

One thing I wish this device had was access to android market, but I guess you can't have everything.

OVERALL
I like this tablet. I think it was a good buy and I would buy another one if this one broke. For the price, you are getting an underpowered tablet, but it still has access to the full internet- which you can use multiple windows in. It is primarily a reader, which makes me wish it were as easy on the eyes as e-ink, but for the market it is being geared towards, you can't really complain about that!

title: Good concept- having difficulty with the application!
text:
GorillaPods are generally respected in the photography world, but I can't bring myself to give a high rating based on reputation alone. I bought this product expecting to be wow-ed, but I find myself with an adequate product at best. Overall, this product will get the job done, but it may be a pain in the butt getting there. The magnets in the feet are a great idea, but if sometimes, if the weight of the video camera is too much, it will slide. What I hate is the head- the turning function doesn't work as well as it should. There is a button on the side that is supposed to release the adjustment arm (the arm you turn and tilt to move the head of the tripod), but when you push it, it doesn't re-engage to lock the arm like it should, so trying to tilt and pan is difficult. I find that I have to move the arm really slowly or else it will slip and the arm will move but the head of the tripod won't pivot. It is frustrating.
Trying to fix my tilt and pan problem, I tried adjusting the tension- if I go tight, it is really hard to move the head, and makes video jerky. If I loosen, the arm doesn't lock in like it should and then it doesn't work. I will keep trying to get it right, because I really want to love this product, but for now, it is 3 stars at best.
Also note- this will work great if you don't want to move the camera around!

title: Great camera!
text: I absolutely love my Nokon D5000.  As far as DSLRs go, this is a pretty easy camera to operate, though, for someone who is used to only point and shoot cameras, you may find that it will take a little bit of time and reading before you can use your camera to the fullest potential.  I recommend picking up a guide for this camera if you are not a frequent SLR or DSLR user!  Overall, the price is great for what you get!  While it is larger than a point and shoot, it is still on par as far as portability- it is smaller than some of the higher end DSLRs.  The display is awesome since it flips out and rotates- this is great for tripod use!  The pictures are nice and crisp, but again, you should know how to use a DSLR to get the best results!  If you want to learn a new DSLR or if you want to upgrade to a better camera- this camera is great and I can't recommend it enough!

title: Good but not great
text:
This is for the “WiFi 6 Bluetooth YABER Pro V8 450 ANSI Lumen Native 1080P HD Projector” (more people should put their product in the review).

I really want to like this but I’m having a hard time.

First the positives….

It is lightweight. It doesn’t make much noise. The keystone adjustments are great. At about 8-10 feet from the screen it is really really good. It is a good value for the money.

Now the negatives…

It won’t connect to WiFi. At all. So I can’t update firmware or cast from my wireless devices.

I’m connected using Apple TV and I can’t get to the projector management screen to make any adjustments. I have to disconnect Apple TV and then I can access the projector menus. This is a real inconvenience.

8-10 feet seems to be the sweet spot. But I moved mine back to 16 feet so I could have it dead center to the screen. While I am still within the focal range, the focus does not seem crisp and the light appears slightly too dim. I read somewhere that a firmware update may help this… but I can’t connect the unit to the internet to get the update. This is almost a deal breaker for me. If I was still within my return window I would probably return it.

The lens cap can be difficult to remove and you can very easily touch the lens when removing the cap. It should be much easier or it should screw on.

Overall I would give this “good” but not great marks. Value for the money is good but not great if you can’t use all the features or suffer from mediocre focus and brightness. You may be happy. I’m almost regretting my choice.

title: Awesome upgrade from the original fire stick
text:
I have the original fire stick and I love it. I have 2 TVs, 1 in my living room and 1 in my bedroom. Because I love the original fire stick (gift from my son ❤) I finally decided to get a 2nd for my bedroom. I bought this upgraded fire stick on Prime Day. I got it yesterday. I'm amazed that the remote can link to my TV and control the TV. I read from other reviewers that it powers on their TV. If this is true, then I will be ecstatic. My TV remote is HUGE and I hate it. The TV was built in 2006 so the TV and remote are huge. Both work great. I was originally going to just use my Chromecast as I love the casting from room to room without losing my place. However, since the fire stick remote controls the TV I am rethinking my thoughts. I was amazed that the fire stick was soooooo easy to set up. It recognized my Wi-Fi ID and my password for the WI-FI. I did not need to give the code. I think that it picked up all the information that the original fire stick has, including Wi-Fi information. This makes the upgraded fire stick the easiest set up ever. I also noticed that the speed of the processor is incredible. Not once have I noticed any buffering. I do get buffering from my other 3 devices. Guess it's time to replace my original fire stick with this one. This fire stick replaced my Roku which I've had for years and still works fine. The reason why I replace the Roku was that Roku seems to be incompatible with Hulu Live (love it BTW). It keeps shutting off the program that i am watching making me yo go back into my Hulu account again. Just imagine, you're watching a show and just at the most interesting part, it flicks and goes back to the home screen. Ahhhhh!!!! Since this fire stick performs so well, I'm thinking of not even using my 2 Chromecasts anymore. Now that's progress! The 2 Chromecasts do have some lagging and that's why I'm thinking of just using the fire stick and buying a new one for the living room. If anyone was on the fence about buying this fire stick, don't be. This purchase was well worth the money. Go for it!! I was going to upgrade my internet because I thought the lagging was them, nope. This fire stick has out performed my wildest dreams. Go buy this, fire stick you won't be sorry!! Oh one last thing, I've noticed that some reviewers have complained about opening up the battery case. It's actually easy, you simply press dojwn on the circle at the top and push the cover to the opposite side. You will hear a little pop. That's releasing the lock. Then you will see a small space where the circle is, just stick your fingernail (presuming your nail is not so bitten to the point where it's below the nail line) and push. Easy peasy! Amazon clearly have their products hooked up! I love the ease of Amazon, hands down. ❤. If my opinion changes about the upgraded fire stick, I'll post an update.

UPDATE: Its very easy to navigate the fire stick but if you can't find something all you have to do is ask Alexa and she will find it for you. It also fully takes charge of your TV. There is nothing you need With the original clunky remote. Unless you want to access your HDMI ports. But with all that the fire stick offers, you don't need another dongle. I will be using the fire stick only. It's so wonderful to use one small, comprehensive remote. Basically Amazon has updated the fire stick to make it a universal remote. Now I'm going to buy a remote cover so I can easily see my new "universal" remote in the dark. ❤😎

I purchased a second Fire Stick from a big box store. I'm sorry that I did. When you buy a Fire Stick through Amazon, they load it with your account information making set up super easy. When you buy one through the box box stores they are generic and set up was a bit more difficult. Suggestion folks but your Fire Stick through Amazon and forget the big box stores! Wish I would have known this before I purchased my second one! Never again!!

title: Downloading may be an issue...
text:
I own a DM-620 and love it. But I left it out of state and needed another recorder asap. Spending $140 did not make me happy, however I am a fan of Olympus, so I did it.

The extendable USB. Seriously, what are people thinking? This can maybe plug into my laptop, but a PC? No. Am I going to crawl behind my tower? Well, actually, I had to and it would not fit into the space available for plugs. I have USB ports on the front, but they are sunken for cords. I could not download the recorder on my PC. I had to hunt down and purchase a USB double plug (male to female) and then it was fine. But how annoying and impractical. Seriously, Olympus? What were/are you thinking?

The device itself is virtually weightless, 2.5 oz. Almost to the point of feeling cheap. I don't mind that when I am packing, but some weight makes the item easier to hold on to.

Since the recorder needs to plug into the side of a laptop to charge, I could not replenish the Ni-MH (rechargeable) battery. It does run on one AAA, the DM-620 uses two AAA. Luckily, I could use an alkaline battery until I found the cord. I haven't switched back yet, but I will.

The traditional Olympus quality is there in the sound. It has three mics, sound canceling and many features I have yet to use. Sound does matter, so I offer 4 stars. But ease of use should be up there in importance. When recording is part of your business, you don't want to have difficulty plugging a device into something.

title: This computer is a great value, handles most games of today, and can be upgraded
text:
This computer is a great deal for the money. It has been able to run every game I have thrown at it from simpler games such as Heroes of the Storm to more graphically intensive games such as Destiny 2. The quality is good and having the name brand and warranty behind it is even better.

Regarding the internal specifications, here's a quick rundown for you:

1. The processor is rarely taxed, even with multiple applications open (I use dual monitors, but be aware this rig has 2 display port adaptors and one HDMI so you will most likely need an adaptor) and can be exchanged up to an i7-7 series.

2. The RAM is acceptable for my dual monitor use and handles multiple applications simultaneously. You can expand the RAM to 16gb using two 8gb ddr4 ram (only two slots).

3. The motherboard is good and can handle everything so far, I don't predict you would need to change this during the life of the computer.

4. The storage is a Toshiba 1TB mechanical drive. It's pretty slow and can be taxed quickly depending on what you're doing. Most of the time if you notice the computer slowing it's due to this component. I would recommend you add a 500 GB or 1 TB SSD eventually, but note you will need a new power supply explained below and it would be useful to increase the RAM and exchange the processor.

5. The power supply unit is 80 bronze rated, and is a cheap Chinese made 300 W supply. It does the job, but one of the first components I would recommend you exchange is the PSU. Try for 500w or above.

6. The video card (graphics card) is a great quality card, although note this card doesn't look very aesthetically pleasing. It's a shortened card to fit in the case. The GTX 1060 can handle most new games on max settings. It's VR ready. It was the best card out there just a few years ago. It can be upgraded to a MINI gtx 1080 if the PSU is upgraded.

As explained above the computer can be upgraded and for the price this is the best deal you can find on the market (unless you find a Black Friday deal, notice the date of this review) but I would highly recommend this unit to most gamers.

text: So after 6 weeks of issues with my internet and countless hours on the phone with Spectrum support and field tech's, several of the escalation senior resources recommended that I purchase my own hardware.  Reason being...I work from home and dial into a VPN connection everyday all day and they have decided (without informing customers) that they were no longer going to support VPN on residential accounts.  The Support person said that I should go Asus since it was one of the few routers that supported Cisco Anyconnect.  Purchased and came within 2 days.  Put the antennas on, plugged it in a called into Spectrum for what SHOULD have been no more than a 15 minute call.... well, 2 1/2 hours later... when they changed the code from "spectrum owned" to "customer owned", the wifi went down immediately.  Not sure what Spectrum is doing these days but I had to upgrade to business class to get back to my job.  With business class, you actually get upgraded hardware but you HAVE to use their hardware.  Unfortunately, this one is going back.  I think it worked great while Spectrum "owned" the equipment in their systems.  Very fast. Just don't have time to try to make it work.

First of all, the print on the enclosed manual is tiny but I got it up and running without having to go through the entire manual so thank g-d for that! I have even gotten a new Mac in the time since I got this webcam and it was just a matter of plug and play. My new Mac and this camera kissed and become beautiful friends instantly.

I am getting a stand for it so that I can have my videos more at face level. I doubt if I will be making award-winning Oscars in the next week. However, I love this camera because it automatically focuses and it has been easy to use. In fact, I will be using this for production on my master's thesis and future YouTube production. It also takes a smaller background area than my previous camera which I really love.

Bottom line: Buy it! Good price and good quality.

Transparency: I have not used the remote and my foray into video production is preliminary.

title: Good beginning camera
text: Got this and had it up and going in minutes. Read the manual in less than 10 minutes. Although it has a wide angle and shows much of the room I am in, I will get that figured out by repositioning. For the money, it is a good little camera to start out with for initial use in webinars and meetings where you want your face seen. I especially like the fact that it has automatic focus. The only thing I don't like is that the manual is god-awful small with tiny font so that needs to just be bigger. Lastly, I am disappointed that it does not zoom in so my whole room does not show.

title: Great materials and build, but...
text:
This is one of the only leather covers I was able to find, and the quality of the materials is top notch. The fit and finish is great. The problem I have, and the only thing that keeps me from a 5-star review, is the built-in stand function.

On the back of the case is a tab that fits flush against the case, and I assume is used to hold the front cover in place, allowing one to watch or use the tablet in landscape mode. At least, I think that was the intended use. Apparently no one took the time to see whether the placement of the tab was correctly positioned so the tablet was properly balanced. It needs to be a bit lower. I work around this by using the notch as the cover holder, as shown in the picture.

All told, quality materials and craftsmanship, let down by a poor design choice.

title: Looks great, works great, but measure first!
text:
I bought this based on the following criteria: a high TDP capacity, lack of noise, good looks (sorry Noctua), and clearance for my RAM. I have an Asus Maximus X Code motherboard, and G.skill Trident Z RAM. As you can see from the picture, it fits. Make sure you install your RAM first, because it covers all the slots with the fan on.

So all said, this is a great cooler. Measure your case and RAM, follow the installation instructions, and it’ll work like a charm.

I don't know why I do this to myself, but I have bought several Belkin items over the years, and they never fail to underwhelm me. Take this case, for example.

I like how it's not bulky; I see people walking around with their Otterboxes, and yeah, they're protected, but they've sacrificed the look of their device on the altar of safety. I'll pass. The sheer color is not as sheer as the picture would lead you to believe, but it's not horrible.

No, what bothers me is the poor fit. I purchased mine from Amazon, and not some third party, specifically because it would be a genuine Belkin product. I suppose it is, because as I mentioned before, there's always something that disappoints me with every Belkin purchase. The sides, top, and bottom are loose on the phone, leaving space between the case and the phone. I've never seen another case like it, and I'm unlikely to ever purchase another Belkin product again.

title: From CRT to LED
text:
I've been using an old 19" CRT for the past few years. The picture is good, but let's face it: there's not a lot of real estate on a 19" monitor. Not to mention things like weight, size, and heat. Yes, it generated a lot of heat.

I finally decided to purchase a new, bigger monitor. I wanted LED back lighting for reduced energy consumption and a flatter panel, and I didn't care to purchase one with speakers. I plugged in my criteria, read the reviews, and selected this monitor.

First off, the display is big. Not in a massive sense; this thing weighs maybe a sixth of my old monitor, but in the sense that I can have multiple windows open, and not feel like it's crowded. I used a THX optimizer from one of my DVD's to set the color and brightness, and it looks really good. Oh, movies! Going from a 19" 4:3 monitor to a 23" 16:9 means that movies fill the entire screen, from narrow bezel to narrow bezel.

Overall, I'm really happy with this monitor. While the stand lacks any height adjustment, and the tilt is only minimal, I also wanted a monitor with VESA mounting. The plan is to procure two more of these for a triple monitor setup. Can't wait to see that.

title: A big improvement over the Smokin' Buds
text:
When my iPod buds finally died on me, I decided I wanted in-ear 'phones. However, I was short on cash, so I decided against the Shures, Etymotics, and the like. I saw the Smokin' Buds in a store for $[...], and gave them a shot.

First off, the sound wasn't terrible. It was at least on par with the Apple buds. I had problems with the fact that the sleeves wouldn't stay put in my ears for any reason, slipping out almost as soon as I'd inserted them. In addition, the cord was rather thin, and anytime it rubbed against my clothing, or heaven forfend, my jacket's zipper, it would create enough noise to drown out my music. The nail in the coffin was the small chrome ring on the left bud. I had foolishly thought it was structural, but when it popped loose it turned out to be merely ornamental.

I took them back for a refund, and sent off a letter to the company expressing my dissatisfaction with their product. Much to my surprise, I was invited to try another pair, with the promise that improvements had been made and I was sure to find them more to my liking.

The buds that arrived in the mail were the Full Metal Jackets. The difference in construction is night and day. Where the bulk of the Smokin' Buds is plastic, these are aluminum. The sleeves never slip from my ears. The cord is far more durable, and thicker as well.

The sound was quite boomy when I first tried them, but I let them run at high volume for 24 hours on static to loosen them up. This helped quite a bit, and the sound continues to improve. It's still bottom-heavy, but turning off the EQ function on my nano helped balance it out. I really like that I can run my nano at half volume and still hear everything clearly. In fact, I would caution against running them at full volume while they're in, as I'm certain one would suffer hearing damage. My battery life has improved tremendously. I'm very happy with the sound and the comfort of these buds. I can't think of a better set of earphones for the price... and the warranty is first-rate.

9 February 2008: I sent my FMJ's back for a warranty repair, which turned out to be a warranty replacement. The jack on my 9mm FMJ's had developed a short, and was causing the left 'bud to cut in and out.

I received an RMA number within moments of contacting them at their website, [...], and while I paid for shipping the 'buds back, they replaced them immediately, free of charge. Not only did they replace them with a new set, they sent the 11mm FMJ's. The jack is a bit longer, in order to provide better strain relief, I suppose. Otherwise, the build quality is identical. More importantly, the sound is far better balanced top to bottom, and while the bass is still great, it no longer dominates the sound spectrum as it did on my 9mm's.

In short, the 9's are really good, and you can't get anything better (in my opinion) at the price, but the 11's are worth the extra money. All the things that made my experience such a positive one with the 9's is improved with the 11's. Definitely a 5-star rating.

title: Works for your MAC with a workaround app!
text:
So far so good. I have a MAC Pro computer and laptop. The Clearlink app/disk does not work with Mac, but there are a couple of work arounds. You just have to search. I searched "Clearlink Bluray alternatives for MacOS". Found several applications. So keep in mind this machine costs more than the purchase price. Eventually, my computer recognized the machine on it's own, but I used an old version of Toast (a small app on the App store) and it worked great. The current Toast App is now a lot more expensive because it does more than burn disks, so I am happy I have the old beta version from a few years back.
The enclosed cords work well, the power cord should be longer, but it is adequate. The machine looks like it is all brushed silver, but it is white with a silver front. Heavy duty, and should be considered for office/home only, but that is what I wanted. Takes a long time to burn, but I think it is the same as a DVD burn, as far as time per gigabyte.
Overall, great burner that is worth finding the work around on my MAC. I am so excited to be able to condense my photo archives on fewer disks. Big time saver!

title: Router died but NETGEAR made things right again!  Very happy!
text:
I love this router and was crushed when the hardware failed recently. The performance can not be matched by my other router (linksys). It was very evident when I had to reconnect the old router again. My house is older and average in size w/full basement and I was able to get a great signal throughout with the Nighthawk. It was very easy to configure and keep the firmware updated. I liked that I had a lot more control over my network. I had four consoles (2 hardwired), three laptops, 3 tablets, 4 cell phones, a pc (hardwired), smart tv (hardwired), a fire stick and roku connected with crisp picture/no lag. I removed one star because of the struggle with support knowledge but this is a five star router.

Extra info: I purchased in July, the router died in December. Contacted support to send back the router and they wanted to charge almost $100 dollars to troubleshoot the hardware failure. I refused because this is a hardware issue (says covered on the website) and an understanding rep allowed me to explain further and prove that there was no way for me to connect to the router to troubleshoot (*amber light, not recognizing anything connected to it, changed power outlets, checked ac adapter, router won't reset); I received the RMA. One call resolution. You have to pay to ship the router back or pay for them to ship your replacement (this includes a prepaid shipping label). It wasn't that much ($16.90) but thought I would include for those who would like to know this information.

Update: Received my replacement unit within a few days and it's working excellent! The registration info was already updated for me. Agent that I worked with afterwards was very friendly and knowledgeable. I'm taking this back up to 5 stars.

title: Great for the $$$
text:
I would have done a video review but I'm not sure how to top the ones already posted :)

Anyhow I would just like to add that this little webcam is wonderful! It's really nice that it has auto light correction because I'm tired of having to use "auto-fix" on my pictures! I have tested it out by using my main light (ceiling fan light - the brightest in my room) and also with just a small desk lamp, both producing very good images. Good enough that you can see the name of the water bottle behind me on the floor, I thought that was neat.

Also the filters are fun to play with. I guess once I learn how to edit a video I will try my hand at youtube.

As far as the video capabilities, I use the video aspect every day as I started a personal vlog. The built-in microphone is excellent! I also use my webcam for Skype calls/video conferences. So far I have not experienced any lag. The microphone is very sensitive... I recorded a diary entry when it was raining the other day and when I replayed it I could hear the raindrops very pronounced. Glad my dogs weren't barking.

If anyone wants to see the clarity of the images, I used my webcam to take a picture of myself today which I'm using as my new profile picture on here.

I have triple monitors and have tried sitting the webcam on each with no issues. The brand of monitors I use are Dell, and two Acers. 17" WS LCD, 20" LCD, and 20" WS LCD. The installation was very easy, I was up and running in about three to five minutes.

In summary, I believe it was an excellent purchase for the price. I have no complaints to add.

text: BUYER BEWARE: Product arrived promptly and is well made but is a complete waste of money. Yes, as others have said each firestick comes with it's own power source but I wanted to have the least amount of cables showing so I opted for this product. Unfortunately, although providing a cleaner looking profile, I began to experience connectivity issues. The streaming became very laggy and would totally lose signal on several occasions. At first, I blamed my internet provider and location of my router but after testing the systems speed as well as relocating the hardware for "better and uninterrupted" service I CONTINUED to have issues. After some more troubleshooting I finally, as a hail mary pass, tried reinstalling the original power hook up and low and behold I have had ZERO problems since. This has been 2 months now and smooth sailing the entire time, plus, as an added perk, the firestick powers up much more quickly than when it did using this product. I really wish that I could have had the cleaner no cable look but I'd rather deal with that problem and have to hide an extra cable than be continually concerned that at any moment the show I'm watching will cut off and not be able to restart. Streaming is now carefree, as watching anything should be.

title: Great sound quality and amazing battery life
text:
I was not ready to invest in a set of Apple, Bose, or Sony headphones, yet I was afraid to buy the cheapest headphones available. i wanted something that wouldn't ruin my music, or break the bank, and based upon other reviews, I believe I found a happy medium with these Anker headphones The bass doesn't sound over amplified, or pushed and it has a nice balance in the mid and high ranges.

At first I used it with my phone, and was terribly disappointed, but on my computer and other bluetooth sound systems, they sounded fantastic. I later learned I would have to re download my entire Apple Music library to enjoy higher bit rate music, so I primarily use these with other devices.

The battery life it amazing. I have not had to charge them in almost a month after daily use of an hour or so. When the battery does get low it takes only a few minutes to get hours of use thanks to its quick charge technology.

They are lightweight, comfortable, and the sound quality is surprising decent for an inexpensive set of headphones. About my only complaint would be that the controls are not as intuitive as I would like, but overall I am very pleased with this purchase, and would highly recommend them.

title: This versatile tripod ticks all the boxes at a bargain price
text:
I am very impressed with this KINGJUE 52'' tripod. It's definitely an upgrade from the typical phone/ring light selfie stick type stands I've been using,

I needed a lightweight, inexpensive tripod that is stable enough to handle a brisk wind, as well as the weight of a DSLR camera. I also wanted something with a small footprint to use on a table or desk.

The leg sections locked firmly in place, with no sliding even when I applied some force, but I wish they had used a heavier grade plastic on the latches and knobs.

It included a remote shutter (with battery) paired effortlessly and works flawlessly.

It also comes with a sturdy phone adapter that accommodates my large phone. In addition, there are two threaded mounting options on the side and back.

Instructions are in English with helpful diagrams.

While it does have some cheap plastic parts, the attachments are solid. Especially the phone holder. It's also a few dollars less than others I found , and priced at only $16 at the time of this review, which makes it a bargain compared to the light stand/selfie sticks that costs a few bucks more.

Overall I think you get a lot of bang for the buck with this tripod set, and I would rate this at 4 1/2 stars.

title: Sturdy and well made laptop stand/riser
text:
The EPN adjustable laptop stand is constructed of heavy-duty aluminum and feels sturdy. I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

I like having a slight angle when I type, and being able to raise my screen's camera to eye level so I am not looking down at it during Zoom meetings for that double chin effect. It's also convenient to have that little nook of space to tuck any cables and SSDs underneath, and out of the way.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.

title: Speedy backup and large file transfers with no glitches
text: I purchased a Samsung T7 last year for my MB Pro and wanted a second SSD to back up my new computer and paid abut $10 more because I wanted a blue one this time. It works great and I was astounded at the speedy transfer rates on my tens of thousands graphic files and pictures. WOW! So far, no glitches on either of them. Very pleased with my purchase and would highly recommend this.

title: Well machined and easy to carry
text: This USB C hub is well machined and works great to extend my limited port on my new MB Pro.

title: Compact-sized full keyboard with comfortable feel, and no key lag
text:
I like the finger feel and key travel on this keyboard. I work on a Mac, and pairing it via blue tooth was quick and painless. However, I haven't been able to connect using WIFI.

At 30 WPM, I am not the fastest typist, but I have not noticed any key lag while using it for work all week.

I love that it is a full keyboard with a numbers pad, which I have really miss when using the laptop's keyboard.

I can set the laptop on a small table and type comfortably with this resting on my lap because it is more compact than my traditional full keyboard.

The instructions specify 3AAA batteries, but it only requires 2. Without a doubt, the best inexpensive keyboard I have used, and I own 3 others that I purchased for at least $10 more. The ctrl key positioning takes a moment to get used to, but no complaints.

title: Ideal for plant tags and securing greenhouse shelves
text: These green zip ties are ideal to attaching plant tags and securing the wire shelves in my greenhouses. Some came with shelf clips and others did not.  Either way, I prefer these ties to the clips. Plus, they match because they are green and the price is right! The only thing that would have made them even more perfect would be if they could be re-useable.

title: Good with some caveats
text:
The biggest selling point for me is the variety of battery sizes this battery charger accommodates, especially 9V, C, and D cells because those odd do not often need to be replaced, so I don't keep spares on hand.

I like that it can detect bad cells with my AA and AAA batteries because they are replaced more frequently and can only be cycled so many times with constant use.

Alkaline batteries can be quite expensive and I have been relying on rechargeable batteries more and more.

The only cons for me would be that it does not include an AC adapter option and it is limited to NiMH and NiCD cells only. I also use IMR18650 Li-ion batteries, which this does not accommodate.

title: Yay, I finally have enough sockets!
text: This 16 socket power strip is a fantastic upgrade to my existing surge protector with 4 USB ports for recharging all of my electronic devices. The heavy-duty 5' cord is plenty long and accommodates all of my home office and appliance needs.

title: A must have for indoor and outdoor gardens
text: Ii have wanted a light meter for the longest time because I grow exotic plants using natural and artificial lighting. My greenhouse is only so big and and the youngest plants can still benefit from the LED lighting inside the tent, but the bigger ones have outgrown that space and I have to count on natural sunlight. This meter halos my locate the best area with the strongest rays. I know I need at least 150 FC for my flowering perennials and now I finally know the exact measurement of light intensity without having to guess at it using the eyeball method.

title: Bulky mounting bracket
text:
I needed a webcam for my large external monitor because I usually don't face my small laptop screen when I am on Zoom meetings. Instead of forcing myself to look at the smaller screen with the internal camera. i thought adding a camera to my big screen would be a better solution

I like the adjustable color temperature, dimming features and the 360 degree rotation. However, I dislike the the bulky spring loaded mounting bracket. It places too much tension on the thin bezel with too much overhang.

The picture quality isn't bad, but I was expecting better clarity in this price range. and the lens is more wide angle than I would like at the distance I am using it.

There are many cameras in this price range that have fill-in lighting, optical zoom, and a better mounting bracket that would better suit my needs

title: Cleans up a multii-cable mess and works great!
text:
This YARE 13 in 1 USB C Docking Station solves the biggest problem with my 2020 13" MacBook Pro due to the limited amount of USB-C ports and their inconvenient location. The two ports are located on the left (wrong) side and my power strip is to my right, which makes it an annoying tripping hazard.

I couldn't imagine. having all those wires coming out of my attached hub and dangling across legs. My new computer only supports a single external monitor, but my 2017 MB Pro will support two, so this will work great with both computers.

it's powered and doesn't drain my computer's battery, which isn't a big problem with the 2020 MB Pro, but it is a huge issue with the 2017 laptop because it has always had limited battery life. And it's so nice to only have a single cable whether the computer is on my lap or the arm of my couch.

My external drive is no longer dangling and rests atop the dock. Best of all, I am not having to step offer several cables when I get up. No more tripping hazards and it works great! I highly recommend this.

title: High-quality cable at a bargain price

title: Performs flawlessly without key lag or dropoff
text:
[[VIDEOID:193b985fb1908f0d05b23fd84bdd9707]] The OMOTON Ultra-Slim Bluetooth Keyboard has the upscale look of the Apple keyboard at a fraction of the cost. As a web developer, I rely on my computer for my income and needed an alternative keyboard since my 2017 MB Pro butterfly keyboard went kaput (one key at a time). There isn't much I can do about it until this pandemic is over.

This compact keyboard looks great, pairded quickly, and functions flawlessly right out of the box. I like that it doesn't rely on an internal battery since they only last so long after multiple charges, and it requires 2-AA batteries, which are not included.

The key travel and spacing are very compfortable, and I find that I am making fewer typos than usual. There is no connection dropoff or key stroke lag time whatsoever. If I were to be nit picky, the spacebar is a bit noisier than expected, but the rest of the keys are quiet and operate smoothly.

This is an amazing bargain and you absolutely cannot go wrong with this choice. Especialy at this price. I really like this one a lot and it would be a great keybard at almost twice the price. I highly recommend this!

title: Much better than the others I have tried
text:
[[VIDEOID:abd460f7a915ff20ace934be46d26118]] So far, I really like this keyboard. Right out of the box, I was wowed by the brightly lit backlighting in seven vivid and dazzling colors. Much nicer than an identical looking keyboard I recently tried. I have inluded pic of both.

The butterfly keyboard on my MB pro needs replacement, so I needed a reliable alternative until I can get it fixed. But I will have to iwait until afer after this pandemic because I cannot afford to lose my cmputer for a month or more. Most Pre 2019 MB Pro owners know what I am talking about.

I love the key height, smooth key travel, and compact size, but it keeps dropping the Bluetooth connection every few seconds or so. Very frustrating.

I realized I didn't set it to t to the correct IOS setting, and the instructions and keyboard Fn key markings are in disagreement. I settled on Fn D and/or Fn E for my MB Pro laptop, but the instructions seem to indicate this keyboard is mostly geared for tablets. And the settings differ between iPad size, Windows, and Android tablet operating systems.

I eventually got it working at an acceptable level. It's too soon to comment on battery life, but so far, I really like this keyboard compared to others I have used (and plan to return). Right now, I would rate this at about 4 1/2 stars. It's attractive and lightwieght with adjustable liight levels. I'm digging it!

title: Comforatble and accurate typing with no drop off
text:
I purchased this 12.9'" iPad Pro keyboard case and have been using it pretty regularly for a few months. The key travel height is comfortable, and accuracy has been excellent. Reminds me of my MB Pro keyboard when all the keys still worked. I would love to find this Bluetooth keyboard available for laptops.

This backlit iPad keyboard and trackpad was probably the least expensive model ($35) at the time, and I wasn't expecting much, but I took a chance and I am glad I did. It paired quickly, and it was easy to connect the trackpad feature via accessibility settings.

The RGB lighting is around the keys, and I would have preferred it if the letters were translucent and lit up as well.

My only complaint would be the rigid frame on the case. It made me a bit nervous, and felt like I had to force it a bit, but it fit well once I got it in. I wish it were a bit softer and more flexible at the corners.

Overall, I would say it's a good value and would recommend it.

title: Prefer better cooliing at higher RPMs to quiet

This is the sixth cooling pad I have tried and only two do an adequate job, but this is not one of them.  Those of us that use our computers to the max are more concerned with effective cooling with higher  RPMs. if you are more interested in the noise level this may be ideal for you. I work my laptop very hard and need maximum cooling power, so it was insufficient for me.

title: Worse than my messed up butterfly keyboard
text:
I really want to love the Arteck HB030B Universal Slim Portable Wireless Bluetooth keyboard. You can't beat the price, and I purchased it because my MacBook Pro has a messed-up butterfly keyboard, so I was seeking a cost-effective solution to tide me over until I can get it fixed during this pandemic.

I find myself going back to my MBPro keyboard because the key travel to be very stiff, especially on such a compact, lightweight keyboard. It's just not working right, and since I am not a touch typist, I am looking at what I am doing. When I look up, I find it is typing keys I never hit and there is a lot of lag time.

If you are a touch typist, you will be very unhappy. I have key repeat turned off on my computer. yet keys on this keyboard are occasionally repeating.

I was considering leaving all the mistakes in but wanted others to be able to read this clearly. This will probably be returned.

Update 10/27/2020
The seller provided excellent customer service and offered to send me a replacement. I have the feeling it won't be any different. The key travel and stiffness is a big issue for me. I subsequently purchased another keyboard from another alphabet soup named manufactured and even though they look identical, the performance is NOT. The key travel is smoother and the brightness of the backlighting and color selection is not even comparable I am very disappointed that this is an Amazon Choice product.

title: Best eyeglass cleaning cloths EVER!
text: Without a doubt, the K&F Concept Microfiber Cleaning Cloths are the best eyeglass cleaning cloths I have used and I would even trust them for use with my expensive camera lenses. I love the individual packets ,so I'll always have a clean cloth in my purse or camera bag.

title: Long and slim HDMI Cable  works welland stays connected
text: The ten-foot Pasow HDMI Cable Ultra-Thin HDMI cable is thin, lightweight, works well, and stays in place. It makes me crazy and I have gone as far as trying to tape it in place. title: Works great with Mac, but read this first...
text:
The Atto TileRec Mini Recorder works great with my Mac Book Pro, but it took a while till the "NO NAME" drive was able to mount. I was just about to write an unfavorable review. but...

The issue may have been caused by the battery not being fully charged and the instructions were not very clear about the device name. However, I went to the Atto Digital website and watched the video, which was mostly the unboxing of the device. When the device FINALLY appeared in FINDER it was listed as "NO NAME" and once I clicked on the device the VOICE file appeared. I clicked once and to my delight, I found several files from my "Testing, hello, hello" to my voice-activated recordings of increasing levels of frustration all neatly cataloged and time-stamped.

PROS:
- Tiny stealth device
- Sensitive mic
- Simple to use (once the battery is charged)
- Excellent voice clarity on playback

CONS:
- Requires a computer to listen to the recordings. It would be great if I could use it with earbuds as an option.

SUMMARY:
This is an excellent device and can be used for Dr visits, job interviews, school, or any number of situations that would require a compact and stealthy voice activated recorder. At first, I wondered if I would really want to spend $59 on something that I probably wouldn't use very often, but it's good to know I have it. Just in case... hey, ya never know?

title: Sound quality is decent, but somewhat bright at higher volume
text:
[[VIDEOID:aedbd047bdcee111326af43f1b70c93c]] After experimenting with several small speakers to use with my Echo Dot, I became enamored with the Doss Soundbox Touch because it had the best overall sound quality compared to other speakers in its price range. It is larger than my original Doss Soundbox, and I was expecting the same well rounded dynamic range with a little more volume. This speaker paired effortlessly with all of my devices.

The touch controls are my favorite. It not only gives this speaker a sleek modern look, but they also make it a breeze to change functions effortlessly. It's like swiping my phone screen between apps and I have become spoiled by not having to push or press anything. It sounds like a small thing, but once you live with it you will find anything that that requires more effort to be an inconvenience.

The Soundbox Plus boasts an increased battery life when using it without the light feature. The light show is fun, but it's not a big draw for me since I use this near my computer monitor and it's somewhat distracting.

The sound quality is decent, but it is not what I had expected. It has larger drivers and moves more air, so there is increased volume but the sound quality degrades and becomes too bright. I hear mostly the mid and high ranges with slightly muddled bass. However, at a lower volume, the sound quality improves and becomes more balanced. I love the touch control features, and it's attractive enough for use in every room.

As a side note, Doss customer service is second to none. The best I have ever experienced outside of Amazon's support team.
