** If you found this review to be helpful at all, please take a moment and click the button below to let Amazon know. Thank you so much 😊 **

title: Versitile wall mounted power strip with surge protection.
text:
I am delighted with this CyerPower wall mounted power strip because it expands my outlets capacity to 4 sockets and includes 4 USB ports. It's nice to be able to plug my USB powered devices directly into the power without needing an additional adapter.
There are some areas in my home where I would prefer not to have a long ugly power strip on the floor and this works great. Additionally, the outlets swivel so my power cords face sideways against my wall.

Some reviewers complained that this power strip pulled away from the wall, but I have not experienced that. It holds tightly in the top socket and is stabilized by a plastic piece that fits into the grounding hole of the bottom socket.

I have several surge protectors by Cyber Power that I have been using for several months and have found all of them to be of excellent quality.

title: Excellent braided low profille cable
text: Well, this certainly arrived timely. I have an old Mac Pro G5 desktop that is being moved to another room farther away from my modem, and it does not have a wireless card. I know! I just never bothered to install one because of it's proximity to my modem and I don't feel like upgrading it my 14-year-old computer anymore. It's perfectly fine for everyday internet, and this 40' flat braided cable is a perfect solution to span rooms becuase of its low profile and length. It looks very well made and durable with high-quality connections. This Cat-7 cable is compatible with Cat-5, and I am thrilled with the overall build quality.

title: Space saving 6 outlet power strip with surge protector and 2 USB ports
text: This is a fantastic replacement for my corded power strip. Now I can finally get all of my computer equipment and electronics plugged into the wall, and behind my desk instead of using the bulky power strip that sits on the floor, This power strip uses one outlet and has a center screw for added stability. It provides 1080 Joules surge protection to 6 outlets and 2 USB ports located at the top. I have never had any issues with my AmazonBasics products, and you really cannot go wrong for the price. I highly recommend it.

title: Accommodates 17" gaming laptops
text: This large laptop case will easily accommodate your 17" gaming machine and smaller 15" laptops with room to spare. This bag is very well made and has more pockets than I know what to do with, but I will manage to fill them. I always do. This expandable laptop case will hold all of your accessories, paperwork, and other electronics, including a second computer. There is only one padded compartment, but there is plenty of space and adequate cushioning between the compartments for sufficient protection. It's high quality and looks very durable. If you require a larger laptop bag, I highly recommend it.

title: MacBook Pro Worthy
text:
Everything about this PODOOR USB Type C to HDMI cable is high quality. RARELY do I deem a cable Macbook Pro worthy, and this one certainly is.

I've only plugged in a dodgy "shark tooth" cable into my pricey laptop once, and that port hasn't been the same since. Now I look before I leap.

The USC-C connection is smooth and on par with my OEM Apple cables.

The HDMI plug feels weighty with a zinc alloy body. It's undoubtedly the most substantial HDMI connection I've seen, and I have not experienced any issues with it fitting into the back of my monitor.

The included Velcro wrap tie is incredibly grippy. I wish the Velcro on my watchband gripped like that. Holy Cow!

I highly recommend this USB-C/HDMI cable! 5-stars all the way!

title: I found it to be more cumbersome than useful on my desk.
text:
The Bostitch Konnect USB Charging Phone Stand is part of a desk organizing system and provides a stable stand for your phone to keep it upright and out of your way with vertical or horizontal placement. This docking station would also accommodate a smaller tablet. There is a USB port on the front of the base, and it includes a USB/AC power adapter.

The Bostich Konnect looks like an outstanding organizer system if you plan on keeping everything you need at the back of your desk and against a wall.

This phone stand will work best with a short charging cable (not included) to keep clutter off your work area.

As a standalone dock or as part of the Konnect system, it would have made more sense if this were a wireless QI charger, but it's only a large and blocky plastic stand. It requires the addition of a short charging cable that would need to be attached to the front of the unit. I found it to be more cumbersome than useful on my desk.

title: MackBook Pro worthy
text: [[VIDEOID:269e11db08ea30af0433f27c6e8e2581]] This Nonda USB-C/Thunderbolt adapter is top-notch! It's one of the few times I have received an adapter that is MacBook Pro worthy.  I have reviewed and tossed many hubs and adapters becuase of a poorly machined "Shark tooth" USB-C connection. I only made the mistake of plugging one directly into my expensive laptop once, and after that, shark-toothed USB-C hubs were only tested using another hub. I highly recommend this adapter because it is of high quality, and it works.

title: Works great, but Inserting the transmitter battery is challenging
text:
[[VIDEOID:d6b7a8b9b0393d04acea3ab55126063e]] I love the huge selection of musical chimes. Everything from classical music, whimsy, holiday tunes, doorbell chimes, etc. I believe there are 36 options and I enjoyed running through all of them until I made my selection.

The doorbell works great, but Inserting the transmitter battery is nearly impossible. It took three people almost a half an hour to pry the battery cover off. Inserting the batteries into the receiver was pretty standard and I am not sure why they made the transmitter so difficult and user-unfriendly. They have included a pry-off tool just for that purpose. Hopefully, I will not need to change that battery for a very long time.

This kit arrived with mounting hardware and double stick tape plus a single 3032 coin battery for the transmitter along with a pry tool to remove the battery cover. The dual AA batteries for the receiver are not included.

I have the receiver standing on my desk and I am happy that "stand-alone" it is an option. This kit came with mounting hardware as well, but I like the idea of being able to move the receiver to whatever area I happen to be working in since I listen to loud music at work and may not hear it upstairs.

I paid $12.99 at the time of review and you cannot beat that! Had it not been so difficult to insert the transmitter battery I would have rated this doorbell 5 stars. It works well and I recommend it.

title: Perfect case/sleeve for the newest iPad! - looks modern and upscale
text: I was searching for sleeve/case combo for my new 11" iPad, and the Kogzzen Laptop Sleeve is absolutely ideal. The inside is soft, plush, and adequately padded to protect my expensive device. Not only that, it has an outer pocket to accommodate my iPad mini with two interior compartments for my phone and power cables. It looks elegant and smartly designed. Even the zipper pulls look modern and upscale. Most sleeves look utilitarian, but not this one. The orange handle has a slim fit design that makes it perfect as a sleeve inside my backpack and as a case. Every detail is high-end, and I very highly recommend this!

title: Looks and works like OEM Apple cables
text:
The Uelkdef 2Pack Lightning to USB Cable looks and works like my OEM Apple Original Charging cables. I found it a little odd that they included what looks like a cable connection reinforcements to protect the cord from breakage and stress where it connects to the plug. If you choose to use them, assembly is required, but why not just assemble it at the factory? Probably becuase they aren't attractive. They are Apple MFi Certified so you won't have any issues with your device not recognizing it. Honestly, I haven't had that happen in years.

Bottom line: These are good quality spare cables, and the price is right. Great to keep in the car or office. Everyone is always looking for a charging cable in my office, so I am happy to be able to accommodate.

title: Clear sound with distortion free bass
text: I have tested many earbuds that range in price from $10 to over $100, and I must say these sound very decent in this price range and better than some that cost twice as much. They are very bass-midrange centric, but the sound clarity is superb, and they have not distorted at the loudest volume I could stand. I heard instrumental detail I would not have expected in a pair of $25 earbuds. I thought the heavier bass and midrange would seem unbalanced and bothersome, but it wasn't after listening to a range of music for a few hours. I haven't tried them on phone calls yet, but if the music sounds this clean and clear, I am sure my phone calls will as well. I will update my review if it doesn't live up to my expectations. So far I like these earbuds a lot and highly recommend them.

title: Second best invention EVER!
text: I think Zip Ties are one of the best inventions ever. they are incredibly versatile and I use them as wire ties, chain, attaching light fixtures, etc. The clips on one of my hub caps broke and two of these have been holding it on for over a year. I could go on and on, but the only limit to their use is your imagination. This is the best invention since duct tape. The 14" size is the perfect size for most uses and I highly recommend.

title: Amazing sound quality in a tiny speaker 👍🏻
text:
[[VIDEOID:4ffdeb91a608ef10f392ffc0150c5a3b]] The iHome Color Changing Portable Speaker with Speakerphone Soft Rotocast Cabinet is arguably the best speaker I have tried in this class and rivals many of my larger and more expensive speakers by top name manufacturers.

I wasn't expecting much from such a tiny speaker becuase of its size. It can only move so much air to produce a bigger and fuller sound, so I kept my expectations realistic, and in the end, I was blown away by the sound quality and volume this little speaker produced.

The bass, midrange, and treble were in perfect balance without one overpowering over the other. It has a nice clean, clear sound with plenty of volume.

The light show can be adjusted to fast, slow, single color, or off.

The Bluetooth connected immediately to the computer and phone, and it can also be used as a speakerphone to answer phone calls.

I cannot think of any cons with this iHome speaker, and I am genuinely delighted that this speaker performs so well. This tiny, inexpensive speaker produces amazing sound quality, and I highly recommend it!

title: Best cable I own!
text: I've purchased many spare cables in different lengths and port configurations, and I must say I am impressed with this one.  The Mangotek USB C to Lightning Cable is the fastest possible charge you can have with an iPhone. Nothing beats USB-C to Lightning connection for speed. Talk about high-speed data transfer, wow! This cable is thick and sturdy and I like that they included a velcro wire tie to keep it neatly wound when not in use or when you want to adjust your cable length.  I have other USB-C to lightning connection cables, and I went for the pretty color braided cable types only to realize my phone was taking much longer to charge so I was happy when this came up for review because  I have wanted to replace them with a more efficient cable. This  Mangotek cable is now my very best and favorite cable, and I highly recommend it.

title: Great holiday backdrop for family pics or child and pet pics
text: The colors are lovely, and this will make a very festive backdrop for holiday x-mas card pics of your kids, pets, and family as long as they are seated or crouching. The dimensions are stated accurately, and when I hung it, it was shorter than my 5'3" height. The creases seem to work themselves out quite quickly without needing to iron it. I used gaffer's tape to adhere it temporarily, but it doesn't stick well. I think the biggest challenge will be finding a way to hang this to where it stays in place and lays flat.  Maybe push pins or clips would work best. Or better yet, a proper stand, which I am sure I can find at a reasonable price on Amazon. I've always wanted a professional type backdrop for the holidays, and this one is fantastic.

title: Ruggedly handsome retro style briefcase/laptop bag
text:
This beautifully crafted Leather Centric 15 Inch Buffalo Leather Laptop Messenger Bag will undoubtedly turn heads with its rugged good looks and retro style. Even the click lock latches have an authentic early twentieth-century look and feel and are reminiscent of the type used on valises back in the day.

There's no shortage of pockets and compartments to hold your 13"- 14" laptop, tablets, phone, and all the accessories and power cables with plenty of room for paperwork, pens, and accessories you may need for school or the office.

This 100% Buffalo leather case is on the heavy side, but not so much as to become cumbersome. In addition to it's steel reinforsed handle there is an adjustable shoulder strap to make it easier to tote.

Every piece of antique brass finished hardware came carefully wrapped. This is truly a high-quality bag, and about the only thing that concerns me is that it scratched so easily, but over time the accumulation will only add to the aged patina it was meant to have.

I have already used mine, and the finish was not damged by rain, and all of my electronics were well protected during a downpour thanks to the zippered closure on the interior compartment.

This briefcase/laptop messenger style bag is constructed with artisan quality craft and is meant to be shown off.

Everything old is new again and this modern day re-creation has the authentic, classic and timeless look that will remind you of a case your granddad would've used for work. I highly recommend it!

title: Ruggedly handsome with artisan quality workmanship!
text: This Leather Centric Office Laptop Briefcase is ruggedly handsome with a retro style that is classic and elegant with a bit of a hipster vibe. This bag reminds of the type of bag I once used during my early school days; only this is an updated version with tons of pockets, compartments, and dividers to keep your laptop and mobile devices safe and secure. It even has credit card slots. The closures are the type that was used in valises back in the day where they slide and lock into place. There is no question that this is 100% leather and every piece of antique brass hardware came carefully wrapped. This is truly a high-quality bag, and about the only thing that concerns me is that it scratched so easily, but over time the accumulation will only add to the aged look it was meant to have. This briefcase/laptop bag is constructed with artisan quality workmanship, and I cannot wait to show it off. I highly recommend it!

title: 128Gb NVMe SSD drive
text: I thought the Lexar NM500 M.2 2280 NVMe 128GB Solid-State Drive (LNM500-128RBNA) would be great to use as an external boot drive. I've always been pleased with the quality of my Lexar drives and this should be no exception. I ordered a pretty red Sabrent enclosure only to learn it would only accept M Key NVMe drives. ARGH! I am sure this drive works great as all my other Lexar drives do, but now I just need to find the correct case so I can use this as an external drive. That is proving to be a much bigger challenge than I expected.

title: NVMe SSD must be M Key SSD for use.
text: So I was sitting here all ready to install my new SSD only to learn that it had the incorrect pins — something I will need to pay more attention to in the future. The drive is a Lexar NVMe SSD which is incompatible with this case. This case uses M key type pins. The enclosure is a beautiful aluminum alloy and includes everything you need, including the driver. Now I just need to find the correct drive. The search continues... This is a solid case and I highly recommend it.

title: Tremendous sound quality for a tiny speaker. Crisp and clear with no distortion at max volume!
text:
[[VIDEOID:bbb3e1079eb39e7b0d0221b2e128e01d]] I am not an audiophile; however, I know great sound when I hear it, and this tiny speaker delivers crisp, clear sound. I would expect nothing less from Sony. However, it is a little bright with more midrange and treble and it sometimes sounds a little thin. The bass has a little bit of thump and does not distort even with the volume maxed out.

I used an audio cable with my Echo Dot and Bluetooth with my phone and computer.

Steely Dan is my test music, and my EQ is set to flat so I can hear what this speaker is capable of without the help of any adjustments.

I made this video using my largest audio file on my MacBook Pro. You can be the judge.

The only things I do not like are the controls, and I think the volume is lacking. I have the volume set to max on both the speaker and my computer. It can fill the small area I am occupying, but not the room.

It's a very compact speaker, and I think it sounds tremendous when you consider its size. The clarity is impressive, and it does not distort. Overall, I am pretty happy with the sound quality and I would have rated it higher if the price point were lower. At the time of this review, it costs $50 and there are a lot of great speakers at nearly half that cost. If it could produce the same sound clarity with more volume it would be worth every penny.

title: This seems like a high quality cable, but my DP adapter is at fault here
text: Everything about this 10' DP cable screams quality. Unfortunately, I will have to update my review after finding a  working adapter. The fit and finish are outstanding. However, I cannot say the same about my USB-C to DP adapter.

title: Sturdy and adjustable. The perfect solution for my living room office!
text:
My home office consists of my couch's armrest as my laptop desk and my coffee table became my "NEW" monitor stand. I recently received a 32" monitor, and the viewing angle was way too low. I had to come up with a solution to raise the monitor several inches so you cannot imagine how thrilled I was to find this high-quality adjustable Monitor Riser Stand by HUANUO to raise my display above knee height.
I didn't want to use a big computer desk in this area of my home, and I have been unable to find the perfect sized desk or table for this small space.

This HUANUO Metal Monitor Riser Stand was perfect. It's well made, sturdy and offers three adjustment heights. I am currently using the middle setting.

Assembly couldn't have been more straightforward since the bolts are already attached to the metal mesh surface and you only need to screw in the legs, pick your height and you're good to go!.

It's sturdy, stable and lightweight and the perfect size. I highly recommend it.

title: USB-C has too much flex at the connection
text:
[[VIDEOID:41f251da4d25d6fd4136431f27bd286d]] Update... It no longer works with my HDMI cable and doesn't work with my new DP cable. The DP cable is new and this was the only adapter I had so I am not sure whether the new cable is bad or if it is this adapter. I strongly suspect this adapter since the HDMI cable works fine when using a my hubr.

Original Review:

When I plugged the Doitby USB C To Displayport Adapter DisplayPort To HDMI Adapter into my MacBook Pro, it wasn't a smooth fit.

Usually, a well-machined plug will slide in effortlessly and feel tight once it is connected.

It took a minute for my computer to recognize the second monitor and it worked well once it did. However, the edges of the adapter are sharp. It almost feels as though I can cut my skin on it.

What I find most troubling is that the USB-C does not seat well and has too much flex in the connection. I rarely ever use that port so it should be reasonably tight.

I needed this to use a 10' display port cable because I am stepping over a 6" HDMI cable that is not long enough for my set up., but I'm just not comfortable with the flex at the connection to my computer, especially with the weight of that longer cable.

title: Great budget friendly case
text:
I love the heather charcoal twill fabric on this sturdy AmazonBasics Urban Laptop and 17" Tablet Case. I am using the 15" sleeve (not included), and it fits my 15.4" MacBook Pro perfectly.

I ordered the larger 17" size to ensure it will accommodate my computer, accessories, iPads and anything else I may need. It looks a little big, but when it comes to space, I would rather have it and not need it than to need it and not have it.

The center compartment has two generous pockets inside. One spans the entire width, and the other is about 3/4 of the width and will accommodate a large iPad or smaller computer. I wouldn't do that without a sleeve though because the inside pockets do not offer any padding.

One of the zippered outer compartments has a divided pocket that is sized for two iPads, and the other is just a large single zippered compartment that will accommodate your accessories or paperwork.

This case is waterproof. I tested it under the faucet because I live in a state that gets torrential rains every day for half the year. I require Florida proof protection, and this case offers it!

It's a great value, and about the only thing I don't like is that the shoulder padding isn't grippy. It slides a little too easily off my shoulder. Other than that, I think it's a great value and looks good.

title: Bass centric, but doesn't distort. Great choice in this price range!
text: I've tried a nearly a dozen pair of earbuds that cost between $10 - $70 and The HaRuion A001+ in-Ear Earphones perform very well, especially in this price range. They are bass-centric,  but not to the point of completely overpowering the sound, and they do not distort at high volume. The mid-range and treble sound crisp and well balanced, and the overall fidelity was good. I have earbuds that cost almost 5 times as much and do not sound as good, which proves you don't have to spend a fortune to get decent sound quality. They come with 2 sets of ear cushions to fit every ear. I'm very pleased with these earbuds and highly recommend them.

title: Space saving power with USB surge protection
text: I have finally found the perfect power block and surge protector for my bathroom. I only have 2 sockets in my bathroom with a lot of power-hungry appliances that require USB adapters in order to charge. The competition for sockets was becoming fierce and my only options were to alternate which appliances get powered up or take them into another room to charge. I have finally found a solution. This will work great in any room where you do not want a large power block dangling on the floor. I highly recommend.

title: Sturdy, waterproof, cushioned protection for my 15" laptop
text:
It took a long time to save up for my expensive laptop and I wanted and good quality sleeve that will ensure it stays protected when traveling without breaking the bank... again. I have found you don't have to spend insane amounts of money for quality and this is one of those times.

Top reasons why I like this sleeve so much:

1. Accommodates my 15.4" laptop with room to spare and can hold my cables, power supply, and an iPad
2. Stylish fabric with tweed patterned heavy twill fabric. It looks classy.
3. It has thicker padding to protect my investment.
4. It's waterproof. I live in a state that gets torrential downpours every afternoon for half the year so this is a biggie!
5. It's high quality and INEXPENSIVE

I ran it under the sink to test it for water resistance and it is waterproof. What more can you ask of a laptop sleeve? This is a great little sleeve and you cannot beat the price. I highly recommend!

title: Holy Cow! Huge, framless 32" monitor perfroms flawlessly with MacBook Pro
text:
To be honest, I did not know if the GPU on my little 15" MacBook Pro would be able to handle this 32" display without experiencing some headache or performance issue. I still haven't even found the right space to set it up because it is enormous and my laptop's desk is the armrest of my couch. I rearranged my entire living room to accommodate this monitor while crossing my fingers, hoping the effort would be worth it. In the end, It was soooooo worth it.

The ViewSonic VX3276-2K-MHD 32 Inch Frameless Widescreen IPS 1440p Monitor even delivered a surprise. When I plugged the HDMI cable into my laptop, I heard audio coming from the monitor. I didn't know it had built-in speakers. I'll be using my higher end speakers, but It's was a nice bonus. I've been streaming videos for the last hour so now have a 32" 1440P TV in here too. All I can say is Yipppeee!

The display is big, bright and crisp from corner to corner. I am a graphic artist so having such a large screen is a welcome relief to my tired eyes.

I've wanted a 32" frameless monitor for as long as I could remember and was suffering from analysis paralysis when trying to decide which one to choose. When this became available through the Vine program, I jumped on it. It almost seemed too good to be true, so I kept my expectations low.

I am not a gamer, but I am a professional web developer and graphic artist and work in Photoshop. I had to rely solely on my 15" laptop screen when working from home so having this much screen real estate is fantastic. It has made all the difference in my work, and I am no longer suffering from massive eye strain. I really should have gotten one of these sooner.

If you are looking for a good quality large screen monitor with excellent features on a budget, you cannot go wrong with this choice.

---Update----

After almost a week I have been noticing more and more backlight bleed. First, it was at the lefthand corner and now some near the top right towards the corner. Only noticeable when streaming video with a black background, but it hasn't become super bothersome yet. My desktop image is predominantly black and it is only marginally noticeable, but nonetheless, it is noticeable. I have reduced my rating by 1 star. If it gets any worse I will update and the rating will go down accordingly!

title: Very disappointing sound quality.
text: I am usually pleased with Amazon products, so I was disappointed when I tried these. There was virtually no bass or treble, and the midrange is thin and weak. There are holes in the sound where instruments are supposed to be. The sticky rubber on the cord caught everything, and you could hear it rubbing against everything it touched. The sound of the wire rubbing against my arm was the only true fidelity I heard. There are much better earbuds in this price range so don't think you have to spend a fortune for great sounding earbuds; you don't. Sadly, these are not the best choice.

title: Simple laptop case with thick padded shoulder straps and superb quality
text:
The Targus GeoLite Essentials laptop case has everything I need and nothing I don't. Let me clarify... When I first purchased a backpack for my laptop, I wound up buying a large bag with a gazillion pockets and sub-compartments. Fast forward a year down the line, and there is no longer room to for my laptop because it's filled with all manner of office supplies, paperwork, snack food, water bottles, god-knows-what, you name it, it's probably in there. I have lost things within that bag only to be found months later. That backpack was overkill and now weighs over 7 lbs hurts my shoulders. The shoulder straps on this Targus case has very thick comfort padding that can handle over 8 lbs comfortably without shoulder pain. I included a pic comparing my other expensive backpack with the ultra thick straps on the Targus.

I finally found the perfect backpack dedicated exclusively for my laptop. The interior is spacious enough for my 15.4" computer, power adapter, hubs, cables, peripherals, and a few office essentials. It has the right amount of compartments for my laptop, iPad and anything they require. No more, no less.

All of my Targus cases have been very high quality and have outlasted the computers themselves. I expect this one will too. It's a very high-quality laptop case at a very affordable price.I highly recommend it.

title: Limited use due to short Y split cable length
text: I was hoping I could use these to connect two external speakers, but the Y split is not long enough to connect two 8" wide speakers to my device. I can only pair one of them at a time using Bluetooth and I was hoping to have stereo sound using a wired connection. No stereo for me. The overall quality appears to be an upgrade to the old RCA cables I have been using on the control unit for my old Klipsch speakers so they won't be completely useless.

title: HOLY COW! Exceeded all expectations in any price range.
text:
I so wasn't expecting this caliber of sound from such inexpensive earbuds. I use these at work when I need to view videos without forcing my entire office to listen along and needed to find an alternative to my Apple ear pods because they always fall out of my ears.

I tested them out by listening higher fidelity version of my favorite Steely Dan songs and OMG I wasn't expecting this. These super cheap Panasonic ErgoFit In-Ear Earbud Headphones are fantastic and deliver big sound. I heard nuances in the music that I've never noticed before. The sound is balanced, and I even had to turn the volume down on my computer because they are very efficient (loud).

I am not an audiophile, but it sounded perfectly balanced to my ears. The bass isn't boomy, and the mid-range and highs are crystal clear. They sound better than our larger Sonos sound system. In fact, I needed to drown it out because my musical tastes differ widely from my crew.

The cord was plenty long, and I was able to comfortably reach the headphone jack from my desktop computer on the floor to my ears without it interfering or forcing me to sit in an awkward position while using them.

It came with multiple ear cushions to accommodate smaller ears, and I needed to use one of them for my right ear. I am super impressed with these and still cannot get over the price of these outstanding earbuds. Just buy them, you'll be more than happy!

title: Not a great solution. Too many challanges.
text: I have wanted to install a dash cam for the longest time because I live in a place with a disproportionate amount of tourists, elderly (over medicated) drivers and the folks who have road rage as a result. I don't to be the one charged with the ticket I am cut off on the road! I was hoping this would be a great inexpensive solution, but It has too many challenges to overcome. It's a bit large for my windshield and I was hard pressed to find a good spot where it didn't impair my visibility because I already have a transponder occupying the space behind my rear view mirror, which is obscured by some sort of black light diffusing material. The other challenge was the power cord. There is no place in my car where it wouldn't interfere with the center controls on my dash (AC, radio, etc). The only other option would be using the center console auxiliary outlet and taping the cord in several places. It's gonna hang somewhere though. I wonder if there are any solar powered options? This one just is a no go for me. The field of view seemed pretty narrow as well. It was a very inexpensive camera ($16 lightening deal) and I would probably return it if it were not too late. I'll write this off as a learning experience and will have a better idea of what to look for the next time. If I find a way to overcome the challenges I will upgrade my review.

title: FAN-TASTIC!  Sleek, stylish, safe and REALLY moves air!.
text:
[[VIDEOID:5cccf65ebb09ed8723542bed292c2771]] This Sharper Image USB Fan with Soft Blades is stylish, sleek, compact and SAFE! Between the lamp and my laptop it can get uncomfortably warm in my work area so I thought this would also be great solution to keep things cool. My laptop gets pretty hot because I push the processor really hard and my cooling pad isn't always sufficient.

WHAT I LIKE ABOUT IT...

The metal frame has a slim form factor and does not take up valuable space in my crowded little work area. I could even hang it on a wall hook if I wanted to keep it off the surface, which makes it very versatile.

It has 2 speeds, is relatively quiet and moves a lot of air. It's very effective.

Flexible blades keep it safe around fingers and pets.

It works great and does what I need it to do while looking pretty stylish. It's the type of product you would expect from Sharper Image in terms of quality and style and I cannot find anything not to love.

title: Essential for Hurricane season!
text: I ordered the RunningSnail Emergency Hand Crank Self Powered AM/FM NOAA Solar Weather Radio to add to my arsenal of hurricane essentials. Hurricane supplies eat up a good deal of storage space in my small apartment and I was delighted that this is a smaller unit that I can keep handy. The packaging includes a USB cable and Iphone adapter. My expensive power bank didn't even include those. I tested it and found the flashlight to be very bright and the radio worked great. In Florida we get bad storms almost daily for 6 months out of the  the year so it's good to have this around. I won't know about it's longevity till I give it the real world test during a storm and will update if I experience any issues. Right now I'm glad to know I have it.

title: Cheap ill fitting USB-C Connection makes this a FAIL!
text: I have never had an issue inserting a USB-C cable into my MacBook Pro computer before. I had to force it a bit. Not a good fit and when I compared it to my other USB-C plugs the problem was obvious. The other plugs are slimmer and smaller with clean edges. No crimping or scalloping on the inside. I included pics of this one with 3 other USB-C connectors from other devices. One is OEM and the others all have the same standardized fit and flawless finish to match OEM quality. This one is oversized with crimping on the inside edges. Quite a big difference. While I had it plugged in, which I regret, I inserted my original OEM Apple USB-C charging cable in the single USB-C slot to see if it would fit or charge. It was an awkward fit and it did not charge. I then plugged this hub into another cheap hub as a piggyback and it fit okay. Cheap meets cheap. I tested both the USB-2 and USB-3 connections using a low wattage LED ring light and power fluctuated. I will not plug this directly into my laptop again due to the poor fit.

title: Not using it in my expensive laptop! Cheap, crimped, ill fitting USB-C connector.
text: This review is for the 7-in-1 Type C Adapter with 4K USB C to HDMI,USB C Charging Port,1 USB 3.0 Port,2 USB 2.0 Ports. I have never had an issue inserting a USB-C cable into my MacBook Pro computer before. I had to force it a bit. Not a good fit and when I compared it to my other USB-C plugs and when I compared it with well made plugs the problem is obvious. The other plugs are slimmer and smaller with clean edges. No crimping or scalloping on the inside. I included pics of this alongside another USB-C connector for comparison. My other plug has the same standardized fit and smooth finish to match OEM quality. This one is oversized with crimping on the inside edges. Quite a big difference. While I had it plugged in, which I regret, I inserted my original OEM Apple USB-C charging cable in the single USB-C slot to see if it would fit or charge. It was an awkward fit and it did not charge. I then plugged this hub into another cheap hub as a piggyback and it fit okay, however, I will not plug this directly into my laptop again due to the poor fit.

title: OUTSTANDING quality with unique features + Charges Macbook Pro
text:
I have so many hubs, but this one is truly unique. James Donkey is not a name I was familiar with, but I will look for their products in the future because this is a high quality hub that costs less than my expensive - and relatively crappy - hubs. The fit and finish is superb and it works flawlessly on my MacBook Pro. This hub has a unique combination of features for video expansion (VGA + HDMI), Ethernet, USB 3 and USB C. It actually charges my laptop via the USB-C port. I know, why am I so astounded when something works as promised? You can feel the quality of materials and the workmanship is flawless. I love the recessed slot that the main USB C power cord tucks in to for traveling. Some folks aren't a fan of the orange light, but I am. It feels solid and weighty, not like the cheaply made hubs I usually buy. Oh, and those "cheaper" hubs have cost me at least $10 - $30 more than this one. This one is priced at $49 the time of this review. Holy cow, this has totally exceeded my expectations and is my new favorite hub.
This hub includes:
USB C Hub that charges MacBook Pro, Ethernet/RJ-45 port, 1 USB Type-C Female PD max 100W charging port, 4K HDMI port, 1080P VGA port,3 USB 3.0 ports can connect more peripherals contain 1 2.1A fast & efficient charging USB 3.0 port
And they all work!

title: How bad can it be? Malfunctions with annoyingly loud clacky spacebar
text: [[VIDEOID:e87bc7e3133de0040b0fea8820b50692]] The  Verbatim Wireless Slim Keyboard just caused me to lose my unfinished review while typing on it because it malfunctions. The num lock light does not work and the caps lock light goes on and off intermittently. I have to type in order to find out whether it is on or not. The lettering on the keys are odd. I looked at it sideways and it looked the same upright. The J looks like an L and the R looks like an A. I am not a touch typist, but thank goodness I have some idea where the letters are located by now. I am a little dyslexic and visually it is a nightmare to look at. Now for the space bar.  It is annoyingly loud and clacky when touched. I have never heard anything like this before outside of an old school typewriter. I almost expect to hear a "Ding" after using it several times. Just touching the bar without pressing it produces a very loud clacking sound, which is super irritating when typing. All the other keys are relatively quiet when they work. Poor font, poor functionality and poor performance. I am debating whether or not to reduce my review to 1 star for this one.

title: Great power strip and OUTSTANDING customer service.

title: Awesome sound quality. Excellent Customer Support! Just buy it!
text:
From the moment I felt how heavy this little speaker was in the box I knew this was it was probably going to sound pretty good and I was right! It's AWESOME! It fills my entire living room and sounds great all the way to the master bedroom on the opposite side of my apartment. At first I was just looking for an upgraded speaker for my Echo Dot Mini and purchased the Oontz, which was $4 less. I was hating the sound quality of that one because it was a downgrade, not an improvement. Sounded tinny and irritating. I was looking for a good little speaker for my small living room (not the pool area) and liked the controls on this speaker so to give it a try and boy was I impressed. This has a more balanced sound and decent bass. It's not super boomy bass, it's just right for my small space. This speaker paired instantly with my phone, computer and Alexa! The other speaker did not pair with Alexa at all. If you're on the fence about speakers under $30 I'll save you the trouble of wasting time and money by wholeheartedly recommending the Doss Touch.
----Update----
I purchased the the 20W Sounbox Pro, but later found out it doesn't connect with this model for TWS. My attempt to add that speaker messed up the ability of my Doss Touch Sounbox to reconnect with Alexa. I emailed customer support and they contacted me within an hour and were incredibly helpful. They are replacing the speaker and told me I can keep the original one, which still connects to my phone's with bluetooth. I am so impressed by this company and this little speaker. Doss really stands behind their products!

title: Why is this getting such good reviews?! Much better for the money!
text:
I needed a small blue tooth speaker because the Echo Dot sound quality just wasn't cutting it and i would like to add music to whatever room I am working in that may not have a device. I have an Echo Dot 2nd and 3rd gen. The 2nd gen is tinny and the 3rd way too bass centric and boomy, but still better than this speaker. The sound quality doesn't blow me away, in fact, it is pretty bad. Not enough bass and not much of an improvement over my Echo Dot Mini 2nd Gen. Wow, this is so disappointing. The speaker paired easily with my phone and laptop, but had an issue pairing with the Alexa app via blue tooth. The controls are a pain to see in low light. As long as you keep your expectations super low you will be happy.
----Update-----
Lost another star after buying the Doss Touch speaker for $4 more. The Doss has MUCH better sound quality and paired to Echo Dot instantly. The Oontz seems to be having difficulties with Alexa. Probably going to return this and buy the upgraded version of the Doss 20W because I am much more impressed with that speaker as a whole. The sound quality on the Doss is more balanced and it has True Wireless Stereo so both can be used simultaneously. At first it was about being an upgrade to the Echo Dot sound quality, but now it's about better sound with every device. I was never happy with the sound on the Oontz to begin with and now it's completely unacceptable after trying a much better speaker within the same price range.

How Panasonic has managed to have these phones recognize their brand of battery is beyond me.  It is maddening that we are forced to find specific AAA's to keep our phones operative.  Smart marketing if you want to sell more batteries but upsetting to customers that just want good cost effective phones.  We've had these phones for nearly ten years, they've been very descent.  But, when replacement is required, we will, at least look elsewhere and may find something that isn't so specific when it comes to replacement parts.

title: exactly what we needed
text: These speaker pins were exactly what was needed to connect our stranded wire to the spring clip connectors on our speakers. Constructed like a Banana Plug, the pin head guarantees a good connection. The color coded males come 2 to a box, enough to hook up a pair of speakers. Being a staight pin reduces the chance of crossing the leads. The price is very low and includes fast shipping. Sring clip connectors have some shortcomings.  Unless the wire is cleanly stripped and cut to exacting lengths, strands of wire can be loose and short the hot to ground leads.  Also, they can be inconvenient as the wires must be disconnected when moving the speakers or cleaning and dusting near them.  The more often the leads are reconnected, the less the tension holding the wire becomes.  These shortcomings can create noise, stastic, even cause an amplifier to turn off or cause component repair problems.  These inexpensiive connectors reduce the chances of such problems while making a professional looking connection.

title: An excellent product and price
text: I was hesitent to purchase this wire after reading so many negative reviews.  After receiving and reviewing this speaker wire, I'm at a loss to explain those reviews.  I am now retired but had spend a 40 year career working in electronics.  The wire was as described.  Excellent quality, 12 gauge.  It came with a red stripe to identify the hot lead.  The leads were individual strands of copper wire, not coated aluminum.  There was no large solid core surrounded by a few stand in order to cheapen construction while trying to meet the 12 gauge requirement.  The insulation was of high quality and easy to strip.  I've already run the entire 100 feet, it was one solid piece of wire and not pieces of different lengths as another has complained of.  I actually purchased this wire based on reviews at other sights, the reviews here were so bad, I had to see if the complaints were also present elsewhere.  They weren't.  I can't understand why many Amazon reviewers found so many problems when those negative reviews weren't duplicated at other sights (or by me).  It may be the luck of the draw but I am completely satisfied with the product.  It's actually worth quite a bit more than it's sale price, I must recommend it.

title: Not worth the price IMO
text:
Sound: Lots of issues here. Standard stereo quality is good, but not as good as my pair of Sennheiser HD555's. 7.1 quality is muddy and quiet. Tried both the Dolby and DTS and still couldn't find one that didn't sound like it wasn't being played out of a cardboard tube. The positional sound also seemed shifted right for some reason (tested by flipping headset around as well, then it was shifted left). Mic quality was "okay" according to those I spoke to, but sounded "more muffled" than my cheap USB headset. All-in-all, not impressed for the cost.

Comfort: While the ear pieces are comfortable, this is a heavy, large, bulky headset.

Connectivity: Never had any issues, walking around the room or otherwise.

Other: The lights are neat, and the fact that they sync'd up to my Logitech mouse's lights was cool too - but you can't see the lights. They're on your head - and they drop the battery life by 30% when they're on.

title: These are fantastic!!!
text:
I’ll start off saying that I have received zero compensation to write this review. We just like these so well at my home that I had to write a review.

My teen wanted bluetooth earbuds for Christmas. He’s terrible at keeping up with items, so I want buying the pricey big-name ones. My husband had a wireless set of earbuds that have the connector cord made by this company that he really likes, so we read the reviews on these and decided to give them a go.

Kiddo loves them. They stay in his ears while lying in bed and he often wakes up in the morning with one still in his ear! They’re just bulky enough to see when mixed in the sheets, but not bulky enough to be intrusive.

I have a great pair of connected Bluetooth earbuds by a big name company, but was tired of the cord getting in my way. I frequently only wear one bud so I can hear what’s happening around me, and the wire on that pair are in the way when worn like that. I jumped on board and ordered a pair of these for myself.

I love them. They are incredibly comfortable. I can’t wear apple’s buds because they hurt my ears. These are so comfy you have no clue they’re in your ear! Good noise cancelling, good sound.

The best part? Super easy pairing with your device! Literally just hold the button down and they connect. AND some genius made them actually read as “sound peat” in the bluetooth menu on the device. Not a single other bluetooth device we own actually says what it is in that menu- they’re all a string of letters and numbers. My Sony buds are like wic2000, my car is U2, my bluetooth speaker is “bts” but we have 2 so I have to guess. These are a no brainer!

They hold a good charge, the case is sturdy and they clip in there well with the magnet. I marked my headphones with a dot of nail polish and my case with a sticker to differentiate them from my son’s. I wish they came in fun colors, but that’s not a fault. (I didn’t want to do white because of grunge potential.)

So far these have been a great product. I’d def not hesitate to recommend them!

title: Good for birdwatching!
text:
I ordered these to replace a lower powered set for birdwatching in my back yard. These had good reviews, and were affordably priced, so I thought I would give them a go. They are perfect for my needs, which is viewing birds at a feeder or on our fence about 10-20 yards from our porch.

They are a decent size and heft, without being too large. They have a good field of vision and are easy to focus. I added a more padded strap, but it does come with a basic strap and a decent little case with a shoulder strap. title: Durable Camera, Easy to Use, Photo Quality Below Par...
text:
My husband and I are both avid shutterbugs, and my almost 3 year old son really wanted a camera to take his own photos. We had a few gift cards that we had not used, so we invested in this camera. He was very excited to get it and uses it often, he especially likes to take it on Photo Safaris with us. It is also a hit in the neighborhood among all the kids who take photos like crazy with it.

Pros: Seems quite durable. Buttons are easy to use for him, while the batteries and sd card (optional) are easy to keep out of his reach. Photos download easily and cable is included in the kit. The optional SD card (I got a cheapie 512meg) adds storage for over 1000 extra pictures.

Cons: Does go through batteries quickly- but we use rechargables anyway for most things. Photo quality is TERRIBLE- and I just don't mean terrible because we are photographers ourselves, I mean TERRIBLE in general. The photos are most frequently blurry and dark- even with flash or bright sunlight. Also, I don't think they would even print well at 4x6 but we have not tried. We will have to upgrade him to a cheap digital point and shoot once he is able to treat this camera nicely. (I will upload a few sample shots to customer photos.) Another con is the discard photo button is right there on the back- great for them to erase the photo they just took without realizing it.It also makes a rather annoying noise when any button is pushed- which encourages the button pushing to go on and on and on.

OVerall, the camera performs as expected, just wish the photo quality was better, but again, this is a camera for my preschooler so I should not expect too many megapixels I guess.

text:
The only thing keeping me from giving the Tap a full 5-star reviews is an issue with the line-in port. I recently purchased a pico projector — [[ASIN:B005Q2EGG6 AAXA P300 Pico/Micro LED Projector with 60 Minute Battery Life, WXGA 1280x800 Resolution, 400 Lumens, HDMI, Mini-VGA, 15,000 Hour LED Life, Media Player]] — for watching movies out on my patio. The projector comes with speakers but they are not even close enough to project sound over the crickets in the lawn. I figured the Tap would be ideal for this purpose so I plugged each end of a male-to-male audio cable into the projector and Tap. The problem I found is the Tap takes a second to start playing the audio from the line-in, which causes a significant lip syncing lag. Otherwise the Tap is a great product.
If Amazon can somehow fix this lag then I would be willing to change my review but for now this is definitely a negative for me.

title: Made the switch from Apple
text:
I had been shopping around for awhile for a replacement for my 1st Gen iPad which is showing its age. After doing a lot of research I decided to go with the Galaxy Tab Pro 12.2 thanks to the larger screen and that is comes with double the storage of the base model iPad Air. While I love my other Apple products I feel like they have become complacent in the innovation department since their founder's death.
I needed a tablet that my wife could use for laying in bed watching Netflix and/or browsing the web and that I could bring to meetings for note taking and other business needs. I love that this tablet offers the ability to have multiple users that can be switched pretty much on the fly. this way I can have the apps I use front and center like the Hancom Office suite that syncs well with the Office software I'm used to, and cloud software like Evernote and Dropbox.
I also picked up a [[ASIN:B00I3ERXWS Logitech Pro Protective Case with Full-Size Keyboard for Samsung Galaxy Note Pro and Samsung Galaxy Tab Pro (920-006319)]] with it and the two work very well together on a desk.
The only downside I've found is something that I can't control, the fact that it is an anomaly in my otherwise Apple-centric ecosystem, but that is a sacrifice I was willing to make for a superior product.

title: It's big. but powerfull
text:
First, a warning: This card is big, very big in fact. The third in my build since 2009 and an upgrade from the EVGA Geforce 550Ti and the jump in quality is pretty significant. Though I was running Far Cry 3 on Very High settings before there was some annoying pop-in and postfx looked horrid running at around 30 fps. After seeing it running on a friend’s xbox I can say it was running at around console quality. Note: I understand fully that Far Cry 3 is a console developed game first and a PC game second, as many are these days.
After installing the 660 Ti the game is now running at a super sooth 60+fps on Ultra settings and is smooth as butter. I was also able to bring out the draw distance quite a bit and disable the postfx completely, now the game looks gorgeous from high elevations like radio towers and mountain tops. But like I said, this card is huge. Because if its size it blocked two of my SATA ports on my mobo, forcing me to move which ones my two HDDs and DVD drive were using, which caused some minor boot issues that I was quickly able to resolve through BIOS.
It runs quiet and cool but requires more power than my old card but that wasn't an issue for me.

title: Worth the money

Like everyone else I bought this to avoid the new lease fee on my Cisco branded modem I got when I signed up with TWC a little over a year ago. title: Good Idea and price, cheap junk on the inside
text:
Hello
I have purchased this for a small office, I run mail and a file server so I need to have the network up at all times.
The device is nice and easy to setup, concept is good and the price is not bad. This is where the good ends. I received the unit pulled it out of the box and started playing with it everything works well, then I turn off the stereo and I hear a very faint buzz coming from the unit. Since I work with electronics almost daily (component level repairs) I knew that the power supply will die soon, (it was a sign of a cheap ps).
I decided at only $130 im not going to send it back I will fix it myself (i don't really care about warranty).
Under the cover there are 3 boards. 1 relay outlet board, 2 power supply, 3 controller. The controller board (the one with the display) was ok, it didn't look bad at all. The relay outlet board I have found 2 cold solder spots, that would cause malfunctions with an outlet down the line. After fixing it I pull out the power supply and OMG, that this looks like someone was first learning how to solder, the board had a ton of faults, remaining flux and cotton from swabs. I decided to throw the power supply out instead I installed 12v to 5v converter for the controlls and connected 12v for relays. Installed external plug for a 12v ps and it works great with no problems.

This unit is ok.
It should have a good power supply (a $5 ps from china is 100 times better than what it came with)
It should be using solid state relays (it would be silent, and it would last much longer, also you would only need 5v to supply it)

Good Luck

title: Exactly what I wanted, Exactly what was promised.
text:
Pretty much exactly what I was looking for. Received these a while back and was waiting on getting my Corsair RGB K95. These keys look stunning with backlighting on, and off. Front printed caps won't wear down with use for those times when you just need to glance at the keys.

With the fullness of the RGB keyboards' backlighting, it does make all lettering on keys harder to read. I expected this. The whole key is translucent and thus letting the light flow through. If you're in the market for having the letters stand out on keycaps for keyboards, I would suggest looking for doubleshot keycaps designed for backlighting.

The keys feel great to me, and I definitely did not have any burrs or imperfections on the under-side of my keycaps, this includes any adhesive used to keep it on the foam / board. each of my keys came pristine.

I would like to note that if one has purchased directly from max keyboard, they offer standard box packaging, and simple packaging (keys loose in plastic bags) I would say the difference in price is well worth it for the packaging that is delivered with this product.

On a side note, the keycap puller works great, but I prefer a wire key puller when it comes to working with full sets, easier (for me) to grab several before having to drop the key, and go back every time, but that doesn't take away from the experience, especially since they include a key puller for you.

The picture quality was different on both, one screen was super bright, and even with changing the settings you couldn't get the pictures just right. The other one worked fine and then stopped working altogether, leaving us with just the first super bright screen one.
Amazon happily refunded my money, and I reordered these monitors (the reviews lead my to believe is just got some dude). When the replacement monitors came they were in a different box. The screen it self looks the same but the s video different. So instead of just being able to switch out the monitors, I had to comes merely re-wire the whole thing, pain in the butt. Ugh.

We'll see what happens with the new monitors...

title: Great, but missing a few features.
text:
The stereo works as it's supposed to, but there are a few things I would like to have that it doesn't... Like an ATT button, though if you get the remote (JVC RM-RK258), it has an ATT button that works with the stereo.

Also if you want to use the Apps like Waze or another GPS like app you have to connect a cable to the front use port as well as the back, which is ugly. I'd prefer they just have wires running out the back only, but what can you ya do.

Lastly if you have two phone that are connected to the Bluetooth audio then you have to go into the setting manually to switch between which phone can play music through it, even if the phone that is currently connected isn't playing music or even near the car.

Overall, the stereo works well. And if still buy it again.

title: Handy Little Remote
text:
Works.
It's nice to be able to change the volume, source, chapter of a movie, pause movie, etc. Also our stereo doesn't have an "ATT" button, but the remote does and it works, which is always a nice feature.

We use this with a JVC KWV21BT stereo.

title: Love it!
text:
The battery lasts a long time, the surface is easy to clean, and it is compact. Bluetooth works well, as well as the direct jack. It's a little annoying how it always tells me the battery life when I turn it on, but I suppose that's good for some people. I usually use it at home, so it's easy enough to find a plug when I need it. It lasts for a good while after you get the low battery please charge now message so you don't need to go running for the cord right away.

I have the black one, I like it more than the colorful ones made for millennials and children...It's a nice silicone finish, so if I get stuff on it while baking or whatever it wipes right off.

The sound quality isn't quite as good as my larger bose sound wave, but it's much better than other little portable speakers! It fills up the room well, and can get plenty loud enough for me. Don't spend less on the crummy brand, just get this one and you won't have to get another for a long time.

title: Horrible reflections inside and the diffuser is pointless
text:
The frame is pretty sturdy and easy to put together which is the main reason it has 2 stars instead of 1.

I bought this for photographing jewelry. It says it's good for jewelry and eliminates harsh shadows and reflective glare. This is not true at all. The edges of the box make black line reflections. The bumpy reflective surface reflects back onto the metal being photographed and turns what should be a nice flat mirror polish into a horrible bumpy looking mess. The "diffuser" is pretty much pointless, you can still see the lights clearly through it, plus that convenient hole in the top to shoot photos through? That's covered by the diffuser if you use it. Also, whenever anything touches the led boards from above (I mean if you set a light object (like the box flap) on top of the box or touch it with your hand) the lights under the pressure change to a yellowish color.

I wish I had returned this before I recycled the box it came in, I would have been better off making my own lighting setup. I wound up lining the entire inside with paper, and taped paper under the lights for a better diffuser that you can actually see past to take photos from above. I still need to line more spots with paper...

title: Good, but cuts out
text: I've had two phone calls with this so far, and I love the fact that I don't have to put the dirty phone up to my ear to take a call. The downside though is that even if I'm not walking around, the call seems to break up a bit. Not sure if this happens when the cord naturally moves around, but it shouldn't have such a loose connection to cause the call to break up. It could have been the other party I was talking to, but I talk to him often and he made it a point to tell me I was breaking up (and had no idea I was using this), so I don't know. But the sound quality is utterly amazing, just as good as if I hold the phone up to my ear. And I often take dictation, so the receiver makes it a lot easier to type, especially since the phone tends to echo the "clacking" of the keys and cut the speaker off so I miss some words they have said, whereas the receiver does not.

title: Fantastic alternative if your car doesn't have Bluetooth
text:
I had no idea something like this existed until I saw it on one of those "Best Things I Ever Bought on Amazon" lists. I had Bluetooth in my old car, and I miss it. My husband's car doesn't have Bluetooth or, at least, it didn't. It does now, and it's so easy to set up! You simply plug this into your car's cigarette lighter, and it automatically finds the radio station that will work the best, depending on your location. You switch over to that station, and boom, connected! You'll even get a man's voice when you turn your car on telling you "waiting for connection," and then "successfully paired" once it syncs up, which doesn't take long at all.

CONS:
You have to leave the car on that radio station all the time for the Bluetooth to work, so this is better if you don't rely on scanning the radio much for car entertainment and use your phone for music more often. You also have to search for a phone number on your phone itself, so it's not ideal for calling people while driving unless you make the phone call first.

PROS:
There are two USB charger ports, so you can charge two phones at the same time (or two devices that use USBs). And here's an added bonus - the charger is turbocharged! I charged my phone from 14% to 65% in a 20-minute trip - excellent! Also, I was listening to an audio book on and off, and every time I turned the car on, the volume remained the same for the audio book - I didn't have to fiddle with it at all.

I didn't even know adding Bluetooth to your car was this easy. I thought I'd have to pay $300 for a mechanic to install it, so I put it off as something I just can't have in my husband's car. But this device makes it an almost seamless experience. The only true caveat I have with it is that I have to load up a phone number to call before I drive, but other than that, you just can't beat this little device for such a low price!

title: Great for Additional Space
text: We have a Bluetooth speaker with a short cord, so having to plug it in in our room while we were painting, we had to just let it dangle, which can't be good for the socket. I'm so glad to have found this inexpensive, sturdy socket shelf to boost the speaker and amplify the sound (and save the socket). Plus, you just can't beat using vertical space as additional storage.

title: Decent for the price
text:
I love this fitness tracker. I mainly bought it to start tracking my stress level and heart rate, and while I find that the watch itself is not always accurate, the app calculates your stats more accurately. For instance, while doing P90X, it said my heart rate was in the 90s. Uh, no. Though, the app said 140s, which yes, that's much more accurate. However, I honestly don't really care about that. I love getting the little "Move!" notifications, as it reminds me I've been sitting for too long and I need to get up and move around. I can already feel myself shaving inches off my hips by remaining more active. Plus, keeping an eye on my stress level and heart rate has helped me consciously lower both, and it even calculates your average sleep. I thought I was getting at least seven hours a night, but it's actually less, and I wouldn't have known that without the watch. This is due to the fact that I apparently have a lot of light sleep and barely any deep sleep. Ultimately, it serves as a loose reminder to take better care of myself, and even if it's not pinpoint accurate, that's enough for me to justify spending the money on it (bonus points for being able to take it into the shower after a workout!).

EDIT: Also, I find that the app drains the hell out of my phone battery. So I log out once I've logged most of my info for the day, then I log back in the next day to allow it to catch up. It still keeps all the information in the watch, so you don't lose anything, and you can save your phone's battery life.

title: Slower Charger
text: It's a slower charger than I would have liked - I prefer speedy chargers. It takes a whole day to charge the batteries, and even then they don't last long, even when the green light finally turns on. Donating this one and buying a different brand.

title: Delayed reaction, and too many buttons for my "dumb" TV
text: I bought this remote for my TCL LE48FHDF3300ZTA 48-Inch 1080p 240Hz LED HDTV because my dog chewed the one that came with the TV. This does the job, but there is a delay, so I have to press the buttons multiple times for it to register (unless it's just the batteries that came with it that may be going bad already). Also, my TV is not a smart TV, so most of the buttons on here are useless for my TV. It's funny to think that if I ever need another TV, I'll be trying to buy one that matches the remote.

title: Fabulous Headphones
text: I have yet to buy an AmazonBasics product that I don't like, which makes me very curious as to which well-known brand name is more than likely ghost-creating their products. That being said, I forgot how much I love over-the-ear headphones, as opposed to ear buds. For one thing, you can crank them up without fearing blowing your eardrums out. Instead of hearing the noticeable tinniness of the emphasized treble of ear buds, you can instead enjoy the full-throated bass of over-the-ear headphones - and man, do these deliver. The bass is *fantastic.* These are lightweight and cup nicely to the ears, and they are adjustable, of course. The pads on the ears are soft and squishy, and they are excellent at noise-canceling. You really can't beat the price at $14.99 for these. This is truly a great product.

title: Perfect for my needs as a second monitor
text: Much bigger than I had expected, but that actually worked out perfectly, due to my using it as a second monitor. The base is also adjustable, so you can make the monitor go as high or as low as you want it to go, which is EXCELLENT, since I need it to tower over my laptop in order to make an effective second screen. The only con I can really say is that the difference in the screen contrast when going back and forth between my laptop and this monitor sometimes hurts my eyes, but it's not that big of a deal. You just may want to look away for a second before looking between monitors, particularly if you have one display that is newer/fancier than this one.

title: Great for what I need it for (even though it can handle much more than that)

With this hard drive, I can feel confident that I have enough room for the first five years of his life, at least. This is a heavy-duty hard drive, though, so I know it can handle much more than what I'm using it for, but for what I need it for it's perfect just the same.

title: Wonderful Camera

It even has a lithium battery, so you don't have to worry about continuously buying batteries, though the camera needs to be charged for a full four hours before it's operable at all, which includes when you first receive it.

title: If you're in doubt, doubt no more.
text:
I was researching televisions for MONTHS and could not figure out which one to buy. My boyfriend is better at this stuff, so after I spent countless hours comparing TVs in Target, Wal-Mart and PC Richards, (and even securing a pre-order for a Coby, [which I quickly cancelled after hearing bad things]), I told him to see what he could find on Amazon. He found this TV and after sorting out what could be "insider reviews" from genuine ones, we decided that it sounded like a great deal for the money, and though the name is not exactly a household one yet, it was worth a shot, as another buyer said the same thing happened with Vizio a couple of years back.

So, we bought it for each other as a joint Christmas gift, figuring what the hey. If it wasn't as advertised, we'd send it back. And it had a lot to live up to, considering this was essentially our only gift to each other this year. It has been over a month now, and we LOVE this television.

Pros:

- No side glare - you can see the picture well, even if you are sitting on the side of the television.
- It is lightweight and super thin, so it is easy to transport.
- Very clear picture.
- Decent enough sound - you don't really need a sound bar if you don't have one, especially since there are options to change the sound (i.e. "music", "film", "surround sound", etc.)
-Provided you are not signed in to a game system (which you can change the video input from your remote), there is a setting where the TV will automatically shut itself off after 10 minutes of lack of use. This is very helpful if you have a roommate who tends to fall asleep in front of the television.
- There are plenty of settings to customize the picture and sound, as well as "label" your game systems with the pre-loaded options so you know which video input to select for your X-Box or PS3 (for example, I have the PS3 set to "Blue Ray", whereas the X-Box is set to "Game").

Cons:

-It is not a "smart TV", if you are in the market for one of those. It's a simple design, which was perfect for us.
-There are no buttons on the TV itself, so if the remote ever breaks, I have no idea how we are going to turn it on and off, aside from buying a new remote.
-There are a shortage of plugs in the back for cables. For example, I can hook up the cable box, X-Box and PS3, but there is no room now for the sound bar. Not a huge deal, but I could see where some people might find that to be annoying.

This television lived up to all of the positive reviews it received here on Amazon, and I am so thoroughly satisfied that we decided to go with this one that I kept reminding myself to write this review so I could help others who were as in the dark as we were about which TV to buy. I didn't get the dreaded "green screen" upon turning it on, as some people have experienced, and the packaging didn't overly give it away that it was a TV, (though we got the 48" one, so I'm sure people could figure it out).

Bottom line: If you are in as much doubt as we were about which TV to buy, trust us on this one - TCL rocks!

title: Doesn't cooperate with Samsung Galaxy S10+ and Liberty 2 Pro earbuds, awful tech support
text:
Was looking for best way to increase the volume and enhance the tone on my Galaxy S10+ when using with Liberty 2 Pro earbuds. I read alot of reviews on
Amazon and elsewhere saying this was the kit to get. Boy was I disappointed.
First of all, design wise the piece is simple too small and the LED screen window and print is tiny, and dark. Barely legible, and that's inside. I probably could have accepted that had I been able to get it to work. Spent hours trying to set-up, firmware update, resetting all devices codecs to"AAC" only. It did pair its bluetooth connection with my phone, however none of the controls on it had any effect on the phones audio output, so I got from the phone only what I got when Fiio was not connected. Worst part was the Fiio support. In a word, it s*ckec, in my experience. No US tech support or chat support. I sent 3 detailed emails explaining the problem and they were all misconstrued or answered without reading the previous ones. Their genius advice was to change phones and replace the Fiio. Because of the time difference between east coast and asia, replies took a day to answer. I really wanted this device to work, however in the end, and due to their awful/useless tech support I returned it to Amazon, who was great handling the return. My advice is to try another company with good reviews and good tech support. These guys are not that, in my experience, and neither was the device.

title: Quiet, Fast, and Large!
text:
We had a Dell XPS 200 which we sat next to when working. It made you feel as if you were in a jet taking off, often generating headaches due to the infernal racket! A strong desire to hang on to Windows XP motivated us to keep it. It was trusty otherwise, so we endured seven noisy years before the poor thing died one day, taking XP with it.
I'm a bit burned out from paying about $1,000 for a workable computer, going to "Buy and Configure" sites for bargains which are unusable until "configured", which brings your $499 special up to a much higher price. One of my son's friends, a computer science major, found out we were shopping, and gave us one word as advice: REFURB. I'd never considered a refurb, but he explained that a refurb bought from a reliable source was as good as new.
I had used an Optiflex at work and had really liked it, so I was somewhat pre-sold on the 745. It was also a way of avoiding Windows 8.
We've had it about two weeks, and it is silent. It's powerful and sharp looking, with really good graphics and sound. The hard drive is big enough for anyone, and its speed is great. If it keeps up its dependable behavior, it will be around here for a very long time. Strongly recommended, as is Windows 7 Pro, a big and positive step up from XP.

title: Bluetooth Car Kit FOR 2004 Toyota Tacoma
text:
I started off by watching a youtube video on how to pull the radio and install Bluetooth module (another brand). My installation took me about 30 minutes. This module also has a USB and 3.5 mm plug and a mic for additional inputs, mp3 ect. Since I was mounting my module out of sight behind the dash, above the glove box, I also bought, from Amazon, Numkuda USB 3.0 & 3.5mm Car AUX USB Extension Cable 3.3 FT Panel Headphone Male Jack Flush Mount Adapter, which is mounted below the ashtray. I have hooked up my Samsung phone using the aux cable to headphone jack, and also by Bluetooth, To my ear, I find Bluetooth just as clear and bright for music playback. Bonus no additional cable to futz with. I mounted the mic to the left of radio above the clock, a test call with my wife was clear audio over the radio and her only suggestion was to speak up a little bit, I did and then she was hearing me easily. This module is the best add-on I have installed in my truck. Over the years I have used FM transmitters which worked, sort of, on a trip I'd have to readjust the frequency due to bleed-over, not to mention the static... Then I installed an Android mirror also with an FM transmitter, and truth be told it worked pretty well for about a year before getting so much static it became impossible to listen to. The front and rear cameras record good and the GPS works well, so not a total fail.
If you are thinking of getting one of these Bluetooth Car Kits, start by getting the model number off of your OEM radio, located in left lower corner of radio to the right of the SEEK button. By having the model number you will be able to see if you need the Toyota (5+7) Pin plug-in or the Toyota (6+6) Pin plug-in, once you know that, you are 30 minutes away from great sound. As you can see in the pictures I have an Amazon 8 tablet with torque running off of an OBD II Scanner (from Amazon) I had to reposition it due to it hanging down into my leg, so I purchased a y spliter (from Amazon) with switches and was able to plug it into my trucks OBD II plug as it was almost flat when plugged in. I bought my Tacoma new in 2004 and have no plan to get rid of it. Now just like my wife's 2017 Subaru Legacy I get in and start the truck, and I am automatically connected by Bluetooth to the truck, music ready to go...SO SLICK!

title: Will pair with only one device at a time; sounds horrible
text:
In full disclosure, I must admit that I miss my Bose Bluetooth speaker. Their acoustics are impeccable. The "Tribit XSound Go Bluetooth Speakers" only cost a fraction of my Bose speaker. I first purchased the "DOSS Touch Wireless Bluetooth" which is in the same price range; I returned that product because it lacked bass and was unimpressive overall. The Tribit, however, has plenty of bass for such a small speaker. Ironically, the problem that I have is the treble! I think it is an inherent problem with smaller speakers and not this particular device. I have installed an equalizer on my computer which mitigates some of the problems and makes the speaker sound very acceptable.

The pros:
• The speaker is loud! It is perfect for a jam session in your bedroom. I'm not sure it is suitable for large or multi rooms.
• The quality is good, and the speaker looks like a million bucks.
• It has an excellent microphone that works well with phone calls and even to interact with Siri or Cortana.
• The Play button allows one to answer, reject or end a call. It also can play or pause a song. Finally, it allows you to skip a music track forward or backward.

The cons:
• While the bass is fairly impressive, the treble is slightly overriding.
• The battery does not nearly last for 24 hours if you like to blast music as I do
• The speaker can only be paired to one device at a time. If you are listening to music on the computer and the phone tries to connect, the speaker will sometimes disconnect from all devices. The speaker does have an av input one could connect to the computer but obviously, the speaker would no longer be completely portable. This could be a deal breaker for many.

After comparing this speaker with others in its price range, I realize that this speaker has such poor sound quality that I could never recommend it to anyone.
