text:
I’m updating my review because I ended up returning them after several frustrating runs.

I wanted these for exercise but I got fed up after 1) the connection to my iPhone would drop 2) when running they would start to come out of my ears even with many different variations of the ear-wings and the inserts and when you touched them to push them in the touch features would activate 3) Alexa was hit or miss. I would be running on trails where there really was not much noise, but she didn’t always respond to voice commands

So I bought these about two weeks ago at full price and when I logged in to leave this review imagine my surprise to see them at 40 dollars less. Honestly, even at 40 less they are quirky. Sometimes Alexa answers but sometimes you have to say her name several times. I also have trouble when I am jogging out in the woods as it seems like Alexa has to have the WiFi instead of being able to use a cellular connection. As such, if I want to change songs I have to use my phone instead of hands free. In addition sometimes songs just stop for no reason.

The sound is good but I still don’t think it is too much better than the 40 dollar no name versions I have had in the past. The fit is good but that is due to having so many options for both in ear bud and ear wing. (And since I usually use these when working out I bought these because they had an ear-clip/wing option to keep them in.)

I believe these are ok for a first generation Alexa integrated war bud option, but just like Alexa for my car, I think I should have waited for the next generation.

title: Awesome Tablet. I love it!
text:
I purchased this Android 10.0 Tablet to have an extra one around the house for everyone to share, even though we all have smartphones already.
This tablet was already charged when I received it, but fully charged it anyway to get a full maximum charge. This unit is made of very sturdy aluminum and glass and the picture quality is very sharp and colorful. The tablet has a quick response time to my touch and the applications run very smoothly.
The tablet is fairly lightweight, easy to hold, and great for true portability. I like that it comes with 32GB of storage plus a micro SD card slot so I can expand the memory to 128GB if necessary.
I was able to use it an entire day while traveling or visiting people in the hospital without needing access to charge it constantly. I was also able to have ZOOM and TEAMS meetings without having lag issues.

The tablet arrived very quickly and in mint condition. Overall: This is an excellent quality tablet for an affordable price. I would recommend this tablet to all friends and family if they need one.

text:

title: Compact Camera that can do EVERYTHING
text:
For the simple fact that this camera can do EVERYTHING I want it to do in my pocket, it get 5+ stars. I could go on for days about this camera, but I will try to hold this review to my personal game-changers.

HFR: Shooting video at 1080p, 120fps (100MB) and slowing down the footage in post produces better slow-mo videos compared to the HFR feature that can do 1080p 240fps at the best quality. The ultra HFR feature was a big sell for me, but I feel like 480fps and 960fps have garbage quality and it's really really difficult to get the timing right when you are taking the shot in that feature mode because you only have a 2 second timeframe. I must have spent 2 hours trying to get a slow-mo shot of a bee in my garden when I first bought it, but could never get the timing right on pressing record when the stupid bee would start flying. Shooting in normal video mode at 120fps and slowing down in post at 24fps is seriously amazing, and I will likely never use the HFR again.

Time-Lapse: Pay the $9.99 extra to download this app, because holy cow, it is freaking awesome. There is full manual control over intervals, # shots, etc, and it blows me away that it can produce day-night time-lapse with little to no flicker and amazing color with accurate white balance throughout. If you don't want the hassle of editing the stills in post, then you can just have the camera produce a 1080p 24fps video file in-camera, although post allows you more creativity and ability to produce 4k time lapse.
Slog2: I've been shooting all my videos in Slog2 (4k & 1080p) since I bought the camera several months ago, and up until just now I did not have a computer beefy enough to process the footage in post (which is the reason I have waited on posting my review). For the last week, I've been color grading my Slog2 footage with the Color Finale plugin in Final Cut Pro X. The footage is stunning and the dynamic range blows me away. I'm still trying to figure out the over exposure sweet spot of shooting in Slog2, but for the most part it looks really nice when shot at +1 - +2 stops over exposed and re-adjusted in post. There's not as much noise in the shadows as I expected, and I'm about to get the Neat Video Noise Reduction plugin that I expect to help with the little noise that I'm seeing. I went out to Joshua Tree for the meteor shower and shot 4k 24fps video of the stars, which is insane for a little camera like this.

Lens: Having the faster lens fully zoomed in (f2.8) compared to the RX100 M1's f4.9 is changed the way I take photos of my baby. It really was difficult to get a decent bokeh shooting at typical portrait focal lengths with the M1, but very easy now with the M4. Fast, clean and crisp, this lens is great.

Compact Size: I wanted a camera that I can put in my pocket. As long as you don't wear skinny jeans, then you're good to go. I don't wear skinny jeans, but I'm just saying. Cargos are the best, but then I realize that I've become the dad that wears cargos, and then I see the guy in Honduras swapping heavy lenses with a dslr around his neck and don't feel so bad. Although, I often worry when it's in my pocket that the lens ring control might bend and not be as smooth as it is, but that hasn't happened.

Focus Modes: Changing between focus modes is my one gripe about this camera. In a run and gun environment, I have not been able to figure out how to easily toggle between the various auto focus modes. It's easy to go between MF and AF, but trying to toggle between the AF modes when trying to get the right video clip of my active baby is extremely difficult. However, note that using the lens ring in AF mode for rack focusing is possible, which I wasn't able to do on the RX100 M1.

Overall, I wanted a camera that could do EVERYTHING, do everything WELL, and that EVERYTHING it does WELL could fit in my pocket….

title: Filmmakers will love this camera.
text:
If you're looking for Cinema 4K capabilities on a budget, this camera will fit you nicely. Record full 4K 4096x2160 at 24p and UHD 4K 3840x2160 at 30p/24p. This camera records 4K 8 bit at 4:2:0 chroma subsampling (great for color grading), even better at 1080 (10 bit @ 4:2:2). You are able to record 4K, 10 bit @ 4:2:2, but you have to run it to an external recorder. If you do a lot of green screen composites--you'll want this 4K capability (the more resolution, the easy it is to key); talent with long, flowing hair keys perfectly... Also, if your project export will be 1080, for interviews, shooting 4K is a must. You can get the feeling of a two camera setup, using just this camera. For example, you can have a nice medium shot; and punch in for that emotional close up (200%) without any loss of resolution. A few other nice features are the recording format options available (MOV, MP4, AVCHD). It's nice to have options and what works best for your post workflows. And lets not forget the awesome Variable Frame Rate @ 96fps. The 96fps at 24p is so smooth! Love it. Finally, focal peeking. See exactly what areas in the shot are in focus--a great built in feature!

I would also recommend picking up the 64GB Class 10 U3 SD memory cards. This class of memory card is exactly what you need to be sure you're capturing at the fastest rate possible. The max bit rate on the GH4 is 25MB/s and the Class 10 U3 cards are rated at 30MB/s.

The build quality, hands down, is solid. You will not be disappointed!

title: If I have to open my phone to open the Alexa app, what’s the point?
text:
I have Bluetooth audio in my vehicle. This Alexa Auto is not plug and play even after setup is complete. Each time I start the car, I have to change my input on my infotainment screen to Bluetooth Audio first. Then I have to have the Alexa app open on my phone! If I go to SiriusXM, Alexa won’t work again. What is the point of the device other than the additional microphones, when I can set the Alexa app on my phone to use the microphone on the phone. It’s too many steps each time to make it functional, but I think the worst thing is it won’t even play music that is locally on my phone! It only uses Amazon Music’s playlists.
This product unfortunately for me is a dud, and does not add any functionality to my vehicle that I don’t already have. I’m returning it.

title: Speed speed speed. Great router for splitting traffic.
text:
Gigabit ports for plugged devices maximize my cable connection. I have 100Mbs rated Internet. Old netgear router with 100Mb ports would only get 72Mbs speed tests. This Archer 9 gets me 112Mbs throughput on wired connections. I also love the ability to have two radios at 2.4 and 5ghz. I named both of my SSIDs the same, and the router and devices are smart enough to pick the fastest and most efficient radio. Devices like my WiFi printer selected the 2.4ghz, while my apple devices all go on the 5gjz spectrum. The smartphone app is nice to use and is easy to setup the router with basic functionality. You’ll need the browser though if you wish to fine tune settings for the more IT type folks like myself. The app allows you a quick glance to see what/how many devices are connected, and you can easily kick a device off if you choose to.
Overall, I am quite pleased with this Archer AC1900. It performs automatic firmware updates for the latest security patches if needed as well. Aesthetically, it is also pretty cool looking, and not just a square black box. I also like that is stands vertically, so it has a smaller footprint while actually increasing radio coverage.
Overall, I would recommend this router, and it is slightly less expensive than other comparable brands.

In any case, it is a tight fit after getting the screw/bolt in place and then inserting the speaker wire. title: Great Choice, Excellent Price
text:
Update: After less than 60 days of owning the TV, the ENTIRE audio panel died. None of the external audio ports work anymore for no reason whatsoever. Worked fine, then boom just stopped working. Thought it was my soundbar, so I bought a new soundbar, but nope, soundbar works just fine when connected to the cable box. Amazon Prime was awesome in helping me return it, and I'll be picking up a more reliable brand. When it came time to purchase a new TV we approached it the same way we approached buying a house. We made a list of the features we wanted (a SmartTV with Wifi, streaming channels, Amazon Prime, 40” and affordable at around the $250 mark). After looking at our options in terms of price and convenience, we decided that it made the most sense to purchase it through Amazon Prime.

After much research, we decided that the TCL TV’s offered the best value, met our budget requirements, and our decision to purchase the TV through Amazon enabled us to purchase the TV with interest free financing over 6 months.
Appearance.
The TV came in a large box with the stand hardware: remote, power cable and batteries plus simple instructions that were in separate bags. You do not get a HDMI or any other cables. The TV has a simple non-fussy design with approximately half inch bezel all around. The stand that comes with it is simple and screws on with two screws at each side. The stand footprint requires about 8.5 inches of depth to stand on. I like that the stand is low profile raising the screen about 2” above the surface it is standing on.

Setup

The old analog phono inputs are on the back and quite hard to reach once the TV is up on the mantle and they protrude straight out the back which would require more space between the wall and the TV if you use them. The power cable plugs into a recessed area low down on the left side and doesn’t interfere with the location of the tv. All the modern input and output sockets are behind the screen on the right side about 8 inches back. We don’t use any subscription TV service; just a double bowtie antenna mounted on one of the gutter pipes at the back of the house. The coaxial input for the antenna along with three HDMI ports, an optical input, 3.5mm jack and USB socket are all here. We use two of the HDMI sockets one for the 1TB Media hub and the other for our notebook.

Once everything is plugged in and turned on. The TV introduces you to the basic setup process. It takes less than five minutes to find your way around. The remote is minimalist with the most basic controls on the front (Volume Up/Down toggle and mute buttons on the side). It’s small, unfussy and easy to use. The UI for the TV is not flashy but functional and easy to navigate. Setting up WIFI, registering your TV and introducing you to streaming channels and how to add them to your desktop are covered quickly and then you are left to your own devices.

Since we are just using an antenna we were initially a little apprehensive. Wondering how well that would work, or even if the TV had a tuner since everyone seems to use dish or cable these days. It has a tuner that works flawlessly. We managed to pick up almost 3 dozen channels many of them HD. A quick look online showed us a map of where the broadcast towers are and helped us aim our antenna for best reception.

In use.

The TV has a really nice clean picture and since it is an LED TV where a grid array of LED's light the screen uniformly rather than a couple of fluorescent lamps there is practically no limit to the viewing angle. The screen is not high gloss and prevents reflection and most glare from bright light sources. When turned on a non invasive 3” horizontal strip of illuminated plastic at the bottom shows you the TV is powered on. It flashes during startup and goes out when the screen is illuminated.

Image

Image quality is excellent BUT on initial setup it is on a bright echo setting. Which is very high contrast and overly saturated. I guess it is a power saving mode (claimed 16 watts) but it is a bit stark and overwhelming and shows some dithering on smooth color transitions as though it is running at a lower bitrate with fewer colors. When turned to theater mode the quality of the picture is MUCH better with very smooth transitions on subtle colour gradients.

Sound

Sound is similar. Like most LCD style TV’s this one comes with tiny speakers. Again the default sound setting seems to be very flat. Probably to conserve energy. There are about four presets and again we went with theater which gives the broadest range and warm midtones without overdoing the bass. It doesn’t sound too bad and is not thin and reedy like the default setting.

Smart TV functionality.

We originally wanted WIFI because as Amazon Prime members we get a lot of free on demand media. This is similar to Netflix where you can watch a huge catalog of TV and movies for free, buy or rent them for a small fee. The same goes with music. This worked perfectly.

What we weren’t expecting was the sheer volume of streaming media available for free via WIFI. There are hundreds of channels, many of them free to choose from, many mainstream ones that let you view their current episodes of popular shows on demand when you want to watch them. You can also sign up for pay for view services like HBO and showtime individually.

One nice thing is that the TV has a global search option. You can search for anything by title, director, actors name, character, keywords and the TV will find everything relating to your search and list what is available by channel. So you can easily pick out what you want to see.

Mobile devices and streaming from those devices

There are apps for Android and iOS as well as Windows. I was able to control the TV from all our devices. In many ways it is more responsive, especially if you need to type in text. If you have media on your PC there are Apps for the TV that will let you stream from your phone, notebook, desktop computer etc.

Streaming from those devices tends to work ok. I did find that the TV’s built-in media player was a little limited in supported data formats. Setting up our digital media hub with its own channel was very easy and luckily our Western Digital media hub has far more extensive support for many of the more exotic file formats like FLAC lossless digital audio. And other formats are more often limited to computers. The TV does support the more mainstream formats like mp3, mpg, jpg etc.

Conclusion

For us, this TV proved to be a very good and affordable purchase. Especially when you factor in the 6 months interest fee financing Amazon offers prime members. We did sign up for a free month of Netflix too. The remote has a dedicated Netflix and Amazon streaming button. But we were not that impressed with Netflix when our Amazon Prime membership offered all the same features and more thanks to the addition of Amazon Prime music.

When you combine all this TV’s features with our media hub and Amazon Prime we are a bit overwhelmed with the sheer amount of stuff out there to watch. Even if we had no antenna and just a WIFI internet connection. The vast number of free streaming HD channels is extensive making the need for TV subscription plans pretty much obsolete unless you have a very specific need.

We really like this TV and highly recommend it.

title: Okay, brackets could be a little less flexible for my taste
text:
The came well packaged, but with only visual images of random possible settings (of every one except the one I needed), it took a few minutes to figure out how to lay it out. No instructions at all. I was left to figure out if I install the bracket behind or in front of the tv mount. In my case I was mounting a TCL 40" LCD with a Vizio 2.0 Soundbar. Laying both items on a solid flat surface is the best way to figure out how best to mount it. I ended up placing the brackets in a manner that allowed me to flush mount the soundbar to the tv, and I don't see the bracket or wires. I laid the bracket on the tv then the articulating mount over the soundbar bracket. If I did it the other way, the brackets would not have lined up over the screw holes.
To make the TV mount flat and even, I placed two washers in the upper screw holes of the tv to make up for the thickness of the soundbar brackets that attached to the lower two screw holes on the tv.
Overall it looks great, but these brackets probably weren't the best choice for me because the width of the soundbar screws only allowed me to screw the brackets into two holes on the tv instead of four, which I think would have made it more stable. If I push on the soundbar, it will flex backwards a little bit, but I have no actual concern of it falling off.
I wish these came with any kind of instructions to guide me to the best possible install. Luckily, I'm smart and made it work.
These brackets would have to be about 4 inches longer to make an ideal fit for my situation of widely placed screws on the soundbar, and a narrow VESA pattern of 100*150

title: Not good for glasses-wearing customers, but the option to switch ears is great
text: I am, unfortunately, going to have to order a different headset. I had high hopes for this one, based on its reviews, but it is problematic for me. First, what I like: the ability to wear it on your left or right ear is brilliant, and the sound quality is fine--not optimal, I think, but fine. The controls would be convenient for many people, but they are not for me, which leads me to my major frustration with this headset: it is definitely not for glasses-wearers. I should have foreseen this, honestly, but I didn't. The piece that fits behind the ear is quite large, and even though I wear super thin, flexible glasses frames, there really isn't enough room for both the headset and my glasses behind my ear. It is next to impossible to put on this headset one-handed without my glasses on--with them, there's no chance, as far as I can tell. Trying to operate the controls makes my glasses move around on my face, which is definitely unpleasant while driving. I also find the rubber piece that fits in the ear uncomfortable. I switched to the small size option, but it still seems to be a little too large, and its shape is definitely less comfortable than that of my old Bose headset. One last comment--the packaging is terrible to get into, and you have to basically destroy it to open it, which means returning it is not really an option. I'm giving it 3 stars because I think it would be a fine headset for many people, even though it's a poor one for me.

title: Great detailed pictures for adult coloring!
text:
I am a adult who has taken on the new hobby of adult coloring. Having purchased many coloring books, markers, gel pens and colored pencils I was excited to add this to my collection. The pictures in this book are very well drawn with accuracy of the animal/images. I do like that each page is a single image without filling the pages of additional scenery. It definitely allows for the colored image to stand out very well.
I did find the pages to be a bit thinner than other books so that using caution with your pointed pencil/gel pen would be warranted as not to tear when applying pressure for color. The prints are one sided so any bleeding through will not affect the next picture. I would recommend placing a protection between pages (I use piece of poster board) to support this.
This book does not have perforated pages to remove your picture when completed and is the first book that I have gotten that is not bound but stapled together.
This book has 40 images to color which is more than most books have. Each image consists of the subject with a lot of variety of figures within which makes it very fun to color. There is great detail in each animal/tree/fish/bird/plant to make for a very interesting picture when you are finished.
I would recommend this book if you love detail and just be a bit gentle on its production.
I received this product at a discount in exchange for my unbiased and honest review.

title: Incredible sound, fair price.
text:
This product has officially impressed me. I'm glad I went ahead with the purchase, apprehensive though I may have been, as 250.00 dollars isn't chump change for me. I'm upgrading from a god-knows-how-old Klipsch THX 2.1 setup, which has been tried and true, but left me wanting more after all of these years. The highs and mids reveal things to me that I simply had not heard with my old speakers. Crisp, clear and sound true to the real crash of the cymbal and crunch of the guitar... The lows are punchy and tight, powerful, but adjustable and not overbearing (I'm an avid metal listener, and don't often require ridiculous bass). Overall, I have to say the sound is incredible considering I spent what I did. Also, the bluetooth aptX functionality is amazing (provides near-lossless sound over BT), and I appreciate that level of detail.

The only constructive criticism I have regarding the setup as a whole, is the remote. It really is terrible haha. A little hockey puck that is easy to fumble around, and you have to be sure you have it properly oriented every time as it's an IR remote (as opposed to BT or WiFi), meaning you have to have it pointed right at the device for it to work. This can be an annoyance if you are in a darkly lit room.

Still, the product overall is worthy of 5 stars in my opinion. Well done!

title: Bad power supply, seems to be a constant issue with this company.
text: The components that make up this computer are decent, but they tossed in a bad power supply.  The thing would restart itself as soon as you attempted to play a video game, or do anything even slightly demanding of the computer.  After days of frustration and research, finally decided to go to a local retailer and buy a new power supply in order for the device to work as it should.  Its not worth going with pre-built gaming rigs, because if this happens, you end up having to return the whole thing (or at the very least, the faulty component if you are able to figure out what it is) and then jump through hoops and waste more time waiting for it to get fixed.  Find a nerd, give him a six pack and some pizza and have him build you one, its cheaper in the long run.  Also, the computer runs fine now, but that should have been the case right out of the box, not after hours of troubleshooting and spending another 100 bucks.  Two thumbs down for Avatar.

title: Accurate and Easy
text:
I bought this after losing my second Bushnell Neo Ghost. The Phantom is basically the same thing but with a built-in magnet. I’ve used it to golf so for about seven or eight times and it works great. I’ve read complaints about the magnet not being strong enough, but it has worked fine for me. Unless you bump it or knock it off, it stays on through a whole round. Even over rough ground. Bushnell could certainly make it stronger, but I haven’t had a problem with it.

The accuracy is great. I have compared it with other people who are wearing a GPS watch or holding a monocular style GPS rangefinder. It’s always within about 1 yard of everyone else’s. The Phantom also loads much faster than the Ghost did. Usually within 30 seconds it will load a course where the Ghost would take a minute or two or three.

I have used the shot calculator as well to see how far I hit a shot and that is handy. The only thing this doesn’t do that I can tell is tell you how far it is to a hazard. In those cases a monocular would be better. But otherwise, I love using the Phantom. It’s it’s right there on the front bar of the cart and is easily viewable to both golfers.

Battery life is good. I do charge it between every round and it never dies. Once or twice I have forgotten to charge it and it has lasted a second round as well. But I wouldn’t push it past that.

This is my third Bushnell range finder and I love it! Would highly recommend it. And it’s definitely worth it to get the Phantom instead of the Ghost. The ghost is hard to see down in a cup holder and otherwise you have to clip it to your belt or hold it. The Phantom with the magnet is perfect!

title: OBNOXIOUS controls
text:
We were looking for a boom box that didn't require a phone for our 10 year old. We thought this would fit the bill perfectly, but we were disappointed. Although it is convenient that we can load the songs onto an SD card and pop that into the speaker, the controls are so obnoxious that we will be returning it. The volume up/volume down, song forward/song backward, FF/RW buttons are all the same two buttons! You hold them down to turn up/down the volume, you touch them quickly to change song. And you have to press HARD (for a 10 year old) to get them to respond. Try changing songs or changing volume only by the pressure of your fingers while pushing VERY hard! It's such a pain! Whoever designed this thing has never tried to use it. They could have taken up 2 cm more and added the very most important buttons: volume.

Plus the thing always turns on at MAX volume, causing everyone to shriek and cover their ears until you can madly try to turn the volume down.

On the plus side, it's loud and has decent sound. It's also quite portable. If the controls were good, we would have kept it. But they're such a pain to use, we will look for something else. (Never got the remote working--it arrived damaged.)

title: Fantastic Car DVD players!
text:
We bought these DVD players to replace some old Panasonic ones that finally bit the dust, and these RCA's are superior to those in almost every single way! ("Almost" because the old ones were 9" and these have a 7" screen.)

The movies DO restart from wherever you were when you turned off the car, which is by far the most important feature in a car DVD player in my opinion. With all the previews and start-up screens in kids' movies, it can take up to 5 minutes to get a movie anywhere near where it was when you turned off the car. And if you're making multiple stops, it's just not worth it to start and stop it over and over again. It'll make you CRAZY! So if you're in the market for car DVD players, do yourself the favor of trusting me--you don't want a set that doesn't automatically revert to the last spot you watched.

Other features I like about these DVD players are the two movies/two remotes feature. I have a 2 year old and 7 and 8 year olds--they do not have the same taste in movies. So now I can put on something different for the toddler while the older kids watch something more their speed. Or, if it's something they all want to watch, a simple flip of a switch puts them both on the same movie.

Also, each screen has its own remote. So the bigger kids can handle starting and fast forwarding their own screen while I can control the baby's screen. The remotes are color coded, so they never get mixed up. (I attached a couple dots of velcro to the backs and to the sun visor so mine doesn't get lost).

The DVDs are good at playing semi-scratched disks. That's another thing I like. My old DVD players struggled with older/dirty/scuffed DVDs, but this one plays them fine. It also plays when the car is cold, which my old DVD player struggled with.

Overall, I'm VERY happy with this set of DVD players. My only complaints are that the screen isn't bigger, and that the velcro straps included for attaching them to the headrests are hokey. They need to be wrapped around and around and don't hold them on tight. It's not a very elegant way to attach them. It looks like something my 7 year old came up with! I wish they had straps with clickable clasps. (They would lose 1/2 a star for that if Amazon allowed it).

But other than that, I really really like them and wouldn't hesitate to recommend them.

title: As usual, reliable and steady
text:
My 3rd, maybe 4th Nighthawk in 12 years. Average about 4 years per, although one bit it due to my stupidity so...maybe better than 4.

This one is like all the others I've purchased. Installs easily, it simply used a backup from the old Nighthawk to set up. All my network names and passwords were set up, my static ips, just good to go after about 10 minutes with very little input from me. Even if that's not the case for you the app setup is easy and intuitive. If you don't have a smartphone or tablet (really?!) you can setup through your computer either wired or wireless.

Management is done through the app or the typical IP address on your computer. I've always been partial to using the browser but you get good basic controls from the app. You can't set static IP or fine tune settings but you'll manage your wireless networks well enough.

We have a lot of devices. A lot. Too many really. This handles them without issue. Several lights, TV's, game systems, raspberry pi, and smartphones/tablets. I haven't had drops or dips in signal.

I know some have had issues with Nighthawks, but for us they've always provided good or great coverage with good speed and good reliability. I recently tried a different brand and it fell far short of our needs. So baring some horrific issue we will be buying another in 4-6 years.

title: Not a good router.
text:
I had intially thought this was going to be a good replacement for our Nighthawk. Well less than a week and I'm back on it.

This router set up easy, was easy to make changes and seemed to work well for a bit. Then it started dropping the signal. We have a small apartment so coverage wasn't an issue. I tried to give this a chance but it just kept dropping signal. All the other bells and whistles don't matter if it isn't reliable.

So yeah, sent it back. I know enough about tech support to know I don't want to mess with it when I can just return it to Amazon and go back to Netgear.

title: Cuts on, cuts off.
text: Really not a lot to say. Plug one end with the power cable, the other into your pi, push button. I would assume these would work with other products as well. I mean, it's a power switch.

title: Fairly nice pre-made case
text:
I'm pretty happy with this case all in all. The only nitpicking thing I can complain about it lack of SD card access but that's just a once in awhile thing. I'll live.

Since there seems to be a few confused, this is a case. Nothing more. Reading the questions asked about this product makes me lose some faith in humanity. I'd love to live in a world where a screen and case cost this little. Oh, and yes you will most likely have to rotate the screen. Not difficult to do and not a flaw in the case. I mean, I guess you could say it's a flaw but how hard is it to type lcd_rotate=2 in a config file?

Buy the screen and mount the pi to it. Then 4 screws gets the pi mounted to the case. Without the back cover there's a decent amount of room for hats, although you may have to clip off the tabs for the cover. I had to do this to make room for an Ice Tower, not a big deal as I never intended to use the cover. This also leaves plenty of room for the camera cable to be routed should you need.

It stays put but for my application the mount angle is a little too shallow. Not a fault of the case as it's mounted only about 2 and a half feet from floor level.

Overall, not bad. I could have printed one but sometimes it's just easier to purchase something. Using for an Octoprint set up near my printer and it's been doing fine.

title: Do not buy if you intend to use a raspberry pi cam
text:
Well, wanted to like it. Looks good and I needed lower profile in my case. I have the Ice Tower and it keeps the Pi very cool, why wouldn't this one work?

Well, I'll tell you why. the bracket that mounts the heatsink to the Pi has the tiniest cut out to go around the camera socket. Except it doesn't. I installed this thing carefully to make sure nothing was touching. I then installed my cam ribbon cable and noticed the bracket was resting right on/against the black clip. I tried to push down on the clip but nope, won't latch now. The bracket had bent, or stressed that small piece of plastic and it won't engage. Thinking I had screwed it up I took it off and carefully looked to see that the cutout was not....well cut out correctly.

No matter how you position it, the bracket will hit that clip just enough to prevent it locking, and to some degree rub against the ribbon cable.

Maybe I got a dud, one that just was manufactured wrong. Somehow I doubt it and had I even known it was a possiblity I wouldn't have purchased this thing. Now I either have to purchase a replacement socket, or shove a piece of plastic into it to keep the cable attached. Beyond irritated.

title: Worked well until it didn't.
text:

After unplugging it to move some things around the camera would not reconnect, or set up again. It just kept "looking" down and then up no matter the troubleshooting steps I tried. Returned it and went with another suitable option.

title: Not worth $10
text:
First, mine didn’t smell.

Now that I have the positive attributes out of the way let’s discuss why you should avoid this case.
I reluctantly paid $33 for this and I have to wonder what I was thinking. It’s nowhere near worth that much.

It will not/cannot survive a side impact. Well that’s not true. It cannot protect your APM from a hit or drop that could damage them from the top. I’m not sure if it could from the bottom or sides. It’s either molded cardboard or thin plastic covered with fabric. No padding, just fabric.

Internally there is another layer of cardboard (or plastic, thin, very thin) covered in a felt like material. There’s absolutely no drop protection.

The magnets designed to put the APM into “sleep” mode lay flat. You will have to pinch them up while putting your headphones into it if you wish to keep them from clanging together and not using the stock case. Even then the magnets don’t work every time. See my pic.

Overall this is a $10 case marked up cause they can. I mean we have expensive headphones so why not charge us more? We have already proven we will pay.

Skip this thing. Mine is going back. If you want something to protect them in a backpack then still look elsewhere. You can get something equal to this for less.

Thanks for your time.

title: Very happy with these
text:
Initially I purchased these as refurbs, sadly that didn't work out so well. However I liked them so much that I purchased new after Amazon took care of me.

If you're looking for audiophile sound, look elsewhere. If you're looking for good quality sound, easy pairing, and comfort than I've found these to be a perfect choice. I wear them for about 2-3 hours at a time at work, never feel fatigued by them. I find they stay in with little effort and range is good, as I often walk away from my desk. My wife uses hers at work as well but only with 1 bud at a time. She agrees the quality is better than the airpods she has as well.

Like I said, if you're interested in audiophile quality sound, then you'll need to look at other choices. I've found that these seal well an keep most ambient noise out, although there is a setting that allows a touch to let more in. Touch controls weren't the best at first but updates have pretty much got them spot on. Only occasionally do I have it register a single tap instead of a double.

Somewhat durable, I've dropped mine once or twice with no issues.

Overall a good choice.

title: Solid choice, very nice watch.
text:
I've owned a total of 5 watches between Android and Apple. I've had pros and cons with them all. The biggest issue has been battery life by far.

So I ordered this to replace an LG Watch Style and so far have been pretty impressed as well as happy.

Battery life is so much better. With my usual settings I am ending my days (6am-8pm) with around 70% battery left. WiFi off, NFC off, and Always on off, everything else on works well for me. Your mileage may vary, but after intial "new toy" time you will see great battery life.

It's large, no doubt. I'm not a big guy and this looks huge to me. Feels like it's well built and the band is comfortable. Most 22mm bands will fit without issue. Only wish there had been a choice for the OEM black and orange band.

The older Qualcomm chipset works well enough. I like Wear OS well enough but it has it's shortcomings. Sometimes the watch lags a little, never enough to get frustrating unless you're impatient.

Would have liked a different charger, one that stands up. There are some up though.

Overall very solid at $250. 2 days after I got mine it went on sale for $200, but I don't feel cheated. Worth the money.

title: Best Christmas gift for Grandparent!
text: We bought this as a Christmas gift for my grandmother who lives in a nursing home.  She loves it!  With space so limited, the ability to hold an endless slideshow of pictures in a small space is a huge bonus.  It was easy to load even for my techically challenged mother, and now they are downloading pictures from extended family from Atlanta to Tampa to Texas.  My Grandmother can see the screen clearly and hold it in her lap, and the ability to view a slideshow without turning the pages of an album is a plus for her limited mobility.  This gift worked exactly as described, expected, with no difficulties, and filled a need like nothing else.  I can think of a hundred people I would give this to when the price comes down, including myself!

title: A nice, simple device for older adults
text:
UPDATE: I was wrong about its longevity. It lasted barely a month and is now kaput. A big waste of money.

Although this is intended for toddlers, I actually bought it for my age 90+ father. The sound is quite good, although if he were hard of hearing I'd be concerned that the top volume is too low. It just has 3 buttons (on/off, ff, and rewind), so it's easy for him to operate. Any one of the buttons will turn it on. Also has a nice rubbery cover, which makes it seem like it would be up to being dropped occasionally. Definitely recommend for someone older who would find a regular MP3 or other music device overly complicated. Because it's intended for toddlers, it does require a screwdriver for battery replacement. So far, so good!

title: Very happy with this purchase!

Works for me! I've only had this for a day, so I can't speak to its longevity, but the sound is fantastic. I've been playing classical music as I work (recommend Songza), which has been really nice. When my daughter asked me to play a movie trailer for her, my husband and son both came into my office because it sounded so much like we were in a movie theater. Really great sound. I also love the little, round remote that comes with it. I keep it on my desk, in front of my monitor, and just have to move the top a bit to the left to lower the volume or silence it completely. SO much easier than having to deal with the sound icon on the computer. Highly recommended.

I took it on a trip with me to Europe; it packs well and fits into all of my laptop carriers (backpack, briefcase, satchel), the laptop itself is extremely light, as a standalone gaming rig - does it all. The performance is on par with my home desktop (2070 Super, Ryzen 3700). The FPS and refresh don't usually go above 120, but that seems to be more of a game setting. It does get hot but doesn't overheat, a cooling mat was recommended and paid off. It's relatively quiet (the cooling mat is louder). The speakers are great, and I am impressed by the Lenovo software. It did come with Windows 11, and it isn't one 2TB SSD, but two 1TB SSDs. Not really complaining, just an observation. Overall 10/10 would buy again - wish I bought it first before spending on an MSI that broke the hinges the first time I used it...

text:
BUY ONE! This has been my best non-laptop purchase of 2017, hands down.

"Alexa, what's the weather today?"
"Alexa, wake me up at seven thirty am."
"Alexa, remind me to check the laundry in an hour."
"Alexa, play classical music."
"Alexa, play red hot chili peppers."
"Alexa, volume 7."
"Alexa, how many days until Christmas?"
"Alexa, thank you."
"Alexa, tell me a joke."

I speak to Alexa 5-6 times a day on average, create new shopping lists, set reminders, and ... just practically anything and everything. And I can do all of this while I'm in my closet picking out clothes, sorting and folding my laundry, watching TV, in the shower, etc.

text:
I knew the value of this device before I bought it. It has multiple network modes, it's excellent for a mesh net. The firmware is a solid tiny Linux (OpenWRT, 10-20MB depending on configuration) with dynamic Python and precompiled C support. No Bluetooth (but I absolutely hate BT / BLE).

At the end of the day, at work, we prototyped with this chip and decided to use it (actually, the duo - "Arduino" support was invaluable with serial communication support). This is a really solid chip if my description applies.

title: The clear plastic over the metal is fine, the straps are all good
text:
I bought this in August of 2012. I have used it almost daily for college, travel, and excursions. Hiking, sports, thrown into the back of my car and buried under a bunch of junk for a weekend, crashed on my bicycle with it on my back. And you want to know how it's held up? The only thing that's failed on it is the black plastic covering over the main strap on top. The clear plastic over the metal is fine, the straps are all good, it's literally a cosmetic issue.

For someone who used to go through 2-3 backpacks a year with how rough I am on them, this thing has been a godsend. Now, how functional is it? I've dropped this backpack with a laptop in it about three times since August 2012, and it's been hit a few times as well with a laptop in it. The thing absorbs force like nothing else, it's amazing. The bottom is waterproof as well, so I really don't even pay attention to where I throw it or where it goes (and I've literally set it in a very shallow puddle before with a laptop in it - as you may tell by now, I'm a guy that's prone to stupidity and needs something like this - and it's amazing). Oh, and I've loaded this thing, backed it as fully as you can possibly imagine; the reinforced straps are no joke.

So far as comfort, the extra padding on the straps and on the lower back area are sooo nice.

Yeah, I hate spending ~$80+ on a backpack, but this thing is worth every penny. I expect to get at least another 2-3 years out of it before I buy a replacement; for an average person, I'd expect this backpack to last a lifetime.

I bought a Belkin cable at an Apple store several years ago, and it still works! I have purchased some less expensive (non Apple or Belkin brand) lightning cables, and they have all stopped charging my iPhone or iPad. Never again. The colors were pretty, but it's like the old saying, "Beauty is only skin deep".
The only challenge I have with my Belkin cables is remember which way to coil it up to keep it out of the way. I think, if you hold it in your left hand, the coil needs to go in a clockwise direction with new coils on top of the previous coils. I hope this makes sense and helps.

title: These are the poorest charging cables I have ever had
text:

I missed the return window date by trying to figure out if I could make them work.
You can have them for free.
I finally realized I needed to ignore my budget, and purchase Apple brand lightening charging difference—and what a difference! Plug them in a listen for the “ding” tone to let you know they connected. Immediate auditory feedback, unlike these cables which might or might not “ding,” even after I made certain I had inserted the cord directly.

I was in the middle of an online meeting, and was not pleased when my iPad and then my iPhone shut down, even though I had charged them in advance and kept them connected to power during the meeting.. It was humiliating.

title: Very cool ties, colorful, effective!
text:
These rubberized ties are nice to use, particularly for coiling smallish cables and holding them tight.
These ties have helped me to clean up/organize wires across the house. I need probably another 20 at least!
The shorties are really pretty short, and are harder to use. The tip of one of the short ones came off when I was twisting the tie, but I was eventually to push it back on and use it with that particular cable. I might be kind of stubborn, but I did not want to waste it, nor did I want the wires inside of it to be protruding all the time (about 1/16th of an inch).

These are NOT intended to be used around young children with an eye to dismantling your audio visual equipment. You may have met one of those children. If one resides with you or visits often, I would try to enclose the cables in a box, with a hole in and out, so the child could not wreak havoc with the cables. I trust we have all encountered inquisitive children. However, this is not a child-proof twist tie. Just a word for the worried parents and other caretakers among us all.

title: These are the best computer and monitor stands I have ever used
text:

Additionally, the clear glass makes it possible to see things that may have slid under the computer or monitor, and to help you see what you are doing when you plug your computer in to a power source. The glass does not detract from any color scheme you may have; it just sort of disappears from one's awareness except for remembering its great functionality! I have post-its and other small office supplies on the glass that holds my computer, so I can slide the keyboard underneath when I am not working on the computer. I use the other stand for an oversize monitor, and can keep desk items both on the glass stand and underneath it as well.

These stands have really helped me to maximize my work surface. They are so useful and the best desk accessory I have purchased in a long time. I have used several types before these, and these are far better because they are very sturdy and they are clear.

title: Aftermarket HUD's have come a long way since the first models
text:
I've have quite a few aftermarket heads up display devices in the past and I'm pretty happy with this device. The walls on the sides of the display do an excellent job of keeping the sun off the screen providing a good picture. This is something that all of my previous devices had a major draw back on. The price is great as well as this is one of the cheaper HUD devices that I've owned. I do not agree with the other posts saying that the instructions were non-existant as I found them very easy to follow and 1 page was more than enough to explain how to use the product. It does have a few downfalls. I will lay out the pro's and the cons below:

Pro's:
- walls on the side of the HUD make visibility even in sunlight
- cheap price
- tons of functionality
- Pretty accurate after "tweaking"
- Customizable

Con's:
- it's auto-brightness needs some updates as around dusk it will get super bright then dim and go back and forth which can be distracting
- the clock function is military only
- it has a proprietary plug (most have a micro-usb plug that goes into the OBDII port)
- Where the plug is located makes it hard to place on the dash
- the double sided tape is useless, (buy some 3m tape when ordering)

All in all, I really like it, just make sure to have a "window tint install kit" in order to install the film. You want to have that installed as smoothly as possible. The trick that I found for the best install is, power up the HUD, and put a piece of tape on your windshield at the top if the display so you know where you need to get your film installed at. Then turn everything off and place a towel over your dash. soak the area where your film will be installed. place the film on the windshield and then squeegee out all the liquid and bubbles. This will take some time, but it's super important to do it right. This will be the difference between having a good HUD install and a crappy one that you will not be happy with.

title: It packs a lot of features for a good price. The new 6th gen i5 is a ...
text:
I received my ZenBook a little more than a week ago now. After a week of using it, I will say it's a zippy machine. It packs a lot of features for a good price.The new 6th gen i5 is a powerful processor and great for low power consumption...

The Pros:

- Small laptop
- Fast
- Great battery life
- packed with features
- Great picture
- Low Price for what you get

The Cons:

- Heavier than I thought it would be
- Low powered video
- High gloss on the screen making it impossible to see in normal to high light situations
- Multi-touch gestures seem to be hit or miss if they work or not
- Under powered for gaming (even if you are just streaming games across the network to it (xbox streaming))
- Touch Screen + high gloss screen = tons of finger prints that are visible on the screen

Overall I like the device, but I am battling with keeping it. Not because the hardware isn't good, but because it doesn't seem like a machine that I would want to use every day to replace my 13.3 Macbook pro Retina. The refinement isn't quite there like it is in the Mac world; hardware or software wise. Gestures seem iffy at best and Windows 10 seems to operate "clunky" For someone who wants a reasonably priced ultrabook running windows 10, this could be your machine.

For the record, I experienced none of the issues that was posted about poor image quality or hinge issues... everything works and looks as to be expected.

text: Should of paid more attention to reviews I found on the web. Supposed to work wired with existing inside door chime. I mean remove the camera, take out batteries, a start all over from out of the box reset to include the sync module. And speaking of removing it from Mount. What a cheap terrible set up for mounting. If it goes through batteries like many reviews claim it does there is no way that cheap Mount will last with that cheap plastic catch and supplied cheap little paper clip looking tool to remove it. This thing can be stollen in a matter of seconds. I can’t believe Amazon doesn’t have a special set screw to secure it good like on the Ring and Nest as well as some others. Not sure what kind of engineers designed this thing, but Amazon needs to get rid of them and redesign this thing. Couldn’t cost much more for a more secure Mount, resolve the working with existing doorbell and work a bit on the software/firmware and App. Up the price $10 and make this a decent contender in this doorbell camera market. I’m afraid I’m going to have to return this or live with no inside doorbell notification. It doesn’t integrate very good with the Alexa App either. Very very delayed response time. I just can’t think of one positive thing to say about this unit I’m sorry to say and normally I like Amazons Tech Products, but this one is a Lemon all the way! By the way I’m not a no is in the tech industry. I come from a computer IT background, so networking is not the issue here, it’s poor engineering and design plain and simple. They got it on the market fast and are working out the bugs after the fact, but poor physical design is just poor engineering!

title: Great SSD for the Money
text: Appears to be a Great SSD for the money thus far. I cloned a 1TB Mechanical HDD to the SK hynix Gold S31 500GB SSD. I used the Free  AOMEI BackUp Standard Clone Software and in just a few steps it was going and took about 2-hours. Remember to disconnect from the Internet, disable any programs that may try to run while computer is idle like Malwarebytes, your Antivirus Software, Disable your screensaver, etc.. I hooked the New SSD up VIA USB externally, Cloned, then swapped it with the Mechanical Drive. Booted up right away with no issues what so ever and is a True Clone, nothing changed on my computer at all and checked Windows System for Windows 10 Activation and all was good. Did not have to re-enter the product key code as you here some have to do. It's only been two days but I am presently Happy and I have messed with and built computers for years being 61 years old. Keep in mind;  Hynix has been making Computer chips for years and is one of the largest Chip manufactures in the world, I used their OEM RAM for years and so did Dell/HP/Compac and others. My point is they are not New to this Industry, simply New to the SSD Market, but this is right up their alley and their first entry tests out toe to toe with the best of them in the SSD Market. Hope this helps out some of you. I will update should anything change.

title: I was surprised
text: I've installed and maintained antennae for myself and family over the years and have seen some rip off deals. I have been insistent on an outdoor yagi style antenna for years. Having moved recently I found a decent yagi online and was prepared to pay about 3 times the cost of this antenna. Then the wife found this one and I decided to give it a shot because it was cheap. I figured I'd end up giving it to someone at work and buying the yagi antenna I had picked. I sat it on a table and connected it to my Amazon recast and reception was a bit choppy. Then I put the amplifier in line and plugged it in. I pulled in every channel available crystal clear. No stutter or tiling in the picture for any channel. Our stations broadcast anywhere between 20 to 40 miles away. I currently have the antenna sitting on a window sill until The weekend comes and I can run the cable and mount it in the attic. Works great at 40 miles or less. Would love a chance to try it out at 70 miles away just out of curiosity but I'm not about to move again to try it!

title: Good for the price, just wish it had a backlight!
text:
I like this keyboard and I am happy with it for the price. It is comfortable to use, the wrist placement feels good for me. I type all day at work and this keyboard is much better on my upper back than my laptop. The wireless functions have worked well and the mouse is responsive. But there are a few tweaks I would make if I were the product designer, or maybe an upgraded model:

-It's loud. The click clicking of every key is annoying when you listen to it all day and it would be a lot of background noise in something like telemarketing/cubicle environments. The noise is awkward when I am trying to take notes on a conference call.
-The keys have a bit more resistance than I am used to. I wish they were a little more recessed into the keyboard and quieter (like the buttons on most newer laptops)

-It really needs a background light, with dim and bright settings. I work into the evenings and my keyboard is in the ergonomic drawer of my desk. It's perfectly placed for long work hours, but then I tend to go back to laptop so I can see the keys while I work. This is particularly useful when using the 10-key and F functions, as well as the sound controls at the top.
-Similarly, I wish there was a light on the CAPS lock so I can see when I have accidentally pressed it. I find myself defaulting to my laptop for this as well.

title: Good sound quality, great customer service!

The sound quality is better than expected and it has a few different input/output options (auxiliary, RCA) . It never turns off and has a blue light on top so you can easily see when it's in pairing mode. I haven't tested the distance on it because I have an open floorplan and all of my devices are within 15 ft of the Esinkin. The first one of these that I ordered came in as a dud, no light, no pairing with any device. I contacted the seller and they responded quickly, asked for my address and sent me a new one right away. Customer service was awesome and I'm glad I got the new one because I love it!

It also means you're stuck with bass if your roommates want to sleep which has cut down my music listening time quite a bit. The remote control is handy but only has on/off and volume features which is disappointing because I thought the ability to change bass and trebel would be there as well. Last but not least, I hate the way the remote is attached to the speakers. It has a Y shaped cord so it constantly gets wrapped up in my mouse cord or power cord to my lap top. It is a fairly inflexible cord so it is constantly in the way. The sound is quality and I like Logitech speakers but I would definitely recommend ordering the version with the ability to control the subwoofer independently.

title: WRONG FORMAT
text: Buyers should note that this drive is formatted in exFAT. Without knowing this, I plugged it in to a running computer and began to transfer some files. The computer was shut down for the night. The next morning, I found that the computer refused to boot up with the new drive installed. Unplugged the drive, and the computer booted up fine. Finally checked the file system. Found it to be exFAT. Moved the files off and re-formatted the drive to NTFS and the problem went away. I suggest anyone purchasing this unit just save yourself the time and trouble and reformat it right out of the box. The software on the drive isn't needed anyway. I have several Western Digital external drives and this is the first one that arrived in a format other than NTFS.

title: Not worth the trouble
text: Worked less than a year. I began having all manner of boot issues and connectivity problems. And BSOD when waking from sleep every time. I went through everything in the case with a fine tooth comb never thinking that a simple USB device could cause such major issues. Finally just unplugged everything from the board except the RAM sticks and started reinstalling until the problem showed up. This device was the cause of it all. Some malfunction in it caused the computer to randomly not connect or disconnect from the internet. And it affected both the wired and wireless adapters. It caused the computer to go into BSOD every time when waking from sleep. And actually caused major boot issues. It was causing the BIOS to ignore the designated boot device. Once removed from the system, everything went back to normal.

title: I would recommend it, but be aware of the time it ...
text: Bought this to go with a TP Link T8E wireless card in a new build. Set up the router according to the instructions. Did everything in order. Router would not recognize IPV6 connectivity. Went to the download site and followed the instructions for setting up IPV6 with Comcast. Nothing. Still no IPV6 recognition. Noticed two firmware upgrades available. Downloaded both. Installing them was a nightmare. The factory website only shows the progression of the download to the router. Then you sit and wait while staring at a screen that says, effectively, wait for reboot. The reboot never comes. I waited over 30 minutes for the reboot on the first update, finally just ended the connection. Did the second update the same way. Waited for the 100% on the site and ended the connection. No reboot was ever shown or witnessed on the router itself. But it finally recognized IPV6. After that was over, I checked the wired and wireless speed. With some minor tweaking of the antennae on the T8E, it shows the full 1.3GB connection. The wired speed is hovering around 214Mbps. Far faster than anything that preceded it, on any of my computers. I would recommend it, but be aware of the time it will take to set it up. My setup time was well over two hours. 4 stars because of the time it took to get it sorted out.

title: It’s like the Mary Poppins carpet bag!!!
text:
The very first thing I thought about this when I took it out of the box was that it was way too small. I wanted the larger one, they were not available. But, I’m leaving on a 5 day work trip so I started packing it, resigning myself to still having to take a suitcase.
I WAS WRONG!
This thing is not only stylish and seems very durable, it’s like Mary Poppins carpet bag! It just goes on forever!
I packed 4 pairs of jeans, a hoodie, 4 shirts, undergarments for each day, socks, make up, meds, flat iron for my hair, my I pad(in the secure and padded pocket), phone and chargers, wallet, snacks, pens, my 48 Oz hydro flask in the large side pocket, two charging banks and an extra pair of shoes and I STILL HAVE ROOM!
It’s absolutely ridiculous!
It distributes the weight evenly, the shoulder straps aren’t too small and they are padded, the top opens so wide that I didn’t have to fight with it at all! I love the back pocket to keep my phone/passport, etc. safe and the attached power cord is a huge plus! I, happily, will not be taking a suitcase on this trip! In the future l, when I do, the strap to attached it to the handle will be perfect!

For the price, this was an excellent purchase! Looks more expensive than it was and functions above and beyond what I expected!

title: Simple machine that does nothing
text:
I have spent several hours trying to get this thing to print, mostly repeating the simple instructions over and over and getting the following result every time: I pull up a document to print, I click to print, the printer (which is set as the default, I don't have any others) shows up as "Idle". Then when I click to print, the printer's panel and icon in the dock both up for a half a second, with a number 1 in a circle--just like it's going to print--and then the icon in the dock immediately disappears, and the start button on the printer starts blinking, and nothing prints. Re-started my computer and the printer twice, deleted and re-added the printer twice, etc etc.
If you are so starved for activity that you would enjoy doing this for a good while, by all means buy this printer. But is there a reason why HP can't make a simple printer like this that actually works when you follow the instructions for setting it up? It should not require downloading HP Smart to troubleshoot a thing like this. It should be: plug it in, connect to computer via USB, follow instructions, and print something. It's 20th century technology.

My house is 2400 sq. ft. and the router is upstairs. We pay for high speeds from our ISP but the signal downstairs where we have our big screen TV was weak... so weak that streaming videos was becoming a huge problem. I used a Netgear Nighthawk router with an expensive extender downstairs for the past 4 yrs. It did the trick until recently. The extender just wouldn't do the job downstairs no matter what I did. Additionally, the signal was extremely weak in the front of the house regardless of the extender.

Anyway, I decided to do some research. Thought I'd get a new extender but soon realized that would be like putting a bandaid on an existing problem. So, I asked around and was told to try a mesh system. Reviews for the Orbi are the best PLUS I'm used to Netgear and have had success with the brand in the past. I replaced the Netgear Nighthawk router with the Orbi router rather than using the new Orbi as an access remote. Set up the Orbi extender downstairs. It gave me a few issues in setup initially because I forgot to set up the desktop pc upstairs as "wireless" rather than with the ethernet cable. It finally dawned on me and then everything was okay. I had to reset EVERYTHING with the new wifi connection (cell phones, smart devices, Alexa, Smart TV, Firesticks, etc., etc.). You don't realize how many connections you have until you have to reset everything! LOL! One of the other things that I didn't realize until after I set up the Orbi is that it doesn't differentiate between bands. It just decides automatically which is the best one for your setup. One of the nice surprises is that the Orbi setup works with the Netgear Genie that I had on our upstairs desktop pc... it's a great tool to control the router, change channels, determine traffic, etc. I didn't have to do a thing because it just synched perfectly on its own!

The end result is that we have had ZERO issues with connectivity or signal since installing the Orbi. We now get speeds in excess of 200mbps throughout the house rather than as low as 20mbps downstairs. Of course, the speed is determined by your ISP plan but the signal throughout your property is determined by your equipment of choice. We are so happy with the Orbi and highly recommend it!

title: Good product concept, 4/5 stars on execution.
text:
(Review updated 90 days after purchase, my opinions have improved somewhat, and i will correct a couple errors in my review, and add more content to my review refining my critiques and adding some new observations -jeff)

I really wanted to love this receiver, but the quality control and attention to product usability detail are not what I have come to expect (I'm spoiled by Apple attention to usability, no doubt)..

Let's start with the iControlAV2 iPad app, since that is a major reason why people want this receiver. The functions to setup the audio (eq etc) are nice, but you basically use them once. After that, your main use of the app will be changing volume and input, for zone 1 and zone 2 (if you enable zone two like I have).

Here are the major problems with this app control:

1 The receiver's wired ethernet port will power off with the receiver, and when it powers back on, it doesn't request to renew the same IP address it had before (even if 'before' was 5 seconds ago). This typically results in the receiver getting a different IP address, and the iControl app then giving you an error when you try to control your receiver on next launch. You have to then go back into the iControl settings and 'select your product'. Very annoying, and completely breaks the 'wife+kids friendly' possibilities of using app, completely. UPDATE: You can configure the receiver to make the receiver stay in 'standby' mode so you can turn it back on from the remote. I'll admit I simply missed this option in my earlier setup.

2 The iControl App lets you turn off both zones of the receiver, but if you do, you end up powering off the receiver and guess what? You can't turn it on again unless you physically push the power button on the front of the receiver.. which then gives you problem #1 again. UPDATE: This is rectified by enabling Standby mode in the network settings.

3 While 99% of customers are likely going to use this as an AirPlay device, confusingly AirPlay isn't mentioned anywhere in the user interface or on the Ipad application. You have to select 'H.M.G.' (Home Media Gateway), which then enables airplay. Works fine, but the other 90% of the HMG functionality is useless to me, and simply confuses the user interface. You can control song play / pause / next / last from the iControl App (effectively remote controlling iTunes), but this control is nowhere near the control you get with Apple's Remote app, which you will almost certainly want to use instead of the iControl app.

4 No iPhone / iPod touch version of the app. Pretty dumb, again considering the main use case of the app after the novelty of everything other than input control and volume wear off. UPDATE: There is now!

Problems with the receiver UI:
1) The receiver itself has a decent UI, but to configure many things you will need to have a TV display connected. The menus for this on-screen display look like bad shareware from 1992, but are functional enough. It seems crazy to me however, that a product with built in ethernet / IP networking wouldn't have a simple built in web server to allow configuration of inputs etc (everything the O.S.D. does) from your computer, or better yet your iPad. Navigating the On Screen Display to configure inputs and such is tedious and slow; this should have been completely configurable from my computer / iPad.

2) Zone 2 and 7.1 surround are mutually exclusive. While I knew this when I bought it, there is no reason why Pioneer couldn't have made a simple toggle to turn on zone two and automatically disable two of the surround speakers (which almost certainly wouldn't be used during zone 2 'music' listening anyway'. Perhaps nit-picking here, but an intelligent usability feature went completely overlooked here by a product team that clearly sought no customer input on this capability. UPDATE: OK, I figured out why there is no toggle! You have to wire the speakers completely differently if you want to enable zone two. So if you wire up 7.1 speakers, and want to have another pair of speakers off in another location (I have a pair over my desk), then your only option is to wire the remote speaker pair to what ends up being the 'Speaker B' outputs. These speakers get the same output as the main front R+L speakers, and you can toggle between A+B, A, B, or Both Off (which is pointless, in my opinion). Annoyingly, you cannot toggle the Speaker A/B/A+B/Off setting from the iControl AV2 iPhone/iPad application, which is a shame since this is simply a soft button control on the front of the receiver. This effectively makes the Speaker B -> Remote speakers option useless for me, since I would have to physically walk to where the receiver is from my office (different room). It still seems like Pioneer could have engineered this thing to allow 'soft switching' between 7.1 and 5.1 + Zone 2 settings from the iControlAV2 remote application, this would have provided maximum flexibility. As it is, if you plan on connecting 7.1 speaker setup, the Zone 2 features are completely unusable to you.

Miscellaneous minor complains:
1 No S-Video inputs or coax digital inputs.
2 No native zone-2 via my Harmony 890 (presumably not Pioneer's fault, but if I were the PM for this product I would make an effort to get prolific up to date support for all features in popular 3rd party products).
3) Only 1 subwoofer out (would be nice for a 2nd output for zone 2).
4) No AirPlay Video support. This means I have to add an AppleTV2 to one of the HDMI inputs on the Pioneer.. which means that the built-in AirPlay audio support in the Pioneer now serves no (unique) purpose and would be redundant.

Lastly, I had to return (to Amazon) the first VSX-1021 I was sent; after operating for a few hours, the HMG / network control functions would stop working, and would require a power cycle to rectify. A (lengthy) call to Pioneer tech support led to further frustration, as they wouldn't simply cross ship me a replacement, despite the unit being less than a month old. Their answer is to 'bring it to a Pioneer service center'. Oh yeah? And that service center is going to have a wireless network, ethernet switch, Apple iPad etc etc to duplicate my problem? Seemed fantastically unlikely. Fortunately Amazon picked up Pioneer's poor technical support slack and sent me an New In Box advanced replacement (I had already discarded my shipping box.. thanks Amazon!)

To be fair, i'm only picking on the things I don't like. The sound quality is quite good, and certainly that's incredibly important. All in all though, my main reason for buying this was multi-zone and AirPlay support. In hind-sight, I might just have bought something else and added a $100 AppleTV2 via Toslink digital out and saved myself the trouble (and had AirPlay video support).

3 Stars for now (UPDATE: making it 4) many of my complains could be addressed by a firmware update of the unit and updated iPad (and hopefully iPhone / iPod Touch apps).

After 3 months of use, I do like the Pioneer unit. However since I did expect to be able to use the Zone 2 features, i'm now in a quandary.. do I buy another VSX-1021 (or VSX-1121) to power the speakers above and behind my desk? I want Airplay for those too).

title: Amazing quality, amazing price! Comes with screen!
text:
I've had this particular projector for about 3 months now, and I have to say, I love it. It comes with everything you need to connect it to your hardware (HDMI, rca cables) plus it connects via Bluetooth to your phone tablet to stream video as well!

I took it down off the mounting screw and snapped some pics of it. It's tinier than I thought it would be, but the picture quality is awesome. Tested it with a ps4 and my 360 and it worked like a champ. It's not a 4k projector, but generally you wouldn't want to use a projector for something that detailed anyway. Great for gaming. Only tip is DON'T LOSE THE LENS CAP. Mine stays on until I go to use it, then it's set aside and popped back on later. Saves you problems with dust.

As mentioned, IT COMES WITH A SCREEN! That was an amazing surprise, especially since I had bought a twin sized bedsheet to use as a quick and dirty screen when my main one was down. Beautiful material.

So far, the only downside is the remote. It functions perfectly, but it's not what I had expected at all. It's like a fire remote or a Roku in size, but instead of pushing off the bottom to pop batteries in, you have an indention on the lower side, and just pull upwards/outwards until it pops off. Use a small item like a dime for this. That way you won't accidentally break a nail.

Final review is if you are looking for a great projector at an amazing price, then you have found it. Works with everything I threw at it, and the picture quality is great. Throw in the included cables and the screen, and it's a bargain.

title: It's a good phone, not great, but good.
text:
Picked this up on the gold box deal. Moved from my 25$ a month plan on my LG Optimus V to this one.

In hindsight, while I am not entirely happy with the phone, it is a step up and I kind of don't regret losing the cheaper plan I was grandfathered in on.

Pros!
Battery life is pretty nice.
Screen is bright, looks great.
TONS of room to install apps. As I mentioned above, my old phone was an LG Optimus and had a whopping 200~ megs to install them.
Beats Audio is actually pretty nice.

Cons!
Worst wifi I have ever used in my life. My touchpad, android tablet, old LG phone, etc all got 2-3 signal bars out of 3 while in my house. I barely even get the first little dot indicator on this one.
Not exactly a thorough instruction manual (moving from 2.2 to 4.0 is fairly different).
Phones shape is just, odd to me. It's not flat, and that little bar at the bottom pokes out strangely to me. That being said, I didn't take off any stars from the review for design issues. If it works, it works.
Cell camera is kinda "bleh" but then again all of em are. BRIGHT LED flash lights up the subjects but also washes out the photos.
Worse/slower data than my old LG on the same network.

Basically, as I mentioned before, while I don't entirely regret losing my 25$ monthly plan and moving off my old LG, paying 10$ a month more for literally the same thing stings a bit when I don't like the reason I moved that much. It's a great phone, but there are some fairly strong cons to me about it, the major one being the weak wifi signal.

Still, it cost me 50$ on the gold box deal, so if you can find it for around 50-60 and are upgrading from an older phone model, it's probably worth it. I would not, however, pay MSRP for this thing or anywhere near it.

Virgin Mobile does have some awesome reps though, and when I called in to transfer my phone (mid month, and I wanted to see if I could keep my old month or if I had to start a new one), they peeked at the call record and saw I had only used ~20 minutes. Had me swapped out and going in about 5 minutes and the phone was working for texts in about 10 mins.

4 stars for virgin mobile, 3 for the phone. If the buggy wifi gets fixed soon, then it'd be a 4 to 5 star phone. That slower data than my older device is really what kills the review for me.
