title: HD..Not 4K. CAN'T TELL THE DIFFERENCE
text: I got the newest 4K streaming stick with alexa voice control remote. As of yet i haven't purchased a 4K T.V. but the firestick works on any high def T.V. with a hdmi port. There are lots of free movie and T.V. apps so you can cut the cord and save lots of $$ doing away with cable. You will just have to simply connect a OTA antenna to the back of your TV to receive your local channels. The remote is ok but not great. It does sync easily with your T.V.s CEC control and lets you use the remote for T.V. power on and off. Volume control and alexa voice command. But personally i found it just as quick and easy to manually navigate the apps you want to watch rather than using the button on the remote to ask for a certain app. More times than not the voice control will get what your asking it wrong. But the volume control and power control on the remote is a very good plus over the basic remote. The battery compartment for remote is a little tricky to get opened at first but if you just apply a slight pressure at the same time as sliding the compartment down jt will slide right open. And getting to the streaming quality it will depend on which app you are using. Surprising to me is that the Amazon Prime Video app uses a lot more wifi data than most of the other apps making the shows and movies buffer quite a bit sometimes. I am curious why Amazon Prime uses so much more data vs Netflix or Hulu for example but it surely does. And if you have a Roku device and are used to the Rokus functions it will take a bit of getting used to how the Firestick apps are downloaded and stored compared to the Roku. But they both have equally good and bad comparisons when it comes to their individual functions. Both have excellent picture and sound. What i would really like is for Amazon's firestick to have a remote control app for your android or ios phone. Roku does have the free remote app to download and works great navigating and also has alexa voice control and tou can plug earphones into your phone for private listening. And also remember when buying a firestick to check the gift box if it is going to be used by someone else in their home. If you check the connect to my account box instead all of your information on your other firesticks will be on the new one and also the Amazon buying app with your personal information. So be vigilante and at least have a PIN set up on your Amazon account so no non approved purchases can be made.

title: Best activity tracker on the market - Updated 6/28/16
text:
I've been using it for almost 2 weeks now, I got lucky and got one really early. So far, I love it. Between weight training, elliptical running, biking (outdoor with ant+ sensors connected) and a huge amount of yard work, I am extremely impressed. Unlike previous wrist based trackers I've had, this one actually tracks movement when I cut the lawn or push a shopping cart. I use the GPS for yard work (turn on the walk activity), and it's really cool to see the movement map when I'm done.

For anyone thinking about this, keep in mind that this is an activity tracker with some smart watch functionality. If you're thinking about this or something along the lines of a Gear S2 or Apple Watch, you are comparing the wrong products. If you want something to count steps, go with a Jawbone or FitBit, no need to spend $250 for a pedometer. This also isn't small. My wrists aren't large, but it looks fine on me and the size isn't an issue. If you wear dress shirts a lot (with sleeves down and buttoned), you might have a bit of an issue. I had to wear a suit last week, and it was tough to get the shirt cuff over the watch. Doing that daily would be a problem for me.

The watch faces are good, fairly limited, but good. Actiface is my favorite, it shows time, steps, battery life, date, sunrise/sunset time, calories burned, distance moved, max steps and cal for the week and it also has a graph showing calories and steps over the last 7 days. Great face to see a bevy of stats at a glance.

This was money well spent for me, I'm very active and this can keep up with everything I do and then some. The apps are limited, but again, this isn't a smart watch, it's a smart tracker for more athletic types of people. I love it, it was worth the 2+ months of waiting. I debated getting the Fenix 3 HR, but I'm not at that level of outdoor activity, so this was a perfect choice for me. The fact that it can go in the shower/pool/ocean without turning into a dead device makes this a no brainer in the price range.

5/16/16 Update:
I found out yesterday that, on a long trip, it will count steps in my car. I didn't have that problem with my wife's car. My UP24 did the same thing, so as with that, I will just take it off in the car.

HR tracking while lifting weights is not perfect, it's basically flipped: When lifting, HR goes down because blood flow is restricted, when I drop the weight, it goes up when normal flow returns. As with all wrist based, it's not perfect. For really detailed HR tracking, a chest strap is the best approach. I'm ok with how this works, but I will be getting a chest strap to get a more exact measure for weight training.

I have seen complaints about the size. Get a tape measure and you can easily see how big it will be on your wrist. Negative reviews based on size make no sense to me, it's clear how big it is. Cut a piece of paper or something to the size stated to see how big it will be on your wrist. It's not small, but it's also not as big as the Fenix 3. GPS, HR, touch screen, battery, all of these things need space for components. If you want something small, you'll need to sacrifice features. It can't be much smaller and still make sense to have a touch screen.

After 3 weeks, I'm totally sold on this still.

Update 6/28: 2 months in, I only wish I had this a year ago when I swimming daily. It's not perfect, but it's as close as it comes compared to others I have used. Stair counting could be better, I go up and down at least a dozen times a day (including basement stairs, maybe 2 dozen) and I rarely hit the 10 flight goal, not sure if that's a software or hardware problem, but that's really the only issue I have with it.

I returned $20 replacements and $50 ear pad replacements. They were hard on my ears, not soft and made mud of the sound stage.

These cheap ones were the best of all three. Man, I wish they would promote themselves more. It took years to find and be happy with a Sennheiser 598SE replacement ear-pad. Still not as good as original, it does muddy the soundstage and introduce some more bass but very comfortable and sounds good enough, and I am picky.

title: WOW!WOW!WOW! 4k 30p UHD phone monitoring!!
text:
I bought this knowing it was only 1080p. But I just upgraded the latest firmware 1.3.6 (because it would not work with the old original firmware-no picture) and I was able to change my camera to shoot and record 4k 30P UHD video! New firmware update feature?? I can't tell if its passing 4k to the Benbox or 4k to my phone (or maybe my camera shoots in 4k and spits out 1080p hdmi??) or if its just displaying 1080p on my phone, but I can monitor 4k UHD as my Nikon P1000 records in 4k.

Maybe I don't understand, and maybe it could always do this, but I read into the details that my phones video view would go blank if I switched the camera to 4k. I read that somewhere. I thought, its on the interwebs, must be true! Its not.

tldr
I can record in 4K UHD on my Nikon P1000 while monitoring the video on my Galaxy S9+. Yay!

title: cheap and loses contact
text:
These, remarkably, are better than some others, but the contacts are soft and have no spring to make good contact so it often loses the signal and I have to play with the connection.

Too bad, as the over all build is great, but everything these days is a greedy scam. Manufactures are cheaping out anywhere they can for an extra cent or 2. Hence, the guts, the contacts on these are waaay tooo cheap.

One stopped working. I got a screwdriver out and pried the main contact up as far as I could to get some spring tension back. It worked, but not very well as I could tell how soft the metal was, pot metal, and it would just lose its spring tension too easily.

Seriously, how much more money would an adequate metal contact cost????????

they almost got it right.

title: These kill the Signature Sennheiser 598 sound
text:
Some of us are more discerning than others. To me, these absolutely killed the sound stage and gave the cans a muddy sound, producing more bass (could be a plus) but washes out the crisp mids and highs.

I watch movies with 598SE's. Also classical music and some rock. I sent these pads back. They killed the 598SE incredible sparkly experience.

They were denser and harder and not as comfortable, not even close, as the originals.

They are probably comfortable "enough" if you don't wear them for hours or are not sensitive like that. And, they still sound like decent headphones, but just not great like originals. And, its nearly impossible to find true oem replacements. And if you do, 50 bucks is insane. So, I can see why people buy these. But, not for me.

title: Not original for HD598SE or Sennheiser HD 598SR
text:
Objectively: not original for open back HD598SE (which I own) or Sennheiser HD598SR (both essentially the same). Not soft enough and changes the sound signature- increased bass less sound-stage and less mids/highs.

They however do look oem quality.

Either I got a different product or the people reviewing here are fake on not very skillfully discriminating.

I returned them.

While these may actually be OEM(??), they are hard and uncomfortable, not super-duper plush/soft/comfortable like the original ones I have. And, they sound wrong.

Here's the thing: They feel hard like the pads for the closed back Sennheiser HD598CE (which fits the same sized pads as these). HD598CE is very similar to the other 598's but sound muddier because of the pads and closed backs.

I also own the closed back, HD598CE. They have hard pads, as they are designed for monitoring, to not let sound leak by the pads into your ears so you can discern the music in your headphones from ambient sound and to keep feedback from blowing your ears out. And, like when you record singing or playing guitar while monitoring a track, and you don't want the stuff playing in your headphones to leak out and get picked up on the mic. You need harder, denser pads for this. But, they are way less comfortable with less sound-stage and more bass. ...Just like the pads sold here.

tldr: these are much harder (less comfortable) than original HD598SE/SR pads and feel more like pads on the closed back HD598CE. And, sounds more bassy, less sound-stage, lower mids/highs.

However, just recently, I found out that my photos were gone- poof!- just like that they disappeared because SD cards can have malfunctions in them spontaneously. In order to retrieve these photos, a company is going to charge me $2000 on the off-chance, with no guarantee, of course, that they can even get the photos back. I am completely and utterly devastated that this SD card in which I entrusted has failed me so deeply and now I may never see my beautiful memories captured on photo again. I've tried all of my components individually and it seems to be related to USB, I believe it has some difficulty with any substantial amount of USB devices connected, even if those devices are mostly self-powered.

The IPMI on it is OK, but sometimes crashes with the rest of the system, and other times the system will totally fail to boot or lock up while booting or running, and there's no event in the logs at all, much less something that might help me diagnose. Fan control is lacking, too. It seems to have three speeds for the fans, and the two higher speeds are... quite substantially faster/louder than the lowest speed, nor have I been able to figure out how to control individual fans, which would help me maintain system temperatures without as much noise.

[ 8178.815978] xhci_hcd 0000:18:00.0: xHCI host not responding to stop endpoint command.
[ 8178.816531] xhci_hcd 0000:18:00.0: xHCI host controller not responding, assume dead
[ 8178.816625] xhci_hcd 0000:18:00.0: HC died; cleaning up

Nothing was drawing much power, and the SATA power port was plugged in... there were a fair number of devices connected (mouse, webcam, arduino, three flash drives, a bluetooth adapter... a microusb cable that's not plugged into anything?) but they've all been plugged into my old motherboard and most of them were plugged into my current motherboard without issue before... most of them are plugged into it again right now. title: At these prices, get the 128!
text:
- I have tried so many different SD cards from various manufacturers, at various price points, in the name of trying to save a few bucks. It was really important to me back when a 128GB card cost $50 or more. They all do the same thing, so what’s the difference, really?
What I've found is that it can be extremely aggravating to put up with when the card does not perform well or does not perform at all. I have heard warning stories about cards that are advertised as one size and actually are another size, causing data loss. With that in mind, I have never tried using the very cheapest card or too-goo-to-be-true card deals. But I have purchased cards on sale at the drugstore or even tried some strange brands. What I have come back to is that it’s just not worth the trouble now that prices have dropped so low. When I am trusting 128 GB of data to a single card, it’s just not worth my time and aggravation to have a card that won’t perform. Furthermore, SanDisk cards like this one are all FAST ENOUGH. I’m not a pro photographer, and I don’t have time to figure out whether a card is Class 1 or Class 3 or whatever. I just want it to be good enough that it can keep up with my devices.

I have now purchased several SanDisk cards, and each and everyone of them has arrived in perfect condition and works perfectly every time. They are faster than any other card that I use and I've never suffered data loss. I am putting this card into my Fiio X5ii Digital Audio Player, and it works just fine. During the initial data transfer I have already noticed that the speed is adequate, and I never experience skipping when playing uncompressed high-resolution audio files. I have the same card for my Nintendo Switch, and it works perfectly.

The prices on these are so good now you have no excuse but to buy good name brand like SanDisk. Just buy it and don't worry about it.

title: Just get some command strips
text:
I bought this stacking kit when I purchased the FiiO E12A Mont Blanc IEM Special Edition Portable Headphone Amp, Titanium so I could connect it to my FiiO X5 High Resolution Music Player (2nd Generation)(Titanium). It is easy to set up, but it sure is ugly once you get it on there. Some of you may like that - I thought it looked kind of cool, like a weird set of custom recording gear or something. But the rubber bands used to hold the headphone amp onto the back of the DAP were strange looking. They also get in the way of the E12A’s USB port, so I would have to scoot the bands out of the way when I needed to get in there. They got in the way of the X5’s volume keys too, but you won’t need to use those if you’re using a headphone amp.
I eventually broke the plastic frame on one of the cutaways for the rubber bands when I was trying to put my X5 back in. It’s thin in a few spots, and the plastic cracked. Instead of buying another one, I used some Command Strip Picture Hanging Strips (sort of like velcro, but without the fuzzy strip) to snap them together. It looks neater, and it’s easier to use.

title: My happy introduction to High-Resolution audio.
text:
I have used this DAP for about two years now, and I am very pleased with it. It sounds terrific, and I absolutely love the built-in Line-out function for getting the best possible audio into my other devices.
The interface is a little strange and old-fashioned if you’re used to an iPhone. It’s like a weird iPod, but it’s worse. The scroll wheel doesn’t feel nearly as good as the iPod’s, but it’s still a great way to get around in the interface. The interface responds quickly, and has never glitched or frozen on me.
For music navigation, I always use the folder browsing, to browse through the memory cards using my own organization. This is because of two big failures in the built-in browsing:
1. When browsing by genre, you simply get a listing of EVERY track in that Genre alphabetically. So if I select “Classical”, the next screen simply shows me page after page of tracks that start with “1”.
2. When browsing by artist, it uses the actual “Artist” field, instead of “Album Artist”. That’s a little old fashioned now, and most devices are smart enough to use the album artist. It makes it impossible to browse for an album where there are multiple guest artists, but the album itself should all be under one artist.
To do my organization, I have found that JRiver Media Center. That does NOT come with this - you are on your own for software.
I decided on the X5 after looking into the DAC chips Fiio used, and verifying that this could play the formats I was interested - specifically DSD and 24 bit 192KHz PCM. It does both of those with no trouble, and sounds great doing it. Most of my music is in high-resolution FLAC, and CD-resolution Apple Lossless. They both play very well on the X5.
Most of the time, I use mine with a Fiio E12A Mont Blanc Special Edition headphone amp, and Shure SE215 In-Ear monitors. I will also sometimes connect it using the line-out port to my car AUX input or my home stereo. It sounds great in all cases.
I have used it a few times as an external DAC for my Mac, and it works really well at that too - that allows me to connect my headphones through the amp and get some terrific sound.
It has no moving parts, and I can’t imagine that anything on it will break for a very long time thanks to the sturdy aluminum case. If it ever does, I think the only change I would want in my next DAC would be USB-C (the Micro USB connector is just so flimsy on ALL devices, not just this). I don’t need a bigger screen, and I certainly don’t need any more quality.

title: It's a good monitor for the office, but I wouldn't do photography on it.
text:
I purchased this Monitor to use in my office, because I wanted a larger screen to do work in multiple windows at the same time. It is connected to a 2017 15 inch MacBook Pro. I use a USB-C to DisplayPort adapter to connect it. It will connect with an HDMI cable, but then it is limited to 30 Hz refresh rate at full resolution. That looks terrible, so I insist you get the proper display port cable.
The display itself is fine, but it is of noticeably lower quality than the displays that come in Apple's own computers. The colors and viewing angle are simply not as good. For Excel, Outlook, OmniOutliner, and web browsing, it is perfectly adequate.
I would not get this monitor if you wanted to watch movies, edit photographs, or care deeply about a consistent image at any angle. Colors WILL distort on this monitor depending on your viewing angle. Still, the monitor is an excellent value for the size and picture quality. The material quality is fine, but not as good as Apple. I only bring that up because if you are using this with a MacBook Pro like I am, it will feel like a step down. That said, I have not noticed any creaking plastic, Sharp edges, or any other problems with the materials.

title: Lots of features, poor execution, frustrating, frustrating, frustrating.
text:
I bought the printer because it was affordable, and had lots of features. I wanted something with a duplex document feeder scanner, full duplex printing, color, and flatbed scanning. This seemed to have it all. As a scanner, it's pretty good if you manage to stay away from the HP software. As a printer, the quality is decent, but the ink situation is enough to make me never buy from HP again.

I'm sure HP read lots and lots of letters from angry customers complaining about their ink prices. Indeed, with other HP printers, it can be frustrating to be charged $35 when you run out of black ink. HP's solution to this can be seen with the 564 ink cartridge - the colors are $10 and the black is $12. Seems cheap!

Here's the awful truth: the black ink lasts about 30 - 50 pages. This is not an exaggeration. You need to replace the ink ALL THE TIME. The printer also has a bizarre habit of using ALL of the colors even when you're printing things that look black and white. So even if you're not printing very much in color at all, the printer will inexplicably run out of colors. Since the ink cartridges are so small, it seems like the printer CONSTANTLY has a low ink warning, and is CONSTANTLY stopping with out of ink errors. So even though you're only spending $10 - $12 on each cartridge, you're buying tons of them, and you need a huge stock for replenishment. This is HP's marketing department guiding the hand of their engineering department and delivering a crippled product. You will learn to hate this printer. It will constantly need your care and feeding, and you won't save any money on ink.

Here's a tip: in the print settings on your computer, you can tell it to use black ink only. That's a lifesafer.

Side note: the wi-fi on my unit has gone out twice. Out of warranty though, but the range on the Bluetooth is excellent, so not that big a problem for me. Don't know if it's endemic, or isolated.

title: First impressions very good

After it's in, however, it feels natural and it's so so wonderful to not have to hold anything or dangle anything when you're talking. When I'm at home, I can leave the phone on its charger and walk around talking. The sound starts to break up when I'm in the next room, but that's over 15 feet away AND through a plaster wall. Overall, I'm impressed with the range.
I feel the designer should have paid more attention to the tactile feel of the control buttons. When you're trying to reach behind your ear to press the answer button or adjust volume, it's hard to know which button you're pressing or even whether or not you're pressing a button! It's something I'll get used to I'm sure. Don't let that influence your buying.
Lastly, set up on my T68i was a Breeze! I paired it once, and I never have to configure anything again! Nice job on the setup. It comes with a manual, but you won't need it.

title: Better Than Expected - Buy It
text:
[[VIDEOID:8c9fe6543edf9e4bd0345d22b1eaeac2]] Based on reviews, I wanted a HackRF One, but my auction order was canceled. Since the HackRF One was basically out of stock everywhere or well over $300 and I was too impatient to wait for a shipment from China, I decided to try the NESDR SMArTee XTR SDR in the meantime. It was less than $40, so there wasn't much to lose.

As you can see and here in my video, it works VERY WELL. I expected lots of static and poor performance since even the Great Scott Gadgets tutorial on YouTube had a fair amount of static in lesson 1. Granted, I likely have better signal strength here in South Florida, and I think my antenna is a bit better than the stock telescoping rod they were using in the video. Instead, the RTL-SDR gave surprising good performance.

That said, it's not a replacement for the HackRF One. The first thing you'll notice, if you attempt to build any of the HackRF projects, is that you'll need to drastically reduce the sample rate. The HackRF One can handle a 20MHz sampling rate; the RTL-SDR SMArTee XDR sampling rate is an order of magnitude lower - 2 MHz. Furthermore, the RTL-SDR is receive only and that definitely limits its capabilities. Even so, if you are looking for a cheap introduction to SDR, then definitely buy the RTL-SDR SMArTee XTR. You won't regret it.

title: Good Parking Aid
text:
I like it. As others have noted, the parking distance is not adjustable— it’s 1.5 ft from the sensor. I simply taped the sensor to a small rectangular box and moved the box so that the stop location was where I wanted it.

When the sensor detects your car entering the garage, a green lights flashes. As you get closer, the yellow light flashes. When you reach the stop position a the red light flashes and an audible alert sounds for a couple of seconds; if you are too close to the sensor, the audible alert keeps sounding for about 30 seconds or until you back up to the appropriate distance. Good purchase!

I was looking for something more low tech (a ball hanging from a string), but prices for things like that were about the same on Amazon at the time. This was a better deal.

title: Top Quality Apple Certified Nylon Lightning Cable - BUY IT

title: First Rate Indoor Amplified Antenna.... But It, You Won't be Disappointed
text:
I tried 2 other antennas at this location and was less than thrilled by the results. One was an amplified unit that I purchased years ago that had two vertical antennas that could be independently positioned forward or backward up to a ~45 degree angle from a straight, vertical position with a rotating base. I don't recall it's brand, but it worked fairly well most of the time, but I found myself going back to the old method of adding aluminum foil to get the best reception. The second antenna I tried was an RCA amplified bar antenna. It picked up most channels, but I had to change its direction back and forth depending on whether I wanted the CBS or the NBC affiliate; I could receive most all other channels with either direction. I returned that unit to WalMart.

According to AntennaWeb.org, I should receive 27 channels from 13 stations; the government site stated that I should receive 8 stations with a strong signal, 1 station with a weak signal, and that I would not be able to receive 1 station in the area. With this antenna, my TV found 49 channels this morning when I re-ran the scan, including all the channels listed on both sites that I mentioned previously. The first night that I ran the scan, I was able to pick up over 50 channels, including Channel 5 from Nashville! It was very cloudy that night, and I assume that reception was due to a propagation anomaly since I have not been able to receive that channel since then.

I highly recommend this antenna. For the record, I ran this test 11 floors up in a high-rise apartment building in downtown Louisville. As others have noted, very slight changes in the orientation of the antenna significantly affects reception of some stations. My antenna is currently attach to a window on one side and bends around the frame and attaches to the wall on the other side of the antenna. (I recommend getting some of the 3M replacement strips to attach the antenna so that you can re-arrange it as needed.)

title: Excellent Value for the Money!
text:
The Sony SDM-S73 is a very good monitor for the price. I purchased a lower cost 17" LCD and was very disappointed as its display was not clear and had 2 dead pixels. It went directly to eBay; I purchased this monitor as a replacement for use with my Mac iBook.

When I connected the Sony, my first impression was dismay and a feeling of de ja vu. Was this another bad product? Silver items in the Mac OS X aqua interface (Safari and the mail client in particular) were tinted an ugly shade of pink!!! UGH! This product was almost returned!

Fortunately, I ran the display color calibration and was able to correct all problems. The default Sony SDM-73 profile appears to be off-- at least on my iBook with the version of Mac OS 10.3 that I am running. Run the display color calibration tool in "expert" mode and this is a good monitor for use with Macs. (It may take 2-3 attempts to get it exactly right, but the result is well worth the effort.)

A note to those epecting perfection-- quality is not as good as Apple's LCD cinema displays. Do not expect the same clarity and quality as Apple's higher end cinema displays (but given the price differential, this is to be expected). Apple doesn't offer 17" LCD displays at present...I love the Sony!

text:
Works as advertised once fully set up, though setting it up was really an exercise in trial and error. It's not supposed to matter which wire you connect to which connector on the back of the unit, but for me, it mattered for some reason (one way worked, and the other did not). Much nicer looking than the older, chunkier Ring Doorbell that has the battery option too. If you are able to use a hardwire connection, this is the one to get.

The motion detection notifications could be better since when you tune in live, generally the source of the motion has already moved on and you have to wait for the recording to store for you to start playing it from the start. Would be nice if there were an option to have the recording play from the beginning at 2x speed to catch up to live once you chase the notification.

The main issue I had with setup is that nowhere in the documentation in the box is there an indication that holding the side button for 10-30 seconds resets the device and re-forces a firmware update, which is what I had to do in order to get the doorbell to work as well as actually making the bell in my house ring. I ended up having to call the customer support line to ask what to do when I was only able to get the doorbell outside or in the house to work, and they told me this trick over the phone. I had asked them why this wasn't just in the manual, and the (unacceptable) response I got was basically that "oh not that many people run into this so we just wait for them to call us with problems."

title: Just not worth it (and how about that constant alternator whine at low to no volume?)
text:
1) If this is your first foray into the amplification of your speakers beyond stock you might think it sounds pretty good. On the other hand, if you intend to use this amp as an upgrade to another (like me) you very well may be sorely disappointed as I am. Claimed wattage output just doesn't translate to any meaningful speaker output increase. I will say that hooking it up was a breeze and if it matters to you it has a nice appearance. I recommend you do what I should have and go with a slightly more expensive but truly impressive amp. 2) Are you bothered by that obnoxious squealing (alternator whine). Not your fault. Not your head unit's fault. Not a problem with the wiring. This is a problem with engine noise interfering with your RCA cables leading to amp. Pioneer seems to have thrown all noise suppression out the window to reach this price point. Out came one amp that I am upgrading from that had NO NOISE to this Pioneer and immediate noise. Obviously not the head unit or poor grounding. Being a 4 channel amp I have had to purchase 2 - 2 channel noise suppressors. These go between your "input to amplifier" leads and the amplifier itself. Based on all the other questions and reviews you can just plan on adding these suppressors when you buy the amp. I will attach a link to the suppressors shortly.

Suppressor/Isolator: https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B000K50HJE/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o04_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

title: FANTASTIC SOUND BAR with a remote that is an absolute disaster.  Fix the remote and 5-STARS no question.
text:
The sound from this bar is clean, clear, crisp and LOUD! A very decent amount of BASS, with a sub woofer output should you want to connect one. I found out I ordered a longer bar than is recommended. How did I find out? The packaging for this bar states that it is for a 42" or larger TV. I purchased it for a 32" TV. The concern, I believe, is that if the speakers are too far from the TV's center it will not seem as though the audio is coming from the actors. My brain is making the leap and tricking me so all is well. I use my TV for music for the most part anyway (Comcast Music Choice and Fire TV Music).
It is disappointing that Fire TV Music has such poor audio quality since it is there that I can make personal music choices unlike Comcast. Fire TV just sounds plain bad. It did on the TV speakers and now on the bar; it is just un-listenable. Safe to call it "LOW FIDELITY"
As far as connecting an input to this bar from your TV you have many options and most all the cables you may need are included. I really liked that they included the cord to to connect the bar to a sub. This cord is over and above what is required to connect the bar to the TV...very nice touch VIZIO. Now I need to go to my storage and try to find my sub :-)
My TV only offers 2 audio outputs, head phone and optical. Included with the bar were a headphone-to-2 RCA connector cord, and a fiber optic patch cord, among others. That allowed me what would be considered the worst quality connection and the best quality connection possibilities. If you don't have OPTICAL OUT on your TV do not despair...the worst possible option (headphone-to-RCA patch cord) sounds FANTASTIC! I can detect no loss of fidelity between the two. You will not be missing out.
Now to the reason I gave it 3 stars rather than 5. The back of the remote just keeps sliding off. It is not broken in any way. Just poorly designed. I often use the sound bar in dark or nearly dark conditions. It is taking time to train myself to not go where I normally would to use the any of the buttons. So how about the POWER button? It is not the top left button on the remote as you will see and are used to on any other remote in your home. For some strange reason instead of the power button being in the far upper left of the remote they felt this was a good place to position the INPUT button. Power is upper right. Volume UP/DOWN is traditionally placed on the left side of the remote with a paddle switch or separate buttons. Located in the standard volume UP/DOWN positions are the TruVolume and the TruSurround HD. The volume UP/DOWN are located on a FLAT 1-3/8" (34.9mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) multi-function EVER SO SLIGHTLY RAISED square. To be honest I can't even tell that it IS raised at all most of the time. If you go for the volume in low light you may operate any of 3 other function controls. Lastly, if you were hoping the VOLUME controls are the 2 well raised buttons on the right (traditional location) you would be wrong. Those are your BASS/TREBLE controls.
I am not sure I would buy this bar again knowing what I do now about the remote. As I said I often use the remote in low or no light. The problems I mention here may just be my own...but I doubt it. All of these tiny buttons and controls are all scrunched into a small 2-3/8" (60.3mm) x 1-3/8" (34.9mm) upper 40% of this little remote and they are not raised enough and not far apart enough to be used just by touch. I well believe that just 3 functions on the remote will account for 90% of it's use. POWER (that CAN be felt but it is in the wrong place...you'll get used to that) and the VOLUME UP/DOWN that exist on a square, fully smooth (NO tactile feedback...I'd hate to see a blind person trying to operate), 4-function piece of plastic that is raised about 1/32" (0.8mm). On the bright side for me, I found out fairly quickly that my cable box remote controls the basic functions of the sound bar. I hope you get so lucky.
Knowing what I know now I should have purchased a bar in the 28"-32" (71mm-81mm) class looking for features such as the control panel on the bar being mildly illuminated and a proper remote perhaps with illumination itself. My roommate may buy mine from me for a location that is always well lit and has a 42" TV. I'll lose $20 on the deal but I can get the absolute right bar for me.. I don't return items that are not what I would like due to my own failure in researching. So, for better or worse, the bar is mine. There is one thing you cannot fault; THIS THING SOUNDS AMAZING!
- Good Shopping!!!

title: Low price to be sure...But if you would like to know what that price gets you in quality and reliability read on.
text: Well, I was asked to share my thoughts on this product.  I will give you an excerpt from the most prominent product review company group out there..."A number of secondary brands had reliability records comparable to the major brands, but one—Sceptre—was significantly more problem-prone."  I moved to LG (quality on par with Samsung as far as ratings and reliability are concerned) but at a lower price than Samsung.  Sony beats Samsung in the ratings from the above mentioned product reviewer but just barely, and at a far higher price point.  So for price, satisfaction, and reliability stick with LG first and Samsung second.  Sony is higher priced but that is because of added features.  This proves to be the case in all screen sizes.  Lastly, as specifically regards the 32 inch class televisions you are looking at now, a final quote from the reviewer: "Vizio, Toshiba, and Sharp—appear to offer a nice balance of price and performance, but you may not have to pay much more for an LG, which scored better." As an side, TCL does poorly in the 32" class, but moves to the middle of the pack for sets in the 39" to 43" and  46"to 52" classes. As most all Amazon shoppers know, an extended warranty is offered by a third party company on items such as this. One might think they could just purchase the cheap set with a poor frequency of repair record and then be taken care of by purchasing an extended warranty at checkout. It must be known that regardless of whatever brand you pick in the 32" class, if something goes wrong you will packing up the  TV and sending it off for repairs.  In-home repairs do not generally come into play until your set is 39" or larger.  Buy right the first time. Happy shopping!!!

title: Good enough!
text:
I have an LG TV 47" so I thought another LG product might be the best course of action (of course the money involved had to do with this decision), so I went to my local Best Buy to get a glimpse of what is out there. Besides this LG sound bar they had quite a few choices. I quick referenced them to their reviews and came to the conclusion that most sound bars are just about at the same level in terms of overall performance. I did see a Bowers and Wilkins?, priced around $2200, which is way more expensive than the tv itself (but was taught that audio is supposed to be the greater investment for the true tv viewer), and this sound bar frankly was fantastic, truly a thing to behold. But $2200 Buckaroos are a long way from $300 and I did get the tv at a great bargain price, so cheap instead of expensive became the call of war.
For what I got this soundbar does everything I wanted done. It was very easy to install through the optical option, and even though the first unit I purchased had troubles pairing with the subwoofer and was returned immediately, the second was the charm and now it works very nicely with the added plus that it certainly did not require a Kamikaze investment. Works very well and it adds a great sound capability to the living room in our home which was the intended site. Some shows are better than others but even the subwoofer does its magic and is a lot of fun to crank it up once in a while, specially for the internet type movie sites (like Netflix, Amazon, Vudu, etc.) that come with the smart tv and required some sort of subscription. Their sound, specially amazon and netflix, was way below average and even at maximum volume on the tv it was very sad. I could hear it but one of the members of the tribe is a little more than a little hard of hearing and was always having trouble (probably the main reason why I decided on a sound bar in the first place).
Needless to say this soundbar delivered what was expected of the product and now my living room is one loud area and when the subwoofer is doing its thing you can feel it kind of in the furniture itself, like some of the controllers in PS3 with the added vibration. Minor thing but rather invigorating, for the whole room now sounds like a mini theater without having had to add several speakers coupled with tedious connections, which certainly I am not qualified or inclined to want to do myself. I just put the sound bar in the same table in which the television rest and the subwoofer about 6 feet away and voila! Just waiting for the neighbors to reassure me as to the loudness, kind of like its baptism when they finally complain (makes you feel a little bit proud that you are putting enough noise to draw the attention of nearby houses, silly but what can you do sometimes?), so for now I am very happy with the purchase and glad that when necessary I have the equipment to raise the noise way higher than it was capable before. 4 very solid Stars!

title: Banna plugs are different than reuseable than RCA connectors.
text: Banana connectors fit much tighter than a RCA connector and for a person unaware of the difference; it would be easy to cause damage on ether end of the speaker wire to the female connected components. Therefore, I would recommend studying the literature or talking to the manufacture (for both connected ends if necessary). For instance,: in most cases if unaware, it would be easy to cause physical damage simply installing a banana male into a female component just by the tightness, (no clearance between M/FM parts that can fool you into thinking this is as it should be because the male banana is designed to squeeze into the female end and, probably remain as such even after someone trips over an AV receiver  speaker wire, and the A/V falls on the floor because the banana connector was so tight you could lift the A/V by the speaker wire. A banana male connector is designed to expand during installation. If you are in need of banana connectors, these connectors are extremely well made and are a very good bang for the buck.  They are also reusable and do not need any special tools other than basic wire strippers.

title: A very good antenna but highly directional
text:
The trick with this antenna is not getting frustrated with moving it around and pointing it in the right direction. I mounted mine on the hand rail of my apartment balcony, second floor and now receive all local channels 4-68. Channel 68 being about 45 miles away. All are received in full green in windows media center, without using a preamp.

Previously I had it mounted under and bolted to the 3rd floor balcony to try and keep it out of sight. Reception was iffy on 4 favorite channels. I then moved it to its' present location with the idea that the antennas footprint is considerably smaller than all the satellite dishes mounted on balconies throughout the complex. The mounting bracket and pole that come with it, are the same type satellite dishes use, Very strong and versatile. You will need to buy some good bolts, I used 4, 5/16" x 1- 1/2" Galvanized Lag and flat washers, I predrilled 3/16" pilot holes first. I just thought I'd mention that for those not fastener savvy.

I would guess the antenna mount alone is worth 1/3rd of the entire antenna cost. Recommend a good quad shield coaxial cable with the thick, sollid copper wire. A shorter run is better if possible. I only have about 12 feet to my PC/TV.

Once I figured out how to mount this antenna correctly, a month ago, I haven't had to adjust it.

text: An excellent pci tuner card. You insert the card; install the drivers and WinTV software. A big reason I purchased this card is it has a separate FM\cable\Satellite connection in addition to the digital HD antenna connection. I have a good, long range, outdoor Phillips HD antenna mounted on my apartment balcony and cabled to this card along with a second Hauppauge usb tuner (off a splitter). I can record two channels at once or record one and watch another at the same time. Next I have a FM radio antenna and, the card with media center acts like a digital DJ for playing and recording FM broadcasts. Windows Media Center finds and sets up the signal for both cards and, with a DSL connection will automatically set up your digital TV guide for your area code which you can configure to automatically update, once a week or whenever. The same applies to cable or satellite. All you do is surf the guide, click what you want to watch or record, recordings are automatically saved to your hard drive. I've recorded hundreds of over the air, free, broadcast shows and movies, most of them I was totally unaware of until I bought these tuner cards and set up media center with TV guide. The card comes with WinTV, very good software in its own right, but Media center setup is the cat's meow. I don't have enough time or typing skill to list all the benefits. Very highly recommended!

title: Dissapointed after puchasing four set's of these Eagle Arion
text: My last review was a generous one, only because I didn't allow much time to pass before I did my first review. Things have changed. I have purchased four sets of these speaker systems. The very first set I bought for myself, last Christmas and over a year ago died. Amplifier electronics went bad, I think. This was way after the warranty expired but less than one year. I bought one set each prior to any malfunction, for both of my young adults, and another one for myself. The set I bought three weeks ago was dead when it arrived and the only music it made was a very loud buzzing right out of the box. So, I have two speaker set's that don't work and I will pass judgment after I talk with the manufacturer (Eagle) tomorrow. My big worry now is if the speaker sets' I bought my kids will die in short order. All in all, I am not pleased with the longevity of performances of the Eagle Orion. I purchased a set of Eagle Tech sound stage speakers prior to buying the Orion's and, the Eagle tech 140 watt version still sound great. So, I'm going straight to the manufacturer and see if they will do right by me. I will post what the resolution is, good or bad. This whole debacle is really a shame because they are great looking and sounding speakers and I think more often than not, this sort of thing happens for the speed of sales therefore decreasing quality control and inadequate testing prior to shipping. Two out of four in less than one year or 3 weeks means something isn't right with the process.

title: Great Sound System
text:
I like the sound and power of this system so much,(I say that because it's a lot more than just speakers), That I purchased a smaller set of Eagle tech's to round out my sound system. I use the Eagle Arion's as the front and the Eagle tech's as the rear.
I like the fact that one remote control works both sets. And they look way cool. I have another set of Atecs I use as center speakers and two insignia's as side speakers for 7.1 surround sound. The Eagles blow my other speakers away but I can balance the sound out nicely with my windows VIA equalizer. The remote control for the Eagles has great feature's: Volume, Bass, Treble, Mute, reset. These speakers have their own amplifier and you can plug them in to just about anything, provided you have the right audio adapter. Excellent sound, looks, price. If you plan on using the Eagles as PC speakers, I would highly recommend installing the latest audio drivers for the best sound quality.

title: Added one 4 gigabyte card
text:
My ASUS desktop came with 6 gigabytes of Ram intalled in a three card configuration of 2 gigs per card. I wanted to test if I could get a little faster loading speed by adding more ram and was faced with several choices. Add one 2 gig card or remove all the cards and replace in sets with 4 gig cards up to 16 gigabytes. Doing the later would leave me with 3 extra, not used cards. So I asked Asus about this and was told to replace in set's of two as is the prefered method. I wasn't satisfied with this answer so I went online to a memory manufacturer's site, they scanned my hardware and gave me a list of memory configuration choices. The one I chose was to add one 4 gig card for a total of 10 gigabytes installed. I'm sure this isn't the (optimal configuration) however, my pc is now blazingly fast and startup is in seconds. I also like my future upgrade options.I would also recommend to anyone wanting to tweak their system, to use a good registry repair software, I use System Mechanic.
Download all the latest driver files and install them one at a time, after a complete system backup. Driverzone.com is a state of the art download for free site.

title: Top of the line and worth the price!

Snap in your drive, install two torque bit style screws,(screw driver included) and you're done!

I would give this housing 5 stars just for technical manufacturing accuracy. Everything fit's together perfectly. The USB cord is a good, thick one and the twin fans have to do a fantastic job of cooling.

You can't hear the fans run and the blue lighting is subtle and not overpowering, almost like a very dim night lite. I'd have to say it's the Rolls Royce of exterior drive housings. Knowing what I now have, the price is very reasonable. My only complaint is Thermaltake doesn't make a matching optical drive housing or I'd buy that too!

title: So quiet I can't hear it running
text:
I've installed this hard drive in a Thermaltake USB 3.0 exterior housing and am extremely pleased with the speed, quiet operation and versatility of this drive in the Thermaltake housing.

I formatted the drive NTFS as one big removable mass storage device and transferred 495 GB of recorded movies to the drive in about an hour. Try that with a usb 2.0 backup drive and the thing would be so hot you could fry an egg on it, not to mention it would take a lot longer than an hour.

This is the most quiet drive I've ever installed and when writing to the drive I check the performance monitor because you just can't hear the thing run! I've only had the drive for a week
and it wouldn't be fair to give it 5 stars on that account.

My daughters favorite Disney movie was scratched and skipping a lot so I wanted to fix it.  I wet the cd with the solution and placed it in the machine.  The machine has to be set on a hard flat service. I tried to just hold it in the air and it would not work. I made one round and then reapplied the solution, then cranked the machine around again.  (It goes slowly). I buffed the DVD with the cloth as directed and played the DVD. It skipped less than before, but was still skipping.  I repeated the entire process again, and now the DVD works perfectly!.  I want to try this on some very scratched  DVDs and see how far I can push it. I would recommend this for mild to moderately scratched DVDs/ CDs at this point.  Remember it says it is very important to keep the disc wet with the solution the entire time and rub it throughly with the cloth or it will not work, so do not skip those steps.

title: Does not connect to broadband easily
text:
It fails to connect to the ATT wireless network out of the box. I inserted a sim card, it has data paid, and hotspot doesn't connect to the internet. I have my phone next to the router, phone is able to connect to the router but router itself doesn't connect using sim card.

SIM card works, I tested it by sending text messages to it. I was able to see those test sms on mywebui.net.

I also inserted the card to the phone to test and I was able to get data.

User manual is misleading. It says to install an app Nighthawk and after installation the app says it doesn't support this device.

User manual says ask community for support.

I had to register with Netgear, spent lots of time waiting for an agent to chat, then more time to troubleshoot the router. It took half a day total to fix it.

I had to connect the phone to the router that didn't have internet connection. Then on the phone with no internet connection went to ROUTERLOGIN.NET
entered admin login for the router.

Then poked around, got to Settings> Router>BASIC>DNS and set it from automatic to manual.

And then entered DNS 8.8.8.8 and another DNS 8.8.4.4

After that router reloaded and connected to wireless.

Why this is not in the user guide or manual?!! I downloaded the full manual and it is not there. Just because all these trouble I will give this device one star. This is the first day I use it and I am not sure how long it will last.

title: OK Budget Phone, no NFC, bad sound
text:
This phone A10s is basically the worse version of the old Galaxy S7 Edge from seven years ago. Slightly higher battery capacity - 4000 instead of 3600, same screen size, but the quality of the screen is not as good. S7 screen glass is much better quality, it's smoother and it's scratch resistant. A10 touch screen response time is worse than S7. There is some kind of a split second lag which feels strange after using S7.

Unlike S7, A10 doesn't have wireless charging :(

Blue light functionality doesn't work when I flip the blue light button. Button is there but functionality is not. No physical home button anymore.

NFC is not supported, can't pay in the store using this phone. Item specs here says "Connectivity NFC" which is misleading. Old S7 supports NFC.

Sound is HORRIBLE for single built in speaker. Comparing to old S7 playing the same song this phone is missing low frequencies, sound is flat and unimpressive, no Dolby. S7 sound has lots of volume, low and high frequencies and it feels like surround sound, like movie theater experience.

Dolby Atmos is disabled on A10 for built in speaker. Adaptive sound functionality is completely missing, nada. When I plug in earphones, Dolby Atmos gets enabled but doesn't make any difference and left ear piece is much more quiet than the right one. The phone doesn't distribute sound equally between the left and right ear pieces.

Not possible to opt out from sending Samsung all your phone logs info. All preinstalled apps had rights to mess up phones operation system and access everything on the phone and send your private info everywhere. I had to go through every setting to change that. New icons look ugly.

Good features are dual sim and a radio tuner so one can listen to the local FM radio without wi-fi or cell service. It still has a jack for wired ear phones, the wire is used as an antenna for the radio tuner. Fresh battery holds charge better than a seven years old Galaxy S7 Edge. It was easy to set up and install applications from Google Play. Phone is unlocked and can be used overseas.

It's an OK unlocked budget phone for everyday use that works with certain carriers only. But lack of NFC, no wireless charging, and bad sound is a big No.

This NEWER Lite version is much much worse than my OLD GT-P6200 tablet in EVERY category.

Sound is bad, you can't really enjoy playing music, video is not that good, I don't want to watch movies on it. When I tried to make my own video, it was all grainy, grey, low quality, smaller size, not whole screen, sound was horrible, some cracking and scratching on the background. Photos are also no good. Just makes you upset when you try to make a picture of a beautiful sunset and instead you get something bleak and flat on the screen.

In general it is cheaply made. Even USB cable that came with it is shorter, cheaper, and stiffer in comparison with the GT-P6200. No earphones in the box. No front camera so no video chat. Or turn it around and they will see you but you will not see them. They tried to make it as cheap as possible cutting costs on every corner. Tablet has only three home screens and some kind of Android system with the simplified functionality.

I don't know what to use this tablet for, maybe just to read books or to have it as an external hard drive. I keep it as a backup in case my regular tablet gets discharged. It doesn't break but it doesn't give you a real pleasure of using it either. Just an annoyance. For its functionality I would price is around $50-$60 when new. It's more than TWICE OVERPRICED, it is no good even for a school kid.

My advice is to spend a little bit more money and buy something better.

title: Great case for those with kids!
text:
I really prefer minimalist cases for my electronics, and I loathe built-in screen protectors. As such, this is not the type of case I would normally buy. However, after a close call in which my 7yo accidentally dropped my iPad (broke the glass screen protector, but the screen survived the impact), I determined that my current stage of life requires a little more protection. I got this case installed today and am pleasantly surprised. The strap on the back makes holding the device much more comfortable. The rotatable kickstand is also quite handy. Best of all, the built-in screen protector doesn't completely ruin the picture quality. Is it as good as tempered glass? No. But that would be an unreasonable expectation.
About 8 minutes after the case got installed, my 5yo spilled mac n cheese on the device. Needless to say, I believe my hunch about needing better protection was correct. While this may not be the best case for personal tastes, I can say that it ranks very highly for a thicker case with integrated screen protection.

title: I read an e-reader in direct sunlight!
text: The Kindle is a must-have for any reader. The Paperwhite is a must-have for any reader that doesn't want to annoy their spouse with reading lights in bed. The lighting is superb. The proprietary font is easy to read. Best of all, you can actually read this in direct sunlight. On these cold Alaskan days, it's nice to be able to sit by a window with sunlight coming in and read. Finally, the cost of books makes this a no-brainer. My printed Bible (HCSB Study Bible) cost over $60. I bought the Kindle version for $2.99. The Bible is one book that I prefer to have in print (mostly for tradition and for the off-chance that a solar flare wipes out the grid), but this illustrates the point. After buying four or five books, the Paperwhite device pays for itself. It's a great product. Amazon is in a league of its own with e-reader technology.

title: Amazing machine for the money
text: I bought the Acer Timeline because I just got rid of my MacBook with the intention of buying a MacBook Air. I stumbled across the Timeline and decided that with the cost (roughly 1/3 the price), it would be worth it to try the Timeline. It has turned out to be an awesome machine. I miss MacOSX, but Windows Vista works pretty well. The only drawback is the processor speed. However, the processor itself is a bonus. It is a low-energy processor, so I'm able to use this machine for a long time on a single charge (I've gone up to 9 hours while running FireFox, and up to 8 hours while running Word and MediaPlayer at the same time). So in my opinion, the slower processor is well worth it.

title: 5 Star Product and 6 Star Customer Service
text:
I bought 2 of these around Christmas 2021. One for myself, and a friend of mine as we're both avid users of AirPods Max.

I received the "Version 1" of the product, while my friend received "Version 2."

So let's get into it!

I assembled version 1 and to my distraught face, the stand was incredibly wobbly. The pole piece mostly didn't fit the screw cuttings in the metal and overall the product was incredibly dissatisfying and took forever to essentially assemble wrong (since correct assembly was impossible).

Meanwhile, my friend raves about how great it is (he got version 2). So seeing some folks had similar issues, I contacted support. About a week later I received a very nice message back. The thing I appreciate most is this wasn't a simple PR cut and paste. This sounded like it was directly from someone who really cared.

He took my address and promised to ship out a replacement with Version 2 immediately. Not only that, he actually explained in detail the issues I had experienced and how they had fixed them with Version 2. He even went as far as to confirming version 2 was shipped to my friend.

They explained they had requested amazon remove version 1 but were rejected. So, if you receive a wobbly version 1 product (the serial number is on the top of the base stand), they ENCOURAGE you to contact them and they will happily replace it with version 2.

So, the product was jacked, which this company admits. They're doing absolutely everything in their power to correct the issues and are a fantastic example of how you build customer trust.

Thanks again for everything.

Version 2 of this product is absolutely fantastic, sturdy, does not shake or move at all. The metal is very nice looking and makes for a great set piece on your desk or otherwise. As soon as you pull your headphone off, they reconnect as you're used to when pulling them out of the case. Similarly when you place them on the stand, they'll disconnect instantly.

Great stuff and thanks!

title: Better than expected
text:
Ease of set up: takes it a minute if you have never used windows 8, but watch a few youtube videos and it will speed up the process. The system wakes up with little lag from the sleep/hibernation and even on initial start up. The battery lasted about 6 hours with dim light and constant downloading and setting changes.

The fan, so far, has not made a sound until i held the laptop up to my ear and could hear a slight hmmm.

I'm not a computer expert, but I have used a new work Dell Latitude, and this one looks nicer, has a larger screen, and is much faster (even though all of the specs are lower). I am most impressed with the ease of the laptop "waking up" so quickly with almost no lag.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
UPDATE

I've had the laptop for about a week now and have finally gotten through all of the Windows 8 differences (all but figuring out how to reduce the size of websites, icons, folders and not just the text...but I'm sure there is a way).

As for the laptop, I've never been happier. With the screen dimmed at 50%, I am able to download pretty regularly, surf the web, and write reports for about 6 hours before I need to recharge in one sitting. On one full charge, I was able to go 3 days without charging with minimal web browsing and some downloading of PDF files. Like I've said before, the sleep mode is fantastic. The battery is conserved, and I know that it turns off the internet wifi as our modem beeps every time there is a device deactivated.

The speakers are really good for being a laptop. The noise isn't distorted, and even at the lower end, the clarity is good. I've had a toshiba in the past that you needed to plug into external speakers to really listen to it.

I have had many people over the past year suggest asus, and now it's my turn. I've been impressed from day one, and still find things about this laptop that outperform other $1000 laptops.

I purchased this Patriot Memory Supersonic Pulse 32 GB USB 3.0 Drive (PSF32GSPUSB) from Amazon.com. Arrived in time and was well packed.
However it does not work in a USB 3.0 slot. Only works in USB 2.0 slots.
I thought I purchased a fast USB 3.0 and received a USB performance that runs super hot on a USB 2.0 slot instead of the claimed USB 3.0
I sent trouble report to Patriot about this. I have never received a reply from their support group. I would never buy another product from them with this service.

title: LOC8TOR Lite
text:
I purchased this item to keep track of our cat when traveling in the motorhome. We had lost one cat a few years ago so this looked to be a great device.
The range was very disappointing. About as far as I could throw a house brick on one unit and perhaps 100 feet line of sight on the second. Within a few days, one unit, the 100 foot range one had quit working.
A battery test showed the problem was low batteries and one failed completely. Who knows how long these have been on the retailer's shelf.
An email to the manufacture brought a quick response. A new set of batteries plus a bonus arrived by Royal Mail shortly after my query..
I am satisfied with the performance after the installation of fresh batteries. We are no longer on the road so the requirement for a locating device is not needed now. I feel sure the product will work well for us next time we leave.

title: Superb Quality At A Resonable Price
text:

It offers multiple tilt and swivel adjustments for mounting and viewing - and even after the TV is mounted, you can slide it to the left or right if needed to line up better with surrounding accessories/decor.

title: Work well, as long as you stay seated in the perfect location
text:
The GOOD:
These work well for hearing dialog and hushed speaking, or when it's accompanied with a lot of background noise in certain movies and tv shows. Also work well if someone is hard-of-hearing, so that you don't have to crank up the volume on the tv (the volume of each headset is individually adjustable). We've found it also works well if one person watching tv while others in the room are playing games or watching something else on their tablets.
The BAD:
These are extremely Line-Of-Sight. The base unit has to be aimed directly where you're seated, and if you're sitting just a couple/few feet to either side, you'll start getting more & more static. If I stand up to grab something from the other side of the room, the static will overtake the tv audio dialog completely and I have to take them off my head. Seems strange that the technology is so limited on these, requiring near perfect seating placement. I'll even get brief blasts of static just by raising my hand up to my face, as it seems to partially block the signal coming from the base unit.
Overall worth having but could definitely be improved.
