title: Very good sound quality
text:
I have to admit I was surprised. I didn't in a million years think these would really have good sound quality, but purchased them to use with audio books, so it wasn't on the top of my list of "wants".

They have good sound quality, are exactly what they say they are, and they are reasonably priced.

They appear to be sturdy enough to withstand daily use, but time will tell, as it always does. If anything changes, I'll come back and write an addendum to this review.

title: Sturdier and heavier than I thought it would be
text:
I'm using this on my desk to hold my large monitor and all the accoutrements that go along with having a home office - pens, extra paper, extra headset, remote for the 32"TV I use for a monitor. I was afraid that the monitor wouldn't work with this and I was prepared to be disappointed. Absolutely am not. It is far sturdier than I thought bamboo would be, nice looking, and it is perfect. I think if I ever close down my home office, I'll find a way to keep this and use it.

I'm going to add to this review: While I've had no problem with this unit, per se, I can still see where shoddy workmanship could have affected its use. I think I was lucky, it came undamaged with all the parts in the correct order and space. However, the backs of both drawers are uneven. I guess you could say crooked. It doesn't affect the way the drawer fits into the unit until you look down at the drawer and realize it isn't really a rectangle, more like a trapezoid. I'm glad I was one of the lucky ones who received a working unit, however, I think I'll avoid this company if I buy something similar again.

title: Generic keyboard and mouse
text:
This is a generic keyboard and mouse. I always keep a spare one here in the office, as I manage to ruin keyboards and/or mice quite often.

They work fine, are affordable, are wired (in case you were looking for wireless), and seem to last long, even though I usually destroy them after a couple of months.

title: Cute earbuds
text: These are cute, can be used with my iPod, but cannot be used with my computer without an adaptor, which disappointed me a bit. Then on the first use, I discovered that, when using for Skype or Zoom, there is a lot of background noise that the other people can hear. And it isn't failure of the noise cancellation, it is some kind of feedback from the buds themselves.  I bought an adaptor and in a pink I'll use these with my iPod, but not the best sounds quality.

title: Sound quality not the best
text: I bought these so I could connect my buds to my computer. I'm not sure it is the splitter or the buds, but once I used the splitter, I'm getting a lot of noise coming into my ears, and people I'm speaking with tell me there appears to be some noise coming from the microphone.  But when I use the buds with my laptop, the noise isn't anywhere near as loud.

title: Will not work with a computer
text: I ordered these as an adapter for my PC. No Go. The prongs are not far enough apart to fit into the proper spot. I was sorely disappointed, but the description does say they are for airplanes. I didn't realize airplanes had different sized connection. Shame on me.

title: Fairly good headset
text:
I wear a headset for the better part of a day. I like to use headsets rather than the phone handset because it keeps my hands free.

These definitely do the job with noise cancelling and the volume control works very well. I've been told once or twice that people have trouble hearing me at times, but since I don't know if that's the headset or their phones, I deducted a single star.

My only complaint is the clip that puts the volume control and mute button together is very difficult to hook onto anything other than very thin fabric. I have to struggle to get it on and off my jacket during the day. My suggestion to the manufacturer, make the clip easier to slide fabric into or make it a clip that opens.

title: Not just for gaming use
text:
I used these connected to my computer to answer calls during the day. These interfaced easily with my computer so they turned into my permanent go to's. I have tested these thoroughly with a couple of customers to make sure that what I was saying was getting out there with no interference. Noise cancellation did very well. The sound quality, as I've heard myself recorded also, if very good for a relatively inexpensive set of headphones. I also like the way the ear pads fit more over the ear than on top of it, as compared to a couple other headphones I've used.

I have no idea what these would be like for gaming, as that isn't the reason I bought them, but the clarity would certainly lend itself to gaming. If you are shopping for affordable headphones that are a bit sturdier than others out there, this would be a good choice.

title: Nice headset for listening to audio books
text:
I needed a headset that I could plug into my phone, my kindle, and my computer. These were sort of cute, so I figured what the hey? I'll give them a try.

They fit good, and while listening to audio books, as long as I keep the volume in the mid range (and who wants books screamed at them?), it does great. I wish they'd made the volume control a little bit more intuitive. Instead of dealing with the headset, I used the volume control on whatever I had plugged them into. Be advised, and I would hope this is only mine but don't know, if you turn up the volume too high, there is a lot of distortion and some noise that comes through the headset. The distortion was the most irritating to me, thus why I adjust the volume on the device, and make sure it doesn't go over mid range.

For the money, these are functioning, cute headsets

title: Far sturdier than I thought it would be.
text: When I ordered this, I'd planned to run it behind one of my monitors, assuming that the female connector wouldn't be all that sturdy and I wanted to keep it out of harm's way as I tend to be very rough with things that are on my desk. This was for the headset I wear while I'm on the phone during the day, which came with far too short a cord to be of any use. This extension cable works perfectly and it won't become disconnected easily, which is a huge plus for me!  As always, if something changes, I'll post an addendum here.

title: Nice Tripod
text:
I have two of these now. This one specifically for my iPhone and the one I purchased for my digital camera. This one is the better tripod. It isn't heavy, but is heavier than the others I've owned. When you set it, you can forget worrying about it. Once you have it balanced, it will stay that way, so no worries about it and the iPhone taking a half gainer off the desk (yes, I've had that happen). It is STABLE, which is something that isn't asked in the questions on top of this review. Sturdiness only counts for part of the equation. The rest is, while it is sturdy is it stable as well. And the answer is yes. So far I've only taken a few pictures with this tripod, but I'm clumsy, a real klutz. If I haven 't been able to knock it over, I'd have to say it would work perfectly for most of you.

It is lightweight, easy to pack in my travel case (which was one of the concerns and I noted the size before I ordered. Overall, just starting out with the tripod, I'm pleased. As always, if something comes up that is a problem, I'll be happy to amend this review.

title: My second, and best, light box
text:
I purchased this on the recommendation of someone who does a lot of miniature photography. I love it. It was easy to put together, there were no missing or broken parts. And it was easy to set up (remembering that I'm not overly 'mechanical' when it comes to anything I have to plug in or set up and plug in. This was put together well enough that I didn't have to hesitate and wonder what to do next. The instructions were as clear as any instructions could be (that does NOT mean I can follow them, but in this case I did).

I've only taken pictures so far with my iPhone and not my camera, although I have tripods for both. I set it up on a 2X4 table in my work room so that I had room to put items to be photographed beside it, rather than reaching anywhere else, and it works fine (and stays together, which is what my first one did not do).

Color me very pleased, and as always if I see a problem with it, I will write an amendment to this review.

title: NOT the five pack
text:
UPDATE 4/17/21 I started using two of these, keeping one as a backup, and I'm heartily glad I did. I'm never impressed when something that should work better than the original, just plain doesn't. Out of the three, only one will charge my iPhones now. I don't believe it is the USB end of this, but I know for sure when I plug both iPhones into these cables (or plug the cables into them). nothing happens. Every so often, they'll start the charge, but they will quit for no earthly reason when they've only charged the phones by 10-20%. This, in my world, is not acceptable. I know they weren't expensive, but they had relatively good reviews. I'm here to tell you, unless I got a pack of lemons, they don't deserve the five star reviews they received. And of course, the return window expires about 3 days before they malfunction. Figures.

I didn't order a five pack and didn't receive one. I ordered the three pack and received the correct item. These are far more sturdy than the cords that come with the iPhone. I have two iPhones that I use in my office, and have run through more charging cords than I want to admit to. These are not only far better in quality, they are also longer in length than the standard charging cord, which saves a lot of wear and tear all by itself. Loving these, and highly recommend them!

title: Works like a charm
text:
The backstory to this review is this. I purchased a computer that did not have a built in wifi adapter. No sweat, I thought, and the company I bought the computer from threw in a couple of them. I should have known there was a reason for that. The first one didn't work at all and the second one worked for a day.

Enter the great AMZ and this wifi adapter. This was smaller by almost half to the other two, which made me a little nervous wondering why. I mean size isn't everything, until you're doing comparisons, lol. I plug it in this past Saturday, viola! It works. So I shut it all down, and reboot on Sunday (which is when the others failed), and lo and behold, the little green light on this thing is going to town and there are no breaks in the signals.

For the price, this is one of the best buys I've ever made on Amazon. The other two wifi adapters were retailing at twice the money. Color me pleased, and the fact that I can write this review on my desktop should tell you that its still working!

title: It works
text: It is a little hard to keep everything connected. I was expecting a little less room between the connections, but it works. It just doesn't look very good.

title: Works very well until it doesn't
text:
Update: This stopped working completely on the second day I used it. Luckily I had another and used it instead. I know I could have returned it. Instead it ended up going out in the garbage. It had the strongest signal of any adapter I've used, but only lasted about two days. Disappointing.

I bought a new computer and it was shipped with a wifi adapter that did not work. I have very strong wifi here and the original adapter just sat there looking pretty. Not what you want a wifi adapter to do. So I came to Amazon and looked at the choices, of which there are hundreds, I swear. I chose this one for a combination of price, reviews, and looks. I'm very pleased with this. My wifi signal is strong and steady. I'm not sure it would be strong enough for gaming, I don't do that. But I DO use my computer all day every day and am online for the better part of 8 hours each day. Color me very pleased with the way this works. As always, if something goes wrong and this begins to be a wonky addition to my peripherals, I'll change my review to reflect that.

title: Working just as I needed it to.
text:
I don't have a lot to say about this, since it met every one of my expectations right out of the box. It needed no software, it was plug n play, it has enough room for all of my 15 years of photos (and believe me, I needed this space). Overall this operates just as it is described, and has saved me a lot of fumbling with flash drives that the pics were stored on previously. Now, my flash drives are filled with what they should have been filled with - work. And my pictures are in a safe and backed up place. I'm pleased.

And as an edit and update here. My last portable drive like this has about a quarter of the room of this one, and has no way of the user telling when it is being accessed. This Toshiba External Hard Drive, is complete with a blue light that blinks (helpful to me especially as I may have 3-4 flash drives attached as well as this). But most important, the size is wonderful. And we all know, size really DOES matter. :-)

title: Color me very pleased
text:
First, after reading all the negative reviews (along with the positive), I'd decided that if they arrived in anything other than perfect condition, they would be returned. Well, surprise. They arrived in fine shape. I got them out of the packaging, hooked up my iPod and got on the treadmill. The sound was really, really good with these, considering the price. They adjust well, and their noise cancellation is spot on. I didn't expect them to be perfect with noise cancellation because of the price and quality.

The one thing I can see that would be a deterrent to these is that you HAVE to handle these carefully. You cannot be rough when adjusting, you can't toss them down on hard surfaces. In other words, you have to take care of these headphones, just like they cost 10 or 20 times more. I'm very pleased as I need lightweight phones, not bulky ones, when I work out and when I'm just listening for pleasure.

title: A basic mouse
text:
I read over the reviews here and I'm here to tell you that if I can pay less than $10 for a mouse, I will not complain if it only lasts a year. Or even six months. I've spent upwards of $50 on computer mice that have lasted for fewer months.

All that said, there is one reason I bought it. Amazon stands behind it and it is BASIC. That is all I needed. This isn't for gaming, so no need to spend all that money. I use it for word processing and editing. I use it for online activities. Nothing crucial and nothing that is heavy use. My hand doesn't stay on it, so whether it is ergonomic or not, really doesn't matter to me. I type, then I stop and use the mouse, then I type again. You should always, when purchasing online, read everything carefully, then consider how you will use the item. If you have a large hand, this mouse probably will not be comfortable for you to use constantly. It is small. But then, the description tells you that. If you are looking for a mouse that is functional, doesn't cost a lot, you aren't using it for gaming, and you can lighten your touch, then this is for you. It isn't going to withstand rough usage. This is perfect for me and a lot of other users.

title: Perfect Basic Keyboard and Mouse
text:
One of the big reasons I will always head to Amazon Basics first is that Amazon will stand behind the items. Today, the mouse and keyboard arrived and I was very disappointed to see that the mouse was not in one piece. The keyboard was in great shape but the mouse was broken into three pieces. Five minutes in chat, mouse is refunded, another is ordered, and I'm happy.

These are basic items, just as the name implies. If you are looking for a specific keyboard, or a specific size mouse, don't order these and then complain. The mouse is compact and the keyboard is not a large one. But they both function the way they are supposed to. On top of that, you have Amazon behind them, so if there's a problem, hit that chat button and take care of it. This is the second keyboard and mouse combo I've purchased from them, and I'll do it again. I'm hard on both and these last just as long as other keyboard/mouse combos that are twice as much.

title: Replacement headset
text:
I bought this as a replacement headset for my Dragon software. The first headset, and the one that came with the software, disintegrated when I put it on last week. It seems that everything fell apart at once. This one is a bit different style so I am hopeful it will work out. A couple of things I noticed though. I tend to wear the ear piece high on my ear, but that means the microphone dips too far down. So I've made the headpiece a little larger, moved the earpiece down a bit and it puts the microphone just where it needs to be. The other thing is that the microphone bar, I guess you could call it, is very loose. It only has one position and cannot be adjusted. This doesn't bother me too much, but I realized it might bother other purchasers, so I wanted to make sure I mentioned it.

Overall, it appears to be working well.

title: I love this camera
text:
My Panasonic TZ5 was purchased from Amazon 4 years ago, and I just realized it is no longer showing in my purchase list and I never reviewed it. But it wasn't because it failed as a camera, it just took me longer than I thought to go through all of the different functions.

This camera has gone to Europe, Alaska, and South Africa with me. While it wasn't the only camera I took, it was the only still camera I took. The zoom was phenomenal and the only real complaint I had during any of those trips was that the battery life isn't all that great if you decide to take video with it, which I did at least 2-3 times a day. I didn't really research batteries, which I now regret, so I ended up with three of the normal, standard equipment batteries. While they do well for travel, and I was able to recharge them each night, I wish I'd done my homework and gotten the longer-life, more powerful batteries for the trips.

But what do I really use it for? Jewelry photography. I use a miniature light box with this camera. I mostly shoot earrings and other small items. Occasionally, I'll be photographing necklaces or bracelets, but earrings were always a challenge, and this camera stepped up. With the zoom on this being so wonderful, I'm able to sit at my desk, with the light box in front of me, and use the zoom without having to worry about anything. It is truly point and shoot with jewelry.

Overall, while I'm not a technophile at all, and wouldn't be able to quote you the stats for this camera, I can tell you that in four years, it has caused me no problems, has taken tens of thousands of still pictures and at least 500 videos of varying lengths (none under 1 minute), and it is still my go to camera whenever I need one. I'm shopping for another now, so that I will be able to pack one away in my travel gear and know that I'll be ready with the camera whenever I head out.

title: Solid battery replacement for a traveling laptop
text: This has now been on my traveling laptop for 3 years and it still holds the charge and recharges effectively and quickly.  That contrasts to the original battery and the first replacement both of which only lasted about six month each. This laptop doesn't get used often, so it spends 2-3 weeks at a time shut down.  This is the only battery I've had on it that will boot up with no prior recharging necessary after that length of time.

title: Good performance for the price
text:
I go through headsets very quickly and was tired of spending way too much money on them and having them be destroyed in the various ways I managed to destroy them. This set is ok. I wouldn't give it five stars most probably because they could be a bit larger around the ears. They aren't too small for me, but they don't fit perfectly either. I use these for dictation software and was aware that I needed to use the front plugs on my computer and not the USB when I purchased these. That was fine with me. I also found, in a pinch, they will work with my little Ipod Shuffle when I'm out walking. It doesn't bother me that there is a cord hanging.

The Microphone picks up everything I need it to, with only a little background noise. Since background noise is a problem with dictation software, I was pleased that the TV wasn't picked up by the microphone. Although the microphone appears to be nowhere near my mouth, I bent it slightly so that the end is pointing towards my lips and it works fine on distinguishing words.

Over all I'm pleased. If this breaks, and I know it will because I always manage to run my office chair over them, or set my briefcase down on top of them, or sit on them, I will buy another pair from Cyber Acoustics.

title: It performs very well, and for the price, how can you go wrong.
text:
I ordered this mainly because this was the only one I could find that was tall and would stand on the desk, rather than hook to a monitor or computer. I would have given this five stars if it had a stronger suction cup. It doesn't stick well to surfaces, although I've found if I damped the suction cup with a little water, it appears to work better. I tried it out last night, as soon as it arrived, and it works very well. The picture is clear, the resolution is fine. It didn't need any color adjustment and that alone makes me a happy camper. Nothing worse than Skype conferences with red faces.

Overall, for the price you can't go wrong. I've spent up to four times more for other web cams that didn't work very well at all, so color me very happy to have ordered this.

title: Do Not Buy. That's all I have to say
text: Received this yesterday and was very excited to see it in the mailbox, since my webcam had decided to stop working and I was relying on the built in cam on my laptop, which is terrible resolution.  This camera will not/cannot be clipped to either the screen on my laptop OR the flat screen I use for a secondary monitor.  Neither is WIDE enough for the clip to hang onto and the camera won't adjust up and down to fix the way it hangs down when the clip won't hold on.  But not wanting to completely give up, I tried the camera on Skype anyway. Horrible.  Even with a half hour or trying to adjust, my face is still red, the background is still orange, and now I've packed it up only to discover IT CAN'T BE RETURNED, as per Amazon. So I'm stuck with exactly what I paid for, a cheap webcam and now I've learned my lesson and will NEVER forget that you get what you pay for.

title: A little bit slow on response to the remote, but all in all a good deal!
text: I ordered this as a replacement for a unit that finally just stopped working. Same make and model and since the first one lasted for a few years, I thought I'd replace it.  It isn't exactly the same, in that it works slower than my other unit did.  By that I mean that everything seems to take a second or two longer to react.  When ejecting a DVD, when it turns on, when I hit the play button - everything seems to be slower.  Unfortunately, the other unit won't turn on, so I can't compare them side by side. It works fine, it was easy to hook up, all the cables I needed were there. It turns on, plays well, the buttons on the remote all work well.  I can't really say too much negative about it. I'm pleased that it works as well as it does for a refurbished unit and the only thing I can complain about, if you could call it a complaint, is the slowness in the response of the unit to the remote.

title: Studio is for small items - jewelry, miniatures, and I love it!
text:
Read the description well and you will see that this is for very small items, which suits me fine since I bought it to photograph jewelry and other tiny things that I make.

First, you HAVE to look at the pictures in the directions in order to set this up and tear it down without damaging it. The snaps on the side are plastic, as are the walls, and it takes a gentle hand to put it together without damaging it. It took me a second to realize that if you force any of the parts of this, something's gonna break. So now, I managed to put it together and discovered the backdrops, and for just that one reason, this got five stars. I have no idea who out there in Amazon-land takes pictures of jewelry or small items, but getting the background to blend or contrast well with the subject is very difficult when you don't have a lot of choices. This comes with backdrops of black, white, green, and red. I took pictures with a couple of the colors because I was so pleased at the way they turned out. I use a tiny tripod and a digital camera to take my pictures, and this is a very good height to work with the small tripod. The pendant drop in the first picture is about 1-1/2" long and photographed wonderfully in this studio. I'm sold, and would definitely buy again, and would recommend it for anyone taking pictures of miniatures of any kind.

title: Functional and quiet, the two things I wanted in this keyboard
text: I purchased this to use with my laptop when I'm in a situation where silence is necessary.  It takes a bit of getting used to, as a couple of the keys aren't in the same place as I'm used to finding them, and just today, two of the keys on the left the Q and W stopped working for a time. They're working again now, but I'm wondering when they'll stop and I'll have to send the keyboard back.  For now, it is working fine and doing exactly what I wanted it to do.

title: My new Kindle Fire 10 with Alexa
text:
July 27, 2018 - update. To preface, let me say that my previous Fire tablet was with me for just under 5 years, is still working fine except that it doesn't hold a charge as well as it used to (which is why I went with a new one). This tablet I've had since February so we're talking 5 MONTHS instead of years. As of today, the screen is cracked. Since I don't carry it with me the way I used to carry the previous one, and since the case I have this one in is sturdier than the previous case, and since, to the best of my knowledge, this hasn't been dropped, I'm not pleased. I'm thinking this probably arrived this way, since the crack can only be seen when it is a just the right angle to a bright light. Of course, it won't be covered under the "limited" (that should read VERY limited) warranty, and apparently, I failed to buy the protection plan because I was thinking this was as well built as my previous Kindle. Wrong on all counts. So I will say that it just went down to a 3 star review, partly for the company and not just the Kindle. For all the trouble I had with the books and being able to read books I'd purchased, this was the last thing I expected to happen. If I buy another reader, since I've already figured out I don't like Amazon knowing everything I do through Alexa, it won't be a Kindle.

February 2018 - I just received my new Fire 10 last week. I am moving from my old Fire 8.9, because the battery had decided not to keep a charge, and I was lucky to get 2 hours out of it at one time. Terrible for traveling or using it where there wasn't a plug in available.

I had an unholy amount of problems with the Kindle books on my Fire 10. First once all 1300 books were downloaded, an awful lot of them, at least 20% were unreadable, because of a DRM error. Kindle support did a fine job of straightening that out, although it cost me about 2 hours on chat before it was completed. Then, some books didn't download when they should have so it took what seemed like two days to get them all organized and downloaded. But finally that was straight.

My next problem was with Alexa, whose answer to me is normally, I'm sorry I don't understand. But if the television is on, she apparently can understand the Olympic announcers because she responds to them right away. Because she responds to other voices, once at a restaurant this week, I have to turn her off when we're in public. Obviously, she's far too friendly with strangers. I had heard that this would be a problem, just didn't think it was going to be mine.

I am not a technophile, I can only tell you as an average person using this Fire tablet for all sorts of activities during the day, that it is functional, quick, and works very well with the apps I have loaded. I use my Fire far more that I'll ever use my phone for reading, purchasing, browsing, so I'm very pleased with how it operates. I like the size of the screen, I like the weight. I did not buy Amazon's cover for it, which I'm finding might have been a mistake, but I'll deal with that after the tablet and I have bonded. I can honestly say that when my 8.9 new it didn't work this quickly, so color me pleased.

title: Fire 10 Cover
text:
I bought the blue cover for my new Fire 10 and it is quite nice. My only problem is that because of the way it is built, it puts the on/off button in the wrong place and doesn't protect it from roaming fingers. I like to hold my Kindle and because this doesn't protect the on/off, I am tending to put it to sleep a lot more than I was my Fire 8, whose case fit the same way, but was built up around the button so that it couldn't be accidentally touched.

Otherwise, it stands up well, I like the color, and have no complaints.

title: Perfect for laptop integration
text: I purchased this because the USB ports on my laptop are too close together for me to plug anything more than one USB drive at a time. This is perfect. It is small enough that it fits wherever me and the laptop happen to be.  And I can put my 3 USB Drives in all at once and know that I can access them worry free.  I'm very pleased, especially with the size.  I have other USB hubs which will work on my laptop, but they are larger than this and can't be comfortably used with the laptop and I are traveling.

title: Tight suction mount with adjustable arm
text: I received this today and am super pleased so far.  I tried it first in my car with my handheld GPS, using the smaller adapter that comes with it. I was impressed with the amount of suction it had (I've used some products like it that won't hold at all). It worked like a charm, but since I don't own a Go Pro, I had to borrow my friend's (with a promise to give it back, lol). With the Go Pro I was able to maneuver the arm around to put the camera at different angles. The entire time I played with it the suction held.  I will be curious to see if it will hold that well in extreme temperatures, both hot and cold, but for now, it is firmly attached to my dash and for the price, this was a GREAT deal.  Don't hesitate to try it out! I don't think you will be disappointed.

title: Great tripod for the money!
text: I love this tripod.  For the money, this is the best deal I could have gotten.  It is the perfect height, easily bent into whatever shape I want and whatever length I need. Its very stable. My camera, a Panasomic Lumix fits perfectly and firmly onto the top of the tripod and any adjustments made after the camera is attached are easy to do.

title: Not expensive, yet very satisfactory
text: I ordered these because of the reviews they'd received regarding the sizing and the sound.  All of the good reviews are right on. title: Sound very thin and tinny compared to the Air Pods Pro I lost and tried to replace with this
text:
I read a review that got 300+ 'helpful' votes for this item that said that the sound specifications exceeded that of even the Air Pods Pro, which incentivized me to buy this, along with the fact that it stays in the ear better. (However there are attachments for pretty low cost you can get for Apple Air Pod pros that provide the same little hook piece that slips under a ridge in the ear to hold it in place like the Beats Fit Pro has).

Using the Beats Fit Pro with iPhone 13 Pro Max, running the latest iOS as of this writing, 15.3.1... I can say definitively and on no uncertain terms, that the sound was blatantly and immediately noticeable as having high treble, low base; a distinctly and irritable inescapable lack of fullness, or 'thin and tinny' sound, that I have since read others reported online as well. And adjusting the Music App EQ (e.g. going to the iPhone Music app settings and adjusting the equalizer to add more bass) didn't do much to give it the rich full sound I get with Apples Air Pods and Air Pods Pro.

After losing my Air Pods Pro, I had to use my Air Pods (which don't stay in my ears well enough), prior to getting the Beats Fit Pro I'm reviewing here, and even Apple's cheaper Air Pods (non-pro) sounds WAY better than the Beats Pro Fit do.

The Beats Pro Fit boasts apple's H1 chip which is suggestive of higher compatibility with iOS devices, allowing things like Siri (although I never tried that), but somehow the H1 chip doesn't seem to translate to high quality sound, and sound quality is the primary thing I expect from ear buds, followed by secure comfortable fit, and then all the other usability conveniences.

text:

Setting TV at lowest height it's perfect from viewing from a couch(es), but can easily swing the TV around and away to let both couches and watch it at once if guests come over.

Can get it out of the way when needed to open space up or move away from windows.

Without this I'd have to deal with the awkward locations and limitation I'd have if I mounted the TV on the wall. A flip-down ceiling mount might be a good alternative EXCEPT e *those* don't generally swivel so wouldn't have the flexible viewing options this offers.

Plus, when sitting down I can look under the TV and see my cat on the other couch and so it's just cozy. Flexible bit of equipment. Not exactly artistic or a piece of furniture but it's clean and simple and well painted with a perfect black satin finish so it's pretty unobtrusive, weird as it is. I'm used to how it looks. Sure nice when watching TV.

Note: I able to avoid installing the tray in the middle that makes it ugly, by simply strapping up an Apple TV (small 4" x 4" x 1" unit) on the back, with a small power strip (really light duty one that isn't bulky). So I have one cable running up the back and the TV and Apple TV plug into that small power adapter. Whalla, no need for the ugly tray attachment!

Using one of those tiny Internet TV boxes (in my case the Apple TV) this way is really really practical because most of the smart Internet TV devices like Apple TV, Amazon Fire TV, probably Roku and others offer a huge range of content from a WiFi connection, so I don't even need a cable box anymore. Just an Internet modem, a WiFi router, and an Apple TV (or the other brands as noted).

What I like about this keyboard, is it has a beautiful backlight, nice key placements and the keys are slightly curved so the fingers really register and it's easy and fast to type on. title: This is a pretty nice little keyboard to type on.
text: I ordered mine with Cherry MX Speed Silver keys with the higher activataion point. Because the silver keys register the keystroke earlier in the keypress, it allows me to slip two 40A-R - 0.4mm blue O-Rings onto each keycap, and still get reliable activation on each key. That makes it very quiet and a super light touch, and that allows me to type fast because hardly any pressure or finger movement is required. Some people have said they have too many false key activations when they configured them thin and light with double O-Rings, and I've only been using it for a few minutes and that's not really happening for me. It did, but I believe it will quickly train someone to be a more accurate typist. I think this is the fast keyboard I've been waiting for all my life. It blends in, small, discreet.  For UNIX programmers used to vi, the jkli keys doubling as arrows is intuitive and easy. I don't like having to borrow a finger on the same hand that uses the arrows to hit the FN key that putts those letters into arrow mode, so I will probably reprogram the left CAPSLOCK key to be an FN key and use the right-side CTRL key as the capslock key. But otherwise really sweet.

So I guess the OLED material loses some % of its brightness over time. Wouldn't be noticed probably unless against brighter pixels. I wish I'd known this. https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B074FR4B7H/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o05_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

This combination sounds really good when streaming my iTunes library from iPhone X (it sounded even better when I downloaded the free VOX app with *equalizer* to lower the highest frequencies a tad and raise the mid bass slightly. The speakers have good bass and really crisp treble so the EQ smoothes it out and makes it richer without being shrill). I just now tested them on the table but it really sounded great! I can tell, it is going to be amazing in a 6' x 8' sauna. I have a small Bose bluetooth player, which is phenomenal, given its tiny size is amazing, but still the bass can't approach like this. It sounds good but couldn't saturate the room fully and as deeply as this obviously will.

It took me awhile to figure out what to get for a sauna, weatherproof/water proof obviously, and low to the ground (the lower 2ft of the sauna are much cooler than the warm spot). I first got Polk Audio ceiling mount speakers and built an enclosure and they sounded really bad, but then they advertised self as better for theatre and not higest fidelity, I found out later.

title: Simple, solid, reliable, minimalist. Rental independence. Great. I love it.
text:
WARNING: THIS IS A LONG REVIEW, BUT I MAY HAVE SOME ANGLES ON THIS OTHERS DON'T :-)

Wow. I really like this modem. This is a barebones rock solid dead simple workhorse.

It's got a plug for the cable and one ethernet (RJ-45) port out and I think an on/off switch.
That's it. It makes a connection. And hasn't failed since I got it a month or so ago.

All I had to do was call my ISP and give them the MAC address (on the sticker on the device)
and they updated their tables and that was it. Turn it on. It goes through the startup cycle. Takes a few minutes to connect like they all do and that's it. Set it and forget it.

What prompted me to get it, is I don't like having to rent the modem from the ISP @ $10.00/mo forever. This literally pays for itself in 16 months, and most people will have their Internet connection for many times that long, and time flies. So it's a good investment.

It doesn't have phone connection like the ISP's modem did. So I called the company/provider that owns copper phone lines in the area and ordered landline service. I'm a nerd/techie and don't care what people say about landlines being for old fogeys, it's like having a backup generator ... I know I can use that landline if the power goes out or if the cell tower gets overwhelmed (too many calls or cell traffic at once), or there's radio interference in the area. Technically cable phone is a 'land line' (hardwired cable connection to provider) and the battery backup in the modem (which the ISP charges more for), could give you emergency phone service in an outage, but a cable phone connection can (and does) fail for more reasons than copper wire phone service does. (Those copper wire connections are called POTS - which stands for Plain Old Telephone Service), and copper wire phones are the most reliable.

Having a separate modem from a router is optima for a few of reasons... Generally hybrid units of anything do everything okay, but nothing optimally (for example combination modem-router units like my ISP rents out). Better to keep the modem separate from the router. Then you can swap either out independently to upgrade as needed, disrupting less of your own network configuration doing so, and also help avoid a single point of failure. Plus, you might be able to score a router in a pinch on shorter notice than a cable modem if the router is the component that fails. Then you can choose the router you actually like, for whatever reason, and don't have to settle for whatever bundling du jour your ISP decides is right for you (even if it isn't).

That gets me to the other point. What DID the ISP decide was right for me (but wasn't)?

For awhile my ISP modem connection was dropping briefly in the middle of the morning. My computer came back up connected to the ISP's 'general public' wi-fi connection to their router which did not work for me and I'd have to keep manually switching back to my own internal Wi-Fi LAN (network). That was not only inconvenient but it forced me to investigate was was going on there.

I learned my ISP gives lets passersby connect to their rental-modem's Wi-Fi signal, without giving me any way to disable that service! That really pissed me off to learn. The idea is that people driving around who have accounts with the provider can get internet access around the neighborhoods. If I was a passerby, that could really help me, so at first glance maybe 'why not, be a good samaritan'.

But wait! There may be more too it than that.

Besides the fact that I don't like it (for good reason), they give me no control over that 'feature'!
And I see some downsides. What's good for the ISP isn't necessarily optimal for me.

What I don't like about that 'service' is that one or more people could sit outside and suck down bandwidth (e.g. slow my connection down), unbeknownst to me. It also might cause the unit to use more energy and put out a stronger wi-fi signal than it needs to. Which health conscious people are well advised to be aware of. Wi-Fi is radiation. Not strong and may not ruin your life, but it is a stressor at a cellular level, this is known. And strong signals, persistent signals and people who are more sensitive or have immunity issues can be more vulnerable (headaches, sleep disruption, or worse). But I like Wi-Fi so I settle for whatever unknown health consequences I may not be aware of.

Also it makes me wonder if a hacker might be able to use it as an additional point of access to my home network.

I also wonder if it's 100% clear to law enforcement at first glance who might be visiting sites or doing something nefarious from the connection point. Might it look like the owner is doing something that a passerby did (and even if they can sort it out later, what if it takes awhile to figure out and they make a bad assumption?)

Anyway, I don't have that problem with this modem and I'm just much happier with it all the way around.

Plus it's blazingly fast.

Prolific is the actual manufacturer the PL-2303 chip, and provider of the device drivers to the derivative product vendors. The driver I initially downloaded from the UGREEN t site I got was not up-to-date and didn't work (it's possible I didn't grab the one I thought I did or misread something - they might have had the latest somewhere).

However, going to Prolific's site is ideal because they will always have the most recent version. The PL-2303 is an industry standard chip - the heart of many of the popular USB to Serial adapters; it has been around for years. The driver from Prolific's site worked instantly w/o a glitch.

title: light but sturdy
text:
I do real estate photography. I first purchased the slik sprint but it was way to light and flimsy - I was afraid to leave my camera on it unattended for even a moment for fear it would tip over- I returned that one and bought the pro 700 - the pro 700 was really nice and sturdy but was too stiff and bulky for my needs - if I was doing studio work or if I was going to be using the tripod in a way were I had it set up in a stationary position it would have been perfect - but for moving around room to room - getting in tight corners and having to constantly be adjusted - the 700 wasn't a good fit, so I returned it and got the SLIK PRO AL-324-3W Aluminum Tripod Kit with SH-747.

The AL-324-3W is between the sprint and the pro - it is light weight but not flimsy - its easy to adjust and has three bubbles to help get everything level and small enough to get into tight corners - I can turn my back on it and leave it without fear of it tipping over or get knocked over (easily)

The biggest drawback on this model is the price. This tripod is extremely overpriced at 149.00 it should be maybe 85.00. The 700 pro was more expensive at 189.00 however it felt like an expensive tripod and seemed like a better value.

quite frankly - if I had time to continue shopping I would probably return the PRO AL-324-3W because I feel certain that there is a tripod out there of equal quality for half the price or less - I have other studio tripods that I paid much less for that are higher quality however this one fits my needs and I'm in a time crunch so I will keep it because other than being WAY over priced it is a nice tripod.

It does come with a light nylon carrying bag - it isn't mentioned in the description because it doesn't amount to much .

title: (not really) Good enough for the price after all
text:
Two week update: I took away a star because I found something that goes way beyond annoying... The low battery warning. Instead of just fading away, or beeping once, and maybe sending a signal to the device it's linked to, it beeps. The beep is MUCH louder than the volume I listen to at night... And it doesn't stop. Just keeps going, every few seconds.

Due to the problems it has with the sensitivity (or lack) of the volume, I placed the speaker a good distance from my bed. When the battery started dying, it obviously woke me, and by the time I got up, turned off the speaker, convinced my dogs that the beeping did not indicate an intruder in the house, and their barking was not helpful, then crawled back into bed... I couldn't fall asleep again.

If you have trouble sleeping, find a speaker you can use while it charges, or one that at least has a power meter, so that you're not jolted awake.

I am reasonably pleased with this little speaker. The sound is aggressively average in quality. The bass is (obviously) the weak point, and the volume goes from a little too loud for nights (or most business offices), to "please go get my hearing aid" near silence. The sound gets a little tinny when you go louder, for whole room sound.

The battery life isn't too bad. I've only had this a few days, so I can't say anything regarding longevity for the time it holds a charge.

I do appreciate the little travel case it came with. The tennis ball color is horrifying, and the dogs think it's a toy, but it does protect the speaker.

Hopefully newer versions of this will have a more discreet power indicator, or none at all. The blue light is VERY bright.

title: Incredibly happy with purchase (tests prove it!)
text:
I selected this specific micro to usb type-c adapter because it is gold plated. Gold is highly conductive and whenever adapters are introduced into a circuit, there is a negative impact on performance (in this case charging rate). In order to reduce a main cause of this problem, gold can be used to reduce the impact.

Using an android battery charge monitoring app, I was able to prove that using this adapter caused little to no difference in the rate of charge. I was still able to reach and maintain charging rates as if this adapter was not connected at all.

Also, all 5 of my adapters work and still work till this day (8 months later) including the wear and tear of putting on a micro cable and pulling it off, especially when I was testing for bad cables. This thing held up the whole time (over 50 cables tested)!

I wanted an adapter because I have so many USB micro cables collected over the years. I literally could not bring myself to buy USB type-C cables just because I bought my first USB type-C charging phone. I am glad to say after all this time, I have still not a single USB type-C cable as I use these adapters instead.

title: Not charging at Quick Charge rates
text:
This product is supposed to have USB Quick Charge 3.0 ports. I use battery monitoring apps and am quite familiar with when a port is delivering quick charge speeds and when they are not. These USB ports do not at all perform at Quick Charge speeds.

In fact, they are charging at 50% less. I'm quite disappointed because I had hoped that these were not going to fail. To be clear, I am using the Samsung charging cable that comes with my Samsung devices along with those battery monitoring apps I spoke of earlier. There are many things that do charge at the Quick Charge rates as proved out by these battery monitoring apps, so it is not my device, charging cable or battery monitoring apps at fault. To be clear, I give every object I'm testing as much chance as possible to charge at full rates by completely eliminating all unnecessary apps from running before I connect into the device I'm going to test.

So if your reason for purchasing this device was because of the USB Quick Charge support, look elsewhere. This is not the device for you.

title: Archer C9 router isn't as good on paper as it looks.
text:
Got this to manage the wireless network of a family member. I'm disappointed by limitations which I describe below. After all of it, I still kept the router for it's intended purpose as I got it to work, finally.

1. You have to keep checking your configuration after you save, even if you save and reboot. On several occasions and in several different parts of the configuration, I would set a parameter and save, rebooting where necessary, only to find that the change never really got committed to the router. I saw others complain about this and I thought that maybe they just didn't notice they didn't actually hit the "save" button. Well, I can attest that this does happen as it happened to me. Sometimes it would take 3 or 4 attempts to save a parameter before it was finally committed to the router. Weird. Just don't assume you "know for sure I changed it." You have to keep checking to make sure.
2. You can't subnet off of the byte boundary (i.e., subnets other than /8, /16, or /24) without a massive performance hit. WIth nothing else on the wireless at the time, the TV had rasterization problems. For those who are really techie, please note: the 2.4GHz and 5GHz network were moved to empty channels, so no competition for performance from neighbors!
3. For the life of me, I cannot get the DHCP range of IP addresses to be anything other than what the router puts in there by default, no matter how many times I save it and reboot. To me, this is a security problem as will as a network management problem.
4. Buggy. The router worked fine when I configured it in one location. When it was time to move it to another, NOTHING had to change. When I booted the router, TCP connections would not work at all even though ICMP and UDP got through. Nothing in my router's configuration singled out TCP. Reboots did not help. I had to factory reset (full factory reset, not partial) and put in the same exact configuration. After that, TCP worked fine again. Frustrating!
5. I do not see anything about 802.11 AC speeds in the configuration despite this being an AC router (or so I thought). It only went up to 802.11n. Looking back at the Amazon listing, it lists this router as 802.11 A/C. I didn't notice the slash or maybe at the time I thought it was a typo. Now I do not. I have to look up exactly what that means. If I had devices performing at 802.11 AC now or in the future, I would have returned the router. This network is going to be fairly stagnet with the same devices for years to come.
6. I did experience the DNS problems (not resolving) that is well documented in the forums. I knew at the time that there might be a DNS resolving problem and a subnet masking problem. When I experienced the network delays along with the DNS resolver delays, I changed both the DNS configuration and the subnet masking at the same time with the intent to go back to find out which was really at fault for the DNS resolving delays. When I found the performance hit from the subnet masking, it didn't matter if it caused the DNS resolving problem (by introducing network delays on the DNS packets). I just kept the configuration as is. As such, I never went back and reverted my DNS configuration to see if the DNS resolving problem was being caused solely by the DNS configuration. I am done with the stupid problems and at that point, I didn't care just as long as the router was finally doing it's job. If you want to know what I did with the DNS: I put in OpenDNS servers as the resolvers choosing not to use the Telco's DNS resolvers because of bias in return information. When the resolving problem occurred, I simply put the Telco's DNS resolver IP's back in the configuration.

Please note: Do not forget to put in all the available firmware updates. TP-LINK just released the firmware update for the Krack vulnerability. This is a non-starter if you do not put this firmware update in! This is not a ding against the router. Although late, at least TP-Link has patched the worst wireless vulnerability in the world (yes, practically all wireless devices on earth are vulnerable unless you patch.... I'm not exaggerating either! look it up if you don't believe me.)

Other than all that, the router is now performing satisfactorily, but admittedly, the 12 wireless devices being managed are very low traffic shy of 2 streaming devices)

If you intend on using this for dd-wrt or other open source firmware (which will void your warranty), please look up the plausibility of it working. It's well documented that there is a major issue that may cause you to brick your C9 router. As such, I'm keeping this on TP-Link firmware until the warranty period is over. I'll find another router for dd-wrt with less risk.

title: It broke my USB port.
text:
I would not call this case heavy duty. I have ballistic cases on my smart phones and I drop those all the time and all is good. A couple months ago, I accidentally dropped it from 7ft and I'm so used to everything being okay, I never even checked if it didn't work until my friend asked. Those cases are fabulous. Shame they don't make cases anymore.

My point for talking about that case is to compare it to this case. This case is not "heavy duty." Shock absorption is little bit better than no case at all. The real killer problem about this case is that it puts far too much pressure on the USB cable and I figured it out too late (I first suspected a battery problem, but when I realized it was the port itself, the damage had been done). My USB charging port began to fail 7 months after I first starting using my tablet along with this case. My tablet has stopped charging altogether and is currently on it's way to get repaired by Samsung (who, btw, insists that when their devices are purchased, the serial number of that device must go along with the proof of purchase or they will not provide warranty repair. Thank you Amazon for helping me with that!).

Sure, you can cut out the USB port cover (flap), but then it's not protecting the port. When I finally realized that was my problem and cut it off, the USB port stopped working altogether less than 2 months later.

title: Upgraded, but not "better reception"
text:
I don't get this "Upgraded version" comment for having "better reception." I bought this and 3 other antennae to see what best would work in my house. I will post my results later, but wanted to at least let those thinking of purchasing this one know my results. Of the 4, including the old version of the Vansky 50mi Indoor antenna (white), this performed the worst. How bad? by 19 channels less than the best performing one. The other 2 antennae were 7 channels less than the best one meaning both were at least 12 channels better than this model, including the previous Vansky model (in white).

Truthfully, I was surprised by this outcome. All were tested with the same weather conditions on the same date with one tested immediately after another. They were each positioned in the same place. I checked all its connections and I repeated the test 3 times for this antenna and all 3 times, it was 19 channels less.

I am against any compensation via discounts, coupons, or any other cost break for giving reviews. This review is my true experience.

title: This cable is definitely the pits.
text:
My use for this cable was to just get video between my laptop and my 40" TV. I use it for Telework (Telecommuting). I always use Blue Jeans Cable and had an 8 foot Series-FE HDMI cable from BJC that served this purpose exceptionally well. I don't do gaming and I have to have this working all the time, without fail.

This KabelDirekt 15 foot HDMI cable fell flat on it's face. I am no novice when it comes to computers. I thought with all those 5 stars, I'll spend $12 instead of $43.75 to get a new 15 foot HDMI cable. This KabelDirekt purchase was a complete waste.

It would not sync up to the television. I decided to reboot the laptop since this was the cable's first hookup (Note: I NEVER have to reboot my laptop when I use BJC HDMI Cable. If we didn't rearrange the room such that I now needed a 15ft cable, I would have never tried to buy a cable that was not from BJC. It just pained me that I obsoleted my 8 foot BJC Series-FE HDMI cable only because we rearranged the room I use it in).

I did everything I could to make the synchronization stable. EVERYTHING. If the computer slept, I lost synchronization. If the screen saver came on, I lost synchronization. I wasted time and money on this.

Just to double check I wasn't insane, I temporarily moved my laptop closer to the TV so that the BJC 8 foot Series-FE HDMI cable could reach the TV. The KabelDirekt 15 foot HDMI cable was currently plugged in with the TV not able to synchronize with the laptop. I swapped out the 15 foot KabelDirekt cable with the 8 FOOT BJC cable and within the blink of an eye, the laptop was synchronized with the TV. No reboots, no configuration changes. Merely a swap out of HDMI cables.

This KabelDirekt 15 foot cable is on its way to the electric recycling program. I have ordered my BJC 15 Foot Series FE HDMI cable which is now on Amazon and like all the other cables I order from BJC, I know I made the right decision.... I will NEVER stray from BJC again.

title: BJC, has always been my go to cable company!!!
text:
I cannot say enough about Blue Jeans Cable (BJC)!!!! I've always bought off of BJC's web site because I never saw them here on Amazon. A Google hit brought me here, but not after reading what I needed off of the Blue Jeans Cable website.

I had an 8 foot BJC Series-FE that worked fantastic with my laptop hooking up to my 40" TV. I never had problems with it. When the computer went to sleep, so did the TV. When the computer woke up, so did the TV. It has always been spot on. I use it for Telework (Telecommuting), NOT gaming, but real world work. So it has to work perfectly all the time.

We recently rearranged the room that has all my Telework gear and unfortunately, I now need a 15 foot HDMI cable. I hated the fact that I just obsoleted my 8 foot BJC because of room redesign and thought to myself since I don't need it for anything but video, I'll go with a $12 15 foot HDMI cable here on Amazon. My mistake was thinking that this would suffice in any way, shape, or form.

I noticed there was signal syncing problems and I don't resort to rebooting, but this was the first time I hooked up the 15 foot cheapo cable from Amazon and I thought it should then be able to sync up correctly (please note, this is NOT necessary for a BJC!!!). On reboot, the synchronization happened and I was reconfiguring and saving new settings. When I stopped to get a bite to eat, the laptop went into sleep mode. I came back, woke the computer and total fritz on the TV. I tried quite a number of things to get this to work and it failed. It just could not resynchronize.

Without rebooting the laptop, I moved it in towards the TV so I can try my 8 foot BJC Series-FE HDMI cable. I unplug the cheapo cable from Amazon and plugged in the BJC 8 foot HDMI cable and synchronization occurred in the blink of an eye. NO REBOOT NEEDED!!!!! I was using the same configuration on the laptop.

BJC, please forgive me for losing my way. You always blew away the double and triple priced cables in your category and have never failed me. I have found my way back to you and will never stray again!!!!

Oh yeah, instead of saving $28 with the cheapo HDMI cable, I'm out $12 for wasting a single penny on it. Did I mention BJC tests every cable they send you and they send you the test results too? Sooo kewl! Oh, maybe the test results won't be sent if I order through Amazon? I will update this if I get the test results.

Buying a standard BJC 15 Foot Series-FE HDMI cable on Amazon saved me $4 including shipping. Either way, BJC gets the sale and I'm still a happy Amazon shopper.

BJC forever!

title: Don't waste your money.
text:
The irony here is that I bought this to replace a 20 year old surge protector whose opposite end from where the power cable enters the device was getting so hot, the beige plastic was showing burn marks. I thought with all the technological advancements, 6 AC plugs (the same as the old one) and 2 USB ports, I should fit a device or 2 extra on the new one. Nope. These plugs are so close together, even a plug that is just slightly larger than a standard grounded plug will cause an overlap on the plug next to it thereby rendering the neighboring plug unavailable. Despite going from an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip to an 6 AC plug surge protector power strip, I went from being able to fit 5 plugs in the old strip to only being able, in the best configuration possible, to fit 4 plugs.

I was lucky that I had one plug that was a Samsung wall charger with a Samsung USB charger cable. Since I had to lose something, that was the only one I could lose, but still put on the strip. So what? I was not expecting to lose 1 of the 2 USB chargers to accommodate one of the plugs that had to get bumped.

I probably would have gotten over that, but then when I went to test the performance of the USB charging ports, they fell short. With the Samsung manufactured original cable for my S5, this port only charged at 1.15A. To validate it, I took it to several other devices in the house and with the same S5 device, Samsung wall plug and original cable and the same meter, the S5 pulled 1.75A out of both the Samsung wall charger and the 5 port USB charger that I also bought from Amazon (I have a review there, too).

I gave it 2 stars because overall, this is not such a disaster that I would waste my time and money returning it. There are soooo many surge protector power chargers with USB charge ports on Amazon that at least one of them has to be better than this.

title: Rather my Mom loves it!
text:
My mother contacted me because she needed a USB hub. I don't recall how she found out about them, but off I went to research what she needed. I first questioned her on her requirements, then researched the status of USB standards (now version 3.0 is out compared to the last time I needed to look), and then did my market research. I reduced it down to 3 hubs and this one won hands down due to it's compactness, support of old and new USB standard versions, and it looked like it was going to be easy for her to set it up on her own. My Mom, btw, is 75+ years old.

The report back from her was that it was exactly what she needed. She hooked everything up and it all just started working. No fuss at all, she said. I've got to give her a lot of credit for being pretty good with the computer.

The fact that I didn't have to troubleshoot it from 250+ miles away means I give it 5 stars too!

I bought it for her 3 months ago now and she hasn't had any troubles and I hope it stays that way. Belkin's products are reputable for quality and in this case a little ingenuity. Highly recommended!

title: Used to be an apple fanboy. This watch changed that.
text:
Long time Apple fan but this product has definitely turned me away. The watch looks very nice and has some nice functionality but the quality is subpar. A software update cause my battery to stop updating its life about 3 months after i received it. When I originally contacted support I was told that I would have to send the watch in for repair and could potentially have to go weeks without it. I reluctantly agreed but the support agent never sent me the return box. I was frustrated and just said screw it I can deal with it. Big mistake. Fast forward a few months and my watch battery dies (as it had several times since i had no indicator of battery life). Now it wont turn on without going through hours of what seem like endless reboot loops. This persists until it finally stops booting at all. Now all it does is show an apple logo. Tech support informs me this is not something that can be repaired and my watch must be replaced. For $229. So, for a total cost of $629 I can get a functional watch that now costs $300 a year and a half after ordering it. No thanks.

I am currently balls deep in the apple ecosystem (3 apple tvs, macbook, ipad, 2 iphones, etc) but after this debacle I have begun the process of transitioning away. Long story short, get a fitbit charge 2.

I (and my kids) love the fact that the (fully) enclosed iPad Mini is completely detachable with a minimum of fuss. My 8 year old is actually faster at removing it than me so that he can run off and watch movies/play games. I don't have to worry about him bumping/bruising my $300 device because it's encased in a rubber and plastic housing with integrated screen protector. When it's detached from the keyboard, the integrity of the case is not compromised; there is a plastic shield inside the hole where it attaches. Also, the protector is easy to get on and very difficult to remove (this is a good thing).
The keyboard works great and has good battery life. It makes it a joy to type out those long emails that would ordinarily require me to actually get up off the couch and turn on the iMac or drag out the laptop. It's a perfect companion for those road warriors who like to travel light. For the price of doubling the thickness of your iPad Mini in your bag you get the ability to comfortably type out correspondence or write up reports without thumb fatigue.
Quite frankly, the only thing that would make it more awesome is if it came with a palm strap plug to put in the hole on the back when the keyboard is detached.
Key Points:
+ Water resistant
+ Keyboard is detachable
+ Good battery life
+ Rugged
+ Case attaches securely
- No handle plug (can't have everything)

title: This may be the competition for Apple’s Magic Keyboard. (Update: definitely is)
text:
This keyboard and trackpad case is awesome! The keys feel like the keys on my MacBook Pro. The pros against the Apple keyboard is that this cost $89 before tax and shipping, where as Apple’s Magic Keyboard cost $350. Another plus above Apple’s Magic Keyboard is that this has a function row with many additional features with volume and brightness increase and play pause buttons, and home button and lock button. The only downside is that it ships from China and takes a while to get through customs. I enjoy the feel and look of the keyboard. This case has many viewing angles. The hinge is a swivel hinge that allows the iPad to rotate for more viewing angles and for the iPad to lay flat. I have had this product since July 27th and have not had to charge the keyboard since the initial charge (today is August 17th). I enjoy the backlit keyboard. It also has an auto sleep feature for the keyboard that helps it to be energy saving. The trackpad feels better than I expected and has a physical click and digital click that allows for multiple layers click and gestures. The only thing I do not like is that some of the paint or coating has started wearing of in such a short time. Also you have to make sure to pop iPad out by hinge first when pulling it out. If you pop out the iPad from the other end you will break part of the case. This case is so far worth it for the money it cost and definitely a great value in comparison to the Apple Magic Keyboard. It gets 4 stars because it shows signs of wear too quickly in less than a month.

Update: Today is October 16th 2020, I bought this keyboard on July 27th, 2020 and today the keyboard which hadn’t been charged since July 27th just finally said it needs to be charged with a flashing red light. I think this is the best battery life I have ever had on any device. Another update is that the color of device is wearing off around edges but still works fantastic. I added three pics to show this update.

title: What I've always wanted
text:
I have been wanting a product like this for years to replace wires when I exercise. So far in 2 months of owning these headphones I have not been disappointed. They fit well on my head (I saw reviews where people were upset about this). I am not picky about sound as some may be so perhaps a $$$ Bose may suit others but for the price this set is not bothering me.
I have used it for music (jazz, pop, rock) and even radio app, as well as, to via phone chatting.
The only issue I have had is with using my wifi there is a beep and the sound goes in and out. Not sure if this is universal or not but with regular phone (ATT) signal I have no issues on phone or radio app (nobex).
The battery lasts they say 8 hours but for me seems MUCH longer. I should say I have not timed it out. The instructions say to let the battery die completely and to charge 3 times to help battery last longer. In two months and what feels like hours and hours of listening I have only charged it I think twice. There is a beep that occurs when the battery is low.

As far as use goes... these headphones fit fine when I am jumping on my trampoline so if you are concerned about how they would be while running, I would say they work well.
I can go about 20-30 feet before sound goes in and out because of distance. I haven't measured it out but that seems a good estimate.

title: Just what I was looking for!
text:
Got this Logitech Bluetooth adapter after a while and a bit of researching...

I wanted to connect my iPhone and iPad to my receiver in my living room so I could broadcast music throughout my house (I have speaker located in different rooms)
So I decided it came down to three options.

1. [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]]
2. [[ASIN:B004VM1T5S Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices (980-000540)]]
3. [[ASIN:B0015YJOK2 Apple Airport Express MB321LL/A [NEWEST VERSION]]]

______________

Belkin

I got the Belkin Bluetooth Receiver [[ASIN:B0047T79VS Belkin F8Z492-P Bluetooth Music Receiver]] but I had complaints about range. Even though there is a fix (which requires opening it up and removing a metal piece which other reviewers have said is just added to add some weight)the range with the fix still is not up to par. The Sound quality was below par as well.

__________________
Apple Airport Express

The Apple Airport Express is unique in solving my problem as it has one major advantage... It uses the wireless network in my home to stream music to my receiver (not Bluetooth). Awesome idea and I actually ordered one. This way I could be way out of Bluetooth range (i.e. my backyard)and still control music through my iPhone or iPad through the wireless network.
The only problem with this setup (which in the end I refused to deal with) is that you can only use your iPhone or iPad as a REMOTE to control iTunes on a computer. Meaning that you need to have a computer on with the appropriate songs on at all times if you want to listen to music. Being that we have laptops only and there is no consistent computer in the house, let alone "on", and connected to the wireless network.
This could not work for me.
Second problem with this system is that you can only play iTunes. No Pandora or other music venues such as youtube etc.
And to top it all off this Apple Airport express cost $99!!(plus the use of a computer full time)

_______________________
Logitech Wireless Speaker Adapter for Bluetooth Audio Devices

This is very similar to the Belkin but it literally took 2 minutes to hook up and the range that I tested so far is incredible. That being said it is using Bluetooth not Wireless Network so don't expect total wireless connectivity. The Sound quality is on par with the apple but I assume that will degrade with distance to the receiver. Other wise it is perfect.

In summation I am very happy with this product at this price. I would gladly pay $100-$200 for a system like the Apple Airport express that could play all audio from my iPhone or iPad directly and didn't require me to only use my iPhone as a remote for a computer that can only play iTunes on the network.... Until a reasonable system comes out like that I think this product will do the job nicely.

Or if your so inclined you can quickly rack up a few thousand dollars setting up a Sonos System[[ASIN:B005441AJC Sonos Play:3 All-In-One Wireless Music Player With 3 Integrated Speakers (Black, NEW)]]
But My house is already wired with speakers and such and I don't feel it is worth the investment.

title: Great Indoor Antenna, A Few Caveats
text:
There are so many good reviews here about this antenna, I'll try not to repeat what others have said. I do have a few tips to add,

When setting up your antenna, do yourself a favor and tie a string through the two holes at the top of the antenna. That way you can hang it on one tack/nail as you're searching for the best location. Have extra tacks or nails handy, as they will jump out of your hand and become lost in the carpet (until you find them the next day with a bare foot).

Buy some very small nails. I've discovered that I need to move the antenna around to get reception for some channels. Therefore I have a fair number of nails in the wall that look a little strange. Small nails are less visually distracting. If I get very ambitious, I might even paint them.

This antenna really works best on an exterior wall facing the majority of transmitting antennas you are trying to reach. So if you're working with an interior wall facing the wrong direction, it probably won't work very well.

To up the number of channels you receive, consider buying a signal amplifier (I bought the RCA Digital Amplifier here on Amazon.) They cost about $15. I added 10 additional channels by using one.

Finally, how well these indoor antennas work largely depends on where you live and how close you are to the transmitting antennas. To avoid disappointment, do some research online before purchasing anything.The site that helped me the most was disablemycable.com .

title: Nice Boost for Indoor Antennas
text:
I "Cut the cord" and got rid of my satellite service recently, but did miss watching network TV. Consequently, I bought a Mohu Leaf TV antenna. It works well, but I added this amplifier to see if I could pull in more channels.

Short answer: For me, this amplifier works. It added 10 channels to my lineup. There are several caveats: The effectiveness of this amplifier will vary depending on your location and distance from a major city. (I'm about 60 miles from Denver.) My reception does vary depending on the weather, which can be maddening. On a good day, I can get a total of about 40 channels. Many of these channels (almost half) are religious, Spanish and shopping channels that I don't really watch.

Without the amplifier, I get about 30 channels. I have found that moving my Mohu Leaf around on the wall will improve my reception for certain channels. The important thing is to experiment to see what works for you. Check out the excellent resources online for working with an indoor TV antenna. And think of all the money you are saving!

title: Worth the $$$$
text:
I balked at the price of this cover. What persuaded me to cough up the bucks is that this is a dual-use item: cover and book light.

As a cover, this is great. Heavy-duty pebbled leather, similar to that used in some high-priced purses. The bungee cord is handy -- holds the folded cover flat against the back of your kindle. The lining is a sturdy grey suede-like material. Yeah, it's a little heavy -- but high-quality materials tend to weigh a little more.

The light is also well-designed and handy. I like that I don't have to ever think about bringing a book light with me, wherever I go, as long as my kindle is in this cover. Every once in a while I find myself pushing the light down with my finger to get better illumination to the far lower lefthand corner of the screen. It's not quite as bright down there, as others have noted. Ideally, it would be nice if the light head was somewhat flexible instead of rigid.

So, here's how I justify the cost: leather cover: $30, book light: $20, convenience: $10. It's a luxury, but it's worth the $$$$.

title: THE ONLY cable over 25 feet that works with PS4 Pro @ 4k
text:
This review is for the 35 foot length cable.

This is THE ONLY cable over 25 feet I've found that will transmit the PS4 Pro's signal @ 4k. When set to YUV420, the signal is crystal clear, but it does struggle a bit to push the full RGB 4k signal (I start to see "sparkles" / noise artifacts). Keep in mind however, no other cable over 25 feet will even transmit the 4k YUV420 signal.

There are clearly Leprechauns working away inside these cables!

Now, if only they made a 30 foot version...

title: Failed to transmit 4k [30 foot]
text:
My review is for the 30 foot length cable.

Unfortunately, this cable completely failed to transmit anything more than 1080p signals for me. I tested with an Xbox One S and PS4 Pro (both are wired through a Denon x4200w to a JVC RS520 projector -- I tried with the Denon's video conversion option both on and off). The PS4 Pro seems to be the most difficult to find a compatible HDMI cable over 25 feet for, but this is the first cable that I've tried that wouldn't work with the Xbox One S.

Clearly, results vary wildly among different setups, so take this with a grain of salt.
