title: I'm so disappointed but they're still phenomenal
text:
I got these from Best Buy after reading the glowing and praising reviews, assuming these would compliment my heavily-bassed up music (which is easily more than 3/4 of what I have- I'm literally all about that bass). Honestly, they are terrible when I listen to anything pumped with bass (ie Kesha, Die Antwoord, Zedd, etc). I can't explain it, but something about the sound makes me cringe- it's so distorted and just not good.

HOWEVER, I then tried listening to other genres like rap and rock, and oh my god those songs sound FLAWLESS on these headphones. They just compliment each other so well. It's just so unusual because I thought these headphones were going to bring a whole new positive experience to... well.. bass-y music? Instead it sounds like, well, close your eyes and picture sitting in your car at a red light and hearing one of those annoying people pull up beside you who have a terrible quality radio and speakers and all you hear is distorted and muffled "BOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOM BOOOOM BOOOOOOOOOOOM"s. That's legit what these Skullcandys sound like and that's only when the bass booster is at MID POINT. I tried putting it all the way up to the highest setting and it sounded like pure garbage.

I'm not an audiophile, BUT I am obsessed with bass and can tell when it's good or not- and Skullcandy definitely dropped the ball on these. I would highly recommend finding another pair if your most listened to genre is heavy dance/electronic/pop/club, BUT these are breathtaking if you listen to genres or any music in general with minimal bass.

Other positives- SO comfortable (I used to have other Skullcandy Crushers and they gave me head aches), sleek (old ones were bulky and imo ugly), VERY easy to use (literally took seconds to pair and figure out), feels durable and like it's made with high quality materials, and had absolutely no connectivity issues.

Overall I'm giving this a 4/5. I'm extremely sad that I'm returning them but they just aren't for me. I hyped myself up so much only to be let down by distortion and overpowering buzzing thumping. I won't lie or give these 1 star because I'm sorry but that's just ridiculous. These headphones are wonderful, just not quite on the money.

title: Hate to make this update, but I feel that I must
text:
Update: I found out when my old VPN was expiring that this router will not allow you to use a VPN? It must be open sourced, which PIA is, but uncharacteristically, TP-Links just told me yea we can't support a VPN while using this router, and ask the VPN companies- yea. They just shuffled me off. So after a few months, I'm not sure if I've been having a VPN or not. Norton is encrypted, which TP Links says they do not support for this router, but Norton themselves tells me their VPN is working. When I go on VPNtesting dot com, it says I have a dns vulnerability.

I am going to buy a NEW router that PIA says they support. Sorry, I'm into security, and having to forego a VPN just because I have a router is terrible. It's like buying a car without the steering wheel. I'm sticking with this company because the technical support is as good as it gets (given that they made router like this).

The negative reviews almost stopped me from buying- this thing is flawless. Powerful wifi, blazing fast, probably the highest level of consumer security out there, and immediate customer support (via chat) that completely solved my problem.

I"m not smart enough to use commercial grade, but that is my next step. I would recommend this to a friend, and I'm getting one for my mom.

title: DO NOT BUY!
text:
Brutally terrible customer support. Forget a phone line like Norton has. It's email only, and I asked a VERY simple question that could be answered with one word. Instead they send you a link to a BUNCH of other links where you can't find the answer. We went back and forth when they could have just told me the answer. It was like I was asking to copy their homework. Then they stop responding!

I would say it seems like the entire place is run by teenagers, but teenagers are more responsible than this. They are angry and look down upon you if you ask the easiest question. Can you imagine if you ran into trouble? It's advertised as consumer friendly, but it is not. You would need at least 5 years experience in tech to figure this stuff out on your own- that's not an exaggeration, that's from a friend who has had a tech job for 20 years. I have a newfound respect for those who have a professional understanding of tech, and a newfound disappointment for Firewalla.

title: Average User Beware
text:
I’m a person who has a good consumer level knowledge of the internet, computers phones, etc. and this IS the industry leading product, no doubt. I’m not a programmer, but people do come to me with their questions about internet security.

That being said, these are NOT easy for the average user to configure. Could not get it to work with Facebook on my Mac. Gmail did work, and was straightforward. Instagram does not support it on a desktop.

It is a solid piece of security in that it is physical. Google uses the heck out of it in the workplace (I’m around Google workers all the time, I have more friends that work for Google and Facebook than do not), but I’m just saying if you are a person who’s knowledge of technology is at the consumer level, do not expect this to be a breeze. Also, tech support is email only, so you can’t quickly solve something through the phone or even chat. You will be talking to people who expect you to be in the industry, and it felt like a favor when they helped me.

My review will mark me as not a verified purchase, but that is because I bought directly from Yubico.

I’m not sorry I bought it, because I’m a sucker for cool technology, and it does look modern and sleek in my kitchen, but it would be quicker to just sweep the crumbs off a counter with a paper towel. I would say the suction in this product is more of a side effect, or an after thought. If you were a determined ant, and this thing came hovering down upon you, you’d have a fighting chance.

Still, not the worst thing I’ve ever purchased on Amazon. Kinda fun. Barely cracks into the 3 star category (which for me means would recommend to a friend) but it does.

title: Excellent, but don't get the app
text:
I have had these for a day. They are absolutely amazing. Life changing, worth every penny. I have seen a lot of reviews where they were compared to AirPods Pros, but there is no comparison.

I bought them because I have a noisy (but lovable) neighbor. The noise cancellation on these is superior, but not for low, bassy, external sounds, but rather sounds in the higher range.

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.

title: You have to know how to use them.
text:
The first couple of days I had these, I didn't see the big deal. Yes, they fit better than the originals, the fit was an improvement. But you have to know how to use them. I was just putting them in my ears like normal AirPods Pros.

As soon as I pinched the memory foam first, and then wiggled them in my ears - WOW! They sound exactly like over the ear Beats. Heavy, heavy bass. To the people who have these but gave them low ratings, please try this. I feel like the people who are selling these should tell people this in the first sentence. Like AirFoams Pro- pinch the foam first!

No way the original APP can match this Oh, and once I pinched the foam before putting them in, I thought Noise Cancellation was on- it wasn't! When I then turned on NC, they were even better.

However, as far as integration with my Toyota Prius goes ( and there is a very good chance this is Toyota), it is not as easy as the one you use at home. You must be on the right mode- for me it's the bluetooth mode. You won't hear it if you are tuned to am or fm.

It is slower to respond. At home you say Alexa (baby pause) and then your request. In the car, it's Alexa (WAIT) . . . then speak your command. Half the time it dissolves into no response.

As a result, I don't use it as much as I do the ones at home. And in case you think I'm a rookie, I have 4 Echo products in my one bedroom condo. So I recommend it with reservation. I still want it, I don't want to return it, but it needs work, not sure who to blame.

title: Major flaw makes this unusable.
text:
Update: When you find the right product it works well. It has to be a product that doesn’t require an extra step to turn on.

You can’t use it on something that has its own power switch, even if you leave your appliance on.

I have a fan that I would like to be able to start remotely for my pet when it gets hot. If I say “Alexa turn on the fan”, or do it in the app, it will turn the plug on, but not the fan. If I’m at home, and tell Alexa to turn off the fan, it will, and that’s the end of the cycle- nothing I can do until I turn the fan on again myself .

It’s good for people with dumb homes, but I have a smart home.

Also, the only really solid part is the part you screw into the wall, but in terms of the final stretch for the camera, I would consider it tenuous at best. Floppy would be an apt description. Seeing how poorly the first mount went, I had no desire to set it for another camera. It's a disappointment. It does come further off the wall, that is true and helpful, but the very last part of securing an angle in place is a flop.

title: Good to great with limitations.
text:
They're good cameras for the price. They have some advantages over Nest, which is a camera I also have. First of all, no monthly fees. The image are fairly clear with some limitations. They can't detect motion through glass, which is what I bought them for, and subsequently had to get Nest to handle that.

They catch clear pictures, but motion can mess them up a bit to make the images ghost. Also, their idea of night vision is not the same as infrared. A very bright light will capture the images but will also alert an intruder as to the location of the camera. Also, when I leave the cameras armed and I come home, ay, the lights is so darn blinding.

I liked them enough to not return them it's fun to see what my cat is up to. But in terms of actually clearly catching someone, it's slightly limited.

title: Warning for people thinking of purchasing a second Echo
text:
I actually think the Echo is better than two stars, but if I put 5, no one would see this warning, and learn from my mistake. I was excited to receive my second one today. Because I live in a mansion (ha ha) I thought it would be great to not move the one I had around so much. I imagined requesting a song or a book, and then listening to it as I went from one room to another.

Spoiler alert, the Echos do not sync or connect with each other. Whichever is closest picks up on the command, and that's it. In fact, you could have two songs playing at the same time from the different Echoes, in fact, you would never have one song playing simultaneously from both.

I got mine on Prime Day, so since it was half price, I'm going to keep it, but I was disillusioned, and if I knew that they don't sync, I might have thought twice.

title: First impression

I have Blink and this is my first Nest indoor cam. Both serve their purpose. Blink has no supsceiption fee, cloud storage is free, and it has incidental recording.

Nest is always on (unless you turn it off). Nest is more than twice the price, but the quality! Nest is solid, really amazing. It was a little hard for me to position at first (that's what she said), but these things are addictive. It's really nice to be prepared.

title: A little flimsy, one wore out before I had it for a year
text:
They are, for the most part good if not a little flimsy. One of my cameras has worn out after almost a year and the battery is full and it has a wifi signal. When I went to move them around, the arms on two lost their tensile strength. I was unable to find replacement parts.

The camera quality is crisp, hence the 3 stars, but their idea of night vision is to splash a light on the subject. Yes you do see in the night but it is not infra red (not that they advertised it as such).

What I really like is that there is no subscription to the video, however, Nest puts cameras together that are made of a higher quality. So *sigh*, I guess I'll try to repair the blinks I have, but like I say-on the flimsy side.

title: Went out in under a year, was easily replaced under warranty, but you get what you pay for.
text:
It took less than a year but the speaker stopped working. I connected my phone via bluetooth like I do every morning, and it was super quiet. I turned up the volume and I got nothing but static. Then I realized it was not static but the speaker distorting the sound, making it unlistenable.

I do not recommend this speaker. It just doesn't last long enough.

edit: Saw that there is a one year warranty, will contact the manufacturer and see what happens. I will update my review after I see what happens.

[UPDATE]

I contacted the manufacturer and they had awesome customer service. I sent them my receipt along with a picture of the product and they sent me a replacement. It wasn't blue, that model is out of stock, but I got a red one.

Two complaints: The red one costs $10 less than the blue one on Amazon so I feel a little ripped off, but just a little. Second, the replacement still has some issue with static and I feel I can't turn the volume all the way up without some distortion. Maybe it's the music files, I know some are louder than others, so again I only feel a little bad about it.

I love the JAM speaker they make, sounds wonderful with all my music. This one is definitely a step down but it works and sounds better than my phone or laptop's built in speakers. And man their customer service is great, reminds me of my place of business; quick and courteous, and wanting to satisfy the customer.

I am upgrading my rating from 1 star to 3 because of the customer service and the fact that the replacement works. I would have done 4 stars if they had blue to send me, as I said above I feel just a little ripped off. I will keep using it and update if needed.

title: This is a great car stereo
text:
I bought this to replace the factory stereo in my car. It has many good things and very few bad things going for it. First, the good.

It was easy to install and easy to connect to my phone and iPad. When I start my car it automatically connects and starts playing where it left off. It has some cool options like different color lights for the display and buttons and the ability to have them change automatically. It plays CDs great and the radio sounds good. My rear left speaker was sounding bad with my old stereo, like the bass was distorted and it needed replacing, but when I installed this stereo the speaker sounds fine now.

The bad? The screen is very small, I thought it was bigger based on the pictures. Also, you can't have the time displayed AND the song info, something my factory stereo could do. I hate not being able to see the time.

That's it. A good stereo and a good price.

--- UPDATE ---

I figured out how to display the clock on the screen so it never goes away, and I can still see track and other info. I set it up with my phone so when I start my car it connects and autoplays the track my phone is on. It takes a while to download my phone info on to the stereo for calling, but once it's on there I can use the stereo to select numbers to call. The mic works great, no one ever has issues hearing me and I can hear them through the stereo speakers just fine.

I love technology, and this stereo. After 6 months of use the only issue I have is that I could not find an install bracket that fit the stereo for my car, so it's not secure but it is snug and not easily moved around.

title: Wanted to love; frustrating to use!
text:
We wanted to love this, like talk ourselves into tolerating it love this. At its root, it’s a great idea! The case is a nice added feature and the FreeTime program is great. I like that the majority of the content is child friendly, but at the same time, my little ones can download stuff willy nilly, which creates clutter. I do not like the formatting or the controls. We endlessly swipe through apps or have to search it once it’s gone from the Recently Opened tab. There’s no true “home screen” where you have your apps laid out. Instead, it’s very similar to browsing Netflix, which is something I do not want in a tablet. The controls are a joke and some are difficult to navigate. The swipe down controls are always accessible, letting my littles always get into mischief like disconnecting the internet, dimming the screen so low I can’t see it to fix, and turning on the sleep mode color way. There is no way to pin the screen to a specific app (like guided access to keep the tablet on Netflix during a long car ride) and there is no way to create dead zones so controls can’t be messed with. The lock button is small and easily missed being lumped in with all the other buttons. We often find ourselves frustrated with the entire device.

We loved the concept and the warranty behind the device. That is the sole reason we are keeping it. However, it is frustrating to use. We much prefer an iPad where we can hand select content and use features like guided access.

title: Vs. Panasonic: Good Quality, Outstanding Value
text:
Having worn out several Panasonic headsets like this, I decided I'd try a less expensive alternative. Glad I did. The quality is on par with, or better than, the Panasonic versions that I've had (KX-TCA430). Voice quality and volume levels (on both ends) are as good or better.

The mute is a sliding switch. At first I expected to really dislike it as I was used to the Panny's push button. However I find that if you're muting yourself for more than a couple of seconds, the sliding switch is much better. Not having to hold a button in the entire time you're coughing or having a quick side conversation during a conference call is a nice plus.

The only issue, and it's minor, is the tension is a tiny, TINY bit tight on my noggin. That said, I've had LONG conversations with this on and never once thought about it. No pain or discomfort even after extended calls.

Overall, I'm extremely happy with this headset, especially for the price. Time will tell, but based on its construction and appearance, I expect it to last through several years of moderate use. In fact, I think I'll buy at least one more as a backup!

title: It's tiny, very affordable AND surprisingly good...
text:
Bought this mostly for video because of the large aperture, but it's actually very good for photography too. Also have a similar 25mm CCTV for M4/3 lens (NOT from Rainbow Imaging, though likely the same thing) and it vignettes a ton. (Knew it going in; got that one more as a special effects video lens.)

The depth of field on this wide open is extremely shallow, which is likely why most people get it. At 1.7-2.5 or so, the corners are soft, but that's part of its appeal. Stop it down a bit and you've got a versatile little lens. And it is little! Looks like a toy on your EM5, GH2 or GH3, but don't let that—or the low price—stop you. If you're at all interested in anything besides Intelligent(?) Auto, add this to your gear. No, it's not going to perform like a lens that costs $300 or more. But, for the price, you can't go wrong.

Amazon Underground gets me games and apps that would cost actual money from Google and Apple... but for free. It might not be the fastest device or have the best display but this thing is absolutely the best bang for the buck. It is durable and inexpensive and if you are an reader or any sort, you seriously can't afford to not own a Kindle. The Fire is the best value and most diverse in its abilities.

title: The greatest upgrade you can make for an old computer
text:
These are $20 a pop. This is the greatest performance to price upgrade you can make for your old computer.

Although I have been using laptops with SSD's since 2012, I have never exactly purchased one as an upgrade since they came always stock. However, prices have become so low for NAND memory that it is economically feasible to just throw these into all my obsolete computers to give them new life. I popped these in several very old Core 2 Duo laptops that my parents still use and now they run Windows 7 with ease even if they are only running at SATA II speeds. Anyways, 4k random read/write speeds are the most important for OS execution, so the sequential read/write speeds don't have to be the fastest.

You will need to purchase a SATA to USB cable as they do not provide one.

I also recommend that you use Aomei Backupper to clone all your partitions. EaseUS does not work very well with Kingston drives for some reason.

text: I'm really disappointed. First, the software was not included in the box and I could not find it on their website. If you search by model number you only get support documents and such. I found it (on their website) and discovered that the software that I needed is not the software I was looking for. I'm not 100% but I think I'm supposed to be using Power Alert Agent Console??? There is NOTHING that describes what I should be using so this is a complete shot in the dark. Second, I can't get the software to work properly. It doesn't recognize the device and is blank. There is no wizard or "find new device" type thing I can find. So given the software mystery none of this is much of a surprise. This all seems very much in line with the Belkin garbage that went into the landfill a week after I received them. Our power went out the other day and the UPS - a 900va version, which had been plugged in for a week - shut down after 5 minutes. MUCH shorter time than I expected when the only thing plugged into it was a laptop and a monitor. I'm not sure if UPS devices are just not meant for me or these I happen to be buying one piece of junk after another. This entire confusing and dead-end experience confirms the fact that the product managers at Tripp-Lite are stuck in the 1990's and are probably big fans of Microsoft Bob.

title: Not Sure If It Works Or Not
text:
I was hopeful for this product given some of the positive reviews. We're using this in our kitchen to turn on sofit and undercounter lighting when anyone walks in (very cool, btw). We used X10 for years without a problem but really wanted to integrate this into our new SmartHub/Things setup.

Installing any Ecolink product is a little frustrating since the instructions are merely: plug it in and follow your controller manufacturer's instructions for adding a device. Well, the SmartThings hub is brilliant but it takes awhile for any Ecolink device to be found and I usually have to unplug and re-plug them in several times to get it to work. This, however, is simply a BATTERY OPERATED stand-alone device so it's a bit more cryptic so had to pop the battery out a few times to get it to work. I finally got it working after replacing battery with a fresh one. The battery it shipped with was dead.

Behavior. I set this up to turn on the lights and then off when there is no movement. We expected this sensor to have PIR (ON while motion is in the room). Well it does not PIR so it keeps turning the light off at the end of the timer whether there is motion or not. The sensor simply does not sense again for about 5-10 minutes after the original movement. Not sure how to figure that out. We're going to try to figure it out but without knowing what kind of sensor this is we're probably going to return it or trash it.

title: Work Great! Size and Sound Quality An Issue
text: I bought these when they first came out. I really wanted something sleek and simple. The setup was a breeze. Once fully charged they work just like any bluetooth headset. These include answer/command, volume, next/prev track, etc. The box includes three different sized in-ear rubbers (I don't know what they are really called. Their position and size REALLY MATTER for sound quality. The sound can be shallow and sound like an old phone unless you get the position and in-ear depth right. Once they are seated (their design makes this easy) they can sound great. However, I have a big head. Some would say in more than one way, but these physically do not fit my head. The buds do not actually press into my ear. Therefore, the sound I get is very tin-ee (that "phone" quality). Unless these seat into your ear like any ear-bud they will sound cheap. Which is not really the case if you just press them in slightly with you index fingers. You'll really hear the great quality then. Overall, these are great headphones... if you have a small head.

title: WAY Over-Priced, Not Very Good Camera
text:
I bought this camera after having one of the Mavicas for several years - thinking of course that Sony has improved upon their features and design. I was very very wrong.

There are several things about this camera that make it seem cheap, and quite returnable:

1. Battery: The batteries (rechargeable AA type) must be removed from the camera to be charged. This is the most cumbersome task for the price of this camera.

2. Lenses: For any other lens you must use a large plastic ring that attaches not to the camera's lens but to the camera itself. Any type of wide angle lens (I've tried several) causes the edges of the so-called "adapter" to actually be in the photographs. This is a very useless and cheap ploy by sony to make this camera versatle. With the plastic ring and then with your desired lens it makes the camera look like a toy. This is not "my first Sony". It is quite an embarasing thing to see and use.

3. Flash Recharge: The Mavica never had this problem. It takes about 7-10 seconds for the flash to recharge. This is - again - a very embarassing thing about this camera... to have your friends sit there and wait for that "spontaneous" snapshot kind of loses the moment when I'm watching the flash recharge indicator blink...blink...blink... Rediculous.

4. Zoom: You can't zoom in movie mode. This is the dumbest thing about this camera. You can't zoom in movie mode? Touted with such a great zoom and... well, 'nuff said.

My initial impression was that this camera would be a professional, high-quality, Sony product. However, due to the curious shortfalls of basic features I was very misslead by the hype over this camera. There are other issues: 50% of all photographs - even in good light or on a tripod - are out of focus.

And, of course, there's the classic Sony snapshot delay. Those of you with Sony cameras will know exactly what I mean. You'd think that after 7-8 years of this that they would fix that. Nope. In fact, on this camera, it's worse. I can't tell you how many pictures of the ceiling or the floor or someones foot I have taken because of this. Dear Sony; Fix this problem.

I feel sorry for Sony over this camera. It should be about $199 when you compare it to the features and design of competitor cameras. Glad I kept the box.

P.S. I just heard that the DSC-F828 (their brand new 8mp camera) was suddenly discontinued with no explaination. Perhaps they are finally rethinking (or thinking about) their design and usefulness.

In the end, this is the reverse camera i kept on my car because of the quality and also the convenience of having its own lcd screen. ( no pulling apart dash to reach dvd screens rca cables)

title: Great memories all on one product
text:
A few years ago i purchased an electronic photo viewer as i was tired of replacing pictures in picture frames and moving them etc.

That photo viewer has always been a pleasant centerpiece in the house and got updated frequently with pictures of the kids and family.

When asked to review this item i was skeptical as i already liked my old one and didnt want that to hinder my review for any reason. Boy, am i glad i said yes to the review because this one offers so many more features and boasts a much better picture than my previous one.

To get started the display is sharp and can be seen from a wide angle on its 10" display. The pictures look as good on this product as they do on your high end phone or camera.

The options are endless - calendar, clock, still pictures, pictures with sound, videos, or just music player.

The unit comes with a remote that works up to about 15-18 ft and can control everything from menus to picture selection to volume.

The product supports all kinds of file types, in fact i havent had a file type that hasnt worked. (Jpeg, BMP,mp3,mp4,wma,flv,avi,mov)

This product supports sd, mmc, and usb for reading any of the above file types.

The menus are easy to learn and navigate whether controlled through the buttons on back or the remote. The product does come with a manual in case you become confused with how to operate it at any given point.

After testing this product in many different ways with different files and media i am confident that anyone who purchases this will be as happy as i am with the product.

As stated before i did receive this item in exchange for my honest review and that has not changed my opinion in any way.

title: Good
text:
I bought these to help with getting neighborhood dogs on camera so I can put stop to dog excavating in my yard since HOA is useless. Catching any robbers would be just a bonus, haha!

Pluses:
The cameras are very easy to set up, just ten minutes with software max. Outside very easy too, just a screw and its up (although you might want a ladder and good screwdriver). Only time is really that you have to just think through where exactly you want them outside. Easy to angle once up too. The visibility/clarity is good with day excellent and night good. You can set sensitivity, how long video clips are, and other controls. Easy stuff.

Area for improvement:

Not much, but I noticed my clips have twice stopped when someone stops in my yard. Once when guy stopped with dog in my yard. But I couldn't see anything after they stopped. I tweaked the restart trigger time and lengthened the clip recording time to 50 seconds. The second time it just stopped recording the lady completely with no pick back up. So hopefully the length change will fix both. The only other thing - mine are out in full weather conditions. They are waterproof and temp proof so far. The camera lens can get temporarily foggy just due to being exposed, but the inner box hasn't been affected. I don't think there's much you can do about the lenses in heavy rain, unless it is under a shelter. So just an observation. May need to have a little edge or something.

Overall - I love these, feel more in control and want more - haha! Building a fort! Kidding But good value for price and technology.

title: Do not buy! Awful quality and no customer service.
text: We purchased these for my 9 y/o son to listen to music after he was jealous of his teenage brother's wireless earbuds. We wanted something that wasn't "in ear" due to his young age and was inexpensive in case he really didn't end up using them much. Initially he loved these. The sound is nothing to write home about but it isn't awful, the battery life was decent, and they fit him well (but would not be a good fit for an adult or larger child). Last week, less than 2 weeks after the 90-day warranty expired, the headband snapped in half while he was putting them on. While he is only 9, he is very mature for his age and is very gentle and trustworthy with his belongings so the issue was not abuse. Being so close to the warranty period and having such a serious design flaw I decided to write the company to see if they would fix or replace them. Nope. They asked me to jump through a bunch of hoops as though they were going to do the right thing, then said, "Contact a local technician to repair them". Right. For a $30 pair of headphones. I certainly didn't expect them to last forever - they *are* cheap - but I DID expect he would get a year's worth of use out of them for the price. Do not bother with these. The company does not stand by their products.

title: Great sound, versatility and ease of use!
text:
Great ear buds, and they arrived super quickly as well!

The ear buds come with a charging case, usb charging cord, several size ear pieces, and the ear buds themselves.
The charging case comes almost all the way charged, mine was at 98% upon delivery, and the ear buds were also fairly well charged at about 80%. They're held in the case with magnets, which is nice for storage and piece of mind, knowing they will stay put while charging. The charging case can actually be used as a power bank for your phone/mobile device too, which is pretty awesome! I didn't realize this at purchase, so it was a nice bonus.

After fully charging both for first time use, the buds will auto pair with each other when taken off the charging case. They paired very easily with my galaxy s9, and I was actually pleasantly surprised by the sound quality.
They touch sensitive area on the ear buds is most of the outer area shown when put into your ear, so be sure to get the situated first, and then turn your music on to avoid awkward on/off mishaps while putting them on.

The instructions included are very clear. Left ear is long hold volume down, right is long hold volume up, skipping tracks back or forward is quick press of either ear. Answering and ending calls can be done from either ear also.
These can also be used in single ear mode (using the left as the "master" pod), and will auto switch to the right pod as master if the left dies, so you can continue single ear use while charging the left.

Overall these are very nice little ear pods for a great price. If you are shopping around, I absolutely recommend buying these!

title: Not super easy to assemble but overall a good purchase for the price.
text:
Ok...so I just finished mounting my monitors on these arms. It looks great and feels sturdy. But one important thing to note is that it takes a LOT of strength to get the nuts tight enough to hold the monitor’s position, especially in regards to up-and-down tilt. I kept tightening...and tightening...and tightening...until I thought my thumb was going to break off. I finally got them tight enough to stop drooping and hold the position. The same is true for the main arm which holds up the crossbar. I’m still a little leery that it’s going to start slipping after a while, but for now, I think it’s probably secure. I will tighten up the bolts again in a few days just to be sure. It would be nice if they included some time of tool that was easier to grip rather than an Allen wrench, especially when that much tightening is needed.

I will say that the clamp and main post are heavy duty and feel very sturdy. Also, the arms are easy to move and reposition side to side and back and forth. I also like that I was able to mount the monitors without a second person, due to the assisting bolts where you can “hang” the monitor on the bracket until you get everything screwed tight (like a ceiling fan).

Overall 4 stars due to my hands and arms are going to be sore tomorrow due to all the required tightening.

title: Works great for me!
text:
This is a pretty good case and keyboard for the iPad mini 2, but there are a few drawbacks. There's more positive than negative, though.

First, the negatives: (1) the backspace key is not in the top right corner, it's one row below. You will hit the "=" button way more than you want to while looking for the backspace button. (2) the apostrophe is on the L key and you have to press the Function button to use it. You will type "it;s" way more than you want to. (3) there are extra keys on the keyboard such as cmd, alt, option, and a weird symbol that looks like a swirly for which my iPad has no function that I am aware of.

Now, the positives. They keyboard is smaller than usual (of course) but pretty easy to use with a little practice. The screen tilt function is fantastic. It can hold the tablet at an unlimited amount of angles. The screen can spin 360 degrees so it can be used with the keyboard as a prop in a triangle format, with the keyboard in the back for movie watching, or out flat for typing in bed with the tablet propped up on your knees. I like how it makes my tablet into a mini laptop. I also love how the keyboard tucks in behind the screen for coloring or sketching with a stylus.

The case is very sturdy, made of a rubbery feel type material, and nice to look at and touch. Not cheaply made at all. It has lights for charging, battery, and Bluetooth pairing. All the holes, speakers, and cameras are exposed where they need to be. I have a tempered glass screen protector on the iPad and it does not get in the way of the case at all.

The keyboard does add some weight to the tablet, but this does not bother me. Overall I am very pleased with this product.

title: 2012 Mac Mini 2.6 GHz/16GB RAM OS X Mavericks 10.9.1 Results
text:
2012 Mac Mini 2.6 GHz/16GB RAM Mavericks 10.9.1: Startech's drivers from their website do not work at all for me as of Feb 18 2014 (I have the USB to DVI + USB port model). I did an uninstall first, then reinstalled. Still nothing. Restarting many times did nothing. Unplugging the USB video card while fresh installing did nothing. I've tried every permutation of scenarios.

I then tried a driver from Magic Control Technology Corp (link is at end of the review) that another reviewer (Kevin Mentch) said worked on an older OS X 10.8.4. It is a driver from 2012 which last worked on OS X Mountain Lion. Here is my experience with that driver running in OS X 19.1.1: Short story is that it is useable, but not any better than buying a cheaper USB 2.0 video driver for half the price.

The driver works on my 27" Apple 1920x1200 display. However, when I scroll any window on the monitor attached to this USB video card, the bottom third of my 27" 1920x1200 Apple DVI display shows flickers of scrambled up screen, for split seconds during movement. Sometimes it's the whole screen. It's super annoying. Basically when there's any on screen movement, whether a screensaver or simple web browser, or text document, the display flickers. I'm also running two other identical 27" 1920x1200 displays on the Thunderbolt & HDMI ports along with this USB adapter. They run fine regardless of the USB video card problems.

Huge warning: I just messed up the USB card by switching resolution from 1920x1200 to a lower one. I only have vertical lines on the screen and can't see anything at all on the desktop, even after uninstalling and reinstalling the driver still brings up the lines. I figured out how to get back to the 1920x1200 resolution even with the USB powered screen completely unreadable: In the other monitors, go to the System Prefs ->Displays and hit in the bottom right of the control panel "Gather Windows" and voila - all three displays preferences show up on the one display you're working on. I switched resolutions on the USB screen. Unfortunately, though the screen is now visible through the USB adapter, but there are ghosts of the previous bands on the screen which faded away after 10 minutes. This Adapter is being returned, until the Mavericks issues are fixed on Apple's end (That's where all the tech support articles say the problem lies).

The link of the alternate (old) drivers: "It is made by a company called Magic Control Technology Corp, and you can find the drivers needed here: [...]and the direct link to the zip download here: [...]

title: Excellent HDMI to SPDIF optical and analog converter
text:
This is an excellent HDMI to optical digital & analog converter. Sound & video output are excellent.

Pluses
1. Very simple, straightforward setup
2. Clear, easy-to-understand, instruction manual
3. Power adapter connector screws onto the back of the converter
4. HDMI video output is just pass-through, no visible (that I can see) video distortion
5. Supports 120Hz/4k output, which matches the output of the Sony PS5
6. The HDMI audio output is converted to both optical digital (SPDIF) and analog (3.5mm stereo) output, providing great flexibility
7. Audio & video sync is great

Minuses
1. None!

I needed an HDMI converter to pass video & sound from a Sony PS5 to a Bose soundbar (optical in) and 27 in. HP gaming monitor (HDMI in). This HDMI converter fits the bill perfectly.
The setup is easy. Video will simply pass-through, allows the full 4k/120Hz video signal from the PS5 to be displayed without distortion; video looked great on the gaming monitor.

The audio output is really the only thing that needs to be configured. If, like my setup, you are connecting the optical out to a soundbar, receiver or other speakers that don't multi-channel sound output, press the "EDID" button until you see the "4k@120Hz, 2.1CH" lit up. The optical out from the converter to the soundbar is excellent. Audio & video play back in sync.

This is an excellent converter. I highly recommend it.

title: Great sound, good looks, great options for expandability
text:
There are quite a few of these "sound tower" Bluetooth speakers in the marketplace. This one from Samsung is quite good. This MX-ST40B is baby in Samsung's MX-STxxx line. Those other 2 speakers have more power & features. I don't know what they sound like, but I can say that the MX-ST40B plays very loud, with clear voices and a nice, low end punch.

Pluses
1. Plays loud, with little distortion (without bass boost engaged)
2. Clear, intelligle voices and highs with sparkle and little harshness
3. Nice low end punch, aided by port at the bottom of the speaker. Bass boost can be selectively activated.
4. 5 different RGB light patterns
5. Lights can be disabled
6. Bluetooth pairing was simple
7. Auxiliary jack panel for hooking up other analog sources or multiple MX-STxx speakers in a "group play" function (group play not tested)
8. Ability to pair another MX-STxx speaker for stereo playback (not tested)
9. Full function remote control with most functions duplicated on top of speaker
10. IPX5 water resistance: auxiliary ports and power cord port covered by rubber gasket
11. Battery powered: take it on the go anywhere, then plug in the cord to charge it. Cord is the type used for electronics, such as a CD or DVD player.
12. Large handle, making it easy to carry around

Minuses
None for me. If you need more power or karaoke functions, upgrade to the most expensive version.

title: Wireless Android Auto in a Hyundai Sonata
text:
After having experienced wireless Android Auto on a recent trip in a rental car, I knew I wanted this feature in my own car, a 2021 Hyundai Sonata.

I read an online article about this AA Wireless unit and a competing model from Motorola. The AAWireless unit had better availability at the same price, so I took the chance and ordered it. I received the unit about a 1.5 weeks later.

In 2 words: it works. I can plug in the adapter into my car's USB port and after about 20 seconds it connects to my phone, a Samsung Galaxy Note 20 Ultra 5G.

However, getting everything working was not without some initial installation woes. Here are my observations.

1. Download the app from the Google Play Store.
2. Plug the unit into your car's USB port that connects to the car stereo
3. Start the app, go through the prompts, then pair the adapter with your phone via Bluetooth. This is where I had some difficulties. Pairing took a bit of time.
4. The app will search for a firmware update. If one is available, download & install the update. Note: the AAWireless adapter forces a Wi-Fi connection to your phone and will download the firmware update using your cellular connection. Poor connection = slow download & update. This was the 2nd source of frustration.
5. Adapter will restart and attempt to reconnect with your phone. This was the 3rd source of frustration. The phone & adapter weren't pairing/connecting. I had to view the FAQ's in the app, then perform a few configuration changes in my phone. This could be a bit much for some users.
6. I ended up doing a reset of the adapter & deleting the app before reinstalling it.
7. After repeating the above steps, the unit paired via Bluetooth & established the Wi-Fi connection necessary for Android Auto. Everything worked perfectly.

Having the wireless Android Auto functionality is a huge benefit. The unit works great & sounds great. I don't notice any delays or interruptions when playing music or audio books, nor any hiccups using Google Maps.

title: Great duo connector USB stick
text:
This is a great USB stick. It's a duo/2-in-1 design: USB-A on one side, USB-C on the other. The size is very small, almost like a toy. It's tiny compared to other, older USB sticks that I own. This can be a good or bad thing, depending on your perspective.

USB-A works perfectly when connecting to my computer or car's USB port.

The USB-C connects to my Samsung Galaxy Note 20 phone & Galaxy Tab S8 tablet perfectly.

I can transfer pictures, videos & music from my computer onto the this USB stick, then plug it into my phone & tablet to transfer & vise-versa. The transfers are much faster over USB than wireless & more convenient than having the phone or tablet plugged into the computer.

title: Surprisingly good sound from an inexpensive speaker
text:
Surprisingly good sound from a small, inexpensive, portable speaker. I was impressed by the quality of sound from the speaker, compared to a pair of computer speakers that are in the same price range. The bass output is fuller, the voice and highs are better delineated and clearer; the sound isn't lean or cupped.

Pluses
1. Bluetooth pairing is straightforward
2. Can aconnect other devices via a 3.5mm cable
3. Supports microSD cards
4. Water resistant; the ports are sealed behind a rubberized cover
5. RGB LED lights on both ends of the speaker
6. Lights fade from one color to the next
7. Surprisingly loud, clear output
8. Can be paired with another unit for stereo sound
9. Battery life was good during initial test (4 hours); didn't test for total run time

Minuses
1. It's a small speaker: don't expect large bass output
2. Didn't see a way to turn-off/disable the lighting

title: Works well with a single computer but uncertain with a 2nd computer
text:
Update 1/22/23
I was able to resolve the HDMI to DisplayPort issue. The HDMI to DisplayPort adapter, along with the corresponding cables, weren't providing a sufficient signal to the KVM switch. I found an active HDMI to DisplayPort unidirectional cable with a USB-A power plug. I didn't have to use the USB-A portion of the cable. But switching to this unidirectional cable resolved my issue fully. I can now fully recommend this KVM switch. If any of you are experiencing an issue converting HDMI to DisplayPort, be sure to find a cable that states the specific signal flow from each end of the cable.

There's a lot to like with this KVM switch. It's compact, supports dual monitors, 4k @ 60Hz display and easy to switch between computers. However, I couldn't get the 2nd computer to display its output onto a single, external monitor.

Pluses
1. Small, compact, unobtrusive
2. Includes 4 DisplayPort cables and USB cables to hookup 2 separate computers
3. 4 USB ports to add keyboard, mouse, etc
4. No noticeable video degradation

Minuses
1. USB power adapter not included
2. Unable to get a 2nd computer to display its output onto a single monitor

I hooked up a Lenovo laptop to the 2nd computer USB port and single DisplayPort using an HDMI to DisplayPort adapter. I tried a few different options, but no matter what was tried, I couldn't get the laptop's output to display onto a single monitor. There was no issue hooking up the laptop's HDMI output directly to the monitor, so maybe the KVM switch just doesn't like the HDMI to DisplayPort adapter. I'm giving the device a 3 star rating because of it.

title: Very good sound and a good value
text:
This is a surprisingly good sounding speaker, a great value at its price point.

Pluses
1. IP67 rated, worked perfectly fine during a light rain shower
2. Good build quality
3. Very good sound quality
4. LED lights on each end, randomly cycles through RGB spectrum
5. LED lights pulse and change colors based upon the beat/tempo of the music being played
6. Can connect to speaker via Bluetooth or 3.5mm stereo audio cable. A MicroSD card can also be inserted to play files back locally
7. Can pair 2 speakers together for stereo sound (not tested)

Minuses
1. Small size equals little bass
2. USB power adapter not included
3. Haven't found a way to turn off LED lights, can be distracting at night

title: Very good quality smart surge protector
text:
This is a very good quality smart surge protector. It has a great mix of features for the price.

Pluses
1. Outlets are widely spaced for large wall "wart" power adapters
2. Smart outlets can be remotely controlled through the app (iOS & Android)
3. Voice assistant compatible
4. USB-A ports allow for additional device charging
5. No "hub" required to use remotely

Minuses
1. Only 6 outlets
2. 2.4 GHz Wi-FI means you need to enable the 2.4 GHz radio on your Wi-Fi router/access point in order to connect to the surge protector remotely
3. USB ports only go up to 5 amps (no fast charging)
4. Only rated to 600 joules, on the low end of surge protection

You can use this surge protector without enabling the smart capabilities. However, once you download the app to your device and connect to the 2.4 GHz radio of your Wi-Fi router/access point, pairing to the device
is pretty straightforward. Using the app is easy and allows for some pretty cool programmming, such as timers to turn on & off the outlets. I haven't tried out the voice assistant capabilities, but I'm assuming they work
as intended.

title: Good quality, thin profile cable
text:
I had 2 Cat 6 ethernet cables that were linked together with a coupler, connected to a router and modem. However, this wasn't an ideal situation.

Enter this 25 ft. Cat 7 shielded cable. It's worked great for me. The slim profile allowed me to run it through small plastic conduit along the wall in my office. Not only does it work great, but its slim profile makes it easy route along or under baseboards.

title: Convenient splitter for large wall wart adapters
text:
This is a really convenient way of being able to plug multiple large power adapters into a UPS with limited outlets.

It's well made and constructed of good quality materials. Even with all 4 outlets being used, the cords never got warm. I have no concerns about using this 4 outlet cable with multiple devices.

title: Works great in a Samsung Galaxy Tab A7
text:
I bought a Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 for a Christmas gift. The 64GB of internal storage wasn't going to be sufficient for holding a lot of media. So the search was on for a microSD card.

Got this Lexar card as a Black Friday special. Great price compared to other name brands, but same high-end performance.

I've had no issues so far with playback of movies & music. Copying files to the card is speedy, no errors observed.

title: Resisted buying one of these, happy I finally did
text:
I had 10 different hard drives laying around, not being used. As part of some spring (winter) cleaning, I decided it was time to part ways with them. But I needed to find an efficient way of erasing them.

This external hard drive dock fit the bill perfectly for me. No drivers were required. The unit comes with a USB cable and a power adapter. I plugged the unit into a USB port, then turned on the power. A drive letter showed up once a hard drive was plugged in.

I used the dock to simultaneously format 2x 500GB hard drives, then a 240GB SSD drive, then a few 1TB & 2TB hard drives. I used WD Diagnostic software to run extended drive tests & erasure. All drives recognized and tests ran successfully.

I was able to (fairly) quickly and efficiently get all of the hard drive cleanup tasks completed using this dock. Worked great for me.

title: Nice, heavy duty power strip
text:
This is a unique power strip. You don't see many of these types in the U.S. However, I saw this type widely available in Asia.

Being able to selectively turn off individual outlets instead of unplugging a cord is very cool. It can also be a curse. An outlet can easily be accidentally turned off, which could cause some problems if a desktop computer, hard drive or NAS were plugged in.

There is decent spacing between the outlets. However, since they're all aligned vertically, some outlets will be blocked if large external power adapters are plugged in.

With that said, the power strip is extremely versatile. The build quality is very good; it's solidly built and seems like it can take abuse.

title: Moisture resistant power strip
text:
I thought this powerstrip worked very well out on my back porch. The number of outlets, wide spacing between outlets and its moisture resistance added up to a good performing product. The power strip was never directly exposed to water, but freezing temperatures and the occasional light snow flurry didn't seem to faze it.

Plus
1. 10 power adapter outlets, all widely spaced for wall adapters
2. Moisture/water resistance
3. Flat, wall hugging plug

Minus
1. Very basic looks

Overall, I felt confident using this power adapter under a covered porch. The widely spaced outlets are a huge plus.

title: Very good surge protector
text:
This is a good and versatile surge protector. I got it to use in a guest bedroom, allowing guests to charge their mobile devices a variety of ways.

Plus
1. 10 power adapter outlets, with 2 spaced widely for wall adapters
2. 3 USB-A outlets
3. 1 USB-C PD with 20 watt power
4. Flat, wall hugging plug

Minus
1. Only 2 of the adapter outlets are widely spaced. You're going to lose access to some outlets if larger wall adapters are plugged in

Overall, I liked the versatility of this power adapter. It allows for a wide variety of charging types, making it easy for anyone to find the one that works best for them.

title: Works great in a Synology NAS
text: Bought this 16 GB stick to add to a Synology DS1621+. Installed easily, booted up just fine. Recommended.

title: A great multi-function USB-C hub for my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6
text:
This USB-C hub worked well with my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6. I didn't have any issues using it.

Pluses
1. Great build quality
2. Aluminum case
3. Braided USB-C cable
4. 3x USB-A ports, 1x SD & Micro SD ports and 1x 4k/60p HDMI port
5. Plug and play; no drivers needed

Minuses
1. No USB power pass-through to charge a mobile device while using the hub
2. The USB hub draws power from the device it's connected to, limiting the number of devices that can be connected & used at any given time

I was able to plug the USB hub directly to my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6's USB-C. I connected a 32GB flash drive, a 128GB MicroSD card and a HDMI cable to the hub. The hub was instantly recognized by the tablet & showed the drives connected to it. I could browse the contents of both drives using Samsung's My Files app. Once I connected the hub to my Vizio PX 4k HDTV, the tablet's display was mirrored to the TV. Movies, TV shows and streaming videos from popular websites all played back flawlessly.

There were 2 downsides found while using the hub. The first one was not being able to charge my tablet while using the hub. The second one deals with using an unpowered hub such as this with mobile devices that provide limited power to their USB port. While the flash drive & SD cards worked fine during my use, I can see where higher power draw input sources can fail. My tablet only provides so much power, so it can't provide enough power for sources like unpowered external hard drives.

title: No frills USB to HDMI adapter
text:
This is a well made, no frills USB-C to HDMI adapter.

It comes in a anodized aluminum case. The case is smooth on all edges and cool to the touch. There is no internal fan; the aluminum case acts a heatsink to keep the internals nice & cool.

The documentation that comes packaged with the adapter says it supports up to 8k resolution. I don't have an 8k source and display, so I can't confirm that. However, I did play back 4k UHD & 1080p content via my Samsung Galaxy Tab S6 to a Vizio PX series LCD TV. I can report there was no lag or stuttering, audio was in sync and the picture quality looked great.

My only concern is that it's an unpowered pass-through adapter. As such, your tablet or mobile device can't be charged while using it. As long as you're fully juiced up before using it, everything will be fine.

title: Nice braided USB cable
text:
Using this cable to replace a broken I use in the car for Android Auto. The original USB cable that came with my Samsung phone starting having problems with frequent disconnects. It was time for a replacement.

This cable fits the bill. It's a little longer than I needed, but works like a champ. It allows the phone to charge at full speed using the car's 5v USB-A port. The phone no longer randomly disconnects from Android Auto. The blue color braid is icing on the cake.

title: Good value binoculars
text:
This is a good value set. It comes with a decent case, a shoulder strap, lens cleaning cloth and an instruction book. I can't say that these are the best optics. And they're the traditional style, so they're a little bulky.. At this price point, expectations need to be tempered.

However, for casual viewing by someone who isn't going to be highly critical (my wife), these binoculars will allow her to simply enjoy the view: seeing wildlife (birds, deer, whales, etc) from a different perspective. If this is you, then you might like these binoculars as well.

title: Works great
text: Worked great for me. Allowed me to convert a USB-C to USB-C cable to USB-A. I can now use this cable to plug into my car for Android Auto. And there's more flexibility when using power adapters.

title: Very good photo frame but setup was a little tricky
text:
There is a lot to like about this photo frame. But there are a couple of issues that are holing me back from rating it higher.

The good
1. Display resolution is high, high resolution photos look great
2. Display is bright & colorful
3. Photos can be uploaded to frame remotely using the app
4. App is easy to use
5. Good options for customizing slide shows and display settings
6. Ability to program the frame to turn on/off using schedules
7. Can plug-in an external drive for slide shows
8. Motion detection can be turned on/off

The not so good
1. Frame only supports MicroSD cards, no other cards supported
2. The max supported size of the MicroSD card is only 32GB
3. Internal memory is limited to about 10GB
4. Can only upload 9 pictures at a time
5. Setup was a little tricky for me
6. Some pixelation and banding visible

Setup was tricky. I had to plug/unplug the unit several times just to get to main screen. No Wi-Fi networks were visible. Even going into the Settings and doing a factory reset didn't help. This prevented the app from connecting to the unit.

I removed the the memory card, then restarted the unit.. After reboot,, it started working dramatically better. I was able to pair my Wi-Fi to the frame with no further issues. Linking the app to the frame is made easier by scanning a QR code in the Settings menu of the frame. Setup was straightforward.

I believe the initial setup issues were attributed to plugging in that fully loaded 128GB memory card. If I were to do it again, I would set it up first using the basic instructions before adding any peripherals to the mix.

The good certainly outweighs the not so good. Follow the directions and setup should be (hopefully) better than my initial experience.

title: Very good USB-C cables **UPDATE**
text:
**Update 7/31/21**
I'm lowering the star rating to 3. After spending time using the 10 ft cable with 45w & 60w Samsung fast chargers, the cable doesn't appear to support fast charging. The initial on-screen prompt says fast charging, but charging is slow. And even slower when using the phone while charging.

These cables appear to be very well made. The braided cover looks great. The metal connectors have a nice matte finish. I'm using the 10 ft. cable as I'm writing this review. It supports super fast charging when used with a compatible charger; in my case, I'm using a Samsung 45w charger to charge my Samsung Galaxy Note 20 Ultra.

These 2 cables represent a really good value. Recommended!

title: Could not get this camera to pair to the app & my Wi-Fi network
text:
I wanted a motion tracking security cam so that I could track our cats when they use the restroom. One of my cats has urinary tract issues, so it's important to know how much & often he's using the litter box. I got this unit in the hopes it would satisfy my needs.

Pluses
1. Cute BB-8 look & motion, especially when starting up the unit
2. Good build quality
3. User manual & app have the potential of making the setup of the camera easy

Cons
1. Works only on 2.4GHz Wi-Fi network
2. Couldn't get the cam to connect to 2 different 2.4GHz Wi-Fi networks

I tried really hard over 2 days to get this camera to connect & pair with the app & my Wi-Fi network. I reset the cam multiple times as described in the user manual each time I attempted to run the setup. I followed the instructions from the manual & the app to the letter. Nothing I tried would work. Maybe I just got a bad unit or it doesn't like my Asus Wi-Fi router. I don't have a problem with other devices (smart light bulbs, PET feeders) that use the 2.4GHz network, so I do know it can't be the router.

title: Good surge protector with nice long cord
text: This power strip is replacing a 6 outlet multi-tap. It's bright color helps it to be easily seen when working in the garage. I like that there's decent spacing between the outlets & that there's a outlet at the very end that easily accomodates a wall wart adapter that doesn't impede the other outlet above it. The extra long cord, high joule rating & flat plug to the wall are all big pluses.

title: No coasters - nough said
text: I've never had any coasters with these Verbatim discs. No quality issues, no play back issues so far; 6+ years and going strong.

title: Great external drive unit, but check compatibility first
text:
I bought this external drive case for an old internal HD-DVD disc drive. Installation was a breeze. The external drive unit is well made and of high quality.

After plugging it in, nothing worked. Checked connections, then tried again a few times. Still nothing. After some head scratching and saying a few choice words, I pulled the drive out. I plugged in a new Blu-ray drive and it worked perfectly fine.

Discovered the old drive's power requirements exceeded the power output of the OWC external drive case. Bummer. Check the power requirement of your internal drive for compatibility before you buy.

title: Great USB 3.1 hub if only a few ports needed
text:
Completed a new ITX computer build & wanted to expand the number of USB 3.1 ports. This Amazon hub fit the bill for my needs.

Decent length of cable with "C" connector. All of the external hard drives connected with zero issue. No software driver required, all UPNP. Would buy again.

title: Good drive, handles most discs with no issues
text:
Got this drive to allow playback of 4k UHD discs, as long as certain firmware versions are installed.

Drive has worked nearly flawlessly, handling a variety of DVD's, Blu-ray's & 4k Blu-ray's. A few discs can give it trouble. And I had layer break issues when recording with Ritek dual-layer BD's & this drive.

title: Great for protecting hard drives
text: These work great for sealing up hard disk drives. A little bit of a snug fit, but to tears and the bag is sealable. Nuff said.

title: Disappointed with disc layer burning issues
text:
Tried using these Ritek dual layer blanks with a LG 14x Blu-ray burner and burning software. The discs would always complete burning with no initial errors detected.

However, when attempting to play them on a stand-alone Blu-ray player, the disc would cause the player to freeze up at the layer break. No matter the burn speeds or software used, the discs would never play back properly.

After half the pack turned to coasters, I stopped trying. I'm switching media in the hopes that it's simy a disc compatibility issue with the burner or I just got a bad batch of discs.

title: Great card, even better value when on sale
text:
When I upgraded from a Samsung Galaxy Tab S2 to an S6, I decided to upgrade the microSD card from 128GB to 512GB.

Looked around and narrowed the choices to Samsung and SanDisk. When the SanDisk when on sale during November, I pulled the trigger.

I've had 4 other SanDisk memory cards and have never had any issues with any of them. This card is fast, and at 512GB, holds my entire music library, a full picture library & many 1080p movies with plenty of room to spare.

Read speeds are outstanding. While I haven't done any writing speed tests, it copies content from my PC & NAS via USB very quickly. I have no complaints with the card's performance.

title: Good braided HDMI cable, compatible with 4k
text:
This cable replaced an older Monoprice cable that was damaged during a recent installation of audio gear.

I have this cable hooked up between a Marantz receiver and Vizio 4k TV. No HDMI handshake issues at 15 ft; it just works. And the cable looks good with the braided outer cover. If in the market for another cable, I would buy it again.

title: Good screen protector for Galaxy Tab S6
text:
Got a Samsung Galaxy Tab S6 to replace an aging S2. Needed a screen protector, but needed 1 compatible with the in-screen fingerprint reader. Unfortunately the glass screen protectors just wouldn't work. So enter the Supershieldz.

This was relatively easy to install and fits the S6's screen perfectly. However, use of the S6's in-screen fingerprint scanner with the screen protector installed is a bit of hit-and-miss. It could very well be that my dry skin (from frequent washing & drying) is causing reading errors with the scanner. However, your results may vary.

title: Works great, but a little expensive
text:
Bought this battery as a backup for my Arlo Pro 2. It's replacing a non-Arlo brand battery, which didn't work very well. Not sure if the off-brand battery was defective (only lasted weeks on a full charge compared to months with Arlo-branded one) or somehow the Pro 2 knows it's not a genuine Arlo accessory and just drains the hell out of it.

Pro: Arlo-branded battery lasts months on a charge

Con: Pricey compared to competitors

title: Perfect replacement battery for Skybell HD
text: Worked as a perfect replacement battery for the expanding battery in our Skybell HD door cam. Plugged right in with a bare minimum of fuss. Space is tight, but workable.

title: Good Arlo battery charger
text:
Unit is compact and allows 2 batteries to be charged. LED indicators advise battery charge status. There's no real manual, but the box info tells you all you need to know.

Gave 4 stars as the first unit received had defective LED's & didn't charge the battery very well. But after troubleshooting with Amazon via chat, the unit was deemed defective & a replacement was received in 2 days. The second unit has worked flawlessly. Great service provided by Amazon.

title: Good replacement battery
text: Great replacement battery for Arlo Pro2 cameras. Fits into camera perfectly and lasts just as long on a single charge (med. recording performance, about 3 mo.).

title: Good extension cable
text: This power cord extension has worked great in the few months I've had it. Good quality & perfect length for my need. However, the USB cable position wouldn't allow the outdoor outlet protected cover to close. Got a 90 degree angle converter & then everything was all good.

title: Big improvement over my old Harmony remote
text:
This Harmony Elite remote is replacing an old Harmony 1000 remote. While the old one still works, it is buggy with spotty IR coverage. I wanted something a little more traditional that fit the bill. Programming the Elite using the improved desktop software was a breeze. The Harmony Hub was recognized instantly and new firmware was automatically installed. All of my equipment was found easily. Once the changes are synced to the remote & Hub, you're ready to use it.

The remote feels great in the hand, with nice weight and a bottom textured surface that keeps it from slipping around. Button placement is very good. Some buttons are a little small, but you get used to it after a bit. You can also download the Logitech Harmony app to smartphones & tablets of you're needing another controller. The Hub is positioned at the top of my equipment stack, so there's been no issues with all of the devices turning on and set to the correct inputs.

However, word of advice. Make sure the Hub is connected to a reliable 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi access point and assign the Hub a static IP address. This will ensure a stable connection within your network to control Wi-Fi devices, specifically the Roku Streaming Stick. Also, the Elite remote does not provide control of RF devices: I wasn't able to setup my Luminoodle bias lighting because of this fact.

title: Works well once setup, but the pain is in the setup
text:
I wanted to be able to incorporate the Harmony Hub Extender with Harmony Elite remote into my existing Z-wave network, to control lighting. It was easy enough to pair it with the Hub and download new firmware to it.

However, there was quite of bit of trial & error to get it paired with my Qolysys Z-wave panel. Many times it would not pair properly. And the Extender & Hub kept going offline, making it hard to do anything.

So I read some advice online and did the following: (1) do a reset to factory defaults for both the Harmony Hub & Extender, (2) swap the power adapter for a fast charger, giving the unit a more robust power supply, (3) made sure Hub was connected on the 2.4 GHz side of my Asus Wi-Fi Lyra mesh system, (4) assigned a static IP address to the Hub, (5) added & removed the Extender several times from the panel and (6) not try to make the Extender a secondary controller of the Z-wave network.

Eventually using the mobile Harmony app, the Extender started recognizing all of my devices. I can now reliably control lighting & the thermostat from the remote. It complements the control I have from the panel & the Alarm.com app.

Was it worth the effort? Probably not. But got the Harmony Elite, Hub & Extender as refurbished units for half the price of new, so that dampens the frustration some.

title: Great quality, works perfect for my receiver stack
text:
I recently installed some new shelving and was having an issue of where to put the other components of my home theater system. Stacking the other items on top of the receiver would be ideal (space wise), but not good that they would block the top vents of the receiver. I searched around and found the Aircom products. They had products to fit just about any top or bottom stack config and different options to force hot air out the front or rear of the unit.

I purchased the T10 unit. The LCD display is a nice touch, letting you see current temp, fan speed & alarm indicator. Setup is a breeze. Unit comes packed in a nice gift box. Aesthetically, it looks and feels like a high quality component. It matches up with my Marantz receiver beautifully. Recommended for anyone looking to vent hot air from their receiver stack.

title: Very good quality 1080p camera for Alarm.com integration
text: Got this camera as an addition to my other Alarm.com 720p security cameras. Image quality is much better than the older models. It integrates perfectly with Alarm.com, so you can watch remotely in small chunks. You can set quality vs. speed, recording time & frames per second. Setup & pairing with Alarm.com can be a little tricky, but if you follow the directions carefully, you'll be up & running in no time. While this doesn't have the fastest motion detection, or best night vision coverage, nor recording more than 10 FPS, it works well enough for home monitoring.

title: Wanted to love this mount but ultimately returned
text: Excellent reviews for this mount. All of the materials were high quality. The mount itself seemed like it could hold 2 TV's! I really wanted to keep it, but ultimately couldn't. The wall mount bracket just wasn't wide enough to accommodate the extra wide VESA pattern of my Panasonic plasma TV. Would recommend this mount to anyone using a more modern day LCD/OLED TV though.

title: Very good quality with a lot of extras for the price
text: Got this set for a spare bedroom TV & Blu-ray player. The braided cables look very nice. No issues with passing 1080p signals between the TV & player. You also get some bonus items, which is very cool.

title: 15ft. worked great for my 4k home theater
text: I have no issues with the 15ft. version of this cable. Passes full 4k, HDR, Dolby Vision from my Sony 4k Blu-ray player thru my Marantz receiver out to my Vizio LCD TV. Buying the certified premium cable provides me assurance that it'll work with all of the latest HDMI 2.0a/b & HDCP 2.2 compatible products. Don't waste money on more expensive brands that promise the world but are delivering the same signal as these cables. Highly recommended.

title: High quality cable that was custom cut to my specifications

title: Great little sattelite speaker at a modest price
text: I already had 3 of these Min 22 speakers in an older 5.1.2 Atmos setup. However, I moved to a new home that didn't already have in ceiling speakers. So I bought 4 more of these to get my 5.1.2 Atmos system back up and running. Build quality and finish are excellent. These little guys put out an amazing sound for such a small speaker. Note that they will not play exceptionally loud in a large room, nor will they produce any real bass to speak of on their own; they need to be paired with a good quality subwoofer. The color matches my living room décor so it definitely complements the room. Would in-ceiling and in-wall speakers been a better décor friendly choice? Absolutely. But I didn't want to spend a bunch of (wasted) money on running wires in the walls (would have been difficult & expensive). The speakers are unobtrusive and look good. title: Excellent heavy duty mount for plasma TV
text: I was looking to hang an old Panasonic TH-50PZ850U on my office wall. Looked around a few different mounts. A Sanus model I bought at a membership store (you know which one) looked promising and worked well for my Vizio LCD TV, but it did not look strong enough candidate for my plasma TV. Another recommended brand I bought on Amazon was sturdy enough, however the VESA mount pattern on the Panny was too wide to fit onto the wall bracket itself. I searched around and then found this one. It had a wide enough wall bracket to fit the extra wide Panny VESA pattern & was rated to easily support the weight. The bracket supports the TV very well and was relatively straight forward to put together. Just be careful about the brackets that actually fit onto the TV. If you swap the left & right, you'll have a difficult time in locking down the tilting tension. It was a pain to get the TV onto the wall (over 95 lbs) & I have no desire to take it down and swap the brackets. In any case, there are plenty of ways to get the right tilt, swivel & leveling for a full motion mount. Recommended for any old heavy plasma TV's.

title: Easy to forget about
text: Forgot that I bought this a few months ago until Amazon remind me about it. Works as advertised AFAICT. As you can see from the pic, it gets a decent amount of usage. We recently upgraded our fios to 400/400 and the current bottleneck seems to be the moca adapter I use to take advantage of internal coax wiring (not this switch).
