It's maximum size is 55" and that's what I was planning to put on there exactly. It's not over the 88lb limit and honestly no where near it but it's still 55" Samsung Curved TV.

I got it on there with relative ease despite the instructions being written in the smallest available font size known to mankind. I was a little surprised that it is even holding it up. The legs at the bottom spread way out and it looks like the little rods on the legs are bending a bit. I replaced the cotter pin with a heavier duty bolt. It's not super stable and if someone bumped it I don't think the TV would survive. There is no true cable management with it really just a way to guide wires down it neatly.

For the price I really can't complain much more, but I don't like being sold a speaker mount in place of a TV mount. If it would've failed or does fail who is responsible for the damage? Just because it can hold a 55" I wouldn't recommend it for anything larger then a 46" no matter how light and even then I don't really think it's going to be stable. I can find another use for it hopefully so it won't be a total loss.

title: Excellent Ni-MH/Ni-CD Battery Charger
text: To be clear I only used this with Ni-MH batteries so I am not sure how it does with Ni-CD aka NiCad the old batteries with the memory,  It charged the NI-MH batteries very fast and completely.  This was an excellent charger and I was using some batteries I purchased from the same company a long time ago.  This is a solid company that went to great lengths to make an issue that I brought up right in the past so I decided to go to them for their charger since one of my old ones dies.  I didn't regret the decision and am very happy with the charging ability of this device.

title: Excellent Easy To Use Extender/AP
text: This would be perfect if it was AC1200 but it only does 2.4 Ghz which still needs boosting to get to my roof cameras.  I got this to extend my WiFi coverage to the roof but didn't want it to be too strong.  This was an excellent choice.  it added the range I needed with the appropriate speed and signal strength.  I used it to extend a Night hawk R8000 2.4GHz portion.  The setup was really simple and cause me no problems.  I was getting close to the 300 Mb/s transfer rate last time I checked.  My 2.4 GHz uses only IEEE 802.11 N on it so this works well.  I only used the extender portion and didn't set it up as an AP but that's all I needed it for.  You can't go wrong with this device at this price.

title: Works Great in tight places
text: This is great for cleaning air vents and between keys on a keyboard.  It leaves no residue behind which was my biggest concern with it. It looks like the goo my daughter used to play with, but it does seem to have the capability of killing bacteria. English in on bottle could be better.

title: Very Handy!!
text:
First off my only problem with this is it is a bit too big but that's almost unavoidable because of the size of the old cigarette lighter ports. Personally I don't even know why they are still in our cars. I like this adding an extra two ports while providing a 5V 2.5A USB port as well as a QC 3.0 port. The extra fuse is good to have because they can be hard to locate if you ever need to replace it. This will not work in all cars because as far as I can tell you cannot change the way it bends. You can always install it sideways if you must but most cars have multiple power ports now already.

I got this because it has the two USB charging ports while still keeping the cigarette lighter style ports available for other uses. I don't think these ports will be around much longer but they will not be going away any time soon because they are still installed in new cars. This is a really good price for all the things you can use this for. You can never have enough ways to plug/charge things.

title: Great NVR Was Great Now No Longer Listed or supported!
text:
EDIT: Can't find any upgrade firmware or anything on it. No longer even listed here as an NVR showing a camera instead. Wow was I really ripped off.

This was a very good NVR by itself. There is a long story behind this but too shorten it I was just trying to setup a fully functional security system with some fairly basic WiFi cameras. I ended up getting this in order to get all the camera's to work with a computer software called Blue Iris. Turns out with this there is no need for Blue Iris. This allowed most of the cameras even some cloud based ones to connect to it. It can use PoE, ethernet or wireless IP address to access your devices as well as RTSP streams and a whole lot more. It's still an ongoing project at this point and I fully intend on making a video of the completed system once all camera's are installed and working properly. Right now there just aren't enough hours in the day.

For now I abandoned BI completely and installed a 5 TB HDD in this NVR. I have most of the camera's working through it now and the few I don't are using a 3rd party app that I despise but until I replace those I might be stuck with. The software on the NVR is a bit confusing at first but I acclimated to it quickly. I wish it had USB keyboard support but for some reason I can't get a USB keyboard to work and I have tried many of them. It's kind of funny because a wireless Logitech trackball installed and worked fine which is what I never expected to work, but a wired USB keyboard will not as of yet. I still haven't given up but am still working to get everything working right.

There are a lot of settings and features that are available. There is also an Android app that I haven't yet tried that is supposed to work with the NVR. As soon as I can find the time I intend on updating this but for now this NVR is a life saver.

title: Incredible USB C Hub
text:
I am very happy with the Totu 12 in 1 USB C Hub. I am very impressed with almost every aspect of this device. The port placement is perfect for my needs and preferences. It has every port you could really need for the next 6 months to a year, at least considering how fast tech changes. I love the Display port on it as it's the first USB hub I have owned with a DP on it. I go through a lot of USB hubs but this one I am going to try to hang onto. The only thing I don't understand is why they bothered to put USB 2.0 ports on there when they are all backwards compatible, at least as far as I know. I'm guessing it has something to do with interference but I am not sure on that.

I think the size is perfect because of all the features, but it is a little larger the some but still extremely portable. The USB ports on this do not charge devices very well but that is normal and to be expected. I really don't use the HUB for video very often so I really didn't use graphics ports more then to test out the display port to add a fourth monitor to my system. It had no problems working with my Alienware M17xR4 with AGA, The AGA has an ASUS Rog Strix 1080 Ti in it with 2 27" Monitors and a 55" TV attached to it. I was able to add a fourth monitor using the DP on the USB hub, but the 4th monitor also worked through the video card as well. It took a little load off the graphics card but seemed to slow down the system a bit. It's kind of like using the internal monitor on the laptop when docked. I am guessing it was attempting to use the internal GTX 1080 or Intel graphics adapter but didn't confirm my theory on that. The fact that it worked at all actually kind of surprised me. My laptop usually stays docked and attached to the Alienware Graphics Amplifier. When I do take it with me this hub is a true life saver.

Data transfer rates were higher then expected even when using multiple ports at once. This is also the first USB C hub that I have found that allowed a second USB C hub to be installed on a different USB C port. Not sure if it's designed that way or just luck though. Usually both are not detected only one, but for some reason I am able to connect both and that's how it should be considering that was the goal of USB in the first place.

Overall this is one of the best hubs I have owned to date. It adds a lot of functionality for a good price. The Micro-SD and SD card readers are easy to access and use. It's very user friendly and required no real setup even in my advanced environment. That kind of shocked me to be honest. It even works with virtual machines when configured. This is an excellent product that pretty much stays connected to my system now. In my opinion it's definitely worth the price and you won't regret this purchase.

title: Standard Flat Cat 6 Cable
text: This is good quality cable.  Have it running to a WiFi camera on the roof and it works great.  Very good price for the length of the run. It would be hard to make it yourself for this price unless you already had all the tools and supplies.

title: Good Connection with Cat 6
text: Worked great extending a CAT 6 run.  No packet loss or issues using them.

title: Good Power Extension
text: This is good power extension cables for CCTV.  Works as advertised and does the job fine.  Not really much else can be said.

title: Awesome Little Alarm Clock
text:
I loved everything about this little alarm clock. First off it's small and light enough to easily take with you. I keep my ringer and notifications off on my phone for the little sleep I do get so this is great to have with me everywhere. I love the three different alarm times you can set and then just select when days you want them to be active with one switch. It is a little limited to Monday-Friday, Monday-Sunday and Monday - Saturday. However you can easily on the same switch turn it off.

The instructions were simple and easy to follow. Loved the light sensor on it. Built in thermometer is extremely useful to me. Nice bright back light when pressing the light button on top. The one button switch from 12/24 hour system is incredibly convenient for me. So far it appears to use very little battery because I installed 3 AA Amazon Basic Alkaline batteries the minute it arrived and their is no decrease in their output yet.

To be so small and priced so well this alarm clock by Octing is full of well thought out features. I was very impressed by this product and would be hard pressed to find a better value anywhere. I highly recommend this product.

title: Very Good Power Extension Cable
text:
These are good outside power cables for CCTV cameras. The connections are tight and create a good seal but I still wrap then with a water proof tape or seal inside a homemade junction box. Avoid installing outside if they are going to be exposed to direct sunlight constantly. Also I wouldn't bury these especially at any real depth but would be fine to cover with dirt to keep out of light. Make sure you wrap the connections if using outside even with the tight plugs.

Using both extension cables and have had zero problems. They are holding up well.

title: Solid Antenna!
text: This is a solid antenna and it worked great on a router after getting the corrected SMA adapter for it.  It's a bit heavy for the style connector it uses.  It would break most connectors of things it's attached to if your not really careful.  It is a really good antenna overall though.  Served my purposes.

title: Great Set of Adapters
text: This has every connector adapter you need for SMA and RP-SMA nut barrel connections for WiFi, FOV, POV, Wireless CCTV and anything else that uses SMA connections to connect an antenna.  Great product and good quality connectors.

title: Good CCTV or power extension cable
text: These I don't believe were listed for use outside but are doing just fine out of the sun and not buried.  I like the flat cables for most uses and I needed white to match the paint.  The white cable was needed to match the white background.  These are holding up really well and were very well priced.  I have had sturdier and better cables but these are exactly what they say they are.

title: High Quality
text: Works as designed and makes a great extension if needed.  No complaints here.  Great product!

title: Good Quality works outside if covered correctly
text: I needed this to split one power extension into two connectors to connect two cameras that were right next to each other.  These didn't say they were outside use but I installed them in a waterproof box and covered the connections with electrical tape for good measure.  These worked exactly as I needed them to although for the price they could've made them slightly longer after the Y on the two separate connections, but it is exactly as described.

title: Quality Low Loss RF Coax
text: This is quality low loss RF coax cable.  It worked great for replacing a bad WiFi antenna on a wireless camera.  I used to to replace the wire from the WiFi board to the bulk head.  The camera is working again and no problems thus far.

title: Great Connectors
text: These are a great set of SMA, RM-SMA both male and female.  It covers just about every kind of adapter you could possibly need in SMA.  Good quality.  Very happy with these.

title: Alright, but not great
text: It doesn't give much of a noticeable improvement over the antenna that comes with the router or WiFi camera.  I have tried it on several different devices and just can't see any real improvement.  I think this design is flawed.

title: Fairly Unique Item
text:
It was hard to find this, at least the way or reason I was going about it. I got a Noctua fan to replace the one in my Alienware Graphics Amplifier not realizing it was 12v. I didn't want to replace the PSU yet so I found this as a way to hook it up to an external power connection without having to splice or modify the chasis at all. It works like a charm and tested perfectly on my meter before I used.

This is a truly handy and unique item in my opinion. Wish I had thought of it.

title: Quality Connectors
text: Worked great for replacing a broken antenna wire going to a WiFi camera.

title: Unbranded Generic SD Card
text: I have no problems with this cad it works fine but doesn't match speeds stated but I never expected it to.  Don't know why so many people are angry about these though because they aren't pretending to be anything else.  Was free of viruses or malware and is still storing data fine after 20 formats.

title: Worked Really Well for a while
text: I'm not sure if this cable is defective or it's a poorly made cable yet.  It worked great for a while at 4K@40Hz  on a R270 Pro screen.  However after some time it started flickering and switching cables has resolved it.  I only really game at 1980x1080@240Hz for obvious reasons and the cable is still causing flickering at 240Hz setting.  Works fine on a ASUS screen G-Synced at 144Hz though.  I am giving it the benefit of the doubt since it is VESA compliant that it's just a bad cable.  Further testing will be required.  R270 Pro is working fine on a CableMatters cable right now.  I am going to contact this company and see if they will replace this one so I can see if it's just this cable or their product or maybe a in incompatibility with my display.  I will update the review as I know more.  The cable feels well made and fits properly.

title: Excellent Cable For Gaming and 3D
text: This HDMI cable is great.  It worked better then I could've hoped and I have had no problems or seen no degradation or loss of picture quality over time.  Cable is well made and flexible.  It does great with G-Sync 144Hz.  Quality product for a great price.  Will be looking at PowerBear for future cable needs.

title: Incredible Cable That Makes a Difference!
text:
It does it's job better then any other I've used in HDMI. The This cable is going to to the 55" screen and the others use DP cables. It's going to an Alienware M17xR4 with an Alienware Graphics Amplifier housing an Asus Rog Strix GeForce1080 Ti https://www.amazon.com/STRIX-GeForce-Gaming-Graphics-ROG-STRIX-GTX1080TI-11G-GAMING/dp/B06XY25VTC/ref=sr_1_3?keywords=asus%2Brog%2Bstrix%2Bgeforce%2B1080ti&qid=1580100749&sr=8-3&th=1
The cable actually makes a difference in the image quality on that screen. Although when I game I turn off all but the middle monitor or the ASUS to the left. Don't go cheap on your cables if going for quality or speed because you will end up regretting it.

title: Great Value, Speeds not true
text: These are a great value and work just fine for most things.  I even used them in WiFi cameras and haven't had any problems yet but we will see.  Regardless for the price these are a steal!  Upon further testing these test just as good as Sandisk Ultra's.

title: Cheaply made but works
text: This is a poorly made connector but at least it's actually 3 pin to 3 pin.  Most of the connectors like this 4 pin to 3 pin put two pins to one and one the the other which is fine for some fan types.  Cables does the job but has no extra shielding and is just cheap wire.  Nothing special here but it'll work in a pinch.

title: Well made and shielded
text: These were very well made and they put some shielding over it which is a nice touch.  I was really impressed with this cable and it worked exactly like I needed it to.

title: Easy to use and convenient
text: These are great for stopping the fan vibrations and replacing the screws with easy to remove pegs,  The worked perfectly but they are a bit over priced.

title: The Ansolute Best I've Used Ever!
text:
This is an extremely well thought out and designed tripod. They truly thought of everything and I don't know how they can afford to sell it at such a great price. You can adjust everything on this including each leg independently meaning you can set it up on practically any surface not matter how uneven. I have spent a lot of time with this Joilcan 80-inch Tripod and can safely say that it is incredible. It's still light enough to carry comfortably and to travel or hike with but sturdy enough for anything you want to do.

It has withstood some serious abuse and isn't even scratched. It folds down to about 18 inches and stands up to 80 inches tall. The larger then average 38mm ball bearing makes a big difference in stability and adjustability. Have better metal materials makes a huge difference as well. To top it all off the legs are much thicker then average which makes it much more durable and stable. There didn't appear to be any cheap plastic parts on this anywhere which is great. There are so many different configurations you can use to shoot your photographs. I still haven't done nearly everything possible with this yet and I have been using it for a good while. The mono-pod is even sturdy enough to safely use as a crutch or hiking stick if you needed it.

The things you can do with this and use it for are too many to even begin to count. This is probably one of the best purchases I have made and couldn't be happier with it. I have zero complaints about this tripod. I had a whole video on the many things I did with this, but unfortunately the camera with it on it was damaged before I could upload it to the cloud. Thanks so much for making such and incredible product!!

title: Good but needs improvements
text:
I hates this at first because the instructions where incomplete and impossible to read. You would think it would be simple enough to put together but it's anything but. After contracting the supplier who sent me some better instruction it only got better from there. It's size adjustable and fully setup is quite large. After finally getting it assembled correctly and using it for a while I discovered that it's actually a very good product. It's well built and the carrying case it great to have. I was able to iron the backdrop easily which is rarely the case with them. It's very light weight and that makes it a little less sturdy but the trade off is worth it.

I can't wait to try a green screen on it. Other then that they just really need to have the instruction updated and make them easy to understand. Overall this is a pretty good product and I am happy with it.

title: Worked Perfectly for the Acer Monitor
text: It worked as advertised for the Acer monitor but besides that and a few other products it's not a commonly used adapter so it really is limited once that monitor is no longer in service.  Unfortunately the monitor I got it for was cracked so I really have no use for it at the moment, but who knows if I might need it again in the future.  It was such an odd voltage/amp combo that I was afraid to try a universal adjustable adapter.

title: Good USB Hub
text:
I had no problems with this USB hub and I have been actively using it sense Mid November. It has traveled with me on many different tri[s and cam in handy too many times to count. It's a bit larger then some of the others I have used in the past and I am not particularly fond of the port placement, but that's personal preference. I haven't used the triple display function myself because I use an Alienware laptop with built in NVidia Ge-force 1070M. However I let a friend borrow it and she told me it worked wonderful but was a little limited on 4K quality.

The Ethernet connection sure comes in handy on Android devices. I had no problems with this so far and don't see any coming in the future unless it's something I cause.

title: Works but limited
text: It works but doesn't do well with high resolution.  Problems if going to a spilitter or switch.  Works fine from regular VGA-HDMI with audio AUX.

title: It Works Good
text: It's your standard SVGA cable for connecting a VGA port to a monitor.  Simple old school SVGA cable but it does exactly what it's supposed to do and there is something to be said for that.  It's a heavy cable and very well built and sturdy.  Probably the last SVGA cable I will ever purchase.

title: Very Well Made and Durable
text: This is a great cable.  It handled being pulled down an unused fireplace and run into the house connecting to an AP installed on the roof.  Great bandwidth and data speeds, so much better then WiFi was providing from that access point.

title: Great Thing to Have
text: This is a great thing to own especially when you use a lot of different A/C adapters. It's easy to lose one and they can get expensive to replace.  This has saved me a fortune in replacements.  I could use a dozen more like it but will probably try a few different brands for comparison but I am very happy with this one.  It has worked flawlessly on every device I have used it on.  It's so simple to use and is quite versatile. I don't know what I would do without mine.

title: Awesome Micro SD Card
text: I use these in a lot of different WiFi IP Cameras because they are good and they are not expensive.  Camera's recording live  are constantly writing to these depending on the setup.  After a while this type of storage degrades and will eventually die. These are cheap and disposable but they are lasting a lot longer then I expected and are well worth the price for them.  Great all around Micro SD Card!!

title: Great Performance, Name Brand for Great Price, Authentic G.Skill
text:
This is an excellently performing SD Card and it has performed and tested well. I have had no problems or degradation of this SD Card at all and it has been running in a WiFi Camera non stop recording to it since I got it.

I will definitely be using more of these in the future.

title: One of the best Ethernet cables ever. Certainly the best looking! :)
text:
This is a top of the line Cat 7 Ethernet cable. The braided nylon is not only extremely durable but it's actually quite eye catching. The gold, red, and silver imprint on it makes it sort of designer looking. If you have to have exposed cables I would go with this. It's completely flat which allows you to easily run it wherever it needs to go even under carpet. The gold plated connectors make a lot of difference at least in my opinion. I haven't gotten close to maxing out the capabilities of this cable but I will soon enough I'm sure. I'm using these as LAN-WAN patch cables and from a router to firewall. I have had no problems and have no complaints with this product. As a matter of fact I am going to buy more of these and replace most of my other cables with them.

They even have a lifetime replacement warranty which is great if you use as many cables as I do. Doubt I'll ever need it but it's nice to know it's there. This is an extremely great value and I would recommend it to anyone needing any Ethernet cables. Cat 8 is better but for the next 3-5 years it will be a little overkill for most situation and this is perfect. Incredible Product!!

title: Great Motion Video Camera, Decent Still Image Performance, Poor Closeup Still Images
text:
This is an excellent 4k UHD action camera. I've experienced no major problems with it. Does great underwater which is where this camera seems to excel. If you want it for still photography then this really isn't going to work for you, especially if you want to shoot any thing close up because it was made for movement, After speaking with the seller this camera uses a prime lense instead of a focus lense. I have not done any research into that so I am just going on what I was told.

The micro HDMI and Micro USB are both nice features but I haven't been able to transfer files with it which is a little bothersome. It does charge the battery and it comes with two batteries which is great because the battery life is not very great. Not sure why it only accepts a maximum of 64GB SD-Card because that's not a lot when recording 4k UHD video. I found it works great in driving mode as a dash cam. It does have a lot of interesting features like the adjustable view angles and finally the best feature is the touch screen. I just wish I knew a way to make it a little brighter. I am still waiting to hear back from them on that.

It really comes with a lot of great accessories including the double battery charger and the many different mount types. As I was saying before this is a good product that could use a little improvement but it excels in a lot of areas also. It's also extremely light when not in the case. The tripod in the photo's doesn't come with the camera it was just attached when I photographed it. As I said before this wasn't the camera for close up still shots but does great while driving and underwater.

This would be great for beginners and people that are just interested in taking quick videos but not for much more then that. For the price though it's a great little back up device and because it's so light and small it's east to take with you.

An update to this review might be pending depending on what I hear from the seller.

title: Great Cable, Huge Difference!!!
text: Really great cable can really notice a difference in bandwidth and speed.  I am using it between a router and an access point as an uplink/internet cable and it made a huge difference over the Cat 6 I had on there because I had forgotten about it.  I had to use it in a pinch because it was all I had at the time and really wasn't near taxing my bandwidth so it wasn't noticeable until later on.  As soon as I added a switch and brought more systems online it quickly became apparent there was a bottle neck somewhere.  You can never underestimate the importance of a cable.

title: If only it worked with Windows Hello!
text: This is almost as good as a Yubbi key and in a few ways better. I have no idea why this is so difficult.  I could understand in a DoD, MARSOC, JSOC  or other secure building and secured computers but there is no excuse for non-FIPS systems not to work just fine with this.  I don'r understand what;s so hard about this and why it isn't easily accomplished.  If I wanted to buy more Yubbi keys I could have it working kinda. First company to actually solve it and have it work with all the other sites gets my business.  Good luck!

title: Excellent Product
text: I have been using this almost everyday since I got it and it's been working great.  It is one of the first I have had that truly supports the USB C speeds.  I use it it attach mainly a encrypted USB C UDRIVE and keep 2 remaining USB C ports open.  The added Ethernet connection works great in a bind.  I was able to attach it to my Samsung S10 and use a wired connection with no problems.  This was well designed and well made.  They didn't try to make it too complicated and just perfectly functional.  I love this device and would've know what to do without it now.

title: Worked Very Well to be so Simple
text: This little device allows you to make older equipment and cars Bluetooth compatible for audio.  I like that you can insert an SD card and then send music to the card or use the USB cable to upload music to the SD card itself.  It really lasts about 8 hours on a full charge.  You cannot control the volume from the device itself that has to be done from the paired device unless I am missing something.  You can fast forward tracks and playlist songs from the device. The audio was crystal clear and it worked flawlessly.  I did change some developer options for Bluetooth on my phone though.  It shows up as X6 in your Bluetooth connections list.  Paired quickly and easily.  The SD/TF card goes all the way in I just left it out so everyone could see where and how it installs. title: Worked for HD CCTV Camera
text: I didn't test the speed of this like I usually do but it has worked just fine in a constantly recording camera so far.  I have seen no signs of deterioration or degradation in performance.  I have used Patriot before in mobile devices and things like that, but I figured I would try it out in a CCTV WiFi camera to see how it works.  I have had no problems with it and next time I remove it for maintenance I will check and update the review if need be.

title: Works As Designed, Good Quality Product
text: This worked good and was very well priced.  Worked exactly as designed!

title: Incredible Camera, Easy To Configure and  Install, Crystal Clear Image with Amazing Zoom!!
text:
This is an incredible WiFi IP Camera. The SV3C 5X Optical Zoom WiFi IP Camera is one of the best camera's I have worked with in it's price range. I was originally trying to mount this in a different location but decided that this was a good spot because it can easily be moved as well. I personally wouldn't recommend this installation to anyone because the camera can easily be stolen, especially if you don't have multiple camera's. The only wire is a power wire which is necessary for almost all good IP Cameras. It has worked with the majority of applications I have tried it on. I can easily access it home and away. It is easiest to configure while connected to the Ethernet port and then install the camera where ever you want it. I highly doubt that I am going to keep it there due to the obvious reasons and because they can get fairly warm.

The 5MP resolution make it great for larger displays and much better image quality while the digital zoom 5x allows you to zoom in anywhere in your cameras FOV. These feature alone make a big difference in quality over other cameras in this price range. It can use H.265 or H.264 compression which helps with network performance if you configure it correctly. (May require more work then normal configuration) You do have to open it up to get to the SD Card but it's very easy to do and the directions come with it in English. The Auto focus feature works really well because I usually disable it on most camera systems and this actually helped. It still takes a little time to adjust but is actually worth it.

I have had it running for two weeks and had no problems out of it at all. It has been rained on for two days and didn't have a problem so it's truly IP66 rated. This was very well built and designed camera that should do everything you need it to and more. Dynamic DNS is easy to setup and there is a place for it in the main setup screen of the camera directly from your local LAN IP address login setup. I cannot speak to it's audio capabilities because I don't use audio on my network. I can say that it will trigger the alarm and make a selected sound whenever motion is detected if you enable it.

You need to setup areas or quadrants if you want motion activated alarms that email you pictures because even on low the motion detector is very sensitive and will pick up trees blowing or anything else that moves. The email setup seems to confuse a lot of people but it's fairly simple as long as you know your ISP's outgoing mail server address. If you don't setup areas then you probably don't want any audible alarms and you certainly don't want to be constantly getting emails with 1-3 high resolution pic per message. I have configured it using P2P and ONVIF successfully with ease. I would suggest setting it up first with the simple P2P client on the manufacturers web site just to get a feel for the settings and camera's capabilities especially if you aren't familiar with surveillance system configurations.

I would highly recommend this camera to anyone needing a quick and easy security solution or to keep eyes on something valuable. The fact that it can easily be configured for offsite backup is a great thing also. I promise you will not be disappointed by this camera unless you are a security expert that is use to $1000 cameras everywhere. Please keep in mind that incorrect configuration can lead to people using your own camera to spy on you. There is always a risk when transmitting anything over WiFi especially not encrypted.

This, in my opinion, is one of the very best camera's out there you can get for anywhere near this price. You can't go wrong with this camera because it has everything you need and more for any home or civilian work security system. title: This is an Incredible Product
text:
Amazon rejected this review once because they accused of bad deed. Let me give some context. I am a private investigator and an independent journalist. Noting I did with this camera was illegal or nefarious therefore this review is not breaking any rules. I spent a lot of time using this product and this was my unbiased opinion and recommendation based on my experience with this device!

I was blown away by this camera’s versatility and its incredibly sturdy design. The instructions were well written and easy to follow. I tested this camera in some extreme conditions that it wasn't designed for and it worked very well. It held up in both high and low temperatures with no problems. I don’t advise trying this but, it was accidentally dropped into a water fountain. Luckily, I was able to recover it quickly, shut it off and remove the SD card. I let it dry for 24 hours expecting it to be dead, but both the camera and SD card were fine.

It was tested with 10 different brands and makes of 128Gb SDXC Micro SD cards. It worked with every brand card that I installed in it including Samsung, SanDisk, PNY, Gigastone, Kingston, Adata and Lexar brands. I tested it only with the Pro+, Extreme, Elite and/or Evo+ versions of SDXC Micro SD cards. The reason I tested it with so many different brands was to help you guys know for sure that whichever one you pick, that if I listed it here it worked fine. I am not recommending a brand just telling you which ones worked for me.

I loved the location of the Micro SD card slot directly above the USB connector which are protected by a cap. The audio recording could have had a little better range, but a better mic would be hard to fit inside the device. Being able to switch between audio and video recording was a huge bonus. It had exceptional battery life for the polymer Lithium 550mAH battery installed in it. I was able to get around 2 1/2 hours of 1080p video recording out of this battery. The audio recording doesn't use nearly as much charge so it'll last a lot longer. I recharged the camera over 200 times in the course of the month I tested it and didn't notice any battery degradation yet.
It recorded in both 720p and 1080p resolutions flawlessly. It did well in low light environments also. My only issue with this camera was the placement of the LED light. Its current location could unintentionally expose the device to the subject you are legally recording or interviewing. The LED should be somewhere out of sight. Even in its current location it would be difficult for the subject to notice due to the LED being dim. I believe it was designed to use a lower brightness LED for that very reason. The subject would have to be standing over you for them to notice it happened to blink for any reason i.e. low battery.

This was one of the best spy cameras I have ever used in its price range. It might seem a little plain on the outside, but it is supposed to. Overall this camera performed admirably for the month I tested prior to writing this review.

** Again, this was used for private investigation and only in single party consent states. Everything in this review was perfectly legal. I genuinely was amazed by this and felt compelled to write this review and fight for it. This doesn't in ANY way violate Amazons guidelines.

title: An Upgrade with Minor Imperfections
text: Purchased this about 3 weeks after getting a 47 in LG LED tv. The built in TV speakers left a lot to be desired, a full surround system was out of the question money wise, so figured getting a sound bar was the next obvious step. Didn't want anything too high end, nor anything with a big bulky sub woofer so settled on the LG NB2520A to keep the brand the same with the TV. While this has built in sub woofers (as tiny as they are) the bass leaves a whole lot to be desired. This is great for the room it is in, and for those in my house who are actually using it, but this is clearly a quick fix upgrade. The number of HDMI imputs is fine, given one will be for a cable box, another for 3D blu-ray player and the third for an Xbox/PS3, as well as AUX imput for an ipod or any music player i wish to play through the speakers. The thing that is most bothersome is the sound bar remote does integrate with the LG tv, but both still need to powered on and off separately (there are 2 separate power buttons on the remote, one for the sound bar and one for the TV power). Another bizarre thing is there is no auto or off dim setting for the display on the sound bar. Every time the sound bar is turned on the lcd will stay on, the only way to shut off the lcd is by hitting the sleep button on the sound bar remote once. Granted, not a deal breaker, but something as menial as that is an option on many other sound bars on the market today. For the price i paid (approx $100) i cannot complain, it is an upgrade decent enough for the occasional action flick or sporting event.

title: Works & Sounds Great...But Is Not Flawless
text: Have been using the headphone jack on my iphone in my car since i have had an iphone. Decided to give this a chance, and wow there is clearly a difference in sound quality, much much better. Like other reviews have said it does not stay snug and when driving can easily become loose. The biggest problem i have is it, for whatever reason, it did not work with my existing aux cable, which was a griffin flat cable. I figured it should work with any set of headphones or any aux cable, does not seem to be the case as i tried a pair of JVC earbuds i use with the phone and only produces sound on ones side. We will see how long i can last with this and these minors annoyances, but when it does work with the provided aux cable, it does sound fantastic. At this point i cannot go back to using the headphone jack on the iphone knowing the major difference in sound quality with the PocketDock plugged in.

title: Almost Perfect...
text:
Works extremely well, and through walls! Price was almost $80 less than Best Buy. My setup has a tv in one corner and another about 100 feet in another room with a wall between the two and work great, 1080i picture, crisp clear sound, no lag or flicker. The only down side is the IR transmitter is not currently compatible with Comcast Cisco cable boxes(due to dual band IR that comcast remotes use), so right now changing the channel from the the room with the receiver is impossible. Was told by IOgear tech support that a fix is on the way, so those with Comcast Cisco boxes, do not fear!

Would like to update that my original box was replace by IOGEAR with the newest version of the firmware and now is compatible with Comcast tv remotes. Unfortunately this box is still not compatible with my Cisco Cable Box but works great between 2 floors with my Scientific Atlanta DVR HD box.

title: The Cable/Satellite Terminator that Performs Updates during NFL Playoff Games
text:
Overall it works well. And I love the no-monthly fee part of this unit. Though the unit runs slowly, as if it runs on a 1990-circa CPU.

The setup was super easy and straight forward. Picked up about 70 channels in the Denver market. (Didn't know there were that many.) Though half of them didn't actually broadcast anything. Then I had to narrow it down to about 10 channels that broadcast meaningful contents. It took a long time to download and apply updates during the initial setup. Took about 2 hours.

The menu navigates slowly. Each action took about 3-5 seconds for the unit to finish. The OnePass makes recording a series far more complicated than necessary. I have to jump through many hoops to make it happen. On my cable remote, I can simply press the record button twice to setup a series recording.

I really like how seamlessly TiVo integrates with my Netflix, Amazon Prime and Youtube accounts and leads me directly to the episodes. It is very convenient to use and it's quite a pleasant surprise.

My only gripe is when I view a recorded program and navigate the menu, I cannot exit the menu to go back to full screen viewing of my recorded program. The "back" button only backs out to the main menu. So I have to select the recorded program and resume viewing. For live TV, I can simply click on the "Live TV" button to go back to full screen viewing.

Despite its imperfection, the TiVo with no monthly fee is an outstanding value. For those who are looking to cut the cable or ditch the dish, this is the way to go.

[Update 2017.01.24] Downgrading from 5 to 3 stars. TiVo is supposed to do periodic updates only overnight, but two Sundays in a row, the unit attempted to perform updates during the day. The first update froze the unit so we missed 3 quarters of a NFL playoff game. The second time we caught it in time, so only missed a few minutes of another playoff game.

title: No Switch Light.  Only Protects up to 90 Joules.
text:
Right off the bat, the green switch light does not turn on (is there really a light in it?) Though the power is still passed through.
According to the packaging, this surge protector only protects up to 90 Joules. That's rather weak comparing to most economy models that protect from 300 to 750 Joules.
The only highlight is its small and flat green plug. It fits in just about anywhere.
This is best served as a (short) extension cord.

title: Must Have For Flying
text:
To protect your hearing, I highly recommend that everyone uses noise cancelling headphones while flying.

Took several long flights with this set. I estimate that this has reduced the cabin noise by about 20 decibels, or about three quarters of the volume. I can still hear some hissing noise, but it really made my ears feel comfortable. And I can still hear the captain speaking loud and clear. This is much easier to carry onboard than those bulky over-the-ear models. Though I think those models may work better.

I also wear this while mowing or using power tools.

The music quality isn't good. It sounds a bit muddy even in a quiet surrounding. It's a notch below my iPhone 6's headset (which isn't a strong performer.)

title: Works well, though I have to give it a couple of chances.
text:
Works well, though I have to give it a couple of chances. When I first got it, it was making a grinding noise. So I put some bicycle chain oil in it to quiet it down. Then my car's cassette player spitted it out twice. I thought oh plucking great. I cleaned the excess oil and tried again. It has never given me a problem since. I've used it on several 8-9 hour long road trips and it never skipped a beat. It's not as convenient as those Bluetooth/FM adapters, but the sound quality is far superior, comparable to CD player.

I use it to play music with my iPhone 6 if that matters. Haven't used it for phone calls since I use a Bluetooth speakerphone.

title: Works so well for gaming, I'm being accused of cheating/hacking.
text:
I've been using a 60 Hz / 8 ms monitor for gaming. Once I switched to this 144 Hz / 1 ms Asus monitor, it made a world of difference. All movements are so smooth, it's easy to aim with FPS games. I'm now playing so well that some gamers have accused me of cheating and some game server admins have "spec'ed" me to make sure that I'm not hacking. It's quite an honor.

My old monitor was top-of-the-line when I bought it 6 years ago. Yet the Asus monitor's image quality surpasses it in just about every way. The black is very dark and the white looks like a piece of paper. The color accuracy is good and vibrant right out of the box. The stand is solid and stable.

Be sure to use the dual-link DVI cable that came with the monitor to achieve 144 Hz. I got lazy and used the old DVI cable at first, and was wondering why it didn't show the 144 Hz setting in Windows. Hope this helps you.

title: Slow Processing and Unresponsive Screen
text:
This GPS feels like a piece of outdated and crude electronics from the mid-1980's. It is slow to respond, slow to process, slow to do anything. The screen resolution and its ambiance resemble cheap kids electronic toys. Sometimes it takes multiple taps for the touch screen to register and get on with it. The LCD display quality seems to be old tech passive matrix. My 2002 Lexus RX300's navigation system works much better and runs faster than this (yes, 2002.) Even the old Magellan that we bought 5 years worked better than this. Not sure why so many others give this unit such a high mark.

It is also not very intuitive. It took us 20 minutes to figure out how to turn down the stupid clicking sound, and we are both computer savvy. And it took 2 hours to pinpoint our location for the first time, even though we put it on the deck with wide open view to the sky (no trees, no clouds.)

Yes, it will get my wife from point A to point B, but it's frustrating to use. It's 2014, we demand better.

title: Outstanding Zoom Lens.  So-so Picture Quality.  SkyDrive Upload Works but Not Convenient.
text:
This compact camera has an outstanding zoom lens. And it reaches to 18x zoom quickly with little noise. Though like most compact digital cameras, the 18x zoom is exaggerated. It's more like 6x to me. It has a wide angle lens so it's great for taking group photos. I didn't have to read the manual to figure out how to use this camera. It's quite intuitive, the way technology should be.

The picture/video quality is not as good compared to my other cameras, which is fine in this low price range. The colors seem washed out a bit compared to my iPhone 5's and Sony Cybershot's. Its anti-shake feature seems to work well.

Samsung puts the flash at a location where my finger can block it partially, so need to be careful when taking flash photos. It does not come with a separate battery charger. We can spend all day taking over 200 photos and a few videos, yet it still have a bit of battery life left.

Overall this camera is easy to use, easy to hold and priced right. If you want a long zoom compact camera at a low price, this is a great buy. Those who want high quality photos should look elsewhere.

Update 4/23/2013 - The SkyDrive upload works now, which allows backing up photos while traveling (without lugging along a laptop.) Apparently SkyDrive has decided to increase the file size limit. It does not allow bulk upload. I need to select each photo to be uploaded, not very convenient when we take 200+ photos in one day.

title: Overall it's good, but misses the mark on OC and video card - what gamers need
text:
Pro:

Very good clearance for over-sized CPU cooler
Auto OC feature for OC beginners
Very stable board @ 100% load 24x7
Good suite of utilities from Asus
Tons of USB ports
Outstanding audio, quite a standout from the rest

Con:
No space between the two PCI-E slots, so the first video card gets little airflow and runs hot in a dual card setup (SLI or Crossfire)
Its built-in auto OC feature can only OC the i7 2600K to 4.4GHz*
* can be manually tweaked to go higher.
Once OC'ed, the M/B creates serious radio interference to garage door opener
Cannot control the secondary CPU fan speed
No DVI port
No built-in Wireless LAN

Overall it works fine, but I would've bought something else if I got to do this all over again

title: Great LCD HDTV and an outstanding value
text: Got it for $1,700 shipped vs. $1,900-$2,300 sold elsewhere.  Great high definition picture and very good standard definition.  The best viewing angle of any LCD screen that I've seen.  Sound quality is atypical, with good simulated bass.  Built-in virtual surround sound eliminates the need for a home theatre system except for audiophiles.  Like most LCD, it does not do black color well.  Human skin tone looks cartoonish at closeup, a negative for this set.  There is no blur motion, even with NASCAR.  The on-screen menu is very easy to navigate, so no need to read the manual on the CD.  Lots of connectivity options on the back and a few jacks on the side for camcorder (no HiDef.)  Auto-sizing is always correct on screen size - unlike some other HDTVs that sometimes get it wrong.  There is a green/red status LED so that I know whether the TV is actually on or in standby mode (less than 1W with EnergyStar.)  The set is heavy at 110 pounds, but that also helps deter theft I reckon.  The shining and narrow black frame is absolutely beautiful.  Overall, I highly recommend this 52" monster.

text:

Looks good on the dash and the safety features of the ADAS do work fairly well but it does often have a hard time distinguishing a two-lane road or highway as the one lane that I occupy. Like another review I read and I agree with, is that it does have some bastardized version of Android because I tried putting in a standard Android app and it would not take it.

The voice prompts can't really be understood. Not because the speaker isn't good or anything but it's in some kind of mix between a bad English speaking Chinese person and a real British accent. The manual is no help in telling you what the voice prompts are supposed to be saying. In fact it wasn't until just recently that I figured out what one of the prompts was.

The software isn't as good as it can be. On the main screen it displays your speed as kilometers per hour which is great if your country uses metric. Here in the United States we use miles per hour and there's absolutely no way that I found that I could change the speed display to mph. By the way there's almost no piece of tech that I can't figure out. Just saying. The manual again was no help in this matter.

As many times as I put it to the setting to recognize my cell phone network time and date it will not sync the correct time and date of my cell phone. So I had to use a little trig to figure out how to get it to at least go into night mode when using the GPS when it started to get dark because the time and date would never program correctly in the automatic mode. Try manual mode you say, yeah tried that, it never saves it.

A month into owning it the unit stopped recognizing the memory card that was in it. I removed it cleaned it reinserted it still did not recognize it. I removed it again cleaned it some more put it back in it recognized it but asked for it to be reformatted.

I'm going to be eating a lot of humble pie if this unit doesn't last at least 1 year. My wife for one can't wait till I'm eating that humble pie.

My verdict: Not worth the over $200 price tag. Maybe half that would be a reasonable price.

Update 5/29/20

So the camera just went out today and anything slightly bright just white washes the screen it's horrible this didn't even last a month! Another thing I forgot to add before was the keyboard that pops up when trying to enter a GPS address is a lot of it is still in Chinese. The picture show the difference between the front Cam and the rear cam at night.

title: FANTASTIC for a Graduate Student
text:
I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.

text:

However, I always felt lacking, as everyone at all the airports always carried these far superior looking Swiss packs -- and I needed to get one too!

Sure glad I did. This thing is nice. Carries my 15" dell with PLENTY of room for leftovers. I'd venture to guess that there is no way I could use all the space. What I can say is, when I fly out this coming tuesday for a one day trip, that I won't need a suitcase of any kind. I'll just pack my tablet and clothes inside of it.

I'll be the envy of other non-Swiss pack owners, and hopefully they'll see the value in making the switch as well. Now -- if I could only get my hands on an iPhone 6.

I was streaming an old standup comedy (thanks to it having wireless internet connectivity...how awesome is that?) and the picture...streaming over the internet...came across in blu-ray quality.

The set-up on this thing is so intuitive, it's not even funny. The remote it comes with will be powering all of your add-ons within mins of turning the TV on for the first time. Don't remember the codes? Don't worry, Vizio has you covered.

My only "con" I have w/ the TV, isn't even with the TV itself. It's the remote. Poor design. Feels very cheap and the qwerty keyboard slide out is horrible. I've gone ahead and paired my apple bluetooth keyboard to the TV and that problem was solved.

I ordered this TV directly through dell.com. With 3 year extended warranty, tax, etc. It was delivered to my tv stand for $1600.xx

Buy this tv.

title: Simple to Use and Dependable
text:
I did a lot of research before making this purchase. I'm training for my first half marathon and wanted something that could track my distance and time, as well as my heart rate...but at the same time I needed it to be very simple. This watch had great reviews across the board.
Each day you run the watch has to reset position (unless you just wear it throughout the day). Do not hit the GPS button until you are outside and clear of your home/building. A couple of times I tried to get a jump start on the watch and hit the button while getting ready inside. My run was off by nearly 200 feet. This may not seem like a lot but when you are running multiple miles it adds up.
As long as you hit the GPS button while outside though you won't have any problems. It was dead on every time when I did this.
The battery life lasts (depending on your distance) about four days with consistent use.
It recharges very quickly so if you run in the morning and at night, you will easily have a full charge prior to your second run...typically takes 3 hours or so for a full charge from completely dead.
Definitely recommend the watch, especially for beginner and intermediate runners.

title: Prepare to Contact the Geek Squad
text:
I bought a new laptop and didn't want to slow it down by downloading a bunch of software of music or videos. So, I purchased this product. When it arrived I plugged it in and transferred all of my iTunes music and videos immediately. I also put Rosetta Stone onto it. There was a constant humming sound but I didn't think much of it - assumed it was just working. I left it plugged in and put the computer on the table. I came back about a week later and tried to access my song files. No go. The computer would no longer even acknowledge that the Seagate FreeAgent was attached. I shut it all down, unplugged the Seagate, waited and then restarted everything...No go. I put the Seagate on a second computer - nothing. I tried a third computer - Nothing. I no longer have access to any of my files. All iTunes downloades are permanently locked away and cannot be accessed. Luckily Rosetta Stone had CDs but as for any other files, they're gone forever.
I tried Seagate and was told to retry what I had already tried which obviously did not work. Basically I paid for a black brick. I would not put any money towards this product or company again. I can't even begin to replace all that was lost.

title: Worth the Money
text: Every where I go I carry a camera.  You never know when you'll need to video or photograph something or someone.  When I purchased this camera I was very excited to see how it held up.  There really are only two settings you'll use - video and basic photograph.  But I have to say, I've never seen a camera take such sharp photographs as this camera.  You literally just point and shoot and the contrast is amazing.  The video footage is very clear but you'll need to make certain that it's completely in focus prior to hitting the record button. If not, the camera will take about a minute to refocus so the first part will be somewhat blurry.  Once in focus the camera may as well be a full-fledged video camera.  The sharpness is as distinctive as the protographs it produces.  I love this camera and everyone who has seen the photographs have gone out to buy one for themselves.  It's literally dummy-proof.

text: I don't know why I keep buying Fire tablets for my kids. Probably because they are so much cheaper than ipads. I think I would have been better off just paying for ipads after how much time I've spent fixing problems for my kids' Fire tablets. We even bought Free Time and there are still problems where apps won't load, won't open. The charging cable is loose for each tablet and has to be positioned a certain way for each tablet to charge. I thought it was a problem with the cable or maybe a one kid's tablet but each tablet has that problem. We have even tried different charging cables. It's like we have a system where we prop the tablet up with the charging cable plugged in and supported so it can't move. No one is allowed to touch anything or else it won't charge. We talked to friends and their Fire tablets have the same problem. My daughter's tablet is constantly shutting off while she is in the middle of using it. I am so tired of apps not opening and having no idea why it isn't working. There are so many ads on the Fire tablets. I wish I would have known that before. I definitely don't recommend getting a Fire tablet for your kids. It is not worth the savings. Just buy the ipad. Trust me, and take my advice!

title: Super Easy / Very affordable alternative to the subscription plan
text:
Had the system for a little over a year now, and a good 6 months were with the free cloud storage. I like the cloud storage, but I just don’t need another bill. At the time, the USB storage was not ready, but finally it came and for 14.99, it’s well worth the price! Click it in, get a notification, confirm the code and your recording clips again!

In testing the process, it records exactly as the cloud did, the clips are 100% viewable and deletable on the app. The only note, the clips load almost instantly on the cloud, but take maybe and extra second using the USB (who cares). All other functions (zones, clip length, sensitivity, etc…) are all present. The only features I noticed not available are the “snapshot” mode, which takes a photo each hour and plays them back, and the “Edit” mode for the cloud (where you can delete large groups of clips at once, instead of each one during view on the USB). Would I like these features, yes, do I consider it a deal breaker for paying the subscription fee? Absolutely not.

Great system for the price, and incredibly easy to use. The USB gives the recording back at a great price!

title: Excellent Camera for all!  I give it  4 1/2 stars
text:
I purchased both the Canon S40 and the Canon G2 just before Christmas. The G2 was for me and the S40 was for my girlfriend. The reasoning was I thought that the "Bulky sized" G2 would be good for the "serious" shots and the "Light" S40 would be for the "fun party" casual pictures. I was wrong. First of all the Canon G2 is a fine camera and for the most part takes nice pictures. Here are the good points of the S40.
Size of Camera
First it is lightweight, easy to hold and easy to put a shirt pocket (but for a short while, if you needed both hands for something else).
Picture Quality
The still picture quality is very good to excellent but I still feel that a good 35mm still has a slight edge in quality. Every once in a while about 1 in 10 one comes out blurry, but if you can with a digital camera you can take it again. Motion pictures (object is moving) are ok but I have not had a lot of luck with the quality again the good 35mm would win. The video quality is fair to good and at a 30 second time limit we only use it for fun or when our sheep dog a does something silly it just quicker to video tape it on the Camera are email it too friends! That is really nice.
Cameras ease of use
This is where the Canon S40 really shines. This camera is very easy to use it's an almost pick up and use right away. If your not sure about a button Canon User manuals very user friendly. To view the picture, just slide the Power/Replay Lever to the right and there you go. This is a very simple Camera to use it is fro the first time user or the experienced photographer. The battery life is good, it last for almost a complete dinner party sometimes I wish I had two of them. I do like that the battery comes out and goes into the mini charger with is easy to take along rather than the bulky one the G2 came with.
Print quality
I may write about this later as me printer is old put I have printed an 8 by 10 at a friends house and wow it looks great!
Recommendations
Get the largest Compact flash card available i.e. 128 or 256 they are really getting inexpensive. You will be happy you did. Second get a Palm pilot screen protector (cut to size) for the LCD monitor you will be happy when you do. And third get a card reader for picture transer to you PC, they are work the same price is not a factor and if you have Windows XP it will recognize the card reader and install its own software.
This is a great Camera all in all I am glad I bought the 4-mega pixel instead of the 3-mega-pixel version. You will truly enjoy it as for the G2, well look for it on Ebay!

title: Know your battery's charge before you fly.
text:
Such a simple tool. But, probably one of the most important for you to carry when you take your RC out to play. I have several RC aircraft and vehicles that use LiPo batteries. I charge the batts before I go out. Then, check each one, before I connect it to the RC.

This battery checker from Fly RC checks the overall battery charge and the level of each cell. This helps identify a dying or defective battery and prevents the failure, damage or loss of your aircraft or RC vehicle. The checker works with five different battery types and has near perfect accuracy. Five stars.

title: Great economy pack of excellent flash drives.
text:
My BIL recently asked me to restore a Microsoft Surface tablet that he purchased through eBay. It already had someone else's credentials and was locked. I spent hours, days, gathering the required components and instructional material to perform that task. (Note: Microsoft was a pretty decent source. But, I still had to modify their instructions somewhat to get the job done.) One thing I needed was a specific size flash drive. I didn't have one. So, I ordered these. I didn't need this many. But, I always have a use for them and they don't go bad. So, why not?

These MicroCenter flash drives are great. Using the latest (USB3.1) drivers, they connect instantly. They are already formatted to FAT32, the most common platform. They have a tiny red LED to indicate data activity. 64GB is plenty of storage for most of my uses. The speed at which they transfer data is fast enough for anything I could use them for. Good purchase.

title: Perfectly ruggedized tablet!
text:
If you have read any of my other reviews, you know that I always tell you why I ordered the product. I also sometimes give a backstory. This one deserves both.

First, how I consider myself to be an authority on ruggedized computers. I have spent several years in the telecommunications industry. We always used ruggedized laptops and tablets in the field. And, as a police officer and paramedic, we also used these tools. Finally, I spent 13 years of my professional life as an information technology manager for the federal government. I supported all the branches that used this type of equipment in the field. So, I know this type of equipment from the user's standpoint, AND the support side.

This tablet from HOTWAV is exactly the type of equipment I would send out to the field with any operation, with confidence.

It should be noted that this device is heavy. It must be to endure all the abuse it takes. Anything less will wind up being repaired or trashed within a week of being deployed. I know. I have repaired or rebuilt countless machines that were not well suited for work in the field. The metal body (with heavy rubber guard) and Corning Gorilla Glass face make this device extremely durable. You'd have to intentionally abuse it to damage it. It's also highly water resistant. All ports are well sealed. Even the speakers are waterproof. The hand strap ensures that you won't accidentally drop your tablet when used.

I wanted a tablet like this to use in the field for my drone operations. I'm always outdoors, in all kinds of weather and often in very austere conditions. I needed a tablet that could stand up to the harshest of environments. This is the one.

Now, about the I.T. side of things. The RAM and ROM are excellent as is. And the ROM can be expanded up to 1TB by simply inserting a micro-SD card with the capacity you need. The octo-core processor is incredibly fast. It handles multitasking with ease. You can install the SIM card for any carrier you want, and the device is then service ready as a comms unit. The drone piloting business has gotten very complicated with the new legal requirements. Having cellular comms has become particularly important in that respect.

The Android 12 OS is very intuitive and full of features. Syncing this tablet to another Android device and duplicating all your apps and other features is effortless.

The display is bright and crystal clear, even in the brightest daylight. The front and rear 16MP cameras are good enough to serve most utilitarian needs. Granted, they don't match the quality images of most cell phones. But, this is not the sole purpose of this tablet. I've included a couple of shots with the camera to illustrate the clarity of the images. they're good enough for my purposes.

I am very pleased with this HOTWAV ruggedized tablet. I'm more than happy that I am adding it to my 'Drone Operations Go Kit'. In fact, my BIL is a crane operator and spends a lot of time sitting on his butt in the crane, waiting for his turn at the task at hand. He spends a lot of that time online. I'm sure he'd like one of these to help pass the time. Good purchase.

text:

The quality of the sound is definitely Sony. Nice deep rumbling bass and crisp clear treble. The top end volume will rattle windows and is crystal clear. No vibration, or crackle. I'm very happy.

title: Just like the ones that came with the dash camera.
text:
I traded my Jeep in for a GMC 2500HD pickup truck. I kept my radar detector and dash camera. I bought these clips to run the wiring around the windshield with.

These clips are exactly the same as the OEM clips that came with the dash camera. They are well designed and well made. The clip has two ways to run the wires. One way is to just lay the wire in the clip and snap it shut. The other way is through a split-ring, built into the clip. I was able to run three wires (radar detector, dash camera power and rear camera lead) through the clips and they are still securely fastened.

The 3M tape on the clips holds very well. However, you will need to do what you can to prevent the cabin from getting too hot. Extreme temps will cause them to loosen and fall off. Here in central Texas, it gets really hot in the summer. I use a windshield sun guard to keep the cabin a little cooler. I also installed some AVS window vent shades. I'm able to leave the windows cracked just a little. This also helps to keep the cabin a little cooler.

This very economical pack of 100 will help a lot. I have two more vehicles to tidy up. This is a great product at a very low price. Five stars.

title: Much better sound (and a light show)!
text:
[[VIDEOID:e1ecfa5e6b7fdff679f691ee32a8937f]] I have a very nice laptop with Bang and Olufsen built-in speakers. But, they could never sound as good as a nice set of external speakers.

I watch a lot of videos and listen to music through my laptop and was always left wanting for better sound. I ordered this set of Nylavee speakers based on a recommendation from a 'gamer' friend.

Being a gamer, a lot of his experience is based on the light show. I got to watch and listen as he went through some multi-player war games and was really impressed with the quality of the sound coming from his speakers. I'm not a gamer. The light show wasn't that important to me. However, the color changing LEDs are pretty cool. So, I bought this set for myself.

Here at home, I'm still impressed at the sound. The treble is nice a crisp. The bass is good enough that I don't think I would need a subwoofer set. The lights are easily controlled through the touch switch at the top of the right-hand speaker.

I have only one nit to pick at. The speaker's faces should be mirror images of each other, not duplicate. The way they are now, it looks like two left speakers, instead of a left and right. This is minor. But, still bugs me.

Otherwise, this is a really good set of computer speakers for the money and I am very comfortable with giving these Nylavee speakers five stars.

title: Lacks one critical feature, electronic image stabilization.
text:
This is a great camcorder for the price. It has a lot of wonderful features. It would be great, set up on a tripod or for any other static position, where the camera itself is not moving. The 4K is crisp and clear. The stereo mic produces true stereo audio recordings. The touch screen menu makes navigating through the features a breeze.

But, as a 'portable' camcorder, intended to be handheld and mobile, it's missing the EIS function or 'anti-shake' as many manufacturers call it. Without EIS, even the smoothest movement by the camera operator is still going to result in shaky video and blurry images.

So, awesome for stationary stuff. But, not so much for action shots.

title: For the vinyl enthusiast.
text:
Wifey has a vast collection of vinyl. She has about 200 albums stored in her player cabinet and only God knows how many more, stored in large plastic totes. A lot of these albums are rare and collectable, fetching big money on the vinyl trading market. We will sit in her office/nest talk, and just listen to music.

There is something about music recorded on vinyl. No, it's not the best medium for the purest sound. But, it DOES have a quality to it that has been lost to all the new tech out there. It's warm, rich and even the little pops and clicks you hear from well worn records is somehow comforting.

This little record cleaning kit helps us preserve the quality of the records and the music on them. It's simple, easy to use and worth every penny. We clean every record before we play it. And, using the included gel, we clean the stylus at the beginning of every session. Good purchase.

title: Perfect replacement for your cordless phone batteries.
text: Our cordless phones are about 12 years old. The batteries finally gave out. These are perfect replacements. They have a slightly longer plug wire than the OEM ones. I'm sure that's so they can reach the plug on various models. The batteries work just fine and I'm sure that they will last another 12 years.

title: It depends on the power grid and your home's wiring.
text:
I read a lot of reviews on this thing, before I bought it. There were just as many bad reviews as good ones. So, this leads me to believe that how well it works depends a lot on how efficient the power grid in your neighborhood is, and how well your home was electrically engineered.

We live in a new subdivision with a state-of-the-art power grid. Our home, being only 12 years old, was very well designed, maximizing electrical efficiency at every circuit. I have only noticed a slight decrease in my electric bill. So slight, that I can't say it was cooler weather or how well this thing works.

I can't say that this is an inferior product. I'm sure that folks living in older homes in older communities can benefit from it. It just didn't do much for me.

(I didn't rate it for traveling. That's kind of a stupid thing to rate this product on. Why would you want to take this with you on the road?)

title: Hisense is my new favorite brand of TV!
text:
[[VIDEOID:267840d14ce75413e8d122dc58af11f8]] I bought a Hisense TV for my garage, as you can see it hanging on the wall. (I watch TV while I'm detailing my bike or working on other projects.) I liked it so much that when it came time to replace the TV in the living room, I went with Hisense again. I was not disappointed!

The Hisense new 'Quantum ULED' has a picture that is better than any other TV at this price point. (I did a lot of research.) The blacks are REALLY black. title: A shift in function.
text:
There has been an unpleasant shift, from who is responsible for supplying the power adapters for USB powered appliances. And, for the number of simple household appliances that now require those adapters. I suppose that I can see the logic in it. Newer electrical devices now require lower power. Thence, adapters. At first, they came with the device, like cell phones were supplied with the wall adapters. Eventually, you had to buy your own adapters. Even now, you have to be careful in selecting an adapter. There are basic ones that only have 3 amps. Some have 5 amps or more. Some only split all their power between multiple ports. Some are 'smart' and provide all the amps needed to multiple devices. Now, that's pretty much the rule. You gotta do it yourself and you better know what you're looking for. Disappointment is more common than satisfaction, in this new game.

These outlet adapters from Mifusa probably wouldn't have been my optimum choice, had the listing been a little more informative. But, based on what I read and how it works, it will do well enough.

The six outlets are too close together for bulky plugs or those that have the transformers built into the plugs. The total amperage across all three USB ports is only 3 amps. So, don't look to power multiple USB devices efficiently. BUT, you CAN plug six AC (that's alternating current, not air conditioning) of a low enough power draw, and three USB powered devices, IF they will all fit in the MIFUSA device, and know that they also have surge protection, as indicated by the little green light.

One star being crap and five stars being spectacular, I rate these as being 'okay'.

title: Definitely has the true audiophile 'wow factor'!
text:
[[VIDEOID:1be91bfc02339bd396543d05da1fee38]] There are SO many things about the Angel's Horn turntable that impress me. But, first, you need to be a true audiophile to appreciate the way this turntable was designed and built.

Gone are the days of the automatic turntable, where you just drop on a stack of records and walk away. Those things were the WORST! Sure, you were free to do other things for longer periods of time. But, they were very harmful to your records. A true collector would NOT even consider having one of those things.

First, the body of the turntable is ONE SOLID PIECE OF OAK! No particle board, no hollow box, no cheap crap!

Then, there is the direct one-belt drive, no multiple gears or belts. And the motor has ONE job, the turntable. Changing the records and setting the tonearm are YOUR job, as is true with any turntable worth it's status as 'top of the line' with this one.
