text: These are decent sturdy stands for the price.  They do the job for smaller, rear surround sound  speakers.  My only complaint is that the key hole mounts were too large for my Samsung speakers.  I had to drill out the keyholes on the back of my speakers a bit to make them fit.  So, either Samsung’s keyholes are not standardized, or the pegs on these stands aren’t.  Overall though I like the stands.  They are stylish and work well.  Check the height for your intended use.  I originally wanted to place them behind my sectional, but the stands were too short so they were lower than the sectional back.

title: Decent for the price
text: These speakers are ok when connected to my Samsung soundbar/subwoofer.  They are not completely wireless, as you must connect speaker wire to the hub which then connects wirelessly to the soundbar.  Speaker wire should be longer, especially for those using this in a larger area.  As to sound quality, this is not for someone looking for a deep, rich, powerful surround sound experience.  I like to watch music concerts and videos and this set up is a bit lacking for my personal preference.  You must set rear speaker level to six, the highest setting, to really produce much sound.  The instructions that come with them are very, very lacking.  I had to research how to utilize the settings, such as equalizer and rear volume control on the internet.  It is pretty good for basic television watching and ok for movies, but not a system in which you’re going to feel immersed in sound.  Overall. considering the price and style I’m pleased with the speakers.  The set up was easy and they have worked consistently since I got them.  I would recommend if you’re not concerned about high end audio but are just looking for a basic system to enhance the sound of your tv viewing.  Very basic and average for listening to music via Bluetooth from a tablet or phone.  Audiophiles will be disappointed.

title: Nice Device for Nightstand
text: I bought this device primarily to use as a fancy alarm clock.  It is a nice looking device and looks really sharp and modern on the night stand.  I also bought the premium swivel and tilt stand which I like a lot and makes adjusting the device to exactly the position you like very easy.  Sound quality is similar to the 3rd gen echo dot.  I would not recommend if you are considering this to listen to music, although it does ok for low level casual listening.  Voice recognition is good and the display is clean and clear, albeit small.  This is not a device I’d want to watch movies on, but the size is ok for short term viewing (think about size of a cellphone screen).  Several different options for clock face, or you can customize with your own personal photos.  Like many other reviewers, I do not like the “try this” suggestions which constantly come up on the screen.  It’s like an Amazon propaganda machine.  Yes, you can switch off the continuous rotation in settings, but you cannot turn if off completely.  Every time you interact with this Echo, you have to endure a brief period of “try this” suggestions.  Cannot understand why Amazon does not do something to get rid of this as so many users have raised it as a issue.  I like the device and will most likely keep it, but I do wish the display was more customizable and that I could completely shut off the “try this” suggestions.

title: Nice Device

If sound quality for music is important for you this is not your answer, although I don’t believe it was designed to function primarily as a speaker. It functions well as a
smart device to control paired outlets, lights, etc. and other functions and skills offered via the Alexa app. Although some skills still need some serious work, for example the a DirectTv app is spotty and works inconsistently for me. This is not related to the device itself however. I also do not like the new power cord on this one. Previous version had a standard usb/charging style cord that could be plugged into a charging cube, or a port on a computer, alarm clock, tv, etc. This generation device does not, but rather just has a standard type 120 cord. Not a deal breaker for me, but not as convenient as my old dot which I just plugged into the back of my alarm clock and didn’t have to take up another electrical outlet. Al in all, a decent device that performs as advertised. If you want something for better sound quality for music, I would recommend considering an upgrade to the larger Echo device.

title: Where's the documentation?
text: Very heavy keyboard. Certainly doesn't feel like a mechanical keyboard. The tiny insert offers ZERO CLUES as to how the keyboard is supposed to function, ie there is no documentation. The web site reads more like an ad, no clues there, either. The flashing color LEDs remind me of a 1980s video arcade game. You can reduce the brightness down to zero but that's about it. There's a really ugly and difficult to read quasi-sci-fi typeface used on the key caps. The keyboard itself is quite nice, quite heavy. Little kickstand-type feet if you want it angled. A small plastic ramp is included if  you want to rest  your left hand. What's missing here is a MANUAL of some kind. Even a PDF would be just great. Otherwise it's a mystery how this keyboard is supposed to work, what the features are. Somebody blew it. It's nicely designed with some interesting features, but unless you enjoy hardware sleuthing, how are you supposed to know what works, and how it works? Rather maddening. So I don't see this being used, I'll go back to my older keyboard which actually has mechanical clickity click key responses. It's baffling that with  the attention to detail paid to this keyboard that they wouldn't include or provide some DOCUMENTATION. It's basic.

So something like this is ideal for my purposes, plenty of teats on the hog and a shore power supply. It's surprising how quickly HDDs, fans, lights, scanners populate your physical desktop, and all of them want a USB port, it seems like. The killer thing about this (nicely packaged btw) USB port is its style, with COOLING FINS -- now, how hot is a USB port going to get? Not that hot, right? But what a great look, masculine, intractable, like Darth Vader(tm) with the shiny black plastic finish, but the COOLING FINS totally slay me, they look awesome. Please see photo.

title: A nice surprise
text:
Surprisingly robust sound in a desktop package. Please refer to photos.

I'm a long-time Logitech fan, so my expectations were fairly high. The speakers were nicely packaged and easy to set up. Wordless instructions for neophytes were printed on the flaps of the box, impossible to miss as you opened it.

The bass unit is surprisingly thin given its sound. Small footprint. The left and right speakers are heavier than they look. The control puck has a Bluetooth connection button you press for three seconds to scout around for a Bluetooth source. It's also got an on/off switch and the entire face of it is a volume control. There's a bass control on the back of the bass which I left at about halfway.

The Bluetooth connection is functional, but pales in comparison to the wired connection. The novelty isn't really worth it. My understanding is that Bluetooth was not intended to carry sound. For whatever reason, the wired connection is much better.

Plenty of wire to separate channels. The sound is very good for a desktop setup, and by that I mean when I listened to songs I am familiar with, each instrument was nuanced and shaded, for lack of a better word, distinct and separate. I've never heard better sound from a system this size, really impressive. Nothing muddy or blurry about it.

Bluetooth aside, this sounds so much better than previous desktop speaker solutions I've tried it's hard to compare them. This has genuinely good sound. It's not going to fill a room, but it's an outstanding personal sound solution. I'm not a fan of headphones or earbuds, so this is ideal.

This would make an excellent gift.

title: There are more robust dashcam solutions out there
text:
Frustrating. Could not get the iPhone app to work at all, I'd slide the WiFi button to be informed that the WiFi was not functioning. Do I need to set up a local hotspot to use the WiFi feature to download the videos? Which appears to be about the only distinguishing feature of this dashcam. This is NOT a Sony product, apparently it uses licensed Sony technology. The dashcam itself is reasonably well designed. There's a horrid mechanical-female voice which I don't see how to disable. The user experience overall is poor. The manual is not bad as far as legibility, but the content is minimum. Minimal content in four or five languages.

The mounting scheme is atrocious, a joke. I'm not going to put self-adhesive cable anchors anywhere in my car, period. It's just plain dumb. I'm tempted to use a suction cup mount from another dashcam. Or cable ties on my rear-view mirror. But if you're homebrewing a solution right out of the box, maybe you're better off with another product altogether. The mounting suggestion is just a show-stopper. Not a good thing.

The video itself seems good, I mean, dashcams in general are fascinating and useful. But if you're expecting to have consumers put something in their car, it had been not involve defacing any part of the car or reducing its value. Leftover adhesive footprints would be an obvious problem.

I'm uploading a photo of the box. Green type on a black background. Not really a great design. Generally type and packaging tells you more about a product than the manufacturer might have intended. Just not that sophisticated.

Overall there are better dashcams out there. The ability to use WiFi to download video from the camera seemed promising, but I couldn't get it to work at all. The audio feedback from the device was far too loud and I couldn't turn it off. The mounting idea was dead on arrival, not happening.

Disappointing. Cannot recommend this product. A swing and a miss, as they say in baseball.

title: Excellent Toslink cable
text: Another brilliant Amazon Basics product -- great attention to detail, perfect functionality and a great price. Could not be happier. You'd expect to pay more for this cable and not be assured of its quality.

title: Good quality cable for BNC home surveillance cameras
text: Neat solution! Good and long (60 feet!) with a BNC connector and a 12V jack on either end, this also includes two male-to-male BNC connectors, which is really thoughtful. Good thick cable. A very good value.

title: Unique solution to the problem of two female BNC connectors
text: Unique and handy solution to the problem of two female BNC connectors. Keep a bag of these in your tool box to keep headaches to a minimum!

title: Very useful four-tail 12V power supply for home surveillance cameras
text: Clever and useful 4-tail 12V power supply for home surveillance cameras -- no more fighting for a teat on the power strip, one power block with four tails is a much smarter way to go.

title: Excellent subwoofer cable
text: Excellent quality, not any longer than it needs to be. Excellent attention to details, well-designed. Exceptional value compared to at least one brand of overpriced cables that I won't mention. Say goodbye to annoying, hard-to-trace hum from your subwoofer. Another excellent Amazon Basics product.

title: Zero results
text:
This just did nothing whatsoever, no matter where I positioned it, indoors or out. I could pick up one UHF station from Mexico. It looks neat, but it just didn't function at all for me and we live on a hill in a suburban area. The front cover of the box was full of typographical errors, which didn't inspire confidence. The product itself is nicely made.

I received this unit for review purposes at a deep discount.

title: Outstanding quality in an everyday electronics item.
text: Another outstanding AmazonBasics product. The cable itself is supple and not at all stiff. The plugs are large enough to easily grasp. The ferrule surrounding the male jacks are well designed and well made. The yoke where the RCA L and R jacks branch off is reinforced, not a simple join. Overall, the quality is excellent. What I admire is that EVERY AmazonBasics product I've had occasion to try has been equally as well designed and produced. It's brilliant to address lower-end everyday items and to produce a superior product to what's available in the marketplace. Rather than buying a cheap and cheaply made 3.5 to RCA L/R cable, buy this one, which is clearly built to last.

title: Interesting HDMI Audio Extractor -- an audio skeleton key
text:
An interesting and unique kind of "skeleton key" for HDMI audio. Please see photos of inputs and outputs. ** I received one of these units for review purposes at low/no cost **

This comes beautifully packaged and once you pry it out of its soft foam sleeve the product itself is very attractive, that kind of shiny hard plastic Darth Vader(tm) black material. It's not too big, either, smaller than an AppleTV. The vertical edges are nicely curved. It's far from ugly. Both a good package design and a good product design inspire confidence.

There's a panel with the power switch and lights indicating 2.1, 5.1, 7.1 and ARC (Audio Return Channel) operation, on another panel is a 3.5mm headphone jack, a Toslink socket and HDMI input and output. A third panel is for the included 5V power adapter.

Now, what I've been struggling with along with some other users of Windows 10 is the fact that, apparently, if your motherboard manufacturer didn't pay a fee to Dolby Labs, no matter what you do you cannot get a 5.1 stereo surround sound option. I've ordered a Toslink cable and I think that this little box might be the answer to this conundrum. I've got an older 5.1 receiver and I want to get 5.1 sound out of my Windows 10 PC. MSFT support forums do not hold out any real hope. So this really caught my eye. Ear. You know what I mean.

The intended uses are delivering HDMI sound from an Xbox of PS3 or Blu-Ray player to a "Smart TV" or 4D HD set which can play the audio output of an HDMI signal, meaning that you don't have to worry about separate audio cables. It's an interesting little device that provides several options to solve various audio problems and issues. I've never seen anything like this CSRET device before. I'm impressed.

The only thing I can find to complain about is the small size of the type in the three-fold instruction brochure. I'm old. I want BIG TYPE. Make it easy to read.

title: Powerful and easy to use.
text:
Powerful and easy to set up. What brings your household to a standstill? If the WiFi goes out, right? This modem is superior to any other cable modem we've used, fast, powerful, easy to set up. Probably second only to our refrigerator as far as important appliances go. Make your teenagers happy and keep peace in your home by installing a top quality modem.

Follow the simple instructions and you won't have any problems setting this up in no time.

---

Was I unclear? The thing about getting a Not-The-Cheapest-Kind cable modem is that you can get all the bandwidth you're paying for, and with a decent router you can deliver faster page loads to your family members, and if you have kids they're probably playing online games which eat up a lot more bandwidth than geezer users like myself who are happy just to have Amazon's pages load.

title: The fastest router I've ever used!
text: FAST. Pages pop up with no wait time, even at the far end of the house where my ancient MacBook crawls along. Very nicely packaged and easy and fun to assemble (I'm a nerd). I've had a couple of drops using the faster of the two bands on a desktop with Windows 10 which is in the same living area as the router, not sure what to make of those. I played an arcade-like online game I like and it was really snappy, low ping and good frame rate, but the real connoisseurs, my kids, will give the new router a test, they both play online games. I'm positive that they'll approve once they get past the first-world problem of a new router SSID and password! The router looks great, kind of like one of those stealth planes or battleships, low-key black with various angles. The antennae are kind of paddle-shaped. There's a Netgear website which helps you configure the router. Everything is painless, no headaches involved. Easily the fastest router I've ever used.

title: Your basic FM antenna.
text: Ugly as sin, but it works great. Brings in otherwise dodgy signals. There's always some obscure FM station at end of the dial that needs one of these.

title: Step up your stereo connections -- look like a pro put your system together
text: These look awesome and work great. Never again will I find myself trying to twist and shove bare speaker wires into a connection. Neat, permanent fix.

title: Fast and bulletproof as far as I can tell.
text: No complaints at all, fast and bulletproof as far as I can tell. Amazingly, impossibly small. Buy a few of these. More and more products need them to function. Keep them on hand like batteries.

title: Absolutely fascinating little dash cam!!!
text:
Absolutely fascinating little video recorder! The manual was well-written and big enough to read easily, not more than a touch of "Engrish" which is sometimes a real challenge to figure out. It's SMALL but has a surprisingly bright and colorful 2" screen. It ships with a suction cup attachment, a USB cord, a 12V power cord (Mine was DOA, so I used a Sony 12V power cord which worked great). You'll want to charge the tiny internal battery with a USB cable overnight. I swapped out the 8GB card (included) for a 32GB card (MicroSD) so I won't run out of recording space. There are a couple simple menus.

I have to laugh at myself for watching the videos of... me driving to the market and home again. I mean, they're not terribly interesting, but I find them fascinating like I was watching a NASA documentary on a space shot or something. Surprisingly good picture. It looked best on my Windows 10 PC as opposed to my elderly MacBook Pro, which dropped frames.

The relatively clear manual made the biggest difference in understanding this device. I had a chance to review another dash cam a month or so ago and the manual was set in excruciatingly tiny type and was written in "Engrish" meaning that it wasn't easy to figure out what they were talking about. Not so with this dash cam. Now I want to go back and re-evaluate the other dash cam now that I have some clue what they must have been talking about.

Really a fascinating little object. I haven't been so captivated by a little First World toy like this in as long as I can remember. Plus you can use this as a web cam should you be so inclined.

title: Great looking, works great, too.
text: Looks great, works great. I use this to connect my PC to my stereo. I just wish that Windows 10 supported 5.1 audio! Little details like this product really make a PC your own. STYLISH.

title: Astounding camcorder with excellent still photo capabilities
text:
An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.

title: Gorgeous earbuds in a stunning package
text:
Truly gorgeous earbuds, almost more like jewelry than audio hardware. These come packaged in a STUNNING plain cardboard box (please see photos!) -- sophisticated and impressive, demonstrating the use of materials in an artful manner. Inside the box you'll find the earbuds and related materials presented in a beautiful, magical way. As if you'd bought these at a museum gift shop or Japanese garden. Everything is beautifully presented. There's a small notebook and pen (!) as well as a few different sized rubber collars for you to choose from. The wood on the earbuds is gorgeous. They fit well.

Now, the bad news. The sound is a bit muddy, even listening via iTunes on my Mac with the equalizer. The high end is somewhat lacking. They're more than adequate, but the fact of the matter is that the sound is a little bit on the muddy side of things. The sound is beautifully rendered, but I'd love a little more brightness at the high end of things.

Overall these are easily the most beautiful earbuds I've ever seen. These would make a stunning gift! Truly gorgeous. Quite unique.

I received this at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: Adorable little USB fan for your desktop!
text:
[[VIDEOID:71860a6cce0c1cd8b795cd7774cf2aa8]] Great little desktop fan which looks just like a large floor-standing fan. Runs off of battery power or a USB connection. Rotates up and down. Makes a huge difference on a hot day! Made of hard black plastic which blends in an office setting. Please see the video -- moves quite a bit of air! Little rubber feet to keep it from creeping.

I received this at a discount in exchange for my honest and unbiased opinion.

title: These look incredible, weigh next to nothing, and have truly magnificent sound
text:
1. Gorgeous -- best looking cans I've ever seen
2. Comfortable, they fit great
3. Great packaging and presentation, would make a killer gift. Came in a nicely designed big white box, not a blister pack.
4. Easy to understand controls and documentation and all that.
5. Super lightweight

It kills me to say so, but the sound is a little bit muddy from my iPhone 5. The bass is covered and then some, nicely defined. The midrange is all there, but there's a certainly brightness missing from the sound, even with the volume up a ways, which helps. The stereo separation is outstanding, the "sound landscape" as I heard it described. The sound overall is VERY good, but I find myself wishing that there was a bit more of a sparkle at the high end, you know? Like a car that's perfect aside from needing a decent coat of wax to shine nicely. Connected via Bluetooth to my MacBook where I can tweak the EQ, I can get the sound I want. Something to consider. Set your songs with the EQ you want them played back with. This is worth the extra effort and will deliver the sound you want.

That said, these are just about the best Bluetooth cans or speakers I've ever heard. These would be fantastic paired with a Pono type of Hi Fi music player. There's an aux cable included in the box along with the charging cable (internal battery charges via USB). I'd heard (ha) that Bluetooth isn't a particularly robust solution for sound playback, but these headphones leave very little to ask for. The absence of a wire to get tangled up in is worth the compromises of the Bluetooth connection. The connection is not always 100% reliable. Which is frustrating. That's the tradeoff here. Nearly perfect connection, but not 100%.

title: Snappy performance, clear instructions. Good value.
text: Powerful dual-band router. Easy to set up, even though I managed to take a few wrong turns on the way. Get your phone and take a photo of the password on the bottom of the router after you have it connected and before you sit down to get everything functioning. I'd purchased a cheap router last year and this product tells me that buying the cheapest kind isn't always a bright idea -- this router is much more powerful and a lot faster than the El Cheapo I had. My kids ought to be thrilled, they both play online games. When I want to scare them, I tell them stories about 14.4K modems from 25 years ago... This router was easy to set up, comes with very clear instructions (so simple a guy can follow them). Now that I have it set up, the things I stumbled over seem inconsequential. I'm on a Mac, so things are fairly clear anyway, compared to Windows. This router is a major upgrade from the hardware I had been using. Now -- should I tell my kids the 5GHz password or let them use the 2.4GHz speeds?!?

title: Serious and functional.
text: Tough, edge-loading padded travel sleeve for 15" laptops. Tough polyester material on the large sides, kind of a rubberized material on the edges aside from the handle and the zippered opening. Not a lot of padding, but robust protection against scrapes or the elements. All-business, no fluff or decoration. Nothing showy, kind of like a tactical containment device for your laptop. Oversized zipper fob, easy to grasp. The handle is made out of the same tough polyester material and when you're not holding the case by the handle, it flattens out, slides on either side into a channel that keeps it out of the way. Excellent solution overall. If you're going to travel any distance, this is a really nice accessory for your laptop. Serious and functional.

title: Looks great, works great!
text:
I received a lamp for review purposes free of charge.

Fantastic LED USB lamp! Quite bright fully lit, it can be dimmed with a touch. Fits well in a USB port. Looks really good, flexible black metal with a black plastic lamp, looks much better than any other LED USB lamp I've seen before! Please see the photo. Provides a nice pool of light when working at or near your computer. I had it plugged into a desktop in the photo, all my everyday clutter is easily visible. Beautifully designed. I'll be ordering another one or two of these! The great thing is that with a USB plug-in adapter, you can add these little lights anywhere you have a socket OR a USB port! I often find I just need a little area illuminated rather than turning on an overhead incandescent light. I'm pretty excited about this product -- looks great, works great!

title: Very nicely designed solar walkway lamps
text: Attractive and well-designed outdoor solor LED lights for dark steps. These have a AA rechargeable battery in them. Sophisticated design, nothing horsey about them. Quite slim, a flattened triangle with the solar panel facing up and the light facing down. Comes with two wood screws and wall anchors for mounting. Great item, nicely realized.

title: Snug and attractive. Brilliant design.
text: Snug and attractive. Fits great. High quality hardware, like the rubberized fob on the zipper. Every detail thoughtfully considered. The cool part about this sleeve is that it's an Amazon house brand product. Something simple but perfectly realized. Brilliant design. Kind of a wetsuit material with semi-rubberized end pieces. Stylish.

title: Totally brilliant translucent design -- feels great in the hand, works great!
text:
Totally brilliant design, it looks incredible and it works great!!! No installation on Windows 10, just unplug your old mouse and plug the included transmitter (very small) into a USB port.

The mouse has a nice weight to it, though it's not very big. It tracks and scrolls perfectly and doesn't feel cheap. The translucent plastic is really delightful -- just brilliant, something functional that isn't boring. It runs on two included AAA batteries and has a tiny ON/OFF switch on the bottom. I'd replace the batteries if I were you. The top rear shell slides off to install the batteries AND there's a tiny "parking garage" space for the USB transmitter! THAT'S GREAT DESIGN!!!

How excited can you be over a peripheral? If it's this mouse, pretty excited! The design and execution are outstanding! A MOUSE YOU CAN LOVE!!! Life is too short to settle for cheap boring mice!

Look at the photo and see how this mouse is packaged -- a gorgeous object, beautifully displayed! AND it comes in different colors AND there are matching translucent keyboards, also wireless! A very satisfying item, indeed. This would make a fantastic gift. Keep some extra AAA batteries on hand, though!

title: Unique solution to a curious audio problem
text: Unique solution to the problem of splitting RCA L/R audio. I wanted to use a TV's speakers which I have facing the kitchen along with a surround sound box that I devoted the "B" speakers of also facing the kitchen, But I had only one set of RCA output jacks on the back of the DVD player! This is ideal, the second cable actually connects in the rear of these cables, splitting the signal with zero loss of quality (we are talking about RCA connectors, here, so don't expect miracles). This makes a huge difference for me when watching movies like "Theater of Blood" which was recorded in MONO(!!!!) and which sounded terrible when played on the tiny TV stereo speakers. This cable allows me to maintain the sound from the TV along with the processed/amplified sound via the surround box, which GREATLY IMPROVES the audio! Delighted!

title: Very fast, huge capacity, a name you can trust
text:
Bulletproof, very large capacity, and FAST if you have USB 3.0 ports to use it with. Backwards compatible. Given a USB 3.0 port, this single drive would be IDEAL for backups, and it's so small you can take it with you rather than worrying about storing an external drive. Beautiful but tough exterior with a big ring for keychains or lanyards. YOU CANNOT HAVE TOO MANY BACKUPS. That's a fact. Set yourself up to look like a genius by having current data on one of these flash drives. USB 3.0 is (theoretically) TEN TIMES as fast as USB 2.0! That's a big deal. Slow drives aren't used as much, people don't want to sit and watch a progress bar crawl along. Samsung is a solid name, I'm much happier trusting a big name than a fly-by-night I've never heard of. Back up your photos and music and business files, then back up the backups. This is a terrific little device, looks great, good and fast. Highly recommended.
---
Surprisingly fast transferring data from a 2.x USB port but it REALLY flies when moving files via a 3.0 USB port!

title: Small and sexy like a 1960s Japanese sports car
text:
Small and sexy like some kind of classic 1960s Japanese sports car. James Bond would use a laptop like this one.

Weighs next to nothing (2.6 lbs). Dark, smooth metal finish. Pry it open, there's a surprisingly large trackpad (4.5 x 2.5 inches) and a responsive keyboard. I wish the keyboard were backlit. Surprisingly comfortable keyboard. You click the bottom of the trackpad, which took me a minute to figure out. I have big hands and didn't have any trouble using the keyboard.

This thing is so small and sleek that it reminds me of jewelry. Especially the very tiny power and HDD indicators, set in the front edge. Clearly visible, but out of the way and ultra-sophisticated in appearance. The whole laptop is groomed and polished, nothing clunky about it.

On the left side there's the power plug socket, volume control, on/off, a Micro-SD card slot, Micro-HDMI port, a USB 3.0 socket and a USB 3.1 Type-C socket. On the right side there's the 3.5mm audio jack and a USB 2.0 socket.

Packaging and initial setup is as smooth as silk, totally professional and seamless, no bumps in the road, no weird stuff. Cohesive and enjoyable.

Windows 10 is quite nice! I am happily surprised! There's a new browser called "Edge" which is impressive in that you can annotate, draw, and type on web pages, make notes on a web page as if it was paper. Very clever. I was not happy with Windows 8 and it looks like Windows 10 has addressed complaints people had with that OS iteration. I'm usually disparaging of Windows at best (user since Win 2) and this is actually not bad at all. Kind of a nice surprise.

I very cautiously opened the laptop past 180 degrees… very slowly. This did not feel natural or advisable. But it works great! You can use laptop mode, "tent" mode, "stand" mode and "tablet" mode with a virtual keyboard that appears. The "stand" or "easel" mode, where you'd have the keyboard rotated to make a stand would be useful for presentations. Folding the keyboard all the way around behind the screen would give you a tablet. I'm actually kind of interested in using this in tablet mode streaming a movie from Amazon while on the treadmill. Have to use a bungie cord to secure the device, I guess.

The touchscreen feature has a fairly extensive set of motions which I will need to use the included cheat sheet to learn. This is terra incognita for me. The whole touchscreen concept is kind of baffling at this point in time.

Connectivity is good, completely transparent. You may not want to run Photoshop on this device, but for general use, it's more than adequate, more than fast enough. It comes with a 64GB flash drive which is mighty snappy.

I am VERY interested in finding software and a style that might work with the touchscreen to draw on. Electronic paper?! Sign me up. I'm not sure this is possible or if it would work that way, but I want to find out. I think this is just a daydream.

Setup with painless from start to finish. Battery charged up in no time.

The big-as-they-could-make-it display (1366 x 768) is saturated with color, very impressive. The sound is surprisingly good for the size of the laptop. I can't imagine how they achieved that. Now I'm reading that there's custom software onboard called "Asus AudioWizard EQ software" which delivers the sound via one of five preset modes. Nice touch.

Overall surprisingly fast and powerful for its size. I'd read a complaint about the screen resolution not being up to 2015 standards but I certainly have zero complaints. It looks great and this is as powerful as any other modern computer I own and the form factor will make your jaw drop. I was expecting a kind of glorified tablet, but this is a full-on computer, no compromises or apologies. And the thing is you're not going to be lugging around a battleship-sized laptop. That's heavy baggage. This will fit easily in a backpack. Which means you'll take it with you when you're out of the house. Perfect size. Looks professional. You would not be embarrassed taking this with you to a business meeting. Charge lasts a surprising long time.

Gorgeous little laptop, sexy as can be. Small and powerful. Can you imagine such a device back around, oh, 1995? Laptops weighed 15 pounds back then and could barely load a spreadsheet. It pains me to say that this little gem is as well put together and functional as a MacBook. I never thought I'd say that about any PC.

title: Remarkable sound for the price and size
text: For the price and for their size, these S120 speakers are remarkable. I'd bought a pair for a PC build and was fooling around with them today -- I've got a space music Internet radio station on, and the sound is outstanding, really gorgeous, full music. I bought them to get booms and ka-pows playing video games on that PC. These things are cheap, robust, and cost next to nothing!

title: Outstanding, gorgeous translucent WIRELESS keyboard!!!
text: Gorgeous translucent blue keyboard with nicely rounded key caps -- reminds me of my old Olympic typewriter! Sets itself up in no time at all. Compatible with PC and Mac, but the "Alt" key is next to the spacebar, so you'd need to re-train yourself for this exact keyboard. Comfortable to type on, nice big numeric keypad. Runs on two included "AAA" batteries and a very tiny USB transmitter. Apparently there's a matching wireless mouse. This keyboard is so much more stylish than the usual black keyboards you see! It's fun! Life is too short to settle for boring peripherals!!!

title: Works great but the LEDs are insanely bright
text: Works great, but I had to put a foil heart-shaped sticker over the flashing red LED and then add a folded Post-It note to mute the colors of the other LEDs a bit. I like it a lot more with the diffuse, softer lights!

title: Greatest art tool EVER.
text: Incredible. Best art tool EVER. Works great. IT'S BIG which is what you want! I had a 6x8 Wacom and it just wasn't big enough. You want ROOM TO MOVE YOUR ARM while you draw. Buy one of these and treasure it! And do yourself a favor and check out SmithMicro's "Manga Studio" which is now renamed "Clip Studio" for some reason. Works MUCH better with a graphics tablet than Illustrator, Photoshop, or Painter. Painter has a history of very weird behavior and bizarre crashes... Manga Studio is stable and tablet friendly!

title: Complete and utter dog excrement.
text: I spent money on this thing and have spent the past seven hours trying to get any picture from it. Remember the first Moon landing? The video was better from the surface of the Moon in 1969. Why did I spend money or time on this thing? Complete and utter dog excrement. Sucks out loud. Oh, how I wish I could use more colorful language and still have my review published. DO NOT WASTE YOUR TIME. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY.

title: The best computer I've ever owned
text:
The best computer I've ever owned. I used my original MacBook 17" until it died and the local Mac place insisted that it could not be resurrected. I was stuck. I didn't want a "new" Mac with the dubious new OS (I like Snow Leopard, 10.6.8). I didn't want a PC (Windows 7? No, thank you. Windows 8? Are you mad??). So I was VERY happy to find a reasonably mint MacBook on Amazon!!! The screen works, the keyboard is intact -- I mean, it looked new! I had an SSD installed which makes performance pretty snappy. And at a very reasonable price! I'm completely happy. I should buy another one before this second one dies -- this really is the best computer I've ever used.
(Purchased from Wegener Media via Amazon)
---
2017, needed ANOTHER MacBook Pro (do not leave your coffee cup close to your MacBook) and was happy to be able to find another "MA897LL/A" from jvcom via Amazon. It's immaculate!!! They said "minor cosmetic imperfections" but I can't find any defects whatsoever. I am so pleased to have a replacement MacBook Pro! I'm keeping my coffee far away from this one.

title: Gorgeous, stylish replacement for the generic CAT5 cable -- BRILLIANT!
text: Another typically brilliant redesign of a common cable by Belkin. THIS LOOKS AWESOME. It's a matter of style -- the standard clunky CAT5 cable or this black, FLAT CAT5 cable? Little details such as this cable make you look more professionally and generally increase your awesomeness. That someone at Belkin noticed this and acted on it is genius.

title: Excellent quality speaker wire.
text: As good as any 16-gauge speaker wire I've ever used. Do yourself a favor and buy some banana clips for a solid installation.

title: Fantastic sound for their size!
text: Fantastic sound for their size! I use these with the Pono Player along with a "Topping TP20-MK2 MKII TA2020 Class T" amp -- the sound is incredible! Nuanced -- I hear things I've never heard before. Could not be more pleased. These are not going to fill a big living room with sound, but as desktop/bookshelf speakers they're an almost unbelievable value!!!

title: GREAT sound!!!
text: Bought this and a pair of Micca speakers to use with my Pono Player. The amp sounds incredible. I hadn't had a "real' stereo for 10 years or so, so between the Pono, this amp and the speakers, I am thoroughly impressed and satisfied.

title: Gorgeous, powerful laptop with amazing speed and display cursed by Windows 8.1
text:
It's a beautiful laptop, 17"x11" shut, the screen is huge, 17" measured diagonally. This is NOT a small laptop. It looks tough, almost tactical, with battleship-like lines and a somewhat menacing dark grey color.

The presentation or unboxing is sensational: it comes in a kind of large dark grey cardboard suitcase complete with handle. You open the box and there is the laptop along with two small rectangular insets in the top part of the box. No clutter, no plastic bags, even the power cable (which is also huge) is nestled, hidden, in a compartment near the hinge of the box.

Setup is magnificent and smooth as can be, a real delight. Nothing clunky about it, a genuine pleasure. The keyboard is enormous and includes a full numeric keypad to the right. The trackpad is (oddly) centered below the keyboard, not centered on the body and features two mouse-click areas below it.

The sound is as good as a laptop is going to have, which is somewhat tinny with no bass. You will want a set of external speakers. I had a Windows 7 home built computer which I stole a $10 set of Logitech speakers from which provided more than adequate sound.

The keyboard, function keys, Alienware logo and top and front lights are all PROGRAMMABLE, meaning you can set not only customized keystroke functions for the function keys, but set detailed COLORS for all of the elements to dream up customizable schemes, which sounds goofy but looks *awesome*. This is a gorgeous laptop from top to bottom, stem to stern. Easily the nicest laptop I've ever seen.

Would you use this for business? As in tote it to a business meeting? Probably not, you know, it looks great, but it's not business-drab styled. It's meant for gaming, and it truly rocks at that.

The screen has nearly unbelievable saturation and brightness, the colors almost drip off the screen, they're so rich. The tactical sensation of the keyboard is outstanding, it's not a mechanical "click" keyboard but rather the standard sensation with buttery-smooth Rolls-Royce operation. There is no optical drive, but that doesn't really matter these days. I was able to download a copy of Painter Essentials which would not run on my Mac, which ran great on the Alienware laptop.

I downloaded a trial copy of Illustrator and put it through its paces, the laptop had no trouble with anything I could throw at it. Plenty of RAM, no heating problems, a battery which lasts quite a long time uncoupled from shore power.

In short, the laptop is outstanding -- fantastic. Second to none. Beautifully designed, faster than any other laptop I've ever seen with a display better than any desktop computer I've ever used. The sound is weak, but it's impossible to squeeze decent speakers into that form factor -- external speakers or headphones are required. Software on board will support any sound system you want to add. It's all ready to roll and buffed like a body builder. Incredible!

And now, gentle reader, I need to address the sole problem I had with the Alienware laptop, and it's a big one: it ships with Windows 8.1.

The killer part of this is that having a gorgeous laptop like this with Win 8.1 is like having a yacht when you live in the desert. One doesn't really function without the other. I found Windows 8.1 impossible to use, it simply made no sense to me. Windows would pop up I never asked for, navigation was absurdly difficult -- it made no sense to me on a fundamental level. I was not a fan of Windows before, but Windows 7 on my homebrew game box functioned and was comprehensible to me, things MADE SENSE.

But Windows 8? I ran across a video critique (http://dottech.org/94027/this-hilarious-video-explains-why-windows-8-sucks-video/) of the interface and the fundamental flaws built into it -- one has to be curious what Microsoft was thinking. The interface choices simply make no sense. Why would they release such a horrible dog of an operating system?! I'm not a n00b when it comes to computers. And I could not make heads or tails out of Windows 8.1, which soured my experience with the Alienware laptop. Here we have a laptop which is outrageously powerful with a gorgeous display and an OS which I don't have anything good to say about. It's awful, truly, honestly awful.

My point being that if you want to get anything DONE with this laptop, beware Windows 8. If you're happy with getting your favorite games set up and playing those, then you'll be satisfied. For example, you're expected to enter or create a new e-mail account in order to proceed -- well, that I did, and in the month I've been trying to use this laptop, I've NEVER gotten the Microsoft e-mail account to function properly! Internet Explorer is included, and it's kind of buggy and suffers from the computer either changing programs or bringing up windows I never asked for ALL THE TIME. It's maddening. I'm not exaggerating or joking -- this thing is a train wreck, a real crazymaker.

Why not ship this laptop with some flavor of Linux? Or cobble together a Dell version of an OS? Windows 8 really is that bad. You can imagine the frustration of an OS that is the equivalent of an insane person on your laptop. Your beautiful, perfect laptop. It would have been great if there was a simple downgrade path to Windows 7. Or XP, or Win95 -- seriously, it's THAT BAD.

OK, enough of that. The OS is not Alienware's fault, but it does greatly interfere with the use of the laptop. Perhaps you'll have a better experience. For me, it was a major stumbling block EVERY TIME I TURNED THE LAPTOP ON. Absolute endless frustration. I just cannot figure out what Microsoft was thinking.

So, to sum up: this is the best laptop I've ever seen, absolutely ideal for gaming, and the other "serious" programs I got to run on it all performed beautifully. You will want to add external speakers and possibly an external CD/DVD drive if you need one. There are plenty of USB ports and the other sockets you expect. Support for sound is outstanding.

But the Windows 8 OS is like a rock in your shoe which makes every single step you take painful. With a different OS, this may well be the PERFECT laptop for personal gaming use. Absolutely gorgeous!

---

You should DEFINITELY UPGRADE TO WINDOWS 10!!! The difference is remarkable! A massive improvement in user experience compared to Win 8.1!!!

title: Quite substantial
text: Quite substantial, a big, black USB cable. Twice the width of my other USB cables. The heads are equally chunky. Really robustly-made.

title: These are great!
text: These are great! I'd never used them before -- yes, I've been stuffing bits of frayed copper speaker wire into connections all these years! What an improvement! Totally awesome little gadgets! Get your wire cutters, your wire strippers and a couple of pairs of small pliers out of your toolbox, and pay attention to which wire you're attaching (don't cross red/black). They glide right into the speakers! I love these!

title: Save your money
text: This does...nothing. At all. I spent money on this?

title: Does this work? I like the idea a lot.
text: I honestly can't tell if this is doing my laptop any good or not, but I like the idea. I've got a utility that reports on temperatures at various spots in my laptop, CPU, GPU, heat sinks, et cetera. It adds about 3/4" of an inch which isn't that big an adjustment when you're typing. I like the idea of a fan under the computer a lot. I'm tempted to find a plunge router and hog out a space in my Ikea desk for this thing to sit in, you know, put in some kind of screen material so it is supported and then have my laptop at desk height.

title: Great little mouse
text: No-nonsense mouse. It's got your left button, it's got your right button, it's got your scroll wheel -- and it was CHEAP on Amazon! I bought two against my new kitten chewing through the mouse cord again. IT'S NOT CAT PROOF but it's a great little mouse! And I trust Kensington computer peripherals -- I cannot believe how long I've been using Kensington products!

title: Great item for digital cameras
text: Perfectly fine. I can't believe I can buy a 32Gb CF card for under $1000... amazing storage for cameras, THIS IS NOW FILM!!! And you don't want to run out on vacation, so buy a couple of these. They're small, they work great. You can't have too many of these.

title: Fabulous camera
text:
I waited years and years and years to buy a used 30D and I'm not disappointed in the slightest. It took a while for what I used to know about "real" photography to come back, and I had to stop looking for the various dials I remembered from film cameras. I leave the 30D set on "M" for "Manual" and I'm happier than a clam in mud at high tide, as my mother used to say. I bought the inexpensive Canon 50mm 2.8 lens which fit my budget. The 1.6 crop factor is not something I'm wild about, but I'm willing to live with it to finally have real control over photos again after 10+ years of point-and-shoot digital cameras.
This is a beauty -- not too big or too heavy, and not too light or small for my big fat hands, either. Watch a couple of videos so that you never use the "Automatic" Mode. In just a week I've figured the camera out to my satisfaction and am taking the best photos of my entire life. I have a lot of photographic experience and this is a fantastic tool -- why did I wait to buy it? Cheap, I guess. The used 30D I found was under $300 and in pretty good shape. Another $100 or so for the lens. $10 for a battery charger. It is a genuine pleasure to be taking good photos again, with extensive control.

title: Outstanding style, very good audio quality for a Bluetooth connection
text:
Beyond the way it looks, it's relatively easy to pair via Bluetooth, you can charge your phone via USB or NFC, the wireless near-field connection scheme. I'd have given a tooth for an external speaker like this back in the 80s, when battery-powered speakers for the Sony Walkman existed. It's more than adequate for a dorm room or office space, it's lightweight, it seems to be pretty durable, each of the EIGHT speakers have a metal screen protecting the cones. CX -- No, I was wrong, there are NOT eight speakers, there are FOUR speakers, plus four extra cones which amplify the sound. I counted the grilles and assumed they were all speakers. My error!

This comes in a beautiful package, it would make a fantastic gift. It promises up to 8-10 hours of play, which is more than decent. There's a Mic In jack, which I'm somewhat baffled by, and an Aux jack, which is very handy if you own an older non-Bluetooth iPod. There's a Talk button for use with your phone. I'm unclear how that would function. This can be mounted on a wall, AND THEY INCLUDED THE WALL ANCHORS AND SCREWS. Very thoughtful.

The main thing, the sound quality, is better than I've heard with other Bluetooth speaker solutions, which, honestly, is not saying that much. I'm looking for a software EQ on my iPhone and I don't find one. I don't want to ask for the Moon, but an EQ on the speaker would be worth more to me than the NFC charging scheme.

A very good Bluetooth speaker solution. It looks gorgeous, it's easily paired, the sound is relatively bright and clear. Room-filling sound. It won't replace home stereos, but that's not what it's meant to do. Anyone young enough to NOT remember how good vinyl LPs sound will be positively thrilled with this device!

---

This device actually sounds better filling a room with sound than it does just sitting on your desk. For whatever that's worth. It sounds better if it's not right under your nose.

---

This device does match up with my iPhone very well, and without a lot of fuss or headaches like other Bluetooth solutions I've tried. If I can't get each device to sniff one another's butt, I lose interest pretty quickly. This device matches up on its own and easily, so that's a major plus.

title: Lousy programming, zero effort by XM/Sirius
text: I had one of these, and as far as the concept and hardware, it worked great. But what I found was that XM/Sirius was just mailing it in, you know, their effort at decent programming was SORELY LACKING. I'm talking about lack of effort on the music channels, not the Howard Stern Show bait and switch disaster, but seriously crappy music programming, the same setlist repeated every two hours, you know, ALL THE STUFF YOU HATED ABOUT CORPORATE FM RADIO PROGRAMMING IN THE FIRST PLACE. You're better off with another service altogether IMHO. I hate it when somebody or some company DOESN'T MAKE AN EFFORT. Life is too short to do a poor job on anything. LACK OF EFFORT!

title: Small but functional
text: Really lightweight and no-frills. I used it when my internal DVD player started acting up. USB powered. It's so light that the cables weigh more than the drive does. I haven't had any trouble with it at all. I use it to watch DVDs on my computer. You don't want to know what external DVD drives used to cost. This thing is  a real bargain!

title: Great little AB switch
text: I wanted to share an external HDD between two Macs - this is perfect! First dismount the drive (if it's mounted), push the button, the LED will change from the A to B color (two LEDs, one green, one blue) -- voila! Perfect! No more cable juggling! It ships with two USB cables and you've already got the first USB cable out of the three you'll need if you have your HDD/printer/whatever set up already. Great solution!

title: Requires a MIC IN 3.5mm socket -- Mac users pay attention
text:
I bought a pair of these for Kid #2's birthday. Kid #1 was QUITE envious (he has a cheap headset for his PC). Unfortunately, there are TWO 3.5mm jacks, so on a Mac, which have not had a "Sound in" jack for years, you'll need a solution like Griffin's iMic: [[ASIN:B000BVV2IC Griffin Technology iMic USB Audio Device]] -- fortunately I had one on hand, but I have yet to be granted permission from Kid #2 to get it working -- but I'm reasonably certain that is what is missing, and why she couldn't get these working at first. Apple discontinued the "Sound in" or MIC input quite a long time ago. So that could stop you cold. Overall, however, these look really good, and judging from Kid #1's being impressed, they have a good reputation. I'll report back once I get the Griffin iMic working and hopefully get all the features on the headset functioning.
...

Now I see this kind of external USB sound card [[ASIN:B0058P0I2C Logitech USB To 3.5mm Jack Audio Adapter]] which would obviously be the cheaper way to go compared to buying a device like the iMic! I'd never seen a USB-3.5mm device before and it looks like this is what is missing on the Mac end to use this headset!

title: Smart solution
text: Inexpensive, well-made -- the right angle makes this thing worth the price all on its own. Having a 3.5mm connector sticking straight out of your PC case (or airline seat, or car iPod receptable) isn't always such a great solution. Count the rings on the plug end -- this is a stereo solution. Not sure why you'd want a mono plug. Long and short of it is that this is a robust product which functioned perfectly. Zero complaints! Buy two or three and keep some on hand. This would also be a clever stocking stuffer type of gift, especially for teenagers.

title: Defective bottom row of keys
text: I bought this locally and it was defective. I noticed that more than half of the boxes were taped back together -- they'd been returned. Which makes me think there was as least one bad run of these keyboards and that maybe you ought to look elsewhere for something that's not going to disappoint you and waste your time.

title: Quite impressive in operation -- remote monitoring
text:
This is the best overview of the components I've seen so far:

Nexia Home Bridge (this is the key component)
Schlage touch screen deadbolt w alarm
Schlage home keypad lock
Schlage home dimmer/appliance module
Schlage home indoor camera
Schlage home outdoor camera
Trane home energy management thermostat
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) remote thermostat
Trane ComfortLink ((tm)) II Control
American Standard AccuLink((tm)) Platinum ZV control (?)
Schlage home door/window sensor
Schlage home motion sensor
Other Z-Wave sensor
Other Z-Wave thermostat
Other Z-Wave lighting device
Other Z-Wave wall switch and outlet

They might have considered making the 9V battery compartment in the "Bridge" just a little bit bigger. It's a mighty snug fit and you have to remove the battery to get the MAC ID. In fact, you have to remove the 9V battery so often it's a curiosity why the battery door is such a pain to remove and why the battery is so difficult to get out of its little bay. I was actually using a flat screwdriver to pry the battery out, it's that tight.

---

Overall, now that the camera, light dimmer and lock and installed, "enrolled" and apparently functional..? WHAT A GREAT SYSTEM!!! The components look great, they're top-quality. Now that I see everything in action (especially video of my home on my iPhone) the subscription fee seems like not such a high price to pay for what you're getting. I know that I'm going to be sorely tempted to add more cameras.

The deadbolt operates with a passcode OR with a physical key. At first I was thinking that you could lock yourself out accidentally but after examining the lock and playing with the buttons I see that is not the case.

I also understand why the light dimmer module goes so well with the indoor camera -- when it gets dark, you'd want to be able to ramp up the light enough for the camera to see! It's a temptation to put the indoor camera in one of my kids room, which is what I might have done when they were small. That would be a rude intrusion these days. So it's outside a hallway that all traffic must pass through. The field of vision nearly covers the two main doors into and out of our home, also. So I can keep an eye on who's getting home when and all that parent-of-teenagers type stuff.

Is there a controller for exterior lights? Or some kind of interface that would allow me to remotely control wired exterior lights?

The only downside to this system, aside from the kludge-y installation process, is that you will want to add more components, and they aren't cheap.

Bottom line: top-quality components, frustrating "enrollment" process -- once you get it all up and running, it's quite impressive. It's nearly worth the frustration to see it all in operation. It would be nice if you could pan-and-zoom the camera. Perhaps that will be forthcoming in another camera model.

I can't help but feel that the process of "enrolling" the components couldn't be made more simple or more streamlined.

Now to budget for an exterior camera... maybe two...

---

Now that I've seen the system in operation I grasp what the manufacturer is actually offering -- remote control of your home administered via your iPhone or iPad. Ideal for working professionals. Getting everything connected and communicating was a little effort, but it's really a beautiful system in operation. You will definitely want to add more light controls and cameras, at least I would. I wonder if there's an exterior light module? There must be. Once you see it in operation the subscription will not be an issue. You are getting more than what you're paying for.

An excellent upgrade to your home and a clever way to keep tabs on a vacation home.

title: Not bad at all
text:
The novelty of a Bluetooth speaker weighs in its favor. Setup is fairly easy, just know that you need to pull open the accordian-like back end of the speaker to get it to turn on and power up! A little bass heavy, but it's such an improvement over listening to music via the dime-sized speakers in laptops that the improvement is dramatic!

---

I had purchased this as a Christmas gift for my teenage daughter. Who did not find it cool, or interesting. So as we used to say on the aircooled VW list, "Your Mileage May Vary". I thought it was a really neat solution. Maybe you want to think about a gift card for your teenagers instead. I was disappointed that my kid didn't find this speaker useful.

title: Did I actually spend money on this thing?
text:
OK. Deleted the original review. Figured I had the wrong kind of television set. My bad. So I thought I'd try it on my daughter's Sony digital set. I actually got more channels on the analog set than on the digital set. So my initial feeling that this is (COMPLETELY UNPUBLISHABLE SENTENCE HERE, HIDE YOUR EYES) was confirmed.

No need to fuss or flail. I'll just pack it back up and return it. And make a note the next time I think about wasting money on something like this. Perhaps this thing functions under different circumstances, but I'm on a hill in San Diego with four broadcast towers not terribly far away and I got NOTHING from this device. Nothing at all!

---

I must NOT have a TV set of the stripe necessary to use this thing. And a cheap DAC would cost about $40. Plus the $$ for this thing and I'm up around $90, which is about as much as a month's ATT television service, so buying this antenna and the DAC leaves me no better off than just one more month's gouge from ATT to watch the NFL playoffs.

Your mileage may vary. I had zero luck with this thing. Why did I bother?

title: Don't waste your time
text:
What occurred to me after wasting half an hour with this thing is that what is needed is an iPhone app to control your television and stereo, not a single freaking light bulb and a long, long list of codes printed in mouse type.

See photo. The remote looks good, shiny Darth Vader black. There are three manuals, one of which is about an ounce and a half. One is a long list of codes and the third unfolds to about 10x17 so that between the three differently-sized printed manuals you have a lap full of clutter which is difficult to manage while you're trying to press buttons in some order.

I couldn't get it to do much of anything, and by the time I realized that half an hour had gone by and I was getting hot under the collar, I thought: FAIL. Why waste any more of my time? Ah, but by THAT time I was and am good and frustrated at this RCA product. RCA. Who knew they were still in business? Who the heck would buy an RCA product? I'm sure they made great gramophones back in the day, but Sony came by and ate their lunch and even that was forty years ago.

If you were an RCA exec, wouldn't you want to make certain that anything your company made was functional? I've got a couple college degrees. I can tie my own shoes. I can do all kinds of things, but I couldn't figure out how to program this little (EXPLETIVE DELETED) thing. Which frustrates me.

The first thing I noticed (after I cut the I-dare-you-to-open-me hard plastic packaging) was that it hurt to open the battery compartment. There's some idiotic L-shaped trigger you have to depress, meaning that you're digging it under your fingernails, which I think most people would find painful. Just a dumb design move. No other word for it. Dumb.

The remote looks good and has some interesting ribs underneath it. The buttons are not what you might expect, the volume and channel buttons are flabby feeling and weak, not definite-feeling. The center "OK" button is kind of clicky, like cellophane. There's a whole array of buttons, but it's not worth my time to try and program each one. And I grew to dislike the hard plastic feeling of the remote. There are other plastic materials that feel better to the hand. LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS, RCA, LOOK AT SONY PRODUCTS FOR A FREE CLUE.

I'm annoyed and frustrated. This seemed like such a neat idea. But sitting on my couch juggling three differently-sized manuals AND this remote and wondering why none of these instructions were doing anything was really frustrating, just not how I want to spend my free time. I'll happily continue to exist with my TV remote, my surround-sound remote, my AppleTV remote and the AT&T cable box remote, you know? BECAUSE THEY WORK and they work without frustrating me.

Here's my idea: RCA hires an app developer and somehow figures out how to have your devices tell the app what their codes area. Something like that. Because the notion of combing through a manual full of codes in tiny type is worse than doing your income taxes.

THE WORLD HAS MOVED ON, RCA and you are apparently living in the 1970s with burgundy leisure suits and avocado-colored kitchen appliances.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS REMOTE, IT WILL ONLY FRUSTRATE YOU and dig in the skin under your nails. Ouch. Did this thing really have to be so frustrating? Do you imagine this is the kind of experience consumers are after? Not just one more freaking remote control, but one that promises convenience and delivers frustration? Not a good product. Stay away from it.

title: HDCP? This thing doesn't work with AppleTV
text: I'd never HEARD of HDCP until I got an error trying to use this little switchbox with AppleTV. No luck. Nothing happening. And my Sony TV has just exactly ONE HDMI jack. I am not amused in the slightest. Some greedy-lawyer-Hollywood "protection" scheme just deposited seagull manure on my home entertainment plans. It was only $16 but I'll bet that "HDCP" is nothing anyone wants or needs. And this thing can't handle whatever "HDCP" lawyer-talk requirements there are to FUNCTION. Save your cash.

title: Handy size, maybe not 45x
text:
The magnifier is SMALL, which is the thing I liked about it. The optics are decent and the two LEDs provide more than enough light. It's not perfect, but it was extremely inexpensive -- it's the IDEAL size to fit in a toolbox and not take up valuable space or add weight. I have a 30x magnifier that must be four times the size of this little thing. It's probably not 45x magnification, but the image is decent. It comes with an equally tiny cloth bag with a velcro closure. You're getting really good value for your money with this thing. I can see buying another and keeping it with the knife sharpener to inspect the edges of blades.

I would like to get a more powerful magnifier, but this is impressive for the price.

title: Adorable looking excellent protection
text: Really nicely made sleeve for a 13.3" MacBook, which is what I gave my daughter for Christmas. This sleeve really makes the laptop a lot more friendly looking. And it's girly. Nice fit, excellent protection, you can charge the laptop when it's in the sleeve. A great little solution. I'd purchased an all-black Case Logic version for my son (who also got a 13.3" MacBook for Christmas) and my daughter was unhappy about this being mostly pink. I thought it was charming looking. Anyway, I'm happy that they have protection for the computers when they take them places. Excellent product.

title: Cheap, functional and SMALL
text: Nothing that you don't need and nothing more than you do need. Somewhat fragile but functional USB 2.0 CD-ROM -- I have to say that I did not have any luck getting Mac OS 9 to recognized this USB 2.0 drive as a boot CD, which is what I was hoping to use it for. But I doubt that's an application most potential buyers are considering, so no problem.

title: Impressive stereo imaging in a wireless solution
text: I find myself listening to my MP3 collection all over again to hear what I've been missing by listening with my iPod earbuds or my iPod boombox from Apple (anyone remember those?) or through my dime-sized laptop speakers. NO MORE. Even thinking back to the big speakers I had when I was in college, these headphones reproduce each and every note beautifully. The over-the-ear design takes a little getting used to compared to wearing earbuds, but the fact that there's no wire to tangle is a major plus. The sound was a little on the boom-y side of things until I used the iTunes EQ. Very impressive headphones, they look great and, most importantly, they sound fantastic. I had zero setup issues, in fact the device had connected to the tiny transmitter before I could put them on. And my kids won't march up to my iPod boombox and turn the sound down on me while I'm listening through these. Keeps my music to myself. These would be great to wear while working (but don't wear them during staff meetings).

title: Kind of a neat idea for the mobile user
text:
Before opening the box: I notice and am concerned about the three logos I see (Buffalo, Cloudstor and Pogoplug), all of which look amateurish and unprofessional. The box design is another cause for concern. It's unsophisticated, like a rough draft. These are, in my experience, not good signs. It's not as if you can't throw a rock and hit a graphic designer.

---

Well, it was a breeze to set up and appeared eager and willing to store everything I have on hand and make it accessible from anywhere you can establish a web connection. There's a $35/month subscription which I understand makes it possible to stream your music or movies. I can see where this would be a neat device for someone who was on the go a lot and might want their personal or especially their business data at their fingertips.

Since I use a Mac the non-standard interface freaked me out. My kids have Windows computers and anything that remotely resembles that kind of interface makes my blood pressure rise, anticipating problems. Since the User Agreement said that the device was for 18+ users only that was kind of an issue -- could I use this for their data? I didn't think so.

If you have an iPhone or Android or a phone or device like that I can see where this would be a great device to have, unfortunately I don't own any kind of smart phone.

Overall, sorry to say, the non-standard interface, the companies I'd never heard of, the first-draft feeling of the graphics didn't inspire me to trust the device. If I were a Windows user this thing might seem like the greatest idea since sliced bread. Slick, fast, seems to do everything it promises to do -- I think I might be too much of a couch potato non-mobile user to get much out of this device, really. I have a couple external drives for backups or photo storage and seldom stray from home. This isn't a bad product, but I get the feeling that I'm not in the target market group for this kind of device.

---

Six months later: I didn't grasp what this device was for initially. Now that the light bulb has come on over my head I realize that it's remarkably cool, useful and PAINLESS to operate. Somehow initially it struck me as a kind of convoluted hard drive setup, now it seems intuitive and rather suave. I'm not clear on why it took me so long to figure it out, or for the fog to lift.

title: Astounding little camera for the price
text:
My Canon S410 Powershot gave up the ghost, even after a trip back to Canon for repairs ($100, ouch). I was tired of not having a camera and this one crossed my path at the right time and I bought it after debating for months which camera to go with.

This is MUCH lighter than my Canon S410, and far sleeker -- all the knobs and buttons and whatnot are smooth and out of the way. It won't snag on things like the boxy S410 tended to do. This camera is as light as a plastic disposable camera. I remember my first digital camera back in 1999 which weighed a pound and then some.

The LCD screen is ENORMOUS compared to my old camera(s). It takes up almost the entire back of the camera body. Amazing. The controls are scrunched together compared to the S410 controls. Having had the S410 I was familiar with the Canon layout and the way the camera works, which was nice.

An earlier review mentioned that the startup time and the time between shots was long -- I didn't find that to be the case. It powers up almost instantly, and even taking photos at the largest image size the time between shots is only a second or two. My first digital camera would tend to "submarine" for six or seven seconds between shots!

Overall I'm VERY, VERY happy to have a camera that works again, and the cost wasn't all that much, like half of what I paid five years ago for the S410. Half the cost, half the weight... I still daydream about getting a "real" camera, a digital SLR (DSLR) with a nice heavy L-series prime lens... but it wouldn't fit in my pocket, would it?

Don't hesitate -- this is a beautiful little device, thoughtfully designed and nicely manufactured. If you're traveling or if you're a parent (or both) you know you simply cannot take too many photos. I bought a 4GB card for this, one of those little big-as-your-thumbnail chips, and even at the highest resolution the photos are about 2MB apiece, so you can shoot a lot of photos and never run out of space. Included with the camera was a cable to attach to a television, which I thought was a neat idea. I'll have to play with that sometime.

My only caveat would be based on my experience having sent my S410 in for repair to Canon -- for $100 the repair didn't last long at all, I wonder if they just sent me a refurbished unit they had. Anyway, don't DROP your camera and you won't have to send it in to be repaired.

title: Impressive drive for hard-core gamers or video pros
text:
The first hard drive I ever bought was a Seagate. It was a 20MB internal. Once I'd gotten it installed I thought "I'll never fill up all this space." That was more than twenty years ago (and it turns out I did fill up all that space).

Here is the latest and possibly the last of the Seagate Barracuda drives, and it's a beauty. I just cannot get over how BIG the drive is. Two terabytes is TWO TRILLION BYTES. And it flies! Until SATA3 becomes the de facto standard, this drive will satisfy the needs of any hard-core gamer or video editing pro.

I'd read about earlier large Seagate HDs having issues in multi-disk arrays on Mac or Linux systems, but I found that this drive works and plays well with everything I've got plugged in to my system. Installation was easy. The drive is remarkably quiet. The capacity reminds me of those stretch limousines you see on the freeway, amazingly large but moving right along.

100% recommended. This is a terrific hard drive. And it's HUGE.

---

Months later: I've been trying to choke this thing somehow or other and it laughs off my every attempt. Really a nice bulletproof drive.

title: Works well for what it is
text: And what it is would be a cheap little card reader. The tiny blue door broke off instantly. It does what I want it to do, so I can't complain. title: The perfect beginning camera for film work
text:
Solidly built, this camera offers beginners FULL MANUAL CONTROL over all aspects of their photography. Nearly bulletproof, this camera belongs with you at all times. Coupled with a 55mm lens (approximately what your eye sees) you are ready to capture what is around you. I have nothing whatsoever bad to say about this camera, though I sold mine years ago in favor of a cheap pocket digital camera.

This is one of the best cameras ever produced for the mass market. No, it is NOT a point-and-shoot camera. YES it will afford you control that you might find only in much higher-end cameras, which is CRUCIAL for learning.

Photo student? BUY THIS CAMERA NOW WHILE IT IS STILL AVAILABLE!

title: Fantastic value for a desktop machine
text:
My kids love these (we own two) because it can runs Windows and they can play PC games. I've never seen Windows run faster.

On the Mac side, this thing is loaded -- everything you'd want is built-in (I love the Airport antenna being standard) and Apple's OSX software bundle is exceptional -- everything works together seamlessly. If you're used to putting up with the ragged Windows OS, this will be a major step up for you, and a painless one!

You cannot go wrong choosing this computer. It's fast, cheap and robust. Once you use the Mac OS you will never go back to Windows.

title: Terrific point-and-shoot camera for the price
text:
