We need to get a Secure Digital Memory card with a greater capacity, but otherwise everything we needed was in the box and it works great with our Mac without installing any drivers.

I'm fascinated to see what photos she takes -- and how clever of her to ask for a camera as a gift.

title: Very nice FRS device -- great for camping
text:
I've found over the three years we've used the T6220s that suburban range is often greater than you'd imagine, but where these little radios really shine is giving one to your kid to keep instant tabs on them "just in case," and when you're camping these are the greatest thing since tents for not losing any kids at Scout camp! They're also very useful at the swap meet or someplace like Disneyland to keep track of subsets of your group.

They're tough, we haven't killed one yet. You'll have to look at a few pages in the manual to see how to work the radios, but it's not like it's trigonometry or anything like that. You can easy learn to operate these radios.

Simple, bulletproof, decent performance... this is a good product and I'm glad that I bought a pair.

We tried a VOX headset but it was not a big success. I do like the NOAA feature on this radio, get weather/emergency information when you really need it.

Dandy little radios.

title: Desktop power in a portable form factor
text:
When you're a grown-up, "toys" include notebook computers, and this is a honey. Between the combo drive and the built-in WiFi antenna, you've got just about everything covered, everything you'd want to do (homework? No, watch a DVD!) is wrapped up in one tight little package, and it's fast enough to run OSX, which is the best OS I've ever used, and I'm old and crusty. Battery life is always an issue with any notebook. And it's usually overstated. I'd look into buying a second battery if I were you.

I'm a dedicated Apple user, and I'd say that this notebook is a tremendous value!!!

title: Great FX, no story... I'm glad it's over
text:
Perhaps George Lucas just got lucky with Episode IV in 1977 -- he certainly doesn't seem to have had a clue about storytelling since that time. Maybe it was Alec Guiness and Harrison Ford that carried the first movie. And I must say even Mark Hammill was excellent in Episode IV. I just didn't care about the "Jedis" who turned out to be boring intergalactic narcs.

The special effects are great, but what movie doesn't have great FX these days? How hard would it have been to make Anakin REALLY BELIEVABLY EVIL?

The first two "prequels" could easily have been condensed into about ten minutes of flashback. Whoever played Obi Wan Kenobi is certainly not going to become any sort of Alec Guiness caliber actor. The whole thing was weak. Episode IV was magnificent, the other movies have just been the sound of cash registers ringing up marketing tie-ins, toys, video games, toothbrushes, condoms, everything else you can think of. I WANT A GOOD STORY. SCREW THE SPECIAL EFFECTS. TELL ME A GOOD STORY.

"Since the end is never told, we pay the teller

off in gold, in hopes he will return

but he cannot be bought or sold..."

title: Very nice little camera
text:
Quite impressive overall. It's SMALL yet I wish it was just a little bit smaller. I have yet to read the manual cover to cover but have enjoyed snapping pictures in the automatic and manual modes so far.

The size of the S410 was one of its two biggest selling points. I want a camera I will have with me, not one that's at home taking up space. The other thing I wanted was decent to good image quality, and what I've seen so far makes me think that this camera is a good choice.

I ordered a second battery and used an inverter I already owned to charge it in the car. Much cheaper than the Canon car charger. The manuals are (somewhat comically) also very small little books. A useful road-map poster of features is included along with a quick-start guide, which is always square one as far as I'm concerned.

Color reproduction seems very good. Clarity is decent at this point. I obviously need to read the manual to understand everything that's going on, and it's clear that there's a LOT of technology stuffed into this little gem. The controls are well-placed and the menus seem concise, operation overall is quite snappy. I'm pleased. The LCD screen is extraordinarily bright and crisp. Time between shots is acceptable, pretty quick, really, and time-to-first-shot is very good.

I don't think you'd need a case for the camera. Wrap it in a handkerchief if you're worried it will get scratched. I like the lens being covered by two little doors that close on power-off. Keeps the lens safe and you don't have a loose lens cap to worry about. The camera is smooth, no protrusions to catch on anything. It's a great looking little thing. It's a little bit heavier than you'd think it would be. I wish it was a little bit lighter and a little bit smaller. Which seems greedy given how light and small it is now!

One thing I like in particular is the B&W setting. Shooting in black and white is something a lot of folks who didn't spend time taking Intro to Professional Photo back in college may not have experienced, and it's worth checking out, particularly for portraits. Black and white can tell a better story than color.

I'm probably being unfair giving this camera only four stars -- there are certainly no glaring faults, far from it, but this was a realistic choice for me, a camera that I can take everywhere with me, and, no, for this price it's not going to perform like a Canon D20 which is ten times the price, but it is MUCH smaller and twice the resolution of my beloved old Nikon 950 (circa 1999). Maybe I'm expecting D20 performance at a S410 price..?

For its size and the price, this camera is quite a good value and is everything I expected, very well put-together and quick. A good choice. Not film-quality images, but very good for what it is. A good balance of resolution, size and weight. A handy, good quality camera to snap photos of the kids with, small enough to have with you everywhere you go. Not that I'd mind the "inconvenience" of having a Canon D20 over my shoulder 24/7... but that's simply not in the budget!

No regrets at all having chosen the S410!

Five years later: I had dropped my S410 and I couldn't use most of the functions, so I shipped it off to Canon to be repaired (for $100, ouch)... and it stopped working after about a month. I was sharply disappointed. I didn't want to send it off AGAIN (another $100), and I was unhappy having no camera. Canon offered a "loyalty program discount" or whatever they called it, I could buy a refurbished next-step-up camera from them for about $150, but after the $100 wasted on a not-very-robust repair I was reluctant to do that. I ended up buying a used S410 off a popular auction site. I expect things to last basically forever, so I was disappointed that I was clumsy enough to drop my camera and disappointed again that Canon's repair was extremely short-lived.

title: Sensational little disposable -- BUY IT!
text:
It's just about the only camera I needed for a vacation to Maui. I hauled along my digital camera, my "real" 35mm camera and a handful of dry-land disposables, and this underwater camera KICKED BUTT as far as quality of shots, quality of hardware, ease of use and general cool/fun vortex rating, plus, it's almost indestructible and weighs next to nothing!
YES the prints are a bit "dark" when printed without correction -- so CORRECT them! This is a Fuji-Kodak thing, I think, so ASK your processor to print them a bit lighter. The colors are outrageously rich, even the deeper-underwater shots have very good colors throughout. You have GOT to have one of these on your wrist while you snorkel!
Really an excellent little product - the next time I need a dry-land disposable, I'm going to give Fuji a try based on how great this underwater Fuji was to use!

title: I thought the photos would be sharper
text: It's a beautifully made little camera but it just hasn't produced very sharp photos so far.  I wanted a film camera since I was tired of the images I was getting out of my Nikon 950 (digital = fuzzy pictures faster).  The colors from the Sureshot76 are excellent and it's just so darn cute I have a hard time saying anything critical about it, but looking at images I'd taken with an old, cheap 35mm camera with an old, cheap 55mm lens I'd rather drag around a "real" camera than have to settle for images that really look as if they'd been taken with a disposable camera. But for a grandma-point-and-shoot camera it's dandy, I'll give it to my wife, it's her speed.

called due to battery not charging although we spent the money to hard wire it..... and got an email from them. box says it works to -5F. this is what the email states..... Important temperatures

The following are key temperatures to watch out for in regards to your batteries.

36°F (3°C): The battery may not hold a charge as effectively, resulting in you having to charge the unit more frequently.
32°F (0°C): The battery may not charge at all. Even hardwired configurations may not charge the battery.
-5°F (-20.5°C): The battery may stop working completely until temperatures warm up.
What to do when it gets cold

Bring your device inside: When it gets cold and your device's battery runs out, bring your entire device inside and charge the battery with a USB cord. This will allow your device to warm up while the battery charges.
Make sure your battery is charged to 100%: When charging your battery, be sure that it reaches 100% before your remount the device. While the battery still won't be as effective as when the temperatures are warmer, making sure that the battery is at 100% will allow your device to work as long as possible.
Monitor your charge and the temperature: As long as the temperature hovers around the points listed above, you may have issues with battery charge. Therefore it's important to constantly monitor your battery life when it gets cold to make sure your device is always working.

title: Defective item that Amazon did not stand behind!
text:
I purchased this item for a trip to Ireland, having traveled there many times with cheaper converters and adapters with no bad luck. Figured paying a little more for an all-in-one unit would make the trip a bit simpler. I followed the instructions (which were not easy to understand, since they were largely picture based), and plugged it in to my flat iron. Immediately, I heard a buzzing sound and my flat iron melted all the way through in the middle.

Upon returning from my trip (during which I could not plug in any electrical items since my converter was not trustworthy), I notified Amazon and was told that the 30-day return window had closed but they would make a "special exception" and allow me to return it for a refund. They gave me a $20 credit for the "inconvenience", which might have satisfied me for the true inconvenience of not being able to use my phone charger, hair dryer, or now-dead flat iron during the trip. However, they were not willing to compensate me for even part of the $100 to replace my flat iron. I am shocked to see that Amazon does not replace items damaged by their faulty products. I'll think twice about ever buying electronic items from them again!

title: If you travel, you want this one!!!
text: This is a great, little device!  First of all, I think it's beautiful and sleek, and easy to use.  Just slide it open, plug in the cable that links to your iPod, and if you are using batteries, that's it, good to go.  Just plug in the AC cord if you aren't using batteries.  Uses 4 AAA batteries, so the batteries are small, don't add any noticeable weight to the unit.  Your iPod stays in it's own protective case, no fitting it onto a dock slot.  I've had one Altec Lansing speaker set and one Sonic Impact speaker set that the slot became damaged, so I'm glad I don't deal with that anymore.  This thing is light, small, about the size of a very, VERY large eyeglasses case so it packs very nicely in a purse, carry-on or suitcase, even better if you can get along without the bulky AC cord and just use batteries.  But it's about the sound, isn't it?  If you are looking for sound in your hotel room, or bathroom, mobile home, bedroom, kitchen, garage, den, etc., you are going to LOVE this little guy, and it will be more than loud enough, it can crank!  The sound is really great!  It looks great, performs great, and I just bought another one for a friend going to Mexico in a week.  Now, if you want a loud, space-filling but still portable speaker, get the In-Motion IM9 unit, as I did also.  I have both.  The IM9 is too big for the suitcase, and it's REALLY heavy, but it's screaming loud, great for the backyard or tailgating or any party setting, and very compact and portable while protecting the iPod within it's great loading system.  But this JBL is your OTHER speaker system for light weight travel or just to fill a room at home.  If you don't love it as I do, I don't know what planet you live on!

title: My first HDTV
text: I haven't written a review before, but in case there were others like me who were thinking about buying their first HDTV, don't be fooled by the low price.  This is a great TV!  The colors are magnificent, bright and bold, but best of all, true, and true throughout the screen.  The contrast amazes me.  The blacks are really black while somehow delivering really bold, bright colors.  In automatic mode, the TV always subtly changes the picture size for watching standard broadcast or HD programs.  You never have to adjust anything yourself.  Pictures also look great using my regular DVD player, but my best movie experience is always watching HBOHD.  The sound is great too, but I've connected my home theater sound system, and now TV watching is a breath-taking experience!  Watching sports is the best experience.  The wide format allows you to see more of the game, and the sharp detail allows you to see things you missed before.  Hockey has always been hard to enjoy on regular TV, so if you love hockey, you have to get HD. Finally you can follow the puck, and the cameras don't have to move so much because of the wide screen.  You will love watching sports on this TV!  I used to do other things while watching TV, but now it commands my attention.  This is a great set for watching within 10 feet, so if you have a cozy area for gathering around the set, or say in the bedroom, it's more than enough size.  It only weighs about 40 lbs, so it's really light, easy for one person to get a grip on it and move it around.  If you're worried about such a low price for an HDTV, don't, not with this set.  It's highly rated by the editors at [...], and highly rated by me, too!  I'm really loving this TV!

text: Didn’t think I would enjoy this, but I actually do & happy that I made the purchase. The best part is the clock. I love that it dims with the light.

title: Not sturdy at all
text: Doesn't last. Not sturdy at all.

title: Do NOT waste your money!!
text: It has potential of being a great player. The picture quality and all the apps are really nice...when the darn thing works. This player has the habit of shutting itself off randomly. And forget customer service. Useless. Also, wifi connect is very poor. Finally had to connect by Ethernet. Great for the 5-10 minutes it works. I love my LG TVs, but going elsewhere for a blu-ray player.

title: Case not as pictured
text: Purchased for my boyfriend who prefers low profile. Case that was sent was not as pictured and didn't have a clasp. For the amount, pointless to return.

title: Beautiful cover
text: Hesitant to purchase after some previous reviews, this has held up quite well and I receive so many compliments. Unfortunately, I am a designer purse snob, and still this case is much preferred over my genuine leather and even Kate Spade cover, merely for its aesthetics, versatility and functionality. I do wish that it would hold steadier in portrait views but find myself utilizing landscape more often. Oh, and I don't like my apple logo unsecured, but easily remedied by utilizing the plastic that came with the case as a shield. Very pleased, especially or the price.

title: Five Stars
text: Love!

title: Great stand for the Wyze camera
text:
Pros: Overall this camera stand is great. It comes with a small wire and plug and so you don’t ever see the wires when it’s plugged in. It does just what you’d expect and allows you to mount a camera at an outlet.

Cons: the plug wasn’t as secure in the outlet as I would have expected. If I left it as it shows in the picture it falls out of the outlet pretty easily. I put this in my kitchen and have my Alexa plugged In with it so the plug from the Alexa is plugged into the bottom outlet and holds the mount In securely.

If you are looking for a way to plug in your Wyze camera and not have a big cord showing get this stand.

text: Wrong charger

title: Good

title: Good
text: Just what I expected

title: Bright, good colors, but battery stops holding a charge
text: This color flood light is perfect for various lighting situations and the magnet on the back is super helpful. The biggest problem is if you use it for hours a day with it plugged in, the built in battery’s life expectancy is reduced.  I was able to have it light stay on full brightness for at least 40 minutes when new, now the battery is so won out after 3-4 months, that it only stays on full brightness for about 10 minutes before it needs to be plugged in

title: Use the included cable! Bogs down after
Annoying and un-initiative power on/power off, kills usability
text: Sound quality and fit is perfect but the power on process kills it. You need to hold down AND release the power button to turn the earbuds on, but the problem is there is no sound/light that gives you feedback on when you can release the button. And if you hold down the button too long, it won't power on at all. Not only that, the power-on sound only plays a couple seconds AFTER releasing the power button. Essentially, these ear buds are a pain to turn on especially if you put them down for a little bit and you don't know if they're already on, or already off.

title: Delicate power mosfets, burns out too easily.
text: This is a neat circuit for experimenting/demonstrating induction heating, but the circuit is highly is highly fragile and prone to burning out the power mosfets if too much mass is being heated or if the metal isn't placed absolutely in the center of the coil. This is the second one that I burned out after using the first one for less than 24 hours. The moment it burns out, you'll see a small puff of white smoke come out near the toroidal inductor, the power LED will stills stay on, but will no longer heat up. Because of how delicate this is, there's really not much you can use it this circuit for other than heating up paperclips

title: Warning - Not a flat plug as advertised!
text: The power strip was simply and functionally packaged - good solid cord and minimalist design, but I cannot use it because the power plug is nothing like what is shown in the photos. The power plugs one of the older style plugs where it sticks out 90 degrees from the wall and not a flat connector for low profile plug as expected. This makes it nearly impossible to squeeze behind the bookshelf I was planning to use it for.

title: Every feature works, programs as expected! Soldering a little crusty, but fully self contained!
text: Comes with a handy case and a set of breakout pins. All the connectors work, so does the OLED display, wifi controller and the 5 position joystick switch. Has a dedicated power button. Takes some tinkering to find out the right Arduino board manager(it ended up being ESP2866 - 2.7.4, WeMos D1 R1) and upgrading the standard ESP libraries. The best feature about this board is that it comes with an 18650 battery holder so you don't need any external power source, fully self contained palm sized micro controller with display.

title: 5 stars because it works just like the old one and came new as described
text: Bought this for my parent's 10 year old DVD player because the batteries in their old remote leaked and ruined the connections. This remote is the exact same as the old one so 5 stars for working exactly as expected. Came new, shipping was amazon fast.

title: Great picture quality's but difficult connecting to WiFI
text: The picture quality and brightness is great. It's probably the best value in picture quality for the price of this TV, but the main problem is that won't connect to Wifi in my living room that is using a WiFi range extender. I have an iPhone and other wifi devices that have no problems connecting to the same extender, but this TV doesn't. I tried moving the TV closer to my main wifi router and it connected and was able to complete the setup process. Otherwise this TV is excellent with the number of HDMI ports, screen brightness and clarity. The room it's in doesn't get a lot of direct sunlight, so I can't speak to it's display quality in bright lighting, but generally happy with it except for the wifi problems.

title: No problem, it works - added bluetooth to Windows 10, no software needed
text: Contrary to some other reviews, my Windows 10 Home Edition recognized this USB bluetooth adapter the instant it was plugged in, no other software or drivers needed. Had no problems connecting both my bluetooth mouse and keyboard to it. Pretty low latency, was able to play video games and had no noticeable lag on either the mouse or keyboard. The only drawback is Windows doesn't seem to wake from standby mode when your keyboard or mouse is pressed and connected over bluetooth.

title: Excellent value for the money - does exactly what you expect this to do
text: What's to rate on this? If you're looking at this listing, you're pretty much sure this thing does exactly what it's supposed to - split a 3.5mm head phone jack into two separate RCA channels for connecting to things like amplifiers and recorders. Cable is braided and pretty flexible, there's no static in the line and seems to be well shielded to not pick up any interference from a power supply the cable runs next to.

title: Outperforms on sound quality!
text: These are amazing for the price, since it's in-ear ear buds, it does a great job of isolating and blocking out outside noise. Initially, I wasn't expecting much from these due to the low price of 15 dollars, I bought them to replace my set of Plantronics Backbeat GO's whose battery no longer holds a charge. But after powering these new ones on(battery came dead from the factory), it blew my mind on how good the sound quality was - base is deep and clear - these do seem to lean base heavy, so make sure that's your thing.  I'm not able to get 10 hours of play time, but at least closer to 8, but that's not a problem considering Apple's AirPods gets a measly 4 hours at best. The back of these have a little magnet inside of them so they stick together. The build quality is pretty good, but I doubt these are water resistant or sweat proof, considering they use a hard plastic flap to cover the micro USB charging port instead of silicon or rubber. Pairing it with your phone does take a few tries, definitely read the manual

title: Decent signal extender - hard to setup dual band with WPS
text: Like the other reviewers, the basic setup is super simple - I was able to get it connected at 2.4G (802.11g) pretty easily with the one touch WPS setup, but using the same setup process to connect to 802.11n and ac modes over the 5Ghz spectrum didn't work, even with the extender right next to the router. The WPS light kept flashing and eventually timed out with no 5Ghz signal. Not a problem, had to login to the interface via the built in webpage and connect to the 5Ghz hotspot manually. But in the end, I ended up disabling 5G on the extender to router side because it was actually slowing the connections down because the 5Ghz band has a harder time going through walls than the 2.4Ghz band. Overall, this range extender works as well as one can hope for the 22 dollars it cost. Was able to expand the indoor range of the router's signal by at least 50 feet in a brick, wood and stucco house.

title: Does 4k @ 60hz with no problems!
text: Don't let the cheap price fool you, this hdmi cable works well! It's not fancy with 24k gold contacts, silver wires and ostrich leather wrapped connectors, but it sends the videos to TV like it is. HDMI is digital, so it either works or it doesn't. This cable works even with such as low price. The rubber is flexible and the connectors slide smoothly in or out of the HDMI slots without any lube.

title: Works perfectly, what else to say???
text: If you're looking at this, it's pretty easy to figure out what this does. If you're looking for something to do what this thing looks like it does, then this 3.5mm audio splitter does that perfectly! The leads are a good length, there's no static or interference, the contacts make a clean clear connection! I used this to split the audio out so one line goes to speakers and another to a subwoofer. Works well!

title: Excellent value SSD drive
text: This is an excellent value hard drive - sure, you can get a faster SSD drive out there, but you get roughly 80% of the speed at 1/3rd of the price compared to gaming SSD drives, so it's a no brainer for a budget gaming PC or doing simple things like watch videos, surf the web etc. Easy to install, the only down side is that it doesn't come with any screws or a SATA cable. Comes in easy to open packaging, basic and no thrills, but who buys a hard drive for packaging???

title: does exactly what you expect!
text: If you’re looking at this time, odds are you know exactly what it does and what you need. Yes, this harddive mount does exactly that, the metal is stiff and doesn’t bend, holds 2.5 inch laptop and ssd drives in place! Comes with mounting screws for both bottom mount ssds and to the 3.5 inch case caddy!

title: So much thermal paste! Great value!
text: I used this to keep a high power LED chip with a 50watt thermal dissipation cool. The LED chip was 2 inches x 2.75 inches and half of one tub was more than enough to cover everything! This thermal paste did an excellent job transferring the heat to the heatsink. It was a little runny, but not to the point that it will drip. Good adhesion and ultra fine particles to fill any cracks between the two surfaces. Does tend to leave a nasty grey stain on your skin. This pack is enough to probably do 10+ cpus.... no idea what I’m going to do with the other 4 tubes. The syringes came well pack with caps, there was no leakage.

title: Excellent all around monitor for the money!
text: It's hard to find a 4k monitor in the 27-32 inch size and out of all 4k monitors in this size range, this monitor is a great value - the colors are bright, supports VESA mounts and has both HDMI and Display Port inputs. The bezel isn't the thinnest, but at only half an inch, it's still good form to function. There is only 1 multi function joystick type button for all display settings and power. Has 3.5mm speaker out for DisplayPort and HDMI audio. One huge bonus is that it uses a standard computer cord and doesn't require an external power brick unlike a majority of the 4k displays. Has multiple display modes for gaming/reading/movies/etc, but I wish I had a dark room/reduced blues/night setting.

title: A little bulky, but definitely protects!
text: I got this for my parent''s iPad - they're a bit clumsy so they're constantly dropping things, but after 2 years and many drops later, their iPad is still working with no cracks in the screen because of this case. It's solid and definitely protects at all four corners

title: 5 stars because it works as advertised!
text: I'm amazed at all the batteries this charger can recharge. I had no problems recharging some 14500 AA sized cells and some 18650 Samsung cells for my Zebralight. The nice thing about this charger is that it shows the amount of charge left in the battery the moment you put it in(since it's never a good idea to drain a lithium battery down to 0). The charger is cheap, but works fantastically, it shuts off automatically. And it even quick charges the battery in the first slot(if two batteries are put in simultaneously). No problems charging regular NiMH batteries either, it's smart enough to recognize the battery type the moment you put it in.

title: Successfully met my low expectations!
text: It’s a battery holder! It holds my 18650 batteries to make a 6v power pack with no issues. Holds my batteries snug! This thing has one job and it does it!

title: Excellent travel size and 6 month long battery life!
text:
Updated 1 year later(May 3, 2020)

Down grading from 5 stars to 3 stars because it turns out there might be a bug in the mouse that once you pair it with 2 different computers over bluetooth, you cannot reset the mouse to use the wireless dongle. There is also no support on the Logitech website - try searching their website for the manual for this mouse, it's absolutely missing. You'll see an FAQ section and some various sections on tech spec, but no setup guide or manual!

*********

If you're tried of replacing batteries, this mouse is for you! I'm impressed by how long a single AA battery lasts in this mouse. I haven't had to replace the battery since getting it 6 months ago even with daily use. The two modes is nice since it lets me connect this mouse to two computers! The bluetooth is strong and connects well to my MacBook Pro, while the included radio frequency receiver is plugged into a iMac and I can switch between computers with a. simple button click.

title: Good range, but asks for excessive personal info to register/active
text: This is a great range extender hardware wise, it has 3 modes, lets you extend your wifi to wifi, wifi to ethernet port, or as an access point(ethernet port to wifi). The range is good and I like the simple wall plug format. The biggest drawback is you can't use this without registering your email address and registering 2 extreme sensitive personal questions such as my mother's maiden name, what city my mother/father was born, best friend's name, etc... Why do I need to give such sensitive information just to use a wifi range extender???

title: Best networked web cam for the price, backed by Amazon!
text: I got this for a around 60 during the prime day special - the cam was easy to setup and although the iPhone app is a bit basic, it does the job done. The good thing about the amazon cloud cam is that it's backed by Amazon so there's less concern about the company going out of business and losing support for the camera. Got the basic plan, which offers 24 hours or video recording. The motion detection seems to work ok, 👍 and the night vision is very usable. I would buy it again, since it works exactly as expected

title: A full 128 GB and not a byte less! (at 1,000,000,000 bytes per GB)
text: Unless you're a computer programmer where a byte is really base 8 and 1GB is really 1,073,741,824 bytes! Well, this is a micro SD card, it works just as you would expect a microSD card to work - you shove it into places that has a matching slot and voila! you have 128GBs of pure digital fairy dust. I use this on a GoPro Hero 5 Session and it can record 4k video without a problem!

title: Huge monitor and comes with high speed USB charging ports in the back!
text: Monitor came well packaged and works well on both the HDMI and display port connection! I managed to use it with an IBM laptop and a MacBook Pro over the display port! There's also an ambient light sensor to automatically adjust the brightness depending on the indoor lighting conditions! Monitor is almost too big, but it's not too heavy. Colors are bright and there are no dead pixels. No built in speakers even though the HDMI says there's an audio connection. Works as expected so 5 stars!

title: A battery holder - does exactly what it looks like it does.
text: Took about 2 weeks for this to arrive from the seller because it's drop shipped from over seas, but it's definitely worth the wait and price. The plastic is heavy duty and the hinge is flexible enough that I don't think it'll break off from lots of opens and closes.There is a little snap button tab that keeps the case closed. This thing has 1 job and 1 job only, to hold AA batteries, and it's does a perfect job at that.

title: 4 stars because it works, but connection lose sometimes
text: Works way better connecting my 2016 Macbook pro touch bar to a Samsung wide screen monitor than the other USB-C to HDMI converters, down 1 star because the cable doesn't seem shielded, so every time I have my phone next to the cable, the monitor blanks out, and if I move the laptop, the monitor also flickers

title: Excellent quality cable. Works perfectly on my MacBook Pro Touchbar
text: Excellent cable for charging my MacBook Pro with the touch bar using an Anker charger. Can charge at full power

title: Fits well, but comes off easily. Neither happy or unhappy with it.
text: It fits well but it does come off the keyboard easily on my 2016 MacBook with the touch bar. It doesn't interfere with the typing except it does make the already shallow keys on the new keyboard design more muted with less tactile feedback. Overall I don't know if I would buy it again or return it, neither happy or unhappy with the keyboard protector..

title: Does not work with a MacBook Pro!
text: [[VIDEOID:6bee765e8c7af8f122e3326b49df78b8]] Build quality is decent and the cable length/size is perfect, but it just doesn't work. The moment I plug it into a 2016 13 inch MacBook Pro(with the new USB-C ports), the laptop's screen does a couple angry flashes then... nothing, absolutely nothing. The screen on the laptop goes back to normal, but nothing is displayed on the monitor(a Samsung WQHD 2k monitor - not that it makes much of a difference). In the video I uploaded, you can see the monitor working when it's connected to my iPhone using the iPhone to HDMI connector, but once I switch that HDMI cable to the Nice Cable USB-C to HDMI connector, nothing happens. I tried connecting the HDMI end first, then a second try by connecting the USB-C end first, still nothing.

title: Works just as expected!
text: 5 stars because this looks like what was displayed, and works just as expected with my 2016 MacBook Pro with the touch bar. was able to connect it with a usb 3.0 external hard drive. the computer and hard drive didn't even know there was this adapter in between them.

title: Seems flimsy and doesn't seem to hold the charge for too long.
text: Seems a bit flimsy - it feels like it's made from lightweight plastic and definitely not water/dust resistant. Battery only holds a charge for about a week before needing to be recharged. Otherwise, it works as expected. Allows you to find the locator using your phone, or if you click the button on the finder, it makes your phone ring. Good if you frequent lose your phone or keys, but as someone who doesn't, then its restricted to being a novelty item.

title: 1.5 volts - works perfectly in 2010 mini mac.
text: Works perfectly in upgrading our old 2010 Mini Mac - you don't need to get this in pairs! Our mac came with 2GBs with 1GB in each of the 2 slots. Removed one of the existing samsung 1GB memory sticks in the top slot(because it's the first and easiest to remove slot), and popped this Cosair 4GB SODIMM in, computer booted right up, recognized the memory and started using it right away. With the High Sierra OS upgrade, it was definitely running slow before, now it's almost like day 1.

title: Works just as expected!
text: 5 stars because it work just like expected - usage is very simple, just plug the ribbon cable into the camera connector on your Raspberry Pi 2, then run raspi-config to enable the camera hardware and that's it. You can run the built in command raspistill to start taking photos. I've had this over a year now and it still works great as a webcam

title: Perfect length of 3.5 feet. Even comes with reusable cable tie!  Used to change a GoPro
text: Perfect length of 3.5 feet(purely objective observation, depends on who's asking). It works to charge my GoPro, it's a freeking cable, like what can possibly go wrong or be bad about it? It even came with a free plastic bag and a reusable cable tie. The cable tie is made from velcro and soft like a cactus. Even if the USB-C cable breaks, I'll still have the awesome cable tie and plastic bag that it came with!

title: Does absolutely what it looks like it should do
text: Doesn't take much of an explanation to figure out what this plug splitter does. It achieves the results beautifully - plug one end into the wall, plug 2 other things into the other ends to get 2x the power sockets!

title: Pelican cases speak for themselves
text: Pelican cases are the standard for hard shelled cases to protect valuables from shock, dust, water and humidity. The stuff in this case won't survive a trip to the bottom of the ocean(though the case itself might), but it'll definitely protect any equipment you have if your basement gets flooded for instance. Comes with a block of foam on the inside with cutouts you can tear off to make a form fit for the stuff you want to protect. Latches shut with a reassuring snap

title: Great router - probably future proof for the next 3-5 years
text: I bought this with the intention of hacking it and putting Linux on it, but surprisingly, it works straight out of the box with all the features I need. The only drawback is that the firmware is buggy in the diagnostic side. It often shows devices connected over WiFi as connected over an ethernet/LAN port. The speed is way faster than what my cable provider provides. Also, for wireless MAC control, the built in firmware does not display the netbios name for the machine - requiring you to enter in mac addresses manually.

title: It's an SD card! Reputable brand - 128GB, it works, what's to hate
text: It's an SD card! Works well recording 4k video in my GoPro session 5.

title: Good cable. Fabric/braided covering, no problems
text: If you're looking of this cable, you know exactly what you're getting into. An extension cable for a male - female HDMI pair. I used it move a Roku stick away from the back of my TV because the TV is mounted on a brick wall and it seems to reduce the Roku's wifi reception

title: Decent keyboard, good range, long battery life, touch pad a bit weird.
text: Works as expected, the only down side is the touch pad doesn't seem to be that sensitive. It's hard to explain, but if you use a touch pad on an macbook or the apple magic touch pad, there's a significant difference in sensitivity, and texture, but overall the keyboard is good for occasional one off uses

title: Terrible software and iPhone/mobile app makes the camera unusable
text:
The video quality of the camera is pretty good, but the deal breaker for this GoPro is the horrible Capture iphone/mobile app. In order to use the iPhone Capture app to preview images and change the various image/video settings, you must register an account with GoPro before the Capture app will connect with the GoPro Hero Session. By itself it isn't a show stopper, but the Capture app automatically logs you out of the account every week or so, seemingly at random - the major problem with this it requires an internet connection/wifi/cell access to login again. The brilliant engineers at GoPro didn't think of this and realize that people tend to use their GoPros in remote places that won't always have internet access/wifi like backcountry skiing, or far from shore snorkeling or scuba diving.

Another major issue with the camera is on a 32GB memory card, up to 3-4GB is used up saving the .LRV files for the previews and there are no options to turn the creation of those files off.

title: Prepare yourself on spending time + effort
text: oh wow, such a tiny board, but wow, a fully functioning computer for 30 bucks! Yeah, its not windows or a mac, but you can get a fully functional computer with this thing.

title: Hey, it's an memory card... what could go wrong?
text: Odds are that if you're looking at this product, you're already know what this thing does and what you need it for. I used it for a raspberry pi and I have also used it for a dash cam tor record 720p video without any problems

title: There's nothing wrong with this cable
text: There's nothing wrong with this cable. It's 6 feet, and I used it to connect electronic audio doodads together. Because it works as expected, it gets 5 stars. If looking for a cable like this, you ought to know what you need it for.

title: Fits perfectly, lots of parts
text: Fits the Raspberry PI2 perfectly, there are many layers that need be placed ontop of each other.

title: Regulates voltage! Boosts low volts to higher volts. Provides decent current load.
text: Works exactly as described - used it to boost 12V to 34V for a 100W high power LED. At 34V, it was able to output 1.9A without any problems. I was able to get it up to 36.2 volts before it maxed out the variable resistor. But I wouldn't run it at the over voltage since the capacitors are only rated at 35V. It does get fairly warm, and there's a minor half second lag between an voltage change and the actual voltage being displayed on the readout. Operates silently, it does get a little warm, (34V @ 1.5A). Was able to take input from another switching power supply that provides 20V. The only minor problem is the screw terminals do not seem to hold a wire that well. For permanent use, I recommend using the solder tabs.

title: Super quiet, tiny, usb powered
text: This is super tiny, and usb powered, so theres not any messy power adapter cables to tug around. Its whisper quiet and runs cool. USB 3.0 worked fine with my older USB 2.0 slot. Had to reformat when using it on my mac.

title: Not bad, only if you don't want an [ESC] key
text: This keyboard is missing the escape key, the escape key is just a square and I have yet to find out what it does. Not good if you want to exit full screen mode for a lot of video programs or online videos like netflix. It also does not report the battery level remaining, unlike Apple's magic mouse/keyboard/trackpad. It seems to go to sleep pretty quickly, so if it's waking up, the first few key strokes won't get registered. It would be nice if it uses AA batteries instead of AAA

title: Good sound, but non standard ear tips
text:
The bass on these are way better than the JayBird Freedoms that this replaced, but the problem is these don't use the same standard sized ear tips that nearly every other earbud manufacturer seems to use(these require a hole in the tip that's significantly bigger than others). If you lose them, then you'll end up paying $5 + shipping for a set(which is essentially 2), where as I can get a pack of 10 for $2 off any site. Switching to more comfortable gel tips are not an option too.

Another warning is that the microusb charge plug doesn't have the same feel/pop/click feeling when plugging them in to charge, the first time I kept pressing the charge cable and I almost broke the tip or wonder if I used the right plug.

The plus side is that the bass is really good, way better than my JayBirds, and it has the nice battery level indicator on my iPhone.

title: Well designed and functional alarm clock.
text: This is a perfect no thrills alarm clock radio. You can select the alarm time and either the beeper or radio as your wake up sound. It's not digital tuning, so if you're constantly changing radio stations, this might not be for. But the radio reception is great, and the power cord is the antenna so there are now weird wires dangling around. The face of the alarm is smooth and glossy and the led display is a soothing amber color that is not too bring for small rooms but perfectly readable. The important buttons to set the alarm time and to turn on the radio is easily accessible and memorizable on top of the radio, while the buttons to set the time are well hidden in the back. Got this from target to save on shipping so that the radio will keep my dog company while I'm away. Does a good job of waking me up too

title: Such a classic device
text: Served me well for over 3 years until I left it on the charger in my car on a hot sunny day in the middle of the nevada desert during the summer, the battery went dead after that. Was 30GB, but my iPhone 5 has the same amount of memory now for the exact same price! the touch wheel was smooth, and let me click lots of clicks.

title: No problems, it's a flash memory drive!
text: It's a flash memory drive, i'm able to record 720p and 1080p uncompressed video to it without any problems with write speeds. using it with a contour roam. it's tiny, make sure kids and dogs don't swallow it.

title: Great except there's no way to disable the beeps on a Mac
text: I love this camera, too bad the Contour is no longer in business. The form factor is great, and the simple slide to record feature makes turning it on and recording the action so painless. I don't get why people love the GoPros, they are the most ugly looking cameras, why would it be a square that sticks out like a sore thumb?!?!? WTF. The video recorded during the day is perfect in both 720 and 1080p, the rotating lens lets you mount it in any direction. I use it for a dash cam while driving.

title: Great for the price
text: This isn't a Bose, but then I'm not paying 200+ for it either. It's a great subwoofer to replace commonly blown out one in the jeep wranglers. Sounds a lot better than the stock subwoofer. Installation will take about an hour to remove the old subwoofer from the enclosure and was a great fit.

title: It fits really well! but feels kind of cheap, wait it is cheap!
text: it's a simple plastic case, but feels a bit cheap, oh wait, it is cheap. The plastic smell does seem to make my dog want to chew on my phone, I can't imagine the gorilla glass being good for his digestive system.

title: These seem pretty universal
text: and fits pretty much every ear buds type head phones that I have. My dog keeps swallowing the old ones and I'm not digging them out of his poo.

title: Sticks to the windshield, has a good hold
text: Sticks to the windshield to make a dash cam my contour camera. Holds well, I can't even pull it off! It only fell off once during the winter when I got really cold.

title: Tight fit
text: Tight fit, I can't seem to remove the top case because it snaps on so tight, but the rubbery texture feels good and doesn't  show fingerprints or smudges. After 2 months, a corner of the case cracked because of the stress from being on so tight, the crack is small so it's not a problem. The case doesn't add too much to the thickness of my macbook pro 13.

title: Fast delivery and easy setup on a iMac with Mac os mavericks
text: The setup couldn't be any more simple if you're using a Mac. (using it with a 2010 iMac 21inch) The UPS was automatically recognized by the Energy Saver utility in Mac OS Maverick's system preferences panel. There was no other third party utilities that I needed to install or configure. I'm not sure if this is the case when using this with a Windows machine. The front UPS display shows run time, battery percentage, power events, but the best feature is that it shows real time power use(in watts) by all the things plugged into the UPS. Because of this, I found out my mac uses about 50Watts in idle, and about 105 when doing heavy video processing. It's a great way to monitor power usage. Plenty of power ports in the back and seem easily capable of powering the mac for about 30 minutes. It even has a test mode that switches it to battery power without unplugging anything

title: It simply works

title: problematic operation
text:
UPDATE (12/27/2019):
After getting this dash cam, I was expecting an improvement over the performance of the first dash cam I had bought this past July. However, it STILL has to have the date and time reset when I drive. The dash cam arrived on Tuesday, December 24. I plugged it in to a charging device and set the date and time as well as format my 256 GB micro SD. The menus work well. However, there is no menu option to set the behavior under low light conditions.

On Wednesday, I connected it to my car. All video was correctly stamped with the date and time. Friday I drove to a friend’s house. The date and time had reset on its own to 2018-06-05. See photo.

After it was dark and I was on my way home, I found that the dash cam still has a problem with FLARE. See photo.

Bottom line: I’m still looking for a better dash cam. I cannot set the date every time I get in my vehicle, and I want to have a clear image / video of what is happening in front of me as I drive. Other dash cams advertise an image angle of 165-170 degrees. That is a little too wide to produce sharper images.

UPDATE (12/23/2019):
The company responded and promised another dash cam would be checked out and then sent to me. In return, I will return the dash cam I bought last July - no cost to me for shipping. I just need to change my review from 1-star. I am keeping my fingers crossed that the new dash cam will perform better, and I will update after I have had a chance to try it. Who knows? I might even give this dash cam a higher rating.

UPDATE (10/5/2019):
One would expect the company would respond when they saw a 1-star review. But NOPE.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (8/5/2019):
When I saw this camera has the ability to record video to a higher capacity SD card, I thought I would order it for a trip I was planning to take. I also ordered a 128 GB micro SD card AND a 256 GB micro SD card. I decided to use the 256 GB card since the trip would take a minimum of 16 hours. As it turned out there are 500 3-minutes clips for a total of 1,500 minutes if each was a full 3 minutes. That works out to be 25 hours of recorded video clips.

I connected the camera to my portable charging block and set the date as well as other settings. Those other settings included 30 FPS (frames per second), image size of 1920 x 1086 and 3 minutes clip size. In the event the card filled up, the oldest video was to be erased first.

The problem was that the date was reset to the date of manufacture - it was either 2018-06-06 or 2018-06-05. It was NEVER recording with the correct date and time. This is a problem in case an event occurs that needs a date and time stamp.

Night vision is one problem. See the photo. When a vehicle is directly in front, the tag reflects so much light that the tag number cannot be read. If stopped at a light, I can turn off my headlights and record the tag number of the vehicle in front.

During the daytime, the tag number cannot be read unless the vehicle is within about 20 feet such as at a stop light.

I will go back to searching for a decent dash cam that can record using large capacity cards and has much better image quality, especially at night.

title: Quality camera and image
text:
UPDATE (8/4/2019):
After some recent system updates, I have found that the 5 sec video may not be accessible until after someone has left the area. It was not that snappy before, but now it seems to be slower in accessing the video from my phone.
Additionally, I have had packages put on my front deck / steps that is 10 feet away from my front door and the Blink XT2 camera, but the video was never triggered. The Blink is aimed in that direction. So I have changed the sensitivity from 5 to 9, the highest. Also, I have changed the clip length to 10 seconds. We shall see how this functions.

Since I have had the Blink XT2 less than a week, I will update when I know more about how long the batteries last.

READ THE INSTRUCTIONS BEFORE BEGINNING INSTALLATION.

Download the app first. Once the app is downloaded, it will prompt you as to what has to be done. Use the device to take a photo of (read) the camera’s ID (QR code) OR enter the Serial Number manually.

Open the camera - Remove the back cover by holding down the gray ‘button’ while pulling the bottom of the back cover away from the camera body. It has a rubber or silicone gasket in the groove around the cover. Because it has a friction fit, it can be difficult to pry off the cover. I could put a little lube on the sealing gasket, but it might cause problems if it reacts with either the plastic or the gasket.

All synching has to be done while the camera is open, then it is put together before mounting it. The Sync module has to remain plugged into an AC outlet, so find a convenient place for the module to rest or hang.

The back cover is replaced by pressing it firmly where the posts are located until a ‘click’ is heard near each corner.

I used the base of the mount to locate and drill 2 small holes in the wood. Then I put the screws into the mount and the base and attached the mount to the house. After the base is attached, the cam is pressed onto the mount. That was the hard part.

The mount attaches to the hole in the back cover by pressing the assembled camera onto the mount. This should be done after the mount is attached to the desired location using the two screws included.

I had installed the camera as high as I could above my front door. Most of the videos showed the top of my head, nothing as to identifying me from my face. So I thought I would move it a little lower, still above the door; and as I turned the camera so I could use a long screwdriver to remove the screws, it came off the mount and fell onto the floor. Apparently, it suffered no ill effects. Perhaps the very warm temperatures made the plastic loose enough for it to come off easily. I would like to have a more secure mounting system. I have ordered a mount that has a cover to hold Blink XT2 securely.

At bottom of the Home screen of the app, be sure to slide the switch so that it says Armed.
Had to go into settings (not labeled as that) and ENABLE motion sensor. On the Home screen of the app, the serial number of the camera is printed less than halfway down and on the left. On the right side, a symbol of three lines appears. Press this and it opens Camera Settings. This is where Enable is located for MOTION DETECTION.

The video length can be set but the default is 5 seconds. It can be turned on for Live View which is almost continuous recording. 

In the next week, I will attempt to “see” what is happening at my front door. I am hoping there will be no problem getting notifications when someone comes to my front door.

UPDATED AFTER USING A FEW DAYS:
In a location that has no Wi-Fi access and spotty cell coverage, I was able to view the delivery person bringing my package to my door.

The mount I ordered is a two-piece plastic enclosure that is attached to an aluminum base that is attached to the wall using 3 screws. First I drilled 3 pilot holes (5/64" drill bit) for the screws. They were tightened using a manual screwdriver so the aluminum would not crack. I plugged the hole on the bottom of the case where the USB cable could be used to charge rechargeable batteries. The foam that is used to package the Blink is too dense and stiff, so I used some closed-cell foam that came with another product.

title: Securely holds the Blink camera
text:
When I installed my Blink XT2, I found I needed to move it a little lower so I could maybe see the face of the delivery person. Thinking I could unscrew the mount without removing the camera, I turned the camera to one side so I could access the screws. The camera fell to the floor. A little bit of friction is not sufficient to hold these cameras. That is when I started looking at these mounts which SHOULD be included in the box.

This is in several parts. Plastic camera-enclosing parts are held together with 4 small screws. The metal part is attached to the wall with 3 flat-head #6 screws.

Unscrew the adjusting part so the base of the mount can be attached to the wall. Do not try to adjust the angle unless this part is loose. Use care when tightening the screws - do it manually so the screws are not over-tightened. The aluminum base could be cracked by over-tightening.

The small screws that are used to attach the back cover to the front should be machine screws, and the posts into which they are screwed should be metal. This is my opinion and is because these screws will have to be removed and reinstalled every time the batteries are replaced.

One piece of plastic had a small 'tab' on it that had to be cut off before the back cover would attach to the front.

A hole in the bottom of the plastic is there to allow a charging cable to be attached. If you do not plan to use rechargeable batteries and have no need for the USB cable, plug the hole so insects do not go inside looking for a new home. I used a small piece of closed cell foam packing material (photo).

If you want to use these mounts with the earlier Blink cameras, you might want to use some foam so the camera does not move around inside the enclosure (photo).

My devices - SSDs and 4-bay HDD enclosure - that are plugged into this hub have been disconnecting for no apparent reason. When the enclosure was connected to this hub, I kept seeing that warning that my drives were Not Ejected Properly

Connected this to my computer's USB 3.0 port. Plugged in the dongle for my battery powered mouse. Mouse began acting erratically, had to remove the dongle and reinsert it to reconnect. Functioned properly for a short while but disconnected.
Finally had to plug dongle in the port on my wired keyboard before it would stay connected and not perform erratically. Something must be interrupting the signal even when the LEDs indicate the hub is connected even during periods when my computer is asleep.

title: Look elsewhere - poor manufacturing and materials
text:
Almost 4 years ago I bought this charger. I left 3 different charging cables plugged into it.

It rarely had to be used, but when I wanted to use it today, I found one of the cables unplugged. When I attempted to plug in the cable again, it caused the power light to go out. Upon closer examination, I found the white plastic part that is supposed to aid in aligning the USB plug into the port was inside the plug, not in the charger port. When I plugged in the charger in another outlet, I found that it was dead. Evidently, the cable plug made contact across the port's metal connectors and shorted out the charger.

The photo shows that the metal contacts were mashed down into the port. They were supposed to be in the grooves of the plastic divider that broke off into the cable plug.
