Does what it is designed to do - store data.
For me, the SSD is connected to my USB dock with a short cable - no housing / case required. I can clone my current hard drive and then replace it with the newer SSD. Not too difficult.
The SSD was to be delivered by USPS but when the envelope arrived, someone had torn a hole in the envelope end and removed the SSD, then they used packing tape to tape it back together. Contacted Amazon about the theft and received the replacement a couple days later. Then I received an email asking / reminding me to return the damaged SSD. Haha!

title: Software update possible? - needed
text:
[[VIDEOID:f161ff87285aa6d07841ddc9c7fe9548]] Sadly, while this dash cam shows me how the traffic moved in the area in front of my vehicle, it lacks the ability to show clearly the license tag numbers except when the other vehicle is directly in front of mine AND when it is daylight with the sun NOT ahead. IOW, it cannot handle darkness very well (pixelated images), it cannot handle very bright scenes, it does not adjust well for lights at night, and tags cannot be read at night. And the recordings are set to the maximum quality - 1920 x 1080 pixels.

A minor drawback is that all of the video clips are arranged in chronological order on the memory card and are not saved in a separate folder for each date.

On July 29 heading toward Atlanta from Florida on I-75, I recorded a motor home roll-over on the opposite / southbound side of the interstate. However, because of the high median barrier, it was not possible to see what caused the roll-over. A lot of red dust came up indicating it was off the road. Video may be attached - if it's not too large. It is 960 x 540 pixels to keep its size manageable.

title: good Logitech mouse
text:
UPDATE (3/30/2019):

This mouse is still functioning as when it was new. I have replaced my 10-year-old Mac Pro with the 2018 Mac mini. I am still using the original Apple Cinema Display. The Logitech Control Center app was installed so the M705 / Marathon mouse would function properly. From time to time I have to unplug the unifying receiver and reinsert it to regain full access to the mouse and its correct assignments of the buttons.

NOTE: There is a newer version of the M705 mouse that does NOT have the side button (left side next to the thumb). The price I paid was $20 recently, but I have not used the newer version yet since this one that HAS the side button still functions.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (November 13, 2017 ):

This mouse was bought to replace the 4-year-old Logitech Performance Mouse - rechargeable battery - because the mouse acted erratically due to lint and other debris that got into the space between the bottom and the plastic covers over the buttons. It prevented drag-and-drop when it would disconnect while dragging. Sometimes the file being moved ended up in another folder that meant I had to UNDO the move and start over. What a pain.

(I began buying Logitech mouse designs after spending too much - $80 - for the Microsoft M6000 laser mouse that was terrible.)

The duration of the parallel battery design makes it last a longer time - I have not had to replace the original batteries yet, but I have been using this only since March of this year (8 months).

The pointer has a tendency to become up to 5 times larger if I move the mouse quickly back and forth left and right. I don't know if this is the mouse or the computer software. I find this interesting, but it does not concern me so I have not asked if anyone else has had the same experience.

One star has been deducted because the scrolling wheel can be used to move up or down the window I am viewing but the window jumps back to where I started. It does not do this all the time, but when I want to scroll up or down to see what has been displayed, it is a pain to have it jump back down or up to where the page had been.

The weight of the mouse is irrelevant when one uses the mouse. It stays on the mouse pad / surface just fine. I am not sure why someone would object to having a second battery in this mouse. For those who have forgotten any high school physical science, the parallel arrangement maintains the 1.5 volts of a single battery but doubles the capacity / run-time of one battery.

As for the mouse specifications: (height x width x depth): 2.6 x 4.3 x 1.6 in; 70.0 x 109.0 x 40 mm (these are from the Logitech site; I would say these measurements are width x length x height considering the way it usually is positioned). Mouse weight: 4.8 oz; 135 g. Compatible OS: Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 10, Windows XP, Windows Vista, Mac OS X 10.5 or later, Chrome OS.

For anyone who needs a wireless full-size mouse, I recommend the Logitech M705.

title: Not that reliable in the long term
text:
These batteries worked fine for the first year, and they held a charge for a period of time when they were idle.
However, after 4 years of sporadic use and being charged no more than 20 times total, these batteries were on stand-by in my Canon for a couple of months. When I turned on my Canon today to take some photos, the pair of these batteries showed 39% power remaining. This is not what I expect from these batteries (but it is better than the 'original' Canon LP-E6 batteries).

I ordered a second pair last month to replace the pair of Canon LP-E6 batteries that were not holding a charge - behavior was more like NiCd than Li-Ion batteries. We shall see how they hold up over longer than one month. I had charged the 'new' pair when I got them, and they had 95-98% power remaining today when I installed them.

title: Unrecognized by phone and computer - and it was a 64 GB SDXC card
text:
After I bought this 64 GB micro SD card, I put it in a box with my other SD and micro SD cards until I bought my new phone last year. I installed it with my new phone and SIM card.
Since that time, I have been unable to 'see' the micro SD card, so I could not set it to be used for all the photos and videos that I take with my phone. I connected my phone to my computer and transferred music with no problem since that was stored on my phone's internal memory. I could not download any photos, so I have been having to transfer the photos via my Google photos on my computer. I even removed the micro SD card and inserted it in my card readers and plugged one into a USB port. NOTHING.
So I inserted another micro SD card - this one is 128 GB. VOILA! I was able to see it in my computer as well as in my phone where I was able to access it as well as to format it – finally.

This micro SD card must have been defective from the start, a waste of $35. If I had used it immediately – although I didn't 'need' it at the time, I could have returned it. Now I will find out if the company really guarantees this for 10 years.

title: fit my camera
text: These batteries fit my camera and charged when I received them.

title: streak-free cleaner
text:
Cleans the TV screens without leaving streaking.
The spray bottle that was delivered does NOT leak.

title: Good keyboard protection
text:
For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.

title: good keyboard protection
text:
UPDATE (12/25/2021):

I have removed this skin (bought on January 27, 2020) for 3 reasons.
1. The keys were not so visible below the skin because it has become more translucent instead of remaining transparent.
2. The shift key on the left side was ripped from being used and from my fingernail, I would think. IOW, it's not so tough.
3. A sticky liquid has formed between my keyboard and the skin. I removed it with more than just wiping. No solvent has been used at any time. Perhaps the silicone reacted with the plastic keys. Nothing has ever been spilled on the keyboard. Still, I have a skin on the keyboard as protection against any liquid OR dust OR hair getting into my keyboard that I have been using since 2008 when it was new.

My replacement (Allinside) is now in place and I can once again see the keys.
The skin fits the keys such that it does NOT have to wrap around the edges of the keyboard.

UPDATE (7/14/2018): After one year I have to replace this keyboard skin because it is wearing out in several places, mainly the left side command key where there is a ¼ inch slit. When I have to type a long document / letter, I remove the skin so I can type faster on the aluminum keyboard because the keys require only a light touch. I have not switched to a BT keyboard because this one is so good, and the fact that it is wired is not a problem with a little tape to keep the cable out of the way when I slide the keyboard shelf in and out. The skin I received is transparent with nothing printed on any of the keys.

For those who have the wired Apple aluminum extended keyboard (with keypad), this product fits correctly to protect the keyboard from dust and spills. It is in use on my Mac Pro (early 2008). The description says for iMac, but it fits any of these keyboards of this style, not just the iMac keyboard.

It arrives folded, but that does not matter if it comes from a seller in the US who delivers it in a timely manner.

The keyboard cover does make it necessary to slow down the typing speed. That's not a real problem unless one is a touch typist or writer who spends a lot of time on the keyboard.

title: Good protection - so far.
text:
UPDATE (3/30/2019):

The edges of the glass screen protector has been on my phone for about 2 years. It has survived falling onto hard surfaces. However, around the edges the glass screen protector has quite a few chips but NO cracks across the screen that would prohibit my being able to use my phone.

ORIGINAL REVIEW (April 18, 2017 ):

Usable and functional, but it is narrower than the width of the screen, and it can trap dust where the edges do not meet the glass of the display since the display is curved at the edges.

Unlike plastic protector films, this glass screen protector allows fingerprints to be cleared from its surface easily.

If any problem occurs, I will update this review. I have owned it only 4 months.

title: good case
text:
Very adequate case for the WD Passport Ultra 2 TB hard drives as well as the 1 TB HDDs.

The case has 2 sides, one for the HDD and the other for the cable to connect the HDD to the computer. I have other flash drives in the mesh pocket and the cable is left connected to my USB hub.

title: Better now that it is not "LOST / STOLEN"
text:
UPDATE:
Stayed on the phone for over an hour to speak with a couple different customer service persons on January 2. After finding out that my "registered" Echo Dot had stopped, all they could come up with was that it had been reported as "lost" or "stolen" to explain why it would not register later. And then, after getting it straight with the customer service folks, I EDITED MY ORIGINAL REVIEW. For some reason, Amazon did not include it in my reviews; so here I am again.

Now Alexa responds when I say "Alexa" - or if an ad on the TV says "Alexa."

Alexa may be used more in the future as the abilities are expanded. Right now Alexa does not always understand what I am asking, especially when the TV is producing noise.

Alexa app keeps a record of whatever I have requested - on my phone (Android) as well as the iPad. On my desktop computer, I also can check my devices that are registered through Amazon. Now the Echo Dot shows up as one of my devices.

ORIGINAL REVIEW:
Alexa cannot answer simple questions such as "Who won the Gator Bowl?"
The music Alexa played is NOT my Prime Music, although Alexa did play Adele songs - shuffled. And another person was correct - no iTunes music.

Then, several hours later, it / she told me the Dot had to be connected to the internet … again, after having set up the Dot.

Alexa tells me I am not registered even though I had set up the Dot using my iPad and had been asking Alexa questions and getting various replies for several hours. Alexa is good at telling me the temperature in a nearby place - 10 miles away, although Google Maps has my location accurate.
So I attempt to reconnect using the app on my iPad and continue getting an error message that login failed as it nears the last ⅓ of the progress bar.
The Help is not available from the app because it stays on the error message.
So I use the app on my phone to see if I can access Help. I am told to reset the Dot. How often is this going to occur?
Of course I have other Wi-Fi devices. That should NOT be a problem.

This is NOT ready for prime time … no pun intended.

I do NOT intend to have to set up this device every couple hours.

The second connection attempt failed. Nothing wrong with my Wi-Fi or my internet connection. Maybe the problem is that it is raining.

I'm trying a reset and reregistering again this morning; then I'll decide whether I'll have to return the Echo Dot.

title: Plastic case broke after 18 months
text:
Fine for about 18 months. After a couple of drops ON CARPET, the plastic broke off on the bottom end.
This is not satisfactory, even for the price, so I do not recommend it.
I'm replacing it with another brand, and I hope to have better luck with the replacement.

title: nice charger
text:
This is better than the Nitecore i4 because its display shows the charging info / state. The Nitecore i4 did not.

My only complaint is that the manufacturer could make this charger wider to accommodate 26650 batteries. The slots would have to be wider and the Nitecore D4 would have to be wider. Additionally, the contacts would have to be adjusted so the 26650 batteries would not slip off the positive contact. Currently, I can charge only two 26650 batteries at a time - in slots separated by an empty slot. Even then I have to be careful not to bump the charger once I position the batteries or else the positive tips will slip off the charger's contacts.

Hey! If the charging slots are wider, maybe I could also charge my D cells in the Nitecore D4. Right now they are charged in the dumb chargers I bought from Harbor Freight and Amazon.

title: Good security camera
text:
After setting up and connecting, the camera kept telling me "User does not exist."
I had followed the instructions, but it seems the camera needs to be set up using the DEFAULT settings BEFORE changing them for security. This I learned after emailing the company.
Now it works very well. The movement using the app is quick - it may take a bit of patience to get it situated correctly.
It remains to be seen how fast this eats up my phone's data when a Wi-Fi signal is not available.

UPDATE: I will NOT buy another one of these cameras (or ANY OTHER DEVICE) from this company because of their refusing to support the dash cam I bought from them which has to have the date reset every time it is activated.

title: poor design.
text:
These allow me to use 2 AA rechargeable batteries in place of 1 D battery, so I have 4 AA rechargeable batteries in 2 of these to power my 2-cell LED Mag-light.
I decided to check them, and the light did not come on when I replaced them. The negative end is recessed in the plastic and does not make contact except with the first battery's positive tip. This means that SOMETIMES the spring in the end-cap of the Mag-light will contact the negative end of the adapter, but usually it does not. In other devices that have smaller springs, this would be no problem.
In those kid's toys that use D-cell batteries this probably is not a problem.
Bottom line: The negative end of the adapter is probably in need of a redesign to ensure it is ABOVE the plastic case, not below it.

title: look elsewhere
text: Replaced two of these in two iPods. They do not hold a charge when they are removed from either the computer or the clock-radio dock. Surely some manufacturer makes a replacement battery that will last as long as the original, and that was more than two years.

title: Good for storage and transport of files
text:
Formatted this when I got it a year ago. Transferred a lot of files / photos to it for backups. Had to move some of those files onto a 2 TB WD Passport. No problem with any of the processes.

Now the price is $50.

Whether those files are accessible 5 or 10 years from now will determine its real value.

Ditto for the 128GB PNY (except the price).

title: Increases the usability of my Mac Pro
text:
This PCI-e card allows my 2008 Mac Pro (OS X 10.10.5 Yosemite) to use the 7-port USB 3.0 hub and have faster transfer speeds than USB 2. Transfer speeds are definitely higher when using to clone my startup (SSD) to another SSD. Instead of ~3 hours using USB 2, this took less than 34 minutes. The device does NOT work when I boot into OS X 10.5.8

Installation requires opening up the case, and that's a good thing since it means I am reminded to vacuum out the dust that has accumulated as the fan has sucked a lot of dust into the tower.

The drawback is that I get a notification that the attached device has been disconnected improperly whenever my computer wakes from sleep - "Disk Not Ejected Properly". But that's not a problem since no writing is being done while it is asleep..

title: Heavy but good replacement for the original transformer.
text:
It does the job that the original transformer stopped doing - powering our halloween fiber-optic lighted pumpkin.

To get the original plug to fit into this barrel outlet plug, I squeezed the 2 ends of the original together so they would maintain contact with the inner and outer metal parts of the new adapter plug.

I am not sure why these manufacturers use AC-to-AC transformers to power items with what could easily be a DC motor (to power the color-changing wheel) as well as the halogen lamps - which I replaced with LED lamps. AC-to-DC transformers are half as expensive.

This one is heavy, but it IS a 3-amp transformer instead of a 1-amp.

title: QC assembly problem
text:
This functions as expected. However, it came out of the box with the enclosed SSD card / contacts misaligned - indicative of poor quality control at the assembly line.

I was able to plug in a SATA-to-USB cable and it does what it is designed to do. It formatted as expected, and I cloned my SSD so it can be used to boot my computer.

title: Nice men's purse
text:
This can hold things that I don't want to put in my pockets. It's almost too nice in appearance (more suitable for a woman).

However, the zippered pocket on the back side away from the flap is not deep enough for my cellphone.
The front pocket under the flap has an open top with 2 zippers on the sides. The problem is that with the zippers all the way down it still is not easy to reach into the pocket. This is the pocket that has 3 slots for credit cards.

The main zippered compartment is full-length and full-width, so it can accommodate most everything I would want to carry.

It would be nice to have a couple of narrow pockets for a penlight and a pen.

title: Very good fitting case
text: This case is a little longer than my WD Passport Ultra 2 TB hard drive so that I also can keep the USB 3.0 cable in the mesh pocket and at least a couple of my USB flash drives in the case. It has one zipper, not two, and this makes it easier to open and close. The size is also large enough to hold my Inateck 2.5-inch HDD enclosure and its USB 3.0 cable.

title: It charges 18650 batteries
text: Good for recharging the 18650 batteries, but there is barely enough room to charge two 26650 batteries side-by-side.

title: received with wider and longer and thicker post
text:
This will work ... after I used a knife to cut down the rectangular piece / post that fits in the slot on the dash cam. Before I trimmed it, it would not go into the slot.
Trimmed off the width and could insert it into the dash cam slot but not all the way into the slot.
Trimmed some more and could get it all the way down into the slot but unable to slide it sideways to make sure it would stay in the slot.
Trimmed some more to make the post thinner and finally able to slide it into the slot of the dash cam.

title: good solution
text: Someone complained that he could charge batteries only in pairs, but that is not a problem since I use batteries in sets of four for my Mr Beams MB726 Battery Powered Motion Sensing LED Nightlights. This allows me to charge 2 sets / 8 batteries at the same time.

title: insufficient to charge
text: Using a volt-ampere device to measure how the iPhone 4 was charging, it was found that the voltage was 5 volts but the current was only 0.25-0.29 ampere, insufficient to charge the iPhone unless it were to be turned off - and that is not practical. Other brands / types (Aduro and iXCC) of charging cable allowed the iPhone to draw close to 1 ampere from the same charger. The other brands have thicker insulation which is greater protection of the wire inside.

title: Tiny video camera with Wi-Fi and GPS.
text:
This is an abbreviated review, and it's main purpose is to prevent anyone from expecting this to be able to record more than 2 hours of 1080p - HD video by using any higher capacity card other than the SDHC cards. When I inserted my 64GB SDXC, it acted as though I had started recording but had a flashing message on the display. I thought maybe I would have to format the card, but that didn't solve anything.

I switched to a 32GB SDHC. It recorded with no problem. I removed the card, inserted it into a SDHC adapter, and looked at the video. No problems.

The charging of its battery cannot be done while the camera is in the waterproof housing.

I'll update my review after I play with it some more.

title: It DOES NOT work reliably.
text:
UPDATE 7/13/2017: This dash cam fell off the mount yesterday. I examined it and found the plastic on the top had cracked. This is the ORIGINAL dash cam which still functions well. I am not using the more recent dash cam that Amcrest refused to update (see below for the 4/18/2017 update). Too bad it could not have been manufactured with a metal top or outer casing that would stand up to removing and replacing and repositioning.

The most recent comments (UPDATES) apply to the more recently bought WICKEDHD dash cam that carries the name AMCREST on the box.

UPDATE 4/18/2017 - When I emailed AMCREST about the problems with the camera, I was told on April 11 "Thank you for contacting Amcrest Support, my name is Kirby and I'm the Product Support Specialist here and I will do my best to assist you with any issues or questions you may be having.

We are currently working on an updated for this device. I am very sorry for the inconvenience. I will put your ticket on hold so that I can do a follow up."

Today, 4/18/2017, however, I received this from the same AMCREST person.
"Unfortunately, we no longer service this product. It has been discontinued. I am very sorry for the inconvenience."

So they waited until the 30-day return limit passed before telling me the product is discontinued. Now I am stuck with a dash cam that has to have the date set every time it is powered.

Because of this treatment / experience, I will not be buying any more AMCREST products.

UPDATE 4/9/2017 - Bought another camera, expected it to function as the first one.
HOWEVER, several problems have reared their ugly heads.
1. The date resets to 01/01/2014 whenever it is turned OFF.
2. Recording does not start when the ignition is turned on and power is supplied to the camera. The green light on the plug-in to the DC outlet is ON but the camera will not turn on.
3. Recording of video clips appear to be in one folder; they are not in folders based on the date as they were on previous cameras.

Comments below apply to the older version(s) of the WICKED HD dash cam. I gave those 4 STARS.

UPDATE 11/1/2015 - No problems except for a few stray spots that are on the sensor or the inner lens. A couple of times one 3-minute video was skipped as the recording went from one folder to another on the same uninterrupted trip. The original micro-SD card has remained in the dash cam all these months.
The camera setting is for 1080p video so that license tags in front of me and gas prices and other signs on the sides of the road will be discernible when viewed on my computer. If my vehicle is stopped for a light, the zoom produces images that are clear enough but it is obvious they are pixelated.

UPDATE 3/9/2015 - The company sent me a replacement that arrived today. Unfortunately, the box contains no rearview mirror mount for the dash cam. That will cost me another $10 to order separately.
The good news is that the micro-SD card stayed in - finally - when I inserted it into the memory card slot. That needs to be redesigned such that the mechanism doesn't eject the card as easily as it does. The cut-out doesn't match the lip on the SD card - it's on the opposite side of where it logically should be. The 'manual' simply says the micro SD card should be inserted as in the [non-existant] "image below; press it until you hear a click." No image and no click. The micro SD card doesn't stay in until just the right position is achieved.

After I have used it, I will post any comments as to the images produced. Hopefully the videos won't have the smears / streaks / spots that the first dash cam had.

UPDATE 3/3/2015 - The company sent me Return Authorization, and I spent $14 (about 25% of the cost of the dash cam - so much for Prime membership) to return the dash cam plus all attachments to them for a replacement. Attaching that mount to the rear-view mirror was not easy, so I don't look forward to having to reattach it. However, I really hope the replacement will come quickly, have a functioning micro SD card slot and not have a defective lens or sensor (streaks).

UPDATE 3/1/2015 - Through Amazon I have requested a replacement dash cam since I am unable to insert a micro SD card fully into the slot, making the dash cam unusable. The Amazon description states that this dash cam has a one-year warranty.

Original review follows- from October 23, 2014, after I had it for about 2 weeks.
This works. However, the instructions only explain what options are available via the cam's menus. They do not explain HOW to use it.

The microSD - NOT mini-SD as others have mentioned - card will not stay in the camera by pushing it with my finger. I have to use a hard object. That's no longer a problem since I discovered how to transfer images to my computer - the instructions are not there in the booklet. (Plug in the USB cable that connects the dash cam to the computer, the dash cam turns on, and press the REC button - Image Capture utility pops up on my Mac computer.)

When I used the default settings - 720 and 60 fps - and I initially set it on my GPS platform on my dash, I got video that was upside down - but clear. Now I have it attached to the rearview mirror stem.

Unfortunately, the zoom is digital, not optical, resulting in extremely pixelated video. I was unable to read license tags or other details along the road (e.g., gas station prices).

The attachment to the mirror requires two hands and standing on my head to see where the cam attaches to the mount. And then, I have to be able to attach it without having the power cable disconnect. Also, I have to double check to ensure it is aimed properly.

It goes without saying that the cam has to be removed and hidden away when parking in a public place.

The fact that it comes on when the vehicle starts is nice. I have remote start, but the cam doesn't turn on until I unlock the door and insert the key and turn the ignition switch to its running position.

Considering the price, it is a good buy (especially compared to the GoPro cams). I may use it whenever I drive somewhere, but I may have to use 1080 resolution to read license tags of those idiots on the road who don't know how to drive.

UPDATE: Today (October 28, 2014) I used 1080p resolution. Now I was able to read the license tags of the vehicles that were not too far in front of me. Also, I was able to read signs on the sides of the road. The size of each 3-minute clip is about 290 MB. That's room for about 110 clips, each of which is 3 minutes long. Using longer clips is not advisable since each clip would be a large file. I see NO gap between one clip and the next.

One problem: Each and every video has a 'smear' which is either on the inside of the lens or on the sensor. Around the smear are several small spots. All of this is in the upper right, 3/10 of the way down and 3/10 of the way in from the right side. (I made a JPEG of an image divided into a 10x10 grid. The smear is in the 3rd segment from the top and 3rd from the right.) It is not enough for me to send it back, but it does tell us about the company's quality control.

title: Replaced the dead AC transformer in our fiber optic pumpkin
text:
It is an AC transformer which is required to operate our fiber optic pumpkin with an AC motor that rotates a color wheel to produce a variety of color combination through the optical fibers. The original transformer required a 2-prong plug, so the 2 prongs were bent so that they would contact both contacts on the barrel plug that is attached to the AC transformer. I had several 1-amp DC transformers, but the motor for the color wheel would not turn without alternating current. Go figure! And most transformers are DC. The price was probably as much (or more than) the cost of the original pumpkin, but at least my wife is happy.

UPDATE: Transformer ordered 10/18/2013. As of 10/13/2014 the transformer is DEAD. It gets hot and produces ZERO voltage. It lasted one season, NOT one year. 5-star review is now down to 1 star.

title: fast
text:
UPDATE (4/23/2017): Reviewing some other items and ran across this. The SSD is still being used in my Mac Pro as my boot drive. That is over 4 years, and it is still behaving as it was intended in my 9-year-old Mac Pro. Since I cannot update the OS further, I will probably replace this Mac Pro with the new version, once it is on the market.

For a bit over a month I have had this as my main drive in my Mac Pro. It's where my apps and documents folders are located. I had cloned my 1 TB HDD that was my startup drive in my Mac Pro after moving items that didn't have to be on a startup disk. This SSD along with Mountain Lion makes everything faster. Safari has not "quit unexpectedly" since the upgrade. Hopefully it will still be going strong a year or more down the road.

NOTE: To install this SSD in my computer, I had to buy a separate adapter that this SSD is screwed into, and then that is attached to the carrier and slid into the bay. Same thing is necessary on most computers, a carrier is required.

The only unusual thing I have been seeing is a note that "Backup destination is a local destination, but we found an embedded server URL." when I have my Time Machine do its hourly back-ups.

title: Nice little light
text:
Good illumination for a replacement night light.

These need just a bit more quality checking since the silicone gasket is slightly too long for the channel and causes difficulty closing the battery cover completely. Otherwise they are fine.

The light can be attached using sticky velcro tape or with screws. The unit lifts out and away from the part that attaches to the wall for replacing the batteries.

These lights require 4 AA batteries each. Another brighter light sold at Amazon with 10 LEDs requires only 3 AA batteries. We will have to see if this increases the life of the light with 4 batteries.

title: Shoe polish?
text:
This case arrived in the specified time in a box that had not been damaged by the carrier as other orders have.

The main problem I have with this case is the odor of shoe polish, so I am leaving it out to air and for the odor to dissipate before I put the new iPad in the case. I wonder, however, whether the color will rub off on my iPad or on anything else that comes into contact with the case. If it does, I'll update this review.

The sleep / wake magnet works the way it is supposed to work, so that part is correct.

title: Too small
text:
This is replacing a Microsoft model (1388) that has stopped functioning.

My MacBook Pro is 15.4 inches diagonally. However, this cooling pad is still too narrow to reach the sides of my MBP. The non-slip feet on my MBP do not contact the surface of the cooling pad, so I will need to apply some silicone or rubber to prevent the MBP from sliding off the cooling pad.

On the back end of the cooling pad are four USB ports, one mini-USB port for the cable to connect with the MBP AND one other port / jack that looks as though a separate AC power adapter could be plugged into the port. HOWEVER, this came with NO instructions, and the port has no indication of what its purpose may be. If one wanted to leave it in one place as a dock with other devices attached to it with the USB ports, it might be helpful to have a separate AC adapter.

The cooling pad should be used with nothing under it - not on a bed, for instance.

Make sure you insert the SD card while the tablet is off. It slides in pretty easily and if it doesn’t, it might need to be flipped over Once the card is installed, go to settings then storage. There is where you should see your SD Card storage. If you don’t see it, the card itself may not have been installed correctly. You can then move all of your apps to the SD card freeing up space. You can also set your options to automatically download movies, apps, music, videos onto the card. There is even an option to erase the entire card as well as stop all SD functions so you can safely remove the card. Totally worth the $12!!!

title: Probably the best value WiFi 6 whole house mesh system
text:

Cons: seamless mesh feature doesn't work that great. Especially when wifi calling and I'm walking around the house as the only way to trigger switching to the better point is to disconnect and reconnect Wi-Fi which drops the call. The support and ui for seamless mesh could be better. I would like it if you could select which exact access point you want for a device and then disable mesh, specifically for smart devices that don't move but will randomly switch points. For what its worth i believe most mesh systems experience the same cons.

title: Keeps laptop from throtteling
text:
Used this with a slim travel laptop to keep it from thermo-throttling during rendering.

Slim travel laptops aren't designed to run at full speed for very long. This leads to throtteling where a top end cpu (i7, etc) can actually result in worse performance than the budget option (i3) in the same case when redering. I packed this along with two of the lightest 120mm fans that I could find in my box of fans. I brought nothing else. On location I proped up the laptop using whatever was at hand and was presently suprised thay this actually worked in cooling the X1 Carbon enough to keep it from throttling. Of doing the same, I recommended looking for slim profile fans.

The only problem might be the extra weight and bulk that this adds, but that's inherent with any grip added on. This is the only reasonable solution to the Nikon battery grip scam for more FPS (I don't think there is any technical limitation for the higher burst rate).

title: Probably the best and last Nikon DSLR
text:
I bought mine from BH, rather than here, but the same viewpoint still applies. I have put over 50,000 on the shutter so far. This might be the most perfect full frame DSLR Nikon made. Normally you had to choose fast or high resolution, but this is both. Some personal observations:

1) This isn't light, but the grip is perfect. I can handhold this for longer than a smaller and lighter mirrorless camera just do to the big grip. The ergonomics are just about perfect. Whatever improvements needed are minor.
2) To get the higher FPS you need to buy a grip and a EN-EL18 battery. This is of course a money making scam and had nothing to do with the power ability of the internal battery. I bought a 3rd party grip (Vello) and 3rd party battery (wasabi) to enable this. This add weight and bulk of course.
3) I wish the buffer was bigger. A Raw+jpeg burst is potentially writing a gigabyte worth of data per burst
4) If you want speed for bursts, the v90 SD cards seem like the best deal for speed to me. I can't tell too much of a difference between say the v90 sony and the v90 prograde while shooting and from running benchmarks, though on paper the sony is supposed to be faster. I haven't tested XQD to see how they compare, but to some the extra theoretical 100mb/s write speed might be worth it.
5) With the latest firmware update the use of cfexpress cards was enabled. I bought two. From my testing the cfexpress cards are slower than v90 SD cards, so using cfexpress is a waste of money with this camera (unless the price of cfexpress goes down considerably).
6) I found the 4k quality decent and the rear screen to be good enough to focus manually with (no focus peaking), better even than my mirrorless camera with focus peaking. But I bought a mirrorless camera because I got tired of putting on and off the microphone+amps+wires every time I wanted to switch. I have since switched to using autofocus on the mirrorless camera for video and haven't used video on this camera since.

The only issue here is that Nikon and Canon has abandoned DSLR development, even though there is no technical limitation in implementing the features found in current mirrorless cameras in DSLR (except for the viewfinder). The only thing I would want from a hypothetical D860 is a much bigger buffer and IBIS.
