title: The most dense heatsink you can get before Noctua NH-D15
text:
I have a Noctua NH-D15 in another case that I use as a workstation. When I was building a Ryzen x570 with a 3700x system I wanted to install something that was more manageable and was more sturdy (I had to ship the end result).

Heat and noise

I was concerned that the end result might be louder, but it ended up working rather well. I settled on a slightly higher idle temperature of 45-50c for the CPU to keep the fans from revving up and down. In the end the issues I had with my build were not with the CPU but rather with the south bridge of the x570 instead.

Clearance

I had no issue with clearance with the board and ram.

Sturdiness

There was no damage to the heat sink. I shipped with fedex in a double box in a fractal define C case.

title: Perfect, almost, if you do not want a window case
text:
This is a nice heavy case that I settled for when I was looking for a windowless case. My criteria was that it had to be quiet, and not have a window yet fit an ATX board. But not being cheap. I wanted a CD-Rom slot as well, but you can't have everything and I settled on an external.

Cable routing

The cable routing was perfect in my configuration. This was paired with an MSI Edge x570 board (I do not recommend this one, go for a more expensive board or stick with x470) and the fan headers being on the bottom were a perfect fit. Of course, I used cable extenders to achieve this.

Noise and heat

It took some time to figure out the fan speed profile for the case. There was no rattle but I had to use an anemometer to figure this out. I only used one fan for the exhaust and three for the intake - with additional filter material. I had to settle for a slightly higher idle temperature as a compromise to get rid of the sound of rev up/down of fans. The only issue is the hot south bridge, but that is a limitation of the x570 rather than the case.

Space

I configured the case with an NVME and two 3.5 hard drives. The bottom half of the bottom fan provides cooling for these hard drives (after you remove the plate in the way). I installed four fans.

title: Runs as expected
text:
Used this for an MSI AMD x570 Edge motherboard. It works well with XMP enabled. Been running them for 6 months now.

I prefer the heatsinks on these over the tall ones for clearance issues - I am only using two so the extra heatsink height is not needed. I was concered with trying to stay at 1.2V as I assumes running higher voltage 1.35v would make these run hot. Not the case. The ram is cool to the touch, unlike the x570 southbridge.

Initially the motherboard would not boot with both sticks at all. I removed one and it booted fine. I think after an update I put the second stick in, and it came up fine with no issues after enabling XMP. Could have been the update or bad contact.

title: It is fast, not that I can tell
text:
I use this as the main OS disk in my build. It is faster than the SATA III stuff. It is hard for me to perceive the difference since we are talking about seconds, even if the difference is in several magnitudes. I bought this over the other SSD mainly due to longer life that comes from being MLC, rather than speed.

My drive idles at 45C and on writes the temperature goes up. I have installed an NVMe heatsink on it, the kind that wraps around (versus the kind that just glues to the top). This buys more time before thermal throttling hit due to temperature.

One thing to keep in mind is that the rated speeds that are posted on most gaming SSDs (at least with Samsung) are for burst writes. That speed drops significantly for sustained writes. Meaning large file copy operations will show slower overall speeds. You would need to buy Enterprise rated SSDs at x4 to x10 the price if that is what you need. With game loads you would want burst speeds anyway. The other problem with NVMe is that by being smaller it reduces how much heat they can dissipate, which also limits large file copy operations. It is an inherent limitation.

title: Another Platinum PSU for me
text:
Compering to my other Platinum PSU, there are no faults that I can find with this unit. I have this installed in a Fractal Design Define C case on the bottom. I do not hear any noticeable noise from this unit.

I only buy Platinum PSU for two reasons. First reason is due to better power efficiency that comes from better components and system power swings. The other reason, and maybe even the main reason, is my expectation that Platinum rated PSU units built with better components will live longer and reduce the risk of catastrophic PSU failure.

The only trick is not loosing those extra cables that I did not use, thankfully the unit comes with a bag.

title: Works as intended
text:
Used this to output composite to a rear projection Hitachi HDTV through HDMI conversion from a laptop. Video and sound works.

In order to make it work I had to fiddle with one cable because I was initially missing a color. On my laptop I also had to pinch my screen in software to get it to fit on the TV. Tested this with two diffrent laptops. This is mostly likely the TVs fault. For sound I had to select the output source on one laptop to get it to play through the TV instead of the laptop speakers. TV oversampling of HD in early TVs is common and is probably not the coverter.

The coverter is always outputting a signal even without an input. This is useful for troubleshooting, but is something to be aware of when turning things off.

Being a rear projection TV there are tradeoffs with picture quality inherent in its design. But since it gets used a week a year at best, it is not frequent enough to warrant replacement or risk of hernia.

title: Does the job, low noise
text: Use these as intake fans. Three of them. Fairly low noise even with three. I used the silicon feet that came with them by rubbing some soap before installation. I also used the Y-splinters to connect them to a single fan header. My CPU is NF-A15 and my exhaust is Noctua NF-A12x25

title: Expensive, impressive performance
text:
This puts out an impressive amount of air for the noise it makes. I used this fan by itself as an exhaust with three NF-F12 on the intake side.

Something to be aware of. On maximum I can hear it. This could be due to the air blowing through a fan shroud of the case itself (I would have to cut the case to remove it). Ironically the noise from the NF-A15 is more noticeable at higher RPM than this fan.

title: Expensive, but perfect under ~3500rpm
text: Installed this on a raid card as a makeshift cooler. I can't hear it below 3500rpm in my case. Expensive, but nothing else is on the market in this segment which comes close which pushes good amounts of air for little noise.

title: Good use as a PC monitor
text:
I use this as a computer monitor for my photo workstation. I use it to preview images in a catalog. At the distance used there is light fall off in the corners, so if you have the funds a curved monitor might work better for the same purpose. For my needs it is not perfect but good enough for a professional adobe display. According to my calibrator this does Adobe 87%. The IPS display it replaced was slightly higher % wise but had an annoying red color cast that I could not calibrate out.

Out of the box I got 4:2:0, I needed to get an NVIDIA 10 series card to do full 4:4:4. This did nothing for color space but did remove annoying purple "frigging" around text. You NEED a card that can do HDMI 1.4 out in order to use this as a computer monitor at 4K. In which case a NVIDIA 10 Series or AMD equivalent.

As a TV it is perfect. The low end reach of the speakers was surprising, I was going to get pc speakers but the one built in are good enough. The included apps work fine.

My only issue is the standby nag screen. If you have the TV on and turn the computer off, the TV might go in to "No signal" screen which does not seem to go away. I had the input set to PC, it should know to turn itself off. You need the remote to change the sound and turn the monitor on and off.

title: The only option for PWM fan control modification
text:
This is the only PWM controller I could find that works. It works very well. You can outright control a PWM fan straight from a power supply or by modifying an existing PWM fan signal from the motherboard. This is designed to be able to drive multiple fans daisy-chained together by having the power option be applied after the signal is modified.

I have tried to find PWM fan controllers, but most controllers that I came across are voltage based which does not work well for granular low speed control. This works well for that. The anti-stall feature did not work for me, but it is not a concern for me.

title: Cost effective USB 3.0 adapter, but not for everyone
text:
This does not come with a power supply. I bought this, thought not from Amazon, specifically because I had a number of power supplies already and was looking for a cheap USB 3.0 adapter for checking hard drives. My unit is labeled stw-25u018, on Windows 7 no drivers are required. I tested this against another USB 3.0 enclosure I had with the same hard drives and the benchmarks are more or less the same.

When transferring a large amounts of files I had this unit drop down to 7mb/s after 30 minutes. I was using a program with verification functions and I'm not sure what to make of this since it's possible this could be normal.

The downside of this unit is the really short cable that limits your options of where you can place this unit. An adapter that has a detachable USB 3.0 cable would be a better choice. If the listing does not explicitly say that a power supply is included, assume it's not included.

title: Cost effective USB 3.0 adapter, but not for everyone
text:
This does not come with a power supply. I bought this, thought not from Amazon, specifically because I had a number of power supplies already and was looking for a cheap USB 3.0 adapter for checking hard drives. My unit is labeled stw-25u018, on Windows 7 no drivers are required. I tested this against another USB 3.0 enclosure I had with the same hard drives and the benchmarks are more or less the same.

When transferring a large amounts of files I had this unit drop down to 7mb/s after 30 minutes. I was using a program with verification functions and I'm not sure what to make of this since it's possible this could be normal.

The downside of this unit, besides the lack of power supply, is the really short cable that limits your options of where you can place this unit. An adapter that has a detachable USB 3.0 cable would be a better choice.

title: Never had any issues
text:
I bought these back in the day for their supposed shelf life rather than their printable ability. For burning these have worked well, and I did not have any issues with them.

Of course, I wouldn't buy them again without rereading reviews as to the current state of media since manufactures do tend to change their suppliers so what was good a few years ago might turn out to be unacceptable.

Otherwise as far as archival GB/$ value is concerned you'd be better off getting an external hard drive. The price difference can be five times in favor of an external hard drive. Though granted you'd be better of buying two for safety sake.

title: Suspiciously low CFM flow
text: It's quite, I can barely hear it at all. The problem is that I can also barely feel any air flow from this fan. I tried to look up the published CFM for this fan but looking at the box and online there is no such spec published anywhere that I could find. Beware.

title: Still going strong
text:
I purchased this to use for an in car dash cam. In this purpose it has served well for several years, still going strong. I have not had any issues with this card.

I have purchased many Transcend memory cards over the years for various applications and have not had any fail so far.

title: Worked
text:
Used this to extend the connection between my USB 3.0 Card and my USB 3.0 card reader. I have a full size ATX case and the cable on the card reader was short by one inch. This cable has a snug fit, but not too snug. Bumping in to it hard enough will move it out of position, so it's best to Velcro it to something. The color match is right on.

At first the card reader didn't work and I thought something was wrong with my card reader or cable. Later realized that I did not plug in the card reader in to power.

title: Works with Atom D525
text:
Installed this in to an Atom Based all-in-one PC using the WiFi slot. The PC has Atom D525, which is pretty useless by most counts. But after installing the card (I had to remove one of the screws to secure it to the motherboard) and downloading software from Broadcom "Crystal HD" I see no issues playing youtube content. The PC as a whole is still quite slow, but at least video play back is not an issue. I opened up the computer after playing a few videos to see how hot the chip got and it was only warm (could have been other components).

This has given new use to an otherwise obsolete computer.

title: My most used lens at some point
text: This was my most used lens at the time. I had no issues with sharpness from F2 onward. I used the inbuilt hood all the time, though I never felt like it was essential since I didn't have flare issues. Focus speed was satisfactory even though it's screw. Bokeh is good, from what I saw better than the 1.4 version. I especially liked to use the in-body IS/AS at night.

title: Great at the time
text: I used this back in college when I was working as a student photographer with good results. The sharpness was good enough through out, even at the long end. The best part was the price. My copy has some green CA. The focus speed was slow and I had constant hunting issues. Often time I'd switch to manual focus instead, especially when trying sport-like shots. Taking sports shots with this lens is frustrating though, a part of me wanted to drill a hole in this thing to put in DIY focus limiter. This is the primary limitation. The weight of this lens can be good for stability, but a downside for travelling. After I finished college I have not used this lens much. For sport use I suspect any modern zoom is better.

title: Sharp, but terrible flare control
text: I bought mine used a long time ago. At the time it was one of the sharpest lenses I had. It wasn't too contrasty but it was sharp. It has a nice solid feel to it. It was also inexpensive. But it is also has the worst flare control of all of the lenses I had. Even small pin point light sources would flare in high contrast situations. The other issue I had with it was the 0.5m minimum focusing distance. Even with those limitations I had many good pictures with it.

title: Great in its day.
text:
I loved this lens on film and on APS-C since it provided an inexpensive zoom before quality APS-C only lenses became available. The downside of this lens is that it's huge, physically, and sometimes when backing away in to corner I found that the physical size of the lens was the limiting factor. While not heavy, the size of the lens when packing can be an issue. Looking at MTF charts this lenses has poor corners, but I never noticed this on film or on APS-C which cuts those of. I do not think this is a lens for high resolution full frame cameras though do to the corners, but not bad other wise for $200 as a starter lens for APS-C or film.

I never had serious flare issues with this lens, or at least not to the point where the contrast of the image was compromised.

title: Several years of use, no issues
text: Have mine for several years now, still works perfectly. The fans do not make much noise and still going strong. Right now it seems about 5% faster than the GTX 960 and about 30% slower than the GTX 970. Though I feel no urge to upgrade since most of the stuff I'm running now is still getting good FPS.

title: Shiny
text:
I have the glossy black version. This is a very attractive minimalistic case. It comes with stand-offs for SSDs. While I didn't realize it at first there are slot for regular hard drives as well on the bottom. it's harder to get to them, but I like how they are out of the way. The case has been designed with minimizing visual clutter so most cabling is hidden away. Of course there is no slot for a DVD drive, but was not an issue for me with using flash disk. The fan on top is 120mm but can support 140mm, but I have not replaced it since it seems adequate. There is filtration built in the fan shrouds on mine.

I'm actually not a fan of window case designs do to the mess that is usually contained inside, but this design is done very well.

title: Trusted go to thermal paste
text:
Have been using Arctic Silver for more than a decade now. I had a 9 gram one that lasted for 7 years, used for various builds and experiments. I was debating getting MX-4 but the price for this is a better deal and lasts longer. Though I suspect after many years the paste does dry up just a bit.

I also use this with Arctic Alumina Thermal Adhesive by mixing it together for more semi-permanent applications where there is no clip to keep heat sinks in place.

title: Perfect match with the 18-55mm kit lens
text:
I got this lens to go along with my [[ASIN:B000ZMCILW Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras]] kit lens. They are a perfect match for travel. This lens is just a tiny bit bigger in my camera bag, but feel about comparable side by side. Even better they take the same filter size, so moving lens caps between the two is a breeze. I didn't expect much from this lens, but sharpness and focus speed is good.

The combination of this lens with the 18-55mm is a much more cost effective approach then getting the [[ASIN:B002JCSV8A Nikon 18-200mm f/3.5-5.6G AF-S ED VR II Nikkor Telephoto Zoom Lens for Nikon DX-Format Digital SLR Cameras]] for the same image quality. But I will admit that not having to change lenses is more convenient. Most of the time the 55-200mm is not the issue, but rather the 18-55mm.

There is also a newer version of this lens [[ASIN:B00RUBK53Y Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-200MM f/4-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction II Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras]] but all it adds is a more compact size, but to begin with the lens is already light and compact. I recommend saving your money and getting this instead. It's also common on the used market.

There is also the [[ASIN:B003ZSHNCC Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 55-300mm f/4.5-5.6G ED Vibration Reduction Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras]] which has more reach, while being larger, heavier and more expensive. In my opinion the compactness, lightness and value of this lens win out. I'd say you'd better of upgrading to the 18-55mm first.

title: Nice kit lens
text:
This is a nice kit lens, better than what canon has (when compering kit lenses at the same prices). The Vibration Reduction (Image stabilization) is a nice bonus. The close focusing distance is acceptable, the focus speed is good. It's small and packs light. The downside is that sharpness tends to fall off when at 55mm, but you'd have to be looking for it to find it. I paired this with the [[ASIN:B000O161X0 Nikon 55-200mm f/4-5.6G ED IF AF-S DX VR [Vibration Reduction] Nikkor Zoom Lens]] for travel which is an even better deal.

There are newer version of this lens that's even smaller [[ASIN:B00HQ4W4PC Nikon AF-S DX NIKKOR 18-55mm f/3.5-5.6G Vibration Reduction II Zoom Lens with Auto Focus for Nikon DSLR Cameras]] but there is no point of getting it in my opinion. The only improvement is the compactness, but this lens is already small and light. You're better off saving your money. These lenses are very common on the used market and can be had quite cheaply.

Lastly if one can afford it for travel the [[ASIN:B002JCSV8A Nikon 18-200mm f/3.5-5.6G AF-S ED VR II Nikkor Telephoto Zoom Lens for Nikon DX-Format Digital SLR Cameras]] is just more convenient since it saves time in changing lenses. But the optical quality "should" be about the same, so the main benefit is convenience.

title: It's great for the price
text:
It's sharp, compact and inexpensive. It's great for the price.

This is a minor point for most, but I wish it had a real focus ring. On my other older lenses when shooting things far away, like from a moving car, I liked to set the lens on infinity. This does not work with this lens the same way. At one point I thought I had infinity focus by focusing at the sky, so I turned the switch to manual. This kept the lens at infinity. I then took the lens off, took some pictures with another lens, and then put the lens back on. If this was an older lens with a real focus ring the focus distance would have remained the same. But on this lens the focus distance resets. Having the lens on the manual focus setting does not hold focus when the lens is removed. Just something to be aware off.

title: Compact, but blocks other outlet
text:
This is a neat compact surge protector, which I have also used as for travel. Being a direct plug in cuts down on clutter.

The downside of this unit is the space it occupies on the outlet, blocking the other outlets.

title: Works well, slightly under sized battery
text:
I had my unit for about 5 years. When purchased new it worked well with my Active PFC power supply computers. The rating on this UPS is slightly higher than other comparable at the same battery size, meaning this does not have the same run time at all. That's ok, I didn't base my purchasing decision on that. But if you do, that means you might find that it will fail to keep your computer on after a few years as the battery ages. The battery in my unit is shot after 5 years, but that's true of any UPS battery.

The LCD screen was useful at first in seeing how much power was being used, I rather have it than not. I never used automatic shut down features of any UPS. The other benefit of having a UPS is that it filters the power going in to your electronics.

title: A good 80-300mm lens, poor at 400mm
text:
I have this in canon mount. Tokina metal construction inspires confidence. This lens feels solid. Considering its range it's not very big and the AF performance is satisfactory on APS-C. The downside of this lens is that past 300mm there is a significant loss of sharpness. At 400mm below F11 I find results are just not acceptable, even for web viewing. At F11 it's just ok, and you'd probably want to stop down to F16.

On the other hand the lens is a great value on the used market. I would not recommend buying it new.

title: Sharp, cheap, small
text:
EDIT: Some time after I wrote this I have rechecked the data on DxO and it seems that the 50mm 1.8 STM and the new Canon IS 2.8 primes have higher resolution on the 5DS than this lens. It's perplexing how the 50mm 1.8 STM is sharper, when the older II which has the same formula does not do as well.

This is the sharpest lens in the 40-50 range under $900. It's sharper than the Canon 50mm 1.8, 1.4, 1.2L, 2.5 macro and the Tamron 45mm F1.8 Di VC USD (I can say this from looking at DxO mark sensor data for the 5DS for all of these lenses). This is not too surprising given that it starts at 2.8. The only other lens that's sharper is the Sigma 50 ART lens. I originally thought that the Canon 50mm 2.5 macro might have the edge, but looking at the MTF charts the 40 still comes on top.

The compact size of this lens make this a no brainier when packing. I use this on an APS-C camera and there is some light fall off if you look closely enough. But I shoot RAW and let Adobe Lightroom correct vignetting at 50% setting. Of course the downside is that at 2.8 it doesn't gather as much light as the other primes and produce as shallow of a DOF.

title: Good, though keep sample variation in mind
text:
This is a good lens for the price, better than what OEM has at 14mm. There are two problems though.

The canon version does not have an AF confirm chip. With a 14mm you "shouldn't" need a confirmation chip since you can focus using hyper-focal distance scale there is a way around this. Instead of getting the Canon mount version for Canon mount you can get the Nikon version and get a Nikon-Canon adapter with an AF confirm chip. This will probably add $50 to the final price though.

The second problem is that with a lens this cheap there is "sample variation." Meaning no two lenses will be exactly the same. So if you get a lens that's not sharp, exchange it.

title: Had mine since 2000
text:
Had these since 2000. The ear pads flaked off completely, but I don't care. Nothing else broke. Still can't beat these. I bent the plug a little by stepping on it, but it still works. The carrying pouch is pretty useful, don't lose it.

I still don't understand what the deal with beats headphones are.

title: Durable, nice for $20. Saved me money.
text:
This is a good pair of inexpensive headphones. They are durable. I have bought both the black and white models - just not for myself. I prefer the white ones since they are easier to find in clutter. These can not touch my SONY V6 headphones, not even close. Of course, I don't want anyone to touch my SONY V6 headphones so these fill that gap nicely. After more than two years of use I was surprised that these did not fall apart. These are not that comfortable but that's not the point, these are nice for being $20. In this same price range I paid more than this for ear bud headphones, all of which fell apart. Most of my ear-bud headphones suffered the same fate of having their cables break on the inside.

it's not fare to compare these to more expensive headphones. If you are buying these for yourself and can afford it, of course get better ones.

title: Brand reliability, useful software
text:
I have this in my gaming PC, though I didn't buy this on Amazon. I have several Samsung drives, they are the only brand of SSD's that I buy now for two reasons. Proven reliability, and Samsung Magician Software.

Speed wise any SSD is good. I also own a Crucial M500 that I installed in my Linux laptop with SATA I, which is reported to be much slower but in practice proved to be x10 faster than the original laptop hard drive. For all of my other computers what makes the Samsung nice is the software. With Samsung Magician Software I can adjust over provisioning and see if any updates are needed. It also gives you a lists (profiles) of some items that you might need to adjust in your OS to make the SSD run optimally. It will also show you the health status, how many writes have been made and it can do a speed benchmark (though this can be done by other free software too). Samsung also provides migration software, but I never used that since I prefer to install from scratch.

Of course the brand reliability is probably the most important. I wouldn't touch OCZ drives for example, even if they were free.

title: Installed 16GB in Lenovo X220, runs at 1333
text: Bought two 8GB sticks instead of the 16GB kit as it proved to be cheaper. Installed in Lenovo X220 with no issues. The reported speed is 1333 though. This is not an issue for me, but something to be aware of. Nice way to give more life to an older laptop.

title: Wish they were cheaper so I could buy more
text:
I have a few of these which my UPS units connect to, to which I connect computers and even an HDTV (mostly for power filtration). When installed it sags a little and usually blocks the other outlet. The unit has two outlets, but only has one plug. But installed on the bottom of a two outlet panel, it will not block the top outlet. These units have a nice solid feel to them. I only wish I had more of them.

The unit hangs without issue in outlets that have the ground on the bottom, but in a commercial setting with the ground on top the unit will hang out from the wall in a noticeable way. But even given that I have not seen these fall out though. There is a kit supplied with this to mount it to the wall outlet, but I have not used it.

title: Works, but best get a bigger card for not much more
text: I have been using Transcend cards for many years, no issues with any of them. Of course you're best of getting the largest card your camera supports.

title: Works, cheap
text:
This works well for what I needed it for. It's aluminium and the threads could be stronger (steel isn't as brittle), but I have not damaged mine during use. Paint will come off easily if scratched, but I do not consider that important. I also have the [[ASIN:B001G445Q4 Fotodiox 7 Step Up Ring Filter Adapter Set, Anodized Aluminum, 49-52mm, 52-55mm, 55-58mm, 58-62mm, 62-67mm, 67-72mm, 72-77mm]] set which is much more cost effect and wish this came with it.

This was used with one of my LTM lenses.

title: Excellent, but expensive
text:
I bought this model used, which replaced my previous 720p dash cam. The video quality is a huge step up, so is the construction. The older dash cam was made of a very cheap plastic which deformed in the car due to heat, the suction cup broke, and the power supply broke as well. This dash cam has fared much better. Though after a year or two of use the battery needs to be replaced.

There is a clone/copy of this model out there for $60 or more. The most obvious difference that I can see is that while the DOD model turns off its LCD after 5 minutes, the cheaper copies do not. This can be distracting. But they are a great value though even with that limitation.

title: Needed these quick
text:
I prefer this battery organizer box type over the rubber ones because these are available in transparent containers, which allowed you to see what you actually have. I have many boxes of these type, and I also have some that I ordered from China. This is sturdy and I have not had one break.

The good thing about Prime and Amazon is that I can order these and have them when I need them, like in the middle of a vacation when I realized that airline security requires that your batteries either be in their original packages or have their terminals protected. Not wanting to leave my rechargeables behind, I ordered these quick.

title: Needed Class 6 card for car dash cam, this works well
text: The primary use I have for a 32GB Class 6 card is for specific model Card DVR Dash cam that supposedly do not like Class 10 cards. For that purpose it works well and I have no issues. Unless you have a specific need for a under class 10 card in 32gb size, there is no reason to get this card.

title: Works, except when it drops the connection and refuses to reconnect
text: This works with my wireless G router and then my wireless N router. Except for one problem. Occasionally the wireless will drop and will not reconnect until I either 1) unplug and re-plug in the adapter 2) disable and re-enable the adapter (sometimes this doesn't work). This happens less than a handful of times a month. This pretty much necessitates for me to keep a monitor, keyboard and mouse connected to the said computer. I'm not sure what the issue is.

title: Good looking switch, with clear presentation
text: Attractive metal case with clearly visable indicator lights. Some other plastic models place cables in the rear and put the indicator lights up in front which only show you if there is traffic going through. The good thing about this is that the layout allows you to tell clearly what is active, and also what is the negotiated connection (100m vs 1g) which saves checking your computers for negotiation issues.

title: Works well, no issues
text: This simple card works for my HTPC use. The radio reception seems to be one bar lower than what I would expect (in contrast to another desktop in the house that came with a built in wireless card) but the reported throughput seems were it should be. I wonder how much the metal case of the computer itself interferes with the signal. There is a trick to antenna orientation, since the higher the db rating the more directional the antenna becomes. Since my router is below the computer, I oriented the antenna parallel with the floor. I didn't have any issue with disconnects or dropped connections after prolonged operation unlike my [[ASIN:B002SZEOLG TP-LINK TL-WN722N Wireless N150 High Gain USB Adapter, 150Mbps, 4dBi External Antenna, WPS Button, Support Windows XP/Vista/7/8]] adapter that I have on another computer which requires me to periodically disconnect or disable/enable to restore the connection.

title: Great for HTPC use
text:
This works even better than I anticipated for HTPC use. I would say a lot of thought went in to the design of this. The connection is easy, just plug in the usb receiver and off you go. No pairing needed. I had no interference issues with wireless that I could notice.

The F1 through F12 are accessed though the FN key like that of a laptop. Otherwise those buttons are HTPC specific playback buttons, and I found them very useful. They even out a left click button on the left side of the keyboard (yellow button) for when you need to hold down the left mouse button and scroll.

The only area of improvement I would wish for is that the F1-F12 keys were separate (in an addition to the HTPC buttons) and didn't require the FN key to activate. If the keyboard was backlit that would also help since when I'm watching TV I usually have the light off.

title: The only option for car CD players
text: I have been using these for years. These mostly get used for music for cars with cd players, that don't have an ipod plug.

title: Functionally no better than a cheap antenna
text:
This is a review of the 50 mile OUS00-0562 model. To summarize: It works. But it's no better than my cheap [[ASIN:B000HKGK8Y RCA Indoor FM and HDTV Antenna]] antenna that I was trying to replace, yet costing several times more.

With my cheap RCA "rabbit ears" antenna I was getting 18 channels, being 8 miles away from the transmitter. According to my digital-to-analog converter most TV signals were in the range of 75% to 30%. I was looking for a better antenna to improve the signal quality, so when I saw that the OUS00-0562 model was on sale I bought it. I didn't believe the 50 mile claim of this antenna since most antennas with this claim are large, more expensive and rather directional. But I figured that even if it was half that it had to be better than my RCA one. Whatever this antenna was directional of not was not specified, I assumed that it was not.

The OUS00-0562 model comes with an antenna with a 20 foot non-removable cord. This was disappointing, but I should have realized this when looking at the product pictures. Having so much cable slack is a waste when it sits 3 feet from the TV. Before I installed the 1byone antenna I took note of signal strength of each channel of my RCA antenna. The OUS00-0562 package also comes with an amplifier, which I connected to my RCA antenna as a test - and was disappointed. Only 3 channels were 10% higher, and that was within margin of error. The OUS00-0562 disappointed me soon after, as there was no change in signal strength on any channel over the RCA antenna (except that it gave me two more channels at 40% signal).

The short version:

RCA "rabbit ears" - 18 channels, 75%-30% (+/- 5%)
RCA "rabbit ears" with 1byone amplifier - 18 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)
1byone OUS00-0562 with 1byone amplifier - 20 channels, 70%-30% (+/- 5%)

I tried to reposition the OUS00-0562 antenna to see if there was a directional issue, if I was out of the "sweat spot." I did notice 5-10% dips here and there but no marked improvements. I didn't spend much time on this and since it wasn't shipped with a stand. You can buy one, but I didn't want to spend any more money on it since to me it was overpriced as is. I promptly returned it.

I will give this antenna one point though. It's better looking than the RCA antenna and it takes up less space. So if looks and space matter, it might be for you.

title: Works well
text: This is my primary card for my D5000. It works well so far, we'll see how it hold up over time.

title: Works, but there are better deals
text: I bought this when it was on sale and cheaper than [[ASIN:B008CVHLT2 Transcend 32GB SDHC Class 10 UHS-1 Flash Memory Card Up to 90MB/s (TS32GSDHC10U1E)]] to supplement the Transcend card. But in practice I use card only when I fill up my Transcend card. It might be imperceptibly slower, but the main reason is that I'm more familiar with the Transcend brand cards. Considering that the Transcend card is cheaper as of this writing, there is no reason to get this unless there is some concrete data demonstrating the ECC feature.

title: Works well, nice upgrade over 100M
text: I got this to upgrade from the 5 port netgear switch that I had since 1999. At first I was worried about the plastic case being an issue with heat retention, but having it for a few months everything seems fine so far. I got this model over other 8 port gigabit switches do to the advertised power saving features. I didn't test this out, but I do not see any issues with dropped connections. Transfer speed looks good for a gigabit connection when transferring files, definitely a nice upgrade over 100M.

title: No front facing camera for Skype calls, wifi issues
text:
This is a good phone for the price. But when I got this I didn't realize that there was no front facing camera for Skype calls, this limited its usefulness. The other problem encountered is that no matter how much I tried I couldn't enter our wireless key in to the phone without the phone "timing out." I have a long wireless key at my house and I had already configured many devices with that key. It almost seems like the key is "too long" for it. It generally takes about 10 to 15 minutes to type it in on my other devices, but they work in the end. I'm not going to shorten it and redo everything in my house just for this phone, so as far as I'm concerned the wifi "doesn't work" on this phone.

Being a windows phone it doesn't have the same software base as say Apple or Android, but I knew that already. On top of that one should be aware that this phone line might get retired or sold off in the future.

title: Used to convert GPU to fanless
text:
I used the plain Arctic Alumina at first and wondered why it didn't stick. Arctic Silver should call this product by a different name to differentiate it from plain Arctic Alumina. Even if this product is just Arctic Alumina (Part A) plus glue (Part B). The glue (Part B) has a somewhat epoxy smell like to it, not pleasant. There was some hardening by the cap area, but it was easy enough to squeeze through.

I used this to glue a heatsink to my GPU heat sink (by cutting it down first), in my project of converting my ATI 3450 to fan less. It holds so far.

Make sure that any time something doesn't work to clean everything (Isopropanol works) and start again rather than trying to reuse thermal compound. I tried to reuse some of the original plain Arctic Alumina I already had applied on the heatsink by applying Part B to the edges, this didn't work. I used clamps and let it sit for 24 hours. I ended up with a lot of excess paste. Make sure to clean up your work area right away since it can dry fast. I only wonder how long Part B will last in the tube.

title: Works, most issues are with the GPS itself
text: Bought this to go along with [[ASIN:B00AXX0I88 Garmin nüvi 2597LMT 5-Inch Bluetooth Portable Vehicle GPS with Lifetime Maps and Traffic]] which didn't have great visibility in direct sunlight. The product works. Of course it can only do so much since the hood can only be so big before it will start blocking the screen.. There was no problem with fit.

title: Works
text:
The whole point of an 8 pin connector on a motherboard is that it can supply more current than a 4 pin port can. Previously I was using a 4 pin to 8 pin adapter and just crossed my fingers that it wouldn't cause 1) stability issues 2) fire. But this design solves that potential problem by giving an additional input.

So far quality seems fine and it's working without issues. It keeps me from having to resort to more expensive or DIY methods.

title: Works well, sturdy - could use a quick release option to make it perfect.
text: When traveling I didn't always pack a full tripod, and when I did I usually left it behind. I used other mini-tripod types before, and this is is by far the most versatile. The gorillapod-type tripods are good idea in theory, but they are just not rigid enough for holding a DSLR. The miniaturized tripod type are more rigid, but still not rigid enough to use in unconventional ways. This tripod seems quite well put together. I can tighten it up, place it on a dashboard of a car and hold it there (granted with a lot of effort) on a bouncing road and the DSLR will not sag. Having the ability to tie it to things with the included Velcro strap proved to be more useful than I thought, and more rigid than the gorillapod-type. The tripod also folds down compactly and I can leave it in a loop on the outside of my small camera bag, instead of leaving it at home or berried somewhere in the bag. A quick release would have helped, but I usually left it on the camera.

title: Good layout and orgonized, but would have liked it to be a little lighter and less bulky
text: This provides very good protection for a Nikon D5000, its three lenses, memory cards, batteries and even a mini-tripod. The bag has ample dividers, I liked the little bag for small parts. Everything is easy to get to. I have no doubts over its build quality and I did get a chance to use the rain cover with good results. It's just that the bag is heavier than I expected it to be. I would have traded some protection for a more canvas like feel to the bag - a more long and flat look of a messenger bag. When walking around I have to use the thigh strap/belt otherwise it bounces around in an uncomfortable way.

title: Good heatsink for its size.
text:
This was the tallest heatsink I could fit in to my HTPC case. This is running on top of an i5-2500. The noise levels are good. Naturally when the CPU is under load it does pick up some but not in a noticeable way. Installation didn't give me issues with clearance.

If size was not a concern, I would have gotten the Cooler Master Hyper 212 EVO instead. I didn't want to spend more than $35-40 or so and this was a good pick. I took off the sticker from the top of the fan plastic shroud, which improved appearance a little but left a sticky residue. I wish the fan was a standard fit rather than propriety, but hopefully since I got a ball bearing fan it will last long enough.

title: Works without issues, but not an upgrade to a DOCSIS 2.0 modem in speed at basic ISP plans
text:
I read through Comcast supported model list and ordered this from another website, so I didn't have to pay their modem rental fee. I ordered Comcast using the online application process (borrowing a wireless connection from a neighbor), and was forced to order their starter package. Supposedly there is a way to refuse this if you call, but I didn't do this. I had a coax cable with me so as soon as I made my order I connected the modem to the coax input in the apartment, and my wireless router to the modem. I did not use a splitter. With my computer I tried to connect to the web which brought me to the comcast activation screen. I had no issues activating based on the info I had from the box and my comcast account number. This part was easy. It's a good thing I had my own cable since the starter package took two weeks to arrive.

My impression of this modem is that there is nothing special to this modem.You can access the modem through its IP address, which gives you several tabs: Status, Signal, Addresses Configuration, Logs, Open Source. No password is needed. You can remotely reboot it, and check to see if there is a signal. Other than that one feature I wished it had is having the ability to export logs. When the modem reboots, the logs get reset.

I have used a DOCSIS 2.0 modem at another location and I think the level of service makes a bigger difference than the DOCSIS version of the modem in use. You might see a difference if you pay for the top end ISP package, but I didn't get that. My plan is Performance which is supposed to be 50 Mbps, but my actual speed is 29 up 6 down.

I have read of some cases of the modem randomly rebooting. I don't have this issue. But I did open my modem and attached an aluminum heat sink as a precaution. I have managed to fit 100x25x10mm heatsink by cutting off a section. From what I read random reboots might be ISP related, but I'm not sure.

*****

As a side note, Comcast is terrible. At one point my service suddenly stopped. One tech service person I talked to hung up on me after half an hour of troubleshooting when see seemingly ran out of ideas to try. The next time I called I demanded a technician, which was scheduled to show up in 10 days at the earliest. I had a service outage for almost a month. The issue was a loose cable in their box. Also at one point my Netflix streaming was heavily throttled until Netlix payed off Comcast.

title: Attrative, inexpensive, simple set up, good stereo effect, but could be louder
text:
These were used with a Toshiba Satellite S70 to make the sound a little louder for watching some quite youtube videos. To start the toshiba speakers have pretty good volume (for a laptop) to begin with. But even they were not loud enough for some quite youtube videos. These were ordered as an inexpensive way to boost the sound volume.

My mother is not computer literate, but she figured out how to connect them to the computer by herself. These are attractive to look at and have good stereo separation. Though they are larger in person than one would think. But they were not louder than the Toshiba Satellite S70 speakers. On the other hand that problem was solved by positioning them closer. She actually prefers these for the stereo separation effect that they provide. I guess if your laptop already has good speakers you'd want a more expensive model, but for all other laptops these are a good, attractive and inexpensive upgrade.

Personally I do not like these speakers. The main issue is that lack of tweeter option which makes human speaks sound muddled. This is something that only I noticed, so it might not be a problem for you.

title: A good value
text:
I found this to be a pretty useful combination. It covered most of the lenses that I had, of course not all. I didn't notice any find metal particles on the adapters that I received.

I also ordered some other odd sized rings from this brand and was not disappointed.

This is a good value, but of course there are better built adapters out there.

title: Great for testing Alkeline batteries
text:
I have been using this for years to test Alkaline AA and AAA batteries along with AA and AAA NIMH batteries. For those purposes this has worked well to quickly determine the relative charge of Alkaline AA and AAA batteries. I have found that when taking a reading you can't break contact or the battery will show up with a lower capacity. The reading can vary for the same battery though, maybe by 20%.

It works in testing NIMH battery charge state, and in some cases with testing NIMH battery health. I have some NIMH batteries that I know are no good because they have a very fast self-discharge. My smart charger will charge them, but a few days later they were dead. I confirmed this after charging them to "full" again, and testing them with the ZTS immediately after.

EDIT: I rewrote this review to take account the following. I discovered that my smart charger will not recognize some NIMH batteries because they have discharged below 0.5 volts. The ZTS tester didn't help here. Initially I thought that these batteries were bad. But I found that it was still possible to charge them if given a "boost" with a dumb charger or another battery. In which case I think that the most reliable indication of battery health is with a test right after charging.

title: Worked fine, long ago
text:
I used this briefly many years ago, but then replaced with a digital recorder.

What I liked about this recorder is having the ability to review recordings at a faster speed than recorded. But in the end a digital recorder is smaller, holds more recordings and best of all has the ability to organize by date, time and name.

title: Works well, finicky with NIMH batteries
text:
This was bought to replace a tape unit to record class lectures for about $50. It is was a major upgrade. It's compact. When you can make recordings they come with a date and time in the file info which makes sorting them much easier. You can also record in to different folders, though you can only edit the folder names on a computer. I have also used this with an external microphone, with which it also worked well.

I use this recorder with NIMH batteries, but it doesn't seem to like them given how it stops recording when the charge of the batteries drops to 40% (tested separately afterwards). I guess this is really meant to be used with alkaline batteries. When the unit quit in class, which I could tell because it beeps when it turns off, I reached for my cell phone. Listening to the cell phone recording afterwards and comparing it to this device I can tell that the cell phone records with background noise and at low sensitivity. While I like that I can use my cell phone as a backup, it would not be my first choice for recording lectures. The recordings from this device, in contrast, have little noise and sound clear.

title: Versatile
text:
What I like about this fan is that it gets similar performance to the much more expensive low noise fans. The lowest speed of the fan don't make those typical annoying clicking noises that usually happen when slowing a fan down. It's not the quietest fan exactly, but it's pretty versatile in that it can be used as either low noise fan or as a mid-level cfm fan.

Previously to this fan I spent a lot of money on a couple of Scythe PWM fans only to discover that the motherboard didn't support fan speed control. This is a much better value.

title: Necessary 10 years ago, but ...
text:
This was my first flash for the canon system 10 years ago. Now, comparing to other flash units that I have used over the years, I'd say it's loud, slow to recycle, and with no features. I prefer using a Metz 54mz-3 in auto mode. The only advantage that this flash has to the Metz is in flash fill exposures of one 1 stop or less from ambient, this is where any E-TTL wins out.

This flash is better than any pop-up flash. It would do well on some cheap DSLR kit. But I'd recommend a better flash otherwise.

title: Good value, if cheap
text:
I bought my example of this fisheye lens from ebay for the EOS mount. I use this on a 1.6x crop and I have also used it on a full frame camera as well. It's not good below f11, but it is good at f16. Ken Rockwell mentions this in his review of this lens. With this lens its best to increase ISO even at the expense of image noise rather than open up the aperture beyond f8. I have tried to use this lens at f2.8 in low light on a 1.6x crop camera and it just does not look good. Not only is there a large loss of sharpness but for some reason the image becomes more orange on my example. I should mention that with my ebay example the coating on the front element wasn't even, so it's possible that it might be from that.

The lens cap on mine doesn't stay on do to a broken tab, which can be annoying since it's specific to the lens.

I think this lens is a good deal, if it can be had for cheap. I'm not sure I would buy another one if I lost mine at the current prices that this lens goes for though. The primary reason would be because a fisheye lens has limited use do to barrel distortion, I'd rather put that money towards a rectilinear wide angle.

title: Attractive laptop, wish it came with windows 7
text:
This laptop was given to me as a present. I use it as a travel laptop. I'll treat the laptop and the OS separately.

The Laptop.

The positives. The laptop is attractive. The hinges and folding design seems robust, at least in my use. The screen is bright, and seems to have good contrast. Good view angles. Touch control works. The power supply is compact. The laptop does not seem to get too hot. The laptop seems light for its size. SSD is nice.

The negatives. No separate mic jack. The screen is glossy, which can be prone to glare. Only two USB ports, though one of them is USB 3.0. Non-removable battery, which means that after regular use of a few years battery replacement will either be a hassle or expensive - I consider this to be the biggest negative here. When folded over and held in ebook mode your fingers will dig in to the keyboard keys. The laptop can only be upgraded to 8gb of ram, I consider this to be low. Function keys F1 through F12 are only available through the FN key. The fan is audible.

The OS

The positive. The task manager is full of a lot of useful information, a great step up.

The negative. I hate windows 8. I had to install a 3rd party start menu program (Start8) just to make it useable. I have wireless issues from time to time, but I'm not sure if this is do to the hardware or the OS. The wireless management software in windows 8 is a step down from windows 7. When it comes to using the ebook mode the built in reader doesn't support making bookmarks in files, it can read them but not make them. Frustratingly the 3rd party pdf readers that I tried do not support automatic screen rotation when held in portrait mode. After a few months I discovered an annoying feature that I had to change (Hybrid Shutdown) which I suspect drains the battery when the laptop is "shut down" and unplugged.

title: Bad LCD, AA batteries a pain
text:
When this camera came out it had a good number of features at around $100 price point. The resolution was high enough for the time and it had image stabilization. This was a present for my mother, and she liked it initially. While the image quality was not great, over time two issues stood out.

One of the main short comings of this camera is the hard to see LCD screen. It's useless in daylight. This is the primary reason why it was eventually replaced with a different model. The second reason was its use of AA batteries.

Using AA batteries is not a feature. When I bought this, I was convinced that having the ability to take AA batteries would be a plus. In practice our Ni-mh batteries were always in need of a recharging when the camera needed to be used. We also went through a few cheap chargers, which seemed to have a habit of dieing. Using AA alkaline batteries is not a solution since they only allow for a few pictures. In order to make this practical, one needs to put some money in to a good charger and low discharge rechargeable batteries. But by doing so the camera will end up costing you more money over time than a more expensive camera with a Lithium-ion battery.

Normally we gift away our older digital cameras, but this one isn't going to be gifted away do to those two reasons.

title: Good deal, if some modificaitons are done
text:
When I bought this it was cheaper than an internal hard drive of the same size. In that sense it was cheap. The downside is that as an external enclosure the unit has no ventilation unless you flip it upside down. I knew this when I bought it, I actually didn't plan to keep it at first. I just removed the cover, and transferred the seagate hard drive in to another enclosure. In to this unit I transferred a hard drive from a WD external that I was only USB 2.0. I thought to leave the unit open, which would made it look a bit unsightly, but instead I drilled some holes in to the top cover and put it all back together. It now functions as a backup hard drive.

The other potential downside of this unit is that this enclosure uses the flimsy USB 3.0 Micro-B connection instead of the more sturdy USB 3.0 Standard-B one. This isn't a big deal, but one should be aware of it.

title: Had potential, but poor quality fan

Worse, the fan is of a thin profile and I could not find a quality replacement fan online. This enclosure is connected to an HP computer with Windows 7 through the USB 3.0 port, yet when the computer is turned off the enclosure does not seem to auto shut down. I have not tried other combinations since that was the reason why I got it. I will not be buying this again.

Update: Fan getting replaced, again, due tl rattling sound. Fan is 80x80x10 mm. There seems to be only one source for these fans and they are low quality. Except for the fan issue, enclosure works fine otherwise.

A 2 oz bottle of their cleaner is 20 bucks (on sale from $30 right now!). So, one gallon of this liquid gold would be over $1200 dollars. Really??!!

I'm all for capitalism and well aware of the fact that I wasn't forced to buy this product but, come on, charge a more reasonable price for your products.

title: Fantastic TV, extremely buggy smart TV apps
text:
The picture of this is awesome. The 4k is the best I'd ever seen anywhere. Event 1080 games look fantastic.

I could literally see the hair follicles on someones nose from my couch.

The refresh rate is not bad. I didn't notice any excessive when playing games.

The sound was surprisingly amazing. I didn't have to buy surround sound like I thought I was going to have to.
When I first got this TV I have live PD on in the background while I making dinner. I got spooked because I heard sirens and it sounded like a cop car was in my drive way! Super trippy to have sound quality that is that good.

All around this is a fantastic TV. But I do have one issue with it, which is why I didn't give it 5 stars.
The smart TV Apps are WAY to buggy.
Everytime you leave the TV idle for an hour or so it cuts internet connection. Which makes sense. Helps save energy. BUT it seems a lot of apps struggle with re-connection issues.
A big one is sling. 7/10 times when I came back to my TV after I had been previously watching sling, it refuses to load any channel unless I do a hard reboot or changed apps. Even when it does work, I often get buffering or dropped frames. Which is def the TVs fault as I do not get this on any other device!
Netflix also locked up on me once when my TV went idle in the search menu and I came back. I could not exit the search or click on any titles. I have to restart my TV.
Honestly, Sony need to realize that making smart TV apps is not a simple task and they can't just leave it to a team of sloppy careless outsourced developers and expect good results.

However the smart TV apps being awful isn't a huge issue as I have a backup firestick and my xbox one that can do the same job but actually work :)

But still, for 3.5k I expected everything to be perfect.

title: Good performance per $ but runs too hot and is way too loud to be in a day-to-day office PC
text:
Immediately after installing I noticed the idle speed just sitting in BIOS to be 50C. That's quite a bit! More than any processor I've come across.
At first I thought I seated it wrong so I undid the heat sink, used really good thermal paste and tried once more.
Same result. Idle temp at 50C.
And under load it's getting up to into the low 60s and termal throttling like crazy. However it seems to perform well even under that heavy load, which is nice if that's all you care about.
But I'm doing a build for my dad and I don't think he'd be content with having to hear a jet engine under his desk day in and day out. So I'm going to have to look elsewhere.
That's on me though. I probably should have known better from my experience with another FX processor. Ah well.
Still considering if I'm returning this or not.

UPDATE:
Ok, I did some more digging and it sounds like my motherboard is not equipped to handle this processor.
WARNING: If you have a MSI 970A-G46 Motherboard DO NOT BUY THIS PROCESSOR.
Go research "MSI 970A-G46 FX 8350"
You'll find numerous testimonials of people who have had terminal issues trying to use a FX 8350 with this board.
Since the MB is at fault for this and I can not accurately benchmark this product, I'll give AMD the benefit of the doubt and make this 5 stars.

title: Good mother board - bad bios settings enabled by default
text:
Pros:
Ample slots for upgrades.
Does it's job well
Nothing broken

Cons:
The BIOS. More specifically the "Fast Boot" option that's enabled by DEFAULT and is know to cause tons of problems!

Oh man. This board REALLY irritated me! When I built my new PC everything went smooth. First thing I did when the built it was flash my BIOS to the latest version.

The smoothness ended when I tied installing windows. For some reason it freeze randomly all the time even with all the latest drivers installed. I swapped out each part in my new build one by one for 3 days trying to diagnose this issue. I eventually narrowed it down to my processor and Mother board. I didn't have any extra parts around to test which one of the two was causing this and I was about to RMA both when I found a forum post about X99-A boards and the freezing problems. Apparently it's caused by this "Fast boot" setting in the BIOS being enabled and thus causing key windows drivers not to load which would cause you system to eventually freeze up. I turned that off and BAM no more freezing. Haven't had one since.

Seriously? Why would this be enabled by default if it's known to cause so many issues Asus?!

The only reason I went with asus is because of the NVME support for 2.5 intel 750 series SSDs. I can guarantee you I will NOT go with asus Mother boards every again after this. I'll stick with my trusty MSI.

tl;dr I subtracted two stars for all the nonsense the "Fast Boot" setting put me through. If you're reading this Disabled Fast boot asap

I love it so much I'll be ordering another one just in case this one gets discontinued or something - hopefully not ever!

text:

This cable is flexible, doesn't tear easily even after months of being used and immersed in teenage angst, teenage hate, and teenage vitrol. Unlike some other brands, this one works well with Apple devices that use the Lighning connector and has done do after about a dozen iOS updates. To date we have not received an incompatible notification that have left other cables rendered useless, including two Amazon Basics cables we bought 3 years ago before switching to Anker. My guess is that they license the DRM chip/code from Apple but I haven't been able to confirm this. To date these have worked for us. We use the 1ft, 3ft, 6ft, and 10ft cables.

text:
The Anker PowerLine+ 6 foot Lightning Cable has been one of the few cables that has survived the rigor of daily use as well as at the hands of two tiny terrors that have destroyed other cables. We have tried about 4 different manufacturers, other than Apple, and Anker has consistently been the durable cable to hold up. We have iPhone 5, 6, and 6s phones at the house as well as an iPad and an iPad mini. Each one of these happily take the Lightning connector with no issues. The RAVPower 24W Dual USB wall chargers, and a Belkin charger, have worked flawlessly with this cable as has Anker and RAVPower lighter/power socket car chargers.

title: 300MbPS but only 10/100 RJ-45 (LAN) Connections
text:
Overall this is a good little feature-rich device but use just the wireless access point features. It was quick to setup but was definitely a time that you wanted to read the fine manual (RTFM (PG version)). It wasn't as easy to setup as the CISCO WES610N that I purchased at the same time BUT it is also feature rich.

I have had it up for a few days and haven't experienced major problems with it. We will see if it stands up to the test of time and gives me 3-4 years of service like my Cisco Linksys devices that are still working 4 1/2 years later.

Nerd Alert - I am a nerd at heart and utilize geek speak way too often. I try to remember that the Amazon audience contains friends, family, and strangers that may or may not know IT.

PROS:
* Feature Rich -
The ZyXEL is 1/2 the price of the comparable Cisco device but it has a much more feature rich set of wireless capabilities. It supports WPS, allowing for easy setup. It supports WDS, allowing you to configure a network that allows you to carry your laptop from room to room in a large house without sacrificing much speed if setup correctly. It can access as a repeater if needed.

* Cabling -
The ZyXEL includes the power supply and a network cable (CAT-5). It supports a standard called MDI/MDIX, which means that you won't need a crossover cable if you connect it to a switch.
* Wireless Distribution Service -
You can make this part of your existing network using WDS, or Wireless Distribution Service, or simply configure it as an access point. I just removed two old Linksys routers from being WDS nodes since replacing my old Actiontec 802.11a/b/g with an Actiontec 802.11b/g/n wireless router. Eventually I will get around to using the ONI port and setting up a network with DD-WRT

CONS:
* LAN ports on the back are are 10/100 -
While the router notes that it supports connection speeds up to 300MbPS it only has two (2) 10MbPS/100MbPS RJ-45 (LAN) connections. Technically you may never truly realize the full throughput available with this device. This is not unlike other wireless access points, such as the Cisco WET610N (single 10/100) or the Cisco WES610N (quad port 10/100 for $10 more). I did what any good geek would do; used it as an excuse to purchase an 8-port Netgear 10/100/1000 switch to replace my 5-port 10/100 switch in my office/lab with the computers and Hyper-V lab systems. I am going to use the Cisco product downstairs with my home server and VMWare ESXi box.

* Setup may be difficult for the average home user -
I most certainly RTFM'd and reading the manual helped. It did take a quick configuration of my network card in order to even get to the point I could setup the device.
The Cisco devices use an APIPA address, which makes setup easier. Why? APIPA is that 169.254.#.# address that your computer gets when it connects to a network that doesn't give out addresses. This allows you to easily setup the Cisco WES610N.

title: Do Not Buy This !!!
text: This is not a good unit. I would recommend purchasing the echo show 5. There is absolutely no way to adjust the clock face on this unit. There is no way to adjust the night clock face on this unit either. I bought this unit so that I would have a larger smart clock in my living room. What a mistake that was. I have 2 echo show 5 units that are excellent. The clocks are actually smaller on the larger screened 8 than on the 5. I simply could not believe it. So I called customer service immediately and it's true. There is no way to adjust the clock faces on the 8. So unless you're just interested in the bigger picture, I recommend skipping this unit because I would not want you to be sitting here like I am tonight writing this and being so disappointed at an obvious flaw that should've been fixed long ago with a simple firmware upgrade. I am returning this unit first thing in the morning.

title: I Was Not Sure but Now I Am
text: I was not sure if I needed this particular device. I already have Eco.systems in every room. But they gave me a deal on it and I decided to try it. Turns out that it is now an essential part of my system. What I like about it most is that it is visual. I can create reminders that are visual just by speaking to the unit. The weather information is visual and far more sophisticated than the audio devices. It has several interesting clocks on it and clock faces which are adjustable. When it is dark in the room it automatically turns into a beautiful nighttime clock that is not bright but easily viewable. It also connects into my blink camera systems that I can also see by voice control. So it is sort of like a visual Alexa system. I have not used the camera portion part of it yet and I have the camera shutter turned off at the present time for privacy reasons. This of course is optional. I consider this to be an excellent addition to the Echo.systems. Very happy that I purchased it.

title: Works really well so far

It comes with some very nice colors that are changeable with a push button on the bottom. I like the moving multiple colors myself. Very nice unit for the price.

title: I Love It
text: The "Billie Eilish" Designer Echo Studio was delivered to my door today. Super easy to hook up to the Amazon system and I also Bluetoothed it to one of my laptops. It was very easy. The sound is beyond excellent and I am able to adjust it with the equalizer in the Amazon App. I had my choice between a basic black and the "Billie Eilish" designer unit. They are the same technically but this designer unit is very beautiful, the colors are stunning and of course it has a very nice picture of this multi-talented and very popular female music artist on the front with her name written on the top. Very cool. Being a music collector my whole life, having this designer Echo Studio adds a lot of class and functionality to my living room.

title: Technology That Is Here to Stay
text: I have actually had the echo dot system since it first came out. They gave me a good price and I simply updated to the latest generation. How much different it is, I am not sure. But here's one thing I do know. It is the most useful product I have ever purchased. The list of what this marvelous product can do is almost endless, and the list will keep on growing as they work on the back end to improve it as the years go on. Operating systems by voice command is the wave of the future. Getting information and music by simply asking a unit was just a fantasy when I was growing up in the 60s. Everyone I talked to who has this unit, meaning the Alexa system have nothing but positive things to say about it. Really one of the best inventions of the 21st century. So my advice is to at least try this unit and see if it helps your life. You can always return it in a reasonable timeframe if it does not. My educated guess is that you will not return it because you will love it like I do and find it useful like I do.

title: High Quality Picture
text: I had never tried out a curved screen before. I am using it as a second screen for my extended display on my computer. I love it. The screen seems to be easier on my eyes because it is curved. It seems to me that reading or watching videos and movies on a curved screen is very different than a flatscreen. I know the science is that the eyes react better to a curved screen. After buying this unit, I would have to agree with that. The picture is stunning. Way better than my flatscreen I had before. I probably will not buy any external device that does not have a curved screen again. It is just simply a better picture. I would buy this unit again.

title: I really like it.

Through the app you can actually change it to whatever color that you like and they have many colors. It also turns on automatically when it is dark or at least when I am near it. It fits in perfectly so it looks like it is part of the unit. I use mine in my bathroom, the echo part being for music or weather reports and the light so I can see what I'm doing at night. title: A Good Quality Microphone
text: So I bought one of these omnidirectional microphones because I really dislike internal computer microphones because they have low sound quality. I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of this microphone. It is truly omnidirectional so you can place it anywhere. It plugs into a USB port or USB hub, both work fine. Another great feature of this microphone is that it has a very long cord which really comes in handy. You can essentially place it anywhere with that length of cord. It has a mute button you can push in the center of it and also a blue light to show that it is connected and working. I liked it so much I bought a second one for my new computer because I wanted a quality microphone that I knew worked well. So I do recommend buying this unit. Of course are more expensive microphones out there for professional recording but this is an excellent microphone for talking with people over the computer, speaking programs etc. it also has some decent weight to it so it does not fall off anything easily. It is not cheaply made in any way.

title: I Nice Addition For Remote Areas

title: Probably the Best Headphones for the Price
text: I realize that these are not inexpensive headphones. I wanted really decent headphones that had a really large bass response. Beats are known for their quality and so that's what I was looking for. Fast charging that will last for a long time, meaning that I only seem to need to charge it every few days, and I use it a lot. Also very beautiful. It has invisible controls on one side of the headset, meaning that if you press one of the sides things will happen, like volume control, and most importantly, if push twice it will skip to the next song depending on how you have your source music set. I have mine set to play randomly so I don't know what is playing next. That is controlled by your unit, not the headphones. These are Bluetooth headphones and you can hook them up to anything that Bluetooth's. It also has an incredible range on it. This is my second apartment I have had them at and it actually goes perfectly from floor to floor right through the cement without sound deterioration of any kind. No I don't know what the range is, and so it may depend on your own situation, but I simply do not think that there are better headphones out there for the price. Like I said, if you are looking for excellent bass response, and I like bass, because I listen to a lot of rock 'n roll and heavy metal, then these headphones are the right ones to get. They are also very sturdy and they fold up so if need be you can put them in your coat pocket. Highly recommended.

title: The Perfect Speaker
text: This item is a Bluetooth speaker that is really powerful. It has a perfect balance of days, midrange and tweeter and sounds great at low or medium and even high volumes. No distortion. I actually have two of these, and they are both hooked up to echo.systems meaning Alexa. They have different kinds of lighting settings. Be aware that you cannot turn off the lights when the unit is on. So if you are using one in the bedroom like I am, I actually cover it with a shirt at night, and there's been no heating issues with that being covered. These are things I look for. You can also hardwire it because it has a 3.5 cm stereo input which is standard. Of course it also is a Bluetooth system in case you want to use any wires. title: Best Product and Technology to Come out in Years. A Winner.
text: This product is a winner. The echo.system is here to stay. I was around during the early days of Internet technology working in the field. I had a knack for knowing what was going to be part of our future of technology and what was not. I still have that knack. This is an amazing product. I bought 2 of them. 1 for the living room. 1 for the bedroom. Every day they work on it from their end to give it more and more functionality meaning more things that it can do. You can pretty much hook it up to any Bluetooth speaker if you decide that you want better sound for music. I purchased speakers for each unit that were not related to Amazon in any way, just because I needed specialty products. I just have the unit you see here and not the ones with the more advanced speakers and so I cannot speak to them. But of the many many abilities it has, the ability to pull up music, TV, movies and more, some of my favorite things are the simplest. Instant forecasts anywhere in the world, timers and an alarm that you activate merely by speaking to it has really helped me in many ways. Do you want to know the time? Ask Alexa. Do you want to know today's forecast or next week's forecast? Just ask. They are meant to be on 24 hours a day and are activated by voice and so there are no lights on to bother a person when they are sleeping. I put the one in the bedroom not just to operate the television, but more of an alarm clock thing. So if I need to take a nap before my next client, wake me up in one hour. It's that easy. Lying in bed at night and asking what time it is or saying: wake me up at 7 AM. Done. I do not believe this product will replace computers remote controls nor telephones, but I think that it will be a wonderful companion to it, infinite information availability, and who knows what's coming in the future. The upgrades are done on their end so you do not have to buy new units as they upgrade. How cool is that? So far both of these units have worked flawlessly and I have had them for about a month now. Completely unobtrusive, and with plug-in units that are available, you can even run your household lights, appliances and more. I purchased a few of these things and they work perfectly. All my guests who have seen how this operates have been astounded and now they all want one. You can't beat the price. Now I am not hooked into Amazon in any way. I just love good solid technology that is the wave of the future. I cannot speak highly enough of these products. I am a very technological person and I have very high expectations for my technology that I purchase and this particular unit that I am reviewing is the one that I have. It works perfectly and I just love it.

title: For eSATA, don't make mistake!
text:
Wouldn't recognize on the eSATA port. It would detect the HDD, but would not format nor store data. I thought it would be plug and play. I submitted a return request (which the seller approved), but after extensive Googling, discovered how to make it work on my machine.

1) For Windows 7 (I think Windows 10 may not have this issue), make sure you have the registry entry to allow AHCI.
2) In BIOS, make sure your boot devices are in proper order.
3) In BIOS, update RAID configuration to AHCI.

After that, it is operating as expected.
