title: We Love To Rub A Dub In This Tub
text:
We purchased this product before we were expecting, knowing that it was neutral gendered and would be perfect for a boy or a girl. When we had our first child, a 9 lb, 11 oz baby girl, I was SO nervous! I didn't know a thing about babies. My eldest sister helped me give her her first bath and complimented our whale tub. She said it was so nice that the green padding in the base would help prevent baby from slipping. By the third bath, I had it down.

As the weeks have gone on, our little one has really loved her tub. She began holding her head up at 4 days old and was doing so independently within a month of her birth. She loved kicking and splashing in her tub. She has never cried in the bath. We use a turtlemeter thermometer and she thinks of it like a little toy with which to play.

I would recommend this tub with the seat in it for a newborn baby up to about 12 lbs. Once our daughter was 13 lbs, she has trouble staying warm in the tub with the seat attached. It simply wasn't deep enough for her while she was lying down and she only got her bottom half wet unless I poured water over her, and the chilly air would then make her cold.

With the seat out, she needs to be sitting on her own so there was a two month gap where we did not use her tub, and instead bathed her with me in the big tub.

Once she was a successful sitter, we returned her to this tub for warmer nights, so she could sit and play in the water. She loves it!

After a bath, I would recommend not only using the drain in the tub, but turning this whale tub upside-down and and then turning it from side-to-side to drain it, as the water tends to get trapped beneath the green padded area. You can also remove the seat to clean under it. Using dish soap and a scrub daddy sponge, I am able to quickly clean the tub in-between uses.

I was expecting some preschool, early years tablet that had limited games, books, activities etc. I was initially elated to find that it was actually a full blown tablet the same as mine with internet, and everything I could do on mine. Including access to everything that I had on my pad, account, subscriptions, passwords, everything.Anything could be downloaded. For sure a lot my fault, I wasn’t as proactive on security and blocking things as I should have been. Just be aware it is a full blown pad despite the cute cover and childish pictures.
To sum it up, it is a great deal, should you be an adult and want an inexpensive tablet, this should do everything you need. And… the cute little cover comes off and it’s just a little black screen.
I would recommend this, just be smarter and more aware than I was with security.

title: Good option for PC to PC transfer
text: Good cable and...just ok software for PC to PC transfer. One thing to note is that out of the box, the speeds you will achieve when connecting from 1 USB 3.0 port on one computer to another USB 3.0 port on another computer is not more than 40-45MB per second. If you want faster speeds on Windows, you should go into Device Manager and find the device labeled "USB 3.0  SD Card Reader USB Device" under Disk Drives. Right-click this device then click "Properties", then click "Policies". From here you should choose the option "Better Performance". Doing this will elevate the speeds to over 150MB per second and sometimes more.

In comes this little puppy which, pretty much as soon as I hooked it up and installed the software, made an immediate difference. Pages that were starting to time out loaded in a flash again, and I could even stream Netflix without buffering 20 times in an hour episode. This ended up being the reason I will need to return it. My wife literally can't watch it due to this. She is very sensitive to visual disturbances and eye strain. #2 it would only project around 80" around 10ft from the wall. My old infocus 860 was over 100" and it is 10 years old. text: At first glance this appears to be an ordinary black case fan, devoid of flashy colors or RGB lights found on many of the competition.. but once you pick it up you can feel the difference immediately. The only area where it falls short is in life expectancy.. despite its build quality its only rated for 40,000 hours whereas my go-to Cougar vortex fans are rated at 150,000 hours (and I have 18 of them in a push pull config on a 3x 360 radiator setup which have been running 24/7 for over a decade, so I believe their life expectancy claims). title: Solid Gaming PC
text:
The Aurora R10 is the first AMD computer I've had in about 15 years since the days of the Athlon64. Its great to see AMD's resurgence and as expected the Ryzen processor provides excellent performance at a very nice price point. Its also been about 10 years since I had an ATI/AMD Radeon card and I'm similarly impressed with the improvements they've made in streamlining and improving their drivers (that was previously a major pain point and reason I've stuck with nvidia cards over the years)

Overall I think this is a great gaming CPU, it has a solid build and great performance for the price. It can run pretty much all current games smoothly as long as you aren't using 4k. If you are planning to run games in 4k then you probably need a more powerful video card setup. My only real complaint about this system is how loud the fans are when gaming.. its fine when doing most activities but the noise becomes quite loud and annoying when the GPU is taxed. I'm not sure if its just the case design or the GPU fan but this is louder than any system I've had in a while. This case does have enough room inside for a 120 radiator if you want to add watercooling, thats not enough to cool both the CPU and GPU but it would definitely be an improvement for not much money.

Pros-
Good performance for the price
Minimal pre-installed bloatware
Excellent array of ports and convenient front inputs
Nice RGB lighting
Case is upgradable and has space for small watercooling loop

Cons-
Overly loud fans while gaming
Appearance/shape of case is not my favorite
Case design wastes space that could be used to improve cooling

title: Mixed Bag
text:
Pros--
-Very comfortable and secure fit even during high intensity exercise
-Solid Bluetooth connection
-Good noise canceling
-Hear thru mode is useful
-Sleek, low profile look
-Decent battery life, charging case is nice
-mic works well for calls or voice commands
-LOTS of bass (I consider this a major negative, but some people will like the bass heavy sound)

CONS-
-Below average sound quality (WAY too much bass, even after using the EQ to turn down the bass its still more than I would prefer for most types of music, the default out of the box sound is the worst I have ever heard on a pair of headphones in this price range.. but that said you can make them sound pretty decent after a bit of tweaking with the EQ)
-Not loud enough, the maximum volume is barely adequate for high external noise situations like airplane (even with the noise cancellation which works pretty well)
-Sealed design is not good for 'active' pursuits because of microphonic effect amplifying internal sounds whenever you move around
-software can be buggy, occasionally when I change settings and they appear to be changed in the software but do not apply to the buds

I think there are certain people who will love these buds, especially if you listen to a lot of rap/hiphop or other bass heavy music as the default sound seems to be tuned for that kind of music. Personally I just can't really get into the sound of these, even after tweaking with the EQ there is too much bass and the soundstage is flat and lifeless. I do like a lot of things about them though, the fit is comfortable and very secure, much better than airpods or galaxy buds on that front.

title: Excellent combination wifi/bluetooth card
text:
Upgrading to this card gave my aging PC a nice boost in performance for both wifi and bluetooth. My previous wireless card was an ASUS one which only supported wireless-N, so several generations out of date. For some reason I never upgraded the wifi card on my PC even though I got a new router last year, so upgrading to this gave me a notable boost in performance as well as getting better signal strength.

Also love that this has bluetooth built in, I previously had a dongle bluetooth adapter on the PC and this one performs much better, again improved signal strength and no dropouts.

The only downsides to this wifi card are that the pigtail cables which connect the antenna may be short for some scenarios (if you don't want to place it right on top of your PC case or you have a very large one). And also its a new chipset with drivers that may still have some kinks to work out.. they have released updates recently which fix the main issue I was having though (occasional wifi dropouts) so hopefully it remains stable.

title: Great duster but needs longer cord
text:
This is a nice blower/duster, it has similar or possibly slightly more power than a typical compressed air can (depending on the attachment used), and it isn't too loud for the amount of power. I'd say its about as loud as a dyson stick vacuum on the high setting. This air blaster doesn't have an annoying high pitched whine like some I've used in the past which is good.

The only downside is that the cord is too short. although its advertised as 10 feet long, mine measures out to just under 9 feet.. which is plenty if you only want to clean one PC with it but in my case I have several things in my office I want to clean and it requires moving it around to 3 different outlets to reach them all, if the cord was a few feet longer I'd be able to reach them all from a single outlet. I also wish they'd included a cord holder at the bottom, the domed shape makes it difficult to wrap the cord around the device for storage.

Aside from dusting, this is also really good for use with vacuum bags like space bags.. just attach to the inlet port at the bottom and it can suck all the air out, I find it more conventient than using my upright vac wand attachment for this purpose.

title: Not perfect but very good for the money
text:
For the price this is a very nice USB microphone, I would agree with other reviewers that it performs on par with or better than similar competing USB condenser mics in this price range such as Blue Snowball or the Behringer C1.

I do wish it came with more accessories though similar to the non-USB version. The Aokeo AK-60 XLR version comes with a scissor boom arm, shock mount and pop filter for the same price.. so if you do happen to have a compatible audio interface with phantom power then I would recommend the XLR version.

The main annoyance with this mic is that when using it in windows 10 the driver does not have native mic gain control option. In many recording programs you can boost the mic gain via other means but if using this mic for gaming or other purposes through the native drivers then you will have to be very close to the mic to produce adequate volume (ie you pretty much need a boom arm) or otherwise you will need to boost gain via external passthrough program such as APO equalizer. I have also tried this mic in linux and the drivers there do have native gain control.

Overall I do think the sound quality and construction of the mic is good for the price and I would recommend it .. just note that if using windows 10 you will probably either need a boom arm or need to use external software to boost the mic gain. A boom arm is strongly recommended anyways to prevent extraneous noises like keyboard clacking, etc..

title: Solid laptop with classic design
text:
This is a large screen laptop with a classic design, it is somewhat bulky but incorporates some features that are often missing on many modern laptops with sleek case designs.. like a built in DVD drive, a keyboard with decent key travel, and a wide array of ports. It has the latest 10th gen Intel processor which offers a lot of performance with minimal power consumption, so this thing operates cool and quietly under normal usage, and even when you stress it by playing games or something the fan noise is pretty mild.

The only downside of this particular build is the lack of SSD. Boot up time and performance under many workloads can be greatly improved by swapping the magnetic hard disk out for a solid state drive. Another benefit of the old-school case design is that it is very easy to take this laptop apart and upgrade the drive yourself (many newer laptops with sleek case designs are very difficult to upgrade).

Overall I think this is a great laptop for the price, perfect for watching DVDs or streaming video with the large screen and plenty of power for most web/office/productivity tasks. The only thing its not ideal for is gaming since it only has the onborad intel GPU which isn't sufficient for most modern games.

title: Great hardware but software is frustrating for advanced users
text:
This router was super easy to set up and has all the features the average user will need. My home is just over 3000 sq ft. and this router provides great signal strength throughout the whole house without any additional mesh nodes. Note that my house is 3 stories though and the router is centrally located on the middle floor. If your house is more spread out then additional nodes may be required to cover 3000 sq ft adequately.

Hardware wise this router seems great, the software is a bit klunky though compared to my previous ASUS router. Also its extremely annoying that they try to force you to use their phone app to set up the router. On the initial setup screens they only show the option to log in via the app (which requires you to create a linksys account on their site). I did find a way to bypass this though by going to the password recovery screen and then canceling out which takes you to the actual router admin login bypassing the setup mode, from there you can login with the default password shown on the bottom of the router near the serial number.

title: Cute headphones
text:
These cat ear headphones are pretty cute, my 6 year old daughter loves them. The sizing is a little big on her even on their smallest size but she would rather use these than her other headphones because cat ears =)

The sound quality is not great but it is decent.. better than most of the other kids headphones we have. If you're looking for sound quality probably look elsewhere but if cuteness is more important to you than sound quality then you will probably love these.

It uses a CR-2032 battery which is kind of annoying but I do like that they include an extra battery (one comes pre-installed and there is a spare in the package).

title: Nice backup drive with attractive enclosure
text:
This is a nice portable drive if you need a large drive to backup all of your files. Note that this is a magnetic HDD and not a SSD based drive, so it is pretty slow and not really ideal for use as a system drive or a work drive for large files like RAW photography, etc.. its great for backup and storage purposes though and the aluminum enclosure looks great with surface pro, macbook and other sleek metal shell laptops.

The drive runs really quiet and the aluminum enclosure does a good job of working as a heatsink to dissipate the generated heat without the need for fans or vents. Like all spinning HDD it does vibrate some when in use but not too bad. Works with both USB-C and USB 3.0 so it should work with pretty much any computer from the past 20 years or so.

Overall, great drive with an attractive enclosure and I would recommend it for backup or general storage purposes but if you need to access files quickly with higher performance I think its worthwhile to spend a little more for an SSD based drive since the prices on those have come down a lot recently.

title: Fast and reliable so far
text:
This TP-link router is competitively priced but has a lot of advanced features which used to only be found on high-end units (or by using 3rd party firmware). I had a previous TP-link router about 6 or 7 years ago which I wasn't super impressed with, primarily I felt the software was lacking on that model. It seems they have made a lot of progress over the past few years as the software on this router is very good, it has all the features I want and a nice user interface also.

So far, this unit has been reliable and while its not the fastest router on the market, the speeds are plenty fast enough for most home use. The only thing it is lacking compared to my old router is a USB port for use with older printers or for sharing files, so if that is a consideration you may want to look at one of the higher end TP-link models which do have that feature.

title: Super durable phone case
text:
I do a lot of cycling, both MTB and road biking.. and I have broken/damaged quite a few phones over the past few years, usually from minor falls that crack the screen or in one case from sweat which seeped through the volume buttons and shorted some components (despite the phone being IP67 rated supposedly).

With my phone stored inside this Pelican case I feel confident that its not going to break even in a nasty spill, which is important since I may need my phone to call for help in that situation.

This case is pretty bulky and doesn't have a ton of room inside.. but it is very well made and durable so if you have a need for a weather proof and durable phone case (or other small fragile items) then this is a winner.

title: Excellent Hardware, Decent Software
text:
As a software developer and tech geek who also dabbles in graphic design and photography, good color calibration is an important thing to me. I find it extremely bothersome when looking at a multi-monitor setup where the colors don't match well. I originally bought a spyder 3 some years ago when I started using a 3 monitor setup with two different types of monitors (a 144hz gaming monitor in the center and two 60hz displays on the sides). While the spyder 3 worked well, it was very slow at calibrating which was frustrating when doing a multi-display setup. I think it took around 5-6 hours to do all 3 displays with the spyder 3 (Note that I was using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal, but the Spyder software was equally as slow)

Last year I replaced all my monitors with new ones which are all the same type and I actually never calibrated them because they looked pretty good from the factory and I never felt like spending the time to use the spyder 3.. but when I saw Datacolor had released a new lens-based Spyder with claims of it being much faster and more accurate I knew I had to try it.

I am reviewing the SpyderX Pro, which has the same hardware as the SpyderX Elite but has software limitations locking some features (the most important being the limited calibration options for gamma/white point/brightness). Because those settings are important to me and I have previous experience with DisplayCal, I am using ArgyllCMS/DisplayCal software with the SpyderX hardware instead of the default Spyder software. (SpyderX support was just added to ArgyllCMS in the latest version 2.1.0 on 4/10/19)

I haven't done a side-by-side comparison with the older baffle based spyder 3 to say whether the lens-based spyderX is more accurate out of the box.. but I will say that the calibration looked good to me and I can vouch for the manufacturers claims that the SpyderX is much faster than the previous generations.. The SpyderX took around 15-20 minutes per display compared to 90-100 minutes per display with the Spyder3.

Overall I am pleased with the SpyderX and think it is a worthy upgrade over its predecessor.. but I would recommend using it with DisplayCal if you really want the best results Note that both ArgyllCMS and DisplayCal are both Free, Open Source Software so you don't have to pay anything extra if you want to use them... the only downside is that they are more complicated than the Datacolor software which is designed to be very user-friendly.

title: Solid enclosure for NVMe drives
text:
This enclosure is perfect for turning an NVMe drive into a portable disk. It is well made, the aluminum construction looks stylish and also serves to dissipate heat without requiring a fan like some other enclosures do (which is important since some NVMe can run quite hot!)

Using it over USB-C, the performance is very good.. obviously not quite as fast as native speeds but still much faster than any other external drive I've ever used. Its great that it can be used with older USB-3.0 devices as well, and the speeds there are still pretty good.

This is my first NVMe enclosure, but I've used a lot of HDD/SDD enclosures in the past and many of them had somewhat poor construction.. this one does not give that impression at all, everything about it seems well built. I have nothing but positive things to say about this product, highly recommended if you are looking for an NVMe enclosure.

title: Blazing fast
text: Speed and storage in a small form factor, good scores in crystalDiskmark and solid performance in real world usage as well.  Very nice upgrade from a traditional SATA SSD if you do a lot of data intensive work.  I didn't have any issues with the install, but it can be tricky on some systems depending on BIOS/driver support.  As others have noted, this drive does run hot, quite a bit hotter than my Samsung NVMe drive.. that does concern me a bit, hoping it doesn't lead to reduced lifespan or data integrity issues down the road but only time will tell, so far it has been working perfectly.

title: Nice FPS gaming monitor
text:
This is a good low-cost 144hz WQHD gaming panel, it is a TN panel so the viewing angles are not quite as good as an IPS.. but that is really only an issue if you are watching movies on it from across the room or something, it won't affect gaming at all. Like all TN panels this has super fast 1ms refresh rate and low input lag, perfect for FPS gaming.

Some TN panels are known for having poor color quality and contrast but this is not one of them, it has excellent color reproduction and the one I received was very well calibrated right out of the box (tested with spyder colorimeter). When placed up next to my Asus 27" IPS monitor, they look almost identical.. really the only way you can tell this is a TN panel is by the viewing angle which is not as wide as IPS, in all other respects it performs as well as my IPS panels, while also having lower input lag.. for that reason I definitely recommend this monitor for competitive FPS gamers looking for a low cost but high quality monitor.

The stand and aesthetics of the monitor are minimalist but high quality, like most Dell monitors. I like the fact that it doesn't have any special 'gamer' emblems like Asus and many other brands tend to do with their gaming monitors.

I knocked off 1 star due to the reduced viewing angles and because it has AMD Freesync instead of G-sync.. but this monitor really is an excellent value and performs as well or better than many more expensive monitors.

title: Not durable
text: This mount broke on the second ride I used it.  I went over the bars at slow speed on a steep sandy section and the mount snapped.  Had I crashed on rocks or at higher speed I would have expected that result, but I was surprised how easily this one broke.  I bought a sturdier aluminum mount (machined by a guy on mtbr forums) and it has held up to several crashes without any issues.

title: A decent thermal imager held back by software issues
text: I've used the 2nd generation FLIR one camera, and also other FLIR models (C2 and i7).  My previous experience with FLIR products have all been positive but unfortunately the FLIR one gen 3 has been plagued by issues ever since release.  The internet requirement that other reviewers complained about has been fixed, you now only need internet to register it once and then it will work without internet.  However, there is still a problem with the latest version of iOS that causes the app to run very slow and drain the battery extremely quickly (the manufacturer has noted this in comments on other reviews here).  As such, I cannot recommend this unit at the present time.  I'm hoping they will get these firmware issues resolved soon, I will update this review and provide more details when they do.  At present, it is clearly not working as intended because it is worse than the 2nd generation FLIR ONE in pretty much every respect.

title: Mediocre sound quality, fit issues
text:
These headphones don't really hit the mark for me -- maybe because I have a small head and smaller ears. They stay on and don't fall off even when running but I can't get the fit correct where the driver stays sealed in my ear the way its supposed to (tried all sets of tips included). When they come loose the sound quality is very bad since these are a sealed design headphone and rely on creating a seal with your inner ear to reproduce low frequencies, so they sound very tinny and harsh. Even when I use my fingers to hold the drivers in place though, the sound quality of these is pretty mediocre compared to my other sony BT headphones.

Also when I tighten the band in the back to prevent cable noise when running, that makes the control pod be on the back of my neck which is kind of awkward to use. I also don't like the overall design which looks and feels kind of bulky, at least they are pretty light weight though. These headphones worked as expected and had no issues with syncing, if they fit better I would have given them 3 or 4 stars but I have a pair of sony bluetooth headphones that sound better, fit better, and look better for about the same cost so I really can't recommend these.

title: Nice antenna, we cut the cord years ago but ...
text: Nice antenna, we cut the cord years ago  but its nice to be able to get local channels occasionally. Installation was easy.  We were able to mount ours out of view but it has a nice look to it so it wouldn't be horrible if you had to leave it exposed.

title: Solid mount
text: Nice mount, install was relatively straightforward although the instructions were somewhat confusing because it shows several options that may not apply to your installation with no text to explain.  I could have done it faster without looking at the instructions.  Solid mount though and I like that it included plastic wall anchors since I only had 1 stud available in the space I needed to mount it.

title: This is a great adapter if you need extra USB ports and the ...
text: This is a great adapter if you need extra USB ports and the motherboard is accessible.  Works perfect for me because I use a danger den torture rack case that has the motherboard exposed, now I have 2 extra USB 3.0 ports on the side of the case which is more easily accessible than the rear of the motherboard.

title: Fits pretty snugly on our 10 inch galaxy note
text: Fits pretty snugly on our 10 inch galaxy note.  It seems pretty flimsy for a 'rugged exoskeleton' but it does afford some level of protection against dropping the tablet.  I would give it 4 stars if it had a stand flap on both sides, as-is I have to choose between having the power/volume buttons accessible when in the upright position, or having the charging port accessible.  If I want to use the other side while its upright I have to remove the case and flip it around.

title: Great if you replace the firmware..
text:
This router has nice hardware but suffers from poor stock firmware. The Linksys firmware lacks features compared to the routers from other manufacturers that use nearly identical hardware (ASUS AC68U and Netgear R7000). I also had problems with stability when using the Linksys firmware, even after updating it to the latest version.

When I first received this router it was not yet supported by any of the major 3rd party firmwares but now it does work with newer builds of DD-WRT and tomato. After replacing the firmware with DD-WRT this router performs as it should, rock solid and better 2.4ghz signal after boosting the transmit power. Just make sure you have adequate airflow if you boost the transmit power because the unit can get pretty hot. With the default linksys firmware I found the 5ghz signal strength to be pretty good but the 2.4ghz signal was weak compared to other routers I have.

If you are comfortable replacing the firmware on your router then I would recommend this model, otherwise you're probably better off with the comparable ASUS model. In my experience ASUS typically has better stock firmware than the other major manufacturers.

title: Great cable for the price
text: Amazon basics cables are well made compared to most other low priced cables.  I have a quite a few of them and have yet to be disappointed, this one is no exception.

title: Quality case for the Note Pro 12"
text:
This is a nice case, good aesthetics and nice texture to the material. Provides good protection for the tablet and the case itself seems to hold up well also. Magnetic closure and multiple viewing angles are both nice features.

The only potential negative is that this case is slightly bulkier than some others, but personally I think it is worth it for the extra protection it provides. Given that the 12" tablets are pretty heavy, the added protective border on this case seems necessary to prevent the tablet from breaking if it is dropped.

title: Zero problems here.. tested on two 70D and a 6D
text:
I was concerned about purchasing one of these given all the negative reviews but I took the plunge anyways because I just couldn't stomach paying what Canon asks for the OEM version.

Maybe I just got lucky but the construction quality of the unit I received seems fine, I've had it for about 3 months now and have used it quite a bit in that time period. As noted in the title, I've used it on two 70D and a 6D with zero problems.

I like the fact that the adapter is not permanently attached to the power brick, that will make it easier to repair when the cable does eventually short out (which is bound to happen sooner or later given the tight bend required to route the cable out of the battery compartment, that applies to the Canon branded cable also though)

title: Nice sealed cans but value isn't as good compared to previous generation
text:
The previous generation of these headphones were well regarded among some audio geeks due to their value. Their sound quality compared favorably to many other entries in the <$100 price range, and especially in comparison with other sealed headphones in that price range.

On this new version they have made a number of upgrades and also raised the price quite a bit. Unfortunately, not all of the changes to this version are improvements in my opinion and the higher price puts these in close competition with other headphones in the $150 range which are only slightly more expensive but have significantly better sound quality and construction.

I've never owned the previous version of these headphones but I have a friend who owns them and I have listened to them side by side with the new version. To my ears they sound very similar, both have a great high end and excellent staging for a sealed headphone but they are both bass heavy which I am not particularly a fan of. I would say the aurvana 2 seems to be even more bass heavy than the original so those who like lots of bass will probably enjoy these headphones.

I do like the new removable cord and the fact that the cord is only on one side of the headphones. I'm not really a fan of the red plastic design element, the old version was very nondescript whereas the new model tries to be flashy but looks kind of cheesy in my opinion. I do think the new shape is more comfortable though and also seems to offer improved noise isolation compared to the original model.

Pros:
Nice high end and midrange, good separation and staging for a sealed headphone in this price range
detachable cord w/ built in mic
comfortable design
good noise isolation (recently used them on a plane trip and they worked well)

Cons:
Excessive bass
Cheap looking plastic design elements
Old version sounds just as good and is quite a bit cheaper
Notably better headphones available from sennheiser, beyer, denon, etc. for only slightly more

title: Good case.. Only fits Galaxy Tab 10.1 v3
text:
As other reviewers have mentioned, this case only fits the Galaxy Tab 3 10.1, do not get it if you have an older galaxy 10.1 because it won't fit.. the galaxy 3 is quite a bit smaller than the older models due to thinner outer bezel around the 10.1" touch surface.

This case works well and fits our Galaxy 3 perfectly. I like how it has three different configurations and in one of them you can slightly adjust the screen angle, its more useful than the 'tri-fold' style of case I have on my galaxy note tablet.

title: Works good, no issues so far.
text:
I have a lot of TP-link network products, including several USB adapters from this series and I find they can be hit-or-miss.. but this one has been working well so far. The small size is nice for use in an older laptop and the signal strength is pretty good despite the lack of external antenna.

I had lots of driver issues and connection drop-outs with the older WN722N adapter, but so far I have had no issues with WN823N or WN822N (the larger version of this adapter with dual antennas) so I would recommend them if you don't need dual band/5GHz support and are looking for a cheap but effective wireless adapter.

title: Nice mount, easy to install
text:
This is a nice mount if you want a simple no-frills, low-profile mount. No tilt, swivel or articulation but its easy to install and doesn't require using lag bolts.

The packaging claimed it was so easy to install you could do it in 10 minutes.. while took me longer than 10 minutes, it was definitely much easier to install than other flat panel mounts I have installed in the past. I also like how easy it is to take the TV off the mount when the need arises.

The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because the included drywall anchors are not very good. I was using this for a 32inch TV and there were no studs in the location where we wanted to mount it so I attempted to install it with the included drywall anchors. They did not have a very secure hold in the wall though, one of them started coming out of the drywall after I set the TV on the mount, and then I was able to pull that anchor out of the drywall with my bare hands.. so I ended up patching the drywall and then using some better drywall anchors which I already had on hand.

title: Airy, open sound in a sealed design, very nice..
text:
I bought these primarily to use as studio monitors. I have or have had a number of high end cans over the years, Grado, Beyerdynamic, Sennheiser, Etymotic Research, etc.. however for recording purposes I have always preferred my AudioTechnica ATH-M40 due to their sealed design and extremely neutral response compared to most of the aforementioned cans which 'color' the sound in one way or another.

I've had the M40 monitors since they first came out in the early 90's and they were really starting to fall apart so I decided to look for a replacement. I was somewhat surprised by all of the praise for these Denon cans considering that last time I paid attention to the headphone scene Denon wasn't even making headphones. However, after looking at the response curves and reading all the glowing reviews from knowledgeable users on these and the D5000 series I decided to give these a shot as my new studio monitors.

Overall, I would say they live up to the hype. These are definitely the best sealed cans I have heard, the highs are very accurate with an airy presence which feels like you are listening to an open headphone. They do not sound quite as neutral as the M40 to me, primarily due to the punchy low frequency response which can be a bit excessive with certain sources but that may soften up once they are properly broken in. Like any good headphone these will greatly benefit from quality amplification, but I must say they sound quite good unamped compared to some of my other high end cans like the Beyer DT990 which I consider useless without proper amplification.

These are also very comfortable although they could have made them a bit smaller, my head is somewhat small and they just barely fit me on the smallest setting.. all of my other headphones are too tight on the smallest setting so I am not sure what denon was thinking when they came up with the sizing for these.

title: Almost great..
text:
I really wanted to like this product, it has good build quality and nice aesthetics but it suffers from a few design flaws which make it unusable for me.

Pros:
* Very nice keyboard (I have not been a fan of many recent logitech keyboards but this one felt very nice to me, slightly mushy but with a subtle tactile response. The integrated wrist cushion is very comfortable)

* Extra powered USB Ports (Despite what some reviewers have written, the external power supply is *not* required to use the keyboard, it is only for the powered USB ports)

* Works with 17" laptops

* Compact and easily portable when folded up

* Overall build quality, aesthetics

Cons:
* Not height adjustable (The height is good on some tables but on my desk the screen stands about 4" above the height of my 24" monitors which is just too high, killing any ergonomic benefits. I returned it and got an XBrand XB-1001 which is adjustable)

* USB cable which connects to the computer is too short, it could barely reach the USB port at the front side of my laptop.

* No integrated audio jacks, front of stand blocks the onboard audio jacks on most laptops which now have the jacks on the front rather than the side, making it impossible to use external speakers.

title: Great cooler, must remove board to install in most cases
text:
This is a great cooler, I recently dropped in a Q6600 to replace my overclocked E6600. Everything went well and the Q6600 was able to hit 3.6ghz easy (400x9). The only problem was that the quad core put a lot more strain on the FSB than the dual core so the northbridge was getting too hot, which was causing some instability at high load.

Actually installing this thing did not lower my idle temps very much (maybe 2-3C, idling at 38C now, was around 40) but the temperature raise under load has been dramatically improved. With the stock NB heatsink (fanless Gigabyte 965p-ds3) my load temps would be in the high 50C range, now they are around 43C, only a slight raise above the idle temp! And the system is stable at 3.6ghz now thanks to this little beast =)

The only thing to watch out for when installing this is to be sure to tighten it to the motherboard enough. When I first installed it was not tight enough and it actually was worse than the stock heatsink. I then tightened it so the top of the screw almost pokes out of the top of the fastening nut and everything works perfectly.

title: nice keyboard with a few reservations
text:
I really like this keyboard, but there are a few qualms that keep me from using it as my primary keyboard. I bought it because I am a huge fan of the comfort curve 2000 keyboard, I am a programmer and thus very picky about my keyboards and I must say that the $10 Microsoft OEM Comfort Curve 2000 is the best keyboard I have ever used.

This keyboard has the same shape as the comfort curve, but the key action is not quite the same, both keyboards are 'low profile', like a laptop keyboard, but this keyboard feels much more like a laptop keyboard than its cheaper brother which has a softer action. Some may prefer this, I personally do not but I still like the feel of this keyboard anyways.

What I do not like about it is the odd placement of certain keys, for instance the 'windows key' is that big blue circle in the bottom center of the keyboard, it looks neat but is not very practical for those of us who heavily use win+key shortcuts. Also the home and end keys are above the backspace key, not sure what they were thinking there =)

The mouse and other functions work suprisingly well, overall I like this keyboard more than the diNovo edge or any other media keyboard i have used, so I will stick with the comfort curve 2000 on my desktop and use this one for HTPC.

title: This is the 24" you've been waiting for..
text:
This is the first high quality 24" I have seen for under $500. Yes, this is one of the new 24" TN (twisted neumatic) panels, but don't let that dissuade you. The 22" TN panels have gotten a bad rap due to their poor performance, most of them have issues with bad color banding and lots of light bleeding at the edges. I should know as I have owned several 22" TN panels (mostly Viewsonic VX2235WM).

This 24" TN panel is far and away superior to any previous TN panels I have seen, it is almost laughable how bad my old 22" TN panel looks up next to this one. I would challenge you to put this 24" TN up against any of the more expensive 24" IPS or S-PVA panels and see the difference for yourself, I doubt you will be able to tell which is which unless you are using a specialized image for gamut testing or you are a graphic designer with an extremely keen eye.

The only downsides that some people may find with this monitor compared to other (usually more expensive) 24" panels are: less inputs, no portrait mode. This monitor only has VGA and DVI(+hdcp) inputs, no component or hdmi, this is not really an issue if you are using it as a computer monitor but may turn off some people who wish to hook up other media devices. Also there is no portrait mode like the other 24" samsung 244T series; however, the stand on this monitor is still extremely high quality and height adjustable.

I would very highly recommend this LCD, better yet, I'd recommend 2 or 3. Why buy a 30" when you could have 3 of these for the same price?!

title: Great Tablet and cell phone mount that fits in pretty much any cup holder
text:
This cup holder Cell phone / tablet mount has worked great for me in several cars. As long as the cup holders are not too far back in the center console it works great. I have not had a problem with it wobbling around or anything like that. The swivel arm is one piece, and the other piece that connects to the swivel arm is the piece that actually holds the device. This holder comes with a tablet piece meant for holding tablets, and a cell phone piece meant for holding cell phones. The cell phone holder is not very easy to operate with one hand--you really need two. But, I mainly use this mount for my tablet anyways and that mount is easily used with one hand.

The mount is able to hold my Samsung Galaxy S2 tablet no problem. It also expands to its advertised diameter allowing it to fit in many cup holders, large and small.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have uploaded.

Pros:
*Cheap
*Easily installed
*Fits a lot of cup holders
*Fits a lot of phones and tablets

Cons:
*Cell phone holder is not easily used with one hand (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
If you need a call phone holder, you may want one that is better suited for one-hand use. Also, be aware of where your cup holder is in your car. If its too far back or something is above the cup holder, it may block this from being usable.

Overall: 4.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 5 stars

title: An excellent mount for mounting tablets or phones in car CD player
text:
This mount has been extremely useful in my vehicle. My CD player is right on the dash in a convenient spot to mount a device. This mount comes with the smaller metal plates made for cell phones and smaller devices. The large plate that is included with this mount works great on the back of my Samsung galaxy Tab. The 3M adhesive on these plates works fantastically. I have tried re-using these plates but I found that getting the plate off tends to bend it--even slightly. Once you bend these plates it does not re-use well. Included in the mount set, is a thin piece of plastic film that you can apply to your device in between the device and the plate. This makes it a lot easier to remove the plate from the device. This does a good job at making the re-use better.

The smaller plate works great on the back of my phones. I also use the plates inside of a phone case and they work great. The magnetic mount holds strong to phones and even tablets. I stuck the plate to the center of my tablet and I can stick the tablet onto the mount and utilize it without it falling off.

Dimensions of the plates and the mount can be seen in the photos I have uploaded.

Included:
-Large plate (with adhesive)
-Small plate (with adhesive)
-Plastic film plate/device separator
-Magnetic mount
-CD mount attachment

Pros:
*Holds a lot of weight (tablets)
*Easy to set up
*High quality adhesive
*Plenty of metal plates included

Cons:
*None

Additional Considerations:
You can get additional metal plates online. I also recommend all of scosche's mounts. Stuff is pretty interchangeable
.

title: Okay hardware with very bad software.
text:
I ended up using this colorimeter to profile and calibrate my monitor. Out of the box I was not very happy with the quality of the product. You end up getting pretty much zero instruction and no manual. I had to figure it out on my own just by looking at the product. Once that annoyance was over I got to experience how terrible the default software from datacolor is.

I looked to the reviews and decided I could make the most of this purchase by using other free calibration software. I used Argyll and DispCalGUI. If you simply download DispCalGUI it will prompt you automatically to download the Argyll color libraries.

You then go into Tools->Instrument->install Argyll CMS instrument drivers...

This will download the drivers you need to run the spyder 5.

After this calibration is possible. I calibrated and it seemed to do a decent job. All in all, the calibration software looked like it was powerful--certainly better than the default.

In the end, I returned the product. I wanted something that would work without me having to go the extra mile to get it to work. At this point, with all of the extra I had to do to calibrate I still don't know if it did a good job or not.

Dimensions can be seen in the photos I have attached.

Included is the unit only.

Pros:
*Calibrates
*Decent price

Cons:
*Terrible OEM software (-2 stars)
*Setup--while not hard--is not immediately obvious. A small pamphlet would have gone a long way (-1/2 a star)

Additional Considerations:
Go for hardware that has good software calibration tools. You cant beat the two working in synergy.

Overall: 2.5/5 stars (>=.5 rounds up, <.5 rounds down) => 3 stars

title: The best heavy duty photography bag I have used
text:
I use this backpack for work everyday to carry all of my camera gear and other work-related equipment. It has performed extremely well. It is easily one of my best investments this year. I have around 55-65lbs of equipment that I haul around everyday and this backpack has not budged at all when it comes to carrying the weight and carrying it in a way that prevents damaging my equipment. I have been using it for a solid 5 months now and it has no signs of wear at all.

This bags camera slot carries a D810 with a 70-200mm NIKOR lens attached to it. You cannot really fit anything much longer than that, which is understandable considering how long that setup is.

This bag includes a rain cover for the bag which is essential if you are going to be in rainy conditions.

The only negative I can see in this bag is the side straps are secured inside of thin plastic. Any real weight here would rip that plastic apart. I have been able to avoid breaking it, but if I put a real tripod there it would break I believe.

Pros:
*Carries 60+lbs of gear comfortably
*Water proof covering that can be put over the bag
*Not only carries the gear but it does it in a way that prevents damage

Cons:
*The side straps that hold a tripod are not durable (-1/2 star)

Additional Considerations:
You may want a separate tripod bag if you have a larger and heavier tripod. My tripod I have in the bag is small and light so it has not broken the side straps yet.

title: Extremely useful for a professional photographer who has to haul a lot of equipment
text:
This lens pen is just what I need in a compact, easy-to-carry product. I am a photographer who has to carry a lot of gear outside. Having something compact and light is essential.

One side is a brush to get rid of fine and large particles of material from the lens. The other side is to remove oils (e.g. fingerprints) and is made of a fine material that has a carbon dust cleaning solution embedded in it.

The first three to five uses can be a bit frustrating as this carbon dust is quite heavy and will actually leave a slight residue on the lens. In this case I just used the brush first, the carbon cleaner second, and then finished up with the brush again to remove any extra carbon. I had no artifacts in my photos at all. After the initial break-in period this lens pen performs flawlessly.

The pen is close to 4 inches long (without the brush extended) and about 3/4 inches wide. Its actually very compact and light. It has a tab on the cap to be able to secure it while its in a pocket, just like a regular pen. The brush is about an inch long and is used by extending it out of the end of the pen. It adds about an inch of length when extended. The carbon cleaner is covered by a cap which is screwed off in order to expose the cleaning surface. I wish there was a spot to put this cap while using the carbon cleaning side. Its the only long term con to this pen.

Pros:
*Light
*Compact
*Cleans lenses well
*Easy to carry in pocket
*Cheap

Cons:
*Carbon dust residue for first 3-5 uses.(-1/4 star)
*Cap has no place to be put on the pen while using it. (-1/4 star)

title: finicky and hurty
text:
I bought mine direct from Samsung and ultimately returned them. I found that I had to fiddle with them constantly to hit the sweet spot for the music to sound like it should instead of like I was listening through a tin can, and while fiddling with them the touch controls become an annoying hassle because you are trying to get the fit right and the music is turning on and off and pausing and skipping, etc, because you are touching them. The buds can't seem to differentiate at all between an actual hold/grip to manipulate them in your ears, and a tap as you would do to actually use a touch control feature.

Don't quote me on this because it's not like I counted every review that appeared male vs female, but I found that they hurt and I think it might be because they were designed by somewhat larger-eared males. I originally assumed the hurty issue was likely because they were designed by some 60 year old man engineer with huge ears (because ears grow our whole lives) and so they were only made to fit kind of older larger ears. I even wrote on my Samsung review that they should have made the fit for the age group of their customer. But now, reading these Amazon reviews, I am noticing that the people saying they fit great seem to mostly be male names and those saying they hurt seem to mostly be female-normative names, so I still think they were designed for larger ears, but maybe for males they will fit better - I truly don't know how different in size male vs female ears are though; it's just a random observation of these reviews of hurt vs feel great.

Bottom line, they hurt my ears and were too picky about being perfectly aligned in my ear. On the rare occasion I hit that sweet spot they sounded great and never felt like they were going to fall out. Too bad it took so much effort to find that spot.

title: Comparing home devices shows huge flaws in Alexa
text:
I've had my two Echo Dots for one year now. Now, a year later, Google Home has really come forward by leaps and bounds while Alexa has basically stayed exactly the same. For Android users, the easiest way to describe it is that the Alexa has become an iPhone vs. Google's Android. I think I am the norm in that there is almost no "Skill" I have use for with Alexa. Instead I ask things that are already built in features: weather, time, set alarm, add things to shopping list, and of course, control home devices like lights. However, ALL home devices can do those things just as easily and intuitively as Alexa does, so to see if you are getting the best device you need to compare other features:

Asking a question - Google wins hands down. Google uses... Google, to get your answer. Alexa uses Bing I think, nuff said. Most of the time the response from my Dot is "I'm sorry, I don't know that" and if it does "know", it is giving an answer to something I'm not truly asking. For example, I asked it what movies were playing on FOX tonight and the response was "I'm still learning about fox. Ask me a fox fact so I can learn more about them." Many times it even just answers to search the internet. Well, if I have to search the internet then I want to use Google to do it and there is no way to set your search engine. Essentially every time it tells me to search the internet, what I hear in my mind is "Use Google" - yeah, I think I just might, Amazon.

"Skills" apps - all but useless for every day life. Skills I can see some possibility of using are the reading a bedtime story if you have kids, or asking Alexa to play a game. But for adult life and for truly being a life/home assistant to you, none of the Skills compare at all to the platform that Google already has in place from decades of being an internet powerhouse. Example: finding your phone. This is a pretty common issue that I think it's reasonable to assume any of these home assist devices should be able to tackle easily. For Alexa you must download a "Skill" (there are a few to choose from) and register your phone number to that app. The major flaws with Alexa doing this are: 1. you need to first tell Alexa to open and use the skill with precise wording for it to work (i.e. "Alexa find my phone" won't work. "Alexa have Tracker find my phone" won't work. "Alexa open the Tracker app. Alexa have Tracker find my phone" won't work. "Alexa open the Tracker app. Alexa ask the Tracker app to find my phone" works). 2. if your ringer is off there is no ability to turn it on for the purpose of finding the phone. Essentially you'd be better off to add "me" to contacts with your own number and just tell Alexa "call me" because that is all you are getting with Alexa's "Skills", it's easier to just do that, and it only has the same flaw of not ringing if ringer is off. In comparison, with Google you download nothing, simply say "Google find my phone", and viola, your phone will ring whether the ringer is on or not. Google also has "Maps" which is huge. "Maps" gives you locations, hours of operation, can list like-businesses, tell you how to get somewhere and how long it will take you, and even tell you which buses to take if you have public transit in your area, etc. Alexa can only utilize Yelp and if a business isn't on Yelp then Alexa has no access to even the very basic info Yelp supplies (hours).

There's one 'Pro' to Echo over any other home device, and that is as it relates to other Amazon devices. Like Google, Amazon is also an internet powerhouse in it's own way. Having a Prime membership is the norm rather than the exception in most households, and obviously that means asking Echo to order something or play a Prime movie or Prime music is going to be smooth and easy with the Echo. Also, where Amazon still leads the pack is with it's Fire Stick, and again, obviously, Echo is going to be well integrated with that device, while other Home Assistants aren't given that level of access to integrate as well. So that's why I give it 2 stars - because I can't use my FireStick AS EASILY if I owned something other than an Echo. But I can still use the remote so that ability is def not worth more than two stars, especially when Google has the ability to take away access to things like YouTube (which it did) from Amazon in retaliation for being denied access to things like FireStick integration into it's own device.

Bottom line, Echo/Alexa seems great until you see how much better the later competitors to the market have improved on the user experience and are continuing to improve by leaps and bounds with each new update, while Amazon rests on 'we were the first'. Or, in other words, don't fall for yet another same ol' iPhone that is introducing features Android users have had for at least five years when instead you could just buy the Android and have the newest and best features right now.

title: Not worth the cost
text:
Got this on Amazon Lightning Deal for $50 but it's just not worth that much, IMO, so I'll be returning it. I do live on the bottom floor of a 3-story apartment building that's built into a hill (so 2 stories on the other side), with a patch of pine trees in front of me, so I fully understand that there are many hurdles for my particular set up. However, I also live in a major city, not 30 miles from all the broadcast towers, and while this antenna can pick up those channels, it's incredibly inconsistent at holding the signal. Pictures do a slight pixelation maybe every five minutes or so; nothing major, but enough to be annoying, and so I don't think this particular antenna is worth fifty bucks - I feel like I could get that same level of "service" from a cheap-y model. I also am using the amplifier.

As far as decor - it's non-obtrusive, and has a long cable so finding good placement for best reception is pretty easy.

My mom snagged one of the Amazon-version ones for $25 a few hours later in the Lightning Deals. I could see paying $25 for this, simply because it's less gaudy than rabbit ears, but not because I believe you're getting anything more reception-wise.

title: Doesn't last long. Dies within a year and a half. Nothing but a disappointment
text:
I have had this laptop / notebook for almost a year and a half. At first it was fun to work with but alas, that didn't last long. This HP laptop works when it wants to. Has only two USB ports that became wobbly quick. No I wasn't rough with them. Had one constantly plugged into a USB hub because this is what you do when you have only two USB ports to work with. The other one was used for an external DVD tray when needed for lack of internal one. Yes an HP laptop in this price range lacks an internal DVD tray, a back-lit keyboard and a user-serviceable battery. I've always kept this notebook indoors only, was extremely gentle with all the ports and am baffled as to why they became so loose and wobbly so quick.

The lack of DVD tray is probably the price to pay for the laptop being so slim. When I reset Windows 10, had to hook up an external tray to reinstall some programs lost in the process of reset, and considering the wobbly ports, it was a huge pain. I honestly thought that the USB port will break loose and just fall out. It however didn't happen but it was a close call.

At some point this laptop started having blackout episodes when the screen goes dark for no reason and without warning. I googled and appears this is a known issue because a solution was posted. You basically have to press the power button, hold on to it for a while, then let go and repeat. Once you notice a glimpse of life on the screen, let go of the button, and the laptop will come to. This happened quite a few times and was very disappointing and frustrating. Why oh why.

It eventually had the final blackout and didn't come out of it. My HP laptop is dead and the shop tells me that the hard drive quit and there's no way to bring it back to life. Honestly, I don't want to invest in yet another hard drive just to see the laptop go kaput. This apparently is a hardware problem. By comparison, one of my older laptops with an old-fashioned user-removable battery, back-lit keyboard, built-in DVD tray and multiple stable USB ports is still going strong for a few years to date. This HP one has lasted only about a year and a half. The warranty was up in June. Oh well.

Bottom line, I am very disappointed in this HP laptop and in the brand in general. Will never buy anything of this brand and don't recommend. There are better choices.

title: Easy to use and reliable
text:
When my old card reader bit the dust rendering me unable to transfer images from my digital camera and onto my computer, this has sent me on a quest for a new one. My requirements were portability and ease of use. Since I already owned the best USB hub in the world made by Plugable that lasts for what seems forever, I decided to purchase a new card reader of the same brand. I am very glad that I have made this choice.

My new bright green Plugable multi-card reader arrived shortly and was promptly put to use. It's a well built gadget; the only con is that it has a fairly short cord so it might not be useful in some setups; however it did just fine in mine. The cord is 4 inches long and the USB plug going into the port is about one inch long, so it's best used on the desktop surface. It does require the included external power cord. Rated as a SuperSpeed USB 3.0, it's backwards compatible with 2.0 as well. This card reader supports Micro SD, SD, SDHC, SDXC, MMC, MS, and MSXC card formats; all the corresponding cards slots are clearly marked which eliminates guesswork. Its bright green top makes it easy to be spotted, especially on the darker shade desk surfaces like mine. The card inserts easily and smoothly.

It works wonders; once a card is inserted, it is being read promptly and then formatted quickly, a telltale sign of a great functioning card reader. I keep it plugged in the USB port of the hub at all times. I can wholeheartedly recommend the Plugable multi-card reader; buy it, you won't regret it.

title: Created a projector room for our house. Everything works ...
text:

2022 Update: we’ve had this projector for 8 years now and we’ve gotten our moneys worth. For the past year it’s been showing signs of age, and now the screen doesn’t roll up all the way (seems to be a manual setting that affects where the screen stops). We can fix it by adjusting the setting with an Allen wrench, but it only lasts for 1-2 uses before basically being useless again. But for 7-8 years of life, we’re still happy with the purchase given how inexpensive it was originally. I’d buy it again to replace if it were still sold.

title: Great idea!
text:
I never new this existed and wish I would have found it sooner. I use it at work and love it. The sync is definately the way to go since it's the only one they make that you can save notes. The writing is light, but the screen is pressure sensitive so you just have to push harder or writing slower works too, but it shows up just fine for me at work. no complaints there. The real magic is when I sync my notes via Bluetooth to my phone/Evernote/Dropbox even, and I can immediately pull up the PDF at work and reference them. Plus if you have OCR in Adobe, Evernote, or another program that does the work, you can convert your notes PDF to a word document making it searchable and editable. I haven't found an OCR that's free yet, but it's not too expensive through adobe or Evernote. A small price to pay for the added functionality.

Only a few things would make this even better than it already is. It would be nice to be able to selectively delete parts of your notes, or erase mistakes (which hasn't been a real issue for me yet, I just cross out the mistake and rewrite it). And, you can edit notes on the computer with OCR, but it would be nice to be able to pull up old notes on the board to correct them or add to them on the board.

All in all I still love this thing and think it was well worth the money. Since I purchased it knowing it's capabilities and limitations there is no way to be disappointed with this. I love it!

Cons:

title: Great docking station for Dell Latitude 5520 Win 10
text:
This has been a great addition to my Work from Home setup. My whole desk now works with a single USB-C cable. Instructions say it doesn't work with a USB extension cable, but I have a 5ft cable that is working fine over. My setup: 2021 Dell Latitude 5520 w/ Windows 10 Pro, connected via one cable to the following:
two 24" 1080p monitors connected via HDMI (triple screen setup with laptop screen)
Logitech HD webcam
Ethernet, tested at full 1 Gbps
Logitech unifying receiver for keyboard and mouse
USB-C power passed through docking station
Occasional (micro)SD cards

I did have one hiccup where a couple devices weren't being recognized over the USB-C extension cable when I first plugged it in. I removed it, turned the connector over and plugged it back in and EVERYTHING started working perfectly. Since then, it doesn't seem to matter which way I plug it in. I think I just didn't wait long enough for Windows to sort out the device/drivers the first time. If you run into issues, act like you're talking to Dell tech support and disconnect/reconnect until it starts working.

title: Buyer BEWARE---G13 Gameboard--after 6 months it gets worse.
text:
Pros:
-Easily programmed.
-Multiple game memory.
-Many, many keys = many, many programming options.
-Digital readout looks good and lets you know exactly what download you are using without reopening Logitech window.

Cons:
-Flat palm positioning is not very comfortable for gaming (and can't be adjusted). My hand tends to cramp due to its bad ergonomics when playing FPS games more than an hour.
-Keypad ergonomics are badly thought out. Key rows are positioned bowing UPWARDS (away from your fingers) instead of downwards, making quick initiation of pinky and index finger keys more difficult.
-G13 is a bit large and can't easily be slid aside when not gaming (not a big deal to me, but somewhat inconvenient).
-Friends tell me that Razer and Logitech downloads interfere with one another, so if you have a Razer mouse or keyboard this may interfere with your use of either.
-Keys are a bit too close together without easily discernible gaps in between. This too often causes my thick fingers to strike 2 keys simultaneously.
-Overpriced for what it offers.

Overall:
Programming=excellent. Ergonomics=horrible.
For me, the keypad layout and palm rest do not work together. They look like they should, but they simply do not. The device concept is quite good, but the ergonomics make it just too difficult to consistently access and manipulate keys for real-time gaming. Very disappointing to me because with Logitech's years of experience in peripherals this should put Nostromo to shame---it simply doesn't because of the badly positioned keys and faulty wrist/palm rest ergonomics.

Follow-up:
-Down from 2 to only 1 Star, and it should be ZERO Stars. This thing is good only for a paperweight to remind me of my wasted time and wasted money.
-6 months down the road and, while gaming, each and every one of my gaming profiles (I have 3) will spontaneously reset to the default profile on their own or, even worse, all the G-keys become unresponsive.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the LCD screen lights up, but no profiles appear, not even default, and no keys respond.
-Sometimes on computer start-up the unit never powers on.
-Logitech's updates do not fix the problem(s). I've deleted the entire gaming software setup and performed reinstalls ad nauseum with no permanent positive result. What's even worse is this: it acts fine for a bit after a reinstall, so you think you've corrected it, then it starts screwing up ALL OVER AGAIN.
-BIOS adjustments do not fix the problems.
-USB ports and motherboard are completely functional throughout my gaming (I've tested/monitored them as I play) and they perform perfectly as the gamepad and/or its software crashes on its own.
-It's only 6 months old, and 2 keys are mechanically non-functional (G20 and the button below the joystick). My Belkin Nostromo n52 lasted for almost 8 YEARS of gaming with no problems whatsoever, and I was gaming three times as much back then. I'd grown used to the G13 so I was willing to overlook the buttons, or blame them on myself, and work around this issue, but when the software/electrical issues began occurring quite regularly I'd run out of patience.
-Forums addressing these (as well as other) issues have found no answers or solutions, only make-shift quick-fixes.
-Numerous forums also share the information that this is happening across a variety and multitude of different computer systems/set-ups.
-Many other owners, myself included, have had additional problems with the G13 when it is used after a computer has hibernated/slept, but we all learned to live with this as one of its quirks. We now see this as an indicator of its many issues.
-Many other owners have said that the problems began occurring after 3 or more months use (I suspect that in my case this took longer as it is only occasionally used for gaming).
-Logitech customer support has denied any fault in these matters and still maintains that their pruduct and programming is NOT the cause of any of these problems, so their help line has been useless. Meanwhile, the price plummets as word spreads.
-Only thing that works for any of us is to constantly disconnect gamepad from its current USB port, reconnect it, and computer may recognize it...but this does NOT always work...sometimes requires reboot as well...and sometimes this doesn't work either...so gamepad is inoperative until it decides to come back on a reconnection or restart. This is a band-aid at best. I refuse to do this to my system over and over.

This thing is getting returned. I advise you to save your money and time by buying some other manufacturer's product.

title: Colossal Fraud
text:
A small, cloudy, dark, grey SPOT appeared last week in the upper right corner of the screen. (About the size of a silver dollar pancake.) Two months after the warranty expired. (I bought it in July of 2020, it’s a year warranty.)

This TV has been sitting in the same place since it arrived. Aside from my using a screen cleaner to occasionally wipe a bit of dust off, nobody has touched it - literally. Its never been moved. Which means this little dark grey cloudy spot just appeared spontaneously in the screen for no apparent reason. Except, perhaps, by design.

That’s really the only thing I can think of for this incredibly convenient/inconvenient timing: Westinghouse has DESIGNED this television to start failing after a year of being used. And voila, so it has. Fourteen months later, to be precise. I’d call that fraud.

I wrote the seller about this… And I got a short note back informing me that the warranty has expired. I’m very aware the warranty expired. I mentioned that in the letter I wrote. So, not only not helpful - didn’t even bother to READ the letter, because all they had to do was check the purchase date and they knew they didn’t HAVE to pay any attention to me.

I repeat: This problem just HAPPENED to pop up TWO MONTHS after the warranty expired. How very convenient for the seller/manufacturer that it should occur with such perfect timing, such that they are no longer responsible for fixing it, and my $350+ purchase is now worthless.

What a colossal joke. A television of such low quality that it breaks after FOURTEEN MONTHS.

title: Get what you pay for, DIDNT LAST LONG!!!!
text: Purchased this one AUG2020....Fast forward to Feb2022 and IS DEAD!!!! I bought this SSD specifically for Steam for Gaming. The loading was MUCH slower then other SSD's I had but I didn't mind.... as time progressed it kept getting slower and slower... until today it was completely dead and the computer would not even detect it. I tried everything to make sure it wasn't another issue and its definitely  gone. I purchased one 500GB(system) and one 1TB (gaming). Again the 1TB is completely dead and the 500 GB takes approximately 3mins to load up windows, I'm sure its probably getting ready to die also. Now in comparison to other SSD's I have... I purchased a WD Green SSD 240GB about 4+ years ago and it still working like the first day I bought it. I recommend going with a better known brand like Crucial/Samsung/Kingston or ScanDisk that will last for much longer and maintain the performance over time.
