text: Of course, my grandson lost the original charger for his Fitbit so having 3 on hand was needed.  The other two are kept as back up.

title: Five Stars
text: Yay for my Firestick! And getting this protection is just what I needed.

title: Love it! Getting rid of cable was the best ...
text: Love it! Getting rid of cable was the best decision ever. I went to several stores looking for a firestick and found it on Amazon. Setting it up was a breeze.

title: Bad product
text:
This was the downgraded version of the 1st Firestick I bought that stopped working.
This one has stopped working. Very frustrating

title: Questionable purchase
text: after 9 months both Firesticks will not work, no matter what we do.

title: maybe
text: does not pick up NBC, as antennas go, it is good

title: Handy set
text: A useful set to have on hand, especially if someone forgets/needs a charging cable. It's easy to use the adapters and they all fit snuggly in the case, so they don't fall out if your not stationary. They also fit snuggly on the cable, so there shouldn't be any power/data blink outs.

title: Holds my tab S8+ well and stays stable
text: It's a tablet sized version of a common phone holder design. It's built strong enough to hold a 12in tablet with a rugged case. The base is large enough to stay stable on a comforter. I wish the little pop-out holders are longer to compensate for my case's built in handle.

title: Great for vid conferencing
text:
These are tuned for vocal range, so they're great for talking to people (vid call, gaming, etc), listening to podcasts or audiobooks, and listening to TV/movie audio. The highs are also pretty clear. There is no bass, at all; even with a bass boosting app running, I'm barely hearing those low notes.
Connecting to two devices was easy and switching between them is simple.
The noise cancelling works great and it's very effective.

title: Basic MP3 player
text:
The device is very small and very light, the closest thing I can think to compare it to is a medium sized disposable vape. Battery life is pretty good and I didn't have any trouble running various TF cards.
Playing MP3s worked fine, though it doesn't support playlists. It plays files in order of when they were copied to the card, so you'll have to tediously copy any folders that need to stay in order one at a time.
I really wish they'd have a separate audiobook app from the music player just for convenience.
Video support is a joke - things have to be encoded at thumbnail res. The ebook reader is also iffy - out of around 10k ebooks in varying formats, it only recognizes 13 of the hundreds of text files. The FM won't even try to transmit over bluetooth - when the transmitter is in the same room, I shouldn't need the headphone wires for an extended antenna. Navigation is a bit irritating - instead of a D-pad, the left and right buttons are the only ones that navigate, the center button is enter, and the bottom one is back. There's no on-board memory, the storage card is it's only storage.
The other tools seem to work well.

title: So cool! (If a bit chunky)
text:
I've been wanting something to help organize all of my little electronic toys for a while and this fits the bill very nearly perfectly. The organizational design is awesome with tons of ways to hold things in place and the accordion/full open is a big plus. Several specialty mics, an anemometer, a point-n-click thermometer, a laser tape measure, several bulky cords, and a usb-c hub are fitting in it nicely, with some room to spare. I have noticed, I have to be conscious of where I'm adding things so that it will all "fit" together when zipped shut.
The only down-side I've seen is that there is nothing besides as handle for attaching it to the outside of a laptop bag/backpack. I was able to use velcro straps around the handle to affix it to my bag, though, so I'm happy with the turnout.

title: Works great for a 10in tab
text:
I'm using this to hold a generic 10in tab and it is doing so wonderfully. There's no problem with tipping - the base is huge and heavy. All features work great, including the telescoping/tilting extension, and rotating from landscape to portrait is a breeze.
Although the base is pretty large, it's mostly flat, so a good place to place things. It also has a slight lip to the edge, so you can put change or roll-y things on it and they'll stay put.

title: Does what it says on the box
text:
I've never had one of these, so I can't say if it's any better or worse than average.
It was very easy to connect (both physically and the BT) and I didn't notice any lag in audio, though to be fair, I've never noticed lag connecting my speaker directly to the Google TV.
I like that it has a battery so that I can use it as a car adapter if the car adapter fries. It would be really cool if there were separate Tx/Rx toggles for the SPDIF and the 3.5mm so that it could be used to convert SPDIF /to or from/ 3.5mm.

title: Works great on 2.4GHz
text:
I'm using this mouse now and I'm quite happy with it. I have a desk mat and the mouse reads it perfectly. The different DPI settings work well and are easy to switch between. All of the buttons/wheel on the mouse work great.
It's a bit small (for travel) but doesn't feel small when using it. There's a slot in the base for the 2.4ghz receiver.
In general, I find it to be an attractive mouse without being flashy. I haven't been using it long enough to run out the battery, but if charge time is any indication, it should last a while.

title: TWS doesn't connect
text:
The biggest thing is that these are meant to be true wireless stereo headphones, and they're not - all the manual says is that they will automatically connect to each other after turning on and before connecting to a phone; I left them in TWS pairing mode for several minutes without them connecting.
I was able to connect to them as two separate devices and got mono sound through both simultaneously. The sound quality wasn't as bad as I've heard on cheap headphones, but it was in the lower 20% - they're basically just very small (and cheap) speakers that sit above the ear canal. There is no bass, and mids/treble are a bit flat. They also do not get very loud due to the design. I will say that I like the concept of having them fit into the top part of the ear and project down and into the canal, but the execution was poorly done.
If I wanted to run dual-output every time I use them, I think they would work well for audiobooks and podcasts, as the vocal range are the frequencies the headphones favor most, and I typically don't feel the need to crank the volume on my audiobooks.

title: Loud and clear, decent bass
text:
I test all of my speakers with a decibel meter placed 6ft away and mounted to a wall; at max volume, I was getting 90dB from lyrics and melody, with it peaking up to 110dB on bass hits.
Sound quality is good, even up to max volume. Battery life is decent for the overall size of the speaker and sound output - I test batteries by running it on constant TV audio and this speaker lasts just about 18hrs on medium volume. The light effects are bright and attractive and easy to cycle through.

title: Comfy, good mids and highs
text:
I'm wearing these now and they're quite comfortable to wear for extended periods. Connection was easy. I wish they had more control buttons instead of just the one. The charging port is also in an odd place (presumably to keep people from charging while wearing) (it's on the left ear-pod).
Sound quality is a little funky and I guess to be expected on a cheap pair of headphones: the biggest thing is that they don't reproduce bass really at all, I can feel the bass hits when the pod hits my ear, but the bass isn't making it to my eardrum; at highest volume there's a bit of distortion but they don't really get /that/ loud; otherwise, at low-medium levels and for treble and mids, the sound reproduction is excellent. I suspect I'm going to like these more for podcasts and audiobooks than music.
If you're not into really bass-y music, and you don't need substantial volume, these will probably be perfect for you.

title: Quite loud, superb highs, good bass
text:
My go-to test for speakers is to use a dB meter I have mounted on the wall about 6ft from me; for this speaker, I was getting mid-90dBs on lyrics and melody with peaks and hits reaching up to 115dB. Though I wasn't using a spectroscope, I could tell by ear that the treble speaker makes a massive difference compared to other midsize BT speakers. The sound is warmer than on my other 50-80W speakers, with excellent frequency response. Bass could hit harder to balance the highs, but it does thump pretty well.
The control board on the speaker is pretty cool - I like the analague volume wheels and the good amount of controls. I would've liked more LCD for TF card use, but if you've set up a playlist, you should be good going by position in que. I like that they included a mic for PA or karaoke - when it said included mic in the details I though it would be built in, lol.
The lights are especially pretty - unlike other speakers I've tested, this will do a rainbow effect, along with some other pretty effects, though a companion BT app with more options would've been 6-star territory. The strap is nice for carrying or "mounting" it from something, and the handles double as protectors for the diaphragms; however, I'm still left wanting a top-carry handle, I'll probably make something with velcro.

title: Awesome for Spoken Word
text:
I really like that these are more of ambient/background headphones. For certain situations, like when I'm around other humans and need to hear what's going on but still need a distraction from the crowd, these will actually be picked before I use my galaxy buds. That said, the sound quality can't even come close to comparing to in-ear, quality headphones. They're also much more noticeable when worn that in ear buds, so should discourage strangers trying to engage me in conversations, lol.
I first tested these with various types of music, including country, trance, and ambient. Most of the music I listened to sounded less warm and flatter than my phone speakers; the ambient sounded better than other genres, but still not as rich as it should have. Between being outside the ear, and the type of driver, these just don't have the frequency range needed for music.
I then switched to podcasts and audiobooks, and that's where these really excel - due to the narrower frequency range of voice, there isn't near as much being lost to the smallness of the drivers. I also suspect that the drivers/firmware are tuned for 85-250hz. I'm not a fan of communication verbally, but I imagine these would be excellent for phone calls.
I do want to note that my order details list my chosen color as black, the main pic shows white, and yet I got silver with a red band around the back of my head. I would've much preferred black, but these look nice, they're just more conspicuous that I wanted.

title: Good option for an outdoor mini-power strip
text:
It works great with velcro on the back and mounted to the wall. I have a couple usb blocks and a thin light plugged into it...the light blocks the plug above it and doesn't fit (facing up) in the above plug due to the prongs' different widths.
The main plug is secure and the cord is extra heavy duty. The plugs are spaced out (though could be more), but I really wish they had not used different size slots for the poles.
The switch is enclosed, solid, and works well.
I think the best use for this will be the next time I go camping - it'll make a great distribution hub at the power pole - I can easily plug in 4 extension cords w/o anything getting in the way, and I can use the velcro to keep it off the ground.

title: Poorly made
text:
I definitely do not recommend this - they're either poorly constructed or made with defective components.
I ordered one which had battery/circuitry issues - the screen doesn't work when charging, it overheats when charging, and the battery drains rapidly when not charging.
I contacted Amazon, told them I had a bad battery, and was sent a replacement. As soon as I put a charger to it, the screen failed permanently.
Amazon has a good (if annoying) return program, so if you really want this, you're not going to be out of luck. If you suspect the battery itself is bad, contact Amazon CS as you shouldn't mail something when you know it's hazardous.

title: Great little speaker
text:
Sound quality for the size is excellent and it gets decently loud. Battery life is really good running it for TV dialogue; music life isn't bad but it drains a lot faster. Accent lights are pretty, though I wish they had more options. TWS works, but there isn't a dedicated button for it.
My only complaint, which could be a benefit for some people, is that it turns itself off if nothing is played for 10-15mins, even if it's kept connected to a device.

title: Small and sounds great
text:
Sound quality for the size is excellent and it gets decently loud. Battery life is really good running it for TV dialogue; music life isn't bad but it drains a lot faster. Accent lights are pretty, though I wish they had more options. TWS works, but there isn't a dedicated button for it.
My only complaint, which could be a benefit for some people, is that it turns itself off if nothing is played for 10-15mins, even if it's kept connected to a device.

title: Mixed Results
text:
I ordered this for the higher wattage and on my primary phone, it does get quite loud; but on my Dex device, it's maxed out is equivalent to about 50% volume on a 10W speaker.
I used a dB meter that was about 6ft away with the speaker pointed towards the meter. At max volume on my main phone (fold3) and at 150% volume, I was getting a consistent mid-90s dB for melody and lyrics, with peaks up to 109dB. On my other device (Note 10+), also at 150%, it was pulling about 70 dB on TV dialogue. I did try testing it with a volume booster, and even with only 110% (on top of the 150%) it was beginning to distort.
I played the TV audio for about 16hrs at moderate and 8hrs on low, and it was reading as still having 70% battery. But after only a few hours of moderate-high volume music, that 70% was gone and it died.
The sound quality is quite good with a warm tone. The highs are clear and the bass is better than I expected for there not to be a dedicated bass cone.
Despite appearances, I think the best use for this will be background music - not too loud will keep it playing all day & night and it will provide a much cleaner and richer sound than a small speaker at similar volume.

title: Interesting device
text:
It does what it's sold to do very well. I've tested several types of ebooks (PDFs, epub, doc, txt), mp3 files of various quality, pics, and vids (avi, x264, and x265) - it read and ran everything well and smoothly.
Basically it's a low-end phone running an old distro of Android. It's super locked down and there's no internet access, so there's no updating and no adding of apps - this includes bluetooth tethering. That being said, a few of the apps are ones I've used for ages and (obv) I like them: specifically moon reader, the ebook reader - it really works well on this device. And I believe the video player is MX Player, also an old fav. Moving files via TF card was a bit of a pain, as the older version of android only supports up to 4GB at a time, but otherwise it moved everything without error. I tested the reader with several cards, from a generic 32gb to a samsung 512gb u3, and they all read well, so you can easily have a large library of media at hand. There's no cam or wifi; and there aren't any sensors, so it can't tell tilt, ambient light, etc. The screen is tiny but looks surprisingly good. The speaker is decently loud, but it def sounds like a phone speaker, still though, it's better than expected.
If you just want a simple media device with some neat features (FM works really well btw), this is great. I both would and wouldn't recommend this for kids - you can't add any educational apps (or games, lol), and they wouldn't be able to access things like their school portal or wiki; but if you only want your kid to have books, vids, and audio with a few tools (calc, calendar, alarm), this is right up your ally. Heads up though, they can swap out the TF card if they have a media collection you don't know about, and Moon Reader supports requiring passwords for opening the app.
If you want something you can do more with, I'd suggest foregoing the 50% off coupon and getting a burner phone at this device's list price. A burner probably won't work as smoothly (because it will have more hardware/software), but it'll have wifi and an app store and updates.
I plan to use this as an extra/backup media device. I'm one of those weird people that has a TF collection in my bag with tons of movies, tv, games, etc. I'm going to put one of those pockets on the back for credit cards, and use a TF card organizing card to hold my cards, so I'll have all my media together and with a device that can play them, in case my phone is AWOL or dead. IMO, after the coupon, it's worth the price as long as you know what you're getting.

title: Impressive!
text:
Sound quality is good with a nice resonance. It's pretty loud for 20W - I have a decibel meter 6ft away, and with my volume maxed out (not not using a booster) I was looking at a steady 90dB on lyrics with instrumental peaks pushing 110db.
The lights are attractive, fun, and pretty cool; the only thing that would make them better would be a companion app with more customization. It does have quite a few modes built in and it's not too hard to find one that fits the ambience.
Battery life is really good - I've gotten about 24hrs of continuous playback of TV show audio (ST - TNG) with the volume at moderate ⅔s of the time and low the rest. The lights were off for the battery test (they'll considerably lower that time frame).
I really like the vertical form factor, it just looks better than standing a horizontal speaker on it's end.
I can't review this without saying - hopestar runner, lol.

title: Wow, I'm thoroughly impressed
text:
Amazon won't let me use the appropriate expletives to describe this, but it is seriously over built.
My highest draw device is 65W, and this handles it with ease, unfortunately I have no way to test the 240W raiting (does anything pull or push that much power on pd yet?).
What really took me by surprise and I find quite impressive is that this cable's steel braided sheath is as robust as the ones on brake lines. It's still flexible and rolls up nicely. The bricks on the plugs are huge, but the plug is long enough to reach through my phone and tablet cases.
Because of the robustness, I'm likely going to integrate it into my hiking vest - I have a 30Ah battery on my back. Not only will it provide full power to my phone, but it can be used as a weapon in an emergency.

title: A very nice combo light
text:
I like this for most times when I don't want a pocket supernova and all I need is to not trip.
The low setting is perfect for navigating a sleeping house or campsite, the high setting isn't crazy bright but it's good for near-and-bright illumination.
The FM radio works pretty well but didn't get very loud. The emergency siren is fairly quiet, especially being that it's a siren.

title: Excellent overnight bag
text:
I just use this this weekend and it worked really well.
I like the more luggage-y shape/design compared to typical laptop backpacks. It's great for organizing and there's lots of space.
The designers took organizing to the extreme and I love it! There're so many pockets and pouches inside compartments. This would be especially nice if you need to carry & organize paperwork - lots of large sections.
Materials and construction look and feel of good quality and I'm hoping this will last years. My only complaint is that wearing it in one shoulder is quite difficult - it tends to slide like Teflon on synthetic or cotton shirts.

title: Clear/strong FM transmission
text:
This defaulted to 88.8, and I was lazy and just bumped it up to 88.9, it's not the clearest channel, but it's as open as I have where I live. I'd hazard to guess the FM antenna is in the wire as this comes through much better and cleaner than my transmitters that are built into the plug. Bluetooth pairing was standard and quick. The QC outlet powers my 15w qi charger well.
Having a secondary display to my phone is fun, but I really wish I could customize the GUI. The color selection of the wheel is simple with the standard 7 options + off; it doesn't dim or give the option to, which kinda sucks at night. Onboard EQ is simple but a nifty feature.
I'm not counting it against them as they do explicitly state it's for mounting on a vent, but I had hoped the attachment on the device-side would be removable so that I could flush mount this, but there is a bracket built into the back of the device that attaches to the vent clip. I intend to shave off the bracket, but want to note this.

title: Small with lots of watts
text:
The unit is smaller than I was expecting and it's surprisingly dense/heavy and it's solid - there's no wiggle or things rattling inside.
It sounds like every bit of a 7w speaker. Maxed out with a volume meter sitting about 6ft away, I was steadily getting 90dB with peaks up to 110dB.
Sound quality is surprisingly good, even maxed out; of course with it being so tiny, there's basically no bass.
I'm not sure I'll use this for music very much, but it makes an excellent speaker for my bedroom TV - I can place it close enough that I can keep the volume down, being small lets it be placed just about anywhere, and the battery life is pretty good (I'm going on 8hrs of moderate volume).
I have no intention of using the TF slot, so it wasn't tested.

title: Cut to fit a generic tab and I'm super happy
text:
I recently picked up a cheap/generic 10" tab, but I've become spoiled having these Paperfeel brand protectors on all my other devices (Samsung flagships).
It was very easy to cut to fit using a sharp razor - it didn't turn out perfect, but for a custom resize I'm pretty happy.
The protector itself is very attractive and feels so much better on my fingers than bare glass. Maybe just because it's different, but matte screens look awesome, and no more black mirror effect. There's no loss in picture quality and I never have problems with it not reading my taps/slides. The generic tab doesn't have fingerprint or a stylus, but I know from my other devices that this brand of protector is compatible with both.

text:

title: Heavy duty bracket - not recommended for off-brand use
text:
Not recommended for off-brand use - I purchased these for non-nest cameras and my cameras are just slightly too wide for these to fit properly. Despite not working for the camera's I'm using at the moment, I'm sure they'll be great mounts for future cams.
The construction is top-notch - the bracket itself is a thick aluminum with what appears to be a thick coat of paint. The pivots and hardware are all smooth and move freely while mainting enough pressure to not move on their own.

title: I'm impressed for the price
text:
I've been playing with this a few days now and I'm liking it as an auxiliary tablet. For comparison, I also have an 8yo Samsung Note Pro with similar specs, running an older version of android. This tablet is a bit slower but entirely capable.
I copied the apps and some settings from my note pro, and it's handling the load just fine (about 150 apps, half a dozen, or so, run continuously in the background). I have noticed I need to stay on top of closing out apps I'm finished with or it gets laggy. I've run the following services on it, some are a bit slow but they will work - YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, Paramount+, ESPN, curiosity stream, frndly, and a handful of free streamers. I've also had good luck with Spotify, audible, Kindle, read era, and a few other media apps. Although it's a few versions behind, I was able to install all but 1 or 2 of the apps I tried adding.
The battery life is phenomenal - it's a large battery and I haven't seen the tab use more than 1,000mA at any given time. It charges on standard 5v - it doesn't support QC or PD. The USB-c port supports basic otg card readers, but I couldn't get it to work with a USB hub.
The screen is adequate. Resolution is a bit low but color and brightness are good. The bezel is huge. I wasn't expecting top-tier glass, but the plastic they used scratches super easy. I ordered some screen protectors, that will need to be custom cut.
I had prepared an SD card on my main phone, and despite it being readable on the phone, I was forced to format it on the tablet and re-add the content; it does work well now though.
TL;DR - it's a nice, functional tablet that is well worth the price tag. Just keep in mind that low price when using it.

title: Really liking this!
text:
I use a tablet for my TV and this stand is great for holding my tablet and letting me move it around.
The medium shelf can be flipped for things larger than it is. The top tray is sturdy and fairly spacious and makes a great table. The mini add-on tray is handy but always seems to be sticking out too far no matter where I put it.
Tripod base is sturdy and the wheels work well on carpet.
Assembly is super simple and everything fits together tightly and securely.
Foam pad seems like a liability - projectors are typically top and side vented, but anything else would have it's vents blocked, and I wouldn't want to use it with a projector anyways just to err on the side of caution.

title: Affordable and works great
text:
The picture quality and transmission are good. I really like that the mounting point is a standard (¼-20) bolt, it made installation easier - the included bracket mounts nearly flush, but the distance from the wooden part of the window box to the glass is longer than the camera. I was able to use a mount from a different kit to add the extra distance.
I probably would have mounted it upside down anyway, but it doesn't tilt down more than a few degrees, so if you sit it on a shelf or cabinet, it won't be able to look down.
FYI: 2k = Full HD (1920x1080), it's no better res than any other full hd cam.

title: Great device for the price!
text:

title: Sound great, interesting design
text:
For buds that sit outside of the ear canal, these sound really good. Frequency range seems superb, bass response is decent for earbuds.
I haven't had anything with a cable braided quite in this manner, but they don't tangle at all. The drivers disconnect from the wires and the plug is swappable. The swappable plugs are really cool for international use, but I don't understand why the drivers aren't permanently attached.

title: Works effortlessly and error free
text:
I tested all of the features*, and it works as expected. LAN connected easily and HDMI, USB, and audio were automatic. The card readers performed better than expected as it will read both slots simultaneously (all hubs I've had previously would only read one or the other). Having USB-c data on board is very nice.
*The only exception is VGA, as I don't have anything with that port.

title: Looks great, sounds good
text:
This matches my turn-table almost perfectly and looks great with it.
The sound quality is good, but there was a noticeable drop in quality when I connected it to my TV by BT - the OEM Vizio built-in speakers shouldn't be better than a speaker this size.
BT connected easily to my Google TV and FM reception is phenomenal.
The remote is a pain as the only display is the analogue dial (which isn't even backlit), so there's no visual confirmation of changes made or indication as to what you've selected via the remote.

title: Tons of features in a small package
text:
I've mainly been using this with an FM transmitter with my TV - quality is good and I love that it's stereo.
The FM scan/auto-program works pretty well - it picked up all the strong stations as well as a few on the edge of reception. I really like that the battery is swappable; I have a lot of 18650 devices and cells, so when I'm on the go I can just swap the battery.
TF playback and recording both work well, though I haven't used either more than testing. Aux-in option is really cool, but I don't have a 3.5mm to usb-c to test it. The flashlight is decently bright and nicely focused.
One cool feature that I rarely see is the ability to punch in stations directly using the number pad.
The only thing I'm not crazy about is that it boots up to TF playback instead of last used mode.

title: Excellent intercom
text:
My elderly mother lives with me due to her infirmities. Using these little guys is so much easier than shouting across the house to each other. Quality is good on low power across a medium house. Despite the EM soup we live in, there's very little distortion or quality loss.
All of the features seem to work well while I was testing them. Unfortunately vox picks up loud background noises too (TV, dog barking, etc), but PTT works just fine. Battery life seems pretty good, but we keep them on charge when not carrying them around.
The size is perfect, I left the clips off as it's just easier to through it in a pocket it's so slim.

title: Great mini-hub
text:
HDMI and USB both connected to my phone immediately and worked fine. Supplied power needs to be PD, I couldn't get it to work on standard USB power, but works fine on PD.
I really like the super small form factor - it's significantly smaller than the average USB c hub.

title: Great little radio in a small package
text:
Sound quality is better than any of my other radios listening to my FM transmitter. It also has reasonable to good reception of local stations. Speaking of, the preset option is nice, though interesting that it came pre-programed - it makes me curious if it's set for stations in a particular city. It's not super loud, but the sound quality is pretty good on moderate volume.
Battery life is reasonable, though you'll want to use a battery pack with it if you plan on all-day/night use.
Bluetooth works well and paired easily.
The TF card and recording function work well with a 32Gbc10 card.

title: Surprisingly good quality
text:
I got these for my mom and just now had a chance to try them out.
And WOW, I'm really impressed! Frequency response is really good and clarity is great. Maxed out volume (spotify on tab, no booster) maintained most of the clarity and was def loud.
Noise cancellation is effective, I had my TV on while testing these and can't hear it over moderate volume.

Battery life is reasonable, though you'll want to use a battery pack with it if you plan on all-day/night use.
Bluetooth works well and paired easily.
The TF card and recording function are a bit iffy and I'd deduct half a star if I could. If I put audio files on the card, they'll play fine, though it puts everything into a flat list. If I use a freshly formated card, the recording functions work great. The problem is when I try to record onto a card with data already on it - it completely crashes/reboots the device. Forced to choose, I'll likely keep a blank card in it, but it would be really nice to have the audio files handy, too. Oh, on the note of the card - I tested several 32GBc10s, a 64GBu1, and a 128GBu3 and they all played media and supported recording, just not on the same card at the same time.

title: Quality/design are awesome!
text:
I mainly got this for adding accessories, or secondary cameras, to my tripod. It articulates well and is large enough that it reaches far enough from the attached pole to use the accessory. It's working excellently right now as a light holder.
The entire contrsuction is aluminum and everything fits perfectly and feels super sturdy. The clamp is great and holds on tightly. Interestingly, they made the attachement for the clamp the same size as the mounting bolt and it's a receiver, so I can use the clamp on it's own to hold something onto a regular tripod, though I think in most cases I'd prefer to mount something to my tripod rather than mount a flashlight or something to a tripod.

title: Effective & built solid
text:
It's especially convenient when I'm using my phone in landscape and I want the cord out of the way.
So far I've used these for PD (max 45w) and connecting to a USB splitter. It transmits power with little or no loss and there wasn't a noticeable difference using it for data.

title: Epic battery capacity (for an emergency radio)
text:
The unit feels solidly built and everything works well.
For an emergency radio this has the largest battery capacity I've yet seen (10Ah) - I had it playing TV audio for 90hrs continuously before it dropped to 50% charge. Analogue tuning is a bit tricky to get a solid lock on even nearby stations, though it was able to pickup my FM transmitter with minimal static. Speaker is decent quality for the size and it gets fairly loud.
The spotlight is bright and narrow. The flood lights on the front are bright and give a good, even lighting. The reading light would probably be good for reading a map on someone's hood, but it's way to bright (and not dimmable) to use as a reading light before turning in for the night.

title: Happily using as a PD cable at 45W
text:
I'm using this for my Samsung tab S8+, which maxes out at 45W on PD. Charging is super fast and the USB-a adapter isn't in the way. The 2nd cable I'm keeping neatly rolled up to have if I need it on-the-go.
I can't speak to data capabilities as I move everything wirelessly.
The cable itself feels very robust and has the rigidity usually associated with thicker wires. Both USB-C tips and the USB-a adapter look like they're good quality.

title: Works great on US (120V-60hz)
text:
I don't have anything that provides a foreign power source too that this on for converting, but it works well on standard US electric supply (120v @ 60Hz). The rotating prongs for using us and au on the same circuit is pretty nifty.
The USB ports work well and the PD port works great with my tablet (45W). The PD port doesn't supply standard power, so if you're using the same cord for your main device and accessories, you'll need to move the cable from the PD to one of the standard USB-C ports.

title: A good, solid hub
text:
I've been running this for a few days connected to a Samsung note 10+ - all functions work great and there've been no errors leaving it running. I have cat 5e, FHD, a portable hard drive, 4 USB card readers, a USB 3 splitter, a dongle for a mouse, and a micro SD plugged in right now.
It feels solid and all connections are secure.

title: Works great
text: I've been using this with my Samsung tab S8+ and it works great! Response is pretty quick and I haven't run into any errors. I'm a little worried about longevity - materials feel cheap and it's put together a bit loose.

title: Quality construction, good size, attractively practical
text:
I'm using this for my on-the-go electronics and accessories and it works really well. My favorite aspect is the shape - like a suitcase, the squareness makes packing easier. The pockets and organization are nice, and I figured if the one pocket keeps wet in, it should be a good place to put things I want to make sure stay dry. The side straps are perfect for my tripod.
I like that I can expand the main compartment and that the laptop sleeve is easily removable. The big padded handle is really nice - I'm typically wearing a gear vest when I'm doing something I'm bringing my tripod and stuff for so I won't be using the shoulder straps much.
I like the look of the grey, it's clean and understated, and it's generally attractively designed.

title: Great for non-continuous monitoring
text:
Installation was easy and the picture quality is great. Getting it setup, including with the sd card, was quick and easy.
Image quality is great, FoV is pretty decent, and nightvision works really well.
Accessing it through the app is easy and it does a good job of detecting motion/people.
My only complaint is that I can't find a setting for continuous recording/monitoring. Even with the app open to the camera, it will time out after a few minutes. I'm guessing this is to save battery so the solar panel's low output will be enough - I don't mind plugging it in and I wish there was a setting to turn on continuous video.

title: Excellent USB power strip
text:
I like to leave accessory chargers plugged in and use them as needed. I paired this with an additional 4-port hub, and they are great for charging all my accessories - from 30Ah batteries to my Galaxy buds, it gives strong and consistent power. Being able to turn individual ports on and off is a really cool feature.
I haven't pushed the amperage draw to the limit, but charging a few batteries and a few small accessories at once provide a quick charge to all devices. I mounted it under a table, and the port on the end is perfect for a USB light.
Material construction is really nice, it feels very solid & sturdy.
*I haven't (and don't plan to) use this for data, so I can't say how it handles it.
*Surprisingly the end port isn't USB 3, I would've thought the placement would be perfect if you wanted to gang up several of these.

title: Shifts a lot of heat
text:
The one thing this needs to do well, it does - it moves the heat away from my laptop's woefully inadequate vent. The design allows it to be off if the computer is just "idling", and the fan is pretty quiet on low. If you're overclocking and pushing your machine, it may start to sound like it's going to lift off on max, but it moves a lot of air doing it.
The lights are pretty, though a BT companion app would be really cool to customize them.
It's not thin by any means, but it will raise the computer a few inches off a surface.

title: Sounded great recording as FLAC
text:
In testing, this little guy performed surprisngly well.
I had to turn gain down from what I assume was default for phone mics, I didn't test the low-end of the volume spectrum (I don't have a quiet enough environment) but I'm guessing this will pick up some soft and quite sounds. With dB gain down, it did an excellent job recording environmental noices, voice, and a sound system. Recordings were *mostly* clear - there was a bit of background noise and I'll be picking up wind guards ASAP. With the sound cleaned up, recordings were crisp and clear, stereo is noticeable.
It works just as well on a usb-c extension cord and a y-plug.
*Although the notes/documentation say that samsung phones require a special app, I was able to record from the usb-c microphone in all the apps I've tried. I tested it with a Fold 3 and a tab S8+ and it worked as well on both.

title: Particle Board & non-Adjustable Height
text:
This is nice and sturdy and the accessories are cool, but....
The main board is particle board, so it's a lot heavier than expected.
The legs aren't adjustable and are about twice as long as I'd like and are just over too long to even be useful for my situation.

The vaneer seems nice, but there wasn't a peice of cardboard between the product and shipping box and while opening the box, I put a line across the center of the top of the board.
The USB hub is a nice touch, but the cup holder is really really small.

I'm thinking this will be good to take camping - not for a lap tray, but to set on a table as a raised table; the usb hub and extra long legs should be great for this limited use.

title: A really nice extension, except...
text:
The usb-c connector doesn't extend far enough out from the bend for it to plug in either my phone or tablet (both have cases). Usually when this happens I just trim the elbow back a bit, but this is wrapped in metal. I'm hoping to find a use for this, probably on a power bank.
It feels extra sturdy and I don't doubt the 100w raiting.

title: Crystal clear and large image to the human eye
text:
Image quality is great and the 15x zoom is good, especially in a small package. I especially like the tripod receiver (and included tripod). 50mm field of view is good and a standard.
I would love to have given this 5 stars, but I just CAN'T get my phone's camera to both line up properly AND focus on the image. I'm going to keep attempting it and I'll post an update if I'm successful.
I suspect this would make a good spotting scope for a larger telescope, but I'm an admirer, not practitioner, of astrophotography, so I don't know in practical terms.

title: Exactly as expected
text: I haven't tried these with data, but they work wonderfully with 5v or QC 2/3. I got them to make the power setup on my EDC gear more streamlined and they work great!

title: Nice quality and attractive design
text:
I ordered this for my mother - she's going in for extensive surgery in a week and just bought a laptop. I decided on a backpack for the convenience. She wasn't originally crazy about getting a backpack versus a messenger bag, but when she saw it she loved it.
This backpack is well constructed and the overall design is both very functional and looks premium. I expect it will take a bit of a beating over the next month or so, and both stay intact and protect the contents.

title: Impressive from both ends!
text:
I had my doubts when ordering this, but WOW is it what it claims to be. The vacuum works amazingly and gets up everything from fine dust to clumps of dog fur. It's also super easy to clean. FYI - I did notice that on one chair I vacuumed, there was a powder that passed straight through the filter and out the back; so don't aim the air at yourself when you're vacuuming! The blower side works as well as canned air and it comes with a good assortment of attachments.
Battery life is impressive and charges reasonably quickly.
It's a cool feature that the handle rotates, though this doesn't dictate the side you can use. Also, it seems that most of the attachments can be used on either side.

title: Great mechanical-feel keyboard
text: Button press isn't excessive but it's a bit more than the average keyboard. I like the round keys, they're quirky and it didn't take any time for my fingers to get comfy with it. Typing speed is really good. Plug & play worked just fine.

title: So close to being perfect
text: The station was easy enough to set and the Bluetooth to connect. I found the ideal station at radio-locator and it transmits beautifully. The remote is a nicer feature than I thought it would be. It's handy, but it needs volume controls. It would also be nice if the buttons needed more force to click as it's really easy to press one while spinning the steering wheel. The main unit really needs a mini battery to just last a few seconds for when you bump the device and it disconnects.

title: Good design, extremely functional, nicely portable
text: I love that the grounding pole is on a separate pivot in case you're using an old socket or have to plug in upside down. The 120v sockets work well and hold a plug firmly, though I'd have preferred them to not be asymmetric. They're spaced far enough apart to allow plugging in multiple power bricks. The USB plugs work fine, but are limited to 5v. The usb-c will push 3A @5v but doesn't meet PD standards. For traveling, I would recommend this, along with a high wattage power brick (I like to use 45W PD) - charge your phone or power banks off the brick and use the USB ports on this for lower power devices.

title: Internal design seems great, external... Not so much
text:
Works well for sending BT as FM. It allows me to broadcast on any frequency. FM output needs to be stronger - my local airwaves are quite crowded and I'm constantly getting static or bleed-through. About the design - idk what it is, but I CAN'T get it to work in my car's socket without it resetting every few seconds. I got a USB to 12v adapter and it works just fine now. So to make it work I have it plugged into a 12v adapter that's plugged into a USB adapter that is plugged into the 12v socket.
I decided against using it in the car and it's working pretty well in the house.

title: Excellent radio, so nice I ordered a second
text:
It's the multifunctionality that really wins me over, and in such a small package. I've replaced my EDC bt speakers with these. Bluetooth volume and clarity are on par with Altec Lansing's mini-H2O speakers. Battery life is awesome, I can go 8-10 hours on mid-volume Bluetooth. It also runs & charges at the same time. Radios have good reception & favs is a good feature. I really appreciate the scan feature, especially with shortwave. Button lock is handy. Having a wheel in addition to seek buttons is a nice feature, as is analogue volume. The tf software has a lot to be desired, considering the lcd panel, they really should've offered a menu for sd contents.

I'd like to request, in the future, offer audio-out - either a headphone jack or ability to send radio over BT to a device... Basically, I want to be able to record, or at least use my galaxy buds to listen to shortwave, using my phone as the host. If you release an upgraded model with the aforementioned features and more radio bands (TV audio, CB, USB (upper side band), LSB, air, and marine) I'll be first in line for one.

title: So awesome, I got a 2nd a week after the 1st
text:
It's the multifunctionality that really wins me over, and in such a small package. I've replaced my EDC bt speakers with these. Bluetooth volume and clarity are on par with Altec Lansing's mini-H2O speakers. Battery life is awesome, I can go 8-10 hours on mid-volume Bluetooth. It also runs & charges at the same time. Radios have good reception & favs is a good feature. I really appreciate the scan feature, especially with shortwave. Button lock is handy. Having a wheel in addition to seek buttons is a nice feature, as is analogue volume. The tf software has a lot to be desired, considering the lcd panel, they really should've offered a menu for sd contents.

I'd like to request, in the future, offer audio-out - either a headphone jack or ability to send radio over BT to a device... Basically, I want to be able to record, or at least use my galaxy buds to listen to shortwave, using my phone as the host. If you release an upgraded model with the aforementioned features and more radio bands (TV audio, CB, USB (upper side band), LSB, air, and marine) I'll be first in line for one.

title: Great for tablets & small laptops
text: First impression is how well constructed it is, if the contents were secured well enough, I can see this being able to take a beating. There are more pockets and better organization than I was anticipating; and, overall, has a pretty good capacity. I got this as an add-on to my EDC vest, a couple s-clips are all it takes to make it a compact backpack, even over top of the packs I already have on my back. Computer slot is padded, though I still intend to use my OtterBox case.

title: Good capabilities, a bit basic, but good quality.
text:
AM(MW) and FM work great. I'm still new to shortwave, but I was able to find a few stations within about 10mins. As I learn more about SW, I'll update this review if this radio is significantly better or worse than average.
Having a TF card slot is handy, but it doesn't display folder hierarchy or playlist, it just puts everything into a simple flat list. I believe it's based on alphabetical order, but I've yet to put enough effort into it to know for sure. I just loaded up a bunch of single-file audiobooks on a card and kept the file list on my phone for reference. It seems to jump from one book to the next easily and has no trouble playing them. You can also punch in the number for the audio file. I can't find any other use for the keypad.
Speaker is clear and loud, but I didn't push it to max.
The light is reasonably bright, and you can put the radio on it's side and put a water bottle over the light to get a lantern.
I love that it has an 18650 battery bay. I use this size for a variety of electronics, so I've always got a few handy. You can also find this cell size in a lot of devices with internal batteries - a great feature for emergencies.
My only complaint is that it uses a MINI USB plug - everything you see in life is either micro, USB-C, or apple. If you lose the charging cable you'll likely not find one IRL and will need to await delivery.

title: Does what it's supposed to and does it well.
text: Most of the PCs I work on predate usb3, but this is faster than my other USB 2 or 3 readers on usb2 ports. I really like that the card inserts from the "outside". I use it for portable apps and it gets a lot of low-volume, high-frequency data transfer. I've only had it disconnect if I've bumped it while removing something else. Worth great will splitters, hubs, and otg. Small size/low profile was a primary reason for buying it and I've been happy with it's size.

title: Well worth the price tag
text: Got this so I can plug various drives/dongles in at once for work. I have a Bluetooth adapter and a u3 (running portable apps) plugged in all the time and I haven't had any errors, disconnects, or brown outs adding a second flash drive.

title: Good zip tie for almost all occasions
text: I'd first like to say that I think these are a great product and that I plan to buy more as I need them. Imo the re-useability isn't as useful as the fact you can loosen, adjust, and re-tighten; as opposed to cutting the old one off and putting a new one on (if they were regular ties). The weight raiting is also inconsistent, I think it's based on a gradual work up to 100lbs not a sudden addition of weight...I popped one instantly when I hung a ~20lb backpack on it and just let go without thinking, there was only a few inches of slack but that was enough to generate enough force to snap the head off the zip tie.

title: Keeping the Desk Neat and Watch Visible
text:
Great way to make the puck charger like the previous gear chargers, much neater than just having my watch laying around loose.
The included charger works well and seems just as good as the factory one.
When I first got a watch with this design of charger I wasn't crazy about it, but after 4yrs of using it I couldn't do just the puck.
PS to Amazon: why is there a rating for battery life? This contains no battery XD

title: Not full 1080, but a solid adapter
text: Although it works great, it only outputs at a max of 1600x900 to a standard 1080 tv. It's not my computer or tv as I had a different style adapter previously that outputted 1080 with no problems. That being said it does give a clear and clean picture with no lag. Not sure on audio as I don't use audio on this computer.

title: Excellent portable device stand
text: Works great with phone in landscape or portrait, strong/study enough to hold my 12in tab without there being any close calls or accidents. The cradle is also deep enough for an encased phone, but not a battery case, though it still holds my phone fine with the phone itself overhanging. I love that it folds flatter than a slim wallet and is just the right size for wherever I want to stash it. I do prefer an articulated metal stand at home, but for price and portability this really can't be beat.

title: Works as expected
text:
I've tried this on standard usb3 and on a usb-c hub, both instances it works great. Transfer speeds are good on normal usb3 and only slightly slower on usb-c to usb3. On one hub, it needed external power to work, otherwise it would shut down the hub.
I use two regularly, one on an extension cable to an older pc with usb2, for things like flash drives, it works without external power, but it needs it for hard drives; the other I have connected to a usb-c hub without external power and it gets enough power throughput to run an external hdd.

title: Works great, use daily
text:
I got this for my home set-up. I love that I can leave everything plugged in (incl power) and it's always good to go when I plug in my computer. (Other brand hubs I've bought tend to need to be power cycled at least a few times a week, if not daily.)
When my batt isn't full, it pulls as much as 40W on usb-c pd and the hub handles the throughput just fine with no overheating.
VGA is stable and as clear as it can be. USBs are both highspeed and work fine with a second usb3 hub (with or without power to it). Usb-c port is secure and cable stays plugged in despite occasional tugs. I haven't tested the LAN, HDMI, or audio jack, so I can't comment on them.

title: Does exactly what I wanted it to
text: I use 2 of the 3 to put my bluetooth receiver in just the right position. There doesn't seem to be any sound degradation and they stay securely connected.

title: Decent receiver, very good for the price
text: I use this daily in my car and it works great, sound quality is on-par with the basic, factory sound system. Had to add a little dot of velcro to easily feel which button is which. Also needed to add some 3.5mm right angle adapters to put it where I want, I don't like it sticking straight out from the dash and wasn't crazy about having it on a wire. Biggest problem is there is nothing to filter out noise from the charger. If you're planning to use it for more than a couple hours (or forget to charge it when not using it) plan to have a battery to charge it with or you'll get static from a 12v usb adapter (I've tried expensive ones and cheap ones, they all do it).

title: My go-to hub
text: I use this on a daily basis. It works great and has a high transfer speed on the USB ports. The micro-sd port is rather slow. It pulls enough power to run 2 external hard drives.

title: Works so great I'm ordering another
text: Got this for the compact size and multiple speeds for work. It's excellent - low fan speed is equivalent to one of the DG usb fans and mostly all I use. I charged it up last night and have been using it off and on all day and it's still blowing well on low. Almost no noise and sits perfectly still. Not crazy about the pivot points, having them at "3 o'clock" and "9 o'clock" would be better. Going to buy another for the bedside table.

title: I wish I had found this years ago
text: So handy for keeping the little things organized. Also nice having memory cards and a reader always at hand.

title: Great case for notebook PCs and large tablets
text: This is perfect for my Galaxy Book and many accessories. Side pockets are bit small but are a good size for back up batteries. I do wish it was just a half inch thicker as adding my tablet (in an otter box) really gets things tight. The front also likes to droop with molle bags attached.

title: handy light, dimming is a nice feature
text: Not quite as bright as another brand of these I bought, but they are very handy and super low power. I like to use several with liptstick batteries for a soft area light.

title: Good frequency range and clear sound. Construction is a bit poor.
text:
I ordered one, the back was bulged out like when a battery expands and I returned it. I then ordered 2 for the stereo pairing. Both have the same bulge. Upon examination it is caused by poor assembly: the battery appears fine, but there was a glob of silicon under the battery that looked as if it had spilled over from the waterproofing and was keeping the battery from seating properly. End result is the back case doesn't quite fit right and I'm a bit skeptical if it is still waterproofed. Even after removing the excess silicon and seating the battery properly, the case is still bowed out.
The sound is AMAZING for such a small package. They've used two speakers, presumably one to fill in the lows. It by no means thumps, but watching movies and playing games sounds very good. Getting the stereo pairing set-up was a bit tricky, and once it was set up it sounded out of sync occasionally. I mostly use these to have sound come from the monitor a video is on instead of my main computer.

title: Great Earbuds
text:
I've been using the LG Tone Ultras for about a year now, and decided to switch to these because of the external speakers.
Sound quality is about the same, both very good. I don't listen to anything with heavy bass, so these cover my music's full frequency range very effectively.
The external speakers are like having a cell phone speaker on each shoulder - not very loud or great range, but it's nice to be able to listen to music while still hearing my surroundings; I also like to leave the external speakers on when not listening to anything for the read-out alerts.
Step counter is a cool idea but compared to my fitbit and smartwatch, it's WAAAAY off - 1200 steps vs 3700 on fitbit and 3000 on the watch, and I only take the headphones off at night.
Battery life is excellent, I can listen to music more/less all day and they're still not dead when I plug them in at night.
I've been using necklace style headphones for about 2 years, so I'm very used to them, but I find these especially comfortable. They also resist rotating better than the Ultras.
The ends aren't as long as the Ultras so relearning muscle memory (button location) took a bit, but now that I'm used to them I prefer the smaller size, they're less in-the-way.
Only thing that disappoints me is the mic - when on a call the other party can barely understand me and usually complains of muffled-sound. Just a note to LG or any other manufacturers out there: combine this with a high-end headset for calls and I'd happily pay 200-300 for it, as is I wear these and carry a headset for calls in my pocket.

title: Required accessory for 360 cameras
text:
Got this for my Samsung Gear 360 camera. Works great! Sticks pretty strong to my roof. Going to figure out a way to secure it to something else before doing any speed test, but it did fine at 45.
FYI for those like me that don't know squat about cameras - this will screw directly into the camera itself, so if you don't need to aim and prefer low-profile, this is all you need.

title: Legit OEM charger
text: Works the same as what came with my tablet, so exactly what I wanted.

title: Very handy and bright
text:
Love these little things, great night-time light. Also makes a great alternative to a candle when coupled with a "lipstick" battery. Seems to auto-shut down after a while - I was testing how long it would run on a certain battery but it turned off during the night, despite the battery still having juice.
Dimming feature is really nice, I just wish this had some sort of "memory" so I could put it somewhere remote and turn it on and off by turning the power source on and off

title: Convenient and functional
text:
Very nice keyboard.
Back-light is nice and bright.
Larger and more comfortable size than most portable keyboards.
Folding in on itself makes it its own case, I love that I can just toss this in my computer bag and not worry.

title: functional and pretty
text:
Bumpy start, but the seller helped me out.
Great little keyboard, ridiculously thin, colors are pretty, and makes a great portable keyboard.

title: Disappointing, runs hot
text:
They advertise usb 3 speeds. I can't attest to the speed on the USB 3 side, but usb c is incredibly slow.
I played 360p videos off it all night and it was hot in the morning, there is no reason such small videos should be pulling much load.
It is a convenient, somewhat large storage option, but don't expect to use it to transfer large amounts of data between devices unless you plan a Netflix binge.

title: Satisfied customer
text: Works great on my phone, read/write speed is good, 183GB of actual/formatted space, which was expected.

title: Best cord I own
text: Supports quick charging, carries a high amperage, and good length. They feel durable and of high quality. They even come in fancy faux leather cases. I've bought 6 so far and I may buy more. I definitely recommend these.

title: Works great
text: These have worked very well for me all but one time, and that time may have been my phone. The metal casing gives a felling of quality and durability. I recommend these.

title: I do not recommend these nor will I be buying from this manufacturer again.
text: Disappointed these don't support quick charging and a bit angry that they carry hardly any amperage. The 6ft cord can't keep up with power used when using phone, even on low brightness, the 3ft cord charges VERY slowly and can't keep up if brightness over 85%, the mini cord is good for emergencies but isn't particularly fast even being so short.

title: doesn't work with note 4
text: Works with my note pro but not note 4, I haven't tried it with anything else yet. 3 stars because I mostly wanted it for the note 4.

title: Works great.  Very fast.
text: Works great.  No problems.

title: Almost Perfect
text: Nearly perfect for use as a lap desk because you can use it flat for eating and tilted at several levels to use with various technology without worry of things sliding off because there is a tilt up lip to hold things in place.  I was hoping the mouse pad would pull in and out like a drawer, but instead you have to open the lid and take out the mouse pad; then slide it into the left or right slot and click it into a slot.  To remove you must push a button and wiggle it out and open the and put it in the storage section under the lid.  I still highly recommend the product.

title: Good cables
text: We've been happy with these and the length is great.

title: Nice to have added security
text: I purchased a Melnor Water Timer.  I've had one before and they are wonderful, but they can break faster than I wish, so I decided a small insurance policy was worth the cost since Water Timers are kind of expensive.  In this case, it does give peace of mind.

title: Really happy with this product
text: I've very happy with these bands.  They are a perfect exchange for our Fitbit.  We found an unbeatable deal on our Fitbit bands, but before ordering them, we wanted to make sure we could change the bands at a reasonable price and these bands are perfect.  They were super easy to put on the device and are sturdy.

title: Works good enough.
text: I had a computer mishap.  Short story I had to marks on my computer I was trying to clean up and I listened to a well meaning person on Facebook and used Goof off to remove the marks and it worked too well.  It removed the rubbery covering and made it look terrible.  So, I thought I would try a computer skin.  It did help a lot, but you can see all the seems, but its better than the alternative.  At least I can say I learned a valuable lesson.

title: Worked for Roku TV but not Roku device
text: We bought two. One worked for Roku TV, but my Roku device is out of luck.

title: Great, then not.
text: When I first received these I was rather happy and initially gave a 5 start review and bought a second set.  My only complaint was I wished the magnets were a little stronger.  Five months in, the cables themselves are good but the piece that goes in the phone are not that great.  The first one all but lost it's magnetic pull.  I tried cleaning it in case there was dirt I couldn't see but that didn't help.  So I switched to the other adapter that came in the second set and in no time the metal ring that attached to the plastic on the adapter feel off.  I took shoe goo and put a little on the plastic and reattached the metal ring and it is working again, but they shouldn't wear it this fast.  I bought them believing they'd last longer than traditional cables, but so far they don't.

title: Not bad

title: Too Awesome for Words (and yet I'll use some)
text:
I bought this mouse to replace an inexpensive laser mouse that died after about eight months. I've been using it for about a month and I couldn't be more pleased.

I'm not that tech savy so I rely a lot on Amazon ratings and reviews whenever I need to buy an electronic item (or anything else for that matter). The reviews for this mouse were good and the price was amazing so I took the plunge. I'm always a little wary about buying items that are inexpensive or discounted because I'm afraid they might be a terrible product that Amazon (or the manufacturer) is trying to unload. But this mouse is awesome and I'm so glad I bought it.

First of all, it feels so perfect in my hand. The indentation on the left side is perfect for resting your thumb. I never realized what a strain holding my thumb out of the way was on my hand. Plus, the upward curve of the top is the perfect shape for my hand. It's like it's a special hand rest designed for people with carpel tunnel syndrome (which I have) rather than a tool I'm forced to use for hours every day. I'm a woman with fairly long, slender hands so I can't say that the curve would be perfect for someone with significantly larger or smaller hands than mine but I have a feeling that it would be comfortable for almost anyone.

This mouse is ultra precise with the placement and control of the cursor. You won't have to fight with it to get the cursor where you want it to be. The wheel is also easy to control and the amount of scroll can be set with the settings adjustment as can many other features. The two buttons on the left side are 'page forward' and 'page back' which I don't use much but some people would, I guess.

Instillation was a snap. The little dongle (or whatever you call it) plugs into a port and automatically installs the drivers. Pop in a battery and you're ready to go!

I'm so impressed with the quality of design that went into this device that I would eagerly try anything this company manufactures - as long as the ratings and reviews were positive, of course. I'm not a 'power reviewer' or anything. I just really like this product.

Sometimes it freezes and goes to black screen so you lost Waze or Google Maps. I tether to my hotspot on phone with Visible Wireless and been working for me. But if you ever installed a stereo you will figure it out  I do not believe this unit has dual zone feature so that's a huge bummer.  And if the video out feature doesn't work it will get exchanged.  A purchase is only as good as the tech support when needed. That's why my rating is what it is.  Can't drag and change the screens as seen on other units.
